　　李渊道：“他们肯定也会考校二郎和三郎，若是……”
　　窦氏道：“没有若是。郎君尽可以相信二郎和三郎。不过我只有一个要求。”
　　李渊道：“夫人请说。”为了结这门亲，让夫人去郑氏受辱，他也确实有些愧疚。
　　窦氏冷哼道：“若是郑氏想和二郎和三郎结亲，必须拒绝！”
　　李渊先一愣，然后失笑：“好！我们家只能有一个郑氏的女儿。就是他们求我，我们也不把二郎和三郎给他们。”
　　窦氏这才消气。
　　哼，等你们看到二郎和三郎，有你们后悔的！
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 8: Seeking a Marriage for Her Son, a Mother Suffers Humiliation

After Lady Dou cooled her anger, she had initially intended to leave the two children behind and travel to Xingyang alone.

But Li Sanniang had persuaded her, saying, "Mother, Sanlang's health is much better this year, and Erlang has made him quite lively. Erlang no longer needs to watch over his brother by the bedside, so he is even more energetic than in previous years. If you are not here, Grandmother has always doted on her grandsons to a fault. I fear I will not be able to keep them in line."

At the thought of Li Shimin leading Li Xuanba to tear down the roof the moment she left, Lady Dou shuddered.

Thus, Lady Dou ultimately took her two sons with her to Xingyang.

Daxing City was four hundred and fifty kilometers away from Zhengzhou's Xingyang. In later generations, driving on a highway would take a mere five hours.

But in this era, the journey required at least three days.

By this time, the soil fertility of the Guanzhong and Guandong regions had already declined. Daxing City could hardly sustain itself and relied on grain supplies from the east. Consequently, the Wei River and the Yellow River were constantly dredged to remain navigable.

However, the stretch of the Yellow River near what later generations called Sanmenxia was exceptionally treacherous. Water transport there was incredibly perilous, claiming countless vessels over the years.

Although this water route had been in use since the Qin Dynasty, it was merely a desperate measure born of necessity.

Traveling with children, Lady Dou naturally would not choose to force a crossing through the dangerous Sanmenxia.

Upon reaching the vicinity of Sanmenxia, she disembarked with her two sons, bypassed the most dangerous stretch of the Yellow River by carriage, and then boarded another boat to continue toward Xingyang.

Had Lady Dou been traveling alone, she would have taken a carriage straight to Xingyang once she reached Sanmenxia.

However, the children were young, and carriages were far too bumpy. She preferred water travel whenever possible; the extra time spent on the road mattered little, as they were in no hurry.

After disembarking, Lady Dou even took Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to sightsee at Sanmenxia and Mount Dizhu.

Mount Dizhu rose only nine meters above the water's surface, but like an iceberg, its submerged mass was immense.

Standing squarely in the middle of the riverbed, Mount Dizhu was the greatest "killer" of the Yellow River.

Through the reefs at the base of Dizhu, successive dynasties had carved out three channels, known as the "Gate of God," "Gate of Ghosts," and "Gate of Men." Only by navigating these three channels could transport vessels pass safely.

Yet, in the raging torrents, where the underwater terrain was invisible and ships could barely turn, how difficult was it to keep from veering off course?

Thus, the three gates of "God," "Ghosts," and "Men" also carried the connotation that even gods, ghosts, and men found them nearly impossible to cross.

Li Xuanba was actually quite a chatterbox with a strong desire to share. Otherwise, after paying off his parents' debts in his past life, he wouldn't have chosen to work as a content editor for a social media marketing account for his retirement.

Hampered by his sub-healthy physical state, talking too much exhausted him, so Li Xuanba vented all his desire to share onto Li Shimin.

Gazing up at Mount Dizhu, Li Shimin listened with rapt attention, occasionally asking for gossip about the mountain.

Since the reefs of Mount Dizhu had always been a key crossing point, it was also a strategic military stronghold contested by all.

Li Xuanba spoke of the various crossing battles at Mount Dizhu as if counting his own family treasures. Li Shimin listened with a face full of excitement, wishing he could fight one himself.

"But Ah Xuan, if water transport is so treacherous, why not use land transport?" Li Shimin asked in confusion.

Li Xuanba then explained to his second brother the difference in cost between water and land transport.

*[However, after the fall of the Sui, the navigation conditions of the Yellow River will worsen. When transporting grain from the east to Guanzhong, the stretch from Luoyang to Shanzhou will have to be traveled by land, and then switched back to water from Shanzhou to Chang'an. Oh, right, Chang'an is Daxing.]*

Li Shimin froze, then reached out and clamped his hand firmly over Li Xuanba's mouth.

Li Xuanba made muffled "wuh-wuh" noises, his face turning bright red.

Lady Dou, who had been curiously wondering what Sanlang was saying to make Erlang so excited, quickly rescued Li Xuanba from Li Shimin's clutches.

She scolded, "Erlang, why are you bullying your brother?!"

Li Shimin replied, "I wasn't bullying him. Mother, you have no idea what he said... Actually, never mind. It's better if you don't know."

The young Li Shimin clasped his hands behind his back with great effort, looking up at the pillar in the midst of the torrent as he sighed deeply.

Such agonizing knowledge, he could only bear it alone.

Seeing Li Shimin's reaction, Lady Dou asked in bewilderment, "Sanlang, what did you say to your second brother?"

Li Xuanba replied with mock honesty, "I only spoke of the hardships of water transport."

Lady Dou grew even more puzzled. If he only spoke of the hardships of water transport, why would Erlang get so worked up?

Yet no matter how she pressed them, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's "testimonies" remained perfectly aligned.

It was just water transport. They had spoken of absolutely nothing else!

Lady Dou was helpless.

Since childhood, these twins had only shared secrets with each other. Even if she, as their mother, felt a bit envious, what could she do?

Once they boarded the carriage, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba immediately "reconciled." Li Shimin leaned close to his younger brother again, continuing to listen to his stories, whispering in his ear from time to time to ask questions he didn't want their mother to hear.

"The late Emperor actually led hundreds of thousands of Daxing citizens to Luoyang just to beg for food?"

*[Yes, and the subsequent emperors did the same. Later, they all lived in Luoyang and refused to return to Chang'an... I mean, Daxing.]*

"Then why build the capital in Daxing in the first place?"

*[That is complicated. It starts with the Northern Wei Dynasty established by the Yuan clan.]*

"Take your time. I'm listening."

Li Shimin popped a piece of candied fruit into his brother's mouth, then popped one into his own.

One for younger brother, one for me; one for younger brother, one for me.

When Li Xuanba said he didn't want any more, Li Shimin stuffed the remaining candied fruit into his own mouth. Then he pulled out some dried meat, tore it into pieces, and fed it to them: one piece for younger brother, one for me; one piece for younger brother, one for me...

When Li Xuanba said he was full, Li Shimin switched to something else.

Only when Li Xuanba insisted he couldn't eat another bite did Li Shimin hand him a cup of water, eating the rest himself while continuing to listen to the "story."

The historical tales Ah Xuan told were far more interesting than reading history books himself.

Lady Dou was truly curious and asked once more what the two children were whispering about.

There was nothing to hide from their mother regarding historical events, so Li Xuanba said, "I was telling Brother about the Eight Pillar Generals and the establishment of the capital in Daxing."

"Ah, the Eight Pillar Generals..." Lady Dou beckoned to Li Shimin, telling him to stop leaning against Li Xuanba, who was already sweating from the heat.

Li Shimin shifted over to Lady Dou's side, snuggling against her without a care for the heat.

"Do Erlang and Sanlang know who the eight generals of the Eight Pillar Generals are?" Lady Dou asked.

Li Shimin nodded.

Li Xuanba also ran through the details of the Eight Pillar Generals in his mind.

The Eight Pillar Generals of the Northern Wei were Yuwen Tai, Yuan Xin, Li Hu, Li Bi, Zhao Gui, Yu Jin, Dugu Xin, and Houmo Chenchong.

Li Hu was Li Shimin's great-grandfather, whose descendants inherited the title of Duke of Tang in the Sui Dynasty. Li Bi's great-grandson was Li Mi, who would later contest the empire with the Li Tang dynasty, and his descendants inherited the title of Duke of Xing in the Sui Dynasty. Yu Jin's title of Duke of Yan, granted during the Northern Zhou, also continued into the Sui Dynasty.

Zhao Gui, originally the Duke of Chu of the Northern Zhou; Dugu Xin, originally the Duke of Wei of the Northern Zhou; and Houmo Chenchong, originally the Duke of Liang of the Northern Zhou, had all been killed after becoming entangled in the imperial struggles of the Northern Zhou. However, although their descendants did not inherit the ducal titles in the Sui Dynasty, they still held high offices, all appointed as Grand Generals of the Sui.

Yuwen Tai was the founder of the Northern Zhou, and his direct descendants had already been slaughtered by Yang Jian. Yuan Xin was a member of the Northern Wei imperial clan, included among the Eight Pillar Generals to represent the power of the Northern Wei emperor, but his lineage had also declined during the dynastic transition.

Yet, to demonstrate benevolence toward the previous dynasty, every emperor would allow collateral branches of the former imperial clans to hold office. Those who made outstanding contributions during the dynastic transition were especially trusted. Thus, although the imperial houses of Yuwen and Yuan were destroyed, the Yuwen and Yuan clans still held prestigious positions in the Sui Dynasty.

Lady Dou also explained what she knew of the Eight Pillar Generals to her two children: "The Eight Pillar Generals rose to prominence during the Yuan clan's Northern Wei. Through the Eastern and Western Wei, the Northern Zhou and Northern Qi, and down to the current Sui Dynasty, they have intermarried and remained closely bound to one another. This is just like the Five Surnames and Seven Clans, who also rose during the Northern Wei."

"The former Northern Wei nobility, represented by the Eight Pillar Generals, controlled the border garrison armies. Born from a tribal system, they represent the 'martial' aspect of the Sui. The Five Surnames and Seven Clans once possessed private fortress armies, but most have now been integrated into the garrison militia, and they can no longer deploy troops privately; they support the 'civil' aspect of the Sui." Lady Dou patted the back of Li Shimin's hand and said unhurriedly, "Just like the descendants of the Eight Pillar Generals, the Five Surnames and Seven Clans mostly intermarry among themselves, refusing to wed outsiders."

"The Great Sui imperial house is secure, and the realm is at peace. I fear those of us holding military power will draw His Majesty's suspicion. Gradually transitioning from martial to civil affairs is perhaps an inevitable path." Lady Dou smiled. "The primary wife of the Duke of Tang's estate will no longer be chosen from military families, but from the prestigious and pure Five Surnames and Seven Clans. Perhaps His Majesty will recognize our loyalty."

Lady Dou was indeed very pleased. Although her husband had not heeded her advice, he still maintained a degree of vigilance toward the Emperor and possessed a clear understanding of the path ahead for the Duke of Tang's estate.

Now that the realm was settled, this world belonged to the Yang clan. It was no longer a realm shared by the military nobility of the Northern Zhou, which had resembled a tribal confederation.

During the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui, he had continuously curtailed the power of the military nobility.

Whether it was mixing Han and Hu soldiers within the garrison militia or replacing the original Northern Zhou military nobles with imperial princes to command the armies, these were all manifestations of Emperor Wen's efforts to weaken the military nobility.

Furthermore, with the realm at peace, there were few battles left to fight. For noble military families, transitioning from martial to civil pursuits was the only way to ensure long-lasting wealth and honor.

In this realm, civil and military officials had always been interchangeable, with no distinct boundary between them. As long as the Duke of Tang's estate allied through marriage with the Five Surnames and Seven Clans, they could ride the coattails of their prestigious reputation to transition into civil governance.

Li Jiancheng's friends in Daxing City were also mostly sons of prominent Guanzhong families, and he enjoyed quite a reputation among the gentry.

Li Shimin wiggled his little feet. "So this marriage is very important for our family."

"Indeed." Hearing Li Shimin's adorable tone, Lady Dou could not help but pull him into her arms and give him a good squeeze.

Li Xuanba quietly nudged himself to the side.

A playful smile, reminiscent of a young maiden, appeared on Lady Dou's no-longer-youthful face. She grabbed Li Xuanba, who was trying to slip away, and pulled him into her embrace, squeezing them both together.

Li Xuanba said weakly, "Mother, it's so hot being squished like this."

Lady Dou laughed. "Mother isn't hot."

Li Shimin added, "I'm not hot either!"

Li Xuanba said, "But I am."

Li Shimin said, "Ah Xuan, you mustn't be unfilial. Since Mother and Brother aren't hot, you aren't hot either. Be good."

Li Xuanba: "..."

He really wanted to pluck out that stray lock of hair on his second brother's forehead. How infuriating!

...

Having understood the necessity of marrying into the Five Surnames and Seven Clans, a fire of fighting spirit ignited in Li Shimin's eyes.

Li Xuanba thought his second brother was out of his mind.

It's not like you're the one getting married. Why are you so fired up?

But since Li Shimin was fired up, Li Xuanba, as his twin, could only be passively ignited by him.

"Alright, Brother, what do you want to do?" Li Xuanba said, his head spinning from being shaken by Li Shimin. "Tell me so I can sleep. I'm tired."

Li Shimin grinned mischievously. "When we go to the Zheng family, they will definitely test our knowledge to judge our elder brother's scholarship."

Li Xuanba immediately guessed what his second brother was up to. "You want me to help you cheat?"

Li Shimin said with a straight face, "What do you mean 'help me cheat'? It's the two of us cheating together... No, wait. We are winning against them with our own abilities. How can that be called cheating?"

Although Li Xuanba had no desire to save face for Li Jiancheng, "slapping the faces" of prestigious clans was something any transmigrator would enjoy.

What was cheating anyway? Did cheats not count as their own ability? They were winning by their own merits!

"However, if we actively provoke the Zheng family children, it might lower their opinion of us." Li Xuanba's spark of excitement died down instantly, returning him to an incombustible state. He yawned and said, "Go to sleep, stop making trouble. We are finally going to see Father. Do you want to get beaten by him?"

Li Shimin muttered, "Yeye wouldn't beat me... Fine, we won't actively provoke them. But what if they actively provoke us?"

Li Xuanba narrowed his eyes. "Then they are courting death."

"Hehe." Li Shimin slipped into the covers. "Goodnight, Ah Xuan."

"Mm, goodnight..." Li Xuanba yawned a few more times, finally able to sleep.

The temporary inn they found was rather crude; the bed could not fit one adult and two children.

Lady Dou had the servants sleep on the floor in the hallway outside while she slept in the adjacent room.

Tossing and turning, she felt uneasy, so she threw on a robe to check on the two children and see how they were sleeping.

And then, she overheard the two little rascals' face-slapping plan.

Lady Dou smiled helplessly and returned to her room to sleep in peace.

Since they still had the energy to plot mischief, they would surely sleep well.

Another half-day passed, and Lady Dou and the two children finally arrived in Xingyang.

Li Yuan had skipped his official duties early to wait outside the city.

The carriage stopped. Just as Li Yuan dismounted, a little chubby figure came rushing over.

"Yeye!"

Li Shimin leaped up from where he stood. Li Yuan bent down to catch him, and Li Shimin hung securely around Li Yuan's neck.

"Oof, Yeye's Erlang has grown heavy again." Li Yuan laughed, nuzzling his second son's cheek.

Li Shimin laughed and nuzzled back. "I'm not heavy, I've grown. Ah Xuan has grown too."

Only then did Li Yuan notice the short child with stubby arms and legs who was trying to help his mother down from the carriage.

Li Xuanba bowed respectfully. "Greetings, Father. I hope Father is well."

"Good, very good." Li Yuan felt a bit awkward.

Why was this child so formal? He didn't even know how to respond.

Li Shimin not only hung from Li Yuan's neck with both arms but also wrapped his short legs around Li Yuan's torso, looking exactly like a sloth.

"Ah Xuan, come quickly! Let Yeye hug you too." Sloth Li Shimin enthusiastically invited Li Xuanba to join him in being a sloth.

Li Xuanba took a step back, hiding behind Lady Dou and pretending to be shy. "I'll pass."

Looking at his timid third son, then weighing his second son in his arms, Li Yuan thought to himself that the second son was still the best.

Lady Dou pulled Li Xuanba out from behind her and said, "You haven't seen Yeye in so long. Hurry and follow Erlang's example to get close to your father. If you miss this chance, who knows when you will see him again?"

Li Yuan joked, "Is Madam blaming me?"

Lady Dou smiled. "How would I dare?"

Li Xuanba said with mock solemnity, "Alright."

He shuffled over to Li Yuan step by step, then leaned against him half-heartedly.

Li Yuan: "..."

Li Shimin leaned close to his father's ear and whispered, "Ah Xuan always cares too much about his dignity. Whenever he acts like this, Mother pulls him into her arms and vigorously ruffles his hair. You should do it too, Yeye! His reaction is hilarious."

With that, he let go of Li Yuan, signaling his father to put him down and go "bully" his younger brother.

A mischievous grin appeared on Li Yuan's face.

He set Li Shimin down, then suddenly scooped Li Xuanba up and tossed him high into the air.

Li Xuanba's eyes widened like brass bells. Dazed, he was thrown up and caught, then thrown up again.

Li Yuan was a master archer who could fire seventy arrows in rapid succession. His arm strength was astonishing, making tossing a child child's play.

Lady Dou's face paled. "My Lord! Do not frighten Sanlang!"

Li Yuan laughed. "Rest assured, I will definitely catch him!"

Watching his brother's plight, Li Shimin doubled over, clutching his stomach as he roared with laughter.

Seeing that his father and second brother wanted to make a fool of him, Li Xuanba stubbornly shut his eyes, curled into a ball clutching his knees, and refused to give them the satisfaction of begging for mercy.

Looking at his third son, who had curled into a ball with a face full of stubbornness, Li Yuan burst into hearty laughter.

Just as Erlang had said, his third son was indeed highly entertaining!

Lady Dou paced anxiously, not daring to snatch her son away for fear of dropping him. She could only call out in vain for her husband to stop, before landing a sharp blow on the head of Li Shimin, who was still laughing at his brother.

Li Shimin clutched his head. "Ouch!"

Li Xuanba opened his eyes, and seeing his brother get beaten, he smiled.

Lady Dou could not help herself either, covering her mouth as she giggled.

The family of four blocked the middle of the road, laughing together. Passersby who had intended to scold them for blocking the path could only shake their heads with a smile, sighing as they allowed this long-reunited family to enjoy their warm moment a little longer.

"Come, Yeye will take you to eat some delicious food!"

"Alright, Yeye!"

"Yes, Father."

"Call me Yeye."

"No."

"Yeye, tickle Ah Xuan! Ah Xuan is most afraid of being tickled!"

"Li Shimin!!! Ah, hahahaha, I was wrong, I was wrong! Yeye, Yeye, I was wrong!"

Lady Dou wiped away the tears of laughter. The stifling gloom built up from managing the household chores back at the Duke of Tang's estate vanished instantly, and her spirits soared.

...

Thanks to the meddling of that mischievous boy Li Shimin, even though Li Xuanba was reluctant to get too close to Li Yuan, he had no choice but to do so.

Otherwise, his shameless father would tickle him.

Furious, Li Xuanba rode on top of Li Shimin, raining down soft, childish punches on his second brother.

Li Shimin howled as he was beaten by the "infinitely strong" Li Xuanba.

Once Li Xuanba collapsed to the side, panting with exhaustion, Li Shimin jumped up and down on the bed, making faces and mocking his brother for not hurting him at all.

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes in frustration.

*If I were truly the infinitely strong Li Xuanba from the legends, I would definitely hang you from a tree!*

Resting for only a single day, the energetic Li Shimin dragged Li Xuanba to prepare for the Zheng family's evaluation.

Even if they did not actively strike, what if the Zheng family provoked them first?

Li Xuanba could only listlessly accompany his brother in flipping through books, preparing in advance for any provocative scenarios they might encounter.

On the other side, Lady Dou grew worried after hearing Li Yuan's words.

"No girls of suitable age?" Lady Dou said. "Even the closest in age would require Dalang to wait ten years. Dalang is already sixteen!"

Li Yuan said calmly, "Daughters of the Five Surnames and Seven Clans are betrothed early, around ten years of age. How could there be any of a suitable age for Dalang? The primary wife of our Duke of Tang's estate must not only come from the main branch of the Xingyang Zheng clan, but she must also be the daughter of a high-ranking official."

For a woman marrying out, whether she was born of a wife or a concubine was not of paramount importance; Li Yuan's two daughters by concubines had both married well.

But for the great clans, the daughters of the main branch were the most noble. Furthermore, Li Yuan privately desired that the father of the bride hold a high official rank; otherwise, the name "Xingyang Zheng" alone would be of little help to the Duke of Tang's estate.

After much deliberation, Li Yuan found the daughter of Zheng Jibo, the Governor of Kuazhou, to be the most suitable.

However, the daughter of Zheng Jibo, the Governor of Kuazhou, was currently only six years old—the same age as Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Lady Dou hesitated. "Since she is the same age as Erlang and Sanlang..."

Li Yuan scolded, "I know you favor Erlang and Sanlang, who grew up by your side, but the order of seniority and status must not be disrupted! If Erlang or Sanlang marries a daughter of the main branch of the Five Surnames and Seven Clans, how noble would the primary wife of the estate have to be to command authority over them? My imperial cousin does not have a daughter of suitable age to marry Dalang!"

Lady Dou lowered her head. "It was my slip of the tongue. Do not be angry, My Lord. I only thought that perhaps Erlang and Sanlang could be betrothed to daughters of the Zheng clan's collateral branches, while Dalang might seek a daughter from another of the Five Surnames and Seven Clans?"

Li Yuan shook his head. "How could it be so easy? Although the Five Surnames and Seven Clans do not hold as much power as we do now, they are extremely proud of their ancestral heritage. If Dalang's match with the Zheng family falls through, the other clans, being closely bound to the Zhengs, will absolutely refuse to arrange a marriage with Dalang. That would be offending the Zheng family."

Lady Dou was deeply distressed. "Then must Dalang truly wait ten years for the young lady of the Zheng family? Can they not allow her to marry earlier?"

Li Yuan shook his head again. "No. Zheng Jibo dotes on his daughter and insists she must reach sixteen before marrying."

Lady Dou said in annoyance, "Then has the Zheng family not already decided everything? Why did they even ask me here to discuss it!"

Li Yuan took Lady Dou's hand and patted it. "This is far from decided. Do you think a daughter of the Zheng family is so easy to marry? If I were not currently serving as the Governor of Zhengzhou and concurrently the Prefect of Xingyang, granting many conveniences to the Xingyang Zheng family, it would not even be our turn."

Lady Dou ground her teeth. "So you mean they invited me here just to pick and choose when it comes to our Dalang?"

Li Yuan sighed. "Madam, the daughters of the Five Surnames and Seven Clans are indeed precious. Please endure it for now."

The Zheng family's invitation to Lady Dou was indeed to observe her character and temperament, to see if she was worthy of intermarrying with the Zheng family.

For the Zheng family, any daughter marrying outside the Five Surnames and Seven Clans had to have her future in-laws carefully vetted, lest it tarnish their family name.

But to Lady Dou, this was a sheer insult.

Lady Dou's mother was Princess Xiangyang of the Northern Zhou, her father came from one of the Eight Pillar Families, and her husband was Li Yuan, the Duke of Tang, who was also a descendant of the Eight Pillar Generals. Furthermore, Li Yuan's mother was the elder sister of the late Empress.

The Duke of Tang's estate could proudly claim to be imperial relatives and a noble family of the highest order. In terms of court influence, the Zheng family, which now relied on nothing but its ancestral name, could not even begin to compare.

Lady Dou certainly did not believe her status was inferior to the Zheng family, who relied on nothing but the dry bones of their ancestors.

Yet, seeing that Li Yuan was absolutely set on this marriage, and knowing that if the Duke of Tang's estate did not wish to choose a daughter-in-law from among the military nobility, only a daughter of the Five Surnames and Seven Clans would be worthy, Lady Dou could only swallow her anger. "Then I shall go meet the Zheng clan. I would like to see just how formidable they truly are."

Li Yuan consoled her, "They certainly cannot compare to your intelligence, Madam."

Lady Dou's eyes darted around, and she pursed her lips with a smile. "Then I shall bring Erlang and Sanlang along as well."

Li Yuan said, "They will surely evaluate Erlang and Sanlang as well. If..."

Lady Dou said, "There are no 'ifs.' You can trust Erlang and Sanlang completely. However, I have only one condition."

Li Yuan said, "Please speak, Madam." He did feel a twinge of guilt for letting his wife suffer humiliation at the hands of the Zheng clan just to secure this marriage.

Lady Dou snorted coldly. "If the Zheng clan wishes to arrange a marriage for Erlang or Sanlang, we must refuse!"

Li Yuan was taken aback for a moment, then burst into laughter. "Very well! Our family shall only have one daughter of the Zheng clan. Even if they beg me, we will not give them Erlang or Sanlang."

Only then did Lady Dou's anger dissipate.

*Hmph, once you lay eyes on Erlang and Sanlang, you will surely regret it!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第9章 为母额间帖花钿
chunks.chineseText:
第9章 为母额间帖花钿

窦氏去告诉李世民和李玄霸好好准备，要去郑家做客时，李世民正趴在矮榻上，李玄霸把李世民当靠背盘坐，正一起翻看《晋书》。
　　他们所看的《晋书》是南朝梁的沈约所编撰。除了《晋书》，李世民还拿了同是沈约编撰的宋、齐、梁三代史书垫着胸口和下巴，好让自己趴得更舒服一些。
　　对于普通六岁孩童而言，现在读史书还太早了些。
　　李世民虽已经识得很多字，本也耐不住性子直接啃没有句读的史书。
　　李玄霸之前和他解说“五姓七望”时，他其实没听太懂。
　　比如什么“贾南风”啊，“八王之乱”啊，“永嘉之乱”啊，“国史之乱”啊，李世民都没听说过。
　　李玄霸和他说了“五姓七望”后，他才突然感兴趣，去史书里翻翻魏晋时期世家贵族的灭门史。
　　李玄霸原本以为自己所说的二哥都听得懂。因为二哥表现得他很懂的模样。
　　等到了李渊这里，李世民从李渊书房搬了晋、宋、齐、梁四代史书皱眉自学，李玄霸才知道，他这二哥居然还有一个嘴硬逞强的毛病。
　　你不知道就和我说啊，我给你解释。李玄霸腹诽。
　　但李世民就不。他要自己翻书学。
　　李玄霸没有揭穿二哥，和李世民一起看书。
　　沈约的《晋书》在后世已经失传。传世的《晋书》是许敬宗、房玄龄编撰的版本，人称“魔法晋书”，是一本很好看的玄幻小说集，堪称史书版《搜神记》。
　　沈约所编的《宋书》也入了“二十四史”，其玄幻程度比“魔法晋书”好一些。
　　但沈约这个人有个大毛病，他出身吴兴沈氏，南朝又继承了东晋极重门阀的毛病。导致他的《宋书》中有半数都是在为高门士族作传，狂吹海嘘。
　　比如琅邪王微的传记居然全是王微写给友人的信，不知道的人还以为这是王微文集。
　　沈约编撰的《晋书》也有这个毛病。

　　有了李玄霸事先打的预防针，李世民看着沈约吹嘘高门士族的内容，都是带着批判和看笑话的心态来看，时不时回头和弟弟吐槽。
　　窦氏进来了，正好听见李世民给李玄霸说“魏晋南北朝乱一次高门士族被屠满门一次，说不定现在他们的后人其实是他们的仇人”这个地狱笑话。

　　“别胡说，三日后我们要去郑家做客，你可别说错话了。”窦氏假装生气道，“那些高门大族的后人都有族谱为证，哪能做得假。”

　　李世民还没反应过来，李玄霸先脸色一垮。
　　他没好气道：“我还不知道哪家孩子去做客时，要被主人家考校抽背的。怎么，郑家想通过我和我哥的本事，去推测兄长的本事？”

　　虽然窦氏自己心里膈应，但不会这样对儿子们说。
　　为了自家女儿，“雀屏中选”这种事很正常，郑家只是做得太过。以后荥阳郑氏是唐国公府的亲家，窦氏不希望两个儿子和荥阳郑氏交恶。
　　再者郑家小娘子嫁进唐国公府后掌管中馈，若自己比丈夫早去世，两个儿子和其新建立的小家庭还得仰仗长嫂。
　　窦氏嫁人之后，才知道后院能悄悄恶心人的地方有多少。所以她哪怕心里不满，也要向两个儿子说郑家的好话。
　　若只有李世民在这里，可能就信了。
　　但李玄霸是不信的。
　　确实为了自家女儿，打探亲家背景为人，考验女婿才干品行，这都很正常。
　　可这次自己和二哥是临时决定来的，“考验”却肯定是提前订好的。
　　也就是说，这群家伙要考验的是自家母亲？！
　　哪家选女婿的时候不是让女婿“雀屏中选”，而是让亲家母和亲家公去射雀屏？！这不纯纯的侮辱人吗！！
　　但看着母亲竭力为郑家说好话，李玄霸知道自家大概把这门亲事看得极重，有气也只能憋着。
　　他瓮声瓮气道：“那如果我和哥太张扬，把郑家的儿子们比得一无是处，会得罪他们吗？”
　　窦氏微笑：“你俩才几岁？若他们和你们一般计较，那荥阳郑氏可就在五姓七望中抬不起头了。若是他们不考校你们就罢了，若是敢考校，你们就尽管张扬。你们若能把他家子弟全压下，他们还得捏着鼻子为你们扬名。”

　　说完，李世民摇摇头，嘴里继续嘀咕“阿玄真笨”“书读得再多也笨”。
　　李玄霸一口气闷在胸口。
　　他没有经历过这些豪门争斗，不知道不是很正常吗？才六岁就能和人玩心眼的二哥才是不正常好吗？！
　　“二郎说得有理。”窦氏颔首赞同，“三郎不用担心。”
　　李世民蹭到窦氏怀里：“娘放心，我和阿玄不会丢娘的脸。”
　　窦氏把李世民和李玄霸抱进怀里揉了揉：“娘定是放心的。还有，如果他们看你二人很厉害，悄悄遣自家小娘子和你们好，你们可千万别上当。”
　　李玄霸：“……”看来娘心底也不是没有怨气。

　　将来唐太宗的后宫里，可是有荥阳郑氏出身的贤妃。为了笼络五姓七望，可由不得你要不要。

　　李玄霸冷冷道：“不过是待价而沽。”
　　李世民好奇：“怎么个待价而沽法？”
　　李玄霸换成心声道：【哥，你知道并嫡吗？前朝有两家高门士族都把女儿送给同一个男人，生儿子争嫡长子的位置。】
　　李世民脸色一僵：“这也太匪夷所思。”
　　李玄霸：【高门士族嫁女儿还有一个‘补门第彩礼’的规矩。按照我们这种高门，门当户对的时候向来讲究厚娶厚嫁，嫁女儿的时候不仅会将彩礼充作女儿的嫁妆，还会补上一份差不多的嫁妆。】
　　李世民点头：“这个我知道。”
　　李玄霸：【高门大族会开放旁支女婿名额给门第不高，甚至出身商贾的人，让他们付出高额彩礼。高门大族会扣下大部分彩礼，其彩礼和嫁妆的差额，就是‘补门第’的钱。】
　　这种事在唐初也很普遍，唐太宗专门骂过，所以李玄霸记忆较为深刻。
　　李世民盘坐起来，挠挠头：“一个要钱，一个要名，也算一拍即合了。”
　　李玄霸：【不过高门士族的女儿“教养”确实是好。在前朝那么混乱的时代，只有他们还教育女儿三从四德，为夫守贞。就算被夫家休弃，也有许多世家女子以孤老终生为荣。有些女子还会殉节。所以很多人家都希望迎娶高门士族的女儿当当家主母。】
　　李玄霸露出讥笑的表情。乱世就是贵族也朝不保夕，这时还要教女儿守“规矩”。
　　李世民歪着头想了想：“听你这么说，他们家女儿的教养的确好。但如果我的女儿也要给夫家守什么贞，我就打她屁股！狠狠地打！”
　　李玄霸：“……我觉得女儿的屁股是不能打的。”封建时代的局限性就罢了，哥你居然是双标狗！
　　李世民叉腰：“那就打手板心！”
　　李玄霸：“你随意……”
　　“哼哼。”李世民得意洋洋地哼哼了两声，也不知道他得意什么。
　　得意完后，李世民就拉着李玄霸准备“作弊”。
　　能作弊为什么要和他们公平战斗？你看哪个带兵打仗的将军要和敌军公平战斗？
　　李世民小小年纪就运用上了兵法。
　　李玄霸也没有欺负小孩子的愧疚。
　　先撩先贱，古今真理！
　　……
　　三日后，盛装打扮的窦氏，带着同样穿金戴银珠宝架子李世民和李玄霸，前去拜访荥阳郑氏的祖宅。
　　在打扮时，窦氏和李渊出现了分歧。
　　李渊本来想让窦氏尽可能地贴近士族的穿衣风格。
　　窦氏反对道：“郎君，若论汉族士人的风雅，谁能比得过汉族世家？我若模仿她们穿戴，最后只会落得画虎不成反类犬。我们唐国公府乃是皇亲国戚，就该拿出皇室的气度。女人打扮的事，请郎君听我的。”
　　窦氏都说“女人打扮的事”了，李渊便只能听窦氏的。
　　李世民围着盛装打扮的母亲蹦蹦跳跳：“这还是我的娘娘吗？是神仙菩萨娘娘！”
　　窦氏抿嘴笑：“是，是二郎和三郎的神仙菩萨娘娘。”
　　李玄霸也震惊得说不出话来。
　　他出生这么多年，母亲就是被皇后召进宫里的时候都没有穿戴如此华丽。
　　比如那支垂着剔透红宝石珠子的镶彩宝凤簪，在阳光下反射的光芒都让他有些眼花了。
　　窦氏见李玄霸注意到她头上的流苏凤簪。她微笑着扶了一下凤簪，脸上露出怀念的神色：“这是舅父舅母送给我的嫁妆，用来应付郑氏足够了。”
　　李渊原本看着盛装打扮后风姿绰约的夫人眼神都直了，听了窦氏这句话后，他立刻皱眉道：“夫人，不是说好了不要再提他们？”
　　窦氏立刻垂眸道：“只是顺口和二郎三郎说一下凤簪来历，一时说漏了嘴，以后会注意。”
　　李渊加重语气道：“一定要注意。”
　　窦氏道：“是，郎君安心。”
　　李世民不明白为何父亲要训斥母亲，正想询问，被李玄霸拉住手。
　　李玄霸：【外祖母是北周襄阳长公主，娘的舅父舅母，就是北周武帝和武德皇后。】
　　李世民眨了眨眼睛，神色未变，仿佛没听到李玄霸的话似的，只是捏了一下李玄霸拉着他的手，表示自己听到了。
　　李玄霸在心底叹了口气。
　　母亲自幼被北周武帝宇文邕接在宫里教养，比所有外甥都得宠。宇文邕暴毙北征路上时，母亲悲伤至极，仿若失去了亲生父亲。
　　后来隋文帝篡北周，并杀掉了宇文家族所有直系男丁，母亲哭泣“恨我不为男，以救舅氏之难”。
　　这话现在应该还未传出来，应是唐朝建立后才从窦家人或者李渊口中传出的。
　　其实李玄霸猜测，外公外婆和舅舅的去世，也和隋文帝有关系。
　　虽然窦氏还有娘家，但这娘家是指“窦氏”一族。
　　窦氏如今仍旧还是名门望族，在隋朝从中央到地方都任大官，十分显赫。但窦氏的父母兄弟，已经全部去世。
　　窦氏的长兄窦文殊在北周伐齐时战死，三兄窦照在隋代北周前去世，暂且不提。
　　窦氏的父亲窦毅在隋朝虽拜定州总管，隋文帝常常说非常信任窦毅，但窦毅在隋文帝篡北周的第二年就故去了。
　　襄阳长公主也同年去世。
　　而在他们去世的前一年，隋朝刚改朝换代，外祖父和外祖母就急匆匆让才十一二岁的母亲和父亲完婚。
　　更巧的是，窦氏仅剩的兄弟窦招贤刚袭了神武公没多久，也突然病逝。
　　北周武帝的遗孀武德皇后，也与李玄霸的外公外婆同卒于开皇二年。

　　武德皇后身为当时还没分裂的突厥可汗的女儿，嫁妆极其丰厚，全是从现在还未畅通的丝绸之路彼端运来的珠宝香料兽皮。

　　郑家开了侧门来迎接窦氏。

　　虽开侧门也不算不礼貌，但如果对自己母亲这个未来的亲家母稍稍更敬重一些，开个正门也不算违反规矩。
　　这就只是看郑家人想不想了。
　　还好郑家人也没有太矜持。待窦氏下马车时，郑家辈分与窦氏同辈的宗妇已经在马车停靠处等着迎接窦氏。
　　她看着窦氏的马车，脸色有点僵。
　　人是不是有点多？
　　窦氏没有立刻下马车。
　　她后面的马车车门先打开，出来一群身着绸缎的小厮婢女。
　　小厮在地面铺上绸缎，婢女打起遮阳的伞，又在马车下放好绣墩，窦氏所乘坐的马车车门才打开。
　　两个孩子先踩着绣墩下马车，然后一左一右齐齐伸手。
　　窦氏虚扶着两个孩子的手，踩着绣墩走下了马车。
　　长长的曳地裙落在了铺着绸缎的地上。曳地裙下，窦氏那一双缀着东珠的绣花鞋只露出了半个脚尖。
　　窦氏仰起头，对前来迎接她的郑家的女眷露出雍容又和蔼的微笑。
　　她仰头时，云鬓间的镶彩宝金凤微微一颤，吐露的红色流苏擦过乌黑的发梢，狠狠闪了一下郑家女眷的眼睛。
　　郑家也是豪富，本不应该羡慕窦氏。
　　但郑家的女眷皆是出自高门大族，所以她们很有眼力，一眼就看出了窦氏所戴所穿，皆是宫廷御用。
　　特别是这一支发簪，应是皇后规格，连公主没有特别允许都不能佩戴。
　　窦氏这一身穿金戴银虽庸俗了一些，但一身金银珠宝绫罗绸缎皆是宫廷御用，她们就不好说庸俗了。
　　郑家宗妇笑道：“早听闻唐国公夫人贵气，这一身……真是百闻不如一见。”
　　窦氏温婉道：“母亲乃是文献皇后长姊，家中一应用具皆是宫中所赐。唐国公府节省，很少置办新首饰，便只能用些赏赐的物事勉强装点。让夫人见笑了。”
　　郑家宗妇立刻敛容：“怪不得。”
　　窦氏搭在李世民手中的右手抬起，轻轻扶了一下额间花朵：“只这朵花钿，是二郎和三郎仿古籍中的花钿亲手为我做之。”
　　郑家女眷立刻齐齐把视线投向窦氏身侧的两个孩子。
　　李世民和李玄霸不由自主挺起了胸脯。
chunks.englishText:
**Chapter 9: Adorning Mother's Brow with a Floral Decal**

When Lady Dou went to tell Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to prepare themselves for their visit to the Zheng family, Li Shimin was lying prone on a low couch. Li Xuanba was sitting cross-legged, using Li Shimin as a backrest, and the two of them were flipping through the *Book of Jin* together.

The version of the *Book of Jin* they were reading was compiled by Shen Yue of the Southern Liang Dynasty. In addition to the *Book of Jin*, Li Shimin had also piled up the histories of the Song, Qi, and Liang dynasties—likewise compiled by Shen Yue—under his chest and chin to make himself more comfortable as he lay there.

For ordinary six-year-olds, reading history books was far too premature.

Although Li Shimin already knew many characters, he normally lacked the patience to tackle unpunctuated history books directly.

When Li Xuanba had previously explained the "Five Surnames and Seven Clans" to him, he had not really understood.

For instance, Li Shimin had never heard of "Jia Nanfeng," the "Rebellion of the Eight Princes," the "Disaster of Yongjia," or the "Disaster of the National History."

It was only after Li Xuanba mentioned the "Five Surnames and Seven Clans" that he suddenly became interested, prompting him to flip through the history books to read about the extermination of noble families during the Wei and Jin dynasties.

Li Xuanba had originally thought his second brother understood everything he said, because his second brother always acted as though he knew it all.

It was only when they arrived at Li Yuan's place and Li Shimin brought over the histories of the Jin, Song, Qi, and Liang dynasties from Li Yuan's study to teach himself with a frown that Li Xuanba realized his second brother had a habit of putting on a brave face and refusing to admit defeat.

*If you didn't know, you could have just told me, and I would have explained it to you,* Li Xuanba grumbled inwardly.

But Li Shimin refused. He insisted on flipping through the books and learning it himself.

Li Xuanba did not expose his second brother and simply read along with him.

Shen Yue's *Book of Jin* was lost to history in later generations. The version passed down to posterity was compiled by Xu Jingzong and Fang Xuanling, known to some as the "Magic Book of Jin"—a highly entertaining collection of fantasy stories, practically the historical version of *In Search of the Supernatural*.

Shen Yue's *Book of Song* was also included in the *Twenty-Four Histories*, though its level of fantasy was slightly more grounded than the "Magic Book of Jin."

But Shen Yue had a major flaw: he came from the Shen clan of Wuxing, and the Southern Dynasties had inherited the Eastern Jin's obsession with noble lineages. As a result, half of his *Book of Song* consisted of biographies of high-ranking noble clans, filled with wild boasting and exaggeration.

For example, the biography of Wang Wei of Langya consisted entirely of letters Wang Wei had written to his friends. Anyone who didn't know better would think it was Wang Wei's collected works.

Shen Yue's *Book of Jin* suffered from the same flaw.

The version from the Zhenguan era was the "Magic Book of Jin," while Shen Yue's was the "Book of Jin: Biographies of High Clans," which complemented each other. If the two of them wanted to understand the noble clans since the Wei and Jin dynasties, Shen Yue's books were perfect.

Thanks to Li Xuanba's advance warnings, when Li Shimin read Shen Yue's boasts about the noble clans, he did so with a critical and amused mindset, occasionally turning around to complain to his younger brother.

When Lady Dou walked in, she happened to hear Li Shimin telling Li Xuanba a dark joke: "Every time there was a rebellion in the Wei, Jin, Southern, and Northern Dynasties, the noble clans were slaughtered to the last man. Maybe their descendants today are actually the descendants of their mortal enemies."

Half-amused and half-exasperated, Lady Dou stepped forward and delivered two sharp slaps to the prone Li Shimin's buttocks.

"Don't talk nonsense. We are going to be guests at the Zheng family's home in three days. Don't say the wrong thing," Lady Dou scolded, feigning anger. "The descendants of those great clans all have genealogies as proof. How could they be fake?"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba simultaneously put on obedient, innocent faces.

Lady Dou was helpless. At times like this, the brothers, despite their vastly different personalities, truly looked like twins.

"During this visit, the elders of the Zheng family might test your learning. Read the *Analects* a few more times," Lady Dou said. "And the *Thousand Character Classic* as well. Even though you learned it long ago, they might ask you to recite it from memory. Review it a few more times."

Before Li Shimin could react, Li Xuanba's face fell.

He said crossly, "I've never heard of a host testing and quizzing guest children when they visit. What, does the Zheng family want to use my brother's and my abilities to gauge our eldest brother's talent?"

Lady Dou explained with a smile, "Marriage is a lifelong matter. It is not wrong for them to be a little cautious."

Although Lady Dou felt uncomfortable about it herself, she would not say so to her sons.

For the sake of one's daughter, things like "winning the screen" were normal. The Zheng family was just taking it too far. In the future, the Zheng clan of Xingyang would be in-laws with the Duke of Tang's estate, and Lady Dou did not want her two sons to have bad blood with them.

Furthermore, once the young lady of the Zheng family married into the Duke of Tang's estate, she would manage the household affairs. If Lady Dou passed away before her husband, her two sons and their future families would still have to rely on their eldest sister-in-law.

Only after getting married did Lady Dou realize how many subtle ways there were to make someone's life miserable in the inner courtyard. Therefore, even if she was dissatisfied in her heart, she still spoke well of the Zheng family to her two sons.

If only Li Shimin were here, he might have believed her.

But Li Xuanba did not.

It was indeed normal to investigate the background and character of the in-laws and test the son-in-law's talent and conduct for the sake of one's daughter.

But his and his second brother's arrival this time was a last-minute decision, yet the "test" was definitely planned in advance.

In other words, the person these fellows wanted to test was actually their mother?!

When choosing a son-in-law, who doesn't have the son-in-law "win the screen," but instead makes the mother-in-law and father-in-law do it?! Isn't this a pure insult?!

But seeing his mother trying her best to speak well of the Zheng family, Li Xuanba knew his family probably valued this marriage alliance extremely highly. He could only swallow his anger.

He said in a muffled voice, "Then what if my brother and I are too outstanding and make the Zheng family's sons look completely useless? Will we offend them?"

Lady Dou smiled. "How old are you two? If they lower themselves to bicker with you, the Zheng clan of Xingyang won't be able to hold their heads up among the Five Surnames and Seven Clans. If they don't test you, so be it. But if they dare to, you should show off as much as you like. If you can suppress all the children of their family, they will have to swallow their pride and sing your praises to save face."

Li Xuanba frowned. "Are they that magnanimous?"

Li Shimin said with mock gravity, "Ah Xuan, you are so foolish. How is that being magnanimous? There is no wall in the world that doesn't leak wind. The news of us crushing the Zheng family's children cannot be hidden. They will naturally praise us to the skies to show that their defeat was justified. In my opinion, they might even want to kill us with praise, instigating the children of other noble clans to 'besiege' us brothers."

After saying that, Li Shimin shook his head, continuing to mutter, "Ah Xuan is so foolish," "No matter how many books he reads, he's still foolish."

Li Xuanba felt a wave of frustration rise in his chest.

He had never experienced these noble family power struggles. Wasn't it normal for him not to know? His second brother, who was only six years old but could already play mind games with people, was the abnormal one, okay?!

"Erlang is right," Lady Dou nodded in agreement. "Sanlang, you don't need to worry."

Li Shimin snuggled into Lady Dou's arms. "Don't worry, Mother. Ah Xuan and I won't embarrass you."

Lady Dou pulled Li Shimin and Li Xuanba into her arms and ruffled them. "Mother is naturally at ease. Also, if they see how remarkable you two are and secretly send their young ladies to cozy up to you, you must absolutely not fall for it."

Li Xuanba: "..." It seemed Mother wasn't entirely without resentment in her heart.

Li Shimin snorted coldly. "They look down on us, and I look down on them. I won't like any young lady of the Zheng family."

Li Xuanba glanced at his second brother.

In the future, Emperor Taizong's imperial harem would indeed include a Virtuous Consort from the Zheng clan of Xingyang. To win over the Five Surnames and Seven Clans, it wouldn't be up to him whether he wanted her or not.

However, the Zheng clan's shift from haughty to subservient—first being incredibly picky even about the position of the primary wife of the Duke of Tang's estate, and later eagerly sending their daughter into the palace to serve as a consort—was indeed quite amusing.

Lady Dou had dressed very simply for her trip to Xingyang.

To uphold the prestige of the Duke of Tang's estate at the Zheng family's home, Lady Dou had specially ordered people to rush new clothes and jewelry from the Duke's estate by fast horse, which would arrive in a day or two.

In addition, she needed to procure some local jewelry, clothing, rouge, and powder. There were some in Li Yuan's official residence, but Lady Dou had to have her servants alter them.

Thus, after telling her two sons to review well, Lady Dou left in a hurry.

Li Shimin leaned back over his books. "Are the daughters of noble clans really that precious? Even our Duke of Tang's estate has to humble itself?"

Li Xuanba said coldly, "They are merely waiting for the highest bidder."

Li Shimin was curious. "How so?"

Li Xuanba switched to his inner voice: *[Brother, do you know about "co-primary wives"? In the previous dynasty, two noble clans sent their daughters to the same man, and they gave birth to sons who fought for the position of the legitimate eldest son.]*

Li Shimin's face stiffened. "That is too bizarre."

Li Xuanba: *[The noble clans also have a rule of "supplementing the family status with betrothal gifts." For noble families like ours, when the status is equal, we always emphasize lavish marriages from both sides. When marrying off a daughter, not only will the betrothal gifts be used as her dowry, but a comparable dowry of their own will also be added.]*

Li Shimin nodded. "I know this."

Li Xuanba: *[But the great noble clans will open up slots for branch-family sons-in-law to men of lower status, or even merchants, demanding exorbitant betrothal gifts. The noble clans will keep most of the betrothal gifts, and the difference between the betrothal gifts and the dowry is the money paid to "supplement their family status."]*

This practice was very common in the early Tang Dynasty, and Emperor Taizong had specifically condemned it, which was why Li Xuanba remembered it so clearly.

Li Shimin sat up and scratched his head. "One wants money, the other wants prestige. I suppose they hit it off."

Li Xuanba: *[However, the "upbringing" of the daughters of noble clans is indeed excellent. In such a chaotic era as the previous dynasty, only they still educated their daughters in the Three Obediences and Four Virtues, and to remain chaste for their husbands. Even if they were divorced by their husband's family, many noblewomen took pride in spending the rest of their lives alone. Some would even commit suicide to preserve their chastity.]*

Li Xuanba sneered. In a chaotic world, even nobles could barely survive, yet they still taught their daughters to follow "rules."

Li Shimin tilted his head and thought. "Hearing you say that, their daughters' upbringing is indeed good. But if my daughter ever tries to keep some chastity for her husband's family like that, I'll spank her! Hard!"

Li Xuanba: "...I don't think you should spank a daughter's buttocks." The limitations of the feudal era aside, brother, you are such a double-standard hypocrite!

Li Shimin put his hands on his hips. "Then I'll slap her palms!"

Li Xuanba: "Suit yourself..."

"Hmph, hmph." Li Shimin snorted triumphantly, though no one knew what he was so proud of.

After gloating, Li Shimin pulled Li Xuanba to prepare to "cheat."

Why fight them fairly when they could cheat? Had anyone ever seen a general leading troops into battle insist on fighting the enemy fairly?

Even at a young age, Li Shimin was already applying the art of war.

Li Xuanba felt no guilt about bullying children either.

The one who provokes first is the contemptible one—a truth for all ages!

...

Three days later, Lady Dou, dressed in her finest, led Li Shimin and Li Xuanba—who were also decked out in gold and silver like walking jewelry racks—to visit the ancestral residence of the Zheng clan of Xingyang.

When they were dressing, Lady Dou and Li Yuan had a disagreement.

Li Yuan originally wanted Lady Dou to dress as closely as possible to the style of the noble clans.

Lady Dou objected, "My Lord, when it comes to the elegance of Han scholars, who can compare to the Han noble clans? If I try to imitate their style, I will only end up looking like a tiger drawn as a dog. Our Duke of Tang's estate is of imperial kin; we should display the dignity of the imperial family. In matters of women's dress, please listen to me, My Lord."

Since Lady Dou had framed it as "matters of women's dress," Li Yuan could only yield to her.

Li Shimin bounced around his splendidly dressed mother. "Is this still my mother? You look like a divine bodhisattva!"

Lady Dou smiled. "Yes, yes, the divine bodhisattva of Erlang and Sanlang."

Li Xuanba was also too stunned for words.

In all his years since birth, his mother had never dressed so magnificently, not even when she was summoned to the palace by the Empress.

For instance, the gold phoenix hairpin inlaid with colorful gems, from which hung translucent ruby beads, reflected the sunlight so brightly that it slightly dazed him.

Seeing Li Xuanba notice the dangling phoenix hairpin on her head, Lady Dou smiled and gently adjusted it, a look of reminiscence appearing on her face. "This was part of the dowry given to me by my uncle and aunt. It is more than enough to deal with the Zheng family."

Li Yuan, who had been staring blankly at his splendidly dressed and graceful wife, immediately frowned upon hearing this. "My lady, didn't we agree not to mention them again?"

Lady Dou immediately lowered her eyes. "I was just casually telling Erlang and Sanlang about the origin of the phoenix hairpin. It was a slip of the tongue. I will be careful in the future."

Li Yuan said with emphasis, "You must be careful."

Lady Dou said, "Yes, My Lord, rest assured."

Li Shimin didn't understand why his father was scolding his mother. Just as he was about to ask, Li Xuanba pulled his hand.

Li Xuanba: *[Our maternal grandmother was Grand Princess Xiangyang of Northern Zhou. Mother's uncle and aunt were Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou and Empress Wude.]*

Li Shimin blinked, his expression unchanged, as if he hadn't heard Li Xuanba's words. He merely squeezed Li Xuanba's hand to show he understood.

Li Xuanba sighed in his heart.

His mother had been raised in the palace by Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, Yuwen Yong, since childhood, and was more favored than any of his other nieces and nephews. When Yuwen Yong died suddenly on the northern expedition, his mother was devastated, as if she had lost her own father.

Later, when Emperor Wen of Sui usurped the Northern Zhou throne and slaughtered all the direct male descendants of the Yuwen family, his mother wept, saying, "I regret that I am not a man, to save my uncle's family from this disaster."

These words probably hadn't spread yet; they would likely be passed down by the Dou family or Li Yuan after the Tang Dynasty was established.

In fact, Li Xuanba suspected that the deaths of his maternal grandparents and uncles were also related to Emperor Wen of Sui.

Although Lady Dou still had her maternal family, this "maternal family" referred to the Dou clan as a whole.

The Dou clan was still a prominent and noble family, holding high offices from the central government to the local levels in the Sui Dynasty, and was highly illustrious. However, Lady Dou's parents and brothers had all passed away.

Lady Dou's eldest brother, Dou Wenshu, died in battle when Northern Zhou attacked Qi. Her third brother, Dou Zhao, died before Sui replaced Northern Zhou, so they could be set aside.

Although Lady Dou's father, Dou Yi, was appointed Commander-General of Dingzhou in the Sui Dynasty, and Emperor Wen of Sui often claimed to trust him deeply, Dou Yi passed away in the second year after Emperor Wen usurped the Northern Zhou throne.

Princess Xiangyang also passed away in the same year.

And in the year before their deaths, just as the Sui Dynasty had changed regimes, her maternal grandparents had hurriedly married off their mother, who was only eleven or twelve, to their father.

Even more coincidentally, Lady Dou's only remaining brother, Dou Zhaoxian, died suddenly of illness not long after inheriting the title of Duke of Shenwu.

Empress Wude, the widow of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, also died in the second year of Kaihuang, the same year as Li Xuanba's maternal grandparents.

Empress Wude of Northern Zhou was the daughter of the Tujue Khagan and had once been neglected by Emperor Wu. Lady Dou had advised her uncle to treat her aunt generously to appease the Tujue. Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou followed his niece's advice, which was why he became friendly toward Empress Wude. Empress Wude was extremely grateful to and fond of Lady Dou. Having no children of her own with Emperor Wu, she regarded Lady Dou as her own daughter, and Lady Dou was very close to her aunt.

Although there was no evidence that Emperor Wen of Sui had a hand in it, and perhaps they all died of illness out of fear because Emperor Wen slaughtered the entire Yuwen imperial family, looking at it from the conspiratorial perspective of a modern person, dying of fear could also be considered a form of being hounded to death, right?

As the daughter of the Tujue Khagan before the khaganate split, Empress Wude's dowry was extremely lavish, consisting entirely of jewelry, spices, and animal pelts transported from the other side of the Silk Road, which was not yet fully open.

Empress Wude left her entire dowry to Lady Dou.

Emperor Wen of Sui and Empress Dugu did not lay a hand on Empress Wude's dowry and even generously added more to it for Lady Dou.

Therefore, although Lady Dou had no close living relatives of her generation, her dowry was so immense that even princesses could not compare.

People had originally mocked Li Yuan for "winning the screen" only to marry an orphaned girl.

But when they saw Lady Dou's dowry, and the Dou clan stepped forward to back her, declaring that the entire clan was her maternal family, the mockery turned to envy.

Li Xuanba felt that if his maternal grandparents and uncles were still alive, perhaps seeing his mother's life in the Duke of Tang's estate, they would praise her virtue and filial piety to outsiders while privately comforting her.

Li Xuanba also knew that his mother, who had suddenly gone from being a favored daughter of heaven to an orphan in the second year of Kaihuang, must harbor resentment toward Emperor Wen of Sui.

His father probably knew this too, which was why he forbade his mother from mentioning Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou again.

The matters involved were complex and serious, not something two children like Li Shimin and Li Xuanba could butt into.

They could only watch as their father scolded their mother a few more times, stopping only when her eyes turned slightly red.

The originally cheerful atmosphere of the family's departure turned somber.

Li Yuan had official duties, so Lady Dou took the two children to visit the Zheng family alone.

It wasn't that Li Yuan was unwilling to take leave to accompany them, but rather that the Zheng family wanted Lady Dou to come alone.

This was probably also part of the "test."

Li Shimin stuck his head out of the carriage window, waved goodbye to his father, and said to his mother, "Mother, I will definitely make you proud!"

Lady Dou took out a small silver mirror to touch up the makeup around her eyes, her elegant and gentle smile already restored. "Good."

Li Xuanba's fingers twitched inside his sleeve.

Originally, after he and his second brother made this flower together, they saw Li Yuan drawing their mother's eyebrows and felt too embarrassed to bring it out and disturb their parents.

He took a deep breath and pulled a small box from his sleeve. "Mother, if you paste this between your brows, it will look even more beautiful than cinnabar."

Li Shimin immediately said, "Ah Xuan and I made it! Ah Xuan was too embarrassed to bring it out earlier. Hmph, but he brought it out anyway."

Lady Dou smiled. "Let Mother see."

She opened the small box. Inside was a translucent lotus flower.

Lady Dou was surprised. "How beautiful! What is it made of?!"

Li Shimin covered his mouth and laughed. "Ah Xuan and I caught dragonflies in the courtyard and dyed their wings to make it. While Ah Xuan was catching them, he kept saying how cruel we were. Pfft."

Li Xuanba said solemnly, "It was indeed cruel."

Then he whispered, "But it is indeed beautiful."

Lady Dou smiled. "Do I paste it directly between my brows, like a yellow floral decal?"

The practice of applying yellow floral decals had existed since ancient times, where women painted their foreheads golden-yellow or pasted golden petals on them. However, this was generally the adornment of unmarried daughters.

Li Xuanba said, "Legend has it that Princess Shouyang of the Southern Dynasties once adorned her brow with plum blossoms, calling it a *huadian*. In fact, women decorated themselves with *huadian* as early as the pre-Qin period, though it is no longer popular now."

Li Shimin hugged Lady Dou's arm and said in a sweet voice, "Mother is the most beautiful. Once Mother wears the *huadian*, it will become popular again, and then Ah Xuan and I can sell them in a shop. That's what Ah Xuan said!"

Li Xuanba froze, then said in embarrassed anger, "I was only joking!"

Li Shimin mocked, "You said it yourself! You dare to say it but don't dare to admit it. Ah Xuan is not a real man."

Lady Dou burst out laughing. "Alright, alright, Mother will help you sell them. Do I use water to paste it?"

Li Xuanba glared at Li Shimin first, then took out a box of transparent bone glue. "Use this today. It's more secure and won't fall off."

Lady Dou lowered her head, and Li Xuanba carefully pasted the *huadian* onto her forehead.

He and Li Shimin had ruined many dragonflies to paste together a layered, three-dimensional effect.

Li Shimin pulled open the carriage curtain, letting the sunlight reflect off his mother's brow. "Mother! The *huadian* is glowing! It's so beautiful!"

Looking at the beautiful flower on her forehead in the silver mirror, Lady Dou smiled. "Yes, it is indeed beautiful."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba exchanged a look.

Li Xuanba: *[Mother is finally happy.]*

Li Shimin gave Li Xuanba a thumbs-up. This was the gesture of praise his younger brother had taught him.

Seeing the two children exchanging glances, Lady Dou's smile grew even brighter.

To have such sons was enough for a mother.

...

The Zheng family opened their side gate to welcome Lady Dou.

If Li Yuan had come, they would have opened the main gate. Lady Dou was only a woman of the inner courtyard, so they were more reserved.

Lady Dou didn't think much of it, but Li Shimin and Li Xuanba both darkened their faces.

Although opening the side gate wasn't considered impolite, if they had shown a bit more respect to their mother, the future mother-in-law, opening the main gate wouldn't have violated any rules.

It was simply a matter of whether the Zheng family wanted to or not.

Fortunately, the Zheng family wasn't too aloof. When Lady Dou stepped down from the carriage, a noblewoman of the Zheng family of the same generation was already waiting at the carriage stop to welcome her.

As she looked at Lady Dou's carriage, her expression stiffened slightly.

Weren't there a bit too many people?

Lady Dou did not alight immediately.

The door of the carriage behind hers opened first, and a crowd of servants and maids dressed in silk stepped out.

The servants laid silk fabric on the ground, the maids held up sunshades, and an embroidered footstool was placed beneath the carriage before the door of Lady Dou's carriage finally opened.

The two children stepped onto the footstool first to alight, then reached out their hands in unison, one on each side.

Lady Dou lightly rested her hands on the children's hands and stepped down from the carriage onto the footstool.

Her long, trailing skirt fell onto the silk-covered ground. Beneath the skirt, only the tips of Lady Dou's embroidered shoes, adorned with Eastern pearls, were visible.

Lady Dou raised her head and offered a graceful and gentle smile to the Zheng family's female relatives who had come to welcome her.

As she raised her head, the gold phoenix hairpin inlaid with colorful gems in her high bun trembled slightly, its dangling red tassels brushing past her dark hair, dazzling the eyes of the Zheng family's women.

The Zheng family was also immensely wealthy and shouldn't have envied Lady Dou.

However, the women of the Zheng family all came from prominent clans, so they had keen eyes. They could tell at a glance that everything Lady Dou wore was for imperial court use.

Especially that hairpin; it was of the Empress's specifications, something even princesses could not wear without special permission.

Although Lady Dou's attire of gold and silver was somewhat ostentatious, since every piece of jewelry and silk was for imperial use, they could hardly call it vulgar.

The Zheng family's noblewoman smiled. "I have long heard of the Duchess of Tang's nobility. This attire... indeed, seeing is believing."

Lady Dou said gently, "My mother was the elder sister of Empress Wenxian. All the household items in our estate were bestowed by the palace. The Duke of Tang's estate is frugal and rarely procures new jewelry, so I can only use these bestowed items to barely adorn myself. I have made a fool of myself before you, Madam."

The Zheng family's noblewoman immediately turned solemn. "No wonder."

Lady Dou raised her right hand, which had been resting on Li Shimin's, and gently touched the flower on her forehead. "Only this *huadian* was handmade for me by Erlang and Sanlang, who imitated the designs in ancient texts."

The women of the Zheng family immediately turned their gazes to the two children beside Lady Dou.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba puffed out their chests in unison.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第10章 不如玩个小游戏
chunks.chineseText:
第10章 不如玩个小游戏

=
　　李世民和李玄霸是一对同卵双胞胎，他们二人的长相应该是一模一样。
　　但无奈李世民身强体壮，李玄霸自幼病弱，所以李世民包括五官在内，都比李玄霸大上一圈。
　　再者李世民脸上总带着开朗的笑容，眼眸大而明亮；李玄霸平时眼睛总是微眯着，嘴也紧紧抿着，李世民老说他“阿玄不是发呆就是犯困”。
　　这太过明显的气质和身材差别，导致两人站在一起时，如果不特意去观察他们二人的五官，竟然难以发现他们居然是一对双生子。
　　郑家女眷仔细观察后，才开始感叹神奇，言语间终于透出了些许羡慕。
　　双生子这样的祥瑞太重，可不是一般人家能消受得起的。唐国公夫人真是富重之人，令人艳羡。
　　窦氏见众人将注意力转移到一双孩子身上，微微抿嘴一笑，不再提衣衫配饰之类的事，只不断夸李世民和李玄霸。
　　李世民竖起耳朵，听母亲把他和阿玄以前做的调皮事一件一件挑出来闲聊，脸上表情越发得意。
　　李玄霸无奈：【哥，娘这是在嘲笑我们二人以前调皮，你有什么好得意？】
　　李世民瞥了李玄霸一眼，继续得意。
　　就是很得意，你不服，你也得意啊。
　　李玄霸继续在心里叨叨：【好无聊，好困，好累，她们就这样让我们两个小短腿走着去内院？】
　　李世民停下脚步。
　　窦氏疑惑：“怎么了，二郎？”
　　李世民走到李玄霸身前，蹲下道：“上来。”
　　李玄霸本来想说不用，扫见周围人好奇的神色，便顺势趴在了二哥的背上。
　　李世民站起身，颠了颠背上的弟弟：“唉，阿玄，你该多吃些，怎么还是这么轻。娘，我们继续走吧。”
　　窦氏焦急道：“三郎累了？怎么不和娘说？”
　　李世民笑道：“阿玄不是累了，就是犯懒。这么多外人在，若让娘或者奴仆抱着阿玄走，那太不礼貌了。我也是小孩，诸位长辈应该不会计较我爱护阿玄。”
　　李玄霸道：“马车上颠簸太久，我年幼，实在是腿疼，各位恕罪。”
　　说完，他十分坦然地靠在二哥背上打瞌睡。
　　郑家宗妇脸上闪过一丝尴尬。
　　去内院的路其实没有这么远。只是她之前与郎君和长辈商议，要让唐国公夫人看看荥阳郑氏祖宅的底蕴，所以绕了些远路，让唐国公夫人把祖宅中最漂亮的几个园子逛一逛。
　　这其实是好意。
　　郑家迎接其他客人时也会稍稍绕一绕，让客人观赏郑家祖宅的美景。
　　客人一般都会对沿路美景赞不绝口，有些有才华的人还会留下墨宝，然后郑家人将墨宝悬挂在亭台阁楼上，又能成为下一个客人眼中的美景。
　　郑家宗妇领着女眷簇拥着唐国公夫人逛园子，沿路指指点点，这个楼阁有谁题诗题字，这丛花木又有怎样的雅事流传，既展现了郑家的底蕴，也拉近了和唐国公夫人的距离，应该是两全的事。
　　但现在李玄霸和李世民这一番做法，却似乎责怪郑家待客不周——唐国公夫人带着两个幼子来做客，之前在马车上已经颠簸了一个多时辰，你还带着人绕远路，看，人家孩子都走不动了。
　　窦氏原本以为进来的门和要赴宴的地方真的就这么远。
　　她毕竟是在皇宫里长大，出嫁后因隋文帝和独孤皇后喜爱李渊的缘故，她也常常入宫讨好独孤皇后，从小到大所见的皇家园林十分雄伟，所以还真没发现郑家女眷正带着她绕远路。
　　待看到郑家宗妇眼底尴尬的神色时，她念头一转，才发觉了郑家人的心思。
　　窦氏没拆穿郑家宗妇，而是低着头对李玄霸道歉：“是娘没注意到。还是让娘来抱吧。你二人年幼，不会有人责怪你们。”
　　李世民摇头：“娘的力气还不如我，走啦走啦。”
　　李世民背着李玄霸蹦跳了一下，还围着窦氏跑了一圈：“看，我背着弟弟也速度飞快。娘，别担心。”
　　李玄霸懒洋洋道：“娘，就让哥背我吧。若娘来抱我，我肯定会不好意思，就只能自己走路了。”
　　窦氏被逗笑了。
　　她对郑家宗妇道：“我两个孩子顽劣，让你们见笑了。”
　　郑家宗妇赶紧道：“二郎友悌幼弟，怎能叫顽劣？”
　　她赶紧换了一条近路。
　　郑家是结亲，不是结仇。虽然嫁女前要把架子端高一些，但私下还是要安抚好亲家的情绪。
　　加快脚步时，郑家宗妇忍不住多看了李世民和李玄霸几眼。
　　她有些狐疑，这两个孩子是真的累了，还是不满自己在绕路？或者是想在郑家刷友悌的名声？
　　李世民没有自我吹嘘，他的身体确实强壮。又走了小半炷香的时间，来到一处石榴林前时，李世民还能蹦蹦跳跳，丝毫没感觉到累。
　　此时初夏，正是石榴花开时节。
　　绿枝红花，环绕着一汪有活水注入的池塘。一座白玉桥横跨潺潺流水之上，通向一处位于池塘正中间的高台。
　　高台已经被绢丝帷幕环绕，里面影影绰绰，看不清有多少人影，只有丝竹乐声隐隐传来。
　　窦氏一看池中高台上用作帷幕的薄绢，心头陡然一紧又一松。
　　之前李渊专门拿着江南产的绢，想为李世民和李玄霸赶做两个罩衣。
　　李渊炫耀，这绢千金难买，他还是托人才拿到。去郑家做客，正好给两个孩子做遮阳避蚊的罩衣。
　　但窦氏认为，高门士族彼此同气连枝。北方高门世家也有许多旁支在南方。自己认为江南稀罕的事物，说不定高门士族随手可得。
　　所以李世民和李玄霸现在身上衣物，也都是宫廷御赐布料。不说布料质量如何，布料上的花纹只有宫中能用，以彰显其御赐的来历。
　　果然，郑氏豪富，就算唐国公府也难以匹敌。
　　若是两个孩子做罩衣的布料，正好是郑家用来罩台子的布料，那真是没脸了。
　　郑家不知道李渊托人去江南拿了些南方流行的绢布，这只是巧合而已。
　　“唐国公夫人喜欢这些帐子？”郑家宗妇殷勤道，“这是江南现在正流行的碧罗纱，十分轻薄，是江南高门士族如今最爱的糊窗户的料子。”
　　糊窗户的料子……窦氏神色未动，道：“确实喜欢。二郎三郎不耐暑热，窗户又要避光又要透气，选了许多绢布都不合意。不愧是江南水乡，若要隔闷热，糊窗户的料子还是得去江南找啊。”
　　郑家宗妇点头：“是这个理。”
　　李世民不满道：“娘，是三郎不耐暑热，不是我。”
　　李玄霸没好气道：“行，你耐暑热，下次睡觉别把我当竹枕。”
　　李世民道：“那可不行。我不是把你当竹枕，是你体温太凉，哥哥替你暖手脚。”
　　见两个孩子丝毫不怕生，竟在这么多陌生人面前你一言我一语地争执起来，众人皆忍俊不禁。
　　窦氏捏着帕子掩嘴笑道：“行，下次娘给二郎一个竹枕，给三郎一个暖炉，让你们分开睡。”
　　李玄霸：“好。”
　　李世民：“绝不！我要保护阿玄！”
　　李世民瞪大眼睛，不敢置信地回头看着背上的弟弟：“阿玄！”
　　别说窦氏忍不住了，其他女眷皆笑得花枝乱颤。
　　李世民疑惑。笑什么笑？这有什么好笑？
　　听着这里的笑声，一位老夫人拄着拐杖从帘子中走出来。
　　“哎哟我瞧瞧，这是哪里的菩萨和神仙童子来了？”老夫人笑道。
　　窦氏因有诰命在身，没有福身下拜，只双手交握胸前，叉手一礼：“崔老夫人可别笑话我了。”
　　李玄霸拍了拍二哥的后脑勺，让李世民把他放下来。
　　兄弟二人拱手长揖行礼。
　　“好孩子，都是好孩子。”崔老夫人笑着亲自弯腰把两个孩子扶起来，“阿婆这里没什么好东西，送你们两个长命锁玩。”
　　两个美貌丫鬟端着托盘上前，托盘上是两个用红绳系着的一模一样金镶玉长命锁。
　　崔老夫人取下长命锁，递给李世民和李玄霸。
　　李玄霸习惯性地把自己手中的长命锁挂李世民脖子上。
　　李世民道：“阿玄，你做什么？”
　　李玄霸道：“哦，就顺手……给我。”
　　李玄霸抢了李世民手中的长命锁，挂在了自己脖子上。
　　两个孩子这小动作，看得崔老夫人笑得合不拢嘴。
　　“夫人的孩子如此友爱，真是令人羡慕。”崔老夫人笑道。
　　窦氏没有谦虚，她微笑应道：“有这样的孩子，我也认为此生很是幸运。”
　　崔老夫人引着窦氏和两个孩子进入帷幕中。
　　帷幕中俱是年老的妇人和未束发的孩童，除了几个还未束发的男童之外，没有其他异性。
　　窦氏先将视线扫过几个行礼的女童，然后笑着让仆从也端来匣子，无论男女，赠送之物皆是镶嵌彩宝的佛牌，让孩子们自己挑选。
　　“都是开过光的，讨个吉利而已。”窦氏笑道。
　　但郑家的孩子都未动。
　　直到崔老夫人对他们点头，才有最年长的孩子接过匣子。看样子，是要私下分配。
　　崔老夫人笑道：“孩子们都活泼，恐怕是不耐烦和我们这些长辈相处。”
　　她对最年长的孩子道：“玄毅，你带唐国公府的二郎和三郎，到林中玩吧。”
　　众人都还未取字，所以以名称呼。
　　窦氏介绍了李世民和李玄霸的名字。
　　当听到李玄霸的名字时，众人纷纷侧目。
　　李玄霸：【迟早拔了他的氧气管。】
　　李世民疑惑地看向李玄霸。
　　李玄霸：【没什么，自言自语。】
　　李玄霸说的自然是李渊。
　　显然自己在出生的时候，李渊看着病病恹恹的李玄霸，就没想过能养活，所以取名特别敷衍。
　　看看老大老二，“建成”是希望守住家业，“世民”是希望儿子将来济世救民，都是好寓意。
　　老四原名李劼，“劼”是谨慎的意思，现在叫李元吉；老五原名李稚诠，“诠”是明事理的意思，现在叫李智云。
　　而自己呢？“玄”的意思是排名第三，“霸”……那真是霸气十足呢。
　　排名第三的小霸王是吧？！还不如叫李玄呢！！
　　李玄霸曾经试图求李渊改名。但这个时代的人都很迷信。李渊见李玄霸居然没夭折，坚信自己的名字取得好，说永远不会给李玄霸改名。
　　李玄霸每次报名字的时候，都会引来别人侧目。
　　习惯了，习惯了。
　　就等着拔氧气管了。
　　李玄霸神色岿然不动，像是没看到周围人蕴含着笑意的眼神似的。
　　他这样坦然，倒让那些心里笑话他名字的人有些尴尬了，纷纷收回视线。
　　崔老夫人在心中点了下头。这个孩子虽身体看上去弱了些，但很是沉稳，唐国公府的家教不错。
　　窦氏留在高台中与其他女眷闲聊，顺带接受考验。
　　李世民和李玄霸手牵手跟着郑玄毅等郑家男童离开，顺带接受考验。
　　郑玄毅约十一二岁，一副家中兄长做派，将一众弟弟和李世民、李玄霸引到了石榴林中一处凉亭里。
　　凉亭里也缠着帷幕，里面放着冰块和书案、书架。
　　书案上有笔墨纸砚，书架上各种书籍琳琅满目。
　　李世民和李玄霸对视一眼。啧，准备真是充分。
　　入座后，那些绷着脸的郑家男童精神松懈了不少。有的人干脆直接抱起了瓜果啃了起来，非常没有礼貌，和刚才在长辈面前判若两人。
　　郑玄毅用眼神训斥，但没人理睬他。
　　他只能拱手道：“弟弟们被惯坏了。”
　　李世民和李玄霸点头，随意找了一处坐下。
　　“五兄，磨磨蹭蹭干什么？赶紧结束，我还想回去休息。”一郑家孩童不满道。
　　郑玄毅瞪了那人一眼，道：“十二郎，有客人在，注意礼仪。”
　　世家大族的子弟排行是同辈通排，郑玄毅虽是父母长子，但在家称郑五郎。
　　郑十二郎叹气，对李世民和李玄霸拱手：“二公子，三公子……”
　　李世民道：“叫我和阿玄李二郎、李三郎便是。”
　　郑十二郎立刻改口：“李二郎，李三郎，你们也嫌无趣对不对？我们要不要来比一比学问？再拿些钱财出来当彩头。”
　　郑玄毅高声：“十二郎，你！……”
　　李世民打断道：“确实有些无趣。你说如何考校？”
　　郑玄毅不断作揖道歉：“十二郎顽劣，请李二郎别放在心上。我们吃些瓜果，看些书，随意聊聊可好？若是喜欢写字作画，那里也有纸墨。”
　　李玄霸：【这一唱一和的可真好听。说是玩耍，这里一个玩具都没有，难道真把我们赶到这里读书？】
　　李世民小幅度点头。就是就是。要做什么就做，遮遮掩掩，真不痛快。
　　李玄霸语气平静，语速缓慢道：“说比一比，火气太大了。不如玩些文字的游戏，诸位看如何？比如……”
　　李玄霸随手抽出一卷论语：“以我们年龄，大多只是蒙童，恐怕只有郑五郎你书读得稍多。”
　　郑玄毅闻弦知雅意：“李三郎的意思是，玩《千字文》之类的文字接龙？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“那多没意思。我的意思是，我们谁读了什么书，自己兄弟肯定是清楚的。我们李家和你们郑家各出一人背诵，再出一人在书架上取背诵者熟背的书籍，由持书者给背书者出题。”
　　李玄霸对着众人笑了笑：“自家兄弟出题考自家兄弟，这就是玩耍了，是吧？”
　　郑玄毅见李玄霸这表情，就知道李家人应该已经猜到了自家的想法。
　　他颇有些不好意思道：“确实是玩耍。”
　　长辈有长辈的考量，他也有他的考量。
　　将来自己会出仕。唐国公府的两位公子是皇帝的表侄，将来仕途肯定很顺利。以后大家同朝为官，不宜弄得太尴尬。
　　其实原本不会这么麻烦，是家中选出的小娘子的父亲不乐意将女儿嫁给唐国公府，才多加了些内容，要看看唐国公府的诚意。
　　郑家现在少有身居高位的有实职之人。郑继伯叔父身居刺史之位，认为自己的女儿嫁作王妃都足够。且女儿年幼，而那李建成已经十六岁，待女儿嫁给他时，说不得庶子都有了。
　　但郑家因前一个领头人郑译不得隋文帝喜爱，仕途几经浮沉，虽然其子继承了爵位，但已经淡出朝堂核心范围。郑家急需回到朝堂中枢，唐国公府宗妇之位，简直是瞌睡就送来枕头。
　　若不是唐国公太挑剔，非要看女子父亲的官职，也不至于这么麻烦。
　　所以这一场考校，是唐国公和郑继伯双方都要求太高的结果。算是一个愿打，一个愿挨吧。
　　郑玄毅接了这差事就很头疼。李玄霸的提议解了他的困境，他立刻就同意了。
　　郑家其他小郎也提起了兴致。
　　“李三郎，要如何出题？可有规矩？”一个身穿红衣的郑家小郎问道。
　　李玄霸微笑道：“别急，且听我慢慢道来。我们玩打擂台如何？打擂台即一个守擂，一个攻擂。守擂者先出题，攻擂者必须用守擂者的题。”
　　“比如……”李玄霸翻开了《论语》，“‘子曰：学而时习之’下面十字。”
　　李世民答道：“不亦说乎有朋自远方来。”
　　李世民对李玄霸眨了眨眼：“简单。”
　　李玄霸笑道：“守擂者答完后，攻擂者只需要也选出他手持书中任意‘下十字’就行。出题只出‘上下’。是不是很简单？”
　　他伸手，李世民从怀里取出一个小沙漏放在李玄霸手中。
　　“沙漏的沙子漏完还未答出，就淘汰。”李玄霸道，“我和哥只有两人，就由我们先守擂。”
　　郑家几位小郎都露出了感兴趣的神色。
　　“好像很有趣！”郑十二郎道，“真的不来些彩头吗？”
　　郑玄毅叹气：“十二郎，不可赌博。”
　　李玄霸摇头：“只是一些彩头，不算赌博。就这样吧，我看我们都挂有玉佩。参与者各出一个玉佩代表擂台资格，输了就把玉佩赠予赢了的人。有几个玉佩，就代表能有几次可以答错，或者跳过题目的机会。到长辈来寻我们时，各自手中的玉佩就当做彩头了。”
　　郑十二郎击掌道：“这个好！”
　　李玄霸把自己腰间玉佩递给李世民：“我身体弱，就不和你们一起玩，只给我哥当出题者了。你们若不想玩，也可把玉佩赠予别人。”
　　郑家几位小郎纷纷摇头。
　　就算郑家内部也是有竞争的，他们可不想被人说怯战。
　　“那就开始吧。”李玄霸将《论语》放下，拿起一本《春秋》。
　　郑家小郎纷纷一怔。
　　李家二郎三郎居然已经开始读《春秋》了？
　　郑十二郎扫了众人一眼，取下一本《诗经》交给郑玄毅：“我先攻！”
　　李玄霸笑道：“‘夏，楚人围巢。秋，滕子来朝’。上十字。”翻转沙漏。
　　李玄霸：【来朝。二月庚子。子叔姬卒。】
　　李世民装模作样地屈指算了算，一个字一个字道：“来朝二月庚子子叔姬卒。”
　　郑玄毅道：“‘谁能亨鱼？溉之釜鬵’。上十字。”翻转沙漏。
　　郑十二郎迅速掐算，道：“‘嘌兮！顾瞻周道，中心吊兮！’”
　　李玄霸翻页：“‘冬十月，滕子来会葬’，上五十字。”
　　郑玄毅提醒道：“《春秋·襄公三十一年》在这一句之前没有五十字。”
　　李玄霸道：“上五十字，是这本书的上五十字。”
　　郑玄毅和郑十二郎的脸色都僵住。
　　李玄霸翻转沙漏，和李世民对视一眼。兄弟二人露出如出一辙的温和微笑。
　　郑十二郎头上沁出汗珠。
　　……
　　“咦？那是大郎、二郎、三郎和四郎？他们不是正与友人清谈吗？”
　　正聊着的女眷们，从帷幕敞开赏景的那一面，眼尖地看见对岸四个行色匆匆的俊秀少年。
　　这四人皆已经束发，其中一人还已经戴冠。
　　“去看看。”崔老夫人看着窦氏着急的神色，心里也不由着急。
　　难道是自家小郎们和李二郎、李三郎起冲突了？
　　她只是说考一考这二人蒙学学得如何，不应该会起冲突啊。
　　窦氏顾不上再保持雍容的姿态，提起裙角就朝着岸边小跑。
　　郑家女眷们也不由加快了脚步。
　　……
　　“时间到了，承让！”李世民得意洋洋把最后一块玉佩放到身旁的石桌上。
　　石桌上，玉佩已经堆积如小山。
　　郑玄毅苦笑。他的玉佩也输出去了。
　　凉亭中，郑家小郎们皆面如土色。
　　“抱歉，我等来晚了！”郑大郎匆匆进入凉亭，拱手道，“我和三位堂弟在送别友人，现在才到。李二公子，李三公子，实在是抱歉。”
　　李玄霸放下手中《易经》，与李世民一起拱手回礼。
　　兄弟二人异口同声道：“无事无事，君可要继续攻擂？”
　　郑家此辈四位最年长者，看着弟弟们眼巴巴的神情，咬牙道：“攻！”
　　李世民和李玄霸笑得露出森森白牙：“请！”
