**Chapter 12: Using the Zheng Family to Win Fame Across the World**

"Excellent!" the middle-aged man praised, before sweeping a harsh gaze over the Zheng family youths present.

When the Eldest Young Master of the Zheng family met his gaze, he quickly lowered his head.

Zheng Xuanyi followed behind his father, Zheng Renji, wiping the beads of sweat that had broken out on his forehead from running.

Zheng Renji's heart was filled with fury.

As a prominent "Commandery Clan," the Zheng clan of Xingyang possessed immense local influence.

Not only in Xingyang, but in almost every minor branch of the Zheng clan, there were members serving as local officials, ranging from county magistrates to commandery governors.

Yet, within the imperial court, it had been many years since anyone from the Zheng clan had held a high-ranking position.

Originally, the Zheng clan of Xingyang had rendered great service when Emperor Wen of Sui replaced the Northern Zhou dynasty. At that time, the Zheng clan's spokesman in the court was Zheng Yi, who had studied alongside Emperor Wen, Yang Jian. Their relationship should have been rock-solid.

However, Emperor Wen had used Zheng Yi's alleged moral failings as an excuse to repeatedly grind down and suppress him, along with the Xingyang Zheng clan behind him. The Zheng clan had gnashed their teeth in frustration, yet they were utterly powerless.

Although Emperor Wen restored Zheng Yi's noble title and official post on his deathbed, granting him posthumous honors, the Zheng family had already been marginalized from the core of the imperial court, with no opportunity to return.

After the death of Zheng Renji's father, his branch of the family also drifted away from the center of power. Zheng Renji's eldest brother, Zheng Qianyi, had been stationed at the border to guard against the Tujue, making it difficult for him to return to the Central Plains. Zheng Renji himself, relying on ancestral privilege, served as a Secretariat Drafter of the upper sixth rank.

The Secretariat Drafter was responsible for receiving and transmitting imperial decrees, a post often held by prominent scholars and elites. It was in this position that Zheng Renji had made the acquaintance of Li Yuan. He was also the one who had brokered the marriage alliance between Li Yuan and the Zheng clan of Xingyang.

With the current Emperor constructing the Eastern Capital of Luoyang, Zheng Renji had been pulling strings everywhere, trying to secure the post of Eagle-Soaring Commandant of Huanyuan Prefecture for his eldest brother.

The Eagle-Soaring Commandant of Huanyuan Prefecture guarded the Eastern Capital. Although its rank was not much different from his brother's current post, it would finally allow him to return to the prosperous Central Plains instead of eating wind and sand at the border.

Nowadays, the Emperor's own brothers were either dead or imprisoned. His only surviving close relative of the same generation was his cousin, Li Yuan. Although Li Yuan did not yet hold a high office in court, given the Sui Emperor's contradictory nature of guarding against relatives while practicing nepotism, Li Yuan—as the Emperor's sole cousin—would undoubtedly be trusted and heavily relied upon.

Furthermore, the Emperor prided himself on filial piety. The more rumors of patricide circulated throughout the empire, the more he would display respect for his elders.

Old Lady Dugu was the Emperor's only living close elder relative. Although she rarely asked the Emperor for favors, it was precisely for this reason that if she spoke a few good words to the Emperor on behalf of Zheng Qianyi, the position of Eagle-Soaring Commandant of Huanyuan Prefecture would be secure.

If not for the fact that neither Zheng Qianyi nor Zheng Renji had suitable daughters of their own, they would have stepped forward themselves long ago. Why would they have let other clansmen reap this benefit?

Zheng Renji looked at the Zheng family youths, his heart filled with both anger and disappointment.

The slightly capable members of this generation of the Xingyang Zheng clan were all serving as officials elsewhere. The children they valued were mostly kept by their sides for instruction. The children left behind in the ancestral home of Xingyang were either too young, neglected, or from low-status collateral branches.

Had these juniors stayed in the ancestral home for so long that they truly believed themselves to be local tyrants, looking down on noble families like the Duke of Tang's Estate?

Or was it that they hadn't intended to be so excessively rude at first, but simply prided themselves on their high talent, only to lose to two six-year-old prodigies, letting their tempers flare and losing their composure?

It was likely a mix of both.

Zheng Renji glanced at his son.

Zheng Xuanyi shrank his neck even further.

When Zheng Renji heard that the family wanted to test the talent and character of the Duke of Tang's two legitimate younger sons—to gauge whether being the principal wife of the Duke of Tang's clan would be an easy task—he had immediately recommended his own son to "lead" the matter.

He had feared that these Zheng family youths, spoiled by the clan's reputation, would look down on the Li family's Second and Third Young Masters.

He never expected his own son to be so useless!

Fortunately, his son had remembered his instructions and summoned him in time. Otherwise, he wouldn't even know how this mess could have been resolved.

"I have long heard that the names of the Duke of Tang's two young masters as child prodigies have spread throughout Daxing City. Whenever Duke Li drinks with me, he often boasts about them. Seeing them today, they truly live up to their reputation." Wearing a warm, benevolent smile, Zheng Renji first praised the Li family's Second and Third Young Masters, then cupped his hands to Lady Dou. "Madame Dou, we have been discourteous today."

Zheng Renji had previously been a guest at the Duke of Tang's Estate. Knowing he was her husband's friend, Lady Dou showed him due respect and said calmly, "Greetings, Drafter Zheng. Erlang, Sanlang, Drafter Zheng is a friend of your father's. You should address him as Uncle."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba cupped their hands. "Uncle Zheng."

Seeing that Lady Dou did not seem angry, Zheng Renji breathed a sigh of relief and said, "The Zheng family has passed down the tradition of poetry and literature for generations. Our children begin reading and writing as soon as they learn to speak, so these juniors all pride themselves on their high talent. In this region of Xingyang, they indeed have no rivals. Suddenly encountering someone who can match them, their blood rushed to their heads, and they lost their composure. Alas, their fathers are all serving as officials elsewhere, taking only the children who have already begun formal schooling with them. With only the womenfolk left at home, they have been far too indulgent with them."

Having said this, Zheng Renji glared at the youths once more. "Did you think this was just brothers playing around? 'When three walk together, there must be a teacher among them.' Even a child many years younger than you may have something worth learning from. When you compete in literary battles behind closed doors within your own family, peers look only at talent, not age. But these are guests! Do you want word to spread that the Zheng family used over a dozen people to wage a literary battle against two six- or seven-year-old children, and that one of you had already reached adulthood?!"

When Zheng Renji appeared, the flared neck feathers of the Zheng family youths, who had been acting like fighting cocks, had already flattened.

Hearing Zheng Renji's scolding, they repeatedly bowed and apologized to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

The Eldest Young Master of the Zheng family was no exception.

He repeatedly cupped his hands to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. "It was my mistake. I should have restrained my cousin, but seeing him so distressed, I lost my reason."

The Second, Third, and Fourth Young Masters of the Zheng family, who had come with him, also said, "Though brotherly affection is important, neglecting guests is a breach of etiquette. We failed to balance the two and truly deserve punishment."

Lady Dou's expression remained calm, while Li Shimin looked somewhat dazed.

He did not understand how a situation that had been so tense and hostile just moments ago had suddenly pulled a sharp U-turn, veering so fast that the carriage cabin felt as if it were about to fly off.

When in doubt, consult Ah Xuan. Li Shimin immediately questioned Li Xuanba with his eyes.

Li Xuanba: *[This Uncle Zheng is smoothing things over. Although he is apologizing to us, he is also giving those severely discourteous Zheng family youths a way out. This indicates that this Uncle Zheng is likely someone who supports the marriage alliance between the Zheng family and ours. Don't speak, just listen quietly.]*

Li Shimin was incredulous!

Even after all this, the Zheng family and his family were still going to form a marriage alliance?!

He looked toward his mother.

Lady Dou had already resumed her previous elegant smile. "To have the disciples of the Xingyang Zheng clan, whose literary fame spans the world, disregard age to engage in a literary battle with them—though my heart aches for Erlang and Sanlang, I also feel proud. I find myself unable to stay angry. Erlang, Sanlang, why haven't you thanked your uncle for his praise?"

Li Shimin was still dissatisfied, pouting and refusing to comply.

Li Xuanba: *[Listen to Mother. Don't be stubborn.]*

Li Shimin took a deep breath, suppressing the frustration in his heart. Once again, in perfect unison and with identical movements, he and Li Xuanba bowed. "Thank you for your praise, Uncle."

The Eldest Young Master of the Zheng family looked extremely displeased. Were these two really going to use him as a stepping stone to win fame?!

Though dissatisfied, one could not disobey elders in the Zheng family, lest they face clan punishment. He could only suppress his resentment deep in his heart, planning to write a letter to his father in private to complain.

Lady Dou said, "You must also thank the young masters of the Zheng family. It was they who gave the two of you the opportunity to prove your talents. Quickly, thank your elder brothers."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba bowed. "Thank you, elder brothers of the Zheng family."

This time, Zheng Xuanyi did not disappoint his father. He immediately returned the bow. "We dare not accept. It was we who were discourteous."

With Zheng Xuanyi taking the lead, the other Zheng family youths were swept along, returning the bow and apologizing once more.

Lady Dou said, "Very well, return the jade pendants. Play is play, but taking others' property is improper. Even if they started it, you must not allow your own moral character to waver."

Li Shimin: "!!" *What! I won these jade pendants with my own skills, why should I return them?!*

Li Xuanba: *[Listen to Mother.]*

Li Shimin aggrievedly swallowed his protests. Together with Li Xuanba, they personally returned the jade pendants one by one.

Returning them one by one, bowing one by one.

The Zheng family youths had no choice but to apologize to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba one by one in return.

Li Xuanba: *[Tiring.]*

Li Shimin: *[Aaaaaahhhhhh!!!!!]*

Li Xuanba: *[Hahahahaha.]*

Li Xuanba couldn't help himself; he was amused by his second brother's sky-shattering "Aaaah."

Everyone's eyes fell upon him.

Li Xuanba casually made up an excuse. "I felt very angry earlier, but looking back now, the game just now was actually quite fun. I only feel pity for my brother. I wonder how many days his voice will remain hoarse."

Li Shimin very cooperatively covered for Li Xuanba, putting on an aggrieved expression. "Ah Xuan, are you mocking your brother?"

Li Xuanba nodded. "Yes."

Li Shimin tugged at Lady Dou's skirt. "Mother! Look at Ah Xuan! Quickly, punish him!"

Lady Dou burst into a chuckle. "Alright, Mother will punish him. Sanlang, stretch out your hand."

Li Xuanba extended his hand.

Lady Dou lightly tapped Li Xuanba's palm. "There, Mother has punished Sanlang on Erlang's behalf."

After this playful banter between Lady Dou, Li Shimin, and Li Xuanba, the atmosphere on the scene eased slightly.

At this moment, a foolish child stepped forward, completely breaking the tension.

A chubby child who looked to be around the same age as Li Shimin and Li Xuanba hesitated for a moment, then yanked off the jade plaque around his neck. He eagerly held up both his jade pendant and jade plaque, offering them forward. "You are both so amazing. Can you accept my jade pendant and plaque, and be my big brothers in the future? Father always says I'm stupid, and that without an elder brother to guide me, I'll definitely be carried off by wolves in the future."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba: "??"

Zheng Xuanyi quickly pulled the foolish child back. "What are you saying? You have so many elder brothers at home, why are you looking for other brothers?" *Who is this cousin anyway? Why don't I have any memory of him?*

Just as the foolish child was about to answer, a woman whose clothes were slightly more worn than those of the other female relatives rushed forward. She pulled the foolish child into her embrace and repeatedly apologized to everyone, "My child has been foolish and slow since he was small. He can't even memorize the *Thousand Character Classic* properly. I have made a fool of myself before Madame Dou. Da Sha, you're acting foolish again!"

The foolish child bit his finger, looking utterly bewildered.

His silly appearance successfully made everyone laugh.

Even Li Shimin couldn't help but chuckle.

Li Xuanba didn't find it funny, but since everyone was laughing, he politely curled the corners of his mouth.

The foolish child looked around at everyone's smiles and lowered his head.

Li Xuanba sighed in his heart: *[Brother, wipe clean that broken copper coin you picked up and give it to him.]*

Though Li Shimin didn't understand why, he still complied.

He carefully wiped the copper coin clean on his sleeve, then stood on his tiptoes to hand it to the foolish child cradled in his mother's arms. "For you."

The foolish child's eyes lit up, and he hastily reached out, clutching the copper coin tightly in his hand.

Li Xuanba said, "Once the Duke of Tang's Estate and the Xingyang Zheng clan become in-laws, my second brother and I will indeed be your elder brothers. When you grow a bit older, come visit our home as a guest."

He remembered that this foolish child had originally shrunk to the very back of the crowd, only to be pushed forward by his elder brothers to compete with them. Indeed, he couldn't even stammer out the *Thousand Character Classic*.

During the competition, the foolish child had clutched his jade pendant tightly, tears welling in his eyes. Yet after losing, he had handed the jade pendant over with a face full of admiration, causing quite a laugh among those present.

When Li Xuanba was boiling water, this foolish child had also tried to help, but had been stopped by him.

With such a silly demeanor, Li Xuanba had truly worried the boy would get burned.

But at least the foolish child had good intentions. Compared to the other arrogant and rude Zheng family disciples, he could be considered foolish but kind-hearted.

Seeing Li Xuanba take the initiative to invite the foolish child to their home, Li Shimin understood.

Although Ah Xuan would find a mountain of excuses to hide his soft-heartedness, he surely just couldn't bear to watch this crowd mock an innocent, slow-witted child who had done nothing wrong.

"What is your name?" Li Shimin flashed his signature bright smile at the foolish child.

The foolish child said, "Zheng Guang! Brother, my name is Zheng Guang!"

Li Shimin smiled and nodded. "I'll remember that."

The foolish child let out a silly grin, his nose running, which triggered another round of laughter from the crowd.

His mother smiled along with everyone, quickly wiping her child's nose.

Zheng Renji looked at the child. He couldn't remember whose family the boy belonged to, but judging by his attire, he was likely from a distant collateral branch. Still, Zheng Renji breathed a sigh of relief.

The child's foolish antics had successfully and completely defused the tension.

*When I return, I must look into whose family this child belongs to and provide them with some financial assistance.*

Listening to the laughter of the crowd, Li Xuanba lowered his eyes slightly.

Li Xuanba: *[Brother, tell Mother that your throat hurts terribly and you want to go home.]*

Li Shimin ran back to Lady Dou's side and said coaxingly, "Mother, my throat hurts a bit. Can we go home? I miss Father. Father is still waiting for us to return, saying he will personally roast a lamb for Ah Xuan and me tonight."

Li Xuanba: "..." *What roasted lamb? Second Brother really just makes things up on the fly.*

Li Xuanba said, "Mother, I miss Father as well."

Taking the cue offered by Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Lady Dou said, "Erlang and Sanlang are still young, and their father hasn't seen them in a long time. Before we left today, he repeatedly instructed us to return in time to roast a lamb. I shall take my leave now."

Zheng Renji shot a glance at Old Lady Cui.

Old Lady Cui immediately stepped forward and said, "Let me escort you out, Madame."

Lady Dou hastily replied, "How could I trouble you, Old Madame?"

Old Lady Cui smiled. "It is no trouble. I truly adore this pair of children. I only wish I could spend more time with you all."

Lady Dou said, "Then I shall respectfully accept your kind offer."

Old Lady Cui personally escorted Lady Dou out the door.

As an outside male relative, even though Zheng Renji had just stepped in to smooth things over, it was still inappropriate for him to personally escort Lady Dou out.

He remained where he was. Only after Lady Dou had departed did his face darken completely.

"What on earth do you think you are doing?!" Zheng Renji barked. "If I hadn't happened to be in the estate today, how would you have resolved this? Do you still remember that the Zheng family is supposed to form a marriage alliance with the Duke of Tang's Estate?! Go back and reflect on your actions! I will write to your fathers and have them deal with you!"

Zheng Renji swept his sleeves and departed.

Under the resentful, accusing glares of the other Zheng family youths, who silently branded him a "snitch," Zheng Xuanyi hunched his back and jogged after his father.

The female relatives led their respective children away, each soothing them with heartache, saying they had been wronged.

Only the foolish child's mother quietly withdrew, wiping away her tears.

Little Zheng Guang stretched out his hand, the copper coin in his palm slick with sweat. "Mother, I have new big brothers. My new big brothers are very amazing. Mother won't have to look for big brothers for me by sewing clothes for others anymore."

The tears the woman had just stopped could not help but well up again.

She kissed the forehead of her son, who had become slower than other children due to a high fever, but did not answer him.

***

"I remember now!" Li Xuanba slapped his forehead.

Li Shimin asked curiously, "Ah Xuan, what did you remember?"

Li Xuanba said, "Nothing. I'll tell you when you're sixteen."

Li Shimin: "??!"

He lunged forward to tickle Li Xuanba, only to be pulled away by Lady Dou. "The carriage is moving fast, stop fooling around."

Li Xuanba hid behind his mother.

He couldn't very well tell his second brother right now that the foolish boy named Zheng Guang was highly likely to be his future confidant—the one who, during the Jinyang Uprising, would throw himself into the Prince of Qin's Estate alone as a mere soldier at the tender age of sixteen.

Zheng Guang's political status during the Zhenguan era was not high, and historical records of him were scarce. During the reign of Emperor Gaozong of Tang, he had once commanded an army alone, but all the glory had gone to his deputy, Xue Rengui. His talent and family support were both quite mediocre.

Yet, every time Emperor Taizong promoted meritorious officials, he would raise Zheng Guang's official post and noble title. He even instructed Emperor Gaozong to have Zheng Guang buried in the Zhao Mausoleum alongside him, showing just how much he favored him.

As a member of the Xingyang Zheng clan, Zheng Guang had clung tightly to the Prince of Qin, "demeaning himself" by starting as a common soldier and low-ranking officer. When Li Xuanba had researched this historical data in his past life, he had found it strange.

Guessing from today's events, could it be that in the original history, Zheng Guang had also run into his second brother by chance?

Seeing that Li Xuanba was ignoring him, Li Shimin changed the subject himself. "Sigh, isn't the Xingyang Zheng clan a prestigious noble family? Aren't prestigious families supposed to understand rules and etiquette? Is this their idea of rules?"

Li Xuanba said, "Mother, Father will still form a marriage alliance with the Zheng family, right?"

Li Shimin's eyes widened. "Mother, the Zheng clan is so annoying, are we really still going to form an alliance with them? No way, I hate them."

Lady Dou smiled bitterly.

Li Xuanba said expressionlessly, "Brother, do you know why the Zheng clan is so insufferably arrogant? It is precisely because of this. Even if they are unreasonable, others will overlook it for the sake of the Xingyang Zheng clan's reputation, and will still eagerly seek marriage alliances with them."

Li Shimin clutched his head and shook it. "I'm not listening, I'm not listening! I hate the Zheng family! I don't want a Zheng family daughter to be my eldest sister-in-law!"

Li Xuanba said, "What Father wants is the brand of the Xingyang Zheng clan and their local influence. Now, thanks to Mother's quick wit, the Zheng clan has agreed to let the two of us use their disciples' reputations to win fame as an apology. The Duke of Tang's Estate not only suffers no loss but even gains a small advantage. Therefore, Father should be satisfied with today's trip."

Li Shimin continued to shake his head while clutching it. "What small advantage? Could you and I not win fame without the Zheng family? We are the Second and Third Young Masters of the Duke of Tang, and we know plenty of powerful nobles! As long as we have talent, how could we lack opportunities to make a name for ourselves? Why would we need the Zheng family to make us famous? If all else fails, we still have our Imperial Uncle! If our Imperial Uncle praises us personally, wouldn't that be better than the Zheng family? Why does it sound like we're the ones taking advantage of them?!"

Li Xuanba shrugged. "Such is the way of the world. Second Brother, have you not read up to the Northern Qi dynasty in your history studies yet?"

Li Shimin, who was still shaking his head, paused. "Almost, almost... Sigh, Ah Xuan, don't rush me."

Li Xuanba said, "I'm not rushing you. In every generation, the Xingyang Zheng clan selects their most brilliant talent and pours the entire clan's resources into sending them to the center of the imperial court as their spokesman. During the Northern Wei dynasty, the Zheng clan's spokesman in court was named Zheng Daozhao. He was the leader of the scholars of his time, and everyone praised his demeanor."

Li Shimin maintained his head-clutching posture. "And then?"

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes. "His legitimate eldest son, Zheng Yanzu, was greedy and covetous, and committed incest with his cousin. His granddaughter first married Yuan Ti, the Prince of Guangping, and later married Gao Huan, committing incest with her own son. Their obscene and lawless behavior was known throughout the land."

Lady Dou covered her face and sighed, "Ah Xuan, you... sigh!"

Li Shimin gasped, clutching his head. "Wow!"

Li Xuanba continued, "When the Sui dynasty was first established, the helmsman of the Zheng family in court was Zheng Yi. Zheng Yi's greed was rare in this world, and he was extremely unfilial to his stepmother. He neither allowed her to return to her maternal home nor would he support her, casting her out of the estate to fend for herself. Even Emperor Wen of Sui couldn't bear to watch, gifting him a copy of the *Classic of Filial Piety* and stripping him of his official posts to make him a commoner."

Li Shimin gasped again, clutching his head. "Heavens!"

Li Xuanba said, "When Zheng Yanzu was alive, he served as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial. After his death, he was posthumously grandly titled Commander-in-Chief of Yu, Yan, and Ying Provinces, Duke of Sikong, and Governor of Yu Province. Zheng Yi had his original posts and titles restored before his death, and was given the posthumous name 'Da' after he passed. Their notorious reputations were known to all, yet the world still claims the Xingyang Zheng clan has a pure family style and noble threshold, and that their disciples are exemplars of the scholarly world."

Li Xuanba said, "The threshold of the Zheng family daughters from Zheng Yanzu's lineage is still worn down by suitors. Everyone curses Zheng Yanzu and Zheng Dache for being obscene and lawless, yet they simultaneously praise the Zheng family daughters for their noble character, deeming them ideal wives."

"Do you understand now, Brother? What is noble about these prestigious clans is their plaque. The world praises them only because of that plaque, not because they are truly noble or outstanding. The prestigious clans hold the majority of the writing brushes; those articles that win them fame are just them boasting about one another."

"Others need to display noble character and outstanding talent to join them, but they themselves do not."

"It is just like the Nine-Rank System. A low-ranking scholar from a humble background must be exceptionally outstanding to catch the Emperor's eye, while a high-ranking noble clan member is considered high-ranking even if they are mentally disabled."

"Heh, 'pure family style'? The more prestigious the clan, the fewer rules they have, because they don't need to follow rules—they are the ones who make the so-called rules of the prestigious clans!"

Li Shimin lowered his arms, squeezed next to Li Xuanba, and patted his younger brother's head.

Li Xuanba: "...What are you doing?"

Li Shimin said, "Ah Xuan, don't get worked up. Brother knows you are very angry, but don't get worked up. Your health is poor; getting too worked up will make you feel unwell, and talking too much is tiring. Come, take a deep breath with Brother."

Li Xuanba: "...I'm not worked up."

Li Shimin nodded. "Yes, yes, yes. Come, take a deep breath, calm down, and why don't you just close your eyes and sleep on Brother's shoulder for a bit?"

Li Xuanba turned his face away. "I'm not sleeping."

He took small, shallow deep breaths. Li Shimin used his sleeve to wipe the cold sweat from Li Xuanba's face.

Lady Dou let out a deep sigh, feeling a profound weariness.

She forced herself to cheer up and said, "I have inquired about your future eldest sister-in-law's reputation. She is a virtuous and kind woman, not the kind of wicked person who relies on the Zheng clan's empty name. Don't worry. As for today's matter, Mother will definitely demand justice for you. I will absolutely not let this go until the Zheng family bleeds heavily for this."

Li Shimin nodded. "I believe Mother. Ah Xuan, quickly say you believe Mother! Stop being angry, and you are not allowed to get worked up again."

"I'm not angry, nor am I worked up," Li Xuanba said weakly. "Of course I believe Mother... Ha... *yawn*."

Once he calmed down, he really did feel sleepy.

Li Shimin pointed to his own shoulder. "Sleep here."

Li Xuanba leaned over and lay down on his mother's lap, closing his eyes.

Li Shimin laughed and scolded, "You rascal, Ah Xuan, you're still rejecting my shoulder as uncomfortable, aren't you?"

The corners of Li Xuanba's mouth curled up slightly.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第13章 唐国公府得三赢
chunks.chineseText:
第13章 唐国公府得三赢

=
　　李世民虽然精力充沛，今日也太累了。
　　别说顺背时大多时候他真的是自己背，就是重复李玄霸的话，足足念书几个时辰，如果不是他意志坚定，也难以撑住。
　　李世民挪动到窦氏另一边，也倒头枕在母亲的腿上。
　　两个孩子头顶着头，各自枕着母亲的一条腿闭目睡觉的模样，那真是一模一样。
　　窦氏低头看着这睡着后终于像双子的孩子，眼中隐忍许久的悲伤和愤怒终于漏了一丝出来。
　　她此时分外想念父母，想念兄长，想念舅父舅母。
　　若是他们还在，自己何至于强忍着怒气，还劝孩子们隐忍。
　　窦氏闭上眼，马车晃悠。
　　父母兄长和舅父舅母的音容在她眼前浮现又消失。
　　她睁开眼，眼中复于平静。
　　诚然如三郎所说，此事结果是不错的，所以丈夫不仅不会生气，还会欣喜。但她仍旧可以为两个孩子多讨要些好处。
　　马车驶入家门时，李渊已经在门口等着了。
　　李世民揉了揉眼睛，自己从马车上跳下来。
　　李玄霸也想自己起身，但身上很沉重，脑袋晕晕沉沉，起身后身体老晃。
　　李世民拉了拉李渊的衣角：“耶耶，快把阿玄抱下来。”
　　李渊笑骂道：“你还指挥你耶耶做事？不孝子。”
　　虽然这么说，李渊还是从窦氏怀里将李玄霸接过来，不熟练地拍了拍李玄霸的背：“辛苦了。”
　　李玄霸趴在父亲的肩膀上，有气无力地点了点头，然后闭上眼继续睡觉。
　　李渊把李玄霸抱到房间，让下人帮李玄霸和李世民换衣服，用温水擦洗脸和身体。
　　李世民恢复了精神，李玄霸更困了。
　　“阿玄再坚持一下，我去厨房看看有什么好吃的，吃点东西再睡。”李世民拍了拍弟弟的脸。
　　李玄霸闭着眼睛：“嗯。”
　　李世民跳下床榻，往厨房跑。
　　李世民说李渊会亲自烤小羊羔是现编的借口，但因李世民早几日就在吵着要吃小羊羔，今日李渊还真的很碰巧让人烤了小羊羔等窦氏和两个孩子凯旋。
　　当然，不是亲自烤的。
　　李渊提前考校了两个孩子的学习进度，虽然李玄霸拘着李世民一同藏拙了，李渊也很满意，心想就算是荥阳郑氏，同年龄的孩童如自家二郎三郎这样的也不多，所以早早就准备着为他们“庆功”。
　　李世民和李玄霸离开后，窦氏一边换衣服，一边将今日之事告知李渊。
　　在听到两个孩子被郑氏十几个孩子围攻，还有已经及冠的郑家子来找场子时，李渊疑惑：“郑氏门风不至于此，是否是二郎和三郎太高傲，与他们有了口角？”
　　窦氏垂眸道：“郎君，即使是二郎和三郎有错在先，他们就能这样？”
　　李渊忙道：“当然不是，只是，唉……还好结局是好的。”
　　窦氏道：“对我们而言，五姓七望并非高高在上。我看二郎三郎如此羞辱他们，他们仍旧有结亲的意向，或许我们不该太客气。若太客气，就不是荥阳郑氏为大郎所用，而是我们为荥阳郑氏而用。”
　　李渊摆了摆手：“我知道，你不用说了。朝堂上的事，你不懂。”
　　窦氏心中闪过一丝疼痛。
　　她多次向丈夫进言，丈夫总是让她管好家里事即可。
　　“大郎是个爱护弟弟的好孩子。他年轻气盛，大概是不理解荥阳郑氏的好处的。再者，若宗妇仗着荥阳郑氏的名望对唐国公府不敬，也不是件好事。”窦氏换了内宅的角度。
　　这次李渊听进去了。
　　他皱眉：“这倒是。”
　　窦氏道：“郑舍人已经暗示会补偿二郎三郎，让二郎三郎借郑氏扬名。”
　　李渊大喜：“有如此好事？好，好，我明日就与郑舍人见面，问问他我该如何配合！”
　　他大喜之后，又忍不住叹气：“唉，没想到二郎三郎如此厉害。若早知道，我该带他入宫去面见陛下。”
　　窦氏想要阻止，但她因为皇帝的事与李渊多次不痛快。明知丈夫不会听她的，她便适时地沉默。
　　再者，如果皇帝感兴趣，自己两个孩子也是跑不掉的。
　　窦氏见李渊听了进去，便继续委婉地和李渊商议，要怎么在郑氏那里给孩子们讨些好处。
　　李世民猫着腰从窗户下面偷偷溜走，眼睛里含着两泡眼泪要掉不掉。
　　他是来叫父母一起吃小羊羔，碰巧偷听到对话。
　　家里安全，李世民常甩开仆从自己乱跑。天色昏暗，一个小孩在庭院里乱窜，下人都没有发现李世民偷听了。
　　李世民找了草丛蹲着，眼泪终于掉了出来。
　　他瘪着嘴抹眼泪。
　　他很喜欢耶耶，但阿玄总是不肯和他一起亲近耶耶。
　　阿玄虽然从未说过耶耶的坏话，但李世民怎么可能没发现，阿玄不仅不喜欢耶耶，甚至还有些防备。
　　这次也是。阿玄断定耶耶不会为他们二人出头。
　　“不过是个荥阳郑氏，不过是依靠冢中枯骨。”小小的李世民不会怨恨父亲，把仇都记在了荥阳郑氏身上。
　　待胳膊上被蚊虫咬了好几个红包后，李世民才受不了痒，从草丛里钻出来。
　　他使劲地擦了擦眼睛，然后笑着跑回卧室，把已经忍不住趴下睡觉的李玄霸摇醒：“阿玄，醒醒，醒醒，今天真的有小羊羔。”
　　李玄霸睁开眼，视线先落到二哥红肿的双眼上，又落到二哥胳膊上的红疙瘩上。
　　“蚊虫这么多？”李玄霸皱眉，“你等等。”
　　李玄霸努力爬起来，使劲拍了拍脸，伸了个大大的懒腰，又打了好几个哈欠，勉强清醒过来。
　　他打开带来的行李木箱子，翻找出一个小漆盒。
　　“胳膊伸出来。”李玄霸拿出防蚊虫的药膏，给李世民涂药。
　　李世民笑着道：“凉滋滋的，一下就不痒了。”
　　李玄霸斥责道：“哥，我说多少次了，去庭院里玩的时候把防蚊虫的罩衣穿上，还有，不要因为抄近路就钻草丛……”
　　李世民打断道：“哎呀，好啦好啦，阿玄你现在说话又不累了？好啰嗦。”
　　“哼。”李玄霸用布擦干净手中的药膏，打开了一罐乳白色的药膏，“闭上眼。眼睛都肿了。”
　　李世民抿了一下嘴，乖乖闭上眼。
　　李玄霸：【你该不会是偷听了父亲和娘亲的对话？】
　　李世民沉默了一会儿，待药擦完了，他才小小地“嗯”了一声。
　　李玄霸：【大人自有大人的考量，不像我们想的那样单纯。别难过。】
　　李世民嘴角微微上弯：“嗯。”
　　窦氏来找两个孩子吃饭时，李世民和李玄霸都恢复了以往的模样。
　　李世民扑到窦氏怀里，抱怨蚊虫讨厌，把自己胳膊上的红疙瘩给窦氏看。
　　等见到了李渊，李世民又把自己胳膊上的红疙瘩给李渊看。
　　李渊笑着道：“这耶耶可帮你出不了气，耶耶也被蚊子咬了。”
　　他撸起胳膊，也露出胳膊上的红疙瘩。
　　父子二人对视大笑。窦氏也忍不住失笑。
　　只有李玄霸还在打瞌睡。
　　你们这饭究竟吃不吃了？困。
　　……
　　孩童的喉咙很脆弱。李世民昨日喉咙使用过度，晚上又对抹了辛香料的小羊羔大快朵颐，第二日他起床时，喉咙就肿得说不出话来。
　　李玄霸十分懊恼。
　　父母不懂，自己还不懂吗？他昨日难道太困，把脑子困没了？居然忘记了这件事。
　　李世民喉咙肿了后，引起了扁桃的发炎，扁桃的发炎又引起了低烧。
　　活泼的李世民变得和李玄霸一样蔫哒哒的，把窦氏和李渊都急得如热锅上的蚂蚁。
　　李渊本不是个好脾气的人。
　　他不仅脾气不好，还小心眼。
　　昨晚他还觉得两个儿子和郑氏的冲突是孩子间的小事，现在李世民因昨日之事病倒了，他就忍不下这口气了。
　　李渊骂了来拜访的郑仁基一顿，并写信给郑继伯，骂了郑继伯一顿，质疑郑继伯的家风，还扬言如果二郎有什么三长两短，就算郑家是自己的亲家，也不会善罢甘休。
　　听闻大海寺有双王像，据说向其祈祷，对治愈疾病效果很好。李渊又捐造石弥勒像一尊，为李世民祈福。
　　郑家没想到会造成如此严重的后果，终于慌乱起来。
　　其他世家都在看郑氏的笑话。
　　虽然大家同为世家，大部分时候都同气连枝，但彼此之间也有强弱之分。
　　你弱一分，我就强一分，笑话还是要看的。
　　郑氏的人一合计，见瞒不住，又是自家理亏，终于同意了郑仁基的提议，帮唐国公府捧个神童出来。
　　门阀中不乏用普通子弟去捧其他士人的例子。
　　虽然他们一般不这样做，但若是对方已经碾压他们，自己主动为其扬名，还能给自己家留下一个宽宏大度，甚至慧眼识珠的好名声。自己那些平庸的子弟还能借此机会，贴着那个贤才扬名。
　　“换个意思，就是吸血。”李玄霸削了桃子，切成小块喂给李世民。
　　病来如山倒，病去如抽丝，何况孩童。
　　李世民这病情反反复复，窦氏为了照顾李世民都累得病倒一回。
　　李玄霸这个病秧子倒是出乎众人意料，没有病倒，能帮母亲照顾二哥。
　　李世民说话仍旧难受，但还是忍不住说话：“我终于明白阿玄为何不爱说话了。以后阿玄不说话，我再不吵你。你想当哑巴，哥哥也随你。”
　　“闭嘴，我不想当哑巴。”李玄霸恶狠狠地把桃子塞进二哥嘴里。
　　有桃子吃还不闭嘴，噎死你！
　　李玄霸怀疑，二哥喉咙好得这么慢，肯定是不听医嘱，刚能发声就非要说话闹的。
　　又过了一月，李世民终于好得七七八八。
　　海棠残红已经落尽，桂子花香悄然弥漫。
　　郑家和唐国公府家终于交换了庚帖，定下了这门亲事。
　　不仅如此，郑家为了表示诚意，还送了一位旁支的刚到双十芳华的寡居女给李建成当妾，并且暗示若庶长子从此女肚中出来，就可以留下。
　　荥阳郑氏人口众多，偏远支系者除了有个姓氏，若不付出，几乎得不到家族任何支援。这个寡居女家境贫寒，夫死归家后，家中本来就相看高官中。
　　身居高位者年纪不会小，儿女大概都和她差不多大。同是当妾，给一个十六岁的少年郎当妾，还是人生第一个有名分的妾，并允许生下庶长子，她心里自然是乐意的。
　　那四五岁就传出贤良淑德名声的唐国公府未来宗妇，据说也很赞同这件事。
　　据说这件事就是她提出来的。
　　自己年幼，未婚夫空等自己十年，耽误夫家子嗣，实在是不贤惠。所以她特意向家里求来姐妹一同出嫁，也是一桩美谈。
　　李世民和李玄霸得了名声，李建成得了娇妻美妾，唐国公府和荥阳郑氏达成联姻。
　　唐国公府三赢。
　　李玄霸得知这个结果时，正踮着脚折下一枝桂花，想要给李渊刚给他们置办的小书房增添一缕幽香。
　　闻言，李玄霸护住手中桂花枝，嗤笑一声，正想说什么，突然头上花枝颤抖，金色桂子落了满头。
　　他抬头一看，二哥不知道什么时候爬上了金桂树，摘了一捧桂花散在他头上。
　　“阿玄，来树上！”李世民笑着对李玄霸伸出手。
　　李玄霸想了想，气沉丹田，发出罕见的超大声音：“娘亲！哥哥爬桂花树！好高好危险！”
　　李世民笑容僵硬。
　　“李、世、民！！给我下来！！”
　　窦氏提着裙子从屋里冲出来，李玄霸立刻把手中桂花枝奉上。
　　他拍了拍头上的桂花，吹了一声口哨。
　　金秋八月，桂子飘香，岁月静好。
　　宜看娘亲揍哥。
　　……
　　李渊自来郑州当刺史后，为长子李建成求郑氏女，求了快整整两年，终于如愿以偿。
　　李建成本来十三岁相看人家，十四岁相中郑氏女，拖到了十六岁，这婚事终于订成了，还得了一美妾。
　　他在朋友中受尽艳羡之语，对给他挣得此番好处的弟弟终于多了一分亲近。
　　至于李世民和李玄霸的神童之名，李建成是不嫉妒的。
　　身为未来的唐国公，他早早被教导，弟弟所有的成就都是他的助力。如现在，李世民和李玄霸“力战”郑家十数子弟，不就为他挣得了娇妻美妾和荥阳郑氏的助力？
　　原本李建成对李世民和李玄霸得了祖母和母亲的嫁妆铺子的事有些不满。
　　他倒不是在乎这点财产。唐国公府所有财产都会是他的，他还不至于计较祖母和母亲的嫁妆，只是厌恶吐了他一身的李玄霸而已。
　　现在李建成虽然仍旧不喜李玄霸，但对祖母和母亲私下补贴两个弟弟的行为也不再抵触，和朋友游玩时还会经常夸奖李世民和李玄霸，说自己教他二人读书时，他二人表现得有多聪慧。
　　唐国公府出了两个连荥阳郑氏都赞叹不已的神童，也传到了正在洛阳行宫的杨广耳中。
　　洛阳新城还未修好，但洛阳曾是北魏的都城，原本旧城就很繁华，有隋朝的行宫。
　　杨广刚登基，最喜“祥瑞”。
　　他当即给李渊下令，让窦氏带李世民和李玄霸来洛阳面圣。

Chapter 13: A Triple Win for the Duke of Tang's Residence

Even though Li Shimin was usually boundlessly energetic, today had completely exhausted him.

Not to mention that when reciting backward, he had truly memorized most of it himself; repeating Li Xuanba's words and reciting books for hours on end would have broken anyone without iron willpower.

Li Shimin wriggled to the other side of Lady Dou and tumbled over, resting his head on his mother's other lap.

The two children rested head-to-head, each lying on one of their mother's thighs with eyes closed in sleep. They looked identical in that moment.

Lady Dou looked down at the children who finally looked like true twins once asleep. A flicker of sorrow and anger that she had bottled up for a long time finally leaked through her eyes.

At this moment, she missed her parents, her elder brother, and her uncle and aunt immensely.

If they were still alive, why would she have to swallow her anger and even persuade her sons to endure?

Lady Dou closed her eyes as the carriage swayed.

The voices and faces of her parents, brother, uncle, and aunt flickered before her eyes before vanishing.

When she opened her eyes again, tranquility had returned to them.

Indeed, as Sanlang had said, the outcome was favorable. Therefore, her husband would not only refrain from being angry, but he would also be overjoyed. Still, she could demand a few extra benefits for her two children.

***

By the time the carriage pulled into the estate gate, Li Yuan was already waiting at the entrance.

Li Shimin rubbed his eyes and jumped down from the carriage on his own.

Li Xuanba also wanted to get up, but his body felt impossibly heavy, his head was spinning, and he wobbled after standing up.

Li Shimin tugged at Li Yuan's hem. "Father, quick, lift Ah Xuan down!"

Li Yuan laughed and scolded lightly, "Ordering your father around already? Unfilial child!"

Despite his words, Li Yuan took Li Xuanba from Lady Dou's arms and awkwardly patted his back. "You've worked hard."

Li Xuanba leaned limply against his father's shoulder, nodded weakly, closed his eyes, and drifted back to sleep.

Li Yuan carried Li Xuanba to his room and had the servants help both boys change clothes and wipe their faces and bodies with warm water.

Li Shimin recovered his energy, while Li Xuanba grew even groggier.

"Ah Xuan, hold on just a bit longer. I'll go check the kitchen for delicious food. Have a bite before sleeping," Li Shimin patted his younger brother's cheek.

Li Xuanba kept his eyes closed: "Mhm."

Li Shimin hopped off the bed and dashed toward the kitchen.

Li Shimin saying that Li Yuan would personally roast a lamb was a made-up excuse, but because Li Shimin had been clamoring to eat roasted lamb a few days prior, Li Yuan coincidentally happened to have a lamb roasted today, waiting to celebrate the triumphant return of Lady Dou and the two children.

Of course, he hadn't roasted it himself.

Li Yuan had tested the two boys' study progress beforehand. Although Li Xuanba had restrained Li Shimin so they could hide their true brilliance, Li Yuan was still immensely satisfied. He thought to himself that even among the prestigious Zheng Clan of Xingyang, there weren't many children their age as talented as his Erlang and Sanlang. Thus, he had prepared a "victory feast" early on.

***

After Li Shimin and Li Xuanba left, Lady Dou changed her clothes while informing Li Yuan of the day's events.

Upon hearing that their two boys were swarmed by over a dozen Zheng children, and that an adult Zheng family member had even come to salvage their honor, Li Yuan was puzzled: "The Zheng Clan's family tradition shouldn't be like this. Could it be that Erlang and Sanlang were too arrogant and got into a squabble with them?"

Lady Dou lowered her eyes and said, "My Lord, even if Erlang and Sanlang were in the wrong first, does that give them the right to act like that?"

Li Yuan quickly said, "Of course not. It's just... sigh, well, at least the outcome was good."

Lady Dou said, "To us, the Five Names and Seven Clans are not unreachable beings. Seeing how Erlang and Sanlang humiliated them so thoroughly, yet they still intend to form a marital alliance, perhaps we shouldn't be too polite. If we are overly deferential, it won't be the Zheng Clan of Xingyang serving Dalang, but rather our family being used by them."

Li Yuan waved his hand. "I know, say no more. You don't understand matters of the court."

A sharp pang of heartache flared in Lady Dou's chest.

She had offered counsel to her husband many times, but he always told her to just manage household affairs.

"Dalang is a good boy who loves his younger brothers. He is young and hot-blooded, so he likely doesn't understand the benefits of the Zheng Clan of Xingyang. Furthermore, if the future primary wife relies on the prestige of the Zheng Clan to disrespect the Duke of Tang's estate, that would hardly be a good thing either." Lady Dou shifted to the perspective of household affairs.

This time, Li Yuan took it to heart.

He frowned. "That is indeed true."

Lady Dou said, "Secretariat Drafter Zheng has already implied they will compensate Erlang and Sanlang, letting them build a reputation at the Zheng Clan's expense."

Li Yuan was overjoyed. "There is such a good thing? Good, excellent! I shall meet with Secretariat Drafter Zheng tomorrow and ask him how I should cooperate!"

After his joy passed, he could not help sighing, "Sigh, I didn't expect Erlang and Sanlang to be so formidable. Had I known earlier, I should have taken them to the palace to have an audience with His Majesty."

Lady Dou wanted to stop him, but because she and Li Yuan had suffered many disagreements over matters regarding the Emperor, knowing her husband would not listen, she remained silent at the right moment.

Besides, if the Emperor became interested, her two children wouldn't be able to escape it anyway.

Seeing that Li Yuan had listened, Lady Dou continued to tactfully discuss with him how to exact more benefits for the children from the Zheng Clan.

***

Li Shimin was crouching below the window, quietly slipping away, tears welling up in his eyes, barely held back.

He had come to fetch his parents to eat the lamb together, only to overhear their conversation by chance.

The estate was safe, so Li Shimin often ran around without servants following him. In the dim twilight, a small child scurrying through the courtyard went unnoticed by the servants, who didn't realize Li Shimin had eavesdropped.

Li Shimin found a patch of bushes and crouched inside. Tears finally tumbled down his cheeks.

He pursed his lips and wiped his tears away.

He liked his father very much, but Ah Xuan was always reluctant to get close to Father alongside him.

Although Ah Xuan had never spoken ill of Father, how could Li Shimin fail to notice? Ah Xuan not only disliked Father, but was even somewhat on guard against him.

This time was no different. Ah Xuan had been certain that Father would not stand up for the two of them.

"They are nothing more than the Zheng Clan of Xingyang, relying on decaying bones in a grave!" Young Li Shimin would not resent his father; instead, he pinned all his hatred on the Zheng Clan of Xingyang.

Only after several large, red mosquito bites swelled on his arms did Li Shimin, unable to stand the itching, crawl out of the bushes.

He rubbed his eyes vigorously, then ran back to the bedroom with a smile, shaking awake Li Xuanba, who had already slumped down onto the bed to sleep. "Ah Xuan, wake up, wake up! There really is roasted lamb today!"

Li Xuanba opened his eyes, his gaze landing first on his second brother's red, swollen eyes, and then on the red welts on his arms.

"So many mosquitoes?" Li Xuanba frowned. "Wait a moment."

Li Xuanba forced himself up, slapped his own face vigorously, took a massive stretch, and let out a few large yawns, barely managing to clear his mind.

He opened the wooden luggage trunk he had brought along and rummaged out a small lacquered box.

"Extend your arm." Li Xuanba pulled out an anti-mosquito salve and applied it to Li Shimin.

Li Shimin laughed and said, "It's so cool and refreshing, it stopped itching immediately."

Li Xuanba scolded, "Brother, how many times have I told you? When playing in the courtyard, put on your mosquito-repellent smock. And don't crawl through the bushes just to take a shortcut..."

Li Shimin interrupted, "Aiya, alright, alright! Ah Xuan, talking doesn't tire you out now? So naggy!"

"Hmph." Li Xuanba wiped the remaining salve off his hand with a cloth and opened a small jar of milky-white ointment. "Close your eyes. Your eyes are swollen."

Li Shimin pursed his lips and obediently closed his eyes.

Li Xuanba: 【Did you happen to overhear Father and Mother's conversation?】

Li Shimin remained silent for a moment. Once the ointment was applied, he let out a soft "Mm."

Li Xuanba: 【Adults have their own considerations; they aren't as simple-minded as we think. Don't be sad.】

The corners of Li Shimin's mouth curled up slightly. "Mm."

***

When Lady Dou came to fetch the two boys for dinner, both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had returned to their usual selves.

Li Shimin threw himself into Lady Dou's arms, complaining about the annoying mosquitoes and showing her the red bites on his arm.

Upon seeing Li Yuan, Li Shimin again showed his arm's red bites to Li Yuan.

Li Yuan laughed and said, "Father can't avenge you for this—I was bitten by mosquitoes too!"

He rolled up his sleeves, revealing red bites on his own arms as well.

Father and son looked at each other and laughed heartily. Lady Dou could not help chuckling as well.

Only Li Xuanba was still dozing off.

*Are you two going to eat this meal or what? I'm exhausted.*

……

A child's throat is fragile. Li Shimin had strained his throat excessively yesterday, and then feasted on spicy roasted lamb that night. When he woke up the next morning, his throat was so swollen he couldn't utter a word.

Li Xuanba felt extremely annoyed at himself.

His parents didn't know better, but didn't *he*? Had he been so sleepy yesterday that his brain melted away? How could he have forgotten this?

After Li Shimin's throat swelled, it triggered tonsillitis, which in turn brought on a low-grade fever.

The lively Li Shimin became as listless and droopy as Li Xuanba, driving both Lady Dou and Li Yuan frantic like ants on a hot skillet.

Li Yuan was never a mild-tempered man to begin with.

Not only did he have a short temper, but he was also petty.

Last night, he had thought the conflict between his two sons and the Zheng Clan was just a trivial matter between children. But now that Li Shimin had fallen ill because of yesterday's events, he could no longer swallow this anger.

Li Yuan gave Zheng Renji—who had come to visit—a fierce tongue-lashing, and wrote a letter to Zheng Jibo cursing him, questioning his family's honor. He even declared that if anything happened to Erlang, even if the Zheng family was his in-law, he would not let the matter rest.

Hearing that Dahai Temple housed the Twin Kings Statues, which were said to work wonders for curing illnesses when prayed to, Li Yuan donated funds to carve a stone Maitreya statue to pray for Li Shimin's recovery.

The Zheng family had not expected such severe consequences and finally fell into a panic.

The other prestigious aristocratic clans were all watching the Zheng Clan's humiliation.

Although they were all great aristocratic houses and stood together in solidarity most of the time, there were still hierarchies of strength among them.

If you weaken by a fraction, I grow stronger by a fraction. A spectacle was still a spectacle to be enjoyed.

The Zheng Clan conferred among themselves. Realizing they couldn't cover it up and were in the wrong, they finally agreed to Zheng Renji's proposal: to help the Duke of Tang's estate elevate a child prodigy into fame.

Among the great clans, it was not uncommon to use ordinary children to elevate other scholars.

Although they did not usually do this, if the opponent had already completely crushed them, taking the initiative to promote their opponent's fame would instead leave them with a reputation for magnanimity—and even a sharp eye for talent. Their own mediocre children could even leverage this opportunity to ride the coattails of that prodigy to gain fame.

"In other words, it's freeloading." Li Xuanba peeled a peach, sliced it into small pieces, and fed them to Li Shimin.

Sickness comes like a landslide and recedes like unwinding silk, let alone in young children.

Li Shimin's illness relapsed repeatedly. Lady Dou became so exhausted taking care of him that she fell ill once herself.

Surprisingly, Li Xuanba, the chronic invalid, did not fall sick. Instead, he was able to help his mother look after his second brother.

It was still painful for Li Shimin to speak, but he couldn't help himself: "I finally understand why Ah Xuan doesn't like to speak. In the future, when Ah Xuan stays quiet, I won't pester you anymore. If you want to be a mute, your brother will go along with you."

"Shut up. I don't want to be a mute." Li Xuanba viciously stuffed a piece of peach into his brother's mouth.

*You still won't shut your mouth while eating peaches? Choke on it!*

Li Xuanba suspected that the reason his brother's throat was recovering so slowly was definitely because he refused to follow medical advice—the moment he could make a sound, he insisted on speaking and causing a ruckus.

***

Another month passed, and Li Shimin had finally mostly recovered.

The lingering red of the begonias had completely fallen, and the sweet fragrance of osmanthus flowers quietly permeated the air.

The Zheng family and the Duke of Tang's family finally exchanged horoscopes and finalized the marriage contract.

Not only that, but to show sincerity, the Zheng family also sent a widowed woman from a branch lineage, who had just turned twenty, to be a concubine for Li Jiancheng. They subtly implied that if an eldest son born of a concubine came from her womb, he would be allowed to be kept.

The Zheng Clan of Xingyang had a massive population. Those from distant branches received almost no support from the family unless they offered something in return. This widowed woman came from a poor household; after her husband died and she returned home, her family was already looking to marry her off to a high-ranking official.

High-ranking officials were rarely young; their children were likely around her age. Between being a concubine to an old man or becoming a concubine to a sixteen-year-old youth—and his very first official concubine, with permission to bear his eldest son—she was naturally more than willing.

The future primary wife of the Duke of Tang's estate, who had been renowned for her virtue and propriety since she was four or five years old, was said to strongly approve of this arrangement.

Supposedly, she was the one who proposed it.

Since she was young and her fiancé would have to wait ten years for her in vain, delaying the family line of her husband's family was truly unvirtuous. Thus, she specifically requested her family to allow her sister to be married off together with her, which was praised as a story of fine virtue.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba gained fame; Li Jiancheng gained a charming wife and a beautiful concubine; and the Duke of Tang's residence achieved a marital alliance with the Zheng Clan of Xingyang.

A triple win for the Duke of Tang's estate.

***

When Li Xuanba learned of this result, he was standing on tiptoes breaking off a branch of osmanthus blossoms, wanting to add a touch of lingering fragrance to the small study Li Yuan had just set up for them.

Hearing this, Li Xuanba protected the osmanthus branch in his hand, let out a sneer, and was just about to say something when suddenly the blossom-laden branch above his head shook violently, showering golden osmanthus petals all over his head.

He looked up to see his second brother, who had climbed the golden osmanthus tree at some unknown point, plucking a handful of osmanthus flowers and scattering them over his head.

"Ah Xuan, come up the tree!" Li Shimin reached out to Li Xuanba with a smile.

Li Xuanba thought for a moment, gathered his breath into his dantian, and let out a rare, roaring shout: "Mother! Brother climbed the osmanthus tree! It's so high and dangerous!"

Li Shimin's smile froze.

"Li! Shi! Min!! Get down here right now!!"

Lady Dou pulled up her skirt and rushed out of the house. Li Xuanba immediately offered up the osmanthus branch in his hand.

He patted the osmanthus petals off his head and blew a whistle.

Golden autumn, eighth month, osmanthus fragrance filling the air, peaceful and tranquil years.

A fine day to watch Mother beat Brother.

……

Ever since Li Yuan became the Inspector of Zhengzhou, he had sought a daughter of the Zheng Clan for his eldest son, Li Jiancheng. After trying for nearly two full years, his wish was finally fulfilled.

Li Jiancheng had originally started looking for a marriage partner at age thirteen, took a liking to the Zheng Clan's daughter at fourteen, and dragged it out until he was sixteen before this marriage was finally settled, along with gaining a beautiful concubine.

He was showered with envious words among his friends, and finally felt a bit closer to the younger brothers who had secured these benefits for him.

As for the child prodigy reputation of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Li Jiancheng felt no jealousy.

As the future Duke of Tang, he had been taught early on that all the achievements of his younger brothers were stepping stones for him. For instance, didn't Li Shimin and Li Xuanba "fighting fiercely" against over a dozen children of the Zheng family earn him a charming wife, a beautiful concubine, and the support of the Zheng Clan of Xingyang?

Originally, Li Jiancheng was somewhat dissatisfied that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had received their grandmother's and mother's dowry shops.

He didn't actually care about that bit of property. All the assets of the Duke of Tang's estate would belong to him eventually; he wouldn't begrudge his grandmother's and mother's dowries, but he merely loathed Li Xuanba for vomiting all over him.

Now, although Li Jiancheng still disliked Li Xuanba, he no longer resisted his grandmother and mother privately subsidizing his two younger brothers. When hanging out with friends, he would frequently praise Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, bragging about how brilliantly the two had performed when he taught them to read.

News that the Duke of Tang's estate had produced two child prodigies praised even by the Zheng Clan of Xingyang reached Yang Guang, who was currently at the imperial palace in Luoyang.

The new city of Luoyang was not yet completed, but Luoyang had once been the capital of Northern Wei, so the old city was already very prosperous and housed imperial palaces of the Sui Dynasty.

Yang Guang had just ascended the throne and favored "auspicious omens" above all else.

He immediately issued an order to Li Yuan, instructing Lady Dou to bring Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to Luoyang for an imperial audience.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第14章 李家二子独面圣
chunks.chineseText:
第14章 李家二子独面圣

=
　　此时刚到八月。
　　今年是大业元年，杨广修洛阳城、修洛阳西苑、修显仁宫、修通济渠……上线一大堆工程。
　　经过百万劳工的拼命干活，付出了“累死者十之四五，载尸车相望于道”的代价，大业元年上线的大工程只剩下洛阳新城还没有完工。
　　荥阳就在通济渠边上。
　　杨广的令使是通过通济渠来的。虽然通济渠现在还不允许闲杂人等下水，但李渊是杨广表亲，窦氏又带着两个年幼的孩子，杨广特意让窦氏可以与令使一起从通济渠去洛阳，免于旅途劳顿。
　　李渊十分得意，不由又笑了窦氏一场，说窦氏猜忌表弟实在是没必要。
　　窦氏赔笑，说自己确实想错。
　　李渊有公职在身，不能随行。窦氏忐忑不安地带着李世民、李玄霸和一众仆从，从通济渠乘船去洛阳面圣。
　　船上，李世民和李玄霸恶补自己家的亲戚关系，背下了一大堆名字和名字主人的生平，以免皇帝问起来的时候，他们都不知道说的是谁。
　　两个孩子背得直打哈欠。
　　李世民背一会儿，倒在铺了毯子的甲板上滚一圈，把百无聊赖阐述得淋漓尽致。
　　李玄霸咬牙坚持了一会儿，也不行了。
　　他大字躺在甲板上，任由二哥滚过去碾他一遍，滚过来又碾他一遍，一动不动。
　　李玄霸以前看西方玄幻涉及贵族的小说时，对那些贵族居然要熟背贵族谱系感到无语。谁知道自己投胎到了隋朝，居然也要背谱系。
　　哦，这套糟粕是从我们开始，比西方早几千年，不能怪在西方头上。
　　李世民又滚了一圈，把弟弟又碾了一遍，然后也大字躺在李玄霸身边。
　　他打着哈欠道：“原来我们的表伯表叔还有那么多，怎么我老听奉承我家的人说，耶耶是陛下唯一的表亲？”
　　窦氏坐在地毯上看两个耍赖偷懒，听了李世民的话后微笑道：“你父亲是陛下唯一的姨表兄弟。母亲是陛下唯一还在世的母族长辈。”
　　李世民年幼，没听懂窦氏的言下之意。
　　李玄霸帮忙解读：【杨广此人生性凉薄，若长辈还在，他为表现出对文献皇后的孝道，才会认一认表亲。】
　　李世民眨了眨眼睛。
　　也就是说，独孤家其他几位长辈已经去世，导致小辈关系生疏？
　　他在家也未见耶耶与表伯表叔有多少亲密来往，所以对独孤家的人总记不全。看来独孤家与自家也有些生疏了。
　　可祖母强势，为何会与家中兄弟生疏？真奇怪。谱系里会有答案吗？
　　李世民翻身坐起来，道：“我继续背书了！阿玄，不要偷懒，赶紧起来！”推攘推攘推攘推攘。
　　“嗯……”李玄霸打着哈欠坐起来。
　　兄弟二人背靠着背互相为靠椅，伸长着小短腿，强打着精神继续背书。
　　窦氏要来笔墨纸砚，将两个孩子背书的模样画下来。
　　李世民和李玄霸启蒙前就被教着背过家中亲戚的谱系，只是现在忘记了，咬紧牙关努力背诵，捡起来也快。
　　他们在船上度过了一日，又在洛阳杨广安排的别邸里等候了一日，待杨广召见他们时，两人已经将谱系熟背。
　　李世民和李玄霸也从亲戚谱系中，寻到了祖母没有和表爷爷们太过亲近的原因。
　　兄弟二人蒙着被子咬耳朵说着祖辈的逸闻，为明日面圣“复习”。
　　原来曾祖父独孤信一共有三任妻子。原配如罗氏生一子独孤罗，继室太原郭氏生六子两女，第三个继室清河崔氏生文献皇后独孤伽罗。
　　唐国公老夫人也为太原郭氏所生。
　　独孤信投奔西魏的时候将父母妻儿都抛弃在东魏。独孤罗还在襁褓中时就被囚禁，至北周建立，二十余年才被释放，流落民间，贫困潦倒。
　　无论是独孤信还是独孤信的其他儿子都以为独孤罗早就死了，所以以太原郭氏所生子为嫡长。
　　独孤伽罗让杨坚找到独孤罗。太原郭氏所生六子对独孤罗轻视侮辱，又因独孤罗之母出身不高，不认独孤罗为兄长。
　　杨坚建立隋朝后，独孤皇后通过杨坚认独孤罗为独孤家的嫡长家主，重用独孤罗。
　　太原郭氏所生第五子独孤陀心怀怨恨，以巫蛊之术诅咒独孤皇后，被贬为民。
　　那之后太原郭氏还活着的儿子都开始小心谨慎了。
　　李世民：“其实文献皇后对其他异母兄长也不错，每个活到了大隋的表爷爷都不缺高官厚禄，六表祖父此举实属不该。”
　　李玄霸提醒：“六表祖父是文献皇后异母弟，不是异母兄。”
　　李世民惊讶道：“曾祖父娶清河崔氏时曾外祖母还活着，之后还生了一子？不对啊，曾外祖母虽是继室，但也是曾祖父正妻啊！”
　　李玄霸道：“曾外祖母和文德皇后之母都是正妻。曾祖父续娶了二妻。”
　　李世民：“……”
　　李世民抱头：“啊！我刚质疑荥阳郑氏的家风，怎么太原郭氏和清河崔氏也是如此？清河崔氏还是五姓七望和天下四姓之首吧！我听闻耶耶想给兄长求娶崔氏女儿，崔氏婉拒后，即使崔氏中有耶耶的好友，耶耶都只能作罢！”
　　李玄霸摊手：“还是我们家太弱小了。”
　　李世民翻白眼。以前他以为自家特别厉害，现在……看看自家曾外祖父！
　　李玄霸道：“现在表祖父都去世了。当今皇帝上台后，追赠了包括被削爵的六表祖父高官，以显示他对文献皇后的追思。但看族谱，或许皇帝与我们心里其实不会太亲近。母亲所忧虑的没错。”
　　李世民叹气：“可祖母和耶耶都自以为和陛下很亲近。”
　　李玄霸道：“他们是他们，我们是我们，听娘的，小心谨慎无错。”
　　李世民点头：“对，听娘的。”
　　这时，窦氏在门口道：“二郎，三郎，睡着了吗？有没有偷偷聊天不肯睡觉？”
　　李世民想也没想，高声道：“娘亲，已经睡着了！没有偷偷聊天！”
　　李玄霸深吸一口气，双手捂住眼睛。
　　啊，拿什么拯救我即将被娘亲揍屁股的愚蠢哥哥？
　　……
　　第二日，被打扮成珠宝架子的李世民和李玄霸被窦氏带进了宫。
　　李世民坐在马车上，屁股左扭右扭。昨日挨的揍还疼着呢！
　　李玄霸捂着嘴偷笑。
　　李世民的表情十分幽怨。阿玄真坏，居然立刻装睡。娘也偏心，明知道阿玄装睡也不揭穿，只揍了自己的屁股。
　　李世民幽怨的表情一直带到了面圣的时候。
　　皇帝为避嫌，一般不会接见外命妇。
　　窦氏被引去见皇后，只两小孩被引去见皇帝。
　　窦氏本以为皇帝皇后会同时接见她和两个孩子，自己会伴随在孩子身边。没想到皇帝居然是单独接见两个孩子。她心中焦急，却无可奈何，只能寄希望两个孩子能随机应变。
　　李世民和李玄霸独自拜见了皇帝。
　　他们礼仪周全，但杨广一见李世民幽怨的表情，眉头就不由紧皱：“李二郎，你为何面圣还面带不虞？”
　　李世民瘪嘴道：“回陛下，昨夜小儿因面圣太过激动未能早早入睡，被娘亲揍了屁股，现在还疼呢。”
　　李玄霸拱手替兄长解释：“回陛下，二哥不是面带不虞，是臀疼难忍。”
　　杨广一愣，没想到居然得到这样的回答。他还以为是李渊对他不满，所以教唆儿子呢。
　　他大笑：“可要朕派太医给你瞧瞧？”
　　李世民连忙摇头：“不用了不用了，只是有一点乌青，已经上过药，表叔……陛下不用担心。”
　　杨广听李世民说漏嘴，差点叫他“表叔”，不由心头了悟。
　　看来李渊不仅没有异心，还自诩自己的表兄，常对孩子夸耀与自己关系亲近。
　　杨广疑心病极重，一登基就猜忌诸位堂兄。又因李渊曾被隋文帝和文献皇后喜爱看重，和他兄长杨勇关系不错，所以他心中对李渊也很是警惕。
　　此次他单独召见李家二郎三郎，除了真的想看看他们是不是神童“祥瑞”之外，也有通过两个单纯孩童，试探李渊对他的态度的心思。
　　李世民一句“口误”，让杨广心里安定许多。
　　他笑着继续试探道：“叫朕表叔也无事。朕确实是你的表叔。李渊可常在家中称呼朕为表弟？”
　　李世民傻乎乎道：“耶耶确实常自得和陛下是表亲，还对小儿说‘表叔’如何如何。”
　　李玄霸板着小脸道：“每当这时，祖母就会骂父亲不懂尊卑。”
　　李世民：“耶耶总会反驳，陛下宽厚亲切，且和他自幼关系亲近。”
　　李玄霸：“祖母斥责父亲，陛下越是宽厚亲切，父亲就越该恪守君臣之礼，不能僭越。”
　　李世民和李玄霸异口同声总结道：“娘亲母亲说，祖母是长辈，听祖母的。”
　　杨广听李世民和李玄霸你一句我一句，最后还来了个和声回答，被逗得前俯后仰：“哈哈哈哈，没想到李渊私下居然……哈哈哈哈哈。”
　　他彻底放下心来。
　　原来李渊表面上装得很有能力，私底下居然是以外戚身份自得的肤浅之人。
　　李世民悄悄瞥了弟弟一眼。
　　李玄霸：【看，我说的没错吧？隋炀帝就是这样的人。你说父亲在家中也对他毕恭毕敬，他绝对起疑心。把父亲说成自得肤浅的愚蠢外戚，他才会高兴。】
　　李世民背一僵。
　　又来了又来了，阿玄你能不能别再说什么“隋炀帝”了！你就不担心哥哥我不小心说漏嘴，，我们家全家遭殃吗！闭嘴啊阿玄！
　　李玄霸没有意识到二哥的抓狂，还在那里感慨：【现在的隋炀帝真是意气风发丰神俊朗。】
　　别再说什么“隋炀帝”了！
　　李世民使劲憋，在心里憋出了一个字：【闭！】
　　李玄霸回过神：【嗯？】
　　李世民：【嘴！！】
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　李玄霸：【抱歉，我不是故意的，一时口误。】
　　咳，不小心又用了习惯性称呼，失误失误。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 14: The Two Li Brothers Face the Emperor Alone

It was just entering the eighth month.

This was the first year of the Daye era. Yang Guang had launched an overwhelming flurry of grand engineering projects—rebuilding the city of Luoyang, constructing the West Garden of Luoyang, building Xianren Palace, digging the Tongji Canal…

Through the grueling labor of millions of workers, and at the grim cost of "four to five out of ten dying of exhaustion, with corpse-bearing carts lining the roads in plain sight," the only massive project initiated in Daye Year One that remained unfinished was the new capital of Luoyang.

Xingyang was situated right beside the Tongji Canal.

Yang Guang’s imperial envoy had arrived via the Tongji Canal. Although ordinary folk were not yet permitted to travel on the canal waters, Li Yuan was Yang Guang's cousin, and Lady Dou was traveling with two young children. Yang Guang had specifically granted permission for Lady Dou to accompany the imperial envoy along the Tongji Canal to Luoyang, sparing them the grueling exhaustion of an overland journey.

Li Yuan was immensely proud of this favor and could not help teasing Lady Dou again, saying that her suspicions regarding his imperial cousin were utterly unwarranted.

Lady Dou forced a smile and admitted that she had indeed overthought things.

Bound by his official duties, Li Yuan could not accompany them. With an anxious heart, Lady Dou took Li Shimin, Li Xuanba, and an entourage of servants aboard a boat along the Tongji Canal to Luoyang for their imperial audience.

Aboard the vessel, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba frantically crammed their family tree, memorizing a vast array of names along with their life stories to avoid being caught off guard should the Emperor question them.

The two young boys yawned constantly as they memorized.

Li Shimin would recite for a brief while before collapsing onto the carpeted deck to roll around, embodying sheer boredom to the absolute extreme.

Li Xuanba gritted his teeth and persevered for a short time before he, too, threw in the towel.

He sprawled out in the shape of a star on the deck, letting his elder brother roll over and crush him once, then roll back and crush him again, remaining entirely motionless.

In his past life, whenever Li Xuanba read Western fantasy novels involving aristocracy, he had always found it absurd that nobles had to memorize elaborate ancestral pedigrees. Who could have known that after reincarnating into the Sui dynasty, he would end up memorizing pedigrees as well?

*Ah, well. This particular brand of rubbish originated with us thousands of years before the West. Can’t blame the West for that.*

Li Shimin rolled over once more, rolling right across his younger brother again, and then flopped down in an X-shape beside Li Xuanba.

He let out a yawn and said, "Turns out we have so many cousin-uncles. Why do I always hear the flatterers at home saying that Father is His Majesty's only cousin?"

Lady Dou sat on the carpet watching the two boys slack off. Hearing Li Shimin's words, she smiled faintly and said, "Your father is His Majesty's only maternal first cousin. Your grandmother is the only living elder from His Majesty's maternal clan."

Li Shimin was young and did not catch the subtext beneath Lady Dou's words.

Li Xuanba helpfully interpreted in his mind: *【Yang Guang is cold and unfeeling by nature. He only acknowledges his maternal cousins to display his filial piety toward Empress Wenxian while the elders are still alive.】*

Li Shimin blinked.

*In other words, the other elders of the Dugu clan have passed away, causing the younger generation to drift apart?*

At home, he had never seen his father interact closely with those cousin-uncles, which was why he could never remember everyone in the Dugu clan. It seemed the Dugu clan and their own family had indeed grown distant.

*Yet Grandmother is so strong-willed; why would she be distant from her own brothers? How strange. Will the genealogy hold the answer?*

Li Shimin rolled over and sat up, announcing, "I'm going back to memorizing! Ah Xuan, stop slacking off, get up quickly!" He shoved and prodded him repeatedly.

"Ugh..." Li Xuanba yawned and pushed himself up.

The two brothers sat back-to-back, serving as each other's backrest. Stretching out their short little legs, they forced themselves to perk up and resume memorizing.

Lady Dou called for brush, ink, paper, and inkstone, painting a portrait of the two boys earnestly reciting their lessons.

Before beginning their formal schooling, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had already been taught the family lineage. They had simply forgotten it over time. By gritting their teeth and applying themselves, picking it back up proved quite swift.

They spent a day on the boat and another waiting in a detached villa Yang Guang had arranged in Luoyang. By the time Yang Guang summoned them, both had thoroughly committed the genealogy to memory.

From the family records, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba also uncovered the reason why their grandmother had never been particularly close to their great-uncles.

Huddled under the blankets, the two brothers whispered anecdotes about their forebears into each other's ears, treating it as a "review session" for tomorrow's imperial audience.

As it turned out, their great-grandfather, Dugu Xin, had taken three wives in total. His first wife, Lady Ruluo, gave birth to a single son, Dugu Luo. His second wife, Lady Guo of Taiyuan, gave birth to six sons and two daughters. His third wife, Lady Cui of Qinghe, gave birth to Empress Wenxian, Dugu Qieluo.

The Old Madame of the Duke of Tang was also born of Lady Guo of Taiyuan.

When Dugu Xin defected to Western Wei, he abandoned his parents, wife, and child in Eastern Wei. Dugu Luo had been imprisoned while still in swaddling clothes and was only released more than twenty years later when Northern Zhou was established. He ended up destitute and wandering among the common folk.

Both Dugu Xin and his other sons had assumed Dugu Luo was long dead, so they treated the eldest son born of Lady Guo of Taiyuan as the legitimate heir.

Later, Dugu Qieluo had Yang Jian track down Dugu Luo. The six sons born of Lady Guo looked down upon and insulted Dugu Luo, refusing to acknowledge him as their elder brother because his mother was of humble birth.

After Yang Jian founded the Sui dynasty, Empress Dugu had Yang Jian recognize Dugu Luo as the primary heir and head of the Dugu clan, placing him in positions of great power and trust.

Dugu Tuo, the fifth son born of Lady Guo, harbored deep resentment and used witchcraft to place a curse upon Empress Dugu, for which he was stripped of his rank and demoted to a commoner.

From that moment on, the surviving sons of Lady Guo became exceedingly cautious.

Li Shimin said, "Actually, Empress Wenxian treated her other half-brothers quite well. None of the great-uncles who lived into the Great Sui lacked high offices and generous stipends. Sixth Great-Uncle’s actions were truly out of line."

Li Xuanba corrected him, "Sixth Great-Uncle was Empress Wenxian's younger half-brother, not an elder one."

Li Shimin was astonished. "Great-Grandfather married Lady Cui of Qinghe while Great-Grandmother was still alive, and she even gave birth to a son afterward? Wait, that makes no sense. Even if Great-Grandmother was a successor wife, she was still Great-Grandfather's primary wife!"

Li Xuanba said, "Great-Grandmother and Empress Wenxian's mother were both primary wives. Great-Grandfather took successive primary wives."

Li Shimin: "..."

Li Shimin clutched his head. "Ah! I was just questioning the family conduct of the Zheng clan of Xingyang, but how could the Guo clan of Taiyuan and the Cui clan of Qinghe be like this too? The Cui clan of Qinghe is supposed to be the foremost among the Five Clans and Seven Houses and the Four Great Clans of the Realm! I heard Father wanted to arrange a marriage with a daughter of the Cui clan for Eldest Brother, but after the Cui clan politely declined, even with Father's close friends among them, Father had no choice but to drop it!"

Li Xuanba threw up his hands. "It just means our family was too weak back then."

Li Shimin rolled his eyes. He used to think his family was extraordinary, but now... just look at their great-grandfather!

Li Xuanba remarked, "Now all those great-uncles have passed away. When the current Emperor ascended the throne, he posthumously conferred high official titles upon all of them—including Sixth Great-Uncle, who had been stripped of his nobility—just to showcase his longing for Empress Wenxian. But looking at the family tree, the Emperor probably isn't truly close to us in his heart. Mother's worries are entirely justified."

Li Shimin sighed. "Yet Grandmother and Father both genuinely believe they are very close to His Majesty."

Li Xuanba said, "They are them, and we are us. We must listen to Mother. Being careful and cautious is never wrong."

Li Shimin nodded. "Right, we listen to Mother."

Just then, Lady Dou's voice came from outside the door: "Erlang, Sanlang, are you asleep? Are you secretly chatting and refusing to rest?"

Without a second thought, Li Shimin called out at the top of his lungs, "Mother, we are already asleep! We aren't secretly chatting!"

Li Xuanba took a deep breath and covered his eyes with both hands.

*Ah, what can possibly save my foolish brother from the impending spanking?*

……

The next day, dressed up like decorative jewelry stands, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were brought into the palace by Lady Dou.

Sitting in the carriage, Li Shimin squirmed continuously, shifting his weight from cheek to cheek. The thrashing he had received the night before still stung fiercely!

Li Xuanba covered his mouth and chuckled under his breath.

Li Shimin wore a look of utter grievance. Ah Xuan was truly wicked—he had instantly pretended to be asleep. Mother was biased too; knowing full well that Ah Xuan was faking it, she didn't call him out and only thrashed Li Shimin's backside.

Li Shimin carried that aggrieved expression all the way to the imperial audience.

To avoid impropriety, the Emperor generally did not grant private audiences to noblewomen outside the imperial clan.

Lady Dou was escorted to pay her respects to the Empress, leaving only the two children to be led before the Emperor.

Lady Dou had originally thought the Emperor and Empress would grant an audience to her and the children together, allowing her to stay by their side. She had never expected the Emperor to meet the two children entirely on his own. Though frantic with worry, she was helpless and could only pin her hopes on the two boys' ability to adapt to the situation.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba paid their respects to the Emperor alone.

Their etiquette was flawless, but the moment Yang Guang caught sight of Li Shimin's aggrieved pout, his brow furrowed deeply. "Li Erlang, why do you wear such a look of displeasure before your sovereign?"

Li Shimin pursed his lips and said, "Reporting to Your Majesty, this child was so overly excited about meeting Your Majesty last night that I failed to fall asleep early. Mother thrashed my backside, and it still hurts right now."

Li Xuanba cupped his hands to explain on his brother's behalf: "Reporting to Your Majesty, Second Brother does not wear a look of displeasure; rather, his rear end is in unbearable pain."

Yang Guang was caught off guard, never expecting such a response. He had assumed Li Yuan harbored dissatisfaction toward him and had coached his son to show it.

He burst into hearty laughter. "Would you like Zhen to send an imperial physician to examine you?"

Li Shimin waved his hands in a frantic refusal. "No need, no need! It's just a tiny bit bruised, and medicine has already been applied. Cousin-Uncle... Your Majesty need not worry."

Hearing Li Shimin's slip of the tongue—almost addressing him as "Cousin-Uncle"—a sudden realization dawned upon Yang Guang.

It seemed Li Yuan not only harbored no disloyalty, but even prided himself on being the Emperor's cousin, frequently boasting to his children about their close familial ties.

Yang Guang was intensely suspicious by nature. The moment he ascended the throne, he had grown wary of all his paternal cousins. Furthermore, because Li Yuan had once been deeply favored and valued by Emperor Wen of Sui and Empress Wenxian, and had enjoyed a good relationship with his elder brother Yang Yong, Yang Guang remained highly vigilant toward Li Yuan.

This time, his summoning of the Li family's second and third sons was not only to see whether they were truly child prodigies and "auspicious omens," but also to gauge Li Yuan's true attitude toward him through the mouths of two innocent children.

Li Shimin's "slip of the tongue" put Yang Guang's heart vastly at ease.

Smiling, he continued to probe, "Calling Zhen 'Cousin-Uncle' is fine as well. Zhen is indeed your cousin-uncle. Does Li Yuan often refer to Zhen as his cousin at home?"

Li Shimin replied with naive foolishness, "Father indeed often prides himself on being Your Majesty's cousin. He always tells us children, 'Your Cousin-Uncle did this' and 'Your Cousin-Uncle did that.'"

Li Xuanba kept a stern little face and added, "Whenever that happens, Grandmother scolds Father for not understanding the boundaries of status."

Li Shimin said, "Father always argues back, saying Your Majesty is magnanimous and amiable, and that he grew up very close to you."

Li Xuanba continued, "Grandmother rebukes Father, saying that the more magnanimous and amiable Your Majesty is, the more Father must strictly abide by the propriety between monarch and subject without overstepping."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba concluded in perfect unison, "Mother says that Grandmother is the elder, so we must listen to Grandmother."

Listening to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba trade lines back and forth, culminating in a harmonious duet, Yang Guang was amused to the point of rocking back and forth with laughter. "Hahahaha! To think that Li Yuan is actually like this in private... Hahahahaha!"

His suspicions were completely laid to rest.

So, while Li Yuan appeared highly capable on the surface, beneath it all, he was merely a shallow man who took childish pride in his status as an imperial in-law.

Li Shimin shot a subtle glance at his younger brother.

Li Xuanba thought: *【See, wasn't I right? Emperor Yang of Sui is precisely this kind of person. If you had said Father was entirely deferential and reverent to him at home, he would have grown suspicious beyond doubt. Only by painting Father as a shallow, foolish imperial in-law basking in reflected glory would he be truly delighted.】*

Li Shimin's back stiffened.

*Here we go again, here we go again! Ah Xuan, can you please stop saying "Emperor Yang of Sui"?! Aren't you worried that your elder brother might accidentally let it slip, bringing total ruin upon our entire family?! Shut up, Ah Xuan!*

Unaware of his elder brother's internal meltdown, Li Xuanba continued to marvel in his thoughts: *【The Emperor Yang of Sui right now truly is high-spirited, dashing, and extraordinarily handsome.】*

*Stop saying "Emperor Yang of Sui"!*

Li Shimin squeezed his mind with all his might, forcing out a single telepathic word: *【SHUT!】*

Li Xuanba snapped out of his reverie: *【Huh?】*

Li Shimin: *【UP!!】*

Li Xuanba: "..."

Li Xuanba thought: *【Sorry, I didn't mean to. A slip of the tongue.】*

*Ahem, accidentally used the habitual title again. My mistake, my mistake.*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第15章 赚钱讨赏不寒碜
chunks.chineseText:
第15章 赚钱讨赏不寒碜

=
　　李玄霸曾“说漏嘴”一次。
　　李世民特意去翻了谥号， 吓得多吃了一张饼，撑得躺榻上直哼哼，让弟弟帮他揉肚子。
　　那之后， 李世民就像是失忆了似的， 从未和李玄霸提起过这件事， 只是悄悄地将祖母和母亲给的零花钱藏好，读书习武也更勤奋了。
　　李世民完全没有怀疑李玄霸的“预言”。
　　汉武帝时，谶语附会儒学， 借由经义行预言占卜之事。光武帝时，“谶纬之学”达到了最高峰，世人无不相信。
　　经历了魏晋南北朝， “谶纬之学”被兵锋碾碎，迷信的人不多了， 但上位者也会制造谶语为自己造势。
　　乱世之中， 隔三差五就会出现一个会谶语的人为枭雄看相，年幼的李世民看完史书，傻傻地全信了这些人真的会预言。
　　那么自家阿玄会谶语，很正常！
　　除了李世民年幼，没到会怀疑与自己最亲近的双生弟弟的年纪， 隋朝之前，长达三百六十年的乱世， 也让现在所有人都没有想过隋朝会长久。
　　从三国到西晋短暂的一统后，很快就到了东晋五胡十六国并立。一场混战后，又变成南北朝对峙格局。
　　南朝有宋、齐、梁、陈四个朝代， 北朝有北魏、东魏、西魏、北齐、北周五个朝代。这期间许多时候各个朝代还并存， 彼此征战不休。
　　隋朝建立前长达一百多年南北朝时期， 是华夏史上最混乱的时期之一。
　　在这样的情况下， 隋朝的统一就已经是奇迹。
　　之前的大一统王朝只有秦汉，秦还二世而亡。所以隋朝从上到下，都还没有做好天下已经太平的心理准备。
　　李世民早慧。他也被社会气氛影响。再加上弟弟的谶语，他猜到现在这安稳的生活不会长久。
　　可他一个小孩又能做什么？只能让弟弟赶紧闭嘴，小心被史书里那些野心家捉走。
　　李世民也不敢追问。
　　书本里不都是这么写的？偶然泄露天机无事，但主动泄露天机就可能会有事。而且虽然他年纪还小，也不想听太多未来的事。这样让他有一种会被人牵着鼻子走的别扭感。
　　李世民在家人面前大部分时候脾气和泥捏的似的，但他骨子里却藏着他自己都没察觉的桀骜不驯。
　　李玄霸闭上了嘴，李世民将秘密藏在了心底，连母亲都未告诉。
　　这是只属于他们二人的秘密。
　　两个小孩在心声交流的时候，杨广观察力很强，发现了两人在走神。
　　他先是不悦，然后内心失笑着摇摇头。
　　杨广为了当皇帝压抑自己太久，十几年的演员人生的后果就是他太关注外界的风吹草动，时常草木皆兵。
　　再加上他快继位的时候突然差点功亏一篑，同母兄弟皆反，许多人污蔑他是弑父篡位者，让他太在意是否对他尊敬。
　　但李世民和李玄霸只是两个六岁孩童。
　　神童也是孩子。他们已经很努力地回答皇帝的问话，偶尔走神一下，不值得自己疑神疑鬼。
　　虽然有些波折，但杨广还是顺利地坐上了皇帝的宝座，现在正是志得意满的时候。他对没有威胁的人还是很宽和。
　　见两个孩子已经频繁走神，像是有些累了，杨广让人给李玄霸和李世民赐座，还赏赐他们水果和蜜水，准许他们饿了渴了的时候，可以随意取用。
　　“朕是你们表叔，大可自在些。”杨广温和道。
　　李世民和李玄霸异口同声感激道：“谢陛下！”
　　李玄霸：【腿都站麻了，腰都弯酸了，才让我们坐下，这可真自在。】
　　李世民大着胆子问皇帝要了一个软垫，塞在了李玄霸的背后。
　　杨广宽厚地让两个小孩喝了些蜜水润了润喉咙，才继续发问。
　　他这次问的果然是唐国公府众多亲戚的事，着重问了独孤家。
　　同族联系都很紧密，杨广没必要问唐国公府李氏族亲的事；窦夫人的娘家近亲只剩下年幼的外甥，虽然窦氏家族权势尚存，但杨广知道，近亲和族亲还是不同的。
　　独孤家族因为独孤皇后的缘故在隋文帝时期得到重用，现在独孤老夫人成为独孤家族最年长的人，即使她是外嫁女，但按照鲜卑习俗的残余，独孤老夫人在独孤家族也是有一定话语权的。
　　再者，杨广诛杀和囚禁的兄弟都是同母弟，即都是独孤皇后的儿子。他担心独孤家族会不会有怨言。
　　李渊曾深受杨广的父皇母后喜爱，与隋文帝诸子都十分友善。杨广猜忌李渊会和独孤家族联合起来反对他。
　　这些事李世民暂时还想不到，李玄霸也是现在被询问时才想到。
　　但他想起母亲让他们背谱系，并且着重让他们背独孤家的谱系，并在皇帝询问的时候就立刻一字不漏地背诵。母亲是否已经猜到了杨广的心思？
　　两个孩子仍旧按照之前的计划，非常呆板地你一言我一语把独孤家的谱系，和现在还活着的人所担任的官职背出来。
　　背诵的时候，两人背着手摇头晃脑，眼睛微微眯起，就像是老夫子教导蒙童背《千字文》似的。
　　杨广不由再次扶额失笑：“好了好了，朕知道你们的记忆力很厉害，不用背了。”
　　李玄霸睁大眼，眼睛亮晶晶道：“陛下？不用背了吗？我和二哥提前背了所有和我们家有姻亲的大家族的族谱！”
　　李世民也睁大了眼睛。
　　他是被吓得睁大了眼睛。
　　这这这……阿玄你怎么了？吃错了东西？！
　　哦哦哦。李世民想了起来，弟弟提前和他说过，要装一装正常孩童的模样讨好皇帝。
　　但这表情，这动作，这语气，怎么如此熟悉？
　　李世民陷入沉思。
　　他的沉思，在杨广看来，就是孩童背书背累了再次走神。
　　这次杨广已经不在意两个孩子的走神。他对李玄霸的炫耀很得用，顺着李玄霸的话道：“好了，朕知道你二人聪慧了。赏！”
　　美貌的宫女端来早就准备好的笔墨纸砚。
　　李玄霸将大眼睛笑成了弯弯的月牙，连连感谢皇恩。
　　李世民：“……”
　　李玄霸：【哥，你愣着干什么？给我笑。】
　　听着弟弟平静冷漠的心音，李世民陡然松了一口气。
　　太好了，阿玄没吃错东西QAQ。
　　李玄霸学李世民，李世民就做自己，也将明亮的大眼睛笑成了弯月。
　　杨广看着两个孩子连笑容和音调都极其相似，就像是看到了稀奇的玩具，更觉得有趣了。
　　他对唐国公府的双生子神童本来只是看个稀奇。李世民和李玄霸博得了他的好感后，他再看二人，倒是真的带上了一些看有才华的晚辈的眼神。
　　如果李渊是忠于他的，这两个聪慧的孩子正好留给太子。杨广心想。
　　杨广和他的父皇杨坚一样，既猜忌亲戚，又只信任亲戚。
　　比起外臣，还是亲戚更值得信任一些。
　　杨坚晚年猜忌滥杀忠臣，只信任宗室和外戚，导致杨广继位时皇位差点不稳。
　　杨广收拾了一批宗室和外戚，又走上了杨坚的老路，想培养忠于自己的亲戚取代外臣。
　　李渊是他表兄，兄弟皆亡，其夫人也是孤女，杨广理智上知道若要培养亲戚，李渊是最适合成为他心腹重臣的人。可杨广又担心李渊成为第二个“杨坚”。
　　纠结来纠结去，杨广心里矛盾无比。
　　因着这矛盾，杨广才会连两个六岁的孩童都要试探一番。
　　现在试探完之后，杨广又在反思，身为皇帝，居然从六岁孩童那里试探姨母和李渊是否对他忠诚，似乎有些过了。
　　杨广反思后虽不会自我检讨，但会给对方甜头。
　　他想了想，对身边宦官低语了几句，宦官退出去，再回来的时候，他手中多了一个装满了金子的托盘。
　　杨广笑道：“刚才朕作为皇帝赏过了，这是朕身为长辈给你们的赏钱。”
　　李玄霸甜甜道：“谢表叔！侄儿和哥哥正在和阿姊学经营铺子，自己赚钱花。有了表叔的赏钱，侄儿就能把铺子做强做大，赚很多钱给表叔买礼物！”
　　李世民：“？？！”
　　旁边的弟弟仿佛鬼上身……啊不对，自己上身，李世民吓傻了。
　　还有弟弟，你怎么直接称呼陛下表叔了？！
　　李玄霸：【哥，你今天怎么老发愣？快谢恩。】
　　李世民结结巴巴道：“谢，谢表……表陛下！小儿从未见过这么多金子！”
　　杨广终于忍不住了，撑不住皇帝的形象，笑得肚子都痛了：“什么表陛下？叫表叔就好。李渊难道很穷吗？这么点金子都能让你看傻？”
　　李玄霸抱怨道：“父亲可能不穷，但父亲对我和哥哥很吝啬。”
　　李世民：“……”别模仿我了，哥哥看到小一号的自己，感到毛骨悚然了！
　　“耶耶，耶耶不算吝啬。”李世民结结巴巴道，“对我们很好。”
　　李玄霸偏头问道：“那哥哥你见过这么多金子吗？”
　　李世民摇头。
　　李玄霸道：“可表叔说父亲不穷，父亲却从没给我们看过金子！我所见过的金子只有祖母和母亲的首饰！”
　　李世民迷糊了：“是这样吗？可能是耶耶节省？”
　　李玄霸学着李世民迷糊：“原来是因为耶耶节省吗？”
　　杨广笑得眼泪都出来了：“李渊他可不节省，或许是他的金子都用来买好马了。”
　　李玄霸瞪大眼睛：“什么？父亲养好马了？他也从来没给我和哥哥骑过好马。我和哥哥摸都没摸过。表叔，父亲真的好吝啬啊。”
　　果然。李玄霸心头一沉。
　　在杨广不断试探他和二哥的时候，李玄霸就感到了一丝不对劲。
　　虽然史书盖章杨广生性多疑，但这才大业元年，正是杨广最意气飞扬的时候。李渊还没有大业末年的权势，不过是个郑州刺史兼荥阳太守，杨广不应该对李渊有太多不满才是。
　　李玄霸想起了一则关于母亲的“历史逸闻”。
　　相传李渊在担任扶风太守的时候曾得到几匹骏马，母亲劝李渊送给隋炀帝，李渊舍不得。杨广因此对李渊不满。后来李渊回过劲了，多次向杨广赠送猎鹰骏马，才拜得大将军。李渊那时才感慨已经去世的妻子是对的。
　　李渊喜爱收集骏马，肯定不是从担任扶风太守才开始；杨广对李渊的不满猜忌，肯定也不仅仅是眼馋扶风的这几匹骏马。
　　矛盾原来早就埋下。
　　李世民：“……”这个表情又是学自己，这就是阿玄所说的学人精吗？
　　阿玄，你是个“学哥精”！
　　被李玄霸惊吓了几次后，心大的李世民开始习惯，也卖力地配合起来。
　　虽然他不知道为何阿玄突然说耶耶吝啬，昨天阿玄可没提过这件事。但出于对弟弟的信任，李世民仍旧毫不犹豫地与弟弟一唱一和。
　　“真的吗？不会吧？耶耶真的对我们很好。虽然我确实没有摸过好马。”李世民迟疑道，“是不是耶耶还没有买到好马？所以才不给我们摸。”
　　李玄霸也露出了迟疑的神色：“原来是父亲还没买到好马啊。”
　　杨广擦了擦笑出来的眼泪：“他可不是没有买到好马，只是吝啬。他的爱马连朕都不肯送，何况你们？”
　　李玄霸立刻装出委屈表情：“父亲好吝啬。”
　　李世民已经对李玄霸这个“学哥精”麻木，鹦鹉学舌道：“吝啬。”
　　李玄霸拍着小胸脯道：“表叔，我和哥哥像娘亲一样慷慨，不像父亲那样吝啬。我和哥哥有什么好东西，都会立刻先送给表叔一份！”
　　李玄霸：【哥，你今天发呆的时间怎么这么多？快跟上我。】
　　李世民忙道：“啊对，我和阿玄不吝啬！”
　　杨广笑着对两个孩子招手：“来，来朕这里来。”
　　李玄霸欢快地跳着过去。
　　李世民：“……”原来我平时是这副模样。
　　他也硬着头皮跟上去，和李玄霸一左一右被杨广揉脑袋。
　　“是孝顺的好孩子。窦夫人把你们教得很好。”杨广想起窦氏的模样，心头有些痒。
　　不过他随即想起北周武帝，心头那点瘙痒就消失了。
　　杨坚的女儿嫁给了北周武帝宇文邕的儿子，杨广年少时曾跟随杨坚多次面见宇文邕。北周武帝威严的形象，在杨广心中留下了很深的痕迹。
　　杨广一生少有真正敬佩和向往的人，北周武帝是其中之一。
　　因窦氏和北周武帝眉眼间的相似，让杨广因窦氏姿色太出众而产生的旖旎心思都消失了。
　　想到北周武帝，他仔细打量了李世民和李玄霸的五官。
　　恍惚间，他仿佛又看到了北周武帝的模样。
　　民间有句话，外甥肖舅。窦夫人身为女儿身，眉眼间都与北周武帝有几分相似。那长相肖似窦夫人的李世民和李玄霸，长得像北周武帝也不是什么奇怪的事。
　　不由间，杨广对李世民和李玄霸的好感更深了。
　　如果是宇文家的旁系中有长得像北周武帝的人，杨广立刻就会将其诛杀。
　　但李世民和李玄霸与北周武帝的关系很远了，还是自己的表侄，杨广就高兴了。
　　他一高兴，又是大手一挥，送来一匣子南方进贡来的珍珠，给两个孩子当弹珠玩。
　　李玄霸的眼睛这次真正地弯成了月牙。
　　李世民不住地瞥向弟弟那过于高兴的脸。
　　李玄霸：【瞅什么瞅？】
　　李世民收回视线，十分焦急自己无法用心音和弟弟畅谈。
　　但李世民不回答，李玄霸也知道李世民的表情是什么意思。
　　李玄霸：【你是不是好奇我为何突然演了起来？】
　　李世民眨了眨眼睛。对对对！
　　李玄霸：【看看那一盘堆的满满的金子。】
　　李世民看向金子。
　　李玄霸：【再看看这一匣子顶级的珍珠。】
　　李世民看向珍珠。
　　李玄霸；【赚钱，不寒碜。】
　　李世民：“……”
　　我们好歹是堂堂唐国公府的二公子和三公子，阿玄你至于钻进钱眼里吗！
　　李玄霸：【呵，你不爱钱是不是？你不是还想分府养我吗？就算府邸是皇帝赏你的，修缮府邸要不要钱？新的家具和翻修花园要不要钱？衣食住行要不要钱？你将来还想行军打仗，骏马盔甲兵器粮草，哪样不花钱？难道你想让父亲给你出钱？那兄长可就要闹了。】
　　李世民小小的身躯一颤。
　　李玄霸：【如果我们有钱，就不用仰仗父亲兄长鼻息。而且你也猜到了，乱世将至。没钱招兵买马，你怎么保护我和娘、阿姊？】
　　李世民猛地抬起头，一双丹凤眼硬生生地被他睁大成了圆凤眼。
　　那还等什么？赶紧的！
　　表叔，你看我期盼的眼神，可以再多赏一点！
　　“侄儿没有阿玄聪明，但侄儿骑马射箭学得很快！”李世民眼睛亮晶晶，“将来侄儿要当表叔的冠军侯！”
　　杨广一愣，然后大笑着拍了拍李世民的脑袋：“好，表叔等你长大，给表叔当冠军侯。”
　　虽然教杨广读史的人都不喜欢汉武帝，认为汉武帝穷兵黩武，不是明君。但杨广却非常向往汉武帝纵横天下无所匹敌的强大气魄。
　　汉武帝能做到的事，他也想做到，他还能做得更好！
　　汉武帝有卫青和霍去病。李渊现在看来还不够忠心，不堪为他的卫青。但这个小小的表侄，说不定真的是朕的霍去病？
　　杨广对李玄霸道：“那三郎可要成为朕的霍光？”
　　李玄霸正在震惊。
　　自己拿着自己纵横职场的厚脸皮，模仿二哥扮小孩讨隋炀帝欢心，居然不如二哥一句“冠军侯”？
　　二哥这讨人欢心的本事是与生俱来的吗？！
　　李玄霸正色道：“霍光是权臣，侄儿不愿意为霍光。侄儿愿和二哥成为表叔的萧何韩信！”
　　李世民傻眼：“可是阿玄，韩信被杀了啊。”
　　李玄霸道：“二哥，韩信比霍去病活得长。若非要选一个，你还是当韩信吧。”
　　杨广看着满脸不敢置信的李世民，差点笑得呛到。
　　李世民委屈道：“那侄儿不当霍去病，侄儿当李世民。侄儿是表叔的冠军侯李世民，不是什么霍去病。”
　　杨广笑着拍了拍李世民的脑袋：“好，好，你是朕的冠军侯李世民，不是什么霍去病，也不是什么韩信。”
　　杨广又大手一挥，这次竟然赐给了李世民和李玄霸各一匹小马驹。
　　“李渊吝啬，不给你们摸好马，朕赐给你们好马！”杨广拉着两个孩子的手，大步往西苑的马苑走去，竟然要亲自给李世民和李玄霸挑马。
　　李世民和李玄霸兴高采烈地跟上。
　　李世民是真的兴高采烈，李玄霸是装的。
　　李玄霸：【哥，我不行了，好累。我好想就地一躺呼呼大睡。他能不能走慢点，我跟得好艰难。】
　　李世民只能在兴奋之余抽空给了弟弟一个“坚持”的眼神。
　　弟弟，坚持住啊！正如弟弟你所说的，赚钱，不寒碜！
