Chapter 15: There Is No Shame in Making Money and Asking for Rewards

=

Li Xuanba had indeed made a "slip of the tongue" once before.

At the time, Li Shimin had specifically looked up the posthumous titles. The revelation frightened him so badly that he ate an entire extra flatbread, stuffing himself until he lay groaning on the couch, begging his younger brother to rub his belly.

After that incident, Li Shimin acted as if he had amnesia, never bringing it up to Li Xuanba again. He merely stashed away the pocket money given to him by his grandmother and mother, while throwing himself into his studies and martial arts training with far greater diligence.

Li Shimin had never once doubted Li Xuanba's "prophecy."

During the reign of Emperor Wu of Han, prophetic prognostication was grafted onto Confucianism, using scriptural exegesis to divine the future. By the reign of Emperor Guangwu, the study of apocryphal prophecy reached its absolute peak, and everyone under heaven believed in it.

After the turmoil of the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties, the study of esoteric prophecy had been ground beneath the wheels of war, leaving few superstitious believers. Even so, those in power still fabricated prophecies to manufacture political momentum.

In times of upheaval, seers claiming the gift of prophecy would pop up every few days to read the physiognomy of warlords. Having devoured the history books at an early age, the young Li Shimin had naively believed in all of them, convinced that these people truly possessed the gift of foresight.

Therefore, for his own Ah Xuan to know prophecy was completely normal!

Beyond Li Shimin’s tender age—not yet old enough to suspect his closest twin brother—there was also the fact that prior to the Sui Dynasty, the world had suffered three hundred and sixty years of relentless chaos. Because of this, virtually no one alive expected the Sui Dynasty to last.

From the Three Kingdoms to the brief unification under the Western Jin, the land had swiftly devolved into the Eastern Jin and the Sixteen Barbarian Kingdoms. After a prolonged, bloody melee, it split once more into the standoff between the Northern and Southern Dynasties.

The South saw the Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen dynasties; the North saw Northern Wei, Eastern Wei, Western Wei, Northern Qi, and Northern Zhou. Many of these dynasties coexisted and warred incessantly against one another.

The century-plus of the Northern and Southern Dynasties before the founding of the Sui was one of the most chaotic eras in Chinese history.

Under such conditions, the unification achieved by the Sui was already nothing short of a miracle.

Before this, the only unified dynasties had been the Qin and Han—and Qin had collapsed after just two generations. Thus, from top to bottom, the people of the Sui Dynasty simply had not mentally prepared themselves for the idea that peace was here to stay.

Li Shimin was precociously intelligent. He was naturally influenced by the prevailing social atmosphere. Coupled with his brother's prophecy, he deduced that this current peaceful life would not last.

Yet what could a child do? He could only tell his brother to shut his mouth quickly, lest he be abducted by the ruthless opportunists described in the history books.

Nor did Li Shimin dare to pry.

Wasn't that how it was always written in the books? An accidental leak of heavenly secrets went unpunished, but intentionally revealing them invited disaster. Furthermore, despite his youth, he had no desire to hear too much about the future. It gave him an uncomfortable sensation, like having a ring through his nose, being led by someone else.

In front of his family, Li Shimin's temper was usually as soft as clay, but buried deep within his bones was an untamed defiance that even he had not yet realized.

Li Xuanba kept his mouth shut, and Li Shimin buried the secret deep within his heart, telling not even their mother.

This was a secret that belonged to the two of them alone.

While the two children conversed through their minds, Yang Guang, possessing keen observation, noticed their distraction.

His brow initially furrowed in displeasure, but then he shook his head with an internal, self-mocking chuckle.

Yang Guang had repressed his true nature for far too long in his pursuit of the throne. Over a decade of playing the consummate actor had left him hyper-attuned to the slightest shifts in the wind, forever seeing enemies in every shadow.

Compounding this was how close he had come to falling at the final hurdle just before ascending the throne—his brothers by the same mother had all rebelled, and countless voices slandered him as a patricide and a usurper. It made him obsess over whether others showed him true reverence.

Yet Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were merely two six-year-old boys.

Prodigies were still children. They were already trying their best to answer the emperor's questions; occasional daydreaming was hardly worth his suspicion.

Though the road had been rocky, Yang Guang had ultimately secured the dragon throne, and he was currently basking in his triumph. Toward those who posed no threat, he could afford to be magnanimous.

Seeing the two children repeatedly drifting off, looking somewhat fatigued, Yang Guang ordered seats brought for Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, along with rewards of fruit and honey water, permitting them to refresh themselves at will if they felt hungry or thirsty.

"We are your Cousin-Uncle. You may relax in Our presence," Yang Guang said gently.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba chorused gratefully, "We thank Your Majesty!"

Li Xuanba: *【Our legs were numb from standing, and our backs were aching from bowing, before he finally let us sit down. Relaxed, my foot.】*

Steeling his courage, Li Shimin asked the emperor for a soft cushion and tucked it behind Li Xuanba's back.

Yang Guang generously allowed the two boys to drink some honey water to moisten their throats before resuming his questioning.

Sure enough, this time his inquiries turned toward the numerous relatives of the Duke of Tang's household, with particular emphasis on the Dugu clan.

Clansmen were inherently tied together by blood, so Yang Guang had no need to probe into the Li clan of the Duke of Tang; as for Lady Dou's immediate family, only young nephews remained. Though the Dou clan retained considerable prestige, Yang Guang knew full well the difference between close maternal kin and more distant clan branches.

The Dugu clan, on the other hand, had risen to immense prominence during the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui due to Empress Dugu. Today, the Old Matron Dugu was the most senior elder of the Dugu clan. Even though she was a daughter married out into another family, according to the lingering Xianbei customs of their heritage, she still commanded significant influence within the clan.

Furthermore, the brothers Yang Guang had executed or imprisoned were all his full brothers—the sons of Empress Dugu. He harbored lingering anxieties over whether the Dugu clan bore him deep resentment.

Li Yuan had once been greatly cherished by Yang Guang's imperial parents and had maintained excellent relations with all of Emperor Wen's sons. Yang Guang was paranoid that Li Yuan might ally with the Dugu clan to oppose him.

These grand political machinations were beyond Li Shimin for now, and Li Xuanba had only just realized them upon being questioned.

Yet Li Xuanba recalled how their mother had instructed them to memorize genealogies, emphasizing the Dugu family tree above all, and ordering them to recite it verbatim the moment the emperor inquired. Had their mother already anticipated Yang Guang's thoughts?

Adhering to their prior plan, the two children woodenly traded lines, reciting the Dugu lineage along with the official posts held by all living members.

As they recited, they held their hands behind their backs, swaying their heads from side to side with half-lidded eyes, looking precisely like toddlers being drilled in the *Thousand Character Classic* by a stern old village tutor.

Yang Guang could not help but rest his forehead on his hand and laugh again. "Enough, enough. We are well aware of your remarkable memories. There is no need to continue reciting."

Li Xuanba's eyes widened, shining brightly. "Your Majesty? We don't need to recite anymore? Second Brother and I memorized the lineages of all the prominent families related to us by marriage in advance!"

Li Shimin's eyes widened as well.

His, however, widened in sheer terror.

*What... what is this?! Ah Xuan, what's wrong with you? Did you eat something spoiled?!*

*Oh, right.* Li Shimin suddenly remembered: his younger brother had told him beforehand that they needed to act like normal children to curry favor with the emperor.

*But this expression, these mannerisms, this tone of voice... why does it feel so eerily familiar?*

Li Shimin sank into deep contemplation.

To Yang Guang, this pensive look merely appeared to be a child zoning out again after tiring his brain from reciting books.

This time, Yang Guang paid the children's wandering minds no heed. Li Xuanba’s blatant eagerness to show off was immensely endearing. Playing along with Li Xuanba's words, he laughed, "Very well, We know you two are clever lads. Reward them!"

A graceful palace maid brought forth pre-prepared gifts of the Four Treasures of the Study—fine brushes, inkstones, ink, and paper.

Li Xuanba beamed, his large eyes crinkling into crescent moons as he showered the emperor with effusive thanks.

Li Shimin: "..."

Li Xuanba: *【Brother, what are you standing there for? Smile!】*

Hearing his brother's flat, icy inner voice, Li Shimin breathed a profound sigh of relief.

*Thank goodness, Ah Xuan didn't eat anything spoiled after all QAQ.*

Since Li Xuanba was imitating Li Shimin, Li Shimin simply had to be himself, crinkling his own bright eyes into identical crescent moons.

Watching the two children mirror each other's smiles and lilting tones, Yang Guang felt as if he were looking at a pair of rare, exquisite playthings, finding them thoroughly delightful.

Initially, he had only summoned the Duke of Tang's twin prodigies out of sheer novelty. But now that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had won his favor, the gaze he cast upon them genuinely held the warmth one might show toward talented younger kin.

*If Li Yuan proves loyal, these two brilliant children would serve nicely by the Crown Prince's side in the future,* Yang Guang mused.

Like his father, Yang Jian, before him, Yang Guang both distrusted his relatives and trusted *only* his relatives.

Compared to court officials from outside clans, kin remained far more dependable.

In his declining years, Yang Jian had grown paranoid, indiscriminately executing loyal ministers and placing all his faith in the imperial clan and maternal relatives, which had nearly destabilized Yang Guang's own ascension to the throne.

Having purged a faction of imperial kin and imperial in-laws, Yang Guang was now walking down his father's old path again, seeking to groom loyal relatives to replace the outer court officials.

Li Yuan was his maternal cousin. Li Yuan's brothers were all deceased, and his wife was an orphan. Rationally, Yang Guang knew that if he were to cultivate kin, Li Yuan was the prime candidate to become his core confidant and pillar of state. Yet Yang Guang was equally terrified that Li Yuan might become a second "Yang Jian."

Torn back and forth, Yang Guang was rife with internal contradiction.

It was precisely this internal conflict that had driven him to probe even a pair of six-year-old children.

Now that the test was done, Yang Guang reflected on his actions, feeling that using six-year-olds to gauge whether his maternal aunt and Li Yuan were loyal was somewhat beneath the dignity of an emperor.

Though Yang Guang's reflections never led to self-reproach, he was always willing to offer a little sweetness in recompense.

After a moment's thought, he whispered a few words to a nearby eunuch. The attendant bowed out, and when he returned, he carried a tray piled high with gleaming gold.

Yang Guang chuckled. "What We gave earlier was an imperial reward as your sovereign. This is pocket money from Us as your elder."

Li Xuanba said sweetly, "Thank you, Cousin-Uncle! Brother and I are learning how to run shops from Eldest Sister so we can earn our own spending money. With Cousin-Uncle's reward, I can expand our shops and make them grander, and earn heaps of money to buy presents for Cousin-Uncle!"

Li Shimin: "??!"

Watching his younger brother act like he was possessed by a ghost—no, possessed by *himself*—Li Shimin was utterly terrified.

*And brother, how dare you address His Majesty directly as Cousin-Uncle?!*

Li Xuanba: *【Brother, why are you spacing out so much today? Hurry up and give thanks!】*

Li Shimin stammered, "Th-Thank you, Cousin... Cousin-Majesty! I have never seen so much gold in my life!"

Yang Guang finally broke his regal composure entirely, clutching his stomach as he roared with laughter. "What in the world is a 'Cousin-Majesty'? Just call me Cousin-Uncle. Is Li Yuan truly that destitute? Does this pittance of gold really leave you so starstruck?"

Li Xuanba complained, "Father might not be poor, but he is terribly stingy toward Brother and me."

Li Shimin: "..." *Stop copying me! Seeing a smaller version of myself is giving me goosebumps!*

"Dad... Dad isn't stingy," Li Shimin stammered out loyally. "He is very good to us."

Li Xuanba tilted his head. "Then, Brother, have you ever seen this much gold before?"

Li Shimin shook his head.

Li Xuanba continued, "See? Cousin-Uncle said Father isn't poor, yet Father has never shown us gold! The only gold I've ever seen is Grandmother's and Mother's jewelry!"

Li Shimin was thrown into confusion. "Is that so? Perhaps Dad is just thrifty?"

Li Xuanba mirrored Li Shimin's bewildered look perfectly. "So it's because Dad is thrifty?"

Yang Guang laughed until tears welled in his eyes. "Li Yuan? Thrifty? Hardly. More likely, all his gold went into purchasing fine steeds!"

Li Xuanba's eyes flew wide. "What? Father raises fine steeds? He has never let Brother and me ride a good horse either! We haven't even been allowed to touch one! Cousin-Uncle, Father really is so stingy!"

*As I thought.* Li Xuanba's heart sank slightly.

Throughout Yang Guang's repeated probes of him and his brother, Li Xuanba had sensed something amiss.

Though the history books branded Yang Guang as naturally suspicious, this was merely the first year of the Daye era—the zenith of his ambition and pride. Li Yuan did not yet command the sweeping authority he would possess in the twilight of the Daye era; currently, he was merely the Inspector of Zhengzhou and Governor of Xingyang. Yang Guang should not have held so much grievance against Li Yuan.

Li Xuanba suddenly recalled a "historical anecdote" concerning his mother.

Rumor had it that while Li Yuan was serving as the Governor of Fufeng, he had acquired several exceptional steeds. Lady Dou had urged him to present them to Emperor Yang of Sui, but Li Yuan could not bear to part with them. Yang Guang had grown deeply resentful of Li Yuan as a result. Only later, when Li Yuan came to his senses and repeatedly gifted Yang Guang hunting falcons and swift steeds, was he granted the title of Senior General. Only then did Li Yuan lament that his late wife had been right all along.

Li Yuan's passion for collecting prized horses certainly hadn't begun during his tenure in Fufeng, and Yang Guang's resentment and paranoia toward Li Yuan surely didn't stem merely from coveting a few horses from Fufeng.

The seeds of conflict had been sown long ago.

Li Shimin: "..." *That expression is copied from me again. Is this what Ah Xuan calls a 'copycat'?*

*Ah Xuan, you're a copy-brother!*

Having been shocked by Li Xuanba several times already, the big-hearted Li Shimin was growing used to it and began playing along in earnest.

Though he did not know why Ah Xuan was suddenly painting their father as a miser—Ah Xuan hadn't breathed a word of this yesterday—out of unshakeable trust in his brother, Li Shimin chimed in without hesitation.

"Really? That can't be, can it? Dad truly treats us well. Though it's true I've never touched a fine horse," Li Shimin said hesitantly. "Could it be that Dad hasn't managed to buy a truly good horse yet? That's why he hasn't let us touch them."

Li Xuanba adopted a matching look of hesitation. "So it's because Father hasn't bought a good horse yet..."

Yang Guang wiped away the tears of laughter from the corners of his eyes. "Oh, he's bought them all right; he's just a miser! He won't even part with his beloved horses for Us, so why would he let you touch them?"

Li Xuanba immediately put on a deeply wronged pout. "Father is so stingy."

Thoroughly numb to Li Xuanba's mimicry, Li Shimin repeated like a parrot, "Stingy."

Li Xuanba patted his little chest. "Cousin-Uncle, Brother and I are generous like Mother, not stingy like Father! Whenever Brother and I get our hands on good things, we'll always give Cousin-Uncle a share first!"

Li Xuanba: *【Brother, why are you spacing out so much today? Back me up, quickly!】*

Li Shimin hurriedly chimed in, "Ah, yes! Ah Xuan and I aren't stingy at all!"

Yang Guang beamed and beckoned the two boys closer. "Come, come here to Us."

Li Xuanba bounded over merrily.

Li Shimin: "..." *Is that really what I look like usually?*

Hardening his resolve, he followed, allowing Yang Guang to ruffle their hair, one on each side.

"Filial, good boys. Lady Dou has raised you well." A vision of Lady Dou's striking visage flashed through Yang Guang's mind, stirring a faint itch in his heart.

Yet as the memory of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou surfaced, that fleeting spark vanished entirely.

Yang Jian's daughter had married the son of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, Yuwen Yong. In his youth, Yang Guang had accompanied Yang Jian to audience with Yuwen Yong on numerous occasions. The awe-inspiring majesty of Emperor Wu had left an indelible imprint on Yang Guang's soul.

In his entire life, Yang Guang had truly respected and aspired to be like very few men, and Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou was undeniably one of them.

It was precisely the resemblance between Lady Dou's features and those of Emperor Wu that snuffed out any inappropriate thoughts born from her exceptional beauty.

Thinking of Emperor Wu, he studied the facial features of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba more closely.

For a fleeting moment, it seemed as though the countenance of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou had materialized before him once more.

As the common saying went, a nephew resembled his maternal uncle. Even as a woman, Lady Dou bore a striking resemblance to Emperor Wu in the brow and eyes. It was hardly surprising, then, that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, who took after Lady Dou, should also resemble Emperor Wu.

Involuntarily, Yang Guang's fondness for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba deepened.

Had a distant scion of the Yuwen clan borne such a resemblance to Emperor Wu, Yang Guang would have executed him on the spot.

Yet Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were far removed from the imperial line of Northern Zhou and were his own cousin-nephews. This only brought Yang Guang delight.

In his exuberant mood, he waved his sleeve again, ordering a casket of tribute pearls from the south to be brought forward so the two children could play with them like marbles.

This time, Li Xuanba's eyes truly crinkled into crescent moons.

Li Shimin kept sneaking glances at his brother's overly joyous expression.

Li Xuanba: *【What are you staring at?】*

Li Shimin averted his gaze, painfully frustrated by his inability to communicate back through their minds.

Yet even without a reply, Li Xuanba understood his brother's expression completely.

Li Xuanba: *【Are you wondering why I suddenly started putting on a show?】*

Li Shimin blinked. *Yes, yes, exactly!*

Li Xuanba: *【Look at that tray piled high with gold.】*

Li Shimin looked at the gold.

Li Xuanba: *【Now look at this box of top-grade pearls.】*

Li Shimin looked at the pearls.

Li Xuanba: *【Making money is nothing to be ashamed of.】*

Li Shimin: "..."

*We are the proud second and third young masters of the Duke of Tang's household! Ah Xuan, must you throw yourself into the pursuit of coin like this?!*

Li Xuanba: *【Heh, you think you don't need money? Didn't you say you wanted to establish your own manor and support me? Even if the emperor grants you an estate, doesn't it cost money to renovate it? Don't new furniture and garden repairs cost money? What about food, clothing, and daily living? You dream of leading armies into battle in the future—fine steeds, armor, weapons, grain, provisions—which of those doesn't cost a fortune? Do you expect Father to pay for all of it? If he does, Eldest Brother will throw a fit.】*

Li Shimin's little frame trembled.

Li Xuanba: *【If we have our own money, we won't have to live at the mercy of Father and Eldest Brother. Besides, as you've already guessed, chaotic times are coming. Without money to recruit soldiers and buy horses, how are you going to protect Mother, Eldest Sister, and me?】*

Li Shimin snapped his head up, his phoenix eyes stretching wide into fiery saucers.

*Then what are we waiting for? Bring it on!*

*Cousin-Uncle, look at the longing in my eyes! You can reward us with plenty more!*

"I am not as clever as Ah Xuan, but I learn riding and archery very quickly!" Li Shimin proclaimed, eyes glittering with ambition. "In the future, I will be Cousin-Uncle's Champion Marquis!"

Yang Guang froze, then burst into hearty laughter, patting Li Shimin's head. "Splendid! Cousin-Uncle will wait for you to grow up and become My Champion Marquis."

Although the tutors who taught Yang Guang history had always disapproved of Emperor Wu of Han, criticizing him as a warmonger rather than an enlightened ruler, Yang Guang secretly yearned for the sweeping, peerless might of Emperor Wu striding across the world.

Whatever Emperor Wu of Han could achieve, he wished to achieve as well—and do it even better!

Emperor Wu had Wei Qing and Huo Qubing. Li Yuan currently appeared insufficiently loyal, unworthy of being his Wei Qing. Yet this tiny cousin-nephew of his... might he truly become Yang Guang's Huo Qubing?

Yang Guang turned to Li Xuanba with a grin. "Then does Sanlang wish to become Our Huo Guang?"

Li Xuanba was reeling in shock.

*I wielded the shamelessness honed from years in the modern corporate grind, debasing myself to imitate my brother and act like a spoiled child just to flatter the Emperor of Sui... and it gets completely outdone by my brother's single line about the 'Champion Marquis'?!*

*Is this guy's talent for winning hearts literally innate?!*

Li Xuanba assumed a grave, solemn expression. "Huo Guang was an overbearing regent; I do not wish to be a Huo Guang. I wish to stand alongside my brother and become Cousin-Uncle's Xiao He and Han Xin!"

Li Shimin was stunned. "Wait, Ah Xuan, Han Xin was executed!"

Li Xuanba countered, "Second Brother, Han Xin lived much longer than Huo Qubing. If we must choose, you'd better be Han Xin."

Watching Li Shimin's utterly incredulous expression, Yang Guang nearly choked on his own laughter.

Li Shimin pouted with wounded pride. "Then I won't be Huo Qubing! I'll just be Li Shimin! I am Cousin-Uncle's Champion Marquis Li Shimin, not some Huo Qubing!"

Yang Guang laughed warmly and patted Li Shimin's head once more. "Good, good! You are Our Champion Marquis Li Shimin, not Huo Qubing, and certainly not Han Xin."

With another sweeping wave of his sleeve, Yang Guang went a step further, bestowing a young foal upon both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

"Since Li Yuan is too stingy to let you touch fine horses, We shall grant you fine horses Ourselves!" Clasping the two boys by the hand, Yang Guang strode toward the royal stables of the Western Park, fully intending to handpick the foals for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba himself.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba followed along with boundless enthusiasm.

Li Shimin's joy was completely genuine; Li Xuanba's was entirely feigned.

Li Xuanba: *【Brother, I'm done for. I'm exhausted. I just want to drop to the ground right here and sleep like a log. Can't he walk any slower? Keeping up with him is killing me.】*

Amid his soaring excitement, Li Shimin could only spare a reassuring glance back at his brother.

*Hang in there, Brother! Just as you said—making money is nothing to be ashamed of!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第16章 卖艺讨赏不寒碜
chunks.chineseText:
第16章 卖艺讨赏不寒碜

=
　　窦夫人陪着萧皇后说了一会儿话， 表面上陪笑，心里一直惦记着孩子。
　　萧皇后知道窦夫人惦记孩子，但皇帝没有让她放人， 她不敢放。
　　杨广伪装了十几年， 能骗得过隋文帝和独孤皇后， 却骗不过枕边人。
　　即使杨广为了讨得独孤皇后的喜爱，独宠萧皇后十几年。但萧皇后也知道，杨广不是隋文帝， 她也不敢是独孤皇后。
　　所以萧皇后对杨广刚继位就大兴土木虽有微词，也只敢委婉进谏。
　　但杨广可能没听懂，一直没有在意萧皇后的进谏。
　　不过萧皇后倒没有对现在的处境不满意。
　　萧皇后是被大隋所灭的西梁孝明帝之女。西梁虽灭， 但兰陵萧氏尚存。萧皇后入宫时，就得族人耳提面命， 兰陵萧氏是否重获荣光， 全系于萧皇后一人之身。
　　萧皇后在杨广夺嫡的时候也使出了浑身解数，为杨广夺嫡增益不少。
　　现在杨广虽然恢复本性，不再独宠她，也不听她的谏言，但对她仍旧尊重， 兰陵萧氏也是恩遇不断，“缌麻以上， 并随才擢用，于是诸萧昆弟布列朝廷”。
　　兰陵萧氏复兴，皇帝之子又俱是自己所生， 她一生所愿皆得所偿。况且她比皇帝大三岁， 如今已经三十九岁， 想争宠也争不过， 得皇帝敬重就够了。
　　萧皇后过得很舒心，眉间没有多少皱纹，仍旧能窥见当年一二风华。
　　她见窦夫人焦急，抚着窦夫人的手温婉道：“我听闻二郎和三郎受了荥阳郑氏的气。窦夫人为何不来寻我？荥阳郑氏不愿意结亲就罢了，惯得他们！”
　　窦夫人苦笑道：“国公早就与荥阳郑氏定下了这门婚事，只是没寻得合适的人，倒不是他们不愿意结亲。唉，我家二郎和三郎脾气直爽，受不得挑衅，有些过于无礼了。”
　　萧皇后笑道：“既然是郑氏子弟先挑衅，二郎和三郎不过是反击而已，哪叫无礼？我看郑氏才无礼。我见二郎和三郎很喜欢。”
　　窦夫人叹气：“二郎三郎确实讨人喜欢，可惜就是身体太弱，令我揪心。”
　　萧皇后皱眉：“身体弱？孩童年幼，时常生病很正常，窦夫人无须太过忧心。”
　　窦夫人摇摇头，用帕子擦了擦眼角，道：“不能不担心啊。都是我的错，寻常孩童年幼时就容易生病，我一胎双子，他们二人自娘胎里就不足。二郎和三郎自出生起，汤药就没断过。他们性情越是活泼，我就越心焦。”
　　她说着说着，回想起李玄霸的病弱，和李世民这次遭的罪，眼泪真的流了出来。
　　窦夫人哽咽道：“我就不该把他们带去荥阳！两个孩子身体稍好了一些，就闹着要去见父亲。我以为会无事的，我……呜……”
　　窦夫人用帕子捂着嘴，泣不成声。
　　萧皇后见状，一边温言安抚，一边赐下药材，让窦夫人别太忧心。
　　她心里叹了口气。
　　她听闻李二郎和李三郎的聪慧，心中萌生了让兰陵萧氏和这一对双生子结亲的念头。
　　兰陵萧氏虽没有双生女，但年龄相仿的堂姐妹还是有的。以“姐妹嫁双生子”是佳话的借口，说不得能让两个萧氏女进入唐国公府内宅。
　　两姐妹联合起来，不一定不能帮这对双生子之一夺得唐国公的爵位。
　　即便是不行，李家二郎和三郎是皇帝的表侄，自己又有本事，哄得他们好好辅佐太子，待太子继位时，他们二人也少不得高官厚禄，可以帮衬家里。
　　没想到，李二郎和李三郎居然身体不好？
　　萧皇后有些怀疑窦夫人是不是看出了自己想要结亲的心思，故意找借口推脱。
　　但窦夫人哭得情真意切，李二郎和李三郎是否多病又是能随意打听到的事，萧皇后以为窦夫人应该不会用会被轻松揭穿的借口敷衍自己，便信了这件事。
　　窦夫人确实是看出了萧皇后想要结亲的意思。
　　“五姓七望”是山东士族的“首领”，但天下名门并非只有山东士族。天下名门一共有“四姓”——“侨姓”“吴姓”“郡姓”“虏姓”。
　　“侨姓”是衣冠南渡的名门，以“王、谢、袁、萧”为大；“吴姓”是原本吴地的名门，以“朱、张、顾、陆”为首；山东和关中的名门皆为“郡姓”，山东名门地位高于关中名门，以“五姓七望”为尊；代北胡人贵族称“虏姓”，除八柱国后裔外，还有“长孙、陆、源、窦”最为显赫。
　　唐代柳芳的《氏族论》言，隋唐之前，“举秀才，州主簿，郡功曹，非四姓不选”。可见其显贵。
　　虽然隋文帝建立隋朝后，举荐不再限制出身，但朝中外姓官吏仍旧以“四姓”为主。
　　在争夺中原名门的斗争中，“吴姓”“关中郡姓”稍逊一筹，“侨姓”和“山东郡姓”一直打得有来有回。
　　因南北朝争夺中，最终是以“北朝”胜出，“山东郡姓”便压了“侨姓”一头。但“侨姓”可不会就这么认了。
　　窦夫人一点都不想自家卷入汉族名门的斗争中。
　　若是家中儿媳既有“郡姓”，又有“侨姓”，那这个家就别想安稳了。
　　李玄霸确实是体弱。李世民一直陪着李玄霸。李玄霸不出门，李世民也不出门。窦夫人担心兄弟二人因为身体健康不同而心生间隙，从不对外说李世民身体健康。所以她不怕萧皇后去查。
　　窦夫人原本没想过给双生子太早定下婚事，但萧皇后居然盯上两个孩子，为了家门安宁，她只能赶紧去为两个孩子早早寻一门亲事了。可三郎这身体……唉，窦夫人真不知道自己能不能为三郎寻得一个合适的人选。
　　窦夫人一边哭，一边心焦不已。
　　另一边，她挂念的两个儿子却快活得和雏鸟似的，围着小马驹叽叽喳喳叫个不停。
　　李世民在叫，李玄霸在演。
　　有些事仿佛是命中注定一般。
　　李世民学骑射的时候骑过温顺的小马。那时他对马的感觉就那样，虽然喜欢骑马，但对马没有特殊的感情。
　　但杨广为他选的小马驹，李世民就抱着马脖子，对小马驹一见钟情，力气大得小马使劲挣扎都挣扎不出来。
　　李玄霸也想尝试着学习二哥对马发花痴。但他走近之后，马“呲”了他一下，他就打消了主意，并后退三步。
　　他可没有二哥那么大的力气，放弃。
　　无论是李世民抱着小马驹狂蹭的模样，还是李玄霸向前三步又倒退三步的模样，都让杨广忍不住大笑。
　　杨广今日大笑的次数，抵得过之前一整月。
　　自他决定修东京、修运河时，朝堂就有无数嘈杂的声音，令他厌烦。他已经很久没有如此开怀大笑了。
　　“好了，二郎松手，马要踢你了。”杨广慈爱地揉了揉李世民的脑袋，“你就在西苑多住些时日，把马驯服了，表叔带你去游猎。”
　　李世民高兴道：“好！谢表叔！阿玄！快说谢谢啊！”
　　李玄霸：“……谢表叔。”
　　李玄霸忍不住在心中大喊：【哥！谢什么谢！快点想办法！皇帝要让我们留在西苑！】
　　李世民装作没听见。
　　李玄霸絮絮叨叨劝说：【哥，我知道你喜爱骏马。但骏马不是已经赐给你了吗？我们留在西苑，娘亲会担心。】
　　李世民把脸埋在了马脖子上。我再挣扎会儿。
　　李玄霸还想继续劝说，杨广却已经下令给两个孩子腾屋子，就住在萧皇后附近，让萧皇后帮忙照顾。
　　至于窦夫人，杨广对李渊的芥蒂因这两个孩子稍稍消失了一些，决定给李渊机会，自然不会和李渊生出误会，所以没留窦夫人在西苑居住，以免传出不好的传闻。
　　杨广还贴心地派人送窦夫人离开洛阳，并询问窦夫人是想回大兴还是回李渊身边。
　　至于这两个表侄，杨广要效仿先皇，把他们养在身边一段时日。
　　杨广已经决定八月十五就去江都巡游，这两个孩子，他准备带在身边。
　　这是莫大的荣誉。
　　李世民震惊抬头，李玄霸在心底喊“哦豁”。
　　窦夫人听到这个诏令后哭声一停，面露喜色，叩首谢恩。
　　她的指甲掐进了手心。
　　住在西苑，还要随驾南下巡游江都？！我两个孩子才六岁啊！他们哪经得起长时间离开父母长途跋涉？何况伴君如伴虎，两个孩子如果惹了皇帝不快该如何是好？他们只是大臣之子，唐国公的名号在皇帝身边可没有用，他们被人亏待该如何是好？
　　虽然李世民和李玄霸早慧，或许能讨好皇帝，赚得一个较为舒适的环境。但毕竟不比家中，窦夫人不信他们能过得舒心。而且小小孩童如此殚精竭虑，也伤身体啊！
　　窦夫人心中极恨，不知道为何皇帝会突然心血来潮。
　　她焦急万分，心中却想不出任何应对的方法，只能竭力露出欣喜和自豪的表情，不让皇后看出自己心中的不情不愿。
　　隋朝皇帝一家心胸都极其狭小，可不会体恤她一片慈母之情。
　　好在萧皇后是有儿女的人，刚刚窦夫人又因为担忧两个孩子体弱哭了一场，窦夫人没表现出来，她也能了解窦夫人心中的担忧。
　　她宽慰道：“陛下让我来带两个孩子，表嫂还不信我？”
　　萧皇后都称呼窦夫人为表嫂了，窦夫人只能强装笑颜：“信，二郎和三郎能得皇后教导，是妾身之幸事。”
　　她更加担忧了。
　　皇后有让兰陵萧氏和二郎三郎结亲的意图，如果她与二郎三郎相处久之后，又生出心思怎么办？
　　窦夫人决定先去找丈夫商议，然后立刻回大兴，赶紧与二郎三郎相看亲事。
　　虽她一时半会儿可能相不得合适的人选，但可以先相看家族，然后待孩子稍稍长大一些后，再相看族中适合的女子。
　　长子李建成就是如此相看的。他早早就定下和荥阳郑氏联姻，只是没寻得合适的女子，才迟迟没有定亲。
　　只要唐国公府已经订好和某个家族联姻的意愿，皇后兰陵萧氏的出身，就会成为她做出阻拦别人联姻之事的障碍。
　　名门联姻中有许多“潜规则”，皇后既然在乎她那兰陵萧氏的出身，就不会打破名门的“潜规则”。
　　既然已经决定让两个孩子留下，皇帝那里应该试探结束了。萧皇后便带着窦夫人一同面圣。
　　窦夫人的心揪成一团，脑海中全是孩子们强颜欢笑讨好皇帝的模样。
　　谁知道她还未看到两个孩子，就听见李世民响亮的笑声。
　　“哈哈哈哈，表叔，说好的，不可以反悔！我赢啦我赢啦！”
　　“行行行，你赢了，给你。”
　　“谢表叔赏赐！阿玄，快说谢谢！”
　　“谢表叔赏赐。但表叔，别太纵容哥哥，哥哥是谁给他几分颜色，他就能去开个染坊的胡闹性子。”
　　“阿玄，你怎么能这么说你哥哥。表叔，别理他，我们继续比！”
　　窦夫人先面色一僵，然后面色微沉。
　　萧皇后用帕子捂嘴微笑：“你说你家二郎活泼，看来是真活泼，看着不像是体弱的人。”
　　窦夫人眼露悲哀道：“正因为如此，我才揪心。唉，他爱玩爱闹，却和郑氏子弟赌斗背了一会儿书，就病了好几月。”
　　萧皇后叹气道：“辛苦你了。不过孩子活泼是好事，多动一动，身体总会好的。”
　　萧皇后带着窦夫人穿过曲折的花廊，视野豁然开朗。
　　李世民一手挽弓，一手搭箭。李玄霸头上立着的大蒲团上，已经插了三支没有箭头的箭。
　　“嗖”的一声，第四支箭飞了出去，稳稳地扎上李玄霸头顶松松软软的的大蒲团。
　　窦夫人深吸一口气，眼前一黑，伸手扶住旁边仆妇的手，才勉强站稳了身体。
　　萧皇后再次疑惑地看向窦夫人：“你说……二郎这样，真的是体弱？”
　　窦夫人：“……”好想把二郎按在膝盖上狠揍一顿！
　　李世民！你就是这么带弟弟？！你居然让弟弟顶着靶子，你往弟弟头上射箭？！
　　窦夫人脸上狰狞一闪而逝，看得萧皇后心头一颤。
　　她随即醒悟：“你担心他用力过猛，又生病了？”
　　窦夫人深呼吸：“是、是啊。唉，二郎和三郎都极其敬重父亲，努力学习射箭，可是……唉。”
　　李世民听到了窦夫人的声音，立刻转身：“娘亲？”
　　他摊开胳膊，露出脖子上挂着的金银珠宝链子：“娘亲娘亲，你看！我赢了好多表叔的赏赐！”
　　杨广大笑着，又挂了一串绿松石佛珠在李世民脖子上。
　　窦夫人再次倒吸一口气，呼吸停滞，眼前一黑。
　　李世民你在做什么！向皇帝卖艺吗！谁教你的！！
　　李玄霸心虚地移开视线。
　　对不起，我的主意，我教的。

# Chapter 16: Performing for Rewards is Nothing to Be Ashamed Of

Lady Dou chatted with Empress Xiao for a while, smiling on the outside while her heart remained entirely focused on her children.

Empress Xiao knew Lady Dou was worried about her children, but since the Emperor had not given the word to release them, she did not dare to let them go.

Yang Guang had worn a mask for over a decade, successfully deceiving Emperor Wen of Sui and Empress Dugu, but he could not deceive the woman who shared his bed.

Even though Yang Guang had doted on Empress Xiao exclusively for over a decade to win the favor of Empress Dugu, Empress Xiao knew that Yang Guang was no Emperor Wen, and she dared not try to be another Empress Dugu.

Thus, although Empress Xiao had reservations about Yang Guang embarking on massive construction projects immediately upon ascending the throne, she only dared to offer gentle, roundabout advice.

Yet Yang Guang had likely failed to grasp her meaning, completely ignoring her subtle counsel.

Even so, Empress Xiao was not dissatisfied with her current situation.

Empress Xiao was the daughter of Emperor Xiaoming of Western Liang, a state destroyed by the Great Sui. Though Western Liang was gone, the Lanling Xiao clan endured. When Empress Xiao entered the palace, her clansmen had repeatedly drilled into her that the revival of the Lanling Xiao clan's glory rested entirely upon her shoulders.

During Yang Guang’s struggle for the throne, Empress Xiao had exerted every ounce of her strength, providing him with invaluable assistance.

Now, although Yang Guang had reverted to his true nature, no longer doting on her exclusively or listening to her advice, he still treated her with respect. The Lanling Xiao clan continued to receive endless imperial favor; "those within the mourning degrees of *sima* and above were promoted according to their talents, so that the various brothers of the Xiao clan were arrayed throughout the imperial court."

With the Lanling Xiao clan restored to prominence and the Emperor's sons all born of her own womb, her lifelong wishes had been fulfilled. Furthermore, she was three years older than the Emperor, now thirty-nine years of age. She could not compete for favor even if she wanted to; the Emperor's respect was more than enough.

Empress Xiao lived a comfortable life. Her brow bore few wrinkles, and one could still catch a glimpse of her legendary beauty from years past.

Seeing Lady Dou's anxiety, she patted her hand and said gently, "I heard that Erlang and Sanlang suffered at the hands of the Zheng clan of Xingyang. Why did you not come to me, Lady Dou? If the Zheng clan of Xingyang does not wish to form a marriage alliance, so be it. Who do they think they are, behaving so insolently!"

Lady Dou gave a bitter smile. "The Duke of Tang had long agreed to this marriage alliance with the Zheng clan of Xingyang, but we simply had not found a suitable match yet. It is not that they were unwilling. Sigh, my Erlang and Sanlang have straightforward temperaments and cannot tolerate provocation. They were somewhat too impolite."

Empress Xiao smiled. "Since it was the Zheng youth who provoked them first, Erlang and Sanlang were merely retaliating. How is that impolite? If you ask me, it is the Zheng clan that is rude. I find Erlang and Sanlang highly endearing."

Lady Dou sighed. "Erlang and Sanlang are indeed endearing, but unfortunately, their health is far too weak. It breaks my heart."

Empress Xiao frowned. "Weak health? Children are young; it is only normal for them to fall ill from time to time. You need not worry too much, Lady Dou."

Lady Dou shook her head, dabbing the corners of her eyes with a handkerchief. "How can I not worry? It is all my fault. Normal children fall ill easily when young, but I carried twins, and they have suffered from a congenital deficiency since they were in my womb. Ever since Erlang and Sanlang were born, they have never stopped taking medicinal decoctions. The more lively they act, the more anxious I become."

As she spoke, she recalled Li Xuanba's frail health and the suffering Li Shimin had endured this time, and real tears began to flow.

Lady Dou choked up. "I should never have brought them to Xingyang! As soon as the two children's health improved slightly, they clamored to see their father. I thought nothing would go wrong. I... *sob*..."

Lady Dou covered her mouth with her handkerchief, weeping uncontrollably.

Seeing this, Empress Xiao comforted her with gentle words while bestowing precious medicinal herbs, urging Lady Dou not to worry too much.

Inwardly, she sighed.

Having heard of the intelligence of Li Erlang and Li Sanlang, she had harbored the intention of arranging a marriage alliance between the Lanling Xiao clan and these twin brothers.

Although the Lanling Xiao clan had no twin daughters, there were cousin sisters of similar ages. Using the poetic excuse of "sisters marrying twin brothers" as a charming tale, she might have been able to place two daughters of the Xiao clan into the inner chambers of the Duke of Tang's estate.

If the two sisters joined forces, they might even be able to help one of the twins seize the title of Duke of Tang.

Even if that failed, the Li family's Erlang and Sanlang were the Emperor's cousin-nephews and possessed great talent. If she could coax them into assisting the Crown Prince, they would surely receive high offices and handsome salaries when the Crown Prince ascended the throne, allowing them to support her maternal family.

Who would have thought that Li Erlang and Li Sanlang actually suffered from poor health?

Empress Xiao suspected that Lady Dou might have seen through her matchmaking intentions and was deliberately using this as an excuse to decline.

However, Lady Dou's tears were genuine, and whether Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were sickly was something that could easily be verified with a simple inquiry. Empress Xiao reasoned that Lady Dou would not use an excuse so easily exposed to placate her, and thus she believed it.

Lady Dou had indeed seen through Empress Xiao's matchmaking intentions.

The "Five Surnames and Seven Clans" were the leaders of the Shandong gentry, but they were not the only prestigious families in the realm. The great noble families of the world were divided into "Four Categories of Surnames": the "Qiao Surnames" (emigré clans), the "Wu Surnames" (Jiangnan clans), the "Jun Surnames" (regional commandery clans), and the "Lu Surnames" (Xianbei/northern clans).

The "Qiao Surnames" were the prestigious clans that had migrated south during the disaster of Yongjia, with the Wang, Xie, Yuan, and Xiao clans being the greatest. The "Wu Surnames" were the original noble clans of the Wu region, led by the Zhu, Zhang, Gu, and Lu clans. The noble families of Shandong and Guanzhong were all "Jun Surnames"; the Shandong clans held a higher status than those of Guanzhong, with the "Five Surnames and Seven Clans" being the most revered. The Xianbei noble clans of Daibei were called the "Lu Surnames"; aside from the descendants of the Eight Pillar States, the Zhangsun, Lu, Yuan, and Dou clans were the most prominent.

As Liu Fang's *Treatise on Clans* in the Tang dynasty would later state, prior to the Sui and Tang dynasties, "none but those of the Four Categories of Surnames were selected as refined talents, provincial administrators, or commandery officials." This showed just how illustrious they were.

Although Emperor Wen of Sui had established the Sui dynasty and removed birthright restrictions on recommendations, the court officials of other surnames were still predominantly from the "Four Categories."

In the struggle for dominance among the Central Plains' noble families, the "Wu Surnames" and "Guanzhong Jun Surnames" were slightly inferior, while the "Qiao Surnames" and "Shandong Jun Surnames" had always locked horns in a fierce, back-and-forth rivalry.

Because the Northern Dynasties ultimately emerged victorious in the struggles of the Northern and Southern Dynasties, the "Shandong Jun Surnames" had gained the upper hand over the "Qiao Surnames." But the "Qiao Surnames" would never simply accept defeat.

Lady Dou did not want her family entangled in the struggles of the Han noble clans in the slightest.

If her daughters-in-law included both a "Jun Surname" and a "Qiao Surname," her household would never know peace.

Li Xuanba was indeed of weak constitution. Li Shimin had always stayed by his side; when Li Xuanba did not go out, Li Shimin did not go out either. Fearing that the two brothers might grow distant due to the difference in their physical health, Lady Dou never spoke of Li Shimin's robust health to outsiders. Thus, she was not afraid of Empress Xiao investigating.

Lady Dou had not originally planned to arrange marriages for the twins so early. However, now that Empress Xiao had set her sights on the two children, she had no choice but to quickly find betrothals for them to ensure the peace of her household. But with Sanlang's body... sigh, Lady Dou truly did not know if she could find a suitable match for him.

Lady Dou wept while her heart burned with anxiety.

Meanwhile, the two sons she was so worried about were as happy as fledglings, chattering excitedly around a little foal.

Li Shimin was shouting with joy, while Li Xuanba was putting on a performance.

Some things seemed to be written in the stars.

When Li Shimin learned riding and archery, he had ridden gentle ponies. Back then, his feelings toward horses were ordinary; though he enjoyed riding, he had no special affection for them.

But with the little foal Yang Guang had chosen for him, Li Shimin threw his arms around its neck, falling in love at first sight. He held on with such immense strength that the foal could not break free no matter how hard it struggled.

Li Xuanba also wanted to try mimicking his second brother's infatuation with the horse. But as soon as he drew near, the foal snorted aggressively at him. He immediately abandoned the idea and took three steps back.

He did not possess his second brother's monstrous strength. He gave up.

Whether it was the sight of Li Shimin rubbing his face wildly against the foal, or Li Xuanba taking three steps forward only to retreat three steps, Yang Guang could not help but burst into hearty laughter.

The number of times Yang Guang laughed today exceeded his laughter over the entire past month.

Ever since he decided to construct the Eastern Capital and dig the Grand Canal, the court had been filled with countless noisy, irritating voices that vexed him. It had been a very long time since he had laughed so merrily.

"Alright, Erlang, let go. The horse is going to kick you." Yang Guang affectionately patted Li Shimin's head. "You shall stay in the Western Park for a few more days. Once you have tamed the horse, your Imperial Uncle will take you out hunting."

Li Shimin said joyfully, "Great! Thank you, Imperial Uncle! Ah Xuan! Quick, say thank you!"

Li Xuanba: "...Thank you, Imperial Uncle."

Li Xuanba could not help but scream in his heart: *[Brother! Why are you thanking him! Quick, think of something! The Emperor wants us to stay in the Western Park!]*

Li Shimin pretended not to hear.

Li Xuanba nagged and pleaded: *[Brother, I know you love fine horses. But hasn't the horse already been bestowed upon you? If we stay in the Western Park, Mother will worry.]*

Li Shimin buried his face in the foal's neck. *Let me hold out a little longer.*

Li Xuanba wanted to continue persuading him, but Yang Guang had already ordered a room to be prepared for the two children near Empress Xiao's quarters, asking her to help look after them.

As for Lady Dou, Yang Guang's grudge against Li Yuan had dissipated slightly because of these two children. Having decided to give Li Yuan a chance, he naturally did not want to cause any misunderstandings with him. Thus, he did not keep Lady Dou in the Western Park to avoid any unsavory rumors.

Yang Guang even considerately sent men to escort Lady Dou out of Luoyang, asking whether she wished to return to Daxing or go to Li Yuan's side.

As for these two cousin-nephews, Yang Guang intended to follow the late Emperor's example and keep them by his side for a time.

Yang Guang had already decided to embark on a southern tour to Jiangdu on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month, and he planned to bring these two children along.

This was an immense honor.

Li Shimin raised his head in shock, while Li Xuanba cried out "Uh-oh" in his heart.

Upon hearing this imperial decree, Lady Dou's weeping stopped abruptly. A look of joy washed over her face as she kowtowed to express her gratitude.

Yet her fingernails dug deep into her palms.

*Staying in the Western Park, and even accompanying the imperial entourage south to Jiangdu?! My two children are only six years old! How can they endure traveling such long distances away from their parents for so long? Moreover, serving a ruler is like keeping company with a tiger. What if the two children displease the Emperor? They are merely the sons of a minister; the title of Duke of Tang holds no weight before the Emperor. What if they are mistreated?*

*Although Li Shimin and Li Xuanba are precocious and might be able to please the Emperor to secure a relatively comfortable environment, it is still no match for home. I do not believe they can live comfortably. Besides, for such young children to constantly rack their brains will surely harm their health!*

Lady Dou felt a deep resentment in her heart, utterly baffled by the Emperor's sudden whim.

She was anxious beyond measure, yet she could think of no way to counter this. She could only force an expression of joy and pride, determined not to let the Empress see her reluctance.

The imperial family of the Sui dynasty was notoriously narrow-minded; they would never sympathize with her maternal devotion.

Fortunately, Empress Xiao had children of her own. Since Lady Dou had just wept over her children's weak health, even though Lady Dou did not show her reluctance now, the Empress could understand her maternal anxiety.

She comforted her, saying, "His Majesty has entrusted me with the two children. Does Cousin-in-law not trust me?"

Since Empress Xiao had addressed her as "Cousin-in-law," Lady Dou could only force a smile. "I do. It is the fortune of this humble handmaid that Erlang and Sanlang can receive Your Majesty's guidance."

Yet her worries only deepened.

The Empress harbored intentions of marrying girls from the Lanling Xiao clan to Erlang and Sanlang. If she spent a long time with them, what if those thoughts resurfaced?

Lady Dou decided to consult her husband first, then immediately return to Daxing to quickly arrange betrothals for Erlang and Sanlang.

Although she might not find suitable candidates right away, she could first select the families, and then choose suitable daughters from those clans once the children grew slightly older.

Her eldest son, Li Jiancheng, had been betrothed in this exact manner. He had long been set to marry into the Zheng clan of Xingyang, but because they had not found a suitable girl, the wedding had been delayed.

As long as the Duke of Tang's estate had already established an intent to marry into a certain family, Empress Xiao's background from the Lanling Xiao clan would prevent her from interfering with another clan's alliance.

There were many "unwritten rules" in noble marriages. Since the Empress cared deeply about her Lanling Xiao lineage, she would not break the unwritten rules of the great clans.

Since the decision had been made for the two children to stay, the Emperor's testing of them should have concluded. Empress Xiao then led Lady Dou to have an audience with the Emperor.

Lady Dou's heart was in her throat, her mind filled with images of her children forcing smiles to please the Emperor.

Yet before she even laid eyes on the two children, she heard Li Shimin's boisterous laughter.

"Hahaha! Imperial Uncle, we had a deal, you cannot go back on your word! I won, I won!"

"Fine, fine, fine. You won. Here, take it."

"Thank you for the reward, Imperial Uncle! Ah Xuan, quick, say thank you!"

"Thank you for the reward, Imperial Uncle. But Imperial Uncle, please do not indulge my brother too much. He is the sort of mischievous fellow who, if you give him a bit of color, will try to open a dye shop."

"Ah Xuan, how can you say that about your brother! Imperial Uncle, ignore him, let's keep competing!"

Lady Dou's face first stiffened, and then darkened slightly.

Empress Xiao covered her mouth with her handkerchief and smiled. "You said your Erlang was lively, and indeed he is. He does not look like someone of weak health at all."

Lady Dou's eyes filled with sorrow. "That is precisely why I worry. Sigh, he loves to play and cause a ruckus, but just from competing with the Zheng youth in reciting books for a short while, he fell ill for several months."

Empress Xiao sighed. "You have had a hard time. But it is a good thing for a child to be active. Moving around more will eventually improve his health."

Empress Xiao led Lady Dou through a winding corridor of flowers, and their vision suddenly opened up.

Li Shimin held a bow in one hand and nocked an arrow with the other. Atop Li Xuanba's head rested a large straw cushion, which already had three blunt, headless arrows sticking out of it.

With a sharp *whoosh*, a fourth arrow flew through the air and lodged itself firmly into the soft, fluffy straw cushion on top of Li Xuanba's head.

Lady Dou took a sharp breath. Her vision went black, and she had to reach out to grab the hand of a nearby maidservant just to keep herself from collapsing.

Empress Xiao looked at Lady Dou in confusion once more. "You said... Erlang is like this, and he is truly of weak health?"

Lady Dou: "..." *I want nothing more than to pin Erlang over my knee and give him a sound thrashing!*

*Li Shimin! Is this how you look after your younger brother?! You actually made your brother hold the target while you shot arrows at his head?!*

A flash of sheer fury crossed Lady Dou's face, causing Empress Xiao's heart to skip a beat.

She quickly came to her own conclusion. "Are you worried that he will overexert himself and fall ill again?"

Lady Dou took a deep breath. "Y-yes, indeed. Sigh, Erlang and Sanlang both deeply revere their father and strive to learn archery, but... sigh."

Hearing Lady Dou's voice, Li Shimin immediately spun around. "Mother?"

He spread his arms, revealing a neck draped in chains of gold, silver, and precious gems. "Mother, Mother, look! I won so many rewards from Imperial Uncle!"

Yang Guang laughed heartily, draping another string of turquoise prayer beads around Li Shimin's neck.

Lady Dou gasped once more, her breath catching as her vision swam.

*Li Shimin, what on earth are you doing! Performing street tricks for the Emperor?! Who taught you this?!*

Li Xuanba guiltily averted his gaze.

*Sorry, my idea. I taught him.*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第17章 窦夫人唠唠叨叨
chunks.chineseText:
第17章 窦夫人唠唠叨叨

=
　　窦夫人到来后， 杨广没有多说话，让窦夫人领着两个孩子去收拾行李，明日就住进西苑。
　　杨广不是没常识的人， 知道六岁的孩童娇贵， 窦夫人肯定会叮嘱一番。
　　他还特意允许窦夫人可以给每个孩子都留两个用惯的仆人， 若有什么需要，尽可以提。
　　窦夫人领着两个孩子离开，路上的时候， 三人都很沉默。
　　李世民感受到了母亲那里的低气压，不断往李玄霸身边移动，差点把李玄霸挤得贴车厢上。
　　等到了暂住的地方， 窦夫人开着窗户和门，让仆人守在稍远的地方， 才开口：“把今日之事告诉我。”
　　李世民看向李玄霸。
　　窦夫人道：“三郎， 你若累了可以先小睡一会儿，待饭菜做好，娘再叫你。”
　　李玄霸道：“我可以和哥一起……”
　　窦夫人打断道：“快去睡，你明日就要伴驾，别生病了。”
　　李玄霸无奈， 只能到隔壁睡觉。
　　李世民瘪嘴：“娘亲，不公平。”
　　窦夫人板着脸道：“你是兄长！”
　　李世民垂着脑袋。
　　李玄霸：【哥， 除了隋炀帝的事，其他都可以和娘实话实说，是我教唆你讨好皇帝。】
　　李世民对李玄霸点了点头， 又拍了拍胸脯。
　　李玄霸虽然不放心二哥独自接受母亲询问， 但确实累了， 倒头就秒睡。
　　待他醒来， 回到隔壁时，二哥一副要哭不哭的模样，看来只是被娘训了，没挨打。
　　李玄霸伸了个懒腰，偷看了一眼母亲。
　　窦夫人察觉到李玄霸的视线，叹了口气，没好气道：“三郎，虽然二郎把什么事都揽在了他自己身上，但二郎不是会故意讨好别人的孩子，你们隐瞒了什么？”
　　哥把所有责任都揽自己身上了？李玄霸愣了一下，无奈道：“哥，回来的时候怎么说的？实话告诉娘就好了。”
　　李世民吸了吸鼻子：“我是你哥哥。”
　　“这时候你倔强什么……”李玄霸无奈，他对母亲坦白道，“是我让哥讨好陛下。陛下喜欢听好话，又是我和哥的表叔，无论是身为臣子还是晚辈，讨好他都不为错。”
　　窦夫人叹气：“是没错。但射箭是怎么回事？你们的模样很熟练啊，在家里经常玩？”
　　李玄霸点头：“挺好玩。”
　　窦夫人拍了一下桌子：“教你们用弓箭的师傅怎么能让你们做如此危险的事！”
　　窦夫人又气又急。
　　学习的事是丈夫安排的。李世民和李玄霸都很懂事早熟，她忙于伺候婆婆，张罗唐国公府一大家子人的衣食住行，还要与其他贵族夫人交往，没有每日过问李世民和李玄霸的事。
　　她想两个孩子极有主见，也不会想每日被询问。她只是每天都抽出一定时间与两个孩子聊一聊，询问他们是否被欺负，有什么需要，并陪他们读一会儿书。
　　谁知道两个孩子居然经常在家里玩这么危险的游戏？！
　　虽然箭枝没有箭头，弓也只是孩子用的玩具弓，弹到了身上也没有危险，但假如受伤了呢？！
　　李玄霸和李世民对视一眼。
　　显然，他们都以为母亲会对他们不要脸面地讨好皇帝而生气，没想到母亲气的只是他们玩的弓箭游戏。
　　李玄霸：【你和母亲道歉了这么久，都没发现母亲在生气什么？！】
　　李世民：“……”
　　他挠了挠头，道：“娘亲，原来你不生气我们讨好表叔啊？”
　　窦夫人道：“他是皇帝，你们若有本事讨好他，那是好事。”她虽警惕皇帝，但警惕之后也是打消皇帝的戒心所要做的事，与孩子们讨好皇帝所做的事差不多。
　　李世民道：“那娘亲为何还不断追问我，我还以为你生气了。”
　　一旦得知母亲没因为这个生气，李世民立刻把小胸脯挺了起来，不委屈了。
　　就是嘛，我们讨好皇帝兼表叔不是很正常的事吗？看我和阿玄赚了多少赏赐！娘亲应该夸奖我们！
　　窦夫人屈指轻轻敲了一下儿子的脑袋：“娘就是为了吓唬吓唬你们。虽然现在陛下奖赏你们，但伴君如伴虎，君心难测，不要以为你们的小聪明能次次奏效。你们接下来要伴驾，必须小心谨慎。”
　　李世民垂下头：“知道了。”
　　李玄霸道：“娘，我饿了，询问结束，可以吃饭了吗？”
　　趁着母亲被二哥带偏，赶紧把射箭游戏的话题带过去。
　　窦夫人瞥了李玄霸一眼，为三儿子理了理睡乱的头发，道：“你还没说，你们二人为何要玩这么危险的游戏？教你们射箭的师傅都不阻拦？你们知道这有多危险吗？”
　　李世民和李玄霸再次对视一眼。
　　唉，没有把话题岔过去。
　　李世民又想把责任揽在自己身上的时候，李玄霸抢先道：“是我们错了。我们以为没有箭头的箭不会有危险，就经常玩神箭手的游戏。”
　　他低头看着脚尖道：“也是我先玩的。二哥射箭很厉害，几乎百发百中。我就把靶子拿着跑，让二哥射移动靶子。就是……就是好玩。”
　　李玄霸确实是因为觉得好玩才玩这个游戏。
　　他知道历史中李世民神箭手的名号有多响亮。见到二哥现在拿着启蒙用的玩具弓都能百发百胜，就起了玩闹的心思。
　　闹厉害了，李玄霸拿着靶子上下左右挥舞，李世民追着靶子射，是兄弟二人最常玩的游戏。
　　李世民对自己射箭很有自信，李玄霸比李世民本人对李世民的射箭技术更有信心，又只是没有箭头的玩具弓，所以他们都没想过这游戏的危险性。
　　“其实我也常拿着弓对着二哥射。”李玄霸讪讪道，“不过我十支箭会有五支箭脱靶。二哥拿着靶子的时候，一边躲避我脱靶的箭，一边把靶子往我箭上凑。”
　　李世民补充：“非常好玩！哎哟。”
　　窦夫人又敲了一下李世民的脑袋，真是哭笑不得：“你们就把常玩的游戏拿去讨陛下喜欢了？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　听到隋炀帝要带他和二哥去江都，为了在龙舟上拥有更多自主权，李玄霸强打精神让二哥拿出杀手锏。
　　隋炀帝在历史中是出了名的好游猎。若是二哥拿出他拿手的弓箭本事，肯定能进一步讨隋炀帝欢心。
　　自己也能靠着当靶子强打精神，免得忍不住打哈欠。
　　等他们玩完这个游戏，也可以以射箭和当靶子都很累为借口，向逗他们逗得太开心，忘记让他们休息的隋炀帝请辞了。
　　窦夫人真是拿这两个孩子毫无办法。
　　她当时气得不行。但冷静下来之后，她又认可了两个孩子对皇帝“卖艺”讨欢心的做法。
　　窦夫人虽然自尊心很强，但她很理智，知道对皇帝有自尊心，大概就会被皇帝厌恶。
　　两个孩子正是不需要在乎脸面的时候，何况皇帝还是他们表叔，晚辈讨长辈开心是“孝”，传出去都是美名。
　　但弓箭游戏还是太危险了。
　　“娘给你们做个头盔和皮甲，以后你们想玩，穿好防护后再玩。”窦夫人让两个孩子伸出手掌，在他们手心各打了五下当做惩罚后，道，“善于泅水的人最容易溺水。就算对自己再自信，也要做好受伤的准备，明白吗？”
　　李世民和李玄霸本来都做好了以后不再玩弓箭游戏的打算，听母亲允许他们继续玩，都很惊讶。
　　李世民扑到窦夫人怀里撒娇道：“娘娘，我和阿玄可以继续玩吗？”
　　窦夫人叹气道：“你和三郎都心高气傲，将来肯定是想自己闯出一番事业。二郎你肯定会上战场，三郎虽然不需要上战场，也要有些自保的本事。你们兄弟二人从小互相学习射箭和躲避箭矢，总比等上了战场时再学习强。”
　　她摸了摸两个孩子的脑袋，道：“想来你们师傅允许你们玩这个游戏，也是如此想。”
　　或许丈夫也早就知道了，只是觉得习武的事，没必要告诉自己。
　　李世民蹭了蹭母亲的脸颊：“娘娘放心，我非常非常厉害，将来一定能再得个爵位，把娘娘和阿玄都接去我的府邸享福。”
　　窦夫人失笑：“你把三郎接走就行了。”
　　“不要嘛不要嘛，我要娘娘，阿玄也要娘娘。”李世民不依不饶，“阿玄，你也快说说。”
　　李玄霸点头：“哥说得对。”
　　他还没从母亲居然会为他们想得这么远中回过神。而且母亲也判断这短暂的“盛世”会结束？
　　这时的人都还不相信，会再有一个如汉朝一样的超越百年以上的大一统王朝出现呢。
　　“好了，不是说饿了？还吃不吃饭了？”窦夫人笑道，“吃完饭，娘和你们说说该如何与皇后相处。”
　　唉，不知道要怎么和两个才六岁的孩子说，皇后想和他们联姻的事。
　　吃饱喝足后，李世民和李玄霸躺在窦夫人的腿上，听窦夫人轻言细语叮嘱他们伴驾时需要注意的事。
　　窦夫人主要细数了皇帝身边哪些人比较正直，哪些人与丈夫交好，可以庇佑两个孩子。
　　李玄霸闭上眼，将母亲所提到的名字与自己的记忆一一对应。
　　此次隋炀帝一游江都，伴驾者大多都是宗室。他在滕王杨纶和卫王杨集两个名字下面打了着重号。
　　隋炀帝继位后，大概是因为弑父的谣言，对宗室都很不信任，恨不得自灭满门。滕王杨纶和卫王杨集最先遭殃，应该是在一游江都的时候就会事发。
　　他和二哥得绕着这两个宗室走。
　　听着听着，李玄霸又睡着了。
　　李世民小声道：“弟弟居然还打呼噜。”
　　窦夫人道：“三郎肯定是十分累了。二郎，在龙舟上时，你要压一压你的性子，好好照顾弟弟。”
　　李世民道：“娘放心。”
　　窦夫人道：“皇帝身边有最好的医师和最好的药材。你们既然已经得到了他的喜爱，就不要客气，尽力去寻名医好药，每日都去给你弟弟检查一次身体。”
　　李世民道：“我记住了。嘿嘿，错过这次机会，即使是我们唐国公府也不好每日请御医来为阿玄诊治。”
　　窦夫人脸上也浮现些许浅笑。或许这是两个孩子伴驾时，唯一能让她心里感到安稳的事。
　　“我和皇后说了你也体弱，你也要装一装。”窦夫人道，“若皇后不管不顾，非要询问你们亲事，你们只管推说年幼不懂，全仗父母决定。”
　　李世民道：“本来就该如此。”
　　窦夫人道：“若皇后在你们面前说荥阳郑氏不好，你们可千万不能附和。”
　　李世民点头：“都记住了。”
　　窦夫人仍旧放心不下，又絮絮叨叨了一遍。
　　李世民虽然也困了，但也坚持听完，不断保证自己听进去了。
　　直到他实在撑不住，开始不断打哈欠，窦夫人才恋恋不舍地把孩子抱到床上。
　　窦夫人起身离开，为两个孩子准备行李，选好护身的忠仆。
　　第二日，杨广没有派人来催。窦夫人和两个孩子用完早膳后，才把李世民和李玄霸送入行宫中。
　　李世民和李玄霸一见到杨广就喊“表叔”，看得窦夫人眼角直抽筋。
　　特别是李玄霸那几乎和李世民一个模子印出来的撒娇表情，看得窦夫人脚指头都扣紧了。
　　没想到自家三郎还有这本事。看来自己能再放心一些了。
　　窦夫人将两个孩子送进行宫后，立刻乘船回到荥阳，将此事告诉李渊。
　　她提防皇帝，甚至不敢提前派人去告诉李渊此事，担心皇帝会误解她对两个孩子伴驾的事不满意。
　　窦夫人道：“二郎和三郎说，陛下说郎君你吝啬，每每获得好马都不肯送他。”
　　李渊失笑：“表弟坐拥天下，还惦记着我的好马？”
　　窦夫人已经知道不可能让李渊警惕皇帝，换了个方向道：“陛下让两个孩子叫他表叔，看来是把我们家当亲戚处。亲戚就要有来有回，怎么能因为亲戚富有就少了礼数？”
　　李渊沉思了一会儿，仍旧摇头：“陛下就是陛下，怎能将其当作普通亲戚？我若是向陛下进献珍宝，恐会被人说是谄媚贿赂，有损名声。”
　　窦夫人在心里叹了口气。
　　丈夫重名声是好事，但太重虚名就是负担了。
　　这一点，大郎也学了丈夫。
　　她想到二郎三郎卖力讨好皇帝的模样。丈夫和大郎，还不如二郎三郎两个孩子通透啊。
　　“但现在二郎和三郎在陛下身边，郎君或许还是应该送些礼物给陛下。若郎君什么多不做，陛下恐会认为郎君不在乎二郎三郎。”窦夫人又退了一步。
　　这次李渊被说服了：“这倒是，我得送些礼物，请求陛下多多照顾二郎和三郎。唉，二郎三郎才六岁，你怎么能让陛下把二郎三郎留在身边，甚至还要南下？若是二郎三郎水土不服怎么办？”
　　窦夫人低头道：“是我的错，不该把二郎和三郎养得太讨人喜欢。”
　　李渊：“……”
　　他扑哧笑道：“好吧，确实是如此。是二郎和三郎太讨人喜欢的错。”
　　李渊也知道，陛下的决定，自家夫人也不能阻止。只是他又不能抱怨陛下，只能抱怨夫人一句。
　　被窦夫人顶回来后，他也不生气，顺着这句话就过去了。
　　何况李渊也很自豪，自家二郎三郎就是很讨人喜欢，没办法啊。
　　“有了此次伴驾的经历，肯定会有许多世家和勋贵子弟想要结识二郎和三郎，或许该为他们提前准备小字。”李渊兴致勃勃，“夫人，你可有主意？”
　　窦夫人道：“郎君，这个先暂且放下。还有件事很重要，必须立刻解决。皇后听闻二郎三郎的才名，有意让二郎三郎同娶兰陵萧氏女。”
　　李渊一愣，然后皱眉：“她还嫌弃兰陵萧氏不够显赫吗？后族和勋贵联姻，这不是上赶着让陛下忌惮？”
　　李渊虽信任皇帝，但不蠢，忌讳还是懂的。
　　再者，郡姓和侨姓那些摩擦，李渊也了解。
　　萧皇后一听二郎三郎压了荥阳郑氏一头，就立刻要与二郎三郎结亲，明摆着就是想把二郎三郎拉进郡姓和侨姓的争夺。
　　“她心大了。”李渊叹气，“希望不要连累太子。太子是很好的储君啊。”
　　窦夫人颔首，同样叹气。太子杨昭，真是贤明宽仁得不像杨家人。
　　李渊道：“二郎的婚事，定是要从虏姓里选。你问问你娘家有没有合适的女子，我也去问一问同僚。”
　　窦夫人道：“那三郎呢？”
　　李渊沉默。
　　半晌，他叹气道：“待三郎再年长些吧。明年，若他明年也没有再得重病，我再给他寻个品行良好的贤惠官宦女子。家世低些无所谓，得能照顾三郎。”
　　窦夫人听着李渊话中一片拳拳爱子之心，神情不由变得温柔：“以三郎的性格，过于贤惠他恐怕也是不喜欢的。三郎体弱，娶的性子得爽利些，立得起来，护得住三郎。”
　　李渊哭笑不得：“哪有妻子保护丈夫的？”
　　窦夫人娇嗔道：“怎么不行？”
　　李渊道：“是是是。”他不和妇道人家一般计较。
　　……
　　既然皇帝都说到他的骏马了，他就送两匹骏马并猎鹰给皇帝。
　　杨广接到李渊的礼物后，对李世民和李玄霸笑道：“你们的父亲终于肯拔一次毛了，真不容易。”
　　李玄霸看着李渊送的礼物，心里叹气。
　　怎么才送这么点？看来父亲还是没开窍。
　　真是不撞南墙不回头。难道父亲非得要撞十几年的墙，等到大业末年再讨好隋炀帝？
　　看来还是得自己和二哥努力。
　　因李世民和李玄霸不断念叨“父亲吝啬”，让杨广把“李渊对朕不够忠诚”，替换成了“李渊只是吝啬”的印象。
　　这次虽然李渊送的东西“吝啬”，但好歹也送了。杨广便对李渊的怀疑度降低了一些，准备之后给李渊一点表现的机会。
　　这是之后的事了。
　　八月十五，杨广第一次南下江都。
　　江都即后世的扬州城。
　　隋文帝开皇九年改吴州为扬州，治江都。杨广当了十几年的扬州总管。扬州就是他的大本营。
　　此次回江都，除了安抚江南的政治意图之外，杨广更有“衣锦还乡”的念头。
　　杨广继位后，就立刻把江都升至“京尹”的级别，并修通济渠贯通了洛阳和江都。
　　现在他终于要以皇帝的身份返回“故地”，心中慷慨之意快要溢出来。
　　杨广所乘坐的龙舟长二百丈，高四十五丈，共有四层。最高层是杨广居住和议事的正殿；中间两层有一百一十间金碧辉煌的房间，供被杨广招上龙舟的大臣和妃嫔使用；最下层是听候差遣的宫女太监。
　　萧皇后所乘坐的翔螭舟构造与杨广相似，只是对比龙舟缩小了一定规格。李世民和李玄霸就跟随萧皇后住在翔螭舟顶层正殿。
　　当龙舟船队开始徐徐启动时，两个孩子趴在船舷上，看着两岸景象惊叹不已。
　　萧皇后坐在他们身边，微笑着让他们小心些。
　　萧皇后的两个儿子都已经弱冠，孙儿又过于年幼，离不开各自母亲，虽有些公主在身边伺候，但仍觉得膝下空虚。
　　李世民和李玄霸长相精致，聪慧可爱，正好弥补萧皇后心里的空缺。
　　李玄霸确实是体弱。李世民虽然平时很活泼健康，但玩久了也会突然陷入疲惫虚弱。
　　正如窦夫人所说，双生子有些先天不足。
　　萧皇后打消了与他们联姻的打算，但对这兄弟二人更加怜爱了。
　　李世民和李玄霸一点一点试探萧皇后的“底线”，现在在翔螭舟的地位仿若皇子。
　　李世民对李玄霸咬耳朵：“我还以为船是划的，怎么是人拉的？”
　　李玄霸：【整个龙舟船队需要八万多民夫拉动。光是皇帝的大龙舟就需要一千民夫才能拉得动。】
　　李世民眨了眨眼。
　　他看着岸边密密麻麻的民夫，脸上的兴奋之色淡去。
　　李世民戳了戳李玄霸，小声道：“阿玄，他们看上去好可怜。”
　　李玄霸看了二哥一眼，又环视翔螭舟上的其他人。
　　不只是他们看到了岸边的民夫。
　　所有的人看到岸边壮观的景象，都露出了骄傲自豪和得意的神色。
　　连宫女和太监也是如此。
　　“嗯。”李玄霸道，“二哥，风太大，我们进船舱吧。”
　　李世民点头：“好。”
　　他和萧皇后说了一声，牵着弟弟离开。
　　离开甲板之前，李世民又回头看了一眼。
　　民夫们已经拉动了纤绳，喊着号子使劲拉船。
　　有官员拿着鞭子狠狠抽打他们的背，让他们加快速度。
　　他们乘坐的船上，已经演奏起了歌舞。
　　前方皇帝乘坐的龙舟，还有战鼓声响起，似乎是在演奏激昂的战乐。
　　身后的船只也传来了欢笑声。还有僧尼道士高唱佛号道号，称颂大隋强盛。
　　李世民将视线回到正前方，牵着弟弟走进翔螭舟宫殿中属于兄弟二人的房间。
　　热闹没什么好看，不如陪弟弟睡午觉。
