Chapter 17: Lady Dou's Nagging

After Lady Dou arrived, Yang Guang did not say much. He had her take the two children to pack their luggage, as they were to move into the West Park the following day.

Yang Guang was not lacking in common sense; he knew that six-year-old children were delicate and that Lady Dou would surely have much to instruct them on.

He even specially permitted Lady Dou to leave two familiar servants for each child, adding that she could raise any other needs they might have.

Lady Dou led the two children away. On the road, all three remained silent.

Li Shimin felt the low pressure radiating from his mother and kept shifting closer to Li Xuanba, nearly pinning him against the carriage wall.

Once they arrived at their temporary lodging, Lady Dou opened the windows and doors, ordered the servants to stand guard at a distance, and finally spoke: "Tell me what happened today."

Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba.

Lady Dou said, "Sanlang, if you are tired, you may take a short nap first. Once the meal is ready, Mother will wake you."

Li Xuanba said, "I can stay with Brother..."

Lady Dou interrupted, "Go to sleep. You have to attend to the Emperor tomorrow. Do not fall ill."

Helpless, Li Xuanba could only go to the next room to sleep.

Li Shimin pouted. "Mother, that's not fair."

Lady Dou said with a stern face, "You are the older brother!"

Li Shimin hung his head.

Li Xuanba: *[Brother, except for the matter regarding Emperor Yang of Sui, you can tell Mother the truth about everything else. Tell her I was the one who instigated you to please the Emperor.]*

Li Shimin nodded at Li Xuanba and patted his chest reassuringly.

Although Li Xuanba was worried about leaving his second brother to face their mother's questioning alone, he was indeed exhausted. He fell asleep the moment his head hit the pillow.

When he woke up and returned to the next room, his second brother looked as if he were on the verge of tears. It seemed he had only been scolded by their mother and had not been beaten.

Li Xuanba stretched and stole a glance at his mother.

Detecting his gaze, Lady Dou sighed and said in an annoyed tone, "Sanlang, although Erlang took all the blame upon himself, he is not a child who would deliberately flatter others. What are you two hiding?"

*Brother took all the responsibility himself?* Li Xuanba was stunned for a moment, then said helplessly, "Brother, what did we agree on when we came back? You should have just told Mother the truth."

Li Shimin sniffled. "I am your older brother."

"Why are you being stubborn at a time like this..." Li Xuanba sighed. He confessed to his mother, "It was I who told Brother to please His Majesty. His Majesty loves to hear sweet words, and he is also our cousin-uncle. Whether as subjects or juniors, there is nothing wrong with trying to please him."

Lady Dou sighed. "That is true. But what was that archery display about? You two looked so practiced. Do you play that often at home?"

Li Xuanba nodded. "It's quite fun."

Lady Dou slapped the table. "How could the master who taught you archery allow you to do something so dangerous!"

Lady Dou was both angry and anxious.

Their education had been arranged by her husband. Because both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were sensible and mature beyond their years, and because she was busy serving her mother-in-law, managing the food, clothing, and shelter of the entire Duke of Tang's household, and socializing with other noble ladies, she did not inquire about their daily affairs every single day.

She figured the two children were highly independent and would not want to be questioned daily. She merely set aside some time each day to chat with them, ask if they were being bullied, see if they needed anything, and accompany them in reading for a while.

Who could have known that these two children actually played such a dangerous game at home on a regular basis?!

Even though the arrows had no tips and the bows were just toy bows for children, posing no real danger even if they hit, what if they got hurt?!

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin exchanged a glance.

Clearly, they had both assumed their mother would be angry at them for shamelessly flattering the Emperor. They had not expected that she was only angry about their archery game.

Li Xuanba: *[You apologized to Mother for so long, yet you didn't even realize what she was actually angry about?!]*

Li Shimin: "..."

He scratched his head and said, "Mother, so you aren't angry that we pleased Cousin-Uncle?"

Lady Dou said, "He is the Emperor. If you have the ability to please him, that is a good thing." Although she was wary of the Emperor, her wariness was aimed at dispelling his suspicions, which was essentially the same goal as the children's attempts to please him.

Li Shimin said, "Then why did you keep questioning me, Mother? I thought you were angry."

Once he learned his mother was not angry about that, Li Shimin immediately puffed out his little chest, no longer feeling aggrieved.

*Exactly! Isn't it perfectly normal for us to please the Emperor, who is also our cousin-uncle? Look at how many rewards Xuan and I earned! Mother should be praising us!*

Lady Dou tapped her finger lightly against her son's forehead. "Mother only did that to scare you. Although His Majesty is rewarding you now, accompanying a ruler is like keeping company with a tiger. The imperial mind is unpredictable; do not think your clever tricks will work every time. You will be accompanying the Emperor next, so you must be cautious and prudent."

Li Shimin hung his head. "I understand."

Li Xuanba said, "Mother, I'm hungry. Now that the questioning is over, can we eat?"

He wanted to take advantage of his second brother throwing their mother off-track to quickly move past the topic of the archery game.

Lady Dou glanced at Li Xuanba, smoothed her third son's messy hair from his nap, and said, "You still haven't told me why you two play such a dangerous game. Did the master who taught you archery not stop you? Do you know how dangerous this is?"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba exchanged another glance.

*Sigh, the topic didn't change.*

Just as Li Shimin was about to take the blame upon himself again, Li Xuanba beat him to it. "It was our fault. We thought that arrows without tips wouldn't be dangerous, so we often played the divine archer game."

He looked down at his toes and said, "I was also the one who started it. Second Brother is amazing at archery, hitting the mark almost every time. So I would run around holding the target, letting Second Brother shoot at a moving target. It was... it was just for fun."

Li Xuanba had indeed played the game because he found it fun.

He knew how legendary Li Shimin's reputation as a divine archer was in history. Seeing his second brother hitting every target even with a toy bow used for early training, he had felt playful.

When they got carried away, Li Xuanba would wave the target up, down, left, and right, while Li Shimin chased and shot at it. This was the game the two brothers played most often.

Li Shimin was highly confident in his archery, and Li Xuanba had even more confidence in Li Shimin's skills than Li Shimin did himself. Since it was only a toy bow without arrowheads, neither of them had considered the danger of the game.

"Actually, I often hold the bow and shoot at Second Brother too," Li Xuanba said sheepishly. "But five out of ten of my arrows miss the target. When Second Brother holds the target, he dodges my stray arrows while moving the target to meet my shots."

Li Shimin added, "It's incredibly fun! Ouch."

Lady Dou tapped Li Shimin's head again, caught between laughter and tears. "So you took a game you play all the time and used it to please His Majesty?"

Li Xuanba nodded.

Upon hearing that Emperor Yang of Sui wanted to take him and his second brother to Jiangdu, in order to gain more autonomy on the dragon boat, Li Xuanba had forced himself to stay alert and had his second brother bring out his trump card.

Emperor Yang of Sui was famously fond of hunting in history. If his second brother showed off his superb archery skills, it would surely please the Emperor further.

He could also use the role of the target to force himself to stay awake, preventing himself from yawning uncontrollably.

Once they finished the game, they could also use the excuse of being exhausted from shooting and acting as a target to take their leave of the Emperor, who had been so thoroughly entertained that he forgot to let them rest.

Lady Dou was truly at her wits' end with these two children.

She had been furious at the time. But after calming down, she approved of the children's method of "performing" to please the Emperor.

Although Lady Dou possessed strong self-esteem, she was highly rational. She knew that showing pride before an emperor would likely only incur his dislike.

The two children were at an age where they did not need to worry about losing face. Moreover, the Emperor was their cousin-uncle; a junior pleasing an elder was considered "filial piety," which would only bring them a good reputation if word got out.

Still, the archery game was too dangerous.

"Mother will make you a helmet and leather armor. In the future, if you want to play, you must wear proper protection before doing so." Lady Dou had the two children stretch out their palms, gave each of them five light slaps as punishment, and then said, "Those who are good at swimming are the most prone to drowning. No matter how confident you are in yourselves, you must always be prepared for the possibility of injury, do you understand?"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had originally planned to stop playing the archery game altogether. Hearing their mother permit them to continue playing left them both very surprised.

Li Shimin threw himself into Lady Dou's arms, acting spoiled. "Mother, can Xuan and I really keep playing?"

Lady Dou sighed and said, "Both you and Sanlang are proud and ambitious. In the future, you will surely want to carve out your own careers. Erlang, you will definitely go to the battlefield. Although Sanlang does not need to go to the battlefield, he still needs some ability to protect himself. It is better for you two brothers to learn archery and arrow-dodging from each other from a young age than to start learning only when you are on the battlefield."

She stroked the two children's heads and said, "Presumably, your master allowed you to play this game with this very thought in mind."

Perhaps her husband had also known about it long ago, but simply felt there was no need to inform her about matters of martial training.

Li Shimin rubbed his cheek against his mother's. "Don't worry, Mother. I am very, very formidable. In the future, I will definitely earn another noble title and bring both you and Xuan to my estate to enjoy a life of leisure."

Lady Dou laughed. "It will be enough if you take Sanlang with you."

"No, no, I want Mother, and Xuan wants Mother too," Li Shimin insisted stubbornly. "Xuan, speak up quickly."

Li Xuanba nodded. "Brother is right."

He had not yet recovered from the shock of his mother thinking so far ahead for them. Moreover, did his mother also judge that this brief "prosperous age" would come to an end?

At this time, people still did not believe that another unified dynasty lasting over a century, like the Han Dynasty, would ever appear again.

"Alright, didn't you say you were hungry? Are we going to eat or not?" Lady Dou smiled. "After dinner, Mother will tell you how to get along with the Empress."

*Sigh, I don't know how to explain to two six-year-old children that the Empress wants to arrange marriages for them.*

After eating and drinking their fill, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba lay on Lady Dou's lap, listening to her gentle, soft voice instructing them on what to watch out for while accompanying the Emperor.

Lady Dou mainly listed which people around the Emperor were relatively upright and which ones were on good terms with her husband, who could protect the two children.

Li Xuanba closed his eyes, matching the names his mother mentioned with his own memories.

During this first southern tour of Emperor Yang of Sui to Jiangdu, most of those accompanying him were members of the imperial clan. He mentally underlined two names: Yang Lun, Prince of Teng, and Yang Ji, Prince of Wei.

After Emperor Yang of Sui ascended the throne, likely due to the rumors of patricide, he was highly distrustful of the imperial clan, to the point of wishing to wipe them out himself. Yang Lun, Prince of Teng, and Yang Ji, Prince of Wei, would be the first to suffer, and their downfall would likely occur during this very tour of Jiangdu.

*Second Brother and I must steer clear of these two imperial kinsmen.*

As he listened, Li Xuanba fell asleep again.

Li Shimin whispered, "Little brother is actually snoring."

Lady Dou said, "Sanlang must be utterly exhausted. Erlang, when you are on the dragon boat, you must restrain your temper and take good care of your brother."

Li Shimin said, "Don't worry, Mother."

Lady Dou said, "The Emperor has the best physicians and the finest medicinal ingredients by his side. Since you have already won his favor, do not be polite. Do your best to seek out famous doctors and good medicines, and have them check your brother's body once every day."

Li Shimin said, "I'll keep that in mind. Hehe, if we miss this opportunity, even our Duke of Tang's estate wouldn't find it easy to invite imperial physicians to treat Xuan every day."

A faint smile appeared on Lady Dou's face. Perhaps this was the only thing that could bring her peace of mind while the two children accompanied the Emperor.

"I told the Empress that you are also of weak constitution, so you must also put on an act," Lady Dou said. "If the Empress disregards everything and insists on asking about your marriages, just say that you are too young to understand and that everything depends on your parents' decision."

Li Shimin said, "That is how it should be anyway."

Lady Dou said, "If the Empress speaks ill of the Zheng clan of Xingyang in front of you, you must absolutely not agree with her."

Li Shimin nodded. "I've remembered it all."

Still unable to set her mind at ease, Lady Dou nagged them once more.

Although Li Shimin was also sleepy, he insisted on listening to the end, repeatedly assuring her that he had taken it to heart.

It was only when he could no longer hold out and began to yawn continuously that Lady Dou reluctantly carried the children to bed.

Lady Dou stood up and left to prepare the children's luggage and select loyal servants to protect them.

The next day, Yang Guang did not send anyone to rush them. Only after Lady Dou and the two children finished their breakfast did she send Li Shimin and Li Xuanba into the imperial palace.

The moment Li Shimin and Li Xuanba saw Yang Guang, they called him "Cousin-Uncle," causing the corners of Lady Dou's eyes to twitch.

In particular, Li Xuanba's spoiled expression, which looked almost identical to Li Shimin's, made Lady Dou's toes curl in embarrassment.

*Who would have thought my Sanlang had this talent? It seems I can rest a bit easier.*

After delivering the two children to the imperial palace, Lady Dou immediately took a boat back to Xingyang to inform Li Yuan of the matter.

Wary of the Emperor, she had not even dared to send someone ahead to inform Li Yuan, fearing the Emperor would misunderstand and think she was dissatisfied with the children accompanying him.

Lady Dou said, "Erlang and Sanlang said that His Majesty called you stingy, Husband, saying you refuse to send him any good horses you obtain."

Li Yuan laughed. "My cousin rules the entire world, yet he still covets my good horses?"

Knowing it was impossible to make Li Yuan wary of the Emperor, Lady Dou shifted her approach: "His Majesty had the two children call him Cousin-Uncle. It seems he treats our family as relatives. Relatives must have mutual exchanges; how can we neglect our manners just because our relative is wealthy?"

Li Yuan pondered for a moment but still shook his head. "The Emperor is the Emperor. How can we treat him as an ordinary relative? If I present treasures to His Majesty, I fear others will accuse me of flattery and bribery, which would damage my reputation."

Lady Dou sighed in her heart.

It was a good thing for her husband to value his reputation, but valuing empty fame too much was a burden.

In this regard, Dalang had also taken after his father.

She thought of how hard Erlang and Sanlang had worked to please the Emperor. Her husband and eldest son were not even as clear-headed as these two young children.

"But now that Erlang and Sanlang are by His Majesty's side, perhaps you should still send some gifts to His Majesty, Husband. If you do nothing at all, His Majesty might think you do not care about Erlang and Sanlang." Lady Dou took another step back.

This time, Li Yuan was convinced. "That is true. I must send some gifts and request His Majesty to take good care of Erlang and Sanlang. Alas, Erlang and Sanlang are only six years old. How could you let His Majesty keep them by his side, and even take them south? What if they cannot adapt to the local climate and water?"

Lady Dou lowered her head and said, "It is my fault for raising Erlang and Sanlang to be too likable."

Li Yuan: "..."

He burst out laughing. "Well, that is indeed the case. It is the fault of Erlang and Sanlang for being too likable."

Li Yuan also knew that his wife could not have stopped the Emperor's decision. It was just that he could not complain about the Emperor, so he could only complain to his wife.

After being retorted by Lady Dou, he was not angry either, letting the matter slide with her words.

Besides, Li Yuan was also very proud. His Erlang and Sanlang were just too likable; there was nothing to be done about it.

"With this experience of accompanying the Emperor, there will surely be many children of noble families and meritorious officials who want to get to know Erlang and Sanlang. Perhaps we should prepare childhood names for them in advance," Li Yuan said enthusiastically. "Wife, do you have any ideas?"

Lady Dou said, "Husband, let us put that aside for now. There is another very important matter that must be resolved immediately. The Empress heard of Erlang and Sanlang's talent and reputation, and she intends to have them both marry daughters of the Lanling Xiao clan."

Li Yuan was taken aback, then frowned. "Does she still think the Lanling Xiao clan is not prominent enough? An alliance between the Empress's clan and meritorious nobility—isn't this practically begging to arouse His Majesty's suspicion?"

Although Li Yuan trusted the Emperor, he was not stupid; he understood what was taboo.

Furthermore, Li Yuan was well aware of the friction between the northern commandery surnames and the southern emigre surnames.

The moment Empress Xiao heard that Erlang and Sanlang had suppressed the Zheng clan of Xingyang, she immediately wanted to form a marriage alliance with them. It was obvious she wanted to drag Erlang and Sanlang into the struggle between the commandery and emigre surnames.

"Her ambitions have grown too large," Li Yuan sighed. "I hope she does not implicate the Crown Prince. The Crown Prince is an excellent heir."

Lady Dou nodded and sighed as well. Crown Prince Yang Zhao was indeed so wise and benevolent that he did not seem like a member of the Yang family at all.

Li Yuan said, "Erlang's marriage must be chosen from the Xianbei surnames. Ask your maternal family if there are any suitable girls, and I will also ask my colleagues."

Lady Dou said, "And what about Sanlang?"

Li Yuan fell silent.

After a long while, he sighed. "Let us wait until Sanlang is older. Next year, if he does not fall gravely ill again, I will find him a virtuous daughter of an official with good character. It does not matter if her family background is a bit lower, as long as she can take care of Sanlang."

Hearing the deep fatherly love in Li Yuan's words, Lady Dou's expression softened. "With Sanlang's personality, he probably wouldn't like someone who is overly gentle and submissive. Sanlang is weak in body, so his wife must have a brisk and decisive temperament—someone who can stand on her own feet and protect him."

Li Yuan was caught between laughter and tears. "How can a wife protect her husband?"

Lady Dou said petulantly, "Why not?"

Li Yuan said, "Yes, yes, yes." He would not argue with a woman.

...

Since the Emperor had mentioned his fine steeds, he sent two fine horses and a hunting falcon to the Emperor.

Upon receiving Li Yuan's gifts, Yang Guang smiled at Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. "Your father is finally willing to pluck a feather. It truly wasn't easy."

Looking at the gifts Li Yuan had sent, Li Xuanba sighed in his heart.

*Why did he only send this much? It seems Father still hasn't figured things out.*

*He really won't turn back until he hits a brick wall. Does Father really have to hit a wall for over a decade and wait until the end of the Daye era to finally please Emperor Yang of Sui?*

*It seems Second Brother and I still have to work hard ourselves.*

Because Li Shimin and Li Xuanba kept muttering about how "Father is stingy," they successfully replaced Yang Guang's impression of "Li Yuan is not loyal enough to me" with "Li Yuan is just stingy."

Although the things Li Yuan sent this time were "stingy," he had at least sent them. Yang Guang's suspicion of Li Yuan decreased slightly, and he prepared to give Li Yuan an opportunity to perform later on.

But that was a matter for the future.

On the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month, Yang Guang made his first southern tour to Jiangdu.

Jiangdu was the Yangzhou of later generations.

In the ninth year of the Kaihuang era of Emperor Wen of Sui, Wuzhou was renamed Yangzhou, with its seat of government at Jiangdu. Yang Guang had served as the Area Commander of Yangzhou for over a decade; Yangzhou was his stronghold.

This return to Jiangdu, apart from the political intent of pacifying the Jiangnan region, was also driven by Yang Guang's desire to "return home in glory."

Immediately after ascending the throne, Yang Guang elevated Jiangdu to the status of a metropolitan prefecture and constructed the Tongji Canal to connect Luoyang and Jiangdu.

Now, he was finally returning to his "old stomping grounds" as the Emperor, and his heart was overflowing with grand, sweeping emotions.

The dragon boat Yang Guang rode was two hundred zhang long and forty-five zhang high, with four decks in total. The topmost deck was the main hall where Yang Guang resided and held court; the middle two decks contained one hundred and ten magnificent rooms for the ministers and concubines summoned aboard by Yang Guang; the lowest deck housed the palace maids and eunuchs awaiting orders.

The Xiangchi Boat ridden by Empress Xiao was similar in structure to Yang Guang's dragon boat, only scaled down slightly. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba stayed with Empress Xiao in the main hall on the top deck of the Xiangchi Boat.

As the fleet of dragon boats slowly set off, the two children leaned against the ship's railing, marveling at the scenery on both banks.

Empress Xiao sat beside them, smiling as she told them to be careful.

Empress Xiao's two sons had already reached adulthood, and her grandsons were too young to leave their respective mothers. Although she had some princesses serving by her side, she still felt a void in her life.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were exquisitely handsome, intelligent, and adorable, perfectly filling the void in Empress Xiao's heart.

Li Xuanba was indeed weak in body. Although Li Shimin was usually lively and healthy, he would also suddenly fall into a state of exhaustion and weakness after playing for too long.

Just as Lady Dou had said, twins often suffered from some congenital deficiencies.

Empress Xiao had abandoned her plans for a marriage alliance, but she grew even more affectionate toward the two brothers.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba tested Empress Xiao's "boundaries" bit by bit, and their status on the Xiangchi Boat was now almost like that of imperial princes.

Li Shimin whispered into Li Xuanba's ear, "I thought boats were rowed. Why are people pulling them?"

Li Xuanba: *[The entire fleet of dragon boats requires over eighty thousand conscripted laborers to pull. The Emperor's grand dragon boat alone requires a thousand laborers to pull it.]*

Li Shimin blinked.

As he looked at the dense crowd of laborers on the banks, the excitement on his face faded.

Li Shimin nudged Li Xuanba and whispered, "Xuan, they look so pitiful."

Li Xuanba glanced at his second brother, then looked around at the other people on the Xiangchi Boat.

It was not just them who saw the laborers on the banks.

Everyone else, upon seeing the spectacular sight on the banks, wore expressions of pride, glory, and smug satisfaction.

Even the palace maids and eunuchs were the same.

"Yes," Li Xuanba said. "Second Brother, the wind is too strong. Let's go inside the cabin."

Li Shimin nodded. "Alright."

He spoke to Empress Xiao, then led his younger brother away.

Before leaving the deck, Li Shimin looked back once more.

The laborers had already pulled the towlines taut, chanting in unison as they strained to pull the boats.

Officials held whips, viciously lashing their backs to make them speed up.

On the boat they rode, singing and dancing had already begun.

From the dragon boat carrying the Emperor ahead, the sound of war drums echoed, seemingly playing a stirring martial tune.

Laughter also drifted from the boats behind them. There were even Buddhist monks, nuns, and Daoist priests chanting holy names, praising the prosperity and might of the Great Sui.

Li Shimin brought his gaze back to the front, holding his brother's hand as they walked into the room belonging to the two brothers inside the palace of the Xiangchi Boat.

There was nothing worth seeing in the bustling excitement; it was better to accompany his younger brother in taking an afternoon nap.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第18章 孩童不该想的事
chunks.chineseText:
第18章 孩童不该想的事

=
　　“好吵啊。”李世民捂住耳朵。
　　“吵死了！”李玄霸抓狂地挠哥哥的胳膊。
　　跟随李世民和李玄霸来的两位乳母， 心疼地缝着布垫：“再忍忍，很快就缝好了。”
　　李玄霸挠完哥哥后，有气无力道：“不急， 小心些， 别扎着手。”
　　乳母笑道：“不会扎着手， 放心。”
　　李玄霸点点头，继续低头挠哥哥的胳膊。
　　抓狂啊。
　　李玄霸以为自己做了万全的准备，但他万万没料到， 龙舟上这群人的精力过分充沛。
　　隋文帝在位时，按照地区特色设置了七种特色歌舞“七部伎”，即国伎、清商伎、高丽伎、天竺伎、安国伎、龟兹伎、文康伎。杨广继位， 增加了康国伎和疏勒伎，增至“九部伎”。
　　在包括李世民和李玄霸所乘坐的几艘为首大船上， “九部伎”轮流演出， 轻歌曼舞彻夜不停。
　　李世民：“别唱了，救命！”
　　李玄霸：“来点舒缓催眠的音乐好不好，谢谢！”
　　歌舞看腻了？没关系，在每一轮“九部伎”的间隔，还有伎人牵着珍奇异兽表演百戏杂耍， 称“曼衍鱼龙”。
　　“曼衍鱼龙”中最有意思的是运用各种火焰的杂耍。这类杂耍会从入夜开始，一直到凌晨才停止。太监和侍卫彻夜值班， 以免火焰杂耍不小心点燃船只。
　　李世民：“能不能别大半夜还在甲板上蹦跳！这是用脚在打鼓吗！”
　　李玄霸：“困……别折磨我的耳膜了。”
　　夜晚时，甲板上还会点燃篝火。
　　篝火架在铜器之中，里面烧的木头都是最上好的沉香木。当火焰燃起的时候， 异香弥漫， 仿佛身处仙境之中。
　　李世民：“阿嚏。”
　　李玄霸：“阿嚏。”
　　最初几天， 李世民和李玄霸还会手牵手去看热闹。很快， 别说李玄霸抓狂，李世民都蔫了。
　　这群大人们，他们都不睡觉吗！
　　两个孩子除非必要，再也不出门了。
　　他们一直躺在房间里，就算睡不着也眯着，尽可能地闭目养神。
　　李玄霸急中生智，让乳母在细密的细麻布里封了好几层绢丝，做成厚厚的隔音耳罩。
　　他和李世民先用纸条堵了耳朵，又戴上厚厚的隔音耳罩，终于睡了一次好觉。
　　就是耳朵塞久了纸条有点疼。
　　两个孩子躲在房间里不出来，萧皇后很担心，命御医日日给李世民和李玄霸检查身体，时时调整药方。
　　在两个孩子委屈巴巴的神情中，御医给他们开了一些安神的药，然后委婉地对皇后道，两个孩子年幼体弱，经不得太多人气冲撞，建议把孩子移到比较清静的船上休养。
　　萧皇后叹气：“窦夫人说两个孩子先天不足，很是难养。我之前还笑话她过于忧虑。自己带着养了一段时日，才体会到窦夫人的辛苦。”
　　让两个孩子到其他船上是不可能的。萧皇后不放心别人照顾李世民和李玄霸。
　　她让李世民和李玄霸从一层的正殿搬到了二层中段的房间。房间小了许多，但离甲板远了，让两个孩子耳边清静不少。
　　李世民和李玄霸终于能取下纸条，只戴着隔音耳罩睡觉了。
　　睡了几日囫囵觉，李世民终于恢复了精神。
　　他还不到七岁，居然有一种劫后余生之感：“我宣布，我以后再也不看‘九部伎’和‘曼衍鱼龙’！”
　　李玄霸白了二哥一眼：【不可能。】
　　李世民抱着软乎乎的枕头在床榻上滚来滚去：“就不看，就不看。”
　　李玄霸不喜欢硬枕头。他让人用羽绒、兽毛、谷壳、草药等材料做了许多枕头、抱枕。
　　李三郎的就是李二郎的。李世民学习了李玄霸的坏习惯，走到哪都自带枕头和抱枕。
　　李玄霸不理睬又恢复活力的二哥。
　　他静静地躺着，双目放空，放松头脑，继续养神。
　　“这些天都在屋里用餐，我们今天出去吃！”李世民把躺懒了的弟弟拉起来，“听闻岸边每日都会进贡当地美食，阿玄一定很想吃。”
　　李玄霸：【不，我不想。】
　　李世民把李玄霸拖下床，强拽着骨头都躺松了的弟弟去甲板运动。
　　御医说了，补足觉后就要多动动。小孩子要多动，身体才好。
　　见李世民和李玄霸“病愈”，萧皇后松了一口气。
　　她让两个孩子坐在她的左右，就像是对待自己的孩子一样，亲自为他们挑选食物。
　　萧皇后面前放了两米长，一米宽的大桌。宫女和太监轮番端来食物，水果、点心、炙菜、汤菜、蒸菜应有尽有。
　　食物刚端上来，杨广来了。
　　他人未至，声音先到：“二郎，三郎，听说你们病了？现在身体可还好？”
　　李世民和李玄霸忙站起来道：“已经大好。”
　　杨广揉了揉两个孩子的脑袋，道：“不必拘束，朕只是来看看你们。今日就在这里用午膳。”
　　皇帝一来，满桌的菜还没吃，就连着桌子一起被搬了下去。
　　太监抬来一张更长的雕龙画凤的餐桌，重新上菜。
　　杨广每日都要沿岸上贡珍稀食材。
　　这些食物不一定都要到杨广面前，但杨广会派人去清点。若是进贡的食材很珍贵很丰盛，官吏就可能升官；如果杨广不满意，那么官吏的帽子就不保了。
　　在用膳的时候，御膳房会拿着每日进贡的食材现做一百道“创意菜”，一一呈现给杨广。
　　杨广看中了就吃一筷子，看不中就端下去，特别喜欢也顶多只吃两筷子。
　　一百道菜流水般的从杨广面前端过。
　　杨广先吃，萧皇后其次，李世民和李玄霸非常荣幸地紧随其后。
　　李玄霸只吃了一半就饱了，李世民坚持到了最后。
　　杨广见李世民食量这么大，夸赞道：“以你的食量，将来肯定能给朕当冠军侯！”
　　李世民揉了揉肚子，道：“谢表叔夸奖。”
　　杨广对李玄霸道：“李三郎，你可要多吃些。”
　　李玄霸苦笑：“侄儿努力。”
　　杨广也吃撑了，带着李世民和李玄霸在甲板上散步，观看两岸秀丽景色。
　　岸边，民夫仍旧在努力地拉动着纤绳。
　　李玄霸看向河边的纤夫。
　　他没有在河边长大。虽然从书本中读过“纤夫”这个职业，听说过在黄河三门峡和长江三峡水流最湍急的地方，若船只想要越过峡口逆流而上，就需要纤夫在两侧岸上拉船。但脑海里对其并没有画面。
　　跟着隋炀帝坐了一次龙舟，李玄霸才第一次见到现实中的纤夫。
　　人工运河水面很平静，水流速度不快。无论顺流还是逆流，都能靠着划桨和风帆让船只动起来。只有在遇到强逆风的时候，才需要纤夫在两岸拉船。
　　但龙舟太大太沉了，若要让这样大的船动起来，全程都需要纤夫拉动纤绳。
　　“阿玄，这龙舟不像是龙舟，倒是像一辆大大的马车。只是拉车的不是牛马，而是人。”李世民私下悄悄对李玄霸道。
　　李玄霸正思索着二哥那过分恰当的比喻，二哥的惊呼打断了他的思索。
　　“表叔！他们在做什么？为什么要把一整只烤牛都埋起来？”李世民惊讶地指向岸边，“这是在祭祀神灵吗？”
　　杨广远眺壮丽河山的视线随着李世民的手指，落在了近处的两岸边。
　　他皱眉看向身边宦官。
　　宦官低着头为皇帝解惑道：“官员和百姓仰慕陛下，每日进贡食物太多，过了夜就不新鲜，便就近掩埋了。”
　　杨广斥责道：“胡闹！”
　　李世民使劲点头。
　　对啊对啊，真是胡闹。好端端的食物怎么能埋了？唐国公府每日的饭菜也吃不完，都分给了仆人。若遇上府中设宴，食物过多，仆人也吃不完，娘亲就会挑些完好的送往佛寺，让佛寺代为救济穷人，其余的喂给牲畜。
　　窦夫人经常教育李世民和李玄霸，哪怕唐国公府极富贵，也不可过于铺张浪费，否则必定损害自家福气。
　　宦官立刻跪下道：“陛下息怒，是底下人懒惰了，居然污了陛下的眼睛。”
　　杨广愤怒地踹了宦官一脚。
　　宦官非常熟练地在杨广踹他的时候顺势往后一滚，既卸了力道，又装出很痛的模样，在地上翻滚了几圈后，再继续磕头告饶。
　　杨广唤来太常少卿裴蕴，只指着岸边食物掩埋地，面色阴沉，一言不发。
　　裴蕴立刻道：“臣立刻下令，让他们远离岸边十里再掩埋，以免玷污两岸好景。偷懒之人，臣定重罚！”
　　杨广冷哼道：“不要这点事还要朕命令你。”
　　裴蕴忙告罪。
　　杨广又骂了裴蕴几句，才让裴蕴去处理岸上的事。
　　见了这等肮脏事，杨广大好的心情蒙上了阴霾。
　　李世民茫然地看着皇帝发怒，小小的脑袋瓜子有些不太明白发生了什么。
　　他本准备开口询问，被李玄霸用心声提醒“闭嘴等着，赶紧装傻”，便没有开口。
　　杨广发完怒后，看着两个孩子害怕的模样，身为长辈的理智上线，将怒气压下，道：“一些渎职之人扰了兴致。二郎三郎别怕，朕已经处理了。”
　　李世民更加迷糊。皇帝表叔所做的事，和他想象的完全不一样。
　　李玄霸一言不发，只继续装作被皇帝怒气吓到的模样，怯生生地点头。
　　心情被打扰，杨广没了继续带孩子赏景的兴致。
　　他让人把李世民和李玄霸带给萧皇后，自己回到了为首的龙舟上，继续就此事大发雷霆。
　　李世民和李玄霸借口困了，回到自己的小房间。
　　李世民抱着软乎乎的抱枕，终于把憋在心底的疑惑说了出来：“表叔生气的地方好奇怪啊。”
　　李玄霸趴在房里窗口上，继续看着窗外。
　　李世民把李玄霸往旁边挤了挤，也趴着看向岸边。
　　他们的小窗口，也能看到食物掩埋地。
　　宫人将食物掩埋了一半，被赶来的官吏训斥了一番后，将挖好的坑匆匆填土，剩余的食物抬上车，运向了更远的地方。
　　岸上的民夫轮番拉船休息。休息的民夫悄悄刨开泥土，想要挖出里面的食物。
　　船上又下来了一个官吏。这个官吏带了一队卫兵。
　　卫兵将挖开地面的民夫按在地上捆了起来，然后不知道押去了何地。
　　地上的坑再次被填上。
　　李世民和李玄霸静静地看完了整场。
　　李玄霸：【所过州县，五百里内皆令献食；后宫厌饫，将发之际，多弃埋之。】
　　李世民：“什么？”
　　李玄霸；【隋炀帝一游江都。】
　　李世民抿住嘴唇，这次没有提醒弟弟别乱说话。
　　他继续茫然地看向窗外。
　　半晌，李世民道：“吃不完的饭菜为何不能分给岸边的人？他们连土里的饭菜都要挖出来，应该是很饿了。”
　　李玄霸这次没有在心里说话。
　　他开口讥笑道：“是啊，为什么。”
　　李世民看向李玄霸：“阿玄也不知道？”
　　李玄霸道：“不知道不知道。”
　　李世民鼓起腮帮子：“阿玄你一定知道，为何不和哥哥说？”
　　李玄霸道：“说了有什么用？哥哥你自己看，自己想。”
　　李世民把李玄霸扑倒，狠狠挠了李玄霸一顿痒，在李玄霸告饶后，才翻身躺到李玄霸身旁：“好烦。算了，我还小，想不明白就想不明白。等我长大了，自然就明白了。”
　　李玄霸擦了擦被挠痒痒笑出来的眼泪，没好气道：“这是娘和阿姊经常敷衍我们的话。你倒是学到了。”
　　“嘿嘿。”李世民咧嘴笑了笑。
　　他笑完后，将手放在胸口处。
　　完好的食物宁愿掩埋也不肯给岸边的民夫食用。皇帝发怒却不是因为浪费食物，而是因为食物掩埋地被他看见。
　　这一切都让年幼的李世民疑惑不解。
　　此时，他想起了弟弟说漏嘴的“隋炀帝”，想起了自己偷偷翻书找到的“炀”的含义。
　　李世民抱住了脑袋，在床上滚来滚去：“啊，不想了。我还小，想那么多干什么！”
　　李玄霸点头：“对。等你长大了再慢慢想。”
　　李世民抱着头滚了许久，才停下了滚动招式。
　　他大字躺在榻上，手脚都搭在了李玄霸的身上。
　　李玄霸嫌弃地把二哥往旁边推。
　　李世民：“阿玄，我长大了就能想明白吗？”
　　李玄霸：“谁知道？过去！”
　　李世民：“阿玄，哥哥胸闷，让哥哥靠一下。”
　　李玄霸：“不给！去去去，热死了！”
　　李世民使劲往李玄霸身上凑，李玄霸手脚并用把二哥推开。
　　兄弟二人就躺在床榻上“打”了起来。
　　杨广回龙舟发了一顿脾气后，回想起李世民和李玄霸的神情，总觉得当时两个小孩的神色似乎有些不敬。
　　他立刻派人去查看李世民和李玄霸正在做什么。
　　派出的宫女回禀：“李二公子和李三公子正在榻上厮打。”
　　杨广挑眉：“哦？厮打？他兄弟二人感情不是很好吗？怎么会厮打？”
　　宫女道：“奴婢问了守门的仆妇。仆妇说似乎是李二公子要把李三公子当枕头，李三公子嫌弃李二公子太重，于是两人就打了起来。”
　　杨广：“……”
　　他扶额失笑：“这理由……还真是孩童才会有的理由。”
　　他在心底摇摇头。或许是今日太生气，他连两个六岁孩童的神情都怀疑起来。
　　若李世民和李玄霸暗藏不敬之色，小孩是没有城府的，那肯定是李渊教的。
　　说白了，杨广现在对连个孩子的怀疑，本质上还是对李渊不放心。
　　“他们今日受惊了，拿些金珠子给他们玩。”杨广道，“还有，传朕的命令，兄弟要友悌。为这点小事打架可不像话。若他们再打，朕可是要罚他们抄书了。”
　　宫女领命退下，陪坐的官吏皆失笑。
　　……
　　李世民和李玄霸“打了一架”，居然还得了皇帝赏赐。
　　萧皇后得知后，笑得眼角都泛出了泪花。
　　她对来请安的长女南阳公主道：“你来母后这里住几日，多摸摸唐国公府这两个活宝贝。你的肚子现在都还没动静，母后实在是忧心。你赶紧生个像李家二郎三郎这样的活宝贝给母后带。”
　　南阳公主是萧皇后和皇帝的长女，十四岁嫁给许国公之子宇文士及，如今刚二十。夫妻二人都深受皇帝皇后喜爱，皆伴驾南巡。
　　宇文士及是李渊的好友，南阳公主与窦夫人相处也不错。
　　她笑道：“确实是活宝贝，窦夫人每每提及他们就咬牙切齿，说他们在家中很是顽皮。”
　　萧皇后笑道：“还有这事？窦夫人倒是和我说，他二人自幼体弱，让她很是怜惜呢。”
　　自幼体弱？南阳公主稍一沉思，就明白了窦夫人为何如此说。
　　恐怕是母后得知李家双生子下了荥阳郑氏的脸面，很高兴地想让娘家族中女儿与李家双生子定亲吧。
　　唐国公府的大公子娶了荥阳郑氏，其余几子的妻子肯定得稍逊一些。南阳公主无奈，母后太看重娘家，这个念头有些不妥当了。
　　她笑道：“是啊，李家二郎和三郎既顽皮，又体弱，窦夫人教训了会心疼，不教训又担心他们学坏，真是头疼极了。”
　　萧皇后笑得更加厉害：“是这个理。别岔开话题，母后还给你求了送子观音……”
　　南阳公主见话题没岔过去，捂着红彤彤的脸道：“母后，娘亲，娘娘！再给女儿一些时间，会有外孙的，会有的！”
　　萧皇后道：“你总是如此说。好吧好吧，你脸皮薄，送子观音先不给你了。你去揉揉李二郎和李三郎的脑袋，这总行吧？”
　　南阳公主捂着脸，无奈道：“行，女儿把李二郎和李三郎抱怀里使劲揉脑袋！”
　　萧皇后笑道：“来人啊，赶紧把李二郎和李三郎带来！”
　　于是李世民和李玄霸一脸迷茫地被叫来，然后被南阳公主抱怀里使劲揉搓了一顿脑袋。
　　李世民晕乎乎的。
　　怎么回事，为什么要搓我的脑袋？
　　李玄霸使劲板着脸。
　　我是玩具，我是玩具，我不尴尬，我没有感情。
　　南阳公主看着两个孩子可爱的模样，心头一暖，还真想生个和李二郎李三郎一样可爱的孩子了。
　　她笑着道：“我捏了你们脸，作为补偿，可有什么想要的？”
　　萧皇后笑道：“你还真是慷慨。二郎，三郎，想要什么尽管提，她手中的好东西可多了。”
　　母女俩都兴致勃勃地好奇这两个有“神童”之名的孩子，会索要什么“补偿”。
　　李玄霸揉着被捏红的脸：【我们随意要两件首饰送给祖母和娘如何？】
　　李世民犹豫了一下，对南阳公主道：“我可以悄悄和公主说吗？”
　　南阳公主低下头，把耳朵附过去：“说吧。”
　　李世民双手捧着嘴，在南阳公主耳边小声道：“我听闻南阳公主最受陛下喜爱。公主可否劝谏陛下，吃不完的食物别埋了，送给岸边拉船的人？我看他们好像非常饿。如果他们太饿，就拉不动船了，陛下也不会开心。”
　　南阳公主杏眼微睁。
　　她抬起头，仔细地打量怀里的孩童一番。
　　李世民满脸恳求地望着南阳公主。
　　李玄霸看看自家二哥，又看看南阳公主，小小的眉头紧皱。
　　二哥究竟说了什么恳求？
　　李玄霸：【二哥，你说什么了？】
　　李世民看向岸边，然后收回视线。
　　李玄霸想了想，道：【你该不会想让南阳公主劝隋……隋朝皇帝节俭？】
　　李世民眨了眨眼睛。
　　李玄霸又想了想，道：【朝中肯定有人就节俭一事劝过皇帝，没用的。】
　　萧皇后好奇道：“李二郎和你说什么了？”
　　南阳公主回过神，笑道：“他想给窦夫人讨要首饰。唉，这有什么好悄悄说的。”
　　李世民愣住。
　　李玄霸拉住李世民的手：【公主如此说，就证明皇帝如果得知你的话会很不高兴。她在护着你。】
　　李世民抿了抿嘴唇，握紧了弟弟的手。
　　南阳公主揉了揉李世民的脑袋，道：“母后，我想带着李二郎和李三郎去给郎君看看，让郎君也沾沾两个孩子的聪明气。”
　　萧皇后笑道：“去吧，晚上记得送回来。”
　　南阳公主点头：“好。”
　　她让自己的侍女抱起李玄霸，自己抱着李世民，回自己居住的船上找丈夫宇文士及。
　　路上，南阳公主悄声道：“父皇最不喜人劝谏。世民，你心善是好的，但不要被父皇听到了。”
　　她很郑重地称呼了李世民的名字。
　　李世民垂下脑袋，有些沮丧。
　　南阳公主心中叹息。
　　听李世民这么一说，她也有些怜惜岸边的民夫了。
　　但她既为最得宠的公主，自然深知父皇喜恶。
　　这话是说不得的。以父皇性格，进贡的东西就是烧了，也不可能给低贱的庶民用。
　　皇帝怎能与庶民吃同样的食物？
　　其实这件事，早就有大臣劝过。
　　无论是令沿岸州县进贡食物，还是将吃不完的食物掩埋，平昌县公宇文弼劝谏过好几次。父皇私下常常辱骂宇文弼。
　　南阳公主见状，自然是不敢触父皇霉头的。
　　李玄霸一直注视着自家二哥。
　　待他们下了船，又上了船，李玄霸才在心里开口。
　　李玄霸：【哥，别想了。我俩都还是小孩子，你想得也太多了。你能不能想些符合我们这个年龄的孩子该想的事？比如吃什么玩什么。】
　　李世民抬起头，转头对李玄霸努力咧嘴傻笑：【好！】
　　兄弟二人跟着南阳公主先拜见了驸马宇文士及，又跟着宇文士及前往船上朝中重臣的房间串了一会儿门。傍晚时分，他们才被南阳公主亲自送回了萧皇后的船上。
　　两人累得沾枕头就睡。
　　第二日，船队继续航行。
　　李世民再未和李玄霸提起过不该小孩子考虑的话题。
　　十二月中旬，李世民和李玄霸终于抵达了江都。

Chapter 18: Things Children Shouldn't Think About

“It’s so noisy!” Li Shimin covered his ears.

“So noisy I could die!” Li Xuanba scratched his brother’s arm in frustration.

The two wet nurses who accompanied them were sewing cloth pads, their hearts aching for the boys. “Bear with it a little longer, young masters. It will be finished very soon.”

After scratching his brother, Li Xuanba said listlessly, “No rush. Be careful not to prick your hands.”

The wet nurse smiled. “We won't prick our hands, don't worry.”

Li Xuanba nodded, lowered his head, and resumed scratching his brother’s arm.

He was driven half-mad.

Li Xuanba thought he had prepared for every contingency, but he had never expected the people on this dragon boat to possess such boundless energy.

During the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui, seven types of regional music and dance had been established as the "Seven-Part Music"—namely Guoji, Qingshangji, Gaoliji, Tianzhuji, Anguoji, Qiuciji, and Wenkangji. When Yang Guang ascended the throne, he added Kangguoji and Shuleji, expanding it into the "Nine-Part Music."

On the lead vessels—including the one carrying Li Shimin and Li Xuanba—ensembles of the "Nine-Part Music" performed in shifts, their soft singing and graceful dances continuing without pause throughout the night.

Li Shimin: “Stop singing, help!”

Li Xuanba: “Could we get some soothing, hypnotic music instead, please and thank you!”

Tired of the singing and dancing? No matter. In the intervals between rounds of the "Nine-Part Music," entertainers led exotic beasts to perform acrobatic spectacles known as the "Manyan Yulong"—the Grand Dragon and Fish Illusions.

The most enthralling part of these performances involved fire acrobatics. Such acts began at dusk and continued unabated until dawn. Eunuchs and guards stood watch all night to ensure the fire tricks did not accidentally set the vessel ablaze.

Li Shimin: “Can you stop stomping on the deck in the middle of the night?! Are you drumming with your feet?!”

Li Xuanba: “So sleepy... Stop torturing my eardrums.”

At night, bonfires were also lit on the deck.

The bonfires rested within bronze braziers, fueled by the finest agarwood. As the flames burned, an exotic fragrance pervaded the air, making one feel as if they were floating in a realm of immortals.

Li Shimin: “Achoo!”

Li Xuanba: “Achoo!”

For the first few days, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba would hold hands and go watch the commotion. But soon, let alone Li Xuanba being driven mad, even Li Shimin wilted.

Don't these adults ever sleep?!

Unless strictly necessary, the two children refused to step foot outside.

They lay in their room constantly, keeping their eyes closed to rest their spirits even if they couldn't fall asleep.

In a stroke of desperation, Li Xuanba had the wet nurses seal several layers of silk within fine linen to craft thick, sound-dampening earmuffs.

He and Li Shimin first plugged their ears with rolled paper, then donned the thick earmuffs, finally managing to get a good night's sleep.

Though keeping paper stuffed in their ears for too long left them a bit sore.

Seeing the two children hiding in their room and refusing to come out, Empress Xiao grew worried. She ordered the imperial physicians to examine Li Shimin and Li Xuanba daily and adjust their prescriptions constantly.

Under the two boys' aggrieved stares, the imperial physician prescribed them some soothing mind-calming remedies, then tactfully suggested to the Empress that the children were young and frail, unable to bear the clash of so much boisterous human presence, and recommended moving them to a quieter boat to recuperate.

Empress Xiao sighed. “Lady Dou mentioned that both boys suffered from congenital weakness and were quite difficult to raise. I used to laugh, thinking she was overly anxious. Only after taking care of them myself for a while do I appreciate her hardship.”

Moving them to another vessel was out of the question; Empress Xiao did not trust anyone else to care for them.

Instead, she had Li Shimin and Li Xuanba moved from the main hall on the first deck to a room in the middle section of the second deck. The room was much smaller, but being farther from the main deck granted the two boys a good deal of peace and quiet.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba could finally remove the paper plugs and sleep with just their earmuffs.

After a few days of sound sleep, Li Shimin finally recovered his vigor.

Though not yet seven years old, he actually felt a sensation of having survived a great calamity: “I declare that I will never watch the 'Nine-Part Music' or the 'Grand Dragon and Fish Illusions' again!”

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes at his second brother: 【Impossible.】

Li Shimin hugged his soft pillow and rolled around on the bed: “I won't watch them! I just won't!”

Li Xuanba disliked hard pillows, so he had people make a variety of pillows and bolsters filled with down, animal fur, grain husks, and medicinal herbs.

Whatever belonged to Li Sanlang also belonged to Li Erlang. Li Shimin had adopted Li Xuanba's bad habit, bringing his own pillows and bolsters wherever he went.

Li Xuanba ignored his revitalized second brother.

He lay quietly, eyes blank, relaxing his brain to continue resting his spirit.

“We've been eating inside the room all these days. Let's eat outside today!” Li Shimin dragged his lazy younger brother up. “I heard the shore towns present local delicacies every day. Ah Xuan must really want to try them!”

Li Xuanba: 【No, I don't.】

Li Shimin dragged Li Xuanba out of bed, forcing his brother—whose bones had turned to jelly from lying down—to go to the deck for exercise.

The imperial physician had said that after catching up on sleep, one ought to move around more. Children needed exercise to stay healthy.

Seeing Li Shimin and Li Xuanba "recovered," Empress Xiao breathed a sigh of relief.

She had the two boys sit to her left and right, treating them as her own, personally selecting food for them.

Before Empress Xiao stood a massive table two meters long and one meter wide. Palace maids and eunuchs brought dish after dish in turns—fruits, pastries, roasted dishes, soups, and steamed delicacies of every description.

Just as the food was served, Yang Guang arrived.

His voice arrived before his person: “Erlang, Sanlang, I heard you fell ill? How are your bodies feeling now?”

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba hurriedly stood up and bowed. “We have completely recovered.”

Yang Guang patted the two children's heads and said, “No need for formality. I merely came to see you. I shall take lunch here today.”

The moment the Emperor arrived, before a single bite of the food on the table could be eaten, the entire table along with the feast was carried away.

Eunuchs brought in an even longer dining table carved with dragons and phoenixes, serving a fresh spread of dishes.

Every day, local officials along the river were required to present rare and prized ingredients.

These foods did not necessarily all reach Yang Guang's plate, but Yang Guang had officers audit the tribute. If the submitted ingredients were rare and abundant, the local officials stood a chance of promotion; if Yang Guang was dissatisfied, their official caps were lost.

During meals, the Imperial Kitchen would use the daily tribute to prepare a hundred "novel dishes" on the spot, presenting them one by one to Yang Guang.

If Yang Guang took a liking to a dish, he would taste a single morsel; if not, it was whisked away. Even if he favored a dish immensely, he would eat two mouthfuls at most.

A continuous stream of a hundred dishes flowed past Yang Guang.

Yang Guang dined first, followed by Empress Xiao, with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba honored to follow right after.

Li Xuanba was full halfway through, but Li Shimin persevered to the very end.

Seeing Li Shimin's massive appetite, Yang Guang praised, “With an appetite like yours, you will surely become my Marquis of Champion in the future!”

Li Shimin rubbed his belly and said, “Thank you for the praise, Cousin-Uncle.”

Yang Guang said to Li Xuanba, “Li Sanlang, you ought to eat more.”

Li Xuanba gave a wry smile. “Your nephew will try his best.”

Yang Guang himself was stuffed, so he took Li Shimin and Li Xuanba for a walk on the deck to admire the picturesque scenery along both banks.

Along the shore, laborers were still straining against the towropes.

Li Xuanba looked toward the trackers on the riverbank.

He had not grown up by the river. Though he had read about the profession of "trackers" in books—hearing that in the most treacherous rapids of Sanmenxia on the Yellow River and the Three Gorges of the Yangtze, trackers were needed on both banks to haul ships upstream through the gorges—he had no mental picture of it.

Only by taking this trip on the dragon boat with Emperor Yang of Sui did Li Xuanba witness real-life trackers for the first time.

The waters of the man-made Grand Canal were calm, and the current was gentle. Whether going downstream or upstream, boats could be propelled by oars and sails alone. Trackers were only required on both banks when encountering fierce headwinds.

However, the dragon boat was far too massive and heavy. To move such a vessel, trackers were needed to haul the towropes for the entire journey.

“Ah Xuan, this dragon boat doesn't feel like a boat at all; it's more like a giant carriage. Except instead of oxen and horses pulling it, it's pulled by people,” Li Shimin whispered to Li Xuanba privately.

As Li Xuanba reflected on his brother's exceedingly apt comparison, his brother's gasp interrupted his thoughts.

“Cousin-Uncle! What are they doing? Why are they burying a whole roasted ox?” Li Shimin pointed toward the riverbank in astonishment. “Are they offering a sacrifice to the gods?”

Yang Guang, who had been gazing into the distance at the magnificent mountains and rivers, followed Li Shimin's finger down to the nearby shore.

Frowning, he looked toward the eunuch beside him.

The eunuch bowed his head and explained for the Emperor: “The officials and commonfolk revere Your Majesty so greatly that they present vast quantities of food every day. As it loses its freshness overnight, it is buried nearby.”

Yang Guang reprimanded harshly, “Absurd!”

Li Shimin nodded vigorously.

Exactly! Truly absurd! How could good food be buried like that? The Duke of Tang's estate couldn't finish all its daily food either, but the surplus was distributed to the servants. If a banquet was hosted and there was too much food for even the servants to finish, their mother would pick out intact dishes to send to Buddhist temples for the poor, feeding the rest to the livestock.

Lady Dou often taught Li Shimin and Li Xuanba that even though the Duke of Tang's house was immensely wealthy, they must never be overly extravagant, lest they squander their family's blessings.

The eunuch immediately dropped to his knees. “May Your Majesty appease your wrath! It is the laziness of the subordinates below that has soiled Your Majesty's eyes.”

Yang Guang angrily kicked the eunuch.

The eunuch was exceedingly adept at this: as Yang Guang kicked him, he used the momentum to roll backward, mitigating the force while putting on an act of severe pain. After tumbling several times on the floor, he resumed kowtowing for mercy.

Yang Guang summoned Pei Yun, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Pointing at the burial site of the food on the bank, his expression was dark, uttering not a single word.

Pei Yun immediately understood: “Your servant shall order them to bury it ten *li* away from the banks at once, so as not to defile the fine views of the shores! As for those who shirked their duties, your servant will punish them severely!”

Yang Guang snorted coldly. “Must I command you even for matters such as this?”

Pei Yun hastily begged forgiveness.

Yang Guang scolded Pei Yun a few more times before sending him off to deal with the shore affairs.

Witnessing such an unsightly affair cast a shadow over Yang Guang's cheerful mood.

Li Shimin watched the Emperor's rage in bewilderment, his little head unable to grasp what had just happened.

He was about to ask when Li Xuanba warned him mentally: 【Shut up and wait, play dumb quickly.】 So he kept his mouth shut.

After venting his anger, Yang Guang saw the frightened expressions on the two children. His sense of elder decorum returned, and he suppressed his anger, saying, “Some derelict fools have ruined the mood. Erlang, Sanlang, do not be afraid. I have already dealt with it.”

Li Shimin grew even more confused. What Emperor Cousin-Uncle had done was completely different from what he had expected.

Li Xuanba said nothing, merely continuing to act frightened by the Emperor's rage, nodding timidly.

With his mood ruined, Yang Guang lost interest in taking the children sightseeing.

He ordered servants to take Li Shimin and Li Xuanba back to Empress Xiao, while he returned to the flagship dragon boat to continue flying into a rage over the matter.

Excusing themselves as tired, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba returned to their small room.

Hugging his soft bolster, Li Shimin finally voiced the doubt he had bottled up: “The reason Cousin-Uncle got angry is so strange.”

Li Xuanba leaned against the window sill, continuing to gaze outside.

Li Shimin nudged Li Xuanba aside a bit and leaned out to look at the shore as well.

From their small window, they could also see the food burial site.

The servants had only buried half the food when they were scolded by an arriving official. They hurriedly filled in the dug pits, loaded the remaining food onto carts, and hauled it off to a more distant location.

The laborers on shore took turns resting from pulling the boats. Some of the resting laborers quietly scraped away the soil, attempting to dig out the buried food.

Another official descended from the vessel, leading a squad of guards.

The guards pinned the food-digging laborers to the ground, bound them, and marched them off to places unknown.

The pit in the ground was refilled once again.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba silently watched the entire scene.

Li Xuanba: 【"Wherever the royal procession passed, prefectures and counties within five hundred li were commanded to present food; when the inner palace grew sated and tired of it, as the fleet set sail, most of it was discarded and buried."】

Li Shimin: “What?”

Li Xuanba: 【"Emperor Yang of Sui's first tour of Jiangdu."】

Li Shimin pressed his lips together, this time not reminding his brother not to speak recklessly.

He continued to stare blankly out the window.

After a long silence, Li Shimin asked, “Why can't the leftover food be distributed to the people on the shore? They're digging up food from the dirt; they must be starving.”

This time, Li Xuanba did not speak in his mind.

He opened his mouth and said sneeringly, “Yeah, why indeed?”

Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba: “Ah Xuan doesn't know either?”

Li Xuanba said, “Don't know, don't know.”

Li Shimin puffed out his cheeks. “Ah Xuan, you definitely know. Why won't you tell your brother?”

Li Xuanba said, “What's the use of telling you? Look with your own eyes, Brother, and think for yourself.”

Li Shimin tackled Li Xuanba, tickling him mercilessly until Li Xuanba begged for mercy. Only then did he roll over to lie beside Li Xuanba: “So annoying. Forget it, I'm still young. If I can't figure it out, so be it. When I grow up, I'll naturally understand.”

Li Xuanba wiped away the tears brought on by laughter from the tickling, saying crossly, “That's the phrase Mother and Elder Sister always use to brush us off. You sure learned it quickly.”

“Hehe.” Li Shimin grinned.

After laughing, he placed his hand over his chest.

Perfectly fine food was buried rather than given to the starving laborers on shore to eat. And the Emperor grew angry not because food was wasted, but because the sight of the burial spot offended his eyes.

All of this filled the young Li Shimin with confusion.

At this moment, he recalled the phrase "Emperor Yang of Sui" that his brother had accidentally let slip, and he remembered the meaning of "Yang" that he had secretly looked up in books.

Li Shimin clutched his head and rolled back and forth on the bed. “Aagh, I won't think about it anymore! I'm still young, why am I thinking so much!”

Li Xuanba nodded. “Right. Think about it slowly when you grow up.”

Li Shimin rolled around holding his head for a long while before ceasing his rolling technique.

He sprawled in a spread-eagle posture on the couch, flinging his arms and legs over Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba pushed his second brother aside in disgust.

Li Shimin: “Ah Xuan, will I really figure it out when I grow up?”

Li Xuanba: “Who knows? Move over!”

Li Shimin: “Ah Xuan, my chest feels stuffy. Let me lean on you for a bit.”

Li Xuanba: “No way! Go away, go away, it's boiling hot!”

Li Shimin squirmed closer to Li Xuanba with all his might, while Li Xuanba used both hands and feet to shove his second brother away.

The two brothers proceeded to "brawl" right there on the couch.

After returning to his dragon boat and flying into a rage, Yang Guang recalled the expressions of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. He couldn't help but feel that the two children had looked slightly disrespectful at the time.

He immediately dispatched someone to check on what Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were doing.

The dispatched maid returned and reported: “Second Young Master Li and Third Young Master Li are currently brawling on the couch.”

Yang Guang raised an eyebrow. “Oh? Brawling? Is their brotherly affection not usually very deep? How could they be brawling?”

The maid said: “This servant inquired of the door-keeping maidservants. The maidservants said it seems Second Young Master Li wanted to use Third Young Master Li as a pillow, but Third Young Master Li complained that Second Young Master Li was too heavy, so the two started fighting.”

Yang Guang: “...”

He held his forehead and laughed aloud. “This reason... is truly a childish reason through and through.”

He shook his head internally. Perhaps he was simply too furious today, to the point of suspecting even the expressions of two six-year-old children.

If Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had harbored disrespect, children lacked guile; it would surely have been taught by Li Yuan.

At its core, Yang Guang's suspicion of the two children was fundamentally his distrust of Li Yuan.

“They were startled today; bring them some gold pearls to play with,” Yang Guang ordered. “Also, convey my decree: brothers must show sibling affection and harmony. Fighting over such trivial matters is improper. If they fight again, I shall punish them by making them copy books!”

The maid took the order and withdrew, while the attending officials all chuckled.

……

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had "had a fight" and somehow ended up receiving imperial rewards.

When Empress Xiao learned of this, she laughed until tears welled at the corners of her eyes.

She said to her eldest daughter, Princess Nanyang, who had come to pay respects: “Come stay with your Mother for a few days and rub these two treasures of the Duke of Tang's estate often. There's still no movement in your belly, which leaves Mother deeply worried. Hurry up and give Mother a darling treasure like the Li family's Erlang and Sanlang to dote on.”

Princess Nanyang was the eldest daughter of Empress Xiao and the Emperor. She had married Yuwen Shiji, son of the Duke of Xu, at age fourteen, and was now twenty. Both husband and wife were deeply beloved by the Emperor and Empress and accompanied the imperial tour south.

Yuwen Shiji was a good friend of Li Yuan, and Princess Nanyang got along well with Lady Dou.

She smiled and said, “They are indeed treasures. Whenever Lady Dou mentions them, she grits her teeth, saying they are terribly mischievous at home.”

Empress Xiao chuckled. “Is that so? Lady Dou told me that the two of them have been weak since birth, causing her great concern and pity.”

*Weak since birth?* Princess Nanyang pondered briefly and understood why Lady Dou had said so.

Most likely, Mother had learned that the Li twins had embarrassed the Zheng clan of Xingyang, and was happily contemplating betrothing daughters of her maternal clan to the Li twins.

Since the eldest son of the Duke of Tang's estate had married a daughter of the Zheng clan of Xingyang, the wives of the other sons would naturally have to be of somewhat lower status. Princess Nanyang felt helpless; her mother placed too much weight on her maternal family, making such a thought inappropriate.

She smiled and said, “Indeed, the Li family's Erlang and Sanlang are both mischievous and frail. Lady Dou feels her heart ache when she scolds them, but fears they will turn bad if she doesn't. It's truly a headache for her.”

Empress Xiao laughed even harder. “That makes sense! But don't change the subject—Mother even went to pray for a Child-Giving Guanyin for you...”

Seeing that she failed to divert the topic, Princess Nanyang covered her flushed face and pleaded, “Mother, Imperial Mother, Your Majesty! Give your daughter a bit more time. You will have a grandchild, you will!”

Empress Xiao said, “You always say that. Fine, fine, since you're so thin-skinned, I won't give you the Child-Giving Guanyin for now. Go rub Li Erlang and Li Sanlang's heads instead. How about that?”

Princess Nanyang covered her face and sighed helplessly. “Fine, your daughter will hug Li Erlang and Li Sanlang tightly and give their heads a good rubbing!”

Empress Xiao laughed, “Attendants, bring Li Erlang and Li Sanlang at once!”

Thus, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were summoned with bewildered faces, only to be scooped into Princess Nanyang's arms and have their heads vigorously rubbed and patted.

Li Shimin felt dizzy.

*What's going on? Why is she rubbing my head?*

Li Xuanba maintained a deadpan expression with all his strength.

*I am a toy. I am a toy. I am not embarrassed. I have no feelings.*

Looking at the adorable appearance of the two children, Princess Nanyang's heart warmed, and she genuinely felt like having a child as cute as Li Erlang and Li Sanlang.

She smiled and said, “I pinched your faces. As compensation, is there anything you want?”

Empress Xiao chuckled. “You are generous indeed. Erlang, Sanlang, ask for whatever you wish; she has plenty of fine treasures in her possession.”

Both mother and daughter were intensely curious to see what "compensation" these two children, who possessed the reputation of "child prodigies," would request.

Li Xuanba rubbed his red face: 【How about we just ask for two pieces of jewelry to give to Grandmother and Mother?】

Li Shimin hesitated for a moment, then said to Princess Nanyang, “May I tell the Princess secretly?”

Princess Nanyang lowered her head and inclined her ear. “Go ahead.”

Li Shimin cupped his hands around his mouth and whispered into Princess Nanyang's ear: “I heard Princess Nanyang is most favored by His Majesty. Could the Princess persuade His Majesty not to bury the uneaten food, but to give it to the people pulling the boats on the shore? I see they seem very hungry. If they are too hungry, they won't be able to pull the boat, and His Majesty won't be happy either.”

Princess Nanyang's almond eyes widened slightly.

She raised her head, scrutinizing the child in her arms carefully.

Li Shimin looked back at Princess Nanyang with a face full of pleading.

Li Xuanba looked at his second brother, then at Princess Nanyang, his small brow tightly furrowed.

*What plea did Second Brother just make?*

Li Xuanba: 【Second Brother, what did you say?】

Li Shimin looked toward the shore, then withdrew his gaze.

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and said: 【You didn't try to get Princess Nanyang to advise the Sui... Sui Emperor to be frugal, did you?】

Li Shimin blinked.

Li Xuanba thought a bit more and said: 【There must have been people in court who advised the Emperor on frugality; it's useless.】

Empress Xiao asked curiously, “What did Li Erlang say to you?”

Princess Nanyang snapped back to reality and smiled. “He wanted to ask for jewelry to give to Lady Dou. Ah, why be so secret about that?”

Li Shimin froze.

Li Xuanba took Li Shimin's hand: 【By saying that, the Princess proves the Emperor would be furious if he found out what you said. She is protecting you.】

Li Shimin pressed his lips together and held his brother's hand tightly.

Princess Nanyang patted Li Shimin's head and said, “Mother, I would like to take Li Erlang and Li Sanlang to see my husband, so he can soak in some of their cleverness too.”

Empress Xiao smiled. “Go on, just remember to bring them back by evening.”

Princess Nanyang nodded. “Understood.”

She had her maid carry Li Xuanba while she carried Li Shimin, heading back to her own vessel to find her husband, Yuwen Shiji.

On the way, Princess Nanyang whispered, “Imperial Father despises being remonstrated with above all else. Shimin, your kind heart is good, but do not let Imperial Father hear such things.”

She formally addressed Li Shimin by his name with great solemnity.

Li Shimin hung his head, feeling somewhat dispirited.

Princess Nanyang sighed inwardly.

Hearing Li Shimin put it that way, she too felt a pang of pity for the laborers on the banks.

Yet, as the most favored princess, she naturally knew her father's likes and dislikes inside out.

Such words could never be spoken. Given her father's character, tribute items would rather be burned than given to lowly commoners.

How could an Emperor eat the same food as commoners?

In fact, ministers had long since advised against this very matter.

Whether it was commanding prefectures and counties along the river to present food, or burying the surplus uneaten food, Yuwen Bi, Duke of Pingchang, had remonstrated several times. Her father frequently cursed Yuwen Bi in private.

Seeing this, Princess Nanyang naturally dared not provoke her father's wrath.

Li Xuanba kept his eyes on his second brother.

Only after they disembarked from one vessel and boarded another did Li Xuanba speak in his mind.

Li Xuanba: 【Brother, stop thinking about it. We are both still children; you're thinking way too much. Can't you think about things appropriate for kids our age? Like what to eat or play with.】

Li Shimin raised his head and turned to force a silly grin at Li Xuanba: 【Okay!】

The two brothers followed Princess Nanyang to pay respects first to the Emperor's son-in-law, Yuwen Shiji, and then accompanied Yuwen Shiji on visits to the cabins of high court officials on board. At dusk, Princess Nanyang personally escorted them back to Empress Xiao's boat.

Exhausted, the two fell asleep the moment their heads hit the pillows.

The next day, the fleet resumed its voyage.

Li Shimin never again raised topics with Li Xuanba that children shouldn't ponder.

In mid-December, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba finally arrived in Jiangdu.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第19章 赐下了三位老师
chunks.chineseText:
第19章 赐下了三位老师

=
　　杨广曾任扬州总管， 江都是他经营了十年的地方。
　　江都的行宫已经建好。他带着众臣重游故地，在马背上奏乐，做《江都宫乐歌》。
　　“扬州旧处可淹留， 台榭高明复好游。风亭芳树迎早夏， 长皋麦陇送馀秋。
　　渌潭桂楫浮青雀， 果下金鞍跃紫骝。绿觞素蚁流霞饮，长袖清歌乐戏州。”
　　歌伎们怀抱各种乐器，侧坐在马背上边弹边唱。
　　骏马前行的时候， 歌伎衣袂飘飘，仿佛天宫中的仙女。
　　李世民和李玄霸年幼，没有参加这一场马背上的游园会。
　　他们和萧皇后坐在高台上赏景。从栏杆下往下望去， 正好能看到皇帝和众臣的“游园图”。
　　萧皇后笑道：“三郎，你擅长作诗， 据说能五步成诗， 现在可有灵感？”
　　李玄霸“老实”道：“其实我的五步成诗是提前做了准备。去郑家之前，我已经猜到他们可能会出的诗题，大约就是描绘一些景物而已，总不会太过为难我。现在让我作诗，我还要琢磨一会儿。”
　　萧皇后没有因为李玄霸的“坦白”而小瞧李玄霸， 反而更加喜爱李玄霸的聪慧。
　　“不急，慢慢想， 想不到也没关系。”萧皇后揉了揉李玄霸的脑袋，道，“作诗只是小道。”
　　李玄霸点头：“是。”
　　李世民凑到李玄霸耳边小声道：“你不是能看到未来人的诗？真的选不出一首好的？”
　　李玄霸：【人生得意须尽欢， 莫使金樽空对月。】
　　李世民的眼睛扑闪扑闪。这不是挺好吗！
　　李玄霸无奈：【这是诗仙李白不得志时候的诗， 你看我的阅历可能写出这样的诗吗？抄诗也要符合人设， 循序渐进。现在我的阅历就只能抄些单纯的写景诗。再大一些， 可以抄些有少年意气诗。不过我现在确实有一首诗可以用。等皇帝回来，我就献给他。】
　　李玄霸要来笔墨纸砚，写写画画涂涂，装作很努力地在挤诗句的模样。
　　李世民帮李玄霸研墨。
　　萧皇后和后妃、公主都好奇地看“神童”作诗。
　　待杨广玩耍结束，回来邀请萧皇后和后妃去水边散步时，看到李玄霸和李世民的脸上都抹了墨，像是楚州进贡的小花猫似的。
　　杨广朗声笑道：“李二郎，李三郎，你们在做什么！”
　　李玄霸抬起小花脸：“回陛下，我在作诗。”
　　李世民抬起小花脸：“回陛下，在玩笔墨。”
　　杨广听见李玄霸说作诗时好奇地凑上来看李玄霸做的什么诗，听见李世民的话后哭笑不得，抬手敲了一下李世民的脑袋。
　　杨广低头看着李玄霸已经写出来的四句诗，念道：“舳舻千里泛归舟，言旋旧镇下扬州。借问扬州在何处？淮南江北海西头。还行。”
　　是还行，你自己做的诗，能不行？
　　李玄霸现在所写的诗，就是杨广所作的《泛龙舟》。
　　后世人根据《泛龙舟》所描绘景象，认为这是杨广在南下途中写的。但杨广每次有写诗的灵感，都会与萧皇后品鉴，李玄霸确定杨广现在还没有琢磨出《泛龙舟》。
　　李玄霸猜测，这个时空中的《泛龙舟》，可能是杨广在江都回忆南下情形时写的。
　　杨广自己的诗，他应该是喜欢的。而且如果杨广现在心中已经有了“诗意”，李玄霸正好帮杨广把这首诗引出来。
　　杨广曾说，“设令朕与士大夫高选，亦当为天子矣”。他对自己的才华很自傲，很不喜欢别人的才情压过他。
　　李玄霸如果拿来一首李白的诗惊艳四座，不说年龄和阅历不合适，只说“惊艳”，他就完蛋了。
　　李玄霸眼巴巴道：“陛下，接下来侄儿该抒发胸臆了。可侄儿怎么想，在船上的生活都是吵，困，累。”
　　杨广先惊愕，然后失笑：“让你伴驾，你还抱怨了？”
　　李世民帮弟弟解释道：“我们还小，欣赏歌舞对我们来说还太早了。”
　　说罢，他背着手，像个小老头一样沉沉地叹了口气。
　　可惜他脸上那几条墨痕太过滑稽，看着不像少年老成，更加像顽童耍宝。
　　杨广身后的大臣都好奇地看着这两个面对皇帝完全不胆怯的孩童。
　　皇帝将外戚家的孩子养在身边一段时间很常见，如汉武帝就曾亲自培养霍去病，霍去病还嫌弃不肯学。霍去病的儿子霍嬗也是四岁授侍中，常伴汉武帝左右。
　　哦，这两个人都死得早。
　　大臣们在得知皇帝将唐国公府的一对双生子养在皇后处时，都私下道唐国公李渊恐怕是陛下唯一不忌惮的亲戚了。
　　现在看见李二郎和李三郎对皇帝亲近自在的模样，他们心中更加确信了这一点。
　　杨广对喜爱的人十分纵容。现在他对李世民和李玄霸正是有好感的时候，很乐意做这慈祥长辈。
　　他让宫女打来水给李世民和李玄霸擦脸，笑话道：“朕可没让你们去看歌舞，而是让你们好好看看这壮阔山河，增加见识。”
　　正被宫女仔细擦脸的李玄霸将手中的笔双手捧起：“侄儿增长的见识不足以写完这首诗，陛下，帮侄儿添几句。”
　　杨广还未说话，萧皇后已经笑得花枝乱颤：“我让你写诗，你却让陛下来帮你？陛下，可不能帮他写。”
　　李玄霸道：“龙舟宏伟，小儿年幼，实在是写不出能描绘龙舟宏伟意境的诗。”
　　杨广笑着拿起李玄霸双手捧起的笔：“好，朕帮你添几句。”
　　他看着这四句诗时，心中就很自然地浮现出后四句，就好像这四句诗本来就在心中，只是借着李玄霸的诗句引出来而已。
　　略一沉思，杨广运笔如飞，补道：“六辔聊停御百丈，暂罢开山歌棹讴。”
　　李玄霸嘴角为不可见的上弯。
　　杨广沉思了一会儿，写完最后两句：“讵似江东掌间地，独自称言鉴里游。”
　　李世民看着这两句诗，眼中出现向往之情。
　　李玄霸敬佩道：“‘掌间地’和‘鉴里游’二句，只有皇帝能写出来。表叔，你替侄儿补完了这首诗，侄儿能蹭着表叔的诗才传世了。”
　　李世民收起向往的神色，好奇道：“阿玄，这就是你所说的，你和人一起嘎嘎乱杀，表叔负责乱杀，你负责嘎嘎？”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　哥你的思维其实可以不用这么发散！
　　杨广闻言，捧腹大笑。
　　他用颇为自得的语气自谦道：“算不上什么传世佳作，恰恰能看而已。虞世南，你的字最好，你来帮朕重抄一遍这首诗！”
　　一个面相清瘦，鬓间有些许白色发丝的中年人出列，拱手道：“是，陛下。”
　　李玄霸眨了眨眼。嗯？我刚是不是听到了一个很熟悉的名字？
　　他抬头看向虞世南。
　　虞世南挽起衣袖，正想铺开一张新的纸，体贴的李世民立刻伸长小短手，帮虞世南铺好了纸，还殷勤地研墨。
　　李世民道：“早听耶耶……早听父亲说，虞舍人的字是一绝，阿玄阿玄，今日我们能开眼界了！”
　　李玄霸顺着二哥的话道：“对。”
　　他为虞世南捧来一支新的笔。
　　杨广笑道：“李渊确实向朕夸赞过虞卿的字。以虞卿的字配朕的诗，勉强相称。”
　　虞世南先见着两个孩子懂事的模样，眼神不由露出些许暖意。听了皇帝的话之后，他将眼中感情收敛，恢复成波澜不惊的模样。
　　他洗笔蘸墨，笔下字迹如行云流水，一气呵成。
　　杨广大笑一声：“好！给朕装裱起来！”
　　虞世南放下笔，恭敬地退到一边。
　　李世民很小就喜爱书法。他围着虞世南的字绕来绕去，兴奋得停不下来，把杨广和萧皇后都逗得大笑。
　　李玄霸乖巧地站在一边，用眼角余光打量虞世南。
　　他想起来这名字为何耳熟了。
　　虞世南，秦王府文学馆“十八学士”，凌烟阁二十四功臣，我哥的心腹重臣。
　　现在的唐太宗李世民还是一个六岁的孩童，虞世南是一个近五十岁郁郁不得志的中年人。
　　虞世南垂首站在一侧，眼神沉郁如结了冰的古井，把心里所有豪情壮志都封锁其中。
　　他此刻大概都不会相信还有被明君慧眼识珠的一天。
　　李玄霸：【哥，虞世南将来以刚直敢谏闻名于世，时称“德行、忠直、博学、文词、书翰”五绝。】
　　李世民的视线从虞世南的字离开，投向了那个微微躬着身，表现得十分卑微的中年人。
　　这模样不像个刚直敢谏的臣子啊。
　　李玄霸：【现在他还不是。】
　　哦。李世民挠挠头。人的变化真大啊。
　　但虞舍人看上去年纪已经不小了，难道是白发苍苍后才突然变成刚直的人？
　　虞世南注意到李世民的视线。
　　李世民不仅没觉得尴尬，还对虞世南笑了一下。
　　他对杨广道：“陛下，我和阿玄玩了这么久，也该重新拾起学业了。虞舍人的字真好看，我和阿玄可以跟着虞舍人学字吗？”
　　李玄霸：“……”哪有人自己给自己增加功课的？
　　杨广笑道：“朕正有此意。”
　　杨广把李世民和李玄霸带在身边是当做晚辈教养，所以自然是会派人教他们读书识字。
　　只是龙舟上的生活太快乐，杨广把这件事忘记了。
　　萧皇后见两人年幼，在龙舟上又身体不适，也没有提起此事。
　　现在到了江都，两小也该继续上学了。
　　宫中现在还没有正上学的皇子皇孙。杨广琢磨着让李二郎和李三郎试试臣子们教学的本事，算是提前给他以后肯定会有的小皇子和已经出生的小皇孙，提前选拔老师人选。
　　杨广本没将虞世南纳入老师人选。
　　他用李世民和李玄霸试探臣子教学水平，选的老师也是皇子皇孙将来的老师。
　　虞世南虽有才名，但他在杨广面前沉默寡言，唯唯诺诺，只有一手字值得称赞。杨广还看不上他。
　　李世民喜欢虞世南的字，杨广又觉得孩童首先要学会写一手好字，让虞世南给皇子皇孙当教写字的师傅也算合适。
　　定下虞世南后，杨广唤出刑部尚书宇文弼，道：“宇文尚书，你托口年老体衰，不愿与朕一同游玩，那你就暂时给李二郎和李三郎当一段时间师傅，教导他们读书习字如何？朕带他们南巡，若他们疏忽了功课，李渊肯定会埋怨朕。宇文尚书大才，教导孩童应该绰绰有余。”
　　除了李世民，所有人都听出了皇帝语气中的阴阳怪气。
　　李玄霸努力思考。这个名字也有些耳熟，但他一时半会儿记不起来。隋末姓“宇文”的重要臣子太多了。
　　宇文弼平静地拱手道：“是，陛下。”
　　见宇文弼居然十分平静地接受了这件差事，杨广感觉有一口气堵在胸口处，上不去下不来，真快憋死了。
　　宇文弼所在的“宇文”一脉和北周皇室没有关系，不是亲戚。
　　平昌县公宇文弼在北周和隋文帝时都被重用，是威望极重的三朝老臣。他为官极正，慷慨有大节，常向杨广进谏。杨广非常厌恶宇文弼，但又同时知道宇文弼确实是贤才。所以他准备将宇文弼从身边踢走，丢给辅佐太子，教导皇孙。
　　杨广可以好好说话，以施恩的方式任命宇文弼去辅佐太子。但他就是忍不下这口气，非要刺上几句。
　　宇文弼却一副“长者”的姿态，不理睬皇帝的嘲讽，好像皇帝自己在那里无理取闹似的，脸上居然一丝屈辱的神色都看不见。
　　杨广更生气了。
　　但宇文弼顺从地遵守自己的命令，杨广无法以此事责难宇文弼，只能将气忍下，又道：“太常高颎，你来教李二郎和李三郎经义。”
　　一位老者出列领命：“臣遵旨。”
　　咦？李玄霸又听到一个耳熟的名字，但仍旧一时半会儿想不起来。
　　“阿玄，你愣着干什么？赶紧拜师。”众人都因为皇帝选出的这两个“老师”人选而额头冷汗直冒，连萧皇后都收起了笑容，只有李世民在那傻乐，“弟子李世民拜见老师！阿玄！我们拜了举世闻名的贤才为师哦！”
　　“啊……弟子李玄霸，拜见老师。”李玄霸跟着拱手行礼。
　　宇文弼淡然道：“唐国公倜傥豁达，宽仁容众。他的孩子，臣是教得的。”
　　杨广脸色一沉。
　　萧皇后见气氛不妙，立刻打圆场：“拜师怎么能没有拜师礼？来人，把二郎三郎的拜师礼端来。”
　　她笑道：“陛下，是否让二郎和三郎给三位老师磕个头？”
　　杨广沉郁道：“磕吧。”
　　李世民仍旧傻乐傻乐的，拉着李玄霸给三位老师磕头。
　　杨广以让三人备课为由，让三人提前离开。萧皇后又和其他后妃一起夸奖了杨广写的诗，杨广脸色才好转。
　　第二波游园这才再次开始。
　　……
　　跟着皇帝玩耍了半日，李世民和李玄霸也提前离开，去准备明日上学要用的东西。
　　“三位重臣为我们授课，表叔对我们真好。”李世民道。
　　李玄霸道：“皇帝应该是借由我们考校他们三人的授课能力，为教导皇孙做准备。我俩回到洛阳后就会离开皇宫，算不得他们真正的弟子。”
　　李世民拍了拍李玄霸的肩膀：“阿玄啊，我们能有机会跟随宇文公和高公学习一段时间，已经是天下人都会羡慕的事。你还想当他们真正的弟子？娘亲说过，做人不要太贪心，这不好。”
　　李玄霸无视了时不时就要找机会在自己面前“说教”，好彰显他兄长地位的二哥，转移话题道：“宇文公和高公很有名？”
　　李世民得意道：“阿玄，你虽通晓过去和未来之事，怎么对当世的事不上心？耶耶常和我们说起朝中大贤，你忘记了？”
　　李玄霸在心里道，李渊“授课”的时候过于枯燥，说的又大多是自己已经知道的事，自己基本都在睁着眼睛打瞌睡，确实忘记了。
　　李世民见弟弟居然真的不知道，非常高兴地把自己对两人的了解告诉李玄霸。
　　好难得遇到阿玄不懂的事！终于可以教导一次阿玄了！李世民胸口膨胀得快要飞起来。
　　李玄霸听着二哥的描述，与自己前世的记忆作对比。
　　他听着听着，脸色越来越白。
　　李世民还未介绍完两人的功绩，正收拾明日要用的文具的李玄霸手一抖，砚台砸在了桌上，发出“哐当”一声巨响。
　　李世民被吓了一跳。
　　李世民按住弟弟的肩膀道：“阿玄？怎么了？什么完了？你身体不舒服？哥哥去叫御医，你等着！”
　　“别去！”李玄霸拉住二哥，道，“没什么，我只是手滑。”
　　李世民打量李玄霸的神色，见李玄霸确实没有异常，出门问乳母要了一杯温水，让李玄霸喝下后，他才继续与李玄霸收拾东西。
　　之后李玄霸以身体疲惫为由提前睡下。李世民精力还很充沛，去院子里练习射箭。
　　李世民离开后，李玄霸睁开眼，看着床幔发呆。
　　他想起来高颎和宇文弼是谁了。
　　高熲此人在后世网络因与独孤皇后有关，有些“流量”。
　　在网络中流传的故事中，独孤皇后是一夫一妻制的坚决拥护者，因为高熲先为亡妻悲伤不娶，后又让爱妾怀孕，独孤皇后认为高熲对亡妻不忠诚，所以进言隋文帝杨坚疏远高熲，导致高熲被削职为民。
　　网络以此故事来赞扬独孤皇后。
　　事实当然不是如此，这就是单纯的政治斗争而已。
　　独孤皇后虽然管杨坚管得严，但不会闲得去管别人的后院，对儿子的要求也只是别宠妾灭妻。其实独孤皇后倚重的大臣就没有不妻妾成群的。
　　她做此事，只是铲除太子杨勇的支持者。
　　高颎文韬武略，德高望重，因其女为太子杨勇侧妃，是杨勇的重要支持者。隋文帝曾想废太子事，因高颎劝阻“长幼有序”而打消主意。独孤皇后因此想要除掉高颎。
　　所谓“对亡妻不忠诚”之事的全貌是，独孤皇后先让隋文帝给高颎娶继室，高颖以年老拒绝；后高颎有妾室怀孕，独孤皇后进言“高颎因心怀爱妾而拒绝皇帝赐妻，是对皇帝不忠”，让年老后疑心甚重的隋文帝逐渐加深对高颎的猜忌。
　　杨广继位后，发布诏令，说自己要广纳谏言，召回隋文帝晚年卷入夺嫡之争的老臣，高颎也被拜为太常。
　　杨广喜声乐，光收天下乐工，高颎上奏阻止；杨广修运河修东京，之后还要修长城，高颎请求暂缓工程；杨广对启民可汗过于恩宠厚待，高颎认为应该警惕突厥，不可信任厚待过重。
　　大业三年，高颎因“诽谤朝政”被杀，诸子皆被流放。
　　高颎不是什么“反派”，而是隋朝的忠良。
　　同样，宇文弼也因为多次进谏招得杨广厌恶，与高颎同死于“诽谤朝政”。
　　杨广深恶高颎。高颎死后，著名诗人、司隶大夫薛道衡当众赞美高颎的才华，被杨广找借口处死。
　　自己和二哥拜高颎和宇文弼为师，待高颎和宇文弼持续向杨广进谏，惹得杨广厌恶被诛杀后，以杨广的小心眼，恐怕也会对自己和二哥生出恶感，甚至迁怒唐国公府。
　　哪怕这师生关系，是杨广自己牵的。
　　李玄霸没打算将此事过早向李世民“预言”。
　　虽然他偶尔“说漏嘴”，但会给二哥增加过多心理负担的东西，他都瞒得死死的。
　　二哥再早熟，也只是六岁孩童。
　　“得想个法子与他们疏远，让隋炀帝知道我和二哥不喜欢他们。”李玄霸把头蒙进缝了厚毛皮的锦被中，小声嘀咕给自己打气，“能做到的，一定能。”
　　他心里很是慌乱。
　　李玄霸虽然常在李世民面前用后世人的视角“指点江山”“愤世嫉俗”，但他对自己有几斤几两很清楚。
　　隋末唐初群英荟萃，能站在历史舞台上的人无不是人中龙凤。自己若是能和这些人同台竞争，他在现代就不会只是一个历史营销号小编了。
　　杨广杀宇文弼和高颎是注定的，朝堂群臣都劝不住的事，自己一个小孩能做什么？
　　他所能做的，就只有尽可能地拉着二哥与这两个注定会死的大隋忠良撇清关系。
　　后世常说李渊对建立唐朝没有功劳，这不是事实。
　　唐太宗李世民虽有战功，但起兵的资本是唐国公李渊，众人最初投效的也是李渊。
　　在古代，资历、声望、年龄十分重要。
　　李渊没有李世民，可能只能成为割据势力的一员，甚至直接被窦建德等势力吞并，湮灭历史尘埃中；但同样，未及弱冠的李世民也很难独自与群雄逐鹿，即使他救驾的功劳没被吞也不可能。
　　隋朝国公那么多，独李渊能成事，是因为李渊当时有兵权。若不是李渊在大业末年得到杨广的信任，得到了太原的兵权，唐国公府就无法顺利起事。
　　如果杨广因高颎之事忌惮排挤李渊，李渊无法取得杨广的信任，就不可能出镇太原，手握兵权。
　　虽然李玄霸知道历史不会那么容易改写，说不定李渊没有兵权，唐国公府也能通过其他方式募兵起事。但史书中薛道衡的结局，仍旧让李玄霸恐惧。
　　谁不怕死？他装得很淡然，其实心中一直对喜怒无常，有暴虐之名的杨广有些惧怕。
　　“早知道就不该讨好杨广。”李玄霸嘟囔，“但杨广都把我和哥叫到面前了，我们不讨好他也会完蛋。真烦。”
　　李玄霸把脑袋从被子里冒出去，深呼吸了几下新鲜空气，让自己冷静下来。
　　拒绝老师也不行，摆烂不好好读书以让高颎和宇文弼厌恶自己更不行。这老师是杨广给的，如果他们不尊重老师，不努力读书，也会被认为是对皇帝的不尊敬。
　　X的，真烦！
