Chapter 19: Bestowed with Three Teachers

Yang Guang had once served as the Area Commander of Yangzhou; Jiangdu was a territory he had managed for ten years.

The temporary palace in Jiangdu was already completed. Leading his ministers to revisit his old haunts, he played music on horseback and composed the *Jiangdu Palace Music Song*.

"In Yangzhou's ancient haunts, one fain would linger long,
Where lofty towers and terraces invite a joyous throng.
Breezy pavilions and fragrant trees welcome early summer's light,
While long dikes and wheat fields bid late autumn goodnight.
Upon the emerald pool, cassia oars float the blue-sparrow bark,
Beneath the fruit trees, golden saddles leap on purple steeds of mark.
From green cups of frothing wine, we drink the rosy clouds of dawn,
With long sleeves and clear songs, in this land of joy we carry on."

The singing girls cradled various musical instruments, sitting sidesaddle on horseback as they played and sang.

As the fine steeds trotted forward, the girls' sleeves fluttered in the wind, making them look like celestial maidens from the heavenly palace.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, being young, did not participate in this equestrian garden party.

Instead, they sat on a high terrace with Empress Xiao to enjoy the view. Looking down from the balustrade, they had a perfect view of the Emperor and his ministers' "garden stroll."

Empress Xiao smiled and said, "Sanlang, you are skilled in poetry. It is said you can compose a poem in five steps. Do you have any inspiration now?"

Li Xuanba replied "honestly," "To tell the truth, my five-step poetry was prepared in advance. Before going to the Zheng family, I had already guessed the topics they might propose—mostly just describing scenery, nothing too difficult. If you ask me to compose a poem on the spot now, I still need to ponder it for a while."

Empress Xiao did not look down on Li Xuanba because of his "candor"; instead, she grew even fonder of his cleverness.

"No rush, take your time. It does not matter if you cannot think of anything." Empress Xiao patted Li Xuanba's head and said, "Composing poetry is merely a minor art."

Li Xuanba nodded. "Yes."

Li Shimin leaned in and whispered in Li Xuanba's ear, "Can't you see the poems of future generations? Can't you really choose a good one?"

Li Xuanba: *[When life goes well, one must enjoy oneself to the full; let not the golden goblet face the moon in vain.]*

Li Shimin's eyes blinked rapidly. *Isn't that excellent!*

Li Xuanba replied helplessly: *[This is a poem written by the Immortal of Poetry, Li Bai, when he was frustrated and unappreciated. Look at my age and experience—is it possible for me to write such a poem? Plagiarizing poetry must fit one's persona and progress step-by-step. With my current experience, I can only copy simple landscape poems. When I am older, I can copy poems filled with youthful vigor. However, I do have a poem I can use right now. When the Emperor returns, I will present it to him.]*

Li Xuanba called for brush, ink, paper, and inkstone. He began writing, drawing, and scribbling, pretending to struggle mightily to squeeze out some verses.

Li Shimin helped grind the ink for him.

Empress Xiao, the imperial consorts, and the princesses all watched the "child prodigy" compose poetry with curiosity.

By the time Yang Guang finished his amusements and returned to invite Empress Xiao and the consorts for a stroll by the water, he saw that both Li Xuanba and Li Shimin had ink smeared all over their faces, looking like little calico cats sent as tribute from Chuzhou.

Yang Guang laughed heartily. "Li Erlang, Li Sanlang, what are you two doing!"

Li Xuanba lifted his ink-stained face. "Replying to Your Majesty, I am composing a poem."

Li Shimin lifted his own ink-stained face. "Replying to Your Majesty, I am playing with the brush and ink."

Hearing Li Xuanba say he was composing poetry, Yang Guang leaned over curiously to see what he had written. But upon hearing Li Shimin's reply, he didn't know whether to laugh or cry, and reached out to tap Li Shimin on the head.

Yang Guang looked down at the four lines Li Xuanba had already written and read aloud:

"'A thousand miles of sterns and bows, the returning vessel floats,
Returning to the old commandery, down to Yangzhou it goes.
May I ask where Yangzhou lies?
South of the Huai, north of the Yangtze, at the western edge of the sea.'

Not bad."

*Of course it's "not bad." It's a poem you wrote yourself; how could it be bad?*

The poem Li Xuanba was currently writing was none other than Yang Guang's own work, *Sailing the Dragon Boat (Fan Long Zhou)*.

Future generations, based on the scenes described in *Sailing the Dragon Boat*, believed Yang Guang had written it during his journey south. However, whenever Yang Guang had the inspiration to write a poem, he would always appreciate it with Empress Xiao. Li Xuanba was certain that Yang Guang had not yet conceived *Sailing the Dragon Boat* in this timeline.

Li Xuanba guessed that in this timeline, *Sailing the Dragon Boat* might be written by Yang Guang while reminiscing about his journey south during his stay in Jiangdu.

Yang Guang would surely like his own poem. Moreover, if Yang Guang already had the "poetic intent" in his heart, Li Xuanba could use this opportunity to draw the poem out of him.

Yang Guang had once said, "Even if I were to compete in a grand selection alongside the scholar-bureaucrats, I would still deserve to be the Emperor." He was extremely proud of his own talent and loathed being surpassed by others.

If Li Xuanba were to bring out a poem by Li Bai to stun everyone, not only would his age and experience be a poor fit, but that very "stunning" quality would spell his doom.

Li Xuanba said with wide, pleading eyes, "Your Majesty, next, your nephew should express his inner feelings. But no matter how I think about it, life on the boat was just noisy, sleepy, and tiring."

Yang Guang was first startled, then burst into laughter. "I allowed you to accompany my imperial carriage, and yet you complain?"

Li Shimin helped explain on his brother's behalf, "We are still small. Appreciating songs and dances is still too early for us."

Having said that, he put his hands behind his back and sighed heavily like a little old man.

Unfortunately, the ink streaks on his face were too comical. Rather than looking precocious, he looked more like a mischievous child playing the fool.

The ministers behind Yang Guang all looked curiously at these two children, who showed absolutely no fear in front of the Emperor.

It was common for emperors to raise the children of imperial relatives by their side for a time. For instance, Emperor Wu of Han had personally raised Huo Qubing, who even disdained studying. Huo Qubing's son, Huo Shan, was also appointed Palace Attendant at the age of four, constantly accompanying Emperor Wu.

*Oh, both of those people died young.*

When the ministers learned that the Emperor was raising the twin sons of the Duke of Tang's household under the Empress's care, they all whispered in private that Duke Li Yuan of Tang was likely the only relative the Emperor did not fear.

Seeing how close and at ease Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were with the Emperor now, they became even more convinced of this.

Yang Guang was highly indulgent toward those he liked. Since he currently held a favorable opinion of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, he was more than happy to play the role of a benevolent elder.

He ordered the palace maids to fetch water to wipe Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's faces, teasing, "I did not ask you to watch songs and dances, but to take a good look at these magnificent rivers and mountains to broaden your horizons."

As the palace maid carefully wiped his face, Li Xuanba held up the brush with both hands. "Your nephew's broadened horizons are not enough to finish this poem. Your Majesty, please add a few lines for your nephew."

Before Yang Guang could speak, Empress Xiao was already shaking with laughter. "I asked you to write a poem, yet you ask His Majesty to help you? Your Majesty, you must not write it for him."

Li Xuanba said, "The dragon boat is magnificent, but this child is young. I truly cannot write verses that capture its grand spirit."

Yang Guang smiled and took the brush held up by Li Xuanba's hands. "Very well, I shall add a few lines for you."

As he looked at the four lines, the next four naturally surfaced in his mind, as if they had been there all along, merely drawn out by Li Xuanba's verses.

After a brief moment of contemplation, Yang Guang's brush flew across the paper as he added:

"'The six reins are briefly halted to manage the hundred-zhang towline,
Temporarily ceasing the mountain-clearing to sing the oarsmen's song.'"

The corners of Li Xuanba's mouth curved upward imperceptibly.

Yang Guang pondered for a moment and wrote the final two lines:

"'How can this compare to the palm-sized land of Jiangdong,
Where they vainly boast of traveling within a mirror's view?'"

Looking at these two lines, a look of yearning appeared in Li Shimin's eyes.

Li Xuanba said with admiration, "The lines 'palm-sized land' and 'traveling within a mirror' could only be written by an Emperor. Imperial Uncle, you have completed this poem for your nephew. Now, your nephew can ride on Imperial Uncle's poetic talent to be remembered down the generations."

Li Shimin put away his yearning expression and asked curiously, "Ah Xuan, is this what you meant by 'slaughtering the competition together'—where Imperial Uncle does the slaughtering, and you just do the quacking?"

Li Xuanba: "..."

*Brother, your mind really doesn't need to wander this far!*

Hearing this, Yang Guang clutched his stomach and laughed heartily.

In a rather self-satisfied yet falsely modest tone, he said, "It is hardly a masterpiece to be passed down through the ages, merely passable. Yu Shinan, your calligraphy is the best. Come and transcribe this poem for me!"

A thin, middle-aged man with a few silver hairs at his temples stepped forward, bowing with cupped hands. "Yes, Your Majesty."

Li Xuanba blinked. *Hmm? Did I just hear a very familiar name?*

He looked up at Yu Shinan.

Yu Shinan rolled up his sleeves. Just as he was about to spread out a new sheet of paper, the considerate Li Shimin immediately stretched out his short little arms to help spread the paper, and even diligently ground the ink.

Li Shimin said, "I have long heard Yeye... long heard Father say that Secretariat Drafter Yu's calligraphy is peerless. Ah Xuan, Ah Xuan, we are going to have our eyes opened today!"

Following his second brother's lead, Li Xuanba said, "Indeed."

He brought a new brush over for Yu Shinan.

Yang Guang smiled. "Li Yuan indeed praised Minister Yu's calligraphy to me. Matching Minister Yu's calligraphy with my poetry is barely a fitting match."

Seeing how sensible the two children were, a trace of warmth appeared in Yu Shinan's eyes. But upon hearing the Emperor's words, he suppressed his emotions and returned to his calm, unruffled demeanor.

He washed the brush and dipped it in ink. The characters flowed from his brush like moving clouds and flowing water, completed in a single breath.

Yang Guang laughed loudly. "Excellent! Have it mounted for me!"

Yu Shinan put down his brush and respectfully withdrew to the side.

Li Shimin had loved calligraphy since he was very young. He circled around Yu Shinan's writing, unable to contain his excitement, which made both Yang Guang and Empress Xiao laugh heartily.

Li Xuanba stood obediently to the side, observing Yu Shinan from the corner of his eye.

He remembered why this name sounded so familiar.

*Yu Shinan, one of the "Eighteen Scholars" of the Prince of Qin's literary academy, one of the Twenty-Four Meritorious Officials of Lingyan Pavilion, and my brother's trusted minister.*

The future Emperor Taizong of Tang, Li Shimin, was currently just a six-year-old child, while Yu Shinan was a frustrated middle-aged man of nearly fifty.

Yu Shinan stood to the side with his head bowed, his eyes as dark and gloomy as an icy, ancient well, locking away all the grand ambitions in his heart.

At this moment, he probably did not believe that there would ever come a day when a wise ruler would recognize his worth.

Li Xuanba: *[Brother, in the future, Yu Shinan will be world-renowned for his uprightness and daring remonstrances. He will be praised for the "Five Peerless Qualities": virtue, loyalty, erudition, literary style, and calligraphy.]*

Li Shimin's gaze shifted from Yu Shinan's calligraphy to the middle-aged man who was bowing slightly, appearing extremely humble.

*This appearance doesn't look like an upright and daring minister.*

Li Xuanba: *[He isn't one yet.]*

*Oh.* Li Shimin scratched his head. *People really change a lot.*

*But Secretariat Drafter Yu already looks quite old. Could it be that he only suddenly became upright after his hair turned white?*

Yu Shinan noticed Li Shimin's gaze.

Instead of feeling awkward, Li Shimin gave Yu Shinan a smile.

He said to Yang Guang, "Your Majesty, Ah Xuan and I have played for so long; it is time we resumed our studies. Secretariat Drafter Yu's calligraphy is so beautiful. Can Ah Xuan and I study calligraphy under him?"

Li Xuanba: "..." *Who on earth asks for more homework?*

Yang Guang smiled. "I had exactly the same intention."

Yang Guang had brought Li Shimin and Li Xuanba along to raise them as juniors, so he would naturally send someone to teach them to read and write.

It was just that life on the dragon boat had been too joyous, and Yang Guang had forgotten about it.

Seeing that the two were young and had been unwell on the dragon boat, Empress Xiao had not brought it up either.

Now that they had arrived in Jiangdu, the two little ones should continue their schooling.

There were currently no imperial princes or grandsons of school age in the palace. Yang Guang thought of using Li Erlang and Li Sanlang to test the teaching abilities of his ministers, serving as a trial run to select future tutors for his yet-to-be-born princes and his already-born grandsons.

Yang Guang had not originally considered Yu Shinan as a candidate for a teacher.

He was using Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to test the ministers' teaching abilities; the teachers chosen would also be the future tutors of the imperial princes and grandsons.

Although Yu Shinan had a reputation for talent, he was quiet and submissive in front of Yang Guang, with only his calligraphy worthy of praise. Yang Guang did not think highly of him.

Since Li Shimin liked Yu Shinan's calligraphy, and Yang Guang believed children should first learn to write a good hand, letting Yu Shinan serve as a calligraphy tutor for the imperial princes and grandsons seemed appropriate.

After settling on Yu Shinan, Yang Guang called out the Minister of Justice, Yuwen Bi, and said, "Minister Yuwen, you excused yourself on the grounds of old age and physical frailty, unwilling to join me in my amusements. How about you temporarily serve as a tutor for Li Erlang and Li Sanlang, instructing them in reading and writing? I brought them along on this southern tour; if they neglect their studies, Li Yuan will surely complain. With Minister Yuwen's great talent, teaching children should be more than within your capabilities."

Except for Li Shimin, everyone could hear the sarcasm in the Emperor's tone.

Li Xuanba thought hard. This name also sounded somewhat familiar, but he could not recall it for the moment. There were too many important ministers surnamed "Yuwen" in the late Sui Dynasty.

Yuwen Bi calmly bowed with cupped hands. "Yes, Your Majesty."

Seeing that Yuwen Bi accepted the task so calmly, Yang Guang felt a breath of air block his chest, unable to go up or down, nearly suffocating him with frustration.

The "Yuwen" lineage to which Yuwen Bi belonged had no relation to the Northern Zhou imperial family; they were not relatives.

Duke Yuwen Bi of Pingchang County had been heavily relied upon during both the Northern Zhou and the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui, making him a highly prestigious veteran of three reigns. He was extremely upright in office, generous and possessing great integrity, and frequently remonstrated with Yang Guang. Yang Guang detested Yuwen Bi, yet at the same time knew he was indeed a virtuous talent. Therefore, he planned to kick Yuwen Bi away from his side, sending him to assist the Crown Prince and tutor the imperial grandsons.

Yang Guang could have spoken politely and appointed Yuwen Bi to assist the Crown Prince as a favor. But he simply could not swallow his anger and had to throw in a few sharp barbs.

Yet Yuwen Bi maintained the posture of an elder, ignoring the Emperor's mockery as if the Emperor were merely making trouble out of nothing. Not a single trace of humiliation could be seen on his face.

Yang Guang grew even angrier.

But since Yuwen Bi obediently complied with his command, Yang Guang could not find fault with him over this matter. He could only swallow his anger and said, "Director of Imperial Sacrifices Gao Jiong, you shall teach Li Erlang and Li Sanlang the classics."

An elderly man stepped forward to receive the command. "Your servant obeys the decree."

*Eh?* Li Xuanba heard another familiar name, but still could not recall it for the moment.

"Ah Xuan, what are you dazing off for? Hurry and pay your respects to our teachers." While everyone else was breaking into a cold sweat over the two "teachers" the Emperor had chosen—even Empress Xiao had stopped smiling—only Li Shimin was grinning foolishly. "Disciple Li Shimin pays respects to the teachers! Ah Xuan! We have just taken world-renowned virtuous talents as our teachers!"

"Ah... Disciple Li Xuanba pays respects to the teachers." Li Xuanba followed suit, bowing with cupped hands.

Yuwen Bi said calmly, "The Duke of Tang is elegant, open-minded, magnanimous, and tolerant of others. I am well-suited to teach his children."

Yang Guang's face darkened.

Seeing the atmosphere turn sour, Empress Xiao immediately smoothed things over. "How can there be no apprenticeship gifts when taking a master? Someone, bring the apprenticeship gifts for Erlang and Sanlang."

She smiled and said, "Your Majesty, should Erlang and Sanlang kowtow to their three teachers?"

Yang Guang said gloomily, "Let them kowtow."

Still grinning foolishly, Li Shimin pulled Li Xuanba along to kowtow to the three teachers.

Using the excuse of letting the three prepare their lessons, Yang Guang dismissed them early. Empress Xiao and the other consorts praised Yang Guang's poem once more, and only then did his expression soften.

The second wave of the garden stroll finally resumed.

...

After playing with the Emperor for half a day, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba also left early to prepare the items they would need for school the next day.

"Three high ministers instructing us—Imperial Uncle is truly good to us," Li Shimin said.

Li Xuanba said, "The Emperor is likely using us to test their teaching abilities in preparation for tutoring the imperial grandsons. Once we return to Luoyang, we will leave the palace. We cannot be considered their true disciples."

Li Shimin patted Li Xuanba on the shoulder. "Ah Xuan, to have the opportunity to study under Lord Yuwen and Lord Gao for a time is already something the whole world would envy. You still want to be their true disciples? Mother said we must not be too greedy; it is not good."

Li Xuanba ignored his second brother, who constantly sought opportunities to "lecture" him to assert his status as the elder brother, and changed the subject. "Are Lord Yuwen and Lord Gao very famous?"

Li Shimin said proudly, "Ah Xuan, although you know the events of the past and future, why are you so indifferent to the affairs of the present? Yeye often spoke to us of the great sages in the court. Have you forgotten?"

Li Xuanba thought to himself that Li Yuan's "lessons" were far too dry, and most of what he said was stuff Xuanba already knew. He had basically spent those times dozing off with his eyes open, so he had indeed forgotten.

Seeing that his brother truly did not know, Li Shimin was delighted to share his knowledge of the two with Li Xuanba.

*It is so rare to find something Ah Xuan doesn't know! I can finally teach Ah Xuan for once!* Li Shimin's chest swelled with pride, feeling as if he were about to fly.

Li Xuanba listened to his second brother's description, comparing it with the memories of his past life.

As he listened, his face grew paler and paler.

Before Li Shimin could finish introducing their achievements, Li Xuanba, who was packing the stationery for the next day, trembled. The inkstone slipped from his hand and hit the table with a loud clatter.

"We're finished..." he muttered.

Li Shimin was startled. He grabbed his brother's shoulders and asked, "Ah Xuan? What's wrong? What do you mean, 'we're finished'? Are you unwell? I'll go call the imperial physician. Wait here!"

"Don't go!" Li Xuanba held his second brother back. "It's nothing, my hand just slipped."

Li Shimin studied Li Xuanba's expression. Seeing that there was indeed nothing wrong, he went out to ask the wet nurse for a cup of warm water. Only after making Li Xuanba drink it did he continue packing their things.

Afterward, Li Xuanba went to bed early on the pretext of being tired. Li Shimin, still bursting with energy, went to the courtyard to practice archery.

After Li Shimin left, Li Xuanba opened his eyes and stared blankly at the bed curtains.

He remembered who Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were.

In the internet of future generations, Gao Jiong had some "traffic" due to his connection with Empress Dugu.

In the stories circulating online, Empress Dugu was a staunch advocate of monogamy. Because Gao Jiong had initially grieved for his deceased wife and refused to remarry, but later got his beloved concubine pregnant, Empress Dugu believed he was unfaithful to his late wife. Thus, she advised Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, to distance himself from Gao Jiong, leading to Gao Jiong being stripped of his office and reduced to a commoner.

The internet used this story to praise Empress Dugu.

Of course, the truth was nothing of the sort; it was pure political struggle.

Although Empress Dugu kept a tight rein on Yang Jian, she was not so idle as to meddle in other people's backyards. Her only requirement for her sons was not to favor concubines over their principal wives. In fact, almost all the ministers Empress Dugu relied upon had herds of wives and concubines.

She did this solely to eliminate the supporters of Crown Prince Yang Yong.

Gao Jiong possessed both civil and military genius and was highly respected. Because his daughter was a consort of Crown Prince Yang Yong, he was a key supporter of Yang Yong. Emperor Wen had once wished to depose the Crown Prince, but abandoned the idea because Gao Jiong advised him that "order must be maintained between the elder and the younger." Consequently, Empress Dugu wanted to get rid of Gao Jiong.

The full picture of the so-called "unfaithfulness to his deceased wife" was that Empress Dugu had first asked Emperor Wen to arrange a second wife for Gao Jiong, which Gao Jiong refused on account of his old age. Later, when Gao Jiong's concubine became pregnant, Empress Dugu advised, "Gao Jiong refused the Emperor's gift of a wife because he harbors affection for his concubine; this is disloyalty to the Emperor." This caused the aging and increasingly suspicious Emperor Wen to gradually grow more distrustful of Gao Jiong.

After Yang Guang ascended the throne, he issued a decree stating his desire to widely accept remonstrances. He recalled the veteran ministers who had been embroiled in the succession struggle during Emperor Wen's later years, and Gao Jiong was appointed Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

Yang Guang loved music and gathered musicians from all over the world, which Gao Jiong petitioned to stop. Yang Guang built canals, constructed the Eastern Capital, and later wanted to repair the Great Wall, which Gao Jiong requested to postpone. Yang Guang showed excessive favor and hospitality to Qimin Khagan, but Gao Jiong believed they should remain vigilant against the Turks and not trust or favor them too heavily.

In the third year of the Daye era, Gao Jiong was executed for "slandering the court," and all his sons were exiled.

Gao Jiong was no "villain"; he was a loyal and upright minister of the Sui Dynasty.

Similarly, Yuwen Bi had also incurred Yang Guang's hatred due to his repeated remonstrances, dying alongside Gao Jiong under the charge of "slandering the court."

Yang Guang deeply detested Gao Jiong. After Gao Jiong's death, the famous poet and Metropolitan Commissioner Xue Daoheng publicly praised Gao Jiong's talent, only for Yang Guang to find an excuse to execute him as well.

If he and his second brother took Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi as their teachers, once Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi inevitably continued to remonstrate with Yang Guang, incurred his wrath, and were executed, Yang Guang—with his petty mind—would likely develop a distaste for them as well, perhaps even venting his anger on the Duke of Tang's household.

Even though this teacher-student relationship was arranged by Yang Guang himself.

Li Xuanba had no intention of "prophesying" this matter to Li Shimin too early.

Although he occasionally let things slip, he kept anything that would place too much of a psychological burden on his second brother strictly hidden.

No matter how precocious his second brother was, he was still only a six-year-old child.

"I must find a way to distance ourselves from them, to let Emperor Yang of Sui know that my brother and I do not like them." Li Xuanba buried his head in the brocade quilt lined with thick fur, whispering to encourage himself, "I can do it. I definitely can."

His heart was in a state of panic.

Although Li Xuanba often used the perspective of future generations to "critique the realm" and "vent his cynicism" in front of Li Shimin, he knew exactly how much he was worth.

The transition from the Sui to the Tang Dynasty was a gathering of heroes; those who stood on the stage of history were all dragons and phoenixes among men. If he truly had the ability to compete with these giants on the same stage, he wouldn't have been just a history clickbait editor in the modern era.

Yang Guang's execution of Yuwen Bi and Gao Jiong was predestined. If even the entire court of ministers could not dissuade him, what could a mere child like himself do?

All he could do was drag his second brother along to sever ties as much as possible with these two loyal ministers of Sui who were doomed to die.

Later generations often said that Li Yuan had no merit in founding the Tang Dynasty, but this was not true.

Although Emperor Taizong of Tang, Li Shimin, possessed great military achievements, the capital for raising the army belonged to Duke Li Yuan of Tang, and it was Li Yuan whom everyone initially pledged their allegiance to.

In ancient times, seniority, prestige, and age were of paramount importance.

Without Li Shimin, Li Yuan might have only become one of many warlords, or perhaps even swallowed up by forces like Dou Jiande, vanishing into the dust of history. But similarly, the underaged Li Shimin would have found it extremely difficult to contend with the various heroes alone, even if his achievement of rescuing the Emperor had not been usurped.

There were so many dukes in the Sui Dynasty, yet only Li Yuan succeeded because he held military power at the time. Had Li Yuan not gained Yang Guang's trust in the late Daye era and secured military command over Taiyuan, the Duke of Tang's household would never have been able to smoothly launch their rebellion.

If Yang Guang grew wary of and sidelined Li Yuan because of Gao Jiong's affair, Li Yuan would never have gained Yang Guang's trust, making it impossible for him to be stationed in Taiyuan and hold military power.

Although Li Xuanba knew that history was not so easily rewritten—perhaps even without military power, the Duke of Tang's household could have raised an army through other means—the fate of Xue Daoheng in the history books still filled him with dread.

Who wasn't afraid of death? He put on a calm front, but in truth, he had always harbored a deep fear of the mercurial and notoriously tyrannical Yang Guang.

"If I had known, I shouldn't have tried to flatter Yang Guang," Li Xuanba muttered. "But since Yang Guang already summoned my brother and me to his presence, we would have been finished if we didn't flatter him. What a pain."

Li Xuanba poked his head out of the quilt and took a few deep breaths of fresh air to calm himself down.

Refusing the teachers was out of the question. Slacking off and refusing to study hard to make Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi dislike them was even less of an option. These teachers were bestowed by Yang Guang; if they showed disrespect to their teachers or failed to study diligently, it would be seen as disrespect toward the Emperor.

Damn it, what a pain!

chunks.chapterTitle: 第20章 重病了都躲不过
chunks.chineseText:
第20章 重病了都躲不过

=
　　李玄霸想着想着就睡着了。
　　李世民练完弓箭， 回来找李玄霸一起泡热水澡。
　　江都的冬天比大业暖和，但夹杂着湿气的凉风仍旧让人手脚冰凉。李世民不在乎，但李玄霸晚上可能会睡不好觉。
　　见弟弟已经睡着， 眉头还皱着， 李世民伸手想帮弟弟把眉头抚平， 又怕把弟弟吵醒。
　　犹豫了一下，他缩回手，自言自语：“如果我快些长大就好了。”
　　他怎么会看不出弟弟心里藏着事？只是弟弟倔强， 若不想说的事，自己怎么问也问不出来。
　　李世民低头看着自己已经有了薄茧的手掌。
　　现在他拉的弓被弟弟叫“玩具弓”。
　　如果他能拉动耶耶常用的那种强弓，弟弟就会把所有烦心事都告诉自己了吧？
　　李世民让人拿了用毛皮裹着的汤壶塞进李玄霸脚边， 才去洗澡换衣服睡觉。
　　第二日，李世民感到身边居然有比他还烫的热源， 心头一凛， 困意瞬间消退，立刻睁眼起身。
　　“阿玄？阿玄？”李世民晃了晃身边的弟弟。
　　睡得迷迷糊糊的李玄霸艰难地睁开眼：“哥……咳咳。”
　　他捂住嘴，抑制不住一连串咳嗽。
　　李世民的眼泪一下子冒了出来，但眼泪出来时，他立刻使劲揉眼睛把眼泪揉掉， 换上了一副和孩童面貌十分不合适的成熟表情。
　　“阿玄不怕，哥哥在这里。”李世民一边飞速穿衣服， 一边大喊，“叫御医来！为我通报皇后，我要去见皇后！阿玄不怕， 哥哥马上把最好的御医找来。”
　　“咳咳咳。”李玄霸捂住嘴， 小小的身体弓起， 脸色绯红， 就像是一只煮熟了的虾。
　　他心中苦笑。昨日还在愁怎么避开杨广的老师，今日就生病了。
　　他所说的避开，可不是用生病啊。
　　古代这医药水平，小孩一场小病都可能夭折，何况他的身体羸弱。
　　明明他已经近一年没生过大病，只是换季时有些小咳嗽。二哥被郑家折腾生病的时候，他都支撑下来了。龙舟上睡不好觉，他也没有发烧。怎么就愁了一场，便又高烧了？
　　李玄霸很快就烧迷糊了，无法再胡思乱想。
　　御医让人给李玄霸解开了衣服，用温水擦拭身体给他降温，又用银针给他耳垂和手指上放了血。
　　折腾了近一个时辰，李玄霸身上的热度才降下去了少许，恢复了意识。
　　“阿玄，已经没事了，喝完药就好了。”李世民把李玄霸扶起来，让李玄霸靠着他坐起来。
　　李玄霸想接过药碗，但双手发软，端不住，差点撒了一身。
　　李世民及时把药碗扶好：“慢慢喝，我问表叔要了很多你最喜欢的蜜渍桃干，喝完药吃个够。”
　　乳母道：“二公子，我来喂吧。”
　　李世民摇头：“我来。”
　　御医正想说药很苦，李玄霸可能会喝很久，李世民端不住。李玄霸就低下头，李世民抬高碗底，李玄霸咕噜咕噜一口气喝完了满满一碗药。兄弟二人配合默契，好像已经重复过无数次。
　　李世民把药碗递给乳母，从袖口的布袋里摸出一块桃干。
　　李玄霸啃了两口桃干就忍不住干呕。
　　李世民拍了拍李玄霸的背，等李玄霸强忍着呕吐吃完桃干后，才把乳母端着的温开水喂给李玄霸。
　　先吃完一块桃干，又喝下了无味的温水，李玄霸才抑制住呕吐的冲动。
　　御医心中有些感慨。他擅长给孩童治病。孩童身心脆弱，良药苦口，每当喂孩童喝药时都很艰难，如李家三公子这样的孩童真是少见。
　　李玄霸喝完药之后又沉沉睡去。
　　御医特意叮嘱，不要给李玄霸捂汗。
　　他嘱咐给李玄霸盖薄被散热，每隔半个时辰就帮李玄霸用温水擦一遍身体。若李玄霸出现畏寒的情况也不要加厚被子，拿热水给李玄霸泡脚，泡到身体暖和就行。

　　但高颎也跟着宇文弼一同去教导李世民和李玄霸时，也把虞世南拉去了。
　　跟随杨广南巡的重臣都在同一艘楼船上，高颎主动向皇帝请求去教导唐国公府的二公子和三公子，很快就传遍了众臣之耳。
　　何况还有个宇文士及，简直得意得好像李世民和李玄霸是他儿子似的，逢人就炫耀，不想听都不行。
　　于是李世民和李玄霸再次名扬。
　　李玄霸对此只能苦笑。
　　他都重病一场了，还是没躲掉。
chunks.englishText:
Li Xuanba fell asleep amidst his drifting thoughts.

After practicing his archery, Li Shimin returned to find Li Xuanba so they could take a hot bath together.

Winter in Jiangdu was warmer than in Daye, but the damp, chilly wind still left one's hands and feet freezing. Li Shimin did not mind it, but Li Xuanba would likely sleep poorly because of it.

Seeing his younger brother already asleep with a furrowed brow, Li Shimin reached out to smooth it but hesitated, fearing he might wake him.

After a moment of indecision, he withdrew his hand and muttered to himself, "If only I could grow up faster."

How could he not see that his brother had something weighing on his mind? It was just that his brother was stubborn; if there was something he did not want to say, no amount of questioning would pry it out of him.

Li Shimin looked down at his palms, which had already developed thin calluses.

Right now, the bow he drew was dismissed by his brother as a "toy bow."

If he could draw the kind of heavy warbow their father regularly used, surely his brother would tell him all his troubles, wouldn't he?

Li Shimin had a servant wrap a hot water bladder in fur and tuck it by Li Xuanba's feet before he went to bathe, change, and go to sleep.

The next morning, Li Shimin felt a heat source beside him that was even hotter than himself. His heart jolted, his sleepiness vanishing instantly as he snapped his eyes open and sat up.

"Ah Xuan? Ah Xuan?" Li Shimin shook his brother beside him.

Dazed with sleep, Li Xuanba struggled to open his eyes. "Brother... *cough, cough*."

He covered his mouth, unable to suppress a fit of coughing.

Tears instantly welled up in Li Shimin's eyes, but the moment they appeared, he vigorously rubbed them away. He replaced his tears with a mature expression that was entirely ill-suited to his childish face.

"Don't be afraid, Ah Xuan. Brother is here." As Li Shimin swiftly threw on his clothes, he shouted, "Summon the imperial physician! Send word to the Empress, I must see her! Don't be afraid, Ah Xuan, Brother will get the best imperial physician right away."

"*Cough, cough, cough.*" Li Xuanba clutched his mouth, his small body curling up, his face flushed crimson like a boiled shrimp.

He smiled bitterly in his heart. Just yesterday, he had been worrying about how to avoid the teachers appointed by Yang Guang, and today he had fallen ill.

The "avoidance" he had in mind was certainly not through sickness.

With the medical standards of ancient times, even a minor illness could claim a child's life, let alone with his frail constitution.

He clearly hadn't suffered a major illness in nearly a year, only experiencing minor coughs during seasonal transitions. Even when Second Brother had been driven to illness by the Zheng family's schemes, he had managed to hold out. He hadn't even run a fever despite sleeping poorly on the dragon boat. How could a single bout of worry trigger such a high fever?

Before long, Li Xuanba's mind grew hazy from the fever, preventing him from overthinking any further.

The imperial physician had Li Xuanba's clothes loosened, using warm water to wipe down his body to bring down his temperature, and used silver needles to perform bloodletting on his earlobes and fingertips.

After nearly an hour of frantic effort, the heat in Li Xuanba's body finally subsided slightly, and he regained consciousness.

"Ah Xuan, you're fine now. You'll be well once you drink the medicine." Li Shimin helped Li Xuanba up, letting him lean against him.

Li Xuanba wanted to take the medicine bowl, but his hands were weak and limp. Unable to hold it steady, he nearly spilled it all over himself.

Li Shimin caught the bowl just in time. "Drink slowly. I asked Cousin-Uncle for a lot of your favorite honey-preserved dried peaches. You can eat your fill after you finish the medicine."

The wet nurse said, "Second Young Master, let me feed him."

Li Shimin shook his head. "I'll do it."

The imperial physician was about to warn them that the medicine was very bitter and that Li Xuanba might take a long time to drink it, making it hard for Li Shimin to hold the bowl. But Li Xuanba simply lowered his head, Li Shimin tilted the bottom of the bowl, and Li Xuanba gulped down the entire bowl of medicine in one breath. The two brothers coordinated with seamless tacit understanding, as if they had done this countless times before.

Li Shimin handed the empty bowl back to the wet nurse and fished out a piece of dried peach from a small cloth pouch in his sleeve.

Li Xuanba took two bites of the dried peach but couldn't help dry-heaving.

Li Shimin patted his back, waiting until Li Xuanba had forced down the dried peach despite his nausea before feeding him the warm water held by the wet nurse.

Only after finishing the dried peach and drinking the tasteless warm water did Li Xuanba manage to suppress the urge to vomit.

The imperial physician felt a wave of admiration. He specialized in treating children. Children were physically and mentally fragile, and good medicine was always bitter; feeding them was usually an arduous struggle. A child like the Third Young Master of the Li family was truly rare.

Li Xuanba fell back into a deep sleep after drinking the medicine.

The imperial physician specifically instructed them not to bundle Li Xuanba up to sweat out the fever.

He advised covering him with a thin blanket to let the heat escape and wiping his body with warm water every half hour. Even if Li Xuanba showed signs of chills, they were not to add heavy blankets; instead, they should soak his feet in hot water until his body warmed up.

The imperial physician's instructions had actually been mentioned before by Physician Sun, whom Lady Dou had personally invited from Mount Taibai on the outskirts of Daye to nurse Li Xuanba back to health. Although Li Shimin already knew them by heart, he listened intently once more and took notes.

Physician Sun had once said that every illness could present different circumstances; one must not blindly believe in any single "miracle doctor" but trust the physician conducting the physical diagnosis.

Li Shimin specifically noted down the differences between the imperial physician's instructions and Physician Sun's, lest he misremember.

The imperial physician said, "Second Young Master Li, you should rest as well. I will write down the points of attention later."

Li Shimin replied, "I am not tired. I will sleep when I am tired, please do not worry, Physician. I still have to take care of my brother; I will not let myself fall ill."

"I will prescribe some warming medicinal tea for you as a precaution," the physician said.

Li Shimin set down his brush and paper, cupping his hands. "Thank you, Physician."

After the physician left, Li Shimin instructed the wet nurse to keep hot water ready at all times.

He sat nearby with a book, feeding Li Xuanba warm water whenever his brother woke up.

Empress Xiao visited three times, and Yang Guang also came once.

Li Shimin apologized to the Emperor and Empress on behalf of his brother.

Empress Xiao smiled bitterly. "What is there to apologize for? How could falling ill be your fault?"

Princess Nanyang also came to visit Li Xuanba, bringing along the regards of her husband, Prince Consort Yuwen Shiji.

Upon hearing that his close friend's sons were ill, Yuwen Shiji had been anxious. However, since Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were being raised by the Empress's side, surrounded by the Emperor's concubines, it was inappropriate for him to visit, even as the Prince Consort.

Li Xuanba happened to be awake at the moment. Having just wiped his nose, his voice sounded muffled.

Princess Nanyang took out a box of sheep-fat ointment and showed Li Shimin how to apply it to the chafed, reddened skin around Li Xuanba's nose.

"How did he fall so gravely ill?" Princess Nanyang frowned as she watched the imperial physician perform bloodletting again to lower Li Xuanba's temperature.

When Li Xuanba had briefly woken earlier, he had used his inner voice to instruct his second brother to "bribe" the physician into saying he was merely unaccustomed to the local climate and secretly pining for his parents.

Hearing this, the imperial physician guessed that the second and third young masters of the Li family might be using this illness as a pretext to return to their parents.

Although many envied their upbringing in the palace, compared to the envy of others and a grand future, the two children perhaps simply wanted to return to their mother's side.

Princess Nanyang was somewhat touched upon hearing the physician's words.

She touched Li Xuanba's still-feverish forehead and said softly, "Do you miss your mother?"

Li Xuanba squeezed out a weak smile and said, "Cousin-Uncle and Cousin-Aunt treat me very well, but I still worry about whether Mother misses Brother and me."

Princess Nanyang burst into laughter. "Alright, so it's not that you miss your mother, but that you worry she misses you. Reports from Luoyang say that the Eastern Capital will be completed next month. Imperial Father should be setting off for Luoyang very soon. You will be able to see your mother then."

Lying in bed, Li Xuanba cupped his hands. "Thank you, Princess."

"What is there to thank me for?" Princess Nanyang smiled. "Get well quickly. If your body isn't fit for travel by boat, watch out or you might be left behind in Jiangdu."

Li Xuanba immediately said, "I will get well very quickly!"

Princess Nanyang nodded, then shared some amusing anecdotes about the Emperor's tour of Jiangdu and the grand spectacle of Jiangdu welcoming the imperial arrival.

Li Xuanba put on a look of yearning.

Once Li Xuanba covered his mouth to yawn, Princess Nanyang gave a few instructions to the servants attending to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba before taking her leave.

Li Shimin looked at his brother, who was feigning sleepiness. "Can we really go home soon?"

Li Xuanba: *[The Emperor is a perfectionist who wants his image to be completely untarnished. Seeing how easily I fall ill, his enthusiasm for raising a "Champion Marquis" will cool. If I were to fall sick and die by his side, it would be far too inauspicious.]*

Li Shimin leaned close to Li Xuanba and whispered, "You really didn't do this on purpose?"

Li Xuanba replied helplessly: *[Brother, you of all people know how much I fear death.]*

Li Shimin snorted twice, lowering his head to gently bump his forehead against his brother's. "Don't get sick anymore. Stop scaring your Second Brother."

Li Xuanba: *[Is falling sick something I can decide...]*

Li Shimin snorted in displeasure.

Li Xuanba surrendered: *[Fine, I'll do my best.]* If he didn't agree, his brother, Li Erfeng, would keep snorting until he turned into Li Erzhu.

***

Once Li Xuanba's health improved slightly, Yang Guang, wanting the external ministers to see that the cousin-nephew he kept by his side had recovered, specially permitted them to visit.

Yuwen Shiji was the first to arrive.

He actually held Li Xuanba's hand and wept, saying that if anything happened to Li Xuanba, he wouldn't know how to face Li Yuan.

Both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba listened in utter confusion.

Li Xuanba: *[We fell ill while being raised by the Emperor. What does that have to do with him? What does he have to account for? How strange.]*

Li Shimin nodded silently.

To Li Xuanba's surprise, Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Yu Shinan also came to visit him.

After visiting Li Xuanba, Gao Jiong and Yu Shinan merely lamented their brief, shallow fate as teacher and student. Yet Yuwen Bi actually brought a chest of medicinal herbs and a prescription for treating coughs.

"My grandson has also been frail since childhood, constantly plagued by coughs. Drinking this medicinal tea will make you feel better," Yuwen Bi said with a stiff face. "When a young child falls ill, the physical harm is on themselves, but the pain is in the hearts of their elders. You must take care of your health, otherwise, it is a lack of filial piety."

Any other child would likely have been frightened by Yuwen Bi's cold, harsh expression and tone.

Even Li Shimin felt a surge of anger. *My brother is already suffering so much from his illness, and you dare lecture him on filial piety!*

Li Xuanba: *[Don't be angry, Brother. He is speaking to me, but in his heart, he is thinking of his grandson. He is worrying about his grandson's health.]*

"Yes, I will certainly take care of my health and not cause my elders grief," Li Xuanba thanked him.

Yuwen Bi's expression softened slightly.

He then gave detailed instructions on how to prepare and drink the medicinal tea, explaining each herb used in the prescription to Li Xuanba's wet nurse.

Even though Yuwen Bi had brought the written prescription, he still explained everything meticulously.

According to Yuwen Bi, many of the herbs had to be harvested during specific seasons and times, and even the water used to brew the tea was best gathered from morning dew.

As a transmigrator, Li Xuanba felt that this pharmacology leaned a bit too heavily into mysticism and was largely unnecessary. However, Yuwen Bi believed in it, which meant his own herbs were collected in this exact manner, showing just how rare and precious they were.

Yuwen Bi had not brought his grandson with him on this trip, so these herbs should have been kept at his residence in Luoyang. Had he sent someone to rush them all the way from Luoyang?

Li Xuanba suddenly felt that this gift was far too heavy.

After finishing his instructions, Yuwen Bi told Li Xuanba to continue resting, led Li Shimin to the outer room, pulled out a scroll, and began lecturing him.

Li Shimin: "???"

Though utterly bewildered, Li Shimin still listened attentively to Yuwen Bi's lecture and took careful notes.

Yuwen Bi lectured him for half an hour, left some homework, and departed, saying he would return in two days to check Li Shimin's progress.

With his face scrunched up like a steamed bun, Li Shimin told Li Xuanba about this.

Li Xuanba: "..."

Li Xuanba pinched the bridge of his nose. "I have long heard that Minister Yuwen is extremely pedantic... *cough*, extremely stubborn. He probably believes that since we have already kowtowed to him, we are officially his disciples."

Gao Jiong and Yu Shinan both knew this was merely a whim of Yang Guang's; now that they had missed out due to illness, they simply let it go.

*Why must you be so pedantic, Minister Yuwen! We only kowtowed once!*

Li Shimin's bun-like face smoothed out, and he smiled. "Isn't that great? Minister Yuwen... Teacher Yuwen is a great talent of our age! Mother and Father will surely be thrilled!"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Yes."

Li Shimin asked in confusion, "Why do you look unhappy?"

Li Xuanba hesitated for a moment before saying in his mind: *[From my observations, the Emperor deeply detests Minister Yuwen. If Minister Yuwen continues to remonstrate, I fear it will bring about his execution.]*

Li Shimin laughed softly and lowered his voice. "Ah Xuan, although His Majesty dislikes remonstrance, surely he wouldn't execute someone just for speaking out? Wouldn't that alienate the other ministers? Even if His Majesty dislikes Teacher Yuwen, at most he would demote and exile him."

Li Xuanba: *[What if?]*

Recalling Li Xuanba's "ability," Li Shimin frowned. "If it's true, it shouldn't implicate us. But would His Majesty really do such a thing? Isn't that..."

He suddenly remembered the posthumous title of the current Emperor that Li Xuanba had revealed to him, and promptly shut his mouth.

Li Shimin smiled bitterly. "You didn't fall ill because of this, did you?"

Li Xuanba said, "No. Didn't the physician say so? I had accumulated exhaustion during the journey, and once my body relaxed, it all burst out at once. Don't overthink it either. I am only guessing; I cannot see things in such specific detail yet."

Li Shimin nodded. "Alright."

Li Xuanba emphasized, "I really am just guessing. Don't overthink it."

Li Shimin said with a silly grin, "I know."

Looking at his second brother's simple-minded expression, Li Xuanba was half-convinced, half-doubtful.

He must make sure not to let anything slip in the future.

Li Shimin seemed to truly believe him and dropped the subject.

Seeing that Li Xuanba still had some energy, he picked up his book and explained the day's lesson to him. In explaining it to Li Xuanba, Li Shimin's own understanding of the text deepened.

Listening to his second brother's explanation, Li Xuanba felt an itch in his heart.

Books in this era were not only scarce in variety and quantity, but their words were also extremely sparse. Although Li Xuanba possessed the reading comprehension of a modern adult and could force his way through texts lacking punctuation, the experience of having a great scholar explain a text was entirely different from figuring it out on one's own.

A book annotated by past sages was worth a thousand pieces of gold. Why were children of noble families so much more erudite than those of humble origins, despite reading the same Four Books and Five Classics? It was precisely because they possessed more "annotated editions." In particular, annotations by ancestral sages of a clan were treasured heirlooms, completely inaccessible to outsiders.

Because Yuwen Bi was executed, his works did not survive to posterity. However, the *Book of Sui* recorded that Yuwen Bi's rhapsodies alone exceeded two hundred thousand words, and his *Annotations on the Book of Documents* and *Annotations on the Classic of Filial Piety* were the most acclaimed and widely circulated editions of his time.

In modern terms, Yuwen Bi would be the chief editor of textbooks for top-tier universities, a leading authority in his field.

Li Xuanba's sole obsession in his past life had been reading, and now his heart was truly itching with desire.

Knowing his brother's passion, Li Shimin invited him, "If you have the energy, Ah Xuan, attend the lessons with me! Whether Teacher Yuwen teaches one or two, it's all the same to him."

Li Xuanba thought about it and nodded.

Since Yuwen Bi had already come to teach, a connection had been forged regardless of whether he attended.

Although Yang Guang deeply feared and detested Yuwen Bi, Yuwen Bi's power and status were, after all, not as high as Gao Jiong's. After Yang Guang executed Yuwen Bi's entire family, it likely wouldn't spill over to affect others.

When Yuwen Bi returned, Li Shimin requested that he lecture his brother as well.

Li Xuanba said, "I can sit up steadily now. I can listen to the lesson."

"Focus on recovering from your illness. Studying is not a matter of a single moment; do not be impatient," Yuwen Bi refused, scolding him. "You said before that you would take care of your health and not be unfilial. How have you forgotten so quickly?"

Yuwen Bi's anger startled Li Xuanba.

Immediately after, however, he detected a complex mix of heartache, frustration, and appreciation on Yuwen Bi's face.

He understood at once: Yuwen Bi's frail grandson was likely also an avid lover of books.

Li Shimin pleaded, "Even if Teacher does not lecture Ah Xuan, he won't be able to stay idle. He will insist on reading by himself, which will drain even more of his energy. It would be better if Teacher sets a daily reading limit for him. He won't dare disobey his teacher's orders, so he will finally exercise some restraint."

Yuwen Bi sighed and muttered, "He really is just like An'er. Very well, lie down properly. I will lecture you by your bedside."

Yuwen Bi forbade Li Xuanba from sitting up. Instead, he sat by the bed, scroll in hand, and began his lecture.

After Yuwen Bi assigned more homework and left, Li Shimin said to Li Xuanba in surprise, "Ah Xuan, you guessed right again! Teacher Yuwen wasn't actually angry with you; he was worried for you!"

Li Xuanba said, "The 'An'er' he mentioned is probably his frail grandson."

Li Shimin smiled. "He is so good to you, bringing you medicine from thousands of miles away in Luoyang. He must see his grandson's shadow in you. He really is a good man!"

Li Xuanba murmured, "Yes."

He had not expected Yuwen Bi to treat him so well, which made his conscience prickle with unease.

But what could he do? He could do nothing.

Yuwen Bi continued to come and lecture every other day, right up until Yang Guang announced their return to Luoyang.

At this time, the new city of Luoyang was still referred to as the "Eastern Capital." The Eastern Capital was completed in the first lunar month, and Yang Guang was overjoyed, urgently wishing to return to Luoyang immediately to take up residence there.

Yang Guang declared that they must return to Luoyang before the third lunar month, when the warblers fly and the grass grows, so they could witness the most beautiful spring scenery of the Eastern Capital.

Their journey here had taken nearly three months. Although the dragon boats had stopped frequently along the way to receive the worship and food offerings of local officials and commoners, wasting much time, returning such a massive fleet of dragon boats to Luoyang within two months was far too rushed.

To ensure the Emperor's dragon boats returned to the Eastern Capital in time to enjoy the spring scenery, Yang Guang conscripted a vast number of additional laborers in Jiangdu alongside the original ones, forcing them to pull the towlines day and night to accelerate the fleet.

Historical records state that Emperor Yang of Sui went down to Jiangdu on the fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month and returned to the Eastern Capital of Luoyang in the second lunar month of the following year.

Although Li Xuanba had not fully recovered, he was only coughing and no longer had a fever, so he was fit to accompany the dragon boats back to Luoyang.

Though the dragon boats no longer docked along the banks for long periods, the singing and dancing on the leading two tower ships never ceased.

Fearing the noise would disturb Li Xuanba, and considering that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were currently receiving instruction from Yuwen Bi, Empress Xiao—at the request of Princess Nanyang—persuaded Yang Guang to let the two brothers stay with Princess Nanyang.

Yuwen Shiji was delighted, wanting to take Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to visit others every day.

Seeing this, Yuwen Bi gave Yuwen Shiji a harsh scolding.

Although both shared the surname Yuwen, Yuwen Shiji and Yuwen Bi did not belong to the same clan.

Yuwen Shiji's ancestors were originally surnamed Poyetou, servants to Yuwen Sidougui, the chieftain of the Yuwen tribe, who had bestowed the surname Yuwen upon them. Yuwen Bi's ancestors, on the other hand, belonged to a non-ruling branch of the Yuwen clan.

However, Yuwen Bi was upright and unyielding, feared by all officials. Although Yuwen Shiji's family was the foremost favorite in front of Yang Guang, when Yuwen Bi scolded him, he could only listen meekly. Afterward, he would complain to Princess Nanyang with a smile, saying, "Minister Yuwen is indeed terrifying," which amused the Princess greatly, teasing him that he "deserved to be scolded."

Yuwen Shiji truly had Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's best interests at heart. Although both brothers found these social visits rather annoying, they could not easily refuse him since he was their elder.

With Yuwen Bi shielding them, they were finally able to stay in their rooms to read and practice calligraphy, occasionally going up to the deck to enjoy the scenery.

Yuwen Bi still came to instruct them every other day.

Gao Jiong originally had no interest in teaching young children. When Li Xuanba fell ill, he had used it as a convenient excuse to back out.

However, seeing Yuwen Bi teaching the two children so enthusiastically, he began to sense something.

It must be that both children were exceptionally brilliant, making Yuwen Bi delight in their talent!

*How detestable! Minister Yuwen actually kept this from me! He wants to monopolize these two outstanding disciples!*

Gao Jiong was also a world-renowned great scholar. As a great scholar, he naturally shared the passion for teaching outstanding disciples.

Gao Jiong was a proud man. The reputation of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba as "child prodigies" had not caught his eye.

In the Sui Dynasty, official appointments were still primarily based on recommendation, and even the imperial examinations required a recommendation from an official of the fifth rank or higher to participate—essentially a variation of the Han dynasty's recommendation system. Consequently, many literati families manufactured "child prodigy" reputations for their children from a young age. Having seen too much of this, Gao Jiong found nothing extraordinary about it.

Yet Yuwen Bi was even more selective about his disciples than Gao Jiong. Since he had the patience to continuously instruct these two children, their reputation as "child prodigies" was likely no falsehood.

Gao Jiong found Yu Shinan and complained, "He previously claimed he only visited more often because looking at Li the Third reminded him of his own grandson. He was tricking us!"

With a bitter smile, Yu Shinan was dragged along by Gao Jiong to "reason" with Yuwen Bi.

Naturally, Yuwen Bi would not admit to monopolizing the disciples.

*What do you mean, monopolize? Didn't you decline His Majesty yourself?*

The two old men fell into an argument, while Yu Shinan, who held the lowest status and was the youngest, shrank to the side, not daring to utter a word.

Word of this eventually reached Yang Guang's ears.

Yang Guang went to find Li Shimin and Li Xuanba with a smile. "You two are truly talented. Even the haughty Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi are fighting over you."

Li Shimin grinned proudly. "Of course!"

After a brief thought, Li Xuanba said, "Cousin-Uncle recognized my brother's and my talent early on and wished for Duke Gao and Duke Yuwen to instruct us. Originally, Duke Gao and Duke Yuwen had seen too many 'child prodigies' and did not believe in us. Now that they have finally acknowledged us, it only proves that Cousin-Uncle's foresight is superior."

Li Shimin was slightly taken aback, then immediately chimed in, "Exactly! Cousin-Uncle is indeed amazing! A discerning eye for talent! Ah Xuan and I are indeed talents, hehe!"

Yang Guang's smile became more genuine. He rubbed the heads of the two children and said proudly, "As the Son of Heaven, I naturally possess greater discernment than they do."

Yang Guang tested Li Shimin and Li Xuanba on their schoolwork. Delighted by their performance, he bestowed numerous rewards upon them.

He then summoned Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi to boast about his own keen eye for talent.

This time, Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi complimented Yang Guang in a way that perfectly suited his vanity.

As for Yu Shinan, he was merely the accompanying calligraphy tutor and continued to play the role of an invisible bystander.

However, when Gao Jiong joined Yuwen Bi in instructing Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, he dragged Yu Shinan along as well.

The high ministers accompanying Yang Guang on his southern tour were all aboard the same tower ship. The news of Gao Jiong actively requesting the Emperor's permission to instruct the second and third young masters of the Duke of Tang's household quickly spread to the ears of all the ministers.

Furthermore, there was Yuwen Shiji, who was so smug it was as if Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were his own sons. He boasted to everyone he met, forcing them to listen whether they wanted to or not.

Thus, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba once again became famous.

Li Xuanba could only smile bitterly at this.

Even after falling gravely ill, he still hadn't managed to escape.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第21章 一脉相承厚脸皮
chunks.chineseText:
第21章 一脉相承厚脸皮

=
　　李世民和李玄霸终于回到了洛阳。
　　李世民背着小短手站在船头， 望着即将抵达的洛阳城，语气沧桑道：“我们才离开洛阳四个月，好像已经过了四十年。”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　宇文士及和南阳公主夫妻二人肩并肩研墨作画， 就像是后世给可爱小朋友拍照的父母。
　　杨广提前得知李渊已经到了洛阳， 请求面圣。
　　已经失去了养育孩童耐心的杨广， 特意过来把李世民和李玄霸提溜走，完好无损地交到李渊手中。
　　他和萧皇后联袂而来时，就看见李世民和李玄霸被迫在船头背着手装深沉， 南阳公主和宇文士及为其作画的模样。
　　见杨广来了，李世民和李玄霸表情都在放光。
　　李玄霸：【我是第一次如此期待陛下的到来！】
　　李世民：“……”阿玄在心声中真是难得叫一次“陛下”啊。
　　“阿玄身体还未痊愈，你们怎么能让阿玄站在船头吹风？”萧皇后把两个孩子护在怀中， 笑着骂了女儿和女婿一句。
　　杨广看了女儿和女婿的画，笑道：“把李三郎画得过胖了。”
　　李世民拉着李玄霸跑去看把他们画成了什么模样。
　　李玄霸没反应过来， 被拉得一个踉跄， 几乎是被李世民拖着走。
　　“啊，真的好胖！”李世民道，“阿玄，你要努力长这么胖！”
　　李玄霸差点被二哥拉得撞桌角上。
　　他使劲甩手，把二哥甩开， 低头看向画中圆得像个馒头的红肚兜小孩。
　　画中人无论是从相貌还是从衣着，都完全不像我和二哥吧？那我和二哥站在那里当那么久的模特有什么用？！
　　他幽怨地看了宇文士及和南阳公主一眼。
　　年轻小两口都捂嘴笑。
　　萧皇后伸出手指， 点了一下南阳公主的额头：“就顽皮！”
　　杨广对宇文士及道：“朕每次对你委以重任，让你去当刺史，你总不想出远门， 每日就和南阳论诗作画， 真没出息！”

　　李渊得意道：“我家世民的文才，荥阳郑氏同辈子弟与世民和玄霸比试，全军覆没，全军覆没懂吗？”
　　杨广擦着笑出来的眼泪补充：“还有，宇文弼和高颎两个眼高于顶的老匹夫，争着收世民和玄霸当弟子。朕这两位表侄，确实非常聪慧。”
　　听到宇文弼和高颎两个名字，长孙晟终于出现了惊讶的神色。
　　能被宇文弼和高颎看中的孩童，长孙晟有些心动了。
　　他看向收起玩具弓，仍旧一副傻乎乎表情的李世民，又看向一旁的李玄霸。
　　李玄霸立刻咳嗽了一声，装作一副弱不禁风的模样。
　　李世民弱智的表情立刻变得睿智。
　　他皱眉地跑到宦官身旁，把玩具弓递给宦官，自己拿了一杯蜜水跑到李玄霸身边：“润一润嗓子，是吹了风着凉了吗？怎么又咳了？”
　　李玄霸赶紧道：“只是不小心被口水呛着了，没事。”
　　李世民道：“先喝水。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“好。”
　　他喝完水，李世民见弟弟没再咳嗽，才放下心来。
　　李世民把自己的小毛皮披风解下来，在李玄霸同款小毛皮披风上又罩了一层：“哥哥现在有些热，你先穿着。”
　　说完，他指着自己的额头：“你看，我额头都有汗珠了，真的热。”
　　三个大人看着兄弟二人的互动，脸上都不由浮现出慈祥的表情。
　　杨广擦了擦笑出来的眼泪，道：“长孙将军，朕看这个亲事可行。”
　　长孙晟叹气道：“陛下都说媒了，臣还能说什么？只是家女体弱……”
　　李渊道：“先口头定下，待令女十岁时再交换庚帖如何？”
　　长孙晟道：“唐国公如此看得起我，那我就厚颜认下这个亲家了。”
　　他向杨广行礼道谢：“谢陛下说媒。将来这事若能成，臣斗胆请陛下来喝杯喜酒。”
　　李玄霸见李渊愣着，无奈拉着二哥道：“谢陛下做媒。”
　　李世民又露出傻乎乎的神情：“谢陛下。”究竟在干什么啊，我好迷糊。
　　在场有三个人都行礼了，李渊再憨也立刻行礼道：“谢陛下。这次多亏陛下，臣终于输得不亏了！下次陛下能否再找些厉害的人和臣比射箭？臣还有三个儿子。”
　　杨广一愣，笑骂道：“以后朕不会再让其他人与你比射箭了！赢了你输了女儿，谁会愿意和你比射箭？滚远些！”
　　李渊嘿嘿傻笑。
　　杨广和长孙晟都单手遮住眼睛，一副没眼看的模样。
　　李玄霸也想捂眼睛。
　　这表情，这表情啊，二哥和父亲确实是亲父子。
　　李渊对李世民挤眉弄眼：看，耶耶给你“输”来了一个小妻子，开不开心？
　　李世民歪头，不懂父亲奇怪的表情是什么意思。
