Chapter 21: A Shared Lineage of Thick Skins

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba finally returned to Luoyang.

Standing at the bow of the ship with his short arms clasped behind his back, Li Shimin gazed at the approaching city of Luoyang. In a voice heavy with simulated age, he sighed, "We only left Luoyang four months ago, yet it feels as though forty years have passed."

Li Xuanba nodded in agreement.

Nearby, Yuwen Shiji and Princess Nanyang stood shoulder to shoulder, grinding ink and painting. They looked just like parents from a future era taking snapshots of their adorable children.

Yang Guang had received word in advance that Li Yuan had arrived in Luoyang and requested an imperial audience.

Having long since lost his patience for raising children, Yang Guang had personally come to scoop up Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, intending to return them to Li Yuan in one piece.

When he and Empress Xiao arrived hand in hand, they were greeted by the sight of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba forced to stand at the bow with their hands behind their backs, trying to look profound, while Princess Nanyang and Yuwen Shiji painted them.

At the sight of Yang Guang, both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's faces lit up.

Li Xuanba: *[This is the first time I have ever looked forward to His Majesty's arrival so eagerly!]*

Li Shimin: "..." It was truly a rare occasion for Ah Xuan to refer to him as "His Majesty" in his inner thoughts.

"Ah Xuan hasn't fully recovered yet. How could you let him stand at the bow in the cold wind?" Empress Xiao pulled the two children into her embrace, chiding her daughter and son-in-law with a warm smile.

Yang Guang glanced at his daughter and son-in-law's painting and laughed. "You have painted Li Sanlang far too plump."

Li Shimin dragged Li Xuanba over to see what they looked like in the painting.

Caught off guard, Li Xuanba stumbled and was practically dragged along by Li Shimin.

"Ah, they really did make us look so fat!" Li Shimin exclaimed. "Ah Xuan, you must work hard to grow this plump!"

Li Xuanba was nearly pulled headfirst into the corner of the table by his second brother.

Wrenching his hand free, he shook off his brother and looked down at the painting, which depicted a child in a red bellyband who was as round as a steamed bun.

*Neither the appearance nor the clothing of the person in this painting looks anything like Second Brother or me! What was the point of us standing there posing as models for so long?!*

He shot a resentful look at Yuwen Shiji and Princess Nanyang.

The young couple both covered their mouths and giggled.

Empress Xiao reached out and tapped Princess Nanyang's forehead. "Always so mischievous!"

Yang Guang turned to Yuwen Shiji and said, "Every time I entrust you with a heavy responsibility and appoint you as a regional inspector, you refuse to travel far. Instead, you spend every day discussing poetry and painting with Nanyang. How utterly spineless!"

Yuwen Shiji smiled and replied, "Your Majesty, your son-in-law only wishes to grow old together with the Princess. I am indeed that spineless."

Yang Guang did not know whether to laugh or cry. "Fine, fine, have it your way."

Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba: *[Surprising, isn't it? Even an emperor can sometimes interact with his ministers as if they were ordinary commoners.]*

Li Shimin blinked instead of nodding.

Previously, the Emperor had always shown a volatile, suspicious, and paranoid side, even employing "imperial mind games" to test young children like Li Shimin and Li Xuanba from time to time.

Who would have thought that someone could joke with the Emperor like this, and the Emperor wouldn't even get angry?

Yang Guang exchanged a few more jests with Yuwen Shiji. The harmonious atmosphere between them made them look like a biological father and son.

Li Xuanba averted his gaze.

Yang Guang was notoriously harsh on his own biological sons, his suspicion bordering on a persecution complex. Yet, he was exceptionally warm and devoted to Yuwen Shu's family.

Yuwen Shu was Yuwen Shiji's father. His eldest son, Yuwen Huaji, and second son, Yuwen Zhiji, would be the very ones to assassinate Yang Guang at the Jiangdu Palace.

Although Yuwen Shiji had no prior knowledge of the plot, he and Princess Nanyang would never be able to return to how they once were.

Who could imagine now that, more than a decade later, the carefree and untethered Yuwen Shiji would become a Chancellor of the Great Tang renowned for his extreme caution? Or that Princess Nanyang, whose life was currently the epitome of refinement, would allow Dou Jiande to execute her own son before shaving her head to become a Buddhist nun, willingly embracing a life of poverty?

"Ah Xuan, what are you worrying about now?"

"I have no worries."

He simply knew that some sweets left a bitter aftertaste, so even their initial sweetness no longer tasted sweet to him.

...

When Li Yuan arrived for his imperial audience, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were on the training grounds practicing archery with Yang Guang.

Yang Guang hit the bullseye with every shot, and Li Shimin's arrows at least managed to land on the target. Li Xuanba, however, was a different story—no one dared to stand anywhere near his target.

Just as Li Yuan walked in, Li Xuanba's arrow struck the dirt.

Li Shimin clutched his head and shook it violently, looking utterly exasperated. "Ah Xuan, why on earth are you shooting your arrows into the ground?!"

Li Xuanba defended himself. "I wasn't aiming at the ground! I was aiming properly at the target!"

Yang Guang's laughter boomed like a great bell.

Seeing Li Yuan arrive, Yang Guang teased, "Aren't you a master archer? Why haven't you properly instructed Li Sanlang?"

Li Yuan immediately replied, "I taught Shimin how to use a bow, but Xuanba's archery has nothing to do with me!"

Yang Guang laughed even harder.

He tossed a bow and arrow to Li Yuan and said, "Cousin, let me see your skill."

Li Yuan glanced at the target and casually loosed three arrows in rapid succession. All three struck the exact center of the bullseye, as if the target itself had magnetically drawn them in.

Li Shimin hopped up and down, brandishing his toy bow. "Father is amazing!"

Li Xuanba slung his small bow over his shoulder and clapped his hands rhythmically for Li Yuan.

To be fair, if the young Li Yuan were to compete in archery against the future General of Heavenly Policy, Li Shimin, he wouldn't necessarily lose.

The current Li Yuan and Li Shimin could indeed be called a heroic father and son.

Seeing both of his sons cheering for him, a proud smile spread across Li Yuan's face. "Your Majesty, when it comes to archery, this minister will not lose to anyone."

Loving the house and its crows—since Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had pleased Yang Guang, the Emperor's wariness toward Li Yuan had dissipated significantly. Moreover, Yang Guang had achieved military glory in his youth, so he would not envy someone who had yet to prove himself on the battlefield.

Yang Guang smiled. "Is that so? Then how do you compare to General of the Martial Guards, Changsun Sheng?"

Li Yuan said proudly, "This minister has not yet competed against him. However, the General of the Martial Guards is old; I will not compete with him."

"Bah, I think you simply know you cannot beat him and are making excuses," Yang Guang teased. "Guards, summon the General of the Martial Guards!"

Li Yuan cleared his throat, looking slightly embarrassed. "General Changsun is also in Luoyang?"

Yang Guang replied, "I am here, so how could General Changsun not travel with me?"

Li Yuan said with a hint of resentment, "This minister also wished to go to Jiangdu."

Yang Guang said, "I took your two sons with me, so I won't take you. Did your Duke of Tang's residence expect the entire family to go on a pleasure trip to Jiangdu?"

Li Yuan argued, "Why not? This minister's family members are all Your Majesty's relatives..."

Before Li Yuan could finish, Li Xuanba quickly cut in. "Your Majesty can just treat our family as poor relatives coming to seek shelter. Your Majesty possesses the four seas; surely you wouldn't mind adding a few more sets of bowls and chopsticks."

Li Yuan: "..."

Yang Guang had slightly frowned at Li Yuan's insolence, but upon hearing Li Xuanba's words, he couldn't help but laugh. "The Duke of Tang's residence can be called 'poor relatives'?"

Li Yuan said, "Of course not—"

Li Xuanba interrupted again. "Compared to His Majesty, who isn't a poor relative? Right, Second Brother?"

Li Shimin nodded. "Of course! Right, Father?"

Li Yuan: "...Though that is indeed true."

Yang Guang laughed so hard he nearly choked.

Previously, he had felt that Li Yuan was disrespectful, relying on the fact that they were cousins. Now, seeing his two young nephews finish each other's sentences to cut off their father, he began to feel that Li Yuan wasn't being disrespectful, but was simply a bit simple-minded and blunt.

"Fine, I will bring your whole family along next time," Yang Guang chuckled. "I must still look after the poor relatives of my family."

Li Yuan shot his two impudent, interrupting sons a look that clearly said *I'll deal with you two later*, before saying, "Actually, let's not. We cannot have people mocking the Duke of Tang's residence for seeking handouts."

Li Xuanba said, "Father, to be able to seek handouts from His Majesty is our honor."

Li Shimin chimed in, "Exactly, exactly."

Unable to take it anymore, Li Yuan balled his hand into a fist and gave Li Shimin a hard rap on the head.

Li Xuanba bolted instantly, hiding behind Yang Guang and poking his head out. "Cousin, save me! Father is acting out of shame and anger!"

Yang Guang laughed. "Very well, I shall protect you. Li Yuan, hear my decree: you are forbidden from beating Erlang and Sanlang!"

Li Yuan was speechless. "Must this minister accept such a decree?"

Yang Guang feigned anger. "What? Do you wish to defy an imperial decree?"

Li Xuanba urged, "Cousin, Cousin! Father is defying your decree! Rap him on the head to avenge Second Brother!"

Li Xuanba: *[Hurry up and shout along with me.]*

Li Shimin hesitated. *This isn't very good, is it? It feels a bit unfilial.*

Li Xuanba: *[Hurry!]*

Li Shimin squeezed his eyes shut, stiffened his neck, and yelled, "That's right! Cousin, hurry up and rap Father on the head!"

Yang Guang commanded, "Li Yuan, accept the decree at once!"

Li Yuan's face turned livid with rage at his two sons, but with the Emperor pressing him, he had no choice but to kneel and accept the oral decree.

To his immense frustration, Yang Guang actually did rap him twice on the head.

"Erlang, your cousin has avenged you," Yang Guang laughed.

Li Shimin bowed with clasped hands. "Thank you, Cousin. Thank you, Your Majesty."

Li Xuanba ran out from behind Yang Guang and also bowed. "Thank you, Your Majesty!"

Seeing this, Li Yuan was exasperated into a laugh by his two mischievous sons.

"Rise. How long do you intend to remain kneeling?" Yang Guang pulled Li Yuan up.

The way the two of them interacted now was reminiscent of their days in the palace of Emperor Wen of Sui, and the atmosphere had improved considerably.

Li Yuan complained, "Your Majesty, if you spoil them too much, what will we do if they turn out rotten?"

Yang Guang replied righteously, "If a son is untaught, it is the father's fault. That would simply mean you, Li Yuan, failed to raise your children well."

Li Yuan let out a long sigh and glared at Li Shimin and Li Xuanba once more.

The two children had been exceptionally well-behaved when they were in Xingyang. How had spending four months with the Emperor turned them into such rascals?

"Your Majesty, General Changsun has arrived," a eunuch whispered.

Yang Guang smiled. "Send General Changsun in at once. Guards, replace the targets. Li Yuan, no running away!"

Li Yuan said confidently, "I won't run. When it comes to archery, I will not lose."

"What bold words! Let me test your mettle," Changsun Sheng's voice rang out before he even came into view. "This minister pays respects to Your Majesty!"

"Please rise, General Changsun. Come quickly and teach my overly proud cousin a lesson." Yang Guang helped Changsun Sheng up.

When Emperor Wen of Sui passed away, Yang Guang had ordered Changsun Sheng to take control of the palace guards and keep the death a secret. Only after Yang Guang had secured control of the imperial court and ensured a smooth succession was the mourning announced. Thus, Changsun Sheng had played a key role in Yang Guang's ascension and was one of his most trusted confidants.

Changsun Sheng was fifty-three years old this year. Because he had spent many years in the north guarding against the Tujue, his face looked far more weathered than those of the pampered court officials of his age. However, the muscles in his shoulders and arms were incredibly robust, and his hands were like eagle talons—clearly the mark of a formidable warrior.

Li Xuanba pulled Li Shimin along to bow to Changsun Sheng, taking the opportunity to educate his brother on Changsun Sheng's legendary achievements through his inner voice.

The early Tang Dynasty, much like the early Han Dynasty, was a period of history that was highly famous yet paradoxically existed in a "historical blind spot." Most people in future generations could talk about it broadly, but very few understood the finer details of its early history.

For instance, Changsun Sheng's name was not particularly well-known in the future; many did not even realize he was the father of Empress Changsun.

Yet, anyone who had completed nine years of compulsory education would certainly know the idiom "shooting two eagles with one arrow." The historical figure behind this idiom was none other than Changsun Sheng.

Looking across the entirety of Chinese history, his abilities ranked him among the very greatest diplomats.

During the Northern and Southern Dynasties, the Tujue were incredibly powerful. Almost all the Northern Dynasties required their backing to establish themselves. The Tujue viewed the Central Plains dynasties as puppet states they had propped up, often referring to themselves as the "father."

To maximize their own interests, the Tujue constantly aided weaker factions and suppressed stronger ones to keep the Central Plains divided.

Emperor Wen of Sui took an extremely hardline stance against the Tujue, intending to drive their influence out of the Central Plains. However, when the Sui Dynasty was first established, its military strength was not yet sufficient to wage all-out war against them. Furthermore, the south had not yet been unified, and there was great concern that the Tujue would seize the opportunity to cause trouble.

It was at this critical juncture that Changsun Sheng stepped up to shoulder the burden.

Emperor Wen granted Changsun Sheng full authority over matters concerning the Tujue. Traveling among the various Tujue tribes year after year, Changsun Sheng executed the strategy of "befriending the distant and attacking the near, dividing the strong and uniting the weak."

Utilizing his superb diplomatic maneuvers, he successfully split the Tujue into the Eastern and Western Tujue, eliminating Emperor Wen's worries of a northern invasion while he sent his armies south to conquer the Chen Dynasty.

He then pitted one faction against another, supporting Qimin Khagan while destroying Buga Khagan. Without engaging in any large-scale military campaigns, he reduced the Tujue to a scattered mess. By the year Yang Guang ascended the throne, the threat of the northern Tujue was essentially resolved, ensuring a decade of peace on the borders. It was this very peace that gave Yang Guang the capital to squander and run wild.

Li Xuanba: *[When the Sui Dynasty was founded, the Tujue could still call themselves the "father" of the Central Plains dynasties. Then, General Changsun Sheng spent twenty-three years playing them until they were half-crippled. If General Changsun Sheng had lived during the Spring and Autumn or Warring States periods, he could have easily gone toe-to-toe with Zhang Yi and Su Qin. Whether in terms of capability, perseverance, or loyalty, General Changsun Sheng deserves to be remembered by the world.]*

Unfortunately, he was not remembered by the world.

Li Xuanba believed that what these figures of the early Tang lacked was simply a masterpiece like the *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*. The *Romance of the Sui and Tang Dynasties* of later eras was simply too lacking. He wondered if he might be able to fill this gap himself.

In any case, he was bound to become a playboy prince of leisure in the future, which would be the perfect occupation for writing novels.

After listening to Li Xuanba's introduction, Li Shimin's large eyes completely transformed into shining stars.

*So incredible!*

Having spent years traveling among the Tujue, Changsun Sheng possessed incredibly sharp senses. He immediately detected Li Shimin's gaze, and his eagle-like eyes swept toward the boy.

Li Shimin: *Starry-eyed stare!*

Changsun Sheng: "..." Who is this child?

Li Xuanba: *[Hurry up and introduce yourself!]*

Li Shimin immediately puffed out his chest and bowed. "Greetings, General Changsun! My name is Li Shimin. I have long heard of your legendary feat of shooting two eagles with a single arrow, and your renown for traveling alone among the Tujue for twenty-three years to eliminate their threat to the Great Sui! Meeting you today, I truly cannot contain my excitement and admiration. Please forgive my forwardness, General!"

"It wasn't exactly traveling alone..." Changsun Sheng's expression softened slightly as he carefully sized up Li Shimin. "Are you one of the prodigy twins from the Duke of Tang's residence?"

Li Shimin immediately pulled Li Xuanba, who had shrunk back to lower his presence, to his side. "Only when my brother and I are together are we called the prodigy twins."

Changsun Sheng was amused and let out a laugh. "Indeed."

Li Yuan felt a twinge of jealousy. "Shimin, you said before that the person you admired most was your father."

Li Shimin looked up, feigning surprise. "Father has also been to the Tujue lands? Father is so amazing!"

Li Xuanba: "..." *Brother, you are truly something. Are you sure you aren't being sarcastic?*

Yang Guang laughed until his stomach ached. He was starting to feel reluctant to let these two amusing treasures leave the palace.

Li Yuan was left speechless by his son. His face flushed red as he blurted out, "I will go! I will go right now! Your Majesty, dispatch this minister to the Tujue lands at once!"

Yang Guang: "Hahahahaha!"

Changsun Sheng also could not help but chuckle, unable to stop his laughter.

Li Shimin looked at his red-faced father, then at the laughing Emperor and General Changsun. He silently hid his body, which was a size larger than Li Xuanba's, behind his younger brother.

Placing both hands on Li Xuanba's shoulders, he ducked his head and hunched his shoulders to conceal himself.

*Father can't see me, Father can't see me.*

Li Xuanba was speechless. He was grateful to his second brother for drawing their father's ire; perhaps when they left the palace later, their father would only beat Second Brother.

Overwhelmed with embarrassment and anger, Li Yuan dragged Changsun Sheng over, insisting on competing with him to see who could shoot two eagles with one arrow.

Yang Guang, never one to pass up a spectacle, was more than willing to provide his beloved hunting eagles for the trial.

Li Xuanba offered a silent prayer. *Poor eagles.*

Li Yuan forbade anyone from speaking of the outcome, but Yang Guang laughed uproariously.

Li Xuanba: *[Clearly, Father's archery practice these days is mostly limited to targets and docile prey. He is still no match for General Changsun, who spent his life among the Tujue.]*

Li Shimin shot his brother a glance. *Didn't Father say not to speak of it? Does saying it in your head not count?*

"No, you can't just win like that!" The young Li Yuan was a cheerful and free-spirited man.

Having lost, he did not get angry. Instead, he grabbed Changsun Sheng's shoulders and refused to let go, acting completely shameless.

Yang Guang laughed and scolded him, "Cousin, are you a sore loser?"

Li Yuan declared, "I am indeed a sore loser! I must win something back, or else my heart won't be at ease."

Changsun Sheng did not know whether to laugh or cry. "Then what does the Duke of Tang wish to win?"

Li Yuan looked down at his two sons.

Li Xuanba immediately gave his second brother a shove.

Li Shimin stumbled forward a few steps and turned back in confusion. "Ah Xuan, why did you push me?"

Li Yuan smiled and said, "General Changsun, what do you think of my Li Shimin?"

Although he did not know why his father was bringing him up, Li Shimin still puffed out his little chest.

*I am super amazing!*

Changsun Sheng said thoughtfully, "A child who can be kept by His Majesty's side is naturally exceptional."

Li Yuan said, "I heard that a few years ago, you were blessed with a young daughter who happens to be of a similar age to my Shimin."

Li Yuan was not doing this on a whim.

Upon learning that Empress Xiao wished to play matchmaker for the two boys, Lady Dou and Li Yuan had been anxiously searching for suitable daughters-in-law.

However, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were still too young, only six years old. Girls of a suitable age were so young that they were rarely brought out by their parents to visit others, making it impossible to know their character.

Li Yuan and Lady Dou could only screen families based on their background first, looking for suitable households with daughters of the right age.

Changsun Sheng happened to have a three-year-old daughter born to his second wife. Previously, Li Yuan had only considered the Changsun family's daughter as one of many options. But after meeting Changsun Sheng today, he set his heart on this family.

With such an incredible father, the daughter of the Changsun family would surely not be lacking.

Since Li Shimin respected Changsun Sheng so much, he would surely treat his daughter well. The young couple would undoubtedly live in harmony.

Thus, Li Yuan seized this opportunity to act shamelessly and pester him.

Changsun Sheng was stunned for a moment before bursting out in a scold, "My Guanyinbi is only three years old! Li Yuan, have you no shame?!"

Li Yuan said thick-skinnedly, "My Shimin is only six; isn't that a perfect match? Your Majesty, Your Majesty, don't just stand there watching! Please help this minister. My son is also Your Majesty's junior. How can we let the daughter of someone as incredible as General Changsun go to some other family!"

Yang Guang said slowly, "That works out perfectly, then. My eldest imperial grandson happens to be three years old as well."

Li Xuanba: "!!!" *Holy crap! No! Emperor Yang of Sui, shut your mouth!*

Li Xuanba: *[Brother! Your wife is about to run away! Hurry up and grab your father-in-law's leg!]*

He shoved and shoved, pushing with all his might!

"Huh?!" Pushed right next to Changsun Sheng by Li Xuanba, Li Shimin scratched his head in confusion. "What wife? Ah, whatever!"

He lunged and hugged!

Changsun Sheng looked down at the silly boy hugging his waist.

Li Shimin looked up at Changsun Sheng with a foolish grin.

Yang Guang covered his eyes. "Hahahahaha! I can't take it, I'm laughing so hard I can't breathe, hahahaha! Li Yuan, Li Erlang has been corrupted, and it's all your doing! You father and son are truly shameless! Hahaha! Fine, fine, I won't compete with you. General Changsun, just agree to it."

Changsun Sheng looked on the verge of a breakdown. "Your Majesty! My Guanyinbi is only three years old! Three!"

Li Yuan smiled. "My Shimin is really not bad at all. Look at how handsome he is."

Li Xuanba: *[Stand up straight.]*

Li Shimin foolishly let go and stood up straight.

Li Yuan said, "He is already skilled in archery. In the future, he will surely earn an imperial title of nobility for his wife."

Li Xuanba: *[Draw your bow.]*

Li Shimin took his toy bow from the eunuch and struck a pose as if drawing the bow to shoot.

"Pfft!" Yang Guang, who had just managed to stop laughing, burst out once more.

Li Yuan boasted proudly, "As for my Shimin's literary talent, when the peers of the Zheng clan of Xingyang competed against Shimin and Xuanba, they were utterly annihilated. Utterly annihilated, do you understand?"

Wiping away tears of laughter, Yang Guang added, "Furthermore, those two proud old fogeys, Yuwen Bi and Gao Jiong, practically fought to take Shimin and Xuanba as their disciples. These two nephews of mine are indeed exceptionally intelligent."

Upon hearing the names of Yuwen Bi and Gao Jiong, a look of genuine surprise finally appeared on Changsun Sheng's face.

For children to be highly regarded by Yuwen Bi and Gao Jiong, Changsun Sheng could not help but feel swayed.

He looked at Li Shimin, who had put away his toy bow and still wore a silly expression, and then at Li Xuanba standing nearby.

Li Xuanba immediately let out a cough, pretending to be frail and delicate.

Instantly, the silly look on Li Shimin's face vanished, replaced by sharp intelligence.

Frowning, he ran over to the eunuch, handed back the toy bow, grabbed a cup of honey water, and rushed to Li Xuanba's side. "Moisten your throat. Did you catch a cold from the wind? Why are you coughing again?"

Li Xuanba quickly replied, "I just accidentally choked on my own saliva. I'm fine."

Li Shimin insisted, "Drink some water first."

Li Xuanba sighed. "Alright."

Once he finished drinking, Li Shimin finally felt at ease seeing that his brother was no longer coughing.

Li Shimin unfastened his own small fur cloak and draped it over Li Xuanba's identical fur cloak. "Your big brother is a bit warm right now. You wear this first."

With that, he pointed to his own forehead. "Look, there are even beads of sweat on my forehead. I'm truly hot."

Watching the interaction between the two brothers, the three adults could not help but wear warm, affectionate expressions.

Yang Guang wiped away his tears of laughter and said, "General Changsun, I believe this marriage is highly suitable."

Changsun Sheng sighed. "Since Your Majesty has acted as the matchmaker, what more can this minister say? It is only that my daughter is of delicate health..."

Li Yuan suggested, "We can make a verbal agreement first, and then exchange the betrothal certificates when your daughter turns ten. How does that sound?"

Changsun Sheng said, "Since the Duke of Tang thinks so highly of us, I shall shamelessly accept this match."

He bowed to Yang Guang in gratitude. "Thank you, Your Majesty, for matchmaking. If this union comes to pass in the future, this minister will boldly invite Your Majesty to share a cup of wedding wine."

Seeing Li Yuan standing there dazed, Li Xuanba had no choice but to pull his second brother along and say, "Thank you, Your Majesty, for matchmaking."

Li Shimin once again put on his silly expression. "Thank you, Your Majesty." *What on earth are we doing? I'm so confused.*

With three people already bowing, no matter how simple-minded Li Yuan was, he immediately bowed as well. "Thank you, Your Majesty. Thanks to Your Majesty, this minister's loss was not in vain! Could Your Majesty find more formidable opponents to compete with me in archery next time? This minister still has three more sons."

Yang Guang was taken aback, then laughed and cursed, "I will never let anyone compete with you in archery again! If they win against you, they lose their daughters. Who would ever want to compete with you? Get out of my sight!"

Li Yuan chuckled foolishly.

Both Yang Guang and Changsun Sheng covered their eyes with one hand, unable to bear the sight.

Li Xuanba also wanted to cover his eyes.

*That expression... that expression indeed proves that Second Brother and Father are truly cut from the same cloth.*

Li Yuan winked and gestured to Li Shimin: *Look, your father "lost" a little wife for you. Aren't you happy?*

Li Shimin tilted his head, completely failing to understand what his father's bizarre expression meant.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第22章 小小蝴蝶大风暴
chunks.chineseText:
第22章 小小蝴蝶大风暴

=
　　杨广没留李渊吃饭， 李渊一手抱着李玄霸，一手牵着李世民，回他在洛阳的宅子。
　　“我们家在东京也有房子， 现在还在修， 等修好了， 我们一家人再住进去。”李渊揉了揉许久未见的两个儿子，笑道，“我们在洛阳的宅子也很大很漂亮。”
　　东京城在如今洛阳旧城往西约十五公里的地方。修建时， 杨广就给权贵预留了宅院。唐国公府自然不会例外。
　　之后一年，杨广会将老洛阳的住户和河北的工匠、江南的富户迁徙到东京城，称“陪京户”。原本在洛阳旧城有宅院的勋贵人家也会全部搬迁到东京城。
　　李渊还想问一问两个孩子伴驾的感想， 但李世民和李玄霸回到父亲身边，紧绷的心一松， 都困了。
　　双生子肩膀挨着肩膀， 脑袋靠着脑袋，居然已经睡着。
　　李渊看着马车外说了好一会儿，没听到孩子的回答，转头一看，才发觉他们已经睡着。
　　“二郎和三郎都安静下来时， 才能看出他们真是一对双生子。”李渊用手比了比两个人的脸，失笑道， “早听夫人在信里叹气，二郎比三郎大了一圈。还真是一圈。”
　　他把自己上马车后解下的大氅盖在两个孩子身上。
　　“辛苦了。”
　　李渊看着两个孩子疲惫的神情，轻声道。
　　……
　　李世民和李玄霸一觉睡到了第二日。
　　等他们睁眼的时候， 已经换了一身衣服， 躺在了洛阳家中的大床上。
　　李玄霸小幅度地打哈欠， 伸懒腰。
　　李世民像是活泼的猴儿似地从被窝里窜出来， 一边往身上套衣服，一边催促弟弟快起床。
　　我们回家啦！走！去找耶耶玩！
　　李玄霸翻白眼。找李渊有什么好玩？还不是你们两个人射箭，我在一旁观看。
　　“醒了？你们老师都等着了。”李渊听到动静，立刻进来抱怨道，“昨日你们该和我说了老师的事后再睡啊。”
　　虽然这么说，李渊还是顶住压力，不顾可能会被人说礼数不周，也让两个孩子睡到了自然醒。
　　还在打哈欠的李玄霸立刻闭上嘴，利落地从床上爬起来。
　　李世民急匆匆跑出门洗漱：“啊啊啊啊耶耶为什么不早点叫我和阿玄醒来！”
　　李渊笑道：“还没等一会儿，不急……唉，小心！”
　　李渊话音未落，李世民的小短腿就绊在了门槛上。
　　李世民双手抱头，咕噜咕噜滚了出去。
　　李渊吓得直追。
　　衣服套了一半的李玄霸：“扑哧……咳，二哥小心。”
　　他知道二哥摔了他应该关心，但二哥滑稽的动作真的好笑。不能笑不能笑，要友悌。
　　李渊把地上的李世民提起来的时候，李世民拍了拍身上的灰尘，就手臂上有一点乌青，什么事都没有。
　　李渊上上下下检查了一番，哭笑不得：“你还真是皮实。”
　　李世民得意道：“娘亲也这么说！”
　　李渊虚虚在李世民的屁股上拍了一下：“这可不是夸你。赶紧洗漱，你们老师还等着。”
　　李玄霸慢悠悠迈出卧室：“哥，没事吧？”
　　李世民道：“没事！还有！别以为我没听到你刚笑话我！阿玄你等着！”
　　李世民张牙舞爪，要去教训弟弟，被李渊死死拽住后领，扑腾半天扑不动。
　　李玄霸继续慢悠悠去往洗漱的地方走，并且再次响亮地“扑哧”了一声，把李世民气得嗷嗷叫。
　　还好两人想着老师还等着，没有多闹腾。
　　迅速洗漱完后，李世民和李玄霸跟着李渊去拜见老师。
　　宇文弼、高颎、虞世南三人已经喝完了一盏茶汤。
　　李世民和李玄霸连忙道歉。
　　三人笑了笑，都没在意。
　　谁都知道伴驾时有多紧张，两个孩子回家后多睡了一会儿，是小事。
　　“听说你们很快就要回大兴城。我等还要在洛阳伴驾，一时半会儿不能回去。但你们功课不能耽误。”高颎地位最高，最先开口。
　　三位老师都让仆人取出一个很大的木匣子。
　　李世民和李玄霸神情未动，李渊眼皮子跳了跳，有些头皮发麻。
　　三个大匣子里全是要读的书要做的功课？两个孩子真是辛苦了。
　　李世民很开心，大眼睛都笑得眯了起来。
　　李玄霸心情有些复杂。
　　史书中记载，杨广自登基后很少回大兴。大隋的朝中重臣也跟着他东奔西跑。现在他和二哥要回大兴城了高颎、宇文弼和虞世南三人还要继续跟随杨广留在洛阳，他以为他们之间的师生关系或许就断了。
　　没想到三位老师如此负责。
　　高颎、宇文弼和虞世南不仅仅是来送书送功课的。
　　李渊的探亲假时间有限，他前几日就已经和洛阳的朋友们说了离开的时间，明日就会出发。所以三人今日过来，还要再给李世民和李玄霸补补课。
　　李世民和李玄霸都很聪明，书上有了他们的笔记注解，两个孩子应该能在其他老师的辅佐下自学。
　　但他们还是要先把纲要给两个孩子讲解清楚，这样上手会更容易些。
　　李渊本来打算进入带着孩子们去串门，顺带炫耀一下他家这对深得皇帝喜爱的神童双生子。
　　结果三位老师给李世民和李玄霸讲了一日的课，到天色蒙灰的时候才离开。
　　李渊耐着性子陪两个孩子听了一日的课。
　　他送走三位老师时额外又补了一份拜师礼。三人没有拒绝。
　　李渊回来时，对李世民和李玄霸感慨道：“我之前虽听过他们三人的文名，今日一见，才知道他们的才华比文名更加耀眼。”
　　李世民道：“可是耶耶，你打了好几次哈欠，一直在走神。”
　　李玄霸：“……扑哧。”
　　李渊恼羞成怒，把两个孩子抓起来夹腋窝底下，飞速原地旋转身体。
　　李世民“咯咯”笑得像个小鸡。
　　李玄霸闭上眼。幼稚！
　　……
　　李渊命人打包好了行李，本打算用过午膳就出发，却因太子的来访，只好又把回家的时间推后。
　　太子杨昭是一个胖乎乎的和善人，被惹急了也不会骂人，顶多吼一句“大不是”。
　　他的性格与其父杨广是两个极端。
　　杨昭心胸十分宽广，仁爱友善，生活节俭。他自幼就被隋文帝和独孤皇后亲自抚养，深受祖父祖母疼爱。隋文帝和独孤皇后废太子，据说也有因为认可杨昭的缘故。
　　李玄霸听了这个故事，脑海里不由冒出了“好圣孙”三个字。
　　可惜，后世的“好圣孙”都被他们的父亲委以重任，继位之路很顺利。杨广却是不喜欢这个他父皇母后的“好圣孙”。
　　特别是进谏的人大多都围在杨昭身边，希望通过杨昭来劝说杨广。杨广就更不待见这个儿子。
　　对杨昭而言，父皇若对他不满意，他就加倍孝顺，让父皇安心满意就好。他就是这样一个心宽体胖的人，不会因此事怨恨或郁闷。
　　“表伯，表侄阻拦你回大兴，实在是抱歉。”杨昭一来就拱手道歉，“可否请表伯晚些时日回去？嗣昌想与表伯一同回大兴。”
　　李渊和这个表侄很亲近。
　　他装作生气道：“柴绍那竖子，他身为太子的护卫，刚与太子一同来洛阳，怎的说要回去？要回去就自己回，还想蹭我的车？他敢来亲自和我说吗？！”
　　杨昭笑呵呵道：“嗣昌自然是不敢的，所以我不就来帮他了？他五月就要成婚，现在急着回去准备。都拖了一年了，我见他那焦急模样，实在是于心不忍。”
　　李世民好奇道：“太子，为何柴兄非要和我们一同回去？”
　　杨昭有些犹豫：“这个嘛……”
　　李玄霸道：“柴兄想借父亲的势，好向陛下请假。”
　　杨昭立刻道：“我一定会劝说父皇，再多给表伯几日探亲假，不会耽误表伯与家人团聚！”
　　李世民拉了拉父亲的袖子，道：“耶耶，你就同意吧。虽然我很不希望阿姊离开家，但……哼，看在他挂念着阿姊的份上，帮他一把。”
　　“我没说不帮他。”李渊按了一下二儿子的脑袋，“我只是生气他为何如此胆怯，让太子给他当说客，自己不敢来。”
　　杨昭笑道：“他可没有让我给他当说客，是我来拜访表伯和两个神童表弟，顺带替他当说客。”
　　他低头看向李世民和李玄霸：“可还记得我？”
　　李渊拍了一下杨昭的肩膀，笑话道：“刚二郎和三郎都给你行礼，叫你太子了，你说他们可否记得你？”
　　杨昭道：“他们虽然知道我是太子，但不一定记得我曾经抱过他们，他们还曾尿到我身上的事啊。”
　　李世民瞪大眼睛：“还有这事？”
　　李玄霸立刻道：“肯定是二哥干的。”
　　李世民推搡了李玄霸一下：“什么坏事都是我做的是吗？”
　　李玄霸身体晃了晃，严肃道：“对。”
　　李世民又去推李玄霸。
　　李玄霸绕到杨昭身旁。
　　李世民想要“追打”弟弟，被李渊用手指勾住了后衣领，不准他欺负弟弟。
　　杨昭看着两个表弟活泼的模样，想起来自己同样活泼可爱的孩子，笑容越发慈祥。
　　“别在太子面前胡闹。”李渊不轻不重地训斥了两个孩子一顿，吩咐仆人把行李放回去，“太子，你说有事要来找我，是何事？”
　　杨昭道：“我有些事想要请教表伯。”
　　李渊松开勾着二儿子后衣领的手指，驱赶儿子们去庭院玩耍，与杨昭去了书房。
　　李渊刚一松手，李世民就朝着李玄霸乳虎扑食扑了过去。
　　李玄霸只跑了两步就被哥哥追赶上，头顶的揪揪毛都被拽散了，抱头蹲防。
　　李世民嚣张大笑：“你还敢不敢说我坏话！”
　　“不敢……”李玄霸瞅准二哥松懈的时机，踩了二哥一脚。
　　李世民抱着脚跳。
　　李玄霸立刻起身逃跑，但没两步又被李世民追赶上，继续抱头蹲防。
　　李渊和杨昭正走到走廊上，通过走廊的雕花窗户看到这一幕，都无奈极了。
　　杨昭道：“三郎打不过二郎，为何还要挑衅二郎？”
　　李渊道：“大概这就是倔强和自尊吧。”
　　杨昭笑着摇头。
　　两人继续往书房走，没去管兄弟。
　　亲近的兄弟，哪有不打架的。看李世民和李玄霸，也没有真打出火气，不过是玩耍。
　　李世民和李玄霸“互殴”了几回合，待李玄霸气喘吁吁叫停的时候，李世民抱着手臂停下来：“认输了吧？”
　　李玄霸擦着汗道：“认输认输。”我为什么要和天策上将打架？我脑抽了吗？
　　李玄霸每次打输了都会反省，但每次李世民挑衅他，他还会热血上头。
　　这大概就是灵魂被身体激素影响，不得不幼稚吧。
　　“要再玩一会儿吗？还是去看书？”李世民待弟弟气喘匀了，才把弟弟从地上拉起来。
　　“我去看书，你还是再练练你的弓箭。我们在这里多留几日，你未来的岳父一定会来拜访，说不定会考校你的弓箭。”李玄霸擦着汗道。
　　李世民让仆人拿来干净的布给李玄霸擦脸。
　　李玄霸身体虚，玩耍一会儿就会出一身虚汗。仆人随时都备着帕子。
　　“什么未来的岳父？”李世民疑惑。
　　李玄霸更疑惑：“你昨日订下的未来岳父啊。”
　　李世民：“？”
　　李玄霸：“？”
　　两个孩子面面相觑。
　　李玄霸捂脸：“天啦，你该不会现在还没反应过来昨日发生了什么吧？”
　　李世民挠头：“什么？”
　　李玄霸十分无语。他一边和李世民一起往校场走，一边将昨日之事详细解释给李世民听。
　　李世民停住脚步，瞠目结舌：“我现在就有妻子了？我才几岁？那个女娃才几岁？我们兄长都刚订婚！有这么急吗！”
　　李玄霸道：“大概是因为萧皇后想给我们和兰陵萧氏牵线，所以父亲娘亲先给我们定下婚事，成不成没关系，得堵住萧皇后那边的说媒。你的妻子，本就只会在长孙氏、窦氏、独孤氏等勋贵中选择。既然你这么敬仰长孙将军，父亲又和长孙将军比射箭后认可了长孙将军，就顺水推舟给你定下了。”
　　他说了一大串后，觉得累，便换成心声：【父亲借由昨日比射箭定下你和长孙家的婚事还有个好处，这看上去像是父亲突发奇想，还得了皇帝的认可。就算萧皇后听到了，也不会认为是我们家故意给她没脸。】
　　李世民抱头：“好复杂啊。”
　　李玄霸：【放心，你妻子非常好，你一定会喜欢。】
　　李世民惊讶地看向李玄霸：“这个你也知道？她才三岁吧？”
　　李玄霸：【她本就会是你的妻子，只是订婚没这么早。】
　　李世民笑道：“怪不得你昨日那么急。”
　　他压低声音道：“是因为陛下开玩笑说，要让长孙家那女娃和皇孙定下？”
　　李玄霸冷哼。赌上唐太宗黑的尊严，杨广敢拆这对cp，他就敢让自家二哥再增加一条强抢别人未婚妻的污点！我唐太宗黑怕过谁！
　　李世民失笑：“她有多好，你非要这个嫂子？”
　　李玄霸：【你将来见了就知道了。我现在和你说了，你拔高了期待，将来不满意怎么办？她现在也是个孩童而已，肯定不符合你的期望。】
　　李世民双手枕在脑后，和李玄霸继续往校场走：“也对，感情都是处出来的。”
　　李玄霸疑惑：【你这话从哪学来的？】
　　李世民道：“娘亲和阿姊都说过。”
　　李玄霸不说话了。
　　对娘亲和阿姊而言，她们夫妻间的感情处出来了吗？在她们自己看来，应该是处出来了吧。
　　李世民小声道：“阿姊未来如何我还不知道，但我肯定不会像耶耶对娘亲那样，明明娘亲是对的，他就是不听。如果那女娃将来和娘亲一样有本事，我肯定会好好听她说话。”
　　李玄霸不由自主地浮现出笑容：【嗯。不过她大概会和娘一样，太注重别人的看法，宁愿自己受委屈。所以二哥以后要多劝她别太贤惠。只要自己过得好就行，你会保护她，她不贤惠也没关系。】
　　李世民放下手，把着弟弟的肩膀道：“阿玄，这话你和你嫂子说去。”
　　李玄霸：“哈？”
　　李世民理所当然道：“你嫂子，你有什么说不得？”
　　李玄霸：“……”那是嫂子，你让我和嫂子说什么话？算了，二哥还是个孩子，他不懂。在二哥心里，什么结婚大概和过家家似的，他估计还想着不过是一家人里多了个女娃一同玩耍呢。
　　两人来到校场，李世民卖力练习射箭，李玄霸让人取来书本，坐在树荫下慢慢翻书。
　　初春暖风微醺，阳光透过树叶的剪影在书本上慢悠悠移动。
　　李玄霸伸了个懒腰，打了个哈欠，眯着眼睛看二哥终于一箭正中靶心，高兴地双手举着弓蹦蹦跳跳。
　　“三郎，在看何书？”杨昭与李渊聊完了正事，来校场来寻两个孩子。
　　李渊已经大步跨向校场中，要向李世民好好露一手，把李世民转移到长孙晟那里的尊敬抢回来。
　　李玄霸起身恭敬道：“在读《尚书》。”
　　杨昭惊讶道：“读书进度如此快吗？已经在读《尚书》了？”
　　他从李玄霸手中拿过书，让李玄霸不需要客气，他和李玄霸一同坐在了树荫下。
　　杨昭很胖，正坐有些难受。
　　这时佛教已经传入，隋朝人又常骑马，所以裤子已经是合裆，衣摆也很长，所以杨昭便盘坐在地上，就像个胖胖的佛陀。
　　“是高公的字迹。”杨昭一眼就看了出来。
　　他露出些许回忆的神色，道：“当年祖父给我启蒙时，也问高公要的书。”
　　李玄霸好奇：“高先生为太子启蒙过？”
　　杨昭眨了眨眼，狡黠地笑道：“你是不是想问，高公支持我伯父，怎还会为我启蒙？”
　　李玄霸使劲摇头。
　　杨昭笑道：“我知道你聪慧，窦夫人七岁能进谏，你和二郎也七岁了吧。”
　　李玄霸算了算，还真是，他与二哥居然在龙舟上度过了七岁生辰。
　　杨昭道：“你不想说就罢了。少说些也好。”
　　看着杨昭怅然的模样，李玄霸不明白太子为何会对一个孩童露出如此表情。
　　但他知道，现在还意气风发的太子，今年七月就会病逝洛阳。
　　李玄霸什么都知道，但什么都没打算做。
　　他之前一直待在唐国公府，与太子并不熟悉，不可能突然跑出去劝说什么，别人也不会听。
　　“高公说，幸亏有你和二郎在，父皇才没有走陆路回来，又白白耗费许多人力物力。”杨昭道，“谢谢你，三郎。”
　　李玄霸惊讶：“啊？”怎么还和我与二哥有关系？！
　　杨昭笑道：“你竟然不知道？”
　　李玄霸使劲摇头。
　　杨昭道：“你和二郎向南阳和母后进谏，希望体恤民力，还记得吗？”
　　李玄霸先摇头，然后垂首沉思了一会儿，道：“不是我，是二哥。说的是二哥问南阳公主，能不能把吃不完的饭菜给民夫一事吧？不过二哥是悄悄和南阳公主说的，皇后应当不知道。”
　　杨昭道：“那就是南阳告诉了母后。母后和南阳一同劝说父皇，陆路漫长，若遇上暴雨，就赶不上回洛阳赏春了。再者不仅你病了，队伍里有些老臣也身体不适，还是坐龙舟回去更舒适。不然你们若在路上出了意外，这场南巡就不完美了。”
　　李玄霸深吸一口气：“还有这事？”
　　他这时才想起来史书中这个被一笔带过的细节。隋炀帝一下江都返回时，好像确实是走的陆路！
　　史书记载，隋炀帝为了回程的排场，还特意在江都召群臣制定新的舆服和仪仗。
　　负责此事的何稠等人为了讨好隋炀帝，将新的舆服和仪仗做得十分华丽，命令州县进贡艳丽的羽毛，羽毛符合需求的禽兽，几乎被杀绝。
　　隋炀帝用这支长达二十余里的华丽仪仗回东京，把沿途道路堵得水泄不通。
　　上行下效。皇帝穷奢极欲，他不需要对臣子下命令，臣子就会为了讨好他，进献华丽铺张的东西。
　　这次皇帝回江都，因为仍旧是走的水路，用的仍旧是龙舟。虽然因为赶路很急，仍旧累死了不少民夫。但比起换条道走陆路耗费的民力，已经小多了。
　　我不过是和二哥去郑家接受一场“考校”，小小的蝴蝶翅膀居然扇出了这么大的动静？
　　“谢谢你和二郎。”杨昭揉了揉李玄霸的脑袋，“百姓也会谢谢你们。”
　　李玄霸使劲摇头：“我什么都没做，是二哥。”
　　杨昭开玩笑道：“若不是你病重，父皇也不会听劝。如果表兄说你病得恰好，你不会生气吧？”
　　李玄霸抿了下嘴，道：“不生气。我确实病得恰好，病得……很好。”
　　他的声音压得很低。
　　他仍旧不敢置信，他和二哥两个六七岁的小孩，居然能把一场民生浩劫蝴蝶没了。
　　“阿玄，你和太子表兄在说什么！”李世民蹦蹦跳跳走过来，就像是一只兔子。
　　杨昭笑道：“我在感谢你和三郎。”
　　李世民笑着跳到李玄霸身边坐下：“阿玄阿玄，你也听太子说了吗？我们的劝谏成功了！”
　　李玄霸道：“我们那也不算什么劝谏……”
　　李世民道：“就是成功了！太好啦！”
　　小小的李世民握拳：“虽然我和你还年幼，但只要去做，还是有可能成功。若什么都不做，就绝对不可能成功！”
　　李玄霸没回答。
　　他腹诽，是啊，如果再努力些，把唐朝蝴蝶没了就有意思了。
　　但他知道，有些事能蝴蝶没，有些事不可能。
　　只要皇帝还是杨广，隋朝仍旧会在短短十几年就被他玩没。
　　这不是节省一次民力能避免的事，甚至也不是太子和贤臣不死能避免的事。
　　太子不死，将来肯定会被杨广忌惮厌恶；贤臣不死，最好也就是疏远外放。
　　“你们这次确实厉害，但这件事你们要烂在心底，不可对外说。”李渊严肃道，“你们年幼，太过有贤名，不是好事。”
　　李玄霸腹诽，父亲这次倒是聪明了。
　　他道：“是，父亲。”
　　李世民叉腰：“耶耶，你小瞧我，我才不会乱说！”
　　“好，不小瞧你。”李渊对太子道，“太子，这事其实也是碰巧，功劳是皇后和南阳公主的，我两个孩子其实没有多大作用。”
　　杨昭知道李渊的担心，笑道：“我知道，我不会和其他人说，也让高公别对外说。”
　　李玄霸露出犹豫的神色。
　　李世民拍了拍李玄霸的手臂，道：“阿玄，你想说什么就说，何必吞吞吐吐。”
　　李玄霸摇头：“没事。”
　　李世民叹气：“不说就算了。”
　　杨昭在这里待了许久，该回去了。
　　李渊起身去送杨昭，顺便出门议事。
　　他们让两个小孩继续玩耍，不必起身相送。
　　李渊和杨昭离开后，李世民问道：“阿玄，怎么还在犹豫？有什么事这么让你为难？”
　　李玄霸摇头道：“真没什么。”
　　顿了顿，他说了一句没头没脑的话：“我自己都够惨了，还同情别人干什么。”
　　李世民疑惑：“阿玄，我们哪里惨了？我们过得可好了，怎么不能同情别人？”
　　李玄霸：“啊？”
　　李世民老气横秋道：“阿玄，我们是唐国公府的二公子和三公子，是皇帝陛下的表侄，每日锦衣玉食，哪里惨了？你这话真奇怪。”
　　李玄霸愣了一会儿，突然失笑：“是啊，我竟然忘记了，我们过得可不惨。二哥，帮我拦住太子！”
　　李世民笑着翻身起来：“好！”
　　虽然不知道弟弟想做什么，他还是飞速迈动小短腿奔跑，把快出府的杨昭拦住。
　　李玄霸气喘吁吁地跟来。
　　他伸出手，对杨昭道：“太子，我有话想要悄悄对你说。”
　　杨昭虽疑惑，也将李玄霸抱起来。
　　李玄霸趴在杨昭肩上，小声道：“陛下很厌恶高公，认为高公仍旧心向废太子，说迟早会杀高公。太子请劝说高公，辞官归隐，切记不可再进谏。”
　　杨昭的眼睛睁大。
　　李玄霸又道：“因太子最近与高公走得近，陛下也对太子有微词。若陛下让太子回大兴，请太子立刻回程，不要拖延。”
　　杨昭低头看着怀里一边说话，还一边喘气的瘦弱孩童。
　　李玄霸额头上是亮晶晶的汗珠，满蕴着认真和严肃神情的眼眸比额头上反射着太阳光的汗珠还亮。
　　杨昭长叹一口气，无奈苦笑：“我知道了。”
　　他伸手用袖子替李玄霸仔细擦干净额头上的汗珠：“谢谢，阿玄。”
　　因拦车驾，被李渊提起来狠狠揍了一顿的李世民嘀咕：“只有我能叫阿玄，太子也不行。哎哟，刚揍了，还揍！耶耶，我的臀股不是铁做的！”
　　李渊被气笑了，你还很嚣张是吧！
chunks.englishText:
Yang Guang did not keep Li Yuan for dinner. Holding Li Xuanba in one arm and leading Li Shimin with his other hand, Li Yuan headed back to his residence in Luoyang.

"Our family has a residence in Dongjing as well, though it's still under construction. Once it's finished, our whole family will move in," Li Yuan said, ruffling the hair of the two sons he hadn't seen in so long. He smiled. "But our current manor in Luoyang is also very grand and beautiful."

The new Eastern Capital, Dongjing, was located about fifteen kilometers west of the old city of Luoyang. During its construction, Yang Guang had reserved estates for the nobility, and the Duke of Tang's residence was naturally no exception.

Over the following year, Yang Guang would migrate the residents of old Luoyang, artisans from Hebei, and wealthy households from Jiangnan to Dongjing, designating them as "accompanying capital households." The noble families who originally owned manors in the old city of Luoyang would also relocate entirely to Dongjing.

Li Yuan wanted to ask the two children about their experience serving the Emperor, but now that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were back by their father's side, their tense minds relaxed, and drowsiness overtook them.

The twins sat shoulder-to-shoulder, head-to-head, and had actually fallen fast asleep.

Li Yuan had been talking while looking out the carriage window for quite some time. Hearing no response from the children, he turned around and realized they were already asleep.

"Only when Erlang and Sanlang quiet down can you really tell they are twins." Li Yuan measured their faces with his hand and laughed helplessly. "I heard my wife sighing in her letters that Erlang had grown a whole size larger than Sanlang. He really is a whole size bigger."

He took off the heavy cloak he had removed upon entering the carriage and draped it over the two children.

"You've worked hard," Li Yuan murmured softly, looking at the exhausted expressions on their faces.

...

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba slept all the way until the next morning.

By the time they opened their eyes, they had already been changed into fresh clothes and were lying on a large bed in their Luoyang home.

Li Xuanba gave a small yawn and stretched.

Li Shimin scrambled out of the covers like a lively monkey, pulling on his clothes while urging his younger brother to get up.

*We're home! Let's go! Let's find Father and play!*

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes. *What's so fun about finding Li Yuan? It'll just end up with the two of you shooting arrows while I watch from the side.*

"You're awake? Your teachers are already waiting," Li Yuan complained as he walked in upon hearing the noise. "You should have told me about your teachers yesterday before going to sleep."

Despite his complaints, Li Yuan had withstood the pressure, ignoring the risk of being called discourteous, just to let the two children sleep until they woke up naturally.

Li Xuanba, who was still mid-yawn, immediately shut his mouth and scrambled out of bed with practiced agility.

Li Shimin rushed out the door to wash up. "Ahhh! Father, why didn't you wake me and Ah Xuan up earlier?!"

Li Yuan laughed. "They haven't been waiting long, there's no rush... Ah, watch out!"

Before Li Yuan could finish his sentence, Li Shimin's short legs tripped over the high threshold.

Li Shimin clutched his head with both hands and went rolling out like a ball.

Li Yuan chased after him in a panic.

With his clothes only half-on, Li Xuanba let out a snort. "Pfft... Cough, watch out, Second Brother."

He knew he should show concern when his brother fell, but his brother's clumsy tumble was just too hilarious. *Don't laugh, don't laugh. Maintain brotherly love.*

By the time Li Yuan hoisted Li Shimin off the ground, the boy was already brushing the dust off himself. Aside from a slight bruise on his arm, he was completely unharmed.

Li Yuan checked him over from head to toe, caught between laughter and tears. "You really are made of tough stuff."

Li Shimin said proudly, "Mother says so too!"

Li Yuan gave Li Shimin a playful swat on the rear. "That wasn't a compliment. Hurry up and wash, your teachers are waiting."

Li Xuanba strolled out of the bedroom. "Brother, are you alright?"

Li Shimin barked, "I'm fine! And don't think I didn't hear you laughing at me just now! Ah Xuan, you just wait!"

Li Shimin bared his claws, preparing to teach his younger brother a lesson, but Li Yuan grabbed him firmly by the back collar. No matter how much he thrashed, he couldn't budge an inch.

Li Xuanba continued his leisurely stroll toward the washbasin, letting out another loud "pfft," which made Li Shimin howl with frustration.

Fortunately, keeping in mind that their teachers were waiting, the two didn't carry on the ruckus for long.

After a quick wash, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba followed Li Yuan to pay their respects to their teachers.

Yuwen Bi, Gao Jiong, and Yu Shinan had already finished a cup of tea.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba quickly apologized.

The three men smiled, not minding in the least.

Everyone knew how nerve-wracking it was to serve the Emperor. It was only natural for the two children to sleep a bit longer after returning home; it was a trivial matter.

"I hear you will soon return to Daxing City. The rest of us must remain in Luoyang to serve the Emperor and cannot return for the time being. However, your studies must not fall behind." Gao Jiong, holding the highest status among them, spoke first.

The three teachers each had a servant bring forward a large wooden chest.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's expressions remained unchanged, but Li Yuan's eyelids twitched, and his scalp went slightly numb.

*Are those three massive chests filled entirely with books to read and homework to do? These two kids really have it rough.*

Li Shimin, however, was delighted, his large eyes curving into crescents with his smile.

Li Xuanba's feelings were somewhat complicated.

According to historical records, Yang Guang rarely returned to Daxing after ascending the throne, and the high officials of the Great Sui Dynasty constantly traveled back and forth with him. Now that he and his second brother were returning to Daxing City while Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Yu Shinan had to remain in Luoyang with Yang Guang, he had assumed their teacher-student relationship might come to an end.

He had not expected the three teachers to be so responsible.

Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Yu Shinan had not come merely to deliver books and assignments.

Li Yuan's family leave was limited. He had already informed his friends in Luoyang of his departure date a few days ago, and they would set off tomorrow. Thus, the three had come today to give Li Shimin and Li Xuanba some extra tutoring.

Both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were highly intelligent. With the teachers' notes and annotations in the books, the two children should be able to study on their own with the assistance of other tutors.

Nevertheless, they still wanted to explain the core outlines clearly to the two children first, making it easier for them to get started.

Li Yuan had originally planned to take the children visiting today, using the opportunity to show off his pair of prodigy twins who were so deeply favored by the Emperor.

Instead, the three teachers lectured Li Shimin and Li Xuanba for the entire day, only departing when the sky began to turn a dusty gray.

Li Yuan had patiently accompanied the two children through the day's lessons.

When he saw the three teachers off, he presented them with an additional formal teacher-tribute gift, which they did not refuse.

Upon his return, Li Yuan sighed to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, "Though I had heard of their literary renown before, seeing them today makes me realize their true talent shines even brighter than their reputation."

Li Shimin pointed out, "But Father, you yawned several times and kept spacing out."

Li Xuanba: "...Pfft."

Embarrassed and angry, Li Yuan scooped up both children, tucking them under his armpits, and spun around rapidly on the spot.

Li Shimin giggled like a little chick.

Li Xuanba closed his eyes. *Childish!*

...

Li Yuan had ordered the servants to pack their luggage, intending to set off after lunch. However, due to a visit from the Crown Prince, he had no choice but to delay their journey home once again.

Crown Prince Yang Zhao was a chubby, good-natured man. Even when thoroughly provoked, he would not swear, shouting at most, "How utterly improper!"

His personality was the polar opposite of his father, Yang Guang.

Yang Zhao was broad-minded, benevolent, friendly, and lived frugally. He had been raised personally by Emperor Wen of Sui and Empress Dugu since childhood, deeply loved by his grandparents. It was said that one of the reasons Emperor Wen and Empress Dugu deposed the former Crown Prince was their high regard for Yang Zhao.

Hearing this story, the phrase "a fine imperial grandson" naturally popped into Li Xuanba's mind.

Unfortunately, while the "fine imperial grandsons" of later dynasties were entrusted with heavy responsibilities by their fathers and enjoyed smooth paths to the throne, Yang Guang did not like this "fine imperial grandson" favored by his imperial parents.

Particularly because most remonstrating officials gathered around Yang Zhao, hoping to use him to persuade Yang Guang, the Emperor grew even more displeased with his son.

For Yang Zhao, if his imperial father was dissatisfied with him, he would simply double his filial piety to put his father's mind at ease. He was precisely that kind of broad-minded, stout-hearted man, harboring no resentment or depression over such matters.

"Cousin-Uncle, I must apologize for delaying your return to Daxing," Yang Zhao said, bowing with cupped hands as soon as he arrived. "Could I ask you to delay your departure by a few days? Zichang wishes to return to Daxing with you."

Li Yuan was very close to this cousin-nephew.

He feigned anger and said, "That brat Chai Shao! As the Crown Prince's guard, he just arrived in Luoyang with Your Highness. Why is he talking about going back? If he wants to go back, he can go by himself. Does he really want to hitch a ride in my carriage? Does he even dare to come and tell me himself?!"

Yang Zhao chuckled. "Zichang naturally wouldn't dare, which is why I've come to help him, haven't I? He is to be married in the fifth month and is anxious to return and prepare. It has already been delayed for a year, and seeing his anxious state, I truly couldn't bear it."

Li Shimin asked curiously, "Your Highness, why must Brother Chai return with us?"

Yang Zhao hesitated. "Well, about that..."

Li Xuanba spoke up, "Brother Chai wants to use Father's influence to ask the Emperor for leave."

Yang Zhao immediately promised, "I will certainly persuade Imperial Father to grant Cousin-Uncle a few more days of family leave, so it won't delay your reunion with your family!"

Li Shimin tugged at his father's sleeve. "Father, just agree. Although I really don't want Elder Sister to leave home... hmph, for the sake of his concern for Elder Sister, let's give him a hand."

"I didn't say I wouldn't help him," Li Yuan said, patting his second son's head. "I'm just annoyed at how cowardly he is, getting the Crown Prince to act as his lobbyist instead of coming himself."

Yang Zhao smiled. "He didn't ask me to lobby for him. I came to visit Cousin-Uncle and my two prodigy cousins, and decided to speak on his behalf along the way."

He looked down at Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. "Do you still remember me?"

Li Yuan patted Yang Zhao's shoulder and teased, "Erlang and Sanlang just greeted you and called you Crown Prince. What do you think, do they remember you?"

Yang Zhao said, "Though they know I am the Crown Prince, they might not remember that I once held them, or that they once peed all over me."

Li Shimin's eyes widened. "That actually happened?"

Li Xuanba immediately said, "It was definitely Second Brother."

Li Shimin shoved Li Xuanba. "Is every bad thing always my fault?"

Li Xuanba swayed slightly and replied solemnly, "Yes."

Li Shimin went to shove Li Xuanba again.

Li Xuanba dodged behind Yang Zhao.

Li Shimin wanted to chase and hit his brother, but Li Yuan hooked his back collar with a finger, forbidding him from bullying his younger brother.

Watching the lively interaction between his two young cousins, Yang Zhao thought of his own equally lively and lovely children, and his smile grew warmer.

"Stop fooling around in front of the Crown Prince," Li Yuan scolded the two children mildly, then instructed the servants to put the luggage back. "Your Highness, you mentioned you had something to discuss with me. What is it?"

Yang Zhao said, "I have some matters I wish to consult Cousin-Uncle about."

Li Yuan released his finger from his second son's collar, shooed his sons out to play in the courtyard, and accompanied Yang Zhao to the study.

The moment Li Yuan let go, Li Shimin pounced on Li Xuanba like a young tiger hunting its prey.

Li Xuanba only managed two steps before his brother caught up to him. The small topknot on his head was pulled loose, forcing him to squat down and cover his head in defense.

Li Shimin laughed arrogantly. "Do you dare speak ill of me again?!"

"I wouldn't dare..." Li Xuanba seized the moment his brother let his guard down and stomped on his foot.

Li Shimin hopped around, clutching his foot.

Li Xuanba immediately scrambled up to run, but within two steps, Li Shimin caught him again, forcing him back into his defensive squat.

Li Yuan and Yang Zhao happened to walk along the corridor and witnessed this scene through the carved windows, feeling utterly helpless.

Yang Zhao asked, "Since Sanlang can't beat Erlang, why does he keep provoking him?"

Li Yuan replied, "Perhaps that is what we call stubbornness and pride."

Yang Zhao smiled and shook his head.

The two continued toward the study, leaving the brothers to their own devices.

Close brothers always squabbled. Looking at Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, they weren't truly angry; it was merely play.

After several rounds of "mutual combat," Li Xuanba finally panted and called for a truce. Li Shimin crossed his arms and stopped. "Do you admit defeat?"

Li Xuanba wiped his sweat. "I admit defeat, I admit defeat." *Why on earth did I try to fight the future General of Heavenly Strategy? Have I lost my mind?*

Every time Li Xuanba lost, he would reflect on his actions, yet every time Li Shimin provoked him, his blood would still boil.

Perhaps this was the consequence of his soul being influenced by physical hormones, forcing him to act childishly.

"Do you want to play a bit longer, or go read?" Li Shimin pulled his brother up from the ground once the latter had caught his breath.

"I'm going to read. You should practice your archery. Since we are staying here for a few more days, your future father-in-law will definitely come to visit, and he might test your archery skills," Li Xuanba said, wiping his sweat.

Li Shimin had a servant bring a clean cloth to wipe Li Xuanba's face.

Li Xuanba had a weak constitution and would break into a cold sweat after even a brief play session. The servants always kept handkerchiefs ready.

"What future father-in-law?" Li Shimin was puzzled.

Li Xuanba was even more puzzled. "The future father-in-law you were betrothed to yesterday."

Li Shimin: "?"

Li Xuanba: "?"

The two children stared at each other.

Li Xuanba covered his face. "Heavens, don't tell me you still haven't realized what happened yesterday?"

Li Shimin scratched his head. "What?"

Li Xuanba was utterly speechless. As they walked toward the training field together, he explained yesterday's events to Li Shimin in detail.

Li Shimin stopped in his tracks, his jaw dropping. "I have a wife already? How old am I? How old is that girl? Our eldest brother only just got betrothed! Is there really such a rush?!"

Li Xuanba explained, "It's likely because Empress Xiao wanted to play matchmaker between us and the Lanling Xiao clan. So, Father and Mother decided to secure a betrothal for us first. Whether it actually happens doesn't matter; the point is to block Empress Xiao's matchmaking attempts. Your future wife was always going to be chosen from noble clans like the Zhangsun, Dou, or Dugu anyway. Since you admire General Zhangsun so much, and Father acknowledged him after their archery contest, they simply went with the flow and settled it for you."

After speaking such a long string of words, he felt tired, so he switched to his inner voice: *[There is another benefit to Father using yesterday's archery contest to arrange your marriage with the Zhangsun family. It makes it look like a sudden whim of Father's that happened to receive the Emperor's approval. Even if Empress Xiao hears of it, she won't think our family deliberately slighted her.]*

Li Shimin clutched his head. "This is so complicated."

Li Xuanba: *[Don't worry. Your wife is wonderful; you will definitely like her.]*

Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba in surprise. "You even know this? She's only three years old, right?"

Li Xuanba: *[She was destined to be your wife anyway; the betrothal just wasn't supposed to happen this early.]*

Li Shimin laughed. "No wonder you were in such a rush yesterday."

He lowered his voice. "Was it because His Majesty joked about betrothing the Zhangsun girl to an imperial grandson?"

Li Xuanba snorted coldly. *Staking my dignity as a Tang Taizong anti-fan, if Yang Guang dared to break up this couple, I would have dared to let my second brother add another black mark to his record by snatching someone else's fiancée! Who has this Taizong anti-fan ever feared!*

Li Shimin chuckled. "Just how good is she that you insist on having her as your sister-in-law?"

Li Xuanba: *[You will know when you meet her in the future. If I tell you now, your expectations will be sky-high, and what if you're disappointed? Right now, she is just a child, so she definitely won't match your expectations.]*

Li Shimin rested his hands behind his head as he and Li Xuanba continued toward the training field. "True. Feelings are nurtured over time."

Li Xuanba was puzzled: *[Where did you learn that phrase?]*

Li Shimin said, "Mother and Elder Sister have both said it."

Li Xuanba fell silent.

For Mother and Elder Sister, had their marital feelings been nurtured? In their own eyes, they probably had.

Li Shimin whispered, "I don't know how Elder Sister will fare in the future, but I will definitely not be like Father to Mother—even when Mother is right, he just refuses to listen. If that girl turns out to be as capable as Mother in the future, I will definitely listen to her."

Li Xuanba couldn't help but smile: *[Mhm. However, she will probably be like Mother, caring too much about others' opinions and preferring to suffer grievances herself. So, Second Brother, you must advise her in the future not to be too virtuous. As long as she lives well, that's enough. You will protect her, so it doesn't matter if she isn't perfectly virtuous.]*

Li Shimin lowered his hands and slung an arm over his brother's shoulder. "Ah Xuan, you should tell your sister-in-law that yourself."

Li Xuanba: "Huh?"

Li Shimin said as if it were the most natural thing in the world, "She's your sister-in-law. Why shouldn't you speak to her?"

Li Xuanba: "..." *She's my sister-in-law, what do you expect me to say to her? Forget it, Second Brother is still a child; he doesn't understand. To him, marriage is probably like playing house. He likely thinks it's just adding another girl to the family to play with.*

The two arrived at the training field. Li Shimin practiced his archery with great effort, while Li Xuanba had a servant bring over his books and sat under the shade of a tree, slowly flipping through them.

The warm breeze of early spring was slightly intoxicating, and the sunlight filtered through the leaves, casting shifting silhouettes that slowly drifted across the pages.

Li Xuanba stretched and yawned, squinting his eyes to watch his second brother finally hit the bullseye. The boy jumped up and down in joy, holding his bow high with both hands.

"Sanlang, what book are you reading?" Yang Zhao had finished discussing business with Li Yuan and came to the training field to find the two children.

Li Yuan had already strode onto the field, eager to show off his skills to Li Shimin and win back the admiration his son had transferred to Zhangsun Sheng.

Li Xuanba stood up and said respectfully, "I am reading the *Book of Documents*."

Yang Zhao was surprised. "Your studies are progressing so quickly? You are already reading the *Book of Documents*?"

He took the book from Li Xuanba's hands, telling him not to stand on ceremony, and sat down with him in the shade.

Yang Zhao was very stout, making sitting in the formal kneeling posture rather uncomfortable.

By this time, Buddhism had already spread, and since the people of the Sui Dynasty frequently rode horses, trousers with closed crotches had become common, and their robes were quite long. Thus, Yang Zhao sat cross-legged on the ground, looking like a chubby Buddha.

"This is Lord Gao's handwriting," Yang Zhao recognized it at a glance.

A look of reminiscence crossed his face as he said, "When Grandfather initiated my education back then, he also asked Lord Gao for books."

Li Xuanba was curious. "Mr. Gao once tutored Your Highness?"

Yang Zhao blinked and smiled slyly. "Are you wondering how Lord Gao, who supported my uncle, could still tutor me?"

Li Xuanba shook his head vigorously.

Yang Zhao laughed. "I know you are intelligent. Lady Dou was able to offer counsel at the age of seven, and you and Erlang are seven now, aren't you?"

Li Xuanba did the math and realized it was true. He and his second brother had actually spent their seventh birthdays aboard the dragon boat.

Yang Zhao said, "If you don't wish to speak of it, so be it. It is indeed better to speak less."

Looking at Yang Zhao's melancholy expression, Li Xuanba did not understand why the Crown Prince would show such a look to a mere child.

But he knew that this Crown Prince, who was still full of vigor, would fall ill and pass away in Luoyang in the seventh month of this very year.

Li Xuanba knew everything, yet he had no intention of doing anything.

He had lived in the Duke of Tang's residence all this time and was not close to the Crown Prince. It was impossible for him to suddenly run out and offer advice; no one would listen to him anyway.

"Lord Gao said that thanks to you and Erlang, Imperial Father did not return by land, which would have wasted a vast amount of manpower and resources," Yang Zhao said. "Thank you, Sanlang."

Li Xuanba was astonished. "Ah?" *How does this have anything to do with me and Second Brother?!*

Yang Zhao laughed. "You actually didn't know?"

Li Xuanba shook his head vigorously.

Yang Zhao said, "You and Erlang spoke to Nanyang and Mother, hoping they would show consideration for the commoners' labor. Do you remember?"

Li Xuanba shook his head first, then lowered his head in thought for a moment before saying, "It wasn't me; it was Second Brother. You must be referring to when Second Brother asked Princess Nanyang if the leftover food could be given to the laborers, right? But Second Brother whispered that to Princess Nanyang in secret; the Empress shouldn't have known."

Yang Zhao said, "Then Nanyang must have told Mother. Mother and Nanyang together persuaded Imperial Father that the land route was long, and if they encountered heavy rain, they wouldn't make it back to Luoyang in time to enjoy the spring. Furthermore, not only were you ill, but some of the elderly ministers in the entourage were also unwell, so traveling by dragon boat would be far more comfortable. Otherwise, if any of you met with an accident on the road, this southern tour would not be perfect."

Li Xuanba took a deep breath. "That actually happened?"

Only now did he recall this detail that had been glossed over in the history books. When Emperor Yang of Sui returned from his first visit to Jiangdu, he had indeed returned by land!

According to historical records, for the sake of grandeur on his return journey, Emperor Yang had specifically summoned his ministers in Jiangdu to design new imperial carriages, robes, and guards of honor.

He Chou and others in charge of the matter, eager to curry favor with Emperor Yang, made the new carriages and guards of honor incredibly lavish. They ordered the prefectures and counties to tribute vibrant feathers, resulting in the near-extinction of the birds and beasts that met their requirements.

Emperor Yang had returned to Dongjing with this magnificent guard of honor stretching over twenty *li*, completely blocking the roads along the way.

Those below follow the example of those above. When the Emperor was extravagantly wasteful, he did not even need to command his ministers; they would naturally present lavish and ostentatious gifts to curry favor.

This time, because the Emperor returned from Jiangdu by water, he still used the dragon boats. Although many laborers were still worked to death due to the hurried pace, the toll on the commoners' labor was far less than what would have been spent on a land route.

*I merely went with Second Brother to the Zheng family for a "test," and yet a tiny flap of a butterfly's wings has stirred up such a massive storm?*

"Thank you and Erlang," Yang Zhao said, ruffling Li Xuanba's hair. "The common people will thank you as well."

Li Xuanba shook his head vigorously. "I didn't do anything. It was Second Brother."

Yang Zhao joked, "If you hadn't fallen gravely ill, Imperial Father wouldn't have listened to the advice. You won't be angry if your cousin says you fell ill at just the right time, will you?"

Li Xuanba pursed his lips and said, "I'm not angry. I indeed fell ill at just the right time... It was a very good illness."

His voice was very low.

He still found it hard to believe that he and his second brother, two six- or seven-year-old children, had actually managed to butterfly away a massive disaster for the common people.

"Ah Xuan, what are you and Cousin Crown Prince talking about!" Li Shimin came hopping over like a rabbit.

Yang Zhao smiled. "I am thanking you and Sanlang."

Li Shimin sat down beside Li Xuanba with a grin. "Ah Xuan, Ah Xuan, did you hear what the Crown Prince said? Our advice succeeded!"

Li Xuanba said, "Ours could hardly be called advice..."

Li Shimin insisted, "But it succeeded! This is wonderful!"

The young Li Shimin clenched his fist. "Even though you and I are still young, as long as we try, there is still a chance of success. If we do nothing, success is absolutely impossible!"

Li Xuanba did not answer.

He grumbled inwardly, *Yes, and if we try a bit harder, it would be quite interesting to butterfly the Tang Dynasty out of existence too.*

But he knew that while some things could be butterflied away, others could not.

As long as the Emperor was still Yang Guang, the Sui Dynasty would still be ruined by him in a mere dozen years.

This was not something that could be avoided by saving the commoners' labor once, nor was it something that could be prevented even if the Crown Prince and virtuous ministers did not die.

If the Crown Prince did not die, he would surely be feared and detested by Yang Guang in the future; if the virtuous ministers did not die, their best-case scenario would merely be estrangement and exile.

"You two were indeed impressive this time, but you must keep this matter buried deep in your hearts and never speak of it to outsiders," Li Yuan said solemnly. "You are still young. Having too great a reputation for virtue is not a good thing."

Li Xuanba thought to himself, *Father is actually being smart for once.*

He said, "Yes, Father."

Li Shimin put his hands on his hips. "Father, you underestimate me! I would never speak of it carelessly!"

"Alright, I won't underestimate you." Li Yuan turned to the Crown Prince. "Your Highness, this matter was actually just a coincidence. The credit belongs to the Empress and Princess Nanyang; my two children didn't really play much of a role."

Yang Zhao understood Li Yuan's concerns and smiled. "I understand. I won't tell anyone else, and I will also tell Lord Gao not to speak of it."

Li Xuanba showed a look of hesitation.

Li Shimin patted Li Xuanba's arm. "Ah Xuan, if you have something to say, just say it. Why hesitate?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "It's nothing."

Li Shimin sighed. "Fine, if you won't say it, then don't."

Yang Zhao had stayed for a long time and it was time for him to return.

Li Yuan stood up to see Yang Zhao off, intending to go out to discuss some matters as well.

They told the two children to keep playing and that there was no need to stand and see them off.

After Li Yuan and Yang Zhao left, Li Shimin asked, "Ah Xuan, why are you still hesitating? What is making you so conflicted?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "It's really nothing."

After a pause, he muttered a seemingly nonsensical sentence: "I'm miserable enough as it is, why should I waste my sympathy on others?"

Li Shimin was puzzled. "Ah Xuan, how are we miserable? We are living a wonderful life, why can't we sympathize with others?"

Li Xuanba: "Huh?"

Li Shimin said in a mature, lecturing tone, "Ah Xuan, we are the second and third young masters of the Duke of Tang's residence, and the cousin-nephews of His Majesty. We enjoy fine food and clothing every day. How are we miserable? What you said is really strange."

Li Xuanba froze for a moment, then suddenly burst into laughter. "Indeed, I actually forgot that we aren't miserable at all. Second Brother, help me stop the Crown Prince!"

Li Shimin grinned and scrambled up. "Alright!"

Though he didn't know what his younger brother wanted to do, he still sprinted on his short legs, stopping Yang Zhao just as the Crown Prince was about to leave the manor.

Li Xuanba followed, panting heavily.

He reached out his hand and said to Yang Zhao, "Your Highness, I have something I want to tell you in private."

Though puzzled, Yang Zhao picked Li Xuanba up.

Leaning against Yang Zhao's shoulder, Li Xuanba whispered, "His Majesty deeply detests Lord Gao, believing that Lord Gao's heart still lies with the deposed Crown Prince, and has said he will execute Lord Gao sooner or later. Your Highness, please persuade Lord Gao to resign and retire, and remind him that he must absolutely never remonstrate again."

Yang Zhao's eyes widened.

Li Xuanba added, "Because Your Highness has been close to Lord Gao recently, His Majesty has also expressed dissatisfaction with you. If His Majesty orders you to return to Daxing, please set off immediately and do not delay."

Yang Zhao looked down at the frail child in his arms, who was still gasping for breath as he spoke.

Beads of sweat glistened on Li Xuanba's forehead, and his eyes, filled with earnestness and gravity, shone even brighter than the sweat reflecting the sunlight.

Yang Zhao let out a long sigh and smiled helplessly. "I understand."

He reached out and used his sleeve to carefully wipe the sweat from Li Xuanba's forehead. "Thank you, Ah Xuan."

For blocking the carriage, Li Shimin was hoisted up and given a sound thrashing by Li Yuan. He muttered, "Only I can call him Ah Xuan, not even the Crown Prince is allowed. Ow! You just hit me, and you're hitting me again! Father, my backside isn't made of iron!"

Li Yuan was provoked to laughter by his anger. *You're still acting cocky, aren't you!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第23章 无心之言点醒父
chunks.chineseText:
第23章 无心之言点醒父

=
　　杨昭和李渊再次离开。
　　离开时， 李渊对李世民使了个眼色，意思是等回来再收拾他。
　　李世民唉声叹气：“阿玄，每次你闯祸， 都是我挨揍。”
　　李玄霸道：“我没闯祸。”
　　李世民幽怨地看着李玄霸。
　　李玄霸视线偏移， 心虚道：“想听故事吗？我给你讲故事。”
　　李世民双手高举， 振臂小声欢呼：“好耶！你好久没给我讲故事了。每次让你讲故事，你都犯懒。”
　　李玄霸道：“别废话，说想听哪个。”
　　李世民毫不犹豫道：“《西游记》！”
　　李玄霸在心中叹气。果然对小孩子而言， 还是《西游记》最好玩。
　　他自然是记不全原汁原味的《西游记》，但讲故事也不需要背完整本《西游记》。八十一难凑一凑，甚至不用《西游记》原本的八十一难也行。反正他也没想过写个四大名著， 就是说个热闹。
　　但二哥听了《西游记》后就非要练棍法，让他很是头疼。
　　以后天策上将的武器如果多了一根金箍棒， 那也太滑稽了。
　　“快说快说！上次你说到偷袈裟！”李世民催促。
　　李玄霸皱眉。上次说到偷袈裟？糟糕， 记不住顺序了。
　　他冥思苦想，自己把八十一难讲了几个。
　　……
　　李渊傍晚才回来，身上满是酒气。
　　柴绍也一同过来，不仅同样一身酒气，还试图用这一身酒气去熏李世民和李玄霸。
　　李世民把李玄霸护在身后， 手中没有箭头的玩具箭从玩具弓中离弦射出，射中了柴绍的肚子。
　　柴绍“哎哟”一声停住脚步。
　　“阿玄快跑！”李世民先用玩具弓劈了柴绍伸出的手臂， 拉着李玄霸就跑。
　　李玄霸跌跌撞撞往前跑的时候回头看了柴绍一眼。
　　哇哦，我二哥这么早就学会用弓劈人了。
　　柴绍委屈地揉手臂：“丈人，二郎好凶。”
　　李渊哈哈大笑：“我的儿子就该这么凶！来， 继续喝！”
　　柴绍道：“好， 继续喝！”
　　两人勾肩搭背又喝了一顿。
　　跟随在李渊身边伺候李渊生活的万氏去看了他们一眼， 担心他们喝醉了又来吵孩子， 便让李世民和李玄霸睡在她隔壁。
　　万氏是李渊的妾室，出身江都万氏。
　　万氏的曾祖父是南齐高官，祖父是南梁高官。隋朝灭南朝后，万氏的父亲任大隋的利州刺史。
　　这样的出身，到了国公府当然不是一个普通的妾室。
　　国公与三品官皆有媵六人，为从七品。万氏就是媵，有诰命品级在身。窦夫人不在的时候，她能代表国公府的女眷在外面应酬。
　　在隋唐的法律中，五品官以上皆能置“媵”。“媵”算侧室，“媵”之下才是俗话中“妾同买卖”的“妾”。
　　五品官以下官员和庶人没有资格置“媵”，所以置办的小老婆皆是家主可以发卖的“妾”。
　　独孤老夫人时常卧病在床，窦夫人要留在大兴老家伺候婆婆，照顾孩子。万氏就跟在李渊身边，伺候李渊的起居，帮助李渊进行女眷间的应酬。
　　李玄霸出于后世人的角度，最初对万氏有些敌意，总觉得万氏和自家母亲之间会有宅斗之类的不愉快。
　　他稍稍年长后与万氏稍稍熟悉，又观察了万氏和母亲的相处，才发现万氏也是个可怜人，心里很苦。
　　万氏陪同李渊外出做官时，自己所生的儿女只能留在老宅。
　　她回来时儿女皆不认识她，她只能默默抹眼泪，还不敢被李渊和独孤老夫人发现，只有窦夫人会安慰她。
　　待她的儿女长大些，窦夫人时时在她儿女面前说起万氏，她的儿女才对万氏亲近些。
　　万氏曾想能不能和窦夫人换着陪李渊外放，轮流伺候独孤老夫人。她被独孤老夫人责骂得狗血淋头，她的娘家人也写信来斥责她不顾礼数。
　　侧室虽不是妾，但也不能僭越。正室在的时候，侧室没资格伺候婆婆。
　　身为世家官宦家的娘子，万氏连想去伺候婆婆都要被骂没规矩。李玄霸听了此事后，对万氏就提不起敌意了。
　　因窦夫人对万氏的儿女很照顾，万氏对李世民和李玄霸也很好。
　　李建成身为嫡长子，又比弟弟们年龄大太多，与弟弟很生疏，更看不上庶出的弟弟。万氏就绞尽脑汁地悄悄讨好李世民和李玄霸。
　　她生李稚诠的时候伤了身体，之后很难再有孕。国公府除嫡长子之外的诸子都需要自找出路。有兄弟帮衬，肯定比独自打拼好。何况李世民和李玄霸很小就展现出过人的天赋，将来前途一定不错。
　　万氏被独孤老夫人和家里人教训了几次，现在很恪守规矩。窦夫人在的时候，她都静悄悄地把自己关在屋里，不出来找存在感。
　　现在窦夫人在大兴，她才出来照顾李世民和李玄霸。
　　李世民很喜欢万氏，叫万氏“阿姨”。
　　李玄霸别扭了几次，也跟着叫万氏“阿姨”。现在他与万氏仍旧虽不亲近，也不会太生疏，还会给万氏说五弟的一些趣事。
　　另外，万氏的孩子李稚诠也是叫万氏“阿姨”。窦夫人才是李稚诠的“娘亲”。
　　“唉，郎君什么都好，就是好那口酒，一喝多就没了分寸。柴小郎怎么也这样？”万氏一边帮李世民和李玄霸换掉被酒熏入味的衣服，一边小声抱怨，“酒可不是什么好东西，可不能多喝。”
　　李玄霸道：“我不喝酒，二哥也少喝。”
　　李世民道：“啊？我看耶耶和兄长都爱喝酒，我长大了也想喝！”
　　李玄霸道：“饮酒无度是坏毛病。你可以喝一点，但不能喝醉。”
　　李世民眼睛滴溜溜转：“再说吧。”
　　万氏扑哧笑道：“真是亲父子，二郎你还没尝过酒，就好酒了。”
　　李玄霸嫌弃道：“你爱喝就喝，但你以后敢灌我酒，我就揍你。”
　　李世民连忙摆手：“别了，你揍我，我还怕你伤到。”
　　万氏笑得不停。
　　每次见这对双生子“吵架”，她都觉得好可爱。
　　万氏帮两个孩子换完衣服后道：“二郎，三郎，夫人说你们想做生意？阿姨在南边有些货源，能帮阿姨卖些货物吗？”
　　李世民还不懂万氏的意思，李玄霸一听就知道，万阿姨是想借此讨好他们。
　　江都万氏的“江都”即后世的扬州城。万氏的根基在北边虽浅薄，但在江都资产颇丰。
　　在后世地理划分上江都属于江北，但在世人心中和文化圈中，江都就是江南如今最繁华的城市。江南物产都集中在江都。
　　因杨广喜欢江南，现在在大兴和东京的权贵也喜欢江南的货物。有了江都万氏的帮衬，李玄霸和李世民的脂粉铺子就不愁江南新鲜货卖。
　　李玄霸毫不客气道：“好，我就谢过阿姨了。若我和二哥的生意能做成，小五再长大些，我们拉着他一起通过店铺的账本学算术。”
　　万氏笑颜如花；“五郎就交给二郎和三郎教导了。若五郎能学得二郎三郎一二分本事，阿姨就放心了。”
　　李世民插嘴道：“阿姨怎么对小五这么没有信心？小五可乖巧懂事，也勤奋好学，坐都坐不稳就拿着毛笔在纸上学写字，睡觉时都要抱着毛笔。阿玄，虞先生字写得特别好，将来让小五也和我们一样拜师虞先生学写字如何？”
　　李玄霸看了万氏略带紧张的神情，心里叹了口气，道：“小五很勤奋，虞先生肯定会同意。”
　　万氏不自觉绞紧衣角的手指松开，她微笑道：“到时就麻烦二郎三郎引荐了。”
　　李世民把自己的小胸脯拍得啪嗒响：“阿姨放心，小事一桩。”
　　万氏和李世民、李玄霸又闲聊了一会儿，才回到隔壁睡觉。
　　关上门后，万氏拿出儿子曾经戴过的璎珞无声哽咽了一会儿。
　　还好还好，二郎和三郎都是好孩子，记得自己的好，小小年纪就肯提携弟弟。希望二郎和三郎更加得皇帝重视，将来前程远大。
　　“不知道这次回去，五郎是不是又忘记我的脸了。”万氏小声凄婉道，声音低得连在门外隔间守夜的贴身丫鬟都听不见。
　　另一边，李玄霸一边思索自己还有哪些《西游记》故事没讲到，一边用心声给二哥解释万氏此举的用意。
　　他已经讲了一下午《西游记》，实在是记不住唐僧已经过了多少难。
　　李世民趴在床榻上，双手撑着脑袋，歪着头叹气道：“阿姨想得好多啊。耶耶和娘亲肯定不会亏待小五，居然还来讨好我们两个小孩。”
　　李玄霸：【她这样做才聪明。】万阿姨如此小心翼翼地讨好他和二哥，让他都不好意思对李稚诠的死视而不见了。
　　李稚诠就是李智云，现在虽然已经改名，他们还是习惯把他的旧名当小名称呼。待李智云取了小字后，他们可能才会改口。
　　李世民手撑麻了，在床榻上翻滚了两圈，道：“万阿姨这样小心翼翼，看上去好可怜。我们再多照顾小五一点吧。等回家，我们就教小五读书！给他布置好多好多功课！我还要教他射箭！无论天晴下雨都不准偷懒！”
　　李玄霸欲言又止。给小五布置很多功课，并且天晴下雨都要带小五射箭，这就是“多照顾”吗？我真是替小五谢谢你了啊，二哥。
　　“好了，不说烦心事了，《西游记》！《西游记》！”李世民闹腾。
　　“小声点，我正在想。”李玄霸道。
　　他继续皱眉苦思，我究竟还有哪几难没讲？
　　愁啊。下次给二哥讲故事的时候，一定要把已经讲过的情节用笔记下来，免得想得头疼。
　　……
　　又过了五日，李渊终于重新启程。
　　这次队伍里不仅多了一个柴绍，还多了一个刚请了探亲假的长孙晟。
　　长孙晟和李渊给儿女订下了口头婚约。想了几日，向皇帝告假回家处理此事。
　　李玄霸以为李世民与老丈人同行会很紧张，结果只有他这个事外人在紧张，他二哥可自在了。
　　李渊、长孙晟和柴绍都是骑马。李世民闹着和李渊同骑，一路上和长孙晟叽叽喳喳说个不停。
　　李渊嫌弃他，把他丢到长孙晟马上。
　　李世民就非常自来熟地坐在未来老丈人怀里，继续叽叽喳喳问长孙晟突厥的事。
　　李渊对从马车里探出头的李玄霸伸出手：“三郎，要不要骑马？”
　　李玄霸使劲摇头，把脑袋缩了回去。
　　他前世没骑过马，今生身体不好，还没有正式学习骑马，对骑马很好奇。曾经李渊说带他骑马，他就去了。
　　李渊抱着儿子纵马疾驰，回来时发现儿子两条小嫩腿都磨出了血。
　　独孤老夫人这么纵容儿子的老太太，李玄霸还是第一次看见她举起拐杖把李渊揍得抱头乱窜。
　　李渊埋怨道：“三郎啊，你该不会还记着上次我带你骑马把你腿磨破了？”
　　李玄霸无声地盯着李渊。
　　李渊突然坏笑，从马背上跳上了马车，把儿子夹在手臂下抓了出来，又重新翻身上马。
　　李玄霸惊得双目溜圆。
　　父亲你这是玩什么杂耍吗！你不觉得这很危险吗！
　　李世民双手捂嘴偷笑。
　　“不想骑马也得骑。我们唐国公府的小郎怎么能不会骑马！”李渊大笑，“别想跑，老实点！”
　　李玄霸缩在李渊身前，幽怨地瞥了父亲一眼。
　　李渊看着李玄霸这副受气包的模样，笑得更加开心。
　　李世民双手捂着嘴笑够之后，才为弟弟解围：“耶耶，阿玄刚病愈，别欺负阿玄。”
　　“正因为刚病愈，才要好好骑马锻炼身体。”李渊满嘴歪理。
　　万氏不敢阻拦李渊，只好戴好冪离，探身出来，给李渊递了一条毯子：“请郎君给三郎遮一遮风。”
　　“哪需要这么娇贵？”李渊虽然这样说，还是用小毯子把李玄霸裹得严严实实。
　　李渊裹李玄霸就像是在裹什么行李似的，把李玄霸裹成了圆筒形，只留下一个脑袋。
　　李玄霸动了动手臂。嗯，完全动不了。
　　李世民继续双手捂嘴，笑得前俯后仰，后脑勺撞在长孙晟胸口，疼得嗷嗷叫。
　　长孙晟揉了揉胸口，无奈道：“你的脑袋真硬。”
　　李世民抱着脑袋笑道：“谢谢长孙将军夸奖！”
　　长孙晟：“……我不是夸奖你。”
　　李世民不管，他就当长孙将军在夸奖他，后一句话他没听到！
　　李渊低头对李玄霸笑道：“这样好了吧？”
　　李玄霸现在连转头都困难：“父亲，你这是给我裹毯子吗？你这是把我捆了起来。我回去要向祖母和母亲告状，你欺负人。”
　　李渊笑道：“你尽管去告状，我还怕你不成！”
　　李渊为了显示自己真的不怕，还扬起马鞭唱起了歌。
　　李世民双手鼓掌打着拍着，明明不知道词曲，也跟着吱儿哇地乱唱。
　　柴绍为了讨好老丈人，本来跟着一同慷慨高歌，唱着唱着就被李世民带歪了调子，挠挠头不知道该怎么唱下去。
　　被裹得完全不能动弹的李玄霸不断翻白眼。
　　吵死了吵死了，魔音灌脑。
　　李玄霸：“父亲，二哥，难听死了，闭嘴！”
　　李渊和李世民扯着嗓子唱得更大声。
　　柴绍想了想，不管调子和词了，跟着一起乱唱吧。
　　长孙晟笑眯眯地捋了捋胡须。
　　他对这一家父子和乐融融的模样十分喜欢。观音婢嫁给这样的人家，未来应该会过得不错。
　　……
　　窦夫人回到大兴后，对李世民和李玄霸担心不已。
　　得知李世民和李玄霸能和李渊一同回大兴，她时不时就要差人出城问一问，望眼欲穿。
　　终于得到了李渊和两个孩子回来的消息，她等不及他们回府，戴上冪离出门亲自迎接。
　　她还没有看到李世民和李玄霸，骑在马背上的李世民眼力非常好，已经看见了娘亲。
　　“娘！！”他腿一缩，居然站在了马背上。
　　长孙晟吓得不行：“小心，别摔着！”
　　李世民用天真地语气道：“有长孙将军在，我怎么会摔着？娘！看这里看这里！”
　　长孙晟叹了口气，只好双手护住他。
　　李渊低头问李玄霸：“二郎是怎么从一群带着冪离的人中认出他娘？”
　　他现在每日都把李玄霸抓出来骑马，李玄霸又被“捆”在了他身前。
　　李玄霸有气无力道：“我怎么知道？大概二哥有一双鹰一样的眼睛吧。”
　　李渊笑道：“鹰一样的眼睛？正好适合射箭。”
　　李玄霸无语。他父亲究竟有多喜欢射箭？又对自己的射箭技术多自豪？怎么张口闭口就是射箭？
　　窦夫人见李世民居然站在了马背上，吓得花容失色。
　　“李、世、民！坐好！不准站在马背上！”窦夫人怒斥。
　　娘亲叫你的全名了，你就该老实了。
　　李世民乖乖坐好。
　　长孙晟忍俊不禁。
　　李渊勒马。窦夫人走上前与家人团聚。
　　然后，她就看到了李渊身前被毯子捆得严严实实，用表情向她求救的李玄霸。
　　窦夫人哭笑不得：“有你这么裹儿子？快放开！”
　　她伸出手，李渊先把小毯子解开后，才把李玄霸递给窦夫人。
　　窦夫人掂了掂儿子，眼圈一红：“瘦了，轻了好多。”
　　李玄霸摸了摸自己在龙舟上吃得太多，得了一场重病都没瘦下来的下巴。
　　他的尖下巴终于有点肉了，怎么可能瘦了轻了？
　　算了，母亲说他瘦了轻了，他就瘦了轻了。
　　窦夫人把李玄霸放地上后，李世民伸展双臂，甜甜黏黏地叫道：“娘娘，我也瘦了，我好想娘娘，娘娘抱抱！”
　　窦夫人笑着把李世民抱起来，然后笑容一僵，手臂一沉，差点没接住。
　　李渊正下马，见到这一幕，笑得差点滑倒。
　　他从窦夫人手中接住李世民，把李世民放地上，敲了敲李世民的脑袋道：“你也好意思说你瘦了？”
　　李世民不满道：“阿玄都瘦了，我当然也瘦了，哼。”
　　柴绍和长孙晟向窦夫人问候。
　　窦夫人惊讶：“居然是长孙将军。”
　　她赶紧回礼，然后悄悄看向李渊。
　　李渊给她使了一个眼神，又看向李世民。
　　夫妻二人眼神一交流，窦氏就明白了。
　　她笑道：“旅途劳顿，我就不打扰长孙将军与家人团聚了。过几日，我带二郎来拜见将军。”
　　长孙晟点了点头。他想了想，从马背上取下一把弓，递给了李世民。
　　李世民双手平举，差点没接住：“哇，好重！”
　　长孙晟道：“等你能拉开这张弓的时候，我就把女儿嫁给你。”
　　李世民把弓竖着放在地上，抱着弓道：“好！长孙将军你等着，我很快就能拉动！”
　　长孙晟笑了笑，与众人告辞。
　　他故意在城门口说出这句话。这句话应该很快就会传遍整个大兴城。比起特意宣扬长孙家和唐国公府的口头婚约，这样一句勉励后辈的话，显得更随意一些。
　　长孙晟的继室高夫人也亲自来迎接长孙晟。
　　她隔着冪离打量李世民，心头一梗。
　　我家观音婢还不到四岁，至于这么早定下？她心里有些怨念。但长孙晟已经当众说出这句话，就容不得她反对了。
　　她决定回去后，好好打探一下唐国公府的情况。
　　高夫人此次来迎接长孙晟，还带了还不到十一岁的儿子长孙无忌。
　　长孙晟另两个儿子有官职在身，正在当值；女儿观音婢年幼。此次都没有与高夫人同行。
　　长孙无忌已经十一岁，自然听懂了父亲的意思。
　　他不满地看向那个比他矮一个脑袋的幼童。
　　李世民给长孙无忌露出一个友好的笑容。
　　长孙无忌收回视线。不知道为什么，他看到这个笑容后，居然有些气不起来了。
　　算了，父母之命媒妁之言，幼童何辜。
　　李玄霸正在猜测高夫人牵着的孩子是不是长孙无忌。
　　在长孙无忌和二哥眼神“交锋”后，他就确定，这个被自家二哥一眼折服的人肯定是长孙无忌。
　　“阿玄，好重啊，帮我撑一会儿。”李玄霸正在走神，李世民小声求救。
　　李玄霸嫌弃地帮二哥扶住弓：【你撑不住就和父亲说，让父亲帮你拿。】
　　李世民小声道：“那多丢脸。”
　　李玄霸：【让我帮你一起撑着，就不丢脸？】
　　李世民道：“当然不丢脸。”
　　李玄霸无语。搞不懂二哥的脑回路。
　　还好李渊也注意到两个孩子艰难地撑着强弓的模样。
　　他笑着把强弓拿起来：“先归耶耶了。等二郎长大，耶耶再还给你。”
　　李世民道：“耶耶，你可不能偷偷用，把我的弓用坏了。”
　　李渊板着脸道：“谁会用你的弓！”
　　李世民哼哼：“那就不知道了，耶耶特别喜欢的东西，连陛下都不肯给。陛下之前还埋怨你。”
　　李渊疑惑：“陛下埋怨我什么？”
　　李世民道：“还能埋怨什么？陛下也喜欢骏马和猎鹰，耶耶你搜集骏马和猎鹰居然不送给陛下一份。我有什么好东西，都会立刻拿来和阿玄分享。”
　　李渊皱眉。
　　窦夫人微笑道：“郎君，先回去吧。”
　　她去和默默站在一旁的万氏打了声招呼，拉着万氏的手一起上了马车。
　　李玄霸道：“二哥，我们也回马车，我累了。”
　　“哦，好。”李世民跳上马车，对李玄霸伸出手，“来，我拉你上来。”
　　李世民和李玄霸也进了马车。
　　李渊沉思了一会儿，才翻身上马。
　　他想到了窦氏对他说的话。
　　他很自傲，又自诩与陛下少年时便在宫里结识，关系很好，不需要做谄媚的事。
　　现在听二儿子的话，陛下居然对他有怨？
　　陛下可能只是随口抱怨，但心里肯定还是有些不满自己没有送给他好马。
　　看来窦氏说得有些道理。亲戚也需要礼尚往来。
　　“唉，二郎说得对，关系越是好，越该分享好东西。”李渊摇了摇头，然后苦笑，“我居然被儿子提点了。”
　　他扬鞭。
　　该送什么马给表弟？唉，哪匹马都舍不得。心疼！
　　……
　　“嗯？李渊送来的？”杨广先是惊讶，继而笑道，“他怎么想着送我骏马？”
　　宦官将信递给杨广。
　　杨广拆开信后，忍不住对身边的萧皇后笑道：“你看看这李渊，我还以为他心机深沉，结果他是真憨直啊。”
　　萧皇后接过信一看，也不由笑了：“二郎有什么好东西就首先分享给三郎，确实友悌。”
　　杨广道：“李渊被儿子提点后，才想起来和朕分享心爱的骏马，他不如二郎。”
　　太子杨昭闻言，委婉地帮李渊说好话：“唐国公之前只想着君臣之别。他性格耿直，认为身为臣子不该向君王进献珍宝。被李二郎的话点醒后，唐国公才想起他还有一层父皇表亲的身份。这也是唐国公恪守尊卑礼仪的体现。”
　　得了骏马，心情很好的杨广道：“确实如此。他既然记起了表亲的身份，朕也该好好提拔这位表兄。他外放多年，也该征辟入朝了。”
　　萧皇后笑道：“确实该回来了。姨母年老，他留在朝中为官，也能好好照顾姨母。”
　　杨广想了想，道：“就任命为殿中少监吧。”
　　殿中少监虽然只是从四品上，但掌管皇帝的膳食、医药、冕服、马匹等，乃是亲信心腹方能担任的要职。
　　在场之人一听这个官职，就知道唐国公李渊已经得到了皇帝的信任，地位即将腾飞了。
　　杨昭眼睛一亮：“父皇，你要回大兴了？”
　　杨广犹豫了一下，道：“朕还要过些日子。”
　　隋文帝节俭，所以大兴城内的皇宫和园林都不太符合杨广的喜好，杨广还没在刚修好的东京玩够。
　　杨昭无奈。他本想劝谏，父皇登基第二年就离开大兴久久不回，朝中大臣也只能跟着东奔西跑，大兴都不像个都城了，许多勋贵心里都有些不满。
　　但见父皇现在心情正好，唐国公也好不容易才得了父皇的信任，他将劝谏忍了下来。
　　下次吧。
