Chapter 23: Unintentional Words Enlighten a Father

Yang Zhao and Li Yuan departed once more.
As they left, Li Yuan shot a glance at Li Shimin, signaling that he would deal with him upon their return.
Li Shimin sighed dejectedly, "Ah Xuan, every time you stir up trouble, I’m the one who gets the beating."
Li Xuanba replied, "I didn't stir up any trouble."
Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba with a resentful expression.
Li Xuanba shifted his gaze, feeling a pang of guilt, and said, "Do you want to hear a story? I’ll tell you one."
Li Shimin raised both hands, cheering softly, "Yay! You haven't told me a story in ages. Every time I ask, you’re always too lazy."
Li Xuanba said, "Stop blathering. Which one do you want to hear?"
Li Shimin answered without hesitation, "Journey to the West!"
Li Xuanba sighed inwardly. As expected, for a child, *Journey to the West* was still the most entertaining.
Naturally, he couldn't recall the original version of *Journey to the West* in its entirety, but telling a story didn't require memorizing the whole book. He could just piece together the eighty-one tribulations; it didn't even have to be the original ones. In any case, he had no intention of writing one of the Four Great Classical Novels; he was just telling it for fun.
However, ever since his Second Brother heard *Journey to the West*, he had become obsessed with practicing staff techniques, which gave Li Xuanba a massive headache.
If the future General of the Heavenly Strategy were to add a Golden Cudgel to his arsenal, it would be far too ridiculous.
"Hurry up, hurry up! Last time you stopped at the theft of the kasaya!" Li Shimin urged.
Li Xuanba frowned. Last time was the theft of the kasaya? Oh no, he couldn't remember the order anymore.
He racked his brain, recounting a few of the eighty-one tribulations he had already told.
...
Li Yuan didn't return until evening, reeking of alcohol.
Chai Shao arrived with him, not only smelling just as strongly of wine but also attempting to waft that scent toward Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.
Li Shimin shielded Li Xuanba behind him, firing a blunt toy arrow from his toy bow, which struck Chai Shao right in the belly.
Chai Shao let out an "Ouch!" and stopped in his tracks.
"Run, Ah Xuan!" Li Shimin first used his toy bow to swat away the arm Chai Shao had reached out, then grabbed Li Xuanba and bolted.
As Li Xuanba stumbled forward, he looked back at Chai Shao.
*Wow, my Second Brother learned how to swat people with a bow so early.*
Chai Shao rubbed his arm, aggrieved, "Father-in-law, Erlang is so fierce."
Li Yuan laughed heartily, "My son *should* be that fierce! Come, let's keep drinking!"
Chai Shao said, "Fine, let's keep drinking!"
The two draped their arms over each other's shoulders and continued their drinking bout.
Lady Wan, who followed Li Yuan to attend to his daily life, took one look at them. Worried that they would get drunk and come to disturb the children again, she had Li Shimin and Li Xuanba sleep in the room next to hers.
Lady Wan was a concubine of Li Yuan, hailing from the Wan clan of Jiangdu.
Her great-grandfather had been a high-ranking official in the Southern Qi, and her grandfather had been a high-ranking official in the Southern Liang. After the Sui Dynasty destroyed the Southern dynasties, Lady Wan’s father served as the Prefect of Lizhou for the Great Sui.
With such a background, she was certainly no ordinary concubine in the Duke’s mansion.
Dukes and third-rank officials were entitled to six *Ying* (secondary wives), who held the rank of Junior Seventh Grade. Lady Wan was one of these *Ying* and held a formal title. When Lady Dou was away, she could represent the women of the Duke’s mansion in social engagements.
Under Sui and Tang law, officials of the fifth rank and above were permitted to have *Ying*. A *Ying* was considered a secondary wife, whereas those below the rank of *Ying* were the "concubines" of common parlance, who were often treated as mere property.
Officials below the fifth rank and commoners were not qualified to have *Ying*, so the "secondary wives" they took were merely "concubines" that the head of the household could sell at will.
Old Madam Dugu was often bedridden, and Lady Dou had to stay at the ancestral home in Daxing to serve her mother-in-law and care for the children. Thus, Lady Wan stayed by Li Yuan’s side, attending to his daily needs and assisting him with social obligations among the women.
From his perspective as a person from the future, Li Xuanba had initially felt some hostility toward Lady Wan, always fearing there would be "household drama" between her and his mother.
After he grew a bit older and became more familiar with her, observing how she interacted with his mother, he realized that Lady Wan was also a pitiable person with a bitter heart.
When Lady Wan accompanied Li Yuan to serve in official posts away from home, the children she bore had to be left behind at the ancestral estate.
When she returned, her children wouldn't even recognize her. She could only wipe away her tears in silence, not daring to let Li Yuan or Old Madam Dugu find out; only Lady Dou would comfort her.
It wasn't until her children grew older and Lady Dou frequently spoke well of Lady Wan in front of them that they grew closer to her.
Lady Wan had once wondered if she could take turns with Lady Dou in accompanying Li Yuan on his postings, so they could rotate serving Old Madam Dugu. She had been scolded mercilessly by Old Madam Dugu, and her own family had written letters reprimanding her for disregarding propriety.
Although a secondary wife was not a mere concubine, she still could not overstep her bounds. When the primary wife was present, a secondary wife had no standing to serve the mother-in-law.
As a lady from a prominent official family, Lady Wan was scolded for lacking decorum even for wanting to serve her mother-in-law. After hearing this, Li Xuanba could no longer harbor any hostility toward her.
Because Lady Dou was very caring toward Lady Wan’s children, Lady Wan was also very kind to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.
Li Jiancheng, as the eldest legitimate son and being much older than his younger brothers, was quite distant from them and looked down upon his half-brothers. Lady Wan racked her brains to secretly curry favor with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.
She had injured her body giving birth to Li Zhiquan and found it difficult to conceive again. Aside from the eldest legitimate son, all the sons of the Duke’s mansion had to find their own way. Having brothers to support one another was certainly better than struggling alone. Moreover, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had shown extraordinary talent from a very young age, and their future prospects were surely bright.
Having been reprimanded by Old Madam Dugu and her own family several times, Lady Wan was now very observant of the rules. When Lady Dou was present, she would quietly shut herself in her room, not seeking to draw attention.
Only now that Lady Dou was in Daxing did she come out to look after Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.
Li Shimin liked Lady Wan very much and called her "Auntie."
Li Xuanba had been awkward a few times, but eventually followed suit and called her "Auntie." While he still wasn't close to her, he wasn't overly distant either, and would even tell her some amusing stories about their fifth brother.
Incidentally, Lady Wan’s son, Li Zhiquan, also called her "Auntie." Lady Dou was Li Zhiquan’s "Mother."
"Sigh, the Master is perfect in every way, except for his love of wine. Once he drinks too much, he loses all sense of proportion. Why is Young Master Chai the same?" Lady Wan complained softly while helping Li Shimin and Li Xuanba change out of their wine-soaked clothes. "Wine is no good thing; you mustn't drink too much."
Li Xuanba said, "I don't drink, and Second Brother drinks very little."
Li Shimin said, "Huh? I see Father and Big Brother both love to drink. When I grow up, I want to drink too!"
Li Xuanba said, "Drinking without restraint is a bad habit. You can have a little, but you must never get drunk."
Li Shimin’s eyes darted around, "We'll see."
Lady Wan chuckled, "You truly are father and son. Erlang, you haven't even tasted wine yet, and you're already fond of it."
Li Xuanba said with disdain, "Drink if you want, but if you ever dare to force-feed me alcohol in the future, I’ll beat you up."
Li Shimin waved his hands hurriedly, "Don't! If you beat me, I’d be worried you’d hurt yourself."
Lady Wan laughed incessantly.
Every time she saw these twins "arguing," she found them adorable.
After helping the two children change, Lady Wan said, "Erlang, Sanlang, the Lady mentioned that you wanted to do business? Auntie has some sources in the south; would you like me to help you sell some goods?"
Li Shimin didn't yet understand Lady Wan’s intention, but Li Xuanba knew immediately that Auntie Wan was trying to curry favor with them.
The "Jiangdu" of the Jiangdu Wan clan was the Yangzhou City of later generations. While the Wan clan’s foundation in the north was shallow, they possessed significant assets in Jiangdu.
In terms of later geographical divisions, Jiangdu belonged to the north of the Yangtze, but in the hearts of the people and the cultural sphere, Jiangdu was the most prosperous city in the south. The products of the south were all concentrated in Jiangdu.
Because Yang Guang loved the south, the powerful and influential in Daxing and the Eastern Capital also favored southern goods. With the support of the Jiangdu Wan clan, Li Xuanba and Li Shimin wouldn't have to worry about selling fresh southern goods in their cosmetics shop.
Li Xuanba said without hesitation, "Alright, I thank you, Auntie. If Second Brother and I succeed in our business, and once Little Five is a bit older, we’ll bring him along to learn arithmetic through the shop’s ledgers."
Lady Wan beamed, "I leave Wulang’s education to Erlang and Sanlang. If Wulang can learn even a fraction of your skills, Auntie will be at ease."
Li Shimin interjected, "Auntie, why do you have so little confidence in Little Five? Little Five is very well-behaved and sensible, and he’s diligent and eager to learn. Even before he could sit still, he was already holding a brush to practice writing on paper, and he even sleeps clutching his brush. Ah Xuan, Master Yu’s calligraphy is exceptional. How about we have Little Five study under Master Yu with us in the future?"
Li Xuanba looked at Lady Wan’s slightly nervous expression, sighed inwardly, and said, "Little Five is very diligent; Master Yu will surely agree."
Lady Wan’s fingers, which had been unconsciously twisting her hem, relaxed. She smiled, "Then I will trouble Erlang and Sanlang to provide the introduction."
Li Shimin patted his small chest with a thud, "Don't worry, Auntie, it’s a small matter."
Lady Wan chatted with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba for a while longer before returning to the room next door to sleep.
After closing the door, Lady Wan took out a piece of jewelry her son had once worn and sobbed silently for a while.
*It’s alright, it’s alright. Erlang and Sanlang are both good children. They remember my kindness and are willing to help their younger brother at such a young age. I hope Erlang and Sanlang gain even more favor from the Emperor and have a bright future.*
"I wonder if Wulang will have forgotten my face again by the time we return this time," Lady Wan whispered mournfully, her voice so low that even the personal maid keeping watch in the outer room couldn't hear her.
On the other side, Li Xuanba was pondering which *Journey to the West* stories he hadn't told yet, while explaining Lady Wan’s intentions to his Second Brother through his inner thoughts.
He had been telling *Journey to the West* all afternoon and truly couldn't remember how many tribulations Tang Seng had already passed.
Li Shimin lay on the bed, propping his head up with his hands, tilting his head and sighing, "Auntie thinks so much. Father and Mother certainly wouldn't mistreat Little Five; to think she’d go so far as to curry favor with us two children."
Li Xuanba: *She’s smart to do so.* Auntie Wan was being so cautious in currying favor with him and his Second Brother that he felt bad about ignoring the fate of Li Zhiyun.
Li Zhiyun was the current name of the child; although he had already been renamed, they were still accustomed to calling him by his old name as a nickname. They might change how they addressed him once Li Zhiyun received his courtesy name.
Li Shimin’s hands went numb, so he rolled over on the bed twice and said, "Auntie Wan is so cautious, she looks so pitiful. Let’s take even better care of Little Five. When we get home, we’ll teach him to read! We’ll give him lots and lots of homework! I’ll also teach him archery! No slacking off, rain or shine!"
Li Xuanba wanted to say something but stopped. Giving Little Five lots of homework and making him practice archery rain or shine—was this what he called "taking better care" of him? *I really thank you on Little Five’s behalf, Second Brother.*
"Alright, enough of these bothersome things. *Journey to the West*! *Journey to the West*!" Li Shimin clamored.
"Keep your voice down, I’m thinking," Li Xuanba said.
He continued to frown and rack his brain. *Which tribulations have I not told yet?*
*How troublesome.* Next time he told his Second Brother a story, he absolutely had to write down the plot points he had already covered to avoid this headache.
...
Five days later, Li Yuan finally set off again.
This time, the party included not only Chai Shao but also Zhangsun Sheng, who had just taken leave to visit his family.
Zhangsun Sheng and Li Yuan had made a verbal marriage agreement for their children. After thinking about it for a few days, he had asked the Emperor for leave to return home and handle the matter.
Li Xuanba thought Li Shimin would be nervous traveling with his future father-in-law, but it was only he, the bystander, who felt nervous; his Second Brother was completely at ease.
Li Yuan, Zhangsun Sheng, and Chai Shao were all on horseback. Li Shimin insisted on riding with Li Yuan, chatting incessantly with Zhangsun Sheng along the way.
Li Yuan, finding him annoying, tossed him onto Zhangsun Sheng’s horse.
Li Shimin sat in his future father-in-law’s arms with great familiarity, continuing to chatter away and ask Zhangsun Sheng about the Turks.
Li Yuan reached out to Li Xuanba, who was poking his head out of the carriage, "Sanlang, do you want to ride a horse?"
Li Xuanba shook his head vigorously and pulled his head back in.
He had never ridden a horse in his past life, and in this life, his health was poor, so he hadn't formally learned to ride. He had been curious about it once, and when Li Yuan said he would take him riding, he had gone.
Li Yuan had galloped with his son in his arms, only to find upon returning that his son’s two tender little legs had been rubbed raw and bloody.
Old Madam Dugu, a woman who usually doted on her son, had been seen by Li Xuanba for the first time raising her cane and beating Li Yuan until he was scurrying about in a panic.
Li Yuan complained, "Sanlang, you aren't still holding a grudge because I rubbed your legs raw last time, are you?"
Li Xuanba stared at Li Yuan in silence.
Li Yuan suddenly gave a mischievous grin, jumped from the horse onto the carriage, grabbed his son from under his arm, and climbed back onto the horse.
Li Xuanba’s eyes went wide with shock.
*Father, what kind of circus act are you playing? Don't you think this is dangerous?!*
Li Shimin covered his mouth with both hands, giggling.
"Whether you want to ride or not, you’re riding. How can a young master of our Tang Duke’s mansion not know how to ride a horse!" Li Yuan laughed, "Don't think about running, behave!"
Li Xuanba huddled in front of Li Yuan, casting a resentful glance at his father.
Seeing Li Xuanba’s look of a bullied child, Li Yuan laughed even more happily.
After Li Shimin had laughed enough behind his hands, he finally came to his brother’s rescue, "Father, Ah Xuan just recovered from his illness, don't bully him."
"It’s precisely because he just recovered that he needs to ride and exercise his body," Li Yuan spouted nonsense.
Lady Wan dared not stop Li Yuan, so she simply adjusted her *mili* (veil hat), leaned out, and handed Li Yuan a blanket, "Please, Master, shield Sanlang from the wind."
"Why be so delicate?" Although Li Yuan said this, he still wrapped Li Xuanba tightly in the small blanket.
Li Yuan wrapped Li Xuanba as if he were luggage, bundling him into a cylinder shape with only his head exposed.
Li Xuanba tried to move his arms. *Well, completely immobile.*
Li Shimin continued to cover his mouth with both hands, laughing until he was swaying back and forth, his head bumping into Zhangsun Sheng’s chest, causing him to yelp in pain.
Zhangsun Sheng rubbed his chest and said helplessly, "Your head is truly hard."
Li Shimin held his head and laughed, "Thank you for the compliment, General Zhangsun!"
Zhangsun Sheng: "...I wasn't complimenting you."
Li Shimin didn't care; he chose to believe General Zhangsun was complimenting him, and he hadn't heard the second half of the sentence!
Li Yuan looked down and smiled at Li Xuanba, "Is this better?"
Li Xuanba now found it difficult even to turn his head, "Father, are you wrapping me in a blanket? You’ve tied me up. When I get back, I’m going to complain to Grandmother and Mother that you’re bullying people."
Li Yuan laughed, "Go ahead and complain, do you think I’m afraid of you?"
To show he really wasn't afraid, Li Yuan raised his whip and began to sing.
Li Shimin clapped his hands to keep the beat, and even though he didn't know the lyrics or the tune, he joined in, singing gibberish at the top of his lungs.
Chai Shao, wanting to curry favor with his father-in-law, had originally joined in with a hearty song, but as he sang, he was led astray by Li Shimin’s off-key melody, and he scratched his head, not knowing how to continue.
Li Xuanba, wrapped so tightly he couldn't move a muscle, rolled his eyes continuously.
*So noisy, so noisy. It’s like demonic sounds invading my brain.*
Li Xuanba: "Father, Second Brother, it sounds terrible, shut up!"
Li Yuan and Li Shimin sang even louder at the top of their lungs.
Chai Shao thought for a moment, then decided to forget the tune and lyrics and just sing along randomly.
Zhangsun Sheng stroked his beard with a smile.
He was very fond of the harmonious and happy appearance of this father and his sons. If Guanyinbi were to marry into such a family, her future should be quite good.
...
After Lady Dou returned to Daxing, she was worried sick about Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.
Upon learning that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba would be returning to Daxing with Li Yuan, she would send people out of the city from time to time to inquire, her eyes filled with longing.
Finally, when she received the news that Li Yuan and the two children were returning, she couldn't wait for them to reach the mansion and went out wearing her *mili* to welcome them personally.
Before she even saw Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Li Shimin, who was on horseback, had excellent eyesight and had already spotted his mother.
"Mother!!" He retracted his legs and actually stood up on the horse’s back.
Zhangsun Sheng was terrified, "Careful, don't fall!"
Li Shimin said in an innocent tone, "With General Zhangsun here, how could I fall? Mother! Look here, look here!"
Zhangsun Sheng sighed, having no choice but to protect him with both hands.
Li Yuan looked down and asked Li Xuanba, "How did Erlang recognize his mother among a group of people wearing *mili*?"
He was now grabbing Li Xuanba to ride every day, and Li Xuanba was once again "tied" in front of him.
Li Xuanba said weakly, "How should I know? Perhaps Second Brother has eyes like a hawk."
Li Yuan laughed, "Eyes like a hawk? That’s perfect for archery."
Li Xuanba was speechless. *How much does my father love archery? And how proud is he of his own archery skills? Why is he talking about archery every other sentence?*
Seeing Li Shimin actually standing on the horse’s back, Lady Dou turned pale with fright.
"Li! Shi! Min! Sit down! You are not allowed to stand on the horse’s back!" Lady Dou scolded angrily.
*Mother called your full name, so you’d better behave.*
Li Shimin sat down obediently.
Zhangsun Sheng couldn't help but chuckle.
Li Yuan reined in his horse. Lady Dou walked forward to reunite with her family.
Then, she saw Li Xuanba, who was bundled tightly in a blanket in front of Li Yuan, using his facial expressions to beg for help.
Lady Dou was torn between laughter and tears, "Is that how you wrap a son? Let him go!"
She reached out, and Li Yuan unwrapped the small blanket before handing Li Xuanba to Lady Dou.
Lady Dou weighed her son in her arms, her eyes reddening, "You’ve lost weight, you’re so much lighter."
Li Xuanba touched his chin, which hadn't lost any weight despite him eating too much on the dragon boat and falling into a serious illness.
His pointed chin finally had a bit of flesh; how could he have lost weight?
*Forget it, if Mother says I’ve lost weight, then I’ve lost weight.*
After Lady Dou put Li Xuanba on the ground, Li Shimin stretched out his arms and called out sweetly and clingily, "Mother, I’ve lost weight too, I missed you so much, Mother, hug me!"
Lady Dou smiled and picked up Li Shimin, then her smile stiffened, her arms sank, and she almost failed to catch him.
Li Yuan was just dismounting when he saw this scene and laughed so hard he almost slipped.
He took Li Shimin from Lady Dou’s arms, put him on the ground, and tapped Li Shimin on the head, "You have the nerve to say you’ve lost weight?"
Li Shimin said with dissatisfaction, "Ah Xuan lost weight, so of course I lost weight too, hmph."
Chai Shao and Zhangsun Sheng greeted Lady Dou.
Lady Dou was surprised, "It’s actually General Zhangsun."
She hurriedly returned the greeting, then glanced quietly at Li Yuan.
Li Yuan shot her a look and then looked at Li Shimin.
After a brief exchange of glances between the husband and wife, Lady Dou understood.
She smiled, "The journey has been exhausting, so I won't disturb General Zhangsun’s reunion with his family. In a few days, I will bring Erlang to pay a visit to the General."
Zhangsun Sheng nodded. He thought for a moment, took a bow from his horse’s back, and handed it to Li Shimin.
Li Shimin held it with both hands, almost failing to catch it, "Wow, so heavy!"
Zhangsun Sheng said, "When you can draw this bow, I will marry my daughter to you."
Li Shimin stood the bow upright on the ground and hugged it, "Alright! General Zhangsun, just you wait, I’ll be able to draw it soon!"
Zhangsun Sheng smiled and took his leave of them.
He had deliberately said this at the city gate. This statement would likely spread throughout Daxing City very soon. Compared to explicitly proclaiming the verbal marriage agreement between the Zhangsun family and the Tang Duke’s mansion, such a remark of encouragement to a younger generation seemed more casual.
Zhangsun Sheng’s second wife, Lady Gao, had also come personally to welcome him.
She sized up Li Shimin from behind her *mili*, and a lump formed in her throat.
*My Guanyinbi isn't even four years old yet, is there a need to settle this so early?* She felt some resentment. But since Zhangsun Sheng had already said this in public, she could not oppose it.
She decided that after returning, she would thoroughly investigate the situation of the Tang Duke’s mansion.
Lady Gao had also brought her son, Zhangsun Wuji, who was not yet eleven, to welcome Zhangsun Sheng.
Zhangsun Sheng’s other two sons held official posts and were on duty; his daughter Guanyinbi was young. None of them had accompanied Lady Gao this time.
Zhangsun Wuji was already eleven, so he naturally understood his father’s meaning.
He looked with dissatisfaction at the young child who was a head shorter than him.
Li Shimin gave Zhangsun Wuji a friendly smile.
Zhangsun Wuji looked away. For some reason, after seeing that smile, he found he couldn't stay angry.
*Forget it, the commands of parents and the words of matchmakers—what fault does a young child have?*
Li Xuanba was guessing whether the child Lady Gao was holding was Zhangsun Wuji.
After the "clash" of gazes between his Second Brother and Zhangsun Wuji, he was certain that this person who had been won over by his Second Brother’s smile was definitely Zhangsun Wuji.
"Ah Xuan, it’s so heavy, help me hold it for a while." Li Xuanba was lost in thought when Li Shimin whispered a plea for help.
Li Xuanba helped his Second Brother support the bow with disdain: *If you can’t hold it, tell Father and let him hold it for you.*
Li Shimin whispered, "That would be so embarrassing."
Li Xuanba: *And letting me help you hold it isn't embarrassing?*
Li Shimin said, "Of course it’s not."
Li Xuanba was speechless. He couldn't understand his Second Brother’s train of thought.
Fortunately, Li Yuan also noticed the two children struggling to hold the heavy bow.
He smiled and picked up the bow, "I’ll keep it for now. When Erlang grows up, I’ll return it to you."
Li Shimin said, "Father, you mustn't use it secretly and break my bow."
Li Yuan said with a straight face, "Who would use your bow!"
Li Shimin hummed, "That’s hard to say. There are things you love dearly, Father, that you wouldn't even give to His Majesty. His Majesty even complained about you before."
Li Yuan was puzzled, "What did His Majesty complain about me for?"
Li Shimin said, "What else could it be? His Majesty also loves fine horses and hunting falcons, yet you collected fine horses and falcons and didn't even offer one to His Majesty. Whenever I have something good, I immediately share it with Ah Xuan."
Li Yuan frowned.
Lady Dou smiled, "Master, let’s go back first."
She went to greet Lady Wan, who was standing silently to the side, and took her hand as they boarded the carriage together.
Li Xuanba said, "Second Brother, let’s go back to the carriage too, I’m tired."
"Oh, alright." Li Shimin jumped into the carriage and reached out to Li Xuanba, "Come, I’ll pull you up."
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba also entered the carriage.
Li Yuan pondered for a while before mounting his horse.
He thought about what Lady Dou had said to him.
He was very proud and prided himself on having known the Emperor since they were both young in the palace, believing their relationship was good enough that he didn't need to engage in sycophancy.
Now, hearing his second son’s words, the Emperor actually had grievances against him?
The Emperor might have just been complaining casually, but he must certainly be dissatisfied that he hadn't presented him with good horses.
It seemed Lady Dou was right. Even relatives needed to exchange gifts.
"Sigh, Erlang is right. The better the relationship, the more one should share good things." Li Yuan shook his head, then gave a bitter smile, "I was actually enlightened by my son."
He cracked his whip.
*What horse should I send to my cousin? Sigh, I’m reluctant to part with any of them. My heart aches!*
...
"Hmm? Sent by Li Yuan?" Yang Guang was surprised at first, then smiled, "What made him think of sending me fine horses?"
The eunuch handed the letter to Yang Guang.
After Yang Guang opened the letter, he couldn't help but smile at Empress Xiao, who was beside him, "Look at this Li Yuan. I thought he was deep and calculating, but he’s truly simple and honest."
Empress Xiao took the letter and read it, and couldn't help but laugh, "Erlang shares whatever good things he has with Sanlang first; he is truly fraternal."
Yang Guang said, "It was only after being enlightened by his son that Li Yuan thought to share his beloved fine horses with Me. He is not as good as Erlang."
Upon hearing this, Crown Prince Yang Zhao spoke tactfully in Li Yuan’s defense, "The Duke of Tang was previously only thinking of the distinction between sovereign and subject. He has a straightforward character and believed that as a subject, he should not offer treasures to the monarch. After being enlightened by Li Erlang’s words, the Duke of Tang remembered that he also has the identity of being the Emperor’s cousin. This is also a reflection of the Duke of Tang’s adherence to the rites of hierarchy."
Having received the fine horses and being in a good mood, Yang Guang said, "That is indeed the case. Since he has remembered his identity as a cousin, I should also properly promote this cousin of mine. He has been posted away for many years; it is time to summon him to the capital."
Empress Xiao smiled, "He should indeed return. Aunt is old; if he serves as an official in the capital, he can also take good care of Aunt."
Yang Guang thought for a moment and said, "Appoint him as the Junior Chamberlain of the Palace."
Although the Junior Chamberlain of the Palace was only a position of the Upper Fourth Grade, it was in charge of the Emperor’s meals, medicine, ceremonial robes, and horses—a key position that could only be held by a trusted confidant.
Upon hearing this official title, everyone present knew that the Duke of Tang, Li Yuan, had gained the Emperor’s trust and his status was about to soar.
Yang Zhao’s eyes lit up, "Father, are you returning to Daxing?"
Yang Guang hesitated for a moment and said, "I still need to stay for a few more days."
Emperor Wen of Sui was frugal, so the imperial palace and gardens in Daxing City did not quite suit Yang Guang’s tastes, and Yang Guang hadn't had enough fun in the newly built Eastern Capital.
Yang Zhao was helpless. He had wanted to remonstrate, but his father had left Daxing in the second year of his reign and had not returned for a long time, and the officials in the capital had to run around with him, so Daxing didn't even look like a capital anymore, and many nobles were dissatisfied.
But seeing that his father was in a good mood and the Duke of Tang had finally gained his father’s trust, he held back his remonstrance.
*Next time, then.*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第24章 李二郎即将挨训
chunks.chineseText:
第24章 李二郎即将挨训

=
　　李玄霸一回家就懒了好几日。
　　他知道自己有很多事要做。
　　比如收了杨广这么多钱， 他可以推行自己的赚钱计划。
　　但李玄霸趴在床榻上，就算李世民再怎么晃他，他也念着“春眠不觉晓”， 不肯离开床榻。
　　他近几日吃了睡睡了吃， 就连看书都躺在榻上， 恨不得和床榻长在一起。
　　李渊和窦夫人心疼李玄霸之前重病一场，又长途跋涉，纵容李玄霸懒惰。
　　只有李世民锲而不舍地想把弟弟从床榻上拽起来。
　　李玄霸捂住耳朵。不听不听， 二哥念经。
　　李世民道：“我要去和长孙家的四郎玩耍。你真的不来？”
　　李玄霸翻身：“不去。你们玩耍就是射箭，蹴鞠。我累。”
　　李世民今日再次没能把李玄霸从床榻上挖起来，只能叹着气自己出门玩耍。
　　李玄霸打了个哈欠， 从床头摸来一本书，在背上垫了个软垫， 蠕动着支起上半身， 悠闲地看书。
　　看了一会儿，他听见门口窸窸窣窣的声音，还以为二哥回来了。定睛一看，居然是李智云在门口探头探脑。
　　“小五，什么事？”李玄霸放下书。
　　李智云迈动着小短腿， 麻利地蹬掉小布鞋，爬到李玄霸身旁：“三兄， 小五想听故事！”
　　李玄霸叹气：“好，今天想听什么？”
　　李智云道：“葫芦娃救到翁翁了吗！”
　　李玄霸道：“这个……我之前讲到哪了？”
　　李玄霸想了想，继续给李智云讲葫芦娃救爷爷， 去一个被抓一个的倒霉故事。
　　李玄霸给李世民讲故事的时候， 被万阿姨带着来找他们玩的李智云无意间听到。在万阿姨的鼓励下， 李智云就来找蹲在屋里不肯出门的李玄霸听故事了。
　　来了几次， 李智云发现三兄只是面部表情很冷淡，实际上很温和，很好说话，就彻底黏上了李玄霸。
　　李玄霸见讲故事这么有用，一拍脑袋，试图用故事去诱惑李元吉，把现在还小的李元吉拉拢到自己和二哥这边，说不定能帮母亲把李元吉的性格改好。
　　然后李玄霸被那个三岁熊孩子拿着木头剑追着打。
　　为了保护李智云，他吸引火力，没跑过三岁熊孩子，手臂上好大一块乌青。
　　因独孤老夫人和李渊对孩子都很溺爱，李元吉只挨了一顿训斥，李玄霸的小金库又赚了。李玄霸觉得不亏，没打算计较。
　　但李世民与新认识的好友长孙四郎玩耍回来后得知此事，趁着父母不注意，把李元吉按着狠揍了一顿，被关了好几日的禁闭。
　　李玄霸再次“收服”四弟失败。李元吉更讨厌他和李世民了。
　　他自我安慰，希望如母亲所言，等四弟再长大些，不靠本能行事，能懂得尊敬兄长的时候，自己再努力努力。
　　努力了之后还没有结果，他的良心就不会痛了。
　　这叫“免责”。
　　李玄霸和李智云讲了一会儿故事，故意停在五娃也被抓走处，后事如何，请听下回分解。
　　没有什么比断章更有意思。
　　李智云有些不高兴。但他脾气随了亲生母亲，不高兴也只是低下头用脑袋轻轻拱了拱李玄霸，就像是一只小狗狗。
　　李玄霸摸了摸小狗狗弟弟的脑袋：“如果你能坚持描完一张大字，我就给你讲六娃的故事。”
　　李智云噘嘴：“就一张大字，我很快描好。娘亲说，三兄也要写字。三兄今日的字完成了吗？”
　　李玄霸沉默。
　　你一个三岁小孩不仅口齿伶俐逻辑清晰，还会督促哥哥写作业？是不是过分聪明了些？我们李家专出早熟的天才吗？
　　“好吧，一起。”李玄霸叹了口气，慢吞吞往床榻下爬。
　　李智云跟在李玄霸身后往床榻下爬，就像是一只半大的狗狗身后跟着一只小奶狗：“三兄，你拜了虞先生那么厉害的老师，要努力啊。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“好了好了，别催了。”
　　爬下床榻后，李智云熟练且殷勤地帮李玄霸研墨。
　　他自接触写字后，就对写好字特别痴迷。虽然现在他的手腕没有力，还不能好好练字，但他每日仍旧努力用画画的方式描红文字。
　　李玄霸一手楷书相比同龄人，写得相当漂亮。
　　李玄霸从不认为自己是什么天才。他看着像天才，不过是凭借成年人的逻辑和毅力，能够做一些坚持就能获得成绩的功利的事。
　　比如练字。
　　他知道书法是这个时代文人的“脸面”。虽然他估计当不了什么书法家，但只要从小苦练，练一手漂亮的毛笔字问题还是不大。
　　自魏晋后，楷书逐渐发展，是现在最流行的字体之一，将在唐朝发展到鼎盛。
　　李玄霸的字其实不能算是现在流行的模仿魏碑的正楷，而是带了些行楷的笔锋。
　　他在现代虽没练过毛笔字，但一手行楷钢笔字很漂亮。硬笔书法和毛笔书法差别很大，字的结构却可以触类旁通。他曾经习惯写行楷，现在写毛笔字也不由往行楷上靠了。
　　当然，李玄霸的正楷写着写着就偏向行楷，主要还是因为行楷书写速度更快。
　　李玄霸第一次写行楷，是帮因顽皮受罚的二哥抄《孝经》。
　　这种罚抄，敷衍一下就行了，不用把字写得多好。
　　没想到窦夫人看到了李玄霸的字后，就求了朝中许多正楷书法名家的字帖给李玄霸学习。李玄霸每日把这些字帖摹写一次后，再按照他自己的习惯写一篇“风格飘逸”的楷书。
　　李玄霸拜虞世南为习字老师后，虞世南看到了李玄霸的字，很巧地也用了窦夫人教导李玄霸的方式教授李玄霸。
　　李智云对漂亮的书法有一种与生俱来的喜爱。
　　他被亲生母亲带着和李玄霸混熟后，就爱催李玄霸完成练字功课，趴在矮桌上看李玄霸写字。
　　人非圣贤，孰能不虚荣。李玄霸看着弟弟的崇拜的狗狗眼，心里很受用，练字的烦躁都被抚平了。
　　现在他故意每日“偷懒”，等李智云来催他练字。等写完字后，李玄霸就把着李智云的手，教他在字帖上涂红。
　　窦夫人和万阿姨先后来看了一次，都面带慈祥笑容离开，没有打扰两个孩子练字。
　　只有李渊有些惆怅：“四郎也该练字了。”
　　窦夫人道：“四郎在郎君面前很乖巧，或许郎君可以亲自教导四郎练字？”
　　李渊想了想李元吉那坐不住的模样，还没开始教李元吉，就已经头疼：“还是让毗沙门去教吧，也能增进兄弟感情。”
　　窦夫人劝说道：“大郎已经被陛下授予宫廷官职，需要每日当值，实在是无空。且大郎以后和四郎相处的时间很多，郎君与四郎相处的时间却不多。四郎顽皮，还是郎君能管得住四郎。”
　　李元吉虽顽皮，但也聪慧，知道谁能欺负，谁不能欺负。
　　比如李世民揍了李元吉好几次后，李元吉虽然会在背后悄悄吐李世民的口水，但不敢当着李世民的面嚣张。
　　但李玄霸只要一凑近李元吉，李元吉就会狠狠欺负这个打不过他的病弱哥哥。
　　窦夫人猜测，四郎每次都要欺负三郎，也有二郎把四郎揍得太狠，所以四郎要找与二郎长得极像的三郎“报仇”的缘故。
　　李渊长得十分高大，又有“父亲”这个被李元吉身边伺候的仆人过度美化的身份。李元吉在李渊面前很听话。
　　因独孤老夫人拦着，窦夫人不能亲自教导李元吉。
　　现在李渊休假在家，窦夫人就想让李渊管管。
　　经过窦夫人几度劝说后，李渊终于克服了心中教导熊孩子的恐惧，硬着头皮去管教李元吉了。
　　李元吉之后几乎每天都挨了揍。
　　独孤老夫人心疼极了。但儿子好不容易回家教育一次孩子，她不能打消儿子的积极性，只能抱怨窦夫人不能阻拦李渊。
　　窦夫人赔着笑，连说自己没用，劝不住丈夫，敷衍过去。
　　李世民听说父亲每日都要揍李元吉一次，高兴得都不出门玩耍了。
　　李玄霸练字，他揽下了李玄霸之后要做的“工作”，握着李智云的手，教李智云描红。
　　“太好了，我早就和娘娘说，多揍李元吉几次，他就老实了。”李世民兴奋道。
　　李智云缩了缩脑袋：“小五很乖，别揍小五。”
　　李世民道：“我知道你很乖，别怕，你看二兄我像胡乱揍弟弟的人吗？”
　　李智云看向李玄霸。
　　李玄霸道：“是的，他就是。”
　　李智云脑袋又一缩。
　　李世民笑骂道：“阿玄，你是不是找揍？”
　　李玄霸道：“看，他就是胡乱揍弟弟。”
　　李智云小声道：“二兄，不要欺负三兄，你欺负三兄，我就向娘亲告状。”
　　李世民无语：“你还真听他胡扯。阿玄，赶紧解释，小心小五真的以为我欺负你。”
　　李玄霸失笑：“小五，我逗你的。二兄很好，不会欺负弟弟。你二兄打架特别厉害，之后谁欺负你，你就找二兄帮你揍回去。”
　　李世民道：“这个完全没问题。”
　　李智云点头：“好。”
　　李渊从窗户离开，摸了摸胸口。
　　他被李元吉伤害后，总会来这里看看其他三个小儿子。
　　治愈了治愈了，他又可以教导李元吉看书习字了。
　　悠闲的日子如此度过了一旬。
　　这期间李渊和窦夫人带李世民去拜访了长孙家。双方合了八字，正式把这个口头上的婚约定下来。
　　待长孙小娘六岁时，她和李世民就会交换庚帖，缔结婚约。
　　因长孙小娘还年幼，李世民没有见到长孙小娘，只是常常去找长孙无忌玩，顺便在长孙晟处学弓箭和突厥语。
　　李玄霸没有跟着去。
　　他一是懒，二是觉得二哥相看未来媳妇，自己去凑热闹实在是不合适。
　　之后李世民去长孙府玩耍时，李玄霸也能推就推。
　　他相信长孙小娘虽然还小，但高夫人肯定也会带着小小的长孙小娘，在李世民看不到的地方，悄悄观察李世民。
　　虽然三岁孩童说不上什么爱情，但能提前混些眼熟，多些好感，从青梅竹马发展到新婚小夫妻，总比盲婚哑嫁强。
　　只一旬时间，李世民已经完全和长孙无忌混熟了。
　　长孙无忌再不提李世民的年龄。一个十一岁的少年郎，居然能和一个七岁的孩童玩得很开心，连昔日的朋友都忘在了脑后。
　　李玄霸真不知道该怎么评价这件事。他把这件事记在了日记本中，以后用作《隋唐演义》的素材。
　　一旬后，李渊和长孙晟都准备回各自的岗位继续工作时，皇帝的圣旨来了。
　　李渊被征辟入朝，长孙晟则被允许在家中多休息一会儿。
　　现在突厥很安分，皇帝又准备在洛阳多玩耍一段时间，用不上长孙晟护卫，所以就很慷慨地多给了长孙晟一些假期。
　　长孙晟年纪也不小了，又常年在突厥吃风沙。杨广在太子杨昭的劝说下，下旨给长孙晟，让长孙晟好好休养身体。
　　杨广已经规划好了自己的雄主之路。
　　他首先要征讨高句丽。等高句丽投降后，他就要去完成先帝未竟的事业，征服突厥。
　　长孙晟是最了解突厥的人。杨广希望他征服突厥时，长孙晟还能为他所用。
　　长孙晟忙碌了一辈子，现在终于有时间和家人相处，教养儿女，心里很是高兴。他特意让疏于管教的嫡长子长孙安业请假回家，天天盯着长孙安业重新读书习武。
　　长孙晟有四个儿子。庶长子长孙行布两年前死于汉王杨谅叛乱，长孙行布的同母弟因此得封鹰扬郎将。长孙安业是原配所生。长孙无忌是继室高氏所生。
　　长孙晟原配在世的时候，因只有长孙安业这个儿子，对其非常娇纵。长孙晟又常年在塞外，不能教导儿子。
　　现在他难得有空闲，发现儿子居然变成了一个嗜酒如命的纨绔子弟，气得差点晕过去。
　　他的兄长长孙炽得知此事的时候，特意写信来嘲笑他。
　　长孙晟的原配来信中总说长孙安业很优秀。高氏身为继室不敢管教和得罪长孙安业，也常对长孙晟说家中一切安好。
　　长孙炽看不惯长孙安业。但长孙晟常年来只有长孙安业一个嫡子，又对已故原配心存怀念，所以一直以为长孙安业虽然有些纨绔的习性，但在勋贵二代中很常见，算不得什么。
　　远香近臭。现在长孙晟忍不了这个“不算什么”的纨绔儿子了。
　　李玄霸从李世民口中听到了这个“笑话”。
　　虽然长孙安业也是李世民的大舅哥，但李世民对围观这位大舅哥被揍好像特别有兴趣，常去看热闹，还会煽风点火。
　　李玄霸不由捂脸：“你就不怕他恨上你？”
　　李世民长大他无辜的大眼睛：“怎么可能？我只是一个孩童！”
　　我，李世民，七岁孩童，能有什么坏心眼？
　　“行吧。”李玄霸也没当回事。反正最后长孙安业顶多又来一次叛乱，然后被流放。吃亏的又不是自家二哥。
　　“该动起来了。”李玄霸见父亲居然比原本历史中早几年得到殿中少监的官职，自己的蝴蝶翅膀似乎再次有了作用，因春困而懒惰的心稍稍振作了一些。
　　再不振作，阿姊都要嫁人了。
　　想到阿姊嫁人，李玄霸心中不由出现一些烦闷。
　　李世民不再出门疯玩，除了失去了去长孙府玩耍的新鲜感之外，也和三姐即将嫁人，心情烦闷有关。
　　两个孩子因为姐姐嫁人生闷气。窦夫人察觉后，让蹲在家里绣嫁妆的李三娘带着李世民和李玄霸出门透透气。
　　李三娘高兴得眼泪都要流出来了。
　　她被关在小院里不准出门，快憋坏了！
　　“二郎，三郎，你们想去哪里玩？阿姊陪你们玩个够！”李三娘挨个抱抱两个弟弟，感激极了。
　　李世民道：“听阿玄的。阿玄终于要开始他的赚钱计划。”
　　李玄霸道：“阿姊陪我去书店印佛经的工坊，我想印点其他书籍。”
　　李三娘牵着两个弟弟上马车：“印什么？你从陛下那里得了新的佛经？”
　　李玄霸摇头，道：“印儒经。”
　　李三娘惊讶：“三郎，儒经可不能印。儒经是要抄的！”
　　李玄霸道：“现在天下安定，天下富足，读书人逐渐多了起来。我已经征询了高先生和宇文先生的意见，他们同意将自家注释的儒经印刷后，低价卖给寒门士子，以振兴儒学。”
　　李玄霸对李三娘乖巧地笑了笑，道：“将来长兄肯定会与世家大族交好，我和二哥不好再与世家大族的士子多交往，以免分了长兄人脉，引得长兄不满。我从陛下那里听闻今年会增开‘进士’一科选士，将来我想走‘进士’之路当官。”
　　李世民补充道：“我将来能去打突厥赚个爵位，但阿玄肯定是上不了战场的。只以荫蔽当官仰人鼻息，不如自己考个官来做。寒门士子想做官，除了投效高门士族之外，应该也是走阿玄选的这条路。所以阿玄想提前在寒门士子中积攒人脉。”
　　李三娘认真听完后，叹气道：“你们也太早熟了，想得真多真远。”
　　李世民挺起胸脯，骄傲道：“我和阿玄都伴驾南巡过了，当然很厉害！”
　　李三娘笑道：“确实如此。不过阿玄，现在朝中诸公都看不起寒门士子，勋贵人家也不愿意结交寒门士子。你身为唐国公府的公子，若是与寒门士子走得太近，会被人鄙夷。”
　　李玄霸道：“我知道。现在朝中以荫蔽做官为尊，通过明经等考试做官入朝后就先低人一等。”
　　现在的科举不仅需要五品以上官员推荐才有考试资格，科举做官者还饱受歧视。
　　到了唐朝，高门士族仍旧看不起科举晋身的官员。
　　“但我就想考试，和天下读书人比一比。”李玄霸脸上浮现出连双生哥哥都看不懂的表情，“我就想考一次。”
　　李三娘看着李玄霸的表情，虽然不懂，却没来由地心头发酸。
　　她立刻道：“三郎想考就考！寒门士子不一定不如高门士子。三郎和天下寒门士子比一比学识，那是多么畅快的一件事！阿姊支持你！”
　　李世民也道：“哥哥也支持你，阿玄想做什么就做什么！”
　　李玄霸点头：“嗯。”
　　李三娘道：“走，我们现在就去印儒经卖！如果卖不出去，阿姊给你们贴钱！阿姊的嫁妆可丰厚了！”
　　李玄霸失笑：“哪能用到阿姊的嫁妆。放心，阿姊，在儒林士子中，高先生和宇文先生的名声可响亮了，卖他们注释的四书五经不可能没人买。再者，我也不仅卖四书五经。我还想卖一些小说话本。”
　　李世民得意道：“阿姊，你不知道阿玄有多会讲故事。他的故事书肯定很好卖！”
　　李三娘道：“三郎想印什么就印！赚钱我们分，亏欠算阿姊的！不可以推脱，就这么定了！”
　　李玄霸和李世民对视一眼，在李三娘的眼神“威慑”下，只好拱手道谢：“那就谢过阿姊了。”
　　李三娘笑道：“这就对了！要多依靠阿姊啊！”
　　她揉乱了李玄霸和李世民的小揪揪，又帮两人把小揪揪重新绑好。
　　“走！我们印新书去！”
　　“嗯好！”
　　姐弟三人来到了西市书店后面的雕版印刷工坊，见到了早就等候在此的柴绍。
　　柴绍：傻笑。
　　李世民和李玄霸脸上的笑容同时消失。
　　李世民死鱼眼：“我记得成婚前，男子女子不能见面？”
　　李玄霸死鱼眼：“我也记得。”
　　柴绍立刻道：“只是偶遇，偶遇！”
　　他搓手手：“既然偶遇了，我给几位当护卫？”
　　“咳，柴备身，你能不能别笑这么……这么不雅。”一个胖乎乎的青年从一旁走出来。
　　李世民和李玄霸惊讶，立刻就要拜。
　　青年摆摆手制止：“我跟着嗣昌，来看看表弟的书店，表弟不会不欢迎表兄我吧？”
　　李世民和李玄霸皆露出了苦脸：“不敢，欢迎表兄。”
　　表兄？李三娘沉思了一会儿，打量着青年的体形，恍然道：“难道是……”
　　她隔着冪离瞪了柴绍一眼，徐徐拜道：“表兄安好。”
　　这个青年正是太子杨昭。
　　杨昭温和道：“表妹好。”
　　李世民心大，被吓了一跳之后，见太子表兄还是一如既往温和好相处，就变得自在起来。
　　“表兄，你不是在东京吗？怎么回来了？”李世民好奇道。
　　杨昭对李玄霸眨了一下眼睛，道：“这就要问你弟弟了。”
　　李玄霸指着自己：“我。”
　　杨昭笑而不语。
　　李玄霸眼睛睁大。难道是他让太子若遇到杨广让他回大兴，就不要犹豫，立刻回来？
　　等等，这件事不是发生在七月吗？现在才四月！
　　难道杨广在七月之前，也曾让杨昭回大兴，只是杨昭说要在洛阳多待一会儿，杨广就让杨昭又多待了三个月？
　　这确实极有可能。
　　杨昭道：“父亲让我回大兴，我想着正好回来喝嗣昌的喜酒，就回来了。高公和宇文公听闻你要印儒经，也和父亲请了假，过几日应当就会回来。”
　　李世民惊讶道：“啊？二位老师也要回来了？惨了惨了，阿玄我惨了！”
　　李世民立刻露出了一个哭丧脸。
　　杨昭好奇：“二郎，你怎么了？不高兴老师回来？”
　　李玄霸沉沉地叹了口气，虽然语调很悲痛，但嘴角的笑容怎么也压不下去：“这个啊，我和二哥在回大兴前，老师布置了很多功课。二哥回来后认识了长孙四郎这个新朋友，每日都在外面疯玩，功课就……”
　　李玄霸摊手，耸肩：“表兄，你懂的。”
　　“啊！”李世民抱着脑袋使劲甩头，“完了，完了，我完了！”
　　杨昭看着满脸崩溃神情的李世民，又看向满脸幸灾乐祸笑容的李玄霸，忍俊不禁道：“好吧，我懂。二郎，咳，节哀。”
　　高公和宇文公可严厉了，李二郎惨了。

Chapter 24: Li Erlang's Impending Scolding

Once Li Xuanba returned home, he indulged in laziness for several days.

He knew he had many things to do.

For instance, having received so much money from Yang Guang, he could launch his wealth-generating plans.

Yet, Li Xuanba remained sprawled on his couch. No matter how much Li Shimin shook him, he merely mumbled, "In spring one sleeps, unaware of dawn," refusing to budge.

Over the past few days, his routine consisted solely of eating and sleeping. Even when reading, he lay flat on his back, wishing he could fuse with the couch.

Li Yuan and Lady Dou, aching with sympathy over Li Xuanba's recent severe illness and arduous journey, indulged his indolence.

Only Li Shimin remained relentless, constantly trying to drag his younger brother out of bed.

Li Xuanba covered his ears. *I'm not listening, I'm not listening. Second Brother is just chanting scriptures.*

"I'm going to play with the Fourth Young Master of the Zhangsun family," Li Shimin said. "Are you really not coming?"

Li Xuanba rolled over. "No. Your idea of playing is just archery and cuju. I'm tired."

Having failed once again to dig Li Xuanba out of bed, Li Shimin could only sigh and head out to play on his own.

Li Xuanba yawned, reached for a book from the head of the bed, propped a soft cushion behind his back, wriggled his upper body into a semi-upright position, and leisurely began to read.

After reading for a while, he heard a rustling sound at the door. Thinking his second brother had returned, he focused his gaze, only to see Li Zhiyun poking his head in.

"Little Fifth, what is it?" Li Xuanba put down his book.

Li Zhiyun took quick strides with his short little legs, nimbly kicked off his small cloth shoes, and scrambled up beside Li Xuanba. "Third Brother, Little Fifth wants to hear a story!"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Alright. What do you want to hear today?"

"Did the Calabash Brothers rescue Grandpa?" Li Zhiyun asked.

"That..." Li Xuanba pondered. "Where did I leave off?"

After a moment's thought, Li Xuanba resumed telling Li Zhiyun the unfortunate tale of the Calabash Brothers rescuing their grandfather, where they went in one by one only to get captured one after another.

When Li Xuanba had been telling stories to Li Shimin, Li Zhiyun—who had been brought over by Auntie Wan to play—had overheard by chance. Encouraged by Auntie Wan, Li Zhiyun began visiting Li Xuanba, who refused to leave his room, just to listen to stories.

After a few visits, Li Zhiyun realized that while his Third Brother looked cold and expressionless, he was actually very gentle and easygoing. From then on, he became completely attached to Li Xuanba.

Seeing how effective storytelling was, Li Xuanba had a sudden inspiration. He tried to use stories to entice Li Yuanji, hoping to win over the still-young Fourth Brother to his and Li Shimin's side. Perhaps, he thought, he could help their mother correct Li Yuanji's temperament.

Instead, Li Xuanba was chased and beaten by that three-year-old brat wielding a wooden sword.

To protect Li Zhiyun, he had drawn the brat's fire. Unable to outrun a three-year-old, he ended up with a massive bruise on his arm.

Because Old Madame Dugu and Li Yuan doted heavily on the children, Li Yuanji only received a mild scolding, while Li Xuanba's personal coffers grew richer from the compensation. Li Xuanba felt it was a fair trade and had no intention of holding a grudge.

However, when Li Shimin returned from playing with his new friend, the Fourth Young Master Zhangsun, and learned of this, he seized a moment when their parents weren't looking, pinned Li Yuanji down, and gave him a severe thrashing. As a result, Li Shimin was placed in solitary confinement for several days.

Li Xuanba's attempt to "win over" his fourth brother had failed once again. Li Yuanji now detested him and Li Shimin even more.

He comforted himself with the hope that, as their mother said, once their fourth brother grew a bit older, stopped acting on pure instinct, and learned to respect his elders, he could try again.

If he made the effort and still achieved no results, at least his conscience would be clear.

This was what he called a "liability waiver."

Li Xuanba told the story to Li Zhiyun for a while, deliberately stopping right when the Fifth Calabash Brother was captured. *To find out what happens next, tune in to the next chapter.*

Nothing was more satisfying than a good cliffhanger.

Li Zhiyun was a bit displeased. But his temperament took after his birth mother; even when unhappy, he merely lowered his head and gently nudged Li Xuanba with his crown, looking just like a little puppy.

Li Xuanba patted his puppy-like younger brother's head. "If you can finish tracing one page of large characters, I will tell you the story of the Sixth Brother."

Li Zhiyun pouted. "Just one page? I'll finish tracing it in no time. Mother said Third Brother also needs to practice writing. Has Third Brother finished today's characters?"

Li Xuanba fell silent.

*You, a three-year-old child, are not only articulate and logical, but you're also supervising your older brother's homework? Isn't that a bit too clever? Does our Li family specialize in producing precocious geniuses?*

"Fine, let's do it together." Li Xuanba sighed, slowly crawling down from the couch.

Li Zhiyun followed closely behind him, crawling down like a tiny pup trailing a slightly larger dog. "Third Brother, you've taken such an amazing teacher as Mister Yu. You must work hard."

Li Xuanba sighed. "Alright, alright, stop nagging."

After climbing down, Li Zhiyun practiced and eagerly began grinding ink for Li Xuanba.

Ever since he was introduced to writing, he had been utterly obsessed with calligraphy. Although his wrists lacked the strength to practice properly, he still worked hard every day, tracing characters in red ink as if he were drawing.

Compared to his peers, Li Xuanba's regular script (Kaishu) was exceptionally beautiful.

Li Xuanba never considered himself a genius. He only appeared to be one because he possessed the logic and perseverance of an adult, allowing him to diligently pursue practical tasks that yielded results through sheer persistence.

Such as practicing calligraphy.

He knew that calligraphy was the "face" of a scholar in this era. Although he doubted he would ever become a master calligrapher, as long as he practiced diligently from childhood, writing beautifully with a brush would not be a problem.

Since the Wei and Jin dynasties, regular script had gradually developed into one of the most popular styles, and it would reach its zenith during the Tang Dynasty.

Li Xuanba's writing was not exactly the standard regular script that imitated the Wei Stele style popular at the time; instead, it carried the fluid strokes of running-regular script (Xingkai).

Although he had never practiced brush calligraphy in his modern life, his penmanship in running-regular script had been very beautiful. While hard-pen calligraphy differed greatly from brush calligraphy, the structural principles of the characters were transferable. Having been accustomed to writing running-regular script, his brushwork naturally leaned in that direction.

Of course, the main reason Li Xuanba's regular script drifted toward running-regular script was simply that running-regular script was faster to write.

The first time Li Xuanba wrote in running-regular script was to help his second brother, who was being punished for mischief, copy the *Classic of Filial Piety*.

For that kind of punitive copying, a perfunctory effort sufficed; there was no need to write beautifully.

To his surprise, when Lady Dou saw his writing, she sought out copybooks from many renowned masters of regular script in the imperial court for him to study. Every day, after tracing these copybooks once, Li Xuanba would write another piece in his own "elegant and fluid" style of regular script.

After Li Xuanba took Yu Shinan as his calligraphy teacher, Yu Shinan saw his writing and, by coincidence, adopted the exact same method as Lady Dou to instruct him.

Li Zhiyun possessed an innate love for beautiful calligraphy.

Once his birth mother brought him over and he grew close to Li Xuanba, he loved to urge Li Xuanba to finish his writing practice, leaning over the low table to watch him write.

Humans are not sages; who is entirely free of vanity? Looking at his younger brother's adoring, puppy-like eyes, Li Xuanba felt quite pleased, and the tediousness of practicing calligraphy was instantly smoothed away.

Now, he deliberately "slacked off" every day, waiting for Li Zhiyun to urge him to practice. Once he finished writing, Li Xuanba would hold Li Zhiyun's hand, teaching him how to trace the characters in red on the copybook.

Lady Dou and Auntie Wan both came to check on them at different times, leaving with gentle, warm smiles so as not to disturb the two children.

Only Li Yuan felt a bit melancholy. "Fourth Brother should also start practicing his writing."

Lady Dou said, "Fourth Brother is very obedient in your presence, Husband. Perhaps you could personally instruct him in calligraphy?"

Thinking of Li Yuanji's restless nature, Li Yuan already felt a headache coming on before he had even begun. "It is better to let Bishamen teach him. It will also foster brotherly affection."

Lady Dou advised, "Our eldest son has already been granted a court post by His Majesty and must attend duty daily; he truly has no spare time. Furthermore, our eldest son will have plenty of time to spend with Fourth Brother in the future, whereas your time with him is limited. Fourth Brother is mischievous; only you, Husband, can keep him in check."

Though Li Yuanji was mischievous, he was also clever. He knew exactly whom he could bully and whom he could not.

For instance, after Li Shimin beat him up several times, Li Yuanji might secretly spit behind Li Shimin's back, but he dared not act insolently to his face.

Yet, the moment Li Xuanba drew near, Li Yuanji would ruthlessly bully this sickly older brother who could not fight back.

Lady Dou suspected that Fourth Brother bullied Third Brother so relentlessly partly because Second Brother beat him too harshly, prompting Fourth Brother to seek "revenge" on Third Brother, who looked almost identical to Second Brother.

Li Yuan was very tall and imposing, and held the status of "Father"—an identity excessively glorified by the servants attending Li Yuanji. Thus, Li Yuanji was very obedient in front of Li Yuan.

Because Old Madame Dugu intervened, Lady Dou could not personally discipline Li Yuanji.

Now that Li Yuan was home on leave, Lady Dou wanted him to take charge.

After several rounds of persuasion from Lady Dou, Li Yuan finally overcame his inner dread of teaching a brat and braced himself to discipline Li Yuanji.

From then on, Li Yuanji was beaten almost every single day.

Old Madame Dugu was utterly heartbroken. However, since her son had finally returned home to educate his child, she could not dampen his enthusiasm. She could only complain that Lady Dou had failed to stop Li Yuan.

Lady Dou offered apologetic smiles, repeatedly claiming she was useless and could not sway her husband, brushing the matter aside.

Upon hearing that their father thrashed Li Yuanji daily, Li Shimin was so delighted that he stopped going out to play.

While Li Xuanba practiced his calligraphy, Li Shimin took over the "task" Li Xuanba was supposed to do next, holding Li Zhiyun's hand and teaching him how to trace the characters.

"Wonderful! I told Mother long ago that if we beat Li Yuanji a few more times, he would behave," Li Shimin said excitedly.

Li Zhiyun shrank back his head. "Little Fifth is very good. Don't beat Little Fifth."

"I know you are good. Don't be afraid," Li Shimin said. "Do you think your Second Brother looks like someone who beats his younger brothers without reason?"

Li Zhiyun looked at Li Xuanba.

"Yes, he is," Li Xuanba replied.

Li Zhiyun shrank his head back again.

Li Shimin laughed and scolded, "Ah Xuan, are you looking for a beating?"

Li Xuanba said, "See? He beats his younger brothers without reason."

Li Zhiyun whispered, "Second Brother, don't bully Third Brother. If you bully Third Brother, I will tell Mother."

Li Shimin was speechless. "You actually believe his nonsense. Ah Xuan, explain quickly, or Little Fifth will really think I'm bullying you."

Li Xuanba chuckled. "Little Fifth, I was only teasing. Second Brother is very good; he won't bully his younger brothers. Your Second Brother is exceptionally good at fighting. If anyone bullies you in the future, just ask Second Brother to beat them up for you."

"That is absolutely not a problem," Li Shimin declared.

Li Zhiyun nodded. "Alright."

Li Yuan walked away from the window, patting his chest.

Whenever he was exasperated by Li Yuanji, he would always come here to look at his other three young sons.

*Healed, completely healed. Now I can go back to teaching Li Yuanji how to read and write.*

Ten days passed in this leisurely manner.

During this time, Li Yuan and Lady Dou took Li Shimin to visit the Zhangsun family. The two families compared the children's eight characters of birth and formally finalized the verbal betrothal.

When the young lady of the Zhangsun family turned six, she and Li Shimin would exchange their birth charts and formally seal the marriage contract.

Because the young lady of the Zhangsun family was still very young, Li Shimin did not meet her. He merely went to play with Zhangsun Wuji frequently, taking the opportunity to learn archery and the Turkic language from Zhangsun Sheng.

Li Xuanba did not tag along.

Firstly, he was lazy; secondly, he felt it was highly inappropriate for him to tag along when his second brother was visiting his future wife's family.

Afterwards, whenever Li Shimin went to play at the Zhangsun estate, Li Xuanba declined whenever possible.

He believed that although the young lady of the Zhangsun family was still small, Madame Gao would surely bring her along to secretly observe Li Shimin from a place where he could not see.

Although one could hardly speak of love regarding a three-year-old child, becoming familiar early on and fostering some goodwill to transition from childhood playmates to newlyweds was far better than a blind marriage.

In just ten days, Li Shimin had become completely familiar with Zhangsun Wuji.

Zhangsun Wuji no longer brought up Li Shimin's age. An eleven-year-old youth was actually having a wonderful time playing with a seven-year-old child, completely forgetting his former friends.

Li Xuanba truly did not know how to evaluate this. He recorded it in his diary, intending to use it as material for the *Romance of the Sui and Tang Dynasties* in the future.

Ten days later, just as Li Yuan and Zhangsun Sheng were preparing to return to their respective posts, an imperial decree arrived.

Li Yuan was summoned to court, while Zhangsun Sheng was permitted to rest at home a while longer.

Currently, the Turks were behaving themselves, and the Emperor planned to enjoy himself in Luoyang for a while longer. With no need for Zhangsun Sheng's protection, he generously granted him an extended leave.

Zhangsun Sheng was no longer young, and he had spent years enduring the wind and sand of the Turkic lands. At the persuasion of Crown Prince Yang Zhao, Yang Guang issued a decree to Zhangsun Sheng, telling him to recuperate well.

Yang Guang had already mapped out his path to becoming a great sovereign.

First, he would launch a campaign against Goguryeo. Once Goguryeo surrendered, he would complete the unfinished business of the late Emperor and conquer the Turks.

Zhangsun Sheng was the person who understood the Turks best. Yang Guang hoped that when the time came to conquer them, Zhangsun Sheng would still be available for his service.

Having been busy his entire life, Zhangsun Sheng was delighted to finally have time to spend with his family and raise his children. He specifically ordered his neglected eldest legitimate son, Zhangsun Anye, to take leave and return home, keeping a daily eye on him to resume his studies and martial arts training.

Zhangsun Sheng had four sons. His eldest concubine-born son, Zhangsun Xingbu, had died two years prior during the rebellion of Yang Liang, the Prince of Han; Xingbu's full brother had consequently been appointed as a General of the Soaring Eagles. Zhangsun Anye was born of his first wife, while Zhangsun Wuji was born of his second wife, Lady Gao.

When Zhangsun Sheng's first wife was alive, she had excessively spoiled Zhangsun Anye, as he was her only son. Furthermore, Zhangsun Sheng was stationed beyond the border for years and could not discipline him.

Now that he finally had some leisure time, he discovered that his son had turned into an alcoholic, profligate playboy, infuriating him to the point of nearly fainting.

When his elder brother, Zhangsun Chi, learned of this, he specifically wrote a letter to mock him.

In her letters, Zhangsun Sheng's first wife had always claimed that Zhangsun Anye was excellent. As a stepmother, Lady Gao did not dare to discipline or offend Zhangsun Anye, so she also frequently told Zhangsun Sheng that all was well at home.

Zhangsun Chi could not stand Zhangsun Anye. However, for many years, Zhangsun Sheng had only this one legitimate son, and out of nostalgia for his deceased first wife, he had always assumed that while Zhangsun Anye had some playboy habits, they were common among the second generation of nobility and of little consequence.

Distance lends enchantment, but familiarity breeds contempt. Now, Zhangsun Sheng could no longer tolerate this "inconsequential" playboy of a son.

Li Xuanba heard this "joke" from Li Shimin.

Although Zhangsun Anye was also Li Shimin's future brother-in-law, Li Shimin seemed exceptionally interested in watching him get beaten. He frequently went to enjoy the spectacle and would even fan the flames.

Li Xuanba could not help but cover his face. "Aren't you afraid he'll hold a grudge against you?"

Li Shimin widened his innocent eyes. "How could he? I'm just a child!"

*I, Li Shimin, a seven-year-old child, what ill intentions could I possibly have?*

"It's time to take action." Seeing that his father had obtained the post of Vice Director of the Palace Administration several years earlier than in the original history, Li Xuanba realized his butterfly wings were taking effect once again. His mind, made sluggish by spring fatigue, shook off its laziness.

If he did not pull himself together soon, his elder sister would be married off.

At the thought of his sister marrying, a wave of vexation rose in Li Xuanba's heart.

Li Shimin had stopped running wild outside. Aside from losing the novelty of playing at the Zhangsun estate, his sudden lack of enthusiasm was also due to his irritation over their Third Sister's impending marriage.

The two children were sulking over their sister's marriage. Sensing this, Lady Dou instructed Li Sanniang, who was cooped up at home embroidering her dowry, to take Li Shimin and Li Xuanba out for some fresh air.

Li Sanniang was so happy she almost shed tears.

Being confined to her small courtyard and forbidden from going out had nearly driven her mad with boredom!

"Erlang, Sanlang, where do you want to play? Your elder sister will play with you to your hearts' content!" Li Sanniang hugged her two younger brothers one by one, filled with gratitude.

"It's up to Ah Xuan," Li Shimin said. "Ah Xuan is finally going to start his wealth-generating plan."

Li Xuanba said, "Sister, accompany me to the workshop where the bookstore prints Buddhist scriptures. I want to print some other books."

Li Sanniang led her two younger brothers into the carriage. "Print what? Did you obtain new Buddhist scriptures from His Majesty?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "Print Confucian classics."

Li Sanniang was surprised. "Sanlang, Confucian classics cannot be printed. They must be copied by hand!"

Li Xuanba said, "Currently, the realm is stable and prosperous, and the number of scholars is gradually increasing. I have already consulted Mister Gao and Mister Yuwen. They have agreed to let me print their annotated versions of the Confucian classics and sell them at a low price to scholars from humble backgrounds, in order to revitalize Confucian studies."

Li Xuanba offered Li Sanniang an obedient smile and said, "In the future, our eldest brother will surely associate with the great noble clans. It would be inappropriate for Second Brother and me to mingle too much with the scholars of those prominent families, lest we dilute our eldest brother's network and provoke his displeasure. I heard from His Majesty that a new 'Jinshi' category will be added to the examinations this year to select scholars. In the future, I wish to take the 'Jinshi' path to become an official."

Li Shimin added, "In the future, I can go fight the Turks to earn a noble title, but Ah Xuan certainly cannot go to the battlefield. Relying solely on hereditary privilege to become an official and living at the whim of others is far inferior to passing the examinations and earning an office oneself. If scholars from humble backgrounds wish to become officials, aside from pledging allegiance to the great clans, they will likely take the same path Ah Xuan has chosen. Therefore, Ah Xuan wants to build a network among these humble scholars in advance."

After listening intently, Li Sanniang sighed. "You two are far too precocious. You think so deeply and so far ahead."

Li Shimin puffed out his chest and said proudly, "Ah Xuan and I have already accompanied the imperial entourage on the southern tour. Of course we are incredible!"

Li Sanniang smiled. "Indeed. However, Ah Xuan, the ministers in court currently look down on scholars from humble backgrounds, and noble families are unwilling to associate with them. As a young master of the Duke of Tang's estate, if you get too close to them, you will be looked down upon."

Li Xuanba said, "I know. Currently, entering office through hereditary privilege is held in the highest regard, while those who enter court through examinations like the 'Mingjing' are considered inferior from the start."

At present, the imperial examinations not only required a recommendation from an official of the fifth rank or higher to even qualify, but those who became officials through this route also suffered severe discrimination.

Even in the Tang Dynasty, the great noble clans would still look down on officials who rose through the imperial examinations.

"But I just want to take the exam and test myself against the scholars of the world." An expression flickered across Li Xuanba's face that even his twin brother could not decipher. "I just want to sit for it once."

Looking at Li Xuanba's expression, Li Sanniang felt an inexplicable ache in her heart, though she did not understand why.

She immediately declared, "If Sanlang wants to take the exam, then take it! Scholars of humble origins are not necessarily inferior to those of noble birth. For Sanlang to match wits and knowledge with the scholars of the world—what a splendid and liberating thing that would be! Your sister supports you!"

Li Shimin also said, "Your brother supports you too! Ah Xuan can do whatever he wants!"

Li Xuanba nodded. "Mm."

Li Sanniang said, "Let's go! We will print and sell the Confucian classics right now! If they don't sell, your sister will cover the costs for you! My dowry is incredibly bountiful!"

Li Xuanba chuckled. "How could we possibly use Sister's dowry? Rest assured, Sister. In the scholarly world, the reputations of Mister Gao and Mister Yuwen are resounding. There is no way their annotated versions of the Four Books and Five Classics won't sell. Furthermore, I don't plan to sell only the classics. I also want to sell some novels and storybooks."

Li Shimin said proudly, "Sister, you have no idea how good Ah Xuan is at telling stories. His storybooks will definitely sell like hotcakes!"

Li Sanniang said, "Print whatever Sanlang wants! If we make a profit, we split it; if we lose money, it's on me! No refusing, it's settled!"

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin exchanged a glance. Under the "intimidating" glare of Li Sanniang, they could only cup their hands in gratitude. "Then we thank our elder sister."

Li Sanniang laughed. "That's more like it! You must rely on your sister more!"

She ruffled Li Xuanba and Li Shimin's small hair buns, then helped them tie them back up neatly.

"Let's go! Off to print new books!"

"Mm, alright!"

The three siblings arrived at the woodblock printing workshop behind the West Market bookstore, where they found Chai Shao, who had been waiting there for a long time.

Chai Shao: *Silly grin.*

The smiles on Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's faces vanished simultaneously.

Li Shimin gave him a deadpan look. "I recall that before marriage, men and women are not supposed to meet?"

Li Xuanba also gave a deadpan look. "I recall that as well."

Chai Shao immediately said, "It's just a chance encounter, a chance encounter!"

He rubbed his hands together. "Since we've crossed paths, how about I act as your bodyguard?"

"Cough, Guard Chai, could you perhaps not smile in such an... unseemly manner?" A plump young man stepped out from the side.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were startled and immediately prepared to bow.

The young man waved his hand to stop them. "I merely followed Sichang to take a look at my cousin's bookstore. Surely my cousin wouldn't unwelcome his elder cousin?"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba both pulled long faces. "We wouldn't dare. Welcome, Cousin."

Cousin? Li Sanniang pondered for a moment, sizing up the young man's build, and suddenly realized. "Could it be..."

Through her veiled hat (mili), she glared at Chai Shao before slowly curtsying. "Greetings, Cousin."

This young man was none other than Crown Prince Yang Zhao.

Yang Zhao said gently, "Greetings, Cousin."

Li Shimin was broad-minded. After the initial shock, seeing that his Crown Prince cousin was as gentle and easygoing as ever, he quickly relaxed.

"Cousin, weren't you in the Eastern Capital? Why have you returned?" Li Shimin asked curiously.

Yang Zhao winked at Li Xuanba and said, "You'll have to ask your younger brother about that."

Li Xuanba pointed to himself. "Me?"

Yang Zhao smiled but said nothing.

Li Xuanba's eyes widened. *Could it be because I advised the Crown Prince that if Yang Guang ever suggested he return to Daxing, he should do so immediately without hesitation?*

*Wait, wasn't that supposed to happen in the seventh month? It's only the fourth month now!*

*Could it be that before the seventh month, Yang Guang had also suggested Yang Zhao return to Daxing, but Yang Zhao had requested to stay in Luoyang a bit longer, so Yang Guang let him stay for another three months?*

This was indeed highly probable.

Yang Zhao said, "Father told me to return to Daxing, and I thought it would be the perfect time to return and attend Sichang's wedding feast, so I came back. When Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen heard that you wanted to print Confucian classics, they also requested leave from Father. They should be returning in a few days."

Li Shimin gasped in shock. "Ah? The two teachers are returning as well? I'm doomed, I'm doomed! Ah Xuan, I'm doomed!"

Li Shimin immediately pulled a miserable, tearful face.

Yang Zhao was curious. "Erlang, what is wrong? Are you unhappy that your teachers are returning?"

Li Xuanba let out a heavy sigh. Though his tone was mournful, the smile at the corner of his mouth could not be suppressed. "Well, before Second Brother and I returned to Daxing, our teachers assigned us a great deal of homework. But after Second Brother returned, he made a new friend in the Fourth Young Master Zhangsun and ran wild outside every day. As for his homework..."

Li Xuanba spread his hands and shrugged. "Cousin, you understand."

"Ah!" Li Shimin clutched his head and shook it violently. "It's over, it's over, I'm finished!"

Looking at the utterly devastated Li Shimin, and then at the gloating smile on Li Xuanba's face, Yang Zhao could not help but chuckle. "Alright, I understand. Erlang... cough, my condolences."

Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen were exceptionally strict. Li Erlang was truly in for it.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第25章 慷慨皇帝再重赏
chunks.chineseText:
第25章 慷慨皇帝再重赏

=
　　李世民难得蔫了， 全程皱着一张苦脸。
　　杨昭乐呵呵地逗弄李世民。
　　李世民气得背过身，用后脑勺对着太子。
　　杨昭也不恼，说可以帮李世民补课。
　　李世民回头冷哼道：“我今天不睡觉了， 今天就把书看完， 不需要人帮忙！”
　　李玄霸没再在人前笑话二哥， 但在心里道：【说得好！有志气！先生抽背的时候，可别让我帮你作弊。】
　　李世民眼睛瞪得大大的，不敢置信地看向弟弟。
　　你这是什么坏弟弟！居然不帮我！
　　李玄霸走到李三娘身侧， 用阿姊挡住了二哥幽怨的眼神。
　　先生考核功课和去外面装逼不一样，二哥你可不能作弊。挡住！
　　李三娘抬起袖子遮住李玄霸，并故意对李世民笑了笑。李世民的眼神更幽怨了。
　　杨昭笑得肚子都在颤抖。
　　李玄霸偷瞥了一眼杨昭身上的肉， 心道怪不得太子的健康堪忧。
　　从柴绍嘴中，李玄霸得知无论是杨昭， 还是杨昭身边的人， 都因杨昭孔武有力，能开强弓，而对杨昭这肥胖心里一点数都没有。
　　这时候都把肥胖当富贵看待，虽然有医者多次说肥胖不好，但贵族们都没把这当回事。
　　李玄霸又瞥向还满脸幽怨的二哥。
　　二哥他最疼爱的二儿子李泰也是个连走路都困难的大胖子。若二哥对“肥胖”是病有一丁点清醒的认知， 就不会把李泰列入继承人人选。
　　不过历史中的唐太宗也本来没打算废太子就是了。
　　李世民见弟弟在看他，以为弟弟改变心意。
　　他用期待的星星眼看向李玄霸， 李玄霸立刻又把脑袋藏回了李三娘的身侧。
　　李世民生气：【啊！！】
　　李玄霸眼神往一旁飘移。你“啊”也没用。
　　李三娘笑着按了李世民的脑袋一下：“自己学去。没有完成功课，被罚也是应该的。”
　　李世民瘪嘴：“哦。”
　　他瘪完嘴，使劲搓搓脸， 又变回了活泼的笑容。
　　李世民叉腰笑道：“反正今后都要熬夜看书， 之后很快就要被老师训， 现在得玩个够！不苦恼了！走， 阿玄，我们去看工匠如何印刷书！”
　　他猛地冲到李玄霸身边，拉着还没反应过来的李玄霸就跑。
　　李玄霸感觉自己完全是被拖着走。
　　如果现在把这一幕夸张一点画成漫画，那么他一定是两脚离地状态。
　　李三娘赶紧跟上：“二郎，小心些！别把三郎带摔着！”
　　柴绍也赶紧去追一眨眼就跑得快没影的李世民。
　　杨昭跑了两步，喘了两口气，变成慢悠悠走。
　　他气定神闲的模样，有一半原因都是因为胖。胖了急不动啊。
　　李三娘追上李世民和李玄霸时，李世民已经踮着脚趴在桌沿，观看工匠演示印刷佛经。
　　李玄霸双手按在膝盖上气喘吁吁。
　　李三娘帮李玄霸拍了拍背，横了李世民一眼。
　　李世民对着三姐笑了一下，糊弄过去。
　　“阿姊，这不就是一个大号的印章吗？”李世民的双脚上上下下一踮一踮地晃。
　　李玄霸喘口气了，道：“就是大号印章。试试我的法子。”
　　书店原掌柜被独孤老夫人发卖后，新的掌柜十分老实。虽然李玄霸年幼，但也全听李玄霸吩咐，不发表意见。
　　李玄霸让仆从拿来一个小盒子，打开后，里面是一个巴掌大小的奇怪玩具。
　　这个玩具是一个架子。架子上面有两块板，下面有个脚踏板，旁边有个大车轮。
　　李玄霸把玩具架子立好，在上面的板子取下来：“把雕版安装在这个架子上面，这里还有喷墨和刷墨的机关。用这个机巧，就能减少工匠的工作强度，一天印更多书。”
　　李玄霸要来一小块纸，给众人演示了一遍。
　　杨昭好奇道：“李三郎，你这是从哪里看来的？”
　　李玄霸胡扯道：“从一本话本中看到的，我试了试，还真能行。”
　　他自然是从前世打工的地方学到的。
　　前世他的父母撸了高利贷，又向亲朋好友借了一大笔钱跑到国外潇洒后，养育他长大的祖父母被气死，他在高三的寒假辍学，开始打工还钱。
　　他那时才十七岁，当时类似“外卖小哥”这样好的打工职业还不普及，又被讨债公司的人堵着不准出远门，只能从打零工做起。
　　去县里的老旧印刷厂给学校印试卷，是他最初在班主任的帮助下找的第一份工作。
　　带他的老厂长特别喜欢各种老式的印刷机，常做各种老式印刷机的模型玩耍。
　　他后来帮老厂长开了个网店，专门卖各种印刷机模型。
　　老厂长赚了钱，很好心地分给了他五万块。
　　正好这时高利贷被扫黑抓了。他用了四万块还掉部分债务，获得了债主们的信任，终于能离开家乡，揣着剩下一万块踏上了去南方沿海城市的路。
　　所以就算穿越了，他仍旧记得老式印刷机模型怎么做。
　　只是模型，肯定不如真正的老式印刷机精巧。但老式印刷机就是手工机械，没有什么特殊的技术门槛，唐国公府有能工巧匠，李玄霸琢磨琢磨，就能弄个简易版出来。
　　不过现在他只是拿出了能减轻雕版印刷术体力负担的超级简易印刷机，甚至都算不上印刷机。
　　他还是个孩子，不能一口气拿出太精巧的技术。再者，因为汉字字数太多，工匠识字率又不高，印刷佛经、儒经等又只需要大量重复的印版时，还是雕版印刷更好用。
　　等他哥当皇帝后，他才敢把油墨铅活字老式印刷机亮出来。
　　老式印刷机这个东西确实没有多少技术含量。在手工机械时代，手工机械的更新换代除了材料之外，就只是“没往这个方向想”。
　　工坊里的工匠不仅负责印刷，雕版和一些木工活也要做。李玄霸把模型拿出来后，工坊里的印刷工们立刻就意识到了这个模型的用处。
　　这时候的税制是“租庸调制”，对手工业者管理很严格。大部分手工业者都被官府纳入管理，私人手工业者不多，大部分背后还有贵族的影子。
　　贵族官僚所需要的手工业品，要么直接通过俸禄从官府手工业者手中直接获得，要么是自己府中工匠制作。
　　如今蓄奴之风盛行，手艺好的人都愿意卖身给贵族换取平稳的生活。工坊的匠人和李玄霸在府里求教过的工匠，都是唐国公府的奴隶。所以李玄霸很随意地将简陋的雕版“印刷机”拿出来，不担心会外传。
　　柴绍和杨昭先没把这个孩童做的“玩具”当回事，但听到工匠们激动的议论时，才意识到这个东西可能比他们想象中的还要有用些。
　　杨昭此次回大兴，除了喝柴绍的喜酒之外，还有一个原因。
　　他隐晦劝说高颎自己退一步时，撞见高颎和宇文弼正谈起李玄霸请求印刷他们标注过的儒经的事。
　　李玄霸的理由是，雕版印刷能飞速印出很多书籍，但民间只用它来印刷佛经。佛经虽引人向善，但也引人出世，且是外来的经书。我等士人，还是应该多学儒。
　　隋文帝虽然信佛，也大力推广儒经。而士人虽然大多儒释道三修，内在可能还要夹杂一点不可言说的法家兵家纵横家之类的，但经历过魏晋南北朝的放纵后，清醒的士人又开始重拾儒经正统，并尝试用传统的儒释道融合成新的儒经圣学。
　　高颎和宇文弼就是朝中最重视推行儒学的人之一。他们看到李玄霸的信，自然心动。
　　两人叹息，他们曾经见有贫寒人家花钱购买印刷的佛经虔诚供奉，居然没想到雕版也可以印儒经。
　　杨昭也是重儒之人。他深知要治理国家，还是得落在儒学身上。于是他毫不犹豫地回京，想亲自观察这件事。
　　杨昭感慨道：“如此一改，印刷书籍的字迹会清晰许多。用来印儒经，也算合适了。”
　　柴绍惊讶道：“印儒经？这是李三郎想到的主意？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　柴绍夸张道：“朝中这么多大儒都没想到，三郎真厉害。”
　　李世民得意：“那是！我弟弟最厉害！”
　　李三娘笑道：“那你呢？”
　　李世民叉腰：“和弟弟一样厉害。”
　　众人皆笑。
　　李玄霸曲着手指挠了挠脸颊，被夸得有些不好意思。不过他也很疑惑，雕版印刷术已经流行了许久，但在五代后唐时，丞相冯道、李愚才第一次奏请印刷儒经。
　　可能朝中的大人物们确实不太注意民间的事吧。
　　看到李玄霸的“玩具”，杨昭觉得李玄霸的建议大为可行：“表弟，你可以将这机巧献与陛下吗？当然，陛下肯定不会白拿你的东西。”
　　李玄霸道：“陛下随意取用就是。不过一些小玩意儿，哪称得上‘献’字？我可不想传出擅长木工活的名声。”
　　杨昭笑道：“传出又如何？诸葛武侯也擅长机巧，表弟便是诸葛在世。”
　　李玄霸拱手道：“虽我不可能成为诸葛武侯在世，但表兄都能这么夸了，我就当做是对我的勉励，厚着脸皮应了。”
　　李世民眼睛转溜溜，道：“我也想当诸葛武侯！阿玄，我们一起吧！”
　　李玄霸无语：“诸葛武侯还能两个人？”
　　李世民道：“为何不能？诸葛武侯多多益善！”
　　杨昭失笑：“二郎说得对，多多益善。你们二人都成为诸葛武侯。”
　　李世民得意：“表兄也说得对，嘿嘿。”
　　李玄霸更无语。嘿嘿你个头。
　　二哥小时候想成为的人真多，一会儿冠军侯，一会儿卫青，现在还想当诸葛武侯了。
　　不知道二哥当了皇帝之后回忆童年的梦想，会不会感到尴尬。
　　大概率二哥长大了也和现在脸皮一样厚，完全不会尴尬，还会调侃几句。
　　李玄霸慷慨地将模型献给了太子。杨昭让人马不停蹄地将这件事奏给皇帝。
　　杨广得知此事后十分高兴。
　　他本就是好大喜功之人，任何能造成大声势的事他都喜欢。
　　于是他给太子下令，召集工匠研究这个印刷术，先印儒经，再印历法，然后把他登基后发的招贤令等圣旨编撰成“圣言”，印刷后到各地分发。
　　如果印刷效果很好，杨广就想召集人把宫中收藏的孤本编撰成一部图书合集，然后多印刷几部，在东京、江都各藏几部。
　　杨广自己是奢侈的人，所以与隋文帝的抠抠索索不一样，他奖赏得他喜爱的人很慷慨。
　　杨广当即写信给李玄霸，问李玄霸想不想当侍中。
　　侍中现在只是一个虚职，一般是皇帝亲近之人的“加官”。如果单独封侍中，只是拿俸禄，不用干活。
　　李世民得知此事后，高兴得一蹦三张高：“好呀！阿玄先去当官！哥哥随后跟上！”
　　李渊也十分高兴。
　　李建成心里虽有些酸，但还是做出了一副好兄长的模样，恭喜李玄霸。
　　只窦夫人皱眉：“会不会太过招摇？”
　　李玄霸想了想，道：“父亲，请帮我拒绝陛下的好意，换成一些田地钱财。”
　　李渊疑惑：“为何？”
　　李玄霸道：“木秀于林，风必摧之。我和二哥先是伴驾，父亲又被征辟入朝，我又得侍中官职，荣宠太过。如母亲所说，我还年幼，福气太重，不一定能承受得住。古来许多年幼时入朝为官者，命都不太好。”
　　此时不仅很信谶纬之术，也信“命数”。
　　李玄霸只说家中荣宠太过，李渊还不以为意。
　　他身为皇帝表兄，荣宠再过都是应该的。何况他家的荣宠，比起皇帝身边的宠臣宇文述一家大大不如。
　　但李玄霸说“福气过重难以承受”，就让李渊上心了。
　　李玄霸自出生起身体就不好，又显得过分聪慧，很符合史书中那些早夭神童的特征。
　　李玄霸见父亲被说动，又道：“再者，父亲，我想科举入朝。”
　　李渊想也不想道：“不准！科举入朝会受人鄙夷，你没看到先帝科举征辟的人都是什么处境吗？”
　　李玄霸当然知道。
　　虽然后世记载“明经”起自隋文帝，“进士”起自隋炀帝。实际上汉朝察举制时，被举荐的贤才入朝后会通过考试甄选，就已经有了“明经”和“进士”的分科称呼。
　　相反，后世经过考古，隋文帝和隋炀帝关于科举取士的诏令中，没有出现“明经”和“科举”的文字。
　　这不是说隋文帝和隋炀帝没有开这两科。他们只是沿用了古人考试分类称呼，没有特意点明，对科举取士没有后世想象的那么重视。
　　隋文帝是真的不太重视科举招揽的人才，更信任勋贵和世家荫蔽做官的人才。
　　隋文帝一朝通过科举入朝的人才，大部分如王贞，给个县尉就打发了，更多的如刘焯、侯白之人，连官都没得做。
　　甚至侯白自最难考上的“秀才”科入朝为官，隋文帝却把他当逗乐子的人。杨素与侯白交好，每当举荐侯白，隋文帝总说侯白不够格为官，只给了他五品官的待遇。
　　李渊年少时曾伴随隋文帝左右，深得隋文帝喜爱，所以是亲眼见到侯白如何被隋文帝当做俳优对待。
　　李玄霸一说起科举入朝为官，他就立刻膈应。
　　李玄霸道：“父亲，当今陛下和先帝不一样。在伴驾时，我听陛下说，他更希望任用亲自选拔的人才。陛下悄悄和我说，他明年就会增设科目，开科取士，亲自选拔人才。”
　　李渊看向李世民：“真有此事？”
　　我没听过啊！李世民毫不犹豫地回答：“真的！陛下说过！”
　　可能是陛下私下对阿玄说的吧。先帮阿玄说服耶耶！
　　李渊有些意动：“既然陛下都和你们说了此话……”
　　李建成反对道：“即使陛下会重用科举为官的人，但朝中大臣仍旧会鄙夷。我们唐国公府，怎么能出科举之人？太丢唐国公府的脸。”
　　李渊又犹豫了：“确实如此，还是不太好啊。”
　　窦夫人想插嘴，但嘴唇动了几次，她还是没有出声，担心她一出声，丈夫会习惯性地反对。
　　李玄霸给了母亲一个“放心”的眼神，继续道：“我们唐国公府是陛下信任的外戚，如烈火烹油一般鼎盛。若家中兄弟各个权势过重，反而不美。我如果经过科举入朝为官，勋贵世家子弟不屑与我为伍，或许才对唐国公府更好。”
　　李世民也劝道：“对啊耶耶，阿玄本来体力就不好，不能被俗务所累。阿玄就留在京中修修书，别人不去烦他，还乐得自在。我就去边疆为将，自己拼个爵位出来。我们兄弟几人各走不同的路线为官，岂不是更好？”
　　李渊还没被说服，李建成同意了：“父亲，二郎这么一说，似乎也算可行。”
　　窦夫人这才插嘴：“二郎和三郎都想自己挣得官职，如此有志气，郎君就从了吧。至于朝中其他人的看法，只要陛下足够喜爱三郎，谁敢轻视三郎？”
　　李渊的左右摇摆终于结束，点头：“好吧。那三郎，你就好好准备。虽然以我家地位，科举取士‘秀才’之名唾手可得，你也最好让众人信服你的才华。”
　　隋唐“秀才科”才是常科考试中最难的一科，录取人数极低。
　　隋朝自取士到灭亡，“秀才”不足十人；唐初因“秀才科”的要求太高，一直无人通过，很快就废弃了“秀才”一科，“秀才”一词成为恭维读书人的美誉。
　　无论当今皇帝会再开多少科目，唐国公府的公子既然要通过科举入朝为官，那肯定是争夺“秀才”之名。
　　“耶耶，还用你叮嘱吗？我和阿玄的老师可是高公和宇文公呢！”李世民道，“高公和宇文公的弟子怎么可能不是秀才，哼。若不是我想从军，我也去考个秀才。”
　　李渊没好气道：“是是是，你和三郎的老师是高公和宇文公。那二郎你的功课做完了吗？”
　　李世民小脸一垮：“耶耶，我要讨厌你了！”
　　李渊哈哈大笑。
　　李建成先有些羡慕李世民和李玄霸的老师，听了李渊的嘲笑，也不由浮现笑意：“二郎，南朝有人言，‘小时了了，大未必佳’。你如今聪慧不算什么，不可松懈。”
　　李世民垮着脸拱手：“是，兄长。”
　　窦夫人掩嘴笑道：“二郎还是很勤奋的，只是这些日子松懈了些。”
　　李玄霸频频点头。那可真是太松懈了。
　　“前几日二哥还说要熬夜看书，结果这几日又懒散了，总想跑去骑马射箭。”李玄霸唉声叹气道，“我去年勤奋的二哥哪去了？现在的二哥居然如此怠惰！”
　　李世民气愤道：“阿玄！”混蛋弟弟，我刚刚还为你说话，你还和耶耶娘亲兄长一起嘲笑我！
　　窦夫人笑道：“这也有你们父亲的错。他现在无事在家，见陛下赐给二郎小马驹，就非得去教二郎骑马，耽误二郎功课。”
　　李渊无奈：“行行行，我的错。二郎，我把你的小马驹没收了。”
　　李世民嘴张得大大的，能塞进一整只煮鸡蛋：“不！！阿玄！快帮我劝劝耶耶！把我的小马还给我！”
　　李玄霸忍笑：“才不要，谁让你没做完功课。”
　　李世民嘴一瘪，气得“哇哇”大哭起来。
　　窦夫人和李渊笑得更厉害。
　　李玄霸没笑了，给他哥递帕子擦眼泪鼻涕，用心声安慰道：【谁让你不肯好好做功课？难道你真要等老师检查功课后对你失望？老师绕路访友多耽搁了几日，现在也该到了。】
　　李世民把弟弟熊抱住，故意把哭出来的眼泪鼻涕往李玄霸肩膀上揩。
　　李玄霸：“……”脏死了！！！
　　窦夫人和李渊快笑得喘不过气。
　　李建成露出嫌弃的神色。刚刚他还觉得两个弟弟不错，现在听到弟弟刺耳的哭声，看着弟弟眼泪鼻涕一大把的邋遢样，他又不喜欢了。
　　唉，小孩子真烦。
　　……
　　李渊最终写信婉拒了杨广的赏赐。
　　李渊不该知道杨广要增开科举的事，没有多说。
　　李玄霸也写了信，信中说他想与天下有才之士比一比，这样站到陛下身边才理直气壮。再者，听闻科举优秀者能得到皇帝亲自问策，那岂不就是天子门生？
　　本来没李世民什么事，但他仍旧用被两位老师的戒尺抽肿了的手握笔添了几句，“我为表叔征战，阿玄给表叔当门生，我们正好文武双全！”。
　　杨广看到李玄霸的信，视线在“天子门生”四个字上来回扫了许久，然后落在了李世民增添的那句话上。
　　他笑着对最信任的心腹重臣宇文述道：“许国公看这二子，是不是很讨人喜爱？”
　　宇文述道：“陛下的眼光，从来是不会错的。”
　　杨广大笑。
　　见杨广心情不错，宇文述才说了此次面见的正事：“陛下，楚公病了，病中似乎对陛下有怨言，说‘我岂须更活耶’。”
　　杨广笑容敛去，冷哼一声：“确是怨言，但也是有自知之明。”
