Chapter 25: The Generous Emperor Bestows Another Grand Reward

It was a rare sight to see Li Shimin so utterly deflated, his face crumpled in a bitter grimace the entire time.

Yang Zhao gleefully teased him.

Fuming, Li Shimin turned his back, giving the Crown Prince the cold shoulder.

Yang Zhao was not at all offended and offered to help tutor him.

Li Shimin whipped his head back and snorted coldly. "I'm not sleeping tonight! I'll finish reading all the books today. I don't need anyone's help!"

Li Xuanba refrained from mocking his second brother in front of others, but silently thought to himself: *Well said! Such ambition! Just don't ask me to help you cheat when the master calls on you to recite.*

Li Shimin's eyes went wide as saucers as he stared at his younger brother in disbelief.

*What kind of terrible brother are you?! You're actually not going to help me!*

Li Xuanba stepped to Li Sanniang's side, using his elder sister to shield himself from his second brother's resentful glare.

*A master's examination of your schoolwork is different from showing off in public. You cannot cheat on this, Second Brother. Shielded!*

Li Sanniang raised her sleeve to cover Li Xuanba and gave Li Shimin a deliberate smile. Li Shimin's gaze grew even more sorrowful.

Yang Zhao laughed so hard his belly shook.

Li Xuanba stole a glance at the rolls of flesh on Yang Zhao's body, thinking to himself that it was no wonder the Crown Prince's health was in jeopardy.

From Chai Shao, Li Xuanba had learned that both Yang Zhao and those around him were completely oblivious to the dangers of his obesity, simply because Yang Zhao was physically powerful and could draw a heavy bow.

In this era, corpulence was viewed as a sign of wealth and prosperity. Although physicians had repeatedly warned that obesity was harmful, the nobility never took it seriously.

Li Xuanba glanced back at his second brother, who still wore a resentful expression.

*Second Brother's most beloved second son, Li Tai, would also grow up to be so morbidly obese that he would struggle even to walk. If Second Brother had even a shred of awareness that obesity is a disease, he wouldn't have considered Li Tai as a potential heir.*

*Then again, Emperor Taizong of Tang in history never actually intended to depose his Crown Prince anyway.*

Seeing his younger brother looking at him, Li Shimin thought he had changed his mind.

He looked at Li Xuanba with pleading, starry eyes, but Li Xuanba immediately ducked his head back behind Li Sanniang.

Li Shimin fumed: *Ahhh!!*

Li Xuanba's gaze drifted elsewhere. *Screaming "ah" won't help you.*

Li Sanniang smiled and patted Li Shimin on the head. "Go study on your own. If you don't finish your lessons, you deserve to be punished."

Li Shimin pouted. "Oh."

After pouting, he rubbed his face vigorously, his lively smile returning in an instant.

Li Shimin placed his hands on his hips and laughed. "Since I'll have to stay up late reading anyway, and I'll be scolded by the teacher soon enough, I might as well play to my heart's content right now! No more worrying! Come on, Ah Xuan, let's go see how the craftsmen print books!"

He suddenly dashed to Li Xuanba's side, grabbing him and running before the younger boy could even react.

Li Xuanba felt himself being dragged along entirely.

If this scene were drawn as a caricature, his feet would undoubtedly be dangling in the air.

Li Sanniang quickly followed. "Erlang, be careful! Don't trip Sanlang!"

Chai Shao also rushed to chase after Li Shimin, who had vanished into the distance in the blink of an eye.

Yang Zhao took a couple of steps, panted twice, and reverted to a leisurely stroll.

His calm and unhurried demeanor was half due to his weight. When one is fat, one simply cannot rush.

By the time Li Sanniang caught up with them, Li Shimin was already standing on his tiptoes, leaning over the edge of a table to watch a craftsman demonstrate how to print Buddhist scriptures.

Li Xuanba stood with his hands on his knees, panting heavily.

Li Sanniang patted Li Xuanba's back and glared at Li Shimin.

Li Shimin offered his elder sister a sheepish grin, trying to brush it off.

"Sanniang, isn't this just a giant stamp?" Li Shimin bounced up and down on his tiptoes.

Once Li Xuanba caught his breath, he said, "It is indeed a giant stamp. Let's try my method."

After the original shopkeeper of the bookstore was sold off by Old Lady Dugu, the new shopkeeper was exceptionally honest. Although Li Xuanba was young, the man followed his instructions to the letter without offering any unsolicited opinions.

Li Xuanba had a servant bring over a small box. When opened, it revealed a strange, palm-sized toy.

The toy was a frame. It had two plates on top, a foot pedal below, and a large wheel on the side.

Li Xuanba set up the toy frame and removed the top plate. "Mount the woodblock onto this frame. There are mechanisms here for ink spraying and brushing. Using this contraption will reduce the physical labor of the craftsmen, allowing them to print more books in a day."

Li Xuanba asked for a small piece of paper and demonstrated the process to everyone.

Yang Zhao asked curiously, "Li Sanlang, where did you see such a thing?"

Li Xuanba fabricated a story. "I saw it in a popular novel. I tried making it, and it actually works."

Naturally, he had learned this from his part-time job in his past life.

In his previous life, his parents had taken out high-interest loans, borrowed a massive sum of money from relatives and friends, and then fled abroad to enjoy themselves. His grandparents, who had raised him, died of anger. Consequently, he dropped out of school during the winter break of his senior year of high school to start working and paying off the debts.

He was only seventeen at the time. Good part-time jobs like food delivery couriers were not yet widespread, and debt collectors blocked him from traveling far, so he had to start with odd jobs.

Printing exam papers for schools at an old printing factory in the county was the very first job he found with the help of his homeroom teacher.

The old factory director who mentored him was particularly fond of vintage printing presses and often made models of them for fun.

Later, he helped the old director open an online shop specifically to sell these printing press models.

The old director made a profit and kindly gave him fifty thousand yuan.

Coincidentally, the loan sharks were swept up in a crackdown on organized crime around that time. He used forty thousand yuan to pay off a portion of his debts, earning the trust of his creditors. Finally, he was able to leave his hometown, embarking on a journey to a southern coastal city with the remaining ten thousand yuan in his pocket.

Thus, even after transmigrating, he still remembered how to make a model of a vintage printing press.

As it was only a model, it was certainly not as sophisticated as a real vintage printing press. However, a vintage press was merely manual machinery with no particularly high technical threshold. The Duke of Tang's estate possessed skilled craftsmen; with some thought, Li Xuanba could easily have a simplified version constructed.

For now, however, he only presented an ultra-simplified press that could alleviate the physical burden of woodblock printing—it could hardly even be called a proper printing press.

He was still a child and could not produce overly sophisticated technology all at once. Furthermore, because there were too many Chinese characters and the literacy rate among craftsmen was low, woodblock printing remained more practical when mass-producing repetitive texts like Buddhist and Confucian scriptures.

Only after his brother became the emperor would he dare to reveal the vintage ink-and-lead movable type printing press.

A vintage printing press truly did not require much high technology. In the era of manual machinery, the evolution of such devices, aside from materials, was simply a matter of "no one having thought in that direction."

The craftsmen in the workshop were not only responsible for printing but also for woodblock carving and carpentry. Once Li Xuanba produced the model, the printers in the workshop immediately grasped its utility.

The tax system of this era was the *Zu-Yong-Diao* (land-tax, labor-service, and textile-tribute system), which strictly regulated artisans. Most craftsmen were managed by the government; private artisans were few, and most of them had noble backing.

The manufactured goods required by the nobility and bureaucracy were either obtained directly from government artisans as part of their official stipends or made by craftsmen within their own estates.

With the prevalence of keeping bondservants, skilled artisans were more than willing to sell themselves to noble households in exchange for a stable life. The craftsmen in the workshop, as well as those Li Xuanba had consulted in the estate, were all slaves of the Duke of Tang's household. Thus, Li Xuanba could casually present this crude woodblock "printing press" without worrying about the design leaking out.

Chai Shao and Yang Zhao did not take this child's "toy" seriously at first, but upon hearing the excited chatter of the craftsmen, they realized that this device might be far more useful than they had imagined.

Yang Zhao's return to Daxing this time was not only to attend Chai Shao's wedding but also for another reason.

When he had subtly advised Gao Jiong to take a step back, he had happened upon Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi discussing Li Xuanba's request to print the Confucian classics they had annotated.

Li Xuanba's reasoning was that while woodblock printing could rapidly produce many books, the common people only used it to print Buddhist scriptures. Although Buddhist scriptures guided people toward goodness, they also encouraged withdrawal from the world, and they were, after all, foreign texts. As scholars, they ought to study Confucianism more.

Although Emperor Wen of Sui was a devout Buddhist, he had also vigorously promoted Confucian classics. While most scholars practiced a blend of Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism—with perhaps a quiet dash of Legalism, Military Strategy, or School of Diplomacy mixed in—the sober-minded among them, having witnessed the decadence of the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties, began to reclaim the orthodoxy of Confucian classics. They sought to integrate traditional Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism into a new school of sacred Confucian learning.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were among the most prominent advocates for the promotion of Confucianism in the imperial court. Upon reading Li Xuanba's letter, they were naturally intrigued.

The two had sighed, recalling how they had seen impoverished families spend money to buy printed Buddhist scriptures to worship devoutly, yet it had never occurred to them that woodblocks could also be used to print Confucian classics.

Yang Zhao was also a man who valued Confucianism. He knew well that governing a nation ultimately relied on Confucian principles. Thus, he had returned to the capital without hesitation, wanting to observe this matter personally.

Yang Zhao remarked with emotion, "With this modification, the characters of the printed books will be much clearer. It is indeed fitting to use this to print Confucian classics."

Chai Shao asked in surprise, "Printing Confucian classics? Was this Li Sanlang's idea?"

Li Xuanba nodded.

Chai Shao praised extravagantly, "So many great Confucian scholars in the court never thought of this. Sanlang is truly remarkable."

Li Shimin boasted proudly, "Of course! My younger brother is the best!"

Li Sanniang teased, "And what about you?"

Li Shimin placed his hands on his hips. "Just as remarkable as my brother."

Everyone laughed.

Li Xuanba curled his finger to scratch his cheek, slightly embarrassed by the praise. However, he was also quite puzzled. Woodblock printing had been popular for a long time, yet it was not until the Later Tang dynasty of the Five Dynasties period that Chancellors Feng Dao and Li Yu first petitioned to print the Confucian classics.

Perhaps the grand figures of the court simply paid little attention to the affairs of the common folk.

Seeing Li Xuanba's "toy," Yang Zhao felt that his suggestion was highly feasible. "Cousin, would you be willing to present this clever device to His Majesty? Of course, His Majesty certainly won't take your creation for nothing."

Li Xuanba replied, "His Majesty may use it as he pleases. It is merely a trifling toy; how could it deserve the word 'present'? Besides, I have no wish to gain a reputation for being skilled in carpentry."

Yang Zhao laughed. "What of it? Marquis Zhuge Liang was also skilled in mechanics. You, cousin, would be Zhuge Liang reborn."

Li Xuanba cupped his hands. "Though I could never truly be Zhuge Liang reborn, since my elder cousin praises me so, I shall take it as encouragement and accept it with a thick skin."

Li Shimin's eyes darted around. "I want to be Marquis Zhuge too! Ah Xuan, let's do it together!"

Li Xuanba was speechless. "Can there be two Marquis Zhuges?"

Li Shimin argued, "Why not? The more Marquis Zhuges, the better!"

Yang Zhao chuckled. "Erlang is right, the more the better. Both of you shall become Marquis Zhuges."

Li Shimin beamed with pride. "Cousin is right too, hehe."

Li Xuanba was even more speechless. *Hehe your head.*

Second Brother wanted to be so many people when he was young. One moment it was the Champion Marquis Huo Qubing, the next it was Wei Qing, and now he wants to be Zhuge Liang.

I wonder if Second Brother will feel embarrassed when he recalls his childhood dreams after becoming emperor.

In all likelihood, even when grown, Second Brother's skin will be just as thick as it is now. He won't feel embarrassed at all and will probably even joke about it.

Li Xuanba generously presented the model to the Crown Prince. Yang Zhao immediately had someone deliver a memorial to the Emperor without delay.

Yang Guang was delighted upon learning of this.

He was naturally a man who loved grand achievements and ostentation; he relished anything that could create a grand sensation.

Thus, he ordered the Crown Prince to gather craftsmen to study this printing method. They were to print the Confucian classics first, followed by calendars, and then compile the imperial edicts he had issued since his ascension—such as the decrees seeking talented men—into "Sacred Words" to be printed and distributed across the realm.

If the printing proved successful, Yang Guang intended to assemble scholars to compile the rare, unique volumes in the imperial collection into a massive compendium, print multiple copies, and store them in the Eastern Capital and Jiangdu.

As a man of lavish tastes himself, Yang Guang was unlike the stingy Emperor Wen of Sui; he was exceptionally generous in rewarding those who found favor with him.

Yang Guang immediately wrote a letter to Li Xuanba, asking if he wished to be appointed as a *Shizhong* (Palace Attendant).

At this time, *Shizhong* was merely a nominal title, usually bestowed as an honorary addition to those close to the Emperor. If appointed solely as a *Shizhong*, one would receive a salary without having to perform any actual duties.

Upon hearing this, Li Shimin leaped three feet in the air with joy. "Wonderful! Ah Xuan can become an official first, and I will follow right behind!"

Li Yuan was also immensely pleased.

Although Li Jiancheng felt a twinge of jealousy in his heart, he still put on the guise of a benevolent elder brother and congratulated Li Xuanba.

Only Lady Dou frowned. "Is this not too ostentatious?"

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and said, "Father, please help me decline His Majesty's kind offer and request some land and money instead."

Li Yuan was puzzled. "Why?"

Li Xuanba explained, "A tree that stands taller than the forest will be destroyed by the wind. First, Second Brother and I accompanied the imperial carriage, then Father was summoned to court, and now I am to receive the office of *Shizhong*. This favor is too overwhelming. As Mother said, I am still young; such heavy blessings may be more than I can bear. Throughout history, many who entered officialdom at a tender age met with unfortunate ends."

In this era, people believed deeply not only in prophecy and divination but also in "fate and destiny."

When Li Xuanba merely spoke of the family's favor being too overwhelming, Li Yuan had not paid it much mind.

As the Emperor's cousin, no amount of favor seemed excessive to him. Moreover, his family's favor was far inferior to that of Yuwen Shu, the Emperor's favorite minister.

But when Li Xuanba mentioned that "heavy blessings may be more than I can bear," Li Yuan took it to heart.

Li Xuanba had been frail since birth and possessed an extraordinary intellect, which perfectly matched the traits of those short-lived child prodigies recorded in history.

Seeing that his father was swayed, Li Xuanba added, "Furthermore, Father, I wish to enter office through the imperial examinations."

Without a second thought, Li Yuan objected, "Absolutely not! Entering office through the imperial examinations will only bring disdain. Have you not seen the plight of those summoned through the examinations by the late Emperor?"

Li Xuanba naturally knew.

Although later histories recorded that the *Mingjing* (Classicist) category originated with Emperor Wen of Sui and the *Jinshi* (Presented Scholar) category with Emperor Yang of Sui, in truth, during the Han dynasty's recommendation system, recommended talents were selected through examinations upon entering the court, and the terms *Mingjing* and *Jinshi* were already in use to classify these subjects.

Conversely, modern archaeological findings showed that the edicts of Emperor Wen and Emperor Yang regarding the selection of scholars through examinations did not actually contain the words *Mingjing* or *Keju* (Imperial Examination).

This did not mean they had not established these two subjects. They had simply continued to use ancient classifications for examinations without explicitly highlighting them, and they did not value the selection of scholars through examinations nearly as much as later generations imagined.

Emperor Wen of Sui truly placed little value on talents recruited through examinations, preferring to trust those from noble and prestigious families who entered office through hereditary privilege.

Most of the talents who entered office through examinations during Emperor Wen's reign, such as Wang Zhen, were dismissed with minor posts like county sheriff. Many others, like Liu Zhuo and Hou Bai, were not even given official posts at all.

Even Hou Bai, who had entered office through the most difficult *Xiucai* (Outstanding Talent) category, was treated by Emperor Wen as a mere entertainer. Yang Su, who was on good terms with Hou Bai, recommended him repeatedly, but Emperor Wen always claimed Hou Bai was unfit for office, granting him only the stipend of a fifth-rank official.

In his youth, Li Yuan had accompanied Emperor Wen and was deeply favored by him, so he had personally witnessed how Hou Bai was treated as a jester by the late Emperor.

The moment Li Xuanba mentioned entering office through the imperial examinations, Li Yuan felt an immediate aversion.

Li Xuanba said, "Father, the current Emperor is different from the late Emperor. While accompanying him, I heard His Majesty say that he prefers to employ talents he has personally selected. His Majesty quietly told me that next year, he will establish more subjects and hold examinations to personally select talents."

Li Yuan looked at Li Shimin. "Is this true?"

*I've never heard of this!* Yet, without a moment's hesitation, Li Shimin replied, "It's true! His Majesty did say so!"

*Perhaps His Majesty told Ah Xuan in private. I must help Ah Xuan convince Father first!*

Li Yuan was somewhat swayed. "Since His Majesty has spoken such words to you..."

Li Jiancheng objected, "Even if His Majesty intends to employ those who enter through examinations, the ministers in the court will still look down on them. How can our Duke of Tang's estate produce an examination candidate? It would bring shame upon our household."

Li Yuan hesitated again. "Indeed, that is true. It is still not quite proper."

Lady Dou wanted to interject, but though her lips parted several times, she ultimately remained silent, fearing that if she spoke, her husband would oppose her out of habit.

Li Xuanba gave his mother a reassuring look and continued, "Our Duke of Tang's estate is a maternal relation trusted by His Majesty, flourishing like oil added to a blazing fire. If every brother in our family wields too much power, it may not bode well. If I enter office through the imperial examinations, the sons of the nobility and prestigious families will disdain to associate with me, which might actually be better for our household."

Li Shimin also chimed in, "Exactly, Father! Ah Xuan is physically frail and cannot bear the burden of mundane administrative duties. Let him stay in the capital to compile books; with no one to bother him, he can enjoy his leisure. As for me, I will go to the border as a general and win a title of nobility through my own merits. Is it not better for us brothers to pursue different paths in officialdom?"

Before Li Yuan could be fully convinced, Li Jiancheng agreed, "Father, now that Erlang puts it that way, it does seem feasible."

Only then did Lady Dou speak up. "Both Erlang and Sanlang wish to earn their own official posts. Since they possess such ambition, husband, you should grant their wish. As for the opinions of others in the court, as long as His Majesty favors Sanlang, who would dare look down on him?"

Li Yuan's vacillation finally came to an end, and he nodded. "Very well. Then, Sanlang, prepare yourself well. Although with our family's status, the title of *Xiucai* (Outstanding Talent) is within easy reach, it is still best if you make everyone believe in your talent."

In the Sui and Tang dynasties, the *Xiucai* category was actually the most difficult of the regular examinations, with an extremely low admission rate.

From the inception of the examinations in the Sui dynasty until its fall, fewer than ten people passed as *Xiucai*. In the early Tang dynasty, because the requirements for the *Xiucai* category were too high and no one ever passed, the category was soon abolished, and the term *Xiucai* became merely a complimentary title for scholars.

No matter how many new subjects the current Emperor might establish, if a young master of the Duke of Tang's estate was to enter office through the examinations, he would undoubtedly strive for the title of *Xiucai*.

"Father, is there any need for you to remind us? Ah Xuan and I have Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen as our masters!" Li Shimin said. "How could the disciples of Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen fail to become *Xiucai*? Hmph. If I didn't want to join the army, I would take the exam and become a *Xiucai* myself."

Li Yuan said testily, "Yes, yes, yes, you and Sanlang have Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen as your masters. In that case, Erlang, have you finished your lessons?"

Li Shimin's face fell. "Father, I'm going to hate you!"

Li Yuan burst into hearty laughter.

Li Jiancheng had initially felt a bit envious of the masters Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had. Hearing Li Yuan's teasing, he could not help but smile as well. "Erlang, there is a saying from the Southern Dynasties: 'A clever child does not necessarily grow into a brilliant adult.' Your current cleverness is nothing to boast of; you must not slacken."

With a long face, Li Shimin cupped his hands. "Yes, elder brother."

Lady Dou covered her mouth and smiled. "Erlang is still very diligent, he has just been a bit lax these past few days."

Li Xuanba nodded repeatedly. *He has indeed been far too lax.*

"A few days ago, Second Brother said he would stay up late reading, but over the last few days, he became lazy again, always wanting to run off to ride horses and shoot arrows," Li Xuanba sighed. "Where did my diligent Second Brother from last year go? The current Second Brother is actually so indolent!"

Li Shimin fumed, "Ah Xuan!" *You bastard brother, I just spoke up for you, and now you're joining Father, Mother, and Elder Brother in mocking me!*

Lady Dou smiled. "This is also your father's fault. He has nothing to do at home now, and seeing that His Majesty gifted Erlang a pony, he insisted on teaching Erlang how to ride, neglecting Erlang's studies."

Li Yuan said helplessly, "Fine, fine, fine, my fault. Erlang, I am confiscating your pony."

Li Shimin's mouth fell wide open, large enough to fit a whole boiled egg. "No!! Ah Xuan! Quickly help me persuade Father! Give me back my pony!"

Li Xuanba suppressed a laugh. "I won't. Who told you to leave your lessons unfinished?"

Li Shimin's mouth puckered, and he burst into loud, wailing tears of frustration.

Lady Dou and Li Yuan laughed even harder.

Li Xuanba stopped laughing and handed his brother a handkerchief to wipe his tears and nose, comforting him silently: *Who told you to refuse to study properly? Do you really want to wait until the master checks your lessons and is disappointed in you? The master took a detour to visit friends and was delayed for a few days, but he should be arriving just about now.*

Li Shimin wrapped his younger brother in a bear hug, deliberately wiping his tears and snot onto Li Xuanba's shoulder.

Li Xuanba: "..." *So filthy!!!*

Lady Dou and Li Yuan were laughing so hard they could barely breathe.

Li Jiancheng wore a look of disgust. Just moments ago, he had thought his two younger brothers were decent, but now, hearing the grating cries and seeing the messy display of tears and snot, his affection vanished.

Sigh, children are truly annoying.

...

Ultimately, Li Yuan wrote a letter politely declining Yang Guang's reward.

Since Li Yuan was not supposed to know about Yang Guang's plans to expand the imperial examinations, he did not mention it.

Li Xuanba also wrote a letter, stating that he wished to compete against the talented scholars of the realm so that he could stand by His Majesty's side with a clear conscience. Furthermore, he had heard that those who excelled in the examinations would be personally questioned by the Emperor on state policy; would that not make them the "disciples of the Emperor"?

Though it had nothing to do with Li Shimin, he still gripped the brush with hands swollen from being struck by his two masters' rulers and added a few lines: "I shall fight battles for Imperial Uncle, and Ah Xuan shall be Imperial Uncle's disciple. Together, we shall be the perfect combination of civil and military talent!"

When Yang Guang read Li Xuanba's letter, his gaze lingered on the words "disciples of the Emperor" for a long time before falling upon the sentence Li Shimin had added.

He smiled and said to his most trusted confidant and high minister, Yuwen Shu, the Duke of Xu, "Does the Duke of Xu not find these two boys exceptionally endearing?"

Yuwen Shu replied, "Your Majesty's judgment has never been wrong."

Yang Guang burst into hearty laughter.

Seeing that Yang Guang was in a good mood, Yuwen Shu finally brought up the main purpose of his audience. "Your Majesty, the Duke of Chu is ill. In his sickness, he seems to harbor resentment toward Your Majesty, saying, 'Why should I live any longer?'"

The smile vanished from Yang Guang's face, and he let out a cold snort. "Resentment indeed, but at least he possesses some self-awareness."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第26章 被迫与太子打赌
chunks.chineseText:
第26章 被迫与太子打赌

=
　　杨广和宇文述所说的楚王， 名为杨素。
　　杨素此人在后世各种文学创作中颇有存在感，但这存在感……嗯，都有点绿意盎然。
　　唐代孟棨所写笔记小说《本事诗》里， 杨素的爱妾乐昌公主思念前夫徐德言， 杨素让乐昌公主和前夫团聚， “破镜重圆”。
　　唐代刘餗所写笔记小说《隋唐嘉话》里，杨素的宠妾与李百通看上了眼，居然大咧咧地在杨素府中私通， 被杨素逮个正着，但杨素看李百通是个少年俊才，就把宠妾送给了李百通， “成人之美”。
　　唐末杜光庭所写传奇小说《虬髯客传》里，杨素的歌伎红拂又和李靖私奔了， 杨素还是欣然成全了红拂和李， 又来了个“红拂夜奔”。
　　这三个后世耳熟能详的故事，除了“破镜重圆”据考证虽然正史无记载，但有存在的可能性之外，“成人之美”和“红拂夜奔”都是完全虚构的。
　　李百药出身博陵李氏，二十八岁就袭爵安平县公， 是太子杨勇的通事舍人，杨广继位后就被排挤外贬。李靖出身“五姓七望”陇西李氏丹杨房， 更不是《虬髯客传》中的布衣书生。两人都是世家子弟。
　　别说两人出身高贵，性格高傲，做不出私通私奔的事。再者， 他们看上了谁， 随口和杨素提一句， 杨素就会欣然赠送美人。
　　虽然不知道唐人为什么在写小说的时候， 都热衷给杨素头上染点绿，但从他们总想撬杨素家的美人，翘完后还让杨素给主角当送官送钱的贵人，就知道杨素在隋朝权势之重。
　　杨素在隋文帝杨坚手下屡立战功，在隋文帝一朝就已经位高权重，不仅自己被封越国公，其子皆因为他的功劳被隋文帝封爵。
　　他又助杨广夺嫡，轻松帮杨广平定汉王杨谅叛乱。杨广对其厚赏无数。
　　杨素的权势在大业元年达到了鼎盛。
　　而鼎盛后，盛极而衰之快，让杨素所料未及。
　　当杨素助杨广坐稳了皇位，在杨广心中，杨素就成了影响他皇位稳定的因素。
　　即使杨素未有任何错误，还主动把弱点递给杨广，广求家产美姬，甚至做出早上拆房子晚上建房子这种奇葩事，引来众人鄙夷。杨广还是忌惮他。
　　大业二年，太史令上奏杨广“分野有大丧”。
　　时人都信谶纬，太史令其实不是专职的史官，而是官方“占星术士”。“分野”是先秦时传下的占星术用语，即将天上星宿划分成十二个星区，与地上疆域对应，以预言祸福。
　　隋朝的名称取自“随国”，与楚国同属“翼轸”分野。隋文帝和杨广都信这个，所以隋朝没有楚王和楚国公。
　　杨广听了太史公的上奏后，很快就将杨素改为隋朝第一个楚国公。
　　杨素立刻明白了皇帝的用意。
　　汉文帝曾经率领群臣哭死舅父。杨广此举和汉文帝差不多，就是告诉杨素，你现在自己选择去死，还能给自己和家族留个体面。
　　于是改封楚国公后不久，杨素就生病了。
　　杨广一边派名医去为杨素医治，一边暗中打探杨素的病情和对此事的反应。
　　听了宇文述打探回来的消息后，杨广心里对杨素的怨恨有些愤怒，但杨素好歹还是顺从地走上了自己给他安排好的路，杨广大度地原谅了杨素。
　　只要杨素死，他仍旧能厚待杨素的家族。
　　杨广对宇文述道：“若杨素不死，朕必定除其族！”
　　宇文述恭敬道：“陛下请安心，杨素必是不敢不死的。”
　　杨广冷哼：“希望他能识趣。”
　　大兴城中，李世民和李玄霸也得知了这件会让朝野上下轰动万分的事。
　　这时，高颎正手持书卷，敲着李世民的脑袋。
　　李世民很聪明，但有了小马之后，总有点定不下心读书，此次考校又被高颎看出了“赶工”的痕迹。
　　虽然李世民的功课是完成了，学识也掌握得不错。但这时候老师教书不仅看结果，也看重过程。
　　态度至关重要。
　　李世民就是读书态度不端正，必须被敲脑袋。
　　高颎离开大兴时，就感到了皇帝和杨素之间的气氛有些古怪，所以留下了人观察杨素的动静。
　　家仆前来送信时看了李世民和李玄霸一眼。
　　高颎问道：“可是越国公的事？”
　　家仆抱拳：“是。”
　　高颎道：“越国公之事无不可被外人所知的，直说即可。”
　　家仆在心里斟酌了一下语言，简略道：“陛下改封越国公为楚国公，食邑两千五百户。”
　　高颎点头，道：“知道了，下去吧。”
　　待家仆离开后，刚被敲了脑袋却和没事人似的李世民，好奇道：“老师，越国公是谁啊。”
　　李玄霸无语：“哥，你连越国公杨素杨公都不知道？”
　　李世民想了想，道：“你说杨公我就知道了。我还知道，越国公改楚国公，是厚赏！”
　　李玄霸嘀咕：“本来应该是这样。”
　　封王和封公中最高等的封号都是春秋战国的“国号”。从春秋战国时各国国力强盛，划分王爵和公爵中的地位高低。
　　比如“唐国公”的“唐”是春秋不知名小国，地位就比春秋五霸“越国公”的“越”地位低。
　　最高等的爵位，自然是“秦晋楚齐魏燕赵韩”，“秦晋楚”又在这其中独一档。所以杨素从越国公改封楚国公，本应是“晋升”了。
　　高颎虽然年纪大了，但耳力非常好。李玄霸嘀咕得很小声，他仍旧听到了。
　　“李三郎，为何是‘本来’？”高颎问道。
　　他的结论和李世民一样，所以听完家仆传递的消息后就没再在意，以为自己之前察觉的皇帝和杨素之间气氛古怪是错觉，这对君臣关系仍旧很亲近。
　　但高颎已经在教导李玄霸时，见识过李玄霸在政治上异于常人的敏锐，便想听听弟子的意见。
　　李玄霸想了想，没有藏拙：“我与二哥伴驾回洛阳东京时，太史令曾向陛下上奏，‘分野有大丧之气’。”
　　李世民挠头；“有这事？嗯……唔？想起来了！还真有！当时阿玄你就叹了口气！我记得很清楚！”
　　高颎自言自语：“分野……分野……”
　　李世民突然惊呼一声：“哎呀！楚国和随国不是同一个分野吗！”
　　高颎手不自觉地一松，书本落下。
　　书本还未落地，李世民条件反射地窜出去，接住了书本。
　　“给，老师！”李世民洋洋得意。
　　高颎：“……”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　本来现场气氛挺凝重，现在凝重不起来了。
　　高颎面无表情地接过书，又在李世民脑袋上敲了一下。
　　李世民疑惑抱头：“老师为何又敲我？”
　　高颎道：“没什么，就是顺手。”
　　李世民气呼呼地哼哼了两声，爬回坐榻上继续坐着。
　　李玄霸拍了拍二哥的脑壳。
　　李世民：“……干什么？”
　　李玄霸道：“看看二哥的脑壳的硬度有没有进化。”
　　李世民对李玄霸威胁地扬了扬拳头。嘲笑你哥，小心我也敲你脑袋。
　　李玄霸看见二哥要动手了，赶紧转移话题：“老师，今日课程是先中断吗？”
　　高颎摇了摇头，道：“继续上课。今日换一堂课，我给你们讲汉文帝。”
　　高颎继续讲课。
　　当他讲到汉文帝给还没死的舅舅哭丧时，李世民嘟囔道：“和陛下现在所做的事好像啊。但杨公不是陛下的宠臣吗？”
　　李玄霸提醒：“二哥，听课就好好听。朝堂的事离我们很遥远，想那么多干什么？”
　　高颎道：“离你们不遥远。李二郎，你还想到什么？”
　　李世民皱眉苦思了一会儿，道：“难道杨公也是权臣，试图在朝中一手遮天？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“没有。杨公谨小慎微。”
　　李世民道：“那就是杨公名声太好，声望太过？”
　　李玄霸继续摇头：“不是。杨公自当今皇帝继位后，一直对外宣扬贪财好色的名声，时人皆鄙夷。”
　　李世民眉头皱得更紧：“这是本性还是自污？无论是什么，杨公都对陛下没有威胁啊。虽然杨公是个很厉害的大将军，但杨公不仅已经入朝，还已经年老。且杨公对陛下忠心耿耿……想不明白，唉，想不明白。”
　　高颎攥紧了手中的书，面色仍旧平静：“李三郎，你如何想？”
　　李玄霸看了高颎的表情一会儿，心里挣扎了一下，垂首看着桌面：“此事不在杨公是否对陛下有威胁，而在陛下心中如何想。大约是杨公功劳太大，大到了陛下看着就难受的地步。陛下对拥立他上位的功臣都如此，对原本与他有芥蒂之人不知道会如何。”
　　高颎在李玄霸话说了一半时，就神色大变：“三郎慎言！”
　　李世民愣了一下，扑上去捂住弟弟的嘴。
　　但李玄霸还是完整地把自己想说的话说出来了。
　　他静静地抬头直视着高颎的眼睛。
　　高颎与李玄霸对视。
　　他早就察觉了。李玄霸有一双与七岁孩童不符的沉静双眼。
　　虽他见过许多文静的孩子，但“文静”“安静”和“沉静”是不同的。前者只是“静”，后者更在于“沉”。
　　没有经历许多事，不该有一双“沉静”的双眼。
　　高颎这样有智慧的人，不会听不出李玄霸的意有所指。何况李玄霸说得一点都不委婉。
　　他又想起，太子劝他和宇文弼退一步时，似乎隐晦有提到李玄霸和李世民曾在陛下那里听到了什么。
　　高颎道：“三郎，你是想说，陛下对我也起了杀心吗？”
　　李世民看看弟弟，又看看老师，把李玄霸的嘴捂得更死了。
　　“怎么可能！老师别胡思乱想，当今陛下英明神武心胸开阔有容人之才，老师又是举世大贤，陛下一定会厚待老师！”李世民嘴皮子飞快翻动，连珠般地说了一串。
　　李玄霸想把哥哥捂嘴的手扯开。他不仅没扯开，李世民还加了一只手。
　　李玄霸：【放开！你捂着我鼻子，快憋死了！】
　　“啊！”李世民赶紧松开手。
　　李玄霸大喘气。
　　李玄霸，七岁卒于被二哥李世民捂死。
　　二哥，你这辈子七岁就想有杀弟壮举了吗！
　　“好了，老师不问了。”高颎连忙帮李玄霸顺气，瞪了李世民一眼，“你小心些！”
　　李世民瘪嘴：“阿玄才该小心些。”
　　高颎敲了李玄霸的脑袋一下：“是啊，你也该小心些。”
　　李世民不瘪嘴了，他咧嘴笑道：“哈哈哈，阿玄，你也被敲脑袋了。你的脑袋硬度上升了吗？”
　　李玄霸：“……”二哥小气鬼，这点口舌都要争回来。
　　他道：“我以后一定小心谨慎。”
　　李世民插嘴：“老师，以前阿玄和我说过，以后一定的意思是，以后也不一定。”
　　李玄霸：“哥，你故意找我吵架是不是？”
　　李世民摊手：“老师，你看阿玄，他恼羞成怒了！”
　　李玄霸拳头硬了。
　　高颎转手敲了一下李世民的脑袋，让他闭嘴：“都闭嘴。我看这课上不下去了。”
　　说完，高颎开始布置功课。
　　他布置了三倍的功课，连李玄霸的脸色都苍白了。
　　老师这是故意惩罚他们吧！
　　两个孩子垂头丧气地手拉手走了，没心情吵架。
　　说是手拉手，其实每次都是李世民大步向前，拖着走路很慢的李玄霸往前走。
　　高颎捋了捋胡子，他嘀咕道：“李二郎的力气那么大，难道是从小拖李三郎练出来的？”
　　他嘀咕完，摇摇头，失笑。
　　看见这一对活宝双生子，他本来应该抑郁的心情，都抑郁不起来了。
　　高颎坐着沉思了许久，驱车去找宇文弼。
　　这个坏心情，他得找人分享。
　　虽然宇文弼当年没有站在前太子那边，但也没有支持当今陛下，还多次对陛下的政策不满。如果陛下心眼小，宇文弼一定也会被记恨。
　　何况，宇文弼与自己交好，一定会被自己连累。
　　高颎想着宇文弼可能出现的表情，苦中作乐地笑了。
　　……
　　李世民和李玄霸去宇文弼家中上课时，虽然宇文弼什么都没说，但也给两个孩子布置了三倍功课。
　　虞世南听了两个孩子对增加功课的抱怨后，也给两个孩子布置了三倍功课。
　　“高公和宇文公一定是认为你们的学习进度应该将功课增加到三倍了。”虞世南正气凛然道。
　　李世民抱着脑袋甩：“老师，你认真的吗？”
　　李玄霸低着头双手捂脸碎碎念：“功课太多了，太多了……”
　　虞世南忍俊不禁。
　　看着两个孩子烦恼真的很有趣，但功课是不能少的。
　　不过后来一段时间，李世民和李玄霸的三位老师都给他们小小地放了一段时间的假。功课假期后交。
　　这样一算，他们的功课量和平时就差不多了。
　　李世民：“阿玄，我感觉好像被老师耍了。”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　虽然还有功课，但有了假期，两人又出门玩了，顺便给三位老师买些礼物，感谢他们的悉心教导。
　　高颎和宇文弼的礼物很好挑选。虞世南正在守孝丁忧，两个孩子挑了许久都不合适。
　　而且虞世南和兄长虞世基住一起，他们还要选一份礼物给虞世基。双份的礼物，加倍的苦恼。
　　虞世南与杨广的宠臣虞世基是亲兄弟。虽然虞世南年幼时就被过继给了没有子嗣的叔父，两者法理上算堂兄弟。虞世基的母亲几月前过世，虞世南伴驾归来得知此事后，也立刻向皇帝请求丁忧。
　　李玄霸和李世民拜访虞世南的时候，见到过虞世基。
　　虞世基和虞世南才华相仿，但性格大不相同。
　　虞世南性格刚直，生活朴素。他除服后归朝后，一直在七品官和从六品官来回打转。
　　虞世基当发现杨广不喜别人谏言后，就谄媚迎合上意，后来会成为杨广最信任的“选曹七贵”之一，生活也逐渐恣意奢靡。
　　李世民在李玄霸耳边叽叽喳喳说老师和兄长的关系有多亲密，还说以后他和阿玄长大了也会如此亲密。
　　李玄霸：【别诅咒我们。】
　　李世民疑惑：“什么诅咒？”
　　李玄霸：【他们品行和追求不同，以后会分道扬镳。虽然住在同一处，但几乎形同陌路。】
　　李世民捂住耳朵：“弟弟。”
　　李玄霸：“嗯？”
　　李世民道：“哥哥不想听。”
　　李玄霸疑惑：“什么？”
　　李世民苦着脸道：“好好的一天，被你毁了。”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　他道：“是你先说的。”
　　李世民捂着耳朵：“闭嘴闭嘴，我可没让你说这些，你附和我不就行了？我不想听我不想听！才不会这样。”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　李玄霸：“我偏要说呢？”
　　李世民道：“那我就在你最喜欢的书上画画！”
　　李玄霸眼睛瞪圆：“哥！你找打！”
　　李世民道：“你之前说什么来着，先撩先贱！”
　　李玄霸深呼吸。这是什么？哈利波特的梗吗？波特！不要用我的咒语攻击我！
　　“你们又怎么了？”李三娘见两个弟弟突然“掉队”，叉着腰走过来道，“这是我在家中最后一次出门玩耍，不准吵架！”
　　李世民和李玄霸互瞪了对方一眼，哼了一声，瓮声瓮气异口同声道：“好。”
　　李三娘失笑。连闹脾气都这么默契，真好玩。
　　“三娘，二郎，三郎，终于找到你们了！”一个气喘吁吁的声音从他们身后响起。
　　李玄霸顺着声音看去，杨昭正喘着气走过来，丝绸衣服都汗湿了。
　　李玄霸又看向不远处的马车。那应该是太子微服私访的马车。
　　这才几步路？
　　“我今日去唐国公府找二郎和三郎，想告诉你们，你们想要的地已经过户了。”杨昭擦着头上的汗道，“听你们出门玩耍，正好来寻你们，去看地。去吗？”
　　李三娘爽朗笑道：“表兄都来邀请了，怎么能不去？二郎，三郎，你们有自己的地了，开心吗？”
　　李世民道：“是三郎的，和我无关。”
　　李玄霸道：“对，和二哥无关。”
　　李世民转头瞪向李玄霸：“你好小气！之前明明说有我一半！”
　　李玄霸道：“不是你说的与你无关？”
　　“好了，之前刚说好的不吵架！”李三娘抬起拳头，在两个弟弟头顶上各砸了一下。
　　“哎哟！”乘以二。
　　杨昭笑道：“对，不准吵架。走，我带你们去看地。三郎，你想要的地虽然贫瘠，但分属很多人家，要凑齐还真不容易。现在能告诉表兄，你想做什么了吗？我不信你拿一片长不住粮食的地只是因为谦虚谨慎。”
　　背景板柴绍：“什么什么？”
　　杨昭笑眯眯道：“和你无关，别打听。”
　　“哦。”柴绍无奈，“你们是表兄弟，我就只是个外人是吗？我不也是你表妹夫……啊嗷！”
　　李世民和李玄霸同时出拳，一同击中柴绍的腹部。
　　柴绍捂着肚子弯腰。
　　杨昭没忍住，放声大笑。
　　李三娘嗔怒地瞪了柴绍一眼，也忍不住笑。
　　李世民：“我阿姊还没和你成亲！闭嘴！不准污我阿姊清白！”
　　李玄霸：“闭嘴。”
　　杨昭：“哈哈哈哈哈，二郎三郎说得对。”
　　李三娘：“哼！”
　　柴绍苦笑着告饶。
　　“好了，别吵了。”杨昭再次重复了他的问题，“三郎，你要那片不毛之地做什么？一定是很有趣的事。”
　　李玄霸在心中苦笑。
　　李玄霸：【哥，太子也太敏锐了。】
　　李世民的手指敲了敲大腿，当作点头。
　　李玄霸：【谁说太子性格软。这叫性格软？绵里藏针也叫软？】
　　李世民的手指左右摇晃。
　　李玄霸：【好吧，不能叫绵里藏针。】
　　“三郎？”杨昭微笑着催促，“表兄出了这么大的力，不会还要瞒着表兄吧？就算你现在瞒着我，之后我还不是会知道？我只是想提前满足好奇心。”
　　李玄霸道：“我不是瞒着表兄，只是没想好怎么说。”
　　杨昭道：“那你慢慢想？”
　　李玄霸装作沉思了一会儿，道：“我要在那片土地做比澡豆更好的沐浴用品，叫香皂。”
　　杨昭疑惑：“什么香皂？”
　　李玄霸道：“香味的香，皂角的皂。”
　　李玄霸选的那块地位于原本的长安城。
　　隋文帝定都长安后，原本的长安当了几百年的都城，地下水盐碱化十分严重，根本无法饮用，所以在东南方的龙首原南坡新建大兴城。
　　原本的长安城因土地盐碱化破败，变成了罕有人烟的村落。
　　但因为勋贵原本住在旧长安城，所以长安城附近的土地都在勋贵手中。虽然他们搬家后，这些盐碱化严重的土地没了用处，杨昭想要把它们全部买下，也颇费了一些功夫。
　　李玄霸选择老长安城的地，一是因为这块地无人想要，他拿了也不会引起嫉妒；二是这片土地可以制造土碱，土碱过滤后就能制作凝固的香皂。
　　而且这片区域虽然种稻麦粟很难丰收，只能种大豆。大豆却是非常好的油料作物，正好可以榨油做皂基。
　　虽然大豆油含有大量亚油酸，会导致肥皂三个月后就会逐渐变软出油。但那不是更好吗？
　　买得起他香皂的人，一块香皂难道还想用四五个月？那太丢贵族的脸了。
　　“只是澡豆？”杨昭不愿意相信，李玄霸就这点追求。
　　李玄霸道：“是香皂，不是澡豆。”
　　杨昭摇摇头：“有区别吗？宫中所用的澡豆混合了数十种花瓣、香料、药材磨成的粉。你还能做出比这更好的澡豆？贵族家的澡豆都是自己制作，不会向他人买。难道你还想卖给寻常百姓？”
　　李玄霸道：“到时候表兄就知道了。现在只凭嘴说，也说不清楚。”
　　杨昭眨了眨眼，胖乎乎的脸上出现了一个狡黠的神情：“要不要打个赌？”
　　李玄霸立刻摇头：“不赌，赌博不好。”
　　杨昭没想到李玄霸完全不应，被噎得说不出话来。
　　“咳，孤以太子的身份命令你，来，三郎，和表兄打个赌。”杨昭干咳了一声，笑道，“如果你真的能做出来比宫里更好的澡豆，孤就让你的澡豆成为御贡品。”
　　李世民上下挥了挥手，完全不给太子面子地打断道：“可是表兄，如果阿玄做出了比宫里更好的澡豆，就肯定会进献给陛下，让我们的澡豆成为御贡品啊。你这赌资一点都不诚心。”
　　李玄霸：“我不想打赌。”
　　杨昭捏了捏自己的双下巴：“有道理。那……如果三郎赢了，我就准许三郎随时进出宫中藏书阁？”
　　李玄霸：“这个可以有！啊不，我不赌！”
　　李世民摇头：“表兄，若三郎想进宫读书，不就是给陛下写封信的事？陛下才不会不让晚辈进宫借书呢。”
　　杨昭烦恼了：“好像也是啊。那二郎说说，想赌什么？”
　　李玄霸：“我都说了不赌了！”
　　李世民道：“当然是骏马……哎哟！”
　　李玄霸狠狠揪起二哥的脸颊，拉扯得老长然后松手：“我说了我不赌！”
　　李世民揉着弹回来的脸颊软肉：“阿玄，太子的命令，你怎么能不遵守？耶耶和娘亲知道了，肯定会揍你。”
　　李玄霸语塞。
　　杨昭又干咳了一声，附和道：“没错，这是太子的命令！”
　　李世民揉着脸道：“说好了，我要骏马！”
　　李三娘笑眯眯道：“阿姊想要一套宝石头面。”
　　柴绍立刻道：“我送你！”
　　李三娘脸上的笑容消失：“闭嘴，我在和弟弟玩闹。”
　　“哦。”柴绍蔫哒哒道。
　　杨昭笑道：“好，骏马和宝石首饰。阿玄，你还想要什么？当然，御贡资格和进藏书阁的资格也给你。”
　　李玄霸叹了口气，道：“祖母、娘亲和家中几位阿姊各一套首饰，父亲和家中兄长各一匹骏马，两个弟弟各一套贡品笔墨纸砚，我……”
　　他想了想，道：“我没什么想要的。”
　　杨昭摇头：“不行，快说说你想要什么。”
　　李世民和李三娘连连点头：“对，你必须想一个。”
　　李玄霸又叹了口气，道：“行吧。这门生意，我名义上是让阿姊来做。若做成了，就会拉上娘亲。如果表兄看得上，可否让太子妃也入一手？算是为我们保驾护航了。”
　　杨昭笑道：“那岂不是我赚了？我说动母后为你保驾护航吧。该我了。如果你做不出来，给我家侑儿当伴读可好？”
　　李玄霸背部一僵。
　　杨侑，太子第三子，去年刚出生，将来会被李渊扶持上位又被逼退位最后据说是被李渊毒死。
　　这倒是无所谓。
　　关键是，太子已经有两个儿子，长子杨倓颇受杨广偏爱。以杨广的性格，恐怕是更乐意为自己喜爱的孩子铺路，不会管什么嫡庶。
　　李玄霸严肃道：“表兄，我不想卷入夺嫡。”
　　杨昭叹气：“我知道。这是太子妃的请求，我不能拒绝。所以你努力做出更好的澡豆吧。你很有信心，不是吗？”
　　李玄霸：“……”不太好拒绝了啊。

Chapter 26: Forced into a Bet with the Crown Prince

The Prince of Chu whom Yang Guang and Yuwen Shu spoke of was named Yang Su.

This Yang Su possessed quite a presence in various literary works of later generations, though this presence... well, it was always tinged with a rather vibrant shade of green.

In the Tang Dynasty anecdotal novel *Benshi Shi* (Poems of Incidents) written by Meng Qi, Yang Su's beloved concubine, Princess Lechang, longed for her former husband, Xu Deyan. Yang Su allowed Princess Lechang to reunite with her ex-husband, giving rise to the idiom "the broken mirror made whole again."

In the Tang Dynasty anecdotal novel *Sui Tang Jiahua* (Stories of the Sui and Tang) by Liu Su, Yang Su's favored concubine fell for Li Baitong. They went so far as to carry on an affair right inside Yang Su's manor, only to be caught red-handed by Yang Su himself. Yet, seeing that Li Baitong was a brilliant young talent, Yang Su simply gifted his favored concubine to him, "helping others fulfill their wishes."

In the late Tang romance novel *Qiuran Ke Zhuan* (The Legend of the Curly-Bearded Guest) by Du Guangting, Yang Su's courtesan, Hongfu, eloped with Li Jing. Once again, Yang Su gladly blessed Hongfu and Li Jing, giving rise to the tale of "Hongfu's Night Elopement."

Of these three stories well-known to later generations, except for "the broken mirror made whole again"—which, despite lacking records in official history, was historically plausible—"helping others fulfill their wishes" and "Hongfu's Night Elopement" were entirely fictional.

Li Biyao hailed from the Li clan of Boling. At the age of twenty-eight, he inherited the title of Duke of Anping County and served as the Secretariat Drafter for Crown Prince Yang Yong. After Yang Guang ascended the throne, he was marginalized and exiled. Li Jing hailed from the Danyang branch of the Longxi Li clan, one of the prestigious "Five Clans and Seven Lineages," and was by no means the commoner scholar depicted in *The Legend of the Curly-Bearded Guest*. Both were sons of noble, influential families.

Setting aside the fact that both men were of noble birth and proud character, making them highly unlikely to engage in illicit affairs or elopements, if they had actually taken a liking to someone, they only needed to mention it casually to Yang Su, and he would have gladly gifted them the beauty.

Although it remains a mystery why Tang Dynasty writers were so keen on painting Yang Su's head green in their stories, the fact that they always wanted to steal beauties from his household—and, after doing so, still had Yang Su act as a generous patron who bestowed offices and wealth upon the protagonists—showed just how immense Yang Su's power was during the Sui Dynasty.

Yang Su had repeatedly won military distinctions under Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, and had already attained high office and immense power during Emperor Wen's reign. Not only was he himself enfeoffed as the Duke of Yue, but his sons were also granted noble titles by Emperor Wen due to his achievements.

He then assisted Yang Guang in seizing the heir-apparent position and easily helped Yang Guang suppress the rebellion of Yang Liang, the Prince of Han. Yang Guang showered him with countless lavish rewards.

Yang Su's power reached its absolute zenith in the first year of the Daye era.

Yet, after reaching its peak, the sheer speed of his decline caught Yang Su completely off guard.

Once Yang Su had helped Yang Guang secure the throne, in Yang Guang's mind, Yang Su became a threat to the stability of his imperial rule.

Even though Yang Su had committed no errors and had actively presented his weaknesses to Yang Guang—amassing vast estates and beautiful concubines, and even doing bizarre things like tearing down houses in the morning only to rebuild them at night to draw public disdain—Yang Guang remained deeply wary of him.

In the second year of the Daye era, the Grand Astrologer submitted a memorial to Yang Guang, stating, "There is a sign of a great mourning in the celestial division."

People of that era believed deeply in prophecy and omenology. The Grand Astrologer was not actually a dedicated historian, but rather the official "court astrologer." "Celestial division" (fenye) was an astrological term passed down from the pre-Qin period, which divided the constellations in the sky into twelve stellar regions corresponding to territories on earth to predict fortune and misfortune.

The name of the Sui Dynasty was derived from the "State of Sui," which shared the "Yi and Zhen" celestial division with the State of Chu. Both Emperor Wen of Sui and Yang Guang believed in this, which was why there was no Prince of Chu or Duke of Chu in the Sui Dynasty.

Upon hearing the Grand Astrologer's report, Yang Guang quickly changed Yang Su's title, making him the very first Duke of Chu in the Sui Dynasty.

Yang Su immediately understood the Emperor's intent.

Emperor Wen of Han had once led his ministers to weep his maternal uncle to death. Yang Guang's move was much the same as Emperor Wen of Han's; he was telling Yang Su that if he chose to die now, he could still preserve some dignity for himself and his clan.

Thus, not long after being enfeoffed as the Duke of Chu, Yang Su fell ill.

While Yang Guang dispatched famous physicians to treat Yang Su, he secretly pried into Yang Su's condition and his reaction to the matter.

After hearing the news Yuwen Shu brought back, Yang Guang felt some anger at Yang Su's resentment. However, since Yang Su had at least submissively embarked on the path laid out for him, Yang Guang magnanimously forgave him.

As long as Yang Su died, he could still treat Yang Su's clan generously.

Yang Guang said to Yuwen Shu, "If Yang Su does not die, We will surely exterminate his clan!"

Yuwen Shu said respectfully, "Please put your mind at ease, Your Majesty. Yang Su certainly will not dare not to die."

Yang Guang snorted coldly. "We hope he knows what is good for him."

In Daxing City, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba also learned of this matter, which was bound to cause a massive sensation throughout the court and the common populace.

At this moment, Gao Jiong was holding a scroll, tapping Li Shimin on the head with it.

Li Shimin was highly intelligent, but ever since he got his little horse, he had been somewhat unable to settle down and study. In this latest assessment, Gao Jiong had once again spotted traces of "rushed work."

Although Li Shimin had completed his schoolwork and mastered the knowledge well enough, teachers of this era did not just look at the results; they also valued the process.

Attitude was of paramount importance.

Li Shimin's attitude toward studying was simply improper, so his head had to be tapped.

When Gao Jiong left Daxing, he had already sensed that the atmosphere between the Emperor and Yang Su was somewhat strange, so he had left people behind to observe Yang Su's movements.

When the family servant arrived to deliver the letter, he cast a glance at Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Gao Jiong asked, "Is it about the Duke of Yue?"

The servant cupped his fists. "Yes."

Gao Jiong said, "There is nothing about the Duke of Yue's affairs that cannot be known by outsiders. Speak freely."

The servant weighed his words in his mind and said briefly, "His Majesty has changed the Duke of Yue's title to the Duke of Chu, with a fief of two thousand five hundred households."

Gao Jiong nodded and said, "Understood. You may go."

After the servant left, Li Shimin, who acted as if nothing had happened despite just having his head tapped, asked curiously, "Teacher, who is the Duke of Yue?"

Li Xuanba was speechless. "Brother, you don't even know of the Duke of Yue, Lord Yang Su?"

Li Shimin thought for a moment and said, "If you say 'Lord Yang,' then I know. I also know that changing the Duke of Yue to the Duke of Chu is a lavish reward!"

Li Xuanba muttered, "It should have been."

The highest titles for princes and dukes were the names of the states from the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods. The status of these princely and ducely titles was ranked based on the strength of those ancient states.

For example, the "Tang" in "Duke of Tang" was an obscure, minor state during the Spring and Autumn period, so its status was lower than the "Yue" in "Duke of Yue," which was one of the Five Hegemons.

The highest tier of noble titles naturally consisted of Qin, Jin, Chu, Qi, Wei, Yan, Zhao, and Han, with Qin, Jin, and Chu occupying a tier of their own. Thus, Yang Su's change from the Duke of Yue to the Duke of Chu should have been a "promotion."

Although Gao Jiong was advanced in years, his hearing was exceptionally sharp. Even though Li Xuanba had muttered very softly, he still heard it.

"Li Sanlang, why do you say 'should have been'?" Gao Jiong asked.

His conclusion had been the same as Li Shimin's, so he had not paid much attention after hearing the servant's news, assuming that the strange atmosphere he had previously sensed between the Emperor and Yang Su was just an illusion, and that this sovereign and minister remained very close.

However, having already witnessed Li Xuanba's extraordinary political acumen while teaching him, Gao Jiong wanted to hear his disciple's opinion.

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and did not hide his brilliance. "When Second Brother and I accompanied the imperial carriage back to the Eastern Capital of Luoyang, the Grand Astrologer once submitted a memorial to His Majesty, saying, 'There is an aura of great mourning in the celestial division.'"

Li Shimin scratched his head. "Did that happen? Uh... wait? I remember now! It really did! Back then, Xuan, you even let out a sigh! I remember it very clearly!"

Gao Jiong murmured to himself, "Celestial division... celestial division..."

Li Shimin suddenly cried out in surprise, "Ah! Aren't the State of Chu and the State of Sui in the exact same celestial division?!"

Gao Jiong's hand instinctively loosened, and his book slipped.

Before the book could hit the ground, Li Shimin darted forward by reflex and caught it.

"Here, Teacher!" Li Shimin said, beaming with pride.

Gao Jiong: "..."

Li Xuanba: "..."

The atmosphere had originally been quite solemn, but now it was impossible to keep it that way.

Gao Jiong took the book back expressionlessly and tapped Li Shimin on the head once more.

Li Shimin clutched his head in confusion. "Teacher, why did you tap me again?"

Gao Jiong said, "Nothing. It was just convenient."

Li Shimin huffed and puffed in annoyance, then climbed back onto the low couch to sit down.

Li Xuanba patted his second brother's head.

Li Shimin: "...What are you doing?"

Li Xuanba said, "Checking to see if the hardness of Second Brother's skull has evolved."

Li Shimin shook his fist threateningly at Li Xuanba. *Mock your brother, and watch out or I'll tap your head too.*

Seeing that his second brother was about to strike, Li Xuanba quickly changed the subject. "Teacher, shall we pause today's lesson for now?"

Gao Jiong shook his head and said, "We continue. We will change the lesson today; I will tell you about Emperor Wen of Han."

Gao Jiong resumed his lecture.

When he reached the part where Emperor Wen of Han wept at the funeral of his still-living uncle, Li Shimin mumbled, "That sounds so much like what His Majesty is doing now. But isn't Lord Yang a favored minister of His Majesty?"

Li Xuanba reminded him, "Second Brother, just listen to the lesson properly. The affairs of the imperial court are far removed from us. Why think so much about them?"

Gao Jiong said, "They are not far removed from you. Li Erlang, what else did you think of?"

Li Shimin knit his brows and pondered for a moment, then said, "Could it be that Lord Yang is also an overbearing minister who tried to cover the sky with one hand in the court?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "No. Lord Yang is extremely cautious and prudent."

Li Shimin said, "Then is it because Lord Yang's reputation is too good, and his prestige too high?"

Li Xuanba continued to shake his head. "No. Ever since the current Emperor ascended the throne, Lord Yang has constantly publicized a reputation for greed and lust, earning the disdain of everyone at the time."

Li Shimin's brow furrowed even tighter. "Is that his true nature, or is he self-tarnishing? Whichever it is, Lord Yang poses no threat to His Majesty. Although Lord Yang is a formidable general, he has not only entered the civil court but is also advanced in years. Moreover, Lord Yang is fiercely loyal to His Majesty... I don't understand. Sigh, I just don't understand."

Gao Jiong gripped the book in his hand tightly, his expression remaining calm. "Li Sanlang, what do you think?"

Li Xuanba observed Gao Jiong's expression for a moment. After a brief internal struggle, he lowered his head to look at the table. "This matter does not lie in whether Lord Yang poses a threat to His Majesty, but in what His Majesty thinks in his heart. It is likely that Lord Yang's achievements are simply too great—so great that His Majesty finds it unbearable just to look at him. If His Majesty treats the meritorious ministers who helped him ascend the throne like this, one wonders how he will treat those with whom he originally held grudges."

Halfway through Li Xuanba's words, Gao Jiong's expression changed drastically. "Sanlang, watch your words!"

Li Shimin was taken aback, then lunged forward to cover his brother's mouth.

Yet, Li Xuanba still managed to finish saying exactly what he wanted to say.

He quietly raised his head and looked straight into Gao Jiong's eyes.

Gao Jiong met Li Xuanba's gaze.

He had long since noticed it. Li Xuanba possessed a pair of calm, deep eyes that did not belong to a seven-year-old child.

Although he had seen many quiet children, there was a difference between being "gentle," "quiet," and "profoundly calm." The former two were merely quiet, while the latter carried a heavy depth.

Without having experienced many things, one should not possess such profoundly calm eyes.

A man of wisdom like Gao Jiong could not fail to catch the underlying meaning in Li Xuanba's words. Moreover, Li Xuanba had not been subtle in the slightest.

He also recalled that when the Crown Prince advised him and Yuwen Bi to take a step back, he had seemingly made a veiled reference to something Li Xuanba and Li Shimin had overheard from His Majesty.

Gao Jiong said, "Sanlang, are you trying to say that His Majesty has also harbored murderous intent toward me?"

Li Shimin looked at his brother, then at his teacher, and clamped his hand even tighter over Li Xuanba's mouth.

"How could that be! Teacher, do not let your thoughts wander. Our current Emperor is wise, martial, broad-minded, and possesses the capacity to tolerate talent. And you, Teacher, are a great sage of the world; His Majesty will surely treat you with great favor!" Li Shimin's tongue moved incredibly fast, rattling off a string of words like a rapid-fire stream.

Li Xuanba tried to pull his brother's hand away from his mouth. Not only did he fail to pry it off, but Li Shimin even added his other hand.

Li Xuanba: *Let go! You're covering my nose, I'm about to suffocate!*

"Ah!" Li Shimin hastily let go.

Li Xuanba gasped heavily for air.

*Li Xuanba, died at age seven from being suffocated by his second brother, Li Shimin.*

*Brother, are you trying to achieve the grand feat of fratricide at the tender age of seven in this lifetime?!*

"Alright, I won't ask further." Gao Jiong hurriedly helped pat Li Xuanba's back to ease his breathing, then glared at Li Shimin. "Be more careful!"

Li Shimin pouted. "Xuan is the one who needs to be careful."

Gao Jiong tapped Li Xuanba on the head. "Indeed, you should be careful too."

Li Shimin stopped pouting and grinned widely. "Hahaha! Xuan, you got your head tapped too! Has the hardness of your skull increased?"

Li Xuanba: "..." *Second Brother is such a petty miser, he just has to win every little verbal dispute.*

He said, "I will definitely be cautious and prudent in the future."

Li Shimin chimed in, "Teacher, Xuan told me before that 'definitely in the future' actually means 'not necessarily in the future.'"

Li Xuanba: "Brother, are you picking a fight with me on purpose?"

Li Shimin shrugged. "Teacher, look at Xuan. He's flying into a rage out of shame!"

Li Xuanba's fists clenched.

Gao Jiong turned and tapped Li Shimin on the head to shut him up. "Both of you, quiet. I see this lesson cannot go on."

With that, Gao Jiong began assigning homework.

He assigned triple the usual amount of homework, causing even Li Xuanba's face to turn pale.

*Teacher is definitely punishing us on purpose!*

The two children walked away hand-in-hand, utterly dejected and in no mood to bicker.

Though they were said to be hand-in-hand, it was actually Li Shimin taking large strides forward every time, dragging along the slow-walking Li Xuanba.

Gao Jiong stroked his beard and muttered, "Li Erlang's strength is so immense. Could it have been trained from dragging Li Sanlang around since childhood?"

After muttering this, he shook his head and laughed.

Seeing this pair of comical twins, any depression he was supposed to feel vanished completely.

Gao Jiong sat in deep thought for a long while before taking a carriage to find Yuwen Bi.

This bad mood was something he had to share with someone.

Although Yuwen Bi had not sided with the former Crown Prince back then, he had not supported the current Emperor either, and had repeatedly expressed dissatisfaction with the Emperor's policies. If the Emperor was petty-minded, Yuwen Bi would surely be targeted as well.

Moreover, Yuwen Bi was close friends with him, so he would certainly be implicated by association.

Thinking of the expression that might appear on Yuwen Bi's face, Gao Jiong smiled, finding joy in his sorrows.

...

When Li Shimin and Li Xuanba went to Yuwen Bi's manor for lessons, although Yuwen Bi said nothing, he also assigned the two children triple the homework.

After Yu Shinan heard the two children's complaints about the increased workload, he also assigned them triple the homework.

"Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen must have believed that your learning progress warrants tripling your schoolwork," Yu Shinan said with righteous solemnity.

Li Shimin clutched his head and shook it wildly. "Teacher, are you serious?"

Li Xuanba lowered his head, covering his face with both hands as he muttered repeatedly, "Too much homework, too much..."

Yu Shinan could not help but chuckle.

Watching the two children fret was indeed highly amusing, but the schoolwork could not be reduced.

However, over the subsequent period, the three teachers of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba all granted them a brief holiday. The homework was to be submitted after the break.

Calculated this way, their workload was actually about the same as usual.

Li Shimin: "Xuan, I feel like we've been played by our teachers."

Li Xuanba nodded.

Although they still had homework, now that they had a holiday, the two went out to play again, intending to buy some gifts for their three teachers to thank them for their meticulous guidance.

The gifts for Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were easy to choose. However, Yu Shinan was currently in mourning, and the two children searched for a long time without finding anything suitable.

Furthermore, Yu Shinan lived with his older brother, Yu Shiji, so they also had to select a gift for Yu Shiji. Double the gifts meant double the headache.

Yu Shinan and Yang Guang's favored minister, Yu Shiji, were biological brothers. Although Yu Shinan had been adopted by a childless uncle in his youth—making them cousins in legal terms—Yu Shiji's mother had passed away a few months prior. Upon learning of this after returning from accompanying the imperial carriage, Yu Shinan had immediately requested leave from the Emperor to observe the mourning period.

When Li Xuanba and Li Shimin visited Yu Shinan, they had met Yu Shiji.

Yu Shiji and Yu Shinan possessed similar talents, but their characters were vastly different.

Yu Shinan was upright and lived a simple life. After completing his mourning period and returning to court, he would constantly drift between seventh-rank and lower-sixth-rank official positions.

Once Yu Shiji discovered that Yang Guang disliked being remonstrated, he flattered and catered to the Emperor's whims. He would later become one of the "Seven Nobles of the Selection Bureau" most trusted by Yang Guang, and his lifestyle gradually became extravagant and unrestrained.

Li Shimin chattered in Li Xuanba's ear about how close their teacher and his older brother were, saying that when he and Xuan grew up, they would be just as close.

Li Xuanba: *Don't curse us.*

Li Shimin was puzzled. "What curse?"

Li Xuanba: *Their character and pursuits are different; they will part ways in the future. Though they live in the same place, they will be virtually strangers to each other.*

Li Shimin covered his ears. "Little brother."

Li Xuanba: "Hmm?"

Li Shimin said, "Big brother doesn't want to hear it."

Li Xuanba was confused. "What?"

Li Shimin said with a bitter face, "A perfectly good day, ruined by you."

Li Xuanba: "..."

He said, "You were the one who brought it up first."

Li Shimin kept his ears covered. "Shut up, shut up! I didn't ask you to say all that. Couldn't you just agree with me? I don't want to hear it, I don't want to hear it! It won't be like that at all."

Li Xuanba: "..."

Li Xuanba: "What if I insist on saying it?"

Li Shimin said, "Then I will draw doodles in your favorite books!"

Li Xuanba's eyes widened. "Brother! You're asking for a beating!"

Li Shimin said, "What did you say before? 'He who provokes first is the cheap one'!"

Li Xuanba took a deep breath. *What is this? A Harry Potter reference? Potter! Do not use my own spells against me!*

"What is wrong with you two again?" Seeing her two younger brothers suddenly falling behind, Li Sanniang walked over with her hands on her hips. "This is the last time I get to go out and play before my wedding. No bickering allowed!"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba glared at each other, snorted, and said in unison in muffled voices, "Fine."

Li Sanniang laughed. *Even when throwing tantrums, they are in perfect sync. How amusing.*

"Sanniang, Erlang, Sanlang, I've finally found you!" a panting voice called out from behind them.

Li Xuanba looked toward the sound. Yang Zhao was walking over, gasping for breath, his silk robes completely drenched in sweat.

Li Xuanba glanced at the carriage parked not far away. That was likely the Crown Prince's carriage for traveling incognito.

*He only walked a few steps, and he's already like this?*

"I went to the Duke of Tang's manor today to look for Erlang and Sanlang. I wanted to tell you that the land you wanted has already been transferred to your names," Yang Zhao said, wiping the sweat from his brow. "When I heard you had gone out to play, I came to find you so we could go look at the land. Shall we go?"

Li Sanniang laughed heartily. "Since our cousin has personally come to invite us, how can we not go? Erlang, Sanlang, you have your own land now. Are you happy?"

Li Shimin said, "It's Sanlang's. It has nothing to do with me."

Li Xuanba said, "Correct, it has nothing to do with Second Brother."

Li Shimin turned and glared at Li Xuanba. "You are so stingy! You clearly said before that half of it was mine!"

Li Xuanba said, "Didn't you just say it has nothing to do with you?"

"Alright, we just agreed not to bicker!" Li Sanniang raised her fists and rapped both of her younger brothers on the head.

"Ouch!" times two.

Yang Zhao laughed. "Yes, no bickering. Come, I will take you to see the land. Sanlang, although the land you wanted is barren, it belonged to many different households, so it was no easy feat to gather it all. Can you tell your cousin now what you plan to do with it? I don't believe you took a piece of land that can't grow crops simply out of modesty and caution."

Chai Shao, acting as background scenery, chimed in, "What's this? What's this?"

Yang Zhao said with a smile, "It has nothing to do with you. Don't pry."

"Oh," Chai Shao said helplessly. "You are cousins, so I'm just an outsider, is that it? Am I not also your cousin-in-law... Argh!"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba punched simultaneously, both striking Chai Shao right in the stomach.

Chai Shao clutched his stomach and doubled over.

Yang Zhao could not hold back and burst into hearty laughter.

Li Sanniang glared at Chai Shao in mock anger, but she could not help laughing either.

Li Shimin: "My sister hasn't married you yet! Shut up! Do not tarnish my sister's reputation!"

Li Xuanba: "Shut up."

Yang Zhao: "Hahahahaha, Erlang and Sanlang are right."

Li Sanniang: "Hmph!"

Chai Shao pleaded for mercy with a bitter smile.

"Alright, stop fooling around." Yang Zhao repeated his question once more. "Sanlang, what do you want with that barren wasteland? It must be something very interesting."

Li Xuanba smiled bitterly in his heart.

Li Xuanba: *Brother, the Crown Prince is far too sharp.*

Li Shimin tapped his fingers against his thigh, acting as a nod.

Li Xuanba: *Who says the Crown Prince has a soft personality? You call this soft? Is a needle hidden in silk considered soft?*

Li Shimin's fingers swayed side to side.

Li Xuanba: *Fine, maybe not a needle hidden in silk.*

"Sanlang?" Yang Zhao urged with a smile. "Your cousin went to so much trouble; surely you aren't going to keep it from me? Even if you hide it from me now, won't I find out eventually anyway? I just want to satisfy my curiosity ahead of time."

Li Xuanba said, "I am not hiding it from you, Cousin. I just haven't figured out how to explain it."

Yang Zhao said, "Then take your time to think?"

Li Xuanba feigned deep thought for a moment, then said, "I want to make a bathing product on that land that is even better than bath beans. It is called scented soap."

Yang Zhao was puzzled. "What is scented soap?"

Li Xuanba said, "The 'xiang' of fragrance, and the 'zao' of honeylocust."

The land Li Xuanba had chosen was located in the original city of Chang'an.

After Emperor Wen of Sui established his capital in Chang'an, the original Chang'an, which had served as the capital for hundreds of years, suffered from severe salinization of its groundwater, making it completely undrinkable. Consequently, the new Daxing City was built on the southern slope of Longshou Plain to the southeast.

The original city of Chang'an had fallen into ruin due to the salinization of the soil, turning into sparsely populated villages.

However, because the nobility had originally resided in the old Chang'an, the land near the city remained in their hands. Although these heavily salinized lands became useless after they relocated, it still took Yang Zhao quite a bit of effort to buy them all up.

Li Xuanba had chosen the land of old Chang'an for two reasons: first, because no one wanted this land, so taking it would not arouse jealousy; second, because this land could be used to produce natural soda ash, which, after filtration, could be used to make solid scented soap.

Furthermore, although it was difficult to harvest rice, wheat, or millet in this area, it was suitable for growing soybeans. Soybeans were an excellent oil crop, perfect for pressing oil to make a soap base.

Although soybean oil contained a large amount of linoleic acid, which would cause the soap to gradually soften and exude oil after three months, wasn't that even better?

Would anyone who could afford his scented soap actually want to use a single bar for four or five months? That would be far too embarrassing for a noble.

"Just bath beans?" Yang Zhao was unwilling to believe that Li Xuanba's ambition was so small.

Li Xuanba said, "It is scented soap, not bath beans."

Yang Zhao shook his head. "Is there a difference? The bath beans used in the palace are made from a powder blended from dozens of flower petals, spices, and medicinal herbs. Can you really make bath beans better than that? Noble households make their own bath beans and do not buy them from others. Do you intend to sell them to ordinary commoners?"

Li Xuanba said, "Cousin will know when the time comes. Words alone cannot explain it clearly right now."

Yang Zhao blinked, a sly expression appearing on his chubby face. "How about we make a bet?"

Li Xuanba immediately shook his head. "No betting. Gambling is bad."

Yang Zhao had not expected Li Xuanba to refuse so flatly, leaving him momentarily speechless.

"Ahem, We command you in Our capacity as the Crown Prince. Come, Sanlang, make a bet with your cousin." Yang Zhao cleared his throat and smiled. "If you can truly make something better than the palace's bath beans, We will make your soap an imperial tribute."

Li Shimin waved his hand up and down, interrupting without giving the Crown Prince any face. "But Cousin, if Xuan makes something better than the palace's bath beans, we will definitely present it to His Majesty anyway, making our soap an imperial tribute. Your stake in this bet is not sincere at all."

Li Xuanba: "I do not wish to bet."

Yang Zhao pinched his double chin. "That makes sense. Then... if Sanlang wins, I will grant him permission to enter and leave the imperial library at any time?"

Li Xuanba: "That sounds good! Ah, no, I'm not betting!"

Li Shimin shook his head. "Cousin, if Sanlang wants to read in the palace, isn't it just a matter of writing a letter to His Majesty? His Majesty would never forbid a junior from entering the palace to borrow books."

Yang Zhao grew vexed. "That seems true as well. Then Erlang, tell me, what do you want to bet for?"

Li Xuanba: "I already said I'm not betting!"

Li Shimin said, "A fine steed, of course... Ouch!"

Li Xuanba fiercely pinched his second brother's cheek, pulling it taut before letting go. "I said I am not betting!"

Li Shimin rubbed the soft flesh of his cheek. "Xuan, how can you disobey the Crown Prince's command? If Father and Mother find out, they will definitely beat you."

Li Xuanba was left speechless.

Yang Zhao cleared his throat again and chimed in, "Indeed, this is the Crown Prince's command!"

Li Shimin rubbed his face and said, "It's a deal then, I want a fine steed!"

Li Sanniang said with a smile, "Your sister wants a set of gemstone hair ornaments."

Chai Shao said immediately, "I will gift it to you!"

The smile vanished from Li Sanniang's face. "Shut up, I am playing with my brothers."

"Oh," Chai Shao said, instantly deflating.

Yang Zhao laughed. "Very well, a fine steed and gemstone jewelry. Xuan, what else do you want? Of course, the imperial tribute status and the right to enter the library are yours as well."

Li Xuanba sighed and said, "A set of jewelry each for Grandmother, Mother, and my sisters; a fine steed each for Father and my older brothers; a set of tribute-grade brush, ink, paper, and inkstone each for my two younger brothers. As for me..."

He thought for a moment and said, "I don't really want anything."

Yang Zhao shook his head. "No, tell me quickly what you want."

Li Shimin and Li Sanniang nodded repeatedly. "Yes, you must think of something."

Li Xuanba sighed again and said, "Fine. In name, I will have Sister run this business. If it succeeds, we will bring Mother in. If Cousin thinks well of it, could the Crown Princess also take a share? It would serve as a safeguard for us."

Yang Zhao laughed. "Wouldn't that mean I'm the one profiting? I will persuade the Empress to safeguard you instead. Now it's my turn. If you fail to make it, how about you become a study companion for my son, You'er?"

Li Xuanba's back stiffened.

Yang You, the Crown Prince's third son, was born just last year. In the future, he would be propped up by Li Yuan, forced to abdicate, and ultimately rumored to have been poisoned to death by Li Yuan.

That did not matter much.

The key issue was that the Crown Prince already had two sons, and the eldest, Yang Tan, was highly favored by Yang Guang. Given Yang Guang's personality, he would likely prefer to pave the way for his favorite child, regardless of legitimacy or birth order.

Li Xuanba said solemnly, "Cousin, I do not wish to be embroiled in the struggle for the succession."

Yang Zhao sighed. "I know. This is the Crown Princess's request, and I cannot refuse her. So, work hard to make better bath beans. You are very confident, aren't you?"

Li Xuanba: "..." *This is getting rather difficult to refuse.*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第27章 真当我家破落吗
chunks.chineseText:
第27章 真当我家破落吗

=
　　接下来的路上， 马车中还是有说有笑，只有李玄霸一直沉默。
　　不过李玄霸身体本就羸弱，不爱说话。所以他闭目小憩时， 杨昭也没当回事。
　　只有李世民有些担心。
　　他知道弟弟的“不爱说话”只是不爱张口说话， 弟弟在“心中”是个大话痨。
　　现在连心声都安静了， 不会有什么事吧？
　　但太子在车上，李世民不好询问。
　　他唉声叹气，抱怨弟弟身体不好， 出来逛一会儿街就累了，回去说不定又得喝苦药。
　　“别看阿玄在外面表现得很早熟的模样，回家一喝苦药就闹脾气。”李世民唉声叹气道， “闹脾气就罢了，他还说倒胃口， 不肯吃饭。不好好吃饭， 身体怎么能好？”
　　李三娘心中微怔，然后很自然地跟着叹气：“是啊。”
　　李世民把闭目养神的李玄霸手拿起来，帮李玄霸将袖子撸上去，露出一小截瘦弱的手腕。
　　他撸起自己的袖子：“看，还是双生子呢， 他连手臂都比我小一圈。”
　　李玄霸睁开眼，把袖子放下去：“闭嘴， 我困。”
　　说完，他继续闭眼睡觉。
　　李世民摸了摸鼻子，对杨昭委屈道：“表兄， 你看这个弟弟， 一点都不尊敬我这个哥哥。”
　　杨昭笑道：“亲兄弟是这样。阿玄身体不好， 可有找御医调养？”
　　李世民叹气：“有祖母在， 唐国公府哪可能请不来御医？别说御医，娘亲还去太白山请来了隐居的孙医师。但御医和孙医师都说，养着吧，就是先天体弱而已。”
　　李世民说着说着，鼻头一酸，装的变成了真的。
　　他揉了揉眼睛，嘟囔道：“我看孙医师也不算什么神医，居然说我弟弟很难活到弱冠。太子殿下，你若遇到更好的医师，一定请你告诉我。”
　　杨昭心一沉，他不敢置信地看向又无奈睁开眼的李玄霸，然后将视线投向李三娘。
　　李三娘苦笑：“二郎，你现在说这个干什么？孙医师不还说现在三郎的身体已经好多了？能休养好的。唉，你怎么连三岁的事都还能记到现在？你当时居然还咬了孙医师一口。孙医师现在来家里，还指着说手臂上有个印子呢。”
　　李世民噘着嘴：“哼！”
　　“二哥，若医师实话实说，病人就要胡闹，那医师就不敢治病了。”李玄霸没好气道。
　　李世民的嘴噘得老高：“我不信命！”
　　“不信就不信。”李玄霸把手帕拍在李世民的脸上，“医师就是和命运抢人的战士，是病人和期盼病人痊愈的家属的战友，不可寒战友的心。”
　　“我现在又没咬过他了。”李世民用帕子胡乱擦了擦眼睛，“你不是说困吗？不困了？”
　　李玄霸道：“困。所以别吵。”
　　杨昭叹了口气，道：“我听闻西域有神奇的巫师可以治愈一切疾病，若我遇到了，一定让他给李三郎你看看。”
　　李玄霸：【可别了，你的命就是生病时你父亲叫巫师来给治没的。】
　　李玄霸：“我先谢过表兄了。”
　　李世民疯狂眨眼睛。
　　啊啊啊啊弟弟你又在胡说八道什么！你还不如安安静静呢！
　　杨昭笑道：“再睡会儿吧，表兄还等着看你如何赢得赌注呢。”
　　李玄霸勾起嘴角，像个孩童一样地笑了笑，然后继续闭目小憩。
　　待下马车后，李玄霸恢复了精神。
　　杨昭这个太子不愧众口皆赞。他做事非常妥帖，李玄霸挑不出任何需要补充的地方。只需要把工具做出来，再培训一段时间，李玄霸的香皂工坊就能直接开工。
　　堂堂太子，亲自为两个表弟跑这点小事，怪不得朝堂上下都说他宽仁，有“长者之风”。
　　如果李玄霸是古人，估计也对杨昭很有好感。
　　现在……李玄霸对杨昭甜甜笑道：“谢谢表兄！”
　　杨昭憨厚地笑道：“这是你从父皇那里得来的赏赐，谢我做什么？”
　　李玄霸天真地道：“如果没有表兄为我美言，我才拿不到这么好的地。”
　　杨昭看了一眼附近除了杂草和豆苗什么都长不出来的地。
　　好地？
　　李世民看着弟弟天真可爱的笑容，忍不住搓了搓手臂。
　　来了，来了，又来了。弟弟离开皇帝后好不容易变正常，怎么又来学我了！“学哥精”弟弟退退退！
　　李三娘看了一眼躲在远处表情麻木，衣衫褴褛的百姓，道：“这些人是这块地的佃农？”
　　杨昭道：“除了佃农，还有些奴隶。我一并买下，算是我这个表兄给表弟的礼物。”
　　皇帝说赐地，是赐一片原本属于皇室所有的空地。
　　杨昭不仅给李玄霸换来了有主的地，还连佃农和奴隶一同买了下来。
　　李玄霸心里的气稍稍顺了一些。
　　比起去阴晴不定的杨广那里刷掉落，还是在杨昭这里赚钱更划算。
　　李玄霸给杨昭支招，让他提前回大兴，不是对杨昭有多少好感，而是杨昭能保住对他很好的两位老师。
　　另外，杨广这位皇帝非常不爱待在大兴。除了刚即位还没改元的那一年他老老实实待在大兴，大业一共十四年，他待在大兴的时间加起来都不超过一年，路过太原的时间都比待在大兴的时间长。
　　杨广到处乱跑的时候，先是太子杨昭坐镇大兴，后来是杨昭的幼子，也就是杨昭之前开口想让他当伴读的杨侑坐镇大兴。
　　搭上了杨昭这条线，他在大兴做生意才更顺利。
　　但卷入皇孙斗争？双臂画叉！
　　李玄霸结束了“视察”，与杨昭告别，回到了家中。
　　接下来的事他会先告知母亲，让母亲派信任的人去做。
　　李三娘也和两个弟弟一同回家。
　　柴绍幽怨地看向杨昭：“太子殿下，你今日不该来的。你来了，我和三娘都没能说上话。”
　　杨昭哭笑不得：“你马上就把三娘娶进门了，还在乎这点时间？”
　　柴绍叹气：“你不懂。”
　　杨昭无语。我年纪比你大，有什么你懂我不懂。
　　柴绍叹完气，又道：“太子殿下，你真的想让李三郎当伴读？李三郎那身体……”
　　杨昭摇头：“不是我，是太子妃。父皇偏爱倓儿，太子妃过于忧虑。”
　　柴绍道：“皇长孙生母早逝，一直养在太子妃膝下，太子妃实在是过虑了。”
　　杨昭苦笑：“不，正因如此，她才更忧虑。以父皇性格，很可能会把倓儿过继给她，成为名正言顺的嫡长子。”
　　柴绍本想说太子已经有了嫡子，应该不至于。但思及皇帝去年的行事作风，柴绍也不确定了。
　　他叹息道：“唐国公府是断不愿意趟这浑水。太子殿下，陛下正值春秋鼎盛之年。”
　　“我知道。”杨昭和柴绍十分熟悉，所以说话很直接。
　　他自幼养在祖父膝下，能在宫里如鱼得水，为父皇夺嫡助力，怎么可能看不明白？
　　杨昭道：“我和二弟尚且不敢露出丝毫念头，皇孙就开始争夺储位，父皇一定会迁怒我，认为我在窥伺他的位置。”
　　杨昭捏了捏鼻梁：“所以我必须把这件事压住，不让太子妃胡来。京兆韦氏啊……唉，父皇迁都洛阳是对的。”
　　柴绍心道，那可不一定。
　　关中郡姓因地位不如山东郡姓，所以非常热衷与皇室联姻，希望通过从龙之功压过山东郡姓，所以表现得急躁了些。
　　但山东郡姓难道就清心寡欲了？
　　若洛阳东京的位置稳固，山东郡姓肯定也会做出与关中郡姓差不多的事，试图掺和皇室争斗，为家族争权夺利。
　　虽然柴绍和杨昭很熟悉，君臣之别也让他不会说出心中所有话。
　　他越发想念未婚妻，虽然才分别不到一刻钟。
　　心里堵着话难受，若是三娘子在，我就能和三娘子说了。柴绍再次哀怨。
　　杨昭见柴绍说着说着正事，又莫名哀怨起来，扶额长叹。
　　在柴绍成亲之前，他还是别和柴绍说正事了。
　　李玄霸回到家后，就换衣服爬到床上躺着回血条精力条。
　　李世民不安地围着李玄霸爬了一转。
　　李玄霸双手在腹部合十：【哥，你发什么疯？模仿小狗？】
　　李世民听弟弟终于“说话”，松了口气。
　　他躺在李玄霸身边，也学李玄霸双手在腹部合十：“抱歉啊阿玄，我在马车上替你答应太子……”
　　李玄霸打断道：【太子虽然是以开玩笑的口吻，但都说出“太子的命令”，我若还想借他的势，就该顺从了。是我当时没想到。哥你提醒是对的。】
　　李世民嘟囔道：“原本我以为表兄是好的，没想到他居然如此为难你。他口中的嫡子去年才出生，需要什么伴读？”
　　李玄霸：【只是口头定下伴读的名号，等杨侑六岁启蒙时我才当伴读。太子妃这么急，是因为皇长孙杨倓已经三岁，能熟背《千字文》。杨广曾对群臣说要将杨倓带在身边，提前请名师教导。】
　　李世民叹气：“好吧，我明白了，现在我俩非常受陛下喜爱，她担心陛下会让你我成为杨倓的玩伴？”
　　李玄霸：【不仅如此。现在的太子妃是继室，出身京兆韦氏，是关中郡姓。太子原配为山东“五姓七望”中博陵崔氏。当时秦王妃也是博陵崔氏。】
　　李玄霸用心声给李世民讲起了隋文帝末年伴随夺嫡的一桩后院事件。
　　杨坚的五个儿子，长子、四子、五子的王妃都出自“虏姓”，次子杨广的王妃出自“侨姓”兰陵萧氏，三子秦王杨俊的王妃出自关东“五姓七望”的博陵崔氏。
　　从王妃的出身构成，就能看出各世家在朝堂的势力强弱。那时关中郡姓在朝堂的势力，还不如杨坚平定南方后所需要拉拢的“侨姓”望族。
　　但谁也没想到，秦王妃居然会因杨俊姬妾众多而下毒谋害杨俊。事情暴露，秦王妃赐死。太子妃之父是秦王妃堂兄，被坐罪免官。
　　秦王妃犯的是隋文帝规定的“十恶不赦”的“恶逆”之罪，其家族的“妇德”都被牵连。太子妃是秦王妃侄女，自然也被杨昭请求和离。
　　京兆韦氏这才瞅准机会上位。
　　李玄霸：【杨广建洛阳新城为东京，山东郡姓势头再起。别说京兆韦氏对杨侑很紧张，整个关中郡姓士族肯定都站在杨侑这边。所以太子妃的要求，杨昭也不敢轻易否定。】
　　李世民在床上翻滚了几圈，叹气道：“当太子居然也不能随心所欲吗？”
　　李玄霸：【当皇帝都不能，何况太子？】
　　李世民又翻滚了几圈：“好烦啊，好烦啊，什么世家，好烦啊，一箭射穿！一箭射穿！”
　　李玄霸“扑哧”笑出来。
　　李世民鼓着眼睛不高兴道：“难道你不烦吗？我讨厌被人算计！”
　　李玄霸休息够了，从床上爬起来，心声带了一丝笑意：【京兆韦氏不愧是出了名的眼神不好，他以为你我年幼，就可欺吗？唐国公府难道是什么不起眼的小势力？居然敢来我们头上撒野？】
　　李世民也坐起身：“阿玄说得对！就算‘五姓七望’的荥阳郑氏我们都敢惹，京兆韦氏算什么！要怎么做！”
　　李玄霸摊手：“当然是，告家长！”
　　正跃跃欲试的李世民傻眼：“啊？”
　　李玄霸满脸无辜。我们两个只是七岁的孩子，受欺负了不告诉家长，难道让我们自己去？
　　李世民蔫哒哒地跟着李玄霸一起去告家长。
　　这时李渊正亲自侍奉独孤老夫人。
　　独孤老夫人精神很好，与李渊和窦夫人有说有笑。
　　李世民蔫到了门口，一踏进门槛，就打起了精神，扯着嗓子喊：“祖母！耶耶！娘娘！太子妃欺负我和阿玄！快帮我们报仇！”
　　李世民这一嗓子，把李玄霸已经想好的话都堵在了喉咙里。
　　看着瞬间怒气上脸的祖母、父亲、母亲，李玄霸不由在心中为二哥鼓掌。
　　果然，论告状，假小孩的脸皮还是比不过真小孩啊。
　　李渊还未说话，独孤老夫人一拍床沿，怒气冲冲道：“太子妃？京兆韦氏的那个女人？她做什么了！祖母为你们做主！”
　　李渊皱眉：“太子不是对你们很友善吗？太子妃为何会如此无礼？”
　　窦夫人冷静下来：“先听孩子们说。”
　　李玄霸在心里指导，李世民充当润色和发声器，将今日之事一一告诉三位长辈。
　　李玄霸自己说也行，但他太理智，没有他哥的“稚言稚语”杀伤力大。
　　“今天太子表兄来找我和阿玄，说陛下的地赏下来了，带我们一起去看，本来我们都很高兴。谁知道，太子说，太子妃要让阿玄去给她儿子当伴读。”李世民吸了吸鼻子，“她儿子才刚出生呢，要什么伴读？我家阿玄体弱，哪能当得了伴读？”
　　独孤老夫人、李渊和窦夫人若有所思。
　　李世民喘了几口气，又道：“后来太子表兄透露，是皇长孙得宠，太子妃因耶耶得到了陛下的看重，她想让唐国公府帮她。太子表兄还说这是京兆韦氏的意思，所以他也不好直接拒绝。呜呜呜，他不能拒绝丈人家，就欺负我们吗！我们就不是他的亲戚吗！耶耶还是他的表伯呢！”
　　李世民干嚎起来。
　　“啊？怎么了？”李三娘正好进来，赶紧帮李世民擦眼泪。
　　然后她发现，李世民干嚎不掉眼泪。
　　李三娘愣了愣，用帕子使劲擦了擦李世民的眼角，然后把李世民揽在怀里：“别哭了，乖。”
　　李世民把头埋在三姐怀里，继续干嚎：“呜呜呜。”
　　李玄霸呆呆地站在一旁，有些没跟上二哥的演出。
　　“他不能拒绝丈人家就欺负我们”和“耶耶是他的表伯”可不是自己教的，是二哥即兴发挥。
　　“三娘，你今日跟二郎和三郎一同出门。听二郎和三郎说，太子妃要让三郎当皇孙伴读？”窦夫人道，“真的是太子妃的主意？太子的反应如何？”
　　李三娘道：“我正是因此事来寻祖母和父亲、母亲。”她可琢磨了许久要怎么说。没想到两个弟弟也来了。
　　李三娘叹了口气，道：“太子和三郎打了个赌。三郎不是从书中寻了个古方，说要做更厉害的澡豆吗？太子说，如果三郎能做出来比宫廷御用更好的澡豆，这件事他就帮着推了。”
　　“胡闹！”李渊骂道，“先帝时夺嫡之乱近在眼前！太子都还没继位，他们就想再次掀起夺嫡之乱吗？！”
　　独孤老夫人冷声道：“这太子妃的心也太大了，她连皇后都没当上，就先操心儿子的皇位了？”
　　窦夫人平静道：“京兆韦氏因与太子结亲，陛下给予了他们许多恩赐。他们居然还不知足，不思回报陛下，居然想挑起年幼皇孙的争斗，真是可恶。”
　　李玄霸等他们说完，才开口：“父亲，我最担心的是陛下得知此事后会如何想。陛下虽夺嫡胜利，但同母兄弟除一人被贬为平民之外皆死。如此惨烈，陛下肯定心痛之。他定是不希望此事在儿孙身上重演。”
　　李玄霸抬头看向李渊：“父亲刚得到陛下信任，若陛下误会父亲讨好皇孙，对陛下不忠，该如何是好？陛下在洛阳，父亲在大兴，韦氏却有很多人在洛阳伴驾。就算太子拒绝，他们可能也会直接请求陛下。”
　　独孤老夫人手一撑，惊得从床榻上坐起来。
　　李渊赶紧扶住母亲。
　　“他们怎么敢！”独孤老夫人怒急，“谁阻我儿仕途，我就杀了谁！儿妇！拿我的牌子进宫质问太子妃究竟是何意！不需要给她脸面！她这个太子妃，还不一定能坐上皇后之位！”
　　窦夫人道：“大家，儿妇还想回娘家一趟。”
　　独孤老夫人道：“去吧，也和你家里人好好说说此事。对了，你给郑家和长孙家也说一声。唐国公的事，也是他们的事。”
　　窦夫人应道：“是。”
　　独孤老夫人对李渊道：“我这里不需要你伺候了，赶紧拿我的信去找陛下。”
　　李渊严肃道：“我会和陛下直言，三郎体弱，我实在是不忍心他去宫中当伴读。连高公和宇文公这么严厉的老师，教导三郎时都允许三郎偶尔伏案小睡。”
　　他深呼吸，将怒气从脸上压下：“我李氏一脉确实衰败了，但也还不到会被人欺负的地步。”
　　独孤老夫人道：“先去联系你堂兄李安和李哲的儿子。虽然他们现在已经去世，儿子还未身居高职。但他们二人深受先帝信任看重，朝中有许多大臣都受过他们的恩惠。现在我李氏一族终于有了再起之势，这两家人也该动一动他们的人脉了。”
　　李渊道：“是。”
　　李世民目瞪口呆地从三姐怀里露出双眼睛。
　　李玄霸：【祖母很厉害。】
　　李世民使劲喊道：【对！】
　　李玄霸看向事无巨细叮嘱父亲和母亲的祖母。
　　他虽听说过父亲年幼失怙，朝中局势又正值动荡，偌大的唐国公府就是祖母一人扛起。但他自记事起，祖母就已经是一个常卧病榻，总爱在细枝末节折磨母亲的“恶婆婆”。
　　他是第一次看到祖母对外强势又敏锐的一面。
　　李世民和李玄霸告完状后，就被拘在家中陪即将出嫁的李三娘。
　　李渊道：“这些日子就别出门了。三娘，放心，为父会很快回来，定能赶上你的亲事。”
　　李三娘道：“父亲，路上小心。”
　　李渊点头。
　　李玄霸拉住李渊的衣角。
　　李渊好奇道：“三郎有何想说？”三郎还是第一次对他的离开表露出不舍啊。
　　李玄霸板着脸道：“请父亲对陛下说，不需要为我担心，我一定能赢得赌注，不让陛下为难。这件事就只是小孩子之间的玩笑。”
　　李渊笑道：“好，我一定会将这件事告诉陛下。”
　　他把李玄霸抱起来，揉了揉李玄霸的脑袋：“你和二郎名声越来越大，想邀请你们出门玩耍的人越来越多。等我从洛阳回来，就提前给你们取字，期不期待？”
　　李玄霸点头：“期待。”
　　李世民跳着脚道：“期待！”
　　李三娘微笑，眼中微微露出落寞之色。
　　李玄霸道：“父亲，你也要想好阿姊的字。你和母亲就这一个女儿，阿姊的名字，可不能便宜柴绍。”
　　李世民立刻道：“对啊！书上说女子‘待字闺中’，出嫁前会由丈夫或者父亲取字。耶耶，绝对不能便宜柴绍！阿姊的名字我们自家人取！阿姊嫁出去了也是我的阿姊！是我们家的人！哼！柴绍别想欺负阿姊！”
　　李三娘眨了眨眼，手不由自主抬到了胸口处。
　　她笑道：“柴绍才不敢欺负我，二郎放心。”
　　李渊看向李三娘。
　　李三娘身为他唯一的嫡女，虽然吃穿住用和其他女儿没区别，但他和窦氏感情和睦，对李三娘自然还是更加上心些。
　　“好，我回来也给三娘取字。”李渊笑道，“不能便宜柴绍那小子。三娘你等着，为父一定给你取个最好听的名字！”
　　李三娘重重点头：“嗯！”
　　李渊骑马离开。
　　离开前，他嘱咐李建成：“我知道你和关中郡姓走得很近，在韦氏中更是有多位好友。你此次也闭门不出，先冷落一下你的友人。”
　　李建成拱手道：“儿知道，父亲放心。”
　　他结交的友人都是为了有利仕途，分得清孰轻孰重。
　　何况此次与韦氏发难，对他并无坏处。等此事解决，他安抚一下身在韦氏的好友，修复与韦氏的关系，韦氏一族肯定更加亲近他。
　　在那之前，他可得好好生一回气了。
　　在与世家交往中，他得让那些世家子弟明白，自己才占主导地位！
　　……
　　杨昭傻眼：“啊？你被窦夫人进宫骂了？”
　　韦氏哭泣：“妾让三郎入宫陪伴侑儿，这明明是施恩唐国公府，他们居然如此瞧不起侑儿！妾究竟还是不是太子妃，侑儿究竟还是不是你的嫡子！”
　　杨昭想了想，拍了一下胖胖的大腿：“完了，坏了！我只想到二郎和三郎，没想到李渊和姨婆对此事的态度！特别是姨婆……唉，姨婆亲历了当年的风雨，肯定对此事十分敏锐。二郎三郎回去将此事一告诉姨婆，姨婆就明白了你的小心思！”
　　韦氏哭声一滞，继而哭声更大：“什么叫妾的小心思？是妾和侑儿受辱了啊！”
　　杨昭认真道：“姨婆是祖母唯一还活着的同辈至亲。只要姨婆还活着，别说骂你几句，就是骂我，我都得认真听着。是我疏忽了，姨婆卧病在床，足不出户，我忘记了还有这样一位长辈。”
　　韦氏哭不下去了，她不敢置信道：“只是姨婆而已，难道还能比太子你的身份还高贵！”
　　杨昭冷漠道：“你不懂。”
　　父皇夺嫡上位，兄弟相残，还传出弑父谣言。父皇为了堵住谣言，必须展现出对父母的怀念和孝顺。供奉祖父的天经宫便是为此而建。
　　而唐国公府的独孤老夫人身为祖母唯一还在世的同辈至亲，只要她的要求不过分，父皇都得答应。
　　独孤老夫人又是一个非常有智慧的老人。她从未为自己和李渊求过什么，没有在父皇面前使用过任何“长辈”的特权。
　　所以当独孤老夫人开始使用这个特权，且使用对象不是父皇的时候，父皇绝对会支持独孤老夫人。
　　“太子妃，此事我和你说明白。我本是不同意把年幼的两位表弟拉入宫廷斗争，但我需要给你几分薄面，所以才与三郎打了这个赌。”杨昭平静道，“既然这事传到了姨婆耳中，就不由我们了。你若还想坐稳你的太子妃之位，就随我立刻去东京面见父皇母后。”
　　韦氏支支吾吾道：“有这么严重？那唐国公一族就李渊一个人还有实职在身，其他人皆是散官，不过是破落户……”
　　“太子妃，慎言。”杨昭皱眉打断道，“我知道你们京兆韦氏自诩关中郡姓望族，过于高傲。但皇帝表亲，堂堂公爵，你居然说他们是破落户？京兆韦氏是想公开与唐国公府敌对吗？”
　　“不，不是，妾不是这个意思！”韦氏赶紧道，“妾是说他们人丁稀薄，就算他们想做什么，又怎敢真的与我京兆韦氏作对？”
　　杨昭叹气，心里十分烦恼。
　　他好声好气继续解释道：“此事捅到了父皇那里，父皇多疑，你京兆韦氏肯定无事，就像是现在博陵崔氏也无事一样。但你和你的父亲是否有事，你看我前太子妃父女二人现在如何？”
　　韦氏瞬间面色煞白，不断喃喃道：“有这么严重？怎会如此严重？……”
　　杨昭道：“换身衣服，不用准备行李了，今日就出发。一定要赶在父皇的诏令来之前到洛阳。”
　　他站起来，扶了扶腰间的肉肉。
　　唉，真不想出门啊。
