Chapter 30: Unexpected Yet Successful

=

Gao Jiong was not only accomplished in both civil affairs and military strategy, possessing extraordinary personal ability, but he was also broad-minded and passionate about recommending talented individuals without seeking reward. He possessed an exceptional eye for talent; almost all those he recommended went on to achieve great merit, serving as illustrious generals and prime ministers.

Yang Su had entered the imperial court as an official precisely through Gao Jiong's recommendation.

According to the "dual monarchy theory" of aristocratic clan politics during the Eastern Han and Wei-Jin dynasties, Gao Jiong was Yang Su's "patron" and "nominator." If Yang Su betrayed Gao Jiong, he would be despised by all under heaven.

Take Lü Bu of the Three Kingdoms era, for example. In official history, he never took foster fathers, but he was a subordinate recruited by Ding Yuan. By killing Ding Yuan—his "nominator"—while in office, he earned the utter contempt of his contemporaries. Luo Guanzhong, the author of *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, did not fully understand the officialdom of the Eastern Han. Unable to fathom why others could freely change masters while Lü Bu was reviled, he gave Lü Bu an added "foster father."

After the chaos of the Northern and Southern Dynasties, this "dual monarchy theory" had waned, and the bond between recruited officials and their nominators had weakened. Yet even setting tradition aside, Gao Jiong had shown immense kindness to Yang Su.

Gao Jiong had never realized that Empress Dugu was the one who despised him, while Yang Su had merely been scheming tirelessly behind the scenes. Thus, Gao Jiong had always assumed Yang Su was the sole person slandering him before Emperor Wen of Sui, leading to a deep disdain for Yang Su’s character.

Upon hearing of Yang Su's death, Gao Jiong recalled the period when he had been cast aside by Emperor Wen, laughing so hard that he wept bitterly.

He had originally wanted to personally pay his respects at Yang Su's funeral, but his sons—fearing their father might burst out laughing right in front of Yang Su's memorial tablet—pleaded and coaxed until they finally restrained him, offering sacrifices on his behalf instead.

Gao Jiong had only been rejoicing for a few days before Li Xuanba slammed a heavy blow onto his head, leaving him seeing stars.

Gao Jiong remained dazed for a long while before looking at Li Xuanba, who was still bowing low with hands clasped.

His lips parted slightly, and he said, "Sit down. You have a weak constitution; don't fall over."

A trace of guilt welled up inside Li Xuanba.

*My teacher is a good man. Though unrelated by blood, he treats me with great kindness. What I am doing now amounts to taking advantage of a gentleman's righteous nature.*

Yet Li Xuanba quickly swept the guilt aside. With reddened eyes, he said, "Yes, thank you, Teacher."

Gao Jiong poured a cup of warm water for Li Xuanba. "You shouldn't have told me you possess the gift of prophecy."

Li Xuanba replied, "I hesitated before, but I saw that both Mister Gao and Mister Yuwen will be executed next year for criticizing imperial affairs. Both of you are my revered teachers; I could not remain indifferent."

Gao Jiong’s hand trembled, spilling the water. "Ah? That old rogue Yuwen is going to die too?"

Li Xuanba: "..." *Listening to Mister Gao and Mister Yuwen hurl insults at each other every day, I really can't tell if their relationship is good or bad.*

Li Xuanba added, "Also He Ruobi, the Duke of Song."

This time, Gao Jiong was relatively calm. "Him... with a mouth like his, he certainly invites disaster."

Li Xuanba continued, "Besides the three Dukes, there are others. However, the Heavenly Book only names these three; the rest are grouped under 'and others.'"

Gao Jiong asked, "Heavenly Book?"

Li Xuanba hesitated for a moment before "confessing," "Actually, my prophecies cannot truly be called prophecies. Rather, if I share a close enough bond with someone, the phantom image of a book of prognostication appears before my eyes, allowing me to read that person's future deeds."

Gao Jiong became excited. "Could it be that the *Luoshu*—the Book of the Luo River—has reappeared in the world?!"

Li Xuanba knew Gao Jiong wouldn't doubt him. People of this era placed far too much faith in prognostications and omens.

Li Xuanba shook his head, paused hesitantly, and said, "The book of prognostication isn't called the *Luoshu*. It is called..."

He paused, putting on a nervous expression, and whispered, "...the *Book of Sui*."

Gao Jiong's excited expression froze. "What?"

Li Xuanba whispered, "Teacher's book of prognostication is, cough, well... the *Book of Sui: Biography of Gao Jiong*."

Gao Jiong: "..."

Li Xuanba's gaze was entirely innocent and pure.

Gao Jiong silently wiped the table clean and asked, "Which volume? Which biography?"

Li Xuanba replied, "Volume Forty-One, Liezhuan Six."

The corner of Gao Jiong's mouth twitched. "Not bad. What about that old rogue Yuwen Bi?"

Li Xuanba said, "Volume Fifty-Six, Liezhuan Twenty-One."

Gao Jiong nodded in satisfaction. "That's about the only position he's worthy of."

Now it was Li Xuanba's turn to be speechless. *Mister Gao, do you really have to compete over even this? What is there to compete about? Your status was originally far higher than Mister Yuwen's.*

Gao Jiong asked again, "It's for criticizing imperial affairs, not rebellion?"

Li Xuanba answered, "Not rebellion."

Gao Jiong's mouth twitched again. "If he wants to kill me and Yuwen Bi, even falsely accusing us of rebellion would be better... Ah."

Li Xuanba was puzzled. *How could a false accusation be better?*

Seeing Li Xuanba's expression, Gao Jiong shook his head with a bitter smile. "You don't understand."

Li Xuanba nodded. "This student does not understand."

Gao Jiong instructed, "If he falsely accused Yuwen Bi and me of treason, some in the court might think we were indeed dissatisfied with His Majesty, while others might think His Majesty was merely wary of my ties to the former Crown Prince. Whichever the case, this miscarriage of justice would remain confined to us alone, without heavily impacting the court. But accusing us of criticizing imperial policy is entirely different."

Li Xuanba pondered for a moment and said, "His Majesty executing high officials on charges of criticizing state policy means ministers will be punished for their words—so no one will dare to offer honest counsel in the future?"

Gao Jiong sighed. "Yes. Furthermore, His Majesty's reputation will suffer. The court and the common folk do not care if His Majesty eliminates political rivals, but stifling speech will chill the hearts of virtuous men across the realm. Thus, the Great Sui will be in grave danger."

Li Xuanba could not comprehend Gao Jiong's lamentations at this moment.

*Yang Guang is about to execute him, yet his chief concern is not himself or his family, but Yang Guang's reputation and the safety of the Sui Dynasty.*

*Is this what it means to be noble?*

Rationally, he knew that some people were noble, but emotionally, he found it difficult to grasp.

After lamenting for a while, Gao Jiong asked again, "In the Heavenly Book... heh, the *Book of Sui* you saw, does it mention which words brought about my doom?"

Li Xuanba said, "It was cumulative. Teacher opposed His Majesty's summons of tens of thousands of musicians."

Gao Jiong said, "Emperor Tianyuan of the Northern Zhou perished due to his indulgence in music; that cautionary lesson lies right before our eyes."

Li Xuanba said, "Teacher requested to postpone the construction of the Great Wall, the Grand Canal, and the Eastern Capital."

Gao Jiong said, "Forced labor is rampant, livelihoods are ruined, and grievances fill the roads. I fear popular uprisings will erupt."

Li Xuanba said, "The final straw was His Majesty treating Qimin Khagan with excessive generosity."

Gao Jiong sneered, "Though Qimin Khagan is old, he brought his sons to the Central Plains many times to gather intelligence. Once he dies, his sons—in their prime and thoroughly familiar with our lands—will surely become a catastrophe for the Central Plains."

Li Xuanba said, "Teacher complained that court discipline has recently fallen into disorder."

Gao Jiong spat, "Is it not true?! The ministers in court know only how to flatter His Majesty; whoever flatters best gains power. Setting Yang Su aside—at least he possessed some competence—Yuwen Shu knows nothing of military affairs, yet he is His Majesty's most trusted general! If war ignites on the borders, are we to let that incompetent fool Yuwen Shu lead our armies?!"

Li Xuanba lowered his eyes. "Everything Teacher says is correct."

Gao Jiong closed his eyes, his voice choking up. "But His Majesty will not listen."

Master and disciple sat in mutual silence for a long time.

Only then did Gao Jiong open his eyes. "Did you see how much longer the Sui Dynasty's fortunes will endure?"

Li Xuanba asked, "Does Teacher truly wish to know?"

Gao Jiong replied, "I do."

Li Xuanba said, "The Sui Dynasty's fortunes have less than twenty years remaining. But I cannot speak of what comes next, for following the Sui will be a grand unified dynasty lasting nearly three hundred years, during which Huaxia will return to a golden age. Thus, I cannot allow Teacher to prevent the arrival of this flourishing era."

Gao Jiong: "..."

Gao Jiong scrambled up, walked to Li Xuanba's side, and pressed his hands on Li Xuanba's shoulders. "What?! A golden age is coming in twenty years?!"

Li Xuanba: "...Mm."

Gao Jiong scrutinized Li Xuanba's expression carefully.

Li Xuanba met Gao Jiong's gaze without a trace of fear.

Gao Jiong hesitated for a moment, then asked, "Reading the Heavenly Book—what toll does it take on your body?"

Li Xuanba said, "Physician Sun said I wouldn't live to adulthood. Though now, Physician Sun says my health has improved significantly."

He held out his hands, looking down at his small palms, and said calmly, "Perhaps I will live past twenty, but I will remain sickly like this all my life. Every year I live is a gift from Heaven."

With eyes full of heartache, Gao Jiong said, "Making too many prophecies must surely burden your body."

Li Xuanba said, "My life could end at any moment anyway, so such a burden matters little. Compared to divine retribution, the human disasters following the exposure of my prophetic abilities are what truly terrify me."

Gao Jiong frowned. "Since you knew, you shouldn't have told me."

Li Xuanba said earnestly, "Teacher, my life is like a candle flame flickering in the wind, liable to be extinguished at any moment. If Teacher can be saved, my time in this world will not have been in vain. Regrettably, I have pondered for a long time and could not think of how to save Teacher. I could only share the future with you, adding to your worries—I am truly sorry."

Gao Jiong rubbed Li Xuanba's head. "How could you call this adding to my worries?"

He kept rubbing Li Xuanba's head until his young disciple's head bobbed up and down, his eyes filled with tender affection.

Children could not lie unless taught to do so. And what Li Xuanba said now was something others wouldn't even dare fabricate in a lie.

Right now, the Great Sui was at its peak. Who could imagine that in a mere twenty years, it would collapse?

Yet Gao Jiong believed Li Xuanba's judgment.

Because he himself had judged that if the current Emperor continued his tyrannical, fatuous ways, chaos under heaven was only a matter of time.

After the Great Han, there had never been another grand unified dynasty. Even the Jin Dynasty was teetering on the brink of ruin right at its founding.

During the subsequent chaos of the Northern and Southern Dynasties, dynasties rose and fell so rapidly that Gao Jiong alone had lived through the co-existence of Eastern and Western Wei, Northern Qi and Northern Zhou, and then the Sui—three generations of changes, with the Southern Dynasties shifting even more frequently.

Thus, even though the Great Sui had unified the world once more, no one held an optimistic view on how long it could be maintained.

Under such circumstances, most nobles and aristocrats naturally cared only for flattering the Emperor to reap benefits for their own families, giving no thought to upholding the state or bringing peace and governance to the people.

Gao Jiong asked, "Twenty years from now, will the world truly be swiftly reunited, followed by three hundred years of a golden era?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "Not three hundred years of a golden era, but nearly three hundred years of unified rule—precisely over two hundred and eighty years. The golden era itself lasts only a little over one hundred and thirty years."

Gao Jiong laughed. "A hundred-year golden age! This dynasty can rival the mighty Han!"

Li Xuanba nodded. "Indeed."

Gao Jiong said, "I am already old. If I cannot live to see that moment, tell me before I die who it is that will forge this glorious dynasty."

Li Xuanba nodded vigorously. "Alright. So, Teacher, have you figured out how to survive your mortal crisis?"

Gao Jiong smiled and said, "I haven't."

Li Xuanba was puzzled. "Then why are you smiling, Teacher?"

Gao Jiong patted his disciple's head. "Hearing that a golden age is arriving in twenty years, why shouldn't I smile? Dade, you must never tell anyone else about this in the future. By the way, why didn't you tell your father?"

Li Xuanba said with a stern face, "Father faces no mortal calamity. For most people, knowing the future is no blessing, only a burden. If I had not been completely unable to think of a way to save Teacher, I would not have told you either."

Gao Jiong smiled and sighed. "Indeed. Do not tell Yuwen Bi either. He is too fragile and fiercely loyal to the Great Sui; he is not suited to hear such things. Thankfully, the one you told was me."

Li Xuanba thought to himself: *Mister Yuwen also served as an official in Northern Zhou. How loyal could he really be to the Great Sui?*

*He might not be a loyal subject specifically to the Sui, but he is an upright minister who would cast life and death aside to admonish the Emperor.*

Gao Jiong sighed and lamented for a while. Though he knew he was doomed to die and could think of no way to escape this fatal trap, his face was radiant with smiles.

Li Xuanba could barely keep up his act. This had completely defied his expectations.

Li Xuanba had originally thought Gao Jiong would panic and express doubt, allowing him to lead Gao Jiong into his own rhythm and help him execute certain arrangements.

Although Gao Jiong was currently feared and mistrusted by Yang Guang, his position in court remained. Before Yang Guang took action, Gao Jiong could accomplish many things.

Who could have foreseen that Mister Gao would not only refrain from questioning him, but would also smile broadly without uttering a single word about avoiding his mortal fate? How was Li Xuanba supposed to carry on the conversation?

"This disciple won't tell anyone else. But Teacher, you must quickly figure out a solution—this is a disaster that will wipe out your entire clan!" Li Xuanba feigned being on the verge of crying from anxiety.

Gao Jiong smiled and used his sleeve to wipe Li Xuanba's tears. "What's the rush? This is something that will only happen next year. What I've already done cannot be changed, and as for what I haven't done yet, I'm not sure how I'll act either. We'll see when the time comes. Still, I can speak to that old rogue Yuwen Bi and tell him not to run his mouth in private. We must be cautious."

Li Xuanba: "..." *He really isn't taking the bait.*

In truth, what he had told Gao Jiong was half-true and half-false. Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi indeed suffered execution for their words, but the final straw had not been formal admonishments, but rather gathering in private to complain after multiple failed remonstrances.

It was essentially a few old men drinking wine, eating meat, and venting a few complaints together, only to be reported by an informer and beheaded on charges of slandering imperial administration.

This was actually far more explosive than being punished for annoying the Emperor with advice. Their execution not only proved that Yang Guang could tolerate no criticism, but also revealed that Yang Guang maintained private surveillance over his ministers. The court officials not only dared not remonstrate, but even complaining at home could get them killed.

The unraveling of the Daye era's court had already shown its signs from the third year of Daye, starting with the slander of imperial policy case involving Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and He Ruobi.

After that, Yang Guang's ears became blessedly quiet, and his actions grew increasingly reckless and tyrannical.

However, even without the "slander of imperial policy" case, Yang Guang would still act recklessly; it would simply be a different group of people offering futile advice.

Li Xuanba's "spoilers" had zero impact on the future.

Gao Jiong was already sixty-five years old and might not live until the Tang Dynasty was established to serve his Second Brother.

Li Xuanba's purpose in spoiling the future to Gao Jiong—aside from enticing Gao Jiong to collaborate with him in targeting the Jingzhao Wei Clan—was to make Gao Jiong feel closer to him and Second Brother. That way, if Gao Jiong died naturally of old age, his network of connections would not wither away due to execution and could instead be inherited by him and Second Brother.

Both Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were grand scholars who did not belong to the prominent aristocratic clans; they represented the civil officials among the Northern Dynasties nobility. Since the Northern Dynasties nobility consisted mostly of military commanders, those who gathered around Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were primarily scholars of humble origins.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were also extremely generous, frequently teaching others using Confucian classics annotated by themselves, unlike the aristocratic clans who hoarded their inherited annotated texts. Common scholars studying the classics almost all relied on the annotated texts of these two men.

Once Li Xuanba printed the classics annotated by the two, it could be said that these two men were the grandmasters of Confucian learning for all humble scholars across the land.

As for the military aristocracy, his brother alone was enough to keep them in check. Who could rival his brother's merit in conquering the world? His brother was the supreme military commander; all other generals paled in comparison and dared not disobey.

What the aristocratic clans relied on from their ancestral legacy was the "monopoly on interpreting classics." They were not just political oligarchs, but academic oligarchs.

To suppress military lords required a greater military commander; to suppress academic oligarchs required alternative academic pillars.

Li Xuanba was trapped in an awkward predicament.

*Mister Gao isn't playing by the script. How am I supposed to carry on this play?*

Gao Jiong had already calmed down from his initial shock. He expressed concern for Li Xuanba's health again, carefully advising him on how to conceal his "prognostication" ability, and instructed him once more never to reveal it easily to others.

"You were right not to tell Li Yuan. Although you respect your father, Li Yuan—while decent enough—is indecisive, prone to gullibility, and not as broad-minded as he projects. He cannot keep this secret." Gao Jiong bluntly spoke ill of Li Yuan right in front of Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba could only bow his head and say, "I must not listen to such words."

Gao Jiong said, "Just act like you didn't hear it. I'll say what I want."

Li Xuanba feigned a bitter smile.

Gao Jiong asked, "Does Daxiong know your secret?"

Li Xuanba said, "Second Brother knows."

Gao Jiong smiled. "Your Second Brother is no ordinary dragon trapped in a pond. Twenty years from now, he will be in his prime, bound to occupy a paramount position in the new dynasty."

Li Xuanba nodded. *Ah, yes, yes, yes! You're so right, old man. He becomes Emperor, so his position in the new dynasty couldn't be more important.*

After delivering his lecture, Gao Jiong stood up and took Li Xuanba to find Li Shimin.

Since his disciples had come to his door, no matter what shocking events transpired today, Gao Jiong was determined to teach the lesson and assign the homework.

Li Shimin was playing *cuju* with Gao Biaoren, Gao's third son, when he was dragged over with a baffled look for a recitation test by Gao Jiong.

Gao Jiong rolled up a book scroll and whacked his disciple on the head. "Can you not learn from your younger brother and study properly?!"

Li Shimin didn't dare dodge, only clutching his head and crying, "I really did study hard! I could recite it before! I just played cuju and forgot it for a second. Teacher, don't be angry, let me think—I'll remember it very soon!"

He signaled to Li Xuanba with his eyes: *Brother, save me!*

Li Xuanba pretended not to see.

Li Shimin screamed in his heart: *【Save me!】*

Li Xuanba not only pretended not to notice, but even took a step backward.

Li Shimin was incredulous: "Ah-Xuan... Ow! Teacher, stop hitting! 'Endure minor beatings, flee major ones!' Teacher, that really hurts, I'm running!"

With that, Li Shimin scurried away with his head in his hands, hiding behind Gao Biaoren.

Gao Jiong's hand remained frozen in midair, unable to believe his disciple actually dared to run while being scolded.

Running was one thing, but he even quoted classic adages to justify it!

Li Xuanba covered his mouth with both hands: "Pfft."

Gao Biaoren gave a dry laugh. "Don't hide behind me! How can I block him?!"

Li Shimin: "Just let me hide for a bit, don't be so stingy!"

Gao Biaoren: "How is this being stingy?!"

Gao Jiong snorted coldly and said, "Get over here!"

Li Shimin held his head and shuffled in tiny steps back before Gao Jiong, shrinking his head like a tortoise. "Teacher, don't hit me anymore. If you hit me more, I really won't remember. Ah-Xuan once said that a child's head shouldn't be struck—striking it too much makes them foolish. Right, Ah-Xuan?"

Suppressing a laugh, Li Xuanba said, "Right. That's why Mother only spanks Second Brother's butt."

Li Shimin stomped his feet: "Ah-Xuan!"

Gao Jiong couldn't help himself and gently tapped Li Shimin's shoulder with the scroll. "Copy it ten times as punishment."

Li Shimin breathed a sigh of relief. "Yes, Teacher."

Gao Jiong led Li Shimin and Li Xuanba back inside to study.

Li Shimin turned around, pulled a face at Gao Biaoren, and whispered, "Next time I'll definitely crush you at cuju... Ouch! Teacher, you promised no more head hits!"

Gao Jiong sized up Li Shimin with ill intent, devising an even stricter curriculum in his heart.

Now that he knew Li Shimin was destined to shine in the imperial court of a golden age twenty years later, he had to increase Li Shimin's workload.

Previously, he hadn't been overly strict with Li Shimin because the current Emperor was not broad-minded and might not tolerate someone too exceptional. Moreover, Li Shimin was merely the second son of the Duke of Tang, whose title would be inherited by his elder brother, Li Jiancheng. No matter how brilliant Li Shimin was, he could not bypass Li Jiancheng.

But a new dynasty was different. Transitioning from chaos to prosperity would surely offer countless opportunities to earn military and civil merit. Who was to say Li Shimin couldn't earn an official position and noble title even grander than those of Li Yuan and Li Jiancheng?

As for Li Xuanba, Gao Jiong had no intention of becoming harsh.

Li Xuanba's attitude toward learning was already exceedingly proper, needing no supervision. He possessed a frail body and such miraculous divine abilities; Gao Jiong's only worry was Li Xuanba's lifespan.

As dusk drew near, Li Shimin dragged his exhausted body home alongside Li Xuanba, sniffling softly.

Li Xuanba pulled out a piece of dried fruit and stuffed it into his brother's mouth. "Stop fake-crying."

Munching on the dried fruit, Li Shimin's mouth pouted so high it could hang a wine jug. "Why is my homework double yours? That's not fair!"

Li Xuanba said, "That is retribution for neglecting your studies recently."

Li Shimin: "Hmph!"

He crammed the rest of the dried fruit into his mouth, swallowed hard, licked his lips, and stretched. "How did your plan go?"

Li Xuanba switched to heart-telepathy: *【I spoiled to Mister Gao that he will be executed next year for his words, and that the Sui Dynasty will fall within twenty years. Mister Gao was completely calm, not following the script at all... Why are you covering your ears again?】*

Li Shimin smiled bitterly. "Ah-Xuan, you didn't even tell me about this."

Li Xuanba: *【Ah, I didn't?】*

Li Shimin shook his head vigorously.

Li Xuanba: *【That's because I was worried about placing a mental burden on you.】*

Li Shimin covered his ears and shook his head wildly in all directions. "Then why are you telling me now?!"

Li Xuanba gave Li Shimin an exasperated roll of his eyes: *【Because you asked.】*

Li Shimin let out a few soft, wailing screams of "Ahhhh," before dropping his hands listlessly. "What did you want Mister Gao to do?"

Li Xuanba: *【I wanted Mister Gao to collaborate with me and spark a conflict with the Wei Clan in court. The Crown Prince would surely mediate, and Mister Gao could use the momentum to plead guilty to His Majesty, requesting to resign and retire due to old age and illness.】*

Li Shimin pinched his chin. "If Mister Gao steps down, they would also have to step down or demote one or two people. Wow, if that happens, the Wei Clan would just have to swallow the bitter pill in silence. But Ah-Xuan, how were you going to get Mister Gao and the Wei Clan to clash? There has to be a reason for Mister Gao and the Wei Clan to clash."

Li Xuanba: "..."

Li Shimin asked in confusion, "Brother... you didn't think of that, did you?"

Li Xuanba's gaze darted around guiltily.

Li Shimin pressed his hands to his cheeks, his mouth agape. "Heavens, you really didn't think of it!"

Li Xuanba: "..."

Now it was Li Xuanba's turn to hold his head in his hands.

He had only focused on how to shock Mister Gao, then guide him to impeach the Wei Clan, stage a play alongside the Crown Prince, and take the opportunity to retire.

But... right! How was he supposed to direct the blame specifically to the Wei Clan instead of impeaching someone else? Impeaching others and resigning was a great plan, but on what grounds could he impeach the Wei Clan specifically?

Li Xuanba slumped onto the carriage seat, clutching his head, dying of embarrassment.

He had confidently set a trap, only to find the trap's rope was snapped right from the start?

Li Shimin sighed like a world-weary old man and said, "Ah-Xuan, we're still young. How could we possibly outsmart someone as formidable as Mister Gao? Don't do things like this in the future. If you want to do something, discuss it with me first. Adding our ages together, we're barely... well, barely approaching adulthood [twenty]. Maybe together we can spar with adults."

Li Xuanba felt even more embarrassed. His inner soul was no seven-year-old child.

Well, even if a bottom-feeder from his previous life had some street smarts, when it came to court politics, he still had a lot to learn.

...

What Li Xuanba never expected was that, just when he thought his plot had failed, Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi actually attacked the Wei Clan simultaneously!

Their justification for impeaching the Wei Clan was that the Wei Clan had hindered them from printing Confucian classics and secretly spread rumors claiming that classics should only be hand-copied to show respect to ancient sages. Printing classics was an insult to the words of the sages, so all printed copies ought to be burned.

In reality, the Wei Clan was not the only family secretly displeased by Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi printing and selling their annotated Confucian classics, but Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi specifically chose to target the Wei Clan.

Clearly, this was Gao Jiong showing goodwill to Li Xuanba, giving the Wei Clan a kick on behalf of his disciple.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi submitted a joint memorial to Yang Guang:

"The Sage had three thousand disciples, among whom were no shortage of commoners from the wild. The aspiration of the Sage was not to lock up his words in high towers, but to educate and civilize the four seas!

"In ancient times, the words of sages were carved on bamboo slips and wooden tablets, and later written on paper. Great scholars once roamed the land, using twigs as pens and dirt as paper to instruct the ignorant masses.

"Upon ascending the throne, Your Majesty restored schools across the land, promoting trust, cultivating harmony, encouraging morality, and reviving the great undertaking of sage-like education!

"If Confucian classics can be printed, scholars of humble origin throughout the empire will all be able to read and sing praises of Your Majesty's virtue. Your Majesty would be like a Sage reincarnate!

"Does the Wei Clan's interference in this grand endeavor mean they wish to repeat the atrocity of abolishing schools across the realm?

"Your servants pray to publish and print Confucian classics in Your Majesty's name, to instruct the populace and revive the cultural enlightenment of our Great Sui!"

After reading the joint memorial from Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, Yang Guang was profoundly shaken.

He said to Empress Xiao in utter disbelief, "Those two old rogues actually praised Us as a Sage?!"

Empress Xiao smiled and said, "The late Emperor abolished schools across the land. The moment Your Majesty ascended the throne, you rebuilt schools nationwide. To the scholars of the world, you are naturally a Sage."

Yang Guang sighed. "Those two old rogues have slandered Us quite a bit; who would have thought they would call Us a Sage on this matter?"

Empress Xiao was equal parts amused and helpless at the Emperor's repetitive musings.

Yang Guang said, "Still, those two old rogues speak the truth. If We wish to educate all under heaven, this printing technique is indeed immensely useful. We recall the Crown Prince mentioned it before?"

Empress Xiao said, "This matter was indeed spearheaded by the Crown Prince, who had the Li family's Second and Third Young Masters test it under the guise of children's play."

"Seeing they couldn't win over the Duke of Tang's estate, the Wei Clan stooped to such petty tricks?" Yang Guang snorted coldly, also expressing some dissatisfaction toward the Crown Prince. "We have long said Zhao's temperament is indecisive, filled with womanish softness, and this affair proves it once more. A small trial? If this printing technique is truly useful, we can simply print all the Confucian classics for schools across the empire! Doesn't he admonish Us daily to save money? Doesn't this save a massive fortune?"

Empress Xiao sighed in her heart, echoing, "Indeed."

Yang Guang said, "Those two old rogues requested that We open the imperial library to compile a massive collection of rare books from across the realm and print multiple copies. That happens to align with Our previous intention. Who knew they would share the exact same thought as Us on this?"

Empress Xiao said, "Then why not grant their request and commission them to compile the books? That way, they will no longer bother Your Majesty."

Yang Guang's eyes lit up. "Reasonable!"

Seeing Yang Guang agree, Empress Xiao breathed a sigh of relief.

She recalled the private letters from Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi asking for her assistance.

Empress Xiao had always known the Emperor harbored killing intent toward Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi. Though she felt it inappropriate, she had not dared to remonstrate. Now, going with the flow, these two veteran officials would likely be spared from death.

Empress Xiao had not expected that Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi would actually seek help from her.

What unyielding bones Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi had! Precisely because the Emperor knew these two so well and believed they would continue to criticize state affairs, he had developed a desire to kill them.

To think they would voluntarily harbor thoughts of retreat and even flatter the Emperor.

After his excitement subsided, Yang Guang also noticed the intent to flatter from these two senior ministers.

He said, "Perhaps they saw Yang Su's death and felt fear in their hearts. Hmph! Seemingly stubborn, they are ultimately nothing more than cowards who fear death. Forget it, We shall let them go compile books."

Empress Xiao said, "Your Majesty is wise."

...

Li Shimin stood dumbfounded. "Ah?! It actually developed according to your plan! Ah-Xuan, are you hiding something from me?!"

Li Xuanba shook his head vigorously.

*I am super shocked too, okay?!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第31章 宇文弼有些不满
chunks.chineseText:
第31章 宇文弼有些不满

=
　　宇文弼找上门来。
　　李玄霸挪动， 挪动，挪动到了李世民的身后。
　　李世民展开双臂，把弟弟挡在身后：“老师， 别吓唬阿玄， 阿玄胆子小， 身体弱，不禁吓。”
　　宇文弼的脸板不住了。他无奈地招招手：“过来，谁吓唬你？我还能吃了你？”
　　李玄霸从哥哥背后探出脑袋：“老、老师， 你为何生气啊？”
　　宇文弼的脸又板了起来：“你还当我是你老师？！”
　　李玄霸又把脑袋缩了回去。
　　或许因为上辈子读书的生活是李玄霸一生中唯一美好的回忆，所以他对“老师”的敬畏被带到了这一世。李玄霸虽然背着老师们敢算计，当着面就有些怂。
　　“过来！”宇文弼再次招手。
　　李世民叹了口气， 回头道：“阿玄，老师好像没那么生气了， 出去吧。”
　　李玄霸垂着脑袋从李世民身后挪动出来， 乖乖走到宇文弼面前。
　　宇文弼大手按下，使劲揉搓了一下李玄霸的脑袋，不高兴道：“老夫才是你和李二郎第一个老师，那高颎是后来的，还是先嫌弃你们， 后来又眼巴巴地凑上来的！”
　　李玄霸：“……嗯？”什么意思。
　　李世民眼珠子转了转，明白了宇文弼为什么生气。
　　他叹了口气， 道：“难道是高先生将谶纬之事告知老师了？”
　　宇文弼冷笑：“他倒是没告诉我是谁会谶纬，只说是一偶遇的老道士。”
　　高颎找到参加完杨素葬礼回来的宇文弼，说某日游山， 突然大雾弥漫， 正一筹莫展， 遇到一个砍柴的老道士。老道士一见他就唉声叹气， 说他明年有大灾。但看在他是治世能臣，积累了许多功德的份上，所以提醒几句。
　　提醒的内容，就是李玄霸之前提醒高颎的内容了。
　　宇文弼可不信什么老道士，但对高颎所说的谶纬之言半信半疑。
　　他了解高颎，高颎若不是知道更多的内幕，比如皇帝已经对他二人动了杀心，否则不会来找他说这事。
　　但宇文弼没打算退缩。
　　皇帝越是不喜欢进谏，他就越应该进谏。不然皇帝身边就只剩下奸邪小人，这大隋一定会重起动乱。
　　天下才平定没多久，他不想再看到大乱一日的到来了。
　　反正他年纪也很大了，就算最后死在进谏上也没什么，只要让皇帝少做些昏君事就行了。
　　等到太子继位就好了。这个太子一看就是个明君胚子。太子继位，大隋和天下都有救了。
　　但高颎老匹夫告诉宇文弼，对不起，老道士还说，顶多二十年，大隋就灭了。不过有个新王朝迅速崛起，然后持续三百年呢！其中盛世就有一百三十多年呢！
　　老匹夫，你是想死在大隋，还是努努力活到八九十，看到盛世到来的那一日？
　　宇文弼：“……啊？大隋这就要亡了？”
　　高颎：“没错！我确信！”
　　宇文弼不知道高颎为何如此确信这个谶纬之言，但他不信。
　　他觉得高颎就是在骗他，想让他苟活。
　　最后高颎一句话把宇文弼打蒙了。
　　“你现在死了也没关系，还是能单独列传，就是《隋书》卷五十六，列传二十一的位置，嗯，聊胜于无吧。”高颎道，“很配你现在的地位。”
　　宇文弼：“？？？”
　　《隋书》都出来了？你听听你说的是人话吗？你这话如果传出去，你绝对会被灭满门！
　　宇文弼仍旧不信高颎的狗屁话，但还是问道：“那你排多少？”
　　高颎得意洋洋：“卷四十一，列传六。唉，位置还是太低了。这写列传的人，对老夫的评价有失偏颇。”
　　宇文弼知道自己的地位不如高颎。
　　但他在北周时就参与北破突厥，南败陈国，立下不菲战功。大隋建立后，他又参与灭陈之战，继续抵御突厥，战功也不少。
　　至于辗转各州任军政一把手的总管，所到之处皆留下能吏之名，为父守丧都被隋文帝专门下诏书让他别守丧了赶紧复职这点小事，就不用说了。
　　更不说他的文名，就算没在朝当官，宇文弼自信自己直接进儒林列传都能轻松排名前列。
　　谁编撰的《隋书》？
　　才“卷五十六，列传二十一”，是看不起谁呢？
　　高颎道：“就二十年的时间，我们熬不到那个时候，只要没有灭门之祸，我们的儿子肯定能在新王朝为官。”
　　宇文弼冷声道：“哼！你遇见的那个老道士连《隋书》都知道？那他知道写《隋书》的是谁？”
　　高颎笑道：“他可能知道，但我不好再问下去了。谶纬之术肯定会耗费代价，他好心救我，我怎么能害他？等能活到二十年后，我再去问吧。”
　　宇文弼观察了一番高颎的神情，颔首：“你有何计谋？”
　　他被高颎说服了。
　　但高颎没想到的是，宇文弼被他说服，不是因为这一番说辞，而是他在提起“好心救我”这句话时，不自觉地露出了一丝慈祥和无奈。
　　宇文弼对高颎了解颇深，立刻就猜出那所谓“老道士”，应该是高颎信任看重的晚辈。
　　而且这个晚辈肯定不是什么在野之人，自己还绝对认识。否则以高颎和他的交情，高颎没必要瞒着自己。
　　隐瞒会降低谶纬的可信度，高颎宁愿编一个“老道士”，引得自己无端怀疑，也要把这个人的身份隐瞒下来，哼……会是谁呢？
　　宇文弼算了一下高颎可能得到消息的时间，应该就是在杨素举办丧礼，高颎“卧病”这段时间。
　　但他没有特意打探。
　　高颎既然隐瞒了，那他本该假装不知道。
　　但高颎与他商议如何从朝堂漩涡全身而退时，非要把京兆韦氏扯进来揍一顿，他就琢磨出点味了。
　　几乎是直觉一般，宇文弼的心中立刻浮现出李玄霸的身影。
　　李玄霸气质出尘，明明只是一个孩子，却常常一副看透时事的神情，更何况还有一副病弱的身体，简直太符合“天妒”的描述了！
　　本来宇文弼是真的没打算特意打听这个谶纬者的，但一想到此人是李玄霸，他心里的火就冒了出来，忍不住一回大兴就来找李玄霸。
　　李玄霸先一头雾水，在李世民的挤眉弄眼连连比划下，他的智商终于上线。
　　难道……宇文先生是吃醋了？！
　　不、不会吧？
　　李玄霸立刻道：“老师可是为我劝说高先生不要劝谏陛下而来？”
　　宇文弼：“哼！”
　　当李玄霸直接问出来时，这老头突然感到了一点尴尬。
　　这种事有什么好质问的？好像他很在乎似的。
　　李玄霸立刻道：“我本来不敢将此事告知他人。除了二哥之外，连父亲母亲都不知晓。只是我寻不到解救老师的方法，只好趁着所有人的视线都集中在楚国公的葬礼上，悄悄去寻找高先生。”
　　李世民也立刻道：“其实阿玄也是临时起意。高先生因病留在大兴，我们去探病的话，不会引起他人注意。这不正好？本来阿玄还想找个机会直接告诉老师的，但……呃，那个，老师，真的很抱歉，我替阿玄道歉。”
　　李世民拱手作揖。
　　李玄霸也立刻拱手作揖：“学生真的不是不相信老师。”
　　宇文弼更加尴尬了，他立刻将两个学生扶起来，道：“这种事本来就不该告诉他人。我只是生气你们不该将此事告诉高颎。高颎根本不擅长隐瞒，你看，我都能猜出来。若是其他人猜出来，你们会惹火上身。”
　　说到这，宇文弼觉得，还真是这么一回事。
　　他语重心长道：“我知道你们两个孩子心善，但你们无论做何事，都要以自己的安危为重。高颎那个老匹夫，不是可以信任之人。你们以后有什么秘密，不可再告诉他，他……”
　　“宇文弼！你在干什么！”高颎气势汹汹地推开阻拦的仆人，走进来。
　　宇文弼板着脸对李世民和李玄霸道：“你看，我嘱咐下人，说要与你二人单独聊天，他都不要脸地要来偷听。这样的人，怎么能托付秘密？”
　　李世民赶紧对仆人道：“你们退下吧，如果有人来，请拦在外面。就算耶耶和娘娘来，也先通报。”
　　仆人擦着额头吓出来的冷汗告退。
　　高公突然就冲进来，拦都拦不住，颇吓人。
　　李世民驱赶仆人。李玄霸缩在墙角。两位老人已经相约在院子里打了起来。
　　更可怕的是，两人都不是佩剑，而是佩戴着开了刃的宝刀。
　　那宝刀寒光闪烁，刀身略暗，一看就是见过血的。
　　两位六十多岁的老人就这么拿着宝刀乒乒乓乓对砍，一招一招直取要害，仿佛搏命。
　　哪怕前世李玄霸独自在外闯荡的时候和人打过架，但哪见过大刀对砍的阵仗？这两位还都是他的老师。吓得他面无血色，噤如寒蝉，头皮发麻，呼吸都快停滞了。
　　李世民驱散完仆人，又让人去和李渊、窦夫人报信，让他们不用担心。然后他跑到李玄霸身边，拍了拍弟弟的脑袋：“别怕。”
　　李玄霸拉着李世民袖子：“快，快阻止！”不行，紧张得呼吸不畅了！
　　“别怕，深呼吸，深呼吸。”李世民拍着弟弟的背，在李玄霸缓过气后，笑着道，“不过是比试而已，两位老师都没有认真，你看着就好。好好学，这可是战场上搏命的招式，寻常时候老师不会亮出来。”
　　李玄霸顺着胸脯喘气。听听你说的话是不是前后矛盾？一会儿说没认真，一会儿说搏命，逻辑呢！
　　李世民感叹道：“你不常去校场。我去校场学武的时候，校场师傅们互相搏斗偶尔就会用真正搏命的招式，所以我一看就看出来了。”
　　李玄霸急道：“你看出来了还不阻拦！”
　　李世民轻松道：“阻拦什么？”
　　李玄霸急得脑门的汗都冒出来了。你说阻拦什么！
　　他看着庭院里的刀光，闭着眼睛大喊：“老师，别打了，都是我的错！”
　　宇文弼趁着高颎走神，一刀将高颎的刀击落，然后冷哼道：“我可是当过先锋的人，你的战略能力比我略强，但比武力，你差得远。”
　　李世民跳着脚鼓掌：“宇文老师好厉害！”
　　李玄霸的嘴张得老大。
　　宇文弼在他心中，就是一个大儒老师。宇文弼平时也一直是长袍广袖，一副文质彬彬的模样。
　　虽然高颎的儒学造诣也很厉害，但高颎常以武官自居，又早早开府拜大将军，所以在李玄霸心中，有半个老将的身份。
　　现在这是怎么回事？虽然高先生比宇文先生年长几岁，但这几岁，好像武力不该有这么大的差距吧？
　　还有，宇文先生所说的“先锋”是怎么回事？！是我知道的那种军队里身先士卒的先锋吗？
　　李玄霸不由看向李世民。
　　我哥那种先锋？
　　啊啊啊，这还是大儒吗？大儒不都是一副肩不能挑手不能提的柔弱模样吗？
　　李玄霸知道宇文弼有军功，但他以为宇文弼大概就是《三国演义》那种羽扇纶巾的谋士模样。
　　先锋是什么鬼啊？！
　　宇文弼和高颎刚刚还在抽刀互砍，现在高颎输了，两人倒是谈笑起来。
　　高颎笑道：“当年你随武帝伐齐，亲率三百豪侠少年，身上三处重创仍旧杀敌不休。没想到人老了，你身上那股狠劲仍旧不减当年。”
　　宇文弼笑着答道：“我只是人老了，心可不老。”
　　李世民蹦到两位老师之间，眼神中仿佛蕴含着无数星星：“老师老师，我可以跟两位老师学武吗！”
　　宇文弼将刀还鞘：“你若能吃苦，想学什么我都能教。”
　　李世民把自己的小胸脯拍得“啪啪”响：“我可能吃苦了！老师放心。阿玄，你要不要一起学？”
　　李玄霸跳得过快的心脏平复，他唾弃自己的胆子居然还没有真的小孩二哥大。
　　“我、我也想。”李玄霸冷静下来后，也不由心情澎湃。
　　那刀好帅啊！
　　哪个男人没有一颗热爱冷兵器的心？
　　宇文弼立刻道：“不行。你身体太弱，练些修养的内家功夫就行了，不可太劳累。”
　　高颎点头：“你不是认识孙医师那个道士？让他教你几手养身功夫。”
　　宇文弼笑道：“这次是真的老道士了？”
　　高颎笑着应道：“这次是真的老道士。”
　　两人相视一笑。
　　李玄霸感到眼睛有点疼。
　　古人的友谊，真是黏黏糊糊，让旁的人看了觉得脚趾头抠地。
　　“内家功夫，修炼了也没有内力，更不会飞檐走壁，隔山打牛。”李玄霸对“内家功夫”很不满，感觉和后世练的养身太极拳差不多。
　　李世民拍着李玄霸的脑袋道：“养身就行了，你还想飞檐走壁隔山打牛？当写故事吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“我还是可以练练刀的，至少要能自保吧？”
　　高颎道：“要练些刀剑自保，也要等你再大些。而且你这力气，恐怕拿上刀剑也砍不动人。”
　　宇文弼赞同地点头：“还不如多聘用几个壮士当护卫。”
　　李世民再次拍胸口：“有我保护阿玄，阿玄可以不会武艺！”
　　李玄霸被几人嫌弃得直撇嘴。
　　力气再怎么小，身体再怎么弱，只要刀够锋利，哪有砍不死人的？别小瞧我。
　　但高颎和宇文弼都把这位能观看天书《隋书》的弟子当眼珠子护，怎么也不肯让李玄霸去吃苦。
　　李世民倒是说了句实诚话：“其实可以让阿玄去试试。他肯定第一天都坚持不下来，然后他自己就放弃了。”
　　李玄霸揍了他哥一拳。
　　你这实诚话不如不说！
　　李渊听说高颎怒气冲冲要来找宇文弼麻烦的时候，担心万分，立刻前来寻高颎和宇文弼。
　　被李世民派人挡下后，他焦急地在院门外转圈圈。
　　待高颎和宇文弼请他进去的时候，他进门一看，高颎和宇文弼已经在庭院里坐着喝李玄霸泡的饮子。
　　饮子即后世中草药凉茶，是茶叶还被当做汤的时候，民间常喝的饮料。
　　李玄霸泡的饮子其实就是普通的花茶，花瓣晒干后，不加糖、蜂蜜、牛奶等任何调味，只喝花香。
　　两位老人虽然觉得寡淡了些，但他们这个年龄，也不太爱喝味道太重的饮子，平常以喝温开水和淡蜜水为主，现在喝着这寡淡的花茶，只觉别有一番风味。
　　“这名为花茶的饮子，倒是和南边的饮子有些类似。”宇文弼道，“南边的饮子不爱加奶，常用晒干的果脯花瓣。”
　　李玄霸道：“糖吃多了不好，饮食清淡对身体更有益。”
　　高颎问道：“是孙医师的叮嘱？他还有什么养身的方子，你抄一份给我。”
　　宇文弼道：“我也要一份……算了，我现在闲了下来，自己去太白山寻他。”
　　李渊一头雾水。
　　高公和宇文公怎么谈论起养身了？他们不是打起来了吗？
　　李渊道：“我听闻两位公争执，吓坏我了。大德，那花茶给耶耶也来一碗。”
　　李渊咕噜咕噜灌下一碗水，砸吧嘴道：“确实寡淡，应该多加蜜糖。”
　　李玄霸道：“喝水止渴就该喝寡淡些，蜜糖吃多了对身体不好。”
　　李渊道：“谁说的？蜜糖对身体好！”
　　李世民道：“耶耶，孙医师说的。”
　　李渊改口：“蜜糖吃多了对孩童身体确实不好。”
　　李玄霸懒得和李渊争辩。对偏爱高糖高脂肪的隋唐贵族而言，自己要推广养身理念过于困难。
　　孙医师名声那么大，他的振臂疾呼也没人理睬。
　　还好他哥怕他嘴馋，他吃清淡的时候，他哥虽然不愿意，也跟着一起吃。或许能把他哥的口味养得稍稍别那么油腻甜腻。
　　李渊随口和李玄霸、李世民闲谈了几句，让两个孩子去找窦夫人玩耍，自己留下与高颎和宇文弼聊天。
　　皇帝已经同意官方使用雕版印刷术推广儒经。因是李玄霸最先提出，所以李渊也被塞进了负责人的行列中。
　　李渊除了最开始的千牛备身，所当的官一直是文职。
　　没错，现在唐国公李渊还是个纯正的文臣。
　　所以他去推广印刷儒经，负责大业元年刚重建的学校教材供应，正好是本职工作。
　　如此收拢天下文人之心的差事，杨广当然不放心给高颎和宇文弼两个他不信任的老臣。
　　高颎和宇文弼去编书就行了，这种事得心腹和亲戚来干。
　　李渊这个皇帝的表兄，自然最合适，比杨广现在最信任的宇文述一家还合适。
　　既然高颎和宇文弼来了唐国公府，李渊便正好向二人请教此事，不用多跑一趟。
　　李渊还认为，那雕版印刷术应该就是高颎和宇文弼借李玄霸之手推广和改良的。
　　李玄霸才多小的孩子？他怎么会懂那些机巧之术？
　　高颎和宇文弼这样的大贤，才会什么都懂，如诸葛武侯一样。
　　高颎和宇文弼对视一眼，默认了这件事。
　　离开唐国公府时，高颎和宇文弼坐了同一辆马车离开。
　　待马车行驶了一会儿后，高颎道：“大德似乎对李渊有些警惕和排斥。”
　　宇文弼叹息道：“那孩子不是和你说，能看到未来之人，就像是身上有了沉重的枷锁，大概就是如此吧。”
　　高颎道：“李世民和李玄霸都是很好很优秀的孩子，希望李渊不要伤孩子们的心，唉。”
　　宇文弼道：“只要我二人不死，有我二人护着，他不敢。”
　　高颎颔首，然后叹息：“我与你一同去寻孙医师。真希望能多活几年，活到二十年后。”
　　宇文弼道：“尽人事，听天命。但我相信老天将大雄大德送给我二人当弟子，对我二人不薄。”
　　高颎再次颔首。
　　李玄霸有谶纬之能，令人惊叹。但李世民的表现，更是令他们惊讶。
　　一个没有神异的孩童，不仅能替弟弟隐瞒谶纬之能，还在知道未来之事之后也淡然自若，仿佛任何烦恼都不会在他心中留下痕迹。
　　他们都会被“未来”束缚，但李世民这个孩子却对未来毫不在意。
　　当他们询问时，李世民双手枕在脑后笑道：“知道未来，就是为了踏向更好的未来，所以没什么可焦虑的。”
　　李世民无忧无虑的笑容，大概是心思过重的李玄霸没有被“谶纬”压垮的原因之一。
　　他们居然也因李世民的洒脱感到了轻松，对未来不再忐忑不安，怨愤不平。
　　“二十年……二十年后，大雄也长大了。你说那开辟盛世的人会不会……”
　　“应该不是。不到三十岁，年纪太小了，不能服众。何况李渊那时还活着，轮不到大雄。”
　　“但若真的是他……”
　　“那大雄和大德两个孩子就太苦了。”
　　“是啊，唉。”
　　这两人是他们认可的弟子，今生唯一真正收入门的弟子。这样的弟子，如他们亲子一般重要。
　　两位老人都在心里祈祷，祈祷两个孩子能一直无忧无虑。
　　虽然他们知道希望很渺茫。

Chapter 31: Yuwen Bi's Discontent

Yuwen Bi came knocking on their door.

Li Xuanba shuffled, shuffled, and shuffled right behind Li Shimin.

Li Shimin spread his arms, shielding his younger brother. "Teacher, don't scare Ah-Xuan. Ah-Xuan is timid and frail; he can't handle a fright."

Yuwen Bi's stern expression cracked. He waved his hand helplessly. "Come here. Who's scaring you? Am I going to eat you?"

Li Xuanba poked his head out from behind his brother. "T-Teacher, why are you angry?"

Yuwen Bi's face stiffened again. "You still consider me your teacher?!"

Li Xuanba pulled his head right back in.

Perhaps because his academic life in his past life was the only beautiful memory he possessed, his reverence for "teachers" had carried over into this lifetime. Although Li Xuanba dared to scheme behind his teachers' backs, he became rather cowardly when facing them in person.

"Come here!" Yuwen Bi waved again.

Li Shimin sighed, turning his head. "Ah-Xuan, Teacher doesn't seem that angry anymore. Go on out."

Li Xuanba shuffled out from behind Li Shimin with his head hung low, obediently walking up to Yuwen Bi.

Yuwen Bi brought his large hand down, vigorously rubbing Li Xuanba's head, and grumbled, "This old man was the first teacher to you and Li Erlang! That Gao Jiong came later. He even looked down on you two at first, only to eagerly cozy up to you later!"

Li Xuanba: "...Eh?" What did that mean?

Li Shimin's eyes darted around as he realized why Yuwen Bi was angry.

He sighed and said, "Could it be that Master Gao told Teacher about the prophecy?"

Yuwen Bi sneered. "He didn't tell me who made the prophecy. He only claimed it was an old Daoist priest he met by chance."

Gao Jiong had sought out Yuwen Bi, who had just returned from Yang Su's funeral, claiming that while hiking in the mountains one day, a sudden thick fog had rolled in. Just as he was at his wits' end, he encountered an old Daoist woodcutter. Upon seeing him, the old Daoist sighed deeply and warned him of a great disaster awaiting him the following year. However, out of respect for Gao Jiong's status as a capable minister who had accumulated immense merit, the Daoist offered a few words of warning.

The warnings were exactly what Li Xuanba had previously cautioned Gao Jiong about.

Yuwen Bi didn't believe in any old Daoist, but he was half-convinced by the prophetic words Gao Jiong spoke.

He knew Gao Jiong well. If Gao Jiong hadn't learned some deeper inside information—such as the Emperor harboring murderous intent toward the two of them—he wouldn't have come to discuss this.

But Yuwen Bi had no intention of backing down.

The more the Emperor disliked remonstrance, the more he felt obligated to remonstrate. Otherwise, only treacherous sycophants would remain by the Emperor's side, and the Great Sui would surely descend into chaos once more.

The realm had only recently been pacified; he did not wish to see the day when great chaos erupted again.

In any case, he was already well advanced in years. Even if he ultimately died for his remonstrances, it would be worth it as long as he could deter the Emperor from committing foolish acts.

It would be fine once the Crown Prince ascended the throne. The current Crown Prince clearly had the makings of a wise ruler. Once he succeeded, both the Great Sui and the realm would be saved.

But that old scoundrel Gao Jiong had told Yuwen Bi: *Apologies, but the old Daoist also said that within twenty years at most, the Great Sui will perish. However, a new dynasty will rapidly rise and last for three hundred years! And its golden age will span over a hundred and thirty years!*

*You old scoundrel, do you want to die with the Great Sui, or do you want to strive to live to eighty or ninety to see the day that golden age arrives?*

Yuwen Bi: "...Ah? The Great Sui is going to fall just like that?"

Gao Jiong: "Indeed! I am certain of it!"

Yuwen Bi did not know why Gao Jiong was so certain of this prophecy, but he himself remained skeptical.

He felt Gao Jiong was simply lying to him, trying to coax him into clinging to life.

In the end, a single sentence from Gao Jiong left Yuwen Bi utterly dumbfounded.

"It doesn't matter if you die now; you'll still get your own biography. It's in the *Book of Sui*, Volume 56, Biography 21. Well, I suppose it's better than nothing," Gao Jiong had said. "It suits your current standing quite well."

Yuwen Bi: "???"

Even the *Book of Sui* was brought up? Listen to yourself, is that even human speech? If those words got out, your entire clan would absolutely be executed!

Yuwen Bi still didn't believe Gao Jiong's nonsense, but he couldn't help but ask, "Then where do you rank?"

Gao Jiong had smirked triumphantly. "Volume 41, Biography 6. Alas, the position is still too low. The compiler of these biographies was rather biased in his evaluation of this old man."

Yuwen Bi knew his standing was not as high as Gao Jiong's.

But back in the Northern Zhou, he had participated in defeating the Tujue in the north and the Chen State in the south, achieving significant military exploits. After the founding of the Great Sui, he joined the campaign to destroy the Chen State and continued to defend against the Tujue, accumulating no shortage of military merits.

As for his rotations across various provinces as the chief military and civil commander, leaving behind a reputation as an exceptionally capable official wherever he went, or the minor detail of Emperor Wen of Sui issuing a special imperial decree ordering him to cut short his mourning period for his father and immediately resume office—there was no need to even mention those.

Not to mention his literary fame; even if he had never served in court, Yuwen Bi was confident he could easily rank near the top of the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.

Who compiled this *Book of Sui*?

Only "Volume 56, Biography 21"? Who were they looking down on?

Gao Jiong said, "It's only twenty years. We won't last until then, but as long as our clans aren't wiped out, our sons will certainly be able to serve as officials in the new dynasty."

Yuwen Bi said coldly, "Hmph! That old Daoist you met even knows about the *Book of Sui*? Then does he know who wrote it?"

Gao Jiong laughed. "He might know, but I couldn't bring myself to press further. The art of prophecy surely exacts a heavy toll. He saved me out of the goodness of his heart; how could I harm him? Once I survive the next twenty years, I'll ask him then."

Yuwen Bi observed Gao Jiong's expression and nodded. "What is your plan?"

He had been convinced by Gao Jiong.

But what Gao Jiong did not expect was that Yuwen Bi was convinced not by his words, but because when Gao Jiong mentioned "saved me out of the goodness of his heart," an involuntary trace of affection and helplessness had surfaced on his face.

Yuwen Bi knew Gao Jiong deeply and immediately guessed that the so-called "old Daoist" must be a junior whom Gao Jiong trusted and valued highly.

Furthermore, this junior was certainly not some hermit in the wild; Yuwen Bi must absolutely know them. Otherwise, given Gao Jiong's close friendship with him, there would be no need to hide it.

Hiding it would only lower the credibility of the prophecy. Gao Jiong would rather fabricate an "old Daoist" and invite groundless suspicion just to keep this person's identity a secret. Hmph... who could it be?

Yuwen Bi calculated when Gao Jiong might have received the news, which should have been during the time of Yang Su's funeral when Gao Jiong was "bedridden."

But he did not deliberately pry.

Since Gao Jiong was hiding it, he should have pretended not to know.

However, when Gao Jiong discussed with him how to withdraw completely from the court's vortex, he insisted on dragging the Wei clan of Jingzhao into the mud for a beating. That was when Yuwen Bi caught a whiff of something.

Almost by sheer instinct, Li Xuanba's figure immediately surfaced in Yuwen Bi's mind.

Li Xuanba possessed an ethereal temperament. Though he was clearly just a child, he often wore an expression of having seen through the affairs of the world. Moreover, his frail, sickly body perfectly matched the description of one "envied by the heavens"!

Originally, Yuwen Bi truly had no intention of deliberately seeking out the prophet. But the moment he realized it was Li Xuanba, a spark of irritation flared up in his chest. He couldn't resist coming to find Li Xuanba the moment he returned to Daxing.

At first, Li Xuanba was utterly bewildered. But under Li Shimin's frantic winking and gesturing, his intellect finally caught up.

Could it be... Master Yuwen is jealous?!

No... surely not?

Li Xuanba immediately said, "Did Teacher come because I persuaded Master Gao not to remonstrate with His Majesty?"

Yuwen Bi: "Hmph!"

When Li Xuanba asked so directly, the old man suddenly felt a touch of embarrassment.

What was there to question about such a thing? It made it seem as if he cared deeply.

Li Xuanba quickly added, "I originally did not dare to tell anyone about this. Aside from Second Brother, not even Father or Mother knows. It was only because I couldn't find a way to save you, Teacher, that I took advantage of everyone's attention being focused on the Duke of Chu's funeral to quietly seek out Master Gao."

Li Shimin also chimed in immediately, "Actually, Ah-Xuan acted on a whim. Master Gao remained in Daxing due to illness, so our visit to him wouldn't attract any attention. Wasn't that perfect? Ah-Xuan originally wanted to find an opportunity to tell you directly, Teacher, but... er, well, Teacher, we are truly sorry. I apologize on Ah-Xuan's behalf."

Li Shimin cupped his hands and bowed.

Li Xuanba also immediately cupped his hands and bowed. "Your student truly did not mean to distrust Teacher."

Yuwen Bi grew even more embarrassed. He quickly helped his two students up and said, "Such matters should never have been told to others in the first place. I am only angry that you told Gao Jiong. Gao Jiong is terrible at keeping secrets. See? Even I could guess it. If anyone else figures it out, you will bring disaster upon yourselves."

Having said this, Yuwen Bi realized that this was indeed the case.

He said earnestly, "I know you two children are kind-hearted, but whatever you do, you must prioritize your own safety. That old scoundrel Gao Jiong is not someone to be trusted. If you have any secrets in the future, do not tell him again. He..."

"Yuwen Bi! What do you think you are doing!" Gao Jiong pushed past the servants trying to stop him and stormed in aggressively.

Yuwen Bi said with a stiff face to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, "See? I instructed the servants that I wished to speak with you two in private, yet he shamelessly barged in to eavesdrop. How can you entrust secrets to such a person?"

Li Shimin quickly told the servants, "You may withdraw. If anyone comes, please stop them outside. Even if Father and Mother arrive, report to us first."

The servants wiped the cold sweat from their foreheads and retreated.

Duke Gao had suddenly charged in, completely unstoppable and rather terrifying.

While Li Shimin dismissed the servants, Li Xuanba shrank into a corner. The two old men had already agreed to a duel and started fighting in the courtyard.

What was even more terrifying was that neither of them carried ornamental swords; instead, they wore sharp, battle-ready sabers.

The sabers gleamed with a cold light, their blades slightly darkened—a clear sign they had tasted blood.

The two old men, both in their sixties, clashed their sabers with a series of loud clangs, every strike aimed directly at vital points as if they were fighting for their lives.

Even though Li Xuanba had fought with people when wandering alone in his past life, when had he ever witnessed a battle with massive sabers? Moreover, these two were his teachers. He was scared pale, silent as a cicada in winter, his scalp tingling, and his breath nearly stopping.

After dismissing the servants, Li Shimin sent someone to inform Li Yuan and Lady Dou so they wouldn't worry. He then ran over to Li Xuanba's side and patted his brother's head. "Don't be afraid."

Li Xuanba tugged at Li Shimin's sleeve. "Quick, stop them!" No, he was too tense to breathe properly!

"Don't be afraid. Deep breaths, deep breaths." Li Shimin patted his brother's back. Once Li Xuanba caught his breath, Li Shimin smiled and said, "It's just a sparring match. Neither teacher is being serious; just watch. Learn well—these are life-or-death moves used on the battlefield. Normally, our teachers wouldn't show them."

Li Xuanba stroked his chest to ease his breathing. *Listen to yourself, aren't you contradicting yourself? One moment you say they aren't serious, the next you say it's life-or-death. Where is the logic?!*

Li Shimin sighed with admiration. "You don't go to the training grounds often. When I study martial arts there, the instructors occasionally use genuine life-or-death moves when sparring, so I recognized it immediately."

Li Xuanba said anxiously, "You recognized it and you still won't stop them!"

Li Shimin said casually, "Stop what?"

Li Xuanba was so anxious that sweat broke out on his forehead. *What do you mean, stop what!*

Looking at the flashing blades in the courtyard, he closed his eyes and shouted, "Teachers, stop fighting! It's all my fault!"

Taking advantage of Gao Jiong's momentary distraction, Yuwen Bi struck Gao Jiong's saber from his hand with a single blow, then snorted coldly, "I was once a vanguard commander. Your strategic abilities might be slightly superior to mine, but when it comes to martial prowess, you are far behind."

Li Shimin jumped up and down, clapping. "Teacher Yuwen is amazing!"

Li Xuanba's mouth hung wide open.

In his mind, Yuwen Bi had always been a grand scholar. Yuwen Bi usually wore long robes with wide sleeves, looking every bit the refined gentleman.

Although Gao Jiong's Confucian scholarship was also formidable, he often identified as a military official and had been appointed Great General early on, so in Li Xuanba's mind, he was half an old veteran.

What was going on now? Although Master Gao was a few years older than Master Yuwen, those few years shouldn't have caused such a massive gap in martial prowess, right?

And what did Master Yuwen mean by "vanguard"? Was it the kind of vanguard commander who charged at the very front of an army?

Li Xuanba couldn't help but look at Li Shimin.

The kind of vanguard his brother would be?

Ah, was this really a grand scholar? Weren't grand scholars supposed to be frail and physically weak?

Li Xuanba knew Yuwen Bi had military merits, but he had assumed Yuwen Bi would be like the strategists in the *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, wearing a feather fan and a silk cap.

What on earth was a vanguard commander?!

Just moments ago, Yuwen Bi and Gao Jiong had been hacking at each other with drawn sabers. Now that Gao Jiong had lost, the two of them were actually chatting and laughing.

Gao Jiong laughed. "Back then, when you followed Emperor Wu to campaign against the Qi State, you personally led three hundred heroic youths. Even after sustaining three severe wounds, you continued to slay enemies without pause. I didn't expect that even in your old age, your fierce drive would remain undiminished."

Yuwen Bi replied with a smile, "Only my body is old; my heart is not."

Li Shimin bounced over to stand between his two teachers, his eyes practically sparkling with countless stars. "Teachers, Teachers, can I learn martial arts from both of you?"

Yuwen Bi sheathed his saber. "If you can endure hardship, I can teach you whatever you wish to learn."

Li Shimin thumped his little chest. "I can endure any hardship! Rest assured, Teacher. Ah-Xuan, do you want to learn too?"

Li Xuanba's racing heart finally calmed. He despised himself for having less courage than his genuinely childlike second brother.

"I... I want to as well." Once Li Xuanba calmed down, he couldn't help but feel a surge of excitement.

That saber was so cool!

What man didn't harbor a love for cold weapons?

Yuwen Bi immediately refused, "No. Your body is too weak. It is enough for you to practice some internal cultivation techniques to nurture your health. You must not overexert yourself."

Gao Jiong nodded. "Don't you know that Daoist, Physician Sun? Have him teach you a few health-preserving techniques."

Yuwen Bi chuckled. "Is it a real old Daoist this time?"

Gao Jiong replied with a smile, "This time, it is a real old Daoist."

The two shared a knowing smile.

Li Xuanba felt his eyes ache slightly.

The friendship of ancient people was truly overly sentimental, enough to make onlookers cringe.

"Internal cultivation... even if I practice it, I won't gain internal energy, let alone be able to leap across rooftops, walk on walls, or strike a bull from across a mountain." Li Xuanba was highly dissatisfied with "internal cultivation," feeling it was no different from the health-preserving Tai Chi practiced in the future.

Li Shimin patted Li Xuanba's head. "Preserving your health is enough. You still want to leap across rooftops and strike bulls from across mountains? Do you think you're writing a story?"

Li Xuanba said, "I can still practice the saber. At least I should be able to defend myself, right?"

Gao Jiong said, "If you want to practice blades for self-defense, you must wait until you are older. Besides, with your strength, I fear you wouldn't even be able to cut anyone even if you held a weapon."

Yuwen Bi nodded in agreement. "It would be better to hire a few more strong men as bodyguards."

Li Shimin thumped his chest again. "With me protecting Ah-Xuan, Ah-Xuan doesn't need to know martial arts!"

Li Xuanba pouted, thoroughly disdained by everyone.

No matter how small his strength or how weak his body, as long as the blade was sharp enough, how could it fail to kill? Don't look down on me.

But both Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi protected this disciple—who could read the heavenly book *Book of Sui*—like the apple of their eye, absolutely refusing to let Li Xuanba suffer.

Li Shimin, however, spoke an honest truth: "Actually, we could let Ah-Xuan try. He definitely won't last a single day, and then he'll give up on his own."

Li Xuanba punched his brother.

You would have been better off keeping that honest truth to yourself!

When Li Yuan heard that Gao Jiong had angrily come to find trouble with Yuwen Bi, he was extremely worried and immediately rushed over to find them.

After being stopped by the people Li Shimin had stationed, he paced anxiously outside the courtyard gate.

By the time Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi invited him in, he entered only to see the two of them already sitting in the courtyard, drinking the herbal brew Li Xuanba had prepared.

The brew was a type of herbal tea, a common beverage among the common folk back when tea leaves were still treated as soup ingredients.

The brew Li Xuanba prepared was actually just ordinary flower tea. After drying the petals, he added no sugar, honey, milk, or any other flavorings, allowing them to drink only the floral aroma.

Although the two old men found it a bit bland, at their age, they didn't particularly care for heavily flavored drinks either. They usually drank warm water or light honey water, so drinking this mild flower tea now felt uniquely refreshing.

"This beverage called flower tea is somewhat similar to the herbal brews of the south," Yuwen Bi remarked. "The southern brews don't use milk; they often use dried preserved fruits and flower petals."

Li Xuanba said, "Eating too much sugar is bad for you. A light diet is more beneficial to the body."

Gao Jiong asked, "Is that Physician Sun's advice? What other health-preserving recipes does he have? Copy one for me."

Yuwen Bi said, "I want one too... actually, now that I have some free time, I'll go to Mount Taibai to find him myself."

Li Yuan was utterly bewildered.

Why were Duke Gao and Duke Yuwen discussing health preservation? Weren't they supposed to be fighting?

Li Yuan said, "I heard you two were in a dispute and it scared me half to death. Dade, pour a bowl of that flower tea for your father too."

Li Yuan gulped down a bowl of water, smacked his lips, and said, "It is indeed bland. More honey should be added."

Li Xuanba said, "To quench thirst, water should be bland. Too much honey is bad for the body."

Li Yuan said, "Says who? Honey is good for the body!"

Li Shimin said, "Father, Physician Sun said so."

Li Yuan immediately changed his tune: "Eating too much honey is indeed bad for a child's body."

Li Xuanba couldn't be bothered to argue with Li Yuan. For the Sui and Tang nobility who favored high-sugar and high-fat diets, promoting the concept of health preservation was far too difficult.

Even with Physician Sun's immense reputation, his passionate pleas went unheeded.

Fortunately, his brother was afraid he would get cravings, so whenever he ate bland food, his brother would reluctantly join him. Perhaps this could train his brother's palate to be slightly less greasy and sweet.

Li Yuan casually chatted with Li Xuanba and Li Shimin for a bit, then sent the two children to play with Lady Dou while he stayed behind to converse with Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi.

The Emperor had already agreed to officially use woodblock printing to promote the Confucian classics. Since Li Xuanba was the first to propose it, Li Yuan had also been squeezed into the ranks of those in charge.

Aside from his initial post as a Left Imperial Bodyguard, the offices Li Yuan held had always been civil posts.

That's right, the current Duke of Tang, Li Yuan, was still a pure civil official.

Thus, promoting the printing of Confucian classics and overseeing the supply of textbooks for the schools newly rebuilt in the first year of Daye fell perfectly within his official duties.

An errand that so effectively won over the hearts of the realm's scholars was naturally not something Yang Guang would entrust to Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, two old ministers he distrusted.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi could just compile the books; such crucial tasks had to be handled by trusted aides and relatives.

Li Yuan, as the Emperor's cousin, was naturally the most suitable candidate—even more so than the family of Yuwen Shu, whom Yang Guang currently trusted the most.

Since Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi had come to the Duke of Tang's residence, Li Yuan took the opportunity to consult them on the matter, saving himself a trip.

Li Yuan also believed that the woodblock printing technique had actually been promoted and refined by Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi through Li Xuanba.

How old was Li Xuanba? How could he understand such intricate mechanics?

Only great sages like Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi would understand everything, just like Zhuge Liang.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi exchanged a glance and tacitly accepted this assumption.

Upon leaving the Duke of Tang's residence, Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi departed in the same carriage.

After the carriage had traveled for a while, Gao Jiong said, "Dade seems somewhat wary and dismissive of Li Yuan."

Yuwen Bi sighed, "Didn't that child tell you? One who can see the future carries a heavy shackle. That is likely why."

Gao Jiong said, "Li Shimin and Li Xuanba are both wonderful and outstanding children. I hope Li Yuan does not break their hearts. Alas."

Yuwen Bi said, "As long as the two of us do not die and continue to protect them, he wouldn't dare."

Gao Jiong nodded, then sighed, "I will go with you to find Physician Sun. I truly hope to live a few years longer, to survive twenty years from now."

Yuwen Bi said, "Do what is humanly possible and submit to the will of Heaven. But I believe Heaven has treated us well by sending Daxiong and Dade to be our disciples."

Gao Jiong nodded once more.

Li Xuanba's prophetic ability was astonishing. But Li Shimin's performance surprised them even more.

A child without any supernatural gifts could not only hide his brother's prophetic abilities, but also remain calm and unbothered after learning of the future, as if no worries could ever leave a mark on his heart.

They would all be bound by the "future," yet the child Li Shimin paid it no mind at all.

When they had asked him, Li Shimin had rested his hands behind his head and smiled, saying, "Knowing the future is so we can step toward a better future, so there's nothing to be anxious about."

Li Shimin's carefree smile was likely one of the reasons why the overly pensive Li Xuanba had not been crushed by the weight of his "prophecies."

Surprisingly, they too felt a sense of ease from Li Shimin's free-spirited nature, no longer feeling anxious or resentful about the future.

"Twenty years... In twenty years, Daxiong will have grown up. Do you think the one who ushers in that golden age might be..."

"Probably not. Under thirty years old is too young to command the respect of the masses. Besides, Li Yuan will still be alive then; it wouldn't be Daxiong's turn."

"But if it truly is him..."

"Then those two children, Daxiong and Dade, will have suffered too much."

"Indeed. Alas."

These two were the disciples they recognized, the only ones they had truly taken under their wing in this lifetime. Such disciples were as precious to them as their own flesh and blood.

Both old men prayed in their hearts, hoping the two children could remain carefree forever.

Even though they knew the hope was incredibly slim.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第32章 香皂甘油肥皂泡 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第32章 香皂甘油肥皂泡

=

高颎和宇文弼与京兆韦氏对上， 没人怀疑这和李玄霸有关系。

虽然李玄霸是高颎和宇文弼的学生，但高颎和宇文弼可以说是桃李满天下，且李玄霸和李世民两个学生是皇帝强塞给高颎和宇文弼的。

他们不知道高颎和宇文弼平时和李玄霸、李世民相处的模样， 自然不会认为两个七岁孩童能多受这两个六十多岁的老臣看重。

连京兆韦氏都自认倒霉， 觉得自己是撞皇帝刀口上了。这一定是皇帝仍旧为他们之前的试探不满， 趁此机会敲打他们。

不然暗中传谣的世家那么多，怎么非拽着京兆韦氏不放？

他们没打算继续和高颎、宇文弼对着干。两老头都卸掉了身上官职跑去编书了，再穷追猛打实在不好， 且会被皇帝记恨。只能叹一口气，吃了这个哑巴亏。

其他家族见状，明白皇帝确实有意推广儒学， 便一改口风，不再阻拦。

世家不是蠢的。所谓流水的王朝铁打的世家， 但和王朝硬碰硬的世家都被屠了不知道多少次了， 留下来只是世家的名号而已。比如现在弘农杨氏的本宗是隋朝皇帝这一脉。搁谁有点脑子，都知道是怎么回事。

唐国公府现在对外也是宣称两大汉族世家的联合。李渊与“五姓七望”的陇西李氏连了宗，窦夫人与扶风窦氏连了宗。

所以世家内部分裂就很严重，很难力往一处使，合力阻拦一个大权在握的皇帝的政令。

再者汉朝曾经兴起一次“文艺复兴”运动， 即假托从孔庙挖掘出了大小篆书写的儒经旧作，称“古文经”， 以和当时以隶书书写的“今文经”对抗。

在察举制为主的汉朝，争夺“注经权”就是争夺朝堂地位。

东汉末年，许多经学家投身“古文经”研究， 以“我注六经”， 宣扬自己的政治主张， 挽天下于倾颓。

他们广开私学， 将自己注释的经书教给当时人看不起的平民百姓，形成了强大的声势，培养了许多人才。

后来许多魏晋世家的先祖都参与了这场运动，在朝代急速变换的时候获得了巨大的名利，一跃成为顶尖世家。如“五姓七望”的荥阳郑氏和范阳卢氏。特别是荥阳郑氏，“郑贾之学”是如今显学。

这两个世家在听说雕版印刷儒经时，就在暗中搜集雕版印刷的工匠。等皇帝态度明确后，他们就准备热火朝天地开工印刷儒经，恨不得把自己家族的儒经给全天下的读书人人手一本。

荥阳郑氏和范阳卢氏的地位就是靠着桃李满天下积累来的，而不是如一些经学世家敝帚自珍。他们虽瞧不起寒门，但让寒门都成为自己的“门生”，这件事他们可太喜欢了。

当郑家得知最先提出印刷儒经的人是李玄霸之后，家族内部召开会议，急急忙忙将许诺给李建成的郑氏美妾先送进李建成府中，并增添了一成嫁妆。

李建成现在虽然已经成为千牛备身，，但千牛备身只是六品官，他还没有资格置“媵”。所以原本郑家是想等李建成的官职提升到五品后，再把寡居女送给李建成。

堂堂荥阳郑氏，将族中女子送给他人当妾，肯定也必须是有名份的“侧室”，得有诰命在身才不算折辱。

但现在，罢了罢了，唐国公府真是越来越强盛了。郑家又将在这次印刷儒经中得到天大的好处，他们便又退让了一步。

唐国公府也投桃报李。郑氏妾一切待遇等同“媵”。窦夫人还自掏腰包，给郑氏妾增加了三成月例，并许诺在李建成娶妻前，郑氏妾在李建成后院的权力就等同于李建成的妻。

窦夫人还带其他儿女来拜见新婚的大郑氏，让李世民、李玄霸叫大郑氏大嫂，给足了大郑氏和荥阳郑氏的面子。

经历了一次寡居被落白眼，差点被送与白发老翁高官为继室，大郑氏心思已经十分通透。

她一点都不想要什么权力，也不准备端着什么世家女的架子，只一门心思讨好李建成，争取在李建成正妻入门之前多生几个儿子。

嫡庶有别，大郑氏没想过去抢什么嫡长子的位置。只要有了儿子，她就有了底气。就算将来正妻入门她失了宠，嫡长子出生后，也要因为孝悌好好尊敬庶兄。

庶兄怎么都比庶弟强。

看看李世民和李玄霸两兄弟，还与李建成是同母所生。就因为他们年幼，自己卖力获得的好处，大部分都被李建成拿了。李建成身为兄长，什么都不需要做，坐享其成就行。

其实郑家和其他世家也不是没有想给李世民和李玄霸“好处”，只是因为两人太过年幼，所以联姻这种事不好说出口。

他们又不是如长孙晟这种鲜卑勋贵，颇不知礼，三岁的女儿都能定亲。

“呸，他们世家之间指腹为婚的都不少，这还没出生就联姻了呢！他们就是嫉妒我妹妹！”长孙无忌听了酸言酸语，十分生气。

李世民脑袋一点一点：“啊对对对。”

长孙无忌生气了：“你怎么这么敷衍！这时候你不该站出来保护我妹妹吗！”

李世民无奈：“你要我怎么站出来？”

长孙无忌想了想，也确实想不到李世民该如何站出来，只能自己生闷气，抢了李玄霸的果脯啃。

李玄霸低头看着自己的手。

李世民赶紧重新拿了一块果脯塞进李玄霸手里，骂道：“盘子里这么多果脯，你抢阿玄的干什么！”

长孙无忌笑道：“我只是看李三闷闷的模样，想逗逗他。”

这时称呼人除了叫字，还能直接叫排行。特别是同性别的人，连“郎”都不叫，直接叫姓氏加排行。

李玄霸腹诽：【小心我改姓张，以后叫张三，吓死你。】

李世民满头雾水。不懂弟弟为什么要改姓，更不懂“张三”为什么就能吓死人。

李玄霸懒得理睬长孙无忌。

这人自从听到了高夫人抱怨京城贵族女眷圈子诽谤长孙家的家风，一大早就跑过来，从吃早膳一直抱怨到吃午膳。

史书里都没写，长孙无忌居然还跑到唐太宗家里蹭早晚饭的，唉。

李世民也是好脾气，长孙无忌嘴不停地车轱辘似地抱怨了半日，他就听了半日。

长孙无忌啃完从李玄霸手中抢过的果脯，终于停止抱怨了。

李玄霸把耳中丝线团拽出来。

长孙无忌气得又抢了李玄霸手中的果脯。

李世民赶紧又给弟弟手里塞了一块果脯。

李世民抱怨道：“别老抢阿玄的。你多大的人了，怎么如此幼稚？”

长孙无忌冷哼了一声。

李玄霸：【还傲娇上了？恶心心。】

李世民扶额，他用眼神教训弟弟，也不要如此幼稚，一直在心声里不断笑话长孙无忌。

长孙无忌又把从李玄霸那里抢来的果脯啃完，拍了拍手：“李三，阿娘也给了我一个脂粉铺子练手。听说你那个香皂快做好了，我帮你卖？”

李玄霸点头：“好。”

长孙无忌惊讶道：“你就这么同意了？”

李玄霸道：“那不然呢？”

长孙无忌不好意思地摸了摸鼻子，实话实说道：“那铺子说是给我的，其实是给妹妹的。可不是我想占你便宜。”

李玄霸道：“一家人，说什么占便宜。如果卖得好，你和你娘说一声，问高夫人能不能与我合作。我就一家铺子，货太多了卖不完。”

长孙无忌疑惑：“你们唐国公府的铺子很多吧？”

李世民拍了拍长孙无忌的肩膀，压低声音道：“唐国公府的铺子赚的钱进公中，我和阿玄顶多多拿点零花钱。但你家帮忙卖，就是与我和阿玄单独签订……嗯，那个阿玄说的合同，我和阿玄直接从你们家拿钱。”

长孙无忌虽然年纪不大，对商事也不精通，但这么浅显的道理，他也立刻明白了。

“知道了，我让阿娘用嫁妆与你们做生意，这样赚的钱也不会进长孙府的公中。”长孙无忌叹气道，“你们和我一样，有个兄长压在上面，颇不自在。不过话先说在前面，我娘的嫁妆不多，可不敢冒险。”

高夫人是北齐宗室，父亲是北齐乐安王高劢。北周灭北齐后，大部分北齐宗室的财产都被掠夺一空。高家现在的家产，全是高劢在大隋当刺史攒的，与其他勋贵无法比。

大兴居不易，高劢能给嫁给长孙晟当继室的高夫人在西市谋几间铺子，还是托了长孙晟的门路。

这时候女子的嫁妆就代表女子在家中的地位，所以长孙无忌的兄长都瞧不起高氏这个继母，在长孙晟不在家的时候，视继母如父亲的妾。

李玄霸道：“尽管放心。好卖的东西我再放你家铺子。”

长孙无忌笑道：“那我家小妹的嫁妆就全靠你了。唉，李二，你不会嫌弃我家小妹嫁妆少吧？”

李玄霸悄悄地拧了一下自己的大腿，才没笑出来。

可惜现在他不能更新自己的营销号，不然又有新的话题可以水了。

震惊！长孙无忌少年时就露出权臣的尾巴！他居然叫唐太宗“李二”！

李世民无奈：“你说什么傻话？哪怕没有嫁妆，她仍旧是我的妻，我一定会很尊重她。你是在侮辱我家家风吗？”

听到李世民有些生气，长孙无忌低着头道歉道：“抱歉，我是被家里的事弄烦心了，不是侮辱你的家风。”

“我原谅你。”李世民道，“别太在意你兄长。等我和阿玄长大后，你跟着我和阿玄一起建功立业，把你娘接出来住，不受你兄长的气。”

长孙无忌点头：“好！”

李玄霸无语。长孙四郎啊，你年纪比我和哥还大五岁，你就这么自觉地把你自己的地位定位到“跟班”了？

被李世民安慰后，长孙无忌心情好了许多。

长孙晟在家的时候，长孙无忌母子的日子好过了不少，兄长都很收敛。

杨素的葬礼之后，长孙晟假期结束。因杨广还留在东京，所以朝中重臣都要在东京，所以长孙晟又离开了家。长孙无忌的兄长故态复萌，让长孙无忌心中颇为气恼。

李渊本来也该去东京，但杨广给他新安排了编撰和印刷官学教材的工作，他便继续留在大兴了。

李世民和李玄霸都挺开心。哪怕李玄霸悄悄与李渊保持距离，但独孤老夫人有儿子陪着，大半精力都在儿子身上，不再折腾窦夫人。他们看见母亲精神越来越好，自然开心。

终于把长孙无忌哄开心，送走长孙无忌后，李世民双手枕在脑后，长叹一口气道：“如阿玄你说的，家家都有本难念的经。”

李玄霸点头。

他犹豫了一会儿道：“哥，你现在已经快八岁了，心理承受能力强许多了吧？”

李世民双手放下，瞥了李玄霸一眼：“你能不说给我听吗？”

李玄霸道：“关于你未婚妻的事，不听？”

李世民眼皮子跳了跳，垂头丧气道：“说吧。”

李玄霸切换心音：【你岳父大业五年去世，刚去世，长孙安业就把高夫人、长孙无忌和你未婚妻赶出了家门。】

李世民“唰”地一脚踢向庭院小道旁的灌木丛，抬起的脸上眉头紧皱，眼中闪烁着不像孩童的暴戾：“他敢！孝悌之名不要了吗！”

李玄霸点头：【不要了。后来他们三人就寄居在舅舅高士廉家中。高士廉对他们很好，但这段经历应该还是不好受。】

李世民垂眸不语。

待两个孩子回到屋内，李世民抬头道：“阿玄，赚钱的事哥哥不懂，你要哥哥怎么做，哥哥全力配合你。”

李玄霸点头：【只要高夫人肯配合，带着高夫人赚钱的事你放心。我只是想，听长孙四郎说，高夫人已经开始教长孙小娘子识字。二哥何不把自己启蒙教材整理一份，亲手抄写一些长孙小娘子能用的书本送给长孙小娘子？】

李世民不太明白：“这样能对高夫人和长孙无忌的处境有用？”

李玄霸道：【唐国公府现在越来越显赫，你我二人更是早早就在皇帝面前挂了名号，将来前途肯定无量。人皆逐利，我想长孙安业再愚蠢，也应该看在唐国公府的面子，斟酌一下把唐国公未来的儿妇赶出门的影响。】

李世民叹了口气，道：“世人皆逐利。好，我问一问娘亲，能给刚识字的小娘子写什么。”

他没有问弟弟看到的未来中，为何自己的未婚妻会被长孙安业赶出家门，那时候长孙安业就完全不顾唐国公府的脸面吗？

没必要问。

愚蠢的人的想法没必要追究，他只要知道怎么应对就行。

李世民在长孙府玩耍的时候见过长孙安业，那是一个从头至尾都透露着愚蠢和傲慢的人，完全看不出有岳父长孙晟半分影子。

李世民握拳：“将来我的儿子，可不能像长孙安业那样，我一定要严格地管教他。”

李玄霸：【啊？你还是别太严格了。你就是太严格了，以为人人都和你一样抗压，把一群喷子弄你儿子身边。你儿子腰间戴一块玉佩，就被喷成桀纣再世，你还在那说喷得对。再加上你对幼子太过偏爱宽容，他一对比，精神都出问题了，变得疯疯癫癫。】

李世民“啊”了一声，用头撞李玄霸刚制作的花草靠枕。

李玄霸吓了一跳：“哥，你做什么？”

李世民惨叫：“别说了别说了，我不想听这个！不要告诉我这个！为什么我还不到八岁，就要知道我儿子疯了！”

李玄霸眼神游移：“你自己问的。”

李世民抱着枕头满榻打滚：“我没问！我没问！我没问！”

李玄霸双手举起来：“行行行，你没问，我的错。等你儿子满月的时候我再和你说……哎哟！哥，你居然扔枕头砸我？！”

李玄霸不敢置信！

李世民气得声音颤抖：“你听听你说的是人话吗！”

李玄霸歪头。我怎么说的不是人话了？

“啊啊啊啊啊！”李世民又抓了一个枕头砸向李玄霸，“我怎么有你这样的弟弟！我好惨啊！”

李玄霸接住枕头：“……”完了，二哥心态完全崩了。

不过你心态崩了就能扔枕头砸我吗？看招！

李玄霸立刻还击。

窦夫人来看两人的时候，发现屋内一片狼藉。

新作的枕头里的干花干草全部飞了满屋，地上还有遭殃的书本、文房四宝，和一堆被枕头砸到地上的白釉瓷花瓶碎片。

窦夫人深呼吸，顺手抽出花瓶残骸里的花枝：“李世民！李玄霸！”

“快跑！”李世民鞋子都来不及穿，拉着李玄霸就跑，“耶耶！救命！”

窦夫人气笑了：“还想跑？给我拦住他们！”

几个健壮仆婆如饿狼捕猎般扑了出去。

李世民若是一个人，大概能顺利逃到李渊身边。

但无奈，他有个拖油瓶弟弟。

李玄霸努力跑了几步之后，就成了李世民的累赘。

李世民无奈，只好和李玄霸一起被仆婆逮住，像小鸡一样被抓到母亲面前。

李世民和李玄霸的手板心各挨了二十下，并罚抄《孝经》。

李世民因为是兄长，所以罪加一等，罚抄比李玄霸多一倍。

不过李玄霸很有兄弟情，帮李世民抄了一半。

然后，李世民和李玄霸的罚抄各增加了一倍。

窦夫人冷笑：“你们二人模仿对方字迹足以以假乱真。但怎么能瞒得过你们的娘？！”

别说李世民，李玄霸都短暂退回了孩童心智，呜呜呜哭了。

就是成年人罚抄这么多，也要一把鼻涕一把眼泪啊。

李渊特意来观看两个神童哭着罚抄，笑得特别开心。

高颎和宇文弼得知了此事，和窦夫人商议，把《孝经》换成教授的典籍，每种典籍各抄几份，凑够数就行了。

只抄《孝经》是浪费时间，借着罚抄，让两个孩子多学些东西，岂不是一箭双雕？

本来李世民和李玄霸的《孝经》已经背熟了，默写速度特别快。两位老师插手之后，两人完成罚抄的速度至少降低八成。

李世民：“呜呜呜，阿玄，老师欺负人！”

李玄霸咬牙切齿。

就算他再好学，也经不住这样多的罚抄啊！

什么功课！不要啦！什么抄写！崩溃啦！

兄弟二人抱头痛哭。

“以后不打架了。”

“嗯，再不打架了。”

“呜呜呜呜。”乘以二。

……

“哈哈哈哈哈！”李昭笑得前俯后仰。

柴绍帮新婚妻子拍着背，笑道：“你们究竟把屋里糟蹋成什么样子？居然把丈母气成那样？”

李世民和李玄霸瘪嘴瞪视柴绍。

阿姊能笑我们，你算个屁，不准笑！

柴绍看着两个小舅子充满魄力的眼神，干咳了一声，道：“音娘，别笑了，你看他们都恼羞成怒了。”

李昭笑道：“他们可不是生我的气，是不准你笑话。”

李世民抱着手臂：“哼。”

李玄霸道：“别耽误正事。来看看香皂做的如何了。”

柴绍给两个小舅子面子，跟着转移话题：“没想到还居然能做出来。太子那里已经取消了赌约，三郎还要继续打赌？”

李玄霸道：“他承诺的赌注，应该不会昧了吧？”

柴绍道：“那自然不会。”

柴绍好奇地跟在李玄霸身后，参观香皂工坊。

若香皂真的能做出来，柴家肯定要分一杯羹。

他和音娘都已经商量好了，拿了方子后，材料和销售都自行解决，赚的钱给李世民和李玄霸各一成，不告诉唐国公府。

两个孩子将来独自打拼肯定需要很多钱，他们能帮一点是一点。

李玄霸进香皂工坊的时候，工坊里的人见到李玄霸等人到来，激动地给主人们磕了好几个响头。

柴绍疑惑。

李世民解释：“这里的地以前种不出好庄稼，人很穷。阿玄给他们开了工钱，还能直接折算成粮食和布匹，所以他们都很感激。”

柴绍惊讶：“自己家的佃农还要开工钱？”

李世民更惊讶：“不开工钱，难道让他们饿死吗？”

柴绍道：“只要给口吃的不就行了？”

李世民道：“那不如直接开工钱。反正都要给，给工钱他们干活的积极性还高一些。何况我和阿玄也不缺这点钱。”

李昭道：“二郎三郎心善，柴郎，别教坏我弟弟。”

柴绍立刻闭嘴。

他继续好奇地东张西望。

虽然他觉得给佃农和奴隶开工钱很不可思议，因为这时给主人家做活也是广义的“徭役”，是写进法律中的。

不过正如李世民所说，给了这些人工钱，他们干活的态度很认真，又麻利又细致。

李世民见柴绍的表情，似乎是理解他们的做法，得意道：“其实我也没想那么多，是阿玄提的。”

柴绍看向一言不发的李玄霸。

李玄霸道：“我厌恶所有让别人干活又不给工钱的人。”

柴绍失笑：“真不知道你为什么对钱财这么看重。你也没吃过苦啊。”

李玄霸不说话。我吃的苦多得去了。

其实李玄霸对工坊不太满意。

香皂工坊，其实是从提纯土碱开始做。

提纯土碱，和用盐土熬盐是差不多的步骤。

这里的草木还是繁盛，就是长不出果腹的庄稼；河水井水也不少，就是苦涩难以入口。

不远的地方就是繁华的大隋城，但隋文帝实施的户籍制度将人牢牢绑在土地上，他们只能远眺繁华的都市，在这片贫瘠的地方过着饥寒交迫的生活。

李玄霸教他们熬碱土烧碱水提纯土碱，再榨大豆油做香皂。不仅每日都有工钱，如果做的活够好够多，还能计件额外加钱。

若夫妻二人都在工坊做活，每日的口粮养活一家老小还能剩一点。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 32: Scented Soap, Glycerin, and Soap Bubbles

When Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi clashed with the Jingzhao Wei clan, no one suspected that it had anything to do with Li Xuanba.

Although Li Xuanba was a student of Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, the two old ministers had pupils throughout the land. Furthermore, these two students, Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, had been forced upon them by the Emperor.

Outsiders did not know how Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi usually interacted with Li Xuanba and Li Shimin. Naturally, they would not believe that two seven-year-old children could be highly regarded by these two elder statesmen in their sixties.

Even the Jingzhao Wei clan simply cursed their bad luck, believing they had run straight into the Emperor's blade. They assumed the Emperor was still displeased with their previous testing of the waters and was using this opportunity to beat them down.

Otherwise, with so many noble clans secretly spreading rumors, why would he latch onto the Jingzhao Wei clan and refuse to let go?

They had no intention of continuing to oppose Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi. The two old men had already resigned from their official posts to compile books; relentlessly pursuing them would look terrible and would only draw the Emperor's resentment. Thus, they could only sigh and swallow this bitter pill in silence.

Seeing this, the other noble clans understood that the Emperor was indeed intent on promoting Confucianism. They immediately changed their tune and ceased their obstruction.

The great clans were not foolish. There was a saying: "Dynasties flow like water, but noble clans stand firm as iron." However, those clans that had clashed head-on with dynasties had been slaughtered countless times; what remained was often just the name. For instance, the main branch of the Hongnong Yang clan was currently the imperial lineage of the Sui Dynasty. Anyone with half a brain knew exactly what that meant.

The Duke of Tang's household also claimed to be an alliance of two great Han noble clans to the outside world. Li Yuan had linked his lineage to the Li clan of Longxi—one of the "Five Surnames and Seven Clans"—while Duchess Dou had linked hers to the Dou clan of Fufeng.

Consequently, internal divisions within the great clans were severe. It was difficult for them to pull their strength in one direction to jointly block the decrees of an emperor who held absolute power.

Furthermore, during the Han Dynasty, there had been a "Renaissance" of sorts. It was claimed that ancient Confucian scriptures written in large and small seal script had been excavated from the Temple of Confucius. These were called the "Old Text Classics," used to counter the "New Text Classics" written in the clerical script of the time.

In the Han Dynasty, where the recommendation system was dominant, fighting for the "right to annotate scriptures" was equivalent to fighting for status in the imperial court.

In the late Eastern Han Dynasty, many classical scholars devoted themselves to the study of the "Old Text Classics." Using the philosophy of "I annotate the Six Classics," they promoted their own political views to save the world from collapse.

They opened numerous private schools, teaching their annotated scriptures to the commoners whom the elites of the time looked down upon. This created a powerful momentum and nurtured many talents.

Later, the ancestors of many great clans of the Wei and Jin Dynasties participated in this movement. During the rapid succession of dynasties, they acquired immense fame and wealth, leaping to become top-tier noble clans. Examples included the Zheng clan of Xingyang and the Lu clan of Fanyang, both of the "Five Surnames and Seven Clans." The Zheng clan of Xingyang was particularly prominent, as the "Teachings of Zheng and Jia" was currently a dominant school of thought.

Upon hearing about the woodblock printing of Confucian scriptures, these two clans had secretly begun gathering woodblock printing artisans. Once the Emperor's stance became clear, they prepared to print the scriptures with fiery enthusiasm, wishing they could put a copy of their own clan's annotated scriptures into the hands of every scholar in the world.

The status of the Xingyang Zheng and Fanyang Lu clans had been accumulated precisely by having pupils throughout the land, unlike some scholarly clans that hoarded their knowledge like precious trash. Although they looked down on those of humble birth, they absolutely loved the idea of turning all those humble scholars into their "disciples."

When the Zheng family learned that the first person to propose printing the Confucian scriptures was Li Xuanba, they held an internal family meeting. They hurriedly sent the beautiful Zheng clan concubine, whom they had promised to Li Jiancheng, into his manor ahead of schedule, adding an extra ten percent to her dowry.

Although Li Jiancheng had now become an Imperial Bodyguard, it was only a sixth-rank post, and he was not yet qualified to have official concubines of the *ying* rank. Originally, the Zheng family had intended to wait until Li Jiancheng was promoted to the fifth rank before sending this widowed daughter of their clan to him.

For the grand Zheng clan of Xingyang to send a woman of their lineage to be another's concubine, she naturally had to be a "lateral wife" with a formal title. She needed an imperial mandate of noblewoman status to not be considered insulted.

But now, forget it. The Duke of Tang's household was growing stronger by the day, and the Zheng family stood to gain immense benefits from this printing of Confucian scriptures. Thus, they took another step back.

The Duke of Tang's household returned the favor. The Zheng concubine's treatment was made entirely equal to that of a *ying*. Duchess Dou even paid out of her own pocket to increase the concubine's monthly allowance by thirty percent, promising that before Li Jiancheng wed a formal wife, the Zheng concubine's authority in his inner courtyard would be equal to that of a wife.

Duchess Dou also brought her other children to pay their respects to the newly arrived elder Lady Zheng, having Li Shimin and Li Xuanba address her as "Eldest Sister-in-Law," giving her and the Xingyang Zheng clan ample face.

Having experienced the cold shoulders of widowhood and nearly being sent to a white-haired, high-ranking old man as a successor wife, the elder Lady Zheng had become highly pragmatic.

She did not want power at all, nor did she intend to put on the airs of a noble daughter. Her sole focus was to please Li Jiancheng and strive to bear him several sons before his formal wife entered the household.

There was a strict distinction between legitimate and concubine-born children, and Lady Zheng had no intention of fighting for the position of the eldest legitimate son. As long as she had sons, she would have a foundation. Even if she lost favor once the formal wife arrived, any future legitimate son would still have to respect his older half-brothers out of filial piety and brotherly duty.

An older half-brother was always in a better position than a younger one.

Just look at the two brothers, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, who shared the same mother as Li Jiancheng.
