Chapter 33: Monarch and Subject Blow Bubbles Together

When Li Zhao and Chai Shao left, they only took two bars of soap for their parents, but they carried away a large crate of liquid soap.

Li Shimin said, "Big Sister will surely blow bubbles non-stop once she gets home. Ah Xuan, let’s take some home to blow bubbles too!"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Fine."

The soap itself didn't cause much of a stir, but the soapy water was adored by everyone. Was this a case of "buying the casket and returning the pearl"?

After Li Shimin promoted the soapy water throughout the Tang State Duke’s mansion, it indeed became a hit with everyone.

Even Li Yuanji gave Li Xuanba a brief look of favor, refraining from spitting at him the moment he laid eyes on him.

Li Xuanba was truly baffled. To this day, he didn't understand why Li Yuanji hated him so much.

It couldn't possibly be because Second Brother had beaten Li Yuanji up too many times, could it? That had nothing to do with him.

Fortunately, the well-behaved younger brother, Li Zhiyun, healed Li Xuanba’s soul.

"Thank you, Third Brother. Third Brother, let me blow a super big bubble for you!" Li Zhiyun said, clinging to Li Xuanba.

Li Shimin plucked Li Zhiyun in front of him and laughed, "Why only blow bubbles for your Third Brother? What about Second Brother?"

Li Zhiyun answered honestly, "I’ll blow some for Second Brother too, but I’ll blow the biggest one for Third Brother."

Li Shimin pressed, "Why?"

Li Zhiyun puffed out his cheeks and didn't answer.

"Alright, stop teasing Little Five." Li Xuanba pulled Li Zhiyun behind him for protection and said crossly, "Why are you still asking why? It’s because you always make fun of Little Five."

Li Zhiyun was sometimes a bit dazed; he would trip on flat ground or accidentally get ink in his mouth. He looked nothing like the historical records that described him at thirteen as "skilled in archery and horsemanship, and adept at calligraphy and chess."

Li Shimin had a mischievous nature. Whenever his younger brother did something silly, he could laugh so hard it felt like the whole room was roaring with him.

Li Shimin was the same toward Li Xuanba, though Li Xuanba didn't hold it against him.

Li Shimin rubbed his nose, looking embarrassed. "Is that so? I won't laugh at him next time."

Li Xuanba twitched his lips. "You said that last time, too."

Li Shimin replied shamelessly, "The 'me' from last time is not the same 'me' as this time."

Li Xuanba was so amused by his brother's thick skin that he laughed. "Fine, I’ll see when you turn into a 'new you' next time."

Li Zhiyun hugged his Third Brother’s waist and smiled at his Second Brother as well.

Seeing Li Zhiyun’s silly grin, Li Shimin relied on his agility to reach out, pinch Li Zhiyun’s cheek, and run off.

Li Zhiyun covered his face in disbelief, tears welling up in his eyes.

While comforting his younger brother, Li Xuanba scolded, "Don't run! We just agreed not to bully Little Five!"

Li Shimin vanished in a flash, his wild laughter echoing behind him: "I’m not bullying Little Five, hahahaha!"

Unable to catch his brother, who was more agile than a monkey, Li Xuanba could only note this grudge in his little mental book, preparing to complain to their mother later.

"There, there, don't cry. Come, Third Brother will teach you how to blow big bubbles."

Li Xuanba had someone make a slightly larger hoop, heated the soapy water, added some cane sugar, and let it sit for a while. He truly managed to blow a bubble for Li Zhiyun that was larger than the boy's own head.

Holding a fan, Li Zhiyun carefully fanned the bubble toward the sky. "Third Brother, can we keep this bubble?"

Li Xuanba chuckled softly. "We can't, but you can blow even more big bubbles. Want to try?"

After the big bubble burst, Li Zhiyun picked up the new soapy water and tried to blow one himself.

Whenever a big bubble popped, Li Zhiyun’s eyebrows and mouth would droop.

Whenever he successfully blew a big one, he would jump for joy and cheer loudly.

For the first time, Li Xuanba realized that although a child’s voice could be piercing, it wasn't always annoying.

"The big bubble water is fun, and the small bubble water is fun too." Li Xuanba mixed another bottle of soapy water with vinegar.

A stream of tiny bubbles was blown out, looking like pearls floating in the air.

Li Zhiyun blew a big bubble, then a small one, his little head getting dizzy from the excitement.

Lady Wan watched the two brothers playing from the corner of the wall, unable to stop her tears.

A maid whispered, "My Lady, why don't you go out? The Fifth Young Master would surely love to play with you."

Lady Wan shook her head, preparing to leave quietly.

"Eh? Auntie Wan, what are you doing?" Li Shimin suddenly popped out from the bushes behind her, giving her a start.

Hearing his Second Brother’s voice, Li Xuanba rushed over with unprecedented speed and caught him red-handed.

"Go apologize to Little Five right now! Is that any way for a brother to act?" Li Xuanba tugged at Li Shimin’s arm. "Auntie Wan? Are you here to see Little Five? Little Five! Auntie Wan is here, come show her your bubble-blowing skills!"

Li Zhiyun beamed. "Okay! Auntie, Auntie, watch me blow bubbles!"

Lady Wan felt a pang in her heart, but the corners of her mouth curled up involuntarily. She said gently, "Alright, Auntie will watch Fifth Young Master blow bubbles."

Li Xuanba yanked the little topknot on Li Shimin’s head. "Apologize!"

"Ouch, stop pulling, stop pulling! Look, Little Five doesn't even mind... Alright, alright, I apologize." Li Shimin reached out to Li Zhiyun. "Little Five, sorry, I shouldn't have pinched you. Come, Second Brother will blow bubbles for you!"

Li Zhiyun hadn't really been angry to begin with, and he happily blew bubbles with his Second Brother.

Finally freed from babysitting, Li Xuanba sat on the steps to slack off.

"Send the newly mixed soapy water to Big Brother, the Fourth Brother, and our sisters," Li Xuanba thought for a moment and added, "Send some to Grandmother, Mother, and Father as well. Ask Mother if we should send some to our married elder sister."

The nanny bowed and replied, "Yes."

Li Xuanba stretched and leaned back, staring blankly at the wild geese migrating south.

The autumn air was crisp and refreshing. The autumn sky seemed higher above the ground than in other seasons, making one feel drowsy just looking at it.

Although Li Xuanba felt drowsy all year round, he could always find a reason for it.

He yawned, preparing to take a nap right there.

Li Shimin held a finger to his lips and shushed Li Zhiyun.

Li Zhiyun nodded, mimicking his Second Brother’s mischievous expression.

The two brothers handed their bubble water to Lady Wan, then tiptoed toward the dozing Li Xuanba.

Li Zhiyun hunched his body, following behind Li Shimin, his little head bobbing in perfect sync with his brother’s.

Lady Wan handed the bubble water to the maid and covered her mouth with her sleeve to keep from laughing out loud.

The way her eyes curved was seven or eight parts similar to Li Zhiyun’s.

Li Shimin crept up to Li Xuanba, then turned back to pick up Li Zhiyun.

Li Zhiyun tilted his head: "?"

With a wicked grin, Li Shimin placed Li Zhiyun onto Li Xuanba’s rising and falling belly.

Li Zhiyun lay on Li Xuanba, looking dazed, like a little puppy.

Li Xuanba snapped his eyes open: "Ah!!"

Li Shimin: "Hahahahaha, no sleeping! Get up and play with Little Five."

Li Zhiyun, still dazed, reached out and hugged Li Xuanba’s neck.

Li Xuanba was being pressed so hard he couldn't breathe. "Get, get off! Third Brother can't breathe!"

Li Zhiyun remained dazed, not moving an inch.

Li Shimin clutched his stomach, laughing so hard he swayed back and forth, eventually tripping and falling to the ground, where he continued to laugh.

Lady Wan couldn't hold back either; she went to rescue Li Xuanba while laughing.

She picked up Li Zhiyun and gently rubbed her unadorned cheek against his. "Don't bother your Third Brother."

Li Xuanba finally climbed up and lunged at Li Shimin, who was still sitting on the ground laughing.

The two brothers rolled into a ball. Li Xuanba threw punches and kicks, while Li Shimin dodged and parried, mocking his younger brother’s "flowery fists and embroidered legs."

Li Zhiyun blinked and pointed at the ground. "Mother, I want to play too."

Lady Wan smiled and placed Li Zhiyun on the ground. "Go ahead."

Li Zhiyun laughed and pounced on his brothers, who were covered in dust.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba both cried "Ouch!" and, after exchanging a glance, lay down together to tickle their younger brother.

Li Zhiyun rolled on the ground laughing, bumping his head against Li Xuanba and kicking Li Shimin.

The three brothers continued to roll into a ball.

Li Xuanba was the first to be "eliminated" from the fray due to lack of stamina, and after admitting defeat, he lay on the ground like a corpse.

Li Shimin and Li Zhiyun continued to roll around and kick each other.

Li Xuanba thought: *It’s time to find you a tabby cat to raise. The way you and Little Five are fighting is exactly like cats.*

Li Shimin was too immersed in the childish kicking game with his brother, who was three years his junior, to notice Li Xuanba’s mischief.

It wasn't until Lady Dou arrived that the two energetic little ones stopped rolling around.

Lady Dou looked at the three mud monkeys, both angry and amused. She poked Lady Wan’s forehead hard. "You, you just indulge them!"

Lady Wan covered her mouth and laughed.

Lady Dou ordered someone to haul the three mud monkeys off to bathe, deciding it was the perfect time to try the soap Li Xuanba and Li Shimin had brought back.

The three little ones waved at Lady Wan.

Lady Wan waved back with a smile.

She returned to her courtyard, stitching clothes for Li Zhiyun while savoring the day’s joy.

Suddenly, her hand trembled, and the embroidery needle pricked her finger.

A bead of blood stained the silk thread.

Lady Wan’s tears fell, blurring the bloodstain, making it look like a blooming red plum blossom on the emerald branch she had just embroidered.

"He called me 'Mother'," Lady Wan whispered, her voice trembling. "I only just realized it now."

Lady Wan put down the needle, covered her face with both hands, and wept in silence.

Little Five knew she was his mother and had called her "Mother" in secret.

"Lady Dou, thank you, thank you..."

Lady Wan sobbed softly.

...

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba could bathe themselves, and the two brothers could even scrub each other’s backs, so Lady Dou didn't need to worry.

Lady Dou fetched a basin of water and helped scrub the mud off Li Zhiyun beside the tub.

"Lady, I secretly called Auntie 'Mother' just now," Li Zhiyun said, holding his hands high. "But Auntie didn't seem to react. Is Auntie really my birth mother?"

Lady Dou said softly, "She is your birth mother. Lady Wan is like you—sometimes a bit dazed—she must have needed to go back and ponder it for a while before it clicked."

Li Zhiyun pouted. "Little Five isn't dazed!"

Lady Dou laughed. "Alright, alright, Little Five isn't dazed. Little Five, your mother carries a heavy heart. Just call her 'Mother' quietly in her ear, and don't let others hear, or she’ll start worrying about this and that again."

Although Li Zhiyun didn't understand, he nodded obediently.

Actually, he thought the Lady was quite good, and there was no real need for a new mother. But since the Lady taught him this, perhaps it was truly necessary, and he was just too young to perceive it.

Besides, Auntie Wan was very good to him. After getting familiar, he liked her very much and didn't mind calling her "Mother" in secret.

Watching Li Zhiyun’s obedient demeanor, Lady Dou thought of Li Yuanji, her mood becoming very complex.

Lady Dou had never done anything wrong in her life, except for failing her youngest son.

But perhaps she was truly mad; even now, while she knew rationally that she should be good to her youngest son, whenever she saw him, the disgust and fear that had surged when she first gave birth to him would faintly resurface.

Especially after her husband returned and she finally had a hand in Li Yuanji’s education, trying to steer him back on track, only to fail repeatedly—the thought "it is as I feared" would always cross her mind.

This made Lady Dou suffer immensely.

However, Lady Dou’s reason could restrain her emotions, so she still tried her best to teach Li Yuanji, even neglecting Li Shimin and Li Xuanba somewhat.

The more she suffered, the harder she tried to be good to Li Yuanji.

Yet Li Yuanji completely rejected her kindness. He detested his mother, who forbade him from doing this and that, and often went to complain to the Old Lady Dugu.

Li Yuan originally stood on Lady Dou’s side, educating Li Yuanji with her.

But after the Old Lady Dugu said a few words, he hesitated and turned to persuade Lady Dou not to be so strict with Li Yuanji.

Children as intelligent and sensible as Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were naturally good, but the Tang State Duke’s mansion wasn't lacking the food Li Yuanji ate; they could afford to raise a wastrel.

It was impossible for every descendant of the Tang State Duke’s mansion to be excellent. Since Li Yuanji didn't like reading, it wouldn't hurt to be a little more lenient. He could always become an official through the shadow privilege anyway.

Moreover, Li Yuan really didn't want to personally tutor Li Yuanji anymore.

"Lady, do you want to blow bubbles?" Li Shimin appeared from somewhere with a bottle of bubble water.

Lady Dou came back to her senses, looking at her naked son blowing bubbles, and didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "Hurry up and dry off and get dressed! Blowing bubbles while stark naked! Be careful not to catch a cold!"

Li Shimin: "I won't, I’ll blow for a while longer before getting dressed, it’s very hot now!"

Lady Dou took a deep breath. "Li Shimin!"

Li Xuanba, while getting dressed, used his peripheral vision to despise his naked Second Brother, who was running around blowing bubbles while his "little bird" was exposed.

See? Second Brother was just asking for a beating.

Ouch, sure enough, he got smacked. Li Xuanba smiled.

Li Zhiyun bit his finger, his little head unable to understand why his brother knew he would definitely get beaten but still insisted on provoking the Lady.

"Don't learn from your Second Brother." After Li Xuanba was dressed, he helped Li Zhiyun dress with the help of a maid.

Li Zhiyun nodded. Right, don't learn from Second Brother; Second Brother often gets beaten. He would only learn from Third Brother in the future! Third Brother rarely gets beaten!

...

In the Eastern Capital, Yang Guang rested his chin on one hand, his face full of impatience.

Ministers had been remonstrating one after another, begging Yang Guang not to stay in the Eastern Capital and to return to the capital. Seeing the Emperor’s impatience, they sighed and left, missing Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi.

If Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were here, they could lead them in constant remonstrance to the Emperor.

Now that the leaders were gone, none of them dared to take the lead. Seeing the Emperor’s mood, they could only shut their mouths immediately.

After the ministers left, Yang Guang’s expression improved slightly.

"Hmph, return to the capital? Who knows whose capital Daxing is now," Yang Guang cursed.

The palace attendants present wished they could plug their ears.

Just as Yang Guang was losing his temper, an attendant tremblingly reported that the Prince Consort, Yuwen Shiji, requested an audience.

Yang Guang put away his anger and waved his hand. "Let him in."

Yuwen Shiji walked in with a gorgeous box in his hands, his face full of smiles. "Your subject pays respects to..."

"Alright, enough with the empty formalities." Yang Guang looked at Yuwen Shiji’s smile, and the gloom on his face dissipated a little. "You usually love to hide at home and idle away, refusing even to take an official post. Why did you think of seeing me today? What? Finally figured it out and want to strive for something?"

Yuwen Shiji gave a bitter smile to this imperial father-in-law who always loved to urge him to get ahead. "Your Majesty, I am truly not cut out to be an official. I came this time because I have something fun to tell you! Your Majesty, do you remember the bet between Li Sanlang and the Crown Prince?"

Yang Guang had someone bring a couch and let Yuwen Shiji sit opposite him. "The bet? Wasn't that already cancelled?"

Yuwen Shiji laughed. "Li Sanlang said that since it was a bet made between peers for fun, he didn't know why the elders intervened. But since he had accepted it, he had to finish the bet to maintain integrity. And so, the soap he spoke of has been made."

Yang Guang looked curiously at the box Yuwen Shiji had brought. "He asked you to send soap to me?"

Yuwen Shiji said, "Of course not. Li Erlang and Li Sanlang will surely write to you directly. They are very close to you. It’s just that before sending it to you, they sent some to others to get some feedback. I found it interesting, so I came to tell you in advance."

Just as Yang Guang was about to answer, someone else reported that Princess Nanyang had arrived.

Yang Guang quickly had honey water and melons brought out. Before Princess Nanyang even entered, he said, "Why did you two come one after the other?"

Yuwen Shiji’s expression stiffened.

Princess Nanyang walked in, full of anger. She first bowed to her imperial father, then pointed at Yuwen Shiji and scolded, "Li Erlang and Li Sanlang specifically warned in their letter not to tell Father, as they wanted to give him a surprise. And this man actually came secretly!"

Yang Guang was stunned, then slapped his thigh and laughed. "Renren, what is wrong with you?"

Yuwen Shiji said sheepishly, "I was having so much fun that I just wanted to show it to His Majesty, and I accidentally forgot."

Princess Nanyang gritted her teeth and twisted Yuwen Shiji’s arm hard.

Yuwen Shiji yelped in pain and quickly begged for mercy.

Yang Guang laughed loudly. "Alright, alright. Isn't soap just bath beans? How can it be so fun?"

Seeing that he couldn't hide it, Princess Nanyang glared at Yuwen Shiji and opened the box, taking out the bottle of liquid soap that was only half full.

She was surprised: "Wasn't there three bottles?"

Yuwen Shiji apologized with a smile: "It was too fun. When I realized there was only half a bottle left, I suddenly thought of showing it to His Majesty, and so..."

Princess Nanyang was so angry she twisted Yuwen Shiji’s arm again. "I told you to wait until I finished paying respects to Mother before playing, and you played until there was only half a bottle left?"

Yuwen Shiji apologized repeatedly: "I was wrong, I was wrong, I’ll write to Erlang and Sanlang right now and have them send more!"

Princess Nanyang was so angry she laughed. "Do you have no shame!"

Yuwen Shiji said, "My relationship with Shude is so close, there’s no need to be so calculating."

Yang Guang laughed and said, "Alright, stop bullying your husband. What exactly is so fun that even Renren forgot your instructions? That’s a first."

Princess Nanyang sighed and demonstrated for her father.

When Princess Nanyang blew a bunch of bubbles, Yang Guang stood up in surprise, took the bubble water, and blew hard himself.

The bubble went "pop" and exploded all over Yang Guang’s face.

Princess Nanyang covered her mouth and laughed. "Father, don't rush, take your time."

Yang Guang wiped his face and laughed. "That was a bit difficult, let’s try again!"

He finally blew a perfect bubble and was so delighted that he immediately called for Empress Xiao and his favorite concubines to come and blow bubbles together.

Yuwen Shiji said, "Blowing bubbles in the sunlight makes them look even better. I shall take my leave."

*Sigh*, now that the imperial consorts were coming, he couldn't stay and blow bubbles with the Emperor.

Yang Guang waved his sleeve casually, telling Yuwen Shiji to get lost quickly and not delay his bubble-blowing fun.

Princess Nanyang smiled and accompanied her father to continue blowing bubbles in the sunlight.

Bubbles, this novel item, could not only float in the air but also capture rainbows inside them, looking like fairy magic.

Yang Guang and Empress Xiao took turns blowing the remaining half bottle, while the other concubines could only watch longingly.

Yang Guang said, still wanting more, "This is truly too interesting. Did Li Sanlang come up with this?"

Princess Nanyang smiled. "Yes, Li Sanlang found it in an ancient book. It’s quite a story. Li Erlang and Li Sanlang often go to the West Market to play, browsing through interesting things from street vendors, like fragments of ancient books. Usually, these things are mostly fake, and the two brothers just do it for fun. Who knew that this time, they actually restored an ancient formula?"

Yang Guang thought of the chaotic West Market vendors, where not only Han dynasty formulas but even those from the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors were sold, and couldn't help but smile. "That is indeed an interesting story."

Princess Nanyang said, "The formula for this bubble water is made by melting soap; it’s not difficult. It’s just that the soap sent by Erlang and Sanlang is limited, and I can't bear to... Oh no! If Renren goes back, I hope he doesn't melt my soap!"

Yang Guang laughed. "Come, Empress, let’s go catch Renren and see if he really dares to melt the Great Lady’s soap!"

Empress Xiao chuckled. "Alright."

The Emperor and Empress left the concubines behind and took a sedan chair to find Yuwen Shiji.

Princess Nanyang had wronged Yuwen Shiji. Although Yuwen Shiji still wanted to play with the bubble water, he hadn't melted Princess Nanyang’s soap—he had run off to take a bath, blowing bubbles while bathing.

Princess Nanyang didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

Yang Guang was also a mischievous person. He didn't care that Yuwen Shiji was bathing and went straight to the bathhouse.

Yuwen Shiji could only wrap himself in a cloth to pay respects, with bubbles still in his hair.

Yang Guang found it interesting and, on a whim, decided to bathe as well.

Princess Nanyang had long since pulled Empress Xiao to another bathhouse to soak.

Princess Nanyang laughed. "Father will surely be unable to resist bathing, so we shall bathe too. Mother, let me wash your hair. This soap is very comfortable for washing hair."

Princess Nanyang quietly took out the liquid soap. "This is called soap lotion. I didn't tell Renren about this; he’ll surely sneakily use the soap lotion to blow bubbles."

Empress Xiao couldn't help but laugh.

Princess Nanyang opened the bottle of liquid soap, her face changing drastically. "Why is there only half a bottle left? Yuwen Shiji!"

Empress Xiao laughed until she almost choked.

On the other side, Yuwen Shiji was showing off to Yang Guang: "I secretly took half of the soap lotion the Princess hid. This soap lotion is especially comfortable for washing hair and can create many bubbles."

Yang Guang didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "Aren't you afraid Nanyang will pinch you?"

Yuwen Shiji laughed. "Let her pinch. If she pinches hard, it’s her own heart that will ache. Your Majesty, let me wash your hair!"

Yang Guang was eager to try. "I’ll do it myself!"

The two of them scrubbed their heads full of bubbles, laughing like fools.

...

"Hmm? Father has returned to Daxing?" Yang Zhao said happily. "Who persuaded him? I must go thank him!"

The reporter stammered: "Actually... actually..."

Yang Zhao was puzzled. "Is there something hard to say?"

The reporter said: "Perhaps it is the credit of Li Erlang and Li Sanlang."

Yang Zhao laughed. "Oh? What formula did these two children use to remonstrate?"

The reporter said: "Does the Crown Prince remember the soap and bubble water sent by the Tang State Duke’s mansion? His Majesty used it after getting it from Princess Nanyang and found it especially comfortable, so he returned to Daxing to personally ask Li Erlang and Li Sanlang if there was anything better. Originally, His Majesty wanted Li Erlang and Li Sanlang to go to the Eastern Capital, but both Li brothers are ill."

Yang Zhao was stunned for a moment, then sighed helplessly. "Father is truly... *sigh*, never mind, it’s a good thing he’s back. Open the treasury, select some precious medicinal herbs, and send them to the Tang State Duke’s mansion... No, I will go personally."

Yang Zhao thought of the letters Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had written to him, his mood complex.

In the letters, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba said that the bet must continue; it was a child’s bet, and it was truly annoying for elders to intervene, especially since they wouldn't lose anyway.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第33章 君臣一起吹泡泡 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
这本来没什么。杨昭以为唐国公府只是借李世民和李玄霸来向自己示好，将此事定格在孩子的玩闹。唐国公府仍旧与太子亲近，只是不想卷入皇孙间的斗争。

没想到李世民和李玄霸的“打赌”，居然能让倔脾气的父皇回京城，平息勋贵和关中世家的不满。

两个孩子肯定想不到会有这个结局。真的是很凑巧。

但这凑巧已经是第二次了。

第一次是父皇巡幸江都即将返回时，本来想走陆路，又重新制作依仗，耗费巨大人力物力。群臣皆规劝，父皇不听。

但这时李玄霸重病，母后和长姊借此劝说，也有许多老臣水土不服生病，若走陆路遇到意外病故，这首次巡幸就不吉利了。这才让父皇回心转意，朝中非议平息。

“这两个孩子，莫非是上天送给我大隋的祥瑞吉兆？”杨昭琢磨。

杨昭越想越觉得是这么回事。看来他要在唐国公府上花更多心思了。

杨昭想到就立刻着手做。

正好，他听说李建成纳了郑家新妇，却苦于身上官职品阶不够，不能置媵。

于是杨昭探望了李世民和李玄霸后，与李渊、李建成知会了一声，奏请皇帝，将李建成身上的散官品阶提了提，提到刚好正五品。

大隋的官职分散官和职官。散官就是干拿钱不干事的荣誉职介，上朝时也按照散官的品阶排序。职官就是有实权的官职。

北周官制改革后，将鲜卑勋贵和关中世家糅杂在一起，形成了强大的关陇贵族集团门阀，以与当时支持北齐的河东门阀与支持南朝的江南门阀抗衡。

为了拉拢关陇贵族门阀，关陇贵族皆可以通过荫蔽直接授予散官。职官才需要才能考核。这样就能保证关陇贵族门阀子子孙孙皆可为官。

隋朝建立之后，河东门阀“山东郡姓”和江南门阀“江南侨姓”也被纳入这一套荫官体系中。

所以李建成身为唐国公府的嫡长子，即使还年少，不能直接授予职官，但有太子亲自举荐，散官品阶还是可以提一提的。

杨广回到大兴后，欣然批了李建成的升迁，并专门在圣旨中说，这是为了犒赏李世民和李玄霸，但因为两个孩子都小，李渊又刚升迁，所以就赏赐李建成了。

圣旨一出，李世民和李玄霸神童之名再次响彻京城，并随着京中官吏羡慕的家书，朝着天下扩散。

李世民和李玄霸在聪慧之外，还多了友悌的名声。

当李渊到处找人喝酒，说自己升官也是托了李世民和李玄霸这一对孩子的功劳时，这友悌的名声升格成“孝悌”。

后世史书记载了这一幕。时人父对子，兄对弟，都言须学李家二郎三郎孝悌。

什么让梨卧病喂蚊子都弱爆了，看看李二郎和李三郎，他们立功，父兄升官，这才叫真正的孝悌啊。

“这不是太功利了吗？”长孙无忌来探望李世民和李玄霸的时候苦笑，“连我兄长都改变了态度，让我好好读书习武，将来给他赚个高官当当。颇不要脸！自己去啊！”

李世民：“阿嚏！”

李玄霸：“阿嚏！”

两个孩子蜷缩在被窝里，蔫哒哒地瞥着长孙无忌。

他们生病了，为何还要听别人抱怨？

李玄霸：【这长孙四郎真烦人！】

李世民不得不承认，此刻弟弟是对的。

长孙无忌抱怨了许久，手撑着下巴，小声道：“你们难道不生气吗？不感到不公平吗？”

李世民和李玄霸继续打喷嚏，不想说话。

长孙无忌叹了口气，自言自语：“好吧，你们就算感到不公平也不能说。嫡长嫡长，越不过去的高山。”

李世民：“阿嚏！”

李玄霸：“阿嚏！”

李玄霸：【这和嫡长有什么关系？只是因为我和哥你年纪小，现在不可能做官，所以惠及家人而已。】

李世民叹气，然后继续打喷嚏。

他这个朋友什么都好，就是太爱自怨自艾了点。

长孙无忌终于吐完黑泥，神清气爽地离开了。

李世民哑着嗓子道：“阿玄，等我们身体痊愈之前，闭门谢客吧。”

李玄霸：【早该这样了。父亲太爱炫耀了，非让我们接受别人探视。】

李世民：“我酝酿一下，对祖母哭一场，说探病的人吵得不行，更难受了。你努力努力，和我一起哭。祖母管得住耶耶。”

李玄霸点头。他觉得自己这次一定能哭出来。

两个小孩酝酿了一下，成功在独孤老夫人艰难地拄着拐杖来探望他们的时候，表演了一番兄弟抱头嚎啕大哭，告父亲的状。

独孤老夫人叹了口气，安抚好孙儿后，去找李渊抱怨了一番。

这确实是让唐国公府扬名的好时机，但不能本末倒置。两个孩子若休息不好，出了什么意外，就算留下了虚名又有什么用？

独孤老夫人特意去单独找了李建成，把李建成也骂了一顿。

李建成为了展现出自己的友悌和对这两个弟弟的教导，几乎每日都带不同的友人去探病。

“我知你心疼二郎三郎，但他们还小，更需要休息。”独孤老夫人虽骂了，但还是不忍心太过责备自己养大的孩子，便话锋一转道，“你若没得事做，二郎三郎正病着，香皂工坊的事交给三娘子这个外嫁妇还是不合适。你正好去练练手。”

李建成皱眉道：“祖母，不是我不想做事，但工匠和商贾之事，庶孽能做，我身为唐国公府嫡长，怎么能做此等下贱之事？先帝最厌恶商贾，当今陛下应当也是如此。我若插手，即使是为照顾幼弟，也会被人嘲笑。”

独孤老夫人道：“谁让你做了！你后院的郑娘子升了媵，可以做些庶务了。”

李建成这才道：“也是，就让郑媵去做。”

独孤老夫人满意地颔首。

独孤老夫人先和李建成说了此事后，才告诉窦夫人。

窦夫人脸色一变，手指头绞紧了衣摆，道：“香皂生意是两个孩子做的第一份事业。现在才刚做起色，就让给兄长的媵妾。外人得知，或许会怀疑大郎抢幼弟的产业。”

独孤老夫人不满道：“这怎么能叫抢？三郎已经将香皂生意交给了唐国公府，你宁愿让出嫁女管着，也不让大郎管着，这是何意？！难道大郎不在你身边长大，你就要苛待大郎吗！”

窦夫人立刻哭着跪下道：“儿妇不敢。儿妇这是为大郎着想啊。这公中的生意肯定是会交给大郎之妇，可一是郑娘子只是一个媵，哪能主持中馈？将来郑小娘子入门时，郑娘子已经在唐国公府当了多年女主人，郑小娘子要如何自处？”

独孤老夫人皱眉，神色有些犹豫。

窦夫人继续哭道：“再者，这京中谁都知道香皂是二郎三郎琢磨出来的。现在二郎三郎刚病，香皂生意还没有赚到钱，就被大郎的媵拿了。二郎三郎付出那么多心血，岂不是白费了？就算后来我们补偿回来，外人要如何说大郎？大郎肯定是不会不友悌的，他们一定会说郑娘子贪婪，撺掇大郎，这岂不是污了郑娘子的名声？”

窦夫人抹了抹眼泪，观察独孤老夫人的神色。

独孤老夫人气冲冲道：“我已经和大郎说了！”

窦夫人指甲抠紧手心，小心翼翼提议道：“郑娘子贤惠，肯定也是不愿意的。说来这些铜臭之事，大郎本就不该沾手。哪怕是家中妻妾，也该与官宦女眷交往。等二郎和三郎玩闹后，这些事儿妇也会交给奴仆，不会让二郎三郎继续插手。”

独孤老夫人叹了口气，道：“起来吧。”

窦夫人起身，擦干眼泪，垂着头静静等候独孤老夫人思索。

半晌，独孤老夫人叹气道：“二郎和三郎将来也肯定会入仕途，确实也不该过于插手商贾之事。大郎就更不能沾此事了。我本以为郑娘子只是个媵，名声坏了点就算了。但你说得有道理，或许他人会借此污蔑大郎。”

独孤老夫人反省。钱财动人心。虽然香皂现在还未贩卖，但看京中勋贵对香皂的热衷，可以预见这是多大一笔钱财，所以她立刻想到让大郎掌握这笔钱财。

二郎三郎还小，不该拿太多钱，会移了性子。他们应该静心念书，将来才能更好帮助大郎。

而且香皂本来就是唐国公府的生意，唐国公府的就是大郎的，现在不该做得太急躁。等公中赚了钱，让大郎随意取用就是了。

独孤老夫人道：“你去和郑娘子说说，让她拒绝。大郎那里……罢了，还是我去说吧。他本来也不喜商贾之事，我就不勉强他了。不过你要尽快把香皂之事收归公中，不可让外嫁女张罗。你让柴家怎么看我们？”

窦夫人恭敬道：“是，儿妇立刻去办。”

她提起的心终于放了下来。

窦夫人心中浮现李玄霸提起香皂生意未来计划时闪闪发光的表情。

三郎自幼体弱多病，吃尽苦头，导致过于早熟。她从未见过三郎如此开心的模样。

她理解婆婆见了什么好东西都想给大郎的心思。但二郎三郎才多小？兄长抢小九岁的幼弟的事业，旁人听了，可不是会嘲笑大郎？二郎三郎也会对大郎心生不满。

还好婆婆意识到了这是个昏招，没有坚持，唉。
chunks.englishText:
This was originally of little consequence. Yang Zhao had assumed the Duke of Tang’s mansion was merely using Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to curry favor with him, framing the matter as nothing more than children’s play. The Duke of Tang’s mansion remained close to the Crown Prince, simply wishing to avoid being entangled in the power struggles between the Emperor’s grandsons.

He had not expected that the "wager" between Li Shimin and Li Xuanba would actually compel his stubborn father to return to the capital, thereby pacifying the dissatisfaction among the nobility and the Guanzhong clans.

The two children certainly could not have foreseen this outcome. It was truly a coincidence.

But this was already the second such coincidence.

The first occurred when his father was returning from an imperial inspection of Jiangdu. He had originally intended to travel by land, insisting on commissioning new ceremonial carriages and wasting immense manpower and resources. All the ministers had advised against it, but his father would not listen.

However, at that moment, Li Xuanba fell gravely ill. The Empress and the eldest princess used this as a pretext to persuade him, noting that many veteran ministers were also suffering from the change in climate and water. If they encountered an accident or died of illness while traveling by land, the inaugural imperial inspection would be considered ill-omened. Only then did his father change his mind, and the criticism at court subsided.

"Could these two children be auspicious omens sent by the Heavens to our Great Sui?" Yang Zhao mused.

The more Yang Zhao thought about it, the more convinced he became. It seemed he would have to invest more effort into the Duke of Tang’s mansion.

Yang Zhao acted as soon as he thought of it.

As it happened, he heard that Li Jiancheng had taken a new bride from the Zheng family, but was struggling because his official rank was not high enough to legally maintain concubines.

Thus, after visiting Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Yang Zhao informed Li Yuan and Li Jiancheng of his intentions and petitioned the Emperor to raise Li Jiancheng’s honorary official rank to exactly the fifth grade.

In the Great Sui, official positions were divided into honorary titles and functional posts. Honorary titles were prestigious ranks that provided a salary without requiring actual administrative duties; they determined one’s seating order during court assemblies. Functional posts were those that carried real power.

Following the Northern Zhou’s administrative reforms, the Xianbei nobility and the Guanzhong clans had been blended together to form the powerful Guanlong aristocratic clique, established to counterbalance the Hedong clans that supported the Northern Qi and the Jiangnan clans that supported the Southern Dynasties.

To win over the Guanlong aristocracy, members of these clans were granted honorary titles directly through the "shadow privilege" system. Only functional posts required merit-based examinations. This ensured that the descendants of the Guanlong aristocratic families could always hold office.

After the Sui Dynasty was established, the "Shandong Commandery clans" of the Hedong region and the "Jiangnan émigré clans" were also incorporated into this system of hereditary privilege.

Therefore, as the legitimate eldest son of the Duke of Tang’s mansion, even though Li Jiancheng was still young and could not be granted a functional post, his honorary rank could certainly be elevated with the Crown Prince’s personal recommendation.

After Yang Guang returned to Daxing, he readily approved Li Jiancheng’s promotion. In the imperial decree, he specifically stated that this was to reward Li Shimin and Li Xuanba; however, because both children were still young and Li Yuan had just received a promotion himself, the reward was bestowed upon Li Jiancheng instead.

Once the decree was issued, the reputation of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba as child prodigies once again resounded throughout the capital, spreading across the empire along with the letters sent by envious officials in the capital to their families.

Beyond their intelligence, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba gained a reputation for brotherly affection.

When Li Yuan began seeking out people to drink with, boasting that his own promotion was thanks to the merit of his two sons, this reputation for brotherly affection was elevated to "filial piety and fraternal duty."

Later historical records documented this scene. People of that era, when speaking of fathers and sons or brothers, would all say that one must emulate the filial piety and fraternal duty of the Li family’s second and third sons.

Stories like "sharing the pears" or "lying in the bed to feed mosquitoes" were nothing compared to this. Look at the second and third Li sons—they performed meritorious deeds, and their father and elder brother were promoted. That was true filial piety and fraternal duty.

"Isn't this too utilitarian?" Zhangsun Wuji said with a wry smile when he came to visit Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. "Even my elder brother has changed his attitude, telling me to study hard and practice martial arts so I can earn him a high official position in the future. How shameless! Let him go do it himself!"

Li Shimin: "Achoo!"

Li Xuanba: "Achoo!"

The two children huddled under their quilts, looking listlessly at Zhangsun Wuji.

They were sick—why did they have to listen to someone else’s complaints?

Li Xuanba: *[This Zhangsun Wuji is so annoying!]*

Li Shimin had to admit that his younger brother was right.

Zhangsun Wuji complained for a long time, then rested his chin on his hand and whispered, "Aren't you two angry? Don't you feel it's unfair?"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba continued to sneeze, not wanting to speak.

Zhangsun Wuji sighed and muttered to himself, "Fine, even if you feel it's unfair, you can't say it. The legitimate eldest, the legitimate eldest—a mountain that cannot be crossed."

Li Shimin: "Achoo!"

Li Xuanba: "Achoo!"

Li Xuanba: *[What does this have to do with the legitimate eldest? It’s just because Brother and I are young and can't hold office yet, so the benefits go to the family.]*

Li Shimin sighed, then continued to sneeze.

His friend was fine in every other way, but he was just a bit too prone to self-pity.

Zhangsun Wuji finally finished venting his grievances and left, feeling refreshed.

Li Shimin said in a raspy voice, "Ah Xuan, until we recover, let’s close our doors to visitors."

Li Xuanba: *[We should have done that long ago. Father loves to show off too much; he insists on letting others visit us.]*

Li Shimin: "I’ll prepare myself to cry to Grandmother, saying that the visitors are too noisy and making me feel worse. You try your best to cry along with me. Grandmother can keep Father in check."

Li Xuanba nodded. He felt that this time, he would definitely be able to cry.

The two children prepared themselves, and when the elderly Lady Dugu struggled to visit them with her cane, they successfully performed a scene of brothers hugging each other and wailing, lodging a complaint against their father.

Lady Dugu sighed. After comforting her grandsons, she went to complain to Li Yuan.

It was indeed a good time to make the Duke of Tang’s mansion famous, but one could not lose sight of priorities. If the two children did not rest well and something happened to them, what was the use of a hollow reputation?

Lady Dugu specifically sought out Li Jiancheng alone and scolded him as well.

To demonstrate his brotherly affection and his guidance toward his two younger brothers, Li Jiancheng had been bringing different friends to visit them almost every day.

"I know you care for the second and third sons, but they are still young and need rest more than anything," Lady Dugu said. Though she scolded him, she could not bear to be too harsh on the child she had raised, so she changed the subject. "If you have nothing to do, since the second and third sons are ill, it is inappropriate for the third daughter—a married woman—to handle the soap workshop. You should take this opportunity to practice managing it."

Li Jiancheng frowned. "Grandmother, it’s not that I don’t want to do things, but matters of artisans and merchants are for the lowly. As the legitimate eldest son of the Duke of Tang’s mansion, how can I engage in such base work? The late Emperor despised merchants, and the current Emperor is surely the same. If I intervene, even if it is to look after my younger brothers, I will be mocked."

Lady Dugu said, "Who told you to do it yourself! Your concubine, Lady Zheng, has been promoted; she can handle some of the minor affairs."

Only then did Li Jiancheng say, "That is true. I shall let Lady Zheng handle it."

Lady Dugu nodded in satisfaction.

Lady Dugu spoke to Li Jiancheng about this first before telling Lady Dou.

Lady Dou’s expression changed. She twisted her fingers into her skirt and said, "The soap business is the first venture the two children have created. Now that it is just beginning to show promise, to hand it over to the eldest brother’s concubine... if outsiders find out, they might suspect that the eldest brother is seizing his younger brothers' industry."

Lady Dugu said with dissatisfaction, "How can you call this seizing? The third son has already handed the soap business over to the Duke of Tang’s mansion. You would rather let a married daughter manage it than let the eldest son manage it—what is the meaning of this?! Do you intend to mistreat the eldest son just because he did not grow up by your side?"

Lady Dou immediately knelt down, weeping, "Your daughter-in-law would not dare. I am doing this for the sake of the eldest son. The family business will certainly be handed over to the eldest son’s wife, but Lady Zheng is only a concubine—how can she preside over the household? When the future Lady Zheng enters the family, Lady Zheng will have already been the mistress of the Duke of Tang’s mansion for years. How will the new Lady Zheng find her place?"

Lady Dugu frowned, her expression hesitant.

Lady Dou continued to weep, "Furthermore, everyone in the capital knows that the soap was devised by the second and third sons. Now that they are ill and the business has yet to turn a profit, it is taken by the eldest brother’s concubine. If the second and third sons have put in so much effort, wouldn't it all be in vain? Even if we compensate them later, what will outsiders say about the eldest son? The eldest son is certainly not lacking in brotherly affection, but they will surely say that Lady Zheng is greedy and instigated him. Wouldn't that tarnish Lady Zheng’s reputation?"

Lady Dou wiped her tears, observing Lady Dugu’s expression.

Lady Dugu said indignantly, "I have already told the eldest son!"

Lady Dou dug her nails into her palms and cautiously suggested, "Lady Zheng is virtuous and would surely be unwilling as well. Besides, the eldest son should not be touching such base matters of profit. Even the wives and concubines of the household should be interacting with the wives of other officials. Once the second and third sons are done playing, I will hand these matters over to the servants; I will not let the second and third sons continue to interfere."

Lady Dugu sighed and said, "Get up."

Lady Dou rose, wiped her tears, and stood with her head bowed, quietly waiting for Lady Dugu to reflect.

After a long while, Lady Dugu sighed. "The second and third sons will certainly enter the official path in the future; they truly should not be overly involved in merchant affairs. The eldest son should be even less involved. I had thought that since Lady Zheng is only a concubine, it wouldn't matter if her reputation suffered a little. But you have a point; perhaps others would use this to slander the eldest son."

Lady Dugu reflected. Money could move people’s hearts. Although the soap had not yet been sold, seeing the enthusiasm of the capital’s nobility for it, she could foresee what a massive fortune it would be, which was why she had immediately thought of letting the eldest son control it.

The second and third sons were still young; they shouldn't have too much money, or it might corrupt their character. They should focus on their studies so they could better assist the eldest son in the future.

Moreover, the soap business was originally the Duke of Tang’s business, and what belonged to the Duke of Tang’s mansion belonged to the eldest son; there was no need to be so impatient. Once the family earned money, the eldest son could take what he needed.

Lady Dugu said, "Go and tell Lady Zheng to decline. As for the eldest son... never mind, I will tell him myself. He never liked merchant affairs anyway, so I will not force him. However, you must bring the soap business under the family’s direct control as soon as possible; do not let a married daughter manage it. How would that make the Chai family look at us?"

Lady Dou replied respectfully, "Yes, your daughter-in-law will attend to it immediately."

The anxiety in her heart finally dissipated.

In Lady Dou’s mind, the image of Li Xuanba’s face lighting up when he spoke about the future plans for the soap business appeared.

The third son had been weak and sickly since childhood, suffering greatly, which had led him to be overly precocious. She had never seen the third son look so happy.

She understood her mother-in-law’s desire to give everything good to the eldest son. But how young were the second and third sons? If an elder brother seized the business of a younger brother nine years his junior, wouldn't others mock him? The second and third sons would also grow resentful of their elder brother.

Fortunately, her mother-in-law realized this was a foolish move and did not insist. *Sigh.*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第34章 你方唱罢我登场 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第34章 你方唱罢我登场

=

“咳咳， 帮我谢谢张阿婆。”李玄霸对乳娘道，“以我和二哥身体变好为理由，给祖母和母亲身边仆从都送些钱去， 感谢她们照顾我和二哥。年纪大的阿公阿婆， 额外再送份药材。”

乳娘立刻会意， 道：“张婆的腿有些酸疼，奴会帮张婆好好挑选药材。”

李玄霸道：“送药材的时候嘱咐张阿婆，请她保重自己， 不要因为我惹了祖母生气。”

乳娘道：“奴知晓。”

李玄霸的乳娘离开后不久，李世民的乳娘也来了。

虽然是李世民的乳娘，但李世民不耐烦琐碎事， 所以李世民的仆从也是李玄霸在管。

李世民的乳娘说的也是和李玄霸的乳娘所禀报的相同的事，只是一个从独孤老夫人这边的视角， 一个从窦夫人这边的视角。

“母亲应该会很快亲自来和我说。”李玄霸叹了口气， 又咳了几声，道，“辛苦了，去领赏吧。”

李世民的乳娘欢天喜地地谢了三郎君的赏钱。

李玄霸吃了一颗酸梅，压下咳嗽的冲动， 闭目思索。

半晌，李玄霸闭着眼道：“大力。”

一个憨厚的仆从道：“仆在。”

李玄霸睁开眼道：“你帮你那相好的砍柴的时候， 向你相好透露几句，老夫人有意让她家娘子背上贪财的名声。”

大力道：“是，三郎君。”

李玄霸道：“去支取三尺绸子， 送给你相好。”

大力笑道：“谢三郎君！”

李玄霸道：“做完这件事后， 你就去找柴姊婿， 把信交给柴姊婿。”

李玄霸将早就写好的信从袖口拿出来， 递给大力。

大力离开后，李玄霸捏了捏嗓子，用草纸掩着嘴咳了许久。

李世民踹开门进来，手中端着一盅炖梨：“阿玄，快吃炖梨，吃完炖梨就不咳了。”

生同样的病，李世民能从床上爬起来之后身体迅速痊愈，李玄霸却落下了咳嗽的后遗症，不知道还要养多久。

李玄霸强忍着咳嗽的冲动吃完炖梨，喉咙好受了一些。

李世民帮弟弟掖了掖被角：“我向老师请了假，老师说你的功课可以不用做了。”

李玄霸：【还是做吧，我躺着也无聊。】

李世民狡黠地笑道：“我知道你会做功课，才和老师请假啊。你请了假还交了功课，老师肯定很高兴。”

李玄霸：【也对。希望老师高兴之后少给我们布置些功课。】

李世民使劲点头。

李世民和李玄霸说了一些外面的趣事。他身体好之后，就立刻跟着李渊满大兴城串门，与同龄的朋友一起玩耍，就像是被憋狠了的小猴儿。

“他们都很遗憾只有我一人去做客，都说想看唐国公府的双生子。”李世民拍了拍弟弟的被子，“你要赶快好啊。”

李玄霸点头。

李世民笑了笑，然后叹了口气，笑容消失：“我看院里仆人忙忙碌碌，愁眉不展，是不是家里有什么麻烦事？你怎么不告诉我？”

李玄霸：【你不是老捂着耳朵说不想听麻烦事吗？】

李世民道：“已经发生的麻烦事和未发生的麻烦事完全不同！已经发生的事我当然要知道，不然怎么解决？还是说你瞧不起哥哥，认为没有哥哥也一样？”

李玄霸：【当然不是，我早就准备好了事等着你自投罗网。】

李世民假装生气道：“好啊你个大德，居然套路哥哥！”

他扯了一下李玄霸的小揪揪，在李玄霸告饶后，大度道：“说吧，有什么让哥哥做的？”

李玄霸：【去找太子兑现赌约。虽然皇帝还没有正式下诏，但我想香皂成为贡品的事已经是定局。】

李世民疑惑：“就这？写封信不就行了，还需要我亲自去？”

李玄霸：【太子承诺，若我赢了，就让皇后参与香皂制作和贩卖。】

李世民挠了挠头，然后露出恍然大悟的表情。

他眉头紧锁，苦笑道：“惹谁眼红了？”

李玄霸不说话。

李世民伸手把李玄霸的脸颊扯住：“快说！你哥哥我承受得住！”

李玄霸：【还能是谁？祖母偏疼兄长，你又不是不知道。不过祖母暂时改变了主意，不用担心。我只是以防万一。】

李玄霸没和二哥说这是母亲跪着向祖母求来的。

若说了，自己这个暴脾气二哥不知道会闹成什么模样。

李世民松开手，使劲揉搓自己的脸：“啊啊啊啊啊好烦好烦，商贾之事不是小道吗？你选这件事就是以为不会有人伸手，怎么还伸手？”

李玄霸：【可能是此事能讨好皇帝的缘故吧。】

李世民冷哼：“我可不信陛下得知此事后还会被讨好。”

李玄霸在嘴前竖起手指：【慎言。】

李世民气得在屋里跳了几下发泄了一番，待跳累了之后，才爬回榻上：“继续说，我要怎么做！”

李玄霸把自己早就计划好的事告知二哥。

他在思考要如何赚钱的时候，就已经做好了如果有人抢夺胜利成果的应对计划。

李玄霸前世被人抢过一次胜利成果，还差点被人雇的流氓打残废。吃一堑长一智，他早就准备好了。

虽然李世民年幼，但也听懂了李玄霸的分析。

他抱着昏涨的脑袋倒在床榻上慢吞吞来回翻滚：“脑子要裂开了，裂开了。简单来说，你用的是陛下赏赐的钱和地，还有阿姊的嫁妆，一个铜板都没让公中出钱？”

李玄霸点头。

李世民道：“但我们还是不能抛开唐国公府。我俩年纪太小，生意做大了，唐国公府肯定会参与。”

李玄霸：【而且就算是我们用赏赐作为本钱，但小孩子没有私产，包括府里给我们的两个铺子，都只是暂时给我们使用，我们投的那一份仍旧是唐国公府的财产。】

李世民不滚了。

他双手展开，在榻上躺成了一个大字：“那我们现在做的有用吗？”

李玄霸苍白的脸上浮现一个浅浅的笑容，用虚弱沙哑的声音道：“有用。他又不是唐国公。”

……

窦夫人看完李玄霸的账本后，心情很复杂。

李玄霸的账做得十分细致，细致到她都想把家中的账本翻新一遍，跟着李玄霸的学。

这一笔一笔细致的账目告诉她，李玄霸早就防着国公府将香皂工坊收走。

“居然把三郎逼成这样……”窦夫人捂着嘴低泣。

她真的受不了婆婆的偏心了。

婆婆说她偏心二郎三郎，究竟是谁偏心？唐国公府都是大郎的，二郎三郎什么都没有，只能自己打拼，何苦将孩子手中一点钱财都要搜刮走？难道大郎还缺这点钱吗？

窦夫人低泣完之后擦干眼泪，自言自语：“二郎，三郎，放心，娘不会让你们被欺负。”

她拿着账本去找李玄霸，询问李玄霸的计划。

看到这账本她就知道，过于聪慧早熟的三郎，绝对已经预料到如今的事，想好了应对。她只需要帮三郎完善这个应对。

李渊忙完公务回来时，听闻窦夫人病了。

他先派人去询问窦夫人的病情，然后去了万氏那里就寝。

李渊去万氏那里的时候没有通知其他人，只自己悄悄地过去，想给万氏惊喜。

回到家中，李渊常在窦夫人那里就寝，很久没来万氏这里了。

他屏退了下人，悄悄进屋。

万氏似乎没有发现李渊来了，没有提前盛装打扮，正披散着头发对镜梳理头发。

李渊正想提醒万氏他来了，却听见了万氏的呜咽。

他心中一叹，难道是万媵伤心自己冷落他？

李渊温柔道：“万娘子，我来看你了。”

万氏手中木梳落在了桌子上，她胡乱擦了擦眼泪，微笑着迎过来：“郎君怎么来了？”

李渊实话实说道：“夫人今日生病，我担心打扰她休息，就来你这里过一晚。怎么，不欢迎我？”

万氏温婉地笑道：“怎么会呢？”

李渊伸出手指，摩挲着万氏的眼角道：“那你为何抽泣？可是夫人对你不好？”

万氏赶紧摇头：“夫人有多贤惠大度，郎君还不知道吗？郎君若说夫人坏话，妾可要生气了。”

李渊微微一怔，哭笑不得道：“行，行，你和夫人感情最好，我才是多余的那个。”

他拉着万氏的手，与万氏坐在坐榻上：“那你为何难过？”

万氏犹豫。

李渊道：“怎么，这府中还有我解决不了的事？难道是母亲又训斥你了？”

万氏摇头：“妾不敢往老夫人面前凑，她训斥不到妾。”

李渊叹了口气，拍了拍万氏的手背道：“辛苦你了。”

万氏继续摇头：“我怎么能叫辛苦？回来之后，妾一直受夫人照顾，每日都很悠闲自在，还能逗着二小郎君三小郎君和小五玩，妾可开心了，比操心你的衣食住行开心多了。”

李渊装作震惊道：“你这是在嫌弃我？”

万氏掩嘴笑道：“就嫌弃你。”

李渊道：“既然如此开心，你为何忧虑？可是小五不亲你？”

万氏叹了口气：“郎君，你何必追问？既然妾没主动告诉你，就是不好告诉你啊。”

李渊坚持道：“我必须得听。连家中妻妾的烦恼都解决不了，我还是个男人吗？快说！”

万氏再次露出犹豫的神情。

仿佛经过了一段时间的心理挣扎，万氏小声道：“妾说。只是一些任性的话，郎君不要和其他人说，不然传出去，又该被人说妾家教不好了。”

李渊点头：“就我知道。”

万氏叹了口气，眼眶又红了。

她捏着帕子擦了擦眼角，道：“今日一大早，老夫人就把夫人叫去，让夫人把二郎和三郎的铺子收回来，给大郎的媵拿着。夫人跪着请求了许久，老夫人才准许只把生意收入公中，让大郎的媵能任意支取钱财。”

李渊惊讶；“这、这是为何？”

万氏苦笑：“香皂生意入了陛下的眼，又得全京城的权贵喜爱，将来钱财名声都不会少。大郎既然为嫡长，好处自然是大郎拿着。妾知道，妾知道应该如此，但还是……”

万氏用手绢捂着脸道：“这唐国公府所有的都是大郎的，爵位人脉资产全是大郎的，妾知道。可是看着二郎三郎卖力做成的第一笔事业，哪怕只是商贾之事这点别人看不上的事业，也是付出了心血。”

万氏呜呜呜哭了一会儿，又道：“二郎三郎其实应该是不在乎的。他们如此聪慧，小小年纪就在陛下那里扬名。这些东西被收走了就收走了，待他们长大，肯定能自己建功立业。我只是想到了我的小五，我的小五笨笨的，将来可能也就只能拿一些金白俗物傍身……”

“郎君，是妾任性了。”她擦了擦眼泪，哽咽着勉强挤出笑容，“其实二郎三郎从古书里琢磨出古方时，就带着小五来找妾，让小五也出了一份钱，说叫‘入股’。郎君就当是妾贪心了，伤心投入的钱没了吧。郎君可要把妾的本钱补给妾啊。”

李渊面沉如水。

他深呼吸了几下，道：“你说的可是真的？夫人还跪着求母亲？”

万氏苦笑：“郎君，早晨夫人送你出门的时候还好好的呢。”

李渊起身道：“我去看夫人。万娘子，别担心，我唐国公府还没落魄到只能供养一人成才的地步。”

万氏起身拉住李渊的衣角，慌张道：“郎君，你可答应妾了，不把妾的话告诉别人。你若这样，妾以后怎敢再向你诉苦？”

李渊轻轻拢了拢万氏的肩膀，道：“放心，我不会告诉别人。别难过了，这件事我能解决。”

万氏松开手，满脸眷慕道：“好，妾相信郎君。”

李渊离开，万氏站在门口目送李渊，久久不肯离去。

这一幕被人看在眼里，不断感慨万媵真是对唐国公一往情深。

待倚着门站了半刻钟后，万氏回到屋内，让人打来水卸妆。

既要素雅，又要好看，哭了还不能花妆，这脸上的妆画得可不容易。

万氏洗完脸后，愤愤将擦脸的帕子丢到一旁。

女婢道：“娘子别气了，国公既然说能解决，就肯定能解决。”

万氏冷哼道：“他现在倒是硬气，等见着老夫人就不一定了。他在人后硬气，见了老夫人就唯唯诺诺的时候还少吗？”

女婢道：“这次不一样。二郎三郎和五郎都是国公的孩子，他还是会心疼孩子的。”

“哼。”万氏又冷哼了一声，然后真切落下泪来，“连同是夫人肚子里出来的二郎三郎尚且被如此磋磨，我家小五将来在李建成手下讨生活，还能落个好？”

“看看人家二郎三郎，自己手里都没什么东西，得了赏赐给四郎小五一份，铺子经营起来了也要分四郎小五一份。李建成顶多送东西给四郎，从来没有想过我的小五！”万氏又气又难过，不由掩面痛哭起来，“小五怎么摊上这样一个嫡长兄？”

女婢拍着万氏的肩膀，也很是难过。

她跟着娘子从江南来到京城，看着娘子从家中千娇百宠活泼伶俐的世家小娘子，一步一步被磋磨成了谨言慎行的模样，现在又在为五郎君未来忧愁，她怎么能不难过？

她难过也没用，只能轻声安慰自家娘子：“娘子别难过，长兄靠不住，还有二郎君和三郎君。如国公所说，唐国公又不是只能供一人成才。勋贵人家中一门几个国公郡公多常见？以陛下对二郎君和三郎君的宠爱，二郎君和三郎君迟早会封爵。他们一定会帮助五郎君也出人头地。”

万氏头倚在陪嫁女婢的肩膀上，闭着眼睛一边流泪一边点头。

李渊离开万氏的小院时，派去看望窦夫人的仆从刚好回来。

仆从答道：“夫人说没事，只是今日在庭院里吹了些风，头有些疼，于是早早睡了。”

李渊双手握拳：“夫人也不相信我吗？”

仆从心里疑惑，道：“夫人看着气色不错，应当真的是无事。”

李渊挥了挥手，让仆从离开，大步迈向窦夫人居住的院落。

他进门时，窦夫人卧室的蜡烛已经灭掉。

李渊摸着黑走到窦夫人床榻边，坐到窦夫人身边沉默不语。

窦夫人最先开口：“郎君为何不声不响坐在黑暗中？是吓唬我吗？”

李渊道：“我知道你没睡，也知道你能听出我的脚步声。”

窦夫人道：“我只是有些头疼，休息一日就好了。郎君不用担心。”

李渊道：“你是担心我和母亲起冲突吗？”

良久之后，黑暗中才传出幽幽一叹。

窦夫人道：“郎君，帮我把蜡烛点上。”

李渊起身点燃蜡烛。

窦夫人坐了起来。

李渊回到榻边，帮窦夫人披上衣服：“小心着凉。”

他看着窦夫人的眼角，果然也是红的，泪痕都还未干。

窦夫人道：“郎君是国公，国公府的主人，国公府的事自然瞒不过郎君，是我多想了，唉。”

李渊挤出笑容，道：“是，瞒不住我。”

窦夫人道：“观朝中显贵，若是家中长辈出色，子嗣常常多人封爵；若是子嗣自己出色，该封爵时，陛下也不会看他族中是否已经有人封爵。二郎三郎出色，特别是二郎，去边疆立个功劳应是容易的。我一直想，李家的李安、李哲能一门双郡公，我家二郎三郎应该也是能的。”

窦夫人所说的李安、李哲是李渊七叔的儿子，李渊已经去世的堂兄。

李渊道：“不止李安和李哲，我几位叔父也都是高官，唉，哪怕是四叔李毕。”

李渊的大伯和二伯皆早逝，所以是李渊的父亲李昞继承了唐国公的爵位。其余没有继承权的叔叔，皆在当时的北周身居高位，封爵者也不少。

所以哪怕李渊的四叔李毕起兵想要诛杀北周权臣杨坚，失败身死，杨坚建立隋朝后，仍旧重用李家人。

特别是当时站在李毕对立面的李安、李哲颇受杨坚信赖看重，共同掌管京中禁军，一门双郡公。

国公多是开国时就有的，和平年代很难再封国公。但目标指向郡公，李渊也觉得以自家二郎三郎如今的本事，不算好高骛远。

窦夫人道：“虽说为了家族好，大郎能继承国公，国公府的资源应该倾向二郎三郎，再为唐国公一脉增加两位郡公，才是最优的选择。但家人之间岂能如此功利？兄弟间相互扶持就行了。如之前，二郎三郎在外得了名声，大郎自然而然就享受到了好处，根本不需要让兄弟之间相互争夺什么。”

李渊叹气，难得听进去了夫人谈论朝堂之事：“是啊。”

窦夫人道：“人心都是肉长的，若偏向一个，打压另一个，兄弟之间岂有不离心的？才高之人心气肯定也高，二郎三郎连郎君你都不服气。”

李渊这口气叹不下去了。

他扶额，咬牙切齿道：“这两个崽子确实是谁也不服，连对着太子殿下都不够尊重，陛下常常笑话他们。”

窦夫人苦笑：“才华横溢者都是如此。郎君你不也只要说起射箭，就谁也不服？连长孙将军胜过你一次，不还被你拉着赢了回来。”

李渊略有些得意：“这倒是，他二人像我。”

窦夫人道：“商贾本来就是小事。从未听过哪个勋贵以商贾持家，都是吃租子。二郎三郎也是年纪小，才拿给他们胡闹。他们做香皂的时候，都没想过自己赚钱，全用的阿姊们的嫁妆，还问我和万娘子要了嫁妆压箱底的钱，说赚钱了就给我们这群女眷拿着玩。”

李渊深吸一口气：“嫁妆？！”

窦夫人苦笑：“是啊。他们还说，若是真的能赚很多钱，就把没出嫁的姊妹也拉进去。他们能建功立业，将来家产肯定是陛下赏赐。不说食邑，就是多给他们几个好庄子收租，不也比商贾这末流小道强？这做生意之事，本就是女儿家攒些零花钱而已。”

窦夫人拍了拍李渊的手臂，叹着气道：“大家曾经独力支撑唐国公府，郎君那时还小，朝堂上的人脉只能靠钱财拉拢，所以大家才重视钱财。但现在已经不一样了，大郎有郎君这个父亲在，哪还需要用钱财讨好人？他等着别人讨好他就行。我们唐国公府啊，是靠郎君你才变得如此显赫啊。”

李渊捏了捏眉间，道：“母亲或许真的是穷怕了。当时我还没有多少俸禄，逢年过节准备礼物时，母亲就暗自发愁，嫁妆都不知道典当出去多少，还常常进宫向文献皇后借钱，遭了不少白眼。但现在确实是不同了，我还没死呢！李建成又不是孤儿！”

窦夫人失笑：“本来郎君你这么说，我该劝你慎言。但理确实是这个理。郎君你还春秋鼎盛，青云仕途才走没几步，将来前程还大着。等郎君你致仕时，说不定连最年幼的小五都当祖父了。唉，大郎应该想着自己赚个爵位，他当唐国公还早着呢。”

李渊道：“夫人的话极有道理，怎么不和母亲说？”

窦夫人叹气道：“你看我敢说吗？我稍稍一教训大郎，大家立刻说我偏心！所以我才头疼啊。”

李渊讪讪道：“母亲确实过于偏爱大郎。大郎是她亲手养大，她偏爱些也正常。”

窦夫人再次叹气：“是啊。只是大郎将来要肩负唐国公府的重担，太娇纵怎么能行？郎君的祖父和父亲都是在战场上拼杀过的，郎君将来的目标肯定也是拜大将军。打仗可苦了。”

李渊安慰窦夫人道：“夫人不必担心，大郎虽然被母亲偏爱了些，但他弓马娴熟，打猎的本事相当不错。”

窦夫人心道，打猎和打仗能一样吗？但她还是点头道：“郎君这么说，我就放心了。郎君，先安寝吧，这些烦心事，明日再说。唉，要不郎君去万娘子那里？我头还疼。”

李渊道：“不，我就睡这里，我又不吵你，你睡你的。”
