Chapter 34: One After Another, the Players Take the Stage

“Cough, cough. Please thank Granny Zhang for me,” Li Xuanba said to his wet nurse. “Use the excuse that my Second Brother and I are recovering to send some money to the servants serving Grandmother and Mother. Thank them for taking care of us. For the older ones, the grandpas and grandmas, send an extra portion of medicinal herbs.”

The wet nurse understood immediately. “Granny Zhang’s legs have been aching. I will personally select some good herbs for her.”

Li Xuanba said, “When you deliver the herbs, tell Granny Zhang to take care of herself and not to worry about me having angered Grandmother.”

“This servant understands,” the wet nurse replied.

Not long after Li Xuanba’s wet nurse left, Li Shimin’s wet nurse arrived.

Although she was Li Shimin’s wet nurse, Li Shimin had no patience for trivial matters, so his servants were also managed by Li Xuanba.

The report from Li Shimin’s wet nurse was identical to the one from Li Xuanba’s, just viewed from the perspective of Lady Dugu’s household instead of Lady Dou’s.

“Mother will likely come to speak with me personally soon,” Li Xuanba sighed, coughing a few more times. “You’ve worked hard. Go collect your reward.”

Li Shimin’s wet nurse left, overjoyed with the reward money from the Third Young Master.

Li Xuanba ate a preserved plum to suppress the urge to cough, then closed his eyes to think.

After a long while, he spoke with his eyes still shut: “Dali.”

A simple-minded servant replied, “This servant is here.”

Li Xuanba opened his eyes. “When you go to chop firewood for your sweetheart, drop a hint to her that the Old Madam intends to saddle her mistress with a reputation for being greedy for money.”

“Yes, Third Young Master,” Dali said.

“Go and draw three feet of silk to give to your sweetheart,” Li Xuanba added.

Dali grinned. “Thank you, Third Young Master!”

“After you finish that, go find Brother-in-law Chai and deliver this letter to him.” Li Xuanba pulled a pre-written letter from his sleeve and handed it to Dali.

Once Dali left, Li Xuanba massaged his throat and coughed for a long time into a piece of paper.

Li Shimin kicked the door open and walked in, carrying a bowl of stewed pears. “Ah Xuan, eat this quickly. You’ll stop coughing once you’re done.”

Though they had fallen ill with the same sickness, Li Shimin had recovered rapidly once he was able to get out of bed, while Li Xuanba had been left with a lingering cough that seemed as though it would take ages to heal.

Li Xuanba forced himself to finish the stewed pears, suppressing the urge to cough, and his throat felt slightly better.

Li Shimin tucked the quilt around his younger brother. “I asked for leave from our teacher, and he said you don’t need to finish your schoolwork.”

Li Xuanba: *[I should do it anyway. I’m bored just lying here.]*

Li Shimin smiled slyly. “I knew you’d do it, that’s why I asked for leave. If you finish your work even while on leave, the teacher will definitely be pleased.”

Li Xuanba: *[True. I just hope that once he’s pleased, he’ll assign us less work.]*

Li Shimin nodded vigorously.

Li Shimin shared some interesting news from outside. Once his health improved, he had immediately followed Li Yuan around Daxing City, visiting friends and playing with peers like a little monkey that had been cooped up for too long.

“They were all so disappointed that I was the only one visiting. They all said they wanted to see the twins of the Tang State Duke’s mansion,” Li Shimin said, patting his brother’s quilt. “You need to get better soon.”

Li Xuanba nodded.

Li Shimin smiled, then sighed, his smile vanishing. “I see the servants in the courtyard bustling about, looking so troubled. Is there some trouble at home? Why didn’t you tell me?”

Li Xuanba: *[Didn’t you always cover your ears and say you didn’t want to hear about trouble?]*

Li Shimin said, “Trouble that has already happened is completely different from trouble that hasn’t! Of course I need to know about things that have already happened; how else can I solve them? Or do you look down on your brother, thinking you can handle things just as well without me?”

Li Xuanba: *[Of course not. I’ve already prepared the trap waiting for you to walk into it.]*

Li Shimin pretended to be angry. “Oh, you little rascal, you’re actually playing tricks on your brother!”

He tugged at Li Xuanba’s little topknot, and after Li Xuanba begged for mercy, he said magnanimously, “Speak, what do you need your brother to do?”

Li Xuanba: *[Go to the Crown Prince and have him honor our bet. Although the Emperor hasn’t issued an official decree yet, I believe the soap becoming a tribute item is a foregone conclusion.]*

Li Shimin was puzzled. “Just that? Can’t you just write a letter? Do I need to go personally?”

Li Xuanba: *[The Crown Prince promised that if I won, he would allow the Empress to participate in the production and sale of the soap.]*

Li Shimin scratched his head, then his expression shifted to one of sudden realization.

His brows furrowed, and he gave a wry smile. “Whose eyes have we made jealous?”

Li Xuanba remained silent.

Li Shimin reached out and pinched Li Xuanba’s cheeks. “Speak! Your brother can handle it!”

Li Xuanba: *[Who else could it be? You know Grandmother favors our elder brother. But she has temporarily changed her mind, so don’t worry. I’m just taking precautions.]*

Li Xuanba didn’t tell his Second Brother that this was something their mother had obtained by kneeling before their grandmother.

If he told him, he didn’t know what kind of scene his hot-tempered brother would cause.

Li Shimin let go and rubbed his own face vigorously. “Argh, so annoying! Isn’t business supposed to be a lowly pursuit? You chose this because you thought no one would interfere, so why are they reaching out now?”

Li Xuanba: *[Perhaps it’s because this matter can curry favor with the Emperor.]*

Li Shimin snorted. “I don’t believe the Emperor would be pleased once he finds out about this.”

Li Xuanba held a finger to his lips. *[Be careful with your words.]*

Li Shimin jumped around the room a few times to vent his frustration, and once he was tired, he climbed back onto the couch. “Continue, what do I need to do!”

Li Xuanba told his brother the plan he had long since devised.

When he was thinking about how to make money, he had already prepared a contingency plan in case someone tried to snatch the fruits of his labor.

In his past life, Li Xuanba had had his success stolen once, and he had nearly been crippled by thugs hired by his rivals. Once bitten, twice shy; he had been prepared for a long time.

Although Li Shimin was young, he understood Li Xuanba’s analysis.

He clutched his throbbing head and rolled back and forth on the couch. “My brain is going to split open, it’s splitting. Simply put, you used the money and land rewarded by the Emperor, plus Sister’s dowry, and didn’t let the public estate spend a single copper?”

Li Xuanba nodded.

Li Shimin said, “But we still can’t cut ties with the Tang State Duke’s mansion. We are too young; if the business grows too large, the mansion will definitely get involved.”

Li Xuanba: *[And even if we use the rewards as capital, children have no private property. Including the two shops the mansion gave us, they are only for our temporary use. The portion we invested is still the property of the Tang State Duke’s mansion.]*

Li Shimin stopped rolling.

He spread his arms and lay flat on the couch like a starfish. “Then is what we’re doing now even useful?”

A faint smile appeared on Li Xuanba’s pale face, and he said in a weak, hoarse voice, “It is useful. He is not the Tang State Duke.”

……

After Lady Dou finished reading Li Xuanba’s account book, her mood was complex.

Li Xuanba’s bookkeeping was so meticulous that she wanted to redo the mansion’s own ledgers and learn from him.

These detailed entries told her that Li Xuanba had long been guarding against the mansion seizing the soap workshop.

“To think they would push the Third Son to this point…” Lady Dou covered her mouth and sobbed.

She truly could not stand her mother-in-law’s favoritism anymore.

Her mother-in-law claimed she was biased toward the Second and Third sons, but who was the one truly being biased? The Tang State Duke’s mansion belonged to the Eldest Son; the Second and Third sons had nothing and had to fend for themselves. Why must they scrape away the little money the children had? Was the Eldest Son really lacking that bit of money?

After she finished sobbing, Lady Dou wiped her tears and muttered to herself, “Second Son, Third Son, don’t worry. Mother won’t let you be bullied.”

She took the account book and went to find Li Xuanba to ask about his plans.

Seeing this ledger, she knew that the overly intelligent and precocious Third Son must have already anticipated the current situation and thought of a response. She only needed to help him perfect it.

When Li Yuan returned from his official duties, he heard that Lady Dou was ill.

He first sent someone to inquire about her condition, then went to spend the night with Lady Wan.

Li Yuan didn’t notify anyone when he went to Lady Wan’s, wanting to surprise her.

Since returning home, Li Yuan had usually slept in Lady Dou’s quarters and hadn’t visited Lady Wan in a long time.

He dismissed the servants and slipped into the room quietly.

Lady Wan didn’t seem to notice he had arrived; she wasn’t dressed up, and was simply combing her hair in front of the mirror with it draped over her shoulders.

Li Yuan was about to announce his presence when he heard Lady Wan sobbing.

He sighed inwardly. Was Lady Wan sad because he had been neglecting her?

Li Yuan said gently, “Lady Wan, I’ve come to see you.”

The wooden comb in Lady Wan’s hand fell to the table. She wiped her tears hastily and turned to greet him with a smile. “Why has the Master come?”

Li Yuan said truthfully, “My wife is ill today. I was worried about disturbing her rest, so I came to spend the night here. What, are you not happy to see me?”

Lady Wan smiled gently. “How could that be?”

Li Yuan reached out and stroked the corner of Lady Wan’s eye. “Then why were you sobbing? Has my wife been treating you poorly?”

Lady Wan shook her head quickly. “Doesn’t the Master know how virtuous and magnanimous the Lady is? If you speak ill of her, I shall be angry.”

Li Yuan was slightly taken aback, then laughed helplessly. “Fine, fine. You and the Lady are the closest; I’m the one who is redundant.”

He took Lady Wan’s hand and sat with her on the couch. “Then why are you sad?”

Lady Wan hesitated.

Li Yuan said, “What, is there something in this mansion I cannot solve? Has Mother scolded you again?”

Lady Wan shook her head. “I dare not approach the Old Madam; she has no reason to scold me.”

Li Yuan sighed and patted the back of her hand. “You’ve worked hard.”

Lady Wan shook her head again. “How can I call it hard work? Since returning, I have been well-cared for by the Lady. Every day is leisurely and comfortable, and I can play with the Second, Third, and Fifth Young Masters. I am very happy—happier than worrying about your food and clothing.”

Li Yuan feigned shock. “Are you looking down on me?”

Lady Wan covered her mouth and laughed. “Yes, I am.”

Li Yuan said, “Since you are so happy, why are you worried? Is it because the Fifth Son isn’t close to you?”

Lady Wan sighed. “Master, why must you press me? If I didn’t tell you voluntarily, it means it wasn’t easy to tell you.”

Li Yuan insisted, “I must hear it. If I can’t even solve the troubles of my own wives and concubines, am I still a man? Speak!”

Lady Wan showed a hesitant expression once more.

As if struggling internally for a moment, Lady Wan whispered, “I will tell you. But these are just some willful words; please don’t tell anyone else, or it will be said that I lack proper upbringing.”

Li Yuan nodded. “Only I shall know.”

Lady Wan sighed, her eyes reddening again.

She wiped the corners of her eyes with a handkerchief and said, “Early this morning, the Old Madam called the Lady over and demanded she take back the shops belonging to the Second and Third sons to give to the Eldest Son’s concubine. The Lady knelt and begged for a long time before the Old Madam finally allowed the profits to be turned over to the public estate, so that the Eldest Son’s concubine could draw money from them at will.”

Li Yuan was startled. “This… why?”

Lady Wan gave a bitter smile. “The soap business has caught the Emperor’s eye and is loved by all the powerful families in the capital. In the future, there will be no shortage of money or fame. Since the Eldest Son is the heir, the benefits should naturally go to him. I know, I know it should be this way, but still…”

Lady Wan covered her face with her handkerchief. “Everything in this Tang State Duke’s mansion belongs to the Eldest Son—the title, the connections, the assets. I know that. But watching the first business the Second and Third sons worked so hard to build—even if it’s just a merchant’s trade that others look down upon—they poured their hearts into it.”

Lady Wan sobbed for a while, then continued, “The Second and Third sons probably don’t care. They are so intelligent and have already made a name for themselves before the Emperor at such a young age. If these things are taken, so be it. When they grow up, they will surely achieve great things. I was just thinking of my Fifth Son. My Fifth Son is a bit slow; perhaps in the future, he will only be able to rely on some material wealth…”

“Master, I am being willful.” She wiped her tears and forced a smile through her sobs. “Actually, when the Second and Third sons figured out the ancient formula from old books, they brought the Fifth Son to see me and let him contribute some money, calling it an ‘investment.’ Just treat it as me being greedy and sad that the money is gone. Master, you must make up for my capital.”

Li Yuan’s face was as dark as water.

He took a few deep breaths and said, “Is what you say true? The Lady actually knelt and begged Mother?”

Lady Wan gave a bitter smile. “Master, the Lady was perfectly fine when she sent you off this morning.”

Li Yuan stood up. “I am going to see the Lady. Lady Wan, don’t worry. My Tang State Duke’s mansion has not yet fallen to the point where it can only support one person’s success.”

Lady Wan stood up and grabbed the hem of Li Yuan’s robe, looking panicked. “Master, you promised me you wouldn’t tell anyone what I said. If you do this, how will I ever dare to confide in you again?”

Li Yuan gently gathered Lady Wan’s shoulders. “Don’t worry, I won’t tell anyone. Don’t be sad; I can solve this.”

Lady Wan let go, her face full of adoration. “Good, I believe in you, Master.”

Li Yuan left, and Lady Wan stood at the door watching him, unwilling to leave for a long time.

This scene was seen by others, who sighed that Lady Wan was truly devoted to the Tang State Duke.

After leaning against the door for half a quarter of an hour, Lady Wan returned inside and had water brought to remove her makeup.

To look elegant yet beautiful, and to ensure her makeup didn’t run while crying, was no easy task.

After washing her face, Lady Wan threw the towel aside in frustration.

Her maid said, “Don’t be angry, Mistress. Since the Duke said he can solve it, he surely will.”

Lady Wan snorted. “He’s acting tough now, but it might not be the same when he sees the Old Madam. How many times has he been tough behind her back, only to be meek and submissive when he actually faces her?”

The maid said, “This time is different. The Second, Third, and Fifth sons are all the Duke’s children; he will still feel for them.”

“Hmph.” Lady Wan snorted again, then shed genuine tears. “If the Second and Third sons, who were born of the Lady’s own womb, are treated this way, what kind of life will my Fifth Son have living under Li Jiancheng’s thumb in the future?”

“Look at the Second and Third sons; they have nothing for themselves, yet when they get rewards, they give a share to the Fourth and Fifth sons. When they start a business, they share it with the Fourth and Fifth sons. Li Jiancheng at most sends some gifts to the Fourth Son, but he has never once thought of my Fifth Son!” Lady Wan was both angry and sad, and couldn’t help but cover her face and weep. “How did the Fifth Son end up with such an eldest brother?”

The maid patted Lady Wan’s shoulder, feeling equally sad.

She had followed her mistress from Jiangnan to the capital, watching her go from a lively, pampered young lady of a noble family to someone who had to be cautious in every word and deed, and now she was worrying about the future of the Fifth Young Master. How could she not be sad?

But her sadness was useless. She could only comfort her mistress softly, “Mistress, don’t be sad. If the eldest brother cannot be relied upon, there are still the Second and Third Young Masters. As the Duke said, the Tang State Duke’s mansion isn’t limited to supporting only one person. How common is it for noble families to have several Dukes or County Dukes in one household? With the Emperor’s favor for the Second and Third Young Masters, they will surely be ennobled sooner or later. They will definitely help the Fifth Young Master get ahead.”

Lady Wan leaned her head on her maid’s shoulder, closing her eyes and nodding while tears streamed down her face.

When Li Yuan left Lady Wan’s courtyard, the servant he had sent to check on Lady Dou happened to return.

The servant replied, “The Lady said she is fine, just that she caught a bit of wind in the courtyard today and had a headache, so she went to sleep early.”

Li Yuan clenched his fists. “Does the Lady not trust me either?”

The servant was confused. “The Lady looked to be in good spirits; she should truly be fine.”

Li Yuan waved the servant away and strode toward the courtyard where Lady Dou lived.

When he entered, the candles in Lady Dou’s bedroom had already been extinguished.

Li Yuan walked through the darkness to the side of the bed and sat down in silence.

Lady Dou was the first to speak: “Why does the Master sit in the dark without a sound? Are you trying to scare me?”

Li Yuan said, “I know you aren’t asleep, and I know you can recognize my footsteps.”

Lady Dou said, “I just have a headache; I’ll be fine after a day’s rest. You don’t need to worry.”

Li Yuan said, “Are you worried that I will have a conflict with Mother?”

After a long while, a faint sigh came from the darkness.

Lady Dou said, “Master, help me light the candle.”

Li Yuan stood up and lit the candle.

Lady Dou sat up.

Li Yuan returned to the bedside and draped a robe over her. “Be careful not to catch a cold.”

He looked at the corners of Lady Dou’s eyes; they were indeed red, and the tear tracks had not yet dried.

Lady Dou said, “Master is the Duke, the master of the mansion. The affairs of the mansion naturally cannot be hidden from you. It was just me overthinking, sigh.”

Li Yuan forced a smile. “Yes, nothing can be hidden from me.”

Lady Dou said, “Looking at the dignitaries in the court, if the elders are outstanding, the descendants are often ennobled in groups. If the descendants themselves are outstanding, the Emperor won’t look at whether someone in their clan has already been ennobled when it’s time to grant a title. The Second and Third sons are outstanding, especially the Second Son; it should be easy for him to go to the frontier and earn merit. I have always thought that just as the Li An and Li Zhe of the Li family were both County Dukes, our Second and Third sons should be able to achieve the same.”

The Li An and Li Zhe that Lady Dou mentioned were the sons of Li Yuan’s seventh uncle, Li Yuan’s late cousins.

Li Yuan said, “Not just Li An and Li Zhe; several of my uncles were also high-ranking officials. Sigh, even my fourth uncle, Li Bi.”

Li Yuan’s eldest and second uncles both died young, so Li Yuan’s father, Li Bing, inherited the title of Tang State Duke. The other uncles who did not inherit the title held high positions in the Northern Zhou dynasty, and many were ennobled.

Therefore, even though Li Yuan’s fourth uncle, Li Bi, had raised an army to kill the powerful Northern Zhou official Yang Jian and died in failure, Yang Jian still heavily relied on the Li family after establishing the Sui Dynasty.

In particular, Li An and Li Zhe, who had stood against Li Bi at the time, were highly trusted and valued by Yang Jian, both serving as County Dukes.

Most Dukes were created at the founding of a dynasty; it was difficult to be granted such a title in times of peace. But aiming for the title of County Duke, Li Yuan also felt that with the current abilities of his Second and Third sons, it wasn’t overly ambitious.

Lady Dou said, “Although for the sake of the family, the Eldest Son will inherit the Dukedom, the resources of the mansion should be tilted toward the Second and Third sons to add two more County Dukes to the Tang State Duke’s lineage—that would be the optimal choice. But how can there be such calculation between family members? Brothers should just support each other. Like before, when the Second and Third sons gained fame outside, the Eldest Son naturally enjoyed the benefits without any need for competition between brothers.”

Li Yuan sighed, rarely listening so intently to his wife discuss court affairs. “Indeed.”

Lady Dou said, “Human hearts are made of flesh. If you favor one and suppress another, how can the brothers not grow apart? Those with great talent naturally have high aspirations; the Second and Third sons don’t even submit to you, Master.”

Li Yuan couldn’t hold back his sigh.

He held his forehead and gritted his teeth. “Those two brats really don’t submit to anyone. They aren’t even respectful enough to the Crown Prince; the Emperor often makes fun of them.”

Lady Dou gave a wry smile. “Those with overflowing talent are all like this. Don’t you, Master, refuse to submit to anyone whenever archery is mentioned? Even when General Zhangsun beat you once, didn’t you drag him into a rematch until you won?”

Li Yuan was slightly smug. “That’s true, those two are just like me.”

Lady Dou said, “Business is a small matter to begin with. I’ve never heard of any noble family relying on business to maintain their household; they all live off land rents. The Second and Third sons are just young and playing around. When they made the soap, they didn’t even think about making money for themselves; they used the dowries of their sisters and even asked me and Lady Wan for our private savings, saying that if they made money, it would be for us ladies to play with.”

Li Yuan took a deep breath. “Dowries?!”

Lady Dou gave a bitter smile. “Yes. They even said that if they could really make a lot of money, they would bring their unmarried sisters into it. They can achieve great things, and their future assets will surely be rewards from the Emperor. Not to mention fiefs, even if they were just given a few good manors to collect rent, wouldn’t that be better than this lowly merchant’s path? This business matter was just for the girls to save up some pocket money.”

Lady Dou patted Li Yuan’s arm and sighed. “I once supported the Tang State Duke’s mansion on my own. Master was still young then, and connections in the court could only be secured with money, so we valued wealth. But it’s different now. With you as their father, does the Eldest Son really need money to curry favor with people? He just needs to wait for others to curry favor with him. Our Tang State Duke’s mansion has become so prominent because of you, Master.”

Li Yuan rubbed his temples. “Mother is perhaps truly afraid of poverty. At that time, I didn’t have much of a salary. When preparing gifts for the holidays, Mother would worry in secret, not knowing how many dowries had been pawned, and she often went to the palace to borrow money from Empress Wenxian, suffering many cold looks. But it is indeed different now! I’m not dead yet! And Li Jiancheng is not an orphan!”

Lady Dou laughed. “Normally, if you said that, I would advise you to be careful with your words. But the logic is sound. You are still in your prime, Master, and you’ve only just begun your career; your future is still vast. By the time you retire, perhaps even the youngest, the Fifth Son, will be a grandfather. Sigh, the Eldest Son should be thinking about earning his own title; it’s still a long way off before he becomes the Tang State Duke.”

Li Yuan said, “What you say makes perfect sense, why didn’t you tell Mother?”

Lady Dou sighed. “Do you think I dare? If I scold the Eldest Son even a little, everyone immediately says I’m biased! That’s why I have a headache.”

Li Yuan said sheepishly, “Mother is indeed overly fond of the Eldest Son. He was raised by her own hands, so it’s normal for her to favor him.”

Lady Dou sighed again. “Yes. But the Eldest Son will have to shoulder the burden of the Tang State Duke’s mansion in the future; how can he be so spoiled? Your grandfather and father both fought on the battlefield, and your goal, Master, must surely be to become a Great General. War is bitter.”

Li Yuan comforted Lady Dou. “Don’t worry, my dear. Although the Eldest Son is a bit spoiled by Mother, he is skilled in archery and horsemanship, and his hunting skills are quite good.”

Lady Dou thought to herself, *Is hunting the same as war?* But she nodded. “If you say so, Master, then I am relieved. Master, let’s sleep. We can discuss these troublesome matters tomorrow. Sigh, or perhaps you should go to Lady Wan’s? My head still hurts.”

Li Yuan said, “No, I’ll sleep here. I won’t disturb you; you just sleep.”

chunks.chapterTitle: 第34章 你方唱罢我登场 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
说着他就钻进了被子里。

窦夫人哭笑不得，唤人来吹灭蜡烛。

……

“太子殿下，表兄殿下，你赶紧让皇后殿下加入吧，再不加入，我和弟弟就没法继续做更好的香皂了。”李世民拉着杨昭的衣角耍赖，“让我和弟弟给人打白工，我们才不干。若不是我们自己的作坊，谁没事琢磨这些？我们忙于读书习武呢。”

杨昭哭笑不得：“什么表兄殿下？叫表兄就表兄，别不伦不类。你们就该读书习武，琢磨这些工匠商贾之事干什么？”

李世民眨巴着眼睛道：“我和弟弟还小，还不能出仕，除了玩一点商贾游戏，还能做什么？商贾游戏总比投壶有趣。兄长才不应该琢磨商贾之事，他都当官了！”

杨昭皱眉道：“这倒是。我听闻他每日来探望你和三郎，还以为他和你们很友悌。”

李世民翻白眼：“可别每日来探望我们了。我和三郎急需休息，他却非要每日带着狐朋狗友来折磨我们，烦不烦啊。我和三郎向着祖母哭了一场，他才没有继续打扰我们。否则我和三郎肯定现在还病着。”

杨昭疑惑：“探望你还不好了？”

李世民道：“太子殿下肯定也有生病的时候吧？生病时是不是不想说话只想睡觉？若有人每日都拉着你说话……嗯……”

李世民耸肩，摊手，摇摇头，叹气。

杨昭仔细一想，还真是这样。

特别是感染了风寒，咳得嗓子都哑了，谁耐烦说话？

“辛苦了。”杨昭同情道。

李世民道：“其实兄长应该也是好意，只是兄长也还未到弱冠，按照祖母的话来说，兄长也还是个孩子，他不懂怎么照顾孩子。所以我和弟弟还是很感激他来看望我们的。能每日来探望我们，足以表明他对我们的关心。只是这香皂铺子，我和弟弟是想把生意做起来后交给姊妹们。”

李世民不好意思地摸了摸鼻子，道：“还有我未来的丈母，嘿嘿。”

杨昭无语：“你年纪这么小，就开始讨好丈母了？”

李世民挺起胸脯道：“对丈母好，怎么能叫讨好？”

“行行行，你的歪理很有道理。”杨昭道，“我这就去求母后，你要同去吗？”

李世民立刻努力抱住太子殿下那完全抱不住的大胖腰：“要去要去！我好久没见到表叔了。我现在射箭比以前还厉害，我要和表叔炫耀！”

杨昭嘀咕：“你还真是一点都不怕父皇……行，一起去。别挂在我腰上，自己走！”

杨昭带着李世民去面圣。杨广正好在萧皇后处抱怨朝堂。

李世民没有向杨广吐苦水，只炫耀自己的射箭本事又有了长进。

杨广笑着让李世民展示了一下射箭技术，然后坏心眼地让李世民骑在马背上射箭。

李世民还没学骑射，所有箭全部落在了靶子外面，把杨广逗得哈哈大笑。

李世民腮帮子鼓鼓道：“表叔，等我学会了骑射，再给表叔汇报！”

杨广笑着道：“好。”

杨广逗弄晚辈逗弄得十分开心，大手一挥又是许多赏赐，并且又要给李渊和李建成赏赐。

杨昭犹豫了一下，在杨广准备又给李渊和李建成赏赐的时候，起身道：“唐国公教导有方，理应得赏。但李家大郎已经因二郎三郎得过一次赏，若再因二郎三郎得赏，恐朝中会有非议。”

杨广想了想，道：“也罢，就不赏了。”

他很疑惑，这点小赏赐，太子怎么会阻拦？

正因为事情出乎常理，所以杨广就很干脆地听了太子的进谏。

杨广派人把李世民送回家，借口许久没有和太子交流父子感情，离开了皇后宫中，与杨昭一同往东宫走。

杨昭累得脚打颤，但不敢露出喘气的模样，只能强忍着。

“我听闻李建成常说他和大雄大德兄弟友悌，但看你今日的表现，似乎不是如此？”杨广背着手问道，“他可是仗着自己是嫡长，欺负大雄和大德？”

杨昭借着叹气深深喘了口气，道：“站在他的角度，倒也不是欺负。勋贵家族，嫡长子继承爵位，好的东西自然是嫡长子先挑，大雄大德年幼，怎能与长兄比？”

杨广冷哼：“是他怎么与大雄大德比吧？这么大岁数，也没见他文采武功上有什么名声。”

杨昭知道父皇一定会生气。

李二郎和李三郎和父皇当初非常相似，都是头顶上有一个庸才兄长。好不容易夺嫡成功，外界却只因父皇不是嫡长而传播许多离谱的谣言。

父皇现在行事急躁，好大喜功，也是想尽快证明自己才适合当皇帝。

不过杨昭虽然是嫡长，听了李世民言语中隐藏着的心酸，也有些生气。

除了同情李世民和李玄霸之外，更重要的是这香皂工坊是父皇赏赐、他亲自跑下来的。唐国公府说收就收了？这是拿他和父皇不当回事？

杨昭不爱和人告状。且他知道自家父皇小心眼，若自己告状，父皇很容易往重了处罚。

不过唐国公府若是抢了二郎三郎的香皂作坊，这事迟早会传到父皇耳中，到时父皇更加震怒，说不定会牵连唐国公府一家。

唐国公李渊是位贤臣，可不能被后宅之事牵连了。所以杨昭思索之后，还是自己和父皇说了。

“其实这事和唐国公和唐国公夫人没什么关系，只是姨婆她老人家偏疼自己带大的大孙子，所以见大雄和大德琢磨出香皂方子，得了父皇的喜爱，就……唉。”杨昭叹气，“老人的偏疼有时候不讲道理。”

杨广白了儿子一眼，道：“你是想说你祖父母偏疼你不讲道理，还是想说你父皇我偏疼你家大郎不讲道理？”

杨昭立刻抱怨道：“父皇，儿子可没想那么多，你也别想太多。”

杨广回头让跟随的宫人把马车带过来，指着旁边道：“走不动了？一旁休息去。你逞强还能瞒住朕？”

杨昭讪讪道：“我在减肥了，在减了。”

杨广横了大胖儿子一眼，根本不相信。

杨昭赶紧转移话题：“我观姨婆就是看着大雄大德一得赏，李建成就能得赏，就把大雄大德当成为李建成讨赏的工具了。李建成在大雄大德出生前当了九年独子，估计也还没有习惯如何当兄长。大雄大德确实受了一些委屈。不过有唐国公和唐国公夫人护着，他二人还是无事的。”

杨广冷笑：“李渊是出了名的大孝子，他哪敢对他母亲呛声？”

杨广把大胖儿子送上马车后，就回宫发布诏令训斥李渊，让李渊回家反省，反省够了再官复原职，并把李建成的荫官也免了。

诏令大意是，朕赏赐给你儿子的东西，你也敢乱分配，你是不是不把朕放在眼里？！

接到诏书的时候，李渊难得硬气了一回，虽然没有和老母亲吵架，但把李建成狠狠训斥了一顿。

“你祖母年老昏庸不懂，你还不懂？你是未来的唐国公！现在已经是五品的官员！一点黄白之物就能让你迷了眼睛？你居然还宣扬出去了？！”

李渊气得胸口发疼。

他一大早起来，柴绍就来拜访，委婉告诉他，香皂生意的本钱是李昭的嫁妆，唐国公府怎么能一句“外嫁女”就把李昭赶走？李昭不敢忤逆长辈，他却看不下去了。

柴绍刚被他送走，长孙府的高夫人居然亲自来赔罪，说不知道这生意是唐国公府的，还以为是李二郎李三郎闹着玩，所以她为长孙无忌也入了一份，现在问怎么退出。

窦夫人接待的高夫人，李渊在屏风后听着，脸皮都要烧起来了。

很快，大女婿和二女婿也一同登门拜访，说家中娘子已经决定退出香皂生意，请丈人别生气。

李渊：“？？？”我对大娘子二娘子生气什么？！

大女婿和二女婿委婉道，你看香皂生意又赚钱又赚皇帝好感，所以想把生意补贴给李建成的事已经传遍京城了。同时传遍的还有，你家李建成斥责外嫁女插手唐国公府的生意，二郎三郎年幼不懂，外嫁女还不懂吗？还不是因为贪婪？

李渊：“……”不行了，要晕过去了！李建成你在外面胡说什么！

京中风言风语传得极快，三位女婿和未来的亲家都上门了，显然京中宦官贵族估计都知道了。

李渊拿起马鞭就对着李建成一顿抽：“你不劝着你祖母就罢了，你还把这件事说出去？喝了两口马尿，你就管不住自己的嘴了吗！”

李建成原本也是后悔得很。他如寻常一样和朋友喝酒，朋友提起香皂什么时候贩卖，他就得意地说了香皂生意已经是他的，并随口多说了几句。

现在被鞭子抽了，李建成心中那点后悔就变成了委屈：“这又不是我说的！是祖母说的不该外嫁女插手唐国公府的生意！怎么能怪在我身上！”

李渊气得发抖：“你还顶嘴？我抽死你！”

独孤老夫人拄着拐杖赶来，捶胸顿足地哭道：“是我说的！你打大郎干什么！你有本事就打我啊！”

李建成赶紧躲到祖母身后。

李渊无奈道：“母亲！本来这只是一件小事，但他喝醉酒后乱说话，这事传出去后就从小事变成了大事。母亲你也知道朝堂争斗有多激烈，我得了陛下重用，红着眼睛盯着我的人多的是……”

李渊话还未说完，杨广派人来传免官反省的诏令了。

李渊叹了口气，送走了传诏的官员，扬着诏令道：“看吧，我就说陛下肯定会生气。”

李建成惧怕不已，情急之下推了独孤老夫人一把：“又不是我的错！是祖母非要把铺子给我！我还拒绝了！我才不做那些商贾之事！明明是祖母的错！”

独孤老夫人一个踉跄，被张婆扶住了身体。

她不敢置信地回头看着那个满脸惊恐，不断说自己没错的大孙儿。

李渊冷眼看着李建成，握着诏令的手几乎要把诏令捏碎，板着脸一言不发。

独孤老夫人本就苍老，现在她好像更苍老了。

李渊被征辟入朝，回到家中与独孤老夫人团聚后，独孤老夫人的精神好了许多，身体也好了一些，都能拄着拐杖走路了。

现在，她感到身体里的精神气好像被谁抽了出来。

独孤老夫人苦笑：“是，是我的错。渊儿，是我的错，我连累了你和大郎。我亲自去皇宫请罪，是我糊涂。”

……

“祖母虽然知道我把香皂工坊建造在皇帝赏赐的土地上，知道太子有帮忙，但她不如我了解皇帝，只以为按照寻常的道理，赏赐给小孩的东西，自然就是赏赐给父母的，所以唐国公府可以任意取用。”

“用阿姊的嫁妆做本钱的事是我故意瞒着，连母亲都不知道。”

李玄霸垂目。

他没有和二哥说话，也没有和任何人说话，不过是在四处无人的时候自言自语罢了。

这些话他也不会也不能和二哥说，因为二哥对祖母还是有亲情的，对母亲更是亲近无比。

而他这个后世来的孤魂，连最疼爱自己的母亲也不是全然相信的。

自己所能相信的，大概只有史书中盖棺定论的唐太宗李世民。

那个就算因魏徵推举的人都谋反气得推了魏徵的功德碑，冷静下来后又默默把功德碑给重新竖起来的好脾气二哥。

他更不能说……“祖母大概熬不到明年开春了。”

李玄霸叹了口气，捂着嘴又咳了几声，裹紧了自己的小被子。

得赶紧养好病，不然给祖母守灵的时候估计会把身体熬坏。

“啊啊啊啊阿玄！耶耶和兄长都被陛下免职反省了！怎么会这么严重！”

李世民踹门而入。

李玄霸咳着嗽骂道：“你没长手吗！推门不会吗？怎么老踹门咳咳咳……”

“哦。”

李世民出门，关门。

然后，推门，大喊。

“啊啊啊啊阿玄！耶耶和兄长都被陛下免职反省了！怎么会这么严重！”

李玄霸：“？？？”

他无语极了。我未来的唐太宗文皇帝二哥，现在只是一个逗逼。

唉，没办法，只能自己多操心了。

“其实也不算严重。”李玄霸慢悠悠道，“反省几日就会官复原职。”

“哦，那没事了。”李世民扑到床榻上，高兴地滚来滚去，“哈哈哈兄长挨揍了，我自出生以来还是第一次看到兄长挨揍，哈哈哈，畅快！”

“你估计记不全从出生以来的事。”李玄霸随口抬杠，“咳咳咳，别扯我被子！”

“哦。”李世民帮弟弟掖紧被角，然后继续滚来滚去，“哈哈哈哈真畅快。”

李玄霸嘴角上弯。

是啊，真畅快。
chunks.englishText:
With that, he dove under the covers.

Lady Dou was left between laughter and tears, and she called for someone to come and blow out the candles.

……

“Your Highness the Crown Prince, Cousin, you must hurry and have Her Majesty the Empress join us! If she doesn’t, my younger brother and I won’t be able to continue making better soap.” Li Shimin tugged at the hem of Yang Zhao’s robe, acting shamelessly. “We refuse to work for free. If it weren’t our own workshop, who would bother pondering such things? We are busy studying and practicing martial arts.”

Yang Zhao was caught between laughter and tears. “What is this ‘Cousin Highness’? Just call me Cousin; don’t be so improper. You two should be focusing on your studies and martial arts—why are you meddling in the affairs of craftsmen and merchants?”

Li Shimin blinked his eyes and said, “My brother and I are still young and cannot yet enter official service. Besides playing merchant games, what else is there to do? Merchant games are at least more interesting than pitch-pot. My elder brother shouldn’t be the one pondering these things; he’s already an official!”

Yang Zhao frowned. “That is true. I heard he visits you and Third Brother every day; I thought he was being brotherly.”

Li Shimin rolled his eyes. “Please, no more daily visits. Third Brother and I are in desperate need of rest, yet he insists on bringing his band of rowdy friends to torment us every single day. Is it not annoying? Third Brother and I had to cry to Grandmother before he finally stopped bothering us. Otherwise, we would surely still be sick.”

Yang Zhao was puzzled. “Is being visited such a bad thing?”

Li Shimin replied, “Your Highness must have been sick before, right? When you’re ill, don’t you just want to sleep without having to talk to anyone? If someone were to drag you into conversation every day… well…”

Li Shimin shrugged, spread his hands, shook his head, and sighed.

Yang Zhao thought about it carefully, and it really was like that.

Especially when suffering from a cold, with a throat so hoarse from coughing that you can barely speak—who has the patience for chatter?

“You’ve had a hard time,” Yang Zhao said sympathetically.

Li Shimin continued, “Actually, my elder brother likely means well, but he hasn’t reached the age of twenty yet. In Grandmother’s words, he is still just a child, and he doesn’t know how to take care of children. So, my brother and I are still very grateful that he came to visit. The fact that he could visit every day is enough to show his concern for us. It’s just that for this soap shop, my brother and I intended to hand the business over to our sisters once it was up and running.”

Li Shimin rubbed his nose sheepishly and added, “And to my future mother-in-law, hehe.”

Yang Zhao was speechless. “You’re so young, and you’re already trying to curry favor with your mother-in-law?”

Li Shimin puffed out his chest. “How can being good to one’s mother-in-law be called ‘currying favor’?”

“Fine, fine, your twisted logic makes perfect sense,” Yang Zhao said. “I’ll go petition the Empress now. Do you want to come along?”

Li Shimin immediately scrambled to hug the Crown Prince’s rather portly waist—which he couldn’t quite wrap his arms around. “I want to go! I haven’t seen Uncle in a long time. My archery is even better than before; I want to show off to him!”

Yang Zhao muttered, “You really aren’t afraid of the Emperor at all… Fine, let’s go together. Stop hanging off my waist and walk yourself!”

Yang Zhao took Li Shimin to see the Emperor. Yang Guang happened to be at Empress Xiao’s quarters, complaining about the imperial court.

Li Shimin did not pour out his grievances to Yang Guang; he only boasted about how his archery skills had improved.

Yang Guang laughed and let Li Shimin demonstrate his archery, then, with a mischievous glint in his eye, ordered him to shoot while mounted on a horse.

Li Shimin had not yet learned mounted archery, and all his arrows landed wide of the target, sending Yang Guang into a fit of hearty laughter.

Li Shimin puffed out his cheeks. “Uncle, once I’ve learned mounted archery, I’ll report back to you!”

Yang Guang smiled and said, “Very well.”

Yang Guang was thoroughly enjoying teasing his young relative. With a wave of his hand, he bestowed many rewards, and then prepared to grant more to Li Yuan and Li Jiancheng.

Yang Zhao hesitated. Just as Yang Guang was about to bestow further rewards upon Li Yuan and Li Jiancheng, he stood up and said, “The Duke of Tang has taught his sons well and deserves to be rewarded. But since the eldest son of the Li family has already been rewarded once because of the second and third sons, I fear there may be gossip in the court if he is rewarded again for their sake.”

Yang Guang thought for a moment and said, “Very well, then we shall not reward him.”

He was puzzled; why would the Crown Prince block such a small reward?

Precisely because the matter defied common sense, Yang Guang simply followed the Crown Prince’s advice.

Yang Guang sent someone to escort Li Shimin home, then used the excuse of not having spent time with the Crown Prince to leave the Empress’s palace, walking toward the Eastern Palace with Yang Zhao.

Yang Zhao’s feet were trembling with fatigue, but he dared not show any signs of breathlessness, forcing himself to endure.

“I heard Li Jiancheng often speaks of being brotherly with the Daxiong and Dade brothers, but judging by your performance today, that does not seem to be the case?” Yang Guang asked with his hands behind his back. “Is he using his status as the eldest legitimate son to bully Daxiong and Dade?”

Yang Zhao took a deep breath under the guise of sighing. “From his perspective, it is not exactly bullying. In noble families, the eldest legitimate son inherits the title, so naturally, he gets to pick the best things first. Daxiong and Dade are young; how can they compare to their elder brother?”

Yang Guang snorted, “It is a question of how *he* compares to Daxiong and Dade! At his age, I have yet to hear of any reputation he has earned in literature or martial arts.”

Yang Zhao knew his father would be angry.

Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were very similar to how his father had been—both had a mediocre elder brother looming over them. Even after his father had successfully seized the throne, outsiders spread absurd rumors simply because he was not the eldest legitimate son.

His father acted impulsively and craved greatness precisely because he wanted to prove as quickly as possible that he was the one fit to be Emperor.

However, although Yang Zhao was the eldest legitimate son, hearing the hidden bitterness in Li Shimin’s words made him angry as well.

Beyond sympathizing with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, what mattered more was that this soap workshop was a gift from his father, which he had personally helped set up. The Duke of Tang’s household just took it over as they pleased? Did they not take him and the Emperor seriously?

Yang Zhao did not like to tattle. Furthermore, he knew his father was petty; if he complained, his father might overreact with harsh punishments.

However, if the Duke of Tang’s household had snatched the soap workshop from Erlang and Sanlang, the news would reach the Emperor’s ears sooner or later. By then, the Emperor would be even more enraged, and it might implicate the entire Duke of Tang’s household.

Duke of Tang Li Yuan was a virtuous official; he could not be implicated by the affairs of his inner household. So, after some thought, Yang Zhao decided to tell the Emperor himself.

“Actually, this has nothing to do with the Duke of Tang or his wife. It is just that their grandmother dotes on the eldest grandson she raised herself. Seeing that Daxiong and Dade came up with the soap formula and won the Emperor’s favor, she… sigh.” Yang Zhao sighed. “An elder’s doting is sometimes unreasonable.”

Yang Guang rolled his eyes at his son. “Are you trying to say that your grandparents’ doting on you is unreasonable, or that I, your father, am unreasonable for doting on your eldest brother?”

Yang Zhao immediately complained, “Father, I wasn’t thinking that far; don’t overthink it.”

Yang Guang turned back and ordered the accompanying palace attendants to bring the carriage over, pointing to the side. “Can’t walk anymore? Go rest on the side. Do you think you can hide your posturing from me?”

Yang Zhao said sheepishly, “I’m losing weight, really.”

Yang Guang shot his portly son a glance, not believing him at all.

Yang Zhao quickly changed the subject. “I observe that Grandmother simply sees Daxiong and Dade’s rewards as a way for Li Jiancheng to get rewarded as well, so she treats them as tools to secure favors for him. Li Jiancheng was an only child for nine years before they were born; I suppose he hasn’t gotten used to being an elder brother yet. Daxiong and Dade have indeed suffered some grievances. But with the Duke of Tang and his wife protecting them, the two of them will be fine.”

Yang Guang sneered, “Li Yuan is a famously filial son; how would he dare to talk back to his mother?”

After sending his portly son into the carriage, Yang Guang returned to the palace to issue an edict reprimanding Li Yuan, ordering him to return home for self-reflection. He was to resume his duties only after he had reflected enough, and Li Jiancheng’s inherited official rank was also revoked.

The gist of the edict was: I bestowed these things upon your sons, and you dare to redistribute them as you please? Do you not hold me in your eyes?!

When he received the edict, Li Yuan was uncharacteristically firm. While he didn’t argue with his mother, he gave Li Jiancheng a severe dressing-down.

“Your grandmother is old and muddled, but are you? You are the future Duke of Tang! You are already a fifth-rank official! Can a bit of wealth blind you? And you actually went around bragging about it?!”

Li Yuan was so angry his chest ached.

Early that morning, Chai Shao had come to visit, tactfully telling him that the capital for the soap business was Li Zhao’s dowry—how could the Duke of Tang’s household drive Li Zhao away with a single phrase about her being a “married-out daughter”? Li Zhao dared not defy her elders, but he could no longer stand by and watch.

No sooner had he sent Chai Shao away than Lady Gao of the Changsun household came personally to apologize, saying she didn’t know the business belonged to the Duke of Tang’s household and thought it was just Li Erlang and Li Sanlang playing around, which was why she had invested for Changsun Wuji. Now, she wanted to know how to withdraw.

Lady Dou had received Lady Gao, and Li Yuan, listening from behind a screen, felt his face burning with shame.

Soon after, his eldest and second sons-in-law also visited together, saying their wives had decided to withdraw from the soap business and asking their father-in-law not to be angry.

Li Yuan: “???” Why would I be angry at my eldest and second daughters?!

The sons-in-law tactfully explained that the news—that the soap business was both profitable and favored by the Emperor, and that they wanted to subsidize Li Jiancheng with it—had spread throughout the capital. Also spreading was the rumor that Li Jiancheng had scolded his married-out sister for meddling in the Duke of Tang’s business, saying that while the second and third brothers were young and ignorant, surely the married-out sister should know better? Was it not just greed?

Li Yuan: “…” I can’t take it; I’m going to faint! Li Jiancheng, what kind of nonsense are you spouting outside!

The gossip in the capital spread extremely fast. With three sons-in-law and his future in-laws all visiting, it was clear that all the eunuchs and nobles in the capital likely knew.

Li Yuan grabbed a horse whip and lashed out at Li Jiancheng. “It would have been enough if you hadn’t tried to dissuade your grandmother, but you actually went and spread this around? Have you lost control of your tongue after drinking a few cups of horse piss?!”

Li Jiancheng had already been full of regret. He had been drinking with friends as usual, and when they brought up when the soap would be sold, he had proudly declared the business was his and let a few extra words slip.

Now, whipped, his regret turned into grievance. “It wasn’t me who said it! It was Grandmother who said a married-out daughter shouldn’t meddle in the Duke of Tang’s business! How can you blame me?!”

Li Yuan trembled with rage. “You’re still talking back? I’ll whip you to death!”

Old Lady Dugu hurried over, leaning on her cane, beating her chest and wailing, “It was me who said it! Why are you hitting the eldest? If you have the ability, hit me instead!”

Li Jiancheng hurriedly hid behind his grandmother.

Li Yuan said helplessly, “Mother! This was originally a small matter, but after he got drunk and ran his mouth, it turned into a big one. You know how intense the court struggles are; I am favored by the Emperor, and there are plenty of people watching me with jealous eyes…”

Before Li Yuan could finish, Yang Guang’s messenger arrived with the edict to revoke his office and order self-reflection.

Li Yuan sighed, sent the official away, and waved the edict. “See? I told you the Emperor would be angry.”

Li Jiancheng was terrified. In his panic, he shoved Old Lady Dugu. “It’s not my fault! It’s Grandmother who insisted on giving me the shop! I even refused! I don’t want to do those merchant things! It’s clearly Grandmother’s fault!”

Old Lady Dugu stumbled and was caught by Nanny Zhang.

She looked back in disbelief at her eldest grandson, who was trembling with fear and insisting he was innocent.

Li Yuan watched Li Jiancheng with cold eyes, his hand gripping the edict so tightly he almost crushed it, his face set and silent.

Old Lady Dugu was already aged, but now she seemed even older.

After Li Yuan was summoned to the court and returned home to reunite with Old Lady Dugu, her spirit had improved, and her health had gotten better; she had even been able to walk with a cane.

Now, she felt as if the life force had been drained from her body.

Old Lady Dugu smiled bitterly. “Yes, it is my fault. Yuan’er, it is my fault. I have implicated you and the eldest. I will go to the palace myself to beg for mercy; I was muddled.”

……

“Although Grandmother knew I built the soap workshop on land bestowed by the Emperor and knew the Crown Prince helped, she doesn’t understand the Emperor as well as I do. She only thought that, according to common logic, things given to children are naturally given to their parents, so the Duke of Tang’s household could use them as they pleased.”

“Using Sister’s dowry as capital was something I deliberately hid; even Mother didn’t know.”

Li Xuanba lowered his eyes.

He wasn’t talking to his second brother, nor to anyone else; he was merely talking to himself when no one was around.

He would not, and could not, tell these things to his second brother, because his second brother still had affection for their grandmother and was even closer to their mother.

And he, a wandering soul from a later age, did not even fully trust the mother who loved him most.

All he could trust was the Tang Taizong Li Shimin, whose legacy was set in stone in the history books.

The good-natured second brother who, even after being so angry that he pushed over Wei Zheng’s monument because the people Wei Zheng recommended had rebelled, quietly re-erected the monument once he had calmed down.

He couldn’t say… “Grandmother probably won’t make it to next spring.”

Li Xuanba sighed, covered his mouth to cough a few times, and wrapped his small quilt tighter around himself.

He had to get over this illness quickly, or he would likely ruin his health while keeping vigil for his grandmother.

“Ahhhhh Ah-Xuan! Father and Eldest Brother have both been suspended by the Emperor for self-reflection! How could it be so serious?!”

Li Shimin kicked the door open and stormed in.

Li Xuanba coughed and cursed, “Do you not have hands?! Can’t you push the door? Why do you always kick it—cough, cough…”

“Oh.”

Li Shimin went out and closed the door.

Then, he pushed the door open and shouted.

“Ahhhhh Ah-Xuan! Father and Eldest Brother have both been suspended by the Emperor for self-reflection! How could it be so serious?!”

Li Xuanba: “???”

He was utterly speechless. My future Tang Taizong Wen Emperor, my second brother, is currently just a goofball.

Sigh, there’s no helping it; I’ll just have to worry more myself.

“It’s not actually that serious,” Li Xuanba said slowly. “They’ll be restored to their posts after a few days of reflection.”

“Oh, then it’s fine.” Li Shimin flopped onto the bed, rolling around happily. “Hahaha, Eldest Brother got a beating! It’s the first time I’ve seen him get beaten since I was born! Hahaha, so satisfying!”

“You probably can’t remember everything since you were born,” Li Xuanba argued casually. “Cough, cough, stop pulling my quilt!”

“Oh.” Li Shimin tucked the quilt around his younger brother and continued to roll around. “Hahahaha, so satisfying.”

The corners of Li Xuanba’s mouth curled upward.

Yes, it was quite satisfying.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第35章 母亲的嫁妆火珠 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第35章 母亲的嫁妆火珠

=

李建成这个嫡长子的名声是不能被毁掉的。

最终独孤老夫人拄着拐杖， 挨家挨户去孙女婿家道歉，说是自己误会了，不知道孙女是用嫁妆当本钱， 还以为是无偿帮助李世民和李玄霸。此事和李建成无关， 都是她老糊涂， 李建成喝醉酒了，对友人重复了她的话而已。

李渊还想带着李世民和李玄霸去道歉，因为他认为这件事是李世民和李玄霸最先惹出来的。

李玄霸卧病在床， 面无表情地问李渊：“我自换季之后病一直没好，父亲真的要带着生病的我去挨家挨户道歉？父亲这样做，恐怕无法挽回兄长的声誉。”

李世民这次也很不给父亲面子：“父亲， 你就是迁怒我和阿玄吧？我和阿玄错在哪里了？就一个小小的铺子，阿姊们拿嫁妆陪我们玩耍有什么问题？香皂会这么红火难道是我们的错？怪我们太优秀？”

李渊气得拂袖而去。

李世民吐舌头：“我还以为父亲会揍我。”

李玄霸道：“你既然怕挨揍， 还故意去气父亲干什么？我敢气他， 是因为我在生病。”

李世民跳到床榻边坐下，手撑着床沿，小短腿甩了甩：“因为我真的生气啊。明明是兄长的错，为何不让兄长去道歉？哪怕说一句喝多了说胡话，或者干脆不承认。反正只是几个狐朋狗友听到， 他若稍稍把话改了改，难道他的那些狐朋狗友还敢出来反驳吗？”

李玄霸道：“士族门阀是这样， 地位看门第和资历，资源分配已经固化，从出生起就已经确定了他们的未来。唐国公府的嫡长子就算再平庸也不能换人， 如果个人本事不行， 就只能靠他人捧了。若要把兄长从这件事中摘出来， 就得其他人承担责任。”

李世民嘴角下撇：“我本来很难过祖母的偏心， 但现在祖母承担起本来兄长承担的责任，我又很替祖母不值。”

李玄霸道：“她自己养出来的好大孙，自食其果，你同情她，她还嫌你挡了好大孙的路。你说拉我们二人去道歉，能是父亲想出来的馊主意？父亲目前对几个儿子还是一视同仁的。”

李世民眯着眼睛想了想，狠狠一拍双腿，生气道：“还真是！你还在病中呢！父亲带着生病的你去道歉，传出去岂不是说是父亲不慈？那父亲也为兄长承担责任了！”

李玄霸瞥了一眼窗口的阴影，道：“是啊。我就不明白这一点，父亲才是唐国公，父亲的仕途和名声才最重要。现在好像兄长才是唐国公似的。”

李世民不住点头：“对啊对啊，明明父亲才是唐国公……唉，还是叫耶耶吧。本来我很生气，想再也不叫耶耶了，但这么一想，耶耶也好可怜哦。有了大孙子，儿子也是根杂草了。”

李世民唉声叹气。

李玄霸差点憋不住笑出来。

他确信二哥没有发现李渊在窗口偷听。这话真是出自二哥肺腑。

草就草吧，还杂草。二哥你说话的艺术也太厉害了。

李渊被两个儿子的话气得饭都吃不下。

窦夫人不理睬李渊，自己默默吃饭。

待窦夫人的饭快吃饱时，李渊才委屈地问道：“你都不问我为何生气？”

窦夫人板着脸道：“你怎么不问我为何生气？”

李渊：“……”

李渊无奈：“我当然不可能把生病的大德带去给人道歉。我只是做个样子，敷衍一下母亲。母亲都作出了这么大的牺牲，我总要安抚一下。”

窦夫人道：“你可以把大郎带去道歉。”

李渊道：“我倒是想，但母亲坚决不许，说未来的唐国公不能留下污点。”

窦夫人道：“嘴硬到底，让祖母和幼弟来替他承担责任，这难道不是更大的污点？再者，未来的唐国公不能留下污点，难道现在的唐国公就能？”

李渊叹气道：“我正是因为这个生气。你知道大雄那混账小子在说什么胡话？他说自从祖母有了大孙子，我这个儿子就成了杂草！”

窦夫人差点没崩住严肃的表情。

她用指甲掐了一下手心，才勉强没笑出来：“大家对大郎确实宠溺得过了。她明明对郎君就很严格。”

李渊道：“或许是因为母亲年纪大了，也或许是唐国公府的情况好转了。民间母亲对儿子很严厉，但对孙儿无比纵容的事也很常见。”

窦夫人想起了京中勋贵的后院，不得不叹气道：“也是。人或许你我将来老了也会糊涂。女婿家就罢了，大家亲自去道歉，给足了他们的面子，他们不会再说什么。其他勋贵不需要理睬，只要郎君你官复原职，重新获得了陛下重用，他们自会闭嘴。”

李渊道：“现在唯一需要重视的就是挽回陛下的好感。”

窦夫人道：“陛下喜好猎鹰骏马，上次郎君进献猎鹰骏马，陛下就很高兴。这次也最好将此事化作亲戚间的小事。郎君多给陛下送些猎鹰骏马，我嫁妆里有一颗火珠……”

窦夫人眼中复杂之色一闪而过：“当年文献皇后将舅舅为我攒的嫁妆赐予我时，曾开玩笑道，这颗火珠她差点没舍得，当时陛下也在场。”

李渊疑惑：“夫人嫁妆中居然还有如此至宝？可当时文献皇后既然如此说，为何夫人不顺势将火珠献给文献皇后，正好讨个好？”

窦夫人：“……”

她脸上浮现完美无缺的微笑，道：“既然文献皇后都这样对我开玩笑了，就是彰显她的大度，我若顺势献宝，岂不是让文献皇后德行有亏？再者，如此异宝，我也舍不得。”

李渊颔首：“也是，姨母品德高尚，她都这样说了，就算你献宝，她也不会收。唉，我真不想贿赂陛下。但为了不成器的儿子，我这个当父亲也只能暂时放下脸面。儿女都是债啊。”

窦夫人安慰道：“这次教训后，大郎肯定也会有所成长。”

李渊道：“之后我亲自教导他！这下母亲总说不出话了！你将火珠找出来给我。长孙季晟也同陛下一同回了京城。他对突厥最熟悉，我去问问他有没有门道尽快买到突厥的好马。”

见李渊要起身，窦夫人忙拦道：“郎君还是先用了饭再去，总不能去长孙将军家蹭饭？”

李渊苦笑：“也是。”

他开始埋头苦吃，一边吃一边不顾食不语的规矩抱怨：“正如二郎和三郎所说的，大郎才像是我们的唐国公，我这个老唐国公都得给他当垫子。唉，儿女都是债。”

窦夫人安静地听着李渊抱怨。待李渊吃完饭离开，她也起身去放着嫁妆的库房里，将火珠取出来。

听闻父亲离开了，李世民把其实病好得差不多了的李玄霸从被窝里挖出来，拖去找母亲玩。

“啊？娘亲的嫁妆？我也要看！”李世民上蹿下跳，被他拉着的李玄霸被迫东倒西歪。

窦夫人护住怀里的匣子，笑骂道：“小心把火珠摔坏了，卖了你都赔不起娘的火珠！”

李世民踮着脚尖往窦夫人怀里看：“什么火珠什么火珠？让我看看！阿玄，你知道什么是火珠吗？”

李玄霸终于把二哥的手甩掉，就像是终于松开了雪橇三傻的绳子一样。

他缓慢地活动被拽酸的胳膊，慢悠悠道：“知道。火珠就是水晶球。与你之前玩的水晶杯是同一种矿物。但做水晶球需要纯天然的大块水晶，十分难得。火珠即使在西域贡品中，也属罕见。”

窦夫人惊讶。她还是第一次知道，火珠居然与水晶是同一种矿物。

李世民疑惑：“水晶就像是冰一样所以叫水晶，那为何水晶球叫火珠？”

李玄霸道：“第一，珍贵的水晶球多是发晶，即透明水晶球中有金属发丝状矿物，在阳光下会闪烁着极其耀眼的光芒，如有火焰在水晶球内燃烧；第二，凹凸镜原理，水晶球能将阳光集中成一个小点，点燃纸张干草等易燃物，《墨子》中有详细描述。”

李世民捏着下巴歪头：“我还没看过《墨子》呢，听上去好有趣。阿玄，把你写了读书笔记的《墨子》借给我看。”

李玄霸道：“好，不过你可能看不懂。”

李世民叉腰：“哼！小看我！”

李玄霸嘴角扯出一个嘲讽的幅度。

虽然自己高中肄业，所掌握的物理学知识也不是你一个小小的唐太宗能吃透的，哼。

李世民拉着窦夫人的袖子嚷嚷：“娘娘！你看！阿玄他嘲笑我！这个弟弟太可恶了，居然嘲笑哥哥，娘娘罚他抄书！”

窦夫人笑着转移话题：“要不要看看真正的火珠长什么模样？”

李世民笑道：“要看！”

窦夫人拿着火珠走到庭院里。

初冬的阳光仍旧温暖灿烂。

窦夫人将火珠小心翼翼从匣子里取出来，解开包裹着火珠的柔软绢布，双手将火珠捧起，正对着灿烂的阳光。

李玄霸的眼眸闪了闪。

即使他看多了各种现代工艺品，人造水晶可以制造出任何纯净度，但这颗天然水晶球的美丽仍旧震撼了他的心。

这是一颗金色钛金水晶球。基底是透明度极高的淡茶色水晶，水晶球中是如同金色草丛般的金黄色板状钛丝。

窦夫人捧着水晶球时，水晶球中的钛丝反射出极其耀眼的金光，让茶色的水晶基底都呈现出了淡淡的金色光辉，就像是她手心中的是一颗发光的金色小太阳。

看到这一幕，李玄霸不难理解，为何古人会将水晶球叫“火珠”。

李世民眼睛慢慢睁大，瞳孔中倒映着钛丝水晶球耀眼的金光，好像被水晶球的光辉迷了眼睛。

当窦夫人重新用绢丝将水晶球罩起来时，李世民的表情明显很失落。

“好漂亮啊。”李世民道，“娘亲为何不把它摆出来……啊？娘亲，你怎么哭了？”

钛丝水晶球的璀璨光辉立刻从李世民的眼底退去，他慌张地踮着脚为母亲擦拭眼泪。

李玄霸上前一步，然后退后半步，静静地看着二哥为母亲擦拭眼泪。

窦夫人含着泪笑道：“没什么，只是想到了一些往事。”

李世民噘嘴：“不高兴的往事快忘掉！呼……呼……我把娘不高兴的往事都吹走！”

窦夫人摇头：“不是不高兴。”

她摸索着手中的水晶球，道：“这颗火珠是娘的舅父喜爱的宝物之一，娘小时候常看舅父把玩。没想到舅父将它放入了给娘攒的嫁妆中。”

窦夫人不敢将火珠拿出来。她一拿出来，火珠璀璨的光辉中好像就能映出当年自己手撑着脸趴在坐榻上，看舅父把火珠滚来滚去把玩的场景。所以李渊才从未见过她嫁妆中这件珍宝。

文献皇后确实是怜惜窦氏这个小女孩的。她知道窦氏嫁妆里奇珍异宝过多，所以公开的嫁妆单子上隐去了一些珍宝，只把真正的嫁妆单子亲手交给了窦氏。

窦夫人理智上知道自己该感激她的保护，却难以生出感激的心情。

而现在，她要用这颗舅父曾经把玩过的珍宝，去换取家人的安全。

李渊只以为皇帝是一时生气，但窦夫人敏锐地察觉皇帝的猜忌多疑和残暴不仁。

窦夫人知道这次皇帝应该还没到对唐国公府过于猜忌的地步，但很小的事积少成多，都可能成为杀身之祸。所以她要彻底将这件事抹平。

文献皇后十分偏爱如今的皇帝杨广，所以在点评窦夫人嫁妆的时候，都把杨广带在身边。

杨广眼光极高，心性骄傲，虽爱珍宝，但也不至于对一个注定会成为孤女的人的嫁妆起心思。唯独在这颗火珠出现的时候，他脸上出现了惊叹和心疼的神色。

窦夫人相信，皇帝应当是还记得这颗火珠的。

她擦干眼泪，也将心中的回忆压下。

她笑道：“娘没事了。还想看吗？娘让人拿个架子来，今日看个够。”

李世民先高兴道：“好啊！”

然后他挠了挠脑袋，道：“如果娘亲看了难过，就不看了。不看了不看了，我不看了，没什么好看的，对吧，阿玄？”

李玄霸点头：“对。”

窦夫人笑道：“不难过了。二郎，去把四郎和五郎带来，我们一起看火珠。”

李世民点头。

李世民离开后，窦夫人又让女婢去请李建成来。

窦夫人一手抱着匣子，一手牵着李玄霸，往庭院里的亭子走去。

待坐下后，窦夫人把匣子放在石桌上，看向沉默的李玄霸：“大德，你是否不喜祖母和父亲？”

李玄霸眼皮子抬了抬，拱手道：“没有。娘，儿没有不孝。”

窦夫人叹气：“你祖母和你父亲也是疼你的。”

李玄霸道：“儿知道。儿对祖母和父亲一直很好，娘为何这么说？”

窦夫人抿了一下嘴唇，摇摇头：“罢了，娘不说了。就当娘胡说吧。”

她对李玄霸招了招手。

李玄霸道：“我咳嗽还未好……”

窦夫人道：“过来。”

李玄霸只好走到母亲身边，被母亲揉搓脸。

他眼中满是无奈。我脸上的肉又不多，娘去揉搓二哥啊。

窦夫人把李玄霸的脸揉搓红后，才长长地舒了一口气。

她屈指弹了一下李玄霸的额头。

李玄霸捂住额头：“哎哟。”

窦夫人终于笑了：“罢了，你虽然心思重，但也很懒，如果别人不算计你，你也是不屑于算计人的。不过你还小，不要想太多。本来你身体就弱，想太多身体就更好不了。你都比二郎矮半个头了。小心以后你和二郎走在一起，别人还以为你是二郎的儿子。”

李玄霸瞪眼吸气，第一次在母亲面前露出不敢置信的表情：“怎么可能！”

窦夫人忍俊不禁，又弹了李玄霸额头一下。

李玄霸捂着额头，淡然的表情终于裂开了缝。

窦夫人继续弹。

李玄霸转身，用后脑勺对着母亲。

窦夫人就弹李玄霸的光秃秃的后脑勺。

李玄霸磨牙，脑袋一抽，抱着头躲在了桌子下面。

刚蹲下，李玄霸就脸一热，意识到自己现在很蠢。

窦夫人笑得前俯后仰。

李玄霸从桌子底下爬出来，远离欺负儿子的娘亲。

窦夫人对李玄霸招手：“过来。”

李玄霸磨磨蹭蹭，在窦夫人再次呼喊时，苦着脸慢慢挪动过去。

果然，窦夫人又开始揉搓李玄霸的脸。

李玄霸一脸生无可恋，心里疯狂喊救命。

李世民刚踏进心声范围，就被李玄霸疯狂呐喊的“救命”震得直捂耳朵。

可惜捂耳朵是没用的。

还好弟弟们的到来，解救了被母亲当做大玩具的李玄霸。

李玄霸立刻躲到张开双臂，像老母鸡一样保护弟弟的李世民身后。

李世民沉沉叹了口气，道：“娘亲，别欺负阿玄，阿玄病还没好呢。等阿玄病好了，我把阿玄送到娘亲手里，娘亲慢慢玩。”

李玄霸气得高抬腿蹬了二哥屁股一脚。

李世民捂住屁股一个踉跄：“哎哟。”

“哈哈哈哈哈。”李元吉鼓着掌大笑，笑得牙齿都露出来了。

李智云被李元吉爆发的笑声吓了一跳，犹豫自己要不要跟着笑。但他笑不出来啊。

不一会儿，李建成也黑着脸过来了。

他瓮声瓮气拱手作揖道：“母亲，我正在看书，没空与幼弟们一同玩耍。”

窦夫人一言不发地把匣子打开，将水晶球放在了架子上。

璀璨的金色光芒瞬间俘虏了众人的视线，连已经见过一次的李玄霸和李世民，都不由再次被美丽的水晶球吸引。

“这是……这就是传说中的至宝火珠吗？”李建成喃喃道，不由自主上前一步，想要触碰美丽的“火珠”。

窦夫人将火珠递给李建成。

李建成小心翼翼把玩了一会儿火珠。

火珠入手温润，李建成很担心一不小心火珠就会从手中掉下来，便赶紧将火珠放回了架子上。

窦夫人道：“都来摸摸。”

连熊孩子李元吉抚摸火珠的动作都很小心翼翼。

孩童其实很聪明，知道碰坏了什么会挨打。有父母看着的时候，他们一般很乖巧。

李玄霸也上手抹了一把。

水晶而已，不过如此。李玄霸琢磨着等赚钱后，就去买一块大水晶原矿，自己车水晶大珠子玩。

待太阳的角度变换，阳光不再照射进亭子中时，窦夫人才将火珠收起来。

“明日我再拿给府中娘子们开开眼。”窦夫人叹了口气，“过几日，这火珠就不属于唐国公府了。”

众人不解，只有李玄霸皱眉，意识到了什么。

窦夫人直视着李建成的眼睛，道：“大郎，这火珠娘本来是准备传给你的妻子。”

李建成拳头攥紧，声音低沉：“那母亲现在想传给谁？！”

窦夫人平静道：“现在娘要把火珠进献给陛下，请求陛下给你官复原职。”

李建成睁大眼。

窦夫人道：“你祖母在你刚懂事的时候就告诉你，唐国公府都是你的，所有都是你的。所以你过于傲慢，认为自己仿佛就是这天地的中心，什么都会顺着你的心意来。可是毗沙门啊，就算是你父亲，如今的唐国公，也不敢说自己能随心所欲。”

李建成垂下头，拳头攥得更紧了。

窦夫人继续道：“确实，无论你成器或者不成器，唐国公都是你的。你父亲当年只七岁就能当唐国公。可你知道那时你祖母护着你父亲，日子过得有多苦吗？”

李建成道：“儿知道……”

窦夫人训斥道：“不！你不知道！你若知道！就不会和人醉酒胡言乱语！你父亲等了多少年才等到征辟入朝？唐国公府蒸蒸日上的时候，你身边那些奉承你的人中有多少真心盼着唐国公府好？有多少就等着抓唐国公府的错处？”

“是，无论如何，将来唐国公府都是你的。可若是你无能，唐国公府还能剩下什么？一个空荡荡的爵位？就算是爵位，若是皇帝不喜，也会轻松给你摘掉！”

“你祖父为了延续唐国公的爵位，在战场经历过多少场厮杀？你父亲将来也一定会上战场拼命，这才能保证爵位传到你手上的时候仍旧是‘唐国公’。”

“你的弟弟们都可以不用小心谨慎，甚至都可以当个无能的纨绔子弟，唯独你不能！因为你若担不起唐国公的担子，这世上就不会再有唐国公！明白吗！”

李建成跪下，第一次流出了真心悔过的眼泪：“是儿子的错，儿子知错了，是儿子不谨慎。”

窦夫人语气缓和道：“我知道你心里委屈，这件事的起因不是你，为何要怪你。因为你是唐国公啊，无论是你的长辈或是你的身边人，都只是给你出主意的人。拿主意的人是你。将来只有你能替唐国公府做决定。所以你现在就要学会承担责任。”

她起身将李建成扶起来，语重心长道：“起来吧，再好好看看这火珠一眼，把这火珠记在心底。记住这本来应该是你的，现在不是了。”

李建成哭着道：“是，儿子记住了。”

独孤老夫人听到这里的事，担心窦夫人把李建成训得太狠，虽然身体不适，仍旧颤颤悠悠过来劝说。

见窦夫人只是带着孩子们玩耍，独孤老夫人正准备离开，却见到了这一幕。

她深深地叹了口气，想起了曾经的艰难。

独孤老夫人摇了摇头，悄无声息地离开。

回到屋里后，独孤老夫人握着张婆的手，泪水浑浊：“我是不是真的做错了？我是不是真的把大郎宠得太过？”

张婆安慰独孤老夫人道：“大郎君还小，还只是个孩子，现在有些不成熟是正常的。等大郎君娶了妻，有了孩子，自然而然就成熟了。”

独孤老夫人抹着眼泪道：“也是。希望郑媵赶紧给大郎生个孩子。有了孩子，大郎肯定就成熟了。”

张婆为独孤老夫人打来温水，为独孤老夫人布满泪水的脸。

Chapter 35: Mother’s Dowry, the Fire Pearl

The reputation of Li Jiancheng, the eldest son and heir, could not be ruined.

In the end, the elderly Lady Dugu leaned on her cane and went door-to-door to apologize to the families of her granddaughter’s husband. She claimed it had all been a misunderstanding—that she hadn't realized her granddaughter was using her own dowry as capital, and had mistakenly thought it was an uncompensated favor to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. She insisted the matter had nothing to do with Li Jiancheng; it was merely her own senile confusion, and Li Jiancheng had simply repeated her words to his friends while intoxicated.

Li Yuan still wanted to take Li Shimin and Li Xuanba along to apologize, as he believed they were the ones who had started the whole mess.

Li Xuanba, lying in bed, asked Li Yuan with an expressionless face, "Father, I have been ill since the change of seasons. Do you truly intend to drag a sick son from door to door to apologize? If you do this, I fear it will not restore my elder brother's reputation at all."

Li Shimin, for once, showed no regard for his father’s face: "Father, are you just venting your anger on Ah Xuan and me? What did we do wrong? It’s just a small shop. What’s wrong with our sisters using their dowries to play with us? Is it our fault that the soap is so popular? Are you blaming us for being too talented?"

Li Yuan, furious, flicked his sleeves and stormed off.

Li Shimin stuck out his tongue. "I thought Father was going to beat me."

Li Xuanba said, "If you were afraid of a beating, why did you deliberately provoke him? I dare to provoke him only because I am sick."

Li Shimin hopped onto the edge of the bed, dangling his short legs while bracing himself against the frame. "Because I really am angry. It was clearly Eldest Brother’s fault, so why not let him apologize? Even if he just said he was drunk and talking nonsense, or simply denied it entirely. It was only heard by a few drinking buddies; if he had slightly altered the story, would those friends have dared to contradict him?"

Li Xuanba replied, "That is how the aristocratic clans operate. Status is determined by lineage and seniority, and the distribution of resources is already set in stone; their futures are decided from birth. The eldest son of the Duke of Tang cannot be replaced, no matter how mediocre he is. If he lacks personal ability, he must be propped up by others. If we want to extract Eldest Brother from this, someone else must take the blame."

Li Shimin’s mouth turned down. "I was originally sad about Grandmother’s favoritism, but now that she is shouldering the responsibility that should have been Eldest Brother’s, I feel it’s not worth it for her."

Li Xuanba said, "She raised that 'precious grandson' herself, and now she is reaping what she sowed. If you pity her, she would only resent you for standing in his way. Do you think the idea of dragging us to apologize was Father’s? Father still treats his sons equally for now."

Li Shimin squinted in thought, then slapped his thighs hard, angry. "You’re right! You’re still sick! If Father takes a sick son to apologize, wouldn't it get out that Father is uncharitable? So Father is also taking the blame for Eldest Brother!"

Li Xuanba glanced at the shadow by the window and said, "Indeed. I don't understand it. Father is the Duke of Tang; his career and reputation are what matter most. It seems as if Eldest Brother is the Duke of Tang instead."

Li Shimin nodded repeatedly. "Exactly! Clearly, Father is the Duke of Tang... Sigh, I should call him *Yeye* (Father). I was so angry I wanted to stop calling him *Yeye*, but thinking about it now, *Yeye* is quite pitiful. Once he has a grandson, his own sons are nothing but weeds."

Li Shimin sighed heavily.

Li Xuanba almost burst out laughing.

He was certain his Second Brother hadn't noticed Li Yuan eavesdropping at the window. Those words were truly from the bottom of his heart.

*Weeds, he says. Second Brother, your art of conversation is truly impressive.*

Li Yuan was so angered by his two sons' words that he couldn't even eat.

Lady Dou ignored Li Yuan and ate her meal in silence.

When Lady Dou had nearly finished, Li Yuan asked aggrievedly, "Aren't you going to ask why I'm angry?"

Lady Dou replied with a straight face, "Why don't you ask why I am angry?"

Li Yuan: "..."

Li Yuan sighed helplessly. "Of course, I couldn't possibly take the sick Da De to apologize to people. I was just putting on a show to appease Mother. Since Mother made such a great sacrifice, I had to comfort her."

Lady Dou said, "You could have taken Da Lang (Jiancheng) to apologize."

Li Yuan said, "I wanted to, but Mother absolutely forbade it, saying the future Duke of Tang cannot have a blemish on his record."

Lady Dou said, "Stubbornly refusing to admit fault and letting his grandmother and younger brother take the blame—is that not a greater blemish? Furthermore, if the future Duke of Tang cannot have a blemish, can the current one?"

Li Yuan sighed. "That is exactly why I am angry. Do you know what that brat Da Xiong (Shimin) was saying? He said that ever since Grandmother got a grandson, I, her son, have become a weed!"

Lady Dou almost lost her composure.

She pinched her palm to keep from laughing. "Everyone is indeed too indulgent toward Da Lang. She is clearly very strict with you, my lord."

Li Yuan said, "Perhaps it is because Mother is getting old, or perhaps because the situation of the Duke of Tang’s estate has improved. It is common among the people for mothers to be strict with their sons but infinitely indulgent toward their grandsons."

Lady Dou thought of the inner courtyards of the capital’s nobility and sighed. "That is true. Perhaps you and I will be just as muddled when we are old. As for the in-laws, we will go apologize ourselves to give them enough face; they won't say anything more. There is no need to pay attention to the other nobles. As long as you, my lord, are restored to your post and regain the Emperor's favor, they will naturally shut their mouths."

Li Yuan said, "The only thing that matters now is regaining the Emperor's favor."

Lady Dou said, "The Emperor loves hunting falcons and fine horses. Last time you presented them, he was very pleased. It would be best to frame this as a minor family matter. You should send the Emperor more falcons and horses. In my dowry, there is a Fire Pearl..."

A complex look flashed in Lady Dou’s eyes. "When Empress Wenxian bestowed upon me the dowry my uncle had saved for me, she joked that she almost couldn't bear to part with this Fire Pearl. The Emperor was present at the time."

Li Yuan was puzzled. "You have such a treasure in your dowry? But since Empress Wenxian said that, why didn't you take the opportunity to present it to her to curry favor?"

Lady Dou: "..."

A flawless smile appeared on her face. "Since Empress Wenxian joked with me like that, it was to show her own magnanimity. If I had taken the opportunity to present the treasure, wouldn't that have made her appear lacking in virtue? Besides, such a rare treasure—I couldn't bear to part with it either."

Li Yuan nodded. "True. Aunt had noble character; even if you had offered it, she wouldn't have accepted. Sigh, I truly hate bribing the Emperor. But for the sake of my unpromising son, I must set aside my pride. Children are nothing but debts."

Lady Dou comforted him, "After this lesson, Da Lang will surely grow."

Li Yuan said, "I will teach him personally from now on! Mother won't be able to say anything then! Find the Fire Pearl for me. Zhangsun Jisheng has also returned to the capital with the Emperor. He knows the Turks best; I will ask him if there is a way to buy good Turkish horses quickly."

Seeing Li Yuan rise, Lady Dou hurriedly stopped him. "My lord, eat your meal first. You can't go to General Zhangsun’s house to beg for a meal, can you?"

Li Yuan gave a wry smile. "True."

He buried his head in his food, complaining despite the rule of silence while eating: "Just as Er Lang and San Lang said, Da Lang is the one who acts like our Duke of Tang, and I, the old Duke, have to serve as his footstool. Sigh, children are debts."

Lady Dou listened quietly. After Li Yuan finished his meal and left, she rose and went to the storeroom where her dowry was kept to retrieve the Fire Pearl.

Hearing that their father had left, Li Shimin dug Li Xuanba—who was actually mostly recovered—out from under the covers and dragged him off to play with their mother.

"Ah? Mother’s dowry? I want to see too!" Li Shimin jumped around, dragging a stumbling Li Xuanba along with him.

Lady Dou protected the box in her arms, laughing and scolding, "Careful! If you break the Fire Pearl, even selling you wouldn't be enough to pay for it!"

Li Shimin stood on tiptoe to peek into her arms. "What Fire Pearl? Let me see! Ah Xuan, do you know what a Fire Pearl is?"

Li Xuanba finally shook off his Second Brother’s hand, feeling as if he had finally released the leash on a sled dog.

He slowly stretched his sore arm and said languidly, "I know. A Fire Pearl is a crystal ball. It is the same mineral as the crystal cup you played with before. But making a crystal ball requires a pure, natural, large piece of crystal, which is extremely rare. Even among the tributes from the Western Regions, it is a rarity."

Lady Dou was surprised. It was the first time she had learned that a Fire Pearl was the same mineral as crystal.

Li Shimin was puzzled. "Crystal is called crystal because it looks like ice, so why is a crystal ball called a Fire Pearl?"

Li Xuanba said, "First, precious crystal balls are often 'hair crystals'—transparent spheres containing metallic, hair-like minerals that flash with dazzling light in the sun, as if flames are burning inside. Second, the principle of a convex lens: a crystal ball can concentrate sunlight into a single point, igniting flammable materials like paper or dry grass. The *Mozi* contains a detailed description of this."

Li Shimin stroked his chin, tilting his head. "I haven't read the *Mozi* yet; it sounds interesting. Ah Xuan, lend me your *Mozi* with your study notes."

Li Xuanba said, "Fine, but you probably won't understand it."

Li Shimin put his hands on his hips. "Hmph! Don't look down on me!"

Li Xuanba curled his lip in a mocking arc.

*Although I only finished high school, the physics knowledge I possess is not something you, a mere Emperor Taizong, could grasp. Hmph.*

Li Shimin tugged on Lady Dou’s sleeve. "Mother! Look! Ah Xuan is mocking me! This younger brother is too hateful, mocking his older brother. Mother, punish him by making him copy books!"

Lady Dou smiled and changed the subject. "Do you want to see what a real Fire Pearl looks like?"

Li Shimin beamed. "Yes!"

Lady Dou took the Fire Pearl into the courtyard.

The early winter sun was still warm and bright.

Lady Dou carefully took the Fire Pearl from the box, unwrapped the soft silk cloth, and held it up with both hands, facing the brilliant sunlight.

Li Xuanba’s eyes flickered.

Even though he had seen many modern crafts and artificial crystals of perfect purity, the beauty of this natural crystal ball still shocked him.

It was a golden titanium crystal ball. The base was a pale, tea-colored crystal with extremely high transparency, and inside were golden-yellow, plate-like titanium filaments that looked like golden grass.

As Lady Dou held the sphere, the titanium filaments reflected a dazzling golden light, making the tea-colored base glow with a faint golden radiance, as if she were holding a glowing little sun in her palms.

Seeing this, Li Xuanba understood why the ancients called it a "Fire Pearl."

Li Shimin’s eyes widened, his pupils reflecting the dazzling golden light of the titanium crystal ball, as if he were mesmerized by its brilliance.

When Lady Dou covered the sphere back up with the silk, Li Shimin’s expression was clearly disappointed.

"It’s so beautiful," Li Shimin said. "Mother, why don't you display it... Ah? Mother, why are you crying?"

The brilliant light of the titanium crystal ball faded from Li Shimin’s eyes, and he hurriedly stood on tiptoe to wipe his mother’s tears.

Li Xuanba stepped forward, then retreated half a step, watching silently as his Second Brother wiped their mother’s tears.

Lady Dou smiled through her tears. "It’s nothing, just remembering some things from the past."

Li Shimin pouted. "Forget the unhappy things! *Hoo... hoo...* I’ll blow away all the unhappy things for you!"

Lady Dou shook her head. "It’s not unhappy."

She stroked the crystal ball in her hands. "This Fire Pearl was one of the treasures my uncle loved. When I was a child, I often watched him play with it. I never expected he would put it into the dowry he saved for me."

Lady Dou had never dared to take the Fire Pearl out. Whenever she did, the brilliant light seemed to reflect the scene of her younger self, chin in hand, watching her uncle roll the pearl around. That was why Li Yuan had never seen this treasure in her dowry.

Empress Wenxian had indeed felt pity for the young Lady Dou. Knowing her dowry contained too many rare treasures, she had hidden some on the public list and handed the true list to Lady Dou privately.

Lady Dou knew intellectually that she should be grateful for this protection, but she found it hard to feel genuine gratitude.

And now, she had to use this treasure, which her uncle had once played with, to exchange for her family’s safety.

Li Yuan only thought the Emperor was angry for a moment, but Lady Dou had keenly sensed the Emperor’s suspicion, jealousy, and cruelty.

Lady Dou knew the Emperor hadn't yet reached the point of being overly suspicious of the Duke of Tang’s estate, but small things could accumulate into a death warrant. Therefore, she had to smooth this matter over completely.

Empress Wenxian had been very fond of the current Emperor, Yang Guang, and had kept him by her side when reviewing Lady Dou’s dowry.

Yang Guang had high standards and a proud nature; while he loved treasures, he wouldn't have coveted the dowry of a girl destined to be an orphan. Yet, when this Fire Pearl appeared, an expression of wonder and heartache had crossed his face.

Lady Dou believed the Emperor would surely remember this pearl.

She wiped her tears and suppressed her memories.

She smiled. "Mother is fine now. Do you want to see it again? I’ll have someone bring a stand, and you can look at it to your heart’s content today."

Li Shimin was the first to cheer. "Yes!"

Then he scratched his head. "If it makes Mother sad, then don't. Let’s not look, there’s nothing to see, right, Ah Xuan?"

Li Xuanba nodded. "Right."

Lady Dou smiled. "I’m not sad anymore. Er Lang, go bring Si Lang and Wu Lang; we will look at the Fire Pearl together."

Li Shimin nodded.

After Li Shimin left, Lady Dou had a maid invite Li Jiancheng.

Lady Dou held the box in one arm and led Li Xuanba with the other, walking toward the pavilion in the courtyard.

Once seated, Lady Dou placed the box on the stone table and looked at the silent Li Xuanba. "Da De, do you dislike your Grandmother and Father?"

Li Xuanba raised his eyelids and bowed. "No. Mother, I am not unfilial."

Lady Dou sighed. "Your Grandmother and Father love you, too."

Li Xuanba said, "I know. I have always been good to Grandmother and Father. Why do you say that, Mother?"

Lady Dou pursed her lips and shook her head. "Never mind. Forget I said anything."

She beckoned to Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba said, "My cough hasn't healed yet..."

Lady Dou said, "Come here."

Li Xuanba had no choice but to walk to his mother’s side and be rubbed by her.

His eyes were full of helplessness. *There isn't much meat on my face, Mother; go rub Second Brother instead.*

Only after Lady Dou had rubbed Li Xuanba’s face red did she let out a long sigh.

She flicked Li Xuanba’s forehead.

Li Xuanba covered his forehead. "Ouch."

Lady Dou finally smiled. "Enough. Although you are deep in thought, you are also very lazy. If others don't scheme against you, you wouldn't bother scheming against them. But you are still young, don't think too much. Your body is weak; thinking too much won't help you recover. You’re already half a head shorter than Er Lang. Be careful, or one day people will think you are Er Lang’s son when you walk together."

Li Xuanba’s eyes widened as he gasped, showing an expression of disbelief before his mother for the first time. "How is that possible!"

Lady Dou couldn't help but laugh and flicked his forehead again.

Li Xuanba covered his forehead, his calm expression finally cracking.

Lady Dou flicked him again.

Li Xuanba turned around, presenting the back of his head to his mother.

Lady Dou flicked his bald head.

Li Xuanba ground his teeth, twitched, and hid under the table, hugging his head.

As soon as he crouched down, his face grew hot, realizing how stupid he looked.

Lady Dou laughed until she was doubled over.

Li Xuanba crawled out from under the table, keeping his distance from his mother.

Lady Dou beckoned to him. "Come here."

Li Xuanba dragged his feet, and when she called again, he moved over with a bitter face.

Sure enough, Lady Dou began rubbing his face again.

Li Xuanba felt lifeless, screaming for help in his heart.

Li Shimin had just stepped into the range of his inner voice and was stunned by Li Xuanba’s frantic cries for "help," covering his ears.

Unfortunately, covering his ears was useless.

Fortunately, the arrival of his younger brothers saved Li Xuanba from being treated like a giant toy by their mother.

Li Xuanba immediately hid behind Li Shimin, who had spread his arms to protect his younger brothers like a mother hen.

Li Shimin sighed deeply. "Mother, don't bully Ah Xuan; he isn't fully recovered yet. When he is, I’ll hand him over to you to play with as much as you want."

Li Xuanba, furious, kicked his Second Brother’s butt.

Li Shimin stumbled, clutching his rear. "Ouch."

"Hahahaha!" Li Yuanji clapped and laughed, his teeth bared.

Li Zhiyun was startled by Li Yuanji’s sudden laughter, hesitating whether to join in. But he couldn't bring himself to laugh.

A moment later, Li Jiancheng arrived with a dark face.

He bowed stiffly, his voice muffled. "Mother, I am busy reading and have no time to play with my younger brothers."

Lady Dou said nothing, opened the box, and placed the crystal ball on the stand.

The brilliant golden light instantly captured everyone’s gaze. Even Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, who had seen it once already, couldn't help but be drawn in by the beautiful sphere again.

"Is this... is this the legendary treasure, the Fire Pearl?" Li Jiancheng murmured, involuntarily stepping forward to touch the beautiful object.

Lady Dou handed the pearl to Li Jiancheng.

Li Jiancheng played with it cautiously for a while.

The pearl felt warm and smooth in his hand, but fearing he might drop it, he quickly placed it back on the stand.

Lady Dou said, "Everyone, come and touch it."

Even the mischievous Li Yuanji touched the pearl with great care.

Children are actually very smart; they know they will be punished if they break something. When their parents are watching, they are usually very well-behaved.

Li Xuanba also gave it a touch.

*It’s just crystal, nothing special.* Li Xuanba mused that once he made money, he would buy a large piece of raw crystal and carve his own beads to play with.

When the sun shifted and no longer shone into the pavilion, Lady Dou put the pearl away.

"Tomorrow I will let the ladies of the estate see it," Lady Dou sighed. "In a few days, this Fire Pearl will no longer belong to the Duke of Tang’s estate."

Everyone was confused, except for Li Xuanba, who frowned, realizing what was happening.

Lady Dou looked Li Jiancheng in the eyes. "Da Lang, I originally intended for this pearl to be passed to your future wife."

Li Jiancheng clenched his fists, his voice low. "Then who does Mother intend to give it to now?!"

Lady Dou said calmly, "Now, I am going to present it to the Emperor, to request that he restore your official position."

Li Jiancheng’s eyes widened.

Lady Dou said, "Your Grandmother told you from the moment you could understand that the Duke of Tang’s estate was yours, that everything was yours. Because of this, you became arrogant, thinking you were the center of the world and that everything would go your way. But Bishamen, even your father, the current Duke of Tang, cannot say he can do whatever he pleases."

Li Jiancheng lowered his head, his fists clenching tighter.

Lady Dou continued, "It is true that whether you are capable or not, the title of Duke of Tang is yours. Your father became the Duke of Tang at only seven years old. But do you know how hard life was for him while your Grandmother protected him?"

Li Jiancheng said, "I know..."

Lady Dou rebuked him, "No! You don't! If you did, you wouldn't have gotten drunk and spoken nonsense! How many years did your father wait before he was summoned to court? When the estate was thriving, how many of those sycophants around you truly wished for its prosperity? How many were just waiting to find a fault?"

"Yes, no matter what, the estate will be yours. But if you are incompetent, what will be left? An empty title? Even a title can be easily stripped away if the Emperor is displeased!"

"Your grandfather fought through countless battles to preserve this title. Your father will also have to fight for his life in the future to ensure that when the title reaches you, it is still the 'Duke of Tang'."

"Your younger brothers can afford to be careless, they can even be incompetent playboys, but you cannot! Because if you cannot shoulder the burden of the Duke of Tang, there will be no Duke of Tang left in this world! Do you understand!"

Li Jiancheng knelt, shedding tears of genuine repentance for the first time. "It is my fault. I know I was wrong. I was not cautious."

Lady Dou’s tone softened. "I know you feel aggrieved, thinking that since you didn't start this, you shouldn't be blamed. But you are the Duke of Tang. Whether it is your elders or those around you, they are only there to offer advice. You are the one who makes the decisions. In the future, only you can make decisions for this estate. So you must learn to take responsibility now."

She rose and helped Li Jiancheng up, saying earnestly, "Get up. Take one last good look at this Fire Pearl and keep it in your heart. Remember that this should have been yours, but now it is not."

Li Jiancheng wept, "Yes, I will remember."

Lady Dugu, hearing of the matter, worried that Lady Dou was being too harsh, and despite her own poor health, she came over trembling to intervene.

Seeing Lady Dou merely playing with the children, she was about to leave when she witnessed this scene.

She sighed deeply, remembering the hardships of the past.

Lady Dugu shook her head and left silently.

Back in her room, she held Zhang Po’s hand, her eyes clouded with tears. "Did I truly do wrong? Did I spoil Da Lang too much?"

Zhang Po comforted her, "The young master is still a child; it is normal for him to be immature. Once he marries and has children, he will naturally mature."

Lady Dugu wiped her tears. "True. I hope Zheng Yi gives birth to a child for Da Lang soon. Once he has a child, he will surely mature."

Zhang Po brought warm water to wipe Lady Dugu’s tear-stained face.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第35章 母亲的嫁妆火珠 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
她嘴里虽然这样安慰老夫人，心中却不以为然。

那日李建成推老夫人的时候，张婆差点气得扑上去厮打李建成。

在她看来，老夫人年老得病之后，确实处事失之偏颇。

但唯独李建成，没有资格说老夫人不是，因为老夫人偏爱的就是他啊！

若老夫人偏爱的是二郎三郎多好，那两个孩子多可爱多贴心啊。可惜大郎君被老夫人亲自教养了十几年，偏爱得唐国公都要靠后了。

其实张婆总觉得，老夫人如此纵容宠溺大郎君，也有曾经为了让唐国公尽快成长，所以对唐国公太过严格，心中一直有遗憾，所以将一腔母爱投注在大郎君身上的缘故。

可惜，慈母多败儿。

……

“你说的可是真的？”郑氏手一抖，指甲涂歪了。

跪着的女婢道：“应该是真的。大力一直心悦奴，连奴让他帮我们厨房砍柴，他都傻呵呵地照做，丝毫不像个唐国公府的家生子。大力其实早几日就告诉奴此事，奴一直不敢相信，打听了一番才确定。”

郑氏叹气：“你该早些来说的。”

女婢磕头：“奴错了。”

郑氏放下染指甲的凤仙水，将这位陪嫁的小丫鬟扶起来。

她自然知道为何这小丫鬟不敢立刻对自己说。一个厨房里的烧火丫头，哪有胆量在自己面前碎嘴？

这烧火丫鬟现在告诉她，大概是担心她事后得知此事后，会迁怒她知情不告。

不过这丫鬟口齿倒是伶俐，找的借口像模像样，当个烧火丫鬟屈才了。

郑氏道：“今后你就跟着显翠学针线活。”

女婢惶恐道：“谢娘子！”

郑氏随手丢给了女婢一颗银豆子当赏钱，然后瘫坐在坐榻的靠背上。

“好，好得很，为你大孙子敛财，却要折损我的名声？”郑氏气得差点咬碎一口银牙，“还好这事没成，否则陛下怪罪下来，怕不是要把我从媵贬成妾了，那我还不如死了算了！”

郑氏摸了摸自己的肚子。为何还没怀上？若怀上了，看那老婆子敢不敢折腾郎君第一个孩子！

还是说，那老婆子就是不想让自己怀上，才故意坏了自己的名声，好让后入门的郎君正室生嫡长子？

郑氏越想越害怕。

当李建成回来的时候，郑氏就对着李建成哭了一场，说才知道老夫人要让她去抢夺家中小郎君的铺子。

“妾虽卑贱，也是荥阳郑氏的女儿，家风不容侮辱，岂能背上贪财污名。”郑氏跪在地上，取下金簪对着自己的脖子道，“若玷污了荥阳郑氏的家风，妾只能以死明志。”

李建成对郑氏正是喜欢的时候，赶紧半跪在地上将郑氏抱住：“你说什么傻话？唉，此事都是我的错……”

郑氏摇头：“虽妾不该说长辈的坏话，但妾认为郎君无错。郎君只是太信任长辈，在长辈提议时不会过多思索而已。若是换作妾或者任何一人在郎君耳边说这话，郎君都会三思后拒绝。可那是养育郎君长大的祖母，郎君有一丝犹豫，都是对祖母不孝。”

李建成本来已经在反省，被郑氏这么一说，立刻觉得郑氏说得很有道理。

“是啊，我没想那么多，差点连累你了。”李建成将郑氏扶起来，“你放心，以后我绝对三思而后行，不会连累你。”

郑氏低头道：“若为了郎君，妾万死不悔。但唯独门风家教一事，实恕妾无法退让。”

李建成抚摸着郑氏的鬓发道：“你是世家贵女，做我的媵已经是够委屈，有这样的脾气才正常。”

郑氏靠在李建成肩头低泣：“妾为自己难过，也为郎君难过。郎君如此好，却被人误解。这明明不是郎君的错啊。”

李建成轻声安慰着郑氏，想起了那璀璨的火珠，心中不由又对祖母生出了怨愤。

他本来就对商贾之事毫不在意，只是习惯性地顺从祖母而已。他的孝顺，结果反而成了过错。

今日母亲当着众幼弟的面训斥他，也让他在从心疼中清醒后感到了一丝难堪和恼怒。

为何非得当着这么多人的面训斥他？特别是在李世民和李玄霸两人面前训斥他！

郑氏哭完后，道：“郎君，请你告诉老夫人，如果她真的看不上妾，妾宁愿返家，甚至自尽以捍卫家风。”

李建成被郑氏哭得乱了心，道：“好，我去和她说，也叮嘱她以后别再乱来了。都说她偏心我，可她这偏心除了让我更难堪，让外人误以为我不友悌，我何曾得过好处？我什么都不做就能继承爵位，根本不需要她偏心。”

郑氏道：“是这个理，郎君只要不出错就行，越是大度，外人越会说郎君的好。”

李建成安抚好郑氏，气冲冲去找祖母。

祖母一个不过脑子的决定，不仅害得他和父亲丢了官，还让爱妾要自尽以捍卫家风。祖母还是出身鲜卑，太不懂我中原的规矩。荥阳郑氏的贵女，岂是她能随意磋磨的？

……
