Chapter 37: The Old Madam Faints from Anger Again

After the "Fire Pearl Incident," the turmoil within the Duke of Tang’s manor finally subsided.

Li Jiancheng seemed to have truly learned his lesson. He appeared much more composed and was significantly warmer toward Li Xuanba, whom he had previously ignored.

When Li Xuanba made his routine gift deliveries, Li Jiancheng no longer picked them apart; instead, he would specifically send someone to express his gratitude. When going out, he would even occasionally bring back gifts for his younger brothers.

Li Yuan and Old Madam Dugu were both delighted by Li Jiancheng’s growth, and Madam Dou’s worries about her eldest son diminished.

Even Li Shimin, after receiving gifts a few times, remarked to Li Xuanba, "Big Brother is actually a pretty good guy! A brother who knows how to correct his mistakes is a good brother!"

Li Xuanba was utterly speechless.

Previously, his Second Brother had held such deep-seated prejudices against Li Jiancheng. After being treated with kindness for less than half a month and receiving a few gifts, he had already changed his tune to "Big Brother is a good guy"?

Although their relationship with Li Jiancheng had not yet reached the point of open hostility, and the incident had indeed been instigated by Old Madam Dugu with Li Jiancheng merely reacting, wasn't this "forgetting the pain once the wound heals" attitude a bit too naive? Are you a child? Does a little coaxing make you stop being angry?

Oh, right. The future Emperor Taizong of Tang was, at this moment, truly a child who was still two months shy of his eighth birthday.

Li Xuanba silently noted this down.

When he eventually came to write the *Veritable Records of Taizong*, he would start with his brother climbing trees, rolling in the dirt, getting scolded and beaten, and saying, "My brother is actually quite a good person."

Or perhaps he should just write a memoir titled *My Brother, Li Shimin*?

However, Li Xuanba was happy to enjoy the ease brought about by Li Jiancheng’s goodwill.

They had no need for conflict at this stage; wouldn't it be better to live in harmony? Once the Tang Dynasty was established, that would be the time to show their true mettle. Struggling against each other so many years early would only affect their moods, with no real benefit.

Li Xuanba followed the lead of the naive Li Shimin, echoing that "Big Brother is a very good person," and began sending gifts even more frequently.

Beyond giving small, inexpensive tokens, Li Xuanba stopped "disturbing" Li Jiancheng. He also kept a firm grip on Li Shimin, who wanted to go play with his eldest brother, urging him to study hard and improve himself instead of bothering their brother.

"Big Brother has already taken concubines and is working hard to give you a little nephew or niece. Wouldn't it be awkward if you ran into them?" Li Xuanba said with a straight face. "You should be considerate of Big Brother and be a sensible, good younger brother."

Li Shimin pouted, "I always feel like that’s not what you’re really thinking. Sigh, you must still hate Big Brother. Fine, I won’t go."

Li Xuanba wanted to smack his Second Brother. Wasn't it you who hated Big Brother the most? He himself had to offer perfunctory words of praise just to keep his simple-minded Second Brother from offending Big Brother and getting scolded by the Old Madam.

"Hahaha, don't be angry, don't be angry, give me a smile," Li Shimin chirped. "I won't go, I won't go. If you hate him, then I don't like him either. Come on, shall we go find Little Five to play?"

Li Xuanba continued to drag his Second Brother, who was like a sled dog off its leash: "Must you abandon your studies to go play?! Do your homework first!!"

Li Shimin pulled back, dragging Li Xuanba along with him: "There’s still a whole day left! Homework should be done on the very last day! Doing it a day early is a sign of disrespect to the homework!"

Li Xuanba: "..." What kind of twisted logic is that!

"Hmm? Homework should be done on the last day?"

Li Shimin slammed on the brakes, colliding with Madam Dou, who had just arrived to check if they were studying properly.

Li Xuanba couldn't stop in time and smacked his head right into the back of Li Shimin’s skull.

Both children let out an "Ouch!" and crouched down, clutching their heads.

Madam Dou, who had been trying to keep a stern face, almost burst out laughing. She barely managed to hold it in before grabbing her mischievous second son to take him back to do his lessons.

Li Xuanba rubbed his forehead and followed behind, cursing his Second Brother in his heart for the faces he kept making.

Li Shimin pulled down his eyelids with his index fingers and stretched his mouth wide with his thumbs, sticking his tongue out and rolling his eyes, making "bleh-bleh" faces at his younger brother.

Madam Dou looked down. Li Shimin immediately dropped his hands, pulled in his tongue, and assumed a look of innocence.

Madam Dou continued walking. Li Shimin resumed his faces, "bleh-bleh."

Li Xuanba could bear it no longer. He trotted forward, balled his fist, and gave his brother a knock on the head.

Li Shimin immediately tattled: "Mother! Younger Brother hit me!"

Madam Dou took a deep breath, set Li Shimin down, and gave his bottom a firm swat: "Don't bully your younger brother!"

Li Shimin jumped: "He hit me, how is it still me bullying him?!"

Li Xuanba sneered: "Serves you right."

Li Shimin’s eyes darted around. He reached out, yanked a handful of Li Xuanba’s hair, and bolted.

Li Xuanba clutched his messy bird's nest of hair and looked up at his mother, who was taking deep breaths: "Mother, Second Brother is running into the house—isn't he just asking for trouble?"

Madam Dou, who had been genuinely annoyed by her mischievous son, let out a "Pfft." Her anger dissipated, leaving her both amused and exasperated.

"Come, let's go catch him. Today, he must be punished with an extra sheet of calligraphy practice." Madam Dou took Li Xuanba’s hand and went into the house to catch her "trouble-seeking" son.

For once, Li Xuanba showed a bit of childish petulance, looking quite smug with his mother’s backing.

Though he didn't know why his Second Brother loved to court disaster, a good younger brother should help him achieve his goal!

Li Xuanba’s daily routine returned to normal, the only difference being that the soap shop and the bookstore had officially opened for business.

Using his Second Brother’s recent naughtiness as an excuse, Li Xuanba asked their teachers to increase Li Shimin’s martial arts training to burn off his excess energy, ensuring he wouldn't be involved in the business.

As for martial arts, Li Xuanba had already given up on it himself. He only learned to ride a horse—as long as he could get around, that was enough.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi should have disapproved of their disciples engaging in merchant activities. Li Xuanba had already prepared a speech to persuade them, but it turned out to be unnecessary. Both teachers agreed without hesitation. As long as Li Xuanba could complete his assigned lessons, they allowed him to manage his time as he pleased.

Li Shimin shouted that it was unfair.

Yuwen Bi sneered: "Don't want to increase your time practicing archery and horsemanship? This time, I’ll teach you actual hunting. If you can pass the assessment, I will ask the Crown Prince to allow you to play in the Royal Hunting Grounds."

Li Shimin immediately stood at attention and shouted even louder than before: "I’ll do it! I love martial arts!"

Gao Jiong covered his forehead: "You really do change your tune quickly."

Li Shimin laughed, feeling no shame but rather pride in his "He-he" laughter.

Yuwen Bi and Gao Jiong hadn't intended to laugh, but looking at Li Shimin’s deliberately silly grin, they couldn't help themselves.

Li Xuanba made them feel both reassured and worried, while Li Shimin truly made them happy.

Although Yu Shiji, their calligraphy teacher, had little presence—Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi even ignored the fact that their disciples had another teacher—Li Xuanba also dragged his Second Brother to see Yu Shinan. He asked Yu Shinan to assign more homework to his increasingly restless brother to help him cultivate his character.

What kind of teacher is a calligraphy teacher? Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi looked down on Yu Shinan, who was a generation younger than them.

Yu Shinan, who was currently in mourning, pretended he didn't exist, silently teaching Li Xuanba and Li Shimin calligraphy without wasting words.

His brother, Yu Shiji, who was also in mourning, had warned him that even if Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi had retreated from the court to compile books, the Emperor still loathed them and might strike at any moment. For the sake of the Yu family’s safety, he hoped Yu Shinan would not associate too deeply with them.

Yu Shinan silently complied, but he continued to teach Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Yu Shiji had originally hoped that Yu Shinan would use the mourning period to cut ties with the two boys to completely distance himself from Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, but this time, Yu Shinan silently refused.

Later, seeing that the Emperor truly favored his two grand-nephews, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Yu Shiji stopped interfering.

Yu Shinan was usually expressionless, his eyes as calm as a deep pool. Only when he saw his disciples would he show a faint smile.

Yu Shinan’s wife particularly loved it when Li Shimin and Li Xuanba visited, as that was the only time Yu Shinan showed any signs of being a living, breathing person.

After hearing Li Xuanba’s request, Yu Shinan understood something. He had his wife take Li Shimin to the kitchen for pastries and said to Li Xuanba, "You don't want your Second Brother to get involved in merchant affairs?"

Li Xuanba nodded: "Yes."

Yu Shinan sighed: "You shouldn't get too involved either."

Li Xuanba said: "My Second Brother and I will certainly be short of money in the future. I don't care about my reputation. Besides, with this body of mine, it will surely be difficult to enter officialdom. The energy required to be an official is far greater than lying at home and letting managers help make money."

Yu Shinan gently rubbed the head of his precocious disciple: "The energy you spend maneuvering in front of the Emperor is not small, either."

Li Xuanba said: "The Emperor will leave the capital next spring, so I won't spend much more energy on that. However, before he leaves, he will hold an imperial examination to recruit talent from across the land. I intend to participate. Could you guide me on my policy essays?"

Yu Shinan was puzzled: "Why not ask Duke Gao or Duke Yuwen?"

Li Xuanba said helplessly: "I suspect Duke Gao and Duke Yuwen cannot grasp the Emperor’s psychology."

Yu Shinan said gloomily: "I do not know the Emperor’s psychology either."

Li Xuanba said: "It would still be better than Duke Gao and Duke Yuwen. I hope you won't despise me for being a sycophant to the Emperor."

Yu Shinan shook his head: "How can showing talent to a monarch be called sycophancy? Though I am untalented, I can offer you some guidance. Your calligraphy already has its own spirit; you no longer need to trace. I will assign you policy essays as your calligraphy homework."

Li Xuanba immediately bowed: "Thank you, Teacher."

He knew Mr. Yu was being modest.

Both Yu Shiji and Yu Shinan were gifted at guessing the monarch’s mind. The difference between the brothers was that Yu Shiji chose to cater to it, while Yu Shinan chose silence when he found the monarch’s pursuits misaligned with his own.

So, it wasn't that Yu Shinan didn't know Yang Guang’s psychology or how to please him; he simply didn't want to.

But Yu Shinan would not impose his own persistence on his disciples. Moreover, he believed his judgment of character was sharp, and Li Xuanba did not seem like a sycophant.

When Li Shimin returned with a basket of pastries, Yu Shinan had already assessed Li Xuanba’s foundation in writing.

Li Xuanba had a mind full of brilliance, but his prose lacked literary flair and he wasn't skilled in parallel prose.

Qualified parallel prose could be learned through rote memorization. Since he wasn't writing a masterpiece for the ages, just memorizing and writing more would suffice. The difficulty lay in having substance.

Yu Shinan was very satisfied with Li Xuanba.

Although it was a bit early for an eight-year-old to take the imperial examination, and he wouldn't be appointed to office even if he passed, the exam was a chance to spar with scholars from humble backgrounds across the empire. Since his disciple had such ambition, he would naturally support him.

Originally, Yu Shinan thought Li Xuanba was just going to see the world, but if Li Xuanba could articulate his thoughts, he might not just be a one-round participant.

Li Shimin stuffed a pastry into his brother’s mouth, nearly choking him: "Ah Xuan, this is delicious. Teacher’s wife gave us a whole basket!"

Li Xuanba chewed with difficulty, his cheeks bulging: *[Teacher lives a frugal life, and you’re eating his food and taking more? Aren't you ashamed?]*

Li Shimin blinked.

Teacher lives a frugal life? Then they could just send him more gifts during the holidays. But the delicious food had to be taken! Those were two different things!

Not only did he not return it, but he also stuffed a pastry into Yu Shinan’s son, Yu Chang’s, mouth.

Yu Chang was a year younger than Li Shimin and had already become his little follower. He held the pastry and followed behind Li Shimin, nibbling away respectfully, completely forgetting that these pastries were from his own home, and feeling very grateful to his "boss."

Seeing this, Yu Shinan couldn't help but sigh.

Actually, he had previously thought his own son was decent. But after having Li Shimin and Li Xuanba as disciples, it was truly a case of "comparisons are odious."

Li Xuanba wiped his mouth and finally swallowed the pastry.

He pulled out a scroll and handed it to Yu Chang: "This is an introductory book my Second Brother and I used. See if Brother Chang finds it useful."

Yu Chang’s face fell. Children of this age didn't like reading. For him, just starting his education, reading was a nightmare.

But after opening the book and seeing the exquisite illustrations, he immediately raised the corners of his mouth and chirped: "Thank you, Third Brother Li!"

Yu Shinan sighed again.

It was so difficult to even get his own son to start learning, and he didn't even love to read—truly, comparisons are odious.

After dealing a small blow to Yu Shinan’s confidence as a father, Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, who wouldn't let go of the pastries, went to find Li Zhao and Chai Shao.

Li Xuanba had already written the business plan for the soap shop. Since he would be busy preparing for the exams and couldn't often show his face, he entrusted everything to his elder sister.

Although Li Zhao had married Chai Shao, she was currently just like another daughter in the Chai household, learning how to be a mistress, and had not yet consummated the marriage with Chai Shao. Thus, Li Xuanba didn't have to worry about disturbing them.

For noble families, the birth of a legitimate eldest son was of paramount importance. Before that happened, the maternal family kept a close watch on their daughter’s safety, fearing something might go wrong.

Therefore, although noble daughters were betrothed at six or seven and married at thirteen or fourteen, they generally didn't consummate the marriage until sixteen, and the first child usually arrived around eighteen.

This was the case for both Madam Dou and the future Empress Zhangsun.

Before that, noble brides usually brought along maidservants specifically to fulfill the husband’s needs. The two families would agree that if the maid became pregnant with a boy, the child would be aborted or drowned, and if it were a girl, she would be raised.

There were also a few families, like Li Jiancheng’s, where the in-laws would first send a concubine of the same clan, implicitly allowing a male heir to be kept, or like Chai Shao, who didn't sleep with the maidservants and enjoyed a "pure, romantic courtship" with his wife.

After Li Zhao married, Li Shimin didn't like coming to the Chai manor because Chai Shao’s smiles were truly an eyesore.

While Li Xuanba discussed the follow-up matters of the soap shop with Li Zhao, Li Shimin insisted on competing with Chai Shao to see who was the better archer, just to win a moment of pride.

Chai Shao could only leave, looking back every few steps.

Li Xuanba was helpless: "Doesn't Brother-in-law Chai have to be on duty?"

Li Zhao covered her forehead and smiled bitterly: "He specifically asked for leave. His Highness the Crown Prince is generous and granted it."

Li Xuanba was speechless. Chai Shao and his sister had been married for half a year; how much leave had he actually taken? Or was it not continuous, but rather asking for leave every few days to come home and accompany his new wife? It was thanks to the Crown Prince’s benevolence that he was so indulgent.

Li Xuanba changed the subject, not wanting to talk about his lovesick brother-in-law.

It was amazing that his brother-in-law’s parents actually indulged their son’s "lack of ambition."

"When selling the soap, we must categorize it. Not every customer will be able to buy it. The soap of the same quality as the tribute will be one grade lower than the actual tribute, available only for purchase by noble and official families."

Li Xuanba laid out his tiered VIP system.

Tiering, limited quantities, pre-orders, blind boxes. The four great treasures of training customers for a viral shop.

Most noble families had their own workshops and were self-sufficient, rarely buying things outside.

Li Xuanba’s news of "tribute-grade" soap could attract them to try it, but nobles were naturally distrustful of outside goods, believing that buying things in shops was beneath their status, so they rarely shopped in bulk.

Although their status was different from the customers of a "custom shop," their psychology—being few in number, not short of money, and hoping to be treated specially—was the same.

At this time, the shop needed to "set the rules" for the customers. The more "rules" there were, the more the customers felt their purchase was worth it—they weren't buying a product, but a qualification to "enter the circle."

After Li Xuanba had "retired" from his previous life, the owner of the online shop he once knew had told him he hadn't caught the right era. Now, "custom goods" rode the wave of fandom, making them easier to sell. Even if customers were scammed by runaway sellers countless times, they would still obediently pay months in advance without needing any guarantees, just waiting; if they didn't wait, they would be mocked by the circle.

Li Xuanba was now applying this newly learned "knowledge" to the Great Sui.

"The soap in the West Market won't have a fixed quantity, but we will issue VIP cards. Besides an entry fee, the cards will implement a stored-value tier system. For example, storing one thousand coins makes you a C-tier member, allowing you to pre-order certain functional soaps. Once the stored value is used up, you must top up the required amount to continue enjoying the corresponding VIP treatment."

"The East Market will implement a membership system. Any official can enter for free, with VIP tiers based on rank and title. 'VIP Skin Care Sets' will be released in limited quantities, available for all members to purchase; different tiers of VIPs will have pre-order quotas, allowing them to pay in full one month in advance for the skin care products they want. The Emperor has already permitted officials of the third rank and above, as well as Commandery Dukes and State Dukes, to use the cold-process soap tribute he uses."

"VIPs will have exclusive service staff. During holidays, there will be gifts; every month, each tier of VIP will have exclusive activities, such as limited-edition free trial sets of new products, and various seasonal blind boxes..."

Li Zhao looked at the plan Li Xuanba had written and listened to his detailed explanation, her eyes spinning: "Slow down, slow down, Sister doesn't understand."

Li Xuanba took a sip of warm water and gave his sister detailed examples.

Li Xuanba talked until his throat was dry, drank a pot of water, and took a trip to the latrine before Li Zhao finally managed to understand.

Li Zhao rubbed her younger brother’s small head: "Ah, Da De, why do you have so many strange ideas?"

Li Xuanba said expressionlessly: "I read a lot of books. These ideas were all used by wealthy merchants in the past, especially during the Wei and Jin dynasties, where wealthy merchants were numerous and various marketing methods emerged one after another." Anyway, blaming it on the ancients was easy; he didn't believe anyone would check.

Li Zhao didn't doubt Li Xuanba.

The Jin Dynasty was a bizarre era, extravagant from top to bottom, with many wealthy merchants. The fortune of Shi Chong, the richest man during the reign of Emperor Wu of Jin, came from robbing passing wealthy merchants while he was the Inspector of Jingzhou.

Li Zhao said: "You must not let your character change for the sake of money."

Li Xuanba shook his head: "A gentleman loves wealth but acquires it in the right way. I believe that earning money from the wealthy is more 'right' than collecting rent from the poor. Money acquired in the right way will not change one’s character."

Li Zhao always felt something was wrong.

According to worldly logic, collecting rent was the proper way to acquire wealth, while being a merchant was not. But Li Xuanba’s twisted logic actually made it hard for her to refute.

Li Zhao could only smile bitterly: "Our Da De truly has virtue; you have the heart of a Buddha or a saint."

Li Xuanba’s mouth twitched: "Why do I feel like Sister is scolding me?"

Li Zhao tapped Li Xuanba’s forehead: "Sister is not. I am genuinely praising you."

Li Xuanba changed the subject: "Madam Gao’s shops are all in the West Market, and she wants to do business there. She also wants to open a shop to sell cheaper soap, making small profits but quick turnover. Soap is just soap without fragrance. This shop can produce soap on-site, letting the world know that the soap recipe we posted is real."

Li Zhao was curious: "Why make the recipe public?"

Li Xuanba smiled: "If we don't make the recipe public, how can we let others imitate us? If we don't let others imitate us, how can we get people to help us promote it for free? Only when more people use soap will our soap be snatched up like crazy."

Li Zhao said: "If they sell it cheaper than us, won't our customers be snatched away?"

Li Xuanba shook his head: "No. The value of an item lies not only in the material but also in its reputation, just like a person’s reputation. Our soap is a tribute. Precisely because we published the recipe, they will think we have an even greater secret. If they lower their prices, they will be even less able to compete with us."

Li Zhao was half-understanding.

Li Xuanba said: "Sister, if you had your eye on a particularly precious and rare piece of jewelry, and there were two shops that looked about the same, with a price difference of one hundred coins, would you buy from the expensive one or the cheap one?"

Li Zhao immediately said: "Greed for small gains leads to big losses, I’m not short of that little money... Ah, I understand."

She covered her mouth and laughed: "I hope they lower their prices significantly."

The siblings looked at each other and smiled cunningly.

Let them lower their prices. Not only would they not lower theirs, but they would also raise prices or take them off the shelves entirely depending on the season.

Li Xuanba and Li Zhao reached a consensus, and Li Shimin also returned, dejected after losing.

Li Shimin complained to Li Xuanba, but Li Xuanba didn't want to comfort his Second Brother.

You and Chai Shao have such a large age gap, how could you be so confident you could win against Chai Shao!

Sometimes Li Xuanba really didn't know why his Second Brother’s self-confidence was so inflated; it was as if his whole body was made of self-confidence.

"Next time I’ll definitely win!" Li Shimin clenched his fists and swore, flexing his arms.

Li Xuanba gave a perfunctory "Oh" and closed his eyes to rest.

Li Shimin covered his mouth and let out a huge yawn. Archery was physical labor, and he was tired too.

"Ah Xuan, move over."

"The carriage is so spacious, don't crowd me."

"Leaning against the carriage door is uncomfortable, be my pillow."

"Get lost!"

"I’ll be your pillow too, just move over!"

Li Shimin squeezed Li Xuanba aside without further ado.

Li Xuanba was too sleepy to move. So, the two children fell asleep with their heads leaning against each other.

When the wet nurses carried them off the carriage, they still hadn't woken up.

Li Siniang and Li Wuniang were waiting at the carriage stop and told the wet nurses to take a different path back to the courtyard.

Li Siniang whispered: "The back courtyard is causing a scene again, don't run into them."

Li Wuniang reached out and helped the wet nurse carry Li Xuanba: "The courtyard of the Second and Third Brothers is very close to the eldest brother’s. Let’s hide in our courtyard first and go back after the commotion is over."

The wet nurse was puzzled: "Is it that serious? Shouldn't we wake up the Second and Third Young Masters?"

Li Siniang shook her head: "If the Second and Third Brothers go, they might be caught in the crossfire. Let’s hide first."

Siniang and Wuniang also had their own plans. Plus, ever since they had received some dividends from the soap shop with their own pocket money, they had been thinking well of the Second and Third Brothers, so the wet nurse trusted them.

Li Shimin lay in the wet nurse’s arms, Li Wuniang held Li Xuanba steadily, and Li Siniang led the way, taking a wide detour before returning to the small courtyard where Siniang and Wuniang lived. Along the way, Li Siniang and Li Wuniang took turns carrying Li Xuanba for a stretch.

When the servants accompanying Li Shimin and Li Xuanba wanted to carry Li Xuanba, both young ladies shook their heads.

The wet nurse felt helpless. It was clear that both young ladies were overly fond of their Third Young Master.

They arrived at Li Siniang and Li Wuniang’s courtyard. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba slept on the same couch, but Siniang and Wuniang only pointed at Li Xuanba, laughing softly about how cute the Third Brother’s sleeping face was.

Li Siniang said: "Only the Third Sister can control the impulsive Second Brother; the Third Brother is still the most lovable."

Li Wuniang nodded.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第37章 老夫人再次气晕 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
李玄霸睡眠浅，其实在下马车的时候就已经醒过来，只是懒得睁开眼睛。

听到姐姐们让他绕路时，他就更不好醒来，只能继续装睡。

现在听到姐姐们的窃窃私语，李玄霸尴尬得差点装不下去。

他和四姐、五姐其实并不亲近。大隋的后院虽然没有后世男女七岁不同席的规矩，但李四娘和李五娘和李世民、李玄霸非同母，能见面的时间很少，感情无从谈起。

李玄霸只是礼节性地送礼时不忘捎带四姐五姐一份而已。落到两个姐姐嘴里，就夸张成了李玄霸对她们极好极亲近。

这次老夫人那里又闹起来，还闹得很厉害。两位姐姐居然“冒险”来门口等李世民和李玄霸，把两个弟弟藏在自己院子里。

李玄霸觉得这决定有些……咳，天真。但自己都睡着了，是吧？再者，母亲肯定知道姐姐们这里发生的事。母亲没派人来叫他们，应该是默许姐姐们的行为。

还好李四娘和李五娘夸了一阵李玄霸之后，就向李世民和李玄霸的乳母提起了今日后院的事，没让李玄霸继续尴尬下去。

李玄霸闭目听着，心中不由叹气。

他猜测老夫人会熬不到今年春季，主要是通过史书上蛛丝马迹的推断。

史书中没有记载独孤老夫人的生卒年。

但考古挖掘出李渊在大业元年荥阳大海寺，和大业二年在京城附近的草堂寺为李世民立的碑。再加上李世民曾经回忆，年幼时被母亲带着去探望父亲，曾去过刚建好的洛阳，应该就是指这个时候。

也就是说李渊在大业元年到大业二年正月期间，还在当郑州刺史并荥阳太守。窦夫人留守京城，大业元年带李世民去探亲，然后与请了探亲假的李渊一同回京城，途中去了一趟洛阳。

李玄霸这一世也发生过差不多的事。很巧的是，二哥也病了，李渊也为二哥在荥阳立了碑，不过回京后事情太多，他忘记在京城找个寺庙还愿了。

他不知道历史中母亲带着二哥去探亲是不是单纯探亲。

或许上一世母亲路途遥遥赶到荥阳，也是为了定下李建成这门婚事。只是因为二哥病了，郑家如果不想结仇，应该会放弃原本的“考核”计划，只匆匆见一面就罢了。

这一世他和二哥刚到荥阳的时候都精神着，才节外生枝。

大隋官员外放时，家眷是需要随行的。母亲没有随行，很可能需要留在家中照顾婆婆。

之后李渊又当了楼烦太守，那时母亲就已经与李渊住在一起，才能劝李渊献马。

大隋虽然官员守孝需要辞官，但隋文帝和隋炀帝还有个不成文的潜规则，就是亲戚和心腹大臣头七刚过就会被夺情复用，顶多给放一两个月的假，如杨素便是如此。

虞世基和虞世南两兄弟要老老实实守孝三年，是因为现在虞世基还没有成为隋炀帝的心腹宠臣。

李渊是杨广表兄，自然也属于会被立刻起复的行列，不需要辞官三年。所以老夫人可能在李渊就任荥阳太守和楼烦太守之间去世。

当然，李玄霸的推断可能是错误的，母亲也可能是因为其他原因留在京城，独孤老夫人在隋文帝时期就去世了。

但这一世独孤老夫人直到现在都活着，她的身体又衰弱得十分厉害，李玄霸才确定自己的推断。如果独孤老夫人在这个时间点被李建成气病，大概率是熬不过这个冬季的。

因为李渊被征辟入朝而欢喜起来，身体好转，能起床走路的独孤老夫人，在李建成推卸责任时，肉眼可见的精气神颓了不少。

不过当李渊官复原职，李建成只是降级一品，李世民和李玄霸又得到了皇帝的赏赐时，独孤老夫人的身体又好了一些。

当李建成最近变得成熟懂事起来，独孤老夫人更是身体立刻好转，又能拄着拐杖站起来，还请来相熟的女眷来院子里赏还未开败的晚秋菊花，对她们夸赞李建成。

李玄霸以为自己判断失误了，独孤老夫人或许能逃过此劫。

没想到，命运这东西，或许真的存在。

李建成第二次顶撞独孤老夫人是因为郑氏。独孤老夫人最初没回过味，后来越琢磨越觉得自家孙儿这么好，当初怎么会气自己，是不是有小人作祟，就招来赐给李建成的女婢询问。

那女婢不知道说了什么，让独孤老夫人认定这一切都是郑氏的错。

李四娘叹气：“祖母说，长兄之前那么孝顺友悌，就是在纳了郑氏后才行事偏颇。她如此说，父亲和母亲也不好阻止。于是祖母就让郑氏跪祠堂反省。”

李五娘接嘴道：“谁知道，郑氏跪了一会儿晕倒了。医师一查，居然是动了胎气。这下子可把长兄气到了。他坚持说郑氏从未挑拨离间，反倒是劝说他孝顺祖母，友爱弟弟。甚至他送给二郎三郎的礼物其实都是郑氏选的。”

李四娘道：“长兄看上去生气极了，还说当初的事自己除了醉酒把家里的事说了出去，本来也无错，只是没有违背祖母的意愿。那女婢所复述的所谓挑拨离间，不过是郑氏安慰自己只是因为孝顺祖母所以没有坚持拒绝，不必太愧疚。”

李五娘用手指绞了绞落下的发丝：“其实我也觉得郑娘子是遭了无妄之灾。”

李四娘在嘴唇前竖起食指：“妹妹慎言。”

李五娘道：“怕什么？二郎三郎身边的奴仆才不会嘴碎。”

李四娘叹气：“你还是慎言吧。还嫌闹得不够大？唉。”

两位乳母听完后都不住叹气，不敢评价什么。

李玄霸不由悄悄叹气，呼吸声重了一些。

然后，他感到似乎睡得十分沉的二哥抓了一下他的手。

李玄霸：【哥，你也在装睡？】

李世民：【啊！！！！】

李玄霸黑线。你啊屁啊，你这个啊是郁闷还是悲愤还是无语，我怎么知道？

李世民可不管弟弟烦，隔一会儿在心里“啊”一声，直到累得没了声音。

李玄霸默默忍受二哥的“啊”，居然被二哥“啊”困了。

入睡前，李玄霸突然想到女同事的吐槽，“动了胎气会肚子疼反胃恶心流血，才不会晕倒，晕倒那是低血糖，宫斗宅斗晕倒后查出是怀孕都是装的”。

呃，郑娘子是不是装的？

算了，和自己无关。

至少这次真的和自己无关。

李玄霸一觉睡到了第二天，醒来时已经回到了自己的小院中，还换了身衣服。

看来他是真的累了，这次睡得挺沉，中途都没醒。

李玄霸的身旁，李世民还在呼呼大睡。

他蹬开哥哥，爬起来穿衣服的时候，发现母亲正披着衣服趴在他的榻边。

李玄霸一动，窦夫人立刻惊醒，嘴里喊道：“和二郎三郎无关！”

李玄霸心一沉。

窦夫人惊慌地看着李玄霸。

李世民被这一声吵醒，揉着眼睛嘟囔：“咦？我在四姊五姊院子里睡着了吗？唔，这里是我的床啊。我回来后才睡着？”

窦夫人惊恐地站起来，外套落地。待她看到床上的两个孩子时，弯下腰将李玄霸和李世民揽进怀里，不知道是安慰李玄霸和李世民，还是自我安慰：“没事，没事，娘护着你们，不会有事。”

李世民迷迷糊糊道：“娘亲，怎么了？”

窦夫人松开怀抱，抚摸着两个孩子的脑袋：“没事，什么事都不会有。”

李世民使劲揉了揉眼睛，让自己清醒过来：“肯定有事！”

李世民话音刚落，李渊推门进来。

窦夫人一惊，立刻转身将李世民和李玄霸护在身后，声音尖锐道：“我说过了，二郎和三郎一点错都没有！如果大家非要迁怒二郎和三郎，将二郎三郎过继，那不如你休了我，我带二郎三郎离开！”

李世民尖叫：“过继？！”

李玄霸双拳握紧。

李渊停下了脚步，沉默了一会儿，道：“夫人，我知道二郎三郎无错，我不会将二郎三郎过继。孙医师说，母亲快不行了。母亲想见二郎三郎最后一面。”

窦夫人哭道：“见最后一面？最后一面要和二郎三郎说什么？责怪二郎和三郎？二郎三郎做错了什么？他们只是得到了陛下的喜爱而已。二郎三郎所得到的赏赐都分给家人，大郎因二郎和三郎被陛下夸奖，太子还因大郎友悌给大郎升官。两个孩子一切都向着家里，向着兄长，他们究竟有什么错？！铺子是我给的，若说一切的根源，那是我，全是我的错……”

窦夫人本来就没有休息好，激动之下身体一晃就往地上栽倒。

李玄霸和李世民顾不上寒冷，从床上跳下来想护住母亲、两个幼童哪撑得住母亲，他们二人立刻与母亲一同跌倒在地上。

窦夫人想垫在下面，李世民和李玄霸敏捷地躲过窦夫人想揽住他们的手，钻到了母亲身体下方，给母亲当垫子。

李玄霸倒在地上的时候脚一疼，好像扭着了；手掌手臂也火辣辣的，好像擦破了皮。

李渊赶紧冲过去，把窦夫人和两个孩子扶起来。

李世民嘴一张，“呜哇”号啕大哭。

李玄霸垂下头，心中怒火升腾，眼角也默默溢出泪来。

李玄霸深呼吸，尽可能让自己语气平静：“我随父亲去见祖母。香皂方子是我想出来的，和二哥无关，要过继就把我过继了。”

他抬起头，流着泪讥笑道：“反正我很可能活不到弱冠，换得祖母安心和兄长开心很划算。”

李世民扑到弟弟身上，紧紧把弟弟抱住，哭得喘不过气，张嘴想说话，什么都说不出来。

李渊一屁股坐在地上，竟也抹起眼泪来。

“这他娘的究竟是什么破事啊！！”
chunks.englishText:
Li Xuanba was a light sleeper; in truth, he had already woken up the moment he was carried off the carriage, but he was too lazy to open his eyes.

Upon hearing his elder sisters suggest taking a detour, he found it even harder to wake up and could only continue feigning sleep.

Now, listening to his sisters’ whispered conversation, Li Xuanba felt so awkward he nearly failed to keep up the charade.

He was not actually close with his Fourth and Fifth Sisters. Although the Great Sui’s inner courtyard did not strictly enforce the later custom of "men and women not sharing a seat after age seven," Li Siniang and Li Wuniang were not born of the same mother as Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, so they rarely saw each other, and there was no foundation for any deep affection.

Li Xuanba had merely included them in his gift-giving out of courtesy. Yet, in the mouths of his two sisters, this had been exaggerated into Li Xuanba being exceptionally kind and close to them.

The Old Madam had caused another scene in the inner courtyard, and a severe one at that. His two sisters had actually "risked" waiting at the gate for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, hiding their two younger brothers in their own courtyard.

Li Xuanba felt this decision was a bit... *ahem*, naive. But he was already asleep, wasn't he? Furthermore, his mother surely knew what was happening in the sisters' quarters. Since she hadn't sent anyone to summon them, she must have tacitly approved of their actions.

Fortunately, after Li Siniang and Li Wuniang finished praising Li Xuanba, they turned to speak with the wet nurses of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba about the day's events in the inner courtyard, sparing Li Xuanba from further embarrassment.

Li Xuanba listened with his eyes closed, sighing inwardly.

He suspected that the Old Madam would not survive until the spring of this year, a deduction based primarily on clues found in historical records.

The history books did not record the birth or death years of the Old Madam Dugu.

However, archaeological excavations had unearthed steles that Li Yuan had erected for Li Shimin at Xingyang’s Dahai Temple in the first year of the Daye era, and at Caotang Temple near the capital in the second year of Daye. Combined with Li Shimin’s own recollections of being taken by his mother to visit his father when he was young—a trip that included a visit to the newly built Luoyang—it was likely referring to this period.

In other words, between the first year and the first month of the second year of Daye, Li Yuan was still serving as the Prefect of Zhengzhou and the Administrator of Xingyang. Lady Dou had remained in the capital, taken Li Shimin to visit his father in the first year of Daye, and then returned to the capital with Li Yuan, who had taken leave, stopping by Luoyang along the way.

A similar sequence of events had occurred in Li Xuanba’s current life. Coincidentally, his Second Brother had also fallen ill, and Li Yuan had erected a stele for him in Xingyang. However, after returning to the capital, there were too many matters to attend to, and he had forgotten to find a temple in the capital to fulfill his vow.

He did not know if his mother’s trip to visit his father with his Second Brother in history was purely for a visit.

Perhaps in his previous life, his mother had traveled the long distance to Xingyang to finalize the marriage arrangement with the Zheng family. It was only because his Second Brother fell ill that the Zheng family, not wanting to create enmity, likely abandoned their original "assessment" plan and settled for a hurried meeting.

In this life, he and his Second Brother had been full of energy when they arrived in Xingyang, which was why complications had arisen.

When Great Sui officials were posted away, their families were usually required to accompany them. His mother had not accompanied Li Yuan, likely because she needed to stay home to care for her mother-in-law.

Later, when Li Yuan became the Prefect of Loufan, his mother was already living with him, which allowed her to persuade Li Yuan to offer his horses to the Emperor.

Although the Great Sui required officials to resign for a three-year mourning period, Emperors Wen and Yang followed an unwritten rule: close relatives and trusted ministers would be "recalled to service despite their mourning" (duoqing fuyong) shortly after the first seven days of mourning, with at most a month or two of leave granted—as was the case with Yang Su.

The brothers Yu Shiji and Yu Shinan had to observe the full three years of mourning because Yu Shiji had not yet become a favored confidant of Emperor Yang.

Li Yuan, being a cousin to Yang Guang, naturally belonged to the group that would be immediately recalled and did not need to resign for three years. Therefore, the Old Madam could have passed away between Li Yuan’s tenure as Prefect of Xingyang and Prefect of Loufan.

Of course, Li Xuanba’s deduction could be wrong; his mother might have stayed in the capital for other reasons, and the Old Madam Dugu might have passed away during the reign of Emperor Wen.

But in this life, the Old Madam Dugu was still alive, and her health had deteriorated so severely that Li Xuanba was certain of his deduction. If the Old Madam Dugu were to be angered into illness by Li Jiancheng at this point, she would likely not survive the winter.

The Old Madam, who had been cheered by Li Yuan’s appointment to the imperial court and had seen her health improve to the point where she could get out of bed and walk, had visibly lost much of her vitality when Li Jiancheng tried to shirk his responsibilities.

However, when Li Yuan was restored to his original post, Li Jiancheng was only demoted by one rank, and Li Shimin and Li Xuanba received rewards from the Emperor, the Old Madam’s health had improved once more.

When Li Jiancheng recently became mature and sensible, the Old Madam’s health improved immediately; she was able to stand with her cane again and even invited familiar noblewomen to her courtyard to admire the late autumn chrysanthemums, praising Li Jiancheng to them.

Li Xuanba had thought his judgment was flawed and that the Old Madam might escape this ordeal.

Little did he expect that fate, perhaps, truly existed.

Li Jiancheng’s second confrontation with the Old Madam was because of the Lady Zheng. The Old Madam hadn't realized it at first, but the more she pondered, the more she felt that her grandson was so virtuous—why would he have angered her? Was there a villain at work? She summoned the maidservant who had been gifted to Li Jiancheng to question her.

The maidservant must have said something that convinced the Old Madam that all of this was Lady Zheng’s fault.

Li Siniang sighed: "Grandmother said that our eldest brother was so filial and fraternal before, and it was only after taking in Lady Zheng that he began to act with bias. Since she said so, Father and Mother could not stop her. Thus, Grandmother made Lady Zheng kneel in the ancestral hall to reflect."

Li Wuniang added: "Who would have thought that Lady Zheng would faint after kneeling for a while? When the physician checked, it turned out she was pregnant. That really angered our eldest brother. He insisted that Lady Zheng had never sown discord, but had instead urged him to be filial to Grandmother and fraternal to his brothers. He even claimed that the gifts he gave to the Second and Third Brothers were actually chosen by Lady Zheng."

Li Siniang said: "Eldest Brother looked furious. He even said that regarding the previous incident, aside from speaking about family matters while drunk, he had done nothing wrong; he simply hadn't gone against Grandmother’s wishes. The so-called 'sowing of discord' that the maidservant recounted was merely Lady Zheng comforting him, saying he shouldn't feel too guilty because he only acted out of filial piety toward Grandmother."

Li Wuniang twisted a loose strand of hair with her finger: "Actually, I also think Lady Zheng is suffering an undeserved disaster."

Li Siniang held a finger to her lips: "Sister, be careful with your words."

Li Wuniang said: "What is there to fear? The servants around the Second and Third Brothers wouldn't be loose-lipped."

Li Siniang sighed: "You should still be careful. Is the chaos not big enough already? Sigh."

The two wet nurses sighed continuously after hearing this, not daring to comment.

Li Xuanba couldn't help but sigh quietly, his breathing becoming a bit heavier.

Then, he felt his Second Brother, who seemed to be sleeping very soundly, give his hand a squeeze.

Li Xuanba: *[Brother, are you feigning sleep too?]*

Li Shimin: *[Ah!!!!]*

Li Xuanba’s brow twitched. "Ah" your head! Whether that "ah" was one of depression, indignation, or speechlessness, how was he supposed to know?

Li Shimin didn't care about his brother’s annoyance; he continued to "ah" in his heart every few moments until he was too tired to make a sound.

Li Xuanba silently endured his Second Brother’s "ah"s, and was actually lulled to sleep by them.

Before drifting off, Li Xuanba suddenly recalled a female colleague’s complaint: "If you have a threatened miscarriage, you get stomach aches, nausea, and bleeding; you don't just faint. Fainting is low blood sugar. Fainting in palace or household dramas and then being diagnosed as pregnant is always a ruse."

Uh, was Lady Zheng faking it?

Forget it. It had nothing to do with him.

At least this time, it really had nothing to do with him.

Li Xuanba slept until the next day. When he woke up, he was back in his own small courtyard and had been changed into different clothes.

It seemed he was truly exhausted; he had slept quite soundly this time without waking once.

Beside Li Xuanba, Li Shimin was still snoring away.

As he kicked his brother away and climbed up to put on his clothes, he discovered his mother draped in a robe, slumped by the side of his bed.

The moment Li Xuanba moved, Lady Dou woke up with a start, crying out: "It has nothing to do with the Second and Third Brothers!"

Li Xuanba’s heart sank.

Lady Dou looked at Li Xuanba in a panic.

Li Shimin was woken by the noise, rubbing his eyes and muttering: "Eh? Did I fall asleep in the Fourth and Fifth Sisters' courtyard? Hmm, this is my bed. Did I fall asleep after I got back?"

Lady Dou stood up in terror, her outer robe falling to the floor. When she saw the two children on the bed, she bent down and pulled Li Xuanba and Li Shimin into her arms, unsure if she was comforting them or herself: "It’s alright, it’s alright. Mother will protect you; nothing will happen."

Li Shimin asked groggily: "Mother, what’s wrong?"

Lady Dou released her embrace and stroked the heads of the two children: "Nothing, nothing will happen."

Li Shimin rubbed his eyes vigorously to wake himself up: "Something is definitely wrong!"

No sooner had Li Shimin finished speaking than Li Yuan pushed the door open.

Lady Dou was startled and immediately turned to shield Li Shimin and Li Xuanba behind her, her voice sharp: "I have already said it! The Second and Third Brothers have done nothing wrong! If everyone insists on venting their anger on them and having them adopted out, then you might as well divorce me! I will take the Second and Third Brothers and leave!"

Li Shimin shrieked: "Adopted out?!"

Li Xuanba clenched his fists.

Li Yuan stopped in his tracks, remained silent for a moment, and said: "Madam, I know the Second and Third Brothers are innocent. I will not have them adopted out. Physician Sun says that Mother is failing. She wishes to see the Second and Third Brothers one last time."

Lady Dou wept: "See them one last time? What is there to say to the Second and Third Brothers in their final moments? To blame them? What did they do wrong? They only received the Emperor’s favor. All the rewards they received were shared with the family. The Eldest Brother was praised by the Emperor because of them, and the Crown Prince even promoted the Eldest Brother because of his fraternal love. The two children have done everything for the family, for their elder brother—what exactly have they done wrong?! I was the one who gave them the shops; if you want to find the root of it all, it was me. It was all my fault..."

Lady Dou had not been resting well, and in her agitation, her body swayed and she collapsed toward the floor.

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, ignoring the cold, jumped off the bed to try and protect their mother. Two young children could not support her, and they all fell to the ground together.

Lady Dou tried to cushion the fall, but Li Shimin and Li Xuanba nimbly dodged her hands and scrambled beneath her body to act as a cushion.

When Li Xuanba hit the floor, his foot throbbed—he seemed to have twisted it—and his palms and arms burned as if they had been scraped raw.

Li Yuan rushed over and helped Lady Dou and the two children up.

Li Shimin opened his mouth and let out a wail.

Li Xuanba hung his head, fury rising in his heart, and tears silently welled up in the corners of his eyes.

Li Xuanba took a deep breath, trying to keep his voice as calm as possible: "I will go with Father to see Grandmother. The soap formula was my idea; it has nothing to do with Second Brother. If you must adopt someone out, adopt me."

He looked up, laughing mockingly through his tears: "Anyway, it’s likely I won't live to reach adulthood. Trading me for Grandmother’s peace of mind and Eldest Brother’s happiness is a very good deal."

Li Shimin threw himself onto his younger brother, hugging him tightly, sobbing until he couldn't catch his breath, his mouth opening as if to speak, but nothing came out.

Li Yuan sat down on the floor, actually wiping away his own tears.

"What the hell kind of mess is this?!"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第38章 得秀才双喜临门 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第38章 得秀才双喜临门

=

李渊完全没想到事情会往这个方向发展。

老夫人说有人教坏李建成， 人证俱在，只是让郑娘子跪一会儿祠堂，不是什么大的惩罚， 他便同意了。

但郑娘子怎么就怀上了， 他们居然都不知道？

李建成本来正沉默着， 见自己第一个孩子可能会出事，就气得顶撞起老夫人，说郑娘子是被冤枉。

如果只是这样就罢了。真是误会， 他们好声安慰一下郑娘子就行。

李渊想着以母亲对大儿子的重视，既然郑娘子怀上了孩子，她应该也会忍让。

但谁想到， 母亲居然晕了过去？

李渊想去找御医，被醒来的母亲拉住。

“不要叫御医！家丑不可外扬！若外人问起来， 只说我听到郑娘子怀了曾孙， 高兴得晕倒了。”独孤老夫人那时还很清醒。

李渊本以为没事。

哪知道独孤老夫人又晕了过去。供奉的医师扎针也没把独孤老夫人扎醒，求他去请御医或者太白山隐居的孙医师来。

李渊听了母亲的话不敢去找御医，便亲自去找孙医师。

孙医师来了之后叹气，老夫人这是心气散了，就算能醒来， 身体也恢复不了，暗示李渊准备后事。

孙医师给老夫人熬药时， 李渊还是去找了御医。

御医来之后，与孙医师说的同样的话，并且没有留下药方， 只为老夫人施针。

老夫人终于再次醒来， 又喝了药， 口齿终于清晰了。

老夫人似乎也知道自己的寿命将近， 所以屏退众人，只留下李渊和窦夫人安排后事。

独孤老夫人先要将自己嫁妆的一半赠予二郎三郎。

李渊和窦夫人都很疑惑。

虽然嫁妆不算国公府财产，老夫人想给谁就给谁，但一般而言也会依照常理，嫡长子分得七成，其余诸子再分配，嫡子比庶子在剩余财产比例中多分一二成。

独孤老夫人虽然也喜爱李世民和李玄霸，但之前也说自己财产七成是给李建成的。

“是我亏待两个孩子，把嫁妆全部给他们也是应该的。”独孤老夫人冷声道，“儿妇，你也将你的嫁妆分一半给两个孩子。”

窦夫人声音颤抖：“大家，你要做什么？！”

独孤老夫人闭上双眼：“儿啊，我前些时日梦见你的兄长澄儿向我哭诉，他早逝无子，在地下凄凉无比，希望你能过继孩子给他，为他延续香火。他很喜欢大雄和大德，我见这两个孩子将来也是出息的，定能广大澄儿的门扉。过继给澄儿也是嫡子，仍旧养在唐国公府，对两个孩子并无不好。”

窦夫人两眼一黑，坐在地上。

李渊也震惊道：“母亲，你在说什么？为何突然要过继大雄和大德！”

独孤老夫人深呼吸了几下，睁开眼，声音尖锐道：“你还没发现吗？大雄和大德的声势过重了！这次祸端，全是因为他们过分招摇！”

窦夫人咬牙道：“他们被陛下喜爱，是陛下为他们扬名。如果我们责怪他们，岂不是说是陛下的错？何况唐国公府又不是只能有一个国公。他们若有本事，可以自己挣爵位，与大郎并无冲突啊！”

李渊也劝道：“母亲，难道当年兄长没有去世，我就不能出人头地了吗？我堂兄也是一门双郡公，互相扶持……”

“那不一样！”独孤老夫人道，“国公和郡公不一样，你看看他们二人做的事，就是奔着国公去的！”

李渊皱眉道：“母亲，你冷静冷静。二郎三郎才多小？他们怎么可能做这种事。”

窦夫人哭道：“大家，二郎三郎做了什么？被陛下接到身边，是陛下做的；铺子是我给的；打赌是太子主动的；陛下插手我们家的事是大郎喝醉……”

“啪！”独孤老夫人撑起身体，一巴掌扇到窦夫人脸上，“闭嘴！都是你，都是你太偏袒二郎三郎，伤了大郎的心，大郎才会这样！郑娘子的事也是。是不是你将话递在了郑娘子耳中，勾得郑娘子与我作对？”

“对，都是李世民和李玄霸的错。他们出生之前，大郎多好啊，多孝顺啊，没有人说他不好。”

“大郎一直都不喜欢李玄霸。我怎么就没发现呢，一定是大郎一开始就发现了李玄霸没抱好心。”

“我家大郎多好啊，他多乖啊……”

独孤老夫人喃喃自语，眼神一会儿迷糊一会儿清明。

窦夫人一抹眼泪，没有管脸上的红肿，跪地道：“二郎三郎无错。大郎原本也没有嫉妒过二郎三郎。在香皂铺子的事出现之前，大郎还四处夸奖二郎三郎。二郎三郎生病，大郎每日都去探望。大家，你都忘记了吗！三个孩子本来感情很好！”

李渊对窦夫人道：“别说了，让母亲冷静一会儿。”

独孤老夫人眼神又清明起来，她厉声道：“李渊！难道你要让你兄长后继无人吗！你连娘的话也不听了吗！过继孩子的事很常见，李世民和李玄霸的老师虞世南难道不也是被过继给了伯父？”

窦夫人悲泣道：“大家！二郎和三郎也是你的孙子，也是你看着长大的孙子，你甚至直呼他们的名字，把他们当成敌寇了吗？他们没有抢夺大郎任何东西，反而给予了大郎很多东西。就是在今日之前，大郎和二郎、三郎也是很好的兄弟。你这样做，大郎是个好孩子，他也会难过。”

独孤老夫人盯着窦夫人道：“要怪就怪我，是我年老时想着大儿子孤苦伶仃，才逼迫你们夫妻二人做这个决定。”

李渊叹气道：“母亲，你冷静一点，我还是不明白你为什么非得过继二郎和三郎。你说的一切都不成立啊。”

独孤老夫人看了儿子许久，眼神又在浑浊和清明中来回变换。

半晌，独孤老夫人才深深叹了口气，道：“我养的毗沙门，不如儿妇养的大雄和大德。大雄和大德被过继给你的兄长，嫡子的身份也不会变。甚至大雄还能成为嫡长子，能自立一房。以陛下对他二人的喜爱，不会影响他们的前程。”

“但他们留下来……”独孤老夫人沉默了一会儿，艰难道，“就算我走了，毗沙门肯定也会和大雄大德再起冲突。大雄大德无错，但他们也有错，错就是太优秀了，太优秀了啊。把他们过继吧，对毗沙门好，对大雄大德也好。对他们都好。”

李渊本来很坚定的神情出现了一丝犹豫。

窦夫人看到李渊脸上的犹豫，心头一梗，扯下了头上的发簪，发髻落了下来。

她披散着头发道：“大家，你一切都为了毗沙门，哪怕毗沙门现在还根本没想过嫉妒大雄和大德，你也认为毗沙门将来会因嫉妒大雄和大德而与他们生怨？”

独孤老夫人沉默。

李渊深深地叹了口气。

窦夫人道：“说到底，大家是完全没有考虑过大雄和大德。大雄非常黏我和郎君，他在荥阳就重病过一场。如此年幼的孩子，得知因为过于优秀而被父母抛弃，去过继给一个从来没见过的伯父为嗣子，住在自己家中变成了寄人篱下，他会不会再次得病？”

独孤老夫人冷漠地看着窦夫人。

李渊想起李世民对他的亲近，心中的称又朝着窦夫人偏移。

窦夫人继续道：“更别说大德。大德自幼体弱多病，现在抛弃他，就是看着他去死。别说什么还养在家中。我们会因为生气难过生病，孩童更加脆弱。还是说因为大德被预言很难活到弱冠，所以大家就干脆把他放弃了？”

她把簪子丢在地上，冷笑：“大雄大德是从我身上掉下来的肉，我无法放弃他们。何况大家你猜测大雄大德太厉害，所以得毗沙门嫉妒。那他们被过继后就不是李家人吗？大伯去世前是唐国公的嫡长子，他们可是变成了嫡长孙！”

独孤老夫人怒斥道：“你说什么！”

窦夫人一改在独孤老夫人面前的温顺，面不改色道：“大家，你也知道陛下极其宠爱二郎和三郎。若你将他们分出去，陛下一定怜惜他们。就算你将所有事都揽在自己身上，陛下就一定会按照你的想法行动吗？陛下会不会在我们都老去后，以大雄大德被过继给唐国公原本的嫡长子李澄为由，说大雄才是唐国公一脉真正的嫡长，让大雄继承唐国公的爵位？”

李渊：“……”他不敢置信地看着显得十分陌生的夫人。

独孤老夫人又有些糊涂：“不、不会，不会，陛下是我的晚辈，他会照顾我的想法……要不，要不，把大雄和大德过继给……”

窦夫人冷漠道：“过继给已经有亲生子的二伯？让全天下的人都知道我们苛待二郎三郎？这的确不会给毗沙门造成危机，但这会让全天下的人都耻笑郎君！毗沙门是大家你的孙子，难道郎君就不是你的儿子？郎君的仕途才刚起步，你就要让他受到挫折吗！”

说完后，窦夫人不给独孤老夫人回答的机会，低眉顺目道：“儿妇言尽于此，请大家多多考虑。二郎三郎该回来了，儿妇去看看他们，别让他们听到了闲言碎语被吓到。”

窦夫人居然直接转身离去。

独孤老夫人气得浑身颤抖：“她这是不孝！不孝！是十恶不赦的不孝和忤逆之罪！”

李渊叹气：“母亲，你不仅要把大雄和大德赶出门，还要把毗沙门的母亲也赶出门吗？这样对毗沙门真的有好处吗？”

独孤老夫人骂声一滞。

……

“我真的不知道为何母亲会突然犯糊涂，这究竟什么事啊！”李渊坐在地上，也号啕大哭起来。

李玄霸本来很生气，听李渊和二哥李世民差不多模样的哭声，嘴角不由抽搐了几下，心中倒是没那么气了。

李玄霸拍了拍二哥的背：【松开，我有话要和父亲说。】

李世民嗷嗷哭道：“阿玄不准走，你要走我就陪着你，你身体那么弱，一个人该怎么办！”

李玄霸：【松开，我不走，相信我。】

李世民松开手臂，捂着脸继续痛哭。

李玄霸道：“父亲，人的见解来自他们的认知。祖母警惕我和二哥，也是因为祖母的认知。祖母是从南北朝并立的乱世而来，在那个时代没有什么礼义廉耻。先人身没之后，子诬母为妾，兄黜弟为佣，播扬先人之辞迹，暴露祖考之长短，以求直己者，往往而有。”

李玄霸所说的话，出自颜之推的《颜氏家训》。

“独孤家曾经就有此事。祖母的嫡长兄独孤罗与祖母和其余兄弟不是同一个母亲。其诸弟以独孤罗的母亲早逝，无夫人之号为借口，说独孤罗不是嫡长，没资格承袭爵位。他们还因为独孤罗自幼在北齐吃苦，生活十分困窘而嘲笑轻辱独孤罗，不将他当做兄长对待。”

“虽然说祖母的不是不好，但这是文献皇后曾经训斥过的事。祖母也曾经轻辱独孤罗。”李玄霸看向李渊，“正因为祖母做过这样的事，所以才以己度人，认为我们家的家风和独孤家一样，所以才如此紧张。”

“可是父亲啊，现在已经不是礼乐崩坏的乱世。当年文帝和文献皇后都厌恶独孤家夺嫡之事，如今陛下登基时有人传播闲言碎语，陛下肯定更重视礼制。”

“这里是大隋，不是乱世；我们是唐国公府，不是独孤府。”

“我和二哥再优秀也不敢谋夺唐国公的爵位，也没有必要谋夺唐国公的爵位；兄长就算身为嫡长，也不能轻辱我和二哥，因为朝堂上的地位不只是爵位，实职更重要。”

李玄霸对窗外拱手：“劳烦祖母亲自来见我和二哥。祖母认为孙儿说得可对？父亲才华无可挑剔，继承爵位多年后也难以进入朝堂。如果兄长有了对同母胞弟不友悌的污点，他将来的仕途会顺利吗？祖母也别自欺欺人，说这一切都是你做的。关键不是你怎么说，而是陛下和世人如何想。”

坐在地上的李渊愕然转头，本来卧床不起的独孤老夫人居然在仆从的搀扶下来到了这里。

独孤老夫人死死地盯着李玄霸，仿佛他不是自己曾经疼爱过的孙儿，而是自己的仇人。

“实话说，兄长真的很冤枉。他原本对我们很好，也从未想过插手商贾之事。商贾之事本来就是偏房操持。”

“兄长受过教训之后，也已经反省，对我和二哥都很好，我们今日出门时还商量给兄长送什么礼物。”

“唐国公府原本是兄弟友悌，家人和睦。我们本来没有任何冲突。”

李玄霸仰着头看着双目浑浊的独孤老夫人：“祖母，别再挑拨离间我们的兄弟之情了。为了安你的心，我这就去向陛下请求，通过分科考试取得举荐名额。门荫入仕者方为正统，科举入仕者皆受轻视，难以晋升。”

“祖母，我已经退了一步。反正我活不长，如果你逼急了我，我就去找陛下告状。你信不信我跑到大街上说你说兄长嫉妒我，所以要把我过继？”

“我不怕丢脸，我也不怕死，因为我本来就活不长。”

李玄霸上前几步，在众人瞠目结舌中走到独孤老夫人的面前：“还是说，祖母你要现在掐死我？亲手掐死你的孙儿？”

独孤老夫人在李玄霸上前时，居然不由后退了一步。

李玄霸瞥了独孤老夫人一眼，转身对李渊拱手：“祖母不慈，我却不能不孝。若是祖母非要掐死我，那我就死在这里。父亲，儿不能为父亲尽孝了。”

窦夫人把呆滞的李世民抱起来，冷笑道：“好啊，那可真是太好了。祖母亲自在儿子面前掐死病弱的孙儿，不知道传到陛下耳中，我们这唐国公府的牌匾还能不能保得住。也别说什么瞒着，这京城中的事，有什么能瞒得过陛下？”

“大家，我已经问过很多次了，你在乎毗沙门，就一点不在乎郎君吗？”窦夫人质问道，“你考虑过郎君的心情，郎君的前程吗？”

李渊从地上爬起来，他悲伤道：“是啊，你考虑过我吗？我是你唯一的儿子啊。”

“我、我……”独孤老夫人嚅嗫道，“你看，你看三郎居然敢威胁我，将来他一定……”

“母亲累了，请把母亲扶回病床，请御医来诊治。”李渊打断道，“母亲，你在御医面前说的话，一定会传到陛下耳中，请母亲慎言。”

独孤老夫人立刻闭上了嘴。她悲伤地看着儿子。

李渊移开了视线。

独孤老夫人离开，张婆却留了下来，朝着李渊跪了下来。

李渊叹气道：“张阿婆，你有何事？”

张婆磕了几个响头，把额头都磕出血了，哭诉道：“国公，不是老夫人糊涂，不是老夫人不慈啊。是……”

她咬牙，又磕了几个头，道：“大郎在探病的时候又和老夫人吵了一架，说老夫人总是做有害他的事。如果老夫人真的要对他好，不如把二郎三郎过继，这样就没有后顾之忧了。如果做不到这一点，就别说什么为他好。”

李渊不敢置信道：“什么？！”

张婆哭道：“大郎肯定也只是说气话。但老夫人已经糊涂了，她只是糊涂了，糊涂了啊。她不记事了，说了什么，她自己都不知道。她不清醒，国公千万不要生老夫人的气。”

李玄霸看着张婆额头上的血，叹了口气，道：“父亲，孙医师曾经说过，有一种病叫老年癔症。就是老年人会逐渐变得糊涂，偏执，只有一个念头，听不进去话，还会想着总有人会害他们。或许祖母真的只是病了。”

说完，李玄霸身体一软，倒了下去。

李渊立刻接住李玄霸：“大德！……好烫，你怎么在发高烧？御医，御医！”

他抱着李玄霸冲了出去。

窦夫人抱着李世民跟上。

李世民呆呆地趴在母亲怀里，好像完全失了神。

……

初冬的季节，李玄霸没有穿外套站了这么久，立刻发起了高烧。

李世民比李玄霸稍好些，但当晚也发起了低烧。

唐国公府立刻乱作一团。

李渊请了假，亲自给李玄霸擦身体降温。

独孤老夫人没有再次晕倒，只是好像更糊涂了。

现在她嘴里碎碎念着“好，去科举，去科举”，似乎只有这一个念头。

李建成在照顾动了胎气的郑氏。他来探望李世民和李玄霸时，被李渊拖到院子里狠揍了一顿。

“你和你祖母说了什么胡话！”李渊双目赤红，“你难道真的想过继你的弟弟？！”

李建成愣了一下才哭出来：“我只是说气话，让祖母别再挑拨我和二弟三弟的关系，我怎么可能做这种事！”

说完，他左右扇自己的脸：“是我的错，我不该说气话，我这就向祖母道歉。”

“不用了。”李渊心情十分复杂。

李渊想起了三儿子所说的话。

独孤家的家风不好，所以母亲以为兄弟感情就应该是独孤家的那样。

母亲教导自己的时候，自己的兄长已经都去世了，所以母亲没有教过他兄弟之事，他不知道母亲的想法。

母亲教导毗沙门的时候，究竟给毗沙门灌输了什么？是独孤家的那一套吗？

“你去照顾郑娘子，尽量保住你的孩子。”李渊感到很疲惫，“我照顾你祖母，你母亲会照顾弟弟，你顾好自己。”

李建成哭道：“是！父亲！”

看着李建成离开，李渊以只有自己听得见的声音自言自语：“有了孩子就会成熟了，一定是这样，我当年也是有了毗沙门才长大。”

李建成不仅是李渊第一个孩子，还是李渊宠爱了九年的“独子”。

那时他还是千牛备身，住在京城中。李建成既是在独孤老夫人膝下长大，也是在李渊的面前长大。

在李世民和李玄霸出生时，李渊才外放。所以李渊虽然也很喜欢李世民和李玄霸这对时隔九年才又得到的双生儿子，但至少现在，李渊对李建成的感情肯定比聚少离多的李世民和李玄霸深厚。

子不教，父之过。他无法自欺欺人李建成若走偏了路，都是母亲的错。

他自己也教导了李建成，手把手地教导李建成认字，读书，习武，比对李世民和李玄霸认真得多。

李世民和李玄霸还未到八岁。他们这个年龄就有如此成就，几乎是纯粹是吃天赋。

“所以大郎才厌恶二郎三郎吗？”李渊扶额苦笑，笑出了眼泪，“这会显得你更没用，显得为父的教育更失败啊。”

……

李玄霸醒来后已经是一日后。

李世民已经退了烧，但紧紧地抱着李玄霸的手臂不放。别人担心他过了病气，想要把他抱走，他怎么也不肯。

李渊便让李世民陪在李玄霸身边。

李玄霸醒来前，李世民一直没说话，好像哑了似的。连窦夫人唤他，他也只是用点头摇头回应，并不出声。

御医说李世民受了惊，过几日心静了就好了。

李渊和窦夫人很担心，但也只能相信御医。

孙医师好像意识到唐国公府后宅出了比较复杂的事，借口采药，入山跑得不见人影，只留下了药方给李渊。

李渊真想把脚底像是抹了油的孙医师揍一顿。

待李玄霸醒来，众人终于松了一口气。

独孤老夫人本来单独和李渊、窦夫人说要过继李世民和李玄霸，没有外人听到。

窦夫人来到李世民和李玄霸院子的时候担心独孤老夫人过来发疯，先遣散了其他仆人。

但独孤老夫人自己带了仆人来。

李世民和李玄霸病倒之时，窦夫人虽然心急如焚，仍旧迅速控制住了在场的奴仆。

只有李渊想起张婆的话，担心独孤老夫人身边还有其他人知道此事，便将独孤老夫人身边所有奴仆都关押起来，只留下张婆照顾独孤老夫人。

之后这些人被李渊派家兵带走，去向就连窦夫人都不知道。

张婆向李渊请求，如果老夫人去了，自己要陪葬。
