Chapter 39: Few Are Grieving

Old Madam Dugu was dead.

Li Yuan did nothing to Li Jiancheng.

It was not that Li Yuan did not want to.

From the perspective of outsiders, Old Madam Dugu had been deeply concerned for Li Jiancheng, and upon seeing him arrive, she had excitedly lunged toward him.

Li Jiancheng had blocked the view of the Old Madam’s face, so no one else could see how savage and terrifying her expression had been as she tried to lunge forward to bite and claw at people.

Li Yuan had been ready to strike Li Jiancheng at that moment, only to be stopped by the Old Madam.

Though the Old Madam could no longer speak clearly, she still pointed at the terrified Li Xuanba, insisting it was his fault.

Li Yuan’s face was filled with disappointment.

Afterward, the Old Madam made Li Yuan swear an oath. Although she did not specify what the oath was, Li Yuan understood.

The Old Madam kept clutching Li Yuan’s arm, her eyes wide open, her eyeballs nearly bulging out of their sockets.

It was only when Li Yuan compromised, promising not to hold Li Jiancheng accountable and not to let word of today’s events spread, that the Old Madam finally wore an expression of relief.

Yet, she continued to point at Li Xuanba, and that savage look only caused the disappointment in Li Yuan’s eyes to deepen.

Seeing Li Yuan’s expression, the savagery on the Old Madam’s face receded, replaced by pleading and agony.

Her clouded eyes welled up with tears, which spilled out drop by drop as she stared silently at the child who had once relied on her for survival.

Li Yuan wiped the tears from his mother’s face and said, "I will do nothing to Li Jiancheng. He was raised by you, Mother, and he was raised by me as well. If a son is not taught, it is the father’s fault. I will teach him more carefully in the future. You may rest easy, Mother."

The Old Madam wept while waving her hand.

Li Yuan understood his mother’s meaning. He took several deep breaths before saying with difficulty, "Fine. I... I will not hit him, I will not beat him, I will not harm him."

Only then did the Old Madam slowly close her eyes.

Li Yuan told his children to go and bid farewell to the Old Madam.

Li Jiancheng, who had been kneeling in the snow as punishment, stumbled over to the Old Madam’s side and wept bitterly. Li Siniang and Li Wuniang were shedding silent tears, while Li Yuanji looked on with a blank expression.

Li Shimin held Li Xuanba’s hand, standing in the corner of the room, his eyes already swollen like peaches from crying.

When Li Yuan cast his gaze toward them, Li Shimin acted like a startled kitten or puppy, his fur instantly standing on end as he hid his younger brother behind him, as if his father’s very gaze were a threat to his brother.

Li Xuanba, meanwhile, remained wooden and listless, his eyes hollow—the same expression he had worn when Li Shimin had kept watch over him while he was delirious with a high fever after the adoption farce.

Li Yuan withdrew his gaze, finding himself at a loss for how to face this sickly child.

Every time he saw Li Xuanba, that question of his echoed in the depths of his heart.

"Because I might not live to reach adulthood, can I be sacrificed at will?"

It was clearly Li Jiancheng’s fault, yet Mother still wanted to push the blame onto Da De. Because Da De was unlikely to grow up, did it not matter if he took the blame for Li Jiancheng’s unfilial behavior?

Li Yuan understood his mother’s partiality less and less.

He actually found this mother, who had once shielded him from the wind and rain, to be terrifying.

He could not help but wonder: if his own elder brothers had not died young, would he have ended up in Li Xuanba’s position?

Li Yuan had originally been the youngest child, but his elder brothers had all passed away early. The massive Tang State Duke’s mansion was left with only seven-year-old him, who sat ignorantly in the position of the Tang State Duke, bearing the responsibility of revitalizing the Li family line.

When Li Yuan drank with his clansmen, they all envied him, saying that Li Jiancheng could hold the family legacy, and that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had boundless futures; the Tang State Duke’s line was certain to flourish once again.

Back then, the sons of the old Tang State Duke had all been like dragons, which was why they had supported the prosperity of the Li clan. Now, this main branch of the Tang State Duke was set to rise again.

Li Yuan had thought so, too.

But clearly, his mother did not think so.

Li Yuan walked over to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Li Shimin nearly bared his teeth at his father.

Li Yuan patted Li Shimin’s head and scooped Li Xuanba into his arms. "Go and rest. It’s over now; don’t get sick again."

Li Shimin trotted along behind Li Yuan.

He hesitated for a moment, then reached out and tugged on the hem of Li Yuan’s robe.

Li Yuan paused in his stride, then continued walking, feeling a strange urge to shed tears.

In Li Yuan’s arms, Li Xuanba continued his performance of staring into space.

He had once preferred to curry favor with the Old Madam and Li Jiancheng rather than get close to Li Yuan, precisely because he detested the kind of person Li Yuan was.

Li Yuan’s concern for him was genuine; when he was being good to you, he was a perfect father.

It was like a piece of coptis root wrapped in sugar—you were forced to let it melt in your mouth.

After Li Yuan took Li Xuanba and Li Shimin away, he brought over Li Yuanji, who was boredly playing with his fingers, and the anxious Li Zhiyun, telling them all to get some rest.

These four children would have to keep vigil later; if they did not rest now, they would not be able to hold up.

Although Li Yuanji was mischievous, he was not stupid and was very sensitive to the atmosphere. He was very obedient now, climbing onto the bed and falling fast asleep.

Li Zhiyun crawled into Li Xuanba’s arms, clinging to him like an octopus.

Li Xuanba patted Li Zhiyun’s head, wondering what this child had sensed.

After Li Xuanba patted Li Zhiyun’s head, Li Shimin reached out and patted Li Xuanba’s head as well.

He kept a straight face, trying hard to appear composed. "A-Xuan, you should sleep too. Don’t worry, Big Brother is always here."

Li Xuanba sighed and said, "Second Brother, you should sleep too."

Li Shimin forced a smile. "Alright."

The overbearing Li Yuanji had occupied the center of the bed. Li Shimin did not want to argue with him, so he had someone bring over a soft couch. The three brothers—Li Shimin, Li Xuanba, and Li Zhiyun—curled up on the couch together.

Li Zhiyun remained nestled in Li Xuanba’s arms, clutching his neck tightly and refusing to let go.

Li Shimin lay with his back to Li Xuanba, his breathing uneven.

Li Xuanba: [Crying again?]

After a long while, Li Shimin replied: [No!]

Li Xuanba patted Li Zhiyun’s head. "Go to your Second Brother’s arms."

Li Shimin choked out, "No, it’s annoying."

Li Zhiyun lifted his head from Li Xuanba’s chest, released his third brother’s neck, and climbed over Li Shimin like he was climbing a mountain, then hugged Li Shimin’s neck and buried his head in his chest.

Li Shimin tapped Li Zhiyun’s head lightly. "Do you only listen to your Third Brother?"

Li Zhiyun did not speak.

Li Shimin hugged Li Zhiyun tighter, his sobbing growing louder.

Li Xuanba sighed and was just about to offer comfort when Li Yuanji suddenly roared, "Stop crying! It’s so annoying! Second Brother is a crybaby!"

Li Xuanba: "..."

Li Shimin: "!!!"

Li Zhiyun: "Pfft."

Li Shimin gritted his teeth. "Shut up! Go to sleep!"

He wiped his eyes fiercely with the quilt, closed them, and stopped crying.

Li Xuanba marveled. He hadn't expected Li Yuanji to be useful for something.

When Lady Dou had finished arranging the women of the household and had taken Li Siniang and Li Wuniang to rest, she dragged her exhausted body to check on the children.

All the children were asleep. Even Li Yuanji, the youngest, was snoring like thunder, and even Li Xuanba, who was the lightest sleeper, had fallen into a deep slumber.

Lady Dou gently pinched Li Yuanji’s nose.

Li Yuanji grunted a few times, turned over, and his snoring softened slightly.

Lady Dou sighed and looked at Li Xuanba, whose brows were tightly furrowed even in sleep.

Death was the most important matter, but aside from Emperor Wen of Sui, this was the first time she had ever hated someone so much. Even though the Old Madam was already dead, the hatred in her heart remained difficult to dispel.

Lady Dou lightly touched the space between Li Xuanba’s brows.

Li Xuanba’s furrowing was stubborn; she rubbed it several times, but the creases between his brows would not smooth out.

Afraid of waking him, Lady Dou had to withdraw her hand.

She looked at Li Shimin and Li Zhiyun.

Li Shimin’s eyes were red and swollen, and he was sniffing in his sleep, with tears seemingly still leaking out.

Li Zhiyun was clutching Li Shimin’s arm tightly, still looking anxious and fearful even in his dreams.

Lady Dou sat on the edge of the bed, feeling like a failure as a mother.

As a mother, she should have raised her children well, taken care of them, shielded them from the wind and rain, and allowed them to live carefree lives.

But now?

Could the scars in her children’s hearts really heal with the passing of the Old Madam?

Could the rifts between Da Lang, Er Lang, and San Lang really be mended as time went on?

Intelligent people find it hard to be optimistic. Lady Dou could not find optimism.

She could only swear in her heart that she would treat her children twice as well in the future. Especially A-Xuan; he must not suffer anymore.

The Tang State Duke’s mansion was not the wilderness, where the weak were prey to the strong and sickly children had to be discarded.

The weakest child in the family should be the most cherished. Yet, Li Xuanba had been forced to yield in everything, pushed to the point of being abandoned time and again.

Lady Dou’s heart felt as if it were being sliced by a dull blade, the wounds growing deeper and more painful. The tiny, fragmented pains finally merged into one, as if her entire heart were about to shatter.

She sat there for a long time, only rising to leave when Li Yuan came to find her.

Seeing his wife weeping silently, Li Yuan held her gently and patted her shoulder. "We will make it up to them slowly in the future."

Lady Dou nodded silently.

...

Old Madam Dugu had passed away.

People in the capital were not overly surprised.

The Old Madam was already of a great age and had often been bedridden for several years. Lady Dou had frequently served her without taking off her clothes to sleep, which had long been a celebrated story in the capital.

The Old Madam’s passing was also accompanied by a touching tale.

The third son of the Tang State Duke’s mansion, Li Sanlang, was quite rebellious and, for some reason, insisted on taking the imperial examinations.

The Old Madam, however, was a loving grandmother. She had persuaded the Tang State Duke to agree to Li Sanlang’s participation in the exams, and even after she had become delirious with illness, she kept thinking of her grandson’s exams, holding on until her grandson had achieved the title of "Xiucai" and returned to share the good news with her before she passed away with a smile.

People in the capital all said that Li Xuanba must have been the Old Madam’s most beloved child.

Later, the distribution of the Old Madam’s dowry seemed to confirm this.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, the pair who were neither the oldest nor the youngest, had actually received fifty percent of the Old Madam’s dowry between them.

Of the remaining fifty percent, thirty percent went to Li Jiancheng, ten percent was divided between the two unmarried daughters, and the final ten percent was split seven-to-three between Li Yuanji and Li Zhiyun.

However, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were also brotherly; citing the order of seniority, they gifted twenty percent of their share to Li Jiancheng, and five percent each to their unmarried elder sister and their two younger brothers, keeping only ten percent for themselves.

The siblings of the Tang State Duke’s mansion yielded to one another, and in the end, the distribution was settled according to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba’s request.

Li Shimin muttered, "I didn’t even want that ten percent."

Li Xuanba said, "Money itself is not evil. It’s perfect for buying us a good reputation."

Li Shimin couldn't help but laugh and scold, "You mercenary!"

Li Xuanba: "Mm."

Li Shimin said, "You didn’t want that last ten percent either, right? You think it’s bad luck."

Li Xuanba glanced at his brother.

Although he was mercenary, after the soap shop, he really hadn’t set his eyes on the Old Madam’s dowry. He had even been a bit extravagant for a moment, not wanting to deal with it.

However, having made the decision, hearing his Second Brother say it out loud made Li Xuanba feel a bit awkward.

*How did I become so extravagant! This is money!*

Li Xuanba’s penny-pinching, poor-person mindset began to act up.

But since the money had been dispersed until only ten percent remained, he might as well finish the plan.

Originally, Li Xuanba had wanted to use this last ten percent of the dowry to donate a large Buddha statue or build a small temple.

People of this era did things this way when they wanted to do good deeds. He should fit in.

But while his reason told him this was the most convenient and reputation-enhancing path, his inner "poor person" mindset really did not want to throw money at a Buddhist temple.

Li Xuanba agonized over it for a long time, grabbing his brother and tossing and turning as he voiced his dilemma.

Li Shimin covered his ears, but he could not block out the inner thoughts, so he could only lie limply on the rush mat, letting Li Xuanba torment him.

"If you don’t want to do it, then don’t!" Li Shimin said, going crazy. "It’s such a simple thing, what is there to agonize over! If you won’t do it, I will!"

Li Shimin sprang up from the mat like a harrier and ran off to ask their mother for help.

Li Xuanba hurriedly stopped him. "Ah, wait! I haven’t decided yet!"

Li Shimin covered his ears. "Not listening, not listening! I’ve decided!"

Li Xuanba said, "Come back!"

Li Shimin said, "Shut up!"

Li Zhiyun poked his head out and asked Li Yuanji, "What are Second Brother and Third Brother arguing about?"

Li Yuanji looked around, picked up a stone from the ground, and threw it at Li Xuanba. Regardless of whether he hit him or not, he turned and ran.

Li Zhiyun was dumbfounded.

Li Xuanba turned his head.

Li Zhiyun shook his head vigorously. "It wasn’t me, it wasn’t me, it was... anyway, it wasn’t me."

Li Xuanba sighed and beckoned to Li Zhiyun.

Li Zhiyun happily ran to Li Xuanba’s side, and Li Xuanba took his hand to go find Li Shimin, who had already vanished from sight.

Lady Dou was exhausted from presiding over the Old Madam’s funeral, and Li Shimin did not have the heart to disturb her.

His eyes darted around, and he thought of what A-Xuan called a "tool person."

Li Shimin weaved through the guests, crouching low to avoid his younger brother while searching for someone.

"Found him!" Li Shimin’s eyes lit up when he saw a chubby figure.

The chubby person Li Shimin was looking for was, naturally, Crown Prince Yang Zhao.

As the Old Madam was the last elder of the Emperor’s maternal family, Yang Guang had personally come to pay his respects when she passed, and Crown Prince Yang Zhao had even taken the initiative to help out at the Tang State Duke’s mansion in the capacity of a junior.

"Cousin!" Li Shimin lunged forward.

The guards glanced at him, and the hands resting on their sword hilts relaxed.

Yang Zhao smiled. "Da Xiong... sigh, don’t lunge. Come, let me introduce you; you probably don’t know him yet. This is my younger brother, the Prince of Qi, Yang Jiong. You may call him Second Cousin."

Yang Jiong’s brows were arrogant. "Is his surname Xiao?"

Yang Zhao frowned. "Second Brother!"

Li Shimin said, "A distant cousin is still a cousin, and besides, I’m not that distant. If the Prince of Qi is unwilling, I can address you as Your Highness the Prince of Qi. The Crown Prince is my cousin, and the Prince of Qi is the Prince of Qi; we shall address you separately."

Yang Jiong said in surprise, "Are you dissatisfied with me?"

Li Shimin said, "I wouldn’t dare."

Having said that, he tugged on Yang Zhao’s sleeve. "Cousin, I have a favor to ask of you. Let’s go over there to talk."

Yang Zhao glanced at Yang Jiong, who looked away with a face full of irritation.

Yang Zhao sighed. "Alright, let’s go over there to talk."

Yang Jiong reached out and grabbed Li Shimin by the back of his collar.

Li Shimin said indignantly, "What is Your Highness the Prince of Qi doing?"

"What is there that this Prince cannot hear?" Yang Jiong said. "Speak."

Yang Zhao hurriedly shielded Li Shimin. "Father has already reprimanded you; why are you taking your anger out on a child?"

Yang Jiong released Li Shimin and crossed his arms. "I’m not taking my anger out; I’m just curious."

Li Shimin said, "Fine, I’ll tell you. There’s a little money left from what Grandmother left for me and A-Xuan, and A-Xuan wants to use it to do some good. Normally, donating a Buddha statue would be enough; how simple. But A-Xuan insists he doesn’t want the Buddha to help others; he wants to help people himself. And A-Xuan and I are in mourning, so where would we find the energy? That’s why I came to ask Cousin for help. Among the people I know, only Cousin is truly benevolent. Cousin must know how to help others."

Li Shimin shook his head and sighed.

When Yang Jiong heard Li Shimin say "do some good" and "donate a Buddha statue," the words almost slipped out, but they were blocked in his throat by Li Shimin’s follow-up.

After hearing Li Shimin’s words, he looked at his brother’s expression, which was so happy his eyes were nearly invisible, and he finally understood a little why his brother was so close to the Tang State Duke’s mansion.

His brother was benevolent, but his good temper was merely politeness; deep down, he was incredibly proud. Even if he, the younger brother, were to shout stupid things like "I want to be the Crown Prince" in front of his brother, his brother would only look at him with helpless indulgence and tell him to keep his voice down so their father wouldn’t hear.

He looked down on everyone, himself included, let alone others!

Yang Jiong’s mind shifted. "This Prince is bored, too. Whatever you want to do, I’ll help you!"

He looked at his brother. *I’m here to steal your task!*

Yang Zhao said with gratification, "You’re finally being sensible. Good, good, that’s great! You should do more good deeds!"

Yang Jiong: "..."

He didn’t want to do it anymore.

Li Shimin did not care about the undercurrents between these two royal brothers; as long as he achieved his goal and stopped his brother from pestering him, it was fine.

"A-Xuan wants to find a local government school and set up something called..." Li Shimin thought for a moment, "...a scholarship and financial aid program, to reward students who are poor but love to learn."

Yang Jiong asked curiously, "Why not just directly provide relief and raise orphans?"

Yang Zhao’s expression was gratified. *That’s great, my younger brother knows he can provide relief and raise orphans.*

Li Shimin said, "I said that too. But A-Xuan insisted that it was meaningless; he wants to do good in a sustainable way, not a one-off deal."

Li Shimin pinched his chin, tilting his head. "Honestly, I don’t think A-Xuan’s words are very kind. Relief is relief; why bring up 'deals'? This isn’t a merchant’s business."

"Sustainable relief is what makes others follow suit, so more people will be helped," Li Xuanba’s voice sounded from behind Li Shimin.

Li Shimin jumped off the ground and hid behind Yang Zhao.

Li Xuanba was speechless. "What are you hiding for?"

Li Zhiyun echoed, "Second Brother, what are you hiding for?"

Li Shimin emerged awkwardly from behind Yang Zhao. "I was just startled by your sudden appearance. A-Xuan, this is the Prince of Qi."

Li Xuanba said respectfully, "Greetings, Your Highness the Crown Prince. Greetings, Your Highness the Prince of Qi."

Li Zhiyun mimicked Li Xuanba, bowing obediently.

Yang Zhao smiled. "Why are you still so formal? Learn more from Da Xiong; he lunges at me calling me 'Cousin' the moment he sees me."

Li Xuanba said, "Not everyone is as reckless and unreasonable as my brother."

Yang Jiong: "Pfft... *cough*, you two continue."

Yang Zhao smiled and sighed. "Let’s not talk about that. Tell me in detail what you just said."

Li Xuanba organized his thoughts and said slowly, "My funds are limited; I cannot support everyone, nor can I support them forever. But if the people I support can one day become officials or ministers, will they not do the same? In this way, I support a group of people, and perhaps some of them will take up the baton from my hands and pass it to the next person. Moreover, perhaps if those who have known hardship become officials, they might understand the suffering of the common people."

Li Shimin interjected, "But A-Xuan, you said before that some people who have known hardship become even more indulgent once they become officials."

Li Xuanba said, "Of course there are bad people; who can say for sure? To put it bluntly, I just want my money to be spent more valuably. Second Brother isn’t wrong; I’m not inherently kind. Even if a beggar were starving to death on the roadside, I wouldn’t give him alms."

Li Shimin put his hands together and bowed repeatedly. "I was wrong, I was wrong, A-Xuan, stop talking, Big Brother was wrong."

Li Xuanba was helpless. "I’m not saying that out of spite; I’m being serious."

He was doing this to buy a reputation, not out of pure altruism.

Or, to put it in a darker light, he was accumulating a reputation before the chaotic times, and incidentally seeing if he could be lucky enough to fish out a few talented men from humble backgrounds.

"If it proves effective, I will memorialize this to His Majesty. By allocating an extra sum to government schools at all levels in His Majesty’s name to reward and assist poor students, we can make literary education flourish even more," Li Xuanba added.

Yang Zhao keenly sensed from Li Xuanba’s words that this could potentially win the hearts of scholars. However, Li Xuanba was still young and likely did not have such intentions. Besides, the hearts of scholars from humble backgrounds were not worth much anyway.

Li Xuanba’s supplementary words caused Yang Zhao to reach out and pat his head. "As expected of our Great Sui’s youngest Xiucai. Li Xiucai’s policy proposals have drawn endless praise from Father; you truly have great foresight."

The hearts of one or two scholars from humble backgrounds meant nothing, but if all government schools had this system, and if this system could truly win the hearts of such scholars, then the significance would be great.

Li Xuanba bowed. "This is what a subject should do."

Yang Jiong looked at Li Xuanba with curiosity.

He knew there was an eight-year-old Li Xiucai, but he hadn’t paid much attention. The imperial examinations were just a game; his grandfather often privately disparaged those who entered officialdom through the exams, saying they were useless, knew only how to bury their heads in grand principles, and spoke empty words that meant nothing.

Seeing Li Xuanba today, it seemed this Li Xiucai had some ability?

"Leave this matter to me. If I can pull it off, I’ll ask for a reward from Father; maybe he’ll scold me a few times less." Yang Jiong stopped referring to himself as "this Prince," though his tone remained arrogant. "What is your courtesy name?"

Li Shimin said, "My courtesy name is Da Xiong!"

Yang Jiong glanced at Li Shimin. "I didn’t ask you."

Li Shimin laughed. "My younger brother’s courtesy name is Da De, but he doesn’t like it. He says he doesn’t want to be a monk."

"Pfft." Yang Jiong covered his mouth.

Li Xuanba glared at his brother. "We should return to Father and Mother."

Li Shimin said, "Alright. Your Highness the Crown Prince, Your Highness the Prince of Qi, we take our leave."

Yang Zhao said, "Go. I will speak to your father about this later. Once I have reported it to Father, I will come find you. Second Brother, do this well."

Yang Jiong turned his face away. "I know."

After the three brothers bid farewell to the two royal brothers, Li Shimin held Li Xuanba’s hand, Li Xuanba held Li Zhiyun’s hand, and they walked hand-in-hand, from tallest to shortest, back to the rear of the mourning hall to continue staring into space.

Li Yuan, Lady Dou, and Li Jiancheng were in the hall receiving guests. The children stayed behind the hall, ostensibly praying for the Old Madam, but in reality, just being lazy.

Li Siniang and Li Wuniang came to find them, pulling cloth bundles from their bosoms. When they opened them, they revealed sesame-covered flatbreads.

"Don’t tell anyone," Li Siniang and Li Wuniang whispered.

Li Xuanba took a bite; the flatbread was very crispy.

Baked unleavened flour foods only became crispy if a large amount of fat was added. It was clear that animal fat had been added to these flatbreads.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第39章 没几个人在悲伤 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
守孝要吃素，断绝所有荤腥，荤油也算在内。正月没有新鲜的蔬果，他们这几日吃的都是米面，很是没滋没味，连本来就很瘦弱的李玄霸都又瘦了几分。

李玄霸觉得自己还撑得住。他撑一段时间，等李渊被召回朝堂后，就可以出门的时候偷偷煮鸡蛋吃补充营养。

但家人似乎看不下去了。

守孝虽然需要吃素，但对孩童、孕妇和得病之人可以宽容。这些人可以吃荤食，只是不能喝酒、宴请和吃姜蒜韭等有刺激性气味的食物。

毕竟不能守孝把家里人的命给守没了。

李玄霸既年幼又一直病病歪歪，自然属于可以额外“通融”的人群。只是李渊没有提这件事前，李玄霸也不想去找伤心过度的李渊提这件事，免得李渊心里认为他对老夫人有怨言。

四姊五姊能送来加了荤油的胡饼，母亲肯定知道这件事；偷偷送来，是说明父亲还不知道这件事？

李玄霸心思一转，对四姊和五姊道谢，迅速和哥哥弟弟分吃了胡饼，填饱了肚子。

李四娘小声道：“再过几日你们就能吃荤腥了。四郎闹了起来，已经先吃上水煮的肉。”

李玄霸真心诚意道：“四弟真是好人，这次真的感谢他。”

李世民和李智云使劲点头。他们第一次如此喜爱这位兄弟。

……

只过了三日，兄弟几人果然能吃上蛋奶肉了。

后来李四娘和李五娘也悄悄吃上了，只有李渊、窦夫人和李建成还在吃素。

李建成后院怀着孕的郑氏自然也早早不用守孝吃素。窦夫人很精细地安排郑氏的生活，还写信给郑氏的家人，问他们需不需要安排婆子来伺候郑氏，或许会让郑氏更自在一些。

原本荥阳郑氏已经写信给窦夫人，说正在帮郑氏找熟悉生育的婆子。过了几日，他们却又来信，说请窦夫人自行安排，他们不僭越了。

窦夫人正疑惑，李渊给了窦夫人一封郑继伯写来的信。

郑继伯是已经与李建成定亲的亲家公。

窦夫人还没拆信，就知道为何郑氏打消了派人来的主意。打开信一看，果然，郑继伯担心如果郑媵肚子里的是庶长子，给的待遇过高，会影响李建成的嫡子。

“唉。”窦夫人抱怨，“现在就开始担心庶长子和嫡长子不睦了。”

李渊不说话。

他家连同母兄弟都成了闹剧，二儿子三儿子甚至还只是稚童。他真不好说郑继伯的担心不对。

“陛下要召我还朝，并让我随行北巡。”李渊对窦夫人道，“孩子们就拜托你了。特别是三郎的身体，你要多注意。”

窦夫人道：“是，郎君你放心。”

李渊神情低落：“嗯，我自然放心。”现在母亲已经去世，确实府中没有会让妻子为难的事了。

又过了一旬，李渊果然被召回朝堂，仍旧官复原职。

李渊刚回到朝堂，杨广就做了一件大事——改革官制。

李渊回到朝堂，府中其他人也能出门了，只是不能参加宴请。李玄霸和李世民当然也复学了。

高颎和宇文弼每日待在藏书阁，虽不参与朝政，但对朝政之事仍旧十分灵通。

他们得到杨广的诏令后，心情都很复杂。

于是，他们二人便来了一次共同授课，教导李玄霸和李世民解读杨广的诏令。

李世民看到增加殿内省等官僚机构，道：“莫非是陛下嫌弃现在的官吏权力过大，所以需要细分？”

高颎、宇文弼和李玄霸齐齐看向李世民。

李世民疑惑：“我说得不对？我觉得就是这样！”

他想了想，使劲点了点头，十分自信道：“肯定是这样！”

李玄霸移开视线。来了来了，二哥的“自信爆棚状态”已经加载了。

不过二哥确实说对了，不愧是二哥，天生的政治直觉。

高颎深深叹了口气：“你这个孩童都能看出来，朝中大臣肯定都看出来了。”

宇文弼问李玄霸：“大德呢？你看出了什么？”

李玄霸道：“当年先帝继位时，为安抚勋贵，不仅认可先朝爵位，还设置了上柱国等大量功勋散官，凭借门荫即可做官。这样勋贵家家有爵位，代代有官做。先帝与诸勋贵承诺，共享天下富贵。”

高颎再次重重地叹了口气，道：“继续。”

李玄霸道：“陛下将公侯伯子男五等爵位只留公侯，缩减爵位数量；贬上柱国以下至都督的十一等高品散官为九大夫，不仅缩减了散官数量，也降低了散官品阶；前朝爵位不再沿袭，必须寻求立功重新封爵……如是种种，都是削弱勋贵的地位，寻求帝王集权。”

李世民连连点头：“我懂了，陛下是不想和勋贵共享天下了。”

这次连宇文弼都叹气了。

高颎见二人态度，问道：“你们似乎不认为此举有错？”

李世民疑惑：“史书中的明君多是大权在握，陛下这么做，不是所有皇帝都会做的事吗？”

高颎语塞。

宇文弼道：“那若是勋贵不满意呢？”

李世民道：“掀起叛乱吗？那就平叛呗。”

李世民用疑惑的眼神看着老师们。这么简单的问题，还需要问？

高颎和宇文弼看着李世民，表情跟打翻了调色盘似的。

李世民品出点味来：“老师认为陛下这样做不对吗？”

高颎没有回答，他问李玄霸道：“大德，你认为呢？”

李玄霸装作思考了一会儿，道：“削弱勋贵，加强君权，这确实是皇帝都想做的事。开国时皇帝需要和勋贵妥协。但当王朝稳固，皇帝若想更进一步，打造一个盛世，肯定就需要收拢权力，压制勋贵。因为国家的利益，和勋贵个人的利益肯定是冲突的。”

李世民点头如捣蒜：“阿玄说得太对了。我们唐国公府都是不缴税的。国家兴盛需要多收税。唐国公府想要富贵就要占领更多的田地，于是国家能收到的税就少了。嗯嗯，就是这样。”

李玄霸：“……倒也别拿我们家作比喻。”

李世民无所谓道：“不说也是这样，遮遮掩掩干什么？照实说呗。”

李玄霸：“……”哥那坚持要留下玄武门之变详细记录，并且常常感叹玄武门之变细节的少根筋性子现在就有了吗？这就是本性吗！

高颎和宇文弼都仿佛失语，沉默半晌，才继续叹气。

李世民挠头：“老师，你们认为这样做不好吗？”

高颎道：“正如你所说，君王总会走上这一步。只是陛下太急躁了。他若是要削减官爵，就该坐镇京城。可他却老想往外跑，根本定不下性子。”

宇文弼连连叹气道：“我知道陛下很有雄才大略。他要修运河，修东京；要南巡，也要北巡；还要同时削减官爵，收回勋贵特权……这些事的出发点都是对的，但不能同时做啊。如搬运沙土一样，一次搬运一袋沙土，一天就能搬完；一口气把沙土袋子全压在身上，这会出人命。”

李玄霸非常赞同：“没错，所以出人命了。”

高颎、宇文弼、李世民都猛地转头，死死地盯着李玄霸。

李玄霸默默抬起双手，捂住嘴，用眼神告诉他们，自己什么都没说。

高颎和宇文弼见李玄霸这模样，终于知道为何如今花团锦簇的大隋会在二十年内改朝换代了。

他们本来想了许多，比如皇帝和年长的皇子都早逝，没有合适的继承人，于是群雄重启争端之类。

结果大隋是这样完蛋的吗？悟了悟了。

高颎和宇文弼齐齐捂住胸口，有点喘不过气。

李世民和李玄霸赶紧起身帮两位老师顺气。

李世民：“老师啊，别激动，阿玄什么都没说。”

李玄霸：“对对对，我什么都没说。”

李世民：“你看我，无论听到了什么，都当作没听见。”

李玄霸：“对对对，老师，当作没听见可好？”

高颎和宇文弼一人手持一把扫帚，把李世民和李玄霸赶出了门。

李世民对李玄霸叹气：“阿玄，你可长点心吧，别再胡言乱语了。你若进宫了也胡言乱语，哥哥就要陪你去刑场了。”

李玄霸道：“我还没那么蠢……既然早早被赶出来了，去书铺看看？”

李世民点头，压低声音道：“顺带去偷偷吃烤羊肉，嘻嘻。”守孝什么的，才不给她守呢。

许久没吃撒了许多香料的烤羊肉，李玄霸也馋了，便默许了。

二人乘坐马车来到书铺，书铺门口排了长龙。

原来今日书铺正好补了一批高颎、宇文弼注解版《尚书》的货，所以西市一开门，学子们就用百米冲刺的速度赶来排队。

李玄霸和李世民从后门进去时，正好看见掌柜在和一个相貌堂堂的佩剑青年商谈什么。

见到两位主人到来，掌柜立刻拱手道：“事情巧了，二郎君，三郎君，这里有位大人想要本店帮忙印刷诗文集，小的正想把诗文集送给二郎君三郎君看看。”

这是李玄霸在独孤老夫人逝世后，和母亲商议的新生意。

现在唐国公府的书铺都能任由窦夫人使用，西市书铺的印刷儒经又已经得到了文人们的认可，窦夫人便和李玄霸商议，扩大印刷书籍的售卖范围，增加帮文人印刷出版诗文集的业务。

当然不是随便一个人就能让唐国公府帮忙印刷诗文集，得有国子监教授的举荐信，还得把诗文集给国公府先过目。

李玄霸和李世民对那人拱手自我介绍。

那人笑道：“原来是唐国公府有名的神童双生子。在下房乔，与李秀才一样，在先帝开皇十七年，于分科举荐考试入朝。”

李世民笑道：“与阿玄一样是秀才吗？”

房乔摇头：“在下才疏学浅，未能通过秀才科。”

李世民立刻道：“未通过秀才科也不是才疏学浅啊，只是比起方略，有其他更擅长的学问而已。能被举荐到陛下面前并通过考试，肯定都是天下罕有的人才。诗文集不需要看了，我相信房兄。对吧，阿玄？嗯？阿玄，你发什么呆？”

李玄霸脑子急速转动，总觉得“房乔”这个名字很耳熟，但一时记忆卡壳，记不起来。
chunks.englishText:
Observing the mourning period required a vegetarian diet, strictly forbidding all meat and animal fats. With no fresh fruits or vegetables available in the first lunar month, they had been subsisting on nothing but rice and flour for days. It was bland and unpalatable, causing even the already frail Li Xuanba to lose more weight.

Li Xuanba felt he could still hold on. He would endure for a while longer; once Li Yuan was recalled to the imperial court and allowed to leave the residence, he could secretly boil eggs to supplement his nutrition.

However, his family seemed unable to bear the sight of his decline.

While the mourning period demanded a vegetarian diet, exceptions were made for children, pregnant women, and the infirm. These individuals were permitted to consume meat, provided they abstained from alcohol, banquets, and pungent aromatics like ginger, garlic, and chives.

After all, one could not let the family members perish while observing the rites of mourning.

Li Xuanba, being both young and perpetually sickly, naturally fell into the category of those who could be "accommodated." Yet, until Li Yuan brought the matter up himself, Li Xuanba did not want to approach his grief-stricken father, lest Li Yuan think he harbored resentment toward the late Matriarch.

Since his fourth and fifth sisters were able to bring him flatbreads laced with animal fat, their mother must have been aware of it. The fact that they had brought them secretly suggested that their father was still in the dark.

Li Xuanba’s mind raced. He thanked his sisters and quickly shared the flatbreads with his brothers to fill their stomachs.

Li Siniang whispered, "In a few more days, you will be able to eat meat. Fourth Brother made a fuss, so he has already started eating boiled meat."

Li Xuanba said with genuine sincerity, "Fourth Brother is truly a good person. I am truly grateful to him this time."

Li Shimin and Li Zhiyun nodded vigorously. For the first time, they felt a profound fondness for this brother of theirs.

...

Just three days later, the brothers were indeed allowed to eat eggs, dairy, and meat.

Later, Li Siniang and Li Wuniang also began to eat meat quietly; only Li Yuan, Lady Dou, and Li Jiancheng continued their vegetarian diet.

Naturally, the pregnant Lady Zheng in Li Jiancheng’s inner courtyard had long since ceased her vegetarian mourning diet. Lady Dou meticulously arranged Lady Zheng’s life and even wrote to the Zheng family, asking if they needed to send a matron to attend to her, thinking it might make her more comfortable.

The Zheng family of Xingyang had originally written back to Lady Dou, saying they were looking for a matron experienced in childbirth. A few days later, however, they sent another letter, telling Lady Dou to make her own arrangements and that they would not overstep their bounds.

Lady Dou was puzzled until Li Yuan handed her a letter from Zheng Jibo.

Zheng Jibo was the father-in-law to whom Li Jiancheng was betrothed.

Before even opening the letter, Lady Dou knew why the Zheng family had abandoned the idea of sending someone. Upon opening it, it was as she expected: Zheng Jibo was worried that if the child in Lady Zheng’s womb turned out to be the eldest son by a concubine, giving her too much preferential treatment would undermine the position of Li Jiancheng’s legitimate heir.

"Sigh," Lady Dou complained, "They are already worrying about discord between the eldest son by a concubine and the legitimate heir."

Li Yuan remained silent.

In his own family, even brothers born of the same mother had become a farce, and his second and third sons were still mere children. He really couldn't say that Zheng Jibo’s concerns were unfounded.

"The Emperor is summoning me back to the capital and wants me to accompany him on his northern inspection," Li Yuan said to Lady Dou. "I leave the children in your care. Especially Third Son’s health—you must pay extra attention to him."

Lady Dou replied, "Yes, my lord, rest assured."

Li Yuan’s expression was downcast. "Mm, I am naturally at ease." Now that his mother had passed, there was indeed nothing left in the household that would cause his wife distress.

Ten days later, Li Yuan was indeed recalled to the imperial court, his official titles restored.

As soon as Li Yuan returned to the court, Emperor Yang Guang carried out a major undertaking: the reform of the official system.

With Li Yuan back at court, the others in the household were also free to go out, though they were still forbidden from attending banquets. Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, of course, resumed their studies.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi spent their days in the library; though they no longer participated in state affairs, they remained well-informed.

Upon receiving Emperor Yang Guang’s edict, both men felt a complex mix of emotions.

Consequently, they held a joint lesson to teach Li Xuanba and Li Shimin how to interpret the Emperor’s decree.

Seeing the addition of the Palace Administration and other bureaucratic institutions, Li Shimin remarked, "Could it be that His Majesty feels the current officials hold too much power and thus needs to subdivide them?"

Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Li Xuanba all turned to look at Li Shimin in unison.

Li Shimin was puzzled. "Did I say something wrong? I think that’s exactly it!"

He thought for a moment, nodded vigorously, and said with great confidence, "It must be that!"

Li Xuanba looked away. Here it comes, here it comes—Second Brother’s "overflowing confidence" state has already loaded.

However, Second Brother was indeed correct. As expected of him, he had an innate political intuition.

Gao Jiong sighed deeply. "If a child like you can see it, the ministers at court must have certainly seen it as well."

Yuwen Bi asked Li Xuanba, "Dade, what do you see?"

Li Xuanba said, "When the late Emperor ascended the throne, in order to appease the nobility, he not only recognized the titles of the previous dynasty but also established a large number of honorary titles like 'Supreme Pillar of State,' allowing men to hold office through hereditary privilege. Thus, every noble family had titles, and every generation held office. The late Emperor and the nobles promised to share the wealth of the realm."

Gao Jiong sighed heavily again. "Continue."

Li Xuanba said, "His Majesty has limited the five ranks of nobility to only Duke and Marquis, reducing the number of titles; he has demoted the eleven high-ranking honorary titles from Supreme Pillar of State down to Governor to the rank of 'Great Physician,' not only reducing the number of honorary titles but also lowering their status; titles from the previous dynasty are no longer hereditary and must be earned through new merit... All of these actions are aimed at weakening the nobility and centralizing imperial power."

Li Shimin nodded repeatedly. "I understand. His Majesty no longer wants to share the world with the nobles."

This time, even Yuwen Bi sighed.

Seeing their attitude, Gao Jiong asked, "You do not seem to think this is wrong?"

Li Shimin was confused. "Most of the wise monarchs in history books held absolute power. Isn't this what every emperor does?"

Gao Jiong was speechless.

Yuwen Bi asked, "And what if the nobles are dissatisfied?"

Li Shimin replied, "Start a rebellion? Then we just suppress it."

Li Shimin looked at his teachers with a puzzled expression. Such a simple question—did they really need to ask?

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi looked at Li Shimin, their expressions as chaotic as an overturned palette.

Li Shimin sensed something. "Do the teachers think His Majesty is wrong to do this?"

Gao Jiong did not answer. He asked Li Xuanba, "Dade, what do you think?"

Li Xuanba pretended to ponder for a moment before saying, "Weakening the nobility and strengthening imperial power is indeed something every emperor desires. At the founding of a dynasty, an emperor must compromise with the nobles. But once the dynasty is stable, if the emperor wishes to go further and build a golden age, he must consolidate power and suppress the nobility. Because the interests of the state and the personal interests of the nobles are inevitably in conflict."

Li Shimin nodded like a pounding pestle. "Ah Xuan is absolutely right. Our Tang Duke’s mansion doesn't pay taxes. For the country to flourish, it needs to collect more taxes. If the Tang Duke’s mansion wants to remain wealthy, it must occupy more land, which means the state collects less tax. Yes, yes, that’s exactly it."

Li Xuanba: "...Please don't use our own family as an example."

Li Shimin shrugged. "It’s true even if I don't say it, why cover it up? Just speak the truth."

Li Xuanba: "..." Is this the same brother who would later insist on keeping a detailed record of the Xuanwu Gate Incident and often lament its details? Was this his nature all along?!

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi seemed to have lost the power of speech. They remained silent for a long time before sighing again.

Li Shimin scratched his head. "Teachers, do you think this is bad?"

Gao Jiong said, "As you said, a monarch will always take this step. It is just that His Majesty is too impatient. If he wants to reduce official titles, he should sit firmly in the capital. But he is always wanting to run outside; he simply cannot settle his temperament."

Yuwen Bi sighed repeatedly. "I know His Majesty has great ambition. He wants to build the Grand Canal, build the Eastern Capital; he wants to tour the south and the north; and he wants to simultaneously reduce titles and revoke noble privileges... The starting points for these things are all correct, but they cannot be done all at once. It is like carrying sand: if you carry one bag at a time, you can finish in a day. But if you try to pile all the bags on your back at once, it will cost you your life."

Li Xuanba agreed wholeheartedly. "Exactly, that is why it cost him his life."

Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Li Shimin all whipped their heads around to stare fixedly at Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba silently raised his hands to cover his mouth, telling them with his eyes that he hadn't said anything.

Seeing Li Xuanba’s expression, Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi finally understood why the flourishing Great Sui would change dynasties within twenty years.

They had originally thought of many reasons, such as the Emperor and his older princes dying young, leaving no suitable heir, and thus the warlords restarting the struggle.

So, this is how the Great Sui ended? They understood now. They truly understood.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi clutched their chests simultaneously, struggling to catch their breath.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba hurriedly stood up to help their teachers catch their breath.

Li Shimin: "Teachers, don't get excited, Ah Xuan didn't say anything."

Li Xuanba: "Right, right, I didn't say anything."

Li Shimin: "Look at me—no matter what I heard, I’ll pretend I heard nothing."

Li Xuanba: "Right, right, teachers, let’s just pretend we heard nothing, shall we?"

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi each grabbed a broom and chased Li Shimin and Li Xuanba out the door.

Li Shimin sighed to Li Xuanba, "Ah Xuan, you really need to be more careful. Stop spouting nonsense. If you go into the palace and spout such nonsense, I’ll have to accompany you to the execution ground."

Li Xuanba said, "I'm not that stupid... Since we were kicked out early, shall we go check out the bookstore?"

Li Shimin nodded and lowered his voice. "And sneak off to eat some roasted lamb, hehe." Mourning or not, he wasn't going to let that stop him.

Having not eaten roasted lamb sprinkled with plenty of spices for a long time, Li Xuanba was also craving it, so he tacitly agreed.

The two took a carriage to the bookstore, where a long line had already formed.

It turned out that the bookstore had just restocked the version of the *Book of Documents* annotated by Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi. As soon as the West Market opened, scholars had sprinted over to queue.

When Li Xuanba and Li Shimin entered through the back door, they happened to see the shopkeeper discussing something with a handsome young man wearing a sword.

Seeing the two young masters arrive, the shopkeeper immediately bowed. "What a coincidence, Second Young Master, Third Young Master. There is a gentleman here who wants our shop to help print a collection of poetry and essays, and I was just about to show it to you both."

This was a new business venture Li Xuanba had discussed with his mother after the passing of the late Matriarch, Lady Dugu.

Now that the Tang Duke’s mansion’s bookstore was entirely at Lady Dou’s disposal, and the bookstore’s printing of Confucian classics in the West Market had already gained the approval of the literati, Lady Dou had discussed with Li Xuanba the idea of expanding the range of printed books for sale and adding a service to help scholars print and publish their own poetry and essay collections.

Of course, not just anyone could have the Tang Duke’s mansion print their work; they needed a letter of recommendation from a professor at the Imperial Academy, and the collection had to be reviewed by the Duke’s mansion first.

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin bowed and introduced themselves to the man.

The man smiled. "So, it is the famous prodigy twins of the Tang Duke’s mansion. I am Fang Qiao. Like the Li scholars, I entered the court through the recommendation examinations in the seventeenth year of the Kaihuang era."

Li Shimin smiled. "Are you a *xiucai* scholar like Ah Xuan?"

Fang Qiao shook his head. "I am untalented and failed to pass the *xiucai* examination."

Li Shimin immediately said, "Failing the *xiucai* examination doesn't mean you are untalented; it just means you have other strengths beyond strategy. To be recommended to His Majesty and pass the examination, you must be a rare talent in the world. There is no need to look at the collection; I trust Brother Fang. Right, Ah Xuan? Hmm? Ah Xuan, why are you spacing out?"

Li Xuanba’s mind was racing. He felt the name "Fang Qiao" was very familiar, but his memory hit a wall, and he couldn't quite place it.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第40章 经典的一见如故
chunks.chineseText:
第40章 经典的一见如故

=
　　“没什么。”李玄霸回过神， 他的视线落在了诗文集上。
　　房乔带着矜持的笑容，将诗文集递给李玄霸：“请李秀才指点。”
　　李世民道：“房兄别这么客气。我字大雄，阿玄字大德， 呼我们的字便好。”
　　房乔的笑容有一瞬的僵硬。
　　李玄霸瞥了二哥一眼， 想在心里拆穿， 但他经过了短暂的卡壳，在看到诗文集的扉页时已经想起这个“房乔”是谁。
　　诗文集扉页是房乔的自我介绍，清河房氏， 其父司隶刺史房彦谦，姓房名乔字……呵，字玄龄。
　　清河房氏虽不是“五姓七望”， 也是能与清河崔氏攀上姻亲的大贵族，在京中人数不少。
　　李建成与“五姓七望”的荥阳郑氏联姻后， 山东郡姓纷纷向李建成表达善意， 与李建成推杯换盏的狐朋狗友中就有清河房氏的人，李玄霸见过不少。
　　若不是如此，他在唐代听到一个姓“房”的人，肯定脑海里第一反应就是“他是不是房玄龄的谁”。
　　没想到真的见到房玄龄本人时，他居然在房玄龄自报本名时， 记忆卡了几十秒的壳。
　　不过后世知道房玄龄名乔的人也不多，李玄霸还算“知识渊博”了。
　　弱冠的人互相交往都是以字相称。
　　之前李世民和李玄霸自我介绍的时候没有介绍字， 是不太习惯用字忘记了。
　　但房乔这样已经快而立之年的人如果自我介绍的时候没有介绍字，就是委婉地告诉对方“我不想和你深交”的意思。
　　但显然，李世民脑袋里没有这根弦。
　　现在李世民单独介绍他和李玄霸的字， 就把房乔架在了柴堆上。
　　李玄霸本来想告诉二哥房乔的想法， 但发现房乔就是房玄龄后， 李玄霸就给了未来房相一个面子， 没给他在未来领导那里上眼药。
　　房乔默默地看着李世民。
　　李世民只是一个小孩，他应该没有坏心思，唉。
　　房乔再次拱手：“不敢不敢。”
　　李世民道：“有什么不敢？你有官职在身，我只是一个孩童。”
　　房乔：“……”他更尴尬了。
　　李玄霸颇有兴趣地看着李世民用“天真无邪”打得未来的房相措手不及。
　　李玄霸没有隐藏自己的表情。房乔很快就看出李玄霸在看自己笑话。
　　他看看一脸热情的李世民，又看看一脸与年龄不符的意味深长微笑的李玄霸，头皮有些发麻。
　　房乔立刻猜到，李玄霸应该是觉察出了自己不想深交的意图，李世民肯定没有。
　　他虽自傲，也知道不能得罪人，立刻道：“那在下就恭敬不如从命。在下字玄龄，小郎君也可称呼在下的字。”
　　李世民笑道：“我还是叫你房兄吧。我还小，现在就叫你的字，对你不太尊重。等我再大一些，我们再平等相交。”
　　房乔：“……”如果对面不是一个孩童，他都怀疑对面之人想要招揽自己了。
　　“扑哧。”李玄霸忍不住笑了。
　　李世民疑惑：“阿玄，你笑什么？”
　　李玄霸道：“我天生一副笑脸。”
　　李世民立刻伸出手扯住李玄霸的脸颊：“哎哟，真的吗？再给哥哥笑一个。”
　　“去去去。”李玄霸使劲拍打二哥作怪的手。
　　李世民笑嘻嘻地松开手：“你常说一个人读书无聊，今日相遇就是缘分，阿玄何不做东请房兄到隔壁酒楼……饮子铺一聚，顺带说一说文集印刷的事？房兄，别看我家阿玄年纪小，但书铺的事都是他做主。”
　　李玄霸揉着脸道：“是我、你、娘、三姊都能做主。”
　　李世民双手抬起，枕在后脑勺道：“其实就是你做主。”
　　李玄霸叹气，对房乔道：“如果房兄不嫌弃，可否赏脸？”
　　房乔道：“小郎君客气了。”
　　李世民笑道：“我也是小郎君，他也是小郎君，房兄你这样叫，我们分不清。要不叫我李二，叫他李三，要么称呼我们的字，你自己选吧。”
　　房乔再次无语。这个孩童怎么……怎么如此霸道？但这霸道偏偏不引人讨厌，只是让人有些难以招架。
　　李玄霸发现了房乔的窘迫，可不会帮着房乔：“房兄就称呼我为李三郎吧。”
　　李世民捧腹大笑：“阿玄，你又来了。你究竟是对‘大德’这个字有多不满？房兄啊，我和你说，你一定要叫阿玄大德，让阿玄早日习惯。取字之后都是以字行走世间，由得他不乐意？”
　　李玄霸没好气道：“是是是，大雄。”
　　李世民：“啊？叫我做什么？”
　　李玄霸磨牙。
　　李世民歪头。
　　房乔右手虚握放在嘴前，遮住了嘴角的笑意。
　　这对双生子真是有趣。他想起自己的身体，又有些黯然。
　　李世民敏锐地察觉了房乔的黯然，道：“房兄可有什么难事？”
　　李玄霸叹了口气，道：“你别问了。交浅言深，会让人尴尬。”
　　李世民道：“好吧。房兄，抱歉，是我逾越了。”
　　房乔忙摆手：“无事无事。只是看着小郎君……”
　　李世民露出了不赞同的眼神。
　　房乔突然觉得自己的扭捏实在是有些可笑，便失笑道：“只是看着李二郎和李三郎，有些遗憾自己没有子嗣罢了。”
　　李世民挠头：“这个，我也没办法解决。要不你摸摸我和弟弟的脑袋，说不定能沾点福气？长辈们就喜欢这样做。”
　　李玄霸有些震惊了。
　　自家二哥挺骄傲的一个人，居然如此亲近房玄龄？这就是眼缘吗？
　　等等，历史中的唐太宗第一次见到房玄龄时也是“一见如旧”。难道这个“一见如旧”不是史书记载的套话，而是描述的真实情况？
　　李玄霸肃然起敬。有一种历史名场面在自己面前徐徐展开的史诗感。
　　但现在，他挡住了二哥向前伸的脑袋，阻止二哥把自己的脑袋凑到房乔的手中。
　　看看房乔！尴尬得脸都红了！
　　“不是去饮子铺吗？我渴了。”李玄霸道，“房兄，请移步一叙？”
　　房乔真想立刻开溜。他有些后悔来书铺了。
　　房乔十八岁科举入仕，一直蹉跎至今。
　　前些日子，他重病一场，几乎濒死。妻子对他不离不弃，艰难地照顾他至痊愈。
　　房乔身体好些之后，就一改之前倨傲清高，想要尽快谋求一个实职，为妻子赚得一个更舒适的生活。
　　他观察一段时间后，瞄准了唐国公府这家引发了文坛地震的小小书铺，敏锐地察觉到了其中蕴含的机遇——纵使自己不能入了唐国公的眼，文集印刷后传播更广，一定也会有人能慧眼识英才。
　　房乔的父亲房彦谦因为刚直得罪权贵而被外贬，在京中为御史大夫时，他曾与时任左仆射的高颎有着几分浅薄交情。
　　房乔原本自傲，并不愿意走父辈的门路。而且他还发现高颎已经失去了皇帝的信任，与高颎走得太近恐怕会被连累。
　　现在高颎自退一步，皇帝似乎没有赶尽杀绝的意思。房乔咬牙去找了高颎，求了一纸推荐信，只请求能在高颎弟子的书铺印刷文集而已，高颎欣然同意。
　　所以房乔虽尴尬得想转头就走，但还是咬牙跟了上来。
　　唐国公的二郎君和三郎君对他表示了亲近，这正是他想追求的。他不能由着本性躲避。
　　李玄霸把房乔亲笔书写的文集很自然地揣进了怀里。
　　他决定了，这成为他第二件陪葬品。
　　第一件陪葬品是二哥的作业本。
　　李世民和李玄霸带着房乔去了隔壁的饮子铺。
　　那家饮子铺被李昭找关系盘了下来，正好作为他们出游时落脚的地方。
　　李昭还在想办法买下附近更多的店铺，将书铺的规模扩大。
　　饮子铺许多饮品是出自李玄霸之手。关于“加奶、加糖可自由选择”的做法，给这家饮子铺积攒了不少人气。其他饮子铺也跟着模仿。
　　李玄霸选的是没有添加任何佐料的花茶。
　　李世民虽然喜欢甜口，但李玄霸在他耳边一直唠叨，说吃糖吃多了的坏处。特别是他在换牙了。换牙期间吃太多糖，会长一口烂牙。
　　李玄霸还带李世民去拔牙的医师那里坐了一天，特别观察了那些烂牙的小孩。
　　李世民被吓得哇哇大哭，事后又气又恼，一天没和李玄霸说话。
　　那之后，李世民就比较克制自己吃甜食的欲|望。每日早晚和饭后都要努力刷牙，对刷牙有了异样的执着。
　　所以现在李世民也选了和弟弟同款无奶无糖花茶。
　　花茶是晒干的桂花，虽说水没有甜味，却有一种甜香扑鼻的感觉。李世民抿了一口桂花茶，有些惆怅。他居然已经习惯了如此寡淡的饮子，偶尔喝到甜奶时，竟觉得不解渴了。
　　房乔见李世民和李玄霸喝着干花泡的饮子，并称呼这为“花茶”，感到一阵雅意。
　　他也要了同款花茶。
　　“如同花露一般，为何不叫花露？”房乔对桂花茶十分喜爱。
　　李世民道：“我也是这么说的。但阿玄说泡出来的叫花茶，花露的工艺更复杂。现在阿玄犯懒，不肯做。等他做出来，我送给房兄尝尝。”
　　李玄霸叹气道：“你都这么说了，我回家就琢磨。”
　　李世民笑道：“赶紧琢磨去，别懒。”
　　房乔有些羡慕：“采花为露，真是一件雅事。”
　　李世民使劲点头：“阿玄就是喜欢这些风雅的事。”
　　李玄霸道：“别夸我了，你们慢慢聊。我先看看房兄的文集。”
　　李世民立刻把脑袋凑过来：“我也要看！一起。”
　　李玄霸被李世民挤得身形一晃，差点把水杯打翻。
　　他叹了口气，挂着一对倒三角死鱼眼，和二哥一起看文集。
　　房乔握着水杯的手指微微用力，心中生出些紧张。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 40: A Classic Case of "Kindred Spirits at First Sight"

"It’s nothing." Li Xuanba regained his composure, his gaze falling upon the collection of poems and essays.

Fang Qiao wore a reserved smile as he handed the collection to Li Xuanba. "I would appreciate your guidance, Scholar Li."

Li Shimin interjected, "Brother Fang, there is no need for such formality. My courtesy name is Daxiong, and Ah Xuan’s is Dade. Please, just address us by our courtesy names."

Fang Qiao’s smile stiffened for a fleeting moment.

Li Xuanba glanced at his Second Brother, tempted to expose him on the spot. However, after a brief mental hiccup, he had realized exactly who this "Fang Qiao" was the moment he saw the title page of the collection.

The title page contained Fang Qiao’s self-introduction: of the Qinghe Fang clan, son of the Sili Inspector Fang Yanqian, surname Fang, given name Qiao, courtesy name... ah, Xuanling.

Though the Qinghe Fang clan was not among the "Five Surnames and Seven Clans," they were still a major aristocratic family capable of intermarrying with the Qinghe Cui clan, and they held significant influence in the capital.

Ever since Li Jiancheng had married into the Yingyang Zheng clan—one of the "Five Surnames and Seven Clans"—the Shandong gentry had vied to express their goodwill toward him. Among the drinking companions who clinked glasses with Li Jiancheng, there were many from the Qinghe Fang clan, and Li Xuanba had met quite a few of them.

Had it not been for this, hearing the surname "Fang" in the Tang Dynasty would have immediately made his first thought: "Is he related to Fang Xuanling?"

He never expected that when he finally met the real Fang Xuanling, he would experience a mental blank for several seconds while the man was introducing himself.

Then again, not many people in later generations knew that Fang Xuanling’s given name was Qiao, so Li Xuanba could still consider himself "well-read."

When young men who had reached the age of capping (twenty) interacted, it was customary to address each other by their courtesy names.

Earlier, when Li Shimin and Li Xuanba introduced themselves, they hadn't mentioned their courtesy names simply because they weren't used to using them and had forgotten.

But for someone like Fang Qiao, who was nearly thirty, failing to introduce himself by his courtesy name was a polite, indirect way of telling the other party, "I do not wish to be on intimate terms with you."

Clearly, however, Li Shimin didn't have that particular string in his bow.

Now that Li Shimin had unilaterally introduced both his and Li Xuanba’s courtesy names, he had effectively put Fang Qiao on the spot.

Li Xuanba had originally intended to point out Fang Qiao’s intentions to his Second Brother, but upon realizing the man was the future Chancellor Fang, he decided to give the future statesman some face and refrain from causing trouble for him in front of his future boss.

Fang Qiao looked at Li Shimin in silence.

*He is just a child; he surely has no malicious intent. Sigh.*

Fang Qiao cupped his hands again. "I dare not, I dare not."

Li Shimin said, "What is there to dare not? You hold an official position, and I am but a child."

Fang Qiao: "..." He felt even more awkward.

Li Xuanba watched with great interest as Li Shimin used his "innocence" to catch the future Chancellor off guard.

Li Xuanba made no effort to hide his expression. Fang Qiao quickly realized that Li Xuanba was watching him make a fool of himself.

He looked at the enthusiastic Li Shimin, then at Li Xuanba, who wore a meaningful smile quite at odds with his age, and felt his scalp tingle.

Fang Qiao immediately guessed that Li Xuanba must have sensed his intention to keep a distance, while Li Shimin certainly had not.

Though proud, he knew he couldn't afford to offend people, so he immediately said, "Then I shall defer to your wishes. My courtesy name is Xuanling; you may address me by it, young master."

Li Shimin laughed. "I think I’ll stick with Brother Fang. I am still young, and to address you by your courtesy name now would be disrespectful. When I am a bit older, we can interact as equals."

Fang Qiao: "..." If the person opposite him weren't a child, he would have suspected the boy was trying to recruit him.

"Pfft." Li Xuanba couldn't help but laugh.

Li Shimin looked puzzled. "Ah Xuan, what are you laughing at?"

Li Xuanba replied, "I was born with a smiling face."

Li Shimin immediately reached out and pinched Li Xuanba’s cheek. "Oh? Is that so? Give your brother another smile then."

"Go away, go away." Li Xuanba swatted at his Second Brother’s mischievous hand.

Li Shimin let go with a grin. "You often say that reading alone is boring. Meeting today is fate; why don't you play the host, Ah Xuan, and invite Brother Fang to the drink shop next door for a gathering? We can discuss the printing of your collection while we're at it. Brother Fang, don't let Ah Xuan’s age fool you—he’s the one who makes all the decisions regarding the bookstore."

Li Xuanba rubbed his cheek and said, "It’s you, me, Mother, and Third Sister who all have a say."

Li Shimin put his hands behind his head. "In reality, it’s you who decides."

Li Xuanba sighed and said to Fang Qiao, "If Brother Fang doesn't mind, would you do us the honor?"

Fang Qiao said, "You are too kind, young master."

Li Shimin laughed. "I am a young master, and he is a young master. If you call us that, we can't tell who you mean. How about you call me Li Er and him Li San, or just use our courtesy names? You choose."

Fang Qiao was speechless once more. How could this child be... so overbearing? Yet, this overbearing nature wasn't annoying; it was just difficult to handle.

Li Xuanba noticed Fang Qiao’s embarrassment and had no intention of helping him out. "Brother Fang, just call me Li Sanlang."

Li Shimin burst into laughter, clutching his stomach. "Ah Xuan, you’re doing it again. Just how dissatisfied are you with the name 'Dade'? Brother Fang, let me tell you, you must call Ah Xuan 'Dade' to get him used to it. Once a courtesy name is given, one walks the world by it—does he really have a choice?"

Li Xuanba retorted, "Yes, yes, Daxiong."

Li Shimin: "Huh? Did you call me?"

Li Xuanba gritted his teeth.

Li Shimin tilted his head.

Fang Qiao held his right hand in a loose fist before his mouth, masking the smile at the corner of his lips.

These twins were truly interesting. He thought of his own health and felt a pang of melancholy.

Li Shimin keenly sensed Fang Qiao’s sudden gloom. "Brother Fang, are you facing some hardship?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Don't ask. Speaking of deep matters when the acquaintance is shallow only leads to awkwardness."

Li Shimin said, "Very well. Brother Fang, my apologies; I overstepped."

Fang Qiao hurriedly waved his hand. "No, no. It’s just that seeing you young masters..."

Li Shimin gave him a look of disapproval.

Fang Qiao suddenly felt his own hesitation was quite ridiculous, so he laughed self-deprecatingly. "It is just that seeing Li Erlang and Li Sanlang, I feel a bit of regret that I have no children of my own."

Li Shimin scratched his head. "Well, I can't solve that for you. How about you pat our heads? Maybe you’ll catch some of our good fortune? Our elders love doing that."

Li Xuanba was stunned.

His Second Brother, usually such a proud person, was actually being this intimate with Fang Xuanling? Was this what they called "clicking" with someone?

Wait, in history, when Emperor Taizong of Tang first met Fang Xuanling, it was also described as "kindred spirits at first sight." Could this "kindred spirits" not be a cliché recorded by historians, but a description of the actual situation?

Li Xuanba felt a sense of reverence. There was an epic feeling to seeing a historical scene unfolding right before his eyes.

But for now, he blocked his Second Brother’s head, preventing him from leaning into Fang Qiao’s hand.

Look at Fang Qiao! He was blushing from embarrassment!

"Aren't we going to the drink shop? I'm thirsty," Li Xuanba said. "Brother Fang, shall we move there to continue our conversation?"

Fang Qiao really wanted to bolt immediately. He was starting to regret coming to the bookstore.

Fang Qiao had entered officialdom through the imperial examinations at eighteen, only to be left languishing ever since.

Some time ago, he had fallen gravely ill, nearly dying. His wife had never left his side, painstakingly caring for him until he recovered.

Once his health improved, Fang Qiao shed his former arrogance and aloofness, eager to secure a substantive position to earn a more comfortable life for his wife.

After observing for a while, he had set his sights on this small bookstore owned by the Duke of Tang’s estate, which had caused a stir in the literary world. He had keenly sensed the opportunity within—even if he couldn't catch the Duke’s eye, the wider circulation of his essays after printing would surely lead to someone with a discerning eye recognizing his talent.

Fang Qiao’s father, Fang Yanqian, had been demoted for his uprightness in offending the powerful. When he served as Censor-in-Chief in the capital, he had a shallow acquaintance with Gao Jiong, the then-Left Minister.

Fang Qiao had originally been too proud to use his father’s connections. Furthermore, he had noticed that Gao Jiong had lost the Emperor’s trust, and getting too close to him might lead to being implicated.

Now that Gao Jiong had stepped back, the Emperor didn't seem to have any intention of wiping him out. Fang Qiao had gritted his teeth and gone to Gao Jiong to beg for a letter of recommendation, asking only to print his collection at the shop of Gao Jiong’s disciple, to which Gao Jiong had readily agreed.

And so, even though Fang Qiao was so embarrassed he wanted to turn and leave, he gritted his teeth and followed them.

The Duke of Tang’s second and third sons were showing him favor—this was exactly what he was pursuing. He could not let his nature get in the way.

Li Xuanba tucked the collection of essays, written in Fang Qiao’s own hand, into his robes quite naturally.

He had decided: this would be his second burial object.

The first was his Second Brother’s workbook.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba brought Fang Qiao to the drink shop next door.

That shop had been acquired by Li Zhao through his connections, serving perfectly as a place for them to rest during their outings.

Li Zhao was still looking for ways to buy more neighboring shops to expand the bookstore’s scale.

Many of the drinks in the shop were created by Li Xuanba. The practice of "free choice of added milk and sugar" had garnered the shop quite a bit of popularity, and other shops had begun to imitate it.

Li Xuanba chose a flower tea without any additives.

Although Li Shimin liked sweet things, Li Xuanba had been nagging him constantly about the downsides of eating too much sugar, especially since he was in the middle of changing teeth. Eating too much sugar during this period would lead to a mouth full of rotten teeth.

Li Xuanba had even taken Li Shimin to sit for a day at the physician’s office where teeth were pulled, specifically to observe the children with rotten teeth.

Li Shimin had been scared into wailing, and afterwards, he was so angry and annoyed that he didn't speak to Li Xuanba for a whole day.

Since then, Li Shimin had been more restrained in his desire for sweets. He brushed his teeth diligently every morning, evening, and after meals, developing an unusual obsession with brushing.

So, Li Shimin now chose the same sugar-free, milk-free flower tea as his brother.

The flower tea was made of dried osmanthus. Although the water had no sweetness, it had a sweet, fragrant aroma. Li Shimin took a sip of the osmanthus tea, feeling a bit melancholy. He had actually grown accustomed to such bland drinks; occasionally, when he drank sweet milk, he found it didn't quench his thirst anymore.

Seeing Li Shimin and Li Xuanba drinking tea made from dried flowers and calling it "flower tea," Fang Qiao felt a sense of elegance.

He ordered the same.

"It is like flower dew; why not call it flower dew?" Fang Qiao was quite fond of the osmanthus tea.

Li Shimin said, "That’s what I said, too. But Ah Xuan says that what is brewed is called flower tea, and the process for flower dew is more complex. Ah Xuan is being lazy right now and won't make it. When he does, I’ll send some for Brother Fang to taste."

Li Xuanba sighed. "Since you’ve said so, I’ll ponder it when I get home."

Li Shimin laughed. "Get to pondering, don't be lazy."

Fang Qiao felt a bit envious. "Gathering flowers to make dew—what a refined pursuit."

Li Shimin nodded vigorously. "Ah Xuan just loves these elegant things."

Li Xuanba said, "Stop praising me. You two chat; I’ll look at Brother Fang’s collection first."

Li Shimin immediately leaned in. "I want to see too! Together."

Li Xuanba was jostled by Li Shimin, nearly tipping over his cup.

He sighed, his eyes turning into dead-fish triangles, and looked at the collection with his Second Brother.

Fang Qiao’s fingers tightened slightly around his cup, a sense of nervousness rising in his heart.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第41章 抱抱摸摸举高高
chunks.chineseText:
第41章 抱抱摸摸举高高

=
　　房乔娴熟五经， 诗赋只是还行，不过出版已经足够了。
　　薄薄的文集很快就翻完。房乔一直捏紧着水杯，一口水都没喝。
　　“阿玄， 比你写得好多了。”李世民感慨。他说的自然是李玄霸真正写的诗赋。
　　李玄霸点头。
　　房乔只以为李世民和李玄霸是在客套。但既然都客套了， 这件事应该就妥了， 他松了一口气。
　　李玄霸道：“先印一百份可好？”
　　房乔惊讶道：“一百份？这么多？”
　　李玄霸道：“不多。”
　　自印书都是要自己先垫钱的。房乔赶紧从袖子里掏铜钱，庆幸自己多拿了些钱来。
　　李玄霸返还了一半的钱，道：“房兄的文集得到了我兄弟二人的认可， 这垫付的钱就少一半了。对其他人也是如此。”
　　李世民：“？”有这个规定？阿玄说有就有吧。
　　李世民笑道：“若不是担心房兄不自在，我和阿玄本想是不收垫付的钱的。但阿玄总说亲兄弟也要明算账，对品行高洁的人而言， 收钱比不收钱更好。”
　　这下轮到李玄霸“？”了。
　　自己临时决定给房玄龄卖点好，虽然知道二哥肯定会配合， 但二哥这瞎话张口就来， 也太配合了。
　　房乔听了李世民的话后，脸颊又泛起了薄红。
　　这是害羞了？可惜没有手机，李玄霸真想把这一幕照下来。老房现在还只是个二十多岁的年轻人呢。
　　见房乔确实不太习惯应酬，李玄霸也不拉着他了，率先提出有事要告辞。
　　李世民还想拉着房乔聊一会儿。在李玄霸心中说了【烤羊腿】三个字后， 他就立刻的殷勤地送房乔离开。
　　赶紧走吧房兄，走快些走稳些！吸溜！
　　在目前只有八岁的李世民心中， 烤羊腿的重要性显然远远大于这位未来的肱股之臣。
　　房乔告辞后，李世民问李玄霸：“他是不是不太想和我们相处？”
　　李玄霸翻白眼：“你居然发现了？那你为何缠着他？”
　　李世民不好意思地揉了揉鼻子，道：“因为我见他很亲切， 想和他交朋友。我俩这么优秀， 他不想和我们相处， 一定是因为对我们还不了解。等他了解了， 肯定就愿意和我们做朋友！”
　　李玄霸：“……”牛。
　　他以为自己这个在底层摸爬滚打起来的人，在谋取利益的时候已经足够死缠烂打不要脸。没想到二哥居然没有利益，也会因为一个“眼缘”，做到自己只要在想要谋取利益的时候才会做到的事。
　　李玄霸切换心声：【放心，他将来和你相处的时间多得是。他临终的时候，你还握着他的双手哭，给他送终呢。】
　　李世民的脸一下子就垮了：“阿玄啊，你能不能别这么煞风景，刚见面就说到去世？”
　　李玄霸：“哦。”
　　李世民把着李玄霸的肩膀，小声道：“我一见他就觉得他一定特别厉害。他是不是很厉害？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　他在心中为李世民介绍起房乔的情况。
　　李玄霸：【房玄龄虽出生于清河房氏，但他祖父那一辈已经没了爵位，父亲年幼丧父，所以无法以门荫做官。房彦谦在开皇时曾任监察御史，与高先生有旧，后因过于刚直得罪权贵，迁长葛县令。几年后房彦谦“清正廉洁”考核中位居天下第一，升任鄀州司马。房玄龄其品行才华都极效其父。】
　　李世民眼睛一亮：“哇，天下第一！我眼光果然很好！”
　　李玄霸：【无法以门荫入仕，房玄龄便以科举入仕。但谁能想到隋文帝的科举就是骗人感情的，所有科举入仕者几乎等不到授于实职的那一日。房玄龄当了一个羽骑尉的散官很多年。】
　　李世民捏了捏下巴：“这个羽骑尉，是不是陛下废掉的散官职位之一？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　李世民叹气：“怪不得他如此着急。”
　　李玄霸：【他在京城蹉跎了几年，得到了吏部侍郎高构看重，补为隰城县尉。但很快汉王杨谅谋反，他被牵连，免官谪徙上郡。】
　　杨谅谋反是三年前的事。上郡就是后世毛乌素沙漠附近，现在是游牧区，是大隋的边疆，汉朝曾置朔方郡。
　　谪徙和流放不同。流放是重刑，需要承担沉重的徭役。谪徙只是换个户籍，仍旧是普通百姓。
　　秦定百越置桂林、南海、象郡，就以谪徙民以充之。后来文人在贬官时，也爱自称被“谪徙”。
　　房玄龄虽成为了边民，但他毕竟是士人，身上还有个散官。所以只要有足够的盘缠，他就不会被束缚在上郡，可以来到京城讨前程。
　　现在杨广一刀切，没有任何补偿便把一些低等散官给“切了”。房玄龄便完全变成了白身，怪不得会着急了。
　　李世民沉默。
　　偷偷买了烤羊腿后，李世民和李玄霸蹲在市集一处角落里，让仆人在外面守着，就像是蹲坑一样偷偷蹲在地上偷偷啃羊腿。
　　李世民默默地啃完一整只羊腿，并把李玄霸吃不完的半只羊腿也啃了后，才抹抹嘴道：“精简官职的初衷无错，但陛下做得太粗糙。难道陛下以为被裁掉的官员不会有怨言？他竟没有给他们留一条后路。哪怕扩大和重用科举入仕之人，给他们一点希望也好。”
　　他舔了舔嘴唇上的羊油和香料：“反正若是有人抢了我的羊腿，我一定会生气。如果那时我正饿着，肯定会和那个人拼命。房兄看上去家境并不算好，完全没了生计，肯定很为难。”
　　李玄霸倒是没多同情房玄龄。
　　他这个出身底层的人，总会在别人卖惨的时候抬杠。
　　房玄龄有地里刨食的农人苦？地里刨食的农人有遇到天灾的农人苦？遇到天灾的农人有重病残废的人苦？
　　若比惨，是没有极限的。所以李玄霸就算偶尔泛起了一点同情心，也不会太在意这点同情心。
　　但感情是一回事，理智上李玄霸知道，唐朝读书人都是文武双全，上马能带兵下马能治国。你让这群人掉落阶级，且看不到返回原本阶级的希望，他们就会另投“明主”。所以不能让他们太惨。
　　天下熙熙，皆为利来；天下攘攘，皆为利往。世间道理，莫不如此。
　　仆人在马车上的小火炉上烧来热水，拿来香皂给两位小郎君洗手洗脸，“消灭证据”。
　　李世民一边洗脸洗手，一边叹息道：“陛下真是太自信了，他不仅不给这群被裁减的士人活路，还丝毫不担心这群人会不满，居然在颁布了诏令后就要立刻北巡离开京城。就算太子坐镇京城，也不一定能镇住京中不满。”
　　李玄霸道：【他不是自信，是脑海里没这个念头。按照修房子来说，他是个厉害的设计师，能画出美轮美奂的宫殿。但建造的时候，他就一窍不通，连个地基都不挖，平地就开始建房子。】
　　所以后世都说，不怕二代败家，就怕二代奋起。
　　正确的计划谁不会做？后世哪个人不会做吹牛PPT？高大上的蓝图，李玄霸一晚上能整十个出来。如果看蓝图就能当明君，他一定能成为千古一帝。
　　但怎么操作呢？
　　先定个小目标，减掉十斤肉。开始实际操作，隋炀帝说，我必须一天减十斤！做不到的话周围人就去死！
　　那就只能割掉十斤肉或者放掉十斤血了。
　　隋文帝就是一个“蓝图明君”，蓝图做得美轮美奂。
　　不过古往今来都有很多人吃“蓝图明君”这一套，现代许多创业融资，就是创业者拿个“蓝图”就能赚得盆满钵满。
　　隋炀帝好歹还实际操作，他已经努力过了，虽然还不如把钱存银行活期。所以隋炀帝后世有那么多粉，现在也还有那么多相信他的贤臣，也算正常。
　　回去的路上，李玄霸一路上都在心声里给李世民瞎叨叨“蓝图明君”和“减肥目标与实操”。
　　李世民觉得胖很好，不明白李玄霸为什么要说减肥。但李玄霸的叨叨很有趣，把他逗得咯咯直笑。
　　李玄霸唏嘘：【所以许多有大志向又有大才干的人，往往在行事时很保守。他们只做一步，将希望寄托给后人。在条件不成熟的时候，能克制住自己“千古一帝”欲|望的人，才是真的厉害。陛下这就叫志大才疏。】
　　李世民问道：“你说的是文景之治吗？”
　　李玄霸本想说“奋六世之余烈也是”，但他想了想之前那几个老秦王，不像是克制欲|望，而是纯粹是自己昏庸了或者倒霉了。秦始皇继位的时候，秦国状况也并不好，只是六国更拉胯。如果秦始皇真的是奋六世之余烈，估计秦就不是二世而亡了。
　　他摇摇头，张口道：“是啊，就只有文景之治了。”
　　李世民道：“如果秦始皇能想到这一点，克制住自己的欲|望，将许多事交给公子扶苏来做。或许秦也不会亡于二世。”
　　李世民和李玄霸想到一块儿去了，虽然角度不同。
　　不过李玄霸提醒他哥：“秦始皇的继任者是胡亥，不是扶苏。他就算把希望寄托给后人，胡亥也只会让他绝望。”
　　李世民感慨的神情一僵，然后拍着大腿大笑：“对啊，秦始皇好倒霉哈哈哈哈！胡亥是个坏的，扶苏也是个蠢的！”
　　他得意洋洋拍着胸脯道：“要是我是扶苏，不过一使臣尔，连蒙恬也站在我这边，我肯定找借口偷偷逃跑，然后偷偷积攒力量夺回皇位！胡亥倒行逆施，朝野上下不满者众多，我亲自为将，定能一呼百应，斩胡亥赵高等如瓦狗！”
　　李玄霸：“扑哧！”
　　李世民不满地叉腰：“你笑什么！难道你不相信我？”
　　李玄霸：“哈哈哈哈哈哈！”
　　李世民不满地戳弟弟：“你笑什么！笑什么！快如实招来！”
　　李玄霸捂着肚子笑道：“等你再长大些我就告诉你，哈哈哈哈。”
　　等你当皇帝后，我就告诉你后人人讨论历史“假如”话题时，其他明君都是讨论假如多了哪个名臣或者科技会变得如何，唯独你，几乎全是讨论“如果李世民是XXX的儿子，能不能再造X朝”。
　　从公子扶苏到汉献帝，从魏的高贵乡公曹髦到季汉的安乐公刘禅，再到后世的宋徽宗的儿子宋钦宗，明宣宗的儿子明英宗……唐太宗李世民在后世历史圈的吹水中，总在给各个有能力的没能力的皇帝当儿子。
　　哪怕李世民在历史中最大的黑点就是“不孝子”。
　　哦，想让李世民穿越成隋炀帝的人也不少呢。
　　哈哈哈哈哈哈，如果二哥在当皇帝后知道后世人都想让他给其他皇帝当儿子，不知道是该笑还是气得跳脚？
　　“又是之后再说，怎么那么多之后再说。”李世民嘟囔，不开心地去挠弟弟的痒痒，“让你笑，让你笑，让你笑个够！”
　　李玄霸笑得从车座上滚下来，额头上磕了一个包。
　　李世民：“……”完蛋。
　　果不其然，李世民回家就完蛋，屁股蛋开了花。
　　小孩子就该揍屁股，屁股肉多，揍了不会有后遗症。李玄霸摸着额头上的包包，十分小心眼地冷哼。
　　哥你等着瞧，等你当皇帝后，我一定用剧透气死你！
　　……
　　李玄霸本以为再与房玄龄见面，恐怕是很久之后了。
　　就房玄龄那一副“社恐”的模样，估计一点都不想和二哥那个真正的“社恐”再见面。
　　谁知道，只第三日，房乔就满脸无奈地再次拜访。这次，他居然是上门拜访。
　　他身后跟着一个夹杂着风流和豪爽气质的青年人。青年人看着比房乔还年轻许多，只站在那里不动，就吸引了府内不少女婢偷瞟。
　　来人拱手笑道：“听说玄龄结识了李秀才，在下就冒昧借着玄龄的拜帖，厚着脸皮来了。在下京兆杜氏杜如晦，字克明。听闻李秀才家中藏书无数，在下请求能以家中藏书与李秀才互相借阅。”
　　李玄霸想也没想，道：“好呀！”
　　李世民抱着手臂叹气：“阿玄只要听到有没看过的书看，就变得特别爽快。不过见杜兄气度，还以为是一个豪侠，竟也如阿玄一样，是个爱书之人。”
　　杜如晦笑道：“李二郎君认为怎样的人才是爱书之人？”
　　李世民想了想，道：“仔细想想，书这么好，什么样的人都应该爱书。所以杜兄是个爱书之人，也正常。”
　　杜如晦眼中闪过一丝惊叹。
　　他本来只是好奇唐国公府那位大隋最年幼秀才李玄霸，又听闻李玄霸嗜书，常从宫中藏书阁抄写孤本藏于家中。他便厚着脸皮死缠烂打，请求房乔牵线搭桥。
　　没想到掩藏在弟弟文名光辉下的双生子哥哥李世民，也是个妙人。
　　杜如晦也是京兆杜氏的旁支，父亲只是一个长吏。他虽比房乔好一些，不是科举入仕，而是被朝堂征辟为后备官员。但这一“后备”，就等到天荒地老。他现在还是个白身。
　　不过他年仅二十二岁，所以对做官之事并不焦急。他性格豪爽，自诩风流，除了不爱嗑散嗑石钟乳也不爱撒开衣服在街上有碍风化的奔跑，其性子很有些魏晋名士的韵味，做事不爱遵循礼法。
　　所以杜如晦和李世民聊了几句之后，就立刻把李世民引为知己。
　　他甚至还把李世民抱起来揉脑袋，说要吸取李世民的聪明劲，回家和妻子生个和李世民一样厉害的大胖小子。
　　李玄霸不断后撤步，用眼神阻止杜如晦靠近。
　　历史中的杜相是一个十分沉稳低调之人，这个大孩子似的杜如晦究竟是谁？退退退！
　　房乔也跟着不断后撤步。他后悔告诉杜如晦，他与李家二位小郎君“相谈甚欢”的事了。
　　但世上没有后悔药吃，房乔也才二十八岁，是个在好友面前有点好面子，经不住激将法的性子。杜如晦捧了他几句，激了他几句，他就上了头。等清醒过来的时候，他已经站在这里，悔不当初。
　　李玄霸抬头看向房乔：“房兄要不要也去摸摸兄长的脑袋。”
　　房乔使劲摇头。
　　李玄霸压低声音，神秘兮兮道：“房兄还是去摸一摸吧。不然二十年后，一定会后悔。”
　　房乔惊讶地看向李玄霸。
　　李玄霸将手指竖在嘴唇前，然后迅速放下手，就像是什么都没发生过似的，继续看着杜如晦和李世民胡闹。
　　杜如晦居然已经把李世民架在了脖子上。两人去摘院中的桃花，说要做什么桃花蜜饯。也不知道他们是怎么把话题拐到这上面的。
　　房乔手指在袖口中摩挲了一下。这是他思考的习惯动作。
　　“三郎君会看相？”房乔最终忍不住了，蹲在地上，一副破罐子破摔地模样，小声道，“那、那你能看出我何时能让妻子不再为我忧心操劳？”
　　李玄霸惊讶。
　　你问前程就问前程，非得找个妻子的借口，怎么如此别扭……唔，可能不是借口。
　　李玄霸想起了《新唐书》列女传中一则关于房玄龄夫人卢氏的故事。
　　房玄龄被谪徙到边疆后，一度重病濒死，请求卢氏改嫁离开。卢氏自剜一目以示自己眼中看不到别人，不肯离开。
　　宋朝那群人编书的时候，总会找些野史小故事来宣扬自己的思想。这个血腥的烈女小故事，让人看得非常不适。
　　以当时医疗水平，卢氏自剜一目不需要任何治疗，并且受伤途中还能继续照顾重病濒死的丈夫，卢氏大概是超级大隋人了。
　　卢氏还有一个典故是“吃醋”。这个故事来自刘餗创作的笔记小说《隋唐嘉话》，连《新唐书》都没收录，估计只是单纯的逸闻。一些文人就喜欢酸伉俪情深的夫妻，把美好的感情说成惧内和妒妇。
　　卢氏自剜一目的可能性不高，但对重病的房玄龄不离不弃是真的。
　　所以房玄龄表现得如此扭捏，硬着头皮拜访权贵求官，说不定真的是因为想要让妻子不那么辛苦，所以咬牙违背本性。
　　李玄霸道：“君真正的富贵，要等待十年后了。不过要说日子好过些，现在就会好许多。”
　　房乔苦笑道：“十年……十年啊。还要让夫人跟着我苦十年吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“我说的富贵，是指你虽然刚起步，但已经能预见的泼天富贵。房相，你对自己有点信心。”
　　房乔吓得一屁股跌坐在地上。
　　李玄霸看向已经跑远的杜如晦和杜如晦肩膀上的二哥。
　　其他奴仆跟在二哥身后，担心二哥摔着。他们现在四周无人。
　　“房兄，你现在还无子嗣？”李玄霸两眼看向远方。
　　房乔僵硬地点头。
　　李玄霸在心里过了一遍房玄龄的传记。
　　房玄龄颠沛半生，一直无子女。长子房遗直虽生卒年不降，但根据唐代传奇小说《龙城录》记载，房玄龄为相时房遗直刚三岁。既然是唐人写的小说，年龄差距应该不会相差太大。
　　而房遗爱尚高阳公主，高阳公主据其他姐妹出嫁时间推测，应该是武德末年到贞观初年出生。房遗爱只会比高阳公主大。
　　房玄龄的父亲又在太原起事三年前去世，这三年要守孝。所以房玄龄的长子，应该在近五年内就会出生了。
　　李玄霸道：“你和令夫人在五年内就能喜得贵子。就算耽搁一下，也不会超过七年。而且你和你夫人还不止有一个孩子。所以放宽心。”
　　房乔愣住，然后迅速爬起来，朝着杜如晦跑去。
　　他抢过李世民，把李世民抱住揉了揉脑袋，义正词严道：“克明，你这样做太过危险，小心摔着李二郎君，不可胡来。”
　　稍远处的李玄霸捂嘴：“扑哧。”
