Chapter 41: Hugs, Pats, and Being Lifted High

Fang Qiao was well-versed in the Five Classics, and while his poetry and prose were merely passable, they were more than sufficient for publication.
He finished flipping through the thin collection of essays quite quickly. Throughout the process, he kept his water cup gripped tightly, not taking a single sip.
"Ah Xuan, this is much better than what you write," Li Shimin remarked with a sigh. He was, of course, referring to the poetry and prose Li Xuanba actually wrote.
Li Xuanba nodded.
Fang Qiao assumed Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were just being polite. But since they had offered such pleasantries, the matter was likely settled, and he breathed a sigh of relief.
Li Xuanba said, "Shall we start by printing one hundred copies?"
Fang Qiao was surprised. "One hundred copies? That many?"
Li Xuanba replied, "It is not many."
Self-published books required the author to pay the costs upfront. Fang Qiao hurriedly reached into his sleeve for copper coins, feeling fortunate that he had brought extra money.
Li Xuanba returned half the coins and said, "Since Brother Fang’s collection has received the approval of both my brother and me, the upfront payment is halved. This applies to everyone else as well."
Li Shimin: "?" Is that a rule? If Ah Xuan says it is, then it is.
Li Shimin smiled and added, "If we weren't worried about making Brother Fang feel uncomfortable, we would have preferred not to collect any upfront payment at all. But Ah Xuan always says that even between close brothers, accounts must be kept clear. For a man of noble character, paying is better than not paying."
Now it was Li Xuanba’s turn to be: "?"
He had decided on the fly to do Fang Xuanling a favor. While he knew his second brother would definitely play along, he hadn't expected his brother to be so adept at spinning such a smooth lie.
Upon hearing Li Shimin’s words, a faint blush crept onto Fang Qiao’s cheeks.
Is he shy? What a pity there are no mobile phones; Li Xuanba really wanted to take a picture of this. Old Fang is still just a young man in his twenties, after all.
Seeing that Fang Qiao was indeed unaccustomed to social niceties, Li Xuanba stopped detaining him and was the first to suggest they conclude the meeting.
Li Shimin still wanted to keep chatting with Fang Qiao, but after Li Xuanba whispered the words "roasted lamb leg" in his mind, he immediately and enthusiastically sent Fang Qiao on his way.
*Hurry up and leave, Brother Fang, walk faster, walk steadily! Slurp!*
In the mind of the current eight-year-old Li Shimin, the importance of a roasted lamb leg clearly far outweighed that of this future pillar of the state.
After Fang Qiao took his leave, Li Shimin asked Li Xuanba, "Does he not like being around us?"
Li Xuanba rolled his eyes. "You actually noticed? Then why were you pestering him?"
Li Shimin rubbed his nose in embarrassment and said, "Because I find him very amiable and want to be friends with him. We are so outstanding; if he doesn't want to be around us, it must be because he doesn't know us well enough yet. Once he gets to know us, he will surely be willing to be our friend!"
Li Xuanba: "..." Impressive.
He had thought that as someone who had crawled his way up from the bottom, he was already shameless and persistent enough when it came to pursuing interests. He hadn't expected his second brother to do the same thing—without any ulterior motive, simply because of a "fated connection"—that he himself would only do when seeking profit.
Li Xuanba switched to his inner voice: *Don't worry, he will have plenty of time to spend with you in the future. When he is on his deathbed, you will be the one holding his hands, weeping as you see him off.*
Li Shimin’s face fell instantly. "Ah Xuan, can you not be such a killjoy? We just met, and you're already talking about his death?"
Li Xuanba: "Oh."
Li Shimin grabbed Li Xuanba’s shoulder and whispered, "The moment I saw him, I felt he must be extraordinary. Is he very capable?"
Li Xuanba nodded.
In his heart, he began to introduce Fang Qiao’s situation to Li Shimin.
Li Xuanba: *Although Fang Xuanling was born into the Qinghe Fang clan, his grandfather’s generation had already lost their noble title, and his father lost his own father at a young age, so he could not enter officialdom through hereditary privilege. During the Kaihuang era, Fang Yanqian served as an Investigating Censor and had old ties with Master Gao, but because he was too upright and offended the powerful, he was demoted to Magistrate of Changge. A few years later, Fang Yanqian ranked first in the empire in the 'integrity and incorruptibility' assessment and was promoted to Sima of Ruo Prefecture. Fang Xuanling’s character and talent are very much like his father’s.*
Li Shimin’s eyes lit up. "Wow, first in the empire! My judgment is indeed excellent!"
Li Xuanba: *Unable to enter officialdom through his family, Fang Xuanling entered through the imperial examinations. But who could have guessed that Emperor Wen of Sui’s examinations were just a sham to toy with people’s emotions? Almost no one who entered through the exams ever received a real position. Fang Xuanling spent many years as a low-ranking 'Feathered Cavalry Officer' (Yuqiwei).*
Li Shimin pinched his chin. "Is this Yuqiwei one of the low-ranking positions the Emperor abolished?"
Li Xuanba nodded.
Li Shimin sighed. "No wonder he is so anxious."
Li Xuanba: *He wasted several years in the capital, eventually gaining the favor of Gao Gou, the Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, who appointed him as the County Lieutenant of Xicheng. But soon after, Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled, and Fang was implicated, stripped of his office, and exiled to Shang Commandery.*
Yang Liang’s rebellion had been three years ago. Shang Commandery was near the future Mu Us Desert; it was a nomadic region and a frontier of the Great Sui, where the Han Dynasty had once established the Shuofang Commandery.
"Exile" (Zhexie) was different from "Banishment" (Liufang). Banishment was a severe punishment involving heavy forced labor. Exile was merely a change of household registration; one remained an ordinary citizen.
When the Qin Dynasty established the Guilin, Nanhai, and Xiang commanderies, they used exiled civilians to populate them. Later, literati often liked to refer to themselves as being "exiled" when they were demoted.
Although Fang Xuanling had become a frontier dweller, he was still a scholar and held a low-ranking official title. So, as long as he had enough travel funds, he wasn't bound to Shang Commandery and could come to the capital to seek his fortune.
Now that Yang Guang had "cut" everyone with a single stroke, dismissing low-ranking officials without any compensation, Fang Xuanling had become a commoner in every sense. No wonder he was anxious.
Li Shimin fell silent.
After secretly buying a roasted lamb leg, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba squatted in a corner of the market, having their servants stand guard outside, and gnawed on the lamb leg on the ground as if they were hiding in a latrine.
Li Shimin silently finished an entire leg, and after also devouring the half that Li Xuanba couldn't finish, he wiped his mouth and said, "The original intention of streamlining the bureaucracy wasn't wrong, but the Emperor’s execution was too crude. Does the Emperor think the dismissed officials won't hold a grudge? He didn't leave them a way out. Even expanding and making better use of those who entered through the imperial examinations would have given them a glimmer of hope."
He licked the lamb fat and spices from his lips. "Anyway, if someone snatched my lamb leg, I would definitely be angry. If I were hungry at the time, I would definitely fight that person to the death. Brother Fang doesn't seem to come from a wealthy family; with his livelihood completely gone, he must be in a very difficult position."
Li Xuanba didn't feel much sympathy for Fang Xuanling.
As someone who had come from the bottom, he always tended to play devil's advocate when others were "selling their misery."
Was Fang Xuanling’s suffering worse than that of a farmer scratching a living from the dirt? Was a farmer’s suffering worse than that of one hit by natural disasters? Was a farmer hit by disasters worse off than someone suffering from a terminal illness or disability?
If you compare misery, there is no limit. So, even if Li Xuanba occasionally felt a flicker of sympathy, he didn't dwell on it.
But feelings were one thing; rationally, Li Xuanba knew that Tang Dynasty scholars were all skilled in both literature and martial arts—they could lead troops on horseback and govern the state on foot. If you force this class of people to fall and see no hope of returning to their status, they will simply turn to another "enlightened master." Thus, they could not be allowed to suffer too much.
*The world bustles for profit; the world rushes for gain.* This was the way of the world.
The servants heated water on a small stove in the carriage and brought soap for the two young masters to wash their hands and faces, "eliminating the evidence."
As Li Shimin washed, he sighed, "The Emperor is truly too confident. Not only does he leave no path for these dismissed scholars, but he also isn't the least bit worried about their dissatisfaction, choosing to leave the capital for a northern tour immediately after issuing the decree. Even with the Crown Prince holding down the capital, he might not be able to suppress the unrest."
Li Xuanba said: *He isn't confident; he simply doesn't have that thought in his mind. To use a house-building analogy, he is a brilliant designer who can draw magnificent palaces. But when it comes to construction, he is completely clueless—he doesn't even dig a foundation before starting to build on flat ground.*
That is why later generations say: don't fear a second-generation heir who squanders wealth; fear a second-generation heir who tries to "rise up."
Who doesn't know how to make a correct plan? Who in the future doesn't know how to make a flashy PowerPoint? Li Xuanba could churn out ten high-minded blueprints in one night. If one could become an eternal sage-emperor just by looking at blueprints, he would surely be the greatest emperor in history.
But how do you execute it?
*Set a small goal: lose ten pounds.* When it comes to actual operation, Emperor Yang of Sui says, "I must lose ten pounds in one day! If you can't do it, everyone around me dies!"
Then the only option is to cut off ten pounds of flesh or drain ten pounds of blood.
Emperor Wen of Sui was an "Emperor of Blueprints," creating magnificent designs.
However, throughout history, many people have bought into the "Emperor of Blueprints" act. Many modern startups raise funds just because the founder has a "blueprint" that makes them rich.
Emperor Yang of Sui at least tried to operate it; he had worked hard, even if it was less effective than putting money in a bank savings account. So, it is normal that Emperor Yang has so many fans in later generations, and that there are still so many who believe he was a wise minister.
On the way back, Li Xuanba spent the entire time rambling in his inner voice to Li Shimin about "Emperor of Blueprints" and "weight loss goals vs. actual operation."
Li Shimin thought being fat was good and didn't understand why Li Xuanba talked about weight loss. But Li Xuanba’s rambling was interesting and made him giggle.
Li Xuanba sighed: *That is why many people with great ambition and talent are often very conservative in their actions. They only take one step at a time, pinning their hopes on their descendants. Those who can restrain their own desire to be an 'Eternal Emperor' when conditions are not ripe are the truly great ones. The Emperor is what you call 'great ambition but shallow talent.'*
Li Shimin asked, "Are you talking about the Rule of Wen and Jing?"
Li Xuanba wanted to say, "The 'accumulated strength of six generations' also applies," but he thought about those old Qin kings—they didn't seem to be restraining their desires; they were just incompetent or unlucky. When Qin Shi Huang ascended the throne, the state of Qin wasn't in great shape; it was just that the other six states were even worse. If Qin Shi Huang had truly relied on the "accumulated strength of six generations," the Qin Dynasty wouldn't have fallen in two generations.
He shook his head and said, "Yes, only the Rule of Wen and Jing."
Li Shimin said, "If Qin Shi Huang could have thought of this, restrained his desires, and left many things for Prince Fusu to do, perhaps the Qin wouldn't have perished in the second generation."
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were thinking the same thing, though from different angles.
However, Li Xuanba reminded his brother: "Qin Shi Huang’s successor was Huhai, not Fusu. Even if he had pinned his hopes on his descendants, Huhai would only have driven him to despair."
Li Shimin’s contemplative expression froze, then he slapped his thigh and laughed out loud. "That’s right, Qin Shi Huang was so unlucky, hahahaha! Huhai was a villain, and Fusu was a fool!"
He proudly patted his chest and said, "If I were Fusu, it would just be a matter of an envoy; even Meng Tian was on my side. I would definitely find an excuse to escape secretly, then secretly accumulate power to take back the throne! Huhai acted against the will of heaven, and there were many dissatisfied people in the court and the country. If I led the army myself, I would surely have a thousand responses to one call and cut down Huhai and Zhao Gao like weeds!"
Li Xuanba: "Pfft!"
Li Shimin put his hands on his hips, dissatisfied. "What are you laughing at! Don't you believe me?"
Li Xuanba: "Hahahahahaha!"
Li Shimin poked his younger brother, annoyed. "What are you laughing at! What! Tell me the truth!"
Li Xuanba clutched his stomach and laughed, "I'll tell you when you're older, hahahaha."
*When you become emperor, I'll tell you that when later generations discuss historical 'what-ifs,' other sage-emperors are discussed in terms of what if they had one more famous minister or a new technology. Only you—it’s almost all about 'If Li Shimin were the son of XXX, could he have rebuilt the X Dynasty?'*
*From Prince Fusu to Emperor Xian of Han, from Cao Mao of Wei to Liu Shan of Shu, then to the later Song Qinzong, son of Song Huizong, and Ming Yingzong, son of Ming Xuanzong... Tang Taizong Li Shimin, in the idle chatter of later history circles, is always acting as the son for various capable or incapable emperors.*
*Even though Li Shimin’s biggest stain in history is being an 'unfilial son.'*
*Oh, there are also quite a few people who want to transmigrate Li Shimin into Emperor Yang of Sui.*
*Hahahahaha, if Second Brother knew after becoming emperor that later generations all wanted him to be the son of other emperors, would he laugh or jump with rage?*
"Again with the 'tell you later,' why is it always 'tell you later'?" Li Shimin grumbled, unhappily tickling his brother. "Take that! And that! Laugh all you want!"
Li Xuanba rolled off the carriage seat, laughing, and bumped his forehead, leaving a lump.
Li Shimin: "..." Oh no.
As expected, Li Shimin was in trouble when he got home, and his bottom got a good spanking.
*Children should be spanked on the bottom; there’s plenty of meat there, and it won't have any side effects.* Li Xuanba rubbed the lump on his forehead and snorted coldly, feeling very petty.
*Just you wait, Brother. When you become emperor, I will definitely drive you crazy with spoilers!*
...
Li Xuanba had thought that meeting Fang Xuanling again would be a long time away.
With Fang Xuanling’s "social anxiety," he probably didn't want to see Second Brother—a true "socially anxious" person—ever again.
Who would have thought that on the third day, Fang Qiao would visit again, looking completely helpless. This time, he was visiting their home.
Behind him followed a young man with an air of both elegance and boldness. The young man looked even younger than Fang Qiao, and just standing there, he attracted the sidelong glances of many maids in the residence.
The visitor bowed and smiled. "I heard that Xuanling had made the acquaintance of Scholar Li, so I took the liberty of using Xuanling’s calling card to come here, thick-skinned as I am. I am Du Ruhui of the Jingzhao Du clan, courtesy name Keming. I heard that Scholar Li’s home holds countless books, and I request to borrow and exchange books from our respective collections."
Li Xuanba didn't even think. "Alright!"
Li Shimin crossed his arms and sighed. "Ah Xuan becomes so agreeable whenever he hears about books he hasn't read. But seeing Brother Du’s demeanor, I thought he was a bold hero; to think he is a book lover just like Ah Xuan."
Du Ruhui smiled. "What kind of person does Li Er-lang think is a book lover?"
Li Shimin thought for a moment and said, "Now that I think about it, books are so good that everyone should love them. So it is normal for Brother Du to be a book lover."
A flash of amazement crossed Du Ruhui’s eyes.
He had originally just been curious about Li Xuanba, the youngest scholar of the Great Sui in the Tang Duke’s mansion, and had heard that Li Xuanba was obsessed with books, often copying rare editions from the palace library to keep at home. He had been thick-skinned and persistent, begging Fang Qiao to act as a bridge.
He hadn't expected Li Shimin, the twin brother hidden under the brilliance of his younger brother’s literary fame, to be such a fascinating person as well.
Du Ruhui was also from a branch of the Jingzhao Du clan, and his father was merely a low-level official. Although he was better off than Fang Qiao—not entering through the imperial exams but recruited by the court as a reserve official—this "reserve" status had lasted until the end of time. He was still a commoner.
However, he was only twenty-two, so he wasn't anxious about officialdom. He had a bold personality and considered himself elegant. Aside from not being fond of taking drugs or running through the streets with his clothes open in a way that offended public decency, his temperament had the charm of a Wei-Jin scholar, and he didn't like to follow rituals.
So, after chatting with Li Shimin for a few moments, Du Ruhui immediately considered him a soulmate.
He even picked Li Shimin up and rubbed his head, saying he wanted to absorb Li Shimin’s intelligence so he could go home and have a big, healthy son just as brilliant as Li Shimin.
Li Xuanba kept stepping back, using his eyes to stop Du Ruhui from getting closer.
*The historical Chancellor Du was a very steady and low-key person. Who is this big-kid-like Du Ruhui? Back, back, back!*
Fang Qiao also kept stepping back. He regretted telling Du Ruhui that he had "talked happily" with the two young masters of the Li family.
But there was no medicine for regret in this world. Fang Qiao was only twenty-eight, a man who cared a bit about his face in front of friends and couldn't resist a challenge. Du Ruhui had flattered him and provoked him a few times, and he had gotten carried away. By the time he sobered up, he was already standing there, regretting his actions.
Li Xuanba looked up at Fang Qiao. "Does Brother Fang want to go and pat my brother’s head too?"
Fang Qiao shook his head vigorously.
Li Xuanba lowered his voice and said mysteriously, "Brother Fang, you should go and pat it. Otherwise, twenty years from now, you will definitely regret it."
Fang Qiao looked at Li Xuanba in surprise.
Li Xuanba put a finger to his lips, then quickly lowered his hand, acting as if nothing had happened, and continued to watch Du Ruhui and Li Shimin fooling around.
Du Ruhui had actually hoisted Li Shimin onto his shoulders. The two were going to pick peach blossoms in the courtyard, saying they wanted to make some kind of peach blossom preserve. It was unclear how they had steered the conversation to that.
Fang Qiao rubbed his fingers against his sleeve. It was his habitual gesture when thinking.
"Does the Third Young Master know how to read fortunes?" Fang Qiao finally couldn't help himself. He squatted on the ground, looking like he had given up on everything, and whispered, "Can... can you tell when I will be able to let my wife stop worrying and toiling for me?"
Li Xuanba was surprised.
*You ask about your future, but you have to find an excuse involving your wife. Why are you so awkward... well, maybe it’s not an excuse.*
Li Xuanba remembered a story about Lady Lu, the wife of Fang Xuanling, in the "Biographies of Exemplary Women" in the *New Book of Tang*.
After Fang Xuanling was exiled to the frontier, he fell gravely ill and was near death, asking Lady Lu to remarry and leave him. Lady Lu gouged out one of her own eyes to show that she saw no one else in her eyes and refused to leave.
When the people of the Song Dynasty compiled the books, they always looked for wild historical anecdotes to promote their own ideologies. This bloody, "virtuous woman" story was very uncomfortable to read.
Given the medical standards of the time, Lady Lu wouldn't have needed any treatment for gouging out her own eye, and she could still continue to care for her dying husband while injured—Lady Lu must have been a "Super Great Sui" person.
Lady Lu also had an anecdote about "jealousy." This story came from the *Jia Hua of Sui and Tang* written by Liu Shu, which wasn't even included in the *New Book of Tang*; it was likely just a simple anecdote. Some literati just liked to be sour about couples with deep affection, painting beautiful relationships as "fear of the wife" and "jealous women."
The possibility of Lady Lu gouging out her eye was low, but her refusal to abandon the gravely ill Fang Xuanling was true.
So, Fang Xuanling’s awkward behavior—biting the bullet to visit the powerful to beg for an official post—might truly be because he wanted to make his wife’s life less difficult, forcing himself to act against his own nature.
Li Xuanba said, "Your true wealth will come in ten years. But as for having an easier life, it will be much better starting now."
Fang Qiao smiled bitterly. "Ten years... ten years. Do I have to let my wife suffer with me for another ten years?"
Li Xuanba said, "The wealth I speak of is that although you are just starting, you can already foresee immense riches. Chancellor Fang, have a little confidence in yourself."
Fang Qiao was so startled he fell onto his butt.
Li Xuanba looked at the distant Du Ruhui and his second brother on Du Ruhui’s shoulders.
The other servants followed behind his second brother, worried he might fall. They were currently alone.
"Brother Fang, you have no children yet?" Li Xuanba looked into the distance.
Fang Qiao nodded stiffly.
Li Xuanba went through Fang Xuanling’s biography in his mind.
Fang Xuanling had spent half his life in displacement and had no children. Although the birth and death years of his eldest son, Fang Yizhi, were not recorded, according to the Tang legend *Longcheng Lu*, Fang Yizhi was only three years old when Fang Xuanling became Chancellor. Since it was a novel written by a Tang person, the age gap shouldn't be too large.
And Fang Yi'ai married Princess Gaoyang; based on the marriage times of her other sisters, she should have been born between the end of the Wude era and the beginning of the Zhenguan era. Fang Yi'ai would only be older than Princess Gaoyang.
Fang Xuanling’s father had died three years before the uprising in Taiyuan, and he had to observe mourning for those three years. So, Fang Xuanling’s eldest son should be born within the next five years.
Li Xuanba said, "You and your wife will have a son within five years. Even if there is a delay, it won't exceed seven years. And you and your wife will have more than one child. So, set your heart at ease."
Fang Qiao was stunned, then quickly scrambled up and ran toward Du Ruhui.
He snatched Li Shimin away, held him, rubbed his head, and said righteously, "Keming, what you are doing is too dangerous. Be careful not to drop Li Er-lang; you must not act recklessly."
In the distance, Li Xuanba covered his mouth. "Pfft."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第42章 皇帝北巡父离京 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第42章 皇帝北巡父离京

=

就算这个时代的人再相信谶纬之术， 自己和房玄龄才见第二面，又只是一个孩童，房玄龄不应该如此信任自己。

李玄霸仔细想了想。房玄龄现在估计是真的过得很艰难， 且夫妻二人也太想要一个孩子， 所以听了自己的话， 房玄龄就死马当活马医了。

假如行呢？

你根本不知道想要孩子的人为了求子，会做出什么离谱的事。

至于房玄龄是不是从自己的“剧透”中另外猜到了点什么，李玄霸就不知道了。

估计要等十几年后， 李玄霸才能从房玄龄口中问得真相。

嗯，以房相的谨慎，李玄霸觉得自己可能问不出真相。那时房玄龄就算现在没有猜到， 也一定会大夸特夸二哥有龙霸之气。

房乔和杜如晦抱着李世民玩耍时，窦夫人派人来问了一句要不要送些东西来。

李玄霸刚说不需要， 李建成也派了人来， 同样询问要不要送些东西给李世民和李玄霸的朋友。

李玄霸认出了这个人的身份。他是郑媵陪嫁的管事，现在在为李建成做事。

大哥真是有了一个贤内助了。

李玄霸特意与那个男仆聊了几句，让男仆看到房乔和杜如晦幼稚的模样，又“无意间”透露房乔和杜如晦旁支落魄士子的身份，才让那人带着自己对李建成的感谢离开。

唐太宗凌烟阁二十四功臣中， 除了亲戚，和虽与唐太宗没什么交情但仗义执言没有私心的萧瑀之外， 都是落魄世家旁支或者寒门出身。房玄龄和杜如晦算是身份最好的，也不太为这时的统治阶层重视。

李玄霸相信，自己“不小心”透露这二人身份后， 郑氏应该就会放心了。

果然， 男仆离开后就没有再过来。

窦夫人又派人来了一次， 虽李玄霸说不需要， 她仍旧准备了一些果品饮子送来。

李世民被挼得晕乎乎的，清醒后赶紧从新交的朋友怀里跳下来，然后死死拽着李玄霸，不准弟弟走，要弟弟也被抱一抱挼一挼，兄弟二人必须一样。

杜如晦是个促狭性子，有李世民“撑腰”，立刻去捉弄李玄霸。

房乔因李玄霸之前神秘的表现，不敢伸手。

李玄霸叹了口气，主动对房乔伸手：“抱吧。”

房乔心中对李玄霸的畏惧减弱了一些，将李玄霸抱起来。

会谶纬的孩童怎能不让人害怕？即使房乔半信半疑，但一个会对陌生人随意说谶纬之言的孩童真是太怪异了。

李玄霸趴在房乔肩膀上，小声道：“将来我们会互相托付性命，所以我才提前安你的心。你要对我的能力保密哦。”

房乔眨了眨眼，使劲摸了摸李玄霸的脑袋。

李玄霸抱着脑袋，皱着眉怒视房乔。

房乔见李玄霸露出孩子气的恼怒神情，紧张的心情陡然放松。

他笑道：“大德放心。”

李玄霸的脸垮得更厉害了。

房乔没忍住，放声大笑：“你原来真的讨厌这个字？”

李玄霸撇头。

李世民叉腰挺肚肚：“用阿玄自己的话说，阿玄就是矫情！我就很喜欢‘大雄’这个字！”

李玄霸：“啊对对对是是是，李大雄。”

李世民：“对，是我！继续叫！”

李玄霸垂头：【啊！！！！】崩溃！

李世民吓得后退一步，然后气沉丹田，卯足了劲：【啊！！！！！】

他得意洋洋地看着弟弟。虽然我心灵感应能说的字数少，但“声音”比你大！

李玄霸：“……”

他懒得理连这个都要比的幼稚鬼哥哥了。

玩闹了一会儿后，幼稚的二人和被迫跟着一同幼稚的二人终于做起了正事，去看李玄霸的藏书，顺便论一论学问。

在讨论了一会儿学问后，杜如晦又把李玄霸引为知己，并笑道：“世人都说李秀才聪慧谨慎，我怎么看你是个狂士？”

李玄霸平静道：“与世不同便称狂，我倒也没到那地步。”

杜如晦朗声大笑：“你这就是狂了。”

李世民仰头对房乔道：“我弟弟狂吗？我弟弟可懂事可乖巧了，对不对？”

房乔：“……”我怎么知道对不对？

他想起李玄霸动用谶纬之术时那冷漠的神情，道：“还是……狂吧。”

李世民不满地冷哼：“胡说！”

李玄霸无奈道：“哥啊，我对不同的人的态度是不同的，我对你狂什么？”

李世民：“对哦。”

李玄霸扶额：“唉。”有哥在，想装逼都装不了，好烦。

杜如晦和房乔失笑。

有李二郎在，李三郎看来是狂不起来了。

……

有白头如新，有倾盖如故。杜如晦和李家二郎、三郎就是倾盖如故。

至于房乔，他是被杜如晦拉着和李家二郎、三郎倾盖如故。

四人就这么结成了友人，之后常常一同切磋学问。

李玄霸没有什么朋友。李世民是个社牛，把长孙无忌也拉入了这个小圈子。

李世民本来还想把高颎和宇文弼与他们年龄差不多的儿子孙子也拉进来，但高颎和宇文弼拒绝了。

他们在得了李玄霸的预言后，站在更加客观的立场上审视杨广的所作所为，已经确定杨广是真的对他们有杀心。

虽然他们已经退去修书，但谁也不知道杨广会不会仍旧找借口诛杀他们。

李世民和李玄霸很得杨广喜爱，又是杨广亲自给他们牵线的徒弟。即使他们与李世民和李玄霸相处较为密切，将来自己若是出事，不会连累李世民和李玄霸。但换作其他人就不一样了。

所以高颎和宇文弼让儿孙们谨言慎行，闭门不出，既避免出现在杨广视线中，也避免将来连累他人。

所以长孙无忌无奈成了这个小圈子里才学垫底的人。

久而久之，长孙无忌就不想来了。

李世民体贴，与房乔和杜如晦聚会的时候，便不再叫长孙无忌一起来。

但一段时间后，长孙无忌主动前来，并对房乔和杜如晦道歉，希望他们能够指导自己。

李世民有时候体贴，有时候又很促狭。

他毫不客气地嘲笑道：“长孙四郎啊，你是个小气又好面子的性格，居然主动不要面子了？这不像你的性格。”

房乔和杜如晦其实心中隐隐有些瞧不起长孙无忌，不愿意与长孙无忌深交。

不过长孙无忌只有十三岁，他们都是已过弱冠的人，对长孙无忌不会太苛刻。见长孙无忌诚恳道歉，并以弟子晚辈之礼对待他们，他们本想将此事揭过。

没想到李世民不依不饶，两人便略有些尴尬。

长孙无忌知道李世民是个什么性子，李世民损他，他不会像对待其他人那样生气。

他非常老实道：“是妹妹责怪了我。妹妹说，与比自己更聪慧的人做朋友，自己才会变得更聪慧；与比自己更有德行的人做朋友，自己才会变得更高尚。若有了比自己更优秀的朋友，却因为自惭形秽而不愿再与之结交，那就是放任自己成为愚蠢和卑劣的人。”

说完，长孙无忌双手捂脸，羞愧得无地自容：“我妹妹骂人好狠啊。”

旁观的李玄霸赞扬道：“哥，你以后有福气了。”

李世民迷惑：“啊，为什么？”

长孙无忌放下双手，咬牙切齿道：“我有几个妹妹？！”

李世民挠头：“我怎么知道你有几个妹妹？我去你家找你玩的时候，又不会见到你的妹妹。”

长孙无忌和李玄霸：“……”

房乔和杜如晦也很疑惑，不知道为何李玄霸和长孙无忌会如此郁闷。

李玄霸扶额：“哥啊，长孙四郎只有一个妹妹，那就是你的未婚妻，我的准嫂嫂。”

房乔和杜如晦明白了。

他们同时捂嘴笑。

李世民恍然：“哦，她啊。不对啊，她会写字后，给我写的信都是温温柔柔的，不像会骂人的女子……我明白了！一定是因为长孙四郎该骂！观音婢忍无可忍……唔？”

长孙无忌扑上去捂住李世民的嘴，怒斥道：“不要在外人面前说我妹妹的小字！你懂不懂规矩！啊？……啊！！！”

只有八岁的李世民，一个过肩摔把十三岁的长孙无忌摔到地上。

李世民拍了拍手，抬着下巴居高临下道：“太弱了，再练练。别将来文不成，武也不成。”

长孙无忌都快气哭了，又起了逃跑的念头。

房乔见状，心里叹了口气，赶紧去安慰长孙无忌。

李世民道：“别管他，他哭一场就好了。知耻后勇，对吧，阿玄？”

李玄霸不知道说什么好。

历史中的唐太宗也曾经这么对待长孙无忌吗？那长孙无忌还对你忠心耿耿，一定是因为长孙皇后的原因。

李玄霸：【哥，你训长孙四郎就像是训儿子似的。怪不得你以后对长孙四郎说，你对待他如同对待自己的亲儿子。】

李世民：“哈哈哈哈！”

三人用奇怪的眼神看向无故发笑的李世民。

李世民抹着笑出的眼泪道：“是阿玄给我讲了个笑话。”

杜如晦疑惑：“大德张嘴说话了？”

李世民笑道：“我和阿玄是双生子，他说的话，只有我能听到。”

房乔和杜如晦都十分惊讶。长孙无忌……长孙无忌已经习惯了。他常发觉这两兄弟在自己面前说自己听不见的悄悄话。

感情好的双生子了不起吗？！

嗯，就是了不起。

与兄弟不睦的长孙无忌很酸。

经过了长孙小妹的毒舌攻击，长孙无忌硬着头皮融入了这个“学术”小团体。

杜如晦和房乔在相处中发现，长孙无忌其实也是个聪慧好学的人，只是底子薄弱了些，又颇好脸面，之前才表现得那么差劲。

他们又得知长孙无忌学问底子薄弱，是因为父亲长孙晟常年独自在外任职，而掌家的兄长不喜欢异母的弟弟妹妹。他的母亲护住他衣食无忧已经很艰难，所以没有余力为他聘得高师。

两人便对长孙无忌的轻视彻底消失了。

这“卖惨”是李玄霸特意透露的。

对于正人君子而言，“卖惨”是修复裂痕的最好方式。李玄霸可不想这三位贞观贤臣在微末时就起了间隙。

长孙无忌虽然心胸不太宽广，但他记仇也记恩。

杜如晦和房乔得知长孙无忌的遭遇后，十分认真细心地帮长孙无忌补课。

特别是房乔，因为没有孩子，对长孙无忌格外的好。

长孙无忌很感动，回去抱着妹妹哭，说自己第一次遇见如此好的人。

长孙小妹疑惑：“李家二郎三郎难道不好吗？”

长孙无忌道：“李家三郎看似平易近人，但我总觉得他神神秘秘，有些可怕；李家二郎……别提那个混球！他只会欺负人！我见他一次骂他一次！”

长孙小妹笑弯了眉眼。

长孙无忌不高兴道：“我骂他，你居然还笑，是不相信我的话吗？”

长孙小妹笑道：“哥哥这样肆无忌惮地骂他而不担心他生气，说明哥哥相信李家二郎是个心胸宽广的人，也说明李家二郎是哥哥最好的朋友。”

长孙无忌脸一红，把小妹放下，转身就跑。

长孙小妹长长地叹了口气。哥哥还真是容易害羞呢。

她歪着小脑袋，手指点着自己软乎乎的脸颊，想起自己偷偷看到的未来夫君的模样，双颊飞出了粉色的红晕。

我未来郎君笑起来真好看。阿父什么时候回来？阿父不回来，未来郎君都不上门玩耍了。

长孙小妹虽然不懂什么爱情，但是她懂谁长得好看。

那个唇红齿白弯弓射箭的小郎君就最最好看！

今日要和未来夫君说什么呢？要不要悄悄告诉他，阿兄在背后骂他混球？

唔，这样似乎不太好。

……

“阿玄，这个长孙四郎真是嚣张，他居然在背后骂我混球！”李世民拍着桌子大骂。

李玄霸放下书卷，探头看了一眼未来嫂子写的难看的圈圈字。

哦豁，长孙无忌被妹妹“卖”了。

“你可不要告诉长孙四郎，他会埋怨准嫂子。”李玄霸道。

李世民抱着手臂冷哼：“我当然不会告诉他。哼，我会找到法子折腾他。”

李玄霸再次怀疑，历史中的唐太宗究竟是不是真的如他二哥这样和长孙无忌相处。如果是，长孙无忌……辛苦了。

和二哥当青梅竹马的时候，长孙无忌不管打不打得过，总还能扑上来给二哥几拳。

二哥当皇帝后，说长孙无忌与自己儿子一样，长孙无忌还得咬牙切齿说“谢主隆恩”。

李世民骂完长孙无忌后，趴在桌子上道：“耶耶又要离家出走了。”

李玄霸嘴角抽搐：“是离家，不是出走。”

李世民道：“差不多。”

李玄霸道：“差很多。”

李世民道：“我是哥哥，我说差不多就差不多。”

李玄霸懒得和二哥争执：“呵呵。”

李世民继续叹气：“耶耶走后，兄长不会又找事欺负我们吧？”

李玄霸道：“不会。父亲离开后，家里最大的就是母亲。”

李世民高兴了：“也是，那耶耶快走。”

李玄霸心里也是这么想的。

独孤老夫人死后，李渊好像成熟了许多。又可能因为对自己有愧疚，李渊对自己过分好了。每日当值回来都会教他读书习武，休沐时就带着自己骑马。

李渊再不走，他也快撑不住了。

李玄霸知道，自己还是蛮缺爱的，很容易被诱惑。

幸亏李渊要走了。

在李世民和李玄霸与房乔、杜如晦友谊与日俱增的这段时间，朝中发生了诸多大事。

比如《大业律》发布，让朝野上下一致高呼皇帝明君。

隋文帝晚年，虽有《开皇律》，但治罪完全不按照《开皇律》来，而是随隋文帝心意，一切罪责从重处罚，常发生偷盗一钱判斩首，三人偷瓜俱死的之事。

《大业律》减轻了许多隋文帝晚年的刑罚，且规定了农忙等时候不再征发徭役，并不再征发妇人奴婢等人的徭役。受够了隋文帝严酷苛繁刑罚的老百姓纷纷高呼皇帝圣明。

同年，杨广在洛阳附近建造了许多粮仓和义仓，以备东京日常取用，也兼备救灾之能。

河南河东和山东等地是水灾高发地。百姓再次高呼圣明。

但这高呼万岁还没多久，杨广准备北巡了。于是五月，他征发正在高呼万岁的河北百姓，修凿了一条从太行山到并州的驰道。

说好的《大业律》呢？官吏们摸摸脑袋，也没办法，只能无视《大业律》，只能临时胁迫百姓服役。

杨广在征发河北百姓修驰道的时候就北巡了。

太行山到并州这条驰道，要在皇帝陛下走到这里之前就修好。

于是在这驰道两旁，重现了当年修大运河和东京洛阳时的“盛世”情况，累死征夫无数。

除了太行山到并州这条重量级驰道之外，杨广所走的路还有其他小工程。

李玄霸对杨广所说的“烂怂西边没什么好东西”，只是让杨广的行程稍稍缩短了一丁点往西拐的弯，少了一两条短短的驰道。

李渊也跟着出巡了。

离开时，他特意叮嘱李建成一定要照顾好弟弟们。

李建成与李渊挥泪离别的时候，李世民在那里嗷嗷大哭，抱着李渊的腿不放，把李渊的衣摆上蹭得全是鼻涕眼泪。

李渊鼻头一酸，也抱着李世民呜呜地哭。

父子俩那相拥大哭的模样不像是普通离别，像是生死离别，看得窦夫人和李玄霸都露出了无语的表情。

窦夫人和李玄霸对视一眼，双双叹气。

李建成站在一旁也很尴尬。他也很想加入，但真的哭不出来。

而且他也不明白为何父亲和二弟能哭得这样撕心裂肺。

不就是父亲伴驾出游，这有什么好哭的？

李世民不断在李渊衣服上擦鼻涕：“耶耶、耶耶，要注意安全，不、不要乱跑，跟、跟好陛下，别、别丢了。”

李渊哽咽道：“阿雄也要乖乖听你娘亲和大德的话，不要太调皮。”

李世民先点头，然后睁开红肿的眼睛道：“是大德听我的话！我才是兄长！”

李渊哭着道：“你现在哭成这样子，哪里像个兄长？”

李世民嘴一撇，继续哭。

李渊也继续哭。

杨昭此次又是留守大兴城，这次与李渊一同过来，是想向李渊卖个好，说自己一定会照顾好表弟一家人。

他还把齐王杨暕也带来，等李渊离开之后，就和李世民、李玄霸商量资助书院贫困学子的事。

哪知道，他居然看到这么一场……不知道该如何描述的场景。

这有什么好哭的？唐国公和李大雄真的是亲父子啊。

杨昭见时间差不多了，提醒李渊还要赶路，李渊才依依不舍地放下李世民，又抱了窦夫人一下，才一步三回头离开。

待李渊走远了，窦夫人才嫌弃地用帕子擦自己身上被蹭到的李世民的眼泪和鼻涕，并帮李世民擦脸。

窦夫人尴尬道：“让太子殿下和齐王殿下看笑话了。”

杨昭立刻道：“父子情深，怎么能说是笑话？”

杨暕：“是挺好笑，我差点没憋住笑出声来。”

杨昭：“……”

杨暕：“……”

杨昭张开厚厚的肉巴掌给了弟弟一下，压着弟弟的后脑勺道：“抱歉啊窦夫人，我弟弟还小，不懂事。”

窦夫人连忙道：“无事无事，这本来就是笑话……你哭那么厉害干什么？只是伴驾而已！”

窦夫人狠狠拧了李世民的鼻子。

鼻子红得像是涂了红色颜料的李世民瘪嘴道：“我也不知道，就是想哭。”

李建成和李玄霸都嫌弃地叹了口气。

杨昭看着李建成和李玄霸，有些信了李建成已经与弟弟们和好的传言。

看这表情，李建成和李玄霸兄弟二人还是蛮默契的。

李元吉拉着窦夫人，大声嚷嚷道：“我饿了，我要吃肉！”

窦夫人赶紧捂住李元吉的嘴：“守孝吃什么肉，闭嘴！”

李玄霸赶紧上前道：“太子殿下，齐王殿下，之前请求的事，可否进府一叙？”

杨昭笑道：“我正有此意。”

他装作没听见李元吉说的话。

守孝期间不禁止孩童们吃肉是每个贵族家中都会做的事。

孩童脆弱，能长成者寥寥无几，若是因为守孝而饿着孩童，导致孩童夭折，这才是真正的不孝。

只是潜规则这样，为了表示对逝去长辈的孝顺，肯定不能大咧咧嚷嚷出来。

李元吉这样，若被旁的人听到了，定会认为唐国公府家教不好。杨昭自然要装作没听见。

就算是没眼色如杨暕，此刻也当作什么都没听见，仍旧端着他那副标志性倨傲表情，与李玄霸和红眼睛红鼻子李世民一同进府。

李建成犹豫了一下，还是没好意思跟去。

郑氏的肚子大起来了，他正好去看孩子。

郑氏得知此事后，叹了口气。

她很想劝说李建成抓住机会。一点脸皮算什么？

但李建成将脸面看得极重，她若多说了只会惹李建成不高兴。自己一生都系在李建成身上，郑氏便只能忍下。

不过郑氏劝动李建成派人送吃食过去，并悄悄叮嘱派去的仆人打探他们究竟在计划什么。

仆人回来禀报，此事并不是李二郎和李三郎与太子殿下有什么计划，而是李二郎和李三郎准备资助书院贫困学子读书，齐王得知此事后，也想做些善事，便将此事揽在了身上，李二郎和李三郎只负责给钱。

郑氏问道：“现在他们只是来要钱了？”

仆人道：“仆听到的是这样。”

郑氏和李建成都松了一口气。原来只是这点小事。

郑氏道：“看来太子殿下和齐王殿下对表弟们都很亲近，这点小事也愿意帮着做。郎君以后大可多邀请太子殿下和齐王殿下。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 42: The Emperor Tours the North, Father Departs the Capital

Even if people in this era were prone to believing in the arts of prophecy and omens, Xiao Yan and Fang Xuanling had only met twice, and he was merely a child; Fang Xuanling should not have trusted him so readily.

Li Xuanba pondered this carefully. Fang Xuanling was likely having a truly difficult time right now, and both he and his wife were desperate for a child. Thus, upon hearing Li Xuanba’s words, Fang Xuanling had simply decided to treat a dead horse as if it were still alive, hoping for a miracle.

What if it actually worked?

You could never fathom the absurd lengths to which people desperate for an heir would go.

As for whether Fang Xuanling had guessed something else from his "spoilers," Li Xuanba had no way of knowing.

He would probably have to wait over a decade to hear the truth from Fang Xuanling’s own lips.

Hmm, given the Chancellor’s legendary caution, Li Xuanba suspected he might never get the truth out of him. Even if Fang Xuanling hadn't guessed it now, by then he would surely be singing endless praises of the Second Brother’s "imperial aura."

While Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui were holding Li Shimin and playing with him, Lady Dou sent someone to ask if they needed any refreshments sent over.

Just as Li Xuanba was about to say no, Li Jiancheng also sent someone, similarly inquiring if they needed to provide anything for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba’s friends.

Li Xuanba recognized the man. He was a steward from Lady Zheng’s dowry, now working for Li Jiancheng.

The Eldest Brother truly had found himself a virtuous helpmeet.

Li Xuanba deliberately chatted with the servant for a few moments, letting him witness the childish antics of Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui, and then "accidentally" revealed that the two were merely impoverished scions of minor branches of their respective clans. Only then did he let the man leave with his thanks for Li Jiancheng.

Among the twenty-four meritorious officials of Emperor Taizong’s Lingyan Pavilion, aside from his own relatives and Xiao Yu—who had no personal ties to Taizong but spoke righteously without selfish motives—the rest were all from fallen noble branches or humble backgrounds. Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui were considered the best off among them, yet even they were not highly regarded by the ruling class at this time.

Li Xuanba trusted that after he "inadvertently" revealed their status, the Zheng family would be put at ease.

Sure enough, the servant did not return after leaving.

Lady Dou sent someone once more, and although Li Xuanba said it wasn't necessary, she still prepared some fruits and beverages for them.

Li Shimin, having been ruffled and petted until he was dizzy, quickly jumped out of his new friend’s arms once he regained his senses. He then grabbed Li Xuanba tightly, refusing to let his younger brother leave, insisting that his brother also be held and ruffled—the two brothers had to be treated exactly the same.

Du Ruhui, being a mischievous soul, immediately took advantage of Li Shimin’s "backing" to tease Li Xuanba.

Fang Qiao, wary because of Li Xuanba’s mysterious display earlier, didn't dare reach out.

Li Xuanba sighed and took the initiative to reach out to Fang Qiao: "Go ahead and hold me."

The fear in Fang Qiao’s heart diminished slightly, and he picked Li Xuanba up.

How could one not be afraid of a child who knew the arts of prophecy? Even if Fang Qiao was only half-convinced, a child who spoke of omens so casually to strangers was truly bizarre.

Li Xuanba leaned against Fang Qiao’s shoulder and whispered, "In the future, we will entrust our lives to one another, which is why I’ve set your mind at ease in advance. You must keep my abilities a secret, okay?"

Fang Qiao blinked and gave Li Xuanba’s head a firm pat.

Li Xuanba clutched his head, glaring at Fang Qiao with a frown.

Seeing Li Xuanba’s childish, indignant expression, Fang Qiao’s tense mood suddenly relaxed.

He laughed, "Rest assured, Da De."

Li Xuanba’s face fell even further.

Fang Qiao couldn't help but burst into loud laughter: "So you really do hate that name?"

Li Xuanba turned his head away.

Li Shimin stood with his hands on his hips, puffing out his belly: "In Ah-Xuan’s own words, Ah-Xuan is just being pretentious! I really like the name 'Da Xiong'!"

Li Xuanba: "Ah, yes, yes, yes, Li Da Xiong."

Li Shimin: "Right, that’s me! Keep calling me that!"

Li Xuanba hung his head: [Ah!!!!] Breakdown!

Li Shimin jumped back in fright, then gathered his strength and shouted from the bottom of his lungs: [Ah!!!!!]

He looked at his younger brother triumphantly. Although the number of words I can say through telepathy is limited, my "voice" is louder than yours!

Li Xuanba: "..."

He couldn't be bothered to deal with his childish brother who insisted on competing even over this.

After playing for a while, the two childish ones and the two forced to be childish along with them finally got down to business, looking at Li Xuanba’s collection of books and discussing scholarship.

After discussing academics for a while, Du Ruhui once again regarded Li Xuanba as a kindred spirit and laughed, "The world says Scholar Li is intelligent and cautious, but why do I see you as a wild, unrestrained scholar?"

Li Xuanba replied calmly, "To be different from the world is called being wild; I haven't reached that level yet."

Du Ruhui laughed heartily, "That right there is what makes you wild."

Li Shimin looked up at Fang Qiao and asked, "Is my brother wild? My brother is very sensible and well-behaved, right?"

Fang Qiao: "..." How would I know if that's right or not?

He recalled the cold, detached expression Li Xuanba wore when using the arts of prophecy and said, "Still... he is a bit wild."

Li Shimin huffed in dissatisfaction: "Nonsense!"

Li Xuanba said helplessly, "Brother, I treat different people differently. Why would I be 'wild' toward you?"

Li Shimin: "Oh, that's true."

Li Xuanba clutched his forehead: "Sigh." With this brother around, I can't even pretend to be cool. So annoying.

Du Ruhui and Fang Qiao chuckled.

With Li Er-lang around, it seemed Li San-lang would never be able to be "wild."

...

There are friendships where people remain as strangers even after a lifetime, and friendships where people feel like old acquaintances upon first meeting. Du Ruhui and the Li brothers were the latter.

As for Fang Qiao, he was dragged into this "old acquaintance" dynamic by Du Ruhui.

The four of them became friends, often gathering to exchange academic ideas.

Li Xuanba didn't have many friends. Li Shimin, a social butterfly, also pulled Zhangsun Wuji into their small circle.

Li Shimin had originally wanted to include the sons and grandsons of Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, who were of similar age, but they refused.

After receiving Li Xuanba’s prophecy, they examined Yang Guang’s actions from a more objective standpoint and were certain that Yang Guang truly harbored murderous intent toward them.

Although they had already retired to compile books, no one knew if Yang Guang would still find an excuse to execute them.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were highly favored by Yang Guang and were his personally appointed disciples. Even if they associated closely with them, if they were to meet with disaster in the future, it wouldn't implicate the Li brothers. But it was different for others.

Therefore, Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi told their descendants to be cautious, to stay behind closed doors, avoiding Yang Guang’s notice and preventing future trouble for others.

Consequently, Zhangsun Wuji helplessly became the one with the least academic foundation in this small circle.

As time went on, Zhangsun Wuji didn't want to come anymore.

Li Shimin was thoughtful; when gathering with Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui, he stopped asking Zhangsun Wuji to join.

But after a while, Zhangsun Wuji came on his own initiative and apologized to Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui, hoping they could guide him.

Li Shimin was sometimes thoughtful, but other times quite mischievous.

He mocked him without reservation: "Zhangsun Si-lang, you’re such a stingy and face-conscious person; to think you’d voluntarily cast aside your pride? This doesn't sound like you."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui actually held a faint disdain for Zhangsun Wuji in their hearts and were unwilling to form deep ties with him.

However, Zhangsun Wuji was only thirteen, and they were both well past their twenties, so they weren't too harsh on him. Seeing him apologize sincerely and treat them with the respect of a junior disciple, they intended to let the matter slide.

Unexpectedly, Li Shimin wouldn't let it go, leaving the two in an awkward position.

Zhangsun Wuji knew what kind of person Li Shimin was; he wouldn't get as angry at Li Shimin’s teasing as he would with others.

He said very honestly, "It was my sister who scolded me. She said that by making friends with those more intelligent than oneself, one becomes more intelligent; by making friends with those more virtuous than oneself, one becomes more noble. If one has friends more excellent than oneself but refuses to associate with them out of shame, that is simply allowing oneself to become foolish and base."

After saying this, Zhangsun Wuji covered his face with both hands, so ashamed he couldn't find a place to hide: "My sister’s scolding is truly ruthless."

The bystander Li Xuanba praised, "Brother, you’ll be blessed in the future."

Li Shimin was confused: "Ah, why?"

Zhangsun Wuji lowered his hands and gritted his teeth: "How many sisters do I have?!"

Li Shimin scratched his head: "How would I know how many sisters you have? When I go to your house to play, I never see your sisters."

Zhangsun Wuji and Li Xuanba: "..."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui were also confused, not knowing why Li Xuanba and Zhangsun Wuji were so depressed.

Li Xuanba clutched his forehead: "Brother, Zhangsun Si-lang only has one sister, and that is your fiancée, my future sister-in-law."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui understood.

They covered their mouths and laughed simultaneously.

Li Shimin had a realization: "Oh, her. That’s not right, though. Since she learned to write, the letters she’s written to me have all been gentle and soft; she doesn't seem like a woman who would scold people... I understand! It must be because Zhangsun Si-lang deserved to be scolded! Guanyin-bi couldn't bear it anymore... Mmph?"

Zhangsun Wuji pounced on Li Shimin, covering his mouth, and scolded angrily: "Don't say my sister’s childhood name in front of outsiders! Do you understand the rules? Huh? ...Ah!!!"

Li Shimin, only eight years old, used a shoulder throw to toss the thirteen-year-old Zhangsun Wuji to the ground.

Li Shimin clapped his hands, lifted his chin, and looked down at him: "Too weak. Practice more. Don't end up failing at both literature and martial arts in the future."

Zhangsun Wuji was so angry he almost cried, and the thought of running away crossed his mind again.

Seeing this, Fang Qiao sighed inwardly and hurried to comfort Zhangsun Wuji.

Li Shimin said, "Don't mind him, he’ll be fine after a good cry. Shame leads to courage, right, Ah-Xuan?"

Li Xuanba didn't know what to say.

Did the historical Emperor Taizong treat Zhangsun Wuji like this too? If so, the fact that Zhangsun Wuji remained loyal to him must have been because of Empress Zhangsun.

Li Xuanba: [Brother, you lecture Zhangsun Si-lang as if he were your own son. No wonder you told him later that you treated him like your own flesh and blood.]

Li Shimin: "Hahahaha!"

The three looked at Li Shimin, who was laughing for no reason, with strange expressions.

Li Shimin wiped away tears of laughter and said, "Ah-Xuan just told me a joke."

Du Ruhui asked in confusion, "Da De opened his mouth to speak?"

Li Shimin laughed, "Ah-Xuan and I are twins; only I can hear what he says."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui were both very surprised. Zhangsun Wuji... Zhangsun Wuji was already used to it. He often noticed these two brothers whispering things he couldn't hear in front of him.

Are twins who get along well so amazing?!

Well, yes, they are.

Zhangsun Wuji, who did not get along with his own brothers, felt very sour.

After the venomous tongue attack from the Zhangsun sister, Zhangsun Wuji bit the bullet and integrated into this "academic" small group.

Through their interactions, Du Ruhui and Fang Qiao discovered that Zhangsun Wuji was actually an intelligent and studious person; it was just that his foundation was a bit weak, and he was quite vain, which was why he had performed so poorly before.

They also learned that Zhangsun Wuji’s weak academic foundation was because his father, Zhangsun Sheng, was often away serving in posts, and his elder half-brother, who managed the household, disliked his half-siblings. His mother had a hard enough time protecting him and ensuring he was fed and clothed, so she had no energy left to hire high-level tutors for him.

The two men’s disdain for Zhangsun Wuji vanished completely.

This "playing the victim" was something Li Xuanba had deliberately revealed.

For upright gentlemen, "playing the victim" was the best way to mend rifts. Li Xuanba didn't want these three future pillars of the Zhenguan era to develop grudges while they were still in their infancy.

Although Zhangsun Wuji was not particularly broad-minded, he remembered both grudges and kindness.

After learning of Zhangsun Wuji’s plight, Du Ruhui and Fang Qiao began to help him catch up with his studies very earnestly and carefully.

Fang Qiao, in particular, was exceptionally good to Zhangsun Wuji because he had no children of his own.

Zhangsun Wuji was deeply moved and went home to cry to his sister, saying he had met such good people for the first time.

The Zhangsun sister asked in confusion, "Are the Li brothers not good?"

Zhangsun Wuji said, "Li San-lang seems approachable, but I always feel he is mysterious and somewhat terrifying; as for Li Er-lang... don't mention that jerk! He only knows how to bully people! I curse him every time I see him!"

The Zhangsun sister’s eyes curved into crescents as she smiled.

Zhangsun Wuji said unhappily, "I’m cursing him, and you’re actually smiling? Do you not believe me?"

The Zhangsun sister laughed, "Brother, the fact that you can curse him so recklessly without worrying about him getting angry shows that you believe Li Er-lang is a broad-minded person, and it also shows that Li Er-lang is your best friend."

Zhangsun Wuji blushed, put his sister down, and ran away.

The Zhangsun sister sighed deeply. My brother is really easy to embarrass.

She tilted her little head, tapping her soft cheek with her finger, and thought of the appearance of her future husband she had secretly glimpsed, her cheeks flushing with a rosy glow.

My future husband looks so good when he smiles. When will Father return? If Father doesn't return, my future husband won't come over to play.

Although the Zhangsun sister didn't understand love, she knew who looked good.

That fair-skinned, red-lipped young man who could draw a bow and shoot arrows was the best-looking of all!

What should I say to my future husband today? Should I secretly tell him that Brother called him a jerk behind his back?

Hmm, that doesn't seem very nice.

...

"Ah-Xuan, this Zhangsun Si-lang is truly arrogant; he actually called me a jerk behind my back!" Li Shimin slammed the table and cursed.

Li Xuanba put down his scroll and peeked at the ugly, circular characters written by his future sister-in-law.

Oh, wow. Zhangsun Wuji had been "sold out" by his sister.

"You mustn't tell Zhangsun Si-lang, or he’ll blame your future sister-in-law," Li Xuanba said.

Li Shimin crossed his arms and huffed: "Of course I won't tell him. Hmph, I’ll find a way to torment him."

Li Xuanba once again doubted whether the historical Emperor Taizong really got along with Zhangsun Wuji like his Second Brother did. If so, Zhangsun Wuji... you’ve had it tough.

When he was childhood sweethearts with the Second Brother, Zhangsun Wuji could at least pounce on him and throw a few punches, regardless of whether he could win.

After the Second Brother became Emperor and said he treated Zhangsun Wuji like his own son, Zhangsun Wuji still had to grit his teeth and say, "Thank you for your imperial grace."

After Li Shimin finished cursing Zhangsun Wuji, he slumped on the table and said, "Father is going to run away from home again."

Li Xuanba’s mouth twitched: "It’s a departure, not running away."

Li Shimin said, "It’s about the same."

Li Xuanba said, "It’s very different."

Li Shimin said, "I’m the older brother; if I say it’s about the same, then it’s about the same."

Li Xuanba couldn't be bothered to argue with his Second Brother: "Heh."

Li Shimin continued to sigh: "After Father leaves, will Eldest Brother find trouble to bully us again?"

Li Xuanba said, "No. After Father leaves, the head of the household is Mother."

Li Shimin was happy: "That’s true. Then let Father leave quickly."

Li Xuanba felt the same way.

After the death of the Old Lady Dugu, Li Yuan seemed to have matured a lot. Or perhaps because he felt guilty toward them, Li Yuan was overly kind to them. Every day when he returned from duty, he would teach them reading and martial arts, and on his days off, he would take them horseback riding.

If Li Yuan didn't leave soon, he wouldn't be able to hold out much longer.

Li Xuanba knew that he was still quite starved for affection and easily tempted.

Fortunately, Li Yuan was leaving.

During the time when Li Shimin and Li Xuanba’s friendship with Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui was growing day by day, many major events occurred in the imperial court.

For instance, the promulgation of the *Daye Code* caused the entire court and public to unanimously hail the Emperor as a wise ruler.

In the late years of Emperor Wen of Sui, although there was the *Kaihuang Code*, justice was not administered according to it; instead, it followed the Emperor’s whims, with all crimes punished severely. It was common for someone to be beheaded for stealing a single coin, or for three people to be executed for stealing a melon.

The *Daye Code* reduced many of the harsh punishments from the late Sui Wen era and stipulated that corvée labor would not be conscripted during busy farming seasons, nor would women or slaves be conscripted. The common people, who had suffered enough under the harsh and complex punishments of Emperor Wen, hailed the Emperor as sagely.

That same year, Yang Guang built many granaries and public storehouses near Luoyang to prepare for the daily needs of the Eastern Capital and to provide disaster relief.

Henan, Hedong, and Shandong were prone to flooding. The people hailed him as sagely once again.

But before this cheering had lasted long, Yang Guang prepared for a northern tour. So, in the fifth month, he conscripted the Hebei people who were still cheering "Long Live" to build a post road from the Taihang Mountains to Bingzhou.

What happened to the *Daye Code*? The officials scratched their heads, but there was nothing they could do; they had no choice but to ignore the *Daye Code* and temporarily coerce the people into labor.

Yang Guang began his northern tour while conscripting the Hebei people to build the road.

The post road from the Taihang Mountains to Bingzhou had to be completed before His Majesty the Emperor arrived.

Thus, along this road, the "prosperous age" scenes from the construction of the Grand Canal and the Eastern Capital of Luoyang were recreated, with countless conscripted laborers dying of exhaustion.

In addition to this major post road, there were other small projects along the route Yang Guang took.

Li Xuanba’s comment to Yang Guang that "the western side is a dump with nothing good" only caused Yang Guang to shorten his itinerary slightly, avoiding a few detours and a couple of short post roads.

Li Yuan also followed the tour.

Before leaving, he specifically instructed Li Jiancheng to take good care of his younger brothers.

When Li Jiancheng was saying a tearful goodbye to Li Yuan, Li Shimin was there howling, clinging to Li Yuan’s leg and smearing his robes with snot and tears.

Li Yuan’s nose stung, and he hugged Li Shimin, sobbing as well.

The sight of the father and son weeping in each other’s arms didn't look like a normal farewell, but rather a parting of life and death, leaving Lady Dou and Li Xuanba with speechless expressions.

Lady Dou and Li Xuanba exchanged a look and both sighed.

Li Jiancheng stood to the side, feeling very awkward. He wanted to join in, but he really couldn't cry.

Moreover, he didn't understand why his father and second brother could cry so heart-wrenchingly.

It was just his father accompanying the Emperor on a tour; what was there to cry about?

Li Shimin kept wiping his snot on Li Yuan’s clothes: "Father, Father, be careful, d-don't run around, follow the Emperor closely, d-don't get lost."

Li Yuan choked up: "Ah-Xiong must also be obedient and listen to your mother and Da De; don't be too naughty."

Li Shimin nodded first, then opened his red, swollen eyes and said: "It’s Da De who listens to me! I am the older brother!"

Li Yuan cried: "You’re crying like this now, how do you look like an older brother?"

Li Shimin pouted and continued to cry.

Li Yuan continued to cry as well.

Yang Zhao was left to guard Daxing City this time. He had come with Li Yuan to curry favor, saying he would definitely take good care of his cousin’s family.

He had also brought the Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, with him, intending to discuss funding for poor students at the academy with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba after Li Yuan left.

Who would have thought he would see such a... scene that he didn't know how to describe.

What was there to cry about? The Duke of Tang and Li Da Xiong were truly father and son.

Seeing that it was about time, Yang Zhao reminded Li Yuan that he had to get on the road. Only then did Li Yuan reluctantly let go of Li Shimin, hug Lady Dou, and leave, looking back every few steps.

Once Li Yuan was far away, Lady Dou disgustedly used a handkerchief to wipe the tears and snot Li Shimin had smeared on her, and helped Li Shimin wipe his face.

Lady Dou said awkwardly: "I’ve let the Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi see a joke."

Yang Zhao immediately said: "Deep father-son affection, how can that be called a joke?"

Yang Jian: "It is quite funny; I almost couldn't hold back my laughter."

Yang Zhao: "..."

Yang Jian: "..."

Yang Zhao slapped his younger brother with his thick palm and pressed down on the back of his head: "Apologies, Lady Dou, my brother is still young and doesn't know any better."

Lady Dou hurriedly said: "It’s fine, it’s fine, this was indeed a joke... Why are you crying so hard? It’s just accompanying the Emperor!"

Lady Dou pinched Li Shimin’s nose hard.

Li Shimin, whose nose was as red as if it had been painted, pouted: "I don't know either, I just wanted to cry."

Li Jiancheng and Li Xuanba both sighed in disgust.

Yang Zhao looked at Li Jiancheng and Li Xuanba, somewhat believing the rumors that Li Jiancheng had reconciled with his younger brothers.

Looking at their expressions, the Li brothers were quite in sync.

Li Yuanji pulled on Lady Dou, shouting loudly: "I’m hungry, I want to eat meat!"

Lady Dou hurriedly covered Li Yuanji’s mouth: "We’re in mourning, what meat? Shut up!"

Li Xuanba quickly stepped forward: "Your Highness the Crown Prince, Your Highness the Prince of Qi, regarding the matter we requested, may we go inside the manor to discuss it?"

Yang Zhao smiled: "That is exactly what I intended."

He pretended not to hear what Li Yuanji had said.

Not forbidding children from eating meat during the mourning period was something every noble family did.

Children were fragile, and few survived to adulthood; if a child were to die of malnutrition because of mourning, that would be true unfilial piety.

It was just an unspoken rule; to show filial piety to the departed elders, one certainly couldn't shout it out loud.

If Li Yuanji’s words were heard by others, they would surely think the Duke of Tang’s household had poor upbringing. Yang Zhao naturally had to pretend he hadn't heard.

Even someone as tactless as Yang Jian pretended not to hear anything at this moment, still maintaining his signature arrogant expression as he entered the manor with Li Xuanba and the red-eyed, red-nosed Li Shimin.

Li Jiancheng hesitated but didn't feel comfortable following them.

Lady Zheng’s belly was growing, and he decided to go check on the child.

Upon learning of this, Lady Zheng sighed.

She really wanted to persuade Li Jiancheng to seize the opportunity. What was a little pride worth?

But Li Jiancheng valued his reputation highly; if she said too much, she would only make him unhappy. Her whole life was tied to Li Jiancheng, so she had to endure it.

However, Lady Zheng persuaded Li Jiancheng to send food over and quietly instructed the servant to find out what they were planning.

The servant returned to report that it wasn't a plan between the Li brothers and the Crown Prince, but rather that the Li brothers were preparing to fund poor students at the academy, and the Prince of Qi, hearing of this, wanted to do some good deeds, so he took the matter upon himself, with the Li brothers only responsible for providing the money.

Lady Zheng asked: "So they are just coming to ask for money now?"

The servant said: "That is what I heard."

Lady Zheng and Li Jiancheng both breathed a sigh of relief. So it was just this small matter.

Lady Zheng said: "It seems the Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi are very close to our cousins, willing to help with even such small matters. My lord, you can invite them more often in the future."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第42章 皇帝北巡父离京 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
李建成叹气：“你以为我不想吗，宴会和打猎都要等出孝后。我已经在朝为官，不像二郎三郎，摆一壶白水就敢邀请别人。”

郑氏叹息：“说得也是。”

此事于是暂且搁置不提，先等一年孝期结束后再说。

李玄霸送走窦夫人和李建成派来的人后，拿出了自己早就准备好的奖学金、助学金制度介绍，交给了杨昭和杨暕各一份。

杨昭先粗略看了一遍，然后又仔细观看，并思考这个制度能不能用在太学上。

杨暕则在考虑自己需要花多少钱才能显得特别厉害。

两人看完后，虽然李玄霸自认为做得完美无缺，还是又给了几个版本让两人修改。

杨昭和杨暕争论了一番，最后在第一版的基础上小幅度增减了一番，也就是钱财数额问题，并没有多大的变化。但看两人的神情，都很有参与感。

李世民一边用热帕子敷眼睛，一边想着弟弟的话。

“大部分做决定的人都会为了展现出自己很有本事，明明挑不出毛病也会说重做。所以这时候就要给他们准备上中下三策，让他们自行决定。有的聪明人会把上中下策写得差不多，有的人为了凸显自己真正的献策而把其他两策弄得特别离谱。”

“总之，献策和纳策也是心理博弈，很好玩。”

李世民看着杨昭和杨暕。

显然，弟弟说的话在太子殿下和齐王殿下这里很正确，但他还是认为不对。

他就不喜欢弄这些虚的。赶紧决定赶紧做事不好吗？献一个最好的策就好，免得我还选，选择好麻烦。

李世民辩论不赢弟弟。他将此事压在心中，准备去找房乔和杜如晦帮忙。

再加上一个长孙无忌小挂件，他就不信四个人还辩论不赢弟弟，哼。

资助贫困学子确实只是一件小事，杨昭和杨暕很快就离开了。

走的时候，杨暕非常不客气地把李世民和李玄霸自用的香皂给顺走了，连用了一半的都拿了，让李玄霸分外无语。

杨昭也有些脸红，骂道：“虽然父皇为了惩罚你，扣了送给你的贡品香皂，但我不是给了你一些吗？香皂铺子也已经开始贩卖了，你又不是没有购买的资格。你去抢别人的香皂干什么？”

杨暕理直气壮：“来都来了，我总不能空手回去。”

杨昭：“？？？”你是贼吗！！还不能空手回去？！！

杨暕道：“再说了，他们是我的表弟，我这个表兄帮他们做事，他们难道一点都不表示一下？”

杨昭：“？？？”你还对表弟索贿？！那你别来做了，我去做！！

李世民打圆场：“不过是几块香皂，齐王表兄看得起，随便拿。我们都是亲戚，这有什么不好意思。”

杨暕倨傲：“就是！”说完，他不等太子兄长登车，自己先骑马扬长而去。

杨昭无奈，只能不断说着“大不是”，气得胖子捧心。

李世民老气横秋道：“阿玄，家家有本难念的经啊。太子表兄辛苦了。”

李玄霸点头：“太子殿下辛苦了。”

杨昭深呼吸，脑袋有点晕。

他勉强挤出笑容，揉了揉两个表弟的小揪揪，艰难地挪动脚步，咬牙切齿地追着弟弟离开。

杨昭的马夫把马车开出了战车的气势，还为了通行无阻亮出了太子的令牌。

“太子殿下肯定给马夫下了令，一定要追到齐王殿下。”李世民捏着下巴，“真想跟上去看笑话。”

李玄霸道：“有这个时间，不如做功课。明天要交的功课你做了多少了？”

李世民表情一僵。

李玄霸也表情一僵。他不敢置信地问道：“哥！你现在又不能出门打猎，怎么还能欠功课？而且我们不是一直在一起做功课吗？！”

李世民讪讪道：“啊，这个，我做倒是做了，就是，就是有点敷衍。”

李玄霸赶紧拉着李世民去看李世民的功课。

在一张又一张写满功课的纸上，字与字之间画着各种奇怪的小人，写着各种奇怪的口号和……设定？

李玄霸丈二和尚摸不着头脑：“哥，你在写什么？”

李世民对手指，眼神往上瞟：“这个嘛，写功课的时候，就突然那么一想，想象自己狩猎和打仗的场面，就……就记下来了。”

李玄霸默默看了二哥一眼，顺着二哥的话再次观察二哥在功课周围的涂鸦。

哦，原来这个是狩猎，那么前面那个小点就是猎物。小点上面有两个长条……

李世民：“是兔子！”

小点上面有两个山字。

李世民：“是麋鹿！”

小点上面有个王，那肯定是……

李世民张牙舞爪：“是大老虎！”

小点上面有个……锅盖？

李世民叉腰：“是突厥大将军！”

李玄霸问道：“突厥有大将军？不是可汗吗？”

李世民指着另一个奇形怪状的锅盖头：“这个是突厥可汗。”

李玄霸疑惑：“这个锅盖头……这个突厥可汗怎么这么扭曲？”

李世民得意地笑道：“我猎完了他们草原上的猎物，战胜了他们突厥所有勇士，于是突厥可汗就向我献舞表示臣服。”

李玄霸：“……献、献舞？”

李世民道：“就是跳舞啊！”

他说着就给李玄霸来了一段舞，那个胡旋舞转得特别利索。

李玄霸：“……哦，跳舞啊。”

他捏了一把自己的脸。

我是专业的，从来不笑，除非忍不住。

“哈哈哈哈，二哥，这个功课你直接交上去吧。记得把你现在说的话都原封不动地告诉老师。”

“不行不行，阿玄快帮我！”

“帮你什么？你当老师认不出我的字。”

“阿玄，快用你无敌的智慧给哥哥想想办法！”

“滚，虽然你是大雄，但我又不是哆啦A梦。”

“虽然不懂你在说什么，但没关系，你可以是！”

李玄霸和李世民兄弟二人拉拉扯扯，然后不知道谁先绊倒谁，两人滚在地上打了一架。

途中李智云跑来找哥哥们玩耍，见状立刻扑了过去，勇敢地与两个哥哥决斗。

待窦夫人来找万氏时，就看见万氏站在树荫下，看着三个孩子在地上滚来滚去笑作一团。

李玄霸居然支棱起来了，一直到现在还没有躺下。

万氏拉住了想要阻止孩子们的窦夫人，笑眯眯道：“夫人，你说三郎能支撑到什么时候？”

窦夫人叹气。她点了点万氏的鼻尖，道：“促狭鬼，还看孩子们的笑话。”

她仔细观看地上的战况，道：“已经支撑不住了。”

她话音刚落，李玄霸就翻滚出战局，躺平了。

李世民和李智云非常默契地滚到了另一边，进行最后的大决战。

李玄霸见母亲来了，一边大喘着气，一边大声道：“母亲！哥在功课上画小人！我们就把哥画小人的功课交上去吧！自己做的错事要自己承担后果！”

李世民一僵，被李智云一头撞到下巴。

“哎哟。”李世民捂着下巴。

李智云坐起身，得意地大笑。

万氏赶紧跑过去，不顾会弄脏衣服，把泥猴子李小五抱起来，讨好地笑道：“我带小五去洗澡了。”

然后她不等窦夫人回答，抱着儿子就跑。

再不跑，小五也要和二郎三郎一起被惩罚了。

窦夫人见万氏这模样，分外无语。

李渊还在孝期中，不需要女人伺候。又是北巡，路途艰难，女子有些不方便。所以这次万氏没有随行，李渊只带了许多身强力壮的家丁私兵同行。

独孤老夫人又已经去世，万氏不需要再谨小慎微躲在院子里不出来。窦夫人干脆将李智云的小院子挪动到万氏居住的院落一旁，实际上就是让万氏照顾李智云了。

她知道万氏终于能亲自抚养孩子一定会很高兴，但也不能太纵着小五。窦夫人决定等会儿找万氏好好说说。

现在，窦氏找人按住明知道逃不了还想逃跑的李世民。

“先洗澡，然后好好和娘说说画小人的事。”窦夫人露出温婉慈祥的微笑。

李世民立刻伸出手，给了告状狗弟弟的脑壳一下。
chunks.englishText:
Li Jiancheng sighed, "Do you think I don't want to? But banquets and hunting trips must wait until the mourning period is over. I am already an official at court; I cannot act like Erlang or Sanlang, who dare to invite others over with nothing more than a pot of plain water."

Lady Zheng sighed, "That is also true."

The matter was thus shelved for the time being, to be revisited only after the one-year mourning period concluded.

After Li Xuanba saw off Lady Dou and the men sent by Li Jiancheng, he took out the scholarship and financial aid proposals he had prepared and handed a copy to both Yang Zhao and Yang Jian.

Yang Zhao first skimmed through them, then studied them carefully, contemplating whether such a system could be implemented in the Imperial Academy.

Yang Jian, meanwhile, was busy calculating how much money he would need to spend to appear particularly impressive.

After they finished reading, even though Li Xuanba felt his work was flawless, he still provided a few alternative versions for them to revise.

Yang Zhao and Yang Jian debated for a while, eventually making minor adjustments to the first version—mostly regarding the specific monetary amounts—without any significant changes. Yet, judging by their expressions, both felt deeply involved in the process.

Li Shimin, while pressing a hot towel to his eyes, pondered his younger brother’s words.

"Most people in positions of power, in order to show off their own competence, will insist on revisions even when they cannot find a single flaw. That is why you must prepare three options—superior, mediocre, and inferior—and let them decide for themselves. Some clever people will write all three options to be roughly equal, while others will make the other two options intentionally absurd just to highlight the brilliance of their preferred proposal."

"In short, offering and accepting advice is a psychological game. It’s quite fun."

Li Shimin looked at Yang Zhao and Yang Jian.

Clearly, his brother’s words held true for the Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi, but he still felt it was wrong.

He didn't like playing these hollow games. Wouldn't it be better to just make a decision and get things done? Just offer the best plan and be done with it; having to choose is such a hassle.

Li Shimin could not win a debate against his brother. He kept these thoughts to himself, planning to seek help from Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui later.

With the addition of Zhangsun Wuji as a sidekick, he didn't believe the four of them couldn't out-argue his brother. Hmph.

Sponsoring impoverished students was indeed a minor matter, and Yang Zhao and Yang Jian soon took their leave.

As they were leaving, Yang Jian very unceremoniously swiped the soap that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were using for themselves, even taking the half-used bars, which left Li Xuanba completely speechless.

Yang Zhao blushed slightly and scolded, "Even though Father confiscated the tribute soap meant for you as punishment, didn't I give you some? The soap shop has already started selling them; it’s not as if you don't have the means to buy them. Why are you snatching other people's soap?"

Yang Jian was righteous and indignant: "Since I’m already here, I can't leave empty-handed."

Yang Zhao: "???" Are you a thief?! What do you mean you can't leave empty-handed?!!

Yang Jian said, "Besides, they are my cousins. As their elder cousin, I’m doing them a favor. Shouldn't they show some appreciation?"

Yang Zhao: "???" You’re extorting your own cousins?! If that’s how you feel, don't do it—I’ll do it myself!!

Li Shimin smoothed things over: "It’s just a few bars of soap. If Cousin Prince of Qi thinks highly of them, just take them. We’re all family; there’s no need to be embarrassed."

Yang Jian acted haughty: "Exactly!" With that, he didn't even wait for the Crown Prince to board his carriage, instead mounting his horse and galloping away.

Yang Zhao could only sigh helplessly, muttering "What a disgrace," his chubby face flushed with frustration.

Li Shimin said with an air of maturity, "Ah Xuan, every family has its own troubles. Crown Prince Cousin has it rough."

Li Xuanba nodded, "His Highness the Crown Prince has it rough."

Yang Zhao took a deep breath, his head spinning.

He forced a smile, patted his two cousins on their little topknots, and moved his feet with great difficulty, gritting his teeth as he chased after his brother.

Yang Zhao’s coachman drove the carriage with the momentum of a war chariot, even flashing the Crown Prince’s token to ensure an unobstructed path.

"The Crown Prince must have ordered the coachman to catch up to the Prince of Qi at all costs," Li Shimin said, rubbing his chin. "I really want to follow them and watch the show."

Li Xuanba said, "If you have time for that, you might as well do your homework. How much of tomorrow’s assignment have you finished?"

Li Shimin’s expression stiffened.

Li Xuanba’s expression also stiffened. He asked in disbelief, "Brother! You can't even go out hunting right now, so how can you be behind on your homework? And haven't we been doing our homework together the whole time?!"

Li Shimin said sheepishly, "Ah, well, I did do it, it’s just... it’s a bit perfunctory."

Li Xuanba hurriedly pulled Li Shimin over to check his work.

On page after page of homework, between the characters, were drawings of strange little stick figures, accompanied by bizarre slogans and... settings?

Li Xuanba was completely baffled: "Brother, what are you writing?"

Li Shimin fiddled with his fingers, his eyes darting upward: "Well, when I was doing the homework, I just had a sudden thought. I imagined scenes of hunting and warfare, and... and I just wrote them down."

Li Xuanba silently looked at his second brother, then followed his lead to observe the doodles surrounding the homework.

Oh, so this was hunting, and that little dot in front was the prey. There were two long lines above the dot...

Li Shimin: "It’s a rabbit!"

There were two "mountain" characters above the dot.

Li Shimin: "It’s an elk!"

And the dot with a "King" character on it, that must be...

Li Shimin gestured wildly: "It’s a big tiger!"

And the dot with a... pot lid on it?

Li Shimin put his hands on his hips: "It’s a Turkic Great General!"

Li Xuanba asked: "Do the Turks have Great Generals? Isn't it the Khagan?"

Li Shimin pointed to another strangely shaped pot-lid head: "This one is the Turkic Khagan."

Li Xuanba was puzzled: "This pot-lid head... why is this Turkic Khagan so twisted?"

Li Shimin laughed triumphantly: "I hunted all the prey on their grasslands and defeated all their Turkic warriors, so the Turkic Khagan is performing a dance for me to show his submission."

Li Xuanba: "...Performing a, a dance?"

Li Shimin said: "Yes, dancing!"

As he spoke, he performed a dance for Li Xuanba, spinning with the Hu Xuan dance with remarkable agility.

Li Xuanba: "...Oh, dancing."

He pinched his own cheek.

*I am a professional. I never laugh, unless I can't help it.*

"Hahahaha, Second Brother, just hand this homework in as it is. Remember to tell the teacher exactly what you just told me."

"No, no, Ah Xuan, hurry and help me!"

"Help you with what? Do you think the teacher won't recognize my handwriting?"

"Ah Xuan, use your invincible wisdom to think of a way for your brother!"

"Get lost. Even if you are Nobita, I am not Doraemon."

"I don't know what you're talking about, but it doesn't matter—you can be!"

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin wrestled, and before long, it was unclear who tripped whom, and the two rolled onto the ground in a scuffle.

Li Zhiyun ran over to play with his brothers, and seeing the scene, he immediately pounced, bravely joining the duel between his two older brothers.

When Lady Dou came to find Lady Wan, she saw Lady Wan standing in the shade of a tree, watching the three children rolling around on the ground, laughing in a heap.

Li Xuanba had actually managed to hold his own, and he hadn't laid down yet.

Lady Wan held back Lady Dou, who was about to stop the children, and said with a smile, "My Lady, how long do you think Sanlang can hold out?"

Lady Dou sighed. She tapped the tip of Lady Wan's nose and said, "You little rascal, still finding amusement in the children's antics."

She watched the battle on the ground closely and said, "He can't hold out much longer."

No sooner had she spoken than Li Xuanba rolled out of the fray and laid flat.

Li Shimin and Li Zhiyun, with great tacit understanding, rolled to the other side to engage in their final showdown.

Seeing his mother had arrived, Li Xuanba panted heavily and shouted, "Mother! Brother is drawing little people on his homework! Let's hand in his homework with the drawings on it! He has to face the consequences of his own mistakes!"

Li Shimin stiffened and was promptly headbutted in the chin by Li Zhiyun.

"Ouch," Li Shimin clutched his chin.

Li Zhiyun sat up and laughed triumphantly.

Lady Wan rushed over, not caring about getting her clothes dirty, and scooped up the mud-covered Li Xiao Wu, smiling ingratiatingly: "I'm taking Xiao Wu to wash up."

Then, without waiting for Lady Dou’s reply, she ran off with her son.

If she didn't run now, Xiao Wu would be punished along with Erlang and Sanlang.

Seeing Lady Wan’s behavior, Lady Dou was left speechless.

Li Yuan was still in the mourning period and did not require women to serve him. Furthermore, the northern inspection was a difficult journey, which was inconvenient for women. Thus, Lady Wan did not accompany them this time; Li Yuan only took a group of strong, able-bodied servants and private soldiers.

Since the Old Lady Dugu had passed away, Lady Wan no longer needed to be overly cautious and hide in her courtyard. Lady Dou had simply moved Li Zhiyun’s small courtyard next to Lady Wan’s, effectively letting Lady Wan take care of him.

She knew Lady Wan would be overjoyed to finally raise her child herself, but she couldn't let Xiao Wu be too spoiled. Lady Dou decided to have a serious talk with Lady Wan later.

For now, Lady Dou had someone hold down Li Shimin, who was trying to escape even though he knew he couldn't.

"Wash up first, then tell Mother all about these little drawings," Lady Dou said with a gentle, kind smile.

Li Shimin immediately reached out and gave his tattletale younger brother a knock on the head.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第43章 不肖弟子李世民 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第43章 不肖弟子李世民

=

李世民的涂鸦作业还是落到了三位老师手中。

虞世南只是笑了笑， 没有处罚李世民。

高颎和宇文弼见李世民如此有志气，便给李世民增加了军略功课。

宇文弼很想亲自教导李世民，但论军略， 他比高颎大大不如。虽然他很喜欢与高颎争论， 但对高颎的本事是真心佩服的。所以宇文弼退一步， 只教李世民如何观察战场形势，以及在战场上厮杀的真本事。

高颎教的是后方的“帅”，宇文弼教的就是亲临战场的“将”。

李世民对这增加的负担又开心又郁闷。

他把李玄霸的脑壳当木鱼敲：“都怪你， 我现在都没空玩耍了。”

李玄霸忍了忍，忍无可忍，跳下榻去找母亲告状。

李世民拽着李玄霸的手臂， 不准李玄霸去告状。

兄弟二人又打了一架。

窦夫人得知此事后扶额：“他们有一日不打架吗？”

万氏一边绣着小披风，一边笑道：“听闻二郎的武艺， 已经比大他四五岁的少年厉害。但三郎居然每次和二郎打得旗鼓相当， 看来三郎也是真人不露相。”

窦夫人“扑哧”笑得花枝乱颤。

周围仆人也都忍俊不禁。

李玄霸的练武之旅基本已经中断，搏杀的功夫都改成了养生的功夫，武艺老师变成孙医师。

不过高颎认为军略可以不上战场，李玄霸也能学，便把李玄霸也拎着一同加课。

宇文弼琢磨着军略也要了解战场的情况， 李玄霸可以不学，但李世民学的时候他也得看着。李玄霸又加了一场旁听课。

于是李玄霸的负担也加重了。

李世民大笑着“阿玄活该”， 笑掉了一颗大牙，吐出牙和鲜血继续大笑。

李玄霸气得磨牙，也不小心磨掉了一颗牙。

两人掉的牙还是同一处， 回家后嘴里多了一个一模一样的豁洞。窦夫人把肚子都笑疼了。

万氏也笑得直抹眼泪花子：“就算你们是双生子， 也没必要连牙都掉一样的位置。”

李世民张着满是豁洞的大嘴毫不在意地大笑：“没办法， 双生子就是这样。”

李玄霸不想露出满嘴豁洞， 也不想说话漏风，抿着嘴不说话。

看着李世民和李玄霸完全不同的反应，窦夫人和万氏再次笑弯了腰。

李玄霸尴尬得无地自容。李世民却跟着母亲和阿姨一同傻笑，丝毫不能理解弟弟的尴尬。

高颎教了李世民和李玄霸一月的军略后，李玄霸的成绩遥遥领先二哥李世民，李世民成了高颎恨得牙痒痒的朽木庸才。

高颎：先假设一个战场，假设多少敌人，假设地形如何，两方朝堂局势，巴拉巴拉……你要如何做？

李玄霸：先派间谍打探对方情况，再看看能不能用离间计，然后悄悄以其他名义征粮征兵，千里奇袭巴拉巴拉……

李世民：有这么麻烦吗？给我一万铁骑！我亲自领兵出征！把对方主将干掉！

高颎：“？？？”

李玄霸无语扶额。

李世民坚持己见。

高颎按着青筋爆绽的额头，详细给李世民解释兵书。

李世民却摊手：“兵书不过是前人之见，前人就一定比我强吗？我能打得过，为何要那么麻烦？”

高颎想要因材施教，给李世民一万兵，给对方十万兵，然后让李世民演示一下如何阵斩对方主将。

李世民叉腰仰头：“骑兵全带甲，冲进敌阵，不就把他们冲散了！”

高颎捂着胸口深呼吸：“具装骑兵是你这么用的吗？没有人会带着具装骑兵直接往对方军阵中冲锋！骑兵是用来擦过对方军阵，或者贴面射击，以达到逼迫对方军阵变形的目的！就是楚霸王再世，也不是带着骑兵直接和举盾的步兵对冲！你一万人冲到对方十万人的军阵中，那就是自入埋伏！”

李世民道：“那就再冲出来啊。”

高颎呼吸都不畅了，手指头不断点着李世民的半秃的小脑壳，把李世民的小脑壳点得一晃一晃：“再冲出来？四方都是人，就算你骑在马上，也看不到军阵薄弱处！对方也有将领在，会让你冲出去？”

李世民就算小脑壳一晃一晃，还是坚持道：“说不定呢？说不定我就是比他们都厉害！我冲出去再冲进来，再冲出去再冲进来，多冲几次，敌方步兵方阵再强的战斗意识都会被我瓦解！”

高颎太阳穴一抽一抽的疼，身体忍不住晃了一下。

李玄霸本来正捂嘴笑，见状赶紧扶着高颎的手，给老师顺气：“老师，别生气，二哥就是这样，你把能教的都教了，他接下来怎么做，就别管了。”

高颎指着李世民，咬牙切齿道：“我就不信把你掰不过来！”

李玄霸叹气：“这个……以二哥的性格还真是掰不过来，老师你提前放弃吧。”

差点被气出脑溢血的高颎品出点味来，他用惊疑不定的视线在李世民和李玄霸中来回打量。

李世民道：“阿玄，你能预见我未来的成就吗？快和老师说，我未来是不是做到了！”

李玄霸道：“我可不能说。若说你未来做到了，你就会失去冷静和谦虚，到时候说不准变成了庸才；说你没做到，你也可能误入歧途，变得过分谨慎，失去了自己的灵性。所以你先好好学本事，自己思考将要走的路。”

李世民抱着手臂道：“也对，知道了未来就没意思了。而且我肯定比你预见的更厉害！老师，继续！我就不信辩不赢你！”

高颎狠狠戳了李世民的额头一下，把李世民的额头戳了个红印子：“谁和你论兵？老夫我有带兵的实绩，你有什么？等你有了实绩，再和我论兵！”

李世民捂着额头道：“那老师你可要好好养生，一定要活到我成为大将军的时候。”

高颎：“？？？”

李玄霸扶额。二哥这话虽然没错，但听着怎么这么不对劲？

果然，高颎被气得冷笑一声，李世民又被加了作业。

你说不看兵书就不看吗？想要总结出自己的路，就要先穷尽先贤的路，给我抄兵书去！

高颎实在是气得今天不想再看到李世民，布置了作业就把李世民赶走，让他提前去宇文弼那里学习。

宇文弼喜欢当先锋，李世民滚去和宇文弼这个老匹夫混！

李玄霸被高颎留下来，继续传授衣钵。

高颎喝了一碗静心宁神的药后，才让面色被气出来的潮红消退。

他有气无力地道：“大德，你和老师说个准信，你二哥难道未来带兵真的就是这副……奇怪的模样？每次都以身犯险，把运气寄托在天命上？真的扭转不过来了？千金之子坐不垂堂啊！”

李玄霸想了想，叹气道：“二哥带兵确实总是亲自当先锋。”多的，李玄霸便不说了。

高颎道：“就算他必须亲自带兵，但这冲阵方式……”

李玄霸再次叹了口气：“但二哥真的做到了。他带兵冲入对方敌阵，然后瞅准敌阵的薄弱处带兵冲出来，瞅准机会又冲进去，如此往返，鲜血盈袖，箭用完了就用刀砍，刀砍钝了就用弓劈……他真的做到了。”

高颎再次深呼吸，他拿出放着让人清醒的香料包闻了闻，道：“他难道手下就没有猛将可以代替他涉险吗！”

李玄霸想了想，道：“有啊，还不少。比如他麾下有个叫尉迟敬德的，他说他与尉迟敬德二人合作，千军万马都不怕。于是他就带着尉迟敬德，二人跑去当诱饵，遛着敌人几千骑兵入包围圈。”

高颎差点眼前一黑，赶紧俯首猛吸香气：“他的下属就没有人能劝阻他吗？！”

李玄霸摊手：“二哥又没说他去打仗，只说带着人去附近侦查情况。尉迟敬德被迫与他一同当诱饵的时候，估计也没想到这一出。所以老师，别再为二哥生气了，你气不完的。”

高颎命令人又端了一碗汤药来，咕噜咕噜一饮而尽。

高颎深呼吸了十几次，才平静道：“就算有霸王之勇，但刀枪无眼，战场上多少名将毙命冷箭流矢下？就算你的预言中见到他无事，世事变幻无常，怎能将性命寄托在运气上？我必要把他鲁莽的性子拗正！”

李玄霸只能对老师拱手，让老师努力。

二哥在历史中的将帅天赋是天生的，基本没有名师教导。

现在有了名师教导，他相信也不会比以前更差。

如果改了喜欢亲自冲锋的习惯也是好事。

虽然天策上将的武力值很出众，战场上很耀眼，但确实就算没有二哥亲自当先锋先登，主将主帅稍稍稳一点也是能获胜的。

其实二哥自己都说他那冲阵方式很浪，其他人别学。

嗯，他自己都知道很浪，就是喜欢亲自上阵厮杀。

所以他常常在自己的营销号中以此“断定”唐太宗本性是个嗜血暴虐的杀人魔，赚得流量无数，十分开心。

高颎再次高血压快爆头，李玄霸也教不了了。

李玄霸告辞，再次请老师放宽心，别为了不肖弟子气出毛病来。

毕竟这个不肖弟子是一点都不知道反省的。

高颎气得把李玄霸的额头也戳出了红印子。

他发现李玄霸和李世民一样都让他气得胸口疼，不愧是双生子。

高颎冷静了几日，再教导李世民的时候，就着重给李世民介绍了那些历史中马前失蹄、中流矢、被乱兵堵住后路而亡的倒霉猛将。

战场瞬息万变，将帅要先保住自己，才能保住自己的军队不溃败；要先保证军队不溃败，能进退有据之后，才能去争取胜利。

显然，高颎的带兵方式是偏向稳重的一方。

高颎虽因为处于隋朝，所以知名度低了一些。但他跟随北周武帝和隋文帝两代明君南征北战，平定天下，抵御突厥并促使突厥分裂，是很有本事的战略家和军事家。

他的思想在这个时代不仅是顶尖的，甚至是领先时代的。所以李世民很尊重高颎，也很勤奋地向高颎学习。

但高颎教授的知识到了李世民那里，会被李世民用出什么模样，这连李玄霸都无法预言了。

毕竟，他哥这性子是真的闲不住。他是当了皇帝之后还会在禁苑里追兔子的人。

在二哥能带兵打仗的时候，李玄霸很难想象二哥老老实实当个正常的将帅。

没过几日，宇文弼给李世民也加练了。

李玄霸猜测，高先生估计是自己越想越气，越想血压越高，于是荼毒了宇文先生。

又过了几日，李玄霸从高颎和宇文弼府中人那里得知，两位先生正在到处找寻养生的方子，去编书的时间都少了一些，大大延长了休息的时间。

李玄霸单手捂嘴捏脸。不行，要笑出来了。

李世民疑惑：“阿玄，你这什么奇怪的表情？”

李玄霸忍着笑道：“老师被你气得够呛，大概是想要养生，活到你能当大将军那天，好盯着你别乱来。”

李世民失笑：“老师养生，难道不是为了亲眼见到我驰骋沙场、势压天下名将的姿态，好为我骄傲吗？”

李玄霸道：“我觉得还是盯着你别乱来的动机更强。”

李世民摇头：“不，肯定是为了亲眼见证我的伟业！”

两人谁也说不服谁，就将此事记在小本本上，等十几二十年后再拿出来“对质”。

李世民自信道：“我一定会赢。”

李玄霸摇头：“你别自信，等你到时候被老师骂得狗血淋头时，肯定会来找我哭。”

李世民冷哼：“我才不哭。”

李玄霸不信。

两人将此事也记录下来。

李世民还用朱笔着重标注，未来的我！就算被训了也不准哭！不要给现在的我丢脸！

李玄霸将小本本收好，将来必定不让二哥耍赖。

哦，对了，这也是很好的陪葬品啊。陪葬品又加一。

……

功课加重之后，李世民和李玄霸都觉得时间飞逝，每日重复听课、和友人讨论功课、完成功课，日子就这么悄然来到了七月。

香皂铺子和印刷铺子都很红火，再加上李玄霸十分慷慨地将香皂方子发了出来，很快就有其他店家模仿了起来。

不过李玄霸用的是草木灰加石灰水的版本，没有透露土碱和普通的草木灰的区别，所以其他香皂铺子的香皂质量都比不过李玄霸制作的香皂。

再加上李玄霸制作的香皂还有“贡品”的名誉加成，会员制度又戳中了贵族们想要与众不同的虚荣心，所以李玄霸和其合伙人的香皂永远都供不应求，上架就被抢空，预订永远爆满。

从贵族到民间富户，若是接待客人的时候能拿出有着李玄霸店铺印记的香皂，那都是能扬眉吐气的事。

其他店铺不是不想私下制作假冒伪劣的“李家铺子香皂”贩卖。

连御用品都有人敢仿制，何况区区唐国公府的香皂？

但一是香皂质量跟不上，一对比就很容易辨别真假；二是李玄霸从自己铺子卖出去的每一块香皂都有编号，卖给什么人都是有数的。他们难以假冒。

李玄霸所制造的香皂与香皂盒上的编号一模一样，拿着编号就能查是不是自家铺子出品。如果是预定的香皂，贵宾客户还有专门的编号，从编号就能看出贵宾客户已经从香皂铺子领了多少香皂回去。

贵族炫富的时候，又多了一项炫耀香皂盒子编号的娱乐——我编号的位数更大，说明我买得更多，不仅财力出众，也证明我在朝堂很有地位，能拿到更多的限额。

杨暕好脸面，明明杨广在萧皇后的劝说下，已经取消了杨暕的惩罚，让杨暕可以直接取用宫中贡品，他非要给钱从香皂铺子里买，就为了那个编号。

李玄霸道：“齐王殿下，别买了，我送你几块。”

杨暕愤怒道：“你是瞧不起我吗？”

李玄霸道：“怎么可能？是我们产能不够啊。齐王殿下你的权限过高，把别人的香皂都买走了。我们每日就只需要做你的生意，做完就关门，其他人就买不到限定款的香皂了。”

杨暕哈哈大笑，这才没有每日堵门抢货。

杨昭再次气得胖子捧心。

其他勋贵因杨暕的霸道怨声载道，杨昭四处帮弟弟收拾烂摊子，真是操碎了心。

杨广本来让杨暕暂时别做事，好好反省。

杨昭向父皇求助，请求赶紧给杨暕找点正事做。

杨广接到太子的千里加急家书，还以为大兴出了什么大事了。

见到太子居然在头疼齐王堵门抢香皂，杨广差点以为自己眼睛出了问题。

杨广拿着太子书信的手微微颤抖。这一位自诩千古明君雄主的帝王，第一次生出了心累的沧桑感。

他不由召见李渊，抖着书信道：“这是什么儿子，这是债啊！阿孩年幼时极其聪慧懂事，现在怎么会变成这样。”

李渊苦笑着拿出书信，道：“太子殿下给陛下送信的时候，很好心地为臣捎带了家书。陛下看看臣的家书。”

杨广接过李渊怀里的书信。那是李玄霸的告状信。

李玄霸说，高先生教二哥军略，二哥无论遇到什么敌人，都说“我带兵冲锋，把主将砍了完事”。高先生气得几欲晕厥，把二哥赶走后，连灌了两碗苦药才压住心火。

高先生不肯放弃，现在一边喝药一边教导二哥，他很担心高先生会被二哥气出病来。

宇文先生也是如此，只是程度比高先生稍稍轻一点。

杨广愕然：“大雄不是很懂事吗？他怎么能把高颎这样倨傲执拗的人气短寿了？”

李渊苦着脸道：“臣也不知道啊。臣离京的时候，大雄还是个很乖巧懂事的孩子。”

杨广和李渊面面相觑。

两人在身为父亲的不易中找到了共同话语。杨广对李渊亲近了不少。

杨广甚至对高颎都生出了些同情。

他厌恶忌惮高颎，这正是因为认可高颎的本事。

高颎肯将自己用兵的本事教授给李世民，这对李世民来说是天大的机遇。杨广都有些酸，埋怨高颎不肯将本事交给他的儿子。

虽然高颎如果敢教他儿子，杨广肯定会认为高颎图谋不轨杀了高颎。

但这天大的机遇，李世民就用来把高颎气吐血了。杨广觉得好同情……好扬眉吐气！

不愧是朕的表侄！干得好！

杨广私下对宇文述说，如果李大雄能把高颎气死，那他可就太开心了。

谄媚如宇文述都不知道怎么回答。

他真的很好奇。高颎被先帝免官时都泰然自若，让先帝为此十分不满。李二郎究竟是怎么把高颎气得四处寻医问药？

“估计被气得够呛的还有宇文弼。宇文弼也在四处求医问药，问的都是修心养性的养生药。”宇文述奉杨广的命令，一直监视着高颎和宇文弼。

杨广将李二郎干的好事告诉了宇文述。

宇文述沉默了许久，叹着气道：“若是臣，定把李二郎逐出师门。高颎和宇文弼的脾气比臣好。”

杨广大笑。

他专门派人送来自己从突厥得到的骏马雏鹰，送给李世民。

李世民得到赏赐后，疑惑道：“为什么只有我有赏赐，阿玄没有？”

李玄霸从心声道：【这是陛下对你差点气死高先生和宇文先生的赏赐。】

李世民：“……”

他使劲揉脸，不断说“我没有别胡说”，尴尬地想从地上挖个洞钻下去。

李玄霸十分欣慰。二哥终于尴尬了，他大概不会再给老师抬杠了。

二哥也真是倔强。就算心里不赞同，也不必说出来啊。他非得和老师争论，一顿歪理把老师气得够呛。

李玄霸实在是担心高颎和宇文弼。

他好不容易把两个老人家救下来，两个老人家不会被二哥气得短寿吧？所以他才无奈写信给李渊，让李渊好好劝劝二哥。

母亲已经劝过了，没用。或许父母一同劝说，能把二哥劝住。

谁知道，皇帝居然得知了这件事，还奖赏了二哥？

李玄霸背着手唉声叹气。

高先生和宇文先生有二哥这样的学生和杨广这样的上司，真是辛苦了。

之后李世民果然收敛了一些。

虽然高颎和宇文弼看得出来李世民仍旧不服气，但只要李世民不说出来，他们就当没看见。

经过这段时间的折磨，他们已经降低了预期。

教书就是磨，不是弟子被磨，就是老师被磨。高颎和宇文弼相信来日方长，李世民的性子还未定下来，可以改。

至少，你别老是亲自带兵冲锋啊！看看跟在你身后的猛将，他们都是摆设吗？！！

李世民悄悄对李玄霸道：“猛将？那都是保护我冲杀的护卫！”

说完，李世民弓步向前，做了一个持枪往前刺的动作。

李玄霸敷衍：“啊对对对。但你要记得告诉别人别学你，免得误人性命。”

可怜的李道玄，就是这么被你“坑”了。

李道玄是李世民的堂弟，人称“小李世民”。《隋唐演义》那小霸王“李玄霸”就是取的李玄霸的名字，和李道玄的原型。在清朝后因避讳康熙的名讳而改为“李元霸”。

不过像李道玄那样，主将在前方冲杀，副将默不作声地把后路断了，任由主将死在敌军中，最后导致大败，这副将因受李渊喜爱，所以还不受任何惩罚，也是正常人难以遇到的奇葩事。李道玄死得真冤。

怪不得李渊会落得一个“赏罚不明”的评价。

李世民道：“我知道。我是独一无二的！”

他继续弓步向前摆姿势，嘴里还喊着：“冲啊！杀啊！”

李玄霸懒得理睬二哥。

李世民只摆姿势不过瘾，从庭院里捡起两根树枝，一根树枝当马骑，一根树枝当马刀，在庭院里来回奔跑：“驾！众将士听令！随我杀敌立功！杀啊！”

李玄霸打了个哈欠，大声道：“赶紧下雨，让我哥安静下来吧。”
