Chapter 43: The Unfilial Disciple Li Shimin

Li Shimin’s graffiti assignment eventually fell into the hands of his three teachers.

Yu Shinan merely smiled and did not punish Li Shimin.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, seeing that Li Shimin possessed such high aspirations, increased his workload in military strategy.

Yuwen Bi very much wanted to teach Li Shimin personally, but when it came to military strategy, he was far inferior to Gao Jiong. Although he enjoyed arguing with Gao Jiong, he genuinely admired the man’s capabilities. Thus, Yuwen Bi took a step back, teaching Li Shimin only how to observe battlefield situations and the practical skills of fighting in the heat of battle.

Gao Jiong taught the "Commander" who directed from the rear, while Yuwen Bi taught the "General" who stood on the front lines.

Li Shimin felt both happy and depressed by this increased burden.

He knocked on Li Xuanba’s head as if it were a wooden fish: "It’s all your fault. Now I don't even have time to play."

Li Xuanba endured it for a while, but when he could endure no more, he jumped off the couch to go find Mother and tattle.

Li Shimin grabbed Li Xuanba’s arm, refusing to let him go complain.

The two brothers got into another fight.

When Lady Dou learned of this, she rubbed her forehead: "Is there ever a day they don't fight?"

Lady Wan, while embroidering a small cape, laughed: "I heard that the Second Young Master’s martial arts are already superior to youths four or five years his senior. Yet the Third Young Master manages to fight him to a draw every time. It seems the Third Young Master is also hiding his true strength."

Lady Dou burst into a fit of giggles, her frame trembling.

The surrounding servants also struggled to suppress their laughter.

Li Xuanba’s martial arts training had basically been interrupted; his combat drills were replaced with health-preserving exercises, and his martial arts teacher had become Physician Sun.

However, Gao Jiong believed that one could learn military strategy without being on the battlefield, and that Li Xuanba could learn it too, so he dragged Li Xuanba along for the extra lessons.

Yuwen Bi reasoned that to understand military strategy, one must understand the battlefield situation. Li Xuanba didn't have to learn the combat part, but he had to watch while Li Shimin learned. Thus, Li Xuanba was added to an extra auditing class.

Consequently, Li Xuanba’s burden also increased.

Li Shimin laughed loudly, "Ah Xuan, you deserve it!" He laughed so hard he lost a tooth, spitting out the tooth and some blood before continuing to laugh.

Li Xuanba was so angry he ground his teeth, and accidentally ground one off as well.

The two of them lost teeth in the exact same spot. When they returned home, they both had identical gaps in their mouths. Lady Dou laughed until her stomach ached.

Lady Wan was laughing so hard she was wiping away tears: "Even if you are twins, there is no need to lose teeth in the exact same place."

Li Shimin opened his mouth, full of gaps, and laughed carelessly: "Can't help it, that's just how twins are."

Li Xuanba didn't want to show his gap-filled mouth, nor did he want to lisp when he spoke, so he pressed his lips together and remained silent.

Seeing the completely different reactions of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Lady Dou and Lady Wan bent over with laughter once more.

Li Xuanba was so embarrassed he wished he could disappear. Li Shimin, however, giggled along with his mother and aunt, completely unable to understand his younger brother’s embarrassment.

After Gao Jiong had taught Li Shimin and Li Xuanba military strategy for a month, Li Xuanba’s grades were far ahead of his second brother, Li Shimin. Li Shimin had become the "rotten wood" that made Gao Jiong grit his teeth in frustration.

Gao Jiong: "First, assume a battlefield, assume the number of enemies, assume the terrain, the political situation between the two courts, blah blah... what would you do?"

Li Xuanba: "First, send spies to scout the enemy's situation, then see if a strategy of sowing discord can be used, then quietly requisition grain and troops under a different name, then launch a surprise raid from a thousand miles away, blah blah..."

Li Shimin: "Is it really that troublesome? Just give me ten thousand cavalry! I will lead the troops out myself! I’ll take out their commander!"

Gao Jiong: "???"

Li Xuanba speechlessly covered his face.

Li Shimin insisted on his own view.

Gao Jiong pressed his throbbing temple, where veins were bulging, and explained the military manuals to Li Shimin in detail.

Li Shimin spread his hands: "Military manuals are just the opinions of those who came before. Are they necessarily better than me? If I can win the fight, why go through all that trouble?"

Gao Jiong wanted to teach according to aptitude. He gave Li Shimin ten thousand troops, gave the enemy one hundred thousand, and asked Li Shimin to demonstrate how to charge and behead the enemy commander.

Li Shimin put his hands on his hips and tilted his head back: "All the cavalry will wear armor, charge into the enemy formation, and won't that just scatter them!"

Gao Jiong clutched his chest and took a deep breath: "Is that how you use heavy cavalry? No one charges heavy cavalry directly into an enemy formation! Cavalry is used to graze the enemy's flanks or fire at close range to force the enemy formation to deform! Even if the Overlord of Western Chu were reborn, he wouldn't charge cavalry directly into shielded infantry! If you charge ten thousand men into an enemy formation of one hundred thousand, that is walking straight into an ambush!"

Li Shimin said: "Then I'll just charge back out."

Gao Jiong could barely breathe. He kept poking Li Shimin’s partially bald little head with his finger, making it wobble: "Charge back out? There are people on all four sides! Even if you are on horseback, you can't see the weak points in the formation! The enemy has commanders too; do you think they’ll just let you charge out?"

Even with his head wobbling, Li Shimin insisted: "Maybe? Maybe I’m just better than them! I’ll charge out, then charge back in, then charge out, then charge back in—do it a few more times, and no matter how strong the enemy infantry’s fighting spirit is, it will be dismantled by me!"

Gao Jiong’s temple twitched painfully, and his body swayed.

Li Xuanba had been covering his mouth to laugh, but seeing this, he quickly supported Gao Jiong’s hand and helped his teacher soothe his breath: "Teacher, don't be angry. Second Brother is just like this. You’ve taught him everything you can; don't worry about what he does next."

Gao Jiong pointed at Li Shimin, gritting his teeth: "I refuse to believe I can't straighten you out!"

Li Xuanba sighed: "That... with Second Brother’s personality, it really can't be straightened out. Teacher, you should give up early."

Gao Jiong, who had almost been angered into a cerebral hemorrhage, caught a hint of something. He looked back and forth between Li Shimin and Li Xuanba with a suspicious gaze.

Li Shimin said: "Ah Xuan, can you foresee my future achievements? Hurry and tell Teacher, did I achieve it in the future!"

Li Xuanba said: "I cannot say. If I tell you that you achieved it, you will lose your composure and humility, and you might end up becoming a mediocre talent. If I say you didn't, you might go astray, become overly cautious, and lose your own brilliance. So, learn your skills well first, and think about the path you want to take yourself."

Li Shimin hugged his arms: "That’s true, knowing the future would be boring. And I’ll definitely be even more amazing than you foresee! Teacher, continue! I don't believe I can't win this argument against you!"

Gao Jiong poked Li Shimin’s forehead hard, leaving a red mark: "Who is debating military affairs with you? I have actual records of leading troops; what do you have? When you have actual records, then come debate military affairs with me!"

Li Shimin covered his forehead and said: "Then Teacher, you must take good care of your health. You must live until I become a Great General."

Gao Jiong: "???"

Li Xuanba covered his face. Although Second Brother’s words weren't wrong, why did they sound so off?

Sure enough, Gao Jiong sneered in anger, and Li Shimin was given extra homework.

You say you won't read the military manuals? If you want to summarize your own path, you must first exhaust the paths of the sages. Go copy the military manuals!

Gao Jiong was so angry he didn't want to see Li Shimin for the rest of the day. After assigning the homework, he chased Li Shimin away, telling him to go to Yuwen Bi’s place early to study.

Yuwen Bi liked to be a vanguard; let Li Shimin go roll around with that old scoundrel Yuwen Bi!

Li Xuanba was kept behind by Gao Jiong to continue receiving his mantle.

After Gao Jiong drank a bowl of calming medicine, the flush of anger on his face finally faded.

He said weakly: "Da De, give your teacher a straight answer. Is your second brother really going to be this... strange when he leads troops in the future? Always putting himself in danger, pinning his luck on destiny? Is it really impossible to change? A son of a wealthy family should not sit on a dangerous wall!"

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and sighed: "Second Brother does indeed always act as the vanguard when leading troops." Li Xuanba said no more.

Gao Jiong said: "Even if he must lead troops personally, this method of charging the formation..."

Li Xuanba sighed again: "But Second Brother really did it. He would lead troops into the enemy formation, then spot the weak point and lead his men out, then spot an opportunity and charge back in. Back and forth like that, his sleeves soaked in blood. When his arrows were gone, he used his sword; when his sword went dull, he used his bow to hack... He really did it."

Gao Jiong took another deep breath. He took out a pouch of herbs meant to clear the mind and sniffed it: "Does he not have any fierce generals under his command who can take the risk for him?!"

Li Xuanba thought about it and said: "He does, quite a few. For example, there is a man under his command named Yuchi Jingde. He said that when the two of them work together, they fear no army. So he would take Yuchi Jingde, and the two of them would go act as bait, luring thousands of enemy cavalry into an encirclement."

Gao Jiong almost blacked out and hurriedly bowed his head to inhale the fragrance: "Does no one under his command know how to stop him?!"

Li Xuanba spread his hands: "Second Brother didn't say he was going to fight; he just said he was taking people to scout the situation nearby. When Yuchi Jingde was forced to act as bait with him, he probably didn't expect that turn of events either. So, Teacher, don't be angry for Second Brother anymore; you’ll never finish being angry."

Gao Jiong ordered someone to bring another bowl of medicinal soup and gulped it down.

Gao Jiong took a dozen deep breaths before calmly saying: "Even with the courage of an Overlord, swords and spears have no eyes. How many famous generals on the battlefield have died from stray arrows? Even if your prophecy says he is safe, the world is ever-changing. How can one pin one's life on luck? I must straighten out his reckless nature!"

Li Xuanba could only bow to his teacher and wish him luck.

Second Brother’s talent for command in history was innate; he basically had no famous teachers.

Now that he had a famous teacher, he believed it wouldn't be any worse than before.

If he could change the habit of personally charging into battle, that would be a good thing.

Although the martial prowess of the Heavenly Strategy General was outstanding and dazzling on the battlefield, it was true that even without Second Brother acting as the vanguard, a commander could still win by being a little more steady.

Actually, Second Brother himself said that his way of charging formations was reckless and that others shouldn't learn it.

Well, he knew it was reckless, he just liked to personally charge into the fray.

That was why he often "concluded" in his own marketing posts that Emperor Taizong of Tang was a bloodthirsty, tyrannical murderer by nature, earning countless views and feeling very happy about it.

Gao Jiong’s blood pressure was about to explode again, and Li Xuanba couldn't teach him anymore.

Li Xuanba took his leave, once again asking his teacher to relax and not get sick over an unfilial disciple.

After all, this unfilial disciple didn't know how to reflect on himself at all.

Gao Jiong was so angry he poked Li Xuanba’s forehead, leaving a red mark as well.

He discovered that Li Xuanba and Li Shimin both made his chest ache; they were truly twins.

Gao Jiong calmed down for a few days. When he taught Li Shimin again, he focused on introducing those unlucky fierce generals in history who stumbled on the battlefield, were hit by stray arrows, or died after being blocked by chaotic troops.

The battlefield changes in an instant. A commander must first protect himself to keep his army from collapsing; he must first ensure the army does not collapse, and only after he can advance and retreat with order can he strive for victory.

Clearly, Gao Jiong’s way of leading troops leaned toward the steady side.

Although Gao Jiong had a lower profile because he lived in the Sui Dynasty, he followed two brilliant rulers, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou and Emperor Wen of Sui, in battles across the south and north, pacifying the world, resisting the Turks, and forcing the Turks to split. He was a very capable strategist and military expert.

His ideas were not only top-tier in this era but even ahead of his time. Therefore, Li Shimin respected Gao Jiong very much and studied diligently under him.

But what Gao Jiong’s knowledge would turn into once it reached Li Shimin, even Li Xuanba could not predict.

After all, his brother’s personality was truly restless. This was a man who would chase rabbits in the imperial gardens even after becoming Emperor.

When Second Brother was able to lead troops into battle, Li Xuanba found it hard to imagine him acting as a normal, steady commander.

A few days later, Yuwen Bi also added training for Li Shimin.

Li Xuanba guessed that Master Gao probably got angrier the more he thought about it, his blood pressure rising, so he poisoned Master Yuwen’s mind as well.

A few days later, Li Xuanba learned from the people in Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi’s households that the two masters were searching everywhere for health-preserving prescriptions, and even their time for compiling books had decreased, greatly extending their rest periods.

Li Xuanba covered his mouth and pinched his cheeks with one hand. No, he was about to laugh out loud.

Li Shimin was puzzled: "Ah Xuan, what is that strange expression?"

Li Xuanba suppressed his laughter: "Teacher was angered enough by you that he probably wants to preserve his health and live until the day you become a Great General, just to keep an eye on you so you don't do anything reckless."

Li Shimin chuckled: "Teacher preserving his health—isn't it so he can see with his own eyes my posture as I gallop across the battlefield and overwhelm the famous generals of the world, so he can be proud of me?"

Li Xuanba said: "I think the motive of keeping an eye on you so you don't do anything reckless is stronger."

Li Shimin shook his head: "No, it must be to witness my great achievements with his own eyes!"

Neither could convince the other, so they recorded this in their little notebook, planning to "confront" each other in ten or twenty years.

Li Shimin said confidently: "I will definitely win."

Li Xuanba shook his head: "Don't be so confident. When you are scolded until you're covered in dog’s blood by Teacher, you’ll definitely come to me crying."

Li Shimin snorted: "I won't cry."

Li Xuanba didn't believe him.

The two recorded this as well.

Li Shimin even used a red brush to highlight it: The future me! Even if you get scolded, you are not allowed to cry! Don't lose face for the current me!

Li Xuanba put the little notebook away, determined not to let Second Brother renege on this in the future.

Oh, right, this would also be a great burial object. Another burial object added.

...

After the workload increased, both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba felt time flying by. Every day was a repetition of attending lectures, discussing homework with friends, and completing assignments. Just like that, the days quietly arrived in July.

The soap shop and the printing shop were both very prosperous. Furthermore, because Li Xuanba had generously released the soap formula, other shops soon began to imitate them.

However, Li Xuanba used a version with wood ash and lime water, never revealing the difference between earth alkali and ordinary wood ash, so the quality of soap from other shops could not compare to the soap Li Xuanba made.

Coupled with the "tribute" reputation of Li Xuanba’s soap, and the membership system that poked at the vanity of nobles wanting to be unique, Li Xuanba and his partners’ soap was always in short supply. It was snatched up as soon as it hit the shelves, and pre-orders were always full.

From nobles to wealthy commoners, if one could bring out soap with the mark of Li Xuanba’s shop when entertaining guests, it was a matter of great pride.

It wasn't that other shops didn't want to secretly produce fake, inferior "Li Family Shop Soap" to sell.

People even dared to imitate imperial items, let alone soap from the mere Tang Duke’s mansion.

But first, the quality of the soap couldn't keep up, making it easy to distinguish the fake from the real. Second, every bar of soap sold from Li Xuanba’s shop had a serial number, and it was recorded who bought what. They couldn't fake it.

The serial number on the soap Li Xuanba made was identical to the one on the soap box. With the number, one could check if it was produced by their shop. If it was pre-ordered soap, VIP customers even had special numbers, and from the number, one could see how many bars of soap the VIP customer had already taken from the shop.

When nobles showed off their wealth, they had an extra form of entertainment—showing off the serial number on their soap box. "My number has more digits, which means I bought more. Not only is my financial power outstanding, but it also proves that I have status in the court and can get a larger quota."

Yang Jian was vain. Even though Yang Guang, under the persuasion of Empress Xiao, had already canceled Yang Jian’s punishment and allowed him to take tribute items from the palace directly, he insisted on paying money to buy them from the soap shop, just for that serial number.

Li Xuanba said: "Your Highness, Prince of Qi, don't buy anymore. I’ll give you a few bars."

Yang Jian said angrily: "Are you looking down on me?"

Li Xuanba said: "How could that be? It’s just that our production capacity isn't enough. Your Highness, your authority is too high; you’ve bought everyone else’s soap. We only need to do your business every day, and once we’re done, we close the doors. Others can't buy the limited edition soap."

Yang Jian laughed loudly, and only then did he stop blocking the door every day to snatch the goods.

Yang Zhao was so angry his fat chest hurt again.

Other nobles were full of complaints because of Yang Jian’s overbearing behavior. Yang Zhao ran around helping his younger brother clean up the mess, truly exhausting his heart.

Yang Guang had originally told Yang Jian not to do anything for a while and to reflect properly.

Yang Zhao sought help from his father, the Emperor, requesting that he quickly find some proper work for Yang Jian.

When Yang Guang received the urgent letter from the Crown Prince, he thought something major had happened in Daxing.

Seeing that the Crown Prince was actually having a headache because the Prince of Qi was blocking the door to snatch soap, Yang Guang almost thought his eyes were failing him.

The hand holding the Crown Prince’s letter trembled slightly. This emperor, who prided himself on being a brilliant ruler and a hero of the ages, felt the weariness of the world for the first time.

He couldn't help but summon Li Yuan, shaking the letter: "What kind of son is this? This is a debt! Ah Hai was extremely intelligent and sensible when he was young; how did he become like this now?"

Li Yuan smiled bitterly and took out a letter, saying: "When the Crown Prince sent the letter to Your Majesty, he kindly included a family letter for me. Your Majesty, please look at my family letter."

Yang Guang took the letter from Li Yuan’s arms. It was Li Xuanba’s letter of complaint.

Li Xuanba said that Master Gao was teaching Second Brother military strategy, and no matter what enemy he encountered, Second Brother would say, "I’ll lead the troops to charge and just behead the commander." Master Gao was so angry he almost fainted, and after chasing Second Brother away, he had to drink two bowls of bitter medicine to suppress his inner fire.

Master Gao refused to give up and was now drinking medicine while teaching Second Brother. He was very worried that Master Gao would be angered into illness by Second Brother.

Master Yuwen was the same, though the degree was slightly lighter than Master Gao’s.

Yang Guang was stunned: "Isn't Da Xiong very sensible? How could he anger someone as arrogant and stubborn as Gao Jiong to the point of shortening his life?"

Li Yuan said with a bitter face: "I don't know either. When I left the capital, Da Xiong was still a very well-behaved and sensible child."

Yang Guang and Li Yuan looked at each other.

Both found common ground in the hardships of being a father. Yang Guang felt much closer to Li Yuan.

Yang Guang even felt some sympathy for Gao Jiong.

He hated and feared Gao Jiong, which was precisely because he recognized Gao Jiong’s ability.

Gao Jiong being willing to teach his military skills to Li Shimin was a massive opportunity for Li Shimin. Yang Guang was even a bit jealous, blaming Gao Jiong for not being willing to give his skills to his own sons.

Although if Gao Jiong dared to teach his sons, Yang Guang would certainly think Gao Jiong was plotting something and kill him.

But this massive opportunity, Li Shimin used to anger Gao Jiong until he vomited blood. Yang Guang felt so sympathetic... and so vindicated!

Worthy of being my cousin! Well done!

Yang Guang privately said to Yuwen Shu that if Li Da Xiong could anger Gao Jiong to death, he would be very happy.

Even a sycophant like Yuwen Shu didn't know how to answer.

He was truly curious. Gao Jiong had been calm and composed even when the late emperor dismissed him from office, which had made the late emperor very dissatisfied. How exactly did Li Er-lang anger Gao Jiong to the point of seeking medical help everywhere?

"I reckon Yuwen Bi is also angered enough. Yuwen Bi is also seeking medical help everywhere, asking for health-preserving medicine for cultivating the mind." Yuwen Shu, following Yang Guang’s orders, had been monitoring Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi.

Yang Guang told Yuwen Shu about the good deeds Li Er-lang had done.

Yuwen Shu was silent for a long time, then sighed: "If it were me, I would definitely expel Li Er-lang from the school. Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi’s tempers are better than mine."

Yang Guang laughed loudly.

He specially sent someone to deliver a fine horse and a young eagle he had obtained from the Turks to Li Shimin.

After Li Shimin received the reward, he asked suspiciously: "Why is there only a reward for me, and none for Ah Xuan?"

Li Xuanba said from his heart: [This is the Emperor’s reward for you almost angering Master Gao and Master Yuwen to death.]

Li Shimin: "..."

He rubbed his face hard, constantly saying "I didn't, don't talk nonsense," embarrassed and wanting to dig a hole in the ground to hide in.

Li Xuanba was very gratified. Second Brother was finally embarrassed; he probably wouldn't argue with his teachers anymore.

Second Brother was truly stubborn. Even if he didn't agree in his heart, he didn't have to say it out loud. He insisted on arguing with his teachers, using all sorts of twisted logic to anger them.

Li Xuanba was truly worried about Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi.

He had finally saved the two old men; would they be angered into a shortened life by Second Brother? That was why he had helplessly written to Li Yuan, asking him to properly persuade Second Brother.

Mother had already persuaded him, but it was useless. Perhaps if both parents persuaded him together, they could stop Second Brother.

Who knew that the Emperor would actually learn of this and reward Second Brother?

Li Xuanba sighed with his hands behind his back.

Master Gao and Master Yuwen having a student like Second Brother and a boss like Yang Guang was truly hard on them.

Afterward, Li Shimin indeed restrained himself a bit.

Although Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi could tell that Li Shimin was still unconvinced, as long as Li Shimin didn't say it out loud, they pretended not to see it.

After this period of torture, they had lowered their expectations.

Teaching is a process of grinding; either the disciple is ground down, or the teacher is ground down. Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi believed that there was plenty of time ahead, and Li Shimin’s character hadn't been set yet; it could be changed.

At least, don't always personally lead the charge! Look at the fierce generals behind you; are they just decorations?!!

Li Shimin quietly said to Li Xuanba: "Fierce generals? They are all guards protecting me while I charge!"

After saying this, Li Shimin lunged forward, making a motion of thrusting a spear.

Li Xuanba perfunctorily said: "Ah, yes, yes, yes. But you must remember to tell others not to learn from you, lest you cost them their lives."

Poor Li Daoxuan was "pitied" by you just like that.

Li Daoxuan was Li Shimin’s cousin, known as "Little Li Shimin." The little overlord "Li Xuanba" in *The Romance of Sui and Tang* took his name from Li Xuanba and his prototype from Li Daoxuan. During the Qing Dynasty, it was changed to "Li Yuanba" to avoid the taboo of the Kangxi Emperor’s name.

However, like Li Daoxuan, where the commander charged in the front and the deputy commander silently cut off the retreat, letting the commander die in the enemy army, finally leading to a great defeat—and this deputy commander, because he was favored by Li Yuan, didn't receive any punishment—that was also a bizarre situation that normal people rarely encounter. Li Daoxuan died truly unjustly.

No wonder Li Yuan ended up with the reputation of being "unclear in rewards and punishments."

Li Shimin said: "I know. I am one of a kind!"

He continued to lunge forward and pose, shouting: "Charge! Kill!"

Li Xuanba couldn't be bothered to pay attention to his second brother.

Li Shimin wasn't satisfied with just posing. He picked up two branches from the courtyard, one to ride as a horse and one as a saber, running back and forth in the courtyard: "Giddy up! All soldiers, listen to my orders! Follow me to kill the enemy and achieve merit! Kill!"

Li Xuanba yawned and said loudly: "Hurry up and rain, let my brother be quiet."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第43章 不肖弟子李世民 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
他话音刚落，本就阴沉的天空响起了雷鸣。

夏雷阵阵，瓢泼大雨砸了李世民一头。

李世民丢下树枝，抹了一把脸上的雨水：“阿玄，你至于吗？”

李玄霸：“……这是碰巧。”

李世民仰天长叹，垂头丧气“鸣金收兵”。

……

李玄霸没想到，那一日雷阵雨后，大兴居然断断续续下了半月的雨，城里都出现了内涝。

他仔细想了想今年发生的大事，叹了口气。

大兴这场雨……居然还算小的。

《隋书·五行志》记载，“大业三年，河南大水，漂没三十余郡”。

《隋书》没有记载这场大水灾是大业三年何时发生，现在李玄霸估计，就是最近了。

果然，七月底八月初，“河南大水，漂没三十余郡”。

这么大的灾情很快就惊动了京城，灾民都来到了大兴城门下。

太子杨昭焦头烂额地调集钱粮安置京城外的灾民，快马加鞭请求杨广赶紧回来主持大局。

杨广并未回来。

长孙晟训斥突厥可汗不够尊敬大隋皇帝，居然让突厥人举国就役，砍掉牧草，平整土地，从榆林到蓟（后世北京），开了一条宽百步、长三千里的御道供杨广车队通行。

杨广重赏了长孙晟，正是志得意满的时候。他自然不会“功亏一篑”，在最得意的时候提前返回，让这次北巡不圆满。

灾害年年都有，义仓早就建好了。救灾有官吏负责，这点小事难道还需要皇帝亲自主持吗？那皇帝还要不要做大事了？

杨昭无奈给父皇写信，义仓没有粮啊！没有父皇的允许，儿不敢开官仓！

高颎和宇文弼总是会根据实事随时变更教学内容的。他们此时正好给李世民和李玄霸讲解了义仓制度。

隋文帝在民间建立义仓，让村人自己管理，丰年时往里面存粮，灾年时把存下的粮食取出来救灾。

结果当天灾发生，隋文帝要求义仓救灾时发现，百姓根本不往义仓里放粮食，义仓无法赈济灾民。

于是隋文帝震怒，认为百姓短视，应该得到教训，便要求官员不准开官仓赈济。

李玄霸知道这件事。

隋文帝是一个很矛盾的人，他节俭又吝啬，有积极赈灾救济百姓的时候，也会偶尔脑袋一抽觉得百姓活该就不赈济的时候。

李玄霸道：“先帝或许是真的把百姓当亲生子，所以见到百姓没有远见，便想给百姓一个教训，让百姓学会远见。”

李世民看向李玄霸：“阿玄，不要讽刺先帝。”

李玄霸正色道：“我是夸赞先帝圣明。”

李世民：“……哦。”

他挠挠头，道：“阿玄学算术的时候，曾让娘亲带着我俩去庄园上询问管事佃农的亩产，计算每年的支出结余。即使是丰年，大多佃农到了粮食刚结穗还未成熟的时候，头一年的粮食就已经吃光了，需要向庄子借贷粮食，丰收后再偿还。”

此次授课是高颎和宇文弼联合教授，他们二人坐在对面的坐榻上，温和地看着李世民，用眼神鼓励李世民继续说。

李世民又挠了挠头，道：“天灾之后，需要赈济的多是和我家佃农一样家境的百姓吧？他们是不可能有余粮存入义仓的；而每年的粮食吃不完的富户，他们遇到天灾也能吃自己存的粮食，应该用不上义仓，所以或许不会将余粮存入义仓的。”

高颎问道：“你是认为先帝的赈济政策不对吗？”

李世民道：“我不敢言先帝的不是。但我想先帝说得是对的，百姓并无远见。所以君王和朝堂诸公才要替百姓看到更远的地方。赈济应该是有远见的君王和朝堂诸公负责的事。”

高颎沉默不语。

宇文弼叹了口气，眼眶微红，也只叹气不说话。

李世民垂着脑袋，不知道为何，胸口有些闷闷的。

他上次这样的时候，还是在龙舟上看到有人把吃不完的食物埋起来的时候。

李世民问道：“老师，当今陛下难道……难道也不会开仓赈灾吗？”

高颎和宇文弼不语。

李世民看向李玄霸。

李玄霸道：“京中诸位贵人肯定会为灾民建佛寺祈福，”

李世民松了口气，道：“那真是太好了。”

李玄霸问道：“二哥，这真的太好了吗？建了佛寺，那些灾民就有粮吃，有房住，有地耕了吗？”

李世民愣住。

李玄霸道：“我一直不明白，为何诸公表示对百姓怜惜的时候，不肯直接去救助百姓，而是修筑富丽堂皇的寺庙，供养衣着华丽的僧尼日日诵经。百姓真的会为此感激涕零，知道有人为他们诵经之后，连肚子都不会饿了吗？”

李玄霸这问题，后世任何一个人都能回答。

但这时候，无论是年老的高颎宇文弼，还是年幼的未来太宗皇帝李世民，他们都一时难以回答李玄霸的问题。就像是李玄霸抛出的问题有多么惊世骇俗似的。

李玄霸知道他们回答不出来。

就连后世公认能勉强让百姓进入自己视线的唐太宗李世民，在祈福的时候也是建寺庙，释放罪人。

为百姓祈福，钱粮进了寺庙；向百姓表达自己的仁善，把罪有应得的罪犯特赦回社会扰乱治安。

唐太宗也是封建帝王，也有封建帝王的局限性。不然他这个营销号靠什么吃饭？靠复读“太宗改史”吗？

高颎和宇文弼正欲说什么，屋内响起了呜咽声。

高颎、宇文弼和李玄霸赶紧看向李世民。

李世民先是呜咽，然后捂着双眼大哭。

“哥？你哭什么？”李玄霸吓了一跳，赶紧递帕子给二哥擦眼泪。

李世民哭着道：“我听到阿玄所说的话，想着百姓无以为食，贵人们却将钱财捐给寺庙还自以为对百姓好，就忍不住心酸难过，止不住眼泪。呜呜呜呜，为何会如此？为何阿玄说起此事前，我居然从未意识到这样不对，也想着要多捐寺庙？阿玄，这次我们和娘亲说，我们不捐寺庙好不好？”

李玄霸无奈。不愧是看《史书》都能看哭的二哥，真是感情太充沛了。

他严肃道：“不好！”

李世民吸着鼻子道：“为何？”

高颎板着脸道：“所有勋贵都捐寺庙，你们不捐，是想说所有勋贵不是吗？陛下不赈济，你们唐国公府私下赈济，是想替陛下招揽民心吗？”

宇文弼叹着气摇头：“你有这个心就好了。”

李世民哭道：“那我们什么都不做吗？”

高颎道：“我会向陛下谏言，请求他开官仓！”

宇文弼道：“我也会！大雄，大德，你们还小，现在这些事不是你们的责任。我和高公虽老，但还未死，现在的朝堂是我们的责任。”

李玄霸大惊失色：“不可！如果高先生和宇文先生进谏，陛下肯定会记恨先生！”

李世民使劲擦了一下眼泪，把鼻涕眼泪抹得满脸都是。

他立刻叩首道：“请先生不要去。是我一时情急，这也并非先生的责任啊。请先生首先保重自己。”

高颎和宇文弼却摇头。

李玄霸咬了一下牙，道：“先生，陛下不仅不会赈灾，还会征发百姓修建长城。劝不住的！”

高颎和宇文弼猛地站起来。

高颎把李玄霸抱起来，道：“什么？修什么？”

李玄霸道：“修长城。他得知河南多灾民后，就会征发百姓修长城。”

李世民呆呆道：“以工代赈，是不是百姓就有活路了？”

李玄霸：“……嗯，对。”

李世民松了一口气，对高颎和宇文弼道：“老师，你们可以放心了！陛下并非无动于衷！”

高颎和宇文弼却心一沉。

他们想起了李玄霸之前的谶纬——他们将因“诽谤朝政”死在今年。

他们是去阻止了陛下修长城了吗？

高颎和宇文弼满心悲怆，却无法言语。

他们送走了李世民和李玄霸，相对呆坐。

“高公，我们真的要避开这个死劫吗？”

“不避开又如何？在大德的谶纬中，陛下不仅无动于衷，还杀了进谏的我们。”

“可什么都不做，我心里难受啊！”

高颎幽幽叹息：“谁心里不难受？”

宇文弼垂泪。

两人都是勋贵子弟，自幼锦衣玉食。他们心里其实也没有多少百姓，不如李玄霸和李世民那样是真心诚意为百姓难过。

他们是为大隋难过。

遇灾不赈济，还征发百姓去修长城，这不是取死吗？

百姓若活不下去，是一定会生乱的。这天下刚平定，一旦百姓生乱，有野心的人肯定会趁机而起。

所以，如今如烈火烹油的大隋，才只有不到二十年的国运了吗？

他们明明做好了大隋会灭亡的心理准备，但看着大隋一步一步往深渊里走，想要什么都不做，真的太艰难了。
chunks.englishText:
No sooner had he finished speaking than thunder rumbled across the already overcast sky.

A sudden summer downpour descended, drenching Li Shimin from head to toe.

Li Shimin dropped his branch and wiped the rainwater from his face. "A-Xuan, was that really necessary?"

Li Xuanba: "……That was a coincidence."

Li Shimin looked up at the sky and let out a long, dejected sigh, "sounding the retreat."

……

Li Xuanba had not expected that after that day’s thunderstorm, Daxing would experience intermittent rain for half a month, leading to waterlogging within the city.

He carefully recalled the major events of the year and sighed.

This rain in Daxing… was actually considered minor.

The *Book of Sui: Treatise on the Five Elements* recorded, "In the third year of Daye, a great flood in Henan submerged over thirty commanderies."

The *Book of Sui* did not record exactly when during the third year of Daye this great flood occurred, but Li Xuanba now estimated it must be happening right about now.

Sure enough, between late July and early August, "a great flood in Henan submerged over thirty commanderies."

Such a massive disaster soon alarmed the capital, and refugees began to gather at the gates of Daxing.

Crown Prince Yang Zhao was frantic, scrambling to mobilize funds and grain to settle the refugees outside the capital, while sending urgent couriers to beg Yang Guang to return immediately to take charge of the situation.

Yang Guang did not return.

Zhangsun Sheng had rebuked the Tujue Khan for not showing enough respect to the Emperor of the Great Sui, actually compelling the Tujue people to mobilize their entire nation to cut grass and level the earth, carving out an imperial road one hundred paces wide and three thousand *li* long from Yulin to Ji (modern-day Beijing) for Yang Guang’s carriage procession.

Yang Guang had rewarded Zhangsun Sheng handsomely and was currently riding the crest of his vanity. Naturally, he would not "fall short of success for lack of a final effort" by returning early at the height of his triumph, which would make this northern tour feel incomplete.

Disasters happened every year, and the righteous granaries had long been established. Disaster relief was handled by local officials; did such a trivial matter really require the Emperor to preside over it personally? If so, would the Emperor ever have time for great affairs?

Yang Zhao had no choice but to write to his Imperial Father, stating that the righteous granaries had no grain! Without his Father’s permission, he dared not open the official granaries!

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi always adjusted their teaching materials according to current events. At this moment, they happened to be explaining the righteous granary system to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Emperor Wen of Sui had established these granaries among the people, allowing villagers to manage them themselves—storing grain during bountiful years and withdrawing it to provide relief during years of famine.

However, when natural disasters struck and Emperor Wen demanded that the righteous granaries be used for relief, he discovered that the commoners had never actually put any grain into them, rendering the granaries useless for disaster relief.

Consequently, Emperor Wen was furious. Believing the commoners were shortsighted and needed a lesson, he forbade officials from opening the official granaries to provide relief.

Li Xuanba knew of this incident.

Emperor Wen was a deeply contradictory man; he was frugal and stingy, capable of being proactive in disaster relief, yet occasionally prone to bouts of stubbornness where he felt the people deserved their suffering and refused to help.

Li Xuanba said, "Perhaps the late Emperor truly viewed the people as his own children, so when he saw they lacked foresight, he wanted to teach them a lesson so they would learn to look ahead."

Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba: "A-Xuan, do not mock the late Emperor."

Li Xuanba replied solemnly, "I am praising the late Emperor’s sagacity."

Li Shimin: "……Oh."

He scratched his head and said, "When A-Xuan was learning arithmetic, he once had Mother take us to the manor to ask the stewards about the yield per *mu* and calculate the annual balance. Even in a bountiful year, most tenant farmers would have exhausted the previous year's grain by the time the new crops were just forming ears and not yet ripe. They would have to borrow grain from the manor and repay it after the harvest."

This lesson was being taught jointly by Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi. They sat on the mat opposite, watching Li Shimin gently, their eyes encouraging him to continue.

Li Shimin scratched his head again. "After a natural disaster, the people needing relief are mostly those in the same situation as our manor’s tenants, right? They couldn't possibly have surplus grain to store in the righteous granaries. And the wealthy households who have grain left over every year can eat their own stores when disaster strikes; they shouldn't need the righteous granaries, so they probably wouldn't store their surplus there either."

Gao Jiong asked, "Are you suggesting the late Emperor’s relief policy was wrong?"

Li Shimin said, "I dare not speak ill of the late Emperor. But I think the late Emperor was right—the people lack foresight. That is precisely why the monarch and the lords of the court must see further than the people. Disaster relief should be the responsibility of a far-sighted monarch and the lords of the court."

Gao Jiong remained silent.

Yuwen Bi sighed, his eyes reddening, but he too only sighed and said nothing.

Li Shimin hung his head, feeling a strange tightness in his chest.

The last time he felt this way was on the dragon boat, when he saw people burying food they couldn't finish.

Li Shimin asked, "Teacher, could it be that the current Emperor… will also not open the granaries for disaster relief?"

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi did not answer.

Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba said, "The nobles in the capital will surely build Buddhist temples to pray for the refugees."

Li Shimin breathed a sigh of relief. "That is truly wonderful."

Li Xuanba asked, "Second Brother, is it really wonderful? Once the temples are built, will those refugees have grain to eat, houses to live in, and land to till?"

Li Shimin froze.

Li Xuanba continued, "I have never understood why, when the lords express pity for the people, they refuse to go directly to help them, but instead build magnificent temples to support gorgeously dressed monks and nuns who chant scriptures all day. Will the people truly be moved to tears of gratitude, knowing that someone is chanting for them, and find that their hunger has vanished?"

Li Xuanba’s question was one that anyone from a later age could answer.

But at this moment, neither the elderly Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, nor the young future Emperor Taizong, Li Shimin, could answer Li Xuanba’s question. It was as if the question he had posed was something truly shocking.

Li Xuanba knew they couldn't answer.

Even Li Shimin, the Tang Taizong recognized by later generations as someone who at least managed to keep the people in his line of sight, still built temples and pardoned criminals when praying for blessings.

Praying for the people meant money and grain went into the temples; expressing benevolence meant pardoning criminals who deserved their punishment, releasing them back into society to disrupt the peace.

Tang Taizong was also a feudal monarch, bound by the limitations of a feudal monarch. Otherwise, what would his "marketing team" have lived on? Repeating "Taizong revised history"?

Just as Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were about to say something, a sobbing sound filled the room.

Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Li Xuanba quickly looked at Li Shimin.

Li Shimin first whimpered, then covered his eyes and burst into tears.

"Brother? Why are you crying?" Li Xuanba was startled and quickly handed a handkerchief to his Second Brother to wipe his tears.

Li Shimin sobbed, "I heard what A-Xuan said, and thinking of the people with nothing to eat while the nobles donate money to temples and think they are doing good for the people, I couldn't help but feel heartbroken and sad. I can't stop my tears. Wuwuwu, why is it like this? Why, before A-Xuan brought this up, did I never realize this was wrong, and even thought about donating more to temples? A-Xuan, let’s tell Mother this time that we won't donate to the temples, okay?"

Li Xuanba felt helpless. As expected of the Second Brother who could cry while reading the *History Books*, his emotions were truly too abundant.

He said sternly, "No!"

Li Shimin sniffled. "Why?"

Gao Jiong said with a straight face, "All the nobles are donating to temples. If you don't, are you trying to say all the nobles are wrong? If the Emperor doesn't provide relief, and your Duke of Tang’s mansion provides private relief, are you trying to win the hearts of the people away from the Emperor?"

Yuwen Bi shook his head with a sigh, "It is good that you have the heart for it."

Li Shimin cried, "Then are we to do nothing?"

Gao Jiong said, "I will submit a remonstrance to the Emperor, requesting him to open the official granaries!"

Yuwen Bi said, "I will too! Da Xiong, Da De, you are still young; these matters are not your responsibility. Though Gao Gong and I are old, we are not yet dead. The current court is our responsibility."

Li Xuanba was horrified. "No! If Master Gao and Master Yuwen submit a remonstrance, the Emperor will surely harbor a grudge against you!"

Li Shimin wiped his tears vigorously, smearing snot and tears all over his face.

He immediately kowtowed, "Please, Masters, do not go. It was my moment of rashness; this is not your responsibility. Please, Masters, look after yourselves first."

But Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi shook their heads.

Li Xuanba gritted his teeth and said, "Masters, the Emperor will not only refuse to provide disaster relief, he will also conscript the people to build the Great Wall. You cannot stop him!"

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi stood up abruptly.

Gao Jiong picked up Li Xuanba and asked, "What? Build what?"

Li Xuanba said, "Build the Great Wall. Once he learns of the many refugees in Henan, he will conscript the people to build the Great Wall."

Li Shimin said blankly, "If he uses labor as a form of relief, won't the people have a way to survive?"

Li Xuanba: "……Yes, that’s right."

Li Shimin breathed a sigh of relief and said to Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, "Teachers, you can rest easy! The Emperor is not indifferent!"

But Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi’s hearts sank.

They remembered Li Xuanba’s previous prophecy—that they would die this year for "slandering the government."

Had they gone to stop the Emperor from building the Great Wall?

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were filled with sorrow, yet they could not speak.

They saw Li Shimin and Li Xuanba off and sat staring at each other in silence.

"Gao Gong, must we really avoid this death trap?"

"And if we don't avoid it, what then? In Da De’s prophecy, the Emperor was not only indifferent, he killed us for remonstrating."

"But if I do nothing, my heart aches!"

Gao Jiong sighed gloomily, "Whose heart does not ache?"

Yuwen Bi shed tears.

Both were sons of noble families, having lived in luxury since childhood. In truth, they did not care much for the common people; they were not like Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, who were genuinely heartbroken for them.

They were heartbroken for the Great Sui.

To encounter a disaster and provide no relief, but instead conscript the people to build the Great Wall—was this not courting death?

If the people could not survive, they would surely revolt. The world had only just been pacified; once the people rose in rebellion, those with ambition would certainly seize the opportunity.

So, was the Great Sui, now like oil poured on a raging fire, destined to have less than twenty years of national fortune left?

They had clearly prepared themselves for the fall of the Great Sui, but watching it walk step by step into the abyss, wanting to do nothing was truly too difficult.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第44章 友人组初次聚谋 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第44章 友人组初次聚谋

=

李世民回家之后， 抱着双膝不说话。

李玄霸看了一会儿书，见二哥还在自闭，放下书叹气道：“哥， 你我还小， 连朝中诸公都解决不了的事， 你操什么心？”

李世民跟着叹了一口气，呈现大字躺在床榻上：“阿玄，你说老师会劝谏吗？”

李玄霸道：“劝谏和不劝谏的可能性一半一半吧。”

李世民翻白眼：“你是在说废话吗？”

李玄霸道：“确实是废话。我们左右不了老师的选择。”

他已经做出努力了。如果连大隋十几年后就灭亡， 二十年后盛世王朝到来这样大的诱惑都不能阻止老师们走上赴死的路，他也无可奈何。

李世民偏头看着李玄霸：“阿玄，你好冷漠。那可是老师啊。”

李玄霸道：“那我该怎么做， 和你一起抱头痛哭？”

李世民咂巴了下嘴，唉声叹气：“你还是别哭了， 你哭了没人劝我别哭， 给我递纸。”

李玄霸黑线。

李世民继续大字躺着自闭。

李玄霸不理睬他，继续看书。

待窗外的夕阳已经落下了一半，剩下的一半夕阳光辉黯淡得像半枚咸蛋黄的时候，李玄霸才收起书，让人把烛火点亮。

“你还要继续躺着？”李玄霸问道。

李世民揉了揉肚子， 翻身起来：“饿了，走， 去厨房偷烤鸡吃。”

李玄霸道：“柜子里有肉干。”

李世民穿好鞋子，拖着李玄霸就跑：“能吃烤鸡，谁要吃肉干？”

李玄霸跌跌撞撞跟上。

他们到了厨房时， 厨子见他二人来了， 笑着取下在没熄火的灶台上挂着的烤鸡， 给两人切好。

李玄霸只要了一只鸡腿。

李世民抱着一盆鸡肉， 双手左右开弓啃鸡肉。李玄霸慢吞吞吃完一只鸡腿时，李世民已经把盆里的烤鸡解决了一半。

李玄霸擦了擦嘴和手，要了一碗没加糖的温牛奶小口抿着。

李世民也要了一大碗加糖的温牛奶，改成一手拿鸡肉一手端碗豪饮。

李玄霸喝完牛奶，伸了个懒腰，活动了一下脖子和胳膊。

李世民打了个一个响亮的饱嗝：“饱了！”

李玄霸谢过为他们留夜宵的厨子，摸出了一把铜钱赏赐给厨房里的人。

厨子忙说这是夫人留的。

但李玄霸还是坚持给了。厨房里的人都眉开眼笑，殷勤地把两位小郎君送走。

李世民一边揉着吃撑了的肚子，一边叹气道：“吃饱了，可以继续愁了。”

李玄霸分外无语。

李世民搭着李玄霸的肩膀：“阿玄！难道你就不愁吗？你就不想想怎么帮老师吗？”

李玄霸道：“我不愁。老师肯定比我们两个小孩厉害，他们很清楚自己要做什么，做了之后有什么后果。我们才八岁，老师都六十多岁了。”

李世民按住李玄霸的肩膀，把李玄霸晃来晃去：“阿玄，我们总不能什么都不做吧？哪怕在城外搭个棚子施粥……”

刚吃了东西，差点被晃吐的李玄霸伸脚踹二哥的小腿。

李世民就像是兔子一样敏捷侧跳，躲过了李玄霸的袭击。

李玄霸道：“施粥的事不该由我们先做。不过我们可以招工。香皂工坊赚了不少钱，我想把业务扩展一些，推出更多的商品。如果灾民中有会木工活的人，还可以招进印刷工坊。”

李玄霸所谓的招工，就是大量买进奴仆。

此时蓄奴合法。每当灾年，都是豪强大量买入奴仆的好时机。

灾民们也会很积极地自卖其身。只要他们被人买走，基本上就有活路了。

李玄霸虽然在水灾发生后才想起今年有大灾，但华夏这片大地，每年都有大大小小的自然灾害。隋朝是出了名的只屯粮不救灾，他赚钱就是为了买壮仆组建一支秘密私人军队，所以前期计划已经准备好了。

李世民跟在李玄霸后面走了几步，加快脚步跑到了李玄霸身边：“阿玄，我们买下的灾民就能活下去了吗？”

李玄霸：“……”二哥还挺通透，“招工”这个掩饰没骗到他。

李玄霸答非所问道：“我本来只打算买壮仆，你都这么说了，那我一家一户地买。”

李世民笑道：“我就知道阿玄一定会有办法。落单的妇人和孩童……”

李玄霸道：“只要能干活，都算壮仆。”

李世民赞同道：“阿玄说得对！如果钱不够，就把耶耶送给我的小马驹卖掉。”

李玄霸看向二哥：“你确定？”

李世民面露不舍，但语气很果决：“我也要帮忙！再说了，我还有陛下送的更好的小马驹呢。陛下送的小马驹是御赐品，不能卖。”

“扑哧。”李玄霸笑道，“行，我们把你的小马驹卖了。”

李玄霸没有开玩笑。既然二哥有这个想法，愿意付出这样的代价，他就要支持。

第二日，李世民拖着睡得半醒的李玄霸去找窦夫人，将他们对捐佛寺的思考告诉母亲。

“娘亲，我们给佛寺少捐点，敷衍敷衍就行。”李世民爬到窦夫人怀里，抱着母亲的脖子撒娇，“我们留下钱来买奴仆吧。不能白给灾民施粥，我们可以买下来！”

窦夫人看向一旁脑袋一点一点打瞌睡的李玄霸，问道：“大德也是这么想吗？”

李玄霸打了好几个哈欠，才有气无力道：“如果唐国公府需要人手，可以采买一些。采买太多也会引人怀疑。”

窦夫人点头：“大德知道就好。你需要多少奴仆，自己去采买。娘亲知道如何能给他们施粥，佛寺也不是完全一无是处。”

李世民不满道：“我知道佛寺也会施粥，但我们给佛寺的钱，他们至少会吞掉一半。”

窦夫人点了点李世民的脑袋：“总比什么都没有好。这件事交给娘亲。”

李世民道：“好吧。”

万氏微笑着叹气：“你们二人才多点大？这些事还轮不到你们烦恼。”

李世民道：“阿玄也这么说，但什么都不做才会烦恼，只要做了力所能及的事，我就不会烦恼了！”

李世民告别母亲和阿姨，拖着还在打瞌睡的李玄霸出门巡视建立了香皂工坊的庄子，与管事商议买进灾民的事。

万氏道：“二郎真是精力充沛，好像永远闲不下来。”

窦夫人无奈道：“可怜大德了，总是被大雄拖着到处跑。”

万氏道：“多跑跑对身体才好。若是小五再大几岁，我定叮嘱小五，也要跟着二郎多跑跑。”

窦夫人失笑：“小五也已经很活泼了。”

万氏捏着帕子遮掩住嘴角，娇笑道：“还不够活泼，还得多向两位兄长学习。”

窦夫人道：“五郎真的学成了二郎那模样，希望你不后悔。”

万氏怎么可能后悔？看看二郎和三郎，如此年幼就在思考如何帮助灾民。不说这片善心，就说这决策和行动的能力，就让她赞叹不已。

若是小五跟着两位兄长，一定有很多机会做事。

她不担心小五成为兄长的小跟班小帮手，她就怕没人“使唤”自家小五。

窦夫人乐于见兄弟和睦，便默许了万氏的暗示请求。

她又想起李元吉，脑袋有些疼。

李元吉……还是自己亲自带吧。二郎和三郎可管不住这个弟弟。

……

购买奴仆的事，不需要李世民和李玄霸亲力亲为，只需要和管事的说一声即可。

在哪里买奴仆，如何甄选合适的奴仆……管事们都很熟练，不需要李世民和李玄霸班门弄斧。

如果这点小事都要主人家亲自去做，唐国公府的管事就太闲了。

管事一听李世民和李玄霸说要“一家一户的买”“带小孩的寡妇如果能做事也可以买”，就知道两位小主人是想做善事，明白如何做。

吩咐完管事后，李世民又拖着李玄霸去找自己的小伙伴们聚会。

他们两个小孩想不出帮助老师的办法，但这不是还有三位有才华的朋友吗？五个人总能想的比两个人更周全。

听了李世民的请求后，房乔和杜如晦复杂的心情都表现在了脸上。

长孙无忌十分干脆地摊手：“别指望我，我什么都想不出来。”

跟着四位学霸朋友混久了，长孙无忌已经放弃了无谓的自尊心，学会了放弃。

李世民道：“不指望你，你也要想一想。无论想的对不对，总要想一想。”

长孙无忌无奈：“是，是，我努力。”

他抱着手臂，垂头苦思。

李世民对房乔和杜如晦拱手：“房兄和杜兄可有高见？”

房乔犹豫了一会儿。

他知道皇帝忌惮高颎和宇文弼。特别是高颎原本站在废太子身边，做什么都会让皇帝往坏的方面想。出于本心，他不愿意掺和进高颎、宇文弼的事。

但李世民关于灾民的描述触动了他，让他觉得此事如果不说点什么，于心有愧。

杜如晦看向房乔，道：“你犹豫什么？你只管出主意，难道李二李三还会出卖你？”

房乔干咳一声，道：“我当然知道不会。我只是在想该如何做。”

杜如晦道：“其实我们想好了该如何做，高公和宇文公也不一定会采纳。高公和宇文公在朝堂纵横几十年，怎会把我们几个无名晚辈的意见放在眼里？”

李世民拍着胸脯道：“你们只管出主意，后面的交给我们。成与不成，至少要先去做。对吧，阿玄？”

李玄霸无力道：“是，对。”

杜如晦笑道：“李三都这么说了，那我就不藏拙了。”

李玄霸嘴角扯了扯。杜如晦身为世家子弟，老爱把世家的习惯带出来，比如把姓氏加排行当昵称来喊。

其他人好歹在后面加个“郎”或者“郎君”，杜如晦就“李二李三”地喊。

李玄霸觉得被叫“李三”很奇怪，但除了他之外没人觉得奇怪，就像是其他人认为“大雄”“大德”这两个字很好一样。

李玄霸懒得辩驳，便忍了。

虽然每次听着都不习惯，说不定听个几年，他自我介绍也是“李三”了。反正“李三”和“李大德”都充满着乡土气息。

杜如晦想了想，道：“这件事还是得从太子入手。太子是想保下高公和宇文公的，也是想赈济灾民的。”

房乔开口道：“太子仁善孝顺，但仁善孝顺过度就是软弱。若皇帝决定的事，他不敢质疑。”

长孙无忌吓得差点咬住舌头。

什么软弱？房玄龄你胆子太大了，这也敢说！

房乔继续道：“太子只能帮忙递话，最终还是得想着如何讨好皇帝。皇帝不喜劝谏，只爱听好话。无论赈济此事是否能成，若想保住高公和宇文公，劝谏在皇帝耳中，必须是歌功颂德的好话，而不是指责。”

长孙无忌脸色煞白。

不、不是吧？你还是我认识的那位腼腆谨慎不善交际的房玄龄吗？你居然连皇帝都骂！

杜如晦赞同道：“以庆祝陛下北巡降服突厥为名，请求陛下开仓赈济灾民，以举天同庆如何？”

房乔道：“可以一试。至少陛下不会认为这是在指责他。大雄大德，你们认为如何？”

李世民道：“我看好。阿玄，你说呢？”

李玄霸的表情显得有些漠然：“你们忽略了一件事。在我们这位陛下眼中，举天同庆时百姓没资格跟着庆祝。以房兄之策进谏，可能皇帝不会生气，但也绝不会赈灾。”

房乔道：“至少能保住高公和宇文公。”

李玄霸摇头：“老师比我更了解皇帝。他们既然知道这是做无用功，就不会如此进谏。”

李世民道：“我倒觉得老师都不如你了解陛下。阿玄，你也帮忙想想吧，无论成不成，好歹试试。”

李玄霸叹气：“行，我试试。房兄和杜兄所说，以歌功颂德的方式请求皇帝赈济灾民或许不行，如果以对比先帝的方式，或许有一二成成功的几率。”

李世民问道：“如何对比？”

李玄霸道：“先帝因义仓存粮不足而不肯赈济灾民，陛下却慷慨地开官仓赈济灾民，说明大隋在陛下的手中更加繁盛，赈济灾民这点损失对陛下治下的官仓存粮算不上什么。”

房乔嘴角勾起嘲讽的幅度：“且陛下这样做，对比先帝，更显得仁慈？”

李玄霸摇头：“我们这位陛下是真的一点都不在乎仁慈的名声。应该这么说，陛下北巡结束时，突厥可汗会率领突厥贵族同行。灾民聚集在京城和东京附近，有碍京城和东京的整洁。但如果出兵驱赶，可能会闹出更大的乱子，不如给些粮食打发了。”

杜如晦皱眉：“你这话也太……”他想了许久，居然想不出用什么词来形容李玄霸所说的话。

长孙无忌反复做出想捂住耳朵，舍不得捂住耳朵的动作。

他认为这些话真不该听。但和友人们对陛下指指点点，真的好刺激！

李玄霸道：“先帝只是因为官仓粮食不够才不赈济灾民。陛下在突厥可汗面前赈济灾民，就是向突厥可汗宣扬大隋的粮食储备比先帝时期更加充足。粮草充足则兵马强壮，突厥人才会更加惧怕陛下。”

李世民疑惑道：“陛下不在乎百姓死活，却在乎突厥人怎么想？”

李玄霸淡淡道：“嗯。你换成西域人也行。陛下只是对已经到手的不在乎，只看着没得到的那部分而已。大隋的百姓已经臣服于他，所以他已经不在意了。他更在意还未臣服于他的人的想法。”

隋炀帝此举不是崇洋媚外。

隋炀帝其实看不起西域和突厥。他在西域人和突厥人面前讲排场，只是因为他需要让还没有臣服于他的人面前展示自己的财富、权势、威望，好让他们臣服自己。

李世民道：“我总觉得你的话很奇怪，怎么也想不明白。不过既然阿玄你都这么说了，把你的计谋也记下。房兄和杜兄的建议也记下，一同告诉老师。”

李玄霸问道：“只需要告诉老师就行了吗？”

李世民笑道：“不是阿玄你说的，我们还小，能做到的事很少。这件事最终如何，还是得看老师自己选择，我们只要做出了努力，问心无愧即可。”

李玄霸观察了二哥一会儿。二哥是真洒脱。

他真不明白，二哥怎么会如此洒脱。只要做了就行，不管结果？

自己可做不到如此洒脱。他更重结果。没有结果，任何努力都没有意义，越努力反而会越煎熬。

他现在被二哥拉着，不管结果，二话不说先撸着袖子开干。真是身心俱疲。

杜如晦笑道：“李二说得对，我们问心无愧即可。”

他攥起拳头扬了扬：“和你们成为朋友真是再正确不过的事！我辈就该指点朝堂江山，做一番大事！”

房乔心情也很澎湃。

虽然他知道这不应该，不掺和此事才更好。但青年人太容易冲动，他也难以免俗。

“希望此事能做成。”长孙无忌发表不出意见，只能祝福了，“我和父亲写信，求求他如果有机会，在自身安全的前提下为高公和宇文公说说好话。”

李世民狠狠拍了一下长孙无忌的肩膀：“你还说别指望你？说不定我们最后，就靠着你这封信了！”

长孙无忌有些高兴：“嗯……我努力求求父亲，你们可别对我抱太大希望。”

李世民道：“任何一点点希望都弥足珍贵。谢了，长孙四郎！不愧是我的好兄弟！”

李世民给了长孙无忌一个兄弟拥抱。

长孙无忌脸颊绯红：“行了行了。”

李世民又给了房乔和杜如晦拥抱，不顾他的拥抱在这两位已经弱冠的友人那里，就像是儿子抱父亲。

房乔和杜如晦皆忍俊不禁。

“弟弟！”李世民张开手臂。

李玄霸往房乔身后绕。

李世民道：“帮我逮住他！他怎么能不合群！”

杜如晦立刻按住了李玄霸的肩膀，对李玄霸不怀好意地笑了笑。

“弟弟！”李世民扑了过来，把李玄霸脑袋抱在怀里，揉散了李玄霸的小揪揪。

李玄霸骂道：“哥，你有病啊！”

李世民叉腰大笑：“哈哈哈哈，谁让你老是一副老成冷淡模样，不像是八岁，像是八十岁似的。”

其余三人皆跟着大笑，把李玄霸气得直跺脚，要去扯李世民的小揪揪。

李世民以长孙无忌为“盾牌”，一边躲避弟弟的追打，一边扮鬼脸挑衅弟弟。

房乔和杜如晦在一旁兜着手微笑看着年幼的友人打闹。

这种混杂着友人和长辈的心态，真是令人心情复杂啊。

……

李世民和李玄霸送了信就跑，信上还写着阅后即焚，搞得好像在密谋什么似的。

两个真的在密谋的老头相视无语。

宇文弼忍不住道：“我二人看上去是无能到需要孩童来出谋划策的模样吗？”

高颎淡淡道：“就当他们是一片孝心。”

宇文弼道：“我知道他们一片孝心，但……”

但就是尴尬无语。

他们在朝堂当了几十年的官，先后伺候两朝君王，哪不懂如何与君王相处？

两人之前没有谨小慎微，只是因为断定自己身为对大隋和皇帝忠心耿耿的老臣，皇帝再不喜自己，顶多就是一个外放或者免官。

谁能想到，他们身为朝中高官连朝堂情况都不能点评一二，居然能因言获罪？

他们从未想到，陛下还能因“诽谤朝政”来杀人的。

这罪名用来杀平民百姓就罢了，杀朝中大官，这是昏君的行为。

甚至史书中的昏君在杀进谏的官员时，都会另找一个罪名，比如“谋反”。

先帝也曾误杀忠臣，但他都是用的“图谋不轨”的罪名。

“谋反”罪是历代君王手中排除异己的屠刀，因为“谋反”与否，只是君王自己说了算。君王想杀任何人，都可以往这方面靠。

可这位皇帝在李大德的“谶纬”中，居然连这把屠刀都不肯用，直接用“诽谤朝政”滥杀朝臣。

他连名声都不顾了，简直就是另一个天元皇帝。

不，他连天元皇帝还不如呢。天元皇帝虽然昏庸暴虐，但乐运抬着棺材入朝堂痛骂天元皇帝，给天元皇帝列了八项罪名时，天元皇帝还能在内吏的劝说下不仅没有杀乐运，还赏赐了乐运。

知道杨广的本性后，他们就会摸着杨广的底线进谏。

虽然他们无法视而不见，进谏的危险也不可能完全去除，但他们不是自寻死路之人。

他们还想看到弟子口中的盛世，想验证自己心中的猜测。

比如，与李玄霸这位天生神异之人一同诞生的李世民，是不是会有如他们心中所猜测的那样的成就。

“罢了，好歹是一片孝心。”高颎道，“肯定是大雄多做无用之事，大德跟着胡闹。”

宇文弼道：“没错。”

两人抱怨两位弟子，但脸上欣慰又得意的笑容怎么也止不住。

弟子如此尊敬并看重他们，他们怎么可能不欣慰得意？

“两个孩子都如此担心我们了，我们可不能让他们失望。”

“不过又一个天元帝。天元帝我们都能挺过来。”

高颎和宇文弼不是不知道如何应付昏君，只是因为他们没想到杨广是昏君而已。

两人的计划其实与李世民、李玄霸等五人的献策本质一样，都是将献策包装成歌功颂德。

他们先去找太子哭诉，说如果因为不赈灾而产生民乱，平乱所花费的钱粮会比赈灾多。而且民乱一生，陛下震怒，不知道朝中会有多少无辜大臣人头落地。

太子叹息：“是啊，这可如何是好？”

高颎道：“若陛下不想开官仓，以助长百姓懒惰，让百姓依赖朝廷，何不以为先帝先后祈福为名，捐赠钱粮给寺庙，让寺庙向天下百姓施舍善粥？陛下十分孝顺，一定会同意。”

太子道：“这……我试试。高公、宇文公可还有什么进谏？”
