Chapter 45: Li Xuanba is Heavily in Debt

Li Xuanba was left with nothing but a cough. Just when he no longer needed to drink medicine, Li Shimin fell ill.
He had nightmares at night, waking up in a start several times, and by the next day, he had started running a runny nose.
Li Xuanba handed the bitter medicine to Li Shimin, who looked at his younger brother with a deeply resentful gaze.
Li Xuanba met his brother’s eyes without the slightest sense of guilt.
What are you looking at? It has nothing to do with me!
Li Shimin silently drank the medicine, silently feeling aggrieved.
Li Xuanba was curious: [Don’t you want to ask for more details?]
After finishing the bitter medicine, Li Shimin wore a weary expression, as if he had seen through the vanity of life: "I am still young. When I grow up, I will take on these heavy burdens."
Li Xuanba agreed: [I told you long ago not to ask, and to wait until you grow up for me to tell you.]
Li Shimin wanted to wipe his runny nose on his brother!
"What did I ask?!" Li Shimin expressed intense anger at his brother’s distortion of the truth. "I didn’t ask anything!"
Li Xuanba thought for a moment, then let out a series of coughs to brush it off.
Li Shimin recovered his vitality after being ill for only three days.
Li Xuanba, however, continued to cough, even waking himself up at night.
But both the imperial physician and Dr. Sun said that it wasn't good for Li Xuanba’s body to consume too much medicine. Since it was just a minor cough, it was best to let him endure it on his own. If the coughing became truly severe, he could eat a few loquat leaves pickled in honey to soothe his throat.
Nighttime coughing was too draining, so Li Xuanba asked his teachers for leave, catching up on sleep during the day when he wasn't coughing.
Li Shimin still had to attend classes, so Li Xuanba’s nighttime coughing didn't affect him.
Although the two brothers still lived in the same courtyard, they had started sleeping in separate beds upon their eighth birthday. Each had a small room that they could decorate as they pleased.
Li Shimin was a bit worried that Li Xuanba wouldn't sleep well without him there to look after him.
But this was something Li Xuanba had insisted on, because as his second brother began to sprout up in height, his sleeping posture had become incredibly restless.
They were at the age where they were growing rapidly; their legs would occasionally cramp, and they would move wildly in their sleep.
Li Xuanba was relatively quiet, at most turning over a bit more frequently.
Li Shimin, however, was something else. Once, he performed an entire set of long-fist boxing in his sleep, punching Li Xuanba awake.
Li Xuanba sat up in disbelief, watching by the moonlight as his brother practiced boxing in bed, then kicked and ran, and finally combined his limbs, running and throwing punches while muttering "Kill" in his sleep.
Who are you trying to kill?! Are you going to pull a "I like to kill people in my dreams" stunt?!
The sleeping posture of a growing child is truly terrifying.
When Lady Dou learned of this, she laughed heartily and gave them separate rooms.
Their rooms were adjacent, the study remained shared, and there was a small door connecting the rooms directly, so they didn't have to go outside to enter the other.
After that, Li Xuanba finally got a good night's sleep.
However, during their afternoon naps, the two still habitually made do together on the daybed in the study. During the day, Li Shimin was a light sleeper, and his sleeping posture was relatively well-behaved.
Perhaps the young Emperor Taizong wasn't "I like to kill in my dreams," but rather "I like to kill in the night."
When the two children first started sleeping separately, Lady Dou was a bit worried about whether they would get used to it.
Li Shimin also complained that he was used to checking if his brother had covered himself with his quilt upon waking. If he habitually reached out to the side and felt nothing, he would surely wake up in a panic.
Hearing his brother say this, Li Xuanba was slightly touched, but he remained firm in his refusal to sleep with his brother, whose sleeping posture had deteriorated.
That night, a very worried Lady Dou came to see if the two children were struggling. Both were sleeping soundly. Especially Li Shimin, who was sprawled right in the middle of the bed, his limbs splayed out, looking incredibly comfortable.
Lady Dou felt conflicted. Was she the only one who was too worried to sleep?
Especially Erlang! Look how deeply you're sleeping! You don't even wake up when I pinch your nose!
Lady Dou felt inexplicably sad. She only felt better when she saw that although the two children were sleeping in separate rooms, they remained as close as ever.
Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Yu Shinan reduced Li Shimin’s lessons, allowing him to return home earlier to tutor his brother.
Li Shimin would skip home immediately after class to tutor Li Xuanba.
Ever since he started learning archery and horsemanship, Li Shimin’s mind had become restless. He couldn't sit quietly and read like he did at five or six, and his attitude toward his academic studies had become somewhat perfunctory.
Only when Li Xuanba was ill did Li Shimin return to being that obedient student who could settle his heart to read.
"Because now, I am not just a student, but also your teacher." Li Shimin rolled up his book, imitating Gao Jiong’s demeanor while lecturing. "Study hard, don't be lazy."
Li Xuanba listened to the lecture obediently.
Li Zhiyun, whose personality had become more mischievous with age, lay on Li Xuanba’s back, poking his head out from his brother’s shoulder, also listening obediently.
Li Shimin quipped, "You can't really call this obedient, can you?"
Li Zhiyun said, "Little Five is obedient!"
Li Xuanba said, "Isn't Little Five being obedient by lying here?"
Li Shimin rolled his eyes. If Little Five turned into a little rascal like Li Yuanji, it would definitely be A-Xuan’s fault.
By the time Li Xuanba’s cough had completely cleared, Yang Guang had already arrived in Yulin, preparing to return to Luoyang.
At the same time, Yang Guang changed the name of the Eastern Capital, Luoyang, to "Eastern Metropolis" (Dongdu).
The court didn't know what the difference between "Eastern Capital" (Dongjing) and "Eastern Metropolis" was, but it was probably just because the Emperor liked it.
The Emperor not only changed "Eastern Capital" to "Eastern Metropolis," but also changed many titles, such as changing provinces to commanderies and reverting weights and measures to the Han system. Perhaps he was using this method to demonstrate his determination to make the Great Sui as prosperous as the Great Han.
By the time Li Xuanba could attend classes again, the flooding had ended. The disaster victims had stopped wandering and returned to their devastated homelands to rebuild from the silt.
Yang Guang did not go through the Buddhist temples; he distributed relief grain to the victims directly in the name of imperial grace.
He even specifically sent troops to bring the victims to Yulin, then bestowed food upon them in front of the Turkic nobles, including Qimin Khan.
There was plenty of food, and the victims could take away what they couldn't finish, kneeling to thank the Emperor for his heavenly grace.
The Turkic nobles were astonished by the prosperity of the Great Sui and flattered the Emperor’s benevolence.
They said that if they encountered such disasters on the grasslands, the starving herdsmen would simply be abandoned. A herdsman’s value was not even equal to that of cattle or sheep. Only a Central Plains dynasty as wealthy as this would bestow precious grain upon worthless, lowly people.
Although the Turkic nobles were flattering him, they were also speaking the plain truth.
Yang Guang sighed to those around him, "The Turkic Khan is truly too cruel. The people of the Great Sui should rejoice that they are my subjects."
The ministers around him echoed his sentiments.
Although Gao Jiong was no longer at the center of the court, he had countless friends, and news of the Emperor’s northern inspection would quickly reach his ears.
For example, the Emperor demanded that the disaster victims be brought before him so he could personally bestow food upon them;
For example, just as during his inspection of Jiangdu, the Emperor had officials along the way compete to present exquisite food. The Yanmen Governor Qiu He was promoted for presenting fine food, while the Mayi Governor Yang Kuo was dismissed for failing to satisfy the Emperor, leading officials along the route to compete in the luxury of their offerings;
For example, the Emperor had Yuwen Kai build the "Viewing Wind Traveling Palace" and "Traveling City." These were like land-based "dragon boats," so heavy that even horses could hardly pull them, requiring many men to drag them across the land;
For example, when the Emperor reached Yulin, he had a whim to build a Great Wall, so he conscripted a million laborers and finished a wall from Yulin in the west to the Zi River in the east within twenty days;
For example, the Emperor finally arrived in Taiyuan, felt it was a good place, and immediately demanded the construction of the Jinyang Palace;
For example, the Emperor wanted to visit the minister Zhang Heng’s home but didn't want to take a detour, so he conscripted the people of Taiyuan to urgently build a new 90-mile-long imperial road leading directly to Zhang Heng’s house...
As for the excessively luxurious displays used to entertain Qimin Khan, who accompanied him into the pass, those were minor matters.
These were all orders issued by the Emperor before he reached the Eastern Metropolis of Luoyang on the 23rd of the eighth month. And the Emperor had only left the capital for his northern inspection at the end of the fourth month or the beginning of the fifth.
By the time the Emperor returned to the palace in the Eastern Metropolis of Luoyang, the Great Wall and the imperial road were already finished, with only the Jinyang Palace still under overtime construction, which would likely be completed soon.
When Gao Jiong received this news, his face turned ashen.
He was now absolutely certain that he would die during this imperial northern inspection.
Because if he had accompanied the Emperor on the northern inspection, he would surely have been ceaseless in his remonstrations—unlike now, where by the time he learned of what the Emperor had done, even the Great Wall and the imperial road were already built.
Now that the events had already transpired, their remonstrations would only be seen as complaints. Knowing the Emperor wouldn't listen, they couldn't even be bothered to submit memorials.
Gao Jiong was even curious in a "broken-pot-and-let-it-smash" sort of way. He already found what Yang Guang was doing unfathomable; to what extent could Yang Guang go next?
The people had just emerged from chaotic times and had experienced a brief era of peace under the previous Emperor, so their tolerance for suffering was high.
The previous Emperor’s rule wasn't exactly gentle, but compared to the chaos, the people were much happier. They certainly didn't want to return to those chaotic times.
But such endurance had its limits.
The Great Sui’s demise in the second generation was different from the Qin Dynasty’s. The Qin Dynasty was born with congenital defects and was tottering from the start; when it encountered an absurd and tyrannical dim-witted ruler, it immediately plunged into the abyss.
The previous Emperor had already built a prototype of a prosperous age for Yang Guang; this was the dynasty’s rising period. What did Yang Guang have to do to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the Second Emperor of Qin?
After Li Xuanba learned of these things, he also marveled at the endurance and capability of the Great Sui people.
Yang Guang could tour while having the people build imperial roads without delaying his schedule in the slightest; the Great Wall was also ordered on a whim, and it was finished by the time the tour ended.
Comparing this to the speed at which Qin Shi Huang built his roads and walls, the productivity of the Great Sui must have made great strides to achieve such terrifying "Great Sui Speed."
Just looking at the efficiency with which the Great Sui launched and completed massive projects, Yang Guang’s inclusion as a candidate for "Emperor of the Ages" was truly well-deserved.
Li Shimin, Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Zhangsun Wuji all gave Li Xuanba a thumbs-up after hearing his remarks.
Sarcasm—Li Sanlang was truly a master of it.
Among them, except for the dim-witted Zhangsun Wuji, Du Ruhui was the only one who still held hope for the Emperor.
After all, the Emperor had only been on the throne for four years and had changed the reign title three years ago. Du Ruhui believed it was too early to judge what would happen in the future.
In his view, the purpose of some of the Emperor’s decisions was correct; it was just that the implementation process was too crude. Perhaps this was because the Emperor had just ascended the throne and was not yet skilled in handling state affairs.
Although Du Ruhui was from the Jingzhao Du clan, he was not from the main branch and didn't know much about court news. Now that he had received first-hand information from Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, his filter for the Emperor had completely shattered.
He began to consider that instead of waiting for official appointments, he might as well go home and live off his family in seclusion.
Many in the court were just as disheartened as Du Ruhui. Even Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi had retreated to the sidelines; no one dared to stop what the Emperor wanted to do.
Even the kind-hearted Crown Prince dared not.
Gao Jiong had originally held the Crown Prince in high regard. He believed that if Crown Prince Yang Zhao could successfully ascend the throne, he would surely be able to continue the Great Sui.
Unfortunately, the Crown Prince was in poor health and likely wouldn't live as long as Yang Guang.
But now, Yang Zhao’s act of playing deaf and dumb disappointed Gao Jiong.
He knew the Crown Prince’s difficulties and his reluctance to provoke the Emperor’s jealousy. But even just going through the motions, submitting a single edict to show his stance would have been enough.
At least if the Crown Prince did that, the ministers and the people would have a glimmer of hope, believing that the Crown Prince was at least benevolent, and that he only refrained from remonstrating too much because he was just the Crown Prince and a son.
If the Crown Prince was truly too afraid of provoking the Emperor, he didn't have to remonstrate on everything; he could just remonstrate on one thing, like asking for the time requirements for building the Great Wall to be less harsh.
But the Crown Prince did nothing.
He only petitioned the Emperor at the request of Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi when the disaster victims were already at the gates of Daxing City.
The Crown Prince was very kind and benevolent to people, but he was too cautious.
Perhaps this was correct.
The Crown Prince first had to protect his position and his life; only after becoming Emperor could he realize his ambitions. If he displeased the Emperor, his noble character and outstanding talent would be meaningless.
Gao Jiong knew rationally that the Crown Prince’s choice was correct, but he still couldn't help but feel disappointed.
Whenever he thought of the current Crown Prince, he couldn't help but ruffle Li Shimin’s hair.
Although Li Shimin didn't understand why his teacher suddenly ruffled his hair, he sensed that his teacher was very unhappy, so he obediently let him do it.
Watching Li Shimin’s filial and respectful demeanor, Gao Jiong felt both happy and sour in his heart.
Li Shimin was good at everything, except that he was too young.
The northern inspection not only left Gao Jiong completely disappointed in Yang Guang and Yang Zhao, but also made him look at Li Xuanba with renewed respect.
Yang Guang’s final actions were actually quite similar to what Li Xuanba had predicted.
In other words, his own remonstrations had failed, but Li Xuanba must have done something to make Yang Guang follow his schemes.
Although, judging by Li Xuanba’s expression, Yang Guang’s final approach still exceeded Li Xuanba’s expectations, Li Xuanba’s insight into Yang Guang’s mind was definitely deeper than his own.
Was this because Li Xuanba knew prophecy?
Possessing a book of prophecy—it was truly terrifying. And this book of prophecy was actually called the "Book of Sui," which was even more terrifying.
Gao Jiong thought of his own position in the "Book of Sui," and his mood improved slightly.
Yuwen Bi’s mood was even worse than Gao Jiong’s. He had made up his mind never to remonstrate with Yang Guang again.
However, Yuwen Bi had said that before, and Li Xuanba hoped his teacher could hold on a little longer.
For Li Xuanba, the matter of Yang Guang’s northern inspection was completely over.
He had lost a fortune.
The money he had saved from his soap shop and bookstore was all gone, and he had even signed IOUs to his mother and elder sister; he was now heavily in debt.
This money wasn't lost on buying slaves.
In times without famine, ordinary slaves were very cheap. Slaves with average looks and no special talents only cost less than a guan of cash.
When famine struck, the stewards said they could take "whole families," and for just a mouthful of food, many slaves would follow without needing a purchase price.
Even for "excellent" slaves who needed money, the asking price dropped to about a hundred coins, ninety percent cheaper than usual.
Therefore, during famines, it was a great time for wealthy families to happily increase their number of slaves. The Tang Duke’s mansion had reached its capacity for slaves without even spending the money earned from a single limited pre-sale at the soap shop.
Li Xuanba’s money had all been used to bribe Yuwen Shu.
He knew that Yuwen Shu was a corrupt official who kept his word; as long as the money was enough, Yuwen Shu would truly get things done.
So, Li Xuanba used the excuse of sending new soaps and skincare products to make a bunch of boxes inlaid with rare treasures. The gaps in the boxes were filled with pearls and gems, and through his connection with Yuwen Shiji, he successfully got Yuwen Shu to agree to help.
The rare treasures that Yuwen Shu would take a fancy to were not something Li Xuanba could earn from selling soap and books for just a few months.
In addition to the money borrowed from his mother and third sister, the money from selling Li Shimin’s pony was also used for this.
Li Xuanba only told Li Shimin about this after it was done.
Li Shimin was depressed for a long time.
He had sold his pony to give the disaster victims a mouthful of food, not to send money to a corrupt official.
Li Shimin said to Li Xuanba, "A-Xuan, you should have told me that the money for buying slaves was from selling my pony, and the bribe money was what you borrowed. That way, I would have felt much better."
Li Xuanba said, "Then don't feel better; suffer with me."
Li Shimin sulked.
Yuwen Shu! I’ll remember you! Even if you are the father of Prince Consort Yuwen, I’ll remember you!
Seeing Li Shimin’s petty look, Li Xuanba comforted him, "It’s fine, anyway, in the future he..."
Li Shimin immediately covered Li Xuanba’s mouth: "Don't say it! Don't even think it! I’m still young, wait until I grow up to talk about it!"
Whenever Li Xuanba mentioned the future, he remembered how miserably Zhangsun Wuji had died.
Now, whenever he saw Zhangsun Wuji, he couldn't help but sigh, leaving Zhangsun Wuji completely bewildered.
Li Xuanba: [Fine, I won't say it. Let go, you’re suffocating me.]
Li Shimin let go and warned, "Don't you dare say it, never again."
Li Xuanba said helplessly, "Fine. I definitely won't bring it up."
If it was a conditioned reflex or something, then that wouldn't be his fault.
Burdened with heavy debt and now recovered in health, Li Xuanba had to work hard.
He finally managed to produce flower essential oils.
Floral essential oils were extracted through distillation; the only technical difficulty was the separatory funnel.
Li Xuanba only remembered the general appearance of a separatory funnel. There was no glass now, so the craftsmen tried for a long time before they barely managed to fire a simple version of a ceramic separatory funnel.
This funnel couldn't be as convenient as the ones in later generations; when separating the oil from the hydrosol, a lot of oil would remain in the hydrosol.
It didn't matter; the essential oil was meant to be a tribute and sold to the nobility anyway. Things were valuable because they were rare, so he would just sell them at a higher price.
The hydrosol was also a "luxury item" and could be diluted with water to sell, making a massive profit.
Roses were already available. Li Xuanba had planted roses long ago, packaging rose essential oil and rose hydrosol as the most precious items. Once Yang Guang and Empress Xiao used them, Yang Guang didn't say anything yet, but Empress Xiao asked Yang Guang for money, people, and land to help Li Xuanba expand the production of rose essential oil and hydrosol.
"After using the rose essential oil and hydrosol, I can no longer use any other balms," Empress Xiao said, touching her face, which had been treated with the products, and sighed, "It takes a thousand roses to produce a single drop of essence. Truly, only the court of a prosperous dynasty like the Great Han could afford such treasures."
Yang Guang, however, felt the scent of the roses was too voluptuous.
Although he felt very comfortable and in high spirits when he smelled it in the harem—more effective than any aphrodisiac—he didn't want to use that scent himself.
It didn't matter; Li Xuanba had already prepared a men’s special "herbal and woody" essential oil, such as cedarwood essential oil.
Cedarwood was widely cultivated in the Western Regions and India. Because it was very fragrant, monks often used the cedar branches, which were very common in the Western Regions and India, to deceive people as rare items.
Li Xuanba had thought of the popular cedarwood essential oil while preparing to make soap, so he spent money to buy cedar seeds and saplings from Western Region merchants to cultivate them in large quantities.
However, the so-called cedarwood essential oil he used now was just extracted from ordinary local pine trees; the effect was unknown, but at least it wouldn't ruin their skin.
As for why it was called cedarwood—why couldn't a pine tree in the snow be called a cedar? Cedarwood sounded more aloof than a pine tree.
Look, His Majesty was very satisfied with the name "Cedarwood."
News of Li Xuanba collecting cedarwood had already reached Yang Guang’s ears.
Li Xuanba told Yang Guang that the cedarwood used for tribute was from the Western Regions, while the cedarwood essential oil sold to ordinary nobles used locally produced cedar.
By the way, the same went for the rose essential oil.
The nobles used the roses that were already common locally, but the tribute rose essential oil was a palace tribute from a mysterious empire even further west than the Western Regions. He welcomed His Majesty and the Empress to come and provide guidance, to see the cedar and roses he had specially planted for the tribute.
Even if they were both called cedarwood or rose essential oil, what His Majesty and the Empress used was completely different! It was only called a tribute if you couldn't buy it even with money, and couldn't get it even through connections!
Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, was dissatisfied: "Even this Prince can't get it?!"
Li Xuanba took Yang Jian to the garden he had specially planted for the Emperor and Empress.
Beside the garden, there were even people playing soothing Western Region music at regular intervals.
Li Xuanba said, "The people of the Western Regions say that plants have feelings too; only when they hear the music of their homeland will the plants from the Western Regions grow better."
Yang Jian was deeply shocked.
Li Xuanba sighed, "It’s not that I don't want to give it to Your Highness, the Prince of Qi, but the quantity is so small that I can't grow more. Why doesn't Your Highness try helping me buy more tree seeds and flowers from Western Region merchants, and I’ll find people to try planting them?"
Yang Jian walked around the garden, looking at the land that wasn't even as big as his own courtyard, and couldn't find a way to make things difficult for Li Xuanba.
He had walked through Li Xuanba’s "raw material planting base" and really only saw these two small plots.
With so little, it wasn't even enough to make the essential oils and hydrosols for his Imperial Father and Mother.
Yang Jian said angrily, "I don't believe that if it grows in the Western Regions, it won't grow in the Great Sui! You wait, this Prince will send people to the Western Regions to buy more rare flower and tree seeds!"
Li Xuanba bowed to Yang Jian: "Then I leave it to you, Cousin. Cousin doesn't need to be too angry; His Majesty dotes on you, why not write a letter and ask directly? I think His Majesty would still bestow a bottle or two of essential oil and hydrosol upon you."
Yang Jian originally wanted to say that a bottle or two wasn't enough; he would use it all up in one application.
But looking at the narrow garden in front of him, he felt that even his Imperial Father probably couldn't use essential oil and hydrosol to rub his body every day. If he could get a bottle to dab on the tip of his nose and smell the scent every day, that would be good enough.
Yang Jian wrote a letter to Yang Guang, complaining about how hard it was to get raw materials; it was the first time he couldn't use the tribute products to his heart's content, and even soap hadn't been this hard to get before.
Yang Jian also sighed to those around him, telling them not to spend huge sums of money to buy tribute rose and cedarwood essential oils from outside anymore. He had seen it himself; even the raw materials for the essential oils and hydrosols were only a tiny amount. It wasn't even enough for his Imperial Father and Mother, and the palace staff didn't dare take kickbacks when they came to collect the tribute. The tribute rose and cedarwood essential oils sold secretly outside were all fake.
"If even I and the Crown Prince can't get the tribute products, who could possibly buy them?"
After the Prince of Qi’s words spread, many people asked Crown Prince Yang Zhao.
Yang Zhao sighed: "Just use the ordinary rose and cedarwood essential oils; why use those from the Western Regions? Are the roses and cedarwood from the Western Regions really better than those of the Great Sui?"
There, the Crown Prince had subtly indicated that everything the Prince of Qi said was the truth.
"Brother, I don't understand why you told the outside world that the tribute rose and cedarwood are rare, and that they don't exist anywhere except in the imperial palace," Li Shimin said, confused. "Can't we keep some to sell? The tribute products could be sold before."
Li Xuanba, while reading, thought to himself: [We can't monopolize the technology for extracting essential oils and hydrosols. I will soon present it to His Majesty and sell it to other nobles and clans. Essential oils and hydrosols are different from soap; the extraction technology is not complicated. The essential oils and hydrosols sold outside are not much different from what we sell. The only way to make our essential oils sell for more and be better than others is to take the path of 'scarce raw materials.']
Li Shimin still didn't understand: "If we don't sell them, what’s the point of them being scarce?"
Li Xuanba looked up and smiled: [After the reputation of the tribute essential oils and hydrosols is established, customers will think that the other essential oils and hydrosols we sell are also extraordinary. And, heh, the more we emphasize that they can't be bought outside, the more crazy they will become for the tribute products. By then, we just need to sell '90%, 80%, 70% similar' products.]
He didn't mention that the fake tribute products currently on the market were also "stolen and sold" by people he had sent.
The people who "stole and sold" them didn't say they were real tribute products; they only said they were stolen from the workshop. Who knew, maybe some of them were actually tribute products?
The small goal of paying off his debts this year could probably be achieved.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第46章 齐王杨暕不心虚
chunks.chineseText:
第46章 齐王杨暕不心虚

=
　　到了年底的时候， 李玄霸终于凑够了还债的钱。
　　窦夫人和李昭不想收，让李玄霸继续扩大生产。
　　她们不收钱，李玄霸就站在门口不肯走。李世民劝不动， 也只能跟着站着。
　　李玄霸体弱， 窦夫人和李昭哪能让李玄霸一直罚站？只能无奈收钱。
　　李世民悄悄对弟弟道：“阿玄， 娘亲和阿姊想给你钱，你就拿着，以后在其他方面弥补。你这样做太见外， 会伤了娘亲和阿姊的心。”
　　李玄霸摇头：“我不喜欢欠人东西。”
　　李世民叹气：“我知道，但亲人和其他人是不一样的，所以我说你太见外啊。”
　　李玄霸道：“习惯如此。”
　　李世民举双手投降：“行行行。唉， 看来只能我多担待点，哄好娘亲和阿姊， 让娘亲和阿姊别生气。”
　　李玄霸露出无奈的神色。
　　他还钱还能让人生气了？算了， 债还清了就行。他最厌恶的就是背债。
　　欠债的时候，李玄霸好几次梦见前世。
　　他出外打工的时候为了帮店铺省钱，自己读了一些民法书，知道自己其实可以赖掉债务。
　　根据法律规定，他父母变成了老赖， 他不用帮父母还钱。就算他父母死了，只要自己不继承遗产， 也可以不继承债务。
　　李玄霸看到这个法律条款后想了很久，要不要拉黑所有债务人的联系方式。
　　但他就是想一想，一边想一边继续每月按时还债。
　　或许他只是想给自己找一点努力的目标， 或许他只是太厌恶父母， 想做点什么证明自己和父母完全不一样。
　　也或许是祖父母被气死前都拉着他的手， 说一定要还钱， 不能让人戳他们的脊梁骨，如果不还钱，自己就不再是他们的孙儿。
　　祖父母是很老派很正直的人。听说在他很小的时候就过世的外祖父和外祖母也是厚道人。
　　他们宠溺出了自由散漫没有责任感的儿女，然后严格教导自己这个孙儿，害怕自己成为父母那样的人。
　　如果不还债，唯一的亲人不认他，他唯一的家，唯一能回去的地方都没有了。
　　哪怕现在他的家和家人就是一方坟墓，但至少有可以回去坐一坐，烧点香烛纸钱的地方，让他知道自己来到这个世上不是孤身一人。
　　欠债真的难受。如有可能，他再也不想借钱了。
　　“好了好了，别皱着眉头，你不喜欢欠债，以后哥哥努力挣功勋，得到很多很多的钱，让你再也不用借钱。”李世民见弟弟的心情仿佛不好，连忙道，“我以后不劝你了。唉，我真想快点长大。”
　　李玄霸嘴角抽搐：“我借你的钱，不还是借钱欠债？”
　　李世民疑惑：“我给你钱，不是借你钱。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“哥啊，你是你，我是我，你的钱就是你的钱，我的钱就是我的钱，不能混为一谈。”
　　李世民笑道：“我就知道你会这么说。但你想做的事我也想做，你要做的生意我也要掺和一脚。我又懒得动脑子，于是你出力我出钱不是理所当然吗？你说的，亲兄弟也要明算账，你该不会要我欠你债吧？人情债也是债。”
　　李玄霸有些惊讶。他仔细想了想，居然无法反驳。
　　李世民道：“娘亲和阿姊就是不够了解你。如果娘亲和阿姊不说借钱，而是说自己也想这么做，你不就不用还钱了？”
　　李玄霸哭笑不得：“我还没那么无耻。”
　　李世民摇头：“不是无耻。她们本来就是这么想的，只是没想到你这么见外。唉，所以你为什么这么见外啊！”
　　李玄霸狡辩：“我都说了不是见外。”
　　李世民摆手：“行行行，不和你说了。接下来做什么？”
　　李玄霸道：“到冬天了，什么都不做。”
　　李世民不解道：“但铺子里的货快卖完了吧？”
　　李玄霸摊手：“鲜花冬天不会开，材料用完了就没了。雪松之类的精油倒是可以冬天萃取，但气温太低，纯露之类会结冰，所以不卖了。按照季节卖东西，这才更稀有。”
　　李世民完全不明白。明明可以卖，非要找些借口人为制造缺货的假象，这样不是很亏吗？
　　不过弟弟说不忙碌了是好事。看着弟弟之前忙着赚钱，他很担心弟弟累病倒。
　　今年弟弟没有得大病，真是太好了。
　　不过李玄霸说不卖，不是真的不卖。
　　有材料的精油和纯露还是会卖的，但是卖的很少，而且只卖预售，几乎不上架。
　　冬季也有蜡梅之类的花朵，可以做季节限定，当然也是稀有货。李玄霸让店铺贴出告示，现在店铺只卖香皂，纯露和精油都是预售，只做展示，不卖货，等正月才会上架一批冬季限定精油和纯露公开售卖。
　　顾客们看到了告示，仍旧每天询问店小二，一副好像每天多问一句就能让店家改变主意的模样。
　　李玄霸让店小二和顾客们闲聊的时候，趁机透露明年有眉粉、胭脂、粉饼等新产品上架的消息。
　　顾客们立刻问：“那这些东西怎么卖呢？”
　　店小二回答道：“以主人的性格，大概只是做一些小批量的送给家人，剩下的上架。上架多少我们就不知道了。”
　　顾客们继续问：“接受预订吗！”
　　店小二摇头道：“这个我们就不知道了，我们只是听主人提了这么一句。”
　　窦夫人得到消息后，好奇地问李玄霸：“大德，听说你还要做胭脂水粉？”
　　李玄霸疑惑：“谁传的消息？我顶多只做一些给娘亲和阿姊们用。”
　　窦夫人道：“都传开了。”
　　李玄霸道：“哦，我给娘亲和阿姊做了胭脂水粉后，就把法子抄给匠人师傅，匠人师傅或许想将胭脂水粉做出来卖吧。我是没这个空闲的。”
　　窦夫人道：“我想也是。你现在马上要出孝了，该多读书，多和同辈交流，那些胭脂水粉的事还是别做了。”
　　李玄霸点头：“我只给长辈做，怎么会给其他人做？我就复原古方而已。”
　　窦夫人笑道：“真不知道你怎么会有这种爱好。”
　　李玄霸道：“我只是喜欢验证古方。”
　　窦夫人把李玄霸的话传了出去，把李玄霸小小年纪就喜欢女人的胭脂水粉的舆论压下。
　　我家三郎只是喜欢验证古方，做出的东西都是给家中长辈用。若是好用了，就丢给唐国公府的匠人。
　　香皂、精油、纯露和以后的胭脂水粉好卖，和三郎有什么关系？三郎只是验证了古方而已。
　　而且香皂、精油、纯露难道男人不能用？就是胭脂水粉，男人也是要用的。
　　齐王杨暕有一日在听曲的时候听到有纨绔子弟在说此事，直接亲自出手把人打了一顿。
　　“香皂、精油、纯露是贡品，本王的父兄都在用，你说谁是女人？”杨暕打了人之后，还把人丢到官府，以侮辱皇帝、太子、齐王的罪名关了起来，还要上奏皇帝砍了这人的脑袋。
　　杨暕把此事闹得这么大，杨昭焦头烂额地收拾烂摊子。
　　揍就揍了，私下警告就行了，怎么还把此事宣扬得到处都是？小心父皇真的砍了这个人的脑袋，二弟你就是给自己和唐国公府平白无故地树立敌人！
　　杨暕抱着手臂冷哼：“兄长，你怎么什么都怕？你这个太子也当的太憋屈了。这种人既然敢侮辱我们，脑袋砍就砍了，难道不应该砍？！”
　　杨昭按着额头道：“只嘴碎几句就要砍人脑袋，你要砍多少人的脑袋？这些人甚至都不是传播谣言的人，只是被推出来的卒子！”
　　杨暕道：“什么？难道还有人布局？谁布局，我带兵把他们抓了！”
　　杨昭骂道：“你可别再得罪人了！你现在都被父皇拘在京城思过，还不反省吗！”
　　杨暕想着此事都有气。
　　明明他和李家二郎三郎资助贫困学子的事得到了父皇奖赏，他已经可以官复原职了。
　　但不知道哪来的杂碎又弹劾他，害得他出京城又遥遥无期。
　　杨暕本来以为是太子这边的人忌惮他，所以故意给他找碴。但他看着杨昭为他被惩罚急得团团转的模样，还是相信了自家兄长。
　　杨暕虽然想要夺嫡，但也知道自家兄长对亲人确实好，不是会兄弟阋墙的人。
　　“算了，我找李二郎李三郎去了。看见你唯唯诺诺的模样就有气。”杨暕不仅对兄长给他收拾烂摊子没有丝毫感谢，还很烦，气冲冲拂袖而去。
　　杨昭捧着胸口，被气得直喘气。
　　韦太子妃从屏风后出来，抱怨道：“齐王真是不识好歹，给太子殿下惹了这么大的麻烦，还居然来斥责太子殿下。他一点都不敬重太子你这位兄长。”
　　杨昭放下捂着胸口的手，冷漠道：“如果你再说一句二弟的不是，你就回娘家。”
　　韦太子妃惊怒道：“太子殿下何出此言！”
　　杨昭道：“友悌是最重要的妇德。你现在是太子妃，将来是皇后。无论太子妃还是皇后，都将是天下妇德的楷模。二弟的事孤自会处理，不需要你多言。若是你真那么闲，就回娘家让他们管好族人。下次他们再针对唐国公府，孤就会直接将此事告知唐国公府和父皇，不会再替他们遮掩。”
　　韦太子妃立刻垂首道：“我不知道太子殿下你在说什么。”
　　杨昭慢悠悠往屋里走：“不知道？那孤就说得再明白些。孤已经送过一位家中不修妇德的太子妃归家，也可以再送一位。”
　　世家贵女真是烦死了。等儿子长大些，他还是把儿子丢给父皇母后带吧，免得被太子妃教坏。
　　韦太子妃立刻掩面哭了起来，怒斥太子威胁她。
　　但杨昭根本不理睬她。
　　韦氏与唐国公府悄悄针锋相对，他都能当作没看见。但太子妃居然在他面前挑拨他和二弟的关系，这触及了他的底线。
　　杨昭亲眼看到了父亲的夺嫡。他也支持了父亲的夺嫡。
　　但轮到自己，他绝不希望和兄弟兵戎相见。而他和杨暕的关系，也一点都不差。
　　虽然他二弟天天嚷嚷说自己这个太子做得不好，他要夺嫡，但二弟越这么说，杨昭就知道二弟现在没有这个心思。
　　二弟也确实什么都没做，只是嘴里嚷嚷。
　　二弟小时候很聪敏，长大了却直爽得可爱。
　　虽然老喜欢戳他肺管子，老给他惹事，但这也是他们兄弟互相信任的体现。杨昭决不允许有人将他和杨暕的关系引到兄弟相残上。
　　再者，就算杨暕真的有了夺嫡的心思，他已经是太子了，表现得越宽厚就越得父母好感。
　　夺嫡是什么？是争夺父皇的喜爱！不是争夺皇位！父皇还活着呢！
　　他越是表现得不重视皇位而重视兄弟感情，父皇才越属意将皇位传给他！
　　……
　　冬季到了，可怜的李玄霸又患上了小感冒。
　　高颎和宇文弼都想上门上课了，被李玄霸劝了回去。
　　“若让老师劳累，就是我的不是了。”李玄霸道，“哥会把学到的功课交给我，顺便也能让哥努力听课。”
　　高颎和宇文弼想着李世民现在学习态度确实比李玄霸没病的时候认真，便没有坚持。
　　杨暕提着一只大雁来探病，看得李玄霸满脸惊恐。
　　“齐王殿下，你可别说你是来向我家某个阿姊提亲。”李玄霸半开玩笑道，“我阿姊可是都定好了人家了。”
　　杨暕低头看了一眼自己手中的大雁：“对哦，大雁还有提亲这个意思。你想什么呢？这是我今日射到的，顺手给你拎来作礼物。”
　　李玄霸松了口气。
　　他让人把大雁拿去炖了，问道：“现在冬季还有大雁？”
　　杨暕道：“皇家猎场什么猎物没有？你这身体也太差了，等你出了孝，我带你多去打猎。打猎身体就会变好。”
　　李玄霸先带着杨暕去书院资助贫困学生得了杨广的赞许，又让杨暕加盟了铺子，杨暕现在与李玄霸比较亲近。
　　杨暕是很高傲的人，他看得上的人就会全心全意信任，看不上的人就完全不理睬。
　　但杨暕不仅看人不准，而且因为太过高傲坚信自己看人眼光基准，看中的人不是坑自己，然后他自己被坑了。
　　他宠信的人在外面以他的名义贪赃枉法抢夺民妇，他被弹劾了居然都还不清楚，认为是别人诬告。
　　李玄霸真的好奇杨广怎么会忌惮杨暕。
　　杨暕确实不适合成为太子，不是因为他惦记着杨广的位置，而是因为杨暕傻啊。
　　这么傻的直愣子，哪里能夺位了？
　　不过杨暕的“傻”只是性格，事实上他很聪明，学问和武艺都不错。而且他长得极其俊美，简直集父母所有优点于一身。
　　他小时候就因为长得过分可爱，哪怕隋文帝和独孤皇后将杨昭养在身边，也十分喜爱杨暕这个小孙儿。
　　杨暕长大后，他的长相就更加俊美。
　　李玄霸甚至怀疑杨暕非得板着个臭脸，就是不想让人说他面若好女。
　　杨暕与李玄霸熟悉后，就把李玄霸也纳入了自己可信任的人的范围内，叽里呱啦说了一通对太子兄长的不满。
　　李玄霸想着太子给他写的信，十分头疼。
　　杨昭显然知道杨暕在干什么，专门写信请求李玄霸一定要认真听弟弟吐黑泥，好好安慰弟弟，引导弟弟走向正路，不要再惹皇帝生气。
　　李玄霸无语极了。
　　你们兄弟是把我和二哥当润滑调和剂了吗？
　　太子殿下都这么请求了，李玄霸只能咬牙听完杨暕的抱怨。
　　他知道杨暕完全不想听斥责的话，便附和道：“太子殿下一直仁善，与齐王殿下性格不同，又不是今日的事。兄弟二人性格不同很正常，齐王殿下无须动气。你看我和二哥的性格也完全不同。”
　　杨暕撑着下巴叹气：“但我看他唯唯诺诺的样子就是生气！明明是那些人骂了我，他居然还斥责我！”
　　李玄霸道：“我听闻那些人还是得到了惩罚。太子殿下不是斥责齐王殿下，只是担心齐王殿下。不过齐王殿下想得也很对，要把那些人打疼了，他们以后才不会嘴碎。”
　　杨暕立刻道：“对吧！还是李三你懂我！这种人就该狠狠揍一顿！”
　　听到有人支持自己，杨暕立刻不气了。
　　李玄霸便立刻转移话题，道：“父亲给我写信，陛下想让我和二哥在出了孝期后去洛阳。我想齐王殿下也是会一同去的。齐王殿下在洛阳可有铺子？我想把香皂和印书的生意做到洛阳去。”
　　杨暕道：“你在说什么？我怎么可能在洛阳没有铺子？我是齐王！”
　　李玄霸笑道：“也是，是我多话了。”
　　杨暕道：“你在孝期赚点小钱就罢了，怎么出孝期了还做生意？虽然你年纪小，还不能做官，但也可以多交友才是正事。”
　　听杨暕居然在劝说自己读书，李玄霸有些惊讶。
　　看来齐王是真的对自己有了些许善意，居然在为自己着想。
　　李玄霸道：“交友是肯定需要交的，但生意还是得做下去。齐王殿下不缺钱所以不明白，对我来说，一分钱难死好汉啊。出去交友身上没有钱该如何是好？我总不能问家里要。”
　　杨暕疑惑：“怎么不能？”
　　李玄霸苦笑：“我还小，怎么能问公中多要钱？”
　　杨暕问道：“这和你还小有什么关系？你缺钱就问家里要呗，难道父母还能不给你？”
　　李玄霸叹气，压低声音道：“我家和齐王殿下家有所不同。齐王殿下的兄长很仁善宽厚，恨不得亲自补贴齐王殿下。我家是不同的。现在兄长有了孩子，家里该紧着兄长。”
　　杨暕本想说，就算李建成有了儿女，唐国公府难道还缺其他儿子应酬那点钱。
　　话出口的时候，他想起去年京中一些关于李建成的传闻。
　　杨暕不蠢，立刻就明白了李玄霸的言下之意。
　　他皱眉道：“像我兄长那样才正常。罢了，洛阳的事交给我。”
　　李玄霸道：“那就先谢过齐王殿下了。等到了洛阳，我还会请求陛下和西域人做生意，若能成功，齐王殿下可要继续帮忙啊。”
　　杨暕笑道：“怎么？你还能买到西域的好马？”
　　李玄霸道：“我自学了西域的语言，应该能帮上陛下和齐王殿下的忙。”
　　杨暕立刻道：“那可好！你需要什么尽管对我说！”
　　杨暕说完，又抱怨起自己被弹劾的事。
　　他虽然生活奢侈，但那都是用自己的钱。自己妻妾众多，但也都是别人眼巴巴地凑上来，哪还需要欺负良家妇女？弹劾真是没道理！
　　李玄霸想了想，给这位齐王殿下卖了点好。
　　他装作犹豫了一会儿，小声道：“既然外面传得如此有板有眼，连陛下都信了，陛下是英明的人，又很喜爱齐王殿下，应当不是没有证据就故意为难齐王殿下。所以是不是外面有人以齐王殿下的名义故意做坏事？好败坏齐王殿下的名声？”
　　杨暕立刻道：“谁敢！”
　　李玄霸道：“此时为何不交给太子殿下查一查？太子殿下不敢多查，是担心惹怒齐王殿下。若齐王殿下坦然地让太子殿下查，太子殿下一定能还齐王殿下一个公道。”
　　杨暕疑惑：“我自己查就是了，为何要兄长查？”
　　李玄霸压低声音道：“如果真的是诬告，那此事可能不仅仅是对着齐王殿下来的，也是对着太子殿下来的。”
　　杨暕一愣，然后怒气勃发：“是嫁祸给我还是嫁祸给太子？！父皇就两个皇子，他们想做什么！”
　　李玄霸赶紧道：“齐王殿下慎言，我只是推测，说不定只是误会。”
　　杨暕起身，背着手来回走动了几圈，越想越觉得有道理。
　　“父皇确实不会无故指责我。我之前生气我没有做的事，父皇却责骂我。我心里委屈，所以不想辩解。难道真的有人在外面败坏我的名声？还想嫁祸给太子？”杨暕愤怒道，“可恶！是谁干的！”
　　李玄霸道：“是啊，难道齐王殿下不知道？外面还有人传齐王殿下和妻妹有暧昧呢，传得有板有眼。这怎么可能！”
　　杨暕脚步一顿。
　　李玄霸叹气：“齐王殿下的王妃已经去世。殿下若真的看上了某个妻妹，妃位空缺，韦氏女身份不算低，娶进门做继室正合适？还暧昧什么？真是太离谱了。”
　　早逝的齐王妃与太子妃一样出身京兆韦氏，但关系较远，只是祖父是亲兄弟。
　　但齐王嫡长子为齐王妃所出。韦氏内部也有地位争夺。所以太子妃一直很忌惮，担心韦氏中有人支持齐王。
　　杨暕：“……是啊。”他一点都不心虚。
　　杨暕指天发誓，他没有和任何一位妻妹有暧昧。
　　咳，因为和他有暧昧的是已经嫁为元氏妇的妻姊。

Chapter 46: Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, Has No Guilty Conscience

By the end of the year, Li Xuanba had finally scraped together enough money to pay off his debts.

Lady Dou and Li Zhao did not want to accept it, urging Li Xuanba to use the funds to expand his production instead.

When they refused to take the money, Li Xuanba simply stood at the doorway, refusing to leave. Li Shimin couldn't persuade him otherwise, so he had no choice but to stand there with him.

Li Xuanba was physically frail; how could Lady Dou and Li Zhao bear to let him stand there as if he were being punished? They had no choice but to accept the money, feeling helpless.

Li Shimin whispered to his younger brother, "Ah Xuan, Mother and Sister want to give you money—just take it. You can make it up to them in other ways later. Being this distant makes you seem like a stranger, and it will only hurt their feelings."

Li Xuanba shook his head. "I don't like owing people."

Li Shimin sighed. "I know, but family is different from others. That’s why I say you’re being too distant."

Li Xuanba replied, "It’s just a habit."

Li Shimin raised both hands in surrender. "Fine, fine, fine. *Sigh*, it seems I’ll just have to shoulder the burden, coax Mother and Sister, and make sure they don't stay angry."

Li Xuanba wore a look of helplessness.

Could paying back a debt really make people angry? Forget it; as long as the debt was cleared, that was all that mattered. The thing he loathed most was being in debt.

When he was in debt, Li Xuanba had dreamt of his past life several times.

Back then, when he was working odd jobs to help the shop save money, he had read some civil law books and knew that he could actually default on his debts.

According to the law, if his parents became "deadbeats," he wasn't legally obligated to pay their debts for them. Even if his parents died, as long as he didn't inherit their estate, he wouldn't inherit their debts either.

After reading that legal clause, Li Xuanba had thought for a long time about whether he should just block all the creditors' contact information.

But he only thought about it. While thinking, he continued to pay off his debts on time every month.

Perhaps he just wanted to find a goal to strive for; perhaps he just loathed his parents so much that he wanted to do something to prove he was completely different from them.

Or perhaps it was because his grandparents, before they passed away in anger, had held his hands and told him he must pay back the money, that he couldn't let people point fingers at his spine, and that if he didn't pay, he would no longer be their grandson.

His grandparents were old-fashioned, upright people. He had heard that his maternal grandparents, who passed away when he was very young, were also kind-hearted souls.

They had spoiled their own children into being free-spirited and irresponsible, and then strictly taught their grandson, fearing he would become like his parents.

If he didn't pay his debts, the only family he had left wouldn't acknowledge him, and his only home—the only place he could return to—would be gone.

Even if his home and family were now just a grave, at least there was a place he could go to sit for a while, burn some incense, and offer paper money, letting him know that he wasn't alone in this world.

Being in debt was truly miserable. If it were possible, he never wanted to borrow money again.

"Alright, alright, stop frowning. You don't like being in debt? In the future, I’ll work hard to earn merit and get lots and lots of money so you never have to borrow again," Li Shimin said, noticing his brother's poor mood. "I won't try to persuade you anymore. *Sigh*, I really wish I could grow up faster."

Li Xuanba’s mouth twitched. "If I borrow money from you, isn't that still borrowing and being in debt?"

Li Shimin looked puzzled. "I’m giving you money, not lending it."

Li Xuanba sighed. "Brother, you are you, and I am I. Your money is your money, and my money is my money; they cannot be lumped together."

Li Shimin laughed. "I knew you’d say that. But what you want to do, I want to do as well, and I want a hand in the businesses you start. I’m too lazy to use my brain, so isn't it only natural that you provide the effort and I provide the capital? You said it yourself: even brothers must keep clear accounts. You wouldn't want me to owe you a debt, would you? A debt of favor is still a debt."

Li Xuanba was a bit surprised. He thought about it carefully and found he couldn't refute that.

Li Shimin added, "Mother and Sister just don't understand you well enough. If they hadn't said they were 'lending' you money, but instead said they wanted to participate, you wouldn't have to pay them back, would you?"

Li Xuanba was caught between laughter and tears. "I’m not that shameless."

Li Shimin shook his head. "It’s not shameless. That’s what they were thinking all along; they just didn't expect you to be so distant. *Sigh*, why are you so distant anyway!"

Li Xuanba argued, "I told you, it's not being distant."

Li Shimin waved his hand. "Fine, fine, I won't argue with you. What’s next?"

Li Xuanba said, "It’s winter. We do nothing."

Li Shimin was confused. "But the goods in the shop are almost sold out, aren't they?"

Li Xuanba spread his hands. "Flowers don't bloom in winter; once the materials are gone, they're gone. Essential oils like cedarwood can be extracted in winter, but the temperature is too low, and hydrosols will freeze, so we won't sell them. Selling things according to the season makes them even rarer."

Li Shimin didn't understand at all. They could clearly sell them, yet his brother insisted on finding excuses to artificially create a shortage—wasn't that a huge loss?

However, it was a good thing his brother wasn't going to be busy anymore. Seeing his brother working so hard to make money, he had been worried he would work himself sick.

It was a blessing that his brother hadn't fallen seriously ill this year.

But when Li Xuanba said he wouldn't sell, he didn't mean he really wouldn't sell at all.

Essential oils and hydrosols for which he had materials would still be sold, but in very small quantities, and only via pre-order; they would barely be put on the shelves.

There were flowers like wintersweet in winter, which could be used for seasonal limited editions—naturally, these were also rare goods. Li Xuanba had the shop post a notice: the shop would only sell soap for now; hydrosols and essential oils were by pre-order only and for display, not for sale. A batch of winter-limited essential oils and hydrosols would be available for public sale only after the first lunar month.

Customers saw the notice but still asked the shop assistant every day, looking as if they thought asking one more time would make the shopkeeper change his mind.

Li Xuanba had the shop assistant take the opportunity to reveal that new products like eyebrow powder, rouge, and face powder would be launched next year.

The customers immediately asked, "Then how will those be sold?"

The shop assistant replied, "Given our master's personality, he will probably make a small batch for his family, and the rest will be put on the shelves. How many will be available, we don't know."

The customers continued to ask, "Do you accept pre-orders?"

The shop assistant shook his head. "We don't know about that; we only heard the master mention it in passing."

After Lady Dou received the news, she asked Li Xuanba curiously, "Da De, I heard you are going to make rouge and powder?"

Li Xuanba was puzzled. "Who spread that news? At most, I’ll only make some for Mother and my sisters."

Lady Dou said, "It’s spread everywhere."

Li Xuanba replied, "Oh, after I make rouge and powder for Mother and my sisters, I’ll copy the formulas for the craftsmen. Perhaps the craftsmen want to make them to sell. I certainly don't have the time."

Lady Dou said, "I thought as much. You are about to finish your mourning period; you should focus on your studies and socialize more with your peers. You really shouldn't be messing with rouge and powder."

Li Xuanba nodded. "I only make them for my elders; why would I make them for others? I’m just restoring ancient formulas."

Lady Dou laughed. "I really don't know how you developed such a hobby."

Li Xuanba said, "I just enjoy verifying ancient formulas."

Lady Dou spread Li Xuanba’s words, suppressing the rumors that he, at such a young age, was obsessed with women's cosmetics.

*My third son just likes verifying ancient formulas, and everything he makes is for the elders in the house. If it’s good, he just tosses it to the craftsmen at the Tang State Duke’s mansion. If soap, essential oils, hydrosols, and future cosmetics sell well, what does that have to do with my third son? He only verified the formulas.*

*Besides, can't men use soap, essential oils, and hydrosols? Even rouge and powder—men use those too.*

One day, while listening to music, the Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, heard some fops talking about this matter and personally beat them up.

"Soap, essential oils, and hydrosols are tribute products; my father and brother use them. Who are you calling a woman?" After beating them, Yang Jian threw them to the authorities, locking them up on charges of insulting the Emperor, the Crown Prince, and the Prince of Qi, and even threatened to memorialize the Emperor to have their heads chopped off.

Yang Jian made such a scene that Yang Zhao was left scrambling to clean up the mess.

*You beat them, fine, a private warning would have sufficed. Why did you have to broadcast it everywhere? Be careful, or Father might really chop this man's head off, and you, Second Brother, will have created enemies for yourself and the Tang State Duke’s mansion for no reason!*

Yang Jian crossed his arms and snorted. "Brother, why are you afraid of everything? You’re a pathetic Crown Prince. Since these people dared to insult us, their heads should be chopped off—shouldn't they?!"

Yang Zhao pressed his forehead. "If you chop off a head for every loose-lipped remark, how many heads will you take? These people aren't even the ones spreading the rumors; they're just pawns pushed out by others!"

Yang Jian said, "What? You mean someone is plotting this? Who is it? I’ll lead troops to arrest them!"

Yang Zhao scolded, "Stop offending people! You’re already confined to the capital by Father to reflect on your mistakes—haven't you learned anything yet!"

Yang Jian felt angry just thinking about it.

Clearly, he had been rewarded by his father for sponsoring poor students alongside the Li brothers, and he should have been able to return to his post.

But some unknown scum had impeached him again, making his departure from the capital a distant dream.

Yang Jian had originally thought it was the Crown Prince's faction being wary of him and deliberately picking fights. But seeing how anxious Yang Zhao was over his punishment, he believed in his older brother.

Although Yang Jian wanted to seize the throne, he knew his brother was truly good to his family and wasn't the type to engage in fratricidal strife.

"Forget it, I’m going to find the Li brothers. Seeing your timid look makes me angry." Yang Jian didn't thank his brother for cleaning up his mess; instead, he felt annoyed and stormed off, flicking his sleeves.

Yang Zhao clutched his chest, gasping for air in his fury.

Crown Princess Wei emerged from behind a screen and complained, "The Prince of Qi is truly ungrateful. He caused such a huge mess for Your Highness, and yet he comes here to scold you. He has no respect for you as his older brother."

Yang Zhao lowered his hand from his chest and said coldly, "If you say one more word against my Second Brother, you can go back to your maiden home."

The Crown Princess was shocked and angry. "How can Your Highness say such a thing!"

Yang Zhao said, "Fraternal love is the most important virtue for a woman. You are the Crown Princess now, and you will be the Empress. Whether as Crown Princess or Empress, you must be a model of virtue for the world. I will handle my brother's affairs myself; you don't need to interfere. If you are truly that idle, go back to your family and tell them to keep their clansmen in check. If they target the Tang State Duke’s mansion again, I will report it directly to the Duke’s mansion and Father, and I will not cover for them again."

The Crown Princess immediately lowered her head. "I don't know what Your Highness is talking about."

Yang Zhao walked slowly into the room. "You don't know? Then I shall speak more clearly. I have already sent one Crown Princess who lacked virtue back to her home; I can certainly send another."

*Noble families are truly exhausting. When my son is older, I’ll just leave him to Father and Mother to raise, lest he be corrupted by the Crown Princess.*

The Crown Princess immediately covered her face and wept, accusing the Crown Prince of threatening her.

But Yang Zhao ignored her completely.

He could pretend not to see the quiet friction between the Wei clan and the Tang State Duke’s mansion. But the Crown Princess trying to sow discord between him and his brother touched his bottom line.

Yang Zhao had witnessed his father's struggle for the throne. He had supported his father's struggle.

But when it came to his own turn, he absolutely did not want to see his brothers turn weapons against each other. And his relationship with Yang Jian was not bad at all.

Although his Second Brother constantly shouted that he was a poor Crown Prince and that he wanted to seize the throne, the more he said it, the more Yang Zhao knew he didn't have the heart for it.

His brother truly hadn't done anything; it was all just talk.

His brother had been very clever as a child, and as an adult, he was refreshingly straightforward.

Although he loved to poke at his sore spots and cause trouble, it was also a reflection of the trust between them. Yang Zhao would never allow anyone to lead their relationship toward fratricide.

Furthermore, even if Yang Jian really had designs on the throne, he was already the Crown Prince; the more magnanimous he appeared, the more favor he would gain from their parents.

What was the struggle for the throne? It was a struggle for their father's affection! It wasn't a struggle for the throne itself! Their father was still alive!

The more he showed that he didn't value the throne but valued brotherly affection, the more his father would be inclined to pass the throne to him!

...

Winter arrived, and poor Li Xuanba caught a cold again.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi both wanted to come over to teach, but were persuaded back by Li Xuanba.

"If I were to tire my teachers, it would be my fault," Li Xuanba said. "My brother will pass on the lessons to me, and it will also give him a chance to study harder."

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, thinking that Li Shimin’s attitude toward learning was indeed more diligent than when Li Xuanba was healthy, did not insist.

Yang Jian brought a wild goose to visit the sick, leaving Li Xuanba looking terrified.

"Your Highness, please don't tell me you're here to propose marriage to one of my sisters," Li Xuanba joked half-heartedly. "My sisters are already betrothed."

Yang Jian looked down at the goose in his hand. "Oh, right, a goose also signifies a marriage proposal. What are you thinking? I shot this today and just brought it along as a gift."

Li Xuanba breathed a sigh of relief.

He had someone take the goose to be stewed and asked, "Are there still wild geese in winter?"

Yang Jian said, "What game isn't there in the Imperial hunting grounds? Your body is too weak. Once you finish your mourning, I’ll take you hunting more often. Hunting will make your body stronger."

Li Xuanba had first helped Yang Jian gain Emperor Yang’s praise by sponsoring poor students at the academy, and then had Yang Jian invest in his shop; Yang Jian was now quite close to him.

Yang Jian was a very arrogant person; he would trust those he liked with all his heart and ignore those he didn't.

But Yang Jian was not only a poor judge of character, he was also so arrogant that he firmly believed in his own judgment, leading him to be cheated by those he trusted.

The people he favored were out there committing crimes and seizing women in his name, and even when he was impeached, he still didn't realize it, believing it was all a frame-up.

Li Xuanba was truly curious how Emperor Yang could be wary of Yang Jian.

Yang Jian was indeed not fit to be Crown Prince—not because he coveted his father's position, but because he was just too dim.

How could such a foolish, straightforward person seize the throne?

However, Yang Jian’s "foolishness" was just his personality; in fact, he was quite clever, and his scholarship and martial arts were both excellent. Moreover, he was extremely handsome, possessing all the best features of his parents.

Because he was so adorable as a child, even though Emperor Wen and Empress Dugu kept Yang Zhao by their side, they were also very fond of their little grandson, Yang Jian.

As Yang Jian grew up, his looks became even more striking.

Li Xuanba even suspected that Yang Jian insisted on keeping a sour face just so people wouldn't say he looked like a woman.

After becoming familiar with Li Xuanba, Yang Jian included him in his circle of trusted people and rambled on about his dissatisfaction with his older brother, the Crown Prince.

Li Xuanba thought of the letters the Crown Prince had written him and felt a massive headache.

Yang Zhao clearly knew what Yang Jian was doing and specifically wrote to Li Xuanba, begging him to listen to his brother's grievances, comfort him, guide him onto the right path, and stop him from angering the Emperor.

Li Xuanba was speechless.

*Are you brothers using me and my second brother as your personal lubricants?*

Since the Crown Prince had requested it, Li Xuanba could only grit his teeth and listen to Yang Jian’s complaints.

He knew Yang Jian didn't want to hear any scolding, so he chimed in, "The Crown Prince has always been benevolent; his personality is different from yours, and that’s nothing new. It’s normal for brothers to have different personalities, so you don't need to get angry. Look at me and my second brother—our personalities are completely different."

Yang Jian propped his chin on his hand and sighed. "But I get angry when I see his timid look! Those people insulted me, and he actually scolded me!"

Li Xuanba said, "I heard those people were punished. The Crown Prince wasn't scolding you; he was just worried about you. But you are also right—you have to make them feel the pain so they won't be loose-lipped in the future."

Yang Jian immediately said, "Right! Li San, you understand me! People like that deserve a good beating!"

Hearing someone support him, Yang Jian immediately stopped being angry.

Li Xuanba then shifted the topic. "My father wrote to me saying His Majesty wants my second brother and me to go to Luoyang after our mourning period ends. I assume you will be going as well. Do you have any shops in Luoyang? I want to expand my soap and printing business there."

Yang Jian said, "What are you talking about? How could I not have shops in Luoyang? I am the Prince of Qi!"

Li Xuanba laughed. "Of course, I spoke too much."

Yang Jian said, "It’s fine to earn a little pocket money during your mourning, but why continue doing business after it ends? Although you are young and cannot hold office yet, socializing should be your priority."

Hearing Yang Jian actually advising him to study, Li Xuanba was surprised.

It seemed the Prince of Qi truly had some goodwill toward him and was actually thinking of his future.

Li Xuanba said, "Socializing is definitely necessary, but the business must continue. You don't lack money, so you don't understand—for me, a single penny can stump a hero. How can I socialize if I have no money? I can't keep asking my family."

Yang Jian was puzzled. "Why not?"

Li Xuanba smiled bitterly. "I’m still young; how can I ask for more money from the family estate?"

Yang Jian asked, "What does your age have to do with it? If you lack money, just ask your family. Surely your parents wouldn't refuse you?"

Li Xuanba sighed and lowered his voice. "My family is different from yours. Your brother is benevolent and generous; he would love to subsidize you personally. My family is different. Now that my eldest brother has children, the family resources must be prioritized for him."

Yang Jian had wanted to say that even if Li Jiancheng had children, surely the Tang State Duke’s mansion didn't lack the money for a younger son's social expenses.

But as the words left his lips, he remembered some rumors from the capital last year regarding Li Jiancheng.

Yang Jian wasn't stupid; he immediately understood what Li Xuanba was implying.

He frowned. "It’s only normal to be like my brother. Never mind, leave the Luoyang business to me."

Li Xuanba said, "Then I thank you in advance. Once we reach Luoyang, I will also petition His Majesty to trade with the Western Regions. If that succeeds, you must continue to help me."

Yang Jian laughed. "What? Can you even buy good horses from the Western Regions?"

Li Xuanba said, "I have taught myself the languages of the Western Regions; I should be able to help His Majesty and you."

Yang Jian immediately said, "That would be great! Just tell me what you need!"

After saying this, Yang Jian began complaining again about being impeached.

Although he lived luxuriously, he used his own money. He had many wives and concubines, but they were all people who threw themselves at him—why would he ever need to bully innocent women? The impeachment was completely unreasonable!

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and decided to do this Prince a favor.

He pretended to hesitate for a moment and whispered, "Since the rumors outside are so detailed that even His Majesty believes them—and His Majesty is a wise man who is very fond of you—it’s unlikely he would deliberately make things difficult for you without evidence. So, could it be that someone is deliberately doing bad things in your name to ruin your reputation?"

Yang Jian immediately said, "Who would dare!"

Li Xuanba said, "Why not ask the Crown Prince to investigate? He doesn't dare to investigate too deeply because he worries about angering you. If you openly ask him to investigate, he will surely be able to clear your name."

Yang Jian was puzzled. "I can investigate it myself; why ask my brother?"

Li Xuanba lowered his voice. "If it really is a frame-up, then this matter might not just be aimed at you; it might also be aimed at the Crown Prince."

Yang Jian was stunned, then his anger flared. "Is it a frame-up against me or the Crown Prince?! Father only has two sons; what are they trying to do!"

Li Xuanba quickly said, "Please be careful with your words, Your Highness. I am only speculating; perhaps it’s just a misunderstanding."

Yang Jian stood up and paced back and forth with his hands behind his back, the more he thought, the more it made sense.

"Father indeed wouldn't blame me without cause. I was angry before because Father scolded me for things I didn't do. I felt wronged, so I didn't want to explain. Could it be that someone is really ruining my reputation outside? And wants to frame the Crown Prince?" Yang Jian said angrily. "Damn it! Who did this!"

Li Xuanba said, "Exactly. Don't you know? There are even rumors outside that you are having an affair with your sister-in-law, and they are so detailed. How could that be possible!"

Yang Jian stopped in his tracks.

Li Xuanba sighed. "Your late wife has passed away. If you really took a fancy to one of her sisters, the position of Princess is vacant, and a lady of the Wei clan is of high enough status to be a proper successor. Why would you need an 'affair'? It’s just too absurd."

The late Princess of Qi, like the Crown Princess, was from the Jingzhao Wei clan, but they were distant relatives; their grandfathers were brothers.

However, the eldest son of the Prince of Qi was born to the late Princess. There was also a struggle for status within the Wei clan. That was why the Crown Princess was always wary, fearing that some in the Wei clan supported the Prince of Qi.

Yang Jian: "...Yes, it is." He had no guilty conscience at all.

Yang Jian swore to the heavens that he had no affair with any of his sisters-in-law.

*Ahem*, because the one he was having an affair with was his sister-in-law who had already married into the Yuan clan.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第47章 李玄霸婚事波折
chunks.chineseText:
第47章 李玄霸婚事波折

=
　　杨暕离开的脚步都是飘着的。
　　李玄霸觉得他不仅是心虚， 整个人都虚了。
　　李世民下课回家，正好在门口撞见齐王。
　　他一眼就瞅出了杨暕有点不对劲，立刻跑到弟弟身边询问有没有什么好玩的事。
　　李玄霸：【确实蛮好玩。】
　　他用心声把今日之事简略告诉了李世民， 着重提了小姨子和大姨子的事。
　　他当然知道杨暕偷的是大姨子， 不是小姨子， 后来偷人的事还会成为他被软禁的导火|索。
　　杨昭原本应该大业二年去世。按照常理，杨暕就该被立为太子。
　　当时杨广也确实将杨昭府中包括官吏、护卫在内的几万人全部交给杨暕。天下都以为齐王杨暕会被立为太子，勋贵官僚都围绕在杨暕身边讨好杨暕。
　　杨暕现在的行事虽奢侈， 但还算有章法，御下也没有太无能。他的坏毛病都是在太子死后才被杨广养起来。
　　毕竟现在他才二十二岁，目前还没有弟弟出生， 身为皇帝唯一的儿子，他哪经得起别人的恭维。杨广又是个不着家的， 连大兴城都不肯回， 几乎没有管教过杨暕，杨暕后来越来越蠢很正常。
　　更惨的是，杨广一边将太子的待遇和权力都给了杨暕，一边十年不立太子。
　　杨暕的心态从乖乖等当太子变成了惊疑不定，后来在杨广的幼子和杨昭的孩子逐渐长大后， 惊疑变成了惊恐。
　　杨暕琢磨，难道父皇还想传位给兄长的儿子， 越过自己这一辈不成？
　　自己不仅是嫡子，才干和功劳都有，父皇若是让孙子继位， 别说杨暕心里憋屈， 这是要命的事。
　　杨暕很早就和妻子已经嫁为元氏妇的姐姐勾搭上了， 就等着元氏妇的丈夫什么死， 好把守寡的元氏妇接进王府。
　　他心里焦急，又不敢有其他动作，就天天和元氏妇找些僧道方士诅咒杨昭的儿子早逝，然后说些自己一定会当太子、当皇帝的谶纬之语自我安慰。
　　杨广得知此事后，一拍大腿，这小子果然不是好东西，就把元氏妇赐死，软禁了杨暕。
　　李玄霸：【后世许多人说杨暕是蠢死的，不过以我看来，当杨广认为他有谋夺皇位的野心时，他最好真的有。】
　　李世民瞠目结舌。
　　他只是想回来听个乐子，这个“乐子”也太大了吧？
　　李世民用手捂着嘴，压低声音含糊不清道：“我怎么觉得他找僧道行巫蛊之术时，精神已经不正常了？不过，是个人被磨十年，都会被磨出点问题来。”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　他认识了齐王，见到杨暕如今的模样后，也觉得杨暕在被杨广发现“不臣之心”时，已经心理不正常了。
　　杨暕从小就饱受祖父母和父母的喜爱，杨昭也宠着这个弟弟。不然他也不会胆子大到天天和杨昭说夺嫡的蠢话。
　　他一生都十分顺利，连太子病逝，也是他人生十分顺利的体现。
　　嫡长子去世了，嫡次子不差，又受父母喜爱，正常人都会认为是嫡次子继位。何况太子杨昭的儿子都还十分年幼，不知道活不活得成。
　　杨广也确实将太子杨昭的一切政治资源都交给了杨暕。
　　谁知道，杨广就卡着“太子”这个名号不肯给。
　　大业十一年的时候，杨暕都还带兵保卫被突厥人围了的杨广。那时杨暕都是以齐王之身行太子之事。
　　但杨广就是不让杨暕当太子，就是忌惮这个儿子，就是把一个天不怕地不怕的天之骄子活生生磨成了疑神疑鬼的精神病。
　　李世民抱着脑袋，想得脑袋左歪右歪，也想不出当今皇帝为何将来会那么做。
　　总不可能他和杨暕这个儿子有仇？
　　不对啊，现在齐王杨暕可受宠了。
　　“好可怜。”李世民想不明白，就放下手懒得想了，“现在阿玄让他谨言慎行，他的结局会好些吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“不知道。但至少他府中那些人祸害的人会少一些。”
　　李玄霸不同情杨暕。
　　杨暕府中那些人干的伤天害理的混账事太多了。他有这样的下场是业力回馈。那些被齐王府的宵小祸害的百姓才是真的惨。
　　所以他劝说杨暕，除了卖杨暕一个好，哪日杨昭死了之后，让杨暕继续给他当“保护|伞”之外，就是让他约束一下府中人，少祸害一点百姓。
　　至少在大业十一年前，虽然杨广不让他当太子，但杨暕仍旧是杨广重用的好儿子。杨广出巡时，杨暕时常镇守京城或者东都。
　　过了大业十一年，李渊出任太原镇守，他们就要准备招兵买马谋反了。
　　李世民使劲点头：“对！这件事才最重要！”
　　他点完头后，勾着弟弟的肩膀挤眉弄眼唏嘘：“他还真和别人的妻子好上了？至于吗？齐王长得又不丑。”
　　李玄霸瞥了二哥一眼。
　　好吧，就算是小学生，也会对这些事感兴趣。
　　不怪李世民会唏嘘。杨暕今年才二十二岁，又长得极其俊美，走到路上都有不少女子透过冪离给他抛媚眼。他会和比他年纪大的元氏妇勾搭在一起，实在是匪夷所思。
　　李玄霸道：“有一种爱好叫熟女，还有一种爱好叫曹贼之风。”
　　李世民居然听懂了。他大受震撼！
　　李世民认真道：“我还是喜欢同龄人！”
　　李玄霸无语：“你连九岁都没有，想什么呢？”
　　不过唐太宗的确喜欢少女，这是史籍盖章的。李世民对妃嫔的品阶很吝啬，后期升了份位的妃嫔都是少女。
　　李世民和李玄霸叽里咕噜说了一些年少慕艾的事，然后提到了窦夫人给李玄霸找亲家的困难。
　　勋贵和世家的女儿差不多九岁之前就会把亲事全部定完。女子订亲时一般找同龄或者比自己稍大的男子。
　　李玄霸马上就要到九岁，现在正是选亲家的时候。
　　勋贵和世家合适的女儿家就那么一点，李玄霸九岁的时候选同样九岁的，十岁的时候选比自己小一岁的，这样依次递推，可能要选个好几年才能选到合适的。
　　李建成十三岁才选人家，是因为李建成是唐国公府的嫡长子，妻子人选需要更挑剔一些。
　　但李渊当时虽有爵位，身上没有实职，很难给李建成选一个合适的。所以等李渊出任地方官，身上有了实职之后，才开始为李建成张罗。
　　李建成身上将来有唐国公的爵位，只要李渊在朝中的地位上去了，世家勋贵是不会在意自家女儿和李建成的年龄差。
　　别说差个十几二十岁，夸张一些，若是窦夫人此刻去世了，他们将十岁左右的女儿订给李渊做继室，他们都是肯的。
　　李玄霸只是唐国公府的次子，在世家勋贵那里就不是很走俏了。
　　再者李玄霸可能活不过弱冠，窦夫人急着给李玄霸早早定下亲事，十六岁准时娶妻生子留下香火。所以窦夫人对此事很焦虑。
　　李世民从老师那里听到这件事后，立刻来告诉李玄霸。
　　他本以为弟弟会害羞，没想到李玄霸的表情很漠然。
　　李世民疑惑：“阿玄，难道你不开心吗？你也要有妻子了！”
　　李玄霸：“八字还没有一撇呢，开心什么。”
　　李世民叹气：“好吧，你也确实不能太开心，否则我接下来的话一定会让你难过。”
　　李玄霸挑眉：“怎么？难道我的婚事还能有波折？父亲现在正是陛下面前的宠臣，我在陛下面前也很得宠，难道还有人看不上我？”
　　李世民将手肘放在腿上，手撑着下巴唉声叹气道：“不知道谁把你活不到弱冠的事传了出去，现在京中的人似乎都知道了。”
　　李玄霸微微一愣。
　　他不在意这件事，传出去就传出去了，反正是事实。而且他相信自己的母亲也不会坑亲家，会提前告诉他们自己病弱的事实。
　　但公开的秘密也是秘密，谁会宣扬这件事？这不是和唐国公府结仇吗？
　　说难听些，难道世家勋贵不知道自己身体差，不知道孙医师曾说自己活不到弱冠吗？
　　他们当然是知道的。但他们选择联姻的时候，不会太看重这个因素。
　　他们与唐国公府联姻，只要将不得宠或者旁支的女儿嫁进来，与唐国公府有个联系即可。
　　再说了，若有了儿子，自己的妻子在唐国公府肯定过得不错，只需要开开心心供养儿子成才，说不定比大多数贵妇都舒坦；若没有儿子，如今又不歧视寡妇，嫁过显贵人家的寡妇有时候比未婚女子更抢手，回家再嫁就是。
　　所以李玄霸的婚事，只要要求不太高，只看门扉不看父母地位，其实是不难的。
　　但这“公开的秘密”被公开后，事情就不一样了。
　　这件事世家勋贵本来不会在乎，但外面都传遍了，他们就必须表现得在乎了。不然在外人看来，他们就是把族中女儿送给一个注定会早夭的病秧子，是折辱自己门扉、自甘下贱的事。
　　除非李玄霸真的优秀到能造就“虽然此人病弱，但才华横溢，我女儿甘愿嫁给他”的佳话，否则他是别想讨到合适的妻子了。
　　古代都是盲婚哑嫁，琴瑟和鸣者极其罕见。李玄霸知道自己会早早订婚，到时就学二哥，婚前与妻子多通信，尽力而为培养感情就成，对妻子的家世一点都不在意。
　　但唐国公府会很在意。
　　这事已经和李玄霸无关，而是有人针对唐国公府，打李渊和窦夫人的脸。
　　李玄霸皱眉：“谁这么无聊？难道是嫉妒？”
　　李世民道：“老师也说可能是嫉妒。唉，谁让我家阿玄太优秀了。”
　　李玄霸摇头：“我若真的足够优秀，这点小伎俩就不会奏效了。”
　　李世民撑着下巴道：“本来已经有了许多人家接触娘亲，现在那些人家都说没有合适的女儿。唉，你的婚事真坎坷啊。”
　　李玄霸道：“只要父亲的官职再往上提一步，那些说没有合适女儿的人家就会来告诉母亲，家里平白多出个合适的女儿了。”
　　李世民频频点头：“是的，都是耶耶太没用了。自家儿子连合适的亲事都订不到。”
　　李渊就在门外，脸色精彩极了。
　　窦夫人站在李渊身侧，用袖子捂着嘴，让自己别笑出声来。
　　孙子只需要给祖父母守一年的孝，李世民和李玄霸马上要出孝期了。
　　杨广想起了这两个孩子，说要接他们二人来洛阳。
　　李渊趁此机会早早请假，先回家和家人们一同过完年，再带李世民和李玄霸去洛阳面圣。
　　李渊悄悄回家，没有惊动任何人。
　　他听李世民回来之后，蹑手蹑脚来到儿子这里，想给二儿子和三儿子一个惊喜。
　　李世民和李玄霸之前说杨暕的事他没听到，他刚走到门口，就听见李世民在说“耶耶没用”。
　　李世民的声音超大，嗓门极其洪亮，李渊在门外都听到了。
　　李渊气得轻轻跺脚：“李二郎！”
　　窦夫人促狭道：“二郎难道说错了？若郎君再厉害些，三郎何至于找不到合适的亲家？”
　　李渊的脸涨得通红：“惹急了我，我去求陛下赐婚！”
　　窦夫人道：“你还想让三郎娶公主不成？”
　　李渊梗着脖子道：“怎么？我家三郎难道娶不得公主？”
　　窦夫人嫌弃地瞥了丈夫一眼。她知道丈夫是面子过不去，在说胡话。
　　别说现在没有年龄合适的公主，就是有，皇帝也不可能把公主赐给病弱的三郎。
　　赐给二郎倒是有可能。还好二郎早早定下了亲事。
　　窦夫人道：“此事郎君确实要上心一些。唉，三郎若没本事一些，我就不这么愁了，选一个次一点的就行。”
　　其实还是有很多人家接触窦夫人，愿意和李三郎订亲，但窦夫人不乐意。
　　自家三郎样样优秀，就是那身体，孙医师也说了，现在三郎身体好多了，应该能活过弱冠。窦夫人可不愿给三郎挑差了。
　　李渊点头：“我去问问。大不了我又拉着哪个同僚比射箭。”
　　窦夫人忍笑道：“怎么，你能给二郎赢来一个小未婚妻，还能再给三郎赢来一个？”
　　李渊得意：“那可说不定。”
　　说完，他转身离开。
　　窦夫人疑惑：“不去看二郎三郎了？”
　　李渊冷哼：“看什么看？去把大雄提起来揍一顿吗！”
　　窦夫人失笑。
　　李渊郁闷极了。就算这真的是耶耶还不够厉害，大雄你也不能这么说啊！我怎么会有你这样的儿子！
　　虽然李渊没来见李世民和李玄霸，但用晚膳的时候，一家人还是见面了。
　　李世民仍旧甜甜地叫“耶耶”，挂在李渊脖子上不松手。
　　李渊又是高兴又是郁闷。
　　早知道他当时就推门进去，看看揭穿二儿子在自己背后说坏话时，二儿子是个什么反应。现在他却不好再提起下午的事了。
　　李玄霸仍旧恭敬地和李渊行礼，做足了一个礼仪周到的孝顺儿子模样。
　　他在李渊面前一直都是那样，礼数和乖巧永远很足。那一点点疏离，只有李世民和窦夫人觉察了一丝，其他人完全没发现。
　　现在的父子感情差不多都是内敛的，李建成对李渊也很恭敬，李元吉和李智云则对李渊有些惧怕。所以李玄霸这样的表现，在李渊面前都算是比较亲近了。
　　如李世民和李渊那样黏黏糊糊，李渊出门时父子二人抱头痛哭的奇葩相处方式，才叫怪异。
　　看现在，李世民在李渊怀里坐着玩李渊的胡须，比李世民更年幼的李元吉和李智云则跑得远远的，完全不想靠近严肃的父亲。
　　李世民撒了一会儿娇，李渊就原谅了李世民在背后说他坏话。
　　他甚至觉得，二儿子其实也不是说坏话，而是为他打抱不平，说他职位还不够高，权势还不够大，居然有人欺负唐国公府。
　　李渊对李玄霸招了招手。
　　李玄霸走到李渊身边。
　　李渊揉了揉李玄霸的脑袋：“大德放心，你的亲事为父来定。看为父也给你赢个妻子回来。”
　　李玄霸恭敬道：“谢父亲。”
　　李世民嘟着嘴道：“耶耶啊，你这话好像土匪头子，想要强抢民女给阿玄当妻子。”
　　李渊一巴掌拍到李世民脑袋上。
　　窦夫人伸手捏了一下李世民的嘴唇，把李世民的嘴捏得像鸭子嘴：“你可闭嘴吧。”
　　其他人都忍俊不禁。李玄霸都忍不住勾了勾嘴角。
　　别说，李渊这话听着还真的挺像土匪头子。
　　李渊可不是开玩笑。
　　他回来后，每日都去拜访京中勋贵，找人比射箭拉近感情。
　　长孙晟也从突厥回来，提前请假回家过年。
　　他自从发现嫡长子有些不着调之后，就十分焦急儿子的教育问题。自己的仕途大概也差不多到头了，儿子不行，长孙府刚起色就要没落。
　　他还没有赚到爵位，指望下一代给自己这一支长孙氏赚爵位呢！
　　所以杨广无事后，长孙晟急急忙忙向皇帝请假，回家继续严格教育儿子。
　　他一回来，就发现儿子故态复萌，在他离开的时间对继室和幼子十分不好。
　　长孙晟找到自己的兄长叹气：“我担心他会在我死后欺辱继母和弟弟。”
　　长孙晟的兄长也不好说什么，只让长孙晟好好教导儿子，别操太多心，儿孙自有儿孙福。
　　长孙晟思来想去，未来自己一对年幼儿女可能只能托付给唐国公府了。
　　女儿已经和李世民订婚，儿子又是李世民好友。如果他们将来真的被分家，李世民厉害一些，或许能带着他们过上稍好的日子。
　　长孙晟便把李世民拎到家中，严格教导李世民的武艺，并把自己经略突厥的本事灌输给李世民。
　　李世民的课业又加重了，回家头昏脑涨，连皮一下的精力都没有了。
　　他和小伙伴们的聚会也改在了唐国公府。
　　李世民把脸砸在桌案上，有气无力道：“长孙四郎，你才是你父亲的儿子，你能不能告诉你父亲，让他好好教导你，别折磨我。我虽然聪慧，但也不能事事都学。”
　　长孙无忌憋屈道：“你以为我没说吗？但父亲考校了我的学问后，就丢给我几本书，让我背熟了再教我。”
　　房乔和杜如晦好奇长孙晟教了李世民什么。
　　长孙晟在当世十分有名。谁不敬仰他孤身在突厥的经历？这是一个被曾经还没有分裂的突厥可汗看中，扣下留到身边，陪突厥可汗打猎好几年的英雄人物。
　　李世民掰着手指道：“现在主要是背突厥谱系。天啦，我连唐国公府的姻亲谱系都快忘记了，为什么我还要背突厥谱系？”
　　李玄霸放下水杯，道：“我现在身体差不多好了。下次长孙将军授课，我陪你一起去。”
　　李世民立刻支棱起来，握着李玄霸的双手道：“太好了！阿玄！等丈人再考我的时候，你一定要帮我作弊！”
　　李玄霸无奈：“哥，你能不能别老想着作弊？”
　　难道是自己的错吗？唐太宗怎么能是一个喜欢作弊的人！
　　李世民哭丧着脸道：“你以为我想吗？我也想凭借自己的努力啊，但学得真的太多了，太多了，太多了，我的脑袋要裂开了！”
　　说完，李世民就抱着脑袋使劲晃：“要裂开了。”
　　房乔疑惑：“为何不告诉长孙将军？长孙将军应该不是揠苗助长的人。”
　　李世民抱着脑袋道：“我才不好意思呢。”
　　李玄霸道：“他好面子。而且他确实有能力每次都完成功课。所以长孙将军就给他继续授课了。”
　　房乔失笑：“不肯示弱，那就没办法了。”
　　杜如晦嘲笑道：“李二认为脸面更重要，那就继续努力吧。李三，你可不能帮李二作弊。既然李二能熬过去，还是让他自己熬过去吧。”
　　李玄霸道：“放心，我绝对不会……哎哟！”
　　李世民一把捧住弟弟的脑袋使劲摇晃：“你还是不是我弟弟了！阿玄，你怎么能这样对我！”
　　李玄霸任由二哥摇晃，就是不开口。
　　房乔、杜如晦和长孙无忌皆笑得前俯后仰，不断揉肚子。
　　李玄霸不仅不肯作弊，等见到了长孙晟后，还向长孙晟“告状”。
　　长孙晟无奈：“李二郎你啊，若功课太重，为何不和我说？”
　　李世民道：“我还能撑住。我只是给弟弟开玩笑。”
　　他嘴里这么说，不断在心里【啊！！！！】，愤怒地指责李玄霸。
　　李玄霸不动如山，就当没听见。
　　长孙晟道：“若真的撑不住，就告诉我。”
　　李世民恭敬道：“是。”
　　“哎哟！”一个粉色的小团子从屏风后面滚了出来。
　　李世民和李玄霸齐刷刷地把视线投了过去。
　　穿着粉色袄裙，脖子上围着一圈白色毛绒绒围脖的小团子，捂着脸跪坐在地上，声音俏生生：“看不见我，看不见我。”
　　李世民好奇道：“这位妹妹是？”
　　长孙晟扶额，咬牙切齿：“长孙无忌！”
　　长孙无忌从屏风后面跳出来：“不关我事啊！不是我推的！是妹妹自己脚滑了！”
　　李玄霸惊讶地睁大眼睛，不断打量地上捂着脸的粉团子。
　　李世民先是一愣，赶紧跑上前把粉团子扶起来：“你是观音婢？摔着呢？摔到哪了？长孙四郎，你愣着干什么！都不知道扶一下吗！”
　　长孙晟和长孙无忌都呆住。没想到李世民居然这么不见外。
　　李玄霸嘴角上弯。
　　长孙小妹捂着脸站起来。
　　她先张开指缝偷瞧李世民。
　　李世民笑道：“我就在这里，要看就看，不用遮掩。”
　　长孙小妹红着脸放下手，低下头，手指绞着袖口。
　　李世民惊讶地转头对李玄霸道：“阿玄，好神奇，虽然是第一次见面，但这个妹妹我总感觉好亲切，好像见过！”
　　李玄霸差点咬到舌头。
　　什么“这个妹妹我曾见过”？！你以为你是李宝玉吗！！
