Chapter 51: Arrogant in Public, Humble in Private

Li Xuanba looked at Yang Jishan with a puzzled expression.
Did he have any conflict of interest with the Duke of Chu’s household? Why was this man sneering? Was he born with a naturally mocking face?
While Li Xuanba was lost in thought, Yang Jian and Yang Jishan had already begun a verbal sparring match, their words sharp and barbed.
From their exchange, combined with the lessons Gao Jiong had once taught him, Li Xuanba managed to piece together why Yang Jishan held such animosity toward him.
Yang Jishan was his courtesy name; his given name was Yang Xuande. He was the youngest brother of the current Duke of Chu, Yang Xuangan. Despite his youth, he had been granted the title of *Shang Yitong Sansi* (Senior Official of the Ceremonial Guard) due to the meritorious service of his father, the late Duke of Chu, Yang Su.
The *Shang Yitong Sansi* was a "scattered" honorary rank—a vestige of the Northern Zhou dynasty’s military merit system, specifically bestowed upon the scions of the Guanlong aristocratic group.
The Sui dynasty’s officialdom was incredibly complex, consisting of three distinct systems: honorary ranks (*san shi guan*), non-functional ranks (*san guan*), and functional posts (*zhi guan*).
Functional posts were positions with real power, which needed no explanation.
Non-functional ranks were a continuation of the Wei and Jin dynasties’ clan-based system, where one’s official status was determined directly by family lineage. The saying "no poor scholars in the upper ranks" referred to these positions.
Since the Wei and Jin eras, these non-functional ranks served as an official’s "base grade." Regardless of what functional post one held, their official standing was determined by this base grade. This was why one often saw high-ranking, powerful officials from humble backgrounds bowing and scraping before aristocratic scions who held no real power.
Honorary ranks were a new system created by the Western Wei’s Guanlong military clique to bypass the old Shandong aristocratic families. They replaced the "non-functional ranks" as the "base grade" for officials, effectively serving as the "hereditary privilege" for the Guanlong nobility.
After the Sui dynasty was established, the Guanlong nobles held political power and privilege, while the old Shandong families controlled local influence and scholarly talent. The conflict between them was sharp, and one of its manifestations was the constant adjustment of the status between honorary and non-functional ranks.
Emperor Yang Guang saw this, slapped his forehead, and in the third year of the Daye era, abolished the names of the honorary ranks and the non-functional rank system, merging them into one.
For example, Yang Xuande’s original rank of *Shang Yitong Sansi* (a rank-4b position) was renamed to *Tongyi Dafu* (also rank-4b).
From the non-functional ranks held by Yang Xuande, Li Xuanba, and Li Shimin, one could see that while both were from ducal households, the Tang Duke’s mansion could not compare to the Duke of Chu’s. For a powerful ducal house like the Duke of Chu’s, the initial rank granted to a son by hereditary privilege was the rank-4b *Shang Yitong Sansi*.
Yang Guang’s diagnosis of the problem was accurate, but his method of solving it was completely wrong—much like a doctor who correctly identifies an illness but prescribes the wrong medicine.
With this change, the military nobility was furious.
High-ranking honorary officials like the *Shang Zhuguo* (Supreme Pillar of State) were entitled to establish their own offices and recruit subordinates, a privilege they retained even after retirement. Now that their titles had been converted to civil honorary ranks, they were forced to disband their subordinates the moment they retired, becoming nothing more than idle old men drawing a pension.
The civil officials, primarily from the old aristocratic families, were also unhappy.
Although the names of the non-functional ranks were preserved, the promotion criteria were now based on the honorary rank system. The Sui dynasty stipulated that these ranks could only be obtained through meritorious service to the court, which was difficult for the old civil aristocracy to achieve.
The Guanlong nobility had grown increasingly resentful of Yang Guang since last year’s reforms. Yang Guang knew they hated him, so he promoted his own confidants to suppress the old guard of the Guanlong group.
The Tang Duke’s lineage originally belonged to the old Guanlong nobility, but while the others were being suppressed, Li Yuan had risen to prominence by pandering to the Emperor.
Look at the "good deeds" Li Xuanba had done.
He restored ancient prescriptions as tribute for the Emperor, wrote lyrics because the Emperor enjoyed music, and instead of using his hereditary privilege to enter office, he took the imperial examinations and called himself a "disciple of the Son of Heaven"... The former was fine—flattering the Emperor wasn't shameful, and other nobles did it too. But that last point? It made him a traitor to the nobility!
Although Li Xuanba was young, the nobles all assumed this was Li Yuan’s idea, and that Li Xuanba was merely a tool used to curry favor with the Emperor.
Regardless of how the Duke of Chu and the court nobles schemed against each other, the "Duke of Chu" lineage remained the representative of the Guanlong military group. Even after Yang Su’s death, this would not change.
But since he had met Li Xuanba, Yang Xuande naturally had to put on a cold face to show his disdain.
As Yang Xuande and Yang Jian engaged in their "friendly and cordial" exchange, the banquet circle subtly split into three factions.
Behind Yang Xuande, those watching with cold eyes were almost all scions of the military nobility. The expressions of the old Shandong aristocratic scions clearly showed they were there to watch the show, while the scions of the Jiangnan families and non-noble bureaucratic families stood on the side of the Prince of Qi.
Li Shimin’s fists were clenched; he looked like he wanted to go over and give Yang Xuande a few blows.
Li Xuanba, however, felt a smile tugging at the corners of his mouth. He found it quite interesting.
The political situation of the imperial court was being laid bare at a small banquet for young nobles—was that not fascinating?
Though Li Xuanba was small, he was the catalyst for this "friendly" exchange, so everyone kept a portion of their attention on him.
When Li Xuanba smiled, Yang Xuande immediately said with dissatisfaction, "What are you laughing at?"
Li Xuanba looked puzzled. "His Highness the Prince of Qi invited us to gather. It’s such a happy occasion; if I don’t laugh, should I cry instead?"
Li Shimin, who had been clenching his fists, turned to look at his younger brother with a helpless expression.
Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, laughed aloud. "Exactly! Shouldn't you be laughing at my banquet?"
Yang Xuande looked at Li Xuanba with utter contempt, the words "sycophant" practically written on his face.
Li Xuanba said to Yang Jian, "Cousin, don't lower yourself to his level. It is a fact that I am both sickly and young, and I can neither draw a heavy bow nor throw a 'valiant arrow'."
Li Shimin crossed his arms and snorted, "Your Duke of Chu household certainly has fine manners, mocking even this. It seems your family members were never sick, and were born as full-grown adults, never having to go through the process of growing up from childhood."
It was none of Xue Shou’s business, but his temper was much like his father’s, Xue Daoheng. Unable to stand by, he spoke up righteously, "One should treat the young of others as one treats one's own. Brother Yang, this behavior is uncalled for."
The three of them sang in harmony, pinning Yang Xuande’s actions to the act of "mocking a young child."
Yang Xuande was about to retort when someone behind him tugged on his sleeve.
The reckless anger on Yang Xuande’s face vanished as if it were an illusion. He cupped his hands and said, "I had no such intention."
Just moments ago, during his "friendly" exchange with the Prince of Qi, Yang Xuande hadn't yielded an inch. Yet, when Li Xuanba, Li Shimin, and Xue Shou spoke up, he suddenly became polite and took a step back.
The atmosphere shifted so quickly that not only were the onlookers confused, but Li Xuanba, the party involved, was also left scratching his head.
Li Shimin had been ready to jump into a fight. Regardless of whether he could win, if someone bullied his brother, he was going to throw hands first.
Now that Yang Xuande had apologized, Li Shimin felt the breath catch in his chest, his face turning a deep crimson.
Li Xuanba: [Brother, let it go. He didn't really mock anything, just sneered. No need to hold a grudge.]
Li Shimin snorted.
Li Xuanba: [I am more curious as to why he used me as a stepping stone to argue with the Prince of Qi. What exactly is he trying to test?]
Li Shimin frowned, forcing himself to calm down.
Once the anger receded from his mind, Li Shimin also keenly noticed that after that initial sneer at his brother, Yang Xuande had focused entirely on targeting the Prince of Qi.
Xue Shou was still filled with righteous indignation.
After Li Shimin calmed down, he and Li Xuanba pulled Xue Shou to the side.
Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, didn't want to let it go just like that, but the surrounding noble scions swarmed over to mediate. Yang Xuande also adopted the demeanor of "I was brainless just now, but I've apologized now that I've cooled down; I meant no harm," and drank a penalty cup of wine.
Although Yang Jian felt stifled, there was nothing he could do about Yang Xuande.
Yang Jian knew that Yang Su had been forced to his death by the Emperor. But the fact that the Emperor had so gently waited for Yang Su to die of illness meant that the Duke of Chu’s lineage could not be touched.
Yang Su could die, but the Duke of Chu could not.
The new Duke of Chu, Yang Xuangan, did not possess the power Yang Su once held and was no longer feared by the Emperor. Therefore, if they acted foolishly and arrogantly, it would be difficult for Yang Jian to reprimand them.
Yang Jian was not stupid; he was just too lazy to think. After careful consideration, he roughly guessed why Yang Xuande wanted to play the role of a brainless brute at his banquet to offend him.
Thinking of it that way, he became even angrier.
Who did they think they were looking down on!
Using the excuse of dragging away the still-arguing Xue Shou, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba retreated with him to a secluded corner of the banquet.
Yang Jian’s banquet was held in the garden, with wine, games, and servants everywhere, much like a modern-day garden party. Guests could gather in small groups to do as they pleased.
The three of them hid in a pavilion within a bamboo grove. The pavilion was equipped with servants, a stove, drinks, pastries, and various board games.
They set up the chessboard, dismissed the servants, and began to play, venting their frustrations through the game.
The anger on Xue Shou’s face had yet to fade, as if he were the one who had been insulted.
Li Xuanba, however, remained calm from start to finish, causing Li Shimin to glance at him several times, feeling quite dissatisfied.
While playing against Xue Shou, Li Xuanba asked his brother, who was watching, "Why are you glaring at me?"
Li Shimin said, "A-Xuan, you need to have some backbone. It’s just the Duke of Chu’s household; we are also the sons of a Duke!"
Xue Shou nodded while placing a piece. "Exactly, exactly."
Li Xuanba said helplessly, "He just sneered once, and didn't we mock him back? Tit for tat is enough. Should I have punched him just because he laughed at me?"
Li Shimin clenched his fist. "You should have punched him!"
Xue Shou echoed, "Exactly, exactly, should have hit him hard!"
Li Xuanba was speechless. He knew his brother had a fiery temper, but why was Xue Shou the same?
Xue Shou had only just met Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, yet he was echoing them as if he understood Li Xuanba perfectly.
Li Xuanba rubbed his forehead. Xue Shou, was your past life Zhang Fei? The guy who always said, "Me too!"?
Was this the same Grand Academician of the Prince of Qin’s mansion who was only mentioned in a few lines in the history books?
"Of course I’m not just letting it go... He’s coming." Li Xuanba held a black piece and tapped the sandalwood chessboard.
Modern Go rules, established by a certain island nation, dictate that black goes first. But in ancient China, white always went first, followed by black.
The rustling sound of boots treading on bamboo leaves echoed.
Li Shimin and Xue Shou stopped complaining and turned toward the sound of footsteps.
Yang Xuande had not brought the lackeys who usually followed him; he came through the dense bamboo grove alone.
Yang Xuande heard Li Xuanba’s words and asked curiously, "Did Third Young Master Li know I would come?"
Li Xuanba said, "I didn't know. I simply observed that you are not a reckless man. If you hold us in any regard, you would naturally come quietly."
In ancient times, anyone from the Three Excellencies to a Commandery Governor could have a "cabinet," so "Your Excellency" (*Ge Xia*) was a respectful term for officials of higher status. After the collapse of etiquette during the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties, the term was now commonly used among commoners as well.
Li Xuanba calling Yang Xuande "Your Excellency" was respectful but not fawning. That single term made Yang Xuande feel Li Xuanba’s goodwill.
Yang Xuande bowed deeply, his upper body nearly parallel to the ground. "Scholar Li, I offended you earlier. I was truly helpless."
Li Shimin looked at Yang Xuande’s current demeanor and asked suspiciously, "What do you mean 'helpless'? Is there anyone who could force you?"
Li Xuanba stepped down from the mat and helped Yang Xuande up. "I was quite angry, but seeing that you are even more miserable than I am, I am no longer angry."
Yang Xuande gave a bitter smile.
After hearing his brother’s plan, he had originally thought, *Why go to such lengths for a mere scholar?*
Li Xuanba’s earlier composure and his current display of foresight made him sigh inwardly. His brother’s judgment was indeed the best.
"I will send a gift of apology later," Yang Xuande said. "I came to apologize alone just to let you two know that the Duke of Chu’s household has no intention of opposing the Tang Duke’s household."
He thought for a moment and spoke more bluntly: "The nobility is somewhat dissatisfied with His Majesty, so they pushed me out to test the waters. The Duke of Chu’s household is in decline; we dare not offend anyone. *Sigh*."
Li Shimin frowned. "You dare not offend them, but are you not afraid of offending His Majesty, who stands behind us?"
Li Xuanba glanced at his brother. His brother was getting very good at using the "fox borrowing the tiger's might" tactic.
Yang Xuande continued to smile bitterly. "We are jealous that the second and third young masters of the Li family have won His Majesty’s favor; how could we offend His Majesty?"
He bowed again. "I deeply admire Scholar Li’s talent and had no intention of mocking you. Please forgive me."
Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba.
Li Xuanba said, "We are both of the nobility; it was just a common squabble. Let it pass; no need to take it to heart. Brother, Xue, wait for me a moment. I will see Brother Yang off."
Yang Xuande wanted to refuse. "This..."
Li Xuanba interrupted, "I disturbed the Prince of Qi’s mood; I will go with you to apologize to His Highness. It will be better for both of us. Those nobles who pushed you out will also be happy to see us reconcile."
Yang Xuande hesitated, remembered his brother’s instructions, and nodded. "Very well."
Li Shimin watched Li Xuanba leave, full of confusion.
He looked at Xue Shou. "Brother Xue, can you guess what A-Xuan is thinking? Why is he suddenly so polite to Yang Jishan?"
Xue Shou rubbed his temples. "You are Li Third’s brother; if you can't guess, how could I? I only know it seems like a lot of trouble. *Sigh*, I kind of regret getting involved."
Li Shimin laughed. "Too late. By the way, you are from the Xue clan of Hedong in Guanzhong; do you know Du Ruhui of the Jingzhao Du clan?"
Xue Shou said, "I don't."
Li Shimin said, "You don't, but you can meet him now. I have two good friends in the capital, both over twenty but under thirty: one is Du Ruhui, courtesy name Keming, and the other is Fang Qiao, courtesy name Xuanling. Both are great talents. I think if you met them, you would surely consider them kindred spirits."
Li Shimin briefly introduced Du Ruhui and Fang Qiao.
Xue Shou showed no interest in Du Ruhui of the Jingzhao Du clan, but he was very interested in Fang Qiao, who came from a second-tier aristocratic family.
Xue Shou said, "Is Fang Xuanling the son of Uncle Fang? I should go meet him!"
Li Shimin was curious. "Brother Xue knows Xuanling’s father?"
Xue Shou explained, "Uncle Fang was a good friend of my father’s. But I was adopted at a young age and didn't often serve by my father’s side, so I never got to know Uncle Fang. However, my father often mentioned him in his letters, telling me to learn from Uncle Fang’s integrity and uprightness."
Li Shimin clapped his hands and laughed. "Uncle Fang and Uncle Xue were good friends; it is only fitting that Brother Xue and Xuanling should be friends too! Now that Fang Xuanling and Du Keming have no official duties..."
Xue Shou smiled. "If you host, I will certainly come."
After Li Shimin’s sudden impulse to introduce his friends to Xue Shou, he sighed again. "I wonder what A-Xuan wants to say to Yang Jishan in private."
Xue Shou comforted him, "When Li Third returns, he will surely tell you. Don't worry."
Li Shimin perked up. "Of course! *Sigh*, A-Xuan should have told me beforehand; he really makes one worry."
Seeing Li Shimin complaining about his brother, Xue Shou thought of his own close cousins and couldn't help but chuckle.
In the bamboo grove, Yang Xuande and Li Xuanba walked a few steps before Li Xuanba stopped.
Yang Xuande turned around. "Does Scholar Li have something private to say to me?"
Li Xuanba looked around.
Yang Xuande said, "I had people keep the Prince of Qi occupied. This place is very secluded, and there is no one else. You chose a good spot."
Li Xuanba smiled. "You flatter me."
Yang Xuande curiously sized up this famous Scholar Li, unable to guess what Li Xuanba would say to him.
Li Xuanba lowered his voice. "The fact that the late Duke of Chu was forced to his death is known to all."
Yang Xuande’s heart tightened, and his brow furrowed.
Li Xuanba continued, "As the descendants of dukes, forgive me for offering a reminder: the old Duke of Chu traded his own life to ensure the safety of his descendants. Brother Yang, do not let the old Duke’s intentions go to waste."
Yang Xuande’s eyes were as sharp as an eagle’s, a completely different person from before. "Are you threatening me?!"
Li Xuanba shook his head. "It is merely 'the rabbit dying, the fox grieving'—we are of the same kind."
Yang Xuande was stunned.
Li Xuanba sighed. "As a scion of a ducal house, I have such talent and could enter office through hereditary privilege in a legitimate way. Why would I choose a rocky path? Brother Yang, we are the same."
Li Xuanba cupped his hands. "The nobles mock my Tang Duke’s household for fawning over the Emperor, but when my father inherited the dukedom, he was even younger than I am now, and the Tang Duke’s household had been in decline for decades longer than the Duke of Chu’s. Those nobles were the ones biting at our flesh while we were down. Brother Yang, Duke Yang never kicked us while we were down, which is why I am here to remind you."
Yang Xuande did not speak again. The two left the bamboo grove to apologize to Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, and then, to the disappointment of the guests, reconciled in public.
Yang Xuande remained in the liveliest part of the banquet to exchange cups, while Li Xuanba declined Yang Jian’s invitation and returned to the bamboo grove to find his brother and Xue Shou.
On his way back, he felt that the person hiding in the bamboo grove had already left.
Only then did Li Xuanba’s tense spirit relax, and he felt a wave of exhaustion.
Compared to his frail body, his mental strength was very strong. Aside from allowing him to concentrate more easily and spam his brother with his inner thoughts, this mental strength also made him keenly aware of his surroundings.
If he focused his mental strength, he could vaguely sense the presence of life within a ten-meter radius.
He wasn't particularly sensitive to ordinary animals or insects, but the presence of humans was so strong that he could even simply detect the emotions they leaked.
Based on the few words in history books, it was impossible for Li Xuanba to see through a person’s heart. This keen intuition was his confidence in daring to curry favor with Yang Guang, an unpredictable tyrant.
When Yang Xuande appeared, a strange presence had entered the bamboo grove. It was very close, yet he hadn't seen anyone.
Though the presence was unfamiliar, the feeling it gave Li Xuanba was somewhat familiar. He quickly guessed that this must be an eye sent to monitor Yang Xuande.
Whether this spy was sent by Yang Jian or Yang Guang didn't matter; in the end, all information would converge at Yang Guang’s desk.
When Yang Xuande apologized, he lowered his status significantly and even said he would send a gift of apology later. Li Xuanba realized that Yang Xuande not only didn't want to offend the Tang Duke’s household, but might also be trying to use this contrast—the plight of the Duke of Chu’s household—to win his sympathy.
Perhaps the Duke of Chu’s household wanted to befriend him?
That was a major crisis.
"A-Xuan, you’re back? What did you say to him?" Li Shimin asked with slight anxiety. "He didn't bully you, did he?"
"No," Li Xuanba said. "I just reminded him to be cautious in his words and actions. Both the Duke of Chu’s household and the Tang Duke’s household are subjects of the Emperor; we must prioritize the Emperor."
Li Xuanba: [Damn it! The spy is back!]
Li Shimin heard his brother cursing in his heart, blinked, and yawned. "A-Xuan, there’s nothing fun here. Let’s tell our cousin we’re leaving early. Hmph, I’m still angry! I don’t want to stay here! Brother Xue, do you want to leave together?"
Li Xuanba said, "We have a close relationship with the Prince of Qi, so we can leave early, but don't drag Brother Xue along."
Xue Shou said, "You two go ahead; I’ll stay and drink for a while longer. Li Second, don't forget you promised to introduce me to Fang Xuanling."
Li Shimin said, "And Du Keming. I won't forget. Let’s go, A-Xuan, let’s say goodbye to our cousin. Hmph, that Yang Jishan... Yang Xuande is so annoying!"
Li Shimin took his brother’s hand; his palms were covered in sweat.
Li Xuanba: [Relax.]
Li Shimin squeezed his brother’s hand, winked at him, and gave a relaxed smile.
The two said goodbye to Yang Jian. Li Shimin even leaned into Yang Jian’s ear to whisper a few bad things about Yang Xuande, asking Yang Jian to help him pour a few more cups for Yang Xuande before leaving with Li Xuanba.
In the carriage, Li Shimin wiped the sweat from his palms onto his robes and then rubbed his face vigorously. "It was just a banquet! Was all that necessary!"
Li Xuanba: [It was. The Emperor is worried the Duke of Chu will rebel, and in five years, they really will. Stay away from them.]
Li Shimin turned his head sharply, then clutched his neck and wailed, "My neck, my neck... Ah, it hurts, I pulled a muscle!"
Li Xuanba: "...Pfft."
Li Shimin wailed, "You jerk, A-Xuan! You scared me and then laughed at me?! I don't want you as a brother anymore!"
Li Xuanba covered his mouth and giggled. "I didn't. My mouth didn't even move; I didn't say anything."
Li Shimin clutched his neck, looking resentfully at his mischievous brother.
Just now, when his brother mentioned the rebellion in his heart, was it a slip of the tongue, or was he trying to scare him on purpose?
Good heavens, how could he have such a brother!
Li Shimin’s intuition was also very keen. He had a sharp premonition that as he grew older and his mental fortitude increased, his brother would scare him more and more often.
No! I don't want to hear it!
Li Shimin began to suffer in advance.
Li Xuanba continued to giggle. The anxiety, repression, and frustration of the day dissipated upon hearing his brother’s wails.
As a hater of Emperor Taizong, watching him make a fool of himself was truly the best way to relieve stress.
While the brothers were laughing and chatting in the carriage (Li Shimin: I was not!), the news reached Yang Guang’s ears.
He snorted coldly and sneered, "Third Young Master Li is indeed shrewd... It’s good to be shrewd. I hope Yang Xuangan can be shrewd as well."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第52章 剧透解压真快乐
chunks.chineseText:
第52章 剧透解压真快乐

=
　　李世民又被李玄霸“吓唬”了一番后， 两人没再说话，沉默地回到了家中。
　　李渊还没回来。
　　两个孩子换了衣服后，回屋小睡了一会儿， 补足今日精力的消耗。
　　当李渊来叫他们起床时， 李世民已经恢复了活力， 吊在李渊脖子上，要耶耶休沐时带他去骑马打猎。
　　杨广也好游猎，东都附近有许多禁苑猎场。李世民可馋了。
　　“你这么点大， 还游猎？我担心你被野兽叼走成为猎物。”李渊拍了拍二儿子的屁股，对一旁发呆的李玄霸道，“如果大德想去打猎， 我就带你们去。”
　　李玄霸揉着惺忪的睡眼抬头。和我有什么关系？
　　李世民赶紧道：“阿玄！快帮我求耶耶！”
　　李玄霸强忍着哈欠道：“好，请父亲带二哥去游猎。我留下看家。”
　　他完全不能理解打猎的乐趣。
　　李世民扯着李渊散落的鬓发道：“耶耶， 阿玄太懒了， 一定要带他去打猎。我们李家的人怎么能不喜欢打猎！”
　　李渊把自己的头发从调皮儿子的手中夺回来，煞有其事地点头：“没错！明日耶耶就去找陛下，让他同意我带你们去狩猎！”
　　李玄霸忍不住哈欠了：“我不想去。”
　　李世民嚣张：“由得你想不想？打猎也是功课！”
　　李渊看着早熟的三儿子那满脸不耐的郁闷表情，忍着笑道：“大雄说得对，这是功课。”
　　李玄霸无语地看着这对父子。你们二人就是故意合起来整我吧？
　　李渊把李世民放下来， 把李玄霸抱起来，揉了揉脑袋。
　　李玄霸身体微微一僵， 道：“父亲，我已经长大了。”
　　李渊笑道：“长大了也是我儿子。你们今日发生了什么事？”
　　李世民好奇：“耶耶怎么知道？”
　　李渊瞥了李世民一眼：“以你的人来疯性子，去赴宴却早早回家， 肯定发生了什么。”
　　人来疯？！李世民瞪大眼睛：“什么叫人来疯！耶耶你胡说！”
　　李渊笑道：“是你娘亲说的。”
　　李世民不高兴道：“我才不是人来疯！对不对， 阿玄？”
　　李玄霸移开视线。
　　李世民一看李玄霸这表情， 明悟涌上心头：“阿玄， ‘人来疯’这个词不会是你和娘说的吧？”
　　李玄霸没回答，李世民紧接着道：“肯定是你！这古怪的词只有你会造！下来！我看你是欠收拾了！”
　　李世民伸手去扯李玄霸，李渊赶紧护住三儿子，转移话题道：“你们还没说今日遇到了什么。”
　　李世民犹豫道：“这个……嗯，不好说。”
　　李渊疑惑：“还有什么是不好和耶耶说的？”
　　李玄霸道：“父亲，你真的要问？”
　　他拍了拍李渊的手臂，让李渊把他放下来。
　　李玄霸理了理凌乱的衣衫，正坐着对着站在床榻旁的李渊道：“杨积善先找我的麻烦，然后私下向我道歉，说是一些勋贵不喜我们与陛下走得太近，所以推他出来当出头鸟。”
　　李渊皱眉。
　　李玄霸道：“我与杨积善聊天时，发现有人在一旁偷听。杨积善走后，那人离开了一会儿，又回来继续偷听我和二哥说话。我窥到了那人的衣着，应该是齐王府的下人。”
　　听完李玄霸半真半假的话后，李渊思索了一会儿，道：“齐王没这个脑子，应该是陛下在监视杨积善，误伤你们了。”
　　李渊叹了口气，道：“杨素已经病逝，陛下仍旧对楚国公府不放心啊。”
　　李世民好奇道：“楚国公府是不是以前得罪过陛下？为何陛下要逼迫得如此紧？难道老楚国公在世的时候十分嚣张跋扈？”
　　李渊摇头：“杨素一直站在陛下这一边，是陛下的左臂右膀。杨素此人虽然权势颇重，对其他人有些高傲，但对陛下一直毕恭毕敬，行为处事谨小慎微，并无僭越之举。”
　　李世民噘嘴：“听耶耶这么说，老楚国公是陛下的大忠臣啊，那陛下为何……”
　　他没有把心中“刻薄寡恩”一词说出来。
　　李玄霸已经告诉他，唐国公府内部肯定没有皇帝的眼线。
　　他们这次撞上皇帝的眼线，除了齐王身边的人本就是皇帝派去的之外，宴会人多口杂，眼线好混进去也是原因之一。
　　若皇帝的眼线这么广，杨积善兄弟就没可能起兵谋反。
　　虽然李玄霸对李世民说皇帝又菜又爱玩，就突出一个专杀没威胁的人，真心有反意的他一个都逮不住。但李世民第一次遇见皇帝的眼线，心中仍旧忐忑不安，不敢像以前那样直言快语。
　　李世民话语未尽，李渊也能猜到李世民想说什么。
　　李渊此刻想到的是窦夫人曾经劝他不要太信任陛下的话。
　　或许夫人对陛下的偏见是来自舅家被灭门的仇恨，但她误打误撞说中了。
　　“杨素已死，诸子既无声望也无才干，陛下此举过了。”李渊评价，“你们不用担心，陛下不会因为楚国公府想交好你们二人就迁怒你们。”
　　李世民仍旧噘嘴：“真的？我看陛下好小气，就算我和阿玄是孩童，他也不一定会放心。”
　　李玄霸道：“我和杨积善说的话被传回陛下耳中后，他就该对我放心了。”
　　李世民的嘴噘得老高：“他不信你是真心把他当长辈看待，听了你讨好他是有利可图才放心？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　李世民抱着手臂：“哼，他可一点都不自信。若有人对我好，我肯定更相信是因为我很厉害！”
　　李玄霸：“……”不愧是你。
　　李渊被自信心过分膨胀的二儿子逗笑，伸手捏住李世民噘起的鸭子嘴：“是是是，你可厉害了。”
　　李世民甩脑袋躲开父亲的魔爪：“本来就是！我现在的朋友肯定都是因为我足够优秀，他们才愿意和我玩，和我的身份地位无关！对了耶耶，我又交了个新朋友，叫薛收！”
　　李渊也是博闻强识之人，若有心记忆，几乎也能到过目不忘的地步。
　　他一听这个名字，就想起了这个人是谁：“河东三凤之一的薛收？薛孺之子？不错。”
　　李世民疑惑：“薛孺是谁啊？薛兄的父亲不是司隶大夫薛道衡吗？”
　　李玄霸解释道：“薛道衡是河东薛氏的旁支。他因文名过于出众，所以过继了一个幼子给本家。”
　　李世民歪头不解：“文名过于出众，和把薛兄过继给本家有什么关系？”
　　李玄霸道：“自己想，什么都问我，小心变笨。”
　　李世民不高兴道：“小气，你知道就告诉我啊，为什么非要我再想一遍。耶耶，你知道吗？”
　　李渊道：“薛氏本家选择过继的子嗣，当然从有名望的旁支中选，这样能加强两者联系。”
　　李世民道：“这样啊。我听薛兄说起父亲时，嘴里一直提的都是薛大夫。虽然过继给本家或许对他未来有利，但他内心肯定不想离开亲生父母。”
　　李渊心头一酸。他以为李世民想起了老夫人要将他和李玄霸过继的事。
　　李渊狠狠揉了揉李世民的脑袋，道：“当然。”
　　李世民捂着脑袋傻笑：“嗯。”
　　李渊道：“我去求陛下许可我们去禁苑打猎。我不在的时候你也可以带朋友去。”
　　李世民惊讶道：“可以吗？”
　　李渊笑道：“陛下名下有许多猎场都准许臣子进去狩猎。他的猎场太多了，只要花点钱就行。”
　　李玄霸摸了摸下巴。他知道杨广空着的宫殿和禁苑很多，还以为就荒废着，原来还能这样创收？
　　李世民高兴道：“太好了！我正好要写信让房玄龄和杜克明来洛阳玩！”
　　李渊道：“你可以把长孙无忌也叫来。”
　　李世民道：“他要照顾母亲和妹妹，不一定会来。嗯，我还是写信邀请一下。”
　　李渊问道：“大德有何友人？一同邀请来吧。”
　　李玄霸道：“二哥的友人就是我的友人。”
　　李渊无奈：“你这孩子，怎么如此孤僻？”
　　李玄霸不解：“我不孤僻啊。”
　　李渊叹气：“好吧，你说不孤僻就不孤僻吧。勋贵那里的事，你们也不用担心，与其说他们试探我是否站在陛下这边，不如说他们想试探陛下对我的恩宠究竟有多重。现在他们已经试探出来，接下来就该讨好我们了。”
　　李渊没有多说。他与两个孩子一同用过晚饭后，进书房不知道给谁写了什么，烛火燃到半夜。
　　东都沉寂了一日。
　　到了第三日，许多勋贵人家都邀请李世民和李玄霸去做客，还有勋贵人家送来丰厚的礼物为宴会上的事道歉。
　　这都是我们家那纨绔子弟没脑子，不代表我们的本意，你们可别误会！
　　李玄霸道：“他们大概就是这个意思。”
　　李世民翻白眼：“呵呵，别误会。这前倨后恭把我看懵了。我还以为那群勋贵要排挤我们了呢。”
　　李玄霸一边让人记录礼物，之后好还礼，一边在心里道：【二哥，你这就犯了后世历史爱好者研究历史时常犯的二极管错误了。】
　　李世民默默看着弟弟。什么历史爱好者什么二极管，哥哥听不懂啊！
　　李玄霸也不管李世民能不能听懂，继续叨叨：【后世常常划分一个个群体，把一个群体当作一个有统一思想的人对待。比如什么六国旧贵、地方豪强、士族门阀、勋贵武将、科举文官，写到小说里，那隋唐的敌人一定是士族门阀，宋明的敌人一定是仕林文官。】
　　李世民眼皮子狠狠跳了跳。
　　虽然他早就从弟弟的“预言”中猜到了一些事，但弟弟这次直白地将“隋唐”并列，还是让他的小心脏吓得差点从胸膛里蹦出来。
　　李玄霸：【其实哪可能有什么共进退的某群体？划分群体只是让后人更好地理解当时的利益纠葛，但所划分的群体本身，他们并没有自己是一个集体的意识，也不会为了自己这个群体团结一致做什么。比如隋唐，拖后腿的人中有世家门阀，改革时弊的大臣也多出自世家门阀。宋明也一样。】
　　李世民琢磨，那宋明，莫非是隋唐之后的朝代？
　　李玄霸：【杨广的改制确实损害了关陇勋贵的利益。但在隋朝还强势的时候，关陇勋贵可不会联合起来做什么，反而会为了争抢剩余的利益内部竞争更加激烈。直到隋朝虚弱的时候，他们才会趁势而起。隋朝末年农民起义的时候，关陇贵族还努力帮杨广平叛呢。】
　　李世民的眼皮子又狠狠跳了几下。
　　什么叫农民起义？那不是民贼叛乱吗？！弟弟你这话，好像你站在民贼的一方似的！
　　李玄霸：【事实上隋末割据势力除了我们唐国公府之外，薛举虽出身河东薛氏但实际只是旁支，早就迁居兰州金城，是边陲豪强，这‘河东薛氏’的名头是联宗而已；李密就更不必说了，他那瓦岗寨是夺的农民起义军首领翟让的军队，一卑鄙小人而已；除此之外，王世充是胡人、窦建德是平民百姓。】
　　李世民默默记住这几个人的名字。
　　李玄霸：【其实隋末众多势力基本都是农民起义军为主，然后豪强加入农民起义军，夺走他们的军队指挥权，想要借鸡生蛋。堂堂正正举起旗帜从头到尾参与其中的只有我们。当时很多势力都冷眼看着我们，等我们跌个大跟头。】
　　李世民明白了弟弟的意思。
　　从史书上的记载来看，这最先加入逐鹿的势力一般都会被群起攻之，一般来说很难走到最后。
　　若真的到了天下大乱那一日，隋朝积攒了这么多年的实力，灭亡时一定会爆发出极大的伤害。所以那时其他手握兵权的勋贵才按兵不动，等唐国公府率先充当出头鸟，和隋朝军队、其他农民起义……咳，其他民贼消磨。
　　不过之后既然是“隋唐”，证明这些人的瞻前顾后，让他们失去了逐鹿天下的时机。
　　一群懦夫，合该不入逐鹿英雄之名，还不如几个大民贼。
　　李玄霸：【所以纵观历史，无论是关陇贵族还是山东旧门阀，他们为了保住自己的一亩三分地，都谨慎到了怯懦的地步。杨素之前为何能成为关陇集团的领袖？是因为他给关陇集团带来了多少利益吗？不，是因为……】
　　李世民笑着打断：“是因为他得皇帝的看重，权势滔天。”
　　李玄霸对二哥竖起一个大拇指，继续埋头整理礼物清单。
　　李世民凑上前，帮弟弟清点：“这些赔罪的礼物，是不是说明耶耶要成为勋贵集团的首领了？”
　　下人们纷纷侧目，然后赶紧移开视线。
　　李玄霸：【是啊，父亲要提前成为勋贵集团推到最前面的人了。这可不一定是好事。杨广的猜忌心可是很强的。】
　　李世民怅然道：“真难啊。”
　　不知道什么时候造反，这憋屈日子，他真是一日都过不下去了。
　　还是耶耶当皇帝好。耶耶当皇帝，他和阿玄就可以嚣张起来了。看看人家齐王，每日多快乐啊。
　　讨好别人的日子，李世民真的受够了。
　　我家阿玄身体本来就弱，还要琢磨这些讨好人的事，思虑一重，身体就更不好了。还是让别人讨好我和阿玄更开心。
　　李世民虽然在杨广面前跟着弟弟一同卖萌，但他一直很清醒，知道自己这百般讨好是为了什么，对杨广的赏赐没有丝毫谢意。
　　隐藏的小反贼李世民叉腰：这些赏赐是我卖力讨好陛下后应得的！不需要感激！
　　李玄霸虽点头对二哥的话表示赞同，其实他想反驳。现在不是最难的时候，最难的是李渊当皇帝后的那段时间。
　　只是他哥现在年纪还小，剧透这么多就够了，再剧透下去，他哥那九岁的小肩膀，估计会被未来的重负压垮。
　　李玄霸剧透一番后神清气爽。
　　把事情堆在心上谁也不能说，李玄霸真是快憋坏了。遭遇了皇帝的眼线，李玄霸也吓了一大跳，心里惊恐难安，现在心中终于轻快了。
　　李玄霸连“养老”职业都要选择营销号小编，当营销号小编时非常敬业，热衷挑拨评论各种对立，常常得到老板夸奖，很明显有潜在的话痨属性和乐子人属性，分享欲极强。
　　如果现在有网络，他肯定已经扛起键盘，披上马甲，把剧透发得到处都是，破防一个算一个。
　　可惜他无法披马甲，只能对着二哥叨叨一下。
　　二哥快长大，等你成长到能被魏徵拉着袖子骂也能忍耐的时候，我就可以开开心心给你剧透更多的有趣事件了。
　　李世民打了个寒颤，嘀咕仓库太阴凉了。
　　……
　　李玄霸以为自己剧透了这么多，二哥肯定会失眠几晚上。
　　谁知道，李世民的表现比起之前几次被剧透，显得过分淡然。
　　他吃好睡好，第二日仍旧嘻嘻哈哈没心没肺，好像遭遇李玄霸剧透的记忆，被谁回档删除了似的。
　　李玄霸本来等着看二哥笑话，见状十分不解。
　　李世民瞥了满脸写着“没吓到哥哥不开心”的李玄霸一眼，道：“习惯成自然。再说，我如果表现得一惊一乍，你这个坏弟弟肯定会故意吓唬我。我看穿你了，果然你之前不是无意说漏嘴，是故意吓唬我！”
　　李玄霸坚决否认：“我不是，我没有，你污蔑我。我大部分时候都是无心之语。”
　　李世民冷笑：“呵呵，我不信。你下次再吓唬我，我就拉你出去打猎。你吓唬我一次，我就强拽你出门一次。”
　　李玄霸的脸一下子就垮了：“你要互相伤害是吧？”
　　李世民抱着手臂，抬起下巴：“阿玄，你之前怎么说来着？先撩先贱先挨揍！”
　　李玄霸拳头硬了：“可恶！不要用我的魔法攻击我，李波特！”
　　李世民好奇：“什么魔法？什么波特？算了，之后再解释，走，出门打猎去啰！”
　　李世民整理好戎装，背好弓箭，拉着满脸不高兴的李玄霸出门。
　　他们先乘坐马车去接房乔、杜如晦。薛收离得近，自己先去城门口等着。
　　禁苑在城郊，当日往返时间太紧张，大臣租借猎场的时候，可以在余留的空地搭建帐篷居住。
　　杨广对李世民、李玄霸二人确实亲厚，这两人都在期盼造反的那日快点到来，他还特意准许李世民和李玄霸可以使用禁苑行宫原本准备给大臣的房间。
　　杨广每次狩猎时都有大臣随行，所以行宫中本来就有为大臣准备房间。
　　大臣搭建帐篷的地方，在杨广狩猎的时候也会搭建帐篷，提供给没资格住在禁苑行宫里的随行官吏居住。
　　不过李世民和李玄霸没打算住屋里。都到大猎场玩耍了，当然要住帐篷。
　　就算李玄霸根本不想玩耍，但来都来了，还是要有个旅游的样子。
　　杜如晦出身较高，对李世民和李玄霸借用禁苑的事还算淡然。房乔紧张无比。
　　房乔道：“就我们几个？我们真的能去禁苑狩猎？”
　　杜如晦仔细擦拭自己的弓道：“这你就不知了。从古至今，皇帝的禁苑都会向大臣开放。若是遇到明君，禁苑平时也会向百姓开放。鸟兽怀孕的季节，才会禁止百姓进入禁苑。”
　　房乔努力活动他僵硬的脑子，想起了史书中确实有过类似记载。
　　就算是汉文帝之前，秦汉刑罚最严苛的时期，偷入禁苑者会处死，但皇帝也会颁发凭依给臣子和宗室，允许他们闲暇时去禁苑狩猎。这不仅是表示皇帝对臣子恩宠的方式，也可以为禁苑创造收益。
　　房乔擦了擦额头上的冷汗，道：“我这时才察觉，李二郎和李三郎果然是王公贵族。”
　　李世民挑眉：“什么叫果然是？难道以前我兄弟二人不像王公贵族吗？”
　　房乔道：“是不太像。”
　　杜如晦：“确实不像。”
　　李玄霸想了想，道：“好像是有点不像。”
　　李世民无奈：“阿玄，你附和他们做什么？你究竟站在哪一边？”
　　李玄霸道：“真理的那一边……哎哟，哥，我说了很多次了，不要说不过就动手。”
　　李世民敲完弟弟的脑袋，道：“我发现，对付你还是直接动手更合适。”
　　房乔和杜如晦皆失笑。马车中稍显紧张的气氛一扫而空。
　　待与薛收汇合，薛收没有坐自己的马车，也上了李世民等人的马车。
　　薛收因仰慕房乔的父亲，很快就与房乔混熟。
　　房乔虽然自称不愿意和陌生人深交，但他进入交友状态后就像换了个人似的，很容易就成为群体交流的纽带。
　　借着房乔这根纽带，原本因为同为关中郡望世家，所以显得较为矜持的杜如晦和薛收没一会儿就成为了朋友，聊得十分开心。
　　李玄霸在心底感慨：【不愧是房相，将来你得用的文臣一大半都是房相举荐的。】
　　李世民凑到弟弟耳边小声道：“现在用不着玄龄举荐，你可以提前把玄龄的功劳抢了。”
　　李玄霸：【提前不了，谁看得上你这个扎着两个小揪揪的缺牙孩童？】
　　李世民不高兴了。你骂谁呢？！你不也是！
　　李世民和李玄霸说悄悄话时，房乔、杜如晦和薛收没有打扰。他们看向窗外，诗兴大发，赞叹起东都的繁华。
　　马车行驶了几里路，三人脸上的笑容消失，诗兴卡壳。
　　只几里路，马车就像是驶入了另一个世界。
　　在刚离开东都城门的时候，他们放眼望去，田地中已经冒出了整齐的青苗。百姓在交错的阡陌中扛着锄头惬意地游走，查看田地嫩苗的情况，好一番安居乐业的田园风光。
　　几里路后，田地的青苗坑坑洼洼，有些田居然连地都没有耕好。
　　佝偻的老人艰难地锄地，锄头落下去，跟在他身旁干瘦的幼童就使劲踩锄头，才能让锄头嵌入泥土中。
　　当老人想用锄头翻动泥块时，幼童就一同握着锄头的木杆下端，和老人一同使劲往后拉动锄头。
　　锄头终于翻起了泥块，老人和幼童一个踉跄，几乎要跌倒。
　　一老一幼站直了身体，又继续翻下一块。
　　马车上的几人虽没有种过地，但都熟背节气。所以他们都知道，现在才翻地，早已经错过了农时。
　　如果只是一家一户这样，他们大概只会叹息这家人不容易，然后就继续谈论初春景色，畅想禁苑风光。
　　但离开了东都郊外那只有几里的闲适田园世界后，他们眼中的景象就没有再改变过。
　　他们视野所触及之处，全是稀稀拉拉的青苗，和艰难耕作的老人和幼童。
　　就连河边洗衣的妇人，也都是走路都摇摇晃晃的老人。
　　李世民、房乔、杜如晦、薛收眼中都是不解。
　　青壮呢？
　　别说青壮男丁，怎么连个妇人都没有见到？
　　要知道城中的妇人虽会戴冪离，但在田中耕种的农妇是向来不计较那些繁文缛节的。郊外田地中常有农妇忙碌。
　　只有李玄霸脸上闪过了悟的神情，深深地叹了口气：“陛下又征徭役了。”
　　薛收疑惑：“徭役？什么徭役？就算是有徭役，但陛下已经颁布了律令，妇人已经不需要服徭役。”
　　李玄霸道：“是啊，陛下登基之初，就下诏免除了妇女和奴婢部曲的徭役。就像陛下还在建东都的时候，说‘以简朴为要，务从节俭’一样。”
　　薛收沉默。
　　李玄霸看向窗外，神情略显漠然。
　　“今年陛下下令开凿永济渠，又下令在去年营造的长城基础上再造了一段河西榆谷长城。同时，陛下还腻了已经修好的宫殿，下令修筑汾阳宫。”
　　“所以丁男不足，妇女为丁。”
　　“如此而已。”

Chapter 52: The Joy of Decompressing Through Spoilers

After Li Shimin was "intimidated" by Li Xuanba once more, the two didn't speak again, returning home in silence.

Li Yuan had not yet returned.

After changing their clothes, the two children went back to their room for a short nap to replenish the energy they had spent that day.

When Li Yuan came to wake them, Li Shimin had already regained his vitality. He hung around Li Yuan’s neck, demanding that his father take him horseback riding and hunting during his time off.

Yang Guang was also fond of hunting, and there were many imperial hunting grounds near the Eastern Capital. Li Shimin was itching to go.

"You’re just a little thing; you want to go hunting? I’m worried you’ll be snatched away by a wild beast and become the prey yourself." Li Yuan patted his second son’s bottom and said to Li Xuanba, who was dazed on the side, "If Da De wants to go hunting, I’ll take you both."

Li Xuanba rubbed his sleepy eyes and looked up. *What does that have to do with me?*

Li Shimin hurriedly urged, "A-Xuan! Quick, help me beg Father!"

Li Xuanba suppressed a yawn and said, "Fine. Please take Second Brother hunting, Father. I’ll stay home and watch the house."

He completely failed to understand the joy of hunting.

Li Shimin tugged at Li Yuan’s loose sideburns. "Father, A-Xuan is too lazy. You must take him hunting. How can our Li family not love hunting!"

Li Yuan retrieved his hair from his mischievous son’s grip and nodded as if it were a serious matter. "That’s right! Tomorrow, I will go find His Majesty and ask him to grant me permission to take you both hunting!"

Li Xuanba couldn't help but yawn again. "I don't want to go."

Li Shimin was arrogant. "Since when is it up to you? Hunting is part of our studies, too!"

Li Yuan looked at his precociously mature third son’s impatient and gloomy expression, and holding back a laugh, he said, "Da Xiong is right; this is a lesson."

Li Xuanba looked at this father and son duo speechlessly. *Are you two just conspiring to mess with me?*

Li Yuan put Li Shimin down, picked up Li Xuanba, and ruffled his hair.

Li Xuanba’s body stiffened slightly. "Father, I am already grown."

Li Yuan laughed. "Even if you’re grown, you’re still my son. What happened to you two today?"

Li Shimin was curious. "How did you know, Father?"

Li Yuan glanced at Li Shimin. "With your 'man-crazy' temperament, if you return home early after attending a banquet, something must have happened."

*Man-crazy?!* Li Shimin’s eyes widened. "What do you mean 'man-crazy'! Father, you’re talking nonsense!"

Li Yuan laughed. "That’s what your mother said."

Li Shimin was unhappy. "I am not man-crazy! Right, A-Xuan?"

Li Xuanba looked away.

Seeing Li Xuanba’s expression, a realization dawned on Li Shimin. "A-Xuan, you’re the one who told Mother that phrase 'man-crazy', aren't you?"

Li Xuanba didn't answer, and Li Shimin immediately followed up, "It must be you! Only you could invent such a bizarre term! Get down! I think you’re asking for a beating!"

Li Shimin reached out to pull at Li Xuanba, but Li Yuan quickly shielded his third son and changed the subject. "You still haven't told me what you encountered today."

Li Shimin hesitated. "This... well, it’s hard to say."

Li Yuan was puzzled. "Is there anything you can't tell your father?"

Li Xuanba said, "Father, do you really want to ask?"

He patted Li Yuan’s arm, signaling for him to be put down.

Li Xuanba straightened his disheveled clothes, sat upright, and addressed Li Yuan, who was standing by the bed. "Yang Jishan first made trouble for me, then apologized in private, saying that some nobles were unhappy with us getting too close to His Majesty, so they pushed him out to be the scapegoat."

Li Yuan frowned.

Li Xuanba continued, "While I was chatting with Yang Jishan, I noticed someone eavesdropping nearby. After Yang Jishan left, that person went away for a while, then returned to continue eavesdropping on Second Brother and me. I caught a glimpse of that person’s attire; it should be a servant from the Prince of Qi’s mansion."

After hearing Li Xuanba’s half-truth, Li Yuan pondered for a moment. "The Prince of Qi doesn't have the brains for this. It’s likely His Majesty was monitoring Yang Jishan and accidentally caught you two in the crossfire."

Li Yuan sighed. "Yang Su has already passed away, yet His Majesty still doesn't feel at ease with the Duke of Chu’s mansion."

Li Shimin asked curiously, "Did the Duke of Chu’s mansion offend His Majesty in the past? Why is His Majesty pushing them so hard? Was the old Duke of Chu arrogant and domineering while he was alive?"

Li Yuan shook his head. "Yang Su always stood on His Majesty’s side; he was His Majesty’s right-hand man. Although Yang Su held great power and was somewhat arrogant toward others, he was always respectful and cautious toward His Majesty, never overstepping his bounds."

Li Shimin pouted. "Listening to you, Father, the old Duke of Chu was a loyal subject to His Majesty. Then why does His Majesty..."

He didn't say the words "callous and ungrateful" that were in his heart.

Li Xuanba had already told him that there were definitely no imperial spies inside the Tang Duke’s mansion.

The reason they ran into the Emperor’s spy this time, besides the fact that the people around the Prince of Qi were already sent by the Emperor, was that the banquet was crowded and chaotic, making it easy for spies to blend in.

If the Emperor’s eyes and ears were truly that widespread, the Yang Jishan brothers would never have had the chance to raise an army in rebellion.

Although Li Xuanba had told Li Shimin that the Emperor was both incompetent and loved to play games—specializing in killing those who posed no threat while failing to catch anyone who truly harbored rebellious intent—this was Li Shimin’s first encounter with an imperial spy. He still felt uneasy and dared not speak as bluntly as before.

Even though Li Shimin didn't finish his sentence, Li Yuan could guess what he wanted to say.

At that moment, Li Yuan thought of the words Lady Dou had once used to advise him not to trust the Emperor too much.

Perhaps her prejudice against the Emperor stemmed from the hatred of her maternal family being wiped out, but she had hit the nail on the head.

"Yang Su is dead, and his sons have neither prestige nor talent. His Majesty’s actions are excessive," Li Yuan commented. "You don't need to worry; His Majesty won't take his anger out on you just because the Duke of Chu’s mansion wants to befriend you."

Li Shimin still pouted. "Really? I think His Majesty is very petty. Even if A-Xuan and I are just children, he might not necessarily feel at ease."

Li Xuanba said, "Once the words I spoke to Yang Jishan reach His Majesty’s ears, he should feel at ease with me."

Li Shimin’s pout grew even more pronounced. "He doesn't believe you truly view him as an elder, and only feels at ease after hearing that you were currying favor for profit?"

Li Xuanba nodded.

Li Shimin crossed his arms. "Hmph, he’s not confident at all. If someone is good to me, I’d definitely believe it’s because I’m amazing!"

Li Xuanba: "..." *As expected of you.*

Li Yuan was amused by his second son’s overinflated self-confidence and reached out to pinch Li Shimin’s pouting duck-bill lips. "Yes, yes, yes, you are very amazing."

Li Shimin shook his head to dodge his father’s "claws." "It’s true! My friends now definitely like me because I’m outstanding enough, and they want to play with me, regardless of my status or position! By the way, Father, I’ve made a new friend named Xue Shou!"

Li Yuan was also a man of vast learning; if he put his mind to it, he could almost achieve a photographic memory. Upon hearing the name, he immediately recalled who this person was. "Xue Shou, one of the 'Three Phoenixes of Hedong'? The son of Xue Ru? Not bad."

Li Shimin was puzzled. "Who is Xue Ru? Isn't Brother Xue’s father the Sili Daifu, Xue Daoheng?"

Li Xuanba explained, "Xue Daoheng is a branch member of the Hedong Xue clan. Because his literary fame was too outstanding, he adopted a young son to the main branch."

Li Shimin tilted his head, confused. "What does having outstanding literary fame have to do with adopting Brother Xue to the main branch?"

Li Xuanba said, "Think about it yourself. If you ask me everything, be careful you don't become stupid."

Li Shimin said unhappily, "You’re stingy. If you know, just tell me. Why must you make me think about it again? Father, do you know?"

Li Yuan said, "When the main branch of the Xue clan chooses an heir to adopt, they naturally choose from a prestigious branch to strengthen the connection between the two."

Li Shimin said, "I see. When I heard Brother Xue talk about his father, he always referred to him as 'Daifu Xue.' Although being adopted into the main branch might be beneficial for his future, he surely didn't want to leave his biological parents."

Li Yuan’s heart ached. He thought Li Shimin was remembering the time the Old Madam wanted to have him and Li Xuanba adopted out.

Li Yuan ruffled Li Shimin’s hair hard. "Of course."

Li Shimin covered his head and giggled. "Mm."

Li Yuan said, "I’ll go ask His Majesty for permission for us to hunt in the Forbidden Park. You can also take your friends when I’m not around."

Li Shimin was surprised. "Can I?"

Li Yuan laughed. "His Majesty has many hunting grounds that allow officials to hunt. He has too many; as long as you spend a little money, it’s fine."

Li Xuanba touched his chin. He knew Yang Guang had many empty palaces and forbidden parks, but he thought they were just abandoned. *So, they can generate revenue like this?*

Li Shimin said happily, "That’s great! I was just about to write to Fang Xuanling and Du Keming to come to Luoyang to play!"

Li Yuan said, "You can also invite Zhangsun Wuji."

Li Shimin said, "He has to take care of his mother and sister; he might not come. Well, I’ll write to invite him anyway."

Li Yuan asked, "Does Da De have any friends? Invite them along too."

Li Xuanba said, "Second Brother’s friends are my friends."

Li Yuan sighed helplessly. "You child, why are you so antisocial?"

Li Xuanba was puzzled. "I’m not antisocial."

Li Yuan sighed. "Fine, if you say you’re not, then you’re not. As for the matter with the nobles, you don't need to worry. Rather than testing whether I stand with His Majesty, they are testing how much favor His Majesty truly holds for me. Now that they’ve tested it, it’s time for them to curry favor with us."

Li Yuan didn't say much more. After having dinner with his two children, he went into his study and wrote something to someone, the candle burning until midnight.

The Eastern Capital was silent for a day.

By the third day, many noble families invited Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to be guests, and some even sent generous gifts to apologize for the incident at the banquet.

*It was just that good-for-nothing kid in our family who had no brains; it doesn't represent our true intentions. Please don't misunderstand!*

Li Xuanba said, "That’s probably exactly what they mean."

Li Shimin rolled his eyes. "Heh, 'don't misunderstand.' This 'arrogant first, humble later' attitude has me stunned. I thought that group of nobles was going to ostracize us."

Li Xuanba, while having someone record the gifts so they could return the favor later, thought to himself: *[Second Brother, you’ve fallen into the 'binary' trap that later history enthusiasts often fall into when studying history.]*

Li Shimin looked at his younger brother silently. *What history enthusiast, what binary? Big brother doesn't understand!*

Li Xuanba didn't care if Li Shimin understood or not and continued to ramble: *[Later generations often divide people into groups and treat a group as a single person with a unified ideology. For example, the 'Old Nobles of the Six States,' 'Local Magnates,' 'Aristocratic Clans,' 'Military Nobles,' or 'Imperial Examination Scholars.' When written into novels, the enemy of the Sui and Tang is always the Aristocratic Clans, and the enemy of the Song and Ming is always the Scholar-Officials.]*

Li Shimin’s eyelids twitched violently.

Although he had already guessed some things from his brother’s "prophecies," his brother’s blunt pairing of "Sui and Tang" still made his little heart almost jump out of his chest.

Li Xuanba: *[In reality, how could there be any group that acts in total unison? Dividing groups only helps later generations better understand the conflicts of interest at the time. But the groups themselves have no consciousness of being a collective, nor will they unite to do anything for the sake of their group. Take the Sui and Tang, for example: among those holding back progress were the aristocratic clans, but the officials who reformed the abuses were also mostly from those same clans. The Song and Ming are the same.]*

Li Shimin pondered: *That 'Song and Ming,' could it be the dynasties after the Sui and Tang?*

Li Xuanba: *[Yang Guang’s reforms did indeed harm the interests of the Guanlong nobles. But while the Sui Dynasty was still strong, the Guanlong nobles wouldn't unite to do anything; instead, they competed even more fiercely among themselves to grab the remaining interests. Only when the Sui Dynasty was weak did they seize the opportunity. During the peasant uprisings at the end of the Sui, the Guanlong nobles were still trying to help Yang Guang suppress the rebellions.]*

Li Shimin’s eyelids twitched a few more times.

*What do you mean 'peasant uprisings'? Aren't those just bandit rebellions?! Brother, the way you talk makes it sound like you’re on the side of the bandits!*

Li Xuanba: *[In fact, apart from our Tang Duke’s mansion, most of the separatist forces at the end of the Sui were peasant armies. Xue Ju, although from the Hedong Xue clan, was actually just a branch member who had long since moved to Jincheng in Lanzhou; he was a frontier magnate, and the 'Hedong Xue' name was just a claim of kinship. Li Mi goes without saying; his Wagang Army was stolen from the peasant uprising leader Zhai Rang—a despicable man. Besides them, Wang Shichong was a Hu, and Dou Jiande was a commoner.]*

Li Shimin silently memorized these names.

Li Xuanba: *[In truth, many of the forces at the end of the Sui were primarily peasant armies, with magnates joining them to seize command of their troops, hoping to 'borrow a chicken to lay eggs.' The only ones who raised the flag upright and participated from beginning to end were us. At the time, many forces were watching us coldly, waiting for us to take a big fall.]*

Li Shimin understood his brother’s meaning.

Judging from the historical records, the first forces to join the struggle for the throne are usually attacked by all sides and rarely make it to the end.

If the world truly descended into chaos, the strength accumulated by the Sui Dynasty over so many years would surely erupt with great destructive power when it collapsed. That was why the other nobles holding military power sat still, waiting for the Tang Duke’s mansion to be the first to stick its neck out and wear itself down against the Sui army and other peasant uprisings... *cough*, other bandit rebellions.

However, since it is called "Sui and Tang," it proves that their hesitation caused them to lose the opportunity to compete for the world.

A bunch of cowards; they don't deserve the name of heroes, not even as much as a few great bandits.

Li Xuanba: *[So, looking at history, whether it’s the Guanlong nobles or the old Shandong clans, they were so cautious that they were cowardly, all to protect their own little acre of land. Why was Yang Su able to become the leader of the Guanlong group before? Was it because of how much benefit he brought them? No, it was because...]*

Li Shimin interrupted with a smile, "It was because he was favored by the Emperor and held immense power."

Li Xuanba gave his second brother a thumbs-up and continued to bury his head in organizing the gift list.

Li Shimin leaned in to help his brother count. "Do these gifts of apology mean that Father is about to become the leader of the noble group?"

The servants glanced over, then quickly looked away.

Li Xuanba: *[Yes, Father is about to be pushed to the forefront by the noble group ahead of schedule. This might not be a good thing. Yang Guang’s suspicion is very strong.]*

Li Shimin said wistfully, "It’s really hard."

Not knowing when to rebel—he really couldn't live this stifling life for another day.

It would be better if Father were the Emperor. If Father were the Emperor, he and A-Xuan could be arrogant. Look at the Prince of Qi; how happy he is every day.

Li Shimin was truly fed up with the days of currying favor with others.

His A-Xuan was already physically weak, and having to ponder these ways to please people only made him worry more, which was bad for his health. It would be much happier to let others curry favor with him and A-Xuan.

Although Li Shimin followed his brother’s lead in acting cute in front of Yang Guang, he remained clear-headed, knowing why he was doing all this fawning, and felt no gratitude for Yang Guang’s rewards.

*Hidden little rebel Li Shimin puts his hands on his hips:* These rewards are what I deserve after working hard to please His Majesty! No need to be grateful!

Although Li Xuanba nodded in agreement with his second brother’s words, he actually wanted to refute him. Now was not the hardest time; the hardest time would be the period after Li Yuan became Emperor.

But his brother was still young. These spoilers were enough; if he spoiled any more, his brother’s nine-year-old shoulders would likely be crushed by the weight of the future.

Li Xuanba felt refreshed after spilling the spoilers.

Keeping things bottled up inside with no one to tell—Li Xuanba was truly about to burst. Encountering the Emperor’s spy had given him a huge fright, and he had been terrified, but now his heart finally felt light.

Li Xuanba had even chosen "marketing account editor" as his "retirement" career. He was very professional when working as an editor, keen on inciting controversy and opposition, often receiving praise from his boss. It was clear he had a latent talkative and mischievous nature, with a strong desire to share.

If there were an internet now, he would definitely have picked up his keyboard, put on a mask, and spread spoilers everywhere, breaking the defenses of everyone he could.

Unfortunately, he couldn't hide behind a mask and could only ramble to his second brother.

*Second Brother, grow up fast. When you grow to the point where you can endure being scolded by Wei Zheng while he pulls on your sleeves, I can happily spoil more interesting events for you.*

Li Shimin shivered and muttered that the warehouse was too chilly.

...

Li Xuanba thought that after spoiling so much, his second brother would definitely suffer from insomnia for a few nights.

To his surprise, Li Shimin’s performance seemed overly indifferent compared to the previous times he had been spoiled.

He ate well and slept well, and the next day he was still laughing and carefree, as if the memory of being spoiled by Li Xuanba had been rolled back and deleted by someone.

Li Xuanba had been waiting to see his second brother make a fool of himself and was very puzzled.

Li Shimin glanced at Li Xuanba, whose face was written with "I’m unhappy I didn't scare my brother," and said, "Habit becomes nature. Besides, if I acted all jumpy, you, the bad younger brother, would definitely try to scare me on purpose. I’ve seen through you; it turns out you didn't let things slip by accident before, you were scaring me on purpose!"

Li Xuanba firmly denied it. "I didn't, I wasn't, you’re slandering me. Most of the time, it was unintentional."

Li Shimin sneered. "Heh, I don't believe it. If you scare me again, I’ll drag you out to hunt. Every time you scare me, I’ll drag you out of the house."

Li Xuanba’s face fell instantly. "You want to hurt each other, is that it?"

Li Shimin crossed his arms and lifted his chin. "A-Xuan, what did you say before? 'He who provokes first is the cheapest and gets beaten first!'"

Li Xuanba’s fists tightened. "Damn it! Don't use my own magic to attack me, Li Potter!"

Li Shimin was curious. "What magic? What Potter? Forget it, explain it later. Let’s go, let’s go hunting!"

Li Shimin tidied his military uniform, slung his bow and arrows over his shoulder, and dragged the unhappy Li Xuanba out the door.

They first took a carriage to pick up Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui. Xue Shou was nearby and went to the city gate to wait for them.

The Forbidden Park was in the suburbs, and the round trip in one day was too tight. When officials rented the hunting grounds, they could set up tents to live in the remaining open spaces.

Yang Guang was indeed affectionate toward Li Shimin and Li Xuanba—both of whom were looking forward to the day of rebellion—and he specifically granted them permission to use the rooms in the Forbidden Park palace originally prepared for officials.

Every time Yang Guang hunted, officials accompanied him, so there were rooms prepared for them in the palace.

The places where officials set up tents were also used for tents during Yang Guang’s hunts, provided for the accompanying officials who were not qualified to stay in the palace.

However, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba didn't intend to stay in the rooms. Since they were going to a big hunting ground to play, they naturally had to stay in tents.

Even if Li Xuanba didn't want to play at all, since they were already there, they had to look like they were on a trip.

Du Ruhui came from a higher background and was relatively calm about Li Shimin and Li Xuanba borrowing the Forbidden Park. Fang Qiao, however, was extremely nervous.

Fang Qiao said, "Just us? Can we really go hunting in the Forbidden Park?"

Du Ruhui carefully wiped his bow. "You don't know this. From ancient times to the present, the Emperor’s forbidden parks have been open to officials. If there is a wise ruler, the forbidden parks are even open to the common people during normal times. Only during the season when birds and beasts are pregnant is the public forbidden from entering."

Fang Qiao struggled to activate his stiff brain and remembered that there were indeed similar records in historical books.

Even before Emperor Wen of the Han, during the period when the laws of the Qin and Han were the most severe, those who snuck into the forbidden parks were executed, but the Emperor would also issue passes to officials and the imperial clan, allowing them to hunt in the parks during their leisure time. This was not only a way to show the Emperor’s favor to his subjects but also a way to generate revenue for the parks.

Fang Qiao wiped the cold sweat from his forehead. "Only now do I realize that Li Er-lang and Li San-lang are indeed royalty and nobility."

Li Shimin raised an eyebrow. "What do you mean 'indeed'? Did my brother and I not look like royalty and nobility before?"

Fang Qiao said, "Not really."

Du Ruhui: "Indeed, not really."

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and said, "It does seem a bit unlike it."

Li Shimin sighed helplessly. "A-Xuan, why are you agreeing with them? Whose side are you on?"

Li Xuanba said, "On the side of truth... Ouch! Brother, I’ve said it many times, don't use your fists just because you can't win an argument."

Li Shimin finished tapping his brother’s head and said, "I’ve discovered that it’s more appropriate to just use my hands when dealing with you."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui both laughed. The slightly tense atmosphere in the carriage was swept away.

When they met up with Xue Shou, he didn't take his own carriage and boarded theirs instead.

Because Xue Shou admired Fang Qiao’s father, he quickly became familiar with Fang Qiao.

Although Fang Qiao claimed he didn't want to make deep friendships with strangers, once he entered "social mode," he was like a different person, easily becoming the bond for group interaction.

Through Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui and Xue Shou, who had been somewhat reserved because they were both from prestigious Guanzhong families, soon became friends and chatted happily.

Li Xuanba sighed in his heart: *[As expected of Prime Minister Fang; most of the capable civil officials you use in the future will be recommended by him.]*

Li Shimin leaned into his brother’s ear and whispered, "No need for Xuanling to recommend them now; you can steal Xuanling’s credit in advance."

Li Xuanba: *[Can't do it in advance. Who would look twice at a gap-toothed child with two little hair buns like you?]*

Li Shimin was unhappy. *Who are you scolding?! Aren't you the same!*

While Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were whispering, Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Xue Shou didn't disturb them. They looked out the window, feeling poetic and marveling at the prosperity of the Eastern Capital.

After the carriage had traveled a few miles, the smiles on the three men’s faces vanished, and their poetic inspiration stalled.

In just a few miles, it was as if the carriage had driven into another world.

When they had just left the city gates of the Eastern Capital, they looked out and saw neat green sprouts in the fields. Commoners walked comfortably through the crisscrossing paths, carrying hoes to check on the condition of the young seedlings—a scene of peaceful and prosperous pastoral life.

A few miles later, the green sprouts in the fields were patchy, and some fields hadn't even been plowed properly.

A hunched old man was struggling to hoe the ground. As the hoe fell, a thin young child beside him would step hard on the hoe to help it sink into the soil.

When the old man wanted to use the hoe to turn over the clods of earth, the child would hold the lower end of the handle with him, and they would pull back together with all their might.

The hoe finally turned the soil, and the old man and child stumbled, almost falling over.

The old and the young stood up straight and continued to turn the next patch.

Although the people in the carriage had never farmed, they all knew the solar terms by heart. So they all knew that plowing now meant they had already missed the farming season.

If it were just one family, they might have sighed that the family was having a hard time and then continued to talk about the scenery of early spring and imagine the beauty of the Forbidden Park.

But after leaving the leisurely pastoral world of the Eastern Capital’s suburbs, the scene before their eyes never changed.

Wherever they looked, there were only sparse green sprouts and old people and children struggling to farm.

Even the women washing clothes by the river were old women who swayed as they walked.

Li Shimin, Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Xue Shou all had expressions of confusion.

*Where are the able-bodied men?*

*Never mind the men, why aren't there even any women?*

It was known that although women in the city would wear veils, farm women working in the fields never cared for such cumbersome etiquette. There were usually farm women busy in the fields on the outskirts.

Only Li Xuanba’s face showed a flash of realization, and he sighed deeply. "His Majesty has levied corvée labor again."

Xue Shou was puzzled. "Corvée labor? What corvée labor? Even if there is, His Majesty has already issued a decree that women are no longer required to serve."

Li Xuanba said, "That’s right. When His Majesty first ascended the throne, he issued an edict exempting women and slaves from corvée labor. Just like when His Majesty was building the Eastern Capital, he said, 'Simplicity is the priority; practice frugality.'"

Xue Shou fell silent.

Li Xuanba looked out the window, his expression slightly indifferent.

"This year, His Majesty ordered the excavation of the Yongji Canal and ordered the construction of another section of the Hexi Yugu Great Wall on top of the one built last year. At the same time, His Majesty grew tired of the palaces that were already finished and ordered the construction of the Fenyang Palace."

"Therefore, there are not enough men, so women are counted as men."

"That is all."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第53章 李二郎初猎大虎
chunks.chineseText:
第53章 李二郎初猎大虎

=
　　几人都是怀有赤子之心书生意气的人， “如此而已”四个字，好像是铜钟在几人耳边撞响。
　　暖春四月的熏风吹在几人脸庞，似乎也多了几分寒意。
　　薛收紧了紧衣襟， 道：“运河和长城还能说修着有些道理， 只是急躁了些。可宫殿……陛下还觉得宫殿不够多吗？”
　　杜如晦冷笑：“京城的宫殿不够大吗？若不够大， 他不是三年前刚在东都修了显仁宫和西苑？”
　　房乔皱眉：“陛下巡游江都时，在运河两岸修建的小行宫不提，光是在江都以北长阜苑内， 就有归雁宫、回流宫、九里宫、松林宫、枫林宫、大雷宫、小雷宫、春草宫、九华宫、光汾宫，整整十座宫殿。”
　　李玄霸平静道：“扬子有临江宫，渭南有崇业宫， 临淮有都梁宫，涿郡有临朔宫， 去年还在太原建了晋阳宫， 但陛下还是觉得不够。”
　　李世民双手枕在脑后，靠在马车座背上，看着摇摇晃晃的马车顶出神。
　　李玄霸将视线从马车外收回。
　　“帝无日不治宫室”。他们刚才报菜名似地报出的一连串宫殿名，全是自大业元年起修建。
　　而现在只是大业四年春。
　　【哥，唐末皮日休曾写道《汴河怀古之二》， “尽道隋亡为此河，至今千里赖通波。若无水殿龙舟事， 共禹论功不较多。”】
　　李世民的后脑勺砸在了马车壁上。
　　啊？我家大唐还没来，就唐末了？！
　　【皮日休是讽刺隋炀帝的骄奢淫逸，但后世却忽视了“若无水殿龙舟事”， 只感慨“共禹论功不较多”， 居然把这首诗当做夸赞隋炀帝。皮日休若得知后世人对他这首诗的评价， 恐怕得以头抢地， 号哭不止。】
　　李世民揉了揉后脑勺，幽怨地瞥了一眼面色十分平静，完全看不出正在心里义愤填膺絮絮叨叨的弟弟。
　　【皮日休正处于黄巢称帝时期，亲眼见到辉煌的唐朝崩塌的模样。比起处于安史之乱时期杜甫等人眼见着唐朝由盛转衰，好歹还有唐朝兴复的念想。皮日休面临的是伸手不见五指的绝望。】
　　李世民的脑袋隐隐作疼。
　　安史之乱是什么？黄巢又是谁？大唐就这么崩塌了？一点希望都没有了？
　　为什么我要在大唐还没建立的时候，听弟弟说大唐由盛转衰甚至干脆崩塌了？？？
　　【唐朝崩塌后是什么？是比魏晋南北朝更加黑暗的五代十国，一段因为过于残忍而在各种影视小说中几乎隐形的时代。皮日休就正站在这个界线上。】
　　李世民瞳孔地震。
　　什么？！还能比南北朝更加黑暗残忍？？阿玄你是开玩笑对吧？你肯定是开玩笑对吧？
　　啊不！！为什么马车上还有三个外人！！我都不能开口让阿玄闭心！！
　　【皮日休一生的诗歌都在写忠孝，抒发自己对时局的郁闷，痛骂糜烂的朝堂和黑暗的社会，在诗歌中指着昏君暴君的鼻子骂。结果他借古讽今，用隋炀帝讽刺当时唐朝昏君的诗，居然成了隋炀帝登上网庙十哲的台阶，这大概是另一种荒诞的“借古讽今”了。】
　　李玄霸表面上八风不动，心里思维发散，唏嘘不已。
　　身为资深“太宗黑”，评论区为他摇旗呐喊的人中大部分都是网庙十哲笃信者。他很明白后世人吹捧隋炀帝的心态。
　　罪在当代，功在千秋。苦处让隋朝的老百姓吃了，好处被后世人捡了，那可不使劲吹一番。
　　可惜隋炀帝建的大运河和宫殿已经湮灭在战火中，若是能留到后世成为名胜古迹，他的评价应该会更高。
　　三年时间建了数十座大小宫殿哪里够，最好修个上百座，每个城市一座。
　　许多人把隋炀帝比作低配版秦始皇。
　　秦始皇修驰道修长城花了十余年，巡游全国时就整修了一下六国的旧宫殿，还经常风餐露宿住帐篷。当了第一个统一王朝的皇帝，他就在咸阳修了新宫殿，阿房宫甚至才打了个地基。
　　秦始皇算什么？给广神提鞋都不配。
　　李玄霸感叹：【后世常有人说隋朝灭亡是得罪了关陇集团。百姓活不下去，遍地农民起义，关陇集团没劝隋炀帝轻徭薄赋？劝了啊，劝了的人都被杀了。真想让那些广神粉穿越隋炀帝时期，看看哪个穿越者能阻止隋朝灭亡。他们真是太瞧得起自己，太瞧不起宇宙大广神啊。哥，你干什么？！】
　　李世民转头，把脑袋一下一下地往马车壁上磕。
　　正愤慨的房乔、杜如晦和薛收也吓了一跳：“李二，你怎么了？”
　　李世民碎碎念：“我怎么？我能怎么？阿玄不闭嘴，我就撞死在这里。”
　　三人满头雾水地看向李玄霸。
　　李玄霸眨了眨眼睛，神情仍旧很平静，平静且安静，乖巧。
　　李世民揉了揉额头上的红印子，抱怨道：“阿玄，你能不能分一分场合？虽然我心很大，但我还小！养气功夫不到家！如果我暴露了怎么办！”
　　李玄霸眼神飘忽了一下：“我做什么了？我什么都没做。”
　　李世民扯住李玄霸凹陷的小脸：“阿玄！李三郎！李大德！”
　　三人虽不知道发生了什么事，还是赶紧阻止李世民“欺负”弟弟。
　　“李二，你做什么？”
　　“怎么如此生气？先松手！”
　　“怎么了？怎么突然吵起来了？”
　　李世民被三人拉开。
　　李玄霸摸了摸自己的脸颊，见二哥似乎真的生气了，辩解道：“我又没说什么不能说的话，你反应这么大干什么？”
　　李世民气得抬起脚。房乔赶紧把李世民的脚压下去。
　　与李世民和李玄霸相识了几月，房乔和杜如晦都猜到了这两兄弟估计有什么他们察觉不到的交流方式。
　　杜如晦道：“李三，你也别太过分了。”
　　薛收看看几人。怎么就只剩下自己满头雾水了？你们究竟知道了什么？
　　房乔见薛收露出了被孤立的神情，解释道：“李二和李三是双生子，双生子似乎有外人不了解的交流方式。”
　　薛收惊讶：“居然有这等神异？”
　　他打量李世民和李玄霸，啧啧称奇。
　　薛收没有问李玄霸说了什么让李世民“暴跳如雷”。既然是悄悄话，即使李玄霸说“没什么不能说的话”，大概也是他们不好打听的。
　　但他虽然在书中读到过一些双生子的奇妙心灵感应，今日真的见到了，还是很好奇。
　　年轻人的情绪变幻的很快。百姓的事虽然让他们悲愤，但他们都知道以自己现在的身份地位，唯一能做的只有悲愤。几人都不是被情绪左右的人，便借着李世民和李玄霸的“争吵”转移了注意力。
　　薛收好奇道：“介意我问一下你们的心灵感应到何种地步吗？”
　　李世民道：“就是模模糊糊能感觉到一些。”
　　薛收总觉得这对双生子的心灵感应不仅是“模模糊糊”，但李世民都这样说了，他虽和李世民一见如故，但也只是刚结识不久，不宜交浅言深，便笑了笑作罢。
　　李世民叮嘱李玄霸：“别说了，听到了吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“好好好，行行行。”
　　李世民趁着几人不注意，又伸手扯住了李玄霸的脸：“敷衍！”
　　李玄霸叹气：“好，行。”
　　李世民这才松开手。
　　杜如晦笑道：“我有时候真的很好奇李三说了什么，能让你这么激动。”
　　李世民冷笑：“你真想知道？”
　　房乔捂住杜如晦的嘴：“不，他不想知道。”
　　房乔想起了李玄霸预言的事，脑门上冒出冷汗。
　　李玄霸道：“再过些年，我一定告诉你们。”
　　杜如晦把房乔的手挡开，抱怨道：“你捂我的嘴干什么？李二李三不是小气的人。”
　　房乔扶额。你对李三的威力一无所知！
　　房乔已经隐隐猜到李世民突然激动的真相。
　　以李玄霸那初次见面就能把谶纬砸你身上的性格，他对李世民肯定说了更多的谶纬。
　　房乔就郁闷了，谶纬不是很困难的事吗？怎么李玄霸做起来就像是吃饭喝水一样简单？
　　李世民道：“对，不小气。如果阿玄认为可以对你们说了，自会和你们说的。”
　　李玄霸看向二哥：“哥，你真的同意我说出去？”
　　李世民道：“嗯……一般而言，你还是不说为好。但若你认为可以说，那就说吧。反正我不在乎这个。”
　　李玄霸打趣道：“现在你不在乎，以后你也不在乎？”
　　李世民笑着揉了揉李玄霸的脑袋：“我不知道我以后会如何，但我现在肯定不在乎。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“有话好好说，别揉脑袋。”
　　李世民双手揉头：“就揉。你再厉害也是我弟弟，我揉我弟弟的脑袋怎么了？”
　　薛收再次感到了自己被孤立。这两人打什么哑谜？
　　他看向房乔。
　　房乔叹气：“习惯就好，谁让他们是双生子。”
　　杜如晦笑道：“他们说他们的，我们聊我们的。刚不是说作诗吗？现在继续！”
　　薛收道：“你们还有兴致继续作诗？”
　　李世民一边欺负弟弟，一边道：“怎么没兴致？世间意难平的事太多，若见一次愁很久，还不把自己愁死了？能解决的事就解决，解决不了的事就搁置一边，该吃吃该喝喝该玩玩。忧愁也不能改变现状，快乐也不能改变现状，为何不快乐些？”
　　杜如晦嘴角含笑：“李二言之有理。”
　　房乔苦笑着摇摇头：“在心胸宽广上，我常自省不如你。”
　　薛收叹了口气，拱手道：“李二郎，在下受教了。”
　　李世民矜持地点点头，得意道：“好说好说，我这人的优点还有很多，你们慢慢学。”
　　三人大笑，李玄霸也不由笑了。
　　他想起史书中的唐太宗就是出了名的爱嘚瑟，“朕之功业，大小竹帛，岂能尽载”。
　　等他哥再说这句话的时候，他一定要在二哥说第一个字的时候，就在心里帮他把整句话补全，不知道二哥还会不会厚着脸皮把整句话说出来。
　　真是期待啊。
　　……
　　到了禁苑猎场，李世民如他所说的那样，立刻将不愉快的事抛到了脑后。
　　李玄霸与禁苑的官吏沟通的时候，他已经如撒了绳子的猎犬一样冲了出去。
　　这时候没有士人不会骑马。但李世民骑马冲刺的速度太快，瞬间把房乔、杜如晦和薛收抛到了身后，只有唐国公府的护卫跟了上去。
　　三人面面相觑。
　　李玄霸骑着马慢吞吞过来，薛收有一点焦急道：“李三郎，李二郎瞬间就没影子了，是不是该派人去找找？”
　　李玄霸道：“不用理睬他。护卫跟上就行了。”
　　他话音刚落，李世民就从林子冲冲了出来。
　　在他的马前面，有只慌不择路的兔子。
　　已经弯弓搭箭的李世民弓箭离手，箭狠狠扎入可怜的兔子的脖子中，把兔子钉在了地上。
　　李世民放慢速度，脚勾在马镫上，一手抓着缰绳，一个侧身倒挂把兔子从地上拔起来，握住缰绳的手一使劲，身体回到了马背上。
　　他笑着晃了晃手中的兔子：“拔得头彩！”
　　薛收揉了揉眼睛。刚刚的弓箭箭头是不是都没入地面了？
　　杜如晦拍手夸赞道：“李二，你这样的年纪就有如此的射术和骑术，将来一定能驰骋沙场！”
　　李世民把兔子绑在马屁股上：“我现在就可以驰骋沙场，可惜耶……父亲总说我还小，不准我去边疆。”
　　李玄霸没好气道：“你还真想去？”
　　李世民笑道：“为什么不可以想呢？不多说了，赶紧的，猎物还有很多！”
　　见李世民已经射到了兔子，薛收、杜如晦和房乔被激起了胜负心，一个个摩拳擦掌。
　　总不能比不过一个九岁的孩童吧？
　　四人都策马进入了林子中，李玄霸在一群护卫的围绕下，慢吞吞骑马散步。
　　他骑术还行，但射箭……告辞！
　　李玄霸不是瞄不准，是真的拉不动能射动猎物的弓。
　　若有猎|枪就好了，他只需要瞄准，狩猎成果不一定比二哥差。
　　可惜他就算是穿越者，也完全不知道该如何制造枪支。
　　黑火|药的配方他倒是记得，但黑火|药的那点威力，实在是浪费了他的期待。
　　不知道古代那些威力强大的火|药是怎么做的。等李家快造反的时候，自己再慢慢琢磨吧。
　　反正不琢磨，他哥也能砍翻这个乱世，不急。
　　“三郎君，前面好像有猛兽。”一个护卫道。
　　李玄霸问道：“你怎么知道的？”
　　护卫道：“附近太安静了。”
　　李玄霸道：“那就绕……”
　　他话音未落，就听见二哥的奋的大叫声：“前面有老虎！你们都别动手！看我的！”
　　李玄霸身上汗毛倒竖，破口大骂道：“二哥他疯了吗！别管我，赶紧过去！”
　　围绕在李玄霸身边的护卫只留了两人，其他都飞速策马去李世民的身边。
　　李玄霸也慌慌张张策马缀在后面。
　　猎场的猛兽都被圈养磨去了野性，对手持弓箭的人类而言不危险。但就算是后世动物园里的老虎也可能杀人，李玄霸不知道自家只有九岁的二哥怎么会胆子大到和老虎单挑。
　　李玄霸赶到现场的时候，李世民已经和老虎绕起弯来。
　　李世民在前面绕，老虎在后面追，护卫们在老虎后面追，房乔、杜如晦和薛收三人在一旁心惊胆战地看着。
　　见到老虎之后，三人正想商量要怎么让护卫围住老虎，安全地捕获这个大猎物，李世民居然轻踢了一脚马腹，独自冲了出去。
　　三人吓得快从马背上晕过去。
　　“李三郎，快劝劝你哥！”房乔焦急道。
　　李玄霸对着李世民怒吼：“哥！今日之事我一定会写信告诉母亲！”
　　李世民脸上的笑容一滞。
　　他拧身后转，手中弓箭连发，两支箭居然准确无误地钉入了老虎瞪得如铜铃般的双眼中。
　　老虎立刻双爪捂住眼睛，满地翻滚，张大嘴咆哮，陷入狂暴。
　　李世民策马转向，放下弓箭，手持长矛，朝着老虎投掷。
　　在李世民投掷长矛的时候，跟在老虎身后追逐，但不敢放箭，怕误伤李世民的唐国公护卫已经持刀追上了老虎。
　　他们骑马靠近盲眼狂暴老虎，手中马刀往下一划，然后驱使马匹离开，与老虎擦身而过。
　　每次擦身而过，他们的刀都能在老虎身上落下一道血痕。
　　当护卫呈现“X”型全部擦过一次老虎后，老虎已经没了力气。
　　李世民的长矛投到，扎入了老虎的后颈中。
　　老虎怒吼一声，趴到了地上不动弹了。
　　李世民双手高举欢呼：“成功了！”
　　李玄霸翻身下马，来到李世民的马前，拽着二哥的腿，把二哥拖下了马。
　　李世民：“哎？小心些，我会摔到！”
　　“你还知道小心？！独自一个人和老虎搏斗是不是很爽？啊？这么多护卫，需要你一个人逞强？如果马不小心脚滑了，你是不是要给老虎一个滑铲给老虎送饭啊？”李玄霸对着李世民破口大骂，口水星子都溅到了李世民的脸上，“你不要命啦？！”
　　李世民用袖子擦了擦脸：“我有分寸……”
　　李玄霸骂道：“你有个屁的分寸！”
　　李玄霸的心脏都快从喉咙里跳出来了。
　　以前他从史书中看到李世民的“浪”，只是感慨唐太宗确实厉害。
　　现在看到二哥才九岁就撩拨老虎，哪怕是猎场被驯养的老虎，李玄霸都吓得头发都差点竖了起来。
　　他再想起史书中二哥做的那些事。
　　战场上就算了，二哥这个过分喜爱打猎的混蛋，当了皇帝都会抛下侍卫去与熊下马搏斗。
　　你是毛子吗！
　　还是说毛子学的你？！
　　人进化到如今长了脑子就是为了趋利避害和使用工具，你赤手空拳和熊搏斗，是要返祖到野人吗！
　　李世民讪讪道：“喂喂，我没有和熊搏斗。”
　　李玄霸骂道：“是还没有！”
　　李世民捂住耳朵：“别念了别念了，什么只带着一个人亲自当诱饵，没事在禁苑追兔子追鹿，独自和熊搏斗的事我一件都没做过，不要用我没做过的事骂我啊。”
　　李玄霸骂道：“是现在还没有！”
　　在场的人都呆住了。
　　薛收不敢置信地看向房乔：“李三郎这是……这是……”
　　杜如晦高声道：“李三，别说了，还有我们这些外人在呢。”
　　李玄霸话锋一转：“小时候偷针，长大后偷牛！你现在就敢撩拨老虎，长大后肯定会做这些事！我只是未雨绸缪！”
　　李世民翻白眼。弟弟这转折也太生硬了。
　　不过看着围观众人赞同的眼神，李世民无奈地发现，虽然弟弟的转折很生硬，但大家都信了弟弟的鬼话。
　　哦，看房玄龄那满头冒汗的模样，或许只有房玄龄没信。
　　李世民低着头道：“是是是，我错了，我一定反省。放心，将来我一定不会再冒险。”
　　李玄霸磨牙：“你等着，我一定会告诉母亲！你等着挨打吧！”
　　李世民叹气：“行，你告诉吧。”
　　反正母亲得到信后也是许多日后了，等母亲来到东都又是许多日后，他就算要挨打，也要等很久。
　　未来的事未来再说，先把弟弟哄骗住了，好继续打猎。
　　哇哦，我真厉害！居然打到了大老虎！
　　李世民见李玄霸似乎消气了，蹦蹦跳跳来到老虎身旁：“可惜虎皮破了。阿玄！父亲见到我猎的老虎肯定会很羡慕！哼哼，谁让他不陪我打猎，老虎没他的份！”
　　李玄霸刚消气，又憋气。
　　二哥这是完全没反省吧？！
　　不仅李世民没有反省，杜如晦和薛收也下马来到了老虎旁，十分羡慕地夸奖李世民。
　　虽然刚刚看着很惊险，仔细一想，这老虎腿本来就有点瘸，跑不快，所以李世民才会带着老虎遛弯，瞅准机会射中老虎的眼睛。
　　两人冷静下来，才发现李世民不是鲁莽，是真的很自信，在动手的时候已经做好了全盘准备。
　　李二郎真是了不起！
　　李玄霸远离着老虎，背靠着树干生闷气。
　　房乔走到李玄霸身边，压低声音道：“他以后真的还是如此鲁莽？”
　　李玄霸磨牙：“他就算快老死了，性格和现在也没有丝毫改变！”
　　一样的开朗，一样的嘚瑟，一样的浪里个浪！
　　什么唐太宗啊，现在是熊孩子，未来是熊得不行的老顽童！至死都是少年！
　　房乔失笑：“那样也不错。”
　　李玄霸抬头看了房乔一眼，视线重新落到了在老虎身旁跳起了奇奇怪怪舞蹈，还试图拉着杜如晦和薛收一起跳舞的二哥。
　　“嗯，对你们而言，确实不错。”李玄霸平静道。
　　房乔看向被人群环绕的欢快的孩童。
　　这个孩童，真的是他未来的主君吗？真是少年英雄啊。
