Chapter 53: Li Erlang’s First Tiger Hunt

The few of them were all men of scholarly spirit and pure, youthful hearts. The four words "That is all" rang in their ears like the tolling of a bronze bell.

The warm breeze of April blew across their faces, yet it seemed to carry a sudden chill.

Xue Shou tightened his collar and said, "One could argue there is some logic to building the Grand Canal and the Great Wall, even if the pace is reckless. But the palaces... does His Majesty truly feel he does not have enough palaces?"

Du Ruhui sneered, "Are the palaces in the capital not grand enough? If they weren't, didn't he just finish building the Xianren Palace and the Western Garden in the Eastern Capital three years ago?"

Fang Qiao frowned. "When His Majesty toured Jiangdu, he built small auxiliary palaces along both banks of the canal. And that’s not even counting the ten palaces built within the Changfu Garden north of Jiangdu alone: the Guiyan Palace, Huiliu Palace, Jiuli Palace, Songlin Palace, Fenglin Palace, Dalei Palace, Xiaolei Palace, Chuncao Palace, Jiuhua Palace, and Guangfen Palace."

Li Xuanba said calmly, "There is the Linjiang Palace in Yangzi, the Chongye Palace in Weinan, the Douliang Palace in Linhuai, the Linshuo Palace in Zhuojun, and just last year, the Jinyang Palace was built in Taiyuan. Yet, His Majesty still feels it is not enough."

Li Shimin rested his hands behind his head, leaning back against the carriage seat, staring blankly at the swaying roof of the carriage.

Li Xuanba withdrew his gaze from outside the carriage.

"The Emperor spends every day building palaces." The string of names they had just recited, as if listing dishes on a menu, had all been constructed since the first year of the Daye era.

And now, it was only the spring of the fourth year of Daye.

[Brother, Pi Rixiu of the late Tang Dynasty once wrote in his "Lament for the Bian River (Part II)": 'They all say the Sui perished because of this river, yet for a thousand miles, we still rely on its flowing waves. If not for the water-palace and the dragon boat, its merits would rival those of Great Yu.']

Li Shimin’s head slammed against the carriage wall.

*What? My Great Tang hasn't even arrived yet, and we're already at the end of the Tang?!*

[Pi Rixiu was satirizing the extravagance and debauchery of Emperor Yang of Sui, but later generations ignored the "If not for the water-palace and the dragon boat" part and only sighed that "its merits would rival those of Great Yu," actually using this poem to praise Emperor Yang. If Pi Rixiu knew how later generations evaluated his poem, he would likely bash his head against the ground in endless wailing.]

Li Shimin rubbed the back of his head and cast a resentful glance at his brother, whose face remained perfectly calm, showing no sign of the righteous indignation and incessant muttering happening inside his heart.

[Pi Rixiu lived during the time Huang Chao declared himself emperor, witnessing with his own eyes the collapse of the glorious Tang Dynasty. Compared to Du Fu and others who lived through the An Lushan Rebellion and saw the Tang decline from its peak, at least they still held onto the hope of the Tang’s restoration. Pi Rixiu faced a darkness so absolute he couldn't see his own hand.]

Li Shimin’s head began to throb.

*What is the An Lushan Rebellion? And who is Huang Chao? Did the Great Tang just collapse like that? Is there no hope at all?*

*Why am I hearing from my brother that the Great Tang declined and even collapsed before it was even established???*

[What came after the collapse of the Tang? The Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms, an era even darker than the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties—a period so brutal it is almost invisible in films and novels. Pi Rixiu stood right on that precipice.]

Li Shimin’s pupils dilated.

*What?! Could it be even darker and more cruel than the Northern and Southern Dynasties?? Axuan, you’re joking, right? You must be joking, right?*

*Oh no!! Why are there three outsiders in this carriage!! I can't even tell Axuan to shut his heart!!*

[Pi Rixiu’s poetry was entirely dedicated to loyalty and filial piety, expressing his frustration with the times, cursing the rotting court and the dark society, pointing his finger at the faces of foolish and tyrannical rulers. In the end, his use of ancient history to satirize the present—using Emperor Yang of Sui to mock the foolish rulers of the Tang—actually became the stepping stone for Emperor Yang to enter the "Ten Sages of the Net Temple." This is perhaps another form of absurd "using the past to mock the present."]

Li Xuanba remained outwardly composed, though his mind wandered, sighing incessantly.

As a veteran "Taizong hater," most of the people cheering for him in the comment sections were devout believers in the "Ten Sages of the Net Temple." He understood perfectly well the mentality of later generations who praised Emperor Yang of Sui.

*The sin is in the present, but the merit lasts for a thousand generations.* The common people of the Sui bore the suffering, while later generations reaped the rewards—of course they would praise him to the skies.

It was a pity that the Grand Canal and the palaces built by Emperor Yang had already been consumed by the flames of war. If they had survived to become historical sites, his reputation would likely be even higher.

Three years to build dozens of palaces? That was nowhere near enough. He should have built hundreds, one for every city.

Many people compared Emperor Yang of Sui to a low-spec version of Qin Shi Huang.

Qin Shi Huang spent over a decade building the imperial highways and the Great Wall. When he toured the country, he only refurbished the old palaces of the six states and often slept in tents. As the emperor of the first unified dynasty, he only built new palaces in Xianyang; the E-Pang Palace didn't even get past the foundation.

What was Qin Shi Huang? He wasn't even fit to tie the shoes of the "Great Guang God."

Li Xuanba sighed: [Later generations often say the Sui perished because it offended the Guanlong Group. The people couldn't survive, peasant uprisings were everywhere—did the Guanlong Group not advise Emperor Yang to reduce taxes and labor? They did, but those who advised him were all killed. I really wish those "Guang God" fans could travel back to the Sui Dynasty and see if any transmigrator could stop the Sui from falling. They truly think too highly of themselves and too lowly of the "Universal Great Guang God." Brother, what are you doing?!]

Li Shimin turned his head and began banging it against the carriage wall, over and over.

Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Xue Shou, who were just getting indignant, were startled. "Li Er, what’s wrong with you?"

Li Shimin muttered, "What’s wrong? What could be wrong? If Axuan doesn't shut up, I’ll just bash my brains out here."

The three men looked at Li Xuanba, completely bewildered.

Li Xuanba blinked, his expression still very calm—calm, quiet, and well-behaved.

Li Shimin rubbed the red mark on his forehead and complained, "Axuan, can you pick your moments? Even if I have a big heart, I’m still young! My cultivation of inner peace isn't there yet! What if I expose myself?"

Li Xuanba’s eyes drifted. "What did I do? I didn't do anything."

Li Shimin grabbed Li Xuanba’s sunken little cheeks. "Axuan! Li Sanlang! Li Dade!"

Although the three men didn't know what was happening, they hurriedly stopped Li Shimin from "bullying" his younger brother.

"Li Er, what are you doing?"

"Why are you so angry? Let go first!"

"What’s wrong? Why did you suddenly start arguing?"

Li Shimin was pulled away by the three.

Li Xuanba touched his cheeks. Seeing that his second brother seemed genuinely angry, he defended himself, "I didn't say anything I shouldn't have. Why are you reacting so strongly?"

Li Shimin was so angry he raised his foot. Fang Qiao hurriedly pressed Li Shimin’s foot down.

Having known Li Shimin and Li Xuanba for a few months, Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui had both guessed that these two brothers likely had a way of communicating that they couldn't perceive.

Du Ruhui said, "Li San, don't go too far."

Xue Shou looked at them. *Why am I the only one left completely in the dark? What on earth do you all know?*

Seeing Xue Shou’s isolated expression, Fang Qiao explained, "Li Er and Li San are twins. Twins seem to have a way of communicating that outsiders don't understand."

Xue Shou was surprised. "There is such a miraculous thing?"

He scrutinized Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, clicking his tongue in wonder.

Xue Shou didn't ask what Li Xuanba had said to make Li Shimin "fly into a rage." Since it was a secret conversation, even if Li Xuanba said "nothing I shouldn't have," it was likely something they shouldn't pry into.

But although he had read about the mysterious telepathy of twins in books, seeing it in person today made him quite curious.

Young people’s emotions shifted quickly. Although the plight of the common people made them indignant, they all knew that with their current status, the only thing they could do was feel indignant. None of them were people to be swayed by emotion, so they used the "argument" between Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to shift their focus.

Xue Shou asked curiously, "Do you mind if I ask to what extent your telepathy goes?"

Li Shimin said, "It’s just that we can vaguely sense some things."

Xue Shou always felt that the telepathy between these twins was more than just "vague," but since Li Shimin had said so, and although he felt an instant rapport with Li Shimin, they had only just met, so it wasn't appropriate to delve too deep. He just smiled and let it go.

Li Shimin cautioned Li Xuanba, "Stop talking, do you hear me?"

Li Xuanba said, "Fine, fine, alright, alright."

Li Shimin, taking advantage of the others not looking, reached out and tugged at Li Xuanba’s face again. "You’re just humoring me!"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Fine, alright."

Li Shimin finally let go.

Du Ruhui laughed, "I’m sometimes really curious about what Li San says that can make you so agitated."

Li Shimin sneered, "You really want to know?"

Fang Qiao covered Du Ruhui’s mouth. "No, he doesn't want to know."

Fang Qiao remembered the things Li Xuanba had predicted, and cold sweat broke out on his forehead.

Li Xuanba said, "In a few years, I’ll definitely tell you."

Du Ruhui pushed Fang Qiao’s hand away and complained, "Why are you covering my mouth? Li Er and Li San aren't stingy people."

Fang Qiao held his forehead. *You have no idea the power of Li San!*

Fang Qiao had already vaguely guessed the truth behind Li Shimin’s sudden agitation.

Given Li Xuanba’s personality—the kind who would throw prophecies at you the moment he met you—he must have told Li Shimin even more prophecies.

Fang Qiao felt depressed. *Aren't prophecies supposed to be difficult? How is it that Li Xuanba does it as easily as eating or drinking?*

Li Shimin said, "Right, not stingy. If Axuan thinks it’s okay to tell you, he will tell you himself."

Li Xuanba looked at his second brother. "Brother, do you really agree to let me tell them?"

Li Shimin said, "Hmm... generally speaking, it’s better if you don't. But if you think it’s okay, then tell them. I don't care about that anyway."

Li Xuanba teased, "You don't care now, but will you not care in the future?"

Li Shimin smiled and ruffled Li Xuanba’s hair. "I don't know how I’ll be in the future, but I certainly don't care now."

Li Xuanba sighed. "If you have something to say, say it properly. Don't ruffle my hair."

Li Shimin used both hands to ruffle it. "I’ll ruffle it. No matter how impressive you are, you’re still my younger brother. What’s wrong with me ruffling my brother’s hair?"

Xue Shou felt isolated again. *What kind of riddles are these two talking about?*

He looked at Fang Qiao.

Fang Qiao sighed, "Just get used to it. They’re twins, after all."

Du Ruhui laughed, "Let them talk their talk, we’ll talk ours. Didn't we say we were going to write poetry? Let’s continue!"

Xue Shou said, "You still have the mood to write poetry?"

Li Shimin, while still bullying his brother, said, "Why wouldn't I? There are too many injustices in the world. If I felt sorrow every time I saw one, wouldn't I just worry myself to death? Solve what can be solved, set aside what can't, and just eat, drink, and be merry. Worrying won't change the status quo, and being happy won't change it either, so why not be happy?"

Du Ruhui smiled. "Li Er speaks the truth."

Fang Qiao shook his head with a bitter smile. "In terms of broad-mindedness, I often reflect that I am not your equal."

Xue Shou sighed and bowed. "Li Erlang, I have learned much from you."

Li Shimin nodded reservedly and said proudly, "It’s nothing, nothing. I have many other virtues; you can learn them slowly."

The three of them burst into laughter, and Li Xuanba couldn't help but smile too.

He remembered that in history books, Tang Taizong was famous for being a show-off: "My achievements, both great and small, are recorded in bamboo and silk; how could they all be contained?"

When his brother said that line in the future, he would definitely complete the entire sentence in his heart the moment his brother said the first word. He wondered if his brother would still have the thick skin to say the whole thing out loud.

*I’m really looking forward to it.*

...

When they arrived at the imperial hunting grounds, Li Shimin, as he had said, immediately cast the unpleasant matters to the back of his mind.

By the time Li Xuanba finished communicating with the officials of the hunting grounds, Li Shimin had already bolted out like a hunting dog off its leash.

In this era, there wasn't a scholar who didn't know how to ride. But Li Shimin’s speed was so fast that he left Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Xue Shou behind in an instant, with only the guards from the Duke of Tang’s estate keeping up.

The three men looked at each other.

Li Xuanba rode over slowly. Xue Shou said with a hint of anxiety, "Li Sanlang, Li Erlang disappeared in an instant. Shouldn't we send someone to look for him?"

Li Xuanba said, "No need to mind him. As long as the guards follow, it’s fine."

No sooner had he finished speaking than Li Shimin charged out of the woods.

In front of his horse was a rabbit, running blindly in panic.

Li Shimin, who had already drawn his bow and notched an arrow, let it fly. The arrow pierced the poor rabbit’s neck, pinning it to the ground.

Li Shimin slowed his pace, hooked his feet into the stirrups, held the reins with one hand, and with a side-hanging maneuver, plucked the rabbit from the ground. With a tug on the reins, he swung his body back onto the horse’s back.

He laughed and shook the rabbit in his hand. "First blood!"

Xue Shou rubbed his eyes. *Did the arrowhead just bury itself into the ground?*

Du Ruhui clapped and praised, "Li Er, to have such archery and horsemanship at your age, you will surely gallop across the battlefields in the future!"

Li Shimin tied the rabbit to the back of his horse. "I could gallop across the battlefields right now, but unfortunately... Father always says I’m too young and won't let me go to the frontier."

Li Xuanba said irritably, "You actually want to go?"

Li Shimin laughed. "Why shouldn't I want to? Enough talk, hurry up, there’s plenty of prey left!"

Seeing that Li Shimin had already bagged a rabbit, Xue Shou, Du Ruhui, and Fang Qiao were stirred by a competitive spirit, all of them rolling up their sleeves.

*We can't be outdone by a nine-year-old child, can we?*

The four of them spurred their horses into the woods, while Li Xuanba, surrounded by a group of guards, slowly strolled along on his horse.

His horsemanship was decent, but archery... *no thanks!*

It wasn't that Li Xuanba couldn't aim; it was that he truly couldn't pull a bow strong enough to bring down prey.

If only he had a hunting rifle, he would only need to aim, and his hunting results wouldn't necessarily be worse than his brother’s.

It was a pity that even as a transmigrator, he had absolutely no idea how to manufacture firearms.

He remembered the formula for black powder, but the meager power of black powder was a disappointment to his expectations.

He wondered how the powerful gunpowder of ancient times was made. When the Li family was ready to rebel, he would slowly figure it out then.

Anyway, even if he didn't figure it out, his brother could still hack his way through this chaotic world. No rush.

"Third Young Master, there seems to be a beast ahead," a guard said.

Li Xuanba asked, "How do you know?"

The guard replied, "It’s too quiet nearby."

Li Xuanba said, "Then let’s go arou—"

Before he could finish, he heard his brother’s excited shout: "There’s a tiger ahead! Don't any of you move! Watch me!"

Li Xuanba’s hair stood on end, and he cursed, "Is my brother insane?! Don't mind me, hurry over there!"

Only two guards remained around Li Xuanba; the others spurred their horses at full speed toward Li Shimin.

Li Xuanba also hurriedly spurred his horse to follow behind.

The beasts in the hunting grounds were all raised in captivity and had lost their wild nature, making them not dangerous to humans armed with bows and arrows. But even a tiger from a zoo in his past life could kill a person. Li Xuanba didn't know how his nine-year-old brother could be bold enough to challenge a tiger one-on-one.

By the time Li Xuanba arrived at the scene, Li Shimin was already circling with the tiger.

Li Shimin was circling in front, the tiger was chasing behind, the guards were chasing behind the tiger, and Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Xue Shou were watching from the side, terrified.

Upon seeing the tiger, the three of them had been discussing how to have the guards surround it to safely capture such a large prize, when Li Shimin suddenly gave his horse a light kick and charged out alone.

The three were so scared they almost fainted from their saddles.

"Li Sanlang, hurry and persuade your brother!" Fang Qiao said anxiously.

Li Xuanba roared at Li Shimin, "Brother! I will definitely write a letter to Mother about today’s events!"

The smile on Li Shimin’s face froze.

He twisted his body, fired his bow and arrows in rapid succession, and two arrows accurately pinned themselves into the tiger’s eyes, which were wide as copper bells.

The tiger immediately covered its eyes with its paws, rolling on the ground, roaring with its mouth wide open, falling into a frenzy.

Li Shimin turned his horse, put down his bow, grabbed a spear, and threw it at the tiger.

As Li Shimin threw the spear, the Duke of Tang’s guards, who had been chasing behind the tiger but dared not fire for fear of hitting Li Shimin, had caught up with their sabers.

They rode close to the blinded, frenzied tiger, slashed downward with their sabers, and then spurred their horses away, brushing past the tiger.

Every time they brushed past, their blades left a bloody gash on the tiger’s body.

When the guards had all passed the tiger in an "X" formation, the tiger had no strength left.

Li Shimin’s spear arrived, piercing the back of the tiger’s neck.

The tiger let out a roar and collapsed to the ground, motionless.

Li Shimin raised his hands in celebration. "Success!"

Li Xuanba dismounted, walked to the front of Li Shimin’s horse, grabbed his second brother’s leg, and dragged him down.

Li Shimin: "Hey? Be careful, I’ll fall!"

"You know how to be careful?! Is it fun to fight a tiger all by yourself? Huh? With so many guards, do you need to show off alone? If your horse had slipped, were you going to give the tiger a 'sliding tackle' and serve yourself up as a meal?" Li Xuanba cursed at Li Shimin, his spit flying onto Li Shimin’s face. "Do you not want your life?!"

Li Shimin wiped his face with his sleeve. "I had it under control..."

Li Xuanba cursed, "You had nothing under control!"

Li Xuanba’s heart was about to jump out of his throat.

In the past, when he read about Li Shimin’s "wildness" in history books, he only marveled that Tang Taizong was indeed impressive.

Now, seeing his nine-year-old brother provoking a tiger—even if it was a domesticated one from the hunting grounds—Li Xuanba was so scared his hair almost stood up.

He thought of the things his brother did in the history books.

The battlefield was one thing, but this jerk, who was overly fond of hunting, would even abandon his guards to fight a bear on horseback after becoming emperor.

*Are you a Russian?! Or did the Russians learn it from you?!*

*Humans evolved to have brains to avoid harm and use tools. You fight a bear with your bare hands—are you trying to revert to a savage?!*

Li Shimin said sheepishly, "Hey, hey, I didn't fight a bear."

Li Xuanba cursed, "You haven't yet!"

Li Shimin covered his ears. "Stop lecturing, stop lecturing. All that stuff about being a one-man bait, chasing rabbits and deer in the hunting grounds, and fighting bears alone—I haven't done any of that. Don't scold me for things I haven't done."

Li Xuanba cursed, "You haven't yet!"

Everyone present was stunned.

Xue Shou looked at Fang Qiao in disbelief. "Li Sanlang is... this is..."

Du Ruhui said loudly, "Li San, stop talking, there are outsiders here."

Li Xuanba changed his tone. "Stealing needles when young, stealing cows when old! You dare to provoke a tiger now, you’ll definitely do those things when you grow up! I’m just taking precautions!"

Li Shimin rolled his eyes. *My brother’s transition is too stiff.*

However, looking at the approving expressions of the onlookers, Li Shimin realized helplessly that although his brother’s transition was stiff, everyone believed his brother’s nonsense.

*Oh, looking at the sweat on Fang Xuanling’s forehead, perhaps only Fang Xuanling didn't believe it.*

Li Shimin hung his head. "Yes, yes, yes, I was wrong, I will definitely reflect on this. Don't worry, I will never take risks again in the future."

Li Xuanba gritted his teeth. "Just you wait, I’m definitely telling Mother! You wait to get a beating!"

Li Shimin sighed. "Fine, go ahead and tell her."

*Anyway, it will be many days before Mother gets the letter, and many more days before she comes to the Eastern Capital. Even if I have to get a beating, it’ll be a long time from now.*

*Future things can be dealt with in the future. Let’s just coax my brother first so I can keep hunting.*

*Wow, I’m so amazing! I actually hunted a big tiger!*

Seeing that Li Xuanba seemed to have calmed down, Li Shimin hopped over to the tiger. "It’s a pity the tiger skin is ruined. Axuan! Father will definitely be envious when he sees the tiger I hunted! Hmph, who told him not to come hunting with me? No tiger for him!"

Li Xuanba had just calmed down, and now he was fuming again.

*My second brother hasn't reflected at all, has he?!*

Not only did Li Shimin not reflect, but Du Ruhui and Xue Shou also dismounted and came to the tiger’s side, praising Li Shimin with great envy.

Although it looked dangerous just now, upon closer inspection, the tiger’s leg was already a bit lame and it couldn't run fast, which was why Li Shimin had been able to lead it around and wait for the opportunity to shoot it in the eyes.

The two calmed down and realized that Li Shimin wasn't reckless; he was truly confident and had made full preparations before acting.

*Li Erlang is truly remarkable!*

Li Xuanba stayed away from the tiger, leaning against a tree trunk, fuming.

Fang Qiao walked to Li Xuanba’s side and lowered his voice. "Will he really be this reckless in the future?"

Li Xuanba gritted his teeth. "Even when he’s about to die of old age, his personality won't have changed a bit!"

*Just as cheerful, just as showy, just as wild!*

*What kind of Tang Taizong is this? Right now he’s a brat, and in the future, he’ll be an old rascal who’s impossible to control! A youth until the day he dies!*

Fang Qiao chuckled. "That’s not bad either."

Li Xuanba looked up at Fang Qiao, then his gaze fell back on his second brother, who was dancing a strange dance next to the tiger and trying to pull Du Ruhui and Xue Shou into it.

"Hmm, for you all, it is indeed not bad," Li Xuanba said calmly.

Fang Qiao looked at the happy child surrounded by the crowd.

*Is this child really his future lord? What a young hero.*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第54章 奉旨填词李三郎
chunks.chineseText:
第54章 奉旨填词李三郎

=
　　李世民完全没把李玄霸的怒骂放在心上。
　　狩猎了一日， 房乔、杜如晦和薛收的胳膊腿都酸软得睡不好觉，李世民和没事人似的。
　　第二日他挨个叫好友们去狩猎，见没人陪他去， 就独自去狩猎了。
　　李玄霸醒来后， 连忙骑马去寻二哥， 担心二哥又去找猛兽。
　　头一日李玄霸特意去寻找了禁苑的官吏，让他们把猛兽赶得远远的。
　　李世民确实有再猎一头猛兽的想法，可惜没能见到。
　　他想让禁苑的官吏放几头猛兽出来， 但看到弟弟那比猛兽可怕多了的眼神，他只能遗憾地只和兔子、狐狸和鹿玩耍。
　　第三日，房乔、杜如晦和薛收才再次与李世民一起狩猎， 猎物自然不比李世民猎得多。
　　李玄霸每日就只骑马遛弯，一只兔子都没猎到。
　　李世民把自己的猎物挂了一半到李玄霸的马屁股上， 笑道：“就当是阿玄你猎到的了。”
　　李玄霸回头看着血淋淋的马屁股， 露出了嫌弃的神色：“收到马车里去，难道你想挂在马屁股后面招摇过市？”
　　李世民叉腰道：“我就想挂在马屁股后面！”
　　就要炫耀！必须炫耀！
　　李玄霸道：“猎好的猎物要立刻处理了，不然肉会腐坏。你想载一堆腐肉回去？”
　　李世民叉腰的手放了下来，脑袋耷拉得像霜打了的茄子。
　　杜如晦笑着挼了挼李世民垂下的脑袋。
　　房乔从李玄霸的话中预测出李世民会是他将来的主君，本来想矜持些。但看着李世民毫不反抗地被杜如晦挼的模样， 手一痒，也忍不住上前挼了两把。
　　未来主君的脑袋啊。怪不得李三郎让我赶紧挼， 现在不挼，以后就没机会了。
　　李世民看向薛收：“你不摸吗？”
　　薛收：“……你就这么喜欢被人摸脑袋？”
　　李世民叹气：“不喜欢，但习惯了。”
　　薛收犹豫了一会儿， 也上前摸了两把李世民的脑袋。他其实不想摸， 但不能不合群。
　　薛收笑道：“李二郎真是少年英雄。多摸几下， 让我也沾染些英雄气。”
　　房乔和杜如晦纷纷点头赞同。
　　此时论虚岁， 十岁就能猎老虎，也太厉害了。
　　杜如晦道：“当朝猛将韩擒虎十三岁生擒老虎，李二郎十岁猎虎，堪比大隋第一猛将了。”
　　李世民谦虚道：“生擒老虎比猎虎难多了，何况我不是独自猎虎。若没有护卫在，我也不敢与老虎游斗。此次猎虎，护卫有一半功劳，当赏。阿玄，你可不能罚他们。”
　　李玄霸道：“我没说我要罚他们。”
　　李世民道：“我是让你在父亲娘亲面前说说好话，就说是我突然窜了出去，护卫很勇敢地来保护我，明白吗？”
　　李玄霸扫了一眼护卫感激的眼神，叹气道：“好。”
　　他在心里道：【你既然知道你的鲁莽可能会让护卫受罚，就不该这么做。】
　　李世民挠了挠头，有些尴尬地笑了笑。他这不是等猎到老虎后，才想起这件事嘛。
　　见李世民从狩猎的兴奋冷静下来后，第一件事就是叮嘱弟弟一同撒谎保护忠心的护卫，房乔心里涌出暖意。
　　三岁看老，十岁已经完全能看出一个人的内在。
　　怪不得李玄霸说大唐能在李二郎手中迎来盛世，就凭李二郎现在露出的英雄气和一颗仁心，就能看出李二郎未来明君的模样。
　　杜如晦和薛收不知道李二郎会成为他们主君的事，只是单纯越发欣赏李世民。
　　之前他们只是认为李世民这个孩童很聪慧，愿意不看年龄和李世民相交。
　　但人都是崇拜英雄的。李世民虚岁十岁在护卫的帮助下猎到了瘸腿的老虎，武力值先不说，这临危不惧的模样，和现在表现出来的细心和仁慈，都让他们对这位年少的朋友多了几分敬意。
　　三日狩猎结束，李世民带着已经分割好的猎物，十分快乐地回东都。
　　路上，他骑马拦住了一个坐在田埂上休息的老农，询问村长的位置。
　　“这些肉你拿着，虽然不多，也可以邀请村里的老人一起喝一锅肉汤。”李世民将分好的肉都拿了出来，“我当着村人的面把肉给你，可不要独吞。”
　　李世民没有留下姓名，笑着扬鞭离开。
　　沿路又看到了一个村庄，他只留了虎皮和几张较为完整、毛色也较为漂亮的狐狸皮、鹿皮和兔皮，其他的都给了村长，让村长在村民的监督下拿皮子去换钱。
　　把猎物发完后，李世民就没有再停留，径直回城。
　　薛收疑惑李世民的行为。
　　李世民笑道：“我现在做什么都是杯水车薪，但做点事总比不做好。如果沿路撒钱，恐怕会给家里惹来麻烦，只是沿路送掉刚猎的猎物，不过是炫耀而已。这不是什么善事，只是随性而为罢了。”
　　三人心情复杂。
　　正如李世民所说，只是送一点猎物，算不上多大的善事。但这件事就真的没有意义吗？
　　接下来，他们没有偏离回东都的官道，只是在沿路看到了村庄后，也将自己的猎物送了出去。
　　“至少念头通达了。”薛收对李世民作揖道，“此事李二郎当为我师。”
　　李世民摆手：“不敢不敢。下次有机会，我们还一起去狩猎。”
　　薛收直起身体道：“好。”
　　李世民道：“如果有什么诗会也叫我和阿玄一起去玩。杜克明和房玄龄最近也会留在东都，我们多聚聚。”
　　薛收道：“我这就去准备！”
　　结识了新朋友，他当然要和老朋友炫耀炫耀。
　　薛收有一个号称当世第一文人的生父，交友圈子更广泛。
　　杜如晦对自己在隋朝大展宏图的未来还有幻想，很乐意在薛收这里结识更多的人脉。
　　房乔窥见了未来，心态平和了不少。不过现在多结识些人也不错，可以帮主公提前筛选班底。
　　房乔见到了李世民和李玄霸神异的一面，已经完全相信李玄霸的谶纬。
　　再者，他实在是对当朝皇帝太失望了。
　　他知道以自己的性格，在大隋不可能有多远大的前途，一个县令就顶天了。所以李玄霸口中的“房相”，就算是镜中花水中月，他也忍不住想要去相信。
　　反正信一点，又不会对自己有什么危害，为什么不信？
　　回到家后，李世民向李渊炫耀了自己猎到了老虎，李玄霸向李渊告状二哥去猎老虎。
　　李渊先训斥李世民冒险，然后对二儿子亲亲抱抱举高高。
　　大雄真厉害！不愧是我李渊的儿子！
　　李世民得意洋洋：“耶耶射中雀屏的眼睛，我射中老虎的眼睛，我们父子二人都很厉害！阿玄，学着点！”
　　李渊朗声笑道：“阿玄，这一点你一定要向大雄学习。”
　　李玄霸瓮声瓮气道：“是。”这就去给母亲写信！
　　李玄霸的信发出去的时候，李世民把猎到的虎皮、虎鞭和老虎头骨经由李渊送给了杨广。
　　杨广对李世民大夸特夸，给李世民提了半级，李世民升到了从八品的守义尉，俸禄又增加了。
　　杨广开玩笑道：“李三郎，你和二郎是双生兄弟，官职一致才好。你现在可有什么办法让朕升你的官？”
　　李玄霸呈上了早已经准备好的奏疏。
　　杨广惊讶道：“你还真有办法？让朕看看。”
　　他饶有趣味地打开李玄霸的奏疏。
　　李玄霸的奏疏，说的是早已经准备好的定词牌一事。
　　杨广颇好声乐，裴蕴就是广召天下乐户，将宫廷乐人至三万余人，以此讨好了杨广，后来成为杨广朝中“五贵”之一。
　　宋词又名曲子词。如“诗”一样，“诗”最初也是民间歌谣；后来文人参与创作，《诗经》已经颇具文学性；再后来韵律越来越严格，绝句、律诗脱离了音乐，成为一种文体。
　　现在曲子词正好处于“民间歌谣”的时期；到了唐朝，“民谣词”才成为“文人词”；宋朝进入曲子词创造高峰，格律如诗歌发展一样固定；宋朝之后，词便脱离了音乐，也成为一种文体。
　　单凭李玄霸一人，想把“民谣词”往前推一大步，提前进入“文人词”是不可能的。
　　但杨广可以。
　　李玄霸就算要讨好杨广，他仅剩不多的朴素道德观也让他不可能做出危害百姓的事。
　　什么给杨广搜罗几万乐工是不可能的，李玄霸准备给杨广开辟一条新音乐赛道——让文人都来为杨广写歌词。
　　歌曲可以先写曲再填词，也可以先填词再谱曲。
　　杨广是个喜新厌旧的人，现在三万乐工也已经没有新鲜感了。让天下文人来为他写词，他再让乐工依照词来谱曲，用个人在声乐上的爱好创造一个新文体，将宋词变成隋词，提前迎来曲子词的文化盛世。这不是很符合杨广的“大业”？
　　李玄霸这个奏疏完美地戳中了杨广的心。
　　杨广一直坚信自己文武双全。他想要创造的不仅是武功盛世，文化盛世也要创造。
　　杨广很喜欢写诗。他的诗写得也确实不错，但他的嫉妒心非常强，不能容忍其他人的才华在自己之上。
　　薛道衡和王胄的死与诗才无关。但杨广在薛道衡死后，曾道“更能作‘空梁燕落泥’否？”，又在王胄死后，道“‘庭草无人随意绿’，复能作此耶？”，对薛道衡和王胄写出了比他更好的诗耿耿于怀。
　　杨广什么都想当第一。
　　李玄霸将“民谣词”变作当世流行文体的奏疏，既满足了杨广对声乐的喜好，又能满足杨广对文坛开宗立派的野心。
　　杨广心情激动之下，居然起身将李玄霸抱了起来：“是朕嘉侄！”
　　李玄霸僵硬：“陛、陛下，请放侄儿下来，侄儿已经长大了！”
　　李世民嘴角微微抽搐，手收拢在袖子里掐了手背一把，才忍住了笑。
　　杨广将李玄霸放在地上，使劲揉了揉李玄霸的脑袋，开怀笑道：“前人写了几百年的诗，确实该换一换了！朕命你为协律郎，为朕作新声！”
　　李玄霸跪地领命：“臣遵旨！谢陛下！”
　　杨广将李玄霸扶起来，又拍了拍李玄霸的脑袋：“李三郎既为八品职官，从八品的守义尉就不适合你们二人了。今日起，你和李二郎都为正八品的怀仁尉。李三郎为秀才，李二郎能射虎，若不是你二人年幼，至少该由从五品朝散大夫起。”
　　大隋以散实官为本阶。杨广将散实官的“实”和散官的“名”合二为一后，新的散官品阶就是官员的本阶。
　　协律郎是太常寺正八品职官。杨广将李世民和李玄霸的散官官职也提到了正八品，李玄霸入太常寺当值的时候，就不用对比他职官品阶低的官员行礼。
　　李世民和李玄霸都欢喜地谢恩。
　　杨广又道：“李三郎年幼，不需要每日当值，你只用填好词交给太乐署令即可。”
　　杨广想了想，改口道：“还是直接交给朕吧。今日之后，你要稍稍努力些，奉旨为朕填词！先定十首词牌，朕好广召天下文人为朕填词！”
　　李玄霸道：“是。陛下请放心，臣写奏疏的时候，就已经准备好了。”
　　杨广笑道：“你应当也是准备好了。”
　　李世民和李玄霸离开宫殿时，两人脸上的喜色消失。
　　马车上，李世民挠头：“陛下应当是在奖赏我们吧？但陛下的神情和言语，我怎么总觉得有些古怪，心里有些堵？”
　　李玄霸看向马车外繁华的东都城：“为皇帝做‘新声’的协律郎，是一个典故。”
　　李世民抿嘴：“陛下果然话中有话。什么典故？”
　　李玄霸道：“协律郎原称协律都尉，汉武帝因李夫人的兄长李延年善新声，为其置此官。”
　　李世民脸色一沉，磨牙道：“他在侮辱你，侮辱我们家。”
　　李玄霸叹了口气，有些头疼：“应当不是我俩的错。最近勋贵皆对父亲很殷勤，有将父亲捧向勋贵领头人的趋势。他是在敲打我们家。”
　　李延年和李夫人出身倡家。李延年年轻时就因罪遭遇腐刑，在宫廷中养狗，后因其妹李夫人得宠而颇受汉武帝喜爱。
　　李玄霸自己不在乎杨广将他比作李延年。
　　李延年是西汉著名音乐家，所做的事和他一样，就是为音律作新词。其《佳人曲》是后世五言诗的开端。
　　后世极文雅的诗词文体都是由乐工率先填词作为开端，而后再被文人发扬光大。李玄霸现在所做的事，和李延年区别不大。只是李延年是无意开创了五言诗，李玄霸是故意推动“民谣词”向“文人词”发展。
　　但对于唐国公府而言，这确实是侮辱。
　　李延年姓李，唐国公府也姓李。
　　李延年是外戚，唐国公府也能挨上外戚的边。
　　李延年的家族在李夫人死后，先因其弟李季“奸”乱后宫，李延年和李季被族灭，在外攻打大宛的李广利逃过一劫。
　　太子刘据因巫蛊之祸自尽后，李广利与左丞相刘屈氂想要推举李夫人所生皇子刘髆为太子，惹正思念太子的汉武帝震怒，李广利也被族灭。
　　李家至此彻底覆灭。
　　杨广想用李延年之事来敲打李渊。汉武帝时李家的富贵都是因汉武帝起，当他们对汉武帝不忠诚的时候，就举家族灭，生了皇子都没用。
　　李渊的一身富贵也都系于他，若是李渊不忠诚，他也能灭了李渊一族。
　　可唐国公一脉是先因功劳当了唐国公，后碰巧和隋文帝成了连襟，才从勋贵挨上了外戚的边。
　　现在许多勋贵和世族都被赐婚公主，难道他们都变成了外戚？
　　李延年一家还是故倡。用倡人比唐国公府，这侮辱的劲头真是太大了。
　　李世民这么心大的人，都被气得捂着胸口，感到胸口闷疼。
　　气红了眼的李世民道：“我家现在对陛下没有任何不敬不忠，你我二人更是对他百般讨好，他为何如此侮辱我们！”
　　李玄霸帮二哥拍背顺气：“他就是这样多疑，习惯就好。”
　　李世民憋着气，回家后将此事禀报给李渊。
　　李渊沉默了半晌，道：“大德，你不该上这奏疏，过于谄媚了。”
　　李玄霸道：“是我思虑不周。”
　　李世民皱着脸道：“耶耶，你这话就没道理了。他是皇帝，还是我和阿玄的表叔。我们与他之前关系一直不错。无论是身为臣子，还是身为晚辈，阿玄有了新奇的点子都应该告诉他。撰写新词难道是什么丢人的事？不是文人的雅事吗？明明是陛下阴晴不定突然侮辱人没道理，怎么还能说是阿玄的错？”
　　李渊被李世民堵得脸色有点青。
　　李世民看到父亲有些生气，仍旧不依不饶：“陛下此举，明显是敲打父亲，我和阿玄遭了无妄之灾。父亲不自己反省，还怪被牵连的我和阿玄？父亲你怎么如此没担当……哎哟！你恼羞成怒！”
　　李世民被李渊按着揍了一顿。
　　李世民躺在榻上养伤，李渊气冲冲出门，不知道找谁倾诉心中郁闷了。
　　李玄霸黑着脸给二哥背上和屁股上擦药。
　　“二哥，你……”
　　“喂喂，你不会也学父亲，说遭了无妄之灾的我有错吧？”
　　“父亲就是没担当，好面子，你揭穿做什么？活该挨打。”
　　“哼，我就是看不惯他把责任推到我们身上的嘴脸，呕！”
　　李世民就算挨了打，仍旧大逆不道地说父亲的坏话。
　　李玄霸道：“是推到我身上，不是你身上。”
　　李世民将手臂垫在下巴下，回头瞥了弟弟一眼：“我俩一同进宫，一同被陛下侮辱，怎么变成你一个人的事了？你哥我可不是父亲，不肯承担责任。”
　　门外哐当一声，然后是重重的脚步声由近到远消失。
　　李世民和李玄霸同时将视线投向门外。
　　“是父亲吧？”
　　“父亲大概有些后悔，结果走到门口听见你还在骂他，就生气地离开了。”
　　“难道我不该骂他？”
　　“按照孝道，子不言父之过，不该。”
　　“孔子可没这么说过，孔子曰，‘事父母几谏’，见到父母不对的地方要劝谏！”
　　“哥，‘几谏’的含义是委婉劝说，不是直言劝谏。而且这句话后面的‘见志不从，又敬不违，劳而不怨’被你吃了吗？”
　　“对，我饿了，被我吃了。”
　　“……无语。”
　　李渊冷静下来后，有些愧疚地来看望被他一时气昏头揍了的李二郎。
　　走到门口，就听见李二郎骂骂咧咧，气得拂袖而去，把手中带来的药罐都砸了。
　　刚走出院门，李渊又犹豫地停下脚步。
　　他反省后，李二郎说得确实没错，此事不过是陛下借题发挥，故意找茬，两个孩子只是如平常像对待长辈那样对待陛下，很无辜地遭了无妄之灾。李二郎向来护李三郎护得很紧，年纪又小，口不择言，不算什么大事。
　　他不早就知道李大雄是个什么性子？怎么能为孩童置气？
　　于是李渊吩咐身边的仆人再去拿一罐药膏来，转身再次回到了门口。
　　李世民和李玄霸正在争论“子曰”。
　　李渊驻足听了一会儿，听见了李世民的胡搅蛮缠和李玄霸的长吁短叹，心中的恼羞成怒不由消散了不少。
　　他扶额苦笑。
　　罢了罢了，李世民就是这个性子。
　　李渊推开门，板着脸骂道：“大雄，你反省了吗？”
　　李世民扯着嗓子道：“我没错，我为什么要反省？父亲，你反省了吗？”
　　给自己找个台阶下的李渊：“……”
　　李玄霸赶紧张开手臂挡在床榻前：“反省了，我反省了，父亲不要再打二哥了，都是我的错，是我不该为陛下填词，让陛下认为我是在谄媚他，借李延年的典故敲打我。都是我的错……”
　　哭啊！李玄霸！你快哭！
　　干！完全哭不出来！
　　李玄霸正在努力憋眼泪的时候，他身后发出一声响亮的“哇”。
　　“哇呜呜呜！父亲你为什么要欺负弟弟！弟弟根本没错！坏父亲！阿玄！我们回大兴！我们回去找娘亲！不要父亲了！我讨厌父亲！！”
　　李世民悲从心来，之前挨打都倔强地没掉眼泪，现在李玄霸主动揽锅认错，他再也忍不住，呜哇大哭起来。
　　听到二哥的哭声，李玄霸虽然心里不悲痛也不委屈，但不知为何也鼻头一酸，眼眶一红。
　　李渊看着号啕大哭的二儿子，和垂着头无声呜咽的三儿子，手足无措。
　　“不不不，是耶耶的错，别哭了，都别哭了，都是我的错！”
　　李渊掏出帕子不知道该先给谁擦眼泪，一时心中又是愧疚，又是焦急，又是因为皇帝猜忌侮辱他而悲愤，竟也落下泪来。
　　于是屋中父子三人哭作一团。
　　后来李渊和从床榻上爬起来的李世民抱在一起嚎哭。李玄霸的眼泪干涸了，默默地看着这父子二人抱头痛哭。
　　尴尬。
　　脚指头都扣紧了。

Chapter 54: Li Sanlang, Filling Lyrics by Imperial Decree

Li Shimin did not take Li Xuanba’s angry scolding to heart at all.
After a full day of hunting, Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Xue Shou were so sore in their limbs that they couldn’t sleep well, yet Li Shimin acted as if nothing had happened.
The next day, he went around calling his good friends to go hunting again. Seeing that no one would accompany him, he went off to hunt alone.
After Li Xuanba woke up, he hurriedly rode out to find his Second Brother, worried that he might go looking for wild beasts again.
The previous day, Li Xuanba had specifically sought out the officials of the Imperial Park and instructed them to drive the wild beasts far away.
Li Shimin did indeed have the thought of hunting another beast, but unfortunately, he couldn’t find any.
He wanted to ask the officials to release a few, but upon seeing his younger brother’s gaze—which was far more terrifying than any beast—he could only settle for playing with rabbits, foxes, and deer with a sense of regret.
On the third day, Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Xue Shou finally joined Li Shimin for the hunt again, though their haul naturally didn't compare to Li Shimin’s.
Li Xuanba spent every day just riding around, not catching a single rabbit.
Li Shimin hung half of his own prey onto the rear of Li Xuanba’s horse, laughing, "Just pretend these are what you caught, A-Xuan."
Li Xuanba looked back at the bloody horse rump and showed a look of disgust: "Put them in the carriage. Do you intend to parade through the streets with them hanging off the back of the horse?"
Li Shimin stood with his hands on his hips: "I *want* to hang them off the back of the horse!"
He wanted to show off! He had to show off!
Li Xuanba said, "Game must be processed immediately, or the meat will spoil. Do you want to haul a pile of rotting meat back?"
Li Shimin dropped his hands from his hips, his head drooping like a frost-bitten eggplant.
Du Ruhui smiled and ruffled Li Shimin’s drooping head.
Fang Qiao, having predicted from Li Xuanba’s words that Li Shimin would be his future lord, had originally intended to be more reserved. But seeing Li Shimin allow himself to be ruffled by Du Ruhui without any resistance, his hands felt itchy, and he couldn't help but step forward to ruffle his hair a few times as well.
The head of a future lord, indeed. No wonder Li Sanlang told me to hurry up and ruffle it; if I don't do it now, I won't have the chance later.
Li Shimin looked at Xue Shou: "Aren't you going to touch it?"
Xue Shou: "...Do you really like having your head touched that much?"
Li Shimin sighed: "I don't like it, but I'm used to it."
Xue Shou hesitated for a moment before stepping forward to pat Li Shimin’s head a few times. He didn't actually want to, but he couldn't be the odd one out.
Xue Shou laughed, "Li Erlang is truly a young hero. Let me touch a few more times so I can rub off some of that heroic spirit."
Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui nodded in agreement.
At his current age, to be able to hunt a tiger at ten was truly formidable.
Du Ruhui said, "The great general of the current dynasty, Han Qinhu, captured a tiger alive at thirteen. Li Erlang hunting a tiger at ten is comparable to the greatest general of the Sui."
Li Shimin said modestly, "Capturing a tiger alive is much harder than hunting one, and besides, I didn't hunt it alone. If not for the guards, I wouldn't have dared to engage the tiger in a skirmish. In this hunt, the guards deserve half the credit; they should be rewarded. A-Xuan, you must not punish them."
Li Xuanba said, "I never said I was going to punish them."
Li Shimin said, "I mean, you should put in a good word for them before Father and Mother. Just say that I suddenly darted out and the guards bravely came to protect me, understand?"
Li Xuanba glanced at the grateful looks on the guards' faces and sighed: "Fine."
He thought to himself: *Since you knew your recklessness might get the guards punished, you shouldn't have done it in the first place.*
Li Shimin scratched his head and gave an awkward laugh. He hadn't thought of that until after he’d already hunted the tiger.
Seeing that after Li Shimin calmed down from the excitement of the hunt, his first priority was to instruct his brother to lie together to protect the loyal guards, warmth surged in Fang Qiao’s heart.
A person’s character can be seen at three; at ten, one can fully see a person’s inner nature.
It was no wonder Li Xuanba said the Great Tang would usher in a golden age under Li Erlang. Just by the heroic spirit and the benevolent heart Li Erlang was showing now, one could already see the image of a future wise monarch.
Du Ruhui and Xue Shou didn't know that Li Erlang would become their lord; they simply admired Li Shimin more and more.
Before, they only thought this child was very intelligent and were willing to overlook his age to befriend him.
But people always admire heroes. Li Erlang, at ten years old, had hunted a lame tiger with the help of his guards. Putting aside his martial prowess, his composure in the face of danger, and the care and benevolence he displayed, all made them hold this young friend in higher regard.
The three-day hunt ended, and Li Shimin returned to the Eastern Capital, very happy with his butchered game.
On the way, he stopped his horse to talk to an old farmer resting on a ridge, asking for the location of the village head.
"Take this meat. Although it’s not much, you can invite the village elders to have a pot of meat soup together," Li Shimin said, bringing out all the divided meat. "I am giving this to you in front of the villagers, so don't keep it all for yourself."
Li Shimin didn't leave his name; he just smiled, flicked his whip, and rode off.
Along the way, he saw another village. He kept only the tiger skin and a few of the more intact, beautiful fox, deer, and rabbit pelts, giving the rest to the village head and telling him to exchange the skins for money under the supervision of the villagers.
After distributing the game, Li Shimin didn't linger and headed straight back to the city.
Xue Shou was puzzled by Li Shimin’s actions.
Li Shimin laughed, "Whatever I do now is just a drop in the bucket, but doing something is better than doing nothing. If I were to scatter money along the road, it would likely bring trouble to my family. Giving away the game I just hunted is merely showing off. This isn't some great act of charity; it’s just acting on a whim."
The three of them felt conflicted.
Just as Li Shimin said, giving away a little game didn't count as a great act of charity. But was this act truly meaningless?
From then on, they didn't deviate from the main road back to the Eastern Capital, but whenever they saw a village along the way, they also gave away their own game.
"At the very least, my mind is now clear," Xue Shou said, bowing to Li Shimin. "In this matter, Li Erlang shall be my teacher."
Li Shimin waved his hand: "I wouldn't dare. Next time there's an opportunity, let's go hunting together again."
Xue Shou straightened up and said, "Agreed."
Li Shimin said, "If there are any poetry gatherings, call me and A-Xuan to join in. Du Keming and Fang Xuanling will also be staying in the Eastern Capital recently, so let's gather more often."
Xue Shou said, "I shall go prepare at once!"
Having made new friends, he naturally wanted to show off to his old ones.
Xue Shou had a father known as the foremost man of letters of the age, and his social circle was even wider.
Du Ruhui still had fantasies about making great achievements in the Sui Dynasty and was very happy to build more connections through Xue Shou.
Fang Qiao had caught a glimpse of the future and his mindset was much more peaceful. However, making more acquaintances now wasn't bad; he could help his future lord screen his staff in advance.
Having seen the miraculous side of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Fang Qiao now completely believed in Li Xuanba’s prophecies.
Furthermore, he was truly too disappointed in the current emperor.
He knew that with his personality, he couldn't have a grand future in the Great Sui; being a county magistrate would be the limit. So, even if the "Prime Minister Fang" Li Xuanba spoke of was like a flower in a mirror or the moon in the water, he couldn't help but want to believe it.
Besides, believing a little wouldn't do him any harm, so why not?
Upon returning home, Li Shimin boasted to Li Yuan about hunting a tiger, while Li Xuanba complained to Li Yuan about his Second Brother going to hunt a tiger.
Li Yuan first scolded Li Shimin for taking risks, then kissed and hugged his second son, lifting him high.
*Daxiong is truly amazing! Worthy of being my, Li Yuan’s, son!*
Li Shimin was triumphant: "Father shot the eye of the peacock on the screen, and I shot the eye of a tiger. Both of us father and son are very capable! A-Xuan, learn from this!"
Li Yuan laughed heartily: "A-Xuan, you must learn from Daxiong in this regard."
Li Xuanba said in a muffled voice: "Yes." *I’ll go write a letter to Mother right now!*
When Li Xuanba’s letter was sent out, Li Shimin had the tiger skin, tiger penis, and tiger skull sent to Yang Guang through Li Yuan.
Yang Guang praised Li Shimin profusely and promoted him by half a rank, making Li Shimin a Shouyi Lieutenant of the Minor Eighth Rank, with an increase in his salary.
Yang Guang joked: "Li Sanlang, you and Erlang are twins; it would be better if your official ranks were the same. Do you have any way for Me to promote you?"
Li Xuanba presented a memorial he had long since prepared.
Yang Guang was surprised: "You really have a way? Let Me see."
He opened Li Xuanba’s memorial with great interest.
Li Xuanba’s memorial was about the matter of standardizing "Ci" (lyric) patterns, which he had long since prepared.
Yang Guang was quite fond of music. Pei Yun had once gathered tens of thousands of court musicians from across the realm to please Yang Guang, later becoming one of the "Five Nobles" in Yang Guang’s court.
Song Ci is also known as "Quzi Ci" (song lyrics). Like "Shi" (poetry), "Shi" was originally folk songs; later, literati participated in their creation, and the *Book of Songs* already possessed significant literary quality; later still, the rhythms became increasingly strict, and Jueju and Lushi broke away from music to become a literary genre.
Currently, Quzi Ci was in the "folk song" stage; by the Tang Dynasty, "folk lyrics" would become "literati lyrics"; the Song Dynasty entered the peak of Quzi Ci creation, with prosody fixed just like the development of poetry; after the Song Dynasty, lyrics would break away from music and also become a literary genre.
For Li Xuanba alone to push "folk lyrics" a big step forward and enter the "literati lyrics" stage ahead of time was impossible.
But Yang Guang could.
Even if Li Xuanba wanted to please Yang Guang, his remaining simple moral compass made it impossible for him to do anything that would harm the people.
Gathering tens of thousands of musicians for Yang Guang was out of the question, so Li Xuanba prepared to open a new musical track for Yang Guang—letting the literati come and write lyrics for him.
Songs could be written by composing the melody first and then filling in the lyrics, or by filling in the lyrics first and then composing the melody.
Yang Guang was a person who liked the new and tired of the old; he no longer felt any freshness from the thirty thousand musicians he already had. Letting the literati of the world write lyrics for him, and then having the musicians compose melodies based on those lyrics, using his personal hobby in music to create a new literary genre, turning "Song Ci" into "Sui Ci" and ushering in a cultural golden age of Quzi Ci ahead of schedule—didn't this fit perfectly with Yang Guang’s "Great Enterprise"?
Li Xuanba’s memorial struck a chord with Yang Guang.
Yang Guang had always firmly believed that he was talented in both civil and martial arts. He wanted to create not only a golden age of martial achievements but also a golden age of culture.
Yang Guang loved writing poetry. His poetry was indeed quite good, but he was extremely jealous and could not tolerate anyone else’s talent surpassing his own.
The deaths of Xue Daoheng and Wang Zhou had nothing to do with their poetic talent. But after Xue Daoheng died, Yang Guang had said, "Can you still write 'The swallows fall into the mud from the empty beam'?" And after Wang Zhou died, he said, "'The garden grass grows green as it pleases without anyone,' can you still write this?" He held a grudge because they had written poems better than his.
Yang Guang wanted to be number one in everything.
Li Xuanba’s memorial to turn "folk lyrics" into the popular literary genre of the day not only satisfied Yang Guang’s love for music but also his ambition to be the founder of a school in the literary world.
In his excitement, Yang Guang actually stood up and picked Li Xuanba up: "You are truly My good nephew!"
Li Xuanba stiffened: "Your... Your Majesty, please put me down, I have already grown up!"
The corners of Li Shimin’s mouth twitched slightly; he tucked his hands into his sleeves and pinched the back of his hand to hold back his laughter.
Yang Guang set Li Xuanba on the ground, ruffled his hair vigorously, and laughed heartily: "People have been writing poetry for hundreds of years; it is indeed time for a change! I appoint you as a Harmonizer of Rhythms (Xielü Lang) to compose new sounds for Me!"
Li Xuanba knelt to accept the order: "Your subject obeys the decree! Thank you, Your Majesty!"
Yang Guang helped Li Xuanba up and patted his head again: "Since Li Sanlang is now an official of the eighth rank, the Minor Eighth Rank Shouyi Lieutenant is no longer suitable for the two of you. From today on, you and Li Erlang are both Eighth Rank Huairen Lieutenants. Li Sanlang is a *Xiucai* (cultivated talent), and Li Erlang can hunt tigers; if it weren't for your youth, you should have started at least as a Minor Fifth Rank Court Gentleman for Ceremonial."
The Great Sui used the "scattered official rank" as the base rank. After Yang Guang merged the "actual" and the "name" of the scattered officials, the new rank became the official’s base rank.
The Harmonizer of Rhythms was an Eighth Rank official in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Yang Guang had raised the scattered official ranks of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to the eighth rank, so when Li Xuanba went to serve in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he wouldn't have to bow to officials of lower rank than his own.
Both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba happily thanked him for the grace.
Yang Guang added: "Li Sanlang is young and does not need to be on duty every day; you only need to fill in the lyrics and hand them to the Director of the Office of Music."
Yang Guang thought for a moment and changed his mind: "Actually, just hand them directly to Me. After today, you must work a little harder and fill in lyrics for Me by imperial decree! First, set ten lyric patterns so I can widely summon the literati of the world to fill them in for Me!"
Li Xuanba said: "Yes. Please rest assured, Your Majesty; I had already prepared them when I wrote the memorial."
Yang Guang laughed: "I suppose you were already prepared."
When Li Shimin and Li Xuanba left the palace, the joy on their faces vanished.
In the carriage, Li Shimin scratched his head: "His Majesty should be rewarding us, right? But why do I feel that His Majesty’s expression and words were a bit strange, and I feel a bit stifled in my heart?"
Li Xuanba looked at the bustling Eastern Capital outside the carriage: "The Harmonizer of Rhythms who creates 'new sounds' for the emperor is an allusion."
Li Shimin pursed his lips: "His Majesty really had hidden meaning in his words. What allusion?"
Li Xuanba said: "The Harmonizer of Rhythms was originally called the Commandant of Harmonizing Rhythms. Emperor Wu of Han established this office because Lady Li’s elder brother, Li Yannian, was skilled at new sounds."
Li Shimin’s face darkened, and he ground his teeth: "He is insulting you, insulting our family."
Li Xuanba sighed, feeling a headache coming on: "It shouldn't be our fault. Recently, the nobles have all been very attentive to Father, with a trend of pushing Father toward becoming the leader of the nobility. He is warning our family."
Li Yannian and Lady Li came from a family of entertainers. Li Yannian had been subjected to castration due to a crime in his youth and had raised dogs in the palace; later, because his sister, Lady Li, was favored, he was highly regarded by Emperor Wu of Han.
Li Xuanba himself didn't care about being compared to Li Yannian by Yang Guang.
Li Yannian was a famous musician of the Western Han Dynasty, and what he did was the same as what he was doing—composing new lyrics for melodies. His *Song of the Beautiful Lady* was the beginning of the five-character poetry of later generations.
The highly refined poetic styles of later generations all started with musicians filling in lyrics, which were then carried forward by the literati. What Li Xuanba was doing now was not much different from Li Yannian. It was just that Li Yannian had accidentally pioneered five-character poetry, while Li Xuanba was deliberately pushing "folk lyrics" toward "literati lyrics."
But for the Tang Duke’s mansion, this was indeed an insult.
Li Yannian’s surname was Li, and the Tang Duke’s mansion was also surnamed Li.
Li Yannian was an imperial relative by marriage, and the Tang Duke’s mansion could also be considered an imperial relative.
After Lady Li died, Li Yannian’s family was wiped out because his younger brother, Li Ji, committed adultery in the inner palace; Li Yannian and Li Ji were executed, while Li Guangli, who was attacking Dayuan, escaped the disaster.
After Crown Prince Liu Ju committed suicide due to the witchcraft disaster, Li Guangli and the Left Chancellor Liu Quli wanted to push the prince born to Lady Li, Liu Bo, as crown prince, which enraged Emperor Wu of Han, who was missing his crown prince, and Li Guangli’s family was also wiped out.
The Li family was completely destroyed from then on.
Yang Guang wanted to use the affair of Li Yannian to warn Li Yuan. The wealth of the Li family during the time of Emperor Wu of Han was all due to Emperor Wu; when they were not loyal to him, the whole family was wiped out, and even having a prince didn't help.
All of Li Yuan’s wealth was tied to him; if Li Yuan were not loyal, he could also wipe out Li Yuan’s entire clan.
But the Tang Duke’s lineage had become the Tang Duke first due to merit, and then happened to become brothers-in-law with Emperor Wen of Sui, only then touching the edge of being imperial relatives.
Now, many nobles and aristocratic families had been granted princesses in marriage; did that mean they all became imperial relatives?
The Li Yannian family were also former entertainers. Using entertainers to compare to the Tang Duke’s mansion was a truly massive insult.
Even someone as thick-skinned as Li Shimin was so angry that he clutched his chest, feeling a dull pain.
With red eyes from anger, Li Shimin said: "Our family has shown no disrespect or disloyalty to His Majesty, and you and I have been doing everything to please him. Why does he insult us like this!"
Li Xuanba patted his Second Brother’s back to help him breathe: "He is just this suspicious; you’ll get used to it."
Li Shimin held his breath, and upon returning home, he reported the matter to Li Yuan.
Li Yuan was silent for a long while before saying: "Dade, you shouldn't have submitted this memorial; it was too sycophantic."
Li Xuanba said: "It was my lack of consideration."
Li Shimin frowned and said: "Father, that makes no sense. He is the Emperor, and also our cousin-uncle. Our relationship with him has always been good. Whether as a subject or a junior, if A-Xuan has a novel idea, he should tell him. Is writing new lyrics something shameful? Isn't it an elegant pursuit for a literatus? It is clearly His Majesty who is fickle and insulting people for no reason; how can you say it is A-Xuan’s fault?"
Li Yuan’s face turned a bit green from being blocked by Li Shimin.
Seeing his father getting angry, Li Shimin remained unrelenting: "His Majesty’s action is clearly a warning to you, Father, and A-Xuan and I have suffered an unprovoked disaster. You don't reflect on yourself, Father, but instead blame A-Xuan and me for being implicated? How can you be so irresponsible... Ouch! You’re acting out of shame!"
Li Shimin was pinned down and beaten by Li Yuan.
Li Shimin lay on the couch recovering from his injuries, while Li Yuan stormed out, not knowing who to vent his frustration to.
Li Xuanba applied medicine to his Second Brother’s back and buttocks with a dark face.
"Second Brother, you..."
"Hey, hey, don't tell me you're going to learn from Father and say that I, who suffered an unprovoked disaster, am at fault?"
"Father is just irresponsible and cares about his face; why did you have to expose him? You deserved the beating."
"Hmph, I just can't stand the look on his face when he pushes the responsibility onto us, ugh!"
Even after being beaten, Li Shimin still spoke ill of his father in an unfilial manner.
Li Xuanba said: "It was pushed onto me, not you."
Li Shimin rested his chin on his arms and glanced back at his younger brother: "We both went into the palace together and were both insulted by His Majesty together; how did it become your own affair? Your brother here is not like Father; I am willing to take responsibility."
There was a clatter outside the door, followed by heavy footsteps that faded from near to far.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba both turned their gazes to the door.
"Was that Father?"
"Father probably regretted it, but walked to the door, heard you still scolding him, and left in anger."
"Should I not have scolded him?"
"According to filial piety, a son should not speak of a father’s faults; you shouldn't have."
"Confucius never said that. Confucius said, 'In serving one’s parents, one may gently remonstrate.' When you see your parents doing something wrong, you should remonstrate!"
"Brother, the meaning of 'gently remonstrate' is to advise tactfully, not to speak bluntly. And did you eat the part of that sentence that says, 'If they do not follow your will, you should still be respectful and not disobey, and work hard without resentment'?"
"Right, I was hungry, so I ate it."
"…Speechless."
After Li Yuan calmed down, he felt a bit guilty and came to visit Li Erlang, whom he had beaten in a fit of rage.
When he reached the door, he heard Li Erlang cursing and swearing, and he left in a huff, smashing the medicine jar he had brought with him.
Just as he stepped out of the courtyard gate, Li Yuan hesitated and stopped.
After reflecting, Li Erlang was indeed right; this matter was just His Majesty making a mountain out of a molehill and deliberately looking for trouble. The two children had just treated His Majesty as they would any elder, and they had innocently suffered an unprovoked disaster. Li Erlang had always been very protective of Li Sanlang, and being young, he spoke without thinking; it wasn't a big deal.
Hadn't he known what kind of personality Li Daxiong had for a long time? How could he get angry at a child?
So, Li Yuan ordered his servant to get another jar of ointment and turned back to the door.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were arguing about "The Master said."
Li Yuan stopped to listen for a while, hearing Li Shimin’s sophistry and Li Xuanba’s long sighs, and his anger and shame couldn't help but dissipate quite a bit.
He held his forehead and smiled bitterly.
*Forget it, forget it. Li Shimin is just this kind of person.*
Li Yuan pushed the door open and scolded with a straight face: "Daxiong, have you reflected on yourself?"
Li Shimin shouted at the top of his lungs: "I did nothing wrong; why should I reflect? Father, have you reflected on yourself?"
Li Yuan, who was looking for a way to step down: "..."
Li Xuanba hurriedly spread his arms to block the bed: "I have reflected, I have reflected! Father, please don't hit Second Brother anymore; it’s all my fault. I shouldn't have filled in lyrics for His Majesty, making him think I was sycophantic and using Li Yannian’s allusion to warn me. It’s all my fault..."
*Cry! Li Xuanba! Hurry up and cry!*
*Damn! I can't cry at all!*
Just as Li Xuanba was trying hard to squeeze out tears, a loud "waa" came from behind him.
"Waa-hoo-hoo! Father, why are you bullying my brother! My brother did nothing wrong! Bad Father! A-Xuan! Let’s go back to Daxing! Let’s go back and find Mother! We don't want Father anymore! I hate Father!!"
Li Shimin felt a surge of sorrow; he hadn't shed a tear even when he was beaten earlier, but now that Li Xuanba had taken the blame, he couldn't hold back anymore and burst into loud sobs.
Hearing his Second Brother’s crying, although Li Xuanba didn't feel sorrowful or aggrieved, for some reason, his nose felt sore and his eyes turned red.
Li Yuan looked at his second son wailing loudly and his third son sobbing silently with his head down, and he was at a loss.
"No, no, no, it’s Yeye’s fault. Don't cry, neither of you cry, it’s all my fault!"
Li Yuan took out a handkerchief, not knowing whose tears to wipe first. For a moment, he felt both guilty and anxious, and then, feeling indignant at the Emperor’s suspicion and insult, he also burst into tears.
And so, the father and his two sons in the room cried together in a heap.
Later, Li Yuan and Li Shimin, who had climbed off the bed, hugged each other and wailed. Li Xuanba’s tears had dried up, and he watched the father and son hugging and crying.
Awkward.
His toes were curled tight.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第55章 准备派人去南海 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第55章 准备派人去南海

=

“李渊把李二郎狠揍了一顿， 李二郎伤得起不了身？”杨广听了汇报，有些愕然。

探子道：“回陛下，李二郎和李三郎回府后将升官之事告知了唐国公， 唐国公给他们解释了李延年的典故后， 就发怒要揍李三郎。李二郎担心李三郎病弱， 经不住唐国公的教训，便自愿替李三郎，多挨了一倍的棍子， 所以伤势有些严重。”

探子犹豫了一番，还是继续禀报道：“唐国公还说，说李延年是汉武帝男宠……”

杨广手一挥， 桌案上的果盘杯盏“哗啦”扫落，碎了一地。

杨广冷笑道：“怎么？李渊认为我对李三郎有非分之心？！”

探子忙磕头道：“唐国公可能没有此意， 只是骂李三郎不知检点， 谄媚陛下，侮辱唐国公府门风。”

杨广深呼吸，将心中怒气压下：“李二郎和李三郎如何说？”

探子道：“李二郎和李三郎辩解，他们只是对待陛下如亲父一样，陛下对待他们也如亲子一般， 并无谄媚之事。”

杨广沉默许久，让宫人把地上碎片收起来， 命探子回唐国公府。

杨广屏退众宫人，低头翻看李玄霸呈上来的奏疏。

半晌，杨广叹息道：“朕该直接敲打李渊。”

他本以为李渊是一个心思深沉的人， 自己敲打他的儿子， 就等于敲打他。谁知道李渊居然将过错全部推给了年幼的李世民和李玄霸， 还连累李世民挨了一顿毒打。

杨广想起， 姨母在世的时候，似乎因为李渊和老夫人偏袒李建成，闹出了很大的笑话。

李二郎和李三郎为嫡长兄让路是合乎礼法的事。杨广虽然自己夺嫡，但不希望其他人挑战礼法。

但李二郎和李三郎毕竟与他更亲近些，见到李二郎和李三郎被毒打辱骂，杨广又想起唐国公府偏心之事，难免有些不喜李渊的做法了。

“不直接敲打李渊，也该敲打李建成，不该把李二郎和李三郎牵扯进去。”杨广又道，“看来唐国公府，只有李渊和李建成二人有敲打的价值。”

……

李玄霸此次来洛阳，要把书铺和香皂铺子的产业铺到东都。

杨广非常不喜欢回大兴。他除了南巡北巡，其他时间都待在东都。在大业期间，东都比京城更繁华，西域客商、外国使团都在东都云集，李玄霸更容易赚钱和花钱。

李世民虽挨了一顿打，但李渊是用手揍的，背上和屁股肿得厉害，消得也快。

李玄霸见二哥无事，留二哥自己趴着把兵书当闲书看打发时间，自己出门巡视产业。

东都城是新建的，就连赐给勋贵的宅子都宽敞许多，市集店铺后面的工坊面积也比大兴城宽广。

印刷工坊设在市集内，香皂工坊仍旧在东都城郊的庄子中。

杨广又兴徭役，一些不堪重负的人家自卖其身逃避沉重徭役。李玄霸趁机买进了一些人，充实了洛阳的工坊。现在工坊早已经营业。

李玄霸先巡视了城郊的香皂工坊，然后回到城内，与印刷工坊内的校对师傅聊了几句。

汉字是象形文字，排版工匠可以不识字，比对图形排版就行。但校对的人会识字，效率和准确率都会高许多。

现在寒门士子仍旧很难找到出仕的机会，只能在世家勋贵招门客、文吏的时候投名帖碰运气。

一些小世家或者世家旁系子弟也要先在世家勋贵中做家臣，等候被主家举荐的机会。

当年名噪一时的“王谢”世家，谢安发迹前就在王家当过家臣。

很多文人在等候机会时都要找些事做。只要识字，工作很好找。抄书的，代写信的，卖字画的，当账房先生的，只要肯拉下脸来，读书人是稀缺资源，总能找到事干。

原本书铺抄书是读书人赚取生活费的最主要途径。印刷术兴起后，他们本来抱怨少了一大笔进账。没想到唐国公府的印刷铺招的文人比以前还多。

文人们不需要再抄书，只需要坐在印刷工坊里帮忙校对。因印刷书籍很多，所以校对任务很紧张，需要的文人不少，除了油墨味道难闻了些，包吃住还有奖金，待遇相当不错。

贫寒学子们不再抱怨了，挤破了头想入职。

都城居不易，寻一个包吃住的地方很不容易。何况这可是唐国公府的铺子，有机会碰到贵人。说不定哪一日自己就被贵人看中，被招为家臣文吏了。

李玄霸确实存了用校对师傅这个职位招揽寒门遗漏人才的心思。不然他就让唐国公府的家仆们来当校对师傅了。家仆们大多都是识字的，只需要给月俸，花的钱更少。

没有印刷术的时代，寒门读书极其困难，很难出现人才。他知道捡漏的可能性不大，不如按照史书上二哥下属的名字挨个敲门。

但二哥的下属是二哥的，李玄霸自己也需要人手。

李建成的下属就盯着李建成嫡长子的地位，连二哥都看不上，自己更别想了。李玄霸想了想自己的性格，还是从寒门士子中寻找吧。

刘邦和朱元璋能从自家穷哥们中扒拉出一群开国元勋，可见先天条件虽然很重要，后天培养也不能忽视。自己又不是扒拉开国元勋，只是一个小小亲王府的官吏而已，只要能识字，够机灵，再观察一下品行，还是能找到能用的人。

现在李玄霸就对面前这个校对师傅很满意。

校对师傅叫颜真，字自实，与写《颜氏家训》的颜家没有任何关系。

寒门士子不代表普通老百姓。颜真是官宦之后，祖父当过陈朝的县令，父亲在家耕读，现在已经是正宗的寒门。

颜真也想走科举的路。但大隋的科举和察举制差不多，没有五品官的推荐，颜真连科举的资格都没有。

颜真心高气傲，总觉得自己的才华不错，一定能被贵人看中，于是凑了些盘缠来东都找机会。

李玄霸不记得史书中有颜真这个人。

或许他碰壁后灰溜溜回家了，或许他如愿以偿当了个没资格入史书的官吏。

颜真的学识很一般，这是寒门士子的通病。但他脑袋很灵活，又放得下身段，是李玄霸招的校对师傅中难得能与印刷工坊的工匠们打成一片的人。

颜真与工匠们关系不错，不是演出来给他人看的人设。因为这个时代的人对身份地位十分看重，他们不会认为堂堂唐国公府的小郎君们居然喜欢这种离经叛道的人设。

李玄霸虽然现在是唐国公府的三郎君，但他的灵魂本质还是前世那个底层小市民，所以他对颜真感官不错。

李玄霸在心中把颜真划到自己名下后，便常与颜真讨论经书，补足颜真的短板。

他从接触中知道颜真虽是“寒门”，家父在家耕读，但家母经商有道，其实不缺钱。颜真努力挤进印刷铺子当校对师傅，是冲着高老师和宇文老师注解的儒经来的。

虽说可以购买印刷版，但颜真认为来当校对师傅，每日都会重复看很多遍儒经，不仅省钱，背诵效率也更高，还能与印刷工坊的匠人们谈天说地，比自己一个人闷头读书有趣。

李玄霸问道：“你对金钱斤斤计较，看来也是个经商的好苗子。若我让你替我经商如何？”

颜真笑道：“能替三郎君做事，我就算发达了，经商也没关系。反正我若没出息，回家后也是要继承母亲衣钵，跟着母亲经商的。”

李玄霸道：“如果要出远门，去外夷经商呢？”

颜真笑得更开心了：“去外夷经商，那就不是普通商人了。三郎君是要收我做家臣吗？”

李玄霸道：“我还小，没资格收家臣。不过你若是肯帮我，待我能收家臣的时候，你就是我的家臣了。”

听到李玄霸肯定的话，颜真却笑不出来了。

初次见面的时候，李玄霸显得很沉默冷峻，不似孩童。但多见了几次，颜真发觉李玄霸其实挺健谈，偶尔也会开玩笑，所以和李玄霸说话时较为随意。

但李玄霸毕竟年纪不大，他虽早听闻唐国公府三郎君的才名，只以为李玄霸只是在读书上是神童，没想到李玄霸居然真的要招他为家臣。

颜真严肃道：“若三郎君抬举在下，在下愿为三郎君效犬马之劳。只是三郎君不再考虑吗？以三郎君的地位，长大后选家境较差的世家子弟为家臣文吏也轻而易举。”

李玄霸道：“我用人不看家世，只看眼缘。”

颜真愣了一下，苦笑道：“是眼缘，不是才华？”

李玄霸半开玩笑道：“你还没有显示出自己的才华，我如何看才华？所以这次我给你一个展现自己长处的机会。”

颜真叹了口气，拱手作揖道：“在下惶恐。但……请三郎君给在下这个机会！”

李玄霸道：“好。不过你还是先写信告知父母。若你父母认为‘父母在，不远游’，你还是以孝为主。我可以为你寻其他事做。”

颜真道：“兄长在家奉养父母。我自来东都后，父亲母亲就笑称，当做没我这个儿子，让我自行寻找前程。若实在是过不下去，再回家磕头认错，给我一份家产从商去。所以三郎君尽可放心。”

李玄霸道：“那就过来，我和你介绍一下你需要做的事。”

李玄霸带着颜真来到了印刷工坊中自己休息的房间，从怀里拿出了一卷书稿递给颜真。

这一卷书稿记录了南海诸国的情况。

李玄霸道：“陛下即将派屯田主事常骏、虞部主事王君政出使赤土国。我已经和常主事和王主事说好，你以商人身份跟随使臣前往赤土国，在沿路诸国为我搜集一些特产。”

赤土国的位置在后世的马来半岛，即东南亚。

颜真本以为李玄霸是想搜集象牙、香料等传统海货。李玄霸在各个国家标注的想要搜集的特产，却是一些如今大隋也能见到的农作物，比如小麦、水稻、甘蔗之类。

颜真好奇：“三郎君可否能告知在下挑选特产的原因？在下才好知道该定什么标准。”

李玄霸道：“令尊耕读，你跟着下过地吗？”

颜真道：“在下会种地。”

李玄霸道：“育种选种有了解吗？”

颜真思索了一会儿，恍然大悟道：“种田的种子不能一直用自家田地留存的种子，产量会逐年降低。父亲常与周围农家交换种子，一块地里有时候还会种上从不同地方搜集的同样种类的种子。三郎君是想引进外夷的种子？”

李玄霸没想到颜真居然一口说中了重点。看来颜真父亲的“耕读”不是做个样子，是真的有认真在耕种。

他对颜真的父亲有一些好奇了。

县令之子也是官宦之子，他还娶了豪商之女，家境肯定不差。这样的人能认真琢磨农事，说不定好好培养一下，能写部农书出来。

李玄霸道：“我让你搜集外夷作物，确实是想试着与中土作物混杂种植，看能不能培育出更好的品种。再者，他们本地一些特色农作物，说不定也能移植到中土来。”

李玄霸虽然没有亲手种过田，但网上讨论种田是热门话题，他对简单的种田知识略知皮毛，知道一个国家的粮食种子种类越杂越好，许多高产作物都是杂交出来的。

虽然后世的救荒高产作物大多来自美洲，除非他哥当皇帝，否则自己想要去寻找美洲十分困难。但东南亚和南亚也有许多农作物可以引进。

比如甘蔗和粗绒棉。

华夏很早就开始种植甘蔗，但制造蔗糖的技术不发达，甘蔗多直接取汁食用。

东南亚和南亚的甘蔗品种更好，出汁率更高，还有独特的制糖技术。

隋唐高层都嗜甜，唐太宗就是其中翘楚。

唐太宗曾派人去印度求取更好的甘蔗品种，学习甘蔗制糖技术。“留学生”学成归来后，唐朝的制糖技术很快就远超西域和印度。

李玄霸先帮他哥把这件事做了，让他哥在能吃糖的年龄吃腻甜食，别老了还嘴馋。

李家人的三高和糖尿病，大部分都是自己贪图口腹之欲作出来的。李玄霸为了规正二哥的饮食习惯，真是操碎了心。

李玄霸科学素养不高。他就算引进了东南亚的作物，也不能让唐朝的农业技术有多少突破。

让颜真去外域搜集特色作物，不过是一个迷惑他人的幌子，顺带给自己刷一层忧国忧民的名声。

虽然将来他当了大唐亲王，在大隋的名声不重要。但有一层忧国忧民的名声，他才能更好招揽人才。

不过，李玄霸让颜真随同出使赤土国搜集东海诸国特色农作物，只是计划的第一步。

当颜真往返几次外域后，李玄霸就会图穷匕见，让颜真搜集一些禁用物资。

比如武器、甲胄、马匹。

南海诸国很早就与中原有交流，冶铁技术也得到了发展；东南亚和南亚的一些马种也不比西域差；在战船技术上，南海诸国更是遥遥领先。

唐初和倭国会有一场水战——白江口之战。虽然那是唐高宗时期的事，但李玄霸想试试为大唐提前攒一攒战船，在倭国挑衅大唐之前，能不能让他哥提前打到倭国本土去。

历史中倭国画唐朝地图的时候，曾把九州岛直接画做了大唐领土，厚颜无耻地自称大唐人。

李玄霸是个好心人，想为他们正名。

倭国其他地方太穷太远，但九州岛还是很不错的，可以允许他们加入大唐。

李玄霸自穿越后，一直着眼于自己和小家。

为唐倭水战做准备，是李玄霸目前唯一想做的有利于后人的大事。

如印刷术或者收集良种的事，虽然有利于当下，但对整个华夏历史而言，早一些或晚一些做这些事，对华夏的未来影响都微乎其微。

这些目的，李玄霸现在不会告诉颜真。

若颜真能圆满完成他现在布置的任务，真的成为了他的心腹，他才会将后续事交给颜真。

之后李玄霸的心腹都会丢到海船上历练。

陆地上太安稳了，海上更能锤炼人的意志。

李玄霸对以后跟随自己的心腹要求不高，只要意志够强，出身和学识都无所谓。

他甚至不担心属下有野心。因为反正再有野心，在太宗朝谋叛，那简直是经验宝宝。

李玄霸会厚待自己的下属，把他们养得肥肥的。如果他们野心过大，正好宰了补足唐初穷得连老鼠来了都会摇头的国库。

李玄霸在为颜真教授南海诸事时，一个黑红脸的憨厚汉子过来敲门。

李玄霸开门后，让那人进门，对颜真道：“你先回去仔细把这卷书背熟，再找些南海外夷人学学语言。使团很快就要出发，提前抱佛脚，总比一无所知强。”

颜真开玩笑地抱怨道：“三郎君该早些告诉在下，让在下多一些准备时间。”

李玄霸道：“这也算对你的考验。”

颜真叹气：“那在下可要努力了。”

李玄霸将工作布置下去后，带着黑红脸的憨厚汉子离开。

憨厚汉子做护卫状，为李玄霸驾车。

李玄霸坐在他身旁，装作学习如何驾车。

他年纪增大后，不仅要学骑马，也要学驾车。

这个憨厚汉子是去年水灾时进入唐国公府，驾的一手好车，被李玄霸要了过来，专门教他和二哥驾车。

马车行驶起来后，驾车的两人压低声音说话，即使周围没有遮掩，其他人也很难听到。

李玄霸道：“向固，辛苦了。”

向固有些后怕道：“陛下很生气。”

他将宫中的事告知了李玄霸，道：“这样说真的没关系吗？”

向固一进入唐国公府就被李玄霸发现了身份。

李玄霸的感知很敏锐，向固自以为很隐秘的偷听，立刻就被李玄霸揪了出来。

李玄霸没有立刻揭穿向固，而是去寻了向固的家人，将他的家人控制起来。

向固自以为是孤儿，没想到只是与家人走散。他的家人恰好因为水灾逃难，李玄霸便将这家人买了进来。

后来李玄霸给向固摊牌，如果他没有找到向固的家人，大概就会将向固交给父亲处理。

向固不知道李玄霸是如何寻到他的家人。但他有了家人后，就算他不想投靠李玄霸，李玄霸将这件事捅出来，皇帝也不会再信任他。

何况他已经暴露了，结局不是死在皇帝手中，就是死在唐国公手中。

如果是以前，向固不惧怕死亡。

但有了家人，家人还一直在寻找自己。在以为自己已经去世后，家人连逃难都带着自己的牌位。向固就有了软肋。

杨广在各家安插探子只是一步闲棋。其实杨广对这些探子的控制力度极差。

无论是勋贵还是旧世族，都是刚从魏晋南北朝的乱世走来。他们的府邸中有许多私兵，打造得如铁桶一般。杨广哪可能打探得到消息。

向固本来想敷衍一点，就说自己被唐国公打发得远远的，偷听不到唐国公府多少事。

李玄霸却让他偶尔递一些唐国公府的家里长短给皇帝，既显示他确实没有被重用，打探不到核心机密，又能让他在杨广面前有点存在感，混淆杨广的判断。

李玄霸让向固给杨广传递的消息，多是家中如何偏心，李渊对他和李世民如何严厉。

这点消息对唐国公府不痛不痒，对杨广也没什么用处。杨广只把向固当做其他探子那样按时禀报琐事的庸人，没有怀疑向固连这点小事都在骗他。

这次李玄霸又让向固给杨广递了消息，把被罚的事添油加醋。

向固好奇道：“主人如此年幼，就要自污了吗？”

李玄霸笑道：“不是自污，只是让陛下知道，他若想打击唐国公府，别从我和二哥动手。我和二哥只是小喽啰，他打击我二人对唐国公府一点用都没有。相反，如果他将来想拆分唐国公府，就要对我和二哥好。”

向固感到毛骨悚然。

三郎君这么年幼就想着与长兄争夺唐国公的位置了吗？

三郎君是想为二郎君争夺唐国公府继承人，还是……不，三郎君和二郎君的感情极好，一定不会对二郎君动手。

向固把自己恐怖的猜测压下。

李玄霸道：“我将派颜真随同大隋出使赤土国的使臣，去南海为我做些事。你若有兴趣，可一起去。”

向固道：“小的任由主人安排。”

李玄霸摇头：“我是真心想培养你。赤土国遥远，海船虽然沿着海岸线行驶也可能会遇到危险。我若直接派你去，担心你会猜测我要除掉你，所以我才问你自己的决定。”

向固面色忐忑：“不，不，小的怎么会如此揣度？”

李玄霸道：“将来我的人都会去海上逛一圈。如果你愿意去，将来就跟着我。如果你不愿意去也没关系，你好好练一练骑马射箭，将来跟着我二哥。放心，你帮了我许多，我不会亏待你。”

向固咬了一下牙，做出了选择：“请让我跟随主人！我愿意去南海！”

虽然向固本心更倾向于李二郎君，但就算李三郎君说给他选择的权力，他又哪敢选？

李玄霸道：“那好。你做好准备。你不会晕船吧？”

向固道：“我会水。”

李玄霸道：“在海上会水也没用，只要不晕船就好。”

李玄霸又说了些海上需要注意的事，道：“你的任务和颜真不同，待回去后我再告知你。”

李玄霸知道自己给了向固选择，向固也不敢选。但无所谓，他已经给了向固选择，是向固自己不敢抓住，将来向固就只能跟着自己了。

如果向固敢当着自己的面说要跟着自家二哥，就凭这胆识，李玄霸就愿意给向固一次机会。

可惜，没了。

李玄霸回家后，用心声将今天的事告诉了还趴着的李世民。

李世民咋舌：“你倒是真会吹，这都敢说，也不嫌弃恶心。”
