### Chapter 55: Preparing to Send Envoys to the South Seas

“Li Yuan gave Li Erlang a brutal beating, and now Li Erlang is so injured he cannot even rise from his bed?” Emperor Yang Guang asked, looking somewhat stunned after hearing the report.

The spy replied, “Reporting to Your Majesty, after Li Erlang and Li Sanlang returned to the manor, they informed the Duke of Tang of their promotion. The Duke, after explaining the allusion of Li Yannian to them, flew into a rage and intended to discipline Li Sanlang. Li Erlang, fearing that Li Sanlang’s frail health would not withstand the Duke’s punishment, volunteered to take the blows in his stead, receiving double the lashes. That is why his injuries are quite severe.”

The spy hesitated for a moment before continuing, “The Duke of Tang also remarked… that Li Yannian was a male favorite of Emperor Wu of Han…”

Yang Guang flicked his hand, and the fruit platter and cups on the table were swept away with a crash, shattering across the floor.

Yang Guang sneered, “What? Does Li Yuan think I harbor improper intentions toward Li Sanlang?!”

The spy hurriedly kowtowed, “The Duke of Tang likely did not mean that, Your Majesty. He was merely scolding Li Sanlang for his lack of propriety and for currying favor with Your Majesty, claiming it insulted the reputation of the Duke of Tang’s household.”

Yang Guang took a deep breath, suppressing the anger in his heart. “What did Li Erlang and Li Sanlang say?”

The spy said, “Li Erlang and Li Sanlang defended themselves, stating that they treat Your Majesty as a father, and Your Majesty treats them as his own sons; there was no act of sycophancy involved.”

Yang Guang remained silent for a long time. He had the palace servants clear the shards from the floor and ordered the spy to return to the Duke of Tang’s manor.

Yang Guang dismissed all the palace servants and lowered his head to read the memorial submitted by Li Xuanba.

After a long while, Yang Guang sighed, “I should have struck at Li Yuan directly.”

He had originally thought Li Yuan to be a man of deep schemes, and that by striking at his sons, he was effectively striking at him. Who would have thought that Li Yuan would shift all the blame onto the young Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, even going so far as to let Li Shimin suffer a vicious beating?

Yang Guang recalled that when his aunt was still alive, there had been quite a scandal because Li Yuan and the old matriarch favored Li Jiancheng.

It was in accordance with ritual and law for Li Erlang and Li Sanlang to yield to their eldest brother. Although Yang Guang had seized the throne himself, he did not wish for others to challenge the established order of ritual.

However, Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were, after all, closer to him. Seeing them beaten and insulted, and recalling the favoritism within the Duke of Tang’s manor, Yang Guang could not help but feel displeased with Li Yuan’s methods.

“If I am not to strike at Li Yuan directly, I should strike at Li Jiancheng, not involve Li Erlang and Li Sanlang,” Yang Guang added. “It seems that in the Duke of Tang’s manor, only Li Yuan and Li Jiancheng are worth striking at.”

……

Li Xuanba had come to Luoyang this time to expand his bookstore and soap shop businesses into the Eastern Capital.

Yang Guang detested returning to Daxing. Aside from his southern and northern tours, he spent all his time in the Eastern Capital. During the Daye era, the Eastern Capital was even more prosperous than the capital city; with merchants from the Western Regions and foreign envoys gathering there, it was much easier for Li Xuanba to both earn and spend money.

Although Li Shimin had been beaten, Li Yuan had used his hands, and while his back and buttocks were badly swollen, the injuries would heal quickly.

Seeing that his Second Brother was fine, Li Xuanba left him to lie on his stomach and pass the time reading military treatises as light literature, while he himself went out to inspect his businesses.

The Eastern Capital was newly built, and even the residences granted to the nobility were much more spacious. The workshops behind the market shops were also larger than those in Daxing.

The printing workshop was located within the market, while the soap workshop remained in a villa on the outskirts of the Eastern Capital.

Yang Guang had once again levied heavy corvée labor, and some families, unable to bear the burden, sold themselves into servitude to escape. Li Xuanba had seized the opportunity to purchase some of these people to staff his Luoyang workshops. By now, the workshops were already in operation.

Li Xuanba first inspected the soap workshop on the outskirts of the city, then returned to the city to chat with the proofreaders in the printing workshop.

Chinese characters are logograms; the typesetters did not need to be literate, as they could simply match the shapes. But the proofreaders had to be literate, which significantly increased both efficiency and accuracy.

At present, scholars from humble backgrounds still found it difficult to secure official positions, often having to submit their names to noble families in hopes of becoming retainers or clerks.

Even descendants of minor noble families or cadet branches of great clans had to serve as house retainers, waiting for the chance to be recommended by their masters.

The once-famous “Wang and Xie” families—Xie An himself had served as a retainer in the Wang household before he rose to prominence.

Many scholars had to find work while waiting for an opportunity. As long as one was literate, work was easy to find. Copying books, ghostwriting letters, selling calligraphy and paintings, or working as an accountant—as long as they were willing to lower their pride, scholars were a scarce resource and could always find something to do.

Originally, copying books for bookstores was the primary way scholars earned their living expenses. After the rise of printing, they had complained about the loss of a major source of income. Unexpectedly, the printing shop of the Duke of Tang’s manor recruited more scholars than ever before.

The scholars no longer needed to copy books; they only needed to sit in the printing workshop and help with proofreading. Because there were so many books being printed, the proofreading tasks were intense, requiring many scholars. Aside from the smell of ink being a bit unpleasant, the pay was quite good, with meals, lodging, and bonuses included.

The impoverished scholars stopped complaining and scrambled to get hired.

Living in the capital was not easy, and finding a place that provided food and lodging was rare. Moreover, this was the Duke of Tang’s shop; there was a chance to encounter a noble. Perhaps one day, they would be noticed by a powerful figure and recruited as a retainer or clerk.

Li Xuanba indeed harbored the intention of using the proofreader position to recruit talented individuals overlooked by the elite. Otherwise, he would have just had the servants of the Duke of Tang’s manor do the proofreading. Most of the servants were literate, and he would only need to pay them a monthly salary, costing even less.

In an era without printing, it was extremely difficult for scholars from humble backgrounds to study, making it hard for talent to emerge. He knew the chances of finding a "hidden gem" were slim, so he thought it better to go knocking on doors based on the names of his Second Brother’s subordinates from history books.

But his Second Brother’s subordinates belonged to his Second Brother, and Li Xuanba needed his own men.

Li Jiancheng’s subordinates were all focused on his status as the legitimate eldest son and didn't even look at his Second Brother, let alone him. Thinking of his own personality, Li Xuanba decided to look among the scholars of humble origin.

Liu Bang and Zhu Yuanzhang were able to pull a group of founding fathers from among their own poor friends, which showed that while innate conditions were important, later cultivation could not be ignored. He wasn't looking for founding fathers, just officials for a small princely manor; as long as they were literate, sharp, and had decent character, he could find people to use.

Currently, Li Xuanba was very satisfied with the proofreader in front of him.

The proofreader was named Yan Zhen, courtesy name Zishi. He had no relation to the Yan family who wrote the *Family Instructions of Master Yan*.

"Scholars of humble origin" did not mean ordinary peasants. Yan Zhen was a descendant of officials; his grandfather had been a county magistrate during the Chen Dynasty, and his father farmed and studied at home, making them authentic "humble scholars."

Yan Zhen also wanted to pursue the imperial examination path. But the Sui Dynasty’s examination system was similar to the recommendation system; without the recommendation of a fifth-rank official, Yan Zhen didn't even have the qualifications to take the exam.

Yan Zhen was proud and arrogant, always feeling his talent was sufficient to be noticed by a noble, so he had scraped together some travel funds to come to the Eastern Capital to seek an opportunity.

Li Xuanba did not remember a person named Yan Zhen in the history books.

Perhaps he had hit a wall and slunk home, or perhaps he had succeeded in becoming a minor official unworthy of being recorded in history.

Yan Zhen’s academic knowledge was average—a common trait among scholars of humble origin. But his mind was flexible, and he could set aside his pride, making him a rare person among the proofreaders who could get along well with the craftsmen in the printing workshop.

Yan Zhen’s good relationship with the craftsmen was not an act put on for others. In this era, people placed great importance on status and rank, and they would never imagine that the young masters of the Duke of Tang’s manor would actually like such an unconventional character.

Although Li Xuanba was currently the Third Young Master of the Duke of Tang’s manor, his soul was still that of the grassroots commoner from his previous life, so he had a good impression of Yan Zhen.

After mentally marking Yan Zhen as his own, Li Xuanba often discussed the classics with him to fill in his gaps.

Through their interactions, he learned that although Yan Zhen was of "humble origin" and his father farmed and studied, his mother was skilled in business, so they were actually not short of money. Yan Zhen’s effort to squeeze into the printing shop as a proofreader was aimed at the Confucian classics annotated by the high-ranking teachers and the Yuwen teachers.

Although he could purchase printed versions, Yan Zhen believed that by working as a proofreader, he would read the classics many times every day, which not only saved money but also improved his memorization efficiency. Plus, chatting with the craftsmen in the printing workshop was more interesting than studying alone in silence.

Li Xuanba asked, “You are meticulous about money; it seems you are a good candidate for business. How about you handle business for me?”

Yan Zhen laughed, “If I can work for the Third Young Master, I will have made it, and business is fine by me. In any case, if I don't achieve anything, I would eventually have to inherit my mother’s mantle and go into business anyway.”

Li Xuanba said, “What if you had to travel far away to trade with foreign lands?”

Yan Zhen smiled even more happily, “Trading with foreign lands? That would make me more than an ordinary merchant. Is the Third Young Master planning to take me on as a retainer?”

Li Xuanba said, “I am still young and have no authority to take on retainers. But if you are willing to help me, when I am old enough to do so, you shall be my retainer.”

Hearing Li Xuanba’s firm words, Yan Zhen could no longer smile.

When they first met, Li Xuanba had appeared silent and cold, unlike a child. But after meeting a few more times, Yan Zhen realized that Li Xuanba was actually quite talkative and occasionally joked, so he was relatively casual when speaking with him.

But Li Xuanba was still young. Although he had heard of the Third Young Master’s reputation for talent, he had assumed Li Xuanba was just a child prodigy in his studies; he hadn't expected Li Xuanba to actually want to recruit him as a retainer.

Yan Zhen said seriously, “If the Third Young Master thinks highly of me, I am willing to serve you with the loyalty of a dog or horse. But would the Third Young Master reconsider? With your status, it would be easy to select a retainer from the children of lesser noble families when you grow up.”

Li Xuanba said, “I do not look at family background when using people; I only look at whether they catch my eye.”

Yan Zhen was stunned for a moment, then gave a wry smile, “It’s about catching your eye, not talent?”

Li Xuanba joked, “You haven't shown me your talent yet, so how can I judge it? That is why I am giving you this opportunity to show your strengths.”

Yan Zhen sighed, bowed, and cupped his hands, “I am overwhelmed. But… please, Third Young Master, give me this opportunity!”

Li Xuanba said, “Very well. But you should still write to your parents first. If your parents believe that ‘while parents are alive, one should not travel far,’ you should prioritize filial piety. I can find other things for you to do.”

Yan Zhen said, “My elder brother is at home serving our parents. Since I came to the Eastern Capital, my father and mother have jokingly said to consider me as if I were not their son, and to let me find my own future. If I truly cannot make it, I can return home, kowtow, and apologize, and they will give me a portion of the family property to go into business. So, the Third Young Master can rest assured.”

Li Xuanba said, “Then come over, and I will introduce you to what you need to do.”

Li Xuanba led Yan Zhen into his private room in the printing workshop, took a manuscript from his robe, and handed it to him.

This manuscript recorded the conditions of various countries in the South Seas.

Li Xuanba said, “His Majesty is about to send the Tuntian official Chang Jun and the Yubu official Wang Junzheng as envoys to the Red Earth Kingdom. I have already arranged with them that you will follow the mission as a merchant to the Red Earth Kingdom and collect some local specialties for me from the countries along the way.”

The Red Earth Kingdom was located in what is now the Malay Peninsula, in Southeast Asia.

Yan Zhen had assumed Li Xuanba wanted to collect traditional maritime goods like ivory and spices. However, the specialties Li Xuanba had marked for collection in each country were crops that could already be found in the Sui Dynasty, such as wheat, rice, and sugarcane.

Yan Zhen asked curiously, “Could the Third Young Master tell me the reason for selecting these specialties? So I know what standards to set.”

Li Xuanba said, “Your father farms and studies; have you ever worked the fields yourself?”

Yan Zhen replied, “I know how to farm.”

Li Xuanba asked, “Do you understand anything about breeding and seed selection?”

Yan Zhen pondered for a while, then suddenly realized, “Seeds for farming cannot always be kept from one’s own fields, or the yield will decrease year by year. My father often exchanges seeds with neighboring farmers, and sometimes he even plants seeds of the same variety collected from different places in one field. Is the Third Young Master looking to introduce foreign seeds?”

Li Xuanba had not expected Yan Zhen to hit the nail on the head so quickly. It seemed Yan Zhen’s father’s "farming and studying" was not just for show; he was truly serious about agriculture.

He became somewhat curious about Yan Zhen’s father.

The son of a county magistrate was also the son of an official, and he had married the daughter of a wealthy merchant; his family background was certainly not poor. For such a person to seriously study agriculture—perhaps if he were properly cultivated, he could write a book on farming.

Li Xuanba said, “I want you to collect foreign crops because I want to try mixing them with Central Plains crops to see if we can cultivate better varieties. Furthermore, some of their unique local crops might be transplantable to the Central Plains.”

Although Li Xuanba had never farmed himself, discussions about farming were a popular topic online. He knew a little bit about basic farming knowledge—that the more diverse a country’s grain seed varieties were, the better, and that many high-yield crops were the result of hybridization.

Although most of the high-yield famine-relief crops of later generations came from the Americas, unless his brother became Emperor, it would be very difficult for him to reach the Americas. But Southeast Asia and South Asia also had many crops that could be introduced.

For example, sugarcane and coarse-staple cotton.

China had been growing sugarcane for a long time, but the technology for making sugar was not advanced, and sugarcane was mostly eaten directly for its juice.

The sugarcane varieties in Southeast Asia and South Asia were better, with higher juice yields, and they possessed unique sugar-making techniques.

The upper echelons of the Sui and Tang dynasties were all fond of sweets, and Emperor Taizong of Tang was the most prominent among them.

Emperor Taizong had once sent people to India to seek better sugarcane varieties and to learn sugar-making techniques. After the "overseas students" returned, the Tang Dynasty’s sugar-making technology quickly surpassed that of the Western Regions and India.

Li Xuanba would do this for his brother first, so that his brother would get tired of sweets by the time he was old enough to eat them, rather than being a glutton in his old age.

The high blood pressure and diabetes of the Li family were mostly self-inflicted by their own gluttony. Li Xuanba was truly worried sick about correcting his Second Brother’s dietary habits.

Li Xuanba’s scientific literacy was not high. Even if he introduced Southeast Asian crops, he could not bring about many breakthroughs in Tang Dynasty agricultural technology.

Having Yan Zhen collect unique crops from foreign lands was merely a smokescreen to confuse others, while also earning himself a reputation for being concerned about the country and the people.

Although his reputation in the Sui Dynasty wouldn't matter once he became a Prince of the Tang, having a reputation for being concerned about the people would make it easier for him to recruit talent.

However, having Yan Zhen accompany the mission to the Red Earth Kingdom to collect crops was only the first step of his plan.

Once Yan Zhen had made a few trips to foreign lands, Li Xuanba would reveal his true intentions and have him collect prohibited materials.

Such as weapons, armor, and horses.

The countries of the South Seas had long had exchanges with the Central Plains, and their iron-smelting technology had also developed; some horse breeds in Southeast Asia and South Asia were no worse than those of the Western Regions; and in terms of warship technology, the South Sea countries were far ahead.

In the early Tang Dynasty, there would be a naval battle with Japan—the Battle of Baekgang. Although that was a matter for the reign of Emperor Gaozong of Tang, Li Xuanba wanted to try to stockpile warships for the Tang in advance, to see if he could let his brother strike at the Japanese mainland before they could provoke the Tang.

In history, when Japan drew maps of the Tang Dynasty, they had once drawn Kyushu as Tang territory and shamelessly called themselves Tang people.

Li Xuanba was a kind person and wanted to "correct their names."

Other parts of Japan were too poor and too far, but Kyushu was quite good; he could allow them to join the Tang.

Since his transmigration, Li Xuanba had always focused on himself and his small family.

Preparing for the Tang-Japan naval war was the only major task he currently wanted to do that would benefit future generations.

As for things like printing or collecting good seeds, while they were beneficial for the present, their impact on the overall history of China would be minimal whether they were done earlier or later.

Li Xuanba would not tell Yan Zhen these goals now.

Only if Yan Zhen could successfully complete his current tasks and truly become his confidant would he entrust him with the subsequent matters.

Afterward, all of Li Xuanba’s confidants would be thrown onto sea ships for training.

The land was too stable; the sea could better temper a person’s will.

Li Xuanba did not have high requirements for the confidants who would follow him; as long as their will was strong enough, their background and education did not matter.

He was not even worried about his subordinates having ambition. Because no matter how ambitious they were, rebelling during the Taizong era was simply handing out experience points.

Li Xuanba would treat his subordinates well and fatten them up. If their ambition grew too large, he would just slaughter them to replenish the national treasury, which in the early Tang was so poor that even the mice would shake their heads in despair.

While Li Xuanba was instructing Yan Zhen on matters of the South Seas, a sturdy man with a dark red face came to knock on the door.

After Li Xuanba opened the door and let the man in, he said to Yan Zhen, “Go back first and memorize this manuscript thoroughly, and find some people from the South Seas to learn their languages. The mission will be departing soon; cramming in advance is better than knowing nothing at all.”

Yan Zhen complained jokingly, “The Third Young Master should have told me earlier so I could have had more time to prepare.”

Li Xuanba said, “This is also a test for you.”

Yan Zhen sighed, “Then I must work hard.”

After Li Xuanba finished assigning the work, he left with the sturdy, dark-red-faced man.

The man acted as a guard and drove the carriage for Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba sat beside him, pretending to learn how to drive.

As he grew older, he had to learn not only how to ride a horse but also how to drive a carriage.

This sturdy man had entered the Duke of Tang’s manor during the floods last year. He was an expert at driving, and Li Xuanba had requested him specifically to teach him and his Second Brother.

Once the carriage was moving, the two men driving lowered their voices, making it difficult for anyone else to hear, even without cover.

Li Xuanba said, “Xiang Gu, thank you for your hard work.”

Xiang Gu was still a bit fearful, “His Majesty was very angry.”

He told Li Xuanba about what had happened in the palace and asked, “Is it really okay to say it like that?”

Li Xuanba had discovered Xiang Gu’s identity the moment he entered the Duke of Tang’s manor.

Li Xuanba’s perception was keen; he had immediately caught Xiang Gu eavesdropping, which Xiang Gu had thought was very secretive.

Li Xuanba did not immediately expose Xiang Gu but instead went to find his family and brought them under his control.

Xiang Gu had thought he was an orphan, not realizing he had only been separated from his family. His family happened to be refugees from the flood, so Li Xuanba had bought them into the manor.

Later, Li Xuanba laid his cards on the table: if he hadn't found Xiang Gu’s family, he would have handed Xiang Gu over to his father to deal with.

Xiang Gu did not know how Li Xuanba had found his family. But now that he had a family, even if he didn't want to defect to Li Xuanba, if Li Xuanba exposed him, the Emperor would no longer trust him.

Moreover, he was already exposed; his end would be either death at the hands of the Emperor or at the hands of the Duke of Tang.

If it were before, Xiang Gu would not have feared death.

But with a family, and a family that had been searching for him—thinking he was dead, they had even carried his spirit tablet while fleeing—Xiang Gu now had a weakness.

Yang Guang planting spies in various households was just a casual move. In fact, Yang Guang’s control over these spies was extremely poor.

Whether they were nobles or old aristocratic clans, they had just emerged from the chaotic times of the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties. Their manors were filled with private soldiers and were built like iron barrels. How could Yang Guang possibly gather information?

Xiang Gu had originally intended to be perfunctory, saying he had been sent far away by the Duke of Tang and couldn't overhear much about the manor’s affairs.

Li Xuanba, however, had him occasionally pass some domestic trifles of the Duke of Tang’s manor to the Emperor, which both showed that he was indeed not being reused and couldn't gather core secrets, and allowed him to maintain a sense of presence in front of Yang Guang, confusing his judgment.

The information Li Xuanba had Xiang Gu pass to Yang Guang was mostly about how the family was biased, and how Li Yuan was strict with him and Li Shimin.

This information was harmless to the Duke of Tang’s manor and useless to Yang Guang. Yang Guang only regarded Xiang Gu as a mediocre person who reported trivial matters like other spies, never suspecting that Xiang Gu was lying to him even about these small things.

This time, Li Xuanba had again had Xiang Gu pass a message to Yang Guang, embellishing the story of their punishment.

Xiang Gu asked curiously, “Master is so young, yet you are already willing to sully your own reputation?”

Li Xuanba laughed, “It’s not sullying my reputation, but letting His Majesty know that if he wants to strike at the Duke of Tang’s manor, he shouldn't start with me and my Second Brother. We are just small fry; striking at us won't do anything to the Duke of Tang’s manor. On the contrary, if he wants to split the Duke of Tang’s manor in the future, he should be good to us.”

Xiang Gu felt a chill run down his spine.

Was the Third Young Master already thinking about competing with his eldest brother for the position of Duke of Tang at such a young age?

Was the Third Young Master trying to fight for the heirship of the Duke of Tang’s manor for the Second Young Master, or… no, the relationship between the Third Young Master and the Second Young Master was excellent; he would certainly not move against his Second Brother.

Xiang Gu suppressed his terrifying speculation.

Li Xuanba said, “I am going to send Yan Zhen to follow the Sui mission to the Red Earth Kingdom to do some things for me in the South Seas. If you are interested, you can go along.”

Xiang Gu said, “I will leave it to Master’s arrangements.”

Li Xuanba shook his head, “I genuinely want to cultivate you. The Red Earth Kingdom is far away, and although sea ships travel along the coastline, they may still encounter danger. If I sent you directly, I was worried you would suspect I wanted to get rid of you, which is why I asked for your own decision.”

Xiang Gu looked uneasy, “No, no, how could I ever suspect such a thing?”

Li Xuanba said, “In the future, all my people will take a trip to the sea. If you are willing to go, you will follow me in the future. If you are unwilling, that is fine too; you can practice your riding and archery well and follow my Second Brother in the future. Rest assured, you have helped me a lot, and I will not treat you unfairly.”

Xiang Gu gritted his teeth and made his choice, “Please let me follow you, Master! I am willing to go to the South Seas!”

Although Xiang Gu’s heart leaned more toward the Second Young Master, even if the Third Young Master gave him the power to choose, how could he dare to choose?

Li Xuanba said, “Very well. Prepare yourself. You don’t get seasick, do you?”

Xiang Gu said, “I can swim.”

Li Xuanba said, “Swimming is useless at sea; as long as you don’t get seasick, that’s enough.”

Li Xuanba said a few more things to watch out for at sea, then added, “Your mission is different from Yan Zhen’s. I will tell you after we return.”

Li Xuanba knew he had given Xiang Gu a choice, and Xiang Gu hadn't dared to choose. But it didn't matter; he had already given him the choice, and it was Xiang Gu himself who hadn't dared to grasp it. In the future, Xiang Gu would have no choice but to follow him.

If Xiang Gu had dared to say to his face that he wanted to follow his Second Brother, Li Xuanba would have been willing to give him a chance just for that courage.

Unfortunately, he didn't.

After returning home, Li Xuanba used his inner voice to tell Li Shimin, who was still lying on his stomach, about today’s events.

Li Shimin clicked his tongue, “You really know how to blow smoke; you even dared to say that, and you aren't even disgusted by it.”

chunks.chapterTitle: 第55章 准备派人去南海 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
李玄霸：【皇帝自己都不嫌弃恶心，我这个受害者说什么恶心？】

李世民道：“有用吗？他会同情我俩，以后不折腾了？”

李玄霸微笑：【等着瞧。我也好奇他会如何做。】

李玄霸没等多久，杨广就撤了他的实职。

杨广下旨，他想起李建成作为唐国公府嫡长子都还没有职官，不能让长幼无序，所以李建成接替李玄霸进入乐坊。

为了弥补李玄霸，李玄霸和李世民的散官再升半阶。

杨广还特别叮嘱李玄霸，“奉旨填词”的事仍旧是李玄霸的差事，但只是长辈对晚辈的要求，与君臣无关，让李玄霸不要太在意这件事，当做个爱好就成，不要耽误了学业，累坏了身体。

李世民和李玄霸还是垂髫少年，即使李玄霸考得了秀才，李世民猎到了老虎，他们的年龄和资历都还很浅。

如果两人因李渊的功劳得封散官，哪怕成了从五品以上的“大夫”，朝中其他人也不会有多意外。

凭借父荫封官很正常，甚至直接封郡公县公的都有，算不得多奇怪。

但杨广给李世民和李玄霸封官却不是以奖赏李渊的名义，只是单纯因两个孩子本身而奖赏。这就很引人注目了。

李世民和李玄霸刚得了九品散官，短短一两月就跃居从七品的绥德尉。升官速度，让寻常官吏遥不可及。

本来还有人对李玄霸“擅新声”颇有嘲讽。杨广先抹去了李玄霸的职官，又给李玄霸加封了散官品阶，立刻堵住了这些人的闲言碎语。

于是朝中人又开始叹息，原来皇帝并没有折辱李玄霸的意思，只是碰巧而已。

自汉武帝置协律都尉一职，后世无数士人担任过这个官职，其中不乏高门士族子弟。“协律”说到底就是制定乐声，而礼乐不分家，制定乐声就是制定礼仪，不是什么粗鄙的官职。

皇帝看来没有想太多，只是被人提醒后才意识到不对。

嗯……等等，皇帝意识到不对，怎么还让李建成继续担任协律郎？！

朝中人糊涂了。

皇帝这是意识到还是没意识到？是想澄清还是想证实？还是说皇帝认为他本来没有此意，其他人误解他对唐国公不满，所以皇帝反其道行之，专门让唐国公府的嫡长子担任这个职务，以表示他堂堂正正，没有坏心？

李渊一口血堵在喉咙中。

他骂道：“这哪是坦荡？明明是他认为这敲打还不够，想要进一步折辱我！”

李世民翻白眼。

我和阿玄被折辱的时候，你就说是我和阿玄的错。现在兄长被推上这个位置，你怎么不骂是兄长的错？父亲真偏心。

李世民私下和李玄霸小声吐槽：“父亲不会将来也和祖母一样偏心吧？”

李玄霸道：“无所谓，我们又不当那个唐国公。”

李世民瘪嘴道：“你应该安慰我，父亲不会偏心。”

李玄霸道：“嫡长继承制是绕不过的坎，你现在计较这些也没用。不是你说的吗？做好自己能做的事就行。”

李世民不满道：“那能一样吗？不一样，那可是父亲，是我们的父亲……”

李玄霸道：“啊，你又要哭了？”

李世民捂住眼睛使劲揉了揉，放下手：“我才没哭。”

李玄霸见二哥如此，本想让二哥提前一点别太信任李渊，现在有些不忍了。

李玄霸安慰道：“不过此次父亲生气，并不是偏心兄长，而是陛下扇了我们家两次巴掌，侮辱性更大了。”

李世民语塞。

半晌，他抄起靠枕抱在怀里，在坐榻上滚来滚去，低声哀嚎道：“啊！！！！！陛下真是……啊！！！！！”

他滚了一会儿，翻坐起来，压低声音，神秘兮兮道：“这烂怂大隋，我们反了吧！”

李玄霸白了二哥一眼，懒得理睬二哥的胡言乱语，提笔继续写给颜真和向固的出游指南。

李世民自己低声发泄了一番后，胸下垫着靠枕，像毛毛虫一样蛄蛹蠕动到案前，手一撑，将下巴搁在案上：“蛮夷之地，你那么在乎干什么？”

李玄霸一边写一边道：“蛮夷之地？你知道四大文明古国吗？”

李世民道：“每当你问我知道不知道的时候，就很明显知道我不知道，所以你为什么要问废话？”

李玄霸的笔在纸上落了个墨点。

他转头给了二哥一个白眼，道：“世界很大，大唐虽然屹立在世界之巅，但其他文明也不是没有可取之处。”

李世民道：“大唐现在还不存在呢。阿玄，你是不是该用心声和我说话？”

“哦。”李玄霸切换心声，【来，我给你画一张世界地图。】

虽然李玄霸画不出详细的地图，但世界地图的轮廓还是没问题。

李玄霸把粗陋版世界地图画出来，将那些地方的特产标注出来。

他世界历史不好，不知道在隋唐这个时间段各国发展水平如何，只能通过西域商人的描述推断。

不过以隋唐的科技水平，也不太可能和外国有太多的交流，所以他现在的了解就足够了。

李世民眼睛一亮：“世界这么大吗？要是这些都归我们就好了！”

李玄霸正想解释为何大唐的疆域不可能扩张得太狠，李世民就自己摇头：“不行，疆域太宽广管理不过来。如果朝中发布诏令，快马走几月都传达不到地方，那这块地名义上是朝廷的地盘，实际上与自治无异。勉强管理，有害无益。”

李玄霸叹了口气。

李世民好奇：“你叹什么气？难道舍不得这么大一片土地？贪多嚼不烂啊，别贪心。”

李玄霸摇头，笑道：“后世人站在前人的肩膀上，都难以看清这件事。他们都认为，给你一支军队，你能占领全球。”

李世民问道：“难道后世已经有人统一世界了？”

李玄霸摇头：“后世人也做不到。”

李世民失笑：“连后世人都做不到的事，他们凭什么认为先人能做到？如果今不如古，那后世子孙也太没用了。后世子孙应该有自信些，他们都做不到的事，别指望先人比他们还厉害。”

李玄霸对二哥竖起大拇指：“你这句话我要记下来。”

李世民道：“记呗。”

他坐起身，伸了个懒腰：“不过不能占领，也可以有其他方式为我中土效力。将来我们一起出海吧，我想看一看这个世界有多宽广！”

李玄霸面色古怪：“你估计不行。”

李世民笑了笑，没说话。

一些事情他们已经有了默契，不过李世民不想说出来，也不想问。

现在他还小，没必要想那么远，他更希望快乐地过好眼前的每一天。

以后的烦恼，就让以后的自己去烦恼。

现在他身边没有烦恼，何苦庸人自扰？

“快和我说说南海的事！”李世民督促道，“你把我的兴趣都勾起来了，我也要派人去。你说杜兄和房兄如何？”

李玄霸嘴角抽搐：“他们现在还不是你的下属，别逼得他们以后不跟你了。”

“哈哈哈哈哈。”李世民大笑不已。

李玄霸无语叹气。

二哥还这么小，就有欺负“臣子”的爱好？

三岁看老，九岁的二哥已经无药可救。

救不了，等死吧，告辞。

李玄霸嘴角含笑：“不过我们可以问一问他们有没有兴趣。反正他们现在也入不了皇帝的眼，不会做多大的官。在家蹉跎十几年，不如出去逛逛。”

李世民把住弟弟的肩膀，挤眉弄眼：“来，我们商量一下怎么诓骗他们。”

两张容貌差不多的脸上，露出了如出一辙的坏笑。
chunks.englishText:
Li Xuanba: [If the Emperor himself doesn't find it disgusting, why should I, the victim, complain about it?]

Li Shimin asked, "Is it useful? Will he sympathize with us and stop tormenting us in the future?"

Li Xuanba smiled: [Wait and see. I am also curious to see how he handles this.]

Li Xuanba did not have to wait long before Yang Guang stripped him of his official duties.

Yang Guang issued an imperial decree, stating that since Li Jiancheng, as the eldest legitimate son of the Duke of Tang’s estate, had yet to receive an official post, it would be improper to ignore the order of seniority. Thus, Li Jiancheng was to replace Li Xuanba in the Music Bureau.

To compensate Li Xuanba, both he and Li Shimin had their honorary titles (san-guan) raised by half a grade.

Yang Guang also specifically instructed Li Xuanba that "composing lyrics by imperial command" remained his duty, but emphasized that this was merely a request from an elder to a junior, having nothing to do with the relationship between monarch and subject. He told Li Xuanba not to take it to heart, to treat it as a hobby, and not to let it interfere with his studies or exhaust his health.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were still young boys with their hair in tufts. Even though Li Xuanba had passed the Xiucai examination and Li Shimin had hunted a tiger, their age and seniority were still quite shallow.

If the two had been granted honorary titles due to Li Yuan’s merits, even if they had become "Grand Masters" of the fifth rank or higher, no one in the imperial court would have been particularly surprised.

It was common to receive titles through the shade of one’s father; some were even directly enfeoffed as Dukes of Commanderies or Counties, which was not considered strange at all.

However, Yang Guang conferring titles on Li Shimin and Li Xuanba was not in the name of rewarding Li Yuan, but purely as a reward for the two children themselves. This was what made it so eye-catching.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had just received ninth-rank honorary titles, and within a month or two, they had jumped to the rank of Assistant Commandant of Suide (seventh rank). Such a speed of promotion was unreachable for ordinary officials.

Originally, there were those who mocked Li Xuanba for his "unorthodox musical talents." By first stripping Li Xuanba of his active post and then raising his honorary rank, Yang Guang immediately silenced the gossip of these people.

Consequently, the court began to sigh, realizing that the Emperor had no intention of humiliating Li Xuanba; it had merely been a coincidence.

Ever since Emperor Wu of Han established the post of Commandant of Music (Xielü Duwei), countless scholars throughout history had held the position, many of them from prestigious, high-ranking families. "Regulating the music" (Xielü) ultimately meant establishing musical standards, and since ritual and music were inseparable, establishing musical standards meant establishing ritual—it was by no means a vulgar position.

It seemed the Emperor hadn't thought much of it, only realizing something was amiss after being reminded.

Hmm... wait. If the Emperor realized something was wrong, why did he let Li Jiancheng continue to serve as the Music Official (Xielü Lang)?!

The court was confused.

Did the Emperor realize it or not? Was he trying to clarify or confirm? Or did the Emperor believe he had no such intention, and since others misunderstood his dissatisfaction with the Duke of Tang, he decided to do the exact opposite—specifically appointing the eldest legitimate son of the Duke of Tang’s estate to the post to show that he was upright and harbored no ill will?

Li Yuan felt a mouthful of blood rising in his throat.

He cursed, "This isn't being upright! It’s clearly that he thinks this slap wasn't enough and wants to further humiliate me!"

Li Shimin rolled his eyes.

When Ah Xuan and I were humiliated, you said it was our fault. Now that our elder brother has been pushed into this position, why don't you curse that it's his fault? Father is truly biased.

Li Shimin whispered to Li Xuanba in private, "Do you think Father will be as biased as Grandmother in the future?"

Li Xuanba replied, "It doesn't matter. We aren't going to be the Duke of Tang anyway."

Li Shimin pouted, "You should be comforting me, saying Father won't be biased."

Li Xuanba said, "The system of primogeniture is an unavoidable hurdle; there's no point in worrying about it now. Isn't that what you said? Just do what you can."

Li Shimin was dissatisfied, "How can that be the same? It's different—that's Father, he's our father..."

Li Xuanba said, "Ah, are you going to cry again?"

Li Shimin covered his eyes and rubbed them hard, then lowered his hands: "I wasn't crying."

Seeing his second brother like this, Li Xuanba, who had originally wanted to warn him not to trust Li Yuan too much, now felt a bit soft-hearted.

Li Xuanba comforted him, "However, Father is angry this time not because he favors our elder brother, but because the Emperor slapped our family twice—the insult is even greater."

Li Shimin was speechless.

After a long while, he grabbed a cushion, hugged it to his chest, rolled back and forth on the daybed, and wailed in a low voice: "Ah!!!!! The Emperor is truly... ah!!!!!"

After rolling for a while, he flipped up and sat cross-legged, lowering his voice and acting mysterious: "This rotten Sui Dynasty, let's rebel!"

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes at his second brother, too lazy to pay attention to his nonsense, and picked up his brush to continue writing the travel guide for Yan Zhen and Xiang Gu.

After Li Shimin finished venting in a low voice, he crawled toward the desk like a caterpillar with the cushion under his chest, propped himself up, and rested his chin on the desk: "It's a land of barbarians, why do you care so much about it?"

Li Xuanba said while writing, "A land of barbarians? Do you know about the four ancient civilizations?"

Li Shimin said, "Whenever you ask if I know something, it's obvious that you know I don't, so why do you ask such nonsense?"

Li Xuanba’s brush left a blot of ink on the paper.

He turned his head and gave his second brother a side-eye, saying, "The world is vast. Although the Great Tang stands at the pinnacle of the world, other civilizations are not without their merits."

Li Shimin said, "The Great Tang doesn't even exist yet. Ah Xuan, shouldn't you be speaking to me with your thoughts?"

"Oh." Li Xuanba switched to his inner voice, [Come, I'll draw a world map for you.]

Although Li Xuanba couldn't draw a detailed map, the outline of a world map was no problem.

Li Xuanba drew a rough version of the world map and marked the specialties of those regions.

His knowledge of world history was poor, and he didn't know the level of development of various countries during the Sui and Tang periods, so he could only infer from the descriptions of merchants from the Western Regions.

However, given the technological level of the Sui and Tang, it was unlikely there would be much exchange with foreign countries, so his current understanding was sufficient.

Li Shimin’s eyes lit up: "Is the world this big? If only all of this belonged to us!"

Just as Li Xuanba was about to explain why the territory of the Great Tang couldn't expand too aggressively, Li Shimin shook his head himself: "No, the territory is too vast to manage. If the court issues a decree, and it takes months for a fast horse to reach the local area, then that land is nominally the court's territory, but in reality, it's no different from being autonomous. Forcing management is more harmful than beneficial."

Li Xuanba sighed.

Li Shimin was curious: "Why are you sighing? Are you reluctant to part with such a large piece of land? Greed leads to indigestion; don't be greedy."

Li Xuanba shook his head and smiled: "People of later generations, standing on the shoulders of their predecessors, still find it hard to see this clearly. They all think that if you give them an army, they can conquer the entire globe."

Li Shimin asked, "Has someone in later generations already unified the world?"

Li Xuanba shook his head: "Even people of later generations can't do it."

Li Shimin laughed: "If even people of later generations can't do it, why do they think their ancestors could? If the present is worse than the past, then the descendants of later generations are too useless. Descendants should be more confident; if they can't do it themselves, don't expect their ancestors to be more capable than them."

Li Xuanba gave his second brother a thumbs up: "I'm going to write that down."

Li Shimin said, "Go ahead."

He sat up and stretched: "But even if we can't occupy it, there can be other ways to serve our Central Plains. Let's go to sea together in the future; I want to see how vast this world is!"

Li Xuanba’s expression was strange: "You probably can't."

Li Shimin smiled and said nothing.

There was already a tacit understanding between them about some things, but Li Shimin didn't want to say it, nor did he want to ask.

He was still young, and there was no need to think so far ahead. He preferred to live each day in front of him happily.

Let future troubles be worried about by his future self.

Right now, there were no troubles around him, so why bother troubling himself?

"Tell me about the South Sea quickly!" Li Shimin urged, "You've piqued my interest, and I want to send people there too. What do you think of Brother Du and Brother Fang?"

Li Xuanba’s mouth twitched: "They aren't your subordinates yet; don't force them to the point where they won't follow you in the future."

"Hahahaha." Li Shimin laughed heartily.

Li Xuanba sighed speechlessly.

His second brother was still so young, yet he already had a hobby of bullying his "subjects"?

One can see a person's character at age three; the nine-year-old second brother was already beyond saving.

Can't save him, just wait for the end, goodbye.

Li Xuanba smiled: "However, we can ask them if they are interested. Anyway, they aren't in the Emperor's eyes right now and won't hold any significant office. Wasting a dozen years at home is better than going out to take a look."

Li Shimin grabbed his younger brother’s shoulders, winking and gesturing: "Come, let's discuss how to trick them."

On two faces that looked nearly identical, a matching, mischievous smirk appeared.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第56章 宇文弼的不满意
chunks.chineseText:
第56章 宇文弼的不满意

=
　　常骏和王君政很快就带着大隋的使臣团出发。颜真和向固忐忑不安地随行。
　　李玄霸亲自将两人送出东都。
　　李世民当然要来凑热闹。他不仅自己来了， 还带着杜如晦、房乔、薛收和终于来到了东都和朋友们相会的长孙无忌一起来了。
　　“我对南海诸国很好奇，多搜集些他们的书籍回来。”李玄霸的下属就是李世民的下属，李世民十分不客气地布置任务， “最好再抓两个当地贵族回来。”
　　李玄霸叹气， 更正道：“不是抓， 是请。”
　　李世民道：“都一样。”
　　李玄霸问道：“哪里一样？”
　　李世民吹口哨。
　　李玄霸觉得自家二哥是故意找揍。
　　李玄霸叮嘱：“千万别听我二哥的，别去绑架别国的贵族！”
　　颜真和向固哭笑不得，心中的忐忑都缓解了不少。
　　这还用叮嘱吗？他们怎么可能去绑架别国的贵族！
　　房乔等人听着李世民在那胡扯， 都笑话李世民。
　　杜如晦道：“李二，你这么有本事，怎么不亲自去抓几个他国贵族回来？”
　　长孙无忌嫌弃道：“他就知道口花花。”
　　薛收叹气：“李二郎， 你少说几句，祸从口出。”
　　房乔严肃道：“不可以引起他国纷争。”
　　李世民捂住耳朵：“听不到听不到。”
　　杜如晦、长孙无忌、薛收三人笑着继续调侃李世民， 房乔有点忧愁。
　　希望未来的主君只是开玩笑， 不要将来当了皇帝之后，真的下令去抓他国贵族到朝堂前逗乐。
　　李玄霸送别颜真和向固时，拜访了常骏和王君政，请求常骏和王君政照看颜真和向固。
　　他之前已经悄悄赠送给常骏和王君政许多财物，这次只是口头拜托。
　　常骏和王君政也装出一副没拿过李玄霸的财物， 只谈论感情的模样。
　　送走颜真和向固后，李世民又闹着要去打猎。
　　李玄霸这次有事， 没有跟着二哥一起去打猎。他对朋友们挨个叮嘱，让他们看好了自家二哥，可别让二哥又去找猛兽。
　　长孙无忌蠢蠢欲动：“狩猎猛兽？这么有意思？”
　　李玄霸死鱼眼道：“你是想让我向长孙将军告状吗？”
　　长孙无忌无语：“李二郎说你是告状小狗， 这话还真没错。”
　　李玄霸道：“没错， 我就是， 你可以试试看。”
　　长孙无忌捂住嘴， 做出一个“闭嘴”的动作。
　　李世民笑道：“放心，我有分寸。”
　　李玄霸道：“放心，你说的‘放心’，我一点都不放心。”
　　李玄霸又挨个叮嘱了一番，重点警告长孙无忌不准跟着二哥乱来，才惴惴不安地离开。
　　长孙无忌眼珠子转了一下，对李世民勾肩搭背道：“他越说不能做，我们就越要做，凭什么听他的？”
　　房乔皱眉道：“若遭遇危险，你能负责？”
　　杜如晦揶揄道：“既然长孙四郎这么有自信，李二，我们都别出手，看长孙四郎单挑老虎。”
　　薛收好奇道：“长孙四郎也能独自狩猎老虎？”
　　李世民哈哈大笑，拍着长孙无忌的肩膀道：“没错！他一定能！不止老虎！他就算独自面对狼群都浑然不惧！我们可以把他丢进狼群试试！”
　　长孙无忌：“不，我不能。你想谋杀我就直说。”
　　李世民继续哈哈大笑：“试试嘛！”
　　长孙无忌收回搭在李世民肩膀的手，离李世民远远的。
　　杜如晦和薛收跟着李世民一起笑起来。房乔的眉头松开，但心里对长孙无忌有些警惕。
　　长孙无忌将来不会带坏主君吧？希望长孙无忌识相点。
　　李世民等人在欢声笑语中又去禁苑狩猎，李玄霸来到了宇文弼的家中。
　　李玄霸与宇文珠定亲后，没有拜访宇文家。
　　宇文弼的孙儿刚早夭，一家人都很悲痛，李玄霸此时去和宇文珠联络感情，那就不止叫没情商，而是脑子贵恙了。
　　早夭的孩童因为“不吉利”，不能葬入祖坟，甚至不能立碑，也不会有人为他们守孝。
　　很多人对早夭的孩童，只是随意在野外找了块地，用布一裹，随意埋葬。
　　宇文家没有“嫌弃”宇文伉早夭的“不吉利”，宇文伉虽没能葬入祖坟，也选了一块风水宝地，立了碑堆了坟。他们还在家中为宇文伉树了牌位，逢年过节和忌日都会给宇文伉上香。但守孝是不必的。
　　“但小娘非要为安儿守孝，独自去了别院居住。”宇文弼叹气，“我本想让她与你见一面，但她说在为安儿守完孝前，不想与外人联系。她有些任性，希望你不要责怪她。”
　　李玄霸摇头道：“她为感情深厚的兄弟逝世悲伤，这不是任性。”
　　宇文弼道：“你不介意，我就放心了。”
　　宇文弼虽然知道李玄霸是个待人温和的好孩子，但孙女的举止有违世俗规矩，他还是有些忐忑。见李玄霸确实不在乎，他才松了口气。
　　一边是弟子，一边是孙女，若两人之后不和睦，宇文弼真不知该如何是好。
　　在面对晚辈的时候，在外人面前强硬无比的宇文弼也不过是个普通疼爱晚辈的老人家而已。
　　拉了几句家常，又询问了李玄霸他与李世民的功课后，宇文弼才说正事。
　　宇文伉早夭后，宇文弼因悲伤过度病倒，但不准李世民和李玄霸来探望。
　　孩童早夭是不吉利的事。谁家孩童早夭，都会闭门谢客一段时间，等晦气消失后再与外人接触。李世民和李玄霸不在乎世俗规矩，但宇文家也要顾忌世俗舆论。
　　宇文弼本来还想在家里为孙儿哀悼一段时间。他提前将李玄霸唤来，是因为杨广改口让李建成当协律郎一事。
　　向固的事，是高颎和宇文弼帮李玄霸处理的。
　　高颎和宇文弼当了四代帝王的重臣，手腕是不差的。特别是高颎，他应付皇帝的探子很有经验。
　　他二人在原本历史中会被杨广杀掉，只是吃了不懂杨广性格的亏。
　　高颎在夺嫡之争中都能全身而退；宇文弼更是完全中立。以他们的年龄和资历，只要他们不忤逆，基本不可能遭遇杀身之祸。
　　因“诽谤朝政”被杀这种事，别说他二人，就是大隋满朝臣子都不可能想到。
　　当他们得知杨广的性格，又对杨广彻底失望之后，应付杨广就很轻松了。
　　之前高颎和宇文弼在引诱杨广开仓赈济水灾时，就利用了杨广安插在他们身边的探子。
　　李玄霸现在这一手，与他们所做的事一模一样。宇文弼又知道向固的存在，自然听到杨广旨意的改变，就猜到了李玄霸做了什么。
　　宇文弼有点担心李玄霸太专注阴谋诡计之事移了性情，又担心李玄霸过于小看皇帝露出马脚，所以不顾自己还病着，也不顾孙儿早夭的晦气，赶紧把李玄霸叫来叮嘱。
　　李玄霸虚心听教。
　　宇文弼见李玄霸没有因算计了杨广而得意，心里对李玄霸很满意。
　　既然弟子没有沉浸在阴谋诡计中，宇文弼便放心教导李玄霸在这件事上的疏漏。
　　虽然不能被阴谋诡计移了性情，但李玄霸还是得熟练这些阴谋诡计。阴谋诡计有时候很有用，更重要的是，能熟练运用阴谋诡计的人，才不会被其他人算计。
　　宇文弼教导了李玄霸整整一个时辰，将李玄霸从给杨广写的奏疏，到李玄霸引导杨广把注意力放在李建成身上，所有的事都细细整理了一遍。
　　李玄霸努力将老师的教导记下。
　　他这次转移杨广注意力的计划其实很粗糙，多是仗着自己的年幼，让其他人轻视疏忽，才能轻松得逞。
　　虽然李玄霸在推行计划时就利用了自己年幼，不会被人怀疑这一点，但李玄霸会长大，提前学会更缜密的谋划没有坏处。
　　下次李玄霸会试着将自己当做成年人，不利用自己年幼这个优势，再好好谋划一番。
　　宇文弼道：“趁着你还年幼，不会引人怀疑，你可以多试几次，积攒一些经验。这些话你不要和高昭玄说，他太迂腐。”
　　李玄霸心道，巧了，高老师在前不久送来的信中说了同样的话，让我积攒经验，但不要告诉你。
　　李玄霸乖巧道：“弟子知道。”
　　宇文弼道：“房乔、杜如晦、薛收不错，你结交的朋友很好。他们将来是否在新王朝有一席之地？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　宇文弼道：“不要太依赖你的谶纬。太信任命运者，会被命运所玩弄。”
　　李玄霸道：“是，老师放心。我没有主动与他们结交，与他们提前相遇只是碰巧。”
　　李玄霸将房乔想要在书铺中印刷文集，杜如晦借着房乔的关系来唐国公府拜访，薛收和二哥在齐王的宴会上一见如故的事描述给宇文弼听。
　　宇文弼听后，悲伤许久的他拈着胡须，时隔许久露出笑容：“命运会改变，并已经向更好的方向改变。你也该放轻松一些了。”
　　李玄霸疑惑：“我一直很轻松。”
　　宇文弼摇头：“你一直紧绷着。”
　　李玄霸不解。他没感觉到自己一直紧绷着啊。
　　宇文弼揉了李玄霸的脑袋一下，道：“你还是个孩童，学学你二哥，多玩耍，少操心。”
　　李玄霸敷衍地点头。他猜测，可能是因为他太不像孩童，所以老师才认为他一直紧绷着。
　　但他本来就不是孩童，扮孩童才叫不轻松。何况就算是孩童，也不是人人都和二哥一样闹腾。他就喜欢安静。
　　不过老师关心他，李玄霸没必要反驳。他只需要乖乖听着就行。
　　讲完今日的“课”后，宇文弼精力不济，没有留李玄霸用饭，让人送李玄霸离开。
　　李玄霸离开前犹豫了一下，问道：“我带了些礼物给……那个，咳，就是……”
　　宇文弼失笑：“你吞吞吐吐做什么？是带给小娘吧？”
　　李玄霸道：“她正在守孝，我现在赠送礼物，是不是不太好？”
　　他本来只是想着都来了宇文家，给未婚妻带礼物是普通礼节。没想到宇文珠在为宇文伉守孝，他就不知道该不该送了。
　　宇文弼道：“礼物留下吧。她就算是守孝，礼物也是可以收的。”
　　李玄霸松了口气，留下礼物后离开。
　　李玄霸送的礼物只是一卷书，没有特意包装。
　　外男送给女子的礼物，就算是未婚夫妻，也要经过长辈检查后才会给予。
　　宇文弼翻开书，自言自语：“看笔迹，应是大德亲手抄写……《千金方稿》？孙神医不会也将大德当做弟子，连未写完的医书都给大德过目。”
　　他粗粗翻完了整本书，脸上露出了不满的表情。
　　这整本书居然真的只是抄写了孙思邈部分较为浅显的医书手稿，一点私人话语都没有传递。
　　宇文弼本以为李玄霸肯定会在书本中夹带几句对孙女的问候。
　　他与高颎离开朝堂权力中枢后，许多朝臣不再忌讳和他们交流。长孙晟因李世民是他和高颎弟子，与他们私下书信往来增多。
　　长孙晟曾抱怨，李世民实在是太过“嚣张”。以前李世民与长孙小娘子交换书籍，只是在书本上写几句心得。现在两人直接变成了书信往来，交换的书本就是用来夹信的。
　　宇文弼本以为，有李世民这样的兄长，李玄霸肯定也是个“嚣张”之人，都做好了心理准备。
　　如果李玄霸太过孟浪，他一定要提醒李玄霸，现在他和自家孙女还小，不要太早谈论儿女之事。
　　但李玄霸一点私人话语都没传递，宇文弼又不满了。
　　有李大雄这样的兄长作为榜样，大德怎么如此木讷，都不学着大雄一些？
　　宇文弼决定等病好之后就把李世民叫来叮嘱一二，让李世民好好教教弟弟。
　　“不过这礼物，珠儿肯定很喜欢。”宇文弼想着孙女对医术的痴迷，露出了慈祥的笑容。
　　虽然仍旧很担心李玄霸的病弱，但除开身体，孙女给自己选的未来夫婿真的是太有眼光了。
　　不说前途，李玄霸能支持孙女继续研读医书，光这一点，世间男子都很难做到。
　　“大德，你可要好好保重身体啊。”
　　宇文弼对这位弟子兼孙女婿越来越满意了。
　　……
　　李玄霸回到家时，正想着要不要赶去禁苑突击检查二哥老不老实，被杨广的口谕叫去了宫里。
　　李玄霸还以为杨广要检查他填词的作业，特意揣了几首词在身上应付杨广，没想到杨广给他介绍了几个倭国人。
　　杨广笑道：“李三郎是我们大隋年纪最小的秀才。别看他年幼，他的才华绝对是大隋年轻一辈中顶尖。让他给你们做老师，你们一定会受益无穷。”
　　李玄霸：“？？？”
　　哈？！让我给倭国人当老师？！我能拒绝吗？！
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 56: Yuwen Bi’s Dissatisfaction

Chang Jun and Wang Junzheng soon set off with the Sui Dynasty’s diplomatic mission. Yan Zhen and Xiang Gu followed along, feeling deeply uneasy.

Li Xuanba personally saw the two of them out of the Eastern Capital.

Li Shimin, naturally, had to join in the excitement. He didn’t just come himself; he brought Du Ruhui, Fang Qiao, Xue Shou, and Zhangsun Wuji, who had finally arrived in the Eastern Capital to meet up with his friends.

"I am quite curious about the nations of the South Seas. Collect as many of their books as you can," Li Shimin said, acting as if Li Xuanba’s subordinates were his own, and began assigning tasks without the slightest bit of reserve. "It would be best if you could capture a couple of local nobles and bring them back."

Li Xuanba sighed and corrected him: "Not capture. Invite."

Li Shimin replied, "It’s all the same."

Li Xuanba asked, "How is it the same?"

Li Shimin whistled.

Li Xuanba felt that his Second Brother was deliberately asking for a beating.

Li Xuanba urged the envoys: "Whatever you do, do not listen to my Second Brother! Do not go around kidnapping nobles from other countries!"

Yan Zhen and Xiang Gu were left between laughter and tears, their inner anxiety significantly eased.

Did he really need to warn them? How could they possibly go about kidnapping foreign nobles!

Fang Qiao and the others listened to Li Shimin’s nonsense and teased him for it.

Du Ruhui said, "Li Er, if you’re so capable, why don’t you go and capture a few foreign nobles yourself?"

Zhangsun Wuji added with disdain, "He’s all talk and no action."

Xue Shou sighed, "Second Young Master Li, say less. Trouble comes from the mouth."

Fang Qiao said sternly, "You must not provoke conflicts between nations."

Li Shimin covered his ears: "Can’t hear you, can’t hear you."

Du Ruhui, Zhangsun Wuji, and Xue Shou continued to tease Li Shimin with laughter, but Fang Qiao felt a bit worried.

He hoped that his future lord was merely joking, and that he wouldn’t truly order the capture of foreign nobles to amuse himself in the imperial court once he became Emperor.

When Li Xuanba saw off Yan Zhen and Xiang Gu, he visited Chang Jun and Wang Junzheng to request that they look after the two men.

He had already quietly gifted Chang Jun and Wang Junzheng a great deal of wealth previously, so this time it was merely a verbal request.

Chang Jun and Wang Junzheng also pretended they had never received any wealth from Li Xuanba, acting as if they were discussing nothing but friendship.

After sending Yan Zhen and Xiang Gu off, Li Shimin began clamoring to go hunting.

Li Xuanba had matters to attend to this time and did not follow his Second Brother. He warned his friends one by one, telling them to keep a close eye on his Second Brother and not to let him go hunting for wild beasts again.

Zhangsun Wuji was eager to try: "Hunting wild beasts? Is it that interesting?"

Li Xuanba gave him a deadpan look: "Are you trying to make me report you to General Zhangsun?"

Zhangsun Wuji was speechless: "Second Young Master Li says you’re a little snitch, and he’s really not wrong."

Li Xuanba replied, "That’s right, I am. You can try me."

Zhangsun Wuji covered his mouth, making a "zip it" gesture.

Li Shimin laughed, "Don’t worry, I know my limits."

Li Xuanba said, "Don’t worry? When you say ‘don’t worry,’ I am not at ease at all."

Li Xuanba gave them one last round of warnings, specifically cautioning Zhangsun Wuji not to follow his Second Brother into trouble, before leaving with a heavy heart.

Zhangsun Wuji’s eyes darted around. He draped an arm over Li Shimin’s shoulder and said, "The more he says we can’t do something, the more we should do it. Why should we listen to him?"

Fang Qiao frowned: "If you encounter danger, can you take responsibility?"

Du Ruhui teased, "Since Fourth Young Master Zhangsun is so confident, Li Er, let’s not intervene. Let’s watch Fourth Young Master Zhangsun take on a tiger alone."

Xue Shou asked curiously, "Can Fourth Young Master Zhangsun hunt a tiger by himself?"

Li Shimin burst into laughter, patting Zhangsun Wuji on the shoulder: "That’s right! He definitely can! Not just a tiger! He wouldn’t even be afraid if he faced a pack of wolves alone! We could throw him into a wolf pack and see!"

Zhangsun Wuji: "No, I can’t. If you want to murder me, just say so."

Li Shimin continued to laugh heartily: "Just try it!"

Zhangsun Wuji pulled his arm back from Li Shimin’s shoulder and moved far away from him.

Du Ruhui and Xue Shou joined in Li Shimin’s laughter. Fang Qiao’s brow relaxed, but he remained somewhat wary of Zhangsun Wuji in his heart.

Will Zhangsun Wuji lead the lord astray in the future? I hope Zhangsun Wuji knows his place.

As Li Shimin and his companions went off to the imperial hunting grounds amidst laughter, Li Xuanba arrived at the home of Yuwen Bi.

After Li Xuanba became betrothed to Yuwen Zhu, he had not yet visited the Yuwen household.

Yuwen Bi’s grandson had just died prematurely, and the whole family was grieving. If Li Xuanba had gone to build rapport with Yuwen Zhu at such a time, it would not just be a lack of emotional intelligence, but a sign of a failing mind.

Children who die young are considered "unlucky" and cannot be buried in the ancestral graves; they cannot even have tombstones, and no one is required to observe mourning for them.

Many people simply find a random spot in the wilderness, wrap the child in cloth, and bury them casually.

The Yuwen family did not "disdain" the "bad luck" of Yuwen Kang’s premature death. Although he could not be buried in the ancestral grave, they chose a plot with good feng shui, erected a tombstone, and built a mound. They even set up a spirit tablet for him in their home, offering incense on holidays and the anniversary of his death. However, formal mourning was not required.

"But the young lady insisted on observing mourning for An’er and moved to a separate villa to live alone," Yuwen Bi sighed. "I intended for her to meet with you, but she said she did not wish to contact outsiders until she finished mourning for An’er. She is a bit headstrong; I hope you do not blame her."

Li Xuanba shook his head: "She is grieving for a brother with whom she shared a deep bond; this is not being headstrong."

Yuwen Bi said, "If you do not mind, then I am relieved."

Although Yuwen Bi knew that Li Xuanba was a gentle and kind child, he was still somewhat anxious because his granddaughter’s behavior violated social norms. Seeing that Li Xuanba truly did not care, he finally breathed a sigh of relief.

One was his disciple, the other his granddaughter. If the two did not get along in the future, Yuwen Bi truly wouldn’t know what to do.

When facing his juniors, Yuwen Bi, who was incomparably tough in front of outsiders, was just an ordinary old man who doted on his kin.

After chatting about family matters and asking about the progress of Li Xuanba and Li Shimin’s studies, Yuwen Bi finally brought up the real business.

After Yuwen Kang’s death, Yuwen Bi had fallen ill from excessive grief, but he had forbidden Li Shimin and Li Xuanba from visiting.

The premature death of a child is an unlucky event. Any family in such a situation would close their doors to guests for a period, waiting for the bad luck to dissipate before interacting with outsiders. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba did not care for social conventions, but the Yuwen family had to consider public opinion.

Yuwen Bi had originally intended to mourn his grandson at home for a while. He had summoned Li Xuanba early because of Yang Guang’s change of heart regarding appointing Li Jiancheng as the Harmonizer of Music.

The matter of Xiang Gu had been handled for Li Xuanba by Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi.

Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi had served as high-ranking officials for four generations of emperors; their political acumen was not lacking. Especially Gao Jiong, who was very experienced in dealing with the Emperor’s spies.

In the original history, the two of them would be killed by Yang Guang, but that was only because they suffered from not understanding Yang Guang’s personality.

Gao Jiong had been able to retreat unscathed during the succession struggles; Yuwen Bi was even more completely neutral. Given their age and seniority, as long as they did not defy the Emperor, it was basically impossible for them to face a death sentence.

The idea of being killed for "slandering the government" was something that neither of them, nor any official in the Sui court, could have imagined.

Once they learned of Yang Guang’s personality and became thoroughly disappointed in him, dealing with him became quite easy.

Previously, when Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi lured Yang Guang into opening the granaries to provide disaster relief, they had utilized the spies Yang Guang had planted around them.

Li Xuanba’s current move was exactly the same as what they had done. Since Yuwen Bi knew of Xiang Gu’s existence, he naturally guessed what Li Xuanba had done the moment he heard of Yang Guang’s change in decree.

Yuwen Bi was worried that Li Xuanba would become too focused on schemes and tricks, changing his nature, and also worried that Li Xuanba would underestimate the Emperor and leave behind evidence. Thus, despite his illness and the bad luck of his grandson’s death, he had urgently called Li Xuanba over to warn him.

Li Xuanba listened with an open mind.

Seeing that Li Xuanba was not smug about having outmaneuvered Yang Guang, Yuwen Bi was very satisfied with him.

Since his disciple was not becoming immersed in schemes, Yuwen Bi felt at ease teaching Li Xuanba about the oversights in this matter.

Although one should not let schemes change their nature, Li Xuanba still had to be proficient in them. Schemes were sometimes very useful, and more importantly, only those who could skillfully use them would not be schemed against by others.

Yuwen Bi taught Li Xuanba for a full hour, meticulously reviewing everything from the memorial Li Xuanba had written to Yang Guang, to how he had guided Yang Guang to focus his attention on Li Jiancheng.

Li Xuanba tried his best to commit his teacher’s lessons to memory.

His plan to divert Yang Guang’s attention this time was actually quite crude; it relied mostly on his youth, allowing others to underestimate and overlook him, which was why it had succeeded so easily.

Although Li Xuanba had utilized his youth to avoid suspicion while executing the plan, he would eventually grow up. There was no harm in learning more sophisticated planning in advance.

Next time, Li Xuanba would try to treat himself as an adult and plan carefully without relying on the advantage of his youth.

Yuwen Bi said, "While you are still young and won’t arouse suspicion, you can try a few more times to accumulate experience. Do not tell Gao Zhaoxuan about these things; he is too pedantic."

Li Xuanba thought to himself, what a coincidence—Teacher Gao had said the exact same thing in a letter sent not long ago, telling him to accumulate experience but not to tell you.

Li Xuanba replied obediently, "This disciple understands."

Yuwen Bi said, "Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Xue Shou are excellent. The friends you have made are very good. Will they have a place in the new dynasty in the future?"

Li Xuanba nodded.

Yuwen Bi said, "Do not rely too much on your prophecies. Those who trust fate too much will be played by fate."

Li Xuanba said, "Yes, Teacher, please rest assured. I did not actively seek to befriend them; meeting them in advance was just a coincidence."

Li Xuanba described to Yuwen Bi how Fang Qiao wanted to print a collection of essays in a bookstore, how Du Ruhui had visited the Tang Duke’s mansion through his connection with Fang Qiao, and how Xue Shou and his Second Brother had hit it off at the Prince of Qi’s banquet.

After listening, Yuwen Bi, who had been grieving for so long, stroked his beard and smiled for the first time in a long while: "Fate can change, and it has already changed in a better direction. You should also relax a little."

Li Xuanba was puzzled: "I have always been relaxed."

Yuwen Bi shook his head: "You have always been tense."

Li Xuanba did not understand. He didn’t feel that he had been tense at all.

Yuwen Bi rubbed Li Xuanba’s head and said, "You are still a child. Learn from your Second Brother; play more and worry less."

Li Xuanba nodded perfunctorily. He guessed that perhaps it was because he didn’t act like a child that his teacher thought he was always tense.

But he wasn’t a child to begin with; pretending to be one was what made it not relaxing. Besides, even among children, not everyone was as boisterous as his Second Brother. He liked quiet.

However, since his teacher was concerned about him, there was no need for Li Xuanba to argue. He just needed to listen obediently.

After finishing today’s "lesson," Yuwen Bi was exhausted and did not keep Li Xuanba for a meal, having someone see him out.

Before leaving, Li Xuanba hesitated and asked, "I brought some gifts for... well, ahem, that is..."

Yuwen Bi chuckled: "Why are you stammering? It’s for the young lady, isn’t it?"

Li Xuanba said, "She is observing mourning. Is it inappropriate for me to give gifts now?"

He had originally thought that since he was already at the Yuwen house, bringing a gift for his fiancée was just common courtesy. He hadn’t expected that Yuwen Zhu would be mourning for Yuwen Kang, so he hadn’t been sure whether to give it.

Yuwen Bi said, "Leave the gifts. Even if she is mourning, she can still accept gifts."

Li Xuanba breathed a sigh of relief, left the gifts, and departed.

The gift Li Xuanba brought was just a scroll of books, without any special packaging.

Gifts from a man to a woman, even between betrothed couples, had to be inspected by elders before being handed over.

Yuwen Bi opened the book and muttered to himself: "Looking at the handwriting, it should be Da De’s own transcription... *The Thousand Gold Prescriptions Manuscript*? Don’t tell me the Divine Doctor Sun also treats Da De as a disciple, letting him see even unfinished medical texts."

He flipped through the entire book roughly, a look of dissatisfaction appearing on his face.

The entire book was really just a transcription of some of Sun Simiao’s more elementary medical manuscript drafts, without a single word of personal message included.

Yuwen Bi had expected that Li Xuanba would surely tuck a few words of greeting to his granddaughter inside the book.

After he and Gao Jiong left the center of court power, many officials no longer avoided communicating with them. Zhangsun Sheng, because Li Shimin was a disciple of both him and Gao Jiong, had increased his private correspondence with them.

Zhangsun Sheng had once complained that Li Shimin was simply too "arrogant." In the past, when Li Shimin exchanged books with the young Lady Zhangsun, he would only write a few insights in the margins. Now, the two had directly turned to exchanging letters, and the books they swapped were merely used to hold the letters.

Yuwen Bi had thought that with an older brother like Li Shimin, Li Xuanba would surely be an "arrogant" person as well, and he had mentally prepared himself.

If Li Xuanba were too brazen, he would have to remind him that he and his granddaughter were still young and should not talk about matters of the heart too early.

But since Li Xuanba hadn’t passed on a single personal word, Yuwen Bi was dissatisfied again.

With a brother like Li Da Xiong as a role model, why was Da De so dull? Why didn’t he learn from Da Xiong?

Yuwen Bi decided that once he recovered from his illness, he would call Li Shimin over to give him some advice and have him properly teach his younger brother.

"However, Zhu’er will surely love this gift." Yuwen Bi thought of his granddaughter’s obsession with medicine and revealed a kindly smile.

Although he was still very worried about Li Xuanba’s frail health, aside from his physical condition, the future husband his granddaughter had chosen for herself truly had excellent taste.

Not to mention his prospects, the fact that Li Xuanba could support his granddaughter in continuing to study medicine—even that alone was something few men in the world could do.

"Da De, you must take good care of your health."

Yuwen Bi was becoming more and more satisfied with this disciple and future grandson-in-law.

...

When Li Xuanba returned home, he was just thinking about whether to rush to the imperial hunting grounds to conduct a surprise inspection of his Second Brother’s behavior, when he was summoned to the palace by an imperial oral decree from Yang Guang.

Li Xuanba thought Yang Guang wanted to check his homework on composing lyrics, so he tucked a few poems into his robes to deal with Yang Guang. He never expected that Yang Guang would introduce him to a few Japanese envoys.

Yang Guang laughed: "Third Young Master Li is the youngest scholar in our Great Sui. Don’t let his youth fool you; his talent is absolutely top-tier among the younger generation of the Great Sui. Let him be your teacher, and you will surely benefit infinitely."

Li Xuanba: "???"

Huh?! You want me to be a teacher for the Japanese?! Can I refuse?!

chunks.chapterTitle: 第57章 想办法换个使臣
chunks.chineseText:
第57章 想办法换个使臣

=
　　李玄霸愣了许久， 才在对方字正腔圆的自我介绍中，从记忆的角落里挖出了关于这几个倭国人的历史记载。
　　为首的倭国人叫小野妹子。
　　公元607年，也就是大业三年， 倭国向大隋派出使团， 为首使官为小野妹子， 于年底到达东都洛阳。
　　李玄霸去年在大兴守孝。大隋每年接待的外夷使团又很多，这点小事自然不会传到大兴城中。
　　李玄霸努力回忆了一下，飞速整理了一番这段历史。
　　小野妹子带来的使臣团中有许多留学生。这些留学生在华夏生活了几十年， 经历了隋唐的变革，学习了大量先进知识。
　　他们回到倭国后，于公元645年推动了大化改新， 倭国全面学习唐朝先进经验，从奴隶制社会过渡到封建制社会， 并正式改名“日本国”。
　　“日本”从此诞生。
　　大化改新与明治维新是倭国历史中最重要的两次社会变革。李玄霸虽然没有关注过世界历史， 但“遣唐使”和“留学生”促进了倭国的进步是唐太宗的“黑点”之一，李玄霸自然会深入了解“大化改新”的事。
　　抛开职业素养，李玄霸当然不认为是唐太宗“资敌”。
　　首先，后人不能因为未来发生的事，去指责先人没有未卜先知。
　　倭国当大唐的狗时， 与现在当老美的狗一样乖巧。唐太宗对乖巧的外夷都很和善。
　　再者，推动大化改新的倭国进步人士大多是大隋大业三年就来到华夏的资深留学生。
　　说得更远一些， 倭国在汉朝时就与华夏王朝有经济和文化的交流。
　　一个强大的国家，肯定会有周边国家来“取经”。
　　强大就一定会开放包容其他国家其他文化，不会闭关锁国不允许其他国家的人来交流。而只要交流， 先进的文化就肯定会传播出去。
　　当时大唐文化辐射很广， 不仅是倭国受益。唐太宗在输出大唐先进文化和制度时， 也派留学生去周边国家学习先进技术。制糖技术就是唐太宗派官方使团去学的。
　　事实上， 初唐和盛唐时期，大唐最爱给留学生教导先进文化和经验，输出文化；然后派自己的留学生去学习外面的技术，输入技术。
　　李玄霸从自己浅薄的认知出发，觉得大唐做得不错。
　　大业三年，倭国使团到达；大业四年，隋炀帝派裴世清出使倭国，小野妹子随行；九月，倭国天皇派小野妹子陪同裴世清回大隋。
　　从此倭国与华夏的官方交流出现了第一次高|潮。
　　时间短暂，李玄霸只在脑海中粗略回忆了一遍这段历史。
　　他很快回过神，用嫌弃的目光扫视了一遍倭国使臣，然后对杨广道：“陛下的命令，臣不得不遵从。只是这师徒名义还是算了吧。臣收弟子还是得看身份。”
　　杨广失笑：“是朕口误。你只需要闲暇时候教导他们一二，没有什么师徒关系。朕怎会让你收蛮夷为徒？蛮夷没有资格拜师。”
　　李玄霸道：“陛下圣明！”
　　当杨广把自己创死人的话对向倭国人的时候，李玄霸觉得这话前所未有的悦耳。
　　杨广一口一个“蛮夷”，倭国人本来对大隋皇帝居然让他们向一个垂髫孩童拜师不满，现在就更不满。
　　但他们不满，也不敢对大隋皇帝表示不敬。
　　他们还得对李玄霸点头哈腰，满脸堆笑，请李玄霸多多指教。
　　倭国谦恭的礼仪一直做得特别足，特别是在有求于人的时候。
　　李玄霸因为心里膈应，很想拒绝此事。
　　但他还是忍下了恶心，答应了杨广的要求。
　　大隋和倭国已经互派使臣，两国交流不可避免。自己拒绝之后，倭国人也会有新的老师。
　　而且就算自己答应教导倭国使臣，倭国使臣也还会花钱去找其他大隋人求教，学习更多的大隋知识，不会吊在自己一人身上。他阻止不了倭国对外学习，也阻止不了倭国“大化改新”的历史进程。
　　别说现在是大隋，李玄霸无法左右杨广的选择，就是到了大唐，李玄霸也不可能拉着他哥去把倭国平了。
　　倭国只有几个矿有点价值，而这些矿不需要战争就可以拿下。对倭国举国用兵，对大唐毫无益处。
　　即便现在平了倭国，以目前的科技水平不可能管理好一个远离大陆的岛国，倭国将来仍旧会自立。
　　若是李玄霸自己一个人跳进富士山口能引发富士山火山喷发，哪怕他再惜命也会跳进去。
　　但让他因为解未来之气，让大唐好儿郎白白牺牲在倭国，他做不到。
　　他知道，就算二哥知道了未来的事也不会对倭国出兵。因为比起很久远的未来，大唐百姓的生活才更重要。
　　未来的事该未来人来解决，身为大唐皇帝，二哥只会注重当下。
　　李玄霸反复在心底告诉自己要“冷静”，将情绪压下，做出了理智的决断。
　　虽然阻挡不了历史进程，但他如果参与其中，或许能为大唐谋夺更多的利益。
　　比如离大陆很近，自己把自己画进了大唐地图中的九州岛。
　　华夏所有士族都对外夷很倨傲。李玄霸对倭国使臣的态度傲慢很正常。
　　杨广不仅没有因为李玄霸给倭国使臣甩脸色生气，还很赞赏李玄霸对倭国使臣的嫌弃。
　　杨广马上就要让裴世清出使倭国。在派使臣出使倭国之前，杨广特意把李玄霸召来，就是用年幼的李玄霸羞辱倭国使臣。
　　我大隋一个垂髫孩童就如此厉害，你倭国赶紧给我趴着！
　　让倭国使臣退下后，杨广才将真实意图告诉李玄霸，让李玄霸在“苏因高”离开大隋前，好好以教导的借口羞辱倭国使臣。
　　苏因高是小野妹子在大隋的名字。
　　李玄霸一口答应。
　　杨广咬牙切齿：“一弹丸蛮夷，居然也敢自称天子。若不是高丽和突厥在朕卧榻之侧，朕定会派兵灭了倭国！”
　　杨广在历史中出了名的特别厚待外夷。能把这样的杨广惹生气，倭国也是真有一番本事。
　　杨广说出这话时，李玄霸在脑海中又冒出一段相关的历史记载。
　　小野妹子出使大隋，递交给隋炀帝的国书抬头是“日出处天子致书日没处天子无恙”，把隋炀帝气得够呛。
　　自汉朝起，华夏一直是东亚老大，其他小国都要向华夏王朝朝贡。在朝贡体系中，只有华夏的皇帝能自称“天子”。
　　倭国本是汉朝的藩国，现在倭国国王不仅自称天子，还说自己是“日出处的天子”，隋炀帝是“日没处的天子”，其居心叵测，简直溢于言表。
　　隋炀帝当时气得直骂“蛮夷书有无礼者，勿复以闻”。但他是个特别重视外夷的人，外夷越不重视他，他就越重视。所以次年，隋炀帝还是派使臣出使倭国。
　　大业五年小野妹子再次出访大隋时，倭国将国书抬头改为“东天皇敬白西皇帝”，自称“天皇”，避开了天子的称谓，隋炀帝居然就这么满意了，与倭国正式建交。
　　李玄霸记起这段记载后，十分不解。
　　“东天皇敬白西皇帝”对隋炀帝而言也算十分不敬了吧？隋炀帝这么骄傲的人，居然忍下了这口气，之后还对倭国十分礼遇，接纳了许多倭国留学生留在大隋学习华夏先进文化。
　　当年汉光武帝刘秀可是赐予倭国“倭奴国”金印，倭国不过是大汉附属国之一。现在倭国国王自称“东天皇”，叫你“西皇帝”，你还满意？你还礼遇？你要脸吗？！
　　李玄霸满心不解地回到家，破天荒地拿出小弓箭去凌虐可怜的校场稻草人。
　　李渊回家后，发现李玄霸居然在练习射箭，吓得他赶紧摸着李玄霸的额头叫医师。
　　李玄霸无奈道：“父亲，我没生病。”
　　李渊道：“难道是谁惹你生气了？你刚从宫里回来，难道是陛下又侮辱我们唐国公府？”
　　李玄霸本来不想与李渊交流正事。不过李玄霸转念一想，李渊作为这个时代的勋贵，他的思想或许能解决自己的疑惑，便回答道：“今日陛下让我教导倭国使臣大隋诗书。我听闻倭国原本是大汉一个属国，被大汉赐名‘倭奴国’。如今倭国国王居然对陛下自称‘日出天子’，贬称陛下为‘日没天子’，陛下居然还愿意与倭国建交。我实在是难以理解。”
　　李渊皱着眉头想了许久，才想起来“倭国”和“倭奴国”是什么。
　　他道：“倭国与高丽隔水相望，陛下有进攻高丽的心，或许想联合倭国一同进攻高丽。至于倭国的不敬，可以先解决高丽之后，再做打算。”
　　隋唐所说的“高丽”就是指高句丽。
　　“高丽”本是“高句丽”简称，但正式国称是“高句丽”。但华夏王朝与高句丽交往时，总爱在正式文书上直接写简称“高丽”。
　　高句丽：我们全称是高句丽。
　　南北朝统治者：好的，高丽。
　　高句丽：请尊重我们的国名，我国正式名称是高句丽！
　　隋文帝：高丽。
　　隋炀帝：高丽。
　　唐太宗：高丽。
　　唐高宗：高丽。
　　于是南北朝时，“高句丽”和“高丽”还混用；隋唐时，所有史籍都将高句丽记载为“高丽”。高句丽人也自称“高丽”，改名“高丽国”了。
　　现在没有高句丽国，只有高丽国。
　　朝鲜王氏王朝建立的时候，为了一些众人皆知的小心思，将国名定为“高丽”。王氏高丽和隋唐时的高丽没有任何关系，所以后世历史研究就将隋唐的高丽称为“高句丽”，与王氏高丽做区分。
　　已经灭亡的高句丽委屈。他们才是真正的高丽，先来者被迫为后来者让名。
　　高丽是扶余人朱蒙趁着西汉式微的时候自立的华夏边疆小国，在魏晋南北朝中原混乱时，抢夺了不少中原王朝的领土，是华夏领土上的割据势力。
　　华夏统一后，肯定要收复故土，灭掉割据势力，所以大隋与高丽的战争是肯定会发生的。
　　隋文帝就对高丽动过兵，只是因为天气原因临时撤兵。杨广继位之后，朝堂都知道大隋会完成隋文帝时的未竟之功，灭掉高丽割据势力。
　　如果不是杨广要修东都、运河、长城、很多很多行宫，大隋早就与高丽开战了。
　　李渊很清楚皇帝对高丽磨刀霍霍，所以轻松猜出了皇帝的心思。
　　李渊对李玄霸道：“倭国无礼，但只是一个弹丸蛮夷，陛下懒得与它争辩。待收拾高丽之后，若它仍旧无礼，再收拾它不迟。”
　　看着李渊淡然的神情，李玄霸明白了为何杨广会忍得下这口气。
　　因为大隋看不起倭国，认为倭国蛮夷不懂礼仪很正常，与倭国计较都是自跌身份。
　　不只是杨广，华夏王朝所有人都认为，与其和蛮夷计较蛮夷根本不可能懂的礼仪，不如注重实际利益。
　　现在倭国对大隋的利益，就是能帮大隋攻打高丽。
　　李玄霸对李渊道：“倭国不会出兵。”
　　李渊道：“不出兵也无所谓，别捣乱就行。陛下所做的事是远交近攻。”
　　他冷笑道：“陛下虽对臣子过于刻薄寡恩，但为君的基本常识还是有。”
　　李玄霸沉默。在高丽被灭前，杨广会一直容忍倭国了。
　　但高丽被灭时，大隋都被灭了很多年了，啧。
　　看来在大隋灭亡前，他能对倭国做的事不多。隋炀帝真没用。
　　李玄霸问道：“不过以陛下的脾气，应该不会直接忍下这口气。父亲，陛下给倭国国王的国书，会斥责倭国国王吗？”
　　李渊道：“当然会。以陛下的性格，绝对会在国书中把倭国国王狠狠嘲讽一顿。如果倭国国王看到了陛下的国书后，仍旧愿意派遣使臣前来，就说明倭国国王自知失礼，向陛下赔罪。陛下才会考虑与倭国建交。陛下给倭国国王的国书，就是大隋的试探。”
　　李玄霸脸上浮现出清浅的笑容：“父亲，你说倭国使臣会不会将国书遗失？”
　　李渊道：“陛下不是派出了使臣吗？国书应当在大隋使臣手中，怎么会遗失？”
　　李玄霸微笑道：“假如呢？”
　　李渊想了想，道：“如果真的出现这种事，只可能是倭国使臣贿赂大隋使臣。为何你会如此想？大隋使臣肯定会以大隋利益为主。”
　　李玄霸道：“我只是以最大恶意揣度倭国而已。我听闻倭国有小礼无大义，自汉时起就该做一些自欺欺人的事。他们或许会故意‘遗失’大隋斥责的国书，然后与大隋建交，还厚颜无耻称大隋天子承认倭国国王也是天子。”
　　李渊失笑：“大德，你似乎很讨厌倭国？”
　　李玄霸道：“倭奴国居然自称日出国天子，贬称陛下为日没国天子，我怎能不厌恶？他们这并不仅仅是贬低陛下，而是贬低我们整个华夏中土。”
　　李渊听李玄霸这么一说，虽然觉得蛮夷小国不懂礼仪正常，也觉得十分膈应。
　　他安慰李玄霸道：“蛮夷多不懂礼仪，你若生气，是气不完的。不过你担心的也有道理，这次出使倭国的使臣是谁？我去和他说说，让他一定要把国书带到。”
　　李玄霸道：“裴世清。”
　　李渊沉默。
　　半晌，他扶额道：“裴世清是个极其贪财的人。听你这么一说，我也担心他真的可能会做出收了倭国使臣的贿赂，把国书不小心遗失的事了。”
　　李玄霸心道，果然如此。
　　历史中小野妹子就是“遗失”了隋炀帝给倭国国王的国书。
　　历史学家猜测，隋炀帝不是好脾气的人，他给倭国国王的国书中一定用词激烈。有可能是小野妹子担心倭国国王迁怒他，主动丢弃了国书；也有可能是小野妹子私下把国书先给倭国国王看了，倭国国王让小野妹子托词国书丢弃，所以小野妹子遗失国书这么大的事也没有受到惩罚。
　　但国书应该是大隋使臣递交给倭国国王，怎会被小野妹子弄丢？
　　而且以隋炀帝之后对倭国的态度，他似乎以为倭国已经臣服于他。否则就算需要“远交近攻”，以隋炀帝的臭脾气，对惹怒他的倭国过于礼遇，实在是不正常。
　　隋炀帝很可能不知道国书丢失，以为倭国服软。
　　所以在“国书遗失”事件中，大隋使臣裴世清一定难辞其咎。
　　如果这次隋炀帝的国书被大隋使臣当众念出来了呢？倭国国王会有什么反应？仍旧厚着脸皮装作什么都没听到，继续与大隋建交？
　　李玄霸很想知道。
　　李玄霸道：“父亲，虽然只是微小的可能，但倭国侮辱我大隋天子在先，这口气必须讨回来！父亲可有办法让陛下换一个更刚直的使臣？”
　　李渊还是第一次见到三儿子有求于他。
　　他立刻拍着李玄霸的脑袋，十分自信地保证道：“这点小事，交给父亲！”
　　李玄霸努力挤出仰慕的神情：“父亲真厉害！”
　　李渊被李玄霸一吹嘘，第二日一大早，就递牌子去面圣。
　　“陛下！臣听闻倭国蛮夷小国，居然对大隋的天子无理！这口气陛下能忍，臣也不能容忍！臣请出使倭国！”
　　杨广：“……”
　　他十分无语。即使他忌惮李渊，但李渊作为大隋堂堂唐国公，自己的表兄，自己能侮辱，出使倭国？倭国哪配？
　　在李渊的胡搅蛮缠下，为了不让唐国公出使倭国，杨广换了一队最会骂人的使臣，让他们务必痛骂倭国国王一顿。
　　裴世清遗憾地没了这个会有丰厚收益的好差事，对李渊心生不满。
　　唐国公府中。
　　李渊得意道：“大德，父亲是不是很厉害！”
　　李玄霸夸赞道：“父亲太厉害了！”
　　这次李玄霸的夸赞是真心的。
