Chapter 57: Finding a Way to Replace the Envoy

Li Xuanba stood stunned for a long time. It was only when the other party introduced himself in crisp, articulate Chinese that he managed to dredge up historical records regarding these Wa people from the corners of his memory.

The leader of the Wa delegation was named Ono no Imoko.

In 607 AD, the third year of the Daye era, the Wa state sent a diplomatic mission to the Great Sui. The chief envoy was Ono no Imoko, who arrived in the eastern capital of Luoyang at the end of the year.

Li Xuanba had been in Daxing observing a mourning period last year. Since the Great Sui received many foreign delegations every year, such a minor detail naturally would not have reached Daxing City.

Li Xuanba struggled to recall and quickly organized this segment of history in his mind.

The delegation brought by Ono no Imoko included many students studying abroad. These students lived in China for decades, witnessed the transition from Sui to Tang, and acquired a vast amount of advanced knowledge.

After returning to the Wa state, they spearheaded the Taika Reform in 645 AD. The Wa state comprehensively adopted the advanced experiences of the Tang Dynasty, transitioned from a slave society to a feudal society, and officially renamed itself "Nihon" (Japan).

Thus, "Japan" was born.

The Taika Reform and the Meiji Restoration were the two most significant social transformations in Japanese history. Although Li Xuanba had never paid much attention to world history, the fact that "Kentoshi" (envoys to Tang) and "international students" had facilitated Japan's progress was considered one of the "stains" on Emperor Taizong of Tang's record. Naturally, Li Xuanba had delved deeply into the "Taika Reform."

Setting aside professional ethics, Li Xuanba certainly did not believe that Emperor Taizong of Tang was "aiding the enemy."

First of all, later generations cannot blame their ancestors for failing to foresee the future based on events that had not yet occurred.

When the Wa state acted as a dog for the Great Tang, they were as obedient as they were when acting as a dog for the Americans in the future. Emperor Taizong of Tang was always benevolent toward obedient foreigners.

Furthermore, most of the progressive Wa figures who pushed for the Taika Reform were veteran students who had come to China as early as the third year of the Daye era of the Great Sui.

To look further back, the Wa state had been engaged in economic and cultural exchanges with Chinese dynasties since the Han Dynasty.

A powerful nation will inevitably attract surrounding countries to "seek wisdom."

Strength necessitates openness and inclusivity toward other nations and cultures; it does not involve closing the borders and forbidding interaction. As long as there is exchange, advanced culture will inevitably spread.

At that time, the cultural influence of the Great Tang was vast, and it was not only the Wa state that benefited. While Emperor Taizong of Tang exported the advanced culture and institutions of the Great Tang, he also sent his own students to neighboring countries to learn advanced technologies. Sugar-making technology, for instance, was learned by official delegations sent by Emperor Taizong.

In fact, during the early and high Tang periods, the Great Tang was most eager to teach advanced culture and experience to international students, exporting its culture; then, it would send its own students abroad to learn foreign technologies, importing them.

Based on his own shallow understanding, Li Xuanba felt the Great Tang was doing quite well.

In the third year of Daye, the Wa delegation arrived; in the fourth year of Daye, Emperor Yang of Sui sent Pei Shiqing as an envoy to the Wa state, with Ono no Imoko accompanying him. In the ninth month, the Wa Emperor sent Ono no Imoko to accompany Pei Shiqing back to the Great Sui.

From then on, the first climax of official exchange between the Wa state and China occurred.

Time was short; Li Xuanba only roughly recalled this history in his mind.

He quickly regained his composure, swept a look of disdain over the Wa envoys, and then said to Yang Guang, "Your Majesty’s command, I must obey. However, let us forgo the title of teacher and student. When I take on disciples, I must consider their status."

Yang Guang laughed, "It was a slip of my tongue. You only need to instruct them in your spare time; there is no master-disciple relationship. How could I let you take barbarians as disciples? Barbarians are not qualified to apprentice themselves to you."

Li Xuanba said, "Your Majesty is wise!"

When Yang Guang directed his lethal tongue toward the Wa people, Li Xuanba found the words more pleasant than ever.

Yang Guang kept calling them "barbarians." The Wa people, already dissatisfied that the Emperor of Great Sui would make them apprentice to a mere child, were now even more displeased.

But however dissatisfied they were, they dared not show disrespect to the Emperor of Great Sui.

They still had to bow and scrape before Li Xuanba, faces plastered with smiles, begging for his guidance.

The Wa state’s performative humility was always excessive, especially when they had something to gain.

Because Li Xuanba felt repulsed, he desperately wanted to refuse.

But he swallowed his disgust and agreed to Yang Guang’s request.

The Great Sui and the Wa state had already exchanged envoys; interaction between the two countries was inevitable. Even if he refused, the Wa people would simply find another teacher.

Moreover, even if he agreed to teach them, the Wa envoys would still spend money to seek out other Sui people to learn more knowledge; they would not hang their hopes on him alone. He could not stop the Wa state from learning from the outside world, nor could he stop the historical process of the "Taika Reform."

Not to mention that this was the Great Sui and he could not influence Yang Guang’s choices; even in the Great Tang, Li Xuanba could not drag his brother to wipe out the Wa state.

The Wa state only had a few mines of value, and these could be seized without war. Deploying the entire nation's military against them would be of no benefit to the Great Tang.

Even if he conquered the Wa state now, with the current level of technology, it would be impossible to manage an island nation far from the continent, and the Wa state would eventually declare independence again.

If Li Xuanba could trigger a volcanic eruption of Mount Fuji by jumping into its crater himself, he would do it, even if he cherished his life.

But he could not let the fine men of the Great Tang sacrifice their lives in the Wa state just to vent his frustration about the future.

He knew that even if his Second Brother knew about the future, he would not launch a campaign against the Wa state. Because compared to the distant future, the lives of the Great Tang’s people were far more important.

Future problems should be solved by future people. As the Emperor of the Great Tang, his Second Brother would only focus on the present.

Li Xuanba repeatedly told himself to "stay calm," suppressed his emotions, and made a rational decision.

Although he could not stop the historical process, if he participated in it, perhaps he could secure more benefits for the Great Tang.

For example, the island of Kyushu, which was very close to the continent and could be drawn into the Great Tang’s map.

All the noble clans of China were arrogant toward foreigners. It was perfectly normal for Li Xuanba to be arrogant toward the Wa envoys.

Yang Guang was not angry that Li Xuanba gave the Wa envoys the cold shoulder; on the contrary, he appreciated Li Xuanba’s disdain.

Yang Guang was about to send Pei Shiqing as an envoy to the Wa state. Before doing so, he specifically summoned Li Xuanba to use the young boy to humiliate the Wa envoys.

*My Great Sui has a child who is already so formidable; you Wa people better stay down!*

After dismissing the Wa envoys, Yang Guang told Li Xuanba his true intent: to use the excuse of "instruction" to humiliate the Wa envoys thoroughly before "Su Yinggao" left the Great Sui.

Su Yinggao was the name Ono no Imoko used in the Great Sui.

Li Xuanba agreed immediately.

Yang Guang gritted his teeth, "A mere speck of a barbarian nation, yet they dare to call themselves the Son of Heaven. If it weren't for Goguryeo and the Turks at my bedside, I would certainly send troops to wipe the Wa state off the map!"

Yang Guang was historically known for being exceptionally generous to foreigners. For the Wa state to provoke such a Yang Guang, they truly had some "talent."

As Yang Guang said this, another relevant historical record surfaced in Li Xuanba’s mind.

When Ono no Imoko went to the Great Sui, the state letter he handed to Emperor Yang of Sui began with, "The Son of Heaven where the sun rises sends a letter to the Son of Heaven where the sun sets, hoping you are well," which had infuriated Emperor Yang.

Since the Han Dynasty, China had been the leader of East Asia, and all other small nations were expected to pay tribute. In the tribute system, only the Chinese Emperor could call himself the "Son of Heaven."

The Wa state was originally a vassal of the Han Dynasty. Now, the Wa King not only called himself the Son of Heaven but also claimed he was the "Son of Heaven where the sun rises," while Emperor Yang of Sui was the "Son of Heaven where the sun sets." The sinister intent was practically written on his face.

Emperor Yang was so angry at the time that he cursed, "The barbarian letter is disrespectful; do not report it again." But he was a man who valued foreigners greatly; the less they respected him, the more he cared. So, the following year, he still sent an envoy to the Wa state.

When Ono no Imoko visited the Great Sui again in the fifth year of Daye, the Wa state changed the heading of the state letter to "The Eastern Emperor respectfully addresses the Western Emperor," calling himself "Emperor" and avoiding the title of Son of Heaven. Emperor Yang was actually satisfied with this and officially established diplomatic relations with the Wa state.

Recalling this record, Li Xuanba was deeply puzzled.

"The Eastern Emperor respectfully addresses the Western Emperor" was still quite disrespectful to Emperor Yang, wasn't it? For a man as proud as Emperor Yang to swallow this insult and then treat the Wa state with such courtesy, even accepting many Wa students to stay in the Great Sui to learn advanced Chinese culture...

Back then, Emperor Guangwu of Han, Liu Xiu, had bestowed upon the Wa state a gold seal inscribed "Wa Nu Guo" (State of the Wa Slaves), and they were merely one of the Han Dynasty's vassal states. Now the Wa King calls himself "Eastern Emperor" and calls you "Western Emperor," and you are satisfied? You are courteous? Do you have no shame?!

Li Xuanba returned home full of confusion and, for the first time ever, took out a small bow and arrow to vent his frustration on the poor straw man in the training ground.

When Li Yuan returned home and found Li Xuanba practicing archery, he was so frightened that he immediately felt Li Xuanba’s forehead and called for a physician.

Li Xuanba said helplessly, "Father, I am not sick."

Li Yuan asked, "Then who has angered you? You just returned from the palace. Did His Majesty insult our Tang Duke’s mansion again?"

Li Xuanba originally did not want to discuss serious matters with Li Yuan. However, on second thought, as a nobleman of this era, Li Yuan’s perspective might solve his doubts, so he replied, "Today, His Majesty asked me to teach the Wa envoys the poetry and books of the Great Sui. I heard that the Wa state was originally a vassal of the Great Han and was bestowed the name 'Wa Nu Guo.' Now, the Wa King actually calls himself the 'Son of Heaven of the Sun Rise' to His Majesty and disparagingly calls His Majesty the 'Son of Heaven of the Sun Set,' yet His Majesty is still willing to establish diplomatic relations with them. I truly cannot understand it."

Li Yuan frowned and thought for a long time before remembering what "Wa State" and "Wa Nu Guo" were.

He said, "The Wa state is separated from Goguryeo by water. His Majesty has the intention to attack Goguryeo; perhaps he wants to unite with the Wa state to attack them together. As for the Wa state’s disrespect, we can deal with them after Goguryeo is settled."

The "Goryeo" mentioned in the Sui and Tang periods referred to Goguryeo.

"Goryeo" was originally an abbreviation for "Goguryeo," but the official name was "Goguryeo." However, when the Chinese dynasties interacted with Goguryeo, they always preferred to write the abbreviation "Goryeo" in official documents.

Goguryeo: Our full name is Goguryeo.
Rulers of the Northern and Southern Dynasties: Understood, Goryeo.
Goguryeo: Please respect our country's name; our official name is Goguryeo!
Emperor Wen of Sui: Goryeo.
Emperor Yang of Sui: Goryeo.
Emperor Taizong of Tang: Goryeo.
Emperor Gaozong of Tang: Goryeo.

Thus, during the Northern and Southern Dynasties, "Goguryeo" and "Goryeo" were used interchangeably; during the Sui and Tang, all historical records referred to Goguryeo as "Goryeo." The people of Goguryeo also began calling themselves "Goryeo" and changed their country's name to the "Goryeo State."

Now, there was no Goguryeo state, only the Goryeo state.

When the Wang Dynasty of Korea was established, for reasons known to everyone, they set the country's name as "Goryeo." The Wang Goryeo had nothing to do with the Goryeo of the Sui and Tang, so later historical research referred to the Sui and Tang Goryeo as "Goguryeo" to distinguish it from the Wang Goryeo.

The long-extinct Goguryeo felt aggrieved. They were the real Goryeo; the predecessors were forced to yield their name to the successors.

Goguryeo was a small frontier state established by the Buyeo people under Jumong when the Western Han was weakening. During the chaos of the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties, they seized much of the Central Plains' territory and were a separatist force on Chinese soil.

After China was unified, it was certain that the lost lands would be reclaimed and the separatist forces destroyed, so war between the Great Sui and Goguryeo was inevitable.

Emperor Wen of Sui had already mobilized troops against Goguryeo, only to withdraw due to the weather. After Yang Guang ascended the throne, the court knew that the Great Sui would complete the unfinished work of Emperor Wen and destroy the Goguryeo separatist force.

If it weren't for Yang Guang’s obsession with building the eastern capital, the Grand Canal, the Great Wall, and numerous palaces, the Great Sui would have gone to war with Goguryeo long ago.

Li Yuan was well aware of the Emperor’s sharpening blade toward Goguryeo, so he easily guessed the Emperor’s intentions.

Li Yuan said to Li Xuanba, "The Wa state is rude, but they are just a speck of a barbarian nation; His Majesty cannot be bothered to argue with them. After dealing with Goguryeo, if they remain rude, it won't be too late to deal with them then."

Looking at Li Yuan’s indifferent expression, Li Xuanba understood why Yang Guang could swallow this insult.

Because the Great Sui looked down on the Wa state, believing it was normal for barbarian nations to be ignorant of etiquette, and arguing with them would only lower one's own status.

It wasn't just Yang Guang; everyone in the Chinese dynasties believed that rather than arguing with barbarians about etiquette they could never understand, it was better to focus on practical interests.

The current interest the Wa state held for the Great Sui was their potential to help attack Goguryeo.

Li Xuanba said to Li Yuan, "The Wa state will not send troops."

Li Yuan said, "It doesn't matter if they don't send troops, as long as they don't cause trouble. What His Majesty is doing is 'befriending the distant to attack the near'."

He sneered, "Although His Majesty is overly harsh and ungrateful to his subjects, he still has the basic common sense of a ruler."

Li Xuanba was silent. Before Goguryeo was destroyed, Yang Guang would continue to tolerate the Wa state.

But by the time Goguryeo was destroyed, the Great Sui would have been gone for many years, *tsk*.

It seemed there wasn't much he could do about the Wa state before the fall of the Great Sui. Emperor Yang of Sui was truly useless.

Li Xuanba asked, "But with His Majesty’s temper, he shouldn't just swallow this insult directly. Father, will the state letter His Majesty gives to the Wa King rebuke him?"

Li Yuan said, "Of course. With His Majesty’s personality, he will definitely mock the Wa King mercilessly in the state letter. If the Wa King is still willing to send envoys after seeing the letter, it means he knows he was rude and is coming to apologize. Only then would His Majesty consider establishing diplomatic relations. The letter His Majesty gives to the Wa King is the Great Sui’s test."

A faint smile appeared on Li Xuanba’s face, "Father, do you think the Wa envoys might 'lose' the state letter?"

Li Yuan said, "Didn't His Majesty send an envoy? The state letter should be in the hands of the Great Sui envoy; how could it be lost?"

Li Xuanba smiled, "What if?"

Li Yuan thought for a moment and said, "If such a thing really happened, it could only be because the Wa envoys bribed the Great Sui envoy. Why would you think that? The Great Sui envoy will surely prioritize the interests of the Great Sui."

Li Xuanba said, "I am merely judging the Wa state with the utmost malice. I have heard that the Wa state has 'small courtesies but no great righteousness' and has been doing self-deceiving things since the Han Dynasty. They might deliberately 'lose' the letter of rebuke from the Great Sui, then establish diplomatic relations, and shamelessly claim that the Son of Heaven of the Great Sui acknowledges the Wa King as a Son of Heaven too."

Li Yuan laughed, "Da'de, you seem to really dislike the Wa state?"

Li Xuanba said, "The Wa Nu Guo actually calls itself the Son of Heaven of the Sun Rise and disparagingly calls His Majesty the Son of Heaven of the Sun Set; how can I not dislike them? They are not just belittling His Majesty, but belittling our entire Central Plains of China."

Hearing Li Xuanba put it this way, although Li Yuan felt it was normal for a small barbarian nation to be ignorant of etiquette, he also felt deeply repulsed.

He comforted Li Xuanba, "Barbarians are mostly ignorant of etiquette; if you get angry, you will never finish. However, your concerns are reasonable. Who is the envoy sent to the Wa state this time? I will go and speak with him, telling him he must ensure the letter is delivered."

Li Xuanba said, "Pei Shiqing."

Li Yuan was silent.

After a long while, he rubbed his forehead and said, "Pei Shiqing is an extremely greedy man. Hearing you say this, I am also worried that he might really take a bribe from the Wa envoys and 'accidentally' lose the state letter."

Li Xuanba thought to himself, *as expected.*

In history, Ono no Imoko did "lose" the state letter from Emperor Yang of Sui to the Wa King.

Historians speculated that Emperor Yang was not a man of good temper, and the letter he gave to the Wa King must have been harsh. It was possible that Ono no Imoko feared the Wa King would vent his anger on him and discarded the letter himself; or it was possible that Ono no Imoko showed the letter to the Wa King privately, and the Wa King told him to use the excuse of it being lost, which was why Ono no Imoko was not punished for such a major incident as losing the state letter.

But the state letter should have been delivered by the Great Sui envoy to the Wa King; how could it be lost by Ono no Imoko?

Moreover, given Emperor Yang’s subsequent attitude toward the Wa state, he seemed to think the Wa state had submitted to him. Otherwise, even if he needed to "befriend the distant to attack the near," with Emperor Yang’s foul temper, treating the Wa state that had angered him with such courtesy was truly abnormal.

It was very likely that Emperor Yang did not know the letter was lost and thought the Wa state had yielded.

Therefore, in the "lost state letter" incident, the Great Sui envoy Pei Shiqing was definitely to blame.

What if Emperor Yang’s state letter was read aloud in public by the Great Sui envoy this time? How would the Wa King react? Would he still shamelessly pretend he heard nothing and continue to establish diplomatic relations with the Great Sui?

Li Xuanba really wanted to know.

Li Xuanba said, "Father, although it is only a tiny possibility, the Wa state insulted our Great Sui’s Son of Heaven first; this insult must be repaid! Is there any way for you to help His Majesty replace him with a more upright envoy?"

It was the first time Li Yuan had seen his third son ask him for something.

He immediately patted Li Xuanba’s head and guaranteed with great confidence, "Leave this little matter to Father!"

Li Xuanba tried his best to squeeze out a look of admiration, "Father is truly amazing!"

Flattered by Li Xuanba, Li Yuan submitted a request to see the Emperor early the next morning.

"Your Majesty! I heard that the Wa state, a barbarian nation, has been disrespectful to the Son of Heaven of the Great Sui! If Your Majesty can endure this, I cannot! I request to be the envoy to the Wa state!"

Yang Guang: "..."

He was speechless. Even though he was wary of Li Yuan, Li Yuan was the dignified Duke of Tang of the Great Sui and his own cousin. Could he insult him by sending him to the Wa state? Did the Wa state deserve it?

Under Li Yuan’s persistent pestering, to avoid sending the Duke of Tang to the Wa state, Yang Guang replaced him with a team of the most sharp-tongued envoys, ordering them to make sure they gave the Wa King a thorough tongue-lashing.

Pei Shiqing regretfully lost this lucrative assignment and grew resentful toward Li Yuan.

In the Tang Duke’s mansion.

Li Yuan said proudly, "Da'de, isn't Father amazing!"

Li Xuanba praised, "Father is truly amazing!"

This time, Li Xuanba’s praise was sincere.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第58章 一家人齐聚洛阳 – 第59章 又一不省心老师
chunks.chineseText:
第58章 一家人齐聚洛阳

=
　　杨广派往倭国的使团出发时， 一件事传遍洛阳城。
　　“听说了吗？倭奴国王居然自称天子！”
　　“你这消息已经落后了。听说倭奴国王自称天皇，比天子还高一层。他怕惹怒陛下，才在国书中自称天子。”
　　“我还以为倭奴国王自称日出天子， 说陛下是日落天子， 已经是诅咒大隋日落西山， 十分恶毒。没想到倭奴国王居然还自称天皇。天子是上天的儿子，天皇岂不是……”
　　“慎言慎言！”……
　　李世民狩猎归来，洛阳城最新的热门消息他听不懂了。
　　李世民挠了挠头。他只离开了洛阳城五日而已啊！
　　“阿玄， 那个倭奴是怎么回事？什么天皇天子？”李世民知道弟弟消息一向很灵通，抓不住热点就立刻问弟弟。
　　李玄霸将倭国的事告诉了李世民。
　　李世民沉默了一会儿，小声道：“喂喂阿玄， 倭国的消息不会是你传出去的吧？”
　　李玄霸正色：“怎么可能是我？”
　　李世民道：“好了，我知道了。”
　　李玄霸疑惑， 二哥怎么会猜这么准？
　　李世民见弟弟疑惑， 得意地笑了笑。
　　他其实不是猜得准，只是试探一下。见到弟弟的神情，他就知道自己猜对了。
　　长孙无忌老诽谤阿玄心思太深，让人难以揣摩。但李世民总觉得自家弟弟特别好懂，心思根本不需要猜。
　　“你以前就很讨厌倭国， 现在陛下居然让你与倭国使臣接洽，你肯定很不开心。”李世民道， “我又听闻陛下临时换了使臣团，原因是父亲居然想亲自出使。父亲没理由做这种事，只可能是因为你。”
　　李玄霸撇了一下嘴， 道：“我可没有把倭国的事传出去， 和我无关。只是官宦贵族好奇父亲为何生气， 父亲稍稍解释了一二。”
　　李世民问道：“陛下不生气？”
　　李玄霸道：“父亲因为倭国侮辱陛下， 都不顾自己唐国公的身份，要亲自去倭国出使了，陛下很欣慰父亲的忠诚。父亲又升官了。”
　　李世民叹气：“陛下的心思转变得真快。他才刚敲打了我们家呢，现在又褒奖父亲。揣摩人的心思好累，我做不来。”
　　李玄霸道：“做不来就不做，你傻乎乎的也挺好的。”
　　李世民直接上手揍弟弟：“啊？傻乎乎？你说谁傻乎乎？阿玄，你胆子肥了啊！别跑！”
　　身体好一些了的李玄霸这次本来能成功逃脱，逃出门时撞到了李智云。
　　李智云习惯性地抱住李玄霸的腰。李世民大笑着把李玄霸逮住，把弟弟的脑袋当木鱼敲。
　　李智云心虚想跑，被李玄霸拽住，把脑袋当木鱼敲。
　　一个兄长敲一个弟弟的脑袋，场面非常和谐。
　　“嗯？小五怎么会在这？”
　　等李世民和李玄霸敲完弟弟的脑袋后，才意识到这个问题。
　　李智云抱着脑袋道：“我和娘亲、阿姨一起来的。一家人都来了，我先跑来告诉你们。”
　　李世民拽着李玄霸就跑，埋怨道：“娘亲来了？不早说！”
　　李玄霸拽着李智云跑：“一家人都来了？兄长和四弟也来了？”
　　李智云跟着两个兄长，噘嘴往前跑：“哼，我想说啊，你们不让我说话。都来了，阿姊们也都来了。”
　　李世民和李玄霸到前院的时候，窦夫人和万氏正在指挥下人搬东西。
　　“娘娘！”李世民松开李玄霸的手，朝着窦夫人扑了上去。
　　窦夫人转身接住李世民，一巴掌拍在李世民的背上。
　　李世民：“哎哟！”
　　窦夫人捏住李世民的腮帮子一扯：“猎老虎？二郎你出息了啊！”
　　李世民含糊不清地小声道：“我是很出息。”
　　窦夫人被李世民气笑了。她使劲扯了一下李世民的脸颊，道：“等会儿收拾你。”
　　“哼哼。”李世民揉着脸道，“这么久没见，娘娘见面就训我，我讨厌娘娘。”
　　窦夫人狠狠戳了一下李世民的额头：“行，娘娘也讨厌二郎！”
　　李世民又扑到了窦夫人怀里：“那不行，娘娘不准讨厌我。”
　　李玄霸喘了几口气，缓步走到窦夫人面前：“母亲安好。”
　　窦夫人笑道：“三郎照顾二郎辛苦了。”
　　李玄霸道：“是很辛苦。”
　　李世民从窦夫人怀里抬起头，要去扯李玄霸刚扎好的小揪揪。
　　窦夫人挡住李世民的手，又捏了李世民的腮帮子一下：“别欺负弟弟，一边去，别碍事。”
　　李世民不满道：“娘娘果然讨厌我了。”
　　窦夫人失笑：“对，就讨厌你。你要是以后还自找危险，我还继续讨厌你。”
　　李世民闭上嘴。
　　他有些担心，等会儿自己不会真的挨揍吧？
　　李世民和李玄霸和母亲问好之后，又向万氏等人问好。
　　李智云牵着万氏的手，十分大声地告状：“二兄和三兄一见到我就敲我的头！”
　　万氏笑得前俯后仰：“好！”
　　李智云不敢置信地瞪大眼睛：“什么好？阿姨！我被欺负了！”
　　万氏笑得更厉害，把窦夫人都惹笑了。
　　窦夫人把李智云抱到怀里揉了揉，笑道：“等会儿娘帮你收拾他们。”
　　万氏笑道：“收拾什么？兄弟闹着玩，这是感情好呢。”
　　李智云生气道：“不和他们感情好！”
　　李世民背着手，迈着八字步走来：“哦？不和兄长好是吧？唉，二兄本来想带你去禁苑玩，看来小五是不想去了。”
　　李智云立刻认怂：“小五和二兄、三兄感情好。”
　　窦夫人忍俊不禁，又狠狠戳了李世民的额头。
　　李世民捂着被母亲戳红的额头，十分得意地笑。
　　“照顾”弟弟，他特别擅长！
　　李玄霸张望了一番，道：“兄长和四弟呢？阿姊也不在。”
　　窦夫人道：“你侄女年幼，他们辗转走水路，来的慢些。我们坐马车，到的快些。不过他们明日也该到了，先把院子收拾好。”
　　李玄霸疑惑：“四弟怎么也跟着兄长？”
　　窦夫人叹气：“他闹着坐船，管不住。”
　　万氏也叹气：“让四郎坐马车，他就躺在马车前不肯走，真是……唉，我这嘴，不该说这个。”
　　窦夫人道：“没什么不能说的。是我无能，管不住。”
　　万氏忙道：“夫人别这么说，夫人已经教得够好了。”
　　李世民道：“娘亲是揍少了。你看我小时候挨了那么多揍，现在就很听话。娘亲放心，等小四来了洛阳，我盯着他！”
　　窦夫人本来提起李元吉有些自暴自弃地颓然，李世民这一插嘴，她忍不住笑了：“那好，娘看你怎么盯。”
　　李世民对李玄霸道：“阿玄，你可要离远一点。他小的时候就喜欢欺负你，现在力气大了，你更打不过。”
　　李玄霸：“不至于……”
　　他想起李元吉的个头，讪讪道：“好，我绕着他走。”
　　李智云抱住李玄霸的腰，道：“我帮二兄！哼，我打得过！”
　　看着李智云忿忿的表情，李玄霸摸了摸五弟的头。
　　以前五弟和李元吉虽然关系不是太亲近，但偶尔也会在一起玩。现在五弟怎么好像有些讨厌李元吉了？
　　李玄霸将这件事记在心中，准备之后打探一番。
　　妻妾都来到了洛阳，家中热闹起来，李渊很高兴。
　　李建成等人第二日下午准时到了洛阳城，李渊请了一日假，专门在城门迎接长子。
　　窦夫人问道：“四郎可听话？”
　　李建成笑道：“四弟一直很听话，母亲放心。”
　　李元吉嚷嚷：“没错！我一直很听话！”
　　窦夫人笑着摸了摸李元吉的头：“那就好。”
　　但她仍旧不放心，去询问了女儿们。
　　四娘子、五娘子都说李元吉还好，只年幼的六娘子悄悄和窦夫人说，李元吉一路上都吵着要买这买那，兄长都满足了，李元吉很开心，所以还算听话。
　　窦夫人松了口气。
　　虽然大郎太过纵容四郎，但至少兄弟感情是好的。
　　窦夫人最担心的就是李建成与弟弟们关系不好。
　　李建成来到洛阳后，李世民和李玄霸让出了最大的院子，搬到了较为僻静的地方居住。
　　他们的新院子比以前小了一倍，没有挨着校场和花园，不过有个侧门，出入都很方便。两人并无不满。
　　李建成得了职官原本很高兴，得知这职官的波折后，就有些迁怒李玄霸。
　　不过他迁怒李玄霸的事情多着了，独孤老夫人的账他都没有和李玄霸算，所以多记了一笔账，李建成和李玄霸的相处模式没有什么区别。
　　他们在李渊和窦夫人面前的时候都会装出兄友弟恭的模样，私下见面李玄霸会恭敬地打招呼，李建成都当没听见。
　　李世民十分生气，让李玄霸也别再和李建成打招呼。
　　李玄霸摇头，说当弟弟的还是要好好尊敬兄长。
　　李世民和朋友们吐槽这件事，长吁短叹阿玄的性子太软，总被人欺负。
　　杜如晦和薛收附和李世民，长孙无忌嘟囔“李三就只对兄弟性格好”，只有房乔嗅出了些什么。
　　房乔悄悄叮嘱杜如晦和薛收别与李建成结识。
　　杜如晦笑道：“我就算想结识李建成，他都不屑见我。我这个京兆杜氏的旁支子弟，可入不了他的眼。”
　　薛收道：“我可能能入他的眼，但你们都入不了他的眼，我也还是不入他的眼为好。”
　　房乔见两位好友都不喜李建成，松了口气。
　　至于长孙无忌，他就不用叮嘱了。
　　长孙无忌身为李二郎的妻兄若还能被李建成笼络了去，那李二郎就不会是他的未来的主君了。
　　房乔猜出了一些事，心情有些低落，还无法和友人倾述。
　　他总算知道为何李玄霸对他交浅言深，透露谶纬。
　　这实在是心里有事，不说出来就憋着慌。
　　李玄霸听了房乔的话，点头：“你说得对。我正好有件事憋在心里，房兄……”
　　“告辞！”房乔转身就走，走路速度得比跑还快。


第59章 又一不省心老师

=
　　无论李建成喜不喜欢这个职官， 杨广让他上班，他就得每日当值上班。
　　幸亏李渊刚升了官，所以朝堂中没人再拿“协律郎”的典故说事， 都默认皇帝没什么坏心思， 是其他人想多。
　　李建成遭遇的是其他风言风语。
　　以前李建成躺着升官， 认为是自己应得的事。他又只是散官，不需要当值，接触其他同僚， 所以不用处理职场关系。
　　现在他需要当值了，职场关系复杂，虽然他是唐国公府的嫡长子， 也不是人人都捧着他，难免听到酸言酸语。
　　别人的门荫是父亲立功儿子当官， 李建成的门荫还加上了年幼的弟弟得宠他躺着升官， 真令人羡慕。
　　若李玄霸年纪大一些，这不过是朝堂常态。
　　朝堂中谁身居高位后连带着兄弟族人一起发达很正常。
　　问题就是李玄霸和李世民这两兄弟都还是黄毛小儿。两个九岁的孩子，一个当上了最年轻的秀才，一个有了猎虎的威名，偏偏比弟弟大了近十岁的李建成没什么名声。
　　唐国公府蒸蒸日上， 引了许多人眼红。现在他们总算找到能嘲笑唐国公府的地方，可不可劲儿阴阳怪气？
　　李建成今年刚弱冠（虚岁）， 年轻气盛，又从小被捧到大，哪受过这种委屈？
　　没过多久， 李建成就辞官不干了。
　　杨广改制后， 官员本阶是以散官品阶为主。勋贵子弟不耐烦做低级职官， 辞官者很常见。
　　辞官之后， 李建成感觉天也蓝了，地也绿了，每日呼朋唤友喝酒狩猎，十分快乐。
　　李渊很支持李建成辞官。
　　这官职本来就是皇帝用来侮辱他们的，若不是怕惹怒皇帝，他早就帮李建成拒了。
　　现在李建成来到洛阳当值了一段时间后才辞官，给足了皇帝的面子，想来皇帝也不会再说什么。
　　杨广确实没在意李建成辞官的事。
　　因李渊为了他的脸面都愿意自落身份出使倭国了，杨广在宇文述等近臣的劝说下，认为李渊对他没有不臣之心，只是一些不服他的勋贵故意挑拨他和李渊的关系。
　　杨广是个喜恶变化很快的人，虽特别记仇，但现在他只是没有任何理由地猜忌李渊，李渊还没有做过得罪他的事，所以杨广就把之前的侮辱敲打当做自己对李渊的考验。现在算李渊通过了考验，不再折腾唐国公府了。
　　李建成不想在朝中入职。杨广本就看不上李建成，便没有再提这件事。
　　李建成辞官的时候，李玄霸正好呈上了新写的词，尤其是那首只有上阕的《满庭芳》，让杨广龙颜大悦。
　　李玄霸呈上的《满庭芳》为宋时秦观所作，上阕为：“山抹微云，天连衰草，画角声断谯门。暂停征棹，聊共引离尊。多少蓬莱旧事，空回首、烟霭纷纷。斜阳外，寒鸦万点，流水绕孤村。”
　　其中“斜阳外，寒鸦万点，流水绕孤村”为流传后世的名句。
　　其实这首词化用的杨广之诗《野望》：“寒鸦飞数点，流水绕孤村。斜阳欲落处，一望黯销魂。”
　　古代写文作诗讲究“用典”，有时候“用典”是“整篇用典”，也不会标注。“查重”是后世人的道德观念。
　　所以李玄霸虽然自诩“文抄公”，李世民总不以为然。因为李玄霸抄的诗词只要更改一两字，在当世文坛中就算是“原创”。就算这些诗不是后世的而是前人的，也没人说李玄霸不是。
　　比如宋朝时，宋诗的开创和集大成者是“苏黄”——苏轼、黄庭坚。当时遵循黄庭坚创作理论的文人自称“江西诗派”，是宋诗第一大诗派，其作诗核心思想就是“夺胎换骨”“点铁成金”“无一字无来处”。
　　比如白居易《劝酒寄元九》中云“百年夜分半，一岁春无多”，黄庭坚增四字“百年中去夜分半，一岁无多春再来”就是新诗；王安石《促织》云“只向贫家促机杼，几家能有一絇丝”，黄庭坚改五字“莫作秋虫促机杼，贫家能有几絇丝”就是新诗。时人无不称赞效仿。
　　现在虽无江西诗派，但对“用典”的态度是一致的。
　　李玄霸拆了杨广的诗填词，杨广不仅不会生气，还会十分自得。
　　杨广笑话李玄霸：“大德，怎么只有上阕？难道是朕这首诗只有四句，不够你拆？”
　　李玄霸理直气壮道：“是的陛下，臣就是不够拆！”
　　下半阕用典是“青楼薄幸名”，他这个小身板，写什么青楼啊。
　　杨广挽起袖子：“朕来补！”
　　李玄霸为杨广磨墨，杨广文兴大发，不仅补全了这首词，还即兴又作了一首，笔墨未干，便唤来乐人谱曲演唱。
　　洛阳宫中乐声阵阵，文人的雅词和清商的雅音相得益彰。
　　杨广唤来陪坐的大臣皆捻须微笑，对李玄霸这“胡闹”有了不同的认识。
　　薛道衡身为当世第一才子，自然也被杨广唤来陪坐。
　　他文人尖酸刻薄的气息十足，嘴里难得出句好话，这次居然也夸赞道：“臣本以为乐声靡靡，登不上大雅之堂。文人作词之后，原本轻浮的丝竹竟也登得上大雅之堂了。”
　　杨广虽然一直记恨薛道衡以前不肯为他所用，今日他高兴，便没有在意薛道衡夸奖的话中暗含的讽刺：“薛卿若能作一二好词，朕当日日聆听。”
　　薛道衡拱手道：“既然陛下都如此说了，臣回去就琢磨，定让陛下听到厌。”
　　裴蕴笑道：“薛公所言‘听到厌’，可是子曰‘三月不知肉味’的厌？”
　　裴蕴以太常寺少卿起家，为讨好杨广，广召天下乐家子弟三万余人，得到了杨广的喜爱，现在已经是民部侍郎。
　　虽已经不在太常寺为官，但裴蕴见李玄霸为民间声乐推广“雅词”也很喜欢。
　　杨广所喜爱的声乐越是“高雅”，就显得裴蕴当初为杨广搜集乐工之事不算太“佞臣所为”。
　　薛道衡不喜裴蕴。不过他虽然尖酸刻薄，官场的情商也没烂到当着皇帝的面，甩皇帝宠臣的脸色的程度。
　　薛道衡笑道：“若真能写出如此好词，别人吃不吃肉我不知道，我可以三月不吃肉。”
　　杨广见薛道衡和裴蕴居然能和乐融融地聊天，居然有一种欣慰唏嘘之感，让他对薛道衡的杀心都淡了一些。
　　他对苏夔道：“如果薛卿作词，伯尼当作曲。”
　　苏夔拱手道：“当仁不让！”
　　苏夔好奇地看向侍坐在杨广身侧的李玄霸。
　　苏夔是尚书左仆射苏威之子。尚书左仆射即隋朝的宰相。
　　苏威在隋文帝时期，曾与高颎一同参决朝政，后因结党营私被免官。杨广继位之后，将其重新起复。
　　苏威和高颎在官场的经历十分巧合。
　　高颎从尚书左仆射下来时，苏威便成为尚书左仆射，高颎成为太常寺卿；高颎自请左迁编书，从太常寺卿退下时，苏威便迁太常寺卿，但仍旧参豫朝政，领丞相事。
　　高颎本应该在去年被杨广冤杀，苏威也同因劝阻杨广修长城被免官。不过苏夔是太子挚友，又是大隋最懂乐理之人，所以不仅没被牵连，还被升为从五品司朝谒者，随侍杨广左右。
　　苏威很有才华，但性怯懦，又颇重权势，所以他虽颇受杨广视为长者颇为敬重，但在同辈中名声不怎么好。
　　苏夔则相反，虽性格狂傲，但风评颇好。杨素和苏威为友，都曾多次向苏威戏言，“杨素无儿，苏夔无父”。
　　在这个时空中，因高颎和宇文弼先退一步，没有跟随杨广出巡，便没有成为劝阻杨广修长城的领头人。苏威虽然心中知道应该劝阻，但怯懦的他不敢当这个带头的人，如今没有被免官，仍旧任太常寺卿。
　　苏威常和苏夔叹息，唐国公家的二郎三郎皆为麒麟子，可惜家中没有适龄的女子，被长孙晟和宇文弼捡了便宜。
　　太子杨昭也对苏夔夸赞李玄霸和李世民，但又说李玄霸心思深沉，李世民心胸坦荡，李玄霸可能更受父皇喜爱，他更喜爱李世民。
　　苏夔更相信挚友杨昭的话，所以对李玄霸有偏见。
　　但见李玄霸这个孩童居然真的能坐稳皇帝“宠爱的后辈”的位置，如皇子一般陪伴皇帝左右，苏夔有些想结交这个擅写歌词的李秀才了。
　　苏夔在悄悄观察李玄霸的时候，李玄霸也在观察苏夔。
　　苏威在历史中因在秦王李世民面前倚老卖老，被李世民讥讽“公隋朝宰辅，政乱不能匡救，遂令品物涂炭，君弑国亡。见李密、王充，皆拜伏舞蹈。今既老病，无劳相见也”，终求官不得。
　　但他的两个孙子都是李世民的人。
　　长孙苏勖支持李泰夺嫡，次孙苏亶之女嫁李承乾为太子妃。李承乾和李泰皆因夺嫡抑郁而终，但苏氏子弟因才华横溢继续受唐太宗重用，地位丝毫未损。后人苏勗还是开元时贤相，谥号“文宪”。
　　苏威的家教可是不一般。
　　有才华的人终究会展露光芒。现在苏威一家肯定看不上自己和二哥，李玄霸没打算与他们接触。
　　他只是看到了苏夔的时候，想起了历史中秦王讥讽苏威的事。
　　苏勖为秦王府十八学士之一，很早就跟随秦王李世民。李世民一边重用苏勖，一边当着苏勖的面讥讽他祖父，真是太坏了。
　　二哥，不愧是你。
　　李玄霸决定回去就和二哥剧透他讥讽苏威的事，给二哥加上沉重的心理负担。
　　“大德，薛卿赏识你的才华？你再拜一师如何？”
　　走神的李玄霸：“啊？好……等等？发生了什么？”
　　杨广握拳砸了一下表侄的脑袋，哭笑不得：“你伴驾都能走神？！众卿看看，朕这个表侄真是丝毫没有把朕当皇帝看待啊！”
　　李玄霸捂头，一头的雾水。
　　薛道衡失笑：“够狂妄！陛下，这个弟子臣收了！臣就喜欢狂妄的人！”
　　杨广哈哈大笑：“朕就知道，大德绝对合乎薛卿的喜好！大德，还不快拜师！”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　他虽然很茫然，但皇帝让他拜师，他只能拜师。
　　我拜了谁为师？高老师和宇文老师会不会生气？
　　哦，薛道衡啊，高老师和宇文老师应该会认可自己这个老师。
　　不，等等，怎么是薛道衡？！
　　李玄霸一个头两个大。
　　他还在愁高老师和宇文老师能不能逃过死劫，怎么又来了一个热爱撞杨广刀口上的薛道衡薛老师？
　　隋炀帝给自己安排的老师怎么老是这种他想要杀的人啊！
　　李玄霸觉得自己这拜师的运气过分诡异了。

Chapter 58: The Whole Family Gathers in Luoyang

When the mission sent by Emperor Yang Guang to the Wa Kingdom set sail, a piece of news swept through Luoyang.

"Have you heard? The King of Wa actually calls himself the Son of Heaven!"

"Your information is outdated. I heard the King of Wa calls himself the 'Tenno' (Heavenly Emperor), a rank even higher than the Son of Heaven. He only used 'Son of Heaven' in the official state letter because he was afraid of angering His Majesty."

"I thought that when the King of Wa called himself the 'Son of Heaven of the Land of the Rising Sun' and referred to His Majesty as the 'Son of Heaven of the Land of the Setting Sun,' it was already a malicious curse upon the Great Sui, implying our empire was fading like the setting sun. I never expected the King of Wa to go as far as calling himself 'Tenno.' If the Son of Heaven is the son of the Heavens, then what does that make the 'Tenno'..."

"Careful with your words! Careful!"...

Li Shimin returned from his hunt only to find he could no longer understand the latest trending topics in Luoyang.

Li Shimin scratched his head. He had only been away from Luoyang for five days!

"A-Xuan, what is this business with the Wa Kingdom? What is this about 'Tenno' and 'Son of Heaven'?" Li Shimin knew his younger brother was always well-informed; whenever he missed a hot topic, he would immediately ask him.

Li Xuanba explained the situation regarding the Wa Kingdom to Li Shimin.

Li Shimin fell silent for a moment, then whispered, "Hey, A-Xuan, you didn't leak the news about the Wa Kingdom, did you?"

Li Xuanba looked solemn. "How could it be me?"

Li Shimin said, "Alright, I understand."

Li Xuanba was puzzled. How did his Second Brother guess so accurately?

Seeing his brother’s confusion, Li Shimin smiled triumphantly.

He hadn't actually guessed accurately; he was just testing him. Seeing his brother's expression, he knew he had guessed right.

Zhangsun Wuji often slandered A-Xuan for having a mind too deep and unfathomable. But Li Shimin always felt his younger brother was particularly easy to understand; there was no need to guess his thoughts at all.

"You always hated the Wa Kingdom. Now that His Majesty has actually asked you to liaise with the Wa envoys, you must be very unhappy," Li Shimin said. "I also heard that His Majesty changed the envoy delegation at the last minute because Father wanted to go personally. Father has no reason to do such a thing; it could only be because of you."

Li Xuanba curled his lip and said, "I didn't leak the news about the Wa Kingdom; it has nothing to do with me. It’s just that the officials and nobles were curious why Father was angry, and Father explained a little bit."

Li Shimin asked, "His Majesty isn't angry?"

Li Xuanba replied, "Because the Wa Kingdom insulted His Majesty, Father disregarded his own status as the Duke of Tang and insisted on going to the Wa Kingdom as an envoy. His Majesty was very gratified by Father's loyalty. Father has been promoted again."

Li Shimin sighed, "His Majesty’s mind changes so quickly. He just reprimanded our family, and now he is praising Father. Trying to fathom a person's heart is so exhausting; I can't do it."

Li Xuanba said, "If you can't do it, then don't. Being a bit silly is quite good for you."

Li Shimin immediately reached out to beat his brother. "Huh? Silly? Who are you calling silly? A-Xuan, you've grown bold! Don't run!"

Li Xuanba, whose health had improved, would have normally succeeded in escaping, but as he fled out the door, he bumped into Li Zhiyun.

Li Zhiyun habitually hugged Li Xuanba’s waist. Li Shimin laughed and caught Li Xuanba, using his brother's head like a wooden fish to tap on.

Li Zhiyun, feeling guilty, tried to run but was grabbed by Li Xuanba, who then used his head as a wooden fish to tap on.

One older brother tapping the head of one younger brother—the scene was very harmonious.

"Hmm? Why is Little Five here?"

Only after Li Shimin and Li Xuanba finished tapping their brother's head did they realize this question.

Li Zhiyun held his head and said, "I came with Mother and Auntie. The whole family is here, and I ran ahead to tell you."

Li Shimin grabbed Li Xuanba and ran, complaining, "Mother is here? Why didn't you say so earlier!"

Li Xuanba dragged Li Zhiyun along, running. "The whole family is here? Are Big Brother and Fourth Brother here too?"

Li Zhiyun followed his two older brothers, pouting as he ran. "Hmph, I wanted to say it, but you wouldn't let me speak. Everyone is here, and the sisters are here too."

When Li Shimin and Li Xuanba reached the front courtyard, Lady Dou and Lady Wan were directing the servants to move things.

"Mother!" Li Shimin let go of Li Xuanba’s hand and lunged toward Lady Dou.

Lady Dou turned to catch Li Shimin and slapped him on the back.

Li Shimin: "Ouch!"

Lady Dou pinched Li Shimin’s cheeks and pulled. "Hunting tigers? Er-lang, you've really grown ambitious!"

Li Shimin mumbled indistinctly, "I am quite ambitious."

Lady Dou was amused by Li Shimin's antics. She gave his cheeks a hard tug and said, "I'll deal with you later."

"Hmph." Li Shimin rubbed his face and said, "We haven't seen each other in so long, and the first thing you do is lecture me. I don't like Mother."

Lady Dou poked Li Shimin’s forehead hard. "Fine, Mother doesn't like Er-lang either!"

Li Shimin lunged into Lady Dou’s arms again. "That won't do, Mother isn't allowed to dislike me."

Li Xuanba caught his breath and walked slowly to Lady Dou. "Mother, I hope you are well."

Lady Dou smiled. "It must have been hard for San-lang to take care of Er-lang."

Li Xuanba replied, "It was indeed quite hard."

Li Shimin lifted his head from Lady Dou’s arms and reached out to pull the small topknot Li Xuanba had just tied.

Lady Dou blocked Li Shimin’s hand and pinched his cheeks again. "Don't bully your brother. Go aside and don't get in the way."

Li Shimin complained, "Mother really does dislike me."

Lady Dou laughed. "Yes, I dislike you. If you go looking for danger again in the future, I will continue to dislike you."

Li Shimin shut his mouth.

He was a bit worried—would he really get a beating later?

After greeting their mother, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba greeted Lady Wan and the others.

Li Zhiyun held Lady Wan’s hand and complained loudly, "Second Brother and Third Brother tapped my head as soon as they saw me!"

Lady Wan laughed until she was leaning back and forth. "Good!"

Li Zhiyun widened his eyes in disbelief. "What's good? Auntie! I was bullied!"

Lady Wan laughed even harder, which made Lady Dou laugh as well.

Lady Dou took Li Zhiyun into her arms and rubbed his head, smiling. "Mother will help you deal with them later."

Lady Wan smiled, "Deal with what? Brothers playing around is a sign of good affection."

Li Zhiyun said angrily, "I don't want to have good affection with them!"

Li Shimin walked over with his hands behind his back, strutting with a wide gait. "Oh? You don't want to be on good terms with your brothers? Sigh, Second Brother was planning to take you to the Forbidden Garden to play, but it seems Little Five doesn't want to go."

Li Zhiyun immediately conceded, "Little Five is on good terms with Second Brother and Third Brother."

Lady Dou couldn't help but laugh and poked Li Shimin’s forehead hard again.

Li Shimin covered his forehead, which had been poked red by his mother, and smiled triumphantly.

"Taking care" of his younger brothers—he was particularly good at it!

Li Xuanba looked around and asked, "Where are Big Brother and Fourth Brother? The sisters aren't here either."

Lady Dou said, "Your nieces are young, so they took the water route and are slower. We took a carriage and arrived faster. But they should arrive tomorrow. Let's get the courtyard ready first."

Li Xuanba was puzzled. "Why is Fourth Brother with Big Brother?"

Lady Dou sighed, "He insisted on taking the boat; I couldn't stop him."

Lady Wan also sighed, "When I asked Si-lang to take the carriage, he lay down in front of it and refused to move. It really is... sigh, my mouth, I shouldn't have said that."

Lady Dou said, "There is nothing that cannot be said. It is my incompetence that I couldn't manage him."

Lady Wan quickly said, "Madam, don't say that. You have already taught them well enough."

Li Shimin said, "Mother just didn't beat him enough. Look at me; I received so many beatings when I was young, and now I am very obedient. Don't worry, Mother, when Little Four comes to Luoyang, I will keep an eye on him!"

Lady Dou had been feeling somewhat despondent about Li Yuanji, but Li Shimin’s interruption made her laugh. "Alright then, Mother will see how you keep an eye on him."

Li Shimin said to Li Xuanba, "A-Xuan, you should stay far away. He liked to bully you when he was young, and now that he has more strength, you'll be even less of a match for him."

Li Xuanba: "It's not that bad..."

He recalled Li Yuanji’s size and said sheepishly, "Fine, I'll walk around him."

Li Zhiyun hugged Li Xuanba’s waist and said, "I'll help Second Brother! Hmph, I can beat him!"

Looking at Li Zhiyun’s indignant expression, Li Xuanba patted his fifth brother’s head.

In the past, although his fifth brother and Li Yuanji weren't very close, they would occasionally play together. Why did his fifth brother seem to dislike Li Yuanji now?

Li Xuanba kept this in mind, planning to investigate later.

With his wives and concubines arriving in Luoyang, the household became lively, and Li Yuan was very happy.

Li Jiancheng and the others arrived in Luoyang on time the next afternoon. Li Yuan took a day off to specifically welcome his eldest son at the city gate.

Lady Dou asked, "Was Si-lang obedient?"

Li Jiancheng smiled, "Fourth Brother was very obedient the whole time, Mother, don't worry."

Li Yuanji shouted, "That's right! I was very obedient!"

Lady Dou smiled and patted Li Yuanji’s head. "That's good."

But she was still uneasy and went to ask her daughters.

The Fourth and Fifth daughters both said Li Yuanji was fine, but the young Sixth daughter quietly told Lady Dou that Li Yuanji had been clamoring to buy this and that along the way, and his older brother had satisfied all his requests, so Li Yuanji was very happy and therefore quite obedient.

Lady Dou breathed a sigh of relief.

Although the eldest son was too indulgent toward the fourth, at least the brothers’ affection was good.

What Lady Dou worried about most was that Li Jiancheng would not have a good relationship with his younger brothers.

After Li Jiancheng arrived in Luoyang, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba gave up the largest courtyard and moved to a quieter place.

Their new courtyard was half the size of the previous one and was not adjacent to the training ground or the garden, but it had a side gate, making it very convenient to come and go. Neither of them had any complaints.

Li Jiancheng was initially very happy to receive an official position, but upon learning of the twists and turns behind it, he became somewhat resentful toward Li Xuanba.

However, he had plenty of reasons to resent Li Xuanba; he hadn't even settled the score regarding the Old Lady Dugu incident, so adding another grudge didn't change the dynamic between Li Jiancheng and Li Xuanba.

When they were in front of Li Yuan and Lady Dou, they would pretend to be a harmonious family, but in private, Li Xuanba would greet him respectfully, and Li Jiancheng would act as if he hadn't heard.

Li Shimin was very angry and told Li Xuanba to stop greeting Li Jiancheng.

Li Xuanba shook his head, saying that as a younger brother, he should still show proper respect to his older brother.

Li Shimin complained about this to his friends, sighing that A-Xuan’s nature was too soft and he was always being bullied.

Du Ruhui and Xue Shou agreed with Li Shimin, while Zhangsun Wuji muttered, "Li San only has a good temper toward his brothers." Only Fang Qiao sensed something.

Fang Qiao quietly warned Du Ruhui and Xue Shou not to get acquainted with Li Jiancheng.

Du Ruhui smiled, "Even if I wanted to get acquainted with Li Jiancheng, he wouldn't deign to see me. A collateral branch member of the Jingzhao Du clan like me cannot catch his eye."

Xue Shou said, "I might catch his eye, but since you all can't, it's better if I don't either."

Seeing that his two good friends didn't like Li Jiancheng, Fang Qiao felt relieved.

As for Zhangsun Wuji, he didn't need to be warned.

If Zhangsun Wuji, as the brother-in-law of Li Er-lang, could be won over by Li Jiancheng, then Li Er-lang would not be his future lord.

Fang Qiao had guessed some things, and his mood was somewhat low, unable to confide in his friends.

He finally understood why Li Xuanba had spoken so deeply to him, revealing prophecies.

It was truly because he had things on his mind, and if he didn't say them, he would feel stifled.

Li Xuanba heard Fang Qiao’s words and nodded, "You are right. I happen to have something on my mind, Brother Fang..."

"Farewell!" Fang Qiao turned and left, walking faster than he could run.

Chapter 59: Another Troublesome Teacher

Regardless of whether Li Jiancheng liked this official position, since Yang Guang had ordered him to work, he had to report for duty every day.

Fortunately, since Li Yuan had just been promoted, no one in the court brought up the allusion of the "Xielü Lang" (Music Coordinator) again. Everyone assumed the Emperor had no malicious intent and that others were just overthinking it.

What Li Jiancheng encountered were other rumors and gossip.

Previously, Li Jiancheng had been promoted while doing nothing, thinking it was what he deserved. Since he was only a titular official and didn't need to report for duty or interact with colleagues, he didn't have to deal with workplace relationships.

Now that he had to report for duty, the workplace relationships were complex. Although he was the eldest son of the Duke of Tang’s mansion, not everyone fawned over him, and it was inevitable that he would hear sour remarks.

Other people’s hereditary privileges were based on fathers earning merit for their sons to become officials, but Li Jiancheng’s privilege was compounded by his young brother being favored, allowing him to rise in rank while doing nothing—it was truly enviable.

If Li Xuanba were older, this would just be the norm in the imperial court.

It was normal for someone in a high position to bring their brothers and clansmen along to prosperity.

The problem was that the two brothers, Li Xuanba and Li Shimin, were still mere children. Two nine-year-old boys—one had become the youngest Xiucai, and the other had the fame of hunting a tiger—yet Li Jiancheng, who was nearly ten years older than his younger brother, had no reputation of his own.

The Duke of Tang’s mansion was flourishing, making many people jealous. Now that they had finally found a place to mock the mansion, how could they not be relentlessly sarcastic?

Li Jiancheng had just reached the age of twenty (nominal age) this year. He was young and vigorous, and having been pampered since childhood, when had he ever suffered such grievances?

Not long after, Li Jiancheng resigned from his post.

After Yang Guang reformed the system, the official rank was primarily based on the titular official grade. It was common for the sons of nobles to be impatient with low-level official duties and resign.

After resigning, Li Jiancheng felt the sky was bluer and the ground was greener. He spent his days calling friends to drink and hunt, feeling very happy.

Li Yuan was very supportive of Li Jiancheng’s resignation.

This official position was originally intended by the Emperor to insult them; if not for the fear of angering the Emperor, he would have helped Li Jiancheng refuse it long ago.

Now that Li Jiancheng had come to Luoyang and served for a period before resigning, he had given the Emperor enough face, and he assumed the Emperor would not say anything more.

Yang Guang indeed didn't care about Li Jiancheng’s resignation.

Because Li Yuan had been willing to lower his status to go as an envoy to the Wa Kingdom for the sake of his reputation, Yang Guang, under the persuasion of close ministers like Yuwen Shu, believed that Li Yuan had no rebellious heart and that it was just some nobles who were jealous of him intentionally trying to sow discord between him and Li Yuan.

Yang Guang was a person whose likes and dislikes changed quickly. Although he was particularly vengeful, he currently had no reason to suspect Li Yuan, and Li Yuan hadn't done anything to offend him. Therefore, Yang Guang regarded the previous insults and reprimands as a test of Li Yuan. Now that Li Yuan had passed the test, he stopped tormenting the Duke of Tang’s mansion.

Li Jiancheng didn't want to work in the court. Yang Guang had never thought much of Li Jiancheng anyway, so he didn't bring it up again.

When Li Jiancheng resigned, Li Xuanba happened to present a newly written lyric, especially the one titled "Man Ting Fang," which only had the first stanza, making Yang Guang very happy.

The "Man Ting Fang" presented by Li Xuanba was written by Qin Guan of the Song Dynasty. The first stanza read: "The mountains are brushed by faint clouds, the sky connects to withered grass, the sound of the painted horn breaks at the gate. Pausing the oars of the journey, we share a parting cup. How many old stories of Penglai, looking back in vain, the mist is thick. Beyond the setting sun, ten thousand cold crows, the flowing water winds around a lonely village."

Among them, "Beyond the setting sun, ten thousand cold crows, the flowing water winds around a lonely village" became a famous line passed down to later generations.

In fact, this lyric borrowed from Yang Guang’s poem "Wild View": "Cold crows fly in a few spots, flowing water winds around a lonely village. Where the setting sun is about to fall, one look is soul-stirring."

In ancient times, writing essays and poems emphasized "using allusions." Sometimes "using allusions" meant "using allusions for the whole piece," and it wouldn't be marked. "Plagiarism checking" was a moral concept of later generations.

Therefore, although Li Xuanba considered himself a "literary plagiarist," Li Shimin always disagreed. Because as long as the poems and lyrics Li Xuanba copied were changed by one or two words, they were considered "original" in the literary circles of the time. Even if these poems weren't from later generations but from predecessors, no one would say Li Xuanba wasn't talented.

For example, in the Song Dynasty, the founders and masters of Song poetry were "Su and Huang"—Su Shi and Huang Tingjian. Literary figures who followed Huang Tingjian’s creative theory called themselves the "Jiangxi Poetry School," the largest poetry school of the Song Dynasty. Their core ideology was "taking the fetus and changing the bones," "turning iron into gold," and "not a single word without a source."

For instance, in Bai Juyi’s "Persuading Wine to Yuan Jiu," it says "A hundred years pass in half a night, one year has little spring left," and Huang Tingjian added four words to make it "A hundred years pass in half a night, one year has little spring left to return," which was considered a new poem. When Wang Anshi wrote "Only toward the poor family to urge the loom, how many families can have a skein of silk," Huang Tingjian changed five words to "Don't make the autumn insects urge the loom, how many skeins of silk can a poor family have," which was also considered a new poem. Contemporaries all praised and imitated them.

Although there was no Jiangxi Poetry School now, the attitude toward "using allusions" was consistent.

Li Xuanba took apart Yang Guang’s poem to write a lyric; Yang Guang would not only not be angry but would be very pleased with himself.

Yang Guang teased Li Xuanba: "Da'de, why is there only the first stanza? Is it because my poem only has four lines, not enough for you to take apart?"

Li Xuanba said righteously: "Yes, Your Majesty, your subject just didn't have enough to take apart!"

The allusion in the second stanza was "the name of the fickle one in the brothel." With his small stature, what kind of brothel could he write about?

Yang Guang rolled up his sleeves: "I will complete it!"

Li Xuanba ground the ink for Yang Guang. Yang Guang was in a great mood; not only did he complete the lyric, but he also improvised another one. Before the ink was dry, he called for musicians to compose music and sing it.

Music played in the Luoyang Palace, and the elegant lyrics of the literati complemented the refined music of the Qing-shang style.

The ministers Yang Guang called to sit with him all stroked their beards and smiled, having a different understanding of Li Xuanba’s "mischief."

Xue Daoheng, as the greatest talent of the time, was naturally called by Yang Guang to accompany him.

He was full of the acerbic and biting nature of a literatus, and it was rare for him to say anything nice. This time, he actually praised: "Your subject originally thought the music was decadent and not fit for the halls of elegance. After the literati wrote lyrics, the originally frivolous silk and bamboo music could actually ascend to the halls of elegance."

Although Yang Guang had always held a grudge against Xue Daoheng for refusing to serve him in the past, he was happy today and didn't care about the sarcasm hidden in Xue Daoheng’s praise: "If Minister Xue can write one or two good lyrics, I will listen to them every day."

Xue Daoheng bowed and said: "Since Your Majesty has said so, your subject will ponder it upon returning, and will surely make Your Majesty listen until you are tired of it."

Pei Yun smiled: "When Master Xue says 'listen until tired,' is it the 'tired' of Confucius saying 'not knowing the taste of meat for three months'?"

Pei Yun started as the Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. To please Yang Guang, he recruited more than 30,000 children of musicians from all over the world, which won Yang Guang’s favor. He was now the Vice Minister of the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

Although he was no longer an official in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Pei Yun was very happy to see Li Xuanba promoting "elegant lyrics" for folk music.

The more "elegant" the music Yang Guang liked, the less it seemed that Pei Yun’s collection of musicians for Yang Guang was the act of a "sycophant."

Xue Daoheng didn't like Pei Yun. However, although he was acerbic, his political EQ wasn't so bad that he would slap the Emperor’s favorite minister in the face in front of the Emperor.

Xue Daoheng smiled: "If I can really write such good lyrics, I don't know if others will stop eating meat, but I can go three months without eating meat."

Seeing that Xue Daoheng and Pei Yun could actually chat harmoniously, Yang Guang felt a sense of gratification and sighing, which made his murderous intent toward Xue Daoheng fade a little.

He said to Su Kui: "If Minister Xue writes the lyrics, Bo'ni should compose the music."

Su Kui bowed: "I will not yield!"

Su Kui looked curiously at Li Xuanba, who was sitting beside Yang Guang.

Su Kui was the son of Su Wei, the Minister of the Secretariat. The Minister of the Secretariat was the Prime Minister of the Sui Dynasty.

During the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui, Su Wei had participated in the decision-making of state affairs with Gao Jiong, but was later dismissed for forming a clique for private interests. After Yang Guang ascended the throne, he was reinstated.

The experiences of Su Wei and Gao Jiong in the officialdom were very coincidental.

When Gao Jiong stepped down as Minister of the Secretariat, Su Wei became the Minister of the Secretariat, and Gao Jiong became the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; when Gao Jiong requested to be demoted to compile books and stepped down from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Su Wei became the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but still participated in state affairs and led the affairs of the Prime Minister.

Gao Jiong should have been unjustly killed by Yang Guang last year, and Su Wei was also dismissed for dissuading Yang Guang from building the Great Wall. However, Su Kui was a close friend of the Crown Prince and the person who understood music theory best in the Great Sui, so not only was he not implicated, but he was promoted to the fifth-rank official and served by Yang Guang’s side.

Su Wei was very talented, but he was cowardly and valued power, so although he was respected by Yang Guang as an elder, he didn't have a good reputation among his peers.

Su Kui was the opposite; although he was arrogant, his reputation was quite good. Yang Su and Su Wei were friends and had often joked to Su Wei, "Yang Su has no sons, Su Kui has no father."

In this space-time, because Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi took a step back first and did not follow Yang Guang on his inspection tour, they did not become the leaders in dissuading Yang Guang from building the Great Wall. Although Su Wei knew in his heart that he should dissuade him, he was too cowardly to be the leader, so he was not dismissed and remained the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

Su Wei often sighed to Su Kui that the second and third sons of the Duke of Tang were both Qilin sons, but it was a pity that there were no girls of suitable age in the family, so Zhangsun Sheng and Yuwen Bi had picked up the bargain.

Crown Prince Yang Zhao also praised Li Xuanba and Li Shimin to Su Kui, but said that Li Xuanba’s mind was deep and Li Shimin’s heart was open and honest; Li Xuanba might be more favored by the Emperor, but he preferred Li Shimin.

Su Kui believed his close friend Yang Zhao’s words more, so he had a prejudice against Li Xuanba.

But seeing that Li Xuanba, a child, could actually sit firmly in the position of the Emperor’s "favored junior" and accompany the Emperor like a prince, Su Kui wanted to get to know this Li Xiucai who was good at writing lyrics.

While Su Kui was quietly observing Li Xuanba, Li Xuanba was also observing Su Kui.

In history, because Su Wei acted like an elder in front of the Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, he was mocked by Li Shimin: "You are a Prime Minister of the Sui Dynasty, yet you could not save the country from chaos, leading to the suffering of the people and the death of the Emperor and the fall of the state. You bowed and danced before Li Mi and Wang Chong. Now that you are old and sick, there is no need to see each other," and he ended up unable to get an official position.

But his two grandsons were both Li Shimin’s men.

Zhangsun Suxu supported Li Tai in the succession struggle, and the daughter of his second grandson Su Dan married Li Chengqian as the Crown Princess. Li Chengqian and Li Tai both died in depression due to the succession struggle, but the Su family members continued to be reused by Emperor Taizong because of their overflowing talent, and their status was not damaged at all. His descendant Su Xu was a virtuous prime minister in the Kaiyuan era, with the posthumous title "Wenxian."

Su Wei’s family education was truly extraordinary.

Talented people will eventually shine. Now the Su family certainly wouldn't look up to him and his Second Brother, so Li Xuanba didn't intend to contact them.

He just remembered the incident where the Prince of Qin mocked Su Wei when he saw Su Kui.

Suxu was one of the eighteen scholars of the Prince of Qin’s mansion and followed the Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, very early on. Li Shimin reused Suxu while mocking his grandfather to his face; he was truly bad.

Second Brother, it is indeed you.

Li Xuanba decided to spoil the story of his mocking Su Wei to his Second Brother when he got back, adding a heavy psychological burden to him.

"Da'de, Minister Xue appreciates your talent? How about you take him as another teacher?"

The distracted Li Xuanba: "Ah? Okay... wait? What happened?"

Yang Guang clenched his fist and hit his cousin’s head, laughing and crying: "You can be distracted while accompanying the Emperor?! Look, ministers, my cousin really doesn't treat me as an Emperor at all!"

Li Xuanba covered his head, completely confused.

Xue Daoheng laughed: "Arrogant enough! Your Majesty, I will take this disciple! I just like arrogant people!"

Yang Guang laughed loudly: "I knew it, Da'de definitely fits Minister Xue’s taste! Da'de, hurry up and pay your respects to your teacher!"

Li Xuanba: "..."

Although he was very confused, since the Emperor told him to take a teacher, he had no choice.

Who did I take as a teacher? Would Teacher Gao and Teacher Yuwen be angry?

Oh, Xue Daoheng, Teacher Gao and Teacher Yuwen should approve of this teacher.

No, wait, why is it Xue Daoheng?!

Li Xuanba had a massive headache.

He was still worrying about whether Teacher Gao and Teacher Yuwen could escape their deaths, so why did another Xue Daoheng, Teacher Xue, who loved to crash into Yang Guang’s blade, appear?

Why are the teachers arranged for him by Emperor Yang of Sui always the people he wants to kill?

Li Xuanba felt that his luck in taking teachers was excessively bizarre.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第60章 都是高老师的锅 – 第61章 他们曾经是挚友
chunks.chineseText:
第60章 都是高老师的锅

=
　　李玄霸被杨广推着拜师后， 才知道为何会发生这件事。
　　这口锅该高颎老师来背。
　　薛道衡比高颎大一岁，却是高颎的“迷弟”，十分敬佩高颎的为人和才华。
　　高颎收李玄霸和李世民为徒时， 薛道衡本不在意。得到过高颎指点的人不少， 李玄霸和李世民不算特殊。
　　但之后李玄霸和李世民频繁进出高颎府邸， 其身份明显已经不是普通被高颎指点的人。
　　薛道衡回京后与高颎通信，得知高颎居然将这两个孩子收为确立了师徒名分的弟子，便对李玄霸和李世民生出好感。
　　高颎选中的学生一定很优秀。
　　薛道衡和唐国公府没有多少交情。他即使对李玄霸和李世民好奇， 也不可能自降身份主动接触李玄霸和李世民。何况李玄霸和李世民还在守孝。
　　薛收和李玄霸、李世民偶然结识后，薛道衡很想让薛收把李玄霸、李世民叫到家中看看。
　　但薛收已经被他过继出去，就算招待朋友也是在新家。虽说薛收也可以在薛道衡府邸中招待朋友， 但这要薛收自己主动开口。薛道衡拉不下这个面子。
　　薛收完全没有察觉到生父的暗示。
　　薛道衡心高气傲，不喜欢被人打扰。薛收一直很敬畏薛道衡， 哪可能让新朋友打扰到薛道衡。
　　今日薛道衡终于有机会接触到李玄霸， 李玄霸所做的事又正合他的胃口，便在杨广面前多夸了李玄霸几句，感慨李玄霸不愧是高颎的学生，果然优秀，若是自己也有这样的学生就好了。
　　李玄霸这个学生是杨广塞给高颎的。虽然杨广当时本意是侮辱高颎， 高颎原本没接这个差事。
　　若不是宇文弼因李玄霸的病弱联想到自家孙儿，对离开父母伴驾的李玄霸和李世民多了几分照顾， 意外发现了李玄霸和李世民的才华，让高颎起了胜负心，高颎不会主动去教导李玄霸和李世民。
　　但既然高颎接了这个差事， 在杨广看来就是高颎向他示弱服软。杨广对此事很得意。
　　高颎和宇文弼越夸赞李玄霸和李世民， 杨广就认为高颎和宇文弼是在持续向他示好。
　　当薛道衡也夸赞李玄霸时， 杨广欣慰极了。
　　薛卿终于向朕示好！夸赞朕的眼光好了！
　　杨广立刻就问薛道衡要不要收弟子。这么好的弟子， 你也可以有！
　　高颎的弟子一定是人中龙凤，我必须收！从来不收弟子的薛道衡立刻同意。
　　李玄霸人麻了。
　　隋炀帝你对薛道衡恨得牙痒痒，连薛道衡写个吹嘘隋文帝的赋，你都能恶意揣测薛道衡是在骂你。现在你怎么表现得对薛道衡如此舔？自古君臣以美人爱情作比，你们这是在表演什么求而不得的狗血文学吗？
　　我和二哥是你们君臣之间什么特殊的情|趣道具吗？！！
　　救命！！！
　　李玄霸根本不想拜薛道衡为师。
　　不说薛道衡那尖酸刻薄的文人脾气将来肯定会惹更多事，他这个弟子可能会被牵连，薛道衡擅长的本事，他也没必要去学啊。
　　薛道衡是一位纯粹的文人，擅长文字工作。在隋文帝时期，长期担任秘书机要，为隋文帝撰写诏令。
　　李玄霸学这个干什么？难道将来他哥还能缺帮写诏令的人？
　　李玄霸斟酌利弊后愿意帮助高颎和宇文弼，除了这两位老师真心对他和二哥好之外，也有高颎和宇文弼是文武双全的治世能臣，他和二哥正缺这样的老师的缘故。
　　就算虞世南都只能教他们写字，薛道衡能教什么？作诗吗？好的诗人不是练出来的，是天生的。他和二哥真的没这个天赋。
　　但皇帝都发话了，轮不到李玄霸挑挑拣拣。
　　就是皇帝没发话，薛道衡说要收李玄霸为弟子，李玄霸都只能跪下磕头说受宠若惊。
　　薛道衡可是现在的文坛领袖！
　　李玄霸晕乎乎地多了个老师，众大臣都笑着恭喜他。
　　他有种自己躺在手术台上，周围一群人围着自己鼓掌的幻觉。
　　杨广微笑道：“大德，你的老师都是当世最有才华的人，你要好生学习，不要辱了老师的门扉。”
　　李玄霸苦笑：“陛下，我压力好大。”
　　杨广笑道：“不需要有压力，你是朕的子侄，受得起这样的老师。”
　　李玄霸只能谢恩。
　　杨广和大臣们听完新词新曲，还要商议朝政大事。李玄霸提前出宫，回家告诉二哥这幢“大喜事”。
　　本来李世民也要入宫，但他前些时日沉迷狩猎耽误了功课。
　　高颎要来洛阳送编书的阶段性成果给杨广检阅，顺带检查李世民和李玄霸的功课。
　　宇文弼病好了，也告诉了两位弟子复课的时间。
　　连虞世南都出了孝期官复原职即将来洛阳，提前写信询问李世民和李玄霸有没有认真练字。
　　李世民急得嘴上起了泡。
　　狩猎一时爽，补功课火葬场。
　　李世民向李玄霸求助，李玄霸转手向母亲告了一状。
　　李世民向友人们求助，长孙无忌表示爱莫能助，杜如晦和薛收倒是想帮忙，被房乔狠狠骂了一顿，不敢帮了。
　　李世民只能一边喝着降火的苦药，一边苦哈哈自己赶功课。
　　李玄霸回到家时，李世民正趴在书案上小睡。
　　书案上堆了一小叠刚写好的字帖。李玄霸翻看了几页。虽然这功课是赶出来的，但二哥写得很用心，没有敷衍。
　　赶功课是真的赶，但还是有认真做。
　　“醒醒，我有好消息要告诉你。”李玄霸把李世民摇醒。
　　李世民迷迷糊糊地睁开眼睛，擦了擦嘴角的口水：“不，我不想听。”
　　李玄霸道：“是真的好消息。”
　　李世民捂耳朵，不相信弟弟。
　　但捂耳朵是没用的，李玄霸道：【陛下又给我们找了一个新老师，薛收的亲生父亲薛道衡，如今的文坛领袖，高兴吗？】
　　李世民脸色一垮：“啊？又多了个老师？那不是又要多一门功课？救命！”
　　李玄霸一愣。他没想到二哥会从这个方向哀嚎。
　　李世民抱着脑袋，曲着膝盖，倒在坐榻上滚了起来。
　　“救命，救命，我不想做功课！为什么我要有这么多老师！我不需要这么多老师！我不想写字，不想写注疏，不想写策论，也不想写诗！我什么都不想！只想打猎！”
　　李玄霸看着滚来滚去的二哥，露出了十分无语的表情。
　　狩猎有那么有趣吗？二哥你这样就像是电子游戏瘾犯了的小学生，小心被拉去电疗。
　　“你这么不想，那上门拒绝？”李玄霸站在坐榻边，抱着手臂居高临下地看着打滚的二哥。
　　李世民停止打滚，手脚伸长成大字形，眼神失去了光芒：“陛下金口玉言，薛公还是文坛领袖，我敢吗？呜呜呜，我好惨啊，我不想上课！”
　　说完，李世民又抱着脑袋在坐榻上滚来滚去。
　　这个世界上会有人喜欢上课吗？没有！不可能有！
　　李玄霸见二哥在耍赖摆烂，只能给他下一剂猛药：【没事，薛公很快就会被陛下赐死，你很快就会少一门课。】
　　李世民不滚了。
　　他默默爬起来，用幽怨的眼神看着李玄霸：“阿玄，哥哥最近是得罪你了吗？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“没有。”
　　李世民抓狂：“那你就别告诉我这个啊！”
　　李玄霸耸肩，摊手：“可我不能一个人难受。”
　　李世民使劲地抓挠自己的头发，把两个小揪揪都抓散了：“啊啊啊啊，我也不想难受！闭嘴闭嘴闭嘴！不要说啦！”
　　李玄霸道：“我又没再说什么。而且你不是说你已经淡定了吗？现在怎么不淡定了？”
　　李世民抓起靠垫丢向弟弟：“闭嘴！”
　　李玄霸接住靠垫，反手砸向李世民。
　　李世民也接住了靠垫，再次砸向李玄霸。
　　兄弟二人一边吵架，一边用靠枕打了起来。
　　李智云高高兴兴地来找二哥，问二哥功课写完没有。见二哥和三哥在玩抱枕，他蹦蹦跳跳地加入进来。
　　等兄弟三人玩了一会儿后，李智云才想起自己为什么过来。
　　“啊，娘亲说二哥和三哥的老师来拜访，让二哥和三哥赶紧过去。”李智云道，“快些快些！”
　　李世民和李玄霸异口同声地抓狂：“你怎么不早说！”
　　李智云对手指：“你们又没问！”
　　李世民和李玄霸飞速整理仪容，然后往中堂跑。
　　离开前，两人依次狠狠敲了李智云的脑袋一下，异口同声道：“等会儿收拾你！”
　　李智云捂着脑袋，看着哥哥们奔跑的背影，自言自语：“二哥三哥骂我的话一模一样啊。”
　　他身边的乳母笑着道：“这就是双生子啊。”
　　李智云噘嘴。他也好想和哥哥们成为双生子啊，好像很好玩。
　　来拜访的老师是高颎。
　　李世民一见到高颎，就哭丧着脸道：“高老师，你怎么来得这么快？”
　　正和高颎聊得开心的李渊笑容一僵。
　　李建成忙道：“二弟顽劣，请高公恕罪。”
　　高颎对李世民招招手。
　　李世民小碎步挪动过去。
　　高颎道：“听闻你沉迷狩猎，荒废功课？”
　　李世民立刻转头看李玄霸。
　　李玄霸先和高颎问好后，气定神闲道：“是的，没错，就是我告状。我不仅向高老师告状，宇文老师和虞老师那里我也告状了。”
　　高颎道：“伸手。”
　　李世民默默伸出双手，手心向上。
　　高颎从袖子里掏出戒尺，狠狠敲了李世民的双手手心各二十下。
　　李世民的手心立刻变得红肿。
　　高颎收起戒尺：“李二郎小小年纪就驰猎无度，荒废学业，李叔德，看来你真的很忙，忙到连规正孩子行为的时间都没有了。”
　　李渊：“……”他差点条件反射也伸出手板心挨揍。


第61章 他们曾经是挚友

=
　　高颎素有威严。
　　在李渊还是个十五六岁的少年郎时， 因受到隋文帝和独孤皇后的喜爱，曾经与皇子们一同听过高颎的课。所以高颎拿出戒尺，李渊就梦回了一次少年时代， 差点闹出笑话。
　　李渊干笑道：“是我太忙……不， 我是说， 是我不好，没有好好约束二郎。大雄！以后完成功课前不准去狩猎！”
　　李世民蔫哒哒道：“是，父亲。”
　　李建成替李世民说话道：“二郎年幼， 贪玩些正常，他已经知错了。三郎！为亲者理应相隐，你怎能将二郎的错事散播得四处都是？”
　　高颎皱眉。
　　李渊赞同道：“三郎， 你这事确实做得不应该。”
　　李玄霸恭敬道：“是，我知错了。”
　　李世民不满道：“我做错了事， 阿玄规劝我我不听， 所以阿玄向老师请求帮助，这怎么能叫把我的错事散播得到处都是？何况因贪玩而不做功课这件事，怎么能归入亲者相隐中？连兄弟做错事都不想办法规劝，才是真的不友悌！”
　　李玄霸叹气：“不，二哥， 是我的错。但我下次还会这么做，知错不改。”
　　李建成被李世民的话堵得脸色有些难看。李玄霸这句“知错不改”缓和了气氛， 让故意想找机会刺李玄霸几句的李建成都露出了无奈的神色。
　　“好了，我就知道你会知错不改。”李渊苦笑，“高公啊， 是我的错， 我太纵容他们了。”
　　高颎没有回答。他对李世民道：“你知道不该贪玩而贪玩， 更该反省。不过知道这是自己的错误， 不迁怒规劝你的兄弟，这一点很好。”
　　他站起来，对李渊道：“我要检查二郎和三郎功课，先失陪了。”
　　李渊道：“我也去！”
　　李建成也站起来，想要同去。
　　高颎道：“只是检查孩童功课，不须这么多人看着。”
　　李渊听言，只好给了李世民一个“护不住你了”的眼神，恭敬地送高颎离开。
　　他知道李世民在赶功课，得知高颎到来后，他急忙把高颎拖住，想给李世民反应的时间，结果还是没护住。
　　唉，高公的威严太重，他一句为李世民开脱的话都不敢说。
　　李渊对李建成道：“高公说得无错，驰猎无度不好，你也该放下狩猎，专注正事。”
　　李建成情绪有些低落道：“我没有高公那样的老师。”
　　李渊失笑：“这父亲可帮不了你。二郎和三郎的老师都是陛下定的，那些老师都是以你父亲的面子请不到的人。不过你也别难过，你已经弱冠，求学已经不再是正事。你该多与勋贵和世族子弟交往，积累入仕的人脉。”
　　李建成拱手道：“是，父亲。”
　　李渊劝慰道：“你是未来的唐国公，身上已经是最高的爵位，将来前途无量，低调些更好。你两个弟弟则需要自己打拼，所以才需要显露出才名。你现在做得很好，有我早年的风范。”
　　李建成露出笑容：“父亲，我会继续努力。”
　　李渊拍了拍李建成的肩膀：“好。二郎和三郎大概会被高公教训许久，我们别留在府中了。走，我们爷俩许久不见，一起去狩猎。”
　　李建成笑道：“是！”
　　李渊把刚才还劝李建成别驰猎无度的话忘在脑后，爷俩开开心心狩猎去了。
　　狩猎这爱好，真是深入唐国公府除了李玄霸所有人的骨子里，控制不住啊。
　　高颎与李世民、李玄霸回到他们居住的小院。
　　高颎环视了一圈周围，眉头仍旧紧皱：“你们居住的院落如此僻静狭小？”
　　李世民道：“这里有侧门可以随时偷溜出门，又远离其他人，很安静，我和阿玄很喜欢这里。”
　　李玄霸点头：“僻静些好。”
　　高颎眉头松开：“既然是你们自己选的，僻静些也不错。只是不要随时偷溜出门，注意安全。”
　　李世民和李玄霸道：“是。”
　　高颎又问了李世民和李玄霸生活上的一些琐事，才去检查李世民和李玄霸的功课。
　　李玄霸的功课向来不需要让人操心。李世民已经补了大半功课，功课做得很认真。高颎若晚到几日，估计都发现不了李世民贪玩荒废学业的证据了。
　　他无奈地瞥着李世民道：“你若每日完成一些功课，何至于现在忙碌？”
　　李世民这个弟子，真是让他又爱又气。
　　李世民耷拉着脑袋道：“我知道错了，下次一定！”
　　高颎道：“承诺了就要做到，我希望你没有下次。”
　　李世民脑袋耷拉得更厉害：“是，弟子尽力。”
　　教训人点到即止，知道错，真心反省就行。高颎没有继续训斥李世民。
　　他拿起李世民和李玄霸的功课，给二人讲解功课上出现的错漏，随意讲起课来。
　　李世民和李玄霸一左一右坐在高颎身旁，就像是寻常孙儿陪伴祖父一样，也很随意地听起课来。
　　高颎最初给李世民、李玄霸授课时很严肃。李世民和李玄霸规规矩矩跪坐着听课。
　　熟悉之后，除了正式授课的时候仍旧严肃，高颎与李世民、李玄霸讲解功课时变得随意起来。
　　李世民和李玄霸要学的知识很多，高颎担心把两个孩子绷太紧，所以特意制造闲适的氛围，让两个孩子不要对繁重的功课心生抵触。
　　高颎讲课深入浅出，各种典故信手拈来，再难的知识在高颎口中都能化作一个个具体的事例，让李世民和李玄霸像听故事一样明白他想教授的知识。
　　中途仆人前来添了一次茶水。
　　高颎喝完了一壶茶，如厕回来时才察觉自己喝的水过于解渴。
　　李世民炫耀道：“这是阿玄炒制的茶叶，没有加其他配料，直接冲泡引用。我原本认为茶水过于寡淡，喝习惯淡茶后，竟比喝蜜水还舒坦一些。吃肉时喝茶水也更解腻。老师离开时带些走。唉，我本来早就让阿玄送些茶叶给老师，阿玄总说还不够好，再等等。”
　　李玄霸道：“是还不够好，茶叶味道还有苦涩。”
　　手工茶也是网红手工艺品的智商税产品，磨碎了还能做成护肤品。
　　李玄霸曾经做过一个企划，从茶叶采摘、制备、烘焙，到磨粉做成护肤品，全部流程都是手工亲自制作，并拍成视频。这个取名为“臻品茶”的系列护肤品果然卖脱销，成为店里的招牌明星产品。
　　他只会烘焙红茶、绿茶，各种半发酵茶的火候他掌握不好。而他烘焙的红茶和绿茶，也肯定没有市面上卖的最普通的茶叶好喝。
　　成熟的工业化制作的茶叶，品相是他这个生疏的手工艺者不能比的。
　　到了这一世，李玄霸喝不惯过于甜腻的饮子，一直在摸索散茶炒制。但好的茶叶很贵重，制作散茶还需要许多工具，李玄霸一直没机会。
　　今年李玄霸手中有了钱和人，才把散茶制作出来。但说实话，他现在做的绿茶腥味和苦味都很重，实在说不上好喝，他实在没脸送人。
　　高颎笑道：“又是复原古方？”
　　李玄霸理直气壮：“是的。”
　　高颎道：“我先拿些走。有更好的，你再送来便是。”
　　李世民道：“就是！阿玄太好脸面，不够好就不送，这不好。”
　　李玄霸真想踹二哥一脚。刚挨了揍，你现在就精神了？
　　高颎很自在地拿了弟子的东西，又布置了功课，正打算离开。
　　李玄霸拦住高颎，道：“老师，今日早晨我面圣时，陛下让我和二哥拜薛大夫为师。”
　　高颎道：“薛玄卿为当今文坛魁首。他的本事不仅是文才，文才只是小道。薛玄卿曾为先帝掌文翰，出自他手中的诏令无数。他对政治大局相当有建树，你们可向他求教。”
　　李玄霸本以为薛道衡只是在文学上建树很高，没想到高老师对薛道衡的评价如此高。
　　他反省，自己不该因为史书只记载了薛道衡的文才，就轻视薛道衡的其他才华。
　　冷静下来想一想，能成为皇帝专属秘书的人，肯定不仅仅是文采好。
　　李世民给李玄霸使眼色。
　　高颎问道：“大雄，你有何事？”
　　李世民道：“这个……”
　　他继续看向李玄霸。
　　李玄霸道：“我无意间探听到一件事，有些忐忑，不知该不该和老师说。”
　　高颎叹了口气，半真半假的抱怨道：“每当你这么说的时候，一定是很麻烦的事。说吧，此事和薛玄卿有关？莫非是薛玄卿那臭脾气又惹了陛下？”
　　李世民惊呼：“老师猜得好准！”
　　高颎道：“你们先提起拜师薛玄卿，才说有忐忑事，当然和薛玄卿有关。”
　　李玄霸十分敬佩。老师已经猜得八、九不离十了。
　　李玄霸道：“我在太常寺卿与乐工交流时，无意间听到陛下和苏太常寺卿言，薛大夫曾在归京时呈给陛下《高祖文皇帝颂》，是行《鱼藻》讽谏。”
　　高颎猛地一拍桌案：“荒唐！”
　　《诗经·鱼藻》是歌颂周武王的诗篇，成文时是周幽王时期，所以后世认为此诗是以周武王讽刺周幽王。
　　李世民叹气道：“周武王是开国君王，周幽王已经是第十二代君王。所以以歌颂开国君王讽刺末代君王或许确有此事。但文帝是陛下之父，歌颂陛下的父亲，怎么能叫讽谏陛下？”
　　高颎深呼吸了几下，道：“陛下和苏威说的此事？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　高颎气得笑了出来：“当初薛玄卿被贬岭南，就是与苏威过于亲近，坐苏威结党营私之罪，几近丧命。苏威听陛下怨言，不仅不帮薛玄卿解释，甚至连提醒薛玄卿一句都不肯？好，苏威，真是太好了！”
　　苏威和薛道衡是挚友啊！
