Chapter 60: It’s All Teacher Gao’s Fault

After Li Xuanba was pushed by Yang Guang into taking a master, he finally understood why this had happened.
This entire mess was Teacher Gao Jiong’s fault.
Xue Daoheng was a year older than Gao Jiong, yet he was Gao Jiong’s "fanboy," deeply admiring his character and talent.
When Gao Jiong first took Li Xuanba and Li Shimin as his disciples, Xue Daoheng hadn’t paid much mind to it. Many people had received guidance from Gao Jiong; Li Xuanba and Li Shimin were nothing special.
However, as the two brothers began frequenting Gao Jiong’s residence, it became clear that their status was no longer that of ordinary students receiving casual guidance.
After Xue Daoheng returned to the capital and corresponded with Gao Jiong, he learned that Gao Jiong had officially established a master-disciple relationship with the two children. Consequently, he began to view Li Xuanba and Li Shimin with favor.
A student chosen by Gao Jiong must be exceptional.
Xue Daoheng had little connection with the Duke of Tang’s household. Even if he were curious about the boys, he couldn’t lower his status to approach them proactively. Besides, Li Xuanba and Li Shimin were still in mourning.
After Xue Shou happened to befriend the brothers, Xue Daoheng had been eager for his son to invite them to their home.
But Xue Shou had already been adopted out; even if he entertained friends, it would be at his new home. While Xue Shou could have hosted them at Xue Daoheng’s residence, it would have required Xue Shou to take the initiative, and Xue Daoheng couldn’t bring himself to ask.
Xue Shou remained completely oblivious to his biological father’s hints.
Xue Daoheng was proud and aloof, disliking intrusion. Xue Shou had always held his father in awe; how could he possibly let his new friends disturb him?
Today, Xue Daoheng finally had the chance to interact with Li Xuanba, and what Li Xuanba did was exactly to his taste. He praised the boy to Yang Guang, sighing that Li Xuanba was truly worthy of being Gao Jiong’s student—so talented that he wished he had such a student himself.
Li Xuanba was a student Yang Guang had forced upon Gao Jiong. Although Yang Guang’s original intent was to humiliate Gao Jiong, and Gao Jiong hadn’t initially wanted the task, things changed.
If Yuwen Bi hadn’t seen his own grandson in the frail Li Xuanba and taken pity on the boys who were away from their parents, and if he hadn’t accidentally discovered their talent, which stirred Gao Jiong’s competitive spirit, Gao Jiong would never have taken the initiative to teach them.
But since Gao Jiong had accepted the task, Yang Guang viewed it as Gao Jiong showing weakness and yielding to him. Yang Guang was quite smug about this.
The more Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi praised the boys, the more Yang Guang believed they were continuously currying favor with him.
When Xue Daoheng also praised Li Xuanba, Yang Guang was overjoyed.
*Minister Xue is finally showing favor to me! He’s praising my eye for talent!*
Yang Guang immediately asked Xue Daoheng if he wanted to take on a disciple. *Such a good student—you can have one too!*
*Gao Jiong’s disciple must be a dragon among men; I must take him!* Xue Daoheng, who had never taken a disciple before, immediately agreed.
Li Xuanba felt numb.
*Sui Yangdi, you hate Xue Daoheng so much that even when he writes a rhapsody praising Emperor Wen of Sui, you maliciously speculate that he’s insulting you. Why are you acting like such a sycophant toward him now? Since ancient times, monarchs and ministers have compared their relationships to beauties and lovers—are you two performing some kind of dog-blood drama about unrequited love?*
*Are my second brother and I some kind of special romantic prop for you two?!!*
*Help!!!*
Li Xuanba had no desire to take Xue Daoheng as a master.
Setting aside the fact that Xue Daoheng’s acerbic, scholar-like temper would surely cause more trouble in the future—potentially implicating his disciples—there was no need for him to learn the skills Xue Daoheng excelled in.
Xue Daoheng was a pure man of letters, specializing in literary work. During the reign of Emperor Wen, he had long served as a secretary, drafting imperial edicts.
Why would Li Xuanba need to learn that? Would his brother ever lack someone to help write edicts?
After weighing the pros and cons, Li Xuanba had been willing to help Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi not only because they were genuinely kind to him and his brother, but also because they were capable statesmen, both civil and military—the exact kind of teachers he and his brother lacked.
Even Yu Shinan could only teach them calligraphy. What could Xue Daoheng teach? Poetry? Great poets aren’t trained; they are born. He and his brother truly lacked that talent.
But since the Emperor had spoken, it wasn’t Li Xuanba’s place to pick and choose.
Even if the Emperor hadn’t spoken, if Xue Daoheng said he wanted to take him as a disciple, Li Xuanba would have had to kneel, kowtow, and say he was flattered.
Xue Daoheng was the current leader of the literary world!
Li Xuanba felt dizzy as he gained another master, while the ministers congratulated him with smiles.
He had the hallucination that he was lying on an operating table, surrounded by a crowd of people clapping for him.
Yang Guang smiled. "Da De, your teachers are the most talented men of this age. You must study diligently and not bring shame to their doors."
Li Xuanba gave a wry smile. "Your Majesty, I feel so much pressure."
Yang Guang laughed. "There is no need for pressure. You are my nephew; you are worthy of such teachers."
Li Xuanba could only offer his thanks.
After Yang Guang and the ministers finished listening to the new poems and songs, they had to discuss state affairs. Li Xuanba left the palace early to tell his second brother about this "great joy."
Li Shimin was supposed to enter the palace too, but he had been indulging in hunting lately and had fallen behind on his studies.
Gao Jiong was coming to Luoyang to present the progress of their book compilation to Yang Guang for review, and he would also be checking the boys' progress.
Yuwen Bi had recovered from his illness and had also informed his two disciples of the time for their lessons to resume.
Even Yu Shinan, having finished his mourning period and returned to office, was coming to Luoyang and had written ahead to ask if they had been practicing their calligraphy diligently.
Li Shimin was so anxious that blisters had formed on his lips.
Hunting was fun for a moment, but catching up on schoolwork was a funeral pyre.
Li Shimin sought help from Li Xuanba, but Li Xuanba turned around and tattled to their mother.
Li Shimin sought help from his friends; Zhangsun Wuji said he couldn’t help, and while Du Ruhui and Xue Shou wanted to, they were scolded so severely by Fang Qiao that they didn’t dare to assist.
Li Shimin could only drink bitter medicine to reduce his internal heat while miserably catching up on his work.
When Li Xuanba returned home, Li Shimin was napping on his desk.
A small stack of freshly written calligraphy practice sheets lay on the desk. Li Xuanba flipped through a few pages. Although the work was rushed, his second brother had written with care and hadn’t been perfunctory.
It was rushed, yes, but he had still put in the effort.
"Wake up, I have good news for you." Li Xuanba shook Li Shimin awake.
Li Shimin opened his eyes groggily and wiped the drool from the corner of his mouth. "No, I don’t want to hear it."
Li Xuanba said, "It’s truly good news."
Li Shimin covered his ears, not believing his younger brother.
But covering his ears was useless. Li Xuanba said, [The Emperor has found us another new teacher: Xue Shou’s biological father, Xue Daoheng, the current leader of the literary world. Happy?]
Li Shimin’s face collapsed. "Ah? Another teacher? Doesn’t that mean another subject to study? Help!"
Li Xuanba blinked. He hadn’t expected his second brother to wail from that perspective.
Li Shimin clutched his head, curled his knees, and rolled around on the daybed.
"Help, help, I don’t want to do schoolwork! Why do I have so many teachers! I don’t need so many teachers! I don’t want to write calligraphy, I don’t want to write commentaries, I don’t want to write policy essays, and I don’t want to write poetry! I don’t want anything! I just want to hunt!"
Li Xuanba looked at his rolling second brother with a completely speechless expression.
*Is hunting really that interesting? Second brother, you’re like a primary schooler addicted to video games. Be careful you don’t get dragged off for electroshock therapy.*
"If you don’t want to, why not go and refuse?" Li Xuanba stood by the daybed, arms crossed, looking down at his rolling brother.
Li Shimin stopped rolling, spread his limbs out into a star shape, and his eyes lost their luster. "The Emperor’s word is law, and Master Xue is the leader of the literary world. Do I dare? Wuwuwu, I’m so miserable, I don’t want to go to class!"
After saying this, Li Shimin curled back into a ball and rolled around on the daybed again.
*Is there anyone in this world who likes class? No! It’s impossible!*
Seeing his brother acting like a brat, Li Xuanba decided to administer a strong dose of medicine: [Don’t worry, Master Xue will soon be ordered to commit suicide by the Emperor. You’ll have one less class soon.]
Li Shimin stopped rolling.
He silently crawled up and looked at Li Xuanba with resentful eyes. "A-Xuan, have I offended you recently?"
Li Xuanba shook his head. "No."
Li Shimin went crazy. "Then don’t tell me things like that!"
Li Xuanba shrugged and spread his hands. "But I can’t be the only one suffering."
Li Shimin frantically scratched at his hair, messing up his two little buns. "Ahhhhh, I don’t want to suffer either! Shut up, shut up, shut up! Don’t say it!"
Li Xuanba said, "I’m not saying anything else. Besides, didn’t you say you were calm? Why aren’t you calm now?"
Li Shimin grabbed a cushion and threw it at his brother. "Shut up!"
Li Xuanba caught the cushion and threw it back at Li Shimin.
Li Shimin caught it and threw it back at Li Xuanba.
The brothers started a pillow fight while arguing.
Li Zhiyun came over happily to ask his second brother if he had finished his homework. Seeing his second and third brothers playing with cushions, he hopped over and joined in.
After the three brothers played for a while, Li Zhiyun finally remembered why he had come.
"Ah, Mother said the teacher of the second and third brothers is here to visit, and told them to go over quickly," Li Zhiyun said. "Hurry, hurry!"
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba shouted in unison, "Why didn’t you say so earlier!"
Li Zhiyun poked his fingers together. "You didn’t ask!"
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba quickly straightened their clothes and ran toward the main hall.
Before leaving, they each gave Li Zhiyun a hard knock on the head and said in unison, "We’ll deal with you later!"
Li Zhiyun clutched his head, watching their retreating backs, and muttered to himself, "Second brother and third brother’s scolding was exactly the same."
His wet nurse laughed. "That’s what twins are like."
Li Zhiyun pouted. He also wanted to be a twin with his brothers; it looked like fun.
The visiting teacher was Gao Jiong.
As soon as Li Shimin saw Gao Jiong, he said with a mournful face, "Teacher Gao, why did you come so quickly?"
Li Yuan, who had been chatting happily with Gao Jiong, froze.
Li Jiancheng hurriedly said, "My second brother is mischievous; please forgive him, Master Gao."
Gao Jiong beckoned to Li Shimin.
Li Shimin shuffled over with small steps.
Gao Jiong said, "I heard you have been indulging in hunting and neglecting your studies?"
Li Shimin immediately turned to look at Li Xuanba.
After greeting Gao Jiong, Li Xuanba said calmly, "Yes, that’s right, I was the one who tattled. I didn’t just tattle to Teacher Gao; I also tattled to Teacher Yuwen and Teacher Yu."
Gao Jiong said, "Hands."
Li Shimin silently extended his hands, palms up.
Gao Jiong pulled a ruler from his sleeve and struck Li Shimin’s palms twenty times each, hard.
Li Shimin’s palms immediately turned red and swollen.
Gao Jiong put away the ruler. "Li Erlang, at such a young age, you hunt without restraint and neglect your studies. Li Shude, it seems you are truly busy—so busy that you don’t even have time to correct your children’s behavior."
Li Yuan: "..." He almost reflexively extended his own palms to be struck.

Chapter 61: They Were Once Best Friends

Gao Jiong had always been a man of great dignity.
When Li Yuan was a boy of fifteen or sixteen, he had attended Gao Jiong’s lectures alongside the princes because he was favored by Emperor Wen and Empress Dugu. Thus, when Gao Jiong pulled out the ruler, Li Yuan had a flashback to his youth and nearly made a fool of himself.
Li Yuan gave a dry laugh. "I have been too busy... no, I mean, it is my fault for not properly restraining Erlang. Daxiong! No more hunting until you finish your homework!"
Li Shimin said dejectedly, "Yes, Father."
Li Jiancheng spoke up for Li Shimin. "Erlang is young; it is normal for him to be playful. He already knows he was wrong. Third Brother! Family members should cover for each other’s faults; how could you spread Erlang’s mistakes everywhere?"
Gao Jiong frowned.
Li Yuan agreed. "Third Brother, what you did was indeed improper."
Li Xuanba said respectfully, "Yes, I know I was wrong."
Li Shimin said indignantly, "I did something wrong, and when A-Xuan tried to persuade me, I didn’t listen. So A-Xuan asked the teachers for help—how can that be called spreading my mistakes everywhere? Besides, how can neglecting homework due to playfulness be categorized as 'covering for family'? Not trying to persuade a brother when he is wrong is what truly lacks brotherly love!"
Li Xuanba sighed. "No, Second Brother, it is my fault. But I will do it again next time; I am incorrigible."
Li Jiancheng’s face darkened at Li Shimin’s words. Li Xuanba’s remark about being "incorrigible" eased the atmosphere, causing even Li Jiancheng, who had been looking for a chance to prick at Li Xuanba, to show a helpless expression.
"Alright, I knew you would be incorrigible." Li Yuan gave a wry smile. "Master Gao, it is my fault; I have been too indulgent with them."
Gao Jiong did not answer. He said to Li Shimin, "You knew you shouldn’t be playful yet you were; you should reflect on that. However, knowing it was your own fault and not venting your anger on the brother who tried to persuade you—that is a good trait."
He stood up and said to Li Yuan, "I am going to check Erlang and Sanchu’s schoolwork; please excuse me."
Li Yuan said, "I’ll go too!"
Li Jiancheng also stood up, wanting to join them.
Gao Jiong said, "It is just checking children’s schoolwork; there is no need for so many people to watch."
Hearing this, Li Yuan could only give Li Shimin a look that said, *I can’t protect you anymore*, and respectfully saw Gao Jiong off.
He knew Li Shimin was rushing to finish his work. When he learned Gao Jiong had arrived, he had hurriedly tried to stall him to give Li Shimin time, but in the end, he hadn’t been able to protect him.
*Sigh, Master Gao’s dignity is too heavy; I didn’t even dare to say a single word to excuse Li Shimin.*
Li Yuan said to Li Jiancheng, "Master Gao is right; hunting without restraint is not good. You should also put aside hunting and focus on proper business."
Li Jiancheng said with a downcast mood, "I don’t have a teacher like Master Gao."
Li Yuan laughed. "Your father can’t help you with that. The teachers for Erlang and Sanchu were appointed by the Emperor; they are people who couldn’t be hired even with your father’s influence. But don’t be sad; you have already reached adulthood, and studying is no longer your primary task. You should interact more with the sons of nobles and clans to build connections for your official career."
Li Jiancheng bowed. "Yes, Father."
Li Yuan comforted him. "You are the future Duke of Tang; you already hold the highest title, and your future is limitless. It is better to keep a low profile. Your two younger brothers need to make their own way, which is why they need to show their talent. You are doing very well right now; you have the demeanor I had in my youth."
Li Jiancheng smiled. "Father, I will continue to work hard."
Li Yuan patted Li Jiancheng on the shoulder. "Good. Erlang and Sanchu will probably be lectured by Master Gao for a long time, so let’s not stay in the mansion. Come, we haven’t seen each other in a while; let’s go hunting."
Li Jiancheng smiled. "Yes!"
Li Yuan forgot all about his advice to Li Jiancheng not to hunt without restraint, and the two of them happily went off to hunt.
The hobby of hunting was truly ingrained in the bones of everyone in the Duke of Tang’s household except for Li Xuanba; it was uncontrollable.
Gao Jiong returned to the small courtyard where Li Shimin and Li Xuanba lived.
Gao Jiong looked around and his brow remained tightly knit. "The courtyard you live in is so secluded and cramped?"
Li Shimin said, "There is a side door here so we can sneak out at any time, and it’s far from everyone else, so it’s very quiet. A-Xuan and I like it here."
Li Xuanba nodded. "It’s better to be secluded."
Gao Jiong’s brow relaxed. "Since you chose it yourselves, seclusion isn’t bad. Just don’t sneak out at all hours, and be careful."
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba said, "Yes."
Gao Jiong asked about some trivial matters in their daily lives before checking their schoolwork.
Li Xuanba’s work never required anyone to worry. Li Shimin had already caught up on most of his work, and it was done very diligently. If Gao Jiong had arrived a few days later, he probably wouldn’t have found any evidence of Li Shimin’s playfulness.
He glanced helplessly at Li Shimin. "If you finished some of your work every day, why would you be so busy now?"
This student, Li Shimin, truly made him both love and get angry at him.
Li Shimin hung his head. "I know I was wrong; I will next time!"
Gao Jiong said, "If you make a promise, you must keep it. I hope there won’t be a next time."
Li Shimin hung his head even lower. "Yes, disciple will try his best."
He stopped the lecturing there; knowing the mistake and genuinely reflecting on it was enough. Gao Jiong did not continue to scold Li Shimin.
He picked up their work, explained the errors and omissions, and began to lecture casually.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba sat on either side of Gao Jiong, just like ordinary grandsons accompanying their grandfather, listening quite comfortably.
When Gao Jiong first started teaching them, he had been very strict. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba would kneel properly to listen.
After becoming familiar, aside from formal lectures where he remained strict, Gao Jiong became more relaxed when explaining their work.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had a lot to learn, and Gao Jiong was worried about putting too much pressure on the two children, so he deliberately created a relaxed atmosphere so they wouldn’t develop a resistance to their heavy workload.
Gao Jiong’s teaching was profound yet accessible, and he could draw on all kinds of historical allusions. Even the most difficult knowledge became concrete examples in his mouth, allowing the boys to understand what he was teaching as if they were listening to stories.
Midway, a servant came to refill their tea.
Gao Jiong finished a pot of tea, and only after returning from the latrine did he realize the water he had drunk was unusually thirst-quenching.
Li Shimin boasted, "This is tea leaves stir-fried by A-Xuan. No other ingredients were added; it’s brewed directly. I originally thought the tea was too bland, but after getting used to it, it’s actually more comfortable than drinking honey water. It’s also better for cutting the grease when eating meat. Teacher, take some with you when you leave. Sigh, I had asked A-Xuan to send some to you earlier, but A-Xuan always said it wasn’t good enough and to wait."
Li Xuanba said, "It really isn’t good enough; the tea still has a bitter and astringent taste."
Handmade tea was just another "IQ tax" product of internet-famous crafts; once ground up, it could even be made into skincare products.
Li Xuanba had once made a project plan: from tea picking, preparation, and roasting, to grinding into powder for skincare, the entire process was done by hand and filmed. This series of skincare products, named "Zhenpin Tea," had indeed sold out and become the shop’s signature star product.
He only knew how to roast black and green tea; he couldn’t master the heat for various semi-fermented teas. And the tea he roasted was certainly not as good as the most ordinary tea sold on the market.
The quality of mature, industrially produced tea was something he, a clumsy craftsman, couldn’t compare to.
In this life, Li Xuanba couldn’t get used to overly sweet drinks and had been exploring stir-frying loose tea. But good tea leaves were expensive, and making loose tea required many tools, so he had never had the chance.
This year, with money and people at his disposal, he had finally managed to make loose tea. But to be honest, the green tea he made now had a very strong fishy and bitter taste; it really couldn’t be called good, and he didn’t have the face to give it to anyone.
Gao Jiong smiled. "Another restoration of an ancient recipe?"
Li Xuanba said righteously, "Yes."
Gao Jiong said, "I’ll take some. If there is better, you can send it later."
Li Shimin said, "Exactly! A-Xuan is too concerned with his reputation; if it’s not good enough, he won’t send it. That’s not right."
Li Xuanba really wanted to kick his second brother. *You just got a beating, and now you’re full of energy again?*
Gao Jiong took his disciple’s gift quite naturally, assigned some homework, and was about to leave.
Li Xuanba stopped him. "Teacher, this morning when I had an audience with the Emperor, His Majesty told Second Brother and me to take Doctor Xue as our master."
Gao Jiong said, "Xue Xuanqing is the leader of the current literary world. His ability is not just in literature; literature is only a minor path. Xue Xuanqing once handled documents for the late Emperor, and countless edicts came from his hand. He has considerable insight into the overall political situation; you can seek his guidance."
Li Xuanba had thought Xue Daoheng only had high achievements in literature; he hadn’t expected Teacher Gao to rate him so highly.
He reflected that he shouldn’t have looked down on Xue Daoheng’s other talents just because history books only recorded his literary prowess.
Thinking about it calmly, anyone who could become a personal secretary to the Emperor certainly wouldn’t just be good at writing.
Li Shimin gave Li Xuanba a look.
Gao Jiong asked, "Daxiong, what is it?"
Li Shimin said, "This..."
He continued to look at Li Xuanba.
Li Xuanba said, "I accidentally overheard something, and I’m a bit uneasy. I don’t know if I should tell you, Teacher."
Gao Jiong sighed, complaining half-jokingly, "Whenever you say that, it must be a troublesome matter. Speak. Does this matter concern Xue Xuanqing? Could it be that Xue Xuanqing’s foul temper has offended His Majesty again?"
Li Shimin exclaimed, "Teacher guessed so accurately!"
Gao Jiong said, "You brought up taking Xue Xuanqing as a master first, then said you were uneasy—of course it concerns him."
Li Xuanba was full of admiration. His teacher had already guessed eight or nine parts of it.
Li Xuanba said, "When I was communicating with the musicians at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, I accidentally heard His Majesty talking to the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Su, saying that when Doctor Xue returned to the capital, he presented the 'Ode to Emperor Wen, the Founding Father' to His Majesty, which was a satire in the style of the 'Fish and Algae' poem."
Gao Jiong slammed the table. "Absurd!"
The "Fish and Algae" poem from the *Classic of Poetry* was a poem praising King Wu of Zhou; it was written during the time of King You of Zhou, so later generations believed the poem used King Wu to satirize King You.
Li Shimin sighed. "King Wu of Zhou was a founding monarch, and King You was the twelfth generation. So using the praise of a founding monarch to satirize a terminal one might indeed be the case. But Emperor Wen was His Majesty’s father; how can praising His Majesty’s father be called a satire of His Majesty?"
Gao Jiong took a few deep breaths and asked, "His Majesty and Su Wei talked about this?"
Li Xuanba nodded.
Gao Jiong was so angry he laughed. "Back then, when Xue Xuanqing was demoted to Lingnan, it was because he was too close to Su Wei, and he was convicted of forming a clique with Su Wei, nearly losing his life. When Su Wei heard His Majesty’s complaints, not only did he not help explain for Xue Xuanqing, he didn’t even bother to remind him? Good, Su Wei, truly good!"
Su Wei and Xue Daoheng were best friends!

chunks.chapterTitle: 第62章 却道故人心易变
chunks.chineseText:
第62章 却道故人心易变

=
　　高颎的笑容十分悲愤。
　　高颎在隋文帝时是有名的“伯乐”， 十二岁生擒老虎的隋朝大将韩擒虎，权倾朝野被杨广忌惮的楚国公杨素，以及曾与他共同参决朝政的苏威， 都是由他举荐给隋文帝。
　　他对苏威有举荐之恩， 还有共事之情， 关系自然不错。
　　至少高颎自己认为很了解苏威，与苏威关系不错。
　　苏威很有才干，为官也清廉， 唯一的缺点就是过分追求名声，所以为官时很喜欢与同僚结交，声势过于浩大。
　　当时苏威的儿子苏夔与沛国公郑译、国子博士何妥争论乐理， 大半朝臣都支持苏夔。郑译与何妥是个小心眼的人，状告苏威结党营私。隋文帝因此罢免了苏威的官职， 薛道衡坐罪流放岭南。
　　高颎知道苏威不一定有结党营私的心思， 只是太爱经营名声。而且苏夔赢过郑译和何妥也不是因为苏威结党营私，而是苏夔在乐理上的造诣确实赢过这两人。
　　苏夔在获罪之后著十五篇《乐志》，再次阐明了自己的观点，把郑译和何妥驳得体无完肤。世人皆暗中笑话郑译和何妥。
　　后来隋文帝冷静下来后，也察觉苏威确实没有结党营私的心思， 一年后起复苏威，并将当时因苏威结党营私案获罪的大臣诏还， 薛道衡也在此列。
　　此后薛道衡获得了隋文帝的信任，逐步高升，为隋文帝执掌枢要笔墨。
　　薛道衡与苏威可谓是同苦过。比起只是免职的苏威， 薛道衡流放岭南更加凶险。他们回到朝堂之后， 关系自然更加亲近。
　　当时人总传言薛道衡文人脾气尖酸刻薄， 得罪了很多人。其实薛道衡对朋友是极好的。他心胸坦荡， 身居高位的同僚反而特别喜欢与薛道衡为友。
　　比如薛道衡与杨素就是好友。
　　杨素常为薛道衡写诗，隋文帝时期写了《赠薛内史诗》《山斋独坐赠薛内史二首》。两人关系好到隋文帝因忌惮位高权重的杨素，不敢让薛道衡继续执掌枢要笔墨，将薛道衡外放的程度。
　　杨广继位时，即使薛道衡那时对与杨广交好的杨素颇有微词，但杨素仍旧将薛道衡当作最亲密的朋友。
　　他快死之前连给儿子的遗书都没写，一口气写了整整十四首《赠薛播州》，当作给好友的遗言。
　　这十四首《赠薛播州》一改杨素之前旖旎词风，词气宏拔，气势磅礴，是杨素一生中最顶尖之作。
　　薛道衡悲伤评价，“人之将死，其言也善，岂若是乎”。
　　与野史小说中常爱送人侍妾的心胸宽广形象相反，杨素是个心胸狭窄的人，当权时常党同伐异。
　　能被杨素视为挚友，说薛道衡不会做人，言过其实。
　　高颎和李世民、李玄霸说起往事。
　　他提到了曾经的杨素，曾经的苏威，提到了薛道衡和杨素、苏威的友谊，提到了杨素死前为薛道衡写的十四首《赠薛播州》。
　　人老了，回忆过去时总容易伤神。
　　杨素也是由高颎举荐做官，却为了帮助杨广夺嫡捅了高颎好几刀。高颎在杨素死时因为太过快乐，装不出悲伤的模样，只能装病不去丧礼。
　　但现在提起曾经的杨素，高颎竟然也为杨素晚年风光下的凄凉落下泪来。
　　与高颎一起从北周一路走来的老臣越来越少，他的敌人和朋友都逐渐身影淡去，漫长的人生道路上只有寥寥数人同行。
　　薛道衡在这寥寥数人中，苏威也在。
　　高颎知道以苏威的性格，大概率没有落井下石。
　　他只是默默地听着，默默地隐瞒。
　　他只是什么都没做。
　　但苏威以前不是这样的人。他虽重声望，但性格生性乖僻，遇到自己不认可的事，哪怕对着隋文帝都会发怒，所以官路才会几起几落。
　　高颎不明白，新帝继位之后，他熟悉的了解的为何全部都变陌生了？
　　他悲从心来，潸然泪下。
　　李世民和李玄霸一个递帕子，一个递水，安静地聆听老师的倾诉。
　　高颎离开时，神色恢复了平静，好像什么事都没发生过，只有眼眶略有些红肿。
　　他叮嘱道：“此事我会处理，你二人不可再向其他人提起，无论是薛玄卿还是宇文公辅，都不可以透露。”
　　李世民和李玄霸应下后，高颎仍旧不放心，再三叮嘱之后才离开。
　　目送高颎离开后，李世民叹道：“苏威和薛公都是老师的友人。”
　　李玄霸：“嗯。”
　　他只想到薛道衡对高老师推崇备至，以高老师的性格，应该与薛道衡的关系不错。没想到苏威与高老师、薛道衡也是友人。
　　仔细扒拉一下史书，好像史书中简略的记载中确实有相关蛛丝马迹，只是他忽视了。
　　“不过我也算明白，为何陛下会忌惮老师了。”李世民小声道，“朝中贤能的高官，大多都与老师有旧，不少人还欠着老师举荐之恩。”
　　李玄霸点头：“是啊。朝中不少人都欠着老师恩情，所以他们都盼着老师死呢。”
　　李世民：“啊？！”
　　李玄霸心平气和道：“欠的债太多，可不就盼着债主死？”
　　李世民：“……”他完全没想到，居然还有这种解读方式。
　　李世民抱怨：“你的思考角度总是很奇怪。我本来想说，虽然老师确实厉害，陛下忌惮老师情有可原，但这也显得陛下心胸狭隘，底气不足，身为皇帝，居然认为还不如一个已经快要致仕的老臣。他大不了让老师致仕呗。你怎么会想到‘盼着债主死’那里去？阿玄，不是哥哥我说你，有时候你的想法真的很偏激。这世间还是好人多，你不要……唉？你跑什么？”
　　李玄霸捂耳朵。
　　二哥唠叨起来没完没了，全是“这个世界充满爱，阿玄你要阳光起来”的陈词滥调馊鸡汤，李玄霸最不乐意听这些。
　　李世民小跑着跟上李玄霸，提高声音道：“阿玄，你越不爱听，我就越要说，站住别跑！”
　　李玄霸捂着耳朵拔腿就跑，李世民在后面一边追一边继续大声唠叨。
　　窦夫人正好出来问李世民和李玄霸晚上想吃点什么，被李世民和李玄霸当柱子绕。
　　窦夫人一手拽住一个孩子的后衣领：“别绕了，我眼睛都花了！你们又在闹什么？”
　　李世民叹气：“是阿玄的错，我就说他几句，他居然捂着耳朵逃跑！”
　　李玄霸道：“啰嗦。”
　　两人说着说着，吵了起来。
　　窦夫人见二儿子和三儿子因为这点鸡毛蒜皮的事争吵，颇有些哭笑不得。
　　二郎和三郎太容易争吵，每日都会因一些小事吵架，窦夫人有时都不知道该说这两个孩子感情是好还是不好了。
　　……
　　李玄霸没有偷听到杨广和苏威的谈话。他们俩的谈话是记录在史书中的。
　　这种私下谈话，谁知道史官怎么记录下来。但李玄霸确定苏威确实和杨广有过此番对话。
　　据薛收说，他的父亲在回京之前，苏相曾给他的父亲写过许多信。但他的父亲回朝堂后没多久，苏相对他的父亲似乎较为冷漠了。
　　薛道衡不是个好脾气。你对我冷淡，我也懒得理睬你。所以两人的关系就这么淡了。
　　只是高颎早早离开了朝堂，到京城隐居，所以不太清楚两人关系的变化，还以为两人还是好友。
　　苏威这明显的态度变化，很明显有猫腻。
　　李玄霸虽然当时没有拜薛道衡为师，但薛收已经是他和二哥的好友。他知道薛道衡的结局，虽然不认为自己能改变薛道衡容易得罪人的性格，但也没打算完全无作为。
　　碰巧苏威是太常寺卿，李玄霸没了职官实职，做的还是协律郎的事，苏威是他实际的上司。
　　李玄霸与苏威交谈时，故意与苏威讨论起《诗经》——《诗经》是礼乐必修科目，李玄霸与苏威讨论《诗经》并不突兀。
　　当李玄霸和苏威说起《鱼藻》时，苏威的神色明显不对，还很好心地叮嘱他不要学这讽谏之诗，陛下不喜欢。李玄霸就确定史书中写的八成是真的了。
　　他原本打算再得到更多的证据，就将此事告知薛收。
　　就像他哥所说的，即便是他知道未来难以更改，既然心有不平，做点什么总比袖手旁观好。将来结局注定，他努力过了，心中就不会有太多不甘。
　　拜薛道衡为师后，与他和二哥的关系变得紧密，也与他与二哥的其他老师成为了隐藏的同盟，李玄霸就改变了努力的方向，将此事告知高颎，让高颎帮忙了。
　　比起薛收，李玄霸相信薛道衡应该更听得进去高颎的话。
　　而且高颎劝说薛道衡，薛道衡应该也不会将信将疑地找苏威对峙。他不用百般求证此事真假。
　　事有凑巧，薛道衡的好友，房乔之父房彦谦因在地方上政绩十分出众，在地方官吏考核中再次位列前茅，高升入京，任司隶刺史。
　　房彦谦一回朝，还来不及与也在东都的儿子房乔好好聊一聊，就去了薛道衡家，劝薛道衡闭门谢客，低调避祸。
　　房彦谦道：“我回朝后被陛下接见，陛下听闻我与你为友，向我问起许多你之事，其言语间似乎对你不满。我观陛下心胸狭窄不似明君，玄卿你要小心啊。”
　　历史中的薛道衡也被房彦谦劝说过，但没当回事。
　　薛道衡知道自己就是一个被排除在权力中枢外的文人，没有资格被皇帝忌惮，所以只要自己不做违法乱纪的事，就没理由被皇帝杀害，顶多就是冷落而已。
　　但现在，薛道衡刚被高颎透露了“《鱼藻》之祸”，再听房彦谦之言，他的心情就不同了。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 62: Yet They Say the Hearts of Old Friends Change Easily

Gao Jiong’s smile was filled with profound grief.

During the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui, Gao Jiong was a renowned "Bo Le"—a master at recognizing talent. Han Qinhu, the great general who captured a tiger at the age of twelve; Yang Su, the Duke of Chu whose power eclipsed the court and made Yang Guang wary; and Su Wei, who had once deliberated state affairs alongside him—all had been recommended to Emperor Wen by Gao Jiong.

He had the grace of a patron toward Su Wei, and the bond of shared service; their relationship was naturally quite good. At the very least, Gao Jiong believed he understood Su Wei well and that they were close.

Su Wei was highly capable and incorruptible as an official. His only flaw was an excessive pursuit of fame, which led him to cultivate extensive connections with his colleagues, creating a momentum that was far too grand.

At that time, Su Wei’s son, Su Kui, had engaged in a debate over music theory with the Duke of Pei, Zheng Yi, and the National University scholar He Tuo. Most of the court officials supported Su Kui. Zheng Yi and He Tuo, being petty men, accused Su Wei of forming a faction for personal gain. Consequently, Emperor Wen dismissed Su Wei from office, and Xue Daoheng was implicated and exiled to Lingnan.

Gao Jiong knew that Su Wei did not necessarily harbor the intent to form a faction; he was simply too obsessed with managing his reputation. Moreover, Su Kui’s victory over Zheng Yi and He Tuo was not due to his father’s factionalism, but because Su Kui’s mastery of music theory truly surpassed theirs.

After falling into disgrace, Su Kui authored the fifteen-chapter *Yue Zhi* (Treatise on Music), further clarifying his views and refuting Zheng Yi and He Tuo so thoroughly that they were left with no shred of dignity. The world secretly mocked them both.

Later, after Emperor Wen cooled down, he realized that Su Wei indeed lacked the intent to form a faction. A year later, he reinstated Su Wei and recalled the officials who had been implicated in the case, including Xue Daoheng.

Thereafter, Xue Daoheng gained Emperor Wen’s trust, rose steadily through the ranks, and eventually held the keys to the Emperor’s private correspondence and state secrets.

Xue Daoheng and Su Wei could be said to have suffered together. Compared to Su Wei, who was merely dismissed, Xue Daoheng’s exile to Lingnan was far more perilous. After they returned to the court, their relationship naturally grew even closer.

People often whispered that Xue Daoheng had the sharp, acerbic temperament of a scholar and had offended many. In truth, Xue Daoheng was exceptionally good to his friends. He was open-minded and magnanimous, and high-ranking colleagues were particularly fond of befriending him.

For instance, Xue Daoheng and Yang Su were close friends.

Yang Su frequently wrote poetry for Xue Daoheng, such as the *Poem Gifted to Secretariat Director Xue* and the two *Sitting Alone in the Mountain Studio, Gifted to Secretariat Director Xue* written during Emperor Wen’s reign. Their relationship was so close that Emperor Wen, wary of the powerful Yang Su, dared not let Xue Daoheng continue to handle his private correspondence and went so far as to reassign him to a post outside the capital.

When Yang Guang ascended the throne, even though Xue Daoheng had expressed reservations about Yang Su—who was in Yang Guang’s favor—Yang Su still regarded Xue Daoheng as his closest friend.

Before he died, Yang Su did not even write a final testament for his own sons; instead, he poured his energy into writing fourteen poems titled *Gifted to Xue of Bozhou* as his final words to his dear friend.

These fourteen poems broke from Yang Su’s previously delicate and flowery style; they were grand, soaring, and majestic—the pinnacle of his life’s work.

Xue Daoheng commented with sorrow, "When a man is about to die, his words are virtuous—could it really be so?"

Contrary to the image of a broad-minded man who loved to gift concubines to others as portrayed in unofficial histories and novels, Yang Su was a narrow-minded man who often engaged in factional purges while in power.

To be considered a bosom friend by Yang Su, the claim that Xue Daoheng did not know how to conduct himself was clearly an exaggeration.

Gao Jiong spoke of these past events to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

He mentioned the Yang Su of the past, the Su Wei of the past; he spoke of the friendship between Xue Daoheng, Yang Su, and Su Wei; and he spoke of the fourteen *Gifted to Xue of Bozhou* poems Yang Su wrote before his death.

When one is old, it is easy to feel wounded while reminiscing.

Yang Su had also been recommended for office by Gao Jiong, yet he had stabbed Gao Jiong in the back several times to help Yang Guang seize the throne. When Yang Su died, Gao Jiong felt such joy that he could not feign sadness, and could only pretend to be ill to avoid the funeral.

Yet now, mentioning the Yang Su of old, Gao Jiong actually shed tears for the desolation hidden beneath the splendor of Yang Su’s final years.

The number of old officials who had walked with Gao Jiong since the Northern Zhou dynasty was dwindling. His enemies and friends were gradually fading away, leaving only a handful of companions on the long road of life.

Xue Daoheng was among these few, and so was Su Wei.

Gao Jiong knew that given Su Wei’s character, it was highly unlikely he had kicked a man while he was down.

He had simply listened in silence, silently concealing the truth.

He had simply done nothing.

But Su Wei had not been that kind of man before. Though he valued his reputation, he was naturally eccentric. If he encountered something he did not approve of, he would fly into a rage even before Emperor Wen, which was why his official career had seen so many ups and downs.

Gao Jiong did not understand: after the new Emperor ascended the throne, why had everyone he knew and understood become so unrecognizable?

Grief welled up from his heart, and he wept.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, one handing him a handkerchief and the other a cup of water, listened quietly to their teacher’s outpouring.

When Gao Jiong left, his expression had returned to calm, as if nothing had happened, save for his slightly red and swollen eyes.

He cautioned, "I will handle this matter. You two must not mention it to anyone else—not to Xue Xuanqing, nor to Yuwen Gufu. Do not let a word slip."

After Li Shimin and Li Xuanba agreed, Gao Jiong remained uneasy, repeating his instructions several times before finally departing.

Watching Gao Jiong leave, Li Shimin sighed, "Su Wei and Master Xue are both the teacher’s friends."

Li Xuanba replied, "Mm."

He had only thought that Xue Daoheng held their teacher in the highest regard, and given their teacher’s personality, their relationship should have been good. He had not expected Su Wei to be friends with both their teacher and Xue Daoheng.

Digging through history books, it seemed there were indeed traces of this in the brief records, but he had overlooked them.

"But I finally understand why His Majesty is wary of the teacher," Li Shimin whispered. "Most of the capable high officials in the court have old ties with the teacher, and many still owe him the debt of his recommendation."

Li Xuanba nodded. "Indeed. Many in the court owe the teacher a debt of gratitude, which is why they are all hoping for his death."

Li Shimin: "Ah?!"

Li Xuanba said calmly, "When one owes too many debts, doesn't one hope for the creditor to die?"

Li Shimin: "..." He had never imagined there could be such an interpretation.

Li Shimin complained, "Your way of thinking is always so strange. I was going to say that although the teacher is indeed formidable and the Emperor’s wariness is understandable, it still makes the Emperor look narrow-minded and insecure. As an Emperor, he actually thinks he is inferior to an old official who is about to retire. He could just let the teacher retire. How did you get to 'hoping for the creditor to die'? Ah-Xuan, it’s not that I, your brother, am lecturing you, but sometimes your thoughts are truly extreme. There are still many good people in this world, you shouldn't... hey? Why are you running?"

Li Xuanba covered his ears.

When his Second Brother started nagging, it was endless—all those clichés and "chicken soup for the soul" about how "the world is full of love, Ah-Xuan, you need to be more optimistic." Li Xuanba hated hearing those things the most.

Li Shimin trotted after Li Xuanba, raising his voice, "Ah-Xuan, the more you hate to hear it, the more I have to say it! Stop running!"

Li Xuanba covered his ears and bolted, while Li Shimin chased after him, continuing his loud nagging.

Lady Dou happened to come out to ask what Li Shimin and Li Xuanba wanted for dinner, only to have them circle around her like she was a pillar.

Lady Dou grabbed each boy by the back of his collar. "Stop circling! You’re making me dizzy! What are you two bickering about now?"

Li Shimin sighed, "It’s Ah-Xuan’s fault. I was just saying a few words to him, and he actually covered his ears and ran away!"

Li Xuanba said, "Long-winded."

As they spoke, they started arguing again.

Seeing her second and third sons bickering over such trivial matters, Lady Dou was left between laughter and tears.

Er-lang and San-lang were too prone to arguing; they fought over small things every day. Sometimes Lady Dou didn't know whether to say they had a good relationship or a bad one.

...

Li Xuanba had not eavesdropped on the conversation between Yang Guang and Su Wei. Their talk was recorded in history books.

As for how such private conversations were recorded by historians, who could say? But Li Xuanba was certain that Su Wei had indeed had that dialogue with Yang Guang.

According to Xue Shou, before his father returned to the capital, Minister Su had written many letters to him. But not long after his father returned to the court, Minister Su seemed quite cold toward him.

Xue Daoheng did not have a good temper. If you were cold to me, I couldn't be bothered to pay attention to you either. And so, their relationship faded.

It was just that Gao Jiong had left the court early to live in seclusion in the capital, so he was unaware of the change in their relationship and still thought they were friends.

Su Wei’s obvious change in attitude clearly had something fishy about it.

Although Li Xuanba had not yet taken Xue Daoheng as his teacher at the time, Xue Shou was already a friend to him and his Second Brother. He knew Xue Daoheng’s fate, and while he didn't think he could change Xue Daoheng’s tendency to offend people, he didn't intend to stand idly by.

Coincidentally, Su Wei was the Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Li Xuanba, having no real official post, was working as a Harmonizer of Rites, making Su Wei his actual superior.

When Li Xuanba spoke with Su Wei, he deliberately discussed the *Classic of Poetry*—the *Classic* was a required subject for ritual and music, so it was not abrupt for them to discuss it.

When Li Xuanba brought up the poem *Fish-Algae*, Su Wei’s expression changed noticeably, and he kindly warned him not to study such poems of remonstrance, as the Emperor did not like them. Li Xuanba then became certain that what was written in the history books was likely true.

He had originally planned to gather more evidence before telling Xue Shou.

Just as his brother said, even if he knew the future was hard to change, since his heart was unsettled, doing something was better than standing by. If the outcome was destined, at least he would have tried, and there would be no lingering regrets.

After taking Xue Daoheng as his teacher, his relationship with him and his Second Brother grew closer, and he became a hidden ally to his and his Second Brother’s other teachers. Li Xuanba then changed his approach, telling Gao Jiong and letting him help.

Compared to Xue Shou, Li Xuanba believed Xue Daoheng would be more likely to listen to Gao Jiong.

Moreover, if Gao Jiong advised Xue Daoheng, Xue Daoheng would not be suspicious and go to confront Su Wei. He wouldn't need to go to great lengths to verify the truth of the matter.

As luck would have it, Xue Daoheng’s friend, Fang Yanqian (father of Fang Qiao), had achieved outstanding results in local governance and, having ranked at the top of the local official assessments, was promoted to the capital as the Inspector of the Secretariat.

As soon as Fang Yanqian returned to the court, before he could even have a proper chat with his son Fang Qiao, who was also in the Eastern Capital, he went to Xue Daoheng’s home to urge him to close his doors to visitors and keep a low profile to avoid disaster.

Fang Yanqian said, "After I returned to the court, I was received by the Emperor. Upon hearing that I was your friend, he asked me many things about you, and his words seemed filled with dissatisfaction. I observe that the Emperor is narrow-minded and not a wise ruler. Xuanqing, you must be careful."

In history, Xue Daoheng had also been advised by Fang Yanqian, but he hadn't taken it to heart.

Xue Daoheng knew he was merely a scholar excluded from the center of power; he had no standing to be feared by the Emperor. Therefore, as long as he did nothing illegal or rebellious, there was no reason for the Emperor to kill him—at most, he would just be sidelined.

But now, having just been told by Gao Jiong about the "calamity of the *Fish-Algae*," and hearing Fang Yanqian’s words, his mood was different.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第63章 请大德说个谶纬
chunks.chineseText:
第63章 请大德说个谶纬

=
　　隋文帝死的时候， 薛道衡正在外地任襄州总管。
　　薛道衡给隋文帝当了多年的秘书，虽然隋文帝让他外放是因为他和当时已经权倾朝野的杨素关系过于亲密，但隋文帝对薛道衡的喜爱不减。
　　隋文帝和薛道衡的君臣感情很深厚， 送薛道衡出京的时候， 君臣二人还垂泪惜别。
　　他们都知道， 以他们当时的年龄，恐怕是很难有下一次见面的机会。
　　杨广继位后，迁薛道衡为潘州刺史。薛道衡已经快七十岁， 当了一年潘州刺史就请求致仕。
　　杨广刚平定汉王杨谅的叛乱，急需老臣支持，没有准许薛道衡致仕， 让薛道衡回中央帮他。
　　在这种背景下，薛道衡回京途中不写一篇歌颂隋文帝的文章是不可能的。
　　首先他与隋文帝君臣感情极其深厚。在隋文帝病逝时， 他没能陪伴在隋文帝身边， 心中一直有遗憾。
　　临近京城的时候，薛道衡身为一个大文人，触景生情后自然就真情流露。
　　再者杨广找薛道衡回京，表现出对他的赏识。按照常理，薛道衡得写点什么来讨好杨广。
　　即使薛道衡不喜杨广的为人， 但杨广都当了皇帝了，薛道衡在朝堂混了这么多年， 基本的情商还是会有的。
　　薛道衡回京城的时候，杨广刚改元，正在父孝中， 除了平定叛乱， 其他什么都还来不及做。
　　文人吹捧皇帝也会讲究一个技巧， 不能尴吹。
　　见到爹吹他儿子优秀， 见到儿子吹他爹优秀，是夸人的常态。别说薛道衡这种很会吹的御用笔杆子，就是寻常百姓人家也是这么做。
　　杨广向来表现得很孝顺。隋文帝刚驾崩不久，薛道衡向杨广呈上一篇吹杨广他爹的文章，这很正常吧？
　　房彦谦是薛道衡的好友，其品行深受薛道衡信任。
　　薛道衡隐瞒了消息的来源，对房彦谦大吐苦水：“先帝刚驾崩，陛下本就应该命人给先帝写颂文，历朝历代都是如此。我见他没有命人写颂文，还以为他是等我回来执笔呢！”
　　房彦谦历经官场城府，自以为心态已经足够平和。听到薛道衡的抱怨后，他也没绷住表情，嘴角一个劲地抽搐。
　　房彦谦面圣的时候察觉了皇帝对薛道衡不满，但他万万没想到，这也能不满。
　　谁会在父孝三年还未过去的时候看到有人写给先父的颂文，居然忌恨写颂文的人？
　　怪不得薛道衡没料到他被皇帝厌恶。实在是薛道衡自以为这次一回京就讨好过了皇帝，主动向皇帝服软。
　　薛道衡和皇帝之前有点小摩擦。
　　他被流放岭南的时候，杨广派人给他送信，让他取道江都，杨广会请旨将他留在江都。
　　薛道衡不想成为杨广的属官，就绕道而行，宁愿去岭南吃苦。
　　但这点摩擦，哪能到杀人的地步？
　　且薛道衡回来的第一件事，就是给还在父孝期间的皇帝写他父亲的颂文，做足了“我现在也是陛下的笔杆子，不用陛下说，我就主动写了”的态度。以前那点小摩擦，理应消除了吧？
　　“就算他还记着当年那件事！也不至于为这件事杀我吧？！”若不是高颎对薛道衡说皇帝对他动了杀心，又告诉他苏威疏远他便是因为此事，薛道衡怎么都不肯相信。
　　历史中他直到被杨广赐死时都不敢置信，还想面圣询问，被杨广派人勒死。
　　薛道衡真是想破脑袋也想不明白，杨广对他坚定不移的杀心究竟哪来的，能让已经退出朝堂漩涡的高颎冒险来提点他，让曾经他的至交好友苏威避开他，连初次见到杨广的房彦谦都能看出杀意。
　　薛道衡越想越委屈，越想越生气。
　　他今年都六十八了，除了坐罪岭南那次，他一辈子都没受过这样的委屈。
　　薛道衡都想破罐子破摔，质问杨广究竟为何如此对待他。如果杨广真的想让他死，不如让他为先帝殉葬，他好向先帝哭诉冤屈。
　　房彦谦使尽浑身解数才把薛道衡劝住。
　　老小老小，薛道衡现在对不平事的忍耐可比年轻时弱多了，就像个耍脾气的小孩。若不是房彦谦让他顾及家中儿孙，薛道衡还真的会跑杨广面前“自爆”。
　　老小孩薛道衡在好友面前几乎哭到晕厥。房彦谦实在是担心，就没有住进房乔为他选好的宅院，暂住薛道衡家中陪伴薛道衡。
　　房乔本来还担心父亲询问怎么得到的宅院。
　　房乔结识李玄霸之后，李玄霸见他生活拮据，就让其以学识在书铺中“参了一股”。他没有名声，文集不好卖。但他匿名写的五经启蒙注疏十分好卖，再加上他常为李玄霸的香皂铺子的广告润笔，润笔费也十分可观。
　　很短的时间，房乔就积攒了一小笔财产。
　　唐国公府虽然被杨广敲打了一番，但放眼整个朝堂，正是处于上升期的勋贵。李玄霸又和齐王杨暕关系很好。听闻房乔的父亲返回朝堂中枢，李玄霸就和齐王杨暕说了一声，杨暕很慷慨地把名下一处没用的房产低价转让给了李玄霸，任由李玄霸送人。
　　杨暕本想直接赠送，李玄霸借口家中兄长来了洛阳，他不宜太高调炫耀与齐王友谊为由，要求行买卖之事。
　　杨暕拍了拍李玄霸的肩膀，接受了李玄霸的借口，然后转头去禁苑狩猎，以李建成抢他猎物为借口，把李建成骂了一顿。
　　杨暕：“大德别怕，表兄为你撑腰！”
　　李玄霸谢过杨暕，思及杨暕的未来，心中长叹一声。
　　他的老师们只要离开朝堂的漩涡，就有极大可能从杨广的魔爪下逃离。但杨暕不可能，因为他是杨广的儿子。
　　还好李玄霸道德感不高，长叹一声后就把杨暕的未来抛之脑后。
　　杨暕的悲剧是杨广造成的，该由他爹负责，我无能为力呀，摊手。
　　房乔没有拒绝李玄霸低价转让的宅子。他本以为那是唐国公府的产业。自己与李世民、李玄霸交好，朋友之间相互帮助正常，不需要矫情。但得知这宅子是李玄霸从齐王手中要的，房乔就有心理负担了。
　　他从李世民、李玄霸这里听到了许多皇帝的不好传闻，知道皇帝猜忌心特别重。自己家可不想和皇子有任何关系，以免皇帝乱想。
　　但宅子已经到手了，房乔也不好退回去，免得齐王得知后以为自己对他不满。
　　朋友都不理解房乔的过分谨慎。
　　这宅子从李玄霸手中过了一遍，房乔连齐王的面都没见过。
　　但房乔还是焦虑，不知道该如何与父亲解释这宅子背后错综复杂的关系。
　　谁知道房彦谦完全忽视了儿子和宅子，一门心思扑在了劝慰好友上。房乔焦虑了这么久，完全没有任何意义。
　　杜如晦带头笑话房乔这个儿子是房伯父捡来的。
　　薛收有些不好意思。毕竟房伯父忽视儿子的原因是自家父亲。
　　长孙无忌和李世民是哪里有笑话就跟着笑，笑得特别大声。
　　李玄霸摇摇头，觉得这几个人明明年龄比自己都大，但真的特别幼稚。
　　房乔想起前段时间焦虑到脸上都上火起了疙瘩，就忍不住恼羞成怒。
　　他私下对李玄霸道：“大德，你可有什么能让杜克明难受，又不会给你招来危险的谶纬？我假装是从其他道士那里听来的，去吓唬杜克明一次。”
　　李玄霸道：“我想想。”
　　难得房乔黑化，居然问他要谶纬吓唬人。
　　现在的房相也还是个坏心眼的年轻人呢。自己一定要满足。
　　李玄霸道：“你要他兄长被杀的谶纬，还是要他儿子被杀的谶纬？”
　　房乔：“……”
　　他捂着胸口退后两步，耳边嗡嗡嗡响。
　　自己虽然问李玄霸要能吓唬到杜克明的谶纬，但他万万没想到，这谶纬居然hi这么吓人！
　　杜克明将来怎么会如此悲惨！
　　李玄霸道：“还不够凄惨吗？那他早逝的谶纬如何？”
　　房乔：“……”
　　他颤颤巍巍躬身连连作揖：“我错了，李三郎，我错了，我再也不问你谶纬了！”
　　李玄霸道：“别害怕，除了早逝这个看运气，未来不知道能不能改变。但他哥和他儿子的未来都很容易更改。”
　　李玄霸顿了顿，道：“比如让杜兄从此修身养性不近女色，只要没有儿子，就不会有儿子被杀。”
　　“咳咳咳咳！”李世民翻窗进来，“阿玄，闭嘴吧，别把玄龄吓出好歹来。”
　　李玄霸早就发觉自家二哥在窗户下面偷听：“哥，我可没有吓唬房兄，是他自己问的。”
　　房乔继续作揖：“我错了，我真的错了，我再也不问了！”
　　自己怎么就嘴欠呢！
　　李世民安慰道：“阿玄说能改，就一定能改，别太担心。谶纬是为了避祸，若因为谶纬而过分焦虑，反而会招来祸事。”
　　被一个孩童教训了，房乔还觉得很有道理，心中十分感慨地虚心听教。
　　“不过，阿玄啊，你能不能改一改那随口透露谶纬的臭毛病？”李世民重重叹了口气，“就算这不会给你身体造成负担，但得知你会谶纬，许多人都可能起窥伺之心。再者，人心难测，说不定你好心让别人避祸，他没有避开，反而怨恨你。”
　　李玄霸道：“放心，我透露谶纬的人，都确定他们不会说出去。”
　　现在能危害他安全的只有杨广。而他透露谶纬的人都与杨广不睦，甚至在杨广的“暗杀名单”上。
　　李玄霸虽是乐子人，但也足够谨慎。
　　“至于怨恨……”李玄霸难得露出一个很明显的微笑，“看到对方怨恨还拿我无可奈何，不是很有趣吗？他们不仅拿我无可奈何，说不准见了我的面还得求我，那就更有趣了。”
　　没有“谶纬”看乐子，李玄霸实在是撑不住这永远处在亚健康状态的身体，和隋唐对于现代人而言不算舒适的生活。
　　就算他自称社会底层，也觉得隋唐贵族的生活实在是不够舒适，连电和网都没有。
　　现在他苟一苟，别说他哥当皇帝，就是李渊当了皇帝，自己会谶纬之能传播出去，李渊都得保住他。
　　他可以随意剧透，随意创死人，那些人在背后谩骂自己，当着面还得对自己说谢谢。
　　不过他不想帮李渊，所以还是等二哥当皇帝后再折腾吧。
　　李世民和房乔面面相觑。
　　他们知道李玄霸不会不谨慎，只是仍旧要叮嘱几句。
　　但他们万万没想到，李玄霸“预言”的原因居然是“有趣”。
　　他们还以为李玄霸是为了“拯救忠良”“跑步进入唐朝”之类非常高大上的原因呢！
　　李世民头疼极了：“阿玄，你改改吧。你如果实在是忍不住，就和我说……和玄龄说也行。我看玄龄接受良好。”
　　房乔：“……告辞。”
　　李世民拉住房乔的衣袖：“你都被我抓住了，可不能跑。我不能一个人被阿玄荼毒。难道你不想拯救杜克明了吗？”
　　房乔：“……”纠结。
　　李世民问道：“阿玄，杜克明儿子的事还早，等他儿子长大了再说，我们先别额外增加心理负担。他兄长的事是怎么回事？”
　　李玄霸道：“天下大乱之后，杜兄的叔父投靠其中一个起兵军阀，他嫉妒杜兄的兄长，进谗言杀了杜兄的兄长。”
　　李世民皱眉：“竟是如此无耻之人？那人被我杀了吗？”
　　房乔看了李世民一眼。
　　李玄霸摊手：“没呢。本来杜淹按罪该死，但杜楚客说杜淹虽然杀了兄长，就算没有杀兄长这件事也该死，但杜兄不肯救杜淹，就是让杜家骨肉自相残杀。杜兄被迫醒悟感动，向二哥请求赦免杜淹。”
　　李世民和房乔都露出了嫌弃的神情。
　　李玄霸疑惑：“你们嫌弃什么？之后你们都可喜欢杜淹了。房兄，杜淹入朝为官是你举荐的，二哥，你之后还让杜淹参议朝政大事。”
　　李世民和房乔脸色一僵。
　　李世民疯狂摇头：“你说什么？我不是我没有！你的谶纬向来不准，你谶纬中看到的那个人和我没关系！我才不会这样！”
　　房乔也连连摆手：“不可能不可能，这样品德低下的人，还和杜克明有深仇，我怎么会做这种事。”
　　李玄霸再次摊手：“你觉得我会骗你们吗？”
　　李世民和房乔：“……”
　　李世民转头对房乔道：“玄龄，你看，我说的对吧？谶纬这事真的没必要太过在意。”
　　房乔严肃道：“没错，不用在意。”
　　李世民道：“谶纬算什么？我们绝对比谶纬中厉害。”
　　房乔道：“未来有很多可能，谶纬一定是最坏的一条，不应该当作真正的未来。”
　　李玄霸听二哥和房玄龄疯狂自欺欺人找补，露出了开心的笑容。

Chapter 63: Asking the Great Virtuous One for a Prophecy

When Emperor Wen of Sui passed away, Xue Daoheng was serving as the Governor of Xiangzhou, away from the capital.
Xue Daoheng had served as a secretary to Emperor Wen for many years. Although the Emperor had sent him away because of his overly close relationship with Yang Su—who at the time held power over the entire court—the Emperor’s affection for Xue Daoheng had never waned.
The bond between Emperor Wen and Xue Daoheng was profound. When the Emperor sent Xue Daoheng out of the capital, the two had wept as they bid each other farewell.
They both knew that, given their ages, it was unlikely they would ever have the chance to meet again.
After Yang Guang ascended the throne, he transferred Xue Daoheng to be the Prefect of Panzhou. Xue Daoheng was already nearly seventy years old; after serving as Prefect for one year, he requested to retire.
Yang Guang, having just quelled the rebellion of Yang Liang, the Prince of Han, was in desperate need of support from veteran officials. He denied Xue Daoheng’s request to retire and ordered him to return to the central government to assist him.
Against this backdrop, it was impossible for Xue Daoheng not to write a piece praising Emperor Wen on his way back to the capital.
Firstly, his emotional bond with Emperor Wen was extremely deep. When the Emperor passed away, he had not been by his side, a regret that had weighed on him ever since.
As he neared the capital, Xue Daoheng, being a great man of letters, naturally let his true feelings flow when moved by the scenery.
Furthermore, Yang Guang had summoned him back to the capital, showing him favor. By all logic, Xue Daoheng had to write something to curry favor with Yang Guang.
Even if Xue Daoheng disliked Yang Guang’s character, Yang Guang was now the Emperor. Having spent so many years in the imperial court, Xue Daoheng possessed at least a basic level of emotional intelligence.
When Xue Daoheng returned to the capital, Yang Guang had just changed the reign title and was still in the period of mourning for his father. Aside from quelling the rebellion, he had not yet had time to do anything else.
Scholars also have their techniques for flattering an Emperor; one cannot simply praise him awkwardly.
Seeing a father and praising the excellence of his son, or seeing a son and praising the excellence of his father, is the standard way to offer compliments. Not to mention a master of the pen like Xue Daoheng, even ordinary folk would do the same.
Yang Guang had always presented himself as a filial son. With Emperor Wen having passed away not long ago, was it not perfectly normal for Xue Daoheng to present an article praising Yang Guang’s father?
Fang Yanqian was a close friend of Xue Daoheng, and his character was deeply trusted by him.
Xue Daoheng concealed the source of his information and poured out his grievances to Fang Yanqian: "The late Emperor has just passed away. His Majesty should have ordered someone to write a eulogy for him; this has been the custom through every dynasty. I saw that he hadn't ordered anyone to write one, so I assumed he was waiting for my return to take up the brush!"
Fang Yanqian, having weathered the complexities of officialdom, believed his own composure was sufficient. Yet, upon hearing Xue Daoheng’s complaint, he could not maintain his expression; the corners of his mouth twitched uncontrollably.
When Fang Yanqian had an audience with the Emperor, he had sensed the Emperor’s dissatisfaction with Xue Daoheng, but he never imagined that *this* could also be a cause for resentment.
Who, while still in the three-year mourning period for their father, would see someone write a eulogy for the late Emperor and actually harbor hatred toward the author?
No wonder Xue Daoheng had not anticipated that the Emperor loathed him. It was truly because Xue Daoheng believed he had already pleased the Emperor upon his return to the capital, having taken the initiative to show his submission.
There had been a minor friction between Xue Daoheng and the Emperor before.
When he was exiled to Lingnan, Yang Guang had sent someone to deliver a letter, telling him to take the route through Jiangdu, where Yang Guang would petition to have him kept there.
Xue Daoheng did not want to become a subordinate official to Yang Guang, so he took a detour, preferring to suffer in Lingnan.
But how could such a minor friction reach the point of killing someone?
Moreover, the first thing Xue Daoheng did upon returning was to write a eulogy for the Emperor’s father while the Emperor was still in mourning, fully performing the attitude of, "I am now also your loyal scribe, Your Majesty; I wrote this without you even having to ask." That bit of past friction should have been erased, right?
"Even if he still remembers that incident! It shouldn't be enough to kill me over it, right?!" If Gao Jiong had not told Xue Daoheng that the Emperor had murderous intent toward him, and that Su Wei was distancing himself precisely because of this, Xue Daoheng would never have believed it.
In history, he remained in disbelief even until the moment Yang Guang ordered his execution, still wanting to see the Emperor to ask why, only to be strangled by the men Yang Guang sent.
Xue Daoheng racked his brains but could not understand where Yang Guang’s unwavering murderous intent came from—enough to make Gao Jiong, who had already retreated from the whirlpool of the court, risk his life to warn him; enough to make his once-closest friend Su Wei avoid him; and enough for even Fang Yanqian, who had met Yang Guang for the first time, to perceive the killing intent.
The more Xue Daoheng thought about it, the more aggrieved and angry he became.
He was sixty-eight years old this year. Aside from the time he was convicted and sent to Lingnan, he had never suffered such grievances in his entire life.
Xue Daoheng even wanted to give up on everything and demand to know why Yang Guang treated him this way. If Yang Guang truly wanted him dead, he might as well let him be buried with the late Emperor, so he could weep and plead his grievances before the late Emperor’s spirit.
It took all of Fang Yanqian’s efforts to persuade Xue Daoheng to calm down.
An old man is like a child; Xue Daoheng’s tolerance for injustice was far weaker now than in his youth, and he acted like a child throwing a tantrum. If not for Fang Yanqian urging him to consider his children and grandchildren at home, Xue Daoheng might really have run to Yang Guang to "self-destruct."
The "old child" Xue Daoheng almost cried himself into a faint in front of his friend. Fang Yanqian was so worried that he did not move into the residence Fang Qiao had selected for him, but instead stayed at Xue Daoheng’s home to keep him company.
Fang Qiao had originally been worried about his father asking how he had obtained the residence.
After Fang Qiao became acquainted with Li Xuanba, Li Xuanba saw that he was living in straitened circumstances and allowed him to "take a share" in a bookstore using his scholarship. Fang Qiao had no fame, so his literary collections did not sell well. However, the annotations and commentaries on the Five Classics he wrote anonymously sold very well. Added to that, he often polished advertisements for Li Xuanba’s soap shop, and the fees for his writing were quite substantial.
In a very short time, Fang Qiao had accumulated a small fortune.
Although the Tang Duke’s mansion had been given a warning by Yang Guang, looking at the entire court, they were still a noble family on the rise. Li Xuanba also had a very good relationship with the Prince of Qi, Yang Ji. Hearing that Fang Qiao’s father was returning to the center of the court, Li Xuanba mentioned it to Prince Yang Ji. Yang Ji generously transferred a vacant property under his name to Li Xuanba at a low price, leaving it to Li Xuanba to give away.
Yang Ji had wanted to give it as a gift directly, but Li Xuanba used the excuse that his elder brother had come to Luoyang and it would be inappropriate for him to show off his friendship with the Prince of Qi too ostentatiously, insisting on a transaction.
Yang Ji patted Li Xuanba on the shoulder, accepted the excuse, and then turned to go hunting in the Forbidden Garden, where he scolded Li Jiancheng on the pretext that he had snatched his prey.
Yang Ji: "Da De, don't be afraid! Your cousin will back you up!"
Li Xuanba thanked Yang Ji, but thinking of Yang Ji’s future, he let out a long sigh in his heart.
His teachers could escape Yang Guang’s clutches as long as they left the whirlpool of the court. But Yang Ji could not, because he was Yang Guang’s son.
Fortunately, Li Xuanba did not have a high sense of morality; after a long sigh, he cast Yang Ji’s future to the back of his mind.
Yang Ji’s tragedy was caused by Yang Guang; his father should be responsible for it. I am powerless, he thought, shrugging.
Fang Qiao did not refuse the residence Li Xuanba transferred at a low price. He had originally thought it was property of the Tang Duke’s mansion. He was on good terms with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba; friends helping each other was normal, and there was no need to be overly modest. But upon learning that the house was something Li Xuanba had obtained from the Prince of Qi, Fang Qiao felt a psychological burden.
He had heard many unfavorable rumors about the Emperor from Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, and he knew the Emperor was particularly suspicious. His family did not want to have any connection with the imperial princes, lest the Emperor let his imagination run wild.
But the house was already in his hands, and Fang Qiao could not return it, lest the Prince of Qi think he was dissatisfied with him.
His friends did not understand Fang Qiao’s excessive caution.
The house had passed through Li Xuanba’s hands, and Fang Qiao had never even met the Prince of Qi.
Yet Fang Qiao remained anxious, not knowing how to explain the intricate relationships behind the house to his father.
Who would have thought that Fang Yanqian would completely ignore his son and the house, focusing all his attention on comforting his friend? Fang Qiao’s anxiety for so long had been completely meaningless.
Du Ruhui took the lead in joking that Fang Qiao was a son picked up by Uncle Fang.
Xue Shou felt a bit embarrassed. After all, the reason Uncle Fang ignored his son was because of his own father.
Zhangsun Wuji and Li Shimin followed wherever there was a joke, laughing especially loudly.
Li Xuanba shook his head, thinking that although these people were all older than him, they were truly exceptionally childish.
Fang Qiao recalled how he had been so anxious recently that he had broken out in acne, and he couldn't help but feel a mix of shame and anger.
He said to Li Xuanba in private: "Da De, do you have any prophecies that could make Du Keming uncomfortable without bringing danger to yourself? I will pretend I heard them from other Taoists and go scare Du Keming once."
Li Xuanba said: "Let me think."
It was rare for Fang Qiao to have a dark side, actually asking him for a prophecy to scare someone.
The future Prime Minister Fang was still a mischievous young man. He must satisfy him.
Li Xuanba said: "Do you want a prophecy about his elder brother being killed, or one about his son being killed?"
Fang Qiao: "..."
He clutched his chest and took two steps back, his ears buzzing.
Although he had asked Li Xuanba for a prophecy that could scare Du Keming, he never expected the prophecy to be so terrifying!
How could Du Keming’s future be so miserable!
Li Xuanba said: "Not miserable enough? Then how about a prophecy of his early death?"
Fang Qiao: "..."
He bowed tremblingly and repeatedly: "I was wrong, Third Young Master Li, I was wrong! I will never ask you for a prophecy again!"
Li Xuanba said: "Don't be afraid. Except for early death, which depends on luck, the future might not be unchangeable. But the futures of his brother and his son are very easy to change."
Li Xuanba paused and said: "For example, let Brother Du cultivate his character and abstain from women from now on. As long as he has no son, there will be no son to be killed."
"Cough, cough, cough, cough!" Li Shimin climbed in through the window. "A-Xuan, shut up. Don't scare Xuanling into a bad state."
Li Xuanba had long noticed his second brother eavesdropping under the window: "Brother, I wasn't scaring Brother Fang; he asked for it himself."
Fang Qiao continued to bow: "I was wrong, I was really wrong, I will never ask again!"
Why did he have to have such a loose tongue!
Li Shimin comforted him: "If A-Xuan says it can be changed, it can definitely be changed. Don't worry too much. Prophecies are meant to avoid disaster; if one becomes overly anxious because of a prophecy, it will instead invite disaster."
Being lectured by a child, Fang Qiao felt it made perfect sense and listened with great humility, feeling deeply moved.
"However, A-Xuan, can you break that bad habit of casually revealing prophecies?" Li Shimin sighed heavily. "Even if this doesn't cause a burden on your body, many people might harbor covetous intentions once they know you can prophesy. Furthermore, the human heart is unpredictable. Perhaps you mean well by helping others avoid disaster, but if they fail to avoid it, they might resent you instead."
Li Xuanba said: "Don't worry, the people I reveal prophecies to are all people I am certain will not speak of it."
The only person who could endanger his safety now was Yang Guang. And the people to whom he revealed prophecies were all at odds with Yang Guang, or even on Yang Guang’s "assassination list."
Although Li Xuanba was a prankster, he was cautious enough.
"As for resentment..." Li Xuanba gave a rare, very obvious smile. "Isn't it interesting to see the other party resent me but be unable to do anything about it? Not only can they do nothing to me, but they might even have to beg me when they see me—that would be even more interesting."
Without "prophecies" to amuse himself, Li Xuanba could not endure this body that was always in a sub-health state, nor the life in the Sui and Tang dynasties that was not comfortable for a modern person.
Even if he claimed to be at the bottom of society, he felt that the life of the Sui and Tang nobility was truly not comfortable enough—there wasn't even electricity or the internet.
For now, he would just lay low. Even if his brother became Emperor, or even if Li Yuan became Emperor, as long as his ability to prophesy spread, Li Yuan would have to protect him.
He could spoil the plot at will, drive people crazy at will, and those people would have to curse him behind his back while saying "thank you" to his face.
However, he didn't want to help Li Yuan, so he would wait until his second brother became Emperor before causing trouble.
Li Shimin and Fang Qiao looked at each other.
They knew Li Xuanba wouldn't be imprudent, but they still had to urge him a few times.
But they never expected that the reason for Li Xuanba’s "prophecies" was simply "for fun."
They had thought Li Xuanba was doing it for high-minded reasons like "saving the loyal and virtuous" or "running toward the Tang Dynasty"!
Li Shimin had a splitting headache: "A-Xuan, change your ways. If you really can't help it, tell me... or tell Xuanling. I see Xuanling accepts it quite well."
Fang Qiao: "...Farewell."
Li Shimin grabbed Fang Qiao’s sleeve: "You’ve been caught by me, you can't run. I can't be the only one poisoned by A-Xuan. Don't you want to save Du Keming?"
Fang Qiao: "..." Struggling.
Li Shimin asked: "A-Xuan, the matter of Du Keming’s son is still far off. Let’s wait until his son grows up to talk about it; let’s not add extra psychological burden for now. What’s going on with his elder brother?"
Li Xuanba said: "After the world fell into chaos, Brother Du’s uncle defected to one of the warlords who had raised an army. He was jealous of Brother Du’s elder brother and slandered him, leading to his brother’s death."
Li Shimin frowned: "Such a shameless person? Did I kill him?"
Fang Qiao glanced at Li Shimin.
Li Xuanba shrugged: "Not yet. Originally, Du Yan deserved to die for his crimes, but Du Chuke said that although Du Yan killed his brother, he deserved to die even without that incident. However, Brother Du refused to save Du Yan, which would have meant the Du family killing their own flesh and blood. Brother Du was forced to wake up and was moved, so he requested that the Second Brother pardon Du Yan."
Li Shimin and Fang Qiao both showed expressions of disgust.
Li Xuanba was puzzled: "Why are you disgusted? You both end up liking Du Yan very much later. Brother Fang, it was you who recommended Du Yan to be an official in the court. Second Brother, you even let Du Yan participate in the discussion of major state affairs later."
Li Shimin and Fang Qiao’s faces stiffened.
Li Shimin shook his head frantically: "What are you saying? It wasn't me, I didn't! Your prophecies are always inaccurate; that person you saw in your prophecy has nothing to do with me! I would never do such a thing!"
Fang Qiao also waved his hands repeatedly: "Impossible, impossible. Such a person of low character, and one who has a deep feud with Du Keming—how could I do such a thing?"
Li Xuanba shrugged again: "Do you think I would lie to you?"
Li Shimin and Fang Qiao: "..."
Li Shimin turned to Fang Qiao and said: "Xuanling, look, I was right, wasn't I? There is really no need to take these prophecies too seriously."
Fang Qiao said solemnly: "That's right, no need to care."
Li Shimin said: "What is a prophecy? We are definitely more capable than what is in the prophecy."
Fang Qiao said: "The future has many possibilities. A prophecy must be the worst-case scenario and should not be treated as the true future."
Li Xuanba listened to his second brother and Fang Xuanling frantically deceiving themselves to make up for it, and he revealed a happy smile.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第64章 又一个老师修书
chunks.chineseText:
第64章 又一个老师修书

=
　　薛道衡年纪确实大了， 又没有高颎和宇文弼看得开，即使有好友陪伴，也抑郁成疾， 卧病不起。
　　李玄霸吓了一跳。
　　他不会一番“剧透”， 薛道衡比原定历史还早死几年吧？
　　更让李玄霸惊吓的是， 房彦谦因过于担心薛道衡，像对待亲人一样照顾老友。他年纪也不小了，竟也劳累成疾。
　　房彦谦会死在大唐建立前， 但不是现在啊。不会房彦谦也比原定历史早死几年吧？
　　李玄霸挠挠头，心虚。
　　薛道衡虽然还没有开始教导他，但杨广已经定下了他和薛道衡的师徒名分， 薛道衡又是朋友薛收的生父，李玄霸和李世民理应前去探望。
　　房彦谦也病倒了， 与薛道衡在同一个房间里养病， 两个老人还能聊聊天。李世民和李玄霸顺带探望了房彦谦。
　　房乔很尴尬地住进了薛府，照顾生病的父亲。
　　薛道衡的老妻对房乔很愧疚。
　　自家老头莫名其妙生气病倒，连累了刚回京的老友不说，老头还不准家里人贴身照顾，居然让老友的儿子来照顾他。
　　如果不是薛道衡正病着， 薛道衡的老妻都想和薛道衡打一架。
　　老薛你要脸不！
　　老夫人愧疚道：“玄龄啊，这次真的对不住。”
　　房乔忙道：“没有没有， 这是我应该做的。”
　　他有点疑惑，为何父亲和薛伯父只让自己侍疾。
　　侍疾几日后，房乔明白了。
　　薛伯父和父亲私下里老是嘀咕皇帝的坏话。薛伯父的其他儿子都有官身， 恐怕听不得这些。于是只能让自己这个赋闲在家的人被荼毒了。
　　说是亲手侍疾， 杂事其实都有仆人做， 房彦谦和薛道衡又没到病得起不了身的地步， 所以房乔并不劳累。
　　他甚至怀疑，自家父亲和薛伯父那精神的模样，病是不是装出来的。
　　李玄霸和李世民来探望两位老人的时候，也悄悄交头接耳嘀咕。
　　李玄霸：【吓死我了，我还以为我弄巧成拙了。】
　　李世民抚着胸口顺气，不住点头。
　　李玄霸：【气死我了，我要不要给他们剧透点什么？】
　　李世民捂住李玄霸的嘴。
　　房乔：“……”
　　以前看到李玄霸什么都没说，李世民却捂住李玄霸的嘴的时候，房乔一头雾水。现在他不一头雾水了，只想也把李玄霸的嘴捂住。
　　但同时他又很好奇。
　　房乔趁着李玄霸如厕，悄悄问李世民：“李二郎，李三郎想说什么？”
　　李世民露出不属于他这个年龄的疲惫：“他还没说。我劝你别太好奇。”
　　房乔苦笑：“我知道应该别好奇，就是忍不住。”
　　李世民道：“我当年也是这样，被阿玄折腾了几年，现在已经能管住好奇心了。我不劝你，劝也劝不住。你去找阿玄问问，很快就能制止住好奇心。去吧。”
　　房乔：“……”说什么当年？你现在才几岁？
　　看着李世民如此沧桑的模样，房乔管住了自己的好奇心，这次没有主动撞上去被创。
　　但李世民被创了。
　　李玄霸还是忍不住，在心里对二哥叨叨：【我本来想，如果薛老师因杨广的猜忌失去了求生欲，就告诉他薛收英年早逝，让他为了看好薛收，把求生欲找回来。】
　　李世民抹了一把脸，眼神平静无波。
　　自己好惨啊。
　　别人不想听可以捂耳朵，自己再怎么捂住心口，也逃脱不了弟弟的“奇袭”。
　　他真的不想刚结交朋友，就得知朋友英年早逝的惨事。
　　于是李世民决定去迫害房乔。
　　李世民语速极快道：“玄龄啊，你之前不是好奇阿玄想说什么吗？他说薛收英年早逝。”
　　迫不及防被未来主公背刺的房乔：“……”
　　房乔深呼吸，十分不解地找到李玄霸，悄悄道：“李三郎，怎么又是英年早逝？难道我也是？你给个痛快吧，免得我老想。”
　　李玄霸摇头：“没啊，你好好的。哦，你要好好照顾你父亲，争取让你父亲看到你为相的那一日。”
　　房乔先心梗，然后叹了口气。
　　他差点以为自己没有英年早逝，父亲英年早逝。但很快他回过神，父亲年纪已经不小了，随时都可能老病而去。
　　生老病死，人之常情，虽然自己提前得知父亲的寿命，心有不甘，但也无可奈何。
　　房乔道：“大德，我想我能控制住好奇心了。”
　　他此刻深刻认识到了李玄霸能看到未来的心理压力。
　　有些事能改变，有些事无法改变。这些事压在李玄霸的心中，不知道有多沉重。
　　若是自己面临未来许多不可更改的事带来的压力，恐怕会郁结难解。
　　幸亏李玄霸还有个双生兄长，可以纾解一下心理压力，自己心胸也开阔。这样一想，李玄霸的一些恶趣味也能接受了。
　　李玄霸点头：“看，多听听就免疫了。你还想听……”
　　房乔掩面而走。
　　他错了，他还是不能接受李玄霸的恶趣味。
　　李玄霸捧腹大笑，被出门遛弯的薛道衡撞见，狠狠敲了脑袋。
　　薛道衡生气道：“我正生病，你身为弟子，怎么还大笑？”
　　敲完李玄霸的脑袋后，薛道衡和房彦谦继续在庭院里散步。
　　李玄霸：“……”他真的考虑要不要向薛道衡剧透了。
　　薛道衡年纪大了，他担心薛道衡受不住，所以父债子还，将来找薛收收债吧。
　　得知薛道衡和房彦谦的“病倒”半真半假后，李玄霸就没有再关注装病的两老头。
　　每次去探望薛道衡，薛道衡都要教训他，不知道什么毛病。
　　薛收却很羡慕李玄霸。
　　薛收也没有官职在身，本想来照顾父亲，但被薛道衡以“你年幼经不住事”拒绝了。
　　李玄霸和李世民都可以经常去探望父亲，他却不行。
　　听闻父亲常教训李玄霸，薛收心里酸溜溜的。
　　薛收对李玄霸道：“大约是我被过继的缘故，父亲总是对我很客气，从不训斥我。父亲对李三你如此亲近，真让我羡慕。”
　　李玄霸安慰道：“放心，等你父亲病好之后，我一定想办法让他对你亲近起来。”
　　薛收以为李玄霸开玩笑安慰他，也开玩笑道：“好，一言为定。”
　　房乔和李世民露出一言难尽的神情。
　　薛弟薛兄不要落入李三阿玄的圈套啊！
　　杜如晦和长孙无忌对视了一眼。以前只是李二郎和李三郎有秘密瞒着他们，因为李二郎和李三郎是兄弟，他们就没在意。
　　现在房玄龄也有了秘密，他们就“不满”了。
　　年轻人有时候总会在莫名其妙的地方有胜负心。杜如晦和长孙无忌原本性格不怎么合拍，所以友谊也是淡淡。现在两人站在了“同一个战线”上，决定把房乔的秘密挖出来，关系亲近了不少。
　　既然李二郎和李三郎能把秘密告诉房乔，就证明他们这帮朋友也应该有资格知道。
　　杜如晦：他们一定是认为我后认识他们，才没告诉我。
　　长孙无忌：他们一定认为我不如房兄成熟，才没告诉我。
　　两人决定，想办法把房乔知道的秘密挖出来。
　　杜如晦和长孙无忌悄悄“合谋”，只有薛收还被蒙在鼓里。
　　一个小团体分裂成了几波，薛收是真正被“孤立”的，但他却一无所知，每日傻呵呵的。
　　李世民觉察到了朋友间的暗潮涌动，悄悄与李玄霸分享。
　　李玄霸：“是让我把他们拉进我们的谶纬小团体，还是看他们‘内斗’的笑话？”
　　李世民坏笑：“你告诉他们谶纬也是看笑话，看他们‘内斗’也是看笑话，先看完‘内斗’的笑话，再看‘谶纬’的笑话，不是更有趣吗？”
　　李玄霸对二哥竖起大拇指。看来在恶趣味方面，自己对比二哥也还是个弟弟，还需要更加努力！
　　李世民背着手，矜持颔首。哪里哪里，一般一般，别说的我像个恶人似的。
　　李玄霸这边继续过着无忧无虑的日常生活。杨广那里因为薛道衡的生病起了一点小波澜。
　　薛道衡的病对外称是他与房彦谦旧友重逢，接连贪杯几日，酒醉后就窝在花丛中睡觉着凉所致，颇有魏晋名士之风的病因。
　　听闻薛道衡的病因，杨广哭笑不得，对苏威道：“听闻你也是薛道衡老友，他真的如此不在意身体吗？这么大年纪了，还醉卧花间？”
　　苏威恭敬道：“薛道衡年轻时便贪杯，性格又洒脱。虽然现在他年纪大了，但也本性难改。”果然如高颎所料，陛下会问我此事。
　　他想起高颎的拜访，心里又气又愧。
　　高颎来到洛阳后，依次拜访曾经旧友，与旧友们小聚一番。
　　虽然杨广忌惮高颎，但高颎已经退隐修书，对待他比以前恭敬许多。杨广自诩心胸广阔，没有连高颎访友也猜忌。他询问了探子，得知高颎只是和老友们聊些陈芝麻烂谷子的旧事，吹一吹年轻时的峥嵘岁月，就不再关注高颎访友之事。
　　太子说得对，高颎已经从朝堂退下，现在无权无势，想与谁串联，别人也不会理睬他。自己的皇位又已经很稳固，不用再关注这个已经离开朝堂的风烛残年的糟老头。
　　苏威也是高颎的旧友。高颎自然拜访了苏威。
　　高颎受杨广忌惮厌恶，苏威想疏远高颎。但高颎都亲自上门拜访了，他不可能把高颎赶出去，只能客气接待。
　　高颎与苏威聊了许多往事，特别说起苏威在先帝时因结党营私被免官的那段时日，感慨道：“君如今谨小慎微，闭门谢客，连旧友也很少联系，这很机敏。”
　　苏威叹气：“算是吃一堑长一智了。”
　　高颎道：“曾经我意气用事，年老后才后悔，幸得陛下心胸宽广，能容忍我退隐朝堂，藏身书丛。”
　　苏威拈须颔首：“公急流勇退，有大智慧。”
　　高颎苦笑着摇摇头：“算不上有大智慧，只是看透了一些事。”
　　高颎长叹了一口气，继续道：“我在身居高位的时候，总认为朋友之间会肝胆相照。后来自己虎落平阳，才知道冷眼旁观，不落井下石就算尽了朋友之谊。我该早些醒悟。”
　　苏威本想继续颔首，突然察觉到高颎这话似乎意有所指，狐疑地看向高颎。
　　高颎没有继续这个话题，道：“薛玄卿年老多病，也想致仕了。”
　　跪坐在坐榻上的高颎双手伏地，躬身顿首。
　　在苏威的愕然中，高颎起身离开坐榻，下地告辞。没有等苏威回应，他就拂袖离开。
　　刚才他有多恭敬，现在就有多冷漠。
　　苏威和高颎都是人老成精的人。高颎什么都没说，但又什么都说了。
　　高颎没有指责苏威什么，苏威脸上却燥着慌。
　　他心里埋怨，高颎和薛道衡招惹陛下雷霆之怒，自己整日忐忑，担心被连累。这二人不知道反省，反倒埋怨起自己没有尽到朋友的情谊。
　　但当杨广问起薛道衡的事时，苏威还是帮薛道衡遮掩了一二。
　　薛道衡可能真的是病了，但肯定不是因为喝酒着凉生病。他定是知道了陛下对他的怨言，心中愤懑成疾。
　　若陛下得知此事，薛道衡肯定会获罪，所以高颎才会来拜访自己。
　　苏威心里道，希望薛道衡这次真的能致仕，别以后再给他找麻烦。
　　杨广听了苏威的话，确信薛道衡是真的老了。
　　于是在薛道衡再次请求致仕的时候，杨广准许了薛道衡的请求，但没有让薛道衡离开朝堂，而是让薛道衡也和高颎、宇文弼一起修书。
　　太子的劝说杨广听了进去。
　　此等老臣，用了不放心；但若不厚待，又会伤朝堂其他臣子的心。不如遣去修书，既远离朝堂权力，又能人尽其用。
　　杨广什么事都想做到最好。被人说动修书之后，他就要修一部前无古人的全书。
　　高颎、宇文弼和薛道衡这样的人他不放心用，甚至放在身边都觉得难受。但他们确实才华横溢，遣去为自己修书，的确正合适。
　　有了太子这层缓冲，杨广终于又放过了一个令他厌恶的老臣。他免掉薛道衡司隶大夫的官职，让薛道衡也成功退去修书了。
　　薛道衡得到圣旨后，心头的巨石落下。
　　他赶紧让家中老妻迅速卖掉在洛阳的家产，搬迁至大兴城，远离皇帝的视线。
　　“孝冲，若陛下对你也心生不满，你也自请来修书吧。”薛道衡离开洛阳前，对挚友房彦谦道，“你的性格，大概也不会受陛下喜欢。”
　　房彦谦道：“我的性格确实不合陛下的意。但我官职卑微，陛下不会太在意我，顶多再次贬官外放而已。玄卿不必担心。”
　　薛道衡叹气：“我已经老了，心气不足，只想全身而退。但你还年轻，是该再努力一番。若你我这等人全离开了朝堂，这大隋……”
　　薛道衡的话说到一半，思及杨广对他的杀意，将后半句话咽了下去。
　　他心中唏嘘。自己躲过一次杀身之祸后，性子也不像之前那样肆意了，唉。
　　此时薛道衡对苏威的明哲保身有一点释然了。
　　人皆自私，自保才是第一要务。如高颎、房彦谦这等不畏惧皇帝，前来提醒自己的人很珍贵。但其他人若先想着自保，自己也不应该责怪他们。
　　自己惹来杀身之祸是自己的事，怎么能责怪别人？
　　薛道衡离开洛阳前，给苏威写了首赠别诗，以此诗告诉苏威，自己不在意苏威的冷漠。多年的老友，以后若有机会，再一起喝酒聊天吧。
　　他主动缓和与苏威的关系。
　　苏威看到了薛道衡的诗后，独自喝了一盅冷酒，心中很是怅然。
　　他此刻对薛道衡差点祸及自己的埋怨消失，开始怀念过往的友谊。
　　苏威回了薛道衡一首诗，恢复了与薛道衡的联络。
　　两人的友谊似乎回到了过去。
　　大概吧。
　　……
　　高颎把阶段性稿子呈给杨广之后，没有多停留，很快回了大兴。
　　宇文弼病愈之后也张罗着搬家。
　　他的老家就在洛阳，原本不想离开故乡。但他见薛道衡都搬到了大兴，细思之后，还是下定决心离开自幼生长的老家。
　　避开陛下的视线，保住家人，才是最重要的事。
　　高颎、宇文弼和薛道衡先后离开了洛阳。离开时，他们给李世民、李玄霸留下大量作业。
　　李渊见状，对二儿子、三儿子道：“可惜你们年幼，还离不开父母。否则你们应该回大兴，跟随三位名师继续完成学业。”
　　李世民道：“我不年幼了，现在完全可以回长安！”
　　李渊不开心了：“什么？你居然这么想离开耶耶和娘娘？”
　　李世民抱怨道：“耶耶，是你先说的。耶耶你好幼稚啊。”
　　李渊捶了李世民的脑袋一下，对李玄霸道：“你也想离开洛阳继续求学吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“我现在还有陛下安排的事务在身，不能离开。若要回大兴，至少得明年。不过我担心二哥太过想念父亲和母亲，自己躲在被子里偷偷哭泣。”
　　李渊哈哈大笑，对李世民道：“看，还是大德了解你。”
　　李世民抱着手臂，抬着下巴道：“我绝对不会哭。再说了，如果我实在想念耶耶和娘娘，就回洛阳来见耶耶和娘娘。”
　　李世民和李玄霸都表示自己可以独自待在大兴，但李渊只感慨了一声，没有任何将两个孩子送往大兴城的意思。
　　李世民和李玄霸确实还小，还没成婚，李渊一点都不相信两个孩子能独自生活。
　　李世民悄悄对李玄霸吐槽：“明明是耶耶离不开我们，非说我们离不开他们。”
　　李玄霸点头，心里叹气。现在的李渊确实特别疼爱他们，不舍得与他们分别。
　　高颎、宇文弼从书信中得知，李渊曾开玩笑让李世民和李玄霸单独居住在大兴之事后，非常生气。
　　求学可以通过书信。李世民和李玄霸都是很聪明的人，不需要日日授课，只要隔段时间检查一下功课即可。
　　年幼的孩子应该留在父母身边。若李渊真的把李世民和李玄霸单独丢到大兴城，高颎和宇文弼一定会亲自来洛阳一趟，把不慈的李渊狠狠骂一顿。
　　……
　　薛道衡去了大兴城之后，薛收仍旧留在洛阳。
　　他法理上只是薛道衡的侄子。虽然他的养父母已经去世，也要守着养父母的家业。
　　好不容易与父母团聚，父母又去了大兴，把他独自留在了洛阳。薛收最近心情很是郁闷。
　　还好有志同道合的友人陪伴左右，纾解了薛收心中的烦闷。
　　因房彦谦在朝中做官，杨广在哪，房彦谦就要待在哪。房乔要照顾父亲，自然继续留在了洛阳。
　　他回大兴一趟，把妻子接了过来，暂时在洛阳安了家。
　　杜如晦见好友都在洛阳，便也让妻子搬来洛阳小住。
　　不久后，长孙晟把高夫人和幼女都接到了身边，只让年长已经做官的儿子留在大兴。长孙无忌也能长留洛阳。
　　好友几人在洛阳常常结伴同游，又认识了一些酒肉朋友，很是快活。
　　李玄霸陪着李世民出游几次之后，就懒得再应酬，与在大兴城时一样独自宅在家中。
　　李世民劝了几次后，李玄霸开始装病，他只能作罢。
　　杜如晦对李玄霸开玩笑道：“看来你是嫌弃我们了。”
　　李玄霸认真道：“谁打扰我休息，我就嫌弃谁。”
　　杜如晦失笑，也不再劝李玄霸出游。
　　他们每隔几日，只这几人聚一次，才会邀请李玄霸同往。
　　李世民虽才垂髫，与勋贵子弟交往多了，也很快在洛阳打出了好名声。
　　李玄霸原本名声比李世民大，后来因为常不出门，名声逐渐减弱。洛阳人再次谈论起李玄霸的病弱，不再羡慕嫉妒李玄霸在杨广那里得到的宠爱。
　　杨广曾多次召李玄霸进宫陪他写词听曲。李玄霸扎扎实实地病了几次后，杨广便也不再频繁召见李玄霸了。
　　他对萧皇后叹息：“大德样样都好，就是这身体令人忧心。若他身体更好些，朕肯定会让他留在宫中抚养。”
　　萧皇后很是赞同。
　　别看李玄霸平时对人很冷淡，但对她和陛下的每句话都能讨人欢心。让这样的孩子留在身边，心情一定特别愉快。
　　可惜李玄霸那身子啊。
　　杨广评论李玄霸的话不知道被谁传了出去。
　　这话传来传去就变了味。外人传言，陛下从御医那里得知李玄霸命不久矣。
　　窦夫人气得胸闷头疼。
　　李玄霸得知此事后摇摇头，安慰母亲不要介意。
　　那些人不过是嫉妒他，酸言酸语罢了。自己现在活得好好的，就是生病也不过是头疼脑热的小病，算不上多严重。能用这些小病拒绝没必要的应酬，特别是不用时常进宫讨好帝后，这是好事。
　　“进宫次数多了，我才会真的短寿。”李玄霸对母亲抱怨，“母亲，你不知道陛下有多难伺候。”
　　窦夫人失笑：“娘知道。辛苦大德了。”
　　李玄霸道：“不辛苦。母亲才辛苦。”
　　李玄霸没有客套，他确实心疼母亲的辛苦。
　　到了洛阳后，窦夫人不仅要照顾好家中老小，还要帮李渊应酬。
　　因杨广的猜忌心很强，窦夫人劝李渊不要频繁与他人接触。若有需要，她以女眷的身份帮李渊联络和友人的感情。
　　李渊是很喜欢交友的人。他年轻时就不分贵贱交朋友，现在虽然重身份了，但爱热闹爱排场的本性没有改变。即使李渊知道杨广猜忌心强，窦夫人劝李渊闭门谢客，李渊也不愿意。
　　窦夫人劝了很多次，在薛道衡去修书后，李渊才勉强收敛了一些。
　　为了让李渊安心，无论李渊结交的关系是否必要，窦夫人都悉心维护，耗费了许多心力。
　　当窦夫人主事时，万氏就不能越俎代庖。不过万氏可以帮窦夫人操持家务，李建成的后院又有郑媵操持，本应该减轻窦夫人不少负担。
　　谁知道万氏和郑媵起了冲突。窦夫人在内务上的负担加重了。
　　此次冲突，倒是和李建成无关，而是和李元吉、李智云有关。
　　李元吉和李智云同龄。他们正式上课后，自然在同一个老师那里学习。
　　李元吉因静不下心上课，学习进度稍缓慢；李智云自幼就能被李世民和李玄霸带着描大字，早就养成了很好的学习习惯，学习进度拉李元吉一大截。
　　万氏在独孤老夫人那里学会了小心谨慎。她没有请求李渊为李智云另找老师单独授课，只是自己私下为李智云补课。
　　但李元吉仍旧埋怨李智云让他受老师责备，和李智云打了一架。
　　打架的时候，李元吉说了许多侮辱李智云和万氏的话，并说这是郑媵教的。
　　万氏气笑了。
　　你和我都是媵，你神气个什么？
