Chapter 65: Seizing the Opportunity to Move to the Villa

What began as a mere scuffle between two children had now escalated into a major affair. Concubine Wan was relentless, and Lady Zheng vehemently denied the accusations. Li Yuan could not help but complain that Lady Zheng had failed to manage the inner courtyard properly, which left her feeling so stifled and aggrieved that her chest ached.

The matter was not as complex as it seemed. Lady Zheng possessed a firm grip on the inner courtyard and soon uncovered the truth. As a concubine of Li Jiancheng, she had no reason to speak ill of one brother-in-law to another.

On the journey to Luoyang with Li Jiancheng and Lady Zheng, Li Yuanji had grown fond of his gentle and generous young sister-in-law. After arriving in Luoyang, he often visited Li Jiancheng’s courtyard to play. Since Li Yuanji was still young, there was no need to strictly observe the separation of the sexes, and with the eldest sister-in-law acting as a mother figure, Lady Zheng often received him alongside her husband.

Li Yuanji’s academic progress lagged far behind Li Zhiyun’s. Feeling slighted, he frequently came to Li Jiancheng and Lady Zheng to complain. Li Jiancheng would always tell him that Li Zhiyun was merely a child of a concubine and of a different status, so there was no need to pay him any mind. He told him that the scions of the Tang State Duke’s mansion would have plenty of opportunities to enter the court as officials in the future, so academic knowledge was unimportant; it would be better to focus on martial arts and earn merit on the battlefield.

Lady Zheng had merely offered a few words of agreement.

Yet, in Li Yuanji’s retelling, this transformed into Lady Zheng claiming Li Zhiyun was of low birth, embellished with many insults toward Concubine Wan.

Li Jiancheng insisted he had never spoken ill of Concubine Wan. Even if she was a concubine, she was his father’s concubine, and he had to address her as "Aunt." He might gossip about Li Zhiyun, but how could he possibly gossip about Concubine Wan?

Li Yuanji also insisted that Lady Zheng had taught him these things, even providing plausible times and locations. Lady Zheng, unable to voice her grievances, could only swear by her family’s reputation.

Li Yuan detested Lady Zheng’s habit of swearing by her family’s reputation. She constantly brought up her lineage, boasting of her noble background and elevating her own family to such a degree that it seemed to disparage the Tang State Duke’s mansion. Li Jiancheng had also grown weary of her oaths. When she first did it, he had felt sorry for her and even stood up to the Old Madam Dugu on her behalf. But when the same thing happened again, his sympathy turned to annoyance.

He even brought up past grievances: "You said the same thing back then, and I stood up to Grandmother for you. You are nothing but a source of trouble!"

Lady Zheng was so angry and frustrated she could not speak for tears. How could the matter with the Old Madam be her fault? She had been completely innocent; it was the Old Madam who wanted to secure benefits for Li Jiancheng and had used her name to seize her younger brother’s shop!

This time was the same. Fearing she would be criticized, she had even been tactful when agreeing with Li Jiancheng that Li Zhiyun was just a concubine’s son, changing it to "You and the young master share the same mother," not daring to utter the word "concubine-born." As a concubine herself, how could she look down on her elder’s concubine? If she cursed Concubine Wan, wouldn’t all those words eventually circle back to strike her?

However, Li Jiancheng had not cursed Concubine Wan, and Li Yuanji was just a child. Besides Lady Zheng, who else could be held responsible for sowing discord between the brothers Li Yuanji and Li Zhiyun?

Lady Zheng attempted to ask Concubine Wan to take a step back. This time, Concubine Wan did not give her face. She sneered, "I don’t know who insulted me and Little Five, but I know this matter must be blown up and the culprit must be punished, otherwise Little Five will continue to hear such gossip! If the Master and the Lady are dissatisfied, they can drive me and Little Five away. I will take him back to my maiden home; I will not suffer this indignity!"

With Concubine Wan speaking to this extent—even mentioning returning to her maiden home—it was impossible for Lady Zheng to smooth things over. Lady Zheng realized that Concubine Wan surely knew she was innocent. Concubine Wan’s target was Li Jiancheng, but she could do nothing to him, so she had to focus her rage on Lady Zheng, killing the chicken to scare the monkey, forcing Li Jiancheng to restrain himself.

Lady Zheng wanted to persuade Concubine Wan that this might not have much to do with Li Jiancheng, but she did not know how to convince her. She intuitively felt that the fault lay with Li Yuanji—that he had lied. Li Yuanji had indeed described in detail how Lady Zheng taught him to insult Li Zhiyun and Concubine Wan, but the problem was that his "recollections" were far too detailed. Li Yuanji struggled even with his basic recitations; how could he have the memory to recall the daily gossip of Lady Zheng, down to the exact hour? Did they check the time every time she spoke ill of someone?

Lady Zheng harbored this suspicion but had to keep it to herself, unable to even tell Li Yuan. She had once tried to abandon Li Yuanji, so whatever she did, others saw it as bias. Now, if she suspected him without proof, not only would no one believe her, but they would also accuse her of being unkind to him again.

Lady Zheng did not want to harm the innocent, but someone had to take the blame, and that had to be Concubine Zheng. She first placed Concubine Zheng under house arrest and then dragged her feet, hoping the matter would blow over. Li Yuan quarreled with her over this, accusing her of favoring the concubine in Li Jiancheng’s quarters—was she trying to emulate the Old Madam and spoil Li Jiancheng too much? Lady Zheng was left between laughter and tears.

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin remained outside the vortex of this conflict, but with the household in such an uproar, they could not find peace. Since that day, Li Zhiyun had become sullen, often locking himself in his room and no longer coming to play with them.

Li Shimin held a brush between his nose and lips, pouting as he complained, "Little Five isn’t holding a grudge against us just because we share the same mother as Little Four, is he? If that’s the case, I don’t want this younger brother anymore."

Li Xuanba said, "Perhaps he is worried that we, like Li Yuanji, look down on him."

Li Shimin fiddled with the brush handle on his lip. "If he harbors such malicious suspicions about us, that is his own fault. I don’t want this brother."

Li Xuanba asked, "Really?"

Li Shimin persisted for a long time until the brush finally fell from his lip. He tossed it into the brush holder and said, "This house is too noisy; I want some quiet. We might as well take Little Five back to Daxing with us."

Li Xuanba replied, "Father won’t let us leave Luoyang. Even if someone were to leave, it would be the elder brother who has already reached adulthood staying behind in Daxing, while we, the young ones, stay by our parents' side."

Li Shimin said, "Then let’s drive our elder brother away!"

Li Xuanba glanced at him and said, "I think you’re the one who would be driven away."

Li Shimin complained, "Are we to do nothing but listen to them bicker every day? Mother is the same—wouldn't it have been enough to punish Concubine Zheng and give Aunt Wan an explanation? Why protect her and make Aunt Wan unhappy?"

Li Xuanba said, "Because Mother believes Concubine Zheng is innocent."

Li Shimin said, "If she is innocent, and our elder brother doesn't seem like the type to gossip about Aunt Wan, could it be that Li Yuanji lied?"

Li Xuanba asked, "Why couldn't it be?"

Li Shimin pinched his own soft chin. "Do children lie?"

Li Xuanba was speechless. "Have you and I never lied?"

Li Shimin chuckled. "We’ve told plenty of lies."

Who said children don’t lie? Children are highly skilled at avoiding harm and seeking benefits. If Li Shimin and Li Xuanba didn't know how to lie, how could they have won the Emperor’s favor? Even without the Emperor, Li Shimin had told many lies for the sake of gluttony or play, often ending up with a sore backside after being caught by Lady Zheng. As for Li Xuanba, he had always been full of lies.

Li Shimin deduced, "The cause of this might be that Li Yuanji’s studies aren't as good as Little Five’s, and he grew jealous. He took to heart our elder brother’s words about Little Five’s low birth, and when they fought, he added a little... well, a little bit of filth. He only blamed Concubine Zheng to shift the responsibility."

Li Xuanba said, "Don't underestimate Li Yuanji. His studies may be poor, but he has plenty of petty wit; he instinctively knows who he can provoke and who he cannot."

Li Xuanba had planted eyes and ears in Concubine Zheng’s courtyard; he knew more than Lady Zheng, who did not resort to such underhanded means. At the very least, Lady Zheng did not know that Concubine Zheng had privately cursed Li Yuanji. Li Yuanji instinctively knew Li Jiancheng was his backer, so he completely excluded him from his story. Li Jiancheng’s remarks about Li Zhiyun being a concubine’s son were only revealed when Lady Zheng questioned him before he knew what Li Yuanji had said. In Li Yuanji’s version, Li Jiancheng was absent the entire time.

Li Shimin laughed, "Indeed, he knows who he can provoke. For instance, even now, he refuses to call you elder brother."

Li Xuanba nodded readily. "Yes, he looks down on me and thinks I am someone he can provoke."

Li Shimin’s smile faded. "If this happened to you, I would beat him until he couldn't take care of himself."

Li Xuanba said, "I would do the same. Let’s go. Little Five should be calmer now; we should go visit him."

Li Shimin jumped off the couch, putting on his shoes as he said, "You finally agreed."

Li Xuanba said, "Li Yuanji is our biological brother; it wouldn't be right for us to take sides against him in a fight with Little Five."

Li Shimin snorted, clearly having no affection for that brother.

Lady Zheng handled the situation with great skill. Her "delaying" tactic was perfectly timed. Concubine Zheng was confined for half a month, and by then, Concubine Wan’s anger had subsided significantly. Seeing Lady Zheng’s determination not to harm the innocent, she took a step back and only demanded an apology. Concubine Zheng, who had initially refused to admit fault, softened after the confinement and tearfully apologized to Concubine Wan, claiming she had no malicious intent and had merely spoken without thinking while comforting Li Yuanji.

With both sides taking a step back, the storm appeared to have settled, and Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were finally able to visit Li Zhiyun.

When they reached Li Zhiyun’s courtyard, they saw his little head hanging over the window frame from afar, his nose twitching as he shed tears. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba exchanged a look and quickened their pace.

Li Zhiyun scrambled out of the window, threw himself into Li Shimin’s arms, and sobbed bitterly.

Li Shimin laughed, "Why are you willing to throw yourself at me this time, instead of your favorite third brother?"

Li Zhiyun cried, "Third Brother is in poor health; I’m afraid of knocking him over."

Li Shimin deliberately pulled a long face and drawled, "Oh, I see, you only care about your third brother. Ah Xuan, I don't want this younger brother anymore; you can have him." He pushed Li Zhiyun toward Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba wiped Li Zhiyun’s tears and snot as he said, "Little Five is upset right now; be careful he takes you seriously and really thinks you don't want him."

Li Shimin crossed his arms. "If Little Five is that stupid, then I really can't keep him."

Li Zhiyun’s crying grew louder.

Li Shimin patted Li Zhiyun’s head. "Alright, stop crying. Second Brother knows you’ve been wronged; you’ve had a hard time."

Li Zhiyun shook his head while buried in Li Xuanba’s arms, unable to speak through his sobs. When he first learned that his biological mother was not Lady Zheng, he had been very anxious. Later, both his biological mother and Lady Zheng treated him well, and he had let go of his inner conflict. Li Yuanji’s insults had torn open his hidden scars, forcing him to face the fact that he was an "outsider" in this family.

His father had five sons, four of whom were born to Lady Zheng, and only he was born to a concubine. Li Zhiyun felt terrified and lonely. Even though he knew his second and third brothers treated him well, he dared not approach them after hearing Li Yuanji’s words, fearing they would also despise him.

After Li Zhiyun cried for a while, Li Shimin could no longer bear it and picked him up. "The sun is so hot; if you aren't afraid, Ah Xuan is. Let’s go inside."

Li Shimin held Li Zhiyun, who was three years his junior, firmly. Li Zhiyun said embarrassedly, "I can walk."

Li Shimin set him down. Li Xuanba had a servant bring water, and the three brothers tidied themselves up before continuing their discussion.

Li Xuanba said, "I intend to tell Father that Second Brother and I want to move to the villa in the suburbs. If you are willing, we would like to take you with us. But if you live with us, you will have to leave Aunt Wan."

Li Zhiyun was surprised. "Move out? Why?"

Li Xuanba said, "Second Brother and I are making more friends, and it is not convenient to have outsiders coming in and out of the Tang State Duke’s mansion every day."

Li Shimin sighed with his arms crossed. "Indeed, outsiders."

This was a plan Li Xuanba had devised using the conflict between Concubine Zheng and Concubine Wan. With their friends increasing and their ambitions growing, staying in the small, remote courtyard of the Tang State Duke’s mansion was too restrictive. Taking advantage of the inner courtyard turmoil, Li Xuanba proposed to Li Yuan that they move to the villa to avoid causing their elder brother any displeasure.

Although Li Yuan always blamed Concubine Zheng, he surely suspected whether these words had come from Li Jiancheng. After all, Li Jiancheng looked down on his own biological brothers, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba; it was only natural he would look down on Li Zhiyun and Concubine Wan. But as the head of the house, Li Yuan had to stand by Li Jiancheng and could not allow him to be tainted by the fault of this inner courtyard dispute.

Li Xuanba used some tactics to deepen Li Yuan’s suspicion of Li Jiancheng, framing the matter as Li Jiancheng being wary of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba forming factions within the mansion. To put Li Jiancheng at ease, moving to the villa—nominally to find a quiet environment for study—was a way to declare that they had no designs on the inheritance of the Tang State Duke’s mansion.

Many noble families allowed their secondary sons to move to villas to study, not only for the quiet but also to bolster the prestige of the eldest son by having him hold down the main residence. Li Yuan hoped his sons would be harmonious, even wanting them to live in the same courtyard, but he had to abandon this idea after Li Jiancheng took a concubine.

Li Yuan had never thought of letting Li Shimin and Li Xuanba move out, but if this conflict truly stemmed from Li Jiancheng’s dissatisfaction with them, separating the sons would reduce friction. It was just a pity for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. Even though they were in the same city, Lady Zheng could still look after them, and they would return to the main residence to reunite with their parents whenever Li Yuan had time off. But not seeing their parents every day still made Li Yuan feel he was failing these two young boys.

Li Yuan was hesitant, but the situation with Concubine Zheng added weight to the scale: she was pregnant again. After her confinement was lifted, Lady Zheng had a physician check her, fearing she had fallen ill from depression, only to discover she was a month pregnant, though the fetus was very unstable. For the sake of the child in her womb, there could be no more waves in the inner courtyard.

When Li Xuanba made the decision, he had sought Li Shimin’s opinion beforehand. Although they were "conspiring," Li Shimin felt conflicted. On one hand, he felt stifled in the mansion; on the other, he hoped his father would refuse so he could stay. When Li Yuan hesitated, Li Shimin was truly happy. But now that Concubine Zheng was pregnant, he could only console himself that the unborn niece or nephew was more important, and he should take a step back.

Seeing Li Zhiyun so depressed that he refused to attend classes with Li Yuanji, Li Xuanba felt a pang of sympathy for the brother who had clung to him since childhood and wanted to take him along. Li Shimin naturally agreed. Both his younger brothers were often bullied by that little demon Li Yuanji; they should stay far away from him. Li Shimin truly could not understand why someone could be so detestable from such a young age. Every time he saw Li Yuanji’s face, he wanted to pin him to the ground and give him a sound thrashing.

Li Zhiyun wanted to leave with his two brothers. The thought of staying under the same roof as Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji made him want to curl into a ball. But his biological mother was still here, and he didn't want to leave her to face the insults alone.

Li Xuanba said, "Discuss it with Aunt Wan. Even if you don't live with us, you can often come to visit."

Li Xuanba did not press the matter further to avoid adding to Li Zhiyun’s psychological burden. He wanted to ask about the studies Li Zhiyun had missed, but Li Shimin shoved him, telling him to be quiet. Li Shimin left him to read alone and took Li Zhiyun to play in the courtyard. Li Xuanba shook his head, glanced at the scorching sun outside with a look of disdain, and quietly began to read.

Li Shimin and Li Zhiyun played cuju in the sun, their laughter drifting through the window, making Li Xuanba want to plug his ears with paper. It was so hot, and so noisy.

...

Li Zhiyun told Concubine Wan about the invitation from Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. Concubine Wan couldn't help but hold him and weep.

"Go, you must go, follow your second and third brothers," Concubine Wan said, stroking Li Zhiyun’s head. "They are truly good to you. They are talented, even better than the teachers your father hired. They also have many brilliant friends who can all become your teachers."

Li Zhiyun nestled in her arms. "But Mother, I can't bear to leave you. What if you are bullied?"

Concubine Wan tapped his nose. "I am, after all, your father’s only concubine with a title; I will not be bullied."

Li Zhiyun muttered, "But we were bullied this time."

Concubine Wan sneered, "Only Li Jiancheng can bully us. He hasn't even become the Tang State Duke yet, and he’s already acting like one. He bullies even Second and Third Brother, and Lady Zheng can’t control him; what can we do? It’s better to avoid him."

She stroked Li Zhiyun’s face earnestly. "If you avoid him, you won't be bullied. If you aren't in the mansion, he won't have much contact with me, and I won't be bullied by him. It’s just hard on you, having to leave me at such a young age."

Li Zhiyun shook his head, clutching her neck. "It’s not hard."

Concubine Wan instructed him carefully, "Although your second and third brothers are very fond of you, they are still young and may not be very attentive. If you are unhappy about anything, don't be timid; tell them directly. They won't blame you."

"I will arrange for honest and loyal servants for you. You must also frequently remind them to be obedient, not to cause trouble for your brothers, and not to bring disaster upon yourself."

"You must not only learn archery and horsemanship from Second Brother and reading from Third Brother, but also learn how they conduct themselves. Second Brother has a cheerful personality, and all his friends genuinely love him; Third Brother, though slightly reclusive, is meticulous and very considerate of others' emotions. These are all things you should learn."

"Although you are young, as long as you stay by the side of excellent people and imitate their behavior, you will surely become more excellent than before."

"It is your good fortune that they are willing to take you. You must be obedient..."

Concubine Wan kept chattering on, and as she spoke, Li Zhiyun reached out to touch her face. "Mother, don't cry, I will be obedient." Li Zhiyun choked back tears.

Concubine Wan leaned down and rubbed her head against his. "Yes, don't cry. Mother won't cry."

Don't cry. For the sake of her child, she would never cry again.

...

Lady Zheng strongly opposed Li Shimin, Li Xuanba, and Li Zhiyun moving to the villa. Li Xuanba convinced her by citing the Emperor’s orders.

"His Majesty has had me do many things in private. While not classified, the Tang State Duke’s mansion is full of people with loose tongues, and I would be blamed if word got out," Li Xuanba said in a low voice. "Besides, our courtyard is too small for friends to visit. Moving to the villa will make it much easier to host them. I can also go out to inspect the family estates and better manage our business."

Lady Zheng looked deeply at her third son. After a long while, she sighed heavily and said with a choked voice, "It is Mother’s fault, Mother is useless... Very well, go. It will be easier for the three of you."

She picked up Li Zhiyun and rubbed her cheek against his. "Little Five, Mother has failed you."

Li Zhiyun shook his head and rubbed his cheek against hers in return. "Mother has been very good to me, I know. Please don't be sad."

It was not Lady Zheng’s fault. Li Zhiyun knew that clearly.

The three of them finally succeeded in moving to the villa. Lady Zheng stayed for ten days to get things in order before leaving with reluctance. Concubine Wan did not appear at all, as if it weren't her own son moving away.

The Tang State Duke’s mansion remained as lively as ever, with no changes at all. The only difference was that Lady Zheng persuaded Li Yuan to have Li Yuanji, who already had his own courtyard, move back to their side to live with them, so he could be strictly educated.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第66章 只是想打造铁锅
chunks.chineseText:
第66章 只是想打造铁锅

=
　　不管是不是有人教唆， 李元吉上课不认真，嫉妒优秀的弟弟，辱骂家中的长辈……这一切都证明李元吉现在十分顽劣， 必须严格管教。
　　窦夫人自贬能力， 说自己只会养育孩子， 不会教育孩子。教导已经启蒙的孩子，是家主才能做到的事。
　　这时教育儿子，也确实是父亲的责任。
　　古人云， “子不教，父之过”。自先秦时起，教育儿子就是父亲的责任。纵观流传后世的“家训”， 也都是父亲写给子孙的告诫。
　　对于家中子嗣，家中女眷除了照顾孩童衣食起居， 顶多在孩童开蒙时能看顾一番。除非是寡妇， 否则女眷一般不能插手子嗣教育。
　　李渊是寡母带大，所以才习惯性地把儿子都交给家中女眷照看。而且他常年在外做官，家中女眷子嗣不能随行，所以也没办法自己教育儿子。
　　李渊被窦夫人戴了高帽子，又确实担心李元吉长歪， 只好将李元吉带在身边，再次亲自教导李元吉。
　　他曾经亲自教导过一次李元吉， 被李元吉气得吃不下饭。后来李元吉稍稍乖巧了一些，他又认为李元吉身为嫡幼子不需要太多本事，家里养得起， 便撒手不管了。
　　但李元吉现在变得比以前还顽劣， 李渊只能再次咬牙忍受教导不成器的儿子的折磨。
　　离开父母， 李世民原本有些难过。
　　好不容易父母都团聚在洛阳， 他在父母膝盖上撒娇的日子还没过多久，就被迫住进了别庄。
　　李世民很恋家，即使是自己决定出来住，也难免心生郁闷之意。
　　别庄就挨着洛阳城，位于洛河之畔。
　　洛阳被河流和山脉分割成许多个小盆地，傍水的地方必倚山。
　　大隋自北周而延续下来的勋贵没有不喜欢打猎的，即使杨广定都东都洛阳是为了压制关陇贵族，为了安抚这群关陇贵族，也会在东都附近分给他们大片土地。
　　唐国公府的别庄也很广阔，除了河谷平原，还圈了大片的山林。
　　私人的山林不准普通百姓进入。窦夫人心善，也只是在寒冬腊月允许附近百姓进入唐国公府的山林拾取柴火。若是谁敢砍树，唐国公府是要报官的。
　　如今正值草木茂盛，动物活跃的季节。十分难过的李世民等母亲一离开，就带着李智云钻进了山林狩猎。
　　他本来还想拉上李玄霸。李玄霸指着旁边的洛河，说如果李世民敢强迫自己去狩猎，自己就从这里跳下去。
　　李世民将还不能独自骑马的李智云抱在身前，不住抱怨：“小五，你说至于吗？我让他狩猎，他居然说要跳河？这至于吗！”
　　李智云被两位兄长逗得“咯咯”直笑。
　　李世民怒搓李智云的光脑袋。
　　李智云和他一趟，都是只留了两个小揪揪，其他地方的头发都剃光了，脑袋搓起来特别滑溜舒服。
　　李智云眯着眼睛，就像是小兽一样享受兄长的揉搓。
　　离开娘亲和生母独自在外居住，李智云本来难免害怕。但哥哥们日夜陪伴着他，轮流陪他睡觉，现在还带着他去林子里骑马，他就不害怕了。
　　至于为什么是轮流，自然是因为李世民睡相太霸道，李智云只想和三哥一起睡。李世民认为自己被弟弟嫌弃了，非要把李智云抓着和自己抵足而眠。
　　唐国公府的山林里没有大型猎物，但兔子野鸡在盛夏季节非常充足。
　　李世民天天带着李智云钻林子，很快就“乐不思蜀”，把对父母的想念忘到了脑后。直到李玄霸提醒他该在父亲休沐时回家时，他才恍惚自己已经习惯在别庄的生活了。
　　李渊这些时日饱受亲自教导李元吉的折磨，越发想念聪慧的二儿子和三儿子。
　　今日李世民和李玄霸带着李智云回家，他在门口翘首以盼。
　　当马车上下来一大一小两黑炭时，李渊沉默了。
　　李渊看向唯一相貌没有多少改变的李玄霸：“他们这是怎么了？”
　　李玄霸叹气：“还能怎么？天天钻林子打猎晒的。”
　　就算林子有树叶遮掩，该晒还是晒啊。
　　李家人除了自己之外，体质是真的强。这样晒着，不仅没中暑，皮肤也没有晒伤过，只是变黑了。
　　李渊欲言又止。
　　他本以为二郎一定会想念到他哭鼻子，没想到这混账儿子天天带着幼弟打猎，看样子完全没有想念自己呢！
　　李世民表示自己还是很想念父亲母亲的，还为父亲母亲准备了许多礼物，全是自己和小五猎的。
　　李渊问道：“怎么只有你和五郎的猎物？三郎的猎物呢？”
　　李世民幽怨道：“阿玄说我如果拉他去狩猎，他就从洛河跳下去。”
　　李渊愣住，无奈地看着李玄霸道：“连五郎都喜欢上了狩猎，四郎也说想去狩猎，我们家就你不喜欢狩猎。”
　　李玄霸点头：“对，就我不喜欢。”
　　窦夫人道：“别把孩子拦在外面。赶紧进来，娘今日让人做了牛肉。难得有摔死的小乳牛，你们有口福了。”
　　李世民扑到窦夫人怀里：“好！我一个人要吃一整头牛！”
　　窦夫人笑着掐了一把黑孩儿的脸，又揉了揉另一个小号黑孩儿的脑袋：“快来吧，你阿姨等你好久了。”
　　李智云不好意思地笑了笑。
　　窦夫人又对李玄霸招了招手，在李玄霸生无可恋的表情下捏了李玄霸瘦削的小脸一把，带着三个孩子进门吃饭。
　　饭桌上，李建成对李世民和李玄霸都很客气。特别是对李玄霸，脸色难得的柔和。
　　李玄霸猜测，可能是因为他和二哥搬去别庄，让李建成认为他们主动示弱的缘故。
　　让李玄霸惊奇的是，李元吉居然乖乖叫自己兄长，完全看不出顽劣的模样。
　　这才多久？李元吉就变了性子了？
　　李世民附在李玄霸耳边道：“我见李元吉的手心还是肿的，他肯定没少挨揍。”
　　李玄霸瞥了一眼李元吉。
　　李元吉跪坐在坐榻上的姿态有些扭曲。
　　看来他不仅手心是肿的，臀部也受了重创。
　　“你扭什么？坐没坐相！”李渊训斥道。
　　李元吉身体一抖，乖乖坐直。
　　李玄霸：【揍李元吉的一定是父亲。】
　　李世民点头。而且揍得不轻，嘿！
　　见到李元吉挨了揍，李世民和李玄霸这顿饭吃得很香。
　　他们在府中待了一夜，第二日带着李智云回到了别庄。
　　见他们在别庄过得不错，李渊和窦夫人放下了心，彻底对他们放了权，让他们可以全权处理别庄的事，任意取用别庄的物资。
　　李建成此次很慷慨地提议，干脆将别庄归于李世民和李玄霸二人名下，以后这个别庄就是李世民和李玄霸的私产。
　　见两个弟弟没有和自己争夺国公继承人的心思，李建成良好的继承人教育再次展现了出来。
　　因郑媵有了身孕，郑媵又给李建成寻了新的美妾，李建成爱护郑媵的贤惠大度和体贴，又怜惜郑媵肚子里的孩子，与郑媵关系再次融洽。
　　他对郑媵叹息道：“若他二人不盯着国公的位置，他们越优秀，就对我越有利。原本我与他们关系就不错，若不是祖母当时老糊涂……罢了，不该说已经去世的长辈的不是。”
　　这次郑媵只安静地微笑着听着，不敢再发表任何意见。
　　李建成既然有这个爱护弟弟的心思，李渊和窦夫人很欣慰地接纳了李建成的建议。
　　李渊对李世民和李玄霸道：“你们兄长爱护你们，特意把这个别庄送给你们。”
　　李世民：“……哦。”本来很高兴，现在不高兴了。
　　李玄霸恭敬道：“我和二哥十分感激兄长的爱护，请父亲帮我和二哥转达我们的谢意。”
　　李玄霸：【二哥快道谢！不然我把你的弓劈了当柴烧！】
　　李世民赶紧道：“是、是啊，我和阿玄很感激，请耶耶一定要帮我们把谢意转达到。”
　　李渊欣慰道：“好，我一定转达。”
　　长子与二子、三子的关系重新变好，四子也懂事了许多，五子也很聪慧。这日子终于越过越好了。李渊教导李元吉积累的疲惫都减轻了不少。
　　当李渊走后，李世民脸色一垮，阴阳怪气道：“呵呵，真是谢谢了啊。”
　　李玄霸道：“得到了实惠，谢他一句又如何？他送多少别庄给我，我就给他多少声谢谢。”
　　李世民嫌弃道：“阿玄，你好市侩。”
　　李玄霸点头：“嗯，我就是。”
　　他正想着怎么撺掇父母把别庄划在自己名下，没想到刚想瞌睡，李建成就送来了枕头。
　　别说一声谢，若在现代社会，他开一百个小号帮李建成投千古一帝的票，为李建成打榜都没问题。
　　李玄霸把李智云丢给二哥带，让李智云监督二哥好好读书，不要每日都去打猎。他来到了别庄旁边的工坊，终于能做一件自他穿越后，一直想做的事。
　　打一口铁锅。
　　李玄霸一直以为铁锅只要有铁就能做。穿越之后，他询问了家中供奉的铁匠，才知道铁锅的技术含量原来很高。
　　就如同古代只有最优秀的工匠才能铸造鼎一样，如果能打造出一口受热均匀的铁锅，铁匠的手艺都能打造出盔甲了。
　　怪不得到了宋朝，冶铁业空前发展，铁锅才走入千家万户。
　　宋朝虽然武力很差，但装备是一点都不差的。
　　唐国公府不是没有能打造出铁锅的工匠，但这样的工匠都是供奉着给家中贵人打造盔甲的，李玄霸没可能让他们帮忙打造铁锅。
　　所有别庄都自带一套完整的衣食住行工坊，铁匠铺也在其中。
　　现在别庄被划给了李世民和李玄霸，庄子上的人也都成了李世民和李玄霸的奴仆。李玄霸终于能使唤动他们精进打铁技术，为自己打造一口铁锅了。
　　希望有了小炒后，能把二哥的饮食习惯再改一改，别天天逼二哥吃蔬菜比逼他喝药还难。
　　李玄霸找到铁匠铺子的主事人，告知了铁锅的详细要求。
　　那瘸腿的老铁匠狐疑道：“三郎君，你真的只是想打造一口铁做的锅，而不是盔甲？”
　　李玄霸道：“就是铁锅，满足口腹之欲而已。”
　　老铁匠沉默了许久，叹了口气道：“我已经是三郎君的人，三郎君想打什么都成。这铁锅的要求很高，如今的炉子可能不行，得用有大风箱的炉子。”
　　李玄霸好奇：“如果有炉子，你就能打？”
　　老铁匠道：“能不能，要试试才知道。”
　　李玄霸笑道：“你尽管试，别怕浪费。炉子、燃料和铁矿石的事交给我。等试出来了，还要麻烦老翁多带弟子。我这锅打造好了，是要当礼物送给亲朋好友的。”
　　老铁匠问道：“要打造很多口锅？”
　　李玄霸道：“很多。”
　　老铁匠再次沉默了。
　　“老朽有一子力大无穷，若三郎君不嫌弃，可否给他一点差事？”老铁匠艰难开口。
　　李玄霸道：“我正好缺一个护卫。”
　　老铁匠松了口气：“谢三郎君！老朽一定竭尽全力！”
　　李玄霸鼓励了瘸腿老铁匠几句，带着捡了漏的欢喜去告诉二哥这个好消息。
　　不愧是国公府，底蕴真是深厚，连别庄的铁匠都是敢夸口能做出盔甲的能人巧匠。
　　李玄霸怀疑，国公府的每个别庄，都有这么一个能人坐镇。
　　要知道南北朝时能当国公的人，都是有自己的私军的。就是现在的将领，自己和亲兵的盔甲都是自备。所以唐国公府中有许多能做盔甲的铁匠很正常。
　　李世民得知这件事后，先很欢喜，然后疑惑：“这样是常态吗？那岂不是每个勋贵世家都能自己打造盔甲武器养私兵？”
　　李玄霸道：“确实都能。所以在皇帝强势的时候，家中若搜出盔甲，是按谋逆算。我们只是打造铁锅，二哥不用担心。”
　　李世民小声问道：“阿玄，你以后不会让我顶着铁锅上战场吧？”
　　李玄霸无语：“你身为勋贵子弟，上战场时是能自备盔甲的。你给你自己打造几套备用的盔甲，不算谋逆。”
　　李世民摸着胸口顺气：“那就好。我喜欢金光灿灿五颜六色的盔甲！”
　　李玄霸：“……”金光灿灿还要五颜六色，这是什么流光溢彩的骚包盔甲？你是生怕战场上不够显眼吗？
　　李玄霸的记忆无风自动，检索出了“关键词汇”。
　　唐太宗征辽东的时候，给自己亲自率领的一万具装骑兵“取金漆，涂铁甲，色迈兼金，又以五采染金”，“金光曜日，与李勣会於城下”。
　　二哥是真的很喜欢花里胡哨啊。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 66: Just Wanting to Forge an Iron Wok

Regardless of whether he had been incited by others, the fact remained that Li Yuanji slacked off during lessons, envied his outstanding younger brothers, and hurled abuse at his household elders… All of this proved that he had grown utterly wild and unruly, desperately in need of strict discipline.

Lady Dou belittled her own abilities, claiming she only knew how to nurture children’s daily lives, not how to educate their minds. Instructing sons who had already passed their primary enlightenment was a task that only the master of the household could shoulder.

In this era, teaching sons truly was the father's duty.

As the ancients said, *“To rear without educating is the fault of the father.”* Ever since the pre-Qin era, instructing sons had been the patriarch’s responsibility. A glance through the famed "Family Precepts" passed down through history showed that they were all admonitions written by fathers for their descendants.

When it came to the household's sons, the female family members looked after their daily food and clothing, and at most kept an eye on them during their earliest years of schooling. Unless she were a widow, a woman generally had no hand in a son's higher education.

Li Yuan had been raised by a widowed mother, which was why he had habitually left his sons in the care of the womenfolk. Moreover, he had served as an official away from home for years, where wives and children could not always accompany him, leaving him unable to educate his sons personally.

Having been placed upon a pedestal by Lady Dou, and genuinely worried that Li Yuanji might turn out completely rotten, Li Yuan had no choice but to keep Li Yuanji at his side and resume teaching him in person.

He had tried teaching Li Yuanji once before, only to be so enraged by the boy that he couldn't stomach his food. Later, when Li Yuanji grew slightly better-behaved, Li Yuan had figured that as the youngest son of the legal wife, the boy didn't need extraordinary talents—the family was wealthy enough to support him regardless—and so he had washed his hands of the matter.

Yet now, Li Yuanji had become even more insufferable than before. Li Yuan could only grit his teeth and once again endure the torment of teaching this good-for-nothing son.

***

Leaving his parents had initially made Li Shimin a little downcast.

It had not been easy for his family to reunite in Luoyang. He had barely enjoyed a few days of acting like a spoiled child at his parents' knees before being forced to move into the country villa.

Li Shimin was deeply attached to his family. Even though living out here was his own choice, a twinge of gloom inevitably weighed on his heart.

The villa sat right beside Luoyang, nestled along the banks of the Luo River.

Luoyang was partitioned into numerous small basins by its rivers and mountain ridges; wherever there was water, there were bound to be hills leaning beside it.

Ever since the Northern Zhou, the noble houses that endured into the Great Sui all shared a passion for hunting. Even though Yang Guang had established the Eastern Capital of Luoyang precisely to suppress the Guanlong aristocracy, he still had to grant them vast tracts of land around the city to keep them pacified.

The Duke of Tang’s villa was likewise expansive. Beyond the river valley's fertile flatlands, it enclosed a sprawling swathe of forested mountains.

Common folk were barred from entering private mountain forests. Even with Lady Dou’s gentle heart, she only permitted the local villagers to gather fallen firewood on the Duke's land during the dead of winter. If anyone dared fell a living tree, the Duke's estate would report them to the local magistrate without hesitation.

Right now, the foliage was lush and the beasts were active. Having been quite depressed, the moment his mother left, Li Shimin took Li Zhiyun and dove straight into the mountains to hunt.

He had originally wanted to drag Li Xuanba along as well. Li Xuanba, however, simply pointed at the nearby Luo River and declared that if Li Shimin dared force him on a hunt, he would jump straight in.

Pulling Li Zhiyun—who was not yet able to ride alone—into the saddle in front of him, Li Shimin complained incessantly, "Little Fifth, tell me, is that really necessary? I only asked him to hunt, and he threatened to jump into the river! Does he have to go that far?!"

Li Zhiyun giggled helplessly at his older brothers' antics.

Li Shimin gave Li Zhiyun’s bald head an affectionate, vigorous rub.

Like Li Shimin, Li Zhiyun's head was completely shaved except for two little tufts of hair tied into buns. Rubbing his bare scalp felt exceptionally smooth and satisfying.

Li Zhiyun narrowed his eyes, basking in his brother's rough petting like a pampered little animal.

Living apart from his legal mother and his birth mother in a strange place, Li Zhiyun had naturally felt scared at first. But his older brothers kept him company day and night, taking turns sleeping beside him, and now they were even taking him horseback riding through the forest. All his fear had evaporated.

As for why they had to take turns—it was solely because Li Shimin's sleeping posture was far too aggressive. Li Zhiyun vastly preferred sleeping beside his Third Brother. Li Shimin, feeling spurned by his little brother, had stubbornly insisted on dragging Li Zhiyun to sleep head-to-toe with him every other night.

There was no large game in the Duke’s woods, but hares and pheasants were plentiful in the height of summer.

Li Shimin took Li Zhiyun into the woods day after day, soon having so much fun that he forgot his troubles entirely, tossing all longing for his parents clean out of his mind. It was not until Li Xuanba reminded him that they ought to return home for their father's rest day that Li Shimin realized, in a daze, that he had already grown completely accustomed to life at the villa.

***

Having endured days of sheer agony trying to teach Li Yuanji, Li Yuan missed his intelligent second and third sons more with each passing hour.

Today, knowing that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were bringing Li Zhiyun home, he stood by the gates, craning his neck in anticipation.

When one large and one small lump of charcoal clambered down from the carriage, Li Yuan fell utterly silent.

Li Yuan turned toward Li Xuanba, the only one whose appearance remained unchanged. "What happened to them?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "What else could it be? They spent every single day hunting in the woods and got baked by the sun."

Even if the canopy provided shade, the sun still did its work.

Aside from himself, the men of the Li family truly possessed terrifying constitutions. Spending day after day under the scorching sun, not only did they avoid heatstroke, but their skin hadn't even peeled—they had simply turned pitch-black.

Li Yuan parted his lips, wanting to speak, but held back.

He had assumed his Second Son would miss him so much he'd be in tears. Who could have guessed that the rascal had been spending every waking moment hunting with his little brother, looking as though he hadn't missed his father in the slightest!

Li Shimin earnestly proclaimed that he had missed both his parents dearly, and had even prepared a mountain of gifts for them—all hunted by his and Little Fifth’s own hands.

Li Yuan asked, "Why is it only your and Fifth Son's catch? Where is Third Son's?"

Li Shimin grumbled resentfully, "Ah-Xuan said that if I dared drag him hunting, he’d jump into the Luo River."

Li Yuan froze, then looked at Li Xuanba with exasperation. "Even Fifth Son has grown fond of hunting, and Fourth Son keeps saying he wants to go, too. In our entire family, you are the only one who despises it."

Li Xuanba nodded shamelessly. "Yes, just me."

Lady Dou intervened, "Don't keep the children standing outside. Come in quickly. Mother had the kitchen prepare beef today. A young suckling calf broke its neck in a fall—a rare treat, so you're all in luck."

Li Shimin threw himself into Lady Dou's embrace. "Great! I'm going to eat a whole cow by myself!"

Lady Dou laughed, pinching the dark child’s cheek, then patted the head of the smaller dark child. "Come inside quickly, your aunt has been waiting for you for ages."

Li Zhiyun smiled bashfully.

Lady Dou then beckoned to Li Xuanba. Despite his soul-weary expression, she pinched his slender little cheek affectionately before leading the three boys inside to eat.

At the dinner table, Li Jiancheng was exceptionally courteous to both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. Toward Li Xuanba in particular, his expression was uncharacteristically gentle.

Li Xuanba guessed it was because moving out to the villa had made Li Jiancheng believe they were actively yielding the field to him.

What surprised Li Xuanba even more was that Li Yuanji actually called him "Elder Brother" with utter obedience, showing none of his usual bratty arrogance.

How long had it been? Had Li Yuanji truly had a change of heart?

Li Shimin leaned close to Li Xuanba's ear and whispered, "I saw Li Yuanji’s palms. They’re still swollen red. He definitely got thrashed."

Li Xuanba glanced at Li Yuanji.

The boy was kneeling on his mat in a rather twisted, awkward posture.

It seemed that along with swollen palms, his backside had suffered severe trauma as well.

"What are you squirming for? Sit properly!" Li Yuan snapped in rebuke.

Li Yuanji shivered all over and instantly sat bolt upright.

Li Xuanba: *【The one who beat Li Yuanji was definitely Father.】*

Li Shimin nodded in silent agreement. And beaten thoroughly, at that. *Heh!*

Seeing that Li Yuanji had been thoroughly thrashed made the meal taste infinitely sweeter to both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

***

They spent a single night at the main residence before returning to the villa with Li Zhiyun the following day.

Seeing that they were living well at the villa, Li Yuan and Lady Dou put their worries to rest. They completely relinquished oversight, giving them total authority over the villa's affairs and free rein to use any supplies on the estate.

Li Jiancheng made a remarkably generous proposal this time: he suggested transferring the villa directly under the names of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, turning it into their private property.

Seeing that his two younger brothers had no intention of contesting the succession of the dukedom, Li Jiancheng's impeccable upbringing as an heir shone through once again.

Because Concubine Zheng was now pregnant, she had personally found a new beauty for Li Jiancheng. Pleased with her virtue, generosity, and thoughtfulness, and doting on the unborn child in her belly, Li Jiancheng had once again grown exceedingly warm toward her.

He sighed to Concubine Zheng, "As long as those two do not set their sights on the dukedom, the more exceptional they are, the more beneficial it is to me. Our relationship was quite good to begin with; if not for Grandmother losing her wits in her old age… Ah, forget it. One should not speak ill of elders who have passed."

This time, Concubine Zheng merely listened with a quiet smile, not daring to offer any unwarranted opinions.

Since Li Jiancheng displayed such fraternal affection toward his younger brothers, Li Yuan and Lady Dou were immensely gratified and readily accepted his proposal.

Li Yuan said to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, "Your eldest brother cares deeply for you two. He specially gifted this villa to you."

Li Shimin: "...Oh." He had been quite happy a moment ago, but now his mood soured.

Li Xuanba bowed respectfully. "Second Brother and I are deeply grateful for Eldest Brother’s love and protection. We ask Father to convey our heartfelt thanks to him."

Li Xuanba: *【Second Brother, thank him right now! Otherwise, I’ll chop your bow into firewood!】*

Li Shimin hurriedly chimed in, "Y-yes! Ah-Xuan and I are immensely grateful. Please, Father, you must help us pass on our thanks!"

Li Yuan nodded with relief. "Good, I will certainly convey it."

The eldest son’s relationship with the second and third sons had mended, the fourth son was far better behaved, and the fifth son was exceptionally clever. Life was finally getting better by the day. Much of the exhaustion Li Yuan had accumulated from teaching Li Yuanji seemed to melt away.

Once Li Yuan had departed, Li Shimin's face instantly dropped, his voice dripping with sarcasm. "Heh, my deepest thanks indeed."

Li Xuanba said, "We gained real, tangible benefits. What does giving him a single word of thanks matter? If he gives me ten more villas, I’ll give him ten more thank-yous."

Li Shimin looked at him with disdain. "Ah-Xuan, you are far too mercenary."

Li Xuanba nodded shamelessly. "Yes, I am."

He had just been trying to think of a way to coax his parents into deeding the villa to them, only for Li Jiancheng to hand him a pillow just as he was dozing off.

Let alone a mere verbal thank-you—if this were modern times, he would gladly create a hundred burner accounts to vote for Li Jiancheng as "Emperor of the Millennium" and boost him on the social media leaderboards.

***

Li Xuanba dumped Li Zhiyun onto his Second Brother, tasking the little boy with supervising Li Shimin's studies so he wouldn't go hunting every single day. Meanwhile, Xuanba headed to the workshops adjacent to the villa, finally able to pursue something he had wanted to do ever since transmigrating:

Forge an iron wok.

Li Xuanba had originally assumed that as long as one had iron, making a wok was simple. Only after transmigrating and inquiring with the blacksmiths retained by his household did he discover that making an iron wok required surprisingly advanced metallurgy.

Just as only the finest artisans in antiquity could cast a ritual cauldron, a smith skilled enough to forge an iron wok that distributed heat evenly possessed the craftsmanship required to forge full suits of armor.

No wonder it wasn't until the Song dynasty, when the iron-smelting industry experienced unprecedented breakthroughs, that iron woks finally entered common households.

Though the Song dynasty was militarily inept, their equipment had been nothing short of top-tier.

It wasn't that the Duke of Tang's estate lacked smiths capable of making a wok, but such craftsmen were exclusively retained to forge armor for the family's nobles. There was no way Li Xuanba could have commandeered them just to make a cooking pot.

Every major estate came equipped with its own self-sustaining workshops for food, clothing, shelter, and transport, and a blacksmith's forge was naturally among them.

Now that the villa had been officially granted to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, all the estate’s laborers had become their personal retainers. Li Xuanba could finally command them to hone their ironworking techniques and forge an iron wok for him.

He hoped that once they had stir-fried dishes, he could gradually fix his Second Brother's awful eating habits. Right now, forcing Li Shimin to eat vegetables was harder than forcing him to swallow bitter medicine.

Li Xuanba found the master smith in charge of the forge and laid out the detailed specifications for the wok.

The lame old blacksmith looked at him with deep suspicion. "Third Young Master, do you truly just wish to forge a pot made of iron, and not a suit of armor?"

Li Xuanba replied, "It is merely an iron wok, meant only to satisfy the belly."

The old smith fell silent for a long time before letting out a sigh. "This old servant belongs to Third Young Master now; whatever Young Master wishes to forge, so it shall be. However, the requirements for this iron wok are exceptionally demanding. Our current furnace likely won't suffice; we will need one fitted with large bellows."

Li Xuanba asked with interest, "If you have the furnace, you can make it?"

The old smith said, "Whether I can or cannot, we will only know once we try."

Li Xuanba smiled. "Go ahead and experiment; do not fear waste. Leave the furnace, the fuel, and the iron ore to me. Once you've succeeded, I will have to trouble you to train more apprentices. When these woks are perfected, I intend to gift them to our relatives and friends."

The old smith asked, "You wish to forge many of them?"

Li Xuanba said, "Very many."

The old smith went silent once more.

"This old servant has a son of immense strength," the old smith began haltingly, voice strained. "If Third Young Master does not disdain him, could you perhaps grant him an errand?"

Li Xuanba replied, "I happen to be short of a bodyguard."

The old smith let out a long breath of relief. "Thank you, Third Young Master! This old servant will spare no effort!"

After offering a few encouraging words to the lame old blacksmith, Li Xuanba headed off, brimming with the joy of having unearthed a hidden gem, eager to share the good news with his Second Brother.

As expected of a ducal estate, its foundation ran unfathomably deep. Even a smith on an outlying villa was a master craftsman bold enough to claim he could produce armor.

Li Xuanba suspected that every single estate belonging to the Duke of Tang had a master artisan of this caliber overseeing things.

During the Northern and Southern Dynasties, anyone who held the rank of Duke commanded their own private army. Even in the present day, military commanders and their personal retinues were expected to provide their own armor. It was only natural that the Duke of Tang's estate harbored plenty of smiths skilled in armor-crafting.

When Li Shimin learned of this, he was overjoyed at first, but then grew suspicious. "Is this the norm? Doesn't that mean every noble and prominent clan can secretly forge armor and weapons to raise private armies?"

Li Xuanba replied, "Indeed they can. That is why, during times when the Emperor holds ironclad authority, discovering hidden armor in a household is treated as treason. We are merely forging iron woks, so you need not worry, Second Brother."

Li Shimin leaned in and asked in a low whisper, "Ah-Xuan, you won't make me charge onto the battlefield wearing an iron wok on my head in the future, will you?"

Li Xuanba was speechless. "As the son of a noble house, you are permitted to provide your own armor when going to war. Forging a few spare suits for yourself hardly counts as treason."

Li Shimin patted his chest, letting out a breath of relief. "That’s a relief. I like armor that is brilliant gold and dazzling with vibrant colors!"

Li Xuanba: "..."

*Brilliant gold and dazzling with vibrant colors? What kind of ostentatious, peacocking eyesore is that? Are you that afraid you won't stand out enough on the battlefield?*

Unbidden, Li Xuanba’s modern memory dredged up a specific historical snippet.

During Emperor Taizong of Tang’s eastern campaign against Goguryeo, for the ten thousand heavy cavalrymen he personally led, he had ordered: *“Procure golden lacquer to coat the iron armor, its luster surpassing refined gold, and dye it further with five-colored pigments.”* When they rode out, *“The golden brilliance rivaled the sun as they joined forces with Li Ji beneath the fortress walls.”*

His Second Brother truly, deeply loved being flashy.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第67章 可敢去西域一游
chunks.chineseText:
第67章 可敢去西域一游

=
　　搬到别庄后， 李玄霸整个人都松快许多。
　　李世民最初唉声叹气，念叨想娘娘想耶耶。不出一月，他就感受到了没有父母管的快乐， 不再提起父母。
　　至于李智云， 那就更开心了。
　　他因和李元吉年龄相近， 做什么都和李元吉在一起。平时他对李元吉多番忍让，早就忘记当个顽皮孩子该是什么模样。
　　李智云很想念当初才三四岁时，自己和李元吉分开教养的时候。
　　现在虽然他多了很多功课， 但只要不看到李元吉，他就很快乐。
　　而且他每旬都能回家，也不是很想念父母。
　　现在这兄弟三人就像是住校的中小学生， 还是每隔一周半就能回家那种，确实很难太想念父母。
　　有了宽敞的庄子， 李世民终于能把朋友们都唤到家中游玩。
　　他们从吟诗作对， 到入山林狩猎，玩开心了还去抢庄子中农夫的活干，一边拔草浇水，一边念着陶渊明的《饮酒》。
　　念着念着，不知道谁起了个调， 这群明朗的青年少年们从吟诗变成了大合唱。
　　“结庐在人境，而无车马喧。
　　问君何能尔？心远地自偏。
　　采菊东篱下， 悠然见南山。
　　山气日夕佳，飞鸟相与还。
　　此中有真意，欲辨已忘言。”
　　李玄霸经不起太阳毒晒， 别人种田， 他躲在树荫下偷懒。
　　李世民给李玄霸搬了把琴来。偷懒可以， 背景音乐就由李玄霸负责了。
　　李玄霸无语。
　　不愧是载歌载舞的大隋唐， 连种个田都要自带背景音乐是吗？
　　李智云年纪小拔了一会儿草，气喘吁吁地坐在三哥身边，拿起小鼓，帮三哥伴奏。
　　李玄霸面无表情地拨弄琴弦，李智云傻笑着击打手鼓，李世民领着一群年龄比他大的朋友们高唱《饮酒》。
　　一曲作罢，李世民意犹未尽。
　　“阿玄，琴的声音太慢了，换这个！”李世民让仆人抱来了琵琶。
　　李玄霸：“……”真是够了！
　　李玄霸铁青着脸，调好了琵琶的音，瓮声瓮气道：“弹什么？”
　　李世民手舞足蹈：“破阵乐！”
　　现在虽然没有《秦王破阵乐》，但军队出征的时候都会演奏“破阵乐”。“破阵乐”类似于一种音乐主题。李世民和李玄霸能熟练演奏琵琶后，老师教导的最多的乐曲就是破阵乐。
　　李玄霸叹气：“你种个田和打仗似的……行。”
　　所以为什么隋唐的勋贵子弟还要学琵琶啊！
　　李玄霸横抱着琵琶，跷着二郎腿，运指如飞。
　　李智云一手手鼓一手手铃，手铃击打手鼓，“锵锵咚咚”“叮叮当当”响个不停。
　　李世民撸起袖子：“小的们，努力干啊！”
　　杜如晦笑着踹了李世民屁股一脚，差点把李世民踹进田地里：“谁是小的们？你才是最小的！”
　　李世民揉了揉屁股，嬉皮笑脸道：“兄弟们，努力干！”
　　与李世民关系没有太紧密，只是因为李玄霸和李世民受杨广喜爱，所以被家人逼着来“陪孩童玩耍”的洛阳勋贵子弟们都不由笑出了声。
　　“战乐都奏响了，还不快冲！”
　　一群年轻人冲进了田地里。
　　农夫们看得心惊胆战。
　　快丰收了，你们可不要乱来啊！
　　李玄霸板着脸使劲拨弄琵琶，手指快得起了残影，用乐声宣泄心里的郁闷。
　　要是谁弄坏了田地，他就压着二哥去耕地补回来。
　　谁让二哥带头乱来？
　　非常幸运，这群没吃过苦的纨绔子弟们虽然没种过田，但都侍弄过花草。只是除草浇水的事，他们都做得有模有样。
　　虽然是一时兴起，但看着快丰收的麦田，他们兴奋不已，好像这块田地从头到尾都是他们自己种的似的。
　　“李二，等丰收的时候再邀我们来，我们自己收割。”一位勋贵子弟道。
　　李世民笑道：“好。我们再试试能不能自己磨麦子，做点心，举办个宴会。”
　　李玄霸阴阳怪气：“你是不是还要从现在开始养鸡养鸭啊？到时候要不要再举办个钓鱼会或者狩猎会啊？”
　　李世民对弟弟竖起大拇指：“有道理，准了。钓鱼狩猎交给我，养鸡养鸭交给你和小五。”
　　李智云拍着胸脯道：“好！交给我和三兄！”
　　李玄霸扶额：“小五啊，你不用帮我也答应了。”
　　众人皆笑不可抑。
　　李世民笑嘻嘻地拍着李玄霸的肩膀道：“阿玄，你自己的提议，必须自己负责。哥哥相信你。”
　　李玄霸琢磨着，是不是又该给二哥一点教训了。二哥搬到别庄之后，真是浪到飞起啊。
　　于是在送别宾客后，李玄霸对二哥发起了夺命三连：“二哥，功课做完了吗？交功课的时间快到了。你不会再想挨老师一次戒尺吧？”
　　李世民脸上的笑容消失，整个人就像是褪色了一样。
　　单纯的李智云还给二哥补刀：“二兄，你居然还没完成功课？你不是教导我，完成功课前不可以玩耍吗？”
　　李智云掰着手指头，数着李世民对他的教导：“你还说，要每日规定完成多少功课，这样才能养成良好的习惯。”
　　李世民脑袋耷拉，肩膀一垮：“我知错了，我也只是落了两日的功课……只是两日而已！”
　　李玄霸好心地问道：“需要我给老师写信为你辩解吗？就说你只是落了两日的功课而已。”
　　李世民气得跺脚：“不准说，告状狗！”
　　李世民转身跑走，一边跑一边骂：“阿玄告状狗！不理你了！”
　　李智云拉了拉三哥的袖子，老气横秋道：“二兄好幼稚啊。”
　　李玄霸摸了摸弟弟的脑袋。
　　没错，二哥就是幼稚鬼。
　　……
　　被李玄霸夺命三连后，李世民老实了一阵子，认认真真完成了功课。
　　当他完成功课的时候，李智云抱着半大的公鸡炫耀：“我和三兄养的鸡已经能吃了，时间刚好！”
　　李世民嗤笑：“这么小的鸡，还不够我一个人吃。吃肉还得看我。”
　　他活动了一下肩膀，开开心心地和李玄霸一起把功课寄了出去，拿起尘封的弓箭，约了仨俩射术最精湛的好友，去禁苑猎皇帝的猎物开宴会。
　　杨广得知此事时，对来洛阳探望他的太子杨昭笑道：“李二郎真是不把自己当外人。”
　　杨昭道：“李二郎一向直爽。”
　　杨广道：“李二郎和李三郎一个直爽，一个细心，相得益彰，不愧是双生子。齐王和他们相处久了之后，心也终于定下了一些，没让朕太过操心了。”
　　杨昭高兴道：“二弟终于成熟了。”
　　杨广失笑：“还不能叫成熟，只是稍好一些。”
　　父子二人唠了些家常，说起了正事。
　　杨广今年开凿了永济渠，修了汾阳宫，筑了长城，仍觉得不够。
　　监管张掖互市的吏部侍郎裴世矩察觉了杨广的心思，投杨广所好，将从西域商人那里打探的消息编写成《西域图记》三篇呈给杨广，盛赞西域珍宝，鼓动杨广征讨西域。
　　他甚至根据这些二手消息，在没有任何实地考察中，对杨广保证，“浑、厥可灭，混壹戎夏，其在兹乎”！
　　正觉得今年搞的大事还不够多，不够他评选千古一帝的杨广被戳中了心窝，当即下令让裴世矩经略西域。
　　原本负责经略西域和突厥的是长孙晟。
　　长孙晟对现在征讨西域一事持反对意见。
　　他认为经略西域不在于攻占了多少地，而在于能归化多少地。
　　以大隋的国力，想要征讨吐谷浑轻而易举。但国内如今接连征发大型徭役，已经没有足够的民力和物力将攻占的城池变成“归化”的城池。
　　如果当地没有完全归化大隋，只要大隋力有不逮，吐谷浑肯定会迅速回来，当地会立刻复叛。
　　最终大隋花费了大量人力物力，只得到了一个“攻城略地”的名声，得不到实际好处。
　　杨广认为长孙晟老了，太保守。
　　他倒没有和长孙晟生气，还是很尊敬长孙晟，只是劝说道：“长孙卿，你常年待在突厥，大概不知道现在的大隋有多强大。朕动用的民力，还不到大隋的九牛一毛，哪会没有人力物力去归化攻占地？再者大隋强盛，也不会力有不逮，让吐谷浑有机可乘。”
　　裴世矩也慷慨激昂地陈述自己对经略西域的谋略，让陛下放心交给他。
　　长孙晟见皇帝意已决，朝中将领也希望赶紧开战，他们才能掠夺更多的珍宝，获得更多的功勋，只能沉默。
　　杨广此次召太子来，就是安排太子监督运粮的事。
　　打仗不仅仅是兵将的事。每个兵将至少要配三到五个民夫保障其后勤。这些民夫都是徭役征发而来。
　　大隋不缺粮，缺的只是将粮食运到战场的民夫。
　　今年开凿永济渠、修长城和汾阳宫的时候民夫已经不足，强征了不少妇人服徭役。
　　虽然杨广刚登基就宣布取消妇人和奴婢的徭役，但现在大隋要做大事了，只能继续苦一苦大隋的妇人。
　　大隋没有明下令，但在前面的大工程都已经开始征发妇人服役的前提下，显然这次西征大部分服徭役的人都是妇人。
　　杨昭委婉劝谏道：“我听李三郎说，西域的珍宝只是西域商人随意找了些奇特的故事包装的普通物品，如火珠，只是普通的水晶球罢了。”
　　杨广也想起了此事。
　　但他立刻辩解道：“朕征讨吐谷浑，只是想要征讨不臣，一统南北，造就如汉武般广阔国土，与西域珍宝无关。”
　　杨昭道：“父皇雄心，儿自然知晓。只是父皇不是在继位之初就着手准备征讨高丽吗？何不等征讨完高丽后再图谋西北？”
　　杨广摆手道：“正因为要征讨高丽，才要先把吐谷浑打疼，让他不敢在朕征讨高丽时出手。太子，你没有上过战场，战略之事你不懂。唉，若不是朕不信任高颎，高颎最适合教导你。”
　　杨昭心道，如果高公在这里，一定会坚决反对。
　　这不是什么战略问题，而是今年百姓已经太疲惫了。
　　虽然今年征讨吐谷浑可能还能咬牙坚持，但看着父皇这几年的作风，杨昭很担心明年、后年、再后一年，若父皇还是如之前一样年年压榨民力，恐怕会生出祸端。
　　但杨昭又知道，父皇下定决心后就听不得人劝，特别是劝他休养生息，更是不可能。如果自己再劝下去，就是自己生出祸端了。
　　父皇最厌恶别人说他治下的大隋弱。休养生息就等于说现在他治下的大隋疲软，否定他的丰功伟业。
　　杨昭只能退一步：“裴世矩只是从西域商人那里得知的西域情况，不如长孙将军更了解西域。”
　　杨广道：“朕也是如此想。此次大军出征，长孙晟肯定要随军前往。”
　　杨昭这才松了口气，真心诚意道：“父皇英明！”
　　有长孙将军随行，此战至少不用担心胜负。待战胜吐谷浑后，多抢些牛羊珠宝填充国库，再以此为借口，请求父皇赦免一年赋税吧。
　　此事说完后，杨广想起杨昭所说李玄霸也精通西域，道：“李三郎既然熟悉西域，该让他也来好好学学。他近些时日身体好了许多，应该能去张掖。”
　　杨昭听到父皇居然从现在开始就要让李玄霸做事，心里很是惊讶。
　　李三郎在洛阳又做了什么让父皇高兴的事吗？父皇是真的想像汉武帝培养霍去病那样培养李三郎？但就算要培养大隋的霍去病，也该是去培养李二郎啊。
　　杨昭心思微转，不动声色道：“儿许久没见到李二郎李三郎，也该去和他们好好聚一聚了。此事可否由儿向李三郎提起？李三郎年幼，不一定想去张掖吃苦。若父皇直接询问，他或许不敢拒绝。”
　　杨广笑道：“看来你把李家二郎三郎当亲兄弟看待了。行，你先问问，若李三郎愿意，朕再下旨。李三郎若想去，李二郎肯定也闲不住。他们二人一起去吧。”
　　杨昭拱手：“是，儿明日就去拜访唐国公府。”
　　杨广脸上笑意淡去：“李二郎和李三郎不在唐国公府。他们兄弟二人被赶到城郊别庄居住了。你没必要去拜访唐国公府了。”
　　杨昭惊愕。
　　李二郎和李三郎如此优秀，还能被李渊赶去别院？唐国公府的后院又发生了什么事？
　　杨昭决定今日先去找弟弟杨暕睡一晚，询问东都最近发生的事。
　　杨昭道：“是。儿明日直接去拜访他们。这样也好，我也懒得递拜帖了，直接上门瞧瞧他们在做什么。”
　　听着杨昭故作顽皮的话，杨广恢复了笑容：“去吧。朕问虞世南李二郎和李三郎的学习进度，虞世南好几次都说李二郎沉迷狩猎，临到该交功课的时候才着急。你顺带去问问李二郎，是不是又忘记做功课了。”
　　杨昭失笑：“好。”
　　李世民和李玄霸万万没有料到，他们准备好了食材，正一群人在庭院里生火，想要自己做饭吃时，杨昭和杨暕居然不请自来。
　　李世民和李玄霸先行礼，然后李世民毫不客气地对杨暕抱怨：“二表兄，我之前邀请你，你说不想来。我可没有准备你的肉。”
　　杨暕让人运来一头肥瘦相宜的乳牛：“不用你准备，我自己准备了。你以为我想来陪你折腾吗？我就没有自己烤过肉！不是兄长非要来，我才不来。”
　　狩猎叫他就罢了，什么种地摸鱼自己生火做饭，我堂堂齐王怎么能做这种事！
　　杨暕幽怨地瞥了太子兄长一眼。
　　杨昭笑呵呵道：“我什么都没带。怎么，李二郎李三郎，要把表兄我赶走？”
　　李世民拍着杨暕带来的乳牛开心地笑道：“大表兄的肉，二表兄出了。随便吃！吃撑！”
　　李玄霸叹气：“以你们的厨艺，你确定是吃撑，而不是谁都吃不下去吗？”
　　房乔等人本来见到太子和齐王一起不请自来，还有些拘谨。
　　听到李世民和李玄霸你一言我一语，毫不客气地和齐王、太子开玩笑，他们紧张的心情轻松了许多。
　　虽然他们不敢再大声喧哗，但神情已经恢复了自然。
　　杨昭好奇地扫视了一眼李世民和李玄霸的朋友们。
　　李世民和李玄霸新交的朋友，齐王杨暕都知晓。他们许多朋友都是在杨暕的宴会上结识。
　　因李世民和李玄霸结交的多是寒门出身的官宦子弟和世家旁支，出身不好，年纪也轻，所以所有人都只当这是一群年轻子弟聚在一起做些纨绔事罢了，没有太在意。
　　杨昭本来也不在意。但他见这群人见到他和齐王不请自来，还很快就镇定自若的模样，心里有了计较。
　　物以类聚，人以群分。李二郎和李三郎很优秀，结交的朋友应该也都各有所长。
　　李二郎和李三郎结交的友人身份地位都比他们低，待他们入朝做官时肯定会提拔友人。这些人既是友人，也是他们未来在官场上人脉甚至下属。
　　杨昭虽对这些人的才华如何有些好奇，但没打算结交。
　　他身为太子，身边人才众多，没必要去抢夺表弟身边的朋友。再者将来如果他能继位，就连李二郎和李三郎都是他麾下的人才，他就更不需要在意李二郎李三郎结交的人了。
　　杨昭只是和善地对待李世民和李玄霸的朋友们，自言自己只是以两人表兄的身份来蹭一口吃的，不要太在意，给足了李世民和李玄霸面子。
　　杨暕懒得做表面功夫，搭着李世民的肩膀，去学人解牛。
　　“牛腿是我的！”
　　“牛腿好难烤熟啊，烤得不好吃怎么办？”
　　“嗯……为什么不能让厨子来！”
　　“让厨子来就没趣了。阿玄！你来帮二表兄烤牛腿！”
　　李玄霸：“啊？哦。”
　　行吧，在场大概只有自己勉强算得上会做饭了。
　　其实说是自己烤，也有其他仆人搭手，烧烤酱也早就调好了，李世民、李玄霸几人只是动动嘴皮子。
　　鸡飞狗跳一会儿，在场几人都找到了“自己动手”的乐趣，边吃边笑，还喝起了葡萄酒。
　　李玄霸原本是不想喝酒的，但李世民被李渊带着喝了几次酒，就迷上了酒的味道。
　　为了让二哥不变成酒鬼，他只能提前引导二哥爱上了唐太宗最爱的葡萄酒。
　　二哥果然与葡萄酒一见钟情，现在就开始学着酿造葡萄酒。
　　手工酿造的葡萄酒酒精度很低，李玄霸平时一杯倒，喝了他家二哥酿造的葡萄酒能三杯倒。李世民则喝撑了也不会醉。
　　杨昭本来不喜欢喝酒，抿了一口李二郎亲自酿造的葡萄酒，也爱上了这酸甜的味道。
　　杨暕则很嫌弃：“这和葡萄汁有什么区别？没有劲大的？”
　　李玄霸让人抱来陈酿的粟米酒。
　　杨暕揭开酒坛上的布嗅一口，满意道：“这才是酒。兄长，我给你满上！”
　　杨昭：“啊？我不喝……唉。”
　　杨昭愁眉苦脸地被杨暕拉着灌了三碗酒，吃了十串肉才把酒气压下去。
　　杨昭这食量，看得李玄霸心惊胆战。
　　他总算知道杨昭为什么这么胖了。一直听杨昭说在减肥了，减肥是这么减的？
　　李玄霸揉了揉已经吃撑的肚子，摇摇头离开。
　　饭饱酒足，李世民和李玄霸的友人们见太子和齐王都要留宿，知晓太子和齐王可能有话单独与李世民、李玄霸说。他们自然识趣地告辞。
　　李世民有点遗憾。他本来还准备了夜游活动呢。
　　李玄霸先派人打来凉水给三人洗脸，让三人醒了醒酒，才安排他们入浴更衣。
　　待换了一身衣服出来，杨昭和杨暕的酒意散去了大半。
　　杨暕倚着靠枕，腿架在坐榻的靠背上，懒洋洋道：“该说正事了。大德，父亲想让你跟着裴世矩去张掖。”
　　李世民瞪大眼睛：“什么？陛下要把阿玄流放张掖？我也要一起去！不能让阿玄一个人被流放！”
　　杨暕差点从坐榻上滚下来：“什么流放？我话里有流放两个字？”
　　李世民道：“张掖是西域苦寒之地，那不是流放吗？”
　　李玄霸瞥了二哥一眼，道：“哥，别耍宝了。”
　　李世民收起震惊的神情，对杨暕做了个鬼脸。
　　杨暕得知上当，把李世民拎到坐榻上使劲按压脑袋。
　　杨昭慢条斯理道：“二弟，别欺负李二郎。三郎，你曾说对西域很感兴趣，将来愿意效仿长孙将军，为父皇经略西域。父皇想要征讨吐谷浑，现在派裴世矩去打探西域的情况，你可敢去？”
　　李玄霸正色道：“太子殿下，我胆子很大。我愿意去。”
　　杨昭叹气：“张掖虽行商众多，很是繁华，但气候苦寒，你可能会不适应。”
　　李玄霸道：“我不惧艰苦，只想为陛下效力。”
　　李世民努力从杨暕的胳膊下挣脱出去，站在坐榻上举着双手蹦跳：“我要去！我也要去！”
　　“哎哟！李二郎，你踩到我了！”杨暕怒骂。
　　杨昭和李玄霸绷不住谈论正事的严肃表情了，忍俊不禁。
