Chapter 67: Dare You Take a Trip to the Western Regions?

After moving to the villa, Li Xuanba felt his entire being relax significantly.
Li Shimin had initially spent his days sighing and lamenting how much he missed his mother and father. Yet, within a month, he discovered the joy of living without parental supervision and stopped mentioning them altogether.
As for Li Zhiyun, he was even happier.
Because he was close in age to Li Yuanji, he did everything with him. In the past, he had been forced to yield to Li Yuanji so often that he had long forgotten what it felt like to be a mischievous child.
Li Zhiyun deeply missed the time when he was three or four years old, back when he and Li Yuanji were raised separately.
Although he now had a much heavier workload, as long as he didn't have to see Li Yuanji, he was perfectly content.
Furthermore, he could go home every ten days, so he didn't miss his parents all that much.
The three brothers were now like boarding students, the kind who could return home every week and a half, so it was truly difficult to miss their parents too intensely.

With the spacious villa at his disposal, Li Shimin was finally able to invite all his friends over to play.
They went from reciting poetry and composing couplets to hunting in the mountains. When they were in high spirits, they would even snatch the work from the farmhands on the estate, pulling weeds and watering crops while chanting Tao Yuanming’s "Drinking Wine."
As they chanted, someone started a rhythm, and this group of bright young men turned their poetry reading into a grand chorus.

"I build my hut within the realm of men,
Yet hear no noise of carriage or of steed.
You ask me how this can be done?
With a distant heart, the place itself becomes remote.
I pluck chrysanthemums beneath the eastern hedge,
And leisurely gaze upon the Southern Mountain.
The mountain air is lovely at dusk,
As the flying birds return together.
Within this lies the true meaning;
I wish to explain, but have forgotten the words."

Li Xuanba could not withstand the scorching sun, so while the others farmed, he hid in the shade of a tree to slack off.
Li Shimin brought a zither over to Li Xuanba. Slacking off was fine, but Li Xuanba was responsible for the background music.
Li Xuanba was speechless.
As expected of the song-and-dance-loving Sui Dynasty, did they even need to bring their own background music to farm?
Li Zhiyun, being young, pulled weeds for a while before sitting breathlessly beside his Third Brother, picking up a small drum to provide accompaniment.
Li Xuanba plucked the strings with an expressionless face, Li Zhiyun beat the hand drum with a silly grin, and Li Shimin led his older friends in a loud rendition of "Drinking Wine."
When the song ended, Li Shimin was still unsatisfied.
"A-Xuan, the zither is too slow! Switch to this!" Li Shimin had a servant bring over a pipa.
Li Xuanba: "..." Enough is enough!
With a dark face, Li Xuanba tuned the pipa and said in a muffled voice, "What shall I play?"
Li Shimin danced with excitement: "The 'Breaking the Formation' music!"
Although the "Prince of Qin Breaking the Formation" music did not yet exist, armies would always perform "Breaking the Formation" music when setting out on a campaign. It was a musical theme of sorts. After Li Shimin and Li Xuanba became proficient with the pipa, the piece their teacher taught them most often was the "Breaking the Formation" music.
Li Xuanba sighed: "You treat farming like a war... fine."
So why on earth did the noble sons of the Sui and Tang dynasties have to learn the pipa anyway!
Li Xuanba held the pipa horizontally, crossed his legs, and his fingers flew like lightning.
Li Zhiyun held a hand drum in one hand and a hand bell in the other, striking the bell against the drum, creating a constant "clang-clang-thump-thump" and "ding-ding-dang-dang" sound.
Li Shimin rolled up his sleeves: "Little ones, work hard!"
Du Ruhui laughed and kicked Li Shimin in the backside, nearly sending him into the field: "Who are you calling the little ones? You’re the youngest one here!"
Li Shimin rubbed his backside and said with a cheeky grin: "Brothers, work hard!"
The young nobles from Luoyang, who weren't particularly close to Li Shimin but had been forced by their families to "accompany the children" because Li Xuanba and Li Shimin were favored by Yang Guang, couldn't help but laugh out loud.
"The war music has sounded, charge!"
A group of young men rushed into the fields.
The farmers watched with trepidation.
The harvest is coming soon, please don't mess this up!
Li Xuanba kept a straight face and plucked the pipa vigorously, his fingers moving so fast they left afterimages, using the music to vent his inner frustration.
If anyone ruined the fields, he would force his Second Brother to plow them back to health.
Who told the Second Brother to lead the chaos?
Fortunately, while these pampered young masters who had never known hardship had never farmed, they had all tended to flowers and plants. They handled the weeding and watering quite competently.
Although it was a whim, they were incredibly excited to see the wheat fields nearing harvest, as if they had grown the entire field from start to finish themselves.
"Li Er, invite us back when it's time to harvest, we'll do it ourselves," one noble youth said.
Li Shimin laughed: "Alright. We'll also try to grind the wheat ourselves, make some pastries, and host a banquet."
Li Xuanba said sarcastically: "Are you going to start raising chickens and ducks now too? Do you want to host a fishing or hunting party while you're at it?"
Li Shimin gave his brother a thumbs up: "That makes sense, approved. I'll handle the fishing and hunting, you and Little Five can handle the chickens and ducks."
Li Zhiyun patted his chest: "Okay! Leave it to me and Third Brother!"
Li Xuanba clutched his forehead: "Little Five, you didn't have to agree for me too."
Everyone laughed uncontrollably.
Li Shimin patted Li Xuanba on the shoulder with a grin: "A-Xuan, it was your own suggestion, you must take responsibility for it. Brother believes in you."
Li Xuanba pondered whether it was time to teach his Second Brother another lesson. Ever since moving to the villa, his Second Brother had truly been running wild.
So, after seeing the guests off, Li Xuanba launched a deadly triple-threat attack on his Second Brother: "Second Brother, have you finished your homework? The deadline is almost here. You wouldn't want to taste the teacher's ruler again, would you?"
The smile vanished from Li Shimin's face, and he seemed to lose all his color.
The innocent Li Zhiyun even dealt a finishing blow: "Second Brother, you haven't finished your homework yet? Didn't you teach me that I shouldn't play until my homework is done?"
Li Zhiyun counted on his fingers, tallying up the lessons Li Shimin had taught him: "You also said that I must complete a set amount of work every day to build good habits."
Li Shimin’s head drooped, his shoulders slumped: "I know I was wrong, I only missed two days of work... it was only two days!"
Li Xuanba asked kindly: "Do you need me to write a letter to the teacher to plead your case? I'll just say you only missed two days of work."
Li Shimin stomped his feet in anger: "Don't you dare, you snitch!"
Li Shimin turned and ran away, shouting as he went: "A-Xuan is a snitch! I'm not talking to you anymore!"
Li Zhiyun tugged on his Third Brother's sleeve and said with the air of an old man: "Second Brother is so childish."
Li Xuanba patted his younger brother's head.
Indeed, Second Brother was a childish brat.
...
After being hit by Li Xuanba's triple-threat, Li Shimin behaved himself for a while and diligently completed his homework.
When he finished, Li Zhiyun held a half-grown rooster and showed it off: "The chicken Third Brother and I raised is ready to eat, just in time!"
Li Shimin scoffed: "Such a small chicken isn't even enough for me to eat alone. When it comes to meat, you have to look to me."
He loosened his shoulders, happily mailed off his homework with Li Xuanba, picked up his dusty bow and arrows, and invited a few friends with the best archery skills to hunt the Emperor's game in the Forbidden Park for a banquet.
When Yang Guang heard of this, he laughed to the Crown Prince Yang Zhao, who had come to Luoyang to visit him: "Li Er-lang really doesn't treat himself as an outsider."
Yang Zhao said: "Li Er-lang has always been straightforward."
Yang Guang said: "Li Er-lang is straightforward, and Li San-lang is meticulous; they complement each other perfectly. They are worthy of being twins. After spending time with them, the Prince of Qi has finally settled down a bit, and I don't have to worry about him as much."
Yang Zhao said happily: "My second brother has finally matured."
Yang Guang chuckled: "It's not quite maturity yet, just a little better."
The father and son chatted about domestic affairs before moving on to serious business.
This year, Yang Guang had excavated the Yongji Canal, built the Fenyang Palace, and constructed the Great Wall, yet he still felt it wasn't enough.
Pei Shiju, the Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel who oversaw the Zhangye trade market, sensed Yang Guang's intent. He catered to the Emperor's desires by compiling information gathered from Western Region merchants into three volumes of the "Western Regions Illustrated Record," praising the treasures of the Western Regions and inciting Yang Guang to conquer them.
Based on these second-hand reports, and without any field investigation, he even guaranteed to Yang Guang: "The Hun and the Turk can be destroyed; to unify the Rong and the Xia, this is the moment!"
Yang Guang, feeling that he hadn't done enough "great deeds" this year to qualify as an Emperor for the ages, was struck to the core and immediately ordered Pei Shiju to manage the Western Regions.
Originally, Changsun Sheng was responsible for managing the Western Regions and the Turks.
Changsun Sheng held a dissenting opinion on the current campaign in the Western Regions.
He believed that managing the Western Regions was not about how much land one conquered, but about how much land one could assimilate.
With the Sui Dynasty's national strength, conquering the Tuyuhun would be easy. However, the country had been conscripting large-scale labor, and there were no longer enough manpower or resources to turn the captured cities into "assimilated" ones.
If the local population was not fully assimilated into the Sui, the moment the Sui showed any weakness, the Tuyuhun would surely return, and the region would immediately rebel.
In the end, the Sui would spend vast amounts of manpower and resources only to gain a reputation for "conquering cities and seizing land," without gaining any actual benefits.
Yang Guang thought Changsun Sheng was old and too conservative.
He wasn't angry with Changsun Sheng and still respected him, but he advised: "Minister Changsun, you have spent so many years among the Turks that you probably don't know how powerful the Sui is now. The labor I have mobilized is not even a drop in the bucket for the Sui; how could we lack the manpower and resources to assimilate the conquered lands? Furthermore, the Sui is strong and will not show weakness, giving the Tuyuhun no opportunity."
Pei Shiju also passionately stated his strategy for managing the Western Regions, telling the Emperor to rest assured and leave it to him.
Seeing that the Emperor's mind was made up, and that the generals in the court also hoped for war so they could plunder more treasures and earn more merit, Changsun Sheng could only remain silent.
Yang Guang had summoned the Crown Prince this time to arrange for him to supervise the transport of grain.
War was not just a matter for soldiers and generals. Each soldier required at least three to five laborers to ensure logistics. These laborers were all conscripted through corvée labor.
The Sui did not lack grain; it only lacked the laborers to transport the grain to the battlefield.
This year, when excavating the Yongji Canal, building the Great Wall, and constructing the Fenyang Palace, the number of laborers was already insufficient, and many women had been forced into corvée labor.
Although Yang Guang had announced the cancellation of corvée labor for women and slaves upon his accession, the Sui now had great tasks to perform, so the women of the Sui had to suffer once more.
The Sui did not issue an explicit order, but given that women had already been conscripted for previous major projects, it was clear that the majority of those conscripted for this Western expedition would be women.
Yang Zhao tactfully advised: "I heard from Li San-lang that the treasures of the Western Regions are just ordinary items packaged with strange stories by merchants, like 'fire pearls,' which are merely ordinary crystal balls."
Yang Guang remembered this as well.
But he immediately defended himself: "My campaign against the Tuyuhun is merely to punish those who are insubordinate, to unify the north and south, and to create a territory as vast as that of Emperor Wu of Han; it has nothing to do with the treasures of the Western Regions."
Yang Zhao said: "I naturally understand your ambition, Father. But didn't you begin preparing to conquer Goguryeo at the start of your reign? Why not wait until after the conquest of Goguryeo to plan for the Northwest?"
Yang Guang waved his hand: "It is precisely because I intend to conquer Goguryeo that I must first hurt the Tuyuhun, so they dare not strike when I am campaigning against Goguryeo. Crown Prince, you have never been on the battlefield; you do not understand strategy. Alas, if I did not distrust Gao Jiong, he would be the most suitable person to teach you."
Yang Zhao thought to himself, if Minister Gao were here, he would certainly oppose this firmly.
This was not a strategic issue, but a matter of the people being too exhausted this year.
Although they might be able to grit their teeth and persist through the Tuyuhun campaign this year, looking at his father's style over the past few years, Yang Zhao was very worried about next year, the year after, and the year after that. If his father continued to squeeze the people's strength every year as he had before, disaster would surely arise.
But Yang Zhao also knew that once his father had made up his mind, he would not listen to advice, especially advice about resting and recuperating; that was impossible. If he continued to advise him, he would be the one to cause the disaster.
His father hated it when others said the Sui under his rule was weak. Resting and recuperating was equivalent to saying the Sui under his rule was feeble, denying his great achievements.
Yang Zhao could only take a step back: "Pei Shiju only learned about the Western Regions from merchants; he is not as knowledgeable about the region as General Changsun."
Yang Guang said: "I thought the same. For this army's expedition, Changsun Sheng will certainly accompany the troops."
Only then did Yang Zhao breathe a sigh of relief and say sincerely: "Father is wise!"
With General Changsun accompanying them, there would at least be no need to worry about the outcome of this battle. After defeating the Tuyuhun, they could seize more cattle, sheep, and jewelry to fill the national treasury, and then use that as an excuse to request that his father grant a one-year tax amnesty.
After this matter was settled, Yang Guang remembered what Yang Zhao had said about Li Xuanba also being proficient in the affairs of the Western Regions, and said: "Since Li San-lang is familiar with the Western Regions, he should be allowed to come and learn properly. His health has improved quite a bit recently; he should be able to go to Zhangye."
Yang Zhao was very surprised to hear that his father wanted to put Li Xuanba to work starting now.
What had Li San-lang done in Luoyang to make his father so happy? Was his father truly thinking of cultivating Li San-lang the way Emperor Wu of Han cultivated Huo Qubing? But even if he wanted to cultivate a Huo Qubing for the Sui, it should be Li Er-lang.
Yang Zhao's thoughts shifted, and he said calmly: "I haven't seen Li Er-lang and Li San-lang in a long time; I should go and have a good gathering with them. Could I be the one to bring this up to Li San-lang? Li San-lang is young and may not want to go to Zhangye to suffer. If Father asks him directly, he might not dare to refuse."
Yang Guang laughed: "It seems you treat the Li brothers as your own siblings. Very well, you ask him first. If Li San-lang is willing, I will issue a decree. If Li San-lang wants to go, Li Er-lang will certainly not be able to sit still. Let them both go together."
Yang Zhao bowed: "Yes, I will visit the Tang State Duke's mansion tomorrow."
The smile on Yang Guang's face faded: "Li Er-lang and Li San-lang are not at the Tang State Duke's mansion. The two brothers were driven out to live in a villa on the outskirts of the city. There is no need for you to visit the Tang State Duke's mansion."
Yang Zhao was astonished.
Li Er-lang and Li San-lang were so outstanding, yet they could be driven out to a villa by Li Yuan? What had happened in the inner courtyard of the Tang State Duke's mansion?
Yang Zhao decided to go and sleep at his younger brother Yang Jian's place tonight to ask about what had happened in the Eastern Capital recently.
Yang Zhao said: "Yes. I will visit them directly tomorrow. That is fine, I won't have to bother with submitting a calling card; I'll just go and see what they are doing."
Hearing Yang Zhao's feigned playfulness, Yang Guang smiled again: "Go. I asked Yu Shinan about the progress of Li Er-lang and Li San-lang's studies, and Yu Shinan said several times that Li Er-lang is addicted to hunting and only gets anxious when it's time to hand in his homework. You can ask Li Er-lang while you're there if he has forgotten to do his homework again."
Yang Zhao chuckled: "Very well."
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba never expected that just as they had prepared the ingredients and were starting a fire in the courtyard to cook for themselves, Yang Zhao and Yang Jian would arrive uninvited.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba bowed first, then Li Shimin complained to Yang Jian without ceremony: "Second Cousin, I invited you before, but you said you didn't want to come. I didn't prepare any meat for you."
Yang Jian had someone bring over a calf of perfect size: "I don't need you to prepare it, I brought my own. Do you think I want to come and suffer with you? I've never roasted meat myself! If it weren't for my brother insisting on coming, I wouldn't be here."
Hunting was one thing, but farming, fishing, and starting a fire to cook for himself—how could he, the dignified Prince of Qi, do such things!
Yang Jian cast a resentful glance at his Crown Prince brother.
Yang Zhao laughed heartily: "I didn't bring anything. What, are Li Er-lang and Li San-lang going to chase their cousin away?"
Li Shimin patted the calf Yang Jian brought and laughed happily: "Big Cousin's meat, Second Cousin's effort. Eat as much as you want! Eat until you're stuffed!"
Li Xuanba sighed: "With your cooking skills, are you sure we'll be stuffed, or that no one will be able to eat it at all?"
Fang Qiao and the others had been a bit reserved when they saw the Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi arrive uninvited.
But hearing Li Shimin and Li Xuanba joking with the Prince of Qi and the Crown Prince without any ceremony, their nervous tension eased significantly.
Although they didn't dare to be loud, their expressions had returned to normal.
Yang Zhao curiously scanned Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's friends.
The Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, knew all of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's new friends. Many of these friends had been met at Yang Jian's banquets.
Because Li Shimin and Li Xuanba mostly associated with low-ranking officials from humble backgrounds and branches of noble families, their status was low and they were young, so everyone assumed this was just a group of young people gathering to do some spoiled things, and didn't pay much attention to them.
Yang Zhao hadn't intended to pay attention either. But seeing that this group remained calm and composed even after he and the Prince of Qi arrived uninvited, he began to think.
Birds of a feather flock together. Li Er-lang and Li San-lang were outstanding, so the friends they made should also have their own strengths.
The friends Li Er-lang and Li San-lang associated with were lower in status than them, so they would surely promote these friends when they entered the government. These people were not just friends, but also their future connections and even subordinates in the officialdom.
Although Yang Zhao was curious about their talents, he had no intention of befriending them.
As the Crown Prince, he had plenty of talent around him; there was no need to snatch his cousins' friends. Furthermore, if he were to succeed to the throne in the future, even Li Er-lang and Li San-lang would be his subordinates, so he had even less need to care about the people they associated with.
Yang Zhao treated Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's friends kindly, saying he was only here as their cousin to grab a bite to eat and that they shouldn't mind him, giving Li Shimin and Li Xuanba plenty of face.
Yang Jian couldn't be bothered with superficial pleasantries; he threw his arm around Li Shimin's shoulder and went to learn how to butcher the calf.
"The leg is mine!"
"The leg is so hard to roast, what if it doesn't taste good?"
"Hmm... why can't we let the cook do it!"
"It wouldn't be fun if the cook did it. A-Xuan! Come and help Second Cousin roast the leg!"
Li Xuanba: "Ah? Oh."
Fine, he was probably the only one here who could barely be considered a cook.
Actually, while they said they were roasting it themselves, other servants were helping, and the barbecue sauce had already been prepared; Li Shimin, Li Xuanba, and the others were just doing the talking.
After a bit of chaos, everyone found the joy of "doing it yourself," eating and laughing, and even drinking wine.
Li Xuanba had originally not wanted to drink, but Li Shimin had been taken drinking by Li Yuan several times and had become obsessed with the taste of wine.
To prevent his Second Brother from becoming an alcoholic, he had to guide him to fall in love with the grape wine that Emperor Taizong of Tang loved most.
His Second Brother had indeed fallen in love with grape wine at first sight and was now learning how to brew it.
Hand-brewed grape wine had a very low alcohol content; Li Xuanba usually got drunk after one cup, but could handle three cups of his Second Brother's brew. Li Shimin, on the other hand, wouldn't get drunk even if he drank until he was stuffed.
Yang Zhao had originally disliked drinking, but after sipping the grape wine Li Er-lang had brewed himself, he fell in love with the sweet and sour taste.
Yang Jian was very disdainful: "What's the difference between this and grape juice? Isn't there anything stronger?"
Li Xuanba had someone bring over some aged millet wine.
Yang Jian lifted the cloth on the jar and took a sniff, satisfied: "This is real wine. Brother, let me fill yours!"
Yang Zhao: "Ah? I'm not drinking... sigh."
Yang Zhao was dragged by Yang Jian to drink three bowls of wine with a miserable face, and only after eating ten skewers of meat did he manage to suppress the alcohol.
Li Xuanba was terrified by Yang Zhao's appetite.
He finally understood why Yang Zhao was so fat. He had always heard Yang Zhao say he was on a diet; was this how he dieted?
Li Xuanba rubbed his stuffed stomach and shook his head as he walked away.
After they were full of food and wine, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's friends saw that the Crown Prince and the Prince of Qi were staying the night, and knowing that they might have things to discuss with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba in private, they tactfully took their leave.
Li Shimin felt a bit regretful. He had even prepared a night tour activity.
Li Xuanba first sent people to fetch cold water for the three of them to wash their faces and sober up, before arranging for them to bathe and change.
After they changed their clothes and came out, the alcohol had mostly worn off for Yang Zhao and Yang Jian.
Yang Jian leaned against a cushion, his legs propped up on the back of the couch, lazily saying: "Time for business. Da-de, Father wants you to follow Pei Shiju to Zhangye."
Li Shimin's eyes widened: "What? The Emperor wants to exile A-Xuan to Zhangye? I'm going too! I won't let A-Xuan be exiled alone!"
Yang Jian nearly rolled off the couch: "What exile? Did I use the word exile?"
Li Shimin said: "Zhangye is a cold and bitter place in the Western Regions; isn't that exile?"
Li Xuanba glanced at his Second Brother and said: "Brother, stop playing the fool."
Li Shimin put away his shocked expression and made a face at Yang Jian.
Realizing he had been tricked, Yang Jian grabbed Li Shimin and pressed his head down hard onto the couch.
Yang Zhao said in a measured tone: "Second Brother, don't bully Li Er-lang. San-lang, you once said you were very interested in the Western Regions and would be willing to emulate General Changsun and manage the Western Regions for Father in the future. Father wants to conquer the Tuyuhun and is now sending Pei Shiju to investigate the situation in the Western Regions; do you dare to go?"
Li Xuanba said solemnly: "Your Highness, I am very bold. I am willing to go."
Yang Zhao sighed: "Although Zhangye has many merchants and is very prosperous, the climate is cold and bitter; you might not adapt."
Li Xuanba said: "I do not fear hardship; I only wish to serve the Emperor."
Li Shimin struggled to break free from Yang Jian's arm, stood on the couch, and jumped up with both hands raised: "I want to go! I want to go too!"
"Ouch! Li Er-lang, you stepped on me!" Yang Jian cursed.
Yang Zhao and Li Xuanba could no longer maintain their serious expressions and couldn't help but laugh.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第68章 杨昭的推心置腹
chunks.chineseText:
第68章 杨昭的推心置腹

=
　　杨暕和李世民装模作样打了起来。
　　杨昭和李玄霸懒得理睬两个幼稚鬼， 让他们继续胡闹，移到隔壁继续谈论正事。
　　杨昭叹气：“阿孩这性格……唉，我真是担心啊。”
　　阿孩是齐王杨暕的小字。李玄霸看着杨昭愁眉不展的模样， 安慰道：“齐王现在已经成熟多了。”
　　在李玄霸的提醒下， 杨暕不仅与元氏妇断了联系， 还揪出了几个打着他的名义行不法之事的人。史书中列举的乔令则、库狄仲锜、陈智伟等人都在其列。
　　李玄霸看得出来，杨暕能反应这么迅速，定是太子暗中动手， 帮杨暕铲除了府中的不稳定因素。
　　看出这一点后，他有点敬佩这个大隋太子。
　　身在大隋这混乱的皇室中，亲眼看到了自己父亲如何杀兄杀弟， 杨昭虽有心计，却对杨暕是真心好。
　　这可能也有杨昭很自信， 绝对不会被杨暕取代的缘故。
　　但杨昭能如此自信， 正说明他的才干和声望，甚至对父皇心情的揣摩都远胜过杨暕。这也是他优秀的证明。
　　杨昭道：“父皇即将西征。以父皇的性格，一定会御驾亲征，我会随行。到时我会请求父皇让阿孩坐镇京城。唉，我本来想让你帮我看着阿孩， 你也要去西边，我真不知道该找谁了。”
　　李玄霸道：“我不过是孩童， 即使能明辨是非，也很难劝服齐王。齐王身边应当有老成持重之人。”
　　杨昭扶额：“阿孩这性格和父皇差不多，听不得老成持重之人的劝谏……罢了， 我不说这个了。大德， 我本来有些担忧你心思过于深沉， 太过喜欢钻营。”
　　李玄霸没回答。他当然看得出来杨昭对二哥的好意更真心。
　　这很正常。因为自己也没有真心。
　　杨昭接着道：“不过思及你为了救朝中忠良， 冒险向我泄露父皇对我的怨言；如今你又在李建成的咄咄逼人之下自愿多次让步。我想我错怪你了。李三郎为人仁善赤忱，手段并不是品德的表现。”
　　杨昭拱手行礼：“表兄向你道歉。”
　　李玄霸惊讶地将杨昭扶起来：“太子殿下，何至于此？”
　　杨昭笑道：“就算我不道歉，以你的性格，仍旧会与我为善。但我心里过不去。”
　　他从弟弟那里得知李玄霸和李世民在东都的遭遇后，长吁短叹许久，心里堵得难受。
　　李玄霸在京城的一些手段，如果不看他的年龄，将他当做成年人，那么李玄霸的水平并不高超。
　　杨昭和李玄霸接触许久，确定李玄霸的心思确实深沉。比如提前对铺子做的打算，就确实存了和李建成争夺利益的心思。
　　虽然杨昭很理解李玄霸的处境，也主动帮助了李玄霸。但李玄霸如此年幼就城府过深，难免让人不适。
　　所以他对杨暕和至交提起李玄霸时，都告诉他们李玄霸才华横溢，可以结交，但不要深交。
　　此次他来洛阳，杨暕嘲笑了他一番，说他错看了李玄霸。
　　于公，李玄霸提议文人写词，将父皇在声乐上的爱好转移到了创建新的文人词上，从广召乐工变成广召文人，连薛道衡都夸赞李玄霸；
　　于私，李玄霸在李建成来洛阳后两次主动退让，一次住进了靠偏门的小院，一次干脆搬出了本家住进了别庄，成功与李建成修复关系。
　　“大德只是聪慧，但他的心很好。”杨暕道，“对朝堂，他能委婉劝谏父皇；对小家，他以兄弟和睦为重。是兄长错看了他。对了，这次你和我去别庄，会见到一个叫李智云的小孩。那是李家庶出的五郎。”
　　杨暕说起李智云因学习比李元吉优秀，自己和生母被李元吉侮辱的事。
　　“他们把李五郎也带到了别庄照顾，避免李五郎和李四郎再起冲突。”杨暕道，“听大雄说，他本来没想这么细，是大德的提议。”
　　说完一大堆话后，杨暕洋洋得意，得意得甚至用上了年幼时的称谓：“阿兄，你总说我识人不清。这次我识人绝对比你清！”
　　杨昭听了杨暕之言，又惊讶又欣慰。
　　弟弟这一番说辞，很明显真的有认真观察和思考。
　　弟弟幼时十分聪慧，长大后却懒得用脑子，让自己十分担忧。
　　杨昭从来都不担心杨暕抢自己的太子之位。如果杨暕动手，自己什么都不需要做，只要他有夺嫡的意图，父皇就绝对不会容忍他。
　　他是真的担心弟弟做事不过脑子，惹父皇震怒。
　　现在弟弟终于用上了脑子，杨昭都忍不住热泪盈眶了。
　　杨暕得意地把杨昭带到李世民和李玄霸居住的别庄。杨昭看见趴在正在烤肉的李玄霸背上撒娇的李家五郎时，彻底相信了杨暕的话。
　　小孩对好恶感知十分明锐，而且李玄霸没有必要讨好庶出的幼弟。所以李玄霸对李五郎表现出的善意都是真实的。
　　连对庶出弟弟都如此友好，李玄霸确实心善。
　　杨昭反省后，就决定和李玄霸坦白并道歉。
　　李玄霸很尴尬。
　　杨昭其实没必要道歉。论迹不论心，杨昭一直在帮他。若不算那只有自己能确认的救命之恩，其实是自己欠杨昭许多人情。
　　毕竟虽然他知道杨昭那时不回大兴会病死，但未来既然已经改变，当事人并不知晓自己会遭遇的事。他对杨昭所说的话，也只是让杨昭避开杨广的猜忌而已。
　　至于杨昭在背后说自己心机深沉，喜欢钻营……咳，杨昭说的是真的。自己还没小气到别人说真话还记恨的程度。
　　现在杨昭因为自己不存在的品德为自己道歉，李玄霸难免脚指头抠紧鞋底。
　　李玄霸对着一墙之隔的二哥把这里的事用心声说了一遍，然后在心里大喊：【救命！赶紧过来！】
　　李世民隔着墙给了他一个【哈】，隔了一会儿，又传过来一个【哈】。
　　最后，他在李玄霸的期盼中，传来了一个超级洪亮的【不】字。
　　李玄霸脸色一垮。这个二哥不能要了。
　　他只能自己缓解尴尬的气氛：“表兄何出此言？表兄照顾我良多，我感谢表兄还来不及。至于表兄的误会……”
　　李玄霸顿了顿，苦笑道：“表兄不是误会。我确实善钻营。高老师和宇文老师都提醒过我，不要太过依赖‘术’，会移了心性。表兄看人很准。”
　　杨昭道：“你这样说，我更无地自容了。高公和宇文公会提醒你不要移了心性，我却只是……唉。”
　　杨昭皱起了他的大胖脸，像一个超大的包子：“这样一想，我何尝不是落入了‘术’中，差点移了心性？”
　　太子之“术”，也是“术”啊。
　　李玄霸赶紧转移话题：“表兄，既然话已经说开了，我们就别提了。继续说西域之事可好？陛下不是想要征讨高丽吗？听闻陛下已经在做准备了，怎么突然又要去征讨吐谷浑？”
　　杨昭见李玄霸的耳根都红了，心中莞尔，对李玄霸真实的性情又多了几分认识。
　　他顺从地转移话题，埋怨道：“是吏部侍郎裴世矩献策。”
　　杨昭一直将李玄霸当做同龄贤才对待，现在误会解除，他也没有将李玄霸看作孩童，很仔细地将裴世矩之事告知了李玄霸。
　　李玄霸说是学习，其实相当于是给裴世矩当直接下属，需要多了解裴世矩。
　　李玄霸一边听杨昭对裴世矩的评价，一边在心中把裴世矩相关的史书记载搜索了出来。
　　裴世矩，贞观年间改名裴矩，在史书中是超低配的长孙晟。但因为《大唐双龙传》中他的角色是石之轩的马甲，戏份颇重，所以知名度比长孙晟高多了。
　　裴世矩是隋唐两朝重臣，他在隋唐的表现完全不一样。
　　在大隋时，他是隋炀帝身边“选曹七贵”之一，曲意奉承隋炀帝的喜好，撺掇和支持隋炀帝耗费大量民力攻打吐谷浑和高丽，从不谏诤。
　　隋炀帝接待外藩使臣和商人时，要求百姓必须身着盛装没有盛装就不准出门，召集四方艺人在端门街陈列百戏，店肆在店门口大摆宴席让番民白吃白喝，甚至把树上都裹了丝绸……这些建议，都是裴世矩提的。
　　他在西域也行了如长孙晟的离间之举。
　　长孙晟实施离间计后，不仅成功分裂了突厥，被分裂的突厥可汗们仍旧很喜爱长孙晟，丝毫不认为是长孙晟和大隋的错。
　　隋文帝时的北疆在长孙晟的经略下十分安稳。
　　裴世矩离间之后，所有人都知道是他在行离间之计，对大隋非常愤怒。东突厥始毕可汗因此拒绝向隋炀帝进贡，还带兵围了隋炀帝。
　　隋炀帝时的北疆在裴世矩的经略下战火频发。
　　说他是亡隋之臣，一点都不夸张。
　　但裴世矩辅佐李渊时经略西域却稳扎稳打，运用“远交近攻”之策，给唐朝留下了足够休养生息的空间，让李渊派李世民平定天下时，没有遭遇后方危机。
　　唐太宗继位后，裴世矩又常直言劝谏唐太宗的过失，帮唐太宗顺利度过了继位之初的焦头烂额。
　　唐太宗任裴世矩为民部尚书。裴世矩撑着八十岁的高龄帮唐太宗理顺了一团乱麻的户籍，在贞观元年末病逝。唐太宗很感激他，给他的谥号是“敬”。
　　观裴世矩在唐朝的行为举止，是名副其实的佐唐忠直之臣。
　　李玄霸：【裴世矩佞于隋而忠于唐，非其性之有变也；君恶闻其过，则忠化为佞，君乐闻直言，则佞化为忠。是知君者表也，臣者景也，表动则景随矣。】
　　墙那边：【啊？】
　　李玄霸：【后世《资治通鉴》中对裴世矩的评价。】
　　墙那边：【啊？？】
　　李玄霸：【夸你呢！】
　　墙那边：【哦。】
　　墙那边又传来哐当的声音。
　　李玄霸和杨昭同时扶额。
　　“他们难道还在打？”
　　“唉！”
　　李玄霸和杨昭的正事谈论不下去了。
　　杨昭草草总结：“裴世矩颇具才干，你跟随他会学到很多本事。但此人过分钻营……”
　　说到这，杨昭想起自己刚说过李玄霸善钻营，不由失笑。
　　“你可别学他，更加钻营了。”杨昭开玩笑道，“他的钻营已经失了忠直之心了。”
　　李玄霸道：“不会。表兄此次也要随陛下亲征，表兄的身体吃得消吗？”
　　杨昭笑道：“你别小看我，我也是能开强弓的。我陪父皇西行，你知道父皇喜好，我这一路也一定很舒坦，不会受累。”
　　他叹了口气，笑容淡去：“你心智早熟不似孩童，我就直说，不找借口了。当年父皇和叔父皆有战功，唯独伯父留守后方。群臣都支持父皇，是真的不服他啊。父皇亲征，我无论如何也要随行的。蹭军功啊，明白吗？”
　　李玄霸点头：“明白了。”杨昭确实心思通透。
　　杨广每次亲征都是修个大宫殿住进去，马车也像移动的行宫一样华丽。他出征时，皇后妃嫔公主，宫女乐工歌伎，都会随行，亲征路上确实很舒服。
　　李玄霸道：“表兄要保重身体。”
　　杨昭颔首微笑：“你也一样。特别是你师从高公和宇文公，可别学了他们的刚直。遇到不能劝谏的事就不要劝谏，命没了，劝谏也不会成功。留得一条命在，你才能做更多的事。明白吗？你之前委婉的劝谏就很好。”
　　李玄霸知道太子是真心劝告，拱手道：“是。谢表兄提点。”
　　墙那边又传来哐当噪音。
　　杨昭扶着额头慢吞吞下地：“过去看看吧，我担心他俩把屋里都砸了。”
　　李玄霸跟着杨昭快速往隔壁走。
　　隔壁房间，李世民和杨暕正各拿了一根竹竿，身上绑了个毛皮抱枕，开心地对打。
　　李玄霸看着满地狼藉，脸色青黑。
　　你们要打出去打啊，别砸东西！
　　杨昭苦笑：“别生气，别生气，我赔，表兄赔给你！阿孩！住手！你的岁数比大雄大一倍，你还要脸吗！”
　　杨暕恼羞成怒：“不准叫我阿孩！”
　　李玄霸跑步向前，揪住李世民头顶的小揪揪使劲扯，然后转头对窗户道：“小五！我不是让你睡觉了吗！”
　　李智云从窗户探头：“我听见好大的动静，就很好奇……啊，三兄别生气！我这就去睡！”
　　李世民惨叫：“别扯了别扯了，发髻要掉了！”
　　杨昭：“阿孩啊，你能不能让我省点心？”
　　杨暕怒斥：“都说了不要叫我阿孩！”
　　李智云又从窗户探出小脑袋，捂嘴偷笑。
　　……
　　第二日，李智云就笑不出来了。
　　李智云眼泪汪汪：“啊？二兄和三兄都要去张掖，那我呢？不要丢下我一个人啊，我会害怕。”
　　李玄霸道：“你暂时回家。李元吉被父亲教训得很厉害，他不敢再欺负你。”
　　李世民揉着李智云的脑袋道：“等我和阿玄回来会检查你的功课，不要偷懒。”
　　李智云抱住二哥和三哥的手臂：“不要！我不要回去！我要和你们一起去！你们能去，我也能去！呜哇！我不要！”
　　李智云这些时日真是太开心了，可没开心几月，就要回到唐国公府。李智云一想到在唐国公府与李元吉一起上课的日子，就头皮发麻。
　　李元吉是可能不敢欺负自己了，但自己仍旧要和李元吉一起学习啊。而且为了照顾李元吉，他仍旧只能藏拙。
　　不想藏拙！不想被李元吉拖累学习进度！想被夸！
　　在这里，二哥三哥每天都会夸他聪明，功课做好了，还有很多奖励。
　　不要回去，不要嗷嗷嗷！！！
　　李智云发挥出了李家人（除了李玄霸）的特长，瞬间哭成了泪人。
　　李世民见状，眼泪也不由涌了出来，抱着李智云一同痛哭。
　　李玄霸把胳膊从李智云怀里抽出来，狠狠踹了二哥一脚：“你哭什么啊！”
　　李世民呜呜道：“不知道，就是忍不住。”
　　我X你大爷的……李玄霸把粗口艰难地咽下去。
　　李世民这一跟着哭，李玄霸都不好和李智云讲道理了。
　　李智云不是不懂道理，不知道他这个年龄无法远行。他只是真的怕再和李元吉一同学习。
　　哭累之后，李智云很懂事地认错，说自己一定会乖乖等二哥三哥回来。
　　李世民见李智云这么懂事，又哭了一场。
　　李玄霸忍无可忍，一脚把李世民踹翻在地：“闭嘴！别哭了！”
　　李智云目瞪口呆。
　　天啦！三兄居然能把二兄踹翻！二兄还是我那个病弱的二兄吗！
　　他赶紧捂住嘴，不敢再哭。
　　只是没站稳的李世民拍了拍衣服上的灰尘，抱怨道：“阿玄，你的血是冷的吗？这么感动都不哭。”
　　李玄霸的白眼翻得一点眼珠子都看不见：“谢谢，你在娘胎里把我的泪腺都带走了，这辈子我的眼泪大概都由你帮着流了，所以你才变成现在这样的大哭包。”
　　“扑哧。”李智云努力捂住嘴。
　　李世民哭不出来了。
　　他敲了一下李智云的脑袋，对李玄霸抱怨道：“别胡说，小心小五当真。”
　　李智云捂着嘴小声道：“我才不会当真，我不笨。”
　　李世民擦干眼泪，像雨过天晴一样露出明朗的笑容：“好，小五不笨。小五乖乖在家里等你二兄和三兄回来。如果李元吉再欺负你，你就向娘亲告状，学你告状狗三兄，当一只可爱的告状小狗。”
　　李智云点头：“好，我是告状小狗。”
　　李玄霸：“……”能说出这句话，你还说你不笨？我愚蠢的弟弟啊。
　　送李智云回去的时候，李世民和李玄霸也暂时回家。
　　他们已经答应皇帝去张掖，这件事就定下来了，父母反对也无法更改。
　　李渊和窦夫人的脸色都很难看，想把李世民和李玄霸揍一顿，又舍不得。
　　李渊找人给两个孩子用细铜丝赶制了软甲小褂。铜丝软甲做出来后，他又觉得软甲太过沉重，又命人拆改了自己的披甲，给两个孩子做了一身皮制护甲。
　　窦夫人挨家挨户找上了曾经去过张掖的贵妇人家中，询问她们在张掖生活需要注意什么，给李世民和李玄霸准备药物和衣物。
　　李建成也想去。但问了弟弟们只是去张掖市集学习后，他就歇了心思。
　　唐国公府消息很灵通，已经知道皇帝想要对吐谷浑动手。
　　以皇帝如今对李渊的信任，李渊肯定也会随军去混功勋。李建成若想上战场，可以与李渊一起去。
　　李渊和窦夫人还给裴世矩备上重礼，希望裴世矩照顾好两个孩子。
　　裴世矩拒绝了几次都拒绝不了，苦笑不已。
　　哪还需要唐国公给自己送礼让自己照顾好李二郎李三郎啊，他都想反过来送礼，求李二郎李三郎照顾好自己。
　　陛下真是会使唤人，自己经略西域，还带着两个孩子同去？就是汉武帝培养霍去病，也不是这个培养法啊。
　　李渊和窦夫人还求了长孙晟，让李世民和李玄霸在长孙府小住一段时日。
　　长孙家和李家已经定亲，李渊和窦夫人原本不需要特意请求，长孙晟就会帮助李世民和李玄霸。但无奈长孙晟生病了。让长孙晟在病中为李世民和李玄霸授课，确实为难人。
　　幸亏长孙晟病得不重，体谅了李渊和窦夫人的父母之心。
　　李世民和李玄霸来到长孙府后，发现高夫人的神情很憔悴。
　　李世民把长孙无忌拖到角落询问后，对李玄霸道：“伯父不放心裴世矩，陛下也更信任伯父。伯父要带病西行，领走一路为大隋打探吐谷浑的消息。”
　　李玄霸皱眉。史书中没写这一段啊。
　　不过史书中虽然没写，但经略西域本就是长孙晟的特长，杨广又对长孙晟很信任，征讨吐谷浑可能不会特意绕开长孙晟。
　　再者，征讨吐谷浑是杨广对外战争中难得的大胜。
　　虽然之后没能归化，隋末吐谷浑卷土重来，比之前更强了。杨广无论是分裂突厥，还是攻打吐谷浑和高丽，都像是给对方送经验似的，给唐朝帮敌人升级刷装备。
　　但征讨吐谷浑如此顺利，难道长孙晟真的在这其中做了什么？
　　李玄霸捏了捏下巴，沉思。
　　长孙晟和裴世矩根据西域商人的二手消息画地图搜集消息不同，长孙晟是实干派。他经略西域，就是要亲自走遍要经略的地方，甚至陪突厥可汗打了几年猎。
　　若长孙晟要对吐谷浑动手，肯定会亲自潜进吐谷浑打探消息。
　　而长孙晟在明年病逝，难道和此次带病西行有关？
　　李世民叹气：“长孙四郎希望我们能劝他父亲别去西域。我们怎么劝？”
　　李玄霸不怀好意道：“我来。这时候就要我放绝招了。”不管明年长孙晟的病逝是不是和此次带病西行有关，先阻止再说！
　　李世民倒吸一口气：“刀下留情！”
　　李玄霸：【你丈人可能会在明年病逝。说不定就是因为这次……啊！】
　　李世民拉着李玄霸就跑，差点把李玄霸拽摔倒：“赶紧去扎他心口一刀！赶紧的！对了，我能听吗？”
　　李玄霸一边跑一边道：“我建议你别听。”
　　李世民松了口气，欣喜道：“连我都不能听，那这刀可太狠了，我相信我们稳了！”
　　李玄霸无语，在心里道：【这是稳了的问题吗？难道不是你该担心你妻子和大舅子的问题吗！】
　　李世民小声道：“你都说了我和观音婢肯定会成婚，我还怕什么？就算丈人病逝，他们应该也无事……就是过得不好，对吧？”
　　李玄霸叹了口气，点头。
　　李世民勾起嘴角，一把推开长孙晟书房的门，把弟弟往里面一推，然后把门关上。
　　“离开离开，都离开，阿玄有陛下的口谕要告诉伯父，赶紧走。”
　　李世民把仆人全部驱赶走，自己坐到台阶上，双手托腮，等着书房里的动静。

Chapter 68: Yang Zhao’s Heart-to-Heart

Yang Ji and Li Shimin were putting on a show of fighting. 
Yang Zhao and Li Xuanba, too lazy to pay any mind to the two childish spirits, let them continue their rowdiness and moved to the next room to discuss serious matters.
Yang Zhao sighed, "A-Hai’s personality... alas, I am truly worried."
A-Hai was the childhood nickname of the Prince of Qi, Yang Ji. Watching Yang Zhao’s furrowed brow, Li Xuanba comforted him, "The Prince of Qi has matured quite a bit recently."
Under Li Xuanba’s earlier reminders, Yang Ji had not only severed ties with the Yuan woman but had also rooted out several individuals who had been using his name to commit illicit acts. The figures listed in historical records—Qiao Lingze, Kudi Zhongqi, Chen Zhiwei, and others—were all among those purged.
Li Xuanba could tell that for Yang Ji to react so swiftly, the Crown Prince must have acted in the shadows to help him clear out the unstable elements within his estate.
Having realized this, he felt a touch of admiration for this Crown Prince of the Great Sui.
Living within the chaotic imperial family of the Great Sui and having witnessed with his own eyes how his father had killed his own brothers, Yang Zhao, despite his own schemes, was genuinely kind to Yang Ji.
This might also be because Yang Zhao was confident enough to know he would never be replaced by Yang Ji.
Yet, Yang Zhao’s ability to be so confident was precisely proof that his talent, reputation, and even his grasp of the Emperor’s temperament were far superior to Yang Ji’s. This was proof of his excellence.
Yang Zhao said, "Father is about to launch a western expedition. Given his personality, he will certainly lead the campaign in person, and I will be accompanying him. When that time comes, I will request that Father leave A-Hai to oversee the capital. Alas, I had originally hoped you could help me keep an eye on A-Hai, but since you are also heading west, I truly do not know who else to turn to."
Li Xuanba replied, "I am merely a child. Even if I can distinguish right from wrong, it would be difficult for me to persuade the Prince of Qi. There should be someone mature and steady by his side."
Yang Zhao rubbed his forehead, "A-Hai’s personality is much like Father’s; he cannot listen to the admonitions of the old and steady... Never mind, I shall not speak of this further. Da De, I originally worried that your mind was too deep and that you were too fond of maneuvering."
Li Xuanba did not answer. He could, of course, see that Yang Zhao’s good intentions toward his second brother were more sincere.
This was normal. After all, he himself did not possess a sincere heart.
Yang Zhao continued, "However, thinking back on how you risked yourself to leak Father’s grievances against me in order to save loyal officials at court, and how you have now voluntarily conceded multiple times in the face of Li Jiancheng’s aggressive posturing, I think I have wronged you. Li Sanlang is a person of kindness and sincerity; one’s methods are not a reflection of one’s character."
Yang Zhao bowed, "Your cousin offers you an apology."
Li Xuanba was startled and quickly helped Yang Zhao up, "Your Highness, why go to such lengths?"
Yang Zhao laughed, "Even if I did not apologize, given your personality, you would still treat me with kindness. But I could not let it sit on my conscience."
After learning from his younger brother about the encounters Li Xuanba and Li Shimin had in the Eastern Capital, he had sighed for a long time, feeling a heavy weight in his chest.
If one did not consider his age and treated him as an adult, Li Xuanba’s methods in the capital were not particularly sophisticated.
Yang Zhao had been in contact with Li Xuanba for a long time and was certain that Li Xuanba’s mind was indeed deep. For instance, his early planning for the shops was indeed driven by a desire to compete with Li Jiancheng for profit.
Although Yang Zhao understood Li Xuanba’s situation and had actively helped him, it was inevitably unsettling that someone so young should be so calculating.
Therefore, whenever he mentioned Li Xuanba to Yang Ji or his close friends, he would tell them that while Li Xuanba was overflowing with talent and worth knowing, one should not become too deeply involved with him.
This time, when he came to Luoyang, Yang Ji had mocked him, saying he had misjudged Li Xuanba.
Publicly, Li Xuanba had proposed that scholars write *ci* poetry, shifting the Emperor’s interest in music toward the creation of new literary forms. He turned the focus from recruiting musicians to recruiting scholars, earning praise even from Xue Daoheng.
Privately, after Li Jiancheng arrived in Luoyang, Li Xuanba had twice taken the initiative to yield—once by moving into a small courtyard near the side gate, and once by moving out of the main family residence entirely into a villa, successfully repairing his relationship with Li Jiancheng.
"Da De is merely clever, but he has a good heart," Yang Ji had said. "In the court, he offers tactful advice to Father; in the family, he prioritizes harmony between brothers. It was you, elder brother, who misjudged him. By the way, when you come to the villa with me this time, you will meet a child named Li Zhiyun. He is the fifth son of the Li family, born of a concubine."
Yang Ji then spoke of how Li Zhiyun had been insulted by Li Yuanji because he was a better student than him.
"They brought the fifth Li son to the villa to be cared for, to prevent further conflict between him and the fourth son," Yang Ji said. "According to Da Xiong, he hadn't thought of it so thoroughly; it was Da De’s suggestion."
After saying all this, Yang Ji was immensely proud, so proud that he even used his childhood address: "Elder brother, you always say I am a poor judge of character. This time, my judgment is definitely clearer than yours!"
Hearing Yang Ji’s words, Yang Zhao was both surprised and gratified.
His brother’s reasoning clearly showed that he had truly observed and thought things through.
His brother had been very clever as a child but had become lazy with his brain as he grew older, which had caused Yang Zhao great worry.
Yang Zhao never worried about Yang Ji snatching his position as Crown Prince. If Yang Ji were to make a move, Yang Zhao wouldn't need to do anything; the moment he showed the intent to usurp the throne, their father would never tolerate him.
He was truly worried that his brother would act without thinking and provoke their father’s fury.
Now that his brother was finally using his head, Yang Zhao could not help but tear up.
Yang Ji proudly brought Yang Zhao to the villa where Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were staying. When Yang Zhao saw the fifth Li son acting affectionately on the back of Li Xuanba, who was busy roasting meat, he completely believed Yang Ji’s words.
Children have a sharp sense of likes and dislikes, and Li Xuanba had no need to curry favor with a concubine-born younger brother. Therefore, the kindness Li Xuanba showed toward the fifth Li son must be genuine.
To be so friendly even to a half-brother—Li Xuanba was indeed kind-hearted.
After reflecting on this, Yang Zhao decided to be honest with Li Xuanba and apologize.
Li Xuanba felt incredibly awkward.
Yang Zhao really didn't need to apologize. Judging by actions rather than intentions, Yang Zhao had always been helping him. If one didn't count the life-saving favor that only he could verify, he actually owed Yang Zhao many favors.
After all, although he knew Yang Zhao would have died of illness had he not returned to Daxing, the future had already changed, and the parties involved did not know what they would have faced. The words he spoke to Yang Zhao were merely to help him avoid Emperor Yang’s suspicions.
As for Yang Zhao speaking behind his back about him being calculating and fond of maneuvering... *cough*, Yang Zhao was telling the truth. He wasn't so petty as to hold a grudge when someone spoke the truth.
Now that Yang Zhao was apologizing for a virtue he didn't possess, Li Xuanba couldn't help but curl his toes inside his shoes.
Li Xuanba sent his thoughts through the wall to his second brother, shouting in his heart: 【Help! Get over here immediately!】
Li Shimin sent a 【Ha】 through the wall, and after a moment, another 【Ha】.
Finally, to Li Xuanba’s desperate hope, he sent back a super loud 【NO】.
Li Xuanba’s face fell. This second brother was beyond saving.
He had no choice but to ease the awkward atmosphere himself: "Cousin, why say such things? You have taken good care of me; I should be the one thanking you. As for your misunderstanding..."
Li Xuanba paused and smiled bitterly, "It was not a misunderstanding. I am indeed fond of maneuvering. Teacher Gao and Teacher Yuwen have both warned me not to rely too much on 'tactics,' as it might warp one’s character. Your judgment of people is very accurate."
Yang Zhao said, "Hearing you say that, I feel even more ashamed. Master Gao and Master Yuwen would warn you not to warp your character, yet I only... alas."
Yang Zhao wrinkled his chubby face, looking like an oversized steamed bun, "Thinking about it, have I not also fallen into the trap of 'tactics' and nearly warped my own character?"
The "tactics" of a Crown Prince are, after all, still "tactics."
Li Xuanba quickly changed the subject: "Cousin, since we have cleared the air, let us not speak of it anymore. Shall we continue discussing the Western Regions? Did His Majesty not want to conquer Goguryeo? I heard he is already making preparations; why the sudden decision to conquer Tuyuhun?"
Seeing that the tips of Li Xuanba’s ears were red, Yang Zhao felt amused and gained a bit more insight into Li Xuanba’s true nature.
He obediently changed the subject and complained, "It was a strategy proposed by Pei Shiju, the Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel."
Yang Zhao had always treated Li Xuanba as a peer of talent. Now that the misunderstanding was cleared, he no longer saw Li Xuanba as a child and carefully explained the situation regarding Pei Shiju to him.
Li Xuanba’s "learning" was essentially serving as a direct subordinate to Pei Shiju, so he needed to understand him better.
As he listened to Yang Zhao’s evaluation of Pei Shiju, Li Xuanba searched his memory for the historical records related to the man.
Pei Shiju, who changed his name to Pei Ju during the Zhenguan era, was a low-spec version of Zhangsun Sheng in historical records. However, because his character in *Twin of Brothers* was an alias for Shi Zhixuan and had a significant role, he was much more famous than Zhangsun Sheng.
Pei Shiju was a high-ranking official in both the Sui and Tang dynasties, but his performance in each was completely different.
In the Great Sui, he was one of the "Seven Nobles of the Selection Bureau" around Emperor Yang of Sui, fawning over the Emperor’s preferences and inciting him to waste vast amounts of manpower and resources to attack Tuyuhun and Goguryeo, never offering a word of dissent.
When Emperor Yang received foreign envoys and merchants, he demanded that the commoners wear fine clothes, and those without them were forbidden from going out. He gathered entertainers from all over to perform at Duanmen Street, ordered shops to set up banquets at their doors for foreigners to eat and drink for free, and even wrapped the trees in silk... these suggestions were all Pei Shiju’s.
He also carried out sowing discord in the Western Regions, much like Zhangsun Sheng.
After Zhangsun Sheng implemented his strategies of sowing discord, he not only successfully split the Turks, but the divided Turkic Khans still liked him and did not blame him or the Great Sui at all.
The northern frontier during the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui was very stable under Zhangsun Sheng’s governance.
After Pei Shiju sowed discord, everyone knew it was his doing, and they were furious at the Great Sui. The Shibi Khan of the Eastern Turks refused to pay tribute to Emperor Yang and even led troops to surround him.
The northern frontier during the reign of Emperor Yang of Sui was plagued by constant warfare under Pei Shiju’s governance.
To call him the minister who destroyed the Sui is no exaggeration.
However, when Pei Shiju served Li Yuan in the Western Regions, he was steady and methodical, using the strategy of "allying with the distant to attack the near," leaving enough room for the Tang Dynasty to recover. This allowed Li Yuan to send Li Shimin to pacify the world without facing crises in the rear.
After Emperor Taizong of Tang ascended the throne, Pei Shiju often spoke directly to admonish the Emperor’s faults, helping him navigate the chaos of his early reign.
Emperor Taizong appointed Pei Shiju as Minister of the Ministry of Revenue. At the age of eighty, he helped the Emperor sort out the tangled household registers before passing away at the end of the first year of Zhenguan. The Emperor was very grateful and gave him the posthumous title "Jing" (Respectful).
Looking at Pei Shiju’s behavior in the Tang Dynasty, he was a truly loyal and upright minister.
Li Xuanba: 【Pei Shiju was a sycophant under the Sui but loyal under the Tang; it was not his nature that changed. If a ruler hates hearing his faults, loyalty turns to sycophancy; if a ruler loves hearing straight talk, sycophancy turns to loyalty. Thus, one knows that the ruler is the object, and the minister is the shadow; when the object moves, the shadow follows.】
Across the wall: 【Huh?】
Li Xuanba: 【An evaluation of Pei Shiju from the later *Zizhi Tongjian*.】
Across the wall: 【Huh??】
Li Xuanba: 【I’m praising you!】
Across the wall: 【Oh.】
A clattering sound came from across the wall again.
Li Xuanba and Yang Zhao both rubbed their foreheads.
"Are they still fighting?"
"Alas!"
Li Xuanba and Yang Zhao could no longer continue their serious discussion.
Yang Zhao summarized hastily, "Pei Shiju is quite talented, and you will learn many skills by following him. But this man is overly calculating..."
At this point, Yang Zhao remembered he had just said Li Xuanba was fond of maneuvering and couldn't help but laugh.
"Don't learn from him and become even more calculating," Yang Zhao joked. "His maneuvering has already lost the heart of loyalty and uprightness."
Li Xuanba said, "I will not. Cousin, you are also accompanying His Majesty on the expedition; will your health hold up?"
Yang Zhao laughed, "Don't underestimate me; I can draw a heavy bow, too. I am accompanying Father on the western journey, and since I know his preferences, the journey will surely be comfortable and I will not be burdened."
He sighed, his smile fading, "Your mind is mature beyond your years, so I will speak plainly without excuses. Back then, both Father and Uncle had military achievements, but only our eldest uncle remained in the rear. The officials all supported Father, and they truly did not respect him. Since Father is leading the campaign, I must accompany him no matter what. To 'hitch a ride' on military achievements, do you understand?"
Li Xuanba nodded, "I understand." Yang Zhao was indeed clear-minded.
Every time Emperor Yang led a campaign, he would build a grand palace to live in, and his carriages were as magnificent as a mobile palace. When he went on an expedition, his empresses, concubines, princesses, palace maids, musicians, and singers would all accompany him; the journey was indeed very comfortable.
Li Xuanba said, "Cousin, please take care of your health."
Yang Zhao nodded with a smile, "You too. Especially since you are studying under Master Gao and Master Yuwen, do not learn their rigidity. If you encounter something that cannot be advised upon, do not advise. If you lose your life, the advice will not succeed. Only by staying alive can you do more things. Understand? Your previous tactful advice was very good."
Li Xuanba knew the Crown Prince’s advice was sincere and bowed, "Yes. Thank you for your guidance, Cousin."
Another clattering noise came from across the wall.
Yang Zhao rubbed his forehead and slowly stood up, "Let’s go see; I’m worried they might smash the whole room."
Li Xuanba followed Yang Zhao quickly to the next room.
In the next room, Li Shimin and Yang Ji were each holding a bamboo pole, with a fur pillow tied to their bodies, happily sparring.
Li Xuanba looked at the mess on the floor, his face turning black.
*If you want to fight, go outside! Don't smash the furniture!*
Yang Zhao gave a bitter smile, "Don't be angry, don't be angry, I will pay for it! Cousin will pay for it! A-Hai! Stop! You are twice the age of Da Xiong, have you no shame!"
Yang Ji was embarrassed and angry, "Don't call me A-Hai!"
Li Xuanba ran forward, grabbed the small topknot on Li Shimin’s head, and pulled hard, then turned to the window and said, "Little Five! Didn't I tell you to go to sleep!"
Li Zhiyun poked his head through the window, "I heard a loud noise and got curious... Ah, Third Brother, don't be angry! I’m going to sleep now!"
Li Shimin screamed, "Stop pulling, stop pulling, my hair bun is coming off!"
Yang Zhao, "A-Hai, can you please let me have some peace of mind?"
Yang Ji scolded, "I told you not to call me A-Hai!"
Li Zhiyun poked his little head out of the window again, covering his mouth and giggling.
...
The next day, Li Zhiyun couldn't laugh anymore.
Li Zhiyun was teary-eyed, "Ah? Both Second Brother and Third Brother are going to Zhangye? What about me? Don't leave me alone, I’ll be scared."
Li Xuanba said, "You are going home for now. Li Yuanji has been severely disciplined by Father; he won't dare to bully you again."
Li Shimin rubbed Li Zhiyun’s head, "When Ah Xuan and I return, we will check your lessons. Don't be lazy."
Li Zhiyun hugged his second and third brothers’ arms, "No! I don't want to go back! I want to go with you! If you can go, I can go too! Waaah! I don't want to!"
Li Zhiyun had been so happy these past few days, but he hadn't even been happy for a few months before he had to return to the Tang Duke’s mansion. The thought of taking lessons with Li Yuanji at the mansion made his scalp tingle.
Li Yuanji might not dare to bully him, but he still had to study with him. And to accommodate Li Yuanji, he still had to hide his brilliance.
*I don't want to hide my brilliance! I don't want to be dragged down by Li Yuanji! I want to be praised!*
Here, his second and third brothers praised him for being smart every day, and when his lessons were done well, there were many rewards.
*I don't want to go back, I don't want to, waaaah!!!*
Li Zhiyun displayed the special talent of the Li family (except for Li Xuanba) and instantly became a teary mess.
Seeing this, Li Shimin couldn't help but let his own tears flow, hugging Li Zhiyun and crying bitterly together.
Li Xuanba pulled his arm out of Li Zhiyun’s embrace and kicked his second brother hard, "What are you crying for!"
Li Shimin sobbed, "I don't know, I just can't help it."
*Damn you...* Li Xuanba swallowed his curse with difficulty.
With Li Shimin crying along, Li Xuanba couldn't reason with Li Zhiyun.
Li Zhiyun wasn't unreasonable; he knew he was too young to travel far. He was just truly afraid of studying with Li Yuanji again.
After crying until he was tired, Li Zhiyun obediently admitted his mistake, saying he would wait for his second and third brothers to return.
Seeing Li Zhiyun so sensible, Li Shimin cried another round.
Li Xuanba couldn't take it anymore and kicked Li Shimin to the floor, "Shut up! Stop crying!"
Li Zhiyun was stunned.
*Oh my god! Third Brother actually kicked Second Brother down! Is Second Brother still my sickly Second Brother!*
He quickly covered his mouth, not daring to cry anymore.
Li Shimin, who hadn't stood steadily, patted the dust off his clothes and complained, "Ah Xuan, is your blood cold? You aren't even crying when it’s so moving."
Li Xuanba rolled his eyes until only the whites were visible, "Thanks, you took all my tear ducts while we were in the womb. I guess you’re flowing all my tears for this lifetime, which is why you’ve turned into such a crybaby."
"Pfft." Li Zhiyun tried hard to cover his mouth.
Li Shimin couldn't cry anymore.
He tapped Li Zhiyun on the head and complained to Li Xuanba, "Don't talk nonsense, be careful that Little Five takes it seriously."
Li Zhiyun whispered while covering his mouth, "I won't take it seriously, I’m not stupid."
Li Shimin wiped his tears and smiled brightly, as if the rain had cleared, "Good, Little Five isn't stupid. Little Five, be good at home and wait for Second and Third Brother to return. If Li Yuanji bullies you again, tell Mother, just like your 'tattletale' Third Brother, and be a cute little tattletale dog."
Li Zhiyun nodded, "Okay, I’m a tattletale dog."
Li Xuanba, "..." *You can say that, and you still say you aren't stupid? Oh, my foolish younger brother.*
When they sent Li Zhiyun back, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba also returned home temporarily.
They had already promised the Emperor to go to Zhangye, so the matter was settled; even if their parents objected, it could not be changed.
Li Yuan and Lady Dou’s faces were very ugly; they wanted to beat Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, but they couldn't bring themselves to do it.
Li Yuan found someone to make small soft armor vests for the two children using fine copper wire. After the copper armor was made, he felt it was too heavy, so he ordered his own armor to be dismantled and modified to make a set of leather protective gear for the two children.
Lady Dou went from house to house to visit noblewomen who had been to Zhangye, asking what they needed to pay attention to while living there, and prepared medicine and clothing for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.
Li Jiancheng wanted to go too, but after asking his brothers and learning they were only going to the Zhangye markets to learn, he gave up the idea.
The Tang Duke’s mansion was well-informed and already knew the Emperor wanted to take action against Tuyuhun.
Given the Emperor’s current trust in Li Yuan, Li Yuan would certainly accompany the army to gain military merit. If Li Jiancheng wanted to go to the battlefield, he could go with Li Yuan.
Li Yuan and Lady Dou also prepared heavy gifts for Pei Shiju, hoping he would take good care of the two children.
Pei Shiju refused several times but couldn't escape it, and he smiled bitterly.
*Why does the Tang Duke need to give me gifts to take care of Li Erlang and Li Sanlang? I want to give them gifts and beg them to take care of me.*
*His Majesty really knows how to use people. I am governing the Western Regions, and I have to take two children with me? Even Emperor Wu of Han didn't train Huo Qubing like this.*
Li Yuan and Lady Dou also begged Zhangsun Sheng to let Li Shimin and Li Xuanba stay at the Zhangsun residence for a while.
The Zhangsun and Li families were already betrothed, so Li Yuan and Lady Dou wouldn't have needed to ask specifically; Zhangsun Sheng would have helped Li Shimin and Li Xuanba anyway. But unfortunately, Zhangsun Sheng was ill. It was truly difficult to ask him to teach the boys while he was sick.
Fortunately, Zhangsun Sheng’s illness was not severe, and he understood the hearts of Li Yuan and Lady Dou as parents.
When Li Shimin and Li Xuanba arrived at the Zhangsun residence, they found Lady Gao’s expression very haggard.
After Li Shimin dragged Zhangsun Wuji into a corner to ask, he said to Li Xuanba, "Uncle doesn't trust Pei Shiju, and His Majesty trusts Uncle more. Uncle is going to travel west despite his illness to lead a path and scout for information on Tuyuhun for the Great Sui."
Li Xuanba frowned. This part wasn't in the history books.
However, although it wasn't written in the books, governing the Western Regions was Zhangsun Sheng’s specialty, and Emperor Yang trusted him, so the campaign against Tuyuhun might not have intentionally bypassed him.
Furthermore, the campaign against Tuyuhun was a rare major victory in Emperor Yang’s foreign wars.
Although they couldn't be assimilated later, and Tuyuhun made a comeback at the end of the Sui Dynasty, stronger than before. Whether it was splitting the Turks or attacking Tuyuhun and Goguryeo, Emperor Yang seemed to be handing out experience points to the enemy, helping the Tang Dynasty’s enemies level up and get better gear.
But for the campaign against Tuyuhun to be so smooth, did Zhangsun Sheng really do something in it?
Li Xuanba pinched his chin, deep in thought.
Unlike Pei Shiju, who drew maps and collected information based on second-hand news from Western Region merchants, Zhangsun Sheng was a man of action. To govern the Western Regions, he would personally travel to every place he intended to govern, and he even spent years hunting with the Turkic Khans.
If Zhangsun Sheng wanted to take action against Tuyuhun, he would certainly sneak into Tuyuhun himself to gather information.
And since Zhangsun Sheng would pass away from illness next year, could it be related to this western journey while ill?
Li Shimin sighed, "The fourth Zhangsun son hopes we can persuade his father not to go to the Western Regions. How can we persuade him?"
Li Xuanba said with ill intent, "I will. It’s time for me to use my ultimate move." *Regardless of whether Zhangsun Sheng’s death next year is related to this journey, I must stop him first!*
Li Shimin gasped, "Spare him!"
Li Xuanba: 【Your father-in-law might pass away next year. Maybe it’s because of this... ah!】
Li Shimin dragged Li Xuanba and ran, almost tripping him, "Go stab him in the heart! Hurry! By the way, can I listen?"
Li Xuanba said while running, "I suggest you don't."
Li Shimin breathed a sigh of relief and said happily, "If even I can't listen, then this move must be ruthless. I believe we’ve got this!"
Li Xuanba was speechless and said in his heart: 【Is this a matter of "got this"? Shouldn't you be worried about your wife and brother-in-law?】
Li Shimin whispered, "You said Guanyinbi and I will definitely marry, so what am I afraid of? Even if my father-in-law passes away, they should be fine... just not living well, right?"
Li Xuanba sighed and nodded.
Li Shimin curled his lips, pushed open the door to Zhangsun Sheng’s study, shoved his brother inside, and closed the door.
"Leave, leave, everyone leave. Ah Xuan has an imperial decree from His Majesty to tell Uncle, everyone get out."
Li Shimin drove away all the servants, sat on the steps, rested his chin in his hands, and waited for the movement inside the study.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第69章 纵横家绝不认输
chunks.chineseText:
第69章 纵横家绝不认输

=
　　李玄霸被李世民推得一个踉跄， 差点摔倒。
　　长孙晟正在书房里来回踱步思考要给皇帝的献策，见李玄霸差点摔倒，扶住李玄霸道：“什么口谕？陛下有口谕让你传？”
　　李玄霸道：“别听二哥胡扯。”
　　长孙晟气笑了：“陛下口谕是能乱传的吗？这事如果传出去， 唐国公也保不住他。”
　　说完， 长孙晟就要出门去教训准女婿。
　　李玄霸赶紧拉住长孙晟：“等等， 我有事要和伯父说。”
　　长孙晟停下脚步，低头看着李玄霸道：“有什么事非得用假传口谕的借口来告诉我？”
　　李玄霸把长孙晟拉到书桌后的坐榻上坐好，还帮长孙晟把坐榻上的靠背放好。
　　长孙晟脸上狐疑的神色更重：“你有事要请求我帮助？”
　　李玄霸向来性格冷淡， 虽对长辈礼数很周到，但讨好人的事，长孙晟只见到李玄霸对皇帝做过。
　　李玄霸自己搬了个坐墩放在书桌对面， 坐下后刚好露个肩膀出来。
　　“不是请求伯父帮助，是有重要的事要告诉伯父。”李玄霸板着脸， 严肃道， “伯父很受陛下信赖，应该知晓陛下一直忌惮高老师和宇文老师。高老师和宇文老师原本是直言敢谏的性格，现在却早早退出朝堂编书，伯父不奇怪吗？”
　　长孙晟面无表情道：“不奇怪。”
　　李玄霸；“……”怎么不按照常理出牌。
　　李玄霸又道：“薛老师性格乖僻，文人习气很重。他也退出朝堂……”
　　长孙晟打断道：“不奇怪。但大德， 你在背后说老师的不是，很不好。”
　　李玄霸：“……”他有点头疼了。
　　李玄霸看得出来， 长孙晟不是不好奇，但显然长孙晟不愿意把话语的主导权交给自己。
　　长孙晟有何本事？放到战国就是张仪苏秦这样的纵横家，后世尊称外交家。自己不过是个底层小市民， 论言语交锋， 怎么比得过纵横家外交家？
　　李玄霸露出头疼表情时， 长孙晟严肃的面容上浮现出浅浅的笑意。
　　李玄霸确实聪明， 即使现在进入朝堂，都能比大部分大臣优秀。但比起自己，他这点嘴皮子上的本事还是太嫩了。和李世民一样，都需要来自长辈的教育。
　　长孙晟三言两语抢回主动权后，用桌上的水壶给李玄霸倒了一杯水，推到李玄霸面前：“你要说什么就直说。”
　　李玄霸叹了口气，道：“我本来想有点铺垫。”
　　长孙晟道：“你可以多想一会儿，我先出去教训完大雄再回来听你说。”
　　李玄霸嘴角抽搐了两下，道：“好吧，我不铺垫了。伯父，我有谶纬之能。”
　　长孙晟笑了。
　　他给自己也倒了一杯水，先抿了一口，才道：“高公、宇文公和薛公是听了你的谶纬，相信陛下会杀他们，才退出朝堂？”
　　李玄霸正想点头，长孙晟却摇头。
　　“以他们的性格和见识，不会轻易相信谶纬。”长孙晟道。
　　李玄霸道：“他们真的相信。”
　　长孙晟却继续摇头：“以你的性格和聪慧，也不会轻易说出会谶纬。让我猜猜，你可能对高公和宇文公说了谶纬，但薛公并不知晓。薛公因病辞官前，高公曾来洛阳。或许是那时高公劝说薛公离开朝堂。”
　　李玄霸：“……”他想跑了。
　　长孙晟道：“不过高公明知道陛下忌惮他，还要出手帮薛公……嗯，既然你说你有谶纬之能。看来是你对高公说了什么。”
　　李玄霸的脑袋上再次冒出了省略号。长孙晟的乐子他不想看了。
　　长孙晟说完自己的推断之后，板着的表情却变得缓和起来，没有了之前咄咄逼人的气势。
　　他叹了口气，道：“我还是同样的推断，以你的性格和聪慧，不会轻易说出谶纬。你不会不懂如果让陛下知道你会谶纬，你将会遭遇什么。高公和宇文公不会说出你会谶纬，是因为陛下如果有机会一定会杀了他们。他们就算告诉陛下你的能耐，陛下也会先杀他们，再处置你。”
　　长孙晟把手边的糕点推到李玄霸面前：“这葡萄干奶糕很好吃。”
　　李玄霸拿起奶糕，默默喝水吃奶糕。
　　虽然不知道长孙晟为什么突然投喂他，但不吃白不吃，他正好有点饿。
　　待李玄霸吃完一块奶糕，把手上的糕点屑擦干净后，长孙晟才继续道：“我与高公和宇文公不同，与陛下极亲近。就算李大雄是我的准女婿，你也不该告诉我这件事。”
　　李玄霸板着脸道：“伯父猜了很多事，不如再猜猜？”
　　长孙晟失笑：“这还用猜？你定是来劝我不要带兵去西域。大概我会病死，导致四郎和观音婢……”
　　长孙晟的话没有说完，就被他的叹气声打断。
　　他脸上的笑容淡去，眉头紧锁。
　　“就算你说出谶纬，我也难以相信安业会做出欺辱弟妹的事。”长孙晟道，“他出生后，我因经略西域，常常几年甚至十几年不归家。待我从西域归来时，发须已经斑白。”
　　长孙晟摸了摸自己的鬓发，刚毅的面容上出现了些许老态疲惫。
　　“子不教，父之过，是我之错。”长孙晟道，“四郎和观音婢将来会如何？”
　　李玄霸道：“挺好的，一个当了皇后，一个当了宰相。”
　　长孙晟面上悲伤疲惫的神情一僵。
　　李玄霸道：“真的，没骗你。”
　　长孙晟：“……”他猛地喝了口水缓了缓。
　　这次轮到李玄霸脸上浮现出清浅的笑意了。
　　长孙晟喝完水后，神情复杂地看着李玄霸：“你就是这么和高公、宇文公说的谶纬？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　长孙晟扶额：“谶纬不是应该、应该……”
　　李玄霸道：“说些摸不到头脑的诗句，再辅以看相看风水云气？这个我真不会。”
　　长孙晟苦笑：“那你要如何让人相信你的谶纬？”
　　李玄霸道：“我说我的，信不信就不关我事了，佛曰，‘好言难劝该死鬼，慈悲不渡自绝人’。我已经尽力了。”
　　长孙晟沉默了许久，才道：“佛祖没说过。”
　　李玄霸道：“就当佛祖说的吧。”
　　他坐直身体，再次板起脸严肃道：“我知道伯父是陛下亲近之臣，但事关伯父未来，所以只能冒险了。不过正如伯父所说，我这冒险也不算冒险。伯父如果把我的谶纬告诉陛下，我不一定会死，陛下还要询问我谶纬。但伯父一家就不一定了。”
　　长孙晟打量了李玄霸一番，认真地问道：“你要不要跟我学经略之术？”
　　李玄霸道：“谢伯父夸奖。”
　　长孙晟靠在了李玄霸为他搬来的靠背上，懒洋洋道：“继续说吧。”
　　他将主动权交给了李玄霸，不再压制李玄霸。
　　李玄霸道：“伯父明年会病逝。《隋书》中没有记载伯父病逝前两年的事迹……”
　　长孙晟半合的眼睛睁开：“什么？你说什么书？”
　　李玄霸道：“我观看的天书叫《隋书》。”
　　长孙晟：“……”
　　他总算知道为何高颎、宇文弼会相信李玄霸的谶纬了。
　　《隋书》？！谁编撰的？？
　　李玄霸问道：“伯父是想询问，自己的传记在《隋书》中的排序吗？”
　　长孙晟终于绷不住脸色，嘴角微抽：“高颎和宇文弼问过了？”
　　李玄霸：“……”啊，都直呼老师的姓名了？他就说，长孙晟一直站在杨广那一边，应该和高老师和宇文老师算是半个政敌，怎么会如此客气。
　　李玄霸点头。
　　长孙晟没好气道：“你不是说观音婢要当皇后吗？我入什么《隋书》？”
　　李玄霸道：“可能因为伯父去世得过早？”
　　长孙晟手有点痒：“你也是这么和高颎、宇文弼说话？”
　　李玄霸再次点头。
　　长孙晟道：“他们没教训你？”
　　李玄霸道：“老师偏爱我。”
　　长孙晟气笑了。还偏爱你？是你病弱，怕把你揍出问题吧？
　　他摆了摆手：“若我入《隋书》，不可能在高颎之前，不问也罢。你继续。《隋书》之后难道是《唐书》？怎么，我那准女婿将来还能当开国雄主？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“开国雄主是我父亲。”
　　长孙晟皱眉：“怎么可能？若天下大乱，李渊或许能割据一方，但以他优柔寡断的性格，怎可能成为开国雄主？他或许在天下大乱之处能有雄主的模样，但一旦有了一块较为安定的地盘，他肯定不会愿意再冒险。”
　　李玄霸道：“等父亲稳定下来之后，让二哥去征伐天下，平定中原不就当开国雄主了。”
　　长孙晟：“……你真是什么话都敢说。”
　　李玄霸微笑。
　　怎么？不服气？那你去告啊，告诉杨广或者李渊啊。唐太宗的老丈人？
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 69: The Political Strategist Never Concedes Defeat

=
　　Stumbled by Li Shimin's shove, Li Xuanba nearly fell flat on his face.

　　Zhangsun Sheng had been pacing back and forth in his study, pondering the policy proposals he planned to submit to the Emperor. Seeing Li Xuanba almost fall, he caught and supported him, asking, "What imperial decree? His Majesty gave you an oral decree to pass on?"

　　Li Xuanba replied, "Don't listen to Second Brother's nonsense."

　　Zhangsun Sheng was so exasperated he let out a laugh. "Is an imperial oral decree something to be bandied about carelessly? If word of this gets out, even the Duke of Tang won't be able to protect him."

　　With that, Zhangsun Sheng turned toward the door, intending to go out and discipline his prospective son-in-law.

　　Li Xuanba quickly caught his sleeve. "Wait, Uncle, I have something important to discuss with you."

　　Zhangsun Sheng stopped in his tracks, looking down at Li Xuanba. "What matter could possibly require fabricating an imperial decree just to speak with me?"

　　Li Xuanba pulled Zhangsun Sheng over to the couch behind the desk, helping him sit down and even adjusting the backrest for him.

　　The suspicion on Zhangsun Sheng's face deepened. "Are you here to ask for my help?"

　　Li Xuanba had always possessed an aloof temperament. While impeccably courteous to his elders, ingratiating behavior was something Zhangsun Sheng had only ever seen him display before the Emperor.

　　Li Xuanba fetched a cushioned stool, set it across the desk, and sat down, his head and shoulders just peeking over the edge.

　　"I am not asking for your help, Uncle. I have a matter of grave importance to tell you." Li Xuanba straightened his face and said solemnly, "Uncle enjoys His Majesty's deep trust, so you must know that His Majesty has always been wary of Master Gao and Master Yuwen. Masters Gao and Yuwen were originally men of forthright speech who never hesitated to remonstrate, yet now they have retreated from the imperial court early to compile books. Doesn't Uncle find that strange?"

　　Zhangsun Sheng replied expressionlessly, "Not at all."

　　Li Xuanba: "..." *Why isn't he playing by the rules?*

　　Li Xuanba continued, "Master Xue is eccentric by nature and steeped in the arrogant habits of literati. He has also withdrawn from court..."

　　Zhangsun Sheng cut him off. "Still not strange. But Dade, speaking ill of your teacher behind his back is very unseemly."

　　Li Xuanba: "..." His head was starting to throb.

　　Li Xuanba could tell that Zhangsun Sheng wasn't lacking curiosity; rather, he simply refused to surrender control of the conversation.

　　What was Zhangsun Sheng's true forte? In the Warring States period, he would have been a master of diplomacy and political maneuver on par with Zhang Yi and Su Qin, what later generations reverently termed a diplomat. Li Xuanba was merely an ordinary commoner in his past life; in a war of words, how could he outmaneuver a consummate political strategist?

　　Seeing Li Xuanba's pained expression, a faint smile appeared on Zhangsun Sheng's stern face.

　　Li Xuanba was indeed clever; even if he were thrust into the imperial court right now, he would outshine most ministers. Yet compared to an old hand like himself, the boy's verbal fencing was still far too green. Just like Li Shimin, he needed a proper lesson from an elder.

　　Having seized the initiative with just a few words, Zhangsun Sheng poured a cup of water from the pot on the desk and slid it in front of Li Xuanba. "Whatever you have to say, speak plainly."

　　Li Xuanba sighed. "I was hoping to build up to it a bit."

　　Zhangsun Sheng countered, "You are welcome to ponder it longer. I'll go outside, give Daxiong a good thrashing, and come back to listen."

　　Li Xuanba's mouth twitched twice. "Fine, no buildup then. Uncle, I possess the gift of prophecy."

　　Zhangsun Sheng chuckled.

　　He poured himself a cup of water, took a sip, and only then remarked, "So Lord Gao, Lord Yuwen, and Lord Xue heard your prophecies, believed His Majesty would execute them, and withdrew from court because of it?"

　　Just as Li Xuanba was about to nod, Zhangsun Sheng shook his head.

　　"Given their character and discernment, they would never easily put their faith in mere omens and prophecies," Zhangsun Sheng said.

　　Li Xuanba replied, "They really did believe me."

　　Zhangsun Sheng continued to shake his head. "Given your personality and intelligence, you wouldn't lightly claim to possess prophetic sight, either. Let me guess: you may have shared your prophecies with Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen, but Lord Xue knows nothing of this. Before Lord Xue resigned on grounds of illness, Lord Gao visited Luoyang. It was likely then that Lord Gao persuaded Lord Xue to leave the court."

　　Li Xuanba: "..." He suddenly wanted to run away.

　　Zhangsun Sheng continued, "Yet Lord Gao knew very well that His Majesty was wary of him, yet still stepped in to help Lord Xue... Mm. Since you claim to have prophetic vision, it seems you must have revealed something critical to Lord Gao."

　　An ellipsis hovered over Li Xuanba's head once more. He didn't feel like being the source of Zhangsun Sheng's amusement anymore.

　　Having laid out his deduction, the sternness in Zhangsun Sheng's expression softened, losing its earlier aggressive edge.

　　He sighed and said, "My conclusion remains the same: given your nature and intellect, you would never reveal such prophecies lightly. You cannot fail to understand what would happen to you if His Majesty learned of your ability. Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen would never expose your gift because His Majesty will seize any chance to kill them. Even if they told His Majesty of your powers, His Majesty would execute them first before dealing with you."

　　Zhangsun Sheng pushed a plate of pastries near his hand toward Li Xuanba. "This raisin milk cake is quite delicious."

　　Li Xuanba picked up a milk cake, eating and sipping water in silence.

　　Though he had no idea why Zhangsun Sheng was suddenly feeding him, free food was free food, and he happened to be hungry anyway.

　　Once Li Xuanba finished the milk cake and brushed the crumbs from his hands, Zhangsun Sheng continued, "I am different from Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen. I am extremely close to His Majesty. Even if Li Daxiong is my future son-in-law, you should never have revealed this matter to me."

　　Li Xuanba kept a straight face. "Uncle has deduced so much, why not guess a bit further?"

　　Zhangsun Sheng laughed despite himself. "Does that even need guessing? You've surely come to persuade me not to lead troops to the Western Regions. Presumably, I would fall ill and die, leaving Silang and Guanyinbi..."

　　Zhangsun Sheng trailed off, cut short by his own heavy sigh.

　　The smile faded from his face, replaced by tightly furrowed brows.

　　"Even if you speak of prophecies, I find it hard to believe Anye would mistreat his younger brother and sister," Zhangsun Sheng said. "After he was born, because of my campaigns and management in the Western Regions, I often went years—even over a decade—without returning home. By the time I came back from the west, my hair and beard were already streaked with white."

　　Zhangsun Sheng touched his temples, weariness and age creeping into his resolute features.

　　"To raise a child without teaching him is the father's fault; the blame lies with me," Zhangsun Sheng murmured. "What will become of Silang and Guanyinbi in the future?"

　　Li Xuanba replied, "Quite well, actually. One becomes Empress, and the other becomes Prime Minister."

　　The sorrow and fatigue on Zhangsun Sheng's face instantly froze.

　　Li Xuanba added, "Truly. I'm not lying to you."

　　Zhangsun Sheng: "..." He took a fierce gulp of water to steady his nerves.

　　Now it was Li Xuanba's turn for a faint smile to play upon his lips.

　　After setting down the cup, Zhangsun Sheng looked at Li Xuanba with a thoroughly conflicted expression. "Is this how you delivered your prophecies to Lord Gao and Lord Yuwen as well?"

　　Li Xuanba nodded.

　　Zhangsun Sheng pressed a hand to his forehead. "Aren't prophecies supposed to... supposed to..."

　　Li Xuanba said, "Recite cryptic, baffling verses accompanied by physiognomy, geomancy, and reading the clouds and mists? I truly don't know how to do that."

　　Zhangsun Sheng smiled wryly. "Then how on earth do you expect anyone to believe your prophecies?"

　　Li Xuanba replied, "I say what I have to say; whether they believe it is none of my concern. As the Buddha said: 'Kind words cannot persuade a ghost bound for death; mercy cannot deliver those who bring about their own doom.' I have done my best."

　　Zhangsun Sheng remained silent for a long moment before remarking, "The Buddha never said that."

　　Li Xuanba said, "Just pretend he did."

　　He sat up straight, adopting a stern and solemn expression once more. "I know Uncle is a trusted confidant of His Majesty, but since this concerns your future, I could only take the risk. However, just as Uncle said, this risk of mine isn't much of a gamble. If Uncle reports my prophecies to His Majesty, I won't necessarily die—His Majesty would want to question me about the prophecies. But Uncle's family might not be so fortunate."

　　Zhangsun Sheng scrutinized Li Xuanba thoroughly, then asked in all seriousness, "Do you want to study statecraft and frontier strategy with me?"

　　Li Xuanba replied, "I thank Uncle for the compliment."

　　Zhangsun Sheng leaned back against the cushion Li Xuanba had arranged for him, speaking lazily, "Go on, then."

　　He yielded the initiative to Li Xuanba, no longer pressing him down.

　　Li Xuanba said, "Uncle will succumb to illness next year. The *Book of Sui* records none of your deeds during the two years before your death..."

　　Zhangsun Sheng's half-closed eyes snapped open. "What? What book did you say?"

　　Li Xuanba said, "The Heavenly Book I read is titled the *Book of Sui*."

　　Zhangsun Sheng: "..."

　　He finally understood why Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi had believed Li Xuanba's prophecies.

　　The *Book of Sui*?! Who compiled it?!

　　Li Xuanba asked, "Does Uncle wish to inquire about the ordering of your biography in the *Book of Sui*?"

　　Zhangsun Sheng could finally no longer maintain his composure, the corner of his mouth twitching slightly. "Did Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi already ask that?"

　　Li Xuanba: "..." *Ah, he's addressing my teachers by their bare names now?* He had known all along that Zhangsun Sheng was firmly aligned with Yang Guang, making him practically half a political rival to Master Gao and Master Yuwen; there was no reason for him to be overly polite to begin with.

　　Li Xuanba nodded.

　　Zhangsun Sheng snapped, thoroughly vexed, "Didn't you say Guanyinbi is going to be Empress? Why would I be recorded in the *Book of Sui*?"

　　Li Xuanba replied, "Perhaps because Uncle dies too early?"

　　Zhangsun Sheng's hands itched with the urge to beat him. "Is this how you talked to Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi as well?"

　　Li Xuanba nodded again.

　　Zhangsun Sheng asked, "They didn't thrash you?"

　　Li Xuanba replied, "My teachers dote on me."

　　Zhangsun Sheng let out an exasperated chuckle. *Dote on you? It's because you're so sickly they're terrified beating you might break something!*

　　He waved a hand dismissively. "If I am recorded in the *Book of Sui*, there is no way my entry precedes Gao Jiong's, so there is no point in asking. Continue. What comes after the *Book of Sui*—the *Book of Tang*? What, is my future son-in-law destined to become a founding sovereign?"

　　Li Xuanba shook his head. "The founding sovereign is my father."

　　Zhangsun Sheng frowned deeply. "How could that be possible? If the realm descends into chaos, Li Yuan might carve out a territory of his own. But given his indecisive nature, how could he possibly become a dynastic founder? He might carry the demeanor of a warlord in the early days of turmoil, but once he secures a stable foothold, he would never be willing to take further risks."

　　Li Xuanba replied, "Once Father establishes his foothold, he can just send Second Brother to conquer the realm and pacify the Central Plains. That's how he becomes the founding sovereign."

　　Zhangsun Sheng: "...You truly dare say anything."

　　Li Xuanba smiled faintly.

　　*What? Not convinced? Go report it then—go tell Yang Guang or Li Yuan. Father-in-law of Emperor Taizong of Tang?*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第70章 纵横家决定认输
chunks.chineseText:
第70章 纵横家决定认输

=
　　长孙晟眼神颇为复杂地看着李玄霸。
　　李玄霸收起了微笑， 面无表情地看向长孙晟。
　　长孙晟的手指在袖口里动了动。
　　手痒，想给面前这熊孩子一巴掌。
　　长孙晟深呼吸，语气温和道：“这就是你敢告诉我这些， 不担心我告密的依仗？你认为， 我如果告诉陛下此事， 我也难逃一死？”
　　李玄霸没有回答长孙晟的话，他在多次向长孙晟提问被抢夺主导权后，再次发问：“伯父是否好奇我的命定的结局？”
　　长孙晟还未说话， 李玄霸就抢先答道：“我会在十六岁病逝。”
　　长孙晟的眼睛微微睁大，嘴唇抿成一条直线。
　　李玄霸刚抿成一条直线的嘴唇却学长孙晟刚才那样，弯成了温和的幅度。
　　他用平静中略带笑意的声音说道：“虽然我现在努力养身， 但谁知道我能不能活过十六岁。活过十六岁后呢？我这样的身体，任何一场小病都可能成为我的绝症。我每活一天， 都不知道明天自己是不是还活着。”
　　“这时候我脑子里……”李玄霸指着自己的脑袋， “有太多的秘密，好难受啊。”
　　长孙晟的瞳孔微微颤抖。身为纵横家，他看人极准。他本以为自己看李玄霸也已经很透彻，但现在李玄霸却像是换了个人似的。这种感觉很新奇。
　　李玄霸放下指着自己脑袋的手指：“伯父分析得不错。除了二哥，现在知道我有谶纬之能的有四人。除了伯父， 还有高老师、宇文老师和房玄龄。”
　　“我透露未来之前，确实思考过是否安全。高老师和宇文老师都站在隋炀帝的对立面， 且他们成为我的老师时，很快就会面临杀身之祸。”
　　“房玄龄是中等世家门阀的旁系子弟，在没有出人头地之前， 家世与寒门士子没有区别。他已经近而立之年， 是老成持重、秀外慧中之人。一个成为‘房相’的未来， 足以让他保守秘密。”
　　“至于伯父……”李玄霸的笑容变深了些， “伯父说得对，我是这么想的。不过，说白了我这一切都是预测，是赌。哪怕有九成的胜率，还是赌。最好的做法是什么都别说，等唐国公府羽翼丰满时再说。对吗？”
　　长孙晟没有回答李玄霸的问题，他甚至有些不明白李玄霸为何要说这个。
　　他只是喃喃道：“隋炀帝啊……”
　　李玄霸也不管长孙晟是否回答，仿佛自言自语道：“可那时候，我可能已经死了啊。隋末再波澜壮阔，和我一点关系都没有。”
　　长孙晟眼皮子猛地一跳：“你告诉别人未来，难道只是因为这个？！”
　　为了在隋末波澜壮阔的乱世中有点参与感？！
　　李玄霸点头：“对。随时都可能早夭，我总要找点有趣的事排解心理压力。其实唐也没什么好的，虽然持续三百年，但一百三十多年后就走下坡路了；虽然后世仍旧以唐为荣，但唐后五代十国比魏晋南北朝还乱，之后更是几国并立一直到突厥入主中原……嗯，反正都是草原民族，就当是突厥吧。”
　　长孙晟：“……你究竟能看多少年？”
　　李玄霸道：“一千多年。”
　　长孙晟差点把舌头咬到。他开始担心李玄霸的精神状态了。
　　李玄霸皱着眉头，露出郁闷的表情：“所以伯父你明白了吧？我其实有点厌烦现在的生活。”
　　“我虽然有很努力地挑选了倾诉未来的对象，但实际上也没有很在意这些。唐没了也会有其他王朝。说不定换个王朝，还不一定有五代十国和宋元呢。”
　　“而且二哥有天命在身，在他出现之前歌颂明君多提尧舜，在他之后无论是文人还是君王说起明君常以唐太宗作比。我觉得他没有那么容易死。”
