　　好难得看弟弟破防一次啊，李世民心里涌出一种难以言喻的快乐。
　　看别人被弟弟透露未来破防很乐，看弟弟破防也好乐。
　　李玄霸狠狠剜了二哥一眼。
　　李世民赶紧把翘起的嘴角下撇。
　　李玄霸阴阳怪气道：“嫂子本来会十三岁就嫁给你，十六七岁就同房；现在十六岁才嫁给你，弱冠才同房。你难过吗？”
　　李世民严肃道：“阿玄，你说什么胡话呢？还有什么比你嫂子的身体更重要？你回去和孙医师写信问问，男女要如何避孕不伤身体。”
　　李玄霸：“哦。”这种事问什么孙医师，问我就好。虽然我没有实际经验，但理论经验丰富。
　　现在没有完全避孕的手段，但避开危险期，再辅以羊肠之类的辅助，能把怀孕概率尽可能地降低。
　　大不了让嫂子生育孩子之后就熬夜长胖，争取患上多囊。多囊在古代可是妇女的救命富贵病。咳，李玄霸把自己脑海中不合实际的胡思乱想打散。
　　李世民拍了拍李玄霸的脑袋，让弟弟低下头，把弟弟被他打散的总角重新绑好：“丈人的命能救回来吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“不知道。”
　　李世民道：“尽人事，待天命。我们尽力即可，你不要有心理负担。”
　　李玄霸疑惑：“我能有什么心理负担？”
　　李世民笑道：“你当我自言自语。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 70: The Strategist Decides to Concede

Zhangsun Sheng looked at Li Xuanba with a rather complex expression.
Li Xuanba withdrew his faint smile and looked back at Zhangsun Sheng, his face devoid of emotion.
Zhangsun Sheng’s fingers twitched within his sleeves.
His hands were itching; he wanted to give this brat a slap.
Zhangsun Sheng took a deep breath and said in a gentle tone, "Is this your reliance for daring to tell me all this, without fearing that I might report you? Do you think that if I were to tell His Majesty about this, I wouldn't be able to escape death either?"

Li Xuanba did not answer Zhangsun Sheng’s question. After having his initiative stolen multiple times by Zhangsun Sheng’s questions, he asked one of his own: "Does Uncle feel curious about my destined end?"
Before Zhangsun Sheng could speak, Li Xuanba answered for him: "I will die of illness at sixteen."
Zhangsun Sheng’s eyes widened slightly, his lips pressed into a thin line.
Li Xuanba, whose lips had just been pressed into a thin line, mimicked the gentle curve Zhangsun Sheng had worn earlier.
He spoke in a voice that was calm yet tinged with a faint smile: "Although I am working hard to nourish my health now, who knows if I can live past sixteen? And what if I do? With a body like mine, any minor illness could become a terminal one. Every day I live, I don't know if I will still be alive tomorrow."
"At times like this, my mind..." Li Xuanba pointed to his own head, "...is filled with too many secrets. It’s so uncomfortable."

Zhangsun Sheng’s pupils trembled slightly. As a master strategist, his judgment of people was razor-sharp. He had thought he understood Li Xuanba thoroughly, but now, Li Xuanba seemed like a completely different person. This feeling was novel.
Li Xuanba lowered his finger. "Uncle’s analysis is correct. Besides my Second Brother, there are four people who now know of my ability to interpret omens. Besides you, there is Teacher Gao, Teacher Yuwen, and Fang Xuanling."
"Before I revealed the future, I did consider the safety of it. Teacher Gao and Teacher Yuwen both stand in opposition to Emperor Yang of Sui, and when they became my teachers, they were soon to face mortal peril."
"Fang Xuanling is a scion of a mid-tier aristocratic family. Before making a name for himself, his background was no different from that of a common scholar. He is nearly thirty, a man of steady character and hidden brilliance. The future of becoming a 'Chancellor Fang' is enough to ensure he keeps the secret."
"As for you, Uncle..." Li Xuanba’s smile deepened. "You are right; that is exactly what I thought. But to put it bluntly, all of this is just a prediction—a gamble. Even with a ninety percent chance of success, it is still a gamble. The best approach would be to say nothing and wait until the Tang Duke’s estate has grown strong enough. Right?"

Zhangsun Sheng did not answer Li Xuanba’s question; he didn't even understand why Li Xuanba was saying this.
He merely murmured, "Emperor Yang of Sui..."
Li Xuanba didn't care whether Zhangsun Sheng answered or not, as if talking to himself: "But by that time, I might already be dead. No matter how magnificent the end of the Sui Dynasty is, it will have nothing to do with me."
Zhangsun Sheng’s eyelid twitched violently: "You told others the future just for this?!"
Just to have a sense of participation in the tumultuous end of the Sui Dynasty?!
Li Xuanba nodded: "Yes. Since I might die young at any moment, I have to find something interesting to relieve my psychological pressure. Actually, the Tang Dynasty isn't all that great either. Although it lasted three hundred years, it started going downhill after a hundred and thirty years. Even though later generations still take pride in the Tang, the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period that followed was even more chaotic than the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties. After that, several kingdoms stood side-by-side until the Turks entered the Central Plains... well, they are all steppe peoples anyway, let's just call them the Turks."

Zhangsun Sheng: "...How many years into the future can you see?"
Li Xuanba said: "Over a thousand years."
Zhangsun Sheng nearly bit his tongue. He began to worry about Li Xuanba’s mental state.
Li Xuanba frowned, looking dejected: "So, Uncle, you understand now, right? I’m actually a bit bored with my current life."
"Although I tried very hard to choose the right people to confide in, I didn't really care much about the consequences. If the Tang falls, there will be other dynasties. Perhaps with a different dynasty, there wouldn't even be the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms or the Song and Yuan periods."
"Besides, my Second Brother carries the Mandate of Heaven. Before he appeared, people praised wise rulers by citing Yao and Shun; after him, whether they were scholars or monarchs, they often compared wise rulers to Emperor Taizong of Tang. I don't think he will die so easily."
"I have tried very hard to restrain myself, but if I misjudge, and you, or Teacher Gao, Teacher Yuwen, or Fang Xuanling leak this, it actually seems quite interesting."
"Emperor Yang of Sui certainly wouldn't kill me immediately. He would want to verify your words and summon me for questioning. Could I deceive him? Or would I flee to the deep mountains with my Second Brother and become a leader of a peasant uprising when the chaos of the late Sui begins?"
Li Xuanba asked very sincerely: "Uncle, do you think such a development would be more interesting than the present? Returning to your earlier question, you asked what my reliance was for daring to tell others the future? I think my reliance is that I have no need for reliance. Are you satisfied with this answer, Uncle?"

Zhangsun Sheng refilled Li Xuanba’s water and pushed the plate of milk cakes closer to him: "Eat some more; you must be hungry."
Li Xuanba obediently picked up a milk cake and nibbled on it.
Cold sweat soaked Zhangsun Sheng’s clothes behind his back.
Having spent decades walking the high-wire among the Turkic nobility, Zhangsun Sheng’s ability to read people had reached a near-supernatural level.
Therefore, he could tell that Li Xuanba was telling the truth; he wasn't pretending.
Although Li Xuanba had carefully selected the targets for his omens, he truly didn't care whether these preventive measures worked or not.
Was he not afraid of bringing disaster upon himself? Was he not afraid of bringing disaster upon Li Yuan, Lady Dou, and Li Erlang?
No, he did care.
Zhangsun Sheng reached the conclusion in an instant.
If Li Xuanba didn't care, he wouldn't have carefully selected the targets for his omens.
Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi would absolutely not leak the secret. Once they were on guard, no one else would be able to pry the secret from them.
The reason they were almost killed by the Emperor was that they didn't know the Emperor would kill them.
Not to mention them, Zhangsun Sheng prided himself on understanding the Emperor well, yet when he saw the Emperor’s murderous intent toward Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, he was also puzzled as to why the Emperor would do something so harmful and useless.
As for Fang Qiao, he didn't know him. But Li Xuanba had just said "Chancellor Fang," so this person must be Li Erlang’s confidant and right-hand man, a great talent confirmed by the *Old Book of Tang*. Fang Qiao was nearly thirty; the talent he would have in the future should already be present now. Therefore, knowing he could never be heavily employed in the Great Sui, he would definitely seize the opportunity to become "Chancellor Fang."
Moreover, Fang Qiao was the son of Fang Yanqian. Given Fang Yanqian’s integrity, his only son’s character surely wouldn't be poor.
The only uncertain factor in Li Xuanba’s choices was, surprisingly, himself.
If he were loyal enough to the Emperor, he might not necessarily believe Li Xuanba’s omens.
Omens were ethereal and invisible; the prosperity of the Great Sui was the fact before his eyes.
Most people would choose to believe the facts before them rather than "demonic words" that "confuse the masses."
To put it bluntly, Li Xuanba’s words could be seen as inciting him to betray the Emperor—they were genuine "demonic words."
This made Zhangsun Sheng almost laugh out of anger.
Because when he reached this conclusion, he became even more convinced that Li Xuanba’s "looking for fun" mentality was real.
If Li Xuanba wanted to persuade him not to go to the Western Regions while ill, he could have used a different method!
Did these almost "treasonous" words have anything to do with persuading him not to go to the Western Regions?!
Even if he wanted to persuade him using "omens," he could have just told him that his future son, Anye, would mistreat his stepmother and younger siblings. He could even have told him that Anye would turn against the Tang Duke’s estate, leading to his own death!

Li Xuanba finished another cake, wiped his hands clean, and cleared his throat with warm water.
"Uncle, have you calmed down?" Li Xuanba asked.
Zhangsun Sheng asked: "It should be me asking you, Dade, have you calmed down?"
Li Xuanba said: "I have always been calm."
Zhangsun Sheng laughed in anger.
He stepped down from the couch, walked over to Li Xuanba, and pressed hard on his little head: "Does your Second Brother know about your mental state? Do you want to find a high monk to chant scriptures for you?"
Li Xuanba held his head and said: "I am inclined toward suppressing Buddhism."
Zhangsun Sheng gasped: "You really dare to say anything. How did I end up with a relative like you?!"
Li Xuanba said: "Because your daughter is the virtuous empress confirmed by history? She was excellent in every way, gave birth to three sons and four daughters—seven children in total. Later generations speculate that she was worn out by giving birth too often, dying at the age of thirty-six."
Zhangsun Sheng staggered, roaring: "Li Xuanba!"
Li Xuanba said: "What are you rushing for? I haven't even mentioned Fourth Young Master Zhangsun..."
Zhangsun Sheng hurriedly waved his hands: "Stop, stop!"
Li Xuanba said: "Then Zhangsun Anye..."
Zhangsun Sheng took a deep breath: "Stop!"
Li Xuanba comforted him: "Don't worry too much. The one who becomes Emperor later is your grandson. Although Fourth Young Master Zhangsun had an unfortunate later life, he was later exonerated, and the Zhangsun lineage regained their titles and remained prosperous."
Zhangsun Sheng gritted his teeth: "Li Xuanba, I told you to stop."
He hadn't felt this bad even when he was being held captive by the Turkic Khan!
Li Xuanba jumped down from the stool and bowed to Zhangsun Sheng: "To avoid future tragedies, please take care of your health, Uncle."
"As soon as you pass away, Zhangsun Anye will drive Lady Gao, Fourth Young Master Zhangsun, and Little Miss Zhangsun out of the house. The three of them will live with their uncle, Gao Shilian, and be raised by him."
"Although Uncle Gao is very good to his nephew and niece, living under someone else’s roof inevitably left an indelible mark on them. Furthermore, Uncle Gao himself was struggling and not well-off. Lady Gao was depressed and passed away early. My Second Sister-in-law married my Second Brother at thirteen to escape."
Li Xuanba looked up: "Just like Mother."
Zhangsun Sheng’s lips trembled, but he ultimately didn't tell Li Xuanba to shut up again.
Li Xuanba said: "Looking at ancient consorts and noblewomen, it is rare for a wife from a good family to be worn to death by excessive childbirth. Uncle, you should understand that a legal wife has the right to refuse when she is at an age unsuitable for childbirth."
His mother had arranged for many concubines for Li Yuan after giving birth to Li Yuanji. Li Yuan had also been very cooperative, mostly just sleeping under the covers with his mother.
Empress Ma of later generations also gave birth to many children like Empress Zhangsun, but almost all were born before Zhu Yuanzhang had made his mark. After becoming Empress, Empress Ma also sent old Zhu to sleep with his concubines.
Li Xuanba said: "My Second Sister-in-law gave birth to many children even at an advanced age. Firstly, there were no elders to teach them these things; secondly, she might have known, but felt she lacked the standing to refuse. Without you, Uncle, the Zhangsun family would have become mere in-laws, not a union of merit and the Emperor. If you were there, she might have had more confidence. Although my Second Brother respects her, she lived under someone else’s roof since childhood and lacked a sense of security."

Zhangsun Sheng took several deep breaths before sitting down on the couch, his feet dangling, his hand gently rubbing his chest: "You even bring up palace matters?"
Li Xuanba said: "My brother’s later years were also unsettled, all stemming from the early death of his wife and the fact that he was a man who truly didn't know how to raise children."
Zhangsun Sheng finally recovered and said irritably: "It’s a good thing there’s a Li Erlang who can keep you in check."
Li Xuanba said displeased: "Don't make it sound like I’m a mad dog."
Zhangsun Sheng said: "Your self-assessment is quite accurate."
Li Xuanba threatened: "Uncle, if you insult me again, I’ll tell you that my Second Sister-in-law contracted an incurable respiratory illness when she was driven out of the Zhangsun estate and forced to live under someone else’s roof."
Although later generations speculated that Empress Zhangsun’s respiratory illness was congenital, Zhangsun Wuji did not have it, and the congenital illnesses of the children she bore were all inherited from the Li family’s cardiovascular diseases. Her illness might have been left over from a bout of pneumonia in childhood that wasn't properly treated.
The truth in history could not be known, but Li Xuanba had probed the body of his Second Sister-in-law in this world; she did not have congenital asthma.
Zhangsun Sheng’s mouth twitched: "You already told me. If I die early, it will definitely be because I was angered to death by you."
Li Xuanba bowed repeatedly: "I wouldn't dare, I wouldn't dare."
Zhangsun Sheng rubbed his chest again: "Would you be willing to take me as your master?"
Li Xuanba asked in confusion: "When Second Brother was learning archery from you, I was also learning. I have already taken you as my master."
Zhangsun Sheng said with disdain: "Your archery was learned from Li Yuan; it has nothing to do with me. I can't afford to lose face like that. Anye was indeed ruined; Fourth Young Master is clever but not good at reading people; you were born to do what I do. Kowtow to me, and I will pass on everything I have learned. If you want to find the 'fun' you speak of, you can go and cause trouble for the Turks. Once the Turks are destroyed, there are still many small countries around for you to wreak havoc on."
*Go abroad to find your fun! Don't ruin your own people!*
Li Xuanba felt deeply despised by Zhangsun Sheng.
Li Xuanba said: "Then shall I call Second Brother in to take you as his master?"
Zhangsun Sheng said: "Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi are perfect for teaching him, but learning their skills won't be of much use to you. Learning the skills of Xue Daoheng and Yu Shinan is barely acceptable for cultivating one’s character. As for my skills, Li Erlang doesn't need to learn them; he only needs to learn how to use people."
Li Xuanba shook his head: "That won't do. I absolutely do not allow Second Brother to do less homework than me."
Zhangsun Sheng: "..." *This disciple is truly beyond saving!*
He hoped Li Xuanba’s future wife would be fierce enough to add another lock to him. Li Erlang was still too loose a lock, too indulgent of Li Xuanba.
*This person is truly a disaster!*
Zhangsun Sheng said: "Fine. Then call Fourth Young Master... and Guanyin-bi as well. There are some skills she can learn too."
In the past, when Li Erlang said he wanted Guanyin-bi to dress in men’s clothes and attend classes with them, Zhangsun Sheng just wanted to beat Li Erlang up.
*Nonsense!*
Now that he knew Guanyin-bi would be Empress in the future, then let it be nonsense.
Although his wife was kind, she wasn't good at scheming. It was a pity to use his strategies in the inner palace, but it was better than learning nothing.
Moreover, Guanyin-bi would go out to conquer the world with Li Erlang; her skills might not only be used in the inner palace. Once she became Empress, those countries in the Western Regions would also need the influence of noblewomen.
The Emperor would eventually become Emperor Yang of Sui; it seemed the Turks would not only fail to be destroyed but would rise again at the end of the Sui. Marrying into the Turks to exchange for them not attacking the Central Plains—Emperor Wen of Sui did it, and the Great Tang would do it too. For a princess married to the Turks, the upper limit was influencing Turkic decisions, and the lower limit was just a sacrificial lamb.
Whether it was raising a princess for marriage or interacting with powerful Turkic noblewomen, it all depended on Guanyin-bi’s abilities.
Zhangsun Sheng sighed inwardly. If Guanyin-bi spent her energy on more external affairs, she probably wouldn't care so much about Li Erlang. Being a virtuous empress who ruled over three thousand concubines was not an easy job.
Empress and Empress Dowager might be the pinnacle of a woman’s status. But in Zhangsun Sheng’s view, he would rather his youngest daughter be an ordinary noble lady.
Even if Li Erlang became the Duke of Tang in the future, if he bullied Guanyin-bi, he would dare to bring her home.
Zhangsun Sheng, as Li Xuanba wished, had his will to live ignited. He temporarily set aside the cause of completely destroying the Turks and focused his life’s goals on health and cultivating the younger generation.
The only thing Zhangsun Sheng found comforting was that although Li Xuanba was a disaster, he was very kind to his daughter. After his daughter married Li Erlang, she wouldn't have to worry about her relationship with Li Xuanba and his wife.

Li Xuanba pulled his Second Brother, who was already nodding off on the steps, into the room, and forced him to kowtow three times to Zhangsun Sheng and serve tea.
This treatment was originally reserved only for Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi; they hadn't even performed strict apprenticeship rites for Yu Shinan and Xue Daoheng.
After drinking the tea, Zhangsun Sheng said: "I will prepare gifts for my disciples. When you return, have Duke Li make up for your apprenticeship gifts as well."
Li Xuanba said: "Yes, Master."
Li Shimin said dazedly: "Ah? Oh."
Zhangsun Sheng looked with disdain at his bewildered future son-in-law.
*This is the Tang Taizong whom Li Xuanba calls 'not daring to claim to be the Emperor of the Ages, but daring to claim to be the Wise Ruler of the Ages'?*
In the past, he thought everything about Li Shimin was good, but now that he knew Li Shimin’s future achievements, Li Shimin was full of flaws in his eyes.
Zhangsun Sheng said: "Dade, in the future, if you want to reveal omens to anyone, if the situation is appropriate, tell me, and I will analyze it for you."
Li Xuanba sighed: "Yes, Master."
Li Shimin turned to his brother: "A-Xuan, what did you... reveal to Uncle... Master?"
Li Xuanba said: "I said that Second Sister-in-law gave birth to three sons and four daughters for you, and was worn to death by giving birth, dying at thirty-six."
Li Shimin: "..."
Zhangsun Sheng: "..."
Li Shimin immediately sprayed out all his tears and snot.
It really sprayed out.
His knees went weak, and he collapsed onto the floor with a thud: "A-Xuan! What grudge do I have against you! Can't you tell me this first! Father-in-law! I was wrong! Please don't call off the marriage! I will definitely not let Guanyin-bi give birth to so many children!"
Li Xuanba had long ago explained to Li Shimin why Lady Dou’s personality changed drastically when she gave birth to Li Yuanji, letting Li Shimin know how hard Lady Dou’s pregnancies were. So when Li Xuanba said "three sons and four daughters" and "died at thirty-six," he understood.
"Alright, alright, get up." Zhangsun Sheng hurriedly helped Li Shimin up.
Li Shimin was the future Emperor; he couldn't let him suffer too much frustration here. Although Li Shimin was a good child who didn't hold grudges now, who knew if he would settle old scores like the current Emperor once he became Emperor? The frustration he caused Li Shimin would all become a disaster for his daughter in the future.
Although Zhangsun Sheng began to despise Li Shimin in his heart, he would only be more cordial to him on the surface.
"It is a good thing that you and Guanyin-bi have a good relationship in the future." Zhangsun Sheng wiped Li Shimin’s snot and tears, saying gently, "It’s just that for families like ours, having many children is not necessarily a blessing; health is more important. Guanyin-bi’s body is a bit weak; I have let you down. Can we let Guanyin-bi marry you after she turns sixteen, and wait until you come of age to consummate the marriage? I will nourish Guanyin-bi’s health more."
Li Shimin nodded like a garlic-pounding pestle: "Okay, okay, I agree! I’ll talk to Father and Mother about it!"
Zhangsun Sheng smiled: "I will discuss such matters with your parents myself; why would I make it difficult for you? It’s just that your feelings are also important, so I need to ask for your consent. As parents, we hope most for our children’s happiness in marriage and family. The one who will accompany Guanyin-bi until she is old is not me; her reliance is you."
Li Shimin patted his chest: "Father-in-law, rest assured, I will take good care of Guanyin-bi."
Zhangsun Sheng nodded: "I heard that you and Guanyin-bi have a very good relationship in the future, so I am relieved about this marriage. Sigh, I heard that the brothers in the Tang Duke’s estate are not on good terms, and I am actually very worried that Guanyin-bi will be mistreated after entering your home."
Li Shimin shook his head hurriedly, his two hair buns swinging like blurs: "I will absolutely not let Guanyin-bi be mistreated."
Li Xuanba said: "That’s not necessarily true. She won't be mistreated while you are there, but when you are leading troops away in the future, the inner court will be supported by Second Sister-in-law alone... Ouch!"
Li Shimin jumped in front of Li Xuanba, clamped his brother’s head under his arm, and knocked on it hard: "A-Xuan! Your skin is itching! Are you deliberately looking for a beating today!"
Zhangsun Sheng watched happily as Li Xuanba was beaten for a while before hypocritically stopping them.
"Don't be angry, Dade’s words are not false. In the future, Guanyin-bi will also need to face many difficulties alone." Zhangsun Sheng said gently, "When I teach you later, I will let Guanyin-bi listen in as well, so she can learn more skills to deal with difficulties. You two must not leak this, lest it ruin Guanyin-bi’s reputation."
Li Shimin clamped his brother’s head under his arm: "Okay! My mouth is very tight! A-Xuan’s mouth is also very tight!"
Zhangsun Sheng nodded with a smile while swearing in his heart.
*Li Dade’s mouth is tight, my foot!*
Li Shimin, looking terrified, hurriedly dragged Li Xuanba away after Zhangsun Sheng told them to go back and notify Li Yuan to offer formal apprenticeship gifts, almost saying "the wind is blowing, let's pull out."
After getting into the carriage, Li Shimin smoothed his chest and complained: "You really know how to find trouble for your brother! You didn't just say that... what’s with that expression?"
Li Xuanba gritted his teeth: "Damn it, I hate playing tai chi with old foxes who are in high positions!"
Li Xuanba had developed PTSD from chatting with Zhangsun Sheng!
As a low-level commoner, Li Xuanba’s shrewdness was all learned from struggling. Every time he negotiated business or cooperation, he would be frustrated when encountering people in high positions.
Not only did the other party’s status and age suppress him, but what was even more hateful was that their shrewdness also suppressed him! Everything suppressed him, forcing him to be under immense psychological pressure, and most of the time he couldn't get any benefit and found it hard to protect his own interests.
Fortunately, Zhangsun Sheng hadn't seen "crazy literature" yet, so Li Xuanba gave Zhangsun Sheng a little shock of mental illness.
By the end, Li Xuanba wasn't thinking about his goal anymore; he just wanted to suppress Zhangsun Sheng and make him break his defense.
*This is fucking PTSD! Tsk!*
Li Xuanba slapped his thighs with both hands: "I’m so pissed! I hate cunning old men the most!"
Li Shimin looked at his brother’s madness with sympathy: "Hard work. Seeing your reaction, A-Xuan, I finally see a bit of the ability our father-in-law has to make the Turks split and decline."
It was rare to see his brother break his defense, and a sense of indescribable joy welled up in Li Shimin’s heart.
It was fun to see others break their defense when his brother revealed the future, and it was also fun to see his brother break his defense.
Li Xuanba glared fiercely at his Second Brother.
Li Shimin hurriedly pulled down his raised corners of his mouth.
Li Xuanba said sarcastically: "Sister-in-law would have married you at thirteen and consummated the marriage at sixteen or seventeen; now she will marry you at sixteen and consummate it when you come of age. Are you sad?"
Li Shimin said seriously: "A-Xuan, what nonsense are you talking about? What is more important than your sister-in-law’s health? When you go back, write a letter to Doctor Sun and ask how men can use contraception without harming the body."
Li Xuanba: "Oh." *Why ask Doctor Sun for such things? Just ask me. Although I don't have practical experience, I have rich theoretical experience.*
There were no perfect contraceptive methods now, but avoiding the fertile period and supplementing with things like sheep intestines could minimize the probability of pregnancy.
*At worst, I’ll let sister-in-law stay up late and get fat after giving birth, trying to get polycystic ovary syndrome. Polycystic in ancient times is a life-saving 'wealthy disease' for women.* Cough, Li Xuanba dispelled the unrealistic fantasies in his mind.
Li Shimin patted Li Xuanba’s head, told his brother to lower his head, and retied the hair buns that he had knocked loose: "Can our father-in-law’s life be saved?"
Li Xuanba said: "I don't know."
Li Shimin said: "Do your best and wait for Heaven’s will. We just need to do our best; don't have any psychological burden."
Li Xuanba asked in confusion: "What psychological burden could I have?"
Li Shimin smiled: "Consider it me talking to myself."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第71章 究竟谁是预言家 – 第72章 谁在旅途还学习
chunks.chineseText:
第71章 究竟谁是预言家

=
　　李玄霸一路上都气鼓鼓的。
　　李世民看得特别开心， 表情慈祥无比。
　　看到弟弟发脾气，真是太可爱了。
　　希望丈人能多活几年，让弟弟多发几回脾气。
　　李玄霸撕掉了自己在这一辈子养出的文弱贵公子皮， 如前世市井小民一样嘀咕了许多粗言粗语， 骂骂咧咧直到马车回府。
　　回到家后， 李玄霸抹了一把脸，把表情恢复成古井无波的模样。
　　李世民劝道：“你不用假装平静。耶耶娘娘不会因为你发脾气而生气。”
　　李玄霸慢吞吞道：“我不是担心他们生气。别废话，赶紧把拜师的事告诉父亲母亲。”
　　李世民叹了口气， 拍了拍弟弟的后脑勺：“好。”
　　李世民和李玄霸将又拜师的事告诉李渊和窦夫人的时候。
　　窦夫人保持着完美的微笑。李渊扶着额头不断叹气。

　　油封水，能让有些柴的鹿肉变得稍稍柔嫩一些。可惜没有注射器。烤大型猎物时，往肉里注射姜蒜盐水，不仅更加入味，还能让肉质变得鲜嫩。
　　现在大隋贵族最爱的美食就是烧烤。裴世矩吃过许多美味的烧烤，但闻着这鹿肉的香味，也难以抑制口中口水的分泌。
　　裴世矩出身关中郡姓的河东裴氏，现在门第不如山东郡姓，但在魏晋是能与琅琊王氏并称的超级大族，族人中高官频出，现在还是垄断朝纲的关陇贵族中的一员，好东西见了许多。
　　他原本看不上发家很晚的唐国公府。
　　同为关陇贵族也有鄙视链，关中郡姓就视武将勋贵为根基浅显的“寒门”。
　　现在最美味的菜谱都是各家秘方，最好吃的宴会是各个世家勋贵的家宴。世家门阀最兴盛的魏晋南北朝时代，皇帝的御厨都比不上世家门阀的家厨。菜谱的丰富和美味程度，也是家族底蕴的象征。
　　裴世矩心想唐国公府肯定没有多少美味的菜谱秘方，琢磨等会儿看路上能不能撞见猎户和农家，买些新鲜肉食，给唐国公府的两位郎君尝尝河东裴氏的祖传烧烤秘方，给他们开开眼界。
　　看到唐国公府厨子那新奇的烧烤手法后，裴世矩决定，之后买到新鲜肉食，就不做烧烤了。
　　烤肉还没入口，凭借香味，他就发现比不过。
　　裴世矩问道：“听闻李三郎很喜欢复原古方，这是西域的秘法还是古方？”
　　李世民毫不犹豫地胡扯：“是古方。汉时张骞出塞，带回来的芝麻能榨出很香的油脂，边用这很香的油脂刷在肉上一同烧烤，美味至极。”
　　李玄霸用眼角余光瞥了二哥一眼。
　　二哥什么时候练就的一副随口胡扯出“出处”的本事？这算“创史”还是“改史”？回忆录中要记一笔。
　　裴世矩不疑有他，感慨道：“原来如此。我也重口腹之欲，看来得多淘一些残本，看能不能也找到一些有趣的失传古方。”
　　鹿烤好了。
　　不出裴世矩所料，外酥里嫩的口感就像是吃家养的肉鹿似的，香辛料的调配更是精妙绝伦，吃得裴世矩赞不绝口，当即愿意用一张面点、一张蒸菜的秘方换唐国公府烤肉的秘方。
　　虽然李玄霸和李世民说可以白送，但裴世矩还是在之后的那顿饭，让随行的厨子把面点和蒸菜做了出来，得到李玄霸和李世民好评之后，才拿走了李玄霸现写的烤肉秘方。
　　交换菜谱后，裴世矩与李玄霸、李世民关系亲近不少。
　　他邀请李玄霸和李世民同乘，沿路给李玄霸和李世民介绍张掖的事，并愿意临时充当李玄霸和李世民的老师，帮李玄霸和李世民补足缺失的功课。
　　路上，他还问了高颎、宇文弼、薛道衡、虞世南和长孙晟给李玄霸、李世民布置的功课，非常热心地监督二人在晚上住宿时完成功课。
　　李世民死鱼眼：“这人怎么如此讨厌？我将来真的尊敬他？”
　　李玄霸点头：“他讨厌，你也真的尊敬他。”
　　李世民抱着脑袋发疯：“啊啊啊啊，路上这么累了，为什么还要完成功课！他烦不烦啊！”
　　李玄霸点头：“好为人师是病，他甚至给我们加了功课。”
　　兄弟二人齐齐发誓，以后如果有机会，也要给裴世矩增加很多“功课”，让他知道自己现在的苦！
　　唐朝建立时他都七十多了又如何？没听过老当益壮吗！
　　啊啊啊啊啊，为什么这么累还要做功课！
　　在驿站的另一个房间，裴世矩挑灯帮两个少年郎批改功课。
　　他一边看一边拈须微笑：“我还以为他们会十分疲惫，没想到还有精力完成功课。这才华，怪不得高公他们抢着收徒。可惜我的资历不够……”
　　裴世矩想着高颎、宇文弼和薛道衡的声望，遗憾自己不好意思让李世民和李玄霸拜师。
　　至于虞世南，只教写字算什么老师？
　　裴世矩忽视了长孙晟。
　　长孙晟在经略西域上的声望堪称魁首，若他教导李世民和李玄霸这方面的本事，高颎、宇文弼和薛道衡也说不得一句不满。
　　但裴世矩自诩也擅长经略外夷，所以内心把长孙晟视作不过运气好早得机会的对手，不想太涨他人志气。
　　虽不愿意涨他人志气，李世民和李玄霸也是长孙晟的弟子这件事不是忽视就能忘记的。
　　裴世矩见才心喜的同时也起了胜负心，虽无师徒之名，但陛下把两个少年托付给他时也叮嘱过他好好教导两个少年，所以裴世矩就光明正大地充当起了李世民和李玄霸的老师，沿路开展了他的教学。
　　李世民和李玄霸再爱学习，也想发疯。
　　啊啊啊啊张掖什么时候才到啊！我们不要在马车上听课！裴世矩讲课又讲得没意思，马车晃来晃去昏昏欲睡啊！
　　李玄霸决定不陪着二哥死撑了。他当即表演一个面白如纸，书本一丢，病了。
　　我，李家三郎，出了名的病秧子。
　　李世民赶紧哭了一场，每日守着弟弟侍奉汤药。
　　裴世矩：“……”啊？我把他们折腾病了？这……
　　唐国公府的随行医师忍不住抱怨：“旅途本就劳累，公还让李二郎君李三郎军耗费精力听课……唉，裴公，我说过很不妥了。”
　　李玄霸：假装奄奄一息。
　　李世民：假装心急如焚。
　　裴世矩疯狂冷汗。
　　糟糕！不小心做过火了！如果李二郎李三郎出事该怎么办？！
　　当李玄霸和李世民见裴世矩心虚后，与医师说了一声，医师宣布李玄霸痊愈，可以继续旅途。
　　裴世矩之后的路程中，再也没有提过李玄霸和李世民功课的事。两人看书的时候，他还劝两人别劳累。
　　李玄霸和李世民击掌，提着刚从农户那里买的小公鸡给孙医师道谢。
　　孙思邈捋了捋胡须，微笑道：“不用谢。”
