**Chapter 71: Who Exactly Is the Prophet?**

Li Xuanba remained sullen throughout the journey.
Li Shimin watched him with immense delight, his expression one of boundless affection.
Seeing his younger brother throw a tantrum was truly adorable.
He hoped his father-in-law would live for many more years, just so his brother could throw a few more tantrums.
Li Xuanba had long since shed the skin of the frail, refined young nobleman he had cultivated in this life. Like a commoner from his past life, he muttered a string of coarse words, grumbling and cursing until the carriage returned to the manor.
Once home, Li Xuanba wiped his face, restoring his expression to one of undisturbed stillness.
Li Shimin urged, "You don't need to pretend to be calm. Father and Mother won't be angry just because you threw a fit."
Li Xuanba replied sluggishly, "I'm not worried about them being angry. Stop the nonsense and hurry up and tell Father and Mother about the apprenticeship."
Li Shimin sighed and patted his brother on the back of the head. "Fine."

When Li Shimin and Li Xuanba told Li Yuan and Lady Dou about the new apprenticeship, Lady Dou maintained a perfect smile, while Li Yuan held his forehead and sighed incessantly.
Li Yuan said, "How are you two again... *Sigh*. I told you to visit the famous scholars of the court one by one, but are you planning to take every single one of them as your master? My lady, you used to say that my socializing with too many friends was too ostentatious and might provoke the Emperor’s suspicion. Look at Dexiong and Dade now!"
Lady Dou said gently, "It’s only four teachers. General Zhangsun is our in-law, so it doesn't really count."
Li Yuan’s previous words were just a joke. He knew four teachers weren't too many; he was simply proud of his sons' exceptional talent for securing apprenticeships.
*As expected of my sons, they are just so likable. My in-law was hesitant before, claiming illness to avoid teaching Erlang and Sanlang. Yet, even while still 'ill,' he has now formally accepted them as students?*
Regardless of how Erlang and Sanlang had managed to win over Zhangsun Sheng, Li Yuan sent the apprenticeship gifts that very day, ensuring Zhangsun Sheng had no chance to go back on his word.
Li Yuan and Zhangsun Sheng were already in-laws, and that marriage had been secured by Li Yuan’s "thick-skinned" archery victory. Thus, the rest of the court assumed Li Yuan was simply being thick-skinned once more and didn't pay much attention.

Zhangsun Sheng finished writing his proposal and brought it to the palace himself.
At the palace gates, he slowly collapsed, terrifying the guards.
While the guards were stunned, his servants wept as they carried him back to the carriage and returned him to his manor.
When Yang Guang heard the news, he hurriedly dispatched imperial physicians.
The imperial physicians and the physician retained by the Zhangsun household held a joint consultation, concluding that Zhangsun Sheng’s illness had not healed and that he was suffering from extreme exhaustion, requiring absolute bed rest.
Having stayed up all night, Zhangsun Sheng slept soundly, then struggled to rise, asking Zhangsun Wuji to draft an apology to the Emperor on his behalf. He expressed guilt for being hindered by his body and feared he could not travel west, offering only a clumsy strategy in hopes of assisting the Emperor.
Although Zhangsun Sheng had previously disagreed with Yang Guang in court, Yang Guang still trusted and valued him greatly.
Yang Guang sent the Crown Prince, Yang Zhao—who was still in Luoyang—to personally visit Zhangsun Sheng with precious medicinal herbs, telling him to focus on his recovery and not to worry.
Zhangsun Sheng knelt on his bed, kowtowing toward the palace in gratitude, tears streaming down his face.
After Yang Zhao reported back, Yang Guang sighed, "Zhangsun Sheng is getting old. Fortunately, I have Pei Shiju to carry on his mantle."
Yang Zhao joked, "General Zhangsun likely thinks Dade can carry on his mantle."
Yang Guang laughed, "Dade is a minister I have reserved for you. In the future, it will be your turn to promote him."
Yang Zhao put away his smile and knelt to thank him.
Yang Guang said, "Rise. Between father and son, we don't need such empty formalities."
After rising, Yang Zhao continued, "General Zhangsun is very eager to serve you; even in his illness, he insists on teaching Li Erlang and Li Sanlang, urging them to perform well."
Yang Guang nodded with satisfaction, "Zhangsun Jisheng is very loyal."
Only when he heard his father stop calling the General by his full name and finally use his courtesy name did Yang Zhao feel the heavy stone in his heart drop.
*Father’s paranoia is truly a headache. The General fainted in front of everyone at the palace gate, and the physicians confirmed his chronic illness, yet Father still suspected he was feigning illness to avoid the western campaign because he disagreed with it in court.*
This suspicion was not only baseless but also inconsistent with the General’s character and interests.

After returning to the Eastern Palace that Yang Guang had built for him in Luoyang, Yang Zhao gently rubbed his chubby waist.
*It’s so tiring.*
Sometimes, Yang Zhao envied his younger brother, Yang Jian, for his carefree, heartless life.
Though he knew rationally that he had to be the Crown Prince, otherwise he, his wife, and his children would all die in vain.
"Send a message to Dade; it’s all clear now," Yang Zhao told his confidant. "Tell him not to be too anxious. We are heading west soon; it won't be good if he gets sick."
The confidant acknowledged the order and left.
As the Crown Prince, Yang Zhao not only had confidants who could hide things from his father, but he could also openly exchange items with Li Shimin, Li Xuanba, and Yang Jian without Yang Guang ever suspecting a thing.

After Li Xuanba received the message from Yang Zhao, he informed Zhangsun Sheng.
"Teacher, the Emperor is truly petty. Do you regret following the wrong person?" Li Xuanba asked cheekily.
After finishing his medicine, Zhangsun Sheng tapped Li Xuanba’s head with the empty bowl. "The Emperor was excellent when he was a prince. Even Gao Jiong, who insisted on the eldest son succeeding and opposed the Emperor becoming Crown Prince, had to admit his brilliance."
*Who could have known he would be a different person after ascending the throne?*
The Emperor was thirty-five when he ascended; half his life was already behind him. No one could have predicted that the character he had displayed for thirty-five years would take such a sharp turn.
However, if most of the Emperor’s life had been a facade, Zhangsun Sheng understood why he had acted so abnormally upon taking the throne.
*He had truly been holding it in for too long.*
Zhangsun Sheng had originally been skeptical of Li Xuanba’s prophecies, but he came to believe them completely because Li Xuanba, for the sake of a trivial matter like keeping him from traveling west while ill, had elevated the prophecy to the level of "treason."
*Who would say "we will commit treason in the future" while trying to convince a patient to rest?*
Such a crazy "dissuasion" forced Zhangsun Sheng to believe Li Xuanba was serious.
Furthermore, he was not the first person to whom Li Xuanba had revealed the future.
Zhangsun Sheng had long noticed the excessive abnormality of Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi. He knew them well; they were definitely not cowards who would willingly retreat.
The information Li Xuanba revealed filled in the missing intelligence he needed to judge their behavior.
Given Li Xuanba’s caution, what Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi knew must have been different "future fragments" belonging only to them. If those two old foxes could believe Li Xuanba, Zhangsun Sheng had no choice but to believe as well.
He was not on good terms with Gao Jiong and had no friendship with Yuwen Bi, but he acknowledged their talent and trusted their judgment.

"Alright, you don't need to worry about this anymore. I know how to deal with the Emperor," Zhangsun Sheng said. "How is your Turkic coming along?"
Li Xuanba said helplessly, "I only need to learn Tuyuhun; why must I learn Turkic?"
Zhangsun Sheng retorted, "What is Tuyuhun? It can be wiped out with a flick of a finger. When you go to Zhangye, you must listen for news of the Turks. The Turks are the real threat. You wouldn't want your Second Brother to be stabbed in the back by the Turks while he is pacifying the world at the end of the Sui, would you?"
Li Xuanba’s expression stiffened slightly.
Zhangsun Sheng asked curiously, "What? Did he really get stabbed?"
Li Xuanba said, "Father withstood the pressure and did not recall Second Brother."
Zhangsun Sheng was even more curious, "It seems Li Yuan has some ability after all. But Li Yuan must have wavered, right? And Li Jiancheng—wouldn't he have wanted to run away?"
Li Xuanba said, "Teacher will know when the time comes; why be curious now? Things in the future might change."
Zhangsun Sheng smiled, "So it was Li Jiancheng who suggested moving the capital south to avoid the Turks."
Li Xuanba: "..." *Who is the prophet here?!*
Zhangsun Sheng said, "Even if he demanded Erlang return, it would be too late. Since he fears the Turks, he must have wanted to run."
Li Xuanba: "..." *Who exactly is the prophet?!*
Li Xuanba nodded repeatedly. "Amazing, amazing, as expected of my teacher. But it wasn't my elder brother who proposed moving the capital; he only echoed Father. The dispute over moving the capital wasn't during the pacification of the world, but after. Does Teacher want to hear anything else? I’ll tell you everything!"
Zhangsun Sheng put away his smile. "Stop, I don't want to hear it." *Li Yuan is actually even more cowardly than I imagined?*

Li Shimin walked in carrying a pot of freshly boiled water.
Zhangsun Sheng and Li Xuanba were discussing serious matters and didn't have other servants waiting on them. Li Shimin hurried to curry favor with his father-in-law.
He happened to hear Zhangsun Sheng’s words and chuckled, "I often say what you just said, Teacher. Ah Xuan, don't go too far. Be careful or I’ll stuff Xiao Wu into your bed tonight. Xiao Wu is growing, and he kicks his legs in his sleep; his sleeping posture is even worse than mine."
Li Xuanba curled his lip, "Turning your back on your own kin."
Li Shimin set down the kettle and said seriously, "How can you call my father-in-law an outsider?"
*Pah!* Li Xuanba spat at his Second Brother in his heart.
He would definitely record this damn sycophantic look of his Second Brother so that future generations could properly admire it.
*Memoirs, I am definitely writing them!*

Zhangsun Sheng hurriedly gave Li Xuanba and Li Shimin a few more lessons, and in the blink of an eye, it was time for them to follow Pei Shiju to Zhangye.
Zhangsun Xiaomei gave Li Shimin a prayer pouch she had sewn herself, which didn't look very good.
Li Xuanba also received a pouch from his fiancée. He glanced at his Second Brother’s pouch. *Hmm, my fiancée’s embroidery is better than Zhangsun Xiaomei’s.*
Yuwen Zhu not only sent a gift for the first time, but she also wrote to Li Xuanba for the first time since their engagement.
She wrote that she had been in mourning for her younger brother, so it was inconvenient to write to Li Sanlang. But with Li Sanlang going to the Western Regions, she was worried and could only disregard the etiquette of mourning, asking him not to mind her being in the mourning period.
Yuwen Zhu wrote a few polite phrases in the letter, but the remaining dozen pages were all medical prescriptions.
For cold weather, for nourishment, for digestion, for repelling insects... Besides the prescriptions, she also sent the corresponding prepared pills and powders.
"My medical skills are shallow, and I dare not prescribe for Sanlang. These pills and powders are verified, common medicines, and I have attached the medical texts."
Then, at the very bottom of the letter, Yuwen Zhu wrote a long excerpt on medical techniques.
Li Xuanba silently put away the letter, which felt like a thesis, preparing to use it as bedtime reading.
With the complex mood of receiving a "thesis" as his first letter from his fiancée, Li Xuanba saw for the first time this "Evil King" Shi Zhixuan from *The Legend of the Twin Dragons of the Tang*.
He smiled.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had a private carriage. To make the two children more comfortable, Pei Shiju had provided them with a carriage even more spacious than his own.
In the carriage, Li Shimin asked curiously, "Ah Xuan, why did you smile the moment you saw Pei Gong?"
Li Xuanba said, "A friendly face, a joyful heart."
Li Shimin glanced at his brother, "Heh, be serious."
Li Xuanba said, "There is a novel in the future called *The Legend of the Twin Dragons of the Tang*, which depicts Pei Shiju as the leader of a cult, known as the Evil King."
Li Shimin: "Wow!" He didn't want to hear what else the book wrote; he felt it would kill him.

**Chapter 72: Who Studies While Traveling?**

Although Li Shimin didn't want to know the specific plot of *The Legend of the Twin Dragons of the Tang*, Li Xuanba still told him the general story, omitting the late Tang background.
If he didn't tell his Second Brother, how could he share the snarky thoughts in his heart?
Li Shimin was shocked by the intricate romantic relationships and the fact that two martial arts sects, the Cihang Jingzhai and the Yinkui Sect, could manipulate the rise and fall of dynasties. He was also very dissatisfied that the novel had arranged a love interest for him named Shi Feixuan.
Li Xuanba: [Shi Feixuan is nothing; do you want to hear how many "true loves" you have in future novels?]
Li Shimin covered his ears and shook his head vigorously.
Li Xuanba: [You have epic romances with Empress Xiao, your sister-in-law, your brother’s wife, a Turkic princess, and a Sui princess. Oh, and you even fancied a minister’s wife.]
Li Shimin covered his ears, eyes welling with tears: "Why do people of the future slander me so?"
Li Xuanba thought for a moment and said, "Because it’s interesting."
Li Shimin’s head ached with anger: "People of the future are so annoying!"
Li Xuanba comforted him: "They only write these stories because they like you. There are many people who adore you so much that they want to travel back to ancient times to have an epic romance with you. In those stories, your sister-in-law is usually the jealous villain, deep in schemes and cruel. Tsk tsk."
Li Shimin lowered his hands, his eyes vacant: "That woman must hate me, right? Do they dare slander Guanyinbi to my face? Throw them all in jail!"
Li Xuanba said, "What’s a woman? There are even men who travel back to have epic romances with you."
Li Shimin gagged.
Li Shimin was a staunch resident of Mount Kongtong (a pun for "homophobic")!
Li Xuanba lowered his voice: "Some even praise the epic romances between you and your ministers, like Fang Xuanling and Du Keming."
Li Shimin was shocked: "Huh? Writing people as male concubines and sycophants is called 'praise'?"
Li Xuanba said, "You don't understand. The moral values of the future are different. You must know that those who are willing to write fanfiction for you and give you a beautiful romance truly respect you. It’s the kind of respect where, if someone says something bad about you, they might want to find them and fight them in person. Understand?"
Li Shimin shook his head vigorously. He didn't understand, he really didn't. *Please don't respect me! It’s terrifying!*
Li Xuanba comforted him: "It’s all after you’re dead anyway, so why mind? Just laugh it off. Look at the famous people in history; which one hasn't had a pile of unofficial histories written about them?"
Li Shimin patted Li Xuanba’s shoulder: "You’re right. When you can reveal the future to Du Keming and the others later, remember to tell them the stories of their epic romances with me. And you must emphasize that this is how future generations praise them, just that the moral standards are different. I can't be the only one angered to death by you. Oh, you can tell Fang Xuanling stories as soon as you go back."
He regretted that when Fang Xuanling came to see him off, Li Xuanba hadn't told him the story of the "true" love between monarch and subject.
Li Xuanba gave his Second Brother a thumbs up and stopped torturing him.
*Second Brother is about to kill his own ministers; let him rest for a while.*

After Li Shimin grumbled a few times about how "strange" future people were, he cheekily asked Li Xuanba to tell stories about other people.
He didn't want to hear about the future, but he was very interested in the stories of famous people from the past, especially former emperors.
Li Xuanba had seen too many such stories.
Originally, he wanted to tell his brother the more serious *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, but his brother only wanted to hear "romance." So, Li Xuanba chose fanfiction about the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han, alternating between romance, *danmei*, and original protagonists paired with historical figures.
Li Shimin listened with a beaming smile, his laughter so hearty that even Pei Shiju in the front heard it, wondering what interesting things Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were talking about to be so happy.
Li Xuanba didn't get thirsty telling stories with his inner voice, so he could keep going.
Accompanied by Li Xuanba’s interesting stories, the dull and long journey was not hard to endure at all.
On the way, Li Shimin went out to ride for a while and shot a silly deer that had poked its head out by the roadside.
Pei Shiju exclaimed, "I heard Li Erlang once hunted a tiger; seeing it today, he is truly a young hero."
Li Shimin laughed, "I didn't hunt the tiger alone; the guards surrounded it. Besides, the tigers in the imperial park aren't that fierce. Pei Gong, you flatter me. Ah Xuan! Come help me roast the deer!"
Li Xuanba had long since fished out a jar of barbecue sauce from the supply carriage: "Coming, coming."
*Finally, fresh meat to eat.* Li Xuanba had never looked forward to fresh meat so much.
Pei Shiju was on official business and kept to the main road, only able to supplement with rice and flour at the post stations. Fresh meat spoiled easily, so they had to boil dried meat into soup; they hadn't eaten fresh meat in a long time.
If Li Xuanba had a smartphone and could post on Weibo, he would definitely take pictures of his daily meals to sell his misery.
*Who would have thought? The young masters of the top-tier Tang State Duke’s manor couldn't even get a bite of fresh meat.*
No matter how poor Li Xuanba was, he had eaten boxed lunches with meat on the train in his past life.
Not to mention when he was a marketing editor, he ate meat every meal and even had to specifically eat vegetarian and chicken breast to lose weight.
He pinched his thin arms.
*I will never have the beautiful muscles of my past life in this one.*
He looked at Li Shimin’s arms, which were already solid at just ten years old.
Li Shimin knew what his brother was thinking the moment he saw his gaze, and immediately rolled his sleeves up to his shoulders, posing to show off his muscles.
Li Xuanba looked away.
*Why are the poses for showing off muscles the same from ancient times to now? No creativity, not sour at all.*
Li Shimin grinned, silently mocking Li Xuanba.

Pei Shiju also craved fresh meat.
He was worried Li Xuanba would waste the deer, but since it was Li Shimin’s kill, he couldn't just snatch it from the juniors.
Fortunately, Li Xuanba had self-awareness; he said he was roasting the deer, but in reality, he was directing the cook and only offering pointers.
Most game meat was tough and gamey. Li Xuanba’s barbecue sauce not only contained a large amount of spices, but the most important "secret recipe" was the oil.
The blended oil of soybeans and sesame originally had a slight plant-oil odor, but after being mixed with animal fat and a large amount of spices, the fragrance became very alluring.
The deer meat, brushed with plenty of oil, took on the texture of deep-fried meat on the surface.
While brushing the oil, Li Xuanba also had the cook continuously brush ginger and garlic water onto the scaled deer meat.
The oil sealed in the water, making the somewhat tough deer meat a bit more tender. *It’s a pity there’s no syringe. When roasting large game, injecting ginger, garlic, and salt water into the meat not only makes it more flavorful but also makes the meat tender.*
The favorite food of the Sui nobility was barbecue. Pei Shiju had eaten many delicious barbecues, but smelling the aroma of this deer meat, he couldn't help but salivate.
Pei Shiju came from the Hedong Pei clan, a top-tier clan that could rival the Langya Wang clan during the Wei and Jin dynasties. His clan produced many high officials, and he was currently a member of the Guanzhong nobility that monopolized the court. He had seen many good things.
He had originally looked down on the Tang State Duke’s manor, which had risen late.
Even among the Guanzhong nobility, there was a hierarchy; the Guanzhong clans viewed military nobles as "commoners" with shallow foundations.
The most delicious recipes were secret family formulas, and the best banquets were family feasts of the noble clans. In the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties, even the Emperor’s imperial chefs couldn't compare to the family chefs of the noble clans. The richness and deliciousness of the recipes were also a symbol of family heritage.
Pei Shiju thought the Tang State Duke’s manor certainly didn't have many secret recipes and planned to see if he could bump into hunters or farmers on the road to buy fresh meat, so he could let the two young masters of the Tang manor taste the ancestral barbecue recipe of the Hedong Pei clan and broaden their horizons.
After seeing the novel roasting technique of the Tang manor’s cook, Pei Shiju decided that if he bought fresh meat later, he wouldn't do the barbecue himself.
Before the meat even touched his lips, he knew from the smell that he couldn't compete.
Pei Shiju asked, "I heard Li Sanlang likes to restore ancient recipes. Is this a secret method from the Western Regions or an ancient recipe?"
Li Shimin bluffed without hesitation: "It’s an ancient recipe. When Zhang Qian went out of the frontier during the Han dynasty, he brought back sesame seeds that could be pressed into very fragrant oil. Using this fragrant oil to brush the meat while roasting makes it extremely delicious."
Li Xuanba glanced at his Second Brother from the corner of his eye.
*When did Second Brother develop the ability to casually invent an "origin"? Is this "creating history" or "altering history"? I must record this in my memoirs.*
Pei Shiju didn't doubt it and sighed, "So that’s it. I also have a heavy appetite; it seems I need to hunt for more fragments to see if I can find some interesting lost ancient recipes."

The deer was roasted.
As Pei Shiju expected, the crispy-outside-tender-inside texture was like eating farm-raised deer, and the blend of spices was exquisite. Pei Shiju couldn't stop praising it and immediately offered to trade a secret recipe for pastries and steamed dishes for the Tang manor’s barbecue recipe.
Although Li Xuanba and Li Shimin said they could give it for free, Pei Shiju had his accompanying cook make the pastries and steamed dishes for the next meal. Only after receiving Li Xuanba and Li Shimin’s praise did he take the barbecue recipe Li Xuanba had just written down.
After exchanging recipes, Pei Shiju’s relationship with Li Xuanba and Li Shimin became much closer.
He invited them to ride in his carriage, introduced them to Zhangye along the way, and volunteered to act as their temporary teacher to help them make up for their missing lessons.
On the road, he asked about the assignments given to them by Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, Xue Daoheng, Yu Shinan, and Zhangsun Sheng, and very enthusiastically supervised them in completing their homework at the post stations at night.
Li Shimin had dead-fish eyes: "Why is this person so annoying? Do I really respect him in the future?"
Li Xuanba nodded: "He is annoying, and you really do respect him."
Li Shimin went crazy, clutching his head: "Ahhhhh, it’s so tiring on the road, why do we still have to do homework! Is he annoying or what!"
Li Xuanba nodded: "Being fond of teaching is a disease; he even added extra homework for us."
The brothers swore together that if they had the chance in the future, they would give Pei Shiju a lot of "homework" to let him know the bitterness they were feeling now!
*So what if he’s over seventy when the Tang dynasty is established? Haven't you heard of being old but still vigorous!*
*Ahhhhh, why do we have to do homework when we’re so tired!*

In another room at the post station, Pei Shiju was burning the midnight oil to grade the two young men’s homework.
He stroked his beard and smiled while reading: "I thought they would be exhausted, but I didn't expect them to have the energy to finish their work. With such talent, no wonder Gao Gong and the others are fighting to take them as students. It’s a pity my seniority isn't enough..."
Pei Shiju thought of the prestige of Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Xue Daoheng, and regretted that he was too embarrassed to ask Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to take him as a master.
As for Yu Shinan, what kind of teacher is someone who only teaches calligraphy?
Pei Shiju ignored Zhangsun Sheng.
Zhangsun Sheng’s prestige in managing the Western Regions was second to none. If he taught Li Shimin and Li Xuanba these skills, Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Xue Daoheng wouldn't be able to say a word of dissatisfaction.
But Pei Shiju prided himself on being skilled in managing foreign affairs, so he viewed Zhangsun Sheng as a rival who was just lucky to have had the opportunity early, and he didn't want to boost the other’s morale.
Although he didn't want to boost the other’s morale, the fact that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were Zhangsun Sheng’s students couldn't be forgotten just by ignoring it.
While Pei Shiju was delighted by their talent, he also developed a competitive spirit. Although there was no name of master and apprentice, the Emperor had entrusted the two youths to him and told him to teach them well, so Pei Shiju openly acted as their teacher and began his teaching along the way.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, no matter how much they loved learning, wanted to go crazy.
*Ahhhhh, when will we reach Zhangye! We don't want to listen to lectures in the carriage! Pei Shiju’s lectures are boring, and the carriage is swaying, making us drowsy!*
Li Xuanba decided not to suffer with his Second Brother anymore. He immediately performed a "pale as paper" act, threw down his books, and got sick.
*I, Li Sanlang, am a famous weakling.*
Li Shimin immediately cried and stayed by his brother’s side every day to serve medicine.
Pei Shiju: "..." *Huh? I made them sick? This...*
The Tang manor’s accompanying physician couldn't help but complain: "The journey is already tiring, and you still made the young masters expend energy listening to lectures... *Sigh*, Pei Gong, I told you it was very inappropriate."
Li Xuanba: *Pretending to be at death’s door.*
Li Shimin: *Pretending to be anxious.*
Pei Shiju broke into a cold sweat.
*Terrible! I went too far! What if something happens to Li Erlang and Li Sanlang?!*
When Li Xuanba and Li Shimin saw Pei Shiju feeling guilty, they spoke to the physician, who announced that Li Xuanba had recovered and could continue the journey.
For the rest of the journey, Pei Shiju never mentioned their homework again. When they read books, he even urged them not to overwork themselves.
Li Xuanba and Li Shimin high-fived and took the small rooster they had just bought from a farmer to thank Physician Sun.
Sun Simiao stroked his beard and smiled: "You’re welcome."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第73章 开茶楼不为赚钱
chunks.chineseText:
第73章 开茶楼不为赚钱

=
　　孙思邈隐居太白山中， 离洛阳很远，是宇文弼骑马入山亲自请来的。
　　李玄霸还住在京城时，窦夫人就曾从太白山请来孙思邈给李玄霸诊治。
　　后来李玄霸拿着自己半吊子的医学常识和孙思邈打好了关系。他们一家已经习惯把孙思邈当做半个供奉。
　　不过这次李玄霸和李世民西行路途遥远， 所以李渊和窦夫人没想打扰孙思邈， 只派出了家中供奉的医师。
　　但高颎和宇文弼得知此事之后， 比李渊和窦夫人还急。薛道衡都很奇怪他们急什么，有御医还不够吗？
　　宇文弼因为李玄霸和他先天体弱的孙儿很相似而与李玄霸结了师徒缘分。孙儿病逝之后，宇文弼就完全把对孙儿的感情转移到李玄霸身上。再加上李玄霸成了他的孙女婿， 宇文弼就更加爱护李玄霸。
　　他听说太白山的孙医师对李玄霸的身体很了解，居然亲自入山请孙医师与李玄霸同行。
　　其实以孙思邈对李玄霸这位“小友”的偏爱，不需要多隆重的请求， 只需要李玄霸给他写信，他就会欣然前往。
　　现在宇文弼身为朝中声望极高的老臣， 居然亲自来请他， 让孙思邈颇有些受宠若惊。
　　他见到李玄霸后打趣道：“你那未来丈人，真是视你如己出。”
　　李玄霸毫不谦虚道：“我一直讨人喜欢。”
　　孙思邈拈须笑道：“你这表情学李二郎学得真像。”
　　李世民：“啊？”关我什么事？
　　孙思邈在唐朝是神医，但华夏文明没有断过代，现代中医不可能比一千年差。
　　李玄霸刚结识孙思邈的时候，有种“就这？”的疑惑。他怎么觉得还不如公司楼下每天挂满号的老中医医术好。
　　后来他回过神， 如果一千年后的中医还比不过孙思邈，那中医才太悲哀了。
　　孙思邈的医学知识是超前的， 但史书中一些较为玄幻的记载，什么医龙医虎都是不存在的。
　　史书中对孙思邈的记载较为真实。
　　他治不了长孙皇后的气疾，只能外出避祸；面对挚友卢照邻的风疾也无能为力， 卢照邻不堪病痛四十岁投水自尽。
　　孙思邈对自己医术的评价， 连别人叫他“神医”都会摇头， 只说自己算得上良医而已。
　　孙思邈早就发现许多病只要得了就没法治。他更提倡养生， 把病解决在萌发前。
　　但这世上有多少人能坚持良好的生活作息和饮食习惯？孙思邈自己能当百岁老人，但他给权贵当供奉医师，权贵不一定活得到五十。
　　所以孙思邈对生活自律，又有超常医术见解的李玄霸很喜爱。
　　李玄霸在路上请他配合“装病”，孙思邈欣然同意。
　　在孙思邈看来，李世民和李玄霸这不是偷懒。裴公逼得两个旅途劳累的孩童读书耗费精力，才叫不可理喻。
　　在孙思邈的掩护下，李世民和李玄霸轻松到达张掖，中途没有生病。
　　裴世矩住进官邸后，给李世民和李玄霸腾了一个大院子居住。
　　身为河东裴氏，裴世矩在享受上分外不含糊。
　　裴世矩原本就在张掖监督互市，早早在张掖置办好了宅院。宅院中堆山挖池栽树，与京城和洛阳的贵族府邸没有区别，丝毫看不出处于较为干旱的西域边塞。
　　李世民和李玄霸虽然自己带了被褥衣服用具，裴世矩也给李世民和李玄霸送了一套全新的家用品。这些家用品皆是上等丝绸毛皮。特别是毛皮，其质量在京城和洛阳都算罕见。
　　裴世矩笑道：“张掖这里的物品稀缺和东都不同。凡是西域所出的东西都很便宜，若你们想要江南的特产，那才金贵。所以这些毛皮算不上什么。”
　　李世民和李玄霸谢过裴世矩的照顾，毫不客气地用裴世矩送的东西把小窝布置得舒舒服服，并把孙思邈所住的屋子装饰都包揽了。
　　到达张掖后，李世民和李玄霸先在家中休息了三日，待路途的劳累消散后，就拉着孙思邈一同去市集淘货。
　　裴世矩没有给两人安排功课，只让他们自己学习，若有不懂的再问他。
　　虽然皇帝说让裴世矩教导两个孩子，但李世民和李玄霸年幼，出了路途中李玄霸病倒的事，裴世矩不敢再主动给两人增加负担，只当哄着两个小辈来张掖玩耍了。
　　西域的珍奇草药很多，孙思邈逛得很开心。
　　孙思邈不缺钱，有看上的或者不认识的草药就直接买了，比李世民和李玄霸看上去还阔气。
　　李世民摸了摸腰包：“是不是在场就我最穷？”
　　李玄霸点头：“没错，就……啊！把我的钱包还给我！”
　　李世民抢了李玄霸的钱包塞自己怀里，道：“你的钱就是我的钱。现在我不是最穷了。”
　　李玄霸骂道：“强盗！”
　　李世民笑道：“听说市集小偷不少。就阿玄你那小身板，别人抢了你的钱袋你能追得上？钱还是我管吧。走，你想买什么，哥哥给你买！哥哥可慷慨了！”
　　李世民迈着六亲不认的八字步大摇大摆逛市集。
　　李玄霸骂骂咧咧。你拿我的钱慷慨，你还有脸了！谁需要我们追小偷，护卫是白养的吗！
　　李玄霸新招聘的护卫陈铁牛憨憨道：“三郎君，需要仆帮你抢回来吗？”
　　李世民回头：“这么嚣张？来，试试看抢不抢得到。”
　　陈铁牛还真做出一副要抢东西的动作。
　　李玄霸赶紧阻止：“不用不用。在大街上打闹什么？别挡了别人的生意。”
　　陈铁牛是洛阳别庄铁匠的儿子。他力气很大，又学了些擒拿本事，武艺还算优秀，就是那脑子，有点过于憨直。
　　陈铁牛不认为自己憨直，他只是忠诚。
　　他的主人是李三郎君，所以李二郎君欺负主人，他也该站出来保护主人，怎么能叫憨直？
　　李玄霸试图教导陈铁牛，李世民却在一旁鼓掌叫好，说就该这样。
　　李玄霸见越发憨直的陈铁牛，心想这护卫没救了，看来将来只能给自己当一辈子护卫了。
　　李世民和李玄霸一路吵闹，孙思邈一边搜寻市集上的西域草药，一边用眼角余光看两个孩子顽皮。
　　孙思邈隐居的长白山就在大兴城附近，所以常为勋贵看病。
　　他说是隐居，只是想找个清净的地方编书。但要钻研医术很花钱，且不常常给人看病，医术会退步，所以他没有离开繁华之地太远。
　　孙思邈是第一个将“儿科”单独论述的医者，很擅长给小儿治病，见过的勋贵孩童不少。
　　见过许多勋贵孩童后，孙思邈对李世民、李玄霸更加偏爱。
　　看着他们兄弟打闹，他心情就很好，仿佛这两人是他顽皮的孙儿似的。
　　打闹一会儿后，李世民和李玄霸也找到了自己想买的东西。
　　李世民对骏马宝刀特别感兴趣，李玄霸对贵的东西感兴趣。
　　李世民什么都想买，李玄霸只问价不买。
　　后来李玄霸带来的钱全被李世民花了，李玄霸只为亲人和老师、未婚妻买了礼物。
　　李世民见自己花了太多钱，脸皮再厚也有点不好意思：“我给你打欠条，回去还你！”
　　李玄霸道：“我们俩得到的零花钱和赏赐都被我用来做生意，我赚得的钱你本来就可以随意取用，算什么借？若你觉得我赚钱辛苦，我现在有在张掖赚钱的计划，你来帮我，别叫苦。”
　　李世民道：“赚钱？我们不是来张掖向裴公学习经略西域吗？”
　　李玄霸问道：“你知道裴公是如何向陛下献策的吗？”
　　李世民叹气：“阿玄，你能不能直接说事情，别在说正事前还要先弄个前提反问什么的，啰嗦。”
　　李玄霸：“……”有时候二哥真的很气人。
　　李玄霸懒得和二哥一般见识，道：“裴公的献策，皆是从西域商人口中打听的西域情况。”
　　李世民摸了摸下巴：“这样啊。我们借由做生意，也和西域商人打探消息。等整合消息后，再给裴公看？”
　　李玄霸道：“顺便大赚一笔。”
　　李世民劝道：“阿玄，不要太重金钱俗物，会移了性情。”
　　李玄霸伸手：“行，现在就还钱。以后你也别耗费金钱俗物去买马。你知道马多贵吗？我们买一匹马，能在这张掖置办个宅院！”
　　战马就是豪车，一辆车就是二线城市一套房知道吗！
　　李世民改口：“我的意思是，不要太重，但也不能不重。”
　　李玄霸：“呵呵。”
　　李世民干咳一声，道：“说吧，怎么赚钱，哥哥随你使唤！”
　　李玄霸早就想好了卖什么。
　　要打探情报，还有比茶楼更方便和合适的地方吗？
　　虽然他也可以开食肆，但食肆非常累，不如茶楼一把茶叶一壶水就能营业方便。
　　李玄霸当即盘下一座饮子铺，直接取名“茶楼”，让茶楼早出现几百年。
　　他打着“中原文人雅士喝的茶”的招牌，将这座名为“茶楼”的饮子铺中招牌饮子设置为自己带来的散茶。
　　散茶经过和不同花朵共同烘焙，不仅分红绿茶，还分不同香型，每种都是限量发售。
　　李玄霸又在茶楼中挂上了孙思邈的简介，以孙思邈的名义卖滋补药汤，仍旧是限量发售。
　　其他普通饮子则是不限量发售。
　　除了茶水和饮子，李玄霸还做出扑克、麻将，与各类棋一同在饮子铺售卖或者租借。
　　在开业之初，李玄霸举办了扑克和麻将大赛，教导来客如何打扑克和麻将，设立丰厚的奖金。
　　有钱拿，客人立刻云集。
　　裴世矩虽然没有给李世民和李玄霸安排功课，但一直都关注着李世民和李玄霸所做的事。
　　见李世民和李玄霸来到张掖的第一件事居然是盘下铺子做生意，裴世矩有点失望。
　　名门世家就没有看得起做生意的。他们虽然爱享受，但都说金钱是俗物。
　　李世民和李玄霸两人是唐国公府的郎君，且有官职在身，怎么来了张掖尽折腾赚钱的俗事？即使他们是让奴仆出面置办铺子，太爱做生意也不是什么好事。
　　裴世矩准备等空下来之后就劝告李世民和李玄霸一二。
　　茶楼开张三日后，李世民和李玄霸各抱着一堆纸来找裴世矩。
　　李世民道：“裴公，这是我和阿玄从茶楼搜集的吐谷浑和突厥最新消息。裴公看看是否有用？”
　　李玄霸道：“我着重统计了一下西域商人口中的吐谷浑各部落军队和马匹。差异有些大，我做成了图标，取中位数。”
　　裴世矩：“……什么消息？你们不是在开茶楼赚钱吗？”
　　李世民严肃道：“我和阿玄是开茶楼搜集消息，不赚钱。”
　　李玄霸道：“嗯，不赚钱。”
　　赚了很多很多钱。西域商人的钱真多啊。
　　裴世矩从惊讶中回过神：“你们开茶楼，只是为了搜集消息？”
　　李世民和李玄霸还没回答，裴世矩笑道：“对啊，饮子铺众商云集。他们喝饮子时难免会聊天，是个收集消息的好地方。在饮子铺收集消息，比主动询问，或许准确度更高。”
　　裴世矩把李世民和李玄霸送来的纸张铺开。
　　李世民带来的是给予数据的分析策论，李玄霸则是以数据和图表为主，两人风格有很大区别。
　　裴世矩首先被李玄霸一手漂亮的图表吸引了。
　　裴世矩指着图表上的符号道：“这是你创造的数字符号？”
　　李玄霸道：“我是从残本中学到的。”
　　裴世矩道：“很有意思。”
　　他看了一会儿，又指着饼状图、柱状图和线形图道：“这个图一画，看上去就很直观了。你和陛下写奏章也常用这样的图吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“是。”
　　裴世矩在心中叹了口气。不愧是名满天下的李秀才，光是这手图表就可能看出他处理政事的本事。
　　能将繁杂的数字变得一目了然，赏心悦目，陛下能不爱吗？
　　裴世矩粗略扫了几眼李玄霸带来的数据，又拿起李世民写的厚厚的分析。
　　才刚看几段，裴世矩就拍桌叫好：“李二郎，你居然能从西域商人透露的部落军队数量分布，直接看出他们内部的矛盾冲突，还预测出该如何出击？这是高公教你的本事吗？”
　　李世民刚想说“这是我自己的本事”，在李玄霸瞥了他一眼后，改口道：“是高公教的。”
　　委屈，不相信是我自己厉害吗？
　　裴世矩道：“你们一定很劳累，先休息吧。我细看之后再来寻你们。”
　　李世民和李玄霸拱手：“是，裴公。”
　　目送两人离去后，裴世矩长吁短叹许久。
　　伺候的人好奇道：“主人为何叹气？”
　　裴世矩指着桌上道：“不过羡慕唐国公而已。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 73: Opening a Teahouse, Not for Profit

Sun Simiao lived in seclusion deep within the Taibai Mountains, far from Luoyang. It was Yuwen Bi who had personally ridden into the mountains to invite him.

When Li Xuanba still resided in the capital, Lady Dou had once invited Sun Simiao from the Taibai Mountains to treat him.

Later, Li Xuanba used his own half-baked medical knowledge to strike up a friendship with Sun Simiao. Their family had long since grown accustomed to treating Sun Simiao as a semi-official household physician.

However, because the journey west for Li Xuanba and Li Shimin was so arduous, Li Yuan and Lady Dou had not wanted to disturb Sun Simiao, sending only the family’s retained physicians instead.

But when Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi heard of this, they were even more anxious than Li Yuan and Lady Dou. Xue Daoheng found it strange—was having imperial physicians not enough?

Yuwen Bi had formed a mentor-disciple bond with Li Xuanba because the boy reminded him so much of his own grandson, who had been born with a weak constitution. After his grandson passed away, Yuwen Bi transferred all his affection onto Li Xuanba. Furthermore, with Li Xuanba becoming his granddaughter’s fiancé, Yuwen Bi cherished him all the more.

Hearing that the physician from the Taibai Mountains knew Li Xuanba’s body best, he had personally entered the mountains to invite Sun Simiao to accompany the boys.

In truth, given Sun Simiao’s partiality toward his "little friend" Li Xuanba, he didn't need such a grand invitation. Had Li Xuanba simply written to him, he would have gladly set out.

Now, with Yuwen Bi, a high-ranking and prestigious official in the imperial court, coming to invite him in person, Sun Simiao felt quite flattered.

Upon seeing Li Xuanba, he teased, "That future father-in-law of yours truly treats you like his own flesh and blood."

Li Xuanba replied without a hint of modesty, "I have always been likable."

Sun Simiao stroked his beard and laughed, "The way you say that, you look just like Li Erlang."

Li Shimin: "Huh?" What does that have to do with me?

In the Tang Dynasty, Sun Simiao was a divine physician, but since the continuity of Chinese civilization had never been broken, modern Traditional Chinese Medicine could not possibly be inferior to that of a thousand years ago.

When Li Xuanba first met Sun Simiao, he had felt a sense of doubt: "Is that it?" He couldn't help but feel that the physician's skills were not as good as the old TCM practitioner who had a full schedule of appointments every day downstairs from his company.

Later, he came to his senses: if TCM a thousand years later couldn't surpass Sun Simiao, then TCM would be truly pathetic.

Sun Simiao’s medical knowledge was ahead of its time, but the more fantastical records in historical texts—tales of him healing dragons or tigers—were non-existent.

The historical records regarding Sun Simiao were relatively grounded.

He could not cure Empress Zhangsun’s asthma, and could only leave to avoid trouble; he was also powerless against the gout of his close friend Lu Zhaolin, who, unable to bear the pain, drowned himself at the age of forty.

Sun Simiao was modest about his own medical skills; even when others called him a "Divine Physician," he would shake his head, claiming only to be a "good physician."

Sun Simiao had long realized that many diseases were incurable once contracted. He advocated for health preservation, solving problems before they manifested.

But how many people in this world could maintain good living habits and a healthy diet? Sun Simiao himself could live to be a centenarian, but the aristocrats he served as a physician often didn't live to see fifty.

Thus, Sun Simiao was very fond of Li Xuanba, who was disciplined in his life and possessed extraordinary medical insights.

When Li Xuanba asked him to help "feign illness" on the road, Sun Simiao readily agreed.

In Sun Simiao’s view, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were not being lazy. It was Pei Ju who was unreasonable, forcing two exhausted children to study and drain their energy.

Under Sun Simiao’s cover, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba arrived in Zhangye with ease, without falling ill along the way.

After Pei Ju moved into the official residence, he cleared out a large courtyard for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to live in.

As a member of the Hedong Pei clan, Pei Ju was not one to compromise on his comforts.

Pei Ju had been in Zhangye for some time supervising the border markets and had long since established a residence there. He had built artificial hills, dug ponds, and planted trees within the compound, making it indistinguishable from the noble mansions in the capital or Luoyang, showing no signs of being in the arid Western Regions.

Although Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had brought their own bedding, clothes, and utensils, Pei Ju also sent them a set of brand-new household items. These were all made of top-quality silk and fur. The quality of the furs, in particular, was rare even in the capital and Luoyang.

Pei Ju smiled and said, "Goods here in Zhangye are different from the Eastern Capital. Anything produced in the Western Regions is very cheap; it is the specialties from the Jiangnan region that are precious. So, these furs are nothing."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba thanked Pei Ju for his care and, without standing on ceremony, used the items to decorate their little nest comfortably, even taking charge of decorating the room where Sun Simiao stayed.

After arriving in Zhangye, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba rested at home for three days. Once the fatigue of the journey dissipated, they dragged Sun Simiao along to the market to hunt for goods.

Pei Ju had not assigned them any lessons, telling them only to study on their own and ask him if they had any questions.

Although the Emperor had instructed Pei Ju to tutor the two children, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were still young, and after Li Xuanba had fallen ill on the road, Pei Ju did not dare to burden them further, treating their stay in Zhangye as if they were just two juniors coming to play.

The Western Regions were full of rare medicinal herbs, and Sun Simiao wandered the market happily.

Sun Simiao was not short of money; he bought whatever herbs he took a fancy to or didn't recognize, appearing even more generous than Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Li Shimin patted his purse: "Am I the poorest person here?"

Li Xuanba nodded: "That’s right, just—ah! Give my wallet back!"

Li Shimin snatched Li Xuanba’s wallet and tucked it into his own robe, saying, "Your money is my money. Now I’m not the poorest."

Li Xuanba cursed: "Robber!"

Li Shimin laughed: "I heard there are many thieves in the market. With your frail build, Ah Xuan, could you catch them if they snatched your purse? Better let me handle the money. Come, what do you want to buy? Big Brother will buy it for you! Big Brother is very generous!"

Li Shimin strutted through the market with a swaggering, arrogant gait.

Li Xuanba grumbled. You’re being generous with my money, and you have the nerve to say that! Who needs us to chase thieves? Are the guards we hired just for show?

Li Xuanba’s newly hired guard, Chen Tieniu, said naively, "Third Young Master, do you need me to snatch it back for you?"

Li Shimin looked back: "So arrogant? Come on, try it and see if you can snatch it."

Chen Tieniu actually made a move as if to grab something.

Li Xuanba quickly stopped him: "No, no. Why are you making a scene in the street? Don't block other people's business."

Chen Tieniu was the son of a blacksmith from the Li family’s villa in Luoyang. He was very strong and had learned some grappling techniques; his martial arts were quite good, but his brain was a bit too simple and honest.

Chen Tieniu didn't think he was simple; he just thought he was loyal.

His master was the Third Young Master, so if the Second Young Master bullied his master, he should stand up and protect him. How could that be called simple?

Li Xuanba tried to lecture Chen Tieniu, but Li Shimin clapped and cheered from the side, saying that was exactly how he should be.

Seeing the increasingly simple-minded Chen Tieniu, Li Xuanba thought that this guard was beyond saving; it seemed he would only be able to serve as his bodyguard for the rest of his life.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba bickered all the way, while Sun Simiao searched for Western Region herbs in the market, watching the two naughty children out of the corner of his eye.

Sun Simiao’s place of seclusion in the Changbai Mountains was near Daxing City, so he often treated the nobility.

He called it seclusion, but he just wanted a quiet place to compile his books. However, researching medicine was expensive, and if he didn't see patients often, his skills would regress, so he didn't stay too far from the bustling areas.

Sun Simiao was the first physician to discuss "pediatrics" as a separate field; he was very skilled at treating children and had seen many noble children.

After seeing so many noble children, Sun Simiao grew even more fond of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Watching the brothers bicker, he felt very happy, as if they were his own naughty grandsons.

After playing for a while, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba found what they wanted to buy.

Li Shimin was particularly interested in fine horses and precious blades, while Li Xuanba was interested in expensive things.

Li Shimin wanted to buy everything, while Li Xuanba only asked for prices without buying.

Later, all the money Li Xuanba brought was spent by Li Shimin. Li Xuanba only bought gifts for his family, his teacher, and his fiancée.

Seeing that he had spent too much money, Li Shimin, thick-skinned as he was, felt a bit embarrassed: "I’ll write you an IOU and pay you back when we go back!"

Li Xuanba said, "The pocket money and rewards we both receive are used by me for business. You could have used the money I earned whenever you wanted, so why call it a loan? If you think I earn money with difficulty, I have a plan to make money in Zhangye now. Come help me, and don't complain."

Li Shimin said, "Make money? Aren't we here in Zhangye to learn from Pei Gong about managing the Western Regions?"

Li Xuanba asked, "Do you know how Pei Gong presents his strategies to His Majesty?"

Li Shimin sighed: "Ah Xuan, can you just get to the point? Don't ask a rhetorical question as a premise before talking about serious matters. It’s long-winded."

Li Xuanba: "..." Sometimes his Second Brother was truly infuriating.

Li Xuanba couldn't be bothered to argue with his Second Brother, saying, "Pei Gong’s strategies are all based on information he gathers from Western Region merchants."

Li Shimin stroked his chin: "I see. We can use the business as a cover to gather information from the Western Region merchants as well. After we consolidate the information, we can show it to Pei Gong?"

Li Xuanba said, "And make a fortune on the side."

Li Shimin advised, "Ah Xuan, don't be too obsessed with money and worldly goods; it will corrupt your character."

Li Xuanba held out his hand: "Fine, pay me back now. And don't spend money on horses in the future. Do you know how expensive horses are? If we buy one horse, we could buy a mansion here in Zhangye!"

Warhorses were like luxury cars; do you know that one car is worth an apartment in a second-tier city!

Li Shimin changed his tune: "I mean, don't be too obsessed, but you can't ignore it either."

Li Xuanba: "Heh."

Li Shimin coughed dryly and said, "Alright, tell me, how do we make money? Your big brother is at your service!"

Li Xuanba had already thought about what to sell.

To gather intelligence, what place could be more convenient and suitable than a teahouse?

Although he could open an eatery, eateries were exhausting; it was much more convenient to just have tea leaves and a pot of water to operate a teahouse.

Li Xuanba immediately rented a beverage shop and named it "Teahouse," bringing the concept of a teahouse into existence several hundred years early.

He used the signboard of "Tea drunk by the scholars of the Central Plains" and set the signature drink of this "Teahouse" to be the loose-leaf tea he had brought with him.

The loose-leaf tea was roasted with different flowers, not only divided into red and green teas but also into different scents, each sold in limited quantities.

Li Xuanba also hung a brief biography of Sun Simiao in the teahouse, selling nourishing medicinal soups in Sun Simiao’s name, also in limited quantities.

Other common drinks were sold without limits.

In addition to tea and drinks, Li Xuanba also made playing cards and mahjong, selling or renting them out alongside various board games.

At the beginning of the opening, Li Xuanba held poker and mahjong tournaments, teaching guests how to play and setting up generous prizes.

With money to be won, customers flocked in immediately.

Although Pei Ju had not assigned any lessons to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, he had been keeping a close eye on what they were doing.

Seeing that the first thing Li Shimin and Li Xuanba did upon arriving in Zhangye was to rent a shop and do business, Pei Ju was a little disappointed.

The great noble families never looked kindly upon doing business. Although they loved to enjoy themselves, they all claimed that money was a worldly, vulgar thing.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were young masters of the Tang Duke’s mansion and held official positions; why were they wasting their time on the vulgar business of making money in Zhangye? Even if they had servants handle the shop, being too fond of business was not a good thing.

Pei Ju prepared to advise Li Shimin and Li Xuanba once he had some free time.

Three days after the teahouse opened, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba each brought a stack of papers to find Pei Ju.

Li Shimin said, "Pei Gong, this is the latest news on the Tuyuhun and the Turks that Ah Xuan and I gathered from the teahouse. Please see if it is of any use, Pei Gong?"

Li Xuanba said, "I focused on calculating the armies and horses of the various Tuyuhun tribes as reported by the Western Region merchants. There were some discrepancies, so I created charts and took the median values."

Pei Ju: "...What news? Aren't you busy running a teahouse to make money?"

Li Shimin said solemnly, "Ah Xuan and I opened the teahouse to gather information, not to make money."

Li Xuanba said, "Yes, not to make money."

They had made a lot, a lot of money. The Western Region merchants really had a lot of money.

Pei Ju recovered from his surprise: "You opened a teahouse just to gather information?"

Before Li Shimin and Li Xuanba could answer, Pei Ju smiled and said, "Right, a beverage shop is a gathering place for merchants. They inevitably chat while drinking, making it a good place to collect information. Collecting information in a beverage shop might be more accurate than asking directly."

Pei Ju spread out the papers sent by Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

What Li Shimin brought was an analytical strategy based on data, while Li Xuanba’s was dominated by data and charts; the two had very different styles.

Pei Ju was first attracted by Li Xuanba’s beautiful charts.

Pei Ju pointed to the symbols on the charts: "Are these numerical symbols you created?"

Li Xuanba said, "I learned them from an ancient fragment."

Pei Ju said, "Very interesting."

He looked for a while, then pointed to the pie charts, bar charts, and line graphs: "Once this chart is drawn, it looks very intuitive. Do you often use such charts when writing memorials to His Majesty?"

Li Xuanba said, "Yes."

Pei Ju sighed in his heart. As expected of the world-renowned "Scholar Li," just from these charts, one could see his ability to handle government affairs.

Being able to make complex numbers clear at a glance and pleasing to the eye—how could His Majesty not love it?

Pei Ju scanned the data Li Xuanba brought a few times, then picked up the thick analysis written by Li Shimin.

After reading only a few paragraphs, Pei Ju slapped the table and praised: "Li Erlang, you were actually able to see the internal conflicts of the tribes directly from the distribution of the army numbers revealed by the Western Region merchants, and even predicted how to strike? Is this the skill Gao Gong taught you?"

Li Shimin was just about to say, "This is my own ability," but after Li Xuanba glanced at him, he changed his words: "It is what Gao Gong taught me."

So aggrieved. Don't you believe I'm capable on my own?

Pei Ju said, "You must be very tired, rest first. I will come to find you after I have studied these in detail."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba bowed: "Yes, Pei Gong."

Watching the two leave, Pei Ju sighed long and hard for a long time.

The attendant serving him asked curiously, "Why does Master sigh?"

Pei Ju pointed to the table: "Just envying the Duke of Tang, that is all."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第74章 吐谷浑一触即溃
chunks.chineseText:
第74章 吐谷浑一触即溃

=
　　李世民和李玄霸令裴世矩震惊的本事， 已经是收敛后的了。
　　除了李世民有一点浅显的战略分析之外，两人几乎是纯粹陈列数据。
　　但这一手整理数据的本事，也让裴世矩足够惊讶。
　　李世民对李玄霸小声道：“你非让我说是高老师教的。若高老师看到你我写的东西， 肯定会劈头劈脸把我们骂一顿， 让我们重写。”
　　李世民说罢， 还摇头晃脑学高颎说话：“驴鸣狗吠，蛙鸣蝉噪，纯纯聒耳！”
　　李玄霸忍笑：“虽然高老师确实这么骂过你我， 但这次也没差到那地步。”
　　李世民抱着手臂，小脑袋一点一点：“不是差，是敷衍。真的水平不行， 高老师倒不会骂人，只会悉心教导。高老师最厌恶的就是敷衍。”
　　李玄霸道：“这倒是。不过老师会理解我们藏拙。”
　　李世民叹气：“要是我现在已经十五六岁， 我就不藏拙了。我一篇行军策论惊艳陛下， 弱冠之年就当上冠军侯！”
　　李玄霸道：“你二十岁就永远当不了冠军侯了。”
　　李世民瞠目结舌：“啊？这么早啊？”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　李世民本来不想问的，但没想到会这么早。
　　他把着李玄霸的肩膀，贼兮兮道：“来，阿玄，悄悄和哥说， 我们究竟多少岁……嗯，你明白的。”
　　李玄霸：【你十八岁造反， 十九岁当秦王。】
　　李世民不敢置信：“秦……秦什么？为什么是秦？”
　　他委屈极了。
　　李玄霸疑惑：【秦王不好吗？】
　　李世民瘪嘴：“哪里好？残暴不仁，二世而亡。”
　　李玄霸愣了一会儿，才想到一件事。秦始皇的风评是在近现代才变好。此时秦始皇是暴君的代名词， 连明清立帝庙时都没得贡品吃， 被列为“无道被弑、亡国之主”。
　　历史中唐太宗就非常不喜欢秦， 时常以秦始皇和秦二世事迹自省。
　　李玄霸劝说道：“封爵是以周时诸侯国强盛程度来定封号， ‘秦晋’是第一等的封号。”
　　李世民道：“我可以当晋王！以前当秦王的人都没有好下场！”
　　李玄霸：“啊？我查查。”
　　李玄霸借了裴世矩的书房查了查史书：【魏晋时的秦王都英年早逝，但南北朝时秦王都不错，还有称帝的。】
　　李世民抱着手臂道：“我就不喜欢。”
　　李玄霸：【你可以喜欢，后世对秦始皇的评价很高。再者，你是把“秦”这个称号再次带上巅峰的人。后世也还有很多秦王，但说起秦王，都只会想到秦王嬴政和秦王李世民。如果你不当秦王了，后世就会少一个你穿越回去给秦始皇当儿子的梗，那多无趣。】
　　李世民瞠目结舌，再次被后世人的荒诞震惊。
　　为什么我要去给秦始皇当儿子啊！我才不要给秦始皇当儿子！
　　李世民主动询问剧透，然后被李玄霸的剧透气跑了，半日不理睬李玄霸。
　　半日后，李世民找到李玄霸主动和好：“以后我们和父亲说，我们称号换一换好不好？”
　　李玄霸道：“不换，滚。”李世民怎么能不当秦王呢？
　　李世民气鼓鼓地瞪了弟弟一眼，然后叹气认命。
　　秦王就秦王吧，我要以一己之力扭转“秦王”的印象，握拳！
　　裴世矩备课一日，根据李世民和李玄霸送来的资料数据，结合自己对西域的了解，重新恢复给李世民和李玄霸上课。
　　他担心李世民和李玄霸的身体，本想不给二人增加太多功课负担。但见二人自己都如此努力，裴世矩也不好敷衍了。
　　何况他真的见才心喜。
　　没有旅途劳顿，李世民和李玄霸也能应对裴世矩的授课。
　　经营茶楼和收集情报都有下人张罗，李世民和李玄霸只需要每旬看一眼收集的情报和茶楼的账本，其他时间都跟随裴世矩左右学习。
　　裴世矩授课的本事虽不如李世民和李玄霸其他老师，但他因喜爱李世民和李玄霸的本事，出外公务的时候也将李世民和李玄霸带在身边。两人如同文吏一般帮裴世矩处理政务，受益匪浅。
　　因每日都只有学习和公务，兄弟二人的时间过得飞快。
　　八月，裴世矩为在大隋攻打吐谷浑前削弱吐谷浑，游说铁勒部族攻击吐谷浑，铁勒同意出兵。
　　李世民和李玄霸当面学习了裴世矩谈判的本事。
　　两人在被窝里小声聊天。
　　李世民：“裴公游说的本事还是不错，当个使臣很合格。”
　　李玄霸：“但他不该游说铁勒部落对吧？”
　　李世民叹气：“是啊。裴公的战略眼光不如高老师和丈人。”
　　李玄霸恶意揣度：“也可能他知道，但不在乎。讨好陛下才最重要。”
　　李世民劝说道：“阿玄，裴公对我们很好，不要带着恶意评价别人，这样不好，你要心态阳光些。”
　　李玄霸：“哦。那就是他没用。”
　　李世民无语：“口下留情。”
　　李玄霸不是恶意评价裴世矩。
　　铁勒部族原本是西突厥的一支。
　　隋文帝仁寿三年，长孙晟经略西域，蛰伏多年后图穷匕见，突厥各部分裂，经过突厥内部血腥政权更替后，东西突厥都向隋文帝称番。其中铁勒十余部在长孙晟的离间计下，背叛当时不服从大隋的达头可汗，归附大隋扶持的启民可汗。
　　所以铁勒部族的军队名义上也是大隋的军队。裴世矩的举措看似没错。
　　但吐谷浑不堪一击，大隋现在政治鼎盛。不需要铁勒部族出兵，大隋也能轻易获胜。
　　既然都要打仗了，就要计较收益。
　　铁勒部族名义上归附大隋，但实际上是突厥。若铁勒部族先攻打吐谷浑，以他们的性格，肯定不会出大力气打歼灭战，只会掠夺一番就跑。
　　别说李世民能看出来，李玄霸这个没有打仗天赋的人得到了高颎的教导都能看出来，对草原部落的灭国之战你不打歼灭战，就是等着别人卷土重来。
　　铁勒部族看似消耗了吐谷浑的国力，实际上是打草惊蛇，让吐谷浑主力提前逃跑。
　　而且突厥不会永远臣服大隋。
　　大隋要借突厥的兵，该是两军同行，土地人口归大隋，财物分给突厥一半。
　　若突厥比大隋先出兵，突厥大胜，肯定会占领吐谷浑与突厥接壤的水草丰茂之地，掠夺吐谷浑大量人口。
　　大隋再出兵，就算此战获胜，不仅少许多地，人口减少后开发吐谷浑也会十分困难。
　　攻打吐谷浑的目的是吞下并消化吐谷浑，不是仅得一个大胜的名义啊！
　　李世民和李玄霸都觉得裴世矩此举不妥。但他们只是孩子，裴世矩此举肯定也先禀报过皇帝，他们只能在被窝里嘀咕几句。
　　李世民：“希望铁勒和吐谷浑两败俱伤，陷入僵持。”
　　李玄霸：“我宁愿铁勒战败，也不希望铁勒大胜吐谷浑。”
　　两个孩子祈祷。
　　不到半月，战报传来，李世民和李玄霸祈祷失败。
　　铁勒一战轻松大胜吐谷浑，吐谷浑可汗伏允东逃至西平境内。
　　李世民抱头：“铁勒至少能吃下吐谷浑一半领土吧？”
　　李玄霸道：“还有大半吐谷浑人口。”
　　李世民自我安慰：“吐谷浑可汗伏允不是向大隋请降了吗？降了就好。降了大隋就不用出兵了，白捡剩下的城池和人口，不算输！”
　　李玄霸戳破二哥的幻想：“裴公游说铁勒不是偷偷去的。现在吐谷浑可汗可能被打得猝不及防，还不知道是大隋派裴公游说铁勒攻打吐谷浑。陛下派使臣来迎接吐谷浑可汗，至少需要一旬时间。这一旬时间，吐谷浑可汗一定能打听到是大隋先动的手。”
　　李世民苦着脸道：“等他打探到，就不会投降了？”
　　李玄霸道：“即使他想投降，他手下那些失去了土地、牛羊、牧民的部落贵族也会仇恨大隋，不愿臣服。”
　　李世民叹气：“希望不会。虽然我认为阿玄你说得对。”
　　这次李世民和李玄霸的乌鸦嘴应验。
　　吐谷浑贵族果然不愿意投降大隋，吐谷浑可汗只能带兵西逃。
　　杨广派去的使臣宇文述摇身一变，披甲上阵，引兵追杀，俘获吐谷浑贵族二百人，百姓四千人而归。吐谷浑可汗据守覆袁川。大隋得到了吐谷浑大部分土地。
　　李世民：“但没人。”
　　李玄霸：“吐谷浑大贵族也差不多全逃走了，想要统治当地十分困难。”
　　李世民自我安慰道：“陛下看上去并不想停止兵戈，正在调集大军准备斩草除根。若吐谷浑可汗伏允身死，吐谷浑就会土崩瓦解。”
　　李玄霸道：“前提是一鼓作气，不给吐谷浑大军休养的机会。现在吐谷浑大军虽吃了几场大败，但损失不多，还有一战之力。”
　　李世民笑道：“这个阿玄你就安心了。朝中那么多老将，陛下在当皇子时也曾随军出征，当然不会犯兵家大忌。你先别看你的天书，我们等消息！看我说的对不对。”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　好吧，暂时不搜索记忆，反正搜索了也没用。他记得隋炀帝攻打吐谷浑是大胜，让大隋达到了鼎盛，应该是二哥算对了。
　　不久之后，他们跟着裴世矩得到了皇帝密信。
　　皇帝说，吐谷浑可汗伏允不识好歹，朕一定要把吐谷浑彻底干掉，朕要御驾亲征把他干掉！
　　但是，朕现在脱不开身，要去恒山祭祀。等朕去完恒山祭祀，来到张掖就到秋冬了，太过寒冷。所以朕决定明年开春再御驾亲征，现在这件事就先搁一边明年再说。
　　裴卿啊，你现在的工作是多给朕叫些西域国家来恒山助祭。
　　李世民阿巴阿巴半晌，结结巴巴道：“现在才八月，许国公率领的大军就在此地，现在一鼓作气定能在飘雪之前拿下吐谷浑可汗啊！”
　　以吐谷浑这一触即溃的架势，说不定许国公打完刚好过重阳节！
　　裴世矩教导李世民道：“许国公大胜却不追击，定是早就得了陛下的旨意，要把吐谷浑可汗留给陛下御驾亲征。吐谷浑大势已去，不用再多操心了。接下来我教你们如何向各国致函。”
　　李世民焦急道：“可是吐谷浑已经溃败……”
　　裴世矩拍了拍李世民的肩膀：“陛下的意志最重要。吐谷浑既然已经没有反抗的力量，最后一击自然该由陛下来做，才能彰显陛下的威望。”
　　裴世矩看着天真的李世民，心想少年就是少年，少年才高，但人情世故还差得远。
　　李玄霸拉了拉二哥的袖子：“好了，裴公说得对。”
　　李玄霸：【明年也会获胜的，别担心。】
　　李世民抿着嘴唇，目光低垂。
　　明年大隋肯定能打赢吐谷浑。但本可以一击制胜，现在会多耗费了多少兵力钱粮？若耗费过多，胜得不彻底，吐谷浑这些土地真的能被大隋真正占领吗？
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 74: Tuyuhun Collapses at the First Blow

The abilities of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba that had so stunned Pei Shiju were, in fact, already severely toned down.

Apart from Li Shimin including a bit of rudimentary strategic analysis, the two of them had essentially done nothing more than compile and present raw data.

Yet this skill at organizing data was enough to leave Pei Shiju deeply astonished.

Li Shimin whispered to Li Xuanba, "You just had to insist on saying Teacher Gao taught us. If Teacher Gao saw what we wrote, he would have scolded us within an inch of our lives and made us rewrite it from scratch."

As he spoke, Li Shimin even bobbed his head back and forth, mimicking Gao Jiong's voice: "'The braying of donkeys and barking of dogs, the croaking of frogs and screeching of cicadas—pure and utter noise to the ears!'"

Suppressing a smile, Li Xuanba said, "Teacher Gao might have indeed scolded us like that before, but what we did this time wasn't nearly that terrible."

Li Shimin crossed his arms, his little head nodding rhythmically. "It's not that it was terrible—it was perfunctory. If our ability were genuinely lacking, Teacher Gao wouldn't scold us; he would patiently instruct us. What Teacher Gao despises most is half-hearted effort."

"That is true," Li Xuanba agreed. "Still, our teacher would understand why we're hiding our light under a bushel."

Li Shimin sighed. "If I were already fifteen or sixteen, I wouldn't hide a thing. A single military treatise from me would dazzle His Majesty, and by twenty, I'd already be named the Champion Marquis!"

Li Xuanba replied, "By twenty, you'll never be able to become the Champion Marquis."

Li Shimin's eyes went wide. "Huh? That early?"

Li Xuanba nodded.

Li Shimin hadn't intended to ask, but he never imagined it would happen so soon.

He slung an arm over Li Xuanba's shoulder, wearing a sly look. "Come on, Ah Xuan. Whisper it to your brother. Just how old will we be when... well, you know."

Li Xuanba: 【You rebel at eighteen and become the Prince of Qin at nineteen.】

Li Shimin stared in disbelief. "Prince of... Prince of what? Why Qin?"

A look of deep grievance washed over his face.

Li Xuanba was puzzled. 【Is the Prince of Qin bad?】

Li Shimin curled his lip. "What's good about it? Cruel and tyrannical, perishing after two generations."

Li Xuanba stared blankly for a moment before something dawned on him. The historical reputation of Qin Shi Huang—the First Emperor of Qin—had only been rehabilitated in the modern era. In this day and age, the First Emperor was synonymous with "tyrant." Even when imperial ancestral temples were established during the Ming and Qing dynasties, he wouldn't receive sacrificial offerings, cast aside among the "unprincipled, assassinated rulers who destroyed their own realms."

Historically, Emperor Taizong of Tang had thoroughly disliked Qin, frequently examining his own conduct through the cautionary tales of the First and Second Emperors of Qin.

Li Xuanba reasoned, "Peerage titles are determined by the might of the feudal states during the Zhou Dynasty. 'Qin' and 'Jin' are titles of the very highest rank."

Li Shimin countered, "I can be the Prince of Jin! None of the men who were crowned Prince of Qin in the past ever met a good end!"

Li Xuanba: "Huh? Let me check."

Borrowing Pei Shiju's study, Li Xuanba flipped through historical records: 【The Princes of Qin during the Wei and Jin dynasties all suffered untimely deaths, but during the Southern and Northern Dynasties, they fared rather well; some even declared themselves emperors.】

Li Shimin folded his arms stubbornly. "I still don't like it."

Li Xuanba: 【You can learn to like it. Future generations hold Qin Shi Huang in very high regard. Furthermore, you're the one who will lift the title 'Qin' to its peak once more. There will be many Princes of Qin in history, but whenever anyone mentions the title, they only ever think of Ying Zheng, Prince of Qin, and Li Shimin, Prince of Qin. If you don't become the Prince of Qin, future generations will miss out on the running gag of you transmigrating back to be Qin Shi Huang's son. How dull would that be?】

Li Shimin's jaw dropped, once again appalled by the sheer absurdity of future people.

*Why on earth would I want to be Qin Shi Huang's son?! I don't want to be Qin Shi Huang's son at all!*

Li Shimin had asked for spoilers on his own initiative, only to end up so enraged by Li Xuanba's revelations that he stormed off and ignored his brother for half a day.

Half a day later, Li Shimin sought out Li Xuanba to make peace: "How about we tell Father to swap our titles later on?"

Li Xuanba deadpanned, "No swapping. Piss off." How could Li Shimin not be the Prince of Qin?

Li Shimin glared indignantly at his younger brother, then sighed, resigning himself to fate.

*Fine, Prince of Qin it is. I'll single-handedly turn the reputation of 'Prince of Qin' around!* He clenched his fists in resolve.

***

Pei Shiju spent an entire day preparing his syllabus. Based on the data and materials provided by Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, combined with his own understanding of the Western Regions, he resumed teaching them.

He had originally worried about their health and intended not to burden them with excessive schoolwork. But seeing how diligently the two worked on their own, Pei Shiju felt embarrassed to offer anything less than his best.

Besides, he truly cherished their talent.

Without the weariness of travel, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba handled Pei Shiju's lectures with ease.

Running the teahouse and gathering intelligence were handled by their servants. The brothers only needed to review the compiled intelligence reports and the teahouse ledgers once every ten days. The rest of their time was spent by Pei Shiju's side, learning from him.

Although Pei Shiju's teaching ability wasn't quite on par with their other mentors, his fondness for their brilliance meant that whenever he went out on official business, he brought them along. The two assisted him with administrative affairs just like scribes, benefiting immensely from the hands-on experience.

Occupied daily by nothing but study and official duties, time flew by for the brothers.

In the eighth month, in an effort to weaken Tuyuhun before the Great Sui launched its assault, Pei Shiju persuaded the Tiele tribes to attack them. The Tiele agreed to deploy their troops.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba observed Pei Shiju's negotiation techniques firsthand.

Tucked under the covers that night, the two conversed in low whispers.

Li Shimin: "Duke Pei's persuasive skills are quite impressive. He's very qualified as an envoy."

Li Xuanba: "True, but he shouldn't have incited the Tiele tribes, should he?"

Li Shimin sighed. "Indeed. Duke Pei's strategic vision falls short of Teacher Gao's and my father-in-law's."

Li Xuanba offered a cynical take: "Or perhaps he knows, but simply doesn't care. Pleasing His Majesty is all that matters."

Li Shimin admonished gently, "Ah Xuan, Duke Pei treats us very well. You shouldn't judge people with such malice. It's unhealthy; you need to maintain a brighter mindset."

Li Xuanba: "Oh. Then he's just useless."

Li Shimin was speechless. "Have some mercy with your tongue."

Li Xuanba wasn't merely judging Pei Shiju out of spite.

The Tiele tribes were originally a branch of the Western Turks.

In the third year of Emperor Wen's Renshou era, Zhangsun Sheng had managed affairs in the Western Regions. After biding his time for years, he finally revealed his hand, causing the Turkic factions to splinter. Following a bloody struggle for succession within the Turkic hierarchy, both the Eastern and Western Turks submitted to Emperor Wen as vassals. Among them, more than ten Tiele tribes, swayed by Zhangsun Sheng's discord strategy, betrayed Datou Qaghan—who refused to submit to the Sui—and aligned themselves with Qimin Qaghan, who was backed by the Sui.

Therefore, the army of the Tiele tribes was nominally also an army of the Great Sui. On the surface, Pei Shiju's move seemed sound.

However, Tuyuhun was weak, and the Great Sui was currently at the zenith of its power. Even without the Tiele deploying a single soldier, the Great Sui could easily achieve victory.

Since war was inevitable, one had to weigh the net gains.

Though nominally subservient to the Great Sui, the Tiele were Turks at heart. If the Tiele tribes struck Tuyuhun first, their nature dictated that they wouldn't exert themselves in a war of annihilation; they would simply pillage and run.

Let alone Li Shimin, even Li Xuanba—who lacked military talent but had been tutored by Gao Jiong—could see clearly that in a war aimed at destroying a nomadic state, failing to wage a campaign of total annihilation was merely inviting them to stage a comeback.

The Tiele attack might appear to drain Tuyuhun's national strength, but in truth, it was alarming the snake in the grass, allowing the main force of Tuyuhun to flee ahead of time.

Furthermore, the Turks would not remain subservient to the Great Sui forever.

If the Sui were to borrow Turkic troops, both armies should have advanced side by side, with the land and population going to the Sui, and the plunder split with the Turks.

If the Turks marched before the Sui and won a sweeping victory, they would inevitably seize the lush pastures bordering Tuyuhun and the Turkic lands, abducting vast numbers of Tuyuhun's population.

When the Sui finally launched their campaign, even if they emerged victorious, they would end up with significantly less territory. Moreover, with the drastically depleted population, developing Tuyuhun would become exceedingly difficult.

The whole point of attacking Tuyuhun was to swallow and digest it, not merely to claim the hollow glory of a grand victory!

Both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba felt that Pei Shiju's move was ill-advised. But they were only children, and Pei Shiju had undoubtedly reported this plan to the Emperor beforehand; they could do nothing more than grumble under the covers.

Li Shimin: "I hope the Tiele and Tuyuhun tear each other apart and end up in a stalemate."

Li Xuanba: "I'd rather the Tiele suffer a defeat than score an overwhelming victory over Tuyuhun."

The two boys prayed.

Less than half a month later, military dispatches arrived, proving their prayers completely futile.

The Tiele easily won a crushing victory over Tuyuhun in a single battle. Fuyun, the Tuyuhun Qaghan, fled eastward into the territory of Xiping.

Li Shimin clutched his head. "The Tiele will swallow at least half of Tuyuhun's territory, won't they?"

Li Xuanba added, "Along with the majority of Tuyuhun's population."

Li Shimin tried to console himself: "Didn't the Tuyuhun Qaghan, Fuyun, sue for surrender to the Great Sui? It's fine as long as he surrenders. If he yields, the Sui won't even need to send troops—we can scoop up the remaining cities and people for free. It wouldn't count as a loss!"

Li Xuanba punctured his brother's illusion: "Duke Pei didn't visit the Tiele in secret. Right now, the Tuyuhun Qaghan is probably reeling from the surprise attack and doesn't yet know it was the Sui who sent Duke Pei to instigate the Tiele. For His Majesty to send an envoy to accept the Qaghan's surrender will take at least ten days. In those ten days, the Qaghan will definitely discover that the Great Sui made the first move."

Li Shimin's face fell. "Once he finds out, he won't surrender?"

Li Xuanba said, "Even if he wants to surrender, the tribal nobles beneath him—having lost their lands, cattle, sheep, and herders—will harbor bitter hatred toward the Sui and refuse to submit."

Li Shimin sighed. "I hope not. Though I suspect you're right, Ah Xuan."

This time, the brothers' jinx came to pass once again.

The Tuyuhun nobility indeed refused to submit to the Great Sui, leaving the Qaghan no choice but to lead his forces in a retreat westward.

Yuwen Shu, the envoy sent by Yang Guang, donned his armor and took to the field, leading troops in hot pursuit. He captured two hundred Tuyuhun nobles and four thousand commoners before returning. The Tuyuhun Qaghan retreated to hold Fuyuanchuan. The Great Sui seized most of Tuyuhun's territory.

Li Shimin: "Yet there are no people."

Li Xuanba: "Nearly all the high-ranking Tuyuhun nobles escaped. Governing the region will be extraordinarily difficult."

Li Shimin tried to find a silver lining: "His Majesty doesn't seem inclined to stop the fighting. He is gathering a massive army to pull the weed out by its roots. If Fuyun, the Tuyuhun Qaghan, is slain, Tuyuhun will completely fall apart."

Li Xuanba said, "That hinges on striking while the iron is hot, giving the Tuyuhun army no chance to recuperate. Although they have suffered several defeats, their casualties haven't been catastrophic; they still have the strength left to fight."

Li Shimin chuckled. "On that front, you can rest easy, Ah Xuan. With so many veteran generals at court, and with His Majesty having marched with the army during his days as an imperial prince, he certainly won't commit such a cardinal error of warfare. Put your heavenly book away for now, and let's wait for the news! We'll see if I'm right."

Li Xuanba nodded.

*Fine, I won't search my memories for now—not that it would help anyway.* He vaguely recalled that Emperor Yang's campaign against Tuyuhun was a resounding triumph that brought the Great Sui to the peak of its prosperity. His elder brother was probably correct.

Not long after, they were alongside Pei Shiju when a secret imperial missive arrived from the Emperor.

His Majesty wrote: *Fuyun, the Tuyuhun Qaghan, fails to appreciate our grace. We must eradicate Tuyuhun once and for all, and We shall personally lead an imperial expedition to destroy him!*

*However, We cannot tear Ourselves away at present, as We must attend the sacrificial rites at Mount Heng. By the time We finish the rituals and arrive at Zhangye, it will already be autumn or winter, far too cold for campaigning. Therefore, We have resolved to lead the personal expedition next spring. For now, set the matter aside until next year.*

*Minister Pei, your present task is to summon as many Western states as possible to assist at the Mount Heng sacrifices.*

Li Shimin babbled incoherently for a moment before stammering, "It's only the eighth month! The grand army led by the Duke of Xu is already right here! If we strike now with all our might, we could capture the Tuyuhun Qaghan before the first snowfall!"

Given how Tuyuhun crumbled at the slightest touch, the Duke of Xu might even wrap up the campaign just in time to celebrate the Double Ninth Festival!

Pei Shiju instructed Li Shimin patiently, "The Duke of Xu did not pursue further despite a great victory because he must have received His Majesty's decree long ago—ordering him to leave the Tuyuhun Qaghan for His Majesty's personal expedition. Tuyuhun's cause is already lost; there is no need to worry over them. Next, I shall teach you both how to draft official correspondence to the various nations."

Li Shimin pressed anxiously, "But Tuyuhun is already on the verge of total collapse—"

Pei Shiju patted Li Shimin on the shoulder. "His Majesty's will is paramount. Since Tuyuhun no longer possesses the strength to resist, the final blow naturally belongs to His Majesty, so that his imperial majesty may be magnified across the realm."

Looking at the naive Li Shimin, Pei Shiju thought to himself that youth was youth after all; exceptionally talented though he was, he was still far too green when it came to the ways of the world.

Li Xuanba tugged at his elder brother's sleeve. "Enough, Second Brother. Duke Pei is right."

Li Xuanba: 【We will still win next year. Don't worry.】

Li Shimin pressed his lips together, his gaze cast downward.

Next year, the Great Sui would certainly conquer Tuyuhun. But a decisive blow could have been dealt right now—how much more blood, grain, and coin would be squandered instead? If the cost ran too high and the victory proved incomplete, could these lands of Tuyuhun ever truly be held by the Great Sui?

chunks.chapterTitle: 第75章 李三孵出小金雕
chunks.chineseText:
第75章 李三孵出小金雕

=
　　裴世矩闲了下来。李世民和李玄霸也闲了下来。
　　他们二人打理铺子， 听裴世矩授课，因没有朋友一起玩耍，比在洛阳时更闲。
　　张掖在河套平原中段， 南部祁连横亘， 中部平原广袤， 北部的龙首山和合黎山山势平缓低矮，连绵不绝。景色壮丽秀美，奇瑰多变。
　　趁着雪还没有落下， 李世民和李玄霸带着护卫，聘请了当地人当向导，游历了张掖附近景色。
　　他们爬上了祁连山， 观看悬崖下的云海日出时，杨广正在恒山祭祀， 下诏大赦天下；
　　他们在绿洲扎营， 观看了戈壁的落日时，杨广征召天下一万余人驯鹰师，为他驯养最喜爱的猎鹰；
　　他们结识了一位卖马豪商，被邀去草原上与放养的马群一同纵马奔驰时，杨广任命右翊卫将军薛世雄为王门道行军大将进攻伊吾国。
　　伊吾国即后世新疆哈密， 中心区域在北纬42°，海拔为一千三百米。杨广下令征讨伊吾国的时候为冬季。
　　吐谷浑可汗据守的覆袁川即祁连县八宝河， 中心区域为北纬38°，海拔为一千八百米。杨广下令停止攻打吐谷浑可汗时才八月。
　　薛世雄本与启民可汗相约一同出兵，但这位被大隋扶持的启民可汗却放了隋军的鸽子。
　　薛世雄懒得与突厥人攀扯， 孤军出玉门， 穿沙漠， 奇袭伊吾国。伊吾人已经早知启民可汗不会出兵， 以为隋军也不会独自大冬天跑来，所以毫无防备。薛世雄率领隋军到达伊吾城下时，伊吾国吓得举国投降。
　　李世民穿着羊皮大氅，头戴羊毛毡帽，骑在高大的青黑色马背上，看向西北的方向：“大隋军力极强，严寒隆冬也能出玉门，越沙漠，征服伊吾国。”
　　李玄霸骑在枣红色骏马上，被羊羔皮做成的大氅、帽子、围脖裹得严严实实，怀里还塞了个小型的暖笼。
　　他道：“别再想了。”
　　薛世雄进攻伊吾国的消息传到张掖后，李世民的心情一直很不好。李玄霸才约了新认识的马商朋友，带二哥来草原散心。
　　没想到连成群的骏马和可以策马驰骋的草原都不能让二哥开心。
　　李世民摇了摇头，道：“我知道多想也没用，只是心里难受，忍不住难受。如果是我……”
　　李世民说了一半，停下叹了口气，自言自语道：“吐谷浑还未彻底平定，河曲丰旷之野都未打通，穿越沙漠取得遥远的伊吾有何意义？我想不明白陛下的战略。”
　　李玄霸道：“可能他的战略就是‘朕高兴’，没有战略。”
　　李世民瞥了李玄霸一眼。
　　李玄霸叹气：“好吧，不敷衍你。陛下的战略应该是打通汉时的丝绸之路。只是从丝绸之路的什么地方开始打，他比较随心所欲。反正整条丝绸之路都会全线打通，所以从哪个节点打都一样。”
　　李世民提高语调：“一样？”
　　李玄霸道：“陛下认为一样。”
　　李世民沉默。
　　直到看到马商带着一群仆从从远处策马过来时，李世民才道：“来了这里挺好。等长大后，我大概很难再来这里了。只有亲眼看见了此地，我才知道该如何治理此地。”
　　李玄霸拢了拢袖口。二哥现在就做好了当皇帝的准备？真是狂妄。
　　李玄霸道：“你想太多。你以后带兵南征北战，这里也是要来的。”
　　李世民：“……”
　　他转头看向弟弟：“阿玄，听你的话，我南征北战好像是真的南也征北也战，仿佛就我一个人在奔波劳累似的。巍巍大……咳，难道只有我一个将领？那时我不是才十八岁吗？其他将领呢？朝中有本事的老将不少吧？”
　　李玄霸道：“就算你这么问我，我也不知道怎么回答。反正我们现在已经十一岁了，你何不等七年后自己问……问那位。”
　　李世民狠狠翻了个白眼。弟弟这么说，等自家造反后，难道在天下来回奔波的还真的只有自己一个主将？
　　造反时自己才十八岁，封王时才十九岁。谁家领兵主将十八九岁啊？别说资历，这经验也不够啊。
　　我们大唐难道没有其他将领可用了吗？！！
　　“李二郎君！李三郎君！看我找到了什么有趣的东西！”年轻的大胡子马商兴高采烈地喊道。
　　李世民换了一副开朗的表情：“叶护兄，慢点，小心摔着。”
　　叶护笑道：“我自幼在马背上生活，哪可能摔到。”
　　李世民挑眉：“你骑术很厉害？我们比一比？”
　　叶护赶紧摇头：“我手下骑术最好的护卫都赢不了你，我就不自讨没趣了。吁！停！”
　　叶护的马稳稳停在李世民和李玄霸马前。李世民和李玄霸的马一动不动，丝毫不惧。
　　叶护将一团乱布从怀里掏出来，小心翼翼打开破布，里面有两颗鸟蛋：“猜猜是什么鸟蛋？”
　　李世民道：“金雕吧。”
　　李玄霸道：“金雕。”
　　叶护：“……”
　　叶护不敢置信道：“你们的眼力怎么这么厉害，这都能看出来？”
　　李世民和李玄霸对视一眼，失笑道：“这草原上唯一能让叶护兄献宝的鸟蛋就只有金雕了，其他鸟儿哪可能让叶护兄这么开心？”
　　叶护哈哈大笑：“不愧是李二郎君李三郎君！确实如此。来，送给你们。”
　　李玄霸道：“谢谢叶护兄。二哥，今日我给你下碗面条，多加一个煎蛋，尝尝金雕蛋的味道如何。”
　　叶护连忙道：“喂喂！这可是金雕蛋！难道不是先试试能不能孵化吗？”
　　李玄霸一本正经道：“被金雕夫妇抛弃的鸟窝中孵化出雏鸟的可能性太低了，孵化出后要养大也难。想要金雕，不如直接买驯鹰人的鹰。”
　　叶护把鸟蛋放回怀里：“我不送了。”
　　李世民笑得直不起腰：“阿玄，别逗叶护兄。叶护兄放心，我不会让阿玄把鸟蛋吃了。”
　　“哼。”叶护知道李玄霸在逗他，但还是做出一副生气的表情。
　　他把鸟蛋又拿出来：“李三，你究竟要不要？”
　　李玄霸伸手：“给我。”
　　叶护小心翼翼把鸟蛋递给李玄霸。李玄霸把鸟蛋塞进怀里，放到了暖炉旁边。
　　叶护送出鸟蛋后，恢复了笑容：“我的马如何？以后多和我做生意？”
　　李玄霸道：“如果你能保持如今的骏马质量，我可以把你引荐给陛下。”
　　叶护：“……”
　　叶护抹了额头不存在的汗珠，讪讪道：“我以为勾搭上唐国公府就已经够厉害了，这这这……我就送了你们几匹马，就能面圣了？这好处太大，我有点不敢接。”
　　李世民笑道：“我们结交友人只是看眼缘。如果是因为你送的几匹马，这些时日想送我们马的人就太多了。叶护兄，你是因为人品才成为我兄弟二人的友人，和马有什么关系？同样，我们帮你举荐，也只是因为你是我们友人而已。”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　叶护放下手，叹气道：“我知道。一点小恩小惠哪可能诱惑得到你们。但我还是很忐忑。我只是一回纥普通商人，居然能被唐国公的二郎君和三郎君视为朋友。”
　　李世民道：“我结交朋友，不看身份。”
　　李玄霸没好气道：“你再自谦，那我就认为你的品德降低，不适合与我们成为朋友了。”
　　叶护忙道：“我不自谦，绝对不自谦了！”
　　叶护深呼吸了一下，道：“真的要去面圣啊？我紧张。”
　　李玄霸道：“陛下御驾亲征时会来张掖，到时我和二哥会给陛下进献骏马猎鹰。”
　　李世民笑道：“这就是机会，懂？”
　　叶护严肃道：“懂！我会竭尽全力搜寻骏马和猎鹰！”
　　李玄霸道：“裴公肯定也会搜寻骏马和猎鹰，你悄悄行事，切记不可与裴公争夺。”
　　叶护道：“三郎放心。我有分寸。”
　　李世民道：“不仅骏马，如果有其他奇珍异宝，你也可以一同搜寻一二。我就不和你遮掩了。虽然与你结交时我以为你只是普通豪商。这几日来了这草原后，你觉得我和阿玄会信你只是普通豪商？”
　　他看向叶护身后高大威武的护卫们：“不过你也没想瞒着我们吧？”
　　叶护捏了一下鼻子，不好意思道：“能在张掖做马匹生意的人，当然都在部落里有点地位。不过我虽姓药罗葛，只是旁支而已。非旁支的药罗葛也不会来经商了。”
　　药罗葛是回纥部落首领的姓氏。
　　大业元年，袁纥部与仆固、同罗等联合起来，试图脱离突厥的控制，被中原统称为回纥。他们对外也自称回纥人。
　　现在回纥仍旧在突厥的控制下，直到东突厥灭亡时，回纥才取代东突厥。
　　回纥部族从建立、建国到灭国整个时期，大致上都一直与唐朝交好。当回纥灭国之后，小部分西迁，大部分部族南下归唐。后来西迁的回纥人成为维吾尔族的起源，南迁的回纥人基本汉化。
　　叶护是李玄霸先结识的。
　　李玄霸与叶护结识的原因是听到了叶护的姓氏。他知道回纥首领世代出自药罗葛家族，又知道现在还弱小的回纥会成为唐朝的盟友，所以就让人多留心叶护。
　　后来经过打探，叶护这人急公好义，品行不错，就给了叶护一个机会结交自己。
　　这些事叶护都不知道。
　　他又不知道一百多年后回纥会建国。他一个小小的药罗葛贵族，与唐国公府两位郎君的地位如天壤之别，怎么会猜得到李玄霸是故意结交他。
　　李玄霸结交叶护的方式也很自然。他带着二哥去买马，然后什么都没做，二哥就对着马一顿夸，夸得叶护心花怒放，带着二哥去看更好的马。
　　看马的时候，叶护向李世民吹嘘自己的护卫骑术一流。李世民立刻说要比一比。这一比，交情就有了。
　　交友过程真的很自然。李玄霸再次感慨二哥这个“工具人”真的太好用了。
　　对李世民而言，他确实是纯粹看眼缘与叶护结交，半点利益都没有掺加。
　　大唐的人口兵力和科技，现在不可能像控制中原城池那样控制西域。扶持亲近的势力帮唐朝守西域，是最好的方式。
　　历史中的唐朝也是如此扶持回纥。
　　后来唐朝式微，连吐蕃都打不过。被唐朝扶持的回纥被灭时请求唐朝出兵，唐朝都拒绝了，直接将西域拱手让人。回纥被灭后不久，唐朝也名存实亡。
　　两者的存亡相互依存，真是亲近无比。
　　在回纥的角度上，唐朝皇帝颇不是人。
　　安史之乱是回纥出兵帮唐朝收回都城。但回纥可汗希望唐朝出兵帮忙复国的时候，唐朝皇帝却说“你自己的事，我不管”，气得回纥可汗带着剩余不多的军队对唐朝进行自毁式袭击。
　　不过当时的唐朝皇帝也确实有苦衷。他连中原都压不住了，怎么可能还出兵西征？
　　在李世民结交叶护后，李玄霸对二哥唏嘘了很久回纥灭国的事。
　　李世民举起拳头，问李玄霸是不是想让自己把他一拳头打晕。
　　虽然捂嘴没用，但打晕了，李玄霸就不可能在心里叨叨了吧？
　　李世民一点都不想在大唐还没建立的时候，听大唐末年那些糟心事！
　　现在还在大隋呢！
　　李玄霸乖乖闭嘴。
　　当二哥举起拳头的时候，他是真的会揍人。别指望哥哥揍弟弟时会手下留情。特别是在自己现在没生病的时候。
　　叶护为了感谢李世民和李玄霸，还要再送李世民和李玄霸骏马。
　　李世民拒绝，开玩笑道：“你送我们这么多骏马，我们也不好养，算了。我们相处的时间还多的是，以后慢慢送。”
　　叶护听着李世民开玩笑的话，心里很熨帖。
　　李二郎话中的意思是真的想与自己成为一辈子的朋友，叶护要感动哭了。
　　他一个小部落的贵族，在大隋贵人面前与平民百姓没有区别，怎么能被李二郎如此看重？
　　李世民原本虽然与叶护结交，但也没打算和他成为好友。
　　但听了李玄霸的话后，李世民也觉得唐朝在回纥灭国时有点……唉，虽然唐朝都自身难保了，但真的有点为后人脸红。
　　李世民就想对叶护好一点，对回纥好一点。以后大唐吃肉，一定给回纥汤喝。
　　叶护不知道自己得了后人的恩惠，只对李世民和李玄霸不顾身份尊卑与自己平等结交感动不已。
　　李世民拒绝了叶护送的马之后，叶护仍旧问了李世民和李玄霸护卫的数量，给他们的护卫一人换了一匹好马。
　　这些战马在中原非常贵重，但在草原民族这里，也就是他们日常驯养的动物而已。
　　叶护觉得骏马无法衬托自己与李世民和李玄霸的友谊，他决定回去告诉族长此事，让族长倾尽全族之力与李二郎李三郎交好。
　　一个可以在大隋皇帝面前露脸的机会，足以让全族倾囊结交。
　　李世民和李玄霸在草原上住了几日。叶护把李世民和李玄霸送回张掖后，在城门与他们告别。
　　“面圣事关重大，我要回族里禀告首领和长老。”叶护道，“你们努力孵蛋，希望我回来时。你们已经将金雕孵出来了。”
　　李玄霸脸色古怪：“叶护兄，我想你不用等回来时看孵蛋情况了。”
　　叶护惊讶：“怎么？你把鸟蛋揣破了？”
　　李玄霸默默将用布条做成的鸟窝从怀里掏出来。
　　“叽叽喳喳。”
　　一个鸟头从布条里钻出来。
　　又一个鸟头从布条里钻出来。
　　李世民和叶护皆瞪大眼睛：“啊？！！！”
　　两个小鸟头立刻把脑袋缩了回去。
　　李玄霸赶紧把鸟窝放回怀里，担心刚出生的雏鸟被吓死。
　　“小声点！”李玄霸压低声音道，“小鸟很脆弱！”
　　李世民伸长脑袋：“阿玄，快掏出来给我看看，给我看看！”
　　李玄霸道：“回去看。”
　　叶护道：“我明日再出发！走走走，快回去看金雕幼崽！”
　　李世民给了李玄霸的马屁股一鞭子：“快走！”
　　李玄霸一边拉缰绳，一边骂道：“二哥你别抽我马屁股！”
　　李世民大笑着又给了李玄霸的马屁股一鞭子：“走你！驾！”
　　李玄霸的骏马撒开蹄子跑了起来。
　　李玄霸破口大骂：“在城里驾你个头啊！乖马儿，快停下！”
　　李世民：“哈哈哈哈。”
　　叶护看着李二郎欺负弟弟，也忍俊不禁。
　　他有些羡慕李二郎和李三郎的兄弟感情。草原贵族的兄弟感情，唉，不说也罢。
　　……
　　“这就是金雕幼崽？”裴世矩把脑袋凑到鸟房子旁，模样特别可笑。
　　李世民和李玄霸亲手在卧室给两只雏鸟做了个鸟房子，周围放着暖炉，里面塞着毛皮，特别暖和。
　　因为雏鸟非常胆小，所以鸟房子只开了很细小的洞，让它们可以探出脑袋，其他人难以去打扰他们。
　　他们喂鸟和打扫鸟房子的时候，就把鸟房子的房顶直接拿起来。
　　只要只有他们两人在，这两只雏鸟就不害怕。
　　裴世矩见过金雕，但还没见过刚从鸟蛋里孵出来的金雕。何况这金雕的来历也太神奇，居然是从李玄霸怀里孵化。
　　“你们运气太好了，怎么能碰巧掏到鸟蛋，碰巧在怀里孵化，碰巧孵化的雏鸟是金雕？”裴世矩啧啧称奇，“不愧是有名的双生子，真神奇。”
　　李世民得意洋洋道：“那是，我和弟弟的运气一直很好。”
　　李玄霸道：“确实很好。”
　　裴世矩其实不相信他们是碰巧拿到金雕蛋。
　　马商拿着两个鸟蛋给李世民和李玄霸献宝，肯定是借“临时掏了鸟窝”的借口，拿已经快孵化的金雕鸟蛋来送礼。只是鸟蛋碰巧在李玄霸怀里孵化而已。
　　事实也如此。叶护不断叮嘱李玄霸别煮鸟蛋，鸟蛋肯定会孵化时，李世民和李玄霸就猜出叶护是拿快孵化的金雕鸟蛋来送他们。
　　草原贵族不仅养马，鹰也是如骏马一样必须养的“伙伴”。叶护自己就是很厉害的驯鹰人。
　　他为李世民和李玄霸选了最好的鹰生的鸟蛋，算着鸟蛋快孵化的时候送礼。
　　如果李世民和李玄霸不去草原骑马，他也会将鸟蛋送给李世民和李玄霸。
　　不过鸟蛋就在李玄霸怀里孵化出来，叶护也吓了一跳。
　　这可是太巧了。李家兄弟说不定有神灵护体啊。
　　草原人对金雕如同神灵的使者一般喜爱，对能孵化出金雕的李玄霸自然另眼相看。
　　裴世矩道：“你们有想过把来历如此神奇的金雕送给陛下吗？”
　　李世民心中立刻不喜。
　　我家阿玄孵化的鸟儿，凭什么给陛下！陛下难道还缺这雏鸟吗！
　　李玄霸道：“以陛下的慈爱，我们送雏鸟给他，他肯定会反赐给我们。来回折腾，没什么意义。”
　　裴世矩一听，就知道李玄霸舍不得鸟儿。
　　他道：“陛下赏赐回来，这鸟儿会更加金贵。”
　　李玄霸摇头：“话虽如此，但我明知陛下不会要还进献鸟儿，岂不是故意要一个进献的虚名，成了谄媚之人？我与二哥是陛下表侄，不需要谄媚陛下，赠送给陛下的礼物都是真心诚意希望长辈收下的礼物。我已经与陛下写信炫耀鸟儿。当金雕长大，我还会带着他与陛下一起打猎。到时我一定会赢过陛下的猎鹰。”
　　李世民道：“你的金雕肯定没有我的金雕厉害，我才会赢！”
　　李玄霸道：“我打猎不如你，但我的金雕可不一定。”
　　李世民冷哼：“绝对我能赢！”
　　李玄霸和李世民你一言我一语争论起来，裴世矩脸上有点烧。
　　什么叫做谄媚？他们话中有话？
　　但看着两个少年那天真的争吵，裴世矩又觉得自己是不是想多了。李玄霸很尊敬自己，应该不会话中带刺。
