Chapter 75: Li San Hatches the Golden Eaglets

Pei Shiju had some free time. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were also idle.
They managed their shop and attended Pei Shiju’s lectures, but since they had no friends to play with, they were even more bored than they had been in Luoyang.
Zhangye was situated in the middle of the Hetao Plain. To the south, the Qilian Mountains stretched across the horizon; the central region was a vast expanse of plains, while the Longshou and Heli Mountains to the north featured gentle, rolling, and continuous slopes. The scenery was magnificent, beautiful, and ever-changing.
Before the snow began to fall, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, accompanied by their guards and a local guide they had hired, traveled to explore the landscapes around Zhangye.
When they climbed the Qilian Mountains to watch the sunrise over the sea of clouds beneath the cliffs, Yang Guang was performing sacrifices at Mount Heng and issuing an edict for a general amnesty across the realm.
When they camped in an oasis to watch the sunset over the Gobi, Yang Guang was conscripting over ten thousand falconers from across the land to train his favorite hunting hawks.
When they befriended a wealthy horse merchant and were invited to gallop across the grasslands alongside his herds, Yang Guang appointed General Xue Shixiong of the Right Yijia Guard as the commander of the Wangmendao expeditionary force to attack the Yiwu Kingdom.
The Yiwu Kingdom was located in what would later be known as Hami, Xinjiang, with its central region at 42° north latitude and an elevation of 1,300 meters. It was winter when Yang Guang ordered the conquest of Yiwu.
The Fuyuan River, where the Tuyuhun Khan held his stronghold, was the Babao River in Qilian County, located at 38° north latitude with an elevation of 1,800 meters. It was only August when Yang Guang ordered the cessation of the attack on the Tuyuhun Khan.
Xue Shixiong had originally agreed to launch the campaign in coordination with Qimin Khan, but this Khan, who had been propped up by the Great Sui, stood the Sui army up.
Xue Shixiong, not wanting to waste time bickering with the Turks, led his army alone out of the Jade Gate, crossed the desert, and launched a surprise attack on Yiwu. The people of Yiwu, having long known that Qimin Khan would not send troops and assuming the Sui army would not dare to cross the desert in the dead of winter, were completely caught off guard. When Xue Shixiong led the Sui forces to the gates of Yiwu City, the entire kingdom surrendered in terror.
Li Shimin, wearing a sheepskin cloak and a felt hat, sat atop a tall, dark-blue horse and looked toward the northwest: "The Great Sui’s military might is immense. Even in the depths of a bitter winter, they can march out of the Jade Gate, cross the desert, and conquer Yiwu."
Li Xuanba, riding a chestnut stallion, was bundled tightly in a lambskin cloak, hat, and scarf, with a small hand-warmer tucked into his chest.
He said, "Stop thinking about it."
Ever since the news of Xue Shixiong’s attack on Yiwu reached Zhangye, Li Shimin had been in a foul mood. Li Xuanba had invited their new horse-merchant friend to take his second brother out to the grasslands to clear his head.
He hadn't expected that even the herds of fine horses and the vast, open grasslands wouldn't be enough to cheer his brother up.
Li Shimin shook his head and said, "I know overthinking is useless, but my heart feels heavy; I can't help but feel distressed. If it were me..."
Li Shimin stopped halfway, sighed, and muttered to himself, "The Tuyuhun have not been completely pacified, and the fertile, expansive fields of the Yellow River bend have not yet been secured. What is the point of crossing the desert to seize the remote Yiwu? I cannot understand His Majesty’s strategy."
Li Xuanba said, "Perhaps his strategy is simply 'I am pleased,' and there is no strategy at all."
Li Shimin shot Li Xuanba a glance.
Li Xuanba sighed: "Fine, I won't fob you off. His Majesty’s strategy is likely to reopen the Silk Road of the Han Dynasty. It’s just that he is rather capricious about where to start. Since the entire Silk Road will eventually be opened, it makes no difference which node he starts from."
Li Shimin raised his voice: "No difference?"
Li Xuanba said, "His Majesty thinks there is no difference."
Li Shimin fell silent.
It wasn't until he saw the horse merchant leading a group of servants toward them on horseback that Li Shimin said, "Coming here is good. When I grow up, I will likely find it hard to return. Only by seeing this place with my own eyes can I know how to govern it."
Li Xuanba pulled his sleeves tighter. His second brother was already preparing to be Emperor? How arrogant.
Li Xuanba said, "You’re thinking too much. When you lead troops on campaigns in the future, you will come here eventually."
Li Shimin: "..."
He turned to his younger brother: "Axuan, listening to you, it sounds as if my future campaigns will be a constant cycle of marching north and south, as if I am the only one doing all the labor. The great... *cough*, am I the only general? I’ll only be eighteen then, won't I? What about the other generals? There must be plenty of capable old veterans in the court, right?"
Li Xuanba said, "Even if you ask me that, I don't know how to answer. Anyway, we are already eleven now; why don't you wait seven years and ask... ask that person yourself."
Li Shimin rolled his eyes fiercely. If his brother said that, did it mean that after they rebelled, he would truly be the only commander running across the land?
He would be only eighteen when he rebelled and only nineteen when he was enfeoffed as a prince. What kind of army has an eighteen or nineteen-year-old as its main commander? Forget seniority; he wouldn't even have the experience.
Did the Great Tang really have no other generals to use?!!
"Young Master Li Er! Young Master Li San! Look at what interesting things I’ve found!" the young, bearded horse merchant shouted joyfully.
Li Shimin put on a cheerful expression: "Brother Yehu, slow down, be careful not to fall."
Yehu laughed: "I’ve lived on horseback since I was a child; how could I fall?"
Li Shimin raised an eyebrow: "Your horsemanship is that good? Shall we have a race?"
Yehu shook his head hurriedly: "Even the best rider among my guards couldn't beat you, so I won't invite humiliation. Whoa! Stop!"
Yehu’s horse came to a steady halt in front of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. Their horses remained motionless, showing no fear.
Yehu pulled a bundle of messy cloth from his chest and carefully opened it to reveal two bird eggs: "Guess what kind of bird eggs these are?"
Li Shimin said, "Golden eagles, I suppose."
Li Xuanba said, "Golden eagles."
Yehu: "..."
Yehu said in disbelief, "How is your eyesight so sharp that you could tell even this?"
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba exchanged a look and laughed: "In these grasslands, the only bird eggs that would make Brother Yehu want to show off as a treasure are those of the golden eagle. How could any other bird make Brother Yehu so happy?"
Yehu burst into laughter: "As expected of Young Master Li Er and Young Master Li San! That is indeed true. Here, they are yours."
Li Xuanba said, "Thank you, Brother Yehu. Second Brother, I’ll cook you some noodles today and add a fried egg; let’s taste how a golden eagle egg fares."
Yehu hurriedly said, "Hey, hey! These are golden eagle eggs! Shouldn't you at least try to hatch them first?"
Li Xuanba said with a straight face, "The probability of a chick hatching from a nest abandoned by the parent eagles is too low, and even if it hatches, it’s hard to raise. If you want a golden eagle, it’s better to just buy one from a falconer."
Yehu put the eggs back into his chest: "I’m not giving them to you anymore."
Li Shimin laughed so hard he couldn't stand straight: "Axuan, stop teasing Brother Yehu. Don't worry, Brother Yehu, I won't let Axuan eat the eggs."
"Hmph." Yehu knew Li Xuanba was teasing him, but he still put on an angry expression.
He took the eggs out again: "Li San, do you want them or not?"
Li Xuanba reached out: "Give them to me."
Yehu carefully handed the eggs to Li Xuanba. Li Xuanba tucked them into his chest, placing them next to his hand-warmer.
After handing over the eggs, Yehu’s smile returned: "How are my horses? Shall we do more business in the future?"
Li Xuanba said, "If you can maintain the quality of these fine steeds, I can introduce you to His Majesty."
Yehu: "..."
Yehu wiped non-existent sweat from his forehead and said sheepishly, "I thought getting connected with the Tang Duke’s mansion was already impressive enough, but this... I just gave you a few horses, and I can meet the Emperor? This reward is too great; I’m afraid to accept it."
Li Shimin smiled: "We make friends based on whether we click. If it were just because of a few horses, there would be too many people wanting to give us gifts these days. Brother Yehu, you became our friend because of your character; what does that have to do with horses? Likewise, we are recommending you only because you are our friend."
Li Xuanba nodded.
Yehu lowered his hands and sighed: "I know. Small favors couldn't possibly tempt you. But I’m still nervous. I’m just an ordinary Uighur merchant, yet I am considered a friend by the second and third young masters of the Tang Duke’s mansion."
Li Shimin said, "I don't look at status when making friends."
Li Xuanba said irritably, "If you continue to be so self-deprecating, I will think your character has declined and you are no longer fit to be our friend."
Yehu hurriedly said, "I won't be self-deprecating, absolutely not!"
Yehu took a deep breath and said, "Are we really going to meet the Emperor? I’m nervous."
Li Xuanba said, "His Majesty will come to Zhangye during his imperial tour. When that time comes, Second Brother and I will present fine horses and hunting hawks to him."
Li Shimin smiled: "That is the opportunity, understand?"
Yehu said solemnly, "Understood! I will do my utmost to search for the finest horses and hawks!"
Li Xuanba said, "Lord Pei will certainly be searching for them too. Act quietly; remember, do not compete with Lord Pei."
Yehu said, "Don't worry, Young Master San. I know my limits."
Li Shimin said, "Not just horses; if you find other rare treasures, you can search for those as well. I won't hide it from you. Although I thought you were just an ordinary wealthy merchant when we first met, after being on these grasslands for a few days, do you think Axuan and I would believe you’re just an ordinary merchant?"
He looked at the tall, imposing guards behind Yehu: "But you didn't intend to hide it from us, did you?"
Yehu pinched his nose and said embarrassedly, "Anyone who can do horse business in Zhangye naturally has some status in their tribe. However, although my surname is Yaoluoge, I am only from a branch family. The main branch of the Yaoluoge wouldn't come here to trade."
Yaoluoge was the surname of the Uighur tribal leaders.
In the first year of the Daye era, the Yuanhe tribe joined forces with the Pugu and Tongluo to break free from Turkic control, collectively known in the Central Plains as the Uighurs. They also referred to themselves as Uighurs.
At this time, the Uighurs were still under Turkic control; it was not until the fall of the Eastern Turks that the Uighurs would replace them.
From its establishment and founding to its eventual fall, the Uighur tribe remained on good terms with the Tang Dynasty for the most part. After the Uighur state fell, a small portion migrated west, while the majority of the tribe moved south to submit to the Tang. Later, the westward-migrating Uighurs became the origin of the Uyghur ethnic group, while those who moved south were largely assimilated into the Han.
Li Xuanba had been the first to befriend Yehu.
The reason Li Xuanba befriended Yehu was that he heard his surname. He knew that the Uighur leaders were descended from the Yaoluoge family for generations, and he knew that the currently weak Uighurs would become allies of the Tang, so he had people keep an eye on Yehu.
Later, after some inquiries, he found that Yehu was righteous and of good character, so he gave him a chance to befriend them.
Yehu knew none of this.
He didn't know that the Uighurs would build a nation in over a hundred years. As a minor Yaoluoge noble, his status was worlds apart from the two young masters of the Tang Duke’s mansion; how could he have guessed that Li Xuanba was befriending him on purpose?
Li Xuanba’s method of befriending Yehu was also very natural. He took his second brother to buy horses, and then did nothing; his second brother praised the horses so much that Yehu was overjoyed and took them to see even better ones.
While looking at the horses, Yehu boasted about the top-tier horsemanship of his guards. Li Shimin immediately challenged them to a race. Once they raced, the friendship was forged.
The process of making friends was truly natural. Li Xuanba once again marveled that his second brother, this "tool," was just too easy to use.
For Li Shimin, he had truly befriended Yehu based on a gut feeling, without a shred of ulterior motive.
Given the population, military strength, and technology of the Great Tang, it was impossible to control the Western Regions like they controlled the cities of the Central Plains. Supporting friendly forces to help the Tang guard the Western Regions was the best way.
The historical Tang Dynasty had also supported the Uighurs in this way.
Later, when the Tang Dynasty declined and couldn't even defeat the Tibetans, the Uighurs—who had been supported by the Tang—requested military aid when they were being destroyed, but the Tang Emperor refused, handing over the Western Regions to others. Shortly after the Uighurs were destroyed, the Tang Dynasty also became a mere shell of its former self.
The survival of both was interdependent; they were truly close.
From the Uighur perspective, the Tang Emperor was quite a piece of work.
During the An Lushan Rebellion, the Uighurs sent troops to help the Tang recover their capital. But when the Uighur Khan hoped for the Tang to send troops to help restore his nation, the Tang Emperor said, "Your own affairs are your own business, I will not interfere," which infuriated the Uighur Khan, leading him to launch a suicidal attack on the Tang with his remaining forces.
However, the Tang Emperor at the time did have his own difficulties. He couldn't even control the Central Plains; how could he possibly send troops on a western expedition?
After Li Shimin befriended Yehu, Li Xuanba had sighed to his second brother for a long time about the fall of the Uighurs.
Li Shimin had raised his fist, asking Li Xuanba if he wanted him to knock him unconscious with one punch.
Although covering his mouth was useless, if he were knocked out, Li Xuanba wouldn't be able to nag him in his heart, right?
Li Shimin did not want to hear about the miserable affairs of the late Tang Dynasty while the Great Tang hadn't even been established yet!
They were still in the Great Sui!
Li Xuanba obediently shut his mouth.
When his second brother raised his fist, he would truly hit him. Don't expect a brother to show mercy when beating his younger brother. Especially now that he wasn't sick.
To thank Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Yehu wanted to give them even more fine horses.
Li Shimin refused, joking: "You’ve given us so many fine horses, we can't take care of them all, forget it. We have plenty of time to spend together; you can give them to us slowly in the future."
Hearing Li Shimin’s joking words, Yehu felt very touched.
The implication in Li Er-lang’s words was that he truly wanted to be friends for life; Yehu was moved to tears.
As a noble from a small tribe, he was no different from a commoner in the eyes of the Great Sui’s nobility; how could he be so valued by Li Er-lang?
Although Li Shimin had initially befriended Yehu, he hadn't intended to become close friends.
But after hearing Li Xuanba’s words, Li Shimin also felt that the Tang Dynasty had been a bit... sigh, although the Tang was struggling to save itself, it really made one blush for their descendants.
Li Shimin wanted to be a bit kinder to Yehu and the Uighurs. In the future, when the Great Tang ate meat, they would definitely give the Uighurs some soup.
Yehu did not know he had received the favor of future generations; he was only moved that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had disregarded status and rank to befriend him as an equal.
After Li Shimin refused the horses, Yehu still asked for the number of their guards and replaced each of their guards' mounts with a fine horse.
These warhorses were extremely valuable in the Central Plains, but to the grassland peoples, they were just animals they raised daily.
Yehu felt that fine horses couldn't fully reflect his friendship with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, so he decided to go back and tell the tribal chief about this, urging the chief to use the entire tribe’s strength to befriend Li Er-lang and Li San-lang.
An opportunity to show his face before the Emperor of the Great Sui was enough to make the whole tribe go all out to build this friendship.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba stayed on the grasslands for a few days. After Yehu escorted them back to Zhangye, he bid them farewell at the city gate.
"Meeting the Emperor is a matter of great importance; I must return to the tribe to report to the chief and the elders," Yehu said. "You two work hard on hatching those eggs; I hope that when I return, you will have already hatched the golden eagles."
Li Xuanba’s expression was strange: "Brother Yehu, I don't think you need to wait until you return to see the hatching situation."
Yehu was surprised: "Why? Did you crush the eggs?"
Li Xuanba silently pulled the bird nest made of cloth strips from his chest.
"Chirp, chirp."
A bird’s head poked out from the cloth strips.
Another bird’s head poked out from the cloth strips.
Li Shimin and Yehu both widened their eyes: "Ah?!!!"
The two little bird heads immediately retracted.
Li Xuanba hurriedly put the nest back into his chest, worried that the newborn chicks would be scared to death.
"Keep your voices down!" Li Xuanba whispered, "The chicks are very fragile!"
Li Shimin stretched his neck: "Axuan, hurry up and take them out for me to see, let me see!"
Li Xuanba said, "We’ll look when we get back."
Yehu said, "I’ll set off tomorrow! Let’s go, let’s go, hurry back and look at the golden eagle cubs!"
Li Shimin gave Li Xuanba’s horse a whip on the rump: "Hurry up!"
Li Xuanba pulled the reins while cursing: "Second Brother, stop whipping my horse’s rump!"
Li Shimin laughed and gave Li Xuanba’s horse another whip: "Go! Giddy up!"
Li Xuanba’s stallion kicked up its hooves and started running.
Li Xuanba cursed loudly: "Giddy up in the city? Are you crazy! Good horse, stop!"
Li Shimin: "Hahahaha."
Yehu watched Li Er-lang bullying his younger brother and couldn't help but smile.
He felt a bit envious of the brotherly bond between Li Er-lang and Li San-lang. The brotherly bonds of grassland nobles—sigh, better not to speak of them.
...
"These are the golden eagle cubs?" Pei Shiju leaned his head toward the birdhouse, looking particularly ridiculous.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had personally built a birdhouse for the two chicks in their bedroom, placing a hand-warmer nearby and stuffing it with fur to keep it extra warm.
Because the chicks were very timid, the birdhouse only had a tiny hole, allowing them to poke their heads out while making it difficult for others to disturb them.
When they fed the birds or cleaned the house, they would simply lift the roof off.
As long as only the two of them were present, the chicks were not afraid.
Pei Shiju had seen golden eagles, but he had never seen one that had just hatched. Moreover, the origin of these eagles was too magical—they had actually hatched in Li Xuanba’s chest.
"Your luck is too good. How could you happen to find the eggs, happen to hatch them in your chest, and happen to have the hatched chicks be golden eagles?" Pei Shiju marveled, "As expected of the famous twins, truly miraculous."
Li Shimin said triumphantly: "That’s right, my brother and I have always had great luck."
Li Xuanba said, "Indeed, very good."
Pei Shiju didn't actually believe they had stumbled upon the golden eagle eggs by chance.
The horse merchant bringing the two eggs to offer as a treasure to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba must have used the excuse of "temporarily raiding a nest" to bring eggs that were already close to hatching as a gift. It was just a coincidence that they hatched in Li Xuanba’s chest.
The truth was exactly that. When Yehu kept urging Li Xuanba not to boil the eggs and saying they would definitely hatch, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had guessed that Yehu was bringing them eggs that were about to hatch.
Grassland nobles didn't just raise horses; hawks were "partners" that had to be raised just like fine steeds. Yehu himself was a very skilled falconer.
He had chosen the eggs from the best hawks for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, timing the gift for when they were about to hatch.
Even if Li Shimin and Li Xuanba hadn't gone to the grasslands to ride, he would have still given them the eggs.
However, the fact that they hatched right in Li Xuanba’s chest had startled Yehu as well.
This was just too coincidental. The Li brothers might truly be protected by divine spirits.
Grassland people loved golden eagles as if they were messengers of the gods, and naturally, they looked at Li Xuanba, who could hatch golden eagles, with different eyes.
Pei Shiju said, "Have you considered giving these golden eagles, with such a magical origin, to His Majesty?"
Li Shimin felt an immediate dislike in his heart.
The birds my Axuan hatched—why should I give them to His Majesty! Does His Majesty even lack these chicks!
Li Xuanba said, "Given His Majesty’s kindness, if we give him the chicks, he will surely bestow them back upon us. It’s a pointless back-and-forth, with no meaning."
As soon as Pei Shiju heard this, he knew Li Xuanba couldn't bear to part with the birds.
He said, "If His Majesty bestows them back, these birds will become even more precious."
Li Xuanba shook his head: "That may be so, but if I know His Majesty won't keep them and I still present them, wouldn't I be deliberately seeking the empty name of a presenter and becoming a sycophant? Second Brother and I are the Emperor’s cousins; we don't need to fawn over him. The gifts we give to His Majesty are sincere gifts we hope our elder will accept. I have already written to His Majesty to brag about the birds. When the golden eagles grow up, I will take them to hunt with His Majesty. At that time, I will definitely beat His Majesty’s hunting hawks."
Li Shimin said, "Your golden eagle definitely won't be as good as mine; I’m the one who will win!"
Li Xuanba said, "I’m not as good at hunting as you, but my golden eagle might not be."
Li Shimin snorted: "I will definitely win!"
Li Xuanba and Li Shimin argued back and forth, and Pei Shiju’s face burned a little.
What did they mean by sycophant? Was there a hidden meaning in their words?
But looking at the innocent bickering of the two youths, Pei Shiju wondered if he was overthinking it. Li Xuanba respected him, so he shouldn't be speaking with thorns in his words.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第76章 御驾亲征走三月
chunks.chineseText:
第76章 御驾亲征走三月

=
　　裴世矩劝李世民和李玄霸进献金雕幼崽纯粹是好心。
　　若不是他如今自诩为李世民和李玄霸的老师， 也不会多管闲事。
　　所以李世民和李玄霸虽然心里不舒服，但也没有太在意此事，还给裴世矩寻了一只金雕幼鸟， 让裴世矩也养着玩。
　　裴世矩刚开始很有兴致。亲自喂肉被鸟啄伤之后， 他就放弃了。
　　金雕这鸟性格太烈， 还是别人养，自己看，更有意思。
　　李玄霸自己孵的鸟儿， 金雕幼崽对他特别亲近，从来不会啄他。
　　金雕幼崽会啄李世民。但李世民拿着细木棍与它们搏斗一番后，两只幼崽就乖乖认了这个给它们肉吃还揍它们的“首领”， 一个指令一个动作，比对李玄霸还乖。
　　李玄霸下指令时， 这两只小雕崽会翻肚子装死， 不给肉肉不学习。
　　李玄霸很生气地训斥小雕崽。
　　小雕崽转头用鸟屁股对着李玄霸。
　　李世民震惊：“寒钩和乌镝真聪明！还会和你使小脾气！”
　　李玄霸道：“大金和小金确实聪明。”
　　兄弟俩对视一眼。
　　李世民道：“你取的名字也太敷衍了。你看这只微大一圈的崽崽的嘴尖带一点银色，就像是闪着寒光的弯刀。小一圈的崽崽翅膀长羽毛的尾部是黑色，就像是一支乌黑的箭。叫寒钩和乌镝！”
　　李玄霸道：“太拗口，就叫大金小金。”
　　李世民道：“我养大的雕崽，绝对不能叫这么敷衍的名字！对吧， 寒钩乌镝。”
　　两只雕崽不理睬他。
　　李玄霸伸手：“大金，小金。”
　　两只雕崽转头， 然后小脑袋转回去，继续撅着屁股对着李玄霸。
　　李玄霸对李世民挑眉。
　　李世民不满道：“它们还小，听不懂我取的名字更好。你现在给它们取这么蠢的名字， 以后它们怎么见人？赶紧给我改！现在还来得及！”
　　李玄霸也知道著名玛丽苏取名爱好者唐太宗二哥取的名字比自己好。他只是习惯性地和二哥杠一下。
　　杠完之后， 他就教雕崽新名字。
　　金雕确实聪明， 但雕崽聪明得过了头。特别是在李玄霸面前。
　　金雕属于“猎鹰”， 在科学家做的鸟类脑容量研究中位列第八，仅次于鸦类。它们有完整的逻辑思维，记忆力很好，还特别记仇，能简单模仿人类动作，简单使用工具。
　　但智力需要伴随着身体而成长，就算人类刚出生的时候也是“智障”，只有动物本能。这两只雕崽才出生不到一个月就如此情绪化，智商过高了。
　　李玄霸思索之后，猜测可能有他精神力刺激的原因。
　　自己一直开着精神力“公放”。这点精神力对人类而言连挠痒痒都做不到，但对于脆弱的小雕崽而言，可能刺激过大了些。
　　毕竟就算成年金雕，智商和人类也是远远不能比。若它们的智商和服从力能达到七八岁小孩，就已经是成精了。
　　李玄霸本想试着再培养其他动物。但想起其他动物的寿命很短，自己若是精心培养一只很聪明的动物，一二十年后就要与其告别，李玄霸就放弃了这个打算。
　　金雕人工饲养的平均寿命为四十岁。就算雕崽卡着人工饲养的平均寿命去世，自己也已经五十了。
　　以自己的身体状态，还不知道谁给谁送终。还是只养雕崽就好。
　　李玄霸摸了摸两只雕崽的脑袋：“以后给你们改名，大金叫寒钩，小金叫乌镝。”
　　两只雕崽懵懵懂懂地转头看向李玄霸，没听懂李玄霸的话。
　　不过只要以后在喂食的时候改口，两只聪明的小雕崽一定会记得自己的名字。
　　等它们再长大一些，要不要教它们算术呢？如果教会了它们算术，会不会更顽皮？
　　李玄霸抚摸着小雕崽的羽毛胡思乱想。
　　寒钩乖乖被李玄霸抚摸。乌镝眼珠子转了转，屁股一撅，对着李玄霸发射了一发鸟屎，正中李玄霸手指。
　　“喳喳喳！”乌镝蹦蹦跳跳往李世民那里逃。
　　李玄霸掏出手帕擦掉手上鸟屎，冷笑：“今天你没肉吃了！”
　　李世民双手护住乌镝：“乌镝还小，不吃肉怎么行？别气别气，它才刚出生不久，肯定是无意。”
　　李玄霸骂道：“你看它对着我喷鸟屎，还说是无意？！”
　　李世民坚持：“对！就是无意！”
　　李玄霸道：“你现在这么宠着它们，以后它们要怎么打猎？”
　　李世民道：“以后找最严格的驯鹰师！我知道溺子如杀子，只要我看不见就没问题！”
　　李玄霸被气笑了。他总算知道二哥的儿子为什么会长成那副鬼样了。一边可劲儿把儿子宠得心理脆弱，一边让其他人对着已经被宠成巨婴的儿子使劲压，这能养出心理正常的人才有鬼！
　　李玄霸苦口婆心教训二哥养雕的方式不对。
　　李世民哪辩得赢李玄霸？他连魏徵都辩不过。
　　于是李世民讪讪放弃了教育雕崽的主导权，只给弟弟当辅助，在旁边嘀咕“它们真的还小，别太严格”。
　　李玄霸觉得，二哥一定是后世年轻人养孩子时最讨厌见到的那种长辈。你在教导孩子，他就在旁边吧啦“算了算了”。
　　还好雕崽听不懂太复杂的人话，否则一定会成为废雕。
　　李玄霸把乌镝关了起来，让它看着寒钩吃肉，等寒钩吃完肉后才放出来。
　　“你，没肉吃。”李玄霸把乌镝的脑袋推了个倒仰。
　　乌镝看看寒钩，低头蹭了蹭李玄霸。
　　李玄霸收起手指，把两只雕崽放回鸟房子，关门离开。
　　乌镝：“……”
　　乌镝QAQ。
　　“喳喳喳喳！”
　　肉肉肉肉！我的肉呢？！呜哇哇哇！！
　　李世民在窗口偷看。他视力极好，看到了小雕崽从鸟房子的洞口冒出的小脑袋上，眼泪把绒毛都打湿了。
　　他也哭了。
　　李世民被李玄霸从窗口拖走，哽咽道：“阿玄，你好残忍。”
　　李玄霸面无表情：“哦。”
　　哭包二哥真是没救了。
　　……
　　金雕幼崽成长速度较慢。
　　当李世民和李玄霸十一岁的时候，两只雕崽刚能自己撕咬生肉。
　　当张掖的河水完全融化的时候，两只雕崽才开始换毛。
　　比起身体的成长速度，两只雕崽的智商成长速度更快。当看见自己掉毛的时候，两只雕崽缩在窝里哀嚎痛哭。
　　李玄霸道：“和刚掉牙的二哥你没区别。”
　　还处于换牙期，现在看到牙齿掉落还会眼眶发红，并为牙齿取名字，好好安葬的李世民：“……胡说，我没有！”
　　李玄霸道：“我们马上要变声了。喉咙发肿，声音变沙哑，俗称公鸭嗓子，特别难听。你变声的时候会不会也哭一场？”
　　李世民咬牙切齿：“不会！”
　　他转身就跑去找孙思邈，问孙医师自己是不是真的要变声，好提前做好心理准备。
　　换牙时不好好对待牙齿，以后长出的牙齿就会变丑。变声的时候是不是不好好保护嗓子，声音也会变难听？
　　他不要一辈子都是公鸭嗓子！
　　李玄霸笑话二哥之后，收集了雕崽换下的绒毛，准备与药材和风景图，一起寄给宇文珠。
　　他已经仔细咀嚼完了宇文珠寄给他的“论文”，并把“论文”给孙思邈“勘误”。
　　孙思邈说，这书信中所有方子都是经过了多次验证，没有任何错误，而且很适合李玄霸。
　　方子很正确，可能是宇文珠之前的学识积累。
　　但这些方子中没有任何与李玄霸常患疾病所冲突的药材，宇文珠恐怕已经把李玄霸所有病例都吃透了。
　　也不知道宇文珠从哪得到的自己的病例。李玄霸想。
　　李玄霸从小到大得过很多病。他自己都记不清自己得了什么病，只有孙思邈和府中供奉的医师全记得。
　　即使李玄霸现在心中一想到宇文珠的年龄，就不可能对宇文珠生出男女之情。但从宇文珠的“论文”中猜到她读完了自己所有病例，给自己罗列出这些方子。他内心也是说不出的复杂。
　　感动肯定是有的。
　　所以这次为宇文珠准备礼物时，李玄霸就用心了许多。
　　虽然宇文珠肯定会更喜欢药材和孙医师新的医学见解，但塞外的风景和可爱的雕崽，或许更能体现出自己的善意。
　　河水化冻，张掖往大兴和洛阳的道路也重新变得易于通行。
　　李玄霸和李世民给家人、未婚妻、老师和友人寄去了书信和礼物，没忘记给皇帝、太子和齐王也寄去了一封信。
　　雕崽的事，李玄霸和李世民写到了给皇帝的书信中，说他们二人与雕崽同吃同住，提前学会如何养孩子。
　　他们俩都写到这份上了，两只金雕而已，以杨广的骄傲，不屑于和孩子抢。
　　到时候他们再教雕崽在杨广面前装智障，雕崽就安全了。
　　张掖河水化冻的时候，杨广送走了来洛阳蹭吃蹭喝的启民可汗，开始西征。
　　启民可汗放了隋军鸽子，杨广也没有怪罪启民可汗，听信了启民可汗“我只是因为天气太冷晚到了，没想到薛将军跑那么快”的胡扯，甚至比上次接待启民可汗更加隆重，赏赐更加丰厚。
　　高颎、宇文弼、薛道衡在雪中孤亭中屏退所有下人，围着火炉吃涮锅时小声吐槽，陛下若给朝臣对启民可汗十分之一的宽容和厚待，就是仁君了。
　　涮锅方子是李玄霸送的。三老头特别喜欢，隔三岔五就要聚一起吃一次。
　　二月中旬，杨广到达大兴。
　　三月初二，杨广来到了黄河以西。
　　四月二十七日，早已经过了立夏，已经快芒种时，杨广终于出临津关，渡黄河，到达了西平郡。
　　裴世矩一直派人查探吐谷浑可汗的消息，好在皇帝来的第一时间展现出自己的本事。
　　李世民和李玄霸也得以掌握吐谷浑可汗的近况。
　　二月底的时候，吐谷浑可汗得知了大隋皇帝要御驾亲征的事。
　　他开始排兵布阵，修建堡垒，囤积粮草。
　　三月整整一个月，都立夏了，能闪击伊吾国的大隋强军都还没有影子。
　　吐谷浑可汗率领军队掠夺周围游牧民族吃着春夏水草变肥的牛羊，还去草原上套了许多膘肥体壮的野马。
　　四月整整一个月，大隋军队还没有动静。
　　吐谷浑可汗派人回到原本失去领土中的最坚固的几座城池布防。
　　随着天气越来越炎热，交通越来越方便，裴世矩得到吐谷浑可汗消息的间隙越来越短。
　　李世民也一日比一日更沉默。
　　当杨广终于到达西平郡，那个许国公宇文述在去年八月就到达的地方，李世民问李玄霸，又像是自问：“陛下为何会如此慢？吐谷浑可汗离大隋遥远，花了一月才得知大隋军队的动向，居然还能做整整两月的准备！”
　　李玄霸道：“因为陛下乘坐着他豪华的观风殿，带着妃嫔和宫女，让乐人伶人一路鼓乐作陪，让沿路官吏和百姓夹道欢迎进奉美食，一路走一路吃喝玩乐，所以慢。”
　　李世民双手握拳，两眼赤红，这次没有落下泪来。
　　李玄霸躺在草地上，抬头看着在低空盘旋的寒钩和乌镝。
　　小雕崽都能给他和二哥抓兔子了，隋炀帝御驾亲征的车驾还没到。
　　纵观历史，横观世界，有多少皇帝国王御驾亲征的时候还乘坐着豪华的房车，带着妃嫔宫女乐人伶人？
　　史书中记载唐太宗亲征高丽的“花里胡哨”，是亲自率领一万金光闪闪的具装骑兵，与李勣在辽东城下汇合。
　　就是驴车之神宋太宗和叫门天子明英宗，御驾亲征的时候也没有带妃嫔和宫女。
　　这是打仗吗？陛下？
　　这是打仗啊！陛下！
　　这段御驾亲征在史书中只有寥寥几笔，还是隋炀帝难得的高光时刻，甚至都不是当做隋炀帝“恶政”来描述，而是正面评价。
　　李玄霸看待此世，习惯性站在旁观者的角度，情绪抽离，很冷静。这次他还是被杨广这御驾亲征给逗笑了。
　　这都能赢，实在是大隋太强了，吐谷浑太弱了。
　　哦，吐谷浑在去年一月之内灭国，本来就弱得没眼看。现在养了半年，居然有复国的迹象，这才是奇葩事。
　　李世民松开拳头，往后一倒，也躺在了草地上：“怪不得还有七年，大隋就亡了。”
　　李玄霸道：“所以你别气了。现在正是大隋高光时期你都气得不行。等征高丽的时候，你不得气出病来？”
　　李世民转头，面无表情道：“他还要征高丽，三征？就高丽？”
　　李玄霸道：“他不仅三征高丽，还给高丽‘赠送’大量兵器盔甲，让你亲征高丽时战争胜利，战略失败呢。”
　　李世民不敢置信：“啊？什么叫战争胜利战略失败……我知道了，虽然我与高丽的对战都胜利了，但耗费太大，得不偿失，继续作战会损害国力和百姓，所以我没有灭掉高丽就撤兵了？”
　　李玄霸道：“是。你二月出征，打了七个月，占了十几座城，杀伤俘虏高丽十几万人，缴获马匹武器盔甲无数，九月天冷了粮草不好运就退兵了。然后你捶胸顿足说大失败。后世还以为大唐战败，损失惨重呢。”
　　他的营销号下面，连一些太宗粉都在那长吁短叹唐太宗不该亲征高丽，打了败仗，损失惨重，和杨广征高丽一样。
　　他这个太宗黑都看乐了，挨个点赞。
　　这不怪他们。唐太宗自己都哭“输了输了”，还为此怀念魏徵，把自己推掉的魏徵功德碑又重新立了起来。还能怪别人误解？
　　李世民嫌弃道：“啧。一次不成功，休养生息几年，再打啊。”
　　李玄霸道：“是啊，你回去后短时间打造出大唐海军，开辟海上运输线，准备海陆并进；并持续骚扰高丽，让他们无法休养生息，做足了万全准备。然后……”
　　李世民捂耳朵：“不听了。”
　　李玄霸：【然后你驾崩了，哈哈哈哈哈哈哈！人生最后一场御驾亲征就变成“朕败了”哈哈哈哈哈！】
　　李世民一个扑腾翻身而起，举着拳头朝着弟弟砸下。
　　李玄霸迅速翻滚躲开二哥，抓起一把土洒向二哥的脸。
　　李世民闭着眼睛吐土：“呸呸呸……站住！”
　　李玄霸大笑着逃走：“哈哈哈哈哈！”
　　李世民拔腿就追：“李玄霸！你站住！”
　　李玄霸抡圆了腿使劲跑：“李世民，我不站住！你自己的失误，还怪我啰？”
　　李世民骂道：“放屁！和我有什么关系！”
　　李玄霸嘲笑：“和你没关系，你为何恼羞成怒？”
　　李世民停下脚步：“对哦。”
　　李玄霸也停下脚步：“对吧？啊？哥，你使诈！”
　　李世民狞笑着扑上去，把弟弟按着捶：“这叫兵不厌诈，看拳！”
　　寒钩和乌镝在上空盘旋着交流。
　　妈又被首领揍了。
　　活该，谁让他今天又训我，喳喳喳！

Chapter 76: The Imperial Expedition Takes Three Months

Pei Shiju’s advice to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to present the golden eagle chicks was purely out of good intentions. If he didn’t currently fancy himself the teacher of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, he wouldn’t have bothered to meddle in such trivial matters.

Therefore, although Li Shimin and Li Xuanba felt a bit uncomfortable, they didn’t take it to heart. They even found a golden eagle chick for Pei Shiju to raise for his own amusement.

Pei Shiju was quite enthusiastic at first. But after being pecked by the bird while feeding it meat by hand, he gave up. The golden eagle was simply too fierce by nature; it was far more interesting to watch someone else raise them while he merely observed.

The chicks that Li Xuanba had hatched himself were exceptionally close to him and never pecked him. They did peck Li Shimin, but after Li Shimin fought them off with a thin wooden stick, the two chicks obediently accepted this "leader" who gave them meat and beat them up. They followed his commands with precision, behaving even better than they did for Li Xuanba.

When Li Xuanba gave them commands, the two little eagles would roll onto their backs and play dead—if there was no meat, there would be no learning.

Li Xuanba would scold the little eagles in anger. The little eagles would turn their heads and present their bird-behinds to him.

Li Shimin was shocked: "Han Gou and Wu Di are so smart! They even have little temper tantrums with you!"

Li Xuanba said, "Da Jin and Xiao Jin are indeed clever."

The brothers exchanged a glance.

Li Shimin said, "The names you chose are too perfunctory. Look at this slightly larger chick; the tip of its beak has a silver sheen, like a curved blade flashing with cold light. The smaller one has black tail feathers on its wings, like a dark arrow. Let’s call them Han Gou (Cold Hook) and Wu Di (Black Arrow)!"

Li Xuanba said, "Too much of a mouthful. Let’s just call them Da Jin and Xiao Jin."

Li Shimin said, "The eagle chicks I raised absolutely cannot have such perfunctory names! Right, Han Gou, Wu Di?"

The two eagle chicks ignored him.

Li Xuanba reached out: "Da Jin, Xiao Jin."

The two chicks turned their heads, then turned their little heads back, continuing to stick their backsides at Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba raised an eyebrow at Li Shimin.

Li Shimin said with dissatisfaction, "They are still young; it’s better they don’t understand the names you gave them. If you give them such stupid names now, how will they face people in the future? Hurry up and change them! There’s still time!"

Li Xuanba knew that his second brother, the future Tang Taizong and a famous lover of "Mary Sue" naming conventions, chose better names than he did. He was just habitually bickering with his second brother.

After the bickering, he taught the eagle chicks their new names.

Golden eagles are indeed smart, but these two were smart to a fault, especially in front of Li Xuanba. Golden eagles belong to the "falcon" family, ranking eighth in bird brain capacity studies by scientists, second only to the corvid family. They possess complete logical thinking, excellent memory, are particularly vengeful, can simply imitate human actions, and can use simple tools.

However, intelligence needs to grow alongside the body. Even humans are "mentally disabled" at birth, possessing only animal instincts. For these two chicks to be this emotional less than a month after birth meant their IQs were too high.

After some thought, Li Xuanba guessed it might be due to the stimulation from his spiritual energy. He had been keeping his spiritual energy "broadcast" constantly. This amount of spiritual energy was nothing more than an itch to a human, but for the fragile little eagle chicks, it might have been too much stimulation. After all, even an adult golden eagle’s intelligence is far inferior to a human’s. If their intelligence and obedience could reach that of a seven or eight-year-old child, they would essentially be monsters.

Li Xuanba had wanted to try raising other animals, but remembering their short lifespans—if he carefully cultivated a very smart animal only to say goodbye in ten or twenty years—he abandoned the idea. The average lifespan of a captive golden eagle is forty years. Even if the chicks died at that average, he would already be fifty. Given his own physical state, he didn’t know who would be burying whom. It was better to just raise the eagles.

Li Xuanba stroked the heads of the two chicks: "I’ll change your names later. Da Jin will be called Han Gou, and Xiao Jin will be called Wu Di."

The two chicks turned their heads toward Li Xuanba, bewildered; they didn’t understand his words. But as long as he changed the names during feeding time, these clever little eagles would surely remember their names.

When they grew a bit older, should he teach them arithmetic? If he taught them arithmetic, would they become even naughtier?

Li Xuanba stroked the chicks' feathers, his mind wandering.

Han Gou allowed Li Xuanba to stroke him obediently. Wu Di’s eyes darted around, then it stuck its rear end up and fired a shot of bird droppings, hitting Li Xuanba’s finger squarely.

"Chirp, chirp, chirp!" Wu Di hopped and skipped away toward Li Shimin.

Li Xuanba pulled out a handkerchief to wipe the bird droppings off his hand, sneering: "No meat for you today!"

Li Shimin shielded Wu Di with both hands: "Wu Di is still small, how can it go without meat? Don’t be angry, don’t be angry. It was only born recently; it must have been unintentional."

Li Xuanba scolded: "You saw it spray bird droppings at me, and you still say it was unintentional?!"

Li Shimin insisted: "Yes! It was unintentional!"

Li Xuanba said: "If you spoil them like this now, how will they hunt in the future?"

Li Shimin said: "I’ll find the strictest falconer later! I know that spoiling a child is like killing them, but as long as I don’t see it, it’s not a problem!"

Li Xuanba was so angry he laughed. He finally understood why his second brother’s sons would grow up to be such disasters. On one hand, he spoiled his children until they were psychologically fragile, and on the other, he let others put immense pressure on children who had already been spoiled into giant babies—it would be a miracle if anyone raised like that turned out mentally normal!

Li Xuanba tried to earnestly lecture his second brother on his incorrect way of raising eagles. But how could Li Shimin win an argument against Li Xuanba? He couldn’t even win against Wei Zheng.

Thus, Li Shimin sheepishly gave up the lead in educating the eagle chicks, acting only as an assistant to his younger brother, muttering on the side, "They really are still small, don’t be too strict."

Li Xuanba felt that his second brother was definitely the type of elder that young people in the future hated most when raising children. You’re trying to teach the child, and he’s right there saying, "Oh, let it go, let it go."

Fortunately, the eagle chicks couldn’t understand complex human speech, otherwise, they would surely become "useless eagles."

Li Xuanba locked Wu Di away, letting it watch Han Gou eat meat, and only let it out after Han Gou finished.

"You, no meat." Li Xuanba pushed Wu Di’s head back.

Wu Di looked at Han Gou, then lowered its head and rubbed against Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba retracted his finger, put the two chicks back in their birdhouse, closed the door, and left.

Wu Di: "..."

Wu Di: QAQ.

"Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!"

Meat, meat, meat, meat! Where is my meat?! Waaaaah!

Li Shimin was peeking through the window. With his excellent eyesight, he saw that the little eagle’s head poking out of the hole in the birdhouse had its downy feathers soaked with tears.

He cried too.

Li Shimin was dragged away from the window by Li Xuanba, sobbing: "A-Xuan, you are so cruel."

Li Xuanba was expressionless: "Oh."

His crybaby second brother was truly beyond saving.

...

Golden eagle chicks grow slowly. By the time Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were eleven, the two chicks were just beginning to tear into raw meat by themselves.

When the ice on the Zhangye River had completely melted, the two chicks finally began to molt. Compared to their physical growth, their intelligence grew much faster. When they saw themselves losing feathers, the two chicks huddled in their nest, wailing in pain.

Li Xuanba said: "No different from you, Second Brother, when you first lost your baby teeth."

Li Shimin, who was still in the middle of losing his baby teeth, would still get red-eyed when he saw a tooth fall out, and would even name his teeth and bury them properly: "...Nonsense, I did not!"

Li Xuanba said: "We are about to have our voices change. Our throats will swell, our voices will become hoarse—commonly known as a 'duck voice'—and it will be particularly unpleasant. Will you cry when your voice changes too?"

Li Shimin gritted his teeth: "I will not!"

He turned and ran to find Sun Simiao, asking the physician if he was truly about to have his voice change, so he could prepare himself mentally. If you don’t treat your teeth well when they fall out, the ones that grow in later will be ugly. If you don’t protect your throat when your voice changes, will your voice become ugly too? He didn’t want to have a duck voice for the rest of his life!

After mocking his second brother, Li Xuanba collected the down feathers the chicks had shed, preparing to send them to Yuwen Zhu along with medicinal herbs and landscape paintings.

He had already finished carefully "chewing" on the "thesis" Yuwen Zhu had sent him and had asked Sun Simiao to "proofread" it. Sun Simiao said that all the prescriptions in the letters had been verified multiple times, contained no errors, and were very suitable for Li Xuanba.

The prescriptions were accurate, likely due to Yuwen Zhu’s prior accumulation of knowledge. However, none of these prescriptions contained medicinal herbs that conflicted with the illnesses Li Xuanba frequently suffered from; Yuwen Zhu had likely thoroughly studied all of his medical records.

*I wonder where Yuwen Zhu got my medical records,* Li Xuanba thought.

Li Xuanba had suffered from many illnesses since childhood. He couldn’t even remember what illnesses he had had; only Sun Simiao and the physicians retained by the manor remembered them all. Even though Li Xuanba couldn’t possibly develop romantic feelings for Yuwen Zhu given her age, he felt an indescribable complexity in his heart knowing that she had read all his medical records and compiled these prescriptions for him.

He was certainly touched.

Therefore, he put much more effort into preparing the gift for Yuwen Zhu this time. Although Yuwen Zhu would surely prefer the medicinal herbs and Sun Simiao’s new medical insights, the scenery beyond the Great Wall and the cute eagle chicks might better reflect his goodwill.

As the river ice thawed, the roads from Zhangye to Daxing and Luoyang became easy to travel again. Li Xuanba and Li Shimin sent letters and gifts to their family, fiancée, teacher, and friends, not forgetting to send a letter to the Emperor, the Crown Prince, and the Prince of Qi.

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin wrote about the eagle chicks in their letter to the Emperor, saying that they lived and ate with the chicks, learning in advance how to raise children. Since they had written as much, Yang Guang, with his pride, wouldn’t bother competing with children over two golden eagles. When the time came, they would teach the eagles to act like idiots in front of Yang Guang, and the chicks would be safe.

When the Zhangye River thawed, Yang Guang sent off Qimin Khan, who had been sponging off meals in Luoyang, and began his western expedition. Qimin Khan had stood up the Sui army, but Yang Guang didn’t blame him, believing the Khan’s nonsense that "I was just late because the weather was too cold, I didn’t expect General Xue to move so fast." He even received Qimin Khan more grandly than before, with even more generous rewards.

Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Xue Daoheng huddled around a hotpot in a lonely pavilion in the snow, dismissing all their servants, and whispered their complaints: If the Emperor gave his courtiers one-tenth of the tolerance and generous treatment he gave Qimin Khan, he would be a benevolent ruler.

The hotpot recipe had been a gift from Li Xuanba. The three old men loved it and would gather to eat it every few days.

In mid-February, Yang Guang arrived in Daxing. On the second day of the third month, Yang Guang reached the west of the Yellow River. On the twenty-seventh of the fourth month, long after the start of summer and nearing the Grain Buds solar term, Yang Guang finally exited Linjin Pass, crossed the Yellow River, and arrived in Xiping Commandery.

Pei Shiju had been sending people to scout for news of the Tuyuhun Khan, hoping to demonstrate his worth the moment the Emperor arrived. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were also able to keep track of the Tuyuhun Khan’s situation.

At the end of the second month, the Tuyuhun Khan learned that the Emperor of Great Sui was going to lead the expedition in person. He began to deploy troops, build fortresses, and stockpile grain.

The entire third month passed, and even though it was already the start of summer, there was no sign of the powerful Sui army that could blitz the Yiwu Kingdom. The Tuyuhun Khan led his army to plunder the cattle and sheep of surrounding nomadic tribes that had grown fat on spring and summer grass, and also lassoed many sturdy wild horses on the steppe.

The entire fourth month passed, and the Sui army still hadn’t moved. The Tuyuhun Khan sent men back to fortify several of the most solid cities in the territories he had originally lost.

As the weather grew hotter and transportation became more convenient, the intervals at which Pei Shiju received news of the Tuyuhun Khan grew shorter. Li Shimin also became more silent with each passing day.

When Yang Guang finally arrived in Xiping Commandery—the place where Duke of Xu, Yuwen Shu, had arrived the previous August—Li Shimin asked Li Xuanba, or perhaps asked himself: "Why is the Emperor so slow? The Tuyuhun Khan is far from the Great Sui; it took him a month to learn of the Sui army’s movements, and he still managed to make two full months of preparations!"

Li Xuanba said: "Because the Emperor is traveling in his luxurious Guanfeng Palace, bringing concubines and palace maids, having musicians and entertainers accompany him with music all the way, and having officials and commoners along the way line the roads to welcome him and offer delicacies. He is eating, drinking, and playing all the way, so he is slow."

Li Shimin clenched his fists, his eyes red, though he didn’t shed tears this time.

Li Xuanba lay on the grass, looking up at Han Gou and Wu Di circling in the low sky. The little eagle chicks could already catch rabbits for him and his second brother, but Emperor Yang of Sui’s imperial expedition carriage hadn’t even arrived yet.

Looking through history, looking across the world, how many emperors or kings have led an expedition in person while riding in a luxurious mobile home, bringing concubines, palace maids, musicians, and entertainers?

The "flamboyance" of Tang Taizong’s expedition to Goguryeo recorded in history books was him personally leading ten thousand glittering armored cavalry to meet Li Ji under the walls of Liaodong City. Even the "God of Donkey Carts" Song Taizong and the "Gate-Calling Emperor" Ming Yingzong didn’t bring concubines and palace maids when they led expeditions in person.

*Is this a war, Your Majesty?*

*This is a war, Your Majesty!*

This imperial expedition was only mentioned in a few lines in the history books, and it was even considered one of Emperor Yang of Sui’s rare highlights—it wasn’t even described as one of his "evil policies," but rather evaluated positively.

Li Xuanba viewed this world habitually from the perspective of an onlooker, emotionally detached and very calm. This time, he was still amused by Yang Guang’s imperial expedition. That they could still win was simply because the Great Sui was too strong and the Tuyuhun were too weak. Oh, right, the Tuyuhun had been destroyed in a month the previous year; they were already pathetic. Now, after half a year of recovery, they actually showed signs of restoring their nation—that was the truly bizarre part.

Li Shimin loosened his fists, fell backward, and lay on the grass too: "No wonder the Great Sui will perish in seven years."

Li Xuanba said: "So stop being angry. You’re already furious during the Great Sui’s peak period. When he invades Goguryeo, won’t you be angry enough to get sick?"

Li Shimin turned his head, expressionless: "He’s going to invade Goguryeo, three times? Just Goguryeo?"

Li Xuanba said: "Not only will he invade Goguryeo three times, he will also 'gift' them a massive amount of weapons and armor, making it so that when you personally invade Goguryeo, you win the battles but lose the strategy."

Li Shimin couldn’t believe it: "Huh? What does 'win the battles but lose the strategy' mean... I get it. Although I won all my battles against Goguryeo, the cost was too high, the gains didn’t justify the losses, and continuing the war would damage the national strength and the people, so I withdrew without destroying Goguryeo?"

Li Xuanba said: "Yes. You set out in February, fought for seven months, occupied over a dozen cities, killed or captured over a hundred thousand Goguryeo soldiers, seized countless horses, weapons, and armor, and then in September, when the weather turned cold and grain was hard to transport, you withdrew. Then you beat your chest and stamped your feet, calling it a 'great failure.' Later generations even thought the Great Tang had been defeated and suffered heavy losses."

Under his clickbait articles, even some Taizong fans would sigh and lament that Tang Taizong shouldn’t have invaded Goguryeo, that he had suffered a defeat and heavy losses, just like Yang Guang’s invasion of Goguryeo. He, a Taizong-hater, was amused and liked every one of them. It wasn’t their fault. Tang Taizong himself had cried, "I lost, I lost," and even missed Wei Zheng because of it, re-erecting the merit monument for Wei Zheng that he had previously torn down. How could he blame others for misunderstanding?

Li Shimin said with disdain: "Tsk. If you don’t succeed once, rest and recuperate for a few years, then fight again."

Li Xuanba said: "Exactly. After you went back, you built the Great Tang navy in a short time, opened up maritime transport lines, prepared to advance by sea and land, and continuously harassed Goguryeo so they couldn’t rest, making all the necessary preparations. And then..."

Li Shimin covered his ears: "I’m not listening."

Li Xuanba: *[And then you died, hahahahahaha! Your life’s final imperial expedition turned into 'I have failed,' hahahahahaha!]*

Li Shimin scrambled up, raised his fist, and smashed it down toward his younger brother.

Li Xuanba quickly rolled away to dodge his second brother and grabbed a handful of dirt, sprinkling it into his second brother’s face.

Li Shimin closed his eyes and spat out dirt: "Pfft, pfft, pfft... Stop right there!"

Li Xuanba laughed and ran away: "Hahahahaha!"

Li Shimin chased after him: "Li Xuanba! Stop!"

Li Xuanba ran with all his might: "Li Shimin, I won’t stop! It’s your own mistake, why are you blaming me?"

Li Shimin cursed: "Bullshit! What does it have to do with me!"

Li Xuanba mocked: "If it has nothing to do with you, why are you so ashamed and angry?"

Li Shimin stopped: "Oh, right."

Li Xuanba also stopped: "Right? Huh? Brother, you cheated!"

Li Shimin grinned and pounced on him, pinning his younger brother down and pummeling him: "This is called 'all is fair in war,' take that!"

Han Gou and Wu Di circled overhead, communicating.

*Mom got beaten by the leader again.*

*Serves him right, who told him to lecture me again today, chirp, chirp, chirp!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第77章 吐谷浑再次败逃
chunks.chineseText:
第77章 吐谷浑再次败逃

=
　　李世民和李玄霸在草原上训练雕崽的时候， 杨广虽然到达了西平郡，但仍旧没有立刻出兵。
　　他先为大隋将士讲习武事。
　　大隋的皇帝在高台上口若悬河，大隋将士在高台下强装认真地聆听。
　　杨广从习武骑射之事， 讲到各种兵法和阵法。
　　他讲得滔滔不绝， 仿佛所有战略都在预料之中。
　　大隋的将军咬了一下舌头， 强迫自己把哈欠压下去。
　　给大隋全军挨次讲习了自己的武事心得后，杨广又在拔延山围猎。
　　他将整个拔延山都圈了起来，让大隋将士以围猎来炫耀武力。
　　这些全部折腾完时， 杨广才继续前进。
　　当大隋的军队终于得到杨广的允许朝吐谷浑可汗进攻的时候，已经是五月底了。
　　吐谷浑可汗又多了一个月的休整时间。
　　五月底已经是盛夏，就是在张掖也十分炎热。
　　李玄霸在寒冷的冬季没有生大病， 盛夏时却烧了两日。
　　他退烧后，又一直咳嗽。哪怕是盛夏， 下雨时他仍旧需要穿上较为厚重的长袍， 否则咳嗽就会加重。
　　因李玄霸生病，李世民的注意力终于从杨广那无法理解的战争安排中转移。
　　讲习武事和大型围猎确实是炫耀武力的好方式。但现在是打仗呢！有那个时间弄这些虚的，直接命令大隋将军出战不是更好？
　　许国公宇文述算是大隋水准较差的将领了，都能打得吐谷浑可汗丢盔弃甲。杨广只需要随便派出个有带兵经验的将领，然后就在后方坐等将领自行发挥就行了。
　　就算吐谷浑太弱， 给他半年时间休整也不会掀起多少水花。但大军出征每天都会耗费大量粮草，还有无数百姓离开家乡在军中服徭役。白白浪费的这半年的时间， 每一天有多少百姓因此家破人亡？
　　可现在还是大隋的天下，隋朝皇帝不在乎，唐国公府的两个少年郎在乎也没用。
　　他们继续学习， 养雕， 等着皇帝带着隋朝的大军到来。
　　杨广本以为以去年吐谷浑拉跨至极的战斗水准， 自己随便派支军队就能把他们灭了。
　　大隋的将军们也是如此想。
　　宇文述这个庸才都能轻松获胜， 杨广麾下有许多参与灭陈之战的老将，战功不是手到擒来？
　　这种轻敌下，右屯卫大将军张定和最先付出了生命的代价。
　　张定和是隋文帝时期的名将，出身贫寒，全靠在战场拼杀得到了如今的地位。
　　他孤军冒进，死在了吐谷浑的乱箭下。
　　紧接着左光禄大夫梁默也战败身亡。
　　梁默也是隋文帝时期的名将，曾跟随杨素北征突厥，又平定汉王杨谅的叛乱。
　　他被以逸待劳的吐谷浑可汗伏允击败，力战而亡。
　　一个去年就已经灭国的吐谷浑，让两位名将折戟。战亡的中低层将领和不配有名字的普通士兵，更是染红了覆袁川的水。
　　但吐谷浑面对正处于强盛时期的大隋，胜迹只是昙花一现。很快，大隋就大军压上，吐谷浑可汗伏允再次败逃，并且再次逃掉了。
　　六月，杨广宣布此战大获全胜。
　　他继续西行，要到张掖召见西域众国王，以此大胜来宣扬大隋的强大，令外夷臣服。
　　此时李玄霸的咳嗽终于好了不少，只有在下雨的时候才会喉咙发痒。
　　李世民也有心情继续关注战况了。
　　当李世民听到吐谷浑可汗伏允再次逃走，杨广宣布此战大获全胜时，问李玄霸道：“这样的结果和去年八月有区别吗？伏允未死，吐谷浑就不算消亡。”
　　李玄霸吃完炖梨汤润了嗓子后，才慢悠悠道：“有区别。去年的大胜不属于陛下亲征，今年的大胜属于陛下御驾亲征。”
　　李世民深深叹了口气，不再提此事。
　　在大隋看来，与吐谷浑之战已经结束了，该庆功了。
　　杨广兴致勃勃往张掖赶来，裴世矩已经联系了高昌等二十多个国家的国王和使臣，拜见大隋的天子。
　　李玄霸病好之后，也跟着裴世矩做了一些接待使臣的工作，与使臣们混了个脸熟。
　　因李玄霸记忆力超群，学习语言的速度极快。裴世矩询问过他的身体状况后，就将普通的接待事务全部交给了李玄霸。
　　李世民学语言的速度没有弟弟那么快，就佩刀跟在弟弟身边充当护卫，顺便听弟弟用心声帮他翻译对话。
　　使臣很喜爱能说他们语言的李玄霸，感到了被尊重。
　　后来一件事，让他们对李玄霸的喜爱变成了敬畏。
　　这一切都是因为乌镝这个雕孩子的错。
　　李世民这个“首领”训练寒钩和乌镝时，就像是将军训练他忠诚的士兵，哪怕是很危险、会受伤的动作，寒钩和乌镝也会照做。
　　李世民被李玄霸说服后，明白要经过磨砺才能成为雄鹰，如果一味宠溺只会变成一只会飞的胖鸡，所以狠下心来训练寒钩和乌镝。
　　待寒钩和乌镝受伤时，他连哭都躲着寒钩和乌镝，不在寒钩和乌镝面前损害自己身为首领的威严。
　　寒钩和乌镝越发敬畏李世民，哪怕现在它们的爪子已经能破开李世民的血肉，但小时候屡战屡败的经历让它们不敢挑衅李世民。李世民严厉地训练它们，它们的服从性更强了。
　　但对李玄霸，这两只雕崽就不一样了。
　　比如同样是指挥两只雕崽穿过一棵茂密的大树俯冲，李世民下命令后，两只雕崽就像是不怕疼一样，狠狠砸断无数细小树枝。
　　李玄霸下了命令，寒钩还好，能照做，就是冲得过于慢，一边下降一边扒拉树枝，以免挡住自己。
　　乌镝这个从小就会和李玄霸对着干的雕孩子就不一样了。它就地一躺，肚子朝上，左滚右滚，凄厉哀嚎，好像李玄霸对它做了什么残忍事似的。
　　李玄霸就不明白了，他对两只雕崽就没有纵容宠溺过，为何好像两只雕崽一点都不怕他？
　　说不听话倒也不是，两只雕崽大部分时候都会听李玄霸的话。就是遇到累了困了馋了的时候，或者教学内容有难度的时候，两只雕崽就会一个偷懒一个耍赖，怎么训都没用。
　　李玄霸又大病了一场，没有经历和两只雕孩子斗智斗勇，干脆把雕崽的训练全推给了二哥。
　　等他病好之后，雕崽更加黏他，但也更加爱偷懒耍赖。
　　比如李玄霸叮嘱寒钩和乌镝，平时自己玩，不要暴露自己的聪明。
　　寒钩乖乖装蠢，要么在草原上玩，要么在家里睡觉。
　　乌镝：好啊，装蠢！
　　于是这只雕就自己穿上不会抓伤人的“鞋子”，落到李玄霸肩膀上吐舌头装智障鸟。
　　看看这只雕，它两眼又大又无神，身体是歪的，脑袋是斜的，一看就很不聪明。
　　每当李玄霸坐下与他人说话时，乌镝就顺势从李玄霸的肩膀滑到李玄霸的怀里。
　　李玄霸阻止过。
　　他让人把乌镝带走，乌镝很快又飞回来。
　　更可恶的是，李世民在一旁乐呵呵看笑话，完全不帮忙。
　　很快，使臣中就传言，唐国公府的李三郎君养了一只完全没有雕样的智障鸟，比大公鸡还温顺。
　　虽然温顺的智障雕没人想养，但看着智障雕和李玄霸如此亲近，他们开始传言李三郎被草原的神灵眷顾，草原的神灵才让李三郎帮忙养育一只被抛弃的智障草原精灵。
　　这话不是李玄霸自己传的。
　　李玄霸不知道这些使臣怎么脑补出来一连串神话故事。
　　还是这次换了一身草原贵族打扮来面圣的叶护解答了李玄霸的疑惑。
　　“你学语言太快了。”叶护扯着自己的毛皮领子道，“他们都被你的学识吓到，给你找了个神灵庇佑。唉，为什么一定要穿毛皮？我就不能穿丝绸吗？大热天的……”
　　李世民道：“没办法，陛下眼中的西域贵族一定要裹毛皮，且一定要留大胡子。噗……你的大胡子一留，老了至少二十岁！”
　　叶护摸着自己刚留的大胡子，苦着脸道：“络腮胡子真的很不好吃饭，油脂会进入胡子里，怎么都洗不干净。”
　　李世民道：“这个就要阿玄帮你了。阿玄，我们还有香皂液吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“有，都有。就等着这次西域诸国来拜见陛下，以一百倍的价格卖给他们。”
　　叶护好奇：“什么好东西，一百倍的价格都能卖出去？”
　　李玄霸无奈：“我开玩笑。最多给你们涨个四五倍。香皂在京城都是供不应求的金贵之物，真提价一百倍，你们就买不起了。”
　　李玄霸把香皂和皂液拿来，给叶护示范了一下用法。
　　叶护听了香皂和皂液的价格之后，道：“李三郎，就算一百倍也买得起，不就是一匹战马的价格。来来来，要不要与我合作，我给你香皂换马？”
　　李玄霸叹气：“如果我能做出足够多的香皂，我肯定愿意和你合作。现在的问题是我想卖，都没有足够多的香皂卖给别人。你去大兴城里问问就知道了，连勋贵世家都眼巴巴等着排队预订。”
　　叶护道：“你这么一说，我就更想要了。”
　　李玄霸把桌子上试用的香皂和皂液递给叶护：“这本来就是送你的，你拿着。”
　　叶护惊讶：“白送？”
　　李世民笑道：“你的战马不也是白送给我们？再贵重的东西，作为礼物，就只是一个心意而已。在我看来，这不过是洗手洗澡洗脸洗头的东西，有也行，没有也无所谓。只是因为难以做出来才贵重了些，本身价值其实还好。你随便用。下次见面再送给你一些。”
　　叶护很不自在。
　　他对大隋的贵族，想来是送礼求个关注。现在大隋贵族白送他贵重的东西，他真的不习惯。
　　所以他更珍惜这份友谊。
　　而要珍惜友谊，他就要学会在礼尚往来中“自在”。
　　叶护道：“好，既然是礼物，我就不推辞了。不过如果有余量，一定要让我帮忙卖。没有人比我更熟悉西域各国贵族的爱好，我一定能帮你卖到一百倍的价格！”
　　李世民笑道：“那好。等我们缺钱，你就帮我们卖东西。阿玄，你可要多做些稀罕的商品给叶护卖。”
　　李玄霸道：“放心。叶护，虽然你们自己的习俗不在意被人直呼其名，但在中原行走，你何不也给自己取个字？这样我才好把你介绍给不介意你身份的文人朋友。”
　　李世民给叶护解释了一下字和名的区别：“你除了可以叫我和阿玄李二李三，也能叫我们大雄大德。”
　　叶护道：“我们西域人常以汉名行走世间。我的名字正好像汉名，我便懒得改了。我在家里排行最末，按照汉人习惯，叫幼之如何？”
　　李玄霸道：“叶护，字幼之，一听就很有文化。来，我借你基本诗歌集，你好好背。”
　　李世民大笑：“对对对，取了汉名，还要学作诗。”
　　大胡子叶护捂脸苦笑：“饶了我吧。”
　　李世民架着叶护道：“不行，不能饶。学嘛，又不让你做多厉害的诗，能符合韵律就行。”
　　李玄霸道：“没事，我和二哥写诗的本事也一般，不会嘲笑你。”
　　叶护道：“你觉得我会相信你们吗？”
　　虽然这么说，叶护还是兴高采烈地收起了李世民和李玄霸送的书，比香皂更喜欢。
　　他接触了这么多中原人，怎么可能不对中原的诗歌心仪？
　　现在李世民和李玄霸要教他写诗，将来还要把文人朋友介绍给他，他激动还来不及。
　　交到这样的好朋友，他不知道无意间帮助了哪个神灵。
　　西域诸国的国王和使臣陆续到达了张掖。裴世矩也为杨广修缮了暂时居住的场所。
　　李世民和李玄霸等候杨广来，更等着陪着杨广的父亲带着家书过来。
　　杨广终于来了，带来了噩耗，太子重病。
　　“陛下准备穿越大斗拔谷时，太子从当地人那里探知大斗拔谷最近天气恶劣，气温极低，常有大风和降霰。太子殿下希望陛下能探明情况之后再前行。”
　　“但陛下不相信，说六月盛夏怎么可能气温低？不愿意耽误行程。”
　　“太子殿下跪在陛下帐篷前大半日，陛下仍旧一意孤行。”
　　“穿越大斗拔谷的时候，果然遇上了大风和降霰。还好太子让宫中女眷和将士带上了厚衣，给陛下和皇后也准备了暖手炉和毛皮大氅，且提前提醒过将领，所以勉强熬了过去。只……只冻死了一成的卫卒。”
　　李渊神情疲惫道：“但太子先因久跪而受寒，又在山谷中再次受寒……唉。”
　　李世民和李玄霸皆沉默。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 77: The Tuyuhun Defeated and Fleeing Again

While Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were training their eagle chicks on the grasslands, Yang Guang, though he had arrived in Xiping Commandery, still did not immediately launch his campaign.

Instead, he first lectured the Great Sui soldiers on the arts of war.

The Emperor of the Great Sui held court on a high platform, speaking with eloquent ease, while the soldiers below feigned rapt attention.

Yang Guang spoke on everything from martial arts and archery to various military strategies and formations.

He rambled on incessantly, as if every strategic outcome were already within his calculations.

A Great Sui general bit his tongue, forcing himself to suppress a yawn.

After lecturing the entire Sui army on his personal insights into warfare, Yang Guang proceeded to hold a grand hunt at Mount Bayan.

He cordoned off the entire mountain, forcing the soldiers to display their martial prowess through the hunt.

Only after all this posturing was finished did Yang Guang finally continue his advance.

By the time the Sui army finally received Yang Guang’s permission to attack the Tuyuhun Khan, it was already the end of May.

The Tuyuhun Khan had been granted another month of time to rest and reorganize.

By the end of May, it was already midsummer, and even in Zhangye, the heat was intense.

Li Xuanba had not fallen ill during the freezing winter, but he burned with fever for two days in the height of summer.

After his fever broke, he was left with a persistent cough. Even in midsummer, he had to wear heavier robes whenever it rained, or his coughing would worsen.

Because of Li Xuanba’s illness, Li Shimin’s attention finally shifted away from Yang Guang’s incomprehensible military arrangements.

Lecturing on warfare and holding massive hunts were indeed ways to show off military might, but they were currently at war! If they had the time for such empty displays, wouldn't it be better to simply order the generals to attack?

The Duke of Xu, Yuwen Shu, was considered a mediocre general by Great Sui standards, yet even he had been able to send the Tuyuhun Khan fleeing in disarray. Yang Guang only needed to dispatch any general with experience in leading troops and then sit back and let them handle the rest.

Even if the Tuyuhun were weak, giving them half a year to recover wouldn't change the outcome much. But a marching army consumed vast amounts of grain and fodder every day, and countless commoners had left their homes to serve as corvée laborers for the military. For every day of this wasted half-year, how many families were shattered?

But as it was still the era of the Great Sui, it mattered little that the Emperor didn't care, and even less that two young masters from the Duke of Tang’s estate did.

They continued their studies, raised their eagles, and waited for the Emperor to arrive with the Sui army.

Yang Guang had assumed that given the Tuyuhun’s abysmal combat performance the previous year, any army he sent could easily wipe them out.

The Sui generals thought the same.

If a mediocrity like Yuwen Shu could win easily, then surely the many veteran generals under Yang Guang who had participated in the conquest of Chen would find victory just as effortless?

Under this climate of overconfidence, the Right Tuntun Guard General, Zhang Dinghe, was the first to pay the price with his life.

Zhang Dinghe had been a famous general during the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui. Born into poverty, he had risen to his current position solely through his prowess on the battlefield.

He had pressed forward with an isolated force and died under a hail of Tuyuhun arrows.

Immediately afterward, the Left Guanglu Grand Master, Liang Mo, was also defeated and killed.

Liang Mo was another renowned general from Emperor Wen’s era, having followed Yang Su on the northern expedition against the Tujue and helped suppress the rebellion of Yang Liang, the Prince of Han.

He was defeated by the rested and prepared Tuyuhun Khan, Fuyun, and died fighting to the last.

The Tuyuhun, a nation that had been effectively destroyed the year before, had claimed the lives of two famous generals. The low-to-mid-ranking officers and the countless nameless common soldiers who fell in battle had stained the waters of the Fuyuan River red.

Yet, facing the Great Sui at the height of its power, the Tuyuhun’s victory was merely a flash in the pan. Soon, the massive Sui army bore down on them, and the Tuyuhun Khan, Fuyun, was defeated and fled once again—managing to escape yet again.

In June, Yang Guang announced a total victory in the campaign.

He continued his journey west, intending to summon the kings of the Western Regions to Zhangye to use this great victory to proclaim the might of the Great Sui and force the foreign barbarians into submission.

By this time, Li Xuanba’s cough had improved significantly, leaving him with only an itchy throat when it rained.

Li Shimin finally had the heart to pay attention to the war again.

When Li Shimin heard that the Tuyuhun Khan, Fuyun, had escaped again and that Yang Guang had declared a total victory, he asked Li Xuanba, "Is there any difference between this result and that of last August? If Fuyun is not dead, the Tuyuhun cannot be considered extinguished."

After Li Xuanba finished his stewed pear soup to soothe his throat, he said slowly, "There is a difference. Last year’s victory did not belong to the Emperor’s personal expedition; this year’s victory belongs to the Emperor’s imperial campaign."

Li Shimin sighed deeply and stopped mentioning the matter.

In the eyes of the Great Sui, the war with the Tuyuhun was over, and it was time to celebrate.

Yang Guang traveled toward Zhangye in high spirits, while Pei Shiju had already contacted the kings and envoys of over twenty nations, including Gaochang, to pay homage to the Son of Heaven of the Great Sui.

After Li Xuanba recovered, he assisted Pei Shiju with some of the reception duties, becoming a familiar face to the envoys.

Because Li Xuanba had an extraordinary memory and learned languages with incredible speed, Pei Shiju, after checking on his health, handed over all the routine reception tasks to him.

Li Shimin, whose speed at learning languages was not as fast as his younger brother’s, wore his saber and followed by his brother’s side as a guard, listening to his brother translate the conversations for him through their mental connection.

The envoys grew fond of Li Xuanba, who could speak their own languages, and felt respected.

Later, one incident turned their fondness for Li Xuanba into awe.

It was all the fault of the eagle chick, Wudi.

When Li Shimin, the "leader," trained Hanjou and Wudi, he did so like a general training loyal soldiers. Even for dangerous maneuvers that might cause injury, Hanjou and Wudi would comply.

After being persuaded by Li Xuanba, Li Shimin understood that only through tempering could they become mighty eagles; if he coddled them, they would only become fat, flightless chickens. Thus, he steeled his heart to train them strictly.

When Hanjou and Wudi were injured, he would even hide his tears from them, refusing to compromise his dignity as their leader in their presence.

Hanjou and Wudi grew increasingly in awe of Li Shimin. Even though their talons were now sharp enough to tear through Li Shimin’s flesh, the memory of their repeated failures during their youth kept them from challenging him. Because Li Shimin trained them so rigorously, their obedience was absolute.

But with Li Xuanba, the two eagle chicks were different.

For example, when commanded to dive through a dense tree, Li Shimin’s order would result in the two chicks ignoring the pain and smashing through countless small branches.

When Li Xuanba gave the order, Hanjou would comply, though it would dive slowly, pushing branches aside as it descended to avoid being hit.

Wudi, the chick that had been defying Li Xuanba since it was small, was different. It would simply lie down on its back, roll left and right, and let out a shrill, mournful cry, as if Li Xuanba were committing some unspeakable cruelty against it.

Li Xuanba couldn't understand it; he had never coddled or spoiled the two chicks, so why did they seem not to fear him at all?

It wasn't that they were disobedient—most of the time, they listened to Li Xuanba. But whenever they were tired, sleepy, hungry, or the training was difficult, one would slack off and the other would play the rogue, and no amount of training seemed to work.

Li Xuanba had fallen ill again and lacked the energy to engage in a battle of wits with the two eagle chicks, so he simply pushed all their training onto his second brother.

By the time he recovered, the chicks were even more clingy, but also even more prone to slacking off and acting out.

For instance, Li Xuanba had instructed Hanjou and Wudi to play on their own and not reveal their intelligence.

Hanjou obediently pretended to be dim-witted, either playing on the grass or sleeping at home.

Wudi: "Fine, I'll pretend to be stupid!"

And so, the eagle put on "shoes" that wouldn't scratch anyone, landed on Li Xuanba’s shoulder, and stuck out its tongue, acting like a bird with no brain.

Look at this eagle: its eyes were large and vacant, its body was crooked, and its head was tilted—it looked incredibly unintelligent.

Whenever Li Xuanba sat down to talk with others, Wudi would slide from his shoulder into his lap.

Li Xuanba had tried to stop it.

He would have someone take Wudi away, but the eagle would fly right back.

What was even more infuriating was that Li Shimin would stand by, chuckling at the spectacle, offering no help at all.

Soon, rumors spread among the envoys that the Third Young Master of the Duke of Tang’s estate kept a "dim-witted bird" that didn't look like an eagle at all and was more docile than a rooster.

Although no one wanted to keep a docile, dim-witted eagle, seeing how close it was to Li Xuanba, they began to whisper that the Third Young Master was favored by the spirits of the grasslands, and that the spirits had asked him to raise an abandoned, dim-witted grassland sprite.

Li Xuanba hadn't started these rumors himself.

He had no idea how these envoys had concocted such a series of myths.

It was Yehut, who had changed into the attire of a grassland noble to meet the Emperor, who finally cleared up Li Xuanba’s confusion.

"You learn languages too quickly," Yehut said, tugging at his fur collar. "They are all terrified by your knowledge and have found a god to protect you. Sigh, why must I wear fur? Can't I wear silk? It's so hot..."

Li Shimin said, "It can't be helped. In the Emperor’s eyes, a noble of the Western Regions must be wrapped in fur and sport a large beard. Pfft... once you grow that beard, you look at least twenty years older!"

Yehut touched his newly grown beard, his face pained. "A thick beard really makes it hard to eat. Grease gets into the hair, and it’s impossible to wash clean."

Li Shimin said, "For that, you’ll need Ah Xuan’s help. Ah Xuan, do we have any more soap liquid?"

Li Xuanba replied, "Yes, we do. I’m just waiting for the Western nations to pay homage to the Emperor so I can sell it to them at a hundred times the price."

Yehut asked curiously, "What kind of treasure is it that can be sold for a hundred times the price?"

Li Xuanba said helplessly, "I’m joking. At most, I’ll mark it up four or five times. Soap is a precious commodity in the capital that is always in short supply; if I really raised the price a hundred times, you wouldn't be able to afford it."

Li Xuanba brought out the soap and soap liquid to demonstrate how to use them.

After hearing the price of the soap and liquid, Yehut said, "Third Young Master Li, even a hundred times the price is affordable—isn't that just the price of a warhorse? Come, come, do you want to partner with me? I’ll trade horses for your soap."

Li Xuanba sighed, "If I could make enough soap, I would certainly be willing to partner with you. The problem is that even if I want to sell it, I don't have enough to go around. Just go ask around in Daxing City; even the noble families are waiting in line to place their orders."

Yehut said, "Now that you say that, I want it even more."

Li Xuanba handed the trial soap and liquid on the table to Yehut. "These were meant for you anyway; take them."

Yehut was surprised. "A gift?"

Li Shimin laughed, "Aren't your warhorses also gifts to us? No matter how precious an item is, as a gift, it is merely a gesture of goodwill. To me, these are just things for washing hands, bathing, and cleaning one's face and hair. It’s fine to have them, and it doesn't matter if you don't. They are only precious because they are difficult to make; their inherent value is actually quite modest. Use them as you like. I’ll give you some more next time we meet."

Yehut felt very uneasy.

He was used to sending gifts to Sui nobles to seek their attention. Now that a Sui noble was giving him something precious for free, he truly wasn't used to it.

Therefore, he cherished this friendship even more.

And to cherish the friendship, he had to learn to be "at ease" with the exchange of gifts.

Yehut said, "Fine, since it is a gift, I will not refuse. However, if you have any surplus, you must let me help you sell it. No one knows the preferences of the nobles of the Western Regions better than I do; I will definitely help you sell them for a hundred times the price!"

Li Shimin laughed, "That’s settled then. When we are short on money, you can help us sell our goods. Ah Xuan, you must make more rare items for Yehut to sell."

Li Xuanba said, "Don't worry. Yehut, although your own customs don't mind being addressed by your given name, why don't you take a courtesy name while traveling in the Central Plains? That way, I can introduce you to my literary friends who won't mind your status."

Li Shimin explained the difference between a given name and a courtesy name to Yehut: "Besides calling me and Ah Xuan 'Li Er' and 'Li San', you can also call us 'Daxiong' and 'Dade'."

Yehut said, "We people of the Western Regions often use Han names when traveling the world. My name happens to sound like a Han name, so I’m too lazy to change it. I am the youngest in my family; how about I go by 'Youzhi' according to Han customs?"

Li Xuanba said, "Yehut, courtesy name Youzhi—it sounds very cultured. Come, I’ll lend you some poetry collections; you must memorize them well."

Li Shimin laughed heartily, "Exactly, exactly! Once you have a Han name, you must learn to write poetry."

The bearded Yehut covered his face with a bitter smile, "Spare me, please."

Li Shimin grabbed Yehut by the shoulders, "No, I cannot spare you. Just learn it; I’m not asking you to write anything profound, just something that follows the rhythm."

Li Xuanba added, "It’s fine. My second brother and I are only average at writing poetry ourselves; we won't laugh at you."

Yehut said, "Do you really think I believe you?"

Despite saying this, Yehut happily tucked away the books Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had given him, liking them even more than the soap.

Having encountered so many people from the Central Plains, how could he not be enamored with their poetry?

Now that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were going to teach him to write poetry and introduce him to their literary friends in the future, he was beyond excited.

He didn't know which god he had inadvertently helped to be blessed with such good friends.

The kings and envoys of the Western nations arrived in Zhangye one after another. Pei Shiju also renovated temporary residences for Yang Guang.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba waited for Yang Guang to arrive, but they were waiting even more for their father, who was accompanying Yang Guang, to bring letters from home.

Yang Guang finally arrived, bringing with him grim news: the Crown Prince was gravely ill.

"When the Emperor prepared to cross the Great Douba Valley, the Crown Prince learned from the locals that the valley was experiencing severe weather, with extremely low temperatures, strong winds, and hail. The Crown Prince hoped the Emperor would investigate the situation before proceeding."

"But the Emperor did not believe him, asking how the temperature could be low in the height of summer, and refused to delay the journey."

"The Crown Prince knelt before the Emperor’s tent for most of the day, but the Emperor remained obstinate."

"When they crossed the Great Douba Valley, they indeed encountered strong winds and hail. Fortunately, the Crown Prince had ordered the palace women and soldiers to bring thick clothing, and had prepared hand-warmers and fur cloaks for the Emperor and Empress. He had also warned the generals in advance, so they barely managed to survive. Only... only ten percent of the guards froze to death."

Li Yuan said, his expression weary, "But the Crown Prince had already caught a chill from kneeling for so long, and then caught another in the valley... alas."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba both fell silent.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第78章 大隋极盛时阖眼
chunks.chineseText:
第78章 大隋极盛时阖眼

=
　　这一路上， 李渊也遭了很大的罪。
　　他跟着其他老将上战场混功勋，面临箭雨都没受这么大的罪。
　　虽然太子提前做了准备，但大风和降霰让能见度变得极低， 李渊差点迷路， 好不容易找回了大部队。
　　大部分冻死的卫卒都是死在了迷路中。
　　李渊很庆幸， 这次李建成没有跟着过来。
　　李渊简略地和两个儿子说了几句，告诉了两个儿子太子的情况后，衣服都没换， 澡也没洗，倒头就睡，很快就响起了鼾声。
　　李世民和李玄霸指挥着仆人为李渊更衣脱靴， 李渊鼾声都未停，酣睡不醒。
　　两人离开后， 李玄霸抱着寒钩梳理羽毛， 表情很沉重。
　　乌镝不断用脑袋顶李玄霸，李玄霸也不言语。
　　李世民虽然心里也很沉重，但还是开玩笑逗弟弟：“你怎么这么难过？原来你和太子感情这么好啊。”
　　李玄霸沉默了许久。待乌镝把寒钩从李玄霸怀里挤了下去，用雕头顶他下巴的时候，李玄霸才在心中开口。
　　【史书大多是几百年后才书写。在书写的时候， 前人资料可能已经在战火中遗失，所以史书中的事件不一定准确。史书中唯一肯定的事， 大概只有历史人物盖棺论定的评价。】
　　李世民知道李玄霸口中的“史书”就是“天书”。
　　他道：“这件事你不是早就知道吗？预言当不得真。而且就算预言是真的，我们这些知道预言的人行为改变，未来也不确定了。为何你今日会想这个？”
　　李玄霸一只手捏住乌镝作怪的雕头， 一只手安抚趴在自己身边委屈“唧唧”的寒钩。
　　【《资治通鉴》言， 七月入秋时， 隋炀帝车驾自张掖东还， 行经大斗拔谷时，遇到风雪晦冥，冻死士卒过半，马驴十之八九。】
　　【我知道此事，原本打算等太子和父亲来了张掖后告诉他们。来了张掖，我才能得知大斗拔谷的天气多变。】
　　【二哥，如果父亲死在这场风雪中，你会不会怪……】
　　李世民使劲拍了一下李玄霸的脑袋。
　　李玄霸双手捂头：“哎哟。”
　　李世民皱眉道：“这天气是你唤来的？强行行军是你安排的？你当你哥我是不讲理的人吗？你愿意把你知道未来的事告诉二哥，不就是因为信任我吗？”
　　李玄霸低头：“唉。我知道，只是偶尔也会胡思乱想。”
　　李世民道：“你没有告诉太子和父亲此事，但太子仍旧发现了大斗拔谷的天气异常，并告知了陛下。太子跪在陛下帐篷前大半日都没有改变陛下的决定，你提前告知了陛下和父亲有何用处？”
　　李玄霸想了想，道：“用处是我努力过了，就算以后这件事仍旧发生，我不背锅。”
　　李世民：“……”有点不想安慰坏弟弟了。
　　李世民道：“现在这件事你也不背锅。和你没关系。”
　　李玄霸再次叹了口气。
　　还好李渊没事。
　　现在李渊不能死。他若死了，李建成就是唐国公。
　　隋朝败亡得太快了，那时他和二哥还太小了，不可能开府有私兵。若李建成成了唐国公，他现在手中的产业都保不住。
　　而且李玄霸不得不承认，从他本心而言，他也不希望李渊死。
　　他前世的父母太垃圾了，比李渊垃圾多了。那时他也没希望过父母死。
　　李世民又拍了拍弟弟的脑袋，道：“太子只是病了，不一定有事。”
　　李玄霸道：“我真的没有担心太子。”
　　李世民道：“好好，你没担心。你先静一静，明日我们再去探望太子。”
　　他把李玄霸怀里捣乱的乌镝抱起来，唤了还在委屈的寒钩一声。
　　乌镝乖乖被李世民夹在胳膊窝里。寒钩像一只走地鸡一样收着翅膀，跟在李世民身后摇摇晃晃踱步离开书房。
　　李玄霸往后一倒，躺在坐榻上叹气。
　　他闭上眼，回忆这部分记载，终于翻看到了这一段记载失实的原因。
　　司马光在《资治通鉴考异》中提到过这段记载。在《帝纪》中，此事发生在六月初八，杨广去往张掖途中。
　　但他认为就算西边再寒冷，六月盛夏也不可能下雪冻死人畜，所以怀疑记载失误，其实是杨广在从张掖回大兴时原路返回，再次经过大斗拔谷时冻死的人。那时已经七月入秋，更可能出现冻死人的事。
　　于是他在《资治通鉴》中就采取了此事发生在七月的史料。
　　宋朝人一辈子对西北都只能靠想象，司马光不知道大斗拔谷海拔四千米左右，不知道山中的风霰不是风雪，而是夹杂着冰粒的冻雨。
　　杨广也不知道西北的山底是炎夏，山上是寒冬。他身边的卫卒和宫女穿的还是单薄的夏装。
　　在四千米的高山上，盛夏遇到极端天气是真的能冻死人的。
　　杨广虽上山时衣着单薄，但他行宫般的房车里有足够的衣物和炭火、食物。别说风霰，就是遇上真正的暴风雪，他也死不了。
　　只是卫卒冻死大半而已。
　　在太子的劝告和预防下，这次只死了一成人。
　　但杨广并不开心。
　　他不知道原本自己带来的卫卒会冻死大半。他只知道自己没有听太子的劝告，导致卫卒冻死了一成，太子和他带来的许多妃嫔、公主都受寒生病。
　　杨广身为皇帝是不能错的。
　　当时他不听太子的劝告也是因为“皇帝不能错”这个原因。
　　汉朝的天人感应虽然现在已经不是王朝主导思想，但相信的人也很多。
　　如果遇到不可能出现的极端灾害天气，比如盛夏飘雪，那一定是因为皇帝无道。
　　杨昭对杨广进言，当地人说大斗拔谷可能会出现大风降霰时，杨广第一反应是有人妖言惑众，要杀掉妖言惑众的人。
　　盛夏怎么可能出现大风和降霰？又怎么会刚好在他穿越大斗拔谷的时候出现大风和降霰？
　　这件事在杨广脑海中不是“天气问题”，而是“政治问题”，是打击他声望的“阴谋”。
　　退一步说，就算真的出现了大风和降霰，他也必须穿越大斗拔谷，以彰显他的无所畏惧。
　　看到杨广因为遭遇风霰而震怒，虞世基在与卧病在床的太子杨昭聊过几次之后，对杨广道：“此次盛夏降霰，定有妖孽作祟。幸亏太子窥得先机早做准备，陛下携大隋君威冲破妖孽封锁，才护得我们大隋军队安然无恙。”
　　杨广闻言大喜：“虞卿所言是极！”
　　于是杨广召集巫者来给太子和妃嫔、公主看病。巫者说是杨勇的鬼魂作祟。风霰是杨勇干的，太子和其他妃嫔、公主的生病也是杨勇干的。
　　李玄霸去探望杨昭时，听杨昭说起此事。
　　杨昭沉沉地叹了口气：“吐谷浑可汗拼死一搏，召集族中巫师阻拦大隋皇帝御驾亲征的借口，不是更好吗？”
　　他让虞世基进言时，选的就是这个借口。但他的父皇没有用自己选好的借口，而是把已经死了很多年的伯父拿来当挡箭牌。
　　李玄霸道：“或许陛下不仅仅是找借口，对有鬼魂作祟之事也是半信半疑。”
　　杨昭重重咳了几声，声音仿佛要把心肺都咳出来。
　　他惨然笑道：“也是，父皇可能真的以为是鬼魂作祟。他仍旧不信当地人的话，西北的高山，在盛夏真的会很冷。”
　　李玄霸道：“表兄，别忧虑了。好好休息。”
　　李世民道：“是啊，表兄，你会好起来的。”
　　杨昭摇了摇头，又重重咳了几声。
　　他用手帕捂住嘴，手帕上陈血新血层层晕染，暗红鲜红的色块相叠，好像被夕阳映红的石头。
　　李玄霸看着手帕上的血迹，放在膝盖上的手指微微曲起。
　　肺部毛细血管破裂才会咳出血来，这就已经是重度肺炎了。
　　“我的身体我自己知道。到这时我才后悔没听大德的劝留守京城。”杨昭擦干嘴边的血迹后，似乎舒服了一些，说话连贯了一些，“不过现在说这些也晚了。两位表弟，表兄求你们一件事。”
　　李世民和李玄霸对视一眼。
　　李世民道：“表兄请说，如果是我们能做到，又不损害我们利益的事，我们一定做。”
　　杨昭笑道：“你们真实诚，半点虚话都不说。不过正因为如此，我才放心。我希望你们能好好劝导阿孩，尽可能让阿孩在我的儿子长大前成为太子。”
　　李世民和李玄霸略微有点惊讶。但细思之后，他们明白了杨昭请求的原因。
　　杨昭自己也紧接着说出原因。
　　“父皇偏爱我的庶长子杨倓。以父皇凡事都爱随心所欲的态度，说不定会想越过诸子立杨倓为太子。”
　　“阿孩已经年过弱冠，在朝中颇有权势，我若熬不过这次，他就是父皇嫡长子；三弟虽只有两岁，但待倓儿长大时他也已经长大，身为皇子，他不可能不对皇位有期望。”
　　“倓儿不仅辈分上差阿孩和三弟一代，就是平辈之中，他的弟弟侑儿才是嫡长。且侑儿之母出身京兆韦氏，有母家支持。倓儿之母不仅已经亡故，还只是良家女。”
　　“父皇也是疼爱阿孩的。只是阿孩性格和父皇类似，也是个随心所欲的人。他若只当个皇子还好，若成为储君，父皇一定不能容忍阿孩过于张扬的性格。”
　　杨昭两眼微微放空，眼前仿佛出现了弟弟和儿子们的模样。
　　“请你们告诉阿孩，储君天生分君王一半权势，所以一定要谨慎低调，不能让君王感到威胁。切记切记，只有如此，他才能坐稳储君之位。”
　　“若阿孩在我的孩子们和三弟之前就被封为储君，我的孩子们和三弟只要不谋反，他们的性命就都保住了。”
　　李世民和李玄霸听着杨昭这些本不应该让他们这两位“外人”听到的肺腑之言，一时心情过于复杂，很是沉闷。
　　他们都明白杨昭话语中的未尽之意。
　　若不是最理所当然该继承太子之位的杨暕当太子，那么杨昭的儿子就会与叔父残杀，还会自相残杀。
　　杨昭宁愿自己的孩子不当太子，只希望他们能平安终老。
　　李世民低头不语。
　　太子算尽了一切，万万没算到他的父皇会在短短十五年，就让正处于强盛期的大隋轰然崩塌。
　　无论是他的弟弟，还是他的儿子，都还没来得及自相残杀，大隋就没了。
　　李玄霸道：“能劝我们一定劝。”
　　李世民附和：“嗯。”
　　杨昭笑道：“有你们这句话就够了。如果实在是劝不住，你们还是保重自己，别卷入夺嫡之争。你们置身事外，身居高位，才可能帮我保住一丝血脉。倓儿、侗儿、侑儿中谁都行，庶人也好，流放也罢，只要活着就够了。”
　　杨昭在发现自己可能熬不过去的时候，就做好了自己血脉断绝的最坏预想。
　　只要他的父皇不让二弟按照常理补位成为太子，那么他的儿子一定会卷入夺嫡之争。按照伯父叔父们夺嫡的惨烈，输者肯定会被斩草除根。
　　他的儿子又太小了，就算夺嫡成功，大概率也是傀儡。那时说不定会有大隋代北周的事再次发生。
　　杨昭很聪慧，太聪慧。所以他对自己死后的未来很绝望。
　　李玄霸道：“好，我答应你。若真出现了你担忧的事，我会尽全力至少保下你一个血脉，并争取让他富贵终老。”
　　李世民眉头一跳。
　　杨昭猛地撑坐起身：“你居然答应？”
　　李玄霸道：“表兄你都如此请求了，我必须答应。”
　　杨昭的眼睛闭上，眼泪从眼角溢出：“大德，表兄再次为以前错怪你道歉。”
　　他以为李玄霸和李世民能勉强答应，若情况允许就拉他血脉一把，就已经是极限。
　　他其实不止和李玄霸和李世民说了这件事。许多来探病的人，只要他信得过对方品行，都做出了托孤之事。
　　夺嫡之事牵连很重，谁占谁灭门。杨昭不信任何人会不顾自家安慰来救他的孩子，但为人父，他必须为孩子们做点什么。所以他只是广撒网，能求一个是一个。
　　所有听了他的托孤之话的人都含糊其词，有些人甚至连安慰的话都不敢说，只让他“宽心”，“病一定会好”。
　　唯独被他曾经误解为“擅钻营”“心思深沉”的表弟李玄霸，居然答应了他。
　　甚至李玄霸答应的还不是保住他的子嗣“活着”，而是“富贵终老”。
　　“表弟……”杨昭忍不住抱住李玄霸，呜咽哭了起来。
　　李玄霸努力地伸手拍杨昭难以拍到的背：“表兄你帮了我许多，这是我该做的。”
　　李玄霸：【给太子一个安慰吧。太子确实帮了我们很多忙。而且我们应该做得到承诺。】
　　李世民：“……嗯。”
　　杨昭哭着道：“谢谢，谢谢……”
　　李玄霸劝杨昭重新躺下，又与杨昭聊了几句后，才与李世民离开。
　　李玄霸和李世民离开后，杨昭长叹了一口气。
　　他唤来心腹：“将我今日床前之事告知父皇，一字不差地告知父皇。”
　　心腹担忧道：“连你担心夺嫡之事也告知父皇？”
　　杨昭咬牙道：“一同告知！”
　　他说完后，像是用尽所有的力气一般，声音微弱，几不可闻：“父皇，这是儿最后的劝谏了。”
　　“求你……求你一定要听啊……”
　　大业五年六月十七日，隋太子杨昭高烧晕厥，在一群巫者的驱邪声中病逝。
　　同日，隋朝皇帝杨广来到了燕支山，会见了西域共二十七国的国王和使臣。
　　杨广命令武威、张掖的贵族女性盛装打扮，夹道围观。郡县检查她们的衣服和车马，如果衣服和车马不华丽整齐就勒令更换。
　　西域国王和使臣佩金戴玉，载歌载舞，进献珍宝。
　　被杨广命令来观看此次会面的贵女的车驾堵塞了几十里路。西域国王和使臣看着没有戴冪离的贵女姣好的面容，和她们华美的衣服、车驾，纷纷夸赞大隋强盛。
　　当杨昭在痛苦中阖上双眼时，杨广正高兴地接下西域诸国国王和使臣进献的几千里土地。
　　李世民和李玄霸被杨广叫去随驾。但李玄霸恰好又病了，所以他们没有去现场，只是事后知道了这一场盛大的献地仪式。
　　“阿玄，那名义上献给大隋的几千里土地，有多少能真正落入大隋的口袋？”
　　“谁知道呢。总之，大隋的强盛，此刻就是顶点。”
　　“哦。”
　　“阿玄，太子表兄还好吗？我们离开时，太子表兄似乎病情还很稳定。他知道今日的事，一定会很高兴。说不定心情一好，身体也会好许多。”
　　“不知道。隔得老远，我哪知道？”
　　“唉。”
