Chapter 78: Closing Eyes at the Zenith of the Great Sui

The journey had been a grueling ordeal for Li Yuan.

He had fought alongside veteran generals on the battlefield and faced rains of arrows, yet he had never suffered as much as he did on this trek. Although the Crown Prince had made preparations in advance, the gale-force winds and falling sleet had reduced visibility to almost nothing. Li Yuan had nearly lost his way, and it was only through great effort that he managed to rejoin the main force.

Most of the soldiers who froze to death had perished while lost in the storm.

Li Yuan felt a profound sense of relief that Li Jiancheng had not accompanied them this time.

After briefly speaking with his two sons and informing them of the Crown Prince’s condition, Li Yuan didn't even bother to change his clothes or wash; he collapsed onto his bed and was snoring almost instantly.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba directed the servants to change Li Yuan’s clothes and remove his boots, but Li Yuan’s snoring never faltered; he remained in a deep, comatose slumber.

After the two brothers left, Li Xuanba held Han Gou, stroking its feathers with a heavy expression.

Wu Di kept nudging Li Xuanba with its head, but Li Xuanba remained silent.

Though Li Shimin’s heart was equally heavy, he tried to tease his younger brother to lighten the mood: "Why are you so upset? I never realized you and the Crown Prince were so close."

Li Xuanba remained silent for a long time. It was only after Wu Di nudged Han Gou out of Li Xuanba’s arms and began to nuzzle his chin with its eagle head that Li Xuanba spoke in his heart.

[Historical records are mostly written hundreds of years after the fact. By the time they are written, the primary sources may have already been lost to the fires of war, so the events described in history books are not necessarily accurate. The only thing in history books that can be considered certain is the final judgment passed upon historical figures once the lid of their coffin is sealed.]

Li Shimin knew that the "history books" Li Xuanba spoke of were the "Heavenly Books."

He said, "Haven't you known this for a long time? Prophecies cannot be taken as absolute truth. Besides, even if the prophecies were true, our actions—those of us who know them—have already changed, making the future uncertain. Why are you thinking about this today?"

Li Xuanba used one hand to pinch Wu Di’s mischievous eagle head, while the other hand comforted Han Gou, who was whimpering pitifully beside him.

[The *Zizhi Tongjian* states that in the seventh month, as autumn began, Emperor Yang of Sui returned east from Zhangye. While passing through Daduoba Valley, he encountered wind, snow, and darkness, causing over half of the soldiers to freeze to death, along with eighty to ninety percent of the horses and donkeys.]

[I knew of this event and originally intended to tell the Crown Prince and Father after they arrived in Zhangye. Only after arriving in Zhangye could I learn how volatile the weather in Daduoba Valley truly is.]

[Second Brother, if Father had died in this snowstorm, would you blame...]

Li Shimin gave Li Xuanba’s head a firm smack.

Li Xuanba covered his head with both hands: "Ouch."

Li Shimin frowned and said, "Did you summon this weather? Did you arrange the forced march? Do you think your brother is such an unreasonable person? You are willing to tell me about the future only because you trust me, aren't you?"

Li Xuanba lowered his head: "Sigh. I know, I just let my imagination run wild sometimes."

Li Shimin said, "You didn't tell the Crown Prince or Father about this, but the Crown Prince still discovered the abnormal weather in Daduoba Valley and informed His Majesty. The Crown Prince knelt before His Majesty’s tent for the better part of a day and couldn't change the Emperor’s decision. What use would it have been for you to tell them in advance?"

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and said, "The use is that I tried my best. Even if this happens in the future, I won't be the one to blame."

Li Shimin: "..." He suddenly didn't want to comfort his bratty younger brother anymore.

Li Shimin said, "You aren't to blame for this, either. It has nothing to do with you."

Li Xuanba sighed again.

It was fortunate that Li Yuan was unharmed.

Li Yuan could not die now. If he died, Li Jiancheng would become the Duke of Tang.

The Sui Dynasty was collapsing too quickly. At that time, he and his Second Brother would still be too young to establish their own households or maintain private troops. If Li Jiancheng became the Duke of Tang, the assets he currently held would be impossible to protect.

Moreover, Li Xuanba had to admit that, in his heart, he did not want Li Yuan to die.

His parents in his previous life were trash—far worse than Li Yuan. Even then, he had never wished for their deaths.

Li Shimin patted his younger brother’s head again and said, "The Crown Prince is only ill; he will likely be fine."

Li Xuanba said, "I really wasn't worried about the Crown Prince."

Li Shimin said, "Fine, fine, you weren't worried. Calm yourself for now; we will go visit the Crown Prince tomorrow."

He picked up the troublesome Wu Di from Li Xuanba’s arms and called out to the still-aggrieved Han Gou.

Wu Di obediently tucked itself under Li Shimin’s arm. Han Gou, wings tucked in like a walking chicken, followed behind Li Shimin, waddling out of the study.

Li Xuanba fell backward, lying on the couch and sighing.

He closed his eyes, recalling the records, and finally found the reason for the inaccuracies in this account.

Sima Guang had mentioned this record in his *Zizhi Tongjian Kaoyi*. In the *Imperial Annals*, this event occurred on the eighth day of the sixth month, while Yang Guang was on his way to Zhangye.

However, Sima Guang believed that no matter how cold the west was, it was impossible for it to snow and freeze people and livestock to death in the height of summer. Thus, he suspected the record was flawed, suggesting it was actually the people who froze to death when Yang Guang returned to Daxing from Zhangye, passing through Daduoba Valley again. By then, it was the seventh month and the start of autumn, making it more likely for such a tragedy to occur.

Consequently, he adopted the historical material stating the event happened in the seventh month for the *Zizhi Tongjian*.

People of the Song Dynasty could only imagine the Northwest their entire lives. Sima Guang did not know that Daduoba Valley was about 4,000 meters above sea level, nor did he know that the "wind and sleet" in the mountains were not snow, but freezing rain mixed with ice pellets.

Yang Guang also did not know that the foot of the Northwest mountains was in the heat of summer, while the peaks were in the dead of winter. The soldiers and palace maids around him were still wearing thin summer clothes.

On a 4,000-meter-high mountain, extreme weather in the height of summer could indeed freeze people to death.

Although Yang Guang was thinly dressed when he ascended the mountain, he had sufficient clothing, charcoal, and food in his palace-like carriage. Even without the sleet, he would not have died even if he had encountered a real blizzard.

It was only the soldiers who froze to death in large numbers.

Thanks to the Crown Prince’s warnings and precautions, only ten percent had died this time.

But Yang Guang was not happy.

He did not know that the soldiers he brought would have originally frozen to death in droves. He only knew that he had ignored the Crown Prince’s advice, leading to the death of ten percent of his soldiers, and that the Crown Prince and many of the concubines and princesses he brought had fallen ill from the cold.

As Emperor, Yang Guang could not be wrong.

At the time, he had ignored the Crown Prince’s advice precisely because "the Emperor cannot be wrong."

Although the Han Dynasty’s concept of "Heaven-Man Interaction" was no longer the dominant ideology of the dynasty, many still believed in it.

If an impossible, extreme disaster occurred, such as snow in the height of summer, it must be because the Emperor was devoid of virtue.

When Yang Zhao advised Yang Guang that the locals said Daduoba Valley might experience strong winds and sleet, Yang Guang’s first reaction was that someone was spreading heretical rumors to deceive the public, and he wanted to execute them.

How could there be strong winds and sleet in the height of summer? And how could it happen exactly when he was crossing Daduoba Valley?

In Yang Guang’s mind, this was not a "weather issue," but a "political issue"—a "conspiracy" to damage his reputation.

Even taking a step back, even if there really were strong winds and sleet, he had to cross Daduoba Valley to demonstrate his fearlessness.

Seeing Yang Guang enraged by the sleet, Yu Shiji, after speaking with the bedridden Crown Prince Yang Zhao several times, said to Yang Guang: "The sleet in the height of summer must be the work of evil spirits. Fortunately, the Crown Prince foresaw the danger and made preparations early. Your Majesty, with the might of the Great Sui, broke through the blockade of the evil spirits, thus protecting our Great Sui army from harm."

Yang Guang was overjoyed upon hearing this: "What Minister Yu says is absolutely correct!"

Thus, Yang Guang summoned shamans to treat the Crown Prince, the concubines, and the princesses. The shamans claimed that the ghost of Yang Yong was at work. The sleet was caused by Yang Yong, and the illnesses of the Crown Prince and the others were also the work of Yang Yong.

When Li Xuanba went to visit Yang Zhao, he heard Yang Zhao speak of this.

Yang Zhao sighed heavily: "Wouldn't it have been better to use the excuse that the Tuyuhun Khan was making a desperate struggle, summoning tribal shamans to block the Great Sui Emperor’s imperial expedition?"

He had chosen this excuse when he asked Yu Shiji to speak to the Emperor. But his Imperial Father did not use the excuse he had prepared, instead using his uncle, who had been dead for many years, as a scapegoat.

Li Xuanba said: "Perhaps His Majesty is not just looking for an excuse; he might be half-believing in the existence of ghosts."

Yang Zhao coughed heavily several times, his voice sounding as if he were coughing out his very heart and lungs.

He smiled miserably: "That is true. Father might really think it is the work of ghosts. He still does not believe the words of the locals—that the high mountains of the Northwest can be truly cold in the height of summer."

Li Xuanba said: "Cousin, do not worry. Rest well."

Li Shimin said: "Yes, Cousin, you will get better."

Yang Zhao shook his head and coughed heavily again.

He covered his mouth with a handkerchief. Layers of old and fresh blood stained the cloth, the dark red and bright red patches overlapping like stones reddened by the sunset.

Li Xuanba looked at the blood on the handkerchief, his fingers resting on his knees curling slightly.

Only a rupture of the pulmonary capillaries would cause one to cough up blood; this was already severe pneumonia.

"I know my own body. Only now do I regret not listening to Da De’s advice to stay behind in the capital." After Yang Zhao wiped the blood from his mouth, he seemed more comfortable and spoke more coherently. "But it is too late to say these things now. Two cousins, I have a request."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba exchanged a glance.

Li Shimin said: "Cousin, please speak. If it is something we can do without harming our own interests, we will certainly do it."

Yang Zhao laughed: "You are so honest, not speaking a word of falsehood. But it is precisely because of this that I feel at ease. I hope you can properly advise A-Hai, and do your best to ensure A-Hai becomes the Crown Prince before my sons grow up."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were slightly surprised. But after careful thought, they understood the reason for Yang Zhao’s request.

Yang Zhao immediately explained the reason himself.

"Father favors my eldest son by a concubine, Yang Tan. With Father’s tendency to do whatever he pleases, he might want to bypass his sons and name Yang Tan as Crown Prince."

"A-Hai has already reached adulthood and holds considerable power in the court. If I do not survive this, he will be Father’s eldest legitimate son. Although my third brother is only two years old, by the time Tan-er grows up, he will also be grown. As an imperial prince, it is impossible for him not to have expectations for the throne."

"Tan-er is not only a generation younger than A-Hai and my third brother, but even among his peers, his younger brother You-er is the eldest legitimate son. Moreover, You-er’s mother is from the Jingzhao Wei clan and has the support of her maternal family. Tan-er’s mother is not only deceased but was merely a woman of good standing."

"Father also loves A-Hai. But A-Hai’s personality is similar to Father’s—he is also a person who does as he pleases. If he were just an imperial prince, it would be fine, but if he becomes the heir apparent, Father will certainly not tolerate A-Hai’s overly flamboyant personality."

Yang Zhao’s eyes went slightly vacant, as if he could see his brother and sons before him.

"Please tell A-Hai that the heir apparent naturally shares half the power of the monarch, so he must be cautious and low-key; he must not make the monarch feel threatened. Remember, remember well—only by doing this can he sit securely on the throne of the heir apparent."

"If A-Hai is named heir before my children and my third brother, as long as my children and my third brother do not rebel, their lives will be preserved."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba listened to these heartfelt words, which were not meant for the ears of "outsiders" like them, and felt a complex, heavy weight in their hearts.

They both understood the unspoken meaning in Yang Zhao’s words.

If Yang Yi, who was the most logical choice for Crown Prince, did not become the heir, then Yang Zhao’s sons would be slaughtered by their uncle, and would eventually slaughter each other.

Yang Zhao would rather his own children not be Crown Prince, hoping only that they could live out their lives in peace.

Li Shimin lowered his head, silent.

The Crown Prince had calculated everything, but he had never calculated that his own father would cause the Great Sui, then at its peak, to collapse in a mere fifteen years.

Whether it was his brother or his sons, they would not even have the chance to kill each other before the Great Sui was gone.

Li Xuanba said: "We will certainly advise him if we can."

Li Shimin echoed: "Yes."

Yang Zhao smiled: "Having your word is enough. If you truly cannot persuade him, then take care of yourselves and do not get involved in the struggle for the throne. Only by staying out of it and holding high positions can you possibly help me preserve a sliver of my bloodline. Whether it is Tan-er, Dong-er, or You-er, it doesn't matter. Even if they become commoners or are exiled, as long as they are alive, that is enough."

When Yang Zhao realized he might not survive, he had prepared for the worst-case scenario: the extinction of his bloodline.

As long as his father did not follow convention and name his second brother as Crown Prince, his sons would inevitably be drawn into the struggle for the throne. Given the brutality of his uncles' own struggles for the throne, the losers would certainly be wiped out.

His sons were too young; even if they succeeded in taking the throne, they would likely be puppets. By then, perhaps something like the Northern Zhou being replaced by the Sui would happen again.

Yang Zhao was intelligent—too intelligent. That was why he felt such despair for the future after his death.

Li Xuanba said: "Very well, I promise you. If the situation you fear truly comes to pass, I will do my utmost to at least save one of your bloodline and ensure he lives a life of wealth and peace."

Li Shimin’s brow twitched.

Yang Zhao sat up abruptly: "You actually agree?"

Li Xuanba said: "Since you, Cousin, have requested it, I must agree."

Yang Zhao’s eyes closed, and tears spilled from the corners: "Da De, I apologize again for misunderstanding you in the past."

He had thought that if Li Xuanba and Li Shimin could barely agree to help his bloodline if circumstances permitted, that would already be the limit.

He had not only spoken to Li Xuanba and Li Shimin about this. Many who came to visit him, as long as he trusted their character, had been asked to look after his children.

The struggle for the throne was a heavy matter; whoever touched it would be wiped out. Yang Zhao did not believe anyone would risk their own family’s safety to save his children, but as a father, he had to do something for them. So he cast a wide net, hoping to find at least one person.

Everyone who heard his plea for his children had been vague, and some didn't even dare to offer comfort, only telling him to "set his mind at ease" and that "his illness would surely improve."

Only his cousin Li Xuanba, whom he had once misunderstood as "scheming" and "deep-thinking," had actually agreed to him.

And Li Xuanba had not just promised to keep his descendants "alive," but to ensure they lived a life of "wealth and peace."

"Cousin..." Yang Zhao could not help but embrace Li Xuanba, sobbing.

Li Xuanba tried his best to reach out and pat Yang Zhao’s back, which was difficult to reach: "Cousin, you have helped me a great deal; this is what I should do."

Li Xuanba: [Give the Crown Prince some comfort. The Crown Prince has indeed helped us a lot. And we should be able to fulfill the promise.]

Li Shimin: "...Yes."

Yang Zhao sobbed: "Thank you, thank you..."

Li Xuanba persuaded Yang Zhao to lie back down, and after chatting for a few more moments, he and Li Shimin left.

After Li Xuanba and Li Shimin left, Yang Zhao let out a long sigh.

He summoned his trusted aide: "Tell Father what happened at my bedside today, word for word."

The aide asked worriedly: "Even the part about you worrying about the struggle for the throne should be told to His Majesty?"

Yang Zhao gritted his teeth: "Tell him everything!"

After he finished speaking, as if he had exhausted all his strength, his voice was weak and barely audible: "Father, this is my final remonstrance."

"I beg you... I beg you, please listen..."

On the seventeenth day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Daye, the Sui Crown Prince Yang Zhao fell into a coma from a high fever and passed away amidst the exorcism chants of a group of shamans.

On the same day, the Sui Emperor Yang Guang arrived at Yanzhi Mountain to meet the kings and envoys of twenty-seven Western Regions nations.

Yang Guang ordered the noblewomen of Wuwei and Zhangye to dress in their finest attire and line the roads to watch. The commanderies inspected their clothes and carriages, and if they were not sufficiently magnificent or orderly, they were ordered to change.

The kings and envoys of the Western Regions wore gold and jade, sang and danced, and presented precious treasures.

The carriages of the noblewomen ordered by Yang Guang to watch the meeting blocked the road for dozens of miles. Seeing the beautiful faces of the noblewomen—who were not wearing veils—and their magnificent clothes and carriages, the kings and envoys of the Western Regions praised the strength of the Great Sui.

When Yang Zhao closed his eyes in agony, Yang Guang was happily accepting the thousands of miles of land presented by the kings and envoys of the Western Regions.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were called by Yang Guang to accompany the imperial procession. But Li Xuanba happened to fall ill again, so they did not go to the scene, only learning of the grand land-presentation ceremony afterward.

"A-Xuan, of those thousands of miles of land nominally presented to the Great Sui, how much can truly fall into the pockets of the Great Sui?"

"Who knows. In any case, the strength of the Great Sui is at its zenith right now."

"Oh."

"A-Xuan, is Cousin Crown Prince doing well? When we left, his condition seemed stable. If he knew about today’s events, he would surely be very happy. Perhaps if his mood improves, his health will improve as well."

"I don't know. We are so far away, how would I know?"

"Sigh."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第79章 灿阳下的纸钱雨
chunks.chineseText:
第79章 灿阳下的纸钱雨

=
　　太子病逝是大事， 消息第二日就传到了杨广的耳中。
　　杨广虽然很悲伤，但作为皇帝，完成此次西巡的政治目的更为重要。所以杨广斋戒三日为最疼爱的儿子表示哀悼之后， 继续与诸国国王和使臣宴饮。
　　杨广和地位最高的高昌国国王与伊吾吐屯坐在观风行殿上， 其他使臣分列下座作陪。
　　殿前陈列着宏大的仪仗和仪式， 热闹的鱼龙百戏在九部乐的伴奏声中循环演出，宾主都十分尽兴。
　　杨广高兴之余，赏赐外藩使臣无数珍宝， 又下令大赦天下。
　　杨广对身边重臣洋洋自夸，自古天子有巡狩之礼，江东诸帝多待在深宫不出来， 不知民间疾苦，所以他们活该亡国。我就不一样。
　　近臣们纷纷夸赞皇帝南巡北巡西巡之功。
　　李渊也在近臣中。
　　他闻言后嘴上附和， 心里不以为然。
　　古代确有喜欢巡狩的明君， 但没见过带着妃嫔宫女行宫乐人巡狩的明君。
　　杨昭与自家二郎三郎熟悉，李渊与太子杨昭的关系也较亲近。
　　李渊很欣赏太子杨昭，常与朋友说若杨昭继位，定是一位仁明之君。自己的孩子能成为太子的臣子，是他们的幸运。
　　杨昭身死给了李渊很大的打击。
　　他素有济世安民的念头， 才会给二儿子取名为“世民”。
　　在这之前，李渊只是想成为如高颎、杨素那样的国之重臣， 稍稍一点的奢望也就是结局要比高颎、杨素好，不仅自己一辈子得皇帝信任，自己的儿子们也能成为国之重臣。他所想的“济世安民”， 也只是身为臣子辅佐君王济世安民而已。
　　但跟随杨广御驾亲征这一路， “皇帝”的光辉形象在李渊面前缓缓崩裂。
　　杨昭之死， 给了李渊原本理想重重一击。
　　文臣武将， 当生活足够富足后，“利”已经满足，想要的就只剩下“名”。
　　这样的皇帝，真的能完成自己济世安民的愿望吗？
　　李渊很早就对杨广生出了不满和警惕之心，太子之死，第一次让他对杨广生出了不屑之心。
　　这样的皇帝，这样昏庸还不自知的自大愚蠢皇帝，凭什么立在自己上头？
　　如果是自己，如果是自己……
　　他打了个颤，警觉自己居然生出了忤逆之心，惊出了一身冷汗。
　　李渊赶紧将心中的僭越之意抹去，但念头一旦升起，就在心底扎了根，只等一场风雨发芽。
　　李世民和李玄霸得知太子病逝后，立刻向杨广请求回去拜祭。
　　杨广已经得到了杨昭找许多人“托孤”，只有李世民和李玄霸傻乎乎应下的事。
　　他在儿子病逝后只假装悲伤了三日就继续大摆宴席，也有这个原因。
　　杨广很生气。
　　杨广最厌恶的就是别人质疑他的能力，质疑他的统治不够稳固，质疑他治下的大隋不够强盛。
　　杨昭此举，把杨广的禁忌踩了个遍——杨广还活着，杨昭居然向其他人托孤，还敢擅言储君之位，甚至说出害怕儿子和兄弟自相残杀的话，杨广能不生气？
　　若不是杨昭已经死了，杨广简直动了废储的心思。
　　但又正因为杨昭这个一直顺着他的儿子在临死之前说出了如此多的禁忌之语，杨广无论如何沉浸在宴席中，也无法将这些话忘记。
　　对杨昭托孤的人，杨广也很厌恶。
　　不过他不是厌恶李世民和李玄霸，而是厌恶那些不敢答应的大臣。
　　虽然杨广愤怒杨昭的疯癫之语，但朕的太子都求你们了，你们居然不答应？而且朕一定不会让后代重演自相残杀，朕对朝堂的控制力可不是父皇能比的。杨昭“托孤”的愿望很容易就能完成，你们为何不敢答应？
　　李二郎和李三郎既拒绝卷入储位之争，又承诺就算发生万一，也会尽全力保证杨昭的儿子富贵终老。
　　杨昭病逝之后，“太子”之位吸引来的人大部分都会散去，流动到齐王杨暕那里。
　　在自己还在宴请诸国使臣时，居然只有李二郎和李三郎敢向自己请求回去拜祭太子，不害怕触自己霉头。两人这颗赤诚之心，杨广很感动。
　　杨广问道：“其他人都担心请求拜祭太子会打扰朕的宴请，惹朕不快。为何你们不担心？”
　　李世民疑惑道：“陛下对太子极亲近，为何臣请求拜祭太子会惹陛下不快？”
　　李玄霸道：“为人父母，哪有不爱自己孩子的。陛下先为君王，再为父亲，太子病逝也只能哀悼三日，继续坚持完成君王的责任。我和二哥还小，朝政之事用不上我和二哥。身为陛下的晚辈、太子的表弟，我们就该回太子身边守灵。”
　　杨广心头一暖。
　　是啊，就算他再生气，杨昭仍旧是他最宠爱的儿子，他寄托了无数心血的嫡长子。杨昭病逝，自己怎么可能不难过？
　　因自己表示出杨昭病逝前的疯癫之语不喜，那些大臣居然就怀疑自己的慈父之心，竟然不敢前去拜祭太子，哼！
　　“去吧，告诉世明，朕忙完后就会来看他，让他不要难过。”杨广温和慈爱道，“世明的兄弟和孩子都不在这里，你们身为世明的表弟，是他最亲近的同辈，就以亲兄弟之礼为他守灵，等朕回来吧。”
　　很巧的，杨昭字世明。如果他能继位，李世民就要避讳改名了。
　　杨广赐予李世民和李玄霸九环金带，命李世民和李玄霸回张掖主持太子葬礼。
　　李世民和李玄霸跪地谢恩，领着九环金带回张掖。
　　“束九环金带”是隋文帝首创“贵臣”的特权，如后世赐吉服一样。
　　杨广身边近臣，也不是人人都有这样的特权。两个孩子得了这样的特权，他们都恭喜李渊养了好儿子。
　　李渊这次没有自得。他平静道：“陛下欣赏二郎和三郎与太子的表兄弟情谊，这是他们应做的事，何来恭喜？”
　　李渊除在宴会时刻，其余时间禁酒肉、服素服为太子哀悼。
　　杨广感慨能养出李世民、李玄霸这样好的孩子，李渊也是纯善之人。他对李渊的信任又加重了几分。
　　李世民和李玄霸回到张掖时，张掖正因为太子之死乱作一团。
　　更让当地官员焦头烂额的是，伴随皇帝一同西巡的乐平公主杨丽华也病重了。
　　杨丽华的身份很特殊。她是北周宣帝的皇后。隋文帝对她心中有愧，所以对她极好。
　　杨丽华又颇具政治头脑，早早讨好杨广，多次为杨广进献美人。杨广也对她很亲近。
　　杨广和朝中重臣都不在张掖。张掖剩余的官员完全不知道该如何是好。
　　李玄霸让李世民操办太子杨昭葬礼，自己去照顾杨丽华。
　　早在得知太子生病时，李玄霸就让孙思邈悄悄以采药之名避开，并且在张掖传孙思邈只是“民间吹嘘起来的神医，本事不如御医，你看，他照顾的李三郎仍旧病恹恹”的传言。
　　孙思邈被叶护带走，在草原上躲避，得以逃脱杨广的征召。
　　以杨广的阴晴不定，说不定会让征召的医师为太子陪葬，李玄霸不敢冒险。
　　杨广离开张掖之后，孙思邈偷偷潜了回来。李玄霸让他开了一剂能缓解病患临终痛苦的药，以“我常服用”交给御医检验后，给杨丽华喝了几日。
　　杨丽华的高烧仍旧不退，但精神好了一些，算是回光返照，能留下遗言了。
　　她所说的遗言，果然是李玄霸在史书中看过的遗言——“妾唯一女，不自忧死，深怜之。汤沐乞回与李敏。”
　　杨丽华这一辈子过得既风光又凄苦，所挂念的只有自己唯一的女儿。李玄霸知道杨广会同意此事，安慰道：“公主请放心，陛下对公主很亲近，定会同意公主。”
　　杨丽华欣慰地闭上双眼：“陛下常言李三郎颇懂圣意，李三郎如此说，我安心了。”
　　她意识再次变得模糊，嘴里一直念着“静训”二字。
　　李玄霸知道杨丽华念的名字是谁的。
　　李静训，杨丽华最宠爱的外孙女，去年在汾阳宫病逝。后世因墓葬考古发现，在历史爱好者中颇具名气。
　　李玄霸虽常进宫，但无缘得见这位杨丽华宠爱的外孙女，也无从改变她的命运。
　　他知道很多人或悲惨或不公的命运，但都只是旁观者的“知道”。
　　比如他知道杨丽华最疼爱的独女宇文娥英，会和丈夫李敏一起被杨广赐死，包括杨丽华其余外孙、外孙女在内的所有血脉全部被杀。
　　李玄霸安慰道：“公主请安息。陛下一定会好好照顾你的家人。”
　　杨丽华停下了嚅嗫，神情更加平和。
　　御医摸了杨丽华的鼻息和脉搏，摇摇头。
　　李玄霸恭送乐平公主离世，一边派人向杨广报丧，并呈上亲自记录下的乐平公主的遗言，一边为乐平公主治丧。
　　小小的张掖城，因两位贵人的葬礼满城戴孝。
　　官宦士族人家一边要让家中女眷穿戴着华丽的衣服首饰，乘坐着华丽的马车去为陛下当气氛小组，一边又要在自家挂孝为太子和乐平公主默哀。
　　他们又要哭，又要笑，每日战战兢兢。
　　杨广的旨意到达了张掖。他果然同意了乐平公主的请求，将乐平公主的食邑都赐给了李敏。
　　他让李玄霸将乐平公主的灵堂设在太子一旁，减轻了两个孩子的工作。
　　李世民和李玄霸也得以聚在一起守灵，互相照顾。
　　李玄霸将一张一张的纸钱丢入火盆中。
　　——没有父母不疼爱自己的孩子。
　　李玄霸又为杨丽华填上了香烛。
　　——陛下会好好照顾你的家人。
　　安息吧，带着谎言安息。
　　……
　　大业五年，大隋平吐谷浑，西域诸国纷纷朝贺，献西域几千里土地。大隋新设西海、河源、鄯善、且末等郡，迁天下犯人戍卫。
　　《资治通鉴》曰，“是时天下凡有郡一百九十，县一千二百五十五，户八百九十万有奇。东西九千三百里，南北万四千八百一十五里。隋氏之盛，极于此矣。”
　　大隋最强盛的时刻到来。
　　……
　　杨广回来了。
　　他带着太子杨昭和乐平公主的灵柩，浩浩荡荡抄近路回西京大兴安葬。
　　李渊也跟着杨广离开。李世民和李玄霸跟随处理西域之事扫尾的裴世矩，继续留在张掖。待裴世矩回朝时，再一起回来。
　　杨广离开时，文武百官终于换上了素衣，为太子进行迟来的守孝哀悼。
　　从六朝时开始兴起的祭奠纸钱被赶着做了出来，沿路挥洒。
　　李世民和李玄霸站在张掖城门口，目送大隋皇帝的车驾离开。
　　在大隋最强盛的时刻，一路挥洒着纸钱离开。
　　正午的阳光将天边的云彩都染成了火海，仿佛以最直观的景色来描绘此刻大隋的烈火烹油。
　　而在这灿烂的阳光下，纸钱纷纷扬扬如雨飘落。
chunks.englishText:
**Chapter 79: A Rain of Paper Money Under the Radiant Sun**

The passing of the Crown Prince was a momentous event, and the news reached Yang Guang’s ears the very next day.

Though Yang Guang was deeply grieved, as Emperor, the political objectives of this Western Inspection were of greater importance. Thus, after fasting for three days to mourn his most beloved son, he continued to feast and drink with the kings and envoys of various nations.

Yang Guang sat upon the Guanfeng Pavilion alongside the highest-ranking dignitaries—the King of Gaochang and the Tutun of Yiwu—while the other envoys were seated in descending order of rank to keep them company.

Before the pavilion, grand processions and ceremonies were displayed. The lively "Fish and Dragon" performances unfolded in a continuous loop, accompanied by the Nine Departments of Music. Both host and guests were thoroughly entertained.

In his high spirits, Yang Guang bestowed countless treasures upon the foreign envoys and issued a decree for a general amnesty across the realm.

Yang Guang boasted to the high-ranking officials at his side, "Since ancient times, the Son of Heaven has held the rite of imperial inspection. The emperors of Jiangdong mostly hid in their deep palaces, never emerging, and thus remained ignorant of the hardships of the common people—which is why they deserved to lose their kingdoms. I am different."

The close ministers vied with one another to praise the Emperor’s achievements in his southern, northern, and western inspections.

Li Yuan was among these close ministers.

Upon hearing this, he echoed their sentiments with his lips, but in his heart, he remained unconvinced.

There had indeed been wise monarchs in antiquity who enjoyed imperial inspections, but he had never seen a wise monarch who toured while accompanied by a retinue of concubines, palace maids, and court musicians.

Yang Zhao had been familiar with his second son, Shimin, and his third son, Xuanba; Li Yuan himself also shared a relatively close relationship with the Crown Prince, Yang Zhao.

Li Yuan held the Crown Prince in high regard and often told his friends that if Yang Zhao were to ascend the throne, he would surely be a benevolent and enlightened ruler. He believed it was his children’s good fortune to serve as subjects to such a Crown Prince.

Yang Zhao’s death dealt a heavy blow to Li Yuan.

He had long harbored the ambition to "save the world and bring peace to the people," which was why he had named his second son "Shimin" (a contraction of *ji shi an min*).

Before this, Li Yuan had only aspired to be a pillar of the state like Gao Jiong or Yang Su. His only slightly grander wish was that his ending might be better than theirs—that not only would he enjoy the Emperor’s trust his entire life, but his sons would also become great ministers of the state. The "saving the world and bringing peace to the people" he envisioned was merely the role of a subject assisting his sovereign in doing so.

However, throughout this journey following Yang Guang on his imperial expedition, the glorious image of the "Emperor" had slowly crumbled before Li Yuan’s eyes.

Yang Zhao’s death dealt a crushing blow to Li Yuan’s original ideals.

For civil and military officials, once their lives were sufficiently prosperous and their "profit" satisfied, the only thing left to desire was "fame."

Could such an Emperor truly fulfill his own aspiration of saving the world and bringing peace to the people?

Li Yuan had long ago developed a sense of dissatisfaction and wariness toward Yang Guang. The death of the Crown Prince was the first time he felt a sense of disdain for him.

Such an Emperor—a foolish, arrogant, and oblivious ruler—by what right did he stand above him?

If it were himself... if it were himself...

He shuddered, startled by the realization that he had actually harbored a thought of rebellion, breaking out in a cold sweat.

Li Yuan hurriedly wiped the thought of usurpation from his mind, but once the seed was sown, it took root in his heart, waiting only for a storm to sprout.

Upon learning of the Crown Prince’s passing, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba immediately requested Yang Guang’s permission to return and pay their respects.

Yang Guang had already learned that Yang Zhao had "entrusted his orphan" to many people, and that only Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had foolishly agreed.

This was part of the reason why he had only feigned grief for three days after his son’s death before continuing to host lavish banquets.

Yang Guang was furious.

What Yang Guang loathed most was others questioning his abilities, questioning the stability of his rule, or questioning whether the Great Sui under his governance was strong enough.

Yang Zhao’s actions had stepped on every one of Yang Guang’s taboos—Yang Guang was still alive, yet Yang Zhao had dared to entrust his son to others, dared to speak presumptuously about the succession, and even dared to voice fears that his sons and brothers would slaughter one another. How could Yang Guang not be angry?

Had Yang Zhao not already been dead, Yang Guang would have been moved to strip him of his title.

Yet, precisely because this son, who had always been compliant, had uttered so many forbidden words before his death, Yang Guang could not forget them, no matter how deeply he immersed himself in the festivities.

Yang Guang also felt a deep loathing for those to whom Yang Zhao had entrusted his son.

However, he did not loathe Li Shimin and Li Xuanba; he loathed the ministers who had dared not agree.

Although Yang Guang was enraged by Yang Zhao’s delirious words, he thought: *My Crown Prince begged you, and you dared to refuse? And I will certainly never allow my descendants to repeat the tragedy of fratricide; my control over the court is not something my father could compare to. Yang Zhao’s wish to "entrust his orphan" would have been easy to fulfill—why did you not dare to agree?*

Li Erlang and Li Sanlang had refused to be drawn into the struggle for the succession, yet they had promised that even if the worst were to happen, they would do their utmost to ensure Yang Zhao’s son lived out his life in wealth and comfort.

After Yang Zhao’s death, most of the people attracted by the position of "Crown Prince" would disperse, flowing toward the Prince of Qi, Yang Jiong.

While he was still feasting with the envoys of various nations, only Li Erlang and Li Sanlang had dared to ask him for permission to return and mourn the Crown Prince, unafraid of incurring his displeasure. Yang Guang was deeply moved by their sincere hearts.

Yang Guang asked, "Others were worried that requesting to mourn the Crown Prince would disturb my banquet and provoke my displeasure. Why were you two not worried?"

Li Shimin asked in confusion, "Your Majesty was extremely close to the Crown Prince; why would your subject’s request to mourn him provoke Your Majesty’s displeasure?"

Li Xuanba said, "What parent does not love their own child? Your Majesty is a sovereign first and a father second; even if the Crown Prince has passed, you must mourn for three days before continuing to fulfill your duties as a sovereign. My second brother and I are still young and have no role in court affairs. As your juniors and the Crown Prince’s cousins, we should return to his side to keep vigil."

Yang Guang’s heart warmed.

Indeed, even if he were angry, Yang Zhao remained his most favored son, the eldest son of his primary wife upon whom he had pinned countless hopes. With Yang Zhao dead, how could he not be heartbroken?

Because he had expressed his displeasure at Yang Zhao’s delirious words before death, those ministers had actually doubted his heart as a loving father and dared not go to mourn the Crown Prince. Hmph!

"Go. Tell Shimin that I will come to see him once I am finished here, and tell him not to be sad," Yang Guang said with gentle affection. "Shimin’s brothers and children are not here; as his cousins, you are his closest peers. Keep vigil for him as if you were his own brothers until I return."

Coincidentally, Yang Zhao’s courtesy name was Shimin. If he had succeeded to the throne, Li Shimin would have had to change his name to avoid the taboo.

Yang Guang bestowed upon Li Shimin and Li Xuanba nine-ringed golden belts and ordered them to return to Zhangye to preside over the Crown Prince’s funeral.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba knelt to thank him, then took the nine-ringed golden belts and returned to Zhangye.

"Wearing the nine-ringed golden belt" was a privilege for "noble ministers" first created by Emperor Wen of Sui, much like the bestowing of ceremonial robes in later dynasties.

Not even all of Yang Guang’s close ministers possessed such a privilege. When the two children received it, everyone congratulated Li Yuan on raising such fine sons.

For once, Li Yuan did not feel smug. He said calmly, "His Majesty appreciates the cousinly bond between Erlang, Sanlang, and the Crown Prince. This is what they ought to do; why offer congratulations?"

Aside from the moments he was forced to attend banquets, Li Yuan abstained from wine and meat, wearing plain mourning clothes to grieve for the Crown Prince.

Yang Guang was moved that Li Yuan could raise such fine children as Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, and that Li Yuan himself was a man of pure virtue. His trust in Li Yuan deepened further.

When Li Shimin and Li Xuanba returned to Zhangye, the city was in chaos due to the Crown Prince’s death.

What made the local officials even more frantic was that Princess Leping, Yang Lihua, who had accompanied the Emperor on his Western Inspection, had also fallen gravely ill.

Yang Lihua’s status was unique. She was the Empress of the Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou. Emperor Wen of Sui had felt a sense of guilt toward her, and thus treated her with great kindness.

Yang Lihua also possessed considerable political acumen; she had long since curried favor with Yang Guang, repeatedly presenting him with beauties. Yang Guang was also very close to her.

With Yang Guang and the high ministers absent from Zhangye, the remaining officials were completely at a loss.

Li Xuanba had Li Shimin take charge of the Crown Prince’s funeral, while he himself went to care for Yang Lihua.

Long before he knew the Crown Prince was ill, Li Xuanba had quietly had Sun Simiao slip away under the pretext of gathering herbs, spreading the rumor in Zhangye that Sun Simiao was merely "a miracle doctor hyped up by the common folk, whose skills were inferior to the imperial physicians—look, the Li Sanlang he cares for is still sickly."

Sun Simiao had been taken away by Yehu and hidden in the grasslands, thus escaping Yang Guang’s summons.

Given Yang Guang’s volatile temperament, he might have forced the summoned physicians to be buried with the Crown Prince; Li Xuanba dared not take the risk.

After Yang Guang left Zhangye, Sun Simiao had sneaked back. Li Xuanba had him prepare a decoction to alleviate the pain of the dying, which he then presented to the imperial physicians for inspection under the guise of "medicine I take regularly," before giving it to Yang Lihua for several days.

Yang Lihua’s high fever did not subside, but her spirit improved slightly—a final burst of clarity that allowed her to leave her last words.

The final words she spoke were exactly what Li Xuanba had read in the history books: "I have only one daughter; I do not fear death for myself, but I pity her deeply. I beg that my bathing and grooming revenues be returned to Li Min."

Yang Lihua’s life had been both glorious and miserable; her only concern was her only daughter. Knowing Yang Guang would agree, Li Xuanba comforted her, "Please rest assured, Princess. His Majesty is very close to you and will certainly grant your request."

Yang Lihua closed her eyes with relief. "His Majesty often says that Li Sanlang understands the imperial will well. With Li Sanlang saying this, I am at ease."

Her consciousness became blurred once more, and she kept murmuring the name "Jingxun."

Li Xuanba knew whose name Yang Lihua was speaking.

Li Jingxun was Yang Lihua’s most favored granddaughter, who had passed away at Fenyang Palace the previous year. Due to archaeological discoveries of her tomb, she was quite famous among history enthusiasts in later generations.

Although Li Xuanba often entered the palace, he had never had the chance to meet this granddaughter whom Yang Lihua doted on, nor could he change her fate.

He knew the tragic or unjust fates of many people, but he was merely a bystander who "knew."

For instance, he knew that Yang Lihua’s most beloved only daughter, Yuwen Eying, would be forced to commit suicide by Yang Guang along with her husband, Li Min, and that all of Yang Lihua’s other descendants would be slaughtered.

Li Xuanba comforted her, "Please rest in peace, Princess. His Majesty will surely take good care of your family."

Yang Lihua stopped murmuring, her expression becoming more peaceful.

The imperial physician checked Yang Lihua’s pulse and breath, then shook his head.

Li Xuanba respectfully saw the Princess of Leping off as she passed away. He sent men to report the death to Yang Guang, presented the last words he had personally recorded, and began to arrange her funeral.

The small city of Zhangye was draped in mourning for the two noble figures.

The families of officials and the gentry had to have their womenfolk wear gorgeous clothes and jewelry, riding in ornate carriages to act as a "cheering squad" for the Emperor, while simultaneously hanging mourning banners in their own homes to grieve for the Crown Prince and Princess Leping.

They had to cry and smile at the same time, living in fear every day.

Yang Guang’s decree arrived in Zhangye. As expected, he agreed to Princess Leping’s request and bestowed her fiefs upon Li Min.

He ordered Li Xuanba to set up the mourning hall for Princess Leping beside that of the Crown Prince, which lightened the workload for the two brothers.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were thus able to stay together to keep vigil, looking after one another.

Li Xuanba tossed sheets of paper money into the brazier one by one.

*—There is no parent who does not love their child.*

Li Xuanba added incense and candles for Yang Lihua.

*—His Majesty will take good care of your family.*

Rest in peace. Rest in peace with these lies.

...

In the fifth year of the Daye era, the Great Sui pacified the Tuyuhun, and the various nations of the Western Regions came to pay homage, offering thousands of miles of territory. The Great Sui established new commanderies such as Xihai, Heyuan, Shanshan, and Qiemo, relocating criminals from across the realm to garrison them.

The *Zizhi Tongjian* records: "At this time, the realm had a total of 190 commanderies, 1,255 counties, and over 8.9 million households. It spanned 9,300 li from east to west, and 14,815 li from north to south. The prosperity of the Sui reached its zenith here."

The moment of the Great Sui’s greatest power had arrived.

...

Yang Guang returned.

He brought the coffins of Crown Prince Yang Zhao and Princess Leping, traveling in a grand procession along a shortcut back to the Western Capital, Daxing, for burial.

Li Yuan departed with Yang Guang. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba remained in Zhangye to assist Pei Shiju in handling the aftermath of the Western Regions affairs. They would return together when Pei Shiju returned to the capital.

When Yang Guang left, the civil and military officials finally changed into plain white robes to perform the long-overdue mourning rites for the Crown Prince.

Paper money for the dead, which had begun to gain popularity during the Six Dynasties period, was hurriedly produced and scattered along the road.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba stood at the gates of Zhangye, watching the Emperor of Great Sui’s carriage depart.

At the very moment of the Great Sui’s greatest prosperity, it departed, scattering paper money along the way.

The midday sun dyed the clouds on the horizon into a sea of fire, as if using the most vivid scenery to depict the Great Sui at this moment—like a pot of boiling oil with a flame beneath it.

And under this radiant sun, the paper money drifted down like rain.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第80章 李玄霸初次谋划
chunks.chineseText:
第80章 李玄霸初次谋划

=
　　李世民和李玄霸送别了皇帝和父亲， 没过几日，中原亲朋好友的信到了。
　　他俩原本以为父亲到的时候会捎带信件，没想到过了这么久信件才来。
　　当看到“信件”时， 他们明白为什么会这么晚到了。
　　李世民：“整整五车， 全是信？”
　　李玄霸：“显然不可能全是信。”
　　五驾马车上装满了大小箱子， 李玄霸有了前世拆快递的爽快感。
　　但拆了第一车的箱子，李世民和李玄霸就双双苦脸了。
　　老师们怎么能装满整整一车功课？更可恶的是，这装满功课的马车居然还是第一辆！
　　李世民面无表情地低头扒拉书籍：“每本书都要写注疏？不要吧？”
　　李玄霸：“还有策论和绘制地图……我后悔拜长孙伯父为师。”
　　李世民：“薛老师布置的诗赋作业都能算休息了。”
　　李玄霸：“还是虞老师好， 只说会抽查我们做的其他功课，看字迹是否工整。”
　　李世民：“这是好吗！这不是把所有其他科目的功课都变成了书法功课吗！”
　　已经快十一岁的少年郎李世民抱着脑袋使劲甩，就像是后世的沙雕彩虹小人甩头表情包。
　　李玄霸丢开了第一车老师的“疼爱”， 去往了第二层。
　　当遇到郁闷的事时，就丢一边， 去看一点高兴的事。
　　从第二车开始， 是家人、老师和朋友寄过来的生活用品。
　　窦夫人、万氏和几个出嫁的、未出嫁的姐姐都寄来了亲手缝制的衣服鞋帽，再加上家里仆人做的衣服被褥，装了两大车。
　　第四车是药材，第五车是金银珠宝等贵重财物和众人的信件。
　　李世民先看了母亲的信件，又嘲笑了几句李智云信中的错别字， 然后立刻找出长孙小妹的信件看起来。
　　李玄霸嫌弃地瞥了二哥一眼。
　　李世民坏笑着举着一封信：“宇文小娘子给你的信，想要吗？求我啊。”
　　李玄霸毛发都要竖起来：“你什么时候偷的？还给我！”
　　李世民举着信， 绕着马车“哈哈哈哈哈”跑。李玄霸在后面把腿蹬成了风火轮追赶。
　　大概是老天都看不下去李世民欺负人，李世民一脚踢到了地面凸起来的部分，踉踉跄跄好不容易才稳住身体没有跌倒。
　　李玄霸赶到， 一把抢走自己的信， 又一脚把还在努力保持身体平衡的二哥踹倒在地。
　　“哎哟！”李世民先摔倒， 然后迅速爬起来， 拍了拍身上的灰尘，跟没事人似的，“弟媳写什么了？让我看看。我和你交换。”
　　李玄霸把二哥推开。
　　二哥脸皮极厚，恨不得逢人就炫耀自己和未婚妻感情有多好。他可没有这么不要脸。
　　“唉，你还害羞。”李世民叹了口气，没有继续逗弄弟弟，继续仔细品读未婚妻的来信。
　　李玄霸走到离二哥较远的地方拆开信。
　　宇文珠的信一如既往的“理性”，除了例行问好之外，只询问了李玄霸的身体和自己所附的滋补药方是否有用。
　　李玄霸心情不知道为何，有些许低落。
　　他翻开了下一张信纸。
　　信纸是叠好的一大张纸。
　　李玄霸展开叠好的方块纸，一幅春光图跃然纸上。鲜艳的青绿、湛蓝、火红在纸上流淌，仿佛将灿烂的春光装入了小画中。
　　“塞外风光壮美。大兴城的春景就过于富贵精致，稍显匠气。但毕竟是家乡的景色，三郎君应该不会嫌弃？”
　　李玄霸的手指抚摸过小画上的落款。
　　“你在笑什么？”二哥的大脑袋歪着探了过来。
　　李玄霸上翘的嘴角下撇，迅速把画合上。
　　但李世民已经看到了，打趣道：“弟媳给你画了一幅画，你就笑成这样？我看弟媳还给你绣了东西，你会不会乐得找不着北。嘿嘿，观音婢也给我绣了帕子。”
　　李世民把一个匣子递给李玄霸。
　　他们两人未婚妻的绣品放在同一个匣子里送来。李世民先把匣子抢了。
　　李玄霸打开匣子中宇文珠送来的小包裹，里面还有一封信。
　　他看完信后，嘴角微微抽搐。
　　李世民在一旁偷看，笑得前俯后仰：“哈哈哈哈，谁让你给弟媳说寒钩和乌镝的事？我就知道她们那些小娘子肯定会特别喜爱寒钩和乌镝，故意没和观音婢说。”
　　宇文珠送来了两条大方巾，绣的是云纹与寒钩和乌镝的名字。她曾经看过有人养的猎鹰脖子上系了围脖，希望把这两条大方巾系在寒钩和乌镝的脖子上。
　　给李玄霸的绣品也有。一方手帕，比大方巾小许多，还没有绣名字。
　　宇文珠在信中询问了许多寒钩和乌镝的事，对两只聪明的雕崽好奇极了。她还列了一些听说雕也能吃的滋补药材，让李玄霸千万别亏待雕崽。
　　想想宇文珠给自己写的超级理性的信，再看看宇文珠询问雕崽的语言生动活泼的信，李玄霸一时心情有点复杂。
　　李世民笑得肚子都疼了。
　　他擦着笑出来的眼泪道：“谁让你和弟媳都在洛阳的时候，不找机会偷偷与她相会？你看我，观音婢见过我之后，就对我念念不忘。在弟媳那里，你还是个陌生人呢，还是个第一次写信就送医书的无趣木头陌生人。雕崽都比你有趣。哈哈哈哈！”
　　李玄霸的面子有些挂不住。
　　甜言蜜语都是骗人的东西。自己根据宇文珠的爱好送最实用的东西，信中也不东拉西扯写油腻的废话，怎么能叫木讷无趣？难道要像你那样给嫂子写十遍“想你念你”？
　　你甚至都不肯写诗，非要写土味情话。根据自己从网络上看到的经验，女性一点都不喜欢土味情话，都喜欢实用。
　　嗯，一定是这样。
　　李玄霸瓮声瓮气道：“房玄龄他们的书信和礼物不看了？”
　　李世民见弟弟快恼羞成怒，在李玄霸恼羞成怒的临界点收起嘲讽的笑容，顺着李玄霸的话转移话题：“看！”
　　房乔等人的信除了问候之外，更细细地给李世民和李玄霸说了他们二人离开后，洛阳一些比较值得一提的大事。
　　李世民和李玄霸将这些看上去很琐碎的事一一看过，将他们离开后的洛阳朝中现状拼凑出来。
　　当杨广离开洛阳后，看上去很富足的洛阳没有必要再维持繁华的假象，衣衫褴褛的流民出现在大街小巷。房乔等人猜测对吐谷浑这一战，活不下去的百姓增多了。
　　房乔已经接受了朝堂的任命，去江南担任县令。
　　这是李玄霸为房乔选的地方。
　　二哥将来的肱股之臣大多来自北方，对江南不了解。
　　隋文帝毁掉了江南几座大城。特别是毁掉建业后，在南朝时期已经得到较为充分开发的江南之地出现了经济和文化的倒退。
　　杨广修建大运河之后，江南复苏。将来唐朝建立，北方战火肆虐，恢复生产很艰难。同时加大开发南方的力度，对应对唐初接连的天灾很有利。所以李玄霸和房乔商议，希望他能多了解江南的事。
　　房乔在父亲房彦谦回到洛阳后，一度生出陪伴父亲的念头。
　　但房彦谦训斥了房乔。
　　房彦谦虽然不知道房乔在为多年后谶纬实现的那一刻做准备，但身为父亲，他能察觉房乔在做一件和友人相关的大事。
　　房彦谦训斥房乔：“你若没有答应友人便罢，既然已经答应，为人最重要的品德之一就是守诺。我自有仆从照顾，何须你在一旁做小儿态？赶紧去完成你的事。”
　　房乔惭愧醒悟，与夫人一同南下江南。
　　杜如晦也被选为县令。他本瞧不起县令这小官，不愿意前往。
　　但房乔劝说，千里之行始于足下，有治理一县的经验，亲身接触过百姓，将来身居高位才会得心应手。
　　李世民和李玄霸还没离开时，也常和朋友说起亲近百姓一事。
　　杜如晦受到影响，此次开始认真考虑是否要赴任。
　　如果真要当县令，杜如晦想选一个边疆之地。既然是奔着吃苦积累经验去的，他希望能一步到位。
　　薛收见两位友人都愿意外放当县令，居然也有些不想走清贵的文人之路了，于是写信来询问李世民和李玄霸的意见。
　　李世民道：“既然已经意动，那就出去呗。多增长见识，总不会有错。”
　　李玄霸道：“那就这么写吧。”
　　两人虽然先拆了家人和未婚妻的信，但最先给朋友回信。
　　与家人和未婚妻写信需要斟酌字句和感情，给朋友的信哪怕满篇口水话错别字也没关系，写信速度飞快。
　　花了几日回信和准备礼物，当李世民和李玄霸把信件和礼物寄出去时，他们等待多时的叶护终于带来了好消息。
　　“伏允果然悄悄往河曲草原移动！”叶护兴奋道，“李三！你果然有天神护佑！连这都能猜到！我打探到消息的时候，伏允才刚决定往河曲走！”
　　李世民得意：“我弟弟就是厉害！阿玄，我要赶紧出发了。你好好待在张掖，照顾好自己。”
　　李玄霸听到叶护的消息后，松了口气：“是往河曲草原走就好。我也去。”
　　李世民立刻脸色大变：“阿玄！……”
　　李玄霸摆手阻止了李世民的唠叨：“我做了一些小东西，能极大地降低此战的难度。没有我，你们不会用。而且我要去监督你，免得你热血上头，冲得太厉害。”
　　李世民皱眉：“你的身体能支撑住吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“我现在身体还行，只是骑马跋涉，不上战场拼杀就没问题。”
　　李世民严肃道：“我信你这次。如果你这次受伤或者生病，以后你都别想再上战场。”
　　李玄霸没想到二哥这么好说话。李世民答应的时候，他还愣了一下，才回答：“好。”
　　叶护惊讶：“你们都要去？这这这这很危险啊！我的部族战斗力还是很厉害的，提前埋伏好了，肯定能赢！”
　　李世民道：“我们此战不仅要赢，还要大获全胜，把伏允的脑袋摘下来。一点差错都不能有。让他逃过这次，就难以再寻到杀他的机会。”
　　李玄霸道：“放心，我们会带着私兵前往。”
　　叶护苦笑：“你们都这么说了，行。我已经劝动首领出五百骑兵。虽然人数比伏允少，但都是族中骁勇善战的勇士。首领很重视这份功劳。如果这次伏击能成功，首领还希望能邀请你们去做客。”
　　李玄霸道：“若获胜，我们会立刻回中原将首级献给陛下，以免他人抢夺功劳。下次有机会，我们再与你们首领喝酒。”
　　李世民笑道：“机会多的是。现在把大功劳拿下才是正事。”
　　叶护叹气：“听你们这话，是真的有信心杀掉伏允？首领下达的命令只是尽可能抢夺伏允的物资。”
　　李世民道：“相信我和阿玄。我和阿玄什么时候让你失望过？”
　　叶护笑道：“确实没有。李二郎李三郎都亲自上战场了，我也不能退缩。我会带一百奴隶同往。我不会带兵，这一百奴隶就交给你们。让我看看李二郎李三郎带兵的本事。”
　　李世民拍着叶护的胳膊道：“你这么信任我和阿玄，我们一定不会让你失望。等着拿大功劳吧。”
　　叶护点头：“我们部族的未来就看你们了。”
　　李玄霸让叶护查探之事，就是史书中记载的“吐谷浑可汗伏允北逃党项”的事。
　　因为杨广穿越大斗拔谷时冻死了许多兵士，杨昭和杨丽华也因此病逝，所以大隋停止了继续追击伏允。
　　原本杨广非要带着大隋将士赶时间穿越大斗拔谷，就是为了真的来一场御驾亲征，带着大隋将士去追击伏允。
　　历史中杨广此行冻死的卫卒更多，所以也停止了继续追击伏允。
　　但此前已经扫灭了伏允在吐谷浑的众多势力，虽然大隋还不能完全控制吐谷浑的土地，伏允也不能回到他原本的国土。
　　伏允身边的部族、勇士生计困难，就北上寻找党项羌，在党项羌客居游牧。
　　原本历史中，伏允会等到隋末时从党项羌回到吐谷浑复国。
　　吐谷浑也算古羌人的一支，与中原文明接触较多，文明程度较高。党项羌则现在也过着没有文字，不知农耕的较为原始的游牧生活。
　　党项羌有很多支，青海的黄河上游和四川的松潘以西皆有分布。
　　李玄霸在出发之前，就因为知道伏允会逃往党项羌，向长孙晟了解了党项羌的事。
　　来到张掖之后，李玄霸又搜集了党项羌的具体资料，并根据大隋和伏允的战争局势，不断模拟伏允北逃党项羌的路线。
　　叶护是回纥人。但回纥只是大隋给叶护所在部族联盟的称呼。
　　其实回纥也属于铁勒的一部。之前裴世矩联系的进攻吐谷浑的铁勒人，是另一支较为强大的铁勒部族。
　　中原大部分人都习惯把外夷划分成一个整体，比如突厥、铁勒等。
　　实际上这些“整体”大多是中原人自己的划分习惯。一个“整体”中有许多部族，其中许多部族还彼此为敌，根本不把对方当自己“同族”。
　　长孙晟经略西域，就是靠着把这些部族具体情况一一摸清楚，就像是纵横家在春秋战国时做的那样，挑起他们的矛盾和分裂。
　　回纥是铁勒中袁纥一支，联合仆固、同罗、拔野古等同被突厥压榨的非铁勒部族结成的联盟。他们在铁勒中原本不算强大，组成联盟后也比薛延陀部稍差。
　　薛延陀部是与大隋和突厥联系都最紧密的一支铁勒人。他们在大隋朝堂中的地位就代表着“铁勒”。
　　回纥很想取代薛延陀部在大隋朝堂的地位，自己来成为“铁勒”的代表，这样才能得到大隋更多的资助。
　　这次李世民和李玄霸给了回纥人在杨广面前露脸的机会。虽然他们得到了赏赐，但杨广仍旧没把他们放在眼里，只把他们当做薛延陀部，甚至突厥人的下属。
　　在大隋皇帝眼中，没把西域部族分得太清楚。说什么回纥，他是不知道的。
　　对西域的了解都来自二手资料的裴世矩在这些细节上，比起实地考察的长孙晟也差得有点远，没有认识到“铁勒人”和突厥一样，内部也不是一条心。
　　李玄霸在叶护的引领下，在回纥贵族那里打探到了许多消息，确定回纥已经有强盛的迹象。突厥和铁勒其他几部还没发现这个弱小的部族已经暗中积聚了力量。
　　现在回纥首领很希望做点什么来显示自己的力量，但又担心被突厥和其他铁勒部族围剿。
　　李玄霸适时地递出了合作的邀请。
　　回纥部游牧的范围很广，最远能达到后世杭爱山脚下。
　　杭爱山，就是“燕然勒石”的燕然山。
　　他们的游牧范围，正好能囊括伏允的北逃路线。
　　伏允现在是一块肥肉。不仅大隋盯着他，突厥和铁勒人也希望咬他一口。所以他绕开敌人，北逃去党项羌的路线并不多。
　　他做出了一副要投降大隋的架势，众人都以为他会南下。就算逃，他们也以为伏允应该逃往更西北的天山等地，这才更为安全。
　　无人想到伏允居然会去投奔还是一群原始游牧民族的党项羌，所以他才能安然到达。
　　现在李玄霸将伏允的打算告知了回纥首领，希望回纥能出兵。
　　若能伏击到吐谷浑可汗，将战果告知大隋，回纥在大隋的地位一定能提升，得到大隋更多的资助。
　　回纥原本不相信李玄霸一个黄口小儿的推断。
　　叶护赌上自己的牛羊、牧民给李玄霸担保，说动回纥首领按照李玄霸指的方向去查伏允的踪迹。
　　叶护也是一时冲动。还好李玄霸没有辜负他的信任。
　　这点小事，叶护没有告诉李世民和李玄霸。
　　他们是朋友。为朋友仗义执言怎么能邀功？
　　李世民和李玄霸说出发就立刻出发。
　　他们没有告诉裴世矩真正的原因，只说要去叶护的部族作客。
　　两人没有职官在身，名义上不算是裴世矩的下属。再加上两人身为皇帝看重的表侄的身份，裴世矩没资格限制他们的行为。
　　李世民和李玄霸常在张掖附近出游，裴世矩已经习惯了。这次他也只叮嘱了李世民和李玄霸要小心安全，便同意两人离开。
　　裴世矩还给了两人令牌，让他们如果遇到危险，可以凭借令牌请求大隋卫卒援助。大隋驻守边疆的将军还是比较给他裴世矩面子，一般来说都会出兵。
　　李世民和李玄霸谢过裴世矩后，领着一众护卫离开了张掖。
　　半路上，已经被李世民和李玄霸安排在郊外的，李渊留给他们的两百私兵已经等候多时。
　　其中一百私兵，是李世民和李玄霸在洛阳庄子上的人。李世民在洛阳时对他们进行了简单的训练。
　　李世民和李玄霸写信给李渊，让他庄子上的“青壮”带来。他们已经长大，多点私兵，说不定路上能剿个匪什么的，混些战功。
　　李渊看到两个儿子暴露的“私兵”，心中对两个儿子的才干评价又上了一个台阶。
　　他不仅自掏腰包为这些青壮补足了铁甲武器，还又留了一百唐国公府的私兵，与李世民和李玄霸原本带来的护卫，和在张掖新买的青壮奴隶，凑够了四百壮卒。
　　李渊担心李世民和李玄霸养不起这么多青壮，还特意留下了许多粮草财物，也不知道是从哪扒拉的。
　　李世民和李玄霸猜测，这些粮草财物大概率是父亲“偷”的大隋的军饷。
　　用军饷补贴私兵，是个能带兵的勋贵都会做。李渊虽然第一次带兵，也做得很熟练。
　　不过就算李渊没有留下粮草和财物，李世民和李玄霸也养得起这四百壮卒。
　　他还是小看了李玄霸做生意敛财的本事，也小看了李世民交友的本事。
　　这些私兵原本以为是陪家中的小郎君“过家家”，结果李渊前脚刚走，两个小郎君后脚就不装了，给他们一人配了两匹新的骏马。
　　一个骑兵两匹马，这是精锐骑兵才能有的待遇！李渊留下的唐国公府老卒都惊讶得说不出话来。
　　他们跟着唐国公打吐谷浑的时候，都没这么富裕过。
　　当他们又得到新的武器和铁甲、披甲后，他们已经对两位小郎君死心塌地。
　　“跟着我们打过这一场仗，你们就是我们的兵了。”李世民对新来的私兵道，“回去后都把嘴闭严实了，这些好东西都是打完吐谷浑可汗伏允后缴获的，明白吗？”
　　一群老兵油子带着一群新兵喊道：“明白！”
　　他们激动得身体发抖。
　　不仅有骏马、盔甲和武器，还能有大功劳赚？
　　虽然他们早知道自家二郎君和三郎君非常了不起，但这也过于厉害了！
　　如果这一战能赢，回去后就算唐国公把他们调到其他地方，他们也是二郎君和三郎君的兵！
