Chapter 86: Li Xuanba Refuses to Meet

Seeing that his three elder sisters were all living well, Li Xuanba felt a weight lifted from his heart.

His eldest and second sisters were away from Daxing City, following their husbands who had been posted to regional assignments. Li Xuanba only visited the servants they had left behind at the old family estate, asking them to help deliver letters and gifts.

Li Xuanba remembered that the Feng Shaoshi his eldest sister married was a trusted confidant of his second brother, and that the couple had passed away during the Wude era. His second sister’s marriage to the imperial son-in-law Dou Dan was likely her second.

If the husbands Li Yuan chose for his daughters had died a natural, early death, there would be records of it. For a son-in-law whose records had been wiped clean, it was highly probable that he had severed ties with Li Yuan during the chaos at the end of the Sui Dynasty.

Fortunately, his second sister had been by Li Yuan’s side when he entered Chang'an, so her husband’s family had not gone to extremes and had protected her life.

As for the affection between his second sister and her husband, for most people in this ancient era, speaking of "love" between husband and wife was a luxury; being as respectful as guests was already considered a good marriage.

By comparison, the marriages of his third, fourth, and fifth sisters could be considered truly happy.

In this era, unless there were mutual interests between the maternal family and the husband’s family, even among the nobility, the maternal family did not often keep in touch with their married daughters.

Li Xuanba had just performed a great service, and his official rank was higher than those of his brothers-in-law, who had already reached the age of adulthood and were wearing the cap of manhood. Yet, he still respectfully visited them, bringing belated wedding gifts and blessings to his newlywed sisters and their husbands. The brothers-in-law felt respected, and the sisters felt valued. Even Li Wuniang, after recovering from the daze of her husband’s magnificent beauty, shed tears at Li Xuanba’s thoughtfulness.

Chai Shao, who was well-acquainted with Li Xuanba, said to Li Zhao, "Dede is just as good to you as he was when you were young. You should be at ease now."

Li Zhao laughed and scolded, "Don't slander me. I have always been at ease; it was you who were worried."

Chai Shao smiled and conceded, offering no rebuttal.

Before she was married, the affection Li Zhao received at the Tang Duke’s mansion was no less than that of Li Jiancheng. But after she married, aside from the routine visits during festivals, her maternal family had almost no contact with her.

Even knowing that this was how things were after marriage, Li Zhao could not help but feel sad.

When Li Xuanba was still in Daxing, Li Zhao could often meet her brothers regarding business matters. Once Li Xuanba and Li Shimin left Daxing, business affairs were mostly discussed between the stewards, and Li Zhao’s last channel for frequent contact with her family was severed.

Li Zhao often worried that perhaps, aside from her name, she no longer had any connection to her former kin.

It was only when Li Xuanba came to visit her this time that Li Zhao finally breathed a sigh of relief.

Li Zhao sighed to her closest personal maid, "I used to think that the Second Brother was the closest to me, and that the Third Brother always prioritized etiquette over affection toward his kin. But now that I have seen more of the world, I realize that the Third Brother might actually be the one who values affection the most."

The maid understood what her mistress meant, "It is not that the Second Brother is not close to you, My Lady, it is just that the Third Brother’s thoughtfulness exceeds that of others. Most young masters would not be so attentive and respectful to their sisters after they have married."

Li Zhao nodded and sighed, "I wasn't good enough to him in the past."

The maid said, "My Lady, please don't say that. To secure a path for himself, the Third Brother was willing to share his business with you to help manage. You have also always supported him. The bond between you and the Third Brother is truly rare in this world."

Li Zhao wore a look of reminiscence, "Yes, even back then, he already showed that he was different from others."

Li Siniang and Li Wuniang also spoke to their husbands about the soap shop.

"When we were young, we didn't understand and just thought we were playing along with the Third Brother’s whims. It was only after we married and began managing our own households that we realized how much peace of mind it gives to have that private property in our hands. The Third Brother was already thinking of his sisters back then."

Duan Lun and Zhao Cijing were not familiar with the Tang Duke’s mansion. When they first heard that Li Sanlang had started a soap shop and had even allowed his unmarried sisters to invest in it, they gained a new layer of understanding regarding Li Xuanba.

If he could even take care of his sisters, Li Xuanba must be exceptionally good to his family. Recalling the rumors circulating among the nobility and officials about the discord between the brothers of the Tang Duke’s mansion, both Duan Lun and Zhao Cijing could not help but feel a bit sorry for Li Xuanba.

People value first impressions. Li Xuanba looked gentle and humble, and even before he had reached the age of manhood, he already displayed a refined and noble temperament. Coupled with the fact that Li Xuanba was truly young when the rumors of brotherly discord first emerged, Duan Lun and Zhao Cijing could not help but lean toward favoring him.

Duan Lun said to his wife, "After interacting with Li Dalang, I originally thought he was a man of chivalry, but it seems I misjudged him."

Li Siniang whispered, "It wasn't appropriate for me to speak ill of my own family before. Now that I am your wife, I am part of your family, so I dare to tell you: stay away from Li Dalang."

Duan Lun held his wife’s hand and said, "You know your own family best, my lady. I will listen to you."

Li Siniang exchanged a tender look with Duan Lun, "Mm."

Zhao Cijing also said to Li Wuniang, "You used to praise the Second and Third Brothers often; having met them today, you were right to do so."

Being praised by Zhao Cijing, Li Wuniang was too shy to speak.

Although Zhao Cijing was accustomed to women’s infatuation with him, he found his wife’s excessive shyness rather amusing.

He waved his hand in front of Li Wuniang, "My lady, come back to us. If you continue like this, should I wear a mask to speak with you?"

Li Wuniang covered her face and shook her head vigorously, "I... the Master is right. I just knew you would like the Second and Third Brothers."

Zhao Cijing said, "I haven't met the Second Brother yet, but I have certainly decided to befriend the Third Brother."

Although Zhao Cijing possessed some martial skill, he was not particularly adept at it; his personality leaned more toward that of a scholar who enjoyed splashing ink in a study.

Li Yuan and Li Jiancheng were pure martial men. Although they were very close to him, whenever they met, they would either drag him out to drink or take him hunting—things Zhao Cijing found difficult to handle.

The moment he saw Li Xuanba, he felt they would get along well.

Hearing that the Second Brother was also a man who loved hunting, Zhao Cijing thought that even if the Second Brother was great, he would surely get along better with the Third Brother.

After establishing a preliminary friendly relationship with his brothers-in-law, Li Xuanba did not immediately return to Luoyang.

Returning to Luoyang meant facing his parents and Li Jiancheng, which left him feeling vexed; he wanted some peace and quiet for a while.

He and his second brother had performed great deeds and were promoted to the rank of *Chaoqing Daifu* (Fifth Rank), the same level as Li Jiancheng. However, Li Jiancheng’s rank came from his family’s shadow, while he and his second brother had earned theirs with the heads of the Tuyuhun Khan’s men. Even without considering the age gap, just looking at the reasons for their ranks, Li Jiancheng was completely overshadowed by them.

Li Jiancheng was still a young man in his early twenties, and his heart and cultivation were not yet refined enough; it was inevitable that he would feel uncomfortable seeing them.

His parents hoped for harmony among their children, and seeing this, they couldn't help but feel anxious, often nagging them about it.

Li Shimin was thick-skinned; he would laugh off whatever he heard as if he hadn't heard it at all, spending his days obsessed with hunting.

Li Xuanba was too lazy to listen to his parents’ lectures on brotherly harmony.

Since his teachers were all in Daxing, Li Xuanba wrote a letter back to Luoyang, stating that he intended to study with his teachers for a period of time.

Li Xuanba had loved reading since he was a child. Now that he could finally settle his mind to pursue his studies, even his parents found it hard to disturb him.

Li Yuan said to Lady Dou, "The Second Brother practices his martial arts the moment he returns, and the Third Brother studies the moment he returns. That is why my Second and Third sons are so outstanding."

Lady Dou smiled, "Indeed."

She would wait until the Second Brother returned from his hunt to give him a good scolding.

*Look at your brother, then look at yourself! Do you think I am as easily fooled as your father, believing you are "practicing martial arts"?*

*You have already wasted over a year of studies at the frontier, and instead of thinking about catching up, you just play every day, don't you?*

After returning to her room, Lady Dou sighed, rubbing her temples. Each of the four sons she had given birth to gave her a different kind of headache.

"The Third Brother is hiding in Daxing because he is impatient to see the Eldest, isn't he?" Lady Dou sighed.

After the death of the Old Lady Dugu, Mother Zhang, who had been serving by Lady Dou’s side, spoke in a dull voice, though her words carried a hint of bitterness, "Only by keeping the Second and Third Brothers away from the Eldest will there be brotherly harmony."

Lady Dou lowered her hands and gave a bitter smile, "Perhaps. I always thought that time could mend their relationship. It was clearly much more harmonious before."

Mother Zhang said, "Wasn't that previous 'mending' just the Second and Third Brothers constantly making concessions? Because they are more sensible and filial, they are the ones who must keep yielding. My Lady, how are you any different from the Old Lady now?"

Lady Dou’s bitter smile deepened, "I am not favoring the Eldest."

Mother Zhang said nothing more.

After the Old Lady passed away, Mother Zhang often thought that the Second and Third Young Masters were more filial and thoughtful, especially the Third Young Master’s kindness, which was plain for all to see. If only the Old Lady had favored them instead, how happy they would have been.

That rebellious beast Li Jiancheng, who had literally angered his grandmother to death—why was his life so good, and why did everyone favor him?! Just because he was the legitimate eldest son of the Tang Duke’s mansion? And yet, he *was* the legitimate eldest!

*Heaven, if you have eyes, please send a bolt of lightning to strike this unfilial and unkind beast dead!*

Every time Mother Zhang recalled the entire process of the Old Lady going from being in good health to being angered into illness and eventually death by Li Jiancheng, she was so filled with hatred she couldn't sleep.

What was even more painful than the hatred was that even after such treatment, the only person the Old Lady valued before she died was still Li Jiancheng!

Mother Zhang naturally knew that her Lady was different from the Old Lady. The Old Lady had favored him blindly, while her Lady only hoped that her children could live in harmony, thus tacitly allowing the concessions that the Second and Third Brothers made.

Both the palm and the back of the hand are made of flesh; her Lady had to maintain this harmony.

So, Mother Zhang said nothing more.

It was useless to speak; what was there to say?

She only hoped that her Lady would not be angered to death by that beast Li Jiancheng, just as the Old Lady had been.

Mother Zhang left after serving Lady Dou.

Lady Dou dismissed her personal maid, who looked troubled and seemed to have something to say.

She was left alone in the room.

She sat motionless for a long time, as if something was pressing down on her back, causing her spine and waist to slump bit by bit.

Lady Dou collapsed onto her bedding, sobbing silently.

The Tang Duke’s mansion was flourishing, but in Lady Dou’s heart, she suffered more with each passing day, as if what lay ahead was not a path of blooming flowers, but an abyss.

They were all her children; what could she do?

...

After being scolded by his mother, Li Shimin scratched his head, *Ah, where is my A-Xuan? Where did my big brother go? When did I lose him?*

Lady Dou was amused to anger by her foolish second son, "What do you mean 'lost'? The Third Brother went to Daxing to study, and what are you doing? Hmm? How much longer do you intend to play?"

Li Shimin mumbled, "I wasn't playing, I was honing my martial arts... ah, ouch, ouch, ouch, Mother, Mother, don't twist my ear!"

Lady Dou pinched her second son’s ear and gave it a half-turn, "Hmm? Honing martial arts? Your father might believe your ghost stories, but do you think I will? You crawled out of my belly; do you think I don't know what kind of character you have?"

Li Shimin begged for mercy, "I was wrong, I was wrong, Mother, be gentle! My ear is going to fall off!"

Lady Dou ignored his pleas, only slightly loosening her grip to a force that would hurt but not injure, while continuing to lecture him on his recent playfulness.

Li Shimin pouted and admitted his fault.

The second son’s admission brought Lady Dou no comfort. She saw through them: all four of her sons were quick to admit their faults but stubbornly refused to change.

Every single one of them!

"I'll go to Daxing to pick up my brother, and by the way, I'll continue to study with the teachers," Li Shimin said with a fawning smile after Lady Dou finally let go, clutching his ear.

Lady Dou poked the forehead of her fawning second son, "What 'by the way'? Studying is the 'by the way'!"

Li Shimin said solemnly, "I am going to study, and by the way, I will pick up my brother!"

Lady Dou pinched her son’s lips and scolded him with a smile, "Neither is 'by the way'! You go now and return before the start of winter. The Third Brother is in poor health and has already suffered for a year in the northern frontier; he must spend this winter in Luoyang to recover!"

Li Shimin nodded like a bird pecking at grain, "Yes, yes, yes, I will go right away. Can I take Xiao Wu with me? He has been clinging to me tightly lately."

He now took Xiao Wu with him every day when he went hunting.

Lady Dou stopped smiling and said calmly, "If you take the Fourth Brother with you, I will allow you to take Xiao Wu."

Li Shimin said without hesitation, "Then I won't take him."

Lady Dou’s fingers trembled slightly.

She said earnestly, "The Fourth Brother is also your brother."

Li Shimin knew his mother was hurting inside, but he did not compromise, "If the Fourth Brother treated me and A-Xuan as his brothers, I would naturally acknowledge him as such. But has he? Even if he was ignorant in the past, he is seven or eight years old now, and has been raised by Father and Mother for so long, yet after A-Xuan and I returned..."

Li Shimin snorted coldly and continued, "Mother, he said to our faces, 'I thought you sickly ghost would die in the northern frontier.' He was punished, and I didn't hold it against him. But until he changes, I will not be close to him, and I will stop A-Xuan from being blindly kind."

Li Shimin bowed, "I don't want to make you sad, Mother, so I have always endured. I can keep enduring, but Mother, it’s not that A-Xuan and I haven't tried to be close to him. I am indeed lazy to deal with him, but has A-Xuan ever been bad to him from childhood until now?!"

The more Li Shimin spoke, the more aggrieved he felt.

When they were young, his brother had foolishly been good to Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji, and what did he get in return? Li Jiancheng could at least maintain a facade of harmony, but Li Yuanji had bullied his sickly brother from childhood. Did his mother really think his brother hadn't been good enough to Li Yuanji?

Lady Dou said, "The Fourth Brother is still young; he is just a bit mischievous. He will be sensible when he grows up."

Li Shimin interrupted, "Then let's wait until he grows up and is sensible. A-Xuan’s health is poor; he cannot handle being angered. If you insist on me and Li Yuanji performing brotherly affection, I won't go to Daxing. I can keep Li Yuanji by my side in Luoyang at any time."

Lady Dou felt a pang of sorrow, "How can you say such things? The Fourth Brother is my child, and aren't you and the Third Brother my children too? Have I ever been bad to you? Sigh, go then. But you cannot take Xiao Wu. Second Brother, you should understand what I mean."

Li Shimin lowered his hand and said in a muffled voice, "I understand. Li Yuanji is my brother by the same mother; if I am better to my half-brother than to him, it will be even harder to repair my relationship with Li Yuanji."

Lady Dou said, "As long as you understand. Xiao Wu is being taken care of by Aunt Wan, so you don't need to worry. Xiao Wu has grown up; he understands it himself."

*Li Shimin thought to himself, when it comes to Li Yuanji, he is still young; when it comes to Xiao Wu, he is already grown up. Mother, you really are biased.*

But Li Shimin knew that his mother’s bias was natural. Li Yuanji was her child.

Even if his mother tried as much as possible to treat Xiao Wu as her own in all matters, the feelings were ultimately different.

He could only be thankful that he and A-Xuan were also her children.

Li Xuanba did not know that his second brother was about to be sent to Daxing by their mother.

If he had known, he would have definitely complained to his teachers in advance, asking them to give his second brother a good lesson.

Li Xuanba had written to his second brother when he was preparing to stay and study. His second brother had replied that he was busy hunting and wouldn't come.

He was truly impressed.

As expected of a hobby that even Wei Zheng couldn't dissuade him from.

"Hmph, Wei Zheng couldn't stop him, but Mother is still here," Li Xuanba sneered, "Second Brother just needs a beating from Mother!"

Although he didn't know his second brother was rushing to Daxing, he had accurately guessed his fate, though he couldn't pinpoint the timing.

His three teachers were all very strict, but for Li Xuanba, who loved to learn and had a photographic memory, this bit of academic pressure was nothing.

Xue Daoheng did not teach Li Xuanba poetry, but instead taught him official document writing and the experience he had gained while serving as a local official. Li Xuanba did not encounter any difficulties in his studies.

The difficulty he encountered was when Yuwen Bi asked him if he wanted to meet Yuwen Zhu in secret.

Li Xuanba thought for a long time and refused.

He confessed his original lifespan to Yuwen Bi.

"I may not live past sixteen, so it is better not to meet before then. We can just correspond by letter. If I pass away in the future, Lady Yuwen won't be too heartbroken," Li Xuanba said, "Please keep this a secret for me, Teacher."

Yuwen Bi sighed and said, "I knew you were sickly from the beginning, and I have discussed it with you: if you pass away, Zhu'er will still enter your family."

Li Xuanba said, "I know. With Mother and the Second Brother and his wife taking care of her, Lady Yuwen will live very well and freely. Please rest assured, Teacher."

Yuwen Bi said, "I am sorry that I let Zhu'er marry you for the sake of the status of a Princess."

Li Xuanba shook his head, "It is my blessing to allow an excellent woman to continue her dreams and to have that excellent woman become my wife in name."

Yuwen Bi said, "You will surely survive this death-fated tribulation."

Li Xuanba smiled, "I think so too. Once I pass my sixteenth birthday, I will go see her. Teacher, please do not tell anyone about this."

Yuwen Bi patted Li Xuanba’s head, "Don't worry, I won't tell anyone."

Yuwen Bi was deeply saddened, so saddened that he fell ill.

Li Xuanba felt very guilty. Perhaps he had underestimated his position in Teacher Yuwen’s heart and should have found another excuse.

But he didn't want to hide it from Teacher Yuwen.

If there were no death-fated tribulation, he would have actually liked to meet Yuwen Zhu.

Ten years after transmigrating, the soul of his past life and the body of the child in this life had assimilated. He could fight with his brothers as childishly as any child and treat many things from his past life as mere experience. Only the bone-deep sense of loneliness remained, difficult to resolve.

Li Xuanba’s first stirrings of love in his past life were in middle school.

Like many adolescents, his first stirrings were not directed at any specific person. It was just that one day, he suddenly felt that a girl who brushed past him was cute, and then he realized the existence of romantic love.

The stirrings of adolescence lasted throughout his middle and high school years. He, like most of his peers, threw himself into his studies; there was no early romance, only the palpitations in his heart that would not disappear.

Those palpitations became concrete through the many novels and magazines describing the green love of students, and through the rumored stories of others’ romances.

Then, at seventeen, his palpitations came to an abrupt end along with his youth and stable life.

While struggling to survive, Li Xuanba had no energy to think about love or starting a family, and even less intention of dragging others down.

Only when he was sick, during the New Year, or when he was lying in a hospital bed after being nearly beaten to death, would Li Xuanba desperately hope that someone was with him.

At those times, he would dream of his younger self and a girl whose face he couldn't see, walking hand in hand on a sun-drenched school playground.

All his imaginations about love remained in his youth.

Now that he had truly become a youth, and there was indeed a girl whose face he didn't yet know who would be with him forever, Li Xuanba thought he could cultivate feelings with her smoothly, but he retreated when it came time to meet.

*If we truly develop feelings, but I have to leave this world, what should I do?*

Li Xuanba could leave his parents and brothers with peace of mind.

He knew his father’s kindness would change; he knew that although his mother loved him, she had other children she loved; he knew his second brother would wail for him, but his second brother had Empress Zhangsun, many officials who were like friends, and the world.

His relatives would easily walk out of the sorrow of losing him.

Moreover, his feelings for his relatives were very restrained. Because these relatives came from history books, he knew their future.

All the interpersonal relationships around him were mostly those recorded in history books, mostly relationships his second brother would have had anyway.

He was a vassal, a shadow, a moon that could only be seen by the light of the sun.

But Yuwen Zhu was different. She was the only "character" among those closely related to him who did not exist in the history books.

It was only when he heard they were going to meet that Li Xuanba realized his cowardice.

He regretted it deeply.

*If I had known, I shouldn't have even written the letters.*

"Chirp! Chirp!"

While Li Xuanba was lost in thought, Wudi bumped into him.

Li Shimin took Hanjou hunting, but Wudi insisted on sticking to Li Xuanba, so Li Xuanba brought Wudi to Daxing.

Wudi would fly out to play and hunt on its own during the day and obediently return home at night.

For some reason, it had returned early today.

Li Xuanba stroked Wudi’s head, "What's wrong?"

Wudi couldn't speak; it just looked at Li Xuanba quietly.

Li Xuanba saw his own reflection in Wudi’s dark, round eyes.

*How pathetic.*

...

After serving her grandfather his medicine, Yuwen Zhu returned to her room.

She sat on an embroidered stool, staring blankly at the painting on the table depicting flying snow, a golden eagle, and a youth galloping on horseback.

Although several days had passed, the fact that she had been refused a meeting still made Yuwen Zhu feel stifled.

Even though she knew Li Sanlang was strict with etiquette and there was nothing wrong with not meeting before marriage, she couldn't help but think: *If I had written my letter more interestingly, would it have been different?*

*I must have been disliked.*

"It would be strange if a freak like me wasn't disliked," Yuwen Zhu muttered to herself, "Who would fancy a freak who buries her head in medicinal herbs all day, whose scent of medicine can't even be washed away by soap? What are you expecting?"

She picked up a brush, wanting to draw on the painting on the table.

But when the brush was about to fall on the paper, it remained, as before, suspended an inch above the paper, unable to get any closer.

Yuwen Zhu waved her hand, threw the brush on the table, got up, walked to the bed, took off her shoes and socks, climbed onto the bed, and curled up under the quilt, sitting cross-legged like a small triangular mountain of bedding.

After staying in the quilt mountain for a while, she would regain her calm.

"Chirp! Chirp!"

"Ah?! Where did this big bird come from!! Go away!!"

"Is this someone’s hunting eagle? It even has a silk ribbon tied around its neck. Did it get lost?"

"Chirp, chirp, chirp!"

"Damn hunting eagle! Don't grab my peonies!"

"Ah! It landed on the roof! It’s tearing off the tiles!"

"Chirp! Chirp! Chirp!"

"Is this beast making weird faces to mock us?"

"How can a bird mock a person... Damn! It can even use its claws to throw tiles at people? Is it a bird or a monkey?!"

Yuwen Zhu poked her little head out from a gap in the quilt mountain.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第87章 千里姻缘傻雕牵 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第87章 千里姻缘傻雕牵

=

屋外还在吵闹。

宇文珠穿好鞋子， 整理了一下衣裳，走到窗口，将窗户推开一条缝， 小心翼翼往外探望。

外面乱作一团， 人越聚越多。

这么多人， 好像不危险？

宇文珠再早熟，也有少女活泼的心性。

她抑制不住好奇心，打开门：“发生什么事了？”

“哎哟， 我的小娘子呀，赶紧进去！那是猎鹰！会伤人！”乳母赶紧拦住宇文珠。

宇文珠仰头，一只大鸟蹲在屋檐上， 脑袋左歪右歪，不像是猎鹰， 倒像是猫头鹰。

宇文珠的视线落在大鸟的脖子上。

大鸟脖子上的长羽毛连丝绸围脖都挡不住， 很帅气地披在胸口和背上，在阳光下闪烁着微微的金光。

宇文珠双手捂住嘴：“金雕？……这围脖，乌镝？！”

大鸟胸前垂着的方巾一角上，大大的“乌镝”二字十分显眼。

乌镝展开翅膀：“啾啾！”

他从屋顶上滑翔下来，落在了宇文珠的面前。

“小娘子， 快跑！”乳母挡在宇文珠面前，其他奴仆举起手中的长棍对准了乌镝。

宇文珠忙道：“等等！不要伤它！是我认识的人……金雕！”

乳母惊讶回头：“什么金雕？小娘子认识？”

宇文珠从乳母身后探出小脑袋：“乌镝， 你是来送信的吗？”

她从书本中读到过猎鹰送信的故事。祖父说猎鹰只受猎鹰人控制，若离开猎鹰人太远就会逃走，虽然有极小的概率可以训练送信， 耗费的精力得不偿失， 所以基本只出现在故事中。

但李三郎养的乌镝很聪明， 说不定已经被训练得会送信了。不然怎么会这么巧？

乌镝听到宇文珠的话， 眨了眨眼睛，一张鸟脸，居然做出了一个生动的迷惘表情。

乳母道：“这畜生听不懂……啊！它好凶！”

乌镝眼睛一横，作势要啄人。

奴仆又紧张起来，手中的长棍再次握紧。

这时拿着刀和弓箭的护卫也跑了过来。

宇文珠焦急道：“乌镝，你是乌镝吧？你是为三郎……我是说，李三郎，李、李玄霸，你的主人送信吗？”

乌镝眼睛睁圆，然后摇头。

宇文珠：“……你能听懂我说的话？！”

乳母惊呼：“畜生鸟居然听得懂人话！”

乌镝愤怒：“啾啾啾！啾啾啾！”

乳母赶紧道：“我是说你怎么凶我，你居然听得懂我骂你？我错了，你不是畜生，你是聪明鸟，聪明……金雕对吧？这名字真富贵，好金雕，别生气了，我等会儿从厨房里给你拿肉赔罪。”

乌镝眯起雕眼睛：“啾啾，啾啾啾。”

乳母再次惊呼：“它是在说，让我别骗它吗？天啦，我居然能听懂畜……金雕的话！”

“怎么回事？哪来的畜生鸟！”膀大腰圆的护卫总管挽着弓走来。

乌镝气得跳脚：“啾啾，啾啾啾！啾啾啾啾！”

它展开翅膀使劲扑腾，就像是一个人指着人骂。

宇文珠一手捂着嘴笑，一手拦住护卫大伯：“辛阿伯，不是畜生，是李三郎养的金雕，名为乌镝。它应该是来送信的。”

乌镝一边骂一边摇头。

宇文珠问道：“不是送信？那是来做什么？”

乌镝骂得更加厉害，连刚来的护卫都从一连串鸟语听出了激烈的脏话错觉。

宇文珠苦笑：“我听不懂呀。三郎没让你带什么东西来吗？”

乌镝继续摇头，继续“啾啾啾”。

辛伯道：“李三郎君的雕？难道是迷路了。”

乌镝不屑：“啾！”屁！

辛伯：“……我怎么觉得他在骂我？”

乳母第一次见到一只仿佛精怪的大鸟。因为是自家小娘子的未来郎君养的鸟，所以她没有害怕，反而爱屋及乌喜欢得紧。

她笑道：“把李三郎君请来不就知道了？”

乌镝：“……”

众人非常明显地从乌镝那张不大的鸟脸上，看出了“鸟脸一僵”的神情。

宇文珠试探地问道：“你是自己偷偷来的？”

乌镝：“……”

这次众人居然从鸟脸上看出了“心虚”的神情。

辛伯震惊：“这鸟成精了吗？”

宇文珠赶紧道：“当然没有。只是它是李三郎孵出来的，从小精心教导，比旁的鸟聪明许多。没有成精，辛伯别乱说。”

宇文珠看见乌镝十分通人性的模样，大着胆子从乳母身后走出来，转身挡在乌镝面前，眉头微皱，提高声音：“今日之事，不可对外胡说。若谁对外传一字，我就把他交由祖父祖母打发出去！”

“打发什么？”宇文弼在老妻的搀扶下走来，“听说家里来了一只作乱的鸟？”

宇文珠道：“祖父，不是作乱的鸟，是李三郎的金雕乌镝。”

宇文弼疑惑：“乌镝？”

乌镝从宇文珠身后走出来，翅膀微微拱起，仿佛像顽童叉腰似的。

它仰着头：“啾啾！”

宇文弼带着病气的脸上浮现微笑：“真是神奇的金雕。既然是三郎的金雕，去请三郎过来，问问他怎么回事。”

乌镝脸上又出现心虚的神情，但很快，它的雕目重新变得坚定锐利。

我又没做错！妈来了，还会夸我！

李玄霸出门的时候，乌镝就在空中盘旋，早就记住了李玄霸出行的路线。

有时候李玄霸在老师家读书的时候，乌镝就偷偷藏在屋顶或者树顶打盹。

它可不是来玩的，而是来保护妈的。

所以李玄霸情绪低落时，乌镝聪明的鸟脑袋就发觉，是这个老头让李玄霸难过。

本来它听了李玄霸的话，很低调地隐藏自己。

但李玄霸持续许多日情绪没有好转，乌镝这幼稚的暴脾气就忍不住了。

金雕的心眼出了名的小，有仇必报。它毕竟又还是个小孩，脑容量也不大，哪懂什么隐忍和危险，这就来报复了。

不过它好歹还记得李玄霸对宇文弼恭敬的模样，没有做得太过。

而且李世民早就告诫过它很多次，没有他和李玄霸的命令不准伤人。所以乌镝只是发脾气折腾草木和瓦片。

“还真和三郎说的一样，像个顽童似的。”宇文弼丝毫没有害怕乌镝尖锐的嘴尖和爪尖。

他镇定地走到金雕面前伸出了手。

老妻拉住宇文弼：“小心他啄你！”

宇文弼道：“它若要啄人，早就啄了。”

说罢，他的手按在了乌镝的鸟头上。

乌镝被宇文弼的大手压得脑袋一垂。

在众人心惊胆战中，乌镝只是使劲甩头，甩开了宇文弼的手，然后嫌弃地往宇文珠身后藏。

宇文珠心头一跳，嘴角不由上翘。

宇文弼一愣，失笑道：“三郎大概给你写了许多乌镝的事。乌镝就交给你照顾了。还不快去把三郎叫来。”

辛伯道：“我亲自去吧。”

他扫了周围人一眼：“小娘子说的话你们都记住。”

宇文弼对老妻道：“劳烦你把家里的仆人都聚在一起好好叮嘱。”

老妻笑着抱怨：“都闹得这么大了，一一叮嘱还真麻烦。等三郎来，你一定要好好说说他。”

宇文弼道：“好。”

他扫了一眼狼藉的庭院：“就别收拾了，让三郎自己过来看。”

宇文弼犹豫后，做出了决定。

草原人都说金雕是雪山的精灵，是神灵的使者。今天金雕没有李玄霸的命令却自己过来，或许是上天预示着什么吧。

如果这金雕是李玄霸叫来的，那也证明李玄霸后悔了。

老妻去叮嘱家里的仆人，宇文珠扶住祖父的手。

宇文弼道：“珠儿，你想见李三郎吗？”

宇文珠看到乌镝而雀跃的神情瞬间变得黯淡：“他不想。”

宇文弼平静道：“我只问你想不想。三郎是真的病弱，即使你再面临一次和安儿一样的分别，你也要见他吗？”

宇文珠微微一愣，问道：“李三郎生病了？”他是生病才不来见自己，不是嫌弃自己？

宇文弼道：“现在没有。”

宇文珠犹豫了一会儿，咬了一下下嘴唇，抑制住心中的羞涩：“我总归是要嫁给他。我去换身丫鬟穿的衣服！”

宇文弼脚步一顿，低头疑惑：“为何？”

宇文珠将小脸往旁边一侧，露出绯红的耳根：“他不见我，我见他。”

宇文弼思索了一会儿，才明白孙女的意思。他无奈地笑道：“好。”

乌镝歪头。

虽然它很多话都听不懂，听懂了也不知道这群人在说什么。但它有强烈的直觉，面前这人能呵止其他人对它动手，一定是这里的首领，跟着她总没错。

它迈开两条鸟腿，仰着鸟脑袋，大摇大摆地跟在宇文珠身侧走，引得周围仆人纷纷侧目。

“它飞着扑人的模样很帅，怎么走路的模样鬼鬼祟祟的？”

“收声！它听得懂，小心啄你！而且它是雕，不是鬼鬼祟祟，是鸟鸟祟祟！”

“不是雕雕祟祟吗？”

乌镝的脑袋仰得更高了。

听，他们都在夸我！

宇文弼和宇文珠注意到乌镝的神情，都忍不住笑了。

宇文珠顽皮道：“祖父，既然乌镝听得懂人话，是不是也该教它读书？免得听不懂别人骂它。”

宇文弼忍笑道：“等三郎来了，你和他说。”

宇文珠将脸往旁边一侧，不说话了。

宇文弼看着孙女这模样，心里又是叹息又是疑惑。

他叹息孙女将来若与李三郎分别，大概是会如与安儿分别一样难过。

至于他疑惑的自然是孙女应该没见过李三郎，怎么一副情窦初开的模样？总不能几封信，就让一贯自傲的孙女倾心了？至少也要见得一面再说吧？

大兴城的唐国公府里，李玄霸轻轻咳了一声，将书卷放下，拢了拢大氅上的毛绒绒围脖。

虽然现在只是入秋，但李玄霸身体不好，现在天气阴着，他就披上了有毛绒边的披风。

披风的毛绒边是李世民狩的雪狐皮。

雪狐难见。为了这张漂亮的雪狐皮，李世民特意寻人用金线在白色云纹厚绸子上，仿造绸子本身的花纹多绣了一层金色云纹，给穿着朴素的弟弟做了一件没阳光时看着很低调，一有阳光就闪得厉害的大氅。

李玄霸喜欢黑衣配黑色大氅。李世民对弟弟的衣着审美有微词已久。此次李玄霸出门时，他偷偷换了李玄霸装大氅的衣箱。

李玄霸在天气凉爽后拿大氅出来穿，看着满箱子花里胡哨的大氅，气得胸口疼。

这件大氅已经算是衣箱中较为朴素的了。

“三郎君，三郎君，不好啦！”向固一边跑一边喊。

李玄霸疑惑地站起身：“何事这么慌张？”

向固焦急道：“乌镝，乌镝被抓了！”

李玄霸惊讶：“它被狩猎的勋贵抓了？哪一家？”

向固道：“不是不是，它去宇文公家里捣乱，被宇文公，三郎君你的老师抓了。”

李玄霸脸上表情空白了一瞬：“啊？！”

李玄霸穿的本就是可以出外的衣服。他立刻匆匆跟着向固和辛伯去接自家犯事的雕崽。

路上，李玄霸听辛伯绘声绘色讲起乌镝在老师家做了什么“好事”。

李玄霸连连道歉：“是我的错，我没有教养好他。老师家中的损失我会赔偿。真是抱歉。”

听到乌镝没有伤人，李玄霸松了口气。

这雕孩子，在发什么疯！

李玄霸脑袋都想疼了，也想不明白为何乌镝会去宇文老师家里撒野。

他当然知道有时候乌镝没有出城狩猎，而是悄悄跟着自己。

乌镝一副洋洋得意的模样，以为自己没有看到他。他便和老师说了声后，没有拆穿乌镝。

不过乌镝确实藏着挺好，降落后大部分时候他都找不到乌镝藏哪里。

李玄霸本想把乌镝带去给老师看，但乌镝不耐烦见陌生人，每次他一提，乌镝就满地打滚，第二天更是一大早就飞得没影，他便作罢了。所以三位老师还没见过乌镝。

难道乌镝在宇文老师家隐藏时，被宇文老师家中某个奴仆伤了，所以前去报复？

它为何不和自己说啊？李玄霸和李世民早早教导乌镝和寒钩，遇到生气的事先告诉他们，不要自己去报复。这两只雕崽以前执行得很好，告状很流利，今天究竟怎么回事？

李玄霸百思不得其解，只能先去接雕，再去问当事雕。

到了宇文弼家中后，师母笑着亲自到门口迎接李玄霸：“大德，那雕真不是你派来的？”

李玄霸苦笑道：“师母，我是那样的人吗？”

师母微笑道：“这倒是。来，我领你去看看你那雕做了什么‘好事’。”

李玄霸被师母带到当时雕捣乱现场，看到院子中残花落叶，看到满院子的碎瓦片，头皮一阵一阵发麻，拳头捏紧。

“乌镝在哪？”李玄霸磨牙道。最近是太纵容它了！

师母笑着问道：“你知道这是谁的院子吗？”

李玄霸摇头摇了一半，然后猛地转头看向正屋半掩的门扉。

师母问道：“看出来了？”

李玄霸用指甲掐了一下手心，强装镇定道：“看不出来，但师母如此询问，我大概能猜到。”

师母继续微笑：“大德一直聪慧。好好道歉吧。”

李玄霸就像是木头机关人似的，僵硬地跟着师母穿过半圆形的拱门和曲折的回廊，走到隔壁的小院。

他一度想找借口逃走，但雕孩子做出这种混账事，责任感不允许他逃避。

还未进小院，李玄霸就听见乌镝欢快的鸣叫声。

金雕长得很威武霸气，声音却娇滴滴的，只会“啾啾”叫，像一只撒娇的小鸟。

养了两只雕崽后，李玄霸怀疑，纪录片里的雕鸣不会都是人类为了维护金雕的霸气，找其他鸟配音吧。

乌镝的“啾啾”叫声很轻快，李玄霸的心情沉重无比。

该揍的雕孩子！

“在那。”师母抬手一指。

李玄霸条件反射顺着师母所指，看见一位穿着丫鬟朴素衣服的少女，正捏着一块肉喂雕。

那雕十分不要脸地趴在少女腿上，张嘴讨食讨得欢。

丫鬟？

身穿丫鬟的服饰，头发也只用一根青色的发绳绑了两个发髻，还会赤手不嫌脏地捏着肉喂雕，应该真的是丫鬟？

少女侧对着李玄霸，李玄霸没有看到她的脸，只那双正喂鹰的手十分显眼。

李玄霸的视力很好，一眼就看到少女看似白皙的双手指腹厚厚的茧子。

平常贵族女性都会留指甲。

用颜料染指甲也是贵族女性打扮的一环。而且女性弹琴也需要指甲。不留指甲，与其他贵族女性玩耍的时候肯定会被笑话。

少女的指甲却只刚刚过指间，修建得十分圆润。

再加上她指间那厚茧子，一看就知道是经常干活的手。

李玄霸心情微微安定。

他在心底捏了一把汗，还以为师母要趁此机会带他与宇文珠私会。

但松口气的同时，李玄霸心中又生出一丝遗憾和失落。

“啾啾啾！”

乌镝最先发现李玄霸。但它把嘴里的肉吃完后，才转身对李玄霸扑腾翅膀。

少女用帕子在石桌上的水盆里蘸了一点水，替乌镝擦干净嘴和鸟脸，又不紧不慢地用一旁香皂洗完手，用另一条帕子擦干之后，才起身对李玄霸行礼，口称“李三郎君”。

少女的礼仪挑不出错，好像真的是丫鬟似的。

但李玄霸却和被雷劈了似的，止步不前。

师母问道：“大德，怎么呆住了？”

李玄霸机械地扭头不看行完礼后垂首站在一旁的“丫鬟”。

乌镝大摇大摆地走到李玄霸面前，低头拱了一下李玄霸的腿。

李玄霸低头，一把提起鸟脖子。

乌镝：“啾？”

李玄霸咬牙切齿骂道：“之后收拾你！”

乌镝：“啾啾啾？”为什么要收拾雕？雕在为你出气！

少女听见乌镝的惨叫声，抬头担忧地看了一眼，又立刻把头垂下。

李玄霸骂完乌镝后，就准备赶紧离开。

既然宇文珠没打算展露身份，他现在还可以逃。

李玄霸强装镇定对师母道：“我先把乌镝拎回家好好教训一顿，明日再来拜访老师师母，正式道歉。”

师母道：“不多留一会儿？”

李玄霸摇头：“不留了。我先……乌镝！”

乌镝从李玄霸手中挣脱，就像是一只要被抓去煲汤的大公鸡，展开翅膀连扑带跳冲到这个宅子的“首领”身后。

少女习惯性地微微展开手臂，遮住身后的雕崽。

李玄霸头上的小揪揪都要炸开，表演一番怒发冲胡帽了：“乌镝？！”

少女发现可能会露馅，赶紧放下手。

乌镝：“啾啾啾啾！”救我！

少女听着雕崽凄厉的求救声，表情犹豫。

师母扑哧笑道：“好了，别装了。大德，你一早就发现了，不是吗？”

李玄霸僵硬：“……”

少女惊讶：“发现了？”

师母笑着叹气：“你以为你装得很像？哪家的丫鬟看见贵人进来，还要先不紧不慢洗完手才行礼？”

少女恍惚。这里露馅吗？

她两耳“嗡”的一声，双霞绯红，也如李玄霸一样僵硬了。

师母看看两位先后僵硬的少年少女，笑得满脸皱纹就像是花儿般绽放。

真是开心啊。

“咳咳。”

在曲廊的拐角处，宇文弼拄着拐杖走出来，埋怨地看向老妻。

师母忙道：“我就不打扰你们了。”

说罢，她飞速朝着宇文弼走去，扶着宇文弼瞬间消失在曲廊拐角。

其他仆人也立刻走得干干净净。

李玄霸脖子僵硬得就像是生了锈的机器人似的，嘎吱嘎吱左右转动。

一个仆人都没有了？

整个院子空荡荡的，只剩下我和宇文珠两人？

说好的男女授受不亲呢！孤男寡女独自相会老师师母你们不管管吗！

“啾啾！”乌镝从宇文珠身后探头探脑。

哦，不止两人，还有一只傻雕。

这傻雕丢到二哥那里，放生了吧。

李玄霸还傻着的时候，宇文珠率先鼓足勇气，重新换了叉手礼，再次向李玄霸行礼。

李玄霸慌慌张张躬身作揖还礼。

宇文珠见李玄霸的模样，心中涌出委屈，话不由直了些：“李三郎君见到我很失望？”

李玄霸使劲摇头：“没有没有，我只是……”

只是什么？李玄霸卡了壳，说不下去了。

宇文珠抿了一下嘴，低声道：“乌镝还给你，你想走就走吧。”

说罢，她侧身将乌镝亮了出来。

乌镝：“啾？”

它立刻迈开鸟腿，重新回到了宇文珠的身后。

宇文珠：“……”

李玄霸：“……”

少年少女沉默又尴尬地对视一眼，宇文珠又默默往另一旁踱步。

乌镝十分敏捷地再次躲到了宇文珠的身后。

李玄霸深呼吸：“乌镝，出来！”

乌镝不仅不出来，还展开鸟翅膀，做出了抱腿的动作。

宇文珠结结巴巴道：“你、你自己过来抓？”

李玄霸犹豫了一下，把“这雕崽丢这不管了”的想法按下，绕着走到宇文珠的身后。

乌镝保持着抱腿的动作，鸟腿小碎步移动，与李玄霸隔着宇文珠绕圈子。

李玄霸绕了一圈，乌镝也绕了一圈。

宇文珠：“扑哧……咳，乌镝真可爱。”

乌镝仰头：“啾！”

李玄霸快气炸了，又不能在宇文珠面前骂人，更不能走到宇文珠面前对乌镝拉拉扯扯。

他用眼神威胁乌镝。乌镝把鸟头埋在宇文珠身上，看不见看不见。

李玄霸在心里念“不气不气，它只是一只雕崽，它懂什么”，尽可能心平气和地问道：“你现在知道怕了？今天怎么突然来宇文老师家捣乱？你不怕被人射成了漏子？”

乌镝抬头，委委屈屈地“啾啾啾”。

其实李玄霸见乌镝这反应，已经猜出了事情大概。

Chapter 87: A Thousand-Mile Marriage, Orchestrated by a Silly Eagle

=

The commotion outside continued.

Yuwen Zhu put on her shoes, smoothed her clothes, and walked to the window. Pushing it open just a crack, she peered out cautiously.

The scene outside was in total disarray, with people gathering in ever-increasing numbers.

With so many people around, it didn’t seem dangerous, did it?

No matter how precocious Yuwen Zhu was, she still possessed the lively spirit of a young girl.

Unable to suppress her curiosity, she opened the door. "What happened?"

"Oh, my dear young mistress, get back inside! That’s a hunting eagle! It’ll hurt someone!" Her wet nurse hurriedly tried to block Yuwen Zhu.

Yuwen Zhu looked up. A large bird was perched on the eaves, tilting its head left and right. It didn't look like a hunting eagle; it looked more like an owl.

Yuwen Zhu’s gaze fell upon the bird’s neck.

The long feathers around its neck were so thick that even a silk scarf couldn't hide them. They draped handsomely over its chest and back, shimmering with a faint golden luster under the sunlight.

Yuwen Zhu covered her mouth with both hands. "A golden eagle? ...And that scarf—is that 'Wu Di'?"

On the corner of the square cloth hanging from the bird’s chest, the two large characters "Wu Di" were clearly visible.

Wu Di spread its wings. "Chirp! Chirp!"

It glided down from the roof and landed right in front of Yuwen Zhu.

"Young mistress, run!" The wet nurse stepped in front of Yuwen Zhu, while the other servants raised their long staffs, aiming them at Wu Di.

Yuwen Zhu quickly said, "Wait! Don't hurt it! It’s someone I know... it's a golden eagle!"

The wet nurse turned back in surprise. "What golden eagle? You know it, young mistress?"

Yuwen Zhu poked her little head out from behind the wet nurse. "Wu Di, did you come to deliver a message?"

She had read stories about hunting eagles delivering messages in books. Her grandfather had said that hunting eagles only obeyed their handlers and would flee if they strayed too far; while there was a minuscule chance of training them to deliver mail, the effort required outweighed the gain, so it was mostly the stuff of legends.

But Li Sanlang’s Wu Di was very clever; perhaps it had been trained to deliver messages. Otherwise, how could this be such a coincidence?

Hearing Yuwen Zhu’s words, Wu Di blinked, its avian face actually forming a vivid expression of confusion.

The wet nurse said, "The beast doesn't understand... Ah! It’s so fierce!"

Wu Di glared, making a motion as if to peck someone.

The servants grew tense again, gripping their staffs tighter.

Just then, guards armed with swords and bows rushed over.

Yuwen Zhu said anxiously, "Wu Di, you are Wu Di, right? Are you delivering a message for Sanlang... I mean, Li Sanlang, Li, Li Xuanba, your master?"

Wu Di’s eyes widened, and then it shook its head.

Yuwen Zhu: "...You can understand what I’m saying?!"

The wet nurse exclaimed, "The beastly bird can actually understand human speech!"

Wu Di chirped angrily: "Chirp, chirp, chirp! Chirp, chirp, chirp!"

The wet nurse quickly said, "I meant, why are you being so fierce to me? You can actually understand me scolding you? I was wrong, you aren't a beast, you’re a clever bird, a clever... golden eagle, right? What a wealthy-sounding name. Good golden eagle, don't be angry. I’ll get you some meat from the kitchen later as an apology."

Wu Di narrowed its eagle eyes: "Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp."

The wet nurse exclaimed again, "Is it saying, 'Don't lie to me'? Heavens, I can actually understand the beast... the golden eagle!"

"What’s going on? Where did this beastly bird come from?" The burly head of the guards walked over, bow in hand.

Wu Di was so angry it stomped its feet: "Chirp, chirp, chirp! Chirp, chirp, chirp!"

It spread its wings and flapped them vigorously, looking just like a person pointing and scolding others.

Yuwen Zhu covered her mouth to hide her laughter with one hand, while using the other to stop the head guard. "Uncle Xin, it’s not a beast. It’s a golden eagle raised by Li Sanlang, named Wu Di. It must have come to deliver a message."

Wu Di shook its head while continuing to scold.

Yuwen Zhu asked, "Not delivering a message? Then what did you come here for?"

Wu Di scolded even more fiercely; even the newly arrived guards felt like they were hearing a string of intense profanities in bird-speak.

Yuwen Zhu gave a bitter smile. "I don't understand. Did Sanlang not have you bring anything?"

Wu Di continued to shake its head, continuing its "chirp, chirp, chirp."

Uncle Xin said, "Li Sanlang’s eagle? Could it be lost?"

Wu Di looked disdainful: "Chirp!" *Nonsense!*

Uncle Xin: "...Why do I feel like it’s scolding me?"

It was the wet nurse’s first time seeing a bird that seemed like a spirit. Because it was a bird raised by her young mistress's future husband, she wasn't afraid; instead, she loved the house and its crow, growing quite fond of it.

She smiled and said, "Why don't we just invite Li Sanlang over to find out?"

Wu Di: "..."

Everyone clearly saw a "bird-face stiffening" expression on Wu Di’s small face.

Yuwen Zhu asked tentatively, "Did you come here secretly on your own?"

Wu Di: "..."

This time, everyone saw a look of "guilt" on the bird’s face.

Uncle Xin was shocked: "Has this bird become a spirit?"

Yuwen Zhu quickly said, "Of course not. It was hatched by Li Sanlang and carefully taught since it was small, so it’s much smarter than other birds. It hasn't become a spirit, Uncle Xin, don't talk nonsense."

Seeing how human-like Wu Di was, Yuwen Zhu gathered her courage and stepped out from behind the wet nurse, turning to stand in front of Wu Di. She frowned slightly and raised her voice: "What happened today must not be spoken of outside. If anyone spreads a single word, I will have Grandfather and Grandmother send you away!"

"Send who away?" Yuwen Bi walked over, supported by his wife. "I heard a bird was causing trouble in the house?"

Yuwen Zhu said, "Grandfather, it’s not a bird causing trouble; it’s Li Sanlang’s golden eagle, Wu Di."

Yuwen Bi was puzzled: "Wu Di?"

Wu Di stepped out from behind Yuwen Zhu, its wings slightly arched, looking like a mischievous child with hands on its hips.

It tilted its head up: "Chirp!"

A smile appeared on Yuwen Bi’s sickly face. "What a marvelous golden eagle. Since it is Sanlang’s, go invite Sanlang over and ask him what is going on."

A look of guilt appeared on Wu Di’s face again, but soon, its eagle eyes became firm and sharp once more.

*I didn't do anything wrong! If Mom comes, she’ll even praise me!*

When Li Xuanba left the house, Wu Di had been circling in the air and had long since memorized his route.

Sometimes, when Li Xuanba was studying at his teacher’s house, Wu Di would secretly hide on the roof or the treetops to nap.

It hadn't come to play; it had come to protect Mom.

So, when Li Xuanba was in low spirits, Wu Di’s clever bird brain realized it was this old man who was making Li Xuanba sad.

Originally, it had listened to Li Xuanba and kept a low profile.

But after Li Xuanba’s mood failed to improve for many days, Wu Di’s childish, explosive temper couldn't take it anymore.

Golden eagles were famous for being petty and vengeful. After all, it was still just a child, and its brain capacity wasn't large; how could it understand restraint or danger? So it came to take revenge.

However, it still remembered how respectfully Li Xuanba treated Yuwen Bi, so it didn't go too far.

Moreover, Li Shimin had warned it many times not to hurt anyone without his or Li Xuanba’s orders. So Wu Di only threw a tantrum by messing with the plants and roof tiles.

"It really is just as Sanlang said, like a mischievous child." Yuwen Bi wasn't the least bit afraid of the eagle’s sharp beak and talons.

He calmly walked up to the golden eagle and extended his hand.

His wife pulled at him: "Be careful, it might peck you!"

Yuwen Bi said, "If it wanted to peck someone, it would have done so already."

With that, he pressed his hand onto Wu Di’s head.

Wu Di’s head drooped under Yuwen Bi’s large hand.

Amidst everyone’s trepidation, Wu Di merely shook its head vigorously, threw off Yuwen Bi’s hand, and then hid behind Yuwen Zhu in disgust.

Yuwen Zhu’s heart skipped a beat, and the corners of her mouth couldn't help but curl upward.

Yuwen Bi was stunned, then laughed helplessly. "Sanlang must have written you many things about Wu Di. I’ll leave Wu Di in your care. Hurry and go call Sanlang."

Uncle Xin said, "I will go myself."

He swept a glance at the surrounding people: "Remember what the young mistress said."

Yuwen Bi said to his wife, "Please gather the servants in the house and give them a stern warning."

His wife complained with a smile: "It’s already caused such a ruckus, giving individual warnings is quite a bother. When Sanlang comes, you must give him a good talking-to."

Yuwen Bi said, "I will."

He glanced at the messy courtyard: "Don't clean it up; let Sanlang come see it for himself."

After some hesitation, Yuwen Bi made a decision.

People of the grasslands said golden eagles were spirits of the snow mountains and messengers of the gods. Since the golden eagle had come on its own today without Li Xuanba’s orders, perhaps it was a sign from the heavens.

If this golden eagle had been called by Li Xuanba, it would prove that Li Xuanba regretted his actions.

His wife went to instruct the servants, and Yuwen Zhu held her grandfather’s arm.

Yuwen Bi said, "Zhu’er, do you want to see Li Sanlang?"

The joyful expression on Yuwen Zhu’s face at the sight of Wu Di instantly dimmed. "He doesn't want to."

Yuwen Bi said calmly, "I only asked if *you* want to. Sanlang is truly frail. Even if you have to face another separation like the one with An’er, do you still want to see him?"

Yuwen Zhu was slightly stunned and asked, "Li Sanlang is sick?" *He didn't come to see me because he was sick, not because he disliked me?*

Yuwen Bi said, "Not right now."

Yuwen Zhu hesitated for a moment, bit her lower lip, and suppressed the shyness in her heart. "I am destined to marry him anyway. I’m going to change into a maid’s clothes!"

Yuwen Bi paused in his steps, looking down in confusion: "Why?"

Yuwen Zhu turned her little face to the side, revealing her crimson earlobes. "He won't come to see me, so I will go see him."

Yuwen Bi pondered for a moment before he understood his granddaughter’s meaning. He smiled helplessly: "Very well."

Wu Di tilted its head.

Although it couldn't understand much of what they said, and didn't know what this group was talking about even if it did, it had a strong intuition: the person in front of it could stop others from hurting it, so she must be the leader here. Following her was never a mistake.

It strode forward on its two bird legs, head held high, swaggering along beside Yuwen Zhu, drawing curious glances from the surrounding servants.

"It looked so cool when it was swooping down to attack people, why does it look so sneaky when it walks?"

"Quiet! It can understand you, be careful it pecks you! And it’s an eagle, it’s not being sneaky, it’s being 'bird-y'!"

"Isn't it 'eagle-y'?"

Wu Di held its head even higher.

*Listen, they are all praising me!*

Yuwen Bi and Yuwen Zhu noticed Wu Di’s expression and couldn't help but laugh.

Yuwen Zhu said mischievously, "Grandfather, since Wu Di can understand human speech, shouldn't we teach it to read? So it doesn't fail to understand when others are scolding it."

Yuwen Bi suppressed a laugh: "When Sanlang comes, you can tell him that."

Yuwen Zhu turned her face to the side and said nothing more.

Watching his granddaughter, Yuwen Bi felt a mix of sighing and confusion.

He sighed because if his granddaughter were to be separated from Li Sanlang in the future, she would likely be as heartbroken as she was when she parted with An’er.

As for his confusion, naturally, it was that his granddaughter should have never met Li Sanlang, so why was she acting like a girl in the throes of first love? Surely a few letters couldn't have made his usually proud granddaughter lose her heart? At the very least, they should meet once first, right?

In the Tang State Duke’s mansion in Daxing City, Li Xuanba coughed lightly, put down his scroll, and pulled the fluffy collar of his cloak tighter.

Although it was only early autumn, Li Xuanba’s health was poor, and with the weather being overcast, he had donned a fur-trimmed cloak.

The fur trim was made from the pelt of a snow fox hunted by Li Shimin.

Snow foxes were rare. To get this beautiful pelt, Li Shimin had specifically found someone to embroider a layer of golden cloud patterns onto the thick white cloud-patterned silk, imitating the fabric’s own design. He had made it for his brother, who dressed plainly, so that the cloak would look low-key without sunlight but shine brilliantly the moment the sun hit it.

Li Xuanba liked black clothes paired with a black cloak. Li Shimin had long had reservations about his brother’s aesthetic choices. When Li Xuanba went out this time, he had secretly swapped the contents of Li Xuanba’s cloak chest.

When Li Xuanba took out a cloak after the weather turned cool and saw a chest full of gaudy, flashy cloaks, he was so angry his chest hurt.

This current cloak was already the most modest one in the chest.

"Third Young Master, Third Young Master, it’s bad!" Xiang Gu shouted as he ran.

Li Xuanba stood up, puzzled: "What is the matter that has you so flustered?"

Xiang Gu said anxiously, "Wu Di, Wu Di has been caught!"

Li Xuanba was surprised: "Caught by some hunting noble? Which family?"

Xiang Gu said, "No, no, it went to cause trouble at Duke Yuwen’s house and was caught by Duke Yuwen, your teacher."

Li Xuanba’s expression went blank for a moment: "Huh?!"

Li Xuanba was already wearing clothes suitable for going out. He immediately hurried off with Xiang Gu and Uncle Xin to retrieve his wayward eagle cub.

On the way, Li Xuanba listened as Uncle Xin vividly recounted what "good deeds" Wu Di had done at his teacher’s house.

Li Xuanba apologized repeatedly: "It is my fault; I did not teach him well. I will compensate for the losses at my teacher’s house. I am truly sorry."

Hearing that Wu Di hadn't hurt anyone, Li Xuanba breathed a sigh of relief.

*This eagle child, what kind of madness is it having!*

Li Xuanba’s head ached just thinking about it; he couldn't understand why Wu Di would go and run wild at Teacher Yuwen’s house.

He certainly knew that sometimes, when Wu Di didn't go out of the city to hunt, it would secretly follow him.

Wu Di would act all smug, thinking he hadn't noticed. He had mentioned it to his teacher and hadn't exposed Wu Di.

However, Wu Di was indeed good at hiding; most of the time after it landed, he couldn't find where it was hiding.

Li Xuanba had intended to bring Wu Di to see his teachers, but Wu Di was impatient with strangers. Every time he brought it up, Wu Di would roll around on the ground, and the next day it would fly off at the crack of dawn, so he had given up. Thus, his three teachers had never met Wu Di.

Could it be that while Wu Di was hiding at Teacher Yuwen’s house, it was hurt by one of the servants, and thus went to take revenge?

*Why didn't it tell me?* Li Xuanba and Li Shimin had long taught Wu Di and Hanjou that if they encountered something that made them angry, they should tell them first, not take revenge on their own. These two eagle cubs had executed this well in the past and were very fluent at "tattling." What on earth was going on today?

Li Xuanba couldn't figure it out, so he could only go retrieve the eagle first and then question the eagle in question.

Upon arriving at Yuwen Bi’s house, the teacher’s wife smiled and personally came to the door to welcome Li Xuanba: "Dade, that eagle really wasn't sent by you?"

Li Xuanba gave a bitter smile: "Teacher’s wife, am I that kind of person?"

She smiled: "That is true. Come, I will take you to see what 'good deeds' your eagle has done."

Li Xuanba was led by her to the scene of the eagle’s mischief. Seeing the fallen flowers and leaves in the courtyard, and the shattered roof tiles everywhere, his scalp went numb and his fists clenched.

"Where is Wu Di?" Li Xuanba gritted his teeth. *I’ve been too indulgent with it lately!*

The teacher’s wife asked with a smile: "Do you know whose courtyard this is?"

Li Xuanba shook his head halfway, then suddenly turned his head to look at the half-hidden door of the main room.

She asked: "You figured it out?"

Li Xuanba pinched his palm with his fingernails and feigned calmness: "I couldn't tell, but since you asked, I can probably guess."

She continued to smile: "Dade has always been clever. Go apologize properly."

Li Xuanba moved like a wooden automaton, stiffly following her through the semi-circular archway and the winding corridors to the adjacent small courtyard.

He once wanted to find an excuse to run away, but since the eagle child had done such a disgraceful thing, his sense of responsibility wouldn't allow him to escape.

Before even entering the small courtyard, Li Xuanba heard Wu Di’s cheerful chirping.

The golden eagle looked majestic and imposing, but its voice was delicate, only capable of "chirping" like a spoiled little bird.

After raising two eagle cubs, Li Xuanba suspected that the eagle cries in documentaries were all dubbed by humans looking for other birds to maintain the golden eagle’s aura of dominance.

Wu Di’s "chirping" was very light and cheerful, and Li Xuanba’s mood was incomparably heavy.

*You eagle child that needs a beating!*

"There it is." The teacher’s wife pointed.

Li Xuanba reflexively followed her finger and saw a young girl dressed in simple maid’s clothes, pinching a piece of meat to feed the eagle.

The eagle was shamelessly lying on the girl’s lap, opening its mouth to beg for food happily.

*A maid?*

Dressed in maid’s attire, her hair tied in two buns with only a green hair tie, and not afraid of getting her hands dirty while feeding the eagle—could she really be a maid?

The girl was turned sideways to Li Xuanba, so he couldn't see her face, only her hands, which were feeding the eagle, were very conspicuous.

Li Xuanba had excellent eyesight, and at a glance, he saw the thick calluses on the fingertips of the girl’s seemingly fair hands.

Usually, noble women would grow their nails long.

Dyeing one’s nails with pigment was also part of a noble woman’s grooming. Furthermore, women needed nails to play the zither. If one didn't grow their nails, they would surely be mocked when playing with other noble women.

The girl’s nails, however, were just past the fingertips and trimmed very round.

Coupled with those thick calluses on her fingertips, one could tell at a glance that these were hands that worked often.

Li Xuanba’s mood settled slightly.

He broke into a cold sweat in his heart, thinking the teacher’s wife was going to take this opportunity to arrange a secret meeting between him and Yuwen Zhu.

But while he breathed a sigh of relief, a trace of regret and disappointment arose in his heart.

"Chirp, chirp, chirp!"

Wu Di was the first to spot Li Xuanba. But it only turned to flap its wings at Li Xuanba after it had finished the meat in its mouth.

The girl used a handkerchief to dip a little water from a basin on the stone table, wiped Wu Di’s mouth and face clean, and then unhurriedly washed her hands with the soap on the side. After drying them with another handkerchief, she stood up and bowed to Li Xuanba, addressing him as "Li Sanlang."

The girl’s etiquette was flawless, as if she really were a maid.

But Li Xuanba felt as if he had been struck by lightning, stopping in his tracks.

The teacher’s wife asked: "Dade, why are you stunned?"

Li Xuanba mechanically turned his head, refusing to look at the "maid" who was standing to the side with her head bowed after finishing her bow.

Wu Di swaggered up to Li Xuanba and nudged his leg with its head.

Li Xuanba looked down and grabbed the bird by the neck.

Wu Di: "Chirp?"

Li Xuanba gritted his teeth and cursed: "I’ll deal with you later!"

Wu Di: "Chirp, chirp, chirp?" *Why deal with the eagle? The eagle was venting your anger!*

Hearing Wu Di’s miserable cry, the girl looked up in concern, then immediately lowered her head again.

After scolding Wu Di, Li Xuanba prepared to leave immediately.

Since Yuwen Zhu didn't intend to reveal her identity, he could still escape now.

Li Xuanba feigned calmness and said to the teacher’s wife: "I will take Wu Di home to discipline it properly, and I will come to visit you and Teacher tomorrow to apologize formally."

She said: "Won't you stay a little longer?"

Li Xuanba shook his head: "I won't stay. I’ll first... Wu Di!"

Wu Di broke free from Li Xuanba’s hand, looking like a rooster about to be caught for soup, spreading its wings and flapping and jumping to hide behind the "leader" of this residence.

The girl habitually spread her arms slightly, shielding the eagle cub behind her.

Li Xuanba felt like the little bun on his head was about to explode, performing a scene of "anger raising his hat": "Wu Di?!"

The girl realized she might have given herself away and quickly lowered her hands.

Wu Di: "Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!" *Save me!*

Hearing the eagle cub’s shrill cry for help, the girl looked hesitant.

The teacher’s wife chuckled: "Alright, stop pretending. Dade, you figured it out early on, didn't you?"

Li Xuanba was stiff: "..."

The girl was surprised: "You figured it out?"

The teacher’s wife sighed with a smile: "Do you think you were acting very convincingly? Which maid, upon seeing a noble enter, would insist on unhurriedly washing her hands before bowing?"

The girl was dazed. *That’s where I gave it away?*

Her ears buzzed, her cheeks flushed crimson, and she became as stiff as Li Xuanba.

The teacher’s wife looked at the two teenagers who had stiffened one after the other, laughing until the wrinkles on her face bloomed like flowers.

How truly delightful.

"Ahem."

At the corner of the winding corridor, Yuwen Bi walked out, leaning on his cane, and looked at his wife with a look of reproach.

She quickly said: "I won't disturb you two any longer."

With that, she hurried toward Yuwen Bi, supported him, and instantly disappeared around the corner of the corridor.

The other servants also immediately vanished completely.

Li Xuanba’s neck was as stiff as a rusted robot, creaking as he turned it left and right.

*Not a single servant left?*

*The whole courtyard is empty, leaving only me and Yuwen Zhu?*

*What happened to 'men and women should not touch'? Teacher, Teacher’s wife, aren't you going to manage this lone man and woman meeting in private!*

"Chirp, chirp!" Wu Di poked its head out from behind Yuwen Zhu.

*Oh, not two people, there’s also a silly eagle.*

*I should just dump this silly eagle at Second Brother’s place and release it into the wild.*

While Li Xuanba was still stunned, Yuwen Zhu was the first to muster her courage, performed a *chashou* bow again, and bowed to Li Xuanba once more.

Li Xuanba hurriedly bowed in return, flustered.

Seeing Li Xuanba’s reaction, a sense of grievance welled up in Yuwen Zhu’s heart, and her words became a bit more direct: "Is Li Sanlang disappointed to see me?"

Li Xuanba shook his head vigorously: "No, no, I just..."

*Just what?* Li Xuanba hit a wall and couldn't continue.

Yuwen Zhu pursed her lips and said in a low voice: "I’ll return Wu Di to you; you can leave if you want."

With that, she stepped aside to reveal Wu Di.

Wu Di: "Chirp?"

It immediately strode forward on its bird legs and returned to hide behind Yuwen Zhu.

Yuwen Zhu: "..."

Li Xuanba: "..."

The two teenagers looked at each other in awkward silence, and Yuwen Zhu silently paced to the other side.

Wu Di nimbly hid behind Yuwen Zhu again.

Li Xuanba took a deep breath: "Wu Di, come out!"

Wu Di not only refused to come out, but it also spread its wings and made a motion of hugging her leg.

Yuwen Zhu stammered: "Y-you, why don't you come over and catch it yourself?"

Li Xuanba hesitated for a moment, suppressed the thought of "just leaving this eagle cub here," and walked around to the back of Yuwen Zhu.

Wu Di maintained its leg-hugging posture, moving its bird legs in small, shuffling steps, circling around Yuwen Zhu to keep her between itself and Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba circled once, and Wu Di circled once.

Yuwen Zhu: "Pfft... ahem, Wu Di is really cute."

Wu Di tilted its head up: "Chirp!"

Li Xuanba was about to explode with anger, but he couldn't scold anyone in front of Yuwen Zhu, and he certainly couldn't walk up to her and start wrestling with Wu Di.

He threatened Wu Di with his eyes. Wu Di buried its head into Yuwen Zhu, *I can't see you, I can't see you.*

Li Xuanba chanted in his heart, *Don't be angry, don't be angry, it’s just an eagle cub, what does it know?* He asked as calmly as possible: "Do you know you’re in trouble now? Why did you suddenly come to Teacher Yuwen’s house to cause trouble today? Aren't you afraid of being shot into a sieve?"

Wu Di looked up and chirped aggrievedly: "Chirp, chirp, chirp."

In fact, seeing Wu Di’s reaction, Li Xuanba had already guessed the general idea of what had happened.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第87章 千里姻缘傻雕牵 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
既然乌镝不是迷路，而是故意来捣乱，还很注意分寸，可能是看自己心情不好，以为自己在这里受了欺负，来为自己“报复”。

而且乌镝这个鬼精鬼精的雕崽，估计已经发现宇文家与当初的裴世矩府邸一样，是自己和二哥能护得住它，会纵容它撒野的地方。

所以撒完野后，乌镝就心安理得地在这里吃起了鲜肉，半点没有害怕。

“乌镝，你这样有恃无恐，如果哪天真的遭遇了危险该如何是好？”李玄霸叹气道，“老师现在正在病中，否则你刚撒野，就被一箭射中了。罢了，现在和你说你也听不懂，回去慢慢教训你。”

李玄霸决定一定要让乌镝听懂“一箭双雕”的故事。

幸亏乌镝是在宇文老师家撒野，如果是在长孙老师家撒野，长孙老师会亲自教导乌镝“一箭双雕”的典故。

什么？这是李二郎李三郎养的雕？谁知道啊，先射下来再说。

宇文珠温声细语道：“确实该骂。若不是我认出了他围脖上的字，护院已经用弓箭了。”

她摸了摸乌镝的头：“快回去。难道你真的想一直跟着我？那我问李三郎把你讨来了？”

乌镝迷茫地抬头，没听懂。

李玄霸解释：“我这就走，不要你了。”

乌镝忙松开抱着宇文珠的翅膀，连滚带爬朝着李玄霸扑来，居然“啾啾啾”冒出了眼泪。

李玄霸接住扑来的雕崽，没好气道：“哭了？这就哭了？这么容易害怕，你干什么坏事？”

乌镝：“啾啾啾嘎嘎嘎！！”呜哇哇哇！

李玄霸无语：“都哭出鸭子叫了。”

“扑哧。”宇文珠捂嘴笑道，“乌镝果然如信中一样很有趣。”

李玄霸叹气：“是很调皮，又很娇气。我真担心能不能护得住它。它已经完全不像只雕了。”

说罢，李玄霸狠狠捏了一下雕头。

乌镝继续嘎嘎嘎哭，哭得鸟脸都湿透了。

宇文珠递来帕子：“给它擦擦。”

李玄霸犹豫了一会儿，小心翼翼捏着帕子一角接住帕子，以免碰到宇文珠的手。

看着李玄霸拘谨的模样，宇文珠这次没有怀疑李玄霸嫌弃她。

若嫌弃她，不该是这副模样。

李三郎只是害羞吧？宇文珠这么想，自己也害羞了。

若不是乌镝这么一闹腾，她断不可能鼓起勇气继续与李三郎说话，更别说递帕子了。

勇气已经鼓起来，宇文珠就不想退缩。

她已经与李三郎定亲，将来两人会一起度过一生，怎么也要把心里疙瘩解除了才行。

宇文珠拿起石桌旁小火炉上温着的水，为李三郎倒一杯水：“听闻你喝不惯味道太复杂的饮子，这饮子只放了温和的花瓣。”

宇文珠委婉地邀请，李玄霸硬着头皮拖着抱着他嘎嘎嘎哭的乌镝，乖乖落座。

宇文珠坐到另一边，为自己也倒了一杯花茶。

两人因为有乌镝“嘎嘎嘎”大哭作为背景音，气氛倒是不那么凝滞了。

宇文珠道：“我听闻你不愿意与我见面，还以为你嫌弃我。”

李玄霸忙道：“没有，不是，我……只是我……”

他掐了一把让他落到如此境地的乌镝的翅膀，在乌镝加大的“嘎嘎嘎”哭声中僵硬解释：“我只是，只是想着我可能活不到弱冠，所以不愿意耽误你。”

宇文珠疑惑：“怎么见一面就是耽误了？”

李玄霸：“……”这让他如何解释？

解释担心宇文珠对他动了情？这也太厚脸皮了。

而解释担心自己对宇文珠动了情，那也挺奇怪。

李玄霸支支吾吾，满脸赤红，仿佛变成了哑巴。

宇文珠低头看着自己粗糙的双手：“真不是因为我摆弄草药，不像个士女，才不想见我？”

李玄霸急促道：“不是！这爱好很好啊！”

宇文珠见李玄霸急着解释的模样，不知为何笑了出来：“好什么好？我寻访了许多医师，就是家中供奉的医师也不收女弟子，说是从未听过女子行医。行医要‘望闻问切’，女子如何对外男‘望闻问切’？”

宇文珠说着，神情失落：“若只是对着家中亲人行医，积累不出行医的经验，不过是生套医书，误了病人。”

李玄霸道：“女子无法对外男‘望闻问切’，外男又如何对女子‘望闻问切’？就连孙医师这样的良医在为女眷诊治的时候，也只能悬丝诊脉。这悬丝诊脉的准确度，与当面诊治肯定差了许多。天下有一半为女子，娘子就算只对着天下女子行医，积累的病例也不会少。”

李玄霸当着宇文珠的面叫出“娘子”的称呼时，差点咬了自己的舌头。

现在对陌生女子的称呼都是“娘子”，但到了后世，“娘子”是妻子的代称之一。这让李玄霸分外窘迫。

宇文珠在李玄霸的话说完后，呆怔了许久。

她拧转上半身，不顾礼仪也不顾害羞地直直看着李玄霸：“对女子行医？”

李玄霸躲避宇文珠的视线：“宇文娘子学医不是因为这个吗？天下皆是男医师，无人为女子仔细诊治。比如男子身上若得了生了疮，医师可为其割疮引脓。若换了女子，却只能喝着医师悬丝诊脉开的药硬扛。即使一些年老的医师可以直接为女子诊脉，但他们也不可能对女子做太细致的治疗。”

更不用说女子生育的鬼门关了。

为女子接产的都是稳婆，而稳婆只是生育过孩子的妇女，她们大部分没有医学经验，甚至连字都不识，相信一些神神鬼鬼的愚昧。

有些女子生完孩子后大出血，若有医师在，就可以为其缝线止血。

但此时的孕妇往往在病床上活活流血流到死。

将士们在战场上被砍了胳膊都能救，女子却是不能救的。

李玄霸偷瞟了一眼宇文珠的表情，见她露出了困惑的模样，猜到宇文珠可能只是单纯因照顾幼弟接触了医学后，喜欢上了医学，心里没有太高远的目的。所以她虽然现在对爱好很坚定，但这坚定或许也很脆弱。

宇文珠可能认为喜欢医学真的是离经叛道，除了她“自己喜欢”这个理由之外，没有任何值得她坚持的理由。

其实这样很好。

人最好还是别有太多高大上的理想，这样活着才开心。

只是看着宇文珠委屈的模样，李玄霸还是于心不忍。

偶尔、偶尔有一点高大上的理想，或许也比一直被人否定和自我否定开心？

李玄霸想了想，为宇文述讲了清末的一则故事：“我去张掖时见到了一桩很荒谬的丧事。有一家孕母难产，恰好有民间神医路过此家，就在那家人的同意下进屋施针，母子均安。但那孕母却在身体痊愈后，被村中流言逼得投河自尽。”

宇文珠神情恍惚：“若有女医师，她就不必受这苦。”

李玄霸却摇头：“宇文娘子，你这话不对。女子被男性医师救命时有了肌肤接触，也不该受这苦。男女之别，怎么能比得过性命大事？只是这世间不合情理的规矩难改，不能一蹴而就，就从眼下能做的做起。比如女子行医。”

李玄霸摸着终于结束鸭子哭的乌镝的鸟脑袋，语气十分平静，好像说的是很平常的事：“若宇文娘子成为当世名医，肯定会带动许多女子行医。天底下不知道有许多碍于男女之别，不该病逝却病逝的女子会因此得救。”

“如此善举，于朝堂会青史留名，于民间也会建祠立庙。宇文娘子现在做的就是这样流芳百世的事。夏虫不可语冰，燕雀焉知鸿鹄之志？宇文娘子不必为庸人所扰，请安心。”

宇文珠眨了眨眼，一双杏眼蒙上了水雾，就像是染上了晨露。

她笑道：“我没有鸿鹄那样高远的志向。”

李玄霸道：“论迹不论心。宇文娘子就是鸿鹄。”

宇文珠起身：“你说是就是吧。我还有事，不作陪了。”

她说完，急急转身，提着裙角，消失在李玄霸的视线中。

李玄霸掐着雕翅膀的手僵住。

他低头看着傻乎乎的雕崽。

乌镝：“？”

李玄霸咬牙切齿：“今天我要把你拔毛烤了吃！谁也救不了你！”

乌镝：“？？？！”

“啾啾！！！！”

救命！！！！
chunks.englishText:
Since Wu Di wasn't lost, but had come here to stir up trouble on purpose—and had been careful to keep it within bounds—it was likely that it had sensed his bad mood, assumed he was being bullied here, and had come to "avenge" him.

Furthermore, this wily little eagle cub had probably already realized that the Yuwen estate, much like the Pei Shiju residence back then, was a place where he and his Second Brother could protect it and would indulge its wild behavior.

And so, having finished its mischief, Wu Di was now contentedly pecking at fresh meat, showing not a shred of fear.

"Wu Di, if you act so brazenly, what will you do if you truly encounter danger one day?" Li Xuanba sighed. "My teacher is currently ill; otherwise, you would have been shot down by an arrow the moment you started your antics. Forget it, you wouldn't understand even if I told you now. I’ll teach you a lesson when we get back."

Li Xuanba decided that he must make Wu Di understand the story of "killing two birds with one stone."

It was fortunate that Wu Di was acting up at Teacher Yuwen’s house. If it had been at Teacher Zhangsun’s house, Teacher Zhangsun would have personally taught Wu Di the lesson of "killing two birds with one stone."

*What? This is an eagle raised by Li Erlang and Li Sanlang? Who cares? Shoot it down first, then we’ll talk.*

Yuwen Zhu said softly, "It truly deserves a scolding. If I hadn't recognized the characters on its collar, the house guards would have already used their bows and arrows."

She stroked Wu Di’s head. "Go back quickly. Do you really want to follow me forever? Shall I ask Li Sanlang to give you to me?"

Wu Di tilted its head, looking confused; it hadn't understood a word.

Li Xuanba explained, "I’m leaving right now, and I don’t want you anymore."

Wu Di hurriedly released the wings it had been using to hug Yuwen Zhu and scrambled toward Li Xuanba, actually letting out a "chirp, chirp, chirp" as tears welled up in its eyes.

Li Xuanba caught the lunging eagle cub and said irritably, "Crying? You’re crying already? If you’re so easily frightened, why do you go around causing trouble?"

Wu Di: "Chirp, chirp, chirp, quack, quack, quack!!" *Waaaaah!*

Li Xuanba was speechless. "You’re crying so hard you sound like a duck."

"Pfft." Yuwen Zhu covered her mouth and laughed. "Wu Di is indeed as interesting as you described in your letter."

Li Xuanba sighed. "It’s very naughty, and very delicate. I truly worry about whether I can protect it. It’s not even like an eagle anymore."

With that, Li Xuanba gave the eagle’s head a firm pinch.

Wu Di continued to cry with a "quack, quack, quack," its bird face soaked with tears.

Yuwen Zhu handed over a handkerchief. "Wipe its face."

Li Xuanba hesitated for a moment, then carefully pinched the corner of the handkerchief to take it, avoiding any contact with Yuwen Zhu’s hand.

Seeing Li Xuanba’s reserved demeanor, Yuwen Zhu did not suspect this time that he was disgusted by her.

If he were disgusted by her, he wouldn't be acting like this.

*Is Li Sanlang just shy?* Yuwen Zhu thought to herself, and she felt a blush creep onto her own face.

If not for this commotion caused by Wu Di, she would never have gathered the courage to continue speaking with Li Sanlang, let alone offer him a handkerchief.

Since her courage was already mustered, Yuwen Zhu did not want to retreat.

She was already betrothed to Li Sanlang, and they would spend their lives together in the future; she had to resolve the knot in her heart no matter what.

Yuwen Zhu picked up the water warming on the small stove beside the stone table and poured a cup for Li Sanlang. "I heard that you are not accustomed to drinks with overly complex flavors. This one only contains mild flower petals."

Yuwen Zhu extended a subtle invitation, and Li Xuanba, dragging the still-quacking, crying Wu Di along, sat down obediently.

Yuwen Zhu sat on the other side and poured a cup of flower tea for herself.

With Wu Di’s "quack, quack, quack" wailing providing a background track, the atmosphere felt slightly less stifling.

Yuwen Zhu said, "I heard that you were unwilling to meet with me, and I thought you were disgusted by me."

Li Xuanba hurriedly said, "No, that’s not it, I... it’s just that I..."

He pinched the wing of the eagle that had landed him in this predicament, and amidst Wu Di’s intensified "quack, quack, quack" crying, he explained stiffly, "I just... I just thought that I might not live to reach adulthood, so I didn't want to delay you."

Yuwen Zhu was puzzled. "How could just meeting me be a delay?"

Li Xuanba: "..." How was he supposed to explain this?

Explain that he was worried Yuwen Zhu might develop feelings for him? That would be far too thick-skinned.

And explaining that he was worried he might develop feelings for her? That would be just as strange.

Li Xuanba stammered, his face turning bright red, as if he had suddenly been struck dumb.

Yuwen Zhu looked down at her own rough hands. "Is it really not because I tinker with herbs, and don't act like a proper lady, that you didn't want to see me?"

Li Xuanba said urgently, "No! That hobby is wonderful!"

Seeing Li Xuanba’s hurried attempt to explain, Yuwen Zhu laughed for some reason. "What’s wonderful about it? I have sought out many physicians, but even the physicians retained by my family refuse to take female disciples, saying they have never heard of a woman practicing medicine. Practicing medicine requires 'looking, listening, asking, and feeling the pulse'—how can a woman perform these on strange men?"

As she spoke, her expression turned dejected. "If I only practice on my family, I cannot accumulate any real experience; I would just be reciting medical texts by rote, which would only harm the patients."

Li Xuanba said, "If a woman cannot perform these on strange men, how can a strange man perform them on a woman? Even a great physician like Dr. Sun can only use a silk thread to feel the pulse when treating female patients. The accuracy of that is surely far inferior to a direct examination. Half the world is composed of women; even if you only treated women, you would not lack for cases to study."

When Li Xuanba called her "Niangzi" (Lady/Wife) to her face, he almost bit his own tongue.

While "Niangzi" was a common term for a young woman, in later ages, it was a term for one's wife. This made Li Xuanba feel exceptionally embarrassed.

After Li Xuanba finished speaking, Yuwen Zhu remained stunned for a long time.

She turned her upper body, disregarding etiquette and shyness, and looked straight at Li Xuanba. "Practice medicine on women?"

Li Xuanba avoided Yuwen Zhu’s gaze. "Isn't that why you study medicine, Lady Yuwen? The world is full of male physicians, and no one treats women with care. For example, if a man has a sore, a physician can cut it and drain the pus. But if it were a woman, she would have to endure it while drinking medicine prescribed by a physician using a silk thread. Even if some elderly physicians can directly feel a woman's pulse, they would never perform detailed treatments on her."

Not to mention the death trap of childbirth.

It was always midwives who delivered babies, and midwives were merely women who had given birth themselves; most had no medical experience, were illiterate, and believed in superstitious nonsense.

Some women bled to death after childbirth; if a physician were present, they could have stitched the wound to stop the bleeding.

But at this time, pregnant women often just bled to death on their beds.

Soldiers could be saved even after having their arms hacked off on the battlefield, yet women could not be saved.

Li Xuanba stole a glance at Yuwen Zhu’s expression. Seeing her look of confusion, he guessed that she had likely just stumbled into medicine while caring for her younger brother and had grown to love it, without any grand, lofty goals. Thus, while her current passion was firm, that firmness might also be fragile.

Yuwen Zhu probably thought that loving medicine was truly unorthodox, and besides the reason that "she liked it," there was nothing else to justify her persistence.

Actually, that was fine.

It was best for people not to have too many high-minded ideals; that was the only way to live happily.

But looking at Yuwen Zhu’s aggrieved expression, Li Xuanba couldn't bear it.

Perhaps having a high-minded ideal once in a while was better than being constantly denied by others and by oneself?

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and told her a story from the end of the Qing Dynasty: "When I went to Zhangye, I saw an absurd funeral. A pregnant woman was having a difficult labor, and a folk miracle doctor happened to pass by. With the family's consent, he entered the room and applied acupuncture, and both mother and child were saved. But after the woman recovered, she was forced by village gossip to throw herself into a river and commit suicide."

Yuwen Zhu looked dazed. "If there were female physicians, she wouldn't have had to suffer that."

Li Xuanba shook his head. "Lady Yuwen, you are wrong. She shouldn't have had to suffer that even when saved by a male physician. How can the distinction between men and women be more important than a life? It is just that the unreasonable rules of this world are hard to change; since one cannot achieve it overnight, one must start with what can be done now. For instance, women practicing medicine."

Li Xuanba stroked the head of Wu Di, who had finally stopped its duck-like crying, his tone very calm, as if he were discussing something mundane. "If Lady Yuwen becomes a famous physician of this era, you will surely inspire many women to practice medicine. Countless women in this world who should not have died of illness, but did so because of the barrier between men and women, will be saved."

"Such a virtuous deed will leave your name in the history books of the imperial court, and you will have shrines and temples built for you among the people. What you are doing now is a deed that will be praised for generations. One cannot speak of ice to a summer insect, and how can a swallow know the ambitions of a swan? Lady Yuwen, do not be troubled by mediocre people; please be at ease."

Yuwen Zhu blinked, her almond eyes misting over like they were covered in morning dew.

She smiled. "I do not have such lofty ambitions as a swan."

Li Xuanba said, "Judge by actions, not by intent. Lady Yuwen, you are a swan."

Yuwen Zhu stood up. "If you say so. I have things to attend to, so I will not keep you company."

After saying this, she turned around hurriedly, lifted her skirt, and vanished from Li Xuanba’s sight.

Li Xuanba’s hand, still pinching the eagle’s wing, froze.

He looked down at the foolish eagle cub.

Wu Di: "?"

Li Xuanba gritted his teeth. "Today, I’m going to pluck your feathers and roast you! No one can save you!"

Wu Di: "??？!"

"Chirp!!!!"
