### Chapter 92: The Five Nobles of the Daye Era All Agree

Li Shimin rested for a few days before continuing to lead his troops to suppress the rebels.

Li Xuanba remained in the rear, managing logistics for Li Shimin while playing a game of "Tai Chi" with the local officials.

Even if the local officials didn't come from the local powerful clans, they were still tied to them by mutual interests. Now that the elite garrison troops and grassroots commanders from all over had been transferred to Jizhou, only Li Shimin’s forces were capable of winning battles. Naturally, all these officials hoped Li Shimin would go and support the commanderies and counties where their own clans were based.

Li Xuanba sighed, "My Second Brother is not only young, but he only has three thousand men under his command. You all have at least ten thousand soldiers in your hands, so why is everyone coming to borrow troops from him? Fine, since you have the gall to ask, I will be blunt. The direction in which my brother and I deploy our troops is decided by the one above."

Li Xuanba pointed toward the sky.

"To put it bluntly, regardless of your family background, in His Majesty’s eyes, everyone is treated the same. His Majesty is currently preparing for the campaign against Goguryeo. What is most important right now? It is ensuring the supply of troops and logistics. Will the people you want to save pay their taxes? Will they participate in the corvée labor? If the campaign against Goguryeo is delayed because of this, who will bear the responsibility?"

"Besides, the rebels usually don't target people of high prestige; they are merely after money and grain. Just spend some wealth to avert the disaster. Once His Majesty returns from the Goguryeo campaign, the Great Sui’s grand army will wipe out these rebels in an instant. By then, if you send your retainers to join the Sui army in the campaign, not only will you be able to reclaim your lost property, but you will also earn military merit. Wouldn't that be wonderful?"

Li Xuanba first persuaded them with gentle words, then added firmly, "You all know His Majesty’s decree. My brother and I only obey the Emperor’s orders. If you are dissatisfied with us, you are more than welcome to come with me to see His Majesty and discuss it."

After hearing this, most of the officials could only wipe the cold sweat from their foreheads and take their leave.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were not only backed by the Tang Duke’s Mansion, but they also possessed the "golden halo" of being the "Emperor’s most valued nephews." Even the nobles at court treated them with courtesy; how could these local officials dare to force them to do anything?

The only trouble Li Xuanba encountered was a letter from Li Jiancheng.

The Xingyang Zheng clan had also been affected by the civil unrest, and the ones eyeing Xingyang were none other than the infamous Wagang Army of later generations.

Although the Xingyang Zheng clan was wealthy and powerful, lacking neither private soldiers, fortified manors, weapons, armor, nor horses, they still suffered losses when resisting the rebels themselves. They preferred for Li Shimin to act as their personal bodyguard.

The Xingyang Zheng clan were in-laws to the Tang Duke’s Mansion, and they believed that, for the sake of both sentiment and logic, Li Shimin should come to their aid. It would be best if Li Shimin stationed himself in Xingyang; they would compensate him for any losses in money, grain, or weapons, ensuring he wouldn't suffer.

Li Jiancheng wrote to Li Xuanba, insisting that even if the Zheng clan did nothing, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba should take the initiative to help. He argued that since they were so sincere, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba should rush over immediately, otherwise, the Tang Duke’s Mansion would be the one losing face.

Li Xuanba set the letter aside without replying, using a stalling tactic. Once the Zheng clan wiped out the rebels in their vicinity, they wouldn't need to send troops anymore.

The Wagang Army was merely passing through Xingyang and would not stay long. Once they left, the remaining scattered rebels could be handled by the Xingyang Commandery Governor himself.

Who knew that when Li Jiancheng saw Li Xuanba’s delay in replying, he not only sent a trusted aide but also complained to Li Yuan, prompting him to send his own messenger as well.

The Xingyang Zheng clan also sent someone to rebuke Li Xuanba to his face for disregarding the safety of their in-laws.

The Zheng family retainer was likely not a proper servant, but a scholar from a humble background who had attached himself to the clan. He spoke incessantly, his tongue wagging like a river, and his spittle was almost spraying onto Li Xuanba’s face.

Li Xuanba took a step back to avoid the "spit attack."

Seeing Li Xuanba retreat, the man stepped forward, grabbed Li Xuanba’s sleeve, and raised his voice even louder.

Li Xuanba’s guard, Chen Tieniu, shoved the man away, drew his blade, and stood in front of Li Xuanba, glaring as he roared, "Back off!"

His voice was like a booming bell, shaking the man so hard he landed on his backside.

"Third Young Master, how can you be so rude to someone from the Xingyang Zheng clan!" the aide sent by Li Jiancheng scolded.

Li Xuanba flicked his wrist, unhooking the horse whip from his waist, and with a sharp *crack*, he lashed it across the aide’s face.

The aide clutched his face and howled.

Li Xuanba said languidly, "Whose family are you from? I am the Third Young Master of the Tang Duke’s Mansion, the Emperor’s nephew, and a court-appointed official of the fifth rank. I am being grabbed by the sleeve and berated by a mere servant of the Zheng clan, and you say *I* am being rude?"

With that, Li Xuanba lashed out two more times, specifically targeting the aide’s face. No matter how little strength he had, a whip across the face still stung. The aide sent by Li Jiancheng rolled on the ground, wailing.

"Third Young Master..." Li Chu-wu, the guard sent by Li Yuan, frowned.

Li Xuanba glanced at him, and Li Chu-wu swallowed the rest of his words.

"My brother and I are officials of the Imperial Court, and we lead the Court’s troops. Neither the Xingyang Zheng clan nor the Tang Duke’s Mansion has the authority to make the Court’s army act as their private bodyguards," Li Xuanba sneered. "Qinghe and Zhengzhou are five or six hundred *li* apart. You want my brother and me to trek five or six hundred *li* from Qinghe Commandery to Zhengzhou? Is the Xingyang Zheng clan the Emperor?"

Li Xuanba put away his whip and smoothed his sleeves. "Prepare the horses. I am going to see His Majesty to ask exactly who has the authority to mobilize our troops."

Li Chu-wu hurriedly said, "Third Young Master, please calm your anger. The Tang Duke’s Mansion and the Xingyang Zheng clan are kin; you will offend our in-laws."

Li Xuanba smiled. "Whose side are you on?"

Li Chu-wu quickly replied, "I am, of course, from the Tang Duke’s Mansion!"

Li Xuanba retorted, "You still know you’re a servant of the Tang Duke’s Mansion? I thought you were a dog of the Xingyang Zheng clan."

Li Chu-wu was horrified. "Why does the Third Young Master insult me! I was merely offering honest advice!"

Li Xuanba laughed. "They say a servant by an elder’s side is half an elder himself. You really do want to be my elder, don't you?"

He dropped his smile. "Perhaps I have been too kind, allowing any stray cat or dog to bark at me. Tie these three up and throw them in the dungeon. I am going to ask my father personally: if his servants are disrespectful to me, can I have his entire household kicked out of the Tang Duke’s Mansion?"

Li Chu-wu knelt down in a panic. "Third Young Master! My family has served the Tang Duke’s Mansion for... ah!"

Li Shimin rushed over like a blur, kicking Li Chu-wu to the ground.

He hadn't yet removed his silver armor, and the blood on his face—save for his helmet—had not yet dried. The murderous aura radiating from him left everyone around him too terrified to speak.

Li Shimin cursed, "How have you been guarding A-Xuan? For people like this, you should have gagged them and thrown them in the dungeon immediately, yet you let A-Xuan face them himself? What use are you? All of you, go and receive your punishment!"

Chen Tieniu shouted, "We will go receive our punishment!" and then aggressively moved to tie the men up.

The Zheng clan’s servant had already collapsed when Li Xuanba asked, "Are you the Emperor?" and was now being dragged away by Chen Tieniu like a dead dog.

Li Xuanba said, "Why are you back so early? Calm down. The servants sent by Father, Brother, and the future sister-in-law are all people who are hard to offend; they didn't dare to act on their own."

"The battle was won, and when I heard Brother had sent people, I ditched my guards and came back first," Li Shimin scolded. "They are *your* guards! You are their only master! Even if I were to scold you, they should be standing in front of you! Since they don't know their place, they can all get lost!"

Li Xuanba did not argue with his second brother. "We can teach them slowly."

Li Shimin snorted coldly. "Are you really going to see the Emperor? I’ll go with you."

Li Xuanba said, "I can go by myself. You continue suppressing the rebels."

Li Shimin shook his head. "I don't trust anyone else to guard you. Seeing them like this, I’m worried they might abandon you halfway."

The guards kneeling on the ground hurriedly kowtowed to show their loyalty.

Li Xuanba said, "Let my guards be trained by you, and you send two hundred men to protect me. That will do, right? Don't let this delay the real work."

Seeing his brother’s persistence, Li Shimin could only assign two hundred trusted men to Li Xuanba.

Li Shimin warned them, "If A-Xuan loses a single hair, you will all pay with your lives!"

Li Xuanba countered, "I lose a dozen hairs every day. It seems their lives won't be enough to pay for that."

Li Shimin’s stern-faced trusted men almost failed to keep their composure.

Li Shimin rubbed his forehead, gritting his teeth. "Li Xuanba!"

Li Xuanba waved his hand. "Second Brother, keep training them. I won't say another word."

Distracted by Li Xuanba’s interruption, Li Shimin couldn't maintain his harsh tone and could only nag Li Xuanba to take care of himself.

Li Xuanba packed his bags and, the next day, set off at full speed toward Jizhou.

Because of the rebel mobs blocking the road, even though Li Xuanba and his guards spent money constantly to change horses, it still took them five days to reach Jizhou.

Li Xuanba did not go to see Li Yuan; he directly submitted his tablet to request an audience with the Emperor.

Yang Guang was watching a song and dance performance when he heard Li Xuanba had arrived, and he summoned him with surprise.

Seeing Li Xuanba’s travel-worn appearance, Yang Guang walked down the steps to help him up, looking him over carefully. "What is the matter that has you in such a rush?"

Li Xuanba said, "Your Majesty, please, quickly send a general to replace my brother and me in suppressing the rebels."

Yang Guang was puzzled. "Did you lose a battle and lose your confidence? You and Er-lang are young; victory and defeat are common in military affairs. Why mind it? Don't worry about winning or losing; just go and hone your skills!"

Li Xuanba sighed, "We haven't lost. Second Brother has been winning constantly. It’s just that he’s won too much; every day, someone calls on him to help protect their family estates. My brother and I told them that we lead the Court’s army and have Your Majesty’s orders—how can we run around as we please?"

Li Xuanba did not follow the proper way for a subject to complain to the Emperor; instead, he complained to Yang Guang like a spoiled younger relative.

"My brother and I received the Emperor’s orders to first wipe out the most vicious rebels. Even if the Emperor said we could act at our discretion, we couldn't possibly go too far; we only stay within Qinghe Commandery. But today, one governor says a court minister’s ancestral home is threatened and wants us to be bodyguards, and tomorrow, some local elder of high prestige needs our help. Are we still an Imperial army?"

As Li Xuanba spoke, his eyes turned red. "I’m done, I’m done! Everyone is bullying us because we are young!"

Yang Guang’s face darkened. "There is such a thing?"

Pei Shiju, who was most familiar with Li Xuanba, spoke first. "Third Young Master Li, you and Er-lang are the Emperor’s nephews; who would dare order you around? You could have simply rebuffed them."

Li Xuanba wiped his eyes. "Some I could rebuff, others I could not. I had no choice but to come and beg Your Majesty to send someone to replace us."

Pei Shiju sighed. "Did someone beg the Tang Duke for something? The Tang Duke is truly muddled!"

Yang Guang frowned. "Li Yuan? What did he do?"

Li Xuanba said aggrievedly, "A son does not speak of his father’s faults; I dare not say."

Yang Guang said, "A father is not above the Sovereign. I command you to speak."

Li Xuanba wiped his eyes again and whispered, "The Xingyang Zheng clan asked my brother and me to lead our troops across a thousand *li* to Zhengzhou to prevent civil unrest."

As Yang Guang pondered how the Xingyang Zheng clan had the nerve to demand such a thing, Pei Yun helpfully explained, "The Tang Duke’s eldest son, Li Jiancheng, is betrothed to the Xingyang Zheng clan. Such a marriage is rare, and the Tang Duke, fearing to offend his in-laws, must have written to Li Er-lang and Li San-lang."

Yang Guang said with a dark face, "Zhengzhou is so close to the Eastern Capital; where would there be civil unrest?! Call Zheng Yuan-zu to see me. I want to ask him just how powerful his Zheng clan is that they dare to mobilize troops privately! And call Li Yuan as well!"

Li Xuanba hurriedly knelt. "If Your Majesty punishes my father, then I am an unfilial son."

Yu Shiji said gently, "Third Young Master, you are the Emperor’s subject, and the Tang Duke is also the Emperor’s subject. Loyalty should come before filial piety. Furthermore, the Tang Duke acted incorrectly; by stopping him in time, you have saved him from greater punishment and prevented a larger mistake. That is true filial piety."

Su Wei stroked his beard. "Rest assured, you did the right thing. The Tang Duke will not dare to scold you."

Yang Guang patted Li Xuanba on the shoulder. "Why worry about such a small matter? The Empress is feeling unwell; go visit her and keep her company."

Yang Guang considerately let Li Xuanba leave first so he wouldn't run into Li Yuan.

Li Xuanba kowtowed. "Thank you, Your Majesty."

After Li Xuanba left, Yang Guang’s anger flared.

He returned to his couch and cursed, "The Shandong clans boast of being high-born, so do they really think they are the Emperor? Daring to mobilize troops privately across a thousand *li*?!"

Pei Shiju had wanted to say it was only five or six hundred *li*, not a thousand. But there was no difference; it was still private mobilization. Moreover, he came from the Hedong Pei clan, a Guanzhong clan that had always been overshadowed by the Shandong clans; he was happy to see them suffer in front of the Emperor.

"Your Majesty, please calm your anger. The Zheng family likely just viewed Li Er-lang and Li San-lang as juniors and their troops as servants of the Tang Duke’s Mansion. They were probably just too panicked by the unrest and did something foolish," Pei Shiju said.

Pei Yun added, "Where is there civil unrest in Zhengzhou? Can unrest a thousand *li* away really scare them?"

Pei Shiju wanted to say there was unrest near Zhengzhou, but seeing Yang Guang’s expression and remembering how close Zhengzhou was to Luoyang, he didn't dare tell the truth. "Perhaps their courage is indeed too small."

Su Wei sighed, "It’s not as if Zhengzhou lacks Sui troops to guard it. What were they asking Li Er-lang and Li San-lang to protect from a thousand *li* away? Privately mobilizing the Imperial army—how absurd!"

Yu Shiji was confused. "Are they too rude? Perhaps there is some misunderstanding."

Yuwen Shu listened quietly for a long time, and only after gauging Yang Guang’s attitude did he speak. "I saw that Third Young Master brought a guard with him. Why not ask that guard if there is anything Third Young Master is hiding? He shouldn't have brought the guard to the Empress’s palace; the guard should be waiting outside."

Yang Guang nodded. "Call the guard in. I rarely see Third Young Master so aggrieved; there must be more he is hiding."

The eunuch soon brought in the guard.

The guard who accompanied Li Xuanba was the simple and honest Chen Tieniu.

He had received Li Xuanba’s orders in advance, so as soon as the Emperor asked, he poured out everything that had happened that day.

"The Zheng family sent a servant who grabbed the Young Master’s sleeve and questioned him, even spitting on him. The Young Master answered politely that without Your Majesty’s decree, one cannot mobilize troops privately. Then, the eldest Young Master’s servant scolded the Young Master for not respecting the Zheng family’s servant, and the servant sent by the Duke also scolded the Young Master for offending the Zheng family’s servant."

The more Chen Tieniu spoke, the more aggrieved he felt. He prostrated himself on the ground and cried, "Your Majesty, I don't understand. Why must such a noble Young Master be forced to respect a mere servant? Even the officials sent by Your Majesty to deliver decrees wouldn't spit on the Young Master!"

Just then, Li Yuan and Zheng Yuan-zu, the Duke of Shen, arrived in a hurry.

Zheng Yuan-zu was the son of Zheng Yi, the Duke of Pei. He was from the Donglin branch of the Xingyang Zheng clan and was the highest-ranking member of the clan at court. Although he wasn't highly valued by Yang Guang, he was the most influential voice of the Xingyang Zheng clan at court.

Li Yuan and Zheng Yuan-zu were waiting at the entrance of the main hall, not daring to enter without Yang Guang’s order.

Chen Tieniu’s voice was booming, and they heard every word clearly from the doorway.

Li Yuan was completely bewildered.

He turned to Zheng Yuan-zu and said, "Your family’s servant spat on my Third Son?!"

Zheng Yuan-zu was shocked. "How is that possible?!"

Chen Tieniu continued to cry at the top of his lungs, "The servant sent by the Duke, a man named Li Chu-wu, said that a servant by an elder’s side is half an elder himself, and he wanted to discipline the Young Master on behalf of the Duke! The Young Master had no choice; he couldn't be unfilial!"

Zheng Yuan-zu turned to Li Yuan. "Your servant can act as an elder to your son, and you expect your son to be filial to him?!"

Li Yuan was shocked. "How is that possible?!"

Chen Tieniu looked honest and simple. He was terrified of the Emperor, but his genuine emotions showed when mentioning his master’s plight, to the point where he didn't even care about court etiquette. Yang Guang and his five close ministers believed him, feeling both shocked and furious.

Yang Guang roared, "Li Yuan! Zheng Yuan-zu! Get in here! Li Er-lang and Li San-lang are leading troops to fight for me, and you privately demand they move their troops a thousand *li* away—are you trying to rebel?!"

Li Yuan: "Ah?"

Zheng Yuan-zu: "What?"

They knelt on the ground, dizzy. What had happened? How did this get linked to treason?!

Su Wei said kindly, "Li Er-lang and Li San-lang are suppressing rebels in Qinghe Commandery. Tang Duke, Duke of Shen, how could you write to them, using your status as elders to force them to take troops to Zhengzhou to protect the Xingyang Zheng clan? What were you thinking?"

Li Yuan and Zheng Yuan-zu finally realized what was happening. So that was it!

Li Yuan hurriedly said, "I had no such intention! I only received a letter from the Zheng family asking for support, so I wrote to Er-lang and San-lang asking where they were suppressing rebels, and if they were close, to look after the Zheng family. How could I ask them to mobilize troops privately! It must be that wicked servant who added oil to the fire and fabricated this!"

Li Yuan was sweating cold beads.

At this point, even if he had to break off the marriage with the Zheng clan, he wouldn't dare admit to private troop mobilization!

Li Yuan felt a bit of resentment toward his Third Son. Was this something you report to the Emperor?!

Yu Shiji saw Li Yuan’s resentment and explained for Li Xuanba, "Tang Duke, the servants sent by you and your eldest son were about to use family law on Li San-lang. The matter was so loud it must have spread throughout Qinghe Commandery. If Li San-lang hadn't traveled through the night to report this to His Majesty, His Majesty would have learned of it through an impeachment by the Censorate."

Su Wei said, "Tang Duke, you should be glad you have such a sensible and clever son."

Li Yuan realized the severity of the matter and continued to kowtow. "I am truly wronged in this matter!"

In truth, Li Yuan *was* wronged. He just couldn't refuse the Zheng family’s request, and since Li Shimin had indeed been near Xingyang with his troops, he wrote to them to look after the Zheng family if they were nearby.

Moreover, because Li Shimin’s troops were self-recruited, Li Yuan didn't realize they were considered "Sui troops"; he just thought Li Shimin was fighting with his own retainers, just like when he ambushed the Tuyuhun Khan.

If Li Shimin’s troops had been provided by Yang Guang, Li Yuan would never have opened his mouth, and the Zheng family would never have dared to ask.

Zheng Yuan-zu was confused. "Private mobilization? Isn't Li Er-lang leading the Tang Duke’s Mansion’s own retainers?"

Pei Shiju frowned. "Duke of Shen, what nonsense are you spouting? The Tang Duke’s Mansion has three thousand armored retainers? Those are the Sui army’s rebel-suppression troops, formed under His Majesty’s decree! Do not slander Li Er-lang and Li San-lang!"

Pei Shiju felt a bit sorry for his two disciples.

What kind of "pig teammates" were these? No wonder Li Xuanba, despite his weak health, had to rush to see the Emperor through the night. If he hadn't, their loyalty to the Emperor would have been turned into treason by these idiots!

Su Wei, being older and of high prestige, didn't give Li Yuan and Zheng Yuan-zu any face.

He said bluntly, "With elders like you, Li Da-xiong and Li Da-de are truly pitiful. Tang Duke, Duke of Shen, have you not thought about what 'three thousand armored soldiers' means! No wonder Da-de was scared to tears, kneeling and begging the Emperor to change commanders."

Yu Shiji, thinking of the stories his brother had told about the brothers in the Tang Duke’s Mansion, said, "The Tang Duke dotes on Li Da-lang and likely only considered his need to save face in front of his in-laws, never thinking of the difficulties faced by Li Er-lang and Li San-lang. If they hadn't been so sharp, they might have ended up in a dungeon."

Yuwen Shu, thinking of the treasures Li San-lang had gifted him, also sighed, "Li Da-xiong and Li Da-de could have easily earned you a marquisate. To not cherish such excellent sons—Tang Duke, you are muddled."

Pei Yun, who wasn't familiar with the brothers, joined in to fit in. "Tang Duke, you allowed the Zheng family’s servant to spit on Li San-lang—that is truly uncharitable! If anyone’s servant dared to spit on my son, I would kill him!"

Li Yuan: "..." As if he wouldn't kill him! How could the Zheng family’s servant be so arrogant!

Zheng Yuan-zu couldn't believe it. "Is there some misunderstanding? My family’s servant would never do such a thing!"

Pei Shiju, having spent a year with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, knew them well. He sneered, "Wouldn't do it? When they were children visiting your Zheng house, you sent youths ranging from adulthood down to their own age to challenge them one by one. They competed all day without a drop of water, just to win the Zheng daughter for Li Jiancheng. That was a famous story back then, wasn't it?"

Yu Shiji also remembered his brother mentioning this. "It is said that the sturdy Li Er-lang was exhausted and fell ill for a month or two; I don't know how long the already frail Li San-lang was sick. To treat two children like that, your Zheng clan is truly... sigh. Furthermore, Tang Duke, I have never heard of a man asking for a wife by sending his younger brothers instead of going himself. You dote on Li Da-lang too much."

Su Wei, who was friends with Xue Daoheng—the mentor of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba—naturally favored them. "The eldest son is important, but Li Er-lang and Li San-lang are your sons too. Tang Duke, you are muddled!"

Yuwen Shu shook his head. "I can't bear to watch. If you don't want these two sons, why not give them to me?"

Pei Yun continued to try to fit in. "Your Majesty, Li Er-lang and Li San-lang’s merit in capturing the Tuyuhun Khan is enough to grant them titles, and they have merit in suppressing the rebels. Although they are young, they should be given proper general positions so others know they are Your Majesty’s commanders."

Pei Shiju immediately said, "Your Majesty, I second this!"

Su Wei said, "I also second this."

Yuwen Shu added sarcastically, "Your Majesty, even the lowest-ranking general title would do. If they aren't made generals, some might still think their three thousand soldiers aren't the Sui army."

Yu Shiji sighed, "They should indeed be made generals."

The "Five Nobles of the Daye Era" reached a consensus.

Yang Guang snorted coldly. "Li Yuan, I know you have no intent to rebel, but you are too doted on Li Jiancheng—doted on to the point of being muddled. For the sake of Da-xiong and Da-de’s loyalty, I will not punish you severely this time. For the Goguryeo campaign, you will not lead troops; stay in Jizhou and supervise the transport of grain to make up for your mistakes."

Li Yuan kowtowed. "Thank you, Your Majesty! I will reflect on this!"

He breathed a sigh of relief. It was a good thing San-lang was sharp! He had truly been muddled this time!

Yang Guang said to Zheng Yuan-zu, "You are dismissed from office and sent home to put your family in order. Yu-qing."

Yu Shiji stood up. "I am here."

Yang Guang said, "Investigate how many members of the Xingyang Zheng clan hold positions as local governors or prefects, and dismiss them all. Daring to mobilize my troops privately—I dare not let them govern my lands."

Zheng Yuan-zu collapsed. "Your Majesty! The Xingyang Zheng clan has no intent to rebel!"

Yang Guang said calmly, "Even without the intent to rebel, you dared to mobilize my troops a thousand *li* away. Those with the intent to rebel aren't as arrogant as your Xingyang Zheng clan. I haven't stripped your title and am giving you a chance to recover; that is already for the sake of the old Duke of Pei. Get out. Drag him away."

The guards dragged the collapsed Zheng Yuan-zu away.

The Xingyang Zheng clan had already been suppressed once by Emperor Wen, and few held high office; Yang Guang had no psychological burden in doing this.

The arrogance of the Xingyang Zheng clan served as a warning to Yang Guang.

Some clans relied on their ancestors' shade and didn't take Imperial power to heart; Yang Guang had long loathed them. Originally, he hated the Guanzhong noble clans the most, which was why he didn't want to return to Daxing. He wanted to give the Jiangnan clans, who supported him most, a chance, and he also had the intention of promoting the Shandong clans.

He hadn't expected the Shandong clans to be even more arrogant than the Guanzhong nobles, daring to mobilize troops privately. They were worthy of being the "first-class" clans of Shandong. No wonder his father didn't like the five great Shandong clans.

After using this to beat the Xingyang Zheng clan, he hoped the other Shandong clans would behave.

"Yu-qing, draft a decree for me." Yang Guang tapped his fingers on the desk. "Li Shimin and Li Xuanba first captured the Tuyuhun Khan, then quelled the civil unrest; they have merit to the state. Appoint Li Shimin as General of the Huben Guard and Li Xuanba as General of the Huya Guard, with command over the Qinghe Commandery garrison troops!"

Yu Shiji knelt. "I obey the decree!"

Li Yuan, still kneeling on the ground, was dumbfounded.

I am only a fourth-rank general without command of troops, and Er-lang and San-lang are already commanders of the Guard with actual military power?

Er-lang is even a fourth-rank official! Half a rank higher than me!

For a moment, Li Yuan’s heart was filled with a complex mix of emotions.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第93章 想请知世郎一叙
chunks.chineseText:
第93章 想请知世郎一叙

=
　　隋朝许多官职名称继承自魏晋， 魏晋的官职名称又继承自汉朝。
　　如虎贲郎将的名称就沿袭自虎贲中郎将。
　　虽然名称相同，职责和地位却大不相同。虎贲中郎将最初统领禁军，非亲信不能当， 现在不过是府兵制中一员中层军官。
　　杨广大业三年军制改革， 将遥领天下府兵的十二卫改成十二卫四府， 合称十六卫，新增加的左右备身府和左右监门府将护卫皇帝和守卫宫禁的职权从原本十二卫中剥夺，原本的十二卫所统领的府兵成了“外军”。
　　杨广将原本最基础的卫府骠骑府改成鹰扬府后， 扩充了鹰扬府的数量，基本每个郡都有一两个鹰扬府。鹰扬府数量的增加，让每个鹰扬郎将的权力减少。
　　杨广此举就是削弱朝堂将领对鹰扬府的管理权。扩充的鹰扬府中将士多是本地人， 又得皇帝命令不听从其他鹰扬府的调遣，所以原本属于中央禁军的鹰扬府全部变成了地方军。
　　鹰扬府演变成各自为政的地方军的后果就是先被农民起义军各个击破， 然后残存的鹰扬府纷纷反叛自立， 鹰扬郎将成为地方军阀。
　　隋末那么多“反王”，大多都是原本大隋的鹰扬郎将。
　　虎贲郎将是十二卫大将军的副手，非大战争时期的实际领兵人。虎贲郎将接受皇帝命令，有调动多个鹰扬府的权力。
　　现在虎贲郎将基本还是中央官员，只有在得到皇帝命令出征的时候才会领兵。
　　杨广让李世民担任虎贲郎将， 李玄霸担任副手虎牙郎将，让他们常驻清河郡， 就改变了原本中央派出直属将领领兵的原则，让中高层将领直接驻扎地方。
　　这个改变让朝中大臣很兴奋。
　　隋文帝在扫灭天下的时候，也将军权下放到地方， 在重要关隘设置军政合一的总管府。
　　在天下稳定之后， 隋文帝自然收回地方兵权， 撤销总管府， 将军事权从地方长官手中剥离。
　　如今民贼四起，为了迅速剿灭民贼，再次执行军政合一的政策确实是稳定社稷最好的方式。经过杨坚杨广两代帝王已经撤销的将军开府权力估计也会放开。
　　现在这还只是个苗头。
　　如果民乱很快扫灭，李世民和李玄霸两人肯定会回归中央。现在他们驻扎在清河郡，就是寻常将领出征行为。
　　这么一想，许多朝中大臣勋贵有些希望民乱别那么快平定。
　　魏晋南北朝乱世持续三百六十九年，隋朝的大一统才到第二代。现在朝中重臣大部分都还有乱世的记忆。
　　隋文帝能从权臣篡位，他们为何不能？
　　乱世大舞台，有梦都能来。
　　杨广倒是没想那么多。
　　他没有把民贼和高丽放在心上。高丽就大隋的一个郡那么点大，他倾全国之力压上，肯定是一场酣畅淋漓的大胜仗。
　　等他凯旋，大军回程的时候顺便就把那群民贼像虫蚁一样轻松碾碎。
　　所以杨广特别厌烦那些一脸紧张表情的官吏。
　　学学李二郎和李三郎，朕让你们剿贼的目的是保障徭役兵役的顺利进行，别拖累朕御驾亲征的效率。
　　杨广又不是傻子。世家勋贵家中藏有私兵武器，地方豪强甚至坞堡都没拆，他难道不知道？
　　那点小小的民贼能对豪强世家有多大威胁？豪强世家在朝中跳得厉害的官吏，不过是舍不得出力帮朝堂无偿剿贼。
　　为这点小事中断他御驾亲征的伟业，这些人真是毫不掩饰自己的不忠诚。
　　杨广越想越气，将好几个看到民乱四起，劝说他暂缓征讨高丽的御史下狱。
　　苏威其实也想劝说杨广别这么急，给百姓一点喘息的机会。见此情况，他只好闭嘴，免得惹火上身。
　　他很怀念高颎和宇文弼还在朝堂的时候。
　　这两个老头若还在朝堂，肯定会对皇帝据理力争。
　　苏威想给高颎和宇文弼写信，让他们出头劝说皇帝。但他又担心杨广还厌恶高颎，为免被打成高颎朋党，便作罢了。
　　封了两位少年“郎将”，朝中一石激起千层浪，大小官吏各怀鬼胎。
　　李玄霸达成目的，在涿郡多待了些时日。
　　等叶护的商团带着西域珍宝和鹰犬骏马到来后，李玄霸挨个给大业五贵送完礼，又给杨广包了一个鹰犬大礼包后，才启程离开。
　　这期间，李玄霸先在宫中陪伴杨广和皇后，最后两日才住到了李渊下榻的府上。
　　李渊这几日梳理心情，冷静许多。
　　仔细思考之后，李渊惊出了一身冷汗。他一时疏忽，差点把一家人都往断头台上送了一遭。
　　再见到李玄霸的时候，李渊只有愧疚：“大德，这次是耶耶差点害了你。”
　　李玄霸没好气道：“我和二哥估计只是流放，父亲你绝对会被赐自尽。”
　　李玄霸做了一个抹脖子的动作，被李渊敲了脑袋。
　　李渊见儿子还能没大没小地抱怨，知道儿子没有生气，神情自在了不少。
　　他辩解：“我只是让你们便宜行事，敷衍一下郑家，可没想过让你们去给郑家当护卫。就算真的是我唐国公府的私兵，也没可能去给郑家当护卫。”
　　李渊越想越气，拍桌道：“怎么会传成我让你和二郎去给郑家当护卫了？！”
　　李玄霸道：“可能是荥阳郑氏的名号太响亮，所以连我们唐国公府的家仆都觉得他们高人一等。不是有句话，叫什么‘流水的皇帝铁打的世家’，高门大族比皇族还尊贵吗？大概民间许多人都是这么想的。”
　　李渊讥笑：“铁打的世家？铁打的世家可没少被屠过。”
　　李玄霸不意外李渊会这么说。
　　李渊有注重世家的一面，但注重的只是世家能给他带去的利益，不是真的对世家这块金字招牌有多真情实意的尊敬。
　　当李渊当了皇帝的时候，他做事全凭喜好，一点都不在乎高门世家。他特别偏爱河东裴氏，只是因为裴氏是他起兵的“原始股东”。
　　在荥阳郑氏这里，李渊也表现出了很势利的一面。
　　在为李建成求娶郑氏女时，李渊表现得就像个世家舔狗。
　　等婚事定下，唐国公府又蒸蒸日上后，李渊对郑氏就摆上了唐国公的架子。
　　当初郑氏想入股李玄霸和李世民的香皂铺子、印刷铺子，李渊都借口这是和皇帝皇子一起做生意婉拒了，不想让郑氏分这杯羹。
　　李渊心眼不大，郑氏曾经对他不冷不热，他也就对郑氏只是尽礼数而已。
　　“如果不是因为毗沙门写信求我，我本是想推脱过去。”李渊解释，“毕竟是他丈人家，还是要给点面子。”
　　李玄霸道：“我知道。对父亲和我、二哥而言，郑氏不重要；对大兄而言，郑氏十分重要。大兄大概会走文官的路，需要郑氏的支持。”
　　李渊想起李建成主动来涿郡立功，半路就受不了哭跑回洛阳，眼中不由浮现出失望之情：“唐国公府以后的荣耀，还是得靠你和大雄啊。”
　　李渊拍了拍李玄霸的肩膀，语重心长道：“你兄长是没指望了，能不被削爵，领着国公的俸禄当个富贵闲人就行。我李家以后的辉煌，只能看你和大雄。不过大德，这次事情虽然紧急，你该让大雄与你一起来。你身手这么差，中途出了意外可如何是好？”
　　李渊越说越担忧，便啰嗦起来。
　　中途李玄霸想逃，被李渊双手钳住逃跑失败，被迫听了李渊长达一个时辰的唠叨。
　　李渊抱怨着抱怨着，说起对李玄霸身体的担心，和这次差点触怒杨广的后怕，不由抹起了眼泪。
　　李玄霸还要反过来安慰李渊。
　　他庆幸二哥这次没来，不然肯定会和父亲抱头痛哭，魔音双倍。
　　还好他立刻就要离开了。
　　河道被运粮草的船只堵塞，李玄霸仍旧骑马回清河。
　　李渊将李玄霸送到城门口。
　　离别时，李渊感慨儿子青出于蓝而胜于蓝。
　　虽然都是将军称号，府兵将军和杂号将军完全不同，自己也要努力，早日把儿子们比下去。
　　李玄霸走出了几百米，回头看去，李渊仍旧仰着头望着他。
　　当看到李玄霸回头的时候，李渊朝李玄霸挥手。
　　李玄霸的嘴角不自觉地下撇。他对父亲扬了扬马鞭，加快了离去的速度。
　　他本以为这次自己“告御状”让李渊被惩罚，李渊再怎么不占理也会埋怨自己。
　　未曾想李渊会道歉，会反省，会因为连累他和二哥后怕，还会关心自己的身体。
　　看到二哥的官职超过了自己，李渊虽然有些沮丧不自在，但也表现出欣慰和骄傲。
　　李玄霸想起了前世完全记不得模样的把他拖入深渊的父母。
　　这一世他的父亲和母亲，在后世大部分正常家庭长大的人眼中，一定是很不好吧。
　　李玄霸抑制着自己再次回头的冲动，直到越过一个弯路，才减缓了马匹的速度。
　　他深呼一口气，将心中闷气呼出。
　　“停下。”
　　护卫疑惑勒马。
　　李玄霸道：“改道，我要去一趟泰山。”
　　陈铁牛劝阻道：“郎君，齐鲁民乱也很严重，我们还是先赶紧回去和二郎君汇合吧。”
　　李玄霸道：“我有事要做。这是命令，随我去泰山。”
　　李玄霸伸长手臂。
　　“啾”的一声，乌镝落在了他的手臂上。
　　无论是在清河，还是去涿郡，乌镝一直陪伴着他。
　　杨广和李渊都不知道有只金雕盘旋在上空，每当晚上就大摇大摆地落地吃他们厨房里的肉。
　　“乌镝，这条路你记住了？”李玄霸问道。
　　乌镝摇头。
　　李玄霸叹气：“也是，才走一次，你肯定记不住。那你继续跟着我。”
　　乌镝：“啾啾！”记得住也要说记不住，嘻嘻嘻。
　　李玄霸对一个护卫道：“你先回清河告诉二哥，我会晚些回。别来找我，路上会错过。”
　　离开清河郡的时候，李世民给亲信下令，必须听从李玄霸的任何命令。
　　护卫心里担心，也只能照做。
　　送信的人离开，李玄霸带着剩下的人往济北郡而去。
　　虽然齐鲁也有民乱，但大业七年的大隋统治还很稳固，农民起义军还没到攻城略地的时候。郡城很安全。
　　泰山向来是文人墨客齐聚的地方。就算有民乱，泰山脚下现在也有很多前来游览的士人。
　　他们都带着护卫，并不在意民乱。
　　农民起义军一般也会绕过这些带着护卫的官宦子弟。
　　去泰山时会走一段官道。虽然官道因运送粮草辎重“交通管制”，但李玄霸有官身，仍旧可以走官道。
　　他骑着马与神情麻木的役夫役妇擦肩而过，越过道路两旁零星的尸体和伏在尸体上割肉的行尸走肉，来到了去往泰山的小路。
　　泰山脚下的小镇，食肆的酒旗仍旧随风飘荡。
　　李玄霸寻了一处房屋较为华丽的客栈下马，转头对铁牛道：“去租个大院子，租不到就买，我要在这里住几日。”
　　陈铁牛苦着脸道：“郎君，我求你快回清河吧，二郎君在等着你呢。”
　　李玄霸道：“这是命令，懂？”
　　陈铁牛嘟囔：“懂，懂，不能让郎君把命令说第二遍，我这就去。”
　　护卫皆叹气。
　　领队的周达道：“三郎君，若真的遇到危险怎么办？”
　　李玄霸道：“若真的遇到危险，他们也会恭恭敬敬地把我送走。”
　　周达：“啊？”
　　李玄霸摸了摸胳膊上的金雕脑袋，道：“谁不知道大隋的军队都在备战高丽，只有我二哥李世民李二郎手中精兵所向披靡。这民乱四起，只有二哥一支精兵在奋战捉襟见肘。但谁敢动我……哼。”
　　他环视周围：“我想不会有哪支民贼想最先被二哥盯上。店家，有鲜肉吗？我家雕挑食。”
　　乌镝仰头：“啾！”是的！我挑食！
　　大冬天的，店家小二大概是太忙碌了，额头上居然出了一层汗：“有、有，猎户刚送来的。只、只是，贵人，我们店住不下这么多人啊。”
　　李玄霸道：“没关系，我只是在这里暂时歇脚。”
　　周达点了十人入店护卫李玄霸，其余人在门口歇着。
　　李玄霸买了面饼饮水给他们送去，特意叮嘱了要烧热了的水。
　　古代没什么一喝就倒的蒙汗药，顶多下点巴豆和不纯正的砒|霜。只要喝没味道的温开水，就能避开大部分“毒”。
　　不一会儿，陈铁牛就回来了。
　　他身后跟着一个躬身哈腰，较为富态的中年男人。
　　“郎君，这是当地里正。他想请郎君去他家小住。”陈铁牛道。
　　李玄霸看向里正。
　　里正扑通一声跪下磕头：“拜、拜见将军！将军若不嫌弃，我家挺宽广，可供将军下榻。”
　　李玄霸淡然道：“我喜静。”
　　里正忙道：“我、我们一家会搬到别庄！绝不打扰将军！”
　　李玄霸颔首：“好，那就暂时叨扰了。请起吧。”
　　里正抖抖索索地站起来。李玄霸随里正离开。
　　店小二松了口气。
　　李玄霸快离开客栈的时候，驻足道：“我来此地，是想请知世郎王薄一叙。见过了他，我自会离去。我已经向二哥送信，得早些回去。希望不要让我等太久。”
　　引路的里正和送客的店家皆呆滞。
　　李玄霸说完后就提脚离开，旅客们没听到他离开前的话，纷纷窃窃私语。
　　“刚才那少年郎看着好俊俏，就是太瘦了些，不知道是谁家士子。”
　　“你看见他的护卫了吗？肯定是郡中贵人子弟。”
　　“说不准是更贵的贵人路过此地。”
　　“里正叫他将军，如此年轻的将军，说不定是朝中有门荫的贵人。”
　　“真的？那我们是不是该去拜访？”
　　“就怕惊扰贵人。”……
　　有一个道士捋着长须，看向李玄霸的背影，露出意动的神色。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 93: Wishing to Invite the "World-Knowing Gentleman" for a Chat

Many official titles in the Sui Dynasty were inherited from the Wei and Jin periods, which in turn had inherited them from the Han Dynasty. For instance, the title of *Huben Langjiang* (Tiger-Brave General) was a continuation of the *Huben Zhonglangjiang* (General of the Tiger-Brave Palace Guards).

Although the names were the same, their duties and status were vastly different. The original *Huben Zhonglangjiang* commanded the imperial guards and could only be held by the Emperor’s most trusted confidants; now, it was merely a mid-level officer position within the *Fubing* (militia) system.

During his third year of the Daye era, Yang Guang reformed the military system, reorganizing the twelve guards that remotely commanded the empire’s *Fubing* into the "Twelve Guards and Four Prefectures," collectively known as the Sixteen Guards. The newly created Left and Right Bodyguard Prefectures and the Left and Right Gate-Monitoring Prefectures stripped the original twelve guards of their authority to protect the Emperor and the palace. The *Fubing* previously commanded by the original twelve guards were relegated to "external armies."

Yang Guang changed the most basic *Biaoqi* (Cavalry) Prefectures into *Yingyang* (Eagle-Soaring) Prefectures and expanded their numbers, with basically one or two in every commandery. This increase in the number of *Yingyang* Prefectures diluted the power of each *Yingyang Langjiang* (Eagle-Soaring General).

Yang Guang’s move was intended to weaken the control that court generals held over these prefectures. The soldiers in the expanded *Yingyang* Prefectures were mostly locals, and under the Emperor’s orders, they were forbidden from obeying the summons of other *Yingyang* Prefectures. Thus, the *Yingyang* Prefectures, which once belonged to the central imperial guard, were all transformed into local armies.

The consequence of the *Yingyang* Prefectures evolving into fragmented local armies was that they were first defeated one by one by peasant uprisings, and then the remnants rebelled and declared independence, with the *Yingyang Langjiang* becoming local warlords. Most of the "rebel kings" at the end of the Sui Dynasty were originally *Yingyang Langjiang* of the Great Sui.

The *Huben Langjiang* was the deputy to the Great General of the Twelve Guards and was not a commander of troops during major wars. They accepted orders from the Emperor and held the authority to mobilize multiple *Yingyang* Prefectures. Currently, the *Huben Langjiang* remained essentially a central official, only leading troops when ordered by the Emperor to go on a campaign.

By having Li Shimin serve as *Huben Langjiang* and Li Xuanba as his deputy, the *Huya Langjiang* (Tiger-Tooth General), and stationing them permanently in Qinghe Commandery, Yang Guang had broken the principle of the central government dispatching its own direct generals to lead troops, instead allowing mid-to-high-level generals to be stationed directly in the localities.

This change greatly excited the court ministers. When Emperor Wen of Sui was pacifying the world, he had also devolved military power to the localities, setting up "General Administration Prefectures" at important passes that combined military and civil authority. After the world was stabilized, Emperor Wen naturally reclaimed local military power, abolished these administrations, and stripped military authority from local officials.

Now that "people-thieves" (rebels) were rising everywhere, re-implementing the policy of combining military and civil authority was indeed the best way to stabilize the state. It was estimated that the power of generals to "establish their own offices," which had been abolished by the two generations of Emperors Wen and Yang, would also be restored.

For now, this was just a sign. If the civil unrest were quickly quelled, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba would certainly return to the center. Currently, their stationing in Qinghe Commandery was merely a standard military deployment. Thinking this way, many court ministers and nobles secretly hoped the unrest would not be quelled too quickly.

The chaotic era of the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties had lasted 369 years, and the Great Sui’s unification had only reached its second generation. Most of the high-ranking officials in the court still had memories of that chaotic time. If Emperor Wen could usurp the throne from a powerful minister, why couldn't they? The chaotic world was a grand stage, and anyone with a dream could step onto it.

Yang Guang, however, did not think so deeply. He did not take the rebels or Goguryeo to heart. Goguryeo was only as large as a single commandery of the Great Sui; if he threw the entire strength of the nation at it, it would surely be a resounding, glorious victory. When he returned in triumph, he would simply crush those rebels like ants on his way back.

Therefore, Yang Guang was particularly annoyed by those officials with nervous expressions. *Learn from Li Erlang and Li Sanlang! The purpose of my ordering you to suppress the rebels is to ensure the smooth progress of corvée labor and military conscription, not to drag down the efficiency of my imperial expedition.*

Yang Guang was not a fool. Did he not know that the aristocratic families and nobles hid private soldiers and weapons in their homes, and that local magnates hadn't even dismantled their fortified manors? How much of a threat could those petty rebels pose to the powerful clans? The officials from these clans who were jumping around in court were simply reluctant to help the state suppress the rebels without compensation. To interrupt his great imperial expedition for such a trivial matter—these people truly made no effort to hide their disloyalty.

The more Yang Guang thought about it, the angrier he became, and he threw several censors into prison for suggesting he postpone the expedition against Goguryeo upon seeing the rise of the rebellions.

Su Wei actually wanted to advise Yang Guang not to be so hasty and to give the people a chance to breathe. Seeing the situation, he had to keep his mouth shut to avoid bringing trouble upon himself. He deeply missed the days when Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were still in court. If those two old men were still there, they would certainly have argued with the Emperor on principle. Su Wei wanted to write to them to urge them to step forward, but he feared Yang Guang still held a grudge against Gao Jiong, so he abandoned the idea to avoid being labeled as part of Gao Jiong’s faction.

The appointment of the two young "Langjiang" caused a massive stir in the court, with officials of all ranks harboring their own secret agendas.

Having achieved his goal, Li Xuanba stayed in Zhuo Commandery for a few more days. After the merchant caravan of Yehu arrived with treasures from the Western Regions and fine horses and hounds, Li Xuanba finished distributing gifts to the "Five Nobles of the Daye Era" and packed a grand gift package of hounds and horses for Yang Guang before finally setting off. During this time, he spent his days in the palace accompanying Yang Guang and the Empress, only staying at the residence where Li Yuan was lodging for the final two days.

Li Yuan had spent these days sorting out his emotions and had calmed down significantly. After careful reflection, he broke out in a cold sweat. A moment of negligence had nearly sent his entire family to the executioner's block.

When he saw Li Xuanba again, Li Yuan was filled with nothing but guilt. "Dade, this time, it was your father who almost harmed you."

Li Xuanba replied dryly, "Er-ge and I would probably only have been exiled, but you, Father, would definitely have been ordered to commit suicide."

Li Xuanba made a throat-slitting gesture, for which he was rapped on the head by Li Yuan. Seeing his son still complaining with such lack of decorum, Li Yuan knew he wasn't truly angry, and his expression relaxed considerably.

He defended himself, "I only told you to act as the situation required and to humor the Zheng family; I never intended for you to become their bodyguards. Even if they were truly private soldiers of the Tang Duke’s mansion, there is no way they would be sent to serve as bodyguards for the Zheng family."

The more Li Yuan thought about it, the angrier he got, slamming the table. "How did it get rumored that I sent you and Er-lang to be bodyguards for the Zheng family?!"

Li Xuanba said, "Perhaps the name of the Xingyang Zheng clan is too prestigious, so even the servants of our Tang Duke’s mansion feel they are a cut above. Isn't there a saying, 'Emperors flow like water, but clans are iron-wrought'? That high-born clans are more noble than the imperial family? Most people among the common folk probably think that way."

Li Yuan sneered, "Iron-wrought clans? Plenty of 'iron-wrought' clans have been slaughtered."

Li Xuanba was not surprised by Li Yuan's words. Li Yuan valued the clans, but only for the benefits they could bring him; he didn't have any genuine respect for the "gold-plated" reputation of the clans. When Li Yuan became Emperor, he acted entirely on his own whims and cared little for the high-born clans. He was particularly partial to the Hedong Pei clan, only because they were the "original shareholders" of his uprising.

Regarding the Xingyang Zheng clan, Li Yuan also showed a very snobbish side. When seeking a Zheng woman for Li Jiancheng, he acted like a sycophant. Once the marriage was settled and the Tang Duke’s mansion was on the rise, he put on the airs of a Duke toward them. When the Zheng clan wanted to invest in Li Xuanba and Li Shimin’s soap and printing shops, Li Yuan had declined on the pretext that they were doing business with the Emperor and the princes, unwilling to let the Zheng clan have a slice of the pie. Li Yuan was petty; since the Zheng clan had once been indifferent to him, he treated them with only the bare minimum of courtesy.

"If it weren't for Bishamen (Li Jiancheng) writing to beg me, I would have pushed it aside," Li Yuan explained. "After all, it is his wife's family; one must give them some face."

Li Xuanba said, "I know. To you, Father, and to me and Er-ge, the Zheng clan is unimportant; to Da-xiong (Big Brother), the Zheng clan is very important. He will likely follow the path of a civil official and needs their support."

Li Yuan recalled how Li Jiancheng had volunteered to go to Zhuo Commandery to earn merit, only to break down in tears and run back to Luoyang halfway, and a look of disappointment couldn't help but surface in his eyes. "The future glory of the Tang Duke’s mansion will have to rely on you and Da-xiong."

Li Yuan patted Li Xuanba’s shoulder, saying earnestly, "Your brother is a lost cause; as long as he isn't stripped of his title and can live as a wealthy idler on a Duke's stipend, that's enough. The future brilliance of the Li family can only depend on you and Da-xiong. But Dade, although this matter was urgent, you should have let Da-xiong come with you. Your martial arts are so poor—what would you have done if an accident occurred on the way?"

Li Yuan grew more worried as he spoke, becoming long-winded. Halfway through, Li Xuanba tried to escape, but was pinned by Li Yuan’s hands and forced to listen to a full hour of nagging. As Li Yuan complained, he began to worry about Li Xuanba’s health and felt lingering fear over how close they had come to angering Yang Guang, eventually wiping away tears.

Li Xuanba had to comfort Li Yuan in return. He was glad Er-ge hadn't come this time; otherwise, he would surely have been hugging Father and crying, doubling the "sonic torture." Fortunately, he was leaving immediately.

The river was blocked by grain transport ships, so Li Xuanba still chose to ride back to Qinghe. Li Yuan saw him off to the city gate. At parting, Li Yuan sighed that his son had surpassed him. Although both were "General" titles, a *Fubing* General and a miscellaneous-title General were completely different; he, too, had to work hard to surpass his sons soon.

After Li Xuanba had ridden a few hundred meters, he looked back and saw Li Yuan still looking up at him. When Li Yuan saw him turn, he waved. Li Xuanba’s mouth turned down involuntarily. He flicked his whip at his father and sped up his departure.

He had thought that since his "reporting to the Emperor" had led to Li Yuan being punished, Li Yuan would blame him regardless of who was in the right. He hadn't expected Li Yuan to apologize, reflect, feel fear for having implicated him and Er-ge, and even show concern for his health. Seeing Er-ge’s official rank surpass his own, Li Yuan, though a bit dejected and uncomfortable, had also shown pride and gratification.

Li Xuanba thought of his parents from his previous life, whose faces he couldn't even remember, who had dragged him into the abyss. In this life, his father and mother would certainly be considered very "bad" in the eyes of most people raised in normal families in the future.

Li Xuanba suppressed the urge to look back again until he passed a bend in the road, at which point he slowed his horse. He took a deep breath, exhaling the stuffiness in his heart.

"Stop."

The guards pulled their reins in confusion.

Li Xuanba said, "Change course. I’m going to Mount Tai."

Chen Tieniu tried to dissuade him: "Langjun, the civil unrest in Qilu is also very serious. We should hurry back to reunite with Er-langjun."

Li Xuanba said, "I have something to do. This is an order. Follow me to Mount Tai."

Li Xuanba extended his arm. With a "chirp," Wudi landed on his arm. Whether in Qinghe or Zhuo Commandery, Wudi had always accompanied him. Neither Yang Guang nor Li Yuan knew that a golden eagle was circling above, landing brazenly in their kitchens every night to eat meat.

"Wudi, did you remember this road?" Li Xuanba asked.

Wudi shook its head.

Li Xuanba sighed, "True, you've only walked it once; you wouldn't remember. Then keep following me."

Wudi: "Chirp chirp!" *Even if I remember, I have to say I don't, hee hee hee.*

Li Xuanba told a guard, "You go back to Qinghe first and tell Er-ge that I will be late. Don't come looking for me; we might miss each other on the road." When they left Qinghe, Li Shimin had ordered his confidants to obey any order from Li Xuanba. The guard was worried but had no choice but to comply.

After the messenger left, Li Xuanba led the remaining men toward Jibei Commandery. Although there was unrest in Qilu, the rule of the Great Sui in the seventh year of Daye was still solid, and the peasant armies had not yet reached the stage of seizing cities. The commandery city was safe.

Mount Tai had always been a gathering place for scholars and poets. Even with the unrest, there were many scholars visiting the foot of the mountain. They all brought guards and didn't care about the rebellion. The peasant armies usually bypassed these young nobles with guards.

They would travel a section of the official road to Mount Tai. Although the road was under "traffic control" for grain transport, Li Xuanba held an official rank and could still use it. He rode his horse past the numb-looking conscripted laborers, past the scattered corpses on the roadside and the walking dead gnawing on them, and arrived at the small path leading to Mount Tai.

In the town at the foot of Mount Tai, the wine banners of the eateries still fluttered in the wind. Li Xuanba found an inn with a relatively grand appearance and dismounted, turning to Tieniu: "Go rent a large courtyard; if you can't rent one, buy it. I’m staying here for a few days."

Chen Tieniu said with a bitter face, "Langjun, I beg you, let's go back to Qinghe. Er-langjun is waiting for you."

Li Xuanba said, "This is an order, understand?"

Chen Tieniu muttered, "Understand, understand. Can't let Langjun say the order a second time. I'll go right now."

The guards all sighed. The team leader, Zhou Da, asked, "San-langjun, what if we really encounter danger?"

Li Xuanba said, "If we really encounter danger, they will respectfully send me away."

Zhou Da: "Ah?"

Li Xuanba stroked the golden eagle’s head on his arm and said, "Who doesn't know that the Sui army is preparing for the Goguryeo campaign, and only my Er-ge, Li Shimin, has an invincible elite force? With the unrest rising everywhere, only Er-ge’s elite troops are fighting and stretched thin. But who would dare touch me... Hmph."

He looked around: "I don't think any rebel group would want to be the first to be targeted by Er-ge. Shopkeeper, do you have fresh meat? My eagle is a picky eater."

Wudi looked up: "Chirp!" *Yes! I am picky!*

In the middle of winter, the waiter was probably too busy, as a layer of sweat appeared on his forehead: "Yes, yes, the hunters just sent some. It's just... noble one, our inn can't accommodate so many people."

Li Xuanba said, "It doesn't matter, I’m just resting here temporarily."

Zhou Da ordered ten men to enter the inn to guard Li Xuanba, while the others rested at the door. Li Xuanba bought flatbread and water for them, specifically instructing that the water be boiled. In ancient times, there were no "knockout drops" that worked instantly; at most, people would use croton or impure arsenic. As long as one drank tasteless warm water, one could avoid most "poisons."

Before long, Chen Tieniu returned. Behind him followed a bowing, portly middle-aged man.

"Langjun, this is the local *Lizheng* (village head). He wants to invite you to stay at his home," Chen Tieniu said.

Li Xuanba looked at the *Lizheng*. The man plopped to his knees and kowtowed: "Pa-pay respects to the General! If the General doesn't mind, my home is quite spacious and can accommodate you."

Li Xuanba said calmly, "I like quiet."

The *Lizheng* hurriedly said, "My... my family will move to our villa! We will definitely not disturb the General!"

Li Xuanba nodded: "Good, then I will trouble you for a while. Please rise."

The *Lizheng* stood up, trembling. Li Xuanba followed him away. The waiter breathed a sigh of relief.

As Li Xuanba was about to leave the inn, he paused and said, "I have come here to invite the 'World-Knowing Gentleman,' Wang Bo, for a chat. Once I have seen him, I will leave. I have already sent word to Er-ge and must return early. I hope I won't have to wait too long."

The *Lizheng* leading the way and the shopkeeper seeing him off were both stunned. Li Xuanba walked away after speaking. The travelers hadn't heard his words before he left and began whispering among themselves.

"That young man just now looked so handsome, though a bit too thin. I wonder which family's scholar he is."

"Did you see his guards? He must be a young noble from the commandery."

"Maybe an even higher-ranking noble passing through."

"The *Lizheng* called him 'General.' Such a young general—perhaps a noble with family influence in the court."

"Really? Should we go pay a visit?"

"I'm afraid of disturbing the noble..."

A Taoist priest stroked his long beard, looking at Li Xuanba’s retreating figure with a glimmer of interest.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第94章 意外的鱼咬了钩
chunks.chineseText:
第94章 意外的鱼咬了钩

=
　　李玄霸住进了里正家中。
　　里正把大院子腾出来， 又从库房里拿出最新的绸缎给李玄霸铺床，把妻妾子女迁到别院后，自己留在了偏院等候差遣。
　　李玄霸的护卫接管了院落里外防卫。陈铁牛还特意给当地鹰扬府和郡守送信， 说自家虎牙郎将回清河郡赴任前顺路去泰山观景， 希望行个方便。
　　当地鹰扬郎将和郡守都很遗憾现在自己要剿贼， 没空去拜访李玄霸。
　　这可是如今朝堂最闪耀的双子星少年郎将之一，皇帝最疼爱的表侄，谁不想去混个脸熟？
　　他们都写信希望李玄霸多待一段时日， 最好能绕路来郡城坐一坐，他们一定隆重接待。
　　随着信而来的还有许多礼物，李玄霸全笑纳了。
　　全大隋的人都知道李玄霸爱书， 李世民爱弓。齐鲁之地是儒学起源之地，古籍不少。李玄霸得了不少汉魏珍本。无论珍本是真是假， 没看过的书李玄霸都喜欢。
　　至于那些强弓， 李玄霸觉得自家二哥估计看不上，等回家送给小五玩了。
　　李玄霸在泰山脚下住下，第二日就有来泰山游览的士人送拜帖。
　　无论地位高低，李玄霸都认真看过拜帖后，亲自写信回绝。
　　虽然他一个人没见， 但在士人中传出了平易近人的名声。
　　李玄霸对里正道：“我只在泰山脚下待五日，待久了， 二哥就要亲自来抓我了。你可要让知世郎早些来。”
　　里正做出一副吓哭的模样：“草民绝对和民贼没有勾连！”
　　李玄霸只笑了笑，不说话。
　　李玄霸来到泰山脚下的第三日，等的人还没来。
　　他一点不急， 在书房里生了火， 一边烤火一边整理从当地义庄那里得到的情报。
　　李玄霸早早根据史料记载的民乱地点着重布置了许多义庄， 他辛辛苦苦攒了多年的积蓄现在是全掏空了。
　　布局这么多年， 得到的情报没有辜负李玄霸的付出。
　　选择最先接触的农民起义军首领时，李玄霸原本属意瓦岗寨。
　　瓦岗寨现在不仅是最不起眼的一支，还是全天下人都以为他们会被最先剿灭的一支——这支农民起义军吃了熊心豹子胆，活动范围就在东都洛阳附近。
　　天下人却不知道杨广的性格。
　　杨广性格极其自负，这种自负在打完吐谷浑后达到了顶峰，现在是半句坏话都听不得。若有人和他说东都洛阳附近出现民乱，杨广只会将这人下狱甚至杀掉。所以无论是洛阳附近地方官，还是杨广身边的人，都不敢提洛阳附近有民乱一事。
　　皇帝不下令，不派虎贲郎将来统合地区兵力剿匪，鹰扬府的兵就出不了管辖范围，只能在自己地盘上晃荡。
　　瓦岗寨农民起义军就像后世玩家在即时制地图上打怪似的，怪物有仇恨范围限制，只要看好仇恨范围，就能轻松无伤发育，最后居然发展成最庞大的一支农民起义军。
　　李玄霸分析了一番瓦岗寨农民起义军兴衰过程后，放弃了提前接触。
　　洛阳毕竟是敏感地带，现在瓦岗寨农民起义军灯下黑，等他接触之后就不一定了。
　　再者翟让已经干得很好了，自己在品行上也称得上比窦建德更加光明磊落的完人，才会被李密背信弃义坑了。现在他只需要按照历史中该有的模样发展，就是最完美的情况，不需要自己画蛇添足。
　　筛选后，李玄霸选中了王薄。
　　王薄是隋朝揭竿而起的第一人，但这不是李玄霸选中他的原因。
　　李玄霸认定王薄最适合，是因为王薄曾先降宇文化及，又降窦建德，同年又率众投靠李渊。
　　王薄这反复投靠的行径，证明了他内心的软弱。虽然被迫揭竿而起，但如果给他一个投靠“朝廷”的机会，他一定会抓住。
　　话又说回来，把如此软弱的王薄逼得最先揭竿而起，大隋皇帝也真是厉害了。
　　王薄反复的过程也很有意思。
　　他最先投靠的时候，没有选择更近的军阀或者农民起义军首领，而是千里迢迢去投奔杀了大隋皇帝的宇文化及。
　　在宇文化及快要失败的时候，他开城投靠窦建德还能说只是自保。但他前脚投奔窦建德，立刻就率领下属跑去李渊那里了，摆明了看不上同为农民起义军首领的窦建德，更看好李渊。
　　这说明两点，第一，王薄深恨隋炀帝；第二，在没有隋炀帝的前提下，王薄对贵族阶层很向往。
　　王薄对贵族阶层的向往，就让他在李玄霸面前自矮一头，便于李玄霸说服。
　　明年王薄所率领的农民起义军就会把泰山脚下当做大本营。王薄行军并非没有章法，他在选泰山之前，肯定已经派人来安插过钉子。
　　经李玄霸查探，这个里正是王薄远亲。虽然两人几乎没有来往，但在已经知道王薄明年会把大本营搬到泰山这个既定事实之后，王薄的“钉子窝点”就已经很明确了。
　　李玄霸不认为自己是多聪明的谋士，但有了足够的情报，再从未来倒推现在，应当是不会出错的。
　　至于这件事是否冒险，李玄霸认为冒的险很少。
　　如今虽说是民乱四起，动不动就聚集万人以上，但分摊到各个郡县，也就是山贼水平。
　　大业五年是隋朝最强盛的时刻，现在才大业七年，别说杨广不在意，民乱发生所在地的地方官都没把民贼当回事。农民起义军也没想过做大做强，只是聚集在山窝里求活而已。
　　自己有“战无不胜”二哥作为威慑，又有义庄打响的仁义名声，再加上史书中盖棺论定的王薄心中对贵族阶层的羡慕软弱，李玄霸顶多无功而返罢了。
　　如果他无功而返，那不是自己的损失，是王薄的损失。
　　李玄霸整理情报时，书房外传来嘈杂的声音。
　　李玄霸见陈铁牛气势汹汹地走进来，问道：“终于来了？”
　　陈铁牛抱拳：“有个道士在门口鬼鬼祟祟，不知道是不是王薄的人，我先绑进来了。”
　　“道士？”李玄霸把情报叠好，“带进来。”
　　李玄霸想，不会是什么初唐小说常客袁天罡李淳风吧？
　　他刚生出这个念头，就笑着摇摇头。
　　袁天罡和李淳风，与明朝的刘基刘伯温一样，都是被传奇小说带上了他们本人都瞠目结舌的神棍高度。
　　袁天罡和李淳风不是师徒，身份地位相差甚远，实际上应该没什么交情，《推背图》是后人附会。
　　袁天罡确实是个相士。但此时勋贵对相术谶纬是又相信、又鄙夷，相士更像是一个养在身边供玩乐佞臣。所以袁天罡一生也没做过高官。
　　李淳风则是李世民当秦王时就跟随左右的心腹文臣，贞观年间任太常博士、太史令，唐高宗时授昌乐县男。他在天文、历法、数学上颇有建树，是个正经的高官勋贵，在正史中也没给人看过相。
　　若是李淳风看到后人把他写成神棍，还是袁天罡的“弟子”，肯定气得揭棺而起。
　　再者袁天罡现在在蜀地资官当县令，李淳风还是个垂髫孩童，不可能出现在这里。
　　李玄霸猜测，那道士可能真的是王薄派来的。
　　他整理了一下仪容，摆出了一副和蔼可亲的态度，免得吓跑王薄的探子。
　　被捆着双手的道士被陈铁牛带了上来。
　　李玄霸和气道：“若他没有带武器，就解绑吧。”
　　陈铁牛早就搜了道士的身，把道士腰间唯一一把铁剑收走。
　　闻言，他解开了道士手上的绳索，然后按着腰上刀柄站在李玄霸身侧，瞪大眼睛看着青年道士。
　　乌镝本来正摇头晃脑吃肉条。它歪着头看了陈铁牛一眼，落在了李玄霸另一边的肩膀上，也瞪大眼睛看着青年道士。
　　虽然留了长须，但面容很年轻的道士被陈铁牛和乌镝瞪得萎缩了一下。
　　李玄霸伸手弹了一下乌镝的肚子：“下去，重。”
　　乌镝不满地低头拱了一下李玄霸的脸，拍翅膀飞到陈铁牛肩膀上，继续威风凛凛地瞪着青年道士。
　　青年道士见乌镝如此灵动的表情，心中对传闻中李三郎的神异信了几分。
　　他跪地道：“在下不是鬼祟之人，只是想拜见李三郎君。”
　　李玄霸问道：“那为何不送拜帖，而是在周围游荡？”
　　青年道士苦笑：“在下出身寒微，不敢贸然寄拜帖，所以犹豫了几日。”谁知道就被当贼绑了。
　　李玄霸道：“起身说话吧。你是想投靠我？”
　　青年道士起身，恭敬道：“是。”
　　李玄霸颔首：“敢自投拜帖的寒士不多，你既然有这个勇气，大概是有些底气的。虽然我平时不收投靠之人，但既然你被逮到了我面前，就算你我二人有缘。我给你一个表现自己的机会。如果你真的有才华，我会帮你举荐。”
　　李玄霸仍旧猜测面前这人是王薄派来的，所以他尽可能地展现出自己礼贤下士的态度。待这人“打探”了自己的性情后，就该王薄出场了。
　　王薄再不来，二哥真的要骑马赶来逮人了。
　　青年道士没想到李玄霸如此好说话。
　　勋贵子弟在旁人的印象中都是嚣张跋扈的，何况李玄霸还年幼成名，目无下尘才正常。
　　自己被当做歹人捆了进来，不仅没有被责罚，李三郎君还很和气地夸奖他自投拜帖很有勇气，愿意给自己一个展现自己的机会。青年道士心头一暖，连眼眶都红了。
　　他从怀里掏出一本已经有毛边的书册，躬身低头双手高举，哽咽道：“在下姓魏名徵字玄成，此为在下所作诗文，请三郎君过目。”
　　李玄霸平易近人地微笑道：“好。铁牛，你把诗文册拿……啊？！你姓甚名谁？！”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 94: An Unexpected Fish Takes the Bait

Li Xuanba took up residence in the village head’s home.

The village head cleared out his main courtyard, brought out the finest silks from his storehouse to dress the bed, and after relocating his wives, concubines, and children to a side compound, remained in the servant’s quarters himself, waiting to be of service.

Li Xuanba’s guards took over the security of the compound’s interior and exterior. Chen Tieniu even took the initiative to send letters to the local Eagle-Yang Prefecture and the Commandery Governor, stating that their Tiger-Tooth General was passing through Mount Tai to enjoy the scenery before heading to Qinghe Commandery to assume his post, and hoped for some convenience.

The local Eagle-Yang General and the Commandery Governor were both deeply regretful that they were currently occupied with suppressing bandits and had no time to pay a visit to Li Xuanba.

This was, after all, one of the most dazzling young twin-star generals in the imperial court, the Emperor’s most doted-upon cousin—who wouldn't want to make a good impression?

They all wrote back hoping Li Xuanba would stay for a while longer, and that he might even take a detour to the commandery seat for a visit, promising a grand reception.

Along with the letters came many gifts, all of which Li Xuanba accepted with a smile.

Everyone in the Great Sui knew that Li Xuanba loved books, while Li Shimin loved bows. The land of Qi and Lu was the cradle of Confucianism, and there were many ancient texts to be found. Li Xuanba acquired quite a few rare editions from the Han and Wei dynasties. Regardless of whether the rare editions were genuine or fake, Li Xuanba loved any book he hadn't read before.

As for those heavy bows, Li Xuanba figured his Second Brother probably wouldn't care for them, so he decided to take them home for Little Five to play with.

Li Xuanba settled in at the foot of Mount Tai. By the second day, scholars visiting the mountain began sending in calling cards.

Regardless of their status, Li Xuanba carefully read every card before personally writing letters to decline their visits.

Although he didn't meet a single person, a reputation for being approachable spread among the scholars.

Li Xuanba said to the village head, "I will only stay at the foot of Mount Tai for five days. If I stay any longer, my Second Brother will come to drag me home himself. You had better make sure 'Zhishi-lang' arrives soon."

The village head put on a look of feigned terror: "This humble commoner has absolutely no connection with the rebels!"

Li Xuanba merely smiled and said nothing.

On the third day of Li Xuanba’s stay at the foot of Mount Tai, the person he was waiting for had yet to appear.

He was not in the least bit anxious. He lit a fire in the study and, while warming himself, organized the intelligence he had gathered from the local charity halls.

Li Xuanba had long ago strategically established many charity halls based on historical records of where civil uprisings had occurred. He had exhausted the savings he had painstakingly accumulated over many years to do so.

After years of laying the groundwork, the intelligence he received did not betray his efforts.

When choosing which peasant rebel leader to contact first, Li Xuanba had originally favored the Wagang Army.

The Wagang Army was currently not only the most inconspicuous faction, but also the one everyone in the world assumed would be the first to be wiped out—this group of peasant rebels had the audacity to operate right in the vicinity of the Eastern Capital, Luoyang.

Yet, the world did not understand Yang Guang’s personality.

Yang Guang was extremely conceited. This conceit had reached its peak after the campaign against the Tuyuhun, and now he could not bear to hear a single word of criticism. If anyone told him there was a civil uprising near the Eastern Capital of Luoyang, Yang Guang would only have that person imprisoned or even executed. Thus, neither the local officials near Luoyang nor those in Yang Guang’s inner circle dared to mention the uprisings.

Without an imperial decree or the dispatch of Tiger-Brave Generals to coordinate regional forces for suppression, the troops of the Eagle-Yang Prefecture could not leave their jurisdictions and could only loiter within their own territories.

The Wagang peasant rebels were like players in a real-time strategy game; the "monsters" had restricted aggro ranges. As long as they kept an eye on those ranges, they could develop safely and easily, eventually growing into the largest peasant rebel force.

After analyzing the rise and fall of the Wagang Army, Li Xuanba gave up on contacting them early.

Luoyang was, after all, a sensitive area. The Wagang Army was currently hidden in the shadows, but that might change once he made contact.

Furthermore, Zhai Rang was already doing a fine job. In terms of character, he could be called a more upright and perfect man than Dou Jiande, which was precisely why he was eventually betrayed and sabotaged by Li Mi. Now, he only needed to let things develop as they did in history; that was the perfect scenario. There was no need for him to gild the lily.

After filtering his options, Li Xuanba chose Wang Bo.

Wang Bo was the first person to raise the banner of rebellion in the Sui Dynasty, but that was not why Li Xuanba chose him.

Li Xuanba determined that Wang Bo was the most suitable candidate because Wang Bo had first surrendered to Yuwen Huaji, then to Dou Jiande, and in the same year, led his followers to defect to Li Yuan.

Wang Bo’s history of repeated defections proved his inner weakness. Although he had been forced to rebel, if given a chance to defect to the "imperial court," he would certainly seize it.

Then again, the fact that the Great Sui Emperor had pushed a man as weak-willed as Wang Bo to be the first to rebel was truly something.

Wang Bo’s process of repeated defection was also quite interesting.

When he first defected, he didn't choose a nearby warlord or rebel leader, but traveled thousands of miles to join Yuwen Huaji, the man who had killed the Sui Emperor.

When Yuwen Huaji was on the verge of failure, his act of opening the city to surrender to Dou Jiande could still be called self-preservation. But no sooner had he joined Dou Jiande than he immediately led his subordinates to defect to Li Yuan, clearly showing that he looked down on Dou Jiande as a fellow rebel leader and favored Li Yuan instead.

This proved two things: first, Wang Bo deeply hated Emperor Yang of Sui; second, in the absence of Emperor Yang, Wang Bo yearned for the aristocratic class.

Wang Bo’s yearning for the aristocracy made him feel inferior in front of Li Xuanba, which made him easier for Li Xuanba to persuade.

Next year, the peasant rebel army led by Wang Bo would make the foot of Mount Tai their base of operations. Wang Bo’s military movements were not without method; before choosing Mount Tai, he must have already sent people to plant "nails" there.

According to Li Xuanba’s investigation, this village head was a distant relative of Wang Bo. Although the two had almost no contact, now that it was a known fact that Wang Bo would move his base to Mount Tai next year, the location of Wang Bo’s "nail" was quite clear.

Li Xuanba did not consider himself an exceptionally brilliant strategist, but with sufficient intelligence and the ability to deduce the present from the future, he shouldn't go wrong.

As for whether this was risky, Li Xuanba believed the risk was minimal.

Although it was said that civil uprisings were springing up everywhere, often gathering tens of thousands of people, when broken down by commandery and county, they were really just at the level of mountain bandits.

The fifth year of Daye was the peak of the Sui Dynasty; it was only the seventh year of Daye now. Not to mention that Yang Guang didn't care, even the local officials where the uprisings occurred didn't take the rebels seriously. The peasant rebels themselves hadn't thought about growing strong; they were just huddled in the mountains trying to survive.

With his "invincible" Second Brother as a deterrent, the reputation for benevolence he had built through the charity halls, and the historical certainty of Wang Bo’s weakness and envy of the aristocracy, the worst that could happen was that Li Xuanba would return empty-handed.

If he returned empty-handed, it wouldn't be his loss—it would be Wang Bo’s.

As Li Xuanba was organizing his intelligence, a noisy commotion came from outside the study.

Seeing Chen Tieniu walk in with a menacing air, Li Xuanba asked, "Finally here?"

Chen Tieniu cupped his hands: "There was a Taoist priest acting suspiciously at the gate. I didn't know if he was one of Wang Bo’s men, so I tied him up and brought him in."

"A Taoist priest?" Li Xuanba folded his intelligence reports. "Bring him in."

Li Xuanba thought, it wouldn't be one of those recurring characters from early Tang novels like Yuan Tiangang or Li Chunfeng, would it?

He had just had this thought when he smiled and shook his head.

Yuan Tiangang and Li Chunfeng, much like Liu Ji and Liu Bowen of the Ming Dynasty, had been elevated by legendary novels to a level of mystical status that would have left the men themselves dumbfounded.

Yuan Tiangang and Li Chunfeng were not master and disciple; their statuses and positions were vastly different, and in reality, they likely had no friendship. The *Tui Bei Tu* (Back-Pushing Chart) was a later attribution.

Yuan Tiangang was indeed a physiognomist. But at the time, the nobility both believed in and despised physiognomy and prophecy; a physiognomist was more like a sycophant kept around for amusement. Thus, Yuan Tiangang never held a high office in his life.

Li Chunfeng, on the other hand, was a trusted civil official who had followed Li Shimin since he was the Prince of Qin. During the Zhenguan era, he served as a Taichang Doctor and Grand Historian, and was granted the title of Baron of Changle during the reign of Emperor Gaozong of Tang. He had significant achievements in astronomy, the calendar, and mathematics. He was a legitimate high-ranking official and noble, and in official history, he never practiced physiognomy for others.

If Li Chunfeng saw that later generations had written him off as a mystic and a "disciple" of Yuan Tiangang, he would surely be so angry he’d rise from his grave.

Furthermore, Yuan Tiangang was currently a county magistrate in the Shu region, and Li Chunfeng was still a young child; it was impossible for them to appear here.

Li Xuanba guessed that the Taoist priest might truly have been sent by Wang Bo.

He tidied his appearance and assumed an amiable and approachable attitude, lest he scare off Wang Bo’s scout.

The Taoist priest, his hands bound, was brought in by Chen Tieniu.

Li Xuanba said kindly, "If he is not carrying any weapons, untie him."

Chen Tieniu had long since searched the priest, confiscating the only iron sword at his waist.

At these words, he untied the ropes on the priest’s hands, then stood at Li Xuanba’s side with his hand on the hilt of his sword, eyes wide as he stared at the young priest.

Wudi was busy bobbing its head while eating a strip of meat. It tilted its head to look at Chen Tieniu, then landed on Li Xuanba’s other shoulder, also staring wide-eyed at the young priest.

Though he wore a long beard, the young priest, who had a very youthful face, shrank back under the stares of Chen Tieniu and Wudi.

Li Xuanba reached out and flicked Wudi’s belly: "Down, you're heavy."

Wudi grumbled, lowered its head to nudge Li Xuanba’s face, then flapped its wings and flew onto Chen Tieniu’s shoulder, continuing to glare majestically at the young priest.

Seeing Wudi’s remarkably intelligent expression, the young priest believed the rumors about the miraculous nature of the Third Young Master Li a little more.

He knelt and said, "I am not a suspicious person; I only wished to pay my respects to Third Young Master Li."

Li Xuanba asked, "Then why did you not send a calling card, but instead wandered about the perimeter?"

The young priest gave a bitter smile: "I am of humble origin and dared not send a calling card rashly, so I hesitated for several days." Who knew he would be tied up as a thief?

Li Xuanba said, "Rise and speak. Do you wish to pledge your service to me?"

The young priest stood up and said respectfully, "Yes."

Li Xuanba nodded: "There are not many scholars of humble origin who dare to submit their own calling cards. Since you have this courage, you must have some substance. Although I do not usually accept those who pledge their service, since you have been caught and brought before me, it is fate. I will give you a chance to prove yourself. If you truly have talent, I will recommend you."

Li Xuanba still suspected this man was sent by Wang Bo, so he displayed his attitude of respecting the virtuous as much as possible. Once this man "probed" his temperament, it would be time for Wang Bo to make his entrance.

If Wang Bo didn't come soon, his Second Brother really would ride over to drag him home.

The young priest had not expected Li Xuanba to be so easy to talk to.

In the eyes of others, the children of the nobility were all arrogant and overbearing; furthermore, Li Xuanba had become famous at a young age, so it would be normal for him to be aloof.

Not only was he not punished after being tied up as a villain, but Third Young Master Li had also kindly praised his courage in submitting his own card and was willing to give him a chance to showcase his talent. The young priest felt a warmth in his heart, and his eyes even turned red.

He took a worn book from his bosom, bowed his head, held it high with both hands, and choked out, "My surname is Wei, given name Zheng, courtesy name Xuan-cheng. This is a collection of my poems and essays. I ask that the Third Young Master take a look."

Li Xuanba smiled in a friendly, approachable manner: "Very well. Tieniu, take the book of poems... Ah?! What is your name again?!"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第95章 知世郎请看诗歌
chunks.chineseText:
第95章 知世郎请看诗歌

=
　　青年道士被李玄霸的反问吓了一跳， 结结巴巴道：“魏、魏徵，字玄成。”
　　李玄霸喝了一口温水压惊。
　　他强装镇定：“籍贯？”
　　青年魏徵道：“巨鹿曲阳……”
　　李玄霸又喝了口温水压惊。
　　行了，不必说了， 就是他。
　　为什么我会在泰山脚下遇到魏徵啊！！！
　　李玄霸接过陈铁牛递来的诗文册， 翻书的手有点僵硬。
　　魏徵呈上来的诗文册的字迹端正严谨， 与后世颜真卿所创颜楷近似。
　　李玄霸抬头看了一眼清俊飘逸的长须青年道士，又低头看了一眼诗文册端正严谨的字迹。
　　真不搭啊。
　　魏徵的诗文册如当世文人常见举荐用的诗文册一样，扉页先写了籍贯家世师从。
　　寒门士子在写扉页时特别难受， 真是绞尽脑汁也编不出半页纸。
　　因魏晋遗风，隋朝人也看家世。扉页几乎就决定了这个人能不能被举荐。看着魏徵这诗文册，扉页纸张比后一页皱许多， 可见魏徵吃了多少闭门羹。
　　李玄霸草草扫了一眼魏徵的自我介绍，就翻到了下一页， 品鉴起魏徵在史书上未曾记载的年轻时候的诗文。
　　魏徵见李玄霸将扉页翻过， 紧握的拳头缓缓松开，眼眶又红了。
　　他是多久没见到有人把他的诗文册翻到了第二页了？
　　这诗文册翻出的毛边，都是他每次自投遭拒，自己一页一页看着自己写的诗文，悲郁交加地翻出来的。
　　魏徵虽然传世的文学作品不多， 但留下的寥寥数篇诗文就可以看出他的才情，颇具初唐文质并举的气度。
　　李玄霸想起了自家二哥。
　　原本他以为二哥没有诗才。待看着二哥学了几年诗， 他才知道二哥不是没才华，只是喜好骈俪奢华的辞藻，特别爱写词华意少的宫体诗， 放到后世就是华丽字词堆砌无病呻吟的青少年疼痛散文。
　　二哥直抒胸臆的诗都是不错的， 但他就是不喜欢这么写。
　　魏徵听闻李玄霸叹息， 刚松了的一口气又提了起来， 焦急道：“可、可是在下诗文有何不妥？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“没有不妥，只是看到魏玄成文质并举，想起了二哥。二哥直抒胸臆时如‘昔乘匹马去，今驱万乘来’等句十分豪迈，却偏偏爱作‘摧藏千里态，掩抑几重悲’无病呻吟。若他肯好好深耕豪迈诗文，当世该有他的文名。”
　　李玄霸越说越气。
　　二哥明明有自己没有的诗才，偏偏就不好好打磨。若二哥能把斟酌宫体诗的精力用在直抒胸臆上，唐朝怕不是会早早出一位豪放派出塞风大诗人。
　　可他就不，就是不。
　　什么花啊雪啊云啊雨啊的堆砌一整首诗的华丽辞藻景物描写，再在最后抒发一点愁啊怨啊，李世民每每写了一首“好诗”都逼着李玄霸品鉴，李玄霸都看吐了！
　　李玄霸越想越气，一边继续看魏徵的诗文一边嘀嘀咕咕。
　　魏徵若有所思。
　　翻完魏徵的诗文册后，李玄霸将诗文册放到桌上：“诗文不错。若不介意，可否陪我同游几日？待我去了清河，就将你举荐给二哥。”
　　魏徵忙道：“在下愿意在三郎君手下为吏！”
　　李玄霸摇头：“你气势如刀，我镇不住。乖乖去我二哥麾下，只有他能镇得住你。”
　　魏徵惊讶：“三郎君还会看相？”
　　李玄霸道：“会看一点，不多。你是面相太突出。”
　　魏徵好奇问道：“三郎君观我面相是……”
　　李玄霸叹气：“跟随谁谁死，举荐谁谁叛。”
　　魏徵：“……”气血上涌，眼前一黑。
　　陈铁牛不敢置信扭头看向郎君：“郎君！那你还留他？！”
　　李玄霸失笑：“他克其他主，但能和二哥相辅相成，成就佳话。不过魏玄成，你应该再蹉跎十几年再遇到二哥，现在居然提前向我递了拜帖。要不要先在其他地方试试？说不定那十几年颠沛流离的经历，才造就了你十几年后的才华？”
　　魏徵面色赤红，支支吾吾半晌说不出话来。他能不能不信这个相面？！
　　陈铁牛小声道：“郎君，你都相面他克主了，他还敢投奔其他人吗？”
　　李玄霸开玩笑道：“这房中就我们三人，我不说你不说他也不说，难道乌镝还能在外乱说？”
　　乌镝左右歪头：“啾啾！”
　　魏徵颤颤巍巍拱手：“三郎君，求别吓唬我。”
　　李玄霸见吓到了年轻的魏徵，忍不住笑出声来：“哈哈哈哈，好，不吓唬你，不吓唬你。你都到我面前了，我就不让你多折腾十几年了。先跟着我当一段时间文吏吧，让我见识见识你纵横术的本事。”
　　陈铁牛忙劝道：“郎君，你不是说他克主吗！那他跟着郎君不妥啊！”郎君说什么他都信，说魏徵克主，那魏徵一定克主！
　　李玄霸笑道：“有二哥在，他克不到我。”自己本来就命薄，还能被怎么克？
　　李玄霸吩咐道：“让里正派人给他裁身文吏的衣服，其他一应待遇先得你一半。这是位大才，不要亏待了。”
　　陈铁牛道：“是。”
　　李玄霸对魏徵道：“我虽然知道你是大才，但你还没有展露出自己的才华，只能从最低等的文吏开始积累经验。希望你不要生气。”
　　魏徵忙作揖：“怎么会！在下受宠若惊！”
　　李玄霸道：“先去洗漱整理仪容吧。记得把长须刮了，将来你是我和二哥身边的青年才俊，可别装得太老气。”
　　魏徵摸着自己的长须，苦笑道：“是，郎君。”
　　他再三拜谢后，晕乎乎地跟随铁牛离开。
　　乌镝落到了李玄霸腿上，腿一伸，坐在了李玄霸怀里。
　　李玄霸抱着撒娇的乌镝道：“对他很好奇？”
　　乌镝：“啾啾！”
　　李玄霸失笑：“我说了你能听懂吗？”
　　乌镝扑腾翅膀：“啾啾啾！”听不懂也想听！
　　李玄霸摸着乌镝的翅膀，像是真的和乌镝解释魏徵的事，又像是自言自语。
　　魏徵，字玄成，唐太宗的“铜镜”，著名刚直谏臣。
　　他祖父魏彦官至北魏光州刺史；其父魏长贤原为北齐著作郎，因讥刺时政出为上党屯留令，在魏徵十几岁就去世了。魏徵少孤寒，又自诩志大才高不事生产，便落魄得当了道士。
　　论“成分”，魏徵的出身是标准的寒门士子。
　　寒门也有传家的“经书”，魏徵家族是以治史传家，杰出之辈皆有修史的志向。如比魏徵大几十岁的族叔魏收就是著名史学家，著有《魏书》，哪怕被当世人指为“秽史”也不妥协。
　　魏长贤的志向是修《晋书》。原本他已经快达成志向，却因讥讽时政被外贬与梦想擦肩而过，于是郁郁早逝。
　　“魏徵虽然没能主编《晋书》，但主编了《隋书》，也算达成了父亲的遗愿了。”李玄霸为乌镝顺着毛，对自己提前遇见魏徵唏嘘不已。
　　他观看魏徵的诗文册时，将魏徵的生平细细捋了一遍，发现魏徵此时在齐鲁晃悠的踪迹，其实在史书中也有痕迹。
　　魏徵前半生一直郁郁不得志，见天下大乱，属意纵横之说，一直在寻找投靠的势力。
　　史书中第一次记载魏徵的“官职”，是于大业十三年，在武阳郡丞元宝藏帐下为官。
　　武阳郡与济北郡比邻，泰山就在济北郡中。
　　魏徵籍贯是巨鹿郡，第一次做官却在武阳郡。
　　平常他这样的寒门士子没有机会为官，但在平定民乱的时候，各级官员都会招一些寒门幕僚。
　　显然，魏徵最先是前往了农民起义军最多的齐鲁，寻找为官的机会。
　　没想到现在才大业七年，农民起义军刚揭竿起义的时候，魏徵就已经在齐鲁四处晃荡。
　　李玄霸算了算魏徵的岁数，魏徵现在已经三十一岁。
　　三十一岁还贫寒潦倒一事无成，怪不得魏徵会冒险来齐鲁。
　　想到魏徵在齐鲁四处碰了六年壁，才得到武阳郡丞元宝藏的任用，李玄霸有些佩服魏徵的坚韧了。
　　若换作寻常人，心态早就崩了。魏徵是真的坚信自己很有才华，才怎么磋磨也不妥协。
　　“说起魏徵‘克主’，只是我在打压他，让还心高气傲的他别因为二哥年少就乱跑。”李玄霸轻笑，“其实他随李密归唐时已经是大唐的官吏，在窦建德麾下为官只是因为兵败被俘虏，所以算不上认窦建德为主。他只是比较倒霉和李建成绑在了一起。”
　　但能被太子厚待重用，当时谁会说他倒霉？
　　就像是魏徵推举侯君集和杜正伦有宰相之才的时候，谁又能想到这两人会卷入李承乾叛乱？
　　魏徵就只是单纯很倒霉而已。
　　不过他遇到了唐太宗李世民，霉运都变成幸运了。李世民再生气也就是把他的功德碑推倒，不和他当亲家了，后来还默默地把功德碑重新立了起来。
　　若换作寻常皇帝，他举荐的人涉及谋反，那就是坐罪祸及家人。
　　“没想到啊没想到。”李玄霸双手笑搓乌镝鸟头，“你和寒钩危险了！”
　　乌镝：“啾啾啾？”它只听懂了最后一句。什么情况？为什么危险？
　　李玄霸大笑。
　　……
　　一段李玄霸没想到的小插曲后，当夜，里正前来拜访李玄霸，恭敬地说“知世郎来访”。
　　李玄霸被迫半夜爬起来，灌了两杯蜜水，才把低血压低血糖提起来。
　　他打着哈欠道：“终于来了？”
　　里正伏地道：“知世郎听闻李三郎君对贫寒道人尚能礼遇，才相信李三郎君真心想与他见面。”
　　李玄霸对已经刮了胡子、换下道袍的魏徵笑道：“看来我还是托了你的福了。你敢旁听吗？”
　　魏徵谦恭道：“三郎君，我克三郎君和二郎君之外的主，只能待在三郎君和二郎君麾下。我什么都敢听。”
　　李玄霸失笑：“你胆子确实大。那就好好听，把今日之事告诉我二哥。我懒得自己说。”
　　也对，这位以后的刚直谏臣可是会上瓦岗寨的“反贼”。
　　魏徵道：“是。”
　　他心里十分激动。夜会民贼，这是会满门抄斩的事。他才刚来郎君麾下，郎君居然如此信任他？！
　　陈铁牛挠头。罢了，郎君总是对的，听郎君的。
　　他决定盯紧魏徵。如果魏徵敢逃跑告密，就一刀剁了魏徵的头。
　　李玄霸带着今天刚收的幕僚去见王薄，王薄和里正也吓了一跳，不由对李玄霸更加佩服。
　　里正在露天亭子中烧起一堆篝火。
　　李玄霸披着大氅走到亭子中的时候，一个穿着斗篷的中年人已经在篝火旁喝酒。
　　“‘义薄云天’李二郎，‘德重恩弘’李三郎，在下王薄，久仰。”中年人取下斗篷，对李玄霸拱手。
　　李玄霸满头问号。这是在拍《隋唐演义》吗？怎么还给自己和二哥上诨号了？
　　未来史学家魏徵眼眸一闪，将这两个“诨号”记在心底。
　　“不知道我和二哥什么时候有如此响亮的诨号，还是第一次听到。”李玄霸伸手做出请坐的姿态，好像这里是他的主场似的，“知世郎孤身赴会，真是好胆色。”
　　王薄苦笑：“孤身赴会的难道不是李三郎君吗？”
　　李玄霸坐在亭中已经被篝火烤热的石墩上，松了松大氅的领口：“这大隋还是陛下的大隋，我身为陛下的虎牙郎将，去哪里都不算孤身。”
　　王薄脸色一沉：“李三郎君是要招抚我吗？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“陛下有令，‘都尉、鹰扬与郡县相知追捕，随获斩决’。”
　　王薄骂道：“狗贼皇帝！”
　　李玄霸拿起酒碗，为自己和王薄各斟了一碗，将其中一碗递给王薄。
　　王薄接过酒碗：“那李三郎君特意来这里是为何？”
　　李玄霸笑道：“见一见未来的同僚。知世郎，你信命吗？”
　　王薄沉声：“你是说我命中仍旧会归服狗贼皇帝？不可能！他害我一家饿死，我只想亲手斩下狗贼的头颅！”
　　李玄霸摇头：“你当然不可能归服陛下。那换个话题吧，知世郎，你想过起兵后的未来吗？”
　　王薄直直地看着李玄霸淡漠的双眼：“没有。”
　　李玄霸道：“你倒是坦率。”
　　王薄道：“我只是不想死。所有跟着我上山的人都是只想着现在不死。所以李三郎君，你要和我说什么未来？”
　　李玄霸又转移话题。
　　他问道：“识字吗？”
　　王薄皱眉：“识得一些。”
　　李玄霸道：“你能作《无向辽东浪死歌》，应当是识字的。”
　　李玄霸从怀里掏出诗册：“看看。如果看得上，就将这些诗歌传诵出去。”
　　“诗歌？”王薄一头雾水。怎么一会儿说什么命运未来，一会儿又谈什么识字诗歌？
　　魏徵好奇地看着自己刚认的主家。李三郎君对谁都是这么一副神神叨叨难以捉摸的模样吗？
　　虽然谜语人总会让人窝火地想要狠揍一顿，但谜语人又最能勾起对方的好奇心。
　　王薄把诗册放在膝盖上一手酒碗，一手翻书，借着篝火看了起来。
　　有落款为李白的诗人作《丁督护歌》，怜“水浊不可饮，壶浆半成土”“君看石芒砀，掩泪悲千古”。
　　有落款为白居易的诗人作《卖炭翁》，叹“可怜身上衣正单，心忧炭贱愿天寒”“一车炭，千余斤，宫使驱将惜不得”。
　　有落款为杜甫的诗人作《石壕吏》，悲“一男附书至，二男新战死”“老妪力虽衰，请从吏夜归”。
　　更有那落款为屈大均的诗人作《菜人哀》，“夫妇年饥同饿死，不如妾向菜人市”！
　　王薄诗未看完，酒碗落地，目眦欲裂，喉咙中发出仿佛受伤困兽般的嘶吼呜咽。
　　魏徵愕然地看向王薄，不知王薄读到了什么，竟不复镇定，涕泗横流？
