**Chapter 95: The "Knower of the World" Reads Poetry**

The young Daoist was startled by Li Xuanba’s counter-question. He stammered, "W-Wei Zheng, courtesy name Xuan Cheng."

Li Xuanba took a sip of warm water to steady his nerves.

He feigned composure. "Native place?"

The young Wei Zheng replied, "Jululu, Quyang..."

Li Xuanba took another sip of warm water to steady his nerves.

*That’s it. No need to say more. It’s him.*

*Why on earth am I meeting Wei Zheng at the foot of Mount Tai?!*

Li Xuanba took the book of poems handed to him by Chen Tieniu, his hand stiff as he turned the pages.

The calligraphy in the book Wei Zheng presented was neat and rigorous, bearing a striking resemblance to the Yan-style regular script created by Yan Zhenqing in later generations.

Li Xuanba looked up at the elegant, long-bearded young Daoist, then back down at the precise, disciplined script in the book.

*They really don't match.*

Like most poetry collections used by scholars of the era to seek patronage, the front page listed the author’s native place, family background, and mentors.

For scholars from humble backgrounds, writing this front page was agonizing; they could rack their brains and still fail to fill half a page.

Due to the lingering influence of the Wei and Jin dynasties, the Sui people placed great importance on family lineage. The front page almost entirely determined whether one could be recommended. Looking at this book, the paper on the front page was much more wrinkled than the following pages, a testament to how many doors had been slammed in Wei Zheng’s face.

Li Xuanba gave the introduction a cursory glance before flipping to the next page, beginning to appraise the poems from Wei Zheng’s youth—works that had never been recorded in historical texts.

Seeing Li Xuanba turn past the front page, Wei Zheng slowly unclenched his fists, his eyes reddening.

How long had it been since he last saw someone turn to the second page of his collection?

The frayed edges of the book were the result of him flipping through his own poems, time and again, in a mix of sorrow and frustration after being rejected.

Although few of Wei Zheng’s literary works survived to later ages, the few that remained revealed his talent, possessing the refined yet substantial spirit characteristic of the early Tang Dynasty.

Li Xuanba thought of his own Second Brother.

Initially, he had assumed his Second Brother lacked poetic talent. Only after watching him study poetry for a few years did he realize that wasn't the case; his brother simply favored the ornate, luxurious, and parallel-prose style. He was particularly fond of writing "Palace-style" poetry—all flash and no substance—which, in later generations, would be akin to the melodramatic, flowery prose of a teenager wallowing in angst.

His Second Brother’s poems that spoke directly from the heart were quite good, but he simply refused to write that way.

Hearing Li Xuanba sigh, Wei Zheng’s heart, which had just settled, jumped back into his throat. He asked anxiously, "I-is there something amiss with my poetry?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "Nothing amiss. It’s just that seeing your balance of form and substance reminded me of my Second Brother. When he speaks from the heart, lines like 'Once I left on a single horse, now I return driving ten thousand chariots' are incredibly heroic. Yet, he insists on writing 'Hidden in the state of a thousand miles, suppressing layers of sorrow'—all that aimless, sickly moaning. If he would only focus on cultivating that heroic style, he would be a literary giant of this age."

The more Li Xuanba spoke, the more annoyed he became.

His Second Brother clearly possessed a poetic talent he himself lacked, yet he refused to polish it. If he had spent the energy he wasted on those Palace-style poems on direct, heartfelt expression, the Tang Dynasty might have produced a grand, bold poet of the frontier style much earlier.

But he wouldn't. He just wouldn't.

He would pile up flowery descriptions of flowers, snow, clouds, and rain for an entire poem, only to express a bit of petty sorrow or resentment at the very end. Every time Li Shimin wrote a "good poem" and forced Li Xuanba to critique it, Li Xuanba felt like vomiting!

The more he thought about it, the angrier he got, muttering to himself as he continued to read Wei Zheng’s work.

Wei Zheng looked thoughtful.

After finishing the book, Li Xuanba placed it on the table. "The poems are excellent. If you don't mind, would you care to accompany me for a few days? Once I reach Qinghe, I will recommend you to my Second Brother."

Wei Zheng said hurriedly, "I am willing to serve as a clerk under the Third Young Master!"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "Your aura is like a blade; I cannot suppress it. Go obediently under my Second Brother’s command; only he can keep you in check."

Wei Zheng was surprised. "The Third Young Master knows physiognomy?"

Li Xuanba said, "A little, not much. Your face is just too prominent."

Wei Zheng asked curiously, "What do you see in my face, Third Young Master?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Whoever you follow dies; whoever you recommend rebels."

Wei Zheng: "..." Blood rushed to his head, and his vision went black.

Chen Tieniu turned to his master in disbelief. "Young Master! Then why are you keeping him?!"

Li Xuanba chuckled. "He clashes with other masters, but he and my Second Brother will complement each other and create a legendary partnership. However, Wei Xuan Cheng, you should have spent another dozen years wandering before meeting my brother. To think you’ve handed me your petition so early. Would you like to try your luck elsewhere first? Perhaps those dozen years of displacement are exactly what would have forged your talent?"

Wei Zheng’s face turned beet red, and he stammered for a long time, unable to speak. Could he choose *not* to believe in this physiognomy?!

Chen Tieniu whispered, "Young Master, you’ve already said he clashes with his masters—does he still dare to defect to someone else?"

Li Xuanba joked, "There are only three of us in this room. I won't say it, you won't say it, and he won't say it. Surely Wudi isn't going to go around gossiping?"

Wudi tilted its head from side to side. "Chirp, chirp!"

Wei Zheng bowed tremblingly. "Third Young Master, please, stop scaring me."

Seeing the young Wei Zheng so terrified, Li Xuanba couldn't help but laugh out loud. "Hahaha, alright, alright, I won't scare you. Since you’ve come to me, I won't make you suffer through those extra dozen years. Follow me as a clerk for a while; let me see what you’re capable of with your strategies."

Chen Tieniu tried to persuade him, "Young Master, didn't you say he clashes with his masters! It’s not appropriate for him to follow you!" He believed everything his master said; if the master said Wei Zheng clashed with masters, then he definitely did!

Li Xuanba smiled. "With my Second Brother around, he can't clash with me." *My own life is already so fragile, how much more could he possibly clash with it?*

Li Xuanba ordered, "Have the village head arrange for him to have a clerk’s uniform made, and give him half the salary of the others. This is a great talent; do not treat him poorly."

Chen Tieniu replied, "Yes."

Li Xuanba said to Wei Zheng, "Although I know you are a great talent, you have yet to prove it, so you must start from the lowest clerk position to gain experience. I hope you aren't angry."

Wei Zheng bowed hurriedly. "How could I be! I am overwhelmed by your favor!"

Li Xuanba said, "Go wash up and tidy yourself first. Remember to shave that long beard. In the future, you will be a young talent by my and my Second Brother’s side; don't make yourself look so old-fashioned."

Wei Zheng touched his long beard and smiled bitterly. "Yes, Young Master."

After bowing repeatedly in gratitude, he followed Tieniu away, feeling quite dizzy.

Wudi landed on Li Xuanba’s lap, stretched its legs, and settled into his arms.

Li Xuanba hugged the pouting Wudi. "Are you curious about him?"

Wudi: "Chirp, chirp!"

Li Xuanba laughed. "If I told you, would you understand?"

Wudi flapped its wings. "Chirp, chirp, chirp!" *Even if I don't understand, I want to hear it!*

Li Xuanba stroked Wudi’s wings, as if truly explaining Wei Zheng to the bird, or perhaps just talking to himself.

Wei Zheng, courtesy name Xuan Cheng, would become Tang Taizong’s "Bronze Mirror," a famous, upright, and outspoken official.

His grandfather, Wei Yan, had served as the Inspector of Guangzhou during the Northern Wei; his father, Wei Changxian, was originally an imperial historian for Northern Qi, but because he criticized the politics of the time, he was demoted to the Magistrate of Tunliu in Shangdang, dying when Wei Zheng was only in his teens. Wei Zheng was orphaned and poor in his youth, and claiming to have great ambitions but no means of production, he fell into the life of a Daoist.

In terms of "background," Wei Zheng was a standard scholar from a humble family.

Even humble families had their hereditary "classics." The Wei family passed down the study of history, and their outstanding members all aspired to compile historical records. For instance, his clan uncle Wei Shou, who was several decades his senior, was a famous historian who authored the *Book of Wei*, refusing to compromise even when contemporaries labeled it a "filthy history."

Wei Changxian’s ambition was to compile the *Book of Jin*. He had almost achieved it, but because he criticized the government, he was demoted and missed his chance, dying prematurely in sorrow.

"Although Wei Zheng didn't get to edit the *Book of Jin*, he did lead the compilation of the *Book of Sui*, which counts as fulfilling his father’s dying wish." Li Xuanba smoothed Wudi’s feathers, sighing at the coincidence of meeting Wei Zheng so early.

While reading Wei Zheng’s collection, he had gone over Wei Zheng’s life in detail and discovered that his current wandering in the Qi and Lu regions actually left traces in the historical records.

For the first half of his life, Wei Zheng was frustrated and unsuccessful. Seeing the world in chaos, he leaned toward the school of strategy and was constantly looking for a power to join.

The first time Wei Zheng’s "official position" was recorded in history was in the thirteenth year of Daye, serving under the command of Yuan Baozang, the Assistant Magistrate of Wuyang Commandery.

Wuyang Commandery was adjacent to Jibei Commandery, and Mount Tai was located within Jibei.

Wei Zheng’s native place was Jululu Commandery, yet his first official post was in Wuyang.

Normally, a scholar of his humble background would have no chance to become an official, but during the suppression of civil uprisings, officials at all levels would recruit staff from humble origins.

Clearly, Wei Zheng had first gone to the Qi and Lu regions, where the peasant uprisings were most numerous, to seek an opportunity.

He hadn't expected that it was only the seventh year of Daye, just as the peasant uprisings were beginning, and Wei Zheng was already wandering around the Qi and Lu regions.

Li Xuanba calculated Wei Zheng’s age—he was currently thirty-one.

To be thirty-one, poor, and unsuccessful—no wonder Wei Zheng would risk coming to the Qi and Lu regions.

Thinking of how Wei Zheng had hit walls for six years in the Qi and Lu regions before finally being hired by Yuan Baozang, Li Xuanba felt a bit of admiration for his resilience.

If it were anyone else, their mentality would have collapsed long ago. Wei Zheng truly believed in his own talent, which was why he refused to compromise no matter how he was ground down.

"As for Wei Zheng ‘clashing with his masters,’ that was just me suppressing him, so that he, still arrogant and proud, wouldn't run off just because my Second Brother is young," Li Xuanba chuckled. "Actually, when he followed Li Mi to submit to the Tang, he was already a Tang official. Serving under Dou Jiande was only because he was captured after a defeat, so it doesn't count as him recognizing Dou Jiande as his master. He was just unlucky enough to be tied to Li Jiancheng."

But at the time, being highly favored and trusted by the Crown Prince, who would have called him unlucky?

Just like when Wei Zheng recommended Hou Junji and Du Zhenglun for their prime ministerial talent—who could have imagined that these two would be involved in Li Chengqian’s rebellion?

Wei Zheng was simply, purely unlucky.

However, he met Tang Taizong Li Shimin, and all his bad luck turned into good fortune. No matter how angry Li Shimin got, he only pushed over his monument of merit and broke off their marriage alliance, only to quietly restore the monument later.

If it were an ordinary emperor, the people he recommended being involved in treason would have resulted in his own execution and the ruin of his family.

"I never would have thought," Li Xuanba laughed, rubbing Wudi’s head with both hands, "that you and Han Gou are in danger!"

Wudi: "Chirp, chirp, chirp?" It only understood the last sentence. *What’s going on? Why are we in danger?*

Li Xuanba laughed heartily.

...

After a small interlude Li Xuanba hadn't anticipated, that night, the village head came to visit him, respectfully saying, "The 'Knower of the World' is here to see you."

Li Xuanba was forced to crawl out of bed in the middle of the night, downing two cups of honey water to raise his blood pressure and blood sugar.

He yawned and said, "Finally here?"

The village head prostrated himself. "The Knower of the World heard that the Third Young Master Li could treat a poor Daoist with such courtesy, and only then did he believe that the Third Young Master truly wished to meet him."

Li Xuanba smiled at Wei Zheng, who had shaved his beard and changed out of his Daoist robes. "It seems I owe this to you. Do you dare to listen in?"

Wei Zheng said humbly, "Third Young Master, I only clash with masters other than you and the Second Young Master, and can only stay under your commands. I dare to listen to anything."

Li Xuanba chuckled. "You certainly have guts. Then listen well and tell my Second Brother about today’s events. I’m too lazy to explain it myself."

*That’s right, this future upright, outspoken official is a "rebel" who will eventually join the Wagang Army.*

Wei Zheng said, "Yes."

He was extremely excited. A secret meeting with a rebel leader—this was a crime punishable by the execution of one's entire clan. He had only just arrived under the Young Master’s command, and the Young Master already trusted him this much?!

Chen Tieniu scratched his head. *Fine. The Young Master is always right; I’ll listen to the Young Master.*

He decided to keep a close eye on Wei Zheng. If Wei Zheng dared to run away and inform on them, he would chop Wei Zheng’s head off with one stroke.

Li Xuanba took his newly recruited staff member to meet Wang Bo. Wang Bo and the village head were also startled, and they couldn't help but admire Li Xuanba even more.

The village head lit a bonfire in an open-air pavilion.

When Li Xuanba walked into the pavilion wearing a heavy cloak, a middle-aged man in a cape was already drinking by the fire.

"The 'Righteousness Reaching the Clouds' Second Young Master Li, and the 'Virtuous and Benevolent' Third Young Master Li—I am Wang Bo, I have long admired you." The middle-aged man took off his cape and bowed to Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba was full of question marks. *Is this filming 'Romance of the Sui and Tang'? Why are they giving me and my Second Brother nicknames?*

The future historian Wei Zheng’s eyes flashed, and he committed these two "nicknames" to memory.

"I don't know when my Second Brother and I acquired such resounding nicknames; this is the first I’ve heard of them." Li Xuanba gestured for him to sit, as if he were the host. "For the 'Knower of the World' to come alone to this meeting, you truly have great courage."

Wang Bo smiled bitterly. "Isn't the one who came alone to this meeting Third Young Master Li?"

Li Xuanba sat on the stone stool that had been warmed by the bonfire and loosened the collar of his cloak. "This Great Sui is still His Majesty’s Great Sui. As a Tiger-Tooth Commander under His Majesty, I am never alone wherever I go."

Wang Bo’s expression darkened. "Is Third Young Master here to offer me amnesty?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "His Majesty has ordered: 'Commanders and Eagle-Yang officials are to pursue and capture in coordination with the commanderies and counties, and execute them upon capture.'"

Wang Bo cursed, "That dog-thief Emperor!"

Li Xuanba picked up a wine bowl, poured one for himself and one for Wang Bo, and handed one to him.

Wang Bo took the bowl. "Then why did Third Young Master come here specifically?"

Li Xuanba smiled. "To meet a future colleague. Knower of the World, do you believe in fate?"

Wang Bo said in a deep voice, "Are you saying that it is my fate to eventually submit to that dog-thief Emperor? Impossible! He caused my entire family to starve to death; I only want to cut off that dog’s head with my own hands!"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "Of course you couldn't possibly submit to His Majesty. Let’s change the subject then. Knower of the World, have you ever thought about the future after you raise your army?"

Wang Bo looked straight into Li Xuanba’s indifferent eyes. "No."

Li Xuanba said, "You are certainly frank."

Wang Bo said, "I just don't want to die. Everyone who followed me up the mountain only thinks about not dying today. So, Third Young Master, what future are you talking about?"

Li Xuanba changed the subject again.

He asked, "Are you literate?"

Wang Bo frowned. "I know a little."

Li Xuanba said, "You can write the 'Song of Not Dying in Vain in Liaodong,' so you must be literate."

Li Xuanba took a book of poems from his robes. "Take a look. If you like them, spread these poems."

"Poems?" Wang Bo was confused. *Why is he talking about fate and the future one moment, and literacy and poetry the next?*

Wei Zheng looked curiously at the master he had just recognized. *Is Third Young Master always this cryptic and unfathomable to everyone?*

Although riddlers always made people want to beat them up, they were also the best at piquing one's curiosity.

Wang Bo placed the book on his lap, holding his wine bowl in one hand and flipping through the pages with the other, reading by the light of the bonfire.

There was a poem titled "Ding Du Hu Song" by a poet named Li Bai, lamenting, "The water is too murky to drink, the pot of gruel half-turned to mud," and "You see the Mangdang rocks, hiding tears for a thousand years of sorrow."

There was "The Charcoal Seller" by a poet named Bai Juyi, sighing, "Pity the clothes on his back are thin, he worries the charcoal is cheap and prays for cold weather," and "A cart of charcoal, over a thousand catties, the palace envoy drives it away, he cannot bear to part with it."

There was "The Official of Shishao" by a poet named Du Fu, grieving, "One son sent a letter, two sons newly dead in battle," and "Though the old woman’s strength is failing, she begs to follow the official into the night."

And there was even "Lament for the Vegetable People" by a poet named Qu Dajun: "Husband and wife starve to death together in the famine year, better for the concubine to go to the vegetable market!"

Before Wang Bo could finish the poems, his wine bowl fell to the ground. His eyes were bloodshot, and a roar like a wounded, trapped beast escaped his throat.

Wei Zheng looked at Wang Bo in astonishment, wondering what he had read that caused him to lose his composure and weep so bitterly.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第96章 魏徵不想当谏臣
chunks.chineseText:
第96章 魏徵不想当谏臣

=
　　一个胆敢举起反旗的汉子， 竟然因看了几首诗情绪完全崩溃。
　　李玄霸捧着冰凉的酒碗喝了一口。
　　酒淡如水，带着醪糟的酸味。
　　这让李玄霸想起离开家乡的第一顿生日餐。
　　离开家乡后，他先在工地上做了一段时间包三餐的日结的活， 一边攒钱一边找更合适的工作。
　　工地食堂的阿姨听说他过生日， 给他煮了醪糟荷包蛋， 说过生日吃醪糟荷包蛋是她那里的习俗。
　　那时他过得很惨，但在智力健全身体健康的前提下，只要肯干活， 他就不会饿死。
　　自己居无定所举目无亲背着巨债，可以算是社会底层了。《菜人哀》这首诗，却连自己看了都会心生震撼。
　　李玄霸又喝了一口浊酒， 抿了抿嘴中的酸苦味。
　　真难喝。
　　当王薄发泄情绪时，李玄霸一直安静地等着。
　　王薄终于平静下来时， 李玄霸让陈铁牛把酒坛子递给了王薄。
　　王薄举着酒坛子， 咕噜咕噜将酒液一饮而尽。
　　他用袖子抹了抹脸，问道：“这是三郎君写的诗吗？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“不是我，也不是这个世上的任何人。”
　　王薄了然，他讥笑道：“诗人的名字都是假的？也是，如果谁敢写这种诗， 肯定会被狗皇帝灭满门。”
　　李玄霸道：“你知道就好。”
　　王薄略微惊讶。他没想到李玄霸居然会如此干脆地承认。
　　李三郎君不是最受狗皇帝宠爱的后辈吗？
　　王薄低头看着手中的诗册，不敢再读下去。
　　他将诗册放怀里揣好， 问道：“三郎君为何要我宣扬这些诗？”
　　魏徵借着黑暗白了王薄一眼。
　　一边询问，一边把诗册往怀里揣，你也太虚伪了。
　　他真的很好奇， 三郎君给王薄的诗册上写了什么。
　　李玄霸平和道：“诗你看过了。有许多士人哀民生多艰， 这些诗若留在文人压箱底的诗册里， 不过是无意义的感慨。顶多让后世人读到这些诗后， 为遭受苦难的先人掉几滴同情的眼泪，感恩他们美好的生活。”
　　夜风袭来，李玄霸咳了几声。
　　站岗的乌镝赶紧冲进李玄霸怀里，比陈铁牛递暖炉的速度还快。
　　李玄霸将手放在乌镝暖烘烘的翅膀下，继续道：“在你手中就不一样了。他们的悲怜，会成为你们手中锐利的刀。”
　　王薄将手贴在诗册上：“三郎君为何要帮我？你是想天下早些大乱，好逐鹿天下吗？”
　　李玄霸轻笑一声，道：“现在的天下还不够乱吗？”
　　王薄对李玄霸道：“对达官贵人而言，不乱。”
　　“那就是已经天下大乱了。”李玄霸让陈铁牛把早已经准备好的箱子抬上来，“你们因活不下去而揭竿而起，但揭竿而起之后却成为比官兵更残忍的盗贼。自己淋了雨，却去撕了别人的蓑衣。这样的揭竿而起，我看不下去。我来教你，什么才是真正的揭竿而起。”
　　魏徵惊恐道：“郎君，你……”
　　李玄霸打断道：“魏玄成，我知道我在做什么。我的时间有限，只教你这一晚。知世郎，若你想听就留下，不想听就离开。听完之后不愿意照做也没关系。”
　　王薄被李玄霸的反常吓住了，他问道：“李三郎君就不怕我告密？”
　　李玄霸失笑：“谁会听你告密？”
　　王薄呼吸一滞。
　　他握紧拳头：“没有人会听我们说话。”
　　李玄霸道：“是的。所以我不怕你告密。而且，我相信知世郎的品行。你为何要向你口中的狗皇帝和贪官污吏，告发一个帮助你的好人？”
　　王薄深吸一口气，跪下道：“请三郎君教我！”
　　他知道自己的机会来了！一个比当民贼更大的机会来了！
　　此刻王薄胸口悄然生出了野心。
　　李玄霸没有让王薄起身。他让魏徵帮忙把篝火烧亮了些，拿起箱子里的书籍一一讲解起来。
　　“虽然你们是为了活命而不得不走造反这条路，但要长久地走下去，你们得思考未来。”
　　“整合一个队伍，需要思想和利益双管齐下。”
　　“曾经黄巾起义为何能迅速席卷大汉？”
　　李玄霸从历史中各种农民起义说起。这些农民起义大多失败了，但根据掀起风波大小，也可以得到许多经验。
　　他又提起百姓的基本诉求，以及这些诉求和为了壮大队伍的实际利益的冲突。
　　不服役、不纳粮，人人有田耕。百姓的梦想就这么朴素。
　　但这朴素的梦想，在这个时代却不可能实现。
　　王薄眼睛一会儿明亮，一会儿黯淡，好像是跟着篝火闪烁。
　　李玄霸将闯王和太平天国的事迹改到先秦，将这些失败的事例剖析给王薄听。
　　夜色更凉了。
　　李玄霸又咳了几声。陈铁牛抱来被子给李玄霸裹了一圈，把乌镝也裹了进去，又在被子里塞了好几个小暖炉。
　　李玄霸简略讲完他想教授的内容时，鸡鸣已经响起。
　　王薄跪坐在地上的双腿已经没了知觉。
　　他悲哀道：“就算按照三郎君教授的去做，我也不可能成功吗？”
　　李玄霸淡漠道：“嗯，不可能成功。”
　　王薄痛苦道：“王侯将相宁有种乎？”
　　李玄霸道：“对个人而言，没有。一个出身卑微的人可以成为王侯将相，王侯将相的后人也可能沦为平民甚至奴仆。但就整个阶层而言，是的。你可以加入他们，但不可能带着你手下的人都加入他们。你识得多少字？你手下的人识得多少字？就算你们的势力再怎么扩大，管理百姓的权力仍旧会交到士族手中。”
　　王薄哭着问道：“那我现在所做的有何意义？”
　　李玄霸道：“有。把天下大乱之势波及那些冷眼旁观的士族，让他们看到百姓被逼急了会燃起多大的火。你们不会成功，但可以令他们畏惧。在下一个王朝来临时，百姓的日子就会好过许多。”
　　李玄霸有些困了。他捏了一下手背，压下自己的困意。
　　“古贤人有言，‘君者，舟也；庶人者，水也。水则载舟，水则覆舟’。只读圣贤书，这句话进不了他们的心中。只有让他们真切地体会到你们的力量，他们才会知道这句话的真意。”李玄霸道，“你问我目的，这就是我的目的了。”
　　王薄抬起头，看向李玄霸的眼神带着绝望的空洞感。
　　他原本心中有野心。但听完李玄霸所有教授内容后，他的野心却变成了浓厚的绝望。
　　李玄霸让陈铁牛把裹着他的被子解开。
　　活动了一下手脚后，他把王薄扶起来。
　　“如果你继续当民贼，等大隋覆灭后，你可能会有被其他势力覆灭的一日。”李玄霸道，“如果你按照我的教导做，你可能会提前让大隋覆灭，可能有更高的声望，可能会青史留名。但你的处境会很危险，几乎所有势力都会想杀你。”
　　王薄低头道：“李三郎君将来也会想杀我？”
　　李玄霸道：“我和二哥还太年少。你不一定等得到我和二哥掌权的那一日。”
　　王薄抬起头，看着李玄霸的双眼。
　　他年纪比李玄霸大很多岁，但李玄霸生活比他富裕多了。虽然李玄霸比李世民矮半个脑袋，但比起普通人身姿挺拔太多，所以现在的李玄霸已经和王薄差不多高。
　　王薄想，若不是李三郎君的面容过于稚气，李三郎君已经颇具雄主之相。
　　不，李三郎君这样的作为，不像是雄主，倒像是雄主身后的谋士，是他曾经听过的话本故事中那些神奇的贤臣名相。
　　雄主身边，必有圣贤相助。
　　谁是雄主，谁又是圣贤？
　　王薄将眼中所有绝望的希望的情绪都收敛到眼底，让双眼恢复古井无波的模样：“我这么做能提前灭了大隋？”
　　李玄霸道：“能。”
　　王薄嘴角咧开，露出一个不像是人类，很像是被逼急了的野兽的古怪笑容：“那就干。”
　　李玄霸看着王薄的笑容，听着王薄话语中的坚定语气，心头不由一悸。
　　王薄对隋炀帝的恨，或许已经超越了一切。
　　李玄霸道：“还有一个箱子，里面装的是技艺书籍，记载了农耕技术和工具的改良，治水挖渠建造水车，鸡鸭鱼饲养等技术。不要老想着抢夺，等有了地有了人，还要想着怎么经营。送你九个字，或许能让你活到我和二哥成长到能护住你的那一日。”
　　李玄霸摸了摸肩膀上打瞌睡的雕脑袋，缓缓道：“高筑墙、广积粮、缓称王。”
　　王薄再次跪下磕头：“是，先生！”
　　李玄霸转身离开，王薄一直跪在地上，目送李玄霸离去。
　　李玄霸没有停留，虽然他很困，也立刻与护卫离开了泰山脚下，启程回清河郡。
　　赶路大半日，到达一个较为繁荣的县城时，李玄霸才入城好好睡了一日，补足昨日消耗的精神。
　　他起床时正好是第三日的清晨。洗漱完毕后，李玄霸让护卫买了肉菜调料，自己亲手用胡椒和花椒味调了的锅底，吃了一顿热腾腾的火锅，出了一身汗，身体舒服许多。
　　魏徵第一次见识李玄霸的手艺，本来想矜持一点，还是没忍住多吃了许多。
　　吃饱喝足之后，李玄霸又去床榻上躺着养神，等休息到正午才出发。
　　魏徵坐在床边，欲言又止。
　　李玄霸打着哈欠道：“想说什么就直说。”
　　魏徵问道：“郎君为何要冒险和王薄接触？”
　　李玄霸道：“不冒险。王薄既不敢杀我，也不会告密。就算他手下有人想告密，他们有那个本事让杨广相信，唯一能在剿贼中连战连胜的我和二哥，会和民贼勾连？”
　　李玄霸把在他肚子上打滚的重得要死的乌镝推到一旁：“理由呢？利益呢？我是疯了才会和民贼接触。”
　　魏徵继续问道：“所以理由呢？利益呢？郎君你是疯了吗？”
　　乌镝一跃而起：“啾啾啾啾！”
　　魏徵疑惑：“这只鸟在叫什么？”
　　李玄霸道：“乌镝以为你骂我，所以它在骂你。”
　　魏徵仔细打量乌镝，乌镝继续“啾啾啾”。
　　魏徵打量了一会儿，轻笑道：“护主的好雕。”
　　乌镝仰头：“啾！”
　　李玄霸道：“好了，别烦我。无聊就出去飞一圈，正午前回来。你刚问我理由和利益？我不是和王薄说了我的理由和想获得的利益吗？王薄按照我所说的去做，大隋就会提前崩塌；百姓在天下大乱中会少遭遇些惨事；新王朝建立后达官贵人会稍稍在意一点百姓的命。”
　　魏徵道：“郎君难道是忧国忧民的圣人？”
　　李玄霸叹气：“魏玄成，你好端端的一句话怎么说得和讽刺似的？我当然不是圣人，只是在为下一个王朝铺路。但我不可以是圣人吗？忧国忧民不好吗？”
　　魏徵沉默了许久，道：“很好。”
　　李玄霸道：“你在犹豫什么？难道是后悔跟随我了？”
　　魏徵摇头。
　　他道：“郎君，我熟背史书，历史中绝无闯王和太平天国。”
　　李玄霸道：“那可能是我记混了。”
　　魏徵又沉默了一会儿，双手在袖口中握得更紧。
　　李玄霸无奈：“你有什么话能不能直说？别吞吞吐吐，我脾气好，你说什么我都不会生气。”
　　他猜测魏徵大概是想劝诫吧。他又不是坚持说到做到的傻子二哥，只需要说“好好好，是是是，啊对对对”应付过去就行了。
　　魏徵问道：“郎君，我曾听闻古时有贤人能看到未来。”
　　李玄霸道：“我只是会一点相面。你想问你的未来？”
　　魏徵叹气：“郎君对我如此亲切，如果郎君能看到我的未来，我未来一定和郎君相处不错。”
　　“你和我没关系。你和二哥相处不错。”李玄霸道，“你是担心你将来在二哥身边的位置？放心，你是出了名的谏臣，青史留名的那种。”
　　魏徵却苦笑：“只是谏臣吗？”
　　李玄霸疑惑：“怎么？你难道还能瞧不起谏臣？”
　　魏徵摇头：“谏臣自然值得尊敬。只是如果我的成就只有谏臣，岂不是我这一身本事都没有施展过？”
　　李玄霸本想问“能经常提出有用的谏言，这本事还不够大吗”，但看着魏徵苦涩的神情，李玄霸突然想到了一件事。
　　史书中记载，魏徵似乎钻研的是纵横术。
　　所谓纵横术，就是囊括了军策和内政在内的战略学问。魏徵的纵横术本事，在史书中记载过三次，一次是说魏徵关于瓦岗寨壮大的计策都不被采纳，一次是劝降徐世勣，还有一次是出计帮助李建成以攻心和分化的方式扫灭刘黑闼残党。
　　从后两次记载来看，魏徵说自己擅长纵横术并非虚谈。
　　李玄霸道：“纵横术在王朝稳定时，就是出将入相。魏玄成啊，二哥身边能出将入相的人太多了。”
　　魏徵道：“若争不过，我自会认输。可郎君从相面中看到的那个未来，我没有机会与他们相争，对吗？”
　　李玄霸坐直身体：“你们这些人啊，鬼精鬼精的，我起个头，你们就能把事情全给我猜出来。罢了，我也没想瞒住你。你是个很重身后名的人，既然你知道未来的胜利者是我二哥，就不会背叛我们。”
　　魏徵面色古怪：“只是利益吗？郎君似乎不太信任我的品性。”
　　李玄霸失笑：“信，我信。说吧，你想做什么。等做不到了，再回来当谏臣。”
　　魏徵正色道：“我出将入相，也可以当谏臣。我只是不想只当一个谏臣。”
　　李玄霸摆摆手：“行吧。你既然是现在来找我，是和王薄的事有关？”
　　魏徵神色一松，他心头又是一股暖流涌出。
　　自父亲去世后，魏徵活了三十一年，还是第一次有人如此纵容他。
　　郎君明明才与自己相见，仅凭“相面”就相信自己？魏徵不由生出不服气的心思。
　　未来那个自己，听上去好像也不怎么样。自己明明能更厉害。
　　以谏臣闻名？那岂不是说除了进谏，自己没有其他事可做了？自己一身本事，怎么能沦落如此！
　　魏徵道：“是。我想去王薄身边。”
　　李玄霸按压着太阳穴道：“很危险。”
　　魏徵道：“立功哪有不危险？”
　　李玄霸叹气：“我说你以后以谏臣扬名后世，不是说你的工作只有进谏。你将成为参预朝政的重臣，修史断案什么事都做过。不要置气。”
　　魏徵坚持道：“我不是置气。我明明有更大的本事，就应当立下更大的功劳。进谏的事，我有了出将入相的功劳之后也能做。”
　　李玄霸头疼。
　　王薄身边那么危险，魏徵这一去，别在隋末直接牺牲了？魏徵这人怎么这么倔强？
　　李玄霸又劝了几句，魏徵却去意已决。
　　“王薄只是一个铁匠，郎君虽然教导他，但他不一定能贯彻郎君的计谋。我去辅佐他，一定能让他达成郎君的期望！”魏徵起身拱手道，“请郎君相信我！”
　　李玄霸骂道：“我不是不相信你，我是担心你的安危！”
　　魏徵忍不住笑了起来：“郎君和我未来的明主李二郎君，难道在争霸天下时不会遇到危险？二郎君现在还亲自带兵奋战吧？郎君，我一定能自保。”
　　李玄霸抱头：“天啦，真是服了你。二哥还没开始为你头疼，怎么我先为你头疼了？行行行，去吧去吧，如果你死了，我让二哥给你追封。”
　　魏徵笑道：“那就拜托郎君了。”
　　李玄霸无力道：“真不先看看你未来的君王再离去？”
　　魏徵道：“未来总会见面的，不用急于一时。王薄现在正为郎君的教导心神恍惚，我才好博得他的信任。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“行，去吧。保重。我现在手中的兵不能给你，我会安排人扮作流民去投奔你，给你凑个几百人护卫。”
　　魏徵眼眶微红，跪地叩首道：“谢郎君！我绝不辜负郎君所望！”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 96: Wei Zheng Does Not Want to Be a Remonstrator

A man who dared to raise the banner of rebellion had completely broken down emotionally after reading a few poems.

Li Xuanba held a cold bowl of wine and took a sip. The wine was as thin as water, carrying the sour tang of fermented rice mash. It reminded him of the first birthday meal he had after leaving his hometown.

After leaving home, he had worked for a time on a construction site, taking day-labor jobs that provided three meals a day while he saved money and searched for more suitable work. The auntie in the site cafeteria, hearing it was his birthday, had boiled him some poached eggs in fermented rice mash, saying that eating such a dish on one's birthday was a custom from her hometown.

He had lived a miserable life back then, but as long as he was of sound mind and body, and willing to work, he would not starve. He had been homeless, friendless, and burdened with massive debt—truly at the bottom of society. Yet, even he felt a profound shock when reading the poem "Lament of the Cannibal."

Li Xuanba took another sip of the cloudy wine, smacking his lips against the sour bitterness. It tasted truly awful.

While Wang Bo vented his emotions, Li Xuanba waited quietly. When Wang Bo finally calmed down, Li Xuanba had Chen Tieniu pass the wine jar to him. Wang Bo hoisted the jar and gulped the liquid down in one go. He wiped his face with his sleeve and asked, "Was this poem written by you, Third Young Master?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "Not me, nor anyone else in this world."

Wang Bo understood. He sneered, "The poet's name is fake? Well, that makes sense. If anyone dared to write such a poem, the dog emperor would surely exterminate their entire clan."

Li Xuanba said, "It is good that you know."

Wang Bo was slightly surprised. He had not expected Li Xuanba to admit it so readily. Was the Third Young Master not the junior most favored by that dog emperor?

Wang Bo looked down at the book of poems in his hands, not daring to read any further. He tucked the book into his robes and asked, "Why does the Third Young Master want me to spread these poems?"

Wei Zheng cast a sidelong glance at Wang Bo through the darkness. *Asking questions while stuffing the book into your robes—you are truly a hypocrite.* He was genuinely curious about what was written in the book Li Xuanba had given Wang Bo.

Li Xuanba said calmly, "You have read the poems. Many scholars lament the hardships of the people, but if these poems remain hidden in the private collections of literati, they are nothing more than meaningless sighs. At most, future generations will read them, shed a few tears of sympathy for their suffering ancestors, and then be grateful for their own comfortable lives."

A night breeze swept by, and Li Xuanba coughed a few times. Wudi, who had been on guard, rushed into Li Xuanba’s arms faster than Chen Tieniu could hand him a hand warmer. Li Xuanba placed his hands under Wudi’s warm wings and continued, "In your hands, it will be different. Their pity will become a sharp blade in your grasp."

Wang Bo pressed his hand against the book. "Why does the Third Young Master want to help me? Do you wish for the world to fall into chaos sooner so that you may contend for the throne?"

Li Xuanba chuckled softly. "Is the world not chaotic enough as it is?"

Wang Bo replied, "To the high officials and nobles, it is not."

"Then the world is already in total chaos." Li Xuanba had Chen Tieniu bring over a box he had prepared earlier. "You rose in rebellion because you could not survive, but after rising, you became thieves more cruel than the government troops. You have been drenched by the rain, yet you go and tear apart the straw capes of others. I cannot stand to see such a rebellion. Let me teach you what a true uprising is."

Wei Zheng said in horror, "Young Master, you..."

Li Xuanba interrupted, "Wei Xuan-cheng, I know what I am doing. My time is limited; I will only teach you this one night. Zhi-shi Lang, if you wish to listen, stay; if not, leave. Even after hearing it, you are under no obligation to follow my lead."

Wang Bo was startled by Li Xuanba’s unusual behavior. He asked, "Is the Third Young Master not afraid that I will inform on you?"

Li Xuanba laughed. "Who would listen to your report?"

Wang Bo’s breath hitched. He clenched his fists. "No one will listen to us."

Li Xuanba said, "Exactly. That is why I am not afraid of you informing. Furthermore, I believe in the character of Zhi-shi Lang. Why would you report a good man who has helped you to the very dog emperor and corrupt officials you despise?"

Wang Bo took a deep breath, knelt, and said, "Please, Third Young Master, teach me!"

He knew his opportunity had arrived! A chance far greater than merely being a rebel leader! At that moment, ambition quietly sprouted in Wang Bo’s chest.

Li Xuanba did not tell Wang Bo to stand. He had Wei Zheng help brighten the campfire, then picked up the books from the box and began to explain them one by one.

"Although you were forced onto the path of rebellion to survive, if you wish to walk this path for the long term, you must think of the future."

"To consolidate a team, you need both ideology and shared interests."

"Why was the Yellow Turban Rebellion able to sweep across the Great Han so rapidly?"

Li Xuanba began by discussing various peasant uprisings from history. Most of these had failed, but one could still glean many lessons from the scale of the turmoil they caused. He then brought up the basic demands of the common people and the conflicts between those demands and the practical interests of growing an army.

No forced labor, no grain taxes, and land for everyone to till—the dreams of the people were that simple. Yet, in this era, such simple dreams were impossible to realize.

Wang Bo’s eyes flickered between brightness and dimness, as if following the dancing flames of the fire. Li Xuanba adapted the deeds of the Chuang Wang and the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom to the pre-Qin era, dissecting these failed examples for Wang Bo.

The night grew colder. Li Xuanba coughed again. Chen Tieniu brought a quilt to wrap around him, tucked Wudi inside, and stuffed several small hand warmers into the bedding.

By the time Li Xuanba finished explaining the content he wanted to teach, the roosters had already begun to crow. Wang Bo’s legs, which had been kneeling on the ground, were numb.

He said sorrowfully, "Even if I do as the Third Young Master teaches, will I still not succeed?"

Li Xuanba said indifferently, "Correct, you will not succeed."

Wang Bo asked in agony, "Are kings and nobles born with high status?"

Li Xuanba replied, "For an individual, no. A person of humble birth can become a king or a general, and the descendants of kings and nobles can fall into poverty or slavery. But for the class as a whole, yes. You can join them, but you cannot bring all your followers with you. How many characters do you know? How many do your men know? No matter how much your power expands, the authority to govern the people will still fall into the hands of the aristocratic clans."

Wang Bo cried, "Then what is the point of what I am doing now?"

Li Xuanba said, "There is a point. To let the chaos of the world reach those aristocratic clans who watch from the sidelines, so they can see how great a fire the people will ignite when pushed to the brink. You will not succeed, but you can make them fear. When the next dynasty comes, the lives of the people will be much better."

Li Xuanba was growing sleepy. He pinched the back of his hand to suppress his drowsiness.

"The ancient sages said, 'The ruler is the boat, and the commoners are the water. The water can carry the boat, but it can also capsize it.' If they only read the books of sages, these words will never enter their hearts. Only when they truly experience your power will they understand the true meaning of this." Li Xuanba said, "You asked me for my purpose; this is my purpose."

Wang Bo looked up, his eyes filled with a sense of desperate emptiness. He had originally harbored ambition, but after hearing everything Li Xuanba taught, his ambition had turned into profound despair.

Li Xuanba had Chen Tieniu unwrap the quilt. After stretching his limbs, he helped Wang Bo to his feet.

"If you continue to be a mere rebel, after the Great Sui falls, you will likely be destroyed by other factions," Li Xuanba said. "If you follow my teachings, you might hasten the fall of the Great Sui, gain greater prestige, and perhaps leave your name in history. But your situation will be extremely dangerous; almost every faction will want you dead."

Wang Bo lowered his head. "Will the Third Young Master want to kill me in the future?"

Li Xuanba replied, "My second brother and I are still too young. You might not live to see the day when we hold power."

Wang Bo looked up into Li Xuanba’s eyes. He was many years older than Li Xuanba, but Li Xuanba had lived a much more affluent life. Although Li Xuanba was half a head shorter than Li Shimin, he stood much straighter than the average person, so he was now about the same height as Wang Bo.

Wang Bo thought that if not for the youthful look on his face, the Third Young Master already possessed the bearing of a great ruler. No, the way the Third Young Master acted was not like a ruler, but rather like the strategist behind one—like the miraculous, wise ministers from the storybooks he had heard.

A great ruler must have a sage to assist him. Who was the ruler, and who was the sage?

Wang Bo suppressed all the despair and hope in his eyes, returning them to a calm, stagnant pool. "Can I hasten the fall of the Great Sui by doing this?"

Li Xuanba said, "Yes."

Wang Bo’s lips curled into a strange smile, one that did not look human, but rather like a beast pushed to its limit. "Then let’s do it."

Watching Wang Bo’s smile and hearing the firmness in his tone, Li Xuanba felt a tremor in his heart. Wang Bo’s hatred for Emperor Yang of Sui had perhaps surpassed everything else.

Li Xuanba said, "There is another box containing books on technique. It records improvements in farming and tools, water management, canal digging, waterwheel construction, and the raising of poultry and fish. Do not just think about plundering. Once you have land and people, you must think about how to manage them. I will give you nine words, which may allow you to live until the day my second brother and I are strong enough to protect you."

Li Xuanba stroked the head of the eagle dozing on his shoulder and said slowly, "Build high walls, store grain widely, and delay claiming the throne."

Wang Bo knelt and kowtowed again. "Yes, Master!"

Li Xuanba turned and left. Wang Bo remained kneeling on the ground, watching him depart. Li Xuanba did not linger. Despite his exhaustion, he immediately left the foot of Mount Tai with his guards and set off for Qinghe Commandery.

After traveling for the better part of a day, they reached a relatively prosperous county town, where Li Xuanba finally checked into an inn to sleep for a full day and recover his lost energy.

He woke up on the morning of the third day. After washing up, he had his guards buy meat and seasonings. He personally prepared a hotpot base with peppercorns and Sichuan peppercorns, ate a steaming meal, and broke into a sweat, feeling much better.

It was the first time Wei Zheng had witnessed Li Xuanba’s culinary skills. He had intended to be reserved, but could not help but eat a great deal.

After eating his fill, Li Xuanba went back to bed to rest, not departing until noon. Wei Zheng sat by the bedside, wanting to speak but hesitating.

Li Xuanba yawned and said, "If you have something to say, just say it."

Wei Zheng asked, "Why did you take the risk of contacting Wang Bo, Young Master?"

Li Xuanba said, "It is not a risk. Wang Bo dares not kill me, nor will he inform. Even if someone under him wanted to inform, would they have the ability to make Yang Guang believe that my second brother and I—who have won consecutive victories in suppressing rebels—would collude with them?"

Li Xuanba pushed aside Wudi, who was rolling around on his stomach and felt heavy as lead. "What would be the motive? What would be the benefit? I would have to be insane to contact rebels."

Wei Zheng continued, "So, what is the motive? What is the benefit? Are you insane, Young Master?"

Wudi leaped up. "Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!"

Wei Zheng asked, puzzled, "What is this bird chirping about?"

Li Xuanba said, "Wudi thinks you are scolding me, so it is scolding you back."

Wei Zheng examined Wudi carefully, while Wudi continued to chirp. After a moment, Wei Zheng smiled lightly. "A loyal eagle."

Wudi tilted its head. "Chirp!"

Li Xuanba said, "Enough, don't bother me. If you're bored, go fly a circle and be back by noon. You asked me for my motive and benefit? I already told Wang Bo my reasons and the benefits I hope to gain. If Wang Bo follows my instructions, the Great Sui will collapse sooner; the people will suffer less during the chaos; and after the new dynasty is established, the officials will care a little more about the lives of the people."

Wei Zheng said, "Are you a sage who worries about the country and the people, Young Master?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Wei Xuan-cheng, why do you make such a sincere statement sound like sarcasm? Of course I am not a sage; I am merely paving the way for the next dynasty. But can I not be a sage? Is it bad to worry about the country and the people?"

Wei Zheng was silent for a long time before saying, "It is very good."

Li Xuanba said, "What are you hesitating about? Do you regret following me?"

Wei Zheng shook his head. "Young Master, I have memorized the history books, and there is no mention of a 'Chuang Wang' or a 'Taiping Heavenly Kingdom' in history."

Li Xuanba said, "Then perhaps I remembered it wrong."

Wei Zheng fell silent again, his hands gripping his sleeves tightly.

Li Xuanba said helplessly, "Can you just say what you have to say? Don't mumble. I have a good temper; I won't get angry at anything you say." He guessed that Wei Zheng probably wanted to offer some remonstrance. He wasn't like his stubborn second brother who insisted on doing everything he said; he could just respond with "Yes, yes, you're right, absolutely" to brush it off.

Wei Zheng asked, "Young Master, I have heard that there were sages in ancient times who could see the future."

Li Xuanba said, "I only know a little bit of physiognomy. Do you want to ask about your future?"

Wei Zheng sighed. "You are so kind to me, Young Master. If you can see my future, then I must have a good relationship with you in the future."

"You have nothing to do with me. You have a good relationship with my second brother," Li Xuanba said. "Are you worried about your position beside him in the future? Rest assured, you are a famous remonstrator, the kind whose name is recorded in history."

Wei Zheng gave a bitter smile. "Only a remonstrator?"

Li Xuanba was puzzled. "Why? Do you look down on remonstrators?"

Wei Zheng shook his head. "A remonstrator is naturally worthy of respect. But if my achievements are limited to that, does it not mean I have never truly put my talents to use?"

Li Xuanba had wanted to ask, *Is the ability to offer useful advice not great enough?* But seeing Wei Zheng’s bitter expression, he suddenly remembered something. History recorded that Wei Zheng had studied the "Art of Vertical and Horizontal Alliances" (Zongheng). This was a strategic discipline encompassing military tactics and internal governance. Wei Zheng’s skill in this had been recorded three times: once regarding a failed plan for the growth of Wagang寨, once for persuading Xu Shiji to surrender, and once for helping Li Jiancheng use psychological warfare and division to wipe out the remnants of Liu Heita.

Judging by the latter two, Wei Zheng’s claim to be skilled in this art was no empty boast.

Li Xuanba said, "When a dynasty is stable, the Art of Zongheng is used to become a general or a prime minister. Wei Xuan-cheng, there are already too many people around my second brother who can serve as generals and ministers."

Wei Zheng said, "If I cannot compete, I will admit defeat. But in the future you saw through physiognomy, I have no chance to compete with them, right?"

Li Xuanba sat up straight. "You people are so sharp. I just start a sentence, and you guess the whole thing. Very well, I didn't intend to hide it from you. You are a man who cares deeply about his posthumous reputation. Since you know the future victor is my second brother, you will not betray us."

Wei Zheng’s expression was strange. "Only because of interests? You don't seem to trust my character, Young Master."

Li Xuanba laughed. "I trust you. Tell me, what do you want to do? When you can't achieve it, you can come back and be a remonstrator."

Wei Zheng said solemnly, "I can serve as a general and a minister, and also be a remonstrator. I just don't want to be *only* a remonstrator."

Li Xuanba waved his hand. "Fine. Since you came to me now, is this about Wang Bo?"

Wei Zheng’s expression relaxed, and a warm current flowed through his heart. Since his father passed away, Wei Zheng had lived for thirty-one years, and this was the first time someone had been so indulgent toward him.

The Young Master had only just met him, yet he trusted him based on "physiognomy"? Wei Zheng could not help but feel a sense of defiance. That future version of himself didn't sound very impressive. He was clearly capable of more. *Famous as a remonstrator? Does that mean I had nothing else to do but offer advice? With all my talent, how could I be reduced to that!*

Wei Zheng said, "Yes. I want to go to Wang Bo’s side."

Li Xuanba rubbed his temples. "It is very dangerous."

Wei Zheng said, "Is there any way to achieve great merit without danger?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "When I said you would be famous as a remonstrator, I didn't mean your work was limited to that. You will become a high official participating in state affairs, handling history and legal cases—you will do everything. Don't be stubborn."

Wei Zheng insisted, "I am not being stubborn. I clearly have greater talent, so I should achieve greater merit. I can still offer advice after I have achieved the status of a general and minister."

Li Xuanba had a headache. Wang Bo’s side was so dangerous; what if Wei Zheng died in the chaos of the late Sui? Why was this man so headstrong?

Li Xuanba tried to persuade him a few more times, but Wei Zheng’s mind was made up.

"Wang Bo is just a blacksmith. Although you have taught him, he may not be able to carry out your plans. If I go to assist him, I will surely be able to help him fulfill your expectations!" Wei Zheng stood up and bowed. "Please trust me, Young Master!"

Li Xuanba scolded, "I don't distrust you; I am worried about your safety!"

Wei Zheng couldn't help but laugh. "Will you and my future lord, Li Er-lang, not encounter danger while contending for the world? Is Second Brother not currently leading troops into battle himself? Young Master, I can certainly protect myself."

Li Xuanba clutched his head. "Heaven, I give up. My second brother hasn't started getting a headache over you yet, so why am I the one getting it first? Fine, fine, go. If you die, I will have my second brother grant you a posthumous title."

Wei Zheng smiled. "Then I leave that to you, Young Master."

Li Xuanba said weakly, "Don't you want to see your future lord before you leave?"

Wei Zheng said, "We will meet in the future; there is no need to rush. Wang Bo is currently dazed by your teachings, which is the perfect time for me to win his trust."

Li Xuanba sighed. "Go then. Take care. I cannot give you the troops I have now, but I will arrange for people to pose as refugees to join you, giving you a few hundred men as guards."

Wei Zheng’s eyes reddened. He knelt and kowtowed. "Thank you, Young Master! I will never fail your expectations!"

　　魏徵来了， 魏徵又走了。
　　因李玄霸身边的护卫都是在军中露过面的精锐，李玄霸没办法拨给魏徵，只能让魏徵多带了些财物， 买些壮仆护身。
　　魏徵给李玄霸舞了一段剑， 展示自己的武力值不错。
　　李玄霸敷衍地摆手， 让魏徵快滚。
　　他当然知道魏徵武力值不错，不然怎么能在乱世中行走？
　　魏徵大笑着离去，脸上心中眼底积攒了多年的郁气散去， 颇为潇洒倜傥。
　　看着魏徵离去的背影，李玄霸紧皱的眉头松开，也无奈地笑了出来。
　　“走吧， 该回去了。”
　　李玄霸策马转身，金雕在他头顶盘旋。
　　三日后， 李玄霸刚入清河郡， 就遇到了抱着手臂骑在马背上等他的李世民。
　　李世民的脸色十分难看，李玄霸却一点不惧。
　　“你怎么知道我从这条路回来？”李玄霸好奇。
　　李世民道：“寒钩通知我的。”
　　李玄霸道：“那大概是乌镝乱飞的时候碰到寒钩了。先回去再说，累。”
　　李世民很想把弟弟骂一顿，但看着弟弟满脸疲惫的模样，他只能先忍下。
　　李世民横了陈铁牛等人一眼， 想骂他们没劝住李玄霸，又担心自己贸然骂人， 下次这群人不会听李玄霸的话，心里特别纠结。
　　“这次遇到了很多有趣的事，回去慢慢和你聊。”李玄霸看出了李世民心中的纠结， 道， “别训他们， 他们听从我的命令， 应该奖赏。”
　　李世民叹气：“你说了算。”
　　李玄霸道：“对了，恭喜，虎贲郎将。”
　　李世民无奈道：“好，恭喜，虎牙郎将。你呀，传旨的官吏都比你先到。”
　　李玄霸道：“没办法，我遇到魏徵了。”
　　李世民猛地转头：“啊？谁？！”
　　李玄霸咧嘴龇牙笑：【魏徵，你的铜镜魏徵。】
　　李世民捂住胸口。
　　李玄霸大笑。
　　李世民抹了一把脸，也跟着笑。
　　他其实不怕什么啰嗦的谏臣，只是知道弟弟看到自己“吃瘪”会开心，就顺着弟弟的喜好来而已。
　　没办法，谁让他是哥哥。
　　李玄霸说着“回去再聊”，一路上心声就没停过。
　　李世民表情不断变换，手中马鞭扬起又放下，很想给李玄霸两下，又下不去手。
　　带着一两百人去贼窝？弟弟的胆子也太大了！就算你想去，带我一起去啊！
　　李世民怀疑，李玄霸找了许多借口把他留下，就是想单独去搞事。
　　弟弟羸弱的身体真是拖累了他过于放飞的灵魂。如果弟弟的身体与正常人一样健康，他估计会天天心惊胆战到处找不知道跑哪去的弟弟。
　　可怕。
　　“那些诗给我看看。”李世民道。
　　李玄霸：【啊？你怎么这么淡定？我去私会民贼！还教导民贼怎么做大做强！】
　　李世民：“好好好，是是是，我们不是早就约好了吗？我只是不满你一个人去。但你都安全回来了，我还惊讶什么？所以诗册还有备份吗？可恶，你为什么不先给我看？”
　　李玄霸：【啧。没有，不过我可以背给你听。你确定要听？】
　　李世民：“有什么不能听的，前朝这样的诗歌也很多。”
　　李玄霸：【你是说那首曹操在屠完徐州的几年后路过徐州，感慨徐州“白骨露于野，千里无鸡鸣”吗？】
　　李世民：“这个就太地狱笑话了。”
　　李玄霸：【你已经完全把我的梗学去了。】
　　李世民：“因为很有意思呀。”
　　兄弟二人在马背上越聊话题越偏。
　　在旁人眼中，就是李世民一个人在嘀嘀咕咕自言自语。
　　但他们都知道，这对双生子有奇妙的心灵感应。
　　至于为什么三郎君不开口说话，二郎君要出声，可能是因为二郎君喜欢说话吧。
　　……
　　李世民和李玄霸成了虎贲郎将、虎牙郎将后，就有了在郡城中选择官邸的资格。
　　李世民和李玄霸都是不会亏待自己的人。他们生活的环境虽然不奢华，但也绝对会很舒适，立刻着手搬家。
　　虎贲郎将和虎牙郎将是中高层将领，郡县官吏豪强都会来巴结。豪宅奴仆装修什么的都有人送。
　　李玄霸向来对合适的礼物来者不拒。
　　李世民在李玄霸回来之前把一应事务处理得井井有条。李玄霸检查账本的时候，李世民不仅把账务处理得很好，还提出了改进意见。
　　等弟弟回来，李世民就把后勤粮草和人情世故之类的事全部丢给弟弟，自己只管练兵了。
　　人的精力有限，虽然李世民能做，做得还很好，但有人为自己分担工作，他可不会累着自己。
　　李玄霸将王薄和魏徵的事告诉李世民后，李世民没有太在意。
　　“王薄如果能完成你的教导，我将来会尽力保他一命。”李世民道，“魏徵倒是心高气傲，不知道本事如何。”
　　李玄霸不怀好意地笑道：“如果魏徵真的成功，房杜二人的相位就有点悬了。”
　　李世民跟着笑道：“薛伯褒好好保重身体，活长一点，他们的相位本来就悬了。不过相位可以每年轮换，到时候换着来就成，都能当。”
　　李玄霸点头：“有道理。”
　　李世民道：“再说了，到时候说不定是你当丞相。”
　　李玄霸连连摆手：“我不干。我以后要当个无所事事的纨绔子弟。”
　　李世民叹气：“到时候再说吧。如果真的太累，我也不敢让你当。”
　　大隋的两位少年虎贲郎将虎牙郎将说了一会儿大逆不道的话，小羊羔终于烤好。
　　“阿玄，祝贺你又长一岁。”
　　“二哥也一样，生辰快乐。”
　　两位少年郎拿着葡萄酒碰杯。
　　“今天不醉不休！”
　　“阿玄，那你别喝了。你喝三杯葡萄酒就醉了，羊肉都没法吃。”
　　“让我先喝一杯！”
　　“唉。”
　　仆人们见今日二郎君和三郎君的话居然反了，竟然是三郎君想喝酒，二郎君不让，都忍俊不禁。
　　门口燃起了爆竹的声音。
　　身穿新衣的孩童们将竹节投入火堆中，火堆里响起了噼里啪啦的响声。
　　孩童们拍手欢笑，念着长辈教给他们的驱邪祈福的歌谣。
　　李世民晃着酒杯，听着门外的爆竹声和欢笑声，抿着嘴露出了仿佛醉了的笑意。
　　李玄霸起身。
　　李世民疑惑：“阿玄，你要做什么？”
　　李玄霸面无表情道：“没有火|药的爆竹是没有灵魂的爆竹，看我给他们炸个大的！”
　　李世民的视线落在李玄霸旁边的空坛子上，大惊失色：“我都让你别喝了！阿玄回来！”
　　李世民赶紧放下酒杯，把李玄霸按住。
　　李玄霸高喊：“炸个大的！这是艺术！”
　　李世民阻拦：“不准炸！没有艺术！快把醒酒汤端过来！”
　　李玄霸在心里高喊：【炸他祖宗的隋炀帝！】
　　李世民把弟弟往肩膀上一扛，擦了一把冷汗。弟弟就算醉了，也记得在说大逆不道的话时切换心声，还好还好。
　　李世民和李玄霸的十三周岁生日，就在李玄霸发酒疯中度过。
　　同年同月，隋朝皇帝杨广率一百一十三万隋军，号称两百万大军，水陆并攻高丽。
　　因为上次攻打吐谷浑的时候杨广去的太晚，他带着隋军穿越大斗拔谷时，战争基本已经结束。跟随他的将士又因为大斗拔谷的风雪死伤惨重，虽然隋军胜利了，但杨广无功而返。杨广对此很不满意。
　　所以这次他要和先锋军同行，并下令“凡军事进止，皆须奏闻待报”，不准将领自己决定军事行动。
　　合水令庾质劝阻杨广，兵贵神速，缓行无益，请求皇帝留在后方，让隋朝将领火速出击，攻其不备。
　　杨广震怒。
　　右尚方署监事耿询再次上书恳求，杨广要将耿询处斩，好不容易才被劝下。
　　至此无人敢再劝说杨广。
　　杨广给隋军制定了次序礼法，大军如仪仗队一般，一路上敲着战鼓吹着号角，旌旗连绵不绝九百六十里，耗费了整整四十天，最后一支隋军才从涿郡出发。
　　刚开始打仗，杨广所下的“凡军事进止，皆须奏闻待报”命令惹出了乱子。
　　辽东多河，隋军每当过河的时候，都要先请示杨广，杨广再派人勘察，下令建桥或者造船。
　　这一来一往，高丽军队已经在河对面等着了。
　　杨广拍板，建浮桥！
　　但他没有让人测量河宽，想当然地建了三座浮桥。浮桥一伸过去，杨广就让大隋将士往前冲。结果浮桥短了，隋军到不了对岸。
　　可撤退也得听皇帝的命令，浮桥又是单行道，实在是不好传递信息。隋军就这么堵在了桥上。
　　高丽军队一看，这不是天赐良机？于是一波远程攻击，隋军完全成了靶子。
　　隋军战斗力极强，将士骁勇善战。遇到这样逆境，他们没有退缩，跳下河涉水到对岸与高丽军队搏斗。左屯卫大将军麦铁杖、虎贲郎将钱士雄等皆战死。
　　还好大隋军队人多，这次失利后重新建桥，还是把高丽打跑了。大隋军队兵临辽东城下。
　　杨广为自己的英明战略十分得意，觉得这把稳了。
　　在行军途中，曾大破突厥的隋朝的老将军、右光禄大夫段文振病重。
　　这位老将军见自己快病死了，不用担心进谏后被责罚，于是拉着杨广直抒胸臆。
　　陛下啊，夷狄狡诈，他们的投降你千万别接受！请陛下让大隋水陆两军全速前进，直逼平壤。只要平壤打下来，高丽其他城池就不攻自破！攻打高丽必须在秋雨来临之前结束，否则粮草难以运输，隋军处境就十分困难了！
　　杨广抹着眼泪，卿说得好，卿你安息，赠卿光禄大夫、右仆射、北平郡开国侯，谥号为襄。段文振欣慰合眼。
　　段文振前脚刚死，杨广后脚下令，“高丽若降，即宜抚纳，不得纵兵”。
　　为段文振哭丧的同僚们哭声被噎住，然后哭得更大声了。
　　果然如段文振所料，高丽在辽东的守军得知杨广的诏令后，每当辽东城守不住了，他们就说要投降。
　　隋军只能停下攻城，飞马禀奏杨广。杨广召集群臣商议如何受降。
　　待杨广派出受降的使臣时，辽东城已经缓过气来，增援也来了，于是继续守城。
　　如是再三，隋军死伤无数，一直拖到了六月还没攻下辽东城。杨广仍旧坚持上当受骗。
　　将领求皇帝别听高丽鬼话了，杨广却亲临战场，骂他们贪生怕死，仗着家世显赫怠慢他的命令，才没有攻克辽东城。
　　将领怎么办？继续熬着呗，继续拿大隋将士的命，陪杨广和高丽人玩“我降了，我又不降了”的游戏。
　　另一边，宇文述、贺若弼、薛世雄等大将军共九路军、三十五万人从辽河攻打高丽。
　　这三十五万人有个大问题，就是只有军队，没有后勤民夫，让士卒自己背负重达三石的粮草辎重。
　　谁背得动啊？
　　士卒只能一边行军一边将粮草辎重偷偷埋了。于是路走到一半，隋军就断粮了。
　　不过大军之中，有个刺头子没有听令。
　　这人就是宋国公贺若弼。
　　贺若弼是隋文帝时名将，自恃功高，桀骜不驯。杨广很不喜欢他。
　　他本来会因为和宇文弼、高颎“诽谤朝政”被杀。宇文弼和高颎提前跑了，贺若弼不蠢，嗅到了不对劲，再加上他性格孤僻没多少朋友，自己只在家里抱怨几句没人听到，便一直活到现在。
　　贺若弼本来以为，无论是征讨吐谷浑还是高丽，皇帝都该任命他为主将。
　　但杨广偏爱宇文述，总是让宇文述领军。
　　贺若弼对此十分不满。他私下抱怨，杨素是猛将，韩擒虎是斗将，史万岁是骑将，虽然都不如自己这员大将，好歹算个将。宇文述完全没有为将的本事，只是因为讨得皇帝喜欢而领兵，迟早会出问题。
　　此次攻打高丽，贺若弼再次请求为主将。但杨广以他已经六十八岁高龄为由，只让他领了一路偏军，仍旧让宇文述当主将。
　　宇文述下令后，贺若弼讥笑，究竟是他会打仗，还是老夫会打仗？我听你个鬼！
　　于是贺若弼将辎重减半，没有民夫便精简士卒，裁三分之二为民夫运送后勤，自己领着精兵前往平壤。
　　他一路轻车快马，将宇文述的大军远远甩在身后。到达平壤时，右翊卫大将军来护儿率领的水军刚刚到达。
　　来护儿与贺若弼很熟悉，两人合兵之后。来护儿本来想贪功独自攻打平壤城，被贺若弼骂了一顿，便讪讪作罢，率兵接应宇文述的大军。
　　历史悄然偏转。
　　……
　　“但没偏太多。”李玄霸得到辽东前线战报后，深深叹了口气。
　　杨广所率领的那支大隋军队仍旧损失惨重，但因来护儿和贺若弼接应了宇文述的军队，原本会几乎全军覆没的三十五万隋军偏师没有遭受太大损失。
　　宇文述虽然打仗不行，但很有自知之明。他发现自己打仗确实不行后，就装病将领兵权交给贺若弼，并送信告诉杨广此事。
　　“将”还是老的辣，贺若弼一战攻克平壤，高丽王高元逃走。
　　虽然辽东城还是没打下来，但平壤破了。
　　你以为征伐高丽获胜了？
　　哈哈哈哈，没有。因为高丽王高元派遣使者向杨广投降，杨广就下诏，撤、兵、受、降！
　　贺若弼拒不受命，想要追杀高元，被杨广派去的使者擒拿；隋军撤到辽东，高元回到平壤，休整之后说不降了；杨广勃然大怒，却因秋雨到来后勤难以为继，在八月撤兵返回……这一条条前线消息，真的把李玄霸看得肚子都笑疼了，眼泪都笑出来了。
　　李世民握紧双拳，目眦欲裂：“荒唐！”
　　李玄霸擦着笑出来的眼泪道：“这一征高丽的结局，居然和史书中三征高丽的结局混在一起了。三征高丽的结局就是来护儿大破高丽，高元请降后，杨广就不顾来护儿继续出征的请求，强命来护儿退兵。哈哈哈，伟大的皇帝只是想要个臣服的国书而已，你们还真当他想攻城略地开疆扩土啊。”
　　李世民深吸一口气，按住弟弟的脑袋：“别笑了，笑得比哭还难看。”
　　李玄霸止住笑声。
　　他骂道：“狗日的杨广。”
　　李世民小声道：“嗯。”
　　是岁，去年刚遭遇了大水灾的崤山以东，又遭遇了前所未有的大旱。
　　一涝一旱，饿殍无数，疫病横行。
　　此时，一首《菜人哀》悄然在中原唱响，闻者无不色变。
　　这首诗也传到了清河郡。
　　李玄霸将写着高丽战报的纸丢进火盆，脆弱的纸张很快就化为了灰烬。
　　李世民站在火盆旁，低头看着火盆中的灰烬。
　　“阿玄，天下提前大乱了。”
　　“这是好事。”
