Chapter 97: The Absurd Maneuvers of the Korean Campaign

Wei Zheng had arrived, and now, Wei Zheng had departed.
Since the guards by Li Xuanba’s side were all battle-hardened elites who had shown their faces in the military, Li Xuanba could not spare any for Wei Zheng. He could only let him take more wealth to purchase sturdy servants for protection.
Wei Zheng had performed a sword dance for Li Xuanba to demonstrate that his martial prowess was not to be trifled with.
Li Xuanba waved him off perfunctorily, telling him to get lost.
He knew full well that Wei Zheng’s martial prowess was decent; otherwise, how could he have survived in such chaotic times?
Wei Zheng left with a hearty laugh. The pent-up frustration he had harbored for years in his heart and eyes had dissipated, leaving him looking quite dashing and carefree.
Watching Wei Zheng’s retreating figure, Li Xuanba’s tightly furrowed brows relaxed, and he couldn't help but let out a helpless laugh.
"Let’s go. It’s time to head back."
Li Xuanba turned his horse around, a golden eagle circling high above his head.
Three days later, just as Li Xuanba entered Qinghe Commandery, he encountered Li Shimin, who was waiting for him on horseback with his arms crossed.
Li Shimin’s expression was extremely grim, yet Li Xuanba was not afraid in the slightest.
"How did you know I would return by this route?" Li Xuanba asked curiously.
Li Shimin replied, "Han Gou notified me."
Li Xuanba said, "That must have been when the Black Arrows were flying everywhere and happened to bump into Han Gou. Let’s head back first; I’m exhausted."
Li Shimin desperately wanted to scold his younger brother, but seeing the exhaustion etched across his face, he could only hold his tongue for now.
Li Shimin shot a glare at Chen Tieniu and the others. He wanted to berate them for failing to dissuade Li Xuanba, but he worried that if he scolded them rashly, they wouldn't listen to Li Xuanba’s orders next time. He felt deeply conflicted.
"I encountered many interesting things this time; I’ll tell you all about it when we get back," Li Xuanba said, sensing Li Shimin’s inner turmoil. "Don't lecture them. They were following my orders—they should be rewarded."
Li Shimin sighed. "Whatever you say."
Li Xuanba added, "By the way, congratulations, General Huben."
Li Shimin replied helplessly, "Fine, congratulations to you too, General Huya. You, of all people—the imperial decree officials arrived even before you did."
Li Xuanba said, "I couldn't help it; I ran into Wei Zheng."
Li Shimin whipped his head around. "What? Who?!"
Li Xuanba grinned, revealing his teeth: *[Wei Zheng, your bronze mirror, Wei Zheng.]*
Li Shimin clutched his chest.
Li Xuanba burst into laughter.
Li Shimin wiped his face and joined in the laughter.
In truth, he wasn't afraid of some long-winded remonstrating official; he simply knew his brother enjoyed seeing him "thwarted," so he played along with his brother’s whims.
There was no helping it—who else was there to be the big brother?
As Li Xuanba said "we'll talk when we get back," his inner voice hadn't stopped for a moment along the way.
Li Shimin’s expression shifted constantly. He raised his horse whip and then lowered it, wanting to give Li Xuanba a few lashes but unable to bring himself to do it.
Taking one or two hundred men into a bandit’s den? His brother’s courage was simply too great! Even if you wanted to go, you should have taken me with you!
Li Shimin suspected that Li Xuanba had made up many excuses to leave him behind just so he could go stir up trouble on his own.
His brother’s frail body was truly a burden to his overly unrestrained soul. If his brother’s body were as healthy as a normal person’s, he would probably be terrified every single day, searching for a brother who had run off to who-knows-where.
Terrifying.
"Show me those poems," Li Shimin said.
Li Xuanba: *[Huh? Why are you so calm? I went to meet with rebels in secret! And I even taught the rebels how to grow and become strong!]*
Li Shimin: "Fine, fine, yes, yes. Didn't we agree on this long ago? I’m just unhappy you went alone. But you’ve returned safely, so what else is there to be surprised about? So, are there any copies of the poetry collection? Damn it, why didn't you show me first?"
Li Xuanba: *[Tsk. No, but I can recite them to you. Are you sure you want to hear them?]*
Li Shimin: "What’s there that I can’t hear? There were plenty of such poems in the previous dynasty."
Li Xuanba: *[Are you talking about that poem Cao Cao wrote when he passed through Xuzhou years after slaughtering it, lamenting that in Xuzhou, 'white bones lay exposed in the fields, and for a thousand miles, no rooster crowed'?]*
Li Shimin: "That one is a bit too much of a 'hellish' joke."
Li Xuanba: *[You’ve completely learned my style of humor.]*
Li Shimin: "Because it’s quite interesting."
The two brothers chatted on horseback, their topics drifting further and further afield.
To others, it looked as if Li Shimin was muttering to himself.
But they all knew that these twins shared a marvelous telepathic connection.
As for why the Third Young Master didn't speak while the Second Young Master did, it was likely just because the Second Young Master enjoyed talking.
...
After Li Shimin and Li Xuanba became General Huben and General Huya, they were eligible to select an official residence in the commandery city.
Neither Li Shimin nor Li Xuanba were the type to mistreat themselves. Although their living environment wasn't extravagant, it was certainly comfortable, and they immediately set about moving.
As mid-to-high-level generals, they were courted by commandery officials and local magnates. People sent everything from luxury mansions to servants and decorations.
Li Xuanba had always been one to accept suitable gifts without refusal.
Li Shimin had handled all affairs in an orderly fashion before Li Xuanba returned. When Li Xuanba checked the ledgers, he found that not only had Li Shimin managed the accounts well, but he had also offered suggestions for improvement.
Once his brother returned, Li Shimin dumped all the logistics, grain, and social obligations onto him, focusing solely on training his troops.
Human energy is limited. Although Li Shimin could do it, and do it well, he wouldn't tire himself out if there was someone to share the workload.
After Li Xuanba told Li Shimin about Wang Bo and Wei Zheng, Li Shimin didn't pay much mind to it.
"If Wang Bo can fulfill your teachings, I will do my best to spare his life in the future," Li Shimin said. "Wei Zheng, however, is proud and arrogant; I wonder what his true capabilities are."
Li Xuanba smiled mischievously. "If Wei Zheng truly succeeds, the Prime Minister positions of Fang and Du might be in jeopardy."
Li Shimin laughed along. "As long as Xue Bebao takes good care of his health and lives a long life, their positions were already in jeopardy anyway. Besides, the premiership can be rotated annually; we can just swap them around when the time comes. Everyone can have a turn."
Li Xuanba nodded. "That makes sense."
Li Shimin added, "Besides, by then, it might be you who becomes the Prime Minister."
Li Xuanba waved his hands repeatedly. "I’m not doing it. I intend to be a carefree, idle playboy in the future."
Li Shimin sighed. "We’ll see when the time comes. If it’s truly too exhausting, I wouldn't dare let you take it."
The two young generals of the Great Sui spoke for a while about treasonous matters until the little lamb was finally roasted to perfection.
"Ah Xuan, congratulations on turning another year older."
"Same to you, Second Brother. Happy birthday."
The two young men clinked their wine cups filled with grape wine.
"Let’s not stop until we’re drunk today!"
"Ah Xuan, then you shouldn't drink. You get drunk after three cups of wine, and you won't even be able to eat the lamb."
"Let me have at least one cup!"
"Sigh."
The servants, seeing that the roles of the Second Young Master and Third Young Master had reversed—with the Third Young Master wanting to drink and the Second Young Master forbidding it—couldn't help but suppress their laughter.
Firecrackers began to pop at the entrance.
Children dressed in new clothes threw bamboo segments into the fire, which crackled and popped.
The children clapped and laughed, reciting the songs of warding off evil and praying for blessings that their elders had taught them.
Li Shimin swirled his wine cup, listening to the firecrackers and laughter outside, his lips curling into a smile that looked almost intoxicated.
Li Xuanba stood up.
Li Shimin asked in confusion, "Ah Xuan, what are you doing?"
Li Xuanba said with a blank expression, "Firecrackers without gunpowder are firecrackers without a soul. Watch me set off a big one for them!"
Li Shimin’s gaze fell on the empty jar beside Li Xuanba, and he was struck with alarm. "I told you not to drink! Ah Xuan, come back here!"
Li Shimin hurriedly set down his cup and pinned Li Xuanba down.
Li Xuanba shouted, "Set off a big one! This is art!"
Li Shimin blocked him. "No setting off! There is no art! Someone, bring the hangover soup!"
Li Xuanba shouted in his heart: *[Blow up the ancestor of that Emperor Yang of Sui!]*
Li Shimin hoisted his brother onto his shoulder, wiping away a cold sweat. Even when drunk, his brother remembered to switch to his inner voice when saying treasonous things—thank goodness for that.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba’s thirteenth birthday was spent in the midst of Li Xuanba’s drunken antics.
In the same year and month, Emperor Yang of Sui led 1.13 million Sui troops—claiming a force of two million—to attack Goguryeo by land and sea.
Because Emperor Yang had arrived too late during the previous campaign against the Tuyuhun, the war was essentially over by the time he led the Sui army through the Da Douba Valley. The soldiers who followed him suffered heavy casualties due to the wind and snow in the valley, and although the Sui army won, Emperor Yang returned without any real merit. Emperor Yang was very dissatisfied with this.
Therefore, this time, he insisted on traveling with the vanguard and ordered that "all military movements, whether advancing or halting, must be reported and await approval," forbidding the generals from making their own tactical decisions.
Yu Zhi, the Magistrate of Heshuiling, tried to dissuade Emperor Yang, arguing that speed was the essence of war and that slow movement was useless. He requested the Emperor to remain in the rear and allow the Sui generals to strike rapidly and catch the enemy off guard.
Emperor Yang was furious.
Geng Xun, the Supervisor of the Right Shangfang Office, submitted a petition pleading the same, and Emperor Yang ordered him to be executed; it was only through great effort that he was dissuaded.
From then on, no one dared to advise Emperor Yang again.
Emperor Yang established a strict order and protocol for the Sui army. The massive force moved like a ceremonial procession, beating war drums and blowing horns the entire way. The banners stretched unbroken for 960 *li*, and it took a full forty days for the last of the Sui troops to depart from Zhuojun.
As soon as the fighting began, the order that "all military movements must be reported and await approval" caused chaos.
Liaodong was full of rivers. Every time the Sui army needed to cross a river, they had to request instructions from Emperor Yang, who would then send someone to survey the area and order the construction of bridges or boats.
By the time this back-and-forth was completed, the Goguryeo army was already waiting on the other side.
Emperor Yang made the final call: build pontoon bridges!
But he didn't have anyone measure the width of the river and presumptuously ordered three pontoon bridges to be built. As soon as the bridges were extended, Emperor Yang ordered the Sui soldiers to charge forward. As it turned out, the bridges were too short, and the Sui soldiers couldn't reach the opposite bank.
However, even retreating required the Emperor’s orders, and the pontoon bridges were one-way streets, making it impossible to relay information. The Sui army became stuck on the bridges.
When the Goguryeo army saw this, they realized it was a heaven-sent opportunity. With a wave of long-range attacks, the Sui soldiers became sitting ducks.
The Sui army had immense combat power, and the soldiers were brave and skilled. Faced with such adversity, they did not retreat; they jumped into the river, waded to the opposite bank, and engaged the Goguryeo army in hand-to-hand combat. The Left Tunwei General Mai Tiezhang and General Huben Qian Shixiong were all killed in action.
Fortunately, the Great Sui army had superior numbers. After this setback, they rebuilt the bridges and eventually drove the Goguryeo forces away. The Sui army arrived at the walls of Liaodong City.
Emperor Yang was very proud of his brilliant strategy, feeling that victory was certain.
During the march, the old Sui general and Right Guanglu Grand Master Duan Wenzhen, who had previously crushed the Turks, fell gravely ill.
Seeing that he was nearing death and no longer had to worry about being punished for remonstrating, the old general grabbed Emperor Yang and spoke his mind.
"Your Majesty, the barbarians are cunning; you must never accept their surrender! Please, Your Majesty, allow the Sui naval and land forces to advance at full speed directly to Pyongyang. Once Pyongyang is taken, the other cities of Goguryeo will fall without a fight! The campaign against Goguryeo must be concluded before the autumn rains arrive; otherwise, logistics will be impossible, and the Sui army will be in a dire situation!"
Emperor Yang wiped away tears. "Your words are wise, Minister. Rest in peace. I bestow upon you the title of Guanglu Grand Master, Right Pushe, and Founding Duke of Beiping Commandery, with the posthumous title of Xiang." Duan Wenzhen closed his eyes in peace.
No sooner had Duan Wenzhen died than Emperor Yang issued an order: "If Goguryeo surrenders, they should be pacified and accepted; do not allow the troops to pillage."
The colleagues mourning for Duan Wenzhen had their cries choked off, only to wail even louder.
Just as Duan Wenzhen had predicted, once the Goguryeo defenders in Liaodong learned of Emperor Yang’s decree, whenever Liaodong City was on the verge of falling, they would claim they wanted to surrender.
The Sui army had no choice but to stop the siege and send messengers galloping to report to Emperor Yang. Emperor Yang would then summon his ministers to discuss how to accept the surrender.
By the time Emperor Yang sent his envoys to accept the surrender, Liaodong City had caught its breath, reinforcements had arrived, and they continued to defend the city.
This happened repeatedly. The Sui army suffered countless casualties, and by June, they still hadn't captured Liaodong City. Emperor Yang persisted in being deceived.
When the generals begged the Emperor to stop listening to Goguryeo’s lies, Emperor Yang personally visited the battlefield and berated them for being cowardly and using their noble backgrounds to slack off on his orders, which was why Liaodong City hadn't been captured.
What could the generals do? They just had to keep enduring it, continuing to sacrifice the lives of Sui soldiers to play the game of "I surrender, wait, I don't surrender" with Emperor Yang and the Goguryeo people.
On the other side, nine armies totaling 350,000 men under generals like Yuwen Shu, Heluo Bi, and Xue Shixiong attacked Goguryeo from the Liao River.
These 350,000 men had a major problem: they had an army but no logistical support staff, forcing the soldiers to carry their own heavy grain and supplies, weighing three *shi* each.
Who could carry that?
The soldiers had no choice but to secretly bury their grain and supplies while marching. Halfway there, the Sui army ran out of food.
However, there was one troublemaker in the army who didn't follow orders.
This man was the Duke of Song, Heluo Bi.
Heluo Bi was a famous general during the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui. He prided himself on his great merits and was unruly and defiant. Emperor Yang disliked him intensely.
He would have been executed for "slandering the government" alongside Yuwen Bi and Gao Jiong. Yuwen Bi and Gao Jiong had fled in advance, but Heluo Bi was not stupid; he had sensed that something was wrong. Furthermore, he was a recluse with few friends, and since he had only complained at home where no one heard him, he had survived until now.
Heluo Bi had originally thought that whether it was the campaign against the Tuyuhun or Goguryeo, the Emperor should have appointed him as the commander-in-chief.
But Emperor Yang favored Yuwen Shu and always let him lead the army.
Heluo Bi was deeply dissatisfied with this. He complained in private, "Yang Su is a fierce general, Han Qinhu is a combat general, and Shi Wansui is a cavalry general. Although none of them are as good as me, they at least count as generals. Yuwen Shu has absolutely no ability as a general; he only leads troops because he pleases the Emperor. It will cause problems sooner or later."
During this campaign against Goguryeo, Heluo Bi once again requested to be the commander-in-chief. But Emperor Yang used his advanced age of sixty-eight as an excuse, only letting him lead a flanking force while still keeping Yuwen Shu as the commander-in-chief.
After Yuwen Shu issued his orders, Heluo Bi sneered, "Does he know how to fight, or do I? I’m not listening to your nonsense!"
So, Heluo Bi halved his supplies. Lacking support staff, he streamlined his troops, cutting two-thirds to serve as laborers to transport logistics, and led his elite force toward Pyongyang.
He traveled light and fast, leaving Yuwen Shu’s main army far behind. When he reached Pyongyang, the naval force led by Right Yiwei General Lai Hu'er had just arrived.
Lai Hu'er was well-acquainted with Heluo Bi. After they joined forces, Lai Hu'er initially wanted to claim the credit by attacking Pyongyang alone, but after being berated by Heluo Bi, he sheepishly gave up and led his troops to support Yuwen Shu’s army.
History had quietly shifted.
...
"But not by much." After receiving the frontline reports from Liaodong, Li Xuanba let out a deep sigh.
The Sui army led by Emperor Yang still suffered heavy losses, but because Lai Hu'er and Heluo Bi had supported Yuwen Shu’s army, the 350,000-strong flanking force, which would have been almost entirely wiped out, did not suffer too much damage.
Although Yuwen Shu was poor at fighting, he had self-awareness. After discovering that he truly couldn't fight, he feigned illness, handed over command to Heluo Bi, and sent a letter to Emperor Yang informing him of the situation.
"Ginger" is still spicier when it's old; Heluo Bi captured Pyongyang in a single battle, and the Goguryeo King Gao Yuan fled.
Although Liaodong City still hadn't been captured, Pyongyang had fallen.
Did you think the campaign against Goguryeo was a success?
Hahahaha, no. Because the Goguryeo King Gao Yuan sent envoys to surrender to Emperor Yang, Emperor Yang issued an edict to withdraw the troops and accept the surrender!
Heluo Bi refused to obey the order and wanted to pursue and kill Gao Yuan, but he was captured by the envoys sent by Emperor Yang. The Sui army withdrew to Liaodong, Gao Yuan returned to Pyongyang, and after regrouping, he declared he would no longer surrender. Emperor Yang was furious, but because the autumn rains had arrived and logistics were unsustainable, he withdrew his troops in August... Reading these frontline reports one by one truly made Li Xuanba’s stomach ache from laughter, tears streaming down his face.
Li Shimin clenched his fists, his eyes splitting with rage. "Absurd!"
Li Xuanba wiped away the tears of laughter. "The ending of this first campaign against Goguryeo has actually merged with the ending of the three campaigns against Goguryeo in the history books. The ending of the three campaigns was that Lai Hu'er crushed Goguryeo, and after Gao Yuan requested surrender, Emperor Yang ignored Lai Hu'er’s request to continue the campaign and forcibly ordered him to withdraw. Hahaha, the great Emperor just wanted a letter of submission; you all really thought he wanted to capture cities and expand his territory?"
Li Shimin took a deep breath and pressed down on his brother’s head. "Stop laughing. You look uglier than when you’re crying."
Li Xuanba stopped laughing.
He cursed, "Damn that Yang Guang."
Li Shimin whispered, "Yeah."
That year, the region east of the Xiao Mountains, which had just suffered a massive flood the previous year, was hit by an unprecedented drought.
One flood, one drought—countless people starved to death, and epidemics ran rampant.
At this time, a poem titled *Lament of the Cannibal* was quietly sung throughout the Central Plains, and all who heard it turned pale.
This poem also reached Qinghe Commandery.
Li Xuanba threw the paper containing the Goguryeo war reports into the brazier, and the fragile paper quickly turned to ash.
Li Shimin stood beside the brazier, looking down at the ashes within.
"Ah Xuan, the world has fallen into chaos ahead of schedule."
"This is a good thing."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第98章 被排挤的薛道衡 – 第99章 少年郎将回洛阳
chunks.chineseText:
第98章 被排挤的薛道衡

=
　　杨广班师回朝。
　　比起原定历史中一征高丽只攻克了武厉逻， 给高丽送了一大批辎重。这次隋军虽然也损失了许多兵卒，但至少能平稳退军，把辎重都拖走了， 没有给高丽留太多东西。
　　大隋占领的地盘也比原本历史中稍大一些， 杨广建立的辽东郡不是可怜的一座小城池。
　　但对大隋而言， 这仍旧是一场前所未有的大失败。
　　特别是皇帝被高丽王三番五次戏耍，更是让满朝文武都颜面无光。
　　对杨广而言，这也是他人生中第一次重大失误。
　　他让车队马不停蹄地往东都赶， 想要逃离这个让他丢脸的地方。
　　苏威等了解杨广的重臣此时顾不上党同伐异，悄悄递话给朝中文武，让他们现在闭上嘴， 可千万别提任何关于高丽的事。否则皇帝一发怒，谁也保不住他们。
　　看看立了大功劳却被关在狱中的贺若弼， 你们小心些！
　　高颎远在大兴， 得到高丽消息时杨广已经回到了东都洛阳。
　　宇文弼和薛道衡一起去拜访他的时候，他背挺得笔直，坐在池中央的亭子里弹琴。
　　旱了许久的大兴城终于下起了秋雨，高颎的琴音与秋日寒雨滴落声混在一起，竟分不清哪一种声音更加肃杀。
　　宇文弼和薛道衡撑着簦， 驻足雨中，如两尊雕像。
　　待琴音停止时， 两人才走入亭中。
　　宇文弼把簦放在地上，雨水顺着簦面蜿蜒滴落。
　　他眼神有些黯然。
　　心情郁闷的时候，连看见从簦面落下的雨水都会感慨王朝的风雨飘摇。
　　薛道衡问道：“高公， 你还好吗？”
　　高颎摇摇头， 道：“我能好吗？”
　　薛道衡叹气。
　　比起他和宇文弼， 高颎更深刻地参与了隋朝的建立。
　　高颎早年频繁南征北战， 隋朝大半疆土都有他的心血。
　　现在见到杨广如此败家，高颎心中怎会不煎熬？
　　“当先帝试图改立杨广为太子时，曾让我多次与杨广共事，想改变我支持废太子的立场。灭陈时，我便与他同行。”高颎直呼皇帝的姓名，薛道衡和宇文弼都没有露出惊慌的神色，“与杨广共事后，我更坚信他绝非明君。”
　　高颎讥笑了一声：“废太子确实喜好奢侈美色，但这对储君来说，只要不超过他储君的规格，就不算缺点。他性格宽厚率直，才华平庸但听得进劝说，不会因别人进谏而埋怨猜忌，所以我相信他能当好守成之君。”
　　“反观杨广，我能看出他也是喜欢奢侈美色之人。他能控制住自己的欲|望，所图非小。但其实这也不是缺点，反倒是优点。只是杨广每每忍耐的时候，都显出愤恨不平的态度。这才是我当初警惕的缘由。”
　　高颎长叹了一口气，说起当初灭陈时，杨广看中陈帝贵妃张丽华的事。听了自己的劝告后，杨广放弃纳张丽华，下令将其斩杀。但高颎能看出，杨广对张丽华的不舍，和对自己的不悦。
　　“过分抑制自己的欲|望的人，当他无需忍耐会有两种后果。一种是他已经学会控制自己，不会为外物所动；一种是变本加厉的放纵。我断定杨广是后一种人。”高颎又长叹了一口气，“他就是后一种人。”
　　以前杨广节俭，现在他每年都要修宫殿；以前杨广不好美色，现在他在征讨高丽受挫民乱四起的时候还不忘督促进贡美女；以前杨广强忍着不悦听人劝谏，现在他什么劝谏都不听。
　　杨广的一生太顺畅了，所以一点挫折都受不得。明明他心中也知道高丽王在耍他，但他就是一而再再而三地重蹈覆辙，因为他不肯承认自己的错误，非要高丽王真正向他请降，他才觉得自己赢了。
　　否则就算把高丽王杀了，把高丽夷为平地，他都认为自己失了脸面。
　　宇文弼道：“在杨广看来，征讨高丽的目的已经变成逼迫高丽王投降。他大概想效仿诸葛武侯七纵七擒。”
　　薛道衡冷笑：“画虎类犬。”
　　三位老臣讥笑后，又陷入深深的悲哀。
　　他们都是看着大隋结束乱世统一天下，看着大隋在短短几十年内就彰显出盛世气象。
　　他们原本都以为又一个强汉即将到来。
　　虽然这些年他们已经做好了大隋会在杨广手中败落的心理准备，但看见这么离谱的御驾亲征，他们还是难免抑郁愤怒悲哀。
　　“宋国公还被关在牢中，我想向陛下进言。”沉默许久之后，宇文弼说起了自己的来意，“或许这会很危险，但宋国公刚立了大功劳，不应当被关在牢中。”
　　薛道衡道：“我也要进言。不过我和公辅来此，是劝说你不要进言。陛下仍旧很忌惮你。”
　　高颎沉声：“我知道。若我进言，他没有杀害宋国公之心，恐怕都要生出杀心。”
　　宇文弼道：“你知道就好。”
　　高颎拳头狠狠砸在琴面上，“哐”的一声十分刺耳。
　　宇文弼安慰道：“我知道你难受。此次来，我给你带来了会让你高兴的消息。”
　　高颎抬头：“有比李二郎和李三郎当上了郎将更令人高兴的事？”
　　宇文弼从怀里摸出一卷粗糙的草纸：“从民贼那里查抄出的诗册。你看看。”
　　高颎皱眉：“民贼还会作诗？”
　　他打开诗册，翻书的速度越来越快。
　　薛道衡伸头：“民贼还分发诗册？让我看看……嗯？嗯？！这、这些诗谁写的！！”
　　高颎迅速翻完了诗册，抬头道：“和李二郎……不，肯定是和大德有关！大德又在做什么？！”
　　薛道衡震惊：“李大德写的？不愧是……不，不对，这些诗所用修辞个人风格很突出，不该是同一人所作。”
　　宇文弼笑道：“肯定不是他一人所作，但一定与他有关系。”
　　薛道衡疑惑：“公辅为何如此肯定？”
　　宇文弼叹道：“有几句诗我曾听珠儿提起过。珠儿说这是大德信中所写，从古书中搜集的前人诗句。”
　　高颎面色古怪：“前人？”
　　宇文弼对着高颎微笑：“前人。”
　　两老头对视，心中明了。什么前人，怕不是后人。
　　李大德都能看到《隋书》，多看几首后人的诗作多正常？他们听李大德嘀咕过“唐诗宋词”，说唐朝的诗歌创作十分兴盛。这些隋末的诗，怕不是唐末的诗。
　　高颎又翻了一遍诗册，特别留意了诗句中的地点风物。
　　这些与现实相似但不同的地点风物，可以说是避讳或者复古，也可以有另一种说法，比如现在还没出现。
　　“这……他想干什么？”高颎说完后，就笑骂道，“他是嫌弃大隋崩塌的还不够快啊。”
　　薛道衡震惊：“什么？他要谋反！”
　　高颎和宇文弼被薛道衡吓了一跳。
　　他们注视着薛道衡，又十分疑惑地对视。
　　“咳。”宇文弼问道，“薛玄卿，你知道大德有谶纬之能吗？”
　　薛道衡再次震惊：“什么？什么之能？”
　　高颎和宇文弼再次对视一眼。
　　糟糕，他们还以为薛道衡和他们是一伙的，原来薛道衡什么都不知道吗？
　　薛道衡见两位老友频繁对视的神情，也察觉到了什么。
　　他满是褶皱的脸皮使劲抖动：“你、你们瞒着我什么？”
　　高颎叹气：“我没想过瞒着你什么，只是忘记你不知道。大德还没告诉你？”
　　宇文弼右手虚握放在嘴边，不知道为何有些想笑。
　　薛道衡幽怨道：“宇文公辅，你笑什么？”
　　宇文弼嘴角上翘得更厉害：“我没笑。”
　　薛道衡愤怒地一甩袖子，“刷拉”一声，大袖口被风吹得鼓胀，就像是一只大扑腾蛾子：“李世民！李玄霸！他两个竖子究竟有没有把我当老师！”
　　宇文弼笑道：“以我对大德的了解，他可能只是忘了。”
　　高颎差点也笑出来，他努力板着脸道：“以我对李二郎的了解，他是真的忘了。”
　　薛道衡气得把双手往背后一背，在亭子中来回踱步。
　　高颎起身拉住薛道衡：“别生气别生气，他们二人与我们异地相隔，求教只能用书信。这样重要的事怎么能用书信交流？所以才忘记了。如果你询问，他们肯定会如实相告。”
　　薛道衡瓮声瓮气道：“李大雄和李大德在大兴求教的时候也没有告诉我此事。”
　　宇文弼道：“他们可能真的只是忘了。”
　　薛道衡气得一脚踹向宇文弼。
　　宇文弼扭身躲开。
　　薛道衡破口大骂：“谁不知道李大德是你孙女婿！你只会偏向李大德！”
　　宇文弼慢条斯理道：“这可不对。比起连强弓都拉不开的大德，我更偏向大雄。”
　　高颎继续安慰：“你见他们二人每次托人送来礼物时，我们有的，你难道缺了？你应该知道，你在他二人心中的分量，与我和宇文公辅是一样的。”
　　薛道衡心中难以抑制地涌出委屈：“不一样，肯定不一样。罢了罢了，你们早认识他们，我确实与你们不一样。”
　　薛道衡甩开高颎，气得一屁股坐在石墩上，扭头不去看高颎和宇文弼。
　　高颎和宇文弼再次对视。
　　高颎：生气了，怎么办？
　　宇文弼：哄呗。
　　李世民和李玄霸不知道是不是忘记了，他们二人是真的以为薛道衡早就知道了。
　　不过现在他们倒是为难了。
　　李世民和李玄霸还没把谶纬之事告诉薛道衡，自己是不是不好多嘴？
　　唉。
　　不过他们都说漏嘴了，也不得不告诉薛道衡此事。
　　高颎和宇文弼都做好了等李二郎李三郎造反的准备。薛道衡没做好这个心理准备，将来怕会坑到两个弟子。
　　……
　　“老师送的急信？”李世民拆开信，“什么信这么急？我看看……哇哦！阿玄，薛老师问如果你要编撰《隋书》，会把他列入第几个传记。”
　　正喝水的李玄霸：“噗……咳咳咳！”


第99章 少年郎将回洛阳

=
　　李世民捧腹大笑：“哈哈哈哈哈哈， 我还以为你早就、早就告诉薛老师了，哈哈哈哈，薛老师一定气死了！”
　　李玄霸使劲抓挠头发。
　　他没告诉薛道衡自己会谶纬的事倒不是忘记， 只是没必要， 就没有特意提起。
　　薛道衡已经渡过了死劫， 又不是被杨广忌惮到非死不可的人，李玄霸认为对薛道衡透露未来之事不太安全。
　　后来他们与薛道衡感情加深，薛道衡又和高颎、宇文弼走得很近， 进入了李玄霸划分的“安全范围”时，李玄霸已经离开了大兴。
　　他总不能在书信中对薛道衡透露未来吧？
　　任何会留下痕迹的事都很危险。他给王薄的书籍都是故意做劣质了的印刷本。
　　虽然自己有充足的理由解释此事，但看到薛道衡这封信， 李玄霸还是难免尴尬心虚。
　　李玄霸嘀咕：“都怪高老师和宇文老师，他们为何要和薛老师说此事！”
　　李世民大笑道：“哈哈， 可、可能是以为薛老师知道， 哈哈哈哈，好想看看薛老师的表情！”
　　李玄霸瞥了二哥一眼。
　　他以为自己是个乐子人。没想到二哥也不遑多让。
　　虽然尴尬心虚，但信中不是道歉的好地方。李玄霸只说了几句“老师你开什么玩笑，我哪有编撰史书的本事”敷衍过去，然后让人备上重礼。
　　具体道歉的话， 还是等下次见面时再说吧。
　　李世民笑够之后，把信翻来覆去地看， 看完继续笑。
　　李玄霸不知道二哥的笑点为什么会这么低。
　　李玄霸阴阳怪气道：“很好笑是吗？等见到薛老师，你敢当面笑吗？”
　　李世民笑道：“就是不敢，我才要现在笑个够， 哈哈哈哈。”
　　李世民彻底变成“哈哈怪”， 李玄霸嫌弃地把李世民一个人丢在书房继续笑， 自己出门透气。
　　随着大隋大军返回， 又有李世民的震慑，清河郡的民乱表面上被平息。
　　大部分虎贲郎将平时都待在朝中。李玄霸估摸着洛阳很快就会来圣旨把他和二哥调回去。
　　自己和二哥已经初露头角，明年杨广二征高丽时，说不准会让自己和二哥同行。
　　想到二征高丽，李玄霸心头沉重。
　　今年刚征讨完高丽，又连续遇到水旱灾害，明年还要继续征讨高丽。再厚的家底也不够杨广败的。
　　他原本疑惑杨广哪来的钱粮再次征讨高丽，当了实权官员之后李玄霸才得知，隋朝居然是不赈灾的。
　　当唐朝建立的时候，百姓已经经历了十几年的饥饿和战乱，洛阳附近几个大粮仓中居然还有陈粮。
　　一般而言，王朝末年朝廷都是缺钱缺粮的，连军饷都发不出去。
　　隋朝灭亡的时候，粮仓却还是满的。
　　所以在杨广眼中，他确实可以年年征战。国家还富着呢。
　　李玄霸所料很准。
　　在王朝还稳固的时候，随时驻扎在地方上的虎贲郎将代表不受重视、难以晋升。如李世民和李玄霸这样的勋贵子弟、皇帝宠臣，在办完事之后就会回朝。
　　李世民很不想回去。
　　如果他回去，手中军队就会交到别人手中。虽然他“中饱私囊”，用大隋的钱把自己的私兵装备到了牙齿，但他明面上能带走的私兵顶多一千人。
　　李玄霸道：“回去多送点礼，看能不能说动皇帝让我们去防备突厥。”
　　李世民叹气：“好不容易在清河郡经营了名声，又要从头开始，真是不开心。”
　　李玄霸劝慰道：“我们在这里的义庄还在，名声不会消失。金角银边草肚皮，留在中原发展不易，还是去边疆更好。”
　　李世民疑惑：“留在中原不好？当初曹操就是占据中原繁华之地。”
　　李玄霸道：“现在中原已经被打烂了。而且现在还不是乱世。你想想战国时，是不是与戎狄蛮夷混居的秦楚发展最迅速？”
　　李世民思考了一会儿，笑道：“还真是。边疆能扩展的地方更多，且中原与太多势力接壤，安稳发展不易。怪不得叫金角银边草肚皮。”
　　李世民摸了摸下巴：“这么一想，史书中许多势力变革好像多了许多我以前没想到的有趣因素。我要把史书重看一遍，照着地图看。”
　　李玄霸道：“那你去马背上看，马车上太暗，会伤眼睛。”
　　于是回程时，李玄霸在马车上补觉，李世民就在马背上一边赶路一边看书。
　　路过城池时，郡县官员都会出来招待这两位少年虎贲郎将、虎牙狼将，总会看到李世民在马背上手不释卷的模样。
　　李二郎君好学之名悄然传播开来。
　　至于缩在马车里被颠得快散架的李玄霸，就暂时被人忽视了。
　　李世民劝李玄霸也来骑马，李玄霸以就算被颠散架也还是躺着更舒服为由拒绝。李世民哭笑不得。
　　“等回洛阳后，你多休息一段时日。”李世民道，“家里家外应酬的事都交给我，我不会让别人来打扰你。”
　　李玄霸蔫哒哒道：“就拜托二哥了。”
　　他赶路去蓟州和从蓟州回来时比现在更劳累，他都没感到太难受。这次卸下所有工作回洛阳，他居然受不住路上的颠簸。
　　人一旦闲起来，果然各种毛病都冒出来了。
　　李世民尽可能地放慢了速度，让弟弟旅途别太劳累。所以回程的路，他们整整走了半月才到。
　　两人刚一回洛阳就被杨广召见。
　　杨广就像是炫耀晚辈的家长似的，带着李世民和李玄霸挨个向群臣介绍。
　　坐镇大兴的杨暕也来到了洛阳。他戴着温和的面具与李世民、李玄霸敬酒，看得李世民和李玄霸很是别扭。
　　不过杨暕已经会装模作样，看来比以前成长许多。
　　历史中齐王杨暕在此时就已经被杨广忌惮防备而不自知。现在太子杨暕那温和谦逊的模样，让李世民和李玄霸仿佛从他身上看到了杨昭的影子。
　　宴会后，李世民和李玄霸回到了别庄中躲避多余的应酬。
　　李世民心情有一点低落：“二表兄成长了许多。”
　　李玄霸道：“成长是好事。”
　　两人正聊着，陈铁牛火急火燎地跑来告诉他们有人翻墙。
　　李世民和李玄霸满头问号。
　　谁都知道这个别庄住的什么人，谁这么大胆敢大大咧咧翻墙进来？
　　“大雄！大德！看我带了什么好酒！”翻墙的人大摇大摆地过来了，“来！本王还没祝贺你们当上虎贲郎将虎牙郎将！”
　　李世民和李玄霸：“……”
　　李世民和李玄霸：“二表兄？！”
　　杨暕大笑道：“是我！吓到了吗？”
　　李世民笑着迎上前，和杨暕对了一下掌：“二表兄，你已经不是齐王了，自称什么本王？怎么不走门？”
　　杨暕对李玄霸挤眉弄眼：“这不是三郎说，我当了太子之后最好与你们别这么亲近。我就偷偷乔装打扮来。放心，其他人绝对不知道！”
　　李玄霸无语。你说其他人不知道，其他人就真的不知道吗？他才刚夸二表兄成熟了，结果二表兄还是这么傻。
　　“少喝点。我给你们烤肉，别拉着我灌酒。”李玄霸道，“除了烤肉，还想吃点什么？”
　　李世民用胳膊肘撞了一下杨暕：“我弟弟的厨艺可好了，就是懒得做。你赶紧点菜，把想吃的都点一遍。”
　　杨暕道：“那好，累着大德你别心疼。”
　　李世民笑道：“在这件事上，我绝对不心疼！”
　　李玄霸没好气道：“就算你们点多了，我嫌累也不会做。”
　　说完，他转身去厨房把厨艺最好的厨子从床上挖起来加班。
　　他没发觉，自己转身离开的时候，嘴角是上弯着的。
　　忙碌完夜宵，李玄霸坐在拼酒的杨暕和李世民身边，听两人胡吹自己做的大事。
　　监国是大事，剿贼也是大事，就是吹得太过，连斩龙灭妖都冒出来了。
　　李玄霸在一旁嫌弃撇嘴的时候，陪同杨暕一同来的侍从也在叹气。
　　李玄霸懒得理睬已经变成酒蒙子的杨暕和李世民，与那人搭讪道：“还未问君姓名，照顾二表兄辛苦了。”
　　那人笑道：“在下姓庾名俭，字养廉。李三郎君，久仰。”
　　李玄霸记了起来：“是养廉兄？什么久仰，别笑话我。你比上次见面高了许多，我都不认识了。”
　　李玄霸年幼时和杨暕忙碌“公立书院勤工俭学补助计划”的时候，庾俭就跟随杨暕和李玄霸一起忙碌。
　　杨暕不可能事事亲为，大部分事都是庾俭在做。
　　庾俭其父名为庾质，原本为太史令，后因得罪杨广被贬为合水令。杨广回东都后，又重授庾质太史令。
　　从这可以看出，杨广欣赏庾质的才华，不然也不会在国家大事上询问庾质的意见。
　　庾俭也很有学识。在杨昭把杨暕身边的小人赶走后，庾俭就成为杨暕身边第一得用的人。
　　见李玄霸和庾俭说话，杨暕凑过来抱怨道：“养廉什么都好，就是太啰嗦。大兄去塞外前，拉着养廉的手叮嘱他多劝谏，这人的唠叨就停不下来了。”
　　庾俭道：“不敢辜负元德太子嘱托。”
　　“哼。”杨暕横了庾俭一眼，拉着李世民去另外一处喝酒。
　　李玄霸道：“我们也别理他们，来，吃肉。”
　　庾俭吃了几串烤肉后，与李玄霸回忆了往事，话匣子打开。
　　李玄霸从庾俭这里询问杨暕当太子之后的事。
　　或许是杨昭死前为他铺路的事，让杨暕得到了很大触动，所以杨暕确实比以前成熟许多，下决心要当个不输给兄长的太子。
　　庾俭从杨暕以前资助的学子中选了一些品行端正的人举荐给杨暕。这些人虽然品行端正，学识不错，但因为是吃过苦头的寒门庶族，所以性格大多比较圆滑，和性格高傲的杨暕相处不错。
　　李玄霸看向喝高后和二哥手拉手围着篝火跳起舞的太子杨暕。
　　“二表兄确实越来越出色了。”李玄霸道。
　　庾俭微笑，笑容中含着十分明显的自豪神色：“太子确实很出色。”
　　李玄霸夸了杨暕几句，转移话题，问起大兴城中有没有什么趣事。
　　庾俭妙语连珠，听得李玄霸不住笑。
　　另一边，杨暕和李世民喝嗨了和跳嗨了，不顾秋夜露浓，甩着衣服围着火堆乱嚎。
　　李玄霸和庾俭同时捂住，对视叹气。
　　“好吵啊，快去劝劝你家太子。”
　　“大德先去劝住你二兄。”
　　杨暕和李世民继续拉长脖子扯着嗓子嚎叫。
　　洛阳宫中。
　　第二日，杨广就得知杨暕翻墙去找李世民、李玄霸喝酒，并嚎了半夜之事。
　　杨广皱眉。
　　他本来准备把李世民和李玄霸放在身边执掌宫禁，但太子与李世民、李玄霸交好……
　　“还是外放吧。”杨广想着杨暕劝他释放贺若弼，不悦道。

Chapter 98: The Ostracized Xue Daoheng

Yang Guang led his army back to the capital.
Compared to the original history, where the first campaign against Goguryeo resulted in the capture of only a single minor city and the loss of a massive amount of supplies to the enemy, this time, although the Sui army suffered many casualties, they were at least able to retreat in an orderly fashion, dragging their supplies back with them and leaving little behind for Goguryeo.
The territory occupied by the Great Sui was also slightly larger than in the original history; the Liaodong Commandery established by Yang Guang was not merely a pathetic, tiny city.
Yet, for the Great Sui, this remained an unprecedented and catastrophic failure.
In particular, the Emperor being toyed with time and again by the King of Goguryeo left the entire civil and military court humiliated.
For Yang Guang, this was also the first major blunder of his life.
He ordered the convoy to race toward the Eastern Capital without pause, desperate to flee the place that had brought him such disgrace.
Su Wei and other senior officials who understood Yang Guang’s temperament were too busy to engage in factional infighting; they quietly passed word to the court officials to keep their mouths shut and never mention anything related to Goguryeo. Otherwise, if the Emperor flew into a rage, no one would be able to save them.
"Look at He Ruobi," they warned. "He performed great meritorious service, yet he is rotting in prison. You all had better be careful!"
Gao Jiong was far away in Daxing. By the time he received news of Goguryeo, Yang Guang had already returned to the Eastern Capital, Luoyang.
When Yuwen Bi and Xue Daoheng went to visit him, he was sitting in a pavilion in the middle of a pond, his back straight as a ramrod, playing the zither.
The city of Daxing, which had suffered through a long drought, was finally experiencing an autumn rain. The sound of Gao Jiong’s zither mingled with the patter of the cold autumn rain, making it impossible to tell which sound was more desolate.
Yuwen Bi and Xue Daoheng stood in the rain holding oil-paper umbrellas, as still as statues.
Only when the zither music ceased did the two walk into the pavilion.
Yuwen Bi set his umbrella on the ground, and rainwater snaked down the surface of the canopy.
His eyes were somewhat dim.
When one is depressed, even the sight of rainwater dripping from an umbrella can evoke feelings of a dynasty teetering on the brink of collapse.
Xue Daoheng asked, "Lord Gao, are you well?"
Gao Jiong shook his head and replied, "How could I be?"
Xue Daoheng sighed.
Compared to him and Yuwen Bi, Gao Jiong had been more deeply involved in the founding of the Sui Dynasty.
In his early years, Gao Jiong had frequently campaigned north and south; much of the Sui territory was built upon his hard work.
Now, seeing Yang Guang squandering the empire so recklessly, how could Gao Jiong’s heart not be tormented?
"When the Late Emperor attempted to change the succession and make Yang Guang the Crown Prince, he had me work with Yang Guang many times, hoping to change my stance on supporting the deposed Crown Prince. When we destroyed the Chen Dynasty, I traveled with him." Gao Jiong addressed the Emperor by his given name, yet neither Xue Daoheng nor Yuwen Bi showed any sign of alarm. "After working with Yang Guang, I became even more convinced that he was by no means a wise monarch."
Gao Jiong gave a mocking laugh. "The deposed Crown Prince did indeed love luxury and beauty, but for a crown prince, as long as it did not exceed the standards of his position, it was not a fatal flaw. He was broad-minded and straightforward; though his talents were mediocre, he listened to advice and would not harbor resentment or suspicion against those who remonstrated with him. Thus, I believed he could have been a capable ruler who maintained the status quo."
"Contrast this with Yang Guang. I could see that he, too, loved luxury and beauty. He could control his desires, which meant he had grand ambitions. In truth, this was not a flaw, but a virtue. However, every time Yang Guang restrained himself, he would display an attitude of resentment and indignation. That was the reason for my initial wariness."
Gao Jiong let out a long sigh, recalling the time during the fall of the Chen Dynasty when Yang Guang had taken a fancy to the Chen Emperor’s favorite concubine, Zhang Lihua. After hearing Gao Jiong’s advice, Yang Guang gave up on taking her and ordered her execution. Yet, Gao Jiong could see Yang Guang’s reluctance to let her go and his displeasure toward him.
"A person who excessively suppresses their desires will face one of two outcomes when they no longer need to restrain themselves: either they have learned to control themselves and are unmoved by external objects, or they will indulge in increasingly reckless abandon. I concluded that Yang Guang was the latter." Gao Jiong sighed again. "He is indeed the latter."
In the past, Yang Guang was frugal; now, he builds palaces every year. In the past, he did not care for beauty; now, even while his campaigns in Goguryeo falter and civil uprisings erupt everywhere, he does not forget to demand the tribute of beautiful women. In the past, he would force himself to listen to advice despite his displeasure; now, he listens to no one.
Yang Guang’s life had been too smooth, so he could not endure even the slightest setback. Even though he knew in his heart that the King of Goguryeo was playing him for a fool, he repeated the same mistakes over and over because he refused to admit his error. He insisted that the King of Goguryeo must personally surrender to him before he could feel he had won.
Otherwise, even if he killed the King of Goguryeo and razed the country to the ground, he would still feel he had lost face.
Yuwen Bi said, "In Yang Guang’s eyes, the purpose of the Goguryeo campaign has shifted to forcing the King of Goguryeo to surrender. He likely wants to emulate Zhuge Wuhou’s seven captures and seven releases."
Xue Daoheng sneered, "A clumsy imitation."
After their mockery, the three old officials fell into a deep, sorrowful silence.
They had all watched the Great Sui end the chaos and unify the world, and they had watched it display the signs of a golden age within a few short decades.
They had originally thought that another "Strong Han" era was about to arrive.
Although they had prepared themselves over the years for the possibility that the Great Sui would fall under Yang Guang, seeing such an absurd imperial expedition still left them feeling depressed, angry, and sorrowful.
"The Duke of Song is still locked in prison. I intend to submit a petition to His Majesty." After a long silence, Yuwen Bi stated his purpose. "Perhaps it will be dangerous, but the Duke of Song has just performed a great service; he should not be kept in a cell."
Xue Daoheng said, "I also intend to submit a petition. However, Gongfu and I came here to persuade you not to do so. His Majesty is still very wary of you."
Gao Jiong said in a low voice, "I know. If I speak up, even if he had no intention of killing the Duke of Song, he might well develop the desire to do so."
Yuwen Bi said, "It is good that you know."
Gao Jiong slammed his fist onto the zither, the "clanging" sound harsh and jarring.
Yuwen Bi comforted him, "I know you are distressed. I have brought you news today that will cheer you up."
Gao Jiong looked up. "Is there anything more pleasing than Li Erlang and Li Sanlang becoming Langjiang (Commandants)?"
Yuwen Bi pulled a roll of coarse straw paper from his robes. "A collection of poems confiscated from the rebels. Take a look."
Gao Jiong frowned. "The rebels can write poetry?"
He opened the booklet, his speed of turning pages increasing rapidly.
Xue Daoheng leaned in. "The rebels are distributing poetry booklets? Let me see... Hmm? What?! Who wrote these poems?!"
Gao Jiong finished flipping through the booklet and looked up. "This is related to Li Erlang... no, it must be related to Da De! What is Da De doing now?!"
Xue Daoheng was shocked. "Written by Li Da De? As expected of... no, that’s not right. The rhetorical style of these poems is very distinct; they couldn't have been written by the same person."
Yuwen Bi laughed. "They certainly weren't all written by him, but they are definitely connected to him."
Xue Daoheng asked, puzzled, "Gongfu, why are you so certain?"
Yuwen Bi sighed. "I once heard Zhu'er mention a few of these lines. Zhu'er said they were written in a letter from Da De, who claimed he collected them from ancient books."
Gao Jiong’s expression was strange. "Ancient books?"
Yuwen Bi smiled at Gao Jiong. "Ancient books."
The two old men looked at each other, understanding dawning in their hearts. "Ancient books," indeed—more like "future books."
Since Li Da De could see the *Book of Sui*, was it not normal for him to see a few poems from the future? They had heard Li Da De mutter about "Tang poetry and Song lyrics," saying that poetry in the Tang Dynasty was extremely prosperous. These poems from the end of the Sui were likely poems from the end of the Tang.
Gao Jiong flipped through the booklet again, paying special attention to the locations and scenery mentioned.
These locations and scenery, which were similar to reality but slightly different, could be called a taboo or a stylistic archaism, or there could be another explanation: they simply didn't exist yet.
"This... what is he trying to do?" After Gao Jiong finished speaking, he laughed and cursed, "Is he afraid that the Great Sui isn't collapsing fast enough?"
Xue Daoheng was shocked. "What? He wants to rebel!"
Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi were startled by Xue Daoheng.
They stared at Xue Daoheng, then exchanged a very confused look.
"Cough," Yuwen Bi asked, "Xue Xuanqing, do you know that Da De possesses the ability of prophecy (Chenwei)?"
Xue Daoheng was shocked again. "What? The ability of what?"
Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi exchanged glances once more.
Oh no, they had assumed Xue Daoheng was in on it with them. It turned out Xue Daoheng knew nothing?
Seeing the way his two old friends kept glancing at each other, Xue Daoheng sensed something.
His wrinkled face twitched violently. "You... what are you hiding from me?"
Gao Jiong sighed. "I didn't intend to hide anything from you, I just forgot you didn't know. Hasn't Da De told you?"
Yuwen Bi held his right hand over his mouth, not knowing why he suddenly felt like laughing.
Xue Daoheng said resentfully, "Yuwen Gongfu, what are you laughing at?"
The corners of Yuwen Bi’s mouth curled up even higher. "I'm not laughing."
Xue Daoheng angrily flicked his sleeves. With a "swish," his large sleeves billowed in the wind like a giant moth. "Li Shimin! Li Xuanba! Do these two brats even consider me their teacher?!"
Yuwen Bi laughed. "Based on my understanding of Da De, he probably just forgot."
Gao Jiong almost laughed as well. He tried to keep a straight face and said, "Based on my understanding of Li Erlang, he truly just forgot."
Xue Daoheng, furious, put his hands behind his back and paced back and forth in the pavilion.
Gao Jiong stood up and grabbed Xue Daoheng. "Don't be angry, don't be angry. They are separated from us by a great distance, and they can only communicate through letters. How could they discuss such important matters in a letter? That's why they forgot. If you ask them, they will surely tell you the truth."
Xue Daoheng grumbled, "Li Daxiong and Li Da De didn't tell me about this when they were studying in Daxing either."
Yuwen Bi said, "They probably really just forgot."
Xue Daoheng, in a fit of rage, kicked at Yuwen Bi.
Yuwen Bi twisted his body to dodge.
Xue Daoheng cursed loudly, "Who doesn't know that Li Da De is your granddaughter's husband! You only favor Li Da De!"
Yuwen Bi said calmly, "That’s not true. Compared to Da De, who can't even pull back a strong bow, I actually favor Daxiong more."
Gao Jiong continued to comfort him, "You see that every time they send gifts through others, we get some, and you never go without, do you? You should know that your weight in their hearts is the same as mine and Yuwen Gongfu's."
Xue Daoheng couldn't suppress the sense of grievance welling up inside him. "It's not the same, it definitely isn't. Fine, fine, you knew them earlier; I am indeed different from you."
Xue Daoheng shook off Gao Jiong, sat down on a stone stool in a huff, and turned his head away, refusing to look at Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi.
Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi exchanged glances again.
Gao Jiong: *He's angry, what do we do?*
Yuwen Bi: *Coax him, obviously.*
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba didn't know if they had forgotten; they truly thought Xue Daoheng had known all along.
But now, they were in a bind.
Since Li Shimin and Li Xuanba hadn't told Xue Daoheng about the prophecy, was it their place to speak out of turn?
Sigh.
However, since they had already let it slip, they had no choice but to tell Xue Daoheng about it.
Gao Jimin and Yuwen Bi were prepared for Li Erlang and Li Sanlang to rebel. Xue Daoheng was not prepared for this, and he might end up being implicated by his two students in the future.
...
"An urgent letter from Teacher?" Li Shimin opened the letter. "What could be so urgent? Let me see... Whoa! A-Xuan, Teacher Xue is asking if you were to compile the *Book of Sui*, which volume you would list his biography in."
Li Xuanba, who was drinking water, choked: "Pfft... *cough, cough, cough!*"

Chapter 99: The Young Commandant Returns to Luoyang

Li Shimin clutched his stomach, laughing. "Hahahaha, I thought you had already—already told Teacher Xue! Hahaha, Teacher Xue must be furious!"
Li Xuanba scratched his hair vigorously.
It wasn't that he had forgotten to tell Xue Daoheng about his ability to prophesy; it was just that it hadn't been necessary, so he never specifically brought it up.
Xue Daoheng had already survived his brush with death and wasn't someone Yang Guang feared to the point of needing to be killed. Li Xuanba simply felt it wasn't safe to reveal the future to Xue Daoheng.
Later, as their relationship deepened and Xue Daoheng became close with Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi, entering the "safe zone" Li Xuanba had defined, Li Xuanba had already left Daxing.
He couldn't exactly reveal the future to Xue Daoheng in a letter, could he?
Anything that left a trail was dangerous. Even the books he gave to Wang Bo were intentionally printed as low-quality copies.
Although he had plenty of excuses to explain this, seeing Xue Daoheng’s letter still made Li Xuanba feel awkward and guilty.
Li Xuanba muttered, "It's all Gao-laoshi and Yuwen-laoshi's fault. Why did they have to tell Teacher Xue about this!"
Li Shimin laughed heartily. "Haha, they—they probably thought Teacher Xue knew! Hahahaha, I really want to see Teacher Xue's expression!"
Li Xuanba shot his second brother a glare.
He had thought he was the one who enjoyed stirring up trouble. He hadn't expected his second brother to be just as bad.
Despite his embarrassment and guilt, a letter was not the place for an apology. Li Xuanba wrote a few lines of "Teacher, what jokes are you making? How could I have the ability to compile historical records?" to brush it off, then ordered his men to prepare generous gifts.
He would save the real apology for when they met in person.
After Li Shimin finished laughing, he read the letter over and over again, continuing to chuckle after he finished.
Li Xuanba didn't know why his second brother's sense of humor was so low.
Li Xuanba said sarcastically, "Is it that funny? When you see Teacher Xue, do you dare laugh to his face?"
Li Shimin smiled. "That's exactly why I have to laugh my fill now, hahahaha."
Li Shimin had completely turned into a "laughing machine." Li Xuanba left him alone in the study to keep laughing and went outside to get some air.
With the return of the Great Sui army and the deterrent effect of Li Shimin’s presence, the civil unrest in Qinghe Commandery was, on the surface, quelled.
Most of the Huben Langjiang (Tiger-Gallant Commandants) usually stayed at court. Li Xuanba figured that an imperial decree would soon come from Luoyang to recall him and his second brother.
He and his second brother had already begun to make a name for themselves. When Yang Guang launched his second campaign against Goguryeo next year, it was quite possible they would be ordered to accompany him.
Thinking of the second campaign against Goguryeo, Li Xuanba’s heart grew heavy.
They had just finished the campaign this year, and they had suffered consecutive water and drought disasters; yet, they were going to continue the campaign next year. No matter how deep the empire's foundations were, they wouldn't be enough for Yang Guang to squander.
He had originally wondered where Yang Guang would get the money and grain to launch another campaign. Only after becoming an official with real power did Li Xuanba learn that the Sui Dynasty simply did not provide disaster relief.
By the time the Tang Dynasty was established, the people had already endured over a decade of famine and war, yet the large granaries near Luoyang still contained old grain.
Generally speaking, in the final years of a dynasty, the imperial court would be short of money and grain, unable to even pay the soldiers.
Yet, when the Sui Dynasty fell, the granaries were still full.
So, in Yang Guang’s eyes, he could indeed campaign every year. The country was still rich.
Li Xuanba’s prediction was accurate.
While the dynasty was still stable, being stationed in the provinces as a Huben Langjiang meant one was not valued and had little chance of promotion. Noble scions and imperial favorites like Li Shimin and Li Xuanba would be recalled to the capital after completing their duties.
Li Shimin was very reluctant to return.
If he returned, the army in his hands would be handed over to someone else. Although he had "lined his own pockets" and used Sui funds to equip his private soldiers to the teeth, he could only openly take at most a thousand private soldiers with him.
Li Xuanba said, "Send more gifts when we return. See if we can persuade the Emperor to let us guard against the Turks."
Li Shimin sighed. "I finally built up a reputation in Qinghe Commandery, and now I have to start all over again. It's really frustrating."
Li Xuanba comforted him, "Our charity estate here still exists, and our reputation won't disappear. 'Golden corners, silver edges, grass bellies'—developing in the Central Plains is not easy; it’s better to go to the frontiers."
Li Shimin was puzzled. "Is it bad to stay in the Central Plains? Cao Cao occupied the prosperous lands of the Central Plains."
Li Xuanba said, "The Central Plains have already been shattered. And this isn't a time of chaos yet. Think back to the Warring States period; wasn't it the Qin and Chu states, which lived among the Rong and Di barbarians, that developed the fastest?"
Li Shimin pondered for a while and smiled. "That's true. The frontiers have more room to expand, and the Central Plains border too many factions, making stable development difficult. No wonder they call it 'golden corners, silver edges, grass bellies'."
Li Shimin stroked his chin. "Thinking about it this way, many of the changes in historical powers seem to have had many interesting factors I hadn't thought of before. I need to reread the history books while looking at a map."
Li Xuanba said, "Then read them on horseback. It's too dark in the carriage, and it will hurt your eyes."
And so, on the return journey, Li Xuanba caught up on sleep in the carriage, while Li Shimin read books on horseback while traveling.
Whenever they passed through a city, the local officials would come out to entertain these two young Tiger-Gallant Commandants, and they would always see Li Shimin with a book in his hand, never putting it down.
The reputation of Li Erlang’s love for learning quietly spread.
As for Li Xuanba, who was huddled in the carriage and being rattled to pieces, he was temporarily ignored.
Li Shimin urged Li Xuanba to ride a horse, but Li Xuanba refused, arguing that even if he were rattled to pieces, it was still more comfortable to lie down. Li Shimin didn't know whether to laugh or cry.
"Rest for a while after we return to Luoyang," Li Shimin said. "I'll handle all the social obligations inside and outside the house. I won't let anyone disturb you."
Li Xuanba said listlessly, "I'll leave it to you, Second Brother."
He hadn't felt this exhausted when he traveled to Jizhou and back, yet now, after being relieved of all his duties to return to Luoyang, he couldn't handle the bumps of the road.
Once a person gets idle, all sorts of ailments start to pop up.
Li Shimin slowed down as much as possible so his younger brother wouldn't be too tired. Thus, the return journey took a full half-month.
As soon as the two arrived in Luoyang, they were summoned by Yang Guang.
Yang Guang was like a parent showing off his juniors, taking Li Shimin and Li Xuanba around to introduce them to the court officials one by one.
Yang Jian, who had been holding down the fort in Daxing, had also come to Luoyang. He wore a mask of gentleness as he toasted Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, which made them feel very awkward.
However, Yang Jian had learned to put on a show; it seemed he had grown up a lot since before.
In history, the Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, was already being feared and guarded against by Yang Guang at this time without even knowing it. Now, the gentle and humble appearance of the Crown Prince Yang Jian made Li Shimin and Li Xuanba feel as if they were seeing the shadow of Yang Zhao in him.
After the banquet, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba returned to their villa to avoid unnecessary socializing.
Li Shimin was a little downcast. "Second Cousin has grown up a lot."
Li Xuanba said, "Growth is a good thing."
As they were talking, Chen Tie-niu ran over in a panic to tell them someone was climbing over the wall.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were full of question marks.
Everyone knew who lived in this villa; who was so bold as to climb over the wall so brazenly?
"Daxiong! Da De! Look what good wine I brought!" The person climbing over the wall walked in swaggeringly. "Come! I haven't congratulated you two on becoming Huben Langjiang and Huya Langjiang yet!"
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba: "..."
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba: "Second Cousin?!"
Yang Jian laughed heartily. "It's me! Were you scared?"
Li Shimin smiled and walked forward to high-five Yang Jian. "Second Cousin, you aren't the Prince of Qi anymore; why are you calling yourself 'this prince'? Why didn't you use the door?"
Yang Jian winked at Li Xuanba. "It's because Sanlang said that after I became Crown Prince, it was best not to be so close to you two. So I snuck in disguised. Don't worry, no one else knows!"
Li Xuanba was speechless. *You say no one else knows, but do they really not know?* He had just praised his second cousin for being mature, but it turned out he was still this silly.
"Drink less. I'll grill some meat for you, but don't drag me into a drinking contest," Li Xuanba said. "Besides grilled meat, what else do you want to eat?"
Li Shimin nudged Yang Jian with his elbow. "My brother’s cooking is excellent, he’s just too lazy to do it. Hurry up and order, order everything you want to eat."
Yang Jian said, "Alright, don't feel bad if you tire Da De out."
Li Shimin laughed. "On this matter, I absolutely won't feel bad!"
Li Xuanba said irritably, "Even if you order too much, I won't make it if I feel tired."
After saying this, he turned and went to the kitchen to dig the best chef out of bed to work overtime.
He didn't notice that when he turned to leave, the corners of his mouth were curled upward.
After finishing the late-night snack, Li Xuanba sat beside Yang Jian and Li Shimin, who were drinking and boasting about the great deeds they had done.
Being the regent was a great deed, and suppressing rebels was a great deed, but they boasted so much that they even started talking about slaying dragons and destroying demons.
While Li Xuanba curled his lip in disdain, the attendant who had accompanied Yang Jian also sighed.
Li Xuanba couldn't be bothered to deal with Yang Jian and Li Shimin, who had become drunken messes, so he struck up a conversation with the man. "I haven't asked your name yet. It must have been hard taking care of Second Cousin."
The man smiled. "My surname is Yu, given name Jian, courtesy name Yanglian. Li Sanlang-jun, I have long admired you."
Li Xuanba remembered. "Is it Brother Yanglian? What 'long admired,' don't mock me. You've grown much taller since we last met; I didn't even recognize you."
When Li Xuanba was young and busy with Yang Jian on the "Public Academy Work-Study Subsidy Program," Yu Jian had worked alongside them.
Yang Jian couldn't do everything himself, and most of the work was done by Yu Jian.
Yu Jian’s father, Yu Zhi, was originally the Grand Historian, but was demoted to Magistrate of Heshuo after offending Yang Guang. After Yang Guang returned to the Eastern Capital, he reappointed Yu Zhi as Grand Historian.
From this, it could be seen that Yang Guang appreciated Yu Zhi’s talent; otherwise, he wouldn't have asked for his opinion on national affairs.
Yu Jian was also very knowledgeable. After Yang Zhao drove away the petty people around Yang Jian, Yu Jian became the most trusted person by Yang Jian’s side.
Seeing Li Xuanba and Yu Jian talking, Yang Jian leaned over and complained, "Yanglian is good at everything, except he's too long-winded. Before Eldest Brother went to the frontier, he held Yanglian’s hand and urged him to advise me more, and this man’s nagging hasn't stopped since."
Yu Jian said, "I dare not fail the trust of Crown Prince Yuande."
"Hmph." Yang Jian gave Yu Jian a sideways glance and pulled Li Shimin away to drink elsewhere.
Li Xuanba said, "Let's ignore them. Come, eat some meat."
After Yu Jian ate a few skewers of grilled meat and reminisced about the past with Li Xuanba, he opened up.
Li Xuanba asked Yu Jian about things since Yang Jian became Crown Prince.
Perhaps it was the way Yang Zhao had paved the way for him before he died that had deeply moved Yang Jian, so he was indeed much more mature than before, determined to be a crown prince who wouldn't lose to his elder brother.
Yu Jian had selected some upright people from the students Yang Jian had previously sponsored and recommended them to him. Although these people were upright and knowledgeable, because they were poor scholars who had suffered, most of them were quite tactful and got along well with the proud Yang Jian.
Li Xuanba looked at Crown Prince Yang Jian, who, after getting drunk, was dancing around the bonfire hand-in-hand with his second brother.
"Second Cousin is indeed becoming more and more outstanding," Li Xuanba said.
Yu Jian smiled, his smile containing a very obvious sense of pride. "The Crown Prince is indeed very outstanding."
Li Xuanba praised Yang Jian a few more times, then changed the subject, asking if there were any interesting things happening in Daxing.
Yu Jian was witty and eloquent, making Li Xuanba laugh incessantly.
On the other side, Yang Jian and Li Shimin were having a blast drinking and dancing, ignoring the heavy autumn dew, swinging their clothes and howling around the fire.
Li Xuanba and Yu Jian covered their ears at the same time and sighed, looking at each other.
"So noisy, go and persuade your Crown Prince."
"Da De, go and persuade your Second Brother first."
Yang Jian and Li Shimin continued to stretch their necks and howl at the top of their lungs.
In the Luoyang Palace.
The next day, Yang Guang learned that Yang Jian had climbed over the wall to drink with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, and had howled for half the night.
Yang Guang frowned.
He had originally planned to keep Li Shimin and Li Xuanba by his side to guard the palace, but the Crown Prince was on such good terms with them...
"Better to send them away," Yang Guang thought, feeling displeased as he remembered Yang Jian urging him to release He Ruobi.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第100章 杨暕的再次成长
chunks.chineseText:
第100章 杨暕的再次成长

杨暕兴尽而去。
　　第二日， 他沉着脸再次来访。
　　这次，他是从正门进来。
　　李世民和李玄霸已经得到了外放的消息，正开心地畅想未来。见到杨暕一脸阴沉， 两人都很疑惑。
　　李世民对杨暕勾肩搭背道：“二表兄， 谁惹你了？”
　　杨暕沉声道：“抱歉， 我连累了你们。”
　　李世民：“啊？”
　　杨暕双拳握紧，脑袋低垂，声线十分压抑， 好像压着一团火：“如果不是我，你们就不会被外放。我应该听大德的劝说，我……”
　　杨暕心头压了太多事。李世民和李玄霸被他连累， 成了他情绪崩塌的最后一根稻草。
　　他单手捂着脸，哽咽道：“父皇怎么能这样……”
　　李世民忙安慰道：“什么事？什么连累？我和阿玄好好的啊。二表哥， 冷静点。”
　　李玄霸猜到了内情， 道：“先进屋。”
　　李世民拉着杨暕往里走。
　　李玄霸对周围的人道：“这件事若传出去，你们知道后果。做你们的事去。”
　　仆从立刻散去。
　　李玄霸对脸色晦暗的庾俭道：“你现在带出来的人能保证嘴严？”
　　庾俭苦笑：“我已经不知道了。”
　　李玄霸扫了一眼庾俭带出来的五位侍卫。
　　侍卫的脸上露出紧张的神色。
　　李玄霸收回视线：“你这次带出来的人就这么几个，今日的事若再传出去，很好查。太子是陛下最疼爱的儿子，我和二哥是陛下最器重的晚辈。谁要在陛下面前嚼舌根， 掂量掂量自己的分量。”
　　庾俭道：“我也是这么想。昨日我不该带太多侍卫。”
　　庾俭十分自责。太子本来没打算带太多人，但太子夜游城郊， 最近民贼又太多，庾俭便说服太子多带了些人。
　　他本以为选的都是近卫，且太子向来与李二郎、李三郎交好， 去找李二郎、李三郎玩耍又不是什么坏事， 不需要太过遮掩。
　　庾俭直到现在， 仍旧不能理解为什么会发生这样的事。
　　李玄霸看出了庾俭的自责。他拍了拍庾俭的肩膀：“不是你的责任， 别自责。”
　　庾俭苦笑。不是自己的责任，那是谁的责任？
　　李世民把杨暕拉到屋里聊天。李玄霸去了厨房一趟，端着茶水和点心进屋。
　　庾俭主动留在屋外为他们守门。
　　李玄霸到的时候，杨暕已经抱怨过一场。
　　虽然李玄霸没能听完杨暕全部的抱怨，也能猜到杨暕此次来道歉的缘由。
　　杨广本来想让他和二哥成为宫廷禁军将领。
　　对于勋贵而言，执掌禁军就是踏上了青云直上的阶梯。如杨广器重过的杨素、长孙晟几人，都曾执掌过禁军。
　　若是李世民和李玄霸执掌禁军，将来不需要再出外冒着危险立功，只要等资历够了直接可拜大将军。
　　但因为杨暕与李世民、李玄霸夜会，杨广以己度人，认为李世民、李玄霸和太子走得太近，便不愿意让李世民和李玄霸进入禁军了。
　　当初杨广还是太子的时候，杨勇已经被废，其他弟弟没有竞争力，他太子之位如此稳固，仍旧将禁军牢牢握在手中，严密监控即将驾崩的隋文帝。这才传出他不是继位，而是篡位的谣言。
　　他曾经做过这样的事，自然就警惕杨暕做同样的事。
　　杨暕十分迷茫。
　　他已经尽全力做一个好太子，对杨广也收敛了以前的骄傲脾气，努力学会谦虚和谨慎。
　　可为什么父皇对他的态度仍旧越来越差。连自己与李二郎、李三郎喝顿酒，父皇都要将李二郎、李三郎外放？
　　虽然旨意上说李世民、李玄霸年少，应该积累经验，把两人安排到边疆是给他们立功的机会。
　　可杨暕在李世民、李玄霸回洛阳前就知道杨广已经属意两人进入禁军。杨广明明将旨意都拟定好了，杨暕还看过。
　　杨暕没有告诉李世民和李玄霸，是想给他们一个惊喜。
　　从宫廷禁军到镇守边镇，其中落差之大，杨暕简直不敢置信。
　　就算杨暕再蠢，也知道这不是敲打李世民和李玄霸，而是敲打自己。何况杨暕其实很聪慧。
　　可他认为自己很聪慧，也怎么也想不透为何父皇会对他这样。
　　杨暕哽咽道：“是我做得太好？我是不是做得不好，父皇就不会忌惮我？”
　　李世民给杨暕递帕子，不知道该如何回答。
　　他从李玄霸那里听过杨暕原本的未来。
　　那时杨暕做得很不好，没当上太子，没培养自己的势力，整个人蠢得一看就知道一点威胁都没有。但那个不好的齐王杨暕，比如今这个优秀的太子杨暕更早被杨广忌惮厌恶。
　　怎么做都是错，这根本不是杨暕的问题。
　　李玄霸叹了口气，拿起一块糕点塞住了杨暕的嘴。
　　杨暕哽咽声一滞，不断眨眼睛。
　　“二表兄，你还记得我和你说过的话吗？”李玄霸面无表情道，“对有些帝王而言，太子，甚至所有成年皇子本身就代表着僭越，和你做得好与不好无关。你做得好，他还没有理由直接罚你，只能像现在这样不断给你施压。若你做得不好，你现在就已经被废了。”
　　李世民忙拉住李玄霸：“弟弟，弟弟哎！别说得这么直，对二表兄温柔点！”
　　杨暕默默把李玄霸塞进嘴里的糕点吃掉。
　　他拿起水杯润了润被噎住的嗓子，垂头丧气道：“我记得。”
　　李世民也给李玄霸的嘴塞了块糕点，让弟弟闭嘴，别再刺激已经很崩溃的二表兄。
　　“二表兄，阿玄话糙理不糙，你想想大表兄曾经也是这样谨小慎微。熬过去就好了，历史中许多太子都是这样熬过去的。”李世民道。
　　杨暕悲怆道：“天家父子就不是父子吗？我什么都没做，他凭什么猜忌我，还连累了对他忠心耿耿的你们？他不仅不慈，还忠奸不辨！”
　　李世民递糕点：“你还是吃糕吧，别说了，再说我怕下次我和阿玄从边境回来，你已经被废了。”
　　杨暕气得拿糕点磨牙泄愤。
　　李玄霸安静地吃糕，杨暕怒气腾腾地吃糕，只有李世民在唉声叹气给两人添茶送水伺候。
　　杨暕和李玄霸分了一盘糕。杨暕抢了大半。
　　吃撑后，杨暕靠在坐榻的靠背上，迷茫道：“这日子什么时候是个头。”
　　李世民一边收拾被杨暕吃得到处都是的糕点碎屑，一边道：“陛下喜欢出游，你只要不在他跟前还是很自由的。这次你别为我和阿玄自责，我和阿玄正好想外放。你想想我家的情况，现在我和阿玄连家都不敢回。还是外放的好。”
　　杨暕皱眉：“李建成又做了什么？”
　　李世民道：“这次李建成自知理亏，倒是还好，就是李元吉闹了起来。哎，这畜生怎么还不早夭！”
　　李玄霸捧着茶杯道：“祸害遗千年。”
　　杨暕手撑在腿上，坐直身体：“快把你们家的糟心事说给我听听。如果你们比我还惨，我就被安慰到了。”
　　李世民骂道：“滚蛋！”
　　李玄霸面无表情：“二哥，揍他！”
　　李世民狞笑着扑上榻，和杨暕滚打起来。李玄霸在一旁毫无感情地给二哥加油。
　　杨暕笑骂道：“你还真来？！去了一趟战场就飘了是吧？？”
　　在门外愁眉苦脸的庾俭听到了门里面的笑声，眉头终于舒展开来。
　　他自言自语：“还好有李二郎李三郎在。”
　　看看废太子杨勇的下场，太子可千万别被陛下施加的压力压垮啊。
　　庾俭想到废太子杨勇，心里更不是滋味。
　　杨勇被废，是因为有当朝皇帝和他争夺太子之位；先皇会磋磨杨勇，是因为他还有好几个成年的儿子。
　　可当今陛下呢？太子是他唯一还活着的成年儿子，也是皇后唯一还活着的儿子。无论怎么想，太子在自身没有错误的时候，这打压猜忌都没有道理。
　　君心真是难测。
　　杨暕在李世民和李玄霸家住了一晚才回去。
　　既然偷偷摸摸见面已经被抓住，那不如堂堂正正地交往。
　　杨暕向杨广告罪，说自己因为李二郎、李三郎成了父皇身边近臣，为免他人说自己结党营私，所以才偷偷去探望。他想茬了。
　　他与李二郎、李三郎是表兄弟，自幼感情深厚。当李二郎和李三郎立功后，他本就该堂堂正正去拜访。这样偷偷摸摸，不仅没了太子的气度，也让李二郎和李三郎被人误会。
　　杨暕装作自省道：“儿本很委屈，自己不过是偷偷翻墙和李二郎李三郎喝顿酒，怎么就被父皇责罚了？以前儿也这么做过，父皇都没说我。二郎三郎劝谏儿，儿现在是太子，不是可以肆意妄为的齐王，一举一动都需要三思。父皇以前不罚我，是因为有大兄在；现在父皇罚我，才是看重我。”
　　杨暕叩首：“儿这才明白父皇的苦心，儿知错了，以后会更加谨言慎行。”
　　杨广欣慰道：“你能醒悟便好。二郎三郎是好孩子，你该多与他们交往，多听他们的劝告。”
　　杨暕点头：“儿会一直对他们好。不过二郎三郎真的很啰嗦，我还是少去为妙。”
　　杨广无奈：“刚夸你，你怎么又……唉，罢了，你还年轻，朕还有时间慢慢教你。”
　　杨暕拿着府中智囊团给的剧本，成功挽回了杨广刚生出的忌惮心。
　　杨暕从此更加谦虚谨慎，在朝中风评也更加好。
　　李世民和李玄霸也得到了赏赐。
　　虽然他们仍旧要前往边镇，但散官品阶又提了一级，成为从四品的通议大夫。虽然职官没有升，但散官品阶才是本阶。本阶自五品后，每爬一步都十分艰难。以两人的年龄和升官的速度，朝中人钦羡不已。
　　按照这种升官速度，李世民和李玄霸就算没有爵位，等他们成婚的时候，也能另开一房，脱离唐国公府了。
　　子嗣单开一房，和子嗣分家是不同的概念。
　　子嗣在父母还在的时候分家是家庭不和睦的行为，会被人耻笑。但子嗣若升任高官，有了爵位，宗族就会在族谱上为他们单开一房。这是家族鼎盛开枝散叶的象征，非常令人羡慕的事。
　　老唐国公李昞的兄弟都很出色，个个都单开一房族谱，当年把其他勋贵羡慕得牙都酸了。
　　可惜那帮李家人有的站错了队，有的后人不行，导致现在李家族人的衰败。
　　看看李世民和李玄霸的本事，唐国公一脉又要兴盛了。
　　李渊在涿郡留守了一段时日，现在才赶回来。
　　他把李元吉暴揍一顿，将李世民和李玄霸接了回来。
　　李渊对窦夫人埋怨：“二郎三郎不是你的儿子吗？你怎么能如此偏心？你要好好和大郎解释。将来二郎三郎成亲后就会单开族谱，不会抢他的唐国公世子之位。他们是大郎将来的助力！”
　　窦夫人哭道：“我说了，我怎么没说？可我说不听啊。我只要稍稍一严厉些，四郎就说当初我抛弃他不慈，说我只对二郎三郎好，对大郎也不慈，还要去大家墓前告我，我能怎么办，我真的管不住……”
　　李渊打断道：“这都要怪你当年，你为何要丢掉四郎？我看四郎现在性情如此古怪，都是因为你当年丢弃了他，让他心中不满的缘故。罢了，家里儿子的事你别管了。他们已经长大，本也不该你再管。你别再插手，好好管好内务。”
　　窦夫人疲惫道：“是。”
　　她本也管不住。
　　在皇帝下旨训斥李建成时，窦夫人才知道李建成居然派人去训斥二郎三郎，竟然要二郎三郎领兵去荥阳。
