### Chapter 103: Slowly Dismantling a Mother’s Heart

Although Li Xuanba’s health had improved significantly, Lady Dou remained worried about him and had been staying in the adjacent courtyard.

When the commotion broke out, Lady Dou immediately threw on a robe and hurried over to see what was happening.

Upon seeing Li Yuanji surrounded in the courtyard, her voice rose in alarm: "Fourth Son? Why are you here?"

Li Yuanji was dodging the wings of Han Gou, which were flapping against his face, and shrieked, "Kill this feathered beast for me!"

Han Gou took flight, swooped down, and delivered a resounding slap to both sides of his face.

Having learned from its master for so long, Han Gou often helped him discipline disobedient subordinates and had long since mastered the art of striking people without causing actual injury.

Li Xuanba also draped a robe over his shoulders and stepped out of his room, barefoot.

He leaned against the doorframe, coughing, "What, what happened? *Cough, cough...*"

Lady Dou’s attention immediately shifted from Li Yuanji to Li Xuanba.

She hurried over in a panic: "Third Son, it’s so cold, why did you come out? Go back... and you—why are you barefoot!"

Li Xuanba said, "Mother, I heard Fourth Brother’s voice... *cough, cough*, Han Gou, come back!"

Han Gou brought its talons close to Li Yuanji’s face, making a gesture as if it were about to gouge out his eyes.

Li Yuanji screamed, and just as he stood up, he collapsed back onto the ground.

Han Gou retracted its talons, landed at Li Xuanba’s feet, and crouched down, shielding Li Xuanba’s feet beneath its warm, fluffy belly.

The corners of Li Xuanba’s mouth curled up involuntarily, but he immediately pulled them down, feigning confusion.

"What is going on? Why is everyone gathered in Third Son’s courtyard?" Li Yuan arrived in a rush.

Li Yuan also lived nearby; only Li Jiancheng lived a bit further away. However, Li Jiancheng did not seem to have gone to bed yet, so he had heard the commotion earlier than Li Yuan. Just as Li Yuan arrived, Li Jiancheng also came running, holding up the hem of his robe.

"Why is Fourth Brother in Third Brother’s courtyard... A knife?!" As Li Jiancheng went to help Li Yuanji up, he saw something reflecting the torchlight at Li Yuanji’s feet. He reached out to pick it up and shouted, "Li Yuanji! Why did you bring a knife into Third Son’s courtyard!"

Li Yuan walked over and took the knife into his hand: "Li Yuanji, explain why you brought a knife to Third Son’s courtyard."

Li Yuanji looked puzzled: "It wasn't me! I didn't bring a knife!"

Li Yuan examined the knife and frowned at Li Jiancheng: "This knife... why is it yours?"

Li Jiancheng was struck with horror.

The short blade had no scabbard, and he had only noticed it was a knife, not its appearance. It was only when he saw the gemstone inlaid in the hilt that he recognized it as his own.

Li Jiancheng immediately explained: "Father, please let me take a closer look... This knife is mine, but yesterday Fourth Brother said he liked it, so I gave it to him."

His expression turned dazed, as if he had realized something, and he suddenly turned his head to glare at Li Yuanji: "You wanted to frame me?!"

Li Yuanji was even more terrified: "No, I didn't, I just..."

He stammered, not knowing how to answer.

Lady Dou’s expression was cold; she did not participate in the interrogation.

She tied the cloak she was wearing onto the thinly clad Li Xuanba: "Third Son, go back."

Li Xuanba shook his head: "Mother, no matter what Fourth Brother intended to do, this matter cannot be blown out of proportion. Han Gou, move aside."

Han Gou looked up: "Chirp!"

Li Xuanba gently tapped Han Gou’s fluffy belly with the top of his foot: "Move aside."

Han Gou sighed: "Chirp."

It swayed from side to side and moved away from Li Xuanba’s feet.

Li Xuanba said to Lady Dou, who was blocking his path, "Mother, please trust me."

Lady Dou touched Li Xuanba’s face, and the icy chill from his skin made her heart ache.

She withdrew her hand: "Go on, finish what you need to do and return quickly. And someone, bring Third Young Master’s shoes at once!"

The servants, who had been stunned into silence, finally began to move.

Li Xuanba did not wait for the servants to bring his shoes; he stepped across the cold stone floor to the three father and sons standing in confrontation.

"Father, please send the servants away and question Fourth Brother tomorrow." Li Xuanba bowed to Li Yuan, "His Majesty is currently hesitating over what official position to grant you. At such a critical juncture, we cannot let any negative rumors spread, *cough, cough*."

Li Yuan turned his gaze toward Li Xuanba.

He looked into Li Xuanba’s eyes through the firelight.

Li Xuanba’s expression was filled with undisguised self-mockery and sorrow.

Seeing that Li Yuan did not answer, Li Xuanba continued, "Father, I am fine. Let this matter pass. Fourth Brother is still young; he was merely playing a prank and wandering at night, only to be discovered."

Li Yuan threw the short knife hard onto the ground and turned to the servants: "Are you all dead? Where are the shoes?"

He also draped his own heavy cloak over Li Xuanba.

"It is freezing, why did you come out? What if you fall ill again?" Li Yuan lowered his head and picked Li Xuanba up.

Li Xuanba was startled: "Fa-Father, I am already grown up!"

Li Yuan said, "You are not grown up yet. You are so light, lighter than Fourth... lighter than Fifth Son."

Li Yuan half-carried, half-supported the dumbfounded Li Xuanba back to his bedroom and ordered the servants to bring hot water for him to soak his feet.

"Lock Li Yuanji in the ancestral hall, and lock all the servants who attend to him in the woodshed," Li Yuan commanded in a deep voice. "The servants are lazy, allowing the Fourth Young Master to wander at night and encounter danger. Lady, take good care of Third Son; I will handle the rest."

Lady Dou said, "Yes, my lord."

Li Yuan said, "Eldest Son, go back and get some rest. This matter has nothing to do with you; you need not worry."

Li Jiancheng breathed a sigh of relief. He shot a fierce glare at Li Yuanji and bowed, "Yes, Father. Third Brother, rest well; I will come to visit you tomorrow."

Li Xuanba, soaking his feet on the couch, bowed to Li Jiancheng: "Safe travels, Brother. *Cough, cough...*"

Li Xuanba had caught a chill, and once he started coughing, he couldn't stop.

Li Yuan went to instruct the servants and guards who had gathered, and to deal with Li Yuanji’s entourage. Lady Dou had the servants brew the cough-suppressing herbal tea he usually drank. Seeing that Li Xuanba continued to cough even after drinking the tea, she hurriedly summoned the resident physician.

The physician treated Li Xuanba throughout the night, concluding that he was "frightened" and had "caught a chill," and prescribed medicine for him.

Only after drinking the medicine did Li Xuanba fall into a deep sleep.

Lady Dou stroked Li Xuanba’s face, her eyes filled with both confusion and heartache.

Based on her understanding of Third Son, he was so intelligent that he would not have easily let Li Yuanji sneak into the courtyard. But even if Third Son had intentionally created the opportunity for Li Yuanji, wasn't it Li Yuanji himself who wanted to come over to scare, or even harm, Third Son?!

"What kind of sin have I committed to have a son like him!" Lady Dou sobbed softly.

...

After taking the medicine, Li Xuanba slept until noon the next day.

When he woke up, the physician was wiping sweat from his brow. It turned out he had run a small fever while he slept.

Li Xuanba felt a bit of regret.

Although catching a minor cold was part of his plan, he seemed to have been a bit too arrogant about his physical condition. He had thought his illness was long gone and that standing in the cold wind for a while wouldn't be a problem, yet he had spiked a fever again.

He would have to be more careful with his body in the future.

Upon learning that Li Xuanba had a fever again, not only was Li Yuan extremely anxious and worried, but Li Jiancheng’s concern was also more sincere than before.

Li Xuanba drank some meat porridge and fell into a deep sleep, only to wake up to drink bitter medicine and then sleep again.

This cycle repeated for another day before Li Xuanba’s cough finally subsided.

Looking at Li Xuanba’s pale cheeks, both Li Yuan and Lady Dou were heartbroken.

Li Yuan had also moved to the adjacent courtyard to stay with Lady Dou.

He sat on the couch, his tone heavy: "I now believe that Li Yuanji really did provoke the Eldest Son."

Lady Dou remained silent.

Li Yuan said, "I carefully questioned the conversation between the Eldest Son and Li Yuanji, and interrogated the servants around Li Yuanji. Li Yuanji was indeed intentionally inciting the Eldest Son. To think the Eldest Son could be incited by a nine-year-old child!"

Lady Dou sighed softly.

Li Yuan stood up and bowed to Lady Dou: "It was I who wronged you, having been deceived by Li Yuanji’s cuteness. I apologize to you."

Lady Dou shook her head and supported Li Yuan’s hand: "We are husband and wife; why speak of apologies? Even I refused to believe that Li Yuanji could have such malicious thoughts at such a young age."

Lady Dou sighed again and said, "As long as Second Son and Third Son are outstanding enough, they have no conflict of interest with the Eldest Son. The Eldest Son will inherit the title of Duke of Tang, while the Second and Third Sons will establish their own branches, just like the lord’s cousin. But in Li Yuanji’s eyes, he does not want the Second and Third Sons to be too outstanding. I originally thought he was too young to see this, but I didn't expect this child... to be truly intelligent."

Li Yuan gritted his teeth: "Is this intelligence? It’s just malicious, petty cleverness."

Li Yuanji’s methods were not sophisticated; he simply relied on his young age, assuming his parents would not suspect him.

In this respect, he was the same as the former Li Xuanba. It was just that Li Xuanba was more subtle, mostly leveraging existing situations rather than stepping forward himself. Li Yuanji, however, acted directly.

When Li Xuanba was suspected, others could not find any evidence linking him to the events. When Li Yuanji aroused suspicion, a single investigation revealed everything.

After Li Yuan interrogated the servants around Li Yuanji, he rooted out several people who had been feeding Li Yuanji bad ideas.

Servants all wanted to climb the social ladder and gain their master’s favor. Whatever the master was like, there would inevitably be a group of sycophants around him.

These people would not keep their mouths shut when facing death. In their terror, they often added fuel to the fire.

Some things Li Yuanji had indeed done, while others he hadn't, or hadn't done with malicious intent. But in the mouths of the servants, these all became evil deeds actively committed by Li Yuanji.

To them, Li Yuanji was overly cunning and malicious, sounding nothing like a nine-year-old child.

Li Yuan should have been suspicious, but remembering that he himself had inherited the title of Duke at seven, and that his Second and Third sons had used their own intelligence to seek official positions at nine, it didn't seem too surprising that Li Yuanji had such a mind at nine.

The only difference was that he and his Second and Third sons used their intelligence for proper matters, while Li Yuanji used his for evil.

As for Li Jiancheng, although he was innocent in this matter, Li Yuan’s evaluation of him in his heart dropped a notch.

Li Jiancheng had been carefully cultivated by him and his mother for so many years, yet he could still be used as a tool by a nine-year-old child!

"If it weren't for Han Gou protecting its master, I don't know what would have happened," Li Yuan said angrily. "Li Yuanji said he only used stones to scare Third Son and didn't intend to use the knife; he just carried it with him, and it was knocked away by Han Gou. But even using stones... sigh!"

Li Yuan couldn't continue.

Li Yuanji was, after all, his son, and the youngest legitimate son he had once doted on. Now that he suddenly realized Li Yuanji was a "bad seed," Li Yuan couldn't believe it, even though he had seen it with his own eyes.

Lady Dou said, "This matter must not be publicized. If it gets out, I don't know if His Majesty will blame us again. The lord is only a few steps away from being appointed Grand General; we cannot let this matter delay it."

Li Yuan sighed: "Fortunately, Third Son persuaded us in time. At that moment, I really wanted to ignore everything and beat Li Yuanji up!"

Lady Dou said, "Third Son is already an official, after all; he sees through His Majesty very clearly."

Li Yuan sighed again: "Indeed. In terms of fathoming His Majesty’s thoughts, I am not his equal. I don't know why Third Son is so sharp."

Lady Dou gave a bitter smile: "Need you ask? Third Son has been sickly since childhood, and he is too kind-hearted to bear letting his family worry, so he often observes our expressions and pretends to be fine to put our minds at ease. Now, he is simply applying the skills he practiced since childhood to His Majesty."

Li Yuan recalled how Li Xuanba looked when he was young and nodded: "He was exceptionally patient when he was little, unwilling to let us worry. Second Son would often act like a spoiled child in my arms, while he would just watch silently from the side."

Lady Dou thought to herself, *That doesn't seem to have anything to do with not wanting to worry you.*

However, she still agreed: "That is so."

Li Yuan patted Lady Dou’s arm: "It is fortunate we have Second Son and Third Son. Sigh, although Fifth Son is not your son, you should still cultivate him well. As for Li Yuanji... I will try again."

After Li Yuan finished speaking, he gave a bitter smile: "As parents, it’s not as if one can just give up. He is only nine; perhaps there is still hope."

Lady Dou said, "Yes, my lord."

After Li Yuan finished discussing Li Yuanji with Lady Dou, he moved Li Zhiyun to the vicinity of Lady Dou’s courtyard.

Lady Wan felt very bitter inside.

But she still packed everything for Li Zhiyun and said to him with a smile, "This is a good thing. You must listen well to the Lady."

Li Zhiyun was not in high spirits: "Yes, My Lady."

Hearing Li Zhiyun call her "My Lady" made Lady Wan’s eyes redden.

She pulled Li Zhiyun into her arms: "Good child, you must continue to be close to your Second and Third brothers in the future."

Li Zhiyun said, "I know."

Lady Wan added, "Although you should be close to them, do not deliberately curry favor. They are very sharp people. The way you get along now is very good; only sincerity can be exchanged for sincerity. They are truly sincere in their kindness to you, and you must sincerely respect them."

Li Zhiyun said, "I know, My Lady, please rest assured."

Lady Wan released her embrace and touched Li Zhiyun’s hair: "Good child, if you are wronged, tell me. Even the lord and the Lady will give me some face."

Li Zhiyun tried his best to grin: "I am very smart; I won't be wronged."

Lady Wan also tried to smile: "Yes, I believe in Fifth Son."

When Lady Wan sent Li Zhiyun away, Lady Dou came to Lady Wan’s courtyard and sat for a while.

Lady Dou said, "I used to want Li Yuanji and Little Five to be closer, hoping Little Five would lead Li Yuanji to get along well with Second and Third Sons."

Lady Wan lowered her head: "Lady, Fourth Son is the younger brother of Second and Third Sons; it is only right for you to do so."

Lady Dou sighed: "Second Son heard this and said that if I wanted to force Fourth Son on him, he would have Third Son take Little Five, and he would take Fourth Son alone."

Lady Wan looked up in astonishment.

Lady Dou held Lady Wan’s hand: "Second and Third Sons truly cherish Little Five. Rest assured, with them around, Little Five will be fine even if he is resented by Fourth Son. Although Little Five has moved out of your courtyard, I will have him come to see you often."

Lady Wan shed tears and choked up: "Thank you, Lady. You have worked hard."

Lady Dou said, "As parents, who doesn't work hard? You should also visit Third Son more often. I have to manage the entire household and cannot accompany him often. You go and keep an eye on the people around him; he must not catch a cold again."

Lady Wan hurriedly said, "Yes, I will definitely take good care of Third Young Master."

Lady Dou smiled: "Little Five has two mothers, and so do Second and Third Sons."

Lady Wan felt a warmth in her heart.

After Lady Dou comforted Lady Wan, she stood in the light snow and let out a long sigh.

The brotherly harmony and family peace she wanted seemed destined never to be realized.

She couldn't expect Second and Third Sons to be oppressed forever and never fight back.

Lady Dou brushed the light snow from her hair and shoulders and returned to Li Xuanba’s small courtyard.

Li Xuanba was leaning against Han Gou, holding a hand warmer, and reading a book of poetry.

Lady Dou said worriedly, "Third Son, your illness hasn't fully recovered; don't strain your mind."

Li Xuanba looked up: "It’s just reading poetry; it doesn't strain my mind. Mother, may I have a private word with you?"

Lady Dou laughed: "You are so grown up, yet you still have secrets."

She turned and ordered: "You all step down and close the doors tightly."

The servants retreated and closed the doors and windows.

Old Madam Zhang stood guard at the door, watching to ensure no one approached.

Li Xuanba said, "Mother, I knew Li Yuanji would come, which is why I had Han Gou keep watch."

Lady Dou stroked Han Gou’s bird head and said, "Mother guessed as much."

Li Xuanba said, "People like Li Yuanji fear power but do not cherish virtue; only when he is hurt will he dare not cause trouble."

Lady Dou took a deep breath and said, "Indeed."

Li Xuanba continued, "Mother, when Second Brother and I were suppressing bandits in Qinghe Commandery, we witnessed such a tragedy. Someone poisoned the village well, killing dozens of people."

Lady Dou frowned: "So malicious? What was the grievance?"

Li Xuanba shook his head: "No grievance; it was just a seven-year-old child who poisoned it for fun."

Lady Dou’s eyes widened in surprise.

Li Xuanba said, "I heard that when the child was two or three and just learning to walk, he liked to pull the wings off butterflies, and as he grew older, he would strangle chicks and ducklings with his own hands. By six or seven, he often bullied children younger than himself. His parents were honest people and had beaten him several times for it. This time, he poisoned the well because he had been beaten by his parents again, so he poisoned the well they drank from."

Lady Dou was puzzled: "This... a child, where did he get the poison? How could it kill a whole village?"

Li Xuanba: "..." *Oops, forgot there was no pesticide back then.*

This incident had indeed happened, but in the modern era.

Li Xuanba said solemnly, "The child’s family were hunters, and they had just prepared medicine to poison wild boars. If a wild boar ate this medicine, as long as you didn't eat the internal organs, the meat was not poisonous. Farmers often used this medicine when defending against wild boars coming down from the mountains."

Lady Dou said, "I see. He actually stole the medicine for poisoning wild animals from his home."

Lady Dou had grown up in the inner courtyard and didn't know much about the outside world. Since Li Xuanba said so, she believed him.

Lady Dou sighed: "To think there is such a malicious child."

She roughly guessed what Li Xuanba was trying to persuade her of with this story.

Li Xuanba, as Lady Dou had guessed, continued: "There is a sage who says, 'At birth, human nature is good.' There is also a sage who says, 'At birth, human nature is evil.' In my observation of the world, human nature at birth is both good and evil, like a mass of chaos that requires upbringing to determine good and evil."

Lady Dou gave a bitter smile: "Third Son, are you trying to say that Fourth Son is a born villain?"

Li Xuanba said, "Mother, when you abandoned Li Yuanji, it was I who picked him up."

Lady Dou’s face turned pale.

Abandoning her child had burdened her with a heavy moral weight; it was her eternal heartache.

Li Xuanba said, "Mother is very kind to all children; even those not born to you, you treat them equally. Doesn't Mother find it strange why you are uniquely fearful of Li Yuanji? I also tried to befriend Li Yuanji, and this time I tried my best to teach him. After I failed, I couldn't help but wonder: when Mother abandoned Li Yuanji, was it an instinctive act of self-preservation? Like an animal encountering a natural predator?"

He gave a bitter laugh and said, "Even if I hadn't picked Li Yuanji up, the servants would surely have done so. I originally wanted to hide this to prevent Mother from carrying the psychological burden. Who knew Grandmother would find out? If only I had been more cautious."

Li Xuanba had personally gone to pick up Li Yuanji, not only because he wanted to befriend him at the time and isolate Li Jiancheng and Li Yuan with his brothers, but also because he knew that if this became public, it would be a huge blow to his mother’s reputation, and he wanted to suppress it. Who knew Old Madam Dugu would disregard the reputation of the Tang Duke’s mansion just to seize power and publicize it.

Generally speaking, such family scandals were meant to be kept within the house.

Lady Dou was in a trance.

She hadn't heard the latter part of Li Xuanba’s words.

The question, "Why are you uniquely fearful of Li Yuanji?" echoed in her ears.

Yes, why was she close to all the other children, yet only felt disgust and fear toward Li Yuanji?

Although Lady Dou was a good person, she was also an ordinary person with weaknesses in her heart. When ordinary people face a moral burden that has caused them pain for too long, they inevitably look for excuses for themselves.

*Could it be that it wasn't my fault? Could it be that he was actually at fault?*

Especially those who like to bully others love to find such excuses. That was why Li Xuanba hadn't originally intended to persuade his mother this way.

His mother had always upheld a high moral standard, and he didn't want to tempt her to stain her moral character.

But seeing his mother’s pain, Li Xuanba changed his mind.

If upholding high moral standards made his mother suffer, then it was better for her not to be a moral paragon.

Li Xuanba didn't know if his words could break his mother’s moral defenses, but he had planted a seed in her heart. When Li Yuanji made her suffer again, perhaps she could use this seed to break free from the thorny wall built by "maternal love" and "morality."

Li Xuanba knew it wasn't the time yet. With his mother’s high moral sense, she certainly wouldn't abandon her morality just because of his words of excuse.

To prevent his mother from using her moral sense to re-persuade herself, Li Xuanba changed the subject again.

"Mother, look at this book of poetry," Li Xuanba said. "These are poems sung by the farmers who have risen in rebellion."

Lady Dou was in a daze, and Li Xuanba placed the book of poetry into her hands.

This book had been re-edited by many leaders and strategists of the peasant uprising, and the first page contained the cruel "Lament of the Vegetable People."

Lady Dou was a person with deep empathy. After reading only the preface before the poem, her hands trembled and tears fell. She completely cast her own affairs to the back of her mind; her eyes and heart were filled only with these blood-stained verses.

It took Lady Dou a long time to finish reading the short poem.

With every line she read, she felt unable to bear it and had to look away, only continuing after calming her heart.

After finishing, Lady Dou looked up, crying uncontrollably: "Is this true? Is what is written in the poem true?"

Li Xuanba said calmly, "Since His Majesty ascended the throne, there has been endless corvée labor every year. Last year there was a flood, this year a drought, yet His Majesty refuses to stop the conquest of Goguryeo. The people are already in unbearable misery. This is true. Eldest Brother was originally in Zhuojun with Father, and he returned home sick because he couldn't bear to see such misery. If it is like this even near Zhuojun, let alone the disaster-stricken areas of Shandong."

Lady Dou stroked the book of poetry: "The people outside are already in such dire straits."

She thought sadly, *It is a pity that I am a woman; I can only offer empty sympathy and cannot do anything else.*

Li Xuanba asked, "Mother, when you were young, did you ever say, 'I only hate that I am not a man, unable to save my uncle’s family from danger'?"

Lady Dou’s expression changed drastically: "Dade! Where did you hear that! Do not speak nonsense!"

Li Xuanba said, "So it is true."

Lady Dou said in a panic, "No, I did not..."

Li Xuanba said, "Mother, look at this Great Sui; does it not already show signs of collapse?"

Lady Dou’s defensive voice came to an abrupt halt.

The mother and son remained silent for a long time. The room was so quiet that even the sound of their heartbeats was as loud as thunder.

Lady Dou counted her heartbeats, her hands trembling for a long time before she suddenly clenched her fists.

"Third Son, you and Second Son..." Lady Dou’s voice was hoarse, "Do not act recklessly."

Li Xuanba said, "My brother and I will not act recklessly; we are merely accumulating strength. I see that Father already has ambition, and many nobles in the court have ambition as well. The chaotic times are coming. Mother, you must take care of yourself. If you torture yourself because of people who don't care about you, and you don't live to see the day when your great vengeance is avenged, wouldn't that be a pity?"

Lady Dou’s expression shifted constantly. Uncle, aunt, cousins, father, mother, brothers... those figures she had tried so hard to forget appeared in her mind one by one.

Her uncle’s entire family had been wiped out, her parents and brothers had all died, leaving only her in this world.

She looked as if she were laughing, crying, and angry all at once, and then she reached out and pulled hard on her third son’s cheek.

Li Xuanba felt the pain: "Ouch!"

Han Gou immediately used its wings to support its body and stood up.

Lady Dou looked at Han Gou: "What, you want to protect Dade?"

Han Gou glanced at its mother, then at its mother’s mother, retracted its wings, sat back down, and turned its head away.

Lady Dou laughed: "It really has become a spirit."

She released her hand from Li Xuanba’s face: "Dade, do you know what you are saying? Why are you telling me this?"

Li Xuanba held his face and said, "I just want Mother to shift your focus from the inner courtyard to the world. Mother regrets being a woman, feeling there is little you can do. But if our family rebels, Mother’s inner courtyard will expand to the entire world, and then there will be much more you can do. Mother, think of the beautiful future."

"Beautiful..." Lady Dou didn't know whether to laugh or cry. The world is in chaos, the Tang Duke’s mansion is rebelling, and you call that beautiful?

Lady Dou had never known that one could persuade someone like this.

*Mother, don't be angry at Fourth Brother, because the world is about to be in chaos, and our family is about to rebel.*

*Is that how you persuade someone?!*

Lady Dou realized that she didn't seem to understand this son as well as she had thought.

"Burn this book of poetry; leave no traces, and do not let your father see it," Lady Dou said sternly. "Once His Majesty knows about the poems in this book, he will surely be furious. Everyone who hides this book will be guilty."

Li Xuanba said, "Yes, Mother." He naturally knew this, but he had taken the risk today for his mother’s sake.

Lady Dou hesitated for a moment and lowered her voice: "Although you say your father already has rebellious intentions, I see he hasn't thought that far yet. Do not let him know of your and Second Son’s plans, lest he be foolish and report you."

Li Xuanba said, "Yes. We will be careful."

Lady Dou hesitated again, gritted her teeth, and said, "I will find a way for you and Second Son to take Little Five with you. Teach him well. Little Five is very intelligent and will surely become your right-hand man in the future."

Li Xuanba was surprised.

*Mother’s transformation is too fast, isn't it?!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第104章 血亲仇高于一切
chunks.chineseText:
第104章 血亲仇高于一切

窦夫人离开时， 脚步都是飘着的。
　　她借口受了凉，早早睡下。
　　窦夫人本以为自己会辗转反侧，难以入眠， 没想到刚沾枕头就入睡了。
　　睡着后， 她做了一个已经十几年未做过的梦。
　　梦中的她趴在舅父的怀里。舅父的话她听不太清楚， 但她笑得很开心。
　　舅父起身，牵着她的手迈过高高的门槛，走出宽广的宫殿大门。
　　父亲母亲正在门外迎接她。
　　兄长从父亲母亲身后跳出来， 吓了她一跳。
　　父亲挽起衣袖，握紧拳头，气势汹汹地捶兄长的头。
　　兄长抱头鼠窜， 一边逃跑一边回头对她做鬼脸。
　　小小的自己跳着拍掌笑，好似在为兄长鼓劲。
　　母亲俯身为她理了理衣服， 又转头和舅父笑着说了几句话。
　　然后兄长被父亲押了回来， 自己牵着母亲的手，转身向舅父告别。
　　“等舅父亲征回来，就有空为你寻个好夫婿了。”
　　“唉？我女儿年纪还小，寻夫婿的事还早。再说了，为女儿寻夫婿是我身为父亲的责任。”
　　“朕的命令， 现在这责任是朕的了。”
　　“陛下，你不能这样！夫人， 你劝劝陛下！”
　　“噗……都行，都行。可以先寻着，晚点再出门。我的女儿这么好， 不能太早去别人家， 我心疼， 至少留到十七八岁再出阁。”
　　“夫人所言极是。”
　　“朕也这么想。”
　　小小的自己羞红了脸， 双手捂着脸不愿说话。
　　窦夫人的意识与小小的自己抽离。她冷眼看着这一幕，居然连眼泪都没有落下。
　　她记起这一幕是自己与舅父最后一次见面。
　　舅父即将御驾出征，所以把养在宫中的自己送回母亲手中。
　　她目送意气风发的舅父率领大军离去，谁知道这一别竟然是永别。
　　表兄的皇帝做得很差很差，她早就料到了舅父家的皇位会岌岌可危。
　　她唯一没有料到的是，杨坚居然不顾舅父对他的恩情，将舅父家族中无论近亲远亲所有男丁全部斩杀殆尽。
　　窦夫人从小在宫廷生活。她明白皇权争斗的残酷。
　　表兄的荒诞让他丢掉了皇位。杨坚篡位自立，这是没办法的事。
　　杨坚要杀掉舅父的子嗣，也是没办法的事。
　　她愤怒悲伤，却也难以说杨坚的不是。
　　但她万万没想到，舅父家族所有男丁都难逃厄运。
　　这有必要吗？
　　杨坚连陈朝等他国皇子都能养在宫中，给舅父留一两支远方支脉，并不会威胁他的皇位。
　　这是他皇位来的太容易，心虚吧？
　　窦夫人只能这么想。
　　那时她最害怕的是父母过度的紧张。
　　无论是哪朝哪代的更替，祸都不及已经出嫁的女眷。何况杨坚是篡位，朝中权力基本没有更替。窦家曾经是北周的支柱勋贵之一，现在也是大隋的支柱勋贵之一。
　　乱世朝代更替很频繁，父亲也是跨越几朝的老臣。只要旗帜鲜明的站在皇帝对立面上，改朝换代后，皇帝一般不会清算前朝老臣。
　　所以窦夫人本以为，父母只是忧虑过度。
　　整个窦家都选择了杨坚，他们一家又有什么本事威胁杨坚的统治？父亲母亲在杨坚篡位时也只是明哲保身，没有做过反对杨坚的事。所以杨坚应该顶多只会冷落他们而已。
　　父母早早让她出嫁，窦夫人满心不舍，但也没想到她的未来会有多差。
　　而后父亲官职高升，兄长也被委以重任外放为官，窦夫人真的以为一家人就这么熬过来了。
　　虽然她心里记着舅父的仇恨，但也只能记着。自己一家人更重要。
　　一家人……她的父母，她的舅母，全部都在开皇二年这一年间先后辞世。袭爵的兄长窦招贤也随即英年早逝，连子嗣都没留下。
　　她其余两个兄长窦照和窦文殊，早在隋代北周前已经逝世。转瞬之间，她就变成了无父无母无兄弟的孤女。
　　所有人都说这是碰巧。
　　所有人都这么说。
　　夫家这么说，窦家这么说，全天下的人都这么说。
　　连家中她最信任的医师也这么说，父母只是病逝，兄长也是病逝。
　　或许是真的碰巧吧。
　　或许真的只是碰巧吧。
　　碰巧，碰巧，碰巧……碰巧碰巧碰巧碰巧碰巧……真的只是碰巧。
　　窦夫人戴上面具，遮住了流泪的脸。
　　只是碰巧。
　　她的亲人碰巧在自己刚出嫁不久，碰巧在杨坚篡位刚篡位不久全部去世。
　　她没有仇恨。她只是福薄。
　　窦夫人从梦中惊醒。
　　她摸了一下脸，居然做这样的梦也没有流泪。
　　窦夫人起床时，仆人告诉她，唐国公担心打扰她休息，所以去了别处下榻。
　　她松了一口气，披着衣服起身，提着灯笼去了库房。
　　库房中的嫁妆不仅是嫁妆。在父母去世后，兄长离世后，因兄长没有子嗣，兄长病逝前留下遗言，将所有财产都赠与自己。
　　杨坚在这方面做得很“仁慈大度”，没有插手臣子的家产分配。他一直是这样一副敦厚的长者姿态，舅父才很信任看重他。
　　家中东西很多，为避免别人眼红，窦夫人将家中能变卖的都变卖了，只留下了一些家人的墨迹作为念想。
　　但她出嫁这么多年，来看这些墨迹的时间寥寥无几。近十几年来，更是一次都没有。
　　窦夫人摊开一卷画。
　　画不怎么样。父亲的画真的不怎么样。
　　画中有母亲的题诗，有兄长的印章，还有舅父那稍显浮夸的夸赞。
　　舅父这么夸了，父亲就信了他的画真的很好，所以对这幅“代表作”很是宝贝。
　　窦夫人摸着已经泛黄的纸卷，嘴角上翘想笑一笑，嘴角扯了扯却笑不出来。
　　她哭不出来，也笑不出来。
　　库房里只有窦夫人一人，其他人都被她安排在了门外，所以她可以自言自语。
　　“天下啊……如果他们争夺的不仅仅是唐国公，那么兄弟阋墙就难免了。”窦夫人自言自语，“不仅是兄弟阋墙，还是不死不休。”
　　窦夫人睡了一觉起来，恢复了理智思考。
　　她立刻猜到了那个惨绝的未来。
　　但不知道为何，她嘴里说着担心害怕，心里却毫无波澜。
　　窦夫人合上画卷，双手捂住脸，眼泪终于从指缝中溢出。
　　“原来我不是一个好母亲。”
　　原来只要能报仇，她，夫君，儿子……一切的一切，她都可以放在报仇之后。
　　好想报仇啊。
　　耶耶，娘娘，阿兄，舅舅……我想报仇。
　　二郎三郎要为你们报仇了。
　　我能报仇了。
　　我能报仇了！
　　窦夫人放下双手，眼泪仍旧从眼角不断低落，但嘴角却翘得很高。
　　开心和伤心混杂在一起的表情，是那么扭曲。
　　……
　　李玄霸感觉母亲变了一些，但好像又是错觉。
　　母亲还是对所有人都那么慈祥，将唐国公里的事处理得井井有条。
　　她仍旧对所有孩子一视同仁。若有差别，大概是对李智云更亲近了一些。
　　是错觉吗？李玄霸挠头。
　　很快，李玄霸就没法在意这些细微的不协调了。因为他哥回来了。
　　李世民气势汹汹回来，吓得出门迎接的李玄霸转身就跑。
　　李渊茫然，他对李建成道：“大德跑什么？”
　　李建成也很茫然：“不知道啊。”
　　只有窦夫人在捂嘴笑，轻声叹了句“活该”。
　　李世民见李玄霸转身就跑，从马背上翻身下来，大喊一声：“父亲母亲大兄小五你们稍等，我先去把阿玄揍一顿！”
　　李渊阻拦不及，看着二儿子一个猫腰从自己手臂下钻过去，朝着三儿子追去。
　　李渊喊道：“大雄！你做什么！大德身体不好，不能这么跑！哎！”
　　他赶紧追上去。
　　李建成挠头。
　　这个动作倒让他很像是李世民和李玄霸的兄长了。
　　“母亲，大雄这是什么了？”李建成不解。
　　窦夫人忍住笑，道：“大概是知道三郎又病了一场，生气三郎不照顾好自己。”
　　李建成哭笑不得：“这还能生气？三郎生病难道还是三郎的错了？”
　　他也跟上去劝李世民停手。
　　知道李元吉这个弟弟的恶毒后，李玄霸又仍旧对他恭恭敬敬，李建成把自己心中对二弟三弟的嫉妒芥蒂放下，认认真真想当个好兄长。这正是展现兄弟之情的好时候。
　　与李世民、李玄霸关系最好的李智云则把双手放在嘴边高喊：“二兄快跑！不要被父亲追上！一定要好好教训三兄！”
　　窦夫人笑着点了点李智云的脑袋：“怎么不去保护你的三兄？”
　　李智云放下手，摇头晃脑地笑道：“二兄对三兄一直很纵容，如果三兄把二兄惹生气了，那一定是三兄真的做了很过分的事。虽然我不知道三兄做了什么。”
　　窦夫人笑道：“聪明。”
　　她牵起李智云的手，慢悠悠往李玄霸逃跑的方向走。
　　等窦夫人重新见到李世民和李玄霸的时候，李世民已经把李玄霸按着一顿揍完，正扯着李玄霸的脸咆哮，李玄霸的帽子都掉了，十分狼狈。
　　李渊和李建成在一旁试图劝说，但李世民气势汹汹的模样，让这父子二人都有点犹豫该不该阻止。
　　看二郎这么生气，是不是三郎真的做了什么坏事？
　　窦夫人叹了口气，按住李世民：“好了，多唠叨几句就行，怎么还动手了。你弟弟本就体弱，能经得住你几拳头？”
　　“哼。”李世民松开李玄霸，“等会儿继续训你。”
　　李玄霸躲到窦夫人身后。这时候他顾不上脸面了。二哥的拳头是真的疼啊，我的背……
　　李智云蹑手蹑脚走到李玄霸背后，在李玄霸捂着的地方一戳。
　　“嗷！”李玄霸跳了起来，“小五！”
　　“嘻嘻嘻。”李智云躲到了李世民身后。
　　李玄霸无语。怎么都欺负自己？
　　他看向没用的父亲和李建成。你们别光顾着耍嘴皮子，好歹动手拦一下啊。
　　没用的父亲和李建成对李玄霸耸肩，表示无能为力。
　　“父亲、母亲、兄长，我回来了。”李世民现在才规规矩矩行礼，“小五，我回来了。功课有好好做吗？”
　　李智云脸色一垮：“好好做了，做的可好了。我又不是二兄你，常常玩得忘记做功课……哎哟。”
　　李世民敲了一下李智云的脑袋。
　　李智云抱着头和揉着脸的三兄站在一起。
　　都是被二兄欺负的小可怜弟弟，一起挤挤。
　　李玄霸瞥了李智云一眼，也敲了李智云的脑袋一下。
　　李智云只好躲到了窦夫人的身边。
　　李渊看足了李世民欺负弟弟的笑话，才笑道：“好了，别一回来就欺负人。快去梳洗换衣服，你身上的酸臭味把我都熏着了，你这是几天没洗澡？”
　　李世民道：“我得到阿玄又病了的消息，立刻就骑马赶回来，哪还顾得上洗澡。而且这也不算臭，比起上过战场后，这点味道算什么。”
　　李渊道：“行行行，你说得对，快去洗澡。”
　　“哦。”李世民乖乖去洗澡换衣服。
　　等他洗漱完毕，把湿漉漉的头发用布一裹，再次拉着李玄霸算账。
　　李玄霸举起双手投降：“我承认，我是故意把你支开。你如果在家里，李元吉不敢针对我。”
　　李世民皱眉：“那你和我提前说一声，为什么要瞒着我？”
　　李玄霸道：“我也不知道自己能不能成功。”
　　李世民仍旧觉得弟弟还有其他事瞒着自己：“不成功又如何？难道我还会说你？”
　　李智云悄悄告状：“说不定三兄病的那一场是苦肉计，他要用苦肉计，知道你不同意，才瞒着你。”
　　说完，李智云从坐榻上跳下来，就像一溜烟似的跑得没了影。
　　李玄霸和李世民同时脸色大变。
　　李玄霸抹了一把脸：“二哥，你听我解释。”
　　李世民微笑：“嗯，我听你狡辩。”
　　李玄霸：“嗷嗷嗷！二哥别动手，有话好好说！”
　　李世民：“既然你不想活了，我揍死你这个臭弟弟！”
　　远方，李智云拍着胸口坏笑。
　　母亲的任务他圆满达成，现在去找母亲邀功了。
　　窦夫人得到李智云的回报，露出了慈祥的笑容。
　　自己舍不得动手，还好二郎管得住三郎。
　　李世民回来之后，就差不多要过年了。
　　等过完年，李世民和李玄霸就要出发去边镇。他们要去的地方正好是以前待过的河右之地重镇，张掖。
　　裴世矩回来后，张掖没有大官管理。杨广虽然把两位表侄丢去了边疆，但不是想磋磨他们。原本由裴世矩管理的张掖边市都交给了李世民和李玄霸管理。
　　李世民和李玄霸虽然是虎贲郎将和虎牙郎将，但朝中中高级别的将领在地方上就是天大的官职，他们也要负责一部分地方行政。
　　特别是军营所在地的屯田和市集，以及将士家属的管理，都是他们的责任。
　　这次李智云也会和他们随行。
　　李世民回来这段时间都没见过李元吉。
　　李渊将李元吉送去了学府，给他寻了最严格的老师，说让李元吉吃点苦头才知道家里的好。
　　李玄霸吐槽，没想到古代也有豫章书院。
　　窦夫人劝李渊：“将孩子交给其他人教导终究不是长久之计，最终还是得我们狠下心来好好管教。五郎很听二郎和三郎的话，不如把五郎交给二郎三郎教管。我们夫妻二人好全心全意地教导四郎。”
　　李渊听后有些意动：“五郎和李元吉差不多大，让他离家那么远，是不是不太好？”
　　窦夫人道：“二郎三郎这么大的时候，也已经可以出门游学了。再说了，我们三郎早早就成了秀才，这天底下比他更有学问的人估计都是朝中宿老了，我们也为五郎请不来。”
　　李渊被窦夫人说动了。
　　之后一件事彻底让李渊下定了单独教养李元吉的决心——被皇帝免官为民的张衡被逼自杀。
　　张衡原本是杨广的宠臣，因为杨广在扩建汾阳宫时劝阻杨广少征徭役而被杨广厌恶，被杨广连续找碴后，因杨玄感打小报告而免官回家。
　　李世民和李玄霸在洛阳的大宅院，就是张衡原本的府邸。
　　按照常理，对张衡这种没有大过错的勋贵官吏而言，免官为民就是最大的惩罚了。谁知道杨广征讨高丽失败后心情不好，疑神疑鬼，总觉得有人嘲笑他。据说张衡的一个小妾告御状，状告张衡在杨广征讨高丽失败后说杨广决策失误，杨广就把张衡杀了。
　　李渊得知此事后，觉得整件事莫名其妙。
　　小妾怎么有本事去告御状的？这理由还能更敷衍些吗？
　　不管是谁告的密，张衡因“诽谤朝政”被杀已经是事实。这件事在朝中引起轩然大波。
　　原本历史中，高颎等人因“诽谤朝政”被杀，引起的风波都没有张衡这件事更大。因为朝中大臣都知道高颎是皇帝“政敌”，只当皇帝随便找了个借口杀了高颎。至于宇文弼、贺若弼等人，那是因为与高颎走得太近被牵连。
　　张衡就完全不一样了。
　　张衡在杨广夺嫡时就是杨广的心腹。他此生没有任何对不起杨广的地方，唯一的过错，竟然只是“诽谤朝政”——劝说皇帝少征徭役和感叹皇帝在高丽战场的失误。
　　就因为这个，杨广便把一直跟随他的心腹杀了？
　　现在的魏晋遗风还没有过去，张衡这样的人，在魏晋时代叫“元从”，是就算叛逃他国都不会祸及家人的特殊存在。
　　这“诽谤朝政”说白了就是正常的劝谏。哪家皇帝会因为几句正常的劝谏就把自己的元从杀了？
　　他对元从尚且如此刻薄寡恩，其他人如何自处？
　　张衡死前悲愤地大喊，“我为人作何物事，而望久活！”。
　　李渊得知这个消息后，久久不语，悄悄斋戒禁酒三日，为张衡送行。
　　“天下百姓都被逼得活不下去，民乱四起，陛下却不思休养生息，甚至还杀了劝谏之人。”李渊对李世民和李玄霸道，“张建平被逼死前，悲呼没有为天下百姓做过好事，所以罪有应得。他是以此暗讽陛下……唉。”
　　李渊没有把大逆不道的话说出来，但话说到这里，不用说完也懂了。
　　李渊道：“我们父子三人虽然现在得到了陛下的重用，但这点恩宠远远不如当年张建平。张建平尚且有这样的下场，我们更需要小心谨慎。你们二人以前年纪小，所以声势大一些也没关系。现在你们已经长大，需要尽量低调，否则陛下一定容不下我们。”
　　李世民和李玄霸道：“儿子知道。父亲也请保重。”
　　李世民嘀咕：“我们倒是可以小心谨慎，父亲，你还是把李元吉接回来好好看管吧。如果他像张公那个小妾一样跑去告我们诽谤朝政，我们家就完蛋了。”
　　李渊按着额头道：“是啊，一定要好好盯住他。”
　　李元吉能在家门口诬陷亲生母亲不慈，也肯定会做出诬陷亲生父亲诽谤朝政的事。
　　李渊很后悔，自己以前怎么就被李元吉乖巧的表象蒙蔽。就算夫人真的对李元吉不好，李元吉也应该告诉自己做主，而不是在家门口大声嚷嚷，惹得全洛阳的勋贵都把自家当做谈资。
　　当时真是糊涂了。
　　“我现在被命为右骁卫中郎将，总管右骁卫禁军，事务繁忙。教育你们兄长和李元吉后，难以顾及五郎。”李渊语重心长道，“五郎一直亲近你们，我把五郎交给你们照顾。你们要好好教导他。”
　　李世民和李玄霸道：“父亲请放心。”
　　李渊叹气：“我对你们一直很放心。唉，大郎虽不如你们二人，也算是能守成之人。我总共五个儿子，怎么就李元吉是坏种？”
　　李世民道：“这就要怪阿玄了。说不定阿玄把李元吉捡回来时，捡错小孩了。”
　　李玄霸骂道：“二哥你闭嘴！这话不能胡说！”
　　李世民撇嘴。
　　李渊失笑：“李元吉肯定是你们弟弟。你们母亲生孩子的时候围着许多人，就是大德不把他捡回来，其他人也会把他护好。所谓丢弃，只是安你们母亲的心，做个样子而已，怎可能真的把孩子丢了？”
　　说到这，李渊又唉声叹气：“但就算这样，大德你把李元吉捡回来，也是对他有恩啊。以前你也最纵容李元吉，这次在病中还不忘教导他。他怎么能……唉。”
　　李世民安慰道：“父亲，别愁了。要愁也等我和阿玄离开后你再愁，我可不想被李元吉打扰了好心情。”
　　李渊表情一僵，默默地盯着二儿子。
　　李玄霸不知道该做出什么反应。笑快忍不住了！
　　“咳，父亲，没事我和二哥先走了。”李玄霸道，“父亲别生气，二哥就是这样的人，习惯就好。”
　　李渊哭笑不得：“滚吧！”儿子都是债啊。
　　李世民和李玄霸在家中度过了十四周岁的生日，正月离家前往张掖。
　　李世民高兴极了。张掖是个好地方，四处都是猎场，可以随意狩猎纵马。
　　他对李智云道：“你一定会喜欢那里！”
　　李智云使劲点头。
　　唯一不喜欢狩猎的李玄霸感觉自己格格不入。
　　离开前，李玄霸将义庄的事都交给了母亲，并让母亲联合三姐一起做。
　　“现在父亲已经为右骁卫中郎将，我们一家逐渐显赫，十分引人注目。但世人轻视女子，母亲继续推行义庄，不会引人注意。三姐胸有丘壑，一定能帮助母亲。”李玄霸道，“义庄非常重要，不仅能为我们赚名声，还能收集情报和积攒兵员。我与二哥前往张掖，无暇顾及中原之事，全靠母亲了。”
　　窦夫人踌躇：“我能做好吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“母亲曾经由周武帝亲手教导，又执掌唐国公府中馈这么多年，小小的义庄算什么？这与为唐国公府置办产业没区别。母亲别太把它当作大事。”
　　窦夫人哭笑不得：“你一会儿说这件事很重要，一会儿又让我别把它当作大事，把母亲当小孩哄吗？”
　　窦夫人捏了捏儿子瘦削的脸：“既然你相信娘亲，娘亲不会让你和二郎失望。这件事交给娘亲。二郎，你要照顾好三郎，可不能让三郎再自找生病了。”
　　李世民瓮声瓮气道：“娘娘，你放心，他自找生病前，我会先把他揍趴下。”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　窦夫人笑道：“好，就该这样。”
　　李玄霸无奈。张掖没皇帝也没李渊，自己哪还需要用苦肉计？
　　“是，我知道了。”李玄霸道，“别说了，父亲来了。”
　　终于请到假的李渊策马赶来，送李世民和李玄霸远行。李建成留在家中看守已经回家的李元吉。
　　“哎，你们跑那么快做什么？”李渊笑骂道，“我说我能请到假，肯定就能请到。”
　　李世民笑道：“就是要跑快点，让父亲抓不住。”
　　李渊把马鞭插到腰间，翻身下马去捉李世民：“这样啊？那我一定要把你抓住，别跑！”
　　李世民跳下马车：“抓不到！”
　　李渊和李世民绕着马车兜圈子，李智云坐在马车上笑着给父兄加油鼓劲。
　　窦夫人扶额道：“多大的人了，还这么幼稚。”
　　李玄霸看了一眼路上围观的人，脸上有点烧。
　　母子二人对视一眼：真丢人啊。
　　……
　　李渊和窦夫人把李世民、李玄霸、李智云三兄弟送到了十里外才离开。
　　李渊还想再送一程，被窦夫人劝住。
　　“郎君，你已经是右骁卫中郎将，负责宫禁护卫，就算今日请假不当值，也不能无诏离开洛阳。”窦夫人劝道，“我知道你舍不得二郎三郎和五郎，但陛下现在心情不好，还是小心为上。”
　　李渊这才无奈停下送行的马蹄。
　　待父母离开后，李世民嘀咕：“哼，右骁卫中郎将，好气哦。”
　　李玄霸把第一次出远门，十分不安分的李智云按住，问道：“你气什么？”
　　李世民抱着手臂瘪嘴：“阿玄，你看啊，我们先伏击了吐谷浑可汗，又平息众多民乱，这功劳的质和量都算不错了，但我们还只是小小的虎贲郎将虎牙郎将。父亲就押运了一下粮草，便升任右骁卫中郎将了？不公平！”
　　李玄霸白了李世民一眼：“公平？征伐高丽第一功臣贺若老将军还在牢里呢。”
　　李世民道：“那不一样！”
　　李玄霸道：“好吧，确实不一样。朝中官职不仅要看功劳，也要看资历出身。门荫得的官远远比立功得的官大，这很正常。我们父亲是国公，他只要得了陛下重用，再高的职官都能随便给。我们从零开始打拼，升官速度和父亲怎能一样？”
　　“再者，我们太年少了。你看朝中高官，即使门荫出身，至少也要而立之年才能就任职官。我们能当虎贲郎将虎牙郎将，还是皇帝破格提拔。这官职，在我们弱冠之前算是到头了。”李玄霸劝道，“不过虽然职官品级不会上升，待我们成亲后，得个爵位还是能指望的。再等两年吧，”
　　李世民叹气：“人家冠军侯第一次上战场就封侯。我们第一次上战场斩获首级俘虏也没差到哪去。人头少了点……少了很多，但还有个可汗顶顶呢。”
　　李玄霸无奈道：“冠军侯也是十八岁上战场，十九岁封侯，二十岁为骠骑将军。我们今年才十五岁。何况，陛下不是汉武帝，我们也不是冠军侯，大隋更不是大汉。”他所说的是虚岁。
　　“好吧，你说的有道理，但我还是好气哦。”李世民仍旧不住叹气，“凭什么啊，我年少立功多，不是更应该厚赏吗？”
　　李玄霸把李智云带出马车骑马，留李世民一个人自怨自艾。
　　现在都自怨自艾了，以后怎么办？就让二哥现在开始习惯吧。

Chapter 104: Blood Ties Outweigh All Else

When Lady Dou left, her steps felt as light as if she were walking on air.
She made an excuse about having caught a chill and went to bed early.
Lady Dou had expected to toss and turn, unable to find sleep, but to her surprise, she drifted off the moment her head hit the pillow.
In her sleep, she had a dream she hadn't experienced in over a decade.
In the dream, she was nestled in her uncle’s arms. She couldn't quite hear what he was saying, but she was laughing happily.
Her uncle stood up, took her hand, and led her across the high threshold, walking out through the grand palace gates.
Her father and mother were waiting outside to welcome her.
Her elder brother jumped out from behind their parents, giving her a start.
Her father rolled up his sleeves, clenched his fists, and playfully hammered her brother’s head with a fierce expression.
Her brother scurried away, clutching his head, making faces at her as he fled.
Her younger self jumped and clapped, laughing as if cheering her brother on.
Her mother leaned down to straighten her clothes, then turned to share a few words with her uncle, both of them smiling.
Then, her brother was hauled back by their father, and she took her mother’s hand, turning to bid her uncle farewell.
"Once your uncle returns from his imperial campaign, he will have time to find you a fine husband."
"Eh? My daughter is still young; it’s too early to talk about husbands. Besides, finding a husband for my daughter is my responsibility as a father."
"It is an imperial decree. Now, that responsibility is Mine."
"Your Majesty, you cannot do this! My Lady, please, persuade His Majesty!"
"Pfft... whatever, it’s all fine. You can start looking, but she won't be leaving the house for a while. My daughter is so wonderful; I can’t bear to let her go to someone else’s home too soon. I’ll keep her until she’s at least seventeen or eighteen."
"What you say is most reasonable, my Lady."
"That is what I think as well."
Her younger self blushed, covering her face with both hands, too shy to speak.
Lady Dou’s consciousness detached from her younger self. She watched the scene with cold, detached eyes, not even a single tear falling.
She remembered this as the last time she had seen her uncle.
Her uncle was about to lead an imperial campaign, so he had sent her back to her mother’s side after she had been raised in the palace.
She had watched her uncle, then in his prime and full of spirit, lead his great army away. Who could have known that this parting would be forever?
Her cousin, the Emperor, had ruled so poorly that she had long foreseen the throne of her uncle’s family would be in jeopardy.
The only thing she hadn't expected was that Yang Jian, disregarding the grace her uncle had shown him, would slaughter every male in her uncle’s family, whether near or distant kin.
Lady Dou had lived in the palace since she was a child. She understood the cruelty of power struggles.
Her cousin’s absurdity had cost him the throne. Yang Jian usurping it was inevitable.
That Yang Jian had to kill her uncle’s heirs was also, perhaps, inevitable.
She was furious and grief-stricken, yet she could hardly fault Yang Jian for that.
But she had never imagined that not a single male in her uncle’s family would escape the catastrophe.
Was it necessary?
Yang Jian could keep the princes of the Chen Dynasty and other fallen states in his palace; leaving a branch or two of her uncle’s distant kin would hardly have threatened his throne.
Was it because his throne had come too easily, leaving him with a guilty conscience?
That was the only way Lady Dou could interpret it.
Back then, her greatest fear had been her parents’ excessive anxiety.
Regardless of which dynasty rose or fell, the disaster never reached the women who had already married out. Moreover, Yang Jian was a usurper; the power structure in the court had barely changed. The Dou family had been a pillar of the Northern Zhou nobility, and they remained a pillar of the Sui Dynasty.
In chaotic times, dynasties changed frequently, and her father was a veteran official who had served through several. As long as one didn't stand in clear opposition to the Emperor, the new ruler generally wouldn't purge the old guard.
Thus, Lady Dou had assumed her parents were merely over-worrying.
The entire Dou family had chosen to support Yang Jian; what power did their household have to threaten his rule? When Yang Jian usurped the throne, her parents had simply practiced self-preservation, never once opposing him. Surely, Yang Jian would at most treat them with cold indifference.
Her parents had married her off early. Lady Dou had been filled with reluctance, but she never imagined her future would be so bleak.
Later, her father’s rank rose, and her brother was entrusted with important duties as an official abroad. Lady Dou had truly believed her family had weathered the storm.
Though she kept the hatred for her uncle’s death in her heart, she could only keep it buried. Her own family was more important.
Her family... her parents, her aunt, all passed away one after another in the second year of the Kaihuang era. Her brother, Dou Zhaoxian, who inherited the title, died young shortly thereafter, leaving no heirs.
Her other two brothers, Dou Zhao and Dou Wenshu, had passed away even before the Sui replaced the Northern Zhou. In the blink of an eye, she had become an orphan with no father, no mother, and no brothers.
Everyone said it was a coincidence.
Everyone said so.
Her husband’s family said so, the Dou family said so, the whole world said so.
Even the physician she trusted most in the household said so—her parents had died of illness, and her brothers had died of illness.
Perhaps it really was a coincidence.
Perhaps it really was just a coincidence.
Coincidence, coincidence, coincidence... coincidence, coincidence, coincidence, coincidence, coincidence... it really was just a coincidence.
Lady Dou put on a mask, hiding her tear-stained face.
Just a coincidence.
Her relatives just happened to pass away shortly after she married, shortly after Yang Jian usurped the throne.
She felt no hatred. She was simply ill-fated.
Lady Dou woke up from the dream with a start.
She touched her face; she hadn't even shed a tear during such a dream.
When Lady Dou rose, a servant told her that the Duke of Tang, fearing to disturb her rest, had gone to sleep elsewhere.
She let out a sigh of relief, draped a robe over her shoulders, and carried a lantern to the storeroom.
The dowry in the storeroom was more than just a dowry. After her parents died and her brother passed away without heirs, he had left a will before his death, bequeathing all his property to her.
Yang Jian had been "benevolent and magnanimous" in this regard, not interfering with the distribution of his ministers' estates. He had always maintained the posture of a kind, elderly mentor, which was why her uncle had trusted and valued him so much.
There were many items in the house. To avoid drawing envy, Lady Dou had sold everything that could be sold, keeping only some of her family’s calligraphy and paintings as mementos.
But in all the years since her marriage, she had rarely come to look at these works. In the last decade, she hadn't come once.
Lady Dou unfolded a scroll.
The painting was nothing special. Her father’s painting was truly nothing special.
The scroll bore a poem inscribed by her mother, her brother’s seal, and her uncle’s somewhat exaggerated praise.
Because her uncle had praised it, her father had believed his painting was truly excellent, and thus he had treasured this "masterpiece" dearly.
Lady Dou stroked the yellowing paper, the corners of her mouth lifting as if to smile, but she couldn't force a smile.
She could neither cry nor laugh.
She was alone in the storeroom, having ordered everyone else to stay outside, so she could speak to herself.
"The world... if they are fighting for more than just the title of Duke of Tang, then fratricide is inevitable," Lady Dou whispered to herself. "Not just fratricide, but a fight to the death."
After waking from her sleep, Lady Dou had regained her capacity for rational thought.
She immediately guessed the tragic future that lay ahead.
But for some reason, even as she spoke of fear and worry, her heart remained completely calm.
Lady Dou closed the scroll, covered her face with both hands, and tears finally spilled from between her fingers.
"So, I am not a good mother after all."
As it turned out, as long as she could have her revenge, she could place everything—her husband, her sons... everything—behind the cause of vengeance.
How she longed for revenge.
Father, Mother, Brother, Uncle... I want revenge.
Er-lang, San-lang, you are going to avenge them.
I can have my revenge.
I can have my revenge!
Lady Dou lowered her hands. Tears continued to stream from the corners of her eyes, but the corners of her mouth were curled high.
The expression, a mixture of joy and sorrow, was twisted.
...
Li Xuanba felt that his mother had changed, but it seemed like it might just be his imagination.
His mother was still as kind to everyone as ever, managing the affairs of the Duke of Tang’s residence with perfect order.
She still treated all the children equally. If there was any difference, it was perhaps that she had become a bit closer to Li Zhiyun.
Was it his imagination? Li Xuanba scratched his head.
Soon, Li Xuanba had no time to worry about these subtle inconsistencies, because his elder brother had returned.
Li Shimin returned in a foul mood, scaring Li Xuanba, who had gone out to welcome him, into turning and running.
Li Yuan was bewildered. He asked Li Jiancheng, "Why is Da-de running?"
Li Jiancheng was equally confused. "I don't know."
Only Lady Dou covered her mouth to hide a smile, sighing softly, "He deserves it."
Seeing Li Xuanba turn and run, Li Shimin vaulted off his horse and shouted, "Father, Mother, Eldest Brother, Little Five, wait a moment! I’m going to beat A-Xuan up first!"
Li Yuan couldn't stop him in time, watching his second son duck under his arm and chase after the third son.
Li Yuan shouted, "Da-xiong! What are you doing? Da-de’s health is poor; he can’t run like that! Hey!"
He hurried to chase after them.
Li Jiancheng scratched his head.
This gesture made him look very much like the elder brother of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.
"Mother, what is wrong with Da-xiong?" Li Jiancheng asked, puzzled.
Lady Dou suppressed her laughter and said, "He probably heard that San-lang fell ill again and is angry that San-lang doesn't take better care of himself."
Li Jiancheng was left speechless. "He can get angry at that? Is it San-lang’s fault that he fell ill?"
He also followed to persuade Li Shimin to stop.
After learning of the malice of his younger brother Li Yuanji, and seeing Li Xuanba still treating him with respect, Li Jiancheng had set aside his jealousy and resentment toward his second and third brothers, truly wanting to be a good elder brother. This was a perfect moment to show brotherly affection.
Li Zhiyun, who had the best relationship with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, cupped his hands around his mouth and shouted, "Second Brother, run! Don't let Father catch you! You must teach Third Brother a good lesson!"
Lady Dou smiled and tapped Li Zhiyun’s head. "Why aren't you protecting your Third Brother?"
Li Zhiyun lowered his hands, shaking his head with a grin. "Second Brother has always been very indulgent toward Third Brother. If Third Brother made Second Brother angry, then Third Brother must have done something truly excessive. Although I don't know what Third Brother did."
Lady Dou laughed. "Clever."
She took Li Zhiyun’s hand and walked slowly in the direction Li Xuanba had fled.
By the time Lady Dou saw Li Shimin and Li Xuanba again, Li Shimin had already finished pinning Li Xuanba down for a beating and was now pulling on Li Xuanba’s face, roaring. Li Xuanba’s hat had fallen off, and he looked utterly disheveled.
Li Yuan and Li Jiancheng stood to the side, trying to mediate, but Li Shimin’s fierce demeanor made the father and son hesitate to intervene.
Seeing Er-lang so angry, had San-lang really done something terrible?
Lady Dou sighed and held Li Shimin back. "That’s enough. A few words of scolding would have sufficed; why resort to blows? Your brother is already frail; how many of your punches can he take?"
"Hmph." Li Shimin released Li Xuanba. "I’ll continue lecturing you later."
Li Xuanba hid behind Lady Dou. At this moment, he didn't care about his dignity. Second Brother’s punches really hurt; his back...
Li Zhiyun tiptoed behind Li Xuanba and poked the spot Li Xuanba was clutching.
"Ow!" Li Xuanba jumped up. "Little Five!"
"Hehehe." Li Zhiyun hid behind Li Shimin.
Li Xuanba was speechless. Why was everyone bullying him?
He looked at his useless father and Li Jiancheng. *Don't just stand there talking; at least try to stop him!*
The useless father and Li Jiancheng shrugged at Li Xuanba, indicating their helplessness.
"Father, Mother, Brother, I am back." Li Shimin finally performed a proper salute. "Little Five, I’m back. Have you been doing your studies properly?"
Li Zhiyun’s face fell. "I’ve done them properly, very well indeed. I’m not like you, Second Brother, always playing and forgetting to do your lessons... ouch."
Li Shimin tapped Li Zhiyun on the head.
Li Zhiyun stood next to Third Brother, who was rubbing his face, both of them poor little brothers bullied by the Second Brother, huddling together.
Li Xuanba glanced at Li Zhiyun and tapped his head as well.
Li Zhiyun had no choice but to hide by Lady Dou’s side.
Li Yuan watched enough of Li Shimin bullying his brothers and laughed. "Alright, stop bullying people the moment you get back. Go wash up and change your clothes; the sour smell on you is choking me. How many days has it been since you bathed?"
Li Shimin said, "I heard the news that A-Xuan was ill again and rode back immediately; I didn't have time to bathe. Besides, this isn't that bad. Compared to the battlefield, this is nothing."
Li Yuan said, "Fine, fine, you’re right. Go wash up."
"Oh." Li Shimin obediently went to wash and change.
Once he had finished washing and wrapped his wet hair in a cloth, he dragged Li Xuanba back to settle the score.
Li Xuanba raised his hands in surrender. "I admit it, I did it on purpose to send you away. If you were at home, Li Yuanji wouldn't have dared to target me."
Li Shimin frowned. "Then you should have told me in advance. Why keep it from me?"
Li Xuanba said, "I didn't know if I would succeed."
Li Shimin still felt his brother was hiding other things from him. "And what if you didn't succeed? Would I have scolded you?"
Li Zhiyun quietly snitched, "Maybe Third Brother’s illness was a ruse to gain sympathy. He knew you wouldn't agree, so he kept it from you."
After saying this, Li Zhiyun jumped off the sitting mat and ran away like a puff of smoke.
Li Xuanba and Li Shimin’s expressions changed simultaneously.
Li Xuanba wiped his face. "Second Brother, listen to my explanation."
Li Shimin smiled. "Mm, I’m listening to your sophistry."
Li Xuanba: "Ow, ow, ow! Second Brother, don't hit me! Let’s talk this out!"
Li Shimin: "Since you don't want to live, I’ll beat you to death, you stinking brother!"
In the distance, Li Zhiyun patted his chest and smirked.
He had successfully completed Mother’s mission and was now going to find her to claim his reward.
When Lady Dou received Li Zhiyun’s report, she revealed a kind smile.
She couldn't bear to lay a hand on them herself, but fortunately, Er-lang could keep San-lang in line.
After Li Shimin returned, the New Year was almost upon them.
Once the New Year passed, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba would set off for the border towns. The place they were going to was Zhangye, a key town in the Hexi region where they had stayed before.
After Pei Juju returned, Zhangye had no high-ranking officials to manage it. Although Yang Guang had sent his two nephews to the border, it wasn't to torment them. The border markets in Zhangye, previously managed by Pei Juju, were now handed over to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.
Although Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were Tiger-Bravery and Tiger-Tooth Generals, in the provinces, mid-to-high-ranking generals were effectively the highest authority, and they were responsible for some local administration.
In particular, the garrison farming and markets where the troops were stationed, as well as the management of the soldiers' families, were all their responsibility.
This time, Li Zhiyun would also accompany them.
Li Shimin hadn't seen Li Yuanji during his time back.
Li Yuan had sent Li Yuanji to an academy, finding him the strictest teacher, saying he wanted Li Yuanji to suffer a little so he would know how good he had it at home.
Li Xuanba mused that he hadn't expected the ancient world to have a "Yuzhang Academy" equivalent.
Lady Dou persuaded Li Yuan, "Leaving the child to be taught by others is not a long-term solution. Ultimately, we must be firm and discipline him ourselves. Wu-lang listens to Er-lang and San-lang; why not hand Wu-lang over to them to manage? We two can then focus entirely on teaching Si-lang."
Li Yuan was moved. "Wu-lang is about the same age as Li Yuanji. Is it really okay to send him so far away from home?"
Lady Dou said, "When Er-lang and San-lang were his age, they were already traveling for their studies. Besides, our San-lang became a scholar long ago; I suspect anyone more learned than him in this world is already an elder in the court, and we wouldn't be able to hire them for Wu-lang."
Li Yuan was persuaded by Lady Dou.
Later, one event completely solidified Li Yuan’s determination to raise Li Yuanji separately—Zhang Heng, who had been stripped of his rank and made a commoner by the Emperor, was forced to commit suicide.
Zhang Heng had originally been a favorite of Yang Guang, but because he had advised Yang Guang to reduce forced labor during the expansion of the Fenyang Palace, he had incurred Yang Guang’s hatred. After being repeatedly nitpicked by Yang Guang, he was dismissed and sent home due to a report by Yang Xuangan.
The large mansion Li Shimin and Li Xuanba owned in Luoyang was Zhang Heng’s former residence.
By common logic, for a noble official like Zhang Heng who had committed no major crime, being dismissed to commoner status was the ultimate punishment. Who knew that after Yang Guang’s failed campaign against Goguryeo, he was in a foul mood, suspicious and paranoid, always feeling that people were mocking him. It was said that one of Zhang Heng’s concubines had filed an imperial complaint, accusing Zhang Heng of saying Yang Guang’s decision-making was flawed after the failed campaign, and Yang Guang had killed him.
When Li Yuan learned of this, he found the whole thing bizarre.
How did a concubine have the ability to file an imperial complaint? Could the excuse be any more perfunctory?
Regardless of who the informant was, it was a fact that Zhang Heng had been killed for "slandering the imperial government." This incident caused a massive uproar in the court.
In history, the turmoil caused by the execution of Gao Jiong and others for "slandering the imperial government" had not been as great as this incident with Zhang Heng. Because court ministers knew Gao Jiong was the Emperor’s "political enemy," they assumed the Emperor had just found an excuse to kill him. As for Yuwen Bi, He Ruobi, and others, they were implicated because they were too close to Gao Jiong.
Zhang Heng was completely different.
Zhang Heng had been Yang Guang’s confidant during his struggle for the succession. He had never done anything to wrong Yang Guang in his life; his only "fault" was "slandering the imperial government"—advising the Emperor to reduce forced labor and sighing over the Emperor’s failures on the Goguryeo battlefield.
Because of this, Yang Guang killed the confidant who had followed him all along?
The legacy of the Wei and Jin dynasties had not yet faded; men like Zhang Heng were called "original followers" in the Wei and Jin eras, a special existence whose families would not be harmed even if they defected to another country.
This "slandering the imperial government" was, in plain terms, normal remonstrance. Which emperor would kill his "original followers" for a few normal words of advice?
If he was this cold and ungrateful to his original followers, how were others to conduct themselves?
Before Zhang Heng died, he cried out in grief and indignation, "What have I done to deserve this, to hope for a long life!"
When Li Yuan learned of this news, he remained silent for a long time, quietly fasting and abstaining from alcohol for three days to see Zhang Heng off.
"The common people are being driven to the point where they cannot survive, and uprisings are breaking out everywhere, yet His Majesty does not think of resting and recuperating, and even kills those who offer remonstrance." Li Yuan said to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, "Before Zhang Jianping was forced to his death, he lamented that he had done no good for the people and thus deserved his fate. He was using that to mock His Majesty... sigh."
Li Yuan didn't voice the treasonous words, but having said this much, they understood without him finishing.
Li Yuan said, "Although the three of us are currently valued by His Majesty, this favor is far less than what Zhang Jianping once had. If Zhang Jianping could meet such an end, we must be even more cautious. You two were young before, so it didn't matter if you had a high profile. Now that you are grown, you must be as low-key as possible, or His Majesty will surely not tolerate us."
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba said, "We understand, Father. Please take care of yourself as well."
Li Shimin muttered, "We can be cautious, but Father, you should really bring Li Yuanji back and keep a close eye on him. If he runs off like that concubine of Zhang Gong and accuses us of slandering the imperial government, our family is finished."
Li Yuan pressed his forehead. "Yes, I must keep a close watch on him."
If Li Yuanji could frame his own mother for being uncharitable at the front door, he would certainly be capable of framing his own father for slandering the imperial government.
Li Yuan regretted it deeply; how had he been blinded by Li Yuanji’s obedient appearance? Even if his wife had truly been unkind to Li Yuanji, Li Yuanji should have told him to handle it, rather than shouting at the front door and making their family the talk of every noble in Luoyang.
He had truly been foolish back then.
"I have been appointed as the Middle General of the Right Xiao Guard, in charge of the imperial guards, and I am very busy. After educating your elder brother and Li Yuanji, it is hard for me to attend to Wu-lang." Li Yuan said earnestly, "Wu-lang has always been close to you; I am handing Wu-lang over to your care. You must teach him well."
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba said, "Please rest assured, Father."
Li Yuan sighed, "I have always been at ease with you. Sigh, although Da-lang is not as capable as you two, he is at least someone who can hold the fort. I have five sons in total; how is it that only Li Yuanji is a bad seed?"
Li Shimin said, "That’s A-Xuan’s fault. Maybe when A-Xuan picked Li Yuanji up, he picked the wrong child."
Li Xuanba scolded, "Second Brother, shut up! You can't say things like that!"
Li Shimin curled his lip.
Li Yuan laughed in spite of himself. "Li Yuanji is definitely your brother. There were many people around when your mother gave birth; even if Da-de hadn't picked him up, others would have protected him. The so-called 'abandonment' was just to put your mother’s mind at ease, just for show. How could the child have really been abandoned?"
Speaking of this, Li Yuan sighed again, "But even so, Da-de, you picking Li Yuanji up was a kindness to him. You were always the most indulgent toward Li Yuanji, and even this time while you were ill, you didn't forget to teach him. How could he... sigh."
Li Shimin comforted him, "Father, don't worry. If you must worry, wait until A-Xuan and I have left; I don't want Li Yuanji to ruin my good mood."
Li Yuan’s expression stiffened as he stared silently at his second son.
Li Xuanba didn't know how to react. He could barely hold back his laughter!
"Cough, Father, if there’s nothing else, Second Brother and I will be going." Li Xuanba said, "Father, don't be angry; Second Brother is just that kind of person. You’ll get used to it."
Li Yuan was left speechless. "Get out of here!" Sons were truly a debt.
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba spent their fourteenth birthday at home and left for Zhangye in the first lunar month.
Li Shimin was overjoyed. Zhangye was a great place, full of hunting grounds where they could hunt and ride freely.
He said to Li Zhiyun, "You will definitely like it there!"
Li Zhiyun nodded vigorously.
Li Xuanba, the only one who didn't like hunting, felt like he didn't quite fit in.
Before leaving, Li Xuanba handed the affairs of the charity estate over to his mother and asked her to work with his third sister.
"Now that Father is the Middle General of the Right Xiao Guard, our family is becoming prominent and very conspicuous. But the world looks down on women; if Mother continues to run the charity estate, it won't attract much attention. Third Sister has great depth of character and will surely be able to help Mother." Li Xuanba said, "The charity estate is very important; it can not only earn us a reputation but also collect intelligence and accumulate manpower. With Second Brother and me heading to Zhangye, we won't be able to attend to matters in the Central Plains; it all depends on Mother."
Lady Dou hesitated. "Can I do it well?"
Li Xuanba said, "Mother was personally taught by Emperor Wu of Zhou and has managed the Duke of Tang’s household for so many years; what is a small charity estate? It’s no different from managing the properties of the Duke of Tang’s residence. Mother, don't think of it as a major task."
Lady Dou was left speechless. "One moment you say this is very important, and the next you tell me not to think of it as a major task. Are you coaxing your mother like a child?"
Lady Dou pinched her son’s thin face. "Since you believe in your mother, I will not let you and Er-lang down. Leave this to me. Er-lang, you must take good care of San-lang; don't let him go looking for illness again."
Li Shimin said in a muffled voice, "Mother, don't worry. Before he goes looking for illness, I’ll beat him flat first."
Li Xuanba: "..."
Lady Dou smiled. "Good, that’s exactly what you should do."
Li Xuanba was helpless. There was no Emperor or Li Yuan in Zhangye; why would he need to use a ruse to gain sympathy?
"Yes, I understand." Li Xuanba said, "Stop talking, Father is here."
Li Yuan, who had finally managed to get leave, rode over to see Li Shimin and Li Xuanba off on their long journey. Li Jiancheng remained at home to watch over Li Yuanji, who had returned.
"Hey, why are you running so fast?" Li Yuan laughed and scolded, "I said if I could get leave, I would."
Li Shimin laughed, "We just wanted to run fast so Father couldn't catch us."
Li Yuan tucked his horse whip into his waist, vaulted off his horse to catch Li Shimin. "Is that so? Then I must catch you, don't run!"
Li Shimin jumped off the carriage. "Can't catch me!"
Li Yuan and Li Shimin circled the carriage, while Li Zhiyun sat on the carriage, laughing and cheering for his father and brother.
Lady Dou held her forehead. "How old are they, still so childish."
Li Xuanba glanced at the onlookers on the road, his face burning slightly.
Mother and son looked at each other: How embarrassing.
...
Li Yuan and Lady Dou saw Li Shimin, Li Xuanba, and Li Zhiyun off for ten miles before turning back.
Li Yuan wanted to go further, but was persuaded by Lady Dou.
"My Lord, you are already the Middle General of the Right Xiao Guard, in charge of palace security. Even if you took leave today, you cannot leave Luoyang without an imperial decree." Lady Dou persuaded, "I know you can't bear to part with Er-lang, San-lang, and Wu-lang, but His Majesty is in a foul mood right now; it’s better to be cautious."
Li Yuan then reluctantly stopped his horse.
After his parents left, Li Shimin muttered, "Hmph, Middle General of the Right Xiao Guard, so annoying."
Li Xuanba held down Li Zhiyun, who was very restless on his first trip far from home, and asked, "What are you annoyed about?"
Li Shimin crossed his arms and pouted. "A-Xuan, look, we ambushed the Tuyuhun Khan and quelled many uprisings; the quality and quantity of these merits are quite good, but we are still just small Tiger-Bravery and Tiger-Tooth Generals. Father just transported some grain and was promoted to Middle General of the Right Xiao Guard? It’s unfair!"
Li Xuanba rolled his eyes at Li Shimin. "Fair? Old General He Ruo, the first hero of the Goguryeo campaign, is still in prison."
Li Shimin said, "That’s different!"
Li Xuanba said, "Fine, it is different. Official positions in the court depend not only on merit but also on seniority and background. Positions gained through hereditary privilege are far higher than those gained through merit; this is normal. Our father is a Duke; as long as he is valued by His Majesty, he can be given any high-ranking position. We are starting from scratch; how can our promotion speed be the same as Father’s?"
"Furthermore, we are too young. Look at the high officials in court; even those with hereditary backgrounds must be at least thirty to hold significant office. That we can be Tiger-Bravery and Tiger-Tooth Generals is already due to the Emperor breaking the rules to promote us. This rank is as far as we’ll get before we come of age." Li Xuanba advised, "However, although our official rank won't rise, once we marry, we can look forward to gaining a title. Let’s wait another two years."
Li Shimin sighed, "The Champion Marquis went to the battlefield for the first time and was enfeoffed as a Marquis. Our first time on the battlefield, our tally of heads and captives wasn't much worse. The head count was a bit low... a lot lower, but we had a Khan to top it off."
Li Xuanba said helplessly, "The Champion Marquis also went to the battlefield at eighteen, was enfeoffed at nineteen, and became a General of the Flying Cavalry at twenty. We are only fifteen this year. Besides, His Majesty is not Emperor Wu of Han, we are not the Champion Marquis, and the Great Sui is certainly not the Great Han." He was speaking in terms of nominal age.
"Fine, what you say makes sense, but I’m still annoyed." Li Shimin continued to sigh, "Why? I’ve achieved so much at a young age; shouldn't I be rewarded more generously?"
Li Xuanba took Li Zhiyun out of the carriage to ride a horse, leaving Li Shimin to wallow in self-pity alone.
He was wallowing in self-pity now; what would happen later? He might as well let Second Brother get used to it now.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第105章 女子十五已及笄
chunks.chineseText:
第105章 女子十五已及笄

李世民和李玄霸带着李智云去张掖前， 先路过了大兴。
　　大兴不仅有宇文珠，长孙小妹和长孙晟也在大兴老家歇着没回洛阳。
　　自从长孙晟装病后，他就完全进入了退休生活。
　　仗着杨广对他的宠信还没有淡去， 长孙晟占着大将军的位置不做事， 每日都闲在家中， 偶尔给杨广送礼物并歌功颂德。杨广很纵容他。
　　高颎、宇文弼和薛道衡三老头还要编书，不是白领俸禄。长孙晟把“俸禄蛀虫”表现得淋漓尽致。
　　偷懒在家时，长孙晟用孝道施压， 让长孙安业也辞了职官在家“照顾生病的老父亲”。
　　长孙安业得到了迟来许多年的父亲的关爱和教导，叫苦不迭。
　　如今长孙安业与长孙无忌和长孙小妹的关系亲近不少。因为长孙无忌和他一起扛着父亲充满爱的教导，而妹妹是唯一能说动父亲让他休息的人。
　　李世民对李玄霸吐槽， 看看人家父亲怎么教儿子，我们父亲怎么就不行呢？
　　李玄霸表示， 能在后世留下成语典故的人， 是一般人能比的吗？知不知道“一箭双雕”典故的含金量？
　　李世民道：“我们父亲还是开国皇帝呢！”
　　李玄霸道：“就算他是开国皇帝，他身上也没有关于政治的成语典故。”
　　李世民犹豫了一会儿，小声问道：“那我身上有关于政治的成语典故吗？”
　　李玄霸正色：“有，小鸟依人。”
　　李世民：“啊？我夸观音婢吗？这算什么政治典故？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“你夸褚遂良。”
　　李世民俊脸一黑。
　　褚遂良他认识。褚遂良比他大三岁，也在虞世南老师那里学写字， 虽然没自己去的勤，也有过一点交情。他是个性格较为孤傲的人， 虽然长得确实好看，但小鸟依人真的能形容他吗？
　　李世民使劲摇头：“这一定是后人牵强附会，我怎么会这么夸他？”
　　李玄霸呵呵：“禇遂良学问稍长， 性亦坚正， 既写忠诚， 甚亲附于朕， 譬如飞鸟依人，自加怜爱。”
　　李世民把剥好的橘子皮塞进弟弟嘴里，让他闭嘴，自己吃橘子瓣，再不提自己身上有没有优秀的成语典故的事。
　　李玄霸呸呸吐出橘子皮，在心中小本本上又记了一笔。
　　到了大兴，李世民把好久没见宇文珠，又变得有些扭捏的弟弟直接丢到宇文老师门口，带着五弟扬长而去。
　　李玄霸还没反应过来，就被李世民丢下，孤零零地站在宇文府门口，别说护卫，连只雕都没给他留。
　　寒钩！乌镝！我白疼你们了！
　　“哎？这不是三郎君？”守门的仆从惊讶。
　　李玄霸讪讪说不出话来。
　　李玄霸是府上小娘子的未婚夫，不需要通传，守门的仆从直接将李玄霸迎进了门。
　　宇文弼正好在大门后的院子里练刀，见着李玄霸，十分疑惑道：“你怎么在这？”
　　李玄霸憋屈道：“路过老师门口时，二哥突然让马车停车，把我从马车上丢了下来。”
　　宇文弼先一愣，然后失笑：“是大雄能做出的事。你们要去张掖赴任了？”
　　问到李玄霸两手空空，连换洗衣服都在马车上时，宇文弼骂了李大雄几句。
　　李玄霸刚到大兴，都还没回府上歇息，就被李世民绕路丢下。整件事李玄霸事先没有任何察觉。他觉得自己对二哥太信任是个错误。
　　宇文弼让人准备好洗澡水和换洗的衣服，让李玄霸先沐浴。
　　这个世代的人的衣服都很宽大，宇文弼家中富裕，备有许多新衣，他只需要让人把自己的新衣裁剪一下，就能给李玄霸穿。
　　李玄霸想借马车离开，宇文弼道：“既然都来了，就在我家住几日。我想大雄也是此意。他或许也没想回唐国公府住，而是想在长孙府住几日。”
　　李玄霸头皮一麻。
　　淦（gan）！以二哥的脸皮厚度，真的做得出来这种事！
　　“把小五也带到长孙老师的府上住？”李玄霸嘴角抽搐。
　　宇文弼道：“让李五郎在我家住也没问题，只是你或许不好意思。”
　　他笑着摇摇头，对李世民生出“敬佩”之心。
　　为了脸皮薄的弟弟，李大雄真是操了许多不该操的心，做事太“极端”了。
　　得知了二哥的用意，李玄霸虽然能独自回到唐国公府，但老师都挽留他了，他也不好离开，只能硬着头皮住下。
　　宇文珠得知李玄霸要在自家住下，羞得躲房里不出来。
　　老夫人取笑宇文珠：“若是长孙家的小娘子，已经开开心心拉着她未婚夫的手叽叽喳喳聊个不停了。你和三郎都害羞，都躲，等成婚后该怎么办？你都十六了，再过一两年就该和三郎成婚了。”
　　宇文珠比李玄霸大一岁，今年是十六虚岁。寻常贵族女子此时都可以成婚了，只是李玄霸年纪小，宇文家也舍不得她早出门，才延后几年。
　　宇文珠羞恼道：“我是女子，害羞正常。是三郎不好！”
　　老夫人道：“是是是，三郎不好，那他约你出门踏青，你出去吗？”
　　宇文珠道：“他敢吗！”
　　老夫人提高嗓门：“三郎，珠娘问你敢不敢！”
　　宇文珠表情一僵。
　　门扉打开，宇文弼推门进来。
　　李玄霸站在门口，呆若木鸡。
　　宇文珠僵着，李玄霸也僵着，两人现场表演一二三木头人。
　　老夫人笑得前俯后仰，靠在郎君身旁抹眼泪：“这俩孩子真是太逗了。”
　　宇文弼忍笑道：“你都知道他们脸皮薄，不要逗他们。三郎，还愣着干什么？没胆子吗？”
　　李玄霸艰难地扯出一个笑容。都说到这份上了，他能说没吗？他也是要面子的！
　　“我要在大兴停留五日，采买些家用。”李玄霸掐了自己一把，让表情恢复自然，“我许久没有回大兴，有些不太了解东西市的情况。宇文娘子可否帮我？”
　　老夫人推了宇文珠一把。
　　宇文珠微微踉跄，恼羞地整理了一下头发：“好。”
　　她回头瞪了祖父祖母一眼，突然伸手拉住李玄霸的手臂，拽着李玄霸就跑：“不理你们了！我们走，不要被他们嘲笑！”
　　李玄霸一惊，跌跌撞撞跟着跑。
　　老夫人再次笑得前俯后仰肚子疼：“哎哟，我们家珠娘不是胆子很大吗？”
　　宇文弼板着脸道：“她胆子确实大，拜了孙医师为师后，居然敢扮作道童，与孙医师一同去救助流民。哼，若是染上了疫病……”
　　宇文弼说不下去了。他现在仍旧深深后怕。
　　老夫人抹了抹笑出来的眼泪，道：“你说着不满，不也没阻止她，还为她提供助力？现在抱怨什么。”
　　宇文弼道：“我知道她做的事很对。将来她嫁给三郎，遇到的危险会更多，现在在我的羽翼下多积累些经验是好事。但担忧还是担忧。”
　　老夫人握住郎君的手：“是这个理。你若想抱怨，就只对我抱怨，别让孩子们听到了。珠娘和大德都是心思很重的人。”
　　宇文弼叹气：“知道。”
　　宇文珠鼓起勇气把李玄霸拽走，跑了一会儿之后才意识到和李玄霸有肢体接触似乎有点不好。
　　但事情做都做了，宇文珠也不会纠结。
　　她松开手，打量李玄霸道：“许久不见，我快认不出你了。”
　　李玄霸指着自己的头发：“是因为头发吗？”
　　宇文珠捂嘴笑：“也长高了。”
　　李玄霸留了头发之后，没有梳隋朝男子最普遍的额前系结平顶幞头，而是像汉代男子那样在脑后编了两股辫子收拢散发，然后与前端头发一同在头顶梳了个锥发。
　　他用青布将锥发包裹住，又用木簪将锥发固定，系结的青布条垂在脑后，就像是汉代的古人从画中走了出来。
　　宇文珠在李玄霸说起头发时，才将视线从李玄霸已经褪去稚气的脸上转移到李玄霸的头型上。
　　她摸了摸自己的十字发髻：“你的发髻好像比我还精致。”
　　李玄霸赶紧摇头：“没有你精致。你的发型很好看，很适合你！”
　　宇文珠所梳的是魏晋时少女常见的十字发髻，额前有浅浅的留海，脑后垂着很像后世妹妹头的整齐短发，头顶编成十字发髻，发髻中戴着垂苏珠花，十分活泼。
　　李玄霸见到宇文珠时也吓了一跳，差点没认出来。
　　上次见面时，宇文珠与李玄霸一样，都留着两个小揪揪。
　　再次见面，宇文珠已经及笄，无论是穿着打扮，还是身量容颜，都完全变成了一位妙龄女子。
　　之前见面，李玄霸对宇文珠的紧张和好意，是出于“这是将来会陪伴我一生的家人”。
　　现在他有些不敢直视宇文珠的脸。
　　理智上意识到对方是异性，和感情上意识到对方是异性，是完全不同的感觉。
　　“不是说出门吗？”宇文珠知道李玄霸过于羞涩，虽然自己的勇气也不多，但她比李玄霸大一岁，李玄霸不敢主动，她就要鼓起勇气主动起来。
　　李玄霸点头。
　　他伸出手想牵宇文珠的手，然后想起这个时代的男女之别，又收回手。
　　宇文珠握住李玄霸的手：“扭捏什么？刚已经牵过手了。是不是李二郎和观音婢也会去？他们肯定都等着了。”
　　李玄霸红着脸点头：“嗯。”他前世今生，还是第一次牵同龄女性的手。
　　宇文珠和李玄霸在马车上也没有松开手。
　　他们也没有聊天，只安静地牵着手坐着。
　　待下马车时，他们才耳根绯红地松开手。
　　李世民和长孙小妹果然已经等候多时，已经买了一叠胡饼吃了起来。
　　在他们身旁，李智云腮帮子鼓鼓，不知道已经吃下了多少东西。
　　“你们真是太慢了。”李世民拍了拍手中的胡饼碎屑，对宇文珠作揖，“弟妹，我弟弟是不是很麻烦？你可别嫌弃他啊。”
　　长孙小妹捂嘴笑得花枝乱颤：“大德，你把你平时欺负我兄长的本事拿出来啊，怎么在宇文姐姐面前就变成呆子了？二郎二郎，你看大德的表情，真是好好笑。”
　　李世民点头赞同：“确实很好笑。”
　　未婚小两口笑作一团。
　　李智云继续干饼。这时候他可不会出去找存在感。
　　李玄霸气得脸色黑沉：“你们是不是过于有夫妻相了？”
　　厚脸皮李世民：“谢谢夸奖。”
　　脸皮不薄的长孙小妹：“真的吗？”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　宇文珠叹气，拉了拉李玄霸的袖口：“你别和他们闹，你闹不过他们。”
　　没想到李二郎是与长孙妹妹性情差不多的人。
　　李玄霸冷哼了一声，道：“不是逛街吗？别耽误时间。”
　　李世民看了李玄霸的袖口一眼，很自然地牵起长孙小妹的手：“是你浪费时间。走，今日买东西，明日去郊外踏青。”
　　长孙小妹大大方方握住李世民的手：“我要骑马去！宇文姐姐，你也骑马好不好？”
　　李玄霸和宇文珠看着李世民与长孙小妹十分自然的亲昵模样，心头羞涩不知不觉减轻了不少。
　　李玄霸悄悄看了宇文珠一眼，也伸手牵起宇文珠的手：“骑马吗？你若不会，我教你。”
　　宇文珠红着脸点头。
　　李世民大笑：“哈哈哈哈，观音婢，你听到没，阿玄居然说要教人骑马？他那烂技术，还好意思教人骑马？”
　　长孙小妹戳了戳李世民笑得鼓起来的脸颊：“不可以笑话三郎，三郎又害羞了怎么办？”
　　李世民收起笑容：“哦，好。咳咳，弟妹，其实阿玄骑术还是不错。”
　　李玄霸恼羞成怒：“二哥你闭嘴！”
　　李世民再次大笑。逗弟弟好好玩。
　　李智云默默跟在两对小情侣身后啃饼子。
　　他后悔跟出来了。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 105: A Maiden Comes of Age at Fifteen

Before Li Shimin and Li Xuanba took Li Zhiyun to Zhangye, they first passed through Daxing.
Daxing was home not only to Yuwen Zhu, but also to Zhangsun Xiaomei and Zhangsun Sheng, who were resting at their family estate instead of returning to Luoyang.
Ever since Zhangsun Sheng had feigned illness, he had fully embraced a life of retirement.
Relying on the fact that Emperor Yang Guang’s favor toward him had not yet faded, Zhangsun Sheng occupied the position of Great General while doing absolutely nothing. He spent his days idling at home, occasionally sending gifts to Yang Guang and singing his praises. Yang Guang was very indulgent toward him.
While the three old men—Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and Xue Daoheng—were still busy compiling books and earning their keep, Zhangsun Sheng had perfected the art of being a "salary-sucking parasite."
While lazing at home, Zhangsun Sheng used the pressure of filial piety to force Zhangsun Anye to resign from his official post so he could stay home and "care for his ailing father."
Zhangsun Anye, having finally received the long-awaited love and instruction from his father, was miserable beyond words.
Nowadays, Zhangsun Anye’s relationship with Zhangsun Wuji and Zhangsun Xiaomei had grown much closer. This was because Zhangsun Wuji was shouldering their father’s "loving instruction" alongside him, and their younger sister was the only one who could persuade their father to let him rest.
Li Shimin complained to Li Xuanba, "Look at how that man teaches his son. Why can’t our father do the same?"
Li Xuanba replied, "Can an ordinary person be compared to someone who leaves behind idioms and historical allusions for future generations? Do you know the weight of the ‘killing two birds with one stone’ allusion?"
Li Shimin said, "Our father is a founding emperor, after all!"
Li Xuanba retorted, "Even if he is a founding emperor, he doesn’t have any political idioms associated with him."
Li Shimin hesitated for a moment, then whispered, "Then do I have any political idioms associated with me?"
Li Xuanba replied with a straight face, "Yes, 'a bird leaning on a person' (xiao niao yi ren)."
Li Shimin: "Huh? Am I praising Guanyinbi? How is that a political allusion?"
Li Xuanba shook his head: "You were praising Chu Suiliang."
Li Shimin’s handsome face darkened.
He knew Chu Suiliang. Chu was three years his senior and also studied calligraphy under Master Yu Shinan. Although he didn’t attend as diligently as Li Shimin, they had some acquaintance. Chu was a rather aloof person, and while he was indeed good-looking, could "a bird leaning on a person" really describe him?
Li Shimin shook his head vigorously: "This must be a forced interpretation by later generations. How could I have praised him like that?"
Li Xuanba chuckled: "'Chu Suiliang’s scholarship is profound, and his character is firm and upright. Since he writes with loyalty and is very close to me, it is like a bird leaning on a person, worthy of my affection.'"
Li Shimin stuffed a peeled orange peel into his brother’s mouth to make him shut up, ate the orange segments himself, and never again brought up the topic of whether he had any distinguished idioms to his name.
Li Xuanba spat out the orange peel, ptooey, and made another note in his mental little black book.
Upon arriving in Daxing, Li Shimin tossed his brother—who hadn’t seen Yuwen Zhu in a long time and had become somewhat bashful—directly at the gates of Teacher Yuwen’s residence, then rode off with their fifth brother.
Li Xuanba hadn’t even reacted before he was dumped by Li Shimin, standing alone at the gates of the Yuwen estate. Not only were there no guards, but not even a single eagle had been left for him.
*Han Gou! Wu Di! I wasted my affection on you two!*
"Eh? Isn’t this the Third Young Master?" the gatekeeper asked in surprise.
Li Xuanba stood there awkwardly, unable to speak.
As the fiancé of the young lady of the house, Li Xuanba didn’t need to be announced, and the gatekeeper ushered him straight inside.
Yuwen Bi happened to be practicing his saber in the courtyard behind the main gate. Seeing Li Xuanba, he asked in great confusion, "Why are you here?"
Li Xuanba replied indignantly, "When we passed by Teacher’s gate, Second Brother suddenly ordered the carriage to stop and tossed me out."
Yuwen Bi was stunned for a moment, then burst into laughter: "That sounds like something 'Big Bear' would do. Are you heading to Zhangye to take up your post?"
When he learned that Li Xuanba had arrived empty-handed, with even his spare clothes still in the carriage, Yuwen Bi cursed Li Da-xiong (Big Bear) a few times.
Li Xuanba had just arrived in Daxing and hadn’t even returned to the Tang Duke’s mansion to rest before Li Shimin took a detour to dump him. Li Xuanba hadn’t sensed a thing beforehand. He felt that trusting his Second Brother too much was a mistake.
Yuwen Bi ordered bathwater and fresh clothes to be prepared for Li Xuanba.
People of this era wore very loose clothing, and the Yuwen household was wealthy and well-stocked. Yuwen Bi only needed to have his own new clothes tailored slightly for Li Xuanba to wear.
When Li Xuanba wanted to borrow a carriage to leave, Yuwen Bi said, "Since you’re here, stay at my house for a few days. I imagine that is what Big Bear intended. Perhaps he didn’t want to go back to the Tang Duke’s mansion either, but rather wanted to stay at the Zhangsun estate for a few days."
Li Xuanba’s scalp tingled.
*Damn it! Given Second Brother’s thick skin, he really could do something like that!*
"Taking the Fifth Brother to stay at Teacher Zhangsun’s estate as well?" Li Xuanba’s mouth twitched.
Yuwen Bi said, "It wouldn’t be a problem for Li Fifth Young Master to stay at my house, but you might feel embarrassed."
He smiled and shook his head, feeling a sense of "admiration" for Li Shimin.
For the sake of his thin-skinned brother, Li Da-xiong truly worried about things he shouldn’t, and his methods were far too "extreme."
Upon learning his Second Brother’s intentions, although Li Xuanba could have returned to the Tang Duke’s mansion on his own, he couldn’t very well leave after his teacher had extended an invitation, so he had to bite the bullet and stay.
When Yuwen Zhu learned that Li Xuanba would be staying at their home, she was too shy to come out of her room.
The Old Madam teased Yuwen Zhu, "If it were the young lady of the Zhangsun family, she would already be happily holding her fiancé’s hand and chattering away. Both you and the Third Young Master are so shy, hiding away—what will you do after you’re married? You’re already sixteen; in a year or two, you’ll be married to him."
