**Chapter 107: Using a Great Banner to Make a Tiger Skin**

Household registration records were not merely about population counts; they encompassed the area of uncultivated wasteland, the quantity of already cultivated land, and the number of forests, mountains, and fish ponds available for the common people to harvest.

The Sui Dynasty implemented the Equal-Field System, which it had inherited from the Northern Wei.

Just as Xiao He had salvaged household registration records and official documents before leaving Xianyang, Fang Qiao knew that as long as he obtained the household and land resource data for the various commanderies of Jiangnan, even if the chaos of war were to sweep through the region and cause a sharp decline in population, the Great Tang would still be able to use the local land resource data to immediately redistribute fields and reconstruct household archives.

Unless they were unable to survive, the common people would not flee into the mountains to become "hidden households." The moment the Great Tang completed its land census and initiated a new round of land distribution, the people would descend from the mountains to re-register.

Although they could secretly cultivate land while in the mountains, they were not paying "protection fees" to the government, meaning their personal safety and property could not be guaranteed. Even without formal education, the common people possessed basic survival wisdom; as long as the Tang Dynasty lowered taxes, they would weigh the pros and cons and choose to come down.

From the "Great Investigation of Appearances" (Da Suo Mao Yue) in the third year of Emperor Wen’s Kaihuang era to the strengthening of the "Appearance Examination Law" in the early years of Emperor Yang’s Daye era, the Sui Dynasty had spent nearly thirty years completing the household registration retrieval system as it existed today. If the Tang Dynasty were to start from scratch, it would take at least twenty to thirty years of trial and error.

If Fang Qiao could secure the household registration data for Jiangnan, the Great Tang would be able to utilize the region's means of production the very moment they occupied it.

As for why he needed to scrape this data from the local level instead of taking it directly from the central government, the reason was, of course, that the local officials of the Sui Dynasty were notorious for severely falsifying reports on cultivated land.

Unlike how foreigners listed Emperor Wen of Sui among the "Top 100 People Who Influenced World History," his reputation in later Chinese historical records was not particularly high. While ancient Chinese historians acknowledged his achievements in ending the chaos of war, they did not hold his civil governance in high regard, precisely because the population and land data during his reign were riddled with severe falsehoods.

During the reign of Emperor Wen, the population growth rate was reported at four percent—a figure that even the modern People's Republic of China, with all its technological advantages, only managed to reach three percent. The reported taxable land reached nearly 4 billion mu, whereas the modern PRC, even after developing Xinjiang, Tibet, and the Northeast, only had 2 billion mu. The sheer scale of this data fabrication gave later historians a headache.

This falsified data was layered and compounded. Local data, however, contained fewer errors because it was tied to the actual collection of taxes. The Tang Dynasty had suffered for this at its founding; they had only obtained the central government’s data, while the local records had been lost in the chaos of war. Li Shimin spent over twenty years as Emperor, and for the majority of that time, he was preoccupied with re-surveying the nation's land and population data.

Du Ruhui passed away early, but Fang Qiao served as Li Shimin’s Prime Minister for fifteen years. Of Li Shimin’s twenty-three-year reign, two-thirds were assisted by Fang Qiao, which spoke volumes of his contribution to the "Reign of Zhenguan." Among Li Shimin’s many ministers, Fang Qiao was one of the first to follow him, and it was he who had recommended men like Du Ruhui.

If Du Ruhui’s abilities were slightly short of Zhang Liang’s, then Fang Qiao’s decades of service from following Li Shimin to becoming Prime Minister could absolutely be described as a "reincarnated Xiao He."

Thus, it was only natural that Fang Qiao’s strategic planning would align with that of Xiao He.

On the road to Zhangye, Li Xuanba had also speculated in his thoughts with his Second Brother that Fang Qiao would certainly help them secure the Jiangnan household records.

Li Xuanba: [Fang Xuanling mentioned this to me before he left for his post. However, he is only a minor county magistrate and might not have the opportunity to pull it off. He only said he would try. I also mentioned this to Mother, and she said she would do her utmost to support Fang Xuanling. That Fang Xuanling has this kind of foresight—he is truly the "Xiao He" of the Great Tang.]

Li Shimin scratched his head in frustration.

He desperately wanted to chat with his younger brother, but with Xiao Wu present, he couldn't just blurt out treasonous thoughts.

It wasn't that Li Shimin worried Xiao Wu would betray them; it was simply that Xiao Wu was young, and he feared the boy wouldn't be able to keep a secret.

Li Shimin, of course, also knew of Fang Qiao’s intentions. Whenever he occupied a government office while suppressing bandits in the Central Plains, he would immediately seize the household registration and other official archives.

When the Great Sui army fought, they were like bandits—never leaving empty-handed. Whether it was officials or commoners, everyone assumed the Sui soldiers would strip the area of its wealth, so Li Shimin openly "scraped the ground three feet deep."

As for the impeachment that household records weren't "wealth" and he shouldn't have taken them? Well, hadn't the government office been raided by bandits? It must have been the bandits who did it.

Li Shimin wanted to say that he and Fang Xuanling were truly of one mind. If Fang Xuanling was the "reincarnated Xiao He," then his own vision should also be that of "Xiao He."

No, I should be a combination of Xiao He, Zhang Liang, and Han Xin! Li Shimin proudly put his hands on his hips!

Li Shimin wanted to brag to his brother, but with Xiao Wu here...

Li Shimin nudged the dozing Li Zhiyun awake: "Go sleep in the carriage behind us. I have some serious matters to discuss with your Third Brother."

Li Zhiyun yawned, feeling aggrieved: "Can't I listen?"

Li Shimin said: "You're too young; I'm afraid you'll let something slip. When you're a bit older, I won't hide anything from you."

Li Xuanba: "Pfft."

Li Shimin was puzzled: "What are you laughing at?"

Li Xuanba: [That line sounds so familiar. I used to brush you off with that all the time.]

Li Shimin tried to feign annoyance but couldn't help but laugh: "You have the nerve to say that."

Li Zhiyun looked at his "self-talking" Second Brother, then at his Third Brother, who had definitely said something he couldn't hear. His expression grew even more aggrieved: "Fine, I'll go. You two talk slowly. How old do I have to be to join your conversations?"

Li Shimin thought for a moment and ruffled Li Zhiyun’s hair: "Gan Luo was appointed as a high minister at twelve; Xiao Wu won't be any worse than him. By next year, whatever Ah Xuan and I do, we'll bring you along. But you must work hard; your current skills are far from being able to help us." Next year, Xiao Wu would be twelve by traditional age reckoning.

Upon hearing that he only had to wait until next year to work with his brothers, Li Zhiyun’s grievance vanished instantly.

"I will definitely work hard!" Li Zhiyun gave his Second Brother a hug, then dove into his Third Brother’s arms to act spoiled for a while: "Promise me!"

Li Xuanba held his younger brother: "Mm, I promise."

Li Shimin mocked: "Why don't you start by changing your habit of acting spoiled?"

Li Xuanba said: "Didn't you? Who is it that always rushes into Mother’s arms to act spoiled the moment they get home?"

Li Shimin’s face stiffened.

Li Zhiyun: "Hahahahaha, stop the carriage, I want to get off. Hahahaha, Second Brother, go take your anger out on Third Brother, don't drag me into it."

Li Zhiyun jumped off the carriage, his speed of escape clearly a skill honed since childhood.

Li Shimin flexed his wrists: "Ah Xuan, can you leave me some face in front of Xiao Wu?"

Li Xuanba said: "You didn't avoid Xiao Wu when you were being shameless."

Li Shimin froze. Thinking about it carefully, he supposed that was true.

He lowered his hands: "Forget it, forget it, I won't argue with you. What were you saying before? Oh, right, Fang Xuanling is Xiao He. Look, your brother here thought of that too, and I can also lead troops into battle—I am the trinity of Xiao He, Zhang Liang, and Han Xin!"

Li Xuanba asked: "Then who am I?"

Li Shimin replied without hesitation: "You're a bit worse than me; you're only the duality of Xiao He and Zhang Liang!"

Li Xuanba said: "Are our Great Tang’s Xiao He and Zhang Liang over-qualified? It’s a pity there’s only one Han Xin. Do you want to find another Great Tang Han Xin?"

Li Shimin laughed: "Shouldn't you be the one helping me find him? In your prophetic book, the *Tang Shu*, is there anyone written down who is a military talent only slightly worse than me?"

Li Xuanba was speechless at his Second Brother’s excessive confidence.

What do you mean "slightly worse than me"? How old are you, and how many battles have you fought? You already think your military talent is unrivaled in the world, don't you?

Although that was the truth, Li Xuanba still found his Second Brother’s overconfidence quite annoying.

"Li Jing," Li Xuanba said. "A descendant of the Danyang branch of the Longxi Li clan."

Li Shimin thought for a moment: "I've heard that name. The late Duke of Chu, Yang Su, praised him, and Big Brother has hosted him for banquets as well. Big Brother said he was too arrogant, so he stopped associating with him."

Li Xuanba said: "It’s only natural for him to be arrogant toward us. After our family rose to prominence, we claimed kinship with the Longxi Li clan, but the members of the Longxi Li clan know exactly how that connection came to be; they won't treat us as kin."

Li Shimin sneered: "The Longxi Li clan is one of the 'Five Surnames and Seven Clans' of the Shandong gentry, just like the Xingyang Zheng clan, right? It’s normal for them to have that kind of arrogance."

Li Xuanba teased: "What? Now you have a bad impression of him?"

Li Shimin was curious: "What, does your heavenly book also record that I have a bad impression of him?"

Li Xuanba shook his head: "No, you think very highly of him and kept him in important positions until he passed away in old age."

Li Shimin stroked his chin: "Then he must truly be very talented. And his temperament must have changed quite a bit."

Li Xuanba said: "It changed a lot. He was suppressed heavily by our father, and only under you did he get to be truly utilized."

Li Shimin chuckled: "As expected. His temper was ground away under Father. It seems Father has some skill as an Emperor, being able to grind away the bad tempers of those 'heaven-favored' geniuses. Once I become Emperor, the talented ministers in the court will be well-behaved."

Li Xuanba felt his Second Brother’s words were strange. But thinking about it, it was indeed the case. Because Li Yuan was so excessively self-indulgent as Emperor, by the time his Second Brother took the throne, the ministers all thought his Second Brother was perfect in every way.

However, that was too disrespectful to their father.

Li Xuanba said: "Don't the ministers think you're perfect only because they have Emperor Yang of Sui to compare you to?"

Li Shimin laughed heartily: "That comparison is indeed quite stark. By the way, are there any troublemakers among the ministers I use? I should go and straighten them out in advance."

Li Shimin clenched his fists and flexed his wrists.

Li Xuanba mocked his Second Brother: "You won't be able to bully ministers once you're Emperor, so you're taking advantage of your freedom now to cause enough trouble?"

Li Shimin smiled as he clenched his fists: "Smart."

Li Xuanba joked: "Then go beat up Yuchi Gong in advance. During a court banquet, Yuchi Gong fought with our cousin Li Daozong over seating, punched him in the eye, and nearly blinded him. You scolded him quite angrily, and only then did he change his foul temper. My seat will definitely be higher than his in the future; if this happens again, I fear his fist will land on me."

Li Shimin’s heart tightened for a moment, but he kept a smile on his face: "He dares? If he dares to lay a hand on you, I’ll jump off the dragon bed and beat him to a pulp. I’ll beat him until he loses his teeth and can't get up for a month—not even the entire court of civil and military officials will be able to stop me!"

Li Xuanba said: "You’d better teach him a lesson in advance. Even if you beat him, I’d still have been hit, wouldn't I?"

Li Shimin said solemnly: "Good, I've noted it. When we see him, I'll beat him into submission first. By the way, where is he now?"

Li Xuanba said: "Yuchi Gong’s father is the current Grand General Yuchi Jia. He is fourteen years older than us. As a scion of a noble family, he should be taking advantage of the civil unrest to join the army in Gaoyang to earn merit."

Yuchi Gong was also a scion of a noble family. If it weren't for the fact that his elder clansman Yuchi Jiong was a political enemy of Yang Jian and was killed after raising an army in opposition, the Yuchi family would have had to keep a low profile. With his ability and family background, he would have been an official long ago.

However, he was still a noble scion, so once he joined the army, he was quickly promoted to Court Consultant.

The smile on Li Shimin’s face faded slightly: "Whether it’s Li Jing or Yuchi Jiong, it’s impossible for them to look at us as equals right now."

Li Xuanba shook his head: "If we want to build a connection, given the abilities we've shown, they would certainly be willing to be our friends. But it is absolutely impossible to recruit them."

Was a fourteen-year-old Tiger-Brave General impressive? Yes. But in the sixteen guard offices of the Sui Dynasty, there were several Tiger-Brave Generals in each.

For a fourteen-year-old boy, becoming a Tiger-Brave General was a great achievement. But looking at the court, when a Tiger-Brave General walked down the street, the noble scions wouldn't even deign to give them a glance.

It wasn't just the aristocratic families who were arrogant; the noble scions were the same. Don't look at the fact that Li Jiancheng and other noble scions held low-ranking official positions; their social status was very high.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had saved up some capital in advance, but that capital only gave them a sliver of self-preservation in troubled times. If they wanted to become regional hegemons, anyone with even a slight family background would ignore them.

That was exactly what happened when Li Shimin was recruiting soldiers in Qinghe Commandery.

Li Shimin had released news early on, hoping to gain the assistance of local scholars. But despite his outstanding military achievements, only commoners came to join the army.

Not to mention scholars with some status, even the scions of minor families who hadn't held office for generations didn't come to apply.

The civil clerks and low-level officers in Li Shimin’s army were all household servants brought from the Tang Duke’s mansion.

The more Li Shimin thought about it, the more stifled he felt: "I am young and accomplished; shouldn't I be favored and sought out by talented people?"

Li Xuanba said: "You've muttered that many times already. Fine, it’s the world that is ignorant; there will be plenty of times for them to regret it later."

Li Shimin took a deep breath: "Right! Look at Brother Fang and Brother Du—they are also from official families, and they don't look down on me!"

Li Xuanba said: "They have great insight. How many 'Fang-Du' pairings do you think there have been in five thousand years of Chinese history?"

Five thousand years? When did that start counting from? Li Shimin remembered this unintentional remark from Li Xuanba but didn't ask.

His brother had many secrets, and he had long known they were far more than just "prophecies."

But knowing was enough. His brother didn't hide them, and he wouldn't press him; only then could his brother be at ease in front of him.

Li Shimin nodded repeatedly: "That’s right, that’s right. Sigh, I'm still so dissatisfied. I think if Father were to recruit talent now, many scholars would flock to him. Damn it! I'm clearly much stronger than Father!"

Li Xuanba said slowly: "If they don't choose you, it just means they lack vision and deserve to be suppressed by Brother Fang, Brother Du, and Brother Xue. Oh, right, and Wei Zheng. Since Wei Zheng has joined us early this time, he will also be able to hold his head high in the future."

Li Shimin snorted: "In the future, the Prime Minister position will be rotated among the four of them; no one else gets a turn!"

Li Xuanba couldn't help but laugh: "Hahahahahaha."

Li Shimin laughed along: "Let them be blind. By the way, our abilities will also add to Father’s reputation, right? Yet they abandoned us to join Father—does that count as 'buying the box and returning the pearl'?"

Li Xuanba said: "That definitely counts!"

The brothers' laughter was so loud it carried all the way to the carriage behind them.

Li Zhiyun rested his chin in his hands, his elbows on his knees.

"Sigh, one more year. Time is passing so slowly."

...

While Fang Qiao and Wei Zheng were making their moves, Du Ruhui and Xue Shou were not idle either.

When Yang Yang launched his campaign against Goguryeo, he didn't want Japan to cause trouble, so he sent envoys to Japan. Under Li Xuanba’s suggestion, Xue Shou had infiltrated the envoy group and had not yet returned.

Du Ruhui had become a county magistrate in Zhuojun, wanting to witness the grandeur of the Great Sui army’s expedition up close.

He saw the miserable state of the laborers in Zhuojun and witnessed the excessively extravagant display of Yang Guang.

Du Ruhui once wanted to resign, but he endured it.

If he couldn't bear to look at this now, what would he do after the world truly fell into chaos? Would he just wait in Daxing for Li Erlang and Li Sanlang to arrive with Fang Xuanling? That would be too useless.

Du Ruhui forced himself to endure the discomfort of the incompetent Emperor and the dark court, persisting in his position as magistrate.

He had already guessed the end of the Great Sui.

From the absurdity of the Emperor being repeatedly deceived by Goguryeo, he could see the weaknesses in the Emperor’s character.

Given the Emperor’s personality, he would surely ignore the decline of the Great Sui’s livelihood and launch another campaign against Goguryeo in a short time.

The Great Sui was being smashed to pieces by Yang Guang, hammer blow by hammer blow.

Du Ruhui wanted to watch closely at the very place where Yang Guang was swinging his hammer, to see how a unified dynasty that seemed to be entering a golden age could collapse in an instant at the hands of an absurd Emperor.

He dared not write down his realizations, keeping them all in his heart.

When everything was over, he would compile his experiences and insights into a book to admonish the Emperor of the Great Tang and future generations.

Du Ruhui was frantically absorbing nutrients from the failure of the Great Sui. His political philosophy was rapidly taking shape.

When he received the order for the second campaign against Goguryeo, Du Ruhui knew he could finally escape the sea of misery.

With the current turmoil in the Central Plains of the Great Sui, it was impossible for the Sui army to launch an expedition smoothly.

When the Great Sui army set out and the rear was extremely empty, it was the perfect opportunity to attack the two capitals.

Whether it was the commoner-bandits or the ambitious men in the court, someone would surely raise the banner of rebellion and strike directly at the two capitals. When that happened, the Sui army would be forced to retreat. This battle would never be fought.

Du Ruhui only hoped that the Sui army wouldn't be too chaotic when they retreated, allowing the soldiers and supplies to withdraw safely; otherwise, it would only benefit Goguryeo.

Du Ruhui was only a minor magistrate; he had no standing to offer remonstrance.

However, he was a scion of the Jingzhao Du clan, and even as a branch member, with his official status, he could submit a calling card to visit ministers in the court who were also of the Jingzhao Du clan.

Du Ruhui expressed his concerns to his elders, volunteering to join the supply transport, thinking he might be able to help.

The elder sighed: "Do you think you are the only one in the court who can see this? We can all see it. We have already said everything that could be said; if things aren't being done right, it’s because His Majesty refuses to listen. So, you should stay out of these muddy waters, understand? His Majesty can do no wrong; if something goes wrong, it is the fault of those who carry out the orders."

Du Ruhui sighed: "Yes."

He thought, when the second campaign against Goguryeo fails, I will go find Li Erlang and Li Sanlang.

The blow of the failure of the second Goguryeo campaign would definitely throw the Great Sui into total chaos. By then, Li Erlang and Li Sanlang would surely be short of people.

Du Ruhui inquired about Li Erlang and Li Sanlang from his elders. The last news he had was that they had decided to go to Zhangye.

The elder only knew that they had gone to Zhangye. In such a short time, there wouldn't be any major changes in the court.

Du Ruhui calculated the travel time between Zhangye and Luoyang.

When the Emperor’s second campaign against Goguryeo failed, he would immediately head to Zhangye; surely the news of the failure wouldn't have reached Zhangye yet. Even if the Emperor wanted to mobilize Li Erlang and Li Sanlang, he would wait until he returned to Luoyang. By going to Zhangye in advance, he shouldn't miss them.

"I wonder when Brother Fang will go to Zhangye." Du Ruhui missed his friend.

How happy it was to gather with friends in Daxing and Luoyang. This officialdom of the Great Sui was truly devoid of any interest.

By the time Du Ruhui decided on his departure time for Zhangye, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had returned to Zhangye.

Li Shimin was full of energy and didn't need any rest.

While Li Xuanba and Li Zhiyun rested at home, Li Shimin changed his clothes and went out, visiting everyone he had known in Zhangye one by one.

From border-guarding generals and officials to merchants in the market, Li Shimin knew a great many people, and after ten days, he still hadn't finished visiting them all.

Hearing that Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had returned, nearby Western Region tribes also sent people to visit, hoping to build a connection with them and, through them, link up with the Duke of Tang.

Li Shimin was angry again.

My brother and I are very capable; why must people assume our father is the only one who is capable?

Although Father was indeed not bad.

But since Father wasn't in Zhangye, even though they wanted to cozy up to the Tang Duke’s mansion, they were still being used by Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. Li Shimin suppressed his temper and built friendships with them one by one.

Communication between Zhangye and the Central Plains was poor. For many Western Region people, they might not even know that the dynasty in the Central Plains had changed. Even those who had relations with the court still perceived the Great Sui as it was in the fifth year of Daye—at the height of its power.

It was now only the ninth year of Daye.

In just four short years, according to the thinking of ordinary people, even if the Great Sui wasn't stronger, it should be about the same as before.

Therefore, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba could still rely on the "powerful Great Sui" and didn't have to fear that the Western Region people wouldn't keep their word.

Li Xuanba rested at home for a month before his body adjusted. He also began to take action.

While Li Shimin was training troops and making friends with the Western Region people, Li Xuanba went to visit the Governor of Zhangye.

Emperor Wen of Sui had abolished Zhangye Commandery. It was only after Yang Guang ascended the throne that it was re-established, with Yin Shishi appointed as Governor. After Emperor Wen’s personal campaign against the Tuyuhun ended, Yin Shishi entered the court as a Tiger-Brave General and was now serving as the Garrison Commander of Zhuojun.

The current Governor of Zhangye had only been in office for a few years. Because of the language barrier, he was still feeling his way through the affairs of Zhangye, following old precedents.

Furthermore, Zhangye was a vital military stronghold. The original Governor, Yin Shishi, had held military power, combining civil and military authority. After Yang Guang’s personal campaign ended, he stripped the Governor of his military power, and the current Governor only held administrative authority. But since the affairs of Zhangye were almost entirely related to the military, he had become little more than a figurehead.

When Li Xuanba came to pay his respects, the Governor was quite flattered.

When Yin Shishi was Governor, he held great power, but when Pei Ju came to Zhangye under the Emperor’s orders to oversee the border markets, Yin Shishi had consciously acted as a subordinate who only led troops, transferring all power to Pei Ju.

Now, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had brought their own military power, and the Governor had feared they would bypass him and act as they pleased. He hadn't expected that the Second and Third Young Masters of the Tang Duke’s mansion, despite being highly favored by the Emperor, would be so humble, notifying him before doing anything.

The Governor said respectfully: "Does Doctor Li have any matters? I will certainly give my full support."

In the Sui and Tang officialdom, it was customary to address people by their official titles. To distinguish between Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, officials addressed Li Shimin as "General Li" and Li Xuanba as "Doctor Li"—one using a military title, the other a civil one.

Although the Governor was much older than Li Xuanba, he didn't call him "Third Young Master Li" but "Doctor Li," a subtle way of showing favor and acknowledging the hierarchy between them.

Li Xuanba said: "Governor, why say such things? You are the father-official of Zhangye; it is I who should be assisting you. I studied under General Changsun and General Pei, and they had some ideas regarding the markets of Zhangye. I have compiled them into a document for you to review, hoping to work with you to make Zhangye more prosperous, so that we may return to court together to face the Emperor."

When the Governor heard the names "General Changsun" and "General Pei," his breath hitched for a moment.

Who in the world didn't know the reputation of Changsun Sheng and Pei Ju in managing the Western Regions?

His thoughts raced. He recalled how close Pei Ju had been to Li Erlang and Li Sanlang when he was in Zhangye, and remembered that Changsun Sheng was Li Erlang’s father-in-law. He felt he had figured it out.

No wonder the Emperor sent the accomplished Li Erlang and Li Sanlang to Zhangye. This wasn't a slight; it was because General Changsun and General Pei no longer had the energy to manage the Western Regions, and since Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were their disciples, the Emperor had entrusted this important task to these two young generals.

Don't look at their low official ranks; think of their background and the relationships behind them. The Emperor had handed them the entire power of dealing with the Western Regions—this was a case of low rank but heavy authority!

The Governor carefully pondered the phrase "return to court together to face the Emperor."

Did the Third Young Master mean that in the future, when their mission was complete, they would put in a good word for him before the Emperor, so he wouldn't have to keep eating sand at a border town?

The Governor was overjoyed.

He took a moment to steady his voice and said seriously: "This is my duty. Third Young Master, rest assured, I will definitely not fail the plans of General Changsun and General Pei."

Li Xuanba smiled: "My Second Brother and I will be relying on you, Governor."

The Governor laughed: "I wouldn't dare."

Li Xuanba unfolded the document and explained his reforms for the border markets to the Governor one by one.

The most important point was that since the border was currently peaceful, and the Emperor loved fine horses and hunting dogs, he hoped to open up trade routes directly with the tribes, bypassing middlemen to avoid price markups. They would lead the trade in the name of the Great Sui government, sending merchant caravans to trade goods with the tribes.

"This, of course, is not in the capacity of officials, but rather we will issue special certificates to the merchant caravans that reduce certain taxes, and let the border troops serve as escorts for the caravans," Li Xuanba said with a smile. "Now that the Emperor is personally campaigning against Goguryeo, the court is tight on money. This way, we can self-fund some of our expenses and reduce the burden on the court. Governor, rest assured, my Second Brother and I will take full responsibility, and the Emperor is also aware of this."

The Governor was a bit worried. He thought for a moment and said: "Military matters are for General Li and Doctor Li to decide; I dare not interfere. I will issue the tax-reduction certificates, but the formation of the caravans and the border troop escorts must be decided by General Li and Doctor Li themselves."

A significant portion of market tax revenue was kept by the local government to be used for local finances. So, reducing a certain amount of market tax wouldn't be a problem for him. As for the parts that might lead to blame from the court, he didn't want to get involved.

"Good," Li Xuanba said readily. "We will each perform our own duties."

Hearing Li Xuanba so readily take responsibility, with no intention of dragging him into the mud, the Governor felt a bit ashamed of his suspicions.

He quickly said: "Although it is not my responsibility, as long as it is something I can help with, Doctor Li, please feel free to ask!"

Li Xuanba bowed with a smile: "Then I won't stand on ceremony."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第108章 千里迢迢来投奔
chunks.chineseText:
第108章 千里迢迢来投奔

有了张掖郡守的支持， 李玄霸给二哥攒骑兵战马的进度又迈进一步。
　　李玄霸将中原之事都交给母亲后，这次将颜真和向固带在了身边。
　　“常用突厥语学会了吗？”李玄霸检查下属功课。
　　颜真苦笑：“才背一半。”
　　向固抓耳挠腮。
　　陈铁牛疑惑：“这么简单，怎么会背不下？”
　　颜真和向固无语地看向陈铁牛。
　　李玄霸干咳了一声， 道：“铁牛， 你语言天赋很强， 别拿你擅长的地方和别人比。”
　　陈铁牛更疑惑：“我擅长的又不是说突厥语，是当郎君的护卫！”
　　李玄霸：“……是，你说得对。”
　　颜真：“再给我三天， 我一定全背下！”
　　向固继续抓耳挠腮。
　　叶护失笑：“三郎，你别折磨他们。我给他们翻译。”
　　李玄霸摇头：“我希望他们也能独当一面。这点小事都指望你，你还要不要做大事了？你的精力不能用在给人当翻译上。”
　　叶护心中一暖：“那我来教他们。”
　　李玄霸道：“拜托你了。对了， 二哥在哪？他今日不是说找你玩了吗？怎么你在这？”
　　叶护道：“啊？我没见到二郎，他去找我了吗？是错过了？”
　　李玄霸伸出手：“寒钩。”
　　一声清脆的鸟鸣， 寒钩落到了李玄霸手臂上。
　　“带我去寻二哥。”李玄霸吩咐道， “我有要事要寻他，不准替他隐瞒。”
　　寒钩人性化地叹了口气，点头。
　　虽然乌镝和寒钩是叶护送给李世民和李玄霸的，但每次看到这两只雕过分聪明的表现，叶护还是啧啧称奇。
　　去大隋经商是十分肥美的差事， 他族中常安排年轻贵族轮换同行享乐。不怪这些没见识的人每次见到寒钩和乌镝就膝盖软，认为见到了真正的神灵。
　　李玄霸吩咐道：“你们好好学， 等入夏后就去干活。铁牛，把绳子带上。如果二哥是去玩赌斗鸡斗狗，就把他捆回来。”
　　陈铁牛只听李玄霸的话：“是， 郎君。”
　　颜真忍不住笑道：“勋贵子弟玩斗狗斗鸡很正常。”
　　李玄霸气势汹汹道：“赌什么都不正常。单纯玩可以， 敢上赌桌， 我就写信让母亲骂他。”
　　他发现二哥居然背着他赌斗鸡斗狗的时候， 头发都要炸开了。
　　封建时代不禁“黄”，但“赌”和“毒”，二哥敢沾他就敢立刻策马飞奔回洛阳请母亲出山。
　　就算二哥是孙猴子，母亲的巴掌也能呼死他！
　　见二哥这次出门居然说谎，李玄霸心中警钟大震。
　　李玄霸跟着寒钩气势汹汹出门逮二哥。
　　途中他去寻找了李智云，发现小五被二哥带走了，脸色更加阴沉。
　　二哥不仅自己赌博，还带着小五？！
　　寒钩把李玄霸引到了张掖城郊一处草场上。
　　这草场是李玄霸从张掖郡守手中拿到的公家草场，公器私用给二哥放养部曲的战马。
　　李玄霸疑惑：“只是来骑马？那为什么瞒着我？”
　　寒钩落在了李玄霸的手臂上，抬起爪子为李玄霸指方向。
　　李玄霸下马，让护卫放低声音，轻手轻脚地去看二哥在干什么？
　　不一会儿，他就发现了轻手轻脚没意义。
　　李世民的部曲围成一个大圈子，正在比摔跤。
　　华夏从古至今都有比摔跤的爱好，唐朝时宫廷里还有“相扑棚”专门管理为皇帝表演的摔跤手。
　　李智云拿着锣哐哐敲响：“来来来，下注了！买定离手！看李郎将还能赢几次！”
　　李玄霸：“？”
　　陈铁牛给护卫们使了个眼色，所有跟随李玄霸的护卫退后几步。
　　李玄霸抽出腰间长剑气势汹汹地走进了摔跤场。
　　刚赢了一局的李世民正叉腰大笑，见李玄霸过来，转身就跑：“啊？阿玄你怎么在这？不是，我没赌，你生什么气！和部下角力是训练的一部分！”
　　李玄霸气笑了：“你是不赌了，你祖宗的变坐庄了！”
　　李世民一边逃还一边回头笑：“阿玄，我祖宗也是你祖宗，你骂我什么都会回旋到你自己身上。别跑了，你追不上我。”
　　李智云拦在了李世民面前，还举起了铜锣。
　　李世民：“啊？我草！小五你……”
　　“哐”的一声，躲闪不及的李世民撞到了铜锣上。
　　李智云放下铜锣，对李玄霸乖巧道：“我将功补过。”
　　李玄霸拽住二哥的领子：“你的部下才多少粮饷？赌没了喝西北风？”
　　一个将领立刻道：“三郎君，你误会二郎君了。我们赌的不是钱，是训练量？”
　　李玄霸道：“我不信。如果真的这么正常，他躲什么？”
　　将领犹豫了一下，不知道要不要出卖主将。
　　李世民揉着额头道：“我躲什么？我怎么躲得过你，不过是去找叶护的途中心血来潮而已。”
　　李智云道：“二哥打赌，输光的人要脱光衣服训练。二哥如果战胜的人不够多也一样。”
　　李世民望天，吹口哨。
　　李玄霸歪头震惊。
　　这什么沙雕男高中生行为啊？！你怎么能幼稚到和沙雕男高中生……啊，等等，二哥现在的年龄是比沙雕男高中生更可怕的沙雕男中二生。
　　李玄霸松开手，笑骂道：“你要不要脸？”
　　李世民傻笑糊弄：“嘿嘿。”
　　李玄霸道：“行，既然不赌钱，你随意。我监督你，一定要脱，我还要给你画下来。”
　　李世民认怂：“画下来就不用了……你不生气？”
　　李玄霸认真道：“你自己丢你自己的脸，我生什么气？我还挺想看乐子。”
　　李世民突然就不想坐这个庄了。
　　李智云老气横秋地唉声叹气。
　　如果不是想看二哥脱光了训练丢脸的模样，他才不会给二哥敲锣。
　　知道只是一场闹剧后，李玄霸让他们继续玩，正事等会儿再说。
　　他真的想看这群军汉光着身子在大草原上跑步，一定很壮观。
　　或许是李玄霸看乐子的神情太过明显，本来没脸没皮的军汉子们都扭捏起来。
　　李世民道：“今天把战绩记下，明天再比。阿玄，你明天不能来，你一来他们就欢乐不起来。”
　　李玄霸疑惑：“为什么？”
　　李世民叹气：“你看着就不像胡闹的人，他们看到你都很紧张。”
　　李玄霸困惑极了。他怎么也想不出自己哪里能让人紧张了。自己应该比二哥这个真正的勋贵子弟“屌丝”多了吧？
　　李世民宣布解散后，军汉子们作鸟兽散，跑路的速度好像有老虎在后面追似的。
　　周达曾经执行过保护李玄霸的任务，与李玄霸同去过泰山，与陈铁牛最熟悉。
　　路过陈铁牛的时候，周达勾肩搭背小声道：“跟着三郎君压力很大吧，同情你。”
　　陈铁牛点头：“郎君光风霁月，对自己严格对别人也严格。”
　　李玄霸往陈铁牛那边看，他总觉得有人说他坏话，可能是错觉。
　　“你来找我做什么？不会只是怀疑我赌斗吧？”李世民抱怨，“你怎么不信任我？”
　　李玄霸道：“请你自己反省一下我为什么不信任你。确实有事。商队物资已经准备好了，二哥你点五百人护卫。”
　　李世民好奇：“五百人护卫？这不仅仅是护卫吧？”
　　李玄霸道：“路上扮作突厥人抢劫。”
　　李世民磨拳擦掌：“我想去！”
　　李玄霸给二哥丢了个白眼：“等你先把张掖的军队全部收编后再去，到时候别说抢劫，就是去攻占城池灭掉西域国，我都不拦你。”
　　李世民笑道：“那你可要给我把后勤准备好，我不想打着打着仗饿肚子。唉，听说上次皇帝征高丽时好多人都饿了肚子。”
　　李世民笑容淡去。他摸了摸自己的肚子：“我一日不吃饱就难受得紧。想着前线将士挨饿，后方百姓更是饿殍遍地，我真是难以想象。”
　　李玄霸道：“放心，我不会让你打仗的时候被饿得哇哇直哭。我保障不了你的后勤，也还有小五在。”
　　李智云道：“我不是跟着二兄去打仗吗？”
　　李世民揉了揉李智云的脑袋：“好，我们一起去前线。你三兄不给我们运粮，我们兄弟二人就一起挨饿。等你三兄来的时候就都抱着你三兄哇哇哭，把眼泪和鼻涕都抹他身上。”
　　李智云笑道：“好。三兄，这个我听二兄的。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“我尽力吧。”
　　他急着搞商队搞义庄，就是想着自己死后二哥拿着自己留下的东西，也不会像在历史中那样一边打仗一边饿得哇哇哭，最后打仗还得一边打一边自筹粮草。
　　李世民道：“如果这次任务不是特别重要，我有个小兵想塞进去，给他历练的机会。如果他真的有本事，我想把他放在身边培养。”
　　李玄霸道：“你自己决定就行。”军中的事李玄霸只管后勤。
　　李世民道：“我这是给你介绍我的新朋友，走，去见见他，他今日才到。”
　　李玄霸皱眉：“今日才到？”
　　李世民道：“我出城的时候正好遇到他询问城门守卒去哪里投奔我，我就把他带上了。这次摔跤其实就是为他准备的。不过他太逞强，路上疲惫过度，赢完几场后睡过去了。”
　　李世民想着他倒头就睡的模样，笑道：“有点像我。”
　　李玄霸看着二哥“慈祥”的笑容，感觉古怪极了。
　　你才十四岁，你慈祥什么？
　　李智云叹气：“本来以为二兄这么厉害的人万里挑一，我不和二兄比。没想到又出现一个，好烦。”
　　李玄霸屈指敲了敲李智云的额头：“你烦什么？天生我才必有用，他们有他们擅长的地方，你也有你擅长的地方。再说了，人才多多益善。这么大的国家，能容下很多人才。”
　　李智云笑着点头：“嗯。”
　　“好了，别训小五了，走，不知道他醒没有。”李世民穿好外袍，“乌镝，别躲了，出来。”
　　乌镝从天空落到地上。
　　李玄霸把落在地上的乌镝抱起来：“你没和二哥一起胡闹，我就不会骂你。你怕什么？”
　　乌镝：“啾！”
　　寒钩站在李玄霸肩膀上，嫌弃地叹了口气，扑腾翅膀飞到了李世民肩膀上落下。
　　乌镝之前挨骂，是因为李世民斗鸡的时候把乌镝派了出去。
　　这人不要脸，雕也不要脸，居然说什么落地的猎鹰不如鸡，加入斗鸡很正常。一人一雕都玩疯了。
　　李玄霸询问乌镝二哥做什么的时候，乌镝还帮忙隐瞒，坚称他们就是去训练了。结果被李玄霸抓个正着。
　　李玄霸叹气，来到张掖之后天高地阔，不仅二哥玩疯了，雕也玩疯了。
　　李世民带着李玄霸来到一顶帐篷前。他还没有出声，帐篷门拉开一条缝，冒出个总角小脑袋。
　　“我只是累了！不是输了！不要赶我走！”小孩叫道。
　　李世民哭笑不得：“不赶你走。我给你介绍我弟弟阿玄，李玄霸李三郎。阿玄，这就是我要给你介绍的人，叫罗士信，现在无字，你称呼他名即可。”
　　李玄霸：“哦。”
　　李玄霸：“哦？叫什么？哪里人？！”
　　小孩脖子一缩，然后又觉得这样太怂，梗着脖子道：“我叫罗士信！齐郡人！我十四了！很厉害！比成年人都厉害！”
　　李世民虚虚按了一下手：“安静。我知道你很厉害。接下来我就要让你去执行任务，给你展现自己的机会。”
　　小孩眼睛一亮：“真的？什么任务？”
　　李世民道：“护卫前往回纥的商队，顺便扮作突厥人抢突厥人。”
　　小孩疑惑：“扮作突厥人抢突厥人？这有什么意义啊，他们会相信自己人抢自己人？”
　　李世民解释道：“突厥分许多部落，每个部落都有独立的部曲，彼此只是结盟，不是像大隋这样真的奉可汗为主。”
　　小孩摇头：“听不懂。”
　　李世民板着脸道：“听不懂就好好听，多听多学。只会打仗算什么本事？只会指哪打哪只是能打的莽夫。你还小，现在就这么有本事，多学点东西，将来当统领更多军队的将帅青史留名岂不更好。”
　　小孩苦着脸道：“都听郎君的。”
　　李世民道：“打仗的机会我会给你，但你功课也不能落下。就是在马背上，你也得手不释卷。等你回来我要考。如果完成不了功课，下次就不带你，你乖乖读书。”
　　小孩的脸色更苦了：“郎将，你比我阿父还啰嗦。我阿父都没逼着我读书。”
　　李世民失笑：“你还好意思说。赶紧给家里写信，别让你父母太着急。阿玄，这小孩居然是离家出走，我真是服了。”
　　小孩叉腰道：“我没有离家出走！我投军是得到父母同意的！只是张将军不肯重用我，我另寻他处而已！”
　　李玄霸都听迷糊了：“什么离家出走？二哥，你能不能从头到尾给我详细解释一下。”
　　李世民拍了拍小孩半光的脑袋：“你自己说。”
　　小孩：“哦。”
　　他老老实实把自己的经历讲了出来。
　　罗士信，虚岁十四岁，周岁还没到十三岁。
　　去年底，他谎称自己十四岁，进入张须陀军中效力。张须陀虽然看好他，但因为他年幼，没有将他派往战场。
　　罗士信非常生气。
　　正好他听到了李二郎这个少年郎将的名声，琢磨着李世民也是年少成名，一定能理解自己这个少年天才。于是他借口回家，向张须陀请辞，居然千里迢迢从山东跑到了张掖来投奔李世民。
　　张须陀是个好人，本就怜惜罗士信年幼，便放罗士信离开。谁知道罗士信根本没回家，径直跑张掖来了。
　　李玄霸倒吸一口气，不敢置信地看着这个小鬼头。
　　独自一人跨越大半个华国，从山东跑来甘肃投奔二哥？！
　　看着罗士信倔强的双眼，李玄霸扶住额头：“赶紧给你父母送信！”
chunks.englishText:
**Chapter 108: Traveling Thousands of Miles to Join**

With the support of the Zhangye Commandery Governor, Li Xuanba’s progress in stockpiling warhorses for his Second Brother took another step forward.

Having delegated the affairs of the Central Plains to his mother, Li Xuanba brought Yan Zhen and Xiang Gu along with him this time.

"Have you learned the common Turkic phrases yet?" Li Xuanba checked his subordinates' progress.

Yan Zhen gave a bitter smile. "I’ve only memorized half."

Xiang Gu scratched his head and ears in distress.

Chen Tieniu asked, puzzled, "It’s so simple, how can you not have memorized it?"

Yan Zhen and Xiang Gu looked at Chen Tieniu, speechless.

Li Xuanba coughed dryly and said, "Tieniu, you have a strong talent for languages; don't compare your strengths to others."

Chen Tieniu was even more confused. "My strength isn't speaking Turkic, it’s being the Young Master’s bodyguard!"

Li Xuanba: "…Yes, you’re right."

Yan Zhen: "Give me three more days, I will definitely memorize it all!"

Xiang Gu continued to scratch his head and ears.

Yehu chuckled. "Third Young Master, don't torture them. I’ll translate for them."

Li Xuanba shook his head. "I want them to be able to stand on their own. If they rely on you for such trivial matters, how will you ever accomplish great things? Your energy should not be spent acting as a translator."

Yehu felt a warmth in his heart. "Then I will teach them."

Li Xuanba said, "I’ll leave it to you. By the way, where is Second Brother? Didn't he say he was going to find you to hang out today? Why are you here?"

Yehu asked, "Ah? I haven't seen Second Young Master. Did he go looking for me? Did we miss each other?"

Li Xuanba extended his arm: "Han Gou."

With a crisp cry, a bird landed on Li Xuanba’s arm.

"Take me to find Second Brother," Li Xuanba commanded. "I have urgent matters to discuss with him. You are not allowed to hide him."

Han Gou sighed in a human-like manner and nodded.

Although Wu Di and Han Gou were gifts from Yehu to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, Yehu still marveled at the excessive intelligence of these two eagles every time he saw them.

Trading in the Great Sui was a highly lucrative job, and his tribe often arranged for young nobles to take turns accompanying the caravans for pleasure. It was no wonder these ignorant people went weak at the knees every time they saw Han Gou and Wu Di, believing they had encountered true deities.

Li Xuanba instructed, "You all study hard. Once summer arrives, you’ll be put to work. Tieniu, bring the rope. If Second Brother is out gambling on cockfights or dogfights, tie him up and bring him back."

Chen Tieniu only listened to Li Xuanba. "Yes, Young Master."

Yan Zhen couldn't help but laugh. "It’s quite normal for young nobles to play at dogfights and cockfights."

Li Xuanba said aggressively, "Gambling on anything is not normal. Playing for fun is fine, but if he dares to step up to a gambling table, I will write a letter to Mother to scold him."

When he discovered that his Second Brother was actually gambling on cockfights and dogfights behind his back, his hair nearly stood on end.

In this feudal era, "lust" wasn't strictly prohibited, but if his Second Brother dared to touch "gambling" or "drugs," he would immediately gallop back to Luoyang to ask his mother to intervene.

Even if his Second Brother were the Monkey King, his mother’s palm could slap him into oblivion!

Seeing that his Second Brother had actually lied about going out, alarm bells rang loudly in Li Xuanba’s heart.

Li Xuanba followed Han Gou out, aggressively hunting for his Second Brother.

On the way, he went to look for Li Zhiyun and discovered that the little fifth brother had been taken away by his Second Brother, causing his expression to darken further.

Not only was Second Brother gambling himself, but he was also dragging Little Five along?!

Han Gou led Li Xuanba to a pasture on the outskirts of Zhangye City.

This pasture was public land Li Xuanba had obtained from the Zhangye Commandery Governor, which he had repurposed for his Second Brother to graze the warhorses of his personal troops.

Li Xuanba was suspicious: "Just coming to ride horses? Then why hide it from me?"

Han Gou landed on Li Xuanba’s arm and raised a claw to point the way.

Li Xuanba dismounted, told his guards to lower their voices, and tiptoed over to see what his Second Brother was doing.

Before long, he realized that tiptoeing was pointless.

Li Shimin’s troops were gathered in a large circle, wrestling.

From ancient times to the present, the Chinese have had a penchant for wrestling; in the Tang Dynasty, there were even "Sumo Sheds" in the palace specifically for managing wrestlers who performed for the Emperor.

Li Zhiyun held a gong and struck it: "Come, come, place your bets! Bets are closed! Let’s see how many more times Commander Li can win!"

Li Xuanba: "?"

Chen Tieniu signaled the guards, and all the guards following Li Xuanba stepped back a few paces.

Li Xuanba drew the long sword at his waist and marched into the wrestling ring, looking fierce.

Li Shimin, who had just won a round, was standing with his hands on his hips, laughing. Seeing Li Xuanba approach, he turned and ran: "Ah? A-Xuan, why are you here? No, I’m not gambling, why are you angry! Wrestling with subordinates is part of training!"

Li Xuanba was so angry he laughed: "You aren't gambling? Your ancestors have become the bookies!"

Li Shimin kept running while looking back and laughing: "A-Xuan, my ancestors are your ancestors too; whatever you curse me with will bounce back on you. Stop running, you can't catch me."

Li Zhiyun blocked Li Shimin’s path, holding up the copper gong.

Li Shimin: "Ah? Damn it! Little Five, you..."

With a "clang," the dodging Li Shimin bumped right into the gong.

Li Zhiyun put down the gong and said to Li Xuanba, acting innocent: "I’m making up for my mistakes."

Li Xuanba grabbed his Second Brother by the collar: "How much grain and pay do your subordinates get? If they lose it all gambling, are they going to drink the northwest wind?"

A commander immediately said, "Third Young Master, you’ve misunderstood the Second Young Master. We aren't gambling for money; we’re gambling for training quotas!"

Li Xuanba said, "I don't believe it. If it were really that normal, why was he hiding?"

The commander hesitated, unsure whether to betray his commanding officer.

Li Shimin rubbed his forehead and said, "What was I hiding? How could I hide from you? It was just a whim on the way to find Yehu."

Li Zhiyun added, "Second Brother made a bet: whoever loses has to train naked. If Second Brother doesn't defeat enough people, he has to do the same."

Li Shimin looked up at the sky and whistled.

Li Xuanba tilted his head in shock.

What kind of brain-dead high schooler behavior is this?! How can you be so childish as to... ah, wait, his Second Brother’s current age is even more terrifying than a brain-dead high schooler—he’s a brain-dead middle-schooler.

Li Xuanba let go and scolded with a laugh: "Do you have no shame?"

Li Shimin giggled to brush it off: "Heh heh."

Li Xuanba said, "Fine, since you aren't gambling money, do as you please. I’ll supervise you. You must strip, and I’m going to draw it."

Li Shimin conceded: "No need to draw it... You aren't angry?"

Li Xuanba said seriously, "You’re the one losing face, why would I be angry? I actually quite enjoy the show."

Li Shimin suddenly didn't want to be the bookie anymore.

Li Zhiyun sighed with the world-weariness of an old man.

If it weren't for wanting to see his Second Brother strip and train in shame, he wouldn't have beaten the gong for him.

Knowing it was just a farce, Li Xuanba told them to continue playing and that they would discuss official business later.

He really wanted to see this group of soldiers running naked across the vast grassland; it would certainly be a spectacular sight.

Perhaps Li Xuanba’s amusement was too obvious, as the previously shameless soldiers began to act bashful.

Li Shimin said, "Record the results today and compete again tomorrow. A-Xuan, you can't come tomorrow. They can't have fun when you’re around."

Li Xuanba was puzzled: "Why?"

Li Shimin sighed: "You don't look like someone who would mess around, so they get nervous when they see you."

Li Xuanba was extremely confused. He couldn't figure out why he would make anyone nervous. He should be much more of a "loser" than his Second Brother, who was a genuine young noble, right?

After Li Shimin announced the dismissal, the soldiers scattered like birds and beasts, running as if a tiger were chasing them.

Zhou Da had once carried out a mission to protect Li Xuanba and had traveled to Mount Tai with him, so he was most familiar with Chen Tieniu.

As he passed Chen Tieniu, Zhou Da hooked his arm around him and whispered, "It must be stressful following the Third Young Master. I sympathize with you."

Chen Tieniu nodded. "The Young Master is as bright and clear as the wind and moon; he is strict with himself and strict with others."

Li Xuanba looked toward Chen Tieniu; he always felt someone was bad-mouthing him, but it might just be his imagination.

"Why did you come to find me? Surely not just to suspect me of gambling?" Li Shimin complained. "Why don't you trust me?"

Li Xuanba said, "Please reflect on why I don't trust you. There is indeed business. The caravan supplies are ready; Second Brother, pick five hundred men to guard it."

Li Shimin was curious: "Five hundred guards? This isn't just for protection, is it?"

Li Xuanba said, "Pretend to be Turks and rob people on the road."

Li Shimin rubbed his hands together: "I want to go!"

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes at his Second Brother: "Wait until you’ve fully incorporated the Zhangye army before you go. When that time comes, I won't stop you even if you want to rob, conquer cities, or wipe out Western Region kingdoms."

Li Shimin laughed: "Then you must prepare the logistics for me; I don't want to go hungry while fighting. Sigh, I heard that when the Emperor campaigned against Goguryeo last time, many people went hungry."

Li Shimin’s smile faded. He touched his own stomach: "I feel terrible if I don't eat my fill for a single day. Thinking of the soldiers on the front lines starving, and the people in the rear suffering from famine, I truly can't imagine it."

Li Xuanba said, "Don't worry, I won't let you cry your eyes out from hunger while fighting. If I can't guarantee your logistics, there’s still Little Five."

Li Zhiyun asked, "Am I not going to war with Second Brother?"

Li Shimin ruffled Li Zhiyun’s hair: "Good, we’ll go to the front lines together. If your Third Brother doesn't ship us grain, we brothers will starve together. When your Third Brother comes, we’ll both hug him and wail, wiping our tears and snot all over him."

Li Zhiyun laughed: "Good. Third Brother, I’ll listen to Second Brother on this."

Li Xuanba sighed: "I’ll do my best."

He was in such a hurry to set up the caravan and the charitable estates because he wanted to ensure that after he died, his Second Brother would have the resources he left behind, so he wouldn't end up like in history—crying from hunger while fighting, and having to scrounge for his own supplies mid-campaign.

Li Shimin said, "If this mission isn't particularly critical, I have a young soldier I’d like to insert into the group to give him a chance to gain experience. If he truly has talent, I want to keep him by my side to cultivate him."

Li Xuanba said, "Decide for yourself." Li Xuanba only handled logistics for military matters.

Li Shimin said, "I’m introducing you to my new friend. Come, let’s go see him; he only arrived today."

Li Xuanba frowned: "He only arrived today?"

Li Shimin said, "I happened to run into him at the city gate when he was asking the guards where to find me, so I brought him along. The wrestling match today was actually arranged for him. But he was too stubborn and exhausted from the journey; after winning a few rounds, he fell asleep."

Thinking of the way he had collapsed into sleep, Li Shimin laughed: "He’s a bit like me."

Li Xuanba looked at his Second Brother’s "benevolent" smile and felt it was extremely strange.

You’re only fourteen, what are you being benevolent about?

Li Zhiyun sighed: "I thought someone as amazing as Second Brother was one in ten thousand, so I wouldn't compare myself to him. I didn't expect another one to appear. How annoying."

Li Xuanba tapped Li Zhiyun’s forehead with his finger: "What are you annoyed about? Everyone has their own talent; they have their strengths, and you have yours. Besides, the more talent, the better. Such a vast country can accommodate many talents."

Li Zhiyun nodded with a smile: "Mm."

"Alright, stop lecturing Little Five. Let’s go, I don't know if he’s awake yet." Li Shimin put on his outer robe. "Wu Di, stop hiding, come out."

Wu Di descended from the sky to the ground.

Li Xuanba picked up the eagle that had landed on the ground: "I won't scold you as long as you don't mess around with Second Brother. What are you afraid of?"

Wu Di: "Chirp!"

Han Gou, standing on Li Xuanba’s shoulder, sighed in disdain and flapped its wings to land on Li Shimin’s shoulder.

Wu Di had been scolded earlier because Li Shimin had sent it out during the cockfights.

This man had no shame, and the eagle had no shame either, actually claiming that a hunting falcon on the ground was no better than a chicken, so joining the cockfight was perfectly normal. Both man and bird had gone wild.

When Li Xuanba asked Wu Di what his Second Brother was doing, Wu Di had even helped cover for him, insisting they were just training. As a result, they were caught red-handed by Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba sighed. Since arriving in Zhangye, the sky was high and the land was wide; not only had his Second Brother gone wild, but the eagles had gone wild too.

Li Shimin led Li Xuanba to a tent. Before he could speak, the tent flap opened a crack, and a small head with hair tied in buns poked out.

"I’m just tired! I didn't lose! Don't drive me away!" the child shouted.

Li Shimin was caught between laughter and tears: "I’m not driving you away. Let me introduce you to my brother, A-Xuan, Li Xuanba, the Third Young Master Li. A-Xuan, this is the person I wanted to introduce to you, his name is Luo Shixin. He doesn't have a courtesy name yet, so you can just call him by his given name."

Li Xuanba: "Oh."

Li Xuanba: "Oh? What’s his name? Where is he from?!"

The child shrank his neck, but then felt that was too cowardly, so he stiffened his neck and said: "My name is Luo Shixin! From Qi Commandery! I’m fourteen! I’m very strong! Stronger than any adult!"

Li Shimin pressed his hand down gently: "Quiet. I know you’re very strong. I’m about to have you execute a mission to give you a chance to prove yourself."

The child’s eyes lit up: "Really? What mission?"

Li Shimin said, "Guard a caravan heading to the Huihe, and while you’re at it, pretend to be Turks and rob the Turks."

The child was confused: "Pretend to be Turks and rob Turks? What’s the point of that? Would they believe their own people are robbing them?"

Li Shimin explained: "The Turks are divided into many tribes, each with its own independent troops. They are merely allied with each other, not truly serving a Khan like we do in the Great Sui."

The child shook his head: "I don't understand."

Li Shimin put on a stern face: "If you don't understand, then listen carefully and learn more. What kind of talent is it to only know how to fight? Only knowing how to strike where you’re pointed makes you nothing but a reckless brute. You’re still young, and since you’re so capable now, if you learn more, wouldn't it be better to become a general who commands more troops and leaves a name in history?"

The child said with a bitter face: "I’ll listen to the Young Master."

Li Shimin said, "I will give you opportunities to fight, but you cannot neglect your studies. Even on horseback, you must keep a book in your hand. I will test you when you return. If you don't finish your lessons, I won't take you next time; you can just stay and study obediently."

The child’s face became even more bitter: "Commander, you’re more long-winded than my father. My father never forced me to study."

Li Shimin chuckled: "You have the nerve to say that. Hurry up and write a letter home so your parents don't worry. A-Xuan, this kid actually ran away from home; I’m truly impressed."

The child put his hands on his hips: "I didn't run away from home! My parents agreed to me joining the army! It’s just that General Zhang wouldn't put me to use, so I went looking elsewhere!"

Li Xuanba was completely bewildered: "What running away from home? Second Brother, can you explain this to me in detail from beginning to end?"

Li Shimin patted the child’s partially shaved head: "You tell him."

The child: "Oh."

He honestly recounted his experience.

Luo Shixin, fourteen years old by nominal age, not even thirteen by actual age.

Late last year, he lied about being fourteen and joined Zhang Xutuo’s army. Although Zhang Xutuo thought highly of him, he didn't send him to the battlefield because he was too young.

Luo Shixin was very angry.

Just then, he heard of the young commander Li Erlang, and figured that since Li Shimin was also famous at a young age, he would surely understand a young genius like himself. So, he made an excuse to go home, asked Zhang Xutuo for leave, and actually traveled thousands of miles from Shandong to Zhangye to join Li Shimin.

Zhang Xutuo was a good man and had pitied Luo Shixin for his youth, so he let him go. Who knew that Luo Shixin hadn't gone home at all, but had run straight to Zhangye.

Li Xuanba gasped, looking at the little brat in disbelief.

Traveled across more than half of China all by himself, from Shandong to Gansu to join his Second Brother?!

Looking at Luo Shixin’s stubborn eyes, Li Xuanba held his forehead: "Hurry up and send a letter to your parents!"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第109章 大丈夫不居人下
chunks.chineseText:
第109章 大丈夫不居人下

李玄霸总算知道为什么二哥会一脸慈祥表情了。
　　这熊孩子要是落到自己手上， 保准先一顿揍。自己揍不动就让其他人按着揍。
　　十三岁少年郎独自一人背着包袱骑着瘦马跨越大半个华国，别说如今是乱世，就是在治安良好的现代社会都让人头皮发麻。
　　李玄霸和李世民虽然出远门时年龄更小， 但他们带着一大堆仆从护卫， 和这熊孩子完全不一样。
　　“你是要跟我们回府里住， 还是住在兵营中？”因为罗士信的举动实在是太令人震撼，把李玄霸“什么？罗士信提前到手？”的惊喜都冲淡了。
　　他只剩下满心疲惫。
　　一个放飞的二哥加上一个放飞的罗士信，这下放飞主将副将二人组都齐了。有“副手”的二哥能做出什么事， 历史书上都写了。
　　说什么“吾执弓矢，公执槊相随，虽百万众若我何！”然后带着尉迟恭两人去探阵， 秦王李世民身边的“尉迟恭”就一定要是持马槊的尉迟恭吗？持长矛的罗士信你看得中不得中？
　　两个少年狂战士，那可是太得中！
　　李玄霸都想抱头撞墙了。
　　罗士信虽好， 但在房乔杜如晦薛收长孙无忌四位友人来分担自己的压力前， 请不要用双倍的少年狂战士折磨我！
　　是是是，孤身战千军是二哥的高光，但身为亲人，李玄霸希望二哥一辈子都别来这种高光！
　　我给你搞后勤搞军备是让你无惊无险打碾压局的，不是让你去拼命去受伤的！
　　罗士信道：“我不要特殊待遇！不要小瞧我！我什么苦都能吃！”
　　李玄霸板着脸道：“先写一百张大字。”
　　罗士信不敢置信道：“我是来当兵的！为什么要写大字！”
　　李玄霸对李智云道：“我和你二兄平时事务繁忙， 你不是说无聊吗？罗士信与你年岁相仿，他教你武艺， 你教他经书。”
　　李智云点头：“好！三兄放心，我一定监督他好好写字！”
　　李世民忍俊不禁：“士信，说好什么苦都能吃， 可别逃。”
　　“不逃。”罗士信苦着脸， “三郎君让小郎君教我写字是对我好， 士信不是不辨是非的人。只是……唉， 我真的不喜欢读书写字。”
　　他苦着脸叹了几下气，然后被自己的苦相逗笑了。
　　李玄霸、李世民、李智云三兄弟也不由笑了出来。
　　李玄霸把心中对未来的“担忧”抛到一边，道：“你知道就好。跟我们走吧。”
　　罗士信使劲点头。
　　李智云凑近道：“不用叫我五郎君，我们互相学习，你叫我表字集弘即可。你快给自己取个字啊，直接叫名字好别扭。”
　　罗士信道：“有什么别扭？我要等弱冠功成名就之后，再奏请皇帝为我取字！”
　　李智云竖起大拇指：“牛气。”
　　罗士信自傲道：“我肯定能做到！”
　　李玄霸和李世民走在两个小少年身后。
　　李玄霸看向李世民。
　　李世民摸着下巴，琢磨要给罗士信取什么字。
　　李玄霸：【你给他改名叫罗成，祝贺他功成名就，然后把他原来的名字改成字，如何？】
　　李世民用眼神询问为什么。
　　李玄霸：【后世有本影响力比较大的唐初传奇小说叫《说唐》，将罗士信的名字改成了罗成。后世许多评书和影视小说顺着这本小说给他改名，后世许多人只知道“罗成”，不知道“罗士信”了。】
　　“影视”是个什么东西？算了，那不重要。
　　李世民继续向弟弟投向疑惑的眼神。
　　既然罗士信都能进入后世传奇小说了，在史书中的存在感应该也不会低。史书中没记载罗士信的字？
　　李玄霸：【死得太早，年仅二十三岁就战亡了。他家世又不显，所以关于他生平的记载都很少。】
　　李世民眨了眨眼睛，没想到猝不及防心梗。
　　他看向和小五叽叽喳喳聊得十分开心的骄傲小少年，不敢置信。
　　李玄霸：【还想知道更详细的事吗？】
　　李世民使劲摇头，把脑袋都摇出了残影。
　　李玄霸这次放过了二哥，没给二哥造成心理负担。
　　罗士信是死在跟随秦王李世民征讨刘黑闼途中。
　　李世民需要有人据守洺水城争取时间。王君廓本事一般，李世民担心王君廓守不住洺水城。罗士信主动请命接替王君廓。于是王君廓突围出城，罗士信顺势入城接替王君廓守城。
　　但罗士信入城后天降大雪，能见度极差；洺水城四周又都有河，唐军行动困难，无法支援罗士信。洺水城破，罗士信宁死不屈，被刘黑闼杀害。
　　就算是天才将帅李世民，作战也有胜有负；就算这场战役结局是胜利，途中小战斗也会有拉扯。
　　比如罗士信就死在与李世民一河之隔的地方。
　　史书中留下姓名的都是幸存者，只有寥寥无几的战亡将领能留下姓名。
　　但那些将领只是在后世籍籍无名。
　　李世民每一次作战指挥，牺牲的甚至故意用作诱饵的将领，他一定都一一记得。
　　慈不掌兵。
　　二哥还能保持活泼开朗的心态，意志力太强了。
　　离罗士信阵亡的时间还早，以后再慢慢给二哥剧透。刚见面，先让二哥高兴一会儿。
　　李玄霸：【十年后的事，谁说得准？说不定连敌人都变朋友了。】
　　李世民摸了摸脑袋：“有道理。而且有你在，我绝对不会重蹈覆辙。”
　　李玄霸点头：“嗯。”
　　罗士信还在叽叽喳喳，比划比划。
　　“我就这么冲上去，长矛噗嗤一声给他脖子戳了个对穿。我手再这么一甩，他的脑袋就落地了！”
　　“哇！听上去比我二兄还厉害！”
　　李世民脸色一变：“什么？什么比我厉害，来比比！”
　　他加快脚步追上两人。
　　李玄霸独自落在后面叹气。家里以后会很热闹了。
　　……
　　罗士信给父母的信与李世民、李玄霸的信一同送出。
　　大概是武力值强的人身材都高大，罗士信的身量与李世民相仿，李世民就将自己的衣服给罗士信暂时穿着。
　　罗士信这一路奔波，身上衣服都快成布条了。
　　李玄霸再次感慨罗士信的执拗。
　　其实罗士信如果不跑路，今年他也能在张须陀手下捞到立功扬名的机会。
　　谁知道二哥提前扬名成了蝴蝶翅膀，让这位少年天才猛将不再在张须陀手下等待机会，千里迢迢去投奔另一个已经成名的少年天才将帅？
　　后世传奇小说不知道会给罗士信这段神奇的经历编出多少故事。
　　吃饱饭洗干净后，罗士信虽然不是后世隋唐电视剧里的白面小将军，长相也相当耐看。
　　罗士信家世不显，还是个少年的他在没立功前就能被张须陀看重，相貌当然不会差。
　　李家人都有点颜控，对罗士信更友好了。
　　罗士信对自己现在的待遇有些不敢置信。
　　他虽然自负是少年天才，也知道张将军其实也对自己不错，只是担忧自己年幼经不住事，不给自己上战场的机会。
　　但张将军对自己的好，与李家三兄弟对自己的好完全不一样。
　　李世民和李玄霸不仅都是少年成名，还是最顶尖那波的勋贵子弟，心高气傲是一定的。
　　罗士信已经做好了谦恭的准备，先寻得机会上战场展现自己，之后再慢慢提升地位。现在他的待遇真是想都不敢想。
　　罗士信是知恩图报的人。李家三兄弟对他好，他连写最不喜欢的大字都不头疼了。
　　李智云正无聊，多了个玩伴很开心。
　　他殷勤地给罗士信介绍自己的二兄三兄后道：“你先去军中建功立业。二兄说了，明年我也能和你们一起去军中！”
　　罗士信道：“好，我等你。”
　　白头如新，倾盖如故。友谊有时候几句对话就能缔结。李智云和罗士信俨然已经成了很好的朋友。
　　见李智云开心起来，不复之前无聊苦闷，李玄霸松了口气，将更多的时间投入梳理张掖资源情况。
　　张掖南方是吐谷浑原本的国土，现在还未被大隋完全纳入统治；往西翻越祁连山后就是敦煌郡，再往西就是刚建立的伊吾郡，是还未完全打通的西域丝绸之路。
　　在回到中原前，这两处地方就是他和二哥准备的练兵地。
　　掌握了丝绸之路就掌握了钱财，掌握了吐谷浑故地就掌握了马场。两者缺一不可。
　　“现在以我们的兵力不可能打通西域丝绸之路，不过凭借大隋和西突厥的‘亲密关系’借道，问题应该不大。”李世民盘坐在榻上，把地图放在腿上，指着西突厥的地方，表情有点郁闷，“他们的土地真广阔。”
　　李玄霸道：“游牧民族占领的土地广阔，但只占领不治理，政权难以持续。”
　　李世民道：“对他们的可汗而言政权难以持续，但对我们而言，无论换谁当可汗都一样，都是突厥。西突厥处罗可汗还在杨广那？”
　　李玄霸点头：“杨广带着他和高昌国国王等西域使臣一同攻打高丽。”
　　李世民嗤笑：“什么一同攻打高丽，就是想炫耀自己的武力。一次炫耀不成，第二次要还是炫耀不成，这西域就要乱起来了。嗯，按照你的话来说，这是好事。这里天高皇帝远，我们只需要借着剿灭吐谷浑残党的理由把已经失去控制的西海郡拿下……”
　　李世民重重在地图上一点：“控制张掖和西海，就截断了西域通向中原的通道。我们就可以随意在西域扩张了。”
　　李玄霸的视线也落在西海郡上。
　　杨广虽然征讨吐谷浑成功，但没有吞下吐谷浑的国土。吐谷浑现在是各部落各自为政，大隋的政令仍旧出不了西平郡。
　　西海郡在青海湖以西。青海湖虽然是咸水湖不能引用和灌溉，但青海湖附近河流众多，所以很早就是游牧民族聚集地。
　　如今占据西海郡的吐谷浑名王，名为慕容孝隽，是吐谷浑王慕容伏允最信任的大臣。
　　慕容伏允败逃时，将慕容孝隽留在故地，以待他归来时里应外合。
　　慕容孝隽在慕容伏允死后扶伏允的幼子为可汗，占据西海郡，自立为名王“西海王”；西海郡南边的河源郡被吐谷浑最强大的名王天柱王占据；剩余吐谷浑王宫散布青海高原其他水草繁盛之地。
　　吐谷浑名王都拥有自己的部落、部曲，每个名王大约统治一千户左右牧民。
　　慕容孝隽“携可汗以令吐谷浑”，统治大约三千户牧民；天柱王统治了三个部落，有上万户的牧民，牲畜高达二十多万头。
　　历史中唐太宗再灭吐谷浑时，天柱部落就贡献了二十万头牲畜给将士加餐。
　　看到李玄霸打探来的消息，李世民很是眼热：“要是能吃下天柱王，我们就衣食无忧了。”
　　李玄霸道：“好，我支持你，二哥上！请一个人去！”
　　“滚！”李世民笑骂道，“先打西海郡。慕容孝隽所统领的是伏允残部，战斗力不强。阿玄，要如何离间西海王和天柱王？你肯定已经提前布局了。”
　　李玄霸道：“我派使臣扮作商人给天柱王进贡珍宝，他已经成为天柱王的座上宾。天柱王坐拥万户牧民，那吐谷浑可汗不过是一个已经失去所有部曲和牧民，东拼西凑才勉强凑齐三千户的破落户。大丈夫岂能久久居于人下，天柱王该自立可汗！”
　　后面几句话，李玄霸说得慷慨激昂，神情十分激动，演得非常投入。
　　李玄霸难得皮一下，李世民笑得差点从坐榻上滚下去：“好一个‘大丈夫岂能久久居于人下’，天柱王不听就不是大丈夫。我再给他添把火。”
　　李玄霸道：“二哥要亲自与天柱王见面？”
　　李世民活动了一下肩膀：“最近睁眼闭眼都是文书，真是腻了。我出去活动活动。等罗士信回来我就出发。那小子灭了一个东突厥小部落，俘虏了近千人。他的自傲是真的有本事支撑。”
　　李玄霸道：“有罗士信与你同往，我就不阻止你了。只是你别自仗你和罗士信的武力，去做太冒险的事。”
　　李世民把地图放到案上，伸了个懒腰：“放心。”
　　李玄霸脸色一垮：“每次你说放心，我都更不放心。”
　　李世民哈哈大笑：“反正都能赢，过程不重要。放心放心，我去去就回。香皂多给我几块，我去贿赂他。”
　　李玄霸道：“备礼的事交给我。在雪落之前回来，大雪封路，小心被堵在路上。”
　　李世民摆手：“我又不是杨广，没那么傻。唉，不知道高丽如何了？”
　　李玄霸淡漠道：“打不了，杨玄感应该谋反了。希望父亲能守好洛阳城，别吓着母亲。”
　　原本窦夫人会在今年陪同李渊去涿郡督运粮草，感染疫病去世。
　　涿郡周围的道路上遍布役夫役妇的腐烂尸体，疫病早已经横行。
　　如今李渊不仅提前当上了右骁卫中郎将，还成为洛阳留守，辅佐太子杨暕镇守洛阳，没有去涿郡。所以李玄霸就没有提醒母亲疫病之事。
　　李世民露出讥讽的笑容：“就杨玄感？他给我们父亲提鞋都不配。”
　　李玄霸赞同：“的确。”虽然父亲与其他开国皇帝相比本事不算太强，但拿杨玄感之类臭鱼烂虾比还是侮辱父亲了。
　　李渊在最初也是一员猛将，只是当了皇帝后就不挪窝，连御驾亲征都不肯意思意思，才显得他这个开国皇帝很废物。
　　现在杨玄感遇到的，正是当打之年的李渊，能开强弓，百发百中，俗称大李世民。
　　李世民道：“何况还有二表兄。我与二表兄论过兵，他理论知识很扎实；他又上过战场，实践经验也有。有父亲辅佐，二表兄守城的本事不会差。”
　　李玄霸想起历史中杨广被东突厥围住嗷嗷大哭的时候，齐王杨暕率领西军在崞县筑堡抵御突厥军队，干得确实不错。
　　李玄霸道：“杨玄感不会看洛阳太难啃，放弃洛阳去大兴吧？”
　　李世民笑得前俯后仰，眼泪都出来了：“高老师在那呢！就算高老师不是大兴留守，大兴留守肯定会请高老师出山帮忙守城。宇文老师也在那。上次离别时宇文老师仍旧老当益壮，能压着我打。杨玄感能挨得住宇文老师几下劈砍？”
　　李玄霸捏下巴。
　　李密给了杨玄感上中下三策。下策攻打洛阳，中策攻打大兴，上策攻打涿郡。念着洛阳繁荣，且留守的越王仅九岁，民部尚书樊子盖之前没带过兵，所以杨玄感选了下策，和洛阳死磕，理所当然没磕动。
　　这次杨玄感会如何选择？
