Chapter 109: A Real Man Does Not Submit to Others

Li Xuanba finally understood why his Second Brother had been wearing such a benevolent expression.

If this unruly brat had fallen into his own hands, he would have ensured he received a sound thrashing first. If he couldn't beat the boy himself, he would have had others hold him down while he did it.

A thirteen-year-old boy, alone, carrying a bundle on his back and riding a scrawny horse, had crossed more than half of China. Even in times of peace, this would be hair-raising; in these chaotic times, it was simply madness.

Although Li Xuanba and Li Shimin had traveled far at even younger ages, they had been accompanied by a large retinue of servants and guards. This was completely different from this wild child.

"Do you intend to stay at our manor, or will you be quartered in the barracks?" Because Luo Shixin’s actions were so shocking, they had diluted Li Xuanba’s surprise at "What? Luo Shixin arrived early?"

He was left with nothing but profound exhaustion.

A liberated Second Brother combined with a liberated Luo Shixin—the duo of the "unrestrained commander and his deputy" was now complete. What a Second Brother with a "deputy" like this could accomplish was already written in the history books.

"I shall wield the bow and arrow, and you shall follow with your heavy lance; even a million men could do nothing to me!" Then, he would take Yuchi Gong to scout the enemy lines. But must the "Yuchi Gong" beside the Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, necessarily be the one holding the horse-lance? Could it not be Luo Shixin with his long spear?

Two young berserkers—that would be a perfect match!

Li Xuanba wanted to bury his face in his hands and bang his head against a wall.

Luo Shixin was a fine talent, but until Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, Xue Shou, and Zhangsun Wuji arrived to share his burden, please, do not torture him with a double dose of teenage berserkers!

Yes, yes, fighting an army of thousands alone was his Second Brother’s highlight reel, but as a family member, Li Xuanba hoped his Second Brother would never have to experience such "highlights" in his life!

I provide you with logistics and armaments so you can fight crushing, risk-free battles, not so you can risk your life and get wounded!

Luo Shixin declared, "I don't want special treatment! Don't look down on me! I can endure any hardship!"

Li Xuanba kept a straight face and said, "Start by writing one hundred large-character calligraphy exercises."

Luo Shixin looked at him in disbelief. "I came here to be a soldier! Why do I have to write calligraphy!"

Li Xuanba said to Li Zhiyun, "Your Second Brother and I are usually busy with official business. Didn't you say you were bored? Luo Shixin is about your age; he can teach you martial arts, and you can teach him the classics."

Li Zhiyun nodded. "Alright! Don't worry, Third Brother, I will definitely supervise him to ensure he writes well!"

Li Shimin couldn't help but chuckle. "Shixin, you said you could endure any hardship, so don't try to run away."

"I won't run." Luo Shixin sighed with a bitter face. "The Third Young Master asking the Fifth Young Master to teach me to write is for my own good; I am not someone who cannot tell right from wrong. It’s just... sigh, I really don't like reading or writing."

He sighed a few times with a pained expression, then was amused by his own miserable face.

The three brothers—Li Xuanba, Li Shimin, and Li Zhiyun—couldn't help but laugh.

Li Xuanba cast his "worries" about the future aside and said, "As long as you know that. Come with us."

Luo Shixin nodded vigorously.

Li Zhiyun leaned in and said, "No need to call me Fifth Young Master. Since we are learning from each other, just call me by my courtesy name, Jiehong. You should hurry up and choose a courtesy name for yourself; it’s so awkward calling you by your given name."

Luo Shixin replied, "What’s awkward about it? I will wait until I have come of age and achieved fame and success before I petition the Emperor to grant me a courtesy name!"

Li Zhiyun gave him a thumbs up. "That’s bold."

Luo Shixin said proudly, "I will definitely do it!"

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin walked behind the two young boys.

Li Xuanba looked at Li Shimin.

Li Shimin was stroking his chin, pondering what courtesy name to give Luo Shixin.

Li Xuanba: [How about you change his name to Luo Cheng, congratulate him on his future success, and turn his original name into his courtesy name?]

Li Shimin asked with his eyes why.

Li Xuanba: [In later generations, there is a highly influential legend about the early Tang Dynasty called "The Tale of the Tang," which changed Luo Shixin’s name to Luo Cheng. Many later storytelling performances, films, and novels followed this book and changed his name, so many people in the future only know "Luo Cheng" and not "Luo Shixin."]

"Films"? What was that? Never mind, that wasn't important.

Li Shimin continued to cast a questioning look at his younger brother.

Since Luo Shixin could make it into the legends of later generations, his presence in the history books shouldn't be low. Did the history books not record Luo Shixin’s courtesy name?

Li Xuanba: [He died too young, falling in battle at only twenty-three. His family background wasn't prominent, so there are very few records of his life.]

Li Shimin blinked, not expecting such a sudden, heart-wrenching blow.

He looked at the proud young boy, who was chatting happily with little Fifth, and couldn't believe it.

Li Xuanba: [Do you want to know more details?]

Li Shimin shook his head vigorously, his head blurring from the motion.

Li Xuanba let his Second Brother off the hook this time, not wanting to cause him any psychological burden.

Luo Shixin had died while following the Prince of Qin, Li Shimin, on a campaign against Liu Heita.

Li Shimin had needed someone to hold the city of Ming Shui to buy time. Wang Junkuo’s abilities were mediocre, and Li Shimin was worried he couldn't hold the city. Luo Shixin had volunteered to replace him. Thus, Wang Junkuo broke out of the city, and Luo Shixin entered to take over the defense.

But after Luo Shixin entered the city, a heavy snow fell, reducing visibility to almost nothing. Ming Shui was surrounded by rivers, making it difficult for the Tang army to maneuver and provide support. The city fell, and Luo Shixin, refusing to surrender, was killed by Liu Heita.

Even for a genius commander like Li Shimin, there were wins and losses in war; even if the campaign ended in victory, there would be setbacks in the small battles along the way.

For instance, Luo Shixin had died just across a river from Li Shimin.

Those whose names remained in history books were the survivors; only a handful of fallen generals left their names behind.

But those generals were simply unknown to later generations.

Every time Li Shimin commanded a battle, he remembered every general who sacrificed themselves, or even those he had intentionally used as bait.

"Benevolence does not command armies."

That his Second Brother could still maintain a lively and cheerful disposition showed his willpower was truly formidable.

It was still a long time before Luo Shixin’s death; he would slowly reveal the future to his Second Brother later. Since they had just met, let his Second Brother be happy for a while.

Li Xuanba: [Things ten years from now—who can say for sure? Maybe even enemies will become friends.]

Li Shimin rubbed his head. "That makes sense. And with you here, I will definitely not repeat the same mistakes."

Li Xuanba nodded. "Mm."

Luo Shixin was still chattering away, gesturing wildly.

"I just charged forward like this, and with a *thwack*, my spear pierced his neck right through! Then I gave my hand a flick, and his head hit the ground!"

"Wow! That sounds even more impressive than my Second Brother!"

Li Shimin’s expression changed. "What? What’s more impressive than me? Let’s spar!"

He quickened his pace to catch up with the two.

Li Xuanba lagged behind, sighing. The household was going to be very lively from now on.

...

Luo Shixin’s letter to his parents was sent out along with the letters from Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Perhaps it was true that those with great martial prowess were also tall and sturdy; Luo Shixin’s stature was similar to Li Shimin’s, so Li Shimin gave him some of his own clothes to wear for the time being.

After Luo Shixin’s long, arduous journey, his original clothes had been reduced to rags.

Li Xuanba once again marveled at Luo Shixin’s stubbornness.

In truth, if Luo Shixin hadn't run away, he could have found an opportunity to earn merit and fame under Zhang Xutuo this year.

Who would have thought that his Second Brother’s early rise to fame would become a butterfly effect, causing this young genius general to stop waiting for opportunities under Zhang Xutuo and travel thousands of miles to join another young genius commander who had already made a name for himself?

He wondered how many stories future legends would fabricate about this miraculous experience of Luo Shixin’s.

After a full meal and a wash, although Luo Shixin wasn't the fair-skinned young general from the Sui-Tang television dramas of the future, his appearance was quite striking.

Luo Shixin’s family background wasn't prominent, but for a young man to be valued by Zhang Xutuo before he had even earned any merit, his looks certainly wouldn't be bad.

The Li family were all a bit obsessed with appearances, so they became even friendlier toward Luo Shixin.

Luo Shixin couldn't believe the treatment he was receiving.

Although he was self-confident as a young genius, he knew that General Zhang had actually been good to him, but had worried he was too young to handle things and hadn't given him the chance to go to the battlefield.

But the kindness General Zhang showed him was completely different from the kindness of the three Li brothers.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were not only famous from a young age, but they were also the most elite of the noble youths; they were bound to be proud and arrogant.

Luo Shixin had prepared himself to be humble, to first find an opportunity to show his worth on the battlefield, and then slowly rise in status. The treatment he was receiving now was something he hadn't even dared to imagine.

Luo Shixin was a person who knew how to repay kindness. Because the three Li brothers were good to him, he didn't even find writing the calligraphy he hated so much a headache anymore.

Li Zhiyun was bored, and he was very happy to have a new playmate.

He enthusiastically introduced his Second and Third Brothers to Luo Shixin and said, "You go to the army first to build your career. Second Brother said that next year, I can go to the army with you all!"

Luo Shixin said, "Alright, I'll wait for you."

"New acquaintances become like old friends." Sometimes, a friendship could be forged in just a few sentences. Li Zhiyun and Luo Shixin had already become very good friends.

Seeing Li Zhiyun become happy and no longer bored or miserable, Li Xuanba breathed a sigh of relief and devoted more time to sorting out the resources of Zhangye.

To the south of Zhangye lay the original territory of the Tuyuhun, which had not yet been fully brought under the rule of the Great Sui. To the west, after crossing the Qilian Mountains, was Dunhuang Commandery, and further west was the newly established Yiwu Commandery—the Silk Road of the Western Regions that had not yet been fully opened.

Before returning to the Central Plains, these two places were the training grounds he and his Second Brother had prepared.

Mastering the Silk Road meant mastering wealth; mastering the former Tuyuhun lands meant mastering the horse pastures. Both were indispensable.

"With our current military strength, it's impossible to open up the Silk Road of the Western Regions, but relying on the 'intimate relationship' between the Great Sui and the Western Turks to borrow a path shouldn't be a problem." Li Shimin sat cross-legged on the couch, the map on his lap, pointing at the territory of the Western Turks with a somewhat frustrated expression. "Their lands are truly vast."

Li Xuanba said, "Nomadic peoples occupy vast lands, but they only occupy them without governing them; such regimes are difficult to sustain."

Li Shimin said, "To their Khagan, the regime is hard to sustain, but to us, it doesn't matter who becomes Khagan—they are all Turks. Is the Western Turkic Chuluo Khagan still with Yang Guang?"

Li Xuanba nodded. "Yang Guang took him, the King of Gaochang, and other envoys from the Western Regions along to attack Goguryeo."

Li Shimin sneered, "What 'attacking Goguryeo together'—he just wants to show off his military might. If he fails to show off once, and fails again the second time, the Western Regions will fall into chaos. Hmm, as you put it, this is a good thing. It’s far from the Emperor’s reach here; we only need to use the excuse of wiping out the remnants of the Tuyuhun to take down Xihai Commandery, which has already lost control..."

Li Shimin pointed heavily at the map. "Controlling Zhangye and Xihai will cut off the path from the Western Regions to the Central Plains. Then we can expand into the Western Regions at will."

Li Xuanba’s gaze also fell on Xihai Commandery.

Although Yang Guang had succeeded in his campaign against the Tuyuhun, he hadn't swallowed their territory. The Tuyuhun were now ruled by individual tribes, and the Great Sui’s decrees still could not reach beyond Xiping Commandery.

Xihai Commandery was west of Qinghai Lake. Although Qinghai Lake was a saltwater lake and could not be used for drinking or irrigation, there were many rivers nearby, so it had long been a gathering place for nomadic peoples.

The Tuyuhun noble who currently occupied Xihai Commandery was named Murong Xiaojun, the most trusted minister of the Tuyuhun King, Murong Fuyun.

When Murong Fuyun fled in defeat, he left Murong Xiaojun in the homeland to act as an inside agent for when he returned.

After Murong Fuyun died, Murong Xiaojun supported his young son as Khagan, occupied Xihai Commandery, and declared himself the "King of Xihai." The Heyuan Commandery, south of Xihai, was occupied by the most powerful Tuyuhun noble, the Tianzhu King; the remaining Tuyuhun royal palace was scattered across other lush areas of the Qinghai Plateau.

Each Tuyuhun noble possessed their own tribes and personal guards, with each noble ruling about a thousand households of herdsmen.

Murong Xiaojun "held the Khagan to command the Tuyuhun," ruling about three thousand households; the Tianzhu King ruled three tribes, with over ten thousand households of herdsmen and more than two hundred thousand head of livestock.

In history, when Emperor Taizong of Tang destroyed the Tuyuhun again, the Tianzhu tribe had contributed two hundred thousand head of livestock to feed the soldiers.

Seeing the information Li Xuanba had gathered, Li Shimin was very envious. "If we could take down the Tianzhu King, we would have no worries about food or clothing."

Li Xuanba said, "Alright, I support you. Go for it, Second Brother! Go alone!"

"Get lost!" Li Shimin laughed and scolded. "We'll take Xihai Commandery first. Murong Xiaojun leads the remnants of Fuyun’s forces; their combat effectiveness isn't strong. Axuan, how do we sow discord between the King of Xihai and the Tianzhu King? You must have already laid the groundwork."

Li Xuanba said, "I sent envoys disguised as merchants to offer treasures to the Tianzhu King, and he has already become a guest of honor. The Tianzhu King sits upon ten thousand households of herdsmen, while that Tuyuhun Khagan is nothing but a pauper who has lost all his troops and herdsmen, and only managed to scrape together three thousand households. How can a real man submit to others for long? The Tianzhu King should declare himself Khagan!"

Li Xuanba said the last few sentences with great passion, his expression very excited, acting with total commitment.

It was rare for Li Xuanba to tease like this, and Li Shimin laughed so hard he nearly rolled off the couch. "What a great 'How can a real man submit to others for long'—if the Tianzhu King doesn't listen, he’s no real man. I’ll add some fuel to the fire for him."

Li Xuanba asked, "Is Second Brother going to meet the Tianzhu King in person?"

Li Shimin stretched his shoulders. "I’ve been staring at documents day and night lately; I’m truly sick of it. I’ll go out and get some exercise. I’ll set off as soon as Luo Shixin returns. That kid wiped out a small Eastern Turkic tribe and captured nearly a thousand people. His arrogance is truly backed by ability."

Li Xuanba said, "With Luo Shixin going with you, I won't stop you. Just don't rely on your and Luo Shixin’s martial prowess to do anything too risky."

Li Shimin placed the map on the desk and stretched. "Don't worry."

Li Xuanba’s face fell. "Every time you say 'don't worry,' I worry even more."

Li Shimin laughed heartily. "I’ll win anyway; the process doesn't matter. Don't worry, don't worry, I’ll be back soon. Give me a few more bars of soap; I’m going to bribe him."

Li Xuanba said, "I’ll handle the preparations for the gifts. Be back before the snow falls; if the roads are blocked by heavy snow, be careful not to get stuck."

Li Shimin waved his hand. "I’m not Yang Guang; I’m not that stupid. Sigh, I wonder how things are in Goguryeo?"

Li Xuanba said indifferently, "They can't fight it. Yang Xuangan should have rebelled by now. I hope Father can hold Luoyang and not scare Mother."

Originally, Lady Dou would have accompanied Li Yuan to Zhuojun this year to oversee grain transport and would have died from an epidemic.

The roads around Zhuojun were covered in the rotting corpses of conscripted laborers, and the epidemic had long been rampant.

Now, Li Yuan had not only become the General of the Right Xiaowei ahead of schedule but had also become the Guardian of Luoyang, assisting the Crown Prince Yang Jian in defending the city, and had not gone to Zhuojun. Therefore, Li Xuanba hadn't needed to warn his mother about the epidemic.

Li Shimin showed a mocking smile. "Yang Xuangan? He’s not even fit to tie our father’s shoes."

Li Xuanba agreed. "Indeed." Although their father wasn't as capable as some other founding emperors, comparing him to bottom-feeders like Yang Xuangan was an insult.

Li Yuan had also been a fierce general in his early days; it was only after becoming emperor that he stopped moving, refusing to even lead a campaign in person, which made him seem like a useless founding emperor.

What Yang Xuangan was facing now was Li Yuan in his prime—someone who could draw a powerful bow and hit the mark every time, commonly known as the "Great Li Shimin."

Li Shimin said, "Besides, there’s also our Second Cousin. I’ve discussed military strategy with him; his theoretical knowledge is very solid, and he’s been to the battlefield, so he has practical experience too. With Father assisting him, our Second Cousin’s ability to defend the city won't be bad."

Li Xuanba remembered how, in history, when Yang Guang was surrounded by the Eastern Turks and crying, the Prince of Qi, Yang Jian, had led the Western Army to build fortifications in Guo County to resist the Turkic army, and he had done quite well.

Li Xuanba asked, "Do you think Yang Xuangan will see that Luoyang is too hard to crack and abandon it to attack Daxing instead?"

Li Shimin laughed until he was doubled over, tears streaming down his face. "Teacher Gao is there! Even if Teacher Gao isn't the Guardian of Daxing, the Guardian would definitely invite Teacher Gao to help defend the city. Teacher Yuwen is there too. When we last parted, Teacher Yuwen was still as vigorous as ever and could suppress me in a fight. Could Yang Xuangan withstand a few strikes from Teacher Yuwen?"

Li Xuanba stroked his chin.

Li Mi had given Yang Xuangan three strategies: the inferior one was to attack Luoyang, the middle one was to attack Daxing, and the superior one was to attack Zhuojun. Thinking of Luoyang’s prosperity, and that the Prince of Yue who was guarding it was only nine years old, and the Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, Fan Zigai, had never led troops before, Yang Xuangan had chosen the inferior strategy, stubbornly attacking Luoyang, and naturally, he hadn't been able to crack it.

How would Yang Xuangan choose this time?

chunks.chapterTitle: 第110章 山东全境民乱起 – 第111章 李世民出使河源
chunks.chineseText:
第110章 山东全境民乱起

杨玄感正在做选择。
　　凭他内心， 他想选下策，攻打洛阳。
　　虽然洛阳有其他官员的家属，但攻打大兴和涿郡各有好处， 攻打洛阳的必要性和攻打大兴、涿郡拉不开距离。
　　他选洛阳， 是因为洛阳繁华， 又是大隋国土的正中央，选洛阳很有面子。
　　再者，涿郡有大隋最精锐的将士， 大兴留守刑部尚书卫玄虽带兵的本事不是太强，但高颎还在大兴编书，绝对不会袖手旁观。
　　杨玄感虽然自视甚高， 甚至有“再世项羽”之名，但人的名树的影， 要在军事上胜过高颎， 他只能祈求父亲灵魂上身。
　　洛阳只有太子杨暕和唐国公李渊，看上去似乎是最软的柿子。
　　李渊还没有带过兵，杨玄感本不应该惧怕他，但李二郎的名声太过显赫，让他对李渊忌惮不已。
　　李二郎今年才十四周岁， 已经因功劳升任当朝最年轻的虎贲郎将。
　　看看李二郎立的功劳，初次作战就靠着几百家丁和从铁勒部落借的骑兵俘虏了吐谷浑可汗， 杨广一征高丽民乱四起时他拉着一支临时拼凑的乡勇就能百战百胜，这功绩让人看得头皮发麻。
　　可以说当朝许多老将都没有李二郎这么耀眼的功绩——若不是李二郎实在是过于年少，光是吐谷浑可汗的脑袋就足够李二郎封侯。
　　以前李二郎和李三郎升官的时候， 他还嘲笑李二郎和李三郎只是因为背靠唐国公府， 是杨广的外甥， 才有这样的机会。
　　李三郎这几年没有显露出多大的本事， 原本“少年秀才”的光环淡去。但李二郎实在是太耀眼了，把李三郎一个病秧子都带上了虎牙郎将的位置。
　　唐国公教养的这两个孩子真是厉害。
　　李二郎有这样的本事，李渊肯定不会差。
　　想想李二郎的战绩，杨玄感不得不犹豫。
　　因一个十四岁少年郎将犹豫，杨玄感感到很挫败。
　　可李二郎的战绩真的是很不讲道理。杨玄感都疑惑，为何杨广二征高丽不把李二郎带上。难道是因为担心二征高丽时突厥或者吐谷浑残党骚扰大隋后方，所以让李二郎坐镇张掖，震慑西域？
　　杨玄感犹豫时，献策的李密很失望。
　　现在大隋民乱四起，驿站系统几乎崩溃。各家勋贵现在传递消息都是派出自己的部曲，无法再倚仗官府的驿站系统。
　　洛阳离杨玄感起兵的地方很近。杨玄感只要有所动作，洛阳肯定会防备。何况洛阳有太子在，李渊在朝中也颇有声望，他们的自主权很大。就算没有实际证据，他们也能调集钱粮将士提前准备。
　　长安和涿郡离中原较远，交通被民乱堵塞，别看离他们也远，但他们无法像洛阳那样直接查到自己的动向，需要洛阳留守向他们传递消息。
　　在全国力量都压在高丽的时候，大隋情报系统传递信息很慢。再者长安留守只是一个刑部尚书，他想调集更多兵力得先向皇帝或者太子上报，这一来一往又会耗费许多时间。
　　在李密看来，涿郡虽然有大隋最精锐的将士，但大军粮草不济，且有杨广这个狠狠拖后腿的人，想要达成战略目标较为容易。有风险，但富贵险中求，杀掉杨广和逼降大隋军队主力，毕其功于一役的富贵太大了，值得冒险。
　　选大兴除了大兴的反应速度很慢之外，大兴是关陇勋贵的大本营，而杨广将政治中心转移到东都，又大肆提拔江南士族，让关陇勋贵很是不满。这个被杨广冷落的西都很可能抵抗意愿不强，愿意成为杨玄感的助力。
　　且长安和涿郡都处于中原之外，退可和突厥、高丽联合，容错率非常高。
　　洛阳地处中原，交通十分便利，就意味着大隋的军队可以四面八方支援围堵他们。而且就算占据了洛阳城，之后要发展也非常难。若是输了，更是无路可逃。
　　李密原本以为杨玄感身为杨素的儿子，战略眼光应该有一点。不过他看出了杨玄感想要攻打洛阳的意图，才退而求其次，告诉杨玄感攻打洛阳是下策。
　　但杨玄感居然仍旧想去洛阳？他真的以为攻占洛阳后就能一呼百应天下归心？杨广还没死呢！
　　李密突然觉得杨玄感自诩项羽，还真的有点像项羽，“衣锦还乡”“沐猴而冠”。
　　李密虽然仍旧受杨玄感礼遇，但他心中萌生了退意。
　　杨玄感看着不像是个能成事的人。自己要做好随时逃跑的准备，唉。
　　杨玄感犹豫了许久，对李密道：“我仍旧意属攻打洛阳。我们先去洛阳，若洛阳戒备森严，再取道去涿郡。”
　　李密松了一口气。罢了，至少杨玄感还有基本常识，知道第二选项选直接攻打杨广而不是高颎。
　　杨玄感做好决定后，就紧锣密鼓地开始谋反。
　　他以诬陷来护儿谋反来凑集粮草、征集士卒，然后举兵前往洛阳。
　　李密看着杨玄感的“十万大军”直皱眉。
　　他以为杨玄感既然敢造反，至少准备了一支五千人左右的精兵。
　　好歹战马、盔甲、武器齐全的三千精锐骑兵应该有吧？
　　没想到杨玄感除了自己和少数亲卫有像样的武器，“十万大军”军备极其缺乏，完全没有攻坚的力量。
　　杨玄感不是早就准备谋反了吗？这提前准备做得太差了吧？
　　难道是因为杨广的监视太严密，所以楚国公才没有机会积攒造反的力量？李密给杨玄感找了理由。
　　李密想，杨广威望未坠，又对朝臣监视极严，楚国公无法提前积攒力量很正常，自己不该责怪他。
　　……
　　“阿嚏。”李玄霸揉了揉鼻子。
　　他紧了紧毛皮大氅，将账本最后一笔添上。
　　“西域贵族真是富得流油，简直能和后世的沙漠土大户媲美。”李玄霸露出笑意，“能给二哥养活五百精兵了。”
　　五百具装精锐骑兵，争霸天下可能还有点困难，但要割据一地当诸侯是完全没问题了。
　　李玄霸努力多年厚积薄发，终于能给带领了多年杂牌军的二哥凑一支真正的精兵，让二哥不用顾忌任何领兵之外的事随意发挥他的军事才能，这种成就感，让一贯冷静的李玄霸都忍不住自得感膨胀。
　　这样一点一点偷偷摸摸积攒势力并成功的感觉真是太棒了。
　　算完账后，李玄霸才拆开家人送来的信。
　　父亲的信只是让自己和二哥注意身体，絮絮叨叨了一堆“人生经验”。
　　母亲的信写了中原近况。信送来时，杨玄感还未叛乱，但民乱更频繁了。
　　三月，杨广第二次御驾亲征高丽。同时，他还征伐十万百姓修缮扩建大兴城。
　　母亲在信中叹息，皇帝说是只征丁男，但她去大兴探望女儿时亲眼见到路上服徭役的百姓，竟没见到一个“丁男”。
　　哪有什么丁男。
　　适龄的丁男承担征伐高丽的徭役都不够，壮妇都早就被摊派了徭役。来大兴的“丁男”，全是老幼。
　　李玄霸叹气。
　　杨广三月御驾亲征高丽，三月扩建修缮大兴城。
　　同是三月，济阴（山东曹县）孟海公起义；齐郡（山东济南）孟让起义；北海（山东益都）郭方预起义；平原（山东平原）郝孝德；厌次（山东无棣）格谦；渤海（山东阳信）孙宣雅起义。
　　并非现在所指的崤山以东，而就在后世的山东省范围内，几乎全境叛乱。
　　山东半岛与朝鲜半岛隔海相望，是杨广征高丽搜刮民力最严重的地区。
　　同时，山东半岛在去年和前年连续遭遇极大水旱灾害，本就民不聊生。
　　李玄霸当初去泰山脚下时，山东在靠近郡县的地方，大致还算安稳。现在山东的郡县大概都已经失守了吧。
　　但山东离朝鲜半岛如此近，山东全境民乱郡县失守，竟也没让杨广有丝毫触动。
　　他是真的看不起民乱。
　　看完母亲的信，李玄霸缓了一会儿才消化了这些糟心事，拿起了宇文珠的信。
　　宇文珠也提到了大兴城徭役的事。
　　她本想出外行医，被师傅劝阻，说救不过来，还会引发骚乱，只能不救。
　　“师傅说这天下病了，但我们这些医师只能治人的病，治不了天下的病。我问师傅和祖父，谁能治天下的病，他们都闭口不言。其实我明白，无论是谁，终归和我这等女儿身无关。我询问也无益，不如不问。”
　　李玄霸从字里行间看出了宇文珠的自怨自艾，不由有些出神。
　　等这次回家时，就告诉珠娘救治天下的病她也必须出力吧。母亲会加入，三姐会加入，嫂子也会加入。那珠娘肯定是要辅佐母亲、三姐和嫂子的。
　　宇文珠抱怨了一句后，说起身边人的事。
　　李玄霸看着看着，猛地睁圆眼睛。
　　“观音婢患了气疾，幸亏我发现得早。师傅说，若气疾拖久了就会终身不愈，只能将就养着，把观音婢吓得哇哇大哭。我第一次看到她哭的这么厉害。”
　　“三姐先守孝，又侍疾，身体亏损得厉害，我给她调理了一下。她自己居然没发现身体已经亏损严重。我吓唬她‘身体长久亏损有碍性命’，柴家夫人再不准三姐侍疾，三姐侍疾她就不喝药，逼迫三姐休息。柴家夫人对三姐真好。”
　　“现在京中有好多勋贵夫人娘子邀我为她们调理身体。她们说寻常医师难以为她们仔细诊断，幸亏有我这位女名医。如三郎所言，我的本事真的会有用处。虽然被称为‘名医’心中有愧，但……我真厉害！”
　　李玄霸失笑，心中担忧散去。
　　没错，真的厉害。


第111章 李世民出使河源

李玄霸长长舒了口气。
　　长孙皇后有气疾。平阳昭公主很可能死于产后身体亏损。
　　这两件事他都知道。
　　但他离开大兴的时候， 嫂子并没有患上支气管炎，三姐虽疲惫了些但精神也不错。他以为那是很遥远的事。
　　慢性支气管炎多是在得急性支气管炎后没有及时治疗，被拖成了慢性病。李玄霸发现嫂子并不是自幼就有遗传支气管炎后， 就猜测如果历史中的长孙皇后和嫂子如今身体状况一样， 就可能是在被赶出家门客居舅家时患病。
　　虽然高士廉对妹妹和外甥不错， 但寄人篱下带来的心头苦闷不会消失。长孙皇后和长孙无忌在历史记载中几乎点满了的察言观色能力，显然是从小在谨小慎微中学来。
　　长孙皇后在罹患气疾后，如果只是不严重的咳嗽， 她可能不会太麻烦舅舅为她请名医。何况高士廉会在今年受朋友斛斯政连累贬官岭南。
　　高士廉与斛斯政的关系很远，被牵连只是因为朝中无人为他说话，被当作小卒子随意丢弃——准二儿媳的舅舅这个亲戚身份对李渊来说太远， 何况原本时空中李渊在高士廉被贬官时，在朝中也没有话语权。
　　不过现在不一样了。长孙晟还活着， 二哥也很得皇帝喜爱， 父亲还会在前线与杨玄感作战。不需要他们主动做什么，朝中大臣就会主动把高士廉从被牵连名单上划去。
　　不，高士廉说不定根本不会上名单。
　　“没想到嫂子还是差点患上慢性支气管炎。”李玄霸有点后怕，“三姐也真是……唉，贤惠都是做给别人看的， 哪有自己的身体重要。”
　　李玄霸抚摸着宇文珠的信：“多亏珠娘了。”
　　中医的“望闻问切”，不仅仅是把个脉就算诊断。古人很早就积累了观察病人身体各处情况来判断病情的经验。
　　比如贴耳听胸音就是其中之一。
　　可世间女子从医者十分难得， 除了家学渊源者，大部分女子就算想要学医也无从拜师，只能自学。历史中记载的女性名医寥寥无几。
　　隋朝才从乱世中缓过气来， 乱世中女子生存都困难， 何谈学医。再者学医至少需要识字， 就是勋贵官宦也不会家家都教女儿识字。能识字士女娇贵， 不事生产，基本没机会去做行医那等社会地位不高的工作。
　　支气管炎有时候会伴随肺上的毛病，将愈未愈的时候只有轻微咳嗽，不懂的人可能连止咳的药物都懒得吃。医师只有听胸音才能判断准确的病灶。
　　男性医师怎么可能听女性患者的胸音？就是听诊器发明出来，女性患者也不会将听诊器贴在胸前让男性医师听声音。
　　宇文珠学医时间不长，真正的名医至少要积累二三十年经验。她并非名医，只是略懂皮毛，便能为嫂子和三姐诊断出连勋贵家中供奉医师都诊断不出的疾病，不是她的医术超出这些老医师，不过是她为女病人诊断疾病不是只切脉，甚至只悬丝切脉而已。
　　不过……而已。但竟世间难得。
　　李玄霸难得感慨了一会儿，才提笔写回信。
　　先敷衍父亲，然后宽慰母亲，最后狠狠夸奖珠娘。嗯，写些什么夸奖的话呢？
　　在宇文老师家中住了几日，经历了一同逛街踏青和簪花之后，李玄霸与宇文珠的交流自在许多。就像是宇文珠会在给李玄霸的信中写上抱怨和得意的俏皮话，李玄霸也能在信中和宇文珠侃侃而谈了。
　　二哥带着罗士信离开张掖不知道做什么事去了。李智云独自一人无聊，来找三哥玩。
　　他一到书房门口，就看见露出迷之微笑的三哥奋笔疾书，默默转身离开。
　　一看三哥这表情，他就知道三哥在给三嫂写信。自己还是别打扰了。
　　“唉。”李智云幽怨道，“我也想要未婚妻了。”
　　好孤单啊＿（：з」∠）＿。
　　……
　　李世民这次出门，自然是去执行他之前和李玄霸所制定的计划，与吐谷浑残部天柱王唠嗑去了。
　　李世民生擒吐谷浑王，本应该是吐谷浑部落的仇人。但吐谷浑在慕容伏允被杀后，就名义上向大隋臣服。虽然他们不受大隋管辖，但也不会主动招惹大隋，除非大隋又和他们抢地盘。
　　再者游牧民族部落崇尚强者，李世民主动向天柱王示好，天柱王只会对李世民厚礼以待。
　　罗士信本以为这次跟随李世民去天柱部落“作客”，肯定会有一场恶战。谁知道自家虎贲郎君迅速和天柱王称兄道弟，每日一同游猎，好不快活，看得罗士信直挠头。
　　他对周达问道：“我们真的只是来做客？”
　　周达已经习惯自家郎君超高的亲和力，心中毫无波澜：“不然呢？郎君之前说是来做客，那就肯定只会做客。”
　　罗士信疑惑：“去仇人那里还能真的只作客？”不敢置信！
　　周达失笑：“仇人？哪来的仇人？别说天柱王对原吐谷浑可汗不一定忠心，就是真有仇，只要郎君想，郎君就能和他化敌为友。没有人能抵挡住郎君的热情。”
　　罗士信感叹道：“原来集弘说的是真的。”
　　周达好奇：“五郎君给你说了什么？”
　　罗士信正色道：“集弘说，‘只要需要结交麻烦的人，三兄就会关门！放二兄！’。”
　　周达：“扑哧！”
　　“喂喂喂，我是猎犬还是猎鹰？什么叫‘关门放二兄’？”李世民一身酒气走过来，打着哈欠道，“给我熬醒酒药。真是的，非要喝酒。如果知道我多喝酒，阿玄又会唠叨个不停。”
　　周达忙亲自去熬醒酒药。
　　罗士信为李世民打来温热的洗脸水：“我们还要在这里待多久？”
　　李世民一边洗脸一边道：“怎么？无聊了？”
　　罗士信苦着脸道：“好无聊啊。”
　　李世民擦干净脸上的水：“你将来难道一辈子都只打仗？好好看好好听好好学，将来你若想镇守一方，这些本事都用得上。”
　　罗士信仍旧苦着脸道：“我知道，但是好无聊啊。”
　　李世民大笑：“无聊也得学。”
　　罗士信垂头丧气：“是。”
　　李世民喝完醒酒药后，拍了拍脸让自己清醒了一点，吩咐道：“好了，我知道不止士信，我的兵都无聊了。明日我们就能拔营去西海郡，与天柱王一同游猎。”
　　罗士信和周达眼睛都亮了。
　　周达道：“他终于被说动了？”
　　李世民笑道：“吐谷浑虽然只认慕容家族为可汗，但不当吐谷浑可汗，当天柱可汗不就行了。若是伏允还在，他不会有自立之心。但不过一黄毛小儿也敢在他头上，他就不满了。有强盛的大隋支持，他不心动都难。”
　　草原游牧部落对可汗本来就没有多少忠诚心。就是成吉思汗建立“黄金血脉”后，也有不少野心家想要自立。明朝的瓦剌，也就是清朝的准噶尔，就看不起所谓“黄金血脉”。
　　吐谷浑可汗家族的声望显然远远不如“黄金血脉”，天柱王想要自立很正常。
　　只是如果没有大隋支持，天柱王也不敢贸然出这个头。
　　周达道：“可是郎君和三郎君不是推测陛下二征高丽必定失败吗？”
　　罗士信瞳孔地震。还有这事？！二郎君和三郎君这都敢推断！我真的加入了一个忠君爱国的军队吗！
　　呃，陛下是昏君暴君，好像忠不忠诚也无所谓。
　　罗士信一秒给自己做好心理准备。
　　李世民一直在偷偷观察罗士信的神色，将罗士信迅速从震惊转变成淡然，心中对罗士信评价又高了一层。
　　“所以要趁着消息不对等，在大隋战败的消息传到河源郡之前把这个计划完成。”李世民自信道，“天柱王要带我们去青海湖畔狩猎，目的是让西海王看到他已经与大隋结盟。如果西海王惧怕他与大隋结盟，就不会干预他自立。这是我给他出的主意，哼哼。”
　　罗士信傻乎乎道：“我们不是要攻打西海郡吗？西海王不干预他自立，我们怎么打？”
　　李世民无奈：“他们打不打和我们有什么关系？只要天柱部落不出手就行。”
　　罗士信又学到了：“这样啊！我记住了！”
　　李世民道：“而且就算我们也迫于形势做出不攻打西海郡的承诺，该打的时候仍旧要果断出手。谁和蛮夷讲道义？明白吗！”
　　罗士信再次受教：“明白！”
　　李世民笑道：“孺子可教。呼……困了，我先睡了，明日要拔营的事你们安排。周达，多带带士信。”
　　周达道：“是。郎君放心。”
　　李世民打着哈欠道：“你做事我一直放心。”
　　李世民澡都懒得洗，倒头就睡。
　　周达对罗士信语重心长道：“郎君要培养你，你一定要好好努力。”
　　罗士信点头：“一定！周叔，郎君要让你教我什么啊？”
　　周达道：“教你后勤安排。你若独自领军，必须熟知这个。”
　　罗士信心中暖得脸都烧了起来。
　　郎君对自己太好，他都羞愧了。自己一定要更努力。手不释卷，手不释卷！
　　第二日，恢复充沛精力的李世民与天柱王一同一边狩猎，一边往青海湖前行。
　　天柱王的驻地离青海湖只有两百公里，骑马七日就能到。他们一边走一边游玩，半月也到了。
　　还未看到青海湖，李世民和天柱王就见到了率领骑兵前来“迎接”的慕容孝隽。
　　慕容孝隽愤怒质问道：“天柱王！你为何和可汗的仇人在一起！”
　　天柱王知道自己这样慢悠悠来青海湖，肯定会被慕容孝隽发现。他慢悠悠道：“西海王，你也已经对大隋臣服，怎么能对大隋将军无礼？你是想又和大隋为敌吗？”
　　李世民装作活泼少年，直接在马背上给天柱王鼓掌：“说得好！慕容孝隽，你想与我为敌？”
　　慕容孝隽背后的骑兵不怎么样啊。这是他能凑出来的精锐，还是故意展现出虚弱的一面诱我轻敌。
　　李世民心痒难耐，在心底不断念着“阿玄会骂人”把自己的蠢蠢欲动压下。
　　天柱王和李世民一唱一和，慕容孝隽就算城府再深也不由脸色大变。
　　伏允可汗被杀后，他即使再殚精竭虑，也难以让年幼的新可汗得到其他部落的认可，只能割据一方，其中天柱部落自恃强盛，对年幼可汗最不屑一顾。
　　慕容孝隽早就察觉天柱王有脱离吐谷浑之心，但他怎么也没想到，天柱王居然会对杀了伏允可汗的李世民如此礼遇。
　　有什么比伏允可汗的仇更重要？慕容孝隽想起幕僚对自己的劝说。如果天柱王不顾可汗仇恨与大隋联合就只有一个可能，天柱王不满足自立，想要取代吐谷浑！

Chapter 110: Civil Unrest Erupts Across Shandong

Yang Xuangan was in the midst of making a choice.
In his heart, he wanted to choose the inferior strategy: attacking Luoyang.
Although Luoyang housed the families of other officials, attacking Daxing or Zhuo Commandery each had their own merits; the necessity of attacking Luoyang was no greater than that of attacking the other two.
He chose Luoyang because it was prosperous and sat at the very heart of the Great Sui Empire; choosing Luoyang would grant him great prestige.
Furthermore, Zhuo Commandery held the most elite troops of the Great Sui, and although Wei Xuan, the Minister of Justice left to guard Daxing, was not particularly skilled at leading troops, Gao Jiong was still in Daxing compiling books and would certainly not stand idly by.
Though Yang Xuangan held himself in high regard—even earning the moniker "Xiang Yu Reborn"—a man’s reputation was like the shadow cast by a tree. If he wanted to surpass Gao Jiong in military strategy, he could only pray for his father’s soul to possess him.
Luoyang only held Crown Prince Yang Jian and the Duke of Tang, Li Yuan; it appeared to be the softest persimmon.
Li Yuan had never led troops before, and Yang Xuangan should not have feared him, but the reputation of "Li Erlang" was so illustrious that it made him deeply wary of Li Yuan.
Li Erlang was only fourteen years old this year, yet he had already been promoted to the youngest Huben Langjiang (General of the Tiger Guards) in the imperial court due to his merits.
Looking at the feats Li Erlang had accomplished—capturing the Tuyuhun Khan with only a few hundred household servants and cavalry borrowed from the Tiele tribe in his first battle, and leading a makeshift militia to victory after victory when civil unrest broke out during Yang Guang’s first campaign against Goguryeo—these achievements were enough to make one’s scalp tingle.
It could be said that many veteran generals in the court did not possess such dazzling records as Li Erlang—if not for the fact that he was truly too young, the head of the Tuyuhun Khan alone would have been enough to earn him a marquisate.
In the past, when Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were promoted, he had mocked them, claiming they only had such opportunities because they relied on the Duke of Tang’s estate and were Yang Guang’s nephews.
Li Sanlang had not shown much ability in recent years, and his "young scholar" halo had faded. But Li Erlang was simply too dazzling; he had even dragged his sickly brother, Li Sanlang, up to the position of Huya Langjiang.
The two children raised by the Duke of Tang were truly formidable.
With Li Erlang possessing such talent, Li Yuan could certainly not be inferior.
Thinking of Li Erlang’s combat record, Yang Xuangan could not help but hesitate.
Feeling hesitant because of a fourteen-year-old general made Yang Xuangan feel deeply frustrated.
Yet, Li Erlang’s combat record was truly unreasonable. Yang Xuangan even wondered why Yang Guang had not brought Li Erlang along for the second campaign against Goguryeo. Was it because he feared that the Turks or the remnants of the Tuyuhun would harass the rear of the Great Sui during the campaign, and thus left Li Erlang to garrison Zhangye and deter the Western Regions?
While Yang Xuangan hesitated, Li Mi, who had offered the strategy, was deeply disappointed.
Now that civil unrest was erupting across the Great Sui, the courier system had all but collapsed. The various nobles now sent their own retainers to deliver messages, no longer able to rely on the official government courier system.
Luoyang was very close to where Yang Xuangan was raising his army. As soon as Yang Xuangan made a move, Luoyang would certainly be on guard. Moreover, with the Crown Prince in Luoyang and Li Yuan possessing considerable prestige in the court, they held significant autonomy. Even without concrete evidence, they could mobilize funds, grain, and troops to prepare in advance.
Chang'an and Zhuo Commandery were further from the Central Plains, and transportation was blocked by civil unrest. While they were also far away, they could not directly detect his movements like Luoyang could; they relied on the garrison at Luoyang to relay information to them.
With the nation’s strength focused on Goguryeo, the Great Sui’s intelligence system was slow to transmit information. Furthermore, the garrison commander of Chang'an was merely a Minister of Justice; if he wanted to mobilize more troops, he would first have to report to the Emperor or the Crown Prince, and this back-and-forth would consume much time.
In Li Mi’s view, although Zhuo Commandery held the most elite troops of the Great Sui, the army lacked sufficient grain and fodder, and with Yang Guang there to drag them down, achieving strategic goals would be relatively easy. There were risks, but wealth was sought in danger; the rewards of killing Yang Guang and forcing the main force of the Great Sui army to surrender in one fell swoop were too great to pass up.
Choosing Daxing, aside from its slow reaction speed, was also strategic because it was the base of the Guanzhong nobility. Yang Guang had moved the political center to the Eastern Capital and promoted the Jiangnan gentry on a massive scale, leaving the Guanzhong nobles deeply dissatisfied. This Western Capital, neglected by Yang Guang, would likely have little will to resist and might be willing to become Yang Xuangan’s ally.
Furthermore, both Chang'an and Zhuo Commandery were outside the Central Plains; one could retreat and ally with the Turks or Goguryeo, offering a high margin for error.
Luoyang was located in the Central Plains, and its convenient transportation meant that the Great Sui’s armies could support and surround them from all directions. Even if they occupied Luoyang, future development would be extremely difficult. If they lost, there would be nowhere to flee.
Li Mi had originally thought that as the son of Yang Su, Yang Xuangan would have at least some strategic vision. However, seeing Yang Xuangan’s intent to attack Luoyang, he had settled for the next best thing, telling Yang Xuangan that attacking Luoyang was the inferior strategy.
But Yang Xuangan still wanted to go to Luoyang? Did he really think that by capturing Luoyang, he could call upon the world to follow him? Yang Guang was not dead yet!
Li Mi suddenly felt that Yang Xuangan’s self-proclaimed status as Xiang Yu was truly similar to the original: "wearing fine clothes in the dark" and "a monkey dressed in a hat."
Although Li Mi was still treated with courtesy by Yang Xuangan, he began to harbor thoughts of retreat.
Yang Xuangan did not look like someone who could accomplish great things. He needed to be prepared to flee at any time. *Sigh.*
After hesitating for a long time, Yang Xuangan said to Li Mi, "I still intend to attack Luoyang. We will go to Luoyang first; if it is heavily guarded, we will then take the road to Zhuo Commandery."
Li Mi breathed a sigh of relief. *Fine.* At least Yang Xuangan had basic common sense, knowing that the second option was to attack Yang Guang directly rather than Gao Jiong.
Once Yang Xuangan made his decision, he began to prepare for his rebellion in earnest.
He fabricated charges of treason against Lai Hu'er to gather grain and recruit soldiers, then raised his army and marched toward Luoyang.
Li Mi frowned as he looked at Yang Xuangan’s "army of one hundred thousand."
He had assumed that since Yang Xuangan dared to rebel, he would have at least prepared a crack force of about five thousand men.
Surely there should be at least three thousand elite cavalry, fully equipped with warhorses, armor, and weapons?
He had not expected that, apart from Yang Xuangan himself and a few personal guards who had decent weapons, the "army of one hundred thousand" was extremely ill-equipped, completely lacking the strength to conduct a siege.
Had Yang Xuangan not been preparing for this rebellion for a long time? This preparation was far too poor!
Could it be that because Yang Guang’s surveillance was too tight, the Duke of Chu had no opportunity to accumulate the strength for a rebellion? Li Mi found an excuse for him.
Li Mi thought that since Yang Guang’s prestige had not yet fallen and his surveillance of court officials was extremely strict, it was normal for the Duke of Chu to be unable to accumulate strength in advance; he should not blame him.
...
"Achoo." Li Xuanba rubbed his nose.
He tightened his fur cloak and added the final entry to the ledger.
"The nobles of the Western Regions are truly wealthy beyond measure, comparable to the desert oil tycoons of later generations." Li Xuanba smiled. "This is enough to support five hundred elite troops for Second Brother."
Five hundred heavily armored elite cavalry might be difficult to use to conquer the world, but it was more than enough to carve out a territory and become a regional warlord.
After years of hard work and accumulation, he could finally provide his Second Brother, who had led a ragtag army for so long, with a truly elite force. This would allow his brother to unleash his military talent without worrying about anything other than command. This sense of accomplishment made even the usually calm Li Xuanba feel a surge of pride.
The feeling of secretly accumulating power bit by bit and succeeding was simply wonderful.
After finishing the accounts, Li Xuanba opened the letters sent by his family.
His father’s letter merely told him and his Second Brother to take care of their health, rambling on with a bunch of "life experience."
His mother’s letter detailed the recent situation in the Central Plains. When the letter was sent, Yang Xuangan had not yet rebelled, but civil unrest was becoming more frequent.
In the third month, Yang Guang launched his second personal campaign against Goguryeo. At the same time, he conscripted one hundred thousand commoners to repair and expand Daxing City.
His mother sighed in the letter, saying that although the Emperor claimed to only conscript "able-bodied men," when she went to Daxing to visit her daughter, she saw with her own eyes the commoners performing corvée labor on the road, and she did not see a single "able-bodied man."
There were no able-bodied men left.
The able-bodied men of age were not even enough to cover the corvée labor for the Goguryeo campaign; even the strong women had long been assigned to labor. The "able-bodied men" arriving in Daxing were all the old and the young.
Li Xuanba sighed.
Yang Guang launched his campaign against Goguryeo in the third month, and in the same month, he expanded and repaired Daxing City.
Also in the third month, Meng Haigong rose in rebellion in Jiyin (Cao County, Shandong); Meng Rang rose in Qi Commandery (Jinan, Shandong); Guo Fangyu rose in Beihai (Yidu, Shandong); Hao Xiaode in Pingyuan (Pingyuan, Shandong); Ge Qian in Yanci (Wudi, Shandong); and Sun Xuanya in Bohai (Yangxin, Shandong).
This was not the "east of the Xiao Mountains" as referred to today, but within the territory of modern-day Shandong Province—almost the entire region was in rebellion.
The Shandong Peninsula faced the Korean Peninsula across the sea and was the region where Yang Guang had most severely exploited the people for his Goguryeo campaign.
At the same time, the Shandong Peninsula had suffered from severe floods and droughts for the past two years, leaving the people in dire straits.
When Li Xuanba had gone to the foot of Mount Tai, the counties near Shandong were still relatively stable. Now, those counties had likely all fallen.
But Shandong was so close to the Korean Peninsula, and yet the fact that the entire region was in revolt and the counties had fallen did not seem to touch Yang Guang in the slightest.
He truly looked down upon civil unrest.
After reading his mother’s letter, Li Xuanba took a moment to digest these troubling matters before picking up Yuwenzhu’s letter.
Yuwenzhu also mentioned the corvée labor in Daxing City.
She had wanted to go out to practice medicine, but was dissuaded by her master, who said she could not save everyone and would only incite riots, so she had to stop.
"Master says this world is sick, but we physicians can only treat the illnesses of people, not the illness of the world. I asked Master and Grandfather who could treat the world’s illness, and they both remained silent. Actually, I understand; no matter who it is, it ultimately has nothing to do with a woman like me. Asking is useless, so it is better not to ask."
Li Xuanba read the self-pity between the lines of Yuwenzhu’s letter and couldn't help but feel a bit distracted.
When he returned home this time, he would tell Zhuniang that she must also contribute to curing the world’s illness. His mother would join, his Third Sister would join, and his sister-in-law would join. Then Zhuniang would certainly have to assist his mother, Third Sister, and sister-in-law.
After complaining, Yuwenzhu spoke of the people around her.
As Li Xuanba read, his eyes suddenly widened.
"Guanyinbi has developed a respiratory ailment, fortunately I discovered it early. Master said that if it drags on, it will become a lifelong condition and can only be managed. It scared Guanyinbi so much that she cried loudly. It was the first time I had seen her cry so hard."
"Third Sister has been observing mourning, and then nursing the sick, so her health has suffered greatly; I adjusted her condition. She didn't even realize her health had deteriorated so much. I scared her by saying, 'Long-term physical depletion will harm your life,' and now Lady Chai no longer allows Third Sister to nurse the sick; if Third Sister tries to nurse, she refuses to drink her medicine, forcing Third Sister to rest. Lady Chai is truly good to Third Sister."
"Now many noble ladies in the capital are inviting me to adjust their health. They say ordinary physicians find it difficult to diagnose them carefully, and they are fortunate to have me, a female physician. Just as Sanlang said, my skills will truly be useful. Although I feel ashamed to be called a 'renowned physician,' but... I am really amazing!"
Li Xuanba chuckled, his worries dissipating.
That’s right, she really was amazing.

Chapter 111: Li Shimin’s Mission to Heyuan

Li Xuanba let out a long sigh of relief.
Empress Zhangsun had a respiratory ailment. Princess Pingyang likely died due to physical depletion after childbirth.
He knew both of these things.
But when he left Daxing, his sister-in-law did not have bronchitis, and his Third Sister, though tired, was in good spirits. He had thought those were very distant matters.
Chronic bronchitis was often the result of acute bronchitis that was not treated in time and dragged into a chronic condition. After Li Xuanba discovered that his sister-in-law did not have hereditary bronchitis from childhood, he guessed that if the Empress Zhangsun and his sister-in-law in history were in the same physical condition, they might have fallen ill while being driven out of their home and living with their uncle.
Although Gao Shilian was good to his sister and nephew, the bitterness of living under someone else’s roof did not disappear. The ability to read people’s expressions, which Empress Zhangsun and Zhangsun Wuji had almost mastered in historical records, was clearly learned from a childhood of being cautious.
After Empress Zhangsun contracted the respiratory ailment, if it was just a mild cough, she might not have bothered her uncle to invite a renowned physician. Moreover, Gao Shilian would be demoted to Lingnan this year due to his friend Hu Si Zheng.
Gao Shilian’s relationship with Hu Si Zheng was distant; he was only implicated because no one in the court spoke for him, and he was discarded like a small pawn—the status of "uncle of the future second daughter-in-law" was too distant for Li Yuan, not to mention that in the original timeline, Li Yuan had no say in the court when Gao Shilian was demoted.
But things were different now. Zhangsun Sheng was still alive, his Second Brother was well-liked by the Emperor, and his father would be fighting Yang Xuangan on the front lines. They didn't need to do anything; the court officials would take the initiative to strike Gao Shilian from the list of those implicated.
No, Gao Shilian might not even be on the list at all.
"I didn't expect my sister-in-law to almost develop chronic bronchitis." Li Xuanba felt a lingering fear. "And Third Sister... *sigh*. Virtue is all for show; how can it be more important than one’s own health?"
Li Xuanba stroked Yuwenzhu’s letter: "Thanks to Zhuniang."
In Traditional Chinese Medicine, "looking, listening, asking, and feeling the pulse" was not just about taking a pulse. The ancients had long ago accumulated experience in judging conditions by observing various parts of the patient’s body.
For example, pressing an ear to the chest to listen to breath sounds was one of them.
But it was extremely rare for women in the world to practice medicine. Except for those with family traditions, most women, even if they wanted to learn medicine, had no way to find a master and could only study on their own. There were very few female physicians recorded in history.
The Sui Dynasty had only just recovered from the chaos of war. In such times, it was difficult for women to survive, let alone study medicine. Furthermore, studying medicine required literacy, and not every noble or official family taught their daughters to read. The literate noblewomen were pampered and did not engage in production, basically having no opportunity to do the work of a physician, which held a low social status.
Bronchitis was sometimes accompanied by lung issues; when it was neither fully healed nor worsening, there was only a slight cough, and those who did not understand might not even bother to take cough medicine. Only by listening to chest sounds could a physician determine the exact source of the illness.
How could a male physician listen to a female patient’s chest sounds? Even if a stethoscope were invented, female patients would not place it on their chests for a male physician to listen.
Yuwenzhu had not been studying medicine for long; a true renowned physician needed at least twenty or thirty years of experience. She was not a renowned physician, just someone who knew a little bit, yet she could diagnose illnesses in her sister-in-law and Third Sister that even the physicians serving the noble families could not. It was not that her medical skills surpassed those of the old physicians, but simply that when she diagnosed female patients, she did not just take the pulse, or even just use the "silk thread pulse" method.
However... it was just that. Yet it was rare in the world.
Li Xuanba felt a rare moment of emotion before picking up his pen to write a reply.
He first brushed off his father, then comforted his mother, and finally heaped praise upon Zhuniang. *Hmm, what kind of praise should I write?*
After staying at Teacher Yuwen’s house for a few days, and experiencing shopping, spring outings, and wearing flowers together, Li Xuanba’s communication with Yuwenzhu was much more natural. Just as Yuwenzhu would write complaints and playful boasts in her letters to Li Xuanba, Li Xuanba could also chat freely with her.
His Second Brother had taken Luo Shixin and left Zhangye for some unknown purpose. Li Zhiyun, bored and alone, came to find his Third Brother to play.
As soon as he reached the door of the study, he saw his Third Brother writing furiously with a mysterious smile on his face, and he silently turned and left.
Seeing that expression, he knew his Third Brother was writing to his Third Sister-in-law. He’d better not disturb him.
"Sigh," Li Zhiyun said resentfully, "I want a fiancée too."
*So lonely.*
...
Li Shimin’s trip this time was naturally to execute the plan he and Li Xuanba had formulated: to have a chat with Tian Zhu Wang, the leader of the Tuyuhun remnants.
Li Shimin had captured the Tuyuhun King alive, which should have made him an enemy of the Tuyuhun tribes. But after Murong Fuyun was killed, the Tuyuhun had nominally submitted to the Great Sui. Although they were not under the jurisdiction of the Great Sui, they would not actively provoke it unless the Great Sui tried to seize their territory again.
Furthermore, nomadic tribes admired the strong. Since Li Shimin took the initiative to show goodwill toward Tian Zhu Wang, the latter would only treat him with great hospitality.
Luo Shixin had thought that following Li Shimin to "visit" the Tian Zhu tribe would surely lead to a fierce battle. Who would have known that his own Huben Langjun would quickly become "sworn brothers" with Tian Zhu Wang, going hunting together every day, as happy as could be? It made Luo Shixin scratch his head in confusion.
He asked Zhou Da, "Are we really just here to visit?"
Zhou Da was already used to his master’s incredibly high affinity and felt no ripples in his heart: "Otherwise? Langjun said before that we were here to visit, so we are definitely just visiting."
Luo Shixin was skeptical: "Can you really just visit an enemy?" *Unbelievable!*
Zhou Da chuckled: "Enemy? Where is the enemy? Not to mention that Tian Zhu Wang might not be loyal to the former Tuyuhun Khan, even if there were a real grudge, as long as Langjun wants to, he can turn enemies into friends. No one can resist Langjun’s enthusiasm."
Luo Shixin sighed: "So what Jihong said was true."
Zhou Da was curious: "What did the Fifth Langjun tell you?"
Luo Shixin said solemnly: "Jihong said, 'Whenever you need to deal with a troublesome person, Third Brother will close the door and release Second Brother!'"
Zhou Da: "Pfft!"
"Hey, hey, hey, am I a hunting dog or a falcon? What do you mean 'close the door and release Second Brother'?" Li Shimin walked over, smelling of alcohol, and yawned. "Brew me some hangover medicine. Honestly, they insisted on drinking. If they knew I drank too much, A-Xuan would nag me endlessly."
Zhou Da hurried to brew the hangover medicine himself.
Luo Shixin brought warm water for Li Shimin to wash his face: "How much longer are we staying here?"
Li Shimin said while washing his face: "What? Bored?"
Luo Shixin said with a bitter face: "So bored."
Li Shimin wiped the water from his face: "Do you think you’ll only be fighting battles for the rest of your life? Watch carefully, listen carefully, and learn. In the future, if you want to garrison a region, these skills will all come in handy."
Luo Shixin still said with a bitter face: "I know, but it’s so boring."
Li Shimin laughed: "Even if it’s boring, you have to learn."
Luo Shixin hung his head in defeat: "Yes."
After drinking the hangover medicine, Li Shimin patted his face to wake himself up and ordered: "Alright, I know it’s not just Shixin; my soldiers are bored too. Tomorrow we can break camp and head to Xihai Commandery to hunt with Tian Zhu Wang."
Luo Shixin and Zhou Da’s eyes lit up.
Zhou Da said: "He was finally persuaded?"
Li Shimin smiled: "Although the Tuyuhun only recognize the Murong family as Khans, why not be the Tian Zhu Khan if you can't be the Tuyuhun Khan? If Fuyun were still here, he wouldn't have the heart to stand alone. But he is dissatisfied that a mere yellow-haired child is above him. With the support of the powerful Great Sui, it’s hard for him not to be tempted."
Nomadic tribes on the grasslands never had much loyalty to their Khans. Even after Genghis Khan established the "Golden Bloodline," many ambitious people wanted to stand alone. The Oirat of the Ming Dynasty, also known as the Dzungar of the Qing Dynasty, looked down on the so-called "Golden Bloodline."
The prestige of the Tuyuhun Khan family was clearly far inferior to the "Golden Bloodline," so it was normal for Tian Zhu Wang to want to stand alone.
It was just that without the support of the Great Sui, Tian Zhu Wang would not dare to take the lead rashly.
Zhou Da said: "But didn't Langjun and Third Langjun speculate that His Majesty’s second campaign against Goguryeo would definitely fail?"
Luo Shixin’s pupils dilated. *There’s that too?! Second Langjun and Third Langjun dare to speculate on this! Have I really joined a loyal and patriotic army!*
*Eh, His Majesty is a foolish and tyrannical emperor, so it seems loyalty doesn't really matter.*
Luo Shixin prepared himself mentally in a second.
Li Shimin had been secretly observing Luo Shixin’s expression, and seeing him shift from shock to indifference, his evaluation of Luo Shixin rose another level.
"So we must take advantage of the information asymmetry and complete this plan before the news of the Great Sui’s defeat reaches Heyuan Commandery," Li Shimin said confidently. "Tian Zhu Wang wants to take us hunting by Qinghai Lake, the goal being to let the Xihai King see that he has already allied with the Great Sui. If the Xihai King fears his alliance with the Great Sui, he won't interfere with his self-reliance. This is the idea I gave him, heh heh."
Luo Shixin said foolishly: "Aren't we going to attack Xihai Commandery? If the Xihai King doesn't interfere with his self-reliance, how do we fight?"
Li Shimin was helpless: "What does it have to do with us whether they fight or not? As long as the Tian Zhu tribe doesn't intervene, it’s fine."
Luo Shixin learned again: "So that’s it! I’ll remember that!"
Li Shimin said: "And even if we are forced by the situation to make a promise not to attack Xihai Commandery, we must still strike decisively when the time comes. Who talks about morality with barbarians? Understand!"
Luo Shixin was taught again: "Understood!"
Li Shimin smiled: "The child is teachable. *Hoo*... I’m sleepy, I’m going to sleep first; you guys arrange the camp breaking for tomorrow. Zhou Da, take Shixin under your wing."
Zhou Da said: "Yes. Langjun, don't worry."
Li Shimin yawned: "I’ve always been at ease with how you do things."
Li Shimin didn't even bother to bathe and fell asleep as soon as his head hit the pillow.
Zhou Da said earnestly to Luo Shixin: "Langjun wants to cultivate you, you must work hard."
Luo Shixin nodded: "Definitely! Uncle Zhou, what does Langjun want you to teach me?"
Zhou Da said: "Teach you logistics planning. If you lead an army alone, you must be familiar with this."
Luo Shixin felt so warm inside that his face burned.
Langjun was too good to him, and he felt ashamed. He must work even harder. *Keep reading, keep reading!*
The next day, a refreshed Li Shimin hunted with Tian Zhu Wang while heading toward Qinghai Lake.
Tian Zhu Wang’s base was only two hundred kilometers from Qinghai Lake, a seven-day ride. They played as they went, arriving in half a month.
Before they even saw Qinghai Lake, Li Shimin and Tian Zhu Wang saw Murong Xiaojun leading cavalry to "greet" them.
Murong Xiaojun angrily questioned: "Tian Zhu Wang! Why are you with the Khan’s enemy!"
Tian Zhu Wang knew that his slow arrival at Qinghai Lake would certainly be discovered by Murong Xiaojun. He said slowly: "Xihai King, you have also submitted to the Great Sui, how can you be rude to a Great Sui general? Do you want to be an enemy of the Great Sui again?"
Li Shimin pretended to be a lively youth, clapping for Tian Zhu Wang on horseback: "Well said! Murong Xiaojun, do you want to be my enemy?"
*The cavalry behind Murong Xiaojun doesn't look that great. Is this the elite he can scrape together, or is he deliberately showing weakness to lure me into underestimating him?*
Li Shimin felt an itch in his heart, constantly repeating "A-Xuan will scold me" in his mind to suppress his urge to act.
With Tian Zhu Wang and Li Shimin singing in harmony, Murong Xiaojun’s face changed drastically, no matter how deep his city-dwelling nature was.
After Fuyun Khan was killed, no matter how hard he tried, it was difficult for the young new Khan to gain recognition from other tribes, so he could only carve out a territory. Among them, the Tian Zhu tribe relied on their strength and held the young Khan in the greatest contempt.
Murong Xiaojun had long sensed that Tian Zhu Wang had a heart to break away from the Tuyuhun, but he never expected that Tian Zhu Wang would treat Li Shimin, who had killed Fuyun Khan, with such courtesy.
*What could be more important than the grudge against Fuyun Khan?* Murong Xiaojun recalled his advisor’s persuasion. If Tian Zhu Wang disregarded the Khan’s hatred and allied with the Great Sui, there was only one possibility: Tian Zhu Wang was not satisfied with self-reliance; he wanted to replace the Tuyuhun!

chunks.chapterTitle: 第112章 翩翩少年血盈袖
chunks.chineseText:
第112章 翩翩少年血盈袖

慕容孝隽看向李世民的眼中全是仇恨。
　　李世民满脸笑容地看着他， 转头对天柱王称赞道：“西海王倒是个忠臣。”
　　天柱王看向李世民的眼神十分复杂：“是啊。”这是没心没肺呢，还是专门讽刺？
　　慕容孝隽显然认为李世民在讽刺他。
　　他冷哼道：“归顺大隋是一回事，不能放过可汗的仇人是另一回事。”
　　李世民笑道：“那你去找大隋的皇帝啊。我只是一个小小将领， 听命行事。”
　　李世民在逗弄慕容孝隽的时候， 视线扫过慕容孝隽身后的骑兵。
　　就一千人， 还没带甲？李世民眼中闪过轻蔑。
　　“你现在拦着我，难道是想为你家可汗报仇？”李世民对身后的兵卒道，“盔甲穿上， 有仗打了！”
　　李世民身后表情散漫的骑兵立刻把头盔戴上。
　　慕容孝隽在此处等候的事，天柱王派去的人早就打探到了消息。
　　天柱王只是想给慕容孝隽施加压力，不是想真的和慕容孝隽打起来， 去青海湖畔“狩猎”的时候当然会先通知慕容孝隽一声。
　　为防万一，靠近青海湖畔的时候李世民就要求原地休整半日。出发的时候， 他和所有士卒都穿戴了甲， 只是把头盔挂在马背上懒得戴。
　　天柱王带来的人也穿上了皮甲，并在皮甲上插上了五颜六色的羽毛，以展现他的威严。
　　这是李世民的主意。
　　既然我们要去威吓西海王，自然要把盔甲都穿戴整齐了，让他看到我们威风的模样， 对吧？
　　天柱王深以为然。
　　现在李世民一说有仗打了，本就带甲的下属立刻准备妥当。
　　他们身上散漫的气质顿时一清， 肃杀之气蔓延。
　　李世民未有动作，下属自己小幅度调整位置，很快就组成了整齐的方阵。
　　天柱王不动声色地看慕容孝隽笑话。
　　他当然能看出来， 慕容孝隽肯定不想和隋朝将领起冲突。
　　慕容孝隽现在势弱， 一不小心就会被吐谷浑其他部吞并。他也知道自己暂时不想打， 现在虚张声势， 不过是想保住脸面罢了。
　　毕竟慕容孝隽自称辅佐吐谷浑可汗，就算承认自己自立，也要装出个从容的模样。
　　天柱王甚至怀疑，这位伏允可汗最信任的大臣，现在对李郎将露出的悲愤有几分真实。
　　慕容孝隽严密控制那位年幼的吐谷浑可汗，不准他与其他名王接触时，可不像是多记着伏允可汗恩情的模样。
　　李世民这次出行只带了五百零一个骑兵。
　　其中五百骑兵是他挑选出来的精锐，吃穿住行盔甲武器都是最好的，是跟随他作战多年的老卒。
　　那“零一个”，就是罗士信。
　　罗士信虽然还没有副将之名，但李世民已经把他当副将培养。
　　罗士信第一次出任务，就击破了突厥一个小部落。老卒看着罗士信拼杀的模样都有点心悸。再加上老卒大多是唐国公府家生子或者应征来的平头百姓，罗士信身为寒门士子子弟的身份比不过世家和勋贵，但也会被人高看一眼。
　　有身份，有本事，有功劳，李世民破格提拔罗士信没有引起老卒不满。
　　现在罗士信拍马来到李世民身边，与周达并立李世民左右。
　　周达手握令旗，负责传达李世民的命令；罗士信就只负责给李世民当护卫。
　　李世民像个没城府的熊孩子一样叫嚷：“是不是要打？打不打？不打就赶紧走。我和天柱王要在这里狩猎，别扰了我们狩猎的兴致。还是说你是想陪我们一起打猎？”
　　李世民对天柱王笑道：“西海王想加入我们的狩猎，天柱王可同意？”
　　天柱王捋着胡须道：“那自然是非常欢迎。西海王，可否放下恩怨，给本王一点脸面？”
　　慕容孝隽见天柱王完全站在李世民这边，知道已经没有了回转的余地。
　　李世民虽然偷袭杀掉了伏允可汗，但慕容孝隽轻视李世民的年龄，再加上李世民是大隋勋贵子弟，迟早会回中原，并没把李世民当敌人。他此次的目的只是打探天柱王是否有吞并自己部族的意图。
　　他担忧天柱王有与他开战之意，所以不能惹怒天柱王，才只针对李世民，打探天柱王的态度。
　　慕容孝隽脸色一沉：“天柱王，你确定要脱离吐谷浑了吗？”
　　天柱王叹气：“西海王，吐谷浑早就已经失败了。现在我们依附的是大隋，不是吗？你也派使臣去向大隋皇帝朝贺了。”
　　慕容孝隽道：“吐谷浑实力不如人，我愿意臣服大隋皇帝。但杀了可汗的仇人我绝对不会放过。”
　　天柱王也脸色一沉：“你想如何？”
　　慕容孝隽冷声道：“应该是我问你要如何！你若想自立就自立，为何要把可汗的仇人带到我面前！”
　　天柱王也火大了：“我带就带了，你要如何？”
　　慕容孝隽愤怒道：“我要如何？我决不允许可汗的仇人活着离开这里！”
　　天柱王一听，就知道慕容孝隽要开价了。
　　什么不允许伏允可汗的仇人活着离开这里。他敢冒与大隋和天柱部落同时开战的险杀掉李郎将吗？
　　若他对伏允这么不顾自己的生命和部族，就不会向大隋臣服。
　　再说，李世民已经在张掖几月，可没见慕容孝隽有任何想要攻打张掖的举动。
　　天柱王扫了一眼慕容孝隽身后的一千青壮骑兵。
　　这一千青壮骑兵都没有带甲，马背上也没有背多少弓箭。
　　他心中更加确定自己的猜测。
　　天柱王正色道：“李二郎是我带来，我就要把他平安地带回去。难道你要和我开战？”你开价吧，但别过分。
　　慕容孝隽咬牙切齿道：“天柱王！我看错你了！好，好，我今日……”
　　李世民：“杀。”
　　战马嘶鸣，令旗高立，弓弦鸣叫。
　　李世民率先拍马冲出，周达和罗士信一人手持长刀，一人手持长矛，与挽弓的李世民并驾齐驱。
　　骑兵方阵狠狠撞上了队形散漫的慕容伏允队伍。
　　“士信，你持矛，我挽弓，我们比一比谁杀的吐谷浑人多！”李世民大笑道，“慕容孝隽，你要为慕容伏允报仇，尽管来！”
　　他手中的弓箭应声射出。
　　慕容孝隽大惊失色，连忙躲闪。
　　李世民的箭居然不是直取慕容孝隽，而是一剑射中他身旁壮硕护卫的眼眶。
　　壮硕护卫惨叫一声，吃痛捂住眼睛。
　　罗士信瞅准机会长矛递出，借着马往前奔驰的动力，一矛插穿护卫的胸口。
　　长矛带着壮硕护卫的身体落马，惨叫声立刻消失在战马践踏中。
　　“抢我人头？”李世民又是一箭，射中了慕容孝隽身侧另一个壮硕护卫的马眼睛。
　　战马惨叫一声，马蹄高高扬起。
　　罗士信再次趁机一矛，矛尖刮过慌张勒马的另一个壮硕护卫的脖子。
　　李世民后一箭射来，正中壮硕护卫胸口。
　　罗士信抿嘴。李世民大笑。
　　“变阵！”李世民杀了慕容孝隽队伍中最能打的两人后，立刻下令，“游走！”
　　刚撞散敌人的骑兵随着李世民从侧面穿出，然后方阵变长蛇阵，绕着溃散的敌人游走。
　　李世民就像是借了鹰的视角似的，周围再混乱，他下一次冲锋的地方一定是慕容孝隽所在地方。
　　但他又不直接朝着慕容孝隽冲锋，而是擦着敌人边缘“刮”过去。
　　骑兵除了初次冲锋时弓箭齐射，现在除了李世民外，皆用马槊、长矛、长刀，见人见马就劈砍。他们也不管对方死没死，砍完就骑着战马离开，斜着绕敌人一圈后，继续朝着慕容孝隽的地方冲锋。
　　李世民的弓箭就像是自带导航似的，每当慕容孝隽出声下命令时，总能射中离慕容孝隽身边最近的人，吓得慕容孝隽打断指挥。
　　他宛如狸猫戏老鼠般戏耍敌人，让慕容孝隽组织不起抵抗。
　　天柱王大惊失色，冒出了一脑门的冷汗。
　　他正和慕容孝隽讨价还价，李世民突然冲了出去，率领五百轻甲骑兵瞬间冲垮了没有防备的慕容孝隽。
　　慕容孝隽所率领的一千多人就像是无害的羊群，被头狼领着狼群包围起来。
　　这一千人每次想逃窜的方向，总有李世民骑兵堵住去路，迫使他们往慕容孝隽的地方靠拢。但李世民下一次冲锋，又再次把聚集在慕容孝隽身边的人冲散。
　　如此循环往复，地上倒下的人和马越来越多，李世民所率领的骑兵包围圈越来越小。
　　这根本不是打仗，是围猎！天柱王惶恐，李世民难道是想把慕容孝隽所率领的人全杀了？！
　　“啧！箭用光了。”李世民一弓背砸碎了落马后刚站起来的吐谷浑人脑袋，弓往马鞍上一挂，反手抽出长刀。
　　这次他没有再“戏耍”已经神情崩溃的慕容孝隽，左右劈砍身侧逃窜的吐谷浑人，直接朝着慕容孝隽冲去。
　　骑兵也再次变阵，离慕容孝隽较远处的包围圈出现了一个口子。
　　在被围猎的“羊群”眼中，这个逃生的口子是那么的明显。“羊群”立刻涌向生路。
　　骑兵没有阻拦“羊群”离开，只拦住了“头羊”。
　　慕容孝隽见势不妙，赶紧高喊：“我投降……”
　　“啾！”
　　他话未说完，一只金雕落下，狠狠往他脑袋上一抓，然后迅速升空飞走。
　　“啊！！”头皮被抓掉一块的，慕容孝隽捂头惨叫。
　　他眼前寒光一闪，脑袋滚落，双目失去光芒。
　　“别追了。”李世民收刀，“留点体力，等会儿还要去看看吐谷浑的小可汗。”
　　出手慢了一招的罗士信瘪着嘴收起长矛，下马帮李世民拾脑袋。
　　李世民慢悠悠策马，回到瞠目结舌目瞪口呆噤若寒蝉的天柱王身前。
　　他摘下头盔，甩了甩头盔上的血滴。把头盔挂在马背上后，他又卸掉臂甲，把湿透了的袖子一拧，鲜血如注。
　　“真麻烦，好了，解决了。”李世民露出标志性阳光开朗笑容，“先去西海王的部族借帐篷换身衣服洗个澡，我们继续狩猎。这下没人打扰我们了。”
　　天柱王：“啊？”
　　李世民一边继续拧袖子，一边笑道：“天柱王知道他的部落在哪吗？地上还有没死透的，我去问路？”
　　天柱王使劲摇头，又使劲点头：“不用不用，我知道我知道，我带你去！”
　　李世民道：“牧民归你，牛羊财物归我如何？你缺人我缺钱，给个面子。”
　　“给给给。”天柱王发觉失言，忙道，“我没出力，全是你的！”
　　李世民笑道：“以你我交情，别说这么客气。我说把牧民分给你就分给你。若实在不好意思，派点人帮我把牲畜财物运回张掖。我带的这点人，捉襟见肘啊。”
　　说罢，他扬了扬全是血的手肘。
　　天柱王：“一言为定！”
　　别对我笑了！赶紧走！
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 112: A Youthful Prodigy with Blood-Stained Sleeves

Murong Xiaojun looked at Li Shimin with eyes full of hatred.
Li Shimin gazed back at him with a beaming smile, then turned his head to praise Tian Zhu Wang, "The King of the West Sea is truly a loyal subject."
Tian Zhu Wang’s expression as he looked at Li Shimin was deeply complex. "Indeed." Was this boy being sincere, or was he being deliberately sarcastic?
Murong Xiaojun clearly took it as sarcasm.
He snorted coldly, "Submitting to the Great Sui is one thing; letting the Khan’s enemy go unpunished is quite another."
Li Shimin laughed, "Then go find the Emperor of the Great Sui. I am merely a lowly officer, following orders."
While teasing Murong Xiaojun, Li Shimin’s gaze swept over the cavalry behind him.
Only a thousand men, and not even wearing armor? A flash of contempt crossed Li Shimin’s eyes.
"You are blocking my path now—are you trying to avenge your Khan?" Li Shimin said to the soldiers behind him, "Put on your armor! We have a battle to fight!"
The previously languid-looking cavalry behind Li Shimin immediately donned their helmets.
Tian Zhu Wang’s scouts had long since discovered that Murong Xiaojun was waiting here.
Tian Zhu Wang only wanted to pressure Murong Xiaojun, not actually engage him in a full-scale war, so he had naturally notified Murong Xiaojun when they set out to "hunt" by the shores of Qinghai Lake.
Just in case, Li Shimin had ordered a half-day rest near the lake. When they departed, he and all his soldiers had already donned their armor, merely leaving their helmets hanging from their saddles, too lazy to wear them.
The men brought by Tian Zhu Wang also wore leather armor, adorned with colorful feathers to display his majesty.
This had been Li Shimin’s idea.
Since we are going to intimidate the King of the West Sea, we naturally need to be fully armored so he can see how formidable we are, right?
Tian Zhu Wang had agreed wholeheartedly.
Now that Li Shimin announced a battle, his subordinates, already armored, were instantly prepared.
The listless air about them vanished, replaced by a spreading, murderous chill.
Li Shimin didn't even need to move; his subordinates made minor adjustments to their positions, quickly forming a neat phalanx.
Tian Zhu Wang watched Murong Xiaojun’s predicament with a calm, detached amusement.
He could clearly see that Murong Xiaojun definitely did not want to clash with a Sui general.
Murong Xiaojun was currently weak; one wrong move and he would be swallowed up by the other Tuyuhun tribes. He knew that Murong Xiaojun didn't want to fight right now and was merely posturing to save face.
After all, Murong Xiaojun claimed to be assisting the Tuyuhun Khan; even if he wanted to declare independence, he had to maintain a facade of composure.
Tian Zhu Wang even doubted how much of the grief and indignation this most trusted minister of Khan Fuyun was showing to Li Shimin was actually real.
When Murong Xiaojun strictly controlled the young Tuyuhun Khan, forbidding him from contacting other prominent kings, he didn't look like someone who cherished the memory of Khan Fuyun’s kindness.
Li Shimin had brought only five hundred and one cavalrymen on this trip.
Five hundred of them were elites he had hand-picked—the best in food, clothing, mounts, armor, and weapons—veterans who had fought under him for years.
That "one" was Luo Shixin.
Although Luo Shixin did not yet hold the title of deputy commander, Li Shimin was already grooming him as one.
In his first mission, Luo Shixin had shattered a small Turkic tribe. Even the veterans felt a shiver when they saw him fighting. Furthermore, while most veterans were either born into the Duke of Tang’s household or commoners who had enlisted, and Luo Shixin’s status as a son of a minor gentry family couldn't compare to the great clans or nobility, he was still held in higher regard than most.
With status, ability, and merit, Li Shimin’s exceptional promotion of Luo Shixin did not cause any resentment among the veterans.
Now, Luo Shixin spurred his horse to Li Shimin’s side, standing alongside Zhou Da.
Zhou Da held the command flag, responsible for relaying Li Shimin’s orders; Luo Shixin was solely responsible for acting as Li Shimin’s personal guard.
Li Shimin shouted like a naive, reckless child, "Are we fighting or not? If not, get out of the way! Tian Zhu Wang and I are here to hunt; don't ruin our mood. Or are you saying you want to join us for the hunt?"
Li Shimin smiled at Tian Zhu Wang, "The King of the West Sea wants to join our hunt. Does Tian Zhu Wang agree?"
Tian Zhu Wang stroked his beard and said, "That would be most welcome. King of the West Sea, can you put aside your grievances and grant me a little face?"
Seeing that Tian Zhu Wang was completely on Li Shimin’s side, Murong Xiaojun knew there was no room for negotiation.
Although Li Shimin had ambushed and killed Khan Fuyun, Murong Xiaojun looked down on Li Shimin’s age, and since Li Shimin was a scion of the Great Sui nobility who would eventually return to the Central Plains, he didn't truly view him as a mortal enemy. His goal was merely to probe whether Tian Zhu Wang intended to annex his tribe.
He feared Tian Zhu Wang intended to go to war, so he couldn't afford to anger him, which is why he targeted only Li Shimin to test the waters.
Murong Xiaojun’s face darkened, "Tian Zhu Wang, are you certain you want to break away from the Tuyuhun?"
Tian Zhu Wang sighed, "King of the West Sea, the Tuyuhun has already failed. We are now subjects of the Great Sui, are we not? You, too, have sent envoys to pay homage to the Sui Emperor."
Murong Xiaojun retorted, "The Tuyuhun may be weaker, and I am willing to submit to the Sui Emperor. But I will never let the enemy who killed the Khan go free."
Tian Zhu Wang’s face also darkened, "What do you intend to do?"
Murong Xiaojun said coldly, "That is what I should be asking you! If you want to declare independence, so be it, but why bring the Khan’s enemy before me!"
Tian Zhu Wang grew angry, "I brought him, so what?"
Murong Xiaojun roared, "What do I intend? I will never allow the Khan’s enemy to leave this place alive!"
Upon hearing this, Tian Zhu Wang knew Murong Xiaojun was just posturing for a price.
"Never allow the Khan’s enemy to leave alive"? Would he dare risk a war with both the Great Sui and the Tian Zhu tribe just to kill Officer Li?
If he were so reckless with his own life and tribe for Fuyun’s sake, he wouldn't have submitted to the Great Sui in the first place.
Besides, Li Shimin had been in Zhangye for months, and there had been no sign of Murong Xiaojun attempting to attack the city.
Tian Zhu Wang glanced at the thousand able-bodied cavalrymen behind Murong Xiaojun.
None of them were wearing armor, and there weren't many bows or arrows on their saddles.
His suspicion was confirmed.
Tian Zhu Wang said sternly, "Li Erlang is with me, and I will bring him back safely. Are you trying to start a war with me?" *Name your price, but don't go too far.*
Murong Xiaojun gritted his teeth, "Tian Zhu Wang! I misjudged you! Fine, fine, today I..."
Li Shimin: "Kill."
Warhorses neighed, the command flag stood tall, and bowstrings hummed.
Li Shimin was the first to spur his horse forward, with Zhou Da holding a long saber and Luo Shixin a long spear, riding abreast of Li Shimin as he drew his bow.
The cavalry phalanx slammed into the disorganized formation of Murong Xiaojun’s men.
"Shixin, you take the spear, I’ll take the bow—let’s see who kills more Tuyuhun!" Li Shimin laughed loudly, "Murong Xiaojun, if you want to avenge Murong Fuyun, come and get me!"
The arrow in his hand flew true.
Murong Xiaojun was terrified and scrambled to dodge.
Li Shimin’s arrow didn't aim for Murong Xiaojun at all, but instead pierced the eye socket of a burly guard beside him.
The guard screamed, clutching his eye in agony.
Luo Shixin seized the opportunity, thrusting his spear forward; using the momentum of his charging horse, he impaled the guard through the chest.
The spear carried the guard’s body off his horse, and his screams were instantly silenced under the hooves of the warhorses.
"Stealing my kill?" Li Shimin fired another arrow, hitting the eye of the horse belonging to another burly guard beside Murong Xiaojun.
The horse shrieked and reared up.
Luo Shixin seized the chance again, his spear tip grazing the neck of another guard who was frantically trying to rein in his horse.
Li Shimin’s follow-up arrow struck the guard squarely in the chest.
Luo Shixin pursed his lips. Li Shimin laughed.
"Change formation!" After killing the two most capable fighters in Murong Xiaojun’s group, Li Shimin immediately ordered, "Skirmish!"
The cavalry, having just shattered the enemy, followed Li Shimin as they broke off to the sides, the phalanx shifting into a long snake formation, circling the crumbling enemy.
Li Shimin seemed to have the perspective of an eagle; no matter how chaotic the surroundings, his next charge always targeted Murong Xiaojun’s position.
Yet he didn't charge directly at Murong Xiaojun, but rather "scraped" along the edges of the enemy.
Aside from the initial volley of arrows, the cavalry now used horse-lances, spears, and long sabers, hacking at any man or horse they passed. They didn't care if the target was dead; they would strike and ride on, circling the enemy diagonally before charging toward Murong Xiaojun’s position again.
Li Shimin’s arrows seemed to have their own guidance system; whenever Murong Xiaojun tried to issue an order, he would strike the person closest to him, scaring Murong Xiaojun into silence.
He toyed with the enemy like a cat playing with a mouse, preventing Murong Xiaojun from organizing any resistance.
Tian Zhu Wang was horrified, cold sweat breaking out on his forehead.
He had been in the middle of bargaining with Murong Xiaojun when Li Shimin suddenly charged out, leading his five hundred lightly armored cavalry to instantly crush the unprepared Murong Xiaojun.
The thousand-plus men led by Murong Xiaojun were like a harmless flock of sheep, surrounded by a wolf pack led by an alpha.
Every time the thousand men tried to flee, Li Shimin’s cavalry would block their path, forcing them to huddle back toward Murong Xiaojun. But Li Shimin’s next charge would scatter them once more.
In this cycle, more and more men and horses fell, and the circle drawn by Li Shimin’s cavalry grew tighter and tighter.
This wasn't a battle; it was a hunt! Tian Zhu Wang was terrified—did Li Shimin intend to kill every single one of them?!
"Tch! Out of arrows." Li Shimin smashed the head of a Tuyuhun soldier who had just stood up after falling, hung his bow on the saddle, and drew his long saber.
This time, he didn't "toy" with the mentally broken Murong Xiaojun; he hacked left and right at the fleeing soldiers, charging directly toward him.
The cavalry changed formation again, leaving a gap in the circle far from Murong Xiaojun.
In the eyes of the "flock" being hunted, this escape route was glaringly obvious. The "flock" immediately surged toward the path of survival.
The cavalry didn't stop the "flock" from leaving; they only blocked the "lead sheep."
Seeing the situation was dire, Murong Xiaojun shouted, "I surrender..."
"Screech!"
Before he could finish, a golden eagle dove down, clawing viciously at his scalp before soaring back into the sky.
"Ahhh!" With a chunk of his scalp torn away, Murong Xiaojun clutched his head and screamed.
A flash of cold light passed before his eyes, his head rolled to the ground, and the light faded from his gaze.
"Stop chasing," Li Shimin sheathed his saber, "Save your strength; we still have to go see the little Tuyuhun Khan later."
Luo Shixin, having been a step too slow, pouted as he retracted his spear and dismounted to help Li Shimin retrieve the head.
Li Shimin rode slowly back to the side of Tian Zhu Wang, who stood dumbfounded, his jaw dropped, trembling in silence.
He took off his helmet and shook the blood droplets from it. After hanging it on his saddle, he removed his arm guards and wrung out his soaked sleeves, blood pouring out like a stream.
"What a hassle. Alright, it’s settled." Li Shimin flashed his signature sunny, cheerful smile, "Let’s go to the King of the West Sea’s tribe to borrow some tents, change clothes, and wash up. Then we can continue our hunt. Now, no one will disturb us."
Tian Zhu Wang: "Huh?"
Li Shimin continued wringing his sleeves while laughing, "Does Tian Zhu Wang know where his tribe is? There are still some who aren't quite dead on the ground; should I go ask for directions?"
Tian Zhu Wang shook his head vigorously, then nodded just as hard, "No, no, I know, I know! I’ll take you there!"
Li Shimin said, "How about the herdsmen go to you, and the cattle, sheep, and wealth go to me? You lack people, and I lack money—do me a favor."
"Yes, yes, of course." Tian Zhu Wang realized he had spoken out of turn and quickly added, "I didn't contribute anything; it’s all yours!"
Li Shimin smiled, "Given our friendship, don't be so polite. I said I’d give you the herdsmen, so I will. If you really feel bad about it, just send some men to help me transport the livestock and goods back to Zhangye. The few men I brought are stretched thin."
With that, he gestured with his blood-soaked elbows.
Tian Zhu Wang: "It’s a deal!"
*Stop smiling at me! Just leave already!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第113章 历史悄然小拐弯
chunks.chineseText:
第113章 历史悄然小拐弯

周达和罗士信带着将士打扫完战场， 把耳朵分了分，之后再算功劳。
　　只有慕容孝隽的脑袋完整无缺，等到了慕容孝隽所在的部族时找盐和石灰腌制， 等陛下回东都后送过去邀功。
　　队伍重新启程， 直接向慕容孝隽所建立的吐谷浑小朝廷部族前行。
　　天柱王和他带来的下属表情有些僵硬， 眼底藏着藏不住的忌惮。
　　天柱王此次来西海郡带了五千人。其中两千是青壮骑兵，剩下三千有下属，有仆从， 有美姬，负责后勤和伺候权贵。
　　慕容孝隽带来的一千多骑兵看着人数少，但他只带来了青壮精锐， 只论能打仗的精锐人数没比天柱王少太多。
　　李世民只带了五百精锐，路上依靠隋朝驿站和城镇的补给， 一个后勤人员都没有带， 自己押送干粮和礼物。
　　等李世民到达天柱部落后，就吃天柱王的用天柱王的。这次来青海，他的补给也是和天柱王混在一起。
　　看李世民的人员配置，天柱王料定李世民没想过打仗，才放心把李世民带来威慑慕容孝隽。
　　李世民虽然告诉天柱王自己之后会攻打慕容孝隽。他支持天柱王自立， 就是以天柱王部插手支援慕容孝隽为交换。但天柱王所猜测的是李世民之后会率大军来西海郡。他希望最好隋军和慕容孝隽两败俱伤，自己好轻松获得渔翁之利。
　　谁能猜到这个平时表现十分活泼善良， 连对卑贱的牧民都会微笑着说话的少年郎，居然一言不合直接把慕容孝隽屠了？
　　你有这本事，还和我称兄道弟说什么联合？你这是杀鸡儆猴吧？！
　　天柱王头皮都麻了。
　　他在战场上拼杀多年， 见过无数血腥场景， 自己也不是什么良善人， 杀人取乐的事也做过。他的属下中也有很多心性残忍暴虐， 吃过人肉的都不少。
　　但他还是对李世民突然翻脸的行为心有余悸。
　　他们所做的事都符合逻辑和人设。李郎将是怎么回事？刚刚还笑着说慕容孝隽要和他们一起狩猎，怎么就突然开屠了？而且以李郎将的聪慧，天柱王不相信李郎将看不出慕容孝隽并没有开战的意思，只是随便找个借口和自己讨价还价。
　　天柱王捏着缰绳的手心全是汗。
　　李世民看出天柱王的忌惮，微笑着没有去打扰天柱王在那担惊受怕。
　　怕什么？我又不会转过来把你也屠了。
　　李世民当然不是喜怒无常一时兴起，鲁莽行事。
　　他许多看上去很莽的行为，其实更应该说是“奇”——抓准时机，出奇制胜。
　　西海郡是一定要占领的，慕容孝隽是一定要杀的。首先，慕容孝隽就在李世民必须剿灭的名单上。
　　李玄霸派出的探子打探了慕容孝隽所统率的部族情况，李世民知道慕容孝隽顶多只能凑出接近四千的青壮兵卒，收拢的慕容伏允残部老卒有一千人左右。
　　在这，刚见到慕容孝隽，李世民就在观察慕容孝隽所带兵卒的数量和装备情况。
　　确实如天柱王所想，李世民在看见那些兵卒混乱的队列，就知道慕容孝隽只是虚张声势，没有真想打的意思。
　　但那又如何？

　　卫玄感慨道：“唐国公在洛阳击败杨玄感，李二郎君又为大隋镇守边患。父子二人合在一起，堪称对大隋有再造之功，真是大隋的镇国功臣啊。”
　　高颎捏着棋子的手微微一抖。
　　他严肃道：“卫尚书，此话不可乱说。大隋只是有了一点小叛乱，大体仍旧是繁荣安定的，何谈‘再造’‘镇国’？若你的话传到陛下耳中，你和唐国公父子可能都会被怪罪。”
　　卫玄叹气：“是我失言了，高公。”连最为耿直的高公都被陛下逼成这样了吗？这天底下可还有敢对陛下说真话的人？
　　卫玄转移话题：“杨玄感会攻打关中吗？”
　　高颎淡淡道：“他不敢。”
　　大兴九年七月，杨玄感试探地攻打了几次洛阳，见洛阳防守森严，难以攻克后，立刻北上涿郡，试图截断征讨高丽的隋军粮路。
　　在李密、李子雄的建议下，杨玄感绕过屈突通驻守的河阳渡口，沿着黄河往西行军，到达民乱最多的齐郡，招揽当地民贼共同抗击大隋。
　　齐郡郡守被民贼牵制，杨玄感顺利渡过黄河。
　　与此同时，杨广也仓皇下令从高丽退兵，命宇文述、来护儿由水陆两路迎击杨玄感。
　　杨玄感抵挡不住，眼见溃败在即，杨广突然下令宇文述和来护儿回援。
　　民贼不知道什么时候绕到了杨广后方，偷偷捡走了隋军丢弃的装备，竟把杨广所在的涿郡围了！
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 113: A Quiet Turn in History

Zhou Da and Luo Shixin finished clearing the battlefield with their soldiers, sorting through the severed ears to tally their merits later. 
Only Murong Xiaojun’s head remained intact; they would find salt and lime to pickle it once they reached his tribe, then send it to the Emperor upon his return to the Eastern Capital to claim their reward.
The troop set off again, heading directly toward the small Tuyuhun court and tribe established by Murong Xiaojun.
Tian Zhu Wang and his subordinates wore stiff expressions, their eyes masking a deep-seated dread they could no longer hide.
Tian Zhu Wang had brought five thousand men to Xihai Commandery this time. Two thousand were able-bodied cavalry, while the remaining three thousand consisted of subordinates, servants, and beautiful concubines, all responsible for logistics and attending to the nobility.
Though Murong Xiaojun’s force of over a thousand cavalry seemed smaller, he had brought only his elite, battle-hardened troops; in terms of pure combat strength, he was not far behind Tian Zhu Wang.
Li Shimin, however, had brought only five hundred elites. Relying on Sui Dynasty post stations and towns for supplies along the way, he had brought no logistical staff, personally overseeing the transport of his dry rations and gifts.
Once Li Shimin reached the Tian Zhu tribe, he lived off their supplies. Even his own provisions for this trip to Qinghai had been mixed in with Tian Zhu Wang’s.
Observing Li Shimin’s configuration, Tian Zhu Wang had been certain that Li Shimin had no intention of fighting, which was why he had felt safe bringing him along to intimidate Murong Xiaojun.
Although Li Shimin had told Tian Zhu Wang that he would eventually attack Murong Xiaojun, and that he supported Tian Zhu Wang’s independence in exchange for the Tian Zhu tribe’s intervention against Murong Xiaojun, Tian Zhu Wang had assumed Li Shimin would return later with a massive army. He had hoped the Sui forces and Murong Xiaojun would both suffer, allowing him to reap the rewards as the fisherman.
Who could have guessed that this young man, who usually appeared so lively and kind—even smiling when speaking to the lowliest herdsmen—would suddenly turn into a butcher without a word of warning?
*If you had this kind of ability, why talk to me about "joining forces" as brothers? You’re clearly killing the chicken to scare the monkey!*
Tian Zhu Wang’s scalp went numb.
He had spent years fighting on the battlefield and had seen countless bloody scenes. He was no saint himself and had even killed for amusement. Many of his subordinates were cruel and tyrannical, and more than a few had even tasted human flesh.
Yet, he still felt a lingering fear at Li Shimin’s sudden turn.
Everything they did usually followed logic and established personas. What was wrong with this "General Li"? One moment he was smiling and saying Murong Xiaojun would hunt with them, and the next, he was slaughtering everyone. Moreover, given Li Shimin’s intelligence, Tian Zhu Wang didn't believe he hadn't realized Murong Xiaojun had no intention of starting a war and was merely using a pretext to bargain.
The palms of Tian Zhu Wang’s hands, gripping the reins, were drenched in sweat.
Li Shimin noticed Tian Zhu Wang’s apprehension but smiled, choosing not to disturb him in his state of terror.
*What are you afraid of? I’m not going to turn around and slaughter you too.*
Li Shimin was certainly not moody, impulsive, or reckless.
Many of his seemingly brash actions were, in fact, "extraordinary"—seizing the right moment to win through surprise.
Xihai Commandery had to be occupied, and Murong Xiaojun had to die. First and foremost, Murong Xiaojun was on Li Shimin’s must-eliminate list.
