The scouts sent by Li Xuanba had investigated the state of the tribe led by Murong Xiaojun. Li Shimin knew that Murong Xiaojun could muster at most four thousand able-bodied soldiers, along with about a thousand old veterans from the remnants of Murong Fuyun’s forces.
Upon meeting Murong Xiaojun, Li Shimin had immediately observed the number and equipment of his troops.
It was exactly as Tian Zhu Wang had suspected: seeing the chaotic formations of those soldiers, Li Shimin knew Murong Xiaojun was merely bluffing and had no real intention of fighting.
But so what?
Whether to fight or not depended on whether one could win. If Li Shimin had no certainty of victory, or if there were no benefits to be gained, he naturally wouldn't act.
But what was the situation now?
Murong Xiaojun had provoked him first; he had a righteous cause.
The soldiers Murong Xiaojun brought hadn't expected a battle and their discipline was in shambles; he could win.
The only remaining question was: were there benefits to winning?
Of course! Immense ones!
Although the cavalry Murong Xiaojun brought weren't prepared for battle, one look at their physiques and expressions confirmed they were tribal elites.
If he wiped out these thousand-plus elites and killed Murong Xiaojun right here, the tribe would be caught off guard, losing their leader and over a fifth of their elite force—a fifth that likely included the old veterans of Khan Fuyun. The Tuyuhun people of Xihai Commandery would surely lose the will to resist.
If he went back now to prepare slowly for an assault on Xihai Commandery, Murong Xiaojun might retreat his elites into the semi-abandoned commandery city, using the time to reinforce it. Then, he would be facing a siege.
That would be far more difficult; he would have to slowly surround the city and cut off reinforcements, trapping Murong Xiaojun to death.
Li Xuanba and Li Shimin’s original plan had been exactly that: to lobby surrounding Tuyuhun tribes to isolate Murong Xiaojun, who wanted to "control the Khan to command the nobles," and then slowly wear him down.
But if he struck unexpectedly now, that long war of attrition could be avoided.
Was there danger?
Yes. The danger was whether Tian Zhu Wang would turn on him.
Li Shimin had seen that Tian Zhu Wang wanted Murong Xiaojun and the Sui to suffer mutually so he could reap the benefits. If he killed Murong Xiaojun, would Tian Zhu Wang kill him to steal the spoils?
After deep thought, Li Shimin concluded the possibility was low.
Tian Zhu Wang was based in Heyuan Commandery, far from Xihai. He couldn't abandon Heyuan, and his current strength and number of herdsmen wouldn't allow him to occupy two commanderies.
If he shared some easy spoils with him, he wouldn't risk a falling out with the Great Sui.
To increase the success rate of this "extraordinary strategy," Li Shimin immediately decided to implement a "encirclement and annihilation" tactic, wiping out the enemy's effective strength right in front of Tian Zhu Wang—killing the chicken to scare the monkey!
He ordered his cavalry to maneuver, driving the enemy toward Murong Xiaojun, then scattering them, only to circle the edges of the fleeing troops and herd them back together, "peeling" the enemy away layer by layer like a radish.
But Li Shimin knew he couldn't eat everyone.
Although the Tuyuhun were caught off guard, as they watched their companions being killed one by one, those who remained would eventually fight to the death.
Li Shimin had only brought five hundred men; each one was precious, and he couldn't afford to trade lives.
So, while "kneading the dough" and "peeling the radish," Li Shimin kept a close eye on the expressions of the remaining Tuyuhun.
When he saw they were about to enter a desperate, cornered-beast struggle, he ordered his cavalry to open a gap in the encirclement to let them escape, while he personally took Murong Xiaojun’s life.
He had left Murong Xiaojun for last so the enemy wouldn't scatter too early, which would have failed to intimidate Tian Zhu Wang; once Murong Xiaojun was dead, the cornered beasts would lose their fighting spirit.
These calculations were completed in a flash. By the time Li Shimin finished his mental brainstorming, Tian Zhu Wang and Murong Xiaojun were still posturing at each other.
His mastery of intelligence, prediction of the situation, and grasp of human nature had facilitated this "surprise attack."
The outcome was exactly as Li Shimin had anticipated.
He clapped his hands. Perfect!
It was a pity Ah Xuan wasn't here; he didn't know who to show off to.
Tian Zhu Wang was already terrified; he needed to give him time to "think deeply and feel fear," so it wasn't the right time to boast.
Showing off to his subordinates felt a bit beneath his dignity as a leader.
Li Shimin sighed.
Tian Zhu Wang shuddered. "General Li, why do you sigh?"
Li Shimin bluffed, "I brought too few men, and too many escaped. This hunt had minor flaws."
Tian Zhu Wang: "..." *You really think of this as a hunt?!*
Tian Zhu Wang said, "They will return to the tribe."
Li Shimin laughed. "Once they return to the tribe, they are no longer wild game to be hunted, but penned cattle and sheep—how can they be easily slaughtered? Please, Tian Zhu Wang, restrain your subordinates. Do not harass their herdsmen, lest it cause chaotic conflict and lead to our men getting hurt for nothing. The wealth already in our hands is our own property; we must cherish it."
Tian Zhu Wang nodded. "I understand."
He turned and gave orders for his men to restrain themselves, forbidding looting, promising he would distribute the spoils himself.
Especially the wealth! That belonged to General Li! Anyone who dared to steal would have their hands chopped off!
Even the biggest troublemakers Tian Zhu Wang had brought nodded repeatedly, promising to be well-behaved.
Li Shimin said, "Then I am relieved. Giddyap! Tian Zhu Wang, let’s pick up the pace, don't let them get away!"
Tian Zhu Wang hurriedly whipped his horse to keep up.
Luo Shixin followed behind Li Shimin’s horse, looking dissatisfied, his resentful gaze poking at the back of the Second Young Master’s head.
Zhou Da slowed his horse to ride alongside Luo Shixin and whispered, "What’s wrong? You look miserable despite the victory."
Luo Shixin muttered, "What kind of general steals his subordinates' kills? The Second Young Master killed everyone; what use am I? I’ve never seen a general like him who charges into the fray himself!"
Zhou Da suppressed a laugh. "Well, you’ve seen one now. There’s no helping it, that’s just how the Second Young Master is."
Luo Shixin sighed deeply and laughed bitterly. "I must work harder! Next time, I will definitely beat the Second Young Master!"
Zhou Da sighed with a smile. *So young and full of vigor. Luo Shixin is like that, and so is the Second Young Master.*
*Such young people shouldn't be on the battlefield.*
Zhou Da recalled the times of peace, and the joy of the recent victory faded significantly.
...
When Tian Zhu Wang and Li Shimin arrived at Xihai Commandery, Murong Xiaojun’s tribe indeed had not yet received news that their King of Xihai had been killed.
Those who had fled were likely too panicked and had lost their way, and since Tian Zhu Wang and Li Shimin were on horseback, they arrived a step ahead.
The final step of Li Shimin’s "extraordinary strategy"—borrowing the tiger’s prestige—was achieved.
With only five hundred cavalry, even if he could win, the enemy would see his small numbers and harbor the delusional hope of "giving it a try."
Moreover, he was, after all, a Sui man. The remaining Tuyuhun nobles might not be willing to follow him.
So, Li Shimin handed everyone over to Tian Zhu Wang, turning it into an internal annexation of the Tuyuhun tribes, with himself acting merely as "foreign aid."
Coupled with the fact that Tian Zhu Wang had brought five thousand men, creating a massive momentum, the remaining Tuyuhun nobles naturally lost the heart to resist.
After all, they would remain nobles under Tian Zhu Wang; it was just a change of tribal leader.
As for the feelings of the little Tuyuhun Khan, no one cared.
Li Shimin retreated to the position of "foreign aid," leisurely counting the spoils.
He tied the wealth to the captured cattle, sheep, and horses; whatever couldn't be carried was gifted to Tian Zhu Wang.
Tian Zhu Wang didn't dare accept it. He said he would record these items and exchange them for fine horses to give to Li Shimin, treating it as a business deal.
Li Shimin mused that Tian Zhu Wang was actually a decent fellow. If he didn't have great ambitions in the future, he would appoint him the "Great Pillar King."
*How can a barbarian call himself 'Heaven'? I hope Tian Zhu Wang learns to be sensible in the future.*
When Li Xuanba added another layer of clothing and lit the stove in the room, he finally received news that his Second Brother was returning.
"Killed Murong Xiaojun, wiped out the Xihai Commandery tribe, captured a mountain of livestock and wealth, and wants me to hurry and provide support?" Li Xuanba repeated the message he had retrieved from the feet of the eagle, Wudi.
He looked up, his eyes bright as he stared at Wudi. "My Second Brother is taking risks again?"
Wudi tilted its head. *I’m just a little golden eagle, Mom, I don't know how to answer that.*
"Sigh." Li Xuanba patted Wudi’s head. "You’ve worked hard. Go eat something good first. I’ll have to trouble you to work a little longer and take me to pick them up."
Wudi hopped. "Chirp, chirp!"
Li Xuanba looked at Wudi’s bulging belly and didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "It seems you really did capture a lot of livestock; look at how round your belly is..."
He rubbed Wudi’s stomach, and the eagle lay on the table, belly up, letting him rub it.
Han Gou, who was napping on the bookshelf, opened its eyes, then closed them in disdain.
Li Xuanba gathered his men and set off quickly to support Li Shimin.
Half a day later, he saw his Second Brother, who was in a state of utter chaos trying to herd sheep.
"Ah Xuan, help! These sheep are so hard to herd!" Li Shimin shouted.
Li Xuanba looked at the massive, sprawling sea of livestock and was dumbfounded. "How much did you capture?"
Li Shimin said, "About fifty thousand, I think."
Li Xuanba shouted, "How many?"
Li Shimin said with a bitter face, "Actually, it was sixty thousand originally. But on the way, I couldn't herd them all, so we ate some, sold some, and... *cough*, some got lost. I tried my best!"
Li Xuanba took a deep breath. "You brought five hundred men to herd fifty thousand head of livestock back? This isn't 'trying your best,' Second Brother, you are a genius of animal husbandry!"
Li Shimin’s bitter face turned into a grin. "Really? Well, I think so too. Oh, I’m exhausted. Herding so many animals, I didn't even dare to sleep on the way."
Li Xuanba said, "Hurry back and sleep. As for what comes next..."
He looked at the dense mass of livestock, and his head began to ache.
"Second Brother, why didn't you write how much livestock there was in your letter? I would have brought more men." Li Xuanba complained.
Li Shimin laughed. "I only had five hundred men and managed to herd them back; you can just bring a few people, Ah Xuan."
Li Xuanba’s mouth twitched. "You just wanted to give me a little shock and make a fool of me, right?"
Li Shimin coughed dryly. "The thought crossed my mind."
Li Xuanba sighed deeply and sent men back to call for reinforcements.
The brothers herded sheep together for an hour before the Governor of Zhangye arrived on a fast horse.
"My heavens! It really is tens of thousands of livestock!" The Governor rubbed his eyes. "General Li, did you really take Xihai Commandery?"
Li Shimin said, "If Tian Zhu Wang leaves as agreed, then Xihai Commandery is already empty. We need to send troops immediately."
The Governor said, "Leave it to me! I will scrape together men for you right away!"
*I must have a taste of this merit!*
Li Shimin and Li Xuanba did not refuse the Governor his share of the soup.
Not only the officials of Zhangye, but officials from nearby commanderies would also get a taste. Only when their interests were tied together could they act more unscrupulously.
After returning home, Li Shimin slept for three full days before crawling out to shout that he was hungry.
Seeing that Li Shimin hadn't eaten for three days, Li Xuanba first served him meat porridge.
Li Shimin gulped down a pot of porridge and then ate a small lamb.
Li Xuanba looked at his Second Brother’s stomach in disbelief. He wondered if the volume of food his brother had consumed was already larger than his own stomach?
*This is unscientific!*
After Li Shimin was full and well-rested, he began to boast incessantly to his two younger brothers about his achievements.
He detailed his considerations and told Li Zhiyun to listen and learn well, so he could strive to lead an army independently as soon as possible.
"I’m really exhausted," Li Shimin said, burping. "War is so tiring. Just thinking about how vast the world is and how many more battles I might have to fight, I’m too tired to move."
Li Xuanba retorted, "You say that now, but when there’s a battle, aren't you always the one charging the fastest? And I don't think fighting is what tired you out; it was the sheep herding."
Li Zhiyun was already stunned. "So amazing, I never knew Second Brother was so capable, too amazing!"
Li Shimin tapped Li Zhiyun’s head. "What do you mean 'never knew,' I’ve always been this capable."
Li Zhiyun said, "But before, Second Brother never used five hundred men to herd fifty thousand sheep!"
Li Shimin’s smile faded. "My glorious record doesn't need this detail."
Li Xuanba and Li Zhiyun both laughed.
Li Shimin pretended to be annoyed and embarrassed, but seeing his brothers laughing uncontrollably, he couldn't help but join in.
"I really should keep you by my side, Ah Xuan. There’s no reason for me to handle both the fighting and the logistics alone," Li Shimin said. "I need someone to help me oversee the grain transport and count the spoils."
Li Xuanba said, "You can't blame me for that; you were just too sudden."
Li Shimin said proudly, "Can't help it, opportunities for battle are rare, time waits for no one, I had to strike quickly."
Li Xuanba sighed. "That’s your personality. However, Shixin complained to me that you always charge at the very front. Striking quickly after finding an opening is correct, but a commander always charging at the front, you..."
Li Shimin covered his ears. *Not listening, not listening, Ah Xuan is chanting scriptures.*
Li Zhiyun laughed so hard he rolled onto his Third Brother’s lap.
Li Xuanba switched to telepathy to continue "chanting."
*Charging into battle personally is indeed cool, but the injuries you sustain now are the pain you’ll suffer when you’re old. Other people’s admiration isn't worth as much as your own body. Think about how worried Mother and Sister-in-law would be if they knew you were taking such risks. Every wound on your body is a cut on their hearts, blah, blah, blah.*
Li Shimin covered his ears, his eyes glazed over, and decided to drag Luo Shixin to the training ground tomorrow to beat him up.
*A mere minor general, daring to report me to my brother, your courage has grown, hasn't it!*
Li Zhiyun whispered in Li Xuanba’s ear, "Will Shixin be beaten by the annoyed Second Brother?"
Li Xuanba corrected him, "It’s a sparring match."
Li Zhiyun covered his mouth and laughed. "I want to watch."
Li Xuanba smiled. "Good. Maybe Second Brother will even lose."
Li Shimin turned into a screaming bird. "Absolutely impossible!"
Knowing that he had complained, Luo Shixin knew the Second Young Master would come looking for trouble, so he moved into the military camp early.
When he heard the Second Young Master had arrived, he wore an expression of "As expected, the Young Master is petty."
Li Shimin laughed in anger.
The two of them began clashing with wooden staves, while Li Zhiyun sat to the side eating beef jerky.
*One for me, one for Wudi, one for Han Gou, one for me...*
As for Li Xuanba, he was naturally working overtime, miserable.
After his Second Brother finished being tired, it was his turn to be exhausted.
The brothers worked together; there was always someone who could get some rest.
...
When news of Li Shimin pacifying Xihai Commandery with five hundred men reached Luoyang, Li Yuan and Yang Jian had just won a battle.
Yang Jian had personally gone to the battlefield and hadn't yet taken off his armor.
He wiped the blood from his face, glanced at the head in the wooden box, and laughed. "Truly good news. I didn't expect that sending Daxiong to guard Zhangye would accidentally lead to such a success."
Li Yuan sighed. "I didn't expect the Tuyuhun to be so well-informed. As soon as the Central Plains fell into chaos, they rebelled again. Sigh, taking five hundred men to attack a city, Daxiong’s courage... sigh, why didn't Dade advise him against it... sigh..."
The battle report submitted by Li Xuanba and the Governor of Zhangye naturally claimed that the Tuyuhun were restless, and that Murong Xiaojun, a loyalist of Khan Fuyun, had been betrayed by Tian Zhu Wang while the Sui Emperor was busy with his campaign against Goguryeo. Tiger-Brave General Li Shimin had led five hundred elites on a night raid, achieving a successful decapitation strike.
The Great Sui was in turmoil, the barbarians were stirring, but fortunately, a young Tiger-Brave General of the Sui had settled the situation in one battle, shaking the Western Regions!
Li Yuan was both proud and worried. *Why only five hundred men? Bring more men! Merit is good, but your own safety is most important!*
The old father’s heart was filled with worry; he didn't even dare tell his wife about this.
Yang Jian said, "Yang Xuangan intends to retreat. Let’s report this good news to the Emperor together."
He took a deep breath and let out a long sigh. "Father, it is time to give up the campaign against Goguryeo."
Li Yuan said, "Once the Emperor hears of Yang Xuangan’s rebellion, he will surely retreat immediately. I only worry that the Emperor will retreat too hastily, letting the Goguryeo people take advantage."
Yang Jian hesitated. "It shouldn't happen. The Emperor has been leading campaigns personally since he was a prince, and he is an old veteran; the army’s advance and retreat will surely be steady."
Li Yuan thought to himself, *That’s not necessarily true.*
Yang Jian hesitated for a while longer and said, "Should we send troops to pursue Yang Xuangan, to prevent him from heading north to Zhuojun and disturbing the Emperor?"
Li Yuan said, "The garrison in Luoyang is small, and when Yang Xuangan rebelled, many commoners joined him. If Luoyang’s defenses are empty, it might attract other bandits. The Emperor has a million-strong army, and Yang Xuangan’s forces are just a rabble, easily defeated. We only need to guard Luoyang."
Yang Jian said, "That’s true. Holding Luoyang is most important. Sigh, I really hope his next stop is Daxing."
Li Yuan said, "He wouldn't dare. Duke Gao is in Daxing."
Yang Jian sighed with a smile. "Indeed, Duke Gao is there."
In Daxing, Gao Jiong and the Daxing garrison commander, Wei Xuan, were playing chess.
Wei Xuan smiled. "Congratulations, Duke Gao. Li Second Young Master breaking Xihai Commandery with five hundred cavalry—a great teacher produces a great student."
Gao Jiong shook his head. "How could five hundred cavalry break a city? The Second Young Master likely lured the enemy out of the city, cut off Murong Xiaojun’s head, and let the enemy army collapse on its own."
Wei Xuan said, "Whatever strategy was used, the fact remains that Li Second Young Master wiped out the remnants of Khan Fuyun’s forces with only five hundred men and reclaimed Xihai Commandery for the Sui. Duke Gao, don't be modest."
Gao Jiong laughed. "True, such a great merit should not be met with modesty."
Wei Xuan sighed with emotion. "The Duke of Tang defeated Yang Xuangan in Luoyang, and Li Second Young Master guards the border for the Sui. Father and son together, they can be called the restorers of the Sui; they are truly the pillars of the nation."
Gao Jiong’s hand, holding a chess piece, trembled slightly.
He said sternly, "Minister Wei, such words must not be spoken lightly. The Sui only has a minor rebellion; it remains prosperous and stable. How can you speak of 'restoration' or 'pillars of the nation'? If your words reach the Emperor’s ears, both you and the Duke of Tang’s family might be blamed."
Wei Xuan sighed. "It was my slip of the tongue, Duke Gao." *Has even the most upright Duke Gao been forced to this point by the Emperor? Is there anyone left in this world who dares to speak the truth to him?*
Wei Xuan changed the subject. "Will Yang Xuangan attack Guanzhong?"
Gao Jiong said calmly, "He wouldn't dare."
In the seventh month of the ninth year of Daye, Yang Xuangan probed Luoyang several times. Seeing that the defenses were tight and difficult to overcome, he immediately headed north to Zhuojun, attempting to cut off the grain supply of the Sui army campaigning against Goguryeo.
On the advice of Li Mi and Li Zixiong, Yang Xuangan bypassed the Hekou ferry guarded by Qutu Tong and marched west along the Yellow River, reaching Qi Commandery, where civil unrest was most rampant, recruiting local rebels to resist the Sui together.
The Governor of Qi Commandery was tied down by the rebels, and Yang Xuangan successfully crossed the Yellow River.
At the same time, Yang Guang also hurriedly ordered a retreat from Goguryeo, ordering Yuwen Shu and Lai Hu'er to intercept Yang Xuangan by land and water.
Yang Xuangan could not hold them off, and just as his defeat seemed imminent, Yang Guang suddenly ordered Yuwen Shu and Lai Hu'er to return to support him.
The rebels had somehow circled to Yang Guang’s rear, secretly picking up the equipment discarded by the Sui army, and had actually surrounded Zhuojun, where Yang Guang was located!

chunks.chapterTitle: 第114章 友人齐聚张掖郡 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第114章 友人齐聚张掖郡

涿郡城外， 王薄、翟让、高士达三人坐在帐中首位，但帐中将领却都看着另外三人，隐隐以那三人为主心骨。

这三人便是王薄的谋主魏徵， 翟让的谋主徐世勣， 高士达的谋主窦建德。

十九岁的徐世勣年轻气盛， 十分直爽地问道：“魏公，我们可有胜算？”

魏徵摇了摇羽毛扇，回答得也很干净利落：“没有。”

三人中年纪最大、最老成持重的窦建德叹气。

魏徵放下羽毛扇：“当时我邀诸位前来本就只是为了抢夺隋军物资， 顺带吓唬狗皇帝，让他知道百姓被他压榨到何种程度。诸位怎么想着获胜了？”

王薄已经熟悉魏徵这张嘴，嘴角微微上翘， 强忍着没有笑出来。

高士达对王薄道：“虽然魏公深谋远虑，才高八斗， 但只有知世郎有福消受。”

翟让笑道：“我觉得我也可以， 知世郎可否割爱？”

王薄摆摆手：“魏公想去哪就去哪，岂是我能决定的？”

高士达和翟让眼中闪过对王薄的敬佩。魏徵是王薄心腹谋士，王薄却不约束魏徵的自由。哪怕王薄现在只是客气的话，也可见王薄心胸了。

徐世勣虽有勇有谋，毕竟年少， 心情比较容易外露。

他叹了口气，道：“我们不仅围了涿郡， 还连胜城中守兵，我真以为能一劳永逸。”

魏徵瞥了徐世勣一眼：“以懋功才略，真的以为能一劳永逸？”

徐世勣失笑：“我开玩笑。唉， 只是想多吓唬皇帝一阵子， 若是能把他吓死就好了。”

窦建德也赞同：“要能再多吓唬他几日就好了。”

帐中众将领皆失笑。

王薄笑道：“好了， 吓唬了他几日， 又截了隋军许多粮草辎重，已经够本了。我们赶紧按照既定的计划逃走。再不逃，就要被宇文述和来护儿两个老贼堵住了。”

翟让笑着拱手：“此次一别，不知何时还能再见。诸位保重。”

高士达也拱手：“我们都努力些，争取活到下次见面。”

王薄拱手作揖：“祝愿诸君运势昌盛。”

帐中诸位将领有的抱拳，有的作揖，有的勾肩搭背。

“别死啊小子。”

“不知道还有没有并肩作战的机会。”

“说不定下次见面，我们会为了争地盘兵戎相见呢？”

“哈哈哈哈，有可能。”

“若我们兵戎相见，就说明狗皇帝已经死了吧？”

“这么说，还蛮期待的。我肯定能取你项上人头，嘎达！”

“我现在就砍了你的脑袋。”

“哈哈哈哈哈。”……

围城即将失败，众人即将逃亡，他们脸上却没有丝毫阴霾。

最后一次作战会议结束，王薄借道高丽，翟让借道东突厥，高士达则化整为零回到中原。他们各自的谋主都给他们找好了退路。

辛苦是辛苦，危险也危险，但一想到手中的木棒换成了铁刀，麻衣变成了盔甲，还得到了一大批粮草马匹，最重要的是，他们终于把狗皇帝吓到了，让狗皇帝那眼高于顶的狗眼睛，能够看到他们这群活不下去揭竿而起的平民百姓。

值了！

离开之前，三人杀了带不走的牲畜，在城外狂欢宴饮到半夜。

徐世勣和窦建德向魏徵敬酒：“虽然不能喝醉，但薄酒一杯，请魏公赏赏脸？”

魏徵笑着喝酒：“客气了。”

窦建德看着魏徵的眼神十分炙热：“此次作战成功全倚仗魏公计谋。魏公现在肯定名扬天下了。”

魏徵抹了抹胡子上的酒水，道：“我这点小伎俩离名扬天下还早。三位主公倒是能名扬天下。”

徐世勣道：“等我们的主公逐鹿中原时，我们三人都能名扬天下。”

窦建德心中不知为何有些惆怅，但他还是笑着赞同道：“一定会。到时我们就是对手了。”

魏徵笑而不语。

徐世勣觉得魏徵的笑容有些奇怪：“魏公难道不认为吗？”

魏徵笑着叹气道：“你们认为如果大隋灭亡，我们各自的主公就能逐鹿中原吗？”

徐世勣疑惑道：“为何不能？”

魏徵收起笑容，叹气道：“你看看主公麾下的谋士，可有一位士族跟随？不说高门世家，就是普通官宦子弟，可有吗？这义军中，出身最好的居然是我与懋功你。”

徐世勣虽出身高平北祖上房徐氏，但这个“小世家”小得和寒门无异，家中也无人做官。

徐世勣和窦建德同时皱眉。

窦建德道：“那是我们还不够强大。等我们强大，他们一定会来投靠我们。”

魏徵道：“希望如此吧。”

徐世勣笑道：“现在想这些还早。我们先避过这一劫再说。”

窦建德点头：“也是。”

徐世勣道：“说起士族子弟，你们可听闻唐国公府的李二郎君？”

窦建德叹气：“‘战无不胜’李二郎，谁没听过？”

魏徵的手指头敲了敲酒杯：“不是‘义薄云天’李二郎吗？”

徐世勣道：“那是多久之前的称号了？现在是‘战无不胜’！”

魏徵道：“哦？李二郎又做什么？他不是驻守张掖吗？离我们这挺远的，你们还能得到他的消息？”

窦建德道：“报喜的人到了洛阳，我们在洛阳附近安插了人手，自然都知道了。隋太子也在到处宣扬李二郎的战功，以安抚被楚国公杨玄感挑起不安的官吏。”

徐世勣道：“李二郎只率领八百人就把西海郡给夺了！杀了几万人，捕获了十几万牲畜，啧啧，有点夸张，不知道是不是真的。”

魏徵淡淡道：“肯定是假的。就是几万头羊，八百人也难以抓获，何况几万人。大概是大隋为了安稳人心，故意夸大了李二郎的功绩。”

徐世勣道：“夺回西海郡肯定是真的。虽然我厌恶大隋，但大隋再怎么乱也是我们中原人自己的事，吐谷浑人想趁机来抢劫，活该被李二郎杀了。”

窦建德十分赞同：“无论是突厥、吐谷浑还是高丽，希望他们老实些。”

这次抢辎重的时候他们就和高丽人交了手。高丽人据城而战很厉害，出了城抢东西可不是他们的对手。

虽然高丽打不过他们，也和高丽人与大隋鏖战多日，已经十分疲惫有关系，但中原人一向看不起蛮夷，何况徐世勣和窦建德都自恃才高，寻常人都难以入他们的眼，更不说高丽蛮夷了。

窦建德叹息：“虽然大隋有个狗皇帝，但有许多大臣和将领还是一心为国。中原混乱，李二郎孤军奋战誓死戍边，振我华夏雄威，真是令人佩服。”

徐世勣道：“虽然他很厉害，但若他不是唐国公之子，哪有机会去戍边？若我有这等机遇，我不会比他差，哼！”

窦建德笑道：“懋功也是少年英才，一定比他强。”

魏徵慢悠悠道：“李二郎现在才十四岁。”

徐世勣道：“我十四岁也能！”

魏徵道：“李二郎首战擒获吐谷浑可汗时，才十一岁。那时他还不是将领，只带着自己的家丁。”

徐世勣道：“我也能！而且他不是还说动和回纥帮忙？”

窦建德笑得直不起腰：“我信，我信，你一定能。”

徐世勣讪讪道：“好吧，我不能。才十一岁，他吃什么长大？这他娘的太离谱了！”

魏徵道：“是离谱。”

窦建德擦了擦笑出的眼泪：“近些年李二郎的名声越来越响亮，我倒是注意到隐藏在身后的另一人。”

徐世勣道：“李三郎？李三郎是个好人，救助了许多百姓。”

窦建德摇摇头：“八岁秀才李玄霸，怎么可能只是个好人。”

魏徵道：“听闻李三郎先天体弱，可能这些年的时间都用来养病了，所以名声不显。”

窦建德再次摇头：“如果他的时间都用来养病，为何能得到虎牙狼将的官职？一介病弱书生，却能当上郎将……”

徐世勣捏了捏下巴：“李三郎……他莫不是李二郎谋主？”

魏徵在心中微微叹气，并对面前两位暂时同僚高看一眼，将二人名字记下。

“是又如何，不过仍旧是为狗皇帝效力。”魏徵淡淡道，“无论李二郎还是李三郎，他们空有才华，却助纣为虐，当不得人杰！”

窦建德道：“话不能这么说……唉，各自立场不同吧。不过唐国公这对麒麟子真是厉害，‘战无不胜’和‘算无遗策’，真不愧是双生子。”

徐世勣道：“对哦，他们还是双生子。这也太相辅相成了吧？李二郎出生时自带谋主？这什么天之骄子啊？！”

魏徵道：“不过如此。”

窦建德苦笑：“魏公你……唉，你对勋贵子弟的偏见真大。刚刚你还夸他们呢。”

魏徵冷哼：“不必再提扫兴的人，喝酒！”

徐世勣和窦建德：“是是是。”

魏徵斟满酒，心里嘀咕，郎君太过有本事，自己压力真大啊。

他此次计谋成功，本有些得意。听到主公“八百骑破西海郡”的壮举，他便对现在获得的成就意兴阑珊了。

魏徵把酒一饮而尽。还得继续努力！

……

宇文述和来护儿匆匆护驾到来时，围城义军已经退得干干净净。

义军不仅把周围物资搜刮得干干净净，连城外百姓都跟着义军跑了。涿郡周围杳无人烟。

杨广派出宇文述和来护儿之后，还留了加上民夫在内约二十万人保护自己。

这些人都被困在了涿郡中，又有义军趁着撤退混乱偷偷潜伏进军营和城里放火。现在城中早已经断粮。

隋军挨家挨户搜刮粮食，引起城中民乱大火，引发不小骚乱。

更可怕的是，大火烧到了临朔宫。

杨广灰头土脸逃了出来，虽然一点都不危险，但他从小到大哪吃过这样的苦？就是穿越大斗拔谷冻死十分之一的大隋将士，也和穿着厚厚皮毛大氅烤着小火炉的他毫无关系。

杨广又饿又惧，吓得抱着小儿子杨杲和大孙子杨倓嗷嗷直哭，又吸进了灰尘，大病一场。

等宇文述和来护儿到达涿郡时，杨广仍旧病得起不了身。

苏威等重臣希望杨广把太子杨暕召来涿郡。

杨广在病榻上大骂：“朕还未死！尔等就要弃朕投向太子？！”

朝中重臣被杨广骂得满头雾水。

苏威劝说道：“陛下生病，太子本应侍疾。且大军尚在涿郡，叛贼杨玄感还未擒拿，朝中需要有人主事。我等只是陛下臣子，不应僭越，只有太子能在陛下生病时监国啊。”

苏威在心里道，何况你重病时太子不在身边，不能及时继位，你就不怕将来江山有变吗？

但他不敢说。

他发现皇帝非常恐惧死亡，只能以太子理应侍疾监国为借口。

可就是这样合适又温婉的借口，杨广也难以接受。

杨广砸了手边所有能砸的东西。这时他身边的重臣却不愿意再像以前那样顺着他的意，就是虞世基等人不提太子的事，也没有与群臣辩驳。

第一，杨广重病，不知道能不能熬过去。若太子登基，现在谁反对太子来涿郡，肯定会被清算。

第二，现在急需有人监国。这种事谁沾谁死，除了太子。

所以他们都希望太子赶紧来。

虞世基等人也在私下偷偷抱怨。

皇帝病倒，就该太子监国。寻常皇帝重病时恨不得太子连夜飞过来，生怕有权臣借此生事。自家皇帝难道是病糊涂了？

可无论群臣再怎么劝谏，杨广也不肯下旨。

于是朝中事务瘫痪，没人去追逃跑的义军，也没人继续围剿杨玄感。

杨玄感喘了口气后，攻下了渤海郡，在渤海郡站稳了脚跟。

附近零散义军纷纷投入杨玄感麾下，杨玄感的军队瞬间扩充到十万。

他刚缓过气，就带人攻打附近郡县，掠夺物资。

知道不能一战定乾坤后，杨玄感就改变战略，徐徐图之。

屡次战败锉掉了杨玄感的傲气，让杨玄感对李密和李子雄更加信任。

在李密和李子雄的辅佐下，大隋朝廷又迟迟没有反应，杨玄感的势力再次壮大。

杨玄感乃楚国公，大隋顶尖的勋贵。他麾下自然有善谋略、善治理的士人跟随。

当他站稳脚跟，有了据点之后，这些士人立刻发挥出力量。他们整合附近义军，重定法令，打出“轻徭薄赋”的招牌，吸引百姓来投。

杨玄感还宣布将杨广更改的所有规章制度都废除，所有朝廷制度退回到隋文帝时期，以诱惑勋贵世家投靠他。

一些在隋文帝和杨广两朝被打压的士人被诱惑成功，如被杨广冤杀的史万岁兄弟史万宝、史万寿兄弟二人就前来投靠。

其实史万岁是被杨玄感之父杨素陷害。但为了自己的荣华富贵，史万宝和史万寿把史万岁的死都扣在了隋文帝杨坚头上，选择性无视了杨素干的事。

洛阳城中。

杨暕得到父皇病重的消息之后，就想立刻赶往涿郡，被李渊劝阻。

李渊道：“陛下若想让你去涿郡，自然会给你下令。陛下没下令，你就是无诏离开洛阳。太子殿下，你应该派人去涿郡询问陛下旨意，然后按照陛下旨意行事。”

杨暕忙派人去涿郡请求父皇下旨。无论是去涿郡侍疾，还是继续留守洛阳，希望父皇给一道明确的旨意。

杨广看到杨暕的信后，愤怒道：“他这是在打探朕的死活，想登基了呢！”

或许是愤怒给了杨广力量，杨广恢复了一点精神，下旨封幼子杨杲为赵王，长孙杨倓为燕王，并斥责太子杨暕没有守好洛阳，居然让杨玄感逃走。

群臣皆震惊疑惑不解。

最了解杨广的宇文述、虞世基等人叹了口气，知道自己该站在太子的对立面了。

不是太子不好，也不是太子太好，只是陛下病重时对健壮的太子生出了忌惮厌恶而已。

身在洛阳的太子杨暕得到了杨广的旨意，茫然失措。

他心里回想起李玄霸曾对他说过的话，身上生出冷意。

父皇这是……忌惮我了吗？

只是因为他生了一场重病，就忌惮我了？

杨暕有点悲哀，但又很想笑。

他突然生出了去拜访兄长的念头。

兄长啊兄长，你在去世前故意惹父皇恼怒，好让你的孩子脱离皇位争夺的漩涡，但你还是失策了。

杨倓被封为燕王，他要被迫和叔叔们争夺皇位；你其他儿子，包括嫡长子杨侑居然都没晋封，他们一定很不满。

父皇要亲自打造大隋皇位争夺的乱象，是嫌弃这天下还不够乱吗？

李渊得知此事后，对窦夫人感慨：“我还未见有病重皇帝忌惮太子者。太子本就是储君，皇帝病重，应该做好让太子继位的准备啊。”

窦夫人平静道：“当初隋文帝病重时，不也突然忌惮如今陛下？”

李渊叹气：“这……唉。夫人，我看我们在洛阳待不下去了。我看陛下不愿意把守住洛阳的功劳给太子，估计会全推我头上，到时我就贿赂朝臣寻求外放。还是二郎三郎好啊，在边疆真自由。”

窦夫人道：“郎君想做什么就放心去做，我支持你。”

李渊笑道：“我知道。这次守城辛苦夫人了。”

李渊守城的时候，窦夫人换上荆钗布裙，带领城中妇人为将士做饭缝衣，极大地提升了城中士气。

太子杨暕多次向窦夫人道谢，号召城中其他勋贵女眷向窦夫人学习。

李渊也对窦夫人刮目相看。原来自己夫人还有这等本事，并不是只会后院之事，所以愿意和窦夫人说一点前朝之事了。

中原形势大变时，李世民和李玄霸迎到了房乔和杜如晦。

“玄龄！克明！”李世民一见两人，不顾两人身上风尘，手臂一张，把两人都抱进了怀里。

房乔：“？”

杜如晦：“哈哈哈，李二你放手。”

李玄霸像只乌龟一样，一边打哈欠一边慢吞吞挪动过来。

李玄霸：【二哥，你现在的动作让我想起了后世一句台词，“你们都是我的翅膀”。】

李世民大笑着松开怀抱，转头对弟弟道：“他们确实都是我的翅膀，你也是。”

李玄霸作干呕状。

杜如晦笑着抱怨：“你们又仗着双生子的心灵感应私下嘀嘀咕咕了。”

李世民叉腰：“没办法，双生子就是这样。”

杜如晦拱手：“行行行，你说得对。”

房乔叹气：“离别几年，你二人都创下莫大名声了，怎么一点都没变？”

李世民好奇道：“创下什么名声？还是什么‘义薄云天’‘德重恩弘’吗？”

房乔摇头，道：“是‘战无不胜’和‘算无遗策’。”

杜如晦叹气：“我也听闻了，据说是从义军那里传出来的，他们对你们可推崇了。”

义军？李世民和李玄霸对视一眼。难道是魏徵在为他们扬名？

李玄霸道：“是说的攻克西海郡之事吗？和我没关系，算无遗策的是二哥。我都被吓了一跳。”

杜如晦道：“不急，慢慢说，先让我洗澡换身衣服休息一日。哎呀，累坏我了。”

房乔点头：“大德，先把我带来的书册整理了。”

杜如晦道：“我就带了一点田亩资料。我也想带啊，但陛下就在涿郡，我不敢有太大动作。”

李世民道：“你人平安来了就行，还带什么礼物？当然，带了礼物更好，哈哈哈哈。克明，你这次输给玄龄了。”

杜如晦翻白眼：“是是是，你说得对。”

李玄霸道：“什么叫我先整理了？当然是放着一起整理。你们二人来了，别想再让我一人干活。”

四人虽分别了几年，仍旧如当初一样相处融洽。

房乔和杜如晦洗去风尘后，就住进了李世民和李玄霸家中，顺带认识了罗士信。

听闻罗士信的武力值能与李世民媲美时，两人都啧啧称奇。

杜如晦好奇心很强，私下悄悄问李玄霸道：“这也是你提前为李二寻来的？”

李玄霸摇头：“是他听了二哥的名声，自己跨越万里来投。”

杜如晦感慨道：“李二现在就已经露出明主之相了。”

李玄霸道：“再说了，我以前也没有提前为二哥提前寻找人才。你们不都是自己撞上来要与我和二哥交朋友吗？我可没有主动寻过你们。”

杜如晦道：“也是。唉，你就不能说你是主动寻我们吗？这样我和房玄龄才更有脸面。”

李玄霸摊手：“但你们就是自己贴上来的。”

杜如晦气笑了：“还自己贴上来？你说话越来越过分了。”

李世民赶紧伸手勾住嘴欠的弟弟的脖子，把弟弟勾离已经开始挽袖子的杜如晦身边：“好了好了，克明，阿玄是个什么德性你不是不知道，他就是嘴欠，别在意。”

杜如晦笑骂道：“知道他嘴欠，你就让他改！你就不怕他挨打？”

李世民挑眉：“有我在，谁敢！”

房乔慢悠悠道：“你父母？”

李世民：“……”

他讪讪道：“那我就只能和阿玄一起挨揍了。”

房乔和杜如晦忍俊不禁。

李玄霸翻白眼。他才不会对父母嘴欠。

几人围着篝火，说起了各自经历的事。

李智云和罗士信也乖乖坐在一旁听故事。

最先发言的自然是李世民。

李世民终于有机会吹嘘自己了，那叫一个滔滔不绝文采斐然，简直可以给自己写一篇歌颂的赋。

李玄霸听得直打哈欠。

李智云和罗士信虽然已经听李世民说了很多次，仍旧一副敬仰的表情。

房乔和杜如晦眼中异彩连连。

虽然刚才已经粗略听了李世民攻克西海郡之事，但当李世民将自己在电光石火间的谋划详细说出时，他们才深刻地体会到了李世民的厉害。

不过也并非李玄霸所言，李玄霸什么都没做。前期的情报收集和向两个部族派奸细，都是李玄霸的工作。
chunks.englishText:
### Chapter 114: Friends Gather in Zhangye Commandery

Outside the walls of Zhuojun, Wang Bo, Zhai Rang, and Gao Shida sat at the head of the tent. However, the generals present were all looking toward three other men, implicitly treating them as the true backbone of the group.

These three were Wang Bo’s strategist, Wei Zheng; Zhai Rang’s strategist, Xu Shiji; and Gao Shida’s strategist, Dou Jiande.

Nineteen-year-old Xu Shiji, young and spirited, asked quite bluntly, "Master Wei, do we have any chance of victory?"

Wei Zheng shook his feather fan and answered with crisp finality: "None."

Dou Jiande, the oldest and most composed of the three, sighed.

Wei Zheng lowered his fan. "When I invited you all here, it was merely to seize the Sui army’s supplies and, incidentally, to frighten the dog emperor, letting him see just how far he has pushed the common people. Why are you all thinking about winning?"

Wang Bo, already accustomed to Wei Zheng’s sharp tongue, felt the corners of his mouth twitch as he suppressed a laugh.

Gao Shida said to Wang Bo, "Although Master Wei is a man of deep foresight and immense talent, only the 'Wise One' (Zhishilang) has the fortune to enjoy his service."

Zhai Rang laughed. "I think I could handle it too. Could the Wise One spare him?"

Wang Bo waved his hand. "Master Wei goes where he pleases. How could it be up to me to decide?"

A flicker of admiration for Wang Bo crossed the eyes of Gao Shida and Zhai Rang. Wei Zheng was Wang Bo’s trusted confidant, yet Wang Bo did not constrain his freedom. Even if Wang Bo was merely being polite, it spoke volumes of his magnanimity.

Though Xu Shiji possessed both courage and strategy, he was young, and his emotions were easily read.

He sighed and said, "We not only surrounded Zhuojun but also won consecutive victories against the city’s garrison. I truly thought we could settle this once and for all."

Wei Zheng glanced at Xu Shiji. "With your talent and strategy, Maogong, did you really think it could be settled once and for all?"

Xu Shiji chuckled. "I was joking. Sigh, I just wanted to scare the Emperor for a while longer. It would be wonderful if we could scare him to death."

Dou Jiande agreed, "If only we could have frightened him for a few more days."

The generals in the tent all burst into laughter.

Wang Bo smiled. "Alright, we’ve scared him for a few days and intercepted a great deal of the Sui army’s grain and equipment. We’ve already gotten our money’s worth. Let us follow the established plan and retreat. If we don't leave now, we’ll be blocked by those two old thieves, Yuwen Shu and Lai Hu'er."

Zhai Rang cupped his hands with a smile. "Who knows when we shall meet again after this parting. Take care, everyone."

Gao Shida also cupped his hands. "Let us all strive to survive until we meet again."

Wang Bo bowed deeply. "I wish you all great fortune."

The generals in the tent exchanged farewells—some clasped fists, some bowed, others clapped each other on the shoulders.

"Don't die, kid."

"I wonder if we'll have a chance to fight side-by-side again."

"Perhaps next time we meet, we'll be crossing swords to fight over territory?"

"Hahahaha, quite possible."

"If we do cross swords, it would mean the dog emperor is already dead, right?"

"Thinking of it that way, I'm actually looking forward to it. I’ll definitely be the one to take your head, *clack*!"

"I’ll cut your head off right now."

"Hahahahaha!"...

The siege was about to fail, and they were about to flee, yet there was not a hint of gloom on their faces.

After the final war council, Wang Bo arranged to pass through Goguryeo, Zhai Rang through the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, and Gao Shida broke his forces into smaller units to return to the Central Plains. Their respective strategists had already prepared their escape routes.

It was hard work, and it was dangerous, but the thought of replacing their wooden clubs with iron blades, their hemp rags with armor, and having secured a massive haul of grain and horses—most importantly, having finally frightened the dog emperor, forcing his arrogant, high-and-mighty eyes to see the commoners who had risen up because they could no longer survive—made it all worth it.

Before leaving, the three men slaughtered the livestock they couldn't take with them and held a wild, drunken feast outside the city until midnight.

Xu Shiji and Dou Jiande toasted Wei Zheng. "Though we cannot get drunk, could we trouble Master Wei to honor us with a cup of this humble wine?"

Wei Zheng smiled and drank. "You are too kind."

Dou Jiande looked at Wei Zheng with intense fervor. "The success of this campaign relied entirely on your strategies, Master Wei. You must surely be famous throughout the world by now."

Wei Zheng wiped the wine from his beard. "My petty tricks are far from making me famous throughout the world. It is the three of you who are destined for such fame."

Xu Shiji said, "When our lords vie for the Central Plains, all three of us will be famous throughout the world."

Dou Jiande felt a pang of melancholy for reasons unknown, but he smiled and agreed, "We certainly will. By then, we shall be rivals."

Wei Zheng smiled without a word.

Xu Shiji found Wei Zheng’s smile strange. "Does Master Wei not think so?"

Wei Zheng sighed with a smile. "Do you think that if the Great Sui falls, our respective lords will be the ones to vie for the Central Plains?"

Xu Shiji asked in confusion, "Why not?"

Wei Zheng stopped smiling and sighed. "Look at the strategists under our lords' commands. Is there a single member of the gentry among them? Not even speaking of the great noble clans, but even the sons of ordinary officials—are there any? Among this rebel army, the two with the best backgrounds are actually myself and you, Maogong."

Although Xu Shiji was from the Xu clan of the Gaoping Northern Ancestral Upper House, this "small noble family" was so minor it was no different from a humble household, and no one in his family held office.

Xu Shiji and Dou Jiande frowned simultaneously.

Dou Jiande said, "That is because we are not yet strong enough. Once we are strong, they will surely come to join us."

Wei Zheng said, "I hope so."

Xu Shiji laughed. "It is too early to think of such things. Let us survive this crisis first."

Dou Jiande nodded. "True."

Xu Shiji said, "Speaking of the sons of the gentry, have you heard of the Tang Duke’s second son, Li Erlang?"

Dou Jiande sighed. "The 'Invincible' Li Erlang—who hasn't heard of him?"

Wei Zheng tapped his wine cup with his finger. "Isn't it 'Benevolent and Righteous' Li Erlang?"

Xu Shiji said, "That was how long ago? Now he is 'Invincible'!"

Wei Zheng asked, "Oh? What has Li Erlang done now? Isn't he stationed in Zhangye? That is quite far from us; how are you still receiving news of him?"

Dou Jiande said, "The messengers of good news reached Luoyang. We have agents stationed near Luoyang, so naturally, we know. The Sui Crown Prince is also publicizing Li Erlang’s military exploits everywhere to appease the officials unsettled by the Duke of Chu, Yang Xuangan."

Xu Shiji said, "Li Erlang led only eight hundred men to capture Xihai Commandery! He killed tens of thousands and captured over a hundred thousand head of livestock. Tsk, tsk, it sounds a bit exaggerated; I wonder if it's true."

Wei Zheng said indifferently, "It must be false. Even if it were just tens of thousands of sheep, eight hundred men would struggle to capture them, let alone tens of thousands of people. It is likely the Great Sui exaggerating Li Erlang’s achievements to stabilize public morale."

Xu Shiji said, "Capturing Xihai Commandery must be true. Although I loathe the Great Sui, no matter how chaotic it is, it is our own affair in the Central Plains. The Tuyuhun people wanted to take advantage of the chaos to raid us; they deserved to be killed by Li Erlang."

Dou Jiande agreed wholeheartedly. "Whether it is the Turks, the Tuyuhun, or Goguryeo, I hope they learn to behave."

When they were seizing supplies this time, they had clashed with the Goguryeo people. The Goguryeo soldiers were formidable when defending their cities, but they were no match for them in the field.

Although the Goguryeo forces couldn't beat them, it was partly because they were already exhausted from fighting the Great Sui for days. However, the people of the Central Plains had always looked down upon the "barbarians," and Xu Shiji and Dou Jiande, both priding themselves on their intellect, held few people in high regard, let alone Goguryeo barbarians.

Dou Jiande sighed. "Although the Great Sui has a dog emperor, many ministers and generals are still loyal to the country. The Central Plains are in chaos, yet Li Erlang fights alone, swearing to defend the border and bolster the majesty of our Huaxia. It is truly admirable."

Xu Shiji said, "Though he is formidable, if he weren't the son of the Duke of Tang, how would he have the opportunity to defend the border? If I had such an opportunity, I would be no worse than him, hmph!"

Dou Jiande laughed. "Maogong is also a young talent; you would certainly be better than him."

Wei Zheng said slowly, "Li Erlang is only fourteen years old."

Xu Shiji said, "I could do it at fourteen too!"

Wei Zheng said, "When Li Erlang first captured the Tuyuhun Khan, he was only eleven. At that time, he wasn't even a general; he only brought his own servants."

Xu Shiji said, "I could do that too! And didn't he also persuade the Huihe to help?"

Dou Jiande laughed so hard he couldn't straighten up. "I believe you, I believe you, you certainly could."

Xu Shiji said sheepishly, "Fine, I couldn't. Only eleven? What did he eat growing up? This is damnably outrageous!"

Wei Zheng said, "It is outrageous."

Dou Jiande wiped the tears of laughter from his eyes. "In recent years, Li Erlang’s reputation has grown louder and louder, but I have noticed another person hidden behind him."

Xu Shiji said, "Li Sanlang? Li Sanlang is a good man; he has saved many commoners."

Dou Jiande shook his head. "The eight-year-old scholar Li Xuanba—how could he be merely a 'good man'?"

Wei Zheng said, "I hear Li Sanlang has been physically weak since birth, so perhaps he has spent all these years recovering from illness, which is why his reputation is not prominent."

Dou Jiande shook his head again. "If he spent all his time recovering, how could he attain the rank of General of the Tiger Teeth and Wolf? A sickly scholar, yet he can become a General..."

Xu Shiji pinched his chin. "Li Sanlang... could he be Li Erlang’s strategist?"

Wei Zheng sighed inwardly and took a higher view of his two temporary colleagues, making a mental note of their names.

"Even if he is, he is still serving the dog emperor," Wei Zheng said indifferently. "Whether it is Li Erlang or Li Sanlang, they possess talent but aid the tyrant. They cannot be called great heroes!"

Dou Jiande said, "You cannot say that... sigh, our positions are different, I suppose. But the Tang Duke’s pair of 'Qilin' sons are truly formidable. 'Invincible' and 'Unfailing in Strategy'—they are truly worthy of being twins."

Xu Shiji said, "That's right, they are twins. Isn't that too complementary? Did Li Erlang come into this world with a strategist by his side? What kind of heaven-favored children are they?!"

Wei Zheng said, "Nothing special."

Dou Jiande gave a bitter smile. "Master Wei, you... sigh, your prejudice against the sons of the nobility is truly deep. You were just praising them a moment ago."

Wei Zheng snorted. "No need to mention such mood-killing people again. Drink!"

Xu Shiji and Dou Jiande: "Yes, yes."

Wei Zheng poured the wine, muttering to himself that his young master was too capable, putting him under immense pressure.

He had been somewhat proud of his successful strategy this time, but upon hearing of his lord’s feat of "breaking Xihai Commandery with eight hundred cavalry," his interest in his own achievements had waned.

Wei Zheng drained his cup in one go. He had to keep working harder!

...

When Yuwen Shu and Lai Hu'er arrived in a hurry to protect the Emperor, the rebel army had already retreated completely.

The rebels had not only scoured the surrounding area of all supplies, but even the commoners outside the city had followed them. The area around Zhuojun was now completely deserted.

After Yang Guang sent out Yuwen Shu and Lai Hu'er, he had left about two hundred thousand men, including laborers, to protect himself.

These people were trapped in Zhuojun, and the rebels had taken advantage of the chaotic retreat to sneak into the camps and the city to set fires. Now, the city had long since run out of grain.

The Sui army went door-to-door looting for food, sparking riots and fires within the city, leading to significant chaos.

Even more terrifyingly, the fire spread to the Linshuo Palace.

Yang Guang fled in a disheveled state. Although he was never in any real danger, he had never suffered such hardships in his life. Even when a tenth of the Sui soldiers had frozen to death crossing the Great Douba Valley, it had nothing to do with him, as he was wrapped in thick fur cloaks and warming himself by a small stove.

Yang Guang, hungry and terrified, cried loudly while clutching his young son, Yang Gao, and his eldest grandson, Yang Tan. Having inhaled smoke, he fell into a severe illness.

By the time Yuwen Shu and Lai Hu'er reached Zhuojun, Yang Guang was still too ill to rise from his bed.

Su Wei and other high-ranking ministers hoped that Yang Guang would summon the Crown Prince, Yang Jian, to Zhuojun.

Yang Guang cursed from his sickbed: "I am not dead yet! You all wish to abandon me and turn to the Crown Prince?!"

The high ministers were left bewildered by Yang Guang’s cursing.

Su Wei advised, "Your Majesty is ill, and the Crown Prince should naturally attend to your health. Furthermore, the main army is still in Zhuojun, and the rebel Yang Xuangan has yet to be captured; the court needs someone to take charge. We are merely your subjects and should not overstep; only the Crown Prince can act as regent while Your Majesty is ill."

Su Wei thought to himself: *Besides, if the Crown Prince is not by your side when you are critically ill, and cannot succeed to the throne in time, are you not afraid of a change in the dynasty?*

But he dared not say it.

He realized the Emperor was terrified of death and could only use the excuse that the Crown Prince should attend to his health and act as regent.

Yet, even with such a reasonable and gentle excuse, Yang Guang could not accept it.

Yang Guang smashed everything within reach. At this moment, the ministers around him were no longer willing to indulge him as they had in the past. Even Yu Shiji and others did not mention the Crown Prince, nor did they argue with the other ministers.

First, Yang Guang was critically ill, and it was unclear if he would survive. If the Crown Prince ascended the throne, anyone who opposed the Crown Prince coming to Zhuojun would certainly be purged.

Second, there was an urgent need for someone to act as regent. This was a task that would kill anyone who touched it, except for the Crown Prince.

Therefore, they all hoped the Crown Prince would arrive quickly.

Yu Shiji and others also complained in private.

When the Emperor falls ill, the Crown Prince should act as regent. Usually, when an emperor is critically ill, he is desperate for the Crown Prince to fly over overnight, fearing that powerful ministers might take advantage of the situation. Was their Emperor truly sick in the head?

But no matter how the ministers remonstrated, Yang Guang refused to issue the decree.

Consequently, court affairs were paralyzed; no one pursued the fleeing rebels, and no one continued the siege against Yang Xuangan.

After catching his breath, Yang Xuangan captured Bohai Commandery and established a firm foothold there.

Scattered rebel groups from the vicinity flocked to Yang Xuangan’s banner, and his army instantly expanded to one hundred thousand.

Having recovered, he led his men to attack nearby commanderies and counties to plunder supplies.

Knowing that he could not settle everything in one battle, Yang Xuangan changed his strategy to a slow and steady approach.

Repeated defeats had worn down Yang Xuangan’s arrogance, making him trust Li Mi and Li Zixiong even more.

With the assistance of Li Mi and Li Zixiong, and the Sui court’s continued lack of response, Yang Xuangan’s power grew once again.

Yang Xuangan was the Duke of Chu, a top-tier noble of the Great Sui. Naturally, scholars skilled in strategy and governance followed him.

Once he established a foothold, these scholars immediately exerted their influence. They integrated nearby rebel forces, re-established laws, and raised the banner of "light taxes and low corvée" to attract the common people.

Yang Xuangan also announced the repeal of all regulations changed by Yang Guang, reverting all court systems to the era of Emperor Wen of Sui to entice the noble clans to defect to him.

Some scholars who had been suppressed during the reigns of Emperor Wen and Yang Guang were successfully enticed. For instance, the brothers Shi Wanbao and Shi Wanshou—brothers of Shi Wansui, who had been unjustly executed by Yang Guang—came to join him.

In truth, Shi Wansui had been framed by Yang Xuangan’s father, Yang Su. But for the sake of their own wealth and status, Shi Wanbao and Shi Wanshou pinned Shi Wansui’s death on Emperor Wen, Yang Jian, selectively ignoring what Yang Su had done.

In the city of Luoyang.

After Yang Jian received news of his father’s critical illness, he wanted to rush to Zhuojun immediately, but was dissuaded by Li Yuan.

Li Yuan said, "If His Majesty wanted you to go to Zhuojun, he would naturally issue an order. Since he has not, you would be leaving Luoyang without an imperial decree. Your Highness, you should send someone to Zhuojun to inquire about His Majesty’s will, and then act accordingly."

Yang Jian hurriedly sent someone to Zhuojun to request an imperial decree. Whether it was to attend to his father’s health or to remain in Luoyang, he hoped for a clear instruction.

Upon seeing Yang Jian’s letter, Yang Guang said angrily, "He is probing to see if I am dead or alive, wanting to ascend the throne!"

Perhaps anger gave Yang Guang strength; he recovered a bit of spirit and issued a decree enfeoffing his youngest son, Yang Gao, as the Prince of Zhao, and his eldest grandson, Yang Tan, as the Prince of Yan, while reprimanding Crown Prince Yang Jian for failing to guard Luoyang and allowing Yang Xuangan to escape.

The ministers were all shocked and bewildered.

Yuwen Shu, Yu Shiji, and others who knew Yang Guang best sighed, knowing they had to stand in opposition to the Crown Prince.

It was not that the Crown Prince was bad, nor that he was too good; it was simply that the Emperor, in his critical illness, had developed suspicion and disgust toward his robust Crown Prince.

Crown Prince Yang Jian, in Luoyang, received Yang Guang’s decree and was left at a loss.

He recalled what Li Xuanba had once said to him, and a chill ran down his spine.

Is Father... suspicious of me?

Just because he fell into a serious illness, he is suspicious of me?

Yang Jian felt a touch of sorrow, but also wanted to laugh.

He suddenly had the urge to visit his elder brother.

*Brother, oh brother, you deliberately provoked Father’s anger before you died so that your children could escape the vortex of the struggle for the throne, but you still miscalculated.*

*Yang Tan has been enfeoffed as the Prince of Yan; he will be forced to compete with his uncles for the throne. Your other sons, including your eldest legitimate son, Yang You, were not even promoted—they must be very dissatisfied.*

*Father wants to personally create the chaos of the Sui throne struggle; does he think this world is not chaotic enough?*

When Li Yuan learned of this, he lamented to Lady Dou, "I have never seen a critically ill emperor suspicious of the Crown Prince. The Crown Prince is the heir apparent; when the Emperor is critically ill, he should prepare for the Crown Prince to succeed him."

Lady Dou said calmly, "When Emperor Wen of Sui was critically ill, did he not suddenly become suspicious of the current Majesty?"

Li Yuan sighed, "This... sigh. My lady, I fear we cannot stay in Luoyang much longer. I see that His Majesty is unwilling to give the credit for guarding Luoyang to the Crown Prince, and I estimate he will push it all onto me. When that time comes, I will bribe court officials to seek a post outside the capital. It is better for Erlang and Sanlang; they are truly free at the border."

Lady Dou said, "Do whatever you feel is right, my lord; I support you."

Li Yuan laughed. "I know. You have worked hard guarding the city this time, my lady."

When Li Yuan was guarding the city, Lady Dou had donned simple clothes and led the wives of the city to cook and sew for the soldiers, greatly boosting the morale of the city.

Crown Prince Yang Jian had thanked Lady Dou many times and called on the other noblewomen in the city to learn from her.

Li Yuan also looked at Lady Dou with new eyes. It turned out his wife had such capabilities and was not just limited to the affairs of the inner courtyard, so he was now willing to discuss court affairs with her.

As the situation in the Central Plains changed drastically, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba welcomed Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui.

"Xuanling! Keming!" As soon as Li Shimin saw them, he ignored the dust on their clothes, opened his arms, and pulled them both into an embrace.

Fang Qiao: "?"

Du Ruhui: "Hahaha, Li Er, let go."

Li Xuanba, like a turtle, yawned while slowly shuffling over.

Li Xuanba: *[Second Brother, your current actions remind me of a line from a later era: "You are all my wings."]*

Li Shimin laughed and released them, turning to his younger brother. "They are indeed my wings, and so are you."

Li Xuanba made a gagging gesture.

Du Ruhui complained with a smile, "You two are using your twin telepathy to whisper in private again."

Li Shimin put his hands on his hips. "Can't help it, that's how twins are."

Du Ruhui cupped his hands. "Fine, fine, you're right."

Fang Qiao sighed. "After being separated for a few years, both of you have created such great reputations, so why haven't you changed at all?"

Li Shimin asked curiously, "What reputations? Is it still 'Benevolent and Righteous' or 'Virtuous and Gracious'?"

Fang Qiao shook his head. "It is 'Invincible' and 'Unfailing in Strategy'."

Du Ruhui sighed. "I heard it too; they say it spread from the rebel army. They hold you in such high regard."

*The rebel army?* Li Shimin and Li Xuanba exchanged a glance. *Could Wei Zheng be building their reputation for them?*

Li Xuanba said, "Is it about the capture of Xihai Commandery? That has nothing to do with me; the one who is 'Unfailing in Strategy' is Second Brother. Even I was startled."

Du Ruhui said, "No rush, tell us slowly. Let me wash, change clothes, and rest for a day first. Oh my, I'm exhausted."

Fang Qiao nodded. "Dade, organize the books I brought first."

Du Ruhui said, "I only brought a few records of farmland. I wanted to bring more, but His Majesty is in Zhuojun, and I didn't dare make any big moves."

Li Shimin said, "As long as you arrived safely, what does it matter what gifts you brought? Of course, if you brought gifts, that's even better, hahahaha. Keming, you lost to Xuanling this time."

Du Ruhui rolled his eyes. "Yes, yes, you're right."

Li Xuanba said, "What do you mean 'I organize them first'? Of course, we'll put them together and organize them. Now that you two are here, don't think about making me do all the work alone."

Although the four had been separated for several years, they still got along as harmoniously as before.

After Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui washed away the dust of travel, they moved into Li Shimin and Li Xuanba’s home, and incidentally met Luo Shixin.

Upon hearing that Luo Shixin’s martial prowess rivaled Li Shimin’s, both men were amazed.

Du Ruhui, having a strong sense of curiosity, quietly asked Li Xuanba in private, "Is this also someone you scouted for Li Er in advance?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "He heard of Second Brother’s reputation and traveled thousands of miles to join us on his own."

Du Ruhui remarked with emotion, "Li Er is already showing the appearance of a wise lord."

Li Xuanba said, "Besides, I didn't scout for talent for Second Brother in advance before. Didn't you all bump into us yourselves wanting to be friends with me and Second Brother? I never actively sought you out."

Du Ruhui said, "That's true. Sigh, can't you just say you actively sought us out? That way, Fang Xuanling and I would have more face."

Li Xuanba spread his hands. "But you all stuck to us yourselves."

Du Ruhui laughed in frustration. "Stuck to you ourselves? Your speech is getting more and more outrageous."

Li Shimin hurriedly reached out to hook his sharp-tongued brother’s neck, pulling him away from Du Ruhui, who had already begun rolling up his sleeves. "Alright, alright, Keming, you know what A-Xuan is like. He just has a sharp tongue; don't take it to heart."

Du Ruhui scolded with a smile, "If you know he has a sharp tongue, make him change it! Aren't you afraid he'll get beaten up?"

Li Shimin raised an eyebrow. "With me here, who would dare!"

Fang Qiao said slowly, "Your parents?"

Li Shimin: "..."

He said sheepishly, "Then I can only get beaten up alongside A-Xuan."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui couldn't help but laugh.

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes. He would never be sharp-tongued toward his parents.

The group sat around the campfire, talking about their respective experiences.

Li Zhiyun and Luo Shixin also sat quietly to the side, listening to the stories.

The first to speak was naturally Li Shimin.

Li Shimin finally had the chance to boast about himself, and he did so with such eloquence and literary flair that he could have written a rhapsody in his own praise.

Li Xuanba yawned repeatedly.

Although Li Zhiyun and Luo Shixin had heard Li Shimin speak many times, they still wore expressions of admiration.

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui’s eyes shone with brilliance.

Although they had just heard a rough account of Li Shimin’s capture of Xihai Commandery, it was only when Li Shimin detailed his lightning-fast planning that they truly grasped his brilliance.

However, it was not as Li Xuanba had claimed—that Li Xuanba had done nothing. The initial intelligence gathering and sending spies into the two tribes had all been Li Xuanba’s work.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第114章 友人齐聚张掖郡 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
更重要的是，李玄霸在如此短的时间就给李世民凑齐了五百精锐骑兵装备，这敛财的本事真是令人震撼。

李世民一口气炫耀完后，抱着葡萄酒当水喝。

张掖的葡萄长得特别好，酿成的葡萄酒比大兴和洛阳的葡萄酒更好喝。

房乔和杜如晦品着葡萄酒，吃着烤羊肉，也说起各自的经历。

房乔已经尽可能地收集了江南各郡的户籍等文书，在江南民乱范围扩大之后才离开；杜如晦则将高丽之战记录下来，细细梳理了隋军出征高丽的得失。

这点小事房乔和杜如晦没有多说，他们提起了各自遇到的“奇人”。

房乔提起的“奇人”，自然是指兄弟二人的母亲窦夫人。

房乔感慨道：“窦夫人真是巾帼英雄，怪不得能教养出你们这么优秀的孩子。”

李世民问道：“母亲在洛阳可还好？虽然杨玄感肯定无法攻破洛阳，母亲应该无事。”

房乔道：“我来张掖前先路过了洛阳，我还给你们带来了唐国公和窦夫人的信。他们都很好，具体的事你们自己看信吧。”

房乔顿了顿，道：“太子知道我要去投奔你后，也悄悄托我给你们送来了信。我没拆。”

李世民大大咧咧道：“拆了也没事。我和阿玄什么事都不会瞒着你。哦，我家观音婢和阿玄家珠娘的信不准拆！”

房乔无语：“谁会拆啊！”

杜如晦挤眉弄眼：“我对太子的信不好奇，你们未婚妻的信我倒是真好奇。”

李玄霸道：“你最好别好奇。克明，你遇到了谁？难道是哪个农民起义军的首领？”

“农民起义军啊……是你会说的话。”杜如晦笑着叹息道，“是首领，也不是。李二，李三，你们认识一个叫魏徵的人吗？”

李世民和李玄霸对视一眼，李世民拍着胸脯道：“是我和阿玄的人。”

杜如晦道：“他也说是你和李三的人，来找我要涿郡的城防图。”

李世民和李玄霸瞠目结舌：“啊？！”

杜如晦苦笑道：“这人也太大胆了！他就不怕我出卖他吗？”

李玄霸道：“他要涿郡的城防图干什么？难道想让王薄攻打涿郡？涿郡坚固，又有大量隋军，王薄攻打涿郡，无疑以卵击石。以他聪慧，不会这样做才是。”

杜如晦道：“我也如此对他说。他说，他原本只是想趁着杨玄感吸引了皇帝的注意力，带着义军捡走大隋丢在高丽的辎重，以免便宜高丽人。如果皇帝决策失误，涿郡防备松散，他就带义军去围住涿郡，把涿郡附近军队囤积的粮草兵器盔甲抢了，顺便吓唬一下皇帝。”

李玄霸嘴角抽搐，不知道要怎么评价。魏徵的胆子也太大了！

杜如晦接着道：“他说他不认识我，但你提起过我，那么他就相信我。唉，这人不简单啊。你们一定要好好把握住他，不能让他倒向其他人，否则一定会成为我们棘手的敌人。”

李世民摆手：“不用担心。他已入我彀中，还能逃？”

李玄霸道：“魏徵所愿乃是名垂青史。他所希望的只有二哥能为他实现。其实我已经告诉他未来，他才前往王薄处。”

房乔疑惑：“为何？他不应该留在你和二郎身边吗？”

李玄霸道：“他听了‘房谋杜断’后，对自己只留下‘谏臣楷模’的名声很不满意，说自己修习纵横，本事不比你们差，要和你们比一比。”

李世民默默瞥了弟弟一眼。

来了来了，弟弟的坏心思来了。这是挑拨离间啊！

房乔挑眉：“哦？”

杜如晦捏着下巴道：“这样啊……”

李智云好奇道：“什么未来？什么‘房谋杜断’？”

众人这才“注意”到，李智云和罗士信还在这里。

李玄霸：【说吗？】

李世民点头：“小五已经长大了，应该经得住事了。士信的口风也很严，我相信他。”

李玄霸道：“我有谶纬之能，能为众人看相。”

李智云丝毫不怀疑：“哇，三兄好厉害。三兄，我的未来是什么？”

李玄霸道：“封王。”

李智云得意道：“我就知道，我很厉害！二兄，我和你一样！将来都能封王！”

李世民似笑非笑：“那可不一样。”

李智云疑惑：“封王是最厉害的了吧？”

众人皆扶额叹气失笑，把李智云笑得一头雾水。

罗士信眼皮子直跳：“集弘，只有宗室能封王。寻常臣子最多只能封国公。你傻了吗？这件事连我都知道！”

李智云大惊失色：“对哦！”

惊完后，李智云迅速平静：“我就觉得这大隋一副快要灭亡的模样，原来接下来该二哥当皇帝了啊。”

李世民好奇：“为何是我，不是父亲？”

李智云道：“父亲当皇帝和二哥当皇帝有什么区别？难道还能让长兄当皇帝？他若立讨人厌的长兄当太子，弟弟我帮你夺位！”

李世民切了个羊腿给李智云：“吃你的羊腿，别胡说。你乖乖的，危险的事别掺和。”

李玄霸道：“你护好自己就行。”

李智云恶狠狠地啃羊腿：“刚刚还说我已经长大了，现在还是把我当小孩。哼！你们等着！”

房乔、杜如晦和罗士信三人面面相觑。

李智云也太淡定了吧！不愧是李二郎和李三郎养大的弟弟，和两人真像，造反和夺嫡的事都能轻易说出来，丝毫不惊讶。

罗士信支支吾吾，犹豫不决。

李世民笑道：“你也想问你的未来？”

罗士信先点头，又摇头：“不想不想。”

李世民逗弄道：“怕了？”

罗士信道：“只要我跟着二郎君，未来肯定不会差。”

李玄霸幽幽道：“是不差，二十多岁的剡国公，谥号为‘勇’。”

房乔和杜如晦丝毫不意外。这少年不仅武力高强，还拥有极强的毅力，跨越万里来张掖投奔李二郎，未来成就不可能差，青史留名很正常。

房乔疑惑：“大德，你的表情可不像是夸人。”

杜如晦开玩笑：“怎么？他将来反了？”

罗士信吓得手中的羊肉都掉了：“不可能！郎君对我恩重如山，我绝对不是这种人！”

杜如晦一本正经道：“我知道你不会，才开这种玩笑。如果你是这样的人，我就不会这么说了。”

罗士信表情变得幽怨。

杜如晦对房乔笑道：“逗小孩真好玩。”

房乔忍笑：“够了，以后我们都是同僚。”

杜如晦正色道：“李二还是我主公呢，我还不是要趁着李二还没长大，多欺负他几下？”

房乔嘴角抽搐道：“将来你被大雄关进牢里，可别后悔今日之言。”

李玄霸起哄：“好主意。二哥，等你当皇帝了，就把杜克明关到牢里给你办事。”

李世民与李玄霸一唱一和：“关进牢里还要为我干活，这也太惨了？我会多给他增加点俸禄，把牢里的稻草也多铺一层。”

李智云傻乎乎道：“听说牢里黑黢黢的，要多点一根蜡烛吗？”

李世民和李玄霸异口同声道：“蜡烛管够。”

说完后，兄弟二人为默契击掌。

杜如晦笑骂道：“滚！都把我关进牢里了，居然还让我干活？想都别想！”

罗士信结结巴巴道：“我真的没谋反吧？我没有吧？”

李世民笑着给罗士信切了块肉：“没有。只是你跟着我南征北战英年早逝了。相信我，我绝对不会让未来应验。你这次一定能寿终正寝。”

罗士信松了口气，笑道：“我是将军，马革裹尸理所当然。每次上战场，我都做好了战亡的准备，郎君不必在意。”

他笑眯眯地啃羊肉，心情好极了，半点没有因为自己在战场上英年早逝难过。

李玄霸语重心长道：“我提前告诉你这件事，就是让你上战场时别太拼命。还有，如果你被俘虏了就尽管投降，留得命在，才能偷偷溜回来。”

李世民点头道：“听到没，士信。如果不小心战败了，赶紧投降。哪怕逃不回来，我也能很快把你接回来。你放心，我和阿玄永远相信你。”

罗士信低着头道：“我不会战败。”

李世民道：“你只需要回答，是！”

罗士信咬着牙关道：“是！”

李世民笑道：“这才对，来，继续喝酒。”

李智云不满道：“不用叮嘱我吗？”

李玄霸叹气：“小五，如果我和二哥还要叮嘱你，就白教你这么多年了。”

“嘻嘻。”李智云洋洋得意地啃羊腿。

房乔笑道：“喝酒喝酒。我大概不会上战场，不会有被俘虏的一日。”

杜如晦笑道：“不过李二李三，你们放心，如果真的运气不好被俘，我也绝对会迅速投降，不给你们祭奠我的机会。喝酒！”

李世民和李玄霸举起了酒杯，然后李世民飞速把李玄霸的酒杯抢了。

他们笑闹着吃肉喝酒，都没有去看罗士信，假装无视了罗士信。

罗士信吸着鼻子低头啃肉，眼泪鼻涕糊了一脸。
chunks.englishText:
More importantly, the fact that Li Xuanba had managed to assemble equipment for five hundred elite cavalrymen for Li Shimin in such a short time was truly staggering—his ability to amass wealth was nothing short of shocking.

After Li Shimin finished showing off in one breath, he hugged the wine skin and drank the grape wine as if it were water.

The grapes of Zhangye grew exceptionally well; the wine brewed from them tasted even better than that of Daxing or Luoyang.

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui sipped their wine and ate roasted lamb, sharing their own experiences.

Fang Qiao had collected as many household registers and official documents from the various commanderies of Jiangnan as possible, only departing after the scope of the civil unrest there had expanded. Du Ruhui, meanwhile, had recorded the war in Goguryeo, meticulously sorting through the gains and losses of the Sui army’s expedition.

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui did not dwell on these minor matters; instead, they brought up the "extraordinary people" they had encountered.

The "extraordinary person" Fang Qiao mentioned was, naturally, the brothers' mother, Lady Dou.

Fang Qiao sighed with emotion, "Lady Dou is truly a heroine among women. It is no wonder she was able to raise such outstanding children as you two."

Li Shimin asked, "Is Mother doing well in Luoyang? Although Yang Xuangan certainly cannot breach Luoyang, Mother should be safe."

Fang Qiao replied, "I passed through Luoyang before coming to Zhangye, and I have brought you letters from the Duke of Tang and Lady Dou. They are both well; you can read the letters for the specific details yourselves."

Fang Qiao paused, then added, "After the Crown Prince learned I was coming to join you, he also secretly entrusted me with a letter for you. I did not open it."

Li Shimin said nonchalantly, "It wouldn't have mattered if you had. Ah Xuan and I keep no secrets from you. Oh, but the letters from my Guanyinbi and Ah Xuan’s Zhuniang are not to be opened!"

Fang Qiao was speechless. "Who would open those!"

Du Ruhui winked, "I’m not curious about the Crown Prince’s letter, but I am truly curious about the letters from your fiancées."

Li Xuanba said, "You would do best not to be. Keming, whom did you encounter? Could it be some leader of a peasant uprising?"

"A peasant uprising leader... that sounds like something you would say." Du Ruhui sighed with a smile. "He is a leader, yet he is not. Li Er, Li San, do you know a man named Wei Zheng?"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba exchanged a glance. Li Shimin patted his chest and said, "He is one of our men."

Du Ruhui said, "He also claimed to be your man, and came to me asking for the city defense map of Zhuojun."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were dumbfounded. "Huh?!"

Du Ruhui gave a wry smile. "This man is far too bold! Was he not afraid that I might betray him?"

Li Xuanba asked, "What did he want the Zhuojun defense map for? Did he want Wang Bo to attack Zhuojun? Zhuojun is heavily fortified and holds a large number of Sui troops; for Wang Bo to attack it would undoubtedly be like throwing an egg against a rock. Given his intelligence, he shouldn't be doing that."

Du Ruhui replied, "I said the same to him. He told me that he originally only intended to take advantage of the fact that Yang Xuangan had drawn the Emperor’s attention to lead his rebel army and scavenge the supplies the Great Sui had abandoned in Goguryeo, so as not to let the Goguryeo people have them. If the Emperor made a strategic error and the defenses of Zhuojun were lax, he would lead his army to surround the city and seize the grain, weapons, and armor stockpiled by the troops nearby, while also giving the Emperor a good scare."

Li Xuanba’s mouth twitched; he didn't know how to evaluate this. Wei Zheng’s courage was truly immense!

Du Ruhui continued, "He said he didn't know me, but since you had mentioned me, he trusted me. Sigh, this man is not simple. You must hold onto him firmly; you cannot let him lean toward anyone else, or he will surely become a troublesome enemy for us."

Li Shimin waved his hand. "No need to worry. He is already in my snare; how could he escape?"

Li Xuanba said, "Wei Zheng’s ambition is to leave his name in history. Only Second Brother can fulfill what he desires. In fact, I have already told him of the future, which is why he went to Wang Bo."

Fang Qiao was puzzled. "Why? Shouldn't he have remained by your and Er Lang’s side?"

Li Xuanba said, "After he heard of 'Fang’s Schemes and Du’s Decisions,' he was very dissatisfied with being remembered only as a 'model remonstrating official.' He said he had studied the arts of vertical and horizontal alliances and that his abilities were no less than yours, so he wanted to compete with you."

Li Shimin silently glanced at his younger brother.

Here it comes, here it comes—his brother’s mischief. This was sowing discord!

Fang Qiao raised an eyebrow. "Oh?"

Du Ruhui stroked his chin and said, "Is that so..."

Li Zhiyun asked curiously, "What future? What is 'Fang’s Schemes and Du’s Decisions'?"

Only then did everyone "notice" that Li Zhiyun and Luo Shixin were still there.

Li Xuanba: [Should I tell him?]

Li Shimin nodded. "Xiao Wu is grown up now; he should be able to handle things. Shixin is also very tight-lipped, I trust him."

Li Xuanba said, "I possess the ability of prophecy and can read the fortunes of others."

Li Zhiyun did not doubt it for a second. "Wow, Third Brother is amazing. Third Brother, what is my future?"

Li Xuanba said, "You will be enfeoffed as a Prince."

Li Zhiyun said proudly, "I knew it, I’m very capable! Second Brother, I’m just like you! We will both be enfeoffed as Princes in the future!"

Li Shimin said with a cryptic smile, "That’s not quite the same."

Li Zhiyun was confused. "Being a Prince is the most powerful thing, isn't it?"

Everyone sighed and laughed, covering their foreheads, leaving Li Zhiyun completely bewildered.

Luo Shixin’s eyelids twitched. "Jihong, only members of the Imperial Clan can be enfeoffed as Princes. Ordinary officials can at most be enfeoffed as Dukes. Are you stupid? Even I know that!"

Li Zhiyun was shocked. "Oh, right!"

After his shock, Li Zhiyun quickly calmed down. "I just felt that this Great Sui looked like it was about to perish; so it turns out Second Brother is going to be the Emperor next."

Li Shimin was curious. "Why me, and not Father?"

Li Zhiyun said, "What difference does it make whether Father is Emperor or Second Brother is Emperor? Surely you wouldn't let Eldest Brother be Emperor? If he makes that annoying Eldest Brother the Crown Prince, I, your younger brother, will help you seize the throne!"

Li Shimin cut a lamb leg and gave it to Li Zhiyun. "Eat your lamb leg and stop talking nonsense. Behave yourself and don't get involved in dangerous things."

Li Xuanba said, "Just make sure you keep yourself safe."

Li Zhiyun gnawed viciously on the lamb leg. "A moment ago you said I was grown up, and now you’re still treating me like a child. Hmph! You just wait!"

Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Luo Shixin looked at each other.

Li Zhiyun was far too calm! He was truly the younger brother raised by Li Erlang and Li Sanlang; he was just like them, able to speak of rebellion and seizing the throne so easily without the slightest surprise.

Luo Shixin stammered, hesitant and indecisive.

Li Shimin smiled. "Do you want to ask about your future as well?"

Luo Shixin nodded, then shook his head. "No, no."

Li Shimin teased, "Afraid?"

Luo Shixin said, "As long as I follow the Second Young Master, my future surely won't be bad."

Li Xuanba said softly, "It won't be bad—a Duke of Shan in your twenties, with the posthumous title of 'Valiant'."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui were not surprised at all. This youth was not only highly skilled in martial arts but also possessed immense perseverance, having traveled ten thousand miles to Zhangye to join Li Erlang; it was impossible for his future achievements to be anything less than stellar. It was only natural that he would leave his name in history.

Fang Qiao was puzzled. "Dade, your expression doesn't look like you're praising someone."

Du Ruhui joked, "What? Does he rebel in the future?"

Luo Shixin was so startled that the lamb in his hand fell. "Impossible! The Young Master has shown me great kindness; I am absolutely not that kind of person!"

Du Ruhui said with a straight face, "I know you wouldn't be, that’s why I made such a joke. If you were that kind of person, I wouldn't have said it."

Luo Shixin’s expression turned aggrieved.

Du Ruhui smiled at Fang Qiao. "Teasing children is so much fun."

Fang Qiao suppressed a laugh. "Enough, we will all be colleagues in the future."

Du Ruhui said seriously, "Li Er is still my lord, so I have to take advantage of the time before he grows up to bully him a few more times, don't I?"

Fang Qiao’s mouth twitched. "In the future, when you are thrown into prison by Daxiong, don't regret these words today."

Li Xuanba egged them on. "Good idea. Second Brother, when you become Emperor, just throw Du Keming into prison to work for you."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba sang in harmony: "If he’s in prison, he’ll still have to work for me? That’s too miserable, isn't it? I’ll increase his salary a bit and have them lay an extra layer of straw in his cell."

Li Zhiyun said foolishly, "I heard prisons are pitch black; should we light an extra candle for him?"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba said in unison, "Candles will be provided in abundance."

After saying this, the two brothers high-fived in perfect sync.

Du Ruhui laughed and cursed, "Get out! You’ve already thrown me in prison and you still want me to work? Don't even think about it!"

Luo Shixin stuttered, "I really didn't rebel, did I? I didn't, right?"

Li Shimin smiled and cut a piece of meat for Luo Shixin. "No. It’s just that you followed me on campaigns and died young. Trust me, I will absolutely not let that future come to pass. This time, you will definitely live out your natural life."

Luo Shixin breathed a sigh of relief and smiled. "I am a general; it is only natural to be wrapped in a horse hide upon death. Every time I go to the battlefield, I am prepared to die in battle. The Young Master need not worry."

He gnawed on the lamb meat with a smile, in a great mood, not the least bit saddened by the fact that he would die young on the battlefield.

Li Xuanba said earnestly, "I told you this in advance so that you wouldn't fight too recklessly on the battlefield. Also, if you are captured, just surrender. Only by keeping your life can you sneak back."

Li Shimin nodded. "Did you hear that, Shixin? If you accidentally lose a battle, surrender immediately. Even if you can't escape back, I will be able to retrieve you quickly. Rest assured, Ah Xuan and I will always believe in you."

Luo Shixin lowered his head. "I will not lose a battle."

Li Shimin said, "You only need to answer: Yes!"

Luo Shixin gritted his teeth and said, "Yes!"

Li Shimin smiled. "That’s better. Come, let’s keep drinking."

Li Zhiyun said with dissatisfaction, "Don't you need to give me any instructions?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Xiao Wu, if Second Brother and I still had to give you instructions, we would have wasted all these years teaching you."

"Hee hee." Li Zhiyun gnawed on his lamb leg, looking very pleased with himself.

Fang Qiao laughed. "Drink, let’s drink. I likely won't be on the battlefield, so I won't have a day where I’m captured."

Du Ruhui smiled. "However, Li Er, Li San, rest assured—if I really am unlucky enough to be captured, I will definitely surrender immediately, so as not to give you the chance to hold a memorial for me. Drink!"

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba raised their cups, and then Li Shimin snatched Li Xuanba’s cup away in a flash.

They laughed and joked as they ate and drank, none of them looking at Luo Shixin, pretending to ignore him.

Luo Shixin sniffled as he lowered his head to gnaw on his meat, his face smeared with tears and snot.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第115章 双标的骨肉相残
chunks.chineseText:
第115章 双标的骨肉相残

房乔和杜如晦来到张掖之后， 李玄霸终于能腾出手做自己擅长的事。
　　说实话，内政和吏治不是李玄霸擅长的事。他前世连公务员都没当过，对官僚系统一无所知， 只能拿着自己当网商时的经验硬套。
　　虽然有高颎和宇文述的教导， 李玄霸在这方面的本事已经超出寻常人， 但比起房乔和杜如晦这两个真正的天才，他还是不够看。
　　何况房乔和杜如晦还有“房谋杜断”的合体技。
　　因中原混乱，杨广此刻派不出人手赴任西海郡郡守。李世民身为攻下西海郡的虎贲郎将， 依照战时规则，暂代西海郡郡守。
　　张掖郡的郡守似乎察觉到了什么，隐晦地表示投诚， 主动当起了吉祥物。
　　虎贲郎将虽然从“将军”改名为“郎将”，但这个职位原则上是有开府的权力。现在天下大乱， 别说虎贲郎将， 就是鹰扬郎将都开始自己任命属官。李世民自然也有资格任命属官。
　　张掖郡和西海郡的内政吏治就交到了李世民的属官，房乔和杜如晦手中。
　　西海郡和张掖郡正好在祁连山脉南北，翻山就到。
　　如果不翻山，那么从张掖郡到西海郡，需要沿着祁连山脉走一遍河西走廊， 先往东南经过武威郡和西平郡，然后往西折到西海郡。四个郡呈现“>”的形状。
　　这四个郡都是军事重镇， 皆设有鹰扬府。李世民身为虎贲郎将，是这四个郡鹰扬府郎将的直接领导。
　　将来武威郡鹰扬郎将李轨会杀掉原本时空中的虎贲郎将造反，将河西之地收入囊中， 自称大凉王。
　　李玄霸没有告诉二哥和房乔、杜如晦这个未来， 以免干扰他们的判断。
　　他相信二哥已经是河西之地名义上的最高军事领导， “房谋杜断”肯定能轻松将河西之地收入二哥囊中， 不用自己多嘴。
　　房乔和杜如晦得到李玄霸这段时间搜集的河西之地的资料后，心情很轻松。
　　他们显然也很有自信，迅速将河西之地打造成李世民的根据地。
　　房乔保证道：“别说河西之地，敦煌郡和更远的伊吾郡，也是主公囊中之物。”
　　杜如晦懒洋洋道：“我和老房如果连这都做不到，还当什么宰相？不如让给薛收和魏徵。”
　　李世民被逗笑了：“何至于直呼他们姓名？薛收字伯褒，魏徵字玄成，别乱叫。”
　　杜如晦摊手：“我记忆力不好。”
　　李世民笑得直不起腰，不断拍打李玄霸的手臂：“哈哈哈哈阿玄，笑死我了。”
　　李玄霸嫌弃地躲开二哥的拍击。有什么好笑的，毛病。
　　房乔干咳一声，转移话题：“内政吏治都交给我们，大德，你做什么？后勤？”
　　李玄霸道：“我以后会主管军队后勤，不过现在这些工作暂时给二哥自己管。我要出使西突厥。”
　　房乔大惊失色：“你一个人去？”
　　杜如晦看向李世民，皱眉道：“我不同意，太危险。”
　　李世民叹气道：“你以为我想同意吗？但阿玄说只有他能说动西突厥可汗出兵东突厥，我也没办法。我倒是想和他一起去，可他说我现在需要坐镇张掖。”
　　李世民沉沉地叹了好几口气，继续道：“他已经决定的事，我相信他。我会让周达和罗士信一同承担阿玄的护卫。”
　　房乔道：“大德，为何你突然想要联合西突厥？是担心东突厥与大隋走得太近吗？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“正好相反，东突厥的始毕可汗已经对大隋有反心，他会趁着大隋势颓壮大。”
　　李玄霸冷笑了一声，道：“隋末唐初所有称帝称王的人全部向始毕可汗称臣，包括大唐。”
　　房乔和杜如晦脸色大变。
　　他们看向李世民。
　　李世民耸肩：“虽然我很想说，唐高祖肯定是我父亲，向东突厥称臣和未及弱冠的我没关系。但以我父亲的性格，若不是情况太危急，也不可能做这种事。这件事是大唐整个朝廷作出的选择。父亲真是屈辱啊。”
　　李玄霸道：“没关系二哥，东突厥在你登基当月兵临渭水。你也挺屈辱的。”
　　李世民把李玄霸一按，给李玄霸来了个十字固定，疼得李玄霸“嗷嗷”叫：“阿玄闭嘴！”
　　房乔和杜如晦看得直摇头。
　　房乔道：“未来的事就别说了，反正会改变。”
　　杜如晦道：“以李二的性格，肯定很快就会报复回来。这点小屈辱有什么好说的。”
　　李世民松开可恶的弟弟，道：“对啊，阿玄，快说你预见中的我怎么报复回来的。”
　　李玄霸揉着胳膊道：“贞观四年灭东突厥，俘虏颉利可汗到长安当众献舞。”
　　李世民吹口哨：“哇哦。”
　　房乔拈须：“还行。”
　　杜如晦大笑：“可以可以。”
　　李世民兴致勃勃道：“是我御驾亲征吗？”
　　李玄霸翻白眼：“想什么呢？当了皇帝哪还有机会亲征？乖乖在长安搞你的后勤。”
　　李世民点头：“明白了。你乖乖在长安搞后勤，我御驾亲征。哥的灭国之功就靠你了，阿玄！”
　　李玄霸差点被口水呛到。
　　房乔和杜如晦都忍俊不禁。
　　李世民摆摆手：“行了，你预言中的事多半不会发生，但跳舞可以有。无论东突厥还是西突厥，听说他们都挺会跳舞。阿玄，交给你了，争取让东突厥和西突厥两败俱伤。我当皇帝后，御驾亲征把两个突厥都灭了。”
　　李玄霸道：“东突厥和西突厥灭亡之后，唐朝的经济和科技水平都无法管辖太远的国土，导致了突厥原领地的权力真空，让突厥势力复兴，和回纥国、吐蕃国的崛起。等打败东西突厥后，最好别一口气灭了，把他们分散成几十个小国才更符合大唐的利益，就像是汉朝的推恩令一样。”
　　李世民道：“我也是这么想。等先灭了西突厥和东突厥再说吧。阿玄，要不要等长孙四郎来了再一起去？”
　　李玄霸道：“不用。我离开后，维护包括回纥在内的铁勒诸多部落的关系，就交给长孙四郎。二哥你抓紧时间练兵，最好有机会就找借口和东突厥、吐谷浑残部打仗。没有武力，所有计谋都是空谈。”
　　李世民笑道：“我知道我知道，我才是最重要的，哈哈哈哈哈。”
　　李玄霸点头：“没错，你才是最重要的。”
　　李世民笑声一滞，尴尬地摸了摸鼻子：“阿玄，你还是否认吧。”
　　见到李世民居然会尴尬，这下轮到李玄霸、房乔和杜如晦笑了。
　　计划订下。
　　李世民的负担极重，要一边练兵抽空打仗，一边和房乔、杜如晦一起处理内政吏治，一边维护和铁勒部落的关系。
　　待房乔和杜如晦理顺河西之地的情况之后，李世民才能放手具体的内政吏治事务，只做最后批复拍板；待姗姗来迟的长孙无忌赶到时，李世民才能进一步从琐事中脱身，真正成为“大领导”。
　　现在李世民还要招揽属官，琢磨诏令，这些工作本预定是魏徵或者薛收来干，但这两人归来的时间都遥遥无期，只能李世民自己绞尽脑汁奋笔疾书。
　　李世民叹气：“薛收究竟要在倭国停留多久？他干什么了？薛老师都在信中担心他的安全了。”
　　房乔道：“我路过大兴拜访薛公时，薛公说薛伯褒再不回来，就推荐族侄薛元敬或者薛德音来辅佐你，抢了薛伯褒的位置。”
　　薛元敬、薛德音和薛收是薛氏最厉害的三位族人，都是少年天才，并称“河东三凤”。薛元敬和薛收都跟随李世民，薛德音眼瞎跟了王世充被杀。
　　李玄霸眼眸微动。
　　这一世薛家最有声望的薛道衡没死，坚定不移地站在二哥这边，薛德音如果再眼瞎，那真是活该了。
　　说到底，薛德音怎么能眼瞎到选王世充啊，哪怕选窦建德都行啊。
　　不过薛德音出身“关中郡姓”的河东薛氏，大概是看不起窦建德的平民出身吧。
　　至于不选二哥也很正常。“河东三凤”中的薛元敬和薛收都投奔二哥，他或许认为自己在二哥那里得不到重视。
　　事实上估计也是如此。二哥的眼神很毒辣，对早逝的薛收最为器重直言其可为相，对薛元敬虽信任但只是让其掌文书工作。薛德音擅长的也是文书工作，肯定比不过薛元敬。
　　希望薛德音这次别头昏，不被重用也比掉脑袋强。二哥将来砍掉好友薛收族兄的脑袋时一定会很很为难。
　　李玄霸在心中假惺惺地给薛德音掉了几滴鳄鱼眼泪，并用心声告诉了二哥，薛德音可能会被二哥砍脑袋的未来。
　　李世民狠狠翻了个白眼：【呸！】
　　他才不会自己砍，真的要砍就先支开薛收，把这个差事推给别人。
　　而且薛老师还活着，说不准他和父亲求情几句，薛德音就不必死了。
　　李玄霸在心音中提起了薛德音的死，让李世民联想到了杜如晦的叔父。
　　李世民对李玄霸道：“对了，克明已经知道你会谶纬，他叔父和兄弟的事可能会在未来发生的纠葛是不是该告诉他了？”
　　“哦，对。”李玄霸一拍脑门。
　　还是二哥心细。他事情太多，都差点忘记了。
　　杜如晦心头一紧：“不会我叔父真的对我长兄和幼弟……”
　　李世民道：“你猜对了。你叔父杜淹投奔王世充后，让王世充杀了你兄长，并囚禁你幼弟。”
　　杜如晦破口大骂：“我兄长在家中就已经对他多番忍让！他居然残害子侄？禽兽不如！”
　　李玄霸道：“杜淹乃是继室所生，你父亲虽去世，兄长是家中嫡长，继承家中所有财产和人脉。他与其母自然不忿，想杀你们很久了。剩下的我单独和你说。”
　　李世民道：“去吧。克明，你放心，阿玄的口风很严，他单独告诉你的事，连我都不会告诉。玄龄也是，不用担心他有谶纬之能后会对我透露过多你们的隐私。”
　　房乔道：“我相信他。”
　　杜如晦拉着李玄霸往外走：“我也相信李三。”
　　等杜如晦和李玄霸离开后，李世民对房乔道：“阿玄说，杜淹投奔王世充，本按罪当诛，将来他弟弟会以‘同族之人相残太悲哀’劝说克明援救杜淹，克明只能同意。你将来还会因为杜淹有才，让我招揽他。”
　　房乔平静道：“公是公，私是私。杜淹按罪当诛，岂能因为杜克明私情就获救？这岂不是拿国法当儿戏？谶纬是谶纬，现实是现实。”
　　李世民笑道：“我也如此想。杜淹即使再有才干，这样的品德我不放心用。”
　　李世民的笑声微冷：“不为被害死的兄长伤心，反倒同情杀人的杜淹，克明的幼弟也不是什么好人。”
　　房乔颔首赞同。
　　他心想，以主公对大德和李五郎的爱护，杜克明幼弟对护着他的兄长如此冷漠，主公肯定厌恶至极。这人以后是难以入仕了。
　　杜如晦把李玄霸拉到一边后，道：“有什么是连李二都不能听的？”
　　李玄霸道：“王世充战败后，杜淹按罪当诛。你幼弟杜楚客以你兄长已经被杀了，所以不能杀你叔父，否则同门相残太悲哀为由，逼迫你为杜淹求情。”
　　杜如晦骂道：“杜淹按罪当诛，和我同门相残是什么关系？他岂不是说杜淹无辜，是我陷害？”
　　杜如晦气得背着手来回走了几圈，然后继续骂道：“兄长对他无微不至，我看只有兄长被杀，他还活着，定也有兄长之功。他不思报仇，却想着用这件事搏名声？他究竟是我和兄长的胞弟，还是杜淹的儿子？这为了名声无所不用其极的手段，怎么和杜淹一模一样！”
　　杜淹就是为了名声无所不用其极，故意装隐士等隋文帝征召。隋文帝识破，厌恶至极，将其流放江南，花了好大劲才返回大兴。
　　李玄霸道：“你一眼就识破了他是踩着你和你兄长扬名，倒是很敏锐。”
　　杜如晦苦笑：“若我遇见这件事，即使识破又如何？只能按照他的谋划做。”
　　杜楚客不仅是杜如晦的弟弟，还是“受害人”之一。他都这么说了，杜如晦若不做，就是坐实了杜楚客“杜如晦为报仇陷害杜淹”的事。杜如晦的名声就受损了。
　　如今“家族”十分重要，京兆杜氏又是高门大族，杜如晦不可能不受名声所累，维护“家族”脸面。
　　李玄霸淡漠道：“他劝说你的理由是‘骨肉相残太过悲哀’，但却怂恿二哥次子夺嫡。”
　　杜如晦呼吸一滞，面色一僵。
　　李玄霸讥笑：“虽然二哥的太子后来很荒诞，但他怂恿二哥次子夺嫡的时候，太子还很完美。夺嫡必定伴随骨肉相残，说好的‘骨肉相残太过悲哀’呢？”
　　杜如晦双手攥紧，指甲紧紧镶嵌进手心：“他的结局呢？”
　　李玄霸继续淡漠道：“杜楚客帮魏王夺嫡被贬，一生只是个县令；你次子是二哥女婿，却帮太子谋反，坐罪伏诛，牵连你长子流放岭南；三子没被牵连，虽爵位断了，但将你这一脉顺利延续了下去，仍旧是官宦世家。”
　　杜如晦苦涩道：“主公看在了我的面上，才会如此处理。”
　　李玄霸道：“是啊，谋反都没有牵连你全家。”
　　杜如晦哽咽：“是我无能，教子无方，伤了主公的心。”
　　李玄霸道：“是你早逝，教子不能，导致家门不幸。好好养生，你若活着，杜荷岂敢谋反？对了，杜荷出生没？”
　　杜如晦深呼吸，松开紧握的拳头：”还没。”
　　李玄霸道：“等你次子出生，改个名？”
　　杜如晦故作轻松道：“好主意。”
　　李玄霸没再说话，让杜如晦缓和情绪。
　　半晌，杜如晦神色如常：“怪不得你不告诉主公。”
　　李玄霸道：“我不告诉二哥，不是担心他因你儿子的事迁怒你，而是不想让他过早伤心。”
　　虽然他早早给二哥打了预防针，告诉二哥他未来的太子会变成一个“精神小伙”，但“谋反”和“最爱的两个儿子手足相残”这种事，还是晚点告诉二哥吧。
　　二哥才十四岁，现在就知道这么残忍的事，也太惨了。
　　杜如晦道：“你说得对，他还年少，别给他心里增加太多负担。而且有你在，未来必不会这样。”
　　李玄霸道：“或许吧。缓过劲了？回去？”
　　杜如晦道：“好。”
　　两人回到屋内，李世民正和房乔商议招揽人才的事。
　　见两人回来，李世民抬头：“说完了？克明，你干脆把你兄长也叫来，留你叔父和幼弟两人在一起蛊斗。”
　　“什么蛊斗？李二你会不会说话？”杜如晦黑线，“我会让兄长带杜楚客回大兴。”
　　杜淹和他的兄长都在朝中任职，所以住在洛阳。杜楚客年少，为兄长所养，也住在洛阳。
　　只要避开杜淹，他的兄弟就不会被谋害。
　　李世民问道：“杜楚客你如何处理？”
　　杜如晦道：“长兄如父，兄长在，杜楚客不敢乱来。我和兄长皆在朝中为高官，一家不能出三个高官，他就赋闲在家吧。”
　　李世民笑道：“你对兄长如此推崇，将来记得介绍给我。不过你在朝中为宰相，你兄长就只能外放。他可擅长治理地方？”
　　杜如晦的语气中露出淡淡的自负：“一郡一州之事，轻而易举。”
　　李世民道：“那就这么定了。好了，这件事揭过，赶紧过来帮我一起头疼。可恶啊！我都有‘天下无敌’的名号了，怎么士人还是不肯来投我！”
　　李玄霸慢悠悠道：“是‘战无不胜’，不是‘天下无敌’。谁让你才十四岁？”
　　李世民道：“‘战无不胜’和‘天下无敌’别区别。可恶啊！莫欺少年穷！将来有的是他们后悔！”
　　李玄霸刚说了太多话，正捧着水喝，一口喷到了二哥头上。
　　李世民抹脸：“阿玄，你干嘛？呛到了？”
　　李玄霸：【不，我只是想到了后世的一个笑话，“三十年河东三十年河西，莫欺少年穷，莫欺中年穷，莫欺老年穷，死者为大”。】
　　李世民摸出手帕擦脸的手一顿，将帕子团成一团朝李玄霸砸去。
　　房乔伸手接住帕子：“好了好了，你们兄弟二人要吵，等说完正事再吵。先干正事。”
　　李世民吓唬道：“等会儿收拾你！”
　　李玄霸耸肩。怕你不成。
　　杜如晦被李世民和李玄霸兄弟打闹的欢快感染，心头阴霾散去不少。
　　他想，李三比以前更爱惹李二“生气”了，这是李三所说的“中二期”到了？
　　十月，西突厥射匮可汗同意与李玄霸在伊吾郡相会。
　　伊吾郡在西突厥和大隋的交界处。虽十一月天寒地冻，但张掖到伊吾郡会穿越沙漠，气候干燥，没有大雪封路，只要做好保暖，就能安全到达。
　　大业四年（公元608年），左翊卫将军薛世雄便是在十月率军横跨沙漠，逼降伊吾城。
　　李玄霸准备了充足的炭火和物资，前往伊吾城与射匮可汗会谈。
　　说是秘密前往，但李玄霸都懒得假装商队。西域这一块几乎已经和中原完全失联，消息不经过虎贲郎将李某某传递，根本到不了中原。他就大摇大摆地领着一众兵卒去了。
　　李玄霸刚走半月，长孙无忌就匆匆到来。
　　听到李玄霸没等他时，长孙无忌十分不满，骂李玄霸不够朋友，居然不带他一起去。
　　李世民给他塞了一堆活干，长孙无忌才闭嘴。
　　长孙无忌的到来，带来了中原最新的消息：“陛下的病情好转，已经回到洛阳。太子在陛下重病期间饮酒作乐，被陛下解除所有职位，勒令闭门反省。”
　　李世民叹气道：“二表兄危险了。”
　　他想起二表兄给他和阿玄写的信。
　　杨暕在信中说，大表兄临终前的担忧成真，他心中悲愤，却又无可奈何。
　　杨暕只是在信中一通抱怨，没有说自己将如何应对，也没有向李世民和李玄霸请求什么。
　　他只是……抱怨而已。
　　李世民看出杨暕不想牵连他和弟弟，不由心酸。
　　他下定决心，将来竭尽全力从父亲手中保住二表兄的子嗣。
　　而二表兄的命运，他就无能为力了。
　　长孙无忌道：“太子表现很谦虚恭顺，熬过这一劫，应当无事。”
　　李世民摇头：“只要皇帝开始忌惮太子，无论太子是桀骜还是恭顺，都会加深他的厌恶。当初张衡便是如此。”
　　长孙无忌一愣，然后叹气：“皇帝病愈后，应该会恢复理性。”
　　李世民无奈：“四郎啊四郎，你当着我的面，还遮遮掩掩什么？爽快些。”
　　长孙无忌无语。我爽快什么？爽快地说皇帝坏话？

Chapter 115: The Double Standards of Fratricide

Once Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui arrived in Zhangye, Li Xuanba was finally able to free up his hands to do what he did best.

To be honest, internal affairs and civil administration were not Li Xuanba’s forte. In his previous life, he had never even been a civil servant and knew nothing about bureaucratic systems; he could only force his experience as an e-commerce merchant to fit the mold.

Although he had the guidance of Gao Jiong and Yuwenshu, Li Xuanba’s abilities in this area were already beyond the average person, but compared to true geniuses like Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui, he still fell short.

Moreover, Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui possessed the "combined skill" of "Fang’s Schemes and Du’s Decisions."

Because of the chaos in the Central Plains, Yang Guang was currently unable to spare anyone to take up the post of Governor of Xihai Commandery. As the Huben Langjiang (Tiger-Brave General) who had conquered Xihai, Li Shimin, in accordance with wartime rules, served as the acting Governor of Xihai Commandery.

The Governor of Zhangye Commandery seemed to have sensed something; he subtly signaled his allegiance and took the initiative to become a mere figurehead.

Although the title of "Huben Langjiang" had been changed from "General" to "Langjiang," the position theoretically held the power to establish an independent office. Now that the world was in turmoil, let alone a Huben Langjiang, even the Yingyang Langjiangs had begun appointing their own subordinate officials. Naturally, Li Shimin was also qualified to appoint his own staff.

The internal affairs and civil administration of Zhangye and Xihai Commanderies were thus handed over to Li Shimin’s subordinates, Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui.
