Xihai and Zhangye Commanderies happened to lie on the north and south sides of the Qilian Mountains, accessible by crossing the range.

If one did not cross the mountains, traveling from Zhangye to Xihai required following the Hexi Corridor along the Qilian Mountains, first heading southeast through Wuwei and Xiping Commanderies, then turning west toward Xihai. The four commanderies formed a ">" shape.

These four commanderies were all vital military strongholds, each equipped with an Yingyang Office. As a Huben Langjiang, Li Shimin was the direct superior of the Yingyang Langjiangs in these four commanderies.

In the future, Li Gui, the Yingyang Langjiang of Wuwei, would kill the Huben Langjiang from the original timeline to rebel, take the Hexi region into his own hands, and proclaim himself the King of Daliang.

Li Xuanba did not tell his Second Brother, Fang Qiao, or Du Ruhui about this future, so as not to interfere with their judgment.

He believed that his Second Brother was already the nominal supreme military leader of the Hexi region, and that "Fang’s Schemes and Du’s Decisions" would surely be able to easily bring the Hexi region under his Second Brother’s control without him needing to say anything.

After receiving the information on the Hexi region that Li Xuanba had collected during this time, Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui felt quite relaxed.

They were clearly very confident and quickly set about turning the Hexi region into Li Shimin’s power base.

Fang Qiao guaranteed, "Never mind the Hexi region; even Dunhuang Commandery and the more distant Yiwu Commandery are already within your grasp, my Lord."

Du Ruhui said lazily, "If Old Fang and I couldn't even manage this, what kind of Prime Ministers would we be? We might as well hand the jobs over to Xue Shou and Wei Zheng."

Li Shimin was amused: "Why are you calling them by their full names? Xue Shou’s courtesy name is Bobao, and Wei Zheng’s is Xuancheng. Don't go around calling them whatever you want."

Du Ruhui spread his hands: "My memory isn't very good."

Li Shimin laughed so hard he couldn't straighten his back, constantly patting Li Xuanba’s arm: "Hahahaha, Axuan, you're killing me."

Li Xuanba dodged his Second Brother’s slaps with disdain. What was so funny? He had issues.

Fang Qiao coughed dryly and changed the subject: "Internal affairs and administration are left to us, Dade. What will you be doing? Logistics?"

Li Xuanba said, "I will be in charge of military logistics in the future, but for now, Second Brother will handle those tasks himself. I am going to serve as an envoy to the Western Turkic Khaganate."

Fang Qiao was shocked: "You're going alone?"

Du Ruhui looked at Li Shimin and frowned: "I disagree. It's too dangerous."

Li Shimin sighed: "Do you think I want to agree? But Axuan says only he can persuade the Western Turkic Khagan to send troops against the Eastern Turkic Khaganate, and I have no choice. I would like to go with him, but he says I need to hold down the fort in Zhangye."

Li Shimin sighed heavily several times and continued: "Since he has already made up his mind, I trust him. I will have Zhou Da and Luo Shixin serve as Axuan’s guards together."

Fang Qiao asked, "Dade, why do you suddenly want to ally with the Western Turks? Are you worried that the Eastern Turks are getting too close to the Great Sui?"

Li Xuanba shook his head: "Quite the opposite. The Shibi Khagan of the Eastern Turks already harbors rebellious intentions against the Great Sui; he will take advantage of the Sui’s decline to grow stronger."

Li Xuanba sneered and said, "Every person who proclaimed themselves emperor or king at the end of the Sui and beginning of the Tang bowed to the Shibi Khagan, including the Great Tang."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui’s expressions changed drastically.

They looked at Li Shimin.

Li Shimin shrugged: "Although I would like to say that the Gaozu of Tang must be my father, and that bowing to the Eastern Turks has nothing to do with me, as I haven't even reached the age of twenty, knowing my father's character, he wouldn't have done such a thing unless the situation was dire. This was a choice made by the entire Tang imperial court. Father truly suffered such humiliation."

Li Xuanba said, "It doesn't matter, Second Brother. The Eastern Turks arrived at the Wei River the month you ascended the throne. You were also quite humiliated."

Li Shimin pressed Li Xuanba down and put him in a cross-lock, causing Li Xuanba to howl, "Axuan, shut up!"

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui shook their heads repeatedly.

Fang Qiao said, "Let's not talk about the future; it will change anyway."

Du Ruhui added, "With Li Er’s character, he will surely retaliate soon enough. Why dwell on such a small humiliation?"

Li Shimin released his detestable younger brother and said, "That's right! Axuan, hurry up and tell me how I retaliated in your vision."

Li Xuanba rubbed his arm and said, "In the fourth year of Zhenguan, you destroyed the Eastern Turks and captured the Jieli Khagan, forcing him to dance in public at Chang'an."

Li Shimin whistled: "Whoa."

Fang Qiao stroked his beard: "Not bad."

Du Ruhui laughed heartily: "Acceptable, very acceptable."

Li Shimin asked excitedly, "Did I lead the army in person?"

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes: "What are you thinking? Once you're Emperor, how would you have the chance to lead a campaign in person? Just stay in Chang'an and handle your logistics obediently."

Li Shimin nodded: "Understood. You stay in Chang'an and handle the logistics obediently, and I will lead the campaign in person. My glory in destroying a nation depends on you, Axuan!"

Li Xuanba nearly choked on his own saliva.

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui couldn't help but chuckle.

Li Shimin waved his hand: "Alright, most of the things in your prophecies won't happen, but the dancing can stay. Whether it's the Eastern or Western Turks, I hear they are quite good at dancing. Axuan, I leave it to you. Try to make the Eastern and Western Turks suffer mutual destruction. After I become Emperor, I will lead the campaign myself and wipe out both Turkic tribes."

Li Xuanba said, "After the Eastern and Western Turks are destroyed, the Tang Dynasty’s economy and technology won't be able to govern such distant territories, which will lead to a power vacuum in the former Turkic lands, allowing for the resurgence of Turkic forces and the rise of the Uyghur and Tibetan kingdoms. Once you defeat the Eastern and Western Turks, it's best not to wipe them out in one go. Splitting them into dozens of small states would better serve the interests of the Great Tang, much like the 'Order of Favor' (Tui'en Ling) of the Han Dynasty."

Li Shimin said, "That is what I was thinking, too. Let's wait until we've destroyed the Western and Eastern Turks first. Axuan, do you want to wait for Changsun Silang to arrive before going together?"

Li Xuanba said, "No need. After I leave, maintaining relations with the various Tiele tribes, including the Uyghurs, will be left to Changsun Silang. Second Brother, you must hurry up and train your troops. It's best to find excuses to fight the Eastern Turks and the remnants of the Tuyuhun whenever you have the chance. Without military force, all strategies are just empty talk."

Li Shimin laughed: "I know, I know. I am the most important one, hahahahaha."

Li Xuanba nodded: "That's right, you are the most important one."

Li Shimin’s laughter stalled, and he rubbed his nose awkwardly: "Axuan, you should just deny it."

Seeing Li Shimin actually feel awkward, it was now Li Xuanba, Fang Qiao, and Du Ruhui’s turn to laugh.

The plan was set.

Li Shimin’s burden was extremely heavy: he had to train troops and find time to fight, handle internal affairs and administration with Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui, and maintain relations with the Tiele tribes.

Only after Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui smoothed out the situation in the Hexi region could Li Shimin let go of the specific administrative tasks and only provide final approvals; only when the late-arriving Changsun Wuji arrived could Li Shimin further free himself from trivial matters and truly become the "Big Leader."

For now, Li Shimin still had to recruit subordinates and ponder over edicts. These tasks were originally intended for Wei Zheng or Xue Shou, but since the return of both men was nowhere in sight, Li Shimin had to rack his brains and write everything himself.

Li Shimin sighed: "How long is Xue Shou going to stay in Wa (Japan)? What is he doing? Even Master Xue is worried about his safety in his letters."

Fang Qiao said, "When I passed through Daxing to visit Master Xue, he said that if Xue Bobao doesn't return soon, he will recommend his nephew Xue Yuanjing or Xue Deyin to assist you, stealing Xue Bobao’s position."

Xue Yuanjing, Xue Deyin, and Xue Shou were the three most brilliant members of the Xue clan, all young geniuses known as the "Three Phoenixes of Hedong." Xue Yuanjing and Xue Shou both followed Li Shimin, while Xue Deyin was blind enough to follow Wang Shichu and get himself killed.

Li Xuanba’s eyes flickered.

In this life, the most prestigious member of the Xue family, Xue Daoheng, was still alive and stood firmly on his Second Brother’s side. If Xue Deyin were to be blind again, he would truly deserve it.

When it came down to it, how could Xue Deyin be so blind as to choose Wang Shichu? Even choosing Dou Jiande would have been better.

However, Xue Deyin came from the "Guanzhong Commandery" branch of the Hedong Xue clan; he probably looked down on Dou Jiande’s commoner background.

As for not choosing his Second Brother, that was also normal. Among the "Three Phoenixes of Hedong," Xue Yuanjing and Xue Shou had both defected to his Second Brother; he perhaps felt he wouldn't be valued there.

In fact, that was likely the case. His Second Brother had a sharp eye; he valued the late Xue Shou the most, stating he could be a Prime Minister, while he trusted Xue Yuanjing but only let him handle clerical work. Xue Deyin was also skilled in clerical work and certainly couldn't compare to Xue Yuanjing.

He hoped Xue Deyin wouldn't be foolish this time. Not being valued was still better than losing his head. His Second Brother would surely be in a difficult position when he had to cut off the head of his good friend Xue Shou’s cousin in the future.

Li Xuanba shed a few crocodile tears for Xue Deyin in his heart and told his Second Brother through his inner voice about the future where Xue Deyin might be executed by him.

Li Shimin rolled his eyes fiercely: [Pah!]

He wouldn't do the beheading himself. If it really had to be done, he would send Xue Shou away first and push the task onto someone else.

Besides, Master Xue was still alive; perhaps if he pleaded with their father, Xue Deyin wouldn't have to die.

Li Xuanba mentioned Xue Deyin’s death in his inner voice, which made Li Shimin think of Du Ruhui’s uncle.

Li Shimin said to Li Xuanba, "By the way, Keming already knows you can perform prophecy. Should we tell him about the potential future entanglements involving his uncle and brothers?"

"Oh, right." Li Xuanba slapped his forehead.

His Second Brother was indeed thoughtful. He had too many things on his mind and had almost forgotten.

Du Ruhui’s heart tightened: "Could it be that my uncle really will... to my eldest brother and younger brother?"

Li Shimin said, "You guessed right. After your uncle Du Yan defected to Wang Shichu, he had Wang Shichu kill your eldest brother and imprison your younger brother."

Du Ruhui cursed: "My eldest brother had already shown him great forbearance at home! He actually harmed his own nephews? He is no better than a beast!"

Li Xuanba said, "Du Yan was born to a second wife. Although your father passed away, your eldest brother was the legitimate heir and inherited all the family’s wealth and connections. He and his mother were naturally resentful and had wanted to kill you all for a long time. I will tell you the rest in private."

Li Shimin said, "Go ahead. Keming, rest assured, Axuan is very tight-lipped. What he tells you in private, even I won't be told. The same goes for Xuanling; don't worry that he will reveal too much of your privacy to me after gaining the power of prophecy."

Fang Qiao said, "I trust him."

Du Ruhui pulled Li Xuanba away: "I also trust Li San."

After Du Ruhui and Li Xuanba left, Li Shimin said to Fang Qiao, "Axuan said that Du Yan defected to Wang Shichu and should have been executed for his crimes. In the future, his younger brother will persuade Keming to save Du Yan on the grounds that 'it is too sad for kinsmen to kill each other,' and Keming will have no choice but to agree. You will also suggest that I recruit him in the future because Du Yan is talented."

Fang Qiao said calmly, "Public is public, private is private. Du Yan deserves to die for his crimes; how can he be saved because of Du Keming’s personal feelings? Wouldn't that be treating national law as a child's play? Prophecy is prophecy, reality is reality."

Li Shimin laughed: "I think so too. Even if Du Yan is talented, I cannot trust such character."

Li Shimin’s laughter turned cold: "Not grieving for the brother who was murdered, but instead sympathizing with the murderous Du Yan—Keming’s younger brother is not a good person either."

Fang Qiao nodded in agreement.

He thought to himself that given his Lord’s affection for Dade and Li Wulang, his Lord would surely despise Du Keming’s younger brother for being so cold to the brother who had protected him. It would be difficult for this person to enter officialdom in the future.

After Du Ruhui pulled Li Xuanba aside, he asked, "What is it that even Li Er cannot hear?"

Li Xuanba said, "After Wang Shichu is defeated, Du Yan will be sentenced to death for his crimes. Your younger brother, Du Chuke, will force you to plead for Du Yan on the grounds that your eldest brother has already been killed, so killing your uncle would be too tragic for the family."

Du Ruhui cursed: "Du Yan deserves to die; what does that have to do with kinsmen killing each other? Isn't he saying that Du Yan is innocent and that I am framing him?"

Du Ruhui was so angry that he paced back and forth with his hands behind his back, then continued to curse: "My eldest brother treated him with the utmost care. I see that only my eldest brother was killed while he survived; surely my eldest brother’s efforts were involved. Instead of thinking of revenge, he wants to use this to build a reputation? Is he my and my eldest brother’s biological brother, or is he Du Yan’s son? This unscrupulous method of doing anything for fame is exactly the same as Du Yan’s!"

Du Yan was indeed someone who would do anything for fame, deliberately pretending to be a hermit to wait for Emperor Wen of Sui to summon him. Emperor Wen saw through it and, disgusted, exiled him to the south; it took a great deal of effort for him to return to Daxing.

Li Xuanba said, "You saw through the fact that he was using you and your brother to build his own fame at a glance; you are quite sharp."

Du Ruhui smiled bitterly: "If I encounter this, even if I see through it, what can I do? I can only do as he plans."

Du Chuke was not only Du Ruhui’s brother but also one of the "victims." Since he had said so, if Du Ruhui did not comply, it would confirm Du Chuke’s claim that "Du Ruhui framed Du Yan to avenge his brother." Du Ruhui’s reputation would be damaged.

Nowadays, "family" was extremely important, and the Jingzhao Du clan was a high-ranking noble family. Du Ruhui could not afford to be burdened by his reputation and had to maintain the "family" face.

Li Xuanba said indifferently, "His reason for persuading you was that 'it is too sad for kinsmen to kill each other,' yet he incited your Second Brother’s second son to seize the throne."

Du Ruhui’s breathing hitched, and his expression stiffened.

Li Xuanba mocked: "Although your Second Brother’s Crown Prince later became absurd, when he incited your Second Brother’s second son to seize the throne, the Crown Prince was still perfect. Seizing the throne is bound to be accompanied by kinsmen killing each other. What happened to 'it is too sad for kinsmen to kill each other'?"

Du Ruhui clenched his hands, his nails digging into his palms: "What was his ending?"

Li Xuanba continued indifferently, "Du Chuke was demoted for helping the Prince of Wei seize the throne and spent his life as a mere county magistrate; your second son was your Second Brother’s son-in-law, but he helped the Crown Prince rebel and was executed, implicating your eldest son in exile to Lingnan; your third son was not implicated, and although his title was lost, he successfully continued your lineage and remained an official family."

Du Ruhui said bitterly, "My Lord must have looked at my face to handle it this way."

Li Xuanba said, "Yes, even the rebellion didn't implicate your whole family."

Du Ruhui choked with sobs: "It is my incompetence; I failed to teach my children well and hurt my Lord’s heart."

Li Xuanba said, "It was because you died young and couldn't teach your children, leading to family misfortune. Take good care of your health. If you were alive, would Du He dare to rebel? By the way, is Du He born yet?"

Du Ruhui took a deep breath and unclenched his fists: "Not yet."

Li Xuanba said, "When your second son is born, how about changing his name?"

Du Ruhui feigned relaxation: "Good idea."

Li Xuanba said nothing more, letting Du Ruhui calm his emotions.

After a long while, Du Ruhui’s expression returned to normal: "No wonder you didn't tell my Lord."

Li Xuanba said, "I didn't tell Second Brother, not because I was worried he would take his anger out on you because of your son’s affairs, but because I didn't want him to be sad too early."

Although he had given his Second Brother a vaccination early on, telling him that his future Crown Prince would become a "delusional youth," things like "rebellion" and "the two most beloved sons killing each other" were better told to his Second Brother later.

His Second Brother was only fourteen; knowing such cruel things now would be too miserable.

Du Ruhui said, "You are right. He is still young; don't add too much burden to his heart. Besides, with you here, the future will surely not be like this."

Li Xuanba said, "Perhaps. Have you recovered? Shall we go back?"

Du Ruhui said, "Alright."

The two returned to the room, where Li Shimin was discussing the recruitment of talent with Fang Qiao.

Seeing them return, Li Shimin looked up: "Finished? Keming, why don't you just call your eldest brother over and leave your uncle and younger brother together to fight like poisonous insects?"

"What poisonous insects? Can you even speak properly, Li Er?" Du Ruhui’s face darkened. "I will have my eldest brother take Du Chuke back to Daxing."

Du Yan and his eldest brother both served in the court, so they lived in Luoyang. Du Chuke was young and raised by his eldest brother, so he also lived in Luoyang.

As long as he avoided Du Yan, his brothers would not be murdered.

Li Shimin asked, "How will you handle Du Chuke?"

Du Ruhui said, "The eldest brother is like a father. With my eldest brother there, Du Chuke will not dare to act recklessly. My eldest brother and I are both high-ranking officials in the court; one family cannot have three high-ranking officials, so he will just stay at home."

Li Shimin laughed: "You hold your eldest brother in such high regard; remember to introduce him to me in the future. However, since you are a Prime Minister in the court, your eldest brother can only be sent to a local post. Is he skilled in local governance?"

Du Ruhui’s tone revealed a faint arrogance: "Managing a commandery or a prefecture is easy for him."

Li Shimin said, "Then it's settled. Alright, let’s move past this; hurry over and help me with this headache. Damn it! I already have the title of 'Invincible under Heaven,' so why are scholars still unwilling to join me!"

Li Xuanba said slowly, "It's 'Unbeaten in Battle,' not 'Invincible under Heaven.' Who told you that you're only fourteen?"

Li Shimin said, "There's no difference between 'Unbeaten in Battle' and 'Invincible under Heaven.' Damn it! Don't bully the young because they are poor! They will regret it in the future!"

Li Xuanba had just said too much and was holding water to drink; he sprayed a mouthful onto his Second Brother’s head.

Li Shimin wiped his face: "Axuan, what are you doing? Did you choke?"

Li Xuanba: [No, I just thought of a joke from later generations: "Thirty years east of the river, thirty years west of the river; don't bully the young because they are poor, don't bully the middle-aged because they are poor, don't bully the old because they are poor; the dead are the greatest."]

Li Shimin’s hand, which was wiping his face with a handkerchief, paused. He balled the handkerchief up and threw it at Li Xuanba.

Fang Qiao reached out and caught the handkerchief: "Alright, alright. If you two brothers want to argue, wait until we've finished the business. Let's do the work first."

Li Shimin threatened: "I'll deal with you later!"

Li Xuanba shrugged. As if I'm afraid of you.

Du Ruhui was infected by the cheerful bickering of the Li brothers, and the gloom in his heart dissipated quite a bit.

He thought to himself that Li San was more fond of making Li Er "angry" than before; was this the "middle-school phase" Li San spoke of?

In October, the Shigui Khagan of the Western Turks agreed to meet Li Xuanba in Yiwu Commandery.

Yiwu Commandery was on the border between the Western Turks and the Great Sui. Although it was freezing in November, traveling from Zhangye to Yiwu Commandery meant crossing the desert. The climate was dry, and there was no heavy snow to block the road; as long as they kept warm, they could arrive safely.

In the fourth year of Daye (608 AD), General Xue Shixiong of the Left Yi Guard had led his army across the desert in October to force the surrender of Yiwu City.

Li Xuanba prepared sufficient charcoal and supplies to go to Yiwu City for talks with the Shigui Khagan.

It was said to be a secret trip, but Li Xuanba was too lazy to pretend to be a merchant caravan. This part of the Western Regions had almost completely lost contact with the Central Plains; news could not reach the Central Plains without passing through the Huben Langjiang, Li So-and-so. He swaggered off with a group of soldiers.

Li Xuanba had only been gone for half a month when Changsun Wuji arrived in a hurry.

Hearing that Li Xuanba hadn't waited for him, Changsun Wuji was very dissatisfied, cursing Li Xuanba for not being a good friend and not bringing him along.

Li Shimin stuffed a pile of work into his hands, and Changsun Wuji finally shut up.

Changsun Wuji’s arrival brought the latest news from the Central Plains: "His Majesty’s illness has improved, and he has returned to Luoyang. During His Majesty’s serious illness, the Crown Prince drank and made merry, so he was stripped of all his positions and ordered to reflect in seclusion."

Li Shimin sighed: "Second Cousin is in danger."

He remembered the letters his Second Cousin had written to him and Axuan.

Yang Jian said in his letter that the worries his eldest cousin had before he died had come true; he felt indignant but helpless.

Yang Jian only complained in the letter, did not say how he would respond, and did not ask Li Shimin or Li Xuanba for anything.

He was just... complaining.

Li Shimin could see that Yang Jian did not want to implicate him and his brother, and he felt a pang of sorrow.

He made up his mind that in the future, he would do his best to protect his Second Cousin’s offspring from his father.

As for his Second Cousin’s fate, he was powerless.

Changsun Wuji said, "The Crown Prince is acting very humble and submissive; if he survives this ordeal, he should be fine."

Li Shimin shook his head: "As long as the Emperor begins to fear the Crown Prince, no matter if the Crown Prince is arrogant or submissive, it will only deepen his disgust. That was the case with Zhang Heng back then."

Changsun Wuji was stunned, then sighed: "After the Emperor recovers, he should regain his rationality."

Li Shimin was helpless: "Silang, oh Silang, why are you still being evasive in front of me? Be straightforward."

Changsun Wuji was speechless. What should I be straightforward about? Straightforwardly speaking ill of the Emperor?

chunks.chapterTitle: 第116章 太宗黑毕生事业 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第116章 太宗黑毕生事业

长孙无忌本就有理政的天赋， 除了容易飘，其他没什么大问题。

至于他不爱进谏，喜欢顺着大领导的话奉承， 在李世民这里也不是什么缺点。

毕竟， 现在李世民不仅有“镜子”魏徵， 还有一个从小到大对他没几句好话的弟弟李三强，用不着长孙无忌直言进谏。

长孙无忌加入后，李世民肩头重担又松了一点。

他对好友吐槽：“我现在才有了一点当主公的感觉。之前我过的什么日子啊！什么事都是我和阿玄做！阿玄身体又弱， 我不敢给他太多工作，所有细碎的工作全是我一人承担！”

李世民灌了一口酒，继续拍着大腿吐槽：“就没有我这么憋屈的主公！”

长孙无忌安慰道：“好了好了， 我和房玄龄、杜克明不是来了吗？等薛伯褒也来了，你就轻松了。”

杜如晦冷笑：“还有个魏徵。这人能说动百姓义军围困涿郡， 是个人才， 正好适合在天下大乱时派出去当搅风搅雨。”

房乔差点一口茶水喷出来：“克明，你对魏徵……魏玄成的意见究竟有多大？”

杜如晦道：“没意见，我是在夸他。放心，等他到了面前，我就会亲亲热热叫他魏玄成了。”

房乔嘀咕：“这种人后倨傲的态度可不是君子所为。”

杜如晦挑眉：“我说过我是君子吗？”

长孙无忌茫然道：“魏徵魏玄成？那是谁？”

李世民道：“一个很厉害的人， 我们的伙伴，你的同僚。啊， 你居然还不知道？”

长孙无忌心中涌出一股无名火：“我居然还不知道？！”

李世民淡淡道：“哦，忘记告诉你了。小事，小事。”

长孙无忌真想把手中的羊骨头砸妹婿身上。

这是小事？！他微妙地感觉自己被排挤了。不爽！

李世民打着哈哈道：“丈人肯定知道， 他没告诉你吗？那你问丈人去， 为何他不告诉你。”

长孙无忌又生气又憋屈：“别老拿我父亲来压我。”

李世民无奈道：“不是我想拿丈人来压你， 但丈人不仅是我丈人， 还是我老师，我能怎么办？只能听丈人的。”

房乔打圆场：“辅机，这是没办法的事。”

杜如晦道：“可能长孙将军认为你还需要磨砺。不过长孙将军已经同意你来张掖，应当是认为你已经出师，可以独当一面了。”

李世民道：“对，现在你应该可以什么都知道了。对了，你知道阿玄会谶纬吗？”

长孙无忌破口大骂：“我知道个屁！”

李世民大笑：“哈哈哈哈哈。”

房乔和杜如晦也憋不住笑，忙低头喝水掩饰。

长孙无忌更加委屈，终于没忍住，把羊骨头砸向李世民。

李世民侧身躲开，笑得更加猖狂。

长孙无忌撸袖子要和李世民打一架。

房乔想去劝阻，被杜如晦拉住。

杜如晦笑道：“等他们打，看看长孙四郎有没有得到长孙将军的真传。”

房乔叹气：“真是闹腾。”

他叹完气后，看着不顾一手羊油，毫无章法“扭打”起来的李世民和长孙无忌，也不由笑了。

杜如晦挤眉弄眼道：“长孙四郎还是这样顺眼点。”

房乔点头。

之前长孙无忌对主公恭恭敬敬，提前恪守君臣之道，真是让人看着不舒服。

看主公的反应，他应该也不舒服，才会故意刺激长孙无忌。

或许将来从某一天起，他们必须对主公毕恭毕敬谨小慎微。但不是现在。

人总要有年少轻狂时，否则岂不是白活一场？

“不知道大德旅途是否顺利？”房乔道，“他没看到这一幕，一定很遗憾。”

杜如晦得意道：“我不仅会记下来，还会画下来。不过现在他应该已经发现主公给他的惊喜，正跳脚骂人吧。”

房乔失笑：“应该是。”

在房乔和杜如晦嘀咕李玄霸时，李玄霸确实正在跳着脚骂二哥。

他已经到了敦煌郡，补给物资时顺带去逛一逛这一处后世著名旅游胜地。

现在莫高窟已经开凿，成为僧侣和寺庙的聚集地。李玄霸对满天神佛都是随意拜拜，但莫高窟还是值得去膜拜一二。

安排工作时，李玄霸发现队伍里有个小兵有点眼熟。

他心头一梗，让罗士信把那个小兵“抓过来”。

罗士信脸色一变。

李玄霸心头更梗。

李玄霸骂道：“你知道？！故意瞒着我？”

罗士信支支吾吾。

李玄霸气笑了：“赶紧让他过来！”

罗士信叹了口气，把那“小兵”带来。

李智云用手背抹了抹脸上的灰，笑嘻嘻道：“三兄你好笨，现在才发现。”

李玄霸伸手捏住李智云的脸颊：“你怎么在这里？你知道有多危险吗？”

李智云喊着疼道：“二兄说，我长大了，该来历练历练。”

李玄霸骂道：“天寒地冻，路途遥远，如果生病受伤了该如何是好？”

李智云道：“三兄，我身体比你好，你不会生病，我也不会生病。别拧了，弟弟的脸皮要掉了。这是二兄同意了的！”

李玄霸松开手，有气无力道：“为何不提前告诉我？”

李智云揉着脸道：“二兄知道三兄肯定不会同意，所以让我偷偷混进来。”

李玄霸恶狠狠地瞪了一眼东边，嘴里低声咒骂了几句话。

李智云当作自己没有听到三兄骂人。

李玄霸深呼吸了几下，平复心中愤怒：“他还瞒着我做了什么？”

李智云道：“还有一件事，除此之外没什么了。”

李智云伸出手臂，高喊道：“乌镝！”

一声“啾啾”鸟鸣，和叫声完全不相符的威武霸气金雕从空中落下。

李玄霸：“……”

他再次深呼吸，喊道：“寒钩！”

寒钩也从天空落下。

李玄霸握住寒钩的脑袋：“我是说你最近食量怎么这么大，还以为你因为寒冷想要长膘。你早知道了？”

寒钩缩了缩脖子。

乌镝得意洋洋拍动了两下翅膀。

李玄霸十分无力：“士信，你也知道？”

罗士信垂着头。

周达看不下去，道：“其实我也知道，这是郎君的命令。”

李玄霸磨牙：“是是是，都瞒着我！”

李玄霸离开之后，李世民会继续伺机出战，一边练兵，一边扩大影响力。

所以李玄霸让李世民留一只金雕在身边。从天而降的攻击有时候会有奇效，而且寒钩和乌镝对张掖附近的地形已经很熟悉，可以承担传达军令的责任。

李世民嘴上“好啊好啊”爽快答应，然后不仅悄悄把李智云塞进了李玄霸的队伍，还让乌镝偷偷跟来。

他明知道李玄霸不会同意，所以干脆直接偷偷做了。待木已成舟，他就不信李玄霸还能让李智云和乌镝独自返回。

比起让一人一雕独自返回，李玄霸肯定会认为把这熊孩子熊雕带在身边更安全。

很显然，不仅双生弟弟很了解双生哥哥，双生哥哥想要“算计”双生弟弟也是轻而易举。

物理圣学言，力都是相互的。

李玄霸这次带的人都是李世民亲手安排，由周达和罗士信率领。李玄霸知道自己没有领兵的本事，所以没有插手，直到来到敦煌采购物资时才清点了一下人员。

现在他先打了两只雕的屁股，又敲了李智云的脑袋，然后就无可奈何地继续出发。

不然还能怎么办？

李智云虽然洗掉了脸上的灰，但还是混在小兵里，不愿意与三兄一起住。

李智云振振有词道：“明年我也会入军营。二兄说，练习带兵有个笨办法，就是与兵卒同吃同住，才能知道如何率领兵卒！”

李玄霸只能叮嘱罗士信好好照顾李智云。

反正李智云跟着罗士信，也吃不到太多苦。

乌镝可不需要隐藏了，每日都腻在李玄霸身边，把寒钩赶出去侦查，自己完全变成了一只毛绒绒大宠物。

寒钩实在是忍无可忍，和乌镝狠狠打了一架。

李玄霸扶额。为什么他出使西突厥还要操心雕孩子啊？还是小五好，至少省心。

李玄霸本来是心疼乌镝一直隐藏，没有好好吃饭休息，所以才纵容它几日。见寒钩生气了，李玄霸马上一碗水端平，给两只雕安排好了值班时刻表，不准乌镝再偷懒。

乌镝是不偷懒了，它故意抢寒钩的肉。

寒钩又和乌镝打了一架。

李玄霸掐着乌镝的鸟头：“你是故意惹寒钩生气？为什么？”

乌镝：“啾啾啾啾！”

寒钩用翅膀比划：“啾啾啾啾！”

李玄霸听懂了。

因为李世民发现寒钩更懂事，所以让寒钩一直待在李玄霸身边，乌镝生气了。首领打不过，欺软怕硬的乌镝就去欺负寒钩。

李玄霸扶额倒仰。为什么他和二哥已经很努力，乌镝怎么还是变成了“坏孩子”？他以前嘲笑二哥不会教导孩子，回旋镖了！

“再胡来我就生气了。”李玄霸板着脸道，“我会让你一个人……一只雕回张掖，以后也不带你出门。”

乌镝耷拉着鸟头：“啾。”

寒钩理着自己的羽毛。活该！

李玄霸让乌镝连续值班五日，作为乌镝使小性子的惩罚。

乌镝虽然顽皮了些，但只要给它安排工作，它都会认真完成，没有出过岔子。

李玄霸很欣慰。乌镝本性还是好的。

乌镝不作了，寒钩很快和乌镝和好。兄弟二雕又亲亲密密黏黏糊糊地你给我梳毛，我给你挠痒。

李玄霸松了口气，终于能把注意力从这两只雕孩子身上移开，继续准备和西突厥可汗的会谈了。

在去伊吾城的路上，李玄霸一直在脑海里不断模拟此次会谈。

虽然他有许多和皇帝、高官打交道的经验，但当“外交官”还是第一次。

李玄霸在这一生做了许多“第一次”的事，他认为非自己不可的事不多。

比如后勤，如果没有他，二哥自己也能做。

不就是一边打仗一边还要焦头烂额自己筹粮，如果战局吃紧没空筹粮就饿得哇哇哭而已。反正二哥历史中也是这么过来，能赢。

李玄霸自认为自己唯一无可取代的优势，是基于现代教育下的“全局观”。

史书没有记载细节，改变现在也会改变未来，所以李玄霸的“预知挂”会失去价值。

但“全局挂”不会。

李玄霸对于这个时代的人就像是开了“全局视野”。

他知道同时代有多少国家，这些国家彼此之间有什么摩擦，将来这些国家会遇见什么大事；他也知道地球是圆的，知道地球上有哪些重要的山川河流；他还知道全球一些大的天灾到来的大略时间和影响范围，能提前做出谋划。

所以他确定自己能说服西突厥可汗出兵，帮二哥骚扰东突厥。

李玄霸结束了一段模拟，又完善了会谈细节后，脑袋放空，将胡思乱想当做休息。

说起二哥饿得哇哇哭，李玄霸想起历史中的秦王李世民的出河东一战。

李世民的征战生涯只看结局，打的全是碾压局。李玄霸为了当太宗黑细扒每一条史料，把秦王李世民所有“大局面碾压局”下的危机四伏如履薄冰都捋了出来，才能成为“太宗黑”营销号的扛把子。

比如大众认可的李世民的军事巅峰是“一战擒双王”，其实“一战擒双王”只是李世民表面上最高光的时刻。

若论对唐朝影响最大的一战，其实是李世民奉命东出，击败刘武周。

公元619年，刘武周接受宋金刚建议，以太原为跳板图谋天下。

李元吉丢下守城将士和官吏，连夜悄悄带妻妾弃太原逃走；太常少卿李仲文、左卫大将军姜宝谊，被刘武周的将领黄子英击败；右仆射裴寂全军覆没，只身逃走。

大唐河东之地几乎尽失，精锐也丧失大半。李渊发布手诏，“贼势如此，难与争锋，宜弃大河以东谨守关西而已”。

那时河右之地、巴蜀之地都有割据势力。大唐都被刘武周打得准备放弃逐鹿中原，准备龟缩狭小的关中，当最为弱小的割据势力之一了。

史书为了避尊者讳，没有对此事进行过多评价，对河东之战的描写也不太多。但从手诏就能看出，大唐踩在了“统一王朝”和“割据势力”的分界线上。

关键时刻，镇守长春宫的李世民上奏，“太原王业所基，国之根本，河东殷实，京邑所资。若举而弃之，臣窃愤恨。愿假精兵三万，必能平殄武周，克复汾、晋”。

他请求李渊借给他三万精兵，派他东出河东。

李渊同意，将关中之兵交给李世民率领。李世民东出河东，击败刘武周，大唐这才保住了统一天下的资本。

李玄霸握着缰绳的手微微收紧，脸上泛起不知道是讥笑还是苦笑。

长春宫处于河东去往关中的关隘之处。

近一年的时间，秦王李世民坐镇长春宫，眼睁睁地看着大唐河东之地尽失，却没有得到李渊让他领兵的诏令。

大唐军队遭遇了一连串“全军覆没”，最后李世民能讨来的只有“三万精兵”。

这竟然已经是李渊在关中竭尽全力为他筹集的所有精兵了。

李渊眼睁睁看着大唐连连败退，也不肯派李世民领兵，。那时他已经忌惮李世民了吧。

在这件事后，李渊才重新“起用”李世民。李世民才有后来南征北战的功绩。

在李世民出河东时，李渊亲自来长春宫送行，给足了李世民风光。

但是只有送行这个“风光”。

大唐当时已经岌岌可危，不仅粮草支援不足，也无法保障粮道通畅。

李世民要征河东，只能带着这支大唐最后的精兵，自己到河东征粮。

在奠定胜局那一战，李世民三天未卸甲，两日未进食，每日追击二百余里，只留了一只羊在关键一战前与众将士一起分食，鼓舞士气。

河间郡公刘弘基拉着李世民的马劝说，“深入不已，不爱身乎”？

李世民回答，“吾竭忠徇国，岂顾身乎”。

李玄霸想着历史中唐太宗说的这句话，深吸了一口塞北的凉气，才冷静下来。

后世李世民一生中有许多有趣的小段子，比如到张难堡时守军不敢开门，李世民脱下头盔说“是我”，堡内守军这才喜极而泣地开门迎接。

但很少人知道，这个小段子后面还有一句话，“左右告以王不食，献浊酒、脱粟饭”。

李世民在和全军分食了那只羊后又是许久没进食，一直到了张难堡，才吃到一顿浊酒糙粟的饱饭。

唐太宗，小秦|王，他身上最“苏”的点大概是如此——自己练兵，自己打仗，自己搞后勤筹粮，自己做完所有的事。

可就算李世民的精力无限，他也不可能同一时间，做不同的事。

所以当为了不贻误战机，他没时间筹粮的时候就饿着，没时间养伤的时候就熬着。

然后，他就这样饿着伤着熬着，将地和兵都已经快败光，马上就要离开逐鹿天下舞台的大唐，重新拉回逐鹿天下的舞台上，并给后世人留下一个“这是不值一提的碾压局”的印象。

那可真是太苏了，苏得李玄霸牙痒痒。

李玄霸很庆幸自己只是一个“太宗黑”。

一个正常将领正常打仗的时候，都不会吃这些苦。除了李世民之外的大唐将领打仗的时候，也很少吃这些苦。

但李世民总是在“力挽狂澜”时才被派出来，后勤充足的顺风局用不上这位大唐最强的军事将帅。所以他打仗时后勤供应艰难，友军也无法支援，才只能这么熬。

“美强惨”最苏不过。唐太宗如果不吃这些苦，只剩下“美强”没有“惨”，大概以后世的评价就不够“苏”了。

若自己能做到，简直是“太宗黑”的巅峰时刻，自己可太骄傲了。

李玄霸暗自想。

为了完成“太宗黑”的终极使命，自己要做的事还有很多。时间太过仓促，需要抓紧。

因为卫怀王李玄霸，隋大业十年，公元614年逝世，享年十六虚岁。

现在已经是大业九年，公元613年十一月了。

李玄霸不知道明年自己会不会病逝。毕竟病逝这种死法，在医疗资源极其匮乏的古代真的只能听天由命。

母亲病逝是感染疫病，不去涿郡就好了；自己病逝是先天体弱，这是出生就注定的病因，想抗争都无从下手。

只能听天由命了。

所以自己要趁着还活着的时候，多在“太宗黑”的事业上努力才行啊。

李玄霸胡思乱想一通，将“李世民河东之战”的细节仔细回忆了一遍，才继续在脑海里模拟这次的出使。

就算自己熬不过死劫，二哥也绝不会再几天几夜不吃饭不合眼的厮杀。

房乔、杜如晦、长孙无忌、魏徵、薛收都提前只认二哥为主，把父亲丢一边去了；娘亲还在河东之地经营了那么多“义庄”。

就是没有大唐支援，二哥也绝对不会再自己一边打仗一边愁全军上下吃什么。

哪来的傻逼君王让将领打仗还不提供粮草？二哥不是你儿子，早就哗变谋反了，父亲！

“阿嚏！”

李渊揉了揉鼻子，拿着诏书愁眉苦脸。

“郎君，陛下命你成为山西和河东慰抚使是好事，为何愁眉苦脸？”窦夫人疑惑道。

李渊叹气：“太子被斥责，与太子同守洛阳的我却被拜为右骁卫将军，领山西和河东慰抚使、太原留守，我总怀疑陛下是在给我设下陷阱。”

窦夫人想了想，道：“陛下忌惮太子，不愿意给太子论功。但洛阳防守一战总要给人论功，陛下才将所有功劳都给了郎君，破格提拔郎君。始毕可汗继位后，对大隋逐渐傲慢。陛下命郎君担任慰抚使，应当是想让郎君防备始毕可汗，可能不是阴谋。”

李渊道：“或许是吧。唉，不过我还是低调些为好。”

窦夫人道：“郎君只要深居简出，再多收受贿赂，换成鹰犬骏马送给陛下，陛下应当就不会忌惮郎君。”

李渊颔首：“为夫也是这么想。”

李渊又叹了口气，道：“我镇守一方，二郎也镇守一方，陛下应当不会让一家父子各自镇守一地。我是不是该让二郎主动上书辞去官职？”

窦夫人眼眸微微闪烁，道：“二郎刚立下大功。大隋如今能振奋人心的事很少，二郎此番大胜让陛下心中很是宽慰。现在提议提免了二郎的官，反而会让陛下难做。不如请求陛下命二郎乘胜剿灭吐谷浑残部，等尽了全功后，再将二郎三郎调到郎君身边为将。”

窦夫人笑道：“郎君身为慰抚大使，麾下当有虎贲郎将虎牙郎将效力。寻常勋贵人家中，父子兄弟也有许多同为将军和郎将者。”

李渊拍了一下脑袋，笑道：“夫人说得对。唉，我过于战战兢兢了。我这就上书。”

窦夫人待李渊离开后，叹了口气，赶紧悄悄写信，让人迅速送往张掖。

以二郎三郎的本事，河右之地可能已经快入囊中了，可不能被郎君耽误。

自己只能拖延，要如何破局，还得让二郎三郎自己想办法。

窦夫人又叹了口气，分外头疼。

李渊觐见杨广时，杨广果然如窦夫人所料，不仅没有夸赞李渊识相，反而很烦李渊给他找麻烦。

杨广私下对近臣道：“那李渊有什么本事？不过是凭借门荫和朕对他的信任才升任将军。只是在疲软的贼寇手中守下一座坚固的东都城，换谁都行。李二郎以八百骑破西海郡，才是大隋真正的将军。唉，可惜李渊是李二郎的父亲，朕不好越过李渊单独奖赏李二郎。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 116: The Lifelong Career of "Tianzong-Black"

Changsun Wuji was naturally gifted in governance. Aside from a tendency to get carried away, he had no major flaws.

As for his lack of inclination toward remonstrance and his preference for flattering his superiors, that was hardly a shortcoming in Li Shimin’s eyes.

After all, Li Shimin already had the "mirror" Wei Zheng, and a younger brother, Li Xuanba, who had rarely spoken a kind word to him since childhood. There was no need for Changsun Wuji to be blunt.

With Changsun Wuji joining the fold, the burden on Li Shimin’s shoulders lightened a little.

He complained to his close friend, "Only now do I feel a bit like a lord. What kind of life was I living before? Everything had to be done by me and A-Xuan! A-Xuan is physically weak, so I didn't dare give him too much work. All the trivial, tedious tasks fell entirely on me!"

Li Shimin gulped down a mouthful of wine and continued to slap his thigh in frustration, "There has never been a lord as aggrieved as me!"

Changsun Wuji consoled him, "Alright, alright. Haven't Fang Xuanling and Du Keming arrived? Once Xue Bobao comes as well, you’ll be able to relax."

Du Ruhui sneered, "And there’s still Wei Zheng. That man managed to persuade the commoners' rebel army to besiege Zhuo County. He’s a talent, perfectly suited to be sent out to stir up trouble when the world is in chaos."

Fang Qiao nearly spat out his tea, "Keming, just how great is your opinion of Wei... Wei Xuancheng?"

Du Ruhui replied, "I have no opinion; I am praising him. Don't worry, once he stands before me, I will affectionately call him Wei Xuancheng."

Fang Qiao muttered, "Such backhanded arrogance is not the behavior of a gentleman."

Du Ruhui raised an eyebrow, "Did I ever say I was a gentleman?"

Changsun Wuji asked blankly, "Wei Zheng, Wei Xuancheng? Who is that?"

Li Shimin said, "A very capable man, our partner, and your colleague. Ah, you actually didn't know?"

A nameless fire surged in Changsun Wuji’s heart: "I actually didn't know?!"

Li Shimin said indifferently, "Oh, I forgot to tell you. A small matter, a small matter."

Changsun Wuji really wanted to smash the sheep bone in his hand onto his brother-in-law.

This was a small matter?! He felt subtly ostracized. It was infuriating!

Li Shimin chuckled, "My father-in-law must have known. Didn't he tell you? Then go ask him why he kept it from you."

Changsun Wuji was both angry and stifled, "Stop using my father to pressure me."

Li Shimin said helplessly, "It’s not that I want to use him to pressure you, but he is not only my father-in-law, he is also my teacher. What can I do? I can only listen to him."

Fang Qiao smoothed things over, "Fujie, this is something that cannot be helped."

Du Ruhui added, "Perhaps General Changsun believed you still needed tempering. However, since he has agreed to let you come to Zhangye, he must believe you have finished your apprenticeship and can stand on your own."

Li Shimin said, "Right, you should be able to know everything now. By the way, did you know A-Xuan understands prophecy?"

Changsun Wuji cursed, "I know nothing!"

Li Shimin laughed heartily, "Hahahaha."

Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui couldn't help but laugh as well, hurriedly lowering their heads to drink water to hide it.

Changsun Wuji felt even more aggrieved. Finally, unable to hold back, he threw the sheep bone at Li Shimin.

Li Shimin dodged to the side, laughing even more wildly.

Changsun Wuji rolled up his sleeves, ready to brawl with Li Shimin.

Fang Qiao wanted to intervene, but was pulled back by Du Ruhui.

Du Ruhui laughed, "Let them fight. Let’s see if Changsun Silang has inherited the true teachings of General Changsun."

Fang Qiao sighed, "What a ruckus."

After sighing, he watched Li Shimin and Changsun Wuji, who were "wrestling" in a chaotic mess without regard for the sheep grease on their hands, and couldn't help but smile.

Du Ruhui winked, "Changsun Silang is more pleasing to the eye like this."

Fang Qiao nodded.

Previously, Changsun Wuji had been overly respectful to their lord, strictly observing the etiquette of sovereign and subject, which had been uncomfortable to watch.

Judging by the lord’s reaction, he must have been uncomfortable too, which was why he had deliberately provoked Changsun Wuji.

Perhaps one day in the future, they would have to be respectful and cautious toward their lord. But not now.

People must have a time of youthful recklessness; otherwise, wouldn't life be lived in vain?

"I wonder if Dade’s journey is going smoothly?" Fang Qiao said, "He would surely regret not seeing this scene."

Du Ruhui said smugly, "I will not only write it down, I will draw it. But by now, he should have discovered the surprise the lord left for him and is likely jumping up and down cursing."

Fang Qiao chuckled, "That is likely."

While Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui were whispering about Li Xuanba, Li Xuanba was indeed jumping up and down, cursing his second brother.

He had already reached Dunhuang County and was taking the opportunity to visit this famous tourist destination of later generations while resupplying.

By now, the Mogao Caves had already been excavated and had become a gathering place for monks and temples. Li Xuanba bowed casually to the gods and Buddhas, but the caves were still worth a visit.

While organizing the work, Li Xuanba noticed a soldier in the ranks who looked familiar.

His heart skipped a beat, and he had Luo Shixin "drag" the soldier over.

Luo Shixin’s expression changed.

Li Xuanba’s heart sank further.

Li Xuanba cursed, "You knew?! And you deliberately hid it from me?"

Luo Shixin stammered.

Li Xuanba laughed in anger, "Bring him over, now!"

Luo Shixin sighed and brought the "soldier" over.

Li Zhiyun wiped the dust off his face with the back of his hand and grinned, "Third Brother, you’re so slow. You only just noticed."

Li Xuanba reached out and pinched Li Zhiyun’s cheek, "Why are you here? Do you know how dangerous this is?"

Li Zhiyun cried out in pain, "Second Brother said I’m grown up and should come to gain some experience."

Li Xuanba scolded, "It’s freezing, the road is long—what if you get sick or injured?"

Li Zhiyun said, "Third Brother, my body is better than yours. You don't get sick, and neither do I. Stop pinching, you’re going to peel my skin off. Second Brother agreed to this!"

Li Xuanba let go, feeling drained, "Why didn't you tell me beforehand?"

Li Zhiyun rubbed his face, "Second Brother knew you wouldn't agree, so he let me sneak in."

Li Xuanba glared fiercely toward the east, muttering a few curses under his breath.

Li Zhiyun pretended not to hear his third brother cursing.

Li Xuanba took a few deep breaths to calm his anger, "What else did he hide from me?"

Li Zhiyun said, "There is one more thing, but that’s all."

Li Zhiyun stretched out his arm and shouted, "Wudi!"

With a "chirp," a golden eagle, whose majestic and domineering aura did not match its cry, descended from the sky.

Li Xuanba: "..."

He took another deep breath and shouted, "Han-gou!"

Han-gou also descended from the sky.

Li Xuanba gripped Han-gou’s head, "I was wondering why your appetite has been so big lately. I thought you were just putting on fat for the cold. You knew about this all along?"

Han-gou shrank its neck.

Wudi flapped its wings triumphantly.

Li Xuanba felt utterly powerless, "Shixin, you knew too?"

Luo Shixin hung his head.

Zhou Da couldn't bear it and said, "Actually, I knew too. This was the young master’s order."

Li Xuanba gritted his teeth, "Yes, yes, everyone kept it from me!"

After Li Xuanba left, Li Shimin would continue to look for opportunities to engage in battle, training his troops while expanding his influence.

Therefore, Li Xuanba had let Li Shimin keep one golden eagle by his side. Attacks from the sky could sometimes have miraculous effects, and Han-gou and Wudi were already familiar with the terrain around Zhangye and could take on the responsibility of delivering military orders.

Li Shimin had readily agreed with a "Sure, sure," and then not only secretly stuffed Li Zhiyun into Li Xuanba’s team but also let Wudi sneak along.

He knew Li Xuanba wouldn't agree, so he simply did it in secret. Once the deed was done, he didn't believe Li Xuanba would let the brat and the eagle return alone.

Compared to letting one person and one eagle return alone, Li Xuanba would certainly think it safer to keep this brat and the bear-eagle by his side.

Clearly, not only did the twin brother understand his twin brother well, but the twin brother was also adept at "scheming" against his twin.

According to the laws of physics, forces are mutual.

The people Li Xuanba brought this time were all personally arranged by Li Shimin, led by Zhou Da and Luo Shixin. Li Xuanba knew he had no talent for leading troops, so he hadn't intervened until he reached Dunhuang to purchase supplies and took a headcount.

Now, he first spanked the two eagles and knocked Li Zhiyun on the head, then helplessly continued on his way.

What else could he do?

Although Li Zhiyun had washed the dust off his face, he still hid among the soldiers, unwilling to stay with his third brother.

Li Zhiyun argued, "I will enter the army next year. Second Brother said there is a stupid way to learn how to lead troops: eat and live with the soldiers so you can know how to command them!"

Li Xuanba could only instruct Luo Shixin to take good care of Li Zhiyun.

Anyway, with Luo Shixin, Li Zhiyun wouldn't suffer too much.

Wudi no longer needed to hide and spent every day clinging to Li Xuanba, driving Han-gou out to scout while it turned into a fluffy, giant pet.

Han-gou finally couldn't take it anymore and had a fierce fight with Wudi.

Li Xuanba held his forehead. Why did he have to worry about eagle-children while on a diplomatic mission to the Western Turkic Khaganate? Xiao Wu was better; at least he was worry-free.

Li Xuanba had originally felt sorry for Wudi having to hide and not eating or resting well, which was why he had indulged it for a few days. Seeing Han-gou was angry, Li Xuanba immediately treated them equally, arranging a duty schedule for the two eagles and forbidding Wudi from being lazy again.

Wudi stopped being lazy, but it deliberately snatched Han-gou’s meat.

Han-gou had another fight with Wudi.

Li Xuanba pinched Wudi’s bird head, "Are you deliberately making Han-gou angry? Why?"

Wudi: "Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!"

Han-gou gestured with its wings: "Chirp, chirp, chirp, chirp!"

Li Xuanba understood.

Because Li Shimin found Han-gou more sensible, he kept Han-gou by his side, and Wudi was jealous. Since it couldn't beat the leader, the bullying Wudi went to bully Han-gou.

Li Xuanba leaned back, holding his forehead. Why, even though he and his second brother had tried so hard, did Wudi still turn into a "bad kid"? He used to mock his second brother for not knowing how to raise children; the boomerang had returned!

"If you act up again, I’ll be angry," Li Xuanba said with a straight face. "I will send you back to Zhangye alone—one eagle—and never take you out again."

Wudi drooped its head: "Chirp."

Han-gou preened its feathers. Serves you right!

Li Xuanba made Wudi work for five consecutive days as punishment for its temper.

Although Wudi was a bit mischievous, as long as it was given a job, it would complete it conscientiously without any mishaps.

Li Xuanba was very gratified. Wudi’s nature was still good.

With Wudi behaving, Han-gou soon made up with it. The two eagle brothers were back to being intimate and clingy, preening each other’s feathers and scratching each other’s itches.

Li Xuanba breathed a sigh of relief, finally able to shift his attention away from these two eagle-children and continue preparing for the talks with the Western Turkic Khagan.

On the way to Yiwu City, Li Xuanba kept simulating the talks in his mind.

Although he had plenty of experience dealing with emperors and high officials, this was his first time acting as a "diplomat."

Li Xuanba had done many "firsts" in this life, and he didn't think there were many things that only he could do.

For example, logistics—without him, his second brother could do it himself.

It was just a matter of being overwhelmed while fighting and trying to raise grain, and if the war was tight and there was no time to raise grain, he would just cry from hunger. Anyway, that was how his second brother had lived through it in history, and he still won.

Li Xuanba considered his only irreplaceable advantage to be his "global perspective" based on modern education.

History books did not record the details, and changing the present would change the future, so Li Xuanba’s "prophecy cheat" would lose its value.

But the "global cheat" would not.

To the people of this era, Li Xuanba was like someone with "global vision."

He knew how many countries existed in the same era, what frictions they had with each other, and what major events would happen to them in the future; he also knew the Earth was round and knew where the important mountains and rivers on Earth were; he also knew the approximate timing and scope of major global natural disasters, allowing him to plan ahead.

Therefore, he was certain he could persuade the Western Turkic Khagan to send troops to help his second brother harass the Eastern Turkic Khaganate.

Li Xuanba finished a simulation and refined the details of the talks, then emptied his mind, treating his wandering thoughts as a rest.

Speaking of his second brother crying from hunger, Li Xuanba recalled the Battle of Hedong of the Qin King Li Shimin in history.

If one only looked at the outcome of Li Shimin’s military career, every battle was a crushing victory. To become a "Tianzong-Black" (anti-Tang Taizong) influencer, Li Xuanba had meticulously combed through every historical record, uncovering all the crises and precarious situations beneath Li Shimin’s "crushing victories" to become the leader of the "Tianzong-Black" marketing accounts.

For example, the public recognized Li Shimin’s military peak as "capturing two kings in one battle," but in reality, that was merely his most glorious moment on the surface.

In terms of the battle with the greatest impact on the Tang Dynasty, it was actually Li Shimin being ordered to go east to defeat Liu Wuzhou.

In 619 AD, Liu Wuzhou accepted Song Jingang’s suggestion to use Taiyuan as a springboard to plot for the world.

Li Yuanji abandoned the city’s defenders and officials, fleeing Taiyuan overnight with his wives and concubines; Taichang Shaoqing Li Zhongwen and Left General Jiang Baoyi were defeated by Liu Wuzhou’s general Huang Ziying; Right Puye Pei Ji’s entire army was wiped out, and he fled alone.

Almost all of the Tang’s Hedong territory was lost, and most of its elite troops were gone. Li Yuan issued an imperial edict: "The enemy’s momentum is such that it is difficult to contend; we should abandon the east of the Great River and guard the west of the pass."

At that time, there were separatist forces in the land of Heyou and Bashu. The Tang Dynasty was prepared to give up the struggle for the Central Plains and shrink into the small Guanzhong region, becoming one of the weakest separatist forces.

To avoid disrespecting the sovereign, history books did not comment much on this, and the descriptions of the Battle of Hedong were sparse. But from the edict, one could see that the Tang Dynasty was standing on the dividing line between a "unified dynasty" and a "separatist force."

At the critical moment, Li Shimin, who was guarding Changchun Palace, submitted a memorial: "Taiyuan is the foundation of the royal enterprise and the root of the country. Hedong is prosperous and provides for the capital. If we abandon it, I am filled with indignation. I wish to borrow 30,000 elite troops, and I will surely be able to pacify Wuzhou and recover Fen and Jin."

He requested Li Yuan to lend him 30,000 elite troops and send him east to Hedong.

Li Yuan agreed, handing over the Guanzhong troops to Li Shimin. Li Shimin went east to Hedong and defeated Liu Wuzhou, and only then did the Tang Dynasty preserve the capital to unify the world.

Li Xuanba’s hand holding the reins tightened slightly, his face showing a sneer or perhaps a bitter smile.

Changchun Palace was located at the pass between Hedong and Guanzhong.

For nearly a year, the Qin King Li Shimin had sat in Changchun Palace, watching the Tang’s Hedong territory fall, yet he never received an order from Li Yuan to lead troops.

The Tang army suffered a series of "total annihilations," and in the end, all Li Shimin could beg for were "30,000 elite troops."

This was actually all the elite troops Li Yuan had exhausted his efforts to gather for him in Guanzhong.

Li Yuan watched the Tang Dynasty retreat repeatedly, yet refused to send Li Shimin to lead the troops. He must have been wary of Li Shimin by then.

Only after this incident did Li Yuan "re-employ" Li Shimin. Only then did Li Shimin have the subsequent achievements of his southern and northern campaigns.

When Li Shimin went east to Hedong, Li Yuan personally came to Changchun Palace to see him off, giving Li Shimin plenty of "glory."

But only the act of seeing him off was "glory."

The Tang Dynasty was in dire straits at the time, with insufficient grain supplies and no way to guarantee the safety of the supply lines.

To conquer Hedong, Li Shimin could only take these last elite troops of the Tang and go to Hedong to raise grain himself.

In the battle that decided the outcome, Li Shimin did not take off his armor for three days and did not eat for two days, pursuing the enemy for over 200 miles every day, leaving only one sheep to share with his generals before the key battle to boost morale.

Liu Hongji, the Duke of Hejian, pulled Li Shimin’s horse and advised him, "You are deep in enemy territory; do you not cherish your life?"

Li Shimin replied, "I am exhausting my loyalty to the country; how could I care for my own life?"

Thinking of these words spoken by Tang Taizong in history, Li Xuanba took a deep breath of the cold air of the north to calm himself down.

There were many interesting anecdotes about Li Shimin in later generations, such as when he arrived at Zhangnan Fort and the guards didn't dare open the gates, Li Shimin took off his helmet and said, "It’s me," and the guards inside wept with joy as they opened the gates to welcome him.

But few people knew there was another sentence after this anecdote: "The attendants told him the King had not eaten, so they offered turbid wine and coarse millet."

After sharing that sheep with the entire army, Li Shimin had gone a long time without eating until he reached Zhangnan Fort, where he finally had a full meal of turbid wine and coarse millet.

Tang Taizong, the young Qin King—the most "charming" point about him was perhaps this: he trained his own troops, fought his own battles, handled his own logistics and grain, and did everything himself.

But even if Li Shimin had infinite energy, he couldn't do different things at the same time.

So, when he didn't have time to raise grain to avoid missing military opportunities, he went hungry; when he didn't have time to heal, he endured it.

And so, hungry and injured, he dragged the Tang Dynasty—which had almost lost its land and troops and was about to leave the stage of competing for the world—back onto the stage, leaving later generations with the impression that "this was a crushing victory not worth mentioning."

That was truly too charming, so charming it made Li Xuanba’s teeth itch.

Li Xuanba was very glad he was just a "Tianzong-Black."

A normal general fighting a normal battle wouldn't suffer like this. Other Tang generals, aside from Li Shimin, rarely suffered like this when fighting.

But Li Shimin was only sent out when he had to "turn the tide," and the strongest military commander of the Tang was never used in favorable situations with sufficient logistics. That was why he had to endure so much when he fought, with difficult supply lines and no support from friendly forces.

"Beautiful, strong, and tragic"—nothing is more charming than that. If Tang Taizong hadn't suffered these hardships and only had "beauty and strength" without the "tragedy," the evaluations of later generations probably wouldn't be so "charming."

If he could achieve this, it would be the peak moment of his "Tianzong-Black" career; he could be so proud.

Li Xuanba thought to himself.

To complete the ultimate mission of "Tianzong-Black," there was still much to do. Time was too short, and he needed to hurry.

Because the Prince of Wei, Li Xuanba, died in the tenth year of Daye of the Sui Dynasty, 614 AD, at the age of sixteen.

It was already the eleventh month of the ninth year of Daye, 613 AD.

Li Xuanba didn't know if he would die of illness next year. After all, in ancient times with extremely scarce medical resources, dying of illness was truly a matter of fate.

His mother died of an epidemic; if only they hadn't gone to Zhuo County. His own illness was congenital weakness, a cause determined at birth; even if he wanted to fight it, there was nowhere to start.

He could only leave it to fate.

So he had to work hard on his "Tianzong-Black" career while he was still alive.

Li Xuanba let his thoughts wander, carefully recalling the details of "Li Shimin’s Battle of Hedong" before continuing to simulate the diplomatic mission in his mind.

Even if he couldn't survive his own death tribulation, his second brother would never again fight for days and nights without eating or sleeping.

Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, Changsun Wuji, Wei Zheng, and Xue Shou had all recognized his second brother as their lord early on, casting their fathers aside; his mother was still managing so many "charity estates" in Hedong.

Even without Tang’s support, his second brother would never again have to worry about what the whole army was eating while fighting.

What kind of idiot monarch makes a general fight without providing grain? If his second brother weren't your son, he would have mutinied long ago, Father!

"Achoo!"

Li Yuan rubbed his nose, looking at the imperial edict with a troubled face.

"My lord, it is a good thing that His Majesty has appointed you as the Pacification Commissioner for Shanxi and Hedong. Why are you so troubled?" Lady Dou asked, puzzled.

Li Yuan sighed, "The Crown Prince was reprimanded, yet I, who guarded Luoyang with him, was appointed as General of the Right Xiao Guard, Pacification Commissioner for Shanxi and Hedong, and Garrison Commander of Taiyuan. I always suspect His Majesty is setting a trap for me."

Lady Dou thought for a moment and said, "His Majesty is wary of the Crown Prince and unwilling to reward him for his merits. But the defense of Luoyang had to be rewarded, so His Majesty gave all the credit to you and promoted you exceptionally. After Shibi Khagan succeeded to the throne, he became increasingly arrogant toward the Great Sui. His Majesty appointing you as Pacification Commissioner should be to have you guard against Shibi Khagan; it might not be a conspiracy."

Li Yuan said, "Perhaps. Sigh, but I had better keep a low profile."

Lady Dou said, "As long as you stay out of the public eye and accept more bribes, exchanging them for hawks, hounds, and fine horses to send to His Majesty, he should not be wary of you."

Li Yuan nodded, "That is what I think as well."

Li Yuan sighed again, "I am guarding one region, and Er-lang is guarding another. His Majesty should not let a father and son guard separate regions. Should I have Er-lang voluntarily submit a memorial to resign from his post?"

Lady Dou’s eyes flickered slightly, "Er-lang has just made a great contribution. There are few things that can boost morale in the Great Sui now, and Er-lang’s great victory has brought His Majesty much comfort. Suggesting to remove Er-lang’s post now would only make things difficult for His Majesty. It would be better to request His Majesty to order Er-lang to wipe out the remnants of the Tuyuhun while he is on a roll, and once he has achieved full success, then transfer Er-lang and San-lang to your side as generals."

Lady Dou smiled, "As the Pacification Ambassador, you should have Tiger-Brave and Tiger-Tooth commanders serving under you. In ordinary noble families, there are many fathers and sons who are both generals and commanders."

Li Yuan slapped his forehead and laughed, "My wife is right. Sigh, I am too timid. I will submit the memorial now."

After Lady Dou watched Li Yuan leave, she sighed and hurriedly wrote a letter, having someone send it to Zhangye as quickly as possible.

With the abilities of Er-lang and San-lang, the land of Heyou might already be within their grasp; it must not be delayed by their father.

She could only delay; as for how to break the situation, she would have to let Er-lang and San-lang find a way themselves.

Lady Dou sighed again, feeling an intense headache.

When Li Yuan had an audience with Yang Guang, Yang Guang, as Lady Dou had expected, not only did not praise Li Yuan for being sensible but was annoyed that Li Yuan was causing him trouble.

Yang Guang said privately to his close ministers, "What ability does Li Yuan have? He only rose to the rank of general by relying on his family’s legacy and my trust in him. He only managed to hold a sturdy Eastern Capital against weak rebels; anyone could have done that. Li Er-lang breaking Xihai County with 800 cavalry is the true general of the Great Sui. Sigh, it’s a pity Li Yuan is Li Er-lang’s father; it is not easy for me to bypass Li Yuan and reward Li Er-lang alone."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第116章 太宗黑毕生事业 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
裴世矩道：“唐国公担任太原留守，不过是继续守城而已。李二郎是陛下派往西域征伐和震慑有不臣之心的蛮夷的将领。大隋常有父兄在朝中为官，将领率兵出征的事。唐国公此举过于谨慎了。”

苏威皱眉：“陛下，不能将李二郎召回！中原民贼四起，杨玄感叛乱也还未平定。西域蛮夷无信，说不定会趁机生乱！”

宇文述虽是个擅长奉承的贪官，但也是知兵的老将。

他也赞同道：“陛下，吐谷浑残部是小事。始毕可汗对大隋逐渐傲慢，李二郎在河右之地，还能防备始毕可汗。陛下不仅不该召回李二郎，还该直接任命李二郎为行军大将，乘胜追击，夺回河源郡等被吐谷浑残部占领之地，以免吐谷浑残部和始毕可汗勾结。”

虞世基恭敬道：“陛下，唐国公向来对李二郎、李三郎不慈。自己刚升了官，就想把李二郎李三郎的官职免了，以免压过李建成这个唐国公世子。这次应当也是如此，倒是和什么谨慎没关系。”

虞世基在心中叹息，居然被弟弟猜对，唐国公升官第一件事就是压制李二郎和李三郎。

杨广皱眉：“李渊和李二郎、李三郎父子仍旧不睦？”

苏威听了虞世基的话，也觉得有这么点意思：“不是不睦，只是五指有所长，有所短而已。”

裴蕴听得满头雾水。

每次同僚提起李二郎李三郎的时候，他都一头雾水。哪怕现在他也收了李二郎和李三郎的钱，他还是觉得自己有点格格不入。

怎么他们都对唐国公府这么了解？独独我一无所知吗？

裴蕴只能硬着头皮附和道：“大隋能守城之将繁多。如李二郎那等少年将帅，史书中也罕见。霍去病当冠军侯的时候，汉皇也未曾顾虑过他的父亲。陛下不过秉公论功行赏，唐国公此举说是谨慎，其实是陷陛下于不公了。”

裴世矩、苏威、虞世基、宇文述齐齐偷瞥了裴蕴一眼，琢磨裴蕴是不是与李二郎、李三郎也有瞒着他们的私下友好关系。

心腹都这么说，杨广被说动了。

他想起李世民和李玄霸在杨暕成为太子之后，就故意与杨暕拉开距离。杨暕与李世民、李玄霸看似继续交好，都是主动为之。李世民和李玄霸对太子杨暕，比杨暕还是齐王的时候还冷淡不少。他就对二人好感更甚。

之前他因为担忧李世民和李玄霸与太子杨暕交好，所以没有把李世民和李玄霸留在禁中。现在看来，是他错怪两个孩子了。

不过李世民和李玄霸毕竟还是和太子杨暕有过交情，杨广既想重用两人，又不愿意让两人回到中原。

李世民和李玄霸被他远远放在西域，既不会被太子利用威胁他的统治，又能为他震慑有不臣之心的西域蛮夷，一举两得。

至于李渊，杨广想，自己只要把李渊再次不慈，试图劝自己免了李世民和李玄霸的官职的事告诉他们，两位表侄肯定会与李渊更加离心。

这么一想，李世民和李玄霸非常适合成为自己的心腹。他们被李渊欺辱，只有依靠自己才能逃脱李渊的桎梏。

于是杨广一番细思后，任命李世民为河右行军大将，李玄霸为副将，继续镇守张掖，统率河右之地，扫灭吐谷浑残部。

因杨广被义军围困涿郡受惊，大隋终于要全力剿灭义军了，没有余力向河右之地增援。

一般这个时候，河右之地都会失守。

杨广有基本的为君常识，自然也是知道这件事。

所以他给了李世民和李玄霸经略西域的权力，与隋文帝时的长孙晟一样，自行决定如何处理西域之事。

虽然裴世矩也曾经略西域，但因杨广不喜放权，所以裴世矩当时权力远远不如长孙晟。长孙晟可以凭借自行判断杀突厥的可汗，裴世矩只能先上报计谋，等杨广同意后再执行。

现在李世民和李玄霸也有了长孙晟当年的自主权了。

大隋给不了河右之地后勤支援，所以李世民这个“行军大将”还有自筹军粮的权力，河右之地所有鹰扬府都受他管辖。

因河右之地没有慰抚使，李世民相当于名义上的河右之地慰抚使了。

不过“行军大将”这个职务是临时的，打仗时任命，打完仗就撤掉，与“慰抚使”这个军区常驻一把手职位不一样。李世民又正好刚与吐谷浑残部打了一仗，所以朝中无人觉得这职位过了。

说白了，现在大隋已经抽不出人守卫河右之地，只有靠李世民这个小将了。

杨广没有给李世民和李玄霸升散官品级。

他给李世民和李玄霸画大饼，等两人再次立功之后，一定给两人升个大的官。

“你二人也到该成亲的年龄了，待你们成家，朕才好给你们大官做。”

杨广看着自己仿佛长辈叮嘱晚辈的旨意很满意。

他特意多填了几笔“李渊是个坏的，朕这个表叔对你们好”劝慰之语。李二郎和李三郎肯定会对朕更忠心了。

李渊得知此事后哭笑不得：“我冤枉啊！怎么就变成我对二郎三郎不慈了！若不是陛下太爱猜忌，我至于担惊受怕吗！”

窦夫人安慰道：“陛下不会认为他爱猜忌，所以陛下是无错的，自然是郎君你想太多，是你的错了。正因为陛下爱猜忌，在他猜出你的想法时，才会如此愤怒，故意挑拨你和二郎、三郎感情。说不定，他还会利用二郎和三郎对付郎君。这也是陛下的帝王权术吧。”

李渊叹气：“故意挑拨离间……哼，当初先帝也是这样对我李家。夫人，与长孙家和宇文家说一说，现在天下大乱，未来不知道如何，今年给二郎、三郎把婚事定了。二郎三郎成家后，才能安心立业。我想他们心里也对时局忐忑，会同意。”

窦夫人犹豫道：“但长孙将军特意和我们说了，观音婢还年幼……”

李渊道：“先成亲，待弱冠再圆房。大德也还体弱呢，即使珠娘身体健康，他哪能早早圆房？观音婢和珠娘都养在你身边，你要把她们当亲生女儿照顾。”

窦夫人立刻明白了李渊的意思。

李渊不仅是想让二郎三郎早日成家，好安心立业，也是见到天下大乱，想要提前与宇文弼、长孙晟绑定，以免这两家人投向他人。

再者，窦夫人不确定，丈夫是不是还有将观音婢和珠娘当做与二郎三郎联系纽带的想法。

李渊道：“你要好好教导观音婢和珠娘，让她们知道我和你对二郎、三郎的疼爱，千万不能让二郎、三郎被他人挑拨。”

窦夫人在心中沉沉叹了口气，微笑道：“那是自然。”

……

朝中的事李玄霸一无所知，不过他和二哥早就讨论过，如果父亲再升官，会不会影响他们的事业。

但他们有高颎、宇文弼、薛道衡和长孙晟四位老师在，虞世南老师虽然不声不响，有时候也能起很重要的作用。

兄弟二人将担心的事告诉老师们后，老师们让他们别担心，这点小事，他们会盯着。

李玄霸离开中原时，将与杨广身边近臣的“金钱关系”都交给了长孙晟。

长孙晟能经略西域，也能经略“大隋”。

朝中的事，李世民和李玄霸便高枕无忧，不再担忧。

终于到了伊吾城，射匮可汗亲自来伊吾城门口迎接，俨然将伊吾城当做了自己的城池。

实际上现在伊吾城也已经成了西突厥的地盘。大隋驻扎在伊吾城的将领已经撤走，士卒虽还穿着大隋的衣服，但已经吃西突厥的粮了。到了贞观四年，伊吾城主才归顺大唐。

李玄霸没有如射匮可汗所预想的那样露出羞愤的神色，他笑意盈盈不卑不亢地向射匮可汗行礼：“早听闻可汗威名，今日一见，真是老当益壮，名不虚传。”

射匮可汗听到李玄霸说他“老当益壮”的时候，脸皮抽搐了一下。

射匮可汗打跑了侄子处罗可汗。现在处罗可汗在杨广身边当吉祥物。他长处罗可汗一辈，自然是已经年老了。

历史中，射匮可汗在五六年后就该老逝。现在他已经感到了有些力不从心。

射匮可汗先给李玄霸下马威，李玄霸不接招。

李玄霸又暗损射匮可汗，指出射匮可汗已经年老，将来西突厥不知道落入谁之手。

一来一往，射匮可汗强行认为这是平局了，对年少且羸弱的李玄霸的轻视心少了许多，愿意与李玄霸聊点正事。

射匮可汗没有顾及李玄霸旅途劳累，未给李玄霸休息的时间，就设宴款待李玄霸。

李玄霸没有拒绝。他只要了点时间更衣沐浴，稍稍打理了一下仪容再赴宴。

李玄霸虽瘦弱，容貌还是不错的。西突厥的贵族对李玄霸的好感又多了几分，只是这些充满好感的眼神让罗士信和周达都握紧了腰间的刀柄。

蛮夷贵族都荤素不忌，特别偏爱中原娇生贵养的少年少女。

李玄霸扫了一眼用眼神冒犯自己的人，对射匮可汗道：“可汗，我感到了被冒犯。为了大隋和西突厥的和平，你带来的人可以杀几个吗？”

屋内西突厥贵族大惊失色。有人直接用突厥语骂了出来。

射匮可汗按下众人嘈杂的声音，冷声道：“李郎将，你这是什么意思？”

李玄霸道：“两国会面，若有人冒犯可汗，大隋肯定会处置冒犯的人。难道大隋的使臣在可汗这里没有相同的待遇？我还以为可汗想与大隋交好呢，没想到可汗是来激怒大隋的？”

李玄霸叹了口气，道：“处罗可汗算不上什么，他这辈子大概都不可能再踏上草原了。我本想和你聊一聊萨珊国。萨珊国国王正在攻打拜占庭帝国的耶路撒冷，若他们成功，说不定真的有望恢复当初阿契美尼德王朝的疆域。大隋该与之交好啊。”

射匮可汗心头一梗：“你居然知道萨珊国？！”

李玄霸爽朗笑道：“可汗最亲密的邻国，我怎么会不知道呢？”

射匮可汗沉默了许久。

他指着一个人道：“这个人地位最低，胆敢冒犯贵人，应该处死。”

李玄霸道：“那我给可汗一个脸面，就只处死他吧。士信。”

罗士信走到已经被射匮可汗的护卫按住的西突厥贵族面前，弯刀出鞘又收回，一刀枭首，刀光如行云流水。

人的脖子十分坚硬，罗士信如此轻描淡写砍人脑袋，众人都看出了这个少年郎的力气绝对很大。

射匮可汗思及另一位李郎将的名声，彻底放下了对李玄霸的轻视之心。

他起身相邀道：“你兄长也是李郎将，我比你年长，叫你一声李三郎可好？这里脏了，我们换个地方用宴，安静地谈谈萨珊国的事。”

李玄霸笑道：“射匮可汗是长者，当然可以称呼我为李三郎。请。”

果然，比起丧家之犬的处罗可汗，萨珊国才是西突厥的心腹大患。
chunks.englishText:
Pei Shiju remarked, "The Duke of Tang serving as the Administrator of Taiyuan is merely continuing to guard a city. Li Er-lang is a general dispatched by His Majesty to the Western Regions to conquer and intimidate barbarians who harbor rebellious hearts. It is common for the Great Sui to have fathers and elder brothers serving in the court while their kin lead armies on campaigns. The Duke of Tang’s actions are overly cautious."

Su Wei frowned, "Your Majesty, you must not recall Li Er-lang! Rebels are rising across the Central Plains, and Yang Xuangan’s rebellion has yet to be fully quelled. The barbarians of the Western Regions are untrustworthy; they might seize this opportunity to incite chaos!"

Yuwenshu, though a corrupt official skilled in flattery, was also a veteran general well-versed in military affairs.

He concurred, "Your Majesty, the remnants of the Tuyuhun are a minor matter. Shibi Khan has grown increasingly arrogant toward the Great Sui. With Li Er-lang in the Hexi region, he can still keep Shibi Khan in check. Not only should you not recall Li Er-lang, but you should also directly appoint him as the General of the Expeditionary Army. He should strike while the iron is hot, pursue the enemy, and reclaim Heyuan Commandery and other territories occupied by the Tuyuhun remnants, lest they collude with Shibi Khan."

Yu Shiji said respectfully, "Your Majesty, the Duke of Tang has always been unkind to Li Er-lang and Li San-lang. No sooner had he received a promotion than he sought to strip his sons of their official posts, fearing they might overshadow Li Jiancheng, the heir to the Dukedom of Tang. This is surely the same case; it has nothing to do with any so-called caution."

Yu Shiji sighed inwardly, thinking that his younger brother had actually guessed correctly—the first thing the Duke of Tang did after his promotion was to suppress Li Er-lang and Li San-lang.

Yang Guang frowned, "Li Yuan and his sons, Li Er-lang and Li San-lang, are still at odds?"

Upon hearing Yu Shiji’s words, Su Wei also felt there was some truth to it. "It is not so much that they are at odds, but rather that even the five fingers of a hand are of different lengths."

Pei Yun was left completely bewildered.

Every time his colleagues mentioned Li Er-lang and Li San-lang, he felt utterly lost. Even though he had accepted money from the two brothers, he still felt like an outsider.

*How is it that they all know so much about the Duke of Tang’s estate, while I alone know nothing?*

Pei Yun could only bite the bullet and chime in, "The Great Sui has no shortage of generals capable of guarding cities. Yet, a young commander like Li Er-lang is rare even in the history books. When Huo Qubing became the Marquis of Guanjun, the Han Emperor never concerned himself with the boy's father. Your Majesty is merely rewarding merit impartially; to call the Duke of Tang’s actions 'cautious' is, in truth, to cast Your Majesty in an unfair light."

Pei Shiju, Su Wei, Yu Shiji, and Yuwenshu all cast side-long glances at Pei Yun, wondering if he had some secret, friendly relationship with Li Er-lang and Li San-lang that they were unaware of.

With his trusted aides all speaking in unison, Yang Guang was moved.

He recalled how, after Yang Jian became the Crown Prince, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had intentionally kept their distance from him. Their apparent continued friendship with the Prince seemed to be entirely at the Prince's initiative. Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had been far colder toward Crown Prince Yang Jian than they were when he was merely the Prince of Qi. This only increased his favor toward the two brothers.

Previously, he had not kept them in the Imperial Palace out of concern for their closeness to the Crown Prince. Now, it seemed he had misjudged the two children.

However, since they had once been close to the Crown Prince, Yang Guang wanted to make use of them while simultaneously keeping them far away from the Central Plains.

Keeping them stationed in the distant Western Regions meant they could neither be used by the Crown Prince to threaten his rule, nor would they be close enough to cause trouble; it was killing two birds with one stone.

As for Li Yuan, Yang Guang thought that if he told the two cousins that Li Yuan had once again been unkind and attempted to persuade him to strip them of their titles, they would surely grow even more estranged from their father.

Thinking this way, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba seemed perfectly suited to be his loyal confidants. Bullied by Li Yuan, they would have no choice but to rely on him to escape their father's shackles.

After careful deliberation, Yang Guang appointed Li Shimin as the General of the Hexi Expeditionary Army, with Li Xuanba as his deputy, to continue guarding Zhangye, command the Hexi region, and wipe out the remaining Tuyuhun forces.

Because Yang Guang had been terrified by the rebel armies surrounding Zhuojun, the Great Sui was finally going to commit its full strength to suppressing the rebels, leaving no resources to reinforce the Hexi region.

Usually, in such times, the Hexi region would be lost.

Yang Guang, possessing the basic common sense of a ruler, was well aware of this.

Therefore, he granted Li Shimin and Li Xuanba the authority to manage the Western Regions, much like Zhangsun Sheng had done during the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui, allowing them to decide for themselves how to handle matters in the West.

Although Pei Shiju had also once managed the Western Regions, Yang Guang’s dislike for delegating power meant Pei Shiju’s authority had been far inferior to Zhangsun Sheng’s. Zhangsun Sheng could judge for himself when to execute a Turkic Khan, while Pei Shiju had to report his strategies and wait for Yang Guang’s approval before acting.

Now, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba possessed the same autonomy that Zhangsun Sheng had enjoyed in his day.

Since the Great Sui could not provide logistical support to Hexi, Li Shimin, as the "General of the Expeditionary Army," was also granted the power to raise his own military provisions, and all the Eagle-Yang Garrisons in the Hexi region were placed under his jurisdiction.

As there was no Pacification Commissioner in the Hexi region, Li Shimin was, in name, the de facto Pacification Commissioner of the region.

However, the title of "General of the Expeditionary Army" was temporary—appointed during wartime and revoked afterward—unlike the permanent position of a regional "Pacification Commissioner." Since Li Shimin had just fought a battle against the Tuyuhun remnants, no one in the court felt this appointment was excessive.

To put it bluntly, the Great Sui could no longer spare anyone to guard the Hexi region; they had to rely on this young general, Li Shimin.

Yang Guang did not raise their official ranks.

He dangled a carrot before them, promising that once they achieved further merit, he would certainly grant them high-ranking positions.

"You two are also at the age for marriage. Only when you have settled down and started families can I grant you high office."

Yang Guang was very satisfied with his decree, which sounded like an elder admonishing his juniors.

He specifically added a few lines of consolation, implying, "Li Yuan is a bad man, but I, your uncle, am good to you." Li Er-lang and Li San-lang would surely be even more loyal to him now.

When Li Yuan learned of this, he was left between laughter and tears. "I am wronged! How did it become that I am unkind to Er-lang and San-lang? If it weren't for His Majesty's excessive suspicion, would I be living in such fear!"

Lady Dou comforted him, "His Majesty will never believe he is suspicious, so in his eyes, he is never wrong. Naturally, it is you, my lord, who is overthinking it. It is your fault. Precisely because His Majesty is suspicious, he becomes so enraged when he guesses your thoughts, and he deliberately sows discord between you and Er-lang and San-lang. Perhaps he even intends to use them against you. This is, after all, His Majesty’s imperial art of governance."

Li Yuan sighed, "Deliberately sowing discord... Hmph, the late Emperor did the same to my Li family. My lady, speak with the Zhangsun and Yuwen families. The world is in chaos, and the future is uncertain. Let us finalize the marriages for Er-lang and San-lang this year. Only when they are settled can they focus on building their careers. I suspect they are also anxious about the current situation and will agree."

Lady Dou hesitated, "But General Zhangsun specifically told us that Guanyinbi is still young..."

Li Yuan said, "Let them marry first, and wait until they reach adulthood to consummate the marriage. Dade is also frail; even if Zhuniang is in good health, how could he consummate a marriage so early? Guanyinbi and Zhuniang are both being raised by your side; you must treat them as your own daughters."

Lady Dou immediately understood Li Yuan’s meaning.

Li Yuan not only wanted his sons to marry early so they could focus on their careers, but he also saw the world descending into chaos and wanted to bind himself to Yuwen Bi and Zhangsun Sheng in advance, lest those two families defect to others.

Furthermore, Lady Dou was unsure if her husband still harbored the idea of using Guanyinbi and Zhuniang as links to keep the two brothers tethered to him.

Li Yuan added, "You must instruct Guanyinbi and Zhuniang well. Let them know how much you and I cherish Er-lang and San-lang, and make sure they are never swayed by others."

Lady Dou sighed deeply in her heart and smiled, "That goes without saying."

...

Li Xuanba knew nothing of the court affairs, though he and his second brother had long discussed whether their father’s promotions would affect their own careers.

But they had four teachers—Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, Xue Daoheng, and Zhangsun Sheng—and Teacher Yu Shinan, though quiet, could also play a crucial role when needed.

After the brothers told their teachers their concerns, the teachers told them not to worry; they would keep an eye on such trivial matters.

When Li Xuanba left the Central Plains, he had handed over all the "financial relationships" with Yang Guang’s close ministers to Zhangsun Sheng.

Zhangsun Sheng could manage the Western Regions, and he could certainly manage the "Great Sui."

As for the affairs of the court, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba could rest easy, no longer burdened by worry.

Finally arriving at Yiwu City, Shigui Khan personally came to the city gates to welcome them, acting as if Yiwu City were his own.

In reality, Yiwu City had already become territory of the Western Turks. The Great Sui generals stationed there had withdrawn, and although the soldiers still wore Great Sui uniforms, they were already eating the food of the Western Turks. It would not be until the fourth year of the Zhenguan era that the lord of Yiwu City would submit to the Great Tang.

Li Xuanba did not show the shame or anger that Shigui Khan had expected. Instead, he smiled brightly and bowed to the Khan with neither arrogance nor servility, "I have long heard of your great name, Khan. Seeing you today, you are truly as vigorous as in your youth; your reputation is well-deserved."

Shigui Khan’s face twitched when he heard Li Xuanba call him "as vigorous as in his youth."

Shigui Khan had driven away his nephew, Chuluo Khan, who was now a mere mascot by Yang Guang’s side. Since he was a generation older than Chuluo Khan, he was naturally already advanced in years.

In history, Shigui Khan would pass away in five or six years. He was already feeling the weight of his age.

Shigui Khan had tried to intimidate Li Xuanba, but Li Xuanba had refused to take the bait.

Li Xuanba had then subtly insulted Shigui Khan, pointing out that he was old and that the future of the Western Turks was uncertain.

After this exchange, Shigui Khan begrudgingly considered it a draw. His contempt for the young and frail-looking Li Xuanba diminished significantly, and he became willing to discuss serious matters.

Shigui Khan did not care about Li Xuanba’s travel fatigue and, without giving him time to rest, held a banquet in his honor.

Li Xuanba did not refuse. He only asked for a moment to bathe and change, tidying his appearance before attending the banquet.

Though Li Xuanba was thin and frail, his appearance was quite striking. The Western Turkic nobles felt a surge of favor toward him, though these gazes made Luo Shixin and Zhou Da grip the hilts of their blades.

The barbarian nobles were known for their lack of restraint, particularly favoring the delicate, pampered youths of the Central Plains.

Li Xuanba swept a glance over those who had offended him with their eyes and said to Shigui Khan, "Khan, I feel offended. For the sake of peace between the Great Sui and the Western Turks, may I kill a few of the people you brought?"

The Western Turkic nobles in the room were shocked. Some began cursing in the Turkic language.

Shigui Khan suppressed the clamor and said coldly, "General Li, what do you mean by this?"

Li Xuanba replied, "When two nations meet, if someone offends the Khan, the Great Sui would certainly punish the offender. Does the envoy of the Great Sui not receive the same treatment here? I thought the Khan wished to be on good terms with the Great Sui, but it seems the Khan is here to provoke us?"

Li Xuanba sighed, "Chuluo Khan is of no consequence; he will likely never set foot on the grasslands again. I had intended to talk to you about the Sassanid Empire. The King of the Sassanids is currently attacking Jerusalem in the Byzantine Empire; if they succeed, they might truly restore the borders of the ancient Achaemenid Empire. The Great Sui should be on good terms with them."

Shigui Khan was stunned, "You actually know about the Sassanid Empire?!"

Li Xuanba laughed heartily, "How could I not know about the Khan’s closest neighbor?"

Shigui Khan remained silent for a long time.

He pointed to one man and said, "This man is of the lowest status and dared to offend a noble guest; he should be executed."

Li Xuanba said, "Then I will give the Khan face and only execute him. Shixin."

Luo Shixin walked over to the Western Turkic noble, who was already being held down by Shigui Khan’s guards. He drew his curved blade and sheathed it in one motion, decapitating the man with a single stroke, the movement as fluid as flowing water.

A human neck is quite tough, and seeing Luo Shixin decapitate a man so effortlessly, everyone realized that this young lad possessed immense strength.

Recalling the reputation of the other "General Li," Shigui Khan completely abandoned his contempt for Li Xuanba.

He stood up and invited him, "Your brother is also a General Li. I am older than you; may I call you Li San-lang? This place is soiled; let us move to another room for the banquet and discuss the Sassanid Empire in peace."

Li Xuanba smiled, "Shigui Khan is an elder; of course, you may call me Li San-lang. Please."

Indeed, compared to the stray dog that was Chuluo Khan, the Sassanid Empire was the true heart-and-gut threat to the Western Turks.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第117章 从波斯说到罗马
chunks.chineseText:
第117章 从波斯说到罗马

萨珊国在华国历史中被称为波斯国。公元651年， 即唐高宗永徽二年被阿拉伯帝国所灭。
　　在初唐和盛唐时，无论是波斯国，还是后来被称为大食国的阿拉伯帝国， 仿佛就只有擅长做买卖和能歌善舞的印象。
　　因为华国史籍上， 将所有国家间的礼仪往来统称为“朝贡贸易”。所以仅看字面意义， 好像波斯和大食也是个向大唐俯首称臣的弱小属国。
　　其实波斯和大食在鼎盛时都是横跨亚欧的大帝国，经济文化科技都十分繁荣。
　　此时已经进入君士坦丁堡为首府的东罗马（拜占庭）帝国，虽衰退但还存在；波斯第二王朝萨珊帝国， 于隋末唐初极盛走向灭亡；后世称霸欧亚大陆桥的阿拉伯帝国，从此时诞生。
　　大唐这个“世界顶级大帝国”并非是孤独的。
　　仅仅在隋末唐初这短短的时间，波斯国差点灭亡东罗马帝国， 阿拉伯帝国强势崛起把波斯国灭了，东罗马帝国也被打得只剩下一个名义上的大一统。
　　从中亚到欧洲、北非， 三个帝国打成了一锅粥。
　　若不是有高原和沙漠的阻隔， 路途遥远艰难，出兵不方便，以萨珊帝国和阿拉伯帝国的侵略性，他们绝不会成为热情的波斯商人大食商人。
　　这些事中原人是不知道的。
　　以封建时代的交通状况，哪怕到了明清的时候， 南方发生民乱，可能北京一年后才知晓。中原对西域的了解， 基本是丝绸之路通到哪，地图就画到哪。时效性就更别提了。
　　如裴世矩编写的能让杨广龙颜大悦的“详细”西域地图志，仅仅是在张掖的市集上通过和西域商人聊天搜集信息， 就知道这时人对世界了解的匮乏。
　　现在吐蕃还式微。在大隋人眼中， 西突厥的敌人当然就只是东突厥和大隋。他们游说突厥人， 只会从大隋和另一个突厥出发。
　　东突厥与西域联系不多。
　　东突厥的北边是荒无人烟的西伯利亚大雪原， 南边是大隋，西边是西突厥，东边多走几步就跳海，所以他们的视野很狭小，注意力只放在中原。
　　但西突厥不一样。
　　西突厥的疆域基本在中西亚，最强盛的时候，西边国土濒临里海。
　　虽然他们向往华国中原的繁荣，也想重新把东突厥吞并，但他们与波斯帝国，以及后来的阿拉伯帝国也一直在争夺领土。
　　唐高宗时苏定方俘获贺鲁可汗，西突厥可汗一脉传承断绝，“西突厥汗国”灭亡。但西突厥部落本身西迁，仍旧活跃在西亚和东欧的领土上。
　　这就是后期西突厥残部反复与唐朝拉扯，差点把唐朝财政拖垮的原因。
　　在此时中原人脑海中，并没有世界有多广阔的概念。有些人甚至认为地是有边界的，除了大唐之外全是寸草不生的蛮荒之地。
　　西突厥人被赶走，就应该快灭亡了，怎么还能卷土重来，越打越多？
　　即使古籍中有东罗马，西域商人也带来了波斯和大食的消息，但大部分大唐人亲眼所见的西域就是黄沙戈壁。人很难能想象出自己没见过的事物。
　　所以当李玄霸提起萨珊帝国时，射匮可汗感到的不是惊讶，而是惊悚。
　　如果不是他老成持重，见多识广，很快冷静下来，他手中的酒杯都差点丢出去。
　　李玄霸不仅提到了现在西突厥的心腹大患萨珊帝国，还提到了耶路撒冷之战。
　　耶路撒冷会在明年被萨珊帝国攻陷，也就是说，现在萨珊帝国的军队才刚刚推到耶路撒冷。
　　射匮可汗一直关注着萨珊帝国和东罗马帝国的战争。
　　很显然，萨珊帝国只要在东罗马帝国战争中获胜，下一个目标肯定是调头过来打西突厥。
　　这个消息他才刚刚收到，大隋人是怎么得知的？
　　他的人是在得到消息的第一时间就快马飞驰传递情报。大隋人就算也是第一时间得知消息，难道还能比自己的马更快？
　　射匮可汗对这个完全出乎预料的情况感到棘手。
　　他的汉语、波斯语都很熟练，还搜集了两国书籍阅读。
　　别看射匮可汗长得像个不识字的大老粗，他文化水平相当不错，读过不少华国的兵书，知道华国人各种阴谋诡计层出不穷，比如什么“远交近攻”玩得特别溜。
　　之前西突厥不惧怕大隋人，是因为他们知道大隋对西突厥以西的世界情况两眼一抹黑，就算挑拨离间也只会在东西突厥内部弄。
　　现在李玄霸提起“萨珊王朝”，言语之间对其好像还挺熟悉，射匮可汗就冒冷汗了。
　　你这个阴险的大隋人，该不会想对萨珊王朝远交，然后对西突厥近攻吧？！
　　当一个人掌握了超出常理的信息时，就会给对方形成巨大的心理恐怖压力。
　　一些信息，连西突厥贵族自己都不知道——西突厥仍旧是部落制，上层贵族掌握的信息和中下层贵族不对等，这是他们统治的基础之一。
　　所以射匮可汗赶紧借着李玄霸的杀鸡儆猴，将宴会转移到更私密的地方。
　　他也顾不上在大隋人面前装蛮夷了，精致的菜肴酒水摆上，他要和大隋使臣把酒言欢。
　　射匮可汗只留下了几个心腹作陪，李玄霸也只留下了周达、罗士信等四五个护卫，其余护卫在外面另摆了几桌。
　　射匮可汗为李玄霸斟酒，语气神情和刚才完全不一样：“李三郎居然了解萨珊帝国？我还以为大隋人都瞧不起这等偏远小国。”
　　李玄霸推阻道：“可汗，你也看出来了，我自幼病弱，喝不得酒。这次不能陪你尽兴了。”
　　射匮可汗笑道：“无事，我也老了，不能饮酒过多。来人，换成蜜水。你提起萨珊帝国，可喝过萨珊帝国特产的蜜水？”
　　李玄霸道：“萨珊帝国特产的蜜水，应该指石蜜吧？汉时西域就有进贡，实际上就是凝固的蔗糖而已。说起蔗糖，还是天竺那里的更美味。”
　　石蜜就是蔗糖？不是一种神奇的蜜蜂在石头上产的蜜吗？射匮可汗疑惑，但没有询问。
　　他见李玄霸言之凿凿，不敢暴露自己的信息短板。
　　射匮可汗道：“天竺的石蜜我也尝过，各有千秋。不过天竺比萨珊强盛，石蜜比萨珊的好也理所当然。”
　　李玄霸失笑：“天竺虽然辉煌过，但现在与萨珊比，可是太侮辱萨珊了。”
　　李玄霸当做没发现射匮可汗的试探，对萨珊帝国的历史侃侃而谈。
　　波斯在萨珊王朝之前的独立王朝，叫做阿契美尼德王朝，与华国东周同一个时代。
　　阿契美尼德王朝又被后世称为波斯第一帝国，极盛时包含了如今西突厥的领土。
　　波斯第一帝国想要吞并希腊，反被希腊马其顿帝国所灭。马其顿帝国又被罗马帝国所灭，成为罗马帝国的马其顿行省。
　　李玄霸品着蜜水，笑道：“马其顿行省，在我国古籍中称为蒙奇国。可汗肯定很了解汉时丝绸之路。蒙奇就是汉时丝绸之路的起点。汉和帝时，蒙奇国王遣使内附，被汉和帝赐予金印紫绶。哈哈哈哈，那都是五百年前的事了。”
　　李玄霸叹了口气，笑容颇有些落寞：“看古籍时，才知道强汉强汉，究竟有多强盛。我想波斯人也是如此想。萨珊皇帝御驾南征北战，大概就是想复兴波斯阿契美尼德王朝时的兴盛，就像是我们想要恢复汉时兴盛一样。”
　　射匮可汗握着水杯，力道大得仿佛想要把水杯捏碎。
　　他最讨厌的就是大隋人和他谈历史。
　　射匮可汗低头喝了一口蜜水，忍了。
　　李玄霸继续侃侃而谈，从历史说到了现在，重点提起了萨珊帝国的军队。
　　“萨珊帝国的贵族骑兵可不一般。他们顶尖的贵族也必须随军出征，不仅要配备自己和马的全身甲，还要配齐剑、骑枪、弓，斧锤全套武器，这装备真是华丽啊。”
　　“我二哥也有一支具装骑兵，穿戴的是皮甲和明光甲。听闻萨珊帝国的将领配备的是锁子甲。我已遣人去购买锁子甲，不知道锁子甲和我们的明光甲谁更胜一筹。”
　　“萨珊帝国的建筑很有意思，半球形的穹顶与我们棱角分明的屋檐很是不同。不知道他们这样的建筑形状，是不是受了大汉的‘天圆地方’思想熏陶？”
　　“他们丝织品虽然质量不如我们大隋，但色彩绚丽，很是新奇，我很喜欢。他们的钱币也很有意思，竟然是把皇帝半身像雕刻在上面。但我怎么看，那人形也过于抽象了些，不像个真人……”
　　李玄霸从军事谈到建筑，从建筑谈到艺术，又从萨珊的艺术发散到希腊和罗马的艺术。
　　射匮可汗时不时附和几句，基本都能和李玄霸聊上。
　　他越聊越心惊。
　　如果李玄霸刚才抛出一个“萨珊帝国”的词语，射匮可汗还能怀疑李玄霸是提前做了准备，想要凭借不多的信息吓唬他。
　　现在李玄霸完全打开了谈兴，完全就只是闲聊的态度，让射匮可汗明白，大隋真的了解萨珊，甚至可能比自己更了解。
　　比如他就不知道波斯帝国在一千年前还有个比现在更繁荣的“第一帝国”，更不知道希腊人五百年前居然向大汉称臣内附。
　　希腊离大汉也太远了吧！自己的情报系统都没有远到希腊去，只是从波斯人口中听到过希腊。
　　射匮可汗屡次想要打断李玄霸，让李玄霸说正事。
