### Chapter 119: Li Er and Li San Return to the Central Plains

Changsun Wuji readily agreed to the challenge. Spring in Zhangye was as cold as winter in the Central Plains, yet he rolled up his thick sleeves, revealing the corded muscles on his arms.

Li Xuanba’s expression shifted into that of an old man staring blankly at a smartphone.

He had intentionally pointed out Changsun Wuji’s identity not only to use Master Changsun’s reputation to suppress the Western Turkic Khaganate and ensure they behaved themselves in Zhangye without disturbing the people, but also, naturally, out of a bit of mischievous humor.

It was common knowledge that although the Tang dynasty did not strictly separate civil and military roles—with many officials serving as generals—most people still had a clear distinction between "civil" and "martial" expertise. Changsun Wuji, for instance, was a pure civil official who had never set foot on a battlefield.

Changsun Wuji would certainly have learned mounted archery, but his skills were surely not refined. Otherwise, given his relationship with Li Shimin, he would have been trailing behind Li Shimin, hacking down enemies long ago.

However, Li Xuanba was just looking for a bit of fun; he had no intention of making Changsun Wuji lose face. If Changsun Wuji had declined, he could have just brushed it off by saying, "This person is as naturally frail as I am."

Who would have thought that Changsun Wuji would appear so brimming with confidence, accepting all comers? It gave Li Xuanba a vivid hallucination of his own Second Brother.

What followed surprised Li Xuanba even more.

Changsun Wuji won.

He faced one warrior a day, and he won every single archery match.

Li Xuanba drew a sharp breath, as if he intended to inhale all the cold air in Zhangye to force the city into an early spring.

Seeing Li Xuanba’s shock, Changsun Wuji asked in great confusion, "What are you so surprised about?"

Li Xuanba replied, "I thought you were a civil official more inclined toward poetry and calligraphy?"

Changsun Wuji was stunned. "Ha? Why would you have such a strange misunderstanding? You, Li Er, and I grew up together. Haven't you been watching me diligently practice martial arts every day?"

Li Xuanba pondered. Ah, it seemed that was indeed the case.

The Changsun family, like his own, was a military meritocracy where every generation produced great generals; mounted archery and martial arts were family traditions.

Furthermore, Master Changsun’s archery was peerless. How could Changsun Wuji, taught by his own hand, be anything less than exceptional?

Then, in the original history... oh, in the original history, Changsun Wuji was raised by his uncle, Gao Shilian, and Gao Shilian was a pure scholar.

Li Xuanba looked at Changsun Wuji’s radiant, spirited appearance and suddenly realized that he was indeed very different from the version in his "memories."

"You’ve turned into a young military talent," Li Xuanba remarked with an air of seasoned maturity.

Changsun Wuji was silent for a moment, then asked suspiciously, "Li San, how on earth do you manage to make such plain, unremarkable words sound like you’re begging to be punched?"

Li Xuanba replied, "Isn't that just a problem with your own narrow-mindedness?"

Changsun Wuji clenched his fists. "Li Er isn't here now. No one is going to save you."

Li Xuanba called out loudly, "Xiao Wu! Shixin!"

Li Zhiyun came running, dragging Luo Shixin along. "Coming, coming! Even without the Second Brother, you still have me!"

Luo Shixin hesitated. "Are we really fighting? What if someone gets hurt?"

Changsun Wuji was speechless. "You’re actually calling for backup? Have you no shame?"

Li Xuanba coughed a few times. "You’re challenging a sickly weakling like me to a duel—have *you* no shame?"

Changsun Wuji was so irritated by Li Xuanba that he ground his teeth.

After grinding his teeth, he actually laughed first. "Your personality hasn't changed one bit from when we were younger."

Li Xuanba said, "Isn't that only natural?"

Changsun Wuji crossed his arms. "I heard you can practice divination and physiognomy. Father has finally agreed to let me ask you. Come on, take a look at me?"

Li Xuanba gave Changsun Wuji a thumbs up. "You are destined to be the Emperor’s brother-in-law!"

Changsun Wuji: "..." Your ancestors, that’s not a surprise at all.

Changsun Wuji asked, "Is Li Er on good terms with my little sister? Has he taken any concubines and neglected his wife?"

Li Zhiyun pricked up his ears. Luo Shixin covered his.

Li Xuanba replied, "They are on excellent terms. In fact, they are *too* close; my sister-in-law had too many children, which broke her health."

Changsun Wuji let out a long sigh. "No wonder Father nagged my little sister every day to marry late, and even after marriage, to wait until after he reached adulthood before consummating the union. You had already told Father about this, hadn't you?"

Li Xuanba said, "If I hadn't told Master Changsun about your and your sister-in-law's future, how else would he have been 'jolted from his deathbed'?"

Changsun Wuji’s mouth twitched. "Do you dare to say that line about 'jolted from his deathbed' to my father's face?"

Li Xuanba replied, "I’ve joked with the Master like this before. The Master is broad-minded; he doesn't mind."

Changsun Wuji rolled his eyes fiercely.

He had actually realized long ago that his father was likely far more indulgent and doting toward Li Xuanba than toward him. This must be because of Li Xuanba’s frail health.

Changsun Wuji knew that Li Xuanba was hiding things about his future. This concealment didn't mean Li Xuanba was lying, but rather that before he became the Emperor’s brother-in-law, his life with his little sister was likely not very good; otherwise, his father wouldn't have been "jolted from his deathbed."

When he was young, Changsun Wuji had once heard his drunken elder brother curse that once their father passed away, he would kick his mother, him, and his little sister out of the house.

Changsun Wuji connected this to Li Xuanba’s surprise at his martial arts skills today. If he had lived with his uncle, he probably would never have had the chance to find a master to learn martial arts.

With a little thought, Changsun Wuji guessed a thing or two about his future.

However, he didn't continue to question Li Xuanba. These hardships would not happen; his relationship with his elder brother had already eased. His brother now acted like a degenerate who just wanted to eat, wait for death, and inherit the title, leaving the burden of bringing glory to the Changsun family to him.

There was no need to create a rift with his brother over things that hadn't happened.

His brother was now on good terms with his little sister. This matter couldn't be let his sister know, either; she would surely be heartbroken.

After trading a few barbs and opening up about the secret of "divination and physiognomy," Changsun Wuji and Li Xuanba returned to the familiar, easygoing state of their childhood.

With Li Shimin having left Zhangye, the work of reviewing documents fell upon Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba dumped the Western Turkic delegation onto Changsun Wuji for practice and dragged Li Zhiyun along to help with the work.

Li Zhiyun turned around and "goaded" Luo Shixin into becoming a junior clerk. Watching Luo Shixin scratch his head in frustration, Li Xuanba felt his own fatigue from the work lighten considerably.

After clearing half of the accumulated documents, Li Xuanba finally saw the letter Li Shimin had left for him.

Li Xuanba held the letter, speechless for a long time.

It was one thing that the Second Brother left a letter without telling Changsun Wuji, but to just stuff it into a pile of documents like that—did he have some kind of problem?

Li Xuanba opened the letter. The first sentence read: "Halfway through the work yet?"

He took a deep breath.

Li Zhiyun jumped up from the couch and pressed his hand onto Li Xuanba’s. "Third Brother, if you tear up the letter in your anger now, you’ll just make me help you piece it back together later. Don't increase your little brother's workload!"

Li Xuanba ruffled Li Zhiyun’s hair hard before calming down to continue reading.

Li Zhiyun hugged his head and sat next to Luo Shixin, winking at him.

Luo Shixin: "Is your eye hurting?"

Li Zhiyun: "I mean, this family would fall apart without me!"

Luo Shixin: "Oh."

Li Xuanba glanced at his smug younger brother and continued reading the letter, suppressing his rage.

After a bit of teasing, Li Shimin quickly got to the point.

After Li Xuanba left, Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Changsun Wuji all arrived in Zhangye. Li Shimin had thought he could finally stretch his wings and expand his influence.

But to his surprise, no matter how many notices he posted or benefits he promised, it was difficult to recruit suitable talent.

Li Shimin personally visited the local scholars of renown. They all politely declined, claiming they had no intention of entering official service.

Li Xuanba sighed.

Although his Second Brother already had the three top-tier subordinates—Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Changsun Wuji—a top-tier team still needed a large number of mid-level staff to fill the ranks.

Especially for clerical work, the talent didn't need to be exceptionally brilliant, but the sheer volume of personnel required was immense.

When later generations listed the officials in the Prince of Qin’s mansion, they could name dozens of people with biographies, not to mention the mid-level clerks who didn't qualify for the list.

The Hexi region had few scholars to begin with. Those with even a modicum of ability hoped to hone their skills and try their luck in the Central Plains. Even going to the Western Capital, Daxing, where the Emperor rarely visited, to join a high-ranking aristocratic family was a better prospect.

If it weren't for Li Shimin’s status as the second son of the Duke of Tang, they wouldn't even have let him through the door; they would have likely used the excuse of "visiting friends" to shut him out.

A "marching general" held no appeal in their eyes; he would just be reassigned after the war. Everyone knew Li Shimin still had the Duke of Tang and the heir above him. The downside of following Li Shimin was too great. Unless Li Shimin had a title, they wouldn't send their collateral family members to join him, as it would be an insult to their family name.

The Sui dynasty inherited the customs of the Wei and Jin periods, placing great importance on lineage. While the emphasis on "family officials" and "old retainers" had faded compared to previous dynasties, it could not be ignored. Many aristocratic families in the Hexi region held hereditary official positions, and their kin served as high-ranking officials in the capital. Li Shimin’s "lineage" as the second son of the Duke of Tang was simply too low.

After trying for a while and finding it useless, Li Shimin stopped wasting his efforts.

He wanted to change "tracks" and recruit scholars from humble backgrounds.

But scholars from humble backgrounds were extremely rare in this era, and those who were actually useful were even rarer. Many such scholars considered it a mark of "family learning" if they could keep one or two annotated classics in their homes.

Li Shimin was extremely frustrated.

"No wonder you wanted to develop printing, A-Xuan. Although it's too late to cultivate talent by printing in Zhangye now, we can use the classics annotated by Master Gao, Master Yuwen, and Master Xue to bait the collateral descendants of aristocratic families. Printing is expensive. Tianzhu Wang has invited me as a guest; I'll go there and get some money."

Li Xuanba was stunned for a moment before realizing that while he had been busy raising funds to build his Second Brother’s cavalry and revitalizing the border markets of Zhangye, he had forgotten the "side quest" of spreading printed books.

Although he had been promoting printing in Daxing and Luoyang for several years, without strong support from the imperial court, there were only shops printing Confucian classics near the two capitals and in prosperous counties in the Central Plains. In a remote place like Zhangye, even paper was a rare commodity.

Everything had its priorities. He and his Second Brother were the only two working in Zhangye, and they lacked the energy to attend to everything, so they had to focus on the big picture.

Now with three helpers, he and his Second Brother finally had the time to think about other things.

"The aristocratic families in the Hexi region look down on the second son of the Duke of Tang? What a joke. Do they really think they can climb to a higher status?" Although Li Xuanba had long known of the arrogance of the aristocratic families, he had thought that the collateral descendants of local powerful families, who had no other opportunities, would be willing to join his Second Brother.

Li Zhiyun chewed on his brush handle and said, "Perhaps the collateral descendants are willing to come, but no one wants to be the first. They are afraid of being mocked by others, so they don't dare to come. The worse a scholar's family background, the more they care about their face."

Luo Shixin looked at Li Zhiyun in disbelief.

Li Zhiyun frowned. "What is that expression supposed to mean?"

Li Xuanba laughed. "His expression means, 'I didn't expect you, Fifth Brother, to be so smart.' He’s praising you."

Li Zhiyun muttered, "Don't treat me like a child."

Li Xuanba praised him, "Since you can hit the nail on the head so instantly, how could I still treat you like a child? I intend to hold a literary gathering to make a name for you. Can you take on this heavy responsibility?"

Li Zhiyun said, "No problem! But Third Brother, why not hold the literary gathering in your name?"

Changsun Wuji walked in with some documents. "Because they aren't worthy. Don't forget that your Third Brother is a *Xiucai* (Cultivated Talent)."

Li Zhiyun then remembered that his Third Brother held such a prestigious title.

In the seventh year of the Kaihuang era of Emperor Wen of Sui, an edict was issued: "Three people shall be recommended from each prefecture annually," known as the "Regular Tribute." Those among the "Regular Tribute" who were selected as *Xiucai* were the most outstanding in literary talent and policy debate.

However, although Emperor Wen of Sui started the Regular Tribute, he looked down on recommended talent, only recognizing those who held office through hereditary privilege. Because the Emperor did not value it, the selection of *Xiucai* was controlled by powerful officials.

Later generations evaluated it as: "The superiors had no intention of seeking talent, and there were no candidates to respond to the edict; even if there were one or two, they were envied."

The *Wenxian Tongkao* records that Du Zhengxuan, Du Zhengcang, and Du Zhenglun were three *Xiucai* from one family, and Du Zhengxuan and Du Zhengcang were suppressed by Yang Su and Su Wei, simply because they were jealous.

Even powerful officials like Yang Su and Su Wei would envy the title of *Xiucai*, which was famous throughout the world. Although the *Xiucai* of the Sui dynasty held only an empty title and almost no one reached high office, one could see its honor.

Li Xuanba’s status as a *Xiucai* was entirely "personally appointed" by Yang Guang, who wanted a child prodigy as an auspicious omen; otherwise, he would never have been selected.

But Li Xuanba’s current achievements were enough for the world to recognize him as a true *Xiucai*. Therefore, he could not easily hold a literary gathering in his own name.

After Changsun Wuji explained this to Li Xuanba, he added, "Although I say that, it's not impossible for you to hold a literary gathering. It's just that the scholars of Hexi look down on you, so you naturally have to adopt an attitude of looking down on their learning. Actually, when Li Er was recruiting talent, I suggested that after you returned, we should recruit in your name, but he refused."

Li Xuanba asked, "Why?"

Changsun Wuji shrugged. "He said that since my younger brother is so brilliant, they should be the ones coming to beg for your guidance on their knees, not you inviting them to a literary gathering."

Li Xuanba laughed. "I’ve been hanging around the military camp with the Second Brother for the past few years; they must have forgotten that I still hold the title of *Xiucai*, otherwise they would have come to ask for my guidance long ago."

Changsun Wuji said, "Du Keming thought the same. However, Du Keming agreed with letting them come to beg you on their knees."

Li Xuanba was speechless. What happened to the "Decisive Du"? How was the "Decisive Du" he knew just a professional instigator?

Changsun Wuji said, "Li Er would rather run to Tianzhu Wang to get money to open a printing shop and trade books for talent than have you lower yourself to beg people. So, the literary gathering can be held, but you must not lose face, or Li Er will beat me when he returns."

Li Xuanba said, "You can beat him back."

Changsun Wuji’s mouth twitched. "Shut up. What is your Fifth Brother good at? Although the younger brother taught by you and Li Er certainly won't be bad, we must play to his strengths."

Li Xuanba said, "Xiao Wu is good at calligraphy; even Master Yu has praised him highly."

Changsun Wuji smiled. "Then that’s no problem. Compared to Master Yu’s calligraphy, the writing of any other 'calligrapher' here is like a dog’s scrawl. I knew you would find an excuse that wouldn't lose face to hold a literary gathering once you returned. I’ve already drafted the list for you. Those circled are scholars with poor family backgrounds who might join the mansion. Although they aren't top-tier talent, they’ll be enough to serve as clerks after some training."

Seeing that Changsun Wuji had already prepared everything, Li Xuanba had the illusion of being at a loss because the work was too easy.

No wonder Changsun Wuji was the first among the meritorious officials of Lingyan Pavilion. His strategy was not obvious in the history books; he was likely doing the work of a chief of staff, just as he was now.

With Changsun Wuji having everything ready, Li Xuanba handed the literary gathering over to him, only appearing himself. He continued to devote his energy to internal affairs, not letting such trivial matters distract him.

Li Zhiyun practiced calligraphy with Luo Shixin every day, which Li Xuanba jokingly called "clutching at straws at the last minute."

On the day of the literary gathering, Li Zhiyun, as Li Xuanba and Changsun Wuji had expected, stunned everyone with his running script.

A group of scholars, under the guise of asking for calligraphy advice, quickly gathered around Li Zhiyun. Every day, Changsun Wuji dragged Li Xuanba along to test their learning as if they were picking radishes.

Changsun Wuji: "Still not many who are useful."

Li Xuanba: "Sigh."

It really is hard to dig for talent among the commoners at the end of the Sui dynasty.

...

"A-Xuan should have returned to Zhangye by now." Li Shimin took a sip of strong liquor to warm his body and let out a long sigh.

Zong Luohou, who was very perceptive, asked, "Is the General worried about his younger brother?"

Zong Luohou was a new "rising star" in the military recommended to Li Shimin by Fang Qiao.

Although Li Shimin was not valued by the aristocratic families of the Hexi region, many warriors from the countryside were willing to serve him.

Fang Qiao used the excuse that Xihai Commandery needed a large force to guard it, sending Du Ruhui to work in Xihai, while he himself claimed to be acting under imperial orders to recruit local warriors. He traveled from the prefectures of Hexi to the prefectures of Longxi, recruiting many warriors under the banner of "The Youngest Marching General, the Invincible Li Shimin."

Zong Luohou was from Jincheng Commandery. After Fang Qiao arrived in the area and visited the local people, he heard of Zong Luohou’s reputation for having peerless martial arts since childhood and immediately went to visit him.

The result of the visit pleasantly surprised Fang Qiao. Zong Luohou was not only peerless in martial arts but also brave and resourceful. If he were placed by the side of his lord for a period of time, he would surely become a great general.

Although Zong Luohou had heard of Li Shimin’s reputation, he felt ashamed to serve him because of Li Shimin’s age. But Fang Qiao was so good at dealing with people that the two became friends in a daze, and Zong Luohou had to agree to meet him once to try it out.

After that trial, Zong Luohou, who had been very perfunctory throughout the process, didn't even pack his luggage and never left.

Li Shimin sighed, "A-Xuan is my twin brother, not a younger brother. But I am indeed worried about him. He is frail, and he just went to Yiwu City to serve as an envoy to the Western Turkic Khaganate. I don't know if he caught a cold or fell ill."

Zong Luohou remembered who the "A-Xuan" the young general mentioned was. The rumors of the young general having a "master strategist who never fails" by his side had already spread to the prefectures of Longxi.

Zong Luohou said, "If the General trusts me, you can hand over the soldiers to me to command temporarily. I will surely win victory for the General."

Li Shimin had been invited by Tianzhu Wang to "get rich" this time, which meant attacking other tribes. Whether it was the Tuyuhun, the Qiang, or the Tibetan tribes, Tianzhu Wang had already declared himself Khan, and he would fight anyone who didn't submit.

Tianzhu Wang not only paid Li Shimin as a "mercenary" but also allowed Li Shimin to pick the spoils of war first; he only wanted the herdsmen and pastures.

The terms were so generous that Li Shimin immediately agreed: "Let's do it!"

But he had to do it behind A-Xuan’s back.

Although his brother told him to train the troops, he also emphasized that he shouldn't go when the mountains were blocked by heavy snow and the weather was harsh, and that safety was the most important thing.

But was there ever absolute safety in war? With Tianzhu Wang leading the way and providing logistics, Li Shimin believed the benefits far outweighed the risks, so he had to do it.

By the time he returned to Zhangye with the spoils, it wouldn't matter if his brother was angry.

"I trust you, but you are not yet familiar with my combat style. I will lead you in a few battles first, and then I will give you the opportunity to lead troops independently," Li Shimin said to Zong Luohou and the other generals. "Leading an army in battle is very different from leading local warriors to defend your hometown. I will teach you some orthodox military tactics that you will find useful in the future."

Zong Luohou and the other generals were immediately excited. "Yes!"

Training methods annotated by famous generals, like classics annotated by famous scholars, were often "family heirlooms" that only aristocratic military families could access. Although most of them were local powerful figures who had the opportunity to learn to read, they had no chance to see such "family heirlooms."

Although Li Shimin was young, he was already a young, famous general who ranked among the best in the world, even throughout history. The General was actually teaching them how to train troops and march personally. Those with ambition were flushed with excitement and extremely grateful to Li Shimin.

Zong Luohou was increasingly glad that he had believed his friend’s words. With such a lord, joining early was a profit!

Li Shimin didn't care about his subordinates' excitement.

He knew he would be Emperor in the future, so the generals who followed him first would naturally have the opportunity to be enfeoffed and become generals, and they would eventually lead troops themselves. Taking advantage of the fact that there were few wars in the world now, he would first teach someone who could lead troops independently so that he would have an easier time in the future.

"Rest is over, let's go!" Li Shimin tucked his empty wineskin onto his horse’s rump, waved to the good men behind him, and laughed, "Zong Luohou, you lure the enemy out, and I’ll lead the troops to flank them. Is your acting good enough? Don't hold me back!"

Zong Luohou said, "General, how about you lure the enemy and I flank? My martial arts are definitely up to it!"

Li Shimin laughed and whipped Zong Luohou’s horse’s rump. "Don't even think about it! The frustrating work is for you, and the fun work is for me; I am the General!"

Zong Luohou sighed, "As you command."

After pretending to sigh, he couldn't help but laugh along with the young general.

Zong Luohou waved his horse whip, followed by the young general’s side, treading on the mud where the snow had just melted, galloping toward the direction of the midday sun.

...

In Daxing City, Yuwen Bi and Changsun Sheng were cursing loudly, while Gao Jiong and Xue Daoheng surrounded them to comfort them.

Yuwen Bi cursed, "That scoundrel Li Yuan is not acting like a human! Er-lang and San-lang’s careers have only just started to improve, and he’s making them come back to get married! He even persuaded the Emperor to issue an edict!"

Changsun Sheng cursed, "My Guanyinbi is only thirteen! How can she leave her parents so early!"

Gao Jiong and Xue Daoheng sighed repeatedly.

They were racking their brains to find words to comfort Yuwen Bi and Changsun Sheng when Gao Biaoren, the son of Gao Jiong who stayed at home to take care of his father, ran over in a hurry. "Father! Father! Something terrible has happened!"

Gao Jiong said, "How bad could it be? It can't be that Yang Guang is wary of me again."

Gao Biaoren stopped. "Oh, no. It’s that the Emperor has ordered another expedition against Goguryeo."

Gao Jiong: "..."

He sighed and said to Yuwen Bi and Changsun Sheng, "Why don't you just agree? I see that the world is about to fall into chaos. If you don't hold the wedding now, who knows how many years it will be before you can."

Yuwen Bi hesitated.

Changsun Sheng said with a straight face, "My daughter is still young; it’s just right to marry in a few years!"

Gao Jiong said, "Once Li Yuan raises his army, aren't you afraid that Li Yuan will stuff a few daughters of defeated generals into Li Er-lang’s backyard and produce an illegitimate eldest son before your daughter enters the house? An illegitimate eldest son of an Emperor is much more troublesome than that of an ordinary family."

Changsun Sheng frowned. "Li Er-lang is not that kind of person."

Gao Jiong said, "Don't place your hopes on others. You should marry your daughter off first so you can bargain with the Li family, demanding that no one be allowed into the backyard before Li Er-lang consummates the marriage with your daughter."

Changsun Sheng still frowned.

Gao Jiong said, "I trust Li Daxiong’s character more than you do. I believe he will never do anything that violates his promises. But even if you trust the other party, you should not give away the initiative in matters where you can control it yourself. You should understand this, too."

Changsun Sheng sighed. "Gao Gong is right."

Yuwen Bi said, "I’m still worried about Er-lang and San-lang’s careers."

Gao Jiong said, "San-lang, you go to Zhangye to guard the Hexi region for Er-lang and San-lang. You don't need to do anything; just listen to Fang Qiao, Du Ruhui, and Changsun Wuji. You only need to use your title as the Duke of Bohai to hold down the other officials for them."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第119章 李二李三回中原 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
高颎的次子高弘德受封应国公，已经早逝；三子高表仁虽未出任职官，但在隋文帝时就因为高颎的功劳得封渤海郡公。

所以高颎越看李渊越不喜。

若李渊诸子将来争夺太子之位，那确实是有必争的理由。

但李渊又不知道他将来会当皇帝。李二郎李三郎因为太过优秀而被要求忍让，还被独孤老夫人打压？这也太可笑了。

别说李渊两个次子将来肯定有本事自己赚爵位，高颎的三子高表仁还在牙牙学语的时候就是渤海郡公了。

李渊要有本事，早早给家中诸子赚得爵位，哪需要李建成护个世子的位置护得魔怔。

因功封爵需要熬资历和年龄，但门荫得爵只看父辈功劳。如果李二郎和李三郎早早得爵，争霸天下的时候就不会这么被动。

李渊今年都四十八岁了。杨广穷兵黩武，他混战功的机会多得是，居然还没能给家中幼子赚得爵位，可不是废物？

越临近天下大乱，李渊离皇帝的位置越近，高颎就越看他不顺眼。

高表仁不高兴道：“父亲，我只是不想出仕，但我也不是没有本事，还不至于被三个年纪比我小的人比下去。”

高颎道：“你的本事我比你清楚。你能为能臣，但那三人皆能为名相。”

高表仁瘪嘴：“是。不过父亲，我擅自去张掖，会不会被皇帝忌惮？”

高颎神色淡然：“他此次去高丽，就没有余力再管西域的事了。太子不会坐以待毙。”

长孙晟、宇文弼、薛道衡三人听言皆叹。

薛道衡捶胸顿足：“杨广的两个太子都是好的，偏偏大隋的气数在杨广手中尽了啊！”

长孙晟道：“这是好事。这两个太子再好，能有李二郎好？”

薛道衡指着长孙晟的鼻子骂：“你就是等着当国丈是吗！”

长孙晟慢条斯理道：“是。”

薛道衡：“……”

老头子气得拂袖转身，背对着长孙晟生闷气。

宇文弼打圆场：“事已至此，大隋注定败在杨广手中，玄卿你何必再为大隋难受？杨广试图杀你的时候可没难受。”

薛道衡委屈道：“我知道，但就是难受，就是觉得对不起先帝。”

宇文弼、薛道衡和长孙晟都露出黯然的神色。

只有高颎在心里道，如果隋文帝在天有灵，那自己可太高兴了。

他在隋文帝时就差点被“走狗烹”了。

在同僚哀悼隋文帝时，高颎就拉着儿子叮嘱，让他收住那股清高文人的臭脾气，在张掖郡多吃羊肉少说话。

高表仁叹气。

有两个天才师弟真的好烦啊。他从父亲最爱的幼子变成路边被嫌弃的杂草了。

不过张掖的羊肉真的比大兴的羊肉还好吃吗？吸溜，三郎的手艺可不错，让他给我做了一顿烤全羊再回来成亲！

……

李世民高高兴兴赶着绑着金银绸缎的牛羊回张掖。

李玄霸看着那又见不到头的牛羊，只能长叹一口气。

他就知道，叮嘱是没用的，二哥要能老实，还需要魏徵什么事？

“哎呀，看见哥哥送给你的生辰礼，你笑一笑嘛。”李世民逗弄弟弟，“来，笑一个，迟来的生辰快乐。”

李玄霸从袖口摸出一个卷轴：“迟来的生辰礼。”

李世民打开卷轴，看着上面已经安排好职位的文吏名字，笑容淡去：“你还是利用你秀才的名声……”

李玄霸打断道：“我以为小五寻友的名义召开文会。”

李世民愣住：“啊？小五？小五还这么小？他开什么文会？”

李智云从李玄霸的身后走出，哀怨道：“我就知道二兄不会说我好话，故意藏在三兄身后。”

李世民不仅没有尴尬，还伸手给了李智云脑袋一下。

李玄霸道：“小五擅书，他的书法连河右诸郡自诩擅书者都自愧不如。”

李世民嫌弃道：“河右边塞能有什么擅书者？被贬谪来的吗？还不如我。”

李玄霸无奈：“我们二人都是师从虞老师，天底下字比我们写得好的人不多。你和河右士子比什么？不嫌丢脸。对了，高师兄来了，他说也有生辰礼给我们，要等你来了才说。”

李世民赶紧一手拽一只弟弟往马车上走：“高师兄来了？你不早说。长孙四郎，剩下的事交给你了。啊，周达，罗士信，你们带宗罗睺好好逛逛张掖城。还不快走！”

李玄霸：“痛痛痛！”

李智云：“啊啊啊二兄你轻点！”

长孙无忌看着对他不客气到连基本礼数都不讲的李世民，驾着马车带着弟弟扬长而去，不断嘀咕“交友不慎”。

他抬头看向看不到头的牛羊，心中又是惊喜又是头疼。

“大德啊大德，你之前真是辛苦了。”

……

李世民把马车赶成了战车，仗着张掖现在还不算暖和，城里没多少人，一路风驰电掣回到家。

高表仁正跷着腿一手牛肉干一手书，看得十分投入。

李世民扯着大嗓子喊道：“高三郎，你既然来了，怎么不到门口迎接我？”

高表仁头也不抬：“我堂堂渤海郡公去城门口迎接你？”

李世民笑着冲上前：“对啊，快来拜见行军大将。”

高表仁叹气。

他把肉干和书放下，拍了拍手：“拜见行军大将。”

李世民拱手：“拜见渤海郡公。”

两人装模作样结束后，嘻嘻哈哈勾肩搭背。

虽然高表仁比李世民大了十几岁，但两人相处起来看不出岁数的差距，仿佛兄弟般亲密。

李世民笑道：“师兄，你带了什么生辰礼，这么神秘，还非要我回来才送？”

高表仁从怀里掏出圣旨：“李二郎、李三郎，接旨。”

李世民懒得接旨，他抢过高表仁手中的圣旨：“怎么？陛下终于肯给我和阿玄封爵……啊？什么？赐婚？什么毛病啊，我和观音婢哪还需要他赐婚？哦？这么多赏赐？谢陛下赐婚。”

“市侩。”高表仁嫌弃，“这是你父亲求的旨意，让你们先去太原成婚，再回张掖。”

因为这事太过突然，李玄霸的喜都被惊吓掉了。

李玄霸疑惑道：“为何这么急？”

高表仁道：“父亲推测，一是因为你二人已经十六岁，该是成婚的年龄；二是天下即将大乱，唐国公可能在做准备了，所以想先拴住亲家。”

李玄霸松了口气：“那还好。我还以为他现在就忌惮我们，想阻拦我和二哥的事业。”

高表仁道：“现在还不用担心。你们年少，现在所做的事业不都是他的事业。唉，我怎么没有你们这么好的儿子。”

李世民骂道：“滚！小心以后我当了皇帝，让你改口叫我父亲！”

高表仁道：“好啊，我这就给父亲写信。”

“去去去。”李世民踹高表仁。

李玄霸继续愁眉苦脸：“现在正是紧要关头，希望我们去太原成婚这半年时间不要出事。”

高表仁道：“肯定会出事。陛下又亲征高丽了。所以父亲让我过来帮你们镇守张掖，我渤海郡公的爵位还是很唬人的。”

李世民收起笑容，皱眉道：“陛下派你来帮我们镇守张掖？”

高表仁摇头：“我只是去求了陛下，让我传旨。”

李玄霸和李世民异口同声道：“荒唐！危险！”

高表仁道：“父亲说，此次陛下三征高丽失败，肯定无力掌控西域，我在西域做什么都不会有危险。消息传不到陛下耳中。”

李玄霸和李世民对视一眼。

李世民皱眉不语。

李玄霸叹息道：“二表兄他……他不会是想趁机逼宫吧？”

高表仁道：“父亲是这么推断。”

李世民取下帽子，重重砸在地上：“杨广竟逼迫表兄如此！”

他心中悲怒时，忍不住又涌出一丝迷茫。

我将来……也会被逼迫如此吗？

李玄霸拍了拍二哥的肩膀：“哥，别多想，干就完事。”

李世民扯了扯嘴角：“别学我说话。”

他心里不迷茫了。
chunks.englishText:
Gao Jiong’s second son, Gao Hongde, had been enfeoffed as the Duke of Ying, but he had passed away early. His third son, Gao Biaoren, though he had never held an official government post, had been granted the title of Duke of Bohai during the reign of Emperor Wen of Sui, thanks to his father’s meritorious service.

Because of this, the more Gao Jiong looked at Li Yuan, the less he liked him.

If Li Yuan’s sons were to vie for the position of Crown Prince in the future, they certainly had a reason to fight for it.

But Li Yuan did not know that he would one day become Emperor. That Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were being forced to show restraint and were even being suppressed by the old Lady Dugu simply because they were too outstanding? That was truly laughable.

Not to mention that Li Yuan’s two sons would surely be capable of earning their own titles in the future, Gao Jiong’s third son, Gao Biaoren, had been the Duke of Bohai since he was still a toddler learning to speak.

If Li Yuan had any real ability, he would have earned titles for his sons long ago, rather than needing Li Jiancheng to guard his position as the Heir Apparent with such obsessive madness.

Enfeoffment based on merit required years of service and age, but titles inherited through the "shadow privilege" of one's father depended solely on the father's achievements. If Li Erlang and Li Sanlang had obtained titles early on, they would not have been so passive when the time came to contend for the world.

Li Yuan was already forty-eight years old this year. With Yang Guang constantly waging wars, there were plenty of opportunities to rack up military merit. The fact that he hadn't yet managed to earn titles for his younger sons—wasn't that the mark of a failure?

The closer the world came to chaos, and the closer Li Yuan moved toward the throne, the more Gao Jiong found him an eyesore.

Gao Biaoren said unhappily, "Father, I simply don't wish to enter officialdom, but it’s not as if I lack ability. I’m certainly not going to be outshone by three people younger than me."

Gao Jiong replied, "I know your abilities better than you do. You are capable of being a competent official, but those three are all capable of being legendary chancellors."

Gao Biaoren pouted, "Fine. But Father, if I go to Zhangye without authorization, will the Emperor hold a grudge against me?"

Gao Jiong’s expression was indifferent. "With his current campaign against Goguryeo, he has no energy left to manage affairs in the Western Regions. The Crown Prince will not sit idly by and wait for his doom."

Changsun Sheng, Yuwen Bi, and Xue Daoheng all sighed upon hearing this.

Xue Daoheng beat his chest and stamped his feet, "Yang Guang’s two sons were both fine men, yet the destiny of the Great Sui has been exhausted in Yang Guang’s hands!"

Changsun Sheng said, "This is a good thing. No matter how good those two princes are, can they be better than Li Erlang?"

Xue Daoheng pointed at Changsun Sheng’s nose and cursed, "You’re just waiting to become the Emperor’s father-in-law, aren't you!"

Changsun Sheng replied unhurriedly, "Yes."

Xue Daoheng: "..."

The old man was so angry he flicked his sleeves, turned around, and stood with his back to Changsun Sheng, sulking.

Yuwen Bi tried to mediate, "The matter has reached this point; the Great Sui is doomed to fall at the hands of Yang Guang. Xuanqing, why must you continue to suffer for the Sui? Yang Guang didn't suffer when he tried to have you killed."

Xue Daoheng said aggrievedly, "I know, but it just hurts. I feel I have failed the late Emperor."

Yuwen Bi, Xue Daoheng, and Changsun Sheng all wore somber expressions.

Only Gao Jiong thought to himself: If the late Emperor Wen of Sui had a spirit in heaven, he would be overjoyed.

He had nearly been "discarded like a hunting dog" back during Emperor Wen’s reign.

As his colleagues mourned the late Emperor, Gao Jiong pulled his son aside to warn him: put away that arrogant, scholarly temper, eat more mutton in Zhangye Commandery, and speak less.

Gao Biaoren sighed.

Having two genius junior brothers was truly annoying. He had gone from being his father’s favorite youngest son to a discarded weed by the roadside.

But was the mutton in Zhangye really tastier than the mutton in Daxing? *Slurp.* Sanlang’s cooking skills were quite good; he would make him prepare a whole roasted lamb before he went back to get married!

...

Li Shimin happily drove the cattle and sheep, which were laden with gold, silver, and silk, back to Zhangye.

Li Xuanba looked at the endless herd of cattle and sheep and could only heave a long sigh.

He knew it—warnings were useless. If his Second Brother could be sensible, what would they even need Wei Zheng for?

"Oh, come on, look at the birthday gift your brother brought you. Smile a little," Li Shimin teased his younger brother. "Come on, give me a smile. Happy belated birthday."

Li Xuanba pulled a scroll from his sleeve. "A belated birthday gift."

Li Shimin opened the scroll and looked at the names of the civil officials already arranged for various positions. His smile faded. "You’re still using your reputation as a scholar..."

Li Xuanba interrupted, "I’m holding a literary gathering in the name of Xiao Wu seeking friends."

Li Shimin was stunned. "Huh? Xiao Wu? Xiao Wu is still so young? What kind of literary gathering is he holding?"

Li Zhiyun stepped out from behind Li Xuanba, looking aggrieved. "I knew Second Brother wouldn't say anything good about me, so I hid behind Third Brother on purpose."

Li Shimin didn't feel embarrassed at all; instead, he reached out and gave Li Zhiyun a smack on the head.

Li Xuanba said, "Xiao Wu is skilled in calligraphy. Even those in the various commanderies of Heyou who pride themselves on their calligraphy are put to shame by his."

Li Shimin said disdainfully, "What kind of calligraphy experts could there be on the Heyou frontier? Exiles? They’re not even as good as me."

Li Xuanba sighed helplessly, "We both studied under Teacher Yu; there aren't many people in the world who write better than us. Why are you comparing yourself to the scholars of Heyou? Aren't you ashamed? By the way, Senior Brother Gao is here. He said he has a birthday gift for us, but he’s waiting for you to arrive before he says anything."

Li Shimin hurriedly grabbed a brother in each hand and headed toward the carriage. "Senior Brother Gao is here? Why didn't you say so earlier? Changsun Silang, leave the rest to you. Ah, Zhou Da, Luo Shixin, take Zong Luohou out to explore Zhangye City properly. Hurry up!"

Li Xuanba: "Ouch, ouch, ouch!"

Li Zhiyun: "Ah, ah, ah, Second Brother, be gentle!"

Changsun Wuji watched Li Shimin, who was so impolite that he didn't even observe basic etiquette, drive the carriage away with his brothers, muttering "bad company" under his breath.

He looked up at the endless sea of cattle and sheep, feeling both pleasantly surprised and overwhelmed with a headache.

"Dade, oh Dade, you really have had it hard."

...

Li Shimin drove the carriage like a war chariot. Relying on the fact that it wasn't quite warm yet in Zhangye and there weren't many people in the city, he flew back home at breakneck speed.

Gao Biaoren was sitting with his legs crossed, one hand holding beef jerky and the other a book, reading with great focus.

Li Shimin shouted at the top of his lungs, "Gao Sanlang, since you’re here, why didn't you come to the gate to welcome me?"

Gao Biaoren didn't even look up. "Me, the dignified Duke of Bohai, going to the city gate to welcome you?"

Li Shimin laughed and rushed forward. "That’s right, come and pay respects to the Commanding General."

Gao Biaoren sighed.

He put down the jerky and the book, clapped his hands, and said, "Greetings to the Commanding General."

Li Shimin cupped his hands. "Greetings to the Duke of Bohai."

After their mock formalities, they laughed and threw their arms around each other's shoulders.

Although Gao Biaoren was more than a dozen years older than Li Shimin, there was no visible gap in their ages; they were as close as brothers.

Li Shimin smiled, "Senior Brother, what kind of birthday gift did you bring? It’s so mysterious that you insisted I return before giving it to me."

Gao Biaoren pulled an imperial decree from his robes. "Li Erlang, Li Sanlang, receive the decree."

Li Shimin couldn't be bothered with the formalities; he snatched the decree from Gao Biaoren’s hand. "What? Is the Emperor finally willing to grant titles to me and A-Xuan... Huh? What? A marriage decree? What kind of nonsense is this? Why would Guanyinbi and I need him to grant a marriage? Oh? So many rewards? Thank you, Your Majesty, for the marriage grant."

"Vulgar," Gao Biaoren said with disdain. "This is a decree your father requested. He wants you to go to Taiyuan to get married first, then return to Zhangye."

Because the matter was so sudden, Li Xuanba’s joy was replaced by shock.

Li Xuanba asked, puzzled, "Why the rush?"

Gao Biaoren said, "Father speculates that, first, it’s because you two are already sixteen, the age for marriage; second, the world is about to fall into chaos, and the Duke of Tang is likely making preparations, so he wants to tie down his in-laws first."

Li Xuanba breathed a sigh of relief. "That’s fine then. I thought he was already wary of us and wanted to obstruct the cause you and Second Brother are working toward."

Gao Biaoren said, "No need to worry about that yet. You are young, and isn't the work you are doing now essentially his work? Sigh, why don't I have sons as good as you?"

Li Shimin cursed, "Get lost! Be careful, or when I become Emperor, I’ll make you change your tune and call me Father!"

Gao Biaoren said, "Fine by me, I’ll write a letter to my father right now."

"Go on, go on," Li Shimin kicked Gao Biaoren.

Li Xuanba continued to look worried. "This is a critical juncture. I hope nothing happens during the six months we spend in Taiyuan for the wedding."

Gao Biaoren said, "Something will definitely happen. The Emperor has launched another personal campaign against Goguryeo. That’s why Father sent me here to help you guard Zhangye; my title as the Duke of Bohai is still quite intimidating."

Li Shimin stopped smiling and frowned. "The Emperor sent you to help us guard Zhangye?"

Gao Biaoren shook his head. "I just begged the Emperor to let me deliver the decree."

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin said in unison, "Absurd! That’s dangerous!"

Gao Biaoren said, "Father says that since the Emperor’s third campaign against Goguryeo is bound to fail, he will certainly lack the power to control the Western Regions. Nothing I do in the Western Regions will be dangerous. The news won't reach the Emperor’s ears."

Li Xuanba and Li Shimin exchanged a look.

Li Shimin frowned, remaining silent.

Li Xuanba sighed, "Second Cousin... he wouldn't be thinking of taking this opportunity to force the Emperor to abdicate, would he?"

Gao Biaoren said, "That is what Father inferred."

Li Shimin took off his hat and slammed it hard onto the ground. "Yang Guang has actually forced Cousin to this point!"

As grief and anger welled up in his heart, he couldn't help but feel a sliver of confusion.

Will I... also be forced to this point in the future?

Li Xuanba patted his Second Brother’s shoulder. "Brother, don't overthink it. Just do what needs to be done."

Li Shimin twitched the corner of his mouth. "Don't copy the way I talk."

He wasn't confused anymore.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第120章 父子重逢太原城
chunks.chineseText:
第120章 父子重逢太原城

这“赐婚”旨意砸得李世民和李玄霸猝不及防， 计划都乱了。
　　李世民心很宽。虽然他郁闷了一下，但想着能提前把观音婢娶进门，他瞬间就高兴起来。
　　李玄霸最初表现得豁达， 但一直在为计划被打乱生闷气。
　　虽然李玄霸给自己做了许久心理建设， 未来的唐高祖的位置肯定是李渊坐， 但他也想让二哥早几年登基。
　　他的算盘都打好了，二哥在河右之地发展，趁着中原大乱和边塞失去联系， 把西域、河右和陇西诸郡都扫平了。等父亲起兵的时候，二哥就从陇西挥师东进，在父亲还在呼哧呼哧赶路的时候， 一举攻占大兴，改名长安。
　　李玄霸坚持认为， 二哥在历史中之所以那么被动， 是因为他的战功是李渊起兵后才获得，名义上他那时只是唐高祖李渊的将领，兵权和后勤都要依靠李渊获得。
　　历史中的李世民十六岁出策救驾初显才华，十八岁随父起兵，开始天策上将的一生。
　　如今二哥十岁生擒吐谷浑伏允可汗， 十三岁成为虎贲郎将，十四岁镇守河右收复西海郡。李玄霸都联系好西突厥了， 在隋朝灭亡前拉着二哥给东突厥一个大的，完成在“当皇帝之前超越冠军侯”的成就。
　　众所周知，李世民的战绩“诟病”在于“只”有内战辉煌， 该打外战的时候他就当皇帝不能领兵， 好不容易说服群臣御驾亲征高丽但没达到既定灭国目标。
　　虽然大部分后世人都认为李世民如果不当皇帝， 封狼居胥燕然勒石定有他的名字， 但现实是他当了皇帝，这就成为了永远的遗憾。
　　所以李玄霸为二哥鼓劲：【二哥支棱起来，努力啊，你能完成封狼居胥燕然勒石成就的时间越来越少了！不要遗憾终身！】
　　这话不能说出口，但可以在心声里唠叨。
　　李世民捂住耳朵捂不住心，绕着李玄霸三米远走。
　　感谢弟弟的心声范围没有随着年龄增长而增加，否则会把自己烦死。
　　不过李玄霸这么一叨叨，李世民的心情也沉重了。
　　身为天才将领，谁没有个封狼居胥燕然勒石的愿望？
　　“如果我在当皇帝之前完不成这个目标，就要苦一苦阿玄了。”李世民背着弟弟，拉着长孙无忌的手暗地谋划，“你一定要帮我从京城偷跑御驾亲征。”
　　长孙无忌狠狠翻白眼。
　　你倒是无事，我怕不是会被李三郎下狱吃几个月牢饭，小妹都救不了我！
　　但李世民的请求长孙无忌从小就不知道怎么拒绝，心里再吐槽也只能先应了。
　　李世民和李玄霸离开张掖前，把房乔和杜如晦也紧急叫了回来。
　　当了几年县令，就从腼腆清高文人进化成交际一把手的房乔，对李世民和李玄霸拍胸脯保证：“我会尽全力安抚好河右陇西官吏之心。”
　　杜如晦打着哈欠道：“留点厉害的将领给我，你们养兵全靠抢草原的牛羊，我可没办法领兵。”
　　李世民道：“我会将周达等老将留下，带走从河右新招的将士。克明放心用。”
　　杜如晦道：“商队的钱财也全由我支配？”
　　李世民看向李玄霸。
　　李玄霸想了想，道：“我把颜真留给你。”
　　杜如晦笑道：“有颜七郎在，我放心了。”
　　李世民对长孙无忌道：“观音婢和我成婚，你真的不回去？”
　　长孙无忌没好气道：“你当我不想回去？父亲不准我回去，说河右之地至关重要，不可有闪失。”
　　高表仁不仅带来了圣旨，也捎带了大兴城四个老头的信件。
　　此次成婚因天下大乱，杨广又再征高丽，太子那边又有异动，不宜大办。李渊和长孙晟、宇文弼商议，婚礼稍稍节俭一点，少请点人。
　　再者天下大乱，他们就算是想多请点亲戚，亲戚也来不了。如宇文珠的大伯在外做官，就无法前来。
　　长孙晟劝说儿子和李世民的其他友人，现在只是走个过场，将来的封后大典才是李世民和自家女儿真正的婚礼。
　　高表仁看着长孙晟的信，嘴角抽搐许久。
　　李渊还没当皇帝，长孙将军已经对准女婿当皇帝势在必得。他有一点点同情李渊。
　　突然成亲，不仅打乱了李世民和李玄霸的计划，也让亲事变得不完美。
　　李世民已经下决心封后大典重办一个隆重的婚礼。
　　李玄霸也……李玄霸想，如果自己能活到那个时候，问问宇文珠的意见，如果宇文珠愿意，就算违背礼制也要重办一次。
　　这样匆忙，实在是太委屈宇文珠了。
　　安排好所有事后，李世民带着罗士信、宗罗睺和在河右招的五百壮士回中原。
　　李玄霸从商队里带走了向固，把最熟悉自己手头事务的陈铁牛留给了长孙无忌。护卫他就蹭二哥的了。反正他是副将，也能算二哥带回家的将领之一。
　　四月，李世民和李玄霸回到了大兴城，接长孙晟、宇文弼一同前往太原。
　　高颎和薛道衡没有同行，不准备参加弟子的婚礼。
　　李世民和李玄霸都很遗憾。
　　高颎安慰道：“今年一定会出大事，我和玄卿仍旧被皇帝忌惮，只能低调一些。大丈夫做事，当顾全大局。”
　　薛道衡冷哼：“二郎，别只顾着你妻子的封后大典，记得给三郎的妻子加封，我给你们当司仪！”
　　李世民认真道：“是，老师。”
　　小聚之后，李世民和李玄霸再次启程。
　　其实他们本来准备在洛阳成婚。
　　几家人在洛阳都有宅子，婚礼流程更为简便，也能宴请更多的宾客。
　　但太原内有民贼四起，外有东突厥蠢蠢欲动，李渊脱不开身，便将二子婚礼举办地点改在了太原。
　　此番成亲，三家人都知道是联姻，宇文瑗和长孙晟为各自女儿要到足够多的实际利益后，就在这件事上妥协了。
　　宇文家和长孙家在太原提前置办了宅子，将仆人、嫁妆提前放入宅子中，成婚时两女就从新家出嫁。两处大宅子也将成为两女的嫁妆之一。
　　现在宇文珠和长孙小娘已经在太原备嫁。宇文弼和长孙晟是专门在大兴等李世民和李玄霸回来，好在路上仔细询问他们今后的策略。
　　路上说私密话，安全性比在城中高许多，他们可以畅所欲言。
　　长孙晟听闻李玄霸刚把西突厥使臣请来，相约一同攻打东突厥时，气得眼前一黑，差点晕过去，把李世民和李玄霸吓得手足无措。
　　“有长孙四郎在，一定能维护好和西突厥的关系，老师不必担心。”李玄霸安慰。
　　长孙晟拍着大腿愤怒道：“维护好和西突厥的关系有什么用？他还能变出个李二郎出来攻打东突厥？！”
　　李二郎摸摸鼻子，不敢说话。
　　明明不是自己和阿玄的错，为什么自己和阿玄要被骂。
　　宇文弼也唉声叹气，遗憾不已。
　　如果现在二郎三郎没被叫回来，估计都在准备给东突厥来个狠的了。
　　统一天下时，东突厥是心腹大患，一定会插手中原。明明可以提前预防，却阴差阳错，唉。
　　事已至此，生气也无济于事。长孙晟在马车上赶着给长孙无忌写信支招，教他好好安抚住西突厥使臣，拖个一年半载，不能让人跑了。
　　不，干脆让四郎以“妹妹出嫁，需要回家探亲”的名义，把这支西突厥使臣拐回太原。
　　天柱可汗那里也可以试试，多邀请些西域人来参加婚礼！
　　长孙晟瞬间在脑海中完成谋划，让亲信快马加鞭赶紧交给长孙无忌。
　　他看着亲信飞驰的骏马神色遗憾。
　　虽然他从死劫中挺了过来，但身体毕竟不如年轻时候，已经不能再在草原驰骋了。
　　若再年轻十岁，他就亲自去张掖。等女婿回来时，东西突厥说不准都分裂成东西南北突厥，绝对不会给女婿统一中原的道路上添乱。
　　年轻人天赋还成，经验还是限制了他们的本事啊。
　　宇文弼看长孙晟遗憾的模样，道：“你就服老了？我可不服老。好好养身体，说不准我们还有再建功立业的时候。”
　　长孙晟脸上的遗憾散去，目光坚定：“说得对。”
　　车厢外耳力极佳的李世民给弟弟使眼色。
　　李玄霸：【有话直说。】
　　李世民继续使眼色。要能在心里说，他何至于使眼色。
　　李玄霸：【你是想说，有老师在，你的小伙伴们的相位之争更艰难了。】
　　李世民：【对！】
　　李玄霸：【你可别了。老师年纪大，该是颐养天年的时候。你想累坏老师？】
　　李世民指车厢。
　　李玄霸：【呃，如果老师非要干活，那我们能有什么办法？房玄龄他们还年轻，可以等。就是杜兄和薛兄要好好养生了。话说薛兄究竟哪去了？怎么还没回来？】
　　李世民点头。对啊，薛兄跑哪去了？
　　与此同时，在筑紫岛挖贝壳的薛收打了个大大的喷嚏。
　　薛收摸着鼻子苦笑：“估计是李二李三在念我，也可能是老杜老房在嘲笑我。”
　　陈棱好奇道：“为何？难道不是你的亲人在想念你吗？”
　　薛收叹气：“这是直觉。”
　　陈棱笑道：“如果薛郎急着回去，我可派船送你一程。”
　　薛收摇头：“我既为将军幕僚，当为将军完成此功，再回去好好向友人炫耀。”
　　我薛收虽是书生，也能提三尺剑开疆扩土！
　　李三说这座岛上有金矿。他的使团遇到海盗迷了路，被驻守琉球备战倭国的陈棱救下，好不容易劝动陈将军攻打筑紫岛，怎么能半途而废？
　　况且陈将军智勇双全，自己跟在他身边为幕僚，将来才好劝他投向李二郎。
　　薛收摸了摸鼻子，继续挖贝壳：“现在友人肯定还在熬资历，等我跟随陈将军建功立业，回去嘲笑他们。”
　　陈棱大笑：“好……等等，你说的李二难道是指李世民李二郎？”
　　薛收道：“对。”
　　陈棱有点想打击薛收。
　　他虽然现在从中原得到的消息较为滞后，但李二郎生擒吐谷浑伏允可汗时他还在中原。
　　李二郎十岁就能生擒吐谷浑伏允可汗，现在三年多时间过去，若他能有机会再上战场，肯定没少立功。
　　真是一代英雄出少年啊。
　　陈棱决定对薛收再好几分。薛收的友人都是少年英才，将来前途无量。薛收肯定也一样。
　　……
　　四月初，李世民和李玄霸终于与家人重逢。
　　意气风发的李渊骑着马在百里外迎接两个儿子，见面还没给儿子拥抱，就被李世民抱怨。
　　“耶耶，阿玄刚帮我约好了西突厥可汗一同去吓唬东突厥，你就把我和阿玄叫回来。儿子将来如果错过了封狼居胥燕然勒石，都是耶耶你的错。”李世民不满道。
　　李渊笑容一滞：“有这事？”
　　他看向李玄霸。
　　李玄霸苦笑：“我去年十一月去伊吾城与西突厥可汗会面，真的很不容易。”
　　李渊尴尬得脑门上都冒出汗来：“你们不是刚夺回西海郡吗？怎么就要去打东突厥了？钱和粮哪来的？”
　　刚换完牙的李世民竖起大拇指，露出八颗牙齿咧嘴笑道：“西突厥可汗阔气，他说他出。”
　　李玄霸用老实巴交的语气道：“二哥打吐谷浑残部的时候都是天柱可汗出钱，打完后还让二哥率先挑选战利品。西域人真的很淳朴豪爽。”
　　李渊丈二和尚摸不着头脑。
　　西域人……淳朴豪爽？当他没有接触过来大隋的西域人吗！他还和吐谷浑人打过仗呢！
　　李渊摆手：“我不信。有那么容易？”
　　长孙晟从马车里出来，没好气道：“西突厥可汗和天柱王可汗派来庆贺李二郎李三郎成婚的使团都在路上了。我现在还在愁怎么和陛下说这件事。”
　　宇文弼也叹气：“是啊，现在天下大乱，二郎和三郎的婚事应当低调。如果他们来了，这如何低调？”
　　李渊：“……”
　　虽然被儿子埋怨了，被亲家抱怨了，但他心里美滋滋的！
　　李渊干咳了几声忍住笑意，假惺惺叹气道：“谁能想到你们如此闲不住？我还以为你们刚打完西海郡，肯定会休息一年半载，才让你们赶紧回来成亲。哎，你们兄弟二人真是从小就爱折腾，这可让我为难了。”
　　李渊忍了许久，还是没忍住得意地大笑：“好，好，是耶耶错了，小瞧了你们，哈哈哈哈哈哈。”
　　李世民抱怨地笑道：“耶耶，你别光顾着笑啊，要怎么补偿我！”
　　李玄霸看着二哥隐隐浮现的眷慕神色，心头一叹。
　　他也学着二哥的语气，面无表情道：“父亲，二哥在河右之地招文吏，那里的士人瞧不起二哥年少，都不肯来投效。父亲也开府了，麾下肯定很多文人……”
　　李玄霸单手握住缰绳，伸手：“我们要的不多，先来十个。”
　　李渊打趣道：“十个就够了？”
　　李世民嬉笑道：“多多益善！”
　　李渊用马鞭戳李世民的额头：“你还韩信点兵，多多益善是吗？好，这次是耶耶理亏，耶耶给你备齐人手，你带去张掖。”
　　说完，李渊脸色微沉：“不过是偏远之地豪强而已，居然还自诩世家，瞧不起唐国公府的门第了？哼。”
　　长孙晟和宇文弼从马车换马，听李渊和李世民、李玄霸父子三人闲聊。
　　见李渊这脸色，长孙晟道：“怎么？你又受世家气了？你家大郎不是荥阳郑氏女婿吗？有荥阳郑氏为你撑着，这河东之地难道还有谁敢给你脸色看？”
　　李渊抱怨：“别说荥阳郑氏了，一说就有气。”
　　长孙晟和宇文弼都是自家人，太原又是自己的地盘，李渊没什么不敢说的，便直接抱怨起来。
　　李玄霸仔细聆听，从李渊的抱怨中提取信息。
　　虽然李渊提前几年当上了太原留守和山西、河东慰抚使，但仍旧如原本历史一样，李渊常驻太原，负责山西事务；李建成常驻河东郡（今山西永济），负责河东事务。
　　勋贵都是如此，父辈当官，嫡长子协理。所以许多世子嫡长不会出外为官，父辈有什么权力，他们就有什么权力，如同副手。
　　后世朝代官场也如此。明朝的阁老之子如果本事足够，常常权力不亚于父辈，被称为“小阁老”。
　　李建成虽在朝中辞去职官，但李渊的权力就是他的权力，他是半个唐国公。自然李渊在山西边镇抵御民乱和外敌的时候，李建成也要在河东负责平息民乱，并不仅仅是被李渊派去河东“广结英俊”。
　　同时河东郡在黄河拐角处，三门峡上去一丁点，沿着黄河顺流而下，如果只是行船不是运送物资，都较为便利，离洛阳和郑州（荥阳）都很近。
　　河东虽然是河东薛氏的自留地，但山东五姓七望的势力，特别是荥阳郑氏的势力也较为深厚。
　　李建成在大兴和洛阳时就爱结交世家，又是荥阳郑氏的女婿，李渊认为让李建成主持河东事务，应该较为容易。
　　但没想到，荥阳郑氏根本不怎么理睬女婿。
　　首先，荥阳郑氏因为让李建成“请”李二郎李三郎远赴几百里来帮忙剿匪，吃了杨广好一顿骂，把荥阳郑氏在朝中的领头人莘国公郑元璹免职，让荥阳郑氏和李家的联盟出现裂痕。
　　再者没有这回事，山东郡姓的五姓七望世家也颇为自傲。
　　昔年楚国公杨素权势正值日中天时，为儿子杨玄纵花了大笔聘礼，求得清河崔氏女儿为妻，亲家公崔儦不过一员外散骑侍郎，竟然穿着破衣倒骑驴来送女儿。
　　杨素本来忍了，但崔儦还变本加厉出言不逊，行为颇为无礼。气得杨素拂袖而去，最后还是与之和好。
　　由此可见世家倨傲，也可见他们在社会上的地位有多高。
　　他们连杨素都不放在眼里，更何况李渊？
　　就算郑家在朝中官职不如李渊，那又如何？照旧看不起。
　　不过世家一边倨傲，肆意贬低亲家，一边又毫不吝啬把女儿卖出高聘礼。
　　李建成到现在还没有庶长子时，郑家还问李建成要不要再收一个郑家女，甚至想把手伸到了李二郎和李三郎的后院。
　　总之，嫁女是很倨傲的，但送旁支女或者寡妇，他们一点都不吝啬。
　　所以李建成去了河东郡，除了老丈人家问他要不要换个妾室之外，半点来自郑家的助力都没有。
　　河东郡的郡守和虎贲郎将也不太给李建成面子，只将李建成高高捧着。李建成拿着大笔钱财经常召开聚会，酒肉朋友很多，愿意投靠李家者却几乎没有。
　　李建成是唐国公世子，河东和山东世家不给他面子，就是不给唐国公李渊面子。难怪李渊生气。
　　不过或许他们也是知道不能太得罪李渊，所以虽然不理睬李建成，但还是往李渊府中送了不少自家子弟。李渊才将这口气忍下来。
　　李渊对李世民道：“你在河右之地被冷落，我在河东之地被冷落，我们父子将来一定要给他们好看。”
　　李世民摇头：“耶耶，你这话说得不对。我只是文吏不来，但附近骁勇之士纷纷投奔。士信，罗睺，过来。”
　　罗士信和宗罗睺策马上前，向李渊抱拳行礼。
　　李世民得意洋洋：“这位是罗士信，这位是宗罗睺。别说父亲麾下，就是放眼天下，也难以找到如他们这样智勇双全的将帅之才。哼哼！”
　　罗士信和宗罗睺的脸都有些红。
　　李渊虽不信李世民的自吹自擂，但还是开玩笑道：“这样啊，那你可否割爱，我多给你一百个文吏。”
　　李世民摇头：“天才将帅性格高傲，他们会自己选择主将，就算调到别人麾下也没用。再者，我又不傻，给我千万人我也不换。”
　　罗士信和宗罗睺的脸色更红了。
　　罗士信道：“我只愿意跟随郎君！”
　　宗罗睺道：“承蒙郎君不弃，罗睺必不负！”
　　李渊朗声笑道：“好，好，确实是好将领。二郎，你要好好对他们。”
　　此世一直装透明的李智云嘀咕：“真的吗？士信，二兄让你跟着我打仗，你也不听我的？”
　　罗士信无奈：“我认二郎君为主，和听二郎君的命令与其他人一同打仗没冲突。再者，就你那点带兵的本事，谁听谁啊。”
　　李智云道：“你先把谋略告诉我，我再下令呗。我都当主将了，你不帮我立威？”
　　罗士信无语：“行，随你。”
　　李渊好奇地看着李智云和罗士信。
　　李智云指着罗士信道：“父亲，罗士信是我好友，最好的朋友。”
　　李渊失笑：“交上朋友了？很好，祈健也长大了。”
　　罗士信小声对李智云道：“你不是字集弘吗？”
　　李智云小声道：“祈健是我小字。”
　　罗士信点头：“哦哦。”
　　宗罗睺：“……”罗士信你就这么当着唐国公的面和五郎君嘀嘀咕咕起来，你的胆子也太大了。
　　李渊倒是心胸宽广，没有在意。
　　他继续谈笑风生，意气飞扬。
　　李玄霸将视线从父亲身上移开，看向已经近在眼前的太原城。
　　太原啊……兜兜转转，二哥还是要做一段时间的太原公子吗？
　　哦，现在还要加上自己。
　　“大德，你兄长在河东有点困难，你去帮帮他。”
　　李玄霸正走神，没听清李渊说什么，条件反射：“好……啊？”
　　李渊严肃道：“河东非常重要，你是秀才，文采斐然，河东和山东的郡姓都不会轻视你。你把祈健也带在身边。他这个年龄，也该多交些同层次的友人了。”
　　李玄霸虽有些茫然，还是道：“是。”不然怎么办？父亲之命不能不听。
　　李智云道：“好，士信，你和我一起去。我们俩一起。”
　　罗士信本来心头有点黯然，以为唐国公是在委婉地瞧不起自己，但李智云这么一说，他笑容灿烂道：“好。”
