Chapter 120: Father and Son Reunited in Taiyuan

The imperial decree of "bestowed marriage" hit Li Shimin and Li Xuanba like a bolt from the blue, throwing all their plans into disarray.

Li Shimin was broad-minded. Although he felt a moment of frustration, the thought of being able to bring Guanyinbi into his home early instantly cheered him up.

Li Xuanba, however, while initially appearing magnanimous, remained secretly sullen about their plans being disrupted.

Although Li Xuanba had spent a long time mentally preparing himself for the fact that the future Emperor Gaozu of Tang would undoubtedly be Li Yuan, he had still hoped for his Second Brother to ascend the throne a few years earlier.

His calculations had been perfect: his Second Brother would develop his power in the Hexi region, and while the Central Plains were in chaos and cut off from the borderlands, he would sweep through the Western Regions, Hexi, and the various commanderies of Longxi. By the time their father raised his army, his Second Brother would lead his forces eastward from Longxi, capturing Daxing and renaming it Chang'an while their father was still huffing and puffing on the road.

Li Xuanba firmly believed that the reason his Second Brother had been so passive in history was that his military achievements were only gained after Li Yuan had already raised his banner; nominally, he was merely a general under Tang Gaozu Li Yuan, dependent on his father for military authority and logistics.

In history, Li Shimin had shown his talent at sixteen by devising a plan to save the Emperor, and at eighteen, he followed his father to war, beginning his life as the Heavenly Strategy General.

But now, his Second Brother had captured the Tuyuhun Khan Fuyun at ten, became a Huben General at thirteen, and pacified the Xihai Commandery while guarding Hexi at fourteen. Li Xuanba had even made contact with the Western Turks, intending to drag his Second Brother into dealing a massive blow to the Eastern Turks before the Sui Dynasty collapsed, achieving the feat of "surpassing the Marquis of Champion before becoming Emperor."

As everyone knew, the "criticism" of Li Shimin’s military record was that it was "only" brilliant in civil wars; when it came time for foreign wars, he was already the Emperor and could not lead the troops himself. Even when he finally persuaded his ministers to allow him to personally lead a campaign against Goguryeo, he failed to achieve his set goal of destroying the kingdom.

Although most later generations believed that if Li Shimin hadn't been Emperor, his name would surely have been carved into the Wolf Mountain and Yanran Mountain, the reality was that he *did* become Emperor, which remained an eternal regret.

Therefore, Li Xuanba cheered his Second Brother on: *[Second Brother, buck up! Work hard! You have less and less time to achieve the feat of carving your name into the Wolf and Yanran Mountains! Don't let this be a lifelong regret!]*

He couldn't say these words aloud, but he could nag in his heart.

Li Shimin covered his ears, but he couldn't cover his heart, so he walked three meters away from Li Xuanba.

He was grateful that his younger brother’s "heart-voice" range hadn't increased with age; otherwise, he would have been annoyed to death.

However, after Li Xuanba’s nagging, Li Shimin’s mood also grew heavy.

As a genius general, who didn't have the desire to carve their name into the Wolf and Yanran Mountains?

"If I can't complete this goal before becoming Emperor, I'll have to make Ah Xuan suffer a bit." Li Shimin, with his back to his brother, grabbed Changsun Wuji’s hand and plotted in secret. "You must help me sneak out of the capital to lead the campaign personally."

Changsun Wuji rolled his eyes violently.

*You’ll be fine, but I’ll probably be thrown into prison by Li Sanlang for months, and even your little sister won't be able to save me!*

But Changsun Wuji had never known how to refuse Li Shimin’s requests since childhood, so no matter how much he complained internally, he could only agree for now.

Before Li Shimin and Li Xuanba left Zhangye, they urgently called Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui back.

Having spent a few years as a county magistrate, Fang Qiao had evolved from a shy, aloof scholar into a master of social interaction. He patted his chest and guaranteed to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, "I will do my utmost to pacify the hearts of the officials in Hexi and Longxi."

Du Ruhui yawned and said, "Leave some capable generals for me. You two raise your army by raiding the cattle and sheep of the grasslands; I have no way to lead troops."

Li Shimin said, "I will leave old generals like Zhou Da behind and take the new soldiers recruited from Hexi. Kemin, feel free to use them."

Du Ruhui asked, "And the wealth of the merchant caravans will also be under my control?"

Li Shimin looked at Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba thought for a moment and said, "I will leave Yan Zhen for you."

Du Ruhui smiled, "With Yan Qilang here, I can rest easy."

Li Shimin asked Changsun Wuji, "Guanyinbi and I are getting married; are you really not coming back?"

Changsun Wuji said irritably, "Do you think I don't want to? My father won't allow it, saying that the Hexi region is of vital importance and cannot afford any mistakes."

Gao Biaoren had not only brought the imperial decree but also letters from the four old men in Daxing City.

Because the world was in chaos, Yang Guang was campaigning against Goguryeo again, and there were movements from the Crown Prince's side, this wedding could not be a grand affair. Li Yuan, Changsun Sheng, and Yuwen Bi had discussed it: the wedding would be kept frugal, and fewer people would be invited.

Furthermore, with the world in chaos, even if they wanted to invite more relatives, those relatives couldn't make it. For instance, Yuwen Zhu’s eldest uncle was serving as an official abroad and could not attend.

Changsun Sheng persuaded his son and Li Shimin’s other friends that this was just a formality; the future ceremony of conferring the Empress would be the true wedding for Li Shimin and his daughter.

Gao Biaoren watched Changsun Sheng write the letter, his mouth twitching for a long time.

Li Yuan wasn't even Emperor yet, but General Changsun was already treating his future son-in-law’s ascension as a foregone conclusion. He felt a tiny bit of sympathy for Li Yuan.

This sudden marriage not only disrupted Li Shimin and Li Xuanba’s plans but also made the wedding imperfect.

Li Shimin had already made up his mind to hold a grand, formal wedding during the Empress-conferring ceremony.

Li Xuanba also... Li Xuanba thought that if he could live until that time, he would ask for Yuwen Zhu’s opinion. If she was willing, he would hold another ceremony, even if it went against the rites.

To be so rushed was truly a great injustice to Yuwen Zhu.

After arranging everything, Li Shimin took Luo Shixin, Zong Luohou, and the five hundred brave soldiers recruited from Hexi back to the Central Plains.

Li Xuanba took Xiang Gu from the caravan and left Chen Tieniu, who was most familiar with his affairs, to Changsun Wuji. As for his own guards, he would just mooch off his Second Brother’s. Anyway, as a deputy general, he could count as one of the generals his Second Brother brought home.

In April, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba returned to Daxing City to pick up Changsun Sheng and Yuwen Bi to travel to Taiyuan together.

Gao Jiong and Xue Daoheng did not accompany them, as they were not prepared to attend their student’s wedding.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were both very regretful.

Gao Jiong comforted them, "Something major will definitely happen this year. Xuanqing and I are still viewed with suspicion by the Emperor, so we must keep a low profile. A great man must consider the big picture."

Xue Daoheng snorted coldly, "Er-lang, don't just focus on your wife’s Empress-conferring ceremony; remember to confer a title on San-lang’s wife. I will be your master of ceremonies!"

Li Shimin replied earnestly, "Yes, Teacher."

After a small gathering, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba set off again.

In fact, they had originally planned to get married in Luoyang.

Each family had mansions in Luoyang, making the wedding process simpler and allowing them to invite more guests.

But with bandits rising within Taiyuan and the Eastern Turks stirring outside, Li Yuan could not leave his post, so he changed the location of his two sons' wedding to Taiyuan.

All three families knew this marriage was a political alliance. Once Yuwen Yuan and Changsun Sheng had secured enough practical benefits for their respective daughters, they compromised on the matter.

The Yuwen and Changsun families had prepared mansions in Taiyuan in advance, moving servants and dowries into them beforehand, so the two women would be married from their new homes. These two large mansions would also become part of the women's dowries.

Now, Yuwen Zhu and the young Lady Changsun were already in Taiyuan preparing for the wedding. Yuwen Bi and Changsun Sheng had specifically waited in Daxing for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba to return so they could carefully discuss their future strategies on the road.

Talking about private matters on the road was much safer than in the city; they could speak freely.

When Changsun Sheng heard that Li Xuanba had just invited the Western Turkic envoy to join them in attacking the Eastern Turks, he felt his vision go dark and nearly fainted, scaring Li Shimin and Li Xuanba into a state of panic.

"With Changsun Si-lang there, we will surely be able to maintain our relationship with the Western Turks. Teacher, you need not worry," Li Xuanba comforted him.

Changsun Sheng slapped his thigh in anger, "What is the use of maintaining a relationship with the Western Turks? Can he conjure up a Li Er-lang to attack the Eastern Turks?!"

Li Er-lang touched his nose, not daring to speak.

It clearly wasn't his or Ah Xuan’s fault, so why were they the ones being scolded?

Yuwen Bi also sighed repeatedly, full of regret.

If Er-lang and San-lang hadn't been called back, they would probably be preparing to deal a heavy blow to the Eastern Turks right now.

When unifying the world, the Eastern Turks were a major threat that would surely interfere in the Central Plains. They could have prevented it in advance, but due to a twist of fate... alas.

Since things had reached this point, being angry was useless. Changsun Sheng began writing a letter to Changsun Wuji in the carriage, teaching him how to properly appease the Western Turkic envoy and drag things out for a year or two so they wouldn't run off.

No, he should just have Si-lang use the excuse of "my sister is getting married and needs to visit home" to trick this Western Turkic envoy into coming to Taiyuan.

He could also try to invite more people from the Western Regions to attend the wedding!

Changsun Sheng instantly completed his plan in his mind and had his trusted aide ride at full speed to deliver it to Changsun Wuji.

He watched the horse galloping away with a look of regret.

Although he had survived his brush with death, his body was not what it used to be; he could no longer gallop across the grasslands.

If he were ten years younger, he would have gone to Zhangye himself. By the time his son-in-law returned, the Eastern and Western Turks might have split into Eastern, Western, Northern, and Southern Turks, and they would never have been able to interfere with his son-in-law’s path to unifying the Central Plains.

The young ones had talent, but their lack of experience was still limiting their abilities.

Seeing Changsun Sheng’s regretful expression, Yuwen Bi said, "Have you given in to old age? I certainly haven't. Take good care of your health; perhaps we will have another chance to achieve great things."

The regret on Changsun Sheng’s face vanished, his gaze firm. "You are right."

Li Shimin, who had excellent hearing outside the carriage, winked at his brother.

Li Xuanba: *[Speak your mind.]*

Li Shimin continued to wink. If he could speak in his heart, why would he need to wink?

Li Xuanba: *[You’re trying to say that with Teacher here, the struggle for the chancellorship among your friends will be even harder.]*

Li Shimin: *[Yes!]*

Li Xuanba: *[Oh, stop it. Teacher is old; it’s time for him to enjoy his twilight years. Do you want to exhaust him?]*

Li Shimin pointed at the carriage.

Li Xuanba: *[Uh, if Teacher insists on working, what can we do? Fang Xuanling and the others are still young; they can wait. It’s just that Brother Du and Brother Xue need to take care of their health. By the way, where exactly did Brother Xue go? Why hasn't he returned yet?]*

Li Shimin nodded. That’s right, where did Brother Xue go?

At the same time, Xue Shou, who was digging for seashells on Tsukushi Island, let out a massive sneeze.

Xue Shou rubbed his nose and gave a wry smile, "I suppose Li Er and Li San are thinking of me, or perhaps Old Du and Old Fang are mocking me."

Chen Leng asked curiously, "Why? Could it not be your family missing you?"

Xue Shou sighed, "It’s intuition."

Chen Leng laughed, "If Brother Xue is in a hurry to return, I can send a ship to escort you part of the way."

Xue Shou shook his head, "Since I am a staff member for the General, I must complete this mission for you before returning to properly show off to my friends."

*I, Xue Shou, may be a scholar, but I can also wield a three-foot sword to expand our territory!*

Li San had said there was a gold mine on this island. His mission had gotten lost after encountering pirates and was rescued by Chen Leng, who was stationed in Ryukyu preparing for a campaign against the Wa. How could he give up halfway?

Moreover, General Chen was both wise and brave; by staying by his side as a staff member, he could better persuade him to join Li Er-lang in the future.

Xue Shou rubbed his nose and continued digging for shells, "My friends must still be grinding away at their seniority. Once I achieve great things with General Chen, I’ll go back and mock them."

Chen Leng laughed loudly, "Good... wait, is the Li Er you speak of Li Shimin, Li Er-lang?"

Xue Shou replied, "Yes."

Chen Leng felt like deflating Xue Shou’s ego.

Although his information from the Central Plains was somewhat delayed, he had been in the Central Plains when Li Er-lang captured the Tuyuhun Khan Fuyun.

Li Er-lang had captured the Tuyuhun Khan at ten; now, more than three years later, if he had the chance to return to the battlefield, he must have gained many more merits.

Truly, a hero had emerged from the youth.

Chen Leng decided to treat Xue Shou even better. Xue Shou’s friends were all young talents with boundless futures. Xue Shou must be the same.

...

In early April, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba finally reunited with their family.

Li Yuan, in high spirits, rode his horse a hundred miles out to meet his two sons. Before he could even give them a hug, he was met with Li Shimin’s complaints.

"Father, Ah Xuan just helped me arrange for the Western Turkic Khan to join us in intimidating the Eastern Turks, and you called us back. If I miss out on carving my name into the Wolf and Yanran Mountains in the future, it will all be your fault, Father," Li Shimin said with dissatisfaction.

Li Yuan’s smile faltered, "Is that so?"

He looked at Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba gave a bitter smile, "I went to meet the Western Turkic Khan in Yiwu City last November; it was truly not easy."

Li Yuan broke into a cold sweat, "Didn't you just take back the Xihai Commandery? Why are you going to attack the Eastern Turks? Where would the money and grain come from?"

Li Shimin, who had just finished changing his teeth, gave a thumbs-up and grinned, revealing eight teeth, "The Western Turkic Khan is generous; he said he would pay."

Li Xuanba added in an honest tone, "When Second Brother was fighting the remnants of the Tuyuhun, the Tianzhu Khan paid for everything, and even let Second Brother have first pick of the spoils after the battle. The people of the Western Regions are truly simple and generous."

Li Yuan was completely bewildered.

*People of the Western Regions... simple and generous? Does he think I haven't dealt with the Westerners who come to the Great Sui? I’ve even fought against the Tuyuhun!*

Li Yuan waved his hand, "I don't believe it. Is it really that easy?"

Changsun Sheng emerged from the carriage and said irritably, "The envoys sent by the Western Turkic Khan and the Tianzhu Khan to congratulate Li Er-lang and Li San-lang on their marriage are already on their way. I am still worrying about how to explain this to His Majesty."

Yuwen Bi also sighed, "Indeed. With the world in chaos, Er-lang and San-lang’s wedding should be low-key. If they come, how can it be low-key?"

Li Yuan: "..."

Although he had been complained about by his sons and grumbled at by his in-laws, he felt wonderful inside!

Li Yuan coughed a few times to suppress his laughter and sighed hypocritically, "Who could have guessed you two were so restless? I thought that since you had just finished fighting in Xihai, you would surely rest for a year or two, so I told you to hurry back to get married. Alas, you two brothers have been troublemakers since you were small; this has really put me in a difficult spot."

Li Yuan held it in for a long time, but finally couldn't help but laugh triumphantly, "Good, good, it is Father’s fault for underestimating you, hahahahaha."

Li Shimin laughed complainingly, "Father, don't just laugh; how are you going to compensate me!"

Li Xuanba looked at the faint look of longing on his Second Brother’s face and sighed in his heart.

He mimicked his Second Brother’s tone and said with a blank face, "Father, Second Brother recruited civil officials in the Hexi region, but the scholars there looked down on him for his youth and refused to join him. You have also established your own府 (fu), so you must have many scholars under your command..."

Li Xuanba held the reins with one hand and reached out, "We don't want much; give us ten to start with."

Li Yuan joked, "Ten is enough?"

Li Shimin laughed, "The more, the better!"

Li Yuan poked Li Shimin’s forehead with his riding crop, "You’re acting like Han Xin commanding troops, 'the more the better,' are you? Fine, this time it is Father’s fault. I will prepare the personnel for you to take back to Zhangye."

After saying this, Li Yuan’s expression darkened slightly, "They are just local bullies in a remote land, yet they dare to call themselves a noble family and look down on the Tang Duke’s estate? Hmph."

Changsun Sheng and Yuwen Bi switched from the carriage to horses, listening to the casual chat between Li Yuan and his two sons.

Seeing Li Yuan’s expression, Changsun Sheng asked, "What? Have you been slighted by the noble families again? Isn't your eldest son the son-in-law of the Xingyang Zheng clan? With the Xingyang Zheng clan supporting you, is there anyone in the Hedong region who dares to give you a hard time?"

Li Yuan complained, "Don't even mention the Xingyang Zheng clan; I get angry just thinking about it."

Changsun Sheng and Yuwen Bi were family, and Taiyuan was his own territory, so Li Yuan had nothing to hide and began to complain directly.

Li Xuanba listened carefully, extracting information from Li Yuan’s complaints.

Although Li Yuan had become the Taiyuan Garrison Commander and the Pacification Commissioner for Shanxi and Hedong a few years earlier than in the original history, the situation remained the same: Li Yuan was stationed in Taiyuan, responsible for Shanxi affairs, while Li Jiancheng was stationed in Hedong Commandery (modern-day Yongji, Shanxi), responsible for Hedong affairs.

This was common for the nobility: the father held the official post, and the eldest son assisted. Thus, many heirs did not go out to serve as officials; they held whatever power their fathers held, acting as deputies.

This was also the case in later dynasties. If the son of a Ming Dynasty Grand Secretary was capable, his power was often no less than his father’s, and he was known as a "Little Grand Secretary."

Although Li Jiancheng had resigned from his official post in the capital, Li Yuan’s power was his power; he was half a Tang Duke. Naturally, when Li Yuan was defending against civil unrest and foreign enemies in the Shanxi border towns, Li Jiancheng also had to be responsible for quelling civil unrest in Hedong, not just being sent there by Li Yuan to "make friends with talented men."

At the same time, Hedong Commandery was at the bend of the Yellow River, just a bit above the Sanmenxia. Following the Yellow River downstream, it was quite convenient for travel, and it was very close to Luoyang and Zhengzhou (Xingyang).

Although Hedong was the home turf of the Hedong Xue clan, the influence of the "Five Surnames and Seven Clans" of Shandong, especially the Xingyang Zheng clan, was also quite deep.

Li Jiancheng had loved associating with noble families while in Daxing and Luoyang, and being the son-in-law of the Xingyang Zheng clan, Li Yuan had thought it would be easy for him to manage Hedong affairs.

But to his surprise, the Xingyang Zheng clan paid almost no attention to their son-in-law.

First, because the Xingyang Zheng clan had let Li Jiancheng "invite" Li Er-lang and Li San-lang to travel hundreds of miles to help suppress bandits, they had been severely scolded by Yang Guang, who dismissed the Xingyang Zheng clan’s leader in the capital, the Duke of Shen, Zheng Yuanzu, causing a rift in the alliance between the Zheng clan and the Li family.

Furthermore, even without that, the noble families of the Shandong commanderies were quite arrogant.

In the past, when the Duke of Chu, Yang Su, was at the height of his power, he had spent a large dowry for his son, Yang Xuanzong, to marry a daughter of the Qinghe Cui clan. The father-in-law, Cui Bi, was merely a minor official, yet he had arrived to deliver his daughter wearing tattered clothes and riding a donkey backward.

Yang Su had initially endured it, but Cui Bi had become even more insulting and rude. Yang Su had left in a huff, though they eventually reconciled.

This showed how arrogant the noble families were and how high their social status was.

They didn't even respect Yang Su, let alone Li Yuan.

Even if the Zheng family’s official rank in the capital was not as high as Li Yuan’s, so what? They still looked down on him.

However, while the noble families were arrogant and disparaged their in-laws, they were not at all stingy about selling their daughters for high dowries.

Even though Li Jiancheng didn't have a legitimate eldest son yet, the Zheng family asked if he wanted to take another Zheng woman as a concubine, and even tried to reach into the backyards of Li Er-lang and Li San-lang.

In short, they were very arrogant about marrying off their daughters, but they were not at all stingy about sending off collateral branch women or widows.

So, after Li Jiancheng went to Hedong Commandery, other than his in-laws asking if he wanted to change his concubines, he received no help from the Zheng family at all.

The Governor and Huben General of Hedong Commandery didn't give Li Jiancheng much face either, merely flattering him. Li Jiancheng held large gatherings with his wealth, and while he had many drinking buddies, almost no one was willing to join the Li family.

Li Jiancheng was the heir to the Tang Duke; if the Hedong and Shandong noble families didn't give him face, they weren't giving Li Yuan face. No wonder Li Yuan was angry.

However, perhaps they knew they couldn't offend Li Yuan too much, so although they ignored Li Jiancheng, they still sent many of their own clan members to Li Yuan’s estate. That was the only reason Li Yuan had swallowed his anger.

Li Yuan said to Li Shimin, "You were slighted in the Hexi region, and I was slighted in the Hedong region; our father and son must make them pay in the future."

Li Shimin shook his head, "Father, that’s not right. I was only slighted by the civil officials, but the brave warriors nearby flocked to join me. Shixin, Luohou, come here."

Luo Shixin and Zong Luohou rode forward and bowed to Li Yuan.

Li Shimin said triumphantly, "This is Luo Shixin, and this is Zong Luohou. Not to mention under your command, Father, even looking across the entire world, it would be hard to find military talents as wise and brave as them. Hmph hmph!"

Luo Shixin and Zong Luohou both blushed slightly.

Although Li Yuan didn't believe Li Shimin’s self-aggrandizing, he joked, "Is that so? Then can you spare them? I’ll give you a hundred more civil officials."

Li Shimin shook his head, "Genius generals have arrogant personalities; they choose their own commanders. Even if they were transferred to someone else’s command, it would be useless. Besides, I’m not stupid; I wouldn't trade them for a thousand million men."

Luo Shixin and Zong Luohou’s faces turned even redder.

Luo Shixin said, "I am only willing to follow the Young Master!"

Zong Luohou said, "I am grateful that the Young Master does not abandon me; Luohou will never let you down!"

Li Yuan laughed heartily, "Good, good, they are indeed fine generals. Er-lang, you must treat them well."

Li Zhiyun, who had been acting invisible, muttered, "Really? Shixin, if Second Brother asked you to follow me into battle, would you not listen to me?"

Luo Shixin replied helplessly, "I recognize the Second Young Master as my master; there is no conflict between listening to his orders and fighting alongside others. Besides, with your meager ability to lead troops, who would listen to whom?"

Li Zhiyun said, "You can just tell me the strategy, and I’ll issue the orders. I’m the commander, can’t you help me establish my authority?"

Luo Shixin was speechless, "Fine, whatever you say."

Li Yuan looked at Li Zhiyun and Luo Shixin with curiosity.

Li Zhiyun pointed at Luo Shixin and said, "Father, Luo Shixin is my good friend, my best friend."

Li Yuan laughed, "You’ve made a friend? Very good, Qijian has grown up too."

Luo Shixin whispered to Li Zhiyun, "Aren't you styled Jihong?"

Li Zhiyun whispered back, "Qijian is my childhood name."

Luo Shixin nodded, "Oh, I see."

Zong Luohou: "..." *Luo Shixin, you have a lot of nerve whispering to the Fifth Young Master right in front of the Tang Duke.*

Li Yuan was broad-minded and didn't mind.

He continued to chat and laugh, full of spirit.

Li Xuanba shifted his gaze from his father to the Taiyuan city walls, which were now close at hand.

Taiyuan... after all this, is Second Brother still going to be the "Young Master of Taiyuan" for a while?

Oh, and now he had to include himself.

"Dade, your brother is having some trouble in Hedong; you should go and help him."

Li Xuanba was lost in thought and didn't hear what Li Yuan said clearly, so he replied reflexively, "Okay... wait, what?"

Li Yuan said seriously, "Hedong is very important. You are a scholar with brilliant literary talent; the noble clans of Hedong and Shandong will not look down on you. Take Qijian with you as well. At his age, he should be making more friends of his own level."

Although Li Xuanba was a bit dazed, he said, "Yes." What else could he do? He couldn't disobey his father’s orders.

Li Zhiyun said, "Good, Shixin, you come with me. We’ll go together."

Luo Shixin had felt a bit dejected, thinking the Tang Duke was subtly looking down on him, but upon hearing Li Zhiyun’s words, he smiled brightly, "Okay."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第121章 李二郎规劝三郎
chunks.chineseText:
第121章 李二郎规劝三郎

李玄霸的官职、才干、声望皆高于李建成， 虽然李建成是李玄霸兄长，李玄霸也不可能如辅佐李世民那样去辅佐李建成。
　　别说李玄霸愿不愿意。如果以李建成为主导，还不如李玄霸单干。
　　李渊不傻。
　　他让李玄霸去帮李建成， 只是让他一同完成“唐国公府在河东郡扬名”这个目的。没有谁当主导， 兄弟平行共事。现在最重要的是“唐国公府”这个整体的利益， 可以稍稍牺牲李建成的心情。
　　不过李渊当然也存了让处事经验丰富的李玄霸带一带李建成的想法。
　　他太忙了，没空带李建成。李世民和李玄霸明年就要回河右，难以近距离帮助他。让李建成学李世民打仗的本事是没可能， 他希望李建成能学习一下李玄霸搞后勤的本事，才能辅佐他。
　　上阵父子兵，他将来若要起事， 最放心的还是儿子。
　　趁着李世民和李玄霸回来，李渊要带着李世民在太原练兵、剿匪， 李玄霸的本事正好在河东郡施展。
　　至于李建成， 就在李玄霸身边好好学习吧。
　　这种考虑，李渊没有瞒着长孙晟和宇文弼。
　　李世民正开心父亲更信任他和弟弟，就听弟弟在心里吐槽。
　　李玄霸：【来了来了，现在就来了吗？二郎～，你兄长本事不如你， 你好好为我打仗，将来皇帝你来当～！然后转头就封李建成为太子。】
　　李世民深吸一口气， 眼眸微颤。
　　李玄霸：【现在父亲说什么，三郎，你大兄的本事不如你， 你好好带带你大兄， 父亲最信任的是你。等我真的抢了大兄的风头， 大兄一告状， 又是我故意兄弟不睦了。】
　　李世民：【不……】
　　李玄霸：【不什么？不是还是不信？对父母而言，儿子都是心头肉，谁弱就帮谁。而且身为皇帝，更希望见到一个不强势的太子。二哥你都猜到未来了，还抱什么侥幸？】
　　他虽然什么都没说，但显然二哥已经猜到了。李玄霸也懒得遮掩了。
　　在心里给了一脸茫然的二哥一脚后，李玄霸恭敬道：“父亲何出此言？若兄长听到，一定会沮丧。让兄长难过，岂不是我这个当弟弟的错？”
　　他顿了顿，又叹息道：“何况河东世家不给兄长脸面，只是因为他们还在观望局势，不敢和唐国公世子走得太近。杨玄感谋逆，现在都还未平定，陛下正风声鹤唳。唐国公声势太过，恐非幸事。我和二哥很快就要回河右，他们与我们结交也不算结党，或许才会放心与我们结交。这不是兄长无能。”
　　李渊无奈道：“听你这么说，怎么好像我挑拨你们兄弟感情似的？？”
　　李玄霸笑道：“当然不是。父亲只是还把我们兄弟当孩子。兄长已经弱冠有五，女儿都有了好几个。父亲还是少在外说兄长不是。兄长也没有不是。”
　　李渊摆手：“在场哪有外人？罢了，你说得对。你维护兄长，很好。”
　　李玄霸道：“打虎亲兄弟。我当然维护兄长。”
　　李渊故意板着脸：“你维护兄长，就说父亲不是？”
　　李玄霸道：“忠言逆耳，父亲。”
　　李渊失笑：“去去去，我看你是读书读太多，快成倔书生了。难道你以后还想当谏臣？”
　　李玄霸严肃道：“这是我毕生所愿！”
　　李渊对李世民道：“你怎么带的大德？大德怎么越来越像宇文公了？”
　　李世民回过神：“啊？”
　　宇文弼板着脸道：“我的弟子，不像我像谁？大德说的是，不要在兄弟中挑拨离间！”
　　长孙晟叹气：“哪有你这样的父亲，对幼子说长子无能？你让大德大雄如何回答？”
　　李渊捂耳朵：“我错了我错了，别念了。”
　　李玄霸看着李渊的动作，非常有即视感，不由看向二哥。
　　李世民警觉：“看我做什么！”
　　李玄霸叹气不语。
　　李世民拿鞭子去捅李玄霸的腰。
　　李玄霸扭身躲开，一鞭子抽二哥马背上。
　　骏马跳脚。
　　“哎哟！”李世民颠簸了一下，本来就被弟弟撕开伤口很难受，气得也抽了李玄霸的马屁股一鞭子。
　　二人你抽我马一下，我抽你马一下，骏马疯狂加速跑了起来。
　　李玄霸大喊：“别抽了！跑太快了！”
　　李世民骂道：“谁说的先动手的遭殃？阿玄，我跟你说，晚了！”
　　几位长辈瞪大眼睛看着李世民和李玄霸突然闹起来，然后绝尘而去。
　　李渊揉了揉眼睛：“怎么了？”
　　李智云老气横秋道：“谁知道？二兄三兄从小不都是这样，刚还好好的，莫名其妙就吵起来打起来。大概双生子就是这样吧，连吵架打架也让旁人一头雾水。”
　　李渊：“……原来如此。”
　　宇文弼和长孙晟无语。什么叫“原来如此”？
　　唉，他们才刚说二郎三郎成熟了许多，比李渊看着还成熟，怎么这二人瞬间又变成顽童了？
　　李世民和李玄霸一口气冲了很远。他们都进太原城门里了，李渊等人还在后面慢悠悠“散步”。
　　进城后，李世民和李玄霸放缓速度，在城中勒马缓行。
　　太原城常有佩戴刀剑的士子骑马往来，这里的人没有人认识名满天下的李二郎李三郎。风尘仆仆的二人没有故意隐藏，却像是融于人群中，变成了芸芸众生中普通的一员。
　　“好久没有这么自在了。”李世民道，“在张掖的时候，我俩哪次出门不会引得众人围观？”
　　李玄霸道：“你现在高喊一声‘我乃李世民’，照样能引人围观。”
　　李世民扬起鞭子。
　　李玄霸道：“这是在城里，你敢纵马，我就敢向母亲告状你扰民。”
　　李世民放下马鞭，无奈道：“回到家，你又变成以前的告状小狗了。”
　　李玄霸道：“随你这么说。”
　　兄弟二人停下说话，安静地又沿着街道慢慢前行。
　　他们不知道家在太原城的什么地方。但大隋城池都是坊市结构，勋贵所住的方位都一样，他们朝着那个方向走，总会遇到。
　　太原城也算半个边镇了，所以坊市管理没有洛阳和大兴那么严格。在坊与市连接的道路上，也有小贩挑着炊饼贩卖。
　　坊市之外治安很差，卫兵几乎不管理。所以那些小贩都佩戴着棍棒之类的武器，大约是“自负盈亏”吧。
　　李世民闻到炊饼的香味，下马买了两个烧饼。
　　小贩满脸横肉，但看着李世民的神情却战战兢兢：“小郎君，我的炊饼你可能吃不惯。”
　　李世民疑惑：“难道除了面，你还放了其他不好的东西？”
　　小贩忙摇头，道：“我不做亏心生意。只是贵人吃的肯定是白净的精面，我这面饼……有点粗糙。”
　　李世民笑道：“我刚从边塞回来，麦饭都能吃，带点壳的面饼才吃得香。”
　　小贩松了口气，笑着奉上热腾腾的炊饼：“那小的就不怕了，小郎君，请。”
　　李世民给了小贩几个铜子，将其中一张热腾腾面饼抛给李玄霸。
　　李玄霸伸手接住，骂道：“你递过来不行吗？落地上怎么办？浪费粮食。”
　　两人都没在意手脏，直接拿着炊饼吃了起来。
　　奔波了一路，两人确实是饿了。
　　李世民叼着饼重新上马，啃了一口饼后，单手拿着饼道：“你信不信你若没接着饼，我就能接住？”
　　李玄霸没说信还是不信，只骂道：“你玩杂耍吗？”
　　李世民笑道：“哈哈哈哈。”
　　两人慢吞吞吃饼。
　　现在民间石磨也没有普及，面粉已经算是金贵的东西。
　　但百姓吃的面粉就算是他们自称的“白|面”，其实也是只脱了壳，带着麦皮一起磨成的灰色面粉，吃上去有种沙子的口感。
　　按照权贵家中白|面的磨法，这灰色面粉能再少两三成，连寻常小地主也不敢日日这么吃。
　　不止面粉，稻米粟米也是如此。
　　李世民和李玄霸在唐国公府时钟鸣鼎食，第一次随裴世矩去张掖时吃到粗粮，直觉得嗓子快割破了，难以下咽。
　　吃完糙面炊饼，李世民拍了拍手，压低声音道：“阿玄，我还是相信父亲。未来能改变不是吗？你谶纬中看到的我是不是在父亲起兵之后才展现出才华？那时兄长是嫡长，我的战功不多，父亲立兄长为太子情有可原。现在已经不一样了，很不一样了。”
　　李玄霸没说话。
　　李世民道：“你看，我都把河右收入囊中了，地盘比父亲还大。父亲如果不选我，岂不是可以预见的会有一场内战？若内战发生，我和兄长必死一个……我的意思是，兄长必死。”
　　李玄霸本来很严肃，听到二哥最后补充的话，嘴角微抽。
　　李世民耸肩：“不是我瞧不起兄长，我有兵，他没有。”
　　李玄霸道：“嗯。”
　　李世民道：“我说的对吧？如果父亲一开始就选我当继承人，再让兄长故意谦让一番，我无论是从感情还是从利益，都需要把兄长捧得高高的，也会厚待他的子孙。现在我们的境遇与你看到的未来已经大不一样了。父亲……父亲真的对我们很好。”
　　李玄霸想反问，“真的很好”在哪？
　　但他没有反驳二哥。
　　或许在二哥看来，父亲没有偏袒嫡长，给了他自由发挥实力的机会，就真的对他很好了。
　　虽然以前受了祖母的气，但二哥这个人心大，很多年前的事，他大概已经淡忘了。
　　而且那只是祖母偏心，父亲当时虽然因为孝道必须顺着祖母，暗地里也算是站在他们二人这边。
　　当然，李玄霸没这么想，但他能看出，二哥是这么想。
　　自己有前世的记忆。虽然这一世生活了这么多年，前世已经褪色成画卷，今生也算两个人了，但是仍旧会给他的性格造成影响。
　　二哥却是纯粹的“土著”。他就算再厉害，现在也只是一个纯粹的十六岁少年郎。
　　若按周岁，才十五岁，才高一。
　　而且这个时代父亲对儿子多是过分严厉不苟言笑，只知督促学习，温情很少。
　　他们的父亲却是这个时代难得的宠溺孩子，愿意与孩子亲近打闹的“开明父亲”。
　　若在现代，愿意对孩子亲亲抱抱举高高的父亲很常见。但这个时代，这样的父亲真的是异类。
　　连自己这个现代来的孤魂都难以割舍对李渊那一声“父亲”，何况二哥。
　　李玄霸叹气。
　　所以他才会对软化的二哥说那么重的话，担心二哥放松警惕。
　　虽然放松警惕不会伤害到二哥的根基，但会伤到二哥。
　　“好。二哥说得对。”李玄霸道，“我只是对父亲让我去帮李建成很不舒服，不过我也相信父亲疼爱我们。”
　　李世民笑道：“这就对了。走，你看前面那个大宅子像不像我们的家？”
　　李玄霸翻白眼：“母亲都在门口对我们招手了。”
　　李世民笑着给了李玄霸的马屁股一鞭子，李玄霸的马蹿了出去：“阿玄快跑！”
　　“啊？！李世民！”李玄霸吓得赶紧勒马，担心撞到母亲。
　　显然李玄霸想多了，窦夫人眼皮子都没抬，两个壮仆站在了她面前，一声大喝，马立刻止步。
　　李玄霸从马上跳下来：“母亲！二哥他……”
　　窦夫人把李玄霸护在身后，伸手：“鞭子给我！”
　　李世民嬉笑着下马：“娘娘，别听阿玄胡说，我什么都……啊！还真抽啊！我错了我错了娘亲！”
　　李玄霸抱着手臂，冷眼看着回家第一天就挨抽的二哥冷笑。
　　四月的空气都要被李玄霸的冷眼冷笑给制冷了。
　　叫你皮，活该！
chunks.englishText:
**Chapter 121: Second Brother Li Admonishes Third Brother**

Li Xuanba's official position, talent, and prestige were all higher than Li Jiancheng's. Although Li Jiancheng was Li Xuanba's elder brother, it was impossible for Li Xuanba to assist Li Jiancheng in the same manner he assisted Li Shimin.

Forget whether Li Xuanba was willing or not—if Li Jiancheng were to take the lead, Li Xuanba would be far better off working alone.

Li Yuan was no fool.

His intent in sending Li Xuanba to help Li Jiancheng was merely to have them jointly achieve the goal of "making a name for the Duke of Tang’s Household in Hedong Commandery." Neither would lead; the brothers would work side by side as equals. Right now, what mattered most was the overall interest of the "Duke of Tang's Household," even if it meant sacrificing Li Jiancheng’s feelings a little.

Of course, Li Yuan also harbored the thought of letting the more experienced Li Xuanba guide Li Jiancheng a bit.

He was far too busy to mentor Li Jiancheng himself, and Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were returning to Heyou next year, making it impossible for them to offer close assistance for long. Learning Li Shimin’s military prowess was out of the question for Li Jiancheng, but Li Yuan hoped he could at least pick up Li Xuanba’s talent for logistics to assist him in the future.

When going into battle, a father relies on his sons. If he were to rise in rebellion in the future, those he trusted most were still his own sons.

Taking advantage of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's return, Li Yuan intended to take Li Shimin to train troops and suppress bandits in Taiyuan, while Li Xuanba's talents happened to be perfect for deployment in Hedong Commandery.

As for Li Jiancheng, he could simply stay by Li Xuanba’s side and learn well.

Li Yuan did not hide these considerations from Zhangsun Sheng and Yuwen Bi.

Li Shimin was just feeling happy that their father trusted him and his younger brother more when he heard his brother snorting in his heart.

Li Xuanba: 【Here it comes, here it comes. Is it starting already? *“Erlang~ your elder brother isn't as capable as you. Fight hard for me, and you’ll be the emperor in the future~!”* And then he turns right around and confers the title of Crown Prince onto Li Jiancheng.】

Li Shimin took a deep breath, his eyelids trembling slightly.

Li Xuanba: 【Now Father says, *"Sanlang, your eldest brother isn't as capable as you. Take good care of him and guide him; Father trusts you the most."* Then, once I actually steal Eldest Brother’s thunder and Eldest Brother complains, it’ll be my fault again for deliberately sowing discord between brothers.】

Li Shimin: 【No...】

Li Xuanba: 【"No" what? "No, it won't happen," or "No, I still don't believe it"? To parents, all sons are flesh of their heart; whoever is weaker gets their support. Besides, as an emperor, one would prefer a less forceful Crown Prince. Second Brother, you’ve already guessed the future, so why hold onto wishful thinking?】

Although he had said nothing aloud, Second Brother had obviously guessed it. Li Xuanba did not bother hiding it anymore.

After delivering a mental kick to his bewildered Second Brother, Li Xuanba bowed respectfully and said, "Father, why do you say such things? If Eldest Brother heard this, he would surely feel dispirited. Causing Eldest Brother sorrow—would that not be my fault as his younger brother?"

He paused, then sighed, "Besides, the noble families of Hedong aren't giving Eldest Brother face simply because they're still watching the tide and dare not get too close to the heir of the Duke of Tang. Yang Xuangan's rebellion has yet to be quelled, and His Majesty is extremely jumpy right now. If the Duke of Tang makes too much noise, it might not be a blessing. Second Brother and I will be returning to Heyou soon, so befriending us wouldn't be seen as forming a clique—that is likely why they feel safe socializing with us. This is not due to any incompetence on Eldest Brother’s part."

Li Yuan said helplessly, "Hearing you say it like that, why does it sound as if I'm trying to sow discord between you brothers??"

Li Xuanba smiled. "Of course not. Father simply still views us brothers as children. Eldest Brother is already twenty-five and has several daughters. Father should speak less of his faults in front of outsiders—besides, Eldest Brother hasn't done anything wrong."

Li Yuan waved his hand. "Where are the outsiders here? Ah, fine, you're right. It is good that you defend your elder brother."

Li Xuanba said, "Brothers fight side by side like tiger-hunting kin. Of course I will defend my elder brother."

Li Yuan feigned a stern expression. "You defend your elder brother, yet you criticize your father?"

Li Xuanba replied, "Honest advice grates on the ear, Father."

Li Yuan burst out laughing. "Go, go, go! I think you've read too many books and turned into a stubborn scholar. Do you plan to become a remonstrating official in the future?"

Li Xuanba said solemnly, "That is my lifelong aspiration!"

Li Yuan turned to Li Shimin. "How did you raise Dade? Why is he looking more and more like Master Yuwen?"

Li Shimin snapped back to reality. "Ah?"

Yuwen Bi said with a somber face, "He is my disciple—who else should he resemble if not me? Dade speaks the truth: do not drive wedges between brothers!"

Zhangsun Sheng sighed. "What kind of father tells his younger sons that his eldest son is incompetent? How do you expect Dade and Daxiong to answer?"

Li Yuan covered his ears. "I was wrong, I was wrong! Stop nagging."

Li Xuanba watched Li Yuan's antics and felt an overwhelming sense of déjà vu. He couldn't help looking at his Second Brother.

Li Shimin grew vigilant. "What are you looking at me for!"

Li Xuanba sighed without a word.

Li Shimin used his whip to poke Li Xuanba in the waist.

Li Xuanba twisted away and lashed his whip onto Second Brother’s horse’s flank.

The steed bucked.

"Ouch!" Li Shimin jolted. Already feeling uncomfortable after having his old wounds ripped open by his brother, he lashed Li Xuanba’s horse's rump in a fit of rage.

The two kept whipping each other's horses, sending the steeds into a mad gallop.

Li Xuanba shouted, "Stop whipping! It's running too fast!"

Li Shimin cursed, "Who was it that said whoever strikes first suffers the consequences? Ah-Xuan, let me tell you, it's too late now!"

The elders stared in astonishment as Li Shimin and Li Xuanba suddenly broke into a scuffle and sped off in a cloud of dust.

Li Yuan rubbed his eyes. "What happened?"

Li Zhiyun said with an air of mock maturity, "Who knows? Haven't Second Brother and Third Brother been like this since they were little? One moment they're fine, and the next they're arguing and fighting out of nowhere. I suppose that's just how twins are—even their bickering leaves onlookers baffled."

Li Yuan: "...I see."

Yuwen Bi and Zhangsun Sheng were speechlessly resigned. What did he mean, "I see"?

*Sigh.* They had just praised Second Brother and Third Brother for maturing so much, appearing even more composed than Li Yuan, only for the two of them to instantly turn back into mischievous children.

***

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba sprinted a long distance in one breath. By the time they entered the city gates of Taiyuan, Li Yuan and the others were still taking a leisurely "stroll" far behind.

After entering the city, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba slowed down, reining in their horses to walk slowly through the streets.

Scholars carrying swords on horseback were a common sight in Taiyuan. None of the people here recognized the world-renowned Second Brother Li and Third Brother Li. Though covered in dust from their journey, the two made no deliberate effort to hide themselves, blending seamlessly into the crowd as ordinary members of the masses.

"It's been a long time since I felt this relaxed," Li Shimin said. "Back in Zhangye, which time did we go out without drawing a crowd of onlookers?"

Li Xuanba replied, "If you shout 'I am Li Shimin!' at the top of your lungs right now, you'll still draw a crowd."

Li Shimin raised his whip.

Li Xuanba said, "We're inside the city. If you dare gallop your horse, I'll report you to Mother for disturbing the peace."

Li Shimin lowered his whip and said helplessly, "The moment we get home, you turn back into the same snitching puppy as before."

Li Xuanba said, "Say whatever you like."

The two brothers fell silent, proceeding slowly along the street once more.

They did not know where their home in Taiyuan was located. However, Sui Dynasty cities all followed a ward-and-market grid layout, and noble residences were always situated in the same quadrant. As long as they headed in that direction, they were bound to find it.

Taiyuan was half a border town, so the management of its wards and markets was not as strict as in Luoyang or Daxing. Along the roads connecting the residential wards to the markets, street peddlers carrying pole-baskets sold steamed cakes.

Outside the official markets, public security was poor, and the guards barely enforced order. Thus, those peddlers carried weapons like wooden clubs—essentially taking full responsibility for their own safety.

Catching the aroma of baked cakes, Li Shimin dismounted and bought two of them.

The peddler had a fierce, fleshy face, but he looked at Li Shimin with trepidation. "Young master, you might not be accustomed to my cakes."

Li Shimin asked in confusion, "Did you put bad ingredients in besides flour?"

The peddler hurriedly shook his head. "I don't do dishonest business! It's just that noble folk surely eat refined white flour, while my flatbread... is a bit coarse."

Li Shimin laughed. "I just returned from the frontier. I can eat boiled wheat whole, so flatbread with chaff actually tastes better to me!"

The peddler breathed a sigh of relief and offered the piping hot cake with a smile. "Then I have nothing to fear. Young master, please."

Li Shimin handed the peddler a few copper coins and tossed one of the steaming hot cakes to Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba caught it and scolded, "Couldn't you just hand it over? What if it hit the ground? Wasting food!"

Neither cared about their dirty hands, biting straight into the baked cakes.

After traveling non-stop, they were indeed hungry.

Li Shimin remounted with the cake in his mouth, took a bite, and held it with one hand. "Believe it or not, if you hadn't caught that cake, I would have caught it myself."

Li Xuanba didn't say whether he believed him or not, merely scolding, "Are you performing acrobatics?"

Li Shimin laughed, "Hahaha."

The two munched on their cakes slowly.

Stone mills were not yet widely used among the common people, so wheat flour was already considered a precious commodity.

Even the "white flour" claimed by commoners was actually just de-husked wheat ground with the bran intact, resulting in a grey flour that tasted somewhat gritty like sand.

By the standards of noble households, refining grey flour into true white flour would reduce its yield by another twenty to thirty percent, something even ordinary small landlords did not dare consume daily.

This applied not only to flour, but to rice and millet as well.

When Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were at the Duke of Tang’s residence, they dined off bronze cauldrons and fine tableware. The first time they accompanied Pei Shiju to Zhangye and ate coarse grains, they felt as if their throats were being slashed open, barely able to swallow it down.

After finishing the coarse flour cakes, Li Shimin clapped his hands and lowered his voice. "Ah-Xuan, I still trust Father. The future can be changed, can't it? In the apocrypha you saw, did I only show my talents after Father raised his troops? At that time, Eldest Brother was the legitimate eldest son, and my military achievements weren't significant yet, so it was understandable for Father to make Eldest Brother the Crown Prince. Things are different now—very different."

Li Xuanba remained silent.

Li Shimin said, "Look, I’ve already taken Heyou into my hands; my territory is even larger than Father’s. If Father doesn't choose me, wouldn't a civil war be foreseeable? If a civil war breaks out, one of us—Eldest Brother or I—must die... What I mean is, Eldest Brother would definitely die."

Li Xuanba had been quite solemn, but hearing his Second Brother’s supplementary remark, the corner of his mouth twitched slightly.

Li Shimin shrugged. "It's not that I look down on Eldest Brother, but I have troops, and he doesn't."

Li Xuanba said, "Mm."

Li Shimin continued, "Am I right? If Father chooses me as his heir from the very beginning and asks Eldest Brother to yield gracefully, I would have to hold Eldest Brother in high esteem out of both affection and interest, treating his descendants with great favor. Now, our circumstances are vastly different from the future you saw. Father... Father is truly good to us."

Li Xuanba wanted to retort: *Where exactly is he "truly good"?*

However, he did not refute his Second Brother.

Perhaps in Second Brother’s eyes, the fact that their father did not favor the eldest son and gave him the freedom to display his strength meant he was truly good to him.

Although they had suffered their grandmother's temper in the past, Second Brother was broad-minded; he had likely forgotten things from many years ago.

Besides, that was just their grandmother's bias. Although their father had been forced to obey her out of filial piety at the time, he had secretly stood on their side.

Of course, Li Xuanba did not think this way, but he could tell that Second Brother did.

He possessed memories of his previous life. Even though he had lived in this era for many years, causing his past life to fade like an old painting and making him almost two distinct people, it still exerted an influence on his personality.

Second Brother, on the other hand, was a pure "native." No matter how remarkable he was, he was currently just a sixteen-year-old boy.

If counted by exact age, he was only fifteen—just a high school freshman.

Furthermore, fathers in this era were mostly overly strict and unsmiling toward their sons, caring only about pushing them to study, showing very little warmth.

Their father, by contrast, was a rare "open-minded father" of this era who indulged his children and enjoyed playing with them.

In modern times, fathers willing to kiss, hug, and lift their children high into the air were very common. But in this era, such a father was truly an anomaly.

Even he, a lonely soul from modern times, found it hard to relinquish calling Li Yuan "Father," let alone Second Brother.

Li Xuanba sighed.

That was why he had spoken such harsh words to his softening Second Brother—he worried that Second Brother would lower his guard.

While lowering his guard would not damage Second Brother’s foundation, it would hurt Second Brother personally.

"Fine. Second Brother is right," Li Xuanba said. "I was just uncomfortable with Father telling me to help Li Jiancheng, but I also believe Father loves us."

Li Shimin smiled. "That's more like it. Come on, look at that grand residence ahead—doesn't it look like our home?"

Li Xuanba rolled his eyes. "Mother is already waving at us from the doorway."

Li Shimin chuckled and whipped the rump of Li Xuanba’s horse, sending it shooting forward. "Run fast, Ah-Xuan!"

"What?! Li Shimin!" Li Xuanba gasped, hurriedly reining in his horse for fear of crashing into their mother.

Evidently, Li Xuanba had overthought it. Lady Dou did not even bat an eye. Two burly servants stepped in front of her with a loud shout, bringing the horse to an immediate halt.

Li Xuanba leaped off his horse. "Mother! Second Brother, he—"

Lady Dou shielded Li Xuanba behind her and held out her hand. "Give me the whip!"

Li Shimin dismounted with a grin. "Mother, don't listen to Ah-Xuan's nonsense, I didn't do anything... Ah! You're really hitting me?! I was wrong, I was wrong, Mother!"

Li Xuanba folded his arms, sneering coldly at his Second Brother, who was getting whipped on his very first day back home.

Even the April air seemed chilled by Li Xuanba’s cold gaze and icy sneer.

*That's what you get for being mischievous—serves you right!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第122章 二哥你冤杀功臣
chunks.chineseText:
第122章 二哥你冤杀功臣

李渊一眨眼， 两个儿子就不见踪影。
　　进城后，长孙晟和宇文弼忍着笑和李渊作别，李渊苦笑着往家里赶。
　　希望两个孩子没有迷路， 唉。
　　这么久没见， 李渊还以为两个儿子已经在边塞的风沙中被磨砺得很成熟了， 没想到还是这么令人头疼。
　　李渊对李智云道：“祈健，你可不能学你二兄三兄。”
　　李智云嘴里说“是”，心里翻白眼。
　　不学二兄三兄学谁？父亲， 我又不傻。
　　李渊回到家，听到李世民和李玄霸虽然顺利找到家门口，但李世民刚回来就被夫人一顿抽。
　　李渊无奈：“夫人， 二郎才刚回来，你也太严格了。”
　　窦夫人板着脸道：“刚回来就欺负三郎， 更应该抽！”
　　李智云跟着二哥三哥去了一趟边塞， 胆子大了许多，在长辈面前变得活泼不少。
　　他火上浇油道：“二兄刚回来就当着母亲的面欺负三兄，说明二兄一直都在欺负三兄，才会这么顺手。”
　　李智云一边说一边往窦夫人身后躲。
　　李世民捏拳头。
　　窦夫人瞥了李世民的手。
　　李世民瞬间把手放下去。
　　李智云捂嘴：“噗嗤。”
　　万氏戳了一下儿子的脑袋：“怎么出门一趟，更皮了？”
　　李智云抱住万氏的手臂：“阿姨， 我一点都不皮，不信你问三兄！”
　　李世民瓮声瓮气道：“怎么不问我？”
　　李玄霸没好气道：“为什么不问你？二哥问出这个问题， 不是应该自己反省一下？”
　　李世民又抬起手。
　　窦夫人又瞥过来。
　　李世民再次放下手。
　　“扑哧。”这次是李渊捂嘴笑了。
　　李世民幽怨地看向父亲：“耶耶……”
　　李渊干咳一声，道：“赶紧去沐浴更衣，还要脏到什么时候？沐浴之后耶耶亲自给你们烤小羊羔吃。”
　　李世民给了李玄霸、李智云一个“你们等着”的眼神。
　　三人一同在家中的大澡池子沐浴， 窦夫人不能进去。李世民就要看看， 谁还能救这两个有了父母撑腰就要翻天的弟弟。
　　李玄霸毫不畏惧地回了二哥一个“怕你？”的眼神。
　　二哥刚欺负他和小五， 出了澡池子就要加倍还回来。来啊， 同归于尽啊。
　　李智云坚定不移地站在三哥这边，反抗从小就欺负弟弟的臭二哥。
　　三兄弟的眼神交流没有瞒过窦夫人和万氏。
　　她们对视一眼，眼神中有无奈，有宠溺，也有欣慰。
　　看来兄弟三人的感情很好，她们就放心了。
　　李世民不是会被威胁的人。他越被人威胁，就越要勇往直前。
　　所以，澡池子里弟飞弟跳，哀嚎连连。李玄霸和李智云洗完澡出来时，就好像被迫负重跑了几百里似的。
　　窦夫人都气笑了。
　　她像李世民幼年时一样，将李世民的脸颊拧着转了半周：“娘亲的话你都不听了是吗？让你别欺负弟弟，你还变本加厉？明日就抄书！弓箭没收！”
　　李世民疼得嗷嗷叫，可怜兮兮求饶，并向父亲求助。
　　李渊干咳一声，转身。
　　李世民：“……”
　　李世民乖乖认罚，并悔过下次一定不会再欺负弟弟。
　　李智云对李玄霸悄悄道：“二兄从小保证多少次了？”
　　李玄霸都懒得回答。
　　年幼时他身体很差，说话说多了都喘气，二哥对他多照顾啊。
　　自从他年岁增长，体力恢复到只比正常人偏弱的地步，二哥就变成寻常感情好的亲哥了——弟弟是用来折腾的，不然要弟弟干什么？
　　回家后就闹了一场，虽然李世民挨了罚抄，但家里气氛变得十分和睦亲切。
　　李玄霸甚至怀疑二哥是不是故意的。
　　不过以二哥性格，应当不是故意的。他就只是回家后就放飞自己，变幼稚了而已。
　　李建成带着李元吉住在河东郡，现在还没回来。李世民、李玄霸和李智云三兄弟每日承欢父母膝下，十分开心。
　　李玄霸眼见着二哥因为太开心，每天年龄都在递减，真达成了“笑一笑十年少”的“奇迹”，完全从了边塞无敌小将军，变成了父母的五六岁大宝贝。李智云都没二哥会撒娇，真是没眼看。
　　李世民听了弟弟的嫌弃后，不仅没有尴尬，还嘲笑弟弟装模作样，明明心里也很想和父母撒娇，就是不敢去。
　　窦夫人笑着将李玄霸揽进怀里：“没关系，娘亲主动让你撒娇。”
　　李玄霸闹了个大红脸，气得想把二哥揍一顿，可惜揍不赢。
　　李智云回家后，将好友罗士信介绍给万氏。
　　万氏十分喜欢罗士信，当即让罗士信认了干娘。
　　万氏道：“五郎身边有你这个义兄照顾，我就放心了。”
　　罗士信摇头：“二郎君和三郎君都很照顾集弘，我也只是一同被二郎君和三郎君照顾的人。”
　　李智云嫌弃道：“娘亲客套一下，你还真信？娘亲的意思是让我们互相学习互相进步，别给二兄三兄拖后腿。”
　　罗士信认真道：“好！我一定和集弘一起努力！”
　　万氏用帕子捂着嘴轻笑：“好，好。”
　　万氏还问了罗士信父母的籍贯，请李渊送给罗士信印信，让罗士信借军方驿道回家一趟。
　　她给罗士信准备了许多礼物：“太原和张掖都很安全，士信，你回去劝劝你父母，虽然背井离乡有些难过，但你已经为官吏，他们跟随你进城生活也是该享的福分。”
　　李世民也道：“如果伯父伯母不愿意离家，也最好搬到郡城里住。就算民贼破城，只要积极上缴所征粮食，他们一般也不会太为难城中百姓。”
　　罗士信严肃道：“是，郎君，我会尽力劝说。”他还是希望父母去张掖。张掖才让他有“自己地盘”的感觉。但张掖太偏远，恐怕父母不愿意。
　　李玄霸对宗罗睺和自己的亲信向固道：“劳烦你们陪同士信走一趟。士信年少，伯父伯母可能会不相信士信的功劳。请及时回来，我和二哥成亲还需要你们充当仪仗。”
　　宗罗睺和向固听闻他们能进入二郎君三郎君成亲的仪仗，顿时红光满面：“是！我们一定会及时回来！”
　　宗罗睺来到太原后，心情本来不太好。
　　在张掖时，因李世民这个最大的领导不拘小节，不看出身，所以宗罗睺过得很自在，没感到自己低人一等。
　　来到太原后，虽然他身为二郎君的亲卫，在唐国公府的待遇还算不错，但他总能感到这个地方的气氛与张掖完全不同。
　　比如唐国公府来往贵胄都把他当空气，甚至当脏空气。
　　宗罗睺理智上知道唐国公是除大隋宗室之外最高等的爵位，唐国公府是大隋顶尖的勋贵之家，来往者都是世家勋贵这等出身极高的人物。这群人看不上自己才是理所当然。
　　只是张掖的氛围给了他错觉，让他以为自己能凭借才华和这些人站在平等的位置上。
　　现在两位郎君把他派出太原，让他松了口气。而两位郎君居然不顾他的出身，也不顾他刚投效不久，竟然要让他也进入迎亲的仪仗队伍，更让他感动不已。
　　宗罗睺想通了。自己投奔的是行军大将李世民，上峰是李世民和李玄霸。唐国公只是两位郎君的父亲，所以自己要尊敬他。除此之外，唐国公府就和自己没关系，自己只需要听从上峰的命令。
　　罗士信、向固、宗罗睺离开后，李世民跑到李玄霸的屋里睡了一晚，和李玄霸卧床长叹。
　　李世民叹气道：“我见罗睺近日心情一直低落，真担心罗睺会走。罗睺才高气傲，他在唐国公府受了冷落，可能心有不忿。”
　　李玄霸打着哈欠道：“我倒是反而觉得他会对你更加死心塌地。”
　　李世民苦笑：“因为他看到其他地方对出身过于看重，只有我这里只看才华吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“难道不是吗？”
　　李世民摇头：“阿玄，在外人眼中，我们和唐国公府是一体的。罗睺肯定看出我们有自立之心，他会担心将来若立功，就算我和你对他很好，但父亲可能不会平等对待他。”
　　李玄霸道：“那你只能加倍对他好了。”
　　李世民叹气道：“是啊。”
　　过了一会儿，李世民还在叹气，李玄霸无奈睁开眼：“二哥，别叹气了。罗睺都到你手中了，不可能投向他人。能不能对自己有点自信啊摔！你知道你秦王府除了一个姓封的是墙头拐角处的草之外，就算被严刑逼供也没人背叛你吗？！”
　　李世民瞠目结舌：“啊？都上严刑逼供了？谁这么惨？”
　　李玄霸道：“一个叫张亮的，也是庶民出身。”
　　李世民焦急道：“现在他在哪？”
　　李玄霸没好气道：“不知道。我只知道他的籍贯是荥阳，但荥阳那么大，他名字太大众，又出身贫寒，哪可能找得到。不过将来他还是被你以谋反的罪名杀了。”
　　李世民：“……啊？”
　　李玄霸切换心音安慰道：【没办法，皇帝老了就要为年少的太子铺路。二哥，我之前不是和你说过吗？你原本立的太子被废，后来立的太子太年轻。】
　　【张亮虽无谋反之能，也还没做谋反之事，但他可能有谋反之意；刘洎是太子辅佐，但性格过于狂傲，常说狂言妄语，又与太子政见不合。为了给太子铺路，你爱惜了一辈子的羽毛，也只能在晚年时弄脏双手。】
　　【不过别太愧疚，你冤杀功臣就这么两例，比起其他皇帝算最宽仁的了，不要有心理负担。何况我预见的事已经改变许多，将来你也不一定会再杀他们。】
　　安慰结束，李玄霸翻身就睡。
　　如他所料，他二哥半夜气冲冲回自己房间睡觉去了，没有再打扰他的睡眠。
　　李玄霸：计划通√。
　　不仅当晚李世民没有再来打扰李玄霸睡觉，接下来几日也给了李玄霸足够多的宁静。
　　李玄霸美滋滋看书。
　　回太原后，二哥一会儿担心张掖的班底，一会儿劝自己对父母更亲近些，一会儿又害羞接下来的婚礼。
　　絮絮叨叨，念念叨叨，碎碎叨叨，李玄霸本来也有些婚前紧张，被二哥叨叨得心烦意燥，嘴皮都上火冒了个泡。
　　忍无可忍无需再忍。本来李玄霸没想过在二哥大喜当头的时候给二哥泼冰水，但二哥实在是太不做人，他也只好不当人了。
　　李世民生了李玄霸几日闷气。在李建成和李元吉回太原的前一日，他如小时候一样，扭扭捏捏来找李玄霸和好。
　　李世民瓮声瓮气道：“你就算嫌我吵到你很烦，也不该这么吓唬我。我才不会冤杀大臣。”
　　李玄霸道：【张亮只能算半个冤杀。他养五百义子不算什么，和一群跳大神的交往过密，把儿子的皮肤病说成是龙鳞，大部分皇帝都容不下他。只是因为历史中的你太爱惜羽毛，所以你杀了他，后世人才一副‘好震惊啊’的表情。】
　　李世民被弟弟逗笑了。
　　他小声道：“你只提张亮，那刘洎是真的被冤枉了。”
　　李玄霸没说话。
　　刘洎确实是被褚遂良诬告。唐太宗赐死刘洎时，估计也心知肚明。
　　这个诬告者褚遂良，史书记载中是盖棺论定的品德高尚之人。因为品性太过高尚，这难得的诬告行为，让后世史学家老想为他翻案，猜测是不是许敬宗等奸臣干的。
　　然后史学家们越考据越难过地证明，这事真是褚遂良干的。
　　褚遂良因反对唐高宗立武则天为后，后半生一直颠沛流离，凄凉而终，诸子也被流放。但武则天临死前，却在遗诏中特意点了褚遂良的名字，为褚遂良平反。
　　如果说武则天为王、萧二族平反，是为了换取身后事的妥协，褚遂良只是出身在一个与寒门无太多差别的小世家，无论家族还是故友在朝中早已经没有势力，她特意点了褚遂良的名字，这就和利益关系不大，只是纯粹肯定褚遂良这个人本身了。
　　一个人如果能被原本恨他入骨的政敌肯定，那么他的品性应当是不差的。
　　刘洎死在自己的脾气上。当唐太宗年老，而太子李治不仅年少，当时还披着懦弱的伪装，想要刘洎死的大唐品性良好的大臣太多了。
　　在唐太宗还很宠爱刘洎时，刘洎为了抢夺唐太宗的飞白，在唐太宗刚写好字时就登上龙榻上抢走，当时群臣都奏“刘洎擅登皇帝御床，理应处死”，被唐太宗以“昔闻婕妤辞辇，今见常侍登床”的玩笑保下。
　　后世史学家震惊这一点，是因为汉唐品德高尚之人和宋及宋以后的“品德高尚”不一样。他们为了大义，常常是不择手段的。
　　比如汉朝使臣热衷去藩国碰瓷作死为汉武帝寻找出兵借口，也比如褚遂良等大唐道德模范见到危害大唐的不安定因素跑唐太宗耳边天天叨叨“杀了他他该死杀了他他该死”。
　　不过刘洎就算是死在自己狂妄的性格上，但冤案就是冤案。希望这一世，刘洎就算在性格上吃亏，也顶多只是免官回家，别被逼自尽了。
　　不知道如果在刘洎狂妄的时候，自己带着小五多把刘洎按在地上揍几顿，能不能把刘洎的狂妄治好。
　　李玄霸摸着下巴，露出不怀好意的微笑，并把自己的奇思妙想分享给二哥。
　　李世民拍了拍弟弟的肩膀，严肃道：“阿玄，放开手脚做，哥哥支持你……扑哧，哈哈哈哈哈，不知道他现在在哪，我要趁着我年少，和你一起多揍他几顿！”
　　李玄霸和哥哥击掌：“一言为定，我这就去找！”
　　兄弟二人露出如出一辙的坏笑。
