In the blink of an eye, Li Yuan’s two sons had completely vanished from sight.

After entering the city, Zhangsun Sheng and Yuwen Bi suppressed their laughter as they bade farewell to Li Yuan, leaving him to hurry home with a wry smile.

*I just hope those two boys don't lose their way. Ah...*

Having not seen them for so long, Li Yuan had thought his two sons would have matured amidst the harsh winds and sands of the frontier. He never expected them to remain such a royal headache.

Li Yuan turned to Li Zhiyun and said, "Qijian, you must never learn from your Second and Third Brothers."

Li Zhiyun said, "Yes, Father," while rolling his eyes on the inside.

*If I don't follow Second Brother and Third Brother, who should I follow? Father, I'm not stupid.*

When Li Yuan arrived home, he learned that although Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had successfully found their way to the front gate, Li Shimin had been soundly thrashed by his wife the very moment he stepped inside.

Li Yuan said helplessly, "My lady, Erlang has only just returned. Aren't you being too strict?"

Lady Dou replied with a frosty face, "He bullied Sanlang the moment he set foot in the house! That makes him even more deserving of a thrashing!"

Having accompanied his Second and Third Brothers to the frontier, Li Zhiyun had grown much bolder and far more lively in front of his elders.

Adding fuel to the fire, he chimed in, "Second Brother bullied Third Brother right in front of Mother the second he got back. That proves he's been bullying Third Brother all along—that's why it's second nature to him!"

As he spoke, Li Zhiyun shrank back behind Lady Dou.

Li Shimin clenched his fists.

Lady Dou cast a cold glance at Li Shimin's hands.

Li Shimin immediately dropped his hands to his sides.

Li Zhiyun covered his mouth: "Pfft."

Lady Wan poked her son's head. "How is it that after one trip away, you've gotten even more mischievous?"

Li Zhiyun wrapped his arms around Lady Wan's arm. "Mother, I'm not mischievous at all! If you don't believe me, ask Third Brother!"

Li Shimin grunted sullenly, "Why don't you ask me?"

Li Xuanba replied irritably, "Why *shouldn't* she ask you? Asking a question like that, shouldn't Second Brother reflect on himself first?"

Li Shimin raised his hand again.

Lady Dou glanced over once more.

Li Shimin lowered his hand a second time.

"Pfft." This time, it was Li Yuan who covered his mouth and chuckled.

Li Shimin gave his father a deeply aggrieved look. "Father..."

Li Yuan gave a dry cough and said, "Hurry along and take a bath and change your clothes. How long do you intend to stay covered in grime? After your bath, Father will personally roast a young lamb for you to eat."

Li Shimin shot Li Xuanba and Li Zhiyun a look that clearly said, *Just you wait.*

The three brothers went to bathe together in the estate's large bath house, where Lady Dou could not enter. Li Shimin intended to see who could possibly save these two younger brothers of his, who thought they could turn heaven and earth upside down just because they had their parents backing them.

Li Xuanba fearlessly returned a gaze that said, *Think I'm scared of you?*

Second Brother had just bullied him and Fifth Brother; the moment they left the bath house, they would pay him back twofold. Bring it on—mutual destruction it is!

Li Zhiyun stood firmly by Third Brother's side, uniting to rebel against their rotten Second Brother who had bullied his younger siblings since childhood.

However, the silent eye-contact between the three brothers did not escape the eyes of Lady Dou and Lady Wan.

The two women exchanged a look filled with helplessness, doting affection, and relief.

It seemed the bond among the three brothers was as strong as ever; that put their minds at rest.

Li Shimin was not the sort of person to take threats lightly. The more someone threatened him, the more fiercely he pressed forward.

Consequently, inside the bath house, brothers flew and leapt amid endless wails of misery. By the time Li Xuanba and Li Zhiyun stepped out after their bath, they looked as though they had been forced to run a hundred miles carrying heavy loads.

Lady Dou was amused to the point of anger.

Just as she used to do when Li Shimin was a child, she pinched his cheek and twisted it halfway round. "You won't even listen to your mother anymore, is that it? I told you not to bully your brothers, and yet you double down? Tomorrow, you copy texts! And your bow and arrows are confiscated!"

Li Shimin howled in pain, begging for mercy pathetically as he cast pleading glances toward his father for help.

Li Yuan gave a dry cough and promptly turned his back.

Li Shimin: "..."

Li Shimin obediently accepted his punishment, swearing with deep remorse that he would never bully his brothers again.

Li Zhiyun whispered to Li Xuanba, "How many times has Second Brother promised that since we were kids?"

Li Xuanba couldn't even be bothered to answer.

When he was young and his health was weak, taking a few extra steps left him breathless, and Second Brother had doted on him with utmost care.

Ever since he grew older and his physical strength recovered to the point of being only slightly weaker than a normal person's, Second Brother had turned into an ordinary, affectionate older brother—younger brothers existed to be tormented, after all; otherwise, what were they good for?

Though a big commotion had broken out the moment they stepped through the door and Li Shimin had been sentenced to copying texts, the atmosphere in the household became immensely warm and harmonious.

Li Xuanba even suspected whether Second Brother had done it on purpose.

Then again, knowing Second Brother's personality, it probably wasn't intentional. He had simply let himself loose the moment he got home, reverting to childish antics.

Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji were currently residing in Hedong Commandery and had not yet returned. The three brothers—Li Shimin, Li Xuanba, and Li Zhiyun—spent their days bringing joy to their parents' knees, thoroughly enjoying themselves.

Li Xuanba watched as Second Brother, brimming with bliss, seemed to mentally regress in age with every passing day, truly achieving the miraculous adage that "a smile takes ten years off your age." He had completely transformed from an invincible young general on the frontier into his parents' five- or six-year-old spoiled darling. Even Li Zhiyun couldn't act half as pampered as Second Brother—it was truly an eyesore.

Upon hearing his younger brother's disdain, Li Shimin not only felt no embarrassment, but even mocked Li Xuanba for putting on airs, claiming that in truth, Third Brother desperately wanted to act pampered toward their parents too, but simply lacked the guts.

Lady Dou smiled and pulled Li Xuanba into her arms. "It doesn't matter, Mother will take the initiative to let you act pampered."

Li Xuanba's face flushed bright red. He was so infuriated he wanted to beat Second Brother up, but unfortunately, he couldn't win in a fight.

After returning home, Li Zhiyun introduced his good friend Luo Shixin to Lady Wan.

Lady Wan liked Luo Shixin very much and immediately had him adopt her as his godmother.

Lady Wan said, "With a sworn older brother like you taking care of Wulang, my heart is at ease."

Luo Shixin shook his head. "Second Young Master and Third Young Master both take great care of Jihong. I am merely another person being looked after by Second Young Master and Third Young Master."

Li Zhiyun said with mock disdain, "Mother was just being polite, and you actually took it literally? Mother means for us to learn from each other and make progress together, so we don't drag Second Brother and Third Brother down."

Luo Shixin said earnestly, "Alright! I will definitely work hard together with Jihong!"

Lady Wan covered her mouth with a handkerchief and chuckled gently. "Good, good."

Lady Wan also asked about the native place of Luo Shixin's parents and requested Li Yuan to issue official credentials to Luo Shixin, allowing him to travel back home using the military courier posts.

She prepared many gifts for Luo Shixin and said, "Both Taiyuan and Zhangye are safe. Shixin, when you return, try to persuade your parents. Although leaving one's hometown is hard, you are now an official; following you to live in the city is a blessing they deserve to enjoy."

Li Shimin added, "If your uncle and aunt are unwilling to leave their hometown, it's best if they at least move into the commandery seat. Even if rebel bandits breach the city, as long as the people hand over the requisitioned grain, the bandits generally won't make things too difficult for the townspeople."

Luo Shixin replied gravely, "Yes, Young Master. I will do my utmost to persuade them." He still hoped his parents would go to Zhangye. Only Zhangye gave him the feeling of "his own turf." However, Zhangye was far too remote, and he feared his parents might be unwilling.

Li Xuanba addressed Zong Luohou and his trusted aide Xiang Gu: "I must trouble you two to accompany Shixin on this journey. Shixin is young, so his parents might not believe the merits he has achieved. Please return in time; Second Brother and I will still need you to serve in the honor guard for our upcoming weddings."

Hearing that they would be included in the bridal honor guard for Second Young Master and Third Young Master, Zong Luohou and Xiang Gu instantly beamed with pride. "Yes! We will certainly return in time!"

Ever since arriving in Taiyuan, Zong Luohou had been in a rather foul mood.

In Zhangye, because Li Shimin, the highest-ranking leader, did not stand on ceremony and paid no mind to lineage, Zong Luohou had lived comfortably, never feeling inferior to anyone.

Upon coming to Taiyuan, although he enjoyed fairly decent treatment at the Duke of Tang's estate as Second Young Master's personal guard, he could constantly sense that the atmosphere here was entirely different from Zhangye's.

For instance, the noble figures coming and going from the Duke of Tang's residence treated him like air—or worse, foul air.

Rationally, Zong Luohou knew that the Duke of Tang held the highest noble title under the Great Sui imperial house, and the Tang Ducal Estate was among the pinnacle of noble houses in the empire. Those who frequented it were elite aristocrats and high-born nobility. It was only natural for such people to look down on him.

It was just that the atmosphere in Zhangye had given him an illusion, making him think he could stand on equal footing with these people based on his talents alone.

Now that the two young masters were sending him out of Taiyuan, he felt immensely relieved. Furthermore, that the two young masters disregarded his humble background and the short duration of his service to include him in the wedding honor guard moved him beyond words.

Zong Luohou came to a clear realization. The person he had sworn allegiance to was Li Shimin, the Campaign General, and his superiors were Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. The Duke of Tang was merely the father of his superiors, so he ought to show him respect. Beyond that, the Duke of Tang's estate had nothing to do with him; he only needed to obey his superiors' commands.

After Luo Shixin, Xiang Gu, and Zong Luohou departed, Li Shimin sneaked into Li Xuanba's room to sleep for the night, lying in bed beside Li Xuanba while sighing deeply.

Li Shimin sighed, "Seeing Luohou so despondent these past few days, I was truly worried he might leave. Luohou is proud and talented; being given the cold shoulder at the Duke's estate must have left him resentful."

Yawning, Li Xuanba replied, "On the contrary, I feel he will only become all the more devoted to you."

Li Shimin smiled wryly. "Because he saw how excessively other places value pedigree, while only I care strictly about talent?"

Li Xuanba said, "Is that not so?"

Li Shimin shook his head. "Ah-Xuan, in the eyes of outsiders, we and the Duke's estate are one and the same. Luohou has undoubtedly noticed our ambition to stand on our own. He worries that even if you and I treat him well when he earns military merits in the future, Father might not treat him as an equal."

Li Xuanba said, "Then you can only be twice as good to him."

Li Shimin sighed, "Indeed."

After a while, seeing that Li Shimin was still sighing, Li Xuanba opened his eyes helplessly. "Second Brother, stop sighing already. Luohou is already in your hands; there's no way he'll defect to anyone else. Can't you have a bit of confidence in yourself, damn it?! Do you know that in your Prince of Qin's Mansion, aside from a guy named Feng who was a literal fence-sitter, not a single person betrayed you even under severe torture?!"

Li Shimin was left dumbfounded. "Ah? Severe torture? Who suffered such a tragic fate?"

Li Xuanba said, "A man named Zhang Liang, also of commoner origins."

Li Shimin asked anxiously, "Where is he right now?"

Li Xuanba replied crossly, "I don't know. All I know is that his native place is Xingyang. But Xingyang is huge, his name is extremely common, and he comes from a poor background—how could we possibly find him? Though, in the future, you still had him executed on charges of treason."

Li Shimin: "...Huh?"

Li Xuanba switched to telepathy to comfort him: 【It couldn't be helped. When an emperor grows old, he must pave the way for a young Crown Prince. Second Brother, didn't I tell you before? The original Crown Prince you established was deposed, and the one you appointed later was too young.】

【Although Zhang Liang lacked the capability to rebel and hadn't actually committed treason, he likely harbored treasonous intent. Liu Ji was an advisor to the Crown Prince, but his personality was overly arrogant; he often uttered wild, reckless statements and held conflicting political views with the Crown Prince. To clear the path for your successor, you, who treasured your reputation all your life, had no choice but to dirty your hands in your twilight years.】

【Still, don't feel too guilty. You only executed two meritorious officials unjustly, which makes you the most benevolent compared to other emperors. Don't carry a psychological burden. Besides, the future I foresaw has already changed so much—you might not necessarily kill them in the future anyway.】

Having finished his comfort session, Li Xuanba rolled over and went to sleep.

Just as he expected, his Second Brother stomped off to his own room in a huff in the middle of the night to sleep, no longer disturbing his rest.

Li Xuanba: *Plan successful. √*

Not only did Li Shimin refrain from disturbing Li Xuanba's sleep that night, but he also granted Li Xuanba plenty of peace and quiet for the next few days.

Li Xuanba read his books delightfully.

Since returning to Taiyuan, Second Brother had been fretting one moment about his team in Zhangye, advising him to get closer to their parents the next, and getting shy about the upcoming weddings the moment after that.

Nagging, muttering, and endlessly blabbering—Li Xuanba had originally felt a bit of pre-marital tension himself, but Second Brother's non-stop rambling had driven him so agitated that a blister had popped up on his lip from sheer internal heat.

When endurance reached its limit, there was no need to endure any longer. Originally, Li Xuanba hadn't intended to pour cold water over Second Brother on the eve of his great joy, but Second Brother had truly acted too insufferable, so he had no choice but to act just as ruthless.

Li Shimin sulked at Li Xuanba for a few days. The day before Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji were scheduled to return to Taiyuan, he shuffled over awkwardly to make peace with Li Xuanba, just like when they were children.

Li Shimin grunted sullenly, "Even if you found me annoying and noisy, you shouldn't have scared me like that. I would never unjustly execute my ministers."

Li Xuanba replied mentally: 【Zhang Liang was only half-unjustly executed. Raising five hundred adopted sons was one thing, but he associated far too closely with sorcerers and shamans, even claiming his son's skin disease was 'dragon scales.' Most emperors wouldn't tolerate him. It was only because the historical you guarded your reputation so fiercely that when you killed him, later generations acted all shocked.】

Li Shimin was amused by his younger brother.

He whispered, "You only mentioned Zhang Liang, which means Liu Ji truly was wronged."

Li Xuanba remained silent.

Liu Ji indeed had been falsely accused by Chu Suiliang. When Emperor Taizong of Tang ordered Liu Ji to commit suicide, he likely knew the truth in his heart as well.

This false accuser, Chu Suiliang, was recorded in historical texts as a man of indisputably high moral character. Because his virtue was deemed so noble, this rare act of false accusation led later historians to repeatedly attempt to vindicate him, speculating whether it had been orchestrated by treacherous ministers like Xu Jingzong instead.

Yet, the deeper historians researched, the more sorrowfully they proved that the deed really *had* been done by Chu Suiliang.

Because Chu Suiliang opposed Emperor Gaozong of Tang making Wu Zetian the Empress, he spent the latter half of his life wandering in exile, meeting a desolate end, while his sons were banished. Yet on her deathbed, Wu Zetian specifically named Chu Suiliang in her imperial edict to rehabilitate his reputation.

If Wu Zetian rehabilitating the Wang and Xiao clans was meant to secure a compromise regarding matters after her death, Chu Suiliang had come from a minor gentry family barely different from a humble household, with neither his clan nor old friends retaining any power in court. Her explicit mention of Chu Suiliang had little to do with political interest; it was a pure, unadulterated affirmation of Chu Suiliang's character itself.

If a person could earn the affirmation of a political rival who had once hated him to the bone, his character could not have been bad.

Liu Ji died due to his own temperament. When Emperor Taizong grew old and the Crown Prince Li Zhi was not only young but also wearing a facade of weakness at the time, there were simply too many virtuous Tang ministers who wanted Liu Ji dead.

Back when Emperor Taizong favored Liu Ji immensely, Liu Ji once rushed onto the imperial bed to snatch a piece of *feibai* calligraphy right after Taizong finished writing it. At that time, the ministers submitted a memorial stating, "Liu Ji brazenly stepped onto the Emperor's imperial bed and ought to be executed." Emperor Taizong had shielded him with a joke: "In past times, I heard of the imperial concubine refusing to ride the palanquin; today, I witness an attendant stepping onto the bed."

Later historians were shocked by this because the concept of "high moral character" in the Han and Tang dynasties differed from that of the Song Dynasty and beyond. To achieve righteous ends, Han and Tang figures often used any means necessary.

For example, Han envoys eagerly went to vassal states to pick fights and court death just to give Emperor Wu of Han a pretext for launching military campaigns; similarly, Tang moral exemplars like Chu Suiliang, upon spotting any destabilizing factor threatening the empire, would whisper in Emperor Taizong's ear every single day: "Kill him! He deserves to die! Kill him! He deserves to die!"

Still, even if Liu Ji died because of his arrogant disposition, a tragic miscarriage of justice was still a miscarriage of justice. Hopefully, in this life, even if Liu Ji suffered for his personality, he would at most be dismissed from office and sent home, rather than forced to commit suicide.

*I wonder if, when Liu Ji acts arrogant, Fifth Brother and I could pin him to the ground and beat him up a few times to cure him of his arrogance.*

Li Xuanba stroked his chin, wearing a mischievous smile as he shared his whimsical idea with Second Brother.

Li Shimin patted his younger brother's shoulder and said solemnly, "Ah-Xuan, go all out. Your brother supports you... Pfft, hahahahaha! I wonder where he is right now. While I'm still young, I'm going to join you in beating him up a few more times!"

Li Xuanba high-fived his brother. "It's a deal. I'll go look for him right away!"

The two brothers flashed identical wicked smiles.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第123章 婚礼前宾客如云
chunks.chineseText:
第123章 婚礼前宾客如云

李世民和李玄霸兄弟二人虽然定下了这个坏主意， 但刘洎是荆州江陵人，其曾祖曾为南梁的官，自己也最先投奔大业十三年（公元617年）起兵的萧铣。他一家都在南方， 现在又家世不显， 现在要找到他还挺难。
　　二人就将这个坏主意暂且押后， 以后见到刘洎再说。
　　就算将来李世民不好意思揍刘洎，李玄霸还是可以带着小五一同完成这个计划，不急。
　　他们把这个计划记在两人共有的计划小本本中， 又交头接耳坏笑一通。
　　李世民和李玄霸和好如初。
　　李渊和窦夫人都没有为兄弟二人之前的“冷战”担忧。
　　他们都习惯了，这兄弟俩从小到大就这么折腾。
　　李建成带着李元吉回来时，李渊还对李建成吐槽了一番：“我还以为大雄大德在边塞磨砺了那么久， 现在应该成熟了，没料到还是那么顽皮。”
　　李建成看着父亲嘴上嫌弃， 脸上却满是骄傲的笑容。他嘴里应和， 心中苦涩无比。
　　随着年岁增长，又有李渊手把手教导，李建成的稚嫩和狂妄褪去不少，思想处事都成熟许多，眼界也开阔不少。
　　其他不说， 至少这天下濒临大乱，而自己父亲对大隋有异心这件事， 他和父亲朝夕相处，自然看得很清楚。
　　如果大隋还强盛，李建成思想成熟后， 见到二弟三弟的本事只会放心， 不会再像以前那样嫉妒——二弟三弟越厉害， 越不会对他继承“唐国公”的爵位造成威胁。
　　但现在大隋衰弱， “唐国公”这个爵位的价值就降低了。李建成从小熟读史书，知道乱世之中只有实力最为重要。李玄霸是个病秧子，不足为惧。李世民……唉。
　　李建成现在十分后悔。
　　李世民从小活泼开朗，讨人喜欢，他以前与李世民的感情自认还不错；李玄霸自幼多病阴沉，又特别喜欢黏着他，他既不喜欢李玄霸的性格，又觉得照顾李玄霸十分麻烦，就很不喜欢李玄霸。
　　如今想来，自己真是完全做错了。
　　若是在李玄霸主动接近自己的时候，自己对李玄霸多亲近一点，李玄霸肯定会成为自己的助力。
　　现在李元吉改好之后，对自己很亲近信服。但李元吉的本事远远不能和李玄霸比。如果李元吉和李玄霸都站在自己这边，就算李世民再出色，再加上自己嫡长的出身，也有自信与李世民分庭相抗。
　　所幸现在他与李玄霸的关系也不错，家中也还没有确定要走争霸天下这条路，或许还能弥补。
　　李建成决定，趁着李世民和李玄霸回来成亲，一定要做出一副好兄长的模样。
　　李建成恭敬离开后，李渊笑容淡去，长叹一声。
　　“此去河东，给毗沙门的打击很大啊。”李渊按住额角揉了揉，“真头疼。”
　　以前二郎三郎虽然也很出色，但大郎并不认为自己比他们差。大郎只是走的路与二郎三郎不同，若有同等机会，他自认肯定不输给年少的二郎三郎。
　　李渊其实心里也这么想过。
　　毕竟是自己手把手带大的孩子，大郎还比二郎三郎年长九岁，应当是很有本事，只是没有发挥出来。
　　但他把河东慰抚使的权力交给大郎，让大郎代自己在河东行事，大郎却一无所成。比起二郎三郎几乎白手起家，真是什么借口都想不出了。
　　“如果皇帝没有这么昏庸，二郎再怎么耀眼也无事，大隋容得下一门多国公，可是……唉。”李渊摇了摇头，苦笑不已。
　　自己还在观望时机，没有下定决心起兵，怎么就思考起继承皇位的事了？真是太自负。
　　虽然清楚未来的事说不准，说不定自己一辈子都等不到起兵的最好时机，但李渊还是希望让李玄霸和李建成更亲近一些。
　　李玄霸从小就想和大哥玩，只是李建成嫌弃李玄霸年幼体弱，不愿意带着李玄霸。
　　如果大郎和三郎关系变好，三郎肯定也会高兴。李渊想。
　　而且二郎已经很出色，没有三郎帮忙也能独立行走。掌心掌背都是肉，李渊看着失落的长子心里很不是滋味，希望三郎能拉大郎一把。
　　身为父亲，自然希望每个孩子都很出色。李渊也不例外。
　　李建成回来后，很快就邀请李世民和李玄霸小聚。
　　李元吉和李智云两个兄长的小尾巴也出席了。
　　李元吉与以前判若两人，表现得十分恭敬有礼，连神情都一板一眼，甚至稍显木讷了。
　　李元吉对以前的事向李世民和李玄霸道歉，仿佛已经忘记李玄霸的“算计”。
　　李世民和李玄霸也很客气热情地与李元吉回礼。
　　李智云继续当他的小透明。
　　兄弟私下聚餐十分兄友弟恭，让李渊欣慰不已。
　　但刚回居住的小院子，李世民、李玄霸和李智云就挤在一张床榻上，脑袋凑一起嘀嘀咕咕。
　　李智云搓胳膊：“天啦，我的鸡皮疙瘩都冒起来了，可怕！”
　　李世民严肃道：“阿玄，小五，我看李元吉那精神状态，比以前更加危险。你们一定要小心。”
　　李玄霸若有所思。
　　李世民敲李玄霸的脑袋：“听到没有，小心！不是我不信任他，我在战场上见多了这种人，这根本不是学好了，只是压住了而已！”
　　李玄霸道：“越是压制，爆发时就越可怕，我知道。我只是想，父亲母亲没发现吗？”
　　李世民道：“父亲应当只是以为李元吉改好了，娘亲……我去问问。”
　　李玄霸摇头：“你不好问，我去问。”
　　李世民对李智云道：“你武艺比你三兄强，去河东郡后，你一定要保护好你三兄，不要靠近李元吉。”
　　李智云傲气道：“二兄放心。李元吉再坏，但我可是在边塞磨砺过的人，他比不过我，哼哼！”
　　李世民摸了摸李智云的脑袋：“我相信你，阿玄就交给你了。”
　　李玄霸无奈：“只是一个李元吉，用不着这么紧张。我护卫不会离身。”
　　李世民叮嘱：“小心为上。”
　　李世民的直觉很准。他一见到李元吉就浑身不舒服，这个人绝对藏着什么坏主意。
　　其实李玄霸也一样，这次见到李元吉，比以前更不适。
　　他只是在想，李元吉变成这副木讷的模样，难道真的经历了过分严厉的教育，被磋磨得心理更变态了？
　　古时的人大多不懂教育，常常以为严厉教育就是棍棒加身。北周武帝就是这么过分严厉，把太子教成了变态。
　　李玄霸设计让李元吉暴露本性，好让父母严加管教他。但父母都知道天元帝的教训，应当不会重蹈覆辙才是。
　　第二日，李玄霸找到窦夫人，委婉询问母亲如何教导李元吉。
　　窦夫人叹气道：“你发现了？”
　　李玄霸装傻：“发现什么？”
　　窦夫人点了点李玄霸的额头：“李元吉现在看着很听话懂事，仿佛已经变成了一个好孩子，但他估计不仅本性未变，心里对你、对我，甚至对整个唐国公府都有仇恨了。”
　　李玄霸没想到母亲会回答得如此直白，顿时不知道如何回答。
　　窦夫人继续道：“我就知道这样不行。但你父亲非要把李元吉交给一个以严厉著称的老师，说我们狠不下心。唉，这是狠心就能教好吗？我表兄……罢了，不提这个，你小心为上。”
　　李玄霸道：“是，母亲放心。”
　　窦夫人笑道：“我知道你很有本事，应当无事。本来看你婚事临近很是紧张，娘亲想让你安静休息一会儿。你现在有闲心询问李元吉的事了，那看来也有闲心过问正事。关于义庄，娘亲有事要和你商议。”
　　李玄霸苦笑：“母亲别嘲笑我，我没有紧张。母亲想要找我，随时来问我，还需要等什么？”
　　窦夫人又笑着点了点李玄霸的额头：“你是我的孩子，你紧张没紧张，我还看不出来？”
　　李玄霸不敢说话了。他担心越反驳，母亲就越嘲笑他。
　　窦夫人知道李玄霸在面对亲近的人时脸皮没有对外人那么厚，没有继续笑话他。
　　母子俩凑近了一些说悄悄话，将义庄的事一条一条理顺。
　　窦夫人拿着自己的嫁妆把义庄壮大。现在义庄已经修起坞堡，坞堡内有农田、工匠，确保遇到流寇围困，也能在短时间内自给自足。
　　义庄的坞堡还和乡村联合起来。现在乡村都以义庄坞堡为核心修筑防御工事，重新规正农田，组织乡勇巡逻。
　　他们是坞堡的外围防线，而坞堡是他们的退路。
　　这一番坞堡和乡村联合防御的模式，在东汉末年至魏晋南北朝的中原十分常见。
　　现在如荥阳郑氏等山东望族，家中祖宅中的坞堡仍旧未拆。
　　大隋统治才三十三年，大部分人都还没有抛弃乱世思维，做好了应对乱世的准备。
　　窦夫人虽然一直长在深宫，没有亲身经历过乱世，但无论是北周武帝和父母的教导，还是这么多年唐国公夫人的阅历，她处理此事都得心应手。
　　“现在地方上稍稍有点实力的人都建起了坞堡，豢养私兵，仿佛回到了乱世。”窦夫人轻叹道，“舅舅改革府兵，好不容易把兵权从豪族手中收拢，现在又倒回去了。”
　　李玄霸点头赞同，也不由跟着叹气。
　　后世把隋炀帝捧上网庙十哲的时候，曾经有一个乍看很有道理的观点——隋炀帝北征吐谷浑三征高丽都是为了消磨世家的力量，所以世家才反抗。
　　这是完全不了解隋朝兵制。
　　隋朝的兵制继承北周府兵制。府兵制就是将原本豪强的私兵全部变成直属中央的兵卒。在北周武帝和隋文帝多番改革后，府兵来源以自耕农的富农、小地主为主，他们是隋朝纳税服役的中坚力量。
　　杨广继位之后，不断增加鹰扬府数量，又削弱鹰扬郎将的权力和地位，也是为了让地方军队更好地服从中央的管理。
　　只是后来天下大乱，中央管不到地方，大部分鹰扬府和当地豪族勾连起来，仍旧叛乱了。
　　隋朝出兵用的都是大隋的府兵，先死一批中央直属的府兵，又死一批新征召的府兵，后来三征高丽府兵逃亡严重，杨广为了保护自己，已经召集了一支募兵，也就是现在代替十二卫承担护卫皇帝职责的“骁果军”。
　　杨广把大隋的军队坑得七零八落，豪族趁机招募散兵游勇，重建被北周武帝和隋文帝瓦解的私兵武装。
　　中央军队覆灭，地方军阀就会崛起，这是最基本的常识。这明明是杨广给豪族喂肉。
　　隋末四处建立的坞堡就是地方军阀崛起的第一步。只是地方割据势力刚刚抬头，大唐就建立了，将地方割据消灭在萌芽阶段。
　　现在窦夫人的满腹担忧，就是眼睁睁看到乱世将起，豪强又图谋扩充兵力。
　　李玄霸叹息后，安慰道：“母亲，请相信二哥。他们乱不起来。”
　　窦夫人捏了捏李玄霸的脸。
　　李玄霸愕然地捂住脸，不明白为什么母亲突然捏自己。
　　窦夫人笑道：“我相信他，也相信你，还相信祈健，相信你口中那位未来的将军女儿。”
　　李玄霸捂着脸：“嗯……”不知为何，有点不好意思。
　　说到三姐和三姐夫，窦夫人叹了口气。
　　李世民和李玄霸回大兴时，三姐和三姐夫不在家，他们只留下礼物就离开了。
　　现在听母亲说起，李玄霸才知道三姐夫的母亲身体大不好了，所以三姐和三姐夫一家回了乡间老家，让老人在刚走不久的丈夫墓前静静过完生命最后一程。
　　李玄霸前世看平阳昭公主的生平时，曾疑惑平阳昭公主与丈夫柴绍的感情不错，为何长子根据考据，可能在李渊起兵后才出生。
　　平阳昭公主的病逝，很大可能就是因为两胎距离太近，她的生育年龄在这个时代又算得上大龄，死于产后并发症。
　　现在他猜测，可能是三姐和三姐夫虽早早成婚，但到了可以同房的年龄时，三姐夫的父母先后离世，他们不仅同房的时间有限，三姐的身体可能也在守孝时亏损太多。反倒是三姐在起兵后身体好了起来，后来才能怀孕。
　　只是身体亏损的隐患还在，又连续生育，拖垮了三姐的身体。
　　幸亏珠娘提前发现了三姐身体亏损的隐患。他再提醒一下三姐夫，有了长子后就注意一下避孕，三姐此生的未来应该会改变。
　　窦夫人看出了李玄霸的走神，问道：“你是在担心三娘？三娘难道未来会出什么事？”
　　李玄霸回过神，道：“我只是担心三姊现在还未生育，未来年龄大了，若频繁生育会伤害身体。”
　　窦夫人失笑：“你啊，你从小就关注女人的这些事，真是奇怪。”
　　李玄霸；“……”
　　窦夫人笑道：“不过娘很开心你关心我和三娘。”
　　她把李玄霸揽进怀里，像李玄霸小时候那样揉了揉李玄霸的头发：“放心，娘会好好叮嘱三娘。她将来要当公主，不必在乎子嗣，柴绍不敢负她。”
　　李玄霸道：“有我和二哥在，阿姊们都不会被欺负。”
　　窦夫人又摸了摸李玄霸的脑袋：“对。”
　　她想起李玄霸在幼时居然能发现自己来月事时身体不适，现在又担忧三娘生育不易，心中滋味很是复杂。
　　窦夫人知道男子不应当知晓这些女子的事，但李玄霸这样，她很开心。
　　窦夫人把李玄霸留着揉了许久，李玄霸回去的时候，就像是被母亲吸走了活力，趴在桌上一动不动。
　　李世民戳了戳李玄霸散乱的发髻：“怎么了？”
　　李玄霸有气无力道：“母亲还是把我当小孩啊。”
　　李世民笑道：“你就算七老八十了，还不是母亲的小孩。”
　　李玄霸道：“我得想个法子分散母亲的注意力。”
　　于是李玄霸把无所事事的寒钩和乌镝送给了母亲。
　　窦夫人的注意力果然被这两只“雕孙儿”吸引，不再拉着李玄霸亲近。
　　寒钩和乌镝收着翅膀跟在窦夫人身后摇摇晃晃散步，成为唐国公府一道风景。
　　李渊本来眼馋聪明的金雕，见金雕变成了走地鸡，就不稀罕了。
　　他还是喜欢威武凶猛能打猎的金雕。
　　又过了半月，宾客们逐渐到齐，快临近李世民和李玄霸的良辰吉日了。
　　李渊和亲家们商议，正好李世民和李玄霸是双生子，干脆一起娶亲一起拜堂，也算一则佳话。
　　亲家们都觉得这很有意思，全都同意。
　　至于算八字的人，他们都很识趣，知道怎么帮顾客达成目的。
　　于是神棍掐指一算，双生子合该一起成亲，这是大好事。
　　这件事在太原传开，百姓们就像是过年似的准备好新衣，也准备来凑热闹。
　　唐国公府那对著名的双生子居然要一同成亲，这一听就是很吉利的事，比迎佛像听着更稀奇。
　　现在的百姓和后世网络上转发锦鲤的网友们没太大差别，都是遇见吉祥的事都想去蹭一蹭。
　　反正不要钱。说不定还能蹭几个喜钱了！
　　李渊原本没打算大办，所以宾客请得不多。
　　但越临近婚礼，情势就由不得他不想大办了。
　　或许是李世民和李玄霸的名声太大，许多他没有请的宾客也纷纷上门。
　　比如他最头疼的河东、山东望族纷纷派人上门，不说本来就和李世民、李玄霸有交情的薛道衡、薛收出身的薛家，山东五姓望族也纷纷上门庆贺，连最为清高的天下望族之首崔氏都客客气气来当宾客，比杨素当年和崔氏联姻时还客气。
　　李渊都被吓到了。
　　崔氏来的人笑道：“李二郎和李三郎是天下难得的英才，可惜我们无缘早结识。现在他们大喜，我们怎么能不来庆贺？”
　　李渊听后，回到家对窦夫人捶胸顿足：“如果晚些给二郎三郎定亲，或许我们就能和崔氏联姻了！”
　　清河崔氏啊！
　　窦夫人板着脸道：“郎君，你可千万别这么说。若传出去，你让二郎三郎的亲家如何想？再者我们家已经有荥阳郑氏的儿媳了，不可再入山东郡姓的儿媳。”
　　李渊讪讪道：“我知道，我就是说说。”
　　那可是清河崔氏啊！杨素觍着脸去求亲，还被亲家埋汰的清河崔氏啊！
　　窦夫人无语。
　　清河崔氏又如何？哪有自家两个孩子有本事？不过是依仗祖上门荫而已。
　　她把丈夫抛到一边，自己继续忙碌儿子的婚礼。
　　在李世民和李玄霸回中原前，窦夫人早就开始准备。
　　李世民和李玄霸成亲前很闲，但窦夫人可是忙得脚不沾地。
　　现在宾客越来越多，地位又不一般，婚礼许多原本预定的环节需要更改，窦夫人非常劳累。
　　但她很开心。
　　还有比看到孩子出息更开心的事吗？
　　李渊长吁短叹了一番后，也将这些事抛之脑后，忙着接待宾客。
　　他苦笑着想，本应该是他给儿子们带来人脉，现在怎么感觉是两个儿子给自己带来了人脉？儿子太厉害，让身为父亲的自己压力很大啊。
　　但压力虽大，如窦夫人一样，李渊也对儿子出息非常开心。
　　不过当东西突厥都派人来庆贺时，李渊就不是开心，是惊吓了。
　　李渊把李世民和李玄霸拎到跟前来：“你们怎么还和东突厥有联系了？”
　　李世民挠头：“没有啊。”
　　李玄霸道：“若说有，那就是我们正准备联合西突厥去打东突厥。”
　　李渊纳闷；“那东突厥可汗派人来是怎么回事？”
　　李世民道：“父亲你防备东突厥，说不定东突厥可汗是看在你脸面上呢？”
　　李玄霸道：“或许二哥说得对。”
　　李渊挠头，这是真的吗？他怎么不自信呢？就当这是真的吧。
　　李渊赶紧拉着长孙晟一同接待突厥人，生怕出什么事。
　　“陛下还在亲征高丽，我们可不能让陛下误会。”李渊吓得满头汗。
　　长孙晟笑道：“突厥人只是来讨杯喜酒，你想多了，陛下不会在意。我们将此事告知陛下，说突厥人为了向大隋示好，趁着李二郎李三郎成亲，来让你帮忙转送陛下礼物不就行了？”在意更好，早点把李渊逼反。
　　李渊笑道：“还是你厉害，就这么做。”
　　李渊送出诚惶诚恐的文书，得到杨广赞赏的回信，刚松了口气。一个意外来客，让他的心又提了起来。
　　被皇帝冷落的太子杨暕，居然拿着皇帝为李世民、李玄霸贺喜的旨意，亲自来参加李世民和李玄霸的婚礼。
　　李渊知道皇帝与太子越发不睦，甚至说出杨玄感叛乱是不是太子里应外合的胡话。太子来参加自己儿子的亲事，皇帝不会猜忌自己和太子，以为自己和太子是一伙吧？
　　虽然杨暕的权力已经被皇帝下得差不多，但杨暕现在还是太子，李渊再担心也只能装出一副受宠若惊的模样，恭恭敬敬接待这位重量级宾客。
　　太原城的百姓不知道皇帝和太子不睦，见唐国公的二郎君三郎君居然能让太子亲自参加婚礼，纷纷昂首挺胸，与有荣焉。
　　杨暕以“不用麻烦”为由住在唐国公府里。夜里，杨暕又如曾经在洛阳时那样，翻了李世民和李玄霸的墙。
　　他提着酒坛子笑道：“唐国公不欢迎我，你们呢？”
　　李世民没好气道：“你若不来，我和阿玄才不高兴。”
　　李玄霸点头道：“今夜不醉不归。”
　　杨暕和李世民对视一眼，把李玄霸赶到一边去喝水，两人拼起了酒。
　　杨暕道：“你三杯倒，喝什么喝。”
　　李世民道：“得了吧，你喝了酒还怎么陪二表兄聊天，去去去。”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　他这次是很真心的想和二表兄不醉不归。以前二表兄不是老埋怨自己不和他喝酒，不如二哥和他亲近吗？怎么现在还嫌弃了？

Chapter 123: Guests Gather Like Clouds Before the Wedding

Although Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had settled on this mischievous scheme, Liu Ji was a native of Jiangling in Jingzhou. His great-grandfather had served as an official of the Southern Liang dynasty, and Liu Ji himself would initially join Xiao Xian when the latter raised his troops in the thirteenth year of Daye (617 AD). His whole family was in the south, and his family background was currently obscure, making him quite difficult to locate at present.

Thus, the two brothers put their wicked plan on hold, deciding to deal with Liu Ji whenever they bumped into him in the future.

Even if Li Shimin felt too embarrassed to beat Liu Ji up in the future, Li Xuanba could still carry out the plan alongside Fifth Brother. There was no rush.

Jotted down in the private notebook of shared plans they kept between them, they put their heads together and shared another bout of wicked chuckles.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were back to being as thick as thieves as if nothing had happened.

Neither Li Yuan nor Lady Dou had worried about the brothers' earlier "cold war."

They were used to it—these two brothers had been squabbling and causing a fuss like this since childhood.

When Li Jiancheng returned with Li Yuanji, Li Yuan even grumbled to Li Jiancheng, "I thought Daxiong and Dade would have matured after being tempered on the borderlands for so long. I didn't expect them to still be so mischievous."

Li Jiancheng looked at his father, whose words voiced complaint, yet whose face beamed with proud smiles. He echoed his father's words aloud, but in his heart, he felt an immense bitterness.

As he grew older and received personal guidance from Li Yuan, Li Jiancheng's former naivety and arrogance had faded considerably. His thinking and conduct had matured, and his horizons had broadened significantly.

If nothing else, he saw clearly that the realm was on the brink of total chaos and that his father harbored disloyal ambitions toward the Great Sui dynasty—a fact he naturally picked up on from spending day and night at his father's side.

Had the Great Sui remained strong and prosperous, a mature Li Jiancheng would only have felt reassured upon seeing the formidable abilities of his second and third younger brothers, rather than harboring past jealousies—for the more capable Second Brother and Third Brother were, the less threat they posed to his inheritance of the noble title of "Duke of Tang."

But now that the Sui dynasty was falling into decline, the value of the title "Duke of Tang" had diminished. Having read history extensively since childhood, Li Jiancheng knew that in times of chaos, strength alone mattered most. Li Xuanba was a sickly youth, nothing to fear. But Li Shimin... Sigh.

Li Jiancheng now felt deep regret.

From a young age, Li Shimin had been lively, outgoing, and well-liked, and Li Jiancheng had considered their relationship fairly good. Li Xuanba, on the other hand, had been sickly and gloomy since childhood, yet loved to cling to him. Disliking Li Xuanba's disposition and finding it troublesome to look after him, Li Jiancheng had harbored a strong dislike for his third brother.

Looking back now, he had made a colossal mistake.

Had he been closer to Li Xuanba when the boy actively sought his affection, Li Xuanba would surely have become his greatest pillar of support.

Now, after mending his ways, Li Yuanji was very close and devoted to him. But Li Yuanji's capabilities fell far short of Li Xuanba's. If both Li Yuanji and Li Xuanba were on his side, then even with Li Shimin's brilliance, Li Jiancheng—bolstered by his status as the eldest legitimate son—would have had the confidence to stand as an equal against Li Shimin.

Fortunately, his relationship with Li Xuanba was currently quite decent, and the family had not yet officially committed to the path of contending for supreme power over the realm; perhaps there was still time to make amends.

Li Jiancheng decided that while Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were back home to marry, he must play the part of a loving elder brother to perfection.

After Li Jiancheng respectfully took his leave, the smile faded from Li Yuan's face, replaced by a deep sigh.

"That trip to Hedong was quite a blow to Bishamen." Li Yuan pressed his temples and rubbed them. "What a headache."

In the past, though Second Brother and Third Brother were exceptionally gifted, Eldest Brother never believed he was inferior to them. Eldest Brother simply walked a different path; given equal opportunities, he believed he certainly wouldn't lose to his younger brothers.

Li Yuan himself had shared that sentiment in his heart.

After all, this was the child he had raised with his own hands, and Eldest Brother was nine years older than Second and Third Brother. He should have been highly capable, merely lacking the chance to display it.

Yet when he entrusted Eldest Brother with the authority of Pacification Commissioner of Hedong to act on his behalf, Eldest Brother achieved absolutely nothing. Compared to Second Brother and Third Brother building their success virtually from scratch, there was truly no excuse left to make.

"If the Emperor weren't so foolish and incompetent, no matter how brightly Second Brother shone, it wouldn't matter—the Great Sui could accommodate multiple dukes in one family. But... sigh." Li Yuan shook his head with a bitter smile.

*I'm still biding my time and haven't even resolved to raise troops yet; how have I already begun pondering imperial succession? How arrogant of me.*

Although he knew the future was uncertain—and perhaps he might never encounter the ideal opportunity to rise in rebellion in his entire lifetime—Li Yuan still hoped to see Li Xuanba and Li Jiancheng grow closer.

Ever since he was small, Li Xuanba had wanted to play with his eldest brother, but Li Jiancheng had looked down on him for being young and frail, refusing to drag him along.

*If Eldest Brother and Third Brother's relationship improves, Third Brother will surely be happy as well,* Li Yuan thought.

Besides, Second Brother was already brilliant enough to stand on his own two feet without Third Brother's aid. Both the palm and the back of the hand are flesh; seeing his eldest son so crestfallen left a bitter taste in Li Yuan's mouth, and he hoped Third Brother could lend Eldest Brother a helping hand.

As a father, it was only natural to want every child to excel. Li Yuan was no exception.

Upon his return, Li Jiancheng quickly invited Li Shimin and Li Xuanba for a small gathering.

Li Yuanji and Li Zhiyun, the little tails following their elder brothers, attended as well.

Li Yuanji seemed like a completely changed person, behaving with utmost deference and politeness. His expression was rigid and solemn, even appearing somewhat wooden.

Li Yuanji apologized to Li Shimin and Li Xuanba for his past actions, acting as though he had completely forgotten Li Xuanba's previous "schemes."

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba responded to Li Yuanji's courtesy with equal politeness and warmth.

Li Zhiyun continued to play the role of a quiet nonentity.

The brothers' private banquet radiated filial devotion and brotherly affection, comforting Li Yuan immensely.

However, the moment they returned to their courtyard, Li Shimin, Li Xuanba, and Li Zhiyun piled onto a single daybed, putting their heads together to whisper.

Li Zhiyun rubbed his arms. "Heavens, I've got goosebumps all over! How terrifying!"

Li Shimin said solemnly, "A-Xuan, Little Fifth, from what I can see of Li Yuanji's mental state, he is even more dangerous than before. You two must be careful."

Li Xuanba fell thoughtful.

Li Shimin tapped Li Xuanba's head. "Did you hear me? Be careful! It's not that I don't trust him, but I've seen plenty of people like him on the battlefield. He hasn't reformed at all—he's just repressing it!"

Li Xuanba said, "The more it's repressed, the more terrible the eventual explosion will be. I know. I'm just wondering... haven't Father and Mother noticed?"

Li Shimin said, "Father probably just thinks Li Yuanji has turned over a new leaf. As for Mother... I'll go ask her."

Li Xuanba shook his head. "It's awkward for you to ask. I'll go."

Li Shimin said to Li Zhiyun, "Your martial skills are better than your Third Brother's. Once you go to Hedong Commandery, you must protect your Third Brother well and keep your distance from Li Yuanji."

Li Zhiyun said proudly, "Don't worry, Second Brother! No matter how bad Li Yuanji is, I'm someone who's been tempered on the frontier. He's no match for me, hmph!"

Li Shimin patted Li Zhiyun's head. "I trust you. I'm entrusting A-Xuan to you."

Li Xuanba said helplessly, "It's just one Li Yuanji; there's no need to be so nervous. My guards won't leave my side."

Li Shimin urged, "Caution is paramount."

Li Shimin's intuition was razor-sharp. The instant he laid eyes on Li Yuanji, his skin crawled; that fellow was definitely harbouring some sinister intent.

Truth be told, Li Xuanba felt the same way. Seeing Li Yuanji this time made him feel even more uncomfortable than before.

He was merely wondering whether Li Yuanji's dull, wooden demeanor meant he had truly suffered overly harsh discipline, twisting his psyche into something even more twisted.

Most people in ancient times understood little of pedagogy, often believing that strict discipline simply meant corporal punishment. Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou had been excessively harsh in precisely this manner, driving his crown prince into madness and perversion.

Li Xuanba had engineered Li Yuanji's exposure so their parents would strictly discipline him. But since both parents were well aware of the tragedy of Emperor Tianyuan, they should not have repeated the same mistake.

The next day, Li Xuanba sought out Lady Dou and tactfully inquired how she and his father were instructing Li Yuanji.

Lady Dou sighed. "You noticed?"

Li Xuanba played dumb. "Noticed what?"

Lady Dou tapped Li Xuanba's forehead. "Li Yuanji seems obedient and sensible right now, appearing for all the world like a reformed child. But in reality, not only has his nature remained unchanged, but he likely harbors deep resentment toward you, toward me, and even toward the entire Duke of Tang's estate."

Li Xuanba hadn't expected his mother to be so forthright, leaving him momentarily at a loss for words.

Lady Dou continued, "I knew this wouldn't work. But your father insisted on handing Li Yuanji over to a teacher famous for his severity, claiming we couldn't bring ourselves to be harsh enough. Sigh, can harshness alone properly educate a child? My cousin... ah, never mind that. Just be careful."

Li Xuanba said, "Yes, Mother, rest assured."

Lady Dou smiled. "I know how capable you are, so you should be fine. Seeing how nervous you were as your wedding approached, I originally wanted you to get some quiet rest. But since you have the leisure to ask about Li Yuanji, it seems you also have the leisure to handle serious matters. Regarding the charitable estate, I have some things to discuss with you."

Li Xuanba smiled wryly. "Mother, don't tease me, I'm not nervous. If Mother needs me, you can ask me anytime. Why wait?"

Lady Dou tapped his forehead with a smile again. "You are my child; whether you are nervous or not, do you think I can't tell?"

Li Xuanba did not dare speak another word, fearing that the more he protested, the more his mother would tease him.

Knowing that Li Xuanba wasn't nearly as thick-skinned around family as he was with outsiders, Lady Dou refrained from teasing him further.

Mother and son leaned in to speak in hushed tones, going over the affairs of the charitable estate item by item to get everything in order.

Lady Dou had drawn upon her own dowry to expand the charitable estate. Now, fortified manors had been constructed, complete with farmlands and craftsmen inside to ensure self-sufficiency in the event of a short-term siege by rogue bandits.

The fortified manors of the estate were integrated with the surrounding villages. The local villages now built defensive structures centered around the manors, reorganized their farmlands, and organized local braves for regular patrols.

The villages formed the outer perimeter of defense, while the fortified manors served as their fallback retreat.

This model of joint defense between fortified manors and rural communities was exceedingly common in the Central Plains from the late Eastern Han dynasty through the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern dynasties.

Even now, prominent clans of the Shandong region, such as the Zheng clan of Xingyang, had yet to dismantle the fortified strongholds within their ancestral compounds.

The Great Sui had ruled for a mere thirty-three years; most people had not shed their survival mindset from times of chaos and remained fully prepared for turmoil.

Though Lady Dou had grown up in the imperial palace and never personally experienced an era of chaos, the teachings of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou and her parents, combined with her years of experience as the Duchess of Tang, enabled her to handle these matters with seasoned mastery.

"Now anyone with even a shred of local power is erecting fortified manors and raising private armies, as if we've returned to chaotic times," Lady Dou sighed softly. "My uncle reformed the Fubing system to wrest military authority from the prominent clans with great difficulty, and now everything is reversing."

Li Xuanba nodded in agreement and could not help sighing alongside her.

In future generations, when internet users sarcastically praised Emperor Yang of Sui into the "Hall of Fame," a popular argument that sounded plausible at first glance emerged: that Emperor Yang's northern campaigns against Tuyuhun and three expeditions against Goguryeo were meant to wear down the power of the great aristocratic families, prompting them to rebel.

This showed a complete ignorance of the Sui dynasty's military system.

The Sui military system inherited the Fubing (divisional militia) system of the Northern Zhou. The Fubing system transformed the private armies of powerful clans into troops directly subordinate to the central government. After repeated reforms by Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou and Emperor Wen of Sui, the main source of militia troops consisted of wealthy self-cultivating peasants and small landowners—the very backbone of the Sui dynasty's tax and labor base.

After ascending the throne, Yang Guang continuously increased the number of Eagle-Soaring Mansions while diluting the authority and status of the Eagle-Soaring Generals, all to force local forces to submit to central command.

However, when chaos engulfed the realm and the imperial court lost control over the provinces, most of the Eagle-Soaring Mansions colluded with local aristocrats and rebelled anyway.

The troops deployed by the Sui were all Sui militia troops. First fell the central militia, followed by waves of newly conscripted recruits. Later, during the three Goguryeo campaigns, desertion among the militia became rampant; to protect himself, Yang Guang assembled a recruited force—the Xiaoguo Army—which took over the duty of guarding the Emperor from the Twelve Guards.

Yang Guang had shattered the Great Sui's military into pieces, allowing the prominent families to seize the opportunity to recruit stray soldiers and re-establish the private armed forces that Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou and Emperor Wen of Sui had painstakingly dismantled.

The collapse of the central army inevitably led to the rise of regional warlords—this was fundamental common sense. Yang Guang was practically feeding prime meat straight to the local elite.

The fortified manors erected across the land at the end of the Sui were the first step in the rise of regional warlords. It was only because the Great Tang was founded just as regional forces were raising their heads that these warlord factions were nipped in the bud.

Right now, Lady Dou's profound anxiety stemmed from watching chaos loom on the horizon as powerful clans sought once more to expand their private forces.

After a soft sigh, Li Xuanba comforted her, "Mother, please trust Second Brother. They won't be able to stir up trouble."

Lady Dou pinched Li Xuanba's cheek.

Li Xuanba cupped his face in surprise, at a loss as to why his mother had suddenly pinched him.

Lady Dou smiled. "I trust him, and I trust you. I also trust Qijian, as well as that future general of a daughter you spoke of."

Holding his cheek, Li Xuanba murmured, "Mm..." For some reason, he felt a touch embarrassed.

Speaking of Third Sister and Third Brother-in-law, Lady Dou let out a sigh.

When Li Shimin and Li Xuanba returned to Daxing, Third Sister and Third Brother-in-law had not been home, so the twin brothers simply left their gifts and departed.

Hearing his mother mention it now, Li Xuanba learned that Third Brother-in-law's mother was in failing health. Thus, Third Sister and Third Brother-in-law had taken the family back to their ancestral village so the elderly matriarch could peacefully spend the final leg of her life beside her recently deceased husband's grave.

In his past life, when reading about Princess Pingyang Zhao's life, Li Xuanba had often wondered why—given her good relationship with her husband Chai Shao—historical research suggested their eldest son was only born after Li Yuan raised his troops.

Princess Pingyang Zhao's tragic death was very likely caused by giving birth to two children back-to-back, which, combined with her relatively advanced age for childbirth in that era, led to fatal postpartum complications.

Now he surmised that although Third Sister and Third Brother-in-law had married early, by the time they reached the age to consummate the marriage, Third Brother-in-law's parents passed away one after the other. Not only was their time together severely restricted, but Third Sister's health might have also suffered greatly during the period of filial mourning. Ironically, it was after the uprising began that Third Sister's health improved, allowing her to conceive later on.

However, the underlying damage to her health remained, and back-to-back pregnancies ultimately ruined her physical constitution.

Fortunately, Zhu-niang had discovered Third Sister's latent physical weakness in advance. If he also reminded Third Brother-in-law to practice contraception after their first son was born, Third Sister's future in this life would surely change.

Lady Dou noticed Li Xuanba's distraction and asked, "Are you worried about San-niang? Is something bad going to happen to her in the future?"

Li Xuanba snapped back to reality and said, "I'm just worried that Third Sister hasn't given birth yet. As she gets older, frequent pregnancies could severely harm her health."

Lady Dou burst out laughing. "Oh, you! You've paid attention to these women's matters ever since you were little. How strange of you."

Li Xuanba: "..."

Lady Dou smiled warmth. "Still, Mother is very happy that you care so much about me and San-niang."

She pulled Li Xuanba into her arms, ruffling his hair just as she had when he was a child. "Rest assured, Mother will instruct San-niang thoroughly. She's destined to be a princess in the future; she doesn't need to obsess over heirs, and Chai Shao won't dare mistreat her."

Li Xuanba said, "With Second Brother and me around, none of our elder sisters will ever be bullied."

Lady Dou stroked Li Xuanba's head again. "That's right."

Remembering how Li Xuanba had managed to notice her physical discomfort during her monthly periods when he was just a small child, and how he now worried about San-niang's childbearing struggles, a complex mix of emotions filled her heart.

Lady Dou knew men were not supposed to meddle in or even know of such women's affairs, but seeing Li Xuanba care so deeply brought her immense joy.

Lady Dou kept Li Xuanba back and doted on him for a long time. By the time he returned to his rooms, he looked as though all his vitality had been drained by his mother, collapsing face-down on the table without moving.

Li Shimin poked Li Xuanba's disheveled topknot. "What's wrong?"

Li Xuanba murmured weakly, "Mother still treats me like a toddler..."

Li Shimin chuckled. "Even when you're seventy or eighty years old, you'll still be Mother's little child."

Li Xuanba grumbled, "I need to find a way to divert Mother's attention."

And so, Li Xuanba gifted the idle Hangou and Wudi to his mother.

Sure enough, Lady Dou's attention was captured by these two "eagle grandchildren," and she stopped dragging Li Xuanba over for physical affection.

Wings folded, Hangou and Wudi waddled along behind Lady Dou during her strolls, becoming quite a sight within the Duke of Tang's estate.

Li Yuan had originally lusted after the clever golden eagles, but seeing them reduced to grounded yard-chickens, he lost all interest.

He still preferred mighty, ferocious golden eagles that could hunt.

Another half-month passed, and guests gradually arrived as the auspicious day for Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's weddings drew near.

Li Yuan consulted with his in-laws, suggesting that since Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were twin brothers, they might as well marry and perform the wedding bows on the exact same day, making for a heartwarming story.

The in-laws thought this was a charming idea and readily agreed.

As for the fortune-tellers reading the horoscopes, they were sensible enough to know how to give the clients the exact answer they wanted.

Thus, after counting on his fingers, the diviner declared that twin brothers marrying together was divinely ordained—a grand stroke of good fortune!

When news spread across Taiyuan, the common folk readied their new clothes as if preparing for the New Year, eager to join in the festivities.

Hearing that the famous twin sons of the Duke of Tang were marrying on the same day sounded exceedingly auspicious—even rarer and more intriguing than ushering in a sacred Buddhist statue.

The common people of that era were not much different from modern netizens forwarding images of koi fish for good luck—whenever something auspicious occurred, everyone wanted a piece of the good fortune.

After all, it didn't cost a dime. Who knows, they might even snag a few copper coins thrown as wedding favors!

Li Yuan had not originally intended to throw a grand celebration, so he hadn't invited many guests.

But as the wedding date approached, circumstances forced his hand.

Perhaps because Li Shimin and Li Xuanba possessed such formidable reputations, uninvited guests began arriving in droves.

For instance, the prominent clans of Hedong and Shandong—the very groups that gave him the biggest headaches—sent representatives one after another. Aside from the Xue family of Xue Daoheng and Xue Shou, who already shared close ties with Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, the Five Great Clans of Shandong also sent congratulations. Even the Cui clan, held as the proudest and foremost noble family under Heaven, arrived with polite deference as guests, showing far more courtesy than they ever had when Yang Su sought a marriage alliance with them years ago.

Even Li Yuan was thoroughly shocked.

The representative from the Cui clan smiled and said, "Li Er-lang and Li San-lang are rare talents under Heaven. It is a pity we did not have the chance to make their acquaintance earlier. Now that they celebrate such a joyous occasion, how could we fail to come and offer our congratulations?"

Upon returning home, Li Yuan beat his chest and stomped his feet before Lady Dou. "If only we had betrothed Er-lang and San-lang a bit later, perhaps we could have formed a marriage alliance with the Cui clan!"

The Cui clan of Qinghe!

Lady Dou put on a stern face and warned, "Husband, you must never speak such words. If word gets out, what would Er-lang and San-lang's in-laws think? Furthermore, our family already has a daughter-in-law from the Zheng clan of Xingyang; we must not take in another bride from the noble clans of Shandong."

Li Yuan said sheepishly, "I know, I was just saying..."

*That was the Cui clan of Qinghe! The very same Cui clan that Yang Su had shamelessly begged for a marriage proposal, only to be mocked and looked down upon by them!*

Lady Dou was left speechless.

*What of the Cui clan of Qinghe? Do they possess half the talent of my two sons? They're nothing more than parasites relying on inherited ancestral prestige.*

She tossed her husband aside and went back to bustling about for her sons' weddings.

Long before Li Shimin and Li Xuanba returned to the Central Plains, Lady Dou had already commenced preparations.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were quite idle prior to the wedding, but Lady Dou was rushed off her feet.

With guest numbers swelling and their statuses far from ordinary, many pre-planned wedding proceedings had to be altered on short notice, leaving Lady Dou thoroughly exhausted.

Yet, she was overjoyed.

Could there be anything more delightful than seeing one's children accomplish great things?

After sighing and groaning for a while, Li Yuan cast those thoughts aside as well, busying himself with receiving the guests.

He thought with a bitter smile: *It was supposed to be me bringing connections to my sons, so why does it feel like my two sons are bringing connections to me? Having sons who are too outstanding really puts a lot of pressure on a father.*

Pressure aside, Li Yuan was just as thrilled as Lady Dou about his sons' achievements.

However, when envoys from both the Eastern and Western Tujue arrived to offer congratulations, Li Yuan was no longer pleased—he was utterly terrified.

Li Yuan hauled Li Shimin and Li Xuanba before him. "How on earth are you two in contact with the Eastern Tujue as well?"

Li Shimin scratched his head. "We're not."

Li Xuanba said, "If there's any connection, it's that we're currently preparing to ally with the Western Tujue to strike the Eastern Tujue."

Li Yuan was puzzled. "Then why did the Khagan of the Eastern Tujue send envoys here?"

Li Shimin suggested, "Father, you're tasked with guarding against the Eastern Tujue. Perhaps the Eastern Tujue Khagan sent them out of respect for your dignity?"

Li Xuanba agreed, "Perhaps Second Brother is right."

Li Yuan scratched his head. *Is that really true? Why do I feel so unconfident? Ah well, let me just take it as true.*

Li Yuan hurriedly pulled Zhangsun Sheng along to entertain the Tujue envoys together, terrified that something might go wrong.

"His Majesty is still personally leading the expedition against Goguryeo; we cannot allow His Majesty to misunderstand us!" Li Yuan wiped cold sweat from his brow.

Zhangsun Sheng laughed. "The Tujue envoys have merely come for a cup of wedding wine; you're overthinking it. His Majesty won't mind. We'll simply report this to His Majesty, explaining that the Tujue wished to show goodwill to the Great Sui, using Li Er-lang and Li San-lang's weddings as an opportunity to ask you to forward gifts to His Majesty. Wouldn't that solve it?" *If he does mind, even better—it'll drive Li Yuan to rebellion all the sooner.*

Li Yuan smiled relievedly. "You truly are brilliant. We'll do just that."

Li Yuan dispatched a memorial filled with trembling deference and received an approving reply from Yang Guang. But just as he breathed a sigh of relief, an unexpected visitor brought his heart right back up into his throat.

Crown Prince Yang Jian, who had fallen out of favor with the Emperor, arrived in person to attend Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's wedding, carrying an imperial edict from the Emperor offering congratulations to the twin brothers.

Li Yuan knew that the friction between the Emperor and the Crown Prince was worsening by the day, to the point where the Emperor had even uttered paranoid nonsense about whether Yang Xuangan's rebellion had been coordinated with the Crown Prince from within. With the Crown Prince attending his sons' wedding, wouldn't the Emperor suspect him of being in cahoots with the Crown Prince?

Although Yang Jian had been stripped of almost all his power by the Emperor, he was still the Crown Prince. No matter how anxious Li Yuan was, he could only put on a look of overwhelmed honor and respectfully receive this heavyweight guest.

The common people of Taiyuan City were unaware of the rift between the Emperor and the Crown Prince. Seeing that the Duke of Tang's Second and Third Young Masters were important enough to warrant the Crown Prince's personal attendance at their wedding, they held their heads high, beaming with shared pride.

Citing that he "didn't want to cause trouble," Yang Jian stayed directly in the Duke of Tang's estate. At night, just as he had back in Luoyang, Yang Jian scaled the wall into Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's quarters.

Carrying a wine jar, he laughed, "The Duke of Tang doesn't welcome me, but what about you two?"

Li Shimin said testily, "If you hadn't come, A-Xuan and I would've been furious."

Li Xuanba nodded. "Tonight, we drink until we drop!"

Yang Jian and Li Shimin traded a glance, shoved Li Xuanba to the side to drink water, and began competing against each other in drinking wine.

Yang Jian said, "You pass out after three cups! What drinking are you talking about?"

Li Shimin added, "Give it a rest. If you get drunk, how are you going to chat with Second Cousin? Go, go, shoo!"

Li Xuanba: "..."

He had genuinely wanted to drink to his heart's content with Second Cousin tonight. Hadn't Second Cousin constantly complained in the past that he never drank with him and wasn't as close to him as Second Brother was? Why was he being spurned now?

chunks.chapterTitle: 第124章 成亲与满天星河
chunks.chineseText:
第124章 成亲与满天星河

隋时成亲遵循古礼， “六礼为聘”。
　　“六礼”即为“纳采”求婚、“问名”问姓名八字、“纳吉”合八字定吉凶、“纳征”送聘礼、“请期”定婚期、“亲迎”成亲。
　　李世民和李玄霸两个甩手新郎官，前面五个步骤都是双方父母定了，他们只需要等到迎亲那一日。
　　杨暕对李世民和李玄霸笑道：“我本来准备陪同你们一同去迎亲， 给你们帮衬帮衬。谁知道你俩居然同时迎亲？”
　　李世民指李玄霸， 李玄霸指李世民， 兄弟二人异口同声道：“二表兄去帮他。”
　　杨暕捧腹大笑：“了解你们的人知道你们是想让对方好，不了解的还以为你们嫌弃我这个太子呢。”
　　李世民打趣道：“怎么就不能是我真的嫌弃你长得太英俊，抢了我这个新郎的风头。”
　　李玄霸打量了二表兄虽然消瘦颓废但美貌不减的脸， 认真点头：“二哥说得对。”
　　杨暕笑得更厉害，眼泪都笑出来了。
　　他伸出两只手拍着两位表弟的肩膀：“好吧，为了不让你们二人风头被抢， 我就在唐国公府等你们。”
　　李玄霸犹豫了一瞬，道：“要不……要不二表兄来帮我吧。如果丈人家要考我射箭什么的， 我肯定需要外援。”
　　李世民道：“说得对， 二表兄去帮阿玄。”
　　杨暕微笑。
　　他知道李世民和李玄霸的心意。两人这样说，是对他表示不在乎皇帝对他的冷落和忌惮。
　　这两个表弟，在自己与皇位无缘的时候与自己很亲近，在自己权势如日中天时故意疏远，当自己即将滑入深渊时却又毫不忌讳地仍旧与自己交好。
　　他这一世， 在兄弟缘分上肯定是超出常人远矣。
　　“我在唐国公府等你们。”杨暕难得一次对两位表弟露出身为兄长的成熟表情，“东西突厥都派人来参加你们的婚礼， 没有我镇场子，我怕父皇会疑心。”
　　那皇帝就不会对你起更多的疑心吗？还是已经无所谓了？
　　李世民和李玄霸兄弟二人对视一眼，将疑问藏在心中， 接受了杨暕的好意。
　　见到杨暕时， 两人本来劝说杨暕不要冲动。杨广好脸面， 他已经有了杀兄弟的名声， 只要杨暕一直忍耐，他只会磋磨杨暕，不会在杨暕没有过错的时候背负杀子之名。
　　但杨暕只是笑而不语。
　　两人便不再多劝。
　　临到天下大变之时，杨暕无论是自保还是为了保住大隋，奋力一搏或许都是唯一能做的事。
　　李玄霸心中很不是滋味。
　　他的二表兄不是历史中那个连死的时候都稀里糊涂的漂亮花瓶。
　　二表兄有名师教导，有贤才陪伴，已经是一个很优秀的大隋太子，在民间和朝中声望已经不输已故的长兄。
　　所以这样的人，他的心志也一定很坚定。
　　虽然与杨暕交好可能会在杨广那里留下不好的印象，影响他们二人的计划，但不提李世民，就是心思深沉如李玄霸，也不是纯粹以利益处事的人。
　　杨暕对他们好，他们便对杨暕好。
　　少年时若不识得“情和义”，岂不白白当一次少年郎。
　　李世民和李玄霸顶着父母长辈担忧的神情，顶着其他宾客探究的眼神，与太子杨暕谈笑风生，然后骑上骏马，各自迎亲而去。
　　李世民上马前还在笑话长孙无忌：“二表兄，有空来张掖，我请你喝羊奶酒。长孙四郎来了太原，没等到我和他妹妹成亲又匆匆回去，气得都快哭了。我们到时一起好好嘲笑他。”
　　李玄霸无语：“你娶长孙四郎的妹妹，居然还嘲笑他？世上怎么会有你这样的人？”
　　李世民和杨暕皆大笑，李玄霸苦笑摇头。
　　杨暕站在原地，目送李世民和李玄霸离去。
　　待看不到两人背影后，杨暕才对李渊道：“唐国公，不用担心，这是我最后一次叨扰。”
　　李渊背后冷汗都冒出来了，忙道：“太子何出此言？以后也请太子多多照顾臣的两位犬子。”
　　杨暕微笑，他与李渊一起进府等候李世民、李玄霸回来，老弱的护卫与他同行。
　　宾客们纷纷在心中叹息。
　　堂堂太子，此次出行的护卫竟然皆是老弱之人，只有一位年轻文吏看着像个真正的太子属官。
　　庾俭佩着长剑跟在杨暕身后，任由周围人打量，目不斜视，坚定不移地跟随在太子杨暕身侧。
　　……
　　唐国公府的两位公子成亲，仪仗吹吹打打穿城而过，分成两路迎接新娘。
　　宗罗睺和罗士信已经回来。罗士信的父母仍旧不想离开家乡。见老人倔强，罗士信只能留下钱财和地图，让他们见势不妙就躲进郡城。
　　回来后，宗罗睺陪同李世民迎亲，罗士信被李智云拉着一同帮李玄霸迎亲。
　　李建成留在唐国公府帮李渊招呼宾客，李元吉则在李世民的迎亲队伍里。
　　杨暕的到来转移了一点李玄霸心中对新婚的紧张。当骑马走在迎亲的路上时，李玄霸终于又紧张起来。
　　乐声嘈杂，人声鼎沸。
　　路旁老百姓都在翘首踮脚看着这长长的迎亲队伍拍手欢笑。
　　李玄霸却像是与这个世界隔了一层什么，声音和景象在他的视野中都变得模糊。
　　这一路上好像很长，长得他把与宇文珠相识相遇的点点滴滴都回忆了一遍不说，还又回忆了一遍前世的家庭。
　　他已经很久没有再想过、梦过前世的事，仿佛已经完全变成了大唐的李三郎君。
　　现在想起前世的家人，李玄霸恍若隔世……嗯，是已经隔了一世了。
　　这一路又好像很短。
　　李玄霸还在神思恍惚中，李智云就大喊道：“停停停，三兄！到了！”
　　李玄霸回过神，竟已经到了宇文家在太原新置办的宅院门前。
　　老师和丈人面容慈祥地看着自己，对自己微笑。
　　李玄霸昏呼呼地下马，昏呼呼地被人簇拥着上前，仿佛木偶般一板一眼地按照迎亲流程，一步一步走到了后院。
　　他念了催妆诗，又给了催妆钱。
　　宇文珠以团扇掩面，在母亲的搀扶下走出门。
　　“三兄，你怎么又发呆了？”李智云无奈道，“你高兴傻了吗？”
　　李智云的声音超大，引得周围人纷纷大笑。
　　宇文弼笑着摇摇头。自己这弟子平时都很机灵，见到了珠儿就喜欢发呆犯傻。
　　不过这对珠儿来说是好事啊。
　　李玄霸从宇文珠过分盛装的打扮中回过神，结结巴巴地继续背着要说的词。
　　宇文珠弯腰一笑，扇子差点没遮住脸。
　　她对李玄霸伸出手：“好了，别傻了。”
　　宇文珠的声音响起时，蒙在李玄霸心头那层雾突然散去。
　　无论是周围人还是周围的声音都重新入了眼入了耳，不真实的梦境变成了触手可及的现实。
　　李玄霸的神思清明，对宇文珠伸出手。
　　李智云在背后怪叫：“牵什么手！三兄快上！把三嫂背上马车！”
　　李智云一怪叫，陪同李玄霸来迎亲的李氏宗族子弟和宇文家的子弟都纷纷起哄。
　　李玄霸蹲下来：“来。”
　　宇文珠哭笑不得：“你和他们胡闹什么？”
　　李玄霸转头笑道：“没办法，我抱不动你，只能背了。”
　　宇文珠气恼道：“你这是嘲笑我重？”
　　李玄霸眨巴着眼睛道：“是我自认很弱，你知道的，我连强弓都拉不开。”
　　宇文珠一愣，被李玄霸逗得笑得花枝乱颤。
　　她在母亲无奈的摇头下趴在了李玄霸背上，一只手勾着李玄霸的脖子，一只手继续握着遮住脸的团扇。
　　李玄霸虽然拉不开强弓，但也是个正常力气的少年人，背一位体态匀称的同龄女子没有问题。
　　他稳稳将宇文珠背起来，朝着门外走去。
　　宇文珠的体温透过两人厚重的华服传递到李玄霸背上。
　　五月炎热，李玄霸和宇文珠的汗珠混在了一起，让两人的脸颊更加绯红。
　　宇文珠凑在李玄霸耳边小声道：“你回太原后为何不来见我？我好想你。”
　　李玄霸耳根绯红，道：“我和二哥试图翻墙来找你和嫂嫂，都被丈人揍了。”
　　宇文珠愕然：“有这事？”
　　李玄霸道：“丈人没告诉你？”
　　宇文珠咬牙切齿：“没有。”
　　李玄霸道：“我们还打算用寒钩和乌镝送信，宇文老师说要效仿长孙老师来个一箭双雕。丈人倒是说可以，但他也被宇文老师揍了。”
　　宇文珠失笑：“我记得有一日父亲嘴角乌青，难道是那一日被祖父揍了？”
　　李玄霸道：“可能是吧。”
　　宇文珠道：“以前祖父恨不得我与你多见面，现在怎么能这样？连寒钩和乌镝都不能来送信，让我平白忐忑。”
　　李玄霸道：“就是。”
　　宇文弼：“咳咳。”
　　李玄霸和宇文珠立刻闭嘴。
　　他们二人心虚地往侧后方瞟了一眼宇文弼。老师祖父什么时候到身边了？
　　宇文弼无奈：“定下婚期后，婚前不可见面，这是常识！”
　　李玄霸和宇文珠缩了缩脑袋。
　　宇文弼：“……”怎么刚成亲，这两人就如此有默契了？
　　他心里酸酸的。
　　自己最疼爱的孙女还是嫁出去了。
　　看着孙女上了婚车，宇文弼转头想向儿子诉苦。
　　而嫁女儿的儿子正在傻笑，看着十分高兴的模样。
　　宇文弼：“……”
　　他手痒了。谁家嫁女儿还笑着啊！
　　宇文弼深呼一口气，暗自憋闷。
　　他的老妻见状，差点笑出声来。
　　回程的时候，李玄霸心中的紧张就少了许多。
　　两方仪仗相互通报了时间，两对新人正好同时到达唐国公府。
　　李世民先在马背上对李玄霸拱手一笑，李玄霸也回以拱手一笑，以示相互庆贺。
　　然后两人同时下马，扶新娘下马车。
　　宇文珠稳稳走下马车，长孙小妹却是轻快地跳下来。
　　长孙晟见状不由扶额，担心自己是不是把女儿宠得太过了。
　　李玄霸“谶纬”中的长孙皇后肯定没有女儿这么活泼。
　　两对小夫妻一同进门，一同拜堂。
　　李渊和窦夫人都笑得合不拢嘴。
　　不过拜堂之后，闹婚房等步骤就要省去了。
　　两对小夫妻都是先成婚，几年后才圆房。所以李世民和李玄霸念了却扇诗后，就回到前堂招呼宾客。
　　长孙小妹和宇文珠自己卸了盛装，换上了常服，也去女眷那里欢乐，不必干坐着等在新房中。
　　李世民和李玄霸成婚后各自拥有一个独立的小院子。
　　窦夫人特意把两人的小院子凑成隔壁，能随时串门。
　　此外他们虽然不常住在太原，也各有一个比邻的大宅子。
　　之后长孙小妹和宇文珠的嫁妆会放在大宅子里。那里才算得上她们的小家。
　　李世民拉着神思不定的李玄霸喝酒：“虽然你酒量浅，但今日的酒还是需要喝一点。对了，你知道吗？我丈人给观音婢取名了，名为‘康宁’，长孙康宁，名字很吉利对吧！”
　　李玄霸无语：“我怎么可能知道长孙老师给嫂子取的名字？嫂子的名字请不要拿出来到处说！”
　　李世民道：“我又没有到处说，只是和你炫耀观音婢的名字很好听，很吉利！丈人取名的本事真厉害，你看，‘安业’‘恒安’‘行布’‘无忌’‘康宁’，全是祝福的话！”
　　李玄霸不知道这样的取名算什么厉害，但二哥说什么就是什么吧。
　　虽然不知道原本历史中长孙皇后有没有名字，但长孙老师知道嫂子可能会早早病逝后，给嫂子取名为“康宁”，倒是很合适。
　　李世民把着李玄霸的肩膀，酒气喷在李玄霸脸上，嘀嘀咕咕不断说自己迎亲时看到新娘时心情有多激动。
　　总而言之，我的新娘真好看！
　　李玄霸道：“我也很激动。”
　　李世民摇头：“你真的有激动吗？不是傻了吗？小五说你傻掉了，还被宇文老师嫌弃。”
　　李玄霸把满身酒气的二哥推开，满场寻找李智云。
　　李世民又倒在杨暕身上大笑：“二表兄，你看我弟弟是不是很傻？阿玄真好玩！”
　　杨暕扶着李世民道：“你少喝点吧。虽然不需要圆房，但你等会儿不和你新婚夫人聊一聊？”
　　李世民挤眉弄眼得意道：“我又不是阿玄，我喝再多酒，洗个澡就清醒了。”
　　杨暕道：“但你满身酒气，就不怕新娘嫌弃？”
　　李世民神情更加得意：“无论我如何，观音婢都不会嫌弃我，永远不会。”
　　杨暕见李世民这模样，心中有点羡慕。
　　他眼珠子一转，恶从心生：“真的？我不信，来试试。来，继续喝！”
　　杨暕拉着其他勋贵子弟一起给李世民灌酒，要把李世民灌趴下。
　　李玄霸借口寻找李智云逃离了酒宴，早早洗澡换衣，回到小院安静地等待宇文珠回来。
　　事有凑巧，李玄霸刚把头发晾干，宇文珠就回来了。
　　两人在挂着灯笼的小院撞见，都有些拘束。
　　仆从侍女悄悄退去，留两人独自相处。
　　李玄霸悄悄深吸一口气，起身道：“可吃饱了？”
　　宇文珠点头：“饱了。她们在拼酒，我不爱喝酒，就先逃了。”
　　李玄霸摸了摸鼻子：“我也是。”
　　宇文珠忍俊不禁：“看来我们家以后不需要有酒……啊，不行，观音婢爱喝葡萄酒，得给她备一些。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“对，要给二哥二嫂备酒。原来二嫂也爱喝酒。”
　　宇文珠叹气：“何止爱喝？酒量可大了。我常劝她节制，注意身体。她老说自己身体壮得像一头小牛犊。哪有女子说自己身体壮得像小牛犊？”
　　李玄霸和宇文珠打趣了二哥二嫂之后，都忍不住笑出声，用相同的话题打消了独处的害羞。
　　李玄霸牵着宇文珠的手进屋，帮宇文珠整理她即将住的房间。
　　虽然唐国公府已经准备好了一切，但卧室还是自己整理一番，才睡得更舒服。
　　宇文珠从箱子里拿出一个草药袋给李玄霸。这是她给李玄霸绣的新锦囊，但装的草药太多，变成了一个大袋子。
　　李玄霸非常喜欢，正好用来当睡觉的枕头。
　　两人点起蜡烛，将坐墩搬到了门口，说起各自的事。
　　李玄霸炫耀自己与西突厥可汗唇枪舌剑，那得意洋洋的表情，仿佛二哥附体。
　　宇文珠说起自己与孙医师一同行医，在孙医师的医书上留下了自己的见解。
　　“你在信中说，药物最好先经过动物实验。虽然感觉有些残忍，但比起直接用在人身上，确实只能这样了。”宇文珠开玩笑道，“听闻你很会做饭，看来杀鸡杀鸭的事可以交给我了。”
　　李玄霸也开玩笑道：“那好，顺带可以在处理鸡鸭前，给它们喂会让它们肉质更鲜美的草药。”
　　宇文珠横眉道：“我是医师，不是厨子。”
　　李玄霸笑道：“药膳不分家，都一样。”
　　宇文珠拧了李玄霸的胳膊一下，然后也跟着笑了。
　　两人笑着笑着就靠在了一起，好像五月的夜晚也很凉，需要依偎着取暖似的。
　　宇文珠抬头看着天空：“今天只是月牙，但星空好明亮。”
　　李玄霸问道：“要不要去屋顶看星星？”
　　宇文珠犹豫了一会儿，点头：“好！”
　　在新婚之夜爬上屋顶看星星听着很离经叛道，但她的夫君不是个循规蹈矩的人，她也不用约束自己。
　　小两口命令仆人搬来梯子，他们小心翼翼爬上了屋顶。
　　仆人还送上来毯子，让他们盖在瓦当上，可以躺着看星星。
　　“珠娘，你知道张衡吗？不是陛下赐死的那个大臣，是汉朝的张衡。”
　　“我知道。我知道他说‘浑天如鸡子，天体圆如弹丸，地如鸡子中黄，孤居于天内’。听着好神奇啊。”
　　“这是真的。我们脚下的大地是球形，天上的星星也是球形。我们围绕着太阳转动，月亮围绕我们转动。”
　　“要怎么证明呢？”
　　“我之后想想办法给你证明。”
　　“嘻嘻，好。那天上的星星也都是星球吗？”
　　“大部分都是。有些是气态行星。我们将天空划分成不同星座，外国也一样。你看那个，他们叫天琴座。”
　　“那不是织女牛郎星吗？”
　　“对，天琴座的故事也和爱情有关。”
　　李玄霸看着星空口若悬河。
　　他前世就喜欢看星星。那时城市灯火还不彻夜通明，就是在城市里都能看到璀璨的银河。
　　当夜深人静时，他独自一人找一处昏暗的地方，抬头看着星星，想象星座中的那些故事。好像这样，他就仿佛不孤单了。
　　他有皓月群星做伴，并不孤寂。
　　投胎转世后，星座的知识用不上，就算要看星星辨别方位，华夏自有自己古老的星相学知识体系。
　　李玄霸很多年没有谈过星空。现在开口，他发现这些故事都烙印在他的灵魂中，可以滔滔不绝说很久。
　　仿佛在很久之前，他就等着与人分享星空故事那一刻似的。
　　宇文珠躺在屋顶，星月银河倒映在她的眼眸中。
　　她身下是狭窄的后院，眼前是浩瀚的星空。
　　宇文珠曾经一个人看过星星，数过星星，朗诵过关于星星和月亮的诗歌。
　　她读过很多书，但从未看过李玄霸口中那些关于星星的神话故事，也没有从哪本书上看到过太阳系、银河系的词语。
　　她不知道李玄霸为何会知道这么多奇怪的故事，但她不会打听这些故事的来历，也不会质疑李玄霸口中的故事。
　　宇文珠相信那些都是真的。
　　有着奇怪故事的西方文明是真的，会相互吸引互相环绕的星球也是真的。
　　世界就是这么大，宇宙就是这么大。
　　“我不知道望远镜的原理是什么，但可以试试。一年、两年、十年，总有一天，我可以带你看到月球真正的模样。你就会相信我了。”
　　“我现在就相信你，但月球我也要看。一言为定。”
　　宇文珠侧头，眼中的星空倒影变成了李玄霸的倒影。
　　李玄霸也侧头看向宇文珠，他笑得就像是一个寻常意气风发开朗少年郎。
　　“一言为定。”
　　两人相视而笑，又继续仰面看着浩瀚的星空，美丽的弦月，璀璨的银河。
　　有流星从夜空中划过。
　　李玄霸道：“听说看到流星在心中默默许愿会实现。”
　　宇文珠遗憾道：“可惜错过……啊，又是一颗！”
　　李玄霸和宇文珠惊讶地睁圆眼睛。
　　在少年少女的眼眸中，一颗一颗的星星在夜幕中划过，仿佛星落成雨。
　　李玄霸和宇文珠不知何时双手紧握，眼睛一眨不眨看着天空，一直到最后一颗流星消失。
　　“三郎，你许的什么愿望？”
　　“嗯……不能说，说了就不灵了。”
　　“那我也不说。”
　　少年少女继续躺在夜空下，继续讨论着星星的故事。
　　小院外，笑闹声仍旧喧嚣。
