Chapter 124: The Wedding and a Sky Full of Stars

Marriages during the Sui Dynasty followed ancient customs, governed by the "Six Rites of Betrothal."

The "Six Rites" consisted of *Nacai* (proposing), *Wenming* (asking for names and birth dates for divination), *Naji* (determining auspiciousness), *Nazheng* (presenting betrothal gifts), *Qingqi* (setting the wedding date), and *Qinying* (welcoming the bride).

As hands-off grooms, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had their parents settle the first five steps; all they needed to do was wait for the day of the procession to fetch their brides.

Yang Jian smiled at Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. "I originally planned to join your procession and lend you a hand. Who knew the two of you would be fetching your brides at the exact same time?"

Li Shimin pointed at Li Xuanba, and Li Xuanba pointed at Li Shimin. The two brothers spoke in unison: "Second Cousin, go help him!"

Yang Jian doubled over with laughter. "Those who know you would say you're looking out for each other, but those who don't might think you're looking down on me, the Crown Prince!"

Li Shimin bantered back, "Why couldn't it be that I truly dislike how handsome you are, afraid you'll steal my thunder as the groom?"

Li Xuanba studied his second cousin's face—though gaunt and dispirited, its striking beauty remained undiminished—and nodded earnestly. "Second Brother is right."

Yang Jian laughed even harder, tears welling in his eyes.

He reached out both hands and clapped them on his two cousins' shoulders. "Alright, then. So I don't steal your thunder, I'll wait for you at the Duke of Tang's estate."

Li Xuanba hesitated for a moment before saying, "Or... maybe Second Cousin should help me. If my father-in-law tests me on archery or something, I'll definitely need reinforcement."

Li Shimin agreed, "That's true! Second Cousin, go help Ah Xuan."

Yang Jian smiled faintly.

He understood Li Shimin and Li Xuanba's intentions. By speaking this way, they were showing him that they did not care about the Emperor's coldness and suspicion toward him.

These two cousins had been close to him when he was far from the throne, deliberately kept their distance when his power was at its zenith, and now, as he hovered on the brink of an abyss, they befriended him openly without the slightest reservation.

In this life, his fortune with brotherhood far surpassed that of ordinary men.

"I will wait for you at the Duke of Tang's estate." For once, Yang Jian displayed a mature, elder-brotherly expression toward them. "Both the Eastern and Western Turks have sent envoys to attend your wedding. If I don't stay behind to keep order, I fear Royal Father will become suspicious."

*Won't the Emperor suspect you even more? Or does it simply no longer matter?*

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba exchanged a glance, swallowing their doubts, and accepted Yang Jian's goodwill.

When they first met Yang Jian, the brothers had tried to persuade him not to act impulsively. Yang Guang was obsessed with his public image; having already earned a reputation for fratricide, as long as Yang Jian endured, the Emperor would only torment him, not bear the infamy of filicide without cause.

But Yang Jian had only smiled without a word.

So they pressed no further.

As the world stood on the precipice of grand upheaval, whether for self-preservation or to safeguard the Great Sui, giving it his all might be the only thing left for Yang Jian to do.

Li Xuanba felt a bitter pang in his heart.

His second cousin was not the foolish, pretty vase of history who had met an utterly confused end.

Guided by renowned mentors and accompanied by virtuous talents, Second Cousin had already grown into an exceptional Crown Prince of the Great Sui, his prestige among the populace and court no less than that of his late elder brother.

Thus, a man like him possessed a mind of unwavering resolve.

Though staying close to Yang Jian might leave a bad impression on Yang Guang and undermine their plans, neither Li Shimin nor the deep-thinking Li Xuanba were people who acted solely out of cold self-interest.

If Yang Jian was good to them, they would be good to him.

If one failed to understand sentiment and loyalty in their youth, would they not have spent their youth in vain?

Under the worried gazes of their elders and the prying eyes of the guests, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba chatted and laughed naturally with Crown Prince Yang Jian. Then, mounting their fine steeds, each rode off to fetch his bride.

Before mounting, Li Shimin was still teasing Zhangsun Wuji: "Second Cousin, when you have time, come to Zhangye and I'll treat you to sheep's milk wine! Fourth Brother Zhangsun came to Taiyuan, but had to rush back before waiting for me to marry his sister—he was almost crying with rage! We must mock him properly when the time comes."

Li Xuanba was speechless. "You're marrying Fourth Brother Zhangsun's sister, and you're still making fun of him? How can someone like you exist in this world?"

Both Li Shimin and Yang Jian burst out laughing, while Li Xuanba shook his head with a bitter smile.

Yang Jian stood where he was, watching Li Shimin and Li Xuanba depart.

Once their silhouettes faded from sight, Yang Jian turned to Li Yuan and said, "Duke of Tang, do not worry. This is the last time I shall disturb you."

Cold sweat broke out on Li Yuan's back. He hurriedly said, "Why does Your Highness say such a thing? I pray Your Highness will continue to look after my two young sons in the future."

Yang Jian merely smiled. Accompanied by his feeble guards, he entered the estate alongside Li Yuan to await the return of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

The guests all sighed inwardly.

The dignified Crown Prince was accompanied on this journey by guards who were all elderly or frail; only one young scribe appeared like a true official of the Crown Prince's household.

Yu Jian walked behind Yang Jian with a long sword at his hip, unbothered by the scrutinizing gazes around him, his eyes fixed ahead as he faithfully stayed by the Crown Prince's side.

……

The wedding of the two young masters of the Duke of Tang's estate was announced by festive music and guards of honor marching through the city before splitting into two routes to retrieve the brides.

Zong Luohou and Luo Shixin had returned. Luo Shixin's parents still refused to leave their hometown; seeing their stubbornness, Luo Shixin could only leave money and maps, instructing them to hide in the commandery seat if trouble arose.

Upon returning, Zong Luohou accompanied Li Shimin's procession, while Luo Shixin was dragged along by Li Zhiyun to assist Li Xuanba.

Li Jiancheng stayed at the Duke of Tang's estate to help Li Yuan entertain the guests, while Li Yuanji joined Li Shimin's bridal procession.

Yang Jian's arrival had temporarily distracted Li Xuanba from his wedding jitters, but riding along the path to fetch his bride, the nervousness rushed back once more.

The music blared, and the crowd bustled with excitement.

Townsfolk lining the streets stood on tiptoe, watching the long procession with applause and laughter.

Yet Li Xuanba felt as though a barrier separated him from the world; the sounds and sights turned hazy in his perception.

The journey felt endlessly long—so long that he reminisced over every detail of his acquaintance with Yuwen Zhu, and even recalled his family from his past life.

He hadn't thought or dreamed of his previous life in a very long time, feeling as if he had completely transformed into Third Young Master Li of the Tang.

Thinking of his past family now felt like a lifetime ago... well, it *was* literally a lifetime ago.

Yet the journey also felt fleetingly short.

While Li Xuanba was still lost in thought, Li Zhiyun shouted, "Halt, halt, halt! Third Brother, we're here!"

Li Xuanba snapped back to reality to find himself already standing before the gates of the Yuwen family's newly acquired residence in Taiyuan.

His master and father-in-law looked at him with kindly faces, smiling.

Lightheaded, Li Xuanba dismounted, was ushered forward by the crowd, and moved step by step into the inner courtyard like a wooden puppet, strictly adhering to the wedding procedure.

He recited the poem for makeup-rushing and handed over the makeup-rushing money.

Yuwen Zhu emerged from the room, her face veiled behind a round fan, supported by her mother.

"Third Brother, why are you daydreaming again?" Li Zhiyun said helplessly. "Are you foolish with joy?"

Li Zhiyun's loud voice prompted laughter from everyone around.

Yuwen Bi shook his head with a laugh. His disciple was usually so sharp, yet he always spaced out whenever he saw Zhu'er.

*Still, for Zhu'er, that is a wonderful thing.*

Li Xuanba snapped out of his daze upon seeing Yuwen Zhu's radiant, ornate attire, stuttering through his memorized lines.

Yuwen Zhu bent slightly in amusement, her fan nearly slipping away from her face.

She reached out a hand to Li Xuanba. "Alright, stop being silly."

The moment Yuwen Zhu's voice sounded, the fog enveloping Li Xuanba's mind dissipated.

The surrounding people and voices re-entered his eyes and ears; the surreal dream transformed into tangible reality.

With clarity restored, Li Xuanba extended his hand to Yuwen Zhu.

Li Zhiyun hollered from behind, "What holding hands? Third Brother, move! Carry Third Sister-in-law on your back to the carriage!"

At Li Zhiyun's hooting, the Li kinsmen and Yuwen family youths joining the procession broke into boisterous cheers.

Li Xuanba squatted down. "Come on."

Yuwen Zhu was caught between tears and laughter. "Why are you fooling around with them?"

Li Xuanba turned his head and grinned. "Can't be helped. I can't lift you in my arms, so I can only carry you on my back."

Yuwen Zhu huffed, "Are you teasing me for being heavy?"

Li Xuanba blinked innocently. "I'm admitting I'm weak. You know I can't even draw a heavy bow."

Yuwen Zhu paused, then burst into chuckles at his reply, trembling like blossoms in the breeze.

As her mother shook her head helplessly, she leaned onto Li Xuanba's back, wrapping one arm around his neck while holding the round fan over her face with the other.

Though Li Xuanba couldn't draw a heavy bow, he was still a young man of normal strength; carrying a well-proportioned girl his age posed no problem.

He lifted Yuwen Zhu steadily and walked toward the gate.

Her warmth seeped through their heavy ceremonial attire onto his back.

In the hot May air, beads of sweat mingled between them, flushing their cheeks a deeper crimson.

Yuwen Zhu leaned close to Li Xuanba's ear and whispered, "Why didn't you come to see me after returning to Taiyuan? I missed you so much."

Li Xuanba's ears turned red as he replied, "Second Brother and I tried to scale the wall to find you and Sister-in-law, but Father-in-law beat us up."

Yuwen Zhu was astonished. "That happened?"

Li Xuanba said, "Father-in-law didn't tell you?"

Yuwen Zhu gritted her teeth. "No."

Li Xuanba continued, "We also planned to send letters using Han Gou and Wu Di, but Master Yuwen said he would imitate Master Zhangsun and shoot down two birds with one arrow. Father-in-law thought it was fine, but Master Yuwen beat him up too."

Yuwen Zhu giggled. "I remember Father had a bruised jaw one day. Was that when Grandfather beat him?"

Li Xuanba said, "Probably."

Yuwen Zhu complained, "Grandfather used to be so eager for us to meet. How could he do this now? Not even letting Han Gou and Wu Di deliver letters, leaving me anxious for no reason."

Li Xuanba agreed, "Exactly."

Yuwen Bi cleared his throat: "Ahem."

Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu immediately shut their mouths.

The two guiltily glanced back at Yuwen Bi. *When did Master-Grandfather get so close?*

Yuwen Bi sighed helplessly. "Once the wedding date is set, the bride and groom must not meet before the wedding. That is common sense!"

Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu ducked their heads simultaneously.

Yuwen Bi: "..." *How do these two already have such tacit understanding when they just got married?*

A wave of sorrow brushed through his heart. His beloved granddaughter was truly marrying off.

Watching her step into the bridal carriage, Yuwen Bi turned to vent his feelings to his son.

Only to find his son, who was giving away his daughter, grinning foolishly with an immensely delighted expression.

Yuwen Bi: "..."

His fists twitched. *Who smiles like that when giving away their daughter!*

Yuwen Bi took a deep breath, suppressing his exasperation.

Seeing this, his wife nearly burst out laughing.

On the return journey, Li Xuanba felt much less nervous.

The two guards of honor communicated their timing, allowing both pairs of newlyweds to arrive at the Duke of Tang's estate at the exact same moment.

Li Shimin cupped his hands and smiled at Li Xuanba from horseback, and Li Xuanba returned the smile and gesture in mutual celebration.

Then both dismounted simultaneously to assist their brides out of the carriages.

Yuwen Zhu stepped down gracefully, whereas Little Sister Zhangsun leaped down with brisk agility.

Seeing this, Zhangsun Sheng couldn't help facepalming, worrying if he had spoiled his daughter too much.

The Empress Zhangsun of Li Xuanba's "prophecies" certainly hadn't been this lively.

The two young couples entered together and performed the ceremonial bows together.

Li Yuan and Lady Dou grinned from ear to ear.

However, after the ceremony, teasing the bridal chamber was skipped.

Since both couples were marrying young and would consummate their marriages years later, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba simply recited the poems for removing the fans before returning to the front hall to entertain guests.

Little Sister Zhangsun and Yuwen Zhu removed their heavy wedding finery, changed into everyday clothes, and joined the female guests in festivities, freed from waiting idly in the bridal chambers.

After marriage, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba each had an independent courtyard.

Lady Dou had intentionally arranged their courtyards side-by-side so they could visit each other anytime.

Furthermore, although they didn't often reside in Taiyuan, each possessed a large, neighboring mansion.

Later, the dowries of Little Sister Zhangsun and Yuwen Zhu would be placed in those mansions, which were their true private homes.

Li Shimin dragged the distracted Li Xuanba over to drink. "Even though your liquor tolerance is low, you must drink a little today! By the way, do you know? My father-in-law named Guanyinbei! Her name is 'Kangning'—Zhangsun Kangning. A very auspicious name, right?"

Li Xuanba was speechlessly annoyed. "How could I possibly know what name Master Zhangsun gave Sister-in-law? Please don't go around boasting about Sister-in-law's name!"

Li Shimin defended, "I'm not going around telling everyone! I'm just showing off to you that Guanyinbei's name sounds so nice and auspicious! Father-in-law is truly amazing at naming. Look: 'Anye', 'Hengan', 'Xingbu', 'Wuji', 'Kangning'—all of them are blessings!"

Li Xuanba didn't see what was so amazing about that naming style, but whatever Second Brother said went.

Though he didn't know if Empress Zhangsun had a recorded name in original history, given that Master Zhangsun knew she might die young, naming her "Kangning" (Health and Peace) was indeed very fitting.

Li Shimin slung an arm around Li Xuanba's shoulder, exhaling alcohol-laden breath onto his face while rambling endlessly about how thrilled he felt upon seeing his bride during the procession.

In short: *My bride is so beautiful!*

Li Xuanba said, "I was very excited too."

Li Shimin shook his head. "Were you really? Weren't you just stunned silly? Fifth Brother said you went dumb and got disdained by Master Yuwen."

Li Xuanba pushed his drunk brother away and scanned the hall for Li Zhiyun.

Li Shimin flopped onto Yang Jian, laughing boisterously. "Second Cousin, look at my brother! Isn't he silly? Ah Xuan is so much fun!"

Yang Jian supported Li Shimin, saying, "Drink less. Even if consummation isn't needed tonight, aren't you going to talk with your new bride later?"

Li Shimin winked cockily. "I'm not like Ah Xuan. No matter how much I drink, a bath will clear my head right up."

Yang Jian teased, "Reeking of alcohol like this, aren't you afraid your bride will find you repulsive?"

Li Shimin's expression grew even prouder. "No matter what I do, Guanyinbei will never dislike me. Never."

Seeing Li Shimin like this, Yang Jian felt a pang of envy.

Rolling his eyes, mischief surged in his mind. "Really? I don't believe it. Let's test it out. Come, keep drinking!"

Yang Jian gathered other noble youths to pour wine for Li Shimin, intent on drinking him under the table.

Li Xuanba used finding Li Zhiyun as an excuse to escape the banquet. After bathing early and changing clothes, he returned to his courtyard, waiting quietly for Yuwen Zhu.

As luck would have it, just as Li Xuanba dried his hair, Yuwen Zhu returned.

Meeting in the courtyard hung with lanterns, both felt a bit shy.

Servants quietly withdrew, leaving the two alone.

Li Xuanba took a stealthy deep breath, stood up, and asked, "Did you eat enough?"

Yuwen Zhu nodded. "I'm full. The ladies were drinking heavily, and since I don't care for wine, I snuck away first."

Li Xuanba rubbed his nose. "Me too."

Yuwen Zhu couldn't help laughing. "Looks like our household won't need wine in the future... Ah, wait, no. Guanyinbei loves grape wine, so we must keep some stocked for her."

Li Xuanba sighed, "Right, we need to prepare wine for Second Brother and Second Sister-in-law. I didn't know Second Sister-in-law liked to drink too."

Yuwen Zhu sighed as well, "More than just liked it—her tolerance is huge! I often urge her to drink in moderation and take care of her health, but she always says she's as strong as a calf. What young woman describes herself as strong as a calf?"

Teasing Second Brother and Second Sister-in-law, both broke into laughter, dispelling the bashfulness of being alone.

Li Xuanba held Yuwen Zhu's hand as they went indoors, helping her arrange the room where she would sleep.

Although the estate had arranged everything, arranging the bedroom oneself made it feel cozier.

Yuwen Zhu took an herbal sachet from her trunk and handed it to Li Xuanba. It was a new pouch she had embroidered for him, but because it contained so many medicinal herbs, it had turned into a large pouch.

Li Xuanba loved it; it was perfect to use as a pillow.

Lighting candles, they moved stools to the doorway and chatted about their experiences.

Li Xuanba boasted about his verbal spar with the Western Turkic Khan, his proud expression making him look as if he were possessed by Second Brother.

Yuwen Zhu spoke of practicing medicine alongside Physician Sun and writing her own insights into Physician Sun's medical texts.

"You mentioned in your letter that drugs are best tested on animals first. Though it feels a bit cruel, compared to testing directly on humans, it is indeed the only way," Yuwen Zhu joked. "I hear you're a great cook. Looks like slaughtering chickens and ducks can be left to me."

Li Xuanba joked back, "Great! While we're at it, before slaughtering them, we can feed them herbs that make their meat taste even better."

Yuwen Zhu raised her brows indignantly. "I'm a physician, not a chef!"

Li Xuanba chuckled, "Medicinal food shares the same root; it's all the same."

Yuwen Zhu pinched Li Xuanba's arm, then dissolved into laughter with him.

As they laughed, they leaned against each other, as if the May night was chilly enough to require snuggling for warmth.

Yuwen Zhu looked up at the sky. "It's only a crescent moon tonight, but the stars are so bright."

Li Xuanba asked, "Do you want to go up to the roof and watch the stars?"

Yuwen Zhu hesitated a moment, then nodded. "Okay!"

Climbing onto the roof to watch stars on one's wedding night sounded scandalous, but her husband was no stickler for convention, nor did she need to constrain herself.

The young couple had servants bring a ladder and carefully climbed onto the roof.

The servants brought up blankets to lay over the roof tiles so they could lie down to gaze at the stars.

"Zhu'niang, do you know Zhang Heng? Not the minister executed by His Majesty, but Zhang Heng of the Han Dynasty."

"I know him. I know he said, 'The heavens are like a hen's egg, the celestial sphere round as a crossbow pellet, and the earth like the yolk inside the egg, dwelling solitary within.' It sounds so wondrous."

"It's true. The earth under our feet is a sphere, and the stars in the sky are spheres too. We revolve around the sun, and the moon revolves around us."

"How can that be proven?"

"I'll figure out a way to prove it to you later."

"Hee-hee, alright. Are the stars in the sky all heavenly spheres as well?"

"Most of them are. Some are gas giants. We divide the sky into different constellations, and so do foreign lands. Look at that one—they call it Lyra."

"Isn't that the Weaver Girl and Cowherd stars?"

"Yes, the myth behind Lyra is also a story of love."

Li Xuanba spoke fluently as he gazed up at the night sky.

He had loved stargazing in his past life. Back then, city lights didn't burn bright all night long, and one could see the brilliant Milky Way even within the city.

In the quiet of the night, he would find a dark spot alone, look up at the stars, and imagine the stories behind the constellations. It felt as though doing so kept him from feeling lonely.

With the bright moon and stars for company, he was not isolated.

After reincarnation, western astronomical knowledge had little practical use; even if he needed to read the stars for navigation, China possessed its own ancient astrological tradition.

Li Xuanba had not spoken of the starry sky for many years. Now, opening up, he found these stories indelibly branded onto his soul, flowing effortlessly for hours.

It was as if, long ago, he had been waiting for this very moment to share these stories of the stars with someone.

Lying on the roof, Yuwen Zhu reflected the stars, the moon, and the Milky Way within her eyes.

Beneath her was a narrow courtyard; before her was the vast universe.

Yuwen Zhu had once watched stars alone, counted stars alone, and recited poems of the stars and moon.

She had read many books, yet she had never encountered the star myths Li Xuanba spoke of, nor had she seen terms like "Solar System" or "Milky Way Galaxy" in any text.

She did not know why Li Xuanba knew so many strange tales, but she would not pry into their origin, nor would she doubt his words.

Yuwen Zhu believed it was all true.

The Western civilization with its strange tales was real, and the celestial spheres attracting and orbiting one another were real.

The world was indeed this vast, and the universe truly this grand.

"I don't know the principle behind telescopes yet, but we can try. One year, two years, ten years—someday, I'll show you what the moon truly looks like. Then you'll believe me."

"I believe you right now, but I still want to see the moon. It's a deal."

Yuwen Zhu turned her head, the reflection of stars in her eyes replaced by the reflection of Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba turned to look at her as well, smiling like an ordinary, spirited, cheerful youth.

"It's a deal."

The two looked at each other and laughed, then turned back to gaze up at the boundless sky, the lovely crescent moon, and the brilliant Milky Way.

A shooting star streaked across the night sky.

Li Xuanba said, "I heard that if you silently make a wish upon a shooting star, it will come true."

Yuwen Zhu said regretfully, "Pity I missed it... Ah, another one!"

Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu widened their eyes in astonishment.

In the eyes of the young youth and maiden, star after star sliced across the dark canopy, like a rain of falling stars.

Without realizing it, Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu held hands tightly, their eyes unblinking as they watched the sky until the very last meteor vanished.

"Sanlang, what wish did you make?"

"Mm... I can't tell you. If I say it out loud, it won't come true."

"Then I won't tell you mine either."

The young couple continued lying under the night sky, chatting endlessly about stories of the stars.

Outside the quiet courtyard, the merry noise and laughter of the feast still buzzed softly.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第125章 宇文珠委婉劝说
chunks.chineseText:
第125章 宇文珠委婉劝说

小两口的温馨看星星新婚夜， 结束于隔壁小院的醉鬼嚎叫。
　　醉醺醺的李世民和醉醺醺的长孙康宁回到自己的新婚小院，不知道交流了什么，两人在院子里燃起了篝火， 围着篝火嗷嗷嗷欢快地跳舞嚎叫。
　　李玄霸和宇文珠默默坐起身， 盯着隔壁院子里的跳舞醉鬼看。
　　李世民先跳起了突厥的舞蹈， 又跳起了吐谷浑的舞蹈，再跳起了回纥的舞蹈，最后舞蹈混杂在了一起， 还融入了大唐，啊不，大隋的舞蹈， 突出个群魔乱舞。
　　李玄霸真的很震惊二哥的舞蹈天赋。
　　二哥若在现代，不仅穿着上可能是非主流精神小伙， 还是一个随时就能在街头来一段哟哟哟舞蹈的非主流精神小伙。
　　李玄霸扶额， 深呼吸。
　　宇文珠拉着李玄霸的衣袖，笑着指着能隔壁小院道：“之前我和你说观音婢过分活泼，你还不信。你看看她，这是不是过分活泼？”
　　李玄霸这才将视线从舞姿过分魔性的二哥身上收回，转移到因为个头太小， 有点不起眼的嫂子身上。
　　长孙康宁挽起了袖子，将两截手腕露了出来， 挥拳踢腿，居然舞的是一套看上去颇有实战作用的“养生拳法”。
　　打着打着拳，长孙康宁似乎是被旁边一个人舞出了群魔乱舞效果的李世民感染， 也舞了起来。
　　她舞的是不知道从哪学的胡旋舞。那个圈圈转的， 把李玄霸的眼睛都转晕了。
　　李玄霸捂住额头：“一个二哥就够头疼了， 再来个二嫂……还好， 现在有你帮我承担一半。”
　　宇文珠忍俊不禁：“我才不要！”
　　李玄霸严肃道：“我能按住我哥，难道还能去教训嫂子？这责任只能由珠娘来承担了。”
　　宇文珠笑得花枝乱颤：“现在下去按住他们吗？”
　　李玄霸叹气：“当然。我担心这两个醉鬼扑到火堆里去。”
　　宇文珠道：“我让人熬醒酒药，等会儿给他们灌下去。”
　　李玄霸担忧道：“你真的能按得住二嫂？我叫母亲……哎，新婚之夜，叫母亲处理这事，会不会对二嫂声誉不好？”
　　宇文珠笑道：“给观音婢这个醉鬼灌醒酒药，我已经很熟练了。”
　　李玄霸肃然起敬。
　　小两口从屋顶爬下，去按住隔壁两醉鬼。
　　李世民和长孙康宁不仅不肯消停，还要拉着李玄霸和宇文珠一起。
　　李玄霸和宇文珠一边叫人熬醒酒药，一边苦口婆心劝他们远离火堆。
　　当仆从端来醒酒药的时候，李玄霸和宇文珠已经一人抱着琵琶，一人抱着琴，给两个醉鬼伴奏了。
　　堵不如疏，想强行按住两个醉鬼是不可能的，只能顺从他们，把他们的舞蹈改得温和一点，跳舞场地离篝火远一点，让他们把精力发泄干净了，才能灌下醒酒药，强迫他们去睡觉。
　　显然，李玄霸和宇文珠对此都十分熟练了。
　　仆从将汤药放在石桌上凉着。
　　李玄霸和宇文珠合奏，李世民拉着长孙康宁开心地跳着没有章法的圈圈舞。
　　窦夫人知道李世民和长孙康宁都喝得有点多，安抚好彻夜欢庆的宾客后，匆匆来照顾儿子儿媳。
　　看到篝火旁的两对小夫妻后，她停下脚步，伸手挥了挥，让身边的仆从安静，悄悄地离开了小院。
　　半路上，她遇见了正在单独聊天的李渊和杨暕。
　　李渊担忧道：“大雄喝了很多酒，醒酒药喝下去了吗？”
　　杨暕忍笑道：“他晕了吗？”
　　窦夫人无奈地笑道：“太子殿下，郎君，你们知道今日二郎新婚，还给他灌酒？”
　　李渊干咳了一声。杨暕笑着连声说“抱歉”。
　　窦夫人笑道：“二郎小夫妻俩在跳舞，三郎小夫妻俩在奏乐，他们玩得正开心。”
　　杨暕惊讶：“这都没醉？”
　　李渊得意地捋了捋胡须：“不愧是我儿子。”
　　窦夫人道：“我看二郎小夫妻俩肯定都醉了，只是醉了还在玩。”
　　杨暕失笑：“不愧是他。”
　　李渊无奈：“不愧是我儿子。”
　　窦夫人道：“三郎和珠娘已经备好了醒酒药了，他们会照顾二郎和观音婢。不用担心。”
　　李渊摇头叹气：“明明大德身体更弱，现在怎么似乎大德照顾大雄的时间更多？”
　　杨暕道：“幼时二郎十分照顾三郎，恨不得每日把三郎背在背上。现在轮到三郎照顾二郎，这大概是佛教所说的轮回吧。”
　　李渊无语：“轮回不是这个意思。”
　　窦夫人道：“二郎三郎开心便好。”
　　杨暕点头赞同。
　　虽然他很想去看看醉了的李世民的舞蹈，但今天李世民和李玄霸新婚，他还是别去打扰两对小两口的新婚夜了。
　　杨暕向李渊告辞，回自己居住的小院休息。
　　杨暕离开后，李渊脸上的笑容淡去，忧愁涌上眉头。
　　窦夫人问道：“太子可是吩咐了郎君棘手的事？”
　　李渊摇头：“他什么都没吩咐，只是与我聊了一点过去的事……过去元德太子还在时的事。”
　　窦夫人叹息道：“只是拉家常吗……”
　　李渊道：“是啊。夫人，我见他这模样，有点难过。”
　　杨暕与李渊叙旧的时候，李渊也想起了曾经那个行事无所顾忌，直爽到有点愚蠢的齐王殿下。
　　哪有皇子天天大大咧咧嚷着“夺嫡”？真正要夺嫡的皇子都会把心思藏得紧紧的。齐王殿下那副做派真是让人看着直摇头。
　　怪不得陛下和太子每每提到齐王殿下都是苦笑摇头，满脸宠溺。
　　李渊当时想，齐王殿下不知道是真的傻还是误打误撞，他的行为处事让皇帝和太子都很放心。
　　谁也不知道太子会突然病逝，而那个鲁莽愚蠢的齐王殿下会成长成一位让人赞不绝口的好太子。
　　一位行事与先太子完全不同，锋芒毕露的大隋太子。
　　李渊道：“我知道天下无不忌惮壮年太子的老年皇帝。但陛下只有这一位成年皇子，他逼废了毫无过错的太子，可想过大隋的将来？”
　　窦夫人道：“内贼未定，陛下却又要亲征高丽，此时他也没想过未来。”
　　李渊长叹一口气，道：“是啊。”
　　夫妻二人相对良久，然后互相搀扶着回前堂继续招呼宾客。
　　这群人真是太能喝了，难道真的要喝一整晚吗？
　　夫妻二人头疼不已。
　　……
　　第二日李世民起床，头疼欲裂。
　　“啊啊啊啊，我的脑袋……阿玄，快帮我揉揉。”李世民惨叫。
　　坐在李世民床头看书的李玄霸瞥了二哥一眼：“我有个方法治头疼。据说把头往墙上砸，就能有效治疗各种头疼。”
　　李世民抱着脑袋道：“只要晕过去就不会疼了是吧？啊啊啊啊，好疼啊。”
　　李玄霸冷哼了一声，放下书，没好气地把药端了过来：“喝药。”
　　李世民蔫哒哒地喝完苦药，抱着头继续嚷嚷：“啊啊啊啊，好苦……疼疼疼，我的脑袋啊……观音婢呢？她昨日也喝了许多酒，我要去看望她。”
　　李玄霸道：“珠娘在照顾二嫂。你这样子，还是别去了。”
　　李世民道：“我洗个澡换身衣服就去。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“都让你别去了。二嫂现在与你还不熟悉，很注重形象。她不会愿意你看到醉酒后颓废的一面。”
　　李世民坚持道：“那我更该去了。我们是夫妻，哪一面不能见？”
　　李玄霸道：“以后慢慢见，现在给二嫂一点面子。你也是，喝醉了自己去发酒疯，拉着二嫂跳什么舞？”
　　李世民咧嘴笑道：“因为开心啊。”
　　李世民即使喝醉了也不会断片，哪怕喝晕了也能把半梦半醒间发生的事记得很清楚。所以昨夜他和新婚妻子围着篝火跳舞的事，他都记得。
　　李玄霸道：“那你记住现在的开心吧，将来别辜负她。”
　　李世民疑惑：“你把你哥我当做什么人了？我怎么会辜负观音婢？”
　　李玄霸切换心音：【你将来会当皇帝，二嫂将来会当皇后，你们不仅是夫妻，也是君臣，相处模式肯定会发生变化。我现在只是提醒你一句。人的关系越亲近，越容易忽视亲近的人的感受，直到失去了才追悔莫及当初对她还不够好。】
　　李玄霸说了一句仿佛废话的肺腑之言。
　　李世民沉默良久，道：“我记住了。”
　　李玄霸：【不过原本历史中的唐太宗就对长孙皇后很好，我二哥肯定比历史中那个唐太宗对二嫂更好。是我多嘴了。】
　　李世民笑道：“不，阿玄的劝告哥记在心中。以后你也要多多劝告。虽然听你说将来我的谏臣很多，但我的性格我自己知道，不是什么人的劝谏都能听进去。”
　　李玄霸点头：【没错。具体行为，等你再长大一点，心理承受能力再强一点，我再和你说你执政晚期的事。现在你还没有当皇帝，先让你开心一下。】
　　李世民抱着脑袋倒在床上：“不，你别说了，我头更疼了。哎哟，阿玄快滚，我不想看到你。我不想听那么远的事！”
　　李玄霸见李世民放弃了去寻找二嫂，笑着关门离开，去厨房看看青菜肉粥熬好没有。
　　早这样乖乖地养宿醉病不就行了？非逼自己用大招。
　　另一边卧室，长孙康宁用薄被子把自己裹成了一个蚕宝宝，蛄蛹蛄蛹滚来滚去。
　　宇文珠按住蚕宝宝，笑话道：“现在知道害羞了？谁让你昨天喝那么多酒？我劝了你你还不听，非说自己酒量特别好，喝不醉。”
　　长孙康宁带着鼻音黏糊糊道：“我不想让唐国公府的同族女眷看轻我。”
　　宇文珠无奈：“拒绝过量饮酒怎么会让她们看轻你？你怎么在莫名其妙的地方这么有胜负欲？好吧，现在畅快了？”
　　长孙康宁讨好地笑道：“还挺开心的。谢谢宇文阿姊照顾我。”
　　宇文珠道：“现在你是我嫂子。”
　　长孙康宁道：“二郎是三郎的兄长，你是我的阿姊，我们各论各。”
　　宇文珠刮了长孙康宁鼻头一下：“胡闹。快起来喝药了。”
　　长孙康宁蚕宝宝继续蛄蛹蛄蛹滚来滚去：“不要不要，我讨厌喝药。”
　　宇文珠冷笑：“别逼我给你灌下去。”
　　长孙康宁撒娇道：“阿姊才不会这么残忍。”
　　宇文珠道：“我会。”
　　长孙康宁噘着嘴松开被子保护层，乖乖爬起来喝药。
　　虽然不想喝药，长孙康宁喝药的速度却很快。她幼时体弱，早就练就了一身如何喝药最不难受的本事。
　　药刚喝完，宇文珠就递过来蜜水。
　　长孙康宁咕噜咕噜把蜜水一饮而尽，挂在了宇文珠身上：“好难喝。”
　　宇文珠道：“再睡一会儿，过一炷香再喝粥，然后泡个澡。”
　　长孙康宁摸着头发道：“宿醉后洗头会头疼吧？”
　　宇文珠道：“三郎弄了个手摇风扇，前面可以放火炭吹热风，能把头发较快吹干，就是有点热。不过宿醉后发些汗更好，我用过了，很舒服。”
　　长孙康宁问道：“二郎也在宿醉吗？”
　　宇文珠捂嘴笑道：“他比你惨多了，三郎让我给他开了治疗头疼的药。”
　　长孙康宁道：“那我要赶紧洗澡吹头发，打扮得美美的去照顾他。”
　　宇文珠点了一下长孙康宁的鼻头：“你照顾他做什么？乖乖躺着，别太殷勤。”
　　长孙康宁道：“可是我已经是他妻子，怎么能不……”
　　宇文珠捏住长孙康宁的嘴唇。
　　长孙康宁：“呜呜呜……”
　　宇文珠道：“我知道你贤惠，但不要在自己身体不适的时候去照顾别人，你自己才最重要。这不仅是我的担忧，也是三郎对你的劝告。”
　　长孙康宁摇晃着脑袋，挣脱了宇文珠的手，疑惑道：“为何三郎要说这话？”
　　宇文珠道：“你出嫁前，长孙将军应当和你说过三郎有奇异的本事。”
　　长孙康宁眼眸闪了闪，垂下头道：“谶纬。”
　　宇文珠道：“昨日哄你们这对醉鬼夫妻俩时，三郎对我叹息，他担心你过于贤惠，亏了自己的身体。你现在有父兄撑腰，即使将来当了皇后，也可以蛮横一些。不舒服就休息，不开心就发脾气，不乐意做的事就不要做。你要相信二郎比你想象中的更在乎你。”
　　长孙康宁结结巴巴道：“真、真是三郎说的？三郎怎么会说这种话？这种……”
　　宇文珠眉眼间露出无奈的神情：“是啊，他怎么还管着兄长后院事，和嫂子说这等胡话。不过此话他肯定是不会亲自对你说的，只有我帮他转达了。我会好好照顾你这个不省心的妹妹。”
　　说罢，宇文珠狠狠捏了一下长孙康宁的腮帮子。
　　长孙康宁捂脸：“哎哟，为什么掐我？”
　　宇文珠心里想，你的事让我昨夜哭了一场，我怎么不掐你？
　　宇文珠和长孙康宁成亲前，宇文弼和长孙晟都将之前隐瞒的一些需要她们知道的事告知了她们。
　　身为李世民和李玄霸的枕边人，管理后院只是小事。两人更重要的“角色”，当是李世民和李玄霸最信任的“同伴”。
　　之前李世民和李玄霸就和两位老师商议过，看是他们主动告知宇文珠和长孙康宁秘密，还是两位老师提前告知。
　　宇文弼和长孙晟当然提前告知，好教导宇文珠和长孙康宁。
　　昨夜终于把两个醉鬼丢去睡觉时，李玄霸对宇文珠吐露了长孙康宁原本的“未来”。
　　父亲早逝，自己和母亲、兄长被赶出家门，母亲郁郁而终，自己为了避祸早早嫁人……早年的颠沛流离虽然成为一代贤后长孙皇后坚韧品性的养料，但也让她变得过分谨小慎微。
　　无论是劝说兄长拒绝相位，还是在太宗病时说会殉情不做吕后，都显示出她过分谨慎的一面。
　　不拒绝过于频繁的生育也是。
　　女子生育本就是过鬼门关，年龄超过三十五岁之后死亡率更是飙升。贵族女眷在年长后往往会拒绝同房保命，皇后也有拒绝的权力，但长孙皇后没有用过。
　　女子的事，很多男人是不懂的。他们只会将过多生育当做是对妻子的爱。
　　“二哥在某些方面很迟钝，不亲口告诉他，他就不会知道。所以要相信他，多沟通。我可不希望二哥成为那个失去妻子后时常对着妻子陵墓哭泣的人。”
　　李玄霸的话让宇文珠吓了一跳。
　　她早知道李玄霸不是循规蹈矩的人，但一位男子居然说这些话，已经不是不循规蹈矩，而是离经叛道了。
　　但她很喜欢。
　　所以她不仅没有劝说李玄霸，还很愿意为李玄霸一起做这些离经叛道的事，改变小姐妹的命运。
　　还有比帮亲近的人改命更开心的事吗？
　　不过听到李世民和长孙康宁未来凄美的爱情故事，宇文珠还是大哭了一场，哭得形象全无，把李玄霸吓得如热锅上的蚂蚁。
　　宇文珠觉得这很丢脸，所以要狠狠欺负长孙康宁。
　　“别捏了……别挠了，虽然不知道我哪里得罪了阿姊，我错了，阿姊饶命！”
　　长孙康宁满床打滚，又躲进了被子里，只露出一个小脑袋。
　　宇文珠恶狠狠道：“记住，虽然你嫁人了，但你还是你，要以自己为重。你想想你父母兄弟，不要让他们难过。我们在家里千娇百宠地长大，嫁人不是来被人磋磨的。”
　　长孙康宁小心翼翼道：“唐国公府的家风极好，怎么会磋磨我们？”
　　宇文珠道：“我知道。如果不是唐国公府的家风好，我们父母也不会让我们嫁过来。他们都盼着我们好，但我们自己也要争气。”
　　长孙康宁点头：“知道了知道了。唉，其实我也不是很想去照顾他，我好困啊，好饿啊。可恶的二郎，为什么要拉着我跳舞！都是他的错！”
　　宇文珠嘴角抽搐。都是他的错？你啊你，我让你爱护自己，不是让你甩锅啊。
　　“是，都是他的错。所以你一定要好好休息。”宇文珠拍了拍鼓鼓的被子，“躺好，我给你按摩脑袋。免得你等会儿头疼。”
　　“好！”长孙康宁乖乖躺好，眯着眼睛道，“阿姊最好了。哎哟，轻点！”
　　在李玄霸和宇文珠的照顾下，李世民和长孙康宁休息了一日，第三日就满血复活。
　　李世民对李玄霸和宇文珠作长揖：“感谢弟弟弟妹救我一命。”
　　长孙康宁也装模作样长揖：“感谢叔郎姊姊救我一命。”
　　李世民扭头对长孙康宁道：“夫人，怎么还叫我弟妹姊姊？”
　　长孙康宁道：“我和阿姊这么亲近，才不要改称呼，各论各的！”
　　李世民道：“哦，好吧。”
　　长孙康宁嘴角荡漾起浅笑。果然如阿姊说的，李二郎很好，嫁人后也可以任性。
　　李玄霸扶额长叹：“我没救你们的命，但谁救我的命啊。救命，我还指望二嫂管着二哥，我不要加倍的二哥！”
　　长孙康宁叉腰：“叔郎，你怎么说话呢！我哪里不好了？”
　　她话音刚落，自己就笑出声来：“好啦好啦，前日是我得意忘形了，以后绝对不贪杯。二郎，你也不准贪杯。”
　　李世民正色：“我也是太高兴了，我以前从来不贪杯。”
　　李玄霸：“呵。”
　　李世民：【闭！】
　　李玄霸：【什么？】
　　李世民：【嘴！】
　　李玄霸：【啧。】
　　宇文珠拉了一下李玄霸的手，让他别在长孙康宁面前拆李世民的台。
　　兄弟二人私下怎么闹都行，但在嫂嫂面前，必须给嫂嫂脸面。
　　宇文珠转移话题道：“身体好了，我们一起去整理院子？”
　　李世民道：“弟妹现在就想搬出去吗？”
　　宇文珠叹息：“医术学习如逆水行舟，不进则退。我学医不仅要摆弄草药，还要……二兄应当知道，军中医师一手处理外创的本事该如何练习。”
　　李世民皱眉：“那确实……唉，父亲母亲想把我和阿玄留到过完年再回张掖，不然弟妹和我们一同回张掖才最自在。我能给你找很多尸体练手。”
　　“咳咳。”长孙康宁道，“委婉点。”
　　李世民道：“哦哦，张掖有许多病人练手。”
　　李玄霸忍不住吐槽：“已经离世的病人是吗？”
　　李世民道：“你就说弟妹需不需要吧！”
　　李玄霸抱拳：“需要，很需要，以后就拜托二哥了。”
　　李世民笑道：“交给我。”
　　长孙康宁叹气：“可是我和阿姊要留在太原……”
　　李世民打断道：“我说能带你们走就一定能带你们走，相信我和阿玄，对吧阿玄？”
　　李玄霸点头：“嗯。请放心。”
　　他和二哥怎么会把新婚妻子留在太原？
　　长孙康宁眨了眨眼，道：“其实就算你们把我和阿姊留下，我们也会偷偷乔装跟上，对吧阿姊？”
　　宇文珠：“咳咳。”
　　长孙康宁捂嘴：“啊，说漏嘴了，噗嘿。”
　　李世民笑道：“我们想到一块去了。”
　　小两口对着眨眼睛。
　　李玄霸把宇文珠拉走：“我们去收拾行李。”
　　宇文珠：“好。”
　　李世民和长孙康宁跟上：“哎，别走啊，一起一起。”
　　两对小夫妻结伴离开。墙角拐弯处，冒出一个小脑袋。
　　李智云幽怨道：“二兄三兄成亲后，身边没有我的位置了。呜呜呜，士信，我好难过。我也要成亲！”
　　罗士信背靠着墙壁，抱着手臂有气无力道：“嗯嗯嗯，好好好，去问问国公夫人什么时候给你寻一个？”
　　李智云道：“那多不好意思啊。对了，你还没定亲？啊，你都这么大了居然还没定亲，好逊。”
　　罗士信差点从墙上滑下去。
　　他恶狠狠道：“你找打是吧！天下未定，何以成家！我要先立业再成家！”
　　李智云做鬼脸：“借口。”
　　两人打了起来。
　　李世民听到动静，回头眺望：“小五和士信在干什么？”
　　李玄霸道：“不知道。看来他们很无聊，抓来帮我们搬东西。”

Chapter 125: Yuwen Zhu's Tactful Persuasion

The newlyweds' cozy star-gazing wedding night came to an end with drunken howls from the neighboring courtyard.

A thoroughly tipsy Li Shimin and an equally drunken Zhangsun Kangning had returned to their own wedding courtyard. No one knew what they had said to each other, but the two of them lit a bonfire in the middle of the yard, dancing and howling with merry wildness around the flames.

Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu sat up in silence, staring at the dancing drunks next door.

Li Shimin started off with a Turkic dance, switched to a Tuyuhun dance, transitioned into a Uyghur dance, and finally mashed them all together—even blending in dance moves from the Great Tang—ah, no, Great Sui—resulting in a glorious, wild frenzy of movement.

Li Xuanba was genuinely astonished by his second brother’s dancing talent.

If Second Brother were in modern times, he wouldn't just dress like an eccentric street youth—he’d be the kind of eccentric youth who could break into a street-side hip-hop routine out of nowhere at any moment.

Li Xuanba pressed his hand to his forehead and took a deep breath.

Yuwen Zhu pulled on Li Xuanba’s sleeve, pointing toward the neighboring courtyard with a giggle. "I told you before that Guanyinbei was overly lively, but you didn’t believe me. Look at her now—isn’t that overly lively?"

Only then did Li Xuanba tear his gaze away from his second brother’s ridiculously spellbinding dance moves and shift it to his sister-in-law, who was somewhat easy to miss due to her petite posture.

Zhangsun Kangning had rolled up her sleeves, exposing her pale wrists as she threw punches and kicked her legs—surprisingly executing a set of "health-preserving fist forms" that looked quite practical for combat.

As she punched away, she seemed infected by Li Shimin, who was dancing like a chaotic demon next to her, and began dancing as well.

She broke into a Sogdian whirl dance she must have learned somewhere. Spinning around in circle after circle, she made Li Xuanba's eyes dizzy just watching her.

Li Xuanba held his forehead. "One Second Brother is headache enough, and now we add Second Sister-in-law... Thank goodness you're here to share half the burden with me now."

Yuwen Zhu couldn't help laughing. "I refuse!"

Li Xuanba said gravely, "I can pin my brother down, but could I possibly lecture my sister-in-law? This responsibility can only fall on Zhuniang's shoulders."

Yuwen Zhu giggled so hard her shoulders shook. "Should we go down and hold them back now?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Of course. I’m worried those two drunks will tumble right into the bonfire."

Yuwen Zhu said, "I'll have someone brew some sobering soup to force down their throats later."

Li Xuanba asked worryingly, "Can you really hold Second Sister-in-law down? Should I call Mother... Ah, but calling Mother to deal with this on their wedding night—would that hurt Second Sister-in-law's reputation?"

Yuwen Zhu smiled. "Pouring sobering soup down drunk Guanyinbei's throat is something I'm already quite practiced at."

Li Xuanba felt a surge of deep respect.

The young couple climbed down from the roof to restrain the two drunks next door.

Not only did Li Shimin and Zhangsun Kangning refuse to settle down, but they also tried to drag Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu into the madness.

While Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu instructed servants to brew the sobering soup, they earnestly urged the drunk couple to stay away from the bonfire.

By the time the servants brought the sobering soup, Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu were already holding a pipa and a guqin respectively, providing musical accompaniment for the two drunks.

Dams were useless against floods; forcefully restraining two drunks was impossible. The best approach was to go along with them, steer their dancing into something gentler, move the dance floor farther from the bonfire, and let them exhaust their energy before pouring the sobering soup down their throats and forcing them to sleep.

Clearly, both Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu were highly experienced in this.

The servants set the bowls of herbal medicine on the stone table to cool.

As Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu played their duet, Li Shimin happily dragged Zhangsun Kangning along, spinning around in wildly haphazard circles.

Lady Dou knew that Li Shimin and Zhangsun Kangning had drunk quite a bit. After comforting the guests who were celebrating through the night, she hurried over to take care of her son and daughter-in-law.

Seeing the two young couples beside the bonfire, she halted, waved her hand to quiet her attending servants, and quietly slipped out of the courtyard.

On her way back, she ran into Li Yuan and Yang Jian chatting privately.

Li Yuan asked anxiously, "Daxiong drank a lot of alcohol. Has he taken the sobering soup yet?"

Yang Jian stifled a smile. "Did he pass out?"

Lady Dou chuckled helplessly. "Your Highness, Husband, you knew today was Erlang's wedding—yet you still forced so much drink on him?"

Li Yuan coughed dryly. Yang Jian laughed and offered repeated apologies.

Lady Dou smiled. "Erlang and his bride are dancing, while Sanlang and his wife are playing music. They’re having a wonderful time."

Yang Jian was surprised. "He's still not knocked out?"

Li Yuan stroked his beard proudly. "As expected of my son."

Lady Dou said, "I think Erlang and his wife are definitely drunk, but they're still playing around in their drunken state."

Yang Jian chuckled softly. "Classic Shimin."

Li Yuan said with helpless affection, "As expected of my son."

Lady Dou added, "Sanlang and Zhuniang have already prepared the sobering soup. They will take care of Erlang and Guanyinbei. There is no need to worry."

Li Yuan shook his head and sighed. "Dade is clearly the frail one, so how is it that Dade seems to spend more time taking care of Daxiong?"

Yang Jian said, "When they were children, Erlang doted on Sanlang endlessly, wishing he could carry Sanlang on his back every single day. Now it's Sanlang's turn to take care of Erlang. This is probably what the Buddhists call samsara—the wheel of karma."

Li Yuan was speechlessly amused. "That's not what reincarnation means."

Lady Dou said, "So long as Erlang and Sanlang are happy, that is all that matters."

Yang Jian nodded in agreement.

Although he really wanted to go see what drunk Li Shimin's dancing looked like, today was the wedding night of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, so he decided not to disturb the two young couples.

Yang Jian took his leave from Li Yuan and returned to his own courtyard to rest.

After Yang Jian left, the smile faded from Li Yuan's face, replaced by a heavy brow of worry.

Lady Dou asked, "Did the Crown Prince task you with something troublesome, Husband?"

Li Yuan shook his head. "He didn't task me with anything. He merely reminisced about the past... back when Crown Prince Yuande was still alive."

Lady Dou sighed softly. "Just making casual conversation..."

Li Yuan said, "Indeed. My lady, seeing him like this makes me feel a bit sorrowful."

As he reminisced with Yang Jian, Li Yuan also recalled the Prince of Qi of the past—a reckless man who acted without restraint, straightforward to the point of foolishness.

What imperial prince would go around loudly blustering about 'contending for the throne' every single day? Real contenders for the throne hid their ambitions deep within. The Prince of Qi's former antics had truly made observers shake their heads.

No wonder His Majesty and the late Crown Prince had always chuckled helplessly with fond indulgence whenever the Prince of Qi was mentioned.

Back then, Li Yuan had wondered if the Prince of Qi was truly foolish or just stumbled into good fortune, for his behavior put both the Emperor and the Crown Prince completely at ease.

No one could have foreseen that the late Crown Prince would suddenly fall ill and die, nor that the rash and foolish Prince of Qi would grow into an exemplary Crown Prince praised by all.

A Crown Prince of Sui whose style was entirely different from the late prince—sharp, formidable, and overflowing with brilliance.

Li Yuan whispered, "I know that under heaven, no aging emperor does not fear a Crown Prince in his prime. But His Majesty has only this one adult son left. If he forces the deposition of a completely blameless Crown Prince, has he thought of Great Sui's future?"

Lady Dou replied, "Internal rebels remain unsubdued, yet His Majesty insists on leading a personal campaign against Goguryeo. Even right now, he isn't thinking of the future."

Li Yuan let out a long sigh. "Indeed."

The husband and wife stood facing each other in silence for a long moment, then supported each other as they returned to the front hall to continue entertaining their guests.

This crowd was far too fond of drinking—were they really going to drink through the entire night?

The couple nursed a growing headache.

***

When Li Shimin woke up the next day, he had a splitting headache.

"Aaaah! My head... Ah Xuan, quick, rub my temples for me!" Li Shimin shrieked in agony.

Li Xuanba, who was sitting by Li Shimin's bedside reading a book, glanced at his second brother. "I have a method to cure headaches. They say smashing your head against a wall effectively cures all kinds of headache."

Li Shimin clutched his head. "As long as I pass out, it won't hurt anymore, right? Aaaah! It hurts so much!"

Li Xuanba snorted softly, put down his book, and brought the medicine over with an annoyed expression. "Drink your medicine."

Li Shimin dispiritedly downed the bitter decoction, clutching his head as he continued to wail, "Aaaah, so bitter... Ow ow ow, my head... Where is Guanyinbei? She drank a lot of wine yesterday too. I need to go see her."

Li Xuanba said, "Zhuniang is taking care of Second Sister-in-law. In your state, you'd better not go."

Li Shimin insisted, "I'll take a bath and change into clean clothes before going."

Li Xuanba sighed. "I told you not to go. Second Sister-in-law isn't familiar with you yet and cares a lot about her image. She won't want you to see her in a haggard, post-drunken state."

Li Shimin remained stubborn. "Then that's all the more reason for me to go! We're husband and wife—is there any side of her I shouldn't see?"

Li Xuanba said, "You can see it slowly in the future; save Second Sister-in-law some face for now. And you—getting drunk and throwing a drunken fit on your own was one thing, but why did you have to drag Second Sister-in-law into dancing with you?"

Li Shimin grinned widely. "Because I was happy!"

Even when drunk, Li Shimin never blacked out; even if he drank until he was dazed, he could remember events from that half-awake, half-dreaming state clearly. Thus, he remembered everything about dancing around the bonfire with his new bride last night.

Li Xuanba said, "Then remember this happiness, and do not let her down in the future."

Li Shimin looked bewildered. "What kind of person do you take your brother for? How could I ever let Guanyinbei down?"

Li Xuanba switched to heart-voice: *【You will become the Emperor in the future, and Second Sister-in-law will become the Empress. You won't just be husband and wife; you will also be ruler and subject, so your dynamic will inevitably change. I'm just giving you a reminder. The closer people are, the easier it is to overlook the feelings of those nearest to them, only to regret bitterly after losing them that they weren't good enough to them.】*

Li Xuanba uttered words that sounded like a cliché, yet came from the deep recesses of his heart.

Li Shimin remained silent for a long moment before saying, "I've taken it to heart."

Li Xuanba: *【Then again, Emperor Taizong of Tang in the original history treated Empress Zhangsun exceptionally well, and my Second Brother will definitely treat Second Sister-in-law even better than that historical Taizong did. I was just being overly talkative.】*

Li Shimin smiled. "No, your brother has taken Ah Xuan's advice to heart. You must continue to advise me often in the future. Although you mentioned I'll have many remonstrating ministers in the future, I know my own temperament best—I won't listen to just anyone's remonstrance."

Li Xuanba nodded: *【That's true. As for the specifics, once you're a bit older and mentally stronger, I'll tell you about your late reign. For now, since you aren't emperor yet, enjoy your happiness.】*

Li Shimin grabbed his head and collapsed back onto the bed. "No, stop talking, my head hurts even more now! Ouch, Ah Xuan, scram! I don't want to see you! I don't want to hear about things so far in the future!"

Seeing that Li Shimin had given up on looking for Second Sister-in-law, Li Xuanba smiled, closed the door, and went to the kitchen to check if the vegetable and meat porridge was ready.

Wouldn't it have been fine to just rest obediently and nurse his hangover from the start? He just had to force him to use his ultimate move.

***

In the bedroom on the other side, Zhangsun Kangning wrapped herself in a thin quilt like a silkworm cocoon, wriggling and rolling back and forth on the bed.

Yuwen Zhu pinned down the little silkworm cocoon and teased, "Now you know to feel embarrassed? Who told you to drink so much yesterday? I tried to stop you, but you wouldn't listen, insisting you had a high tolerance and couldn't get drunk."

Zhangsun Kangning said in a nasal, clingy voice, "I didn't want the female relatives of the Duke of Tang's estate to look down on me."

Yuwen Zhu said helplessly, "How could refusing excessive alcohol make them look down on you? Why are you so competitive over the strangest things? Fine, are you satisfied now?"

Zhangsun Kangning smiled coaxingly. "It was actually pretty fun. Thank you for taking care of me, Sister Yuwen."

Yuwen Zhu said, "You are my sister-in-law now."

Zhangsun Kangning said, "Erlang is Sanlang's elder brother, and you are my elder sister. We'll each address each other in our own way!"

Yuwen Zhu flicked Zhangsun Kangning's nose. "Nonsense. Hurry up and get up to drink your medicine."

The silkworm cocoon continued wriggling and rolling around. "No, no, I hate drinking medicine."

Yuwen Zhu sneered playfully, "Don't force me to pour it down your throat."

Zhangsun Kangning acted spoiled. "Sister wouldn't be so cruel."

Yuwen Zhu said, "I would."

Pouting, Zhangsun Kangning shed her protective quilt layer and obediently got up to drink the medicine.

Despite her reluctance, Zhangsun Kangning drank it very quickly. Weak and sickly in her youth, she had long mastered the trick of taking medicine with minimal discomfort.

The moment she finished the bowl, Yuwen Zhu handed over a cup of honey water.

Zhangsun Kangning gulped down the honey water in one breath, then threw herself over Yuwen Zhu, whining, "It tastes so terrible."

Yuwen Zhu said, "Sleep a bit more, have some porridge in an incense stick's time, and then take a bath."

Zhangsun Kangning touched her hair and asked, "Washing one's hair after a hangover causes headaches, doesn't it?"

Yuwen Zhu said, "Sanlang put together a hand-cranked fan with hot charcoal placed in front to blow warm air. It dries hair quite quickly, though it's a bit warm. But breaking a bit of sweat after a hangover is actually good for you. I've used it before; it's very comfortable."

Zhangsun Kangning asked, "Is Erlang nursing a hangover too?"

Yuwen Zhu covered her mouth and laughed. "He's far worse off than you. Sanlang had me prescribe a headache remedy for him."

Zhangsun Kangning said, "Then I must quickly bathe, dry my hair, dress up beautifully, and go take care of him!"

Yuwen Zhu tapped Zhangsun Kangning's nose. "Why should you take care of him? Lie down obediently and don't be overly attentive."

Zhangsun Kangning said, "But I am already his wife, how could I not..."

Yuwen Zhu pinched Zhangsun Kangning's lips together.

Zhangsun Kangning: "Mmm mmm mmm..."

Yuwen Zhu said, "I know you are virtuous, but do not push yourself to care for others when your own body is unwell. You yourself come first. This is not just my concern, but also Sanlang's advice to you."

Zhangsun Kangning shook her head to break free from Yuwen Zhu's hand, asking in confusion, "Why would Sanlang say such a thing?"

Yuwen Zhu said, "Before you married, General Zhangsun must have told you that Sanlang possesses extraordinary abilities."

Zhangsun Kangning's eyes flickered, and she lowered her head. "Prophetic foresight."

Yuwen Zhu said, "Yesterday, while trying to soothe you two drunk newlyweds, Sanlang sighed to me. He worried that you are overly virtuous and will harm your own health. You have your father and brother backing you now, so even if you become the Empress in the future, you can afford to be a bit willful. Rest if you feel unwell, vent if you are unhappy, and refuse to do things you don't wish to do. You must believe that Erlang cares about you far more than you imagine."

Zhangsun Kangning stammered, "D-did Sanlang really say that? How could Sanlang say such things? Words like..."

Yuwen Zhu showed a helpless expression between her brows. "Indeed, why is he poking his nose into his brother's rear inner court affairs and telling his sister-in-law such outrageous nonsense? But of course he wouldn't say this to you in person, so I can only pass it along for him. I will take good care of you, my troublesome little sister."

With that, Yuwen Zhu pinched Zhangsun Kangning's cheek hard.

Zhangsun Kangning clutched her cheek. "Ouch! Why did you pinch me?"

Yuwen Zhu thought to herself: *Hearing your story made me cry last night, so why wouldn't I pinch you?*

Before Yuwen Zhu and Zhangsun Kangning married, Yuwen Bi and Zhangsun Sheng had informed them of certain matters that had previously been hidden from them.

As the confidantes sharing the beds of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, managing the inner household was a mere trifle. Their far more critical "role" was to be the most trusted "companions" of Li Shimin and Li Xuanba.

Li Shimin and Li Xuanba had previously discussed with their two masters whether they should reveal the secrets to Yuwen Zhu and Zhangsun Kangning themselves, or let their masters inform them beforehand.

Yuwen Bi and Zhangsun Sheng naturally chose to inform them beforehand so they could properly instruct and guide Yuwen Zhu and Zhangsun Kangning.

Last night, when they finally hauled the two drunks off to bed, Li Xuanba had revealed to Yuwen Zhu the original "future" of Zhangsun Kangning.

Losing her father at a young age, being driven out of the house alongside her mother and brother, her mother dying in grief and depression, marrying young to escape calamity... Though the hardships of her early years nourished the resilient character of Empress Zhangsun, a famed virtuous empress of a generation, it had also rendered her overly cautious and self-effacing.

Whether it was persuading her brother to refuse the position of Prime Minister, or declaring during Taizong's illness that she would commit suicide to follow him into death rather than become a tyrannical regent like Empress Lu, all reflected her extreme caution.

Her inability to refuse overly frequent childbirth was another example.

Childbirth for women was akin to passing through the gates of hell, and the mortality rate spiked dramatically after thirty-five. Noblewomen often refrained from sexual relations in their later years to preserve their health and lives; as Empress, she had every right to refuse, yet Empress Zhangsun had never exercised it.

Many men simply did not understand women's matters. They merely regarded frequent childbearing as a testament of love for their wives.

"Second Brother is quite dense in certain respects; unless told directly, he won't realize it. So she must trust him and communicate more. I really don't want Second Brother to become a man who spends his later years weeping before his wife's tomb after losing her."

Li Xuanba's words had startled Yuwen Zhu.

She had long known that Li Xuanba did not stick to conventional norms, but for a man to voice such thoughts crossed beyond being non-traditional—it was downright rebellious.

Yet she liked it very much.

Thus, far from dissuading Li Xuanba, she was more than willing to join him in doing these rebellious things to alter her dear friend's destiny.

Was there anything more fulfilling than changing the fate of someone close to you?

However, upon hearing the poignant, tragic love story of Li Shimin and Zhangsun Kangning in that future, Yuwen Zhu had still broken down in tears, crying so inconsolably that she lost all posture, reducing Li Xuanba to a panic like an ant on a hot pan.

Yuwen Zhu felt it was thoroughly embarrassing, which was why she wanted to tease Zhangsun Kangning mercilessly now.

"Stop pinching... stop tickling! Even though I don't know how I offended you, Sister, I was wrong! Spare me, Sister!"

Zhangsun Kangning rolled around the bed, ducking back under the quilt with only her small head poking out.

Yuwen Zhu said fiercely, "Remember, even though you are married, you are still yourself, and you must prioritize your own well-being. Think of your parents and brothers—don't bring them sorrow. We were raised as cherished darlings in our homes; we didn't get married just to be worn down and mistreated."

Zhangsun Kangning asked cautiously, "The Duke of Tang's house has an exceptional family atmosphere. How could they mistreat us?"

Yuwen Zhu said, "I know. If the Duke of Tang's family values weren't so good, our parents wouldn't have let us marry in. They all wish the best for us, but we must also stand up for ourselves."

Zhangsun Kangning nodded. "Got it, got it. Sigh, honestly, I didn't really want to go take care of him anyway. I'm so sleepy and hungry! Damned Erlang, why did he have to drag me into dancing! It's all his fault!"

Yuwen Zhu's lips twitched. *All his fault? Oh, you, I told you to love yourself, not to shift the blame!*

"Yes, it's all his fault. That's why you must get plenty of rest." Yuwen Zhu patted the bulged quilt. "Lie still, and I'll massage your head so you won't suffer a headache later."

"Okay!" Zhangsun Kangning lay down obediently, squinting her eyes. "Sister is the best! Ouch, gentler!"

Under the care of Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu, Li Shimin and Zhangsun Kangning rested for a day and were fully revived by the third day.

Li Shimin made a deep, formal bow to Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu. "My thanks to my brother and sister-in-law for saving my life."

Zhangsun Kangning also mimicked a deep bow playfully. "My thanks to my brother-in-law and sister for saving my life."

Li Shimin turned to Zhangsun Kangning and said, "My lady, why do you still call my younger brother's wife 'Sister'?"

Zhangsun Kangning said, "Sister and I are so close, I'm not changing how I address her! We'll each use our own terms!"

Li Shimin said, "Oh, alright then."

A faint smile rippled across the corners of Zhangsun Kangning's lips. Just as Sister had said, Li Erlang was wonderful, allowing her to be willful even after marriage.

Li Xuanba held his forehead and sighed longly. "I didn't save your lives, but who will save mine? Help! I was hoping Second Sister-in-law would keep Second Brother in check—I don't need double the Second Brother!"

Zhangsun Kangning placed her hands on her hips. "Brother-in-law, what kind of talk is that! Where am I anything like him?"

The moment the words left her mouth, she broke into laughter herself. "Alright, alright. I carried away the day before yesterday, but I definitely won't overindulge in alcohol again. Erlang, you aren't allowed to overindulge either."

Li Shimin took on a serious posture. "I was just overly overjoyed. I never used to overindulge."

Li Xuanba: "Ha."

Li Shimin: *【Shut!】*

Li Xuanba: *【What?】*

Li Shimin: *【Up!】*

Li Xuanba: *【Tch.】*

Yuwen Zhu gave Li Xuanba's hand a gentle tug, signaling him not to undercut Li Shimin in front of Zhangsun Kangning.

No matter how the brothers squabbled in private, they had to give respect in front of their sister-in-law.

Yuwen Zhu shifted the topic: "Now that you're feeling better, shall we go clean up the courtyard together?"

Li Shimin asked, "Sister-in-law, do you want to move out already?"

Yuwen Zhu sighed. "Studying medicine is like rowing upstream; to fail to advance is to fall back. Learning medicine doesn't just involve handling herbs, but also... Second Brother should know how military physicians practice their skills in treating external trauma."

Li Shimin frowned. "That is true indeed... Sigh, Father and Mother want to keep Ah Xuan and me here until after the New Year before we return to Zhangye. Otherwise, it would be most comfortable if Sister-in-law traveled to Zhangye with us. I could find you plenty of corpses to practice on."

"Cough cough," Zhangsun Kangning interjected. "Be a bit more tactful."

Li Shimin corrected himself: "Oh, oh! Zhangye has plenty of patients for you to practice on."

Li Xuanba couldn't help snorting, "Patients who have already departed this world, you mean?"

Li Shimin demanded, "Just tell me whether Sister-in-law needs them or not!"

Li Xuanba cupped his hands in respect. "She needs them, very much so. I will rely on Second Brother in the future."

Li Shimin grinned. "Leave it to me."

Zhangsun Kangning sighed. "But Sister and I have to stay in Taiyuan..."

Li Shimin interrupted, "If I say we can bring you along, then we definitely can. Trust me and Ah Xuan. Right, Ah Xuan?"

Li Xuanba nodded. "Mhm. Please rest assured."

How could he and his brother possibly leave their newlyweds behind in Taiyuan?

Zhangsun Kangning blinked and said, "Actually, even if you left Sister and me behind, we would just secretly disguise ourselves and follow you, right, Sister?"

Yuwen Zhu: "Cough, cough."

Zhangsun Kangning covered her mouth. "Ah, slipped up! Teehee!"

Li Shimin laughed. "Great minds think alike."

The young couple winked at each other.

Li Xuanba pulled Yuwen Zhu away. "Let's go pack our luggage."

Yuwen Zhu: "Alright."

Li Shimin and Zhangsun Kangning followed behind. "Hey, don't leave! Let's go together!"

The two young couples left together. Around the corner of the wall, a small head popped out.

Li Zhiyun said resentment-filled, "Now that Second Brother and Third Brother are married, there's no room left for me beside them. Waaah, Shixin, I'm so heartbroken! I want to get married too!"

Luo Shixin leaned against the wall, arms crossed, saying weakly, "Yeah, yeah, sure, sure. Why don't you go ask the Duke's Lady when she'll find one for you?"

Li Zhiyun said, "How embarrassing would that be? By the way, aren't you betrothed yet? Ah, you're already this old and still not betrothed? How lame!"

Luo Shixin nearly slipped down the wall.

He glared fiercely. "Are you begging for a beating?! How can one establish a family before the world is settled?! I will establish my career before starting a family!"

Li Zhiyun made a face. "Excuses!"

The two started scuffling.

Hearing the commotion, Li Shimin turned back to look. "What are Little Fifth and Shixin doing?"

Li Xuanba said, "No idea. Looks like they're very bored. Let's grab them to help us move stuff."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第126章 李玄霸随手闲棋
chunks.chineseText:
第126章 李玄霸随手闲棋

小夫妻的轻松日常没持续几天。当宾客散去后， 李世民和李玄霸也开始干正事，辅佐父亲李渊在山西、河东站稳脚跟。
　　李渊把李建成、李世民、李玄霸叫到一起，父子四人开了个会， 梳理山西河东的错综复杂的世家豪强和官场关系。
　　山西隋朝朝廷直属力量更强。
　　山西排得上号的世家为“太原王氏”， 名义上是天下最顶尖的大世家。
　　但此世的太原王氏先经过永嘉之乱， 后最显赫的王愉一脉被刘裕灭门，仅留王慧龙孤身投奔北魏。太原王氏名声还在，但无论是在官场还是地方上的影响力都已经衰退， 全靠祖上名声支撑门面。
　　入唐之后，太原王氏名义上是顶尖世家，其实地位已经和二等世家无异。“崔卢李郑”四姓世家在婚姻上常不带太原王氏玩。
　　因经济和政治上的双重弱势， 太原王氏对李渊的工作很是配合，与寻常地方豪强没区别。
　　但河东就不一样了。
　　河东是关中郡姓世家的起源地， 自魏晋以来， 就是世家掌控的地方。
　　关中郡姓以“韦、裴、柳、薛、杨、杜”为首。光是河东一郡，有河东薛氏、河东柳氏、河东裴氏三个郡姓。
　　关中郡姓是关陇贵族的一部分，薛柳裴三姓在朝堂上也占据高位，并不给李渊面子。
　　李渊被命为山西、河东慰抚使，名义上军政一把手。但河东世家在天下大乱之后自修坞堡， 以组织乡勇的名义蓄养私兵，河东官吏也以河东世家为尊。李渊无法插手河东事务。
　　听着李渊介绍河东开展工作的困难时， 李玄霸一边收集情报，一边和二哥科普后世一些关于河东的谣言。
　　后世盛唐安史之乱这一段历史养活了许多营销号，出现了许多谣言。
　　比如说安史之乱是大唐不带支持窦建德的河东玩， 所以河东就叛了。还有更甚者， 说河东一直是半独立。
　　就算只是识得唐朝几个“薛柳裴”的名人， 也说不出这等荒唐话。
　　掌控河东郡的薛氏、裴氏、柳氏身为关陇贵族的一员， 是支持李唐的中坚力量。三家在唐初出了许多宰相，与李唐联姻者也不少。
　　窦建德麾下几乎没有河东世家的人。民间百姓纪念他，但世家对他冷眼相待。
　　那时社会的经济文化命脉都握在世家手中。初唐盛唐关中郡姓在朝堂占据绝对优势，河东郡是他们的大本营，他们不可能不惠及自己家乡。
　　窦建德之死造成了唐初窦建德部下多次叛乱，但与盛唐时中原的混乱已经没有关系。
　　安史之乱的原因很复杂，究其本质仍旧是王朝由盛转衰时“经济基础决定上层建筑”，“土地兼并造成混乱让野心家找到机会”那一套陈词滥调，这里暂且不提。继续说世家。
　　河东世家站位很及时，倒是山东世家在唐初没有慧眼识珠，登上李唐这条大船，所以在唐初政治地位较低。
　　唐高宗夫妻俩打击的不是山东世家，而是试图抬起山东世家打压关陇贵族。重视科举只从表面上看，也是对诗书传家的山东、南方世家更有利。
　　黑暗的五代十国拉着世家一同进地狱后，宋之后的科举才是对寒门更有利。
　　安史之乱之后，唐朝关陇贵族遭到极大打击，山东世家通过科举迅速上位，唐朝中晚期宰相多出自山东世家。
　　排一下宰相名单，就可以看出初唐盛唐的宰相多是出自关中郡姓，中唐晚唐的宰相多是出自山东郡姓。
　　不过山东郡姓虽然依靠科举大量进入朝堂，但又厌恶科举这个非门荫的选拔人才方式。
　　当山东郡姓的官僚彻底占领朝堂中枢之后，就多次希望废除科举，并歧视科举出身的官员。颇有一种自己过了河就要砍桥的美。
　　李世民听着弟弟在心中碎碎念，眼珠子时不时地转一下，十分难受。
　　好想和弟弟聊天。但是他的心灵感应不过关，只能一个字一个字地蹦出来，蹦得还特别累。若说五六个字，快和急行军的疲惫相提并论了。
　　为什么要在我无法回答的时候碎碎念这么有趣的话啊！我想多听听那些世家的丑事！
　　李渊分享完情报和现状时，李玄霸也意犹未尽地结束了自己在心里的碎碎念。
　　这时他才想起来，自己好像不小心对二哥说了“唐高宗夫妻俩”。
　　不过也无事，他没有把女帝的事说出来。
　　如果这次嫂子没有英年早逝，太子又出生较晚，估计就是太子正常继位，或许便没有女帝的事了。
　　不过也有可能女帝将来仍旧成为太子宫中妃嫔，或者干脆女帝和自己一样穿越到这个时代某个李唐后人身上。未来谁说得准？
　　自己闭眼后的事，还是懒得折腾了。
　　如果唐朝出现华夏第一位女帝，也挺有意思。
　　不过女帝的父亲在李渊刚来太原时就带着家产投奔李渊，成为初唐建国的功臣之一。李玄霸来到太原后，却没有在唐国公府见到一个“武”姓的原豪商。
　　他隐约猜到，或许是天命之子不共存原理，这位女帝原本的命运已经改变，要“错峰出行”了。
　　李玄霸暗暗希望乐子大一点，如果武则天带着记忆穿越成某个李唐的公主就好玩了。
　　因有孝道和外戚的助力，太后篡儿子的位置很容易，但公主继位，那就是地狱难度了。一般而言，就算皇帝没有儿子，就会过继宗室子弟，不会考虑公主。
　　如果武则天带着记忆穿越，能打破这个“前所未有”吗？
　　李玄霸欢乐地祈祷，如果女帝真的要穿越成公主，希望穿越到自己还没死的时候。
　　如果对立下无字碑的武则天剧透后世对她褒贬不一的评价，重点剧透最坏的评价，一定和对着唐太宗剧透“唐太宗成为皇帝白月光的重要原因之一还有他死的时机刚刚好”一样有趣。
　　历史营销号乐子人可不是只想看唐太宗一人的乐子。
　　“阿玄，都结束了，你还发什么呆？”李世民拉着多次试图撞墙撞树的李玄霸“脱离险境”。
　　李玄霸条件反射回答：“我在想如果我养的营销号能被历代明君看到，我指着他们鼻子骂，他们隔着时空对我无能狂怒，真是太有趣了。”
　　李世民不知道什么是“营销号”，但当了李玄霸这么多年的双生哥哥，一些词听不懂，他也能明白李玄霸话中大概意思。
　　李世民道：“如果你骂的是真事，如果你骂的人也真的都是明君，我想可能他们不会愤怒，反而会视你为良师益友。”
　　李玄霸打趣道：“是那种不用担心自己怒气上头砍了后追悔莫及的良师益友？”
　　李世民大笑道：“对，就是那种。”
　　兄弟二人肩膀把着肩膀，为不可能发生的乐子一起大笑，并谋划如果真的发生这种事，要对先代有为君主剧透些什么。
　　“肯定要对秦始皇说他二世而亡对吧？”
　　“那是肯定的哈哈哈哈哈哈！”
　　两人笑声传老远，书房里愁眉不展的李渊都听到了。
　　他揉了揉眉头，失笑道：“年轻人的心态真好，出门时他们还愁着，现在就笑得如此开心了。”
　　儿子的笑声感染了李渊，他抛去了心头的阴霾，继续仔细梳理情报，思索要如何在河东破局。
　　如果破不了局，至少要把山西牢牢地掌控住。
　　……
　　李渊给李世民、李玄霸安排任务之后，李玄霸就要启程去河东郡了。
　　时间紧迫，李渊不能把李世民和李玄霸留太久，河右之地需要他们镇守。
　　所以李渊急急忙忙拉着李世民出征，把山西周围比较顽固的势力扫灭；李玄霸也迅速和李建成南下河东郡，争取能获得河东郡姓的支持。
　　李玄霸争取到河东世家支持是极有可能的。
　　薛道衡出身河东薛氏，裴世矩出身河东裴氏。两人教导过李玄霸，所以河东薛氏和河东裴氏会把李玄霸当做是“自家人”——世家之间建立关系，除了姻亲故吏就是师徒了。
　　从李世民和李玄霸成亲时，河东薛氏和河东裴氏都派出了家族中掌握话语权的子弟赴宴，就可以看出他们对李世民和李玄霸的亲近。
　　虽然李建成是李世民、李玄霸的兄长，但唐国公在河东世家眼中是“非世家”，所以他们的关系是只对单人，不对家族。李建成享受不到李世民、李玄霸和薛道衡、裴世矩这层师徒关系带来的便利。
　　宇文珠刚收拾好屋里，又打包行李与李玄霸一同南下。
　　路上，李玄霸对宇文珠道：“这次去河东郡的破局点可能不是我，而是在珠娘。”
　　宇文珠立刻会意：“三郎的意思是，让我从女眷入手？”
　　李玄霸道：“对。世家与勋贵一样，就算再有权有势，但世间女子为医师者甚少，医术高超者更是罕见。珠娘已经在大兴和洛阳扬名，我想世家女眷肯定早就念着珠娘来了。”
　　宇文珠有点担忧道：“我能做到吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“不需要多做什么，只要治好她们，和她们建立良好关系就行。我们又不求着他们什么。”
　　李玄霸笑了笑，道：“夫人大可倨傲些。相信我，将来是他们求我们，不是我们求他们。我现在与他们交好，只是让他们提前成为我们的助力。如果他们眼瞎，那将是他们自己的损失。”
　　宇文珠心中忐忑减弱不少：“好，那我就争取让河东世家多欠我一点人情！”
　　李玄霸道：“对，就是这个气势。”
　　宇文珠深呼吸。这是她嫁给郎君后的初战，一定要旗开得胜！
　　李玄霸看着宇文珠给自己打气的模样，有点想笑，又怕宇文珠误会，很艰难地忍住。
　　与宇文珠和二嫂近距离相处后，他发现宇文珠和二嫂脾性有一点很相似——倔强。
　　如果用后世中二一点的说法，就是“我XX一生不弱于人”，颇具竞争精神，希望在自己能做到的事上做到最好。
　　小到与女眷拼酒，大到自己的事业，她们都斗志满满，全力以赴。
　　二嫂的性格较为外显。自家珠娘则将这种性格隐藏在心底，可能她自己都没发现。
　　但珠娘的行为却更为激进。
　　别说谁家女子，就是已经成名的医师，也很少有亲手解剖死尸的。
　　真不知道孙医师教了珠娘什么。他是真的倾囊相授啊。
　　说来孙医师跑哪去了？怎么自己的婚礼都不参加？
　　李玄霸问道：“孙医师可还在大兴？”
　　“怎么说到老师了？”宇文珠道，“他不在，云游去了。我也不知道他在哪里。”
　　李玄霸装作恶狠狠道：“他居然不来参加我俩的婚礼。下次逮住他，我一定要狠狠骂他一顿，把他积攒的好药材都敲诈走！”
　　宇文珠“扑哧”笑道：“好，我帮你。我也生气老师不来参加我的婚礼。”
　　李玄霸笑道：“一言为定。”
　　宇文珠想起老师与她道别前，对李玄霸身体的担忧。
　　她和李玄霸成亲后，两人都没有提李玄霸可能早逝的事。
　　这件事从她与李玄霸谈婚论嫁时就开始讨论。在两人还未见面的时候，他们就已经定下了李玄霸早夭后宇文珠的路。
　　李玄霸需要一个妻子抵挡其他家族的联姻。
　　她需要一个能让她完成梦想，不约束她的地方。
　　两者一拍即合。
　　当李玄霸离世后，她仍旧会待在唐国公府。
　　她会成为王妃，会打着为李玄霸守寡的名义用着李玄霸留下的资源，继续完成她的梦想。
　　两人有了感情之后，这件事就变成宇文珠会在李玄霸去世后替李玄霸照顾家人，替李玄霸继续看着这个一定会走向盛世的世界。
　　她要替李玄霸看看未来的大唐。
　　但这些谋划和讨论，在他们成亲时戛然而止。
　　该讨论的内容已经结束，现在他们只想以白头携手为前提，享受相处的每一个瞬间。
　　扫兴的话不会说，扫兴的事不要想。
　　现在、明天、后天，每一天都应该是开心的，雀跃的，值得期盼的。
　　宇文珠收起心中的惆怅，笑道：“我还是有点担心去了河东世家家中胆怯。三郎，你再和我多说说世家的事。我听闻你曾被荥阳郑氏为难，世家人是不是很不好相处？”
　　李玄霸道：“荥阳郑氏平常也不会故意倨傲，我和二哥那次被折腾，是因为我们要去求亲。一旦我们需要求着别人，那么被人折辱也无话可说了。”
　　宇文珠摇头：“求亲是两家的喜事，被人折辱是结亲还是结仇？我看那荥阳郑氏的家风也不过如此。”
　　李玄霸道：“世家家风都差不多，他们只是吃着祖上的余荫，所以你不必高看他们。”
　　他细细梳理起河东郡姓的来历和现状，比如河东薛氏是河东的外来者，比如河东裴氏和柳氏曾经南渡。
　　宇文珠听着李玄霸梳理的事，脑海中关于河东世家的印象越来越清楚，心中也越来越安稳。
　　只要揭开了世家这层由祖上余荫带来的神秘面纱，其实也就不过如此。
　　宇文珠饱读诗书，见多识广，她坚信自己一定能获胜。
　　打气，再次打气！能赢！
　　李玄霸见宇文珠都悄悄握拳了，脸朝向窗外，假装呼吸新鲜空气。
　　真可爱，扑哧。
　　宇文珠没有看到李玄霸捂着嘴笑，继续低着头努力给自己打气。
　　……
　　正如李渊所料，李玄霸一到河东郡，所受到的欢迎程度远不是李建成能比的。
　　李玄霸刚到城门口，河东薛氏、河东裴氏留守在家的最有才华的子弟就拉着河东柳氏子弟一起，在城门口迎接李玄霸。
　　薛氏和裴氏的子弟将柳氏子弟介绍给李玄霸，陪同李玄霸来到李建成家，并给他介绍城中闲置的宅子，说要喝乔迁酒。
　　李玄霸什么都没有展示，河东三姓世家子弟就对李玄霸仿佛多年不见的老友，一副恨不得立刻拉李玄霸喝酒的模样。
　　李玄霸苦笑：“我想老师肯定给家中写过信，提过我真的不能喝，让你们别拉着我喝酒。”
　　薛氏和裴氏的子弟对视一眼，皆笑：“确实叮嘱了，但我们不信啊。”
　　李玄霸挽起袖子：“行吧，我来给你们表演个三杯倒。”
　　两家子弟拉着李玄霸道：“来来来，我来看你是不是真的三杯倒。”
　　柳氏子弟在后面抿嘴笑，吩咐人去拿酒。
　　他对宇文珠拱手道：“薛兄和裴兄性格疏朗，但粗中有细，不会真的灌醉李三郎，嫂嫂不必担心。”
　　宇文珠微笑道：“我不担心，你们玩去，我给你们熬药。”
　　她真的不担心，因为李玄霸真的三杯倒。
　　李玄霸还未梳洗，刚下马车就被薛氏、裴氏、柳氏子弟拉去接风洗尘，而这三家子弟打着“为长辈的弟子接风洗尘”的名号，愣是把李建成给排挤出去了。
　　李建成心里愤怒，面上还要露出一副好兄长的表情，别提多难受。
　　李元吉见状，若有所思。
　　他有点不明白，以李玄霸的阴险狡诈，不可能看不出兄长的心情。如果李玄霸开口让兄长一起去，河东三姓子弟可能会顺势将兄长纳入其中。
　　为何李玄霸什么都不说？
　　李元吉隐约抓住了什么，心中有点兴奋。
　　李玄霸被人拉去喝酒时，宇文珠留在家中整理行李。
　　李建成派人来帮忙，李元吉也做出一副好弟弟模样，和李智云一起指挥下人。
　　他正百无聊赖地胡乱指挥时，发现李智云不见了。
　　李元吉便借口寻找李智云，随意找了处地方躲懒。
　　“你要乖乖的，别担心，我们很快就把你送去张掖。”
　　李智云的声音从墙那头响起。
　　李元吉悄悄从墙角探出头，看到李智云对一个书童打扮的人道。
　　他心头一惊，想到什么，猛地一退，弄出了点动静。
　　李智云立刻警觉：“谁？”
　　李元吉转身就跑。
　　李智云等了一会儿，慢悠悠对罗士信道：“去看看。”
　　罗士信走过去，回头道：“已经走了。”
　　李智云拍了拍一脸傻相的书童一下：“记得该怎么演吗？”
　　书童点头。
　　李智云让书童回去换回丫鬟的衣服。
　　他对罗士信道：“三兄计谋这么粗糙，真的能行？他稍稍打探一下，就知道太子殿下没有儿子吧？”
　　罗士信道：“三郎君说，成与不成都没关系，只是一手闲棋。再者，正因为是‘私生子’，太子殿下才能将其送走。”
　　李智云点头：“很有道理。”
　　他摸了摸下巴，和罗士信一起往回走：“不知道李元吉会不会真的去告密。如果他真的去告密了，我和二兄三兄就再也不用担心他将来背刺我们。”
　　罗士信没回答。他总觉得有点心慌，一定是错觉。
　　三郎君算无遗策，应该做好了所有最坏的打算。他杞人忧天了。
　　“哇！”罗士信突然激动大叫。
　　李智云吓了一跳：“你鬼叫什么？”
　　罗士信得意道：“我刚胡思乱想时，居然用了‘杞人忧天’这个典故！”
　　李智云疑惑：“这又如何？”
　　罗士信道：“说明我书读得多！”
　　李智云：“……”自己这个好友有时候好憨啊。
　　果然两杯就开始晃悠的李玄霸被新结识的世家子弟灌了醒酒药，世家子弟喝酒他喝水，一直玩到半夜，撑得半死才回家。
　　刚回家，就看见李智云扑过来，笑着说“成了”。
　　李玄霸揉着全是水的肚子，有气无力道：“这件事之后就别管了，当做没发生过。”
　　李智云道：“啊？就没有后续了吗？”他刚准备大展拳脚呢！
　　李玄霸道：“现在给他心中植入一颗怀疑的种子就行了。接下来顺应局势变化，再做打算。”
　　李智云蔫哒哒道：“好吧。”唉，他还以为这次终于能把李元吉一拳打飞到自己永远也看不到的地方。
　　送走李智云后，李玄霸和宇文珠道了声平安，回到书房梳理自己从接风宴席上获得的最新情报。
　　杨玄感还没死，杨广居然仍旧要征高丽，实在是难以揣摩杨广在想什么。
　　薛氏、裴氏、柳氏族中有伴随杨广出征者，他们的消息比李渊还更灵敏些。
　　据从酒宴上打探出的消息来看，杨广将中原大乱的过错推到了高丽不肯投降，降低了他的威信上。他坚信只要能让高丽投降，逆贼就会重新惧怕和臣服他。
　　真是荒唐啊。
　　杨广在出征前，也对镇压逆贼作出了指示。
　　他仍旧说出了历史中很著名，但网络上不出名的那句话，“益知天下人不欲多，多即相聚为盗耳”。
　　李玄霸按住额头，嘴角噙着讥笑：“真不愧是隋炀帝。”
