Chapter 129: An Unexpected Harvest of Talent

Luo Shixin reunited with Qin Qiong and Pei Xingyan. The three of them began fooling around without the slightest hint of distance or awkwardness.

Pei Xingyan’s status and background differed vastly from Qin Qiong and Luo Shixin’s, yet the three interacted as naturally as ordinary close friends.

Qin Qiong was slightly older than Pei Xingyan. He usually had an honest, upright expression and handsome, dignified features, looking like a simple and dependable man.

However, once he obtained Li Xuanba and Li Zhiyun’s consent and pinned Luo Shixin to the ground for a beatdown, his ferocious expression instantly made Li Xuanba recall the legendary door gods of later generations.

Who would have thought that the later generations' depictions of Qin Qiong as a Door God actually captured his true essence so perfectly? This was truly an exceptionally amusing realization.

Li Xuanba watched with a beaming smile as Luo Shixin received a thorough lesson from his two older brothers. Clapping his hands, Li Zhiyun laughed, "Serves you right!"

Luo Shixin flashed an offensive gesture at Li Zhiyun and barked, "Jihong, just you wait!"

Li Zhiyun smirked playfully. "I'm waiting, I'm waiting! I'm waiting for you to get beaten until you can't crawl out of bed so I can stand by your bedside and mock you."

Li Xuanba shook his head with a helpless laugh. If Little Fifth ended up getting beaten by Luo Shixin later, he truly would have brought it upon himself.

*Just who did Little Fifth pick up this infuriatingly cheeky attitude from?*

Having finished "disciplining" Luo Shixin, Pei Xingyan looked thoroughly refreshed and dragged Liu Heng and Xue Yuanjing over for a drinking contest.

Li Zhiyun leaned in and asked Liu Heng if his niece was good-looking.

Liu Heng looked at Li Zhiyun with an exceedingly complicated expression.

What respectable noble scion would ask about a woman's looks during marriage negotiations? Weren't political alliances supposed to focus solely on family background and moral character?

Yet, seeing the bright, sparkling look in Li Zhiyun's eyes, Liu Heng inexplicably found himself unable to feel any annoyance.

Pei Xingyan pointed at Liu Heng’s face and laughed, "Just look at his features! Do you even need to ask about his niece's looks?"

Catching the hint, Li Zhiyun attentively poured wine for Liu Heng, treating him with the deference due to a father-in-law.

Liu Heng drank the wine poured by Li Zhiyun.

The niece he intended to introduce to Li Zhiyun was the younger sister of Liu Shi—the very niece who would have come in his place had he not returned to Hedong Commandery.

Since Liu Shi's father had already passed away, the family was currently under the care of the elder generation, meaning Liu Heng himself. When the time came to marry off his niece, he would fulfill the duties of a father. Therefore, he could indeed be considered Li Zhiyun's future father-in-law, making this cup of wine quite appropriate.

Luo Shixin had only suffered a few light bruises. Both Qin Qiong and Pei Xingyan knew when to hold back, ensuring the punishment inflicted pain without actual injury.

After resting for a while, a wincing Luo Shixin led Qin Qiong over to greet Li Xuanba, pulling Li Xuanba aside to speak in private for a moment.

Qin Qiong bowed respectfully and said, "Please forgive my presumption in coming to offer my allegiance so abruptly, Third Young Master."

Li Xuanba chuckled. "Could anyone be more abrupt than Shixin? He bumped into my Second Brother outside the gates of Zhangye, and the two of them went straight into the military camp to spar and gamble on a duel."

Qin Qiong cast a glance at Luo Shixin.

Luo Shixin rubbed his nose self-consciously.

Qin Qiong said, "It is precisely because Brother Luo possesses such audacity that he was able to pledge himself to a wise master."

Li Xuanba motioned for Qin Qiong to take a seat and ordered a servant to bring warm honeyed water.

He could tell that Qin Qiong was likely hungry, but seemed reluctant to eat before finishing their conversation—or perhaps felt uncomfortable sitting at the same table as those aristocratic scions. Thus, Li Xuanba served honeyed water first to stave off his hunger.

Li Xuanba said, "Moisten your throat first, then we can speak at length."

After offering his thanks, Qin Qiong took the honeyed water and drank most of it, a bright glint flashing in his eyes.

Luo Shixin leaned close to Qin Qiong's ear and whispered, "The Third Young Master was worried you were hungry."

Li Xuanba said helplessly, "Must you blabber about everything?"

Luo Shixin made a zipping-his-lips gesture.

Understanding filled Qin Qiong's heart. It was clear that Luo Shixin genuinely loved his current place, and truly hoped that he would stay as well.

Seeing Qin Qiong hesitate, Li Xuanba guessed he might feel awkward talking about his former superior, so he took the initiative to ask, "I recall Shixin mentioning that your courtesy name is Shubao. May I presume to address you by your courtesy name?"

Qin Qiong hastened to reply, "Please, Third Young Master, feel free."

Li Xuanba said, "I heard you used to serve under General Zhang [Zhang Xutuo]. General Zhang clearly trusted and valued you quite highly. May I ask why you gave up the seniority and prospects you built under General Zhang to come to Hedong and join the Duke of Tang's residence?"

Qin Qiong said, "I received a letter from Shixin. He told me that under Second Young Master Li, promotion depends solely on military merit, regardless of one's background."

Having said this, Qin Qiong closed his mouth, adding nothing more.

Though Qin Qiong said no more, Li Xuanba understood his reason for leaving Zhang Xutuo.

Seeing earlier that Pei Xingyan hadn't known Luo Shixin was serving under his Second Brother, Li Xuanba had assumed Qin Qiong didn't know either. In truth, Luo Shixin had secretly written to Qin Qiong, so Qin Qiong was well aware.

Luo Shixin's reasons for keeping it from Pei Xingyan were simple: first, sneaking away had somewhat shamed General Zhang, who had actually treated him well, so he naturally kept a low profile; second, Pei Xingyan was from a prominent aristocratic clan whose father was a high-ranking court official with a glowing future ahead, so there was no need for Luo Shixin to "give him pointers."

Although Qin Qiong was fierce and valiant, he came from a humble background just like Luo Shixin, making advancement exceedingly difficult.

Qin Qiong had once served under Lai Hu'er. When Qin Qiong's mother passed away, Lai Hu'er had even sent emissaries to offer condolences.

The *Old Book of Tang* recorded Lai Hu'er's response to his subordinates' doubts: *"This man is brave and fierce, possessed of noble ideals and integrity. He is bound to win wealth and honor through his own merits—how could I treat him as a mere commoner?"*

Yet this response proved both that Lai Hu'er valued Qin Qiong and that Qin Qiong's position in Lai Hu'er's army at the time differed little from an ordinary foot soldier; being treated as "humble" was the norm.

Thus, despite Lai Hu'er showing high regard for him, Qin Qiong still joined the army nearby after his period of maternal mourning ended, transferring to serve under Zhang Xutuo, who was then the Vice Magistrate of Qi Commandery.

Li Xuanba sorted through the historical records regarding Qin Qiong.

It was seemingly not until December of this year that Qin Qiong and Luo Shixin would display their extraordinary courage and martial arts in Zhang Xutuo's army, gradually rising in status.

Yet Qin Qiong's origins were simply too lowly. Even after years of accumulating numerous military merits—including being the first to scale enemy walls—he had only been promoted to a Lieutenant of Established Valor, a rank of the sixth grade.

And even that official post was only possible under Zhang Xutuo, who paid no heed to conventional rules when promoting talented individuals.

It was not yet July, so Qin Qiong likely had not yet found an opportunity to achieve major military exploits under Zhang Xutuo, leaving him frustrated. Seeing Luo Shixin's letter, combined with the fact that Pei Xingyan—an aristocratic youth who admired him—was heading to join the Duke of Tang's residence, Qin Qiong had decided to come along.

Li Xuanba asked, "Did General Zhang ask you to pass along a message?"

Qin Qiong froze. "How did you know, Third Young Master?"

Li Xuanba smiled faintly. "General Zhang is a renowned commander of our age; he surely recognizes your abilities and Shixin's, even if circumstances made it difficult to promote you. Though he didn't know Shixin came to us, when you left, you undoubtedly took your leave of him."

Qin Qiong hesitated for a moment before speaking truthfully: "When General Zhang couldn't find Shixin in his hometown, he guessed that Shixin might have traveled west to seek out Second Young Master Li."

Luo Shixin almost spat out his honeyed water. "No way?!"

Qin Qiong looked at Luo Shixin as if looking at a little fool. "You were constantly asking about Second Young Master Li's deeds in the army, speaking of him with deep admiration. When you left the military without going home, who else could you have gone to seek?"

Luo Shixin gave a foolish grin. "Was it really that obvious?"

Qin Qiong sighed, drew a letter from his robe, and presented it respectfully to Li Xuanba. "I originally intended to hand this letter to Second Young Master Li..."

"But giving it to Third Young Master is the same as giving it to Second Young Master! Second Young Master will drag Third Young Master to read it together anyway," Luo Shixin chimed in. "It's better if Third Young Master takes a look first to see if it's appropriate to hand over."

On the surface, Li Xuanba seemed stern while Li Shimin appeared easy to get along with. Yet Luo Shixin's instincts were sharp; he always felt that Third Young Master Li was easier to reason with, whereas Second Young Master Li carried a far more intimidating majesty.

In front of his master, even knowing he wouldn't be blamed, Luo Shixin wouldn't blabber carelessly.

*Perhaps this is the aura of a true sovereign,* Luo Shixin thought.

Li Xuanba unfolded the letter while wondering aloud, "Why wouldn't it be appropriate... Wait, what?!"

*"Stinking brat! How dare you steal away two of my fierce generals?! If we ever meet face to face, I will give you a sound beating! Not even His Majesty could protect you!"*

Li Xuanba took a deep breath.

The letter was long, but what was up with this opening line? *General Zhang, you may be a general now, but you started out as a civil official—is it really okay for you to have such a explosive temper?*

Li Xuanba looked toward Qin Qiong.

Qin Qiong gave a bitter smile.

Luo Shixin grinned. "Brother Qin is an honest man and genuinely intended to hand the letter straight to Second Young Master. What if Second Young Master gets angry? Well, although Second Young Master certainly wouldn't be angry, he might take the opportunity to pick a fight with General Zhang."

"Second Brother isn't that kind of person..." Li Xuanba paused, slapping his forehead. "No... he's *exactly* that kind of person."

Given Second Brother's playful and wild temperament, he might actually use this excuse to visit Zhang Xutuo just to spar with him.

Li Xuanba let out a sigh and continued reading the letter.

After pulling rank with his opening joke, Zhang Xutuo provided a detailed account of Qin Qiong's performance in the military, using his own reputation to vouch for and recommend Qin Qiong to Li Shimin.

He also complained briefly about Luo Shixin in the letter, remarking that the boy was hot-tempered and hoping Second Young Master Li wouldn't hold it against him. If Li Shimin truly didn't like him, he could simply send Luo Shixin back so Zhang Xutuo could discipline him properly.

Li Xuanba turned the letter over and read it several times, seeing only references to "Second Young Master Li" and not a single mention of the "Duke of Tang."

"You wish to pledge allegiance to my Second Brother, not to the Duke of Tang's residence?" Li Xuanba asked.

Qin Qiong replied, "Serving under the Duke of Tang would likely be little different from serving under General Zhang."

Li Xuanba said, "In a few days, travel to Taiyuan with Brother Pei to see my Second Brother, and set off immediately after your meeting. Zhangye desperately needs fierce generals. The journey will be arduous—thank you for your hard work."

Qin Qiong quickly cupped his hands, saying with emotion, "It is no trouble at all!"

Leaving General Zhang this time had left him feeling extremely apprehensive.

His humble background set a hard ceiling on his promotions. Finding a superior who appreciated him was exceedingly rare, so staying with General Zhang might have been the more sensible choice.

Though General Lai Hu'er had also admired his valor, General Zhang had promised him real opportunities to earn glory and military distinction, assuring him that so long as he earned merit, promotions would not be withheld. To Qin Qiong, General Lai's condolences upon his mother's passing had deeply moved him, but General Zhang was the true mentor who recognized his worth.

Furthermore, Qin Qiong's hometown was in Qi Commandery. With the world falling into chaos, he had harbored doubts about leaving his native homeland.

Yet General Zhang had personally sought him out, instructing him to accompany Pei Xingyan to seek out Second Young Master Li.

*"Suppressing peasant rebels is no true achievement. You would do better to follow Second Young Master Li to fight foreign barbarians. Do not worry about your hometown; so long as I am here, nothing will go wrong."*

Zhang Xutuo had always been ruthless toward rebels, rarely taking captives. This was the first time Qin Qiong had ever seen General Zhang show signs of weariness.

*So General Zhang himself is not entirely unmoved by the suppression of these rebellions after all.*

*"Second Young Master Li is merely the second son of the Duke of Tang. Even though he has accumulated stellar military exploits at a young age, recruiting talent remains difficult for him. Moreover, the frontier region cares little for lineage. Following Second Young Master Li should be a fine prospect for you. Though I do not know how Shixin is faring, the fact that he hasn't returned means he is doing well with Second Young Master Li."*

If Zhang Xutuo had asked Qin Qiong to stay, Qin Qiong certainly would have stayed.

General Zhang had given him the break of a lifetime. Even though he had not yet had the chance to perform great deeds, he was profoundly grateful for Zhang's appreciation.

However, since General Zhang had personally written a letter to recommend him, Qin Qiong had no choice but to leave—otherwise, he would be betraying General Zhang's trust.

Besides, he too felt a growing weariness toward suppressing domestic rebellions.

When serving under Lai Hu'er, Qin Qiong had witnessed firsthand the tragic horrors of forced corvée labor, and many of his own fellow villagers had lost their homes and lives because of it.

The rebels who pillaged their own hometown elders were truly abhorrent, and Qin Qiong showed them no mercy. Yet... fighting foreign barbarians felt infinitely lighter on his heart.

He was determined to achieve grand exploits under Second Young Master Li so as not to tarnish General Zhang's name.

Li Xuanba sighed, remaining silent for a long time.

Zhang Xutuo was a brilliant general with a keen eye for talent. Sadly, he stood against the tide of history and would eventually perish suppressing the peasant uprisings at the end of the Sui Dynasty.

This letter briefly sparked a desire in Li Xuanba to see if he could somehow change Zhang Xutuo's ultimate fate.

Yet he quickly snapped back to reality—that was an impossibility.

Zhang Xutuo was loyal to the Sui Dynasty and to Emperor Yang Guang, who had raised him up. He would spare no effort in crushing the peasant revolts.

He was already advanced in years; dying on the battlefield was practically his preordained destiny.

Still, before that time came, perhaps he and Second Brother could write to Zhang Xutuo to discuss military strategy.

Though Zhang Xutuo was hailed as a famous general in his day, his brilliance burned too briefly, and his formidable skills were spent suppressing rebel armies. Consequently, later generations knew little of him.

If he corresponded with Second Brother, borrowing a fraction of "Emperor Taizong of Tang's" radiance, perhaps more people in the future would notice those few lines recorded in the history books and recognize a tragic master general whose talents were squandered on the wrong cause.

Then again, he was repaying the nation's grace and his lord's patronage, and the ruler who promoted him trusted and relied upon him deeply. Who could truly say Zhang Xutuo's devotion was misplaced?

Li Xuanba refrained from speaking the mood-killing truth: *"The next time you meet General Zhang, you might be enemies on the battlefield."*

They might never cross paths with Zhang Xutuo. Even if they did, he could suggest that Second Brother reassign Qin Qiong and Luo Shixin to fight elsewhere, sparing them from a painful moral dilemma.

For matters that could be avoided, there was no need to cause them unnecessary anguish.

"Go join them for a drink. None of those three seem like people who look down on others based on status," Li Xuanba said. "Even if they were, once they join Second Brother's command, they must learn not to be."

A radiant smile broke across Luo Shixin's face.

He downed his honeyed water in one gulp and said to Qin Qiong, "You're definitely going to love it here with me. Come on, let's go drink wine and eat meat! Hey, Qin Shubao, can you help me beat up Jihong?"

Qin Qiong's face darkened. "No!"

*Luo Shixin used to be arrogant under General Zhang, but he wasn't this recklessly brainless!*

*You're actually asking a newcomer like me to help you beat up Fifth Young Master Li? Are you out of your mind?!*

Li Xuanba laughed and scolded, "You're already stronger than Little Fifth, yet you want to bring reinforcement to beat him up? I think you're asking for Second Brother to tie you up and hang you upside down from a tree. Playful banter is one thing, but do you really think Second Brother won't get mad if you genuinely bully Little Fifth?"

Luo Shixin rubbed his nose. "I was just speaking off the cuff. Of course I wouldn't actually do it."

Li Xuanba said, "Go on then."

Luo Shixin asked, "Third Young Master isn't coming over?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "I don't drink wine, so they might feel constrained around me. I'll head over after a while."

He decided to wait until they had consumed a bit more alcohol before dropping by.

Once Luo Shixin and Qin Qiong headed over, the others indeed paid no mind to their background, enthusiastically matching drinks with them.

Nor did they pay much attention to Li Xuanba, who was quietly eating meat off to the side.

Since Third Young Master Li didn't drink, he could be safely left to his own devices.

Li Xuanba was speechless. *Drinking alcohol really is bad—it's a terrible vice of this era!*

*Whatever, I'll just keep eating meat.*

Li Xuanba ate until his stomach bulged comfortably.

...

The next day, just as Li Xuanba wrote a letter detailing the good news to his Second Brother, a celebratory letter from Li Shimin arrived as well.

However, calling it a letter of good news was generous; it was mostly filled with complaints.

The moment Li Shimin announced his recruitment of talented individuals, prospective candidates nearly battered down his threshold.

Although talent flooded in swiftly, Li Shimin was in no cheerful mood.

Back in Heyou, he had effectively been the top military and civil authority, yet recruiting talent had been nightmarishly tedious, with local gentry barely according him face. Now, upon arriving in Taiyuan, simply brandishing the title of "Second Young Master of the Duke of Tang's Residence" transformed his courtyard from deserted to overflowing with visitors.

Although Li Shimin knew that these people joined him partly due to his own capabilities, he still felt aggrieved and stifled.

*"Though it might sound disrespectful to Father, my military exploits are greater than his, and the territory I govern is larger than his—how am I inferior to him in any way?! Are age and noble titles really that important?!"*

Li Xuanba pressed a hand to his forehead. Not only did he lack the urge to comfort his Second Brother, but he also felt an overwhelming urge to snark.

*Haven't you already complained about this dozens of times back in Zhangye? It's not like Second Brother doesn't know the answer, yet he keeps nagging, whining, and muttering on and on—just stop!*

"As expected, recruiting talent in Taiyuan is child's play for Second Brother." Li Xuanba was not surprised by the fruits of his brother's recruitment drive.

Even in original history, when Second Brother possessed only the title of "Second Young Master of the Duke of Tang's Residence," countless people had still rushed to join him. Now that his godlike prowess was recognized across the empire, those who seemed hesitant were merely holding onto temporary "decorum," waiting for a convenient pretext.

Pledging loyalty to the Duke of Tang's residence on paper was precisely the pretext they sought.

In reality, these men were all coming specifically for Second Brother, and the allegiance in their hearts belonged solely to him.

It was just the nominal title... *Sigh.*

Even his own smooth operations in Hedong required leaning on the golden signboard of the "Duke of Tang's Residence" to initiate negotiations.

Li Xuanba rubbed his temples, muttering in frustration, "How did I end up infected by Second Brother's nagging too?"

He stepped out of the courtyard gate, intending to take a walk and clear his mind.

Yuwen Zhu, who was drying medicinal herbs, pointed up at the sky. "Sanlang, look! Aren't those two hunting falcons up there remarkably like Han Gou and Wu Di? Many people in Hedong Commandery keep hunting falcons as well."

Li Xuanba looked up, black lines mentally covering his forehead. "What do you mean 'like'? It *is* them. What on earth are they playing at now?"

Li Xuanba extended his arm. "Come down!"

The two circling golden eagles swooped down—yet instead of landing on Li Xuanba's arm, they landed firmly on the ground.

Wu Di even tumbled onto his rear.

Li Xuanba grabbed Wu Di's wing and hauled him upright. "I asked you to land on my arm! What are you doing landing on the ground?"

Han Gou and Wu Di glanced at the thin silk sleeves covering Li Xuanba's arms.

Li Xuanba said, "If you're careful, you won't scratch me."

Han Gou and Wu Di answered him with their eyes: *It's less trouble to land on the ground—no need to control our force.*

"Why did you hover up there so long before coming down?" Li Xuanba rubbed the heads of the two eagles. "Wait, why did both of you come?"

The two eagles gestured simultaneously with their wings.

Li Xuanba sighed. "Stop gesturing, I know it was Second Brother's idea."

Yuwen Zhu giggled. "They probably wanted to see how long it would take for you to notice them."

Li Xuanba: "...Pointless."

Han Gou and Wu Di: *"Chirp chirp chirp!"*

Li Xuanba squatted down. "Lift your feet. Let me see what extra secret message Second Brother sent."

Yuwen Zhu did not step away, poking her head forward out of curiosity.

Tied to Han Gou's leg was a letter; tied to Wu Di's leg was only a small parcel.

Li Xuanba opened the parcel first, revealing exquisite Tujue gold ornaments inside.

Li Xuanba said in bewilderment, "Did Second Brother go off and rob a merchant caravan? Zhuniang, Second Brother sent these for you."

Yuwen Zhu accepted them with a bright smile.

Li Xuanba then unsealed the letter, his eyes widening in astonishment.

Spotting the three characters for "Liu Wenjing" on the paper, Yuwen Zhu covered her mouth in shock. "Elder Brother is truly..."

"Truly formidable," Li Xuanba said with a smile. "No matter how many people he has recruited into his estate right now, none of them can compare to this single name."

Taiyuan Commandery was governed from Jinyang, and Liu Wenjing was currently the Magistrate of Jinyang County.

In the original timeline, Liu Wenjing could be considered Li Yuan's primary right-hand man when planning the uprising. In terms of impact, calling him the second-in-command outside the Duke of Tang's family was no exaggeration.

Although Li Xuanba knew Liu Wenjing would pledge allegiance to Second Brother sooner or later, he had never anticipated it happening at such an early stage.

With Liu Wenjing present, even if he and Second Brother traveled far away to Zhangye in the future, they would not need to worry about their father's military affairs back home.

After the initial surge of joy, Li Xuanba calmed down.

"It's too early," Li Xuanba sighed.

Yuwen Zhu asked in confusion, "Isn't earlier better?"

Li Xuanba said, "It is wonderful for Second Brother, but dangerous for Liu Wenjing. Liu Wenjing is Father's subordinate. How could it make sense for him to pledge loyalty to Father's son immediately upon meeting him?"

Yuwen Zhu asked, "Are you worried that Liu Wenjing's allegiance is a fake test?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "It is hard to determine true from false. If it's real, then Liu Wenjing's personality is far too reckless, and he will eventually invite disaster upon himself. If it's a test, it means Father already harbors wariness toward Second Brother. Neither outcome is good."

Considering the historical records regarding Liu Wenjing, Li Xuanba leaned toward the former.

In the original timeline, when Li Yuan executed Liu Wenjing, some claimed it was simply a case of "slaughtering the hounds once the hares are dead," while others argued it was Li Yuan's warning to Li Shimin.

Many historians and history enthusiasts had analyzed this event. The prevailing theory, based on the timing of Liu Wenjing's execution and surrounding events, was that his death was indeed connected to his alignment with Li Shimin, but the person Li Yuan sought to admonish was not Li Shimin himself.

This seemed contradictory at first glance, but it wasn't. Li Yuan had not yet grown excessively wary of Li Shimin at that point. Leaving aside senior senility or ruthless purge of meritorious officials, from the perspective of a normal emperor, Li Yuan killed Liu Wenjing because Liu Wenjing had bypassed him to serve his son, attempting to meddle in the struggle for succession.

It had nothing to do with *who* Liu Wenjing supported; it was about the act of *engaging in the succession struggle* itself. Li Yuan used the execution of Liu Wenjing—a key pillar of the Taiyuan uprising—to intimidate other restless ministers and suppress the nascent succession disputes brewing in court.

Simply put, Liu Wenjing was supposed to be Li Yuan's right hand, yet he turned to Li Yuan's son. To Li Yuan, that was a monstrous betrayal.

In fact, countless trusted officials around Li Yuan eventually aligned themselves with Prince of Qin Li Shimin. Li Yuan hadn't purged them simply because he hadn't noticed. Liu Wenjing, perhaps relying too heavily on his great achievements, had been exceptionally reckless, flashy, and clumsy at hiding his ties, allowing Li Yuan to catch him and make an example of him to warn the rest.

Yet while Li Yuan believed he was "killing the chicken to scare the monkeys," the actual result was chilling the hearts of his loyal veterans, driving them to align even closer with Prince of Qin Li Shimin.

Liu Wenjing's death wouldn't negatively impact Second Brother's ascension to the throne, but it was a tragic waste for such a talented man to die so wrongfully.

Li Xuanba shook his head, sighing in a low mutter, "What can I do about it anyway? Can I change Liu Wenjing's personality?"

Yuwen Zhu asked in confusion, "Sanlang, what are you saying? Change whose personality?"

Li Xuanba said, "I suspect Liu Wenjing isn't a ploy by Father, but rather that he's just too reckless himself. Sigh, if Father discovers this, he'll be in grave danger."

Yuwen Zhu thought for a moment and said, "Since you're worried, Sanlang, why not have Elder Brother speak directly with Liu Wenjing and advise him to be cautious and discreet? Wouldn't that work?"

Li Xuanba froze.

Yuwen Zhu asked shyly, "Is it too naive of me to suggest that?"

Li Xuanba waved his hands hastily. "No, no, no! Zhuniang, your words have awakened the dreamer! Indeed... it really is that simple."

Li Xuanba knocked on his own head. "It seems I've spent too much time overthinking conspiracies, seeing twists and turns in everything. This matter can be handled directly: let Second Brother lay out the dangers of such recklessness to Liu Wenjing. Liu Wenjing is capable enough to serve as Magistrate of Jinyang, after all. If he insists on going his own way even after being cautioned, then he's bringing death upon himself, and we'll have done everything within our power."

Yuwen Zhu let out a breath of relief and smiled. "I'm just glad I could help you, Sanlang."

Li Xuanba declared, "I'll write to Second Brother right away!" *I must praise Zhuniang's brilliance to him!*

Li Xuanba took a few steps toward his study, then turned back to look at the two golden eagles on the ground, a look of realization dawning on his face. "I understand why Second Brother sent both of you over. One eagle to carry my letter back, and one eagle to stay here to protect my safety?"

Han Gou and Wu Di nodded.

Li Xuanba grumbled, "I already told him you aren't needed here in Hedong Commandery—he's the one fighting battles out there who needs you... Oh well. Go grab a good meal, rest for a day, and then send the letter. Which of you is going?"

Han Gou raised his left wing, while Wu Di raised his right wing.

Then the two eagles looked at each other.

*"Chirp chirp chirp!"*

*"Chirp chirp chirp chirp chirp!"*

The two eagles began wrestling and rolling around together.

Yuwen Zhu flustered, waving her arms. "Ah? Don't fight, don't fight! Talk it out nicely! Sanlang, Sanlang! Quick, help me separate them!"

Li Xuanba covered his eyes.

*Did Second Brother really not designate who would fly back in advance? Did he do this on purpose?!*

...

Li Shimin sneezed.

He rubbed his nose and muttered to himself, "The letter should have arrived by now."

*Since I didn't specify who carries the letter back, Han Gou and Wu Di are probably fighting right now, aren't they? Hahaha, Ah Xuan must be having a massive headache.*

Li Yuan carved off a piece of roasted mutton and handed it to Li Shimin. "What is it? Missing Ah Xuan? When you were fighting in Zhangye, weren't you often separated from him as well? Why acting like a clingy child this time?"

Li Shimin took the mutton and grinned. "I've always acted like a child in front of Father."

Li Yuan laughed helplessly. "Yes, yes, yes. Just now, when wiping out the Tujue scouts, you charged so fast I couldn't even call you back! And you still claim you act like a child?"

Li Shimin gave a light chuckle and didn't argue with his father. At the time, he had deduced that a larger main force followed behind the scouts and that intercepting this vanguard team immediately was imperative; hence he acted directly without taking time to request orders.

*Father is great, but having to report and request permission at every turn before acting is annoying—it's so easy to miss tactical opportunities.*

He shifted the subject, saying, "The Eastern Tujue's harassments are becoming increasingly frequent. I fear they are preparing a major move."

Li Yuan replied, "That is for His Majesty to worry about. Our duty is to defend Taiyuan well. When the Eastern Tujue make their move, we need only report it to His Majesty."

"Understood." Li Shimin gnawed on his mutton, saying no more.

He saw clearly through the unspoken meaning behind his father's words.

If the Sui Dynasty plunged deeper into chaos, the father and son both knew tacitly that they would inevitably raise troops to contend for the world.

Father meant that if the Eastern Tujue invaded southward, the Sui Empire would fall into even greater turmoil, which might prove more advantageous for their own uprising. They might even be able to leverage the Eastern Tujue's momentum. Thus, there was no need to report this to the Emperor in advance.

Li Shimin disapproved.

*This is the realm of Huaxia—how could we allow foreign barbarians to run rampant across our lands?*

Persuading his father would be difficult, so he didn't bother opening his mouth. Once he returned to Zhangye, he would take it upon himself to guard against the Eastern Tujue.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第130章 你也是他的主公
chunks.chineseText:
第130章 你也是他的主公

河东薛氏、河东裴氏、河东柳氏一族送出一个人才后， 其他士人就不再观望，纷纷拜访李玄霸、李建成，或者干脆径直前往太原郡。
　　李玄霸暂时闭门谢客， 让李建成接待后续投靠的人， 做出一副退让的态度。
　　他如此谦逊， 让河东士人对其好感更甚。
　　在李玄霸迅速融入河东士族时，李建成心里本来很难受。当李玄霸退让时，李建成才松了口气。
　　同时， 他又将其当做理所当然。
　　因为从小到大都如此，李玄霸做出了成绩，然后将功绩拱手让人， 自己退居其后，不慕名利。
　　身为弟弟， 将光芒让给兄长是理所当然的。
　　李世民对李玄霸时， 肯定也是如此想。
　　“阿嚏！”李世民狠狠打了个喷嚏。
　　他看着前来拜访的四人，疑惑地挠了挠头：“阿玄自己决定就好，还非要我出面下令吗？”
　　裴行俨常年生活在军营，又因为同是朝中高官之子，他说话很直接：“主公只有一个。你也是他的主公。”
　　李世民大大咧咧道：“行吧。看来我要尽快学会如何当个好主公啊。那么接下来该做什么？”
　　柳亨疑惑道：“接下来该做什么不是你来定吗？”
　　李世民笑道：“主公不是做决定的人吗？你们要先提议， 我才能做决定。如果事事都由主公亲力亲为，我麾下这么多贤才猛将不是白来了？”
　　听到李世民此言， 在场几人心中都有熨帖之感。
　　裴行俨道：“我和秦琼现在就想去张掖，李二郎君安排一下？”
　　李世民道：“正好我要送一批文吏过去，裴兄可帮我随行保护？秦叔宝， 你暂时留下， 我回张掖时如果路途不顺， 需要猛将护卫。我也需要先了解你的能力。”
　　秦琼恭敬抱拳：“是， 郎君。”
　　裴行俨指着自己：“我呢？不需要了解？”
　　李世民无奈道：“我能教秦叔宝的事，裴兄自幼就学过了。你又有带兵的经验，现在赶紧去张掖帮忙才是正事。长孙四郎虽然有丈人教导，但他没有经验。罗睺，你和裴兄一起回张掖，暂为裴兄副将，好好辅佐裴兄。”
　　充当李世民近卫的宗罗睺抱拳道：“遵命。”
　　李世民对裴行俨道：“罗睺是我副将，熟悉河右之地情况。请裴兄信任他。”
　　裴行俨没想到自己立刻就被重用，心里倒是有点忐忑了：“还是我为副将吧。不用在意我的出身，我能从小兵做起。”
　　李世民叹气：“不是我在意裴兄出身，实在是张掖缺人。如裴兄这样自幼被父辈教导兵书武艺的人，在我麾下实在是太少。罗睺士信都是天生猛将，需要有人带着教导用兵。裴兄担子很重，拜托了。”
　　李世民作揖。
　　裴行俨压力更大了。但李世民把他架了起来，他又素来自傲，不能说不做，便咬牙答应下来。
　　李世民又对柳亨道：“柳兄请先暂留太原郡，将小五亲事定下后，可否也提前去张掖？”
　　柳亨笑道：“张掖缺少有治理地方经验的官员？”
　　李世民点头：“看来柳兄已经看出来了。我真的是捉襟见肘啊。”
　　柳亨道：“我与裴兄一同去张掖。五郎君的亲事我已经请求长辈操办，郎君不必担心。”
　　李世民道：“那我就放心了。房玄龄和杜克明都是很有才华的君子，柳兄一定能与他们相处愉快。”
　　薛元敬指着自己：“我呢？”
　　李世民开玩笑道：“这要看侄儿擅长什么。”
　　薛元敬：“……”
　　裴行俨朗声失笑。秦琼和宗罗睺努力绷紧脸。
　　薛元敬幽怨道：“虽然二郎君和我叔叔是好友，但请各论各的，别占我便宜。”
　　李世民诚恳道：“薛伯褒爱护你，我是他兄弟，我自然也视你如最亲近的子侄。你说吧，你想做什么。”
　　薛元敬：“我现在就回河东郡，再见。”
　　柳亨也忍不下去了，转身肩膀颤抖。
　　李世民伸手勾住薛元敬的脖子，挤眉弄眼：“上了我这条船还想下来？你做什么梦？”
　　薛元敬嫌弃地瞥李世民。
　　李世民笑道：“伯褒说你文学天赋比他还强一丝，其实你在阿玄身边帮忙才最好。不过阿玄让你过来，自然有他的道理。我猜不到，你能猜到吗？”
　　薛元敬想了想，道：“或许郎君有需要我执笔的地方？”
　　李世民眼睛一亮：“对啊，以后我的文书就全部交给你代笔了。”
　　现在打完仗，李世民还要俯首案前自己整理文书。
　　打仗不是打完就算了事，后勤和作战方方面面都需要留下文书痕迹，以便管理和复查。如果文书混乱就等于后勤混乱，作战指令混乱。
　　以前李世民全部自己完成，偶尔李玄霸空下来帮他分担一二。虽然房乔和杜如晦到来后帮了一些忙，但他们有更重要的工作。他都忘记这些事应该有专门信任的文吏来做。
　　李世民唏嘘道：“阿玄老抱怨我这里是草台班子。你们来了，我这里终于不是草台班子了。”
　　虽然几人没听过“草台班子”这个词，但从字面就能猜出一二意思。
　　裴行俨笑道：“别抱怨了。你才十六岁便有如此成就，还有什么可抱怨的？”
　　李世民故作哀怨道：“正因为我十六岁就有如此成就，我才抱怨啊。很显然，我付出的努力和遭遇的困难都比常人多。”
　　几人看着李世民这不要脸的模样，都忍俊不禁。
　　秦琼真的不想笑，但也没忍住。
　　他看向旁边笑得很开心的宗罗睺。
　　宗罗睺笑道：“主公就是这样，你随意笑，他不会生气。他说这话就是想逗笑我们。”
　　秦琼：“……”真古怪的人，但感觉不坏。
　　李世民和几人插科打诨，迅速拉近了距离后，问起了李玄霸和河东郡的事。
　　得知李玄霸闭门谢客，将风头让给李建成后，李世民脸上的笑容带了一丝嘲讽的意味：“阿玄自幼就谦让大兄。我猜大兄肯定没有感谢阿玄，只当这都是理所当然。哼，我看河东郡也张罗得差不多了，阿玄该回来了。若不回来，大兄说不定会强行让阿玄待客。”
　　李玄霸每逢换季必定会病一阵子，眼见着快到七月流火，李世民很是心焦。
　　虽然弟弟现在身边有弟媳照顾，但李世民仍旧很不放心。
　　薛元敬安慰道：“三郎君身体看上去很健康，郎君请放心。如果有事，河东与太原不到五百千里，快马加鞭两三日信件就能到达。”
　　李世民道：“也是。”寒钩和乌镝的信这么还没到？它们不会赖在阿玄那里不肯走了吧？
　　李世民正心焦，寒钩终于回来。
　　它一回来就“啾啾”尖叫，信件刚取走就在地上打滚，李世民还以为自己看错雕，是乌镝回来了。
　　他一边安抚寒钩一边看信。
　　心有灵犀，李玄霸的信开篇就提了乌镝和寒钩都不想送信的事。
　　“我让乌镝和寒钩比赛，谁先把吊在树上的肉取回来，谁就留在河东郡。谁知道乌镝居然在爪子上抓了一把土洒向寒钩，成功先飞一步……天啦，谁教的它的？是不是你？！”
　　李世民摸了摸鼻子。嗯，没错，是我。
　　他对躺在地上的寒钩道：“我都和你说了，战胜敌人要无所不用其极。既然你和乌镝要比试，就要把它视作敌人。现在吃亏了吧？”
　　寒钩翻身，用雕屁股对着李世民。
　　李世民失笑，继续看信。
　　打趣了几句雕崽后，李玄霸又说自己身体不错，让李世民别担心，才谈起正事。
　　李玄霸着重提了此次前来投效几人的能力，让李世民心中有数。
　　他特别提起让李世民叮嘱刘文静，并炫耀这是宇文珠提醒他的。
　　李世民将信反复看了几遍，把信中内容都背下后，才将信纸烧掉。
　　“要装病避开风头吗？希望李建成识趣些。”李世民按了一下身边雕崽的后脑勺，“帮我送信，这次争取让乌镝送信，你留下。”
　　寒钩用翅膀撑着身体，从地上爬起来站好：“啾啾！”
　　李世民失笑：“好气势！”
　　……
　　寒钩再次回到河东郡的时候，李玄霸正应付完李建成的宴会。
　　正如李世民所料，李玄霸闭门谢客几日后，李建成就成为唯一一个能让李玄霸赴宴的人。
　　李玄霸不能不给兄长面子，便隔三岔五去一次。
　　反正他只是在角落里默默看着主宾喝酒跳舞，除了无聊点，其他没什么。
　　至于有人想要“挑衅”自己，在自己面前展露才华，甚至想踩着自己上位，李玄霸就只能拿出文抄公的本事把这些真正的人才压下去了。
　　真的很对不起这些人才，他没有道德。
　　李建成和李玄霸仿佛回到了李玄霸小时候，年长的大兄领着友人们来炫耀自己聪慧的弟弟。
　　李世民多次请求李渊，希望能让李玄霸回到太原郡。
　　但李渊犹豫之后，还是让李玄霸继续留在河东郡。
　　他知道现在李建成虽然门庭若市，但若没有李玄霸的帮衬，恐怕还是难以笼络河东英俊。
　　李渊对李世民道：“大德明年开春就会和你一同回张掖，现在在河东多结识贤才，对他也很有好处。太原有你结交贤才，河东有大德结交贤才，山西河东的贤才才能尽入我们囊中。”
　　李世民道：“但我担心阿玄身体。每逢换季，他一定会生病。”
　　李渊安慰道：“他已经成亲。珠娘是很有本事的医师，已经被河东郡士女奉为座上宾。你又不会医术，阿玄生病你也只是干着急。再者河东气候比太原温和，正因阿玄体弱，才更该待在河东。”
　　李世民听了李渊的话后，勉强被说服了。
　　确实河东郡气候比太原郡稍温和，换季时，阿玄在河东郡养病或许更合适。
　　李世民道：“那阿玄不回来，我去河东！”
　　李渊一巴掌拍二儿子后脑勺，哭笑不得：“你和大德都长大了，怎么还如此黏糊？他才刚成亲，该和妻子培养感情。你乖乖留在太原，耶耶这里离不开你。”
　　李渊看见二儿子的交友能力叹为观止。自己求不来的人才，二儿子去一趟，别人就愿意和二儿子结为忘年交。
　　自家二儿子自幼讨人喜欢，与人结交的天赋就像是吃饭喝水般的本能。
　　再加上李世民打仗天赋和经验都很出色，省了李渊许多事，让李渊可以将更多注意力放在经营太原上，出兵就交给李世民。
　　李渊好不容易轻松了一点。半年后李世民和李玄霸就要回张掖了，在儿子们回张掖前，他得在李世民和李玄霸的帮助下，把山西河东全部掌控。
　　如果不是舍不得河右之地已经打下的根基，李渊真想让李世民和李玄霸留下来，给自己当左臂右膀。
　　于是换季时，李玄霸就在河东郡养病了。
　　李建成带着新结识的友人来探望了李玄霸几次，宇文珠忍无可忍，当着李建成友人的面请求李建成不要再来打扰李玄霸养病。
　　“郎君担心影响兄弟感情，妇人来做这个恶人。”宇文珠道，“我们已经委婉说过很多次，郎君需要静养，他必须静养！”
　　宇文珠低声啜泣，宾客们纷纷掩面愧走。
　　李建成脸面无光，再也不上李玄霸的门。
　　李玄霸昏睡一日后，得知宇文珠把李建成和宾客赶了出去，愧疚道：“是我无能，该我出面把大兄送走，他现在一定怨了你。”
　　宇文珠没好气道：“让他怨！我真是服了，我们委婉拒绝了多少次，他就仗着自己上门我们不好意思赶他出门，非要一次又一次地打扰你。他如果像兄公那样，能照顾生病的你，他每日都住在这里，我还高兴呢！”
　　宇文珠真是烦透了。你带一群人来嘘寒问暖，连郎君睡下了都要把人叫醒“问候”，这不是故意折腾人吗！
　　李玄霸看着宇文珠气红的脸，笑道：“他小时候学到的探病就是这个探法。他习惯了，我也习惯了。倒是忘记我现在已经有底气拒绝他的探病了。”
　　宇文珠心头酸涩：“三郎辛苦了。”
　　李玄霸闭上眼：“有你护着，怎么会辛苦了。珠娘才辛苦了。”
　　宇文珠将手放在李玄霸眼睛上：“快睡吧，我一直在这里。”
　　“嗯。”李玄霸任由自己意识沉入睡眠中。
　　他终于可以好好休息，睡个好觉。
　　李玄霸没有告诉李世民他生病了。
　　在他生病的时候，天下大势突然急速变化。
　　太子杨暕谋逆逼宫，被皇帝制服。
　　皇帝要处死太子，天下有识之士皆为太子喊冤。
　　皇帝震怒，牵连下狱者超过百人。
chunks.englishText:
After the Hedong Xue, Hedong Pei, and Hedong Liu clans each presented a talent, the remaining scholars and gentry stopped sitting on the fence. They flocked to visit Li Xuanba and Li Jiancheng, or simply headed straight for Taiyuan Commandery.

Li Xuanba temporarily closed his doors to visitors, leaving Li Jiancheng to receive the subsequent defectors and talents, deliberately striking an attitude of deferential retreat.

His humility only endeared him all the more to the scholars of Hedong.

When Li Xuanba had swiftly integrated into the elite circles of the Hedong gentry, Li Jiancheng had felt deeply uneasy. Only when Li Xuanba stepped back did Li Jiancheng finally breathe a sigh of relief.

At the same time, he took it completely for granted.

For it had always been this way since childhood—Li Xuanba would accomplish great things, hand the credit over on a silver platter, and step into the background, indifferent to fame and fortune.

As a younger brother, yielding the spotlight to his elder brother was only proper.

He was certain Li Shimin thought the exact same way regarding Li Xuanba.

"Achoo!" Li Shimin sneezed loudly.

Looking at the four men who had come to visit him, he scratched his head in confusion. "Ah-Xuan could have just decided this himself. Was it really necessary for me to step forward and issue an order?"

Having spent years in military camps, and being the son of a high official himself, Pei Xingyan spoke directly: "There is only one lord. You are his lord as well."

Li Shimin said casually, "Fair enough. It seems I must learn how to be a good lord as quickly as possible. So, what should we do next?"

Liu Heng asked, puzzled, "Isn't deciding what to do next supposed to be your job?"

Li Shimin laughed. "Isn't a lord simply the one who makes the final decision? You all must propose ideas first before I can decide. If a lord had to do everything himself, wouldn't all the capable talents and fierce generals under my command be here for nothing?"

Hearing Li Shimin's words, a warm sense of appreciation washed over everyone present.

Pei Xingyan said, "Qin Qiong and I want to head to Zhangye right now. Could Second Young Master Li make the arrangements?"

Li Shimin replied, "As it happens, I am about to send a group of scribes and clerks over. Brother Pei, could you accompany and protect them for me? Qin Shubao, you will stay behind for now. If the journey is treacherous when I return to Zhangye, I will need a formidable warrior to guard me. Besides, I need to get to know your capabilities first."

Qin Qiong cupped his fists respectfully. "Understood, Young Master."

Pei Xingyan pointed at himself. "What about me? You don't need to get to know my capabilities?"

Li Shimin said helplessly, "The things I can teach Qin Shubao are things you have studied since childhood, Brother Pei. Plus, you already have experience leading troops, so getting you to Zhangye to help out right away is what's most urgent. Although Fourth Young Master Zhangsun has his father-in-law's guidance, he lacks practical experience. Luohou, return to Zhangye with Brother Pei and serve temporarily as his deputy general to assist him properly."

Zong Luohou, who served as Li Shimin's personal guard, cupped his fists. "Understood!"

Li Shimin said to Pei Xingyan, "Luohou is my deputy general and is well-acquainted with the situation in Heyou. Please trust him, Brother Pei."

Pei Xingyan hadn't expected to be entrusted with such heavy responsibility right away, which made him feel a bit apprehensive. "Perhaps I should be the deputy general instead. Don't worry about my background; I can start as a common soldier."

Li Shimin sighed. "It's not that I'm focusing on your background, Brother Pei; it's simply that Zhangye is severely lacking in talent. People like you, who have been trained in military tactics and martial arts by their elders since childhood, are far too rare under my command. Luohou and Shixin are both natural born fiercely valiant generals, but they need someone to guide them in command strategy. Yours is a heavy burden, Brother Pei. I am entrusting this to you."

Li Shimin bowed deeply with cupped hands.

The pressure on Pei Xingyan grew even heavier. But Li Shimin had put him on a pedestal, and being a naturally proud man, he couldn't bring himself to decline, so he gritted his teeth and accepted.

Li Shimin then said to Liu Heng, "Brother Liu, please stay in Taiyuan Commandery for the time being. Once Little Fifth's marriage proposal is settled, could you also head to Zhangye ahead of schedule?"

Liu Heng smiled. "Does Zhangye lack officials with experience in local administration?"

Li Shimin nodded. "It seems Brother Liu has already figured it out. I truly am stretched thin."

Liu Heng said, "I shall go to Zhangye together with Brother Pei. I have already requested my elders to handle Fifth Young Master's marriage, so you need not worry, Young Master."

Li Shimin said, "Then I can rest easy. Fang Xuanling and Du Keming are both exceptionally talented gentlemen; I am sure you will get along wonderfully with them, Brother Liu."

Xue Yuanjing pointed at himself. "What about me?"

Li Shimin joked, "That depends on what my nephew is good at."

Xue Yuanjing: "..."

Pei Xingyan burst out laughing, while Qin Qiong and Zong Luohou struggled to keep straight faces.

Xue Yuanjing said aggrievedly, "Although Second Young Master is good friends with my uncle, let's keep our generations separate, please. Don't take advantage of me."

Li Shimin said earnestly, "Xue Bobao cares deeply for you, and as his brother, I naturally view you as my closest nephew. Speak up—what is it you wish to do?"

Xue Yuanjing said, "I'm heading back to Hedong Commandery right now. Goodbye."

Liu Heng couldn't hold it in any longer either, turning away as his shoulders shook with laughter.

Li Shimin threw an arm around Xue Yuanjing's neck, winking at him. "Now that you're on my boat, you think you can just step off? What kind of dream are you having?"

Xue Yuanjing gave Li Shimin a look of utter disdain.

Li Shimin chuckled. "Bobao mentioned that your literary talent is a hair superior even to his own. Truth be told, it would be best for you to assist Ah-Xuan. But since Ah-Xuan sent you here, he must have his reasons. I can't guess them—can you?"

Xue Yuanjing pondered for a moment and said, "Perhaps Young Master has need of someone to handle writing and official correspondence?"

Li Shimin's eyes lit up. "Exactly! From now on, all my official documents and correspondence are handed over to you!"

Currently, even after finishing a battle, Li Shimin still had to hunch over his desk to organize documents himself.

Warfare was not over simply because the fighting stopped; logistics and every aspect of combat operations required written records for management and review. Disorganized paperwork meant chaotic logistics and confused military commands.

Previously, Li Shimin had handled everything on his own, with Li Xuanba occasionally helping out whenever he was free. Although Fang Qiao and Du Ruhui had eased his burden after their arrival, they had far more vital responsibilities. He had almost forgotten that such tasks were meant to be handled by trusted, dedicated scribes.

Li Shimin sighed wistfully. "Ah-Xuan always complains that my operation is just a slapdash, ragtag crew. Now that you've all arrived, it's finally not just an amateur setup anymore."

Although the others had never heard the phrase "slapdash crew," they could guess its approximate meaning from the words.

Pei Xingyan laughed. "Stop complaining. You're only sixteen and have already achieved all this—what could you possibly have to complain about?"

Li Shimin feigned grief. "Precisely because I have achieved so much at just sixteen, that's why I'm complaining! Obviously, the effort I've put in and the hardships I've faced are far greater than those of ordinary men."

Looking at Li Shimin's shamelessly boastful manner, none of them could help laughing.

Qin Qiong really hadn't intended to laugh, but he couldn't hold it back either.

He looked over at Zong Luohou, who was laughing heartily beside him.

Zong Luohou grinned. "My Lord is just like this. Laugh all you want, he won't take offense. He only says these things to amuse us."

Qin Qiong: "..." *What an eccentric man, though he doesn't seem bad at all.*

After cracking jokes and banter to quickly break the ice, Li Shimin asked about Li Xuanba and the situation in Hedong Commandery.

Upon learning that Li Xuanba had shut his doors to guests and yielded all the spotlight to Li Jiancheng, a trace of mockery touched the smile on Li Shimin's face. "Ah-Xuan has deferred to Eldest Brother ever since we were children. I wager Eldest Brother didn't feel a shred of gratitude toward Ah-Xuan and took it all for granted. Hmph, I see that things in Hedong Commandery are nearly settled anyway; it's high time Ah-Xuan returned. If he doesn't, Eldest Brother might try to force him to entertain guests."

Li Xuanba inevitably fell ill during seasonal transitions, and with the cooler autumn weather approaching in the seventh month, Li Shimin felt extremely anxious.

Although his younger brother was now looked after by his sister-in-law, Li Shimin remained ill at ease.

Xue Yuanjing offered comforting words: "Third Young Master appeared to be in good health, so please rest assured, Young Master. If anything happens, Hedong is less than five hundred li from Taiyuan—a fast rider can deliver a letter in just two or three days."

Li Shimin said, "True enough." *Why haven't the letters carried by Hangou and Wudi arrived yet? Could those eagles be lounging at Ah-Xuan's place, refusing to leave?*

Just as Li Shimin was fretting, Hangou finally returned.

As soon as it arrived, it squeaked and shrieked "Chirp, chirp!", rolling around on the ground the moment the letter was taken from it. Li Shimin almost thought he had misidentified the eagle and that Wudi had returned instead.

He coaxed and stroked Hangou while opening the letter to read.

As if connected by telepathy, the opening line of Li Xuanba's letter mentioned that both Wudi and Hangou had been unwilling to deliver the letter.

*"I held a contest between Wudi and Hangou: whichever bird brought back the meat hanging from the tree first got to stay in Hedong Commandery. Who knew Wudi would grab a handful of dirt in its talons and throw it right at Hangou, allowing it to take off first... Good heavens, who taught it such dirty tricks? Was it you?!"*

Li Shimin rubbed his nose. *Ahem, yes, indeed, it was me.*

He said to Hangou, who was lying on the ground, "I told you before that to defeat an enemy, you must leave no stone unturned and use any means necessary. Since you were competing with Wudi, you should have treated it as the enemy. Now look at you, taking the loss!"

Hangou flipped over, presenting its eagle rump straight at Li Shimin.

Li Shimin chuckled and turned his attention back to the letter.

After poking fun at the eagle chick for a few lines, Li Xuanba reassured Li Shimin that his health was fine and told him not to worry before moving on to official business.

Li Xuanba emphasized the capabilities of the several talents who had come to offer their allegiance, ensuring Li Shimin had a clear picture of what each man could do.

He made a special note for Li Shimin to give a word of caution to Liu Wenjing, even boasting that Yuwen Zhu had been the one to remind him of it.

Li Shimin read the letter several times until he had committed its contents to memory, only then burning the parchment to ashes.

"Feigning illness to dodge the spotlight? I hope Li Jiancheng knows what's good for him." Li Shimin patted the back of the eagle chick's head. "Deliver a letter for me. Try to get Wudi to be the messenger next time so you can stay."

Hangou pushed itself off the ground with its wings and stood tall, letting out a sharp, enthusiastic "Chirp, chirp!"

Li Shimin laughed. "That's the spirit!"

……

By the time Hangou returned to Hedong Commandery once again, Li Xuanba had just finished dealing with one of Li Jiancheng's banquets.

Exactly as Li Shimin had predicted, after Li Xuanba had shut his doors to guests for a few days, Li Jiancheng became the only person who could successfully invite Li Xuanba to a banquet.

Unable to refuse his elder brother's requests without causing offense, Li Xuanba attended every few days.

In any case, he merely sat quietly in a corner watching the host and guests drink and dance. Apart from being somewhat dull, it was harmless enough.

As for those who attempted to "challenge" him, show off their literary brilliance in his presence, or even step on his reputation to advance themselves, Li Xuanba had no choice but to pull out his stolen classic poetry skills to crush these genuine talents into submission.

He truly felt sorry for those talented scholars—he possessed no literary morality whatsoever.

Li Jiancheng and Li Xuanba seemed to have reverted to the days of Li Xuanba's childhood, when the elder brother would lead his friends around to show off his prodigiously intelligent younger brother.

Li Shimin repeatedly petitioned Li Yuan, hoping to bring Li Xuanba back to Taiyuan Commandery.

But after some hesitation, Li Yuan decided to let Li Xuanba remain in Hedong Commandery.

He knew that although Li Jiancheng's doorway was currently crowded with visitors, without Li Xuanba's support, he would likely still struggle to win over the elite talents of Hedong.

Li Yuan said to Li Shimin, "Dade will return to Zhangye with you next spring. Meeting more talented men in Hedong right now will be of great benefit to him as well. With you recruiting talents in Taiyuan and Dade gathering talents in Hedong, the gifted minds of Shanxi and Hedong can all be brought under our wing."

Li Shimin said, "But I am worried about Ah-Xuan's health. Whenever the seasons change, he inevitably falls ill."

Li Yuan comforted him, "He is already married. Zhu-niang is a highly skilled physician who is now revered as an honored guest among the noble ladies of Hedong. You don't know medicine anyway; if Ah-Xuan falls ill, you'll only worry uselessly. Furthermore, the climate of Hedong is milder than Taiyuan's. Precisely because of Ah-Xuan's frail constitution, he ought to stay in Hedong all the more."

Hearing Li Yuan's reasoning, Li Shimin was grudgingly persuaded.

Indeed, the climate in Hedong Commandery was somewhat gentler than in Taiyuan Commandery. When seasons shifted, recuperating in Hedong might indeed be better for Ah-Xuan.

Li Shimin declared, "If Ah-Xuan won't come back, then I'll go to Hedong!"

Li Yuan slapped his second son on the back of the head, caught between tears and laughter. "Both you and Dade are grown men! Why are you still so clingy? He just got married and needs to cultivate his bond with his wife. Stay put in Taiyuan—your father can't spare you here."

Li Yuan was filled with marvel whenever he observed his second son's uncanny ability to make friends. Talents that Li Yuan could never win over himself would readily form deep, lifelong friendships across generations after a single meeting with Li Shimin.

His second son had been beloved by everyone since childhood; his knack for forming bonds with people was as natural as breathing.

Combined with Li Shimin's brilliant military talent and seasoned combat experience, he saved Li Yuan immense effort, allowing Li Yuan to focus on administering Taiyuan while leaving troop deployments to Li Shimin.

Li Yuan had finally caught a breather. Half a year from now, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba would return to Zhangye; before his sons left, he needed to secure total control over Shanxi and Hedong with their assistance.

Were it not for his reluctance to abandon the solid foundation they had already established in Heyou, Li Yuan truly would have loved to keep Li Shimin and Li Xuanba by his side to serve as his right and left hands.

And so, as the seasons shifted, Li Xuanba nursed his illness in Hedong Commandery.

Li Jiancheng brought his newly acquired friends to visit Li Xuanba several times until Yuwen Zhu, unable to bear it any longer, publicly begged Li Jiancheng in front of his guests to stop disturbing Li Xuanba's recovery.

"My lord worries about damaging brotherly affection, so I shall play the villain," Yuwen Zhu declared. "We have politely stated many times that my lord needs quiet rest. He *must* have quiet rest!"

Yuwen Zhu sobbed softly, causing the guests to cover their faces in shame and beat a hasty retreat.

His pride utterly disgraced, Li Jiancheng never set foot in Li Xuanba's house again.

After sleeping fitfully for a whole day, Li Xuanba learned that Yuwen Zhu had driven Li Jiancheng and his guests out. He said guiltily, "It was my own weakness. I should have stepped forward to send Eldest Brother away. He must resent you now."

Yuwen Zhu snapped crossly, "Let him resent me! I'm thoroughly sick of it. No matter how many times we politely declined, he just took advantage of the fact that we were too courteous to throw him out, intruding upon your rest time after time! If he were like Second Brother, capable of taking proper care of you while sick, I would be delighted even if he stayed here every single day!"

Yuwen Zhu was utterly exasperated. Bringing a crowd of people to spout empty pleasantries and even waking her husband up from sleep just to "check on him"—wasn't that pure torment?!

Looking at Yuwen Zhu's flushed, angry face, Li Xuanba smiled. "That was how he learned to visit sick people when he was a child. He's used to it, and I used to be used to it too. I simply forgot that I now have the standing and confidence to refuse his visits."

Yuwen Zhu felt a twinge of sorrow in her heart. "San-lang, you've suffered so much."

Li Xuanba closed his eyes. "With you protecting me, how could I suffer? It is Zhu-niang who has worked hard."

Yuwen Zhu gently placed her hand over Li Xuanba's eyes. "Go to sleep. I'll stay right here."

"Mm." Li Xuanba allowed his consciousness to sink into sleep.

He could finally rest properly and enjoy a good sleep.

Li Xuanba did not tell Li Shimin about his illness.

While he lay ill, the geopolitical tides of the empire underwent a sudden and drastic shift.

Crown Prince Yang Jian attempted a treasonous palace coup, only to be subdued by the Emperor.

The Emperor intended to execute the Crown Prince, sparking outcries of innocence for the Prince from insightful men across the realm.

Furious, the Emperor launched a bloody purge, imprisoning over a hundred people in connection to the case.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第131章 始作俑者无后乎
chunks.chineseText:
第131章 始作俑者无后乎

隋大业十年， 杨广不顾天下已经大乱，再次亲征高丽。
　　当杨广来到涿郡时，一路上役夫和兵卒不断逃亡。
　　他将抓来的逃卒全部斩杀， 以肉做祭祀， 以血涂祭鼓， 用他们的命祭祀黄帝。
　　大隋无数熟读经史子集的人站在祭台下，看着这血腥的一幕。
　　他们脑海里浮现出孔子的一句话。
　　“始作俑者，其无后乎。”
　　西周时已经抛弃了人祭的野蛮习俗。春秋开端时各国君王为了攀比， 先是厚葬，后来做人俑，再后来人祭之风复苏。
　　孔子站在这个节点上， 敏锐地察觉了社会风气的变化。
　　现在就将原本的草狗祭品换做了人俑，将来这些人还会做什么事？岂不是恢复活人祭祀了？
　　所以孔子才说出了这句话。
　　魏晋南北朝是乱世， 你杀我我杀你天下无人不杀红了眼， 血腥事不罕见。
　　但纯粹的杀戮和人祭却是两回事。
　　杀戮是野蛮，祭祀却是“礼”。荒诞的君王很多，但以人祭祭祀上古贤王者……
　　杨暕心中也浮现出这句话，“始作俑者，其无后乎”。
　　而现在站在祭台上的皇帝后人是谁？他自嘲的想。
　　荒诞的人祭结束。满朝群臣已经习惯捂住眼睛耳朵和嘴巴， 他们不会对杨广有任何谏言。
　　血腥的人祭或许会成为史书上被人翻过就忘的寥寥几笔记载，在这时， 大隋皇帝做的荒唐事已经够多了，不差这一点，竟没有引起道貌岸然的士人口诛笔伐。
　　时间一个月一个月的过去， 虽然杨广征召的士兵多逃逸， 但大隋余威还在， 他们的职业军人尚且能打。
　　高丽在大隋连翻打击下， 这次又没有在杨广二征高丽时得到大隋丢下的辎重回血，仅仅是来护儿率领的水军就把他们打得溃不成军。
　　杨广十分高兴。
　　他一生中唯一的耻辱就要洗刷干净了。
　　杨广大摆宴会，让使者做好了受降的准备。
　　他连邀请西域诸国和东西突厥可汗的使臣团都备好了。
　　在杨广的心中，一切都好起来了。只要高丽王投降，他还是那个伟大的千古一帝，将重现万国来朝。
　　而这时，农民起义军趁着大隋中央的军队都在高丽，燃起的火焰越来越大。
　　杨玄感经过隋朝军队连番打击遁入深山，这次也趁机出山，有东山再起之势。
　　边疆也乱了起来。
　　扶风起义军首领唐弼立了个不知名人士李弘芝为天子，聚集了十万乱民，自封唐王。
　　同一时间，天下农民起义军首领纷纷称王。
　　后世演义中的“十八路反王”纷纷出现，数量远远高于十八路。
　　杨广仍旧闭目塞耳，在歌舞中做着千古一帝的美梦。
　　直到杨暕提剑走进他正在享乐的宫殿。
　　杨广看着杨暕冷笑，神情十分镇定：“你以为朕不知道你要谋反吗？”
　　杨暕缓步走上前，刀斧手从两边帷幕中悄然走出。
　　他目不斜视地看着台上冷静自若的父皇：“我身边只剩下老弱，本就不可能逼宫。我知道是你故意授意身边护卫，让他们配合我行事。”
　　杨广皱眉。
　　一切计划都按照他的预想进行。他想的果然没错，这个儿子就是想谋反。
　　群臣都没发现，都被杨暕的表象蒙蔽。他发现了，他是正确的。
　　但杨暕不仅没有惶恐害怕，还一副仿佛一切也在自己预料中的淡然表情，让杨广心里分外愤怒。
　　在杨广的打量中，杨暕卸下盔甲跪在地上。
　　他将长剑拔出，平放在腿上：“儿此番前来不是逼宫，而是兵谏。”
　　年轻的太子抬起头，神情一如既往的倨傲。
　　“如果不兵谏，父亲听不进去。”
　　“父亲，睁开眼睛吧！天下已经大乱了！大隋已经濒临灭亡了！”
　　“自你一征高丽时谋反的民贼，没有一支被剿灭！”
　　“西域原本臣服的诸国已经纷纷倒向突厥。东突厥已经集结雄师百万，对中原虎视眈眈！”
　　“父亲你在二征高丽时当做的心腹大患杨玄感，现在也还没死！”
　　“秦亡的钟声来自于陈胜吴广民贼！汉亡的钟声来自于黄巾民贼！现在隋亡的钟声，父亲你掩住耳朵当做听不到，它的声音只会越来越大！”
　　“求父亲收兵回西都，平定叛乱，轻徭薄赋，与民休息！”
　　杨暕怀抱长剑叩首不止，额头叩出的血沁入了眼角，泪水与血一同从脸颊滑落。
　　“父亲！你难道想效仿暴秦，二世而亡吗！”
　　“难道你想要当秦二世吗！”
　　杨暕之言，震耳发聩，让台上君臣一时间没有反应过来，居然给了他将话全部说出的机会。
　　公卿身形摇摇欲坠，恨不得晕过去。
　　杨广脸色胀红，双目怒瞪，从坐榻上暴起。
　　他拿起矮桌上果盘狠狠砸向杨暕。
　　杨暕不躲不避，任由果盘砸在头上，鲜血如注。
　　裴蕴见状，忙拉住杨广：“陛下，太子殿下一定是被高丽人巫术魇住了，得了失心疯胡言乱语！请陛下赶紧命人制止住发狂的太子殿下，请巫医诊治驱邪！”
　　杨暕抬起满是鲜血的脸，怒视裴蕴：“诸位公卿，乱世过去不过半百，在你们心中，大概还未认可大隋为主，不在意大隋的基业。大隋乱了之后，正好是你们争夺天下的机会。”
　　“但史笔如刀，昏君身边必有奸臣，如秦二世身边赵高李斯。你们助纣为虐，就不怕遗臭万年吗！！！”
　　裴蕴怒斥道：“太子殿下请慎言，何为‘助纣为虐’？你是在贬低陛下！”
　　杨暕大笑：“大隋都要二世而亡了，何谈贬低？裴大夫，你素来才高，掌握天下户籍。民贼之事，你真的看不见？你扪心自问，是你看不见，还是欺瞒君王，闭目塞听！可还是那句话，史笔如刀，你现在的隐瞒，对后世史书有用吗？”
　　“不说你看不见的未来，就说现在你看的见的现在。如果大隋亡了，天下哪个雄主敢用你这个奸臣？”
　　“无论是谁，必灭你这个奸臣的满门！”
　　“若大隋二世而亡，请裴大夫为大隋陪葬！”
　　杨广怒吼：“够了！太子疯了，杀了他！”
　　刀斧手却犹豫。
　　杨广更加愤怒：“朕的命令，你们听不到吗？！杀了他！”
　　苏威的双手在袖子中握紧又松开。他深吸了一口气，起身跪下道：“陛下圣明，岂能在宫中当众杀子？请陛下将太子下狱，以律法论处。”
　　裴世矩也出列：“臣附议！”
　　宇文述在心中长叹一声，劝慰道：“陛下息怒，今日之事不会传出去。殿下只是疯了，请陛下息事宁人，不要将宫中丑闻外传，有伤陛下颜面。”
　　虞世基道：“陛下，先平息此事最为重要。”
　　他瞪了裴蕴一眼。
　　裴蕴心里十分愤怒，恨不得立刻杀了太子杨暕。
　　但他也知道这时若真的让皇帝当众杀了太子，恐怕自己奸臣的名声就真的要传遍天下，遗臭万年了，只好也跪下道：“请陛下息怒。”
　　杨暕冷笑，还想继续开口。
　　苏威焦急道：“住嘴！还不快把太子殿下的嘴捂住！”
　　刀斧手这才走出，将杨暕压在地上，捂住了他的嘴。
　　出鞘的长剑落在地上，割破了杨暕的脸。
　　他艰难地抬起头，面容更加狰狞：“父亲！记住我的话！永远记住我的话！”
　　裴世矩骂道：“还不快把太子殿下带走！”
　　杨暕被拖走，在地上留下长长的血痕。
　　杨广在宠臣的劝慰下，终于重新坐回了榻上。
　　他扫了在场的人一眼，眼中闪过冷光。
　　苏威、裴世矩、裴蕴、宇文述、虞世基心头一凉。
　　他们可能不会有事，但在场的护卫恐怕全部要被灭口了。
　　但这些护卫都是来自皇帝新招募的骁果军。
　　民乱四起后，皇帝担忧安全，不信任府军，另外开内库招募勇士，建立了只听从皇帝命令的骁果军。
　　骁果军现在已经基本替代了原本卫军，成为皇帝真正的禁卫军。
　　埋伏在宫中的骁果军皆是军中最骁勇善战之人，地位都不低。现在把他们全都杀了，骁果军会不会军心不稳？
　　可他们不敢劝谏。
　　太子兵谏，骂皇帝要效仿秦朝二世而亡。他们自己能听了这话活下来就算陛下开恩，哪还有余力去救别人？
　　最终情况发展如这几个聪明的宠臣所料，杨广以护卫不利为借口，将当时宫中护卫、宫人全部处死。
　　骁果军本以为这是立功的好机会，所以能充当刀斧手的皆是军中有一定地位的小军官。
　　于是军中鹰扬郎将以下的军官被杀戮大半，军中底层将领几乎被清空。
　　此举果然让骁果军人心惶惶。裴世矩请求皇帝奖赏剩余的骁果军，才暂时压住骁果军的士气。
　　杨暕此次兵谏还是起了作用。
　　杨广每日做噩梦，都是杨暕那张满是鲜血的脸。
　　他还重新梦到了杨勇，梦到了自己其他兄弟，梦到了隋文帝怒斥他。
　　杨广醒来后震怒，将太子贬为庶人，还要将他五马分尸。
　　重臣们再次苦劝。
　　有人希望给太子留个体面，毒酒或者白绫赐死；有人认为太子并无谋反之意，流放即可；还有人为太子喊冤，说太子劝谏得对。
　　后者全部被下狱。
　　杨广和疯了似的，要杀光所有为太子说话的大臣。
　　苏威等人只能暂时将杨广杀人的命令按下，等待杨广冷静下来。
　　实在是压不住了，苏威来到狱中，请求杨暕：“太子殿下，我知道你心系大隋，但你现在这样做，不是将大隋推入深渊吗？请太子殿下向陛下求饶，收回前言。陛下与太子殿下父子连心，定不会为难太子殿下。”
　　杨暕坐在地上，形容仿佛乞丐。
　　杨广没有派医师给他治伤，他额头上和脸颊上已经留下狰狞的疤痕，不复原本俊美。
　　“不破不立，如果他能被我说动，只要回关中励精图治，大隋可救。”杨暕淡淡道，“如果他执迷不悟，大隋早几年灭亡和晚几年灭亡有什么区别？仍旧二世而亡尔。不过苏公你来劝我，看来父亲是一点都没有悔改。”
　　苏威不语。
　　杨暕突然失笑，他问道：“苏公，你担心遗臭万年吗？”
　　苏威身形佝偻，掩面而去。
　　杨暕站起来，背着手看着牢狱门外。
　　他笑道：“还知道遮住脸，或许有救。”
　　但苏威可能有救，我大隋还有救吗？
　　李二郎，李三郎，如果大隋亡了，你们会如何？
　　杨暕想起自己那两个才能冠绝天下的表弟。
　　他心中已经预感到了一些事。
　　但他没有被背叛的愤怒。
　　有什么好愤怒的？这大隋亡了，谁当皇帝不是当？
　　他只是悲哀。
　　“兄长，原来我也能成为忧国忧民的太子。”杨暕仰面笑道，泪水从眼角滑落，“这可真的一点都不像我。我本不是这种人，我本做不来这种事。”
　　兄长，你因父亲的错误决定病故的时候，可曾想到这一日？
　　……
　　杨广杀了护卫和宫人，但太子兵谏的事还是传了出去。
　　他怀疑地看着自己的近臣，近臣却以一句苦笑打消了他的疑虑。
　　太子不仅骂杨广有亡国之相，还骂他们是遗臭万年的奸臣。谁愿意传出这样的名声？
　　那么这些话是谁传出去的？
　　难道有人偷听？还是那些被杀的护卫和宫人在死之前对外嚼舌头？或者是太子自己放出去的风声？
　　杨广又开始杀人。
　　太子东宫所有属官都被处死，与太子最亲近的庾俭更是被灭了满门。
　　庾俭在刑场向父亲庾质叩首告别，呜咽连累了庾质时，被庾质斥责。
　　“你做了正确的事，因而招致了灾祸，这怎么能是你的错？”庾质道，“如果你因此后悔，为父才耻于有你这个儿子。”
　　庾俭哭泣道：“儿不悔！”
　　庾质欣慰道：“好。”
　　父子双双赴难，观刑百姓痛哭不止，与行刑兵卒发生冲突，有数十百姓在此冲突中受伤。
　　薛德音站在观刑人群中看着这一幕，趁着混乱花钱托人为庾家人收殓后，回到了涿郡一个小院。
　　在小院内，有个身怀六甲的女子正呆呆地仰望天空。
　　薛德音沉声道：“现在涿郡正混乱，正是我们离开的机会。”
　　女子低头：“太子殿下能活下来吗？”
　　薛德音没有说话。
　　女子道：“我不该问这个问题。对太子殿下而言，活下来才更痛苦。但我必须活下来。”
　　薛德音道：“中原不安全，我们去张掖。李二郎和李三郎都是义气中人，他们一定会帮你隐藏。”
　　女子道：“一切凭公吩咐。”
　　薛德音买通城门卫卒，与女子连夜悄悄离开。
　　出城后，薛德音将马车停下，对着城门叩首。
　　然后他起身，驾起马车，头也不回地离开。
　　……
　　“咳咳咳，兵谏……”李玄霸咳嗽不止。
　　他用手帕捂住嘴，低头看着手帕上的点点血迹，将手帕握紧。
　　宇文珠哭泣道：“三郎，你本就得病，如果心情太过郁卒，恐会伤了心腑。”
　　李玄霸微笑着安慰道：“我知道，我会努力控制。”
　　宇文珠抹干眼泪，笑道：“好。我去给郎君熬药。”
　　她背过身，眼泪又落了下来。
　　郎君说得轻巧，她也劝得轻巧，但人的心情，哪是说控制就能控制得住的？
　　李玄霸目送宇文珠离去，又咳了几声。
　　他靠在床头软垫上，盯着床幔发呆。
　　李玄霸与杨昭、杨暕结识时都没有多少真心。
　　杨昭离世时他虽感伤，但很快就能收拾心情。
　　这位历史中荒唐的齐王兵谏被俘，为何自己心头痛楚和愤怒却难以抑制？
　　李玄霸闭上眼，无论怎么深呼吸，泪水也从眼眶涌出。
　　“隋炀帝，隋炀帝，你怎么能不二世而亡！”
　　他不断深呼吸，胸口起起伏伏，泪水很快覆盖了面容。
　　“咳，咳咳咳……”
　　李玄霸捂着嘴不断咳嗽。
　　宇文珠站在门外，没有进来。
　　乌镝和寒钩收着翅膀站在宇文珠身侧，都低着头一动不动。
　　门中的咳嗽声中渐渐混杂了低沉的呜咽声，而后呜咽声越来越大，变成了咳嗽声一样响亮的失声痛哭。
　　宇文珠转身离开。
　　“乌镝，寒钩，帮我送信。”
　　乌镝和寒钩：“啾！”
　　宇文珠不知道为何三郎非要向兄公隐瞒病情，但她顾不上三郎的心情了。
　　如果、如果三郎真的出事……
　　宇文珠停住脚步，双手捂脸。
　　至少要见最后一面……
　　……
　　“李世民！你要做什么！”李渊拦住晚上偷偷牵马出门的李世民，“我知道你和太子殿下感情深厚，但这件事你绝对不许掺和，你是想我们满门被牵连吗！”
　　李世民道：“我知道我就算去向陛下进谏也没用，我只是想送二表兄最后一程。”
　　李渊对左右人吩咐道：“把他关起来。”
　　李世民焦急道：“父亲！”
　　李渊疲惫道：“我知道你是个重情义的好孩子，但这件事绝对不允许你任性。”
　　李世民跪下请求道：“我真的不会给家里招祸。”
　　李渊道：“陛下已经疯了。你做任何事都可能触怒他。如果你还当我是你的父亲，就听我的话。”
　　李世民哭泣道：“父亲，请不要逼迫我。”
　　李渊俯身将李世民拉起来：“不是我逼迫你，是你不要逼迫我。没有什么比家人更重要，太子是，皇帝是，大隋也是，明白吗！你难道要让你的父母兄弟都为太子陪葬吗？！带他走！”
　　李世民垂着头，任由父亲的亲卫将他送上马车。
　　窦夫人道：“郎君，我担心三郎也难过，请让三郎回来。二郎三郎都暂住别庄，他们兄弟二人或许能尽快从悲伤中走出来。”
　　李渊犹豫了一会儿，叹气道：“毗沙门写信，现在不仅河东，连周围郡县都有人仰慕唐国公府的威名前来投奔。”
　　窦夫人垂首：“结交才俊之事可以交给大郎。”
　　李渊再次叹气：“知子莫如父，才俊大多心高气傲，若见到投奔者不如自己，怎么会安心投奔？虽然他们看中唐国公府的门第，也要看我的继承人如何。如大雄在太原，原本迟疑的贤才纷纷来投，大德此时必须在河东。天下即将大乱，我们必须抓紧时机。大德正生病，他不会乱跑去涿郡，就让他留在河东吧。”
　　窦夫人道：“那我可否去河东？三郎生病，我心里焦急，想要去照顾三郎。”
　　李渊都：“你不会医术，去了有何用。河东柳氏要和五郎结亲，你赶紧把此事定下。而且四郎的婚事你也要尽快找了。我看弘农杨氏的女子就不错。”
　　窦夫人皱眉，心中虽然焦急，也无可奈何。
　　家中子嗣的婚事只有她能张罗，她走不开。
　　窦夫人想让万氏去河东郡，但也被李渊阻止。
　　万氏毕竟只是媵，李渊认为窦夫人在太原郡，却让万氏去河东郡，可能会让河东世家不满。不如让宇文珠结交士女。
　　宇文珠不仅是李玄霸的新婚妻子，还是大儒宇文弼的孙女，还有一手在贵女间小有名气的医术，河东士族女眷一定会把宇文珠奉为座上宾。
　　窦夫人又建议道：“还是把三郎生病的消息告诉二郎吧。听到弟弟得病，二郎可能就不会乱跑了。”
　　李渊没好气道：“然后他就要死要活，非要抛下一切事务去河东吗？他与毗沙门本就不合，见大德去了河东居然生病，肯定会责怪毗沙门没有照顾好大德，兄弟之间又生出怨恨。大德每逢换季都会小病一场，不是什么大事。这次有珠娘照顾，他肯定好得更快。你操心过度了。”
　　窦夫人攥紧袖子：“或许吧。”
　　或许郎君是对的。但想到三郎生病时母亲和依赖的兄长都不在身边，窦夫人心中就难受。
　　她只能不断告诉自己，现在三郎已经成婚，有妻子照顾，一定无事。
　　这样的自欺欺人，在乌镝送信后被击碎。
　　窦夫人拿着书信寻找李渊，李渊却已经出征边塞，防备突厥和民贼联合。
　　李世民也被他带着一同离开，联系不上。
　　窦夫人便派人去安抚宇文珠，自己加紧将手中事转给万氏，并向前来说亲的柳氏、杨氏长辈道歉，准备启程去河东郡照顾李玄霸。
　　……
　　李元吉再次确认自己当时见到的人真的就在李玄霸身边，而且莫名从男童变成了女童。
　　一定是李玄霸偷梁换柱，将原本是太子私生子的男童隐藏起来，换做了女童。
　　他感到自己报仇的机会来了。
　　李元吉从李建成书房收集了李玄霸写下的诗词文章，描摹裁剪粘贴，凑成了一封密信。
　　然后，他趁着李建成醉酒，从家中偷偷跑出，敲开了河东郡丞丁荣的门。
　　他看着河东郡丞拆开信，脸上露出了灿烂的笑容。
