Chapter 131: Was He Who First Made Wooden Images Left Without Posterity?

In the tenth year of Daye of the Sui Dynasty, ignoring the rampant chaos engulfing the realm, Yang Guang once again launched a personal campaign against Goguryeo.

By the time Yang Guang arrived at Zhuo Commandery, conscripted laborers and soldiers had been deserting constantly along the way.

He executed every recaptured deserter he could lay hands on, using their flesh as sacrificial offerings and smearing their blood onto the ceremonial drums, sacrificing their very lives to the Yellow Emperor.

Below the sacrificial altar, countless scholars of the Sui Dynasty—men deeply versed in the classics, histories, masters, and anthologies—stood watching this bloody spectacle.

In their minds echoed a single line spoken long ago by Confucius:

"Was he who first made wooden images to bury with the dead left without posterity?"

The barbaric custom of human sacrifice had already been abandoned during the Western Zhou Dynasty. Yet at the onset of the Spring and Autumn Period, rulers of various states competed in ostentation—first with lavish burials, then with human figurines, until eventually the custom of human sacrifice resurfaced.

Standing at that crucial juncture, Confucius keenly perceived this shift in social norms.

If men now replaced the traditional straw dogs with human figurines for sacrifices, what might they do next in the future? Would they not end up reviving live human sacrifice altogether?

That was why Confucius uttered those words.

The Wei, Jin, Northern and Southern Dynasties had been an era of turmoil, a blood-soaked age where everyone slaughtered each other with bloodshot eyes, and gory atrocities were far from rare.

Yet pure slaughter and human sacrifice were two entirely different matters.

Slaughter was barbarism, but sacrifice belonged to the sacred realm of "Rites." Monstrous rulers were many, but one who sacrificed human beings to ancient sage-kings...

The same line surfaced in Yang Jian's mind: "Was he who first made wooden images left without posterity?"

*And who stands on the altar now, as the descendant of an emperor?* he thought self-deprecatingly.

The absurd human sacrifice concluded. The assembled court ministers had long grown accustomed to covering their eyes, ears, and mouths; they would offer no remonstrance to Yang Guang.

Perhaps this bloody human sacrifice would become nothing more than a few fleeting lines in the history books, skimmed and forgotten. By now, the Sui Emperor had committed so many outrageous absurdities that one more hardly mattered, failing even to spark the usual denouncements from sanctimonious scholars.

As months drifted by, though many conscripts summoned by Yang Guang deserted, the residual prestige and power of the Sui Dynasty endured, and its professional military remained formidable in battle.

Having suffered successive blows from Great Sui—and lacking the abandoned supply trains from Yang Guang's second campaign to replenish their strength this time—Goguryeo was shattered into complete disarray by Lai Huer's naval forces alone.

Yang Guang was overjoyed.

The single stain upon his life's honor was finally about to be washed clean.

Yang Guang hosted extravagant banquets and instructed his emissaries to prepare to accept the enemy's surrender.

He had even readied delegations to invite envoys from the Western Regions and the Khagans of the Eastern and Western Göktürks.

In Yang Guang's mind, everything was taking a turn for the better. So long as the King of Goguryeo surrendered, he would remain that immortal emperor of the ages, restoring the grand spectacle of a thousand nations paying homage to his court.

Yet at this very moment, while the central army of the Sui Dynasty was occupied in Goguryeo, the fires of peasant rebellions burned ever hotter.

Yang Xuangan, who had fled into the deep mountains after repeated blows from the Sui military, seized this opportunity to emerge once more, showing signs of a grand comeback.

The borders, too, fell into chaos.

Tang Bi, leader of the Fufeng rebel army, installed an obscure figure named Li Hongzhi as the Son of Heaven, gathered a hundred thousand insurgents, and proclaimed himself King of Tang.

At the same time, leaders of peasant rebellions across the land declared themselves kings one after another.

The "Eighteen Rebel Kings" later mythologized in popular tales emerged in rapid succession—their actual numbers far exceeding eighteen.

Yang Guang kept his eyes shut and ears plugged, indulging in music and dance as he dreamt his sweet dream of being an immortal emperor.

That was until Yang Jian stepped into the palace where he was making merry, sword in hand.

Yang Guang sneered at Yang Jian, his expression extraordinarily calm. "Did you think I didn't know you intended to rebel?"

Yang Jian stepped forward unhurriedly as axe-bearing guards emerged silently from behind the curtains on both sides.

Looking straight ahead at his coolly composed royal father on the dais, he said, "I have only the old and weak left around me; a palace coup was impossible from the start. I know it was you who deliberately instructed your personal guards to cooperate with my actions."

Yang Guang's brow furrowed.

Everything had proceeded according to his plan. He had been right all along: this son of his truly harbored treasonous intent.

None of the court ministers had noticed, all blinded by Yang Jian's superficial front. He alone had uncovered it; he was right.

Yet Yang Jian showed no dread or panic. Instead, he maintained a placid composure, as if everything were equally within his own expectations—a sight that infuriated Yang Guang to his core.

Under Yang Guang's scrutiny, Yang Jian unbuckled his armor and knelt upon the ground.

Unsheathing his longsword, he laid it flat across his thighs. "Your son has not come today to force a palace coup, but to present an armed remonstrance."

The young prince raised his head, his countenance as arrogant as ever.

"Without an armed remonstrance, Father would never listen!

"Father, open your eyes! The realm is already in utter chaos! Great Sui is on the brink of destruction!

"Not a single group of rebel insurgents that rose during your first Goguryeo campaign has been eradicated!

"The states of the Western Regions that once submitted to us have turned to the Turks one after another. The Eastern Göktürks have amassed a million-strong army, eyeing the Central Plains like tigers stalking prey!

"Yang Xuangan—the grave threat that consumed your thoughts during the second campaign—is still alive and well today!

"The death knell of the Qin Dynasty was sounded by the rebel commoners Chen Sheng and Wu Guang! The death knell of the Han Dynasty was sounded by the Yellow Turban rebels! And now, as for the death knell of Sui, though Father covers his ears and pretends not to hear, its tone will only grow louder and louder!

"I beg Father to withdraw our troops, return to the Western Capital, quell the rebellions, lighten taxes and corvée, and grant rest to the people!"

Cradling his longsword, Yang Jian kowtowed repeatedly. The blood trickling from his forehead seeped into the corners of his eyes, streaming down his cheeks mingled with tears.

"Father! Do you truly wish to imitate the tyrannical Qin and perish after just two generations?!

"Do you truly wish to become a Second Emperor of Qin?!"

Yang Jian's words rang out like a deafening thunderclap. The sovereign and ministers upon the dais were rendered speechlessly stunned for a moment, inadvertently granting him the opportunity to say every last word.

High officials swayed on their feet, wishing they could simply faint on the spot.

Yang Guang's face flushed a furious red, his eyes bulging wide as he leapt up from his couch.

Snatching a fruit platter from his low table, he hurled it viciously at Yang Jian.

Yang Jian neither dodged nor flinched, allowing the platter to strike his head. Blood gushed forth in torrents.

Seeing this, Pei Yun hurriedly restrained Yang Guang. "Your Majesty, His Highness the Prince must have been bewitched by Goguryeo sorcery, afflicted by madness and raving wildly! I beg Your Majesty to immediately order men to restrain the manic prince and summon shamans to treat him and dispel the evil!"

Yang Jian raised his blood-soaked face, glaring furiously at Pei Yun. "My lord ministers, barely half a century has passed since the age of chaos! In your hearts, you likely have never accepted Great Sui as your true master, nor do you care for its foundation! Once Great Sui falls into ruin, it will simply afford you all the perfect opportunity to vie for supreme power under heaven!

"Yet the brush of history is as sharp as a blade! Beside a foolish tyrant there inevitably stand treacherous ministers—just as Zhao Gao and Li Si stood beside the Second Emperor of Qin! By abetting a tyrant in his evil, are you not afraid of leaving a foul name that stinks for ten thousand years?!"

Pei Yun snapped in rage, "Your Highness, mind your words! What do you mean by 'abetting a tyrant in his evil'?! You are slandering His Majesty!"

Yang Jian laughed boisterously. "Great Sui is about to perish in its second generation—what is left to slander?! Grandee Pei, you have always been known for your great talent, holding authority over the household registries of the empire. Do you truly fail to see the rise of the rebel insurgents? Ask your own conscience—is it that you cannot see, or that you deceive your sovereign, closing your eyes and plugging your ears?! Yet I say again: the brush of history is as sharp as a blade. Will your present deception avail you anything before the annals of posterity?

"Forget the future you cannot see; let us speak of the present before your very eyes! If Great Sui falls, which ambitious lord in this world would dare employ a treacherous minister like you?

"Whoever conquers the land will surely exterminate your entire line!

"If Great Sui perishes after two generations, then I ask Grandee Pei to be buried alongside Great Sui as a sacrificial offering!"

Yang Guang roared, "Enough! The prince is mad! Kill him!"

Yet the axe-bearing guards hesitated.

Enraged even further, Yang Guang yelled, "Do you not hear My command?! Kill him!"

Su Wei's hands tightened into fists inside his sleeves, then slowly relaxed. Taking a deep breath, he rose, knelt down, and said, "Your Majesty is wise and enlightened—how could you execute your own son publicly within the palace? I beg Your Majesty to commit the prince to prison and deal with him according to the law."

Pei Shiju also stepped forward. "Your servant seconds the motion!"

Yuwen Shu sighed deeply in his heart and offered placating words: "May Your Majesty quell your anger. Today's events shall not leak out. His Highness has merely lost his mind. I pray Your Majesty let the matter rest to prevent this royal scandal from spreading, lest it tarnish Your Majesty's dignity."

Yu Shiji added, "Your Majesty, quelling this affair at once is of paramount importance."

He cast a sharp glare at Pei Yun.

Pei Yun was furious inside, wishing nothing more than to execute Prince Yang Jian on the spot.

Yet he also realized that if the Emperor truly executed the prince publicly now, his own reputation as a treacherous minister would indeed spread across the world, stinking for ten thousand years. Thus, he had no choice but to kneel as well and say, "May Your Majesty quell your anger."

Yang Jian sneered and opened his mouth to speak further.

Su Wei called out anxiously, "Silence! Quickly, gag His Highness!"

Only then did the guards step forward, pinning Yang Jian to the ground and muffling his mouth.

The unsheathed longsword fell to the floor, slicing across Yang Jian's cheek.

Struggling to lift his head, his face contorted in grim ferocity: "Father! Remember my words! Remember my words forever!"

Pei Shiju barked, "Drag His Highness away this instant!"

As Yang Jian was dragged out, he left a long trail of blood across the floor.

Soothed by his favored ministers, Yang Guang finally sat back down upon his couch.

He swept his gaze across everyone present, a cold gleam flashing in his eyes.

A chill ran through the hearts of Su Wei, Pei Shiju, Pei Yun, Yuwen Shu, and Yu Shiji.

They themselves might escape unharmed, but every guard present in the hall would likely be silenced forever.

Yet these guards belonged to the newly recruited Xiaoguo Army.

After rebellions erupted everywhere, the Emperor grew anxious about his safety. Lacking trust in the territorial garrison troops, he had opened the imperial treasury to recruit brave warriors, establishing the Xiaoguo Army that answered exclusively to his commands.

By now, the Xiaoguo Army had largely replaced the original imperial guards, becoming the Emperor's true elite palace guard.

The Xiaoguo guards stationed in ambush within the palace were all the fiercest and most valiant fighters in the military, holding respectable ranks. If all of them were slaughtered now, would it not destabilize the morale of the entire Xiaoguo Army?

Yet none of the ministers dared to offer remonstrance.

The prince had mounted an armed remonstrance, denouncing the Emperor for following in the footsteps of the Qin Dynasty to perish in the second generation. That they themselves could survive after hearing such blasphemy was already an act of imperial mercy—how could they spare any energy to save others?

In the end, events unfolded precisely as these clever favorite ministers foresaw: under the pretext of dereliction of guard duty, Yang Guang executed every guard and palace servant present that day.

The Xiaoguo guards had originally believed this assignment to be a prime opportunity to earn merit; thus, those selected to act as axe-bearers were lower-tier officers holding a degree of rank within the military.

Consequently, the majority of officers below the rank of Eagle-Soaring General were slaughtered, virtually wiping out the lower echelon of commanders in the army.

As expected, this act threw the Xiaoguo Army into panic and unrest. Only when Pei Shiju petitioned the Emperor to bestow lavish rewards upon the remaining Xiaoguo troops was their morale temporarily stabilized.

Yet Yang Jian's armed remonstrance was not entirely without effect.

Night after night, Yang Guang was plagued by nightmares, haunted by the sight of Yang Jian's blood-soaked face.

He even dreamed anew of Yang Yong, of his other brothers, and of Emperor Wen of Sui berating him in fury.

Upon waking, an enraged Yang Guang demoted the prince to a commoner and demanded that he be torn apart by five horses.

The senior ministers remonstrated bitterly once more.

Some hoped to preserve the prince's dignity by bestowing poisonous wine or a white silk cord for suicide; some argued that the prince had harbored no intent of treason and that exile was sufficient; still others spoke out in defense of the prince, declaring that his remonstrance had been correct.

All who spoke in his defense were thrown into prison.

Like a man possessed, Yang Guang sought to slaughter every official who dared speak up for the prince.

Su Wei and the others could only temporarily hold back the execution orders, waiting for Yang Guang to regain his senses.

When it became impossible to delay any longer, Su Wei visited the prison and pleaded with Yang Jian: "Your Highness, I know your heart belongs to Great Sui, but by acting thus, are you not driving Great Sui into the abyss? I beg Your Highness to plead for mercy from His Majesty and retract your earlier words. Father and son are linked in heart and blood—His Majesty will surely not make things difficult for you."

Yang Jian sat upon the cold floor, looking like a beggar.

Yang Guang had dispatched no physician to treat his wounds; horrific scars now marred his forehead and cheeks, wiping away his former handsome looks.

"Destruction precedes creation. If he could be moved by my words and return to Guanzhong to rule with vigor and wisdom, Great Sui could still be saved," Yang Jian said indifferently. "If he remains stubbornly unrepentant, what difference does it make whether Great Sui falls a few years earlier or later? It will still perish in its second generation. Yet Duke Su, for you to come persuade me... it seems Father has not repented in the slightest."

Su Wei remained silent.

Yang Jian suddenly burst into a dry laugh and asked, "Duke Su, do you fear leaving a foul name that stinks for ten thousand years?"

Su Wei's posture slouched, and covering his face, he departed in silence.

Yang Jian stood up, placing his hands behind his back as he gazed past the prison gate.

He smiled softly. "At least he knows enough to hide his face—perhaps there is hope for him yet."

*Su Wei might be saved, but can our Great Sui still be saved?*

*Li Erlang, Li Sanlang... if Great Sui perishes, what will become of you?*

Yang Jian recalled those two maternal cousins of his, whose talents surpassed all under heaven.

In his heart, he had already sensed what was to come.

Yet he felt no fury at the prospect of betrayal.

What was there to be angry about? If Great Sui fell, did it matter who sat upon the imperial throne?

He felt only sorrow.

"Elder Brother, it turns out I, too, could become a crown prince who worries for the state and pities the people," Yang Jian laughed, looking upward as tears trickled from the corners of his eyes. "This truly isn't like me at all. I was never such a person, nor was I ever suited for such deeds."

*Elder Brother, when you died of illness due to Father's flawed decisions, did you ever foresee this day?*

...

Though Yang Guang had executed the guards and palace servants, news of the prince's armed remonstrance slipped out nonetheless.

He cast suspicious glances at his close ministers, but they dissolved his doubts with a bitter chuckle.

The prince had not only cursed Yang Guang as bearing the marks of a ruined sovereign, but had also denounced them as treacherous ministers who would stink for ten thousand years. Who among them would willingly spread such a reputation?

Who, then, had leaked these words?

Had someone been eavesdropping? Or had the executed guards and servants spread rumors before their deaths? Or had the prince himself leaked the news?

Yang Guang began killing once more.

All officials belonging to the Eastern Palace of the Crown Prince were executed, and Yu Jian, who was closest to the prince, had his entire family wiped out.

At the execution ground, as Yu Jian kowtowed in farewell to his father, Yu Zhi, weeping that he had dragged his father into ruin, Yu Zhi reprimanded him.

"You did what was right, and it brought about calamity—how can this be your fault?" Yu Zhi said. "If you feel regret for it now, only then would your father be ashamed to call you my son."

Yu Jian wept, "Your son does not regret it!"

Yu Zhi said with gratification, "Good."

Father and son met their end together. The spectating commoners wept bitterly, clashing with the execution squad, resulting in dozens of civilians injured in the commotion.

Xue Deyin stood among the crowd watching this scene. Seizing the chaos, he paid someone to collect the remains of the Yu family before returning to a small courtyard in Zhuo Commandery.

Inside the courtyard, a heavily pregnant woman stood gazing blankly at the sky.

Xue Deyin said in a deep voice, "Zhuo Commandery is in utter turmoil right now; this is our chance to leave."

The woman lowered her head. "Will His Highness live?"

Xue Deyin remained silent.

The woman murmured, "I should not have asked. For His Highness, living would only be more agonizing. But I must live."

Xue Deyin said, "The Central Plains are no longer safe. We shall head to Zhangye. Li Erlang and Li Sanlang are both honorable and righteous men; they will surely help conceal you."

The woman replied, "I shall follow your every instruction, sir."

Xue Deyin bribed the gate guards and slipped away with the woman under the cover of night.

Once outside the city, Xue Deyin halted the carriage, turned toward the city gates, and kowtowed deeply.

Then he rose, urged the horse forward, and departed without looking back.

...

"Cough, cough, cough... an armed remonstrance..." Li Xuanba coughed incessantly.

Covering his mouth with a handkerchief, he looked down at the flecks of blood staining the cloth and clenched it tightly in his palm.

Yuwen Zhu wept, "Sanlang, you were already ill. If you remain so deeply overwhelmed by gloom, I fear it will damage your internal organs."

Li Xuanba offered a gentle smile of comfort. "I know. I will do my best to manage it."

Wiping her tears, Yuwen Zhu forced a smile. "Good. I shall go brew your medicine, husband."

Turning her back, her tears fell once more.

Words came easily to her husband, just as advice came easily to her, but how could one simply control human emotions at will?

Li Xuanba watched Yuwen Zhu depart, coughing a few more times.

Leaning against the cushions at the head of the bed, he stared blankly at the bed curtains.

When Li Xuanba first became acquainted with Yang Zhao and Yang Jian, there had been little sincerity in his heart.

When Yang Zhao passed away, though he felt sorrow, he was quickly able to compose himself.

Now that Prince Qi—an absurd figure in history—had been captured after mounting an armed remonstrance, why was the anguish and rage in his chest so impossible to suppress?

Li Xuanba closed his eyes, yet no matter how deeply he breathed, tears welled from his eyes and spilled over.

"Emperor Yang of Sui... Emperor Yang of Sui... how could your dynasty *not* perish in its second generation?!"

His chest heaved up and down as he took deep breath after deep breath, his face swiftly soaked in tears.

"Cough, cough, cough..."

Li Xuanba covered his mouth, coughing uncontrollably.

Yuwen Zhu stood outside the door, refraining from entering.

Wudi and Hangou stood beside her with folded wings, their heads bowed and completely still.

Gradually, low sobs mingled with the coughing from inside the room. The weeping grew louder and louder until it broke into heartbroken, agonizing wails as intense as the coughing fits.

Yuwen Zhu turned and walked away.

"Wudi, Hangou, deliver a letter for me."

Wudi and Hangou chirped: "Chirp!"

Yuwen Zhu did not know why Sanlang insisted on hiding his illness from his elder brother, but she could no longer afford to care about Sanlang's feelings.

If... if something truly happened to Sanlang...

Yuwen Zhu stopped in her tracks, burying her face in her hands.

*At the very least, they must see each other one last time...*

...

"Li Shimin! What do you think you are doing?!" Li Yuan stopped Li Shimin, who was secretly leading his horse out at night. "I know you share a deep bond with His Highness, but you are absolutely forbidden from getting involved in this! Do you wish to bring ruin upon our entire family?!"

Li Shimin said, "I know that remonstrating with His Majesty would be useless. I only wish to see Second Cousin off on his final journey."

Li Yuan instructed his attendants, "Lock him up."

Li Shimin pleaded anxiously, "Father!"

Li Yuan said exhaustedly, "I know you are a good child who values loyalty and affection, but I will absolutely not allow you to act recklessly in this matter."

Li Shimin fell to his knees, begging, "I truly will not bring disaster upon our house."

Li Yuan said, "His Majesty has gone mad. Anything you do could provoke his wrath. If you still regard me as your father, obey my words."

Li Shimin wept, "Father, please do not force me."

Li Yuan bent down and pulled Li Shimin to his feet. "It is not I who am forcing you; it is you who must not force me! Nothing is more important than family—not the prince, not the Emperor, and not Great Sui! Do you understand?! Do you intend to make your parents and brothers be buried alongside the prince as sacrifices?! Take him away!"

Head hanging low, Li Shimin allowed his father's personal guards to usher him into the carriage.

Lady Dou said, "Husband, I fear Sanlang is grieving deeply as well. Please let Sanlang return. If Erlang and Sanlang stay at the villa together, the two brothers might be able to emerge from their sorrow sooner."

Li Yuan hesitated for a moment before sighing. "Pishamen wrote in his letter that not only Hedong, but even neighboring commanderies and counties have talented men coming to seek refuge, admiring the prestige of the Duke of Tang's estate."

Lady Dou lowered her head. "The task of associating with talents can be left to Dalang."

Li Yuan sighed once more. "No one knows a son better than his father. Most men of talent are proud and haughty; if they see that those already seeking refuge are inferior to themselves, how could they feel at ease pledging allegiance? Though they value the standing of the Duke of Tang's house, they also look to see what my heir is like. Just as Daxiong in Taiyuan caused hesitant scholars to flock to us, Dade must remain in Hedong at this time. The world is on the verge of chaos, and we must grasp this opportunity. Besides, Dade is ill; he won't run off to Zhuo Commandery. Let him stay in Hedong."

Lady Dou asked, "May I go to Hedong then? Sanlang is sick, and I am sick with worry—I want to go care for him."

Li Yuan replied, "You are not skilled in medicine; what good would your going do? The Liu clan of Hedong wishes to form a marriage alliance with Wulang—you must settle this matter quickly. Furthermore, you must arrange Silang's marriage as soon as possible. I think a daughter of the Yang clan of Hongnong would be suitable."

Lady Dou frowned. Though anxious at heart, she was helpless.

Only she could arrange the marriages of the family's children, so she could not leave.

Lady Dou thought to send Concubine Wan to Hedong Commandery, but Li Yuan stopped that as well.

Concubine Wan was, after all, merely a concubine. Li Yuan felt that if Lady Dou remained in Taiyuan Commandery while sending Concubine Wan to Hedong Commandery, it might spark dissatisfaction among the prominent families of Hedong. It would be better to let Yuwen Zhu socialize with the noble ladies there.

Yuwen Zhu was not only Li Xuanba's newlywed wife, but also the granddaughter of the great Confucian scholar Yuwen Bi, possessing medical skills well-known among noble ladies. The female relatives of the Hedong gentry would surely treat Yuwen Zhu as an honored guest.

Lady Dou suggested again, "Then at least tell Erlang the news of Sanlang's illness. Hearing that his younger brother is sick, Erlang might stop trying to run off."

Li Yuan snapped, "So he can pitch a fit and demand to throw aside all duties to rush to Hedong? He is already at odds with Pishamen; seeing that Dade fell ill after going to Hedong, he will certainly blame Pishamen for failing to take good care of Dade, creating even more resentment between brothers! Dade catches a minor ailment every seasonal change—it is no big deal. With Zhuniang taking care of him this time, he will surely recover even faster. You are worrying far too much."

Lady Dou clenched her sleeves tightly. "Perhaps..."

Perhaps her husband was right. Yet at the thought of Sanlang being ill without his mother or the elder brother he depended upon by his side, Lady Dou felt an ache in her heart.

She could only repeatedly tell herself that now that Sanlang was married and cared for by a wife, he would surely be fine.

Such self-deception was shattered after Wudi delivered the letter.

Lady Dou took the letter to find Li Yuan, only to learn that Li Yuan had already marched out to the northern frontier to guard against a collusion between the Turks and the rebel insurgents.

Li Shimin had also been taken along by him, leaving no way to contact them.

Lady Dou thus dispatched servants to comfort Yuwen Zhu while hurriedly transferring her responsibilities to Concubine Wan. She offered apologies to the elders of the Liu and Yang clans who had come to discuss marriage matches, preparing to set off for Hedong Commandery to care for Li Xuanba.

...

Li Yuanji confirmed once again that the person he had seen back then was indeed by Li Xuanba's side—and had somehow transformed from a boy into a girl.

It had to be Li Xuanba pulling off a secret swap, concealing the boy who was originally the prince's illegitimate son and replacing him with a girl.

He felt that his opportunity for revenge had finally arrived.

Gathering poems and essays written by Li Xuanba from Li Jiancheng's study, Li Yuanji traced, cut, and pasted the characters together to forge a secret letter.

Then, taking advantage of Li Jiancheng's drunkenness, he slipped out of the house unnoticed and knocked on the door of Ding Rong, the Vice-Governor of Hedong Commandery.

Watching the Vice-Governor open the letter, a brilliant smile spread across his face.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第132章 黄雀更在螳螂后 – 第133章 李五郎献计藏身
chunks.chineseText:
第132章 黄雀更在螳螂后

李玄霸高烧了几日， 烧得嘴唇都干裂了。
　　宇文珠拿起装着甘油的小罐，给李玄霸嘴上和脸颊涂抹甘油。
　　她对李玄霸笑道：“还记得你最初给我写的信吗？你把甘油说成了神药，可把我惊呆了。”
　　已经退烧的李玄霸微笑道：“甘油对许多皮肤病确实是神药， 我没骗你。”
　　“嗯。”宇文珠笑道， “老师也十分看重甘油， 你送我的甘油大半都落入了他手中，被他弄去炼药。”
　　李玄霸嘴角微抽：“炼药？怎么炼？不会是炼丹吧？”
　　宇文珠帮李玄霸把脸颊上的甘油抹均匀：“我看差不多。就是把甘油和各种药材金石混合在一起，然后先给羊服用， 看有没有毒，没有毒就自己尝试。老师炸了好几次炉子，可吓人了。”
　　李玄霸嘴角抽搐：“你应该没有以身试药过吧？”
　　宇文珠微笑：“你猜？”
　　李玄霸道：“你可不能以身试药。”
　　宇文珠道：“那你赶快好起来， 把我盯住。”
　　李玄霸道：“好。”他感觉自己应该快好了。
　　秋日已至，冬天也快了。
　　今年如果能挺过去， 或许他就有希望活到中年。
　　与宇文珠白头偕老他不敢奢望， 携手一二十年的愿望应该不奢侈吧？
　　李玄霸一直躺在床上，身上也需要擦拭。
　　原本李玄霸不愿意让宇文珠做，但宇文珠坚持她是医师，李玄霸是她的病人，再者他们是夫妻， 没什么害羞的。
　　宇文珠在李玄霸烧昏迷时为李玄霸擦拭了几次身体降温，李玄霸便没办法再羞涩了。
　　他暗暗自嘲， 病人在医生眼中就是一块散发着病气的腐肉，实在是没有什么好害羞的。
　　在宇文珠的精心照顾下，李玄霸从每天晚上高烧， 变成了隔一两日才高烧， 后来隔几日的高烧变成了低烧。
　　笑容回到了小两口的脸上， 愁绪就像是雨后的乌云一般渐渐散去。
　　快在床上窝臭了的李玄霸终于洗了个澡， 神清气爽。
　　李玄霸身体转好后，又关心了一下天下大势。
　　太子杨暕仍旧被关在狱中。
　　杨广被说动了，在两国交战时杀子不吉利，要等高丽王投降再杀杨暕。
　　李玄霸不由苦笑自己的怯懦。
　　他为二表兄感到伤心难过愤怒，但唯独没有想过现在去涿郡为二表兄送行。
　　他知道杨广那个神经病，现在谁去谁死。他不能拿自己和家人的命冒险。
　　“不知道二哥会不会冲动。不过父亲和母亲肯定能把他拦下来。”李玄霸对宇文珠道，“河东的事差不多了，我们提前回太原吧。我大病初愈想念家人，大兄没理由拦我们。”
　　宇文珠点头：“好。”
　　她抬头看着天空：“乌镝怎么还没回信？”
　　李玄霸道：“让寒钩再送一封去，就说我们要回来了，让二哥带人来接我们。现在太原和河东也有许多盗贼流窜，小心为上。”
　　寒钩不满地“啾”了一声。
　　李玄霸喂了寒钩一条肉干：“送完信就赶紧回来。我身边没有你和乌镝，也不自在。”
　　寒钩这才满意地点头。
　　李玄霸笑了笑，擦了擦手，提笔写信。
　　虽然他现在仍旧有点咳嗽，但痰里已经不带血丝，赶路是没问题了。
　　死劫应该是能过了。
　　“把小五和士信叫来，我们要回太原了。”
　　终于松了口气的李智云被李玄霸派去向李建成辞别，却见李建成已经人走宅空。
　　……
　　涿郡。
　　杨广拿着河东郡丞丁荣写来密信，先是愤怒，待看完后，愤怒变成疑惑。
　　他将信递给裴世矩：“你与李二郎李三郎最熟悉，你看他二人会为太子谋逆吗？”
　　裴世矩接过信，看完后皱眉：“太子殿下……私生子？怎么可能？”
　　杨广道：“确实不可能。他府中一切女眷子嗣朕都知道，连他曾经……”
　　杨广顿了顿，没有把杨暕曾经和臣子妇有暧昧的事说出来。
　　虽然他已经十分厌恶杨暕，但这件已经过去许多年，且止步于暧昧。杨暕已经给他抹了足够多的黑，他不想再在脸上多抹一层黑。
　　裴世矩道：“丁郡丞已经将密信送来，有一人能识得二郎三郎字迹。”
　　虞世基上前道：“请陛下召见吾弟虞世南。”
　　杨广叹息道：“虞舍人还是朕给二郎三郎介绍的习字老师。”
　　裴蕴观察皇帝的神情，猜到皇帝并没有猜忌李二郎和李三郎，不由惊讶。
　　按理说李二郎和李三郎和太子交好，皇帝就算不猜忌，也该迁怒。没想到李二郎和李三郎在皇帝心中信任度如此高？
　　虞世南是起居舍人，一直伴随杨广左右，很快就来觐见。
　　他看了一眼密信，眼露嫌弃：“画虎类犬。这字迹不仅并非李三郎，恐怕任何一个认真习字的士人都不会写得如此糟糕，简直污了臣的眼睛。陛下，若你不告诉臣这是密信，臣还以为是孩童胡乱描画。”
　　几位大臣相互交换视线，杨广也若有所思。
　　杨广的书法也很好。他将密信拿过细看后，皱起眉头：“拿笔来。”
　　虞世基恭敬地奉上蘸好墨的笔。
　　杨广在密信上圈点，将难以入目的字都标记出来。
　　在场之人都博闻强识，过目不忘。他们看了一眼剩下的字句，在脑海中打乱重组，虽然组成的字句不多，但总有那么一两句能认出来。
　　苏威愤怒道：“这人怕不是偷了三郎的诗词，胡乱描画诬告！他不知道三郎在河东作的词已经传到涿郡了吗！”
　　杨广将笔放下：“朕被孽畜蒙蔽，立那孽畜为太子时，朝中无人不奉承太子，唯有李大雄和李大德冷眼待之。他们早就看出太子心有不轨，不愿与之为伍，又怎会为太子背叛朕？”
　　杨广愤怒时想把曾经奉承太子、在自己面前说过太子好话的人都杀了。
　　但他梳理之后，发现就算是自己最信任的臣子也曾经交好太子，夸奖太子。
　　太子曾经深受他喜爱，又是他唯一成年皇子，也是自己仅存的嫡子，朝臣若不与他交好才是怪事。
　　细思之后，杨广发现，居然只有李二郎李三郎早早与太子疏远。虽然太子对两人很亲近，但两人却从未主动讨好过太子。
　　放眼群臣，李二郎与李三郎竟是对太子杨暕最冷漠的人了。
　　杨广心中宽慰。
　　二郎三郎不愧是自己从小看到大的好孩子，没有辜负他的亲近爱护。
　　“让二郎三郎来涿郡自辩。”杨广淡然道，“虞舍人，你亲自去一趟，别让两个孩子吓到。他们刚成亲，朕忙于国事不能前往，此次让他们把各自妻子也带来给朕和皇后看看。皇后一直念着。”
　　虞世南心中大定：“臣遵旨。”
　　杨广道：“众卿能想到是谁诬告吗？”
　　裴世矩装作思索了一会儿，道：“臣曾听闻唐国公有一逆子，曾诬陷其母。唐国公大怒，将其交予严师管教。”
　　杨广也想到了这个人。
　　李元吉李四郎可太出名了，让东都勋贵看够了唐国公一家的笑话。
　　他心有戚戚道：“各家都有讨债的孽子啊。幸得朕是明君，不会轻易猜忌大臣。”
　　众臣恭敬道：“陛下英明！”
　　……
　　李玄霸迎来河东郡守丁荣的拜访。
　　他惊讶道：“四弟诬告我私藏太子私生子？太子……太子哪来的私生子？”
　　河东郡守丁荣道：“本官本也不信，但招来李建成后，李建成坚称是你和李二郎所为，与他无关。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“你听他这话，就因为他也知道此事，并作证我真的做了？”
　　丁荣道：“难道不是？”
　　李玄霸道：“既然丁郡丞已经将密信交给陛下，一切就等陛下定夺吧。”
　　丁荣见李玄霸如此镇定，心中生出疑虑：“你真的没有背叛陛下？”
　　李玄霸无奈道：“陛下对我恩重如山，我岂会背叛陛下？再者就算太子殿下有罪，陛下宽仁，顶多将太子殿下子嗣贬为庶人流放，难道还会害自己年幼的孙儿不成？何况太子殿下真的没有儿子，这是众人皆知的事。”
　　丁荣道：“明面上没有……”
　　李玄霸打断道：“陛下和太子殿下都对太子殿下无子嗣一事十分苦恼。我说难听些，若谁为太子殿下诞下子嗣，哪怕是臣子妇，曾经深深看重太子殿下的陛下都会找借口让那臣子妇和离，改头换面送入太子殿下府中。太子殿下的子嗣何其重要？从谁肚子里出来有什么关系？”
　　丁荣思索之后，也认为李玄霸言之有理。
　　听李元吉描述，太子殿下的私生子已经是七八岁的稚童。七八年前，太子殿下还是大隋最嚣张跋扈的齐王殿下，藏个私生子干什么？
　　丁荣道：“我是很想相信你，但你大兄和四弟皆作证，本官只能将你软禁，等待陛下决断。”
　　李玄霸拱手：“这是郡丞之责。郡丞可带我书信去寻我二哥，让我和二哥一起在河东郡等候陛下召见。郡丞放心，二哥看到书信，绝对会立刻前来。”
　　丁荣道：“好，你修书一份，本官派人去送信。虽然我将你软禁，但你若缺什么尽管和我说，我也相信这事有误会。”
　　丁荣本就对才名远播的李玄霸有好感，且李玄霸与河东三个大世家都交好，唐国公又手握兵权，无论李玄霸是否收留太子私生子，他都没打算把唐国公府逼急了。
　　再者……收留太子私生子又如何？这本不算谋逆，可以悄悄按下不提。
　　可是李元吉来大义灭亲，他就只能上报皇帝。
　　希望无事。
　　丁荣本来以为等到陛下来人就无事了，但他万万没想到，就在他拜访李玄霸的当晚，李玄霸被软禁的城郊别庄着火，有盗贼假借他的名义袭击李玄霸。
　　……
　　城郊，李密看着大火，摇着羽毛扇，回头对副将道：“七月流火，流的也可以是烧掉大隋的火。”
　　李密本是带着杨玄感的命令来劝李渊一同谋反。
　　李渊在山西和河东的动作，杨广眼瞎，他们不瞎，看出了李渊的野心。
　　李渊老谋深算，李密知道直接劝说很难奏效，所以他本想从李建成这里入手。
　　天下谁人不知唐国公有一对麒麟子。
　　身为麒麟子的兄长，李建成的压力一定很大。李密想以支持李建成为筹码，让李建成劝李渊起事叛隋。
　　若事成，有自己主公的全力支持，李建成的地位一定能跃居站在大隋这一边的李二郎、李三郎之上。
　　谁知道，他居然看到了这样一场好戏。
　　天赐良机，他岂能不推波助澜一把？李三郎被杀，纵使李渊不愿意为子报仇，皇帝岂会对李渊放心？
　　“可惜了李三郎，真的是世上难得一见的少年才俊。”李密摇摇头，转身道，“收拾好手脚。该去太原了。”


第133章 李五郎献计藏身

李玄霸醒来时， 身下摇摇晃晃，让他的脑袋有点晕。
　　他恍惚了一会儿，昨夜的记忆才回笼。
　　晚上他睡得正香， 罗士信突然带着人叫他起床， 说有人放火。
　　虽然李玄霸确信无论是杨广还是丁荣都不会为难自己， 但以防万一，他都让家中人合衣枕兵睡觉。家中女眷也不例外。
　　李玄霸迅速起床，来不及思考， 就有人喊着“皇帝有令，诛杀李三郎”冲进来。
　　幸得罗士信和护卫身手矫健，李智云一手射术也十分了得， 迅速护着李玄霸和宇文珠逃离着火的宅院。
　　李玄霸暂住的别院在城郊，旁边就是一片山林。
　　山林全部燃起火焰， 幸亏李玄霸这个有些许被害妄想症的人在河中藏了船。他们跳入河中游到藏船的地方， 顺流而下借着烟火的掩护冲进了黄河中。
　　摆脱了追兵和火势后，李玄霸身体本就没有痊愈，又跳入了深秋冰凉的河水，很快又发起了高烧，沉睡过去。
　　“三郎君醒了， 终于醒了！”守着李玄霸的仆从惊喜地叫道，“我去叫娘子， 娘子刚歇下！”
　　李玄霸拉住仆从的衣角，声音嘶哑道：“不要打扰珠娘，让珠娘好好休息。”
　　仆从焦急道：“可娘子不醒来， 谁给郎君看病？”
　　李玄霸道：“把小五叫进来。”
　　仆从虽然心头焦急， 也只能听命令。
　　李智云正抱着弓在船头打瞌睡， 听到李玄霸醒来后哭着扑进来。
　　李玄霸摸着李智云的脑袋道：“别哭， 听我说。”
　　李智云一边抹眼泪一边点头。
　　李玄霸道：“珠娘背着的医药箱里，写着‘退烧’二字的药为我熬一副。”
　　李智云抽泣道：“嫂嫂休息前吩咐了如果三兄醒来就熬什么药，已经熬着了。”
　　李玄霸的眼睛往船舱外瞟：“珠娘在哪里休息？”
　　李智云道：“在船尾。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“我的船备得太小。”
　　李智云摇头：“不是小船够隐蔽，我们就逃不出来了。三兄你继续休息，接下来交给我。”
　　他使劲揉了揉眼睛，挤出笑容，拍了拍胸脯道：“交给我！”
　　李玄霸看着李智云惶恐不安的神情，道：“好，不过我还是要问点事。随着我们离开的有多少人？”
　　李智云回答道：“大多都四散逃跑了，仆从和婢女只剩下两人，护卫除了士信还剩十人。”
　　李玄霸心头一沉。
　　只剩下这么点人，并不是四散逃跑的原因，而是这条船只能装下这么多人。
　　他闭上了一会儿眼睛，将心中情绪压下，待再睁开眼时，眼神恢复冷静。
　　“袭击者应当不是丁荣，而是有我们不知道的第三者势力参与。”李玄霸道，“虽然我暂时想不出他的目的，但他伪造皇帝的命令想要杀我们，就不会留我们的命。我们逃跑仓促，一定会被他们发现踪迹。要尽快上岸，寻一个城池隐藏踪迹。”
　　李智云道：“寻、寻哪个？”
　　李玄霸又揉了揉李智云的脑袋，道：“我现在烧得有点糊涂，很难思考。你与珠娘、士信商量。珠娘常随孙医师行医，士信有孤身西行的经验，他们一定能与你一起商议出去处。”
　　李智云问道：“我们不去太原寻父亲和二兄吗？要不我们干脆回张掖！”
　　李玄霸道：“我虽然推断袭击者应当不是丁荣，但我没有证据。如果真的是皇帝下令杀我，我们暴露身份就会死。就算不是皇帝的命令，追杀我们的人肯定会猜测我们回太原或张掖，一定布置了人手。”
　　虽然有多条道路可以前往太原和张掖，但李玄霸现在的身体不支持他翻山越岭。且假如正好撞上了追兵呢？
　　现在躲藏起来，静待后续情况发展才是最好的应对方式。
　　李玄霸匆匆交代几句后，汤药端了上来。
　　宇文珠受了惊，睡眠很浅，还是听到动静醒来，给李玄霸诊脉喂药。
　　宇文珠安慰道：“你醒来了就没事了，放心，有我在，这点小病肯定能治好。”
　　李玄霸微笑道：“我的身体就拜托珠娘了。”
　　药效发作，李玄霸再次沉沉睡去。
　　李玄霸睡着后，宇文珠脸上强撑的微笑崩塌，捂着嘴无声哭了起来。
　　李智云担忧道：“三兄的病……”
　　宇文珠哽咽道：“如果有足够的药，我一定能把三郎的病情压下来，可……”
　　药不够了。
　　李智云深呼吸，强自冷静下来：“或许、或许有个去处，就是有点冒险……”
　　宇文珠道：“叔郎请说。现在三郎生病，你是能主事的人。”
　　李智云摇头：“主事的人是我、你和士信。我们三人一起决定。我去把士信叫醒。”
　　罗士信酣战一夜，现在还没睡醒。
　　李智云将罗士信叫醒后，对罗士信和宇文珠说了一件只有很少的人知道的事。
　　“贼帅王薄身边谋主魏徵是二兄和三兄的人。前几日我帮三兄整理情报时听到王薄正前往瓦岗寨，与另一个贼帅翟让商议结盟拦截大隋军队后勤辎重。现在黄河水湍急，我们已经漂流一夜，距离瓦岗寨贼军控制的黄河渠道不远了。”
　　罗士信皱眉：“以三郎君身份投奔贼帅，岂不是谋逆？二郎君三郎君曾说过，现在还不是起兵的好时机。”
　　宇文珠问道：“魏徵可信吗？”
　　李智云道：“虽然我没有见过，但三兄说这人可信，那就一定可信。”
　　宇文珠又问道：“民贼有足够多的草药吗？”
　　罗士信道：“我听过王薄的名声，他与其他贼帅不同，占了一块地后屯田经营，并不仅靠打家劫舍过活，物资应当是充足的。”
　　宇文珠道：“你们不要出面，我扮作魏徵族中女子去投奔他。叔郎，你将魏徵家中情况都告知我。三郎肯定和你说过。你们再找机会上岸，多买几身女子衣服和冪离。”
　　李智云犹豫道：“不会我们都扮作女子吧？”
　　宇文珠道：“三郎和你都必须扮作女子，士信扮作我弟弟。我们因为兵役徭役家破人亡，听闻族兄在知世郎王薄麾下效力，士信小有武力，便带着家中姊妹去投奔族兄。”
　　罗士信道：“好。我和王薄都是齐郡人，还可以攀一攀老乡。”
　　李智云道：“那你得教我和嫂嫂齐郡的口音。”
　　罗士信白了李智云一眼：“你都要扮作女子了，还能说话？”
　　李智云捏着嗓子秒切换女音：“轻而易举～。”
　　罗士信露出震惊的神色。
　　李智云得意洋洋道：“二兄也会。我们和府中口技伶人学的！”
　　罗士信：“……主公学这个干什么？”
　　李智云一本正经道：“逗生病的三兄笑。”
　　罗士信再次露出震惊的神色。
　　宇文珠掩嘴，自遇袭后第一次露出真正的笑容：“是兄公会做的事。”
　　罗士信结巴道：“你还是闭嘴装哑巴吧，我怕被你吓到。”
　　李智云道：“总有需要开口的时候。那就这么说定了？”
　　宇文珠道：“我的药还能支撑两日，需要加快速度了。”
　　即使知道魏徵是兄公和三郎的人，宇文珠仍旧很害怕去贼窝。
　　在她的耳中，民贼都是一群无恶不作的人。
　　但她不能露出害怕的神色。
　　三郎病倒，叔郎还小，自己必须挺住。
　　李玄霸再次醒来时，宇文珠告诉了他要去投奔魏徵的事。
　　李玄霸昏昏沉沉地点头赞同，又很快睡去。
　　如此三日，在宇文珠的药耗尽一日之后，他们终于寻到了瓦岗寨义军的踪迹。
　　……
　　河东郡的那把火，烧得整个河东郡都人心惶惶。
　　丁荣当即四处张贴告示，表明这把火不是自己烧的，而是有盗贼假借自己的名义袭击李三郎。
　　他一边安抚百姓，一边派人向李渊和杨广报信。
　　丁荣快急疯了。
　　李元吉告密后，丁荣低调行事，就是不想逼迫唐国公。
　　首先这件事就算是真的，和唐国公也没关系，陛下不一定会怪罪唐国公；再者隋朝大军还在攻打高丽，如果镇守山西、河东的唐国公被逼反，皇帝被迫返回，自己估计也要担罪。
　　所以丁荣悄悄召见李建成，并在李建成极力撇清自己之后，放李建成悄悄离开河东郡，好安唐国公的心，告知他自己并没有相信李元吉的告密。
　　他只扣下李玄霸，除了李玄霸是李元吉状告的当事人之外，还因为李玄霸只是唐国公府一个病弱的三郎君。
　　李三郎君虽然天纵奇才，但自幼体弱，御医曾断定他活不不到弱冠。他也确实时常生病。
　　丁荣知道父母虽然怜惜多病的孩子，但也肯定早早做好了放弃这个孩子的准备。所以他扣留李玄霸应付皇帝，放走李建成安李渊的心。
　　何况他不会为难李玄霸。
　　大部分官宦都懂做事留一面的道理。丁荣既要应付皇帝，又不想得罪李渊，只软禁李玄霸是最好的应对。
　　李元吉状告的是李世民和李玄霸两人，丁荣却没有派人去太原质问李世民，就很明显地表现出了他对此事的倾向。
　　不过丁荣暗示了李建成离开时知会李玄霸一声，让李玄霸心中有数，没想到李建成直接跑了。
　　正是李建成这过分惶恐不安的表现，才让本来相信李二郎和李三郎的丁荣警觉，布置人手封锁了李玄霸宅院后，才去寻李玄霸问事。
　　现在无论是李玄霸的镇定自若，还是那一场不知道是谁的袭击，都让丁荣确信李元吉确实是诬告了。
　　看来李建成慌乱，只是因为被自己“陛下已经杀了几千余名与太子亲近的勋贵子弟”吓破了胆。
　　又或者，他本就不在乎李三郎的死活？
　　丁荣嘴角都急得起了泡，不由暗骂河东鹰扬郎将无能，居然已被贼人渗透到如此地步！

Chapter 132: The Oriole Lies Behind the Mantis

Li Xuanba had been running a high fever for several days, so severe that his lips were parched and cracked.
Yuwen Zhu picked up a small jar of glycerin and gently dabbed it onto Li Xuanba’s lips and cheeks.
She smiled at him. "Do you still remember the very first letter you wrote to me? You called glycerin a miraculous medicine, which completely astounded me."
Li Xuanba, whose fever had finally broken, gave a faint smile. "Glycerin truly is a miracle drug for many skin ailments. I didn't lie to you."
"Mhm," Yuwen Zhu chuckled. "Master also values glycerin very highly. Most of what you sent me ended up in his hands to use in his alchemy."
Li Xuanba's lip twitched slightly. "Alchemy? How does he use it? He isn't trying to refine Daoist pills with it, is he?"
Yuwen Zhu gently spread the glycerin evenly across his cheeks. "It looks pretty close to that, honestly. He mixes glycerin with various herbs and minerals, feeds the concoction to a sheep first to test for toxicity, and if the sheep survives, he tries it on himself. He blew up his furnace several times—it was terrifying."
Li Xuanba's lip twitched again. "You haven't tried any of those experimental medicines yourself, have you?"
Yuwen Zhu smiled softly. "Guess?"
"You must never test untested medicine on yourself," Li Xuanba said solemnly.
"Then you had better recover quickly and keep a close eye on me," Yuwen Zhu replied.
"Alright," Li Xuanba agreed. He felt that he was finally on the mend.
Autumn had already arrived, and winter was not far off.
If he could make it through this year, perhaps he might stand a chance of living into middle age.
He did not dare indulge in the extravagant hope of growing old together with Yuwen Zhu till their hair turned white, but was it too greedy to wish for twenty years together, hand in hand?
Confined to his bed for so long, Li Xuanba required sponge baths to stay clean.
At first, Li Xuanba had been reluctant to let Yuwen Zhu do it. But she insisted that she was a physician and he was her patient—and besides, they were husband and wife, so there was no cause for bashfulness.
After Yuwen Zhu wiped down his body several times to cool him off while he lay unconscious with high fever, Li Xuanba could no longer cling to his shyness.
He mocked himself in secret: *To a doctor, a patient is just a piece of ailing meat. There really is nothing to be embarrassed about.*
Under Yuwen Zhu's meticulous care, Li Xuanba's condition improved from burning up with a high fever every night, to once every couple of days, and eventually to a mild low-grade fever every few days.
Smiles returned to the young couple's faces, and their worries scattered like dark clouds after a rainstorm.
Having nearly turned foul from being cooped up in bed for so long, Li Xuanba finally took a proper bath, feeling refreshed and invigorated.
Once his health stabilized, Li Xuanba turned his attention back to the state of the realm.
Crown Prince Yang Jian was still imprisoned.
Yang Guang had been persuaded that executing his own son while the empire was at war was an ill omen; he intended to wait until the King of Goguryeo surrendered before executing Yang Jian.
Li Xuanba could not help but laugh bitterly at his own cowardice.
He felt grief, sorrow, and anger for his second cousin, yet he had never once considered going to Zhuo Commandery to see him off.
He knew that with Yang Guang's current unhinged state of mind, anyone who went to intercede would be seeking death. He could not gamble his own life or the lives of his family.
"I wonder if Second Brother will act rashly. But Father and Mother will surely hold him back," Li Xuanba said to Yuwen Zhu. "The affairs in Hedong are mostly settled, so let us return to Taiyuan ahead of schedule. As I am just recovering from a severe illness, I miss my family. Eldest Brother will have no reason to stop us."
Yuwen Zhu nodded. "Alright."
She looked up at the sky. "Why hasn't Wudi returned with a reply yet?"
Li Xuanba said, "Send Hangou with another letter. Tell Second Brother that we are coming back and ask him to lead a detachment to escort us. Bandit groups are roaming Taiyuan and Hedong now, so we must err on the side of caution."
Hangou let out a disgruntled *chirp*.
Li Xuanba fed Hangou a strip of dried meat. "Come back quickly as soon as you deliver the letter. I feel uneasy without you and Wudi by my side."
Only then did Hangou nod in satisfaction.
Li Xuanba chuckled, wiped his hands, and picked up a brush to write.
Although he still coughed occasionally, there was no longer any blood in his phlegm. He was fit enough to travel.
It seemed he had safely bypassed his fatal calamity.
"Fetch Fifth Brother and Shixin. We are leaving for Taiyuan."
A greatly relieved Li Zhiyun was sent by Li Xuanba to bid farewell to Li Jiancheng, only to find that Li Jiancheng had already packed up and departed, leaving behind an empty residence.
...
Zhuo Commandery.
Holding the secret report sent by Vice-Governor Ding Rong of Hedong Commandery, Yang Guang was initially furious, but as he finished reading, his rage turned into confusion.
He handed the letter to Pei Shiju. "You are the most familiar with Li Erlang and Li Sanlang. Do you think the two of them would commit treason for the Crown Prince?"
Pei Shiju took the letter, read it through, and furrowed his brows. "His Highness the Crown Prince... an illegitimate son? How could that be possible?"
Yang Guang said, "It is indeed impossible. I am well aware of every female member and child in his household, even that affair he once..."
Yang Guang paused, refraining from mentioning Yang Jian's past entanglement with a courtier's wife.
Though he now utterly despised Yang Jian, that scandal had occurred many years ago and had gone no further than improper flirtation. Yang Jian had already dragged his name through enough mud, and Yang Guang did not wish to smear his own face any further.
Pei Shiju remarked, "Vice-Governor Ding has forwarded the confidential letter. There is someone here who can recognize Erlang and Sanlang's handwriting."
Yu Shiji stepped forward and said, "May it please Your Majesty to summon my younger brother, Yu Shinan."
Yang Guang sighed. "Court Secretary Yu was the very calligraphy teacher I introduced to Erlang and Sanlang."
Pei Yun observed the Emperor's expression and was secretly astonished to deduce that the sovereign harbored no suspicion toward Li Erlang and Li Sanlang.
By logic, since Li Erlang and Li Sanlang had been close to the Crown Prince, even if the Emperor did not suspect them, he ought to have vented his fury upon them by association. Who would have thought that Li Erlang and Li Sanlang enjoyed such a high degree of trust in the Emperor's heart?
As a Secretariat Drafter of the Imperial Diary, Yu Shinan was constantly by Yang Guang's side and arrived shortly for an audience.
Glancing at the secret letter, his eyes filled with disdain. "A clumsy imitation that falls pathetically short! Not only is this handwriting definitely not Li Sanlang's, but no scholar who has seriously studied calligraphy would ever write so wretchedly. It positively defiles your servant's eyes. Your Majesty, had you not informed me that this was a confidential letter, I would have assumed it was the meaningless scribblings of a child."
The ministers exchanged subtle glances, while Yang Guang sank into deep thought.
Yang Guang was himself a skilled calligrapher. Taking the confidential letter back to examine it closely, he knitted his brows. "Bring me a brush."
Yu Shiji respectfully presented a brush dipped in ink.
Yang Guang began circling and dotting the document, marking out all the unsightly, poorly written characters.
The ministers present were all men of vast erudition and photographic memories. They glanced at the remaining characters, rearranging and reassembling them in their minds. Though few full phrases remained, one or two distinct lines emerged.
Su Wei declared in anger, "This rascal must have stolen Sanlang's poetry and copied it haphazardly to frame him! Does he not know that the lyrics Sanlang composed in Hedong have already spread to Zhuo Commandery?"
Yang Guang set down the brush. "Back when I was blinded by that beast and created him Crown Prince, there was no one in court who did not flatter him—save for Li Daxiong and Li Dade, who treated him with cold detachment. They foresaw long ago that the Crown Prince harbored treacherous intent and refused to associate with him. How could they possibly betray Me for his sake?"
In his fury, Yang Guang had felt inclined to execute everyone who had ever flattered the Crown Prince or spoken kindly of him in his presence.
Yet upon reflection, he realized that even his most trusted ministers had once befriended and praised the Crown Prince.
The Crown Prince had once been his doting favorite, his only adult son, and his sole surviving legitimate heir. It would have been strange if the court officials had *not* tried to ingratiate themselves with him.
Upon careful consideration, Yang Guang realized that only Li Erlang and Li Sanlang had distanced themselves from the Crown Prince early on. Although the Crown Prince had treated them with great affection, the two brothers had never once taken the initiative to fawn upon him.
Looking across the entire court, Li Erlang and Li Sanlang were, ironically, the most indifferent of all toward Crown Prince Yang Jian.
Yang Guang felt deeply comforted.
Erlang and Sanlang were indeed good children whom he had watched grow up; they had not betrayed his fond affection and favor.
"Have Erlang and Sanlang come to Zhuo Commandery to defend themselves," Yang Guang said calmly. "Court Secretary Yu, go in person, lest those two boys be frightened. They have both recently wed, and as I was consumed by state affairs, I could not attend. This time, have them bring their wives so that the Empress and I may meet them. The Empress has been speaking of them constantly."
Yu Shinan felt a wave of relief wash over him. "Your servant obeys."
Yang Guang asked, "Can my ministers guess who framed them?"
Pei Shiju feigned deliberation for a moment before speaking up. "Your servant has heard that the Duke of Tang has an unfilial son who once falsely accused his own mother. The Duke of Tang was furious and handed him over to a strict master for discipline."
Yang Guang immediately remembered him as well.
Li Yuanji, the fourth son, was far too notorious; his antics had provided the noble families of the Eastern Capital with endless amusement at the Duke of Tang's expense.
Feeling a sympathetic resonance, Yang Guang sighed, "Every family has its unfilial spawn coming to collect debt. Fortunately, I am a wise ruler who does not lightly harbor suspicion against his ministers."
The assembled ministers bowed respectfully. "Your Majesty is wise indeed!"
...
Li Xuanba received a visit from the Vice-Governor of Hedong Commandery, Ding Rong.
He feigned astonishment. "Fourth Brother accused me of hiding the Crown Prince's illegitimate son? The Crown Prince... where would the Crown Prince get an illegitimate son from?"
Vice-Governor Ding Rong replied, "I did not believe it at first either. But when I summoned Li Jiancheng, he adamantly insisted that it was your doing alongside Li Erlang, and had nothing to do with him."
Li Xuanba sighed. "Listen to his words. Did he say that simply because he knew about it, testifying that I truly did such a thing?"
Ding Rong asked, "Is that not the case?"
Li Xuanba said, "Since Vice-Governor Ding has already dispatched the secret letter to His Majesty, let us wait for His Majesty's royal decree."
Seeing Li Xuanba so composed, suspicion sprouted in Ding Rong's mind. "Have you truly not betrayed His Majesty?"
Li Xuanba said helplessly, "His Majesty's benevolence toward me is as vast as a mountain; how could I betray him? Furthermore, even if His Highness the Crown Prince were guilty, His Majesty is benevolent. At most, he would demote the Crown Prince's offspring to commoners and exile them—would he truly harm his own young grandchild? Besides, the Crown Prince truly has no sons; this is common knowledge."
Ding Rong said, "Not on the surface..."
Li Xuanba interrupted, "Both His Majesty and the Crown Prince were deeply troubled by His Highness's lack of male heirs. To put it bluntly, had any woman borne a son for the Crown Prince—even if she were a courtier's wife—His Majesty, who prized the Crown Prince so highly back then, would have found an excuse to grant her a divorce, change her identity, and send her into the Crown Prince's estate! How precious would an heir to the Crown Prince be? What difference would it make whose womb he came from?"
Upon careful consideration, Ding Rong also felt that Li Xuanba's words made complete sense.
According to Li Yuanji's description, the Crown Prince's illegitimate child was already a young boy of seven or eight years old. Seven or eight years ago, the Crown Prince was still the most arrogant and domineering Prince of Qi in the Great Sui Empire—why would he bother hiding an illegitimate son back then?
Ding Rong said, "I truly wish to believe you, but since your eldest brother and fourth brother have both testified, I can only place you under house arrest while awaiting His Majesty's decision."
Li Xuanba cupped his hands in respect. "That is the Vice-Governor's duty. You may take a letter from me to my Second Brother, so that he and I may await His Majesty's summons together in Hedong Commandery. Rest assured, Vice-Governor, once my Second Brother sees the letter, he will certainly come immediately."
Ding Rong said, "Very well. Write the letter, and I will dispatch a courier. Although I am placing you under house arrest, if you lack anything, simply let me know. I, too, believe there must be a misunderstanding."
Ding Rong already had a good impression of Li Xuanba, whose scholarly fame was renowned far and wide. Furthermore, Li Xuanba was on good terms with the three prominent aristocratic families of Hedong, and the Duke of Tang held military power. Regardless of whether Li Xuanba had actually harbored the Crown Prince's illegitimate son, Ding Rong had no intention of pushing the Tang Duke's house into a corner.
Besides... what if he *had* harbored an illegitimate son of the Crown Prince? It was not strictly treason, and could have been quietly swept under the rug.
However, since Li Yuanji had come to report his own family out of righteous duty, Ding Rong had no choice but to report it to the Emperor.
He only hoped no disaster would come of this.
Ding Rong originally thought everything would be fine once the Emperor's envoy arrived. What he never expected was that on the very night he visited Li Xuanba, a fire broke out at the suburban manor where Li Xuanba was detained, and a band of bandits attacked Li Xuanba under Ding Rong's name.
...
In the suburban countryside, Li Mi watched the blazing inferno, waving his feather fan. He turned to his lieutenant and said, "The fiery stars of mid-autumn descend—and the fire that flows may well be the one that burns down the Great Sui."
Li Mi had originally come under Yang Xuangan's orders to persuade Li Yuan to join their rebellion.
Yang Guang was blind to Li Yuan's maneuvers in Shanxi and Hedong, but Li Mi and his master were not; they clearly perceived Li Yuan's ambitions.
Li Yuan was old and scheming. Li Mi knew a direct persuasion would yield little result, so he had intended to approach Li Jiancheng first.
Everyone under heaven knew that the Duke of Tang possessed a pair of prodigy sons—his two "kirin boys."
As the elder brother of these prodigies, Li Jiancheng's pressure must have been immense. Li Mi had planned to use his backing of Li Jiancheng as leverage to push Li Jiancheng into persuading Li Yuan to rise in revolt against the Sui.
If successful, with the full support of Li Mi's master, Li Jiancheng's standing would surely eclipse that of Li Erlang and Li Sanlang, who stood on the side of the Sui court.
Who could have foreseen that he would stumble upon such a marvelous play instead?
With such a heaven-sent opportunity, how could he not add fuel to the flames? If Li Sanlang were killed, even if Li Yuan proved unwilling to avenge his son, how could the Emperor ever trust Li Yuan again?
"A pity about Li Sanlang—he truly was a rare young talent under heaven." Li Mi shook his head, then turned around. "Clean up all traces. It is time to head for Taiyuan."

Chapter 133: Fifth Brother Li Devises a Scheme for Concealment

When Li Xuanba awakened, the swaying beneath him made his head spin.
He remained in a daze for a moment before the memories of the previous night flooded back.
Last night, while he was sound asleep, Luo Shixin had abruptly burst in with his men to wake him up, reporting that someone had set the manor ablaze.
Although Li Xuanba was confident that neither Yang Guang nor Ding Rong would harm him, just in case, he had instructed his household to sleep fully clothed with their weapons beside them. The women of the household were no exception.
Li Xuanba had gotten up swiftly, but before he even had time to think, assailants rushed in shouting, "By imperial decree, execute Li Sanlang!"
Fortunately, Luo Shixin and the guards were agile and skilled, and Li Zhiyun's archery was superb. They quickly protected Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu as they escaped the burning compound.
The manor where Li Xuanba was temporarily staying was located in the suburbs, adjacent to a mountain forest.
The forest was engulfed in flames. Fortunately, Li Xuanba—paranoiac that he was—had hidden a boat in the river beforehand. Jumping into the water, they swam to the hidden vessel and drifted downstream, plunging into the Yellow River under the cover of smoke and fire.
After breaking free from the pursuers and the flames, Li Xuanba—whose body had not yet recovered—succumbed to the icy waters of late autumn. A high fever soon seized him again, plunging him into a deep slumber.
"Third Young Master is awake! He's finally awake!" the servant keeping watch beside him called out in joy. "I'll go fetch the Lady—she just lay down to rest!"
Li Xuanba tugged at the servant's sleeve, his voice raspy. "Do not disturb Zhu'niang... let her rest."
The servant said anxiously, "But if the Lady does not wake, who will tend to Young Master's illness?"
Li Xuanba said, "Call Fifth Brother inside."
Though anxious, the servant could only obey.
Li Zhiyun had been dozing at the bow of the boat, hugging his bow. Hearing that Li Xuanba was awake, he rushed in weeping.
Li Xuanba stroked Li Zhiyun's head. "Don't cry. Listen to me."
Li Zhiyun nodded as he wiped his tears.
Li Xuanba said, "In the medicine box Zhu'niang carried out, find the herbs labeled 'Fever Relief' and decoct a batch for me."
Li Zhiyun sobbed, "Before Sister-in-law rested, she already gave instructions on what medicine to brew if Third Brother woke up. It's already simmering."
Li Xuanba glanced outside the cabin. "Where is Zhu'niang resting?"
Li Zhiyun said, "At the stern."
Li Xuanba sighed. "The boat I prepared was too small."
Li Zhiyun shook his head. "If the boat hadn't been small and stealthy enough, we wouldn't have escaped. Third Brother, rest up. Leave the rest to me."
He rubbed his eyes vigorously, forced a smile, and patted his chest. "Leave it to me!"
Noticing the anxiety lingering in Li Zhiyun's expression, Li Xuanba said, "Alright. But I must ask a few things first. How many came away with us?"
Li Zhiyun replied, "Most scattered and fled. Only two male and female servants remain, and besides Shixin, ten guards are left."
Li Xuanba's heart sank.
The reason so few were left was not that the others had fled, but because this small boat could only hold this many people.
He closed his eyes briefly, suppressing his emotions. When he reopened them, his gaze had turned cold and composed.
"The attackers were likely not sent by Ding Rong, but rather a third party we are unaware of," Li Xuanba said. "Though I cannot guess their motive for now, since they forged an imperial decree to kill us, they will not rest until we are dead. Our hurried flight will surely leave traces for them to track. We must go ashore as soon as possible and find a town in which to conceal ourselves."
Li Zhiyun asked, "Which... which town should we head for?"
Li Xuanba stroked Li Zhiyun's head once more and said, "My head is hazy with fever, making it difficult to think clearly. Discuss it with Zhu'niang and Shixin. Zhu'niang has traveled extensively with Physician Sun to practice medicine, and Shixin has experience traveling west alone. Together, they will surely help you decide on a destination."
Li Zhiyun asked, "Shall we not go to Taiyuan to find Father and Second Brother? Or should we simply return to Zhangye!"
Li Xuanba said, "Though I deduce that the attacker is not Ding Rong, I have no proof. If it truly was the Emperor who ordered my execution, revealing our identities means death. Even if it was not the Emperor's order, our pursuers will certainly guess that we might return to Taiyuan or Zhangye, and will surely lay ambushes along those routes."
Although multiple paths led to Taiyuan and Zhangye, Li Xuanba's current physical condition could not endure trekking across mountains and ridges. And what if they happened to run straight into their pursuers?
Hiding away for now and waiting for developments was the best course of action.
After Li Xuanba hurriedly gave these few instructions, the decoction was brought to him.
Yuwen Zhu, having been shaken by the raid, slept lightly and woke up at the sound of activity. She checked Li Xuanba's pulse and helped him drink the medicine.
Yuwen Zhu comforted him, "Now that you've woken up, everything will be fine. Don't worry—with me here, I will definitely cure this minor illness."
Li Xuanba smiled faintly. "I leave my health in your hands, Zhu'niang."
As the medicine took effect, Li Xuanba sank back into a deep sleep.
Once Li Xuanba was asleep, the brave smile Yuwen Zhu had maintained collapsed. She covered her mouth and wept silently.
Li Zhiyun asked anxiously, "Third Brother's illness..."
Yuwen Zhu choked back a sob. "If I had enough herbs, I could certainly keep Sanlang's condition under control, but..."
*The medicinal herbs were running out.*
Li Zhiyun took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. "Perhaps... perhaps there is a place we can go, though it is a bit risky..."
Yuwen Zhu said, "Please tell me, Fifth Brother. Now that Sanlang is sick, you are the one in charge."
Li Zhiyun shook his head. "The ones in charge are you, me, and Shixin. The three of us will decide together. I'll go wake Shixin."
Luo Shixin had fought fiercely all night and was still asleep.
After waking Luo Shixin, Li Zhiyun revealed a secret known to very few people.
"Wei Zheng, the chief strategist beside the bandit leader Wang Bo, is Second Brother and Third Brother's man. A few days ago, while helping Third Brother organize intelligence, I heard that Wang Bo was heading to Wagang Fortress to negotiate an alliance with another bandit leader, Zhai Rang, to intercept the Sui army's supply lines. The Yellow River's current is swift; after drifting all night, we are not far from the river channels controlled by the Wagang rebels."
Luo Shixin frowned. "Seeking refuge with a bandit leader using Third Young Master's identity—is that not open rebellion? Second Young Master and Third Young Master said before that the time is not yet ripe to raise troops."
Yuwen Zhu asked, "Is Wei Zheng trustworthy?"
Li Zhiyun said, "Though I have never met him, Third Brother said he is trustworthy, so he must be."
Yuwen Zhu asked further, "Do the rebels have enough herbs?"
Luo Shixin replied, "I have heard of Wang Bo's reputation. Unlike other bandit chieftains, after seizing territory, he sets up military agricultural colonies and manages them. He doesn't rely solely on pillaging to survive, so his supplies should be ample."
Yuwen Zhu said, "The two of you must not show your faces. I will disguise myself as a female relation of Wei Zheng's clan and seek refuge with him. Fifth Brother, tell me everything about Wei Zheng's family background—Sanlang must have mentioned it to you. Then, find an opportunity to go ashore and buy several sets of women's garments and veiled hats (*mili*)."
Li Zhiyun hesitated. "Surely we aren't *all* disguising ourselves as women?"
Yuwen Zhu said, "Sanlang and you must dress as women, while Shixin disguises himself as my younger brother. We will claim our family was destroyed by military conscription and corvée labor, and upon hearing that our clan brother serves under Wang Bo—the Master Who Knows the World—Shixin, possessing a bit of martial skill, brought his sisters to seek refuge with him."
Luo Shixin said, "Good. Both Wang Bo and I are from Qi Commandery, so I can claim hometown ties."
Li Zhiyun said, "Then you must teach Sister-in-law and me the Qi Commandery accent."
Luo Shixin rolled his eyes at Li Zhiyun. "If you're dressing as a woman, how could you dare speak?"
Li Zhiyun pinched his throat, instantly switching to a high-pitched feminine voice: "With absolute ease~"
Luo Shixin looked utterly flabbergasted.
Li Zhiyun said proudly, "Second Brother can do it too! We learned it from the vocal impressionists in our household!"
Luo Shixin asked, "...Why on earth did the Master learn such a skill?"
Li Zhiyun said in all seriousness, "To make sick Third Brother laugh."
Luo Shixin looked flabbergasted once more.
Yuwen Zhu covered her mouth, letting out her first genuine smile since the attack. "That is indeed something Second Brother-in-law would do."
Luo Shixin stammered, "You'd better just shut your mouth and pretend to be mute. I'm afraid I'll die of fright."
Li Zhiyun said, "There will always be times when we need to speak. Is it settled then?"
Yuwen Zhu said, "My remaining medicine can only last two days. We need to hurry."
Even knowing that Wei Zheng was loyal to Second Brother-in-law and Sanlang, Yuwen Zhu was still terrified of entering a bandit lair.
In her ears, rebels were nothing but a mob of villainous raiders.
Yet she could not show her fear.
With Sanlang ill and Fifth Brother so young, she had to stand strong.
When Li Xuanba woke again, Yuwen Zhu informed him of their plan to seek refuge with Wei Zheng.
Dazed and groggy, Li Xuanba nodded in assent before sinking back into sleep.
Three days passed in this manner. One day after Yuwen Zhu's medicine ran out completely, they finally spotted traces of the Wagang rebel forces.
...
The fire in Hedong Commandery plunged the entire region into panic.
Ding Rong immediately had notices posted everywhere, clarifying that he had not set the blaze, but rather that bandits had used his name to launch a surprise attack on Li Sanlang.
While reassuring the populace, he dispatched messengers to report the incident to Li Yuan and Yang Guang.
Ding Rong was driven nearly out of his mind with anxiety.
After Li Yuanji's betrayal, Ding Rong had maintained a low profile precisely because he did not want to push the Duke of Tang too far.
First of all, even if the allegation were true, it had nothing to do with the Duke of Tang himself, and His Majesty might not necessarily blame the Duke. Furthermore, the Sui imperial army was still campaigning against Goguryeo; if the Duke of Tang, who garrisoned Shanxi and Hedong, were forced into rebellion, compelling the Emperor to pull back his forces, Ding Rong would surely bear the blame.
Therefore, Ding Rong had secretly summoned Li Jiancheng, and after Li Jiancheng did everything to distance himself from the accusation, Ding Rong allowed him to quietly leave Hedong Commandery. This was intended to put the Duke of Tang's mind at ease, signaling that he had not believed Li Yuanji's report.
He had detained only Li Xuanba, not just because Li Xuanba was the primary party accused by Li Yuanji, but also because Li Xuanba was merely a frail, sickly third young master of the Duke's household.
Although Li Sanlang was a peerless genius, he had been weak and sickly since childhood; imperial physicians had once predicted he would not live to adulthood. Indeed, he was frequently plagued by illness.
Ding Rong knew that while parents pitied sickly children, they undoubtedly prepared themselves early on for the prospect of losing them. Thus, he detained Li Xuanba to satisfy the Emperor, while letting Li Jiancheng go to reassure Li Yuan.
Moreover, he had no intention of mistreating Li Xuanba.
Most officials understood the wisdom of leaving room for compromise. Since Ding Rong needed to satisfy the Emperor without offending Li Yuan, placing only Li Xuanba under house arrest was the optimal middle ground.
Li Yuanji had accused both Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, yet Ding Rong had not dispatched anyone to Taiyuan to question Li Shimin. This clearly revealed his true stance on the matter.
However, Ding Rong had hinted that Li Jiancheng should notify Li Xuanba before leaving so that Li Xuanba would be prepared; he had not expected Li Jiancheng to simply flee without a word.
It was precisely Li Jiancheng's excessively panicked behavior that alerted Ding Rong—who had initially believed Li Erlang and Li Sanlang—prompting him to station men around Li Xuanba's residence before going to question him.
Now, whether judging by Li Xuanba's serene composure or that mysterious assault by unknown assailants, Ding Rong was entirely convinced that Li Yuanji had indeed made a false accusation.
It seemed Li Jiancheng's panic was merely because he had been terrified out of his wits by Ding Rong's statement that "His Majesty has already executed thousands of noble youths close to the Crown Prince."
Or perhaps... he simply did not care whether Li Sanlang lived or died?
Blisters broke out around the corners of Ding Rong's mouth from shear anxiety, and he could not help but inwardly curse the incompetence of the Eagle-Soaring Commandant of Hedong, who had allowed bandits to infiltrate the area to such a degree!

chunks.chapterTitle: 第134章 这老天非要他死
chunks.chineseText:
第134章 这老天非要他死

“可能被火烧死了？什么叫可能！”坐在石头上的李密狠狠合上书， 下属惶恐地跪了一地。
　　李密站起来，衣袖一甩，背着手来回走了几圈， 皱眉道：“死要见尸， 绝对不允许出意外！”
　　此次随李密一起前来劝说李渊的韩世谔道：“只是一个黄毛小儿， 值得军师如此看重？”
　　韩世谔是大隋名将韩擒虎的嗣子，在韩擒虎死后，袭封寿光县公。
　　隋文帝晚年猜忌心很强， 许多跟随他的将领都不得善终。韩擒虎是难得劳苦功高还能善终的人。
　　不过杨广继位后，对韩家十分冷落。
　　韩擒虎的弟弟韩僧寿也是一员屡立功勋的猛将，在杨广继位后一直不复任用， 无论是对突厥、吐谷浑还是高丽，杨广都没有给他领兵立功的机会。大业八年， 韩僧寿卒于大兴。
　　韩世谔这个“二代”， 就更没有建功立业的机会。所以杨玄感起兵后，韩世谔思及杨广的凉薄，便投奔杨玄感。
　　杨玄感当时一呼百应，军中多有勋贵子弟投效，大多都是这样的人。
　　韩世谔继承了韩家的勇猛， 跟随杨玄感时立下不少先登之功，是杨玄感麾下最重要的猛将之一。
　　杨玄感派韩世谔保护李密， 可见对李密的看重。
　　经历了攻打洛阳失利，败逃山林又东山再起，杨玄感心中的浮躁倨傲沉淀下来， 逐渐展露出其父杨素老谋深算的风范， 与李密相处越来越融洽。
　　李密原本不屑杨玄感的短视浮躁， 现在也对这个主公越来越满意， 做事很是尽心。
　　李密很会处事，对主公麾下将领都很亲切。
　　韩世谔询问，他虽然在气头上，也耐心解释道：“韩将军，李二郎李三郎在这个年龄就立下无数功劳，恐怕只有你的父亲能与他们作比。”
　　韩世谔道：“父亲年少时没有机会立功，军师不必谬赞，我不会生气。李二郎确实厉害，但李三郎不过只是一个很会读书的病秧子，是死是活应该不重要。我们不是只需要‘杨广派人杀了李渊儿子’这个借口，逼李渊与杨广离心吗？”
　　李密摇头：“李二郎再厉害，但人的精力有限，若只是打仗就罢了，我可是听说张掖已经完全成为他们的地盘。李二郎在前线拼杀的时候，谁来管理后勤？谁来抚民？李二郎的年龄在那里，又只是唐国公次子，恐怕没有多少大才投奔。”
　　韩世谔也皱起眉头：“你是说李三郎是李二郎的谋主？”
　　李密道：“是不是谋主我不知道，但我也是郡姓世家，了解世家的人。河东薛氏、柳氏、裴氏虽不如我陇西李氏，但心气也很高。薛元敬、柳亨、裴行俨三人，是他们年轻一辈中最顶尖的人才。能被这三人视为好友的李三郎，肯定不简单。”
　　韩世谔更加疑惑：“既然李三郎如此厉害，为何我们要接触李建成？与李三郎商议说服其父结盟，岂不是更好？”
　　李密没想到韩世谔会问出这么憨的问题，不由失笑，眉头都展开了：“韩将军，我们的主公是杨公。”
　　韩世谔道：“当然。这和我的问题有什么关系？”
　　李密笑道：“关系大着。我们前来劝李渊起兵，只是让这个天下更加混乱，进一步削弱大隋的力量，可不是我们要去投奔李渊啊。”
　　韩世谔无奈道：“军师，你有话就直说行吗？别绕弯子，让我头疼。你的意思是，将来李渊迟早会成为主公争夺天下的敌人，所以要扶持他无能的大儿子，压制他有本事的二儿子和三儿子。”
　　李密把书拿起来，拍了拍灰尘：“不是压制，是如果有机会，必须除掉他们。这大隋的天下必定会灭亡，李渊现在是否起兵，不过是让大隋早几年还是晚几年灭亡的问题。但李世民和李玄霸的威胁太大了，他们才十六岁，就已经掌控河右之地。若给他们时间发育，他们熬都能熬死我等。”
　　韩世谔想明白了：“原来在军师眼中，李渊不足为惧，李二郎和李三郎才是你重视的人。这次李家人内讧，给了我们杀掉李三郎的机会，比劝李渊起兵更利于主公？”
　　李密笑道：“是这样。”
　　韩世谔道：“怪不得你轻视李渊了。天下大乱，能者居之。纵观南北朝乱世，各个雄主都头疼继任者，让兄弟接班甚至义子接班者比比皆是。如果我有李二郎李三郎这样的儿子……”
　　韩世谔说到一半，想起自己还有个主公，便闭嘴不语了。
　　李密笑得更厉害：“韩将军别怕食言，我们主公心胸宽广，不会责怪我等。我还曾和主公玩笑，我与李渊同姓李，如果我有李二郎李三郎这样的儿子，我肯定想办法自立，才来帮主公做事。”
　　韩世谔好奇道：“主公怎么回答？”
　　李密笑着摇摇头：“主公说如果他有这么厉害的儿子，他就退位让贤，让儿子打天下去，自己坐享其成。”
　　韩世谔不由也失笑：“主公太没志气了。”
　　李密把书揣好：“我也是这么骂他。唉，好不容易找到机会……”
　　李密摇摇头，又叹了口气。
　　逐鹿天下的人都有天命在身，就看谁的天命更大。李世民和李玄霸这对双生子一看就是有天命在身的人，一明一暗，一正一辅，令人惧怕。
　　李密纵观天下英雄，入眼者寥寥无几。这两个今年才十六岁的少年郎，却让他深深警惕。
　　可现在他们最大的敌人是杨广，而李二郎李三郎又借了杨广的势，李密不可能对两人出兵。
　　这次真的是天赐良机。
　　韩世谔道：“既然李三郎这么重要，我亲自带人追击。”
　　李密道：“就拜托将军了。我去太原打探情况，继续劝说李渊。”
　　顺带挑拨离间。
　　李建成应该已经逃回太原了。自己如果将李建成诬告李三郎，导致李三郎葬身火海的事在太原四处宣扬，李二郎会和李建成反目成仇吗？李渊又会帮谁？
　　李密眯起了眼睛。
　　……
　　“我的族侄？”魏徵疑惑。
　　他接过拜帖，刚一拆开就神色一凛：“他们在哪？！”
　　怎么会是三郎君的印章？！
　　王薄疑惑：“你的族人来投奔？我一起去。”
　　谋主的族人，他得好好表现一番。
　　魏徵犹豫了一下，相信王薄的为人，对王薄耳语道：“是三郎君的人。”
　　王薄立刻从坐榻上跳了起来，严肃道：“刚你族人说有人生病？我们赶紧去！翟兄，今日宴会我不做陪了。”
　　三郎君不仅是他的老师，还是他的退路！难得三郎君的人有事相求，自己可不能松懈。
　　翟让道：“魏先生的家人来了？我也一起去。”
　　魏徵拱手道：“抱歉，这次来人有许多女眷。我虽落魄，但族中也是官宦之家，女眷不好见太多外男。”
　　翟让摸了摸头，道：“也对，我忘记你们这些士人很重规矩了。你们去吧，需要什么就告诉我，我一定尽力帮忙。”
　　魏徵弯腰作揖：“谢翟公！”
　　魏徵和王薄匆匆来到自称魏徵族人暂时下榻的地方，罗士信站在门口等候。
　　他见到魏徵并非独自前来，不由握紧手中长|枪。
　　魏徵忙道：“贤侄！辛苦了！”
　　他没见过罗士信，但一看罗士信的年龄，就知道是二郎君三郎君的人。寻常将领可不会放心任用如此年少的小将。
　　王薄看出了罗士信的紧张，安抚道：“别紧张，我带了医师来。”
　　罗士信打量了魏徵和王薄一眼，从面容气质上分别出谁是魏徵。
　　他对魏徵行礼：“族叔，小侄有礼。生病者是我三姊，不好让医师诊断。我大姊懂医术，只是缺少医药。”
　　罗士信口中一个“三”字，把魏徵惊得身体一颤。
　　他咬牙道：“你三姊是我的晚辈，我去探望不用计较男女有别。我也会医术，让我去看看。”
　　罗士信犹豫。
　　一个女声隔着门响起：“三姊说，请族叔进屋。”
　　罗士信侧身让开。
　　魏徵脚步急促地推门进屋。
　　罗士信对王薄抱拳道：“恕我无礼，请知世郎在门外等候。”
　　王薄摆手：“无事无事，我就在这等。拿两个坐墩和一个火盆来。”
　　王薄吩咐完后，就拉着罗士信在一旁坐下：“别担心，魏先生的医术也很高明，你三姊一定会无事。”
　　王薄心里焦急无比。
　　罗士信这一声“三姊”，也让他联想到，莫非是李三郎君扮作女子投奔他。
　　但李三郎君正受狗皇帝信赖看重，现在应该刚回太原郡成婚。他与魏徵还派人扮作商人悄悄送过礼，很遗憾不能亲自前往。
　　这成亲才几月？怎么、怎么……
　　王薄有心打听，又担心罗士信误会，只能不断用焦急的视线瞟着门口，等魏徵出来。
　　魏徵进屋后，招呼魏徵进来的女子声音一沉：“你就是三兄夸赞过的魏玄成？”
　　魏徵惊得跳起来。
　　“女”子对魏徵招手：“快过来，三兄叫你。”
　　魏徵惊疑不定地跟着“女”子进了内屋。
　　一位娇俏少女正卧在病榻上咳嗽，另一位面容略显成熟的女子为她擦拭汗珠。
　　“玄成，给你介绍，这是我的妻子宇文珠，你称呼珠娘即可；他是我和你提过的小五，李智云；门外是二哥麾下猛将罗士信。”李玄霸压抑着咳嗽，勉强挤出笑容，“具体的事士信之后告诉你，先带珠娘去抓药，咳咳。”
　　“三郎君！”魏徵上前几步扑到病榻前，“你、你怎么……”
　　宇文珠冷静道：“请族叔先带我去抓药，其他事之后说。三妹已经断了一日药了。”
　　魏徵跌跌撞撞起身：“好，好，跟我来！”
　　魏徵带着宇文珠出门抓药，忘记告诉李玄霸，王薄在外面。
　　不过李智云透过门扉看到了王薄，告知了李玄霸。
　　李玄霸一边咳嗽一边道：“魏玄成相信知世郎，我相信魏玄成。叫知世郎进来。”
　　李智云便把王薄请进了屋，不过这次他没有转成男子声线，隐藏了一手。
　　王薄忐忑不安地进屋，看着病榻上的妙龄女子不敢相认。
　　李玄霸自嘲道：“我自幼病弱，体格较小，扮作女子是不是很惟妙惟肖？”
　　王薄焦急道：“三郎君这是怎么了？难道狗皇帝害你？”
　　李玄霸道：“是家门不幸，又恰逢不知道是谁的敌人中途下了黑手，才如此狼狈。不过以我的布置，局势应当很快会好转。我先在知世郎这里躲一阵子，待局势明朗后再离开。知世郎放心，我不会给知世郎添麻烦。”
　　王薄苦笑：“我是逆贼，不怕麻烦。倒是三郎君，你一定要隐藏好自己。”
　　李玄霸道：“这就要拜托知世郎帮忙了。”
　　王薄道：“三郎君放心。你相信我，愿意在危难中来寻我，我绝对不辜负三郎君的信任！我明日就离开瓦岗寨，回齐郡！”
　　李玄霸摇头：“知世郎既然有谋划，还是完成谋划再离开更好。我扮作女子，深藏闺中，不会引人注目。”
　　王薄道：“听三郎君的。”
　　李玄霸开玩笑道：“我来这里，不会白吃白喝你的。珠娘是很厉害的医师，你和瓦岗寨若有女眷生病，可让珠娘帮忙看病；等我身体转好，也可给你当一当暂时的谋臣。”
　　王薄露出笑容，抱拳道：“那三郎君的病可要快点好，我好向三郎君问策。我就不打扰三郎君养病了。三郎君有任何需要，就请立刻告知我。”
　　李玄霸让李智云送王薄离开。
　　李智云回来后，叹气道：“三兄与魏玄成相处不多，与王薄更是只有一面之缘。他们二人对三兄的关心却情真意切。”
　　李智云身为唐国公府唯一媵妾生的儿子，自幼便会察言观色，一眼就看出魏徵和王薄对李玄霸的关心是真的。
　　李玄霸咳嗽道：“白首如新，倾盖如故，便是如此，咳咳咳。”
　　李智云给李玄霸倒水：“三兄，接下来你可以放心养病了，以后的事都交给我们。”
　　李玄霸微笑道：“嗯。”
　　魏徵带着宇文珠抓药时，见人便哭诉自己的族侄一家受苦了，狗皇帝不是人。
　　翟让闻言十分感慨，命人告知魏徵需要什么药就告诉他，如果他这里没有，他可以派人混入城里购买。
　　翟让对徐世勣道：“狗皇帝真是让太多人家破人亡。”
　　徐世勣叹气：“我第一次见到魏先生如此难过的模样。我家中小有横财，请翟公准许我回家一趟。”
　　翟让道：“去吧，小心安全。”
　　徐世勣拱手：“是。”
　　徐世勣询问魏徵需要什么药物后，偷偷潜回家凑了些药物，又拿金银混入郡城购买了滋补品，一并给魏徵送来。
　　魏徵千恩万谢，泪流不止，看得徐世勣心头难过极了。
　　罗士信对徐世勣抱拳道：“徐兄之恩，我没齿难忘！将来徐兄有难，我必救之！”
　　徐世勣笑道：“举手之劳，算不得什么恩情。你如此年少，还是先在乱世中活下来再说吧。”
　　罗士信在心里嘀咕，别小瞧我。
　　王薄的声誉极佳，不止在义军中，在豪强中也说得上话。
　　他亲自挨家挨户地请求，很快就凑了许多名贵药材。
　　翟让见王薄对魏徵的族人如此尽心，不由反省自己对部下还不够好。
　　正好他的家人逐渐嚣张跋扈，翟让便以王薄的品行劝谏家人，自己也更加体恤下属。
　　罗士信在义军中逛了一段时间，见到“民贼”不是他所想的那样没有人性。至少翟让和王薄的下属，与他在张将军军中所见相差不离，心中不由触动。
　　李玄霸的病情在猛药压制下，高烧终于没有反复。
　　在李玄霸的同意下，罗士信暂时加入了王薄麾下，帮瓦岗寨打隋军，磨砺自己的武艺。
　　李智云则继续扮作女子，充当李玄霸和宇文珠的护卫。
　　李玄霸以为自己的死劫估计快过去了。
　　但当他的烧完全退下的第二日，起床在屋里慢吞吞转悠，试图恢复体力的李玄霸的胸口突然闷疼。
　　宇文珠站在李玄霸面前，伸出双手，就像是对待刚学走路的孩子一样，笑颜满面地鼓励李玄霸再走几步。
　　然后，李玄霸捂着胸口，在她面前缓缓倒下。
　　“三郎？！”
　　“三兄？！”
　　李玄霸大口大口的深呼吸，眼前的视线逐渐模糊。
　　只一瞬间，他就知道了自己的症状。
　　这是……因肺炎高热带来的心肌炎吧？说起来，老李家本来就有心脑血管遗传病史，真的毫不意外啊。
　　李玄霸闭上眼睛的时候，缓缓叹了口气。
　　天发杀机，地发杀机，人发杀机。
　　一波接一波，目不暇接。
　　这老天，是非要他死呢。
　　……
　　“耶耶，我不管你有什么事，阿玄让我去接他，我必须去！”李世民接到寒钩乌镝送来的接连催促的书信后，无论李渊再怎么说“我们很忙，另外派人去”，他都不干了。
　　十六岁的少年郎干净利落地往地上一趟，居然打起滚来。
　　李渊哭笑不得：“你是十六岁，不是六岁！起来！观音婢都在笑话你了！”
　　长孙康宁捂着嘴，眼睛弯弯道：“我没笑。”
　　李世民满地打滚，一边滚一边道：“我要去接阿玄！我要去接阿玄！”
　　李渊轻轻踢了李世民一脚，笑骂道：“行！赶紧起来！”
　　李世民一个鲤鱼打挺跳起来：“好嘞！我这就走！”
　　李渊拉住李世民：“夜里不安全，明日再去。你母亲已经提前去了，中途你就能接到你母亲和阿玄，不用急。”
　　李世民眼珠子一转：“好，我去换衣服小睡一会儿。”
　　李世民蹦跳着离开。李渊扶额：“他真的长大了吗？六七岁的孩童都不会像他那样走路了！”
　　长孙康宁继续捂着嘴笑道：“郎君在父亲这里永远是没长大的孩童。”
　　李渊先叹气，叹着叹着就笑出来：“都是我太宠溺他的错。我去把他的马关起来。这孩子，绝对想晚上偷偷离开。唉，只一夜，他都等不了吗？”
　　李渊摇着头离开。
　　长孙康宁回头悄悄道：“把我备好的马藏起来，可别被父亲找到。”
　　婢女悄悄离开。
　　李世民洗了个澡，仗着自己身体好，头发没干便倒头就睡。
　　长孙康宁见他头发未干，帮他擦头发时，李世民呼呼大睡，完全没醒。
　　长孙康宁悄悄掐了李世民的脸一把，李世民仍旧闭眼酣睡。
　　她笑道：“不是说要偷跑吗？别睡醒就是第二天了。”
　　李世民翻了个身，像猫儿一样蜷缩在长孙康宁腿上。
　　长孙康宁脸一红，又掐了李世民的脸一把。
　　……
　　“嗯？这是哪？”李世民揉揉眼睛，打了个哈欠，“怎么黑黑的，灯呢？”
　　他刚说完，空间就亮起来。
　　李世民惊讶道：“啊？这不是我在大兴的家吗？我实在做梦？”
　　“应该是吧。”
　　李世民听到熟悉的声音，转头一看。
　　李玄霸如小时候一样，盘坐在放着许多靠枕的坐榻中，抱着手臂看着他。
　　李世民扑上去：“阿玄！我居然梦到你了。”
　　李玄霸伸出手抵住二哥扑上来的脸，叹气道：“这不是普通的梦。普通的梦不会思维如此清楚。”
　　李世民把李玄霸的手挡开，站在坐榻旁好奇道：“难道你心声的能力进步了？我们居然能在梦里见面？一定是因为我太想你了！”
　　李玄霸抬头看了大笑着的二哥一眼，欲言又止，最终只是又叹了口气。
　　李世民脸上的笑容淡去。
　　没有人比双生子更了解彼此。李世民从李玄霸的神情发觉出不对劲。
　　李世民声音颤抖道：“阿玄，喂，你叹什么气？发生什么事了吗？你别吓唬我啊。”
　　李玄霸抱着脑袋：“啊啊啊啊，好烦啊！我也不想刺激你，但总要把事情交代清楚吧。好烦啊！”
　　李世民按住李玄霸的肩膀：“发生什么事了？别急？我马上就来接你。哥哥马上就过来！对了，母亲已经启程了，她应该很快就到河东郡了！”
　　李玄霸嘴角下撇：“那李建成也快到太原郡了。”
　　李世民按在李玄霸肩膀上的手收紧：“什么意思？李建成怎么了？他回太原郡做什么？”
　　李玄霸叹了口气，冷静下来。
　　自己刚倒下就做梦。都托梦了，估计……
　　李玄霸嘴角扯了扯，道：“二哥，抱歉，我估计是见不到你了。”
　　李世民微微歪头，露出傻乎乎的表情：“阿玄，哥哥听不懂，什么意思？”
　　李玄霸道：“抱歉，我大概是……快死了。”
　　真的很抱歉。
