"Burned to death, *possibly*? What do you mean, *possibly*?!" Li Mi, sitting on a rock, slammed his book shut with a heavy snap.

Before him, his subordinates knelt on the ground in total terror.

Li Mi stood up, flicked his sleeves, and paced back and forth with his hands behind his back. Frowning deeply, he snapped, "If he is dead, I must see his corpse. We cannot allow even the slightest unforeseen variable!"

Han Shi'e, who had accompanied Li Mi this time to persuade Li Yuan, remarked, "He is merely a yellow-mouthed child. Is he truly worthy of such high regard from you, Military Advisor?"

Han Shi'e was the adopted son and heir of the famous Great Sui general Han Qinhu, inheriting the title of Duke of Shouguang County after Han Qinhu's death.

In his later years, Emperor Wen of Sui was deeply suspicious, and many generals who followed him met tragic ends. Han Qinhu was one of the rare few who performed meritorious service and still managed to die of old age.

However, after Yang Guang ascended the throne, he gave the Han family a cold shoulder.

Han Qinhu's younger brother, Han Sengshou, was also a fierce general with repeated distinguished service, yet Yang Guang refused to re-employ him. Whether against the Tujue, Tuyuhun, or Goguryeo, Yang Guang never gave him the opportunity to lead troops. In the eighth year of Daye, Han Sengshou passed away in Daxing.

As a "second-generation" noble, Han Shi'e had even less opportunity to carve out a name for himself. Thus, when Yang Xuangan raised his army in rebellion, Han Shi'e, recalling Yang Guang's cold callousness, went to join Yang Xuangan.

At that time, Yang Xuangan's call was met with overwhelming response, attracting many noble scions into his army—most of whom were men in similar circumstances.

Han Shi'e inherited the ferocious bravery of the Han family. Following Yang Xuangan, he achieved numerous first-scaler honors, making him one of the most vital generals under Yang Xuangan's command.

Yang Xuangan dispatching Han Shi'e to protect Li Mi showed just how highly he valued the strategist.

Having weathered the defeat at Luoyang, fleeing into the mountains, and then making a comeback, the impetuous arrogance in Yang Xuangan's heart had settled. He was gradually displaying the deep calculation and shrewdness of his late father, Yang Su, and his rapport with Li Mi grew smoother by the day.

Li Mi had originally held Yang Xuangan's shortsighted impulsiveness in contempt, but now he grew increasingly satisfied with his lord and carried out his duties with utmost devotion.

Li Mi was adept at handling interpersonal affairs and treated all generals under his lord with great warmth.

So when Han Shi'e asked, even though Li Mi was in the heat of anger, he patiently explained, "General Han, for Second Young Master Li and Third Young Master Li to achieve countless meritorious deeds at such a young age—I fear only your father could compare to them."

Han Shi'e said, "My father had no opportunity to achieve military merits in his youth. You need not over-praise them, Military Advisor; I will not take offense. Second Young Master Li is indeed formidable, but Third Young Master Li is merely a sickly scholar who happens to read well. Whether he lives or dies shouldn't matter. Don't we only need the pretext of 'Yang Guang sending someone to assassinate Li Yuan's son' to drive a wedge between Li Yuan and Yang Guang?"

Li Mi shook his head. "No matter how formidable Second Young Master Li is, human energy is finite. If it were merely fighting battles, that would be one thing. But I have heard that Zhangye has completely become their domain. While Second Young Master Li is fighting on the front lines, who manages the logistics? Who placates the populace? Given Second Young Master Li's age and the fact that he is merely the Duke of Tang's second son, I doubt many great talents have pledged allegiance to him yet."

Han Shi'e also knitted his brows. "Are you saying Third Young Master Li is the chief strategist behind Second Young Master Li?"

Li Mi replied, "Whether he is the chief strategist, I cannot say for certain. But I, too, hail from a prominent clan and understand nobility. Although the Xue, Liu, and Pei clans of Hedong are not as prominent as my Longxi Li clan, their pride runs exceedingly high. Xue Yuanjing, Liu Heng, and Pei Xingyan are the top talents among their younger generation. For Third Young Master Li to be regarded as a close friend by these three, he is unequivocally extraordinary."

Han Shi'e grew even more puzzled. "If Third Young Master Li is so formidable, why are we reaching out to Li Jiancheng? Wouldn't it be better to negotiate with Third Young Master Li to persuade his father into an alliance?"

Li Mi had not expected Han Shi'e to ask such a naive question. He burst into laughter, his brow unfurling. "General Han, our lord is Lord Yang."

Han Shi'e said, "Of course. What does that have to do with my question?"

Li Mi chuckled. "It has everything to do with it. Our coming here to urge Li Yuan to raise troops is merely to throw the world into greater chaos and further weaken the Great Sui's power. It is not so that we can go pledge allegiance to Li Yuan."

Han Shi'e gave a helpless sigh. "Military Advisor, can you just speak plainly? Don't beat around the bush; it gives me a headache. What you mean is that Li Yuan will inevitably become our lord's enemy in the contention for the world in the future. Therefore, we must support his incompetent eldest son to suppress his capable second and third sons."

Li Mi picked up his book and dusted it off. "Not suppress—if an opportunity arises, we must eliminate them. The realm of the Great Sui is bound to collapse; whether Li Yuan raises his banner now is merely a matter of whether the Sui falls a few years earlier or later. However, the threat posed by Li Shimin and Li Xuanba is far too immense. They are only sixteen years old, yet they already control the lands of Heyou. If given time to grow, they could grind the rest of us to death merely by outliving us."

Han Shi'e finally understood. "So in your eyes, Military Advisor, Li Yuan is nothing to fear—it is Second and Third Young Master Li who truly warrant your concern. This internal strife within the Li family has granted us an opportunity to slay Third Young Master Li, which is even more beneficial to our lord than persuading Li Yuan to raise troops?"

Li Mi smiled. "Precisely."

Han Shi'e remarked, "No wonder you look down on Li Yuan. In times of chaos, the realm belongs to the capable. Looking at the chaotic era of the Southern and Northern Dynasties, every mighty overlord suffered headaches over their successors. Cases of passing the mantle to brothers or even adopted sons were everywhere. If I had sons like Second Young Master Li and Third Young Master Li..."

Midway through his sentence, Han Shi'e remembered he still had a lord above him, so he immediately bit his tongue and shut his mouth.

Li Mi laughed even harder. "General Han, do not fear speaking out of turn. Our lord is broad-minded and will not blame us. I even joked with our lord once, saying that since Li Yuan and I share the Li surname, if I had sons like Second and Third Young Master Li, I would certainly find a way to establish my own domain before coming to serve him!"

Han Shi'e asked curiously, "How did our lord respond?"

Li Mi shook his head with a smile. "Our lord said that if he had such formidable sons, he would abdicate and yield his position, letting his sons conquer the world while he sat back and enjoyed the fruits of their labor."

Han Shi'e could not help but chuckle. "Our lord lacks ambition."

Li Mi tucked the book into his robes. "I chided him in the exact same way. Sigh, to think we finally found an opportunity..."

Li Mi shook his head and let out another sigh.

Those who contend for the world all carry the Mandate of Heaven; it was merely a question of whose mandate burned brighter. The twin brothers, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba, were clearly destined by the Mandate of Heaven—one in the light, one in the shade; one primary, one supporting—a pair that struck fear into hearts.

Surveying the heroes under heaven, few caught Li Mi's eye. Yet these two youths, who were only sixteen years old this year, filled him with deep vigilance.

However, their greatest enemy right now was Yang Guang, and Second and Third Young Master Li were leveraging Yang Guang's momentum. It was impossible for Li Mi to send troops directly against them.

This truly was a godsent opportunity.

Han Shi'e said, "Since Third Young Master Li is so crucial, I will personally lead troops to pursue him."

Li Mi said, "I entrust this to you, General. I shall head to Taiyuan to scope out the situation and continue persuading Li Yuan."

And sow discord along the way.

Li Jiancheng had likely already fled back to Taiyuan. If Li Mi spread the news far and wide in Taiyuan that Li Jiancheng had falsely accused Third Young Master Li, causing Third Young Master Li to perish in a sea of flames, would Second Young Master Li turn against Li Jiancheng? And whose side would Li Yuan take?

Li Mi narrowed his eyes.

...

"My distant nephew?" Wei Zheng asked in confusion.

He took the visiting card, but as soon as he opened it, his expression turned grim. "Where are they?!"

How could this bear Third Young Master's personal seal?!

Wang Bo asked in confusion, "Your kin came to seek refuge? I'll come along with you."

Since they were kin of his chief strategist, he needed to make a good impression.

Wei Zheng hesitated for a moment. Trusting Wang Bo's character, he whispered in Wang Bo's ear, "It's Third Young Master's people."

Wang Bo instantly leaped up from his seat and said with utmost gravity, "Did your kin just say someone was ill? Let us go at once! Brother Zhai, I cannot stay for today's banquet!"

Third Young Master was not only his teacher, but also his ultimate safety net! It was rare for Third Young Master's people to seek help; he could not afford a single moment of negligence.

Zhai Rang said, "Mister Wei's family has arrived? I shall go as well."

Wei Zheng cupped his hands. "My apologies. Many among the newcomers are female relatives. Though I am down on my luck, my clan is still an official family; it is improper for the female relatives to meet too many outside men."

Zhai Rang scratched his head and said, "Fair point. I forgot you scholars set great store by propriety. Go on then. If you need anything, just let me know, and I will do my absolute best to help."

Wei Zheng bowed deeply. "My thanks to Lord Zhai!"

Wei Zheng and Wang Bo hurried to the place where those claiming to be Wei Zheng's kin were temporarily staying. Luo Shixin stood waiting at the entrance.

Seeing that Wei Zheng had not come alone, he subconsciously tightened his grip on his spear.

Wei Zheng quickly called out, "Worthy nephew! You have worked hard!"

He had never met Luo Shixin, but one look at his youth informed him that he was one of Second and Third Young Master's men. Ordinary generals would never dare trust and employ such a young general.

Wang Bo noticed Luo Shixin's tension and reassured him, "Don't be nervous. I brought a physician with me."

Luo Shixin scrutinized Wei Zheng and Wang Bo, discerning who Wei Zheng was from his facial features and demeanor.

He bowed to Wei Zheng. "Greetings, Clan Uncle. The sick one is my third sister, so it is inconvenient for a male physician to examine her. My eldest sister understands medicine, but we are lacking in drugs and herbs."

The word "third" from Luo Shixin's mouth sent a violent tremor through Wei Zheng's body.

He gritted his teeth and said, "Your third sister is my junior, so there is no need to observe strict propriety between sexes for a visit. I know medicine as well; let me take a look."

Luo Shixin hesitated.

A female voice sounded through the door: "Third Sister says, please ask Clan Uncle to come inside."

Luo Shixin stepped aside to let him pass.

Wei Zheng pushed open the door and stepped inside with hurried strides.

Luo Shixin cupped his fists toward Wang Bo. "Forgive my rudeness, but I must ask Lord Knowledge-of-the-World to wait outside."

Wang Bo waved his hand. "No matter, no matter. I shall wait right here. Bring two stools and a brazier!"

After giving his orders, Wang Bo pulled Luo Shixin down to sit beside him. "Don't worry, Mister Wei's medical skills are superb. Your third sister will surely be fine."

Wang Bo was burning with anxiousness inside.

Luo Shixin's address of "Third Sister" had also led Wang Bo to speculate: Could it be Third Young Master Li disguised as a woman coming to seek refuge with him?

But Third Young Master Li was heavily relied upon and favored by the dog emperor, and should have just returned to Taiyuan Commandery to wed. He and Wei Zheng had even sent people disguised as merchants to secretly deliver gifts, lamenting that they could not attend in person.

It had only been a few months since the marriage! How, how could...

Wang Bo wanted to inquire, but feared Luo Shixin would misunderstand. He could only cast anxious glances toward the doorway repeatedly, waiting for Wei Zheng to come out.

After Wei Zheng entered the house, the voice of the female who had called him in deepened: "Are you the Wei Xuancheng whom Third Brother praised?"

Wei Zheng leaped in shock.

The "woman" beckoned to Wei Zheng, "Come over quickly, Third Brother is calling for you."

Filled with shock and doubt, Wei Zheng followed the "woman" into the inner chamber.

A charming girl lay coughing on the sickbed, while another slightly more mature-looking woman wiped the sweat from her forehead.

"Xuancheng, let me introduce you. This is my wife, Yuwen Zhu; you may address her as Lady Zhu. This is Fifth Brother whom I mentioned to you before, Li Zhiyun. And waiting outside the door is Second Brother's fierce general, Luo Shixin." Suppressing his coughs, Li Xuanba squeezed out a weak smile. "Shixin will fill you in on the details later. First, take Lady Zhu to get the medicine... *cough, cough*."

"Third Young Master!" Wei Zheng stumbled forward a few steps, throwing himself before the sickbed. "You... how did you..."

Yuwen Zhu said calmly, "Please take me to get the medicine first, Clan Uncle. We can discuss other matters later. Third Sister has been without medicine for a full day now."

Wei Zheng scrambled to his feet. "Right, right! Follow me!"

Wei Zheng took Yuwen Zhu out to gather medicine, forgetting to inform Li Xuanba that Wang Bo was waiting outside.

However, Li Zhiyun caught sight of Wang Bo through the door crack and notified Li Xuanba.

Coughing between words, Li Xuanba said, "Wei Xuancheng trusts Lord Knowledge-of-the-World, and I trust Wei Xuancheng. Invite Lord Knowledge-of-the-World inside."

Li Zhiyun invited Wang Bo into the room, though this time he kept his female voice, keeping a trick up his sleeve.

Wang Bo entered the room with an uneasy heart. Looking at the young maiden on the sickbed, he dared not claim recognition.

Li Xuanba mocked himself, "I have been sickly and small of stature since childhood. Disguising myself as a woman—is it not quite lifelike?"

Wang Bo asked anxiously, "Third Young Master, what happened to you? Did that dog emperor harm you?"

Li Xuanba said, "It was family misfortune, combined with an unknown enemy striking from the shadows along the way, that left me in such dire straits. However, with my arrangements, the situation should improve swiftly. I shall hide here with you for a while, Lord Knowledge-of-the-World, and leave once the situation clears up. Rest assured, I will not bring you trouble."

Wang Bo let out a bitter smile. "I am a rebel; I do not fear trouble. On the contrary, Third Young Master, you must hide yourself well."

Li Xuanba said, "Then I must rely on your assistance, Lord Knowledge-of-the-World."

Wang Bo said, "Set your mind at ease, Third Young Master. You trusted me and were willing to seek me out in your time of peril—I will never betray your trust! Tomorrow, I shall leave Wagang Fort and return to Qi Commandery!"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "Since you already have a grand scheme, Lord Knowledge-of-the-World, it is better to complete it before departing. Disguised as a woman and tucked away in the inner chambers, I will not attract attention."

Wang Bo nodded. "I shall do as Third Young Master says."

Li Xuanba joked weakly, "I will not eat and drink your food for free while staying here. Lady Zhu is a skilled physician. If you or Wagang Fort have female relatives who fall ill, you may ask Lady Zhu to treat them. Once my health recovers, I can also act as your temporary strategist."

Wang Bo smiled, cupping his fists. "Then Third Young Master must recover quickly so that I may seek your counsel! I will not disturb your rest any longer. If Third Young Master needs anything at all, please inform me immediately."

Li Xuanba bade Li Zhiyun to see Wang Bo off.

When Li Zhiyun returned, he sighed, "Third Brother, you haven't spent much time with Wei Xuancheng, and you've only met Wang Bo once. Yet their concern for you is so deep and genuine."

As the son of the Duke of Tang's only concubine, Li Zhiyun had learned to read people's expressions and demeanor from a young age. He could tell at a single glance that Wei Zheng and Wang Bo's concern for Li Xuanba was sincere.

Li Xuanba coughed, "'Some grow old together yet remain strangers; others hit it off like lifelong friends at first meeting.' That is precisely how it is... *cough, cough, cough*."

Li Zhiyun poured Li Xuanba a cup of water. "Third Brother, you can rest and recuperate in peace now. Leave everything else to us."

Li Xuanba smiled softly. "Mm."

When Wei Zheng took Yuwen Zhu out to fetch medicine, he wept and complained to everyone he met about how his distant nephew's family was suffering, cursing the dog emperor as a monster.

Hearing this, Zhai Rang felt deeply moved. He ordered his men to tell Wei Zheng to ask for whatever medicine he needed, promising that if it was not available here, he would send men into the city in disguise to buy it.

Zhai Rang said to Xu Shiji, "That dog emperor has truly ruined countless families."

Xu Shiji sighed, "This is the first time I have seen Mister Wei so distraught. My family possesses some wealth; please grant me permission to return home for a trip, Lord Zhai."

Zhai Rang said, "Go on, and be careful."

Xu Shiji cupped his hands. "Understood."

After asking Wei Zheng what remedies were needed, Xu Shiji secretly snuck back to his home to gather medicines. He then brought gold and silver to sneak into the commandery city to purchase tonic supplements, delivering them all to Wei Zheng.

Wei Zheng thanked him profusely, tears streaming uncontrollably down his face, making Xu Shiji's heart ache with sympathy.

Luo Shixin cupped his fists toward Xu Shiji. "Brother Xu, I shall never forget your grace! Should you ever face peril in the future, I will surely save you!"

Xu Shiji chuckled. "It was merely a small effort, hardly worth calling a grand favor. You are so young—focus on surviving this chaotic world first before talking of the future."

Luo Shixin muttered under his breath: *Don't look down on me.*

Wang Bo enjoyed an exceptional reputation, not only among the rebel forces, but also held considerable influence among the powerful local magnates.

He personally went door to door to ask for help, quickly amassing a vast quantity of precious medicinal herbs.

Seeing Wang Bo go to such lengths for Wei Zheng's kin, Zhai Rang could not help reflecting on himself, feeling he had not been good enough to his own subordinates.

Coincidentally, his family members were growing increasingly arrogant and domineering. Zhai Rang used Wang Bo's noble conduct to admonish his kin, while taking extra care to show empathy toward his followers.

Luo Shixin wandered among the rebel forces for a time, realizing that these "popular bandits" were not as devoid of humanity as he had envisioned. At least the subordinates of Zhai Rang and Wang Bo were not much different from the soldiers he had seen in General Zhang's army, stirring a deep resonance in his heart.

Under the suppression of potent medicine, Li Xuanba's high fever finally ceased to relapse.

With Li Xuanba's consent, Luo Shixin temporarily joined Wang Bo's forces to help Wagang Fort fight the Sui army, honing his martial arts skills in the process.

Li Zhiyun continued to disguise himself as a woman, acting as a guard for Li Xuanba and Yuwen Zhu.

Li Xuanba thought his fatal ordeal was likely coming to an end.

However, on the second day after his fever had completely broken, as Li Xuanba paced slowly around the room trying to regain his physical strength, a sudden, suffocating pain seized his chest.

Yuwen Zhu stood before Li Xuanba, holding out her hands like one encouraging a toddler learning to walk, beaming as she urged him to take a few more steps.

Then, clutching his chest, Li Xuanba slowly collapsed right in front of her.

"Sanlang?!"

"Third Brother?!"

Li Xuanba gasped frantically for air, his vision gradually turning blurry.

In a split second, he recognized his condition.

This was... myocarditis brought on by high fever from pneumonia, was it not? Come to think of it, the Li clan had a hereditary history of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases to begin with. It was truly no surprise at all.

As Li Xuanba closed his eyes, he let out a slow, long sigh.

The heavens harbor intent to kill; the earth harbors intent to kill; humanity harbors intent to kill.

Wave after wave, relentless and overwhelming.

The heavens... were determined to see him dead.

...

"Father, I don't care what affairs you have! Ah-Xuan wrote asking me to pick him up, so I must go!" After receiving consecutive urgent letters delivered by Cold-Hook Crow-Feather, no matter how Li Yuan argued that "we are very busy, we'll send someone else," Li Shimin refused to back down.

The sixteen-year-old youth flopped down onto the floor with crisp efficiency and actually began rolling around.

Li Yuan didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "You are sixteen years old, not six! Get up! Guanyinbei is laughing at you!"

Zhangsun Kangning covered her mouth, her eyes curving into crescents. "I didn't laugh."

Li Shimin rolled across the floor, yelling as he rolled, "I want to pick up Ah-Xuan! I want to pick up Ah-Xuan!"

Li Yuan gave Li Shimin a gentle kick and scolded with a smile, "Alright! Get up this instant!"

Li Shimin executed a carp flip and bounced up. "Alright! I'll be off then!"

Li Yuan held Li Shimin back. "It's unsafe at night; go tomorrow. Your mother has already set out ahead of time. You will meet up with your mother and Ah-Xuan along the way, so there is no need to rush."

Li Shimin's eyes darted around. "Fine, I'll go change my clothes and take a quick nap."

Li Shimin skipped away merrily. Li Yuan pressed his hand to his forehead. "Has he truly grown up? Even a six- or seven-year-old child wouldn't walk like that!"

Zhangsun Kangning continued covering her mouth with a soft laugh. "My lord will always be an ungrown child in Father's eyes."

Li Yuan sighed at first, but ended up chuckling. "It is all my fault for spoiling him so. I'll go lock up his horse. That boy definitely plans to sneak off tonight. Sigh, can he not even wait a single night?"

Li Yuan shook his head and departed.

Zhangsun Kangning turned around and whispered softly, "Hide the horse I prepared; don't let Father find it."

Her maid quietly slipped away.

Li Shimin took a bath and, relying on his robust constitution, fell fast asleep before his hair had even dried.

Seeing that his hair was still wet, Zhangsun Kangning helped dry it for him. Li Shimin was sleeping so soundly, snoring softly, that he didn't wake up at all.

Zhangsun Kangning gently pinched Li Shimin's cheek, but he remained fast asleep with his eyes closed.

She smiled softly, "Didn't you say you were going to sneak off? Don't sleep straight through until tomorrow."

Li Shimin rolled over, curling up on Zhangsun Kangning's lap like a cat.

Zhangsun Kangning blushed, giving his cheek another light pinch.

...

"Hm? Where is this?" Li Shimin rubbed his eyes and let out a yawn. "Why is it so pitch black? Where are the lamps?"

The moment he spoke, the surrounding space lit up.

Li Shimin exclaimed in surprise, "Huh? Isn't this my home in Daxing? Am I dreaming?"

"I suppose so."

Hearing that familiar voice, Li Shimin turned his head to look.

Just like when they were young, Li Xuanba sat cross-legged on a couch lined with cushions, arms crossed as he looked at him.

Li Shimin pounced forward. "Ah-Xuan! I actually dreamed of you!"

Li Xuanba extended his hand to block his second brother's lunging face, sighing, "This isn't an ordinary dream. In an ordinary dream, one's thoughts wouldn't be this clear."

Li Shimin brushed Li Xuanba's hand away and stood beside the couch, asking curiously, "Could it be that your mind-reading ability has advanced? We can actually meet in a dream? It must be because I missed you so much!"

Li Xuanba looked up at his laughing second brother. He opened his mouth to speak but stopped, ultimately letting out another quiet sigh.

The smile on Li Shimin's face faded away.

No one understood twins better than twins themselves. From Li Xuanba's expression, Li Shimin sensed that something was terribly wrong.

Li Shimin's voice trembled slightly. "Ah-Xuan... hey, what are you sighing for? Did something happen? Don't scare me like this."

Li Xuanba clutched his head. "Ahhh, this is so frustrating! I don't want to upset you either, but I have to explain things clearly, don't I? So frustrating!"

Li Shimin gripped Li Xuanba's shoulders. "What happened? Don't panic! I'm coming to pick you up right away! Brother is coming over right now! Oh right, Mother has already set out; she should reach Hedong Commandery very soon!"

The corners of Li Xuanba's mouth turned downward. "Then Li Jiancheng is also about to arrive at Taiyuan Commandery."

Li Shimin's grip on Li Xuanba's shoulders tightened. "What do you mean? What happened to Li Jiancheng? Why is he returning to Taiyuan Commandery?"

Li Xuanba took a sigh and calmed himself down.

He had dreamed right after collapsing. Appearing in a dream like this... meant he was likely...

The corner of Li Xuanba's mouth twitched into a faint smile. "Second Brother... I'm sorry. I don't think I'll be able to see you again."

Li Shimin tilted his head slightly, a blank, foolish expression washing over his face. "Ah-Xuan... Brother doesn't understand. What do you mean?"

Li Xuanba said softly, "I'm sorry. I am probably... dying soon."

I am truly, deeply sorry.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第135章 我想与文明同寿
chunks.chineseText:
第135章 我想与文明同寿

坐榻上的李玄霸垂着头看着放在膝盖上的手。
　　坐榻前的李世民低着头看着弟弟头顶的发髻。
　　两人沉默许久。
　　李玄霸挨不住沉默， 抬头挤出笑容道：“我还以为哥你会号啕大哭。”
　　李世民神思恍惚：“我……我哭不出来。”
　　李玄霸嘴唇动了动，双手使劲砸了一下腿，眼眶通红：“我很努力了！”
　　李世民伸出手， 又将手缩回去：“哥哥知道， 知道……阿玄很努力……真的很努力……”
　　李世民脑海中恍惚出现弟弟小时候的模样。
　　那时弟弟的心肺就很不好， 多跑几步路就捂着胸口喊累，请来的御医都说弟弟可能一辈子都需要静养。
　　但弟弟很努力地锻炼、吃药。他都能在草原上尽情纵马，自己都快忘记弟弟先天体弱了。
　　李玄霸抹了一把脸， 又挤出笑容：“不知道这梦的时间有多长，我们抓紧时间。”
　　李世民连连点头：“好，好……让一让。”
　　李世民像小时候那样挤上了坐榻， 和李玄霸挨着靠着坐着。
　　“哥，首先我要向你道歉， 我背着你去算计李元吉， 导致了这次的事。”
　　“啊？你算计李元吉做什么？”
　　“因为这家伙必须死！”李玄霸眉眼间透出一股戾气，“不借着杨广的势杀了他，等父亲起兵后，我们就不可能动得了他。”
　　李世民道：“好吧，或许是这样， 但为什么瞒着我？”
　　李玄霸抱着手臂道：“因为哥年纪还小，不能承受兄弟相残的痛苦……哎哟。”
　　李世民伸手给了李玄霸一下， 道：“哥哥我没有这么脆弱。从头把你……把这件事详细说一遍。”
　　李玄霸点头。
　　他首先从那一步虽然是闲棋，但一定会发挥作用的计谋说起。
　　李玄霸原本以为父亲会严加管教李元吉，若管教不成， 就会对李元吉彻底失望。
　　没有父亲的支持， 李元吉就对他和哥完全没有威胁。
　　谁知道父亲的“严加看管”如此粗暴， 李元吉越发危险， 父亲还又被李元吉的表象迷惑了。
　　发现李元吉越发朝着反社会人格发展，李玄霸做了许多年心理准备，终于下定决心，要借势除掉李元吉。
　　这是李玄霸第一次主动害人性命。
　　“我这个计谋靠的是信息差。在家里人看来，我们和二表兄关系很亲近，又素来讲义气，如果二表兄向我们托孤，我们一定会帮忙。”
　　“但在杨广和其他朝臣眼中，二表兄成为太子之后，朝中大臣没有不奉承讨好太子的，只有我们绕着二表兄走。二表兄当了这么多年太子，我们仅仅与他见了两次，这两次还都是他主动来寻我们。”
　　李世民道：“所以在皇帝和朝中公卿眼中，我们反而是与太子最不亲近的人。”
　　李玄霸点头，继续道：“再者，他们不知道二表兄还是齐王时，府中就几乎被杨广渗透成了漏子。”
　　李世民叹气：“二表兄被立为太子后，皇帝更是对二表兄严加监视。且皇家子嗣本就珍贵，每一个孩子都有记载，外室子也不例外。没有人比皇帝更清楚二表兄有没有一个七八岁的私生子。但阿玄，你怎么知道李元吉真的会去诬告？”
　　李玄霸道：“我不知道。我只是丢了这个诱饵，如果李元吉不上钩，就说明他命不该绝；如果李元吉上钩，那就是他先有害人之心，我是正当防卫。”
　　李世民又给了李玄霸脑袋一下，无奈道：“如果你把这件事告诉我，我和你意见一致。以后不准瞒着我。”
　　李玄霸道：“好，下次一定不瞒着你。”
　　下次……
　　兄弟俩眼神同时一黯，又同时默契地跳过这个词。
　　李世民道：“以你的计谋，你本应该很安全，出了什么意外？”
　　李玄霸按了按眉间，道：“第一件意外是李建成被丁郡丞询问后，口不择言说都是我的错，帮我认罪了。丁荣放他回太原郡，软禁了我。”
　　李世民放在膝盖上的双手握紧：“他疯了吗？这种事难道不是先否认？！”
　　李玄霸道：“丁荣用族叔的事激励他‘大义灭亲’。”
　　杨坚篡位前夕，梁州刺史李璋联合赵王宇文招，试图杀杨坚救北周。
　　李璋的侄子李安向杨坚告发李璋，大义灭亲。李璋身死，李安和兄弟李哲都加官晋爵。
　　李璋和李安的父亲李蔚，与李渊的父亲都是亲兄弟，西魏大柱国李虎之子。
　　丁荣用唐国公长辈旧事说动李建成“大义灭亲”。
　　私藏太子私生子并不能算谋逆，陛下大度，不会牵连家人。如果李建成能大义灭亲，唐国公和李建成说不定还会被皇帝嘉奖，就像是李安和李哲被隋文帝重用一样。
　　李世民经李玄霸提醒，才想起长辈的这桩旧事。
　　他讥笑道：“如果大义灭亲，他不仅会无事，还能除掉我俩这个眼中钉。唐国公府中就无人与他争斗了。”
　　李玄霸没回答。他不知道李建成是否有这个心思，还是单纯吓破胆，但李建成抛下他逃跑是事实。
　　丁荣告诉李建成，可将这事透露给自己，但李建成反而瞒着更紧。
　　或许李建成以为丁荣是在考验他对皇帝的“忠诚”吧。
　　李玄霸道：“历史中李建成也会丢弃兄弟。父亲本该在几年后才成为太原、河东慰抚使。他仍旧如现在一样，自己带着你在太原剿匪戍边，让李建成带着李元吉、李智云在河东结交英俊。”
　　李世民挑眉：“他把小五丢了？”
　　李玄霸道：“是啊。历史中说，因为小五年幼，所以他没有带走小五。小五遇害时年仅十四岁。”
　　李世民哼笑：“小五和李元吉同年，有多年幼？且小五很小就展现出骑射的天赋，十四岁的少年都能参军了，只要给小五一匹马一把弓，小五自己就能逃回太原郡。”
　　李玄霸淡淡道：“或许小五当时正好生病了？”
　　李世民讽刺道：“谁知道呢？说不定他是把小五交给隋朝官吏，换得自己离开。怪不得你从小就讨好他，你是担心自己被他丢掉啊。你早告诉我，我绝对不会让你单独和他处一地。”
　　李玄霸在心里道，这不是怕你承受不住吗？
