Chapter 137: Whoever Harms My Mother Shall Die

The periods during which Li Xuanba's consciousness drifted outside his body grew shorter and less frequent, yet the physical agony he suffered intensified with each passing day.

Wagang Stronghold had limited access to fine medicines. His fragile condition required vast quantities of rare herbs to keep him alive, forcing Sun Simiao and Yuwen Zhu to devise an alternate solution: extracting active essences from cheap, common herbs to treat him.

Their inspiration stemmed from the essential oils Li Xuanba had produced earlier.

If flowers, leaves, and other raw ingredients could yield essential oils and hydrosols when distilled or soaked in spirits—extracting the very essence of those materials—then by that same logic, medicinal herbs subjected to distillation or alcohol immersion should yield concentrated medicinal essences as well.

All medicine carries a degree of toxicity. Consuming massive quantities of raw decoctions was not only unbearable for the stomach, but trace compounds could also accumulate toxic buildup, damaging the body. Extracting pure medicinal essences might bypass this harmful side effect altogether.

In truth, Sun Simiao and Yuwen Zhu's concept was rather naive.

What distillation and spirits extraction produced was not necessarily pure active essence, but merely the lipophilic substances within the raw ingredients. Even if it were the desired compound, the concentrated extract itself could harbor potent toxins, meaning excessive doses would still yield side effects.

Yet in an age when technology could not probe the microscopic world, traditional medicine was a "black box." The earliest remedies had almost entirely relied on trial and error—"I reckon this works"—before testing their hypotheses on animals and humans.

Since the medical arts Master Sun Simiao and his disciple Yuwen Zhu possessed could not cure Li Xuanba, they had no choice but to treat a dead horse as a living one, gritting their teeth to test their whimsical ideas on him.

After all, the absolute worst outcome was merely succumbing to his illness.

Li Xuanba suffered immensely during these treatments.

While traditional herbal brews had bizarre odors, one could still pinch their nose and swallow them down with water. But the concentrated essences extracted by the master-disciple duo bore tastes so pungent and monstrous that even with his formidable willpower, Li Xuanba could barely suppress his dry heaves.

Take, for instance, the most cost-effective extract the duo devised—an oily substance extracted from ginger, scallions, and garlic distilled directly or soaked in spirits before being redistilled. Taking it felt as though his tongue, throat, esophagus, and stomach were all burning simultaneously.

Yet Li Xuanba himself lacked formal medical knowledge. He only knew nitroglycerin could relieve angina and heart failure because the elderly principal who had helped him in his past life took the medication; noticing it shared its name with high explosives, he had looked up a bit of information back then.

Although Li Xuanba vaguely recalled reading somewhere that myocarditis seemed to require antibiotics, he had not the slightest clue how to produce crude antibiotics by primitive methods. Since he was powerless on that front, the only thing he could do was fully cooperate with whatever concoctions Sun Simiao and Yuwen Zhu produced, no matter how excruciating the process of taking the medicine was.

He ate and vomited, vomited and ate, until eventually even drinking water triggered retching. In less than half a month, the slight fullness Li Xuanba had painstakingly nursed back into his cheeks over the past few years vanished into hollow gauntness, rendering him even thinner than in his childhood.

Only then did Sun Simiao realize his "concentrated medicine" was overly destructive to the stomach, prompting him to adjust the prescription to include stomach-soothing remedies.

Yet no matter how he nurtured the stomach, the overwhelmingly abrasive taste of the medicine could not be avoided. Had there been abundant honey to mix in, the harsh flavor might have been barely suppressed. But Wagang Stronghold lacked such luxuries, leaving Li Xuanba with no choice but to endure it through sheer force of will.

After being tossed back and forth like this, Li Xuanba felt it was a genuine miracle that he was still alive.

While testing the new medicines, Li Xuanba also brought up the topic of nitroglycerin with Sun Simiao.

The formula for black powder was simple, but its power was lacking; the black powder he currently used was good for little more than making loud noises to intimidate people.

Li Xuanba had once tried to synthesize modern gunpowder to completely alter the tides of war, but no matter how hard he racked his brain, he could not deduce the exact formula.

If he simply attempted literal trials—such as mixing crude glycerin with nitric acid—it would very likely cost lives. Thus, Li Xuanba had abandoned the endeavor.

Suspecting Sun Simiao might have accidentally refined nitroglycerin, Li Xuanba warned the physician about the extreme danger of this "medicine" while hoping he might obtain a precise prescription from him.

But Sun Simiao was utterly baffled.

"What nitroglycerin?" Sun Simiao wracked his brain, unable to recall anything. "I did mix in saltpeter, but I certainly did not add the kind of strong acid you described."

Li Xuanba opened his mouth, then hesitated, pressing a hand to his forehead with a sigh.

It seemed Physician Sun's creation of nitroglycerin, much like ancient alchemists accidentally discovering black powder in history, was a pure stroke of luck.

To replicate this formula again would likely require numerous perilous experiments.

Perhaps in the future, when he had time to prepare proper safety measures, he could attempt to recreate Physician Sun's alchemical process—but not now.

Li Xuanba instructed Physician Sun to carefully preserve his records of refining medicine with glycerin, and had the idle Li Zhiyun make several transcriptions for future verification.

For now... he had to endure the torment of testing new remedies and strive for a speedy recovery.

When Sun Simiao realized he had unwittingly concocted such a dangerous substance, lingering terror gripped his heart. Yet, thinking of how this medicine could alleviate heart failure, he could not bring himself to destroy the refining records.

In the end, he chose to trust that Li Xuanba would handle this lethal substance appropriately.

Even if he destroyed the records, others might eventually create it anyway. Furthermore, Li Xuanba seemed so knowledgeable about it—perhaps people overseas were already using it expertly.

Sun Simiao knew how vast the world beyond the seas was. If foreign nations across the seas possessed such a dangerous medicine, the Central Plains ought to master it as well, lest they be caught at a disadvantage.

As for the fact that this deadly substance could take countess lives, Sun Simiao could only bury the burden deep within his heart, bearing guilt and fear for the rest of his life.

Li Xuanba knew revealing the nature of nitroglycerin would place heavy psychological stress on the physician. Yet after careful consideration, he chose to explain everything to Sun Simiao in detail anyway.

Even with the emotional burden, Sun Simiao would surely prefer to understand the consequences of his alchemy rather than risk losing his life—or the lives of those around him—in ignorant disaster.

***

While Li Xuanba was struggling desperately to survive, Li Shimin arrived at Zhuo Commandery.

As they drew near Zhuo Commandery, Yu Shinan hesitated for a long time before pulling Li Shimin aside to advise him on how to handle Yang Guang.

"I know you hope His Majesty will deliver justice for you, but I fear His Majesty will not grant your wish. If you insist on punishing Li Yuanji and Li Jiancheng, I am afraid His Majesty will only grow suspicious of you," Yu Shinan said. "Do not view His Majesty as an elder who will back you up, nor as a wise sovereign who will redress your grievances."

Li Shimin lowered his head, his fists clenched tight. "Must I simply stand by and watch Li Yuanji and Li Jiancheng harm Ah Xuan without paying any price whatsoever?"

Yu Shinan said, "Li Jiancheng merely failed to protect the Third Master. Even if you accuse him before His Majesty, in His Majesty's eyes, this will instead appear as proof of Li Jiancheng's loyalty to him."

Li Shimin took a deep breath. "I know, I know! I know Father will protect him too! I cannot make His Majesty punish him! But what about Li Yuanji? He falsely accused Ah Xuan..."

Yu Shinan patted Li Shimin's shoulder, soothing his disciple's emotions. "You cannot request His Majesty to punish Li Yuanji, but your parents can. As a brother, you cannot blame Li Yuanji for his false accusations, but your parents can accuse him of unfilial and unbrotherly conduct."

Yu Shinan analyzed Yang Guang's temperament for Li Shimin. This was the first time he had ever spoken of the Emperor's flaws to another person.

Yu Shinan's elder brother, Yu Shiji, had become one of Yang Guang's most favored ministers. Yu Shinan was no less capable than his brother and was equally adept at reading people's expressions and subtle cues.

He simply refused to become another "Yu Shiji."

Yang Guang had once told Yu Shinan that he disliked remonstrations, and so Yu Shinan never offered a single admonishment to Yang Guang for the rest of his life. He understood clearly that the Emperor meant what he said, knowing how to avoid danger while maintaining his core principles.

Though Yu Shinan had never been promoted, serving merely as an Imperial Diarist by Yang Guang's side, he was able to remain a close attendant without being exiled despite his personality being unliked by the Emperor—a true testament to his formidable skill.

Originally, Yu Shinan had only taught Li Shimin and Li Xuanba calligraphy. This was the first time he shared the accumulated wisdom of his official career with Li Shimin.

"His Majesty cares tremendously about his prestige. Being unfilial, unbrotherly, and unmerciful himself, he cannot tolerate unfilial, unbrotherly, or unmerciful behavior in others. Yet this intolerance depends on who the subject is. For instance, Li Yuanji is unworthy of his notice, but you hold the military and civil power of He-You. Thus, Li Yuanji's false accusation is seen as keeping watch over you in his eyes; if you hold a grudge against Li Yuanji for it, you are being unbrotherly—and harboring disloyal intentions."

Seeing the look of utter incomprehension on Li Shimin's face, Yu Shinan sighed. "Do you know how Pei Yun re-examined the household registries?"

Li Shimin recalled for a moment, then grunted dully, "By having the common people inform on one another."

Yu Shinan said, "Not just for re-registering households. After Yang Xuangan's rebellion, His Majesty also ordered officials to inform on each other. Irrespective of evidence, people were thrown into prison first. Officials turned on one another, dragging countless innocent souls into ruin."

Li Shimin said, "It wasn't just Yang Xuangan's rebellion. When banditry erupted everywhere, His Majesty ordered the populace to report one another, summarily executing suspected thieves on the spot. Powerful gentry colluded with corrupt officials, arbitrarily labeling people as bandits, destroying countless families and seizing their lands and homes."

Yu Shinan nodded mournfully. "So you must understand that even if His Majesty trusts you and the Third Master, you cannot demand punishment for Li Yuanji's false accusations. Because His Majesty actively encourages denunciation. If he punishes Li Yuanji, how can officials and commoners bite at each other as he desires?"

Li Shimin's breathing slowed. The anger and unwillingness on his face settled back into a cold, serene calm. "I will not ask His Majesty to punish Li Yuanji and Li Jiancheng. I will avenge myself."

Yu Shinan's heart trembled.

He had originally intended for Li Shimin to let go of his hatred. Li Yuanji and Li Jiancheng were Li Shimin's brothers—how could Li Shimin turn against his own kin? His moral conscience would normally not allow him to hear a disciple say such words without reprimand.

Yet even a gentleman harbored selfish thoughts, just as he himself practiced self-preservation before Yang Guang.

Thinking of Li Xuanba and the deep bond between the two brothers, Yu Shinan could not bring himself to utter a single word of rebuke.

Ultimately, he offered no further advice on that matter, merely shifting the topic: "You need not worry about feeling overly stifled either. You cannot touch Li Yuanji, but the Duke of Tang will certainly not spare him. If left unchecked, Li Yuanji will target the Duke next. His Majesty thinks nothing of Li Yuanji and will not confer any official titles upon him; all of Li Yuanji's backing relies on the Duke of Tang. Your urgent priority is to let His Majesty understand that even though the Third Master..."

Yu Shinan let out a somber sigh and said, "Even though the Third Master's life and death remain unknown, you harbor no resentment toward His Majesty. It is best if you find another target to blame—be it rebel bandits, Yang Xuangan, or the Tujue. Tell His Majesty that your hatred is focused elsewhere and will not affect your loyalty to him. Given His Majesty's nature, if you pin the blame on the Tujue, he might be even more pleased."

Li Shimin said, "The arsonists were most likely rebel bandits or Yang Xuangan's men."

Yu Shinan replied, "But His Majesty does not *want* it to be rebel bandits or Yang Xuangan. He insists on campaigning against Goguryeo despite the chaos in the Central Plains precisely to deceive himself into believing the Sui Empire is not in turmoil, and that the rebels and Yang Xuangan have been crushed into insignificance. In His Majesty's eyes, the only true enemies left are the foreign barbarians he has yet to subjugate."

The corner of Li Shimin's mouth twitched. "Teacher, I understand. I guarded against the Eastern Tujue, drawing their hatred, so they seized the chance to set the fire and harm Ah Xuan. I wish to return to Zhangye immediately to reorganize border affairs and avenge Ah Xuan."

Yu Shinan sighed. "That will make His Majesty pleased. He will agree to let you return to Zhangye immediately without stripping away your military command."

Li Shimin murmured softly, "How stifling."

Yu Shinan hesitated briefly before raising his hand to stroke the head of his now-grown disciple. "It is indeed stifling. Remember this indignation, and gather your strength well. Your teacher knows you possess grand ambitions."

Li Shimin uttered a nasal "Mm."

Yu Shinan said, "Take this matter as a lesson as well. Do not become a ruler like His Majesty. Encouraging officials and commoners to denounce one another, ignoring reality to see only what one wants to see... none of these are the actions of a wise sovereign."

*They are the actions of a ruler destined to destroy his own dynasty,* Yu Shinan added silently in his heart.

Li Shimin nodded heavily. "I will remember."

Yu Shinan patted his disciple's shoulder once more. "I know how grieved you are right now, yet unable to shed tears. Go find some ginger juice to smoke your eyes and have a good cry. If you do not release these emotions now, you will not be able to control your expressions smoothly before His Majesty."

Li Shimin grit his teeth and forced a smile. "Alright."

Though Yu Shinan had told Li Shimin to use ginger juice to irritate his eyes, he had actually already prepared a handkerchief soaked in ginger juice.

He led Li Shimin to a spot slightly removed from the camp, patted a nearby rock for them to sit down together, and handed the cloth to Li Shimin.

Li Shimin wiped his eyes with the handkerchief, and tears instantly welled up, stung by the ginger juice.

The moment the tears fell, the emotions locked within Li Shimin's chest surged forth like a bursting dam.

He buried his face in his knees, wrapping his arms tightly around his legs, curling into a ball as his entire body trembled uncontrollably.

Yu Shinan gently stroked his trembling disciple's back, his own eyes reddening as tears spilled down his cheeks.

*Cry, cry it out... Even if crying doesn't make it better, at least you won't be crushed by grief.*

Sensing the warm comfort of his teacher's touch upon his back, Li Shimin bit his lip so hard that his mouth filled with the metallic taste of blood.

Ever since childhood, he had been teased by Ah Xuan for being a crybaby.

*"Second Brother, you're way too emotional. You burst into tears at the drop of a hat—you even wail out loud reading history books! Crying is one thing, but must you be so loud? My ears are ringing!"*

That was always how Li Shimin cried. He would yell at the top of his lungs to vent his emotions completely; he might not shed many tears, but his wailing was guaranteed to be thunderous. And once he finished howling, his mood would instantly lift. No matter how painful, difficult, or infuriating the situation was, he could dust himself off, stand up, and sprint forward with a smile.

Ah Xuan had always dismissed his tears as dumping emotional garbage—once he finished crying, it was over, never kept to heart.

But now, Li Shimin buried his face deeply between his knees and arms, biting his lip until he could hardly breathe, weeping without making a single sound.

Even Yu Shinan, sitting right beside him, could not hear a single sob.

Heartbroken, Yu Shinan murmured, "Er-lang, you can cry out loud. We are far from the camp; your subordinates won't hear you."

Li Shimin shook his head violently while clutching his legs, wiping his tears against the hem of his tunic and trousers.

Yu Shinan let out a soft sigh and could only continue patting his disciple's back gently.

He did not know if this offered any solace to Li Shimin, but it was better than doing nothing at all.

***

After a thorough cry, Li Shimin's composure returned to normal, just as Yu Shinan had anticipated. He could now convincingly feign grief and pain, rather than wearing a cold, detached mask. Before Yang Guang, he should be able to pass scrutiny.

After Li Shimin submitted his audience request, Yang Guang—who was nominally leading the imperial expedition in person while actually waiting in Zhuo Commandery for news of victory in Goguryeo—summoned him in confusion.

Li Shimin knelt before Yang Guang, his forehead pressed to the floor, sobbing as he informed the Emperor of how Ah Xuan had been harmed by the Tujue. 

"This subject begs to return to Zhangye, prepare for war against the Tujue, and avenge my brother!" Li Shimin wept. "I know Your Majesty is currently campaigning against Goguryeo and cannot deploy troops against the Tujue. This subject only wishes to return to the Tujue border and fight them myself! They killed my brother, and I will wipe out their entire clan!"

Yang Guang was surprised. "The Tujue actually invaded Hedong Commandery and burned Third Master Li to death?"

Li Shimin's body shuddered. The words denying his brother's death stuck in his throat, and he swallowed them back with great difficulty.

Yang Guang turned to Pei Shiju and asked, "The Eastern Tujue dare to be so audacious?"

An inexplicable emotion flickered in Pei Shiju's eyes. He glanced at Li Shimin before respectfully replying to Yang Guang, "The Khan of the Eastern Tujue no longer obeys Your Majesty's summons, and taking advantage of Your Majesty's personal expedition to Goguryeo, they have repeatedly raided Great Sui's borders. Their wolfish ambitions are already blatantly clear. Unable to defeat the Duke of Tang and Li Er-lang who guard the border, they retaliated against Third Master Li instead. This indeed fits the treacherous nature of barbarians."

Yang Guang wrinkled his brows. "They truly hold the Great Sui in contempt. Once I conquer Goguryeo, I will surely lead a grand army to crush the Eastern Tujue!"

Li Shimin declared, "When Your Majesty personally campaigns against the Eastern Tujue, please appoint this subject as your vanguard!"

Yang Guang sighed and said to Li Shimin, "Rise. You have indeed suffered an unprovoked disaster this time. Yet it was also due to your own carelessness. You must take this as a warning."

Li Shimin respectfully replied, "Yes, your servant will engrave it upon his heart."

Just as his teacher had predicted, though Yang Guang did not trust Li Yuanji, he felt no aversion toward Li Yuanji's false accusations. In Yang Guang's eyes, this actually played into his hands, serving as a convenient pretext to keep the Duke of Tang's residence in check. Even if he trusted the Duke of Tang's house for now and had no intention of stripping their military command, he would still seize any opportunity to beat them into submission—much like training a hawk or a hound.

Li Shimin clenched his fists tightly inside his sleeves. He now understood the kingcraft of this fatuous ruler. *Heh.*

Seeing Li Shimin's respectful demeanor, Yang Guang was immensely pleased. "You have been wronged in this matter. I hereby appoint you Pacification Commissioner of He-You and Garrison Commander of Zhuo Commandery. Prepare well for war against the Eastern Tujue. Once the King of Goguryeo surrenders, I will surely avenge your brother."

Li Shimin acted deeply moved. "I thank Your Majesty for your boundless grace! This subject will willingly shed his blood for Your Majesty!"

Yang Guang added, "However, Li Yuan has failed to govern his household strictly, so a mild punishment is in order. Since he cannot manage Hedong, he shall be relieved of his post as Pacification Commissioner of Hedong. Let him guard Taiyuan proper as Pacification Commissioner of Shanxi. *Sigh,* I wished to grant my maternal cousin a chance, yet he constantly fails to grasp it."

Li Shimin remained silent. As a son, it was inappropriate for him to speak ill of his father.

His silence satisfied Yang Guang greatly.

Having endured the Crown Prince's coup attempt, Yang Guang placed even greater importance on filial piety and human relations. Even if Li Yuan was glaringly biased, Li Shimin could not display dissatisfaction toward him. Only someone who was sufficiently filial would prove sufficiently loyal.

Just as Yang Guang was about to offer a few more words of encouragement to Li Shimin, a palace attendant rushed in to report.

"Reporting to Your Majesty! The Duchess of Tang is beating the drum at the palace gates to present an imperial petition, accusing her son Li Yuanji of unfilial disobedience toward his parents—a crime among the Ten Heinous Offences!"

Yang Guang abruptly stood up from his couch, asking in disbelief, "Who? What crime?"

The attendant's voice trembled. "The Duchess of Tang... accuses her son Li Yuanji of the Ten Heinous Offences!"

The Ten Heinous Offences were capital crimes promulgated in the first year of Kaihuang. *The Kaihuang Code* stipulated that ten major crimes—treason, grand sedition, rebellion, atrocious contumacy, sacrilege, unfilial conduct, discord, unrighteousness, and incest—were excluded from all general amnesties. Li Yuanji had indeed committed "atrocious contumacy" by attempting to murder his own brother. But since Yang Guang actively supported informers, how could he condemn Li Yuanji for "discord"?

Displeasure flared instantly in Yang Guang's heart as he cast a suspicious glance at Li Shimin.

Li Shimin's face was a picture of complete bewilderment and helplessness.

Frowning, Yang Guang withdrew his gaze. "How did the Duchess of Tang get here? Could it be the Duke of Tang?"

Just then, another attendant rushed in, kowtowing frantically. "The Duke of Tang dispatched men to take the Duchess away! A clash broke out, and the Duchess of Tang was injured!"

Li Shimin leaped up from the floor, roaring in fury, "Who dares harm my mother!"

Yang Guang was stunned. "The Duke of Tang... sent men to take the Duchess away?"

Yuwen Shu had been quietly observing the situation. Only now did he speak to Yang Guang: "Your Majesty, please summon the Duchess of Tang to an audience. The Duke of Tang is Your Majesty's maternal cousin after all; Li Yuanji's false accusation is already a scandal within the Duke's house. We must not let this family disgrace escalate any further."

Yang Guang sighed. "What a mess... *Sigh*, quickly invite Lady Dou inside! Er-lang, go escort your mother."

Li Shimin fell back to his knees and declared, "Please grant this subject the authority to execute those treacherous servants!"

Yang Guang waved his hand. "They are servants of your household; how to deal with them is your decision. To dare harm the mistress of the house... they indeed deserve to die."

Li Shimin knocked his head against the floor. "Thank Your Majesty!"

He turned and strode out of the palace hall.

The guards posted outside the hall returned the sword Li Shimin had unbuckled prior to meeting the Emperor.

Li Shimin did not fasten the sword to his waist.

Unsheathing the blade, he held the sword in one hand and the scabbard in the other, marching toward the palace gates.

Outside the palace gates, Lady Dou—who had fallen during the struggle and scraped her arms—drew her dagger once more, thrusting it toward the burly servant attempting to drag her into a carriage.

The burly servant dodged the strike and barked sternly, "Madam, this is the Duke's command!"

Lady Dou gripped her dagger tight. "Regardless of whose order it is, try touching me again if you dare!"

The servant cupped his fists. "Forgive me, Madam! The Duke ordered that by whatever means necessary, we must bring Madam back to Taiyuan!"

"By whatever means necessary?"

A voice suppressed to the extreme rang out alongside the harsh scraping of metal dragging against stone.

Li Shimin was dragging his longsword behind him, its tip sparking against the paved ground.

The servant hurriedly said, "Second Young Master, this is..."

Before he could finish, Li Shimin suddenly leaped into the air. Sweeping his longsword up from the ground, he raised it high and brought it crashing down with murderous force.

Before the servant could even register what was happening, his head had already rolled onto the ground!

The tip of Li Shimin's sword slammed onto the stone floor once more with a sharp *clang*.

Shielding Lady Dou behind him, his eyes blazed with fire toward the remaining servants, yet his facial expression was as cold as frost.

"Whoever harms my mother shall die."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第138章 杀不孝以儆效尤 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第138章 杀不孝以儆效尤

当壮仆的脑袋滚落的时候， 嘈杂的现场立刻鸦雀无声。

窦夫人焦急道：“二郎……”

窦夫人话还未说完，就被李世民打断道：“母亲放心，我已经得到了陛下的同意， 斩杀刁奴。”

李世民带来的人就在宫门前等候。

当窦夫人骑着马朝着宫门奔来， 又有人喊着唐国公的命令追逐时， 秦琼等人都丈二和尚摸不着头脑，不知道自己该怎么做。

李世民一出手，秦琼等人就找到了主心骨， 立刻出手把其他壮仆制服。

秦琼道：“把他们的嘴都堵住……谁去借个木桶来，把地洗干净，别麻烦陛下的侍卫。”

李世民的下属绑人的绑人， 拖尸的拖尸，洗地的洗地， 很快就把现场处理干净。

非常专业。

李世民心中的火气没有因为斩杀了一个刁奴就消失。但秦琼等人效率太高， 速度太快，他还没反应过来，地都被洗干净了。

他只能沉着脸甩了一下剑上的血珠，将剑还鞘。

李世民问道：“母亲，陛下召见你。”

他一边说， 一边查看窦夫人手臂上的擦伤。

李世民上战场时总爱亲自冲杀在前。李玄霸给他准备了小罐装的金疮药，让他在马上追击敌人的时候能抽空涂一下， 聊胜于无。

弟弟虽然不在身边，李世民已经养成了随身带着药膏的习惯。

他先用清水替母亲清洗了一下伤口，然后涂上加了烈酒的药膏：“有点疼， 母亲请忍耐一下。”

手臂传来刺痛感， 窦夫人一声未吭。

等李世民涂完药， 窦夫人压低声音问道：“二郎， 那把火谁放的？”

李世民眼眸闪了闪，沉声道：“东突厥。”

窦夫人点头，表示自己知道了。

母子二人往宫里走去。窦夫人低声将这次冲突的原因告诉李世民。

有些事是她根据李渊的性格猜测，但应该差不离。

李世民一边听窦夫人解释自己告御状和李渊派人来阻拦她的原因，一边和自己从弟弟那里得来的消息做对比。

时间回到李玄霸还在河东的时候。

李玄霸先因为换季例行生病。

这次他病得比较严重，李建成又沉迷喝酒打猎，让李元吉找到机会从李建成书房里偷到李玄霸的墨宝，自己涂改拼凑成书信，向丁郡丞诬告。

丁郡丞找来李建成问事时，宇文珠向太原送信，告知李玄霸病重。

李世民因为想要去涿郡见太子，被李渊软禁，后来被出兵的李渊一同带走，没有接到信。窦夫人看到书信，花了一日时间匆匆将手中的事交给万氏后，乘坐马车前往河东郡照顾李玄霸。

丁郡丞花了几日的时间吓唬李建成。李建成被丁郡丞吓到，又被丁郡丞以族叔前例诱惑，坚称这都是李世民和李玄霸的错，要做大义灭亲的人。

丁郡丞将李建成放回太原郡，向李渊通个口风。

这时李玄霸的病好转，准备回太原。他派金雕给李世民送信，让二哥来接他。

窦夫人此时已经在路上，与成了惊弓之鸟，不敢走大路，所以带着仆从骑马走小路回太原的李建成错过。

李玄霸让李智云去通知李建成自己要回太原时，发现李建成已经人走宅空。

丁郡丞发现李玄霸病愈，想要离开河东郡，派人将李玄霸软禁。

这时变相突生，在丁郡丞和李玄霸见面当晚，未知势力混入换防府兵中放火，李玄霸生死未卜。

窦夫人到达河东郡后，和丁郡丞一同前往涿郡面圣。仆从阻拦不及，快马加鞭回太原郡禀报李渊。

当仆从不眠不休只花了三日就到达太原郡时，李建成也正好回到太原郡。

李渊先把李建成骂了一顿，当得知窦夫人要告御状时大惊失色。

“她糊涂了！”李渊焦急地如热锅上的蚂蚁，“妇道人家无知，还真以为现实和话本上写的一样，遇到冤屈就能告御状吗！她知不知道告御状的人首先会被打板子？！再者，她还记不记得她是北周武帝的外甥女？！现在陛下正因为天下大乱而心烦意乱，太子又犯上作乱……唉！”

剩下的话太过大逆不道，李渊没有说出口。

以夫人的身份，若在敏感时刻出现在皇帝面前，说不定会让皇帝想起“前朝余孽”，误以为太子之事真的和前朝有关。

虽然皇帝没有证据，但李渊现在越来越了解杨广是什么样的人。

杨广做事不看证据，只看心情。就像是现在军报如雪花般飞入都城，但杨广坚信天下仍旧安定，还出兵征讨高丽一样。他如果不肯相信自己的儿子会谋逆，说不定就会脑补一个“前朝余孽”来为太子谋逆找补。

再者家丑不可外扬。李渊准备把李元吉接回来后，让李元吉悄悄病死。如果让皇帝插手，说不定还会牵连唐国公府其他人。

李渊十分焦急，忙让自己私兵火速抄小路火速去涿郡城门口，拦阻窦夫人面圣。

私兵问道：“如果夫人不愿意回来，我们该如何做？”

李渊道：“不管用什么手段，都必须把夫人带回来！不能让夫人见到杨广！”

私兵又问道：“如果夫人反抗……”

李渊打断道：“夫人柔弱，你们只要以我的名义让夫人回头，动作再稍稍强硬一些，夫人就会乖乖跟着你们走。”

私兵得到李渊的同意之后，就立刻骑马前往涿郡，在城门阻拦窦夫人。

即使窦夫人早出发几日，但她乘坐的是马车，速度不会太快。且她和丁荣同行，丁荣要休息的时候，她也只能跟着一同休息。李渊派来的私兵成功在城门口拦到窦夫人。

丁荣见有唐国公府的人求见，知道这是唐国公的家事，带着人躲到一旁不掺和。

窦夫人身边的仆从都听从唐国公的命令，停下了马车。

但私兵万万没想到，柔弱了几十年的夫人会在装作和他们一起离开时突然翻身上马，举着唐国公的令牌让路人让道，朝着行宫奔去。

窦夫人这一举动，让私兵脑袋嗡的一响，只能条件反射跟在窦夫人身后追去。

他们虽然追上了窦夫人，但窦夫人不下马，他们也不敢撞马，怕伤到窦夫人。

几匹马相互纠缠，在行宫前才停下。

窦夫人下马想要往宫门奔去时，私兵才找到机会拉住窦夫人。

但窦夫人居然拿出匕首挥舞，有壮仆怒气上头，才伤到了窦夫人。

之后就是李世民来了。

窦夫人道：“只要我能进宫门，他们就不敢再纠缠，否则就是御前失仪。”

宫门就是“御前失仪”的界限。

别说行宫，就是在都城的宫门外都有百姓云集。

后世明清的规矩比前朝都严格许多，还有小商小贩能在宫门外叫卖食物。还有小商小贩专门做侍卫和上朝官员的餐点生意。

有胆大的小贩甚至捡了宫中令牌，混入宫中卖馒头。

所以宫门口的嘈杂，宫里人是不管的。

但只要进了宫门，就是内廷。再在内廷里追打，就属于御前失仪了。

窦夫人就赌李渊派来的仆从不敢对她太强硬。只要她能进了宫门，就能顺利见到杨广。

其实这几个壮仆只是听从李渊的命令，也没想过真的伤到窦夫人，真是无妄之灾。

但上面人下令，下面的人遭殃，世事就是如此。

李世民问道：“为何母亲一定要来告御状？很危险。”

窦夫人道：“我有诰命在身，告御状可以免于惩罚，不危险。我儿出事了，我如果太冷静，才是奇怪。”

窦夫人用委婉的话告诉李世民，就算不提自己此刻心情，只以理智来判断，唐国公府出了这么大的事，只有李世民一人来澄清，其他人却像是没事人一样，实在是说不过去。

窦夫人“关心则乱”，前来告御状，正好表明唐国公府一家人都被蒙在鼓里，是真正的无辜。

所以她前来告御状，反而不会让杨广猜忌。

“我担心你父亲仍旧心软。”窦夫人压低声音，含糊不清道。

李世民心中的痛苦在听到窦夫人的这句话后，终于消散了一些。

他脸上露出浅浅的瞬息即逝的笑容：“谢母亲。”

窦夫人听到李世民这声“谢”，不由悲从中来，酸涩无比。

这怎么能说谢？自己是二郎三郎的娘亲啊！

半刻钟后，窦夫人来到杨广的面前。

她捋了捋有点散乱的头发，跪趴在地上悲戚道：“唐国公夫人窦慧明，状告逆子李元吉不孝之罪！”

杨广听到窦夫人的自称，神情恍惚了一瞬。

他其实是知道窦夫人的名字的。

窦毅是虔诚的佛教徒，所以给长子取名为“窦文殊”。

但北周武帝很早就试图灭佛，窦毅要支持北周武帝，就给之后的儿女名字改了改，取名为“窦招贤”和“窦慧明”。

隋文帝也是虔诚的佛教徒。他回家后对自己妻儿吐槽过此事。

什么窦招贤窦慧明，其实仍旧是取自“普贤菩萨”和“慧光明菩萨”之名。窦毅说着支持陛下，其实敷衍得很。陛下也知道窦毅很敷衍，但坚称窦毅的敷衍是非常用心的敷衍。

杨坚那时还只是北周忠臣，敬重皇帝，与窦毅友好。

他当着窦毅的面笑道：“陛下，用心的敷衍不还是敷衍？我看窦公不忠，请陛下斩了他！”

窦毅翻白眼：“我夜观星象，预见你才不忠，求陛下斩了他！”

北周武帝当时伏案大笑，让两位不忠之臣都快滚。

因隋文帝和杨广说过这件趣事，所以杨广对窦夫人那“认真的敷衍”名字印象较为深刻。

时隔几十年，他再次听到了这个名字，忍不住又回忆起北周武帝的音容。

杨广仔细端详窦夫人的容貌。

他上次见窦夫人时，李世民和李玄霸还年幼，窦夫人容貌仍旧娇艳。

此刻窦夫人却像是一个普通老妪，神情颓靡，发丝如枯草一般，嘴角和眼角都是皱纹。

她那愁苦的模样，不仅让人看不出她年轻时的美貌，也看不出她眉眼间北周武帝的影子了。

杨广脑海里又出现萧皇后的模样。

虽然他是伪装，但与萧皇后如民间夫妻般相处几十年的时光是真实的。纵然现在他后宫美色充盈，他仍旧尊重自己的皇后，无论去哪都把皇后带在身边。

皇后先是失去了长子，次子又谋逆。她没有请求留下唯一的儿子的性命，只是求自己不要追查次子家眷的动向，给她留下一个次子还有血脉遗留的奢望。

纵然她知道杨广对杨暕后院把控十分严格，杨暕一举一动都在杨广眼皮子底下，杨暕绝对没有七八岁的私生子。但她得知李元吉的诬告后，仍旧有了如此奢望。

皇后的面容，也如此时的窦夫人一样憔悴。

杨广很少共情他人，但萧皇后毕竟还是不同的。他虽然不会因为萧皇后而心慈手软，但看到如萧皇后一样为孩子痛苦的窦慧明，就不由心软了几分。

窦慧明一直跪伏在地上，没有看到杨广软化的眼神。

她虽然在哭泣，声音很清晰，条理也很清楚。

“逆子李元吉出生前，臣妇就梦到他是天生灾星，必会带来灾祸。但三郎心善，悄悄把李元吉捡了回来，救了李元吉一命。”

“李元吉知道三郎救了他，却对病弱的三郎百般折辱。我护着三郎，居然被他踢打咒骂。我稍稍管教，他就跑到街上打滚号哭，诬告我对他不慈！”

“郎君一片慈父之心，仍旧不愿意放弃李元吉，聘请名师教导李元吉。李元吉不仅没有感激郎君的一片苦心，还痛恨郎君。”

“他私通东突厥，诬告唐国公府，想把一家人置于死地！”

“臣妇请陛下治他忤逆不孝大罪！”

窦慧明不住地磕头，将额头都磕破了。

李世民想要扶住母亲，却被窦慧明甩开。

窦慧明面容仿佛癫狂：“李元吉本就该死！若不是三郎救他，郎君怜他，他早就该死！越是对他好，对他有恩的人，他就越恨！他根本不是人！是祸害！”

苏威皱眉道：“李二郎，你母亲所说的是真的？李三郎曾经救过李元吉的命？”

李世民跪着拱手：“是。虽然是多年前的事，但唐国公府老仆都知道这件事。祖母曾经将此事告诉过先帝。”

苏威冥思苦想有没有这事。

如果这事是真的，李元吉恩将仇报，就不是普通的无证据诬告。就算是陛下纵容诬告，也该治李元吉的罪。

而且苏威本来就不赞同支持诬告，只是杨广不听他的。如果能治罪李元吉，说不定能整治一下朝堂民间诬告成风的歪风邪气。

杨广想了想，道：“确实有这事。朕听父皇提过。”

不过父皇当时是骂窦夫人家教不好，居然丢弃孩子，顺带夸奖了保护弟弟的李玄霸几句。

这点小事杨广不会放在心上。但他记忆力很好，窦慧明与李世民一提，他就想了起来。

苏威起身拱手道：“李元吉确实不孝不悌，应当治罪！大隋以孝治国，不能容忍此等不孝之人！”

裴世矩也起身赞同道：“李元吉因为憎恨父亲的严格管教，为了报复父亲，居然私通正在与唐国公作战的东突厥，放火杀害李三郎。这不仅是不孝，也是叛国！陛下，应当严惩李元吉！”

裴蕴不是不想合群，只是不明白：“李元吉憎恨对他严格管教的唐国公情有可原。李三郎对他有恩，为何他要加害李三郎？而且这和李二郎有什么关系？他为何要连李二郎一起诬告。”

李世民面无表情道：“李元吉年幼时谁都打不过，只有阿玄病弱，可以被他折腾。李元吉幼时常欺负阿玄。阿玄脾气好，因为李元吉年幼而忍让，但我忍不了。所以我三天两头就要狠揍他一次。”

裴蕴：“啊？”

几人齐齐看向窦夫人。

窦慧明差点没绷住疯癫的表情。

杨广见窦夫人已经失去了理智，想着可能问不出什么来，就让虞世南觐见。

虞世南身为起居舍人，就在偏殿。

杨广问道：“你曾教导李二郎李三郎习字，李二郎真的常常狠揍李元吉？”

虞世南嘴角微微抽搐，拱手道：“确有此事。李二郎被罚关禁闭，十次有五次是因为把李元吉揍得太厉害。”

李世民继续补充道：“他恨我和阿玄，不仅是因为我小时候常揍他，还因为阿玄自认为把他捡回来，对他有责任，所以对他教育很尽心，常劝说父亲严加管教李元吉。”

杨广和看稀奇似的啧啧道：“原来真的有天生恶人，朕真是开眼界了。”

李世民看着杨广脸上看猴戏似的笑容，垂下头。

他咬了一下牙关，轻轻深呼吸了几下，镇定道：“陛下，母亲悲恸过度，精神不稳定。求陛下让母亲先退下静养。”

窦慧明忙继续磕头：“不，臣妇不走！”

李世民道：“母亲，请不要御前失仪，惊扰陛下。”

窦慧明脖子一缩，做畏缩状：“臣妇没有，臣妇不想侵扰陛下……”

宇文述温和道：“别吓唬你的母亲，陛下心胸最是宽广不过，怎么会责怪一位失去儿子的母亲？陛下，让御医给唐国公夫人看看吧。”

杨广看够了热闹，心满意足道：“好。李二郎，把你母亲扶下去。来人，叫御医。你们就暂住皇后殿里，待你母亲休养好了再离开。”

李世民叩首道：“谢陛下隆恩。”

他扶着似乎被吓到的母亲，倒退着离开了宫殿。

李世民和窦慧明离开后，杨广唏嘘道：“真如民间俗话，家家都有难念的经啊。”

自己的儿子忤逆逼宫，好歹没有存真正的谋害之心。看看唐国公府的李元吉，这才是真正的逆子。

杨广好奇道：“真的会有人从出生起就是恶人吗？”

裴蕴掌管天下刑罚，阅读过许多奇异案例。他听杨广询问，忙道：“天下之大无奇不有，臣判案时也遇到许多次天生恶人犯下的残忍命案。陛下若有兴趣，臣可整理一二事例给陛下观赏。”

裴蕴如此谄媚，连最大的奸臣宇文述都心理不适了。

什么叫做“观赏”，这种事能“观赏”？

但杨广却很满意裴蕴的细心体贴：“不用太急，朕只是好奇，你有空再做。”

裴蕴欣喜道：“是，陛下。”自己又找到可以奉承皇帝的事了！

苏威不满地瞥了裴蕴一眼，将话题转回正事：“陛下，该如何处理李元吉？”

宇文述跟上道：“陛下，请恕臣直谏。大隋以孝治国，太子逼宫，正需要警告天下人秉承孝顺之心。但太子之事只能低调处理，不能示众。李元吉一案，正好用来震慑天下不孝顺之人。”

苏威又瞥了宇文述一眼。顺着陛下的心意，也能称直谏？

裴世矩想了想，道：“臣与李二郎李三郎有旧，本应该避嫌少言。不过宇文大将军所言极是，当务之急是抹平太子之事的影响。李元吉来得正好。”

虞世基厌恶道：“李元吉当枭首示众。传首天下郡县，震慑不忠不孝之人！”

裴蕴也连忙道：“臣附议！”

杨广一琢磨，确实是这么一回事。

太子忤逆，就是不忠不孝。但他就算深恶太子，也顶多赐太子自尽，不足以震慑不忠不孝之人。

李元吉碰巧跳出来，正好代替太子。

杨广颔首：“依众卿家之言，传丁郡丞觐见。”

……

窦慧明喝了一剂加了镇静药物的汤药，在皇后偏殿沉沉睡去。

萧皇后探望后，拉着李世民的手到一旁道：“李二郎，阿孩他真的有孩子遗落民间吗？你照实回答我，话传不到陛下耳中去。”

李世民神色黯然地摇头：“二表兄后院之事，没有谁比陛下更清楚。”

萧皇后喃喃道：“是啊，是啊……是这样啊……”

她颓然道：“你休息吧。遭此无妄之灾，你也辛苦了。”

李世民道：“皇后殿下，如果不麻烦，可否帮我劝说陛下，准许我为二表兄送行。”

萧皇后眼神一暖，道：“你有这个心，陛下会准许。”

李世民拱手道：“谢皇后殿下。”

萧皇后在太子杨暕兵谏后就病倒了，南阳公主一直伺候左右。

萧皇后回到宫殿后，将此事告诉南阳公主。

她叹息道：“阿孩当上太子时，朝堂众人趋之若鹜，李二郎李三郎却远离阿孩；阿孩牢狱之灾后，朝堂众人都掩面避之，李二郎却要去牢中为阿孩送行。怪不得大郎和阿孩都喜爱他们。”

南阳公主神色黯然：“他们确实是好孩子。”

萧皇后拍了拍南阳公主的手背，道：“阿孩出事，你我不能沉浸在悲伤中。若陛下立三郎为太子，你我何处？我的病已经好了，你该去陛下身边了。陛下心里难过，正需要儿女陪伴。”

南阳公主叹气：“是。”

她知道母后的意思。

她的同母兄弟杨昭、杨暕皆无缘帝位，母后又不能再生育，自己不可能有同母兄弟继承王位了。

虽说将来三郎继位，母后仍旧是太后，但依魏晋南北朝那些太后旧例，非生母的太后常得不到尊重，皇帝生母的外戚家族一定会和嫡母外戚家族争夺权利。更别提只能依靠皇帝喜爱才有好日子过的公主。

母后希望父亲能立元德太子之子为皇太孙，将来萧家仍旧是皇帝外戚。

自己虽然不愿意掺和进夺嫡之争，但现在这种情况，也由不得自己不争了。

“母后，我们要为李二郎李三郎多说说好话了。”南阳公主提起精神，献策道，“李二郎李三郎与大郎二郎感情都很深厚。若三郎当太子，恐怕会忌惮他们二人。”

萧皇后眼眸中精光一闪，叹气道：“他们为了自己，也该站在我们这一方。”

窦慧明昏睡了一日，第二日似乎冷静下来，向杨广惶恐赔罪。

**Chapter 138: Executing the Unfilial to Make an Example**

As the burly servant’s head rolled across the ground, the noisy scene fell instantly silent.

Lady Dou called out anxiously, "Erlang..."

Before she could finish, Li Shimin interrupted her softly, "Rest assured, Mother. I have already received His Majesty's permission to execute these treacherous servants."

The men Li Shimin had brought were waiting right outside the palace gates.

When Lady Dou had come charging toward the palace gates on horseback with men pursuing her in the name of the Duke of Tang, Qin Qiong and the others had been utterly baffled, unsure of how to react.

But the moment Li Shimin took action, Qin Qiong and his comrades found their backbone and immediately moved to subdue the remaining burly servants.

"Gag every last one of them..." Qin Qiong commanded. "Someone fetch a wooden bucket and scrub the ground clean. Don't bother His Majesty's guards with this."

Li Shimin's subordinates bound the men, dragged away the corpse, and washed the blood from the stone tiles. In mere moments, the scene was thoroughly cleared.

Highly professional.

The rage in Li Shimin's chest did not dissipate simply because he had slain one treacherous servant. But Qin Qiong and the others operated with such swift efficiency that before he could even register it, the ground was already spotless.

He could only flick the droplets of blood off his blade with a somber expression before returning it to its scabbard.

"Mother," Li Shimin said, "His Majesty grants you an audience."

As he spoke, he checked the abrasions on Lady Dou's arm.

Whenever Li Shimin took to the battlefield, he preferred to charge at the very front. Li Xuanba had prepared small jars of golden wound salve for him, allowing him to quickly apply it while chasing down enemies on horseback—it was better than nothing.

Even though his younger brother was not by his side, Li Shimin had already formed the habit of carrying the salve with him at all times.

He first washed his mother's wound with clean water, then applied the salve mixed with strong liquor. "This will sting a little, Mother. Please bear with it."

A sharp prickle of pain shot through her arm, but Lady Dou did not utter a single sound.

Once Li Shimin finished applying the medicine, Lady Dou lowered her voice and asked, "Erlang, who set that fire?"

Li Shimin's eyes flickered. "The Eastern Göktürks," he said in a low voice.

Lady Dou nodded, signaling her understanding.

The mother and son walked together into the palace grounds. Lady Dou quietly explained the root cause of the conflict to Li Shimin.

Some details were merely her conjectures based on Li Yuan's character, but they were likely close to the truth.

As Li Shimin listened to Lady Dou explain why she was lodging an imperial complaint and why Li Yuan had sent men to stop her, he cross-referenced her words with the intelligence he had received from his brother.

***

The timeline reverted to when Li Xuanba was still in Hedong.

Li Xuanba had first fallen ill as he routinely did during the change of seasons.

This time he fell severely ill. Li Jiancheng was engrossed in drinking and hunting, giving Li Yuanji the opportunity to steal Li Xuanba's calligraphy from Jiancheng's study, alter and piece together letters, and make a false accusation to Vice Prefect Ding.

When Vice Prefect Ding summoned Li Jiancheng for questioning, Yuwen Zhu sent a letter to Taiyuan reporting Xuanba's critical illness.

Li Shimin had been placed under house arrest by Li Yuan for wanting to go to Zhuo Commandery to see the Crown Prince, and was later dragged along when Li Yuan marched out with his army, so he never received the letter. Lady Dou saw the letter, spent a day quickly entrusting her duties to Lady Wan, and took a carriage to Hedong Commandery to tend to Li Xuanba.

Vice Prefect Ding spent a few days intimidating Li Jiancheng. Terrified by Ding and tempted by the precedent of his clan uncle, Jiancheng insisted it was all Shimin and Xuanba's fault and claimed he was acting out of righteousness to sacrifice his kin for justice.

Vice Prefect Ding allowed Jiancheng back to Taiyuan Commandery to drop hints to Li Yuan.

Meanwhile, Xuanba recovered and prepared to return to Taiyuan. He sent his golden eagle with a letter to Shimin, asking his second brother to fetch him.

Lady Dou was already on the road, missing Jiancheng, who was spooked like a startled bird and avoided the main roads, riding back to Taiyuan via backpaths with his servants.

When Xuanba sent Li Zhiyun to inform Jiancheng that he was returning, he found Jiancheng's residence already deserted.

Vice Prefect Ding realized Xuanba had recovered and intended to leave Hedong Commandery, so he sent men to place Xuanba under house arrest.

Then an unexpected turn of events occurred. On the evening Ding met Xuanba, unknown forces infiltrated the rotated garrison troops and set a fire; Xuanba's fate remained unknown.

Upon reaching Hedong Commandery, Lady Dou went with Vice Prefect Ding to Zhuo Commandery to seek an imperial audience. Her servants couldn't stop her in time and rode hard back to Taiyuan Commandery to report to Li Yuan.

When the servants arrived in Taiyuan Commandery after three days of relentless riding, Jiancheng had just returned as well.

Li Yuan berated Jiancheng, but turned pale with shock upon learning Lady Dou intended to lodge an imperial complaint.

"She's lost her mind!" Li Yuan paced anxiously like a cat on a hot tin roof. "An ignorant woman! Does she really think reality is like the storybooks, where one can just present a grievance directly to the Emperor?! Does she not know that anyone filing an imperial complaint is beaten with flogging boards first?! Furthermore, does she forget she is the niece of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou?! Right now His Majesty is distraught over the realm's chaos, and the Crown Prince has committed treason... Sigh!"

The remaining words were far too treasonous, so Li Yuan left them unsaid.

With his wife's background, appearing before the Emperor at such a sensitive time might remind Him of "remnants of the former dynasty," leading Him to mistakenly suspect the Crown Prince's rebellion was connected to Northern Zhou.

Though the Emperor lacked evidence, Li Yuan was coming to understand Emperor Yang Guang more and more.

Yang Guang did not act on evidence, but on impulse. Just as military reports were flooding the capital like snowflakes, yet Yang Guang firmly believed the realm was still peaceful and launched a campaign against Goguryeo. If he refused to believe his own son was rebelling, he might invent a "former dynasty remnant" narrative to explain away the Crown Prince's treason.

Moreover, family scandals shouldn't be aired in public. Li Yuan planned to bring Li Yuanji back and quietly let him "succumb to illness." If the Emperor intervened, it might implicate the rest of the Duke of Tang's household.

Anxious, Li Yuan hastily ordered his private guards to take shortcuts at top speed to the gates of Zhuo Commandery to intercept Lady Dou.

"What if Lady Dou refuses to return?" the guards asked.

Li Yuan said, "No matter what means you use, you must bring her back! She cannot be allowed to see Yang Guang!"

"And if she resists..."

Li Yuan interrupted, "She is frail and gentle. As long as you command her in my name and act with a bit of firmness, she will meekly follow you back."

Armed with Li Yuan's authorization, the private guards rode off to Zhuo Commandery to intercept Lady Dou at the city gate.

Although Lady Dou had set out days earlier, she traveled by carriage, which was slow. Co-traveling with Ding Rong, she had to rest whenever Ding Rong rested. Thus, Li Yuan's guards successfully intercepted her at the gate.

Seeing members of the Duke of Tang's household, Ding Rong knew it was a private family matter of the Tang Household and stayed out of it with his men.

The servants beside Lady Dou obeyed the Duke of Tang's orders and stopped the carriage.

However, the guards never expected that a woman who had been frail and gentle for decades would pretend to comply, only to suddenly mount a horse, brandish the Duke of Tang's token to clear the crowd, and charge directly toward the imperial palace.

This sudden move left the guards stunned; they could only react instinctively and chase after her.

Though they caught up with her, she refused to dismount, and they dared not ram her horse for fear of hurting her.

Several horses became entangled, only coming to a halt before the imperial palace gates.

When Lady Dou dismounted and rushed toward the palace gates, the guards finally found an opportunity to grab her.

Yet Lady Dou actually drew a dagger and brandished it. In the heat of the moment, one of the burly servants grew hot-headed and injured her.

And then, Li Shimin arrived.

***

Lady Dou said, "As long as I could pass through the palace gates, they would not dare harass me further—otherwise, it would be considered impropriety before the Emperor."

The palace gate marked the boundary for "impropriety before the Emperor."

Outside the gates of the capital palace—let alone a temporary imperial palace—commoners gathered.

Rules in the later Ming and Qing dynasties were much stricter than in earlier eras, where small vendors were permitted to hawk food outside palace gates, even catering to guards and officials attending court. Bold vendors had even been known to pick up lost palace passes to sneak inside and sell mantou.

Thus, palace officials didn't care about noise outside the gate.

But once inside the palace gate, one entered the inner court. Pursuing and brawling within the inner court was an act of grave disrespect to the sovereign.

Lady Dou gambled that Li Yuan's servants wouldn't dare be too forceful with her. Once she entered the gate, she would meet Yang Guang smoothly.

In truth, the burly servants were just following Li Yuan's orders and never intended to harm her—it was truly an unexpected disaster.

Yet when superiors issue commands, subordinates suffer the consequences; such was the way of the world.

Li Shimin asked, "Why did Mother insist on lodging an imperial complaint? It was far too dangerous."

Lady Dou said, "I hold a noble title; lodging an imperial complaint waives corporal punishment for me, so it is not dangerous. If something happened to my son and I remained calm, *that* would be strange."

Lady Dou tactfully conveyed to Li Shimin that even putting aside her emotions and looking at it logically, for a crisis of this magnitude in the Tang Household, if only Li Shimin came to clarify while everyone else acted as though nothing had happened, it would make no sense.

Lady Dou acting out of frantic maternal concern to lodge an imperial complaint proved that the entire Tang Household was kept in the dark and was genuinely innocent.

Thus, her coming to lodge a complaint would actually prevent Yang Guang from becoming suspicious.

"I was worried your father would still be soft-hearted," Lady Dou whispered ambiguously.

The pain in Li Shimin's heart finally dissipated somewhat upon hearing her words.

A faint, fleeting smile appeared on his face. "Thank you, Mother."

Hearing this "thank you," Lady Dou felt a surge of sorrow and bitterness in her heart.

How could he say thank you? She was the mother of Erlang and Sanlang!

***

Half an hour later, Lady Dou stood before Yang Guang.

She smoothed her disheveled hair, knelt, and prostrated herself on the ground in grief. "Dou Huiming, wife of the Duke of Tang, accuses her unfilial son, Li Yuanji, of the crime of unfilial rebellion!"

Upon hearing her name, Yang Guang's mind dazed for a moment.

He actually knew Lady Dou's birth name.

Dou Yi had been a devout Buddhist, naming his eldest son "Dou Wenshu."

However, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou attempted to suppress Buddhism early on. To demonstrate support for Emperor Wu, Dou Yi altered his subsequent children's names to "Dou Zhaoxian" and "Dou Huiming."

Emperor Wen of Sui had also been a devout Buddhist and complained about this to his family upon returning home.

"Dou Zhaoxian" and "Dou Huiming" were still derived from "Samantabhadra" and "Wisdom Light" Bodhisattvas. Dou Yi claimed to support the Emperor, but his compliance was thoroughly superficial. Emperor Wu knew Dou Yi was being superficial, yet insisted Dou Yi's superficiality was done with great care.

At that time, Yang Jian was merely a loyal minister of Northern Zhou, respecting the Emperor and on friendly terms with Dou Yi.

He had laughed in front of Dou Yi: "Your Majesty, isn't careful superficiality still superficiality? I see Lord Dou is disloyal; I request Your Majesty execute him!"

Dou Yi rolled his eyes: "I observed the stars at night and foresaw that you are the disloyal one. I beg Your Majesty to execute him!"

Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou laughed heartily over his desk and told both disloyal ministers to scram.

Because Emperor Wen of Sui had shared this humorous anecdote with Yang Guang, Yang Guang had a vivid impression of Lady Dou's "earnestly superficial" name.

Decades later, hearing this name again, he couldn't help but recall the voice and countenance of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou.

Yang Guang scrutinized Lady Dou's appearance.

When he last saw her, Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were still young, and Lady Dou was still youthful and beautiful.

Now, she resembled an ordinary old woman—haggard, with hair like withered grass, and wrinkles lining her eyes and mouth.

Her sorrowful appearance not only erased all traces of her youthful beauty but also obscured any resemblance to Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou in her brows.

The image of Empress Xiao surfaced in Yang Guang's mind.

Though he had put on a pretense, the decades spent with Empress Xiao like an ordinary married couple had been real. Even though his inner palace was now filled with beauties, he still respected his Empress and took her wherever he went.

The Empress had lost her eldest son, and her second son had rebelled. She had not begged to spare her second son's life, but merely asked that he not investigate the whereabouts of the second son's household, holding onto the faint wish that some of his lineage might survive.

Even though she knew Yang Guang maintained strict control over Yang Qian's rear court and that Yang Qian had no eight-year-old illegitimate son, she still harbored such a delusion upon hearing Li Yuanji's accusation.

The Empress's face was just as haggard as Dou Huiming's right now.

Yang Guang rarely felt empathy for others, but Empress Xiao was different. Though he would not grow soft-hearted for Empress Xiao's sake, seeing Dou Huiming suffering for her child just like Empress Xiao softened his heart slightly.

Dou Huiming remained prostrated, unaware of Yang Guang's softening gaze.

Though weeping, her voice was clear and articulate.

"Before the rebellious brat Li Yuanji was born, I dreamed that he was born under an ill star, destined to bring calamity. But Sanlang was kind-hearted and secretly brought him back, saving his life."

"Li Yuanji knew Sanlang saved him, yet subjected the frail Sanlang to endless humiliation. When I protected Sanlang, he even kicked, struck, and cursed me! When I tried to discipline him slightly, he rolled on the street weeping and wailing, falsely accusing me of lacking maternal affection!"

"My husband possessed a father's compassionate heart and refused to give up on him, hiring famous masters to instruct him. Not only did Li Yuanji show no gratitude for my husband's painstaking efforts, he harbored deep hatred toward him."

"He secretly colluded with the Eastern Göktürks, falsely accused the Tang Household, and sought to ruin our entire family!"

"This humble servant begs Your Majesty to punish him for the severe crime of unfilial rebellion!"

Dou Huiming kowtowed repeatedly until her forehead was bruised and bleeding.

Li Shimin tried to support his mother, but she shoved him away.

Her face seemed wild with frenzy: "Li Yuanji deserves to die! Had Sanlang not saved him and my husband taken pity on him, he would have died long ago! The better one treats him, the more kindness one shows him, the more he hates them! He is not human at all—he is a curse!"

Su Wei frowned: "Li Erlang, is what your mother says true? Li Sanlang once saved Li Yuanji's life?"

Li Shimin knelt and cupped his hands: "Yes. Though it happened years ago, the old servants of the Tang Household all know of it. My late grandmother once mentioned this to the Late Emperor."

Su Wei racked his brain trying to remember if this was true.

If true, Li Yuanji's bite of the hand that fed him wasn't just a simple false accusation without evidence. Even if His Majesty tolerated false accusations, Li Yuanji should be punished.

Furthermore, Su Wei originally disapproved of encouraging false accusations; it was just that Yang Guang didn't listen to him. Punishing Li Yuanji might curb the rampant wind of false accusations in court and among the populace.

Yang Guang pondered and said, "Indeed, there was such a matter. I heard my late father mention it."

Though the late emperor had actually criticized Lady Dou's household discipline for abandoning a child, while casually praising Li Xuanba for protecting his younger brother.

Yang Guang wouldn't care about such minor things, but he had a good memory; when Dou Huiming and Li Shimin brought it up, he recalled it.

Su Wei stood up and cupped his hands: "Li Yuanji is indeed unfilial and unbrotherly! He must be punished! Great Sui governs through filial piety; we cannot tolerate such unfilial scoundrels!"

Pei Shiju also stood up in agreement: "He harbored hatred over his father's strict discipline, and to exact revenge, he went so far as to collude with the Eastern Göktürks who are currently fighting the Duke of Tang, even setting a fire to kill Li Sanlang. This is not just unfilial—it is treason! Your Majesty, Li Yuanji must be severely punished!"

Pei Yun didn't want to be left out, but was confused: "It is understandable that Li Yuanji hated the Duke of Tang for disciplining him strictly. But Li Sanlang was kind to him—why did he harm Li Sanlang? And what does this have to do with Li Erlang? Why frame Li Erlang as well?"

Li Shimin said expressionlessly: "When Li Yuanji was young, he couldn't beat anyone else—only Ah Xuan was sickly and frail enough for him to bully. Li Yuanji often bullied Ah Xuan when they were young. Ah Xuan had a good temper and endured it because Yuanji was young, but I could not stand it. Thus, every few days, I would give him a sound thrashing."

Pei Yun: "Ah?"

Everyone turned to look at Lady Dou.

Dou Huiming almost broke her frenzied expression.

Seeing that Lady Dou had lost her composure, Yang Guang thought he might not get more out of her, so he summoned Yu Shinan.

As the Imperial Historiographer, Yu Shinan was in the side hall.

Yang Guang asked, "You once taught Li Erlang and Li Sanlang calligraphy. Did Li Erlang really beat Li Yuanji so often?"

The corner of Yu Shinan's mouth twitched slightly. He cupped his hands and said, "It is indeed true. Out of every ten times Li Erlang was grounded, five were because he beat Li Yuanji too severely."

Li Shimin added, "He hated me and Ah Xuan not only because I beat him often when we were young, but also because Ah Xuan felt responsible for saving him and took great care in educating him, frequently urging Father to discipline him strictly."

Yang Guang marveled as if watching a rare spectacle: "Tsk, so there really are people born evil from birth. I have truly opened my eyes today."

Li Shimin looked at the spectacle-watching smile on Yang Guang's face and lowered his head.

He bit his jaw, took a few quiet deep breaths, and said calmly: "Your Majesty, my mother is overwhelmed with grief and mentally unstable. I beg Your Majesty to allow her to retire and rest."

Dou Huiming hurriedly resumed kowtowing: "No, this servant will not leave!"

Li Shimin said, "Mother, please do not commit an act of impropriety before the Emperor and disturb His Majesty."

Dou Huiming shrank her neck, acting frightened: "I... I did not mean to... I do not wish to disturb His Majesty..."

Yuwen Shu said gently, "Do not frighten your mother. His Majesty is most magnanimous; how could he blame a mother who has lost her son? Your Majesty, pray allow the imperial physician to examine the Lady of Tang."

Having seen enough of the drama, Yang Guang said contentedly, "Very well. Li Erlang, help your mother down. Guards, summon the imperial physician. You shall temporarily stay in the Empress's palace until your mother recovers before leaving."

Li Shimin kowtowed: "I thank Your Majesty for your grand benevolence."

Holding his seemingly terrified mother, he backed out of the palace hall.

***

After Li Shimin and Dou Huiming left, Yang Guang sighed: "Truly, as the folk saying goes, every family has a hard nut to crack."

His own son committed treason and forced his hand, but at least hadn't truly intended to murder him. Look at Li Yuanji of the Tang Household—that is a truly unfilial monster.

Yang Guang asked curiously, "Can a person really be born evil from birth?"

Pei Yun, who oversaw imperial justice and had read many strange cases, hastily replied upon hearing Yang Guang's inquiry: "The world is vast and full of wonders. When trying cases, I have encountered many cruel homicides committed by people born naturally evil. If Your Majesty is interested, I can compile a few cases for Your Majesty to inspect and enjoy."

Pei Yun's flattery was so shameless that even the arch-traitor Yuwen Shu felt uncomfortable.

"Inspect and enjoy"? Could such horrific things be "enjoyed"?

Yet Yang Guang was very pleased with Pei Yun's attentiveness: "No need to rush. I am merely curious; do it when you have spare time."

Pei Yun said joyfully, "Understood, Your Majesty." He had found another way to flatter the Emperor!

Su Wei glanced at Pei Yun with displeasure and brought the topic back to business: "Your Majesty, how should we handle Li Yuanji?"

Yuwen Shu chimed in: "Your Majesty, forgive your servant's frank advice. Great Sui governs by filial piety. The Crown Prince's armed mutiny requires a warning to the world to uphold filial piety. Yet the Crown Prince's affair can only be handled discreetly and cannot be displayed publicly. Li Yuanji's case can be used precisely to intimidate all unfilial people in the realm."

Su Wei glanced at Yuwen Shu again. Following the Emperor's whims counted as "frank advice"?

Pei Shiju thought for a moment and said, "I have old ties with Li Erlang and Li Sanlang, so I ought to recuse myself. However, Grand General Yuwen speaks with great reason. The urgent priority is to smooth over the impact of the Crown Prince's affair. Li Yuanji's appearance comes at the perfect time."

Yuwen Jishi said disgustedly, "Li Yuanji should be beheaded and his head displayed to the public! Send his severed head to all commanderies and counties across the realm to intimidate the disloyal and unfilial!"

Pei Yun hurriedly added, "I second the motion!"

Yang Guang pondered it; indeed, that was the case.

The Crown Prince's mutiny was disloyalty and unfilial behavior. But even if he loathed the Crown Prince, at most he would order him to commit suicide; it couldn't be displayed to intimidate the populace.

Li Yuanji jumping out at this moment happened to serve as the perfect substitute for the Crown Prince.

Yang Guang nodded: "As my ministers advise. Summon Vice Prefect Ding for an audience."

***

Dou Huiming drank a dose of decoction laced with sedatives and fell into a deep sleep in the Empress's side hall.

After visiting, Empress Xiao pulled Li Shimin's hand aside and asked, "Li Erlang, does Ah Hai really have a child left among the common folk? Answer me truthfully; this won't reach His Majesty's ears."

Li Shimin shook his head somberly: "Regarding the matters of the Second Imperial Cousin's rear court, no one knows better than His Majesty."

Empress Xiao muttered, "Yes... yes... so that's how it is..."

She said dejectedly, "Go rest. You have suffered after enduring such an undeserved calamity."

Li Shimin said, "Your Majesty the Empress, if it is not too much trouble, could you help persuade His Majesty to grant me permission to see Second Imperial Cousin off?"

Empress Xiao's gaze softened with warmth: "Since you have such heart, His Majesty will grant it."

Li Shimin cupped his hands: "My thanks to Your Majesty the Empress."

Empress Xiao had fallen ill after Prince Yang Qian's mutiny, and Princess Nanyang had been attending to her side.

After returning to her palace hall, Empress Xiao told Princess Nanyang about this.

She sighed: "When Ah Hai became the Crown Prince, everyone in the court flocked to him, yet Li Erlang and Li Sanlang kept their distance; when Ah Hai suffered imprisonment, everyone in court hid their faces and avoided him, yet Li Erlang wants to go to prison to see him off. No wonder both Da Lang and Ah Hai favored them."

Princess Nanyang looked gloomy: "They are indeed good children."

Empress Xiao patted Princess Nanyang's hand and said, "Now that Ah Hai has met with disaster, you and I cannot remain immersed in grief. If His Majesty establishes Sanlang as the Crown Prince, where will that leave us? My illness has recovered; you should return to His Majesty's side. His Majesty is grieving in his heart and needs his children's company."

Princess Nanyang sighed: "Yes."

She understood her mother's intent.

Her brothers of the same mother, Yang Zhao and Yang Qian, had both lost their chance at the throne, and her mother could no longer give birth. She would no longer have a full brother to inherit the crown.

Although if Sanlang succeeded the throne, her mother would still be Empress Dowager, historical precedents from the Wei, Jin, and Northern and Southern Dynasties showed that Empresses Dowager who were not biological mothers rarely received true respect, and the biological mother's clan would inevitably struggle for power against the legitimate mother's clan. Not to mention a princess who had to rely entirely on the Emperor's favor to live well.

Her mother hoped the Emperor would establish the late Crown Prince Yuande's son as the Imperial Grandson, so the Xiao family would remain the imperial maternal relatives in the future.

Although she didn't want to be involved in the struggle for succession, given the current situation, she had no choice but to fight.

"Mother, we must speak more good words for Li Erlang and Li Sanlang," Princess Nanyang gathered her spirits and suggested. "Li Erlang and Li Sanlang shared deep bonds with both Da Lang and Er Lang. If Sanlang becomes the Crown Prince, he will likely harbor suspicions against the two of them."

Empress Xiao's eyes flashed with a sharp glint, and she sighed: "For their own sake, they ought to stand on our side as well."

Dou Huiming slept for a full day. On the second day, having seemingly regained her composure, she offered a fearful apology to Yang Guang.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第138章 杀不孝以儆效尤 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
杨广是个大度的皇帝，不仅没有怪罪窦慧明，还赐下金银绸缎安慰这位可怜的半疯的母亲。

窦慧明凄惨的模样让杨广想起了发妻。

自太子杨暕逼宫，杨广便对萧皇后冷淡了。

他探望了萧皇后，在最爱的女儿南阳公主的说笑打趣中，夫妻重归于好。

萧皇后趁机道：“阿孩伤透了我的心，我不想去见他。但他毕竟是我身上掉下来的一块肉，若没人为他送行，我心里也难受。李三郎被他牵连，生死不明。既然他自诩为李二郎和李三郎的兄长，也该向二郎道声歉。”

杨广看到李元吉所做的事，觉得杨暕的兵谏虽然让他颜面大失，但也不算太可恨了。

毕竟是自己宠了许多年的儿子，有了更突破下限的逆子对比后，杨广恢复了一点慈父之心。

他温和道：“李二郎也请求朕，想去狱中探望这个逆子。罢了，民间囚犯行刑前也要吃一顿饱饭，就让李二郎带些酒肉给他。”

萧皇后心头一痛，勉强挤出笑容：“陛下仁慈。”

南阳公主把手收在袖子里，将手背都掐乌了，才没有落下泪来。

李世民离开涿郡的前一天，终于得到杨广的准许，提着酒肉去见已经被关入牢中多日的杨暕。

杨暕神色枯槁，衣衫褴褛，脸上全是脏污和疤痕。曾经俊美无俦的王公贵胄，现在仿佛路边的乞丐。

“大雄，你怎么来了？”杨暕见到李世民，大惊失色，“你不该来！”

李世民在牢头离开后，放下手中酒坛和食盒，不顾地上脏污，盘腿坐下道：“我来为你送行。陛下准许了，不用担心。”

杨暕向李世民身后张望：“大德呢？他不会也来了？他身体不好，你别老拉着他乱跑！”

没看见李玄霸的身影，杨暕松了口气：“还好还好，这次算你懂事，没带大德一起来。”

李世民嘴角扯了扯，想告诉杨暕阿玄的事，但他看着杨暕脏污面容上明亮又柔和的眼神，将话咽了下去。

他笑道：“你当我真没分寸吗？你出这么大的事，知不知道我来见你要冒多大的险？阿玄想来，我也会把他打晕了捆起来锁屋里，不准他跟来。”

杨暕没好气道：“好好好，可惜阿玄听不到你这话。我真想看看你当着阿玄的面，敢不敢如此嚣张。”

李世民笑道：“我是他哥，教训弟弟天经地义。”

“是是是。”杨暕打开食盒，“好久没吃上一顿好酒好肉了，来，陪表兄我吃喝个够！”

李世民拿出碗倒酒：“来，不醉不休！”

两人没提兵谏的事，就像是以前那样拼起酒来。

李世民在牢中醉卧一宿。

第二日，李世民向杨暕辞别。

“二表兄，我要回张掖打突厥了。”

“去吧，大隋的边疆交给你了。保重。”

“嗯。二表兄保重。”

李世民头也不回地离开。

杨暕微笑着目送李世民离去。

直到牢门闭合，遮断两人。

杨暕脸上的微笑消失。

他大字躺在地上，喃喃自语：“大德出了什么事吗？难道是生病了？可千万要保重啊。表兄我还等着你们二人逢年过节给我烧点香烛。”

他说完后，长长叹了口气，自嘲道：“我都要死了，还有空关心别人？真奇怪，我怎么对死亡一点都不害怕呢？这不像我。”

自嘲后，他又笑道：“或许是因为现在死去，比眼睁睁看着大隋灭亡再死去，痛苦轻多了。”

……

李世民从牢中出来后，没有洗漱换衣，径直与等候在牢狱门前的下属一同离开了涿郡。

他本想先送母亲回太原，但母亲坚持让他直接回张掖。

窦慧明道：“太原的事交给娘亲，娘亲会好好处理。你要相信阿玄，阿玄说能回张掖，就一定能回去。你赶紧回去等他。”

李世民道：“谢母亲，麻烦母亲了。”

窦慧明哽咽道：“别对娘亲言谢，我是你的娘亲，怎么能叫麻烦？”

李世民抿嘴，挤出笑容道：“抱歉。母亲……娘亲说得对。儿就倚仗娘亲了。娘亲请告诉万阿姨，小五应当无事，阿玄把小五保护得很好。只是小五也还是直接回张掖更好，请恕小五不孝，不能回太原安万阿姨的心。”

窦慧明双手握着李世民的手，道：“小五回张掖才好。他在张掖，在你身边，万娘子才能放心。”

李世民道：“嗯，我会保护好阿玄和小五，娘亲和阿姨都请放心。娘亲，我该走了。”

“去吧去吧，路上小心。”窦慧明松开手，给李世民理了理毛皮大氅的领子，“如果路上积雪未化，你在途中多休息几日，慢慢走，千万注意安全。”

李世民点头：“是，母亲。”

窦慧明心头揪了一下似的疼，脸上笑容未变：“快走吧，再不走天色暗了。娘亲也该出发了。”

李世民和在一旁沉默着的长孙康宁，拜别母亲后，上马离去。

窦慧明看着他们远去后，才登上马车。

“回太原。”
chunks.englishText:
Yang Guang was a generous emperor. Not only did he refrain from blaming Dou Huiming, but he also bestowed gold, silver, and fine silks to comfort this pitiable, half-crazed mother.

Dou Huiming's tragic state reminded Yang Guang of his own wife.

Ever since the Crown Prince Yang Qi had forced his hand in the palace coup, Yang Guang had treated Empress Xiao with cold indifference.

He paid Empress Xiao a visit, and amid the laughing chatter of his favorite daughter, Princess Nanyang, husband and wife reconciled.

Taking advantage of the moment, Empress Xiao said, "A-Hai has broken my heart completely, and I have no desire to see him. But after all, he is flesh of my flesh. If no one goes to send him off, my heart will ache just as well. Li Sanlang was dragged into this by him, his fate now unknown. Since A-Hai always claimed to be the elder brother of Li Erlang and Li Sanlang, it is only right that he offers Erlang an apology."

When Yang Guang saw what Li Yuanji had done, he felt that although Yang Qi's armed remonstrance had caused him to lose immense face, it was no longer quite so abominable by comparison.

After all, he had doted on this son for many years. With an unfilial monster setting a whole new low as a comparison, Yang Guang recovered a trace of his paternal warmth.

He said gently, "Li Erlang also petitioned Us, wishing to visit this rebellious son in prison. Very well. Even common criminals are granted a hearty meal before execution. Let Li Erlang bring him some food and wine."

A sharp pang pierced Empress Xiao's heart, but she managed to force a smile. "Your Majesty is benevolent."

Princess Nanyang tucked her hands deep into her sleeves, pinching the back of her hands until they turned purple just to keep her tears from falling.

The day before Li Shimin was to depart Zhuo Commandery, he finally received Yang Guang's permission. Carrying wine and meat, he went to visit Yang Qi, who had been incarcerated for many days.

Yang Qi was gaunt and haggard, dressed in rags, his face covered in grime and scars. Once a peerlessly handsome prince of noble blood, he now resembled a roadside beggar.

"Daxiong, why are you here?" Yang Qi paled in shock upon seeing Li Shimin. "You shouldn't have come!"

After the head jailer left, Li Shimin set down the wine jar and the food box. Ignoring the filth on the ground, he sat cross-legged and said, "I came to send you off. His Majesty granted permission, so do not worry."

Yang Qi peered behind Li Shimin. "Where is Dade? He didn't come too, did he? His health is fragile—stop dragging him around everywhere!"

Seeing no sign of Li Xuanba, Yang Qi let out a breath of relief. "Thank goodness. For once, you've shown some sense and didn't bring Dade along."

Li Shimin's lips twitched slightly. He wanted to tell Yang Qi about A-Xuan, but looking at the bright, gentle light in Yang Qi's grime-covered eyes, he swallowed his words.

He smiled and said, "Do you really think I have no sense of propriety? With such a major disaster hanging over you, do you know how much risk I'm taking just to see you? Even if A-Xuan wanted to come, I would have knocked him out, tied him up, and locked him in a room to stop him."

Yang Qi grumbled lightheartedly, "Fine, fine. Too bad A-Xuan isn't here to hear that. I'd love to see if you dare act so arrogant in front of his face."

Li Shimin chuckled. "I'm his elder brother. Teaching a younger brother a lesson is only natural."

"Yes, yes, of course." Yang Qi opened the food box. "It's been so long since I've had good meat and fine wine. Come, drink and eat your fill with your cousin!"

Li Shimin pulled out cups and poured the wine. "Come, let us drink until we drop!"

Neither of them brought up the armed rebellion. They simply matched each other cup for cup, just as they used to.

Li Shimin lay drunk in the cell all night.

The next day, Li Shimin bade Yang Qi farewell.

"Cousin Qi, I am returning to Zhangye to fight the Turks."

"Go then. I leave Great Sui's borders in your hands. Take care."

"Mhm. Take care, Cousin Qi."

Li Shimin turned and walked away without looking back.

Yang Qi watched Li Shimin leave with a gentle smile on his face.

Until the prison door shut tight, severing their line of sight.

The smile on Yang Qi's face faded away.

He sprawled out on the floor in an 'X' shape and murmured to himself, "Did something happen to Dade? Could he be ill? He must take care of himself... This cousin of yours is still relying on you two to burn incense and candles for me during the holidays."

After saying this, he released a long sigh and mocked himself, "I'm about to die, yet I still have time to worry about others? How strange... why am I not afraid of death at all? This doesn't sound like me."

After laughing at himself, his smile returned. "Perhaps dying now is far less painful than watching the Great Sui perish before meeting my end."

...

After coming out of the prison, Li Shimin did not wash or change his clothes. He immediately left Zhuo Commandery alongside his subordinates, who had been waiting outside the jail entrance.

He originally intended to escort his mother back to Taiyuan first, but his mother insisted that he head straight back to Zhangye.

Dou Huiming said, "Leave Taiyuan's affairs to your mother. I will handle them properly. You must trust A-Xuan—if A-Xuan said he can return to Zhangye, he definitely will. Hurry back and wait for him there."

Li Shimin said, "Thank you, Mother. I'm troubling you."

Choking back tears, Dou Huiming replied, "Do not thank your mother. I am your mother—how could it ever be a trouble?"

Li Shimin pursed his lips and forced a smile. "Forgive me. Mother... Mother is right. Your son will rely on Mother. Please tell Auntie Wan that Fifth Brother should be fine—A-Xuan has protected him well. However, it is better for Fifth Brother to return straight to Zhangye as well. Please forgive his unfilial behavior in being unable to return to Taiyuan to ease Auntie Wan's mind."

Dou Huiming clasped Li Shimin's hands in both of hers and said, "It is best for Fifth Brother to go to Zhangye. Only when he is in Zhangye by your side can Lady Wan truly rest easy."

Li Shimin nodded. "Mhm. I will protect A-Xuan and Fifth Brother. Mother and Auntie can rest assured. Mother, it is time for me to go."

"Go, go then. Be careful on the road." Dou Huiming released his hands and adjusted the collar of Li Shimin's fur cloak. "If the snow on the roads hasn't melted yet, rest a few extra days on the way. Take your time, and above all, stay safe."

Li Shimin bowed his head. "Yes, Mother."

A sharp pang wrung Dou Huiming's heart, yet the smile on her face never faltered. "Off you go. If you don't leave now, it will grow dark. Mother must set out as well."

Li Shimin and Zhangsun Kangning, who had been standing silently at his side, paid their respects to their mother before mounting their horses and riding away.

Only after watching them disappear into the distance did Dou Huiming board her carriage.

"Back to Taiyuan."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第139章 尚且顾不上悲伤
chunks.chineseText:
第139章 尚且顾不上悲伤

李元吉被收监。杨广已经决定让他的死掩盖太子兵谏， 现在正好又是冬季，万物肃杀的季节，正适合死刑，李元吉很快就被押上刑场。
　　李渊都来不及反应， 去刑场演一场慈父原谅不孝子， 替不孝子收尸的戏码。
　　不过李元吉会被传首各个郡县，震慑不忠不孝之人。他的头颅总会传到太原郡， 李渊还是有机会为这位逆子洒几滴眼泪。
　　为了不让李元吉说不该说的话， 李世民重金贿赂了裴蕴， 提前把李元吉毒哑了。
　　这是李世民第一次亲手做这种事。
　　以前这种事都是李玄霸来做，李世民第一次做这种事，感觉还好。
　　他知道身为主公不应该亲自做这等阴私事，但他觉得很痛快。
　　就这一次。下次他一定如史书中那些主公一样，披上一层道德粉饰的皮， 就像是阿玄说的那样， 成为一口不粘锅。
　　话说不粘锅究竟要怎么打造， 才能炒菜不粘底？
　　李元吉被处斩的时候， 李世民正在黄河边上。
　　现在正是冬季枯水期， 部分河床露出了大量泥沙和石头，寸草不生，原本奔腾的黄河水变得纤细而平静， 河流上的船只也减少了许多，显得有些荒凉。
　　他一边胡思乱想，从李元吉想到不粘锅，从不粘锅想到阿玄， 一边看向黄河南岸。
　　如果现在渡过黄河， 他就能前往瓦岗寨的地方， 问问阿玄在不在那里。
　　“郎君，要渡河吗？”秦琼问道，“如果要渡河，我就把缀在我们身后的尾巴解决掉。”
　　唐国公府出了这么大的事，好奇的人很多。杨广也派出了探子，看看李世民是不是真的对他真的忠心耿耿。
　　再者李世民成为大隋最年轻的慰抚使，还有许多士人缀在李世民身后，一副想要投奔李世民，但又不想过于殷勤，似乎要跟到张掖再去找机会的态度。
　　李世民回过神，淡淡道：“我现在还没做好起兵的准备。”
　　秦琼道：“只要我解决得够利落，不会被人察觉。”
　　这是李世民所有下属的意愿。
　　虽然李世民看似很冷静，但李世民的下属就算不是看着他长大的家奴，也常与李世民并肩作战。看着以前每日笑容爽朗的主公变得沉着冷静，他们实在是生不出“主公越来越成熟”的想法，只觉得难受。
　　李世民回头看向等候他回答的下属，神思一阵恍惚。
　　他看出了下属的心意。
　　“走吧，回张掖。既然阿玄说会来张掖找我，就肯定会来。”李世民道，“我可不希望在阿玄养病的时候传出了我勾结贼帅的风声，让阿玄无法安静休养。”
　　李世民笑道：“走吧，出发。”
　　他策马转身，没有再回头看黄河。
　　纵然他笑完后牙关紧咬得仿佛能尝到血腥味，也没有回头。
　　“阿嚏。”
　　李玄霸刚打完一个喷嚏，李智云就以百米冲刺的速度取来毛皮，把裹得严严实实的李玄霸又裹了一层。
　　李玄霸无奈：“我只是鼻子有点痒，没有受凉。”
　　李智云不信。
　　李玄霸揉了揉鼻子，道：“肯定是二哥在念我。”
　　李智云坐到李玄霸身边问道：“三兄，我们短时间内无法启程去张掖，但是不是该遣人向张掖送信，告知二兄我们平安？”
　　李玄霸叹气：“我也在想这件事。”
　　为了安二哥的心，自己确实应该送信，告诉二哥梦境虽然塌了，但自己还没死。
　　但他又担心自己仍旧熬不过去。
　　现在李玄霸虽然活着，也就是吊着一口气。不是他悲观。为他治病的孙医师和珠娘都不知道自己开的药方有没有用。
　　李玄霸从魏徵那里得知，大隋官府四处张贴告示，官府要将不忠不孝李元吉的脑袋四处悬挂示众，告知百姓准时前来观看。
　　虽然告示上没有写明此事细节，但李玄霸很容易就猜到，肯定是二哥去面圣时对杨广说了什么，鼓励官吏和百姓诬告的杨广才会重罚李元吉。
　　当李玄霸得知二哥成为河右慰抚使后，就更加确定了自己的猜测。
　　二哥能成功让杨广将李元吉枭首，还能哄得杨广开心，升任河右慰抚使，就证明二哥已经从自己死亡的阴影中冷静下来。
　　如果自己告诉二哥自己没死，后来又没熬过去，好不容易做好心理准备的二哥白欢喜一场，已经结疤的伤口又新增一条伤痕，那太折磨人了。
　　李玄霸对李智云说了自己的顾虑后，李智云气鼓鼓道：“三兄不准胡说，你已经好了！很快就会痊愈！”
　　李玄霸艰难地从层层叠叠的锦被毛皮中抽出手，在李智云额头上弹了一下：“我也希望自己能尽快痊愈，但做任何决定都应该先判断最坏的情况。”
　　李智云低着头嘟囔道：“最坏的情况也是三兄一定很快就会痊愈。”
　　李玄霸懒得再和李智云争辩，直接继续话题：“不过我们确实应该先告知万阿姨和宇文老师，你与珠娘都平安。”
　　李智云想了想，摇头道：“虽然我也想尽快安娘亲的心，但还是等三兄病愈，我们启程去张掖的时候再通知娘亲。我担心父亲会扣下我们派去的人，寻找我们的踪迹。我不信任他。”
　　李玄霸听到李智云直白地说不相信李渊，心中一酸。
　　虽然他也不信任，但李智云还小，他本不希望弟弟过早地看透这件沉重的事。
　　李智云道：“至于告不告诉宇文公，三兄还是问三嫂吧。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“珠娘肯定也说不告诉，担心会泄露踪迹。孙医师被魏玄成从宇文家请出来时，珠娘都没有联系家里人。”
　　李智云没好气道：“那三兄你还废话什么？难道还指望我去劝服三嫂？”
　　李玄霸无语：“小五，你是不是对我这个兄长越来越不尊敬了？语气很嚣张啊。”
　　李智云抱着手臂道：“想要教训我，那就快点痊愈啊。”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　小五该不是进入叛逆期了吧？小时候自己和二哥的小尾巴小五多可爱，自己要失去这个可爱的弟弟了吗？
　　李智云神情嚣张地离去，李玄霸长吁短叹。
　　宇文珠端着药进屋时，李玄霸啰啰嗦嗦抱怨了许久。
　　宇文珠忍笑道：“叔郎说得没错，赶紧好起来。等我们回到张掖，你就让兄公教训他。”
　　李玄霸假装愤愤道：“等我见到二哥，一定让二哥狠狠打小五的屁股。”
　　宇文珠忍不住了，失笑道：“是，是，来，三郎，先喝药。”
　　李玄霸的脸色立刻垮了。
　　真不想喝药啊。
　　孙医师和珠娘每日都在调整药方，李玄霸喝药的时候就像是在吃哈利·波特世界里的怪味豆盲盒，还是已经提前把能吃的口味全部挑出去的怪味豆盲盒。
　　宇文珠看见李玄霸的脸色，心有不忍。
　　她安慰道：“等我们回到张掖就好了。”
　　李玄霸勉强挤出笑容安慰妻子，咬牙将药小口小口地喝完。
　　不是他不想将汤药一饮而尽，尽可能减轻对味蕾的刺激，实在是味道太刺激了，一口闷下去一定会吐出来。
　　李玄霸一口药一口温水，药喝完了，肚子都被水撑饱了。
　　他捂着嘴干呕了一会儿，将嗓子里反复往上冒的药水咽下去，折腾了许久，才缓过劲来。
　　每次看到李玄霸这么难受，宇文珠都手足无措，不知道该做点什么缓解李玄霸的痛苦。
　　李玄霸每次自己缓过劲来，都会对宇文珠笑一笑，表明自己没事。
　　这样的笑容，让宇文珠更加难受和无力。
　　李玄霸见宇文珠难过，转移话题道：“知世郎已经回齐郡了吗？”
　　早几日他们就知道王薄回齐郡了。宇文珠知道李玄霸只是转移话题让她别难过。
　　她顺着话题道：“是。魏玄成以联络瓦岗寨的名义留了下来。”
　　李玄霸道：“珠娘，麻烦你跑一趟，把魏玄成请来。”
　　宇文珠担忧道：“你要好好休养，不能劳累。”
　　李玄霸笑道：“只是动动嘴皮子，不算劳累。”
　　宇文珠叹了口气，闷声道：“好。”
　　宇文珠离开后，李玄霸装不下去了，扶着床边又干呕了许久，难受得眼泪鼻涕糊了一脸。
　　好不容易又缓了过来，李玄霸一边擦脸一边自我开导道：“真想念后世打针和输液。如果死后能带着记忆回到前世，我要向领导申请，从唐太宗黑营销号转职成中医黑营销号。”
　　他躺回榻上，闭目养神，让翻腾的胃平静下来。
　　不一会儿，魏徵到来。
　　李智云又冒了出来，乖乖搬了个小坐墩旁听，就像是听课一样。
　　宇文珠将门掩上，继续和孙思邈讨论药方，处理药材。
　　李玄霸还未开口，魏徵就道：“我正好有事要告知三郎君。”
　　李玄霸问道：“李元吉死了？”
　　“李元吉是死了，但我要告诉三郎君的不是这件事。”魏徵神色黯然，“太子被赐自尽，贬为庶人。”
　　李玄霸闻言，脑袋一嗡，神情一片空白。
　　半晌，他才低下头，散乱的发丝垂下，遮住了他的双眼：“被赐自尽就罢了，连一个‘戾’的恶谥都不愿意给，直接贬为庶人吗？”
　　历来太子最差的谥号就是“戾太子”了。
　　杨暕不是谋逆，只是兵谏，按照礼法，应当是“戾太子”。
　　但杨广连“戾太子”都不愿意给，居然直接将杨暕逐出了宗室。
　　李智云抱着手臂，嘟囔道：“杨广这个父亲，还不如我的父亲。”
　　李玄霸道：“拿杨广和我们父亲比，你还是太过了。父亲怎么都比杨广强多了。”
　　李智云敷衍道：“哦。”
　　魏徵问道：“太子被赐死，我们能趁机做什么吗？”
　　李玄霸道：“你是想效仿陈胜吴广起义旧事，以太子的名义召集百姓，扩大义军规模？”
　　魏徵点头：“是。”
　　李玄霸道：“让我想一想。”
　　他来不及为二表兄悲伤，就思考如何利用这件事。
　　半晌，李玄霸问道：“高丽战势如何？”
　　魏徵不屑道：“高丽弹丸小国，大隋早就应该胜利。现在已经三征，高丽肯定撑不住了，就算只有来护儿的水军编制齐全，也能轻易战胜。”
　　李玄霸道：“我知道这次能战胜高丽，我是问战胜后。高丽王投降后，杨广是要求继续进军，还是像一征高丽时那样，只要高丽王一投降，他就傻傻地退兵？”
　　魏徵道：“这个我就不清楚了。”
　　李玄霸道：“去打探。把具体消息告诉我。水军就是从齐郡出发，知世郎在齐郡，消息应该很灵通。”
　　魏徵道：“是。三郎君，得知之后，我们该做什么？我可以提前安排。”
　　李玄霸道：“如果杨广退兵，一定会先回洛阳，再北上召集西域诸国和突厥觐见，用自己征讨高丽的战功震慑西域诸国。那时我们就能趁机行事。所以我要想知道杨广的动向。”
　　魏徵眼露兴奋道：“是！我这就做！”
　　李玄霸道：“你可以提前通知义军。民间不是说你们是十八路反王吗？如果你们十八路反王追杀杨广，一定能轰动天下。”
　　魏徵犹豫道：“我不知道他们敢不敢对杨广动手。”
　　李玄霸道：“杨玄感现在不是又东山再起吗？杨广从高丽回来，一定会对他动手，彻底将他剿灭。所以他一定会率先动手，打杨广一个措手不及。我相信杨玄感为你们拖住大隋军队主力，你们一定能够有机会做这个壮举。”
　　魏徵问道：“我是不是应该去联系杨玄感？”
　　李玄霸道：“等问到杨广动向后，你就可以去游说杨玄感与义军配合攻打杨广了。杨玄感麾下的李密是个不错的谋士，他一定会帮你说服杨玄感。”
　　魏徵笑道：“我早就听闻李密之名，这次去会会他。”
　　李智云好奇：“那李密有多厉害？我们可以收服他吗？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“这个人心高气傲，有自立之心。就算现在他屈居杨玄感之下，待杨玄感衰弱时，他一定会噬主自立。这样的人，也不会甘心屈居我等之下。”
　　李智云对李密兴趣淡去：“哦，那他完了。二兄和三兄将来一定会把他干掉。”
　　魏徵失笑，李玄霸扶额。
　　李玄霸再次确定，弟弟可能真的进入叛逆期了。
　　魏徵兴冲冲离开。
　　李智云爬到榻上，依偎在李玄霸身边：“三兄，想哭就哭吧，弟弟肩膀借给你。”
　　李玄霸道：“我哭什么？”
　　李智云打量三兄的神情：“三兄，你确实没哭，但表情有点可怕。你在想什么危险的事？”
　　李玄霸平静道：“我什么危险的事都没想。”
　　他只是在想，本以为二表兄的离去会非常悲壮。但杨广却一边让李元吉出来吸引人视线，一边悄悄赐死二表兄，让二表兄离去得悄无声息。
　　二表兄都这么努力了，他的丧礼不应该如此冷清。
　　趁着自己还吊着一口气，帮二表兄准备一场配得上他的盛大丧礼吧。
　　比如十八路反王为他举旗发丧，全天下百姓为他恸哭。
　　再比如，送杨广下去给他陪葬。
　　大隋的希望，两位英明的太子都被杨广害死了。无论是杨广还是大隋，都合该是陪葬品。
　　“小五，我突然想到一个办法，就算不通知二哥和宇文老师，也能向他们报平安了。”
　　“嗯？什么办法？”
　　李玄霸笑道：“秘密。过阵子你就知道了。”
　　杨广这样的人，怎么能在大隋亡之前还舒舒服服享乐？他这颗好头颅，怎么还能在死后也安安稳稳地待在他的脖子上？
　　从现在开始，就变成惊弓之鸟吧，直到被人砍掉头颅为止。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 139: No Time for Grief Yet

Li Yuanji was taken into custody. Yang Guang had already decided to use his death to cover up the Crown Prince’s armed rebellion. As it happened to be winter—a season when all creation withered under a bleak frost—it was the ideal time for an execution. Thus, Li Yuanji was swiftly marched off to the execution ground.

Li Yuan did not even have time to react, let alone put on a show at the execution site—playing the benevolent father who forgave his unfilial son and claiming his body.

However, Li Yuanji’s severed head was to be paraded across various commanderies and counties to intimidate the disloyal and unfilial. Eventually, his head would be brought to Taiyuan Commandery, so Li Yuan would still get his chance to shed a few tears for this treacherous son.

To prevent Li Yuanji from blurting out anything he shouldn't, Li Shimin had bribed Pei Yun with a heavy sum to poison Li Yuanji mute in advance.

This was the first time Li Shimin had personally orchestrated such a deed.

In the past, these underhanded matters were always handled by Li Xuanba. Doing it himself for the first time, Li Shimin felt it wasn't too bad.

He knew that as a lord, he shouldn't personally meddle in such dirty affairs, yet he found it immensely satisfying.

Just this once. Next time, he would certainly be like the rulers in the history books, wrapping himself in a veneer of whitewashed morality—or, as Ah Xuan put it, becoming a "non-stick pan."

Come to think of it, how on earth did one forge a non-stick pan so that food wouldn't stick to the bottom when stir-frying?

***

When Li Yuanji was beheaded, Li Shimin was standing beside the Yellow River.

It was currently the dry season of winter. Large expanses of the riverbed lay exposed, strewn with silt and bare stones, devoid of a single blade of grass. The once-raging waters of the Yellow River had dwindled into a slender, placid stream. The vessels plying the river had thinned significantly as well, lending the landscape a desolate air.

His thoughts drifted aimlessly—from Li Yuanji to the non-stick pan, and from the non-stick pan to Ah Xuan—as he gazed toward the southern bank of the Yellow River.

If he crossed the Yellow River right now, he could head into Wagang Stronghold's territory and ask if Ah Xuan was there.

"My Lord, shall we cross the river?" Qin Qiong asked. "If so, I will deal with the tails trailing behind us."

With such a major upheaval in the Duke of Tang’s residence, many were curious. Yang Guang had also dispatched spies to see whether Li Shimin was truly unswervingly loyal to him.

Furthermore, now that Li Shimin had become the youngest Pacification Commissioner in the Great Sui, many scholars trailed after him. They bore the posture of wanting to pledge allegiance to him, yet refrained from appearing overly eager, seemingly intending to follow him all the way to Zhangye before seeking an opportunity.

Li Shimin snapped back to reality and said mildly, "I am not yet ready to raise troops."

Qin Qiong replied, "As long as I deal with them cleanly enough, no one will notice."

This was the shared wish of all Li Shimin’s subordinates.

Though Li Shimin appeared calm on the surface, his subordinates—if not household servants who had watched him grow up—were comrades who had fought side by side with him. Seeing their lord, who used to laugh heartily every day, turn so quiet and composed, they could not bring themselves to think, *Our lord is growing more mature.* They only felt an aching heart.

Li Shimin turned back to look at the subordinates awaiting his answer, his mind drifting for a moment.

He saw through their thoughts.

"Let us go to Zhangye. Since Ah Xuan said he would come to Zhangye to find me, he definitely will," Li Shimin said. "I would hate for rumors of me colluding with rebel chieftains to spread while Ah Xuan is recuperating, disturbing his quiet recovery."

Li Shimin smiled and said, "Let's go. Onward."

He turned his horse around without looking back at the Yellow River.

Even though after his smile passed, his jaw gritted so tightly he could almost taste the coppery tang of blood, he did not turn back.

***

"Achoo!"

Li Xuanba had barely finished sneezing when Li Zhiyun darted over at a full sprint with a fur cloak, wrapping the already swaddled Li Xuanba in yet another layer.

Li Xuanba grunted helplessly. "My nose was just a little itchy. I didn't catch a cold."

Li Zhiyun didn't buy it.

Li Xuanba rubbed his nose and said, "It must be Second Brother missing me."

Li Zhiyun sat down beside Li Xuanba and asked, "Third Brother, we can't set off for Zhangye anytime soon, but shouldn't we dispatch someone to send a letter to Zhangye to let Second Brother know we are safe?"

Li Xuanba sighed. "I've been thinking about that too."

To set Second Brother’s mind at ease, he really ought to send a message, letting him know that although the dream realm had collapsed, he was not dead yet.

Yet he worried he still might not pull through.
