Although Li Xuanba was alive right now, he was barely hanging on by a thread. It wasn't that he was pessimistic; even Physician Sun and Zhuniang, who were treating him, had no idea if the prescriptions they wrote were working.

From Wei Zheng, Li Xuanba had learned that the Sui official government was posting notices everywhere, announcing that the head of the disloyal and unfilial Li Yuanji would be hung in public across various locations, instructing the populace to come watch.

Although the notices didn't detail the specifics of the incident, Li Xuanba easily deduced that Second Brother must have said something to Yang Guang during his audience. Only then would Yang Guang—who actively encouraged officials and commoners to make false accusations—impose such a harsh punishment on Li Yuanji.

When Li Xuanba learned that Second Brother had become the Pacification Commissioner of He-You, he became even more certain of his suspicion.

If Second Brother could successfully coax Yang Guang into decapitating Li Yuanji and even make Yang Guang happy enough to promote him to Pacification Commissioner of He-You, it proved that Second Brother had already composed himself enough to step out of the shadow of his supposed death.

If he told Second Brother he was alive, only to fail to survive later, Second Brother—who had finally braced himself emotionally—would experience empty joy, opening a new wound over a freshly scabbed one. That would be far too cruel.

After Li Xuanba shared his worries with Li Zhiyun, the boy puffed his cheeks in anger and said, "Third Brother, stop talking nonsense! You're already getting better! You'll recover completely very soon!"

Li Xuanba struggled to pull a hand out from the layers of brocade quilts and furs, flicking Li Zhiyun on the forehead. "I also hope to recover quickly, but before making any decision, one must first evaluate the worst-case scenario."

Li Zhiyun lowered his head and muttered, "Even the worst-case scenario is that Third Brother will definitely recover very soon."

Li Xuanba didn't feel like arguing further with Li Zhiyun and steered the topic forward. "However, we should indeed inform Auntie Wan and Teacher Yuwen first that you and Zhuniang are safe."

Li Zhiyun thought about it, then shook his head. "Although I want to ease Mother's worries as soon as possible, it's better to wait until Third Brother gets well and we set off for Zhangye before informing Mother. I'm worried Father might detain our messengers to track us down. I don't trust him."

Hearing Li Zhiyun state so bluntly that he did not trust Li Yuan, Li Xuanba felt a pang of sadness.

Although he didn't trust him either, Li Zhiyun was still young. He hadn't wanted his younger brother to see through such a heavy truth so soon.

Li Zhiyun added, "As for whether to inform Duke Yuwen, Third Brother should ask Third Sister-in-law."

Li Xuanba sighed. "Zhuniang would definitely say no, worrying it might expose our whereabouts. When Wei Xuancheng fetched Physician Sun from the Yuwen Residence, Zhuniang didn't contact her family either."

Li Zhiyun said crossly, "Then why are you talking nonsense, Third Brother? Were you expecting me to persuade Third Sister-in-law?"

Li Xuanba was speechless. "Fifth Brother, are you losing respect for me as your elder brother? Your tone is quite arrogant."

Li Zhiyun crossed his arms. "If you want to lecture me, then hurry up and get well!"

Li Xuanba: "..."

*Could Fifth Brother have entered his rebellious phase? When he was little, he was such a cute little shadow following Second Brother and me around. Am I about to lose my adorable little brother?*

Li Zhiyun strutted off with a cocky expression, leaving Li Xuanba sighing again and again.

When Yuwen Zhu carried in a bowl of medicine, Li Xuanba grumbled and complained endlessly.

Yuwen Zhu suppressed a smile and said, "Your younger brother is right. Get well quickly. Once we return to Zhangye, you can have Elder Brother give him a good discipline."

Li Xuanba feigned righteous indignation. "When I see Second Brother, I'll definitely have him give Fifth Brother a thorough spanking!"

Yuwen Zhu couldn't hold it in anymore and giggled. "Yes, yes. Come, Sanlang, drink your medicine first."

Li Xuanba's face instantly fell.

He *really* didn't want to drink medicine.

Physician Sun and Zhuniang adjusted the prescription every day. Drinking medicine felt like opening a blind box of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans from Harry Potter—except all the palatable flavors had been sorted out in advance.

Seeing the look on Li Xuanba's face, Yuwen Zhu felt a pang of pity.

She comforted him, "It will be better once we get back to Zhangye."

Li Xuanba managed to force a smile to reassure his wife, gritting his teeth as he sipped the medicine down little by little.

It wasn't that he didn't want to gulp down the decoction in one go to minimize the assault on his taste buds; the taste was simply so overpowering that chugging it down would guarantee he'd throw it right back up.

Li Xuanba took a sip of medicine, then a sip of warm water. By the time the medicine was finished, his stomach was bloated with water.

Covering his mouth, he dry-heaved for a while, swallowing back the bitter liquid that kept rising in his throat. Only after a long struggle did he catch his breath.

Every time she saw Li Xuanba in such agony, Yuwen Zhu felt helpless, not knowing what she could do to ease his pain.

Whenever Li Xuanba recovered his breath, he would offer Yuwen Zhu a reassuring smile to show he was fine.

That very smile only made Yuwen Zhu feel even more heartbroken and powerless.

Noticing Yuwen Zhu's distress, Li Xuanba shifted the topic. "Has the Zhishi Lang returned to Qi Commandery?"

They had known days ago that Wang Bo had returned to Qi Commandery. Yuwen Zhu knew Li Xuanba was only changing the subject so she wouldn't feel sad.

She played along with the topic. "Yes. Wei Xuancheng stayed behind under the pretext of contacting Wagang Stronghold."

Li Xuanba said, "Zhuniang, please make a trip to invite Wei Xuancheng over."

Yuwen Zhu said worriedly, "You need to rest properly. You shouldn't overexert yourself."

Li Xuanba smiled. "I'm just flapping my lips; it's not overexertion."

Yuwen Zhu sighed and said softly, "Alright."

Once Yuwen Zhu left, Li Xuanba couldn't keep up the facade any longer. Clinging to the edge of the bed, he dry-heaved violently for a long time, tears and snot smearing across his face from the agony.

Having finally steadied himself once more, Li Xuanba wiped his face while consoling himself: *I really miss modern injections and IV drips. If I die and can return to my previous life with my memories intact, I'm going to ask my boss to let me transfer from being an anti-Emperor-Taizong-of-Tang troll to an anti-Traditional-Chinese-Medicine troll.*

He lay back on the couch, closing his eyes to rest and let his churning stomach settle.

Before long, Wei Zheng arrived.

Li Zhiyun popped up again, obediently pulling over a small stool to sit and listen, just like a student attending a lecture.

Yuwen Zhu pulled the door shut and went back to discussing prescriptions and processing herbs with Sun Simiao.

Before Li Xuanba could speak, Wei Zheng said, "I happen to have news to report to Third Young Master."

Li Xuanba asked, "Is Li Yuanji dead?"

"Li Yuanji is dead, but that is not what I wished to tell you." Wei Zheng's expression darkened. "The Crown Prince was bestowed suicide and demoted to a commoner."

Hearing this, Li Xuanba felt his head buzz, his expression turning completely blank.

After a long silence, he lowered his head, his disheveled hair falling forward to cover his eyes. "Being bestowed suicide is one thing, but not even granting him a derogatory posthumous title like 'Li'... stripping his royal status and reducing him directly to a commoner?"

Historically, the worst posthumous title a Crown Prince could receive was "Crown Prince Li" (The Remorseful Crown Prince).

Yang Jian hadn't committed treason; it was merely an armed remonstrance. According to ritual law, he should have been given the posthumous title of "Crown Prince Li."

Yet Yang Guang was unwilling to accord even "Crown Prince Li," going so far as to expel Yang Jian from the imperial clan entirely.

Li Zhiyun crossed his arms and muttered, "Yang Guang as a father is even worse than mine."

Li Xuanba said, "Comparing Yang Guang with our father is going too far. Father is far better than Yang Guang in every way."

Li Zhiyun gave a perfunctory reply. "Oh."

Wei Zheng asked, "Now that the Crown Prince has been forced to commit suicide, can we seize this opportunity to do something?"

Li Xuanba asked, "Do you intend to follow the precedent of Chen Sheng and Wu Guang's rebellion—mustering the people under the Crown Prince's banner to expand the rebel army's scale?"

Wei Zheng nodded. "Yes."

Li Xuanba said, "Let me think."

Having no time to grieve for his second cousin, he immediately pondered how to leverage this development.

After a long pause, Li Xuanba asked, "How goes the war in Goguryeo?"

Wei Zheng said disdainfully, "Goguryeo is a tiny, insignificant country; the Great Sui should have triumphed long ago. Now on the third campaign, Goguryeo surely cannot hold out. Even if only Lai Hu'er's navy remains fully intact, a victory can still be easily won."

Li Xuanba said, "I know Goguryeo can be defeated this time. I am asking about what happens *after* the victory. Once the King of Goguryeo surrenders, will Yang Guang demand to push further, or will he foolishly withdraw his troops as soon as the king surrenders, just like during the first campaign?"

Wei Zheng said, "That I am not certain of."

Li Xuanba said, "Go investigate. Bring me the specifics. The navy launched from Qi Commandery, and the Zhishi Lang is in Qi Commandery; his sources should be well-informed."

Wei Zheng replied, "Understood. Third Young Master, once we know, what should we do? I can make preparations in advance."

Li Xuanba said, "If Yang Guang withdraws, he will definitely return to Luoyang first, then head north to summon the states of the Western Regions and the Eastern Turks for an audience, using his military exploits in Goguryeo to awe them. That will be our window to act. Therefore, I must know Yang Guang's movements."

Wei Zheng's eyes gleamed with excitement. "Understood! I will see to it at once!"

Li Xuanba added, "You can notify the rebel armies in advance. Doesn't the common folk call you the Eighteen Rebel Kings? If you Eighteen Rebel Kings join forces to hunt down Yang Guang, it will surely shake the entire world."

Wei Zheng hesitated. "I am unsure if they will dare strike at Yang Guang directly."

Li Xuanba said, "Isn't Yang Xuangan making a comeback right now? Once Yang Guang returns from Goguryeo, he will move against him to wipe him out completely. Thus, Yang Xuangan will certainly strike first to catch Yang Guang off guard. With Yang Xuangan tying down the main force of the Sui army, I am confident you will have the chance to pull off this grand feat."

Wei Zheng asked, "Should I make contact with Yang Xuangan?"

Li Xuanba said, "Once you have ascertained Yang Guang's movements, you can go persuade Yang Xuangan to coordinate with the rebel forces in attacking Yang Guang. Li Mi under Yang Xuangan is a fine strategist; he will definitely help you convince Yang Xuangan."

Wei Zheng smiled. "I have long heard of Li Mi's name. I shall pay him a visit this time."

Li Zhiyun asked curiously, "How capable is this Li Mi? Can we recruit him?"

Li Xuanba shook his head. "That man is proud and ambitious, harbouring desires to rule on his own. Even though he currently bides his time under Yang Xuangan, the moment Yang Xuangan falters, he will surely turn on his master and establish his own power. Such a person will never be content serving under us."

Li Zhiyun's interest in Li Mi evaporated. "Oh, then he's doomed. Second Brother and Third Brother will definitely finish him off in the future."

Wei Zheng broke into a laugh, while Li Xuanba rubbed his forehead.

Li Xuanba became increasingly convinced that his younger brother had indeed entered his rebellious phase.

Wei Zheng left in high spirits.

Li Zhiyun climbed onto the couch and snuggled next to Li Xuanba. "Third Brother, if you want to cry, just cry. I'll lend you my shoulder."

Li Xuanba said, "Why would I cry?"

Li Zhiyun scrutinized his elder brother's expression. "Third Brother, you aren't crying, but your expression is a little scary. What dangerous thoughts are running through your head?"

Li Xuanba replied calmly, "I am not thinking of anything dangerous."

He was merely thinking: he had assumed Second Cousin's passing would be tragic and heroic. Yet Yang Guang had pushed Li Yuanji into the spotlight to draw everyone's attention while quietly bestowing death upon Second Cousin, letting him slip away without a sound.

Second Cousin had fought so hard; his funeral should not be so quiet and lonely.

While he himself still hung on by a thread, he would prepare a grand funeral worthy of Second Cousin.

For instance, having the Eighteen Rebel Kings raise banners of mourning for him, and the people of the entire realm weep for him.

Or perhaps... sending Yang Guang down to be buried alongside him.

The hopes of the Great Sui—two wise and brilliant Crown Princes—had both been ruined and slain by Yang Guang. Whether it was Yang Guang himself or the Great Sui Dynasty, both deserved to be sacrificed as funeral goods.

"Fifth Brother, I suddenly thought of a way to let Second Brother and Teacher Yuwen know we are safe, even without sending them direct word."

"Hmm? What way?"

Li Xuanba smiled. "It's a secret. You'll know in a little while."

How could a man like Yang Guang be allowed to live in comfortable luxury before the fall of the Sui? How could that fine head of his still sit securely on his neck even in death?

From this moment on, let him become a bird startled by the mere twang of a bowstring—until the day his head is severed from his neck.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第140章 翟公可向我问策
chunks.chineseText:
第140章 翟公可向我问策

当李玄霸得到杨广消息时， 已经是初冬。
　　在原本历史中，杨广在八月中秋就该结束征讨高丽，然后班师回朝，难得回一趟大兴。
　　或许是这一世农民起义军的烈度更大， 也可能是杨玄感未被彻底剿灭， 杨广征召兵卒、役夫的效率低了一点，九月才结束征讨高丽。
　　但与原本历史相同的是， 杨广仍旧在高丽王请求投降时下令撤兵。
　　这次军中不仅有来护儿试图继续攻打高丽， 宋国公贺若弼也试图违抗杨广的命令。
　　因为高颎和宇文弼离开了权力中枢， 贺若弼也没有像原本历史中那样，在大业三年因言获罪被杀。
　　杨广一征高丽时，因为有贺若弼力挽狂澜，隋军没有溃败。但杨广被高丽王的假投降戏耍，错过了战机， 贺若弼一顿抱怨， 被杨广关入了大牢。
　　因为不是太大的罪， 没有触及杨广的底线， 贺若弼又有战功在身， 所以杨广最终只是削了贺若弼的官职，没有杀贺若弼。二征、三征高丽时，杨广还都带上了贺若弼。
　　或许是因为被杨广关进了大牢的缘故， 贺若弼终于想起父亲被逼自杀前的“锥舌诫子”，变得谨言慎行。
　　所以三征高丽时，杨广任命贺若弼作为分路主将之一。
　　贺若弼老当益壮，和来护儿配合默契， 眼见着要把平壤攻克了。
　　高丽王又又又投降了， 杨广又又又同意了。
　　贺若弼那暴脾气啊， 还是没忍下来，指着杨广鼻子大骂。
　　这也就罢了，但得知太子杨暕兵谏时，贺若弼私下说了许多支持和怜惜太子杨暕的话，被人传到了杨广耳中。
　　于是贺若弼又被下狱了。
　　这次他很快病逝在了狱中，据说是忧愤成疾。
　　不过这次获罪的只有贺若弼一人，他的儿子只是被削掉了官职和爵位，没有像原本历史中那样也被逼自尽。
　　魏徵和李玄霸说起此事时，不住冷笑。
　　李玄霸沉沉叹了口气：“让高丽王投降，或许是杨广的执念了。”
　　后世人能说出无数条征讨高丽的必要性，隋文帝和唐太宗、唐高宗也和高丽敌对。但从历史中杨广的行为来看，杨广征讨高丽真的就是纯粹为了面子。只要高丽王投降，他就心满意足。
　　至于什么地什么人什么边疆安稳，只要高丽王投降就撤兵的隋炀帝，似乎不怎么在乎。
　　不只是这个时空的杨广，原本历史中的杨广也如此。
　　一征高丽时被高丽人的假投降戏耍了那么多次，三征高丽时他还是信了高丽人的假投降，让已经快到平壤城下的来护儿班师回朝，气得来护儿这个颇听杨广话的心腹将领差点违抗圣旨。
　　李玄霸投胎转世十几年，“未来”因为他的蝴蝶翅膀已经更改了许多，他的“预知”已经不再准确。
　　但聪明的穿越者倚仗的从来不是“一成不变”的未来，而是根据原本时空中的历史事件、人物行为来了解历史的大势、人物的性格，再结合现实中搜集的情报，做出“预知性”的判断。
　　比如杨广这死不悔改的性格，就很容易推断出他的行为。
　　他一定会重蹈覆辙，所谓蝴蝶翅膀，不过是把他重蹈覆辙的时间微调一点。
　　魏徵道：“皇帝现在的行为，是否附和三郎君的预料？”
　　李玄霸道：“差不多。你们这次可以试探一下他，追着隋朝大军的尾巴抢夺辎重马匹。对了，涿郡义军首领杨公卿很了解涿郡地形，你们与他合作试试。”
　　原本历史中杨公卿就追着班师回朝的隋军抢劫，夺走了隋军四十多匹好马。
　　魏徵犹豫：“我们这次动作太大，会不会刺激皇帝发重兵征讨我们？”
　　李玄霸笑道：“杨玄感已经有所动作。以杨广的性格，他瞧不起农民义军，甚至农民义军的战况都入不了他的耳，他只忌惮楚国公杨玄感。而且贺若弼已死，宇文述不擅长带兵，隋军班师回朝时阵型一定很混乱。现在比二征高丽时还乱，那时你们跑得了，现在更跑得了。”
　　魏徵叹气：“那时各地义军元帅光脚的不怕穿鞋的，敢把脑袋系在裤腰带上冒险。现在他们大多有了自己的基业，恐怕难以说动。不过知世郎肯定会同意。我再劝说翟元帅试试。”
　　李玄霸道：“这个简单。我想翟让已经差不多猜到我这个病人不是什么魏家族妹了，你可引他见我。”
　　魏徵惊讶道：“三郎君不担心翟让告密？”
　　李玄霸失笑：“如我当初和王薄所说的话一样，谁会听他告密？还是说，他想被大隋招降了？”
　　魏徵也跟着笑了起来：“他肯定是不愿意被大隋招降的。三郎君既然如此有胆量，徵只有听从。不过三郎君切记不要太劳心劳力，身体才最重要。”
　　李玄霸道：“放心吧。我只是找点事做，好转移一下养病的注意力。孙医师和珠娘研制的汤药真的太难喝了。”
　　看着李玄霸的苦相，魏徵笑得超级大声。
　　乖乖“听课”的李智云阴阳怪气道：“三兄既然怕喝药，就赶紧痊愈，别拖拖拉拉。”
　　李玄霸反手给了坐在床边的李智云脑壳一下，没好气道：“这是我不想痊愈吗？”
　　“哼。”李智云冷哼。
　　李玄霸露出头疼的神色。
　　怎么办？弟弟真的叛逆期了。
　　魏徵看着李玄霸和李智云兄弟二人的互动，再次笑了出来。
　　看到三郎君和五郎君的相处，他大概就能猜到主公和三郎君如何相处了。
　　一定很有意思。
　　魏徵与瓦岗寨的人相处了几个月，对翟让的品行有所了解，所以李玄霸想要见翟让时，他很赞同。
　　以三郎君的本事，再加上自己的三寸不烂之舌，说不定又能给主公收服一方势力。
　　翟让确实有所猜测。
　　不过他只是猜测魏徵护着的是被杨广迫害的名士罪臣，所以体贴地没有拆穿。
　　翟让连寒门都算不上，只是略识得字的小吏。
　　因为在官府当值时耳濡目染，翟让对世家名士很是敬仰。
　　他猜到魏徵“窝藏”的是获罪名士后，就对李玄霸等人更加殷勤恭敬，心里很希望魏徵能帮他引荐。
　　如果魏徵不为他引荐，翟让也没有怨言。在翟让看来，名士就该如此高傲，看不起他是正常的。
　　当魏徵暗示，“虽然男女有别，但救命之恩不能不报，族妹想戴着冪离感谢翟公”。
　　翟让嘴上说着不用不用，激动得一晚上没睡着。
　　第二日，他烧水狠狠搓了三次澡，又选了半个时辰的衣冠，还悄悄往晒黑了的脸上扑了点粉。
　　最早投奔他的同乡好友单雄信嘲笑翟让：“你不会是看上魏公的族妹了？”
　　翟让脸色大变，忙训斥道：“不可胡言！”
　　单雄信摸了摸鼻子：“好好好，不胡言，士女名声很重要。唉，都快听你说腻了。懋功，你说是不是？”
　　徐世勣无语道：“单兄，你是真没猜到，还是故意开玩笑？”
　　单雄信疑惑：“什么故意不故意？”
　　翟让和徐世勣对视一眼，眼中满是无奈。
　　单雄信不满道：“你们俩打什么哑谜？喂喂喂，不会有事瞒着我吧？”
　　翟让看着单雄信眼中清澈的愚蠢，深深叹了口气：“等我拜访魏公那位‘族妹’再告诉你。”
　　单雄信丈二和尚摸不着头脑，正想再问，被徐世勣拉住。
　　徐世勣道：“翟公这样做，自有他的打算。你猜不出来，就不要添乱。”
　　单雄信不高兴道：“就你们聪明，排挤我。行，我不问了。”
　　等翟让离开后，单雄信把着徐世勣的肩膀，挤眉弄眼道：“翟公走了，快，悄悄告诉我。我嘴很严，你又不是不知道，我一定能保守秘密。”
　　徐世勣没好气道：“既然翟公说会亲自告诉你，我就不会开口。”
　　单雄信把徐世勣按住：“真不说？不说收拾你！”
　　徐世勣翻白眼：“行啊，去校场，看谁教训谁。”
　　单雄信把徐世勣往屋外拖：“行，嚣张！”
　　他刚出门，就看见翟让站在门口皱着眉看着他，顿时缩了缩脖子：“翟公，你还没走啊。”
　　翟让再次沉沉叹了口气，道：“你这种性格，我怎么放心告诉你秘密？别欺负懋功，等我回来。”
　　单雄信讪讪道：“是。”
　　徐世勣咧嘴对单雄信做嘴型“活该”。
　　翟让道：“懋功，你也不准主动挑衅。”
　　徐世勣道：“哦。”
　　翟让又叮嘱了几句，才离开。
　　没走几步，他又听见身后单雄信自以为声音很低的“密谋”。
　　“告诉我！”
　　“不！”
　　“悄悄告诉我。”
　　“不。”
　　翟让加快脚步。
　　心累。
　　见到魏徵时，翟让不由抱怨起自己这两位兄弟，以及其他性格各异的兄弟。
　　人难带啊。
　　魏徵失笑：“翟公麾下人才如云，这真是幸福的烦恼。”
　　翟让苦笑：“我只是担心我带不动他们……罢了，不说泄气话。”
　　他和魏徵走到李玄霸门口时，整了整衣襟，不住深呼吸。
　　魏徵哭笑不得：“翟公不必紧张。我知道你猜测房中可能是当世名士，其实真不是，只是一位身份不宜公开的年轻士子。”
　　翟让听言，心头一阵失望。
　　不过他还是笑道：“我这卑微出身，就是见到普通士子也会紧张。”
　　魏徵心道，倒也不是普通士子。
　　得知不是什么当朝名士后，翟让没有再在门前踌躇，重新恢复了自信的笑容，推门进屋。
　　屋内，李智云正在给他哥剥橘子。
　　橘子当然是翟让送来讨好“名士”的。
　　翟让看见仍旧做女子打扮的李智云，脚步一顿。
　　他对魏徵道：“不戴冪离？”
　　李智云放下橘子，起身作揖：“我也不是女子。谢翟公收留。”
　　翟让吓了一跳，结结巴巴道：“你、你不是女子？你之前的声音……”
　　李智云切换女声：“假的，是口技。”
　　翟让的表情很精彩：“珠娘难道也……”
　　李智云神色警惕：“珠娘是我三嫂！”
　　“咳，小五！别胡闹。”李玄霸叹气道，“翟公，我身体有恙，只能躺在榻上说话，失礼了。”
　　翟让这才把视线投向躺在病床上的李玄霸。
　　病榻上的少年郎年岁应该不大，两颊凹陷满脸病容，头发披散仿若枯草，但双目十分明亮锐利，仿佛能看透自己，让翟让生出了一点不自在。
　　李智云拱手道：“翟公，失礼了。但珠娘是我三嫂！”
　　李玄霸忍不住伸手捏住李智云的脸颊：“不用一直强调！”
　　李智云“哼哼”：“三兄，你不知道瓦岗寨有多少倾慕三嫂。现在我们要坦白身份，当然要强调这一点。”
　　翟让心头尴尬，忙道：“是我御下不严，请……小郎君恕罪。”
　　李玄霸松开李智云的脸颊，道：“是我教育弟弟不严格，让翟公笑话了。坐好，闭嘴，别捣乱！”
　　李智云乖巧道：“哦。”
　　约束好多嘴多舌的弟弟后，李玄霸面带歉意道：“翟公请坐。”
　　魏徵拉着翟让在李玄霸床榻边的坐墩上坐下。
　　翟让看向魏徵，用眼神询问魏徵为何不为自己介绍。
　　魏徵笑道：“还是让三郎君自己说吧。”
　　李玄霸躺在榻上拱手：“在下大隋虎牙郎将李玄霸，字大德。翟公可能没听说过我……”
　　翟让猛地站起来，坐墩倒地。
　　李智云一脸紧张地按在了腰间短刀上。
　　李玄霸笑道：“看来翟公听说过我。”
　　翟让深呼吸，他没有回答，而是看向魏徵：“魏公，你何苦骗我？”
　　魏徵疑惑：“我骗你什么？”
　　翟让咬牙切齿：“你说不是名士！”
　　魏徵讶异：“原来三郎君已经是当世名士了吗？”
　　李智云松了口气，嬉笑道：“不敢当不敢当。”
　　李玄霸瞥了弟弟一眼。我还没说不敢当，你先替我谦虚了。
　　魏徵帮翟让把坐墩扶起来，再次拉着翟让坐下：“你这下知道为什么三郎君为何要隐藏了？三郎君信任你，你可别辜负三郎君的信任。”
　　翟让脸皮不断抖动：“这、这……李郎将应当很得狗……得皇帝信任，为何会沦落至此？”
　　李玄霸道：“家门不幸。翟公应当已经看过最近的告示。”
　　翟让刚才脑子没转过来，现在李玄霸一提，他立刻想了起来：“李元吉诬告李郎将谋反？”
　　李玄霸道：“他的诬告倒是没什么，只是丁郡丞软禁我时，不知道谁想放火追杀我，导致我落入水中。我本就病弱，这次真是吃够了苦头。”
　　翟让叹气道：“确实是家门不幸。李郎将是大隋忠臣，竟然沦落到瓦岗寨了……唉。不过李郎将放心，李郎将素有仁名，又和李将军在河右抵御蛮夷，我翟某虽然反了大隋，但不会为难李郎将。”
　　李智云插嘴：“什么？二哥居然成将军了？”
　　李玄霸叹气：“小五，你能不能闭嘴，让我好好与翟公聊完再说话。”
　　李智云在嘴上画了个x。
　　翟让失笑：“李将军战功赫赫，威名远扬，当然是将军。”
　　虽然李玄霸真的是当世名士，但因为李玄霸年少，所以翟让震惊之后，心头还算轻松，没有太过紧张拘束。
　　李玄霸问道：“翟公就不问我为何会结识魏玄成和知世郎？”
　　翟让一愣，再次猛地起身，坐墩再次倒地。
　　李智云又把手按在了短刀上。
　　魏徵再次把坐墩扶起来，没好气道：“你再踢倒一次，魏某绝对不帮你扶了！”
　　翟让面红耳赤，连连作揖：“抱歉，抱歉，我……”
　　对啊，唐国公府的李二郎李三郎是出了名的大隋忠臣，怎么会与贼帅结识？
　　李玄霸平和道：“翟公请坐吧。你知道知世郎传播的诗册吗？”
　　翟让猛地睁大眼睛：“难道……”
　　李玄霸平静道：“是我收集的民间士子的诗歌。”
　　翟让沉默了许久，对李玄霸深深作揖：“三郎君高义。”
　　李玄霸开玩笑道：“我只能透露这么多，希望翟公不会怪罪我没有知无不言。”
　　翟让忙道：“不会。三郎君能编纂出那本诗册，已经令翟某敬佩不已。三郎君可要回太原？翟某定派人护送。”
　　魏徵无语：“你派人护送，岂不是坐实了三郎君谋逆？”
　　翟让道：“我会派人伪装。”
　　李玄霸道：“我要回也是回张掖，不回太原。待我身体稍好些，能长途跋涉后，我自会离去，不会叨扰翟公。不过在我养病时，翟公可向我问策。”
　　魏徵道：“三郎君‘算无遗策’的名声如雷贯耳，翟公你有福了。”
　　刚坐下的翟让差点又站起来：“三郎君要为我献策？”
　　李玄霸微笑：“为何不可？”
　　翟让：“……我不明白。”
　　李玄霸道：“我当然自有目的。翟公可听过太子杨暕的名声？”
　　翟让面色崇敬道：“他是好太子。若大隋的皇帝是他，我何至于逃亡？”
　　李玄霸道：“二表兄不该如此沉默地死去。我想为他办一场盛大的葬礼。”
　　翟让品出点味道来。
　　他面色古怪。这位大隋忠臣李三郎，该不会是个潜在的反贼吧？
　　李玄霸道：“昔日陈胜吴广揭竿而起，打出了公子扶苏的名号。既然杨广说兵谏的二表兄谋逆，你们何不打出二表兄的旗号？二表兄死得冤枉，合该为他正名。”
　　翟让很想问，李三郎君你要借太子杨暕的名声做反隋的事，你二表兄知道吗？同意吗？
　　李玄霸看出了翟让的想法，他笑道：“二表兄如果不同意，他跳出来反对啊。既然他已经死了，还管得住我怎么做？”
　　翟让沉默半晌，对李玄霸拱手：“三郎君有话直说吧。”
　　李玄霸道：“我能推算出隋军班师回朝的路线，你能出兵与知世郎合作，像二征高丽时一样抢隋军一把吗？”
　　翟让道：“既然三郎君都敢对我献策了，我当然不会怯懦。”
　　李玄霸道：“我推算杨广会趁着高丽大捷北上，召集蛮夷来朝。而东突厥可汗已经叛出大隋，一定会派兵围攻杨广。你敢趁着杨广刚突围时，截杀如惊弓之鸟的杨广吗？”
　　魏徵道：“知世郎已经同意任由三郎君调遣。就算翟公不去做，我们也是要去做的。”
　　翟让深呼吸了几下，道：“我本就是贼，打的就是狗皇帝。但李三郎君，你为何要如此？是为了争夺天下吗？但以你二兄的本事和唐国公府的力量，应当不会把我们这种人放在眼里。”
　　李玄霸沉默了一会儿，失笑道：“你觉得换个皇帝，百姓就好过了吗？”
　　翟让直直地看着李玄霸。
　　李玄霸看向窗外：“自魏晋九品中正制后，寒门难以晋升，朝堂被世家勋贵把持。他们何尝把百姓放在眼里？我曾对知世郎道，圣人荀子曾言，百姓是水，君王是舟，水能载舟，亦能覆舟。但几百年后的人，却忘记了这件事。”
　　“是该让他们重新记起来了。”李玄霸淡淡道。
　　翟让不理解：“李郎将也是勋贵，这和李郎将有什么关系？”
　　李玄霸笑道：“荀子乃是公卿之后，也不算什么庶民，他不仍旧说出了这句话吗？”
　　翟让仍旧不敢置信。
　　一个高高在上的勋贵突然对你说他怜惜百姓，要帮助活不下去揭竿而起的民贼，这怎么让人相信？
　　就算他已经起兵，但内心自我称呼时仍旧是“贼帅”。连他自己都不认可自己，勋贵怎么会认可？
　　李玄霸道：“我知道你不信。这就是我要帮助你等的原因。你大概已经发现，寒门百姓就算起兵，也难以争夺天下，这天下最后仍旧是勋贵世家的天下。但如果你们能入朝做官，成为新的朝代的勋贵，那么出身草莽的你们，会不会对百姓多一点怜惜？至少你们比我等高高在上的勋贵世家，更明白百姓真正需要什么。将来的百姓，或许也会更相信与他们有同样出身的你等。”
　　他笑着摇摇头，转移话题道：“罢了，谈什么理想，实在是太空泛了。我给了知世郎一些书籍，你若感兴趣，可以借阅。现在我们说利益。”
　　李玄霸轻轻敲打了一下床沿：“理想看不见摸不着，利益却是实实在在的。杨广已经下令，捕获民贼后就地格杀。我想你也不会去赌昏君的好心。只要他活着，一定会派兵杀死你们。只有他死了，天下大乱了，你才安全。”
　　李玄霸微笑着看着翟让：“你们难以掌握杨广的踪迹，但我能。要不要听我一策，给这位高高在上的皇帝一个永生难忘的教训？错过了这次，你可没机会再威胁到他了。”
　　翟让眼神警惕。
　　魏徵不知道从哪摸出羽毛扇，一边扇一边微笑道：“难道翟公还担心三郎君对你设下陷阱？说难听些，以我家主公和三郎君的本事，需要算计你吗？他是纯粹的做好事不求回报啊。”
　　翟让：“……你主公是谁？唐国公？”
　　魏徵笑容消失，没好气道：“晦气。”
　　翟让：“……”
　　魏徵对李玄霸道：“三郎君，我看还是别指望翟公了，他的眼神不好，识人不清，将来难以成大事。”
　　李玄霸扶额：“玄成，你那张嘴啊……别太傲气了，你想还没结盟就得罪盟友吗？”
　　翟让沉声道：“三郎君为何会确定我会成为你的盟友？”
　　李玄霸轻轻摇头：“不是我的盟友，是知世郎的盟友。原因无他，你不杀杨广，杨广就要杀你啊。”
　　翟让再次仔细打量李玄霸。
　　少年神色平静柔和，声音沙哑，神情虚弱。
　　但怎么让他觉得毛骨悚然，后背发凉呢？
　　翟让摸了摸手臂上的鸡皮疙瘩，问道：“魏玄成的主公是谁？”
　　魏徵翻了个鄙夷的白眼。
　　李智云没好气道：“当然是我二兄。”
　　翟让惊诧：“李将军？那也太年少了！”
　　李玄霸失笑：“正因为我二哥如此年少，不才更显得天命所归吗？这不重要。翟公，给你一个机会追杀杨广，你敢不敢接？”
　　翟让犹豫了许久才道：“确实很像天命所归。没想到名满天下的李二郎君李三郎君，居然早早就有了这样远大的志向。唐国公难道也……”
　　魏徵扶额长叹：“你真的是眼瘸啊。”
　　翟让结结巴巴道：“直、直接投奔李二郎君？”
　　魏徵讥笑道：“你对比一下唐国公和李二郎君父子二人，如果他们不是父子，而是同龄人，你选谁？何况李二郎君年少！”
　　翟让犹豫道：“但唐国公是李二郎君的父亲啊，这怎么绕得开？”
　　魏徵道：“就算绕不开，预定了太子的位置不就行了？如果唐国公昏庸到不立我主公为太子，那就更不用着急了，主公可以提前继位。”
　　翟让叹气：“那就要担上不孝之名了。”
　　魏徵鄙视道：“成大事者，不拘小节。你见历代君王，谁在乎这点名声？司马家还指着洛水放屁呢！”
　　翟让皱眉道：“魏公，你这话太粗鄙了。再者怎么能用司马家作比？”
　　魏徵道：“说得也是。大汉高祖皇帝还让项羽分他一块父母的肉呢。”
　　翟让：“啊这……”
　　李智云慢慢睁大眼睛，不明白为何翟让会和魏徵争论起来。
　　李玄霸嘴角微抽。
　　我和你说刺杀皇帝，你百般犹豫纠结的，居然是魏徵主公的事？
　　李玄霸突然想起历史中，翟让曾经因为李密比自己厉害，又是世家子弟，就把瓦岗寨拱手相让。
　　他看向一脸纠结的翟让，眼神逐渐古怪。
　　不会吧不会吧，他只是让翟让去和知世郎合作刺杀个狗皇帝，翟让不会又想拱手让贤了吧？
　　你究竟是多不想当这个义军首领？瓦岗寨不差啊！
　　你就没有一点窦建德的心气，自己争霸天下当皇帝吗？？
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 140: Duke Zhai May Ask Me for a Strategy

By the time Li Xuanba received news of Yang Guang, early winter had already arrived.

In the original history, Yang Guang should have ended his expedition against Goguryeo around the Mid-Autumn Festival in the eighth month and marched his army back to court, making a rare return to Daxing.

Perhaps because the peasant uprisings in this lifetime were far more intense, or because Yang Xuangan had not been completely wiped out, Yang Guang's efficiency in conscripting soldiers and forced laborers was somewhat lower, causing the expedition against Goguryeo to draw to a close only in the ninth month.

Yet, just as in the original history, Yang Guang still issued the order to withdraw his troops the moment the King of Goguryeo begged for surrender.

This time, not only did Lai Hu'er attempt to press the attack against Goguryeo, but Duke of Song He Ruobi also attempted to defy Yang Guang's command.

Because Gao Jiong and Yuwen Bi had left the center of power, He Ruobi did not meet his fate as he had in the original history, where he was executed for his outspoken comments in the third year of Daye.

During Yang Guang's first expedition against Goguryeo, the Sui army had avoided a complete rout thanks to He Ruobi turning the tide. However, after Yang Guang was duped by the King of Goguryeo's feigned surrender and squandered the opportunity for victory, He Ruobi voiced his bitter complaints and was subsequently thrown into prison by Yang Guang.

Since it was not an unpardonable offense that crossed Yang Guang's bottom line, and because He Ruobi possessed formidable military merits, Yang Guang ultimately merely stripped him of his official rank rather than executing him. During the second and third expeditions against Goguryeo, Yang Guang even brought He Ruobi along once more.

Perhaps due to his stint in prison, He Ruobi finally remembered his father's dying admonition—piercing his tongue with an awl to warn him against reckless speech—and began to exercise prudence in his words and actions.

Thus, during the third expedition against Goguryeo, Yang Guang appointed He Ruobi as one of the main commanders of a separate route.

The aging He Ruobi proved himself as formidable as ever, coordinating seamlessly with Lai Hu'er, and was on the verge of capturing Pyongyang.

But then the King of Goguryeo surrendered yet again, and Yang Guang agreed yet again.

He Ruobi's explosive temper simply could not be contained; he ended up pointing right at Yang Guang's nose and cursing him out.

Had it been just that, it might have passed. However, upon learning of Crown Prince Yang Jian's armed remonstrance, He Ruobi voiced considerable support and sympathy for the Crown Prince in private, words that were eventually reported to Yang Guang.

Consequently, He Ruobi was imprisoned once more.

This time, he soon passed away in prison, reportedly having succumbed to illness brought on by sorrow and indignation.

Fortunately, He Ruobi was the only one condemned this time; his son was merely stripped of his official posts and peerage, avoiding the fate of being forced to commit suicide as he had in the original timeline.

When Wei Zheng recounted this matter to Li Xuanba, he could not stop sneering cold laughter.

Li Xuanba let out a heavy sigh. "Forcing the King of Goguryeo to surrender has perhaps become an obsession for Yang Guang."

Future generations could cite endless reasons justifying campaigns against Goguryeo, and Emperor Wen of Sui, Emperor Taizong of Tang, and Emperor Gaozong of Tang had all treated Goguryeo as a bitter adversary. But looking at Yang Guang's actions throughout history, his campaigns were purely out of pride. As long as the King of Goguryeo offered a surrender, his heart was content.

As for territory, populace, or border stability, Emperor Yang of Sui—who would withdraw his troops the moment the King of Goguryeo feigned submission—did not seem to care in the slightest.

This was true not only for the Yang Guang of this realm, but also for the Yang Guang of the original history.

Having been tricked by the Goguryeo trick of false surrenders repeatedly during his first campaign, he still fell for it during the third campaign, ordering Lai Hu'er—who was already practically at the gates of Pyongyang—to turn back his troops. The order infuriated Lai Hu'er, usually a most obedient trusted general, to the point of almost defying the imperial decree.

Having been reincarnated for over a decade, the "future" had already altered significantly due to his butterfly wings, rendering his "foreknowledge" no longer entirely accurate.

However, a clever transmigrator never relied on an "unchanging" future. Instead, they used historical events and individual behaviors from the original timeline to grasp the grand trends of history and the temperaments of key figures, combining these with intelligence gathered in reality to make "predictive" judgments.

For instance, with Yang Guang's unrepentant nature, deducing his actions was remarkably easy.

He was bound to repeat his past mistakes; the so-called butterfly effect merely fine-tuned the timing of his repeated blunders.

Wei Zheng asked, "Does the Emperor's current conduct align with Third Young Master's expectations?"

Li Xuanba replied, "More or less. This time, you can test him by pursuing the tail of the Sui army to raid their supply trains and horses. Ah, right—Yang Gongqing, the leader of the rebel army in Zhuo Commandery, knows the terrain inside out. Try cooperating with him."

In the original timeline, Yang Gongqing had indeed raided the returning Sui army, making off with over forty fine warhorses.

Wei Zheng hesitated. "If our move is too large this time, will it provoke the Emperor into deploying massive forces to crush us?"

Li Xuanba chuckled. "Yang Xuangan has already made his move. Given Yang Guang's nature, he despises peasant rebels; battle reports regarding peasant armies barely even register in his ears. The only one he truly dreads is Duke of Chu Yang Xuangan. Furthermore, He Ruobi is dead, and Yuwen Shu is incompetent at commanding troops, so the Sui army's formation will surely be in disarray during their retreat. It will be even messier than during the second campaign. If you could escape back then, you can certainly escape now."

Wei Zheng sighed. "Back then, the rebel marshals across the lands were bare-footed and feared nothing, willing to gamble their heads on a strap. Now, most of them have established their own strongholds, so it might be difficult to persuade them. Still, Master Zhishi will definitely agree. I shall try persuading Commander Zhai as well."

Li Xuanba said, "That is simple. I reckon Zhai Rang has already guessed that a sick person like me is no younger cousin of the Wei family. You may bring him to see me."

Wei Zheng asked in surprise, "Third Young Master is not worried Zhai Rang will inform on you?"

Li Xuanba burst out laughing. "Just as I said to Wang Bo back then, who would listen to his report? Or does he harbor dreams of surrendering to the Great Sui?"

Wei Zheng laughed along. "He certainly has no desire to surrender to the Great Sui. Since Third Young Master is so bold, I shall obey. However, please remember not to overexert your mind and strength; your health comes above all else."

Li Xuanba replied, "Rest assured. I am merely finding something to do to distract myself while recuperating. The medicinal concoction prepared by Physician Sun and Zhu-niang is truly appalling to drink."

Seeing Li Xuanba's miserable expression, Wei Zheng burst into boisterous laughter.

Li Zhiyun, who had been quietly "listening to the lesson," said sarcastically, "If Third Brother is so afraid of drinking medicine, then hurry up and recover. Stop dragging your feet."

Li Xuanba reached out and gave Li Zhiyun a smack on the back of his head as he sat by the bed, saying exasperatedly, "Is it because I *don't want* to recover?"

"Hmph," Li Zhiyun snorted coldly.

Li Xuanba put on a troubled look.

What to do? His little brother had truly entered his rebellious phase.

Watching the banter between the two brothers, Wei Zheng laughed once more.

Seeing how Third Young Master and Fifth Young Master interacted, he could roughly guess how his Master and Third Young Master got along.

It must be thoroughly entertaining.

Having spent several months with the men of Wagang Fort, Wei Zheng had gained a solid understanding of Zhai Rang's character. Thus, when Li Xuanba expressed his wish to meet Zhai Rang, Wei Zheng fully approved.

With Third Young Master's capability paired with his own glib tongue, perhaps they could win over yet another major faction for his Master.

Indeed, Zhai Rang had his suspicions.

However, he merely assumed that Wei Zheng was protecting a famous scholar or disgraced official persecuted by Yang Guang, so he thoughtfully refrained from exposing it.

Zhai Rang could not even be considered of humble scholarly stock; he was merely a minor petty clerk who barely knew how to read.

Due to what he had seen and heard while working in government offices, Zhai Rang held great reverence for prominent scholars and noble families.

Once he surmised that Wei Zheng was "harboring" a disgraced scholar of renown, he became even more attentive and respectful toward Li Xuanba and his group, harboring a deep wish in his heart that Wei Zheng would introduce him.

Even if Wei Zheng did not introduce him, Zhai Rang had no complaints. In his eyes, distinguished scholars were supposed to be proud and lofty, and it was entirely natural for them to look down on someone like him.

When Wei Zheng hinted, "Though men and women must maintain propriety, a life-saving debt must be repaid. My younger cousin wishes to wear a veiled hat to express her gratitude to Duke Zhai,"

Zhai Rang repeatedly protested that it wasn't necessary, yet was so excited he could not sleep a wink all night.

The next day, he boiled water and thoroughly scrubbed himself three times, spent half an hour selecting his attire and headwear, and even quietly dusted a bit of powder onto his sun-darkened face.

Shan Xiongxin, a close friend and fellow townsman who was among the first to join him, teased Zhai Rang: "You haven't fallen for Duke Wei's younger cousin, have you?"

Zhai Rang's expression changed drastically, and he hastily reprimanded, "Do not speak nonsense!"

Shan Xiongxin rubbed his nose. "Alright, alright, no nonsense. The reputation of a noble lady is paramount—sigh, I've heard you nag about this so much my ears are calloused. Maogong, don't you agree?"

Xu Shiji said speechlessly, "Brother Shan, did you really fail to guess, or are you deliberately joking?"

Shan Xiongxin asked in confusion, "What do you mean deliberate or not?"

Zhai Rang and Xu Shiji exchanged a look, their eyes brimming with helplessness.

Shan Xiongxin grumbled in dissatisfaction, "What charades are you two playing? Hey, hey, hey, you're not keeping secrets from me, are you?"

Looking at the crystal-clear foolishness in Shan Xiongxin's eyes, Zhai Rang let out a deep sigh. "I will tell you after I visit Duke Wei's 'younger cousin.'"

Shan Xiongxin was completely bewildered. Just as he was about to press further, Xu Shiji pulled him back.

Xu Shiji said, "Duke Zhai has his own reasons for doing this. Since you can't figure it out, don't cause trouble."

Shan Xiongxin muttered displeasurably, "Fine, you two are the clever ones and leave me out. Fine, I won't ask."

Once Zhai Rang departed, Shan Xiongxin threw his arm around Xu Shiji's shoulder, winking continuously. "Duke Zhai is gone. Quick, tell me quietly. My lips are sealed—you know that! I can definitely keep a secret."

Xu Shiji replied tartly, "Since Duke Zhai said he would tell you personally, I won't say a word."

Shan Xiongxin pinned Xu Shiji down. "Really won't say? I'll mess you up if you don't!"

Xu Shiji rolled his eyes. "Sure, let's head to the martial grounds and see who teaches whom a lesson."

Shan Xiongxin dragged Xu Shiji toward the door. "Fine, arrogant, aren't you!"

The moment he stepped outside, he saw Zhai Rang standing at the door frowning at him, causing him to shrink his neck back instantly. "Duke Zhai, you haven't left yet?"

Zhai Rang let out another deep sigh. "With a temperament like yours, how could I comfortably trust you with a secret? Don't pick on Maogong. Wait for me to return."

Shan Xiongxin said meekly, "Yes, sir."

Xu Shiji grinned and mouthed at Shan Xiongxin: *Serves you right.*

Zhai Rang added, "Maogong, you aren't allowed to provoke him either."

Xu Shiji replied, "Oh."

Zhai Rang offered a few more instructions before finally taking his leave.

Before he had walked many steps, he heard Shan Xiongxin behind him engaging in what he thought was a low-voiced "conspiracy."

"Tell me!"

"No!"

"Whisper it to me."

"No."

Zhai Rang quickened his pace.

Truly exhausting for his spirit.

Upon meeting Wei Zheng, Zhai Rang could not help but complain about his two brothers, as well as the rest of his brothers who possessed all sorts of colorful personalities.

Leading people was truly hard work.

Wei Zheng laughed helplessly. "Duke Zhai has a gathering of talents under his command like clouds in the sky. This is truly a blissful trouble."

Zhai Rang smiled bitterly. "I am merely worried I won't be able to lead them proper... Ah, enough, let us not speak discouraging words."

When he and Wei Zheng arrived at Li Xuanba's doorway, he straightened his lapels and took several deep breaths.

Wei Zheng was stuck between laughter and tears. "Duke Zhai, there is no need to be so nervous. I know you suspect the person in the room might be a world-renowned scholar, but truly, that is not the case—it is merely a young scholar whose identity cannot be publicly revealed."

Hearing this, a flash of disappointment swept through Zhai Rang's heart.

Nevertheless, he smiled and said, "Given my humble origin, I would get nervous even meeting an ordinary scholar."

Wei Zheng thought to himself: *Well, he isn't exactly an ordinary scholar either.*

Learning that it was no grand scholar of the realm, Zhai Rang hesitated no longer. Restoring a confident smile to his face, he pushed open the door and stepped inside.

Inside the room, Li Zhiyun was peeling an orange for his older brother.

The oranges, naturally, had been sent by Zhai Rang earlier to curry favor with the "renowned scholar."

When Zhai Rang saw Li Zhiyun still dressed in women's attire, his steps faltered.

He turned to Wei Zheng. "Not wearing the veiled hat?"

Li Zhiyun put down the orange, stood up, and bowed. "I am not a woman either. My thanks to Duke Zhai for taking us in."

Zhai Rang was startled, stammering, "Y-You are not a woman? Your voice earlier..."

Li Zhiyun switched to a female voice: "It was fake, a voice trick."

Zhai Rang's expression became quite sightly. "Could Zhu-niang also be..."

Li Zhiyun's expression turned vigilant. "Zhu-niang is my Third Sister-in-law!"

"Cough, Xiao Wu! Stop messing around," Li Xuanba sighed. "Duke Zhai, I am unwell and can only speak while lying on this daybed. Forgive my lack of manners."

Only then did Zhai Rang shift his gaze toward Li Xuanba lying on the sickbed.

The young man on the bed appeared quite young. His cheeks were sunken and his face was pale with illness, his hair disheveled like dry grass, yet his eyes were remarkably bright and sharp, as if able to pierce right through him, making Zhai Rang feel a twinge of unease.

Li Zhiyun cupped his hands. "Duke Zhai, forgive my rudeness. But Zhu-niang truly is my Third Sister-in-law!"

Li Xuanba couldn't resist reaching out to pinch Li Zhiyun's cheek. "You don't need to keep emphasizing that!"

Li Zhiyun grunted softly. "Third Brother, you have no idea how many people in Wagang Fort admire Third Sister-in-law. Now that we are revealing our identities, of course I must emphasize it!"

Embarrassment filled Zhai Rang's heart as he hurriedly said, "It is due to my lax discipline over my subordinates. Please... forgive me, Young Master."

Li Xuanba released Li Zhiyun's cheek and said, "It is because I have failed to discipline my younger brother strictly, making a fool of myself before Duke Zhai. Sit down properly, keep quiet, and stop causing trouble!"

Li Zhiyun replied dutifully, "Oh."

Having restrained his chatterbox brother, Li Xuanba said apologetically, "Duke Zhai, please have a seat."

Wei Zheng guided Zhai Rang to sit down on a stool beside Li Xuanba's daybed.

Zhai Rang looked at Wei Zheng, asking with his eyes why he hadn't introduced his companion yet.

Wei Zheng smiled. "It is better to let Third Young Master speak for himself."

Lying on the bed, Li Xuanba cupped his hands. "I am Li Xuanba, Tiger-Tooth General of the Great Sui, courtesy name Dade. Duke Zhai may not have heard of me..."

Zhai Rang abruptly stood up, sending his stool tumbling to the floor.

Li Zhiyun nervously rested his hand on the short dagger at his waist.

Li Xuanba smiled. "It seems Duke Zhai *has* heard of me."

Zhai Rang took a deep breath. Instead of answering, he looked at Wei Zheng. "Duke Wei, why did you go to the trouble of deceiving me?"

Wei Zheng asked in confusion, "What did I deceive you about?"

Zhai Rang gritted his teeth. "You said he wasn't a world-renowned scholar!"

Wei Zheng gasped in surprise, "So Third Young Master is already considered a world-renowned scholar of our era?"

Li Zhiyun let out a breath of relief and giggled, "We dare not claim such honor, dare not claim it."

Li Xuanba shot his brother a side-eye. *I haven't even demurred yet, and you're already being modest on my behalf.*

Wei Zheng helped right the stool for Zhai Rang and pulled him down to sit once more. "Now do you see why Third Young Master had to conceal his identity? Third Young Master trusts you; do not betray his trust."

Zhai Rang's facial muscles twitched continuously. "Th-This... General Li should be deeply trusted by the dog... by the Emperor. How could he have fallen into such a state?"

Li Xuanba said, "Family misfortune. Duke Zhai should have seen the recent public notices."

Zhai Rang's mind hadn't connected the dots earlier, but with Li Xuanba's reminder, it clicked immediately. "Li Yuanji falsely accused General Li of rebellion?"

Li Xuanba said, "His false accusation was actually of little consequence. It was just that while Vice Prefect Ding placed me under house arrest, someone—who knows who—tried to set a fire to hunt me down, causing me to fall into the river. I was already frail and sickly, and this time I truly suffered terribly."

Zhai Rang sighed, "A family misfortune indeed. General Li is a loyal minister of the Great Sui, yet has ended up at Wagang Fort... Sigh. But General Li, rest assured: you possess a renown for benevolence and fought off the barbarians in Heyou alongside General Li. Though I, Zhai Rang, have rebelled against the Great Sui, I will not make things difficult for General Li."

Li Zhiyun chimed in, "What? Second Brother has actually become a general?!"

Li Xuanba sighed. "Xiao Wu, can you please shut your mouth and let me finish my conversation with Duke Zhai before you speak?"

Li Zhiyun mimed zipping his lips with an 'X'.

Zhai Rang chuckled, "General Li has achieved illustrious military merits and his famous name echoes far and wide; of course he is a general."

Although Li Xuanba was indeed a world-renowned scholar of his generation, his youth made Zhai Rang feel relatively relaxed after the initial shock, without being overly nervous or restrained.

Li Xuanba asked, "Does Duke Zhai not wonder why I am acquainted with Wei Xuancheng and Master Zhishi?"

Zhai Rang froze, then abruptly leaped to his feet once more, knocking the stool over again.

Li Zhiyun rested his hand on his short dagger once more.

Wei Zheng set the stool upright again, saying testily, "If you kick it over one more time, I am absolutely not lifting it for you again!"

Zhai Rang turned beet red and bowed repeatedly in apology. "Forgive me, forgive me, I..."

*That's right—Second Master Li and Third Master Li of the Duke of Tang's residence are famously loyal ministers of the Great Sui! How could he be acquainted with rebel chieftains?*

Li Xuanba said calmly, "Duke Zhai, please sit. Are you aware of the poetry collection circulated by Master Zhishi?"

Zhai Rang's eyes widened dramatically. "Could it be..."

Li Xuanba replied serenely, "It was a collection of poems compiled by me from scholars among the common folk."

Zhai Rang fell silent for a long moment before offering a deep, formal bow to Li Xuanba. "Third Young Master possesses lofty righteousness."

Li Xuanba joked, "I can only disclose this much. I hope Duke Zhai will not blame me for not laying everything bare."

Zhai Rang hastily replied, "Not at all! That Third Young Master could compile such a poetry collection fills me with profound admiration. Does Third Young Master wish to return to Taiyuan? I shall certainly send men to escort you."

Wei Zheng was rendered speechless. "If you send men to escort him, wouldn't that solidify the accusation that Third Young Master committed treason?"

Zhai Rang said, "I will have my men disguise themselves."

Li Xuanba said, "If I return anywhere, it will be to Zhangye, not Taiyuan. Once my body recovers somewhat and can endure long travel, I will depart on my own and burden Duke Zhai no longer. However, while I am recuperating here, Duke Zhai may ask me for strategies."

Wei Zheng added, "Third Young Master's reputation for 'never making a miscalculation' is thunderous to the ear. Duke Zhai, you are fortunate indeed."

Zhai Rang, who had just sat down, nearly leaped up again. "Third Young Master wishes to offer *me* strategies?"

Li Xuanba smiled faintly. "Why not?"

Zhai Rang stammered, "...I do not understand."

Li Xuanba said, "Naturally, I have my own motives. Has Duke Zhai heard of Crown Prince Yang Jian's reputation?"

Zhai Rang's face turned reverent. "He was a fine Crown Prince. If the Emperor of the Great Sui had been him, why would I have ever been forced to flee into outlawry?"

Li Xuanba said, "Second Cousin should not have died in such silent obscurity. I wish to give him a grand funeral."

Zhai Rang caught a subtle flavor in those words.

His expression turned peculiar. *Could this loyal minister of the Sui, Third Young Master Li, actually be a closet rebel?*

Li Xuanba continued, "In days of old, Chen Sheng and Wu Guang raised their banners of rebellion under the name of Young Master Fusu. Since Yang Guang claimed that Second Cousin committed treason through his armed remonstrance, why don't you raise Second Cousin's banner? Second Cousin died unjustly, and his name deserves to be vindicated."

Zhai Rang desperately wanted to ask: *Third Young Master Li, does your Second Cousin know you are borrowing Crown Prince Yang Jian's name to rebel against the Sui? Would he even agree?*

Seeing right through Zhai Rang's thoughts, Li Xuanba chuckled, "If Second Cousin disagrees, he can jump out of his grave and object. Since he is already dead, how can he stop what I do?"

Zhai Rang fell silent for a long while before cupping his hands to Li Xuanba. "Third Young Master, please speak plainly."

Li Xuanba said, "I can deduce the route the Sui army will take on their retreat back to court. Are you able to deploy troops and cooperate with Master Zhishi to raid the Sui army, just like during the second campaign against Goguryeo?"

Zhai Rang replied, "Since Third Young Master is bold enough to offer me strategies, I certainly will not show cowardice."

Li Xuanba said, "I deduce that Yang Guang will take advantage of his supposed grand victory over Goguryeo to head north, summoning the foreign tribes to pay homage. However, the Khagan of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate has already rebelled against the Sui and will surely dispatch forces to besiege Yang Guang. Do you dare to intercept and slay Yang Guang when he has just broken through the siege, trembling like a bird startled by the mere twang of a bowstring?"

Wei Zheng said, "Master Zhishi has already agreed to place himself at Third Young Master's disposal. Even if Duke Zhai does not participate, we intend to carry this out regardless."

Zhai Rang took several deep breaths before speaking, "I am an outlaw to begin with, and fighting that dog Emperor is precisely what I do. But Third Young Master Li, why are you doing this? Is it to compete for supreme rule over the realm? Yet with your Second Brother's talent and the strength of the Duke of Tang's household, you surely wouldn't place people like us in your eyes."

Li Xuanba remained silent for a short while, then laughed softly. "Do you think that changing the Emperor will make life any better for the common folk?"

Zhai Rang stared straight at Li Xuanba.

Li Xuanba looked out the window. "Ever since the Nine-Rank Controller System of the Wei and Jin dynasties, those of humble origins have found it nearly impossible to rise, and the imperial court has been monopolized by noble clans and aristocratic families. When have they ever cared for the common people? I once told Master Zhishi that the Sage Xunzi said: 'The people are water, and the ruler is a boat; water can carry the boat, but it can also capsize it.' Yet those born centuries later have forgotten this truth."

"It is time they were made to remember it once again," Li Xuanba said placidly.

Zhai Rang could not comprehend. "General Li is also part of the aristocracy. What does this have to do with General Li?"

Li Xuanba smiled, "Xunzi was a descendant of high officials himself and hardly a commoner, yet did he not utter those words all the same?"

Zhai Rang still found it hard to believe.

How could anyone readily believe a high-and-mighty aristocrat who suddenly claimed to pity the common folk and wished to aid outlaw rebels who were forced to rise up just to survive?

Even though he had already raised troops, in his heart he still referred to himself as a 'rebel chief.' When he didn't even respect his own status, how could an aristocrat respect it?

Li Xuanba said, "I know you don't believe me. That is precisely why I want to help you. You have likely noticed that even if commoners of humble origin take up arms, it is nearly impossible for them to win the realm; in the end, the land still falls into the hands of the aristocratic families. But if you can enter the imperial court as officials and become the nobility of a new dynasty, wouldn't you—having risen from the rough weeds—feel a bit more compassion for the common people? At the very least, you understand what the people truly need far better than high-and-mighty aristocrats like us. And the people of the future might trust those who share their origins far more."

He smiled and shook his head, shifting the topic. "Ah, enough talking about ideals—it is far too abstract. I gave Master Zhishi some books; if you are interested, you may borrow them to read. Now, let us talk about tangible interests."

Li Xuanba lightly tapped the edge of the bed. "Ideals are intangible, but benefits are real and concrete. Yang Guang has already issued an imperial decree ordering that captured rebels be executed on the spot. I doubt you are willing to gamble on a foolish tyrant's mercy. As long as he lives, he will inevitably send troops to slay you. Only if he dies and the realm falls into turmoil will you be truly safe."

Li Xuanba smiled as he looked at Zhai Rang. "It is difficult for you to track Yang Guang's movements, but I can. Do you wish to hear my strategy and teach this high-and-mighty Emperor an unforgettable lesson? If you miss this chance, you will never get another opportunity to threaten him."

Zhai Rang's eyes flickered with vigilance.

Wei Zheng produced a feather fan from nowhere and gently fanned himself with a smile. "Could Duke Zhai still be worried that Third Young Master is laying a trap for you? To put it bluntly, with the capabilities of my Master and Third Young Master, would they need to scheme against you? He is purely doing a good deed without asking for anything in return."

Zhai Rang muttered, "...Who is your Master? The Duke of Tang?"

The smile vanished from Wei Zheng's face, and he said moodily, "How unlucky."

Zhai Rang: "..."

Wei Zheng said to Li Xuanba, "Third Young Master, I think we shouldn't rely on Duke Zhai. His vision is terrible and he cannot evaluate people properly; he will hardly achieve great things in the future."

Li Xuanba pressed his hand to his forehead. "Xuancheng, that tongue of yours... Don't be too arrogant. Do you want to offend an ally before we've even formed an alliance?"

Zhai Rang said solemnly, "Why is Third Young Master so certain that I will become your ally?"

Li Xuanba shook his head gently. "Not my ally, but Master Zhishi's ally. The reason is simple: if you do not kill Yang Guang, Yang Guang will kill you."

Zhai Rang sized up Li Xuanba carefully once more.

The youth had a calm and gentle expression, his voice raspy, his demeanor feeble.

Yet why did he feel a creeping chill down his spine that made his hair stand on end?

Zhai Rang rubbed the goosebumps on his arm and asked, "Who is Wei Xuancheng's Master?"

Wei Zheng rolled his eyes in contempt.

Li Zhiyun said testily, "My Second Brother, of course."

Zhai Rang gasped in astonishment. "General Li? But he is far too young!"

Li Xuanba burst out laughing. "Precisely because my Second Brother is so young, doesn't it prove all the more that Heaven's Mandate rests upon him? But that is beside the point. Duke Zhai, if I give you an opportunity to hunt down Yang Guang, do you dare to take it?"

Zhai Rang hesitated for a long while before saying, "It truly does sound like Heaven's Mandate. I never expected that Second Master Li and Third Master Li, whose names resound throughout the realm, had already harbored such grand ambitions at so young an age. Could the Duke of Tang also..."

Wei Zheng pressed his forehead and sighed deeply. "You truly are blind as a bat."

Zhai Rang stammered, "Sh-Should we pledge allegiance directly to Second Master Li?"

Wei Zheng sneered mockingly, "Compare the Duke of Tang and Second Master Li, father and son. If they were not father and son, but peers of the same age, whom would you choose? Not to mention Second Master Li has youth on his side!"

Zhai Rang hesitated, "But the Duke of Tang is Second Master Li's father. How can you bypass him?"

Wei Zheng said, "Even if he cannot be bypassed, isn't it enough to reserve the position of Crown Prince? If the Duke of Tang is fatuous enough not to establish my Master as Crown Prince, then there's even less cause for worry—my Master can simply ascend the throne ahead of time."

Zhai Rang sighed, "Then he would bear the stigma of unfilial behavior."

Wei Zheng scoffed with utter disdain, "Those who achieve great things do not bog themselves down in trivialities. Look at the monarchs throughout history—who among them cared about such reputation? The Sima clan even swore a fart of an oath by the Luo River!"

Zhai Rang frowned. "Duke Wei, your words are far too vulgar. Besides, how could you compare them to the Sima clan?"

Wei Zheng acknowledged, "Fair point. Even Emperor Gaozu of Han asked Xiang Yu to share a bowl of his parents' flesh with him."

Zhai Rang: "Ah, well..."

Li Zhiyun's eyes slowly widened, bewildered as to why Zhai Rang and Wei Zheng had started arguing over this.

The corner of Li Xuanba's mouth twitched slightly.

*I am discussing assassinating the Emperor with you, yet after all your hesitations and deliberations, what you end up fretting over is who Wei Zheng's Master is?*

Li Xuanba suddenly remembered from history that Zhai Rang had once handed over Wagang Fort on a silver platter simply because Li Mi was more capable than him and hailed from a noble family.

He looked at the conflicted Zhai Rang, his gaze growing increasingly peculiar.

*No way, right? He merely asked Zhai Rang to cooperate with Master Zhishi to assassinate the dog Emperor, and Zhai Rang is already thinking about stepping down to yield leadership?*

*Just how much do you hate being a rebel leader? Wagang Fort isn't half bad, you know!*

*Don't you have even a shred of Dou Jiande's ambition to compete for supremacy and become Emperor yourself?!*

chunks.chapterTitle: 第141章 翟公我计谋如何
chunks.chineseText:
第141章 翟公我计谋如何

翟让和魏徵话题发散时， 李智云不悦道：“我兄长正在献策，翟公可否给兄长一点尊重，不要顾左右言他？兄长养病，精力不济， 如果翟公不愿意听策， 可与魏公私下聊天，让我兄长先休息。”
　　李玄霸斥责：“李智云！”
　　李智云倨傲地拱手， 敷衍地道歉。
　　李玄霸叹气：“翟公请恕罪， 是我疏忽管教。”
　　翟让忙道：“不不不， 是翟某无礼在先。”
　　他向李玄霸拱手作揖：“翟某只是听闻魏公真正的主公，太过惊讶。”
　　李玄霸微笑道：“我二哥年少，翟公惊讶情有可原。但也正如魏公所说，若一个三四十岁正值壮年的将领有我二哥如今功绩，投奔者一定会踏破我二哥的门槛。而我二哥提前十几年完成这样的功绩， 当比那些三四十岁的人更厉害， 为何还被人轻视了？翟公， 我所言可有道理？”
　　翟让讪讪道：“确实有道理。”
　　魏徵摇着扇子笑道：“主公被轻视， 三郎君可曾不被轻视？若三郎君再长个十来岁， 无论去哪里都会被人倒屣相迎，抵足同眠。现在……”
　　魏徵摇摇头，笑着叹气。
　　翟让面色更红。
　　显然他已经听出来魏徵是在阴阳怪气他。
　　李玄霸正在与他聊天时， 他与魏徵就旁的话题聊了起来。如果李玄霸是一位更年长的士人，他绝对不会这么做。
　　说来还是他因为李玄霸过于年少而无意间生出了轻视之心，没有把李玄霸这位“名士”和“谋士”太当回事。
　　翟让再次道歉。
　　李玄霸微笑：“无事，我已经习惯了。小五， 把地图带来。”
　　他本来想多试探一下翟让的性格， 看翟让能担多少事。
　　知世郎王薄目前的成果大大超出了他的预期， 将来山东诸郡百姓肯定会给他建庙。未来王薄成就未必比窦建德差。
　　若说到隋末农民起义军，瓦岗寨无论是在历史还是演义中都赫赫有名。李玄霸对翟让自然也有过高期待。
　　但现在看来，他失去了期待。
　　不是翟让不好，只是翟让并没有承担大事的意志。
　　他的性格就像是《水浒传》里的宋江一样，你不能说他不是一个合格的首领，但他自己其实并不想当一个“贼帅”，而是对官宦勋贵世家十分羡慕，并且对照顾麾下性格各异的“兄弟们”，颇有点疲惫了。
　　当然，李玄霸也看出，翟让现在还没有生出“让贤”之心。如果现在谁让他让贤，他肯定也会拒绝。
　　翟让只是潜意识地显露出疲态。他自己或许都没有意识到这一点。
　　得知翟让的心态后，李玄霸就没必要给他施压了。
　　既然自己比李密先接触到瓦岗寨，这支队伍他就笑纳了，不必多事。
　　现在李玄霸要做的，就是让翟让佩服他。
　　当翟让认为自己远远比不过李玄霸的时候，李玄霸就能掌握瓦岗寨了。
　　李玄霸又想念起来二哥。这种事本来应该二哥来做。
　　若是以前，李玄霸只需要甄选出需要收复的势力，然后创造一个他们和二哥相处的机会，其他就看二哥发挥“大唐魅魔”本事就成了。完全不需要过多算计。
　　李智云把地图拿出来，铺到李玄霸盖着被子的腿上。
　　翟让当然识得舆图，但他完全看不懂李玄霸所描绘的等高线地图。
　　李玄霸先教翟让看等高线地图，翟让眼神从迷茫到了然，最后转化成了佩服。
　　翟让感叹道：“真是一目了然。李三郎果然是大才！”
　　李玄霸微笑着不回答翟让的夸赞，开始说起杨广班师回朝可能的行军路线，和途中会经过哪些义军首领的根据地，瓦岗寨又能从哪里入手截获隋军装备，并不暴露自身所属，顺利逃走。
　　这次杨广“大胜”，就算他不喜欢回大兴，也得回大兴祭祖献俘，才算完成一场“大胜”的完整流程。
　　从涿郡到大兴这一路上，几乎每个郡都有义军。他们虽然看到隋朝大军不一定敢出手，但如果瓦岗寨等强大的义军出手后，他们一定会来捡便宜。
　　“杨广是个好大喜功的帝王。他的好大喜功不是开疆扩土等实际的利益，只是‘脸面’。杨广最厌恶的就是别人说他是错误的。所以高丽王戏耍他多次，他却每次都上同样的当，高丽王一投降，他就退军，好像一个蠢货一样。”
　　“他当然不是蠢，而是他最初吃了高丽王的亏，他就要在同样的地方赢回来。只有完成‘高丽王投降、自己撤兵、高丽王仍旧称臣’这件事，印证了他最初的判断是正确而不是糊涂，他才算真正完成了征讨高丽的成就。”
　　李玄霸笑了一声，道：“就像是玩游戏一样。”
　　翟让和魏徵琢磨着“游戏”二字，若有所思。
　　不过他们再怎么若有所思，都想不到李玄霸真正的比喻。
　　李玄霸所说的游戏，是指后世有各种成就奖杯的电子游戏。
　　杨广就像是后世刷成就的游戏玩家一样，盯准了一个条件苛刻的成就使劲重开，一次不行两次，两次不行十次。
　　只是后世玩家能重开游戏上百上千次，大隋却不是虚拟的国度，人死不能复生，粮食和军资也不能凭空变出来。
　　杨广这样的性格倒也说不上多罕见，世上有许多固执的人都这样，不能接受自己的错误，特别是三观已经固定的中年人，一次一次地撞南墙，试图侥幸成功一次，好对外吹嘘自己果然没错，是别人眼瘸。
　　只是普通人有这样的性格，只祸害自己的身边人。杨广是皇帝，杀伤力就太大了。
　　“如杨广相信高丽王一定会真心投降，并要用大隋人的命不断打出这个结果一样，他不相信天下民乱真的不可遏止，所以他不会相信有民贼胆敢袭击大隋军队。他身边敢于直谏的人要么被杀，要么被逐，群臣也不敢告诉他这件事。”
　　历史中的义军首领杨公卿带了几千人抢劫走隋军四十多匹好马，狠狠抽了隋军一耳光，也没有被大隋派大军剿灭，就是没人敢告诉杨广这件事。
　　若把民贼胆敢抢御驾亲征的隋军的马的事上报，杨公卿能不能被抓住另说，但上报的人肯定会被恼羞成怒的杨广杀掉。然后杨广身边的近臣就劝慰杨广，“陛下，别相信他们，没有的事，一定是他们管理不力贪污，把马丢卖了”，帝信了，帝大悦，又处死了一批胆敢欺骗他的人。
　　李玄霸细细剖析杨广的性格，翟让和魏徵眼中怒火越来越盛。
　　翟让握紧拳头道：“狗皇帝，真该死！”
　　魏徵把羽扇摇晃得哗啦啦响：“大隋二世而亡，不冤。”
　　李智云递来温水，李玄霸润了嗓子和嘴唇后，温和地问道：“现在翟公可否想出兵抢夺隋军辎重了？”
　　翟让恭敬道：“李郎君所言，让翟某心中困惑一扫而空。翟某当立刻召集下属商议，遣人去与知世郎联合行事！”
　　现在他是半点不敢对李玄霸不敬了。
　　现在翟让麾下唯一能出谋划策的人只有出身豪族，刚及弱冠的徐世勣。但徐世勣作战勇猛，在“谋士”这一方面还较为平庸。翟让早就羡慕王薄有魏徵这样真正的谋主。
　　现在见识到李玄霸的本事，翟让再不敢因李玄霸年少而生出轻视之心。
　　魏徵道：“若三郎君身体稍好一些，可以乘船了，我也该和三郎君一同回齐郡了。”
　　翟让忙道：“虽然坐船不如坐车骑马颠簸，但李君身体需要静养，可以再留几月。”
　　魏徵瞥了翟让一眼：“你现在希望向三郎君问策了？”
　　翟让严肃道：“我一直都很敬仰李郎君！”
　　李玄霸打断魏徵又想阴阳怪气的话，道：“我现在吹不得寒风，玄成可先行一步。若此战能成，翟公肯定会愿意与知世郎有下一步合作。到时我就乘坐翟公的船只来齐郡。”
　　魏徵没好气道：“三郎君不走，我岂敢走？我若独自回齐郡，知世郎就要亲自过来了。”
　　李玄霸道：“知世郎那里缺不得你。我为你修书一封。”
　　魏徵漠然道：“我不走。”
　　李玄霸叹气：“玄成，大事为重！”
　　魏徵呼哧呼哧地扇着扇子，冷笑道：“有比你的身体更重要的大事？”
　　李智云插嘴：“就是！我也希望魏公能留下。当三兄不爱惜身体的时候，好好骂他一顿。我说的话，三兄根本不听。”
　　李玄霸伸手给了李智云一下，对魏徵皱眉道：“这是命令，请听令。”
　　魏徵一愣，气得把羽毛扇子丢在了地上：“李三郎！”
　　李智云乖乖把羽毛扇子捡起来递给魏徵，叹气道：“三兄是不是很讨厌？我懂，我太懂了。”
　　李玄霸：“……”
　　魏徵冷哼：“遵命。”
　　翟让见魏徵居然如此听话，大吃一惊。
　　就是王薄的命令，魏徵不想听的时候都捂耳朵，王薄对他无可奈何。
　　翟让没觉得这有哪里不对。谋主嘛，心高气傲被哄着捧着才正常，自己若有谋主，定做得比王薄还好。
　　现在他才发现，原来魏徵的倨傲只是因为主公另有他人，原来魏徵也有被强迫听命令的时候。
　　这件事知世郎知道吗？还是说知世郎也是……
　　翟让心头一动，不过他自己都不知道他为什么心头一动，便将这激动藏了起来。
　　李玄霸下令后，又宽慰道：“翟公的品德，玄成难道不信任吗？不说翟公，就是徐世勣、单雄信等人，也都是心怀豪义之人，他们都会护我周全。”
　　翟让惊讶道：“李郎君还知道徐世勣和单雄信？”
　　李玄霸笑道：“我已经在瓦岗寨养病许久，怎么会不知道？”
　　翟让道：“他们二人若是知道李郎君如此夸赞他们，一定会很高兴。”
　　李玄霸却摇头笑道：“徐世勣可能会有一点高兴，但单雄信……翟公，你确定他不会挠挠头，问你‘李玄霸是谁’吗？”
　　翟让苦笑：“或许真的会这样。”
　　魏徵又开始扇扇子：“哼。”
　　李玄霸继续劝慰道：“玄成，别生气了，明年正月我就来。”
　　魏徵没好气道：“等见到主公，我一定会将此事细细告知主公。”
　　李玄霸：“……行。”等见到你的主公，我就解脱了。
　　他相信魏徵一定会追着那位过分跳脱的主公天天进谏，把二哥撵得鸡飞狗跳。
　　见李玄霸虽然强硬下令，但又好声好气地哄魏徵，翟让又没来由地心头悸动了一下。
　　他虽然羡慕知世郎王薄有魏徵这样的寒门士子当谋主，自己连寒门士子的门都进不去。
　　但他也知道，魏徵这样的寒门士子，在李玄霸这样的顶级勋贵面前也应该是没有丝毫地位。魏徵和李玄霸的身份，就像是他还是小吏时与官宦的地位一样天渊之别。何况李玄霸还是魏徵主公的双生弟弟，是魏徵主公的谋主，算是魏徵半个主公了。
　　李玄霸对魏徵这样平易近人，真是礼贤下士啊。
　　从李玄霸身上，翟让就能窥见那位年少主公一二风采。
　　垂髫之年就擒获吐谷浑可汗的少年英雄，怪不得让魏徵如此心折，心折到自己问他主公是不是唐国公都直喊“晦气”。
　　魏徵终于脸色好转，李玄霸松了口气，对走神的翟让道：“下一步追杀杨广的计划，就等这次行动圆满成功后，我再告知翟公。若这次没有太大危险的行动成功，我想翟公应当会听一听我下一步献策了。”
　　翟让拱手：“翟某愿意洗耳恭听，请李郎君继续说。”
　　魏徵也道：“三郎君稍等，我先找来笔墨记录，好带给知世郎。”
　　李智云非常体贴地把纸笔拿过来：“我就知道你会需要，已经准备好了。翟公要吗？”
　　翟让有点尴尬道：“我、我就……”
　　李智云道：“我帮翟公记录一份可好？”
　　翟让忙道：“谢过李小郎君。”
　　李智云在腿上铺开纸：“不谢。该是我谢翟公收留。”
　　李玄霸待他们准备好后，继续说起下一步计划。
　　下一步计划，就是历史中的“雁门之围”。
　　如之前所说，以杨广的性格，他一定会重蹈覆辙。杨广去雁门，就是如大隋还兴盛时一样，想要让万夷来朝。
　　他不蠢，知道东突厥已经离心，便想如以前那样亲自去边疆震慑东突厥，让东突厥可汗乖乖来赔罪。
　　但他完全没想到，或者是不愿意去想，现在的大隋已经日落西山，而东突厥正蒸蒸日上。
　　东突厥可汗确实来了，却是带着十万大军来的。
　　后世演员把隋炀帝演成了一个非常有魅力的神经质暴君，就算乱世来临也丝毫不乱，只是癫狂地等待穷途末路。
　　历史中的杨广其实胆子没有影视剧中的杨广那么有魅力。
　　他在雁门郡之围中，每日都抱着自己儿子孙子嗷嗷大哭，半点帝王威严都没有。
　　他在大隋末年下江南，也是终于意识到天下大乱，然后鸵鸟思维不肯回西京坐镇平乱，反而在江都大兴土木，准备迁都江都，与中原乱世“划江而治”。
　　杨广的心态太容易崩了。
　　雁门之围后，杨广就成了惊弓之鸟，成为他将来逃到江南当鸵鸟的最后一根稻草。
　　那时杨广都凑不出来解围的兵，只能承诺厚赏，让天下人来救他。
　　最后因为这件事太丢脸，杨广被救之后就不想大张旗鼓奖励救他的人，所以这厚赏就被吞了。
　　大隋最后一丝政治信用破产。
　　哦，对了，其中救驾赏赐被吞的人中有他二哥李世民。
　　“根据我在张掖打探的消息，东突厥可汗一直对大隋虎视眈眈，想要复刻十六国时让中原称臣的‘辉煌’。东突厥可汗已经养了十万雄师，就等着入主中原。三征高丽后，杨广已经征不出兵来。他既然敢去雁门，东突厥可汗一定会出兵。”
　　李玄霸的话音刚落，翟让就惊诧道：“难道狗皇帝会死于突厥人之手？好事啊！”
　　李玄霸摇头：“大隋气数未尽，纵然征不出兵来，勋贵世家一人凑一点私兵，也能凑齐一支救援的军队。再者东突厥内部有义成公主为内应，外部有铁勒诸部和西突厥虎视眈眈，东突厥可汗也不是果敢之人，只要稍稍给他一点压力，他就会退兵。”
　　翟让一拍大腿，神情十分遗憾。
　　李玄霸讥讽道：“为解围，杨广只能下令厚赏召集天下义士来救；但他好脸面，当解围之后，他定不愿意厚赏救他的人，所以这支临时凑齐的军队肯定会作鸟兽散。”
　　魏徵讥笑道：“是他会做的事。接下来他应当会被劝说回西京重整天下，我们就需要在雁门郡到西京的沿路设防？”
　　李玄霸摇头：“他已经成了惊弓之鸟，纵然再多人劝他回西京，他也一定会回东都。若他去雁门郡时，义军就在太原到洛阳这一路设下埋伏。当援军去救杨广时，风平浪静；待杨广回洛阳时，再掀起波涛……”
　　李玄霸做了一个翻手的姿势，笑道：“纵然杀不死杨广，也一定会吓得杨广睡不着觉吧。翟公，这样是不是稍稍解气一点了？”
　　……
　　李世民回到张掖时，高表仁、房乔、杜如晦和提前回来的长孙无忌提前得到消息，出城二十里迎接他。
　　几人看到马背上风尘满面的李世民，心头都很是苦涩。
　　他们得到李世民回来的消息，自然也得到了李玄霸生死不明的消息。
　　几人都辗转反侧，心中想了许多劝慰的话。但当到看到神色平静的李世民时，他们却什么都说不出来。
　　看着支支吾吾的几位友人，李世民反倒露出劝慰的微笑：“先回城吧。这一路观音婢受了累，需要好好休息。”
　　长孙无忌忙探头看向李世民身后的马车。
　　李世民道：“就是这架马车。”
　　长孙无忌对李世民拱了一下手，钻进了马车看了一眼妹妹，又很快钻了出来：“睡得真香。”
　　高表仁道：“小声点，赶紧回程，我为你接风洗尘。”
　　李世民道：“辛苦你们了。”
　　房乔道：“你陆陆续续送来不少士人，我们已经不辛苦了。现在你已经是慰抚使，有权力任命地方官吏，我们就更轻松了。”
　　杜如晦道：“虽然你只是河右慰抚使，但陇右没有慰抚使，你大可以把势力拓展到整个陇右。”
　　长孙无忌道：“等会儿再说吧，先回去休息。”
　　高表仁拍了拍李世民的肩膀，终于说起了李玄霸的事：“三郎福大命大，肯定无事。他让你回张掖等他，一定就能回来。”
　　李世民道：“我知道。我相信阿玄。”
　　李世民表现得如此平静，众人便不好再劝了。
　　李世民与众人一起回张掖，途中将秦琼介绍给众人。
　　高表仁等人告诉李世民，裴行俨带着宗罗睺等人去草原例行练兵（抢劫），现在不在张掖。
　　高表仁抱怨：“守敬刚来张掖时，还能装出个士子模样，为我们减轻一二文书负担。现在已经完全不落家了。我们管不住他，只能你这个慰抚使来管了。”
　　李世民开玩笑道：“你这个渤海郡公都管不住，我这个慰抚使也不一定管用。”
　　杜如晦促狭道：“你可以率领下属揍他一顿，我们可带不了兵。”
　　李世民看向长孙无忌：“你可以带兵啊。”
　　长孙无忌扶额：“你看我像是打得过他吗？不过你回来了，一定要带着我把他揍一顿，这家伙总嘲笑我。我纵然比不过他，打胡人也绰绰有余，他居然嘲笑我该去和房玄龄杜克明争夺第一谋臣的位置？！瞧不起谁呢！！”
　　李世民笑道：“为什么不能争？文武双全不好吗？不过第一文臣肯定是我家阿玄，你们都争不了。”
　　长孙无忌道：“这倒是。”
　　说到李玄霸，众人又沉默了，倒是李世民还神色自若。
　　高表仁耐不住沉默的气氛，勉强挤出笑容道：“本想今日为你接风洗尘，但你们小夫妻俩肯定都累了。你们先休息，几日后我再来叨扰。”
　　房乔、杜如晦也告别，并拉着长孙无忌一起离开。
　　李世民送他们出门后出了一会儿神，神色平静地回到家中。
　　家中已经提前打扫过，一尘不染。
　　他看向已经凋谢的葡萄架子下的石桌。
　　李玄霸肩膀上披着大氅，腿上放着暖手笼，身侧两边都放着炭盆，一边看书一边打哈欠。
　　“天气冷就回房看书，天寒地冻的还非要架着火盆在院子里看书，阿玄你故意找病生吗？”
　　李世民没好气地训斥道。
　　李玄霸抬头看了啰嗦的二哥一眼。
　　幻象消失。
　　石桌旁没有火盆，也没有人。
　　李世民愣了一下，双拳握紧，神情平静地回屋整理行李。
