Chapter 142: An Undeserved Calamity for Three Loyal Generals

Li Xuanba jolted awake from a dream.

He had dreamt that he was floating before his own grave, where Zhuniang and his Second Sister-in-law were burning joss paper for him. Meanwhile, Second Brother and Little Fifth were crying on the side while stuffing their faces with his sacrificial offerings. The sight had infuriated him so much that his chest throbbed with a dull, suffocating pain.

Li Xuanba clutched his chest and took deep breaths for a long while before he finally managed to catch his breath.

The night-watch servant was awakened by Li Xuanba's ragged breathing and ran to fetch Yuwen Zhu in a fright.

Yuwen Zhu rushed out from the adjacent wing clutching her medicine box and inserted several acupuncture needles into Li Xuanba.

A servant brought over warm decoction. Every day, the moment Li Xuanba opened his eyes, the first thing he had to do was endure acupuncture and drink medicine. His mouth was so full of strange bitter tastes that he could no longer remember what real food tasted like.

Before Yuwen Zhu could voice her worries, Li Xuanba spoke up first. "Zhuniang, the sun is quite nice today. Support me so I can go out for a walk."

Even while recuperating, one could not stay bedridden forever; that would only make the body grow weaker and weaker.

Ever since Li Xuanba became able to get out of bed, he would have someone support him for a few laps inside the small house every day to rebuild his stamina.

After Zhai Rang learned of Li Xuanba's true identity, he yielded his own courtyard to Li Xuanba and posted personal guards around it, forbidding anyone from disturbing him. The medical rooms for Yuwen Zhu and Sun Simiao were also moved to this courtyard. Thus, Li Xuanba could now step outside for a stroll whenever the weather was pleasant.

Though winter had set in, as long as he wrapped up warmly, basking in the sunshine outside felt far more comfortable than staying cooped up indoors.

Both Sun Simiao and Yuwen Zhu were skilled physicians. Knowing that moving around a bit more would help Li Xuanba recover faster, they did not stop his daily routine of walking.

Only Li Zhiyun would grumble incessantly every day while supporting Li Xuanba, a face full of discontent.

Lately, Li Zhiyun's nagging about Li Xuanba not taking care of his body had grown increasingly frequent. In a daze, Li Xuanba thought he saw the shadow of his Second Brother on Li Zhiyun's face, which "scared" him so much that he quickly cast Li Zhiyun out into the field to temper himself.

Since their identities had been laid bare, Li Zhiyun could drop his female disguise, adopt the pseudonym Wei Wu, and go to the battlefield under Luo Shixin's protection to sharpen his martial skills.

The intensity of the Wagang Stronghold's battles was currently low, making it ideal for Li Zhiyun to gain experience. Once they returned to Zhangye, Second Brother could take Li Zhiyun under his wing, and Li Xuanba's ears would finally be completely at peace.

Li Xuanba grumbled softly to Yuwen Zhu, "Little Fifth excels at mounted archery, while Shixin possesses extraordinary valor. The two coordinate with tacit understanding. Shixin even said that Little Fifth is now like a mini version of Second Brother."

Yuwen Zhu smiled gently. "Has my brother-in-law become so formidable already?"

Li Xuanba nodded with a smile. "Though I still think he's far too young, he's just too noisy. Better to chase him onto the battlefield."

Yuwen Zhu shook her head. "Sanlang, that isn't nice of you. He's only worried about you. How can you find him annoying?"

Li Xuanba replied, "I know Little Fifth cares about me, but he really is quite bothersome."

Luo Shixin had approached him in private, quietly telling him that Little Fifth often hid away and cried alone due to nightmares.

Little Fifth was not like himself or Second Brother; his mental fortitude was not yet strong enough to view matters of life and death with indifference. The fact that Li Xuanba had nearly succumbed to illness must have left a deep psychological scar on Little Fifth.

Even so, that was no excuse for Little Fifth to enter his rebellious phase early.

Hearing Li Xuanba's complaints, Yuwen Zhu chuckled and sighed softly. "I don't think he's entering a rebellious phase. He's simply standing up for you in his own way."

The corner of Li Xuanba's mouth twitched slightly. "Shixin told me the same thing, telling me not to misunderstand Little Fifth. Little Fifth told him that my temperament is too soft, my temper too gentle, and my disposition too amiable—not like a noble scion at all—making it easy for others to look down on me. So, he wants to play the role of the typical arrogant noble youth, speaking the uncomfortable words on my behalf. After all, he is young; even if he says something wrong, others won't hold it against him due to his age, and he can just correct it next time."

Yuwen Zhu smiled. "Little Fifth is very clever. Sanlang, you should be happy."

Li Xuanba rubbed his forehead. "Acting arrogant toward strangers can indeed be explained that way. But what about the prickly tone he uses with me?"

Yuwen Zhu said, "He's probably just worried about your health."

Li Xuanba sighed. How did the conversation loop right back? Even if he was worried about his health, he could express his concern in a much more well-behaved manner.

He still maintained that Little Fifth had definitely entered his rebellious phase.

Seeing Li Xuanba sighing and groaning over Li Zhiyun, Yuwen Zhu could not help but laugh once more.

She, for one, felt that Little Fifth was wonderful just as he was.

After walking for less than half an incense stick's time, Li Xuanba returned to his room gasping for breath, his back completely drenched in sweat.

Yuwen Zhu brought servants to help wipe down Li Xuanba's body, change his clothes, and insert dozens of needles into his body while at it.

At first, Li Xuanba would blush, but after being pricked so many times, he was completely desensitized.

Now, he calmly took off his clothes, wiped off his sweat, and lay down, letting Yuwen Zhu insert needle after needle into his body.

Since Physician Sun needed to research medicinal prescriptions, routine therapeutic treatments were left to Yuwen Zhu. She had grown adept at administering acupuncture on Li Xuanba.

By the time Li Zhiyun washed away the reek of blood and arrived with his spoils of war to visit his third brother, the needles had just been removed from Li Xuanba's body.

"Third Brother, Wagang Stronghold is about to decamp and go raid the Emperor! I want to go with them!" Li Zhiyun handed a jar of honey he had pillaged to Yuwen Zhu.

He and Luo Shixin had achieved great merit through their cooperation this time, which would have entitled him to plenty of precious gold, silver, and silk. Yet he took none of that, exchanging his military merits solely for the jar of honey that Xu Shiji had been eyeing.

When Xu Shiji handed the honey to Li Zhiyun, his face had been full of reluctance.

Li Xuanba snapped testily, "Following them to raid a prominent family's merchant caravan won't get you recognized, but if you clash with the Great Sui army, your identity will easily be exposed."

Li Zhiyun replied, "I can disguise myself as a woman for the campaign."

Li Xuanba said, "The Sui army possesses powerful crossbows and heavy bows. You only have a suit of cloth armor right now—it's far too dangerous. I forbid it."

Li Zhiyun flopped down beside Li Xuanba carelessly and grumbled, "Third Brother, you're so annoying! Are you looking down on me?"

Li Xuanba countered, "Even if Second Brother charged into enemy lines without armor, I would scold him just the same."

Li Zhiyun curled his lip. "Fine, then."

He kicked off his boots and squeezed Li Xuanba inward. "Move over, I'm exhausted. Didn't sleep well during the forced march."

He wriggled under Li Xuanba's blanket, buried his face in Li Xuanba's soft pillow, and soon emitted soft snores.

Li Zhiyun did not normally snore; he was truly worn out.

Li Xuanba tucked the corners of the blanket around Li Zhiyun. Yuwen Zhu stifled a smile and quietly slipped out.

Li Xuanba picked up a book of folk anecdotes sent by Zhai Rang and flipped through it. Along the way, Luo Shixin also came to visit Li Xuanba. Seeing Li Zhiyun sleeping so soundly, and with Li Xuanba's indulgence, Luo Shixin pinched Li Zhiyun's nose.

Even so, Li Zhiyun didn't wake up, breathing through his open mouth and continuing to sleep sweetly.

Luo Shixin teased, "He couldn't sleep a wink on the battlefield, yet his arrow release was as steady as ever. Now that he's back by Third Young Master's side, he can finally sleep."

Li Xuanba said, "Thank you for your hard work, Shixin."

Luo Shixin replied, "It's no trouble at all. Third Young Master, when the weather turns warm, will we be returning to Zhangye?"

Li Xuanba answered, "No, I still have some matters to attend to in the Central Plains. We will return after those are finished. However, when spring comes next year, we can send a message to Second Brother so he can coordinate with us. Will you go?"

Luo Shixin shook his head vigorously. "I'm not going! I must protect Third Young Master and Jihong."

Li Xuanba sighed. "If you don't leave, you will likely encounter General Zhang on the battlefield."

Luo Shixin remained silent for a moment before cupping his fists. "Each serving our respective masters, I will not shrink from battle."

Li Xuanba felt thoroughly helpless.

Why was he so stubborn? Ah, well. He would just have to figure out a way to let Luo Shixin avoid Zhang Xutuo himself.

Zhang Xutuo currently served as the Grand Commissioner of Investigation and Suppression for Henan Circuit, making him the principal adversary of Wagang Stronghold and Wang Bo.

In original history, he had repeatedly defeated Wagang Stronghold and Wang Bo, completely shattering the Qijun rebel army and sending Wang Bo and others fleeing in all directions.

In this timeline, however—perhaps due to the guiding framework Li Xuanba provided, or perhaps because Wei Zheng as a chief strategist was truly capable—Wang Bo's force was significantly stronger. He had already captured several small towns around Mount Tai for military farming and brought Qijun rebel forces under Sun Xuanya, Shi Zhishe, and Hao Xiaode into his fold, repelling Zhang Xutuo's assaults multiple times.

Although Qijun did not possess super granaries like those around Luoyang, because the naval fleet departed from Qijun, various counties in Qijun housed smaller transit granaries.

After growing powerful, Wang Bo first breached the fortified manors of local magnates to seize grain and weapons, then swiftly seized the small transit granaries near Mount Tai. This provided the capital to consolidate the Qijun rebel armies and created the conditions for his military agrarian colonies.

Furthermore, Yang Xuangan frequently harried Zhang Xutuo from south of the Huai River, tying down Zhang Xutuo's troop strength. Additionally, Zhang Xutuo lacked three ferocious generals under his command: Qin Qiong, Luo Shixin, and Pei Xingyan. Thus, Zhang Xutuo's achievements in suppressing rebels in this timeline fell far short of his original history, resulting in a stalemate with the Henan rebels.

While Wang Bo was performing splendidly right now, Li Xuanba knew that by standing in opposition to the powerful gentry clans, Wang Bo was drifting further and further from the imperial throne.

Hebei had Dou Jiande, Shandong had Wang Bo, and Henan had Zhai Rang. These were the three most powerful rebel armies in the Central Plains today.

Beyond them, from the Yangtze River to the Huai River, from Shanxi to Guanzhong, from Liaodong to the modern-day Mongolian Steppe, and down to Heyou and Longxi where Li Shimin presided, rebel armies everywhere raised their banners in revolt.

Virtually all commoners who could rebel had done so, while the powerful gentry sat comfortably like fishermen waiting for a bite, watching the Great Sui Emperor continue to court his own ruin.

"Wei Zheng should be arriving at Qijun soon," Li Xuanba said. "Shixin, go along with the Wagang folk this time to test your skills against the Sui army."

Luo Shixin cupped his hands. "Understood."

Li Xuanba pinched the bridge of his nose and suddenly broke into laughter.

Luo Shixin asked in confusion, "Why is Third Young Master laughing?"

Li Xuanba chuckled. "Since Yang Guang's first campaign against Goguryeo... no, since Yang Guang's very first personal campaign against Tuyuhun, where he recklessly forced his way through Dadouba Valley despite snowstorms, through the three Goguryeo campaigns where the King of Goguryeo toyed with him multiple times, and the successive deaths of two crown princes..."

Li Xuanba paused his laughter briefly before laughing once more. "To the common people under Heaven, these were disasters; to the aristocratic lords, they were nothing but jokes. The more they laughed, the less reverence they held for the Emperor and the Great Sui. This time, I'll add two even funnier jokes for the Emperor. I wonder if we can laugh away the Great Sui's national fortune a little sooner."

A joke from later generations was 'laugh a little, lose some karma.' For the Great Sui, it was 'laugh a little, lose some national fortune.'

Luo Shixin said earnestly, "I already have zero reverence for the Emperor. Those high lords hold noble statuses; surely they can't be more humble and submissive than me."

Li Xuanba laughed. "Then you'd be mistaken. Don't belittle yourself—most of those high ministers are far more servile and humble than you."

...

In the tenth month of the tenth year of Daye, as Yang Guang was marching toward the Eastern Capital of Luoyang, rebels wearing black cloth bands on their wrists suddenly emerged at the rear of the Sui army, looting nearly a hundred fine horses.

Fearing punishment, the military officers dared not report the incident and covered it up.

As Yang Guang neared Luoyang, the raids on the Sui army's rear grew increasingly frequent.

After armors, ballistas, weapons, and other supply trains were seized, the officers could no longer keep a lid on it and finally reported the matter to Commander-in-Chief Yuwen Shu.

After pondering for a long while, Yuwen Shu reported to Yang Guang, "Rebel chieftains launched an attack, and the Sui army lost a dozen horses and some armor. Though the losses are minor, the rebel chieftains dared to strike imperial forces. I request Your Majesty to order a severe punishment."

Hearing that the Sui army had only lost a dozen horses and some armor, Yang Guang paid it no mind, waving his hand dismissively. "Let Zhang Xutuo go to Zhuo Commandery to suppress the rebels."

Yuwen Shu said, "The rebel chieftains are cunning and hard to hunt down after hiding in desolate mountains and wild forests for days. Moreover, Zhang Xutuo is advanced in age; I fear his energy is flagging."

Yang Guang frowned. "It's not as if I dispatched Zhang Xutuo alone to quell the rebels. That the rebellion remains unsuppressed must be because the other suppressing generals aren't trying hard enough, leaving Zhang Xutuo to run himself ragged."

Yuwen Shu: "..." *I just wanted to ask for more troops to suppress the rebels. Why is His Majesty scolding the suppressing generals instead?*

Yuwen Shu knew Yang Guang inside out and guessed that His Majesty's sudden tangent must stem from a underlying cause.

Yuwen Shu thought for a moment and asked, "Does Your Majesty believe Generals Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo are intentionally dragging their feet?"

Yang Guang felt immensely gratified in his heart. As expected, the Duke of Xu State understood him best.

Yang Guang sighed, "Yu Juluo was stripped of his official post due to a offense. I originally intended to give him a chance to redeem himself and regain his position, but to think he would fail Me!"

Even someone as brazen and shameless as Yuwen Shu was left speechless by Yang Guang's words for a moment.

Yu Juluo's so-called crime was hardly anything at all. He had merely brought abundant gifts and treasure to present to the Emperor and capital nobles when reporting on his duties.

Every local official entering the capital did this. Had he not done so, he would have incurred the Emperor's displeasure and been impeached by the powerful elites.

Why was Yu Juluo punished despite following official customs? Not because he offended anyone, but because he possessed double pupils in his eyes.

People in the world believed in prophetic omens, and rumors claimed that double pupils were the mark of a sage or sovereign. Thus, Yang Guang detested Yu Juluo.

Even Yuwen Shu, who frequently framed others, found Yang Guang's hatred utterly unreasonable.

Throughout history, among those rumored to have double pupils, none were emperors except Sage Emperor Shun. Aside from Cangjie who invented Chinese characters, others were at best regional warlords, and almost all met grim ends.

Double pupils were not unheard of among commoners. Yu Juluo was no aristocratic noble; his entire glory and wealth were tied to the Emperor. Where would he find the power to rebel and claim sovereignty? Alas, he was truly suffering an undeserved calamity.

What was even more tragic was General Tuwan Xu. Yu Juluo had been assigned to him as a deputy by the Emperor; he had no personal friendship with Yu Juluo to begin with.

Now, the Emperor remembered Yu Juluo and dragged the innocent General Tuwan Xu down alongside him. This was an even greater, innocent disaster.

Yuwen Shu sighed in his heart, but naturally, he would not contradict Yang Guang aloud.

He said respectfully, "Your Majesty is wise. Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo have botched military opportunities; others should be appointed to lead the forces against the rebels."

Yuwen Shu's rare shred of conscience prompted him to shift the topic. If the Emperor agreed, Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo would merely lose their posts.

Yang Guang commanded, "Arrest Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo and bring them back to the Eastern Capital in wooden cangs to answer for their crimes! Hand over the army to Wang Shichong, the Deputy Governor of Jiangdu, to continue suppressing the rebels!"

Yuwen Shu sighed in his heart once more. *In cangs? Then there's no saving them. I did what I could.*

He replied, "Understood."

After saying this, Yang Guang likely realized that punishing only Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo was a bit too blatant. Remembering that someone had impeached Dong Chun, the Garrison Commander of Pengcheng, for cowardice in battle, he added, "Also arrest Dong Chun, the Garrison Commander of Pengcheng, and bring him in cangs to the Eastern Capital for prosecution!"

Yuwen Shu: "..." "Your Majesty, hasn't the Garrison Commander of Pengcheng won battle after battle?"

Yang Guang said with disgust, "Dong Chun claims he has never been defeated and has wiped out countless rebels, yet at the same time submits memorials saying rebel numbers grow day by day. If he wins every battle, where are all these additional rebels coming from? Someone accused him of cowardice and falsely claiming merit, and I say it is certainly so!"

Yuwen Shu: "..." "Your Majesty is wise."

He had thought Yu Juluo suffered an undeserved calamity, and Tuwan Xu even more so. Now it seemed Yu Juluo and Tuwan Xu combined could not compare to Dong Chun.

Whom had Dong Chun offended? Pei Yun and his cohort? Or had his memorial simply landed right on His Majesty's sore spot?

After returning home, Yuwen Shu instructed his sons, "His Majesty is capricious; for ministers, the more you do, the more mistakes you make. If you see His Majesty suffer a setback and you happen to be the ones in charge, you must make preparations well in advance."

Yuwen Shu's true intention was: *run away when it's time to run.*

The Imperial Consort, Yuwen Shiji, indicated he understood. The eldest son, Yuwen Huaji, and second son, Yuwen Zhiji, declared they understood even better than their father and would definitely not mess up.

Yuwen Shu stroked his beard in satisfaction.

His three sons might not be overly capable, but they had mastered seventy to eighty percent of his skill in reading people's expressions and cues. Preserving their family legacy in the future should pose no problem.

Even if the Great Sui fell, with his three sons' skill at reading the wind, they could switch allegiances and still live comfortably.

As the rebel forces continuously harassed and plundered the rear of the Sui army, Yang Guang issued his latest imperial decree for rebel suppression.

Tuwan Xu, Yu Juluo, and Dong Chun were all brought into the capital wearing cangs. Though there was no evidence proving their guilt, Yu Juluo and Dong Chun were sentenced to execution, while Tuwan Xu was stripped of his official rank, demoted to a commoner, and exiled to guard Jian'an.

Yang Guang also knew Tuwan Xu was collateral damage, so he raised his hand in mercy and summoned Tuwan Xu shortly afterward, pardoning his exile.

However, Tuwan Xu failed to appreciate the favor, passing away from grief and depression before his imperial audience, leaving Yang Guang to sigh in dismay for a long while.

To avoid being targeted and tracked, the rebel armies did not display their respective banners this time. Instead, they tied black cloth strips around their arms and raised black banners to signal friendly forces.

According to Five Elements theory, the Great Sui represented the Fire virtue; tying black cloth and raising black banners signified "Water extinguishing Fire."

This joint rebel coalition was led by the three strongest forces in the Central Plains—Zhai Rang, Wang Bo, and Dou Jiande. They roped in minor rebel leaders along the way to set stage-by-stage ambushes, while the primary troops of Zhai Rang, Wang Bo, and Dou Jiande conducted non-stop hit-and-run harassment.

When Yang Guang issued his decree, they thought a tough battle was finally coming. Who could have known that the Emperor's first order was not to send reinforcements to suppress the rebels, but to condemn Tuwan Xu, Yu Juluo, and Dong Chun?

Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo had been suppressing rebels south of the Yangtze River, far from the Central Plains, and were victorious in every battle, repeatedly defeating Liu Yuanjin, Zhu Xie, Guan Chong, and others.

Dong Chun, the Garrison Commander of Pengcheng, was also stationed in the Jianghuai region, a good distance from the Central Plains. He too was undefeated, killing rebel chieftains like Peng Xiaocai one after another.

What kind of wrong medicine had the dog Emperor taken this time? Why execute them of all people?

When the three rebel leaders gathered, all were completely utterly baffled.

Dou Jiande joked, "I almost thought the dog Emperor was our insider agent."

Wang Bo remarked, "A wise person once said, 'A centipede dies but never falls, because decay always starts from within.' Looking at the dog Emperor now, it truly is so."

Zhai Rang glanced at Wang Bo, sorely tempted to ask him whether the "wise person" he spoke of was Third Young Master Li. He was certain he had heard Third Young Master Li say those exact words before.

Unaware that Wang Bo and Zhai Rang shared the same shadow mastermind behind the scenes, Dou Jiande laughed. "As expected of a wise man! His words truly make sense. Now that the dog Emperor is acting as our mole, do you gentlemen dare to raise your banners in open revolt?"

Wang Bo said, "I was going to raise my banner regardless."

Zhai Rang teased, "Does Duke Dou look down on me?"

Dou Jiande bowed repeatedly with cupped hands. "I wouldn't dare! It was merely a joke."

When the meeting ended, although the rebel army still wore their black wristbands, they replaced their banners with white funeral streamers inscribed with the name of "Sui Crown Prince Yang Jian."

At the same time, they turned the event of Yang Jian's armed admonition into ballads and spread them far and wide, claiming they would avenge and redress the wrongs done to Crown Prince Yang Jian.

When Yang Guang learned of this, his vision went black, and he actually fainted!

Upon waking, he was filled with astronomical fury and finally issued imperial decrees to dispatch additional troops against the rebels.

Thus, local officials across the realm received appointments as Bandit Suppression Ambassadors. Though Li Yuan failed to reclaim his position as Pacification Ambassador of Hedong, he gained the title of Shanxi Bandit Suppression Ambassador. The posts of Hedong Pacification Ambassador and Bandit Suppression Ambassador were handed to Yao Junsu, one of Yang Guang's personal bodyguards.

Yao Junsu was merely a Commander of the Eagle-Soaring Corps and originally lacked the standing to become the Hedong Pacification Ambassador. However, Yang Guang utterly loathed the rebel forces marching under the banner of the deposed Crown Prince Yang Jian and feared that ministers in court might genuinely be swayed. Thus, he made an exception to promote his personal bodyguard.

Yao Junsu was deeply grateful for Yang Guang's appreciation, eager to lay down his life for the Emperor.

Li Yuan, who harbored rebellious ambitions, found things much more difficult, forced to ponder and refine his treasonous plans over and over again.

After Dou Huiming returned to Taiyuan, although Li Yuan blamed her for taking such a dangerous gamble that might have endangered the entire family, he comforted her, saying that the outcome was good and she could finally put her mind at ease.

As for Li Jiancheng, he was merely dragged down by Li Yuanji. He had simply done what any normal person would do—rushing back to Taiyuan Commandery to inform his parents after being falsely accused by Li Yuanji, thereby escaping this disaster. Dou Huiming could not blame him and even had to console him.

Lady Wan wept softly and said, "Madam, with you here, I do not dare to hate Li Jiancheng. But if Qijian were still alive, would Li Jiancheng truly let my Qijian go? Even if unintentional, he almost caused a loss of life. Could he trust without reservation that Qijian wouldn't harbor hatred against him?"

Dou Huiming patted the back of Lady Wan's hand and said, "I worry about that as well. In this household, only Second Son can be the heir apparent. If Eldest Son steps back, all my sons can survive, and your Qijian will be safe and sound too."

Lady Wan looked up. "And if Eldest Young Master refuses to step back?"

Dou Huiming wore a look of deep exhaustion. "The palm and the back of the hand are both flesh of my flesh, but I can never fail Second Son and Third Son again."

Lady Wan's heart stirred, and she buried herself in Dou Huiming's embrace, weeping uncontrollably.

Dou Huiming gently patted Lady Wan's back, choking back her own tears.

Her greatest pain right now was not having to make a choice, but discovering that when she did make the choice, there wasn't a single shred of hesitation in her heart.

Even though she had already realized she possessed selfish motives and was not as loving and kind as she had always appeared, abandoning Li Jiancheng without a moment's doubt still tortured her soul.

Li Jiancheng was her first child. Though he had not grown up by her side, his significance to her remained special.

That was why time and again she tried to get close to Li Jiancheng, planning wholeheartedly for him over and over, even breaking the hearts of Second Son and Third Son, who were closest to her.

Dou Huiming had believed that striving to ease the tension between her three children and fostering brotherly harmony was for the good of all her children.

Reality had dealt her a harsh slap in the face.

Yet it was not as though Dou Huiming no longer loved Li Jiancheng at all.

Her very first child—how could she cut him off completely?

"But Eldest Son, the only way your mother can save your life is for you to yield your position."

Dou Huiming was in anguish, yet her mind was crystal clear.

Only, in that crystal-clear mirror, a frail, sickly shadow swayed continuously, refusing to turn back and look at her.

Third Son refused to turn back to look at her.

Even when Third Son entered her dreams, his back was turned to her. No matter how she chased, she could never catch up; no matter how she cried out, Third Son never turned back.

*Sanlang, mother was wrong. I beg you, look back at mother just once...*

*Clack.*

Li Xuanba placed a Go stone.

Li Zhiyun tossed aside his remaining pieces and leaned back against the chair's backrest. "Lost again! I lost again! I can even defeat Second Brother—why can't I ever beat Third Brother?!"

Li Xuanba was currently unwell, and the conditions in the Wagang Stronghold were none too luxurious; low daybeds rarely featured backrests, and outdoors there were only low stools.

Since Li Xuanba wasn't meeting with scholar-officials now and had no need to adhere to formal etiquette, he sought out craftsmen and drew several sketches of chairs for them to figure out.

In the past, he hadn't made chairs because kneeling on daybeds was the proper etiquette for the gentry and could not be lightly altered. Moreover, with backrests and bolsters on daybeds, sitting was comfortable enough, so there was no need to risk being viewed as a freak by the gentry by introducing chairs.

The craftsmanship of chairs was simple, and the craftsmen made them after a single glance. All the generals in Wagang Stronghold who were too lazy to take off their boots embraced the chairs enthusiastically. Li Zhiyun had also fallen in love with sitting in a chair.

Li Xuanba unhurriedly gathered the Go stones. "Because your mind is restless."

Li Zhiyun huffed, "Am I restless every single time I play chess with Third Brother?"

Li Xuanba said helplessly, "Isn't that true? Every time you play chess with me, you don't take it seriously and always try to fool around."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第142章 三忠将无妄之灾 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
李智云善弈。

对弈也需要天赋，李玄霸虽然棋艺不算差，但也只能算熟练工，没有钻研。但李智云不一样，他对待下棋就像是对待弓箭和书法一样，钻研非常勤奋。

不过李智云在李玄霸面前下棋，就像是顽童胡闹一样，几乎不见章法。

按李智云的话来说，就是实验新棋路。

不过现在李智云不是实验新棋路，而是真的心不定。

被李玄霸揭穿，李智云也不装了。

他抱怨道：“士信化名罗成，在战场上出尽了风头。我也想出风头。”

李玄霸嘴角勾起别人看不懂的笑意。

“罗成”这个假名当然是自己取的。这下隋末真的有一个勇猛的小将叫“罗成”了。

李玄霸收好棋子。李智云从椅子上跳起来，把李玄霸扶起来。

李玄霸一边往门外走，一边絮絮叨叨：“你在这时候出什么风头？顶着一个完全猜不出你是谁的假名有什么意思？等回家再出风头。”

李智云叹气：“好。那么三兄，我们什么时候回家？明年开春？”

李玄霸道：“开春先去齐郡，我已经说了很多次了。我现在这身体，也去不了张掖。”

李智云没好气道：“但我们可以回洛阳。只要回了洛阳，二兄就会得到消息，派人来接我们！”

李玄霸淡淡道：“放火的人也能得到我们的消息。你认为是河东离洛阳近，还是张掖离洛阳近？”

李智云瘪嘴：“好吧，不回洛阳。但是三兄，我们是不是该给二兄送信了？”

李玄霸道：“等我们去了齐郡再说。”

李智云沉默了一会儿，狐疑地问道：“三兄，你不给二兄送信，除了担心自己又发病，让二兄空欢喜一场之外，是不是还担心二兄亲自来把你绑走，让你不能在中原胡闹？”

李玄霸抬起手狠狠敲了李智云脑袋一下：“什么叫胡闹？！你三兄我快把整个大隋都点燃了，你说这是胡闹？！”

李智云深呼吸：“你承认了！”

李玄霸：“我承认什么？”

李智云高声嚷嚷：“你就是担心二兄来把你绑走！”

李玄霸：“……”

因为受伤没能参加这次抢劫隋军行动而留守瓦岗寨的徐世勣，抱着家里刚刚偷偷搜寻来的名贵滋补药材，前来拜访李玄霸和李智云。

翟让在经过李玄霸同意后，将李玄霸的身份告诉了徐世勣，但只告诉单雄信屋内住着的是士人，不是士女。

他担心单雄信因为好奇来打扰李玄霸，李玄霸笑着献策：“只要告诉单雄信，我是个十分严肃的儒生，如果进屋记得带经书来向我讨教，否则我就会很生气地骂人。他就不敢来了。”

翟让将信将疑地将李玄霸的话告诉单雄信，单雄信居然真的绕着这个小院走。

单雄信这态度，让翟让头疼不已。

有人肯教授经学，单雄信应该惊喜若狂地讨教，怎么还躲着了？

翟让是小吏出身，在自己乡中也算有小有资产，否则得不到小吏的位置。

徐世勣是家资颇丰的豪族，单雄信也是振臂一呼从乡中拉出千人队伍的小豪强。虽说请不到多优秀的士人当老师，但他们都有钱读书识字。

可单雄信却提起读书就甩脑袋，让翟让叹息不已。

只有一腔勇武，怎么能出人头地？自己这个同乡真是令人无奈。

徐世勣与李世民和李玄霸年岁相差不大。当李世民和李玄霸还在清河郡剿匪的时候，徐世勣就听闻了李世民少年英雄的名声，对李世民心生向往。

只是他不愿意离开家乡，又认为李世民身为唐国公次子估计看不上自己，所以没有去投奔。

如今有机会结识李玄霸，即使他知道李玄霸病愈后一定会离开，与他们这些反贼为敌，他仍旧抓紧机会与李玄霸相处。

翟让虽然告知了徐世勣李玄霸的真实身份，但没有告诉徐世勣这次抢劫隋军的行为其实是李玄霸献策主导。

徐世勣告诉家里自己结识了一个很厉害的士人，家里对徐世勣的资助又上了一层，竭尽全力帮徐世勣搜罗药材。

“你们要离开了吗？”徐世勣遗憾道，“我还想多向李三郎君讨教兵法。”

他对经学不感兴趣，但没想到李玄霸看似病弱，居然熟背兵书，论兵头头是道，让他受益良多。

李玄霸道：“只要有缘，我们会相逢。”

徐世勣苦笑：“下次见面，我们可能就是仇敌了。”

李智云嘟囔：“那可不一定。”

徐世勣想了想，道：“也对，李三郎君应该不会上战场。”

李智云怜惜地看了徐世勣一眼，叹了口气。

徐世勣疑惑：“李五郎君为何叹气？”

李智云老气横秋道：“没什么，只是感伤离别。”

蠢懋功，看看你家翟公的殷勤劲，难道你没发现什么吗？

李玄霸下了一局棋，现在精力不济。徐世勣没有留下叨扰李玄霸，留下药材就离开了。

李智云对李玄霸道：“不知道徐世勣得知翟让有意投靠我们时，会不会离开瓦岗寨。”

李玄霸叫人把药材送给正和孙思邈学习医术的宇文珠，道：“小五，你知道翟让等人，和王薄的义军有什么不同吗？”

李智云完全不像小时候那样乖乖思考：“三兄，你好烦啊，有话直说，别考我。”

李玄霸：“……”等见到二哥，一定让二哥狠狠揍你一顿！

李玄霸道：“王薄是真正的平民百姓，他身边的人也都是贫苦百姓。他们是真的活不下去才揭竿而起。虽是被逼无奈，但起兵也算遵从本心。”

“翟让原是县中小吏，因犯罪入狱，后来被人偷偷释放，逃到瓦岗寨成为逃犯，纠集了一批人起兵；投奔翟让的单雄信是乡中豪强，徐世勣更是一方豪族。他们的地位与世家勋贵无法比，勉强能算上寒门，但也不算普通百姓。”

听了李玄霸解释后，李智云终于转动了他本来就聪明的脑袋瓜子：“翟让倒算得上被逼无奈自保，单雄信和徐世勣既然不是走投无路，为何投靠翟让？”

他想了想，眼睛一亮：“不，单雄信和徐世勣并非不是走投无路。他们只是当地豪强，没有官身，虽然能以钱财免除徭役兵役，但杨广缺兵缺粮，朝廷不会动官宦士人的家产，一定会对他们敲诈勒索！”

李玄霸欣慰地点头：“没错。而且他们如果加入起兵，就能左右义军的动向，不让义军骚扰乡里。”

李智云摸了摸自己没刮干净的青色胡茬：“所以王薄能抢豪族的粮，但瓦岗寨只抢漕运和豪商，现在比王薄穷多了。”

李玄霸引导道：“那么你现在能得出结论，我为何敢向翟让和徐世勣暴露身份，并确信他们会投靠我们？”

李智云笑道：“他们都是寒门，离士人很近，一直向往成为士人，而不是反贼。只是大隋不给他们机会，他们才选择当反贼保命和保财。如果给他们一个机会投效士人，让他们有机会一跃成为士人，他们肯定不愿意当反贼。”

李智云思索了一会儿，补充道：“如果他们没有信心在隋末成功争夺天下，那么肯定会投靠他人。显然翟让与王薄、窦建德不同，他没有为君之心。而徐世勣和单雄信就没有……啊，我还嘲笑徐世勣蠢，他该不会其实对翟让的犹豫心知肚明，也存了给自己留一条后路的心？”

李玄霸道：“徐世勣与单雄信和翟让又有不同。他是迁徙到此地的士族，无论是家财还是家世都远胜普通百姓。他家应当是把他当世家子弟培养。”

李智云戏谑道：“原来这个反贼是来自小世家啊。那他肯定会倾向于我们。说不定翟让不愿意投奔他人，他自己也要选世家投奔呢。”

李玄霸道：“不过你也不要因为他们起兵的心思不纯就轻视他们。这天下连小世家和地方小豪强都快家破人亡了……”

李智云接话道：“就更别说普通百姓。”

李玄霸道：“嗯。他们自救的心是真的。任何人的求生之心都不应该被轻视。”

李智云摩拳擦掌，那动作让李玄霸看着十分眼熟。

李智云搓手手道：“这么说，徐世勣以后可能是我属下？”

李玄霸敲了一下李智云的脑袋：“那你得努力了，否则将来你可能是徐世勣的属下。还不一定谁当主将呢。”

李智云瞪大眼睛：“什么？你居然不徇私！太过分了！”

李玄霸：“……”不徇私不才是理所当然吗？小五你说什么废话？

……

杨广下令后，终于遏制了义军对隋军的抢劫。

大隋宣布大获全胜。

但这宣布，让许多勋贵世家都当笑话。

与其说是大隋把义军击退了，不如说义军抢得差不多了，所以自己跑了。

杨广错过了最初的战机。当他集结了大军时，义军早就化整为零跑得没有踪影。隋军甚至不知道是哪一支义军抢的他们。

因为全天下没有地方没有民贼。

更让大隋朝廷惊恐的是，当义军举起“太子杨暕”的旗帜时，其他民贼纷纷举起了“太子杨暕”的旗帜。

贼帅们纷纷在全国各个地方为太子杨暕发丧，还有已经僭越称王的贼帅追封太子杨暕谥号。

甚至有不读书的贼帅乱给太子杨暕追封了隋朝皇帝，称“隋哀帝”。

这件事没人敢传到杨广耳朵里。

看看那三个将领怎么死的？不就是据实告诉杨广民贼越来越多，怎么剿灭都剿灭不完。

就说了这个大实话，三人明明战无不胜，居然全部都死了。

现在还有谁敢给杨广说实话？

苏威本来都想据实直言了，但这件事他也不敢告诉杨广。

李渊得知此事后，叹息道：“如果陛下知道太子杨暕被追封成皇帝，不知道会迁怒多少人。我们也要加紧准备起兵了。”

这次李渊没有再支支吾吾当谜语人，明明心中早就有了反意，还被下属和儿子推着才装作不甘不愿地起兵。

他发现自己处在一个很危险的界限上——杨广并不太信任他，随时都可能会降罪，所以他就只能早做准备了。

再者，他现在身边只有李建成。李建成正心虚，没有底气劝说李渊起兵。李渊找不到人推锅，只能自己拿主意。

当然，他还是示意属下也多劝说他。

起兵谋反之事，他身为隋朝大臣还是不能做得太果决，要被下属推一把，表现自己是无奈之举才行。

偏远的张掖，李世民迟了几个月才得知这件事。

他得知这件事的时候，张掖的都开了。在中原，恐怕都要穿单衣了。

现在民贼四起，河右之地几乎和中原断绝了联系。李世民可以随意扩充势力。

在李世民得知隋军被抢了的时候，杨广给他加官的圣旨也到了。

杨广很信任没有为太子杨暕求情的李世民，所以这次升任李世民为陇右道慰抚使。

陇右道包括了河右全境和陇西部分郡县，统辖范围比河右慰抚使大多了。

而且杨广还加封了李世民陇右道捕盗大使，给了李世民可以随意在陇右道乱窜，甚至见机行事，帮助其他地方捕盗的权力。

李世民得到旨意后，没有表现得多兴奋，好像理所当然似的。

他有条不紊地把手头工作安排下去，领兵去关西等地招募豪强，很快就有豪强带兵来投。

不过李世民升官后最大的收获却不是他自己招募的，而是姗姗来迟的薛元敬找来的。

李世民匆匆离开太原时没有带薛元敬。

他此行危险，所以让薛元敬派人去张掖通知房乔等人，并收罗太原郡士人，先行前往张掖。

但薛元敬路上感染了风寒，在大兴暂住了一段时间，待开春时才重新出发，所以比李世民迟来张掖几月。

薛家身为河东郡姓世家，当然在两京都有宅邸。

薛元敬在大兴宅邸养病时，居然发现族叔薛德音也在，还带了一个快分娩的女子。

薛德音没有告诉薛元敬女子的身份，薛元敬只当女子是族叔的妾室，没有多想。

薛德音告诉薛元敬，他也准备去张掖投奔李世民，只是女子胎儿不稳，所以先在大兴生下孩子后再出发。

薛元敬虽疑惑族叔为何不多住几月，待女子身体恢复后再离开大兴，但这是族叔的家事，他就没有多嘴。

但他与薛德音一同启程时，一件“意外”让他警觉——女子顺利分娩，但几日后却突然“病逝”。族叔先是愕然，而后非常奇怪地露出了敬佩的神色。

不是悲伤，而是敬佩？薛元敬狐疑。

之后薛德音神色自若地找了一个薛家的家仆当奶娘，带着幼儿继续启程，薛元敬将疑惑藏在心中。

因为要照顾幼儿，叔侄二人走走停停，沿路遇到郡县就会下榻。

陇右也已经民乱四起。路过河右之地的门户金城县时，二人听闻有河东薛氏族人迁徙此地成为当地豪族，便上门拜访请求帮助，希望金城的薛家人派壮丁保护他们去张掖。

虽然薛元敬带了一队兵丁，但他没有带兵的本事，觉得护卫还是越多越好。

金城的薛家人一听来者居然是河东薛氏本族中最负盛名的“河东三凤”之二，薛元敬和薛德音，自然欣喜若狂。

他们虽然确实是从河东迁徙来的薛氏，但和河东薛氏本家人关系远得几乎只剩一个祖宗，平时都不大好意思自称郡望。家中族长薛举也就当了一个小小的校尉。

薛元敬和薛德音承认他们是“河东薛氏”支脉，金城的薛家人惊喜得都哭了。

原本金城薛家族长薛举骁勇魁梧，又家资豪富，虽然现在没有自立之心，也没想过离开家中坞堡去投奔他人。

现在听闻“河东三凤”已经全部投奔年少的陇右道慰抚使李世民李将军，薛举大腿一拍，校尉辞了，亲自召集族人，凑了一千乡勇护送薛元敬和薛德音。

我也是河东薛氏，我也要投奔李将军！
chunks.englishText:
Li Zhiyun was skilled at chess.

Playing chess required talent. Although Li Xuanba's chess skills were not bad, he could only be considered a competent player who had never truly studied the game. Li Zhiyun, however, was different; he treated playing chess just as he did archery and calligraphy, studying it with diligent devotion.

Yet whenever Li Zhiyun played against Li Xuanba, he acted like a mischievous child messing around, displaying almost no order or method.

In Li Zhiyun's own words, he was "testing out new moves."

Right now, however, Li Zhiyun was not testing new moves—his mind was genuinely restless.

Having been exposed by Li Xuanba, Li Zhiyun stopped pretending.

He complained, "Shixin took the alias Luo Cheng and stole the spotlight on the battlefield. I want to show off too."

A subtle, inscrutable smile curled the corners of Li Xuanba's lips.

The alias "Luo Cheng" had, of course, been bestowed by him. Now, in the late Sui dynasty, there truly was a fierce young general named "Luo Cheng."

Li Xuanba put away the chess pieces. Li Zhiyun hopped off his chair and helped Li Xuanba up.

As Li Xuanba walked toward the door, he nagged, "Why show off at a time like this? What's the point of stealing the spotlight under an alias that no one can connect to you? Wait until we go home to show off."

Li Zhiyun sighed. "Alright. Then, Third Brother, when are we going home? Early next spring?"

Li Xuanba replied, "When spring comes, we go to Qi Commandery first. I've said this many times already. In my current physical condition, I can't travel to Zhangye either."

Li Zhiyun grumbled in annoyance, "But we can go back to Luoyang. As long as we return to Luoyang, Second Brother will get the news and send people to pick us up!"

Li Xuanba said indifferently, "The people setting fires would get the news too. Do you think Hedong is closer to Luoyang, or is Zhangye closer to Luoyang?"

Li Zhiyun pouted. "Fine, no returning to Luoyang. But Third Brother, shouldn't we send Second Brother a letter by now?"

Li Xuanba said, "We'll discuss it after we reach Qi Commandery."

Li Zhiyun was silent for a moment before asking suspiciously, "Third Brother, aside from worrying about falling ill again and making Second Brother rejoice for nothing, are you also worried Second Brother will come in person to tie you up and drag you away, preventing you from causing chaos in the Central Plains?"

Li Xuanba raised his hand and rapped Li Zhiyun hard on the head. "What do you mean 'causing chaos'?! Your Third Brother is about to set the entire Sui Dynasty ablaze, and you call that 'causing chaos'?!"

Li Zhiyun took a deep breath. "You admitted it!"

Li Xuanba: "What did I admit?"

Li Zhiyun shouted loudly, "You *are* worried Second Brother will come tie you up!"

Li Xuanba: "..."

Xu Shiji, who had remained behind at Wagang Stronghold due to injuries that prevented him from joining the raid on the Sui army, came to visit Li Xuanba and Li Zhiyun, carrying precious tonic herbs that his family had secretly searched for and procured.

After obtaining Li Xuanba's consent, Zhai Rang had revealed Li Xuanba's true identity to Xu Shiji. However, he only told Shan Xiongxin that a scholar was staying in the house, not a woman of noble birth.

Fearing Shan Xiongxin might disturb Li Xuanba out of curiosity, Li Xuanba had offered a plan with a smile: "Just tell Shan Xiongxin that I am an extremely stern Confucian scholar. If he wants to enter the room, he must bring classic scriptures to seek my instruction, or else I will scold him furiously. That will keep him away."

Zhai Rang had skeptically relayed Li Xuanba's words to Shan Xiongxin, and Shan Xiongxin surprisingly did start giving the small courtyard a wide berth.

Shan Xiongxin's attitude gave Zhai Rang a pounding headache.

If someone was willing to teach the Confucian classics, Shan Xiongxin ought to have been overjoyed and eager to learn; why on earth was he hiding?

Zhai Rang was originally a minor official, and he had possessed modest wealth in his home village; otherwise, he wouldn't have secured a petty clerk position in the first place.

Xu Shiji came from a wealthy landed gentry family, and Shan Xiongxin was a local magnate capable of rallying a thousand men with a single call. Though they couldn't hire top-tier scholars as teachers, they were all wealthy enough to study and become literate.

Yet the moment studying was brought up, Shan Xiongxin would shake his head vigorously, making Zhai Rang sigh repeatedly.

How could one rise to prominence relying solely on brute force and martial valor? His fellow townsman truly left him exasperated.

Xu Shiji was not much different in age from Li Shimin and Li Xuanba. Back when Li Shimin and Li Xuanba were suppressing bandits in Qinghe Commandery, Xu Shiji had already heard of Li Shimin's reputation as a youthful hero and admired him greatly.

It was only because he was reluctant to leave his hometown, and assumed that as the second son of the Duke of Tang, Li Shimin would look down on him, that he hadn't sought him out.

Now that he had the chance to get to know Li Xuanba, even though he knew Li Xuanba would surely leave once he recovered—and eventually become an enemy to rebels like them—he still seized every opportunity to spend time with Li Xuanba.

Although Zhai Rang had disclosed Li Xuanba's true identity to Xu Shiji, he had not informed him that this raid on the Sui army had actually been planned and orchestrated by Li Xuanba.

When Xu Shiji told his family that he had befriended a formidable scholar, his family increased their financial backing even further, sparing no effort to help Xu Shiji gather medicinal herbs.

"Are you leaving soon?" Xu Shiji said regretfully. "I still wanted to consult Third Young Master Li more about military strategy."

He had no interest in Confucian classics, but he hadn't expected that Li Xuanba, though seemingly frail and sickly, possessed a complete mastery of classic military treatises and spoke on warfare with clear, profound logic, benefiting him immensely.

Li Xuanba said, "As long as fate permits, we shall meet again."

Xu Shiji smiled bitterly. "The next time we meet, we might be enemies."

Li Zhiyun muttered, "That's not necessarily true."

Xu Shiji thought for a moment and said, "True enough. Third Young Master Li probably won't be taking the battlefield."

Li Zhiyun gave Xu Shiji a pitying look and sighed.

Xu Shiji asked in confusion, "Why is Fifth Young Master Li sighing?"

Li Zhiyun said in an unnaturally solemn tone, "It's nothing, just feeling a little sad about parting."

*You foolish Maogong, look at how attentive your Lord Zhai is being. Haven't you noticed anything?*

Having played a game of chess, Li Xuanba was low on energy. Xu Shiji did not linger to disturb him further; leaving behind the herbs, he took his leave.

Li Zhiyun said to Li Xuanba, "I wonder if Xu Shiji will leave Wagang Stronghold when he learns that Zhai Rang intends to align with us."

Li Xuanba instructed someone to deliver the herbs to Yuwen Zhu, who was learning medicine from Sun Simiao, and then said, "Fifth Brother, do you know the difference between Zhai Rang's group and Wang Bo's rebel army?"

Li Zhiyun was no longer as obedient as he was in his childhood. "Third Brother, you're so annoying! Just say what you want to say; don't quiz me."

Li Xuanba: "..." *When we meet Second Brother, I'm definitely going to let him beat you black and blue!*

Li Xuanba said, "Wang Bo is a true commoner, and the people around him are all destitute peasants. They rose in rebellion only because they truly had no way to survive. Though forced by circumstances, raising arms was ultimately faithful to their hearts."

"Zhai Rang was originally a minor county official who was jailed for a crime, later secretly released, and fled to Wagang Stronghold as a fugitive, gathering a crowd to raise arms. Shan Xiongxin, who joined him, is a local magnate, and Xu Shiji comes from a prominent local clan. Their status cannot compare to prestigious nobility—at best, they count as low-born landed gentry—but they are certainly not ordinary peasants."

Hearing Li Xuanba's explanation, Li Zhiyun finally put his sharp mind to work. "Zhai Rang can be considered to have acted out of desperate self-preservation. But since Shan Xiongxin and Xu Shiji weren't backed into a corner, why did they join Zhai Rang?"

He pondered for a moment, his eyes lighting up. "No, Shan Xiongxin and Xu Shiji *were* backed into a corner! They are merely local magnates without official ranks. Although they could buy exemption from corvée labor and military service, Yang Guang is short on troops and provisions. The court won't touch the property of high-ranking noble officials, so it will definitely extort them!"

Li Xuanba nodded in approval. "Correct. Furthermore, if they join the rebellion, they can influence the rebel army's actions and keep them from raiding their own local villages."

Li Zhiyun stroked his unshaven stubble. "So Wang Bo could raid the grain of rich local clans, but Wagang Stronghold only raids official grain transport and wealthy merchants. Right now, they're much poorer than Wang Bo."

Li Xuanba guided him further: "So can you deduce why I dared to reveal my identity to Zhai Rang and Xu Shiji, and why I am certain they will align with us?"

Li Zhiyun smiled. "They come from humble gentry backgrounds, close to the scholar-gentry class, and have always yearned to be recognized as scholars rather than rebels. It was only because the Sui Dynasty gave them no opportunity that they chose to become rebels to protect their lives and wealth. If offered a chance to serve a noble family and elevate themselves into the scholar class, they certainly wouldn't want to remain rebels."

Li Zhiyun thought for a while before adding, "If they lack the confidence to conquer the world during these late Sui troubles, they will inevitably seek someone to serve. Clearly, Zhai Rang is different from Wang Bo or Dou Jiande—he harbors no ambition to become emperor. As for Xu Shiji and Shan Xiongxin... Ah, I was mocking Xu Shiji for being foolish, but could he actually be fully aware of Zhai Rang's hesitation and secretly keeping a way out for himself?"

Li Xuanba said, "Xu Shiji is also different from Shan Xiongxin and Zhai Rang. His clan migrated here from elsewhere, and both his family wealth and lineage far exceed ordinary folk. His family likely raised him as a noble gentry heir."

Li Zhiyun teased, "So this rebel comes from a minor aristocratic clan! Then he will definitely lean toward us. Perhaps even if Zhai Rang is unwilling to serve someone else, Xu Shiji himself would choose a noble clan to serve."

Li Xuanba said, "Still, do not look down on them just because their motives for rebelling weren't entirely pure. In this realm, even minor noble clans and local magnates are on the brink of ruin..."

Li Zhiyun chimed in, "...to say nothing of the common people."

Li Xuanba said, "Mhm. Their desire for self-preservation is real. No one's desire to survive should be taken lightly."

Li Zhiyun rubbed his hands together excitedly, a gesture that looked remarkably familiar to Li Xuanba.

Li Zhiyun rubbed his hands, saying, "So, Xu Shiji might be my subordinate in the future?"

Li Xuanba flicked Li Zhiyun's head. "Then you had better work hard, or else in the future, *you* might end up as Xu Shiji's subordinate. It's not yet decided who will be the chief commander."

Li Zhiyun's eyes widened. "What?! You're actually not showing favoritism? That's too much!"

Li Xuanba: "..." *Isn't refusing to show favoritism the natural, right thing to do? Fifth Brother, what nonsense are you spewing?*

……

After Emperor Yang Guang issued his decree, the rebels' raids on the Sui army were finally brought under control.

The Sui court declared a grand victory.

However, many noble families and grand clans treated this declaration as a complete joke.

Rather than saying the Sui army had repelled the rebels, it was more accurate to say that the rebels had pillaged enough and retreated of their own accord.

Yang Guang had missed the initial window of opportunity. By the time he assembled a large army, the rebel forces had long dispersed into smaller groups and vanished without a trace. The Sui commanders did not even know which rebel faction had raided them.

Because there was no corner under heaven that was free of rebel bandits.

What horrified the Sui imperial court even more was that when one rebel army raised the banner of "Crown Prince Yang Jian," other rebel factions followed suit, raising banners for "Crown Prince Yang Jian" as well.

Rebel chieftains across the country held funeral rites for Crown Prince Yang Jian, and some who had usurped royal titles even bestowed posthumous names upon him.

Some uneducated rebel leaders went so far as to posthumously confer upon Crown Prince Yang Jian the title of Sui Emperor, proclaiming him "Emperor Ai of Sui."

No one dared let word of this reach Yang Guang's ears.

Look at how those three generals had died! Was it not simply because they honestly informed Yang Guang that the rebel bandits were multiplying endlessly and could not be eradicated?

Just for telling the plain truth, all three of them—despite being undefeated on the battlefield—had ended up dead.

Who would dare speak the truth to Yang Guang now?

Su Wei had originally intended to speak frankly, but even he did not dare mention this matter to Yang Guang.

Upon learning of this, Li Yuan sighed, "If His Majesty finds out that Crown Prince Yang Jian has been posthumously declared Emperor, there's no telling how many people will suffer his wrath. We must hasten our preparations for raising an army."

This time, Li Yuan no longer beat around the bush or spoke in riddles, acting as though he were reluctantly pushed into rebellion by his subordinates and sons despite long harboring rebellious intent.

He realized he was walking a dangerous tightrope—Yang Guang did not truly trust him and might inflict punishment at any moment, so he had no choice but to prepare early.

Furthermore, currently only Li Jiancheng was by his side. Li Jiancheng was feeling guilty and lacked the confidence to urge Li Yuan to rebel. Having no one else to shift the burden onto, Li Yuan had to make the call himself.

Of course, he still hinted for his subordinates to persuade him more.

As a minister of the Sui Dynasty, he still could not act too decisively when rebelling; he needed to be "pushed" by his subordinates to make it appear as if he had been driven to a desperate course of action.

In distant Zhangye, Li Shimin learned of this matter several months late.

When he learned of this, the flowers in Zhangye were already in bloom. In the Central Plains, people were likely already wearing thin unlined spring robes.

Now rebel bandits were springing up everywhere, and the Heyou region had virtually lost contact with the Central Plains. Li Shimin could expand his power at will.

Just as Li Shimin received news that the Sui army had been raided, Yang Guang's imperial decree promoting him also arrived.

Yang Guang deeply trusted Li Shimin, who had not pleaded for Crown Prince Yang Jian, and thus promoted Li Shimin to Pacification Commissioner of Longyou Circuit.

Longyou Circuit encompassed the entirety of Heyou as well as several commanderies in Longxi; its jurisdiction was far larger than that of the Heyou Pacification Commissioner.

Additionally, Yang Guang bestowed upon Li Shimin the title of Grand Bandit-Suppression Commissioner of Longyou Circuit, granting him the authority to travel freely across Longyou Circuit and even act at his discretion to assist other areas in suppressing bandits.

Upon receiving the decree, Li Shimin showed no great excitement, taking it entirely in stride.

He methodically delegated his current duties and led troops to places like Guanxi to recruit local magnates. Soon enough, local leaders came with their own troops to join his cause.

However, the greatest harvest after Li Shimin's promotion was not recruited by Li Shimin himself, but brought by Xue Yuanjing, who arrived late.

When Li Shimin had hurriedly departed Taiyuan, he had not taken Xue Yuanjing with him.

Since his journey was dangerous, he had asked Xue Yuanjing to send someone to Zhangye to notify Fang Qiao and the others, while gathering scholars from Taiyuan Commandery to set off for Zhangye ahead of time.

However, Xue Yuanjing had caught a cold on the way and stayed in Daxing for a while to recover, setting off again only when spring arrived; hence, he arrived in Zhangye several months later than Li Shimin.

As a prominent clan of Hedong Commandery, the Xue family naturally maintained residences in both capitals.

While recuperating at the Daxing residence, Xue Yuanjing surprisingly discovered that his clan uncle, Xue Deyin, was also there, bringing along a woman who was near labor.

Xue Deyin did not reveal the woman's identity to Xue Yuanjing, so Xue Yuanjing simply assumed she was his clan uncle's concubine and gave it no further thought.

Xue Deyin informed Xue Yuanjing that he also intended to go to Zhangye to join Li Shimin, but because the woman's pregnancy was unstable, they would wait until she gave birth in Daxing before departing.

Although Xue Yuanjing wondered why his clan uncle didn't stay a few months longer for the woman to recover before leaving Daxing, it was his uncle's private matter, so he refrained from prying.

However, when he and Xue Deyin set off together, an "accident" raised his alertness: the woman successfully delivered the child, but passed away from "illness" a few days later. His clan uncle was stunned at first, but then, strangely enough, revealed a look of deep admiration.

Not grief, but admiration? Xue Yuanjing felt suspicious.

Afterward, Xue Deyin calmly hired a servant from the Xue household as a wet nurse and continued the journey with the newborn infant, while Xue Yuanjing kept his doubts to himself.

Because they had to care for the infant, the uncle and nephew traveled at a leisurely pace, staying at commanderies and counties along the way.

Longyou was also plagued by rebel uprisings. Passing through Jincheng County, the gateway to Heyou, the two heard that members of the Hedong Xue clan had migrated there and become local magnates. They visited them to ask for help, hoping the Jincheng Xue family would dispatch able-bodied men to escort them to Zhangye.

Although Xue Yuanjing brought a squad of soldiers, he lacked command skills and believed that having more guards was always better.

Upon hearing that the visitors were actually two of the "Three Phoenixes of Hedong"—the most renowned figures of the main Hedong Xue clan, Xue Yuanjing and Xue Deyin—the Jincheng Xue family was naturally beside themselves with joy.

Although they indeed belonged to the Xue family that migrated from Hedong, their relationship with the main Hedong Xue branch was so distant that they shared little more than a common ancestor, and they were usually too embarrassed to claim the prestigious clan name. Xue Ju, the patriarch of the family, held only the minor rank of commandant.

When Xue Yuanjing and Xue Deyin formally acknowledged them as a side branch of the "Hedong Xue Clan," the Jincheng Xue family wept with joy.

Originally, Xue Ju, the patriarch of the Jincheng Xue clan, was brave, burly, and immensely wealthy. Although he had no ambition for independence at the moment, he had never considered leaving his family's fortified manor to serve anyone else either.

Now, hearing that all "Three Phoenixes of Hedong" had gone to serve the young Pacification Commissioner of Longyou Circuit, General Li Shimin, Xue Ju slapped his thigh, resigned from his commandant post on the spot, and personally rallied his clan, gathering a thousand local braves to escort Xue Yuanjing and Xue Deyin.

"I am also of the Hedong Xue clan, and I want to pledge myself to General Li as well!"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第143章 太子遗腹子来历
chunks.chineseText:
第143章 太子遗腹子来历

薛元敬在去张掖的途中， 就遇到了正驻扎在西平郡的李世民。
　　河右之地即河西走廊，起点在武威郡。西平郡在武威郡以南，以前是大隋防备吐谷浑的军事重镇。
　　河右之地在李世民和李玄霸回太原前就基本被掌控。在李世民和李玄霸离开的这段时间，房乔等人已经掌控了一半西平郡， 将河右之地彻底与中原切断。
　　现在李世民成了陇右慰抚使， 从陇山六盘山以西到青海湖以东，并囊括了后世新疆东部的广大区域都是李世民的势力范围， 西平郡也在李世民的辖区内。
　　李世民这次亲自带兵， 就是将新到手的地盘收服。
　　金城郡也在李世民这个陇右道慰抚使辖区内， 所以他在西平郡休整后，就会拔营去金城郡。
　　金城郡就是后世兰州。
　　金城郡以西的河源郡等原本在吐谷浑残部控制下的郡县，在李世民支持天柱王当上天柱可汗后，已经全部归属李世民。西平郡在被李世民收服后，金城郡已经唾手可得。
　　只是金城郡有薛举这家豪强， 郡中权力基本掌握在薛家手中， 大隋任命的地方官都要仰仗薛家， 所以李世民正琢磨着怎么打服薛家。
　　边疆和中原不一样， 谁拳头大谁道理就大。对地方豪强不需要讲太多道理， 只要展露出自己能剿灭对方的本事，就能顺利将其收服。
　　天高皇帝远，打了他们， 他们也不能向皇帝告状。
　　陇右道看似面积很广阔，但人口稀少。在中原都逐渐失控的时候，大隋对边疆的管理基本上已经完全失控。所以杨广才放心将陇右道交给李世民。
　　大隋已经无法给边疆提供任何支援，既然李世民在张掖干得不错， 就让李世民继续守着。
　　“听闻你们是河东薛氏， 他就跟着来了？”李世民眉头一挑， 心里浮现弟弟的话。
　　这世家的名声，是真的能兑现的。怪不得为了集中君权，必须削弱世家的声望。
　　不过现在薛元敬用河东薛氏的名声帮自己招揽了薛举这一支金城郡豪强，李世民不会没眼色到这时候忌惮薛家。
　　他很高兴地欢迎了前来投奔的薛举，并让秦琼和薛举比试武艺，又自己与薛举比试射箭。
　　“我们边疆的人没有中原人那么多弯弯道道，交朋友就是好好比一场。”李世民擦着自己的弓，笑着对薛元敬和薛德音道，“边塞不仅风沙大野兽多，披着人皮的蛮夷畜生也多，不展现出自己的武勇，没办法在这里过下去。”
　　薛元敬担忧道：“我也要展现出武勇？”
　　薛德音无语地瞥了薛元敬一眼。
　　李世民道：“你们不用展现武勇，只要我这个慰抚使能展现出令人信服的武勇就行了。”
　　薛元敬松了口气。虽然他并非手无缚鸡之力的弱书生，但和边塞人比武勇还是算了。
　　薛元敬道：“李二郎和薛举比试，是为了慑服他？”
　　李世民点头：“薛举之骁勇，我早有耳闻。之前辅机前来金城郡打探过，薛举可不会轻易被他人收复。多亏你们了。”
　　薛元敬笑着拱手：“能帮到你就好。我还担心其他同僚比我先来陇右，没有我发挥本事的机会。”
　　李世民叹气：“等薛伯褒来的时候，大概会心里憋屈许久。他还没有消息吗？”
　　薛元敬扶额：“我都担心他在海上落草为寇了。真不知道他在干什么。”
　　李世民道：“现在我们困于西域，不能出海寻找他。待我在西域站稳脚跟，我会派人到高丽打探他的踪迹。高丽南端与倭国隔海相望，应当有薛伯褒的消息。”
　　薛元敬道：“那就拜托李二郎了。磬之，你怎么一言不发？”
　　虽然薛德音是薛元敬族叔，但平常他们都相互称呼对方的字，如平辈般相处。
　　薛德音道：“你话都说完了，我还说什么？”
　　薛元敬笑道：“对了，李二郎，磬之此次来张掖还带了一个刚出生的幼儿。你可要帮他寻个好住处。”
　　薛德音眼眸闪了闪，没有说话。
　　李世民看了一眼薛德音的神情，道：“私下说？”
　　薛德音惊讶。
　　薛元敬皱眉：“那孩子身份真的有问题？”
　　薛德音看向薛元敬。
　　薛元敬没好气道：“我很了解你，那女子与你相处时，可一点都不像你房中人。薛磬之，不要给李二郎惹麻烦，你……”
　　李世民打断道：“这里很安全，做什么都不会给我惹麻烦。我们单独聊？”
　　薛德音垂着头道：“子诚都猜出来了，就在这说吧。那孩子是太子的遗腹子。”
　　薛元敬虽然早就隐约猜到那个幼儿的真实身份，还是有点心梗。
　　族叔！你这是要为你的忠义赔上全家啊！
　　李世民道：“孩子生母可是元氏妇韦氏？”
　　薛元敬没有喝水，都被唾沫呛到了：“咳咳咳咳，什么？！什么元氏妇？！难道是哪家寡妇？！”
　　薛德音惊讶极了：“这你都能猜到？！”
　　李世民无奈道：“二表兄来太原市，言语间透露要在做大事前拜访故旧。恐怕他就是那时与元氏妇有了……唉。”
　　在薛德音还在组织语言的时候，李世民先说了自己为何能迅速断定薛德音带来的婴孩是杨暕的遗腹子。
　　李世民到了涿郡后，得知虽然萧皇后请求杨广不要追查杨暕女眷的踪迹，但杨广在斩草除根上从不含糊，杨暕的女眷皆在杨暕被赐死后“殉葬”，甚至连杨暕的女儿都没能逃脱。
　　杨暕的王妃早逝后，即使他当了多年太子，杨广也没有再给他选太子妃，府中妾室出身都不高。所以杨广让杨暕女眷殉死的事，没有引起任何波澜。
　　李玄霸之前和李世民私下一同吐槽，说杨广估计一早就忌惮杨暕，所以才不给杨暕重新选太子妃，怕杨暕有妻族支持。
　　“杨广虽然对二表兄府中监视严格，但在臣子府中，他几乎没有眼线，全靠臣子之间和其家人告密。”李世民眼中闪过一丝讽刺，杨广掌控欲很强，但表现得却很废物，“二表兄大概是在元氏妇家中私会。”
　　说到这，李世民又想起了弟弟的吐槽。
　　杨暕与元氏妇私会时，元氏妇的丈夫是默许的。
　　元氏妇的丈夫是个凭借门荫入仕，没什么作为的纨绔子弟，自己玩得就很，男女荤素不忌，与自己妻子不仅各玩各的，有时候还会一起玩耍。
　　李玄霸吐槽，元氏妇与二表兄在家中私会，怕不是元氏妇的丈夫对二表兄也有企图，只是碍于二表兄的身份只能过个眼瘾。二表兄那张脸啊，真是蓝颜祸水。
　　年少的李世民感到了极度的震撼，幼小的心灵遭遇了极大的创伤，并让弟弟闭嘴，不准再说这些肮脏事。
　　现在已经长大的李世民，神色很平静地把从弟弟那里听来的小道消息告诉了薛元敬和薛德音。薛元敬和薛德音露出了与年少李世民同样的大受震撼并大受伤害的神情。
　　李世民感慨：“我在涿郡时，听闻二表兄兵谏后，许多人家都与二表兄撇清关心，元氏妇也迅速‘病逝’，尸骸都入土了。没想到元氏夫妇居然为二表兄藏了一个孩子，我都快相信阿玄的胡言乱语了。”
　　薛元敬的胡须不够长，没办法扯，他只能扯着自己没扎严实的鬓发，把自己的头发扯成了乱鸡窝，嘴唇哆哆嗦嗦，半晌说不出话来。
　　薛德音也神情复杂。
　　他虽然知道为太子生育遗腹子的女子就是元氏妇韦氏，但他只是想到太子与元氏妇余情未了，怎么还扯上元家郎君了？
　　薛德音很想反驳，但听了李世民的小道消息后，他很难不被李世民说服。
　　如果没有元家郎君的掩护，元氏妇怀有孩子的消息不可能不泄露，更何况元家郎君居然还伪造了元氏妇“被病逝”的假象，甚至不知道从哪找了具女尸埋进祖坟。
　　元氏妇出身京兆韦氏。京兆韦氏默许元家郎君为了自保让族中女子病逝，但主母的身份还是得保留，所以祖坟还是得进的。
　　正因为元氏妇被埋进了祖坟，所以没有人怀疑死的不是元氏妇本人。
　　这可是祖坟啊！
　　薛德音深呼吸了几下，双手捂住垂下的脸，长长叹了口气：“是元家郎君有侠义之心，对太子殿下忠诚而已，只是这样而已。”
　　薛元敬嘴角抽搐。族叔，你说这话你自己信吗？！
　　李世民走神。他想，这就是阿玄说的槽点太多，不知道从哪吐起吧？
　　见薛德音心态快崩了，李世民转移话题：“元氏妇自尽，大约是担心别人发现她还活着，继而猜到二表兄遗腹子的事。她真是对二表兄一往情深。我在狱中和二表兄聊天时，二表兄并不知道元氏妇怀着他的孩子，还感慨自己没有子嗣是件好事，杨广总不至于对孙女动手。是庾养廉隐瞒了吗？”
　　杨暕的女儿对杨广没有任何威胁。杨暕以为杨广好脸面，为了展现出仁慈，应当不会对年幼的孙女动手。他真是从始至终都不了解自己的父皇。
　　薛德音放下手，疲惫地回答道：“是。太子殿下重感情，又不善隐瞒，所以庾养廉没让太子殿下知道此事。元氏妇在与太子殿下私……私会的时候，还骗太子殿下喝了避孕药。”
　　李世民的嘴角都抽搐了：“这世上哪来的避孕药？二表兄真是好骗。”
　　李玄霸在李世民叨叨了许多次避孕的事，李世民印象深刻。
　　薛元敬叹气道：“为了给太子殿下留一个遗腹子，庾养廉和元氏夫妇真是用心良苦。”
　　李玄霸吐槽：“这样就衬托着二表兄更像个铁憨憨了。二表兄就算已经成为合格的太子，但还是和以前一样是个铁憨憨。”
　　李世民虽然心里赞同，嘴上还是训斥道：“别这么说二表兄。”
　　薛元敬疑惑：“什么‘别这么说’？”
　　薛德音也疑惑地看着李世民。
　　李世民神情恍惚了一下，很快回过神：“没什么，你们听错了。我的意思是，二表兄真憨厚。”
　　薛元敬：“……”
　　薛德音：“……”
　　叔侄二人异口同声道：“虽然……但是别这么说太子殿下！”
　　李世民摸了摸鼻子，失笑道：“好，不说。磬之，这孩子还是暂时以你庶子的身份养着。你放心，将来我一定会让他恢复姓氏，延续二表兄的香火。这孩子取名了吗？”
　　薛德音神色悲哀道：“他母亲为他取名了，名……名愍，愍悼的愍。”
　　作者有话要说：
　　新的一个月，休息一天，今天只有一更。昨天的承诺明天再兑现，躺平。
　　关于修文，如果章节有标题和作话，修改章节就只是捉虫和润色，不用重看；如果没有作话，就是剧情没写完，建议第二天再瞟一眼。即，作话才是结尾（挠头）。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 143: The Origin of the Crown Prince's Posthumous Child

On his way to Zhangye, Xue Yuanjing encountered Li Shimin, who was currently stationed in Xiping Commandery.

The land of Heyou was the Hexi Corridor, starting at Wuwei Commandery. Xiping Commandery lay to the south of Wuwei, historically serving as a crucial Sui military stronghold against the Tuyuhun.

The Heyou region had largely been brought under control before Li Shimin and Li Xuanba returned to Taiyuan. During their absence, Fang Qiao and the others had already taken control of half of Xiping Commandery, completely severing the Heyou region from the Central Plains.

Now that Li Shimin was the Pacification Commissioner of Longyou, his realm of influence spanned from west of Mount Long and the Liupan Mountains to east of Qinghai Lake, encompassing the vast region of eastern modern-day Xinjiang. Xiping Commandery was naturally within his jurisdiction.

Li Shimin was personally leading troops this time to fully subjugate his newly acquired territories.

Jincheng Commandery also fell within his domain as Pacification Commissioner of the Longyou Circuit. Thus, after resting and regrouping his army in Xiping Commandery, he intended to strike camp and march on Jincheng.

Jincheng Commandery was modern-day Lanzhou.

The commanderies west of Jincheng, such as Heyuan Commandery, which were formerly under the control of Tuyuhun remnants, had all submitted to Li Shimin after he supported King Tianzhu in becoming the Tianzhu Khagan. With Xiping Commandery subjugated, Jincheng Commandery was practically within his grasp.

However, Jincheng Commandery contained a formidable local magnate named Xue Ju. Power in the commandery was mostly controlled by the Xue family, and the local officials appointed by the Sui Dynasty all had to rely on their favor. Thus, Li Shimin was pondering how to beat the Xue family into submission.

The borderlands differed from the Central Plains; here, whoever possessed the bigger fist held the truth. One did not need to reason overmuch with local magnates—simply demonstrating the capability to wipe them out was enough to smoothly subdue them.

The heavens were high and the emperor was far away. Even if he thrashed them, they had no way of filing a complaint with the sovereign.

The Longyou Circuit appeared vast, but its population was sparse. As the Sui's control over the Central Plains gradually unraveled, its governance over the borderlands had essentially broken down entirely. That was why Yang Guang had comfortably handed Longyou Circuit over to Li Shimin.

The Sui Dynasty could no longer provide any support to the frontiers. Since Li Shimin was doing well in Zhangye, Yang Guang simply let him continue guarding it.

"Hearing that you were of the Hedong Xue clan, he just followed you here?" Li Shimin raised an eyebrow, his younger brother's words echoing in his mind.

The prestige of a prominent clan truly held tangible currency. Small wonder that to concentrate imperial power, one had to weaken the prestige of noble families.

Still, now that Xue Yuanjing had used the reputation of the Hedong Xue clan to help him win over Xue Ju—the powerful local warlord of Jincheng—Li Shimin was not so tactless as to harbor suspicion toward the Xue clan at such a moment.

He warmly welcomed Xue Ju, who had come to pledge allegiance, and arranged for Qin Qiong to spar with Xue Ju in martial arts before competing against Xue Ju himself in archery.

"We people of the frontier don't have as many twists and turns as those in the Central Plains. To make friends, we just have a good match," Li Shimin said with a laugh as he wiped down his bow, speaking to Xue Yuanjing and Xue Deyin. "The border regions aren't just full of harsh winds, sand, and wild beasts—they're also full of barbarian beasts in human skin. If you don't display your martial prowess, there's no way to survive here."

Xue Yuanjing asked worryingly, "Do I have to display martial prowess too?"

Xue Deyin cast a speechlessly exasperated glance at Xue Yuanjing.

Li Shimin chuckled, "You two don't need to. It's enough as long as I, the Pacification Commissioner, can display convincing martial prowess."

Xue Yuanjing let out a breath of relief. Although he wasn't a fragile scholar incapable of lifting a chicken, competing in martial strength against frontier folk was out of the question.

Xue Yuanjing asked, "Second Young Master Li, did you compete with Xue Ju to awe him into submission?"

Li Shimin nodded. "I had long heard of Xue Ju's valor. Earlier, Fuji came to Jincheng Commandery to investigate, and he said Xue Ju wouldn't be easily subjugated by anyone. Thanks to you two."

Xue Yuanjing cupped his hands with a smile. "It's good that I could be of help. I was actually worried that other colleagues might arrive in Longyou before me, leaving me with no chance to show my worth."

Li Shimin sighed. "When Xue Bobao arrives, he'll probably feel suffocated with frustration for quite some time. Still no news of him?"

Xue Yuanjing slapped his forehead. "I'm worried he's turned to piracy on the high seas. I really don't know what he's up to."

Li Shimin said, "For now, we are tied up in the Western Regions and cannot set sail to find him. Once I firm up our foothold in the Western Regions, I will send people to Goguryeo to inquire about his whereabouts. The southern end of Goguryeo faces Wa across the sea; there should be news of Xue Bobao there."

Xue Yuanjing said, "Then I leave it in your hands, Second Young Master Li. Qingzhi, why haven't you said a word?"

Although Xue Deyin was Xue Yuanjing's clan uncle, they usually addressed each other by their courtesy names, getting along like peers.

Xue Deyin said, "You've said everything already. What is there left for me to say?"

Xue Yuanjing smiled and said, "By the way, Second Young Master Li, Qingzhi brought a newborn infant with him to Zhangye. You must help him find a suitable place to stay."

Xue Deyin's eyes flickered, but he remained silent.

Li Shimin glanced at Xue Deyin's expression and asked, "Shall we speak in private?"

Xue Deyin was surprised.

Xue Yuanjing frowned. "Is there really a problem with that child's identity?"

Xue Deyin looked at Xue Yuanjing.

Xue Yuanjing grumbled in exasperation, "I know you well. When that woman interacted with you, she didn't look like your concubine at all. Xue Qingzhi, don't bring trouble to Second Young Master Li, you..."

Li Shimin interrupted, "It's safe here, and whatever you do won't bring me trouble. Shall we speak alone?"

Xue Deyin bowed his head and said, "Since Zicheng has already guessed it, let's just speak here. That child is the Crown Prince's posthumous son."

Although Xue Yuanjing had long vaguely guessed the infant's true identity, he still felt a surge of chest tightness.

*Clan Uncle! Are you really going to gamble the entire family's lives for the sake of your loyalty?!*

Li Shimin asked, "Is the child's birth mother Lady Wei, wife of the Yuan clan?"

Xue Yuanjing wasn't even drinking water, yet he choked on his own saliva: "Cough, cough, cough! What?! What wife of the Yuan clan?! Could it be a widow from some house?!"

Xue Deyin was astonished. "You could even guess that?!"

Li Shimin said helplessly, "When Second Cousin came to Taiyuan, his words hinted that he was visiting old acquaintances before taking big action. I fear it was then that he and Lady Wei had... *sigh*."

While Xue Deyin was still gathering his thoughts, Li Shimin explained first why he was able to swiftly conclude that the baby brought by Xue Deyin was Yang Jian's posthumous child.

After arriving in Zhuo Commandery, Li Shimin learned that although Empress Xiao had begged Yang Guang not to hunt down Yang Jian's female dependents, Yang Guang had never been soft-hearted when it came to pulling up weeds by their roots. All of Yang Jian's female household members were forced to be "buried with him" after he was granted death, and even Yang Jian's daughters failed to escape.

After Yang Jian's primary consort died early, even though he served as Crown Prince for many years, Yang Guang never selected a new Crown Princess for him, and the concubines in his manor were of low birth. Thus, Yang Guang forcing Yang Jian's women to be buried alongside him caused no waves whatsoever.

Li Xuanba had previously complained to Li Shimin in private, saying Yang Guang likely harbored deep suspicion toward Yang Jian early on, which was why he refused to choose another primary consort for him—afraid that Yang Jian would gain powerful backing from a wife's family.

"Although Yang Guang monitored Second Cousin's residence strictly, he had almost no informants in his officials' manors, relying entirely on mutual betrayal among officials and their families." A glint of irony flashed in Li Shimin's eyes; Yang Guang had an intense desire for control, yet proved hopelessly incompetent at it. "Second Cousin likely held his secret trysts in Lady Wei's home."

Speaking of this, Li Shimin recalled his younger brother's snarky remarks.

When Yang Jian had his trysts with Lady Wei, her husband tacitly permitted it.

Lady Wei's husband was a playboy who entered officialdom purely through ancestral privilege and possessed zero achievement. He himself led an extremely wild lifestyle, lacking any taboos regarding men or women. Not only did he and his wife pursue their own separate amusements, but sometimes they even indulged in them together.

Li Xuanba had snarked that when Lady Wei and Second Cousin met secretly at her house, her husband might very well have harbored designs on Second Cousin as well, held back only by Second Cousin's status and settling for feast-of-the-eyes eye candy. Second Cousin's face was truly a dangerous distraction.

The young Li Shimin had been profoundly shocked, his innocent mind suffering severe psychic damage, prompting him to tell his younger brother to shut his mouth and stop speaking of such filthy matters.

Now fully grown, Li Shimin calmly relayed the gossip he had heard from his brother to Xue Yuanjing and Xue Deyin. Xue Yuanjing and Xue Deyin immediately wore the exact same deeply shocked and traumatized expressions as the younger Li Shimin once had.

Li Shimin sighed wistfully. "When I was in Zhuo Commandery, I heard that after Second Cousin staged his armed protest, many families severed ties with him. Lady Wei also swiftly 'died of illness,' and her body was laid to rest. I never expected that the Yuan couple would actually hide a child for Second Cousin. I'm almost starting to believe Ah Xuan's wild nonsense."

Xue Yuanjing's beard wasn't long enough to tug on, so he could only yank at his loosely bound hair at the temples, pulling it into a messy bird's nest. His lips quivered uncontrollably, unable to utter a word for a long while.

Xue Deyin's expression was equally complex.

Although he knew that the woman who bore the Crown Prince's posthumous child was indeed Lady Wei, wife of the Yuan clan, he had merely assumed that the Crown Prince and Lady Wei still harbored lingering feelings for each other. How on earth had Young Master Yuan gotten dragged into this?!

Xue Deyin desperately wanted to refute it, but after hearing Li Shimin's gossip, he found it nearly impossible not to be persuaded.

Without Young Master Yuan's cover, it would have been impossible for Lady Wei's pregnancy to remain secret. Furthermore, Young Master Yuan had even fabricated the illusion of Lady Wei's "death by illness," somehow procuring a female corpse from who-knows-where to bury in the ancestral tomb.

Lady Wei hailed from the Jingzhao Wei clan. The Jingzhao Wei clan had tacitly permitted Young Master Yuan to let a daughter of their clan "die of illness" for self-preservation, but her status as the primary wife still had to be preserved—hence, she still had to be buried in the ancestral tomb.

Precisely because "Lady Wei" was buried in the ancestral tomb, no one suspected that the deceased was not Lady Wei herself.

This was the ancestral tomb, after all!

Xue Deyin took several deep breaths, buried his face in his hands, and let out a long sigh. "It is merely that Young Master Yuan possesses a chivalrous heart and was loyal to His Royal Highness the Crown Prince. It is simply that."

Xue Yuanjing's lips twitched violently. *Clan Uncle, do you even believe what you're saying?!*

Li Shimin zoned out for a moment. He thought: *Is this what Ah Xuan calls 'having so many absurd points that one doesn't even know where to start mocking'?*

Seeing that Xue Deyin was on the verge of a mental breakdown, Li Shimin changed the subject: "Lady Wei committed suicide likely out of fear that if others discovered she was alive, they would deduce the existence of Second Cousin's posthumous child. She truly held deep affection for Second Cousin. When I spoke with Second Cousin in prison, he didn't know Lady Wei was pregnant with his child. He even lamented that it was a good thing he had no sons left, reasoning that Yang Guang surely wouldn't move against his granddaughters. Did Yu Yanglian conceal this from him?"

Yang Jian's daughters posed no threat whatsoever to Yang Guang. Yang Jian had believed that since Yang Guang cared greatly about appearances, he would refrain from acting against young granddaughters to project benevolence. From beginning to end, Yang Jian had truly never understood his own imperial father.

Xue Deyin lowered his hands and answered exhaustedly, "Yes. His Royal Highness was deeply sentimental and poor at keeping secrets, so Yu Yanglian kept him in the dark. When Lady Wei held secret... trysts with His Royal Highness, she even tricked him into drinking contraceptive medicine."

Li Shimin's lips twitched. "Where in the world would real contraceptive medicine come from? Second Cousin truly was gullible."

Li Xuanba had nagged Li Shimin about contraception many times, leaving a deep impression on him.

Xue Yuanjing sighed. "To preserve a posthumous child for His Royal Highness, Yu Yanglian and the Yuan couple truly went to extraordinary lengths."

Li Xuanba's snarky voice seemed to echo: *"This just makes Second Cousin look even more like a total airhead. Even if Second Cousin became a proper Crown Prince, he's still as much of an airhead as before."*

Although Li Shimin agreed in his heart, he still chided out loud, "Don't speak of Second Cousin like that."

Xue Yuanjing was bewildered. "What do you mean, 'Don't speak of him like that'?"

Xue Deyin also looked at Li Shimin in confusion.

Li Shimin dazed off for a moment, then quickly snapped back: "Nothing, you misheard. I meant... Second Cousin was truly honest and simple."

Xue Yuanjing: "..."
Xue Deyin: "..."

The uncle and nephew spoke in unison: "Even though... still, don't speak of His Royal Highness the Crown Prince like that!"

Li Shimin rubbed his nose and chuckled helplessly. "Alright, I won't. Qingzhi, for now, raise this child under the guise of your concubine's son. Rest assured, in the future, I will definitely restore his lineage so he can continue Second Cousin's bloodline. Has the child been named?"

Xue Deyin spoke with a sorrowful expression, "His mother gave him a name. His name is... Min. The 'Min' from *Mindao*—lamentation and grief."

***

New month, taking a day's rest, so today only has one update. The promise from yesterday will be fulfilled tomorrow, lying flat.
Regarding text revisions: If a chapter has a title and author's note, the revision is just bug-fixing and polishing, no need to re-read; if there is no author's note, it means the plot wasn't finished writing, so it's recommended to glance at it again the next day. In short, the author's note is the true ending (scratches head).
